verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ prá ǀ śaṃsata ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ śumbhata ǀ naraḥ ǀtā́ ǀ gāyatréṣu ǀ gāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise ye, O men, and glorify Indra-Agni in the holy rites: Sing praise to them in sacred songs.
verses.wilson_translation: Praise, men,Indraand Agni, in sacrifices, decorate them (with ornaments) and hymn them with hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: Praise ye, O men, and glorify Indra-Agni in the holy rites: Sing praise to them in sacred songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता मित्रस्य प्रशस्तय इंद्राग्नी ता हवामहे ।सोमपा सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ mitrásya ǀ prá-śastaye ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ tā́ ǀ havāmahe ǀsoma-pā́ ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra and Agni we invite, the Soma-drinkers, for the fame Of Mitra, to the Soma-draught.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke Indraand Agni, for the benefit of our friend (the instrumental tutor of the rite), drinkers of the Somajuice, to drink the libation.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra and Agni we invite, the Soma-drinkers, for the fame Of Mitra, to the Soma-draught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उग्रा संता हवामह उपेदं सवनं सुतं ।इंद्राग्नी एह गच्छतां ॥
verses.transliteration: ugrā́ ǀ sántā ǀ havāmahe ǀ úpa ǀ idám ǀ sávanam ǀ sutám ǀindrāgnī́ íti ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ gacchatām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong Gods, we bid them come to this libation that stands ready here: Indra and Agni, come to us.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke the two who are fierce (to their foes) to attend the rite, where the libation is prepared;Indraand Agni, come hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong Gods, we bid them come to this libation that stands ready here: Indra and Agni, come to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता महांता सदस्पती इंद्राग्नी रक्ष उब्जतं ।अप्रजाः संत्वत्रिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ mahā́ntā ǀ sádaspátī íti ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ ubjatam ǀáprajāḥ ǀ santu ǀ atríṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra and Agni, mighty Lords of our assembly, crush the fiends: Childless be the devouring ones.
verses.wilson_translation: May those two,Indraand Agniwho are mighty, and guardians of the assembly, render the Rākṣasinnocuous, and may the devourers (of men) be destitute of progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra and Agni, mighty Lords of our assembly, crush the fiends: Childless be the devouring ones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेन सत्येन जागृतमधि प्रचेतुने पदे ।इंद्राग्नी शर्म यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: téna ǀ satyéna ǀ jāgṛtam ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-cetúne ǀ padé ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Watch ye, through this your truthfulness, there in the place of spacious view Indra and Agni, send us bliss.
verses.wilson_translation: By this unfailing sacrifice, by you rendered vigilant,Indraand Agni, in the station which affords knowledge (of the consequence of acts), and bestow upon us happiness.
verses.griffith_verse: Watch ye, through this your truthfulness, there in the place of spacious view Indra and Agni, send us bliss.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXII. Aśvins and Others
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WAKEN the Aśvin Pair who yoke their car at early morn: may theyApproach to drink this Soma juice. We call the Aśvins Twain, the Gods borne in a noble car, the bestOf charioteers, who reach the heavens. Dropping with honey is your whip, Aśvins, and full of pleasantnessSprinkle therewith the sacrifice. As ye go thither in your car, not far, O Aśvins, is the homeOf him who offers Soma juice. For my protection I invoke the golden-handed Savitar.He knoweth, as a God, the place. That he may send us succour, praise the Waters’ Offspring Savitar:Fain are we for his holy ways. We call on him, distributer of wondrous bounty and of wealth,On Savitar who looks on men. Come hither, friends, and seat yourselves Savitar, to be praised by us,Giving good gifts, is beautiful. O Agni, hither bring to us the willing Spouses of the Gods,And Tvaṣṭar, to the Soma draught. Most youthful Agni, hither bring their Spouses, Hotrā, Bhāratī,Varūtrī, Dhiṣaṇā, for aid. Spouses of Heroes, Goddesses, with whole wings may they come to usWith great protection and with aid. Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, and Agnāyī hither I invite,For weal, to drink the Soma juice. May Heaven and Earth, the Mighty Pair, bedew for us our sacrifice,And feed us full with nourishments. Their water rich with fatness, there in the Gandharva's steadfast place,The singers taste through sacred songs. Thornless be thou, O Earth, spread wide before us for a dwelling-place:Vouchsafe us shelter broad and sure. The Gods be gracious unto us even from the place whence Viṣṇu strodeThrough the seven regions of the earth! Through all this world strode Viṣṇu; thrice his foot he planted, and the wholeWas gathered in his footstep's dust. Viṣṇu, the Guardian, he whom none deceiveth, made three steps; thenceforthEstablishing his high decrees. Look ye on Viṣṇu's works, whereby the Friend of Indra, close-allied,Hath let his holy ways be seen. The princes evermore behold that loftiest place where Viṣṇu is,Laid as it were an eye in heaven. This, Viṣṇu's station most sublime, the singers, ever vigilant,Lovers of holy song, light up.

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्युजा वि बोधयाश्विनावेह गच्छतां ।अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-yújā ǀ ví ǀ bodhaya ǀ aśvínau ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ gacchatām ǀasyá ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: WAKEN the Aśvin Pair who yoke their car at early morn: may they Approach to drink this Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Awaken, the Aśvins, associated for the morning sacrifice; let them both come hither to drink of this Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: WAKEN the Aśvin Pair who yoke their car at early morn: may they Approach to drink this Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या सुरथा रथीतमोभा देवा दिविस्पृशा ।अश्विना ता हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ su-ráthā ǀ rathí-tamā ǀ ubhā́ ǀ devā́ ǀ divi-spṛ́śā ǀaśvínā ǀ tā́ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call the Aśvins Twain, the Gods borne in a noble car, the best Of charioteers, who reach the heavens.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke the two Aśvins, who are both divine, the best of charioteers, riding in an excellent car and attaining heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: We call the Aśvins Twain, the Gods borne in a noble car, the best Of charioteers, who reach the heavens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या वां कशा मधुमत्यश्विना सूनृतावती ।तया यज्ञं मिमिक्षतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ vām ǀ káśā ǀ mádhu-matī ǀ áśvinā ǀ sūnṛ́tā-vatī ǀtáyā ǀ yajñám ǀ mimikṣatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dropping with honey is your whip, Aśvins, and full of pleasantness Sprinkle therewith the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, stir up (mimikṣatam = mix intimately, rapidly like a whip) the sacrifice with your whip that is wet the foam (of your horses), and lashing loudly.
verses.griffith_verse: Dropping with honey is your whip, Aśvins, and full of pleasantness Sprinkle therewith the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि वामस्ति दूरके यत्रा रथेन गच्छथः ।अश्विना सोमिनो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ vām ǀ ásti ǀ dūraké ǀ yátra ǀ ráthena ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀáśvinā ǀ somínaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ye go thither in your car, not far, O Aśvins, is the home Of him who offers Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: The abode of the offerer of the libation is not far from you,Aśvins, going thither in your car.
verses.griffith_verse: As ye go thither in your car, not far, O Aśvins, is the home Of him who offers Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यपाणिमूतये सवितारमुप ह्वये ।स चेत्ता देवता पदं ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-pāṇim ǀ ūtáye ǀ savitā́ram ǀ úpa ǀ hvaye ǀsáḥ ǀ céttā ǀ devátā ǀ padám ǁ
verses.english_translation: For my protection I invoke the golden-handed Savitar. He knoweth, as a God, the place.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoke Savitā(Sun), the golden- handed, to protect me; he will appoint the station of the worshippers.
verses.griffith_verse: For my protection I invoke the golden-handed Savitar. He knoweth, as a God, the place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपां नपातमवसे सवितारमुप स्तुहि ।तस्य व्रतान्युश्मसि ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ nápātam ǀ ávase ǀ savitā́ram ǀ úpa ǀ stuhi ǀtásya ǀ vratā́ni ǀ uśmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: That he may send us succour, praise the Waters’ Offspring Savitar: Fain are we for his holy ways.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify Savitā, who is no friend to water, or our protection; we desire to celebrate his worship.(apāmnapāt= son of the waters).
verses.griffith_verse: That he may send us succour, praise the Waters’ Offspring Savitar: Fain are we for his holy ways.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विभक्तारं हवामहे वसोश्चित्रस्य राधसः ।सवितारं नृचक्षसं ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-bhaktā́ram ǀ havāmahe ǀ vásoḥ ǀ citrásya ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀsavitā́ram ǀ nṛ-cákṣasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call on him, distributer of wondrous bounty and of wealth, On Savitar who looks on men.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke Savitā, the enlightener of men, the dispenser of various home-insuring wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: We call on him, distributer of wondrous bounty and of wealth, On Savitar who looks on men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सखाय आ नि षीदत सविता स्तोम्यो नु नः ।दाता राधांसि शुंभति ॥
verses.transliteration: sákhāyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ní ǀ sīdata ǀ savitā́ ǀ stómyaḥ ǀ nú ǀ naḥ ǀdā́tā ǀ rā́dhāṃsi ǀ śumbhati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither, friends, and seat yourselves Savitar, to be praised by us, Giving good gifts, is beautiful.
verses.wilson_translation: Sit down, friends;Savitāverily is to be praised by us, for he is the giver of riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither, friends, and seat yourselves Savitar, to be praised by us, Giving good gifts, is beautiful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने पत्नीरिहा वह देवानामुशतीरुप ।त्वष्टारं सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ ihá ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ devā́nām ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀtváṣṭāram ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, hither bring to us the willing Spouses of the Gods, And Tvaṣṭar, to the Soma draught.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, bring hither the loving wives of the gods, and Tvaṣṭā, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, hither bring to us the willing Spouses of the Gods, And Tvaṣṭar, to the Soma draught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ ग्ना अग्न इहावसे होत्रां यविष्ठ भारतीं ।वरूत्रीं धिषणां वह ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ ihá ǀ ávase ǀ hótrām ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ bhā́ratīm ǀvárūtrīm ǀ dhiṣáṇām ǀ vaha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most youthful Agni, hither bring their Spouses, Hotrā, Bhāratī, Varūtrī, Dhiṣaṇā, for aid.
verses.wilson_translation: Youthful Agni, bring hither for our protection the wives (of the gods),Hotrā(wife of Agni or person nified invocation),Bhāratī(anĀditya), Varutrī (= varaṇīyā, chosen), and Dhiṣaṇā(= vāc or vāg-devī, goddess of speech).
verses.griffith_verse: Most youthful Agni, hither bring their Spouses, Hotrā, Bhāratī, Varūtrī, Dhiṣaṇā, for aid.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि नो देवीरवसा महः शर्मणा नृपत्नीः ।अच्छिन्नपत्राः सचंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ maháḥ ǀ śármaṇā ǀ nṛ-pátnīḥ ǀácchinna-patrāḥ ǀ sacantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Spouses of Heroes, Goddesses, with whole wings may they come to us With great protection and with aid.
verses.wilson_translation: May the goddesses, whose wings are unclipt the protectresses of mankind, favour us with perfection, and with entire felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Spouses of Heroes, Goddesses, with whole wings may they come to us With great protection and with aid.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इहेंद्राणीमुप ह्वये वरुणानीं स्वस्तये ।अग्नायीं सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ indrāṇī́m ǀ úpa ǀ hvaye ǀ varuṇānī́m ǀ svastáye ǀagnā́yīm ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, and Agnāyī hither I invite, For weal, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoke hither,Indrāṇī,Varuṇānī, and Agnāyī, for our welfare, and to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, and Agnāyī hither I invite, For weal, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां ।पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ mimikṣatām ǀpipṛtā́m ǀ naḥ ǀ bhárīma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Heaven and Earth, the Mighty Pair, bedew for us our sacrifice, And feed us full with nourishments.
verses.wilson_translation: May the great heven and the earth be plural ased to blend this sacrifice (with their own dews) and fill us with nutriment.
verses.griffith_verse: May Heaven and Earth, the Mighty Pair, bedew for us our sacrifice, And feed us full with nourishments.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तयोरिद्घृतवत्पयो विप्रा रिहंति धीतिभिः ।गंधर्वस्य ध्रुवे पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: táyoḥ ǀ ít ǀ ghṛtá-vat ǀ páyaḥ ǀ víprāḥ ǀ rihanti ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀgandharvásya ǀ dhruvé ǀ padé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Their water rich with fatness, there in the Gandharva's steadfast place, The singers taste through sacred songs.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise taste, through their pious acts, theghee-resembling waters of these two, (abiding) in the permanent region of the Gandharvas. (Antarikṣa, the sphere of gandharvas,yakṣasandapsarasas, the firmament between heaven and earth).
verses.griffith_verse: Their water rich with fatness, there in the Gandharva's steadfast place, The singers taste through sacred songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्योना पृथिवि भवानृक्षरा निवेशनी ।यच्छा नः शर्म सप्रथः ॥
verses.transliteration: syonā́ ǀ pṛthivi ǀ bhava ǀ anṛkṣarā́ ǀ ni-véśanī ǀyáccha ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thornless be thou, O Earth, spread wide before us for a dwelling-place: Vouchsafe us shelter broad and sure.
verses.wilson_translation: Earth be your wide-spreading, free from thorns, and our abiding plural ce; give us great happiness.
verses.griffith_verse: Thornless be thou, O Earth, spread wide before us for a dwelling-place: Vouchsafe us shelter broad and sure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतो देवा अवंतु नो यतो विष्णुर्विचक्रमे ।पृथिव्याः सप्त धामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: átaḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ avantu ǀ naḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ vi-cakramé ǀpṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ saptá ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods be gracious unto us even from the place whence Viṣṇu strode Through the seven regions of the earth!
verses.wilson_translation: May the gods preserve us (from that portion) of the earth whence Viṣṇu(aided) by the seven metres, stepped.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods be gracious unto us even from the place whence Viṣṇu strode Through the seven regions of the earth!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रेधा नि दधे पदं ।समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरे ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakrame ǀ tredhā́ ǀ ní ǀ dadhe ǀ padám ǀsám-ūḷham ǀ asya ǀ pāṃsuré ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through all this world strode Viṣṇu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep's dust.
verses.wilson_translation: Viṣṇutraversed this (world); three times he plural nted his foot and the whole (world) was collected in the dust of his (footstep).
verses.griffith_verse: Through all this world strode Viṣṇu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep's dust.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रीणि पदा वि चक्रमे विष्णुर्गोपा अदाभ्यः ।अतो धर्माणि धारयन् ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ṇi ǀ padā́ ǀ ví ǀ cakrame ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǀátaḥ ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ dhāráyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Viṣṇu, the Guardian, he whom none deceiveth, made three steps; thenceforth Establishing his high decrees.
verses.wilson_translation: Viṣṇu, the preserver, the uninjurable, stepped three steps, upholding thereby righteous acts.
verses.griffith_verse: Viṣṇu, the Guardian, he whom none deceiveth, made three steps; thenceforth Establishing his high decrees.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यत यतो व्रतानि पस्पशे ।इंद्रस्य युज्यः सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣṇoḥ ǀ kármāṇi ǀ paśyata ǀ yátaḥ ǀ vratā́ni ǀ paspaśé ǀíndrasya ǀ yújyaḥ ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Look ye on Viṣṇu's works, whereby the Friend of Indra, close-allied, Hath let his holy ways be seen.
verses.wilson_translation: Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which (the worshipper) has accomplished (pious) vows; he is the worthy friend of Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Look ye on Viṣṇu's works, whereby the Friend of Indra, close-allied, Hath let his holy ways be seen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः ।दिवीव चक्षुराततं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ paramám ǀ padám ǀ sádā ǀ paśyanti ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀdiví-iva ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ ā́-tatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The princes evermore behold that loftiest place where Viṣṇu is, Laid as it were an eye in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise ever contemplate that supreme station of Viṣṇu, as the eye ranges over the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: The princes evermore behold that loftiest place where Viṣṇu is, Laid as it were an eye in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्विप्रासो विपन्यवो जागृवांसः समिंधते ।विष्णोर्यत्परमं पदं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ vipanyávaḥ ǀ jāgṛ-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ sám ǀ indhate ǀvíṣṇoḥ ǀ yát ǀ paramám ǀ padám ǁ
verses.english_translation: This, Viṣṇu's station most sublime, the singers, ever vigilant, Lovers of holy song, light up.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise, ever vigilant and diligent in praise, amply glorify that which is the supreme station of Viṣṇu.
verses.griffith_verse: This, Viṣṇu's station most sublime, the singers, ever vigilant, Lovers of holy song, light up.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIII. Vāyu and Others.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: STRONG are the Somas; come thou nigh; these juices have been mixt with milk:Drink, Vāyu, the presented draughts. Both Deities who touch the heaven, Indra and Vāyu we invokeTo drink of this our Soma juice. The singers' for their aid, invoke Indra and Vāyu, swift as mind,The thousand-eyed, the Lords of thought. Mitra and Varuṇa, renowned as Gods of consecrated might,We call to drink the Soma juice. Those who by Law uphold the Law, Lords of the shining light of Law,Mitra I call, and Varuṇa. Let Varuṇa be our chief defence, let Mitra guard us with all aidsBoth make us rich exceedingly. Indra, by Maruts girt, we call to drink the Soma juice: may heSate him in union with his troop. Gods, Marut hosts whom Indra leads, distributers of Pūṣan's gifts,Hearken ye all unto my cry. With conquering Indra for ally, strike Vṛtra down, ye bounteous GodsLet not the wicked master us. We call the Universal Gods, and Maruts to the Soma draught,For passing strong are Pṛśni's Sons. Fierce comes the Maruts’ thundering voice, like that of conquerors, when ye goForward to victory, O Men. Born of the laughing lightning. may the Maruts guard us everywhereMay they be gracious unto Us. Like some lost animal, drive to us, bright Pūṣan, him who bears up heaven,Resting on many-coloured grass. Pūṣan the Bright has found the King, concealed and hidden in a cave,Who rests on grass of many hues. And may he. duly bring to me the six bound closely, through these drops,As one who ploughs with steers brings corn. Along their paths the Mothers go, Sisters of priestly ministrants,Mingling their sweetness with the milk. May Waters gathered near the Sun, and those wherewith the Sun is joined,Speed forth this sacrifice of ours. I call the Waters, Goddesses, wherein our cattle quench their thirst;Oblations to the Streams be given. Amrit is in the Waters in the Waters there is healing balmBe swift, ye Gods, to give them praise. Within the Waters—Soma thus hath told me—dwell all balms that heal,And Agni, he who blesseth all. The Waters hold all medicines. O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm,So that I long may see the Sun. Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought.If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me. The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come:O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me. Fill me with splendour, Agni; give offspring and length of days; the GodsShall know me even as I am, and Indra with the Ṛṣis, know.

verses.sanskrit: तीव्राः सोमास आ गह्याशीर्वंतः सुता इमे ।वायो तान्प्रस्थितान्पिब ॥
verses.transliteration: tīvrā́ḥ ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ āśī́ḥ-vantaḥ ǀ sutā́ḥ ǀ imé ǀvā́yo íti ǀ tā́n ǀ prá-sthitān ǀ piba ǁ
verses.english_translation: STRONG are the Somas; come thou nigh; these juices have been mixt with milk: Drink, Vāyu, the presented draughts.
verses.wilson_translation: These sharp and blessing-bearing Somajuices are poured out; come,Vāyu, and drink of them as presented.
verses.griffith_verse: STRONG are the Somas; come thou nigh; these juices have been mixt with milk: Drink, Vāyu, the presented draughts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेंद्रवायू हवामहे ।अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhā́ ǀ devā́ ǀ divi-spṛ́śā ǀ indravāyū́ íti ǀ havāmahe ǀasyá ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Both Deities who touch the heaven, Indra and Vāyu we invoke To drink of this our Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke both the divinities abiding in heaven,Indraand Vāyu, to drink of this Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: Both Deities who touch the heaven, Indra and Vāyu we invoke To drink of this our Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रवायू मनोजुवा विप्रा हवंत ऊतये ।सहस्राक्षा धियस्पती ॥
verses.transliteration: indravāyū́ íti ǀ manaḥ-júvā ǀ víprāḥ ǀ havante ǀ ūtáye ǀsahasra-akṣā́ ǀ dhiyáḥ ǀ pátī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The singers' for their aid, invoke Indra and Vāyu, swift as mind, The thousand-eyed, the Lords of thought.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise invoke, for their preservation,Indraand Vāyu, who are swift as thought, have a thousand eyes, and are protectors of pious acts.
verses.griffith_verse: The singers' for their aid, invoke Indra and Vāyu, swift as mind, The thousand-eyed, the Lords of thought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मित्रं वयं हवामहे वरुणं सोमपीतये ।जज्ञाना पूतदक्षसा ॥
verses.transliteration: mitrám ǀ vayám ǀ havāmahe ǀ váruṇam ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀjajñānā́ ǀ pūtá-dakṣasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitra and Varuṇa, renowned as Gods of consecrated might, We call to drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke Mitraand Varuṇa, becoming present at the sacrifice, and of pure strength, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: Mitra and Varuṇa, renowned as Gods of consecrated might, We call to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतेन यावृतावृधावृतस्य ज्योतिषस्पती ।ता मित्रावरुणा हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛténa ǀ yáu ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhau ǀ ṛtásya ǀ jyótiṣaḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀtā́ ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ huve ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those who by Law uphold the Law, Lords of the shining light of Law, Mitra I call, and Varuṇa.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke Mitraand Varuṇa, who with true speech, are the encouragers of pious acts, and are lords of true lighṭ
verses.griffith_verse: Those who by Law uphold the Law, Lords of the shining light of Law, Mitra I call, and Varuṇa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वरुणः प्राविता भुवन्मित्रो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः ।करतां नः सुराधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: váruṇaḥ ǀ pra-avitā́ ǀ bhuvat ǀ mitráḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀkáratām ǀ naḥ ǀ su-rā́dhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Varuṇa be our chief defence, let Mitra guard us with all aids Both make us rich exceedingly.
verses.wilson_translation: May Varuṇabe our especial protector; may Mitradefend us with all defences; may they make us most opulent.
verses.griffith_verse: Let Varuṇa be our chief defence, let Mitra guard us with all aids Both make us rich exceedingly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मरुत्वंतं हवामह इंद्रमा सोमपीतये ।सजूर्गणेन तृंपतु ॥
verses.transliteration: marútvantam ǀ havāmahe ǀ índram ǀ ā́ ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀsa-jū́ḥ ǀ gaṇéna ǀ tṛmpatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, by Maruts girt, we call to drink the Soma juice: may he Sate him in union with his troop.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke Indra, attended by the Marutsto drink the Somajuice; may he, with his associates, be satisfied.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, by Maruts girt, we call to drink the Soma juice: may he Sate him in union with his troop.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रज्येष्ठा मरुद्गणा देवासः पूषरातयः ।विश्वे मम श्रुता हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra-jyeṣṭhāḥ ǀ márut-gaṇāḥ ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ pū́ṣa-rātayaḥ ǀvíśve ǀ máma ǀ śruta ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, Marut hosts whom Indra leads, distributers of Pūṣan's gifts, Hearken ye all unto my cry.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Maruts, of whom Indrais the chief and Pūṣanis the donor, or benefactor; in what way, is not specified.
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, Marut hosts whom Indra leads, distributers of Pūṣan's gifts, Hearken ye all unto my cry.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हत वृत्रं सुदानव इंद्रेण सहसा युजा ।मा नो दुःशंस ईशत ॥
verses.transliteration: hatá ǀ vṛtrám ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ sáhasā ǀ yujā́ ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-śáṃsaḥ ǀ īśata ǁ
verses.english_translation: With conquering Indra for ally, strike Vṛtra down, ye bounteous Gods Let not the wicked master us.
verses.wilson_translation: Liberal donors, along with the mighty and associated Indra, destroy Vṛtra; let not the evil one prevail against us.
verses.griffith_verse: With conquering Indra for ally, strike Vṛtra down, ye bounteous Gods Let not the wicked master us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वान्देवान्हवामहे मरुतः सोमपीतये ।उग्रा हि पृश्निमातरः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvān ǀ devā́n ǀ havāmahe ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀugrā́ḥ ǀ hí ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call the Universal Gods, and Maruts to the Soma draught, For passing strong are Pṛśni's Sons.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke all the divine Maruts, who are fierce, and have the (many-   coloured) earth for their mother, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: We call the Universal Gods, and Maruts to the Soma draught, For passing strong are Pṛśni's Sons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जयतामिव तन्यतुर्मरुतामेति धृष्णुया ।यच्छुभं याथना नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: jáyatām-iva ǀ tanyatúḥ ǀ marútām ǀ eti ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀyát ǀ śúbham ǀ yāthána ǀ naraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce comes the Maruts’ thundering voice, like that of conquerors, when ye go Forward to victory, O Men.
verses.wilson_translation: Whenever, leaders (of men), you accept an auspicious (offering), then the shout of the Marutsspreads with exultation, like (that) of conquerors.
verses.griffith_verse: Fierce comes the Maruts’ thundering voice, like that of conquerors, when ye go Forward to victory, O Men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हस्काराद्विद्युतस्पर्यतो जाता अवंतु नः ।मरुतो मृळयंतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: haskārā́t ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ pári ǀ átaḥ ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ avantu ǀ naḥ ǀmarútaḥ ǀ mṛḷayantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Born of the laughing lightning. may the Maruts guard us everywhere May they be gracious unto Us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, born from the brilliant lightning, everywhere preserve us, and make us happy.
verses.griffith_verse: Born of the laughing lightning. may the Maruts guard us everywhere May they be gracious unto Us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ पूषञ्चित्रबर्हिषमाघृणे धरुणं दिवः ।आजा नष्टं यथा पशुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ pūṣan ǀ citrá-barhiṣam ǀ ā́ghṛṇe ǀ dharúṇam ǀ diváḥ ǀā́ ǀ aja ǀ naṣṭám ǀ yáthā ǀ paśúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like some lost animal, drive to us, bright Pūṣan, him who bears up heaven, Resting on many-coloured grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent and (swift) moving Pūṣan, bring from heaven the Somajuice, in combination with the variegated sacred grass, as (a man brings back) an animal that was lost.
verses.griffith_verse: Like some lost animal, drive to us, bright Pūṣan, him who bears up heaven, Resting on many-coloured grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा राजानमाघृणिरपगूळ्हं गुहा हितं ।अविंदच्चित्रबर्हिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ rā́jānam ǀ ā́ghṛṇiḥ ǀ ápa-gūḷham ǀ gúhā ǀ hitám ǀávindat ǀ citrá-barhiṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣan the Bright has found the King, concealed and hidden in a cave, Who rests on grass of many hues.
verses.wilson_translation: The resplendent Pūṣanhas found the royal (Somajuice), although concealed, hidden in a secret plural ce, strewed amongst the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Pūṣan the Bright has found the King, concealed and hidden in a cave, Who rests on grass of many hues.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उतो स मह्यमिंदुभिः षड्युक्ताँ अनुसेषिधत् ।गोभिर्यवं न चर्कृषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utó íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ yuktā́n ǀ anu-sésidhat ǀgóbhiḥ ǀ yávam ǀ ná ǀ carkṛṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: And may he. duly bring to me the six bound closely, through these drops, As one who ploughs with steers brings corn.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily he has brought to me successively the six (seasons), connected with the drops (of the Somajuice) as (a husbandsman) repeatedly plural ughs (the earth) for barley.
verses.griffith_verse: And may he. duly bring to me the six bound closely, through these drops, As one who ploughs with steers brings corn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंबयो यंत्यध्वभिर्जामयो अध्वरीयतां ।पृंचतीर्मधुना पयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ambáyaḥ ǀ yanti ǀ ádhva-bhiḥ ǀ jāmáyaḥ ǀ adhvari-yatā́m ǀpṛñcatī́ḥ ǀ mádhunā ǀ páyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Along their paths the Mothers go, Sisters of priestly ministrants, Mingling their sweetness with the milk.
verses.wilson_translation: Mothers to us, who are desirous of sacrificing, the kindred (waters) flow by the paths (of sacrifice) qualifying the milk (of kine) with sweetnesṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Along their paths the Mothers go, Sisters of priestly ministrants, Mingling their sweetness with the milk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमूर्या उप सूर्ये याभिर्वा सूर्यः सह ।ता नो हिन्वंत्वध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: amū́ḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sū́rye ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ sahá ǀtā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ hinvantu ǀ adhvarám ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Waters gathered near the Sun, and those wherewith the Sun is joined, Speed forth this sacrifice of ours.
verses.wilson_translation: May those waters which are contiguous to the Sun, and those with which the Sun is associated, be propitious to our rite.
verses.griffith_verse: May Waters gathered near the Sun, and those wherewith the Sun is joined, Speed forth this sacrifice of ours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपो देवीरुप ह्वये यत्र गावः पिबंति नः ।सिंधुभ्यः कर्त्वं हविः ॥
verses.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ hvaye ǀ yátra ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ píbanti ǀ naḥ ǀsíndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ kártvam ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I call the Waters, Goddesses, wherein our cattle quench their thirst; Oblations to the Streams be given.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoke the divine waters in which our cattle drink; offer oblations to the following (streams).
verses.griffith_verse: I call the Waters, Goddesses, wherein our cattle quench their thirst; Oblations to the Streams be given.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्स्वंतरमृतमप्सु भेषजमपामुत प्रशस्तये ।देवा भवत वाजिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ antáḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ap-sú ǀ bheṣajám ǀ apā́m ǀ utá ǀ prá-śastaye ǀdévāḥ ǀ bhávata ǀ vājínaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Amrit is in the Waters in the Waters there is healing balm Be swift, ye Gods, to give them praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Ambrosia is in the waters; in the waters are medicinal herbs; therefore, divine (priest), be prompt in their praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Amrit is in the Waters in the Waters there is healing balm Be swift, ye Gods, to give them praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीदंतर्विश्वानि भेषजा ।अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवमापश्च विश्वभेषजीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ me ǀ sómaḥ ǀ abravīt ǀ antáḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀagním ǀ ca ǀ viśvá-śambhuvam ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ca ǀ viśvá-bheṣajīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Within the Waters—Soma thus hath told me—dwell all balms that heal, And Agni, he who blesseth all. The Waters hold all medicines.
verses.wilson_translation: Somahas declared to me, 'all medicaments, as well as Agni, the benefactor of the universe, are in the waters'; the waters, contain all healing herbs.
verses.griffith_verse: Within the Waters—Soma thus hath told me—dwell all balms that heal, And Agni, he who blesseth all. The Waters hold all medicines.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपः पृणीत भेषजं वरूथं तन्वे मम ।ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ pṛṇītá ǀ bheṣajám ǀ várūtham ǀ tanvé ǀ máma ǀjyók ǀ ca ǀ sū́ryam ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm, So that I long may see the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, bring to perfection all disease-dispelling medicaments for (the good of) my body, that I may long behold the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm, So that I long may see the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदमापः प्र वहत यत्किं च दुरितं मयि ।यद्वाहमभिदुद्रोह यद्वा शेप उतानृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ āpaḥ ǀ prá ǀ vahata ǀ yát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ duḥ-itám ǀ máyi ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ ahám ǀ abhi-dudróha ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ śepé ǀ utá ǀ ánṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought. If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, take away whatever sin has been (found) in me whether I have (knowingly) done wrong, or have pronounced imprecations (against holy men) or (have spoken) untruth.
verses.griffith_verse: Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought. If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं रसेन समगस्महि ।पयस्वानग्न आ गहि तं मा सं सृज वर्चसा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ adyá ǀ ánu ǀ acāriṣam ǀ rásena ǀ sám ǀ agasmahi ǀpáyasvān ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ tám ǀ mā ǀ sám ǀ sṛja ǀ várcasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come: O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.
verses.wilson_translation: I have this day entered into the waters; we have mingled with their essence;Agni, abiding in the waters, approach, and fill me, thus (bathed), with vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come: O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं माग्ने वर्चसा सृज सं प्रजया समायुषा ।विद्युर्मे अस्य देवा इंद्रो विद्यात्सह ऋषिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ mā ǀ agne ǀ várcasā ǀ sṛja ǀ sám ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ sám ǀ ā́yuṣā ǀvidyúḥ ǀ me ǀ asya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vidyāt ǀ sahá ǀ ṛ́ṣi-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fill me with splendour, Agni; give offspring and length of days; the Gods Shall know me even as I am, and Indra with the Ṛṣis, know.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, confer upon me vigour, progeny and life, so that the gods may know the (sacrifice) of this my (employer), and Indrawith the Ṛṣis, may know it.
verses.griffith_verse: Fill me with splendour, Agni; give offspring and length of days; the Gods Shall know me even as I am, and Indra with the Ṛṣis, know.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIV. Varuṇa and Others.
hymns.anukramani: १५ आजीगर्तिः शुनः शेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः।१ कः (प्रजापतिः), २ अग्निः, ३-५ सविता, ५ भगो  वा, ६-१५ वरुणः।१, २, ६-१५ त्रिष्टुप्, ३-५ गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WHO now is he, what God among Immortals, of whose auspicious name we may bethink us?Who shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother? Agni the God the first among the Immortals,—of his auspicious name let us bethink us.He shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother. To thee, O Savitar, the Lord of precious things, who helpest usContinually, for our share we come— Wealth, highly lauded ere reproach hath fallen on it, which is laid,Free from all hatred, in thy hands Through thy protection may we come to even the height of affluenceWhich Bhaga hath dealt out to us. Ne’er have those birds that fly through air attained to thy high dominion or thy might or spirit;Nor these the waters that flow on for ever, nor hills, abaters of the wind's wild fury. Varuṇa, King, of hallowed might, sustaineth erect the Tree's stem in the baseless region.Its rays, whose root is high above, stream downward. Deep may they sink within us, and be hidden. King Varuṇa hath made a spacious pathway, a pathway for the Sun wherein to travel.Where no way was he made him set his footstep, and warned afar whate’er afflicts the spirit. A hundred balms are thine, O King, a thousand; deep and wide-reaching also be thy favours.Far from us, far away drive thou Destruction. Put from us e’en the sin we have committed. Whither by day depart the constellations that shine at night, set high in heaven above us?Varuṇa's holy laws remain unweakened, and through the night the Moon moves on in splendor I ask this of thee with my prayer adoring; thy worshipper craves this with his oblation.Varuṇa, stay thou here and be not angry; steal not our life from us, O thou Wide-Ruler. Nightly and daily this one thing they tell me, this too the thought of mine own heart repeateth.May he to whom prayed fettered Śunaḥśepa, may he the Sovran Varuṇa release us. Bound to three pillars captured Śunaḥśepa thus to the Āditya made his supplication.Him may the Sovran Varuṇa deliver, wise, ne’er deceived, loosen the bonds that bind him. With bending down, oblations, sacrifices, O Varuṇa, we deprecate thine anger:Wise Asura, thou King of wide dominion, loosen the bonds of sins by us committed. Loosen the bonds, O Varuṇa, that hold me, loosen the bonds above, between, and under.So in thy holy law may we made sinless belong to Aditi, O thou Āditya.

verses.sanskrit: कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानां मनामहे चारु देवस्य नाम ।को नो मह्या अदितये पुनर्दात्पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च ॥
verses.transliteration: kásya ǀ nūnám ǀ katamásya ǀ amṛ́tānām ǀ mánāmahe ǀ cā́ru ǀ devásya ǀ nā́ma ǀkáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahyái ǀ áditaye ǀ púnaḥ ǀ dāt ǀ pitáram ǀ ca ǀ dṛśéyam ǀ mātáram ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHO now is he, what God among Immortals, of whose auspicious name we may bethink us? Who shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother?
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom, or of which divinity of the immortals, shall we invoke the auspicious name? who will give us to the great Aditithat I may again behold my father and my mother.
verses.griffith_verse: WHO now is he, what God among Immortals, of whose auspicious name we may bethink us? Who shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानां मनामहे चारु देवस्य नाम ।स नो मह्या अदितये पुनर्दात्पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च ॥
verses.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ vayám ǀ prathamásya ǀ amṛ́tānām ǀ mánāmahe ǀ cā́ru ǀ devásya ǀ nā́ma ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahyái ǀ áditaye ǀ púnaḥ ǀ dāt ǀ pitáram ǀ ca ǀ dṛśéyam ǀ mātáram ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni the God the first among the Immortals,—of his auspicious name let us bethink us. He shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us invoke the auspicious name of Agni, the first divinity of the immortals, that he may give us to the great Aditi, and that I may behold agin my father and my mother.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni the God the first among the Immortals,—of his auspicious name let us bethink us. He shall to mighty Aditi restore us, that I may see my Father and my Mother.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्वा देव सवितरीशानं वार्याणां ।सदावन्भागमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ deva ǀ savitaḥ ǀ ī́śānam ǀ vā́ryāṇām ǀsádā ǀ avan ǀ bhāgám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: To thee, O Savitar, the Lord of precious things, who helpest us Continually, for our share we come—
verses.wilson_translation: Ever-protecting Savitā, we solicit (our) portion of you, who are the lord of affluence.
verses.griffith_verse: To thee, O Savitar, the Lord of precious things, who helpest us Continually, for our share we come—
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यश्चिद्धि त इत्था भगः शशमानः पुरा निदः ।अद्वेषो हस्तयोर्दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ itthā́ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ śaśamānáḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ nidáḥ ǀadveṣáḥ ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ dadhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wealth, highly lauded ere reproach hath fallen on it, which is laid, Free from all hatred, in thy hands
verses.wilson_translation: That wealth which has been retained in yourhands, and is entitled to commendation, as exempt from envy or reproach.
verses.griffith_verse: Wealth, highly lauded ere reproach hath fallen on it, which is laid, Free from all hatred, in thy hands
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भगभक्तस्य ते वयमुदशेम तवावसा ।मूर्धानं राय आरभे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhága-bhaktasya ǀ te ǀ vayám ǀ út ǀ aśema ǀ táva ǀ ávasā ǀmūrdhā́nam ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā-rábhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through thy protection may we come to even the height of affluence Which Bhaga hath dealt out to us.
verses.wilson_translation: We are assiduous in attaining the summit of affluence, through the protection of you, who are the possessor of wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Through thy protection may we come to even the height of affluence Which Bhaga hath dealt out to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि ते क्षत्रं न सहो न मन्युं वयश्चनामी पतयंत आपुः ।नेमा आपो अनिमिषं चरंतीर्न ये वातस्य प्रमिनंत्यभ्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ te ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ná ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ manyúm ǀ váyaḥ ǀ caná ǀ amī́ íti ǀ patáyantaḥ ǀ āpúḥ ǀná ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ani-miṣám ǀ cárantīḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ vā́tasya ǀ pra-minánti ǀ ábhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ne’er have those birds that fly through air attained to thy high dominion or thy might or spirit; Nor these the waters that flow on for ever, nor hills, abaters of the wind's wild fury.
verses.wilson_translation: These birds, that are flying (through the air), have not obtained,Varuṇa, your bodily strength or your prowess, or (are able to endure your) wrath; neither do these waters that flow increasingly, nor (do the gales) of wind, surpass your speed.
verses.griffith_verse: Ne’er have those birds that fly through air attained to thy high dominion or thy might or spirit; Nor these the waters that flow on for ever, nor hills, abaters of the wind's wild fury.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अबुध्ने राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः ।नीचीनाः स्थुरुपरि बुध्न एषामस्मे अंतर्निहिताः केतवः स्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: abudhné ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ vánasya ǀ ūrdhvám ǀ stū́pam ǀ dadate ǀ pūtá-dakṣaḥ ǀnīcī́nāḥ ǀ sthuḥ ǀ upári ǀ budhnáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ asmé íti ǀ antáḥ ǀ ní-hitāḥ ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ syuríti syuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa, King, of hallowed might, sustaineth erect the Tree's stem in the baseless region. Its rays, whose root is high above, stream downward. Deep may they sink within us, and be hidden.
verses.wilson_translation: The regal Varuṇa, of pure vigour (abiding) in the baseless (firmament), sustains on high a heap of light, the rays (of which) are pointed downwards, while their base is above; may they become concentrated in us as the sources of existence.
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa, King, of hallowed might, sustaineth erect the Tree's stem in the baseless region. Its rays, whose root is high above, stream downward. Deep may they sink within us, and be hidden.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उरुं हि राजा वरुणश्चकार सूर्याय पंथामन्वेतवा उ ।अपदे पादा प्रतिधातवेऽकरुतापवक्ता हृदयाविधश्चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: urúm ǀ hí ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ cakā́ra ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ pánthām ǀ ánu-etavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀapáde ǀ pā́dā ǀ práti-dhātave ǀ akaḥ ǀ utá ǀ apa-vaktā́ ǀ hṛdaya-vídhaḥ ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: King Varuṇa hath made a spacious pathway, a pathway for the Sun wherein to travel. Where no way was he made him set his footstep, and warned afar whate’er afflicts the spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: The regal Varuṇaverily made with the path of the sun, (by which) to travel on his daily course; a path to traverse in pathless (space); may he be the repeller of every afflicter of the heart.
verses.griffith_verse: King Varuṇa hath made a spacious pathway, a pathway for the Sun wherein to travel. Where no way was he made him set his footstep, and warned afar whate’er afflicts the spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं ते राजन्भिषजः सहस्रमुर्वी गभीरा सुमतिष्टे अस्तु ।बाधस्व दूरे निर्ऋतिं पराचैः कृतं चिदेनः प्र मुमुग्ध्यस्मत् ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ te ǀ rājan ǀ bhiṣájaḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ urvī́ ǀ gabhīrā́ ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ te ǀ astu ǀbā́dhasva ǀ dūré ǀ níḥ-ṛtim ǀ parācáiḥ ǀ kṛtám ǀ cit ǀ énaḥ ǀ prá ǀ mumugdhi ǀ asmát ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred balms are thine, O King, a thousand; deep and wide-reaching also be thy favours. Far from us, far away drive thou Destruction. Put from us e’en the sin we have committed.
verses.wilson_translation: Yours, O king, are a hundred and a thousand medicaments; may your favour, comprehensive and profound, be (with us); keep afar from us Nirṛti, with unfriendly looks, and liberate us from whatever sin we may have committed.
verses.griffith_verse: A hundred balms are thine, O King, a thousand; deep and wide-reaching also be thy favours. Far from us, far away drive thou Destruction. Put from us e’en the sin we have committed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमी य ऋक्षा निहितास उच्चा नक्तं ददृश्रे कुह चिद्दिवेयुः ।अदब्धानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि विचाकशच्चंद्रमा नक्तमेति ॥
verses.transliteration: amī́ íti ǀ yé ǀ ṛ́kṣāḥ ǀ ní-hitāsaḥ ǀ uccā́ ǀ náktam ǀ dádṛśre ǀ kúha ǀ cit ǀ dívā ǀ īyuḥ ǀádabdhāni ǀ váruṇasya ǀ vratā́ni ǀ vi-cā́kaśat ǀ candrámāḥ ǀ náktam ǀ eti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whither by day depart the constellations that shine at night, set high in heaven above us? Varuṇa's holy laws remain unweakened, and through the night the Moon moves on in splendor
verses.wilson_translation: These constellations plural ced on high, which are visible by night, and go elsewhere by day, are the undisturbed holy acts of Varuṇa(and by his command) the moon moves resplendent by night.
verses.griffith_verse: Whither by day depart the constellations that shine at night, set high in heaven above us? Varuṇa's holy laws remain unweakened, and through the night the Moon moves on in splendor
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तत्त्वा यामि ब्रह्मणा वंदमानस्तदा शास्ते यजमानो हविर्भिः ।अहेळमानो वरुणेह बोध्युरुशंस मा न आयुः प्र मोषीः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ tvā ǀ yāmi ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ vándamānaḥ ǀ tát ǀ ā́ ǀ śāste ǀ yájamānaḥ ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀáheḷamānaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ ihá ǀ bodhi ǀ úru-śaṃsa ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ prá ǀ moṣīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I ask this of thee with my prayer adoring; thy worshipper craves this with his oblation. Varuṇa, stay thou here and be not angry; steal not our life from us, O thou Wide-Ruler.
verses.wilson_translation: Praising you with (devout) prayer, I implore you for that (life) which the instrumental tutor of the sacrifice solicits with oblations;Varuṇa, undisdainful, bestow a thought upon us; much-lauded, take not away our existence.
verses.griffith_verse: I ask this of thee with my prayer adoring; thy worshipper craves this with his oblation. Varuṇa, stay thou here and be not angry; steal not our life from us, O thou Wide-Ruler.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिन्नक्तं तद्दिवा मह्यमाहुस्तदयं केतो हृद आ वि चष्टे ।शुनःशेपो यमह्वद्गृभीतः सो अस्मान्राजा वरुणो मुमोक्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ náktam ǀ tát ǀ dívā ǀ máhyam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ tát ǀ ayám ǀ kétaḥ ǀ hṛdáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀśúnaḥśépaḥ ǀ yám ǀ áhvat ǀ gṛbhītáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mumoktu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nightly and daily this one thing they tell me, this too the thought of mine own heart repeateth. May he to whom prayed fettered Śunaḥśepa, may he the Sovran Varuṇa release us.
verses.wilson_translation: This (your praise) they repeat to me by night and by day; this knowledge speaks to my heart; may he whom the fettered Śunahśepas has invoked, may the regal Varuṇaset us free.
verses.griffith_verse: Nightly and daily this one thing they tell me, this too the thought of mine own heart repeateth. May he to whom prayed fettered Śunaḥśepa, may he the Sovran Varuṇa release us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनःशेपो ह्यह्वद्गृभीतस्त्रिष्वादित्यं द्रुपदेषु बद्धः ।अवैनं राजा वरुणः ससृज्याद्विद्वाँ अदब्धो वि मुमोक्तु पाशान् ॥
verses.transliteration: śúnaḥśépaḥ ǀ hí ǀ áhvat ǀ gṛbhītáḥ ǀ triṣú ǀ ādityám ǀ dru-padéṣu ǀ baddháḥ ǀáva ǀ enam ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sasṛjyāt ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ádabdhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ mumoktu ǀ pā́śān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bound to three pillars captured Śunaḥśepa thus to the Āditya made his supplication. Him may the Sovran Varuṇa deliver, wise, ne’er deceived, loosen the bonds that bind him.
verses.wilson_translation: Śunahśepas, seized and bound to the three-footed tree, has invoked the son of Aditi; may the regal Varuṇa, wise and irresistible, liberate him; may he let loose his bonds.
verses.griffith_verse: Bound to three pillars captured Śunaḥśepa thus to the Āditya made his supplication. Him may the Sovran Varuṇa deliver, wise, ne’er deceived, loosen the bonds that bind him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव ते हेळो वरुण नमोभिरव यज्ञेभिरीमहे हविर्भिः ।क्षयन्नस्मभ्यमसुर प्रचेता राजन्नेनांसि शिश्रथः कृतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ te ǀ héḷaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ áva ǀ yajñébhiḥ ǀ īmahe ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀkṣáyan ǀ asmábhyam ǀ asura ǀ praceta íti pra-cetaḥ ǀ rā́jan ǀ énāṃsi ǀ śiśrathaḥ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: With bending down, oblations, sacrifices, O Varuṇa, we deprecate thine anger: Wise Asura, thou King of wide dominion, loosen the bonds of sins by us committed.
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇa, we deprecate your wrath with prostrations, with sacrifices, with oblations; averter of misfortune, wise and illustrious, be present amongst us, and mitigate the evils we have committed.
verses.griffith_verse: With bending down, oblations, sacrifices, O Varuṇa, we deprecate thine anger: Wise Asura, thou King of wide dominion, loosen the bonds of sins by us committed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदुत्तमं वरुण पाशमस्मदवाधमं वि मध्यमं श्रथाय ।अथा वयमादित्य व्रते तवानागसो अदितये स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ut-tamám ǀ varuṇa ǀ pā́śam ǀ asmát ǀ áva ǀ adhamám ǀ ví ǀ madhyamám ǀ śrathaya ǀátha ǀ vayám ǀ āditya ǀ vraté ǀ táva ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀ áditaye ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Loosen the bonds, O Varuṇa, that hold me, loosen the bonds above, between, and under. So in thy holy law may we made sinless belong to Aditi, O thou Āditya.
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇa, loosen for me the upper, the middle, the lower band; so, son of Aditi, shall we, through faultlessness in the worship, become freed from siṇ
verses.griffith_verse: Loosen the bonds, O Varuṇa, that hold me, loosen the bonds above, between, and under. So in thy holy law may we made sinless belong to Aditi, O thou Āditya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXV. Varuṇa.
hymns.anukramani: २१ आजीगर्तिः शुनः शेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः। वरुणः। गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WHATEVER law of thine, O God, O Varuṇa, as we are men,Day after day we violate. give us not as a prey to death, to be destroyed by thee in wrath,To thy fierce anger when displeased. To gain thy mercy, Varuṇa, with hymns we bind thy heart, as bindsThe charioteer his tethered horse. They flee from me dispirited, bent only on obtaining wealth,As to their nests the birds of air. When shall we bring, to be appeased, the Hero, Lord of warrior might,Him, the far-seeing Varuṇa? This, this with joy they both accept in common: never do they failThe ever-faithful worshipper. He knows the path of birds that fly through heaven, and, Sovran of the sea,He knows the ships that are thereon. True to his holy law, he knows the twelve moons with their progeny:He knows the moon of later birth. He knows the pathway of the wind, the spreading, high, and mighty wind:He knows the Gods who dwell above. Varuṇa, true to holy law, sits down among his people; he,Most wise, sits there to govern all. From thenceperceivinghe beholds all wondrous things, both what hath been,And what hereafter will be done. May that Āditya, very wise, make fair paths for us all our days:May he prolong our lives for us. Varuṇa, wearing golden mail, hath clad him in a shining robe.His spies are seated found about. The God whom enemies threaten not, nor those who tyrannize o’er men,Nor those whose minds are bent on wrong. He who gives glory to mankind, not glory that is incomplete,To our own bodies giving it. Yearning for the wide-seeing One, my thoughts move onward unto him,As kine unto their pastures move. Once more together let us speak, because my meath is brought: priest-likeThou eatest what is dear to thee. Now saw I him whom all may see, I saw his car above the earth:He hath accepted these my songs. Varuṇa, hear this call of mine: be gracious unto us this dayLonging for help I cried to thee. Thou, O wise God, art Lord of all, thou art the King of earth and heavenHear, as thou goest on thy way. Release us from the upper bond, untie the bond between, and looseThe bonds below, that I may live.

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि ते विशो यथा प्र देव वरुण व्रतं ।मिनीमसि द्यविद्यवि ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ víśaḥ ǀ yathā ǀ prá ǀ deva ǀ varuṇa ǀ vratám ǀminīmási ǀ dyávi-dyavi ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHATEVER law of thine, O God, O Varuṇa, as we are men, Day after day we violate.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as all people commit errors, so do we, divine Varuṇa, daily disfigure your worship by imperfections.
verses.griffith_verse: WHATEVER law of thine, O God, O Varuṇa, as we are men, Day after day we violate.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो वधाय हत्नवे जिहीळानस्य रीरधः ।मा हृणानस्य मन्यवे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vadh��́ya ǀ hatnáve ǀ jihīḷānásya ǀ rīradhaḥ ǀmā́ ǀ hṛṇānásya ǀ manyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: give us not as a prey to death, to be destroyed by thee in wrath, To thy fierce anger when displeased.
verses.wilson_translation: Make us not the objects of death, through your fatal indignation, through the wrath of you so displeasured.
verses.griffith_verse: give us not as a prey to death, to be destroyed by thee in wrath, To thy fierce anger when displeased.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि मृळीकाय ते मनो रथीरश्वं न संदितं ।गीर्भिर्वरुण सीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ mṛḷīkā́ya ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ rathī́ḥ ǀ áśvam ǀ ná ǀ sám-ditam ǀgīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ sīmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: To gain thy mercy, Varuṇa, with hymns we bind thy heart, as binds The charioteer his tethered horse.
verses.wilson_translation: We soothe your mind,Varuṇa, by our praises, for our good, as a charioteer his weary steed.
verses.griffith_verse: To gain thy mercy, Varuṇa, with hymns we bind thy heart, as binds The charioteer his tethered horse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा हि मे विमन्यवः पतंति वस्यइष्टये ।वयो न वसतीरुप ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ hí ǀ me ǀ ví-manyavaḥ ǀ pátanti ǀ vásyaḥ-iṣṭaye ǀváyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vasatī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǁ
verses.english_translation: They flee from me dispirited, bent only on obtaining wealth, As to their nests the birds of air.
verses.wilson_translation: My tranquil (meditations) revert to the desire of life, as birds hover around their nests. =vasyaiṣṭaye =vasumataḥ, precious (i.e. jīvasya, life's).
verses.griffith_verse: They flee from me dispirited, bent only on obtaining wealth, As to their nests the birds of air.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कदा क्षत्रश्रियं नरमा वरुणं करामहे ।मृळीकायोरुचक्षसं ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ kṣatra-śríyam ǀ náram ǀ ā́ ǀ váruṇam ǀ karāmahe ǀmṛḷīkā́ya ǀ uru-cákṣasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When shall we bring, to be appeased, the Hero, Lord of warrior might, Him, the far-seeing Varuṇa?
verses.wilson_translation: When for our happiness, shall we bring hither Varuṇa, eminent in strength, the guide (of men), the regarder of many?
verses.griffith_verse: When shall we bring, to be appeased, the Hero, Lord of warrior might, Him, the far-seeing Varuṇa?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदित्समानमाशाते वेनंता न प्र युच्छतः ।धृतव्रताय दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ samānám ǀ āśāte íti ǀ vénantā ǀ ná ǀ prá ǀ yucchataḥ ǀdhṛtá-vratāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: This, this with joy they both accept in common: never do they fail The ever-faithful worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Partake, (Mitraand Varuṇa), of the common (oblation), being propitious to the giver and celebrator of this pious rite.
verses.griffith_verse: This, this with joy they both accept in common: never do they fail The ever-faithful worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वेदा यो वीनां पदमंतरिक्षेण पततां ।वेद नावः समुद्रियः ॥
verses.transliteration: véda ǀ yáḥ ǀ vīnā́m ǀ padám ǀ antárikṣeṇa ǀ pátatām ǀvéda ǀ nāváḥ ǀ samudríyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He knows the path of birds that fly through heaven, and, Sovran of the sea, He knows the ships that are thereon.
verses.wilson_translation: He, who knows the path of the birds flying through the air; he, abiding in the ocean, knows (also) the course of ships.
verses.griffith_verse: He knows the path of birds that fly through heaven, and, Sovran of the sea, He knows the ships that are thereon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः ।वेदा य उपजायते ॥
verses.transliteration: véda ǀ māsáḥ ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ dvā́daśa ǀ prajā́-vataḥ ǀvéda ǀ yáḥ ǀ upa-jā́yate ǁ
verses.english_translation: True to his holy law, he knows the twelve moons with their progeny: He knows the moon of later birth.
verses.wilson_translation: He, who accepting the rites (dedicated to him) knows the twelve months and their productions and that which is supplementarily engendered.
verses.griffith_verse: True to his holy law, he knows the twelve moons with their progeny: He knows the moon of later birth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वेद वातस्य वर्तनिमुरोर्ऋष्वस्य बृहतः ।वेदा ये अध्यासते ॥
verses.transliteration: véda ǀ vā́tasya ǀ vartaním ǀ uróḥ ǀ ṛṣvásya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀvéda ǀ yé ǀ adhi-ā́sate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He knows the pathway of the wind, the spreading, high, and mighty wind: He knows the Gods who dwell above.
verses.wilson_translation: He, who knows the path of the vast, the graceful, and the excellent wind, and who knows those who reside above.
verses.griffith_verse: He knows the pathway of the wind, the spreading, high, and mighty wind: He knows the Gods who dwell above.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्यास्वा ।साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ sasāda ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ pastyā́su ǀ ā́ ǀsā́m-rājyāya ǀ su-krátuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa, true to holy law, sits down among his people; he, Most wise, sits there to govern all.
verses.wilson_translation: He,Varuṇa, the acceptor of holy rites, the doer of good deeds, has sat down amongs the (divine) progeny, to exercise supreme dominion (over them).
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa, true to holy law, sits down among his people; he, Most wise, sits there to govern all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतो विश्वान्यद्भुता चिकित्वाँ अभि पश्यति ।कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: átaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ ádbhutā ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ abhí ǀ paśyati ǀkṛtā́ni ǀ yā́ ǀ ca ǀ kártvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: From thence perceiving he beholds all wondrous things, both what hath been, And what hereafter will be done.
verses.wilson_translation: Through him, the sage beholds all the marvels that hav ebeen or will be wrought.
verses.griffith_verse: From thence perceiving he beholds all wondrous things, both what hath been, And what hereafter will be done.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नो विश्वाहा सुक्रतुरादित्यः सुपथा करत् ।प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ ādityáḥ ǀ su-páthā ǀ karat ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ tāriṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that Āditya, very wise, make fair paths for us all our days: May he prolong our lives for us.
verses.wilson_translation: May that very wise son of Aditi, keep us all our days in the right path, and prolong our lives.
verses.griffith_verse: May that Āditya, very wise, make fair paths for us all our days: May he prolong our lives for us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बिभ्रद्द्रापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त निर्णिजं ।परि स्पशो नि षेदिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: bíbhrat ǀ drāpím ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ vasta ǀ niḥ-níjam ǀpári ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ ní ǀ sedire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa, wearing golden mail, hath clad him in a shining robe. His spies are seated found about.
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇaclothes his well-nourished (person n), wearing golden armour, whence the (reflected)  rays are spread around.
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa, wearing golden mail, hath clad him in a shining robe. His spies are seated found about.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यं दिप्संति दिप्सवो न द्रुह्वाणो जनानां ।न देवमभिमातयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yám ǀ dípsanti ǀ dipsávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ drúhvāṇaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀná ǀ devám ǀ abhí-mātayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The God whom enemies threaten not, nor those who tyrannize o’er men, Nor those whose minds are bent on wrong.
verses.wilson_translation: A divine (being), whom enemies dare not to offend; nor the oppressors of mankind, nor the iniquitous, (venture to displease).
verses.griffith_verse: The God whom enemies threaten not, nor those who tyrannize o’er men, Nor those whose minds are bent on wrong.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत यो मानुषेष्वा यशश्चक्रे असाम्या ।अस्माकमुदरेष्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ yáḥ ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ yáśaḥ ǀ cakré ǀ ásāmi ǀ ā́ ǀasmā́kam ǀ udáreṣu ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who gives glory to mankind, not glory that is incomplete, To our own bodies giving it.
verses.wilson_translation: Who has distributed unlimited food to mankind, and especially to us.
verses.griffith_verse: He who gives glory to mankind, not glory that is incomplete, To our own bodies giving it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा मे यंति धीतयो गावो न गव्यूतीरनु ।इच्छंतीरुरुचक्षसं ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ me ǀ yanti ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ gávyūtīḥ ǀ ánu ǀicchántīḥ ǀ uru-cákṣasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yearning for the wide-seeing One, my thoughts move onward unto him, As kine unto their pastures move.
verses.wilson_translation: My thoughts ever turn back to him who is beheld of many, as the kine return to the pastures.
verses.griffith_verse: Yearning for the wide-seeing One, my thoughts move onward unto him, As kine unto their pastures move.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं नु वोचावहै पुनर्यतो मे मध्वाभृतं ।होतेव क्षदसे प्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ nú ǀ vocāvahai ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ me ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́-bhṛtam ǀhótā-iva ǀ kṣádase ǀ priyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Once more together let us speak, because my meath is brought: priest-like Thou eatest what is dear to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us together proclaim that my offering has been prepared, and that you, as if the offerer, accept the valued (oblation).
verses.griffith_verse: Once more together let us speak, because my meath is brought: priest-like Thou eatest what is dear to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दर्शं नु विश्वदर्शतं दर्शं रथमधि क्षमि ।एता जुषत मे गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: dárśam ǀ nú ǀ viśvá-darśatam ǀ dárśam ǀ rátham ǀ ádhi ǀ kṣámi ǀetā́ḥ ǀ juṣata ǀ me ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now saw I him whom all may see, I saw his car above the earth: He hath accepted these my songs.
verses.wilson_translation: I have seen him whose appearance is grateful to all; I have beheld his chariot upon earth; he has accepted these my praiseṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Now saw I him whom all may see, I saw his car above the earth: He hath accepted these my songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं मे वरुण श्रुधी हवमद्या च मृळय ।त्वामवस्युरा चके ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ me ǀ varuṇa ǀ śrudhi ǀ hávam ǀ adyá ǀ ca ǀ mṛḷaya ǀtvā́m ǀ avasyúḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cake ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa, hear this call of mine: be gracious unto us this day Longing for help I cried to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear,Varuṇa, this my invocation; make us this day happy; I have appealed to you, hoping for protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa, hear this call of mine: be gracious unto us this day Longing for help I cried to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं विश्वस्य मेधिर दिवश्च ग्मश्च राजसि ।स यामनि प्रति श्रुधि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ víśvasya ǀ medhira ǀ diváḥ ǀ ca ǀ gmáḥ ǀ ca ǀ rājasi ǀsáḥ ǀ yā́mani ǀ práti ǀ śrudhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, O wise God, art Lord of all, thou art the King of earth and heaven Hear, as thou goest on thy way.
verses.wilson_translation: You, who are possessed of wisdom, shine over heaven and earth, and all the world; do you hear and reply (to my prayers), with (promise of) prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, O wise God, art Lord of all, thou art the King of earth and heaven Hear, as thou goest on thy way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदुत्तमं मुमुग्धि नो वि पाशं मध्यमं चृत ।अवाधमानि जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ut-tamám ǀ mumugdhi ǀ naḥ ǀ ví ǀ pā́śam ǀ madhyamám ǀ cṛta ǀáva ǀ adhamā́ni ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Release us from the upper bond, untie the bond between, and loose The bonds below, that I may live.
verses.wilson_translation: Loose us from the upper bonds, untie the centre and the lower, that we may live.
verses.griffith_verse: Release us from the upper bond, untie the bond between, and loose The bonds below, that I may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVI. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १० आजीगर्तिः शुनःशेप स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः। अग्निः,। गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: O WORTHY of oblation, Lord of prospering powers, assume thy robes,And offer this our sacrifice. Sit ever to be chosen, as our Priest, most youthful, through our hymns,O Agni, through our heavenly word. For here a Father for his son, Kinsman for kinsman worshippeth,And Friend, choice-worthy, for his friend. Here let the foe-destroyers sit, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,Like men, upon our sacred grass. O ancient Herald, be thou glad in this our rite and fellowship:Hearken thou well to these our songs. Whate’er in this perpetual course we sacrifice to God and God,That gift is offered up in thee May he be our dear household Lord, Priest, pleasant and, choice-worthy mayWe, with bright fires, be dear to him. The Gods, adored with brilliant fires. have granted precious wealth to usSo, with bright fires, we pray to thee. And, O Immortal One, so may the eulogies of mortal menBelong to us and thee alike. With all thy fires, O Agni, find pleasure in this our sacrifice,And this our speech, O Son of Strength.

verses.sanskrit: वसिष्वा हि मियेध्य वस्त्राण्यूर्जां पते ।सेमं नो अध्वरं यज ॥
verses.transliteration: vásiṣva ǀ hí ǀ miyedhya ǀ vástrāṇi ǀ ūrjām ǀ pate ǀsáḥ ǀ imám ǀ naḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ yaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: O WORTHY of oblation, Lord of prospering powers, assume thy robes, And offer this our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of sustenance, assume your vestments (of light) and offer this our sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: O WORTHY of oblation, Lord of prospering powers, assume thy robes, And offer this our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि नो होता वरेण्यः सदा यविष्ठ मन्मभिः ।अग्ने दिवित्मता वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ naḥ ǀ hótā ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀ sádā ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀágne ǀ divítmatā ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sit ever to be chosen, as our Priest, most youthful, through our hymns, O Agni, through our heavenly word.
verses.wilson_translation: (Propitiated) by brilliant strains, do your, ever-youthful Agni, selected by us, become our ministrant priest, (invested) with radiance.
verses.griffith_verse: Sit ever to be chosen, as our Priest, most youthful, through our hymns, O Agni, through our heavenly word.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ हि ष्मा सूनवे पितापिर्यजत्यापये ।सखा सख्ये वरेण्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ sūnáve ǀ pitā́ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ yájati ǀ āpáye ǀsákhā ǀ sákhye ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For here a Father for his son, Kinsman for kinsman worshippeth, And Friend, choice-worthy, for his friend.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are verily as a loving father to a son, as a kinsman to a kinsman, as a friend to a friend.
verses.griffith_verse: For here a Father for his son, Kinsman for kinsman worshippeth, And Friend, choice-worthy, for his friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो बर्ही रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।सीदंतु मनुषो यथा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀsī́dantu ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ yathā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here let the foe-destroyers sit, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Like men, upon our sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Let Varuṇa,MitraandĀryaman, sit down upon our sacred grass, as they did at the sacrifice of Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: Here let the foe-destroyers sit, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Like men, upon our sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्व्य होतरस्य नो मंदस्व सख्यस्य च ।इमा उ षु श्रुधी गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́rvya ǀ hotaḥ ǀ asyá ǀ naḥ ǀ mándasva ǀ sakhyásya ǀ ca ǀimā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ śrudhi ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O ancient Herald, be thou glad in this our rite and fellowship: Hearken thou well to these our songs.
verses.wilson_translation: Preceding sacrificer, be plural ased with this our sacrifice and with our friendship, and listen to these your praises.
verses.griffith_verse: O ancient Herald, be thou glad in this our rite and fellowship: Hearken thou well to these our songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि शश्वता तना देवंदेवं यजामहे ।त्वे इद्धूयते हविः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ śáśvatā ǀ tánā ǀ devám-devam ǀ yájāmahe ǀtvé íti ǀ ít ǀ hūyate ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whate’er in this perpetual course we sacrifice to God and God, That gift is offered up in thee
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever we offer in repeated and plural ntiful oblation to any other deity, is assuredly offered to you.
verses.griffith_verse: Whate’er in this perpetual course we sacrifice to God and God, That gift is offered up in thee
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रियो नो अस्तु विश्पतिर्होता मंद्रो वरेण्यः ।प्रियाः स्वग्नयो वयं ॥
verses.transliteration: priyáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀ hótā ǀ mandráḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀpriyā́ḥ ǀ su-agnáyaḥ ǀ vayám ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he be our dear household Lord, Priest, pleasant and, choice-worthy may We, with bright fires, be dear to him.
verses.wilson_translation: May the lord of men, the sacrificing priest, the gracious, the chosen, be kind to us; may we, possessed of holy fires, be   loved of you.
verses.griffith_verse: May he be our dear household Lord, Priest, pleasant and, choice-worthy may We, with bright fires, be dear to him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वग्नयो हि वार्यं देवासो दधिरे च नः ।स्वग्नयो मनामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: su-agnáyaḥ ǀ hí ǀ vā́ryam ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ dadhiré ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀsu-agnáyaḥ ǀ manāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods, adored with brilliant fires. have granted precious wealth to us So, with bright fires, we pray to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: As the brilliant (priests), possessed of holy fires, have taken charge of our oblations, so we, with holy fires, pray to you.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods, adored with brilliant fires. have granted precious wealth to us So, with bright fires, we pray to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अथा न उभयेषाममृत मर्त्यानां ।मिथः संतु प्रशस्तयः ॥
verses.transliteration: átha ǀ naḥ ǀ ubháyeṣām ǀ ámṛta ǀ mártyānām ǀmitháḥ ǀ santu ǀ prá-śastayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: And, O Immortal One, so may the eulogies of mortal men Belong to us and thee alike.
verses.wilson_translation: Immortal Agni, may the praises of mankind be henceforth mutually (the sources of happiness) to both, (to ourselves and to you).
verses.griffith_verse: And, O Immortal One, so may the eulogies of mortal men Belong to us and thee alike.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिमं यज्ञमिदं वचः ।चनो धाः सहसो यहो ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvebhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ agní-bhiḥ ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ idám ǀ vácaḥ ǀcánaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ yaho íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: With all thy fires, O Agni, find pleasure in this our sacrifice, And this our speech, O Son of Strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, son of strength, (accept) this sacrifice, and this our praise, with all your fires, and grant us (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: With all thy fires, O Agni, find pleasure in this our sacrifice, And this our speech, O Son of Strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVII. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १३ आजीगर्तिः शुनःशेप स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः। १-१२अग्निः, १३देवाः।।१-१२ गायत्री, १३ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WITH worship will I glorify thee, Agni, like a long-tailed steed,Imperial Lord of sacred rites. May the far-striding Son of Strength, bringer of great felicity,Who pours his gifts like rain, be ours. Lord of all life, from near; from far, do thou, O Agni evermoreProtect us from the sinful man. O Agni, graciously announce this our oblation to the Gods,And this our newest song of praise. Give us a share of strength most high, a share of strength that is below,A share of strength that is between. Thou dealest gifts, resplendent One; nigh, as with waves of Sindhu, thouSwift streamest to the worshipper. That man is lord of endless strength whom thou protectest in the fight,Agni, or urgest to the fray. Him, whosoever he may be, no man may vanquish, mighty One:Nay, very glorious power is his. May he who dwells with all mankind bear us with war-steeds through the fight,And with the singers win the spoil. Help, thou who knowest lauds, this work, this eulogy to Rudra, himAdorable in every house. May this our God, great, limitless, smoke-bannered excellently bright,Urge us to strength and holy thought. Like some rich Lord of men may he, Agni the banner of the Gods,Refulgent, hear us through our lauds. Glory to Gods, the mighty and the lesser glory to Gods the younger and the elder!Let us, if we have power, pay the God worship: no better prayer than this, ye Gods, acknowledge.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वं न त्वा वारवंतं वंदध्या अग्निं नमोभिः ।सम्राजंतमध्वराणां ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvam ǀ ná ǀ tvā ǀ vā́ra-vantam ǀ vandádhyai ǀ agním ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀsam-rā́jantam ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH worship will I glorify thee, Agni, like a long-tailed steed, Imperial Lord of sacred rites.
verses.wilson_translation: (I proceed) to address you, the soverign lord of sacrifice, with praises, (for you scatter our fores) like a horse (who brushes off flies with) his tail.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH worship will I glorify thee, Agni, like a long-tailed steed, Imperial Lord of sacred rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स घा नः सूनुः शवसा पृथुप्रगामा सुशेवः ।मीढ्वाँ अस्माकं बभूयात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ gha ǀ naḥ ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ pṛthú-pragāmā ǀ su-śévaḥ ǀmīḍhvā́n ǀ asmā́kam ǀ babhūyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the far-striding Son of Strength, bringer of great felicity, Who pours his gifts like rain, be ours.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, the son of strength, who moves everywhere fleetly, be propitious to us, and shower down (blessings).
verses.griffith_verse: May the far-striding Son of Strength, bringer of great felicity, Who pours his gifts like rain, be ours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नो दूराच्चासाच्च नि मर्त्यादघायोः ।पाहि सदमिद्विश्वायुः ॥
