verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dūrā́t ǀ ca ǀ āsā́t ǀ ca ǀ ní ǀ mártyāt ǀ agha-yóḥ ǀpāhí ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of all life, from near; from far, do thou, O Agni evermore Protect us from the sinful man.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Agni, who go everywhere, ever protect us, whether near or afar, from men seeking to do us injury.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of all life, from near; from far, do thou, O Agni evermore Protect us from the sinful man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इममू षु त्वमस्माकं सनिं गायत्रं नव्यांसं ।अग्ने देवेषु प्र वोचः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ tvám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ saním ǀ gāyatrám ǀ návyāṃsam ǀágne ǀ devéṣu ǀ prá ǀ vocaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, graciously announce this our oblation to the Gods, And this our newest song of praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, announce to the gods this our offering, and these our newest hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, graciously announce this our oblation to the Gods, And this our newest song of praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो भज परमेष्वा वाजेषु मध्यमेषु ।शिक्षा वस्वो अंतमस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhaja ǀ paraméṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ madhyaméṣu ǀśíkṣa ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ ántamasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us a share of strength most high, a share of strength that is below, A share of strength that is between.
verses.wilson_translation: Procure for us the food that is in heaven and mid-air, and grant us the wealth that is on earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us a share of strength most high, a share of strength that is below, A share of strength that is between.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विभक्तासि चित्रभानो सिंधोरूर्मा उपाक आ ।सद्यो दाशुषे क्षरसि ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-bhaktā́ ǀ asi ǀ citrabhāno íti citra-bhāno ǀ síndhoḥ ǀ ūrmáu ǀ upāké ǀ ā́ ǀsadyáḥ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ kṣarasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou dealest gifts, resplendent One; nigh, as with waves of Sindhu, thou Swift streamest to the worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Citrabhānu, are the   distributor of riches, as the waves of a river are parted by interjacent (islets); you ever pour (rewards) upon the giver (of oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou dealest gifts, resplendent One; nigh, as with waves of Sindhu, thou Swift streamest to the worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमग्ने पृत्सु मर्त्यमवा वाजेषु यं जुनाः ।स यंता शश्वतीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ agne ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ mártyam ǀ ávāḥ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ yám ǀ junā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ yántā ǀ śáśvatīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That man is lord of endless strength whom thou protectest in the fight, Agni, or urgest to the fray.
verses.wilson_translation: The mortal whom you,Agni, protect in battle, whom you incite to combat, will always command (food).
verses.griffith_verse: That man is lord of endless strength whom thou protectest in the fight, Agni, or urgest to the fray.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नकिरस्य सहंत्य पर्येता कयस्य चित् ।वाजो अस्ति श्रवाय्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: nákiḥ ǀ asya ǀ sahantya ǀ pari-etā́ ǀ káyasya ǀ cit ǀvā́jaḥ ǀ asti ǀ śravā́yyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, whosoever he may be, no man may vanquish, mighty One: Nay, very glorious power is his.
verses.wilson_translation: No one will ever be the vanquisher of this your worshipper, subduer of enemies, for notorious in his prowess.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, whosoever he may be, no man may vanquish, mighty One: Nay, very glorious power is his.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स वाजं विश्वचर्षणिरर्वद्भिरस्तु तरुता ।विप्रेभिरस्तु सनिता ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ árvat-bhiḥ ǀ astu ǀ tárutā ǀvíprebhiḥ ǀ astu ǀ sánitā ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he who dwells with all mankind bear us with war-steeds through the fight, And with the singers win the spoil.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who is worshipped by all men, convey us with horses through the battle; may he, (propitiated) by the priests, be the bestower (of bounties).
verses.griffith_verse: May he who dwells with all mankind bear us with war-steeds through the fight, And with the singers win the spoil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि विशेविशे यज्ञियाय ।स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकं ॥
verses.transliteration: járā-bodha ǀ tát ǀ viviḍḍhi ǀ viśé-viśe ǀ yajñíyāya ǀstómam ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ dṛ́śīkam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Help, thou who knowest lauds, this work, this eulogy to Rudra, him Adorable in every house.
verses.wilson_translation: Jarābodha, enter into the oblation for the completion of the sacrifice that benefits all mankind; the worshipper offers agreeable laudation to the terrible (Agni).
verses.griffith_verse: Help, thou who knowest lauds, this work, this eulogy to Rudra, him Adorable in every house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नो महाँ अनिमानो धूमकेतुः पुरुश्चंद्रः ।धिये वाजाय हिन्वतु ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ ani-mānáḥ ǀ dhūmá-ketuḥ ǀ puru-candráḥ ǀdhiyé ǀ vā́jāya ǀ hinvatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this our God, great, limitless, smoke-bannered excellently bright, Urge us to strength and holy thought.
verses.wilson_translation: May the vast, illimitable, smoke- bannered, resplendent Agnibe plural ased with our rite, and grant us food.
verses.griffith_verse: May this our God, great, limitless, smoke-bannered excellently bright, Urge us to strength and holy thought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स रेवाँ इव विश्पतिर्दैव्यः केतुः शृणोतु नः ।उक्थैरग्निर्बृहद्भानुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ revā́n-iva ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀ dáivyaḥ ǀ ketúḥ ǀ śṛṇotu ǀ naḥ ǀuktháiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ bṛhát-bhānuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like some rich Lord of men may he, Agni the banner of the Gods, Refulgent, hear us through our lauds.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agni, the lord of men, the invoker and messenger of the gods, the brilliant-rayed, hear us with our hymns, as a prince (listens to the bards).
verses.griffith_verse: Like some rich Lord of men may he, Agni the banner of the Gods, Refulgent, hear us through our lauds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यो नमो युवभ्यो नम आशिनेभ्यः ।यजाम देवान्यदि शक्नवाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: námaḥ ǀ mahát-bhyaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ arbhakébhyaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ yúvabhyaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ āśinébhyaḥ ǀyájāma ǀ devā́n ǀ yádi ǀ śaknávāma ǀ mā́ ǀ jyā́yasaḥ ǀ śáṃsam ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛkṣi ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glory to Gods, the mighty and the lesser glory to Gods the younger and the elder! Let us, if we have power, pay the God worship: no better prayer than this, ye Gods, acknowledge.
verses.wilson_translation: Veneration to the great gods, veneration to the lesser, veneration to the young, veneration to the old we worship (all) the gods as well as we are able; may I not omit the praise of the elder divinities.
verses.griffith_verse: Glory to Gods, the mighty and the lesser glory to Gods the younger and the elder! Let us, if we have power, pay the God worship: no better prayer than this, ye Gods, acknowledge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVIII. Indra, Etc.
hymns.anukramani: ९ आजीगर्तिः शुनःशेप स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः। १-४ इन्द्रः, ५-६ उलू खलं, ७-८ उलूखल मुसले, ९ प्रजापतिर्हरि श्चन्द्रः, (अधिषवण) चर्म सोमो वा। १-६ अनुष्टुप्, ७-९ गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: THERE where the broad-based stone raised on high to press the juices out,O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds. Where, like broad hips, to hold the juice the platters of the press are laid,O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds. There where the woman marks and leans the pestle's constant rise and fall,O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds. Where, as with reins to guide a horse, they bind the churning-staff with cords,O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds. If of a truth in every house, O Mortar thou art set for work,Here give thou forth thy clearest sound, loud as the drum of conquerors. O Sovran of the Forest, as the wind blows soft in front of thee,Mortar, for Indra press thou forth the Soma juice that he may drink. Best strength-givers, ye stretch wide jaws, O Sacrificial Implements,Like two bay horses champing herbs. Ye Sovrans of the Forest, both swift, with swift pressers press to-daySweet Soma juice for Indra's drink. Take up in beakers what remains: the Soma on the filter pour,and on the ox-hide set the dregs.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र ग्रावा पृथुबुध्न ऊर्ध्वो भवति सोतवे ।उलूखलसुतानामवेद्विंद्र जल्गुलः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ grā́vā ǀ pṛthú-budhnaḥ ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ bhávati ǀ sótave ǀulū́khala-sutānām ǀ áva ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ indra ǀ jalgulaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THERE where the broad-based stone raised on high to press the juices out, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, as the broad-based stone is raised to express the Somajuice, recognize and partake of the effusion of the mortar.
verses.griffith_verse: THERE where the broad-based stone raised on high to press the juices out, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्र द्वाविव जघनाधिषवण्या कृता ।उलूखलसुतानामवेद्विंद्र जल्गुलः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ dváu-iva ǀ jaghánā ǀ adhi-savanyā́ ǀ kṛtā́ ǀulū́khala-sutānām ǀ áva ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ indra ǀ jalgulaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where, like broad hips, to hold the juice the platters of the press are laid, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, (in the rite) in which the two patters for containing the juice, as (broad as a woman's) hips, are employed, recognize and partake of the effusion of the mortar.
verses.griffith_verse: Where, like broad hips, to hold the juice the platters of the press are laid, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्र नार्यपच्यवमुपच्यवं च शिक्षते ।उलूखलसुतानामवेद्विंद्र जल्गुलः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ nā́rī ǀ apa-cyavám ǀ upa-cyavám ǀ ca ǀ śíkṣate ǀulū́khala-sutānām ǀ áva ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ indra ǀ jalgulaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: There where the woman marks and leans the pestle's constant rise and fall, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, (in the rite) in which the housewife repeats egress from and ingress into (the sacrificial chamber), recognize and partake of the effusion of the mortar.
verses.griffith_verse: There where the woman marks and leans the pestle's constant rise and fall, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्र मंथां विबध्नते रश्मीन्यमितवा इव ।उलूखलसुतानामवेद्विंद्र जल्गुलः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ mánthām ǀ vi-badhnáte ǀ raśmī́n ǀ yámitavái-iva ǀulū́khala-sutānām ǀ áva ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ indra ǀ jalgulaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where, as with reins to guide a horse, they bind the churning-staff with cords, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.wilson_translation: When they bind the churning-staff (with a cord), like reins to restrain (a horse),Indra, recognize and partake of the effusion of the mortar.
verses.griffith_verse: Where, as with reins to guide a horse, they bind the churning-staff with cords, O Indra, drink with eager thirst the droppings which the mortar sheds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि त्वं गृहेगृह उलूखलक युज्यसे ।इह द्युमत्तमं वद जयतामिव दुंदुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ tvám ǀ gṛhé-gṛhe ǀ úlūkhalaka ǀ yujyáse ǀihá ǀ dyumát-tamam ǀ vada ǀ jáyatām-iva ǀ dundubhíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: If of a truth in every house, O Mortar thou art set for work, Here give thou forth thy clearest sound, loud as the drum of conquerors.
verses.wilson_translation: If indeed, O Mortar, you are present in every house, give forth (in this rite) a lusty sound, like the drum of a victorious host.
verses.griffith_verse: If of a truth in every house, O Mortar thou art set for work, Here give thou forth thy clearest sound, loud as the drum of conquerors.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्म ते वनस्पते वातो वि वात्यग्रमित् ।अथो इंद्राय पातवे सुनु सोममुलूखल ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ te ǀ vanaspate ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ví ǀ vāti ǀ ágram ǀ ít ǀátho íti ǀ índrāya ǀ pā́tave ǀ sunú ǀ sómam ǀ ulūkhala ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Sovran of the Forest, as the wind blows soft in front of thee, Mortar, for Indra press thou forth the Soma juice that he may drink.
verses.wilson_translation: Lorf of the forest, as the wind genitive ly blows before you, so do thou, O Mortar, prepare the Somajuice for the beverage of Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: O Sovran of the Forest, as the wind blows soft in front of thee, Mortar, for Indra press thou forth the Soma juice that he may drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आयजी वाजसातमा ता ह्युच्चा विजर्भृतः ।हरी इवांधांसि बप्सता ॥
verses.transliteration: āyajī́ ítyā-yajī́ ǀ vāja-sā́tamā ǀ tā́ ǀ hí ǀ uccā́ ǀ vi-jarbhṛtáḥ ǀhárī ivéti hárī-iva ǀ ándhāṃsi ǀ bápsatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Best strength-givers, ye stretch wide jaws, O Sacrificial Implements, Like two bay horses champing herbs.
verses.wilson_translation: Implements of sacrifice, bestowers of food, loud-sounding, sport like the horses of Indrachamping the grain.
verses.griffith_verse: Best strength-givers, ye stretch wide jaws, O Sacrificial Implements, Like two bay horses champing herbs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता नो अद्य वनस्पती ऋष्वावृष्वेभिः सोतृभिः ।इंद्राय मधुमत्सुतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vanaspatī íti ǀ ṛṣváu ǀ ṛṣvébhiḥ ǀ sotṛ́-bhiḥ ǀíndrāya ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ sutam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Sovrans of the Forest, both swift, with swift pressers press to-day Sweet Soma juice for Indra's drink.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you two forest lords, of plural asing form, prepare with agreeable libations our sweet (Soma) juices for Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Sovrans of the Forest, both swift, with swift pressers press to-day Sweet Soma juice for Indra's drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भर सोमं पवित्र आ सृज ।नि धेहि गोरधि त्वचि ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ śiṣṭám ǀ camvóḥ ǀ bhara ǀ sómam ǀ pavítre ǀ ā́ ǀ sṛja ǀní ǀ dhehi ǀ góḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ tvací ǁ
verses.english_translation: Take up in beakers what remains: the Soma on the filter pour, and on the ox-hide set the dregs.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring the remains of the Somajuice upon the plural tters, sprinkle it upon the blades ofkuśagrass and plural ce the reminder upon the cow-hide.
verses.griffith_verse: Take up in beakers what remains: the Soma on the filter pour, and on the ox-hide set the dregs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIX. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ७ आजीगर्तिः शुनःशेप स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः। इन्द्रः। पंक्ति।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: O SOMA DRINKER, ever true, utterly hopeless though we be,Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. O Lord of Strength, whose jaws are strong, great deeds are thine, the powerful:Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. Lull thou asleep, to wake no more, the pair who on each other lookDo thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. Hero, let hostile spirits sleep, and every gentler genius wake:Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. Destroy this ass, O Indra, who in tones discordant brays to thee:Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. Far distant on the forest fall the tempest in a circling course!Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine,In thousands, O most wealthy One. Slay each reviler, and destroy him who in secret injures us:Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kineIn thousands, O most wealthy One.

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा अनाशस्ता इव स्मसि ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ satya ǀ soma-pāḥ ǀ anāśastā́ḥ-iva ǀ smási ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: O SOMA DRINKER, ever true, utterly hopeless though we be, Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Veracious drinker of the Somajuice, although we be unworthy, do your,Indra, of boundless wealth enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: O SOMA DRINKER, ever true, utterly hopeless though we be, Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शिप्रिन्वाजानां पते शचीवस्तव दंसना ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: śíprin ǀ vājānām ǀ pate ǀ śácī-vaḥ ǀ táva ǀ daṃsánā ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Lord of Strength, whose jaws are strong, great deeds are thine, the powerful: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Your benevolence, handsome and mighty lord of food, endures for ever; therefore,Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: O Lord of Strength, whose jaws are strong, great deeds are thine, the powerful: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि ष्वापया मिथूदृशा सस्तामबुध्यमाने ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ svāpaya ǀ mithu-dṛ́śā ǀ sastā́m ǀ ábudhyamāne íti ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lull thou asleep, to wake no more, the pair who on each other look Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Cast asleep (the two feminine le messengers of Yama); looking at each other, let them sleep, never waking;Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Lull thou asleep, to wake no more, the pair who on each other look Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ससंतु त्या अरातयो बोधंतु शूर रातयः ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: sasántu ǀ tyā́ḥ ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ bódhantu ǀ śūra ǀ rātáyaḥ ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero, let hostile spirits sleep, and every gentler genius wake: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: May those who are our enemies, slumber, and those, O hero, who are our friends, be awake;Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Hero, let hostile spirits sleep, and every gentler genius wake: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समिंद्र गर्दभं मृण नुवंतं पापयामुया ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ indra ǀ gardabhám ǀ mṛṇa ǀ nuvántam ǀ pāpáyā ǀ amuyā́ ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroy this ass, O Indra, who in tones discordant brays to thee: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, destroy this ass, (our adversary), praising you with such discordant speech; and do your, Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Destroy this ass, O Indra, who in tones discordant brays to thee: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पताति कुंडृणाच्या दूरं वातो वनादधि ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: pátāti ǀ kuṇḍṛṇā́cyā ǀ dūrám ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ vánāt ǀ ádhi ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far distant on the forest fall the tempest in a circling course! Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us (adverse) breeze, with crooked course, alight afar off on the forest;Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Far distant on the forest fall the tempest in a circling course! Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं परिक्रोशं जहि जंभया कृकदाश्वं ।आ तू न इंद्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ ॥
verses.transliteration: sárvam ǀ pari-krośám ǀ jahi ǀ jambháya ǀ kṛkadāśvám ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śaṃsaya ǀ góṣu ǀ áśveṣu ǀ śubhríṣu ǀ sahásreṣu ǀ tuvi-magha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slay each reviler, and destroy him who in secret injures us: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroy every one that reviles us; slay every one that does us injury;Indra, of boundless wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Slay each reviler, and destroy him who in secret injures us: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine In thousands, O most wealthy One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WE seeking strength with Soma-drops fill full your Indra like a well,Most liberal, Lord of Hundred Powers, Who lets a hundred of the pure, a thousand of the milk-blent draughtsFlow, even as down a depth, to him; When for the strong, the rapturous joy he in this manner hath made roomWithin his belly, like the sea. This is thine own. Thou drawest near, as turns a pigeon to his mate:Thou carest too for this our prayer. O Hero, Lord of Bounties, praised in hymns, may power and joyfulnessBe his who sings the laud to thee. Lord of a Hundred Powers, stand up to lend us succour in this fightIn others too let us agree. In every need, in every fray we call as friends to succour usIndra the mightiest of all. If he will hear us let him come with succour of a thousand kinds,And all that strengthens, to our call. I call him mighty to resist, the Hero of our ancient home,Thee whom my sire invoked of old. We pray to thee, O much-invoked, rich in all precious gifts, O Friend,Kind God to those who sing thy praise. O Soma-drinker, Thunder-armed, Friend of our lovely-featured damesAnd of our Soma-drinking friends. Thus, Soma-drinker, may it be; thus, Friend, who wieldest thunder, actTo aid each wish as we desire. With Indra splendid feasts be ours, rich in all strengthening things wherewith,Wealthy in food, we may rejoice. Like thee, thyself, the singers' Friend, thou movest, as it were, besought,Bold One, the axle of the car. That, Śatakratu, thou to grace and please thy praisers, as it were,Stirrest the axle with thy strength. With champing, neighing loudly-snorting horses Indra hath ever won himself great treasuresA car of gold hath he whose deeds are wondrous received from us, and let us too receive it. Come, Aśvins, with enduring strength wealthy in horses and in kine,And gold, O ye of wondrous deeds. Your chariot yoked for both alike, immortal, ye of mighty acts,Travels, O Aśvins, in the sea. High on the forehead of the Bull one chariot wheel ye ever keep,The other round the sky revolves. What mortal, O immortal Dawn, enjoyeth thee? Where lovest thou?To whom, O radiant, dost thou go? For we have had thee in our thoughts whether anear or far away,Red-hued and like a dappled mare. Hither, O Daughter of the Sky, come thou with these thy strengthenings,And send thou riches down to us.

verses.sanskrit: आ व इंद्रं क्रिविं यथा वाजयंतः शतक्रतुं ।मंहिष्ठं सिंच इंदुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ índram ǀ krívim ǀ yathā ǀ vāja-yántaḥ ǀ śatá-kratum ǀmáṃhiṣṭham ǀ siñce ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WE seeking strength with Soma-drops fill full your Indra like a well, Most liberal, Lord of Hundred Powers,
verses.wilson_translation: Let us, who are desirous of food, satisfy this your Indra, who is mighty, and of a hundred sacrifices, with drops (of Somajuice), as a well (is filled)(with water).
verses.griffith_verse: WE seeking strength with Soma-drops fill full your Indra like a well, Most liberal, Lord of Hundred Powers,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं वा यः शुचीनां सहस्रं वा समाशिरां ।एदु निम्नं न रीयते ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ śúcīnām ǀ sahásram ǀ vā ǀ sám-āśirām ǀā́ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nimnám ǀ ná ǀ rīyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who lets a hundred of the pure, a thousand of the milk-blent draughts Flow, even as down a depth, to him;
verses.wilson_translation: May he who is (the recipient) of a hundred pure, and of a thousand distilled, (libations), come (to the rite), as water to low (plural ces).
verses.griffith_verse: Who lets a hundred of the pure, a thousand of the milk-blent draughts Flow, even as down a depth, to him;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं यन्मदाय शुष्मिण एना ह्यस्योदरे ।समुद्रो न व्यचो दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ yát ǀ mádāya ǀ śuṣmíṇe ǀ enā́ ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ udáre ǀsamudráḥ ǀ ná ǀ vyácaḥ ǀ dadhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: When for the strong, the rapturous joy he in this manner hath made room Within his belly, like the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: All which (libations), being accusative ulated for the gratification of the powerful Indra, is contained in his belly, as water in the ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: When for the strong, the rapturous joy he in this manner hath made room Within his belly, like the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयमु ते समतसि कपोत इव गर्भधिं ।वचस्तच्चिन्न ओहसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ te ǀ sám ǀ atasi ǀ kapótaḥ-iva ǀ garbha-dhím ǀvácaḥ ǀ tát ǀ cit ǀ naḥ ǀ ohase ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is thine own. Thou drawest near, as turns a pigeon to his mate: Thou carest too for this our prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: This libation is (prepared) for you; you approach it as a pigeon his pregnant (mate), for on that account do you accept our prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: This is thine own. Thou drawest near, as turns a pigeon to his mate: Thou carest too for this our prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोत्रं राधानां पते गिर्वाहो वीर यस्य ते ।विभूतिरस्तु सूनृता ॥
verses.transliteration: stotrám ǀ rādhānām ǀ pate ǀ gírvāhaḥ ǀ vīra ǀ yásya ǀ te ǀví-bhūtiḥ ǀ astu ǀ sūnṛ́tā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Hero, Lord of Bounties, praised in hymns, may power and joyfulness Be his who sings the laud to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, lord of affluence, accepter of praise, may genitive ine prosperity be (the reward of him) who offers you laudation.
verses.griffith_verse: O Hero, Lord of Bounties, praised in hymns, may power and joyfulness Be his who sings the laud to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा न ऊतयेऽस्मिन्वाजे शतक्रतो ।समन्येषु ब्रवावहै ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ asmín ǀ vā́je ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀsám ǀ anyéṣu ǀ bravāvahai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of a Hundred Powers, stand up to lend us succour in this fight In others too let us agree.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise up,Śatakratu, for our defence in this conflict; we will talk together in other matters.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of a Hundred Powers, stand up to lend us succour in this fight In others too let us agree.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: योगेयोगे तवस्तरं वाजेवाजे हवामहे ।सखाय इंद्रमूतये ॥
verses.transliteration: yóge-yoge ǀ taváḥ-taram ǀ vā́je-vāje ǀ havāmahe ǀsákhāyaḥ ǀ índram ǀ ūtáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: In every need, in every fray we call as friends to succour us Indra the mightiest of all.
verses.wilson_translation: On every occasion, in every engagement, we invoke as friends the most powerful Indrafor our defence.
verses.griffith_verse: In every need, in every fray we call as friends to succour us Indra the mightiest of all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ घा गमद्यदि श्रवत्सहस्रिणीभिरूतिभिः ।वाजेभिरुप नो हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gha ǀ gamat ǀ yádi ǀ śrávat ǀ sahasríṇībhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀvā́jebhiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: If he will hear us let him come with succour of a thousand kinds, And all that strengthens, to our call.
verses.wilson_translation: If he hear our invocation, let him indeed come to us with numerous bounties, and with (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: If he will hear us let him come with succour of a thousand kinds, And all that strengthens, to our call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनु प्रत्नस्यौकसो हुवे तुविप्रतिं नरं ।यं ते पूर्वं पिता हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ pratnásya ǀ ókasaḥ ǀ huvé ǀ tuvi-pratím ǀ náram ǀyám ǀ te ǀ pū́rvam ǀ pitā́ ǀ huvé ǁ
verses.english_translation: I call him mighty to resist, the Hero of our ancient home, Thee whom my sire invoked of old.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the man (Indra), who visits many worshippers from his ancient dwelling-plural ce--you, Indra, whom my father formerly invoked.
verses.griffith_verse: I call him mighty to resist, the Hero of our ancient home, Thee whom my sire invoked of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा वयं विश्ववारा शास्महे पुरुहूत ।सखे वसो जरितृभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ viśva-vāra ǀ ā́ ǀ śāsmahe ǀ puru-hūta ǀsákhe ǀ vaso íti ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We pray to thee, O much-invoked, rich in all precious gifts, O Friend, Kind God to those who sing thy praise.
verses.wilson_translation: We implore you as our friend, who are preferred and invoked by all, (to be favourable) to your worshippers, protector of dwellings.
verses.griffith_verse: We pray to thee, O much-invoked, rich in all precious gifts, O Friend, Kind God to those who sing thy praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं शिप्रिणीनां सोमपाः सोमपाव्नां ।सखे वज्रिन्त्सखीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ śipríṇīnām ǀ sóma-pāḥ ǀ soma-pā́vnām ǀsákhe ǀ vajrin ǀ sákhīnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Soma-drinker, Thunder-armed, Friend of our lovely-featured dames And of our Soma-drinking friends.
verses.wilson_translation: Drinker of Somajuice, wielder of the thunderbolt, O friend, (bestow upon) us, your friends, and drinkers of the Soma juice, (abundance of cows) with projecting jaws. (śipirṇīnām, genitive plural of the feminine nine śipriṇī, having a nose of a jaw; hence gavām andsamūha(of cows and a herd) are added].
verses.griffith_verse: O Soma-drinker, Thunder-armed, Friend of our lovely-featured dames And of our Soma-drinking friends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तथा तदस्तु सोमपाः सखे वज्रिन्तथा कृणु ।यथा त उश्मसीष्टये ॥
verses.transliteration: táthā ǀ tát ǀ astu ǀ soma-pāḥ ǀ sákhe ǀ vajrin ǀ táthā ǀ kṛṇu ǀyáthā ǀ te ǀ uśmási ǀ iṣṭáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus, Soma-drinker, may it be; thus, Friend, who wieldest thunder, act To aid each wish as we desire.
verses.wilson_translation: So be it, drinker of the Somajuice, wielder of the thunderbolt, our friend, that you will do, through your favour, whatever we desire.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus, Soma-drinker, may it be; thus, Friend, who wieldest thunder, act To aid each wish as we desire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रेवतीर्नः सधमाद इंद्रे संतु तुविवाजाः ।क्षुमंतो याभिर्मदेम ॥
verses.transliteration: revátīḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ índre ǀ santu ǀ tuví-vājāḥ ǀkṣu-mántaḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ mádema ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Indra splendid feasts be ours, rich in all strengthening things wherewith, Wealthy in food, we may rejoice.
verses.wilson_translation: So,Indra, rejoicing along with us, we may have (abundant food) and cows may be ours, robust and rich in milk, with which we may be happy.
verses.griffith_verse: With Indra splendid feasts be ours, rich in all strengthening things wherewith, Wealthy in food, we may rejoice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ घ त्वावान्त्मनाप्तः स्तोतृभ्यो धृष्णवियानः ।ऋणोरक्षं न चक्र्योः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gha ǀ tvā́-vān ǀ tmánā ǀ āptáḥ ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ iyānáḥ ǀṛṇóḥ ǀ ákṣam ǀ ná ǀ cakryóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like thee, thyself, the singers' Friend, thou movest, as it were, besought, Bold One, the axle of the car.
verses.wilson_translation: O Dhṛṣnu, let some such divinity as you are, self-presented, promptly bestow, when solicited, (bounties) upon your praisers, as (they whirl) the axle of the wheels (of a car).
verses.griffith_verse: Like thee, thyself, the singers' Friend, thou movest, as it were, besought, Bold One, the axle of the car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यद्दुवः शतक्रतवा कामं जरितॄणां ।ऋणोरक्षं न शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yát ǀ dúvaḥ ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀ ā́ ǀ kā́mam ǀ jaritṝṇā́m ǀṛṇóḥ ǀ ákṣam ǀ ná ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That, Śatakratu, thou to grace and please thy praisers, as it were, Stirrest the axle with thy strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Such wealth,Śatakratu, as your praisers desire, you bestow upon them, as the axle (revolves) with the movements (of the wagon).
verses.griffith_verse: That, Śatakratu, thou to grace and please thy praisers, as it were, Stirrest the axle with thy strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शश्वदिंद्रः पोप्रुथद्भिर्जिगाय नानदद्भिः शाश्वसद्भिर्धनानि ।स नो हिरण्यरथं दंसनावान्त्स नः सनिता सनये स नोऽदात् ॥
verses.transliteration: śáśvat ǀ índraḥ ǀ pópruthat-bhiḥ ǀ jigāya ǀ nā́nadat-bhiḥ ǀ śā́śvasat-bhiḥ ǀ dhánāni ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ hiraṇya-rathám ǀ daṃsánā-vān ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sanitā́ ǀ sanáye ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: With champing, neighing loudly-snorting horses Indra hath ever won himself great treasures A car of gold hath he whose deeds are wondrous received from us, and let us too receive it.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas ever won riches (from his foes), with his champing, neighing, and snorting (steeds); he, the abounding in acts, the bountiful, has given us as a gift a golden chariot.
verses.griffith_verse: With champing, neighing loudly-snorting horses Indra hath ever won himself great treasures A car of gold hath he whose deeds are wondrous received from us, and let us too receive it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आश्विनावश्वावत्येषा यातं शवीरया ।गोमद्दस्रा हिरण्यवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ aśvinau ǀ áśva-vatyā ǀ iṣā́ ǀ yātam ǀ śávīrayā ǀgó-mat ǀ dasrā ǀ híraṇya-vat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, Aśvins, with enduring strength wealthy in horses and in kine, And gold, O ye of wondrous deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, come hither, with viands borne or many steeds. Dasrās, (let our dwelling) be filled with cattle and with gold.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, Aśvins, with enduring strength wealthy in horses and in kine, And gold, O ye of wondrous deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानयोजनो हि वाँ रथो दस्रावमर्त्यः ।समुद्रे अश्विनेयते ॥
verses.transliteration: samāná-yojanaḥ ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ dasrau ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀsamudré ǀ aśvinā ǀ ī́yate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your chariot yoked for both alike, immortal, ye of mighty acts, Travels, O Aśvins, in the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasrās, your chariot, harnessed for both alike, is imperishable; it travels,Aśvins, through the air.
verses.griffith_verse: Your chariot yoked for both alike, immortal, ye of mighty acts, Travels, O Aśvins, in the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न्यघ्न्यस्य मूर्धनि चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः ।परि द्यामन्यदीयते ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ aghnyásya ǀ mūrdháni ǀ cakrám ǀ ráthasya ǀ yemathuḥ ǀpári ǀ dyā́m ǀ anyát ǀ īyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: High on the forehead of the Bull one chariot wheel ye ever keep, The other round the sky revolves.
verses.wilson_translation: You have one wheel on the top of the solid (mountain), while the other revolves in the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: High on the forehead of the Bull one chariot wheel ye ever keep, The other round the sky revolves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कस्त उषः कधप्रिये भुजे मर्तो अमर्त्ये ।कं नक्षसे विभावरि ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ te ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ kadha-priye ǀ bhujé ǀ mártaḥ ǀ amartye ǀkám ǀ nakṣase ǀ vibhā-vari ǁ
verses.english_translation: What mortal, O immortal Dawn, enjoyeth thee? Where lovest thou? To whom, O radiant, dost thou go?
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, who are plural ased by praise, what mortal enjoy you, immortal? Whom, mighty one, do your affect?
verses.griffith_verse: What mortal, O immortal Dawn, enjoyeth thee? Where lovest thou? To whom, O radiant, dost thou go?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयं हि ते अमन्मह्यांतादा पराकात् ।अश्वे न चित्रे अरुषि ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ ámanmahi ǀ ā́ ǀ ántāt ǀ ā́ ǀ parākā́t ǀáśve ǀ ná ǀ citre ǀ aruṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: For we have had thee in our thoughts whether anear or far away, Red-hued and like a dappled mare.
verses.wilson_translation: Diffusive, many-tinted, brilliant (Uṣas), we know not (your limits), whether they be nigh or remote.
verses.griffith_verse: For we have had thee in our thoughts whether anear or far away, Red-hued and like a dappled mare.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्येभिरा गहि वाजेभिर्दुहितर्दिवः ।अस्मे रयिं नि धारय ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ ní ǀ dhāraya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither, O Daughter of the Sky, come thou with these thy strengthenings, And send thou riches down to us.
verses.wilson_translation: Daughter of heaven, approach with these viands, and perpetuate our wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither, O Daughter of the Sky, come thou with these thy strengthenings, And send thou riches down to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: Thou, Agni, wast the earliest Aṅgiras, a Seer; thou wast, a God thyself, the Gods’ auspicious Friend.After thy holy ordinance the Maruts, sage, active through wisdom, with their glittering spears, were born. O Agni, thou, the best and earliest Aṅgiras, fulfillest as a Sage the holy law of Gods.Sprung from two mothers, wise, through all existence spread, resting in many a place for sake of living man. To Mātariśvan first thou, Agni, wast disclosed, and to Vivasvān through thy noble inward power.Heaven and Earth, Vasu! shook at the choosing of the Priest: the burthen thou didst bear, didst worship mighty Gods. Agni thou madest heaven to thunder for mankind; thou, yet more pious, for pious Purūravas.When thou art rapidly freed from thy parents, first eastward they bear thee round, and, after, to the west. Thou, Agni, art a Bull who makes our store increase, to be invoked by him who lifts the ladle up.Well knowing the oblation with the hallowing word, uniting all who live, thou lightenest first our folk Agni, thou savest in the synod when pursued e’en him, farseeing One! who walks in evil ways.Thou, when the heroes fight for spoil which men rush, round, slayest in war the many by the hands of few. For glory, Agni, day by day, thou liftest up the mortal man to highest immortality,Even thou who yearning for both races givest them great bliss, and to the prince grantest abundant food. O Agni, highly lauded, make our singer famous that he may win us store of riches:May we improve the rite with new performance. O Earth and Heaven, with all the Gods, protect us. O blameless Agni lying in thy Parents' lap, a God among the Gods, be watchful for our good.Former of bodies, be the singer's Providence: all good things hast thou sown for him, auspicious One! Agni, thou art our Providence, our Father thou: we are thy brethren and thou art our spring of life.In thee, rich in good heroes, guard of high decrees, meet hundred, thousand treasures, O infallible! Thee, Agni, have the Gods made the first living One for living man, Lord of the house of Nahuṣa.Iḷā they made the teacher of the sons of men, what time a Son was born to the father of my race. Worthy to be revered, O Agni, God, preserve our wealthy patrons with thy succours, and ourselves.Guard of our seed art thou, aiding our cows to bear, incessantly protecting in thy holy way. Agni, thou art a guard close to the pious man; kindled art thou, four-eyed! for him who is unarmed.With fond heart thou acceptest e’en the poor man's prayer, when he hath brought his gift to gain security. Thou, Agni gainest for the loudly-praising priest the highest wealth, the object of a man's desire.Thou art called Father, caring even for the weak, and wisest, to the simple one thou teachest lore. Agni, the man who giveth guerdon to the priests, like well-sewn armour thou guardest on every side.He who with grateful food shows kindness in his house, an offerer to the living, is the type of heaven. Pardon, we pray, this sin of ours, O Agni,—the path which we have trodden, widely straying,Dear Friend and Father, caring for the pious, who speedest nigh and who inspirest mortals. As erst to Manus, to Yayāti, Aṅgiras, so Aṅgiras! pure Agni! come thou to our hall.Bring hither the celestial host and seat them here upon the sacred grass, and offer what they love. By this our prayer be thou, O Agni, strengthened, prayer made by us after our power and knowledge.Lead thou us, therefore, to increasing riches; endow us with thy strength-bestowing favour.

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अंगिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा ।तव व्रते कवयो विद्मनापसोऽजायंत मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ áṅgirāḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ sákhā ǀtáva ǀ vraté ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ vidmanā́-apasaḥ ǀ ájāyanta ǀ marútaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni, wast the earliest Aṅgiras, a Seer; thou wast, a God thyself, the Gods’ auspicious Friend. After thy holy ordinance the Maruts, sage, active through wisdom, with their glittering spears, were born.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, was th first AṅgirasṚṣi, a divinity, you were the auspicious friend of the deities. In your rite the wise, the all-discerning, the bright-weaponed Marutswere engendered.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni, wast the earliest Aṅgiras, a Seer; thou wast, a God thyself, the Gods’ auspicious Friend. After thy holy ordinance the Maruts, sage, active through wisdom, with their glittering spears, were born.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अंगिरस्तमः कविर्देवानां परि भूषसि व्रतं ।विभुर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय मेधिरो द्विमाता शयुः कतिधा चिदायवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ pári ǀ bhūṣasi ǀ vratám ǀvi-bhúḥ ǀ víśvasmai ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ médhiraḥ ǀ dvi-mātā́ ǀ śayúḥ ǀ katidhā́ ǀ cit ǀ āyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, thou, the best and earliest Aṅgiras, fulfillest as a Sage the holy law of Gods. Sprung from two mothers, wise, through all existence spread, resting in many a place for sake of living man.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, the first and chief Aṅgiras, grace the worship of the gods; sapient, maniforld, for the benefit of all the world, intelligent, the off-spring of two mothers, and reposing in various ways for the use of man.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, thou, the best and earliest Aṅgiras, fulfillest as a Sage the holy law of Gods. Sprung from two mothers, wise, through all existence spread, resting in many a place for sake of living man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव सुक्रतूया विवस्वते ।अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृवूर्येऽसघ्नोर्भारमयजो महो वसो ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ mātaríśvane ǀ āvíḥ ǀ bhava ǀ sukratū-yā́ ǀ vivásvate ǀárejetām ǀ ródasī íti ǀ hotṛ-vū́rye ǀ ásaghnoḥ ǀ bhārám ǀ áyajaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ vaso íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Mātariśvan first thou, Agni, wast disclosed, and to Vivasvān through thy noble inward power. Heaven and Earth, Vasu! shook at the choosing of the Priest: the burthen thou didst bear, didst worship mighty Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, pre-eminent over the wind, become manifest to the worshipper, in approbation of his worship. Heaven and earth tremble (at your power); you have sustained the burden in the rite for which the priest was appointed; your,Vasu, has worshipped the venerable (gods).
verses.griffith_verse: To Mātariśvan first thou, Agni, wast disclosed, and to Vivasvān through thy noble inward power. Heaven and Earth, Vasu! shook at the choosing of the Priest: the burthen thou didst bear, didst worship mighty Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने मनवे द्यामवाशयः पुरूरवसे सुकृते सुकृत्तरः ।श्वात्रेण यत्पित्रोर्मुच्यसे पर्या त्वा पूर्वमनयन्नापरं पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ mánave ǀ dyā́m ǀ avāśayaḥ ǀ purūrávase ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ sukṛ́t-taraḥ ǀśvātréṇa ǀ yát ǀ pitróḥ ǀ múcyase ǀ pári ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ pū́rvam ǀ anayan ǀ ā́ ǀ áparam ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni thou madest heaven to thunder for mankind; thou, yet more pious, for pious Purūravas. When thou art rapidly freed from thy parents, first eastward they bear thee round, and, after, to the west.
verses.wilson_translation: Your,Agni, has announced heaven to Manu; you have more than requited Purūravasdoing homage to you. When you are set free by the attrition of your parents, they bear you first to the east, then to the west (of the altar).
verses.griffith_verse: Agni thou madest heaven to thunder for mankind; thou, yet more pious, for pious Purūravas. When thou art rapidly freed from thy parents, first eastward they bear thee round, and, after, to the west.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने वृषभः पुष्टिवर्धन उद्यतस्रुचे भवसि श्रवाय्यः ।य आहुतिं परि वेदा वषट्कृतिमेकायुरग्रे विश आविवाससि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ puṣṭi-várdhanaḥ ǀ údyata-sruce ǀ bhavasi ǀ śravā́yyaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ ā́-hutim ǀ pári ǀ véda ǀ váṣaṭ-kṛtim ǀ éka-āyuḥ ǀ ágre ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā-vívāsasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni, art a Bull who makes our store increase, to be invoked by him who lifts the ladle up. Well knowing the oblation with the hallowing word, uniting all who live, thou lightenest first our folk
verses.wilson_translation: Your,Agni, are the showerer (of desires), the augmenter of the prosperity (of your worshipper); you are to be called upon as the ladle is lifted up; upon him who fully understands the invocation and makes the oblation, you, the provider of sustenance, first bestow light, and then upon all men.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni, art a Bull who makes our store increase, to be invoked by him who lifts the ladle up. Well knowing the oblation with the hallowing word, uniting all who live, thou lightenest first our folk
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने वृजिनवर्तनिं नरं सक्मन्पिपर्षि विदथे विचर्षणे ।यः शूरसाता परितक्म्ये धने दभ्रेभिश्चित्समृता हंसि भूयसः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ vṛjiná-vartanim ǀ náram ǀ sákman ǀ piparṣi ǀ vidáthe ǀ vi-carṣaṇe ǀyáḥ ǀ śū́ra-sātā ǀ pári-takmye ǀ dháne ǀ dabhrébhiḥ ǀ cit ǀ sám-ṛtā ǀ háṃsi ǀ bhū́yasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, thou savest in the synod when pursued e’en him, farseeing One! who walks in evil ways. Thou, when the heroes fight for spoil which men rush, round, slayest in war the many by the hands of few.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, excellently wise, you direct the man who follows improper paths, to acts that are fitted to reclaim him; you who, in the strife of heroes, (grateful to them) as widely- scattered wealth, destryed in the combat the mighty by the feeble.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, thou savest in the synod when pursued e’en him, farseeing One! who walks in evil ways. Thou, when the heroes fight for spoil which men rush, round, slayest in war the many by the hands of few.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तमग्ने अमृतत्व उत्तमे मर्तं दधासि श्रवसे दिवेदिवे ।यस्तातृषाण उभयाय जन्मने मयः कृणोषि प्रय आ च सूरये ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tám ǀ agne ǀ amṛta-tvé ǀ ut-tamé ǀ mártam ǀ dadhāsi ǀ śrávase ǀ divé-dive ǀyáḥ ǀ tatṛṣāṇáḥ ǀ ubháyāya ǀ jánmane ǀ máyaḥ ǀ kṛṇóṣi ǀ práyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ sūráye ǁ
verses.english_translation: For glory, Agni, day by day, thou liftest up the mortal man to highest immortality, Even thou who yearning for both races givest them great bliss, and to the prince grantest abundant food.
verses.wilson_translation: You sustain,Agni, that mortal (who worships you), in the best immortality by daily food; you bestow on the sage, who is desirous (of creatures) of both kinds of birth, happiness and sustenance.
verses.griffith_verse: For glory, Agni, day by day, thou liftest up the mortal man to highest immortality, Even thou who yearning for both races givest them great bliss, and to the prince grantest abundant food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो अग्ने सनये धनानां यशसं कारुं कृणुहि स्तवानः ।ऋध्याम कर्मापसा नवेन देवैर्द्यावापृथिवी प्रावतं नः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sanáye ǀ dhánānām ǀ yaśásam ǀ kārúm ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ stávānaḥ ǀṛdhyā́ma ǀ kárma ǀ apásā ǀ návena ǀ deváiḥ ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ prá ǀ avatam ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, highly lauded, make our singer famous that he may win us store of riches: May we improve the rite with new performance. O Earth and Heaven, with all the Gods, protect us.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are praised by us for the sake of wealth, render illustrious the performer of the rite; may we improve the act by a new offspring (given by you). Preserve us, heaven and earth, along with the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, highly lauded, make our singer famous that he may win us store of riches: May we improve the rite with new performance. O Earth and Heaven, with all the Gods, protect us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो अग्ने पित्रोरुपस्थ आ देवो देवेष्वनवद्य जागृविः ।तनूकृद्बोधि प्रमतिश्च कारवे त्वं कल्याण वसु विश्वमोपिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ ā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ anavadya ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀtanū-kṛ́t ǀ bodhi ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ ca ǀ kāráve ǀ tvám ǀ kalyāṇa ǀ vásu ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ ūpiṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: O blameless Agni lying in thy Parents' lap, a God among the Gods, be watchful for our good. Former of bodies, be the singer's Providence: all good things hast thou sown for him, auspicious One!
verses.wilson_translation: Irreproachable Agni, a vigilant god amongst the gods, (abiding) in the proximity of (your) parents, and bestowing upon us embodied  (progeny), aweke us. Be well disposed to the offerer of the oblation; for you, auspicious Agni, grant all riches.
verses.griffith_verse: O blameless Agni lying in thy Parents' lap, a God among the Gods, be watchful for our good. Former of bodies, be the singer's Providence: all good things hast thou sown for him, auspicious One!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने प्रमतिस्त्वं पितासि नस्त्वं वयस्कृत्तव जामयो वयं ।सं त्वा रायः शतिनः सं सहस्रिणः सुवीरं यंति व्रतपामदाभ्य ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ tvám ǀ pitā́ ǀ asi ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ vayaḥ-kṛ́t ǀ táva ǀ jāmáyaḥ ǀ vayám ǀsám ǀ tvā ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ śatínaḥ ǀ sám ǀ sahasríṇaḥ ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ yanti ǀ vrata-pā́m ǀ adābhya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, thou art our Providence, our Father thou: we are thy brethren and thou art our spring of life. In thee, rich in good heroes, guard of high decrees, meet hundred, thousand treasures, O infallible!
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are well disposed to us, you are our protector, you are the giver of life to us; we are your kinsmen. Uninjurable Agni, hundreds and thousands of treasures belong to you, who are the defender of pious acts and attended by good men.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, thou art our Providence, our Father thou: we are thy brethren and thou art our spring of life. In thee, rich in good heroes, guard of high decrees, meet hundred, thousand treasures, O infallible!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामग्ने प्रथममायुमायवे देवा अकृण्वन्नहुषस्य विश्पतिं ।इळामकृण्वन्मनुषस्य शासनीं पितुर्यत्पुत्रो ममकस्य जायते ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ prathamám ǀ āyúm ǀ āyáve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ akṛṇvan ǀ náhuṣasya ǀ viśpátim ǀíḷām ǀ akṛṇvan ǀ mánuṣasya ǀ śā́sanīm ǀ pitúḥ ǀ yát ǀ putráḥ ǀ mámakasya ǀ jā́yate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, Agni, have the Gods made the first living One for living man, Lord of the house of Nahuṣa. Iḷā they made the teacher of the sons of men, what time a Son was born to the father of my race.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods formerly made you,Agni, the living genitive ral of the mortal Nahuṣa; they made Iḷā, the instrumental uctress of Manu, when the son of my father was born.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, Agni, have the Gods made the first living One for living man, Lord of the house of Nahuṣa. Iḷā they made the teacher of the sons of men, what time a Son was born to the father of my race.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो अग्ने तव देव पायुभिर्मघोनो रक्ष तन्वश्च वंद्य ।त्राता तोकस्य तनये गवामस्यनिमेषं रक्षमाणस्तव व्रते ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ deva ǀ pāyú-bhiḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ rakṣa ǀ tanváḥ ǀ ca ǀ vandya ǀtrātā́ ǀ tokásya ǀ tánaye ǀ gávām ǀ asi ǀ áni-meṣam ǀ rákṣamāṇaḥ ǀ táva ǀ vraté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worthy to be revered, O Agni, God, preserve our wealthy patrons with thy succours, and ourselves. Guard of our seed art thou, aiding our cows to bear, incessantly protecting in thy holy way.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are worthy to be praised, preserve us who are opulent with your bounties, and also the person ns (of our sons); you are the defender of cattle for the son of my son, who is ever assiduous in your worship.
verses.griffith_verse: Worthy to be revered, O Agni, God, preserve our wealthy patrons with thy succours, and ourselves. Guard of our seed art thou, aiding our cows to bear, incessantly protecting in thy holy way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने यज्यवे पायुरंतरोऽनिषंगाय चतुरक्ष इध्यसे ।यो रातहव्योऽवृकाय धायसे कीरेश्चिन्मंत्रं मनसा वनोषि तं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ yájyave ǀ pāyúḥ ǀ ántaraḥ ǀ aniṣaṅgā́ya ǀ catuḥ-akṣáḥ ǀ idhyase ǀyáḥ ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ avṛkā́ya ǀ dhā́yase ǀ kīréḥ ǀ cit ǀ mántram ǀ mánasā ǀ vanóṣi ǀ tám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, thou art a guard close to the pious man; kindled art thou, four-eyed! for him who is unarmed. With fond heart thou acceptest e’en the poor man's prayer, when he hath brought his gift to gain security.
verses.wilson_translation: Your, four-eyed Agni, blaze as the protector of the worshipper, who are athandfor the (security of the) uninterrupted (rite); you cherish in your mind the prayer of your adorer, who offers the oblation to you, the harmless, the benevolent.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, thou art a guard close to the pious man; kindled art thou, four-eyed! for him who is unarmed. With fond heart thou acceptest e’en the poor man's prayer, when he hath brought his gift to gain security.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्न उरुशंसाय वाघते स्पार्हं यद्रेक्णः परमं वनोषि तत् ।आध्रस्य चित्प्रमतिरुच्यसे पिता प्र पाकं शास्सि प्र दिशो विदुष्टरः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ uru-śáṃsāya ǀ vāgháte ǀ spārhám ǀ yát ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ paramám ǀ vanóṣi ǀ tát ǀādhrásya ǀ cit ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ ucyase ǀ pitā́ ǀ prá ǀ pā́kam ǀ śā́ssi ǀ prá ǀ díśaḥ ǀ vidúḥ-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni gainest for the loudly-praising priest the highest wealth, the object of a man's desire. Thou art called Father, caring even for the weak, and wisest, to the simple one thou teachest lore.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, desire (that the worshipper may acquire) that excellent wealth which is reqquisite for the many-commended priest; you are called the well-intentioned protector. You, who are all-wise, instrumental ucted the disciple, and (define) the points of the horizon.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni gainest for the loudly-praising priest the highest wealth, the object of a man's desire. Thou art called Father, caring even for the weak, and wisest, to the simple one thou teachest lore.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने प्रयतदक्षिणं नरं वर्मेव स्यूतं परि पासि विश्वतः ।स्वादुक्षद्मा यो वसतौ स्योनकृज्जीवयाजं यजते सोपमा दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ práyata-dakṣiṇam ǀ náram ǀ várma-iva ǀ syūtám ǀ pári ǀ pāsi ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀsvādu-kṣádmā ǀ yáḥ ǀ vasatáu ǀ syona-kṛ́t ǀ jīva-yājám ǀ yájate ǀ sáḥ ǀ upa-mā́ ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the man who giveth guerdon to the priests, like well-sewn armour thou guardest on every side. He who with grateful food shows kindness in his house, an offerer to the living, is the type of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, you dend the man who gives presents (to the priests) on every side, like well-stitched armour. The man who keeps choice viands in his dwelling, and with them entertains (his guests), performs the sacrifice of life, and is the likeness of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, the man who giveth guerdon to the priests, like well-sewn armour thou guardest on every side. He who with grateful food shows kindness in his house, an offerer to the living, is the type of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् ।आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानां ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ agne ǀ śaráṇim ǀ mīmṛṣaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ imám ǀ ádhvānam ǀ yám ǀ ágāma ǀ dūrā́t ǀāpíḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ somyā́nām ǀ bhṛ́miḥ ǀ asi ǀ ṛṣi-kṛ́t ǀ mártyānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pardon, we pray, this sin of ours, O Agni,—the path which we have trodden, widely straying, Dear Friend and Father, caring for the pious, who speedest nigh and who inspirest mortals.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, forgive us this our negligence, this path in which we have gone astray; you are to be sought as the protector and encourager of those who offer suitable libations; you are the fulfiller (of the end of rites), you make yourself visible to mortals.
verses.griffith_verse: Pardon, we pray, this sin of ours, O Agni,—the path which we have trodden, widely straying, Dear Friend and Father, caring for the pious, who speedest nigh and who inspirest mortals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मनुष्वदग्ने अंगिरस्वदंगिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्छुचे ।अच्छ याह्या वहा दैव्यं जनमा सादय बर्हिषि यक्षि च प्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: manuṣvát ǀ agne ǀ aṅgirasvát ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ yayāti-vát ǀ sádane ǀ pūrva-vát ǀ śuce ǀáccha ǀ yāhi ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǀ ā́ ǀ sādaya ǀ barhíṣi ǀ yákṣi ǀ ca ǀ priyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As erst to Manus, to Yayāti, Aṅgiras, so Aṅgiras! pure Agni! come thou to our hall. Bring hither the celestial host and seat them here upon the sacred grass, and offer what they love.
verses.wilson_translation: Pure Agni, who goes about (to receive oblations), go in your presence to the halll of sacrifice, as did Manu, and Aṅgiras, and Yayāti, and others of old; bring hither the divine personnages, seat them on the sacred grass, and offer them grateful (sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: As erst to Manus, to Yayāti, Aṅgiras, so Aṅgiras! pure Agni! come thou to our hall. Bring hither the celestial host and seat them here upon the sacred grass, and offer what they love.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व शक्ती वा यत्ते चकृमा विदा वा ।उत प्र णेष्यभि वस्यो अस्मान्त्सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या ॥
verses.transliteration: eténa ǀ agne ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ vavṛdhasva ǀ śáktī ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ cakṛmá ǀ vidā́ ǀ vā ǀutá ǀ prá ǀ neṣi ǀ abhí ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ sám ǀ naḥ ǀ sṛja ǀ su-matyā́ ǀ vā́ja-vatyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: By this our prayer be thou, O Agni, strengthened, prayer made by us after our power and knowledge. Lead thou us, therefore, to increasing riches; endow us with thy strength-bestowing favour.
verses.wilson_translation: .Agni, do your thrive through this our prayer, which we make according to our ability, according to our knowledge; do you, therefore, lead us to opulence, and endow us with right understanding securing (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: By this our prayer be thou, O Agni, strengthened, prayer made by us after our power and knowledge. Lead thou us, therefore, to increasing riches; endow us with thy strength-bestowing favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: I WILL declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder.He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents. He slew the Dragon lying on the mountain: his heavenly bolt of thunder Tvaṣṭar fashioned.Like lowing kine in rapid flow descending the waters glided downward to the ocean. Impetuous as a bull, he chose the Soma and in three sacred beakers drank the juices.Maghavan grasped the thunder for his weapon, and smote to death this firstborn of the dragons. When, Indra, thou hadst slain the dragon's firstborn, and overcome the charms of the enchanters,Then, giving life to Sun and Dawn and Heaven, thou foundest not one foe to stand against thee. Indra with his own great and deadly thunder smote into pieces Vṛtra, worst of Vṛtras.As trunks of trees, what time the axe hath felled them, low on the earth so lies the prostrate Dragon. He, like a mad weak warrior, challenged Indra, the great impetuous many-slaying Hero.He, brooking not the clashing of the weapons, crushed—Indra's foe—the shattered forts in falling. Footless and handless still he challenged Indra, who smote him with his bolt between the shoulders.Emasculate yet claiming manly vigour, thus Vṛtra lay with scattered limbs dissevered. There as he lies like a bank-bursting river, the waters taking courage flow above him.The Dragon lies beneath the feet of torrents which Vṛtra with his greatness had encompassed. Then humbled was the strength of Vṛtra's mother: Indra hath cast his deadly bolt against her.The mother was above, the son was under and like a cow beside her calf lay Danu. Rolled in the midst of never-ceasing currents flowing without a rest for ever onward.The waters bear off Vṛtra's nameless body: the foe of Indra sank to during darkness. Guarded by Ahi stood the thralls of Dāsas, the waters stayed like kine held by the robber.But he, when he had smitten Vṛtra, opened the cave wherein the floods had been imprisoned. A horse's tail wast thou when he, O Indra, smote on thy bolt; thou, God without a second,Thou hast won back the kine, hast won the Soma; thou hast let loose to flow the Seven Rivers. Nothing availed him lightning, nothing thunder, hailstorm or mist which had spread around him:When Indra and the Dragon strove in battle, Maghavan gained the victory for ever. Whom sawest thou to avenge the Dragon, Indra, that fear possessed thy heart when thou hadst slain him;That, like a hawk affrighted through the regions, thou crossedst nine-and-ninety flowing rivers? Indra is King of all that moves and moves not, of creatures tame and horned, the Thunder-wielder.Over all living men he rules as Sovran, containing all as spokes within the felly.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यानि चकार प्रथमानि वज्री ।अहन्नहिमन्वपस्ततर्द प्र वक्षणा अभिनत्पर्वतानां ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ nú ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ prá ǀ vocam ǀ yā́ni ǀ cakā́ra ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ vajrī́ ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ ánu ǀ apáḥ ǀ tatarda ǀ prá ǀ vakṣáṇāḥ ǀ abhinat ǀ párvatānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: I WILL declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
verses.wilson_translation: I declare the former valorous deeds of Indra, which the thunderer has achieved; he clove the cloud; he cast the waters down (to earth); he broke (a way) for the torrents of the mountain.
verses.griffith_verse: I WILL declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष ।वाश्रा इव धेनवः स्यंदमाना अंजः समुद्रमव जग्मुरापः ॥
verses.transliteration: áhan ǀ áhim ǀ párvate ǀ śiśriyāṇám ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ asmai ǀ vájram ǀ svaryám ǀ tatakṣa ǀvāśrā́ḥ-iva ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ syándamānāḥ ǀ áñjaḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ áva ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He slew the Dragon lying on the mountain: his heavenly bolt of thunder Tvaṣṭar fashioned. Like lowing kine in rapid flow descending the waters glided downward to the ocean.
verses.wilson_translation: He clove the cloud, seeking refuge on the mountain;Tvaṣṭa) sharpened his far-whirling bolt; the flowing waters quickly hastened to the ocean, like cows (hastening) to their calves.
verses.griffith_verse: He slew the Dragon lying on the mountain: his heavenly bolt of thunder Tvaṣṭar fashioned. Like lowing kine in rapid flow descending the waters glided downward to the ocean.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषायमाणोऽवृणीत सोमं त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्य ।आ सायकं मघवादत्त वज्रमहन्नेनं प्रथमजामहीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛṣa-yámāṇaḥ ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ sómam ǀ trí-kadrukeṣu ǀ apibat ǀ sutásya ǀā́ ǀ sā́yakam ǀ maghávā ǀ adatta ǀ vájram ǀ áhan ǀ enam ǀ prathama-jā́m ǀ áhīnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Impetuous as a bull, he chose the Soma and in three sacred beakers drank the juices. Maghavan grasped the thunder for his weapon, and smote to death this firstborn of the dragons.
verses.wilson_translation: Impetuous as a bull, he quaffed the Somajuice, he drank of the libation at the triple sacrifice. Maghvan took his shaft, the thunderbolt, and with it struck the first born of the clouds.
verses.griffith_verse: Impetuous as a bull, he chose the Soma and in three sacred beakers drank the juices. Maghavan grasped the thunder for his weapon, and smote to death this firstborn of the dragons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राहन्प्रथमजामहीनामान्मायिनाममिनाः प्रोत मायाः ।आत्सूर्यं जनयन्द्यामुषासं तादीत्ना शत्रुं न किला विवित्से ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ áhan ǀ prathama-jā́m ǀ áhīnām ǀ ā́t ǀ māyínām ǀ ámināḥ ǀ prá ǀ utá ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀā́t ǀ sū́ryam ǀ janáyan ǀ dyā́m ǀ uṣásam ǀ tādī́tnā ǀ śátrum ǀ ná ǀ kíla ǀ vivitse ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Indra, thou hadst slain the dragon's firstborn, and overcome the charms of the enchanters, Then, giving life to Sun and Dawn and Heaven, thou foundest not one foe to stand against thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch,Indra, as you have divided the first-born of the clouds, you have destroyed the delusions of the deluders, and then engendering the sun, the dawn, the firmament, you have not left an enemy (to oppose you).
verses.griffith_verse: When, Indra, thou hadst slain the dragon's firstborn, and overcome the charms of the enchanters, Then, giving life to Sun and Dawn and Heaven, thou foundest not one foe to stand against thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहन्वृत्रं वृत्रतरं व्यंसमिंद्रो वज्रेण महता वधेन ।स्कंधांसीव कुलिशेना विवृक्णाहिः शयत उपपृक्पृथिव्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: áhan ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vṛtra-táram ǀ ví-aṃsam ǀ índraḥ ǀ vájreṇa ǀ mahatā́ ǀ vadhéna ǀskándhāṃsi-iva ǀ kúliśena ǀ ví-vṛkṇā ǀ áhiḥ ǀ śayate ǀ upa-pṛ́k ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra with his own great and deadly thunder smote into pieces Vṛtra, worst of Vṛtras. As trunks of trees, what time the axe hath felled them, low on the earth so lies the prostrate Dragon.
verses.wilson_translation: With his vast destroying thunderbolt,Indrastruck the darkling mutilated Vṛtra; as the trunks of trees are felled by the axe, so lies Ahi prostrate on the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra with his own great and deadly thunder smote into pieces Vṛtra, worst of Vṛtras. As trunks of trees, what time the axe hath felled them, low on the earth so lies the prostrate Dragon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयोद्धेव दुर्मद आ हि जुह्वे महावीरं तुविबाधमृजीषं ।नातारीदस्य समृतिं वधानां सं रुजानाः पिपिष इंद्रशत्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayoddhā́-iva ǀ duḥ-mádaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ juhvé ǀ mahā-vīrám ǀ tuvi-bādhám ǀ ṛjīṣám ǀná ǀ atārīt ǀ asya ǀ sám-ṛtim ǀ vadhā́nām ǀ sám ǀ rujā́nāḥ ǀ pipiṣe ǀ índra-śatruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, like a mad weak warrior, challenged Indra, the great impetuous many-slaying Hero. He, brooking not the clashing of the weapons, crushed—Indra's foe—the shattered forts in falling.
verses.wilson_translation: The arrogant Vṛtra, as if unequaled, defied Indra, the mighty hero, the destroyer of many, the scatterer of foes; he has not escaped the contact of the fate (Indra's) enemies. The foe of Indra has crushed the (banks of the) rivers.
verses.griffith_verse: He, like a mad weak warrior, challenged Indra, the great impetuous many-slaying Hero. He, brooking not the clashing of the weapons, crushed—Indra's foe—the shattered forts in falling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपादहस्तो अपृतन्यदिंद्रमास्य वज्रमधि सानौ जघान ।वृष्णो वध्रिः प्रतिमानं बुभूषन्पुरुत्रा वृत्रो अशयद्व्यस्तः ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́t ǀ ahastáḥ ǀ apṛtanyat ǀ índram ǀ ā́ ǀ asya ǀ vájram ǀ ádhi ǀ sā́nau ǀ jaghāna ǀvṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ vádhriḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ búbhūṣan ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ vṛtráḥ ǀ aśayat ǀ ví-astaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Footless and handless still he challenged Indra, who smote him with his bolt between the shoulders. Emasculate yet claiming manly vigour, thus Vṛtra lay with scattered limbs dissevered.
verses.wilson_translation: Having neitherhandnor foot, he defied Indra, who struck him with the thunderbolt upon his mountain-like shoulder, like one emasculated who pretends to virility; then Vṛtra, mutilated of many members, slept.
verses.griffith_verse: Footless and handless still he challenged Indra, who smote him with his bolt between the shoulders. Emasculate yet claiming manly vigour, thus Vṛtra lay with scattered limbs dissevered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नदं न भिन्नममुया शयानं मनो रुहाणा अति यंत्यापः ।याश्चिद्वृत्रो महिना पर्यतिष्ठत्तासामहिः पत्सुतःशीर्बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: nadám ǀ ná ǀ bhinnám ǀ amuyā́ ǀ śáyānam ǀ mánaḥ ǀ rúhāṇāḥ ǀ áti ǀ yanti ǀ ā́paḥ ǀyā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ vṛtráḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ pari-átiṣṭhat ǀ tā́sām ǀ áhiḥ ǀ patsutaḥśī́ḥ ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: There as he lies like a bank-bursting river, the waters taking courage flow above him. The Dragon lies beneath the feet of torrents which Vṛtra with his greatness had encompassed.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters, that delight the minds (of men), flow over him, recumbent on this earth, as a river (bursts through) its broken (banks). Ahi has been prostrated beneath the feet of the waters, which Vṛtra, by his might, had obstructed.
verses.griffith_verse: There as he lies like a bank-bursting river, the waters taking courage flow above him. The Dragon lies beneath the feet of torrents which Vṛtra with his greatness had encompassed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नीचावया अभवद्वृत्रपुत्रेंद्रो अस्या अव वधर्जभार ।उत्तरा सूरधरः पुत्र आसीद्दानुः शये सहवत्सा न धेनुः ॥
verses.transliteration: nīcā́-vayāḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ vṛtrá-putrā ǀ índraḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ áva ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ jabhāra ǀút-tarā ǀ sū́ḥ ǀ ádharaḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ dā́nuḥ ǀ śaye ǀ sahá-vatsā ǀ ná ǀ dhenúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then humbled was the strength of Vṛtra's mother: Indra hath cast his deadly bolt against her. The mother was above, the son was under and like a cow beside her calf lay Danu.
verses.wilson_translation: The mother of Vṛtrawas bending over her son, when Indrastruck her nether part with his shaft; so the mother was above and the son underneath, and Dānuslept (with her son), like  a cow with its calf.
verses.griffith_verse: Then humbled was the strength of Vṛtra's mother: Indra hath cast his deadly bolt against her. The mother was above, the son was under and like a cow beside her calf lay Danu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतिष्ठंतीनामनिवेशनानां काष्ठानां मध्ये निहितं शरीरं ।वृत्रस्य निण्यं वि चरंत्यापो दीर्घं तम आशयदिंद्रशत्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: átiṣṭhantīnām ǀ ani-veśanā́nām ǀ kā́ṣṭhānām ǀ mádhye ǀ ní-hitam ǀ śárīram ǀvṛtrásya ǀ niṇyám ǀ ví ǀ caranti ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ dīrghám ǀ támaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aśayat ǀ índra-śatruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rolled in the midst of never-ceasing currents flowing without a rest for ever onward. The waters bear off Vṛtra's nameless body: the foe of Indra sank to during darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters carry off the nameless body of Vṛtra, tossed into the midst of the never- stopping, never-resting currents. The foe of Indrahas slept a long darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Rolled in the midst of never-ceasing currents flowing without a rest for ever onward. The waters bear off Vṛtra's nameless body: the foe of Indra sank to during darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दासपत्नीरहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः ।अपां बिलमपिहितं यदासीद्वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अप तद्ववार ॥
verses.transliteration: dāsá-patnīḥ ǀ áhi-gopāḥ ǀ atiṣṭhan ǀ ní-ruddhāḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ paṇínā-iva ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀapā́m ǀ bílam ǀ ápi-hitam ǀ yát ǀ ā́sīt ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ ápa ǀ tát ǀ vavāra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Guarded by Ahi stood the thralls of Dāsas, the waters stayed like kine held by the robber. But he, when he had smitten Vṛtra, opened the cave wherein the floods had been imprisoned.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters, the wives of the destroyer, guarded by Ahi, stood obstructed, like the cows by Paṇis; but by laying Vṛtra,Indraset open the cave that had confined them.
verses.griffith_verse: Guarded by Ahi stood the thralls of Dāsas, the waters stayed like kine held by the robber. But he, when he had smitten Vṛtra, opened the cave wherein the floods had been imprisoned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्व्यो वारो अभवस्तदिंद्र सृके यत्त्वा प्रत्यहन्देव एकः ।अजयो गा अजयः शूर सोममवासृजः सर्तवे सप्त सिंधून् ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvyaḥ ǀ vā́raḥ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ tát ǀ indra ǀ sṛké ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ prati-áhan ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀájayaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ájayaḥ ǀ śūra ǀ sómam ǀ áva ǀ asṛjaḥ ǀ sártave ǀ saptá ǀ síndhūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: A horse's tail wast thou when he, O Indra, smote on thy bolt; thou, God without a second, Thou hast won back the kine, hast won the Soma; thou hast let loose to flow the Seven Rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: When the single resplendent Vṛtrareturned the blow (which had been inflicted),Indra, by your thunderbolt, you became (furious), like a horse's tail. You have rescued the kine; you have won, Hero, the Somajuice; you have let loose the seven rivers to flow.
verses.griffith_verse: A horse's tail wast thou when he, O Indra, smote on thy bolt; thou, God without a second, Thou hast won back the kine, hast won the Soma; thou hast let loose to flow the Seven Rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नास्मै विद्युन्न तन्यतुः सिषेध न यां मिहमकिरद्ध्रादुनिं च ।इंद्रश्च यद्युयुधाते अहिश्चोतापरीभ्यो मघवा वि जिग्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ asmai ǀ vi-dyút ǀ ná ǀ tanyatúḥ ǀ sisedha ǀ ná ǀ yā́m ǀ míham ǀ ákirat ǀ hrādúnim ǀ ca ǀíndraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ yuyudhā́te íti ǀ áhiḥ ǀ ca ǀ utá ǀ aparī́bhyaḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ ví ǀ jigye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nothing availed him lightning, nothing thunder, hailstorm or mist which had spread around him: When Indra and the Dragon strove in battle, Maghavan gained the victory for ever.
verses.wilson_translation: Neither the lightning nor the thunder (discharged by Vṛtra), nor the rain which he showered, nor the thunderbolt, harmed Indra, when he and Ahi contended and Maghvat triumphed also over other (attacks).
verses.griffith_verse: Nothing availed him lightning, nothing thunder, hailstorm or mist which had spread around him: When Indra and the Dragon strove in battle, Maghavan gained the victory for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहेर्यातारं कमपश्य इंद्र हृदि यत्ते जघ्नुषो भीरगच्छत् ।नव च यन्नवतिं च स्रवंतीः श्येनो न भीतो अतरो रजांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: áheḥ ǀ yātā́ram ǀ kám ǀ apaśyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ hṛdí ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ jaghnúṣaḥ ǀ bhī́ḥ ǀ ágacchat ǀnáva ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ srávantīḥ ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhītáḥ ǀ átaraḥ ǀ rájāṃsi ǁ
