verses.english_translation: Whom sawest thou to avenge the Dragon, Indra, that fear possessed thy heart when thou hadst slain him; That, like a hawk affrighted through the regions, thou crossedst nine-and-ninety flowing rivers?
verses.wilson_translation: When fear entered,Indra, into your heart when about to slay Ahi, what other destroyer of him did you look for, that, alarmed, you did traverse ninety and nine streams like a (swift) hawk?
verses.griffith_verse: Whom sawest thou to avenge the Dragon, Indra, that fear possessed thy heart when thou hadst slain him; That, like a hawk affrighted through the regions, thou crossedst nine-and-ninety flowing rivers?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो यातोऽवसितस्य राजा शमस्य च शृंगिणो वज्रबाहुः ।सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनामरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ yātáḥ ǀ áva-sitasya ǀ rā́jā ǀ śámasya ǀ ca ǀ śṛṅgíṇaḥ ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ rā́jā ǀ kṣayati ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ arā́n ǀ ná ǀ nemíḥ ǀ pári ǀ tā́ ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra is King of all that moves and moves not, of creatures tame and horned, the Thunder-wielder. Over all living men he rules as Sovran, containing all as spokes within the felly.
verses.wilson_translation: Then Indra, the wilder of the thunderbolt, became the sovereign of all that is moveable or immoveable, of hornless and horned cattle; and as he abides the monarch of men, he comprehended all things (within him), as the circumference comprehends the spokes of a wheel.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra is King of all that moves and moves not, of creatures tame and horned, the Thunder-wielder. Over all living men he rules as Sovran, containing all as spokes within the felly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: Come, fain for booty let us seek to Indra: yet more shall he increase his care that guides us.Will not the Indestructible endow us with perfect knowledge of this wealth, of cattle? I fly to him invisible Wealth-giver as flies the falcon to his cherished eyrie,With fairest hymns of praise adoring Indra, whom those who laud him must invoke in battle. Mid all his host, he bindeth on the quiver: he driveth cattle from what foe he pleaseth:Gathering up great store of riches, Indra. be thou no trafficker with us, most mighty. Thou slewest with thy bolt the wealthy Dasyu, alone, yet going with thy helpers, Indra!Far from the floor of heaven in all directions, the ancient riteless ones fled to destruction. Fighting with pious worshippers, the riteless turned and fled, Indra! with averted faces.When thou, fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, the Stayer, blewest from earth and heaven and sky the godless. They met in fight the army of the blameless: then the Navagvas put forth all their power.They, like emasculates with men contending, fled, conscious, by steep paths from Indra, scattered. Whether they weep or laugh, thou hast o’erthrown them, O Indra, on the sky's extremest limit.The Dasyu thou hast burned from heaven, and welcomed the prayer of him who pours the juice and lauds thee. Adorned with their array of gold and jewels, they o’er the earth a covering veil extended.Although they hastened, they o’ercame not Indra: their spies he compassed with the Sun of morning. As thou enjoyest heaven and earth, O Indra, on every side surrounded with thy greatness,So thou with priests hast blown away the Dasyu, and those who worship not with those who worship. They who pervaded earth's extremest limit subdued not with their charms the Wealth-bestower:Indra, the Bull, made his ally the thunder, and with its light milked cows from out the darkness. The waters flowed according to their nature; he raid the navigable streams waxed mighty.Then Indra, with his spirit concentrated, smote him for ever with his strongest weapon. Indra broke through Ilībiśa's strong castles, and Śuṣṇa with his horn he cut to pieces:Thou, Maghavan, for all his might and swiftness, slewest thy fighting foeman with thy thunder Fierce on his enemies fell Indra's weapon: with. his sharp bull he rent their forts in pieces.He with his thunderbolt dealt blows on Vṛtra; and conquered, executing all his purpose. Indra, thou helpest Kutsa whom thou lovedst, and guardedst brave Daśadyu when he battled,The dust of trampling horses rose to heaven, and Śvitrā's son stood up again for conquest. Śvitrā's mild steer, O Maghavan thou helpest in combat for the land, mid Tugra's houses.Long stood they there before the task was ended: thou wast the master of the foemen's treasure.

verses.sanskrit: एतायामोप गव्यंत इंद्रमस्माकं सु प्रमतिं वावृधाति ।अनामृणः कुविदादस्य रायो गवां केतं परमावर्जते नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ita ǀ áyāma ǀ úpa ǀ gavyántaḥ ǀ índram ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sú ǀ prá-matim ǀ vavṛdhāti ǀanāmṛṇáḥ ǀ kuvít ǀ ā́t ǀ asyá ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ gávām ǀ kétam ǀ páram ǀ ā-várjate ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, fain for booty let us seek to Indra: yet more shall he increase his care that guides us. Will not the Indestructible endow us with perfect knowledge of this wealth, of cattle?
verses.wilson_translation: Come, let us get to Indra, (to recover our stolen cattle), for he, devoid of malice, exhilarates our minds; thereupon he will bestow upon us perfect knowledge of this wealth, (which consists) of kine.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, fain for booty let us seek to Indra: yet more shall he increase his care that guides us. Will not the Indestructible endow us with perfect knowledge of this wealth, of cattle?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपेदहं धनदामप्रतीतं जुष्टां न श्येनो वसतिं पतामि ।इंद्रं नमस्यन्नुपमेभिरर्कैर्यः स्तोतृभ्यो हव्यो अस्ति यामन् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ ít ǀ ahám ǀ dhana-dā́m ǀ áprati-itam ǀ júṣṭām ǀ ná ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ vasatím ǀ patāmi ǀíndram ǀ namasyán ǀ upa-mébhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ yā́man ǁ
verses.english_translation: I fly to him invisible Wealth-giver as flies the falcon to his cherished eyrie, With fairest hymns of praise adoring Indra, whom those who laud him must invoke in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: I fly, like a hawk to its cherished nest, to that Indrawho is to be invoked by his worshipper in battle, glorifying with excellent hymns, him who is invincible and the giver of wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: I fly to him invisible Wealth-giver as flies the falcon to his cherished eyrie, With fairest hymns of praise adoring Indra, whom those who laud him must invoke in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि सर्वसेन इषुधीँरसक्त समर्यो गा अजति यस्य वष्टि ।चोष्कूयमाण इंद्र भूरि वामं मा पणिर्भूरस्मदधि प्रवृद्ध ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ sárva-senaḥ ǀ iṣu-dhī́n ǀ asakta ǀ sám ǀ aryáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ajati ǀ yásya ǀ váṣṭi ǀcoṣkūyámāṇaḥ ǀ indra ǀ bhū́ri ǀ vāmám ǀ mā́ ǀ paṇíḥ ǀ bhūḥ ǀ asmát ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-vṛddha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mid all his host, he bindeth on the quiver: he driveth cattle from what foe he pleaseth: Gathering up great store of riches, Indra. be thou no trafficker with us, most mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: The commander fo the whole host has bound his quiver (on his back); the lord drives the cattle (to the dwelling) of whom he plural ases. Mighty Indra, bestowing upon us abundant wealth, take not advantage of us like a dealer.
verses.griffith_verse: Mid all his host, he bindeth on the quiver: he driveth cattle from what foe he pleaseth: Gathering up great store of riches, Indra. be thou no trafficker with us, most mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वधीर्हि दस्युं धनिनं घनेनँ एकश्चरन्नुपशाकेभिरिंद्र ।धनोरधि विषुणक्ते व्यायन्नयज्वानः सनकाः प्रेतिमीयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: vádhīḥ ǀ hí ǀ dásyum ǀ dhanínam ǀ ghanéna ǀ ékaḥ ǀ cáran ǀ upa-śākébhiḥ ǀ indra ǀdhánoḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ viṣuṇák ǀ té ǀ ví ǀ āyan ǀ áyajvānaḥ ǀ sanakā́ḥ ǀ prá-itim ǀ īyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou slewest with thy bolt the wealthy Dasyu, alone, yet going with thy helpers, Indra! Far from the floor of heaven in all directions, the ancient riteless ones fled to destruction.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily,Indra, you have slain the wealthy barbarian with your bold; your, singly assailing (him), although with auxiliaries (the Maruts) athand. Perceiving the impending manifold destructiveness of your bow, they, the Sanakas, the neglecters of sacrifice, perished.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou slewest with thy bolt the wealthy Dasyu, alone, yet going with thy helpers, Indra! Far from the floor of heaven in all directions, the ancient riteless ones fled to destruction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा चिच्छीर्षा ववृजुस्त इंद्रायज्वानो यज्वभिः स्पर्धमानाः ।प्र यद्दिवो हरिवः स्थातरुग्र निरव्रताँ अधमो रोदस्योः ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ cit ǀ śīrṣā́ ǀ vavṛjuḥ ǀ té ǀ indra ǀ áyajvānaḥ ǀ yájva-bhiḥ ǀ spárdhamānāḥ ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ diváḥ ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ sthātaḥ ǀ ugra ǀ níḥ ǀ avratā́n ǀ adhamaḥ ǀ ródasyoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fighting with pious worshippers, the riteless turned and fled, Indra! with averted faces. When thou, fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, the Stayer, blewest from earth and heaven and sky the godless.
verses.wilson_translation: The neglecters of sacrifice, contending with the sacrificers,Indra, fled with averted faces. Indra, fierce, unyielding, lord of steeds, (they appeared) when you did blow the disregarders of religion from off the heaven, and earth and sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Fighting with pious worshippers, the riteless turned and fled, Indra! with averted faces. When thou, fierce Lord of the Bay Steeds, the Stayer, blewest from earth and heaven and sky the godless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयुयुत्सन्ननवद्यस्य सेनामयातयंत क्षितयो नवग्वाः ।वृषायुधो न वध्रयो निरष्टाः प्रवद्भिरिंद्राच्चितयंत आयन् ॥
verses.transliteration: áyuyutsan ǀ anavadyásya ǀ sénām ǀ áyātayanta ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ náva-gvāḥ ǀvṛṣa-yúdhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vádhrayaḥ ǀ níḥ-aṣṭāḥ ǀ pravát-bhiḥ ǀ índrāt ǀ citáyantaḥ ǀ āyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: They met in fight the army of the blameless: then the Navagvas put forth all their power. They, like emasculates with men contending, fled, conscious, by steep paths from Indra, scattered.
verses.wilson_translation: (The adherants of Vṛtra) encountered the army of the irreproachable (Indra); men of holy lives encouraged him. Scattered before him, conscious (of their inferiority), like the emasculated contending with men, they fled by precipitous paths.
verses.griffith_verse: They met in fight the army of the blameless: then the Navagvas put forth all their power. They, like emasculates with men contending, fled, conscious, by steep paths from Indra, scattered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमेतान्रुदतो जक्षतश्चायोधयो रजस इंद्र पारे ।अवादहो दिव आ दस्युमुच्चा प्र सुन्वतः स्तुवतः शंसमावः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ etā́n ǀ rudatáḥ ǀ jákṣataḥ ǀ ca ǀ áyodhayaḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ indra ǀ pāré ǀáva ǀ adahaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dásyum ǀ uccā́ ǀ prá ǀ sunvatáḥ ǀ stuvatáḥ ǀ śáṃsam ǀ āvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether they weep or laugh, thou hast o’erthrown them, O Indra, on the sky's extremest limit. The Dasyu thou hast burned from heaven, and welcomed the prayer of him who pours the juice and lauds thee.
verses.wilson_translation: You have destroyed them,Indra, whether weeping or laughing, on the farthest verge of the sky; you have consumed the robber, (having dragged him) from heaven, and have received the praises of the worshipper, praising you and offering libations.
verses.griffith_verse: Whether they weep or laugh, thou hast o’erthrown them, O Indra, on the sky's extremest limit. The Dasyu thou hast burned from heaven, and welcomed the prayer of him who pours the juice and lauds thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चक्राणासः परीणहं पृथिव्या हिरण्येन मणिना शुंभमानाः ।न हिन्वानासस्तितिरुस्त इंद्रं परि स्पशो अदधात्सूर्येण ॥
verses.transliteration: cakrāṇā́saḥ ǀ pari-náham ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ híraṇyena ǀ maṇínā ǀ śúmbhamānāḥ ǀná ǀ hinvānā́saḥ ǀ titiruḥ ǀ té ǀ índram ǀ pári ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ adadhāt ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adorned with their array of gold and jewels, they o’er the earth a covering veil extended. Although they hastened, they o’ercame not Indra: their spies he compassed with the Sun of morning.
verses.wilson_translation: Decorated with gold and jewels, they were spreading over the circuit of the earth; but mighty as they were, they triumphed not over Indra; he dispersed them with the (rising) sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Adorned with their array of gold and jewels, they o’er the earth a covering veil extended. Although they hastened, they o’ercame not Indra: their spies he compassed with the Sun of morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परि यदिंद्र रोदसी उभे अबुभोजीर्महिना विश्वतः सीं ।अमन्यमानाँ अभि मन्यमानैर्निर्ब्रह्मभिरधमो दस्युमिंद्र ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ábubhojīḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ sīm ǀámanyamānān ǀ abhí ǀ mányamānaiḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ brahmá-bhiḥ ǀ adhamaḥ ǀ dásyum ǀ indra ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou enjoyest heaven and earth, O Indra, on every side surrounded with thy greatness, So thou with priests hast blown away the Dasyu, and those who worship not with those who worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, as you enjoy both heaven and earth, investing the universe with your magnitude, you have blown away the robber with the prayers which are repeated on behalf of those who do not comprehend them.
verses.griffith_verse: As thou enjoyest heaven and earth, O Indra, on every side surrounded with thy greatness, So thou with priests hast blown away the Dasyu, and those who worship not with those who worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न ये दिवः पृथिव्या अंतमापुर्न मायाभिर्धनदां पर्यभूवन् ।युजं वज्रं वृषभश्चक्र इंद्रो निर्ज्योतिषा तमसो गा अदुक्षत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yé ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ántam ǀ āpúḥ ǀ ná ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ dhana-dā́m ǀ pari-ábhūvan ǀyújam ǀ vájram ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ cakre ǀ índraḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ támasaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ adhukṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who pervaded earth's extremest limit subdued not with their charms the Wealth-bestower: Indra, the Bull, made his ally the thunder, and with its light milked cows from out the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: When the waters descended not upon the ends of the earth, and overspread not that giver of affluence with its productions, then Indra, the showerer, grasped his bolt, and with its brightness milked out the waters from the darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: They who pervaded earth's extremest limit subdued not with their charms the Wealth-bestower: Indra, the Bull, made his ally the thunder, and with its light milked cows from out the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनु स्वधामक्षरन्नापो अस्यावर्धत मध्य आ नाव्यानां ।सध्रीचीनेन मनसा तमिंद्र ओजिष्ठेन हन्मनाहन्नभि द्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ svadhā́m ǀ akṣaran ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ asya ǀ ávardhata ǀ mádhye ǀ ā́ ǀ nāvyā́nām ǀsadhrīcī́nena ǀ mánasā ǀ tám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ójiṣṭhena ǀ hánmanā ǀ ahan ǀ abhí ǀ dyū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: The waters flowed according to their nature; he raid the navigable streams waxed mighty. Then Indra, with his spirit concentrated, smote him for ever with his strongest weapon.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters flowed to provide the food of Indra, but (Vṛtra) increased in the midst of the navigable (rivers); then Indra, with his fatal and powerful shaft, slew Vṛtra, whose thought were ever turned towards him.
verses.griffith_verse: The waters flowed according to their nature; he raid the navigable streams waxed mighty. Then Indra, with his spirit concentrated, smote him for ever with his strongest weapon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृंगिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिंद्रः ।यावत्तरो मघवन्यावदोजो वज्रेण शत्रुमवधीः पृतन्युं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ avidhyat ǀ ilībíśasya ǀ dṛḷhā́ ǀ ví ǀ śṛṅgíṇam ǀ abhinat ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ índraḥ ǀyā́vat ǀ táraḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ yā́vat ǀ ójaḥ ǀ vájreṇa ǀ śátrum ǀ avadhīḥ ǀ pṛtanyúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra broke through Ilībiśa's strong castles, and Śuṣṇa with his horn he cut to pieces: Thou, Maghavan, for all his might and swiftness, slewest thy fighting foeman with thy thunder
verses.wilson_translation: Indraset free (the waters) obstructed by (Vṛtra), when sleeping in the caves of the earth, and slew the horned dryer up (of the world). You,Maghavan, with equal swiftness and strength, did kill with your thunderbolt the enemy defying you to battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra broke through Ilībiśa's strong castles, and Śuṣṇa with his horn he cut to pieces: Thou, Maghavan, for all his might and swiftness, slewest thy fighting foeman with thy thunder
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि सिध्मो अजिगादस्य शत्रून्वि तिग्मेन वृषभेणा पुरोऽभेत् ।सं वज्रेणासृजद्वृत्रमिंद्रः प्र स्वां मतिमतिरच्छाशदानः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ sidhmáḥ ǀ ajigāt ǀ asya ǀ śátrūn ǀ ví ǀ tigména ǀ vṛṣabhéṇa ǀ púraḥ ǀ abhet ǀsám ǀ vájreṇa ǀ asṛjat ǀ vṛtrám ǀ índraḥ ǀ prá ǀ svā́m ǀ matím ǀ atirat ǀ śā́śadānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce on his enemies fell Indra's weapon: with. his sharp bull he rent their forts in pieces. He with his thunderbolt dealt blows on Vṛtra; and conquered, executing all his purpose.
verses.wilson_translation: The weapon of Indrafell upon his adversaries; with his sharp and excellent (shaft) he destroyed their cities; he then reached Vṛtrawith his thunderbolt, and (by) slaying him, exhilarated his mind.
verses.griffith_verse: Fierce on his enemies fell Indra's weapon: with. his sharp bull he rent their forts in pieces. He with his thunderbolt dealt blows on Vṛtra; and conquered, executing all his purpose.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आवः कुत्समिंद्र यस्मिञ्चाकन्प्रावो युध्यंतं वृषभं दशद्युं ।शफच्युतो रेणुर्नक्षत द्यामुच्छ्वैत्रेयो नृषाह्याय तस्थौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́vaḥ ǀ kútsam ǀ indra ǀ yásmin ǀ cākán ǀ prá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ yúdhyantam ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ dáśa-dyum ǀśaphá-cyutaḥ ǀ reṇúḥ ǀ nakṣata ǀ dyā́m ǀ út ǀ śvaitreyáḥ ǀ nṛ-sáhyāya ǀ tasthau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, thou helpest Kutsa whom thou lovedst, and guardedst brave Daśadyu when he battled, The dust of trampling horses rose to heaven, and Śvitrā's son stood up again for conquest.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, have protected Kutsa, grateful for his praises; you have defended the excellent Daśadyuengaged in battle; the dust of your courser's hoofs ascended to heaven; the son of Śvita, (through your favour), rose up, to be again unborn by men.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, thou helpest Kutsa whom thou lovedst, and guardedst brave Daśadyu when he battled, The dust of trampling horses rose to heaven, and Śvitrā's son stood up again for conquest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आवः शमं वृषभं तुग्र्यासु क्षेत्रजेषे मघवञ्छ्वित्र्यं गां ।ज्योक् चिदत्र तस्थिवांसो अक्रञ्छत्रूयतामधरा वेदनाकः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́vaḥ ǀ śámam ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ túgryāsu ǀ kṣetra-jeṣé ǀ magha-van ǀ śvítryam ǀ gā́m ǀjyók ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀ tasthi-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ akran ǀ śatru-yatā́m ǀ ádharā ǀ védanā ǀ akarítyakaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Śvitrā's mild steer, O Maghavan thou helpest in combat for the land, mid Tugra's houses. Long stood they there before the task was ended: thou wast the master of the foemen's treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: You have protected,Maghavan, the excellent son of Śvitā, when combating for his lands, and encouraged (by you) when immersed in water; do you inflict sharp pains on those of hostile minds, who have long stood (in enmity) against us.
verses.griffith_verse: Śvitrā's mild steer, O Maghavan thou helpest in combat for the land, mid Tugra's houses. Long stood they there before the task was ended: thou wast the master of the foemen's treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIV. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: Ye who observe this day be with us even thrice: far-stretching is you bounty, Aśvins and your course.To you, as to a cloak in winter, we cleave close: you are to be drawn nigh unto us by the wise. Three are the fellies in your honey-bearing car, that travels after Soma's loved one, as all know.Three are the pillars set upon it for support: thrice journey ye by night, O Aśvins, thrice by day. Thrice in the self-same day, ye Gods who banish want, sprinkle ye thrice to-day our sacrifice with meath;And thrice vouchsafe us store of food with plenteous strength, at evening, O ye Aśvins, and at break of day. Thrice come ye to our home, thrice to the righteous folk, thrice triply aid the man who well deserves your help.Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring us what shall make us glad; thrice send us store of food as nevermore to fail. Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring to us abundant wealth: thrice in the Gods’ assembly, thrice assist our thoughts.Thrice, grant ye us prosperity, thrice grant us fame; for the Sun's daughter hath mounted your three-wheeled car. Thrice, Aśvins, grant to us the heavenly medicines, thrice those of earth and thrice those that the waters hold,Favour and health and strength bestow upon my son; triple protection, Lords of Splendour, grant to him. Thrice are ye to be worshipped day by day by us: thrice, O ye Aśvins, ye travel around the earth.Car-borne from far away, O ye Nāsatyas, come, like vital air to bodies, come ye to the three. Thrice, O ye Aśvins, with the Seven Mother Streams; three are the jars, the triple offering is prepared.Three are the worlds, and moving on above the sky ye guard the firm-set vault of heaven through days and nights. Where are the three wheels of your triple chariot, where are the three seats thereto firmly fastened?When will ye yoke the mighty ass that draws it, to bring you to our sacrifice. Nāsatyas? Nāsatyas, come: the sacred gift is offered up; drink the sweet juice with lips that know the sweetness well.Savitar sends, before the dawn of day, your car, fraught with oil, various-coloured, to our sacrifice. Come, O Nāsatyas, with the thrice-eleven Gods; come, O ye Aśvins, to the drinking of the meath.Make long our days of life, and wipe out all our sins: ward off our enemies; be with us evermore. Borne in your triple car, O Aśvins, bring us present prosperity with noble offspring.I cry to you who hear me for protection be ye our helpers where men win the booty.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिश्चिन्नो अद्या भवतं नवेदसा विभुर्वां याम उत रातिरश्विना ।युवोर्हि यंत्रं हिम्येव वाससोऽभ्यायंसेन्या भवतं मनीषिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ cit ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ bhavatam ǀ navedasā ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ vām ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ utá ǀ rātíḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀyuvóḥ ǀ hí ǀ yantrám ǀ himyā́-iva ǀ vā́sasaḥ ǀ abhi-āyaṃsényā ǀ bhavatam ǀ manīṣí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye who observe this day be with us even thrice: far-stretching is you bounty, Aśvins and your course. To you, as to a cloak in winter, we cleave close: you are to be drawn nigh unto us by the wise.
verses.wilson_translation: Wise Aśvins, be present with us thrice today; vast is your vehicle, as well as your munificence; your union is like that of the shining (day) and dewy (night); (suffer yourselves) to be detained by the learned (priests).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye who observe this day be with us even thrice: far-stretching is you bounty, Aśvins and your course. To you, as to a cloak in winter, we cleave close: you are to be drawn nigh unto us by the wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रयः पवयो मधुवाहने रथे सोमस्य वेनामनु विश्व इद्विदुः ।त्रयः स्कंभासः स्कभितास आरभे त्रिर्नक्तं याथस्त्रिर्वश्विना दिवा ॥
verses.transliteration: tráyaḥ ǀ paváyaḥ ǀ mádhu-vā́hane ǀ ráthe ǀ sómasya ǀ venā́m ǀ ánu ǀ víśve ǀ ít ǀ viduḥ ǀtráyaḥ ǀ skambhā́saḥ ǀ skabhitā́saḥ ǀ ā-rábhe ǀ tríḥ ǀ náktam ǀ yātháḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ aśvinā ǀ dívā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Three are the fellies in your honey-bearing car, that travels after Soma's loved one, as all know. Three are the pillars set upon it for support: thrice journey ye by night, O Aśvins, thrice by day.
verses.wilson_translation: Three are the solid (wheels) of your abundance-bearing chariot, as all (the gods) have known (it to be), when attendant on Vena, the beloved of Soma; three are the columns plural ced (above it) for support, and in it thrice do you journey by night, and thrice by day.
verses.griffith_verse: Three are the fellies in your honey-bearing car, that travels after Soma's loved one, as all know. Three are the pillars set upon it for support: thrice journey ye by night, O Aśvins, thrice by day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समाने अहन्त्रिरवद्यगोहना त्रिरद्य यज्ञं मधुना मिमिक्षतं ।त्रिर्वाजवतीरिषो अश्विना युवं दोषा अस्मभ्यमुषसश्च पिन्वतं ॥
verses.transliteration: samāné ǀ áhan ǀ tríḥ ǀ avadya-gohanā ǀ tríḥ ǀ adyá ǀ yajñám ǀ mádhunā ǀ mimikṣatam ǀtríḥ ǀ vā́ja-vatīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuvám ǀ doṣā́ḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pinvatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice in the self-same day, ye Gods who banish want, sprinkle ye thrice to-day our sacrifice with meath; And thrice vouchsafe us store of food with plenteous strength, at evening, O ye Aśvins, and at break of day.
verses.wilson_translation: Thrice in one entire day do you repair the faults (of your worshippers); thrice today sprinkle the oblation with sweetness; and thrice, evening and morning,Aśvins, grant us strength-bestowing food.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice in the self-same day, ye Gods who banish want, sprinkle ye thrice to-day our sacrifice with meath; And thrice vouchsafe us store of food with plenteous strength, at evening, O ye Aśvins, and at break of day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातं त्रिरनुव्रते जने त्रिः सुप्राव्ये त्रेधेव शिक्षतं ।त्रिर्नांद्यं वहतमश्विना युवं त्रिः पृक्षो अस्मे अक्षरेव पिन्वतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ vartíḥ ǀ yātam ǀ tríḥ ǀ ánu-vrate ǀ jáne ǀ tríḥ ǀ supra-avyé ǀ tredhā́-iva ǀ śikṣatam ǀtríḥ ǀ nāndyám ǀ vahatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuvám ǀ tríḥ ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ akṣárā-iva ǀ pinvatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice come ye to our home, thrice to the righteous folk, thrice triply aid the man who well deserves your help. Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring us what shall make us glad; thrice send us store of food as nevermore to fail.
verses.wilson_translation: Thrice,Aśvins, visit our dwelling, and the man who is well-disposed towards us; thrice repair to him who deserves your protection, and instrumental uct us in three-fold knowledge; thrice grant us gratifying (rewards); thrice shower upon us food, as (Indrapours down) rain.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice come ye to our home, thrice to the righteous folk, thrice triply aid the man who well deserves your help. Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring us what shall make us glad; thrice send us store of food as nevermore to fail.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिर्नो रयिं वहतमश्विना युवं त्रिर्देवताता त्रिरुतावतं धियः ।त्रिः सौभगत्वं त्रिरुत श्रवांसि नस्त्रिष्ठं वां सूरे दुहिता रुहद्रथं ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ vahatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuvám ǀ tríḥ ǀ devá-tātā ǀ tríḥ ǀ utá ǀ avatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀtríḥ ǀ saubhaga-tvám ǀ tríḥ ǀ utá ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀ naḥ ǀ tri-sthám ǀ vām ǀ sū́re ǀ duhitā́ ǀ ā ǀ ruhat ǀ rátham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring to us abundant wealth: thrice in the Gods’ assembly, thrice assist our thoughts. Thrice, grant ye us prosperity, thrice grant us fame; for the Sun's daughter hath mounted your three-wheeled car.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, thrice bestow upon us riches; thrice approach the divine rite; thrice preserve our intellects; thrice grant us prosperity, thrice food. The daughter of the sun has ascended your three-wheeled car.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, bring to us abundant wealth: thrice in the Gods’ assembly, thrice assist our thoughts. Thrice, grant ye us prosperity, thrice grant us fame; for the Sun's daughter hath mounted your three-wheeled car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिर्नो अश्विना दिव्यानि भेषजा त्रिः पार्थिवानि त्रिरु दत्तमद्भ्यः ।ओमानं शंयोर्ममकाय सूनवे त्रिधातु शर्म वहतं शुभस्पती ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ divyā́ni ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀ tríḥ ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ tríḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dattam ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀomā́nam ǀ śam-yóḥ ǀ mámakāya ǀ sūnáve ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ śárma ǀ vahatam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice, Aśvins, grant to us the heavenly medicines, thrice those of earth and thrice those that the waters hold, Favour and health and strength bestow upon my son; triple protection, Lords of Splendour, grant to him.
verses.wilson_translation: Thrice grant us,Aśvins, the medicaments of heaven, and those of earth, and those of the firmament; give to my son the prosperity ofŚamyu; cherishers of wholesome (herbs), preserve the well-being of the three humours (of the body).
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice, Aśvins, grant to us the heavenly medicines, thrice those of earth and thrice those that the waters hold, Favour and health and strength bestow upon my son; triple protection, Lords of Splendour, grant to him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिर्नो अश्विना यजता दिवेदिवे परि त्रिधातु पृथिवीमशायतं ।तिस्रो नासत्या रथ्या परावत आत्मेव वातः स्वसराणि गच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ yajatā́ ǀ divé-dive ǀ pári ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ aśāyatam ǀtisráḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ rathyā ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ātmā́-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ svásarāṇi ǀ gacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice are ye to be worshipped day by day by us: thrice, O ye Aśvins, ye travel around the earth. Car-borne from far away, O ye Nāsatyas, come, like vital air to bodies, come ye to the three.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, who are to be thrice worshipped, day by day, repose on the triple (couch of) sacred grass upon the earth, (that form the altar); car-borne Nāsatyas, repair from afar to the threefold (plural ce of sacrifice), as the vital air to (living) bodies.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice are ye to be worshipped day by day by us: thrice, O ye Aśvins, ye travel around the earth. Car-borne from far away, O ye Nāsatyas, come, like vital air to bodies, come ye to the three.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिरश्विना सिंधुभिः सप्तमातृभिस्त्रय आहावास्त्रेधा हविष्कृतं ।तिस्रः पृथिवीरुपरि प्रवा दिवो नाकं रक्षेथे द्युभिरक्तुभिर्हितं ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ síndhu-bhiḥ ǀ saptámātṛ-bhiḥ ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ ā-hāvā́ḥ ǀ tredhā́ ǀ havíḥ ǀ kṛtám ǀtisráḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ḥ ǀ upári ǀ pravā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ nā́kam ǀ rakṣethe íti ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ hitám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, with the Seven Mother Streams; three are the jars, the triple offering is prepared. Three are the worlds, and moving on above the sky ye guard the firm-set vault of heaven through days and nights.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Aśvins, thrice with the seven mother-sttreams; the three rivers are ready; the triple oblation is prepared; rising above thethree worlds, you defend the sun in the sky, who is established for both night and day.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice, O ye Aśvins, with the Seven Mother Streams; three are the jars, the triple offering is prepared. Three are the worlds, and moving on above the sky ye guard the firm-set vault of heaven through days and nights.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व त्री चक्रा त्रिवृतो रथस्य क्व त्रयो वंधुरो ये सनीळाः ।कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ trī́ ǀ cakrā́ ǀ tri-vṛ́taḥ ǀ ráthasya ǀ kvá ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ vandhúraḥ ǀ yé ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀkadā́ ǀ yógaḥ ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ rā́sabhasya ǀ yéna ǀ yajñám ǀ nāsatyā ǀ upa-yātháḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where are the three wheels of your triple chariot, where are the three seats thereto firmly fastened? When will ye yoke the mighty ass that draws it, to bring you to our sacrifice. Nāsatyas?
verses.wilson_translation: Where,Nāsatyas, ae the three wheels of your triangular car? where the three fastenings and props (of the awning?) When will be the harnessing of the powerful ass, that you may come to the sacrifice?
verses.griffith_verse: Where are the three wheels of your triple chariot, where are the three seats thereto firmly fastened? When will ye yoke the mighty ass that draws it, to bring you to our sacrifice. Nāsatyas?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नासत्या गच्छतं हूयते हविर्मध्वः पिबतं मधुपेभिरासभिः ।युवोर्हि पूर्वं सवितोषसो रथमृताय चित्रं घृतवंतमिष्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ gácchatam ǀ hūyáte ǀ havíḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ pibatam ǀ madhu-pébhiḥ ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ hí ǀ pū́rvam ǀ savitā́ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ citrám ǀ ghṛtá-vantam ǀ íṣyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nāsatyas, come: the sacred gift is offered up; drink the sweet juice with lips that know the sweetness well. Savitar sends, before the dawn of day, your car, fraught with oil, various-coloured, to our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Nāsatyas, to the sacrifice; the oblation is offered; drink the juice with mouths that relish the sweet savour. Before dawn, even,Savitāsend (to bring you) to the rite, your wonderful car shining with clarified butter.
verses.griffith_verse: Nāsatyas, come: the sacred gift is offered up; drink the sweet juice with lips that know the sweetness well. Savitar sends, before the dawn of day, your car, fraught with oil, various-coloured, to our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नासत्या त्रिभिरेकादशैरिह देवेभिर्यातं मधुपेयमश्विना ।प्रायुस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ekādaśáiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ yātam ǀ madhu-péyam ǀ aśvinā ǀprá ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ tā́riṣṭam ǀ níḥ ǀ rápāṃsi ǀ mṛkṣatam ǀ sédhatam ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ bhávatam ǀ sacā-bhúvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, O Nāsatyas, with the thrice-eleven Gods; come, O ye Aśvins, to the drinking of the meath. Make long our days of life, and wipe out all our sins: ward off our enemies; be with us evermore.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Nāsatyas, with the thrice eleven divinities; come,Aśvins, to drink the oblation prolong our lives, efface our faults, restrain our enemies, and be ever with us.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, O Nāsatyas, with the thrice-eleven Gods; come, O ye Aśvins, to the drinking of the meath. Make long our days of life, and wipe out all our sins: ward off our enemies; be with us evermore.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो अश्विना त्रिवृता रथेनार्वांचं रयिं वहतं सुवीरं ।शृण्वंता वामवसे जोहवीमि वृधे च नो भवतं वाजसातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ tri-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀ arvā́ñcam ǀ rayím ǀ vahatam ǀ su-vī́ram ǀśṛṇvántā ǀ vām ǀ ávase ǀ johavīmi ǀ vṛdhé ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Borne in your triple car, O Aśvins, bring us present prosperity with noble offspring. I cry to you who hear me for protection be ye our helpers where men win the booty.
verses.wilson_translation: Borne in your car that traverses thethree worlds, bring to us Aśvins, present affluence, attended by (male) progeny; I call upon you both, listening to me, for protection; be to us for vigour in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Borne in your triple car, O Aśvins, bring us present prosperity with noble offspring. I cry to you who hear me for protection be ye our helpers where men win the booty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXV. Savitar.
hymns.anukramani: ११ हिरण्यस्तूप आङ्गिरसः। १ (पादानां क्रमेण) अग्निः, मित्रावरुणौ, रात्रिः, सविता च। २-११ सविता। त्रिष्टुप्, १, ९ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: AGNI I first invoke for our prosperity; I call on Mitra, Varuṇa, to aid us here.I call on Night who gives rest to all moving life; I call on Savitar the God to lend us help. Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal,Borne in his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God who looks on every creature. The God moves by the upward path, the downward; with two bright Bays, adorable, he journeys.Savitar comes, the God from the far distance, and chases from us all distress and sorrow. His chariot decked with pearl, of various colours, lofty, with golden pole, the God hath mounted,The many-rayed One, Savitar the holy, bound, bearing power and might, for darksome regions. Drawing the gold-yoked car his Bays, white-footed, have manifested light to all the peoples.Held in the lap of Savitar, divine One, all men, all beings have their place for ever. Three heavens there are; two Savitar's, adjacent: in Yama's world is one, the home of heroes,As on a linch-pin, firm, rest things immortal: he who hath known it let him here declare it. He, strong of wing, hath lightened up the regions, deep-quivering Asura, the gentle Leader.Where now is Sūrya, where is one to tell us to what celestial sphere his ray hath wandered? The earth's eight points his brightness hath illumined, three desert regions and the Seven Rivers.God Savitar the gold-eyed hath come hither, giving choice treasures unto him who worships. The golden-handed Savitar, far-seeing, goes on his way between the earth and heaven,Drives away sickness, bids the Sun approach us, and spreads the bright sky through the darksome region. May he, gold-handed Asura, kind Leader, come hither to us with his help and favour.Driving off Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the God is present, praised in hymns at evening. O Savitar, thine ancient dustless pathways are well established in the air's mid-region:O God, come by those paths so fair to travel, preserve thou us from harm this day, and bless us.

verses.sanskrit: ह्वयाम्यग्निं प्रथमं स्वस्तये ह्वयामि मित्रावरुणाविहावसे ।ह्वयामि रात्रीं जगतो निवेशनीं ह्वयामि देवं सवितारमूतये ॥
verses.transliteration: hváyāmi ǀ agním ǀ prathamám ǀ svastáye ǀ hváyāmi ǀ mitrā́váruṇau ǀ ihá ǀ ávase ǀhváyāmi ǀ rā́trīm ǀ jágataḥ ǀ ni-véśanīm ǀ hváyāmi ǀ devám ǀ savitā́ram ǀ ūtáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI I first invoke for our prosperity; I call on Mitra, Varuṇa, to aid us here. I call on Night who gives rest to all moving life; I call on Savitar the God to lend us help.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoke Agnifirst, for protection: I invoke for protection,Mitraand Varuṇa; invoke Night, who brings rest to the world; invoke the divine Savitāfor my preservation.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI I first invoke for our prosperity; I call on Mitra, Varuṇa, to aid us here. I call on Night who gives rest to all moving life; I call on Savitar the God to lend us help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ कृष्णेन रजसा वर्तमानो निवेशयन्नमृतं मर्त्यं च ।हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ kṛṣṇéna ǀ rájasā ǀ vártamānaḥ ǀ ni-veśáyan ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ mártyam ǀ ca ǀhiraṇyáyena ǀ savitā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ ā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ yāti ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ páśyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, Borne in his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God who looks on every creature.
verses.wilson_translation: Revolving through the darkened firmament, arousing mortal and immortal, the divine Savitātravels in his golden chariot, beholding the (several) worlds.
verses.griffith_verse: Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, Borne in his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God who looks on every creature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याति देवः प्रवता यात्युद्वता याति शुभ्राभ्यां यजतो हरिभ्यां ।आ देवो याति सविता परावतोऽप विश्वा दुरित�� बाधमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ti ǀ deváḥ ǀ pra-vátā ǀ yā́ti ǀ ut-vátā ǀ yā́ti ǀ śubhrā́bhyām ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ yāti ǀ savitā́ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ bā́dhamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The God moves by the upward path, the downward; with two bright Bays, adorable, he journeys. Savitar comes, the God from the far distance, and chases from us all distress and sorrow.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitātravels by an upward and by a downward path; deserving adoration, he journeys with two white horses; he comes hither from a distance, removing all sins.
verses.griffith_verse: The God moves by the upward path, the downward; with two bright Bays, adorable, he journeys. Savitar comes, the God from the far distance, and chases from us all distress and sorrow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभीवृतं कृशनैर्विश्वरूपं हिरण्यशम्यं यजतो बृहंतं ।आस्थाद्रथं सविता चित्रभानुः कृष्णा रजांसि तविषीं दधानः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí-vṛtam ǀ kṛ́śanaiḥ ǀ viśvá-rūpam ǀ híraṇya-śamyam ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ bṛhántam ǀā́ ǀ asthāt ǀ rátham ǀ savitā́ ǀ citrá-bhānuḥ ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ táviṣīm ǀ dádhānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: His chariot decked with pearl, of various colours, lofty, with golden pole, the God hath mounted, The many-rayed One, Savitar the holy, bound, bearing power and might, for darksome regions.
verses.wilson_translation: The many-rayed adorable Savitā, having power (to disperse) darkness from the world, has mounted his nigh-standing chariot, decorated with many kinds of golden ornaments, and furnished with golden yokes.
verses.griffith_verse: His chariot decked with pearl, of various colours, lofty, with golden pole, the God hath mounted, The many-rayed One, Savitar the holy, bound, bearing power and might, for darksome regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि जनाञ्छ्यावाः शितिपादो अख्यन्रथं हिरण्यप्रउगं वहंतः ।शश्वद्विशः सवितुर्दैव्यस्योपस्थे विश्वा भुवनानि तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ jánān ǀ śyāvā́ḥ ǀ śiti-pā́daḥ ǀ akhyan ǀ rátham ǀ híraṇya-pra_ugam ǀ váhantaḥ ǀśáśvat ǀ víśaḥ ǀ savitúḥ ǀ dáivyasya ǀ upá-sthe ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tasthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drawing the gold-yoked car his Bays, white-footed, have manifested light to all the peoples. Held in the lap of Savitar, divine One, all men, all beings have their place for ever.
verses.wilson_translation: His white-footed coursers, harnessed to his car with a golden yoke, have manifested light to manking. Men and all the regions are ever in the presence of divine Savitā.
verses.griffith_verse: Drawing the gold-yoked car his Bays, white-footed, have manifested light to all the peoples. Held in the lap of Savitar, divine One, all men, all beings have their place for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो द्यावः सवितुर्द्वा उपस्थाँ एका यमस्य भुवने विराषाट् ।आणिं न रथ्यममृताधि तस्थुरिह ब्रवीतु य उ तच्चिकेतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ savitúḥ ǀ dváu ǀ upá-sthā ǀ ékā ǀ yamásya ǀ bhúvane ǀ virāṣā́ṭ ǀāṇím ǀ ná ǀ ráthyam ǀ amṛ́tā ǀ ádhi ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ ihá ǀ bravītu ǀ yáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tát ǀ cíketat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Three heavens there are; two Savitar's, adjacent: in Yama's world is one, the home of heroes, As on a linch-pin, firm, rest things immortal: he who hath known it let him here declare it.
verses.wilson_translation: Three are the spheres; two are in the proximity of Savitā, one leads men to the dwelling of Yama. The immortal (luminaries) depend upon Savitā as a car upon the pin of the axle; let him who knows (the greatness of Savitā) declare it.
verses.griffith_verse: Three heavens there are; two Savitar's, adjacent: in Yama's world is one, the home of heroes, As on a linch-pin, firm, rest things immortal: he who hath known it let him here declare it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि सुपर्णो अंतरिक्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः ।क्वेदानीं सूर्यः कश्चिकेत कतमां द्यां रश्मिरस्या ततान ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ antárikṣāṇi ǀ akhyat ǀ gabhīrá-vepāḥ ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ su-nītháḥ ǀkvá ǀ idā́nīm ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ ciketa ǀ katamā́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ raśmíḥ ǀ asya ǀ ā́ ǀ tatāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, strong of wing, hath lightened up the regions, deep-quivering Asura, the gentle Leader. Where now is Sūrya, where is one to tell us to what celestial sphere his ray hath wandered?
verses.wilson_translation: Suparṇa, (the solar ray), deep-quivering, life-bestowing, well-directed, has illuminated the three regions. Where now is Sūrya Who knows to what sphere his rays have extended?
verses.griffith_verse: He, strong of wing, hath lightened up the regions, deep-quivering Asura, the gentle Leader. Where now is Sūrya, where is one to tell us to what celestial sphere his ray hath wandered?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अष्टौ व्यख्यत्ककुभः पृथिव्यास्त्री धन्व योजना सप्त सिंधून् ।हिरण्याक्षः सविता देव आगाद्दधद्रत्ना दाशुषे वार्याणि ॥
verses.transliteration: aṣṭáu ǀ ví ǀ akhyat ǀ kakúbhaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ trī́ ǀ dhánva ǀ yójanā ǀ saptá ǀ síndhūn ǀhiraṇya-akṣáḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ dádhat ǀ rátnā ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The earth's eight points his brightness hath illumined, three desert regions and the Seven Rivers. God Savitar the gold-eyed hath come hither, giving choice treasures unto him who worships.
verses.wilson_translation: He has lighted up the eight points of the horizon, the three regions of living beings, the seven rivers; may the golden-eyes Savitācome hither, bestowing upon the offerer of the oblation desirable riches.
verses.griffith_verse: The earth's eight points his brightness hath illumined, three desert regions and the Seven Rivers. God Savitar the gold-eyed hath come hither, giving choice treasures unto him who worships.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यपाणिः सविता विचर्षणिरुभे द्यावापृथिवी अंतरीयते ।अपामीवां बाधते वेति सूर्यमभि कृष्णेन रजसा द्यामृणोति ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-pāṇiḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ antáḥ ǀ īyate ǀápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ bā́dhate ǀ véti ǀ sū́ryam ǀ abhí ǀ kṛṣṇéna ǀ rájasā ǀ dyā́m ǀ ṛṇoti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The golden-handed Savitar, far-seeing, goes on his way between the earth and heaven, Drives away sickness, bids the Sun approach us, and spreads the bright sky through the darksome region.
verses.wilson_translation: The gold-handed, all-beholding,Savitātravels between the two regions of heaven and earth, dispels diseases, approaches the sun, and overspreads the sky with gloom, alternating radiance.
verses.griffith_verse: The golden-handed Savitar, far-seeing, goes on his way between the earth and heaven, Drives away sickness, bids the Sun approach us, and spreads the bright sky through the darksome region.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यहस्तो असुरः सुनीथः सुमृळीकः स्ववाँ यात्वर्वाङ् ।अपसेधन्रक्षसो यातुधानानस्थाद्देवः प्रतिदोषं गृणानः ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-hastaḥ ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ su-nītháḥ ǀ su-mṛḷīkáḥ ǀ svá-vān ǀ yātu ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀapa-sédhan ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ yātu-dhā́nān ǀ ásthāt ǀ deváḥ ǀ prati-doṣám ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he, gold-handed Asura, kind Leader, come hither to us with his help and favour. Driving off Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the God is present, praised in hymns at evening.
verses.wilson_translation: May the golden-handed, life-bestowing, well-guiding, exhilarating, and affluent Savitā, be present (at the sacrifice); for the deity, if worshipped in the evening, it athand, driving awayrākṣasandyātudhānas.
verses.griffith_verse: May he, gold-handed Asura, kind Leader, come hither to us with his help and favour. Driving off Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the God is present, praised in hymns at evening.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये ते पंथाः सवितः पूर्व्यासोऽरेणवः सुकृता अंतरिक्षे ।तेभिर्नो अद्य पथिभिः सुगेभी रक्षा च नो अधि च ब्रूहि देव ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ te ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ savitaríti ǀ pūrvyā́saḥ ǀ areṇávaḥ ǀ sú-kṛtāḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀtébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ su-gébhiḥ ǀ rákṣa ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ca ǀ brūhi ǀ deva ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Savitar, thine ancient dustless pathways are well established in the air's mid-region: O God, come by those paths so fair to travel, preserve thou us from harm this day, and bless us.
verses.wilson_translation: Your paths,Savitā, are prepared of old, and free from dust, and well plural ced in the firmament; (coming) by those paths easy to be traversed, preserve us today. Deity, speak to us.
verses.griffith_verse: O Savitar, thine ancient dustless pathways are well established in the air's mid-region: O God, come by those paths so fair to travel, preserve thou us from harm this day, and bless us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVI. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: २० कण्वो घौरः। अग्निः, १३-१४ यूपो वा। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समाः सतोबृहंत्यः (१३ उपरिष्टाद् बृहती। ऐ० ब्रा० २-२ चरणच्छेदः)
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WITH words sent forth in holy hymns, Agni we supplicate, the LordOf many families who duly serve the Gods, yea, him whom others also praise. Men have won Agni, him who makes their strength abound: we, with oblations, worship thee.Our gracious-minded Helper in our deeds of might, be thou, O Excellent, this day. Thee for our messenger we choose, thee, the Omniscient, for our Priest.The flames of thee the mighty are spread wide around: thy splendour reaches to the sky. The Gods enkindle thee their ancient messenger,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.That mortal man, O Agni, gains through thee all wealth, who hath poured offerings unto thee. Thou, Agni, art a cheering Priest, Lord of the House, men's messenger:All constant high decrees established by the Gods, gathered together, meet in thee. In thee, the auspicious One, O Agni, youthfullest, each sacred gift is offered up:This day, and after, gracious, worship thou our Gods, that we may have heroic sons. To him in his own splendour bright draw near in worship the devout.Men kindle Agni with their sacrificial gifts, victorious o’er the enemies. Vṛtra they smote and slew, and made the earth and heaven and firmament a wide abode.The glorious Bull, invoked, hath stood at Kaṇva's side: loud neighed the Steed in frays for kine. Seat thee, for thou art mighty; shine, best entertainer of the Gods.Worthy of sacred food, praised Agni! loose the smoke, ruddy and beautiful to see. Bearer of offerings, whom, best sacrificing Priest, the Gods for Manu's sake ordained;Whom Kaṇva, whom Medhyātithi made the source of wealth, and Vṛṣan and Upastuta. Him, Agni, whom Medhyātithi, whom Kaṇva kindled for his rite,Him these our songs of praise, him, Agni, we extol: his powers shine out preeminent. Make our wealth perfect thou, O Agni, Lord divine: for thou hast kinship with the Gods.Thou rulest as a King o’er widely-famous strength: be good to us, for thou art great. Stand up erect to lend us aid, stand up like Savitar the God:Erect as strength-bestower we call aloud, with unguents and with priests, on thee. Erect, preserve us from sore trouble; with thy flame burn thou each ravening demon dead.Raise thou us up that we may walk and live: so thou shalt find our worship mid the Gods. Preserve us, Agni, from the fiend, preserve us from malicious wrong.Save us from him who fain would injure us or slay, Most Youthful, thou with lofty light. Smite down as with a club, thou who hast fire for teeth, smite thou the wicked, right and left.Let not the man who plots against us in the night, nor any foe prevail o’er us. Agni hath given heroic might to Kaṇva, and felicity:Agni hath helped our friends, hath helped Medhyātithi, hath helped Upastuta to win. We call on Ugradeva, Yadu, Turvaśa, by means of Agni, from afar;Agni, bring Navavāstva and Bṛhadratha, Turvīti, to subdue the foe. Manu hath stablished thee a light, Agni, for all the race of men:Sprung from the Law, oil-fed, for Kaṇva hast thou blazed, thou whom the people reverence. The flames of Agni full of splendour and of might are fearful, not to be approached.Consume for ever all demons and sorcerers, consume thou each devouring fiend.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो यह्वं पुरूणां विशां देवयतीनां ।अग्निं सूक्तेभिर्वचोभिरीमहे यं सीमिदन्य ईळते ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ yahvám ǀ purūṇā́m ǀ viśā́m ǀ deva-yatī́nām ǀagním ǀ su-uktébhiḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ īmahe ǀ yám ǀ sīm ǀ ít ǀ anyé ǀ ī́ḷate ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH words sent forth in holy hymns, Agni we supplicate, the Lord Of many families who duly serve the Gods, yea, him whom others also praise.
verses.wilson_translation: We implore with sacred hymns the mighty Agni, whom other (ṛṣis) also praise, for the benefit of you who are many people, worshipping the gods of you who are many people, worshipping the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH words sent forth in holy hymns, Agni we supplicate, the Lord Of many families who duly serve the Gods, yea, him whom others also praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जनासो अग्निं दधिरे सहोवृधं हविष्मंतो विधेम ते ।स त्वं नो अद्य सुमना इहाविता भवा वाजेषु संत्य ॥
verses.transliteration: jánāsaḥ ǀ agním ǀ dadhire ǀ sahaḥ-vṛ́dham ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ te ǀsáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ihá ǀ avitā́ ǀ bháva ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ santya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men have won Agni, him who makes their strength abound: we, with oblations, worship thee. Our gracious-minded Helper in our deeds of might, be thou, O Excellent, this day.
verses.wilson_translation: Men have recourse to Agni, the augmenter of vigour; offering oblations, we worship you; do you liberal giver of food, be well disposed to us here this day, and be our protector.
verses.griffith_verse: Men have won Agni, him who makes their strength abound: we, with oblations, worship thee. Our gracious-minded Helper in our deeds of might, be thou, O Excellent, this day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र त्वा दूतं वृणीमहे होतारं विश्ववेदसं ।महस्ते सतो वि चरंत्यर्चयो दिवि स्पृशंति भानवः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tvā ǀ dūtám ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ hótāram ǀ viśvá-vedasam ǀmaháḥ ǀ te ǀ satáḥ ǀ ví ǀ caranti ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ diví ǀ spṛśanti ǀ bhānávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee for our messenger we choose, thee, the Omniscient, for our Priest. The flames of thee the mighty are spread wide around: thy splendour reaches to the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: We select you,Agni, the messenger and invoker of the gods, who are endowed with all knowledge. The flames of you, who are mighty and eternal, spread around the rays, touch of the heavens.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee for our messenger we choose, thee, the Omniscient, for our Priest. The flames of thee the mighty are spread wide around: thy splendour reaches to the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवासस्त्वा वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा सं दूतं प्रत्नमिंधते ।विश्वं सो अग्ने जयति त्वया धनं यस्ते ददाश मर्त्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́saḥ ǀ tvā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ sám ǀ dūtám ǀ pratnám ǀ indhate ǀvíśvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ agne ǀ jayati ǀ tváyā ǀ dhánam ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ dadā́śa ǀ mártyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods enkindle thee their ancient messenger,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. That mortal man, O Agni, gains through thee all wealth, who hath poured offerings unto thee.
verses.wilson_translation: The deities Varuṇa,Mitraand Aryamankindle you, (their) ancient messenger. The man who has offered you (oblations), obtains through you,Agni, universal wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods enkindle thee their ancient messenger,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. That mortal man, O Agni, gains through thee all wealth, who hath poured offerings unto thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंद्रो होता गृहपतिरग्ने दूतो विशामसि ।त्वे विश्वा संगतानि व्रता ध्रुवा यानि देवा अकृण्वत ॥
verses.transliteration: mandráḥ ǀ hótā ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ ágne ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ asi ǀtvé íti ǀ víśvā ǀ sám-gatāni ǀ vratā́ ǀ dhruvā́ ǀ yā́ni ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ákṛṇvata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni, art a cheering Priest, Lord of the House, men's messenger: All constant high decrees established by the Gods, gathered together, meet in thee.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are the giver of delight, the invoker and messenger of the gods, the domestic guardian of mankind; the good and durable actions which the gods perform are all aggregated in you.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni, art a cheering Priest, Lord of the House, men's messenger: All constant high decrees established by the Gods, gathered together, meet in thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे इदग्ने सुभगे यविष्ठ्य विश्वमा हूयते हविः ।स त्वं नो अद्य सुमना उतापरं यक्षि देवान्त्सुवीर्या ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ ít ǀ agne ǀ su-bháge ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ hūyate ǀ havíḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ utá ǀ aparám ǀ yákṣi ǀ devā́n ǀ su-vī́ryā ǁ
verses.english_translation: In thee, the auspicious One, O Agni, youthfullest, each sacred gift is offered up: This day, and after, gracious, worship thou our Gods, that we may have heroic sons.
verses.wilson_translation: Youthful and auspicious Agni, whatever oblation may be presented to you, do you, well disposed towards us; either now or at any other time, convey it to the powerful gods.
verses.griffith_verse: In thee, the auspicious One, O Agni, youthfullest, each sacred gift is offered up: This day, and after, gracious, worship thou our Gods, that we may have heroic sons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं घेमित्था नमस्विन उप स्वराजमासते ।होत्राभिरग्निं मनुषः समिंधते तितिर्वांसो अति स्रिधः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ gha ǀ īm ǀ itthā́ ǀ namasvínaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sva-rā́jam ǀ āsate ǀhótrābhiḥ ǀ agním ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ sám ǀ indhate ǀ titirvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ áti ǀ srídhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him in his own splendour bright draw near in worship the devout. Men kindle Agni with their sacrificial gifts, victorious o’er the enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: In this manner the devout adore you, who are such (as described), bright with your own radiance. Men, with (seven) ministrant priests, kindle Agni(with oblations), victorious over their enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: To him in his own splendour bright draw near in worship the devout. Men kindle Agni with their sacrificial gifts, victorious o’er the enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घ्नंतो वृत्रमतरन्रोदसी अप उरु क्षयाय चक्रिरे ।भुवत्कण्वे वृषा द्युम्न्याहुतः क्रंददश्वो गविष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: ghnántaḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ataran ǀ ródasī íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ urú ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ cakrire ǀbhúvat ǀ káṇve ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ dyumnī́ ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ krándat ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ gó-iṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vṛtra they smote and slew, and made the earth and heaven and firmament a wide abode. The glorious Bull, invoked, hath stood at Kaṇva's side: loud neighed the Steed in frays for kine.
verses.wilson_translation: The destroying (deities along with you) have slain Vṛtra; they have made earth and heaven and the firmament the spacious dwelling-plural ce (of living creatures); may Agni, possessed of wealth, when invoked, be a benefactor to Kaṇva, like a horse that neighs in a conflict for cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Vṛtra they smote and slew, and made the earth and heaven and firmament a wide abode. The glorious Bull, invoked, hath stood at Kaṇva's side: loud neighed the Steed in frays for kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं सीदस्व महाँ असि शोचस्व देववीतमः ।वि धूममग्ने अरुषं मियेध्य सृज प्रशस्त दर्शतं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ sīdasva ǀ mahā́n ǀ asi ǀ śócasva ǀ deva-vī́tamaḥ ǀví ǀ dhūmám ǀ agne ǀ aruṣám ǀ miyedhya ǀ sṛjá ǀ pra-śasta ǀ darśatám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seat thee, for thou art mighty; shine, best entertainer of the Gods. Worthy of sacred food, praised Agni! loose the smoke, ruddy and beautiful to see.
verses.wilson_translation: Take your seat,Agni, on the sacred grass, for you are mighty; shine forth, for you are devoted to the gods; adorable and excellent Agni, emit the moving and graceful smoke.
verses.griffith_verse: Seat thee, for thou art mighty; shine, best entertainer of the Gods. Worthy of sacred food, praised Agni! loose the smoke, ruddy and beautiful to see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं त्वा देवासो मनवे दधुरिह यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन ।यं कण्वो मेध्यातिथिर्धनस्पृतं यं वृषा यमुपस्तुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ mánave ǀ dadhúḥ ǀ ihá ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ havya-vāhana ǀyám ǀ káṇvaḥ ǀ médhya-atithiḥ ǀ dhana-spṛ́tam ǀ yám ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ yám ǀ upa-stutáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bearer of offerings, whom, best sacrificing Priest, the Gods for Manu's sake ordained; Whom Kaṇva, whom Medhyātithi made the source of wealth, and Vṛṣan and Upastuta.
verses.wilson_translation: Bearer of oblations, (you are he) whom the gods detained for the sake of Manu; whom, giver of wealth,Kaṇva, the host of pious guests, has detained; whom Indradetained, and whom (now) some other worshipper has detained.
verses.griffith_verse: Bearer of offerings, whom, best sacrificing Priest, the Gods for Manu's sake ordained; Whom Kaṇva, whom Medhyātithi made the source of wealth, and Vṛṣan and Upastuta.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमग्निं मेध्यातिथिः कण्व ईध ऋतादधि ।तस्य प्रेषो दीदियुस्तमिमा ऋचस्तमग्निं वर्धयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ agním ǀ médhya-atithiḥ ǀ káṇvaḥ ǀ īdhé ǀ ṛtā́t ǀ ádhi ǀtásya ǀ prá ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ dīdiyuḥ ǀ tám ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́caḥ ǀ tám ǀ agním ǀ vardhayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, Agni, whom Medhyātithi, whom Kaṇva kindled for his rite, Him these our songs of praise, him, Agni, we extol: his powers shine out preeminent.
verses.wilson_translation: The rays of that Agni, whom Kaṇvamade more brilliant than the sun, pre-eminently shine; him do these our hymns, him do we, extol.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, Agni, whom Medhyātithi, whom Kaṇva kindled for his rite, Him these our songs of praise, him, Agni, we extol: his powers shine out preeminent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रायस्पूर्धि स्वधावोऽस्ति हि तेऽग्ने देवेष्वाप्यं ।त्वं वाजस्य श्रुत्यस्य राजसि स नो मृळ महाँ असि ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyáḥ ǀ pūrdhi ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ devéṣu ǀ ā́pyam ǀtvám ǀ vā́jasya ǀ śrútyasya ǀ rājasi ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mṛḷa ǀ mahā́n ǀ asi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make our wealth perfect thou, O Agni, Lord divine: for thou hast kinship with the Gods. Thou rulest as a King o’er widely-famous strength: be good to us, for thou art great.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, giver of food, complete our treasures, for the friendship of the gods is obtainable through you. You are lord over famous viands; make us hapy, for you are great.
verses.griffith_verse: Make our wealth perfect thou, O Agni, Lord divine: for thou hast kinship with the Gods. Thou rulest as a King o’er widely-famous strength: be good to us, for thou art great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतये तिष्ठा देवो न सविता ।ऊर्ध्वो वाजस्य सनिता यदंजिभिर्वाघद्भिर्विह्वयामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ deváḥ ǀ ná ǀ savitā́ ǀūrdhváḥ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ sánitā ǀ yát ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ vāghát-bhiḥ ǀ vi-hváyāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Stand up erect to lend us aid, stand up like Savitar the God: Erect as strength-bestower we call aloud, with unguents and with priests, on thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Stand up erect for our protection, like the divine Savitā; erect, you are the giver of food, for which we invoke you with unguents, and priests (offering oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Stand up erect to lend us aid, stand up like Savitar the God: Erect as strength-bestower we call aloud, with unguents and with priests, on thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वो नः पाह्यंहसो नि केतुना विश्वं समत्रिणं दह ।कृधी न ऊर्ध्वाञ्चरथाय जीवसे विदा देवेषु नो दुवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ ní ǀ ketúnā ǀ víśvam ǀ sám ǀ atríṇam ǀ daha ǀkṛdhí ǀ naḥ ǀ ūrdhvā́n ǀ caráthāya ǀ jīváse ǀ vidā́ḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ naḥ ǀ dúvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Erect, preserve us from sore trouble; with thy flame burn thou each ravening demon dead. Raise thou us up that we may walk and live: so thou shalt find our worship mid the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Erect, preserve us by knowledge from sin; consume every malignant spirit; raise us aloft, that we may pass (through the world); and that we may live, convey our sealth (of oblations) to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Erect, preserve us from sore trouble; with thy flame burn thou each ravening demon dead. Raise thou us up that we may walk and live: so thou shalt find our worship mid the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पाहि नो अग्ने रक्षसः पाहि धूर्तेरराव्णः ।पाहि रीषत उत वा जिघांसतो बृहद्भानो यविष्ठ्य ॥
verses.transliteration: pāhí ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ dhūrtéḥ ǀ árāvṇaḥ ǀpāhí ǀ ríṣataḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ jíghāṃsataḥ ǀ bṛ́hadbhāno íti bṛ́hat-bhāno ǀ yáviṣṭhya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Preserve us, Agni, from the fiend, preserve us from malicious wrong. Save us from him who fain would injure us or slay, Most Youthful, thou with lofty light.
verses.wilson_translation: Youthful and most resplendent Agni, protect us against evil spirits, and from the malevolent (man), who gives no gifts; protect us from noxious (animals), and from those who seek to kill us.
verses.griffith_verse: Preserve us, Agni, from the fiend, preserve us from malicious wrong. Save us from him who fain would injure us or slay, Most Youthful, thou with lofty light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घनेव विष्वग्वि जह्यराव्णस्तपुर्जंभ यो अस्मध्रुक् ।यो मर्त्यः शिशीते अत्यक्तुभिर्मा नः स रिपुरीशत ॥
verses.transliteration: ghanā́-iva ǀ víṣvak ǀ ví ǀ jahi ǀ árāvṇaḥ ǀ tápuḥ-jambha ǀ yáḥ ǀ asma-dhrúk ǀyáḥ ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ śíśīte ǀ áti ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ripúḥ ǀ īśata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Smite down as with a club, thou who hast fire for teeth, smite thou the wicked, right and left. Let not the man who plots against us in the night, nor any foe prevail o’er us.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, with the burning rays, destroy entirely our foes, who make no gifts, as (potter's ware) with a club; let not one who is inimical to us, nor the man who attacks us with sharp weapons, prevail against us.
verses.griffith_verse: Smite down as with a club, thou who hast fire for teeth, smite thou the wicked, right and left. Let not the man who plots against us in the night, nor any foe prevail o’er us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्वव्ने सुवीर्यमग्निः कण्वाय सौभगं ।अग्निः प्रावन्मित्रोत मेध्यातिथिमग्निः साता उपस्तुतं ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ vavne ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ agníḥ ǀ káṇvāya ǀ sáubhagam ǀagníḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvat ǀ mitrā́ ǀ utá ǀ médhya-atithim ǀ agníḥ ǀ sātáu ǀ upa-stutám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni hath given heroic might to Kaṇva, and felicity: Agni hath helped our friends, hath helped Medhyātithi, hath helped Upastuta to win.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis solicited for power-conferring (affluence); he has granted prosperity to Kaṇva, he has protected our friends, as well as the (sage who was) the host of the holy and (every other) worshipper (who has had recourse to him) for riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni hath given heroic might to Kaṇva, and felicity: Agni hath helped our friends, hath helped Medhyātithi, hath helped Upastuta to win.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निना तुर्वशं यदुं परावत उग्रादेवं हवामहे ।अग्निर्नयन्नववास्त्वं बृहद्रथं तुर्वीतिं दस्यवे सहः ॥
verses.transliteration: agnínā ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ugrá-devam ǀ havāmahe ǀagníḥ ǀ nayat ǀ náva-vāstvam ǀ bṛhát-ratham ǀ turvī́tim ǀ dásyave ǀ sáhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call on Ugradeva, Yadu, Turvaśa, by means of Agni, from afar; Agni, bring Navavāstva and Bṛhadratha, Turvīti, to subdue the foe.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke from afar, along with Agni,Turvaśa,Yaduand Ugradeva; let Agni, the arrester of the robber, bring hither Navavāstu,Bṛhadrathaand Turvīti.
verses.griffith_verse: We call on Ugradeva, Yadu, Turvaśa, by means of Agni, from afar; Agni, bring Navavāstva and Bṛhadratha, Turvīti, to subdue the foe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि त्वामग्ने मनुर्दधे ज्योतिर्जनाय शश्वते ।दीदेथ कण्व ऋतजात उक्षितो यं नमस्यंति कृष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ mánuḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ jánāya ǀ śáśvate ǀdīdétha ǀ káṇve ǀ ṛtá-jātaḥ ǀ ukṣitáḥ ǀ yám ǀ namasyánti ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Manu hath stablished thee a light, Agni, for all the race of men: Sprung from the Law, oil-fed, for Kaṇva hast thou blazed, thou whom the people reverence.
verses.wilson_translation: Manudetained you,Agni, (to give) light to the various races of mankind. Born for the sake of sacrifice, and satiated with oblations, you, whom men reverence, have blazed for Kaṇva.
verses.griffith_verse: Manu hath stablished thee a light, Agni, for all the race of men: Sprung from the Law, oil-fed, for Kaṇva hast thou blazed, thou whom the people reverence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वेषासो अग्नेरमवंतो अर्चयो भीमासो न प्रतीतये ।रक्षस्विनः सदमिद्यातुमावतो विश्वं समत्रिणं दह ॥
verses.transliteration: tveṣā́saḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ áma-vantaḥ ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ bhīmā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ práti-itaye ǀrakṣasvínaḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ yātu-mā́vataḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ sám ǀ atríṇam ǀ daha ǁ
verses.english_translation: The flames of Agni full of splendour and of might are fearful, not to be approached. Consume for ever all demons and sorcerers, consume thou each devouring fiend.
verses.wilson_translation: The flames of Agniare luminous, powerful, fearful, and not to be trusted. Ever assuredly and entirely consume the mighty spirits of evil and all our other adversarieṣ
verses.griffith_verse: The flames of Agni full of splendour and of might are fearful, not to be approached. Consume for ever all demons and sorcerers, consume thou each devouring fiend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: SING forth, O Kaṇvas, to your band of Maruts unassailable,Sporting, resplendent on their car They who, self-luminous, were born together, with the spotted deer,Spears, swords, and glittering ornaments. One hears, as though ’twere close at hand, the cracking of the whips they holdThey gather glory on their way. Now sing ye forth the God-given hymn to your exultant Marut host,The fiercely-vigorous, the strong. Praise ye the Bull among the cows; for ’tis the Maruts’ sportive band:It strengthened as it drank the rain. Who is your mightiest, Heroes, when, O shakers of the earth and heaven,Ye shake them like a garment's hem? At your approach man holds him down before the fury of your wrath:The rugged-jointed mountain yields. They at whose racings forth the earth, like an age-weakened lord of men,Trembles in terror on their ways. Strong is their birth: vigour have they to issue from their Mother; strength,Yea, even twice enough, is theirs. And these, the Sons, the Singers, in their racings have enlarged the bounds,So that the kine must walk knee-deep. Before them, on the ways they go, they drop this offspring of the cloud,Long, broad, and inexhaustible. O Maruts, as your strength is great, so have ye cast men down on earth,So have ye made the mountains fall. The while the Maruts pass along, they talk together on the way:Doth any hear them as they speak? Come quick with swift steeds, for ye have worshippers among Kaṇva's sonsMay you rejoice among them well. All is prepared for your delight. We are their servants evermore,To live as long as life may last.

verses.sanskrit: क्रीळं वः शर्धो मारुतमनर्वाणं रथेशुभं ।कण्वा अभि प्र गायत ॥
verses.transliteration: krīḷám ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ mā́rutam ǀ anarvā́ṇam ǀ rathe-śúbham ǀkáṇvāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ gāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: SING forth, O Kaṇvas, to your band of Maruts unassailable, Sporting, resplendent on their car
verses.wilson_translation: Celebrate,Kaṇvas, the aggregate strength of the Maruts, sportive, with horses, but shining in their car.
verses.griffith_verse: SING forth, O Kaṇvas, to your band of Maruts unassailable, Sporting, resplendent on their car
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये पृषतीभिर्ऋष्टिभिः साकं वाशीभिरंजिभिः ।अजायंत स्वभानवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ pṛ́ṣatībhiḥ ǀ ṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ vā́śībhiḥ ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀájāyanta ǀ svá-bhānavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who, self-luminous, were born together, with the spotted deer, Spears, swords, and glittering ornaments.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, borne by spotted deer, were born self-radiant, with weapons, war-cries and decorations.
verses.griffith_verse: They who, self-luminous, were born together, with the spotted deer, Spears, swords, and glittering ornaments.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इहेव शृण्व एषां कशा हस्तेषु यद्वदान् ।नि यामञ्चित्रमृंजते ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá-iva ǀ śṛṇve ǀ eṣām ǀ káśāḥ ǀ hásteṣu ǀ yát ǀ vádān ǀní ǀ yā́man ǀ citrám ǀ ṛñjate ǁ
verses.english_translation: One hears, as though ’twere close at hand, the cracking of the whips they hold They gather glory on their way.
verses.wilson_translation: I hear the craking of the whips in theirhands, wonderfully inspiring (courage) in the fight.
verses.griffith_verse: One hears, as though ’twere close at hand, the cracking of the whips they hold They gather glory on their way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वः शर्धाय घृष्वये त्वेषद्युम्नाय शुष्मिणे ।देवत्तं ब्रह्म गायत ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárdhāya ǀ ghṛ́ṣvaye ǀ tveṣá-dyumnāya ǀ śuṣmíṇe ǀdeváttam ǀ bráhma ǀ gāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now sing ye forth the God-given hymn to your exultant Marut host, The fiercely-vigorous, the strong.
verses.wilson_translation: Address the god-given prayer to those who are your strength, the destroyers of foes, the powerful, possessed of brilliant reputation.
verses.griffith_verse: Now sing ye forth the God-given hymn to your exultant Marut host, The fiercely-vigorous, the strong.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र शंसा गोष्वघ्न्यं क्रीळं यच्छर्धो मारुतं ।जंभे रसस्य वावृधे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ śaṃsa ǀ góṣu ǀ ághnyam ǀ krīḷám ǀ yát ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ mā́rutam ǀjámbhe ǀ rásasya ǀ vavṛdhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise ye the Bull among the cows; for ’tis the Maruts’ sportive band: It strengthened as it drank the rain.
verses.wilson_translation: Praise the sportive and unresisted might of the Maruts, who were born amongst kine, and whose strength has been nourished by (the enjoyment of) the milk.
verses.griffith_verse: Praise ye the Bull among the cows; for ’tis the Maruts’ sportive band: It strengthened as it drank the rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को वो वर्षिष्ठ आ नरो दिवश्च ग्मश्च धूतयः ।यत्सीमंतं न धूनुथ ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ várṣiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ naraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ca ǀ gmáḥ ǀ ca ǀ dhūtayaḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ántam ǀ ná ǀ dhūnuthá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who is your mightiest, Heroes, when, O shakers of the earth and heaven, Ye shake them like a garment's hem?
verses.wilson_translation: Which is the chief leader among you, agitators of heaven and earth, who shake all around like the top (of a tree)?
verses.griffith_verse: Who is your mightiest, Heroes, when, O shakers of the earth and heaven, Ye shake them like a garment's hem?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि वो यामाय मानुषो दध्र उग्राय मन्यवे ।जिहीत पर्वतो गिरिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ vaḥ ǀ yā́māya ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ dadhré ǀ ugrā́ya ǀ manyáve ǀjíhīta ǀ párvataḥ ǀ giríḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: At your approach man holds him down before the fury of your wrath: The rugged-jointed mountain yields.
verses.wilson_translation: The house-holder, in dread of your fierce and violent approach, has plural nted a firm (buttress); for the many-ridged mountain is shattered (before you).
verses.griffith_verse: At your approach man holds him down before the fury of your wrath: The rugged-jointed mountain yields.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येषामज्मेषु पृथिवी जुजुर्वाँ इव विश्पतिः ।भिया यामेषु रेजते ॥
verses.transliteration: yéṣām ǀ ájmeṣu ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ jujurvā́n-iva ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀbhiyā́ ǀ yā́meṣu ǀ réjate ǁ
verses.english_translation: They at whose racings forth the earth, like an age-weakened lord of men, Trembles in terror on their ways.
verses.wilson_translation: At whose impetuous approach, earth trembles like an enfeebled monarch through dread (of his enemies).
verses.griffith_verse: They at whose racings forth the earth, like an age-weakened lord of men, Trembles in terror on their ways.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्थिरं हि जानमेषां वयो मातुर्निरेतवे ।यत्सीमनु द्विता शवः ॥
verses.transliteration: sthirám ǀ hí ǀ jā́nam ǀ eṣām ǀ váyaḥ ǀ mātúḥ ǀ níḥ-etave ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ánu ǀ dvitā́ ǀ śávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong is their birth: vigour have they to issue from their Mother; strength, Yea, even twice enough, is theirs.
verses.wilson_translation: Stable is their birth plural ce, (the sky), yet the birds (are able) to issue from (the sphere of) their parent; for your strength is everywhere (divided between two--regions, or heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong is their birth: vigour have they to issue from their Mother; strength, Yea, even twice enough, is theirs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदु त्ये सूनवो गिरः काष्ठा अज्मेष्वत्नत ।वाश्रा अभिज्ञु यातवे ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyé ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ kā́ṣṭhāḥ ǀ ájmeṣu ǀ atnata ǀvāśrā́ḥ ǀ abhi-jñú ǀ yā́tave ǁ
verses.english_translation: And these, the Sons, the Singers, in their racings have enlarged the bounds, So that the kine must walk knee-deep.
verses.wilson_translation: They are the genitive rations of speech; they spread out the waters in their courses; they urge the lowing (cattle) to enter (the water) up to their knees (to drink).
verses.griffith_verse: And these, the Sons, the Singers, in their racings have enlarged the bounds, So that the kine must walk knee-deep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्यं चिद्घा दीर्घं पृथुं मिहो नपातममृध्रं ।प्र च्यावयंति यामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tyám ǀ cit ǀ gha ǀ dīrghám ǀ pṛthúm ǀ miháḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ ámṛdhram ǀprá ǀ cyavayanti ǀ yā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Before them, on the ways they go, they drop this offspring of the cloud, Long, broad, and inexhaustible.
verses.wilson_translation: They drive before them in their course, the long, vast, uninjurable, rain-retaining cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: Before them, on the ways they go, they drop this offspring of the cloud, Long, broad, and inexhaustible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
