verses.sanskrit: मरुतो यद्ध वो बलं जनाँ अचुच्यवीतन ।गिरीँरचुच्यवीतन ॥
verses.transliteration: márutaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vaḥ ǀ bálam ǀ jánān ǀ acucyavītana ǀgirī́n ǀ acucyavītana ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Maruts, as your strength is great, so have ye cast men down on earth, So have ye made the mountains fall.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, as you have vigour, invogorate mankind; give animation to the clouds.
verses.griffith_verse: O Maruts, as your strength is great, so have ye cast men down on earth, So have ye made the mountains fall.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्ध यांति मरुतः सं ह ब्रुवतेऽध्वन्ना ।शृणोति कश्चिदेषां ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ha ǀ yā́nti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ha ǀ bruvate ǀ ádhvan ǀ ā́ ǀśṛṇóti ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ eṣām ǁ
verses.english_translation: The while the Maruts pass along, they talk together on the way: Doth any hear them as they speak?
verses.wilson_translation: Wherever the Marutspass, they fill the way with clamour; every one hears their (noise).
verses.griffith_verse: The while the Maruts pass along, they talk together on the way: Doth any hear them as they speak?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यात शीभमाशुभिः संति कण्वेषु वो दुवः ।तत्रो षु मादयाध्वै ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yāta ǀ śī́bham ǀ āśú-bhiḥ ǀ sánti ǀ káṇveṣu ǀ vaḥ ǀ dúvaḥ ǀtátro íti ǀ sú ǀ mādayādhvai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come quick with swift steeds, for ye have worshippers among Kaṇva's sons May you rejoice among them well.
verses.wilson_translation: Come quickly, with your swift (vehicles); the offerings of thekaṇvasare prepared; be plural ased with them.
verses.griffith_verse: Come quick with swift steeds, for ye have worshippers among Kaṇva's sons May you rejoice among them well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्ति हि ष्मा मदाय वः स्मसि ष्मा वयमेषां ।विश्वं चिदायुर्जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ásti ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ mádāya ǀ vaḥ ǀ smási ǀ sma ǀ vayám ǀ eṣām ǀvíśvam ǀ cit ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: All is prepared for your delight. We are their servants evermore, To live as long as life may last.
verses.wilson_translation: The offering is prepared for your gratification; we are your (worshipper), that we may live all our life.
verses.griffith_verse: All is prepared for your delight. We are their servants evermore, To live as long as life may last.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVIII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WHAT now? When will ye take us by both hands, as a dear sire his son,Gods, for whom sacred grass is clipped? Now whither? To what goal of yours go ye in heaven, and not on earth?Where do your cows disport themselves? Where are your newest favours shown? Where, Maruts, your prosperity?Where all your high felicities? If, O ye Maruts, ye the Sons whom Pṛśni bore, were mortal, andImmortal he who sings your praise. Then never were your praiser loathed like a wild beast in pasture-land,Nor should he go on Yama's path. Let not destructive plague on plague hard to be conquered, strike its down:Let each, with drought, depart from us. Truly, they the fierce and mighty Sons of Rudra send their windlessRain e’en on the desert places. Like a cow the lightning lows and follows, motherlike, her youngling,When their rain-flood hath been loosened. When they inundate the earth they spread forth darkness e’en in day time,With the water-laden rain-cloud. O Maruts, at your voice's sound this earthly habitation shakes,And each man reels who dwells therein. O Maruts, with your strong-hoofed steeds, unhindered in their courses, hasteAlong the bright embanked streams. Firm be the fellies of your wheels, steady your horses and your cars,And may your reins be fashioned well. Invite thou hither with this song, for praise, Agni the Lord of Prayer,Him who is fair as Mitra is. Form in thy mouth the hymn of praise expand thee like, a rainy cloudSing forth the measured eulogy. Sing glory to the Marut host, praiseworthy, tuneful, vigorous:Here let the Strong Ones dwell with us.

verses.sanskrit: कद्ध नूनं कधप्रियः पिता पुत्रं न हस्तयोः ।दधिध्वे वृक्तबर्हिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ ha ǀ nūnám ǀ kadha-priyaḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ putrám ǀ ná ǀ hástayoḥ ǀdadhidhvé ǀ vṛkta-barhiṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT now? When will ye take us by both hands, as a dear sire his son, Gods, for whom sacred grass is clipped?
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, who are fond of praise, and for whom the sacred grass is trimmed, when will you take us by bothhandsas a father does his son?
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT now? When will ye take us by both hands, as a dear sire his son, Gods, for whom sacred grass is clipped?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व नूनं कद्वो अर्थं गंता दिवो न पृथिव्याः ।क्व वो गावो न रण्यंति ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ nūnám ǀ kát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ártham ǀ gánta ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀkvá ǀ vaḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raṇyanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now whither? To what goal of yours go ye in heaven, and not on earth? Where do your cows disport themselves?
verses.wilson_translation: Where indeed are you (at present)? When will your arrival take plural ce? Pass from the heaven, not from the earth. Where do they worship you cry (to you) like cattle?
verses.griffith_verse: Now whither? To what goal of yours go ye in heaven, and not on earth? Where do your cows disport themselves?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व वः सुम्ना नव्यांसि मरुतः क्व सुविता ।क्वो विश्वानि सौभगा ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ vaḥ ǀ sumnā́ ǀ návyāṃsi ǀ márutaḥ ǀ kvá ǀ suvitā́ ǀkvó íti ǀ víśvāni ǀ sáubhagā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where are your newest favours shown? Where, Maruts, your prosperity? Where all your high felicities?
verses.wilson_translation: Where,Maruts, are your new treasures? Where your valuable (riches)? Where all your auspicious (gifts)?
verses.griffith_verse: Where are your newest favours shown? Where, Maruts, your prosperity? Where all your high felicities?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्यूयं पृश्निमातरो मर्तासः स्यातन ।स्तोता वो अमृतः स्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ yūyám ǀ pṛśni-mātaraḥ ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ syā́tana ǀstotā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ syāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: If, O ye Maruts, ye the Sons whom Pṛśni bore, were mortal, and Immortal he who sings your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: That you, sons of Pṛśni, may become mortals, and your panegyrist become immortal.
verses.griffith_verse: If, O ye Maruts, ye the Sons whom Pṛśni bore, were mortal, and Immortal he who sings your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा वो मृगो न यवसे जरिता भूदजोष्यः ।पथा यमस्य गादुप ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yávase ǀ jaritā́ ǀ bhūt ǀ ájoṣyaḥ ǀpathā́ ǀ yamásya ǀ gāt ǀ úpa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then never were your praiser loathed like a wild beast in pasture-land, Nor should he go on Yama's path.
verses.wilson_translation: Never may your worshipper be indifferent to you, as a deer (is never indifferent) to pasture, so that he may not tread the path of Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: Then never were your praiser loathed like a wild beast in pasture-land, Nor should he go on Yama's path.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मो षु णः परापरा निर्ऋतिर्दुर्हणा वधीत् ।पदीष्ट तृष्णया सह ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ párā-parā ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ duḥ-hánā ǀ vadhīt ǀpadīṣṭá ǀ tṛ́ṣṇayā ǀ sahá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not destructive plague on plague hard to be conquered, strike its down: Let each, with drought, depart from us.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the most powerful and indestructible Nirṛtidestroy us; let him perish with our (evil) desires.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not destructive plague on plague hard to be conquered, strike its down: Let each, with drought, depart from us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं त्वेषा अमवंतो धन्वञ्चिदा रुद्रियासः ।मिहं कृण्वंत्यवातां ॥
verses.transliteration: satyám ǀ tveṣā́ḥ ǀ áma-vantaḥ ǀ dhánvan ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ rudríyāsaḥ ǀmíham ǀ kṛṇvanti ǀ avātā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Truly, they the fierce and mighty Sons of Rudra send their windless Rain e’en on the desert places.
verses.wilson_translation: In truth the brilliant and vigorous Maruts, cherishes by Rudra, send down rain without wind upon the desert.
verses.griffith_verse: Truly, they the fierce and mighty Sons of Rudra send their windless Rain e’en on the desert places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वाश्रेव विद्युन्मिमाति वत्सं न माता सिषक्ति ।यदेषां वृष्टिरसर्जि ॥
verses.transliteration: vāśrā́-iva ǀ vi-dyút ǀ mimāti ǀ vatsám ǀ ná ǀ mātā́ ǀ sisakti ǀyát ǀ eṣām ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ ǀ ásarji ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a cow the lightning lows and follows, motherlike, her youngling, When their rain-flood hath been loosened.
verses.wilson_translation: The lightning roars like a parent cow that bellows for its calf, and hence the rain is set free by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a cow the lightning lows and follows, motherlike, her youngling, When their rain-flood hath been loosened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवा चित्तमः कृण्वंति पर्जन्येनोदवाहेन ।यत्पृथिवीं व्युंदंति ॥
verses.transliteration: dívā ǀ cit ǀ támaḥ ǀ kṛṇvanti ǀ parjányena ǀ uda-vāhéna ǀyát ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ vi-undánti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they inundate the earth they spread forth darkness e’en in day time, With the water-laden rain-cloud.
verses.wilson_translation: They spread darkness over the day by a water-bearing cloud, and thence inundate the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: When they inundate the earth they spread forth darkness e’en in day time, With the water-laden rain-cloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध स्वनान्मरुतां विश्वमा सद्म पार्थिवं ।अरेजंत प्र मानुषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ svanā́t ǀ marútām ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ sádma ǀ pā́rthivam ǀárejanta ǀ prá ǀ mā́nuṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Maruts, at your voice's sound this earthly habitation shakes, And each man reels who dwells therein.
verses.wilson_translation: At the roaring of the Maruts, every dwelling of earth (shakes), and men also tremble.
verses.griffith_verse: O Maruts, at your voice's sound this earthly habitation shakes, And each man reels who dwells therein.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मरुतो वीळुपाणिभिश्चित्रा रोधस्वतीरनु ।यातेमखिद्रयामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: márutaḥ ǀ vīḷupāṇí-bhiḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ ródhasvatīḥ ǀ ánu ǀyātá ǀ īm ǀ ákhidrayāma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Maruts, with your strong-hoofed steeds, unhindered in their courses, haste Along the bright embanked streams.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, with stronghands, come along the beautifully-embanked rivers, with obstructed progress.
verses.griffith_verse: O Maruts, with your strong-hoofed steeds, unhindered in their courses, haste Along the bright embanked streams.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्थिरा वः संतु नेमयो रथा अश्वास एषां ।सुसंस्कृता अभीशवः ॥
verses.transliteration: sthirā́ḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ santu ǀ nemáyaḥ ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀsú-saṃskṛtāḥ ǀ abhī́śavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Firm be the fellies of your wheels, steady your horses and your cars, And may your reins be fashioned well.
verses.wilson_translation: May the felloes of your wheels be firm; may your cars and their steeds be steady, and your fingers well-skilled (to hold the reins).
verses.griffith_verse: Firm be the fellies of your wheels, steady your horses and your cars, And may your reins be fashioned well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा वदा तना गिरा जरायै ब्रह्मणस्पतिं ।अग्निं मित्रं न दर्शतं ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ vada ǀ tánā ǀ girā́ ǀ jarā́yai ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátim ǀagním ǀ mitrám ǀ ná ǀ darśatám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invite thou hither with this song, for praise, Agni the Lord of Prayer, Him who is fair as Mitra is.
verses.wilson_translation: Declare in our presence, (priests), with voice attuned to praise Brahmaṇaspati(lord of the sacriricial food),Agniand the beautiful Mitra.
verses.griffith_verse: Invite thou hither with this song, for praise, Agni the Lord of Prayer, Him who is fair as Mitra is.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मिमीहि श्लोकमास्ये पर्जन्य इव ततनः ।गाय गायत्रमुक्थ्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: mimīhí ǀ ślókam ǀ āsyé ǀ parjányaḥ-iva ǀ tatanaḥ ǀgā́ya ǀ gāyatrám ǀ ukthyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Form in thy mouth the hymn of praise expand thee like, a rainy cloud Sing forth the measured eulogy.
verses.wilson_translation: Utter the verse that is in your mouths, spread it out like a cloud spreading rain; chant the measured hymn.
verses.griffith_verse: Form in thy mouth the hymn of praise expand thee like, a rainy cloud Sing forth the measured eulogy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वंदस्व मारुतं गणं त्वेषं पनस्युमर्किणं ।अस्मे वृद्धा असन्निह ॥
verses.transliteration: vándasva ǀ mā́rutam ǀ gaṇám ǀ tveṣám ǀ panasyúm ǀ arkíṇam ǀasmé íti ǀ vṛddhā́ḥ ǀ asan ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing glory to the Marut host, praiseworthy, tuneful, vigorous: Here let the Strong Ones dwell with us.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify the host of Maruts, brilliant, deserving of praise, entitled to adoration; may they be exalted by this our worship.
verses.griffith_verse: Sing glory to the Marut host, praiseworthy, tuneful, vigorous: Here let the Strong Ones dwell with us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIX Maruts.
hymns.anukramani: १० कण्वौ घौरः। मरुतः। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समाः सतोबृहत्यः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth,To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design? Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be.Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength. When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing,Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks. Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth:Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now. They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart.Onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company. Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws.Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified. O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours.Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kaṇva's sake. Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us,Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours. For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kaṇva perfectly.O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain. Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might.Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.

verses.sanskrit: प्र यदित्था परावतः शोचिर्न मानमस्यथ ।कस्य क्रत्वा मरुतः कस्य वर्पसा कं याथ कं ह धूतयः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ itthā́ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ śocíḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́nam ǀ ásyatha ǀkásya ǀ krátvā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ kásya ǀ várpasā ǀ kám ǀ yātha ǀ kám ǀ ha ǀ dhūtayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth, To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design?
verses.wilson_translation: When Maruts, who make (all things) tremble, you direct your awful (vigour) downwards from afar, as light (descends from heaven), by whose worship by whose praise (are you attracted)? to what (plural ce of sacrifice), to whom, indeed, do you repair?
verses.griffith_verse: WHEN thus, like flame, from far away, Maruts, ye cast your measure forth, To whom go Ye, to whom, O shakers of the earth, moved by whose wisdom, whose design?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्थिरा वः संत्वायुधा पराणुदे वीळू उत प्रतिष्कभे ।युष्माकमस्तु तविषी पनीयसी मा मर्त्यस्य मायिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: sthirā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ santu ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ parā-núde ǀ vīḷú ǀ utá ǀ prati-skábhe ǀyuṣmā́kam ǀ astu ǀ táviṣī ǀ pánīyasī ǀ mā́ ǀ mártyasya ǀ māyínaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be. Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Strong be your weapons for driving away (your) foes, firm in resisting them; yours be the strength that merits praise, not (the strength) of a treacherous mortal.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong let your weapons be to drive away your foes, firm for resistance let them be. Yea, passing glorious must be your warrior might, not as a guileful mortal's strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा ह यत्स्थिरं हथ नरो वर्तयथा गुरु ।वि याथन वनिनः पृथिव्या व्याशाः पर्वतानां ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ sthirám ǀ hathá ǀ náraḥ ǀ vartáyatha ǀ gurú ǀví ǀ yāthana ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ párvatānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing, Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks.
verses.wilson_translation: Directing Maruts, when you demolish what is stable, when you scatter what is ponderous, then you make your way through the forest (trees) of earth and the defiles of the mountains.
verses.griffith_verse: When what is strong ye overthrow, and whirl about each ponderous thing, Heroes, your course is through the forest trees of earth, and through the fissures of the rocks.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि वः शत्रुर्विविदे अधि द्यवि न भूम्यां रिशादसः ।युष्माकमस्तु तविषी तना युजा रुद्रासो नू चिदाधृषे ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ vaḥ ǀ śátruḥ ǀ vividé ǀ ádhi ǀ dyávi ǀ ná ǀ bhū́myām ǀ riśādasaḥ ǀyuṣmā́kam ǀ astu ǀ táviṣī ǀ tánā ǀ yujā́ ǀ rúdrāsaḥ ǀ nú ǀ cit ǀ ā-dhṛ́ṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth: Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyers of foes, no adversary of yours is known above the heavens, nor (is any) upon earth; may your collective strength be quickly exerted, sons of Rudra, to humble (your enemies).
verses.griffith_verse: Consumers of your foes, no enemy of yours is found in heaven or on the earth: Ye Rudras, may the strength, held in this bond, be yours, to bid defiance even now.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वेपयंति पर्वतान्वि विंचंति वनस्पतीन् ।प्रो आरत मरुतो दुर्मदा इव देवासः सर्वया विशा ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vepayanti ǀ párvatān ǀ ví ǀ viñcanti ǀ vánaspátīn ǀpró íti ǀ ārata ǀ marutaḥ ǀ durmádāḥ-iva ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ sárvayā ǀ viśā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart. Onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company.
verses.wilson_translation: They make the mountains tremble, they drive apart the forest-trees. Go, divine Maruts, whither you will, with all your progeny, like those intoxicated.
verses.griffith_verse: They make the mountains rock and reel, they rend the forest-kings apart. Onward, ye Maruts, drive, like creatures drunk with wine, ye, Gods with all your company.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपो रथेषु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं प्रष्टिर्वहति रोहितः ।आ वो यामाय पृथिवी चिदश्रोदबीभयंत मानुषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpo íti ǀ rátheṣu ǀ pṛ́ṣatīḥ ǀ ayugdhvam ǀ práṣṭiḥ ǀ vahati ǀ róhitaḥ ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ yā́māya ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ cit ǀ aśrot ǀ ábībhayanta ǀ mā́nuṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws. Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified.
verses.wilson_translation: You have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariot; the red deer yoked between them, (aids to) drag the car; the firmament listens for your coming, and men are alarmed.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye to your chariot have yoked the spotted deer: a red deer, as a leader, draws. Even the Earth herself listened as ye came near, and men were sorely terrified.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो मक्षू तनाय कं रुद्रा अवो वृणीमहे ।गंता नूनं नोऽवसा यथा पुरेत्था कण्वाय बिभ्युषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ tánāya ǀ kám ǀ rúdrāḥ ǀ ávaḥ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀgánta ǀ nūnám ǀ naḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ yáthā ǀ purā́ ǀ itthā́ ǀ káṇvāya ǀ bibhyúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours. Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kaṇva's sake.
verses.wilson_translation: Rudras, we have recourse to your assistance for the sake of our progeny; come quickly to the timid Kaṇva, as you formerly came, for our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: O Rudras, quickly we desire your succour for this work of ours. Come to us with your aid as in the days of old, so now for frightened Kaṇva's sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युष्मेषितो मरुतो मर्त्येषित आ यो नो अभ्व ईषते ।वि तं युयोत शवसा व्योजसा वि युष्माकाभिरूतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuṣmā́-iṣitaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mártya-iṣitaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvaḥ ǀ ī́ṣate ǀví ǀ tám ǀ yuyota ǀ śávasā ǀ ví ǀ ójasā ǀ ví ǀ yuṣmā́kābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us, Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours.
verses.wilson_translation: Should any adversary, instrumental gated by you, or by man, assail us, withhold from him food and strength and your assistance.
verses.griffith_verse: Should any monstrous foe, O Maruts, sent by you or sent by mortals threaten us, Tear ye him from us with your power and with your might, and with the succours that are yours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असामि हि प्रयज्यवः कण्वं दद प्रचेतसः ।असामिभिर्मरुत आ न ऊतिभिर्गंता वृष्टिं न विद्युतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ásāmi ǀ hí ǀ pra-yajyavaḥ ǀ káṇvam ǀ dadá ǀ pra-cetasaḥ ǀásāmi-bhiḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ gánta ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ ná ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kaṇva perfectly. O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain.
verses.wilson_translation: Pracetasas, who are to be unreservedly worshipped, uphold (the sacrificer)Kaṇva; come to us,Maruts, with undivided protective assistance, as the lightning (bring) the rain.
verses.griffith_verse: For ye, the worshipful and wise, have guarded Kaṇva perfectly. O Maruts, come to us with full protecting help, as lightning flashes seek the rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असाम्योजो बिभृथा सुदानवोऽसामि धूतयः शवः ।ऋषिद्विषे मरुतः परिमन्यव इषुं न सृजत द्विषं ॥
verses.transliteration: ásāmi ǀ ójaḥ ǀ bibhṛtha ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ ásāmi ǀ dhūtayaḥ ǀ śávaḥ ǀṛṣi-dvíṣe ǀ marutaḥ ǀ pari-manyáve ǀ íṣum ǀ ná ǀ sṛjata ǀ dvíṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might. Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.
verses.wilson_translation: Bounteous givers, you enjoy unimpaired vigour; shakers (of the earth), you possess undiminished strength;Maruts, let loose your anger, like an arrow, upon the wrathful enemy of the ṛṣis.
verses.griffith_verse: Whole strength have ye, O Bounteous Ones; perfect, earth-shakers, is your might. Maruts, against the poet's wrathful enemy send ye an enemy like a dart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XL. Brahmaṇaspati
hymns.anukramani: ८ कण्वो घौरः। ब्रह्मणस्पतिः। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समाः सतोबृहत्यः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: O BRAHMAṆASPATI, stand up: God-serving men we pray to thee.May they who give good gifts, the Maruts, come to us. Indra, most swift, be thou with them. O Son of Strength, each mortal calls to thee for aid when spoil of battle waits for him.O Maruts, may this man who loves you well obtain wealth of good steeds and hero might. May Brahmaṇaspati draw nigh, may Sūnṛtā the Goddess come,And Gods bring to this rite which gives the five-fold gift the Hero, lover of mankind. He who bestows a noble guerdon on the priest wins fame that never shall decay.For him we offer sacred hero-giving food, peerless and conquering easily. Now Brahmaṇaspati speaks forth aloud the solemn hymn of praise,Wherein Indra and Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the Gods, have made their dwelling place. May we in holy synods, Gods! recite that hymn, peerless, that brings felicity.If you, O Heroes, graciously accept this word, may it obtain all bliss from you. Who shall approach the pious? who the man whose sacred grass is trimmed?The offerer with his folk advances more and more: he fills his house with precious things. He amplifies his lordly might, with kings he slays: e’en mid alarms he dwells secureIn great or lesser fight none checks him, none subdues,—the wielder of the thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पते देवयंतस्त्वेमहे ।उप प्र यंतु मरुतः सुदानव इंद्र प्राशूर्भवा सचा ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ brahmaṇaḥ ǀ pate ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ īmahe ǀúpa ǀ prá ǀ yantu ǀ marútaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ índra ǀ prāśū́ḥ ǀ bhava ǀ sácā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O BRAHMAṆASPATI, stand up: God-serving men we pray to thee. May they who give good gifts, the Maruts, come to us. Indra, most swift, be thou with them.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise us, Brhmaṇaspati; devoted to the gods, we solicit you, bounteous Maruts, be nigh athand;Indra, be a partaker fo the libation.
verses.griffith_verse: O BRAHMAṆASPATI, stand up: God-serving men we pray to thee. May they who give good gifts, the Maruts, come to us. Indra, most swift, be thou with them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिद्धि सहसस्पुत्र मर्त्य उपब्रूते धने हिते ।सुवीर्यं मरुत आ स्वश्व्यं दधीत यो व आचके ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ putra ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ upa-brūté ǀ dháne ǀ hité ǀsu-vī́ryam ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ su-áśvyam ǀ dádhīta ǀ yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā-caké ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Son of Strength, each mortal calls to thee for aid when spoil of battle waits for him. O Maruts, may this man who loves you well obtain wealth of good steeds and hero might.
verses.wilson_translation: Man celebrates you, son of strength, for the wealth abandoned (by the foe).Maruts, may be who praises you obtain wealth, yielding excellent steeds and eminent vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: O Son of Strength, each mortal calls to thee for aid when spoil of battle waits for him. O Maruts, may this man who loves you well obtain wealth of good steeds and hero might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिः प्र देव्येतु सूनृता ।अच्छा वीरं नर्यं पंक्तिराधसं देवा यज्ञं नयंतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ etu ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ prá ǀ devī́ ǀ etu ǀ sūnṛ́tā ǀáccha ǀ vīrám ǀ náryam ǀ paṅktí-rādhasam ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ nayantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Brahmaṇaspati draw nigh, may Sūnṛtā the Goddess come, And Gods bring to this rite which gives the five-fold gift the Hero, lover of mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: May Brahmaṇaspatiapproach us;  may the goddess, speaker of truth, approach us; may the gods (drive away) every adversary, and present, conduct us to the sacrifice which is beneficial to man, and (abounds) with respectably-presented offerings.
verses.griffith_verse: May Brahmaṇaspati draw nigh, may Sūnṛtā the Goddess come, And Gods bring to this rite which gives the five-fold gift the Hero, lover of mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वाघते ददाति सूनरं वसु स धत्ते अक्षिति श्रवः ।तस्मा इळां सुवीरामा यजामहे सुप्रतूर्तिमनेहसं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vāgháte ǀ dádāti ǀ sūnáram ǀ vásu ǀ sáḥ ǀ dhatte ǀ ákṣiti ǀ śrávaḥ ǀtásmai ǀ íḷām ǀ su-vī́rām ǀ ā́ ǀ yajāmahe ǀ su-prátūrtim ǀ anehásam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who bestows a noble guerdon on the priest wins fame that never shall decay. For him we offer sacred hero-giving food, peerless and conquering easily.
verses.wilson_translation: He who presents to the ministrant (priest) wealth fit to be accepted, enjoys inexhaustible abundance; for him we worship, Iḷā, attended by brave warriors, inflicting much injury, receiving none.
verses.griffith_verse: He who bestows a noble guerdon on the priest wins fame that never shall decay. For him we offer sacred hero-giving food, peerless and conquering easily.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नूनं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मंत्रं वदत्युक्थ्यं ।यस्मिन्निंद्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा देवा ओकांसि चक्रिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nūnám ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ mántram ǀ vadati ǀ ukthyám ǀyásmin ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ókāṃsi ǀ cakriré ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now Brahmaṇaspati speaks forth aloud the solemn hymn of praise, Wherein Indra and Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the Gods, have made their dwelling place.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily Brahmaṇaspatiproclaims the sacred prayer, in which the divinities,Indra,Varuṇa,Mitraand Aryaman, have made their abode.
verses.griffith_verse: Now Brahmaṇaspati speaks forth aloud the solemn hymn of praise, Wherein Indra and Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the Gods, have made their dwelling place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमिद्वोचेमा विदथेषु शंभुवं मंत्रं देवा अनेहसं ।इमां च वाचं प्रतिहर्यथा नरो विश्वेद्वामा वो अश्नवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ vocema ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ śam-bhúvam ǀ mántram ǀ devāḥ ǀ anehásam ǀimā́m ǀ ca ǀ vā́cam ǀ prati-háryatha ǀ naraḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ vāmā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ aśnavat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we in holy synods, Gods! recite that hymn, peerless, that brings felicity. If you, O Heroes, graciously accept this word, may it obtain all bliss from you.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us recite, gods, that felicitous and faultless prayer at sacrifices; if you, leaders, desire (to hear) this prayer, then will all that is to be spoken reach unto you.
verses.griffith_verse: May we in holy synods, Gods! recite that hymn, peerless, that brings felicity. If you, O Heroes, graciously accept this word, may it obtain all bliss from you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को देवयंतमश्नवज्जनं को वृक्तबर्हिषं ।प्रप्र दाश्वान्पस्त्याभिरस्थितांतर्वावत्क्षयं दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ deva-yántam ǀ aśnavat ǀ jánam ǀ káḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣam ǀprá-pra ǀ dāśvā́n ǀ pastyā́bhiḥ ǀ asthita ǀ antaḥ-vā́vat ǀ kṣáyam ǀ dadhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who shall approach the pious? who the man whose sacred grass is trimmed? The offerer with his folk advances more and more: he fills his house with precious things.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, (except Brahmaṇaspati), may approach the man who is devoted to the gods, by whom the clipped sacred grass is spread; the giver of the oblation has proceeded with the priests (to the hall of sacrifice), for he has a dwelling (abounding) internally with precious things.
verses.griffith_verse: Who shall approach the pious? who the man whose sacred grass is trimmed? The offerer with his folk advances more and more: he fills his house with precious things.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप क्षत्रं पृंचीत हंति राजभिर्भये चित्सुक्षितिं दधे ।नास्य वर्ता न तरुता महाधने नार्भे अस्ति वज्रिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ kṣatrám ǀ pṛñcītá ǀ hánti ǀ rā́ja-bhiḥ ǀ bhayé ǀ cit ǀ su-kṣitím ǀ dadhe ǀná ǀ asya ǀ vartā́ ǀ ná ǀ tarutā́ ǀ mahā-dhané ǀ ná ǀ árbhe ǀ asti ǀ vajríṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He amplifies his lordly might, with kings he slays: e’en mid alarms he dwells secure In great or lesser fight none checks him, none subdues,—the wielder of the thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Let Brahmaṇaspaticoncentrate his strength associated with the regal (divinities), he slays (the foe); in the time of danger he maintains his station; armed with the thunderbolt, there is no encourager nor discourager of him in a great battle or a small.
verses.griffith_verse: He amplifies his lordly might, with kings he slays: e’en mid alarms he dwells secure In great or lesser fight none checks him, none subdues,—the wielder of the thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: NE’ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,The excellently wise, protect. He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich,Whom they preserve from every foe. The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies,And lead him safely o’er distress. Thornless, Ādityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law:With him is naught to anger you. What sacrifice, Ādityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,—May that come nigh unto your thought. That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing,And children also of his own. How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud,Glorious food of Varuṇa? I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles:Only with hymns I call you nigh. Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all fourWithin his hand, until they fall.

verses.sanskrit: यं रक्षंति प्रचेतसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।नू चित्स दभ्यते जनः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ rákṣanti ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀnú ǀ cit ǀ sáḥ ǀ dabhyate ǀ jánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: NE’ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, The excellently wise, protect.
verses.wilson_translation: The man whom the wise Varuṇa,Mitraand Aryamanprotect quickly subdues (his foes).
verses.griffith_verse: NE’ER is he injured whom the Gods Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, The excellently wise, protect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं बाहुतेव पिप्रति पांति मर्त्यं रिषः ।अरिष्टः सर्व एधते ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ bāhútā-iva ǀ píprati ǀ pā́nti ǀ mártyam ǀ riṣáḥ ǀáriṣṭaḥ ǀ sárvaḥ ǀ edhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich, Whom they preserve from every foe.
verses.wilson_translation: Hw whom they heap (with riches), as if (collected) by his own arms; the man whom they defend from the malignant; every such man, safe from injury, prospers.
verses.griffith_verse: He prospers ever, free from scathe, whom they, as with full hands, enrich, Whom they preserve from every foe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि दुर्गा वि द्विषः पुरो घ्नंति राजान एषां ।नयंति दुरिता तिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ duḥ-gā́ ǀ ví ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ ghnánti ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀnáyanti ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ tiráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies, And lead him safely o’er distress.
verses.wilson_translation: The kings (Varuṇaetc.) first destroy their strongholds, and then the foes of those (who worship him), and put aside their evil deeds.
verses.griffith_verse: The Kings drive far away from him his troubles and his enemies, And lead him safely o’er distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुगः पंथा अनृक्षर आदित्यास ऋतं यते ।नात्रावखादो अस्ति वः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-gáḥ ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ anṛkṣaráḥ ǀ ā́dityāsaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ yaté ǀná ǀ átra ǀ ava-khādáḥ ǀ asti ǀ vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thornless, Ādityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law: With him is naught to anger you.
verses.wilson_translation: Ādityas, to you repairing to the sacrifice, the path is easy and free from thorns; no unworthy oblation is here prepared for you.
verses.griffith_verse: Thornless, Ādityas, is the path, easy for him who seeks the Law: With him is naught to anger you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं यज्ञं नयथा नर आदित्या ऋजुना पथा ।प्र वः स धीतये नशत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ yajñám ǀ náyatha ǀ naraḥ ǀ ā́dityāḥ ǀ ṛjúnā ǀ pathā́ ǀprá ǀ vaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ dhītáye ǀ naśat ǁ
verses.english_translation: What sacrifice, Ādityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,— May that come nigh unto your thought.
verses.wilson_translation: Ādityas, guides, may the sacrifice which you come to by a straight path, be to you for your gratification.
verses.griffith_verse: What sacrifice, Ādityas, ye Heroes guide by the path direct,— May that come nigh unto your thought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स रत्नं मर्त्यो वसु विश्वं तोकमुत त्मना ।अच्छा गच्छत्यस्तृतः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ rátnam ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ vásu ǀ víśvam ǀ tokám ǀ utá ǀ tmánā ǀáccha ǀ gacchati ǀ ástṛtaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing, And children also of his own.
verses.wilson_translation: That mortal (whom you favour), exempt from harm, obtains all valuable wealth, and offspring like himself.
verses.griffith_verse: That mortal, ever unsubdued, gains wealth and every precious thing, And children also of his own.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कथा राधाम सखायः स्तोमं मित्रस्यार्यम्णः ।महि प्सरो वरुणस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ rādhāma ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ stómam ǀ mitrásya ǀ aryamṇáḥ ǀmáhi ǀ psáraḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud, Glorious food of Varuṇa?
verses.wilson_translation: How, my friends, shall we recite priase (worthy) of the great glory of Mitra,Varuṇaand Aryaman?
verses.griffith_verse: How, my friends, shall we prepare Aryaman's and Mitra's laud, Glorious food of Varuṇa?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा वो घ्नंतं मा शपंतं प्रति वोचे देवयंतं ।सुम्नैरिद्व आ विवासे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ghnántam ǀ mā́ ǀ śápantam ǀ práti ǀ voce ǀ deva-yántam ǀsumnáiḥ ǀ ít ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāse ǁ
verses.english_translation: I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles: Only with hymns I call you nigh.
verses.wilson_translation: I do not denounce to you him who assails or reviles the man devoted to the gods. I rather propitiate you with offered wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: I point not out to you a man who strikes the pious, or reviles: Only with hymns I call you nigh.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLII. Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: SHORTEN our ways, O Pūṣan, move aside obstruction in the path:Go close before us, cloud-born God. Drive, Pūṣan, from our road the wolf, the wicked inauspicious wolf,Who lies in wait to injure us. Who lurks about the path we take, the robber with a guileful heart:Far from the road chase him away. Tread with thy foot and trample out the firebrand of the wicked one,The double-tongued, whoe’er he be. Wise Pūṣan, Wonder-Worker, we claim of thee now the aid wherewithThou furtheredst our sires of old. So, Lord of all prosperity, best wielder of the golden sword,Make riches easy to be won. Past all pursuers lead us, make pleasant our path and fair to tread:O Pūṣan, find thou power for this. Lead us to meadows rich in grass: send on our way no early heat:O Pūṣan, find thou power for this. Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate:O Pūṣan, find thou power for this. No blame have we for Pūṣan; him we magnify with songs of praise:We seek the Mighty One for wealth.

verses.sanskrit: सं पूषन्नध्वनस्तिर व्यंहो विमुचो नपात् ।सक्ष्वा देव प्र णस्पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ pūṣan ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ tira ǀ ví ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ vi-mucaḥ ǀ napāt ǀsákṣva ǀ deva ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ puráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SHORTEN our ways, O Pūṣan, move aside obstruction in the path: Go close before us, cloud-born God.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣanm convey us over the road, remove the wicked (obsructer of the way). Son of the cloud, deity, go before us.
verses.griffith_verse: SHORTEN our ways, O Pūṣan, move aside obstruction in the path: Go close before us, cloud-born God.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो नः पूषन्नघो वृको दुःशेव आदिदेशति ।अप स्म तं पथो जहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pūṣan ǀ agháḥ ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǀ duḥśévaḥ ǀ ā-dídeśati ǀápa ǀ sma ǀ tám ǀ patháḥ ǀ jahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drive, Pūṣan, from our road the wolf, the wicked inauspicious wolf, Who lies in wait to injure us.
verses.wilson_translation: If a wicked (adversary),Pūṣan, a robber, or one who delights in evil, points out to us (the way we ought not to go), do you drive him from the road.
verses.griffith_verse: Drive, Pūṣan, from our road the wolf, the wicked inauspicious wolf, Who lies in wait to injure us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप त्यं परिपंथिनं मुषीवाणं हुरश्चितं ।दूरमधि स्रुतेरज ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ tyám ǀ pari-panthínam ǀ muṣīvā́ṇam ǀ huraḥ-cítam ǀdūrám ǀ ádhi ǀ srutéḥ ǀ aja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who lurks about the path we take, the robber with a guileful heart: Far from the road chase him away.
verses.wilson_translation: Drive him far away, apart fom the road, the hinderer of our journey, a thief, a deceiver.
verses.griffith_verse: Who lurks about the path we take, the robber with a guileful heart: Far from the road chase him away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तस्य द्वयाविनोऽघशंसस्य कस्य चित् ।पदाभि तिष्ठ तपुषिं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tásya ǀ dvayāvínaḥ ǀ aghá-śaṃsasya ǀ kásya ǀ cit ǀpadā́ ǀ abhí ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ tápuṣim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tread with thy foot and trample out the firebrand of the wicked one, The double-tongued, whoe’er he be.
verses.wilson_translation: Trample with your feet upon the mischievous (body) of that evil-minded pilferer of both (what is present and what is absent), whoever he be.
verses.griffith_verse: Tread with thy foot and trample out the firebrand of the wicked one, The double-tongued, whoe’er he be.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तत्ते दस्र मंतुमः पूषन्नवो वृणीमहे ।येन पितॄनचोदयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ dasra ǀ mantu-maḥ ǀ pūṣan ǀ ávaḥ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀyéna ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ ácodayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise Pūṣan, Wonder-Worker, we claim of thee now the aid wherewith Thou furtheredst our sires of old.
verses.wilson_translation: Sagacious and handsome Pūṣan, we solicit of you that protection wherewith you have encouraged the patriarchs.
verses.griffith_verse: Wise Pūṣan, Wonder-Worker, we claim of thee now the aid wherewith Thou furtheredst our sires of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा नो विश्वसौभग हिरण्यवाशीमत्तम ।धनानि सुषणा कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ naḥ ǀ viśva-saubhaga ǀ híraṇyavāśīmat-tama ǀdhánāni ǀ su-sánā ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: So, Lord of all prosperity, best wielder of the golden sword, Make riches easy to be won.
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore do you, who are possessed of all prosperity and well-equipped with golden weapons, bestow upon us riches that may be liberally distributed.
verses.griffith_verse: So, Lord of all prosperity, best wielder of the golden sword, Make riches easy to be won.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अति नः सश्चतो नय सुगा नः सुपथा कृणु ।पूषन्निह क्रतुं विदः ॥
verses.transliteration: áti ǀ naḥ ǀ saścátaḥ ǀ naya ǀ su-gā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ su-páthā ǀ kṛṇu ǀpū́ṣan ǀ ihá ǀ krátum ǀ vidaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Past all pursuers lead us, make pleasant our path and fair to tread: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.wilson_translation: Lead us past our opponents; conduct us by an easy path; know,Pūṣan, how to protect us on this (journey).
verses.griffith_verse: Past all pursuers lead us, make pleasant our path and fair to tread: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि सूयवसं नय न नवज्वारो अध्वने ।पूषन्निह क्रतुं विदः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ su-yávasam ǀ naya ǀ ná ǀ nava-jvāráḥ ǀ ádhvane ǀpū́ṣan ǀ ihá ǀ krátum ǀ vidaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lead us to meadows rich in grass: send on our way no early heat: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.wilson_translation: Lead us where there is abundant fodder; let there be no extreme heat by the way;Pūṣan, know to protect us on this (journey).
verses.griffith_verse: Lead us to meadows rich in grass: send on our way no early heat: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शग्धि पूर्धि प्र यंसि च शिशीहि प्रास्युदरं ।पूषन्निह क्रतुं विदः ॥
verses.transliteration: śagdhí ǀ pūrdhí ǀ prá ǀ yaṃsi ǀ ca ǀ śiśīhí ǀ prā́si ǀ udáram ǀpū́ṣan ǀ ihá ǀ krátum ǀ vidaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.wilson_translation: Be favourable to us, fill us (with abundance), give us (all goood things), sharpen us (with vigour), fill our bellies,Pūṣan, know how to protect us on this (journey).
verses.griffith_verse: Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate: O Pūṣan, find thou power for this.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न पूषणं मेथामसि सूक्तैरभि गृणीमसि ।वसूनि दस्ममीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ methāmasi ǀ su-uktáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀvásūni ǀ dasmám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: No blame have we for Pūṣan; him we magnify with songs of praise: We seek the Mighty One for wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We do not censure Pūṣan, but praise him with hymns; we solicit the good-looking (Pūṣan) for riches.
verses.griffith_verse: No blame have we for Pūṣan; him we magnify with songs of praise: We seek the Mighty One for wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIII. Rudra.
hymns.anukramani: ९ कण्वो घौरः। रुद्रः, मित्रावरुणौ च, ७-९ सोमः। गायत्री, ९ अनुष्टप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise,That shall be dearest to his heart? That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine,Our cattle and our progeny; That Mitra and that Varuṇa, that Rudra may remember us,Yea, all the Gods with one accord. To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines,We pray for joy and health and strength. He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he,The good, the best among the Gods. May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes,To men, to women, and to kine. O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men,The great renown of mighty chiefs. Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us.Indu, give us a share of strength. Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee,Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.

verses.sanskrit: कद्रुद्राय प्रचेतसे मीळ्हुष्टमाय तव्यसे ।वोचेम शंतमं हृदे ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ prá-cetase ǀ mīḷhúḥ-tamāya ǀ távyase ǀvocéma ǀ śám-tamam ǀ hṛdé ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise, That shall be dearest to his heart?
verses.wilson_translation: When may we repeat a most grateful hymn to the wise, the most bountiful and mighty Rudra, who is (cherished) in our hearts?
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT shall we sing to Rudra, strong, most bounteous, excellently wise, That shall be dearest to his heart?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा नो अदितिः करत्पश्वे नृभ्यो यथा गवे ।यथा तोकाय रुद्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ kárat ǀ páśve ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ gáve ǀyáthā ǀ tokā́ya ǀ rudríyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine, Our cattle and our progeny;
verses.wilson_translation: By which earth may (be induced to) grant the gifts of Rudrato our cattle, our people, our cows, and our progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: That Aditi may grant the grace of Rudra to our folk, our kine, Our cattle and our progeny;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा नो मित्रो वरुणो यथा रुद्रश्चिकेतति ।यथा विश्वे सजोषसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ rudráḥ ǀ cíketati ǀyáthā ǀ víśve ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That Mitra and that Varuṇa, that Rudra may remember us, Yea, all the Gods with one accord.
verses.wilson_translation: By which Mitraand Varuṇa, and Rudraand all the gods, being gratified, may show us (favour).
verses.griffith_verse: That Mitra and that Varuṇa, that Rudra may remember us, Yea, all the Gods with one accord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गाथपतिं मेधपतिं रुद्रं जलाषभेषजं ।तच्छंयोः सुम्नमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: gāthá-patim ǀ medhá-patim ǀ rudrám ǀ jálāṣa-bheṣajam ǀtát ǀ śam-yóḥ ǀ sumnám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines, We pray for joy and health and strength.
verses.wilson_translation: We ask the felicity ofŚaṃyu, from Rudra, the encourager of hymns, the protector of sacrifices, possessed of medicaments that confer delight.
verses.griffith_verse: To Rudra Lord of sacrifice, of hymns and balmy medicines, We pray for joy and health and strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः शुक्र इव सूर्यो हिरण्यमिव रोचते ।श्रेष्ठो देवानां वसुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ śukráḥ-iva ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ híraṇyam-iva ǀ rócate ǀśréṣṭhaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ vásuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he, The good, the best among the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Who is so brilliant asŚaṃyu, who gratifies like gold, the best of the gods, the provider of habitations?
verses.griffith_verse: He shines in splendour like the Sun, refulgent as bright gold is he, The good, the best among the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शं नः करत्यर्वते सुगं मेषाय मेष्ये ।नृभ्यो नारिभ्यो गवे ॥
verses.transliteration: śám ǀ naḥ ǀ karati ǀ árvate ǀ su-gám ǀ meṣā́ya ǀ meṣyé ǀnṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ nā́ri-bhyaḥ ǀ gáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes, To men, to women, and to kine.
verses.wilson_translation: Who bestows easily-obtained happiness on our steeds, our rams, our ewes, our men, our women, and our cows?
verses.griffith_verse: May he grant health into our steeds, wellbeing to our rams and ewes, To men, to women, and to kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे सोम श्रियमधि नि धेहि शतस्य नृणां ।महि श्रवस्तुविनृम्णं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ soma ǀ śríyam ǀ ádhi ǀ ní ǀ dhehi ǀ śatásya ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀmáhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ tuvi-nṛmṇám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men, The great renown of mighty chiefs.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, grant us prosperity more than (sufficient for) a hundred men, and much strength-engendering food.
verses.griffith_verse: O Soma, set thou upon us the glory of a hundred men, The great renown of mighty chiefs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नः सोमपरिबाधो मारातयो जुहुरंत ।आ न इंदो वाजे भज ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ soma-paribā́dhaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ juhuranta ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ indo íti ǀ vā́je ǀ bhaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us. Indu, give us a share of strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the adversaries of Soma, let not our enemies, harm us; cherish us,Indra, with (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not malignities, nor those who trouble Soma, hinder us. Indu, give us a share of strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यास्ते प्रजा अमृतस्य परस्मिन्धामन्नृतस्य ।मूर्धा नाभा सोम वेन आभूषंतीः सोम वेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ párasmin ǀ dhā́man ǀ ṛtásya ǀmūrdhā́ ǀ nā́bhā ǀ soma ǀ venaḥ ǀ ā-bhū́ṣantīḥ ǀ soma ǀ vedaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee, Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, who are immortal, and abide in an excellent dwelling, have regard for your subjects, when at their head in the hall of sacrifice you observe them (engaed in) decorating you.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma! head, central point, love these; Soma! know these as serving thee, Children of thee Immortal, at the highest place of holy law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIV. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १४ प्रस्कण्वः काण्वः। अग्निः, १-२ अग्निः, अश्विनौ, उषाश्च। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समाः सतोबृहत्यः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: IMMORTAL Jātavedas, thou many-hued fulgent gift of Dawn,Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn. For thou art offering-bearer and loved messenger, the charioteer of sacrifice:Accordant with the Aśvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame. As messenger we choose to-day Agni the good whom many love,Smoke-bannered spreader of the light, at break of day glory of sacrificial rites. Him noblest and most youthful, richly worshipped guest, dear to the men who offer gifts,Him, Agni Jātavedas, I beseech at dawn that he may bring the Gods to us. Thee, Agni, will I glorify, deathless nourisher of the world,Immortal, offering-bearer, meet for sacred food, preserver, best at sacrifice. Tell good things to thy praiser, O most youthful God, as richly worshipped, honey-tongued,And, granting to Praskaṇva lengthened days of life, show honour to the Heavenly Host. For the men, Agni, kindle thee as all possessor and as Priest;So Agni, much-invoked, bring hither with all speed the Gods, the excellently wise, At dawn of day, at night, Uṣas and Savitar, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Agni's self:Skilled in fair rites, with Soma poured, the Kaṇvas light thee, the oblation-wafting God. For, Agni, Lord of sacrifice and messenger of men art thou:Bring thou the Gods who wake at dawn who see the light, this day to drink the Soma juice. Thou shonest forth, O Agni, after former dawns, all visible, O rich in light.Thou art our help in battle-strife, the Friend of man, the great high priest in sacrifice. Like Manu, we will stablish thee, Agni, performer of the rite,Invoker, ministering Priest, exceeding wise, the swift immortal messenger. When as the Gods’ High Priest, by many loved, thou dost their mission as their nearest Friend,Then, like the far-resounding billows of the flood, thy flames, O Agni, roar aloud. Hear, Agni, who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods;Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass. Let those who strengthen Law, who bountifully give, the life-tongued Maruts, hear our praise.May Law-supporting Varuṇa with the Aśvins twain and Uṣas, drink the Soma juice.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने विवस्वदुषसश्चित्रं राधो अमर्त्य ।आ दाशुषे जातवेदो वहा त्वमद्या देवाँ उषर्बुधः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ vívasvat ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ citrám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ amartya ǀā́ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ vaha ǀ tvám ǀ adyá ǀ devā́n ǀ uṣaḥ-búdhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: IMMORTAL Jātavedas, thou many-hued fulgent gift of Dawn, Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are immortal, and cognisant of all begotten things, bring from the dawn to the donor (of the oblation) wealth of many sorts, with an excellent habitation; bring hither today the gods awaking with the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: IMMORTAL Jātavedas, thou many-hued fulgent gift of Dawn, Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जुष्टो हि दूतो असि हव्यवाहनोऽग्ने रथीरध्वराणां ।सजूरश्विभ्यामुषसा सुवीर्यमस्मे धेहि श्रवो बृहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: júṣṭaḥ ǀ hí ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ási ǀ havya-vā́hanaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ rathī́ḥ ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǀsa-jū́ḥ ǀ aśví-bhyām ǀ uṣásā ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ asmé íti ǀ dhehi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǁ
verses.english_translation: For thou art offering-bearer and loved messenger, the charioteer of sacrifice: Accordant with the Aśvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame.
verses.wilson_translation: For you,Agni, are the accepted messenger of the gods, the bearer of oblations, the vehicle of sacrifices; associated with Uṣas and the Aśvins, bestow upon us abundant and invigorating food.
verses.griffith_verse: For thou art offering-bearer and loved messenger, the charioteer of sacrifice: Accordant with the Aśvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्या दूतं वृणीमहे वसुमग्निं पुरुप्रियं ।धूमकेतुं भाऋजीकं व्युष्टिषु यज्ञानामध्वरश्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: adyá ǀ dūtám ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ vásum ǀ agním ǀ puru-priyám ǀdhūmá-ketum ǀ bhā́ḥ-ṛjīkam ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ yajñā́nām ǀ adhvara-śríyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As messenger we choose to-day Agni the good whom many love, Smoke-bannered spreader of the light, at break of day glory of sacrificial rites.
verses.wilson_translation: We select today Agni, the messenger, the giver of dwellings, the beloved of many, the smoke-bannered, the light-shedding, the protector of the worship of the worshipper at the break of day.
verses.griffith_verse: As messenger we choose to-day Agni the good whom many love, Smoke-bannered spreader of the light, at break of day glory of sacrificial rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रेष्ठं यविष्ठमतिथिं स्वाहुतं जुष्टं जनाय दाशुषे ।देवाँ अच्छा यातवे जातवेदसमग्निमीळे व्युष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: śréṣṭham ǀ yáviṣṭham ǀ átithim ǀ sú-āhutam ǀ júṣṭam ǀ jánāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀdevā́n ǀ áccha ǀ yā́tave ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ agním ǀ īḷe ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him noblest and most youthful, richly worshipped guest, dear to the men who offer gifts, Him, Agni Jātavedas, I beseech at dawn that he may bring the Gods to us.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise Agniat the break of day, the best and youngest (of the gods), the guest (of man), the universally-invoked, who is friendly to the man that offers (oblations), who knows all that are born, that he may go (to bring) the other divinities.
verses.griffith_verse: Him noblest and most youthful, richly worshipped guest, dear to the men who offer gifts, Him, Agni Jātavedas, I beseech at dawn that he may bring the Gods to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तविष्यामि त्वामहं विश्वस्यामृत भोजन ।अग्ने त्रातारममृतं मियेध्य यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन ॥
verses.transliteration: staviṣyā́mi ǀ tvā́m ǀ ahám ǀ víśvasya ǀ amṛta ǀ bhojana ǀágne ǀ trātā́ram ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ miyedhya ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ havya-vāhana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, Agni, will I glorify, deathless nourisher of the world, Immortal, offering-bearer, meet for sacred food, preserver, best at sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, immortal sustainer of the universe, bearer of oblations, deserving of adoration, I will praise you, who are exempt from death, the preserver of the sacrificer.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, Agni, will I glorify, deathless nourisher of the world, Immortal, offering-bearer, meet for sacred food, preserver, best at sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुशंसो बोधि गृणते यविष्ठ्य मधुजिह्वः स्वाहुतः ।प्रस्कण्वस्य प्रतिरन्नायुर्जीवसे नमस्या दैव्यं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: su-śáṃsaḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǀ mádhu-jihvaḥ ǀ sú-āhutaḥ ǀpráskaṇvasya ǀ pra-tirán ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ jīváse ǀ namasyá ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tell good things to thy praiser, O most youthful God, as richly worshipped, honey-tongued, And, granting to Praskaṇva lengthened days of life, show honour to the Heavenly Host.
verses.wilson_translation: Juvenile Agni, whose flames delight, who ar euniversally invoked, and are praised (by us) on behalf of the worshipper, understand (our wishes), and granting Praskaṇvato live a lengthened life, do honour to the divine man.
verses.griffith_verse: Tell good things to thy praiser, O most youthful God, as richly worshipped, honey-tongued, And, granting to Praskaṇva lengthened days of life, show honour to the Heavenly Host.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: होतारं विश्ववेदसं सं हि त्वा विश इंधते ।स आ वह पुरुहूत प्रचेतसोऽग्ने देवाँ इह द्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: hótāram ǀ viśvá-vedasam ǀ sám ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ víśaḥ ǀ indháte ǀsáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ puru-hūta ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ devā́n ǀ ihá ǀ dravát ǁ
verses.english_translation: For the men, Agni, kindle thee as all possessor and as Priest; So Agni, much-invoked, bring hither with all speed the Gods, the excellently wise,
verses.wilson_translation: All people kindle you,Agni, the sacrificer, the omniscient; do you, Agni, who are invoked by many, quickly bring hither the sapient deities.
verses.griffith_verse: For the men, Agni, kindle thee as all possessor and as Priest; So Agni, much-invoked, bring hither with all speed the Gods, the excellently wise,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सवितारमुषसमश्विना भगमग्निं व्युष्टिषु क्षपः ।कण्वासस्त्वा सुतसोमास इंधते हव्यवाहं स्वध्वर ॥
verses.transliteration: savitā́ram ǀ uṣásam ǀ aśvínā ǀ bhágam ǀ agním ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ kṣápaḥ ǀkáṇvāsaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ sutá-somāsaḥ ǀ indhate ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ su-adhvara ǁ
verses.english_translation: At dawn of day, at night, Uṣas and Savitar, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Agni's self: Skilled in fair rites, with Soma poured, the Kaṇvas light thee, the oblation-wafting God.
verses.wilson_translation: Object of holy rites, (bring hither) on the dawn following the night,Savitā, Uṣas and Aśvins,Bhagaand Agni; the Kaṇvaspouring out libations, kindle the water of the burnt offering.
verses.griffith_verse: At dawn of day, at night, Uṣas and Savitar, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Agni's self: Skilled in fair rites, with Soma poured, the Kaṇvas light thee, the oblation-wafting God.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पतिर्ह्यध्वराणामग्ने दूतो विशामसि ।उषर्बुध आ वह सोमपीतये देवाँ अद्य स्वर्दृशः ॥
verses.transliteration: pátiḥ ǀ hí ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǀ ágne ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ ási ǀuṣaḥ-búdhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ devā́n ǀ adyá ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, Agni, Lord of sacrifice and messenger of men art thou: Bring thou the Gods who wake at dawn who see the light, this day to drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are the protector of the sacrifices of the people, and the messenger (of the gods); bring hither today the gods awaking at dawn, and contemplating the sun, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: For, Agni, Lord of sacrifice and messenger of men art thou: Bring thou the Gods who wake at dawn who see the light, this day to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने पूर्वा अनूषसो विभावसो दीदेथ विश्वदर्शतः ।असि ग्रामेष्वविता पुरोहितोऽसि यज्ञेषु मानुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vibhāvaso íti vibhā-vaso ǀ dīdétha ǀ viśvá-darśataḥ ǀási ǀ grā́meṣu ǀ avitā́ ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǀ ási ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou shonest forth, O Agni, after former dawns, all visible, O rich in light. Thou art our help in battle-strife, the Friend of man, the great high priest in sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent Agni, visible to all, you have blazed after many preceding dawns, you are the protector (of people) in villages, you are the associate of man plural ced on the east (of the altar).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou shonest forth, O Agni, after former dawns, all visible, O rich in light. Thou art our help in battle-strife, the Friend of man, the great high priest in sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि त्वा यज्ञस्य साधनमग्ने होतारमृत्विजं ।मनुष्वद्देव धीमहि प्रचेतसं जीरं दूतममर्त्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tvā ǀ yajñásya ǀ sā́dhanam ǀ ágne ǀ hótāram ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀmanuṣvát ǀ deva ǀ dhīmahi ǀ prá-cetasam ǀ jīrám ǀ dūtám ǀ ámartyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like Manu, we will stablish thee, Agni, performer of the rite, Invoker, ministering Priest, exceeding wise, the swift immortal messenger.
verses.wilson_translation: We plural ce you,Agni, as Manuplural ced you, who are the implement of sacrifice, the invoker, the ministering priest, very wise, the destroyer (of foes), immortal, the messenger (of the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Like Manu, we will stablish thee, Agni, performer of the rite, Invoker, ministering Priest, exceeding wise, the swift immortal messenger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्देवानां मित्रमहः पुरोहितोऽंतरो यासि दूत्यं ।सिंधोरिव प्रस्वनितास ऊर्मयोऽग्नेर्भ्राजंते अर्चयः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ devā́nām ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǀ ántaraḥ ǀ yā́si ǀ dūtyám ǀsíndhoḥ-iva ǀ prá-svanitāsaḥ ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ bhrājante ǀ arcáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When as the Gods’ High Priest, by many loved, thou dost their mission as their nearest Friend, Then, like the far-resounding billows of the flood, thy flames, O Agni, roar aloud.
verses.wilson_translation: When, cherisher of friends, you are present as the Purohitaat a sacrifice, and discharge the mission of the gods, then your flames roar like the resounding billows of the ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: When as the Gods’ High Priest, by many loved, thou dost their mission as their nearest Friend, Then, like the far-resounding billows of the flood, thy flames, O Agni, roar aloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुधि श्रुत्कर्ण वह्निभिर्देवैरग्ने सयावभिः ।आ सीदंतु बर्हिषि मित्रो अर्यमा प्रातर्यावाणो अध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: śrudhí ǀ śrut-karṇa ǀ váhni-bhiḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ agne ǀ sayā́va-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ sīdantu ǀ barhíṣi ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ prātaḥ-yā́vānaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear, Agni, who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods; Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, with sharp ears, hear me; let Mitraand Aryaman, and Aryaman, and (other) early-stirring deities, with all the accompanying oblation-bearing gods, sit down at the sacrifice upon the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear, Agni, who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods; Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शृण्वंतु स्तोमं मरुतः सुदानवोऽग्निजिह्वा ऋतावृधः ।पिबतु सोमं वरुणो धृतव्रतोऽश्विभ्यामुषसा सजूः ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛṇvántu ǀ stómam ǀ marútaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ agni-jihvā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀpíbatu ǀ sómam ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ aśví-bhyām ǀ uṣásā ǀ sa-jū́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let those who strengthen Law, who bountifully give, the life-tongued Maruts, hear our praise. May Law-supporting Varuṇa with the Aśvins twain and Uṣas, drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the munificent Maruts, who have tongues of fire, and are encouragers of sacrifice, hear our praise; let the rite-fulfilling Varuṇa, with the Aśvins, and with Uṣas, drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: Let those who strengthen Law, who bountifully give, the life-tongued Maruts, hear our praise. May Law-supporting Varuṇa with the Aśvins twain and Uṣas, drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WORSHIP the Vasus, Agni! here, the Rudras, the Ādityas, allWho spring from Manu, those who know fair rites, who pour their blessings down. Agni, the Gods who understand give ear unto the worshipper:Lord of Red Steeds, who lovest song, bring thou those Three-and-Thirty Gods. O Jātavedas, great in act, hearken thou to Praskaṇva's call,As Priyamedha erst was heard, Atri, Virūpa, Aṅgiras. The sons of Priyamedha skilled in lofty praise have called for helpOn Agni who with fulgent flame is Ruler of all holy rites. Hear thou, invoked with holy oil, bountiful giver of rewards,These eulogies, whereby the sons of Kaṇva call thee to their aid. O Agni, loved by many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homesMen call on thee whose hair is flame, to be the bearer of their gifts. Thee, Agni, best to find out wealth, most widely famous, quick to hear,Singers have stablished in their rites Herald and ministering Priest. Singers with Soma pressed have made thee, Agni, hasten to the feast,Great light to mortal worshipper, what time they bring the sacred gift. Good, bounteous, Son of Strength, this day seat here on sacred grass the GodsWho come at early morn, the host of heaven, to drink the Soma juice Bring with joint invocations thou, O Agni, the celestial host:Here stands the Soma, bounteous Gods drink this expressed ere yesterday.

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने वसूँरिह रुद्राँ आदित्याँ उत ।यजा स्वध्वरं जनं मनुजातं घृतप्रुषं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ vásūn ǀ ihá ǀ rudrā́n ǀ ādityā́n ǀ utá ǀyája ǀ su-adhvarám ǀ jánam ǀ mánu-jātam ǀ ghṛta-prúṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: WORSHIP the Vasus, Agni! here, the Rudras, the Ādityas, all Who spring from Manu, those who know fair rites, who pour their blessings down.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, do you, in this our rite, worship the Vasus, the Rudras, theĀdityas, or any other (living) being sprung from Manu, sacrificing well and sprinkling water.
verses.griffith_verse: WORSHIP the Vasus, Agni! here, the Rudras, the Ādityas, all Who spring from Manu, those who know fair rites, who pour their blessings down.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुष्टीवानो हि दाशुषे देवा अग्ने विचेतसः ।तान्रोहिदश्व गिर्वणस्त्रयस्त्रिंशतमा वह ॥
verses.transliteration: śruṣṭī-vā́naḥ ǀ hí ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ ví-cetasaḥ ǀtā́n ǀ rohit-aśva ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ tráyaḥ-triṃśatam ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the Gods who understand give ear unto the worshipper: Lord of Red Steeds, who lovest song, bring thou those Three-and-Thirty Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily the discriminating gods are givers of rewards to the offerer (of oblations); lord of red coursers, propitiated by our praises, bring hither the three and thirty divinities.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, the Gods who understand give ear unto the worshipper: Lord of Red Steeds, who lovest song, bring thou those Three-and-Thirty Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रियमेधवदत्रिवज्जातवेदो विरूपवत् ।अंगिरस्वन्महिव्रत प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: priyamedha-vát ǀ atri-vát ǀ jā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ virūpa-vát ǀaṅgirasvát ǀ mahi-vrata ǀ práskaṇvasya ǀ śrudhi ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Jātavedas, great in act, hearken thou to Praskaṇva's call, As Priyamedha erst was heard, Atri, Virūpa, Aṅgiras.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, accomplisher of solemn acts, cognisant of all who are born, hear the invocation ofpraskaṇva, as you have heard those of Priyamedhaof Atri, of Virūpa, of Aṅgiras.
verses.griffith_verse: O Jātavedas, great in act, hearken thou to Praskaṇva's call, As Priyamedha erst was heard, Atri, Virūpa, Aṅgiras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महिकेरव ऊतये प्रियमेधा अहूषत ।राजंतमध्वराणामग्निं शुक्रेण शोचिषा ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi-keravaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ priyá-medhāḥ ǀ ahūṣata ǀrā́jantam ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǀ agním ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sons of Priyamedha skilled in lofty praise have called for help On Agni who with fulgent flame is Ruler of all holy rites.
verses.wilson_translation: The performers of great ceremonies, the offerers of acceptable sacrifices, have invoked for (their protection),Agni, shining amidst the solemnities, with pure resplendence.
verses.griffith_verse: The sons of Priyamedha skilled in lofty praise have called for help On Agni who with fulgent flame is Ruler of all holy rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृताहवन संत्येमा उ षु श्रुधी गिरः ।याभिः कण्वस्य सूनवो हवंतेऽवसे त्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛ́ta-āhavana ǀ santya ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ śrudhi ǀ gíraḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ káṇvasya ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ hávante ǀ ávase ǀ tvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear thou, invoked with holy oil, bountiful giver of rewards, These eulogies, whereby the sons of Kaṇva call thee to their aid.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoked by oblations, giver of rewards, listen to these praises with which the sons of Kaṇvainvoke you for protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear thou, invoked with holy oil, bountiful giver of rewards, These eulogies, whereby the sons of Kaṇva call thee to their aid.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां चित्रश्रवस्तम हवंते विक्षु जंतवः ।शोचिष्केशं पुरुप्रियाग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ citraśravaḥ-tama ǀ hávante ǀ vikṣú ǀ jantávaḥ ǀśocíḥ-keśam ǀ puru-priya ǀ ágne ǀ havyā́ya ǀ vóḷhave ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, loved by many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homes Men call on thee whose hair is flame, to be the bearer of their gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, granter of abundant sustenance, who are beloved of many, the sons of men invoke you, radiant-haired, to bear the oblation (to the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, loved by many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homes Men call on thee whose hair is flame, to be the bearer of their gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि त्वा होतारमृत्विजं दधिरे वसुवित्तमं ।श्रुत्कर्णं सप्रथस्तमं विप्रा अग्ने दिविष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tvā ǀ hótāram ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀ dadhiré ǀ vasuvít-tamam ǀśrút-karṇam ǀ sapráthaḥ-tamam ǀ víprāḥ ǀ agne ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, Agni, best to find out wealth, most widely famous, quick to hear, Singers have stablished in their rites Herald and ministering Priest.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise have plural ced you,Agni, in (their) sacrifices as the invoker, the ministrant priest, the donor of vast wealth, the quick-hearing the far-renowned.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, Agni, best to find out wealth, most widely famous, quick to hear, Singers have stablished in their rites Herald and ministering Priest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वा विप्रा अचुच्यवुः सुतसोमा अभि प्रयः ।बृहद्भा बिभ्रतो हविरग्ने मर्ताय दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ víprāḥ ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀ sutá-somāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ práyaḥ ǀbṛhát ǀ bhā́ḥ ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ ágne ǀ mártāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Singers with Soma pressed have made thee, Agni, hasten to the feast, Great light to mortal worshipper, what time they bring the sacred gift.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise (priests), with effused libations of Somajuice, have summoned you, vast and brilliant Agni, to partake of the (sacrificial food) as they hold the oblation on the part of the individual who presents it.
verses.griffith_verse: Singers with Soma pressed have made thee, Agni, hasten to the feast, Great light to mortal worshipper, what time they bring the sacred gift.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्याव्णः सहस्कृत सोमपेयाय संत्य ।इहाद्य दैव्यं जनं बर्हिरा सादया वसो ॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-yā́vnaḥ ǀ sahaḥ-kṛta ǀ soma-péyāya ǀ santya ǀihá ǀ adyá ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sādaya ǀ vaso íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Good, bounteous, Son of Strength, this day seat here on sacred grass the Gods Who come at early morn, the host of heaven, to drink the Soma juice
verses.wilson_translation: Strength-genitive rated, giver of rewards, provider of dwellings, plural ce here today upon the sacred grass the morning-moving deities, or (other) deified being, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.griffith_verse: Good, bounteous, Son of Strength, this day seat here on sacred grass the Gods Who come at early morn, the host of heaven, to drink the Soma juice
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वांचं दैव्यं जनमग्ने यक्ष्व सहूतिभिः ।अयं सोमः सुदानवस्तं पात तिरोअह्न्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ñcam ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǀ ágne ǀ yákṣva ǀ sáhūti-bhiḥ ǀayám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ tám ǀ pāta ǀ tiráḥ-ahnyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring with joint invocations thou, O Agni, the celestial host: Here stands the Soma, bounteous Gods drink this expressed ere yesterday.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship with conjoint invocations,Agni, the present deified being; bounteous divinities, this is the Somajuice; drink it, for it was yesterday expressed.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring with joint invocations thou, O Agni, the celestial host: Here stands the Soma, bounteous Gods drink this expressed ere yesterday.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVI. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky:High, Aśvins, I extol your praise, Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, yeGods with deep thought who find out wealth. Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames,When your car flies with winged steeds. He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant,Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full. Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nāsatyas, thinking of our words:Drink boldly of the Soma juice. Vouchsafe to us, O Aśvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light,May through the darkness carry us. Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shoreO Aśvins, harness ye the car. The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waitsDrops, with the hymn, have been prepared. Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place:Where will ye manifest your form? Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold:And with its tongue shone forth the dark. The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal:The road of heaven was manifest. The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aśvins give,who save when Soma gladdens them. Ye dwellers with Vivasvān come, auspicious, as to Manu erst;come to the Soma and our praise. O circumambient Aśvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way:Approve with beams our solemn rites. Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aśvins Twain,With aids which none may interrupt.
