verses.sanskrit: एषो उषा अपूर्व्या व्युच्छति प्रिया दिवः ।स्तुषे वामश्विना बृहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣó íti ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ápūrvyā ǀ ví ǀ ucchati ǀ priyā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀstuṣé ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ bṛhát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky: High, Aśvins, I extol your praise,
verses.wilson_translation: The beloved Uṣas, until now unseen, scatters darkness from the sky;Aśvins, I greatly praise you.
verses.griffith_verse: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky: High, Aśvins, I extol your praise,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या दस्रा सिंधुमातरा मनोतरा रयीणां ।धिया देवा वसुविदा ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ dasrā́ ǀ síndhu-mātarā ǀ manotárā ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀdhiyā́ ǀ devā́ ǀ vasu-vídā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Who are divine, of plural asing appearance, children of the sea, willing dispensers of wealth, and granters of dwellings (in recompense of) pious acts.
verses.griffith_verse: Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वच्यंते वां ककुहासो जूर्णायामधि विष्टपि ।यद्वां रथो विभिष्पतात् ॥
verses.transliteration: vacyánte ǀ vām ǀ kakuhā́saḥ ǀ jūrṇā́yām ǀ ádhi ǀ viṣṭápi ǀyát ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ ví-bhiḥ ǀ pátāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames, When your car flies with winged steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Since your chariot proceeds, (drawn) by your steeds, above the glorious heavens, your praises are proclaimed (by us).
verses.griffith_verse: Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames, When your car flies with winged steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हविषा जारो अपां पिपर्ति पपुरिर्नरा ।पिता कुटस्य चर्षणिः ॥
verses.transliteration: havíṣā ǀ jāráḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ píparti ǀ pápuriḥ ǀ narā ǀpitā́ ǀ kúṭasya ǀ carṣaṇíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant, Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.
verses.wilson_translation: (Aśvins); guides; the sun, (the evaporator) of the waters, the nourisher, the protector and beholder of the (solemn) rite, nourishes (the gods) with our oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant, Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदारो वां मतीनां नासत्या मतवचसा ।पातं सोमस्य धृष्णुया ॥
verses.transliteration: ādāráḥ ǀ vām ǀ matīnā́m ǀ nā́satyā ǀ mata-vacasā ǀpātám ǀ sómasya ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nāsatyas, thinking of our words: Drink boldly of the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, accepting our praises, partake of the exhilarating Soma, the animator of your minds.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nāsatyas, thinking of our words: Drink boldly of the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या नः पीपरदश्विना ज्योतिष्मती तमस्तिरः ।तामस्मे रासाथामिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pī́parat ǀ aśvinā ǀ jyótiṣmatī ǀ támaḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀtā́m ǀ asmé íti ǀ rāsāthām ǀ íṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vouchsafe to us, O Aśvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, grant us that invigorating food which may satisfy us, having dispelled the gloom (of want).
verses.griffith_verse: Vouchsafe to us, O Aśvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो नावा मतीनां यातं पाराय गंतवे ।युंजाथामश्विना रथं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ nāvā́ ǀ matīnā́m ǀ yātám ǀ pārā́ya ǀ gántave ǀyuñjā́thām ǀ aśvinā ǀ rátham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore O Aśvins, harness ye the car.
verses.wilson_translation: Come as a ship, to bear us over an ocean of praises; harness,Aśvins, your car.
verses.griffith_verse: Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore O Aśvins, harness ye the car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अरित्रं वां दिवस्पृथु तीर्थे सिंधूनां रथः ।धिया युयुज्र इंदवः ॥
verses.transliteration: arítram ǀ vām ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthú ǀ tīrthé ǀ síndhūnām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀdhiyā́ ǀ yuyujre ǀ índavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.
verses.wilson_translation: Your vessel, vaster than the sky, stops on the seashore; your chariot (waits on the land); the drops (of Soma) are expressed for yor worship.
verses.griffith_verse: The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवस्कण्वास इंदवो वसु सिंधूनां पदे ।स्वं वव्रिं कुह धित्सथः ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ kaṇvāsaḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǀ vásu ǀ síndhūnām ǀ padé ǀsvám ǀ vavrím ǀ kúha ǀ dhitsathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place: Where will ye manifest your form?
verses.wilson_translation: Kaṇvas(ask this of the Aśvins); (How) do the rays (of the sun proceed) from the sky? (How) does the dawn (rise) in the region of the waters? Where do you desire to manifest your own person ns?
verses.griffith_verse: Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place: Where will ye manifest your form?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभूदु भा उ अंशवे हिरण्यं प्रति सूर्यः ।व्यख्यज्जिह्वयासितः ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bhā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ aṃśáve ǀ híraṇyam ǀ práti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀví ǀ akhyat ǀ jihváyā ǀ ásitaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold: And with its tongue shone forth the dark.
verses.wilson_translation: There was light to irradiate the dawn; the sun (rose) like god; the fire shone with darkened flames.
verses.griffith_verse: Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold: And with its tongue shone forth the dark.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभूदु पारमेतवे पंथा ऋतस्य साधुया ।अदर्शि वि स्रुतिर्दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ pārám ǀ étave ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ sādhu-yā́ ǀádarśi ǀ ví ǀ srutíḥ ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal: The road of heaven was manifest.
verses.wilson_translation: A fit path was made for the sun to go beyond the boundary (of night); the radiance of the luminary became visible.
verses.griffith_verse: The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal: The road of heaven was manifest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तत्तदिदश्विनोरवो जरिता प्रति भूषति ।मदे सोमस्य पिप्रतोः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát-tat ǀ ít ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ ávaḥ ǀ jaritā́ ǀ práti ǀ bhūṣati ǀmáde ǀ sómasya ǀ pípratoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aśvins give, who save when Soma gladdens them.
verses.wilson_translation: The worshipper acknowledges whatever boon he receives from the Aśvins, satiate with the enjoyment of Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aśvins give, who save when Soma gladdens them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वावसाना विवस्वति सोमस्य पीत्या गिरा ।मनुष्वच्छंभू आ गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: vavasānā́ ǀ vivásvati ǀ sómasya ǀ pītyā́ ǀ girā́ ǀmanuṣvát ǀ śaṃbhū íti śam-bhū ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye dwellers with Vivasvān come, auspicious, as to Manu erst; come to the Soma and our praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Causers of felicity, co-dwellers with your worshipper, as with Manucome hither to drink of Soma, and (accept) our praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye dwellers with Vivasvān come, auspicious, as to Manu erst; come to the Soma and our praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवोरुषा अनु श्रियं परिज्मनोरुपाचरत् ।ऋता वनथो अक्तुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ śríyam ǀ pári-jmanoḥ ǀ upa-ā́carat ǀṛtā́ ǀ vanathaḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O circumambient Aśvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way: Approve with beams our solemn rites.
verses.wilson_translation: May Uṣas follow the lustre of your approach, circumambient Aśvins, and may you be plural ased with the oblations offered by night.
verses.griffith_verse: O circumambient Aśvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way: Approve with beams our solemn rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उभा पिबतमश्विनोभा नः शर्म यच्छतं ।अविद्रियाभिरूतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhā́ ǀ pibatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ ubhā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatam ǀavidriyā́bhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aśvins Twain, With aids which none may interrupt.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, may you both drink (the oblation), and bestow upon us happiness, through your irreproachable protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aśvins Twain, With aids which none may interrupt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVII. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: १० प्रस्कण्वः काण्वः। अश्विनौ। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समा सतोबृहत्यः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: AŚVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed.Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it. Come, O ye Aśvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of formTo you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call. O Aśvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice.Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds. Omniscient Aśvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice.The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured. O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully,Keep us, O Lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law. O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudās abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car;So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea. Nāsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaśa,Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come. So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here.Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass. Come, O Nāsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy,Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice. With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us;For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aśvins, drunk the Soma juice.

verses.sanskrit: अयं वां मधुमत्तमः सुतः सोम ऋतावृधा ।तमश्विना पिबतं तिरोअह्न्यं धत्तं रत्नानि दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vām ǀ mádhumat-tamaḥ ǀ sutáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛdhā ǀtám ǀ aśvinā ǀ pibatam ǀ tiráḥ-ahnyam ǀ dhattám ǀ rátnāni ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: AŚVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed. Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, encouragers of sacrifice, this most sweet Somais prepared for you; drink it of yesterday's expressing, and grant riches to the donor.
verses.griffith_verse: AŚVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed. Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिवंधुरेण त्रिवृता सुपेशसा रथेना यातमश्विना ।कण्वासो वां ब्रह्म कृण्वंत्यध्वरे तेषां सु शृणुतं हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-vandhuréṇa ǀ tri-vṛ́tā ǀ su-péśasā ǀ ráthena ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ aśvinā ǀkáṇvāsaḥ ǀ vām ǀ bráhma ǀ kṛṇvanti ǀ adhvaré ǀ téṣām ǀ sú ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, O ye Aśvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of form To you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Aśvins, with your three-columned triangular car; the Kaṇvasrepeat your praise at the sacrifice; graciously hear their invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, O ye Aśvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of form To you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्विना मधुमत्तमं पातं सोममृतावृधा ।अथाद्य दस्रा वसु बिभ्रता रथे दाश्वांसमुप गच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvinā ǀ mádhumat-tamam ǀ pātám ǀ sómam ǀ ṛta-vṛdhā ǀátha ǀ adyá ǀ dasrā ǀ vásu ǀ bíbhratā ǀ ráthe ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ úpa ǀ gacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice. Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, encouragers of sacrifice, drink this most sweet Soma; approach today the giver of the offering, you who are of plural asing aspects and bearers of wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice. Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिषधस्थे बर्हिषि विश्ववेदसा मध्वा यज्ञं मिमिक्षतं ।कण्वासो वां सुतसोमा अभिद्यवो युवां हवंते अश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-sadhasthé ǀ barhíṣi ǀ viśva-vedasā ǀ mádhvā ǀ yajñám ǀ mimikṣatam ǀkáṇvāsaḥ ǀ vām ǀ sutá-somāḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǀ yuvā́m ǀ havante ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Omniscient Aśvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice. The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.
verses.wilson_translation: Omniscient Aśvins, stationed on the thrice-heaped sacred grass, sprinkle the sacrifice with the sweet juice; the illustrious Kaṇvas, with effused libations, invoke you.
verses.griffith_verse: Omniscient Aśvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice. The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः कण्वमभिष्टिभिः प्रावतं युवमश्विना ।ताभिः ष्वस्माँ अवतं शुभस्पती पातं सोममृतावृधा ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ káṇvam ǀ abhíṣṭi-bhiḥ ǀ prá ǀ ā́vatam ǀ yuvám ǀ aśvinā ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ sú ǀ asmā́n ǀ avatam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ pātám ǀ sómam ǀ ṛta-vṛdhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully, Keep us, O Lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.
verses.wilson_translation: With such desired aids as you protected Kaṇvawith, do you, cherish of pious acts, preserve us; encouragers of sacrifice, drink the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully, Keep us, O Lords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुदासे दस्रा वसु बिभ्रता रथे पृक्षो वहतमश्विना ।रयिं समुद्रादुत वा दिवस्पर्यस्मे धत्तं पुरुस्पृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: su-dā́se ǀ dasrā ǀ vásu ǀ bíbhratā ǀ ráthe ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ vahatam ǀ aśvinā ǀrayím ǀ samudrā́t ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ asmé íti ǀ dhattam ǀ puru-spṛ́ham ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudās abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car; So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: Good-looking Aśvins, as you brought in your car, bearers of wealth, abundance to Sudās, so bring to us in the riches that many covet, whether from the firmament or the sky beyond.
verses.griffith_verse: O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudās abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car; So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यन्नासत्या परावति यद्वा स्थो अधि तुर्वशे ।अतो रथेन सुवृता न आ गतं साकं सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ nāsatyā ǀ parā-váti ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ stháḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ turváśe ǀátaḥ ǀ ráthena ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ sākám ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nāsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaśa, Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, whether you abide far off or close athand, come to us in your well-constructed car, with the rays of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Nāsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaśa, Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वांचा वां सप्तयोऽध्वरश्रियो वहंतु सवनेदुप ।इषं पृंचंता सुकृते सुदानव आ बर्हिः सीदतं नरा ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ñcā ǀ vām ǀ sáptayaḥ ǀ adhvara-śríyaḥ ǀ váhantu ǀ sávanā ǀ ít ǀ úpa ǀíṣam ǀ pṛñcántā ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ su-dā́nave ǀ ā́ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sīdatam ǀ narā ǁ
verses.english_translation: So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here. Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Let your coursers, the grace of the sacrifice, bring you to be present at our rite; guides (of men) bestowing food upon the pious and liberal donor (of the offering), sit down on the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here. Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेन नासत्या गतं रथेन सूर्यत्वचा ।येन शश्वदूहथुर्दाशुषे वसु मध्वः सोमस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: téna ǀ nāsatyā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ ráthena ǀ sū́rya-tvacā ǀyéna ǀ śáśvat ǀ ūháthuḥ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vásu ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, O Nāsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy, Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Nāsatyas, with your sun-clad chariot, in which you have ever conveyed wealth to the donor (of the offering), to drink of the sweet Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, O Nāsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy, Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उक्थेभिरर्वागवसे पुरूवसू अर्कैश्च नि ह्वयामहे ।शश्वत्कण्वानां सदसि प्रिये हि कं सोमं पपथुरश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: ukthébhiḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ ávase ǀ puruvásū íti puru-vásū ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ ca ǀ ní ǀ hvayāmahe ǀśáśvat ǀ káṇvānām ǀ sádasi ǀ priyé ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ sómam ǀ papáthuḥ ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us; For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aśvins, drunk the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke with chanted and recited hymns, the very affluent Aśvins, to be present for our protection. Have you not ever drunk the Somain the favoured dwelling of the Kaṇvas?
verses.griffith_verse: With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us; For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aśvins, drunk the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVIII. Dawn.
hymns.anukramani: १६ प्रस्कण्वः काण्वः। उषाः। प्रगाथः – विषमा बृहत्यः, समाः सतोबृहत्यः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One. They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us.O Uṣas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great. Uṣas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of carsWhich, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood. Here Kaṇva, chief of Kaṇva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes’ names,—The. princes who, O Uṣas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts. Like a good matron Uṣas comes carefully tending everything:Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up. She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs.O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest. This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun:Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men. To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light.Uṣas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away. Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and beaming on our solemn rites. For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth.Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call. O Uṣas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful.Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee. Bring from the firmament, O Uṣas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice,And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praise and hero might. May Uṣas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about,Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain. Mighty One, whom the Ṛṣis of old time invoked for their protection and their help,O Uṣas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light. Uṣas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven,So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine. Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food,To all-subduing splendour, Uṣas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.

verses.sanskrit: सह वामेन न उषो व्युच्छा दुहितर्दिवः ।सह द्युम्नेन बृहता विभावरि राया देवि दास्वती ॥
verses.transliteration: sahá ǀ vāména ǀ naḥ ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀsahá ǀ dyumnéna ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ vibhā-vari ǀ rāyā́ ǀ devi ǀ dā́svatī ǁ
verses.english_translation: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky, Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, daughter of heaven, dawn upon us with riches; diffuser of light, dawn upon us with abundant food; bountiful goddess, dawn upon with wealth (of cattle).
verses.griffith_verse: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky, Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्विश्वसुविदो भूरि च्यवंत वस्तवे ।उदीरय प्रति मा सूनृता उषश्चोद राधो मघोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: áśva-vatīḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ viśva-suvídaḥ ǀ bhū́ri ǀ cyavanta ǀ vástave ǀút ǀ īraya ǀ práti ǀ mā ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ códa ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ maghónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us. O Uṣas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great.
verses.wilson_translation: Abounding with horses, abounding with kine, bestowers of every sort of wealth, (the divinities of morning) are possessed of much that is necessary for the habitations (of men); Uṣas, speak to me kind words; send us the affluence of the wealthy.
verses.griffith_verse: They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us. O Uṣas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उवासोषा उच्छाच्च नु देवी जीरा रथानां ।ये अस्या आचरणेषु दध्रिरे समुद्रे न श्रवस्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: uvā́sa ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchā́t ǀ ca ǀ nú ǀ devī́ ǀ jīrā́ ǀ ráthānām ǀyé ǀ asyāḥ ǀ ā-cáraṇeṣu ǀ dadhriré ǀ samudré ǀ ná ǀ śravasyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uṣas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of cars Which, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Uṣas has dwelt (in heaven of old); may she dawn today, the excitress of chariots which are harnessed at her coming, as those who are desirous of wealth (send ships) to sea.
verses.griffith_verse: Uṣas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of cars Which, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषो ये ते प्र यामेषु युंजते मनो दानाय सूरयः ।अत्राह तत्कण्व एषां कण्वतमो नाम गृणाति नृणां ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ prá ǀ yā́meṣu ǀ yuñjáte ǀ mánaḥ ǀ dānā́ya ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ tát ǀ káṇvaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ káṇva-tamaḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ gṛṇāti ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here Kaṇva, chief of Kaṇva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes’ names,— The. princes who, O Uṣas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, at your comings wise men turn their minds to benefactions; of these men, the most wise Kaṇvaproclaims the fame.
verses.griffith_verse: Here Kaṇva, chief of Kaṇva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes’ names,— The. princes who, O Uṣas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ घा योषेव सूनर्युषा याति प्रभुंजती ।जरयंती वृजनं पद्वदीयत उत्पातयति पक्षिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gha ǀ yóṣā-iva ǀ sūnárī ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ yāti ǀ pra-bhuñjatī́ ǀjaráyantī ǀ vṛ́janam ǀ pat-vát ǀ īyate ǀ út ǀ pātayati ǀ pakṣíṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a good matron Uṣas comes carefully tending everything: Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, nourishing (all), comes daily like a matron, the directress (of household duties), conducting all transient (creatures) to decay; (at her coming) each biped stirs and she wakes up the birds.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a good matron Uṣas comes carefully tending everything: Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि या सृजति समनं व्यर्थिनः पदं न वेत्योदती ।वयो नकिष्टे पप्तिवांस आसते व्युष्टौ वाजिनीवति ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yā́ ǀ sṛjáti ǀ sámanam ǀ ví ǀ arthínaḥ ǀ padám ǀ ná ǀ veti ǀ ódatī ǀváyaḥ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ te ǀ papti-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ āsate ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ vājinī-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs. O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest.
verses.wilson_translation: She animates the diligent, and sends clients (to their patrons); and shedder of dews, knows not delay; bestower of food, at your rising the soaring birds no longer suspend (their flight).
verses.griffith_verse: She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs. O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एषायुक्त परावतः सूर्यस्योदयनादधि ।शतं रथेभिः सुभगोषा इयं वि यात्यभि मानुषान् ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ ayukta ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ ut-áyanāt ǀ ádhi ǀśatám ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ iyám ǀ ví ǀ yāti ǀ abhí ǀ mā́nuṣān ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun: Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men.
verses.wilson_translation: This auspicious Uṣas has harnessed (her vehicles) from afar, above the rising of the sun; and she comes gloriously upon man, with a hundred chariots.
verses.griffith_verse: This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun: Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वमस्या नानाम चक्षसे जगज्ज्योतिष्कृणोति सूनरी ।अप द्वेषो मघोनी दुहिता दिव उषा उच्छदप स्रिधः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvam ǀ asyāḥ ǀ nanāma ǀ cákṣase ǀ jágat ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ sūnárī ǀápa ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ maghónī ǀ duhitā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchat ǀ ápa ǀ srídhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light. Uṣas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away.
verses.wilson_translation: All living beings adore her, that she may be visible; bringer of good, she lights up the world; the affluent daughter of heaven drives away the malevolent and disperses the absorbers (of moisture).
verses.griffith_verse: To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light. Uṣas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उष आ भाहि भानुना चंद्रेण दुहितर्दिवः ।आवहंती भूर्यस्मभ्यं सौभगं व्युच्छंती दिविष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhāhi ǀ bhānúnā ǀ candréṇa ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀā-váhantī ǀ bhū́ri ǀ asmábhyam ǀ sáubhagam ǀ vi-ucchántī ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky, Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and beaming on our solemn rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Shine around, Uṣas, with cheering lustre, bringing us every day much happiness, and scattering darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky, Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and beaming on our solemn rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्य हि प्राणनं जीवनं त्वे वि यदुच्छसि सूनरि ।सा नो रथेन बृहता विभावरि श्रुधि चित्रामघे हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasya ǀ hí ǀ prā́ṇanam ǀ jī́vanam ǀ tvé íti ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ ucchási ǀ sūnari ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ráthena ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ vibhā-vari ǀ śrudhí ǀ citra-maghe ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth. Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch, bringer of good, as you dawn, the breath and life of all (creatures) rest in you; diffuser of light, come to us with your spacious car; possessor of wondrous wealth, hear our invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth. Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषो वाजं हि वंस्व यश्चित्रो मानुषे जने ।तेना वह सुकृतो अध्वराँ उप ये त्वा गृणंति वह्नयः ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ hí ǀ váṃsva ǀ yáḥ ǀ citráḥ ǀ mā́nuṣe ǀ jáne ǀténa ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ adhvarā́n ǀ úpa ǀ yé ǀ tvā ǀ gṛṇánti ǀ váhnayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Uṣas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful. Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, accept the (sacrificial) food which of many kinds exists among the human race, and thereby bring to the ceremony the pious, who offering oblations, praise you.
verses.griffith_verse: O Uṣas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful. Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वान्देवाँ आ वह सोमपीतयेऽंतरिक्षादुषस्त्वं ।सास्मासु धा गोमदश्वावदुक्थ्यमुषो वाजं सुवीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvān ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ tvám ǀsā́ ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhāḥ ǀ gó-mat ǀ áśva-vat ǀ ukthyám ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring from the firmament, O Uṣas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice, And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praise and hero might.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, bring from the firmament all the gods, to drink the Soma, and to you yourself bestow upon us excellent and invigorating food, along with cattle and horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring from the firmament, O Uṣas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice, And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praise and hero might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्या रुशंतो अर्चयः प्रति भद्रा अदृक्षत ।सा नो रयिं विश्ववारं सुपेशसमुषा ददातु सुग्म्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yásyāḥ ǀ rúśantaḥ ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ práti ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ ádṛkṣata ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ viśvá-vāram ǀ su-péśasam ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ dadātu ǀ súgmyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Uṣas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about, Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain.
verses.wilson_translation: May that Uṣas whose bright auspicious rays are visible all around, grant us desirable, agreeable, and easily-attainable riches.
verses.griffith_verse: May Uṣas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about, Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये चिद्धि त्वामृषयः पूर्व ऊतये जुहूरेऽवसे महि ।सा नः स्तोमाँ अभि गृणीहि राधसोषः शुक्रेण शोचिषा ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ tvā́m ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ ūtáye ǀ juhūré ǀ ávase ǀ mahi ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ stómān ǀ abhí ǀ gṛṇīhi ǀ rā́dhasā ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty One, whom the Ṛṣis of old time invoked for their protection and their help, O Uṣas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Uṣas, whom the ancient sages invoked for protection and for food, do you, (radiant) with pure light, (plural ased) by our offerings, accept our praises.
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty One, whom the Ṛṣis of old time invoked for their protection and their help, O Uṣas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषो यदद्य भानुना वि द्वारावृणवो दिवः ।प्र नो यच्छतादवृकं पृथु च्छर्दिः प्र देवि गोमतीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ yát ǀ adyá ǀ bhānúnā ǀ ví ǀ dvā́rau ǀ ṛṇávaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ yacchatāt ǀ avṛkám ǀ pṛthú ǀ chardíḥ ǀ prá ǀ devi ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uṣas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven, So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, since you have today set upon the two gates of heaven with light, grant us a spacious and secure habitation; bestow upon us, goddess, cattle and food.
verses.griffith_verse: Uṣas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven, So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं नो राया बृहता विश्वपेशसा मिमिक्ष्वा समिळाभिरा ।सं द्युम्नेन विश्वतुरोषो महि सं वाजैर्वाजिनीवति ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ naḥ ǀ rāyā́ ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ viśvá-peśasā ǀ mimikṣvá ǀ sám ǀ íḷābhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀsám ǀ dyumnéna ǀ viśva-túrā ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ mahi ǀ sám ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ vājinī-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food, To all-subduing splendour, Uṣas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Uṣas, associate us with much and multiform wealth, and with abundant cattle, with all foe-confounding fame, and giver of sustenance, with food.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food, To all-subduing splendour, Uṣas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIX. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Uṣas, by auspicious ways:Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice. The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Uṣas light to move,—Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today. Bright Uṣas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir,And round about flock winged birds from all the boundaries of heaven. Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm.Thee, as thou art, the Kaṇvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.

verses.sanskrit: उषो भद्रेभिरा गहि दिवश्चिद्रोचनादधि ।वहंत्वरुणप्सव उप त्वा सोमिनो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ bhadrébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ rocanā́t ǀ ádhi ǀváhantu ǀ aruṇá-psavaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ tvā ǀ somínaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Uṣas, by auspicious ways: Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, come by auspicious ways from above the bright (region of the) firmament; let the purple (kine) bring you to the dwelling of the offerr of Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Uṣas, by auspicious ways: Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुपेशसं सुखं रथं यमध्यस्था उषस्त्वं ।तेना सुश्रवसं जनं प्रावाद्य दुहितर्दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-péśasam ǀ su-khám ǀ rátham ǀ yám ǀ adhi-ásthāḥ ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ tvám ǀténa ǀ su-śrávasam ǀ jánam ǀ prá ǀ ava ǀ adyá ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Uṣas light to move,— Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, in the ample and beautiful chariot in which you ride, come today, daughter of heaven, to the pious offerer of the oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Uṣas light to move,— Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयश्चित्ते पतत्रिणो द्विपच्चतुष्पदर्जुनि ।उषः प्रारन्नृतूँरनु दिवो अंतेभ्यस्परि ॥
verses.transliteration: váyaḥ ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ patatríṇaḥ ǀ dvi-pát ǀ cátuḥ-pat ǀ arjuni ǀúṣaḥ ǀ prá ǀ āran ǀ ṛtū́n ǀ ánu ǀ diváḥ ǀ ántebhyaḥ ǀ pári ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bright Uṣas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir, And round about flock winged birds from all the boundaries of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: White-complexioned Uṣas, upon your coming, bipeds and quadrupeds (are in motion), and the winged birds flock around from the boundaries of the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Bright Uṣas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir, And round about flock winged birds from all the boundaries of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्युच्छंती हि रश्मिभिर्विश्वमाभासि रोचनं ।तां त्वामुषर्वसूयवो गीर्भिः कण्वा अहूषत ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-ucchántī ǀ hí ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā-bhā́si ǀ rocanám ǀtā́m ǀ tvā́m ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ vasu-yávaḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ káṇvāḥ ǀ ahūṣata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm. Thee, as thou art, the Kaṇvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.
verses.wilson_translation: You, Uṣas, dispersing the darkness, illumine the shining universe with your rays; such as you are,Kaṇvas, desirous of wealth, praise you with their hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm. Thee, as thou art, the Kaṇvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN L. Sūrya.
hymns.anukramani: १३ प्रस्कण्वः काण्वः। सूर्यः (११-१३ रोगघ्न्य उपनिषदः, १३ अन्त्योऽर्धर्चः द्विषद् घ्नश्च)। गायत्री, १०-१३ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: HIS bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives,Sūrya, that all may look on him. The constellations pass away, like thieves, together with their beams,Before the all-beholding Sun. His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o’er the world of men,Like flames of fire that burn and blaze. Swift and all beautiful art thou, O Sūrya, maker of the light,Illuming all the radiant realm. Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind,Hither all light to be beheld. With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuṇa,Upon the busy race of men, Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days,Sun, seeing all things that have birth. Seven Bay Steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One,God, Sūrya, with the radiant hair. Sūrya hath yoked the pure bright Seven, the daughters of the car; with these,His own dear team, he goeth forth. Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have comeTo Sūrya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent. Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven,Sūrya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue. To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness,Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritāla trees. With all his conquering vigour this Āditya hath gone up on high,Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.

verses.sanskrit: उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहंति केतवः ।दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyám ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ devám ǀ vahanti ǀ ketávaḥ ǀdṛśé ǀ víśvāya ǀ sū́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: HIS bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives, Sūrya, that all may look on him.
verses.wilson_translation: His coursers bear on high the divine all-knowing Sun, that he may be seen by all (the worlds).
verses.griffith_verse: HIS bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives, Sūrya, that all may look on him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप त्ये तायवो यथा नक्षत्रा यंत्यक्तुभिः ।सूराय विश्वचक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ tyé ǀ tāyávaḥ ǀ yathā ǀ nákṣatrā ǀ yanti ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀsū́rāya ǀ viśvá-cakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: The constellations pass away, like thieves, together with their beams, Before the all-beholding Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: (At the approach) of the all-illuminating Sun, the constellations depart with the night, like thieves.
verses.griffith_verse: The constellations pass away, like thieves, together with their beams, Before the all-beholding Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्रमस्य केतवो वि रश्मयो जनाँ अनु ।भ्राजंतो अग्नयो यथा ॥
verses.transliteration: ádṛśram ǀ asya ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ ví ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ jánān ǀ ánu ǀbhrā́jantaḥ ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ yathā ǁ
verses.english_translation: His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o’er the world of men, Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
verses.wilson_translation: His illuminating rays behold men in succession, like blazing fires.
verses.griffith_verse: His herald rays are seen afar refulgent o’er the world of men, Like flames of fire that burn and blaze.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतो ज्योतिष्कृदसि सूर्य ।विश्वमा भासि रोचनं ॥
verses.transliteration: taráṇiḥ ǀ viśvá-darśataḥ ǀ jyotiḥ-kṛ́t ǀ asi ǀ sūrya ǀvíśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ bhāsi ǀ rocanám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Swift and all beautiful art thou, O Sūrya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Sūrya, outstrip all in speed; you are visible to all; you are the source of light; you shine throughout the entire firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: Swift and all beautiful art thou, O Sūrya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यङ् देवानां विशः प्रत्यङ्ङुदेषि मानुषान् ।प्रत्यङ्विश्वं स्वर्दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: pratyáṅ ǀ devā́nām ǀ víśaḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ út ǀ eṣi ǀ mā́nuṣān ǀpratyáṅ ǀ víśvam ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind, Hither all light to be beheld.
verses.wilson_translation: You rise in the presence of the Maruts, you rise in the presence of mankind, and so as to be seen in the presence of the whole (region) of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou goest to the hosts of Gods, thou comest hither to mankind, Hither all light to be beheld.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येना पावक चक्षसा भुरण्यंतं जनाँ अनु ।त्वं वरुण पश्यसि ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ pāvaka ǀ cákṣasā ǀ bhuraṇyántam ǀ jánān ǀ ánu ǀtvám ǀ varuṇa ǀ páśyasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuṇa, Upon the busy race of men,
verses.wilson_translation: With that light with which you, the purifier and defender from evil, look upon this creature-bearing world.
verses.griffith_verse: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuṇa, Upon the busy race of men,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि द्यामेषि रजस्पृथ्वहा मिमानो अक्तुभिः ।पश्यञ्जन्मानि सूर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ dyā́m ǀ eṣi ǀ rájaḥ ǀ pṛthú ǀ áhā ǀ mímānaḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀpáśyan ǀ jánmāni ǀ sūrya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days, Sun, seeing all things that have birth.
verses.wilson_translation: You traverse the vast ethereal space, measuring days and nights, and contemplating all that have birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Traversing sky and wide mid-air, thou metest with thy beams our days, Sun, seeing all things that have birth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्त त्वा हरितो रथे वहंति देव सूर्य ।शोचिष्केशं विचक्षण ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ tvā ǀ harítaḥ ǀ ráthe ǀ váhanti ǀ deva ǀ sūrya ǀśocíḥ-keśam ǀ vi-cakṣaṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven Bay Steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One, God, Sūrya, with the radiant hair.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine and light-diffusing Sūrya, your seven coursers bear you, bright-haired, in your car.
verses.griffith_verse: Seven Bay Steeds harnessed to thy car bear thee, O thou farseeing One, God, Sūrya, with the radiant hair.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयुक्त सप्त शुंध्युवः सूरो रथस्य नप्त्यः ।ताभिर्याति स्वयुक्तिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: áyukta ǀ saptá ǀ śundhyúvaḥ ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ráthasya ǀ naptyáḥ ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ yāti ǀ sváyukti-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sūrya hath yoked the pure bright Seven, the daughters of the car; with these, His own dear team, he goeth forth.
verses.wilson_translation: The Sun has yoked the seven mares that safely draw his chariot, and comes with them self-harnessed.
verses.griffith_verse: Sūrya hath yoked the pure bright Seven, the daughters of the car; with these, His own dear team, he goeth forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्वयं तमसस्परि ज्योतिष्पश्यंत उत्तरं ।देवं देवत्रा सूर्यमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तमं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ vayám ǀ támasaḥ ǀ pári ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ páśyantaḥ ǀ út-taram ǀdevám ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ áganma ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ut-tamám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come To Sūrya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent.
verses.wilson_translation: Beholding the up-springing light above the darkness, we approach the divine Sun among the gods, the excellent light.
verses.griffith_verse: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come To Sūrya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्यन्नद्य मित्रमह आरोहन्नुत्तरां दिवं ।हृद्रोगं मम सूर्य हरिमाणं च नाशय ॥
verses.transliteration: ut-yán ǀ adyá ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ ā-róhan ǀ út-tarām ǀ dívam ǀhṛt-rogám ǀ máma ǀ sūrya ǀ harimā́ṇam ǀ ca ǀ nāśaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven, Sūrya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue.
verses.wilson_translation: Radiant with benevolent light, rising today and mountina into the highest heaven, do you O Sun, remove sickness of my heart, and the yellowness (of my body).
verses.griffith_verse: Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven, Sūrya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुकेषु मे हरिमाणं रोपणाकासु दध्मसि ।अथो हारिद्रवेषु मे हरिमाणं नि दध्मसि ॥
verses.transliteration: śúkeṣu ǀ me ǀ harimā́ṇam ǀ ropaṇā́kāsu ǀ dadhmasi ǀátho íti ǀ hāridravéṣu ǀ me ǀ harimā́ṇam ǀ ní ǀ dadhmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness, Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritāla trees.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us transfer the yellowness (of my body) to the parrots, to the starlings, or to theharitāla(tree).
verses.griffith_verse: To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness, Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritāla trees.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदगादयमादित्यो विश्वेन सहसा सह ।द्विषंतं मह्यं रंधयन्मो अहं द्विषते रधं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ agāt ǀ ayám ǀ ādityáḥ ǀ víśvena ǀ sáhasā ǀ sahá ǀdviṣántam ǀ máhyam ǀ randháyan ǀ mó íti ǀ ahám ǀ dviṣaté ǀ radham ǁ
verses.english_translation: With all his conquering vigour this Āditya hath gone up on high, Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.
verses.wilson_translation: ThisĀdityahas risen with all (his) might, destroying my adversary, for I am unable to resist my enemy (sickness).
verses.griffith_verse: With all his conquering vigour this Āditya hath gone up on high, Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth;Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good. As aids the skilful Ṛbhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might,Rushing in rapture; and o’er Śatakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory. Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Aṅgirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors.On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight. Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts.When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vṛtra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see. With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest.Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped Ṛjiśvan when the Dasyus were struck dead. Thou savedst Kutsa when Śuṣṇa was smitten down; to Atithigva gavest Śambara for a prey.E’en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead. All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice.Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe. Discern thou well Āryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn.Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals. Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength.Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven. The might which Uśanā hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart.O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vāta, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power. When Indra hath rejoiced with Kāvya Uśanā, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet.The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Śuṣṇa's firm-built forts. Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Śāryāta brought thee those in which thou hast delight.Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky. To old Kakṣīvān, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vṛcayā.Thou, very wise, wast Menā, Vrsanśva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts. The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras.Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses. To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered.May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्यं मेषं पुरुहूतमृग्मियमिंद्रं गीर्भिर्मदता वस्वो अर्णवं ।यस्य द्यावो न विचरंति मानुषा भुजे मंहिष्ठमभि विप्रमर्चत ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tyám ǀ meṣám ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ ṛgmíyam ǀ índram ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ madata ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ arṇavám ǀyásya ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vi-cáranti ǀ mā́nuṣā ǀ bhujé ǀ máṃhiṣṭham ǀ abhí ǀ vípram ǀ arcata ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth; Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Anime with praises that ram, (Indra), who is adored by many, who is gratified by hymns, and is an ocean of wealth; whose good deeds spread abroad for the benefit of mankind, like the rays of light; worship the powerful and wise Indra, for the enjoyment of prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth; Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभीमवन्वन्त्स्वभिष्टिमूतयोऽंतरिक्षप्रां तविषीभिरावृतं ।इंद्रं दक्षास ऋभवो मदच्युतं शतक्रतुं जवनी सूनृतारुहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ īm ǀ avanvan ǀ su-abhiṣṭím ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ antarikṣa-prā́m ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ ā́-vṛtam ǀíndram ǀ dákṣāsaḥ ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ mada-cyútam ǀ śatá-kratum ǀ jávanī ǀ sūnṛ́tā ǀ ā́ ǀ aruhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: As aids the skilful Ṛbhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might, Rushing in rapture; and o’er Śatakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory.
verses.wilson_translation: The protecting and fosteringṚbhushastened to the presence of Indra, of graceful motion, and irradiating the firmament, imbued with vigour, the humiliator of his enemies, the performer of a hundred pious acts; and by them, encouraging words were uttered.
verses.griffith_verse: As aids the skilful Ṛbhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might, Rushing in rapture; and o’er Śatakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं गोत्रमंगिरोभ्योऽवृणोरपोतात्रये शतदुरेषु गातुवित् ।ससेन चिद्विमदायावहो वस्वाजावद्रिं वावसानस्य नर्तयन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ gotrám ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhyaḥ ǀ avṛṇoḥ ǀ ápa ǀ utá ǀ átraye ǀ śatá-dureṣu ǀ gātu-vít ǀsaséna ǀ cit ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ avahaḥ ǀ vásu ǀ ājáu ǀ ádrim ǀ vavasānásya ǀ nartáyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Aṅgirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors. On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight.
verses.wilson_translation: You have opened the cloud for the Aṅgirasasyou have shown the way to Atri, who vexes his adversaries by a hundred doors (by a number ofyantras, means or contrivances); you have granted wealth, with food, to Vimada; you are wielding your thunderbolt in defence of a worshipper engaged in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Aṅgirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors. On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमपामपिधानावृणोरपाधारयः पर्वते दानुमद्वसु ।वृत्रं यदिंद्र शवसावधीरहिमादित्सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयो दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ apā́m ǀ api-dhā́nā ǀ avṛṇoḥ ǀ ápa ǀ ádhārayaḥ ǀ párvate ǀ dā́nu-mat ǀ vásu ǀvṛtrám ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ śávasā ǀ ávadhīḥ ǀ áhim ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ sū́ryam ǀ diví ǀ ā́ ǀ arohayaḥ ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts. When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vṛtra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see.
verses.wilson_translation: You have opened the receptacle of the waters; you have detained in the mountain the treasure of the malignant; when you had slain Vṛtra, the destryer, you made the sun visible in the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts. When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vṛtra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं मायाभिरप मायिनोऽधमः स्वधाभिर्ये अधि शुप्तावजुह्वत ।त्वं पिप्रोर्नृमणः प्रारुजः पुरः प्र ऋजिश्वानं दस्युहत्येष्वाविथ ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ ápa ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ adhamaḥ ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ yé ǀ ádhi ǀ śúptau ǀ ájuhvata ǀtvám ǀ píproḥ ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ prá ǀ arujaḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ prá ǀ ṛjíśvānam ǀ dasyu-hátyeṣu ǀ āvitha ǁ
verses.english_translation: With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest. Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped Ṛjiśvan when the Dasyus were struck dead.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, by the devices, have humbled the deceivers who presented oblations to their own mouths; propitious to men, you have destroyed the cities of Pipru, and have well defended Ṛjiśvan in robber-destroying (contest).
verses.griffith_verse: With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest. Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped Ṛjiśvan when the Dasyus were struck dead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं कुत्सं शुष्णहत्येष्वाविथारंधयोऽतिथिग्वाय शंबरं ।महांतं चिदर्बुदं नि क्रमीः पदा सनादेव दस्युहत्याय जज्ञिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ kútsam ǀ śuṣṇa-hátyeṣu ǀ āvitha ǀ árandhayaḥ ǀ atithi-gvā́ya ǀ śámbaram ǀmahā́ntam ǀ cit ǀ arbudám ǀ ní ǀ kramīḥ ǀ padā́ ǀ sanā́t ǀ evá ǀ dasyu-hátyāya ǀ jajñiṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou savedst Kutsa when Śuṣṇa was smitten down; to Atithigva gavest Śambara for a prey. E’en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead.
verses.wilson_translation: You have defended Kutsain fatal fights with Śuśna; you have destroyedŚambarain defence of Atithigva; you have trodden with your foot upon the great Arbuda; frm remote times were you born for the destruction of oppressors.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou savedst Kutsa when Śuṣṇa was smitten down; to Atithigva gavest Śambara for a prey. E’en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे विश्वा तविषी सध्र्यग्घिता तव राधः सोमपीथाय हर्षते ।तव वज्रश्चिकिते बाह्वोर्हितो वृश्चा शत्रोरव विश्वानि वृष्ण्या ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ víśvā ǀ táviṣī ǀ sadhryák ǀ hitā́ ǀ táva ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ soma-pīthā́ya ǀ harṣate ǀtáva ǀ vájraḥ ǀ cikite ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǀ vṛścá ǀ śátroḥ ǀ áva ǀ víśvāni ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice. Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe.
verses.wilson_translation: In you,Indra, is all vigour fully concentrated; you will delight to drink the Soma; it is known by us that the thunderbolt is deposited in yourhands; cut off all prowess from the foe.
verses.griffith_verse: All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice. Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि जानीह्यार्यान्ये च दस्यवो बर्हिष्मते रंधया शासदव्रतान् ।शाकी भव यजमानस्य चोदिता विश्वेत्ता ते सधमादेषु चाकन ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ jānīhi ǀ ā́ryān ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ dásyavaḥ ǀ barhíṣmate ǀ randhaya ǀ śā́sat ǀ avratā́n ǀśā́kī ǀ bhava ǀ yájamānasya ǀ coditā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ sadha-mā́deṣu ǀ cākana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Discern thou well Āryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn. Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals.
verses.wilson_translation: Discriminate between theĀryasand they who are Dasyus; restraining those who perform no religious rites, compel them to submit to the performer of sacrifices; be you, who are powerful, the encourager of the sacrificer; I am desirous of celebrating all your deeds in ceremonies that give you satisfaction.
verses.griffith_verse: Discern thou well Āryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn. Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनुव्रताय रंधयन्नपव्रतानाभूभिरिंद्रः श्नथयन्ननाभुवः ।वृद्धस्य चिद्वर्धतो द्यामिनक्षतः स्तवानो वम्रो वि जघान संदिहः ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu-vratāya ǀ randháyan ǀ ápa-vratān ǀ ā-bhū́bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ śnatháyan ǀ ánābhuvaḥ ǀvṛddhásya ǀ cit ǀ várdhataḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ínakṣataḥ ǀ stávānaḥ ǀ vamráḥ ǀ ví ǀ jaghāna ǀ sam-díhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength. Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraabides, humbling the neglecters of holy acts in favour of those who observe them; and punishing those who turn away from his worship in favour of those who are present (with their praise); Vamra, while praising him, whether old or adolescent, and spreading through heaven, carried off the accusative ulated (materials of the sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength. Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तक्षद्यत्त उशना सहसा सहो वि रोदसी मज्मना बाधते शवः ।आ त्वा वातस्य नृमणो मनोयुज आ पूर्यमाणमवहन्नभि श्रवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tákṣat ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ uśánā ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ródasī íti ǀ majmánā ǀ bādhate ǀ śávaḥ ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ vā́tasya ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ manaḥ-yújaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pū́ryamāṇam ǀ avahan ǀ abhí ǀ śrávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The might which Uśanā hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart. O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vāta, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power.
verses.wilson_translation: If Uṣanās should sharpen your vigour by his own, then would your might terrify by its intensity both heaven and earth. Friend of man, let the will harnessed steeds, with the velocity of the wind, convey you, replete (with vigour), to (partake of the sacrificial) food.
verses.griffith_verse: The might which Uśanā hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart. O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vāta, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंदिष्ट यदुशने काव्ये सचाँ इंद्रो वंकू वंकुतराधि तिष्ठति ।उग्रो ययिं निरपः स्रोतसासृजद्वि शुष्णस्य दृंहिता ऐरयत्पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: mándiṣṭa ǀ yát ǀ uśáne ǀ kāvyé ǀ sácā ǀ índraḥ ǀ vaṅkū́ íti ǀ vaṅku-tárā́ ǀ ádhi ǀ tiṣṭhati ǀugráḥ ǀ yayím ǀ níḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ srótasā ǀ asṛjat ǀ ví ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ dṛṃhitā́ḥ ǀ airayat ǀ púraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Indra hath rejoiced with Kāvya Uśanā, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet. The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Śuṣṇa's firm-built forts.
verses.wilson_translation: When Indrais delighted with acceptable hymns, he ascends (his car), drawn by more and more obliquely-curving coursers; fierce, he extracts the waters from the passing (cloud) in a torrent, and has overwhelmed the extensive cities ofŚuṣṇa.
verses.griffith_verse: When Indra hath rejoiced with Kāvya Uśanā, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet. The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Śuṣṇa's firm-built forts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ स्मा रथं वृषपाणेषु तिष्ठसि शार्यातस्य प्रभृता येषु मंदसे ।इंद्र यथा सुतसोमेषु चाकनोऽनर्वाणं श्लोकमा रोहसे दिवि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ sma ǀ rátham ǀ vṛṣa-pā́neṣu ǀ tiṣṭhasi ǀ śāryātásya ǀ prá-bhṛtāḥ ǀ yéṣu ǀ mándase ǀíndra ǀ yáthā ǀ sutá-someṣu ǀ cākánaḥ ǀ anarvā́ṇam ǀ ślókam ǀ ā́ ǀ rohase ǀ diví ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Śāryāta brought thee those in which thou hast delight. Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: You mount your chariot willingly,Indra, for the sake of drinking the libations; such as you delight in having been prepared (at the sacrifice of)Śāryāta; be plural ased with them, as you are gratified by the effused Soma(at the sacrifices) of others, so do you obtain imperishable fame in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Śāryāta brought thee those in which thou hast delight. Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अददा अर्भां महते वचस्यवे कक्षीवते वृचयामिंद्र सुन्वते ।मेनाभवो वृषणश्वस्य सुक्रतो विश्वेत्ता ते सवनेषु प्रवाच्या ॥
verses.transliteration: ádadāḥ ǀ árbhām ǀ mahaté ǀ vacasyáve ǀ kakṣī́vate ǀ vṛcayā́m ǀ indra ǀ sunvaté ǀménā ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇaśvásya ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ pra-vā́cyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: To old Kakṣīvān, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vṛcayā. Thou, very wise, wast Menā, Vrsanśva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts.
verses.wilson_translation: You have given,Indra, the youthful Vṛcaya to the aged Kakṣīvat, praising you and offering oblations; you,Śatakratu, were Menā, the daughter of Vṛṣaṇaśva; all these your deeds are to be recited at your worship.
verses.griffith_verse: To old Kakṣīvān, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vṛcayā. Thou, very wise, wast Menā, Vrsanśva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो अश्रायि सुध्यो निरेके पज्रेषु स्तोमो दुर्यो न यूपः ।अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरिंद्र इद्रायः क्षयति प्रयंता ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ aśrāyi ǀ su-dhyáḥ ǀ nireké ǀ pajréṣu ǀ stómaḥ ǀ dúryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yū́paḥ ǀaśva-yúḥ ǀ gavyúḥ ǀ ratha-yúḥ ǀ vasu-yúḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ kṣayati ǀ pra-yantā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras. Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas been had recourse to, that he may assist the pious in their distress. Praise by the Pajras, is (as stable) as thepostof a doorway. Indra, the giver of riches, who is possessed of (who desires to possess, expecting as gifts from the instrumental tutor of the ceremony) horses, cattle, chariots and wealth is present.
verses.griffith_verse: The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras. Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं नमो वृषभाय स्वराजे सत्यशुष्माय तवसेऽवाचि ।अस्मिन्निंद्र वृजने सर्ववीराः स्मत्सूरिभिस्तव शर्मन्त्स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ námaḥ ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ sva-rā́je ǀ satyá-śuṣmāya ǀ taváse ǀ avāci ǀasmín ǀ indra ǀ vṛjáne ǀ sárva-vīrāḥ ǀ smát ǀ sūrí-bhiḥ ǀ táva ǀ śárman ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered. May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.
verses.wilson_translation: This adoration is offered to the shedder of rain, the self-resplendent, the possessor of true vigour, the mighty; may we be aided,Indra, in his conflict, by many heroes, and abide in a prosperoud (habitation, bestowed) by you.
verses.griffith_verse: To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered. May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him.With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,—the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call. Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength,When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vṛtra stayer of their flow. For he stays e’en the stayers, spread o’er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise.Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice. Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,—Beside that Indra when he smote down Vṛtra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible. To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope,When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Tṛta cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through. Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep,What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vṛitra hard to be restrained. The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake.Tvaṣṭar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might. When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vṛtra, causing floods to flow for man,Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see. In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven,When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light. Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderboltIn the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vṛtra, tyrant of the earth and heaven. O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day,Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power. Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven,Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky. Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes:Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee. Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,—Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due. The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted,What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vṛtra.

verses.sanskrit: त्यं सु मेषं महया स्वर्विदं शतं यस्य सुभ्वः साकमीरते ।अत्यं न वाजं हवनस्यदं रथमेंद्रं ववृत्यामवसे सुवृक्तिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tyám ǀ sú ǀ meṣám ǀ mahaya ǀ svaḥ-vídam ǀ śatám ǀ yásya ǀ su-bhváḥ ǀ sākám ǀ ī́rate ǀátyam ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǀ havana-syádam ǀ rátham ǀ ā́ ǀ índram ǀ vavṛtyām ǀ ávase ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him. With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,—the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship well that ram who makes heaven known, whom a hundred worshippers at once are assiduous in praising. I implore Indrawith many prayers to ascend the car, which hastens like a fleet courser to the sacrificer for my protection.
verses.griffith_verse: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him. With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,—the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स पर्वतो न धरुणेष्वच्युतः सहस्रमूतिस्तविषीषु वावृधे ।इंद्रो यद्वृत्रमवधीन्नदीवृतमुब्जन्नर्णांसि जर्हृषाणो अंधसा ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ párvataḥ ǀ ná ǀ dharúṇeṣu ǀ ácyutaḥ ǀ sahásram-ūtiḥ ǀ táviṣīṣu ǀ vavṛdhe ǀíndraḥ ǀ yát ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ávadhīt ǀ nadī-vṛ́tam ǀ ubján ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ járhṛṣāṇaḥ ǀ ándhasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength, When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vṛtra stayer of their flow.
verses.wilson_translation: When Indra, who delights in the sacrificial food, had slain the stream-obstructing Vṛtra, and was pouring down the waters, he stood firm amid the torrents like a mountain, and endowed with a thousand means of protecting (his votaries) increased in vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength, When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vṛtra stayer of their flow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि द्वरो द्वरिषु वव्र ऊधनि चंद्रबुध्नो मदवृद्धो मनीषिभिः ।इंद्रं तमह्वे स्वपस्यया धिया मंहिष्ठरातिं स हि पप्रिरंधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ dvaráḥ ǀ dvaríṣu ǀ vavráḥ ǀ ū́dhani ǀ candrá-budhnaḥ ǀ máda-vṛddhaḥ ǀ manīṣí-bhiḥ ǀíndram ǀ tám ǀ ahve ǀ su-apasyáyā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ máṃhiṣṭha-rātim ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ pápriḥ ǀ ándhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For he stays e’en the stayers, spread o’er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise. Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is victorious over his enemies, who is spread through the dewy (firmament), the root of happiness, who is exhilarated by the Somahim I invoke, the most bountiful Indra, along with learned priests, with a mind disposed to pious adoration, for he is the bestower of abundant food.
verses.griffith_verse: For he stays e’en the stayers, spread o’er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise. Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यं पृणंति दिवि सद्मबर्हिषः समुद्रं न सुभ्वः स्वा अभिष्टयः ।तं वृत्रहत्ये अनु तस्थुरूतयः शुष्मा इंद्रमवाता अह्रुतप्सवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yám ǀ pṛṇánti ǀ diví ǀ sádma-barhiṣaḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ ná ǀ su-bhváḥ ǀ svā́ḥ ǀ abhíṣṭayaḥ ǀtám ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀ ánu ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǀ índram ǀ avātā́ḥ ǀ áhruta-psavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,— Beside that Indra when he smote down Vṛtra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible.
verses.wilson_translation: Tha Indrawhom in heaven the libations sprinkled on the sacred grass replenish, as the kindred rivers hastening to it fill the ocean; that Indra whom the Maruts, the driers up of moisture, who are unobstructed, and of undistorted forms, attended as auxiliaries at the death of Vṛtra.
verses.griffith_verse: Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,— Beside that Indra when he smote down Vṛtra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि स्ववृष्टिं मदे अस्य युध्यतो रघ्वीरिव प्रवणे सस्रुरूतयः ।इंद्रो यद्वज्री धृषमाणो अंधसा भिनद्वलस्य परिधीँरिव त्रितः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ svá-vṛṣṭim ǀ máde ǀ asya ǀ yúdhyataḥ ǀ raghvī́ḥ-iva ǀ pravaṇé ǀ sasruḥ ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ yát ǀ vajrī́ ǀ dhṛṣámāṇaḥ ǀ ándhasā ǀ bhinát ǀ valásya ǀ paridhī́n-iva ǀ tritáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope, When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Tṛta cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through.
