verses.wilson_translation: His allies, exhilarated (by libations), preceded him, warring against the withholder of the rain, as rivers rush down declivities.Indra, animated by the sacrificial food, broke through the defences of Valaas did Tritathrough the coverings (of the well).
verses.griffith_verse: To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope, When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Tṛta cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परीं घृणा चरति तित्विषे शवोऽपो वृत्वी रजसो बुध्नमाशयत् ।वृत्रस्य यत्प्रवणे दुर्गृभिश्वनो निजघंथ हन्वोरिंद्र तन्यतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ īm ǀ ghṛṇā́ ǀ carati ǀ titviṣé ǀ śávaḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ vṛtvī́ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ budhnám ǀ ā́ ǀ aśayat ǀvṛtrásya ǀ yát ǀ pravaṇé ǀ duḥ-gṛ́bhiśvanaḥ ǀ ni-jaghántha ǀ hánvoḥ ǀ indra ǀ tanyatúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep, What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vṛitra hard to be restrained.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Indra, you had smitten with my thunderbolt the check of the wide-extended Vṛtra, who, having obstructed the waters reposed in the region above the firmament, your fame spread afar, your prowess was renowned.
verses.griffith_verse: Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep, What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vṛitra hard to be restrained.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ह्रदं न हि त्वा न्यृषंत्यूर्मयो ब्रह्माणींद्र तव यानि वर्धना ।त्वष्टा चित्ते युज्यं वावृधे शवस्ततक्ष वज्रमभिभूत्योजसं ॥
verses.transliteration: hradám ǀ ná ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ ni-ṛṣánti ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ indra ǀ táva ǀ yā́ni ǀ várdhanā ǀtváṣṭā ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ yújyam ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ śávaḥ ǀ tatákṣa ǀ vájram ǀ abhíbhūti-ojasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake. Tvaṣṭar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might.
verses.wilson_translation: The hymns,Indra, that glorify you, attain unto you, as rivulets (flow into) a lake.Tvaṣṭāhas augmented your appropriate vigour; he has sharpened your bolt with overpowering might.
verses.griffith_verse: The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake. Tvaṣṭar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जघन्वाँ उ हरिभिः संभृतक्रतविंद्र वृत्रं मनुषे गातुयन्नपः ।अयच्छथा बाह्वोर्वज्रमायसमधारयो दिव्या सूर्यं दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: jaghanvā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ saṃbhṛtakrato íti saṃbhṛta-krato ǀ índra ǀ vṛtrám ǀ mánuṣe ǀ gātu-yán ǀ apáḥ ǀáyacchathāḥ ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ vájram ǀ āyasám ǀ ádhārayaḥ ǀ diví ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vṛtra, causing floods to flow for man, Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, performer of holy acts, desirous of going to man, you with your steeds have slain Vṛtra(have set free) the waters, have taken in yourhandsyour thunderbolt of metal, and have made the sun visible in the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vṛtra, causing floods to flow for man, Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहत्स्वश्चंद्रममवद्यदुक्थ्यमकृण्वत भियसा रोहणं दिवः ।यन्मानुषप्रधना इंद्रमूतयः स्वर्नृषाचो मरुतोऽमदन्ननु ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhát ǀ svá-candram ǀ áma-vat ǀ yát ǀ ukthyám ǀ ákṛṇvata ǀ bhiyásā ǀ róhaṇam ǀ diváḥ ǀyát ǀ mā́nuṣa-pradhanāḥ ǀ índram ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ nṛ-sā́caḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ámadan ǀ ánu ǁ
verses.english_translation: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
verses.wilson_translation: Through fear (of Vṛtra, they, the worshippers), recited the suitable hymn of the Bṛhat(Sāma), self-illuminating, strength-bestowing, and ascending to heaven; on which his allies, (the Maruts), combating for men, (guardians) of heaven, and vivifiers of mankind animated Indra(to destroy him).
verses.griffith_verse: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्यौश्चिदस्यामवाँ अहेः स्वनादयोयवीद्भियसा वज्र इंद्र ते ।वृत्रस्य यद्बद्बधानस्य रोदसी मदे सुतस्य शवसाभिनच्छिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: dyáuḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ áma-vān ǀ áheḥ ǀ svanā́t ǀ áyoyavīt ǀ bhiyásā ǀ vájraḥ ǀ indra ǀ te ǀvṛtrásya ǀ yát ǀ badbadhānásya ǀ rodasī íti ǀ máde ǀ sutásya ǀ śávasā ǀ ábhinat ǀ śíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderbolt In the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vṛtra, tyrant of the earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The strong heaven was rent asunder with fear at the clamour of that Ahi, when you,Indra, was inspired by (drinking) the effused (Soma), and your thunderbolt in its vigour struck off the head of Vṛtra, the obstructor of heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderbolt In the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vṛtra, tyrant of the earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिन्न्विंद्र पृथिवी दशभुजिरहानि विश्वा ततनंत कृष्टयः ।अत्राह ते मघवन्विश्रुतं सहो द्यामनु शवसा बर्हणा भुवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dáśa-bhujiḥ ǀ áhāni ǀ víśvā ǀ tatánanta ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ ví-śrutam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ánu ǀ śávasā ǀ barháṇā ǀ bhuvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day, Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power.
verses.wilson_translation: Although,Indra, the earth were of tenfold (its extent), and men multiplied every day, yet,Maghavan, your prowess would be equally renowned; the exploits achieved by your might would be spread abroad with the heavens.
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day, Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमस्य पारे रजसो व्योमनः स्वभूत्योजा अवसे धृषन्मनः ।चकृषे भूमिं प्रतिमानमोजसोऽपः स्वः परिभूरेष्या दिवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ asyá ǀ pāré ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ ví-omanaḥ ǀ svábhūti-ojāḥ ǀ ávase ǀ dhṛṣat-manaḥ ǀcakṛṣé ǀ bhū́mim ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ ójasaḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ pari-bhū́ḥ ǀ eṣi ǀ ā́ ǀ dívam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven, Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: Firm-minded Indra, abiding (secure) in your strength beyond the limit of the wide-expanded firmament, you have framed the earth for our preservation; you have been the type of vigour; you have encompassed the firmament and the sky as far as to the heavens.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven, Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं भुवः प्रतिमानं पृथिव्या ऋष्ववीरस्य बृहतः पतिर्भूः ।विश्वमाप्रा अंतरिक्षं महित्वा सत्यमद्धा नकिरन्यस्त्वावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ bhuvaḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ṛṣvá-vīrasya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ bhūḥ ǀvíśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ satyám ǀ addhā́ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ tvā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes: Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the type of the extended earth you are the lord of the vast god-frequent (svarga) verily with your bulk you fillest all the firmament of a truth, there is none other such as you.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes: Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी अनु व्यचो न सिंधवो रजसो अंतमानशुः ।नोत स्ववृष्टिं मदे अस्य युध्यत एको अन्यच्चकृषे विश्वमानुषक् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ánu ǀ vyácaḥ ǀ ná ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ ántam ǀ ānaśúḥ ǀná ǀ utá ǀ svá-vṛṣṭim ǀ máde ǀ asya ǀ yúdhyataḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ anyát ǀ cakṛṣe ǀ víśvam ǀ ānuṣák ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,— Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due.
verses.wilson_translation: you,Indra, of whom heaven and earth have not attained the amplitude; of whom the waters of heaven have not reached the limit; of whom, when warring with excited animation against the withholder of the rains, (his adversaries have not equalled the prowess); you alone have made everything else, (than yourself), dependent (upon you).
verses.griffith_verse: Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,— Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आर्चन्नत्र मरुतः सस्मिन्नाजौ विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननु त्वा ।वृत्रस्य यद्भृष्टिमता वधेन नि त्वमिंद्र प्रत्यानं जघंथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́rcan ǀ átra ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sásmin ǀ ājáu ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ amadan ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǀvṛtrásya ǀ yát ǀ bhṛṣṭi-mátā ǀ vadhéna ǀ ní ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ práti ǀ ānám ǀ jaghántha ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted, What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: The Marutsworshipped you in this (encounter); all the gods in this engagement imitated you in exultation, when you had struck the face of Vṛtrawith your angular and fatal (bolt).
verses.griffith_verse: The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted, What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvān's dwelling-place;For he hath ne’er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise. Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth:Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee as such we sing this praise. Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own.Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee. Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine.With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food. Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky:May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds. These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vṛtra, Hero Lord,What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vṛtras, thou resistless in thy might. Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength.Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci. Thou hast struck down in death Karañja, Parṇaya, in Atithigva's very glorious going forth.Unyielding, when Ṛjiśvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vaṅgṛida. With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men,With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Suśravas. Thou hast protected Suśravas with succour, and Tūrvayāṇa with thine aid, O Indra.Thou madest Kutsa, Atithigva, Āyu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty. May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra.Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.

verses.sanskrit: न्यू षु वाचं प्र महे भरामहे गिर इंद्राय सदने विवस्वतः ।नू चिद्धि रत्नं ससतामिवाविदन्न दुष्टुतिर्द्रविणोदेषु शस्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ vā́cam ǀ prá ǀ mahé ǀ bharāmahe ǀ gíraḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ sádane ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀnú ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ rátnam ǀ sasatā́m-iva ǀ ávidat ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-stutíḥ ǀ draviṇaḥ-déṣu ǀ śasyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvān's dwelling-place; For he hath ne’er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.
verses.wilson_translation: We ever offer fitting praise to the mighty Indra, in the dwelling of the worshpper, by which he (the deity) has quickly acquired riches, as (a thief) hastily hastily carried (off the property) of the sleeping. Praise ill expressed is not valued among the munificent.
verses.griffith_verse: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvān's dwelling-place; For he hath ne’er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दुरो अश्वस्य दुर इंद्र गोरसि दुरो यवस्य वसुन इनस्पतिः ।शिक्षानरः प्रदिवो अकामकर्शनः सखा सखिभ्यस्तमिदं गृणीमसि ॥
verses.transliteration: duráḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ duráḥ ǀ indra ǀ góḥ ǀ asi ǀ duráḥ ǀ yávasya ǀ vásunaḥ ǀ ináḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀśikṣā-naráḥ ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ ákāma-karśanaḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ tám ǀ idám ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth: Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee as such we sing this praise.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are the giver of horses, of cattle, or barley, the master and protector of wealth, the foremost in liberality, (the being) of many days; you disappoint not desires (addressed to you); you are a friend to our friend; such an Indra we praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth: Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee as such we sing this praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शचीव इंद्र पुरुकृद्द्युमत्तम तवेदिदमभितश्चेकिते वसु ।अतः संगृभ्याभिभूत आ भर मा त्वायतो जरितुः काममूनयीः ॥
verses.transliteration: śácī-vaḥ ǀ indra ǀ puru-kṛt ǀ dyumat-tama ǀ táva ǀ ít ǀ idám ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ cekite ǀ vásu ǀátaḥ ǀ sam-gṛ́bhya ǀ abhi-bhūte ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā-yatáḥ ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ ūnayīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own. Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Wise and resplendent Indra, the achiever of great deeds, the riches that are spread around are known to be yours; having collected them, victor (over your enemies), bring them to us; disappoint not the expectation of the worshipper who trusts in you.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own. Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एभिर्द्युभिः सुमना एभिरिंदुभिर्निरुंधानो अमतिं गोभिरश्विना ।इंद्रेण दस्युं दरयंत इंदुभिर्युतद्वेषसः समिषा रभेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ebhíḥ ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ebhíḥ ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǀ ni-rundhānáḥ ǀ ámatim ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀíndreṇa ǀ dásyum ǀ daráyantaḥ ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǀ yutá-dveṣasaḥ ǀ sám ǀ iṣā́ ǀ rabhemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine. With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food.
verses.wilson_translation: Propitiated by these offerings, be these libations, dispel poverty with cattle and horses; may we subduing our adversary, and relived from enemies by Indra, (plural ased) by our libations, enjoy together abundant food.
verses.griffith_verse: Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine. With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समिंद्र राया समिषा रभेमहि सं वाजेभिः पुरुश्चंद्रैरभिद्युभिः ।सं देव्या प्रमत्या वीरशुष्मया गोअग्रयाश्वावत्या रभेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ indra ǀ rāyā́ ǀ sám ǀ iṣā́ ǀ rabhemahi ǀ sám ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ puru-candráiḥ ǀ abhídyu-bhiḥ ǀsám ǀ devyā́ ǀ prá-matyā ǀ vīrá-śuṣmayā ǀ gó-agrayā ǀ áśva-vatyā ǀ rabhemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky: May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, may we become possessed of riches, and of food; and with energies agreeable to many, and shining around, may we prosper through your divine favour, the source of prowess, of cattle and of horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky: May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते त्वा मदा अमदंतानि वृष्ण्या ते सोमासो वृत्रहत्येषु सत्पते ।यत्कारवे दश वृत्राण्यप्रति बर्हिष्मते नि सहस्राणि बर्हयः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ tvā ǀ mádāḥ ǀ amadan ǀ tā́ni ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyā ǀ té ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ vṛtra-hátyeṣu ǀ sat-pate ǀyát ǀ kāráve ǀ dáśa ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ apratí ǀ barhíṣmate ǀ ní ǀ sahásrāṇi ǀ barháyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vṛtra, Hero Lord, What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vṛtras, thou resistless in thy might.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who were your allies, (the Maruts), brought you joy; protector of the pious, those libations and oblations (that were offered you on slaying Vṛtra), yielded you delight, when you, unimpeded by foes, did destroy the ten thousand obstacles oposed to him who praised you and offered you oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vṛtra, Hero Lord, What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vṛtras, thou resistless in thy might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युधा युधमुप घेदेषि धृष्णुया पुरा पुरं समिदं हंस्योजसा ।नम्या यदिंद्र सख्या परावति निबर्हयो नमुचिं नाम मायिनं ॥
verses.transliteration: yudhā́ ǀ yúdham ǀ úpa ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ eṣi ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀ purā́ ǀ púram ǀ sám ǀ idám ǀ haṃsi ǀ ójasā ǀnámyā ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ sákhyā ǀ parā-váti ǀ ni-barháyaḥ ǀ námucim ǀ nā́ma ǀ māyínam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength. Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci.
verses.wilson_translation: Humiliator (of adversaries), you go from battle to battle, and destroy by your might city after city; with you foe-prostrating associate, (the thunderbolt), you Indra, did slay afar off the deceiver named Namuci.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength. Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं करंजमुत पर्णयं वधीस्तेजिष्ठयातिथिग्वस्य वर्तनी ।त्वं शता वंगृदस्याभिनत्पुरोऽनानुदः परिषूता ऋजिश्वना ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ kárañjam ǀ utá ǀ parṇáyam ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ téjiṣṭhayā ǀ atithi-gvásya ǀ vartanī́ ǀtvám ǀ śatā́ ǀ váṅgṛdasya ǀ abhinat ǀ púraḥ ǀ ananu-dáḥ ǀ pári-sūtāḥ ǀ ṛjíśvanā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast struck down in death Karañja, Parṇaya, in Atithigva's very glorious going forth. Unyielding, when Ṛjiśvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vaṅgṛida.
verses.wilson_translation: You have slain Karañjaand Parṇayawith your bright gleaming spear, in the cause of Atithigva; unaided, you did demolish the hundred cities of Vaṅgrida, when besieged by Ṛjiṣvan.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast struck down in death Karañja, Parṇaya, in Atithigva's very glorious going forth. Unyielding, when Ṛjiśvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vaṅgṛida.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमेतांजनराज्ञो द्विर्दशाबंधुना सुश्रवसोपजग्मुषः ।षष्टिं सहस्रा नवतिं नव श्रुतो नि चक्रेण रथ्या दुष्पदावृणक् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ etā́n ǀ jana-rā́jñaḥ ǀ dvíḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ abandhúnā ǀ su-śrávasā ǀ upa-jagmúṣaḥ ǀṣaṣṭím ǀ sahásrā ǀ navatím ǀ náva ǀ śrutáḥ ǀ ní ǀ cakréṇa ǀ ráthyā ǀ duḥ-pádā ǀ avṛṇak ǁ
verses.english_translation: With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men, With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Suśravas.
verses.wilson_translation: You, renowned Indra, overthrown by your not-to-be- overtaken chariot-wheel, the twenty kings of men, who had come against Suśravasunaided, and their sixty thousand and ninety-nine followers.
verses.griffith_verse: With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men, With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Suśravas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमाविथ सुश्रवसं तवोतिभिस्तव त्रामभिरिंद्र तूर्वयाणं ।त्वमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने अरंधनायः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ āvitha ǀ su-śrávasam ǀ táva ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ táva ǀ trā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ túrvayāṇam ǀtvám ǀ asmai ǀ kútsam ǀ atithi-gvám ǀ āyúm ǀ mahé ǀ rā́jñe ǀ yū́ne ǀ arandhanāyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast protected Suśravas with succour, and Tūrvayāṇa with thine aid, O Indra. Thou madest Kutsa, Atithigva, Āyu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, have preserved Suśravasby your succour, Turvayāṇa by your assistance; you have made Kutsa,Atithigva, and Ātu subject to the mighty though youthful Suśravas.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast protected Suśravas with succour, and Tūrvayāṇa with thine aid, O Indra. Thou madest Kutsa, Atithigva, Āyu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य उदृचींद्र देवगोपाः सखायस्ते शिवतमा असाम ।त्वां स्तोषाम त्वया सुवीरा द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ut-ṛ́ci ǀ indra ǀ devá-gopāḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ te ǀ śivá-tamāḥ ǀ ásāma ǀtvā́m ǀ stoṣāma ǀ tváyā ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǀ drā́ghīyaḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra. Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Protected by the gods, we remain,Indra, at the close of the sacrifice, your most fortunate friends; we praise you, as enjoying through you excellent offspring, and a long and prosperous life.
verses.griffith_verse: May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra. Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength.Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear? Sing hymns of praise to Śakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who heareth thee,Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth. Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway.High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he. The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Śambara,When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and two-edged, against the banded sorcerers. When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which Śuṣṇa kept confined,Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done? Thou helpest Narya, Turvaśa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvīti, Śatakratu!Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles. A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law,Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky. His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma,Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver. Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles.Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure. There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters’ flow: in Vṛtra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed.But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivities. So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people.Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.

verses.sanskrit: मा नो अस्मिन्मघवन्पृत्स्वंहसि नहि ते अंतः शवसः परीणशे ।अक्रंदयो नद्यो रोरुवद्वना कथा न क्षोणीर्भियसा समारत ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ asmín ǀ magha-van ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ áṃhasi ǀ nahí ǀ te ǀ ántaḥ ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ pari-náśe ǀákrandayaḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ róruvat ǀ vánā ǀ kathā́ ǀ ná ǀ kṣoṇī́ḥ ǀ bhiyásā ǀ sám ǀ ārata ǁ
verses.english_translation: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength. Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?
verses.wilson_translation: Urge us not,Maghavan, to this iniquity, to these iniquitous conflicts, for the limit of your strength is not to be surpassed; you have made the waters of the rivers roar; how (is it possible) that the earth should be filled with terror?
verses.griffith_verse: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength. Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्चा शक्राय शाकिने शचीवते शृण्वंतमिंद्रं महयन्नभि ष्टुहि ।यो धृष्णुना शवसा रोदसी उभे वृषा वृषत्वा वृषभो न्यृंजते ॥
verses.transliteration: árca ǀ śakrā́ya ǀ śākíne ǀ śácī-vate ǀ śṛṇvántam ǀ índram ǀ maháyan ǀ abhí ǀ stuhi ǀyáḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇúnā ǀ śávasā ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛṣa-tvā́ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ni-ṛñjáte ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing hymns of praise to Śakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who heareth thee, Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer adoration to the wise and powerfulŚakra; glorifying the listening Indra, praise him who purifies both heaven and earth by his irresistible might, who is the sender of showers, and by his bounty gratifies our desires.
verses.griffith_verse: Sing hymns of praise to Śakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who heareth thee, Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्चा दिवे बृहते शूष्यं वचः स्वक्षत्रं यस्य धृषतो धृषन्मनः ।बृहच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कृतः पुरो हरिभ्यां वृषभो रथो हि षः ॥
verses.transliteration: árca ǀ divé ǀ bṛhaté ǀ śūṣyám ǀ vácaḥ ǀ svá-kṣatram ǀ yásya ǀ dhṛṣatáḥ ǀ dhṛṣát ǀ mánaḥ ǀbṛhát-śravāḥ ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ barháṇā ǀ kṛtáḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ hí ǀ sáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway. High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer exhilarating praises to the great and illustrious Indra, of whom, undaunted, the steady mind is concentrated in its own firmness; for he, who is of great renown, the giver of rain, the repeller of enemies, who is obeyed his steeds, the showerer (of bounties), is hastening hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway. High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं दिवो बृहतः सानु कोपयोऽव त्मना धृषता शंबरं भिनत् ।यन्मायिनो व्रंदिनो मंदिना धृषच्छितां गभस्तिमशनिं पृतन्यसि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ diváḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ sā́nu ǀ kopayaḥ ǀ áva ǀ tmánā ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ śámbaram ǀ bhinat ǀyát ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ vrandínaḥ ǀ mandínā ǀ dhṛṣát ǀ śitā́m ǀ gábhastim ǀ aśánim ǀ pṛtanyási ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Śambara, When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and two-edged, against the banded sorcerers.
verses.wilson_translation: You have shaken the summit of the spacious heaven; you have slainŚambaraby your resolute self; you have hurled with exulting and determined mind the sharp and bright-rayed thunderbolt against assembled Asuras.
verses.griffith_verse: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Śambara, When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and two-edged, against the banded sorcerers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि यद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद्व्रंदिनो रोरुवद्वना ।प्राचीनेन मनसा बर्हणावता यदद्या चित्कृणवः कस्त्वा परि ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ yát ǀ vṛṇákṣi ǀ śvasanásya ǀ mūrdháni ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ cit ǀ vrandínaḥ ǀ róruvat ǀ vánā ǀprācī́nena ǀ mánasā ǀ barháṇā-vatā ǀ yát ǀ adyá ǀ cit ǀ kṛṇávaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ tvā ǀ pári ǁ
verses.english_translation: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which Śuṣṇa kept confined, Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?
verses.wilson_translation: Since you, loud-shouting, have poured the rain upon the brow of the breathing (wind), and (on the head) of the maturing and absorbing (sun), who shall prevent you from doing today (as you will), endowed with an unaltered and resolute mind?
verses.griffith_verse: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which Śuṣṇa kept confined, Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं त्वं तुर्वीतिं वय्यं शतक्रतो ।त्वं रथमेतशं कृत्व्ये धने त्वं पुरो नवतिं दंभयो नव ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ āvitha ǀ náryam ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀ tvám ǀ turvī́tim ǀ vayyám ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀtvám ǀ rátham ǀ étaśam ǀ kṛ́tvye ǀ dháne ǀ tvám ǀ púraḥ ǀ navatím ǀ dambhayaḥ ǀ náva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou helpest Narya, Turvaśa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvīti, Śatakratu! Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.
verses.wilson_translation: You have protected Narya,Turvaśa,Yaduand Turvīti, of the face of Vayya; you have protected their chariots and horses in the unavoidable engagement; you have demolished ninety-nine cities (ofŚambara).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou helpest Narya, Turvaśa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvīti, Śatakratu! Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स घा राजा सत्पतिः शूशुवज्जनो रातहव्यः प्रति यः शासमिन्वति ।उक्था वा यो अभिगृणाति राधसा दानुरस्मा उपरा पिन्वते दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ gha ǀ rā́jā ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ śūśuvat ǀ jánaḥ ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ práti ǀ yáḥ ǀ śā́sam ǀ ínvati ǀukthā́ ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ abhi-gṛṇā́ti ǀ rā́dhasā ǀ dā́nuḥ ǀ asmai ǀ úparā ǀ pinvate ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law, Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: That eminent person n, the cherisher of the pious, (he instrumental tutor of the ceremony), promotes his own prosperity, who, while offering oblations to Indra, pronounces his praise; or who, along with the offerings he presents, recites hymns (in honour of him); for him the bounteous Indra causes the clouds to rain from heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law, Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असमं क्षत्रमसमा मनीषा प्र सोमपा अपसा संतु नेमे ।ये त इंद्र ददुषो वर्धयंति महि क्षत्रं स्थविरं वृष्ण्यं च ॥
verses.transliteration: ásamam ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ásamā ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ prá ǀ soma-pā́ḥ ǀ ápasā ǀ santu ǀ néme ǀyé ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ dadúṣaḥ ǀ vardháyanti ǀ máhi ǀ kṣatrám ǀ stháviram ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma, Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.
verses.wilson_translation: Unequalled is his might; unequalled is his wisdom; may these drinkers of the Somabecome equal to him the pious act, for they,Indra, who present to you oblations, augment your vast strength and your manly vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma, Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्येदेते बहुला अद्रिदुग्धाश्चमूषदश्चमसा इंद्रपानाः ।व्यश्नुहि तर्पया काममेषामथा मनो वसुदेयाय कृष्व ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhya ǀ ít ǀ eté ǀ bahulā́ḥ ǀ ádri-dugdhāḥ ǀ camū-sádaḥ ǀ camasā́ḥ ǀ indra-pā́nāḥ ǀví ǀ aśnuhi ǀ tarpáya ǀ kā́mam ǀ eṣām ǀ átha ǀ mánaḥ ǀ vasu-déyāya ǀ kṛṣva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles. Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: These copious Somajuices, expressed with stones and contained in ladles, are prepared for you; they are the beverage of Indra; quaff them; satiate your appetite with them; and then fix your mind on the wealth that is to be given (to us).
verses.griffith_verse: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles. Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपामतिष्ठद्धरुणह्वरं तमोऽंतर्वृत्रस्य जठरेषु पर्वतः ।अभीमिंद्रो नद्यो वव्रिणा हिता विश्वा अनुष्ठाः प्रवणेषु जिघ्नते ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ dharúṇa-hvaram ǀ támaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ vṛtrásya ǀ jaṭháreṣu ǀ párvataḥ ǀabhí ǀ īm ǀ índraḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ vavríṇā ǀ hitā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ anu-sthā́ḥ ǀ pravaṇéṣu ǀ jighnate ǁ
verses.english_translation: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters’ flow: in Vṛtra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed. But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivities.
verses.wilson_translation: The darkness obstructed the current of the waters; the cloud was within the belly of Vṛtra; but Indraprecipitated all the waters which the obstructor had concealed, in succession, down to the hollows (of the earth).
verses.griffith_verse: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters’ flow: in Vṛtra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed. But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स शेवृधमधि धा द्युम्नमस्मे महि क्षत्रं जनाषाळिंद्र तव्यं ।रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीन्राये च नः स्वपत्या इषे धाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ śé-vṛdham ǀ ádhi ǀ dhāḥ ǀ dyumnám ǀ asmé íti ǀ máhi ǀ kṣatrám ǀ janāṣā́ṭ ǀ indra ǀ távyam ǀrákṣa ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ sūrī́n ǀ rāyé ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ su-apatyái ǀ iṣé ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people. Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow upon us,Indra, increasing reputation; (bestow upon us) great, augmenting, and foe subduing strength; preserve us in affluence; cherish those who are wise; and supply us with wealth from which proceed excellent progeny and food.
verses.griffith_verse: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people. Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: THOUGH e’en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match.Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull. Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width.He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might. Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as’t were, even that famed mountain down.Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed. He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indra-power.A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice. Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind;And men have faith in Indra, the resplendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death. Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art,He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper. Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise.Those charioteers of thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray. Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might.O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.

verses.sanskrit: दिवश्चिदस्य वरिमा वि पप्रथ इंद्रं न मह्ना पृथिवी चन प्रति ।भीमस्तुविष्मांचर्षणिभ्य आतपः शिशीते वज्रं तेजसे न वंसगः ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ varimā́ ǀ ví ǀ paprathe ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ mahnā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ caná ǀ práti ǀbhīmáḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǀ carṣaṇí-bhyaḥ ǀ ā-tapáḥ ǀ śíśīte ǀ vájram ǀ téjase ǀ ná ǀ váṃsagaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOUGH e’en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match. Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.
verses.wilson_translation: The amplitude of Indrawas vaster than the (space of) heaven; earth was not comparable to him in bulk; formidable and most mighty, he has been ever the afflicter (of the enemies of) those men (who worship him); he has his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull (his horns).
verses.griffith_verse: THOUGH e’en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match. Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो अर्णवो न नद्यः समुद्रियः प्रति गृभ्णाति विश्रिता वरीमभिः ।इंद्रः सोमस्य पीतये वृषायते सनात्स युध्म ओजसा पनस्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ arṇaváḥ ǀ ná ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ samudríyaḥ ǀ práti ǀ gṛbhṇāti ǀ ví-śritāḥ ǀ várīma-bhiḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǀ vṛṣa-yate ǀ sanā́t ǀ sáḥ ǀ yudhmáḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ panasyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width. He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.
verses.wilson_translation: The firmament-abiding Indragraps the wide-spread waters with his comprehenisve faculties, as the ocean (receives the rivers); he rushes (impetuous) as a bull, todrikof the Soma; he, the warrior, even covets praise for his prowess.
verses.griffith_verse: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width. He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तमिंद्र पर्वतं न भोजसे महो नृम्णस्य धर्मणामिरज्यसि ।प्र वीर्येण देवताति चेकिते विश्वस्मा उग्रः कर्मणे पुरोहितः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tám ǀ indra ǀ párvatam ǀ ná ǀ bhójase ǀ maháḥ ǀ nṛmṇásya ǀ dhármaṇām ǀ irajyasi ǀprá ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ devátā ǀ áti ǀ cekite ǀ víśvasmai ǀ ugráḥ ǀ kármaṇe ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as’t were, even that famed mountain down. Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.
verses.wilson_translation: You Indra, have not (struck) the cloud for (your own) enjoyment; you rulest over those who are possessed of great wealth; that divinity is known by us to surpass all others in strength; the haughty (Indra) takes precedence of all gods, on account of his exploits.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as’t were, even that famed mountain down. Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इद्वने नमस्युभिर्वचस्यते चारु जनेषु प्रब्रुवाण इंद्रियं ।वृषा छंदुर्भवति हर्यतो वृषा क्षेमेण धेनां मघवा यदिन्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ váne ǀ namasyú-bhiḥ ǀ vacasyate ǀ cā́ru ǀ jáneṣu ǀ pra-bruvāṇáḥ ǀ indriyám ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ chánduḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ kṣémeṇa ǀ dhénām ǀ maghávā ǀ yát ǀ ínvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indra-power. A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.
verses.wilson_translation: He verily is glorified by adoring (sages) in the forest; he proclaims his beautiful vigour amongst men ; he is the granter of their wishes (to those who solicit him); he is the encourager of those who desire to worship (him), when the wealthy offerer of oblations, enjoying his protection, recites his praise.
verses.griffith_verse: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indra-power. A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इन्महानि समिथानि मज्मना कृणोति युध्म ओजसा जनेभ्यः ।अधा चन श्रद्दधति त्विषीमत इंद्राय वज्रं निघनिघ्नते वधं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ mahā́ni ǀ sam-ithā́ni ǀ majmánā ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ yudhmáḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ jánebhyaḥ ǀádha ǀ caná ǀ śrát ǀ dadhati ǀ tvíṣi-mate ǀ índrāya ǀ vájram ǀ ni-ghánighnate ǀ vadhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind; And men have faith in Indra, the resplendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrathe warrior, engages in many great conflicts for (the good of) man, with overwhelming prowess; when he hurls his fatal shaft, every one immediately has faith in the resplendent Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind; And men have faith in Indra, the resplendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि श्रवस्युः सदनानि कृत्रिमा क्ष्मया वृधान ओजसा विनाशयन् ।ज्योतींषि कृण्वन्नवृकाणि यज्यवेऽव सुक्रतुः सर्तवा अपः सृजत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ śravasyúḥ ǀ sádanāni ǀ kṛtrímā ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ vi-nāśáyan ǀjyótīṃṣi ǀ kṛṇván ǀ avṛkā́ṇi ǀ yájyave ǀ áva ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ sártavái ǀ apáḥ ǀ sṛjat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art, He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Ambitious of renown, destroying the well-built dwellings of theasuras, expanding like the earth, and setting the (heavenly) luminaries free from concealment, he, the performer of good deeds, enables the waters to flow for the benefit of his worshippers.
verses.griffith_verse: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art, He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दानाय मनः सोमपावन्नस्तु तेऽर्वांचा हरी वंदनश्रुदा कृधि ।यमिष्ठासः सारथयो य इंद्र ते न त्वा केता आ दभ्नुवंति भूर्णयः ॥
verses.transliteration: dānā́ya ǀ mánaḥ ǀ soma-pāvan ǀ astu ǀ te ǀ arvā́ñcā ǀ hárī íti ǀ vandana-śrut ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛdhi ǀyámiṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ sā́rathayaḥ ǀ yé ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ ná ǀ tvā ǀ kétāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dabhnuvanti ǀ bhū́rṇayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise. Those charioteers of thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.
verses.wilson_translation: Drinker of Soma, may your mind incline to grant our desires; hearer of praises, let your coursers be present (at our sacrifice); your charioteers are skillful in restraining (your steeds); nor,Indra, can crafty (enemies) bearing arms prevail against you.
verses.griffith_verse: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise. Those charioteers of thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्रक्षितं वसु बिभर्षि हस्तयोरषाळ्हं सहस्तन्वि श्रुतो दधे ।आवृतासोऽवतासो न कर्तृभिस्तनूषु ते क्रतव इंद्र भूरयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápra-kṣitam ǀ vásu ǀ bibharṣi ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ áṣāḷham ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ tanví ǀ śrutáḥ ǀ dadhe ǀā́-vṛtāsaḥ ǀ avatā́sáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kartṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ te ǀ krátavaḥ ǀ indra ǀ bhū́rayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might. O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.
verses.wilson_translation: You hold in yourhandsunexhausted wealth; you, renowned (Indra), have irresistible strength in your body; your limbs are invested with (glorious) exploits, as well as (are surrounded by those who come for water); in your member, Indra, are many exploits.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might. O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare.He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds. To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood.To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones. Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak;Wherewith the iron one, fierce e’en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Śushṇa fast in bonds. When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn,Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing. When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved,In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vṛtra dead and broughtest floods of rain. Thou with thy might didst grasp, the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth.Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vṛtra's stony fences through and through.

verses.sanskrit: एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः ।दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ prá ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ áva ǀ tásya ǀ camríṣaḥ ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóṣām ǀ út ǀ ayaṃsta ǀ bhurváṇiḥ ǀdákṣam ǀ mahé ǀ pāyayate ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ rátham ǀ ā-vṛ́tya ǀ hári-yogam ǀ ṛ́bhvasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare. He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Veracious (Indra) has risen up (as ardently) as a horse (approaches) a mare, to partake of the copious libations (contained) in the (sacrificial) ladles; having stayed his well-horsed, golden, and splendid chariot, heplies himself, capable of heroid (actions with Soma).
verses.griffith_verse: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare. He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं गूर्तयो नेमन्निषः परीणसः समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवः ।पतिं दक्षस्य विदथस्य नू सहो गिरिं न वेना अधि रोह तेजसा ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ gūrtáyaḥ ǀ neman-íṣaḥ ǀ párīṇasaḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ ná ǀ sam-cáraṇe ǀ saniṣyávaḥ ǀpátim ǀ dákṣasya ǀ vidáthasya ǀ nú ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ girím ǀ ná ǀ venā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ roha ǀ téjasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood. To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.
verses.wilson_translation: His adorers, bearing oblations, are thronging round (him), as (merchants) covetous of gain crowd the ocean (in vessels) on a voyage ascend quickly, with a hymn to the powerful Indra, the protector of the solemn sacrifice, as wome (climb) a mountain.
verses.griffith_verse: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood. To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स तुर्वणिर्महाँ अरेणु पौंस्ये गिरेर्भृष्टिर्न भ्राजते तुजा शवः ।येन शुष्णं मायिनमायसो मदे दुध्र आभूषु रामयन्नि दामनि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ areṇú ǀ páuṃsye ǀ giréḥ ǀ bhṛṣṭíḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhrājate ǀ tujā́ ǀ śávaḥ ǀyéna ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ māyínam ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ máde ǀ dudhráḥ ǀ ābhū́ṣu ǀ ramáyat ǀ ní ǀ dā́mani ǁ
verses.english_translation: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak; Wherewith the iron one, fierce e’en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Śushṇa fast in bonds.
verses.wilson_translation: He is quick in action, and mighty; his faultless and desructive prowess shines in manly (conflict) like the peak of a mountain (afar), with which, clothed in metal (armour), he, the supressor of the malignant, when exhilarated (by Soma), cast the wilyŚuṣṇainto prison and into bonds.
verses.griffith_verse: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak; Wherewith the iron one, fierce e’en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Śushṇa fast in bonds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवी यदि तविषी त्वावृधोतय इंद्रं सिषक्त्युषसं न सूर्यः ।यो धृष्णुना शवसा बाधते तम इयर्ति रेणुं बृहदर्हरिष्वणिः ॥
verses.transliteration: devī́ ǀ yádi ǀ táviṣī ǀ tvā́-vṛdhā ǀ ūtáye ǀ índram ǀ sísakti ǀ uṣásam ǀ ná ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇúnā ǀ śávasā ǀ bā́dhate ǀ támaḥ ǀ íyarti ǀ reṇúm ǀ bṛhát ǀ arhari-svániḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn, Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine strength waits, like the sun upon the dawn, upon that Indrawho is made more powerful for protection by you, (his worshipper), who with resolute vigour resists the gloom, and inflicts severe castigation uon his enemies, making them cry aloud (with pain).
verses.griffith_verse: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn, Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि यत्तिरो धरुणमच्युतं रजोऽतिष्ठिपो दिव आतासु बर्हणा ।स्वर्मीळ्हे यन्मद इंद्र हर्ष्याहन्वृत्रं निरपामौब्जो अर्णवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yát ǀ tiráḥ ǀ dharúṇam ǀ ácyutam ǀ rájaḥ ǀ átisthipaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́tāsu ǀ barháṇā ǀsváḥ-mīḷhe ǀ yát ǀ máde ǀ indra ǀ hárṣyā ǀ áhan ǀ vṛtrám ǀ níḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ aubjaḥ ǀ arṇavám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved, In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vṛtra dead and broughtest floods of rain.
verses.wilson_translation: . When you, destroying Indra, did distribute the (previously) hidden life-sustaining, undecaying waters through the different quarters of the heaven, then, animated (by Soma), you did engage in battle, and with exulting (prowess) slew Vṛtra, and did send down an ocean of waters.
verses.griffith_verse: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved, In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vṛtra dead and broughtest floods of rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं दिवो धरुणं धिष ओजसा पृथिव्या इंद्र सदनेषु माहिनः ।त्वं सुतस्य मदे अरिणा अपो वि वृत्रस्य समया पाष्यारुजः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ diváḥ ǀ dharúṇam ǀ dhiṣe ǀ ójasā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ sádaneṣu ǀ mā́hinaḥ ǀtvám ǀ sutásya ǀ máde ǀ ariṇāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ví ǀ vṛtrásya ǀ samáyā ǀ pāṣyā́ ǀ arujaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou with thy might didst grasp, the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth. Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vṛtra's stony fences through and through.
verses.wilson_translation: You, mighty Indra, send down from the heaven by your power, upon the realms of earth, the (world) sustaining rain; exhilarated (by Soma), you have expelled the waters (from the clouds), and have crushed Vṛtraby a solid rock.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou with thy might didst grasp, the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth. Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vṛtra's stony fences through and through.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,—Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength. Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee—the offerer's libations like floods to the depth,When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold. To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite,Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed. Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee.Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn. Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper.After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself. Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud.Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.

verses.sanskrit: प्र मंहिष्ठाय बृहते बृहद्रये सत्यशुष्माय तवसे मतिं भरे ।अपामिव प्रवणे यस्य दुर्धरं राधो विश्वायु शवसे अपावृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ máṃhiṣṭhāya ǀ bṛhaté ǀ bṛhát-raye ǀ satyá-śuṣmāya ǀ taváse ǀ matím ǀ bhare ǀapā́m-iva ǀ pravaṇé ǀ yásya ǀ duḥ-dháram ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ viśvá-āyu ǀ śávase ǀ ápa-vṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,— Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer especial praise to the most bountiful, the excellent, th eopulent, the verily powerful and stately Indra, whose irresistible impetuosity is like (the rush) of waters down a precipice, and by whom widely-diffused wealth is laid open (to his worshippers) to sustain (their) strength.
verses.griffith_verse: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,— Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध ते विश्वमनु हासदिष्टय आपो निम्नेव सवना हविष्मतः ।यत्पर्वते न समशीत हर्यत इंद्रस्य वज्रः श्नथिता हिरण्ययः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ te ǀ víśvam ǀ ánu ǀ ha ǀ asat ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ nimnā́-iva ǀ sávanā ǀ havíṣmataḥ ǀyát ǀ párvate ǀ ná ǀ sam-áśīta ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ vájraḥ ǀ śnáthitā ǀ hiraṇyáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee—the offerer's libations like floods to the depth, When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.
verses.wilson_translation: All the world,Indra, was intent upon your worship; the oblations of the sacrificer (flowed) like water (falling) to a depth); for the fatal golden thunderbolt of Indra, when hurling it (against the foe), did not sleep upon the mountain.
verses.griffith_verse: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee—the offerer's libations like floods to the depth, When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मै भीमाय नमसा समध्वर उषो न शुभ्र आ भरा पनीयसे ।यस्य धाम श्रवसे नामेंद्रियं ज्योतिरकारि हरितो नायसे ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ bhīmā́ya ǀ námasā ǀ sám ǀ adhvaré ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śubhre ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ pánīyase ǀyásya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ śrávase ǀ nā́ma ǀ indriyám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ákāri ǀ harítaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áyase ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite, Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful Uṣas, now present the oblation in this rite to the formidable, praise-deserving Indra, whose all-sustaining, celebrated, and characteristic radiance has impelled him hither and thither, (in quest) of (sacrificial) food, as (a charioteer drives) his horses (in various directions).
verses.griffith_verse: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite, Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमे त इंद्र ते वयं पुरुष्टुत ये त्वारभ्य चरामसि प्रभूवसो ।नहि त्वदन्यो गिर्वणो गिरः सघत्क्षोणीरिव प्रति नो हर्य तद्वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ té ǀ vayám ǀ puru-stuta ǀ yé ǀ tvā ǀ ā-rábhya ǀ cárāmasi ǀ prabhuvaso íti prabhu-vaso ǀnahí ǀ tvát ǀ anyáḥ ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ sághat ǀ kṣoṇī́ḥ-iva ǀ práti ǀ naḥ ǀ harya ǀ tát ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee. Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.
verses.wilson_translation: Much-lauded and most opulent Indra, we are thy, who, relying (on your favour), approach you; accepter of praise, no other than you receie our commendations; be plural ased (with our address), as the earth (cherishes) her creatures.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee. Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरि त इंद्र वीर्यं तव स्मस्यस्य स्तोतुर्मघवन्काममा पृण ।अनु ते द्यौर्बृहती वीर्यं मम इयं च ते पृथिवी नेम ओजसे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ vīryám ǀ táva ǀ smasi ǀ asyá ǀ stotúḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ kā́mam ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛṇa ǀánu ǀ te ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ ǀ vīryám ǀ mame ǀ iyám ǀ ca ǀ te ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ neme ǀ ójase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper. After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.
verses.wilson_translation: Great is your prowess,Indra; we are yours; satisfy Maghavan, the desires of this your worshipper, the vast heaven has acknowledged your might; this earth has been bowed down through your vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper. After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तमिंद्र पर्वतं महामुरुं वज्रेण वज्रिन्पर्वशश्चकर्तिथ ।अवासृजो निवृताः सर्तवा अपः सत्रा विश्वं दधिषे केवलं सहः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tám ǀ indra ǀ párvatam ǀ mahā́m ǀ urúm ǀ vájreṇa ǀ vajrin ǀ parva-śáḥ ǀ cakartitha ǀáva ǀ asṛjaḥ ǀ ní-vṛtāḥ ǀ sártavái ǀ apáḥ ǀ satrā́ ǀ víśvam ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ kévalam ǀ sáhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud. Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.
verses.wilson_translation: You, thunderer, have shattered with your bolt the broad and massive cloud into fragments, and have sent down the waters that were confined in it, to flow (at will); verily you alone possess all power.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud. Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: NE’ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvān's messenger.On paths most excellent he measured out mid-air: he with oblation calls to service of the Gods. Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads.His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven? Set high in place o’er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest;Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired. Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar.Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees. With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows,With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies. The Bhṛgus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke;Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race. Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship,The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches. Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers.O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee. Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship.Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: नू चित्सहोजा अमृतो नि तुंदते होता यद्दूतो अभवद्विवस्वतः ।वि साधिष्ठेभिः पथिभी रजो मम आ देवताता हविषा विवासति ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ cit ǀ sahaḥ-jā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ ní ǀ tundate ǀ hótā ǀ yát ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ábhavat ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀví ǀ sā́dhiṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ mame ǀ ā́ ǀ devá-tātā ǀ havíṣā ǀ vivāsati ǁ
verses.english_translation: NE’ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvān's messenger. On paths most excellent he measured out mid-air: he with oblation calls to service of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The strength-genitive rated, immortal Agniquickly issues forth, when he is the invoker of the gods, and the messenger (of the worshipper) (then proceeding) by suitable paths, he has made the firmament, and worships (the deities) in the sacrifice with oblationṣ
verses.griffith_verse: NE’ER waxeth faint the Immortal, Son of Strength, since he, the Herald, hath become Vivasvān's messenger. On paths most excellent he measured out mid-air: he with oblation calls to service of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ स्वमद्म युवमानो अजरस्तृष्वविष्यन्नतसेषु तिष्ठति ।अत्यो न पृष्ठं प्रुषितस्य रोचते दिवो न सानु स्तनयन्नचिक्रदत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ svám ǀ ádma ǀ yuvámānaḥ ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ tṛṣú ǀ aviṣyán ǀ ataséṣu ǀ tiṣṭhati ǀátyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛṣṭhám ǀ pruṣitásya ǀ rocate ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ sā́nu ǀ stanáyan ǀ acikradat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads. His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?
verses.wilson_translation: Undecaying Agni, combining his food (with his flame), and devouring it quickly, ascends the dry wood; the blaze of theconsuming (element) spreads like a (fleet) courser, and roars like a roaring (cloud) in the height of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads. His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्राणा रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिः पुरोहितो होता निषत्तो रयिषाळमर्त्यः ।रथो न विक्ष्वृंजसान आयुषु व्यानुषग्वार्या देव ऋण्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: krāṇā́ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní-sattaḥ ǀ rayiṣā́ṭ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀráthaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vikṣú ǀ ṛñjasānáḥ ǀ āyúṣu ǀ ví ǀ ānuṣák ǀ vā́ryā ǀ deváḥ ǀ ṛṇvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Set high in place o’er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest; Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired.
verses.wilson_translation: The immortal, and resplendent Agni, the bearer of oblations, honoured by the Rudrasand the Vasusthe invoker of the gods, who presides over oblations and is the distributor of riches, praised by his worshippers, and admired like a chariot amongst mankind, accepts the oblations that are successively presented.
verses.griffith_verse: Set high in place o’er all that Vasus, Rudras do, immortal, Lord of riches, seated as High Priest; Hastening like a car to men, to those who live, the God without delay gives boons to be desired.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि वातजूतो अतसेषु तिष्ठते वृथा जुहूभिः सृण्या तुविष्वणिः ।तृषु यदग्ने वनिनो वृषायसे कृष्णं त एम रुशदूर्मे अजर ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ vā́ta-jūtaḥ ǀ ataséṣu ǀ tiṣṭhate ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ juhū́bhiḥ ǀ sṛ́ṇyā ǀ tuvi-svániḥ ǀtṛṣú ǀ yát ǀ agne ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ vṛṣa-yáse ǀ kṛṣṇám ǀ te ǀ éma ǀ rúśat-ūrme ǀ ajara ǁ
verses.english_translation: Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar. Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees.
verses.wilson_translation: Excited by the wind, and roaring loudly,Agnipenetrates easily with his flames and diffusive (intensity) among the timber; when, undecaying and fiercely-blazing Agni, you rush rapidly like a bull amongst the forest trees, your path is blackened.
verses.griffith_verse: Urged by the wind be spreads through dry wood as he lists, armed with his tongues for sickles, with a mighty roar. Black is thy path, Agni, changeless, with glittering waves! when like a bull thou rushest eager to the trees.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तपुर्जंभो वन आ वातचोदितो यूथे न साह्वाँ अव वाति वंसगः ।अभिव्रजन्नक्षितं पाजसा रजः स्थातुश्चरथं भयते पतत्रिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: tápuḥ-jambhaḥ ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ vā́ta-coditaḥ ǀ yūthé ǀ ná ǀ sahvā́n ǀ áva ǀ vāti ǀ váṃsagaḥ ǀabhi-vrájan ǀ ákṣitam ǀ pā́jasā ǀ rájaḥ ǀ sthātúḥ ǀ carátham ǀ bhayate ǀ patatríṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows, With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies.
verses.wilson_translation: The flame-weaponed and breeze-excited Agni, assailing the unexhaled moisture (of the trees), with all his strength, in a volume of fire, rushes triumphant (against all things) in the forest, like a bull, and all, whether stationary or moveable, are afraid of him as he flies along.
verses.griffith_verse: With teeth of flame, wind-driven, through the wood he speeds, triumphant like a bull among the herd of cows, With bright strength roaming to the everlasting air: things fixed, things moving quake before him as he flies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दधुष्ट्वा भृगवो मानुषेष्वा रयिं न चारुं सुहवं जनेभ्यः ।होतारमग्ने अतिथिं वरेण्यं मित्रं न शेवं दिव्याय जन्मने ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhúḥ ǀ tvā ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ rayím ǀ ná ǀ cā́rum ǀ su-hávam ǀ jánebhyaḥ ǀhótāram ǀ agne ǀ átithim ǀ váreṇyam ǀ mitrám ǀ ná ǀ śévam ǀ divyā́ya ǀ jánmane ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Bhṛgus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke; Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race.
verses.wilson_translation: The Bhṛgusamongst men, for the sake of a divine birth, cherished you like a precious treasure Agni, who sacrifices for men, who are the invoker (of the gods), the (welcome) guest at sacrifices, and who are to be valued like an affectionate friend.
verses.griffith_verse: The Bhṛgus established thee among mankind for men, like as a treasure, beauteous, easy to invoke; Thee, Agni, as a herald and choice-worthy guest, as an auspicious Friend to the Celestial Race.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: होतारं सप्त जुह्वो यजिष्ठं यं वाघतो वृणते अध्वरेषु ।अग्निं विश्वेषामरतिं वसूनां सपर्यामि प्रयसा यामि रत्नं ॥
verses.transliteration: hótāram ǀ saptá ǀ juhváḥ ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ yám ǀ vāghátaḥ ǀ vṛṇáte ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀagním ǀ víśveṣām ǀ aratím ǀ vásūnām ǀ saparyā́mi ǀ práyasā ǀ yā́mi ǀ rátnam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship, The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches.
verses.wilson_translation: I worship with oblations that Agniwhom the seven invoking priests invite as the invoker of the gods; who is most worthy of worship at sacrifices, and who is the donor of all riches; I solicit of him wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, the seven tongues' deftest Sacrificer, him whom the priests elect at solemn worship, The Herald, messenger of all the Vasus, I serve with dainty food, I ask for riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अच्छिद्रा सूनो सहसो नो अद्य स्तोतृभ्यो मित्रमहः शर्म यच्छ ।अग्ने गृणंतमंहस उरुष्योर्जो नपात्पूर्भिरायसीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ácchidrā ǀ sūno íti ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaccha ǀágne ǀ gṛṇántam ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ uruṣya ǀ ū́rjaḥ ǀ napāt ǀ pūḥ-bhíḥ ǀ ā́yasībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers. O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Son of strength, favourably-shining Agni, grant to your worshipper on this occasion uninterrupted felicity; offspring of food, preserve him who praises you from sin with guards of metal.
verses.griffith_verse: Grant, Son of Strength, thou rich in friends, a refuge without a flaw this day to us thy praisers. O Agni, Son of Strength, with forts of iron preserve thou from distress the man who lauds thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भवा वरूथं गृणते विभावो भवा मघवन्मघवद्भ्यः शर्म ।उरुष्याग्ने अंहसो गृणंतं प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: bháva ǀ várūtham ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ vibhā-vaḥ ǀ bháva ǀ magha-van ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ śárma ǀuruṣyá ǀ agne ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ gṛṇántam ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship. Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: Variously-shining Agni, be a shelter to him who praises you; be prosperity,Maghavan, to the wealthy (offerers of oblations); protect, Agni, your worshipper from sin; may Agni, who is rich with righteous acts, come (to us) quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: Be thou a refuge, Bright One, to the singer, a shelter, Bounteous Lord, to those who worship. Preserve the singer from distress, O Agni. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni.Centre art thou, Vaiśvānara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar. The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven.Vaiśvānara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Ārya.
