As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaiśvānara, in Agni.Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran. As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald.Vaiśvānara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort. Even the lofty heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, hath not attained thy greatness.Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle. Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Pūru's sons follow as Vṛtra's slayer:Agni Vaiśvānara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Śambara through and shattered down his fences. Vaiśvānara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvājas,Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purūṇītha, son of Śatavani.

verses.sanskrit: वया इदग्ने अग्नयस्ते अन्ये त्वे विश्वे अमृता मादयंते ।वैश्वानर नाभिरसि क्षितीनां स्थूणेव जनाँ उपमिद्ययंथ ॥
verses.transliteration: vayā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ agne ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ te ǀ anyé ǀ tvé íti ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ mādayante ǀváiśvānara ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ asi ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ sthū́ṇā-iva ǀ jánān ǀ upa-mít ǀ yayantha ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni. Centre art thou, Vaiśvānara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever other fires there may be, they are but ramifications,Agni, of you; but they all rejoice, being immortal in you; you,Vaiśvānara, are the navel of men, and suppor tthem like a deep-plural nted column.
verses.griffith_verse: THE other fires are, verily, thy branches; the Immortals all rejoice in thee, O Agni. Centre art thou, Vaiśvānara, of the people, sustaining men like a deep-founded pillar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मूर्धा दिवो ना��िरग्निः पृथिव्या अथाभवदरती रोदस्योः ।तं त्वा देवासोऽजनयंत देवं वैश्वानर ज्योतिरिदार्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: mūrdhā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ átha ǀ abhavat ǀ aratíḥ ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ajanayanta ǀ devám ǀ váiśvānara ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ít ǀ ā́ryāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven. Vaiśvānara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Ārya.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the head of heaven, the navel of earth, became the ruler over both earth and heaven; all the gods engendered you,Vaiśvānara, in the form of light, for the venerable sage.
verses.griffith_verse: The forehead of the sky, earth's centre, Agni became the messenger of earth and heaven. Vaiśvānara, the Deities produced thee, a God, to be a light unto the Ārya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ सूर्ये न रश्मयो ध्रुवासो वैश्वानरे दधिरेऽग्ना वसूनि ।या पर्वतेष्वोषधीष्वप्सु या मानुषेष्वसि तस्य राजा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ sū́rye ǀ ná ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ dhruvā́saḥ ǀ vaiśvānaré ǀ dadhire ǀ agnā́ ǀ vásūni ǀyā́ ǀ párvateṣu ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǀ ap-sú ǀ yā́ ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ ási ǀ tásya ǀ rā́jā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaiśvānara, in Agni. Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran.
verses.wilson_translation: Treasures were deposited in the Agni,Vaiśvānara, like the permanent rays (of light) in the sun; you are the sovereign of all the treasures that exist in the mountains, in the herbs, in the waters, or amongst men.
verses.griffith_verse: As in the Sun firm rays are set for ever, treasures are in Vaiśvānara, in Agni. Of all the riches in the hills, the waters, the herbs, among mankind, thou art the Sovran.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहती इव सूनवे रोदसी गिरो होता मनुष्यो न दक्षः ।स्वर्वते सत्यशुष्माय पूर्वीर्वैश्वानराय नृतमाय यह्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhatī́ ivéti bṛhatī́-iva ǀ sūnáve ǀ ródasī íti ǀ gíraḥ ǀ hótā ǀ manuṣyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀsváḥ-vate ǀ satyá-śuṣmāya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ vaiśvānarā́ya ǀ nṛ́-tamāya ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald. Vaiśvānara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort.
verses.wilson_translation: . Heaven and earth expanded as it were for their son. The experienced sacrificer recites, like a bard, many ancient and copious praises addressed to the graceful-moving, truly-vigorous, and all-guiding Vaiśvānara.
verses.griffith_verse: As the great World-halves, so are their Son's praises; skilled, as a man, to act, is he the Herald. Vaiśvānara, celestial, truly mighty, most manly One, hath many a youthful consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवश्चित्ते बृहतो जातवेदो वैश्वानर प्र रिरिचे महित्वं ।राजा कृष्टीनामसि मानुषीणां युधा देवेभ्यो वरिवश्चकर्थ ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ váiśvānara ǀ prá ǀ ririce ǀ mahi-tvám ǀrā́jā ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ asi ǀ mā́nuṣīṇām ǀ yudhā́ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ cakartha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even the lofty heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, hath not attained thy greatness. Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Vaiśvānara, who knows all that are born, your magnitude has exceeded that of the spacious heaven; you are the monarch ofmanu-descended men; you have regained for the gods in battle, the wealth (carries off by theasuras).
verses.griffith_verse: Even the lofty heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, hath not attained thy greatness. Thou art the King of lands where men are settled, thou hast brought comfort to the Gods in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचंते ।वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वाँ अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शंबरं भेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ vocam ǀ yám ǀ pūrávaḥ ǀ vṛtra-hánam ǀ sácante ǀvaiśvānaráḥ ǀ dásyum ǀ agníḥ ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ ádhūnot ǀ kā́ṣṭhāḥ ǀ áva ǀ śámbaram ǀ bhet ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Pūru's sons follow as Vṛtra's slayer: Agni Vaiśvānara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Śambara through and shattered down his fences.
verses.wilson_translation: I extol the greatness of that showerer of rain whom men celebrate as the slayer of Vṛtra; the Agni,Vaiśvānara, slew the stealer (of the waters) and sent them down (upon earth), and clove the (obstructing) cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: Now will I tell the greatness of the Hero whom Pūru's sons follow as Vṛtra's slayer: Agni Vaiśvānara struck down the Dasyu, cleave Śambara through and shattered down his fences.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानरो महिम्ना विश्वकृष्टिर्भरद्वाजेषु यजतो विभावा ।शातवनेये शतिनीभिरग्निः पुरुणीथे जरते सूनृतावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: vaiśvānaráḥ ǀ mahimnā́ ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭiḥ ǀ bharát-vājeṣu ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀśāta-vaneyé ǀ śatínībhiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ puru-nīthé ǀ jarate ǀ sūnṛ́tā-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vaiśvānara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvājas, Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purūṇītha, son of Śatavani.
verses.wilson_translation: Vaiśvānaraby his magnitude is all men, and is to be worshipped as the diffuser of manifold light in offerings of nutritious viands;Agni, the speaker of truth, praises with many commendations Puruṇītha, the son of Śātavani.
verses.griffith_verse: Vaiśvānara, dwelling by his might with all men, far-shining, holy mid the Bharadvājas, Is lauded, excellent, with hundred praises by Purūṇītha, son of Śatavani.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: As ’twere Some goodly treasure Mātariśvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhṛgu,Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy. Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship.As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer. May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e’en at his birth, is sweet as honey;Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created. Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy.May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling. As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches,Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: वह्निं यशसं विदथस्य केतुं सुप्राव्यं दूतं सद्योअर्थं ।द्विजन्मानं रयिमिव प्रशस्तं रातिं भरद्भृगवे मातरिश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: váhnim ǀ yaśásam ǀ vidáthasya ǀ ketúm ǀ supra-avyám ǀ dūtám ǀ sadyáḥ-artham ǀdvi-jánmānam ǀ rayím-iva ǀ pra-śastám ǀ rātím ǀ bharat ǀ bhṛ́gave ǀ mātaríśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ’twere Some goodly treasure Mātariśvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhṛgu, Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.
verses.wilson_translation: Mātariśvanbrought, as a friend, to Bhṛgu, the celebrated Vahni, the illuminato of sacrifices, the careful protector (of his votaries), the swift-moving messenger (of the gods), the offspring of two parents, (to be to him) as it were a precious treasure.
verses.griffith_verse: As ’twere Some goodly treasure Mātariśvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhṛgu, Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य शासुरुभयासः सचंते हविष्मंत उशिजो ये च मर्ताः ।दिवश्चित्पूर्वो न्यसादि होतापृच्छ्यो विश्पतिर्विक्षु वेधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ śā́suḥ ǀ ubháyāsaḥ ǀ sacante ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ mártāḥ ǀdiváḥ ǀ cit ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ ní ǀ asādi ǀ hótā ǀ ā-pṛ́cchyaḥ ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship. As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.
verses.wilson_translation: Both (gods and men) are the worshippers of this ruler; those who are to be desired (of the gods), and those who are mortal, beaing oblations; for this venerable invoker (of the gods), the lord of men, and distributor (of desired benefits), was plural ced by the officiating priests (upon the altar), before the sun was in the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship. As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं नव्यसी हृद आ जायमानमस्मत्सुकीर्तिर्मधुजिह्वमश्याः ।यमृत्विजो वृजने मानुषासः प्रयस्वंत आयवो जीजनंत ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ návyasī ǀ hṛdáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jā́yamānam ǀ asmát ǀ su-kīrtíḥ ǀ mádhu-jihvam ǀ aśyāḥ ǀyám ǀ ṛtvíjaḥ ǀ vṛjáne ǀ mā́nuṣāsaḥ ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ jī́jananta ǁ
verses.english_translation: May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e’en at his birth, is sweet as honey; Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.
verses.wilson_translation: May our newest celebration come before that Agni, who is sweet-tongued, and is to be engendered in the heart; whom men, the descendants of Manu, sacrificing and presenting oblations to him, beget in the time and battle.
verses.griffith_verse: May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e’en at his birth, is sweet as honey; Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उशिक्पावको वसुर्मानुषेषु वरेण्यो होताधायि विक्षु ।दमूना गृहपतिर्दम आँ अग्निर्भुवद्रयिपती रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: uśík ǀ pāvakáḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀ hótā ǀ adhāyi ǀ vikṣú ǀdámūnāḥ ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ rayi-pátiḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy. May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the desirable, the purifying, the giver of dwellings, the excellent, the invoker (of the gods) has been plural ced (upon the altar) among men; may he be inimical (to our foes), the protector of (our) dwellings and the guardian of the treasures in (this) mansion.
verses.griffith_verse: Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy. May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा वयं पतिमग्ने रयीणां प्र शंसामो मतिभिर्गोतमासः ।आशुं न वाजंभरं मर्जयंतः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ pátim ǀ agne ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ prá ǀ śaṃsāmaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ gótamāsaḥ ǀāśúm ǀ ná ǀ vājam-bharám ǀ marjáyantaḥ ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches, Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: We, born of the race of Gotama, praise you,Agni, with acceptable (hymns), as the lord of riches; rubbing you, the bearer of oblations, (as a rider rubs down), a horse; may he who has acquired wealth by sacred rites, come hither quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches, Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands,My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra. Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor.For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit. To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer,To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver. Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,—Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra. So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as ’twere a horse, through love of glory,To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles. Even for him hath Tvaṣṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle,Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vṛtra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker. As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Viṣṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered.The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain. To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Gods, wove praises.The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not. Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven.Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle. Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vṛtra, drier up of waters.He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty. The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides.Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turvīti. Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vṛtra cast thy bolt of thunder.Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow. Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly,When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen. When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror.May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic. Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o’er much, electeth.Indra hath helped Etaśa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Sūrya. Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee.Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु प्र तवसे तुराय प्रयो न हर्मि स्तोमं माहिनाय ।ऋचीषमायाध्रिगव ओहमिंद्राय ब्रह्माणि राततमा ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ taváse ǀ turā́ya ǀ práyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ harmi ǀ stómam ǀ mā́hināya ǀṛ́cīṣamāya ǀ ádhri-gave ǀ óham ǀ índrāya ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ rātá-tamā ǁ
verses.english_translation: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands, My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer adoration to that powerful, rapid, mighty, praise-meriting, and unobstructed Indra; adoration that is acceptable, and oblations that are grateful, as food (to a hungry man).
verses.griffith_verse: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands, My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु प्रय इव प्र यंसि भराम्यांगूषं बाधे सुवृक्ति ।इंद्राय हृदा मनसा मनीषा प्रत्नाय पत्ये धियो मर्जयंत ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ práyaḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ yaṃsi ǀ bhárāmi ǀ āṅgūṣám ǀ bā́dhe ǀ su-vṛktí ǀíndrāya ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ pratnā́ya ǀ pátye ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ marjayanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor. For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer (oblations, acceptable as) food (to the hungry), to that Indra; I raise (to him) exclamations that may be of efficacy in discomfiting (my foe); others (also) worship Indra, the ancient lord, in heart, in mind, and in understanding.
verses.griffith_verse: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor. For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु त्यमुपमं स्वर्षां भराम्यांगूषमास्येन ।मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyám ǀ upa-mám ǀ svaḥ-sā́m ǀ bhárāmi ǀ āṅgūṣám ǀ āsyéna ǀmáṃhiṣṭham ǀ ácchokti-bhiḥ ǀ matīnā́m ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ sūrím ǀ vavṛdhádhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer, To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer with my mouth a loud acclamation, with powerful and pure words of praise, to exalt him who is the type (of all), the giver (of good things), the great, the wise.
verses.griffith_verse: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer, To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु स्तोमं सं हिनोमि रथं न तष्टेव तत्सिनाय ।गिरश्च गिर्वाहसे सुवृक्तींद्राय विश्वमिन्वं मेधिराय ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stómam ǀ sám ǀ hinomi ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ tát-sināya ǀgíraḥ ǀ ca ǀ gírvāhase ǀ su-vṛktí ǀ índrāya ǀ viśvam-invám ǀ médhirāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,— Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: I prepare praises fo rhim, as a carpenter constructs a car, (that the driver) may thence (obtain) food; praises well deserved, to him who is entitled to commendation, and excellent oblations to the wise Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,— Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु सप्तिमिव श्रवस्येंद्रायार्कं जुह्वा समंजे ।वीरं दानौकसं वंदध्यै पुरां गूर्तश्रवसं दर्माणं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sáptim-iva ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ índrāya ǀ arkám ǀ juhvā́ ǀ sám ǀ añje ǀvīrám ǀ dāná-okasam ǀ vandádhyai ǀ purā́m ǀ gūrtá-śravasam ǀ darmā́ṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as ’twere a horse, through love of glory, To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.
verses.wilson_translation: To propitiate that Indrafor the sake of food, I combinepraise with utterance, as (a man harnesses) a horse (to a car), in order to celebrate the heroic, munificent, and food-conferring Indra, the destroyer of the cities (of theasuras).
verses.griffith_verse: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as ’twere a horse, through love of glory, To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु त्वष्टा तक्षद्वज्रं स्वपस्तमं स्वर्यं रणाय ।वृत्रस्य चिद्विदद्येन मर्म तुजन्नीशानस्तुजता कियेधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ takṣat ǀ vájram ǀ svápaḥ-tamam ǀ svaryám ǀ ráṇāya ǀvṛtrásya ǀ cit ǀ vidát ǀ yéna ǀ márma ǀ tuján ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ tujatā́ ǀ kiyedhā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even for him hath Tvaṣṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle, Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vṛtra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.
verses.wilson_translation: For that Indra, verily Tvaṣṭāsharpened the well-acting, sure-aimed thunderbolt for the battle, with which fatal (weapon) the foe-subduing and mighty sovereign severed the limbs of Vṛtra.
verses.griffith_verse: Even for him hath Tvaṣṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle, Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vṛtra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदु मातुः सवनेष��� सद्यो महः पितुं पपिवांचार्वन्ना ।मुषायद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान्विध्यद्वराहं तिरो अद्रिमस्ता ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ mātúḥ ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ pitúm ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ cā́ru ǀ ánnā ǀmuṣāyát ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ pacatám ǀ sáhīyān ǀ vídhyat ǀ varāhám ǀ tiráḥ ǀ ádrim ǀ ástā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Viṣṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered. The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.
verses.wilson_translation: Quickly quaffing the libations, and devouring the grateful viands (presented) at the three (daily) sacrifices which are dedicated to the creator (of the world), he, the pervadere of the universe, stole the ripe (treasures of theasuras); the vanquisher (of his foes), the hurler of the thunderbolt, encountering pierced the cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Viṣṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered. The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु ग्नाश्चिद्देवपत्नीरिंद्रायार्कमहिहत्य ऊवुः ।परि द्यावापृथिवी जभ्र उर्वी नास्य ते महिमानं परि ष्टः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ devá-patnīḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ arkám ǀ ahi-hátye ǀ ūvurítyūvuḥ ǀpári ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ jabhre ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ asya ǀ té íti ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ pári ǀ sta íti staḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Gods, wove praises. The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.
verses.wilson_translation: To that Indrathe women, the wives of the gods, addressed their hymns, on the destruction of Ahi; he encompasses the extensive heaven and earth; they two do not surpass your vastness.
verses.griffith_verse: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Gods, wove praises. The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदेव प्र रिरिचे महित्वं दिवस्पृथिव्याः पर्यंतरिक्षात् ।स्वराळिंद्रो दम आ विश्वगूर्तः स्वरिरमत्रो ववक्षे रणाय ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ evá ǀ prá ǀ ririce ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ pári ǀ antárikṣāt ǀsva-rā́ṭ ǀ índraḥ ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ viśvá-gūrtaḥ ǀ su-aríḥ ǀ ámatraḥ ǀ vavakṣe ǀ ráṇāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven. Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.
verses.wilson_translation: His magnitude verily exceeds that of the heaven, and earth and sky;Indra, self-irradiating in his dwelling, equal to every exploit, engaged with no unworthy foe, and killed in conflict, calls to battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven. Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदेव शवसा शुषंतं वि वृश्चद्वज्रेण वृत्रमिंद्रः ।गा न व्राणा अवनीरमुंचदभि श्रवो दावने सचेताः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ evá ǀ śávasā ǀ śuṣántam ǀ ví ǀ vṛścat ǀ vájreṇa ǀ vṛtrám ǀ índraḥ ǀgā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vrāṇā́ḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ amuñcat ǀ abhí ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dāváne ǀ sá-cetāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vṛtra, drier up of waters. He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, by his vigour, cut to pieces with his thunderbolt Vṛtra, the absorber (of moisture), and set free the preserving waters, like cows (recovered from thieves); and, consentient (to the wishes)of the giver of the oblation, (grants him) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Through his own strength Indra with bolt of thunder cut piece-meal Vṛtra, drier up of waters. He let the floods go free, like cows imprisoned, for glory, with a heart inclined to bounty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदु त्वेषसा रंत सिंधवः परि यद्वज्रेण सीमयच्छत् ।ईशानकृद्दाशुषे दशस्यंतुर्वीतये गाधं तुर्वणिः कः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tveṣásā ǀ ranta ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ pári ǀ yát ǀ vájreṇa ǀ sīm ǀ áyacchat ǀīśāna-kṛ́t ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ daśasyán ǀ turvī́taye ǀ gādhám ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides. Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turvīti.
verses.wilson_translation: Through his power, the rivers sport, since he has opened (a way for them) by his thunderbolt; establishing his supremacy and granting a (recompense) to the giver (of the oblation), he, the swift-moving provided a resting plural ce for Tūrvīti.
verses.griffith_verse: The rivers played, through his impetuous splendour, since with his bolt he compassed them on all sides. Using his might and favouring him who worshipped, he made a ford, victorious, for Turvīti.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु प्र भरा तूतुजानो वृत्राय वज्रमीशानः कियेधाः ।गोर्न पर्व वि रदा तिरश्चेष्यन्नर्णांस्यपां चरध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ bhara ǀ tū́tujānaḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ya ǀ vájram ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ kiyedhā́ḥ ǀgóḥ ǀ ná ǀ párva ǀ ví ǀ rada ǀ tiraścā́ ǀ íṣyan ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ apā́m ǀ carádhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vṛtra cast thy bolt of thunder. Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who are the quick moving and strength-endowed lord (of all), hurl your thunderbolt against this Vṛtraand sever his joints, as (butchers cut up) a cow, that the rains may issue from him, and the waters flow (over the earth).
verses.griffith_verse: Vast, with thine ample power, with eager movement, against this Vṛtra cast thy bolt of thunder. Rend thou his joints, as of an ox, dissevered, with bolt oblique, that floods of rain may follow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदु प्र ब्रूहि पूर्व्याणि तुरस्य कर्माणि नव्य उक्थैः ।युधे यदिष्णान आयुधान्यृघायमाणो निरिणाति शत्रून् ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ brūhi ǀ pūrvyā́ṇi ǀ turásya ǀ kármāṇi ǀ návyaḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀyudhé ǀ yát ǀ iṣṇānáḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ ṛghāyámāṇaḥ ǀ ni-riṇā́ti ǀ śátrūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly, When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: Proclaim, with new hymns, the former exploits of that quick-moving Indra, when wielding his weapons in battle, he encounters and destroys his enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Sing with new lauds his exploits wrought aforetime, the deeds of him, yea, him who moveth swiftly, When, hurling forth his weapons in the battle, he with impetuous wrath lays low the foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदु भिया गिरयश्च दृळ्हा द्यावा च भूमा जनुषस्तुजेते ।उपो वेनस्य जोगुवान ओणिं सद्यो भुवद्वीर्याय नोधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ giráyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ dṛḷhā́ḥ ǀ dyā́vā ǀ ca ǀ bhū́ma ǀ janúṣaḥ ǀ tujete íti ǀúpo íti ǀ venásya ǀ jóguvānaḥ ǀ oṇím ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ vīryā́ya ǀ nodhā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror. May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic.
verses.wilson_translation: Through fear of him, the stable mountains (are still), and through dread of his appearance, heaven and earth tremble; may,Nodhas, praising repeatedly the preserving power of that beloved Indra, be speedily (blessed) with vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: When he, yea, he, comes forth the firm. Set mountains and the whole heaven and earth, tremble for terror. May Nodhas, ever praising the protection of that dear Friend, gain quickly strength heroic.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा इदु त्यदनु दाय्येषामेको यद्वव्ने भूरेरीशानः ।प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं सौवश्व्ये सुष्विमावदिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyát ǀ ánu ǀ dāyi ǀ eṣām ǀ ékaḥ ǀ yát ǀ vavné ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀprá ǀ étaśam ǀ sū́rye ǀ paspṛdhānám ǀ sáuvaśvye ǀ súsvim ǀ āvat ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o’er much, electeth. Indra hath helped Etaśa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Sūrya.
verses.wilson_translation: To him has that praise been offered which he, sole (victor over his foes), and lord of maniford wealth, prefers (to receive) from those (who praise him).Indrahas defended the pious sacrificer Etaśawhen contending with Sūrya, the son of Svaśva.
verses.griffith_verse: Now unto him of these things hath been given what he who rules alone o’er much, electeth. Indra hath helped Etaśa, Soma-presser, contending in the race of steeds with Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा ते हारियोजना सुवृक्तींद्र ब्रह्माणि गोतमासो अक्रन् ।ऐषु विश्वपेशसं धियं धाः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ te ǀ hāri-yojana ǀ su-vṛktí ǀ índra ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ gótamāsaḥ ǀ akran ǀā́ ǀ eṣu ǀ viśvá-peśasam ǀ dhíyam ǀ dhāḥ ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee. Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, harnesser of steeds, the descendants of Gotamahave offered to you prayers of efficacy to secure your presence; bestow upon them every sort of affluence; may he who has acquired wealth by pious acts, come hither quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus to thee, Indra, yoker of Bay Coursers, the Gotamas have brought their prayers to please thee. Bestow upon them thought, decked with all beauty. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIKE Aṅgiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty.Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer. Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty,Through whom our sires, Aṅgirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle. When Indra and the Aṅgirases desired it, Saramā found provision for her offspring.Bṛhaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph. Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain;Thou hast, with speeders, with Daśagvas, Indra, Śakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala. Praised by Aṅgirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispelled the darkness.Thou Indra, hast spread out the earth's high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven. This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker,That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water. Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever.In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven. Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternationRound heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour. Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship.Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour. Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes.For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons. Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty.As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent. Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted.Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending: strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power. O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal,Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: प्र मन्महे शवसानाय शूषमांगूषं गिर्वणसे अंगिरस्वत् ।सुवृक्तिभिः स्तुवत ऋग्मियायार्चामार्कं नरे विश्रुताय ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ manmahe ǀ śavasānā́ya ǀ śūṣám ǀ āṅgūṣám ǀ gírvaṇase ǀ aṅgirasvát ǀsuvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ stuvaté ǀ ṛgmiyā́ya ǀ árcāma ǀ arkám ǀ náre ǀ ví-śrutāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: LIKE Aṅgiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty. Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer.
verses.wilson_translation: We mediate like Aṅgiras, an acceptable adress to that powerful and praise-deserving Indra, who is to be adored by his worshippers (with prayers) of efficacy, to bring him to the ceremony; let us repeat a prayer to the celebrated leader of all.
verses.griffith_verse: LIKE Aṅgiras a gladdening laud we ponder to him who loveth song, exceeding mighty. Let us sing glory to the far-famed Hero who must be praised with fair hymns by the singer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो महे महि नमो भरध्वमांगूष्यं शवसानाय साम ।येना नः पूर्वे पितरः पदज्ञा अर्चंतो अंगिरसो गा अविंदन् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ mahé ǀ máhi ǀ námaḥ ǀ bharadhvam ǀ āṅgūṣyám ǀ śavasānā́ya ǀ sā́ma ǀyéna ǀ naḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ pada-jñā́ḥ ǀ árcantaḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ávindan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty, Through whom our sires, Aṅgirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, priests, offer to the vast and most powerful,Indra, earnest veneration, a chant fit to be sung aloud; for through him our forefathers, the Aṅgirasas, worshipping him, and knowing the footmark, recovered (the stolen) cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Unto the great bring ye great adoration, a chant with praise to him exceeding mighty, Through whom our sires, Aṅgirases, singing praises and knowing well the places, found the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्यांगिरसां चेष्टौ विदत्सरमा तनयाय धासिं ।बृहस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद्गाः समुस्रियाभिर्वावशंत नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ ca ǀ iṣṭáu ǀ vidát ǀ sarámā ǀ tánayāya ǀ dhāsím ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ bhinát ǀ ádrim ǀ vidát ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ usríyābhiḥ ǀ vāvaśanta ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Indra and the Aṅgirases desired it, Saramā found provision for her offspring. Bṛhaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph.
verses.wilson_translation: When the search was set on foot by Indraand the Aṅgirasas, Suramā secured food for her young; then Bṛhaspatislew the devourer and rescued the kine, and the gods, with the cattle, proclaimed their joy alouḍ
verses.griffith_verse: When Indra and the Aṅgirases desired it, Saramā found provision for her offspring. Bṛhaspati cleft the mountain, found the cattle: the heroes shouted with the kine in triumph.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स सुष्टुभा स स्तुभा सप्त विप्रैः स्वरेणाद्रिं स्वर्यो नवग्वैः ।सरण्युभिः फलिगमिंद्र शक्र वलं रवेण दरयो दशग्वैः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ su-stúbhā ǀ sáḥ ǀ stubhā́ ǀ saptá ǀ vípraiḥ ǀ svaréṇa ǀ ádrim ǀ svaryáḥ ǀ náva-gvaiḥ ǀsaraṇyú-bhiḥ ǀ phali-gám ǀ indra ǀ śakra ǀ valám ǀ ráveṇa ǀ darayaḥ ǀ dáśa-gvaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain; Thou hast, with speeders, with Daśagvas, Indra, Śakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Indra, who are to be gratified with a laudatory and well-accented hymn by the seven priests, whether engaged for nine months, or for ten; and, desirous of (safe) protection, you have terrified by your voice the divisible fructifying cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: Mid shout, loud shout, and roar, with the Navagvas, seven singers, hast thou, heavenly, rent the mountain; Thou hast, with speeders, with Daśagvas, Indra, Śakra, with thunder rent obstructive Vala.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गृणानो अंगिरोभिर्दस्म वि वरुषसा सूर्येण गोभिरंधः ।वि भूम्या अप्रथय इंद्र सानु दिवो रज उपरमस्तभायः ॥
verses.transliteration: gṛṇānáḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ dasma ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ uṣásā ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ ándhaḥ ǀví ǀ bhū́myāḥ ǀ aprathayaḥ ǀ indra ǀ sā́nu ǀ diváḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ úparam ǀ astabhāyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised by Aṅgirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispelled the darkness. Thou Indra, hast spread out the earth's high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyer of foes, praised by the Aṅgirasas, you have scattered the darkness with the dawn, and with the rays of the sun; you have made straight the elevations of the earth; you have strengthened the foundations of the ethereal region.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised by Aṅgirases, thou, foe-destroyer, hast, with the Dawn, Sun, rays, dispelled the darkness. Thou Indra, hast spread out the earth's high ridges, and firmly fixed the region under heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदु प्रयक्षतममस्य कर्म दस्मस्य चारुतममस्ति दंसः ।उपह्वरे यदुपरा अपिन्वन्मध्वर्णसो नद्यश्चतस्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ práyakṣa-tamam ǀ asya ǀ kárma ǀ dasmásya ǀ cā́ru-tamam ǀ asti ǀ dáṃsaḥ ǀupa-hvaré ǀ yát ǀ úparāḥ ǀ ápinvat ǀ mádhu-arṇasaḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker, That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water.
verses.wilson_translation: The deeds of that graceful Indraare most admirable; his exploits are most glorious, in that he has replenished the four rivers of sweet water, spread over the surface of the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: This is the deed most worthy of all honour, the fairest marvel of the Wonder-Worker, That, nigh where heaven bends down, he made four rivers flow full with waves that carry down sweet water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्विता वि वव्रे सनजा सनीळे अयास्यः स्तवमानेभिरर्कैः ।भगो न मेने परमे व्योमन्नधारयद्रोदसी सुदंसाः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvitā́ ǀ ví ǀ vavre ǀ saná-jā ǀ sánīḷe íti sá-nīḷe ǀ ayā́syaḥ ǀ stávamānebhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀbhágaḥ ǀ ná ǀ méne íti ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀ ádhārayat ǀ ródasī íti ǀ su-dáṃsāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever. In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is not to be attained by violence, but (is easily propitiated) by those who praise him with sacred hymns, parted twofold the eternal and united (sphered of heaven and earth); the graceful Indracherished the heaven and earth, like the sun in the august and most excellent sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Unwearied, won with lauding hymns, he parted of old the ancient Pair, united ever. In highest sky like Bhaga, he the doer of marvels set both Dames and earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनाद्दिवं परि भूमा विरूपे पुनर्भुवा युवती स्वेभिरेवैः ।कृष्णेभिरक्तोषा रुशद्भिर्वपुर्भिरा चरतो अन्यान्या ॥
verses.transliteration: sanā́t ǀ dívam ǀ pári ǀ bhū́ma ǀ vírūpe íti ví-rūpe ǀ punaḥ-bhúvā ǀ yuvatī́ íti ǀ svébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀkṛṣṇébhiḥ ǀ aktā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ rúśat-bhiḥ ǀ vápuḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ carataḥ ǀ anyā́-anyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternation Round heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: (Night and dawn), of various complexion, repeatedly born, but ever youthful, have traversed in their revolutions alternately, from a remote period, earth and heaven; night with her dark, dawn with her luminous limbs.
verses.griffith_verse: Still born afresh, young Dames, each in her manner, unlike in hue, the Pair in alternation Round heaven and earth from ancient time have travelled, Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with limbs of splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनेमि सख्यं स्वपस्यमानः सूनुर्दाधार शवसा सुदंसाः ।आमासु चिद्दधिषे पक्वमंतः पयः कृष्णासु रुशद्रोहिणीषु ॥
verses.transliteration: sánemi ǀ sakhyám ǀ su-apasyámānaḥ ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ dādhāra ǀ śávasā ǀ su-dáṃsāḥ ǀāmā́su ǀ cit ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ pakvám ǀ antáríti ǀ páyaḥ ǀ kṛṣṇā́su ǀ rúśat ǀ róhiṇīṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship. Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour.
verses.wilson_translation: The son of strength assiduous in good works, diligent in pious acts, retains his ancient friendship (for his votary). You, (Indra), provide within the yet immature cows, whether black or red, the mature and glossy milk.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich in good actions, skilled in operation, the Son with might maintains his perfect friendship. Thou in the raw cows, black of hue or ruddy, storest the ripe milk glossy white in colour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनात्सनीळा अवनीरवाता व्रता रक्षंते अमृताः सहोभिः ।पुरू सहस्रा जनयो न पत्नीर्दुवस्यंति स्वसारो अह्रयाणं ॥
verses.transliteration: sanā́t ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ avātā́ḥ ǀ vratā́ ǀ rakṣante ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ sáhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀpurú ǀ sahásrā ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ duvasyánti ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ áhrayāṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes. For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons.
verses.wilson_translation: From a remote time the contiguous, unshifting, and unwearied fingers practise with (all) their energies many thousand acts of devotion (towards Indra); and like the wives (of the gods), the protecting sisters worship him who is without shame.
verses.griffith_verse: Their paths, of old connected, rest uninjured; they with great might preserve the immortal statutes. For many thousand holy works the Sisters wait on the haughty Lord like wives and matrons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनायुवो नमसा नव्यो अर्कैर्वसूयवो मतयो दस्म दद्रुः ।पतिं न पत्नीरुशतीरुशंतं स्पृशंति त्वा शवसावन्मनीषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sanā-yúvaḥ ǀ námasā ǀ návyaḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ vasu-yávaḥ ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ dasma ǀ dadruḥ ǀpátim ǀ ná ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ uśántam ǀ spṛśánti ǀ tvā ǀ śavasā-van ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty. As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent.
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful Indra, who are to be praised with holy hymns, the pious who are desirous of holy rites, those who are anxious for riches, and those who are wise, repair to you with veneration; powerful Indra, their minds adhere to you, as affectionate wives to a loving husbaṇḍ+
verses.griffith_verse: Thoughts ancient, seeking wealth, with adoration, with newest lauds have sped to thee, O Mighty. As yearning wives cleave to their yearning husband, so cleave our hymns to thee, O Lord most potent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनादेव तव रायो गभस्तौ न क्षीयंते नोप दस्यंति दस्म ।द्युमाँ असि क्रतुमाँ इंद्र धीरः शिक्षा शचीवस्तव नः शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: sanā́t ǀ evá ǀ táva ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ gábhastau ǀ ná ǀ kṣī́yante ǀ ná ǀ úpa ǀ dasyanti ǀ dasma ǀdyu-mā́n ǀ asi ǀ krátu-mān ǀ indra ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ śíkṣa ǀ śacī-vaḥ ǀ táva ǀ naḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted. Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending: strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power.
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful Indra, the riches that have long since been held in yourhandshave suffered neither loss nor diminution. You, Indra, are illustrious, addicted to good works, and resolute; enrich us, you who are diligent in action, by your acts.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong God, the riches which thy hands have holden from days of old have perished not nor wasted. Splendid art thou, O Indra, wise, unbending: strengthen us with might, O Lord of Power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनायते गोतम इंद्र नव्यमतक्षद्ब्रह्म हरियोजनाय ।सुनीथाय नः शवसान नोधाः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sanā-yaté ǀ gótamaḥ ǀ indra ǀ návyam ǀ átakṣat ǀ bráhma ǀ hari-yójanāya ǀsu-nīthā́ya ǀ naḥ ǀ śavasāna ǀ nodhā́ḥ ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal, Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty Indra,Nodhas, the son of Gotama, has composed for us this new hymn, (addressed) to you, who have been forever, who harness your coursers (to your car) and are the sure guide (of all). May he who has acquired wealth by propitious acts, come hither quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: O mighty Indra, Gotama's son Nodhas hath fashioned this new prayer to thee Eternal, Sure leader, yoker of the Tawny Coursers. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou terrifiedst earth and heaven;When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee. When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder,Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle. Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the Ṛbhus' Lord, heroic, victor.Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Śuṣṇa, That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vṛtra;When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in theirdistant dwelling. This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e’en in the anger of the strongest mortal.Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunder-armed! our foemen. Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict.This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat. Warring for Purukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed! breakest down the seven castles;Easily, for Sudās, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Pūru. O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water—Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever. Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses.Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं महाँ इंद्र यो ह शुष्मैर्द्यावा जज्ञानः पृथिवी अमे धाः ।यद्ध ते विश्वा गिरयश्चिदभ्वा भिया दृळ्हासः किरणा नैजन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ mahā́n ǀ indra ǀ yáḥ ǀ ha ǀ śúṣmaiḥ ǀ dyā́vā ǀ jajñānáḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ áme ǀ dhāḥ ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ te ǀ víśvā ǀ giráyaḥ ǀ cit ǀ ábhvā ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ dṛḷhā́saḥ ǀ kiráṇāḥ ǀ ná ǀ áijan ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou terrifiedst earth and heaven; When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, you are the mighty one, who, becoming manifest in (the hour of) alarm, did sustain by your energies heaven and earth; then, through fear of you, all creatures, and the mountains, and all other vast and solid things, trembled, like the (tremulous) rays of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: THOU art the Mighty One; when born, O Indra, with power thou terrifiedst earth and heaven; When, in their fear of thee, all firm-set mountains and monstrous creatures shook like dust before thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यद्धरी इंद्र विव्रता वेरा ते वज्रं जरिता बाह्वोर्धात् ।येनाविहर्यतक्रतो अमित्रान्पुर इष्णासि पुरुहूत पूर्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yát ǀ hárī íti ǀ indra ǀ ví-vratā ǀ véḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ vájram ǀ jaritā́ ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ dhāt ǀyéna ǀ aviharyatakrato ítyaviharyata-krato ǀ amítrān ǀ púraḥ ǀ iṣṇā́si ǀ puru-hūta ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder, Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Indra, you harness your variously moving horses, your praiser plural ces your thunderbolt in yourhands, wherewith, accom;oisher of undesired acts, you assail your enemies, and glorified by many, destroy their numerous cities.
verses.griffith_verse: When thy two wandering Bays thou drawest hither, thy praiser laid within thine arms the thunder, Wherewith, O Much-invoked, in will resistless, thou smitest foemen down and many a castle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं सत्य इंद्र धृष्णुरेतान्त्वमृभुक्षा नर्यस्त्वं षाट् ।त्वं शुष्णं वृजने पृक्ष आणौ यूने कुत्साय द्युमते सचाहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ satyáḥ ǀ indra ǀ dhṛṣṇúḥ ǀ etā́n ǀ tvám ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ náryaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ ṣā́ṭ ǀtvám ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ vṛjáne ǀ pṛkṣé ǀ āṇáu ǀ yū́ne ǀ kútsāya ǀ dyu-máte ǀ sácā ǀ ahan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the Ṛbhus' Lord, heroic, victor. Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Śuṣṇa,
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, the best of all beings, the assailer and humiliator (of your foes), the chief ot theṚbhus, the friend of man, the subduer of enemies, did aid the young and illustrious Kutsa, and slew Śuṣna, in the deadly and close-fought fight.
verses.griffith_verse: Faithful art thou, these thou defiest, Indra; thou art the Ṛbhus' Lord, heroic, victor. Thou, by his side, for young and glorious Kutsa, with steed and car in battle slewest Śuṣṇa,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र चोदीः सखा वृत्रं यद्वज्रिन्वृषकर्मन्नुभ्नाः ।यद्ध शूर वृषमणः पराचैर्वि दस्यूँर्योनावकृतो वृथाषाट् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ codīḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ yát ǀ vajrin ǀ vṛṣa-karman ǀ ubhnā́ḥ ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ śūra ǀ vṛṣa-manaḥ ǀ parācáiḥ ǀ ví ǀ dásyūn ǀ yónau ǀ ákṛtaḥ ǀ vṛthāṣā́ṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vṛtra; When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in their distant dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: You verily did animate him to (acquire) such (renown) as that which, sender of rain and wielder of the thunderbolt, you (dis-acquire) when you slew Vṛtra, and when, munificent hero, who easily conquer (your foes) you did put to fight the Dasyusin battle.
verses.griffith_verse: That, as a friend, thou furtheredst, O Indra, when, Thunderer, strong in act, thou crushedst Vṛtra; When, Hero, thou, great-souled, with easy conquest didst rend the Dasyus in their distant dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह त्यदिंद्रारिषण्यंदृळ्हस्य चिन्मर्तानामजुष्टौ ।व्यस्मदा काष्ठा अर्वते वर्घनेव वज्रिंछ्नथिह्यमित्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ áriṣaṇyan ǀ dṛḷhásya ǀ cit ǀ mártānām ǀ ájuṣṭau ǀví ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ kā́ṣṭhāḥ ǀ árvate ǀ vaḥ ǀ ghanā́-iva ǀ vajrin ǀ śnathihi ǀ amítrān ǁ
verses.english_translation: This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e’en in the anger of the strongest mortal. Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunder-armed! our foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, who are unwilling to harm any resolute (mortal), set open all the quarters (of the horizon) to the horses of us who praise you, (when we are exposed) to the aversion (of our enemies); and, wielder of the thunderbolt, demolish our foes, as with a club.
verses.griffith_verse: This doest thou, and art not harmed, O Indra, e’en in the anger of the strongest mortal. Lay thou the race-course open for our horses: as with a club, slay, Thunder-armed! our foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां ह त्यदिंद्रार्णसातौ स्वर्मीळ्हे नर आजा हवंते ।तव स्वधाव इयमा समर्य ऊतिर्वाजेष्वतसाय्या भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ árṇa-sātau ǀ sváḥ-mīḷhe ǀ náraḥ ǀ ājā́ ǀ havante ǀtáva ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ ā́ ǀ sa-maryé ǀ ūtíḥ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ atasā́yyā ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict. This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat.
verses.wilson_translation: Men invoke you, such as you are, in the thick-throned and wealth-bestowing conflict. May this your succour, powerful Indra, ever be granted in war, worthy to be enjoyed (by warriors) in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Hence men invoke thee, Indra, in the tumult of battle, in the light-bestowing conflict. This aid of thine, O Godlike One, was ever to be implored in deeds of might in combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र सप्त युध्यन्पुरो वज्रिन्पुरुकुत्साय दर्दः ।बर्हिर्न यत्सुदासे वृथा वर्गंहो राजन्वरिवः पूरवे कः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ saptá ǀ yúdhyan ǀ púraḥ ǀ vajrin ǀ puru-kútsāya ǀ dardaríti dardaḥ ǀbarhíḥ ǀ ná ǀ yát ǀ su-dā́se ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ várk ǀ aṃhóḥ ǀ rājan ǀ várivaḥ ǀ pūráve ǀ káḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Warring for Purukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed! breakest down the seven castles; Easily, for Sudās, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Pūru.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, warring on behalf of Purukutsa, you did overturn the seven cities; you did cut off for Sudāsawealth of Aṅhas, as if (it had been a tuft) of sacred grass, and did give it to him, O king, ever satiating you (with oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Warring for Purukutsa thou, O Indra, Thunder-armed! breakest down the seven castles; Easily, for Sudās, like grass didst rend them, and out of need, King, broughtest gain to Pūru.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्यां न इंद्र देव चित्रामिषमापो न पीपयः परिज्मन् ।यया शूर प्रत्यस्मभ्यं यंसि त्मनमूर्जं न विश्वध क्षरध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyā́m ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ deva ǀ citrā́m ǀ íṣam ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīpayaḥ ǀ pári-jman ǀyáyā ǀ śūra ǀ práti ǀ asmábhyam ǀ yáṃsi ǀ tmánam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ ná ǀ viśvádha ǀ kṣáradhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water— Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever.
verses.wilson_translation: Increase, divine Indra, for us throughout the earth, abundant food, (that it may be as plural ntiful) as water, by which, hero, you bestow upon us (existence), as you cause water to flow on every side.
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, God who movest round about us, feed us with varied food plenteous as water— Food wherewithal, O Hero, thou bestowest vigour itself to flow to us for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अकारि त इंद्र गोतमेभिर्ब्रह्माण्योक्ता नमसा हरिभ्यां ।सुपेशसं वाजमा भरा नः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ákāri ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ gótamebhiḥ ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ ā́-uktā ǀ námasā ǀ hári-bhyām ǀsu-péśasam ǀ vā́jam ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ naḥ ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses. Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: Praises have been offered to you,Indra, by the sons of Gotama; (they have been) uttered with reverence (to you), borne (hither) by your steeds; grant us various sorts of food. May he who has acquired wealthy by pious acts, come hither quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: Prayers have been made by Gotamas, O Indra, addressed to thee, with laud for thy Bay Horses. Bring us in noble shape abundant riches. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIV. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift.I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites. They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain;The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down. Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible.They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven. With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold.The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven. Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers.The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk. The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solemn rites.They lead, as ’twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the never-failing spring. Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way.Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames. Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes;Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might. Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven.Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light. Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice,Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms. They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way.Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o’erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel. The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active OnesTo the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous. Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind.Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth. O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth,Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny. Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught.A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

verses.sanskrit: वृष्णे शर्धाय सुमखाय वेधसे नोधः सुवृक्तिं प्र भरा मरुद्भ्यः ।अपो न धीरो मनसा सुहस्त्यो गिरः समंजे विदथेष्वाभुवः ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ śárdhāya ǀ sú-makhāya ǀ vedháse ǀ nódhaḥ ǀ su-vṛktím ǀ prá ǀ bhara ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀapáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ su-hástyaḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ sám ǀ añje ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ ā-bhúvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift. I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer,Nodhas, earnest praise to the company of the Maruts, the senders of rain and ripeners of fruit, deserving of adoration. Composed, and with foldedhands, I utter the praises conceived in my mind, which are efficacious in sacred rites, (and flow rreadily) as the waters.
verses.griffith_verse: BRING for the manly host, wise and majestical, O Nodhas, for the Maruts bring thou a pure gift. I deck my songs as one deft-handed, wise in mind prepares the water that hath power in solemn rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते जज्ञिरे दिव ऋष्वास उक्षणो रुद्रस्य मर्या असुरा अरेपसः ।पावकासः शुचयः सूर्या इव सत्वानो न द्रप्सिनो घोरवर्पसः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ jajñire ǀ diváḥ ǀ ṛṣvā́saḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ rudrásya ǀ máryāḥ ǀ ásurāḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǀpāvakā́saḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ sū́ryāḥ-iva ǀ sátvānaḥ ǀ ná ǀ drapsínaḥ ǀ ghorá-varpasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain; The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down.
verses.wilson_translation: They were born handsome and vigorous from the sky, the sons of Rudra, the conquerors of their foes, pure from sin, and purifying (all), radiant as suns, powerful as evil spirits, diffusers of rain-drops, and of fearful forms.
verses.griffith_verse: They spring to birth, the lofty Ones, the Bulls of Heaven, divine, the youths of Rudra, free from spot and stain; The purifiers, shining brightly even as suns, awful of form like giants, scattering rain-drops down.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवानो रुद्रा अजरा अभोग्घनो ववक्षुरध्रिगावः पर्वता इव ।दृळ्हा चिद्विश्वा भुवनानि पार्थिवा प्र च्यावयंति दिव्यानि मज्मना ॥
verses.transliteration: yúvānaḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǀ abhok-hánaḥ ǀ vavakṣúḥ ǀ ádhri-gāvaḥ ǀ párvatāḥ-iva ǀdṛḷhā́ ǀ cit ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ pā́rthivā ǀ prá ǀ cyavayanti ǀ divyā́ni ǀ majmánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible. They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Youthful Rudras, and undecaying destructive of those who do not worship (the gods), of unobstructed progress, and immoveable as mountains they are desirous of granting (the wishes of the worshipper), and by their strength agitate all substances, whether of heaven or of earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Young Rudras, demon-slayers, never growing old, they have waxed, even as mountains, irresistible. They make all beings tremble with their mighty strength, even the very strongest, both of earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चित्रैरंजिभिर्वपुषे व्यंजते वक्षःसु रुक्माँ अधि येतिरे शुभे ।अंसेष्वेषां नि मिमृक्षुर्ऋष्टयः साकं जज्ञिरे स्वधया दिवो नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: citráiḥ ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ vápuṣe ǀ ví ǀ añjate ǀ vákṣaḥ-su ǀ rukmā́n ǀ ádhi ǀ yetire ǀ śubhé ǀáṃseṣu ǀ eṣām ǀ ní ǀ mimṛkṣuḥ ǀ ṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ sākám ǀ jajñire ǀ svadháyā ǀ diváḥ ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold. The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: They decorate their person ns with various ornaments; they have plural ced, for elegance, brilliant (garlands) on their breasts; lances are borne upon their shoulders, and with them and their own strength have they been both, leaders, from the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: With glittering ornaments they deck them forth for show; for beauty on their breasts they bind their chains of gold. The lances on their shoulders pound to pieces; they were born together, of themselves, the Men of Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ईशानकृतो धुनयो रिशादसो वातान्विद्युतस्तविषीभिरक्रत ।दुहंत्यूधर्दिव्यानि धूतयो भूमिं पिन्वंति पयसा परिज्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: īśāna-kṛ́taḥ ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ vā́tān ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ akrata ǀduhánti ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ divyā́ni ǀ dhū́tayaḥ ǀ bhū́mim ǀ pinvanti ǀ páyasā ǀ pári-jrayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers. The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk.
verses.wilson_translation: Enriching their worshipper, agitating the clouds, devourers of foes, they create the winds are lightnings by their power; the cirumambient and agitating Marutsmilk heavenly udders, and sprinkle the earth with water.
verses.griffith_verse: Loud roarers, giving strength, devourers of the foe, they make the winds, they make the lightnings with their powers. The restless shakers drain the udders of the sky, and ever wandering round fill the earth full with milk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पिन्वंत्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो घृतवद्विदथेष्वाभुवः ।अत्यं न मिहे वि नयंति वाजिनमुत्सं दुहंति स्तनयंतमक्षितं ॥
verses.transliteration: pínvanti ǀ apáḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ ghṛtá-vat ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ ā-bhúvaḥ ǀátyam ǀ ná ǀ mihé ǀ ví ǀ nayanti ǀ vājínam ǀ útsam ǀ duhanti ǀ stanáyantam ǀ ákṣitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solemn rites. They lead, as ’twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the never-failing spring.
verses.wilson_translation: The munificent Marutsscatter the nutritious waters, as priests at sacrifices the clarified butter; as grooms lead forth a horse, they bring forth the rain from the fleeting-cloud, and milk it, thundering, and unexhausted.
verses.griffith_verse: The bounteous Maruts with the fatness dropping milk fill full the waters which avail in solemn rites. They lead, as ’twere, the Strong Horse forth, that it may rain: they milk the thundering, the never-failing spring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महिषासो मायिनश्चित्रभानवो गिरयो न स्वतवसो रघुष्यदः ।मृगा इव हस्तिनः खादथा वना यदारुणीषु तविषीरयुग्ध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: mahiṣā́saḥ ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ citrá-bhānavaḥ ǀ giráyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ svá-tavasaḥ ǀ raghu-syádaḥ ǀmṛgā́ḥ-iva ǀ hastínaḥ ǀ khādatha ǀ vánā ǀ yát ǀ ā́ruṇīṣu ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ áyugdhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way. Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames.
verses.wilson_translation: Vast, possessed of knowledge, bright-shining, like mountains in stability and quick in motion, you, like elephants, break down the forests when you put vigour into your ruddy (mares).
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty, with wondrous power and marvellously bright, selfstrong like mountains, ye glide swiftly on your way. Like the wild elephants ye eat the forests up when ye assume your strength among the bright red flames.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सिंहा इव नानदति प्रचेतसः पिशा इव सुपिशो विश्ववेदसः ।क्षपो जिन्वंतः पृषतीभिर्ऋष्टिभिः समित्सबाधः शवसाहिमन्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: siṃhā́ḥ-iva ǀ nānadati ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ piśā́ḥ-iva ǀ su-píśaḥ ǀ viśvá-vedasaḥ ǀkṣápaḥ ǀ jínvantaḥ ǀ pṛ́ṣatībhiḥ ǀ ṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ ít ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ áhi-manyavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes; Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might.
verses.wilson_translation: The most wise Marutsroar like lions; the all-knowing are graceful as the spotted deer, destroyign (their foes), delighting (their worshippers); of deadly strength in their anger, they come with their antelopes and their arms, (to defend the sacrificer) against interruption.
verses.griffith_verse: Exceeding wise they roar like lions mightily, they, all-possessing, are beauteous as antelopes; Stirring the darkness with lances and spotted deer, combined as priests, with serpents' fury through their might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रोदसी आ वदता गणश्रियो नृषाचः शूराः शवसाहिमन्यवः ।आ वंधुरेष्वमतिर्न दर्शता विद्युन्न तस्थौ मरुतो रथेषु वः ॥
verses.transliteration: ródasī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ vadata ǀ gaṇa-śriyaḥ ǀ nṛ́-sācaḥ ǀ śūrāḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ áhi-manyavaḥ ǀā́ ǀ vandhúreṣu ǀ amátiḥ ǀ ná ǀ darśatā́ ǀ vi-dyút ǀ ná ǀ tasthau ǀ marutaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀ vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven. Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, who are distinguished in troops, who are benevolent to men, who are heroes, and whose strength is deadly in your anger, you make heaven and earth resound (at your coming); your (glory) sits in the seat-furnished chariots, conspicuous as (a beautiful) form, or as the lovely lightning.
verses.griffith_verse: Heroes who march in companies, befriending man, with serpents' ire through strength, ye greet the earth and heaven. Upon the seats, O Maruts, of your chariots, upon the cars stands lightning visible as light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्ववेदसो रयिभिः समोकसः संमिश्लासस्तविषीभिर्विरप्शिनः ।अस्तार इषुं दधिरे गभस्त्योरनंतशुष्मा वृषखादयो नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvá-vedasaḥ ǀ rayí-bhiḥ ǀ sám-okasaḥ ǀ sám-miślāsaḥ ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ vi-rapśínaḥ ǀástāraḥ ǀ íṣum ǀ dadhire ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀ anantá-śuṣmāḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-khādayaḥ ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice, Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms.
verses.wilson_translation: The Maruts, who are all-knowing, co-dwellers with wealth, combined with strength, loud-sounding, repellers of foes, of infinite prowess, whose weapon (of offence) is Indra, and who are leaders (of men), hold in theirhandsthe shaft.
verses.griffith_verse: Lords of all riches, dwelling in the home of wealth, endowed with mighty vigour, singers loud of voice, Heroes, of powers infinite, armed with strong men's rings, the archers, they have laid the arrow on their arms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्ययेभिः पविभिः पयोवृध उज्जिघ्नंत आपथ्यो न पर्वतान् ।मखा अयासः स्वसृतो ध्रुवच्युतो दुध्रकृतो मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyáyebhiḥ ǀ paví-bhiḥ ǀ payaḥ-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ út ǀ jighnante ǀ ā-pathyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ párvatān ǀmakhā́ḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀ sva-sṛ́taḥ ǀ dhruva-cyútaḥ ǀ dudhra-kṛ́taḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way. Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o’erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel.
verses.wilson_translation: Augmenters of rain, they drive with golden wheels the clouds asunder, as elephants (in a herd break down the trees in their way); they are honoured with sacrifices, visitants of the hall of offering, spontaneous assailers (of their foes), subverters of what are stable, immoveable themselves, and wearers of shining weapons.
verses.griffith_verse: They who with golden fellies make the rain increase drive forward the big clouds like wanderers on the way. Self-moving, brisk, unwearied, they o’erthrow the firm; the Maruts with bright lances make all things to reel.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृषुं पावकं वनिनं विचर्षणिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा गृणीमसि ।रजस्तुरं तवसं मारुतं गणमृजीषिणं वृषणं सश्चत श्रिये ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛ́ṣum ǀ pāvakám ǀ vanínam ǀ ví-carṣaṇim ǀ rudrásya ǀ sūnúm ǀ havásā ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀrajaḥ-túram ǀ tavásam ǀ mā́rutam ǀ gaṇám ǀ ṛjīṣíṇam ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ saścata ǀ śriyé ǁ
verses.english_translation: The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active Ones To the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke with praise the foe-destroying, all-purifying, water-shedding, all-surveying band of Maruts, the offspring of Rudra; (priests) to obtain prosperity, have recourse to the dust-raising and powerful band of Maruts, receiving libations from sacred vessels, and showering down (benefits).
verses.griffith_verse: The progeny of Rudra we invoke with prayer, the brisk, the bright, the worshipful, the active Ones To the strong band of Maruts cleave for happiness, the chasers of the sky, impetuous, vigorous.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नू स मर्तः शवसा जनाँ अति तस्थौ व ऊती मरुतो यमावत ।अर्वद्भिर्वाजं भरते धना नृभिरापृच्छ्यं क्रतुमा क्षेति पुष्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ sáḥ ǀ mártaḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ jánān ǀ áti ǀ tastháu ǀ vaḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ā́vata ǀárvat-bhiḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ bharate ǀ dhánā ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ ā-pṛ́cchyam ǀ krátum ǀ ā́ ǀ kṣeti ǀ púṣyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind. Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth.
verses.wilson_translation: The man whom,Maruts, you defend with your protection, quickly surpasses all men in strength; with his horses he acquires food, and with his men, riches; he performs the required worship, and he prospers.
verses.griffith_verse: Maruts, the man whom ye have guarded with your help, he verily in strength surpasseth all mankind. Spoil with his steeds he gaineth, treasure with his men; he winneth honourable strength and prospereth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चर्कृत्यं मरुतः पृत्सु दुष्टरं द्युमंतं शुष्मं मघवत्सु धत्तन ।धनस्पृतमुक्थ्यं विश्वचर्षणिं तोकं पुष्येम तनयं शतं हिमाः ॥
verses.transliteration: carkṛ́tyam ǀ marutaḥ ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ dustáram ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ śúṣmam ǀ maghávat-su ǀ dhattana ǀdhana-spṛ́tam ǀ ukthyám ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇim ǀ tokám ǀ puṣyema ǀ tánayam ǀ śatám ǀ hímāḥ ǁ
