verses.english_translation: O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth, Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, grant to your wealthy (worshippers a son), eminent for good works, invincible in battle, illustrious, the annihilator (of his adversaries), the seizer of wealth, the deserver of praise, and all-discerning; may we cherish such a son and such a grandson for a hundred winterṣ
verses.griffith_verse: O Maruts, to the worshippers give glorious strength invincible in battle, brilliant, bringing wealth, Praiseworthy, known to all men. May we foster well, during a hundred winters, son and progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्ठिरं मरुतो वीरवंतमृतीषाहं रयिमस्मासु धत्त ।सहस्रिणं शतिनं शूशुवांसं प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ sthirám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vīrá-vantam ǀ ṛti-sáham ǀ rayím ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhatta ǀsahasríṇam ǀ śatínam ǀ śūśu-vā́ṃsam ǀ prātáḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ dhiyā́-vasuḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught. A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant us,Maruts, durable riches, attended by posterity, and mortifying to our enemies; (riches) recknoned by hundreds and thousands, and ever increasing; may they who have acquired wealth by pious acts, come hither quickly in the morning.
verses.griffith_verse: Will ye then, O ye Maruts, grant us riches, durable, rich in men, defying onslaught. A hundred, thousandfold, ever increasing? May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow:Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods: there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones. The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself.The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law. Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream.Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course? Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich.When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth. Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn.A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.

verses.sanskrit: पश्वा न तायुं गुहा चतंतं नमो युजानं नमो वहंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: paśvā́ ǀ ná ǀ tāyúm ǀ gúhā ǀ cátantam ǀ námaḥ ǀ yujānám ǀ námaḥ ǀ váhantam ǁ
verses.english_translation: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow: Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods: there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2] The firm and plural cid divinites followed you,Agni, by your footmarks, when hiding in the hollow (of the water), like a thief (who has stolen) an animal; you, claiming oblations, and bearing them to the gods; all the deities who are entitled to worship, sit down near to you.
verses.griffith_verse: ONE-MINDED, wise, they tracked thee like a thief lurking in dark cave with a stolen cow: Thee claiming worship, bearing it to Gods: there nigh to thee sate all the Holy Ones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सजोषा धीराः पदैरनु ग्मन्नुप त्वा सीदन्विश्वे यजत्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ padáiḥ ǀ ánu ǀ gman ǀ úpa ǀ tvā ǀ sīdan ǀ víśve ǀ yájatrāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself. The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods approached the ways of holy Law; there was a gathering vast as heaven itself. The waters feed with praise the growing Babe, born nobly in the womb, the seat of Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य देवा अनु व्रता गुर्भुवत्परिष्टिर्द्यौर्न भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vratā́ ǀ guḥ ǀ bhúvat ǀ páriṣṭiḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream. Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course?
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] The gods followed the traces of the fugitive; the search spread everywhere, and earth became like heaven; the waters swelled (to conceal him), who was much enlarged by praise, and was manifested as it were in the womb in the waters, the source of sacrificial food.
verses.griffith_verse: Like grateful food, like some wide dwelling place, like a fruit-bearing hill, a wholesome stream. Like a steed urged to run in swift career, rushing like Sindhu, who may check his course?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वर्धंतीमापः पन्वा सुशिश्विमृतस्य योना गर्भे सुजातं ॥
verses.transliteration: várdhanti ǀ īm ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ panvā́ ǀ sú-śiśvim ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónā ǀ gárbhe ǀ sú-jātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich. When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Kin as a brother to his sister floods, he eats the woods as a King eats the rich. When through the forest, urged by wind, he spreads, verily Agni shears the hair of earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुष्टिर्न रण्वा क्षितिर्न पृथ्वी गिरिर्न भुज्म क्षोदो न शंभु ॥
verses.transliteration: puṣṭíḥ ǀ ná ǀ raṇvā́ ǀ kṣitíḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛthvī́ ǀ giríḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhújma ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śam-bhú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn. A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6]Agniis grateful as nourishment, vast as the earth, productive (of vegetable food), as a mountain, delightful as water; he is like a horse urged to a charge in battle and like flowing waters; who can arrest him?
verses.griffith_verse: Like a swan sitting in the floods he pants wisest in mind mid men he wakes at morn. A Sage like Soma, sprung from Law, he grew like some young creature, mighty, shining far.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अत्यो नाज्मन्त्सर्गप्रतक्तः सिंधुर्न क्षोदः क ईं वराते ॥
verses.transliteration: átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ájman ǀ sárga-prataktaḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ īm ǀ varāte ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जामिः सिंधूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्न राजा वनान्यत्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: jāmíḥ ǀ síndhūnām ǀ bhrā́tā-iva ǀ svásrām ǀ íbhyān ǀ ná ǀ rā́jā ǀ vánāni ǀ atti ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] He is the kind kinsman of the waters, like a brother to his sister; he consumes the forest as arājā(destroys) his enemies; when excited by the wind, he traverses the woods, and shears the hairs of the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] He is the kind kinsman of the waters, like a brother to his sister; he consumes the forest as arājā(destroys) his enemies; when excited by the wind, he traverses the woods, and shears the hairs of the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vā́ta-jūtaḥ ǀ vánā ǀ ví ǀ ásthāt ǀ agníḥ ǀ ha ǀ dāti ǀ róma ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: श्वसित्यप्सु हंसो न सीदन् क्रत्वा चेतिष्ठो विशामुषर्भुत् ॥
verses.transliteration: śvásiti ǀ ap-sú ǀ haṃsáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sī́dan ǀ krátvā ǀ cétiṣṭhaḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ uṣaḥ-bhút ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10] He breathes amidst the waters like a sitting swan; awakened at the dawn, he restores by his operations consciousness to men; he is a creator, like Soma; born from the waters (where he lurked) like an animal with coiled-up limbs, he became enlarged and his light (spread) afar.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10] He breathes amidst the waters like a sitting swan; awakened at the dawn, he restores by his operations consciousness to men; he is a creator, like Soma; born from the waters (where he lurked) like an animal with coiled-up limbs, he became enlarged and his light (spread) afar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सोमो न वेधा ऋतप्रजातः पशुर्न शिश्वा विभुर्दूरेभाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ ṛtá-prajātaḥ ǀ paśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ śíśvā ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ dūré-bhāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son,Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds. He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men.Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power. With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home;Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight. He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e’en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame;Master of present and of future life, the maidens’ lover and the matrons’ Lord. To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve.He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.

verses.sanskrit: रयिर्न चित्रा सूरो न संदृगायुर्न प्राणो नित्यो न सूनुः ॥
verses.transliteration: rayíḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrā́ ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ sam-dṛ́k ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ná ǀ prāṇáḥ ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūnúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son, Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2]Agniwho is like wondrous wealth, like the all-surveying Sun, like vital breath, like a well-conducted son, like a rider-bearing steed, like a milk-yielding cow, who is pure and radiant, consumes the forests.
verses.griffith_verse: LIKE the Sun's glance, like wealth of varied sort, like breath which is the life, like one's own son, Like a swift bird, a cow who yields her milk, pure and refulgent to the wood he speeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तक्वा न भूर्णिर्वना सिषक्ति पयो न धेनुः शुचिर्विभावा ॥
verses.transliteration: tákvā ǀ ná ǀ bhū́rṇiḥ ǀ vánā ǀ sisakti ǀ páyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men. Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power.
verses.griffith_verse: He offers safety like a pleasant home, like ripened corn, the Conqueror of men. Like a Seer lauding, famed among the folk; like a steed friendly he vouchsafes us power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दाधार क्षेममोको न रण्वो यवो न पक्वो जेता जनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: dādhā́ra ǀ kṣémam ǀ ókaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raṇváḥ ǀ yávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pakváḥ ǀ jétā ǀ jánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home; Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] Like a secure mansion, he proects property; he (nourishes people) like barley; he is the conqueror of (hostile)) men; he is like a ṛṣi, the praiser (of the gods), eminent amongst (devout) person ns; as a spirited horse (goes to battle), he repairs delighted to the hall of sacrifice; may be bestow upon us food.
verses.griffith_verse: With flame insatiate, like eternal might; caring for each one like a dame at home; Bright when he shines forth, whitish mid the folk, like a car, gold-decked, thundering to the fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋषिर्न स्तुभ्वा विक्षु प्रशस्तो वाजी न प्रीतो वयो दधाति ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ ná ǀ stúbhvā ǀ vikṣú ǀ pra-śastáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ ná ǀ prītáḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e’en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame; Master of present and of future life, the maidens’ lover and the matrons’ Lord.
verses.griffith_verse: He strikes with terror like a dart shot forth, e’en like an archer's arrow tipped with flame; Master of present and of future life, the maidens’ lover and the matrons’ Lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दुरोकशोचिः क्रतुर्न नित्यो जायेव योनावरं विश्वस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: duróka-śociḥ ǀ krátuḥ ǀ ná ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ jāyā́-iva ǀ yónau ǀ áram ǀ víśvasmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve. He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6]Agniof unattainable brightness, is like a vigilant sacrificer; he is an ornament to all (in the sacrificial chamber), like a woman in a dwelling; when he shines with wonderful lustre, he is like the white (sun) or like a golden chariot amongst men, resplendent in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: To him lead all your ways: may we attain the kindled God as cows their home at eve. He drives the flames below as floods their swell: the rays rise up to the fair place of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चित्रो यदभ्राट् छ्वेतो न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: citráḥ ǀ yát ǀ ábhrāṭ ǀ śvetáḥ ǀ ná ǀ vikṣú ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rukmī́ ǀ tveṣáḥ ǀ samát-su ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सेनेव सृष्टामं दधात्यस्तुर्न दिद्युत्त्वेषप्रतीका ॥
verses.transliteration: sénā-iva ǀ sṛṣṭā́ ǀ ámam ǀ dadhāti ǀ ástuḥ ǀ ná ǀ didyút ǀ tveṣá-pratīkā ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] He terrifies (his adversaries) like an army sent (against an enemy), or like the bright-pointed shaft of an archer.Agni, as Yama, is all that is born; as Yama, all that will be born; he is the lover of maidens, the husband of wives.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] He terrifies (his adversaries) like an army sent (against an enemy), or like the bright-pointed shaft of an archer.Agni, as Yama, is all that is born; as Yama, all that will be born; he is the lover of maidens, the husband of wives.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यमो ह जातो यमो जनित्वं जारः कनीनां पतिर्जनीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: yamáḥ ǀ ha ǀ jātáḥ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ jáni-tvam ǀ jāráḥ ǀ kanī́nām ǀ pátiḥ ǀ jánīnām ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं वश्चराथा वयं वसत्यास्तं न गावो नक्षंत इद्धं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vaḥ ǀ carā́thā ǀ vayám ǀ vasatyā́ ǀ ástam ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ nákṣante ǀ iddhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10] Let us approach that blazing Agniwith animal and vegetable offerings, as cows hasten to their stalls. He has tossed about his flames (in every direction), like running streams of water; the rays comingle (with the radiance) visible in the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10] Let us approach that blazing Agniwith animal and vegetable offerings, as cows hasten to their stalls. He has tossed about his flames (in every direction), like running streams of water; the rays comingle (with the radiance) visible in the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सिंधुर्न क्षोदः प्र नीचीरैनोन्नवंत गावः स्वर्दृशीके ॥
verses.transliteration: síndhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ prá ǀ nī́cīḥ ǀ ainot ǀ návanta ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛ́śīke ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King.Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought. He, bearing in his hand all manly might, crouched in the cavern, struck the Gods with fear.Men filled with understanding find him there, when they have sting prayers formed within their heart. He, like the Unborn, holds the broad earth up; and with effective utterance fixed the sky.O Agni, guard the spots which cattle love: thou, life of all, hast gone from lair to lair. Whoso hath known him dwelling in his lair, and hath approached the stream of holy Law,—They who release him, paying sacred rites,—truly to such doth he announce great wealth. He who grows mightily in herbs, within each fruitful mother and each babe she bears,Wise, life of all men, in the waters’ home,—for him have sages built as ’twere a seat.

verses.sanskrit: वनेषु जायुर्मर्तेषु मित्रो वृणीते श्रुष्टिं राजेवाजुर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: váneṣu ǀ jāyúḥ ǀ márteṣu ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vṛṇīté ǀ śruṣṭím ǀ rā́jā-iva ǀ ajuryám ǁ
verses.english_translation: VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King. Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2] Born in the woods, the friend of man,Agniprotects his worshipper, as arājāfavours an able man; kind as a defender, prosperous as a performer of (good) works, may he, the invoker of the gods, the bearer of oblations, be propitious.
verses.griffith_verse: VICTORIOUS in the wood, Friend among men, ever he claims obedience as a King. Gracious like peace, blessing like mental power, Priest was he, offering-bearer, full of thought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्षेमो न साधुः क्रतुर्न भद्रो भुवत्स्वाधीर्होता हव्यवाट् ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣémaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sādhúḥ ǀ krátuḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhadráḥ ǀ bhúvat ǀ su-ādhī́ḥ ǀ hótā ǀ havya-vā́ṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, bearing in his hand all manly might, crouched in the cavern, struck the Gods with fear. Men filled with understanding find him there, when they have sting prayers formed within their heart.
verses.griffith_verse: He, bearing in his hand all manly might, crouched in the cavern, struck the Gods with fear. Men filled with understanding find him there, when they have sting prayers formed within their heart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हस्ते दधानो नृम्णा विश्वान्यमे देवांधाद्गुहा निषीदन् ॥
verses.transliteration: háste ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ nṛmṇā́ ǀ víśvāni ǀ áme ǀ devā́n ǀ dhāt ǀ gúhā ǀ ni-sī́dan ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, like the Unborn, holds the broad earth up; and with effective utterance fixed the sky. O Agni, guard the spots which cattle love: thou, life of all, hast gone from lair to lair.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] Holding in hishandall (sacrificial) wealth, and hiding in the hollows (of the waters), he filled the gods with alarm; the leaders, (the gods), the upholders of acts, then recognize Agniwhen they have recited the prayers conceived in the heart.
verses.griffith_verse: He, like the Unborn, holds the broad earth up; and with effective utterance fixed the sky. O Agni, guard the spots which cattle love: thou, life of all, hast gone from lair to lair.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विदंतीमत्र नरो धियंधा हृदा यत्तष्टान्मंत्राँ अशंसन् ॥
verses.transliteration: vidánti ǀ īm ǀ átra ǀ náraḥ ǀ dhiyam-dhā́ḥ ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ yát ǀ taṣṭā́n ǀ mántrān ǀ áśaṃsan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whoso hath known him dwelling in his lair, and hath approached the stream of holy Law,— They who release him, paying sacred rites,—truly to such doth he announce great wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Whoso hath known him dwelling in his lair, and hath approached the stream of holy Law,— They who release him, paying sacred rites,—truly to such doth he announce great wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजो न क्षां दाधार पृथिवीं तस्तंभ द्यां मंत्रेभिः सत्यैः ॥
verses.transliteration: ajáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣā́m ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ tastámbha ǀ dyā́m ǀ mántrebhiḥ ǀ satyáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who grows mightily in herbs, within each fruitful mother and each babe she bears, Wise, life of all men, in the waters’ home,—for him have sages built as ’twere a seat.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6] Like the unborn (sun) he sustains the earth and the firmament, and props up the heaven with true prayers;Agni, in whom is all sustenance, cherish the plural ces that are grateful to animals; repair (to the spots) where there is no pasturage.
verses.griffith_verse: He who grows mightily in herbs, within each fruitful mother and each babe she bears, Wise, life of all men, in the waters’ home,—for him have sages built as ’twere a seat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रिया पदानि पश्वो नि पाहि विश्वायुरग्ने गुहा गुहं गाः ॥
verses.transliteration: priyā́ ǀ padā́ni ǀ paśváḥ ǀ ní ǀ pāhi ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ agne ǀ guhā́ ǀ gúham ǀ gāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य ईं चिकेत गुहा भवंतमा यः ससाद धारामृतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ cikéta ǀ gúhā ǀ bhávantam ǀ ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ sasā́da ǀ dhā́rām ǀ ṛtásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] He who knows Agnihidden in the hollows; he who approaches him as the maintainer of truth; those who, performing worship, repeat his praises, to them assuredly he promises affluence.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] He who knows Agnihidden in the hollows; he who approaches him as the maintainer of truth; those who, performing worship, repeat his praises, to them assuredly he promises affluence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि ये चृतंत्यृता सपंत आदिद्वसूनि प्र ववाचास्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yé ǀ cṛtánti ǀ ṛtā́ ǀ sápantaḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ vásūni ǀ prá ǀ vavāca ǀ asmai ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि यो वीरुत्सु रोधन्महित्वोत प्रजा उत प्रसूष्वंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yáḥ ǀ vīrút-su ǀ ro��dhat ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ utá ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ pra-sū́ṣu ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10] The wise, (first) honouring Agni, as they do a dwelling, worship him who implants their (peculiar) virtues in herbs, as progeny in their parents, and who, the source of knowledge and of all sustenance, (abides) in the domicile of the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10] The wise, (first) honouring Agni, as they do a dwelling, worship him who implants their (peculiar) virtues in herbs, as progeny in their parents, and who, the source of knowledge and of all sustenance, (abides) in the domicile of the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चित्तिरपां दमे विश्वायुः सद्मेव धीराः संमाय चक्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: cíttiḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ dáme ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ sádma-iva ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ sam-mā́ya ǀ cakruḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COMMINGLING, restless, he ascends the sky, unveiling nights and all that stands or moves,As he the sole God is preeminent in greatness among all these other Gods. All men are joyful in thy power, O God, that living from the dry wood thou art born.All truly share thy Godhead while they keep, in their accustomed ways, eternal Law. Strong is the thought of Law, the Law's behest; all works have they performed; he quickens all.Whoso will bring oblation, gifts to thee, to him, bethinking thee, vouchsafe thou wealth. Seated as Priest with Manu's progeny, of all these treasures he alone is Lord.Men yearn for children to prolong their line, and are not disappointed in their hope. Eagerly they who hear his word fulfil his wish as sons obey their sire's behest.He, rich in food, unbars his wealth like doors: he, the House-Friend, hath decked heaven's vault with stars.

verses.sanskrit: श्रीणन्नुप स्थाद्दिवं भुरण्युः स्थातुश्चरथमक्तून्व्यूर्णोत् ॥
verses.transliteration: śrīṇán ǀ úpa ǀ sthāt ǀ dívam ǀ bhuraṇyúḥ ǀ sthātúḥ ǀ carátham ǀ aktū́n ǀ ví ǀ ūrṇot ǁ
verses.english_translation: COMMINGLING, restless, he ascends the sky, unveiling nights and all that stands or moves, As he the sole God is preeminent in greatness among all these other Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2] The bearer (of the oblations),Agni, mixing them (with other ingredients), ascends to heaven, and clothes all things, moveable and immoveable, and the nights themselves, (with light), radiant amongst the gods, and in himself alone comprehending the virtues of all these (substances).
verses.griffith_verse: COMMINGLING, restless, he ascends the sky, unveiling nights and all that stands or moves, As he the sole God is preeminent in greatness among all these other Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परि यदेषामेको विश्वेषां भुवद्देवो देवानां महित्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ ékaḥ ǀ víśveṣām ǀ bhúvat ǀ deváḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All men are joyful in thy power, O God, that living from the dry wood thou art born. All truly share thy Godhead while they keep, in their accustomed ways, eternal Law.
verses.griffith_verse: All men are joyful in thy power, O God, that living from the dry wood thou art born. All truly share thy Godhead while they keep, in their accustomed ways, eternal Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्ते विश्वे क्रतुं जुषंत शुष्काद्यद्देव जीवो जनिष्ठाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ te ǀ víśve ǀ krátum ǀ juṣanta ǀ śúṣkāt ǀ yát ǀ deva ǀ jīváḥ ǀ jániṣṭhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong is the thought of Law, the Law's behest; all works have they performed; he quickens all. Whoso will bring oblation, gifts to thee, to him, bethinking thee, vouchsafe thou wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] When, divine Agni, you are born living from the dry wood, (by attrition), then all (your worshippers) perform the sacred ceremony, and obtain verily true divinity by praising you, who are immortal, with hymns that reach you.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong is the thought of Law, the Law's behest; all works have they performed; he quickens all. Whoso will bring oblation, gifts to thee, to him, bethinking thee, vouchsafe thou wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भजंत विश्वे देवत्वं नाम ऋतं सपंतो अमृतमेवैः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhájanta ǀ víśve ǀ deva-tvám ǀ nā́ma ǀ ṛtám ǀ sápantaḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ évaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seated as Priest with Manu's progeny, of all these treasures he alone is Lord. Men yearn for children to prolong their line, and are not disappointed in their hope.
verses.griffith_verse: Seated as Priest with Manu's progeny, of all these treasures he alone is Lord. Men yearn for children to prolong their line, and are not disappointed in their hope.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य प्रेषा ऋतस्य धीतिर्विश्वायुर्विश्वे अपांसि चक्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ préṣāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ cakruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eagerly they who hear his word fulfil his wish as sons obey their sire's behest. He, rich in food, unbars his wealth like doors: he, the House-Friend, hath decked heaven's vault with stars.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6] Praises are addressed to him who has repaired (to the solemnity); oblations (are offered) to him who has gone (to the sacrifice); in him is all sustenance, (and to him) have all (devout person ns) performed (the customary) rites. Do you,Agni, knowing (the thoughts of the worshipper), grant riches to him who presents to you oblations, or who wishes (to be able to present them).
verses.griffith_verse: Eagerly they who hear his word fulfil his wish as sons obey their sire's behest. He, rich in food, unbars his wealth like doors: he, the House-Friend, hath decked heaven's vault with stars.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्तुभ्यं दाशाद्यो वा ते शिक्षात्तस्मै चिकित्वान्रयिं दयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ dā́śāt ǀ yáḥ ǀ vā ǀ te ǀ śíkṣāt ǀ tásmai ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ rayím ǀ dayasva ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: होता निषत्तो मनोरपत्ये स चिन्न्वासां पती रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: hótā ǀ ní-sattaḥ ǀ mánoḥ ǀ ápatye ǀ sáḥ ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ āsām ǀ pátiḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] You have abided with the descendants of Manuas the invoker (of the gods); you are indeed the lord of their possessions; they have desired (of you) procreative vigour in their bodies, and, associated with their own excellent offspring, they contemplate (all things) undisturbed.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] You have abided with the descendants of Manuas the invoker (of the gods); you are indeed the lord of their possessions; they have desired (of you) procreative vigour in their bodies, and, associated with their own excellent offspring, they contemplate (all things) undisturbed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इच्छंत रेतो मिथस्तनूषु सं जानत स्वैर्दक्षैरमूराः ॥
verses.transliteration: icchánta ǀ rétaḥ ǀ mitháḥ ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ sám ǀ jānata ǀ sváiḥ ǀ dákṣaiḥ ǀ ámūrāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पितुर्न पुत्राः क्रतुं जुषंत श्रोषन्ये अस्य शासं तुरासः ॥
verses.transliteration: pitúḥ ǀ ná ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ krátum ǀ juṣanta ǀ śróṣan ǀ yé ǀ asya ǀ śā́sam ǀ turā́saḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10] Hastening to obey the commands of Agni, like sons (obedient of the orders) of a father, they celebrate his worship; abounding in food, Agni sets open before them treasures that are the doorf of sacrifice; and he who delights in the sacrificial chamber has studded the sky with constellations.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10] Hastening to obey the commands of Agni, like sons (obedient of the orders) of a father, they celebrate his worship; abounding in food, Agni sets open before them treasures that are the doorf of sacrifice; and he who delights in the sacrificial chamber has studded the sky with constellations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि राय और्णोद्दुरः पुरुक्षुः पिपेश नाकं स्तृभिर्दमूनाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ aurṇot ǀ dúraḥ ǀ puru-kṣúḥ ǀ pipéśa ǀ nā́kam ǀ stṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BRIGHT, splendid, like Dawn's lover, he hath filled the two joined worlds as with the light of heaven.When born, with might thou hast encompassed them: Father of Gods, and yet their Son wast thou. Agni, the Sage, the humble, who discerns like the cow's udder, the sweet taste of food,Like a bliss-giver to be drawn to men, sits gracious in the middle of the house. Born in the dwelling like a lovely son, pleased, like a strong steed, he bears on the folk.What time the men and I, with heroes, call, may Agni then gain all through Godlike power. None breaks these holy laws of thine when thou hast granted audience to these chieftains here.This is thy boast, thou smotest with thy peers, and joined with heroes dravest off disgrace. Like the Dawn's lover, spreading light, well-known as hued like morn, may he remember me.They, bearing of themselves, unbar the doors: they all ascend to the fair place of heaven.

verses.sanskrit: शुक्रः शुशुक्वाँ उषो न जारः पप्रा समीची दिवो न ज्योतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: śukráḥ ǀ śuśukvā́n ǀ uṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ jāráḥ ǀ paprā́ ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyótiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BRIGHT, splendid, like Dawn's lover, he hath filled the two joined worlds as with the light of heaven. When born, with might thou hast encompassed them: Father of Gods, and yet their Son wast thou.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2] White-shining (Agni), like the (sun), the extinguisher of the dawn, is the illuminator (of all) and fills united (heaven and earth with light), like the lustre of the radiant (sun). You, as soon as manifested, have pervaded all the world with devout acts, being (both) the father and son of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: BRIGHT, splendid, like Dawn's lover, he hath filled the two joined worlds as with the light of heaven. When born, with might thou hast encompassed them: Father of Gods, and yet their Son wast thou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परि प्रजातः क्रत्वा बभूथ भुवो देवानां पिता पुत्रः सन् ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ prá-jātaḥ ǀ krátvā ǀ babhūtha ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ pitā́ ǀ putráḥ ǀ sán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the Sage, the humble, who discerns like the cow's udder, the sweet taste of food, Like a bliss-giver to be drawn to men, sits gracious in the middle of the house.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, the Sage, the humble, who discerns like the cow's udder, the sweet taste of food, Like a bliss-giver to be drawn to men, sits gracious in the middle of the house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वेधा अदृप्तो अग्निर्विजानन्नूधर्न गोनां स्वाद्मा पितूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: vedhā́ḥ ǀ ádṛptaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ vi-jānán ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ gónām ǀ svā́dma ǀ pitūnā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Born in the dwelling like a lovely son, pleased, like a strong steed, he bears on the folk. What time the men and I, with heroes, call, may Agni then gain all through Godlike power.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] The wise, the humble, and discrimating Agni, is the giver of flavour to food, as the udder of cows (gives sweetness to the milk); invited (to the ceremony), he sits in the sacrificial chamber, diffusing happiness like a benevolent man, amongst mankind.
verses.griffith_verse: Born in the dwelling like a lovely son, pleased, like a strong steed, he bears on the folk. What time the men and I, with heroes, call, may Agni then gain all through Godlike power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जने न शेव आहूर्यः सन्मध्ये निषत्तो रण्वो दुरोणे ॥
verses.transliteration: jáne ǀ ná ǀ śéva ǀ ā-hū́ryaḥ ǀ sán ǀ mádhye ǀ ní-sattaḥ ǀ raṇváḥ ǀ duroṇé ǁ
verses.english_translation: None breaks these holy laws of thine when thou hast granted audience to these chieftains here. This is thy boast, thou smotest with thy peers, and joined with heroes dravest off disgrace.
verses.griffith_verse: None breaks these holy laws of thine when thou hast granted audience to these chieftains here. This is thy boast, thou smotest with thy peers, and joined with heroes dravest off disgrace.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रो न जातो रण्वो दुरोणे वाजी न प्रीतो विशो वि तारीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: putráḥ ǀ ná ǀ jātáḥ ǀ raṇváḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ vājī́ ǀ ná ǀ prītáḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tārīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like the Dawn's lover, spreading light, well-known as hued like morn, may he remember me. They, bearing of themselves, unbar the doors: they all ascend to the fair place of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6] He diffuses happiness in a dwelling like a son(newly) born; he overcomes (opposing) men like an animated charger; whatever (divine) beings I may along with other men invoke (to the ceremony), you,Agni, assume all (their) celestial nature.
verses.griffith_verse: Like the Dawn's lover, spreading light, well-known as hued like morn, may he remember me. They, bearing of themselves, unbar the doors: they all ascend to the fair place of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विशो यदह्वे नृभिः सनीळा अग्निर्देवत्वा विश्वान्यश्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśaḥ ǀ yát ǀ áhve ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ deva-tvā́ ǀ víśvāni ǀ aśyāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नकिष्ट एता व्रता मिनंति नृभ्यो यदेभ्यः श्रुष्टिं चकर्थ ॥
verses.transliteration: nákiḥ ǀ te ǀ etā́ ǀ vratā́ ǀ minanti ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ebhyáḥ ǀ śruṣṭím ǀ cakártha ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] Never may (malignant spirits) interrupt those rites in which you have given the (hope of) reward to the person ns (who celebrate them) for should (such spirits) disturb your worship, then, assisted by followers like yourself, you put the intruders to flight.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] Never may (malignant spirits) interrupt those rites in which you have given the (hope of) reward to the person ns (who celebrate them) for should (such spirits) disturb your worship, then, assisted by followers like yourself, you put the intruders to flight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तत्तु ते दंसो यदहन्त्समानैर्नृभिर्यद्युक्तो विवे रपांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ tú ǀ te ǀ dáṃsaḥ ǀ yát ǀ áhan ǀ samānáiḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ yát ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ vivéḥ ǀ rápāṃsi ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उषो न जारो विभावोस्रः संज्ञातरूपश्चिकेतदस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ jāráḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ usráḥ ǀ sáṃjñāta-rūpaḥ ǀ cíketat ǀ asmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10] May Agni, who is possessed of manifold light, like the extinguisher of the dawn, the granter of dwellings, and of cognizable form, consider (the desires of) this, (his worshipper); (his rays), spontaneously bearing the oblation, open the doors (of the sacrificial chamber), and all spread through the visible heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10] May Agni, who is possessed of manifold light, like the extinguisher of the dawn, the granter of dwellings, and of cognizable form, consider (the desires of) this, (his worshipper); (his rays), spontaneously bearing the oblation, open the doors (of the sacrificial chamber), and all spread through the visible heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्मना वहंतो दुरो व्यृण्वन्नवंत विश्वे स्वर्दृशीके ॥
verses.transliteration: tmánā ǀ váhantaḥ ǀ dúraḥ ǀ ví ǀ ṛṇvan ǀ návanta ǀ víśve ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛ́śīke ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY we, the pious, win much food by prayer, may Agni with fair light pervade each act,—He the observer of the heavenly laws of Gods, and of the race of mortal man. He who is germ of waters, germ of woods, germ of all things that move not and that move,—To him even in the rock and in the house: Immortal One, he cares for all mankind. Agni is Lord of riches for the man who serves him readily with sacred songs.Protect these beings thou with careful thought, knowing the races both of Gods and men. Whom many dawns and nights, unlike, make strong, whom, born in Law, all things that move and stand,—He hath been won, Herald who sits in light, making effectual all our holy works. Thou settest value on our cows and woods: all shall bring tribute to us to the light.Men have served thee in many and sundry spots, parting, as ’twere, an aged father's wealth. Like a brave archer, like one skilled and bold, a fierce avenger, so he shines in fight.

verses.sanskrit: वनेम पूर्वीरर्यो मनीषा अग्निः सुशोको विश्वान्यश्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: vanéma ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ su-śókaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ aśyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY we, the pious, win much food by prayer, may Agni with fair light pervade each act,— He the observer of the heavenly laws of Gods, and of the race of mortal man.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2] We solicit abundant (food)Agni, who is to be approached by meditation, and shines with pure light, pervades all holy rites, knowing well the acts that are to be addressed to the deities, and (those) which regulate) the birth of the human race.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY we, the pious, win much food by prayer, may Agni with fair light pervade each act,— He the observer of the heavenly laws of Gods, and of the race of mortal man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ दैव्यानि व्रता चिकित्वाना मानुषस्य जनस्य जन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dáivyāni ǀ vratā́ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ mā́nuṣasya ǀ jánasya ǀ jánma ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is germ of waters, germ of woods, germ of all things that move not and that move,— To him even in the rock and in the house: Immortal One, he cares for all mankind.
verses.griffith_verse: He who is germ of waters, germ of woods, germ of all things that move not and that move,— To him even in the rock and in the house: Immortal One, he cares for all mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गर्भो यो अपां गर्भो वनानां गर्भश्च स्थातां गर्भश्चरथां ॥
verses.transliteration: gárbhaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ vánānām ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ ca ǀ sthātā́m ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ caráthām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni is Lord of riches for the man who serves him readily with sacred songs. Protect these beings thou with careful thought, knowing the races both of Gods and men.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] (They offer oblations) on the mountain, or in the mansion, to that Agni, who is within the waters within woods, and  within all moveable and immoveable things, immortal and performing pious acts, like a benevolent (prince) among his people.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni is Lord of riches for the man who serves him readily with sacred songs. Protect these beings thou with careful thought, knowing the races both of Gods and men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्रौ चिदस्मा अंतर्दुरोणे विशां न विश्वो अमृतः स्वाधीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádrau ǀ cit ǀ asmai ǀ antáḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ viśā́m ǀ ná ǀ víśvaḥ ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ su-ādhī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom many dawns and nights, unlike, make strong, whom, born in Law, all things that move and stand,— He hath been won, Herald who sits in light, making effectual all our holy works.
verses.griffith_verse: Whom many dawns and nights, unlike, make strong, whom, born in Law, all things that move and stand,— He hath been won, Herald who sits in light, making effectual all our holy works.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि क्षपावाँ अग्नी रयीणां दाशद्यो अस्मा अरं सूक्तैः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ kṣapā́-vān ǀ agníḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ dā́śat ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ áram ǀ su-uktáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou settest value on our cows and woods: all shall bring tribute to us to the light. Men have served thee in many and sundry spots, parting, as ’twere, an aged father's wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: [5-6]Agni, the lord of night, grants riches to the worshipper who adores him with sacred hymns. Agni, who are omniscient, and  know the origin of gods and men, protect all these (beings dwelling) upon earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou settest value on our cows and woods: all shall bring tribute to us to the light. Men have served thee in many and sundry spots, parting, as ’twere, an aged father's wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एता चिकित्वो भूमा नि पाहि देवानां जन्म मर्तांश्च विद्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ ǀ cikitvaḥ ǀ bhū́ma ǀ ní ǀ pāhi ǀ devā́nām ǀ jánma ǀ mártān ǀ ca ǀ vidvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a brave archer, like one skilled and bold, a fierce avenger, so he shines in fight.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a brave archer, like one skilled and bold, a fierce avenger, so he shines in fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वर्धान्यं पूर्वीः क्षपो विरूपाः स्थातुश्च रथमृतप्रवीतं ॥
verses.transliteration: várdhān ǀ yám ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ kṣapáḥ ǀ ví-rūpāḥ ǀ sthātúḥ ǀ ca ǀ rátham ǀ ṛtá-pravītam ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8]Agni, whom many variously-tinted (mornings) and nights increase, whom, invested with truth, all moveable and immoveable things augment, has been propitiated, and is kindly seated at the holy rite, as the invoker (of the gods), and rendering all (pious) acts (productive) of reward.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8]Agni, whom many variously-tinted (mornings) and nights increase, whom, invested with truth, all moveable and immoveable things augment, has been propitiated, and is kindly seated at the holy rite, as the invoker (of the gods), and rendering all (pious) acts (productive) of reward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अराधि होता स्वर्निषत्तः कृण्वन्विश्वान्यपांसि सत्या ॥
verses.transliteration: árādhi ǀ hótā ǀ sváḥ ǀ ní-sattaḥ ǀ kṛṇván ǀ víśvāni ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ satyā́ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गोषु प्रशस्तिं वनेषु धिषे भरंत विश्वे बलिं स्वर्णः ॥
verses.transliteration: góṣu ǀ prá-śastim ǀ váneṣu ǀ dhiṣe ǀ bháranta ǀ víśve ǀ balím ǀ sváḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [9-10]Agni, confer excellence upon our valued cattle, and may all men bring us acceptable tribute; offering in many laces sacrifices to you, men receive riches from you, as (sons) from an aged father.
verses.wilson_translation: [9-10]Agni, confer excellence upon our valued cattle, and may all men bring us acceptable tribute; offering in many laces sacrifices to you, men receive riches from you, as (sons) from an aged father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि त्वा नरः पुरुत्रा सपर्यन्पितुर्न जिव्रेर्वि वेदो भरंत ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ tvā ǀ náraḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ saparyan ǀ pitúḥ ǀ ná ǀ jívreḥ ǀ ví ǀ védaḥ ǀ bharanta ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: साधुर्न गृध्नुरस्तेव शूरो यातेव भीमस्त्वेषः समत्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: sādhúḥ ǀ ná ǀ gṛdhnúḥ ǀ ástā-iva ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ yā́tā-iva ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ tveṣáḥ ǀ samát-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: (May Agni), who is like one who succeeds (in his undertakings), and acquires (what he wishes for), who is like a warrior casting a dart, and resembles a fearful adversary, who is brilliant in combats, (be to us a friend).
verses.wilson_translation: (May Agni), who is like one who succeeds (in his undertakings), and acquires (what he wishes for), who is like a warrior casting a dart, and resembles a fearful adversary, who is brilliant in combats, (be to us a friend).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LOVING the loving One, as wives their husband, the sisters of one home have urged him forward,Bright-coloured, even, as the cows love morning, dark, breaking forth to view, and redly beaming. Our sires with lauds burst e’en the firm-set fortress, yea, the Aṅgirases, with roar, the mountain.They made for us a way to reach high heaven, they found us day, light, day's sign, beams of morning. They stablished order, made his service fruitful; then parting them among the longing faithful,Not thirsting after aught, they come, most active, while with sweet food the race of Gods they strengthen. Since Mātariśvan, far-diffused, hath stirred him, and he in every house grown bright and noble,He, Bhṛgu-like I hath gone as his companion, as on commission to a greater Sovran. When man poured juice to Heaven, the mighty Father, he knew and freed himself from close embracement.The archer boldly shot at him his arrow, and the God threw his splendour on his Daughter. Whoso, hath flames for thee within his dwelling, or brings the worship which thou lovest daily,Do thou of double might increase his substance: may he whom thou incitest meet with riches. All sacrificial viands wait on Agni as the Seven mighty Rivers seek the ocean.Not by our brethren was our food discovered: find with the Gods care for us, thou who knowest. When light hath filled the Lord of men for increase, straight from the heaven descends the limpid moisture.Agni hath brought to light and filled with spirit the youthful host blameless and well providing. He who like thought goes swiftly on his journey, the Sun, alone is ever Lord of riches.The Kings with fair hands, Varuṇa and Mitra, protect the precious nectar in our cattle. O Agni, break not our ancestral friendship, Sage as thou art, endowed with deepest knowledge.Old age, like gathering cloud, impairs the body: before that evil be come nigh protect me.

verses.sanskrit: उप प्र जिन्वन्नुशतीरुशंतं पतिं न नित्यं जनयः सनीळाः ।स्वसारः श्यावीमरुषीमजुष्रंचित्रमुच्छंतीमुषसं न गावः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ prá ǀ jinvan ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ uśántam ǀ pátim ǀ ná ǀ nítyam ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀsvásāraḥ ǀ śyā́vīm ǀ áruṣīm ǀ ajuṣran ǀ citrám ǀ ucchántīm ǀ uṣásam ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LOVING the loving One, as wives their husband, the sisters of one home have urged him forward, Bright-coloured, even, as the cows love morning, dark, breaking forth to view, and redly beaming.
verses.wilson_translation: The contiguous fingers, loving the affectionate Agni, as wives love their own husbands, plural ase him (with offered oblations), and honour him, who is entitled to honour, (with gesticulations), as the rays of light (are assiduous in the service) of the dawn, which is (at first) dark, (then) glimmering, and (finally) radiant.
verses.griffith_verse: LOVING the loving One, as wives their husband, the sisters of one home have urged him forward, Bright-coloured, even, as the cows love morning, dark, breaking forth to view, and redly beaming.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वीळु चिद्दृळ्हा पितरो न उक्थैरद्रिं रुजन्नंगिरसो रवेण ।चक्रुर्दिवो बृहतो गातुमस्मे अहः स्वर्विविदुः केतुमुस्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: vīḷú ǀ cit ǀ dṛḷhā́ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ ádrim ǀ rujan ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ráveṇa ǀcakrúḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ asmé íti ǀ áharíti ǀ sváḥ ǀ vividuḥ ǀ ketúm ǀ usrā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our sires with lauds burst e’en the firm-set fortress, yea, the Aṅgirases, with roar, the mountain. They made for us a way to reach high heaven, they found us day, light, day's sign, beams of morning.
verses.wilson_translation: Our forefathers, the Aṅgirasas, by their praises (of Agni), terrified the strong and daring devourer, (Paṇi), by the sound; they made for us a path to the vast heaven, and obtained accessible day, the ensign of day, (Āditya) and the cows (that had been stolen).
verses.griffith_verse: Our sires with lauds burst e’en the firm-set fortress, yea, the Aṅgirases, with roar, the mountain. They made for us a way to reach high heaven, they found us day, light, day's sign, beams of morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दधन्नृतं धनयन्नस्य धीतिमादिदर्यो दिधिष्वो विभृत्राः ।अतृष्यंतीरपसो यंत्यच्छा देवांजन्म प्रयसा वर्धयंतीः ॥
verses.transliteration: dádhan ǀ ṛtám ǀ dhanáyan ǀ asya ǀ dhītím ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ aryáḥ ǀ didhiṣváḥ ǀ ví-bhṛtrāḥ ǀátṛṣyantīḥ ǀ apásaḥ ǀ yanti ǀ áccha ǀ devā́n ǀ jánma ǀ práyasā ǀ vardháyantīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They stablished order, made his service fruitful; then parting them among the longing faithful, Not thirsting after aught, they come, most active, while with sweet food the race of Gods they strengthen.
verses.wilson_translation: They secured hi, (Agni, in the sacrificial chamber), they made his worship the source of wealth; whence opulent votaries preserve his fires and practise his rites. Free from all (other) desire, assiduous in his adoration, and sustaining gods and men by their offerings, they come into his presence.
verses.griffith_verse: They stablished order, made his service fruitful; then parting them among the longing faithful, Not thirsting after aught, they come, most active, while with sweet food the race of Gods they strengthen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मथीद्यदीं विभृतो मातरिश्वा गृहेगृहे श्येतो जेन्यो भूत् ।आदीं राज्ञे न सहीयसे सचा सन्ना दूत्यं भृगवाणो विवाय ॥
verses.transliteration: máthīt ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ ví-bhṛtaḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ gṛhé-gṛhe ǀ śyetáḥ ǀ jényaḥ ǀ bhū́t ǀā́t ǀ īm ǀ rā́jñe ǀ ná ǀ sáhīyase ǀ sácā ǀ sán ǀ ā́ ǀ dūtyám ǀ bhṛ́gavāṇaḥ ǀ vivāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Since Mātariśvan, far-diffused, hath stirred him, and he in every house grown bright and noble, He, Bhṛgu-like I hath gone as his companion, as on commission to a greater Sovran.
verses.wilson_translation: When the diffusive vital air excites Agni, he becomes bright and manifest in every mansion, and the instrumental tutor of the rite, imitating Bhṛgu, prevails on him to perform the function of messenger, as a prince who has become a friend sends an ambassador to his more powerful (conqueror).
verses.griffith_verse: Since Mātariśvan, far-diffused, hath stirred him, and he in every house grown bright and noble, He, Bhṛgu-like I hath gone as his companion, as on commission to a greater Sovran.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महे यत्पित्र ईं रसं दिवे करव त्सरत्पृशन्यश्चिकित्वान् ।सृजदस्ता धृषता दिद्युमस्मै स्वायां देवो दुहितरि त्विषिं धात् ॥
verses.transliteration: mahé ǀ yát ǀ pitré ǀ īm ǀ rásam ǀ divé ǀ káḥ ǀ áva ǀ tsarat ǀ pṛśanyáḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀsṛját ǀ ástā ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ didyúm ǀ asmai ǀ svā́yām ǀ deváḥ ǀ duhitári ǀ tvíṣim ǀ dhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: When man poured juice to Heaven, the mighty Father, he knew and freed himself from close embracement. The archer boldly shot at him his arrow, and the God threw his splendour on his Daughter.
verses.wilson_translation: When (the worshipper) offers an oblation to his great and illustrious protector, the grasping (rākṣas), recognizing you,Agni, retires; but Agni, the archer, sends after him a blazing arrow from his dreadful bow, and the god bestows light upon his own daughter (the dawn).
verses.griffith_verse: When man poured juice to Heaven, the mighty Father, he knew and freed himself from close embracement. The archer boldly shot at him his arrow, and the God threw his splendour on his Daughter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्व आ यस्तुभ्यं दम आ विभाति नमो वा दाशादुशतो अनु द्यून् ।वर्धो अग्ने वयो अस्य द्विबर्हा यासद्राया सरथं यं जुनासि ॥
verses.transliteration: své ǀ ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ vi-bhā́ti ǀ námaḥ ǀ vā ǀ dā́śāt ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀvárdho íti ǀ agne ǀ váyaḥ ǀ asya ǀ dvi-bárhāḥ ǀ yā́sat ǀ rāyā́ ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yám ǀ junā́si ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whoso, hath flames for thee within his dwelling, or brings the worship which thou lovest daily, Do thou of double might increase his substance: may he whom thou incitest meet with riches.
verses.wilson_translation: When (the worshipper) kindles you in his own dwelling, and presents an oblation to you, daily desiring it, do you,Agni, augmented in two ways, (as middling and as best), increase his means of sustenance; may he whom you sen dwith his car to battle, return with wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Whoso, hath flames for thee within his dwelling, or brings the worship which thou lovest daily, Do thou of double might increase his substance: may he whom thou incitest meet with riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं विश्वा अभि पृक्षः सचंते समुद्रं न स्रवतः सप्त यह्वीः ।न जामिभिर्वि चिकिते वयो नो विदा देवेषु प्रमतिं चिकित्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ sacante ǀ samudrám ǀ ná ǀ sravátaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǀná ǀ jāmí-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ cikite ǀ váyaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vidā́ḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ prá-matim ǀ cikitvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: All sacrificial viands wait on Agni as the Seven mighty Rivers seek the ocean. Not by our brethren was our food discovered: find with the Gods care for us, thou who knowest.
verses.wilson_translation: All (sacrificial) viands concentrate in Agni, as the seven great rivers flwo into the ocean; our food is not partaken of by our kinsmen, therefore do you, who know (all things), make our desires known to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: All sacrificial viands wait on Agni as the Seven mighty Rivers seek the ocean. Not by our brethren was our food discovered: find with the Gods care for us, thou who knowest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यदिषे नृपतिं तेज आनट्छुचि रेतो निषिक्तं द्यौरभीके ।अग्निः शर्धमनवद्यं युवानं स्वाध्यं जनयत्सूदयच्च ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yát ǀ iṣé ǀ nṛ-pátim ǀ téjaḥ ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ śúci ǀ rétaḥ ǀ ní-siktam ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀagníḥ ǀ śárdham ǀ anavadyám ǀ yúvānam ǀ su-ādhyám ǀ janayat ǀ sūdáyat ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: When light hath filled the Lord of men for increase, straight from the heaven descends the limpid moisture. Agni hath brought to light and filled with spirit the youthful host blameless and well providing.
verses.wilson_translation: May that (digestive) faculty (of Agni) with regards food, be imparted to the devout and illustrious protector of priests, as the source of virile vigour; and may Agni be born as (his) robust, irreproachable, youthful and intelligent son, and instrumental gate him (to acts of worship).
verses.griffith_verse: When light hath filled the Lord of men for increase, straight from the heaven descends the limpid moisture. Agni hath brought to light and filled with spirit the youthful host blameless and well providing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मनो न योऽध्वनः सद्य एत्येकः सत्रा सूरो वस्व ईशे ।राजाना मित्रावरुणा सुपाणी गोषु प्रियममृतं रक्षमाणा ॥
verses.transliteration: mánaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ éti ǀ ékaḥ ǀ satrā́ ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ īśe ǀrā́jānā ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ supāṇī́ íti su-pāṇī́ ǀ góṣu ǀ priyám ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ rákṣamāṇā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who like thought goes swiftly on his journey, the Sun, alone is ever Lord of riches. The Kings with fair hands, Varuṇa and Mitra, protect the precious nectar in our cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun, who traverses alone the path of heaven with the speed of thought, is at once lord of all treasures; the two kings,Mitraand Varuṇa, with bounteoushands, are the guardians of the precious ambrosia of our cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: He who like thought goes swiftly on his journey, the Sun, alone is ever Lord of riches. The Kings with fair hands, Varuṇa and Mitra, protect the precious nectar in our cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो अग्ने सख्या पित्र्याणि प्र मर्षिष्ठा अभि विदुष्कविः सन् ।नभो न रूपं जरिमा मिनाति पुरा तस्या अभिशस्तेरधीहि ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ pítryāṇi ǀ prá ǀ marṣiṣṭhāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vidúḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ sán ǀnábhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rūpám ǀ jarimā́ ǀ mināti ǀ purā́ ǀ tásyāḥ ǀ abhí-śasteḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, break not our ancestral friendship, Sage as thou art, endowed with deepest knowledge. Old age, like gathering cloud, impairs the body: before that evil be come nigh protect me.
verses.wilson_translation: Dissolve not,Agni, our ancestral friendship, for you are cognizant of the past as well as of the present; in like manner as light (speeds over) the sky, so decay impairs (my body); think of me before that source of destruction (prevails).
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, break not our ancestral friendship, Sage as thou art, endowed with deepest knowledge. Old age, like gathering cloud, impairs the body: before that evil be come nigh protect me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOUGH holding many gifts for men, he humbleth the higher powers of each wise ordainer.Agni is now the treasure-lord of treasures, for ever granting all immortal bounties. The Gods infallible all searching found not him, the dear Babe who still is round about us.Worn weary, following his track, devoted, they reached the lovely highest home of Agni. Because with holy oil the pure Ones, Agni, served thee the very pure three autumn seasons,Therefore they won them holy names for worship, and nobly born they dignified their bodies. Making them known to spacious earth and heaven, the holy Ones revealed the powers of Rudra.The mortal band, discerning in the distance, found Agni standing in the loftiest station. Nigh they approached, one-minded, with their spouses, kneeling to him adorable paid worship.Friend finding in his own friend's eye protection, they made their own the bodies which they chastened. Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee,With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amṛta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle. Thou, Agni, knower of men's works, hast sent us good food in constant course for our subsistence:Thou deeply skilled in paths of Gods becamest an envoy never wearied, offering-bearer. Knowing the Law, the seven strong floods from heaven, full of good thought, discerned the doors of riches.Saramā found the cattle's firm-built prison whereby the race of man is still supported. They who approached all noble operations making a path that leads to life immortal,To be the Bird's support, the spacious mother, Aditi, and her great Sons stood in power. When Gods immortal made both eyes of heaven, they gave to him the gift of beauteous glory.Now they flow forth like rivers set in motion: they knew the Red Steeds coming down, O Agni.

verses.sanskrit: नि काव्या वेधसः शश्वतस्कर्हस्ते दधानो नर्या पुरूणि ।अग्निर्भुवद्रयिपती रयीणां सत्रा चक्राणो अमृतानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ kā́vyā ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀ śáśvataḥ ǀ kaḥ ǀ háste ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ náryā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀagníḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ rayi-pátiḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ satrā́ ǀ cakrāṇáḥ ǀ amṛ́tāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOUGH holding many gifts for men, he humbleth the higher powers of each wise ordainer. Agni is now the treasure-lord of treasures, for ever granting all immortal bounties.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, holding in hishandsmany good things for men, appropriates the prayers addressed to the eternal creator. Agni is the lord of riches, quickly bestowing (on those who praise him) all golden (gifts).
verses.griffith_verse: THOUGH holding many gifts for men, he humbleth the higher powers of each wise ordainer. Agni is now the treasure-lord of treasures, for ever granting all immortal bounties.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे वत्सं परि षंतं न विंदन्निच्छंतो विश्वे अमृता अमूराः ।श्रमयुवः पदव्यो धियंधास्तस्थुः पदे परमे चार्वग्नेः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ vatsám ǀ pári ǀ sántam ǀ ná ǀ vindan ǀ icchántaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ ámūrāḥ ǀśrama-yúvaḥ ǀ pada-vyáḥ ǀ dhiyam-dhā́ḥ ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ padé ǀ paramé ǀ cā́ru ǀ agnéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods infallible all searching found not him, the dear Babe who still is round about us. Worn weary, following his track, devoted, they reached the lovely highest home of Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: All the immortals, and the unbewildered (Maruts), wishing for him who was (dear) to us as a son, and was everywhere around, discovered him not; oppressed with fatigue, wandering on foot, and cognizant of his acts, they stopped at the last beautiful (hiding) plural ce of Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods infallible all searching found not him, the dear Babe who still is round about us. Worn weary, following his track, devoted, they reached the lovely highest home of Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो यदग्ने शरदस्त्वामिच्छुचिं घृतेन शुचयः सपर्यान् ।नामानि चिद्दधिरे यज्ञियान्यसूदयंत तन्वः सुजाताः ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ yát ǀ agne ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ śúcim ǀ ghṛténa ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ saparyā́n ǀnā́māni ǀ cit ǀ dadhire ǀ yajñíyāni ǀ ásūdayanta ǀ tanváḥ ǀ sú-jātāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Because with holy oil the pure Ones, Agni, served thee the very pure three autumn seasons, Therefore they won them holy names for worship, and nobly born they dignified their bodies.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch,Agni, as the pure (Maruts) worshipped you, (equally) pure, with clarified butter for three years, therefore they acquired names worthy (to be treated) at sacrifice, and, being regenerated obtained celestial bodies.
verses.griffith_verse: Because with holy oil the pure Ones, Agni, served thee the very pure three autumn seasons, Therefore they won them holy names for worship, and nobly born they dignified their bodies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ रोदसी बृहती वेविदानाः प्र रुद्रिया जभ्रिरे यज्ञियासः ।विदन्मर्तो नेमधिता चिकित्वानग्निं पदे परमे तस्थिवांसं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ vévidānāḥ ǀ prá ǀ rudríyā ǀ jabhrire ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀvidát ǀ mártaḥ ǀ nemá-dhitā ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ agním ǀ padé ǀ paramé ǀ tasthi-vā́ṃsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Making them known to spacious earth and heaven, the holy Ones revealed the powers of Rudra. The mortal band, discerning in the distance, found Agni standing in the loftiest station.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who are to be worshipped, (the gods), inquiring between the expansive heaven and earth (for Agni), recited (hymns) dedicated to Rudra; the troop of mortal (Maruts), with (Indra), the shrer of half the oblation, knowing where Agni was hiding found him in his excellent retreat.
verses.griffith_verse: Making them known to spacious earth and heaven, the holy Ones revealed the powers of Rudra. The mortal band, discerning in the distance, found Agni standing in the loftiest station.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: संजानाना उप सीदन्नभिज्ञु पत्नीवंतो नमस्यं नमस्यन् ।रिरिक्वांसस्तन्वः कृण्वत स्वाः सखा सख्युर्निमिषि रक्षमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-jānānā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sīdan ǀ abhi-jñú ǀ pátnī-vantaḥ ǀ namasyám ǀ namasyanníti namasyan ǀririkvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ kṛṇvata ǀ svā́ḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ sákhyuḥ ǀ ni-míṣi ǀ rákṣamāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nigh they approached, one-minded, with their spouses, kneeling to him adorable paid worship. Friend finding in his own friend's eye protection, they made their own the bodies which they chastened.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods, discovering you, sat down, and with their wives paid reverntial adoration to you upon their knees. Secure on beholding their friend, of being protected, your friends, the gods, abandoned the rest of their bodies in sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Nigh they approached, one-minded, with their spouses, kneeling to him adorable paid worship. Friend finding in his own friend's eye protection, they made their own the bodies which they chastened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिः सप्त यद्गुह्यानि त्वे इत्पदाविदन्निहिता यज्ञियासः ।तेभी रक्षंते अमृतं सजोषाः पशूंच स्थातॄंचरथं च पाहि ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yát ǀ gúhyāni ǀ tvé íti ǀ ít ǀ padā́ ǀ avidan ǀ ní-hitā ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ rakṣante ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ paśū́n ǀ ca ǀ sthātṝ́n ǀ carátham ǀ ca ǀ pāhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee, With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amṛta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: (Devout men), competent to offer sacrifices, have known the thrice seven mystic rites comprised in you, and with them, worshipped you; do you, therefore, with like affection, protect their cattle, and all that (belongs to them), moveable or stationary.
verses.griffith_verse: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee, With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amṛta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विद्वाँ अग्ने वयुनानि क्षितीनां व्यानुषक्छुरुधो जीवसे धाः ।अंतर्विद्वाँ अध्वनो देवयानानतंद्रो दूतो अभवो हविर्वाट् ॥
verses.transliteration: vidvā́n ǀ agne ǀ vayúnāni ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ ví ǀ ānuṣák ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ jīváse ǀ dhāḥ ǀantaḥ-vidvā́n ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ deva-yā́nān ǀ átandraḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ haviḥ-vā́ṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni, knower of men's works, hast sent us good food in constant course for our subsistence: Thou deeply skilled in paths of Gods becamest an envoy never wearied, offering-bearer.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are cognizant of all things to be known, ever provide for the subsistence of men, grief-alleviating (food); so shall you be the diligent bearer of oblations, and messenger of the gods, knowing the paths between (earth and heaven), by which they travel.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni, knower of men's works, hast sent us good food in constant course for our subsistence: Thou deeply skilled in paths of Gods becamest an envoy never wearied, offering-bearer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वाध्यो दिव आ सप्त यह्वी रायो दुरो व्यृतज्ञा अजानन् ।विदद्गव्यं सरमा दृळ्हमूर्वं येना नु कं मानुषी भोजते विट् ॥
verses.transliteration: su-ādhyáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ saptá ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ dúraḥ ǀ ví ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀ ajānan ǀvidát ǀ gávyam ǀ sarámā ǀ dṛḷhám ǀ ūrvám ǀ yéna ǀ nú ǀ kam ǀ mā́nuṣī ǀ bhójate ǀ víṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing the Law, the seven strong floods from heaven, full of good thought, discerned the doors of riches. Saramā found the cattle's firm-built prison whereby the race of man is still supported.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven pure rivers that flow from heaven (are directed,Agni, by you; by you, the priests), skilled in sacrifices, knew the doors of the (cave where) the treasure, (their cattle), were concealed for you Saramādiscovered the abundant milk of the kine with which man, the progeny of Manu, still is nourished.
verses.griffith_verse: Knowing the Law, the seven strong floods from heaven, full of good thought, discerned the doors of riches. Saramā found the cattle's firm-built prison whereby the race of man is still supported.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ ये विश्वा स्वपत्यानि तस्थुः कृण्वानासो अमृतत्वाय गातुं ।मह्ना महद्भिः पृथिवी वि तस्थे माता पुत्रैरदितिर्धायसे वेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yé ǀ víśvā ǀ su-apatyā́ni ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ kṛṇvānā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvā́ya ǀ gātúm ǀmahnā́ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ví ǀ tasthe ǀ mātā́ ǀ putráiḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ dhā́yase ǀ véríti véḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who approached all noble operations making a path that leads to life immortal, To be the Bird's support, the spacious mother, Aditi, and her great Sons stood in power.
verses.wilson_translation: You have been fed, (Agni, with oblations) ever since theĀdityas, devising a road to immortality; instrumental tuted all (the sacred rites) that secured them from failing and mother earth,Aditi, strove with her magnitude to uphold (the world), along with her mighty sons.
verses.griffith_verse: They who approached all noble operations making a path that leads to life immortal, To be the Bird's support, the spacious mother, Aditi, and her great Sons stood in power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधि श्रियं नि दधुश्चारुमस्मिंदिवो यदक्षी अमृता अकृण्वन् ।अध क्षरंति सिंधवो न सृष्टाः प्र नीचीरग्ने अरुषीरजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ śríyam ǀ ní ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ cā́rum ǀ asmin ǀ diváḥ ǀ yát ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ ákṛṇvan ǀádha ǀ kṣaranti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sṛṣṭā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ nī́cīḥ ǀ agne ǀ áruṣīḥ ǀ ajānan ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Gods immortal made both eyes of heaven, they gave to him the gift of beauteous glory. Now they flow forth like rivers set in motion: they knew the Red Steeds coming down, O Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: (The offerers of oblations) have plural ced in this (Agni) the graceful honours (of the ceremony), and the two portions of clarified butter that are the two eyes (of the sacrifice); then the immortals come from heaven, and your bright flames, Agni, spread in all directions like rushing rivers, and the gods perceive it (and rejoice).
verses.griffith_verse: When Gods immortal made both eyes of heaven, they gave to him the gift of beauteous glory. Now they flow forth like rivers set in motion: they knew the Red Steeds coming down, O Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction,Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,—may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling. He who like Savitar the God, true-minded protecteth with his power. all acts of vigour,Truthful, like splendour, glorified by many, like breath joy-giving,—all must strive to win him. He who on earth dwells like a king surrounded by faithful friends, like a God all-sustaining,Like heroes who preside, who sit in safety: like as a blameless dame dear to her husband. Thee, such, in settlements secure, O Agni, our men serve ever kindled in each dwelling.On him have they laid splendour in abundance: dear to all men, bearer be he of riches. May thy rich worshippers win food, O Agni, and princes gain long life who bring oblation.May we get booty from our foe in battle, presenting to the Gods their share for glory. The cows of holy law, sent us by Heaven, have swelled with laden udders, loudly lowing;Soliciting his favour, from a distance the rivers to the rock have flowed together. Agni, with thee, soliciting thy favour, the holy Ones have gained glory in heaven.They made the Night and Dawn of different colours, and set the black and purple hues together. May we and those who worship be the mortals whom thou, O Agni, leadest on to riches.Thou hast filled earth and heaven and air's mid-region, and followest the whole world like a shadow. Aided by thee, O Agni, may we conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, heroes with heroes,Lords of the wealth transmitted by our fathers: and may our princes live a hundred winters. May these our hymns of praise, Agni, Ordainer, be pleasant to thee in thy heart and spirit.May we have power to hold thy steeds of riches, laying on thee the God-sent gift of glory.

verses.sanskrit: रयिर्न यः पितृवित्तो वयोधाः सुप्रणीतिश्चिकितुषो न शासुः ।स्योनशीरतिथिर्न प्रीणानो होतेव सद्म विधतो वि तारीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: rayíḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ pitṛ-vittáḥ ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀ su-pránītiḥ ǀ cikitúṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śā́suḥ ǀsyona-śī́ḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ ná ǀ prīṇānáḥ ǀ hótā-iva ǀ sádma ǀ vidhatáḥ ǀ ví ǀ tārīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction, Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,—may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, like patrimonial wealth, is the giver of food; he is a director, like the instrumental uctions of one learned in scripture; he rests in the sacrificial chamber like a welcome guest, and like an officiating priest, he brings prosperity on the house of the worshipper.
verses.griffith_verse: HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction, Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,—may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा क्रत्वा निपाति वृजनानि विश्वा ।पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: deváḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ satyá-manmā ǀ krátvā ǀ ni-pā́ti ǀ vṛjánāni ǀ víśvā ǀpuru-praśastáḥ ǀ amátiḥ ǀ ná ǀ satyáḥ ǀ ātmā́-iva ǀ śévaḥ ǀ didhiṣā́yyaḥ ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who like Savitar the God, true-minded protecteth with his power. all acts of vigour, Truthful, like splendour, glorified by many, like breath joy-giving,—all must strive to win him.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is like the divine Sun, who know the truth (of things), preserves by his actions (his votaries) in all encounters; like nature, he is unchangeable and, likesoul, is the source of happiness; he is ever to be cherished.
verses.griffith_verse: He who like Savitar the God, true-minded protecteth with his power. all acts of vigour, Truthful, like splendour, glorified by many, like breath joy-giving,—all must strive to win him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवो न यः पृथिवीं विश्वधाया उपक्षेति हितमित्रो न राजा ।पुरःसदः शर्मसदो न वीरा अनवद्या पतिजुष्टेव नारी ॥
verses.transliteration: deváḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ viśvá-dhāyāḥ ǀ upa-kṣéti ǀ hitá-mitraḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́jā ǀpuraḥ-sádaḥ ǀ śarma-sádaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ anavadyā́ ǀ pátijuṣṭā-iva ǀ nā́rī ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who on earth dwells like a king surrounded by faithful friends, like a God all-sustaining, Like heroes who preside, who sit in safety: like as a blameless dame dear to her husband.
verses.wilson_translation: He who, like the divine (Sun), is the supporter of the universe, abides on earth like a prince, (surrounded by) faithful friends; in his presence, men sit down like sons in the dwelling of a parent, and (in purity he resembles) an irreproachable and beloved wife.
verses.griffith_verse: He who on earth dwells like a king surrounded by faithful friends, like a God all-sustaining, Like heroes who preside, who sit in safety: like as a blameless dame dear to her husband.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा नरो दम आ नित्यमिद्धमग्ने सचंत क्षितिषु ध्रुवासु ।अधि द्युम्नं नि दधुर्भूर्यस्मिन्भवा विश्वायुर्धरुणो रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ náraḥ ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ nítyam ǀ iddhám ǀ agne ǀ sácanta ǀ kṣitíṣu ǀ dhruvā́su ǀádhi ǀ dyumnám ǀ ní ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ bhū́ri ǀ asmin ǀ bháva ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ dharúṇaḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, such, in settlements secure, O Agni, our men serve ever kindled in each dwelling. On him have they laid splendour in abundance: dear to all men, bearer be he of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Such as you are,Agni, men preserve you constantly kindled in their dwellings, in secure plural ces, and offer upon you abundant (sacrificial) food; do you, in whom is all existence, be the bearer of riches (for our advantage).
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, such, in settlements secure, O Agni, our men serve ever kindled in each dwelling. On him have they laid splendour in abundance: dear to all men, bearer be he of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि पृक्षो अग्ने मघवानो अश्युर्वि सूरयो ददतो विश्वमायुः ।सनेम वाजं समिथेष्वर्यो भागं देवेषु श्रवसे दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ agne ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ áśyuḥ ǀ ví ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ dádataḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀsanéma ǀ vā́jam ǀ sam-ithéṣu ǀ aryáḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ devéṣu ǀ śrávase ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May thy rich worshippers win food, O Agni, and princes gain long life who bring oblation. May we get booty from our foe in battle, presenting to the Gods their share for glory.
