verses.wilson_translation: May your opulent worshippers,Agni, obtain (abundant) food; may the learned (who praise you) and offer you (oblations), acquire long life; may we gain in battles booty from our foes, presenting their portion to the gods for (the acquisition of) renown.
verses.griffith_verse: May thy rich worshippers win food, O Agni, and princes gain long life who bring oblation. May we get booty from our foe in battle, presenting to the Gods their share for glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य हि धेनवो वावशानाः स्मदूध्नीः पीपयंत द्युभक्ताः ।परावतः सुमतिं भिक्षमाणा वि सिंधवः समया सस्रुरद्रिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ vāvaśānā́ḥ ǀ smát-ūdhnīḥ ǀ pīpáyanta ǀ dyú-bhaktāḥ ǀparā-vátaḥ ǀ su-matím ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀ ví ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ samáyā ǀ sasruḥ ǀ ádrim ǁ
verses.english_translation: The cows of holy law, sent us by Heaven, have swelled with laden udders, loudly lowing; Soliciting his favour, from a distance the rivers to the rock have flowed together.
verses.wilson_translation: The cows, loving (Agni, who has come to thehall of sacrifice), sharing his splendour, have brought with full udders (their milk) to be drunk. The rivers, soliciting his good will, have flowed from a distance in the vicinity of the mountain.
verses.griffith_verse: The cows of holy law, sent us by Heaven, have swelled with laden udders, loudly lowing; Soliciting his favour, from a distance the rivers to the rock have flowed together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे अग्ने सुमतिं भिक्षमाणा दिवि श्रवो दधिरे यज्ञियासः ।नक्ता च चक्रुरुषसा विरूपे कृष्णं च वर्णमरुणं च सं धुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ agne ǀ su-matím ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀ diví ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀnáktā ǀ ca ǀ cakrúḥ ǀ uṣásā ǀ vírūpe íti ví-rūpe ǀ kṛṣṇám ǀ ca ǀ várṇam ǀ aruṇám ǀ ca ǀ sám ǀ dhuríti dhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, with thee, soliciting thy favour, the holy Ones have gained glory in heaven. They made the Night and Dawn of different colours, and set the black and purple hues together.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods), who are entitled to worship, soliciting your good will, have entrusted to you, resplendent Agni, the (sacrificial) food, and, (for the due observance of sacred rites), they have made the night and morning of different colours, or black and purple.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, with thee, soliciting thy favour, the holy Ones have gained glory in heaven. They made the Night and Dawn of different colours, and set the black and purple hues together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यान्राये मर्तान्त्सुषूदो अग्ने ते स्याम मघवानो वयं च ।छायेव विश्वं भुवनं सिसक्ष्यापप्रिवान्रोदसी अंतरिक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́n ǀ rāyé ǀ mártān ǀ súsūdaḥ ǀ agne ǀ té ǀ syāma ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ ca ǀchāyā́-iva ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ sisakṣi ǀ āpapri-vā́n ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antárikṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we and those who worship be the mortals whom thou, O Agni, leadest on to riches. Thou hast filled earth and heaven and air's mid-region, and followest the whole world like a shadow.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, mortals, whom you have directed (to the performance of sacrifices) for the sake of riches, become opulent; filling heaven and earth, and the firmament (with your radiance), you protect the whole world like a (sheltering) shade.
verses.griffith_verse: May we and those who worship be the mortals whom thou, O Agni, leadest on to riches. Thou hast filled earth and heaven and air's mid-region, and followest the whole world like a shadow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वद्भिरग्ने अर्वतो नृभिर्नॄन्वीरैर्वीरान्वनुयामा त्वोताः ।ईशानासः पितृवित्तस्य रायो वि सूरयः शतहिमा नो अश्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: árvat-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ árvataḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ vīráiḥ ǀ vīrā́n ǀ vanuyāma ǀ tvā́-ūtāḥ ǀīśānā́saḥ ǀ pitṛ-vittásya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ví ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ śatá-himāḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ aśyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aided by thee, O Agni, may we conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, heroes with heroes, Lords of the wealth transmitted by our fathers: and may our princes live a hundred winters.
verses.wilson_translation: Defended,Agni, by you, may we destroy the horses (of your enemies) by (our) horses, their men by (our) men, their sons by (our) sons, and may our sons, learned and inheritors of ancestral wealth, live for a hundred winters.
verses.griffith_verse: Aided by thee, O Agni, may we conquer steeds with steeds, men with men, heroes with heroes, Lords of the wealth transmitted by our fathers: and may our princes live a hundred winters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एता ते अग्न उचथानि वेधो जुष्टानि संतु मनसे हृदे च ।शकेम रायः सुधुरो यमं तेऽधि श्रवो देवभक्तं दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ ucáthāni ǀ vedhaḥ ǀ júṣṭāni ǀ santu ǀ mánase ǀ hṛdé ǀ ca ǀśakéma ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ su-dhúraḥ ǀ yámam ǀ te ǀ ádhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ devá-bhaktam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May these our hymns of praise, Agni, Ordainer, be pleasant to thee in thy heart and spirit. May we have power to hold thy steeds of riches, laying on thee the God-sent gift of glory.
verses.wilson_translation: May these our praises, sapient Agni, be grateful to you, both in mind and heart; may we be competent to detain your well-supporting wealth, offering upon you their share of the (sacrificial food of the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: May these our hymns of praise, Agni, Ordainer, be pleasant to thee in thy heart and spirit. May we have power to hold thy steeds of riches, laying on thee the God-sent gift of glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As forth to sacrifice we go, a hymn to a hymn let us say,Who hears us even when afar; Who, from of old, in carnage, when the people gathered, hath preservedHis household for the worshipper. And let men say, Agni is born, e’en he who slayeth Vṛtra, heWho winneth wealth in every fight. Him in whose house an envoy thou lovest to taste his offered gifts,And strengthenest his sacrifice, Him, Aṅgiras, thou Son of Strength, all men call happy in his God,His offerings, and his sacred grass. Hitherward shalt thou bring these Gods to our laudation and to taste.These offered gifts, fair-shining One. When, Agni, on thine embassage thou goest not a sound is heard of steed or straining of thy car. Aided by thee uninjured, strong, one after other, goes he forth:Agni, the offerer forward steps. And splendid strength, heroic, high, Agni, thou grantest from the Gods,Thou God, to him who offers gifts.

verses.sanskrit: उपप्रयंतो अध्वरं मंत्रं वोचेमाग्नये ।आरे अस्मे च शृण्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-prayántaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ mántram ǀ vocema ǀ agnáye ǀāré ǀ asmé íti ǀ ca ǀ śṛṇvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: As forth to sacrifice we go, a hymn to a hymn let us say, Who hears us even when afar;
verses.wilson_translation: Hastening to the sacrifice, let us repeat a prayer to Agni, who fears us from afar.
verses.griffith_verse: As forth to sacrifice we go, a hymn to a hymn let us say, Who hears us even when afar;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः स्नीहितीषु पूर्व्यः संजग्मानासु कृष्टिषु ।अरक्षद्दाशुषे गयं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ snī́hitīṣu ǀ pūrvyáḥ ǀ sam-jagmānā́su ǀ kṛṣṭíṣu ǀárakṣat ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ gáyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, from of old, in carnage, when the people gathered, hath preserved His household for the worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, existing of old, has preserved wealth for the sacrificer, when malevolent men are assembled together.
verses.griffith_verse: Who, from of old, in carnage, when the people gathered, hath preserved His household for the worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत ब्रुवंतु जंतव उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि ।धनंजयो रणेरणे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ bruvantu ǀ jantávaḥ ǀ út ǀ agníḥ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ ajani ǀdhanam-jayáḥ ǀ ráṇe-raṇe ǁ
verses.english_translation: And let men say, Agni is born, e’en he who slayeth Vṛtra, he Who winneth wealth in every fight.
verses.wilson_translation: Let men praise Agnias soon as genitive rated, the slayer of Vṛtra, and the winner of booty in many a battle.
verses.griffith_verse: And let men say, Agni is born, e’en he who slayeth Vṛtra, he Who winneth wealth in every fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य दूतो असि क्षये वेषि हव्यानि वीतये ।दस्मत्कृणोष्यध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ási ǀ kṣáye ǀ véṣi ǀ havyā́ni ǀ vītáye ǀdasmát ǀ kṛṇóṣi ǀ adhvarám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him in whose house an envoy thou lovest to taste his offered gifts, And strengthenest his sacrifice,
verses.wilson_translation: (The sacrificer), in whose house you are the messenger of the gods, whose offering you convey for their food, and whose sacrifice you render acceptable.
verses.griffith_verse: Him in whose house an envoy thou lovest to taste his offered gifts, And strengthenest his sacrifice,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमित्सुहव्यमंगिरः सुदेवं सहसो यहो ।जना आहुः सुबर्हिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ su-havyám ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ su-devám ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ yaho íti ǀjánāḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ su-barhíṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, Aṅgiras, thou Son of Strength, all men call happy in his God, His offerings, and his sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Him,Aṅgiras, son of strength, men call forunate in his sacrifice, his deity, his oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, Aṅgiras, thou Son of Strength, all men call happy in his God, His offerings, and his sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ च वहासि ताँ इह देवाँ उप प्रशस्तये ।हव्या सुश्चंद्र वीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ca ǀ váhāsi ǀ tā́n ǀ ihá ǀ devā́n ǀ úpa ǀ prá-śastaye ǀhavyā́ ǀ su-candra ǀ vītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hitherward shalt thou bring these Gods to our laudation and to taste. These offered gifts, fair-shining One.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring hither, radiant Agni, the gods, to (receive) our praise and our oblations for their food.
verses.griffith_verse: Hitherward shalt thou bring these Gods to our laudation and to taste. These offered gifts, fair-shining One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न योरुपब्दिरश्व्यः शृण्वे रथस्य कच्चन ।यदग्ने यासि दूत्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yóḥ ǀ upabdíḥ ǀ áśvyaḥ ǀ śṛṇvé ǀ ráthasya ǀ kát ǀ caná ǀyát ǀ agne ǀ yā́si ǀ dūtyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Agni, on thine embassage thou goest not a sound is heard of steed or straining of thy car.
verses.wilson_translation: Whenever you go,Agni, on a mission of the gods, the neighing of the horses of your (swift) moving chariot, however audible is not heard.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Agni, on thine embassage thou goest not a sound is heard of steed or straining of thy car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वोतो वाज्यह्रयोऽभि पूर्वस्मादपरः ।प्र दाश्वाँ अग्ने अस्थात् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́-ūtaḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ áhrayaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pū́rvasmāt ǀ áparaḥ ǀprá ǀ dāśvā́n ǀ agne ǀ asthāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aided by thee uninjured, strong, one after other, goes he forth: Agni, the offerer forward steps.
verses.wilson_translation: He who was formerly subject to a superior, having been protected,Agni, by you, now stands in your presence as an offerer (of oblations) without bashfulness, and supplied with food.
verses.griffith_verse: Aided by thee uninjured, strong, one after other, goes he forth: Agni, the offerer forward steps.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत द्युमत्सुवीर्यं बृहदग्ने विवाससि ।देवेभ्यो देव दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ dyu-mát ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ bṛhát ǀ agne ǀ vivāsasi ǀdevébhyaḥ ǀ deva ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: And splendid strength, heroic, high, Agni, thou grantest from the Gods, Thou God, to him who offers gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily, divine Agni, you are desirous of bestowing upon the offerer (of oblations) to the gods, ample (wealth), brilliant, and giving vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: And splendid strength, heroic, high, Agni, thou grantest from the Gods, Thou God, to him who offers gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods,Pouring our offerings in thy mouth. Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Aṅgiras,Our precious, much-availing prayer. Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper?On whom dependent? who art thou? The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou,A Friend whom friends may supplicate. Bring to us Mitra, Varuṇa, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice.Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.

verses.sanskrit: जुषस्व सप्रथस्तमं वचो देवप्सरस्तमं ।हव्या जुह्वान आसनि ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣásva ǀ sapráthaḥ-tamam ǀ vácaḥ ǀ devápsaraḥ-tamam ǀhavyā́ ǀ júhvānaḥ ǀ āsáni ǁ
verses.english_translation: ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods, Pouring our offerings in thy mouth.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept our most exhaustive prayers, propitiatory of the gods, accepting our oblations in your mouth.
verses.griffith_verse: ACCEPT our loudest-sounding hymn, food most delightful to the Gods, Pouring our offerings in thy mouth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अथा ते अंगिरस्तमाग्ने वेधस्तम प्रियं ।वोचेम ब्रह्म सानसि ॥
verses.transliteration: átha ǀ te ǀ aṅgiraḥ-tama ǀ agne ǀ vedhaḥ-tama ǀ priyám ǀvocéma ǀ bráhma ǀ sānasí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Aṅgiras, Our precious, much-availing prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: And then, most wise Agni, chief of the Aṅgiras, may we address (to you) an acceptable and gratifying prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: Now, Agni, will we say to thee, O wisest and best Aṅgiras, Our precious, much-availing prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः ।को ह कस्मिन्नसि श्रितः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ te ǀ jāmíḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ágne ǀ káḥ ǀ dāśú-adhvaraḥ ǀkáḥ ǀ ha ǀ kásmin ǀ asi ǀ śritáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper? On whom dependent? who art thou?
verses.wilson_translation: Who,Agni, is your kinsman amongst people? Who is worthy to offer you sacrifice? Who, indeed, are you and where do you abide?
verses.griffith_verse: Who, Agni, is thy kin, of men? who is thy worthy worshipper? On whom dependent? who art thou?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं जामिर्जनानामग्ने मित्रो असि प्रियः ।सखा सखिभ्य ईड्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ jāmíḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ágne ǀ mitráḥ ǀ asi ǀ priyáḥ ǀsákhā ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou, A Friend whom friends may supplicate.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are the kinsman of people. You are the protector of sacrificers. You are extolled by priests, since you are the friend of all.
verses.griffith_verse: The kinsman, Agni, of mankind, their well beloved Friend art thou, A Friend whom friends may supplicate.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यजा नो मित्रावरुणा यजा देवाँ ऋतं बृहत् ।अग्ने यक्षि स्वं दमं ॥
verses.transliteration: yája ǀ naḥ ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ yája ǀ devā́n ǀ ṛtám ǀ bṛhát ǀágne ǀ yákṣi ǀ svám ǀ dámam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring to us Mitra, Varuṇa, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice. Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship for us,Mitraand Varuṇa; worship for us, all the gods; (celebrate) a great sacrifice; be present in your own dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring to us Mitra, Varuṇa, bring the Gods to mighty sacrifice. Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing?Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations? Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader.May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour. Burn thou up all the Rākṣasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices.Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver. Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated.Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer. As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages,So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.

verses.sanskrit: का त उपेतिर्मनसो वराय भुवदग्ने शंतमा का मनीषा ।को वा यज्ञैः परि दक्षं त आप केन वा ते मनसा दाशेम ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ te ǀ úpa-itiḥ ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ várāya ǀ bhúvat ǀ agne ǀ śám-tamā ǀ kā́ ǀ manīṣā́ ǀkáḥ ǀ vā ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ pári ǀ dákṣam ǀ te ǀ āpa ǀ kéna ǀ vā ǀ te ǀ mánasā ǀ dāśema ǁ
verses.english_translation: How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing? Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations?
verses.wilson_translation: What approximation of the mind,Agni, to you, can be accomplished for our good; what can a hundred encomiums (effect); who, by sacrifices has obtained your might; with what intent may we offer you (oblations)?
verses.griffith_verse: How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing? Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एह्यग्न इह होता नि षीदादब्धः सु पुरएता भवा नः ।अवतां त्वा रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे यजा महे सौमनसाय देवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ agne ǀ ihá ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ sīda ǀ ádabdhaḥ ǀ sú ǀ puraḥ-etā́ ǀ bhava ǀ naḥ ǀávatām ǀ tvā ǀ ródasī íti ǀ viśvaminvé íti viśvam-invé ǀ yája ǀ mahé ǀ saumanasā́ya ǀ devā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader. May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Agni, hither; invoker (of the gods), sit down; be our preceder; for you are irresistible; may the all-expansive heaven and earth defend you, that you may worship the gods to their great satisfaction.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader. May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सु विश्वान्रक्षसो धक्ष्यग्ने भवा यज्ञानामभिशस्तिपावा ।अथा वह सोमपतिं हरिभ्यामातिथ्यमस्मै चकृमा सुदाव्ने ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ víśvān ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ dhákṣi ǀ agne ǀ bháva ǀ yajñā́nām ǀ abhiśasti-pā́vā ǀátha ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ sóma-patim ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ ātithyám ǀ asmai ǀ cakṛma ǀ su-dā́vne ǁ
verses.english_translation: Burn thou up all the Rākṣasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices. Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver.
verses.wilson_translation: Utterly consume all therākṣasas,Agni, and be the protector of our sacrifices against interruption. Bring hither the guardian of Soma, (Indra), with his steeds, that we may show hospitality to the giver of food.
verses.griffith_verse: Burn thou up all the Rākṣasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices. Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रजावता वचसा वह्निरासा च हुवे नि च सत्सीह देवैः ।वेषि होत्रमुत पोत्रं यजत्र बोधि प्रयंतर्जनितर्वसूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: prajā́-vatā ǀ vácasā ǀ váhniḥ ǀ āsā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ huvé ǀ ní ǀ ca ǀ satsi ǀ ihá ǀ deváiḥ ǀvéṣi ǀ hotrám ǀ utá ǀ potrám ǀ yajatra ǀ bodhí ǀ pra-yantaḥ ǀ janitaḥ ǀ vásūnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated. Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke (you), who are the conveyor (of oblations), with your flames, with a hymn productive of progeny (to the worshipper); sit down here with the gods, and do you, who are deserving of worship, discharge the office of Hotā, or of Potāand awaken us, you who are the depository and genitive rator of riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated. Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा विप्रस्य मनुषो हविर्भिर्देवाँ अयजः कविभिः कविः सन् ।एवा होतः सत्यतर त्वमद्याग्ने मंद्रया जुह्वा यजस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ víprasya ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ áyajaḥ ǀ kaví-bhiḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ sán ǀevá ǀ hotaríti ǀ satya-tara ǀ tvám ǀ adyá ǀ ágne ǀ mandráyā ǀ juhvā́ ǀ yajasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages, So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.
verses.wilson_translation: As at the sacrifice of the holy Manu, you, a sage amongst sages, did worship the gods with oblations, so also,Agni, veracious invoker of the gods, do you today (present the oblations), with an exhilarating ladle.
verses.griffith_verse: As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages, So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . How shall we pay oblation unto Agni? What hymn, Godloved, is said to him refulgent?Who, deathless, true to Law, mid men a herald, bringeth the Gods as best of sacrificers? Bring him with reverence hither, most propitious in sacrifices, true to Law, the herald;For Agni, when he seeks the Gods for mortals, knows them full well and worships them in spirit. For he is mental power, a man, and perfect; he is the bringer, friend-like, of the wondrous.The pious Āryan tribes at sacrifices address them first to him who doeth marvels. May Agni, foe-destroyer, manliest Hero, accept with love our hymns and our devotion.So may the liberal lords whose strength is strongest, urged by their riches, stir our thoughts with vigour. Thus Agni Jātavedas, true to Order, hath by the priestly Gotamas been lauded.May he augment in them splendour and vigour: observant, as he lists, he gathers increase.

verses.sanskrit: कथा दाशेमाग्नये कास्मै देवजुष्टोच्यते भामिने गीः ।यो मर्त्येष्वमृत ऋतावा होता यजिष्ठ इत्कृणोति देवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ dāśema ǀ agnáye ǀ kā́ ǀ asmai ǀ devá-juṣṭā ǀ ucyate ǀ bhāmíne ǀ gī́ḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ hótā ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ít ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ devā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: How shall we pay oblation unto Agni? What hymn, Godloved, is said to him refulgent? Who, deathless, true to Law, mid men a herald, bringeth the Gods as best of sacrificers?
verses.wilson_translation: What (oblations) may we offer to Agni? What praise is addressed to the luminous (Agni) that is agreeable to the gods? that Agni who is immortal and observant of truth, who is the invoker of the gods, the performer of sacrifices, and who, (present) amongst men, conveys oblations to the deities.
verses.griffith_verse: How shall we pay oblation unto Agni? What hymn, Godloved, is said to him refulgent? Who, deathless, true to Law, mid men a herald, bringeth the Gods as best of sacrificers?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अध्वरेषु शंतम ऋतावा होता तमू नमोभिरा कृणुध्वं ।अग्निर्यद्वेर्मर्ताय देवान्त्स चा बोधाति मनसा यजाति ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ śám-tamaḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ hótā ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀagníḥ ǀ yát ǀ véḥ ǀ mártāya ǀ devā́n ǀ sáḥ ǀ ca ǀ bódhāti ǀ mánasā ǀ yajāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring him with reverence hither, most propitious in sacrifices, true to Law, the herald; For Agni, when he seeks the Gods for mortals, knows them full well and worships them in spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring hither, with praises, him who is most constant in sacrifice, observant of truth, and the invoker (of the gods), for Agni, when he repairs to the gods on the part of man, knows those (who are to be worshipped), and worships them with reverence.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring him with reverence hither, most propitious in sacrifices, true to Law, the herald; For Agni, when he seeks the Gods for mortals, knows them full well and worships them in spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि क्रतुः स मर्यः स साधुर्मित्रो न भूदद्भुतस्य रथीः ।तं मेधेषु प्रथमं देवयंतीर्विश उप ब्रुवते दस्ममारीः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ krátuḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ máryaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ sādhúḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhūt ǀ ádbhutasya ǀ rathī́ḥ ǀtám ǀ médheṣu ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yántīḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ bruvate ǀ dasmám ǀ ā́rīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For he is mental power, a man, and perfect; he is the bringer, friend-like, of the wondrous. The pious Āryan tribes at sacrifices address them first to him who doeth marvels.
verses.wilson_translation: For he is the performer of rites, he is the destroyer and reviver (of all things), and, like a friend he is the donor of unattained wealth; all men reverencing the gods, and approaching the well-looking Agni, repeat his name first in holy rites.
verses.griffith_verse: For he is mental power, a man, and perfect; he is the bringer, friend-like, of the wondrous. The pious Āryan tribes at sacrifices address them first to him who doeth marvels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नो नृणां नृतमो रिशादा अग्निर्गिरोऽवसा वेतु धीतिं ।तना च ये मघवानः शविष्ठा वाजप्रसूता इषयंत मन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ riśā́dāḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ vetu ǀ dhītím ǀtánā ǀ ca ǀ yé ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ śáviṣṭhāḥ ǀ vā́ja-prasūtāḥ ǀ iṣáyanta ǀ mánma ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Agni, foe-destroyer, manliest Hero, accept with love our hymns and our devotion. So may the liberal lords whose strength is strongest, urged by their riches, stir our thoughts with vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agni, who is the chief director of sacrifices, and the destroyer of enemies, accept our praise and worship with oblations, and may those who are affluent with great wealth, who are endowed with strength, and by whom the sacrificial food has been prepared, be desirous to offer adoration.
verses.griffith_verse: May Agni, foe-destroyer, manliest Hero, accept with love our hymns and our devotion. So may the liberal lords whose strength is strongest, urged by their riches, stir our thoughts with vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवाग्निर्गोतमेभिर्ऋतावा विप्रेभिरस्तोष्ट जातवेदाः ।स एषु द्युम्नं पीपयत्स वाजं स पुष्टिं याति जोषमा चिकित्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ agníḥ ǀ gótamebhiḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ víprebhiḥ ǀ astoṣṭa ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ eṣu ǀ dyumnám ǀ pīpayat ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ sáḥ ǀ puṣṭím ǀ yāti ǀ jóṣam ǀ ā́ ǀ cikitvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus Agni Jātavedas, true to Order, hath by the priestly Gotamas been lauded. May he augment in them splendour and vigour: observant, as he lists, he gathers increase.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus has Agni, the celebrator of sacrifices, and by whom all things are known, been hymned by the pious descendant of Gotama; to them he has given the bright Somato drink, along with the sacrificial food, and gratified by our devotion, he obtains nutriment (for himself).
verses.griffith_verse: Thus Agni Jātavedas, true to Order, hath by the priestly Gotamas been lauded. May he augment in them splendour and vigour: observant, as he lists, he gathers increase.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O JĀTAVEDAS, keen and swift, we Gotamas with sacred song exalt thee for thy glories' sake. Thee, as thou art, desiring wealth Gotama worships with his song:We laud thee for thy glories' sake. As such, like Aṅgiras we call on thee best winner of the spoil:We laud thee for thy glories' sake. Thee, best of Vṛtra-slayers, thee who shakest off our Dasyu foes:We laud thee for thy glories' sake. A pleasant song to Agni we, sons of Rahūgaṅa, have sung:We laud thee for thy glories' sake.

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्वा गोतमा गिरा जातवेदो विचर्षणे ।द्युम्नैरभि प्र णोनुमः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ gótamāḥ ǀ girā́ ǀ jā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇe ǀdyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O JĀTAVEDAS, keen and swift, we Gotamas with sacred song exalt thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.wilson_translation: Knower and beholder of all that exists (jātanām veditaḥ).Gotamacelebrates you,Agni, with praise; we praise you repeatedly with commendatory (hymns).
verses.griffith_verse: O JĀTAVEDAS, keen and swift, we Gotamas with sacred song exalt thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमु त्वा गोतमो गिरा रायस्कामो दुवस्यति ।द्युम्नैरभि प्र णोनुमः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ gótamaḥ ǀ girā́ ǀ rāyáḥ-kāmaḥ ǀ duvasyati ǀdyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, as thou art, desiring wealth Gotama worships with his song: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.wilson_translation: To you; that (Agni) whom Gotama, desirous of riches, worships with praise, we offer adoration with commendatory (hymns).
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, as thou art, desiring wealth Gotama worships with his song: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमु त्वा वाजसातममंगिरस्वद्धवामहे ।द्युम्नैरभि प्र णोनुमः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ vāja-sā́tamam ǀ aṅgirasvát ǀ havāmahe ǀdyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As such, like Aṅgiras we call on thee best winner of the spoil: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you, such as you are, the giver of abundant food, in like manner as did Aṅgiras; we praise you repeatedly with commendatory (hymns).
verses.griffith_verse: As such, like Aṅgiras we call on thee best winner of the spoil: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमु त्वा वृत्रहंतमं यो दस्यूँरवधूनुषे ।द्युम्नैरभि प्र णोनुमः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ vṛtrahán-tamam ǀ yáḥ ǀ dásyūn ǀ ava-dhūnuṣé ǀdyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, best of Vṛtra-slayers, thee who shakest off our Dasyu foes: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.wilson_translation: We praise you repeatedly with commendatory (hymns), who are the destroyer of Vṛtra, and who put the Dasyusto flight.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, best of Vṛtra-slayers, thee who shakest off our Dasyu foes: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवोचाम रहूगणा अग्नये मधुमद्वचः ।द्युम्नैरभि प्र णोनुमः ॥
verses.transliteration: ávocāma ǀ ráhūgaṇāḥ ǀ agnáye ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ vácaḥ ǀdyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A pleasant song to Agni we, sons of Rahūgaṅa, have sung: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.wilson_translation: The descendants of Rāhugaṇa have recited sweet speeches to Agni; we praise him repeatedly with commendatory (hymns).
verses.griffith_verse: A pleasant song to Agni we, sons of Rahūgaṅa, have sung: We laud thee for thy glories' sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE in mid-air's expanse hath golden tresses; a raging serpent, like the rushing tempest:Purely refulgent, knowing well the morning; like honourable dames, true, active workers. Thy well-winged flashes strengthen in their manner, when the black Bull hath bellowed round about us.With drops that bless and seem to smile he cometh: the waters fall, the clouds utter their thunder. When he comes streaming with the milk of worship, conducting by directest paths of OrderAryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, Parijman fill the hide full where lies the nether press-stone. O Agni, thou who art the lord of wealth in kine, thou Son of Strength,Vouchsafe to us, O Jātavedas, high renown. He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song:Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us. O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks,Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Rākṣasas. Adorable in all our rites, favour us, Agni, with thine aid,When the great hymn is chanted forth. Bring to us ever-conquering wealth, wealth, Agni, worthy of our choice,In all our frays invincible. Give us, O Agni, through thy grace wealth that supporteth all our life,Thy favour so that we may live. O Gotama, desiring bliss present thy songs composed with careTo Agni of the pointed flames. May the man fall, O Agni, who near or afar assaileth us:Do thou increase and prosper us. Keen and swift Agni, thousand-eyed, chaseth the Rākṣasas afar:He singeth, herald meet for lauds.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यकेशो रजसो विसारेऽहिर्धुनिर्वात इव ध्रजीमान् ।शुचिभ्राजा उषसो नवेदा यशस्वतीरपस्युवो न सत्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-keśaḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-sāré ǀ áhiḥ ǀ dhúniḥ ǀ vā́taḥ-iva ǀ dhrájīmān ǀśúci-bhrājāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ návedāḥ ǀ yáśasvatīḥ ǀ apasyúvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ satyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE in mid-air's expanse hath golden tresses; a raging serpent, like the rushing tempest: Purely refulgent, knowing well the morning; like honourable dames, true, active workers.
verses.wilson_translation: The golden-haired Agniis the agitator of the clouds when the rain is poured forth, and, moving with the swiftness of the wind, shines with a bright radiance. The mornings know not (of the showers, like honest (people), who, provided with food, are intent upon their own labours.
verses.griffith_verse: HE in mid-air's expanse hath golden tresses; a raging serpent, like the rushing tempest: Purely refulgent, knowing well the morning; like honourable dames, true, active workers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते सुपर्णा अमिनंतँ एवैः कृष्णो नोनाव वृषभो यदीदं ।शिवाभिर्न स्मयमानाभिरागात्पतंति मिहः स्तनयंत्यभ्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ aminanta ǀ évaiḥ ǀ kṛṣṇáḥ ǀ nonāva ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ yádi ǀ idám ǀśivā́bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ smáyamānābhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ pátanti ǀ míhaḥ ǀ stanáyanti ǀ abhrā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy well-winged flashes strengthen in their manner, when the black Bull hath bellowed round about us. With drops that bless and seem to smile he cometh: the waters fall, the clouds utter their thunder.
verses.wilson_translation: The falling (rays), accompanied by the moving (Maruts), strike against (the cloud); the black shedder of rain has roared; when this is done, (the shower) comes with delightful and smiling (drops), the rain descends, the clouds thunder.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy well-winged flashes strengthen in their manner, when the black Bull hath bellowed round about us. With drops that bless and seem to smile he cometh: the waters fall, the clouds utter their thunder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदीमृतस्य पयसा पियानो नयन्नृतस्य पथिभी रजिष्ठैः ।अर्यमा मित्रो वरुणः परिज्मा त्वचं पृंचंत्युपरस्य योनौ ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ īm ǀ ṛtásya ǀ páyasā ǀ píyānaḥ ǀ náyan ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ rájiṣṭhaiḥ ǀaryamā́ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ tvácam ǀ pṛñcanti ǀ úparasya ǀ yónau ǁ
verses.english_translation: When he comes streaming with the milk of worship, conducting by directest paths of Order Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, Parijman fill the hide full where lies the nether press-stone.
verses.wilson_translation: When this, (the lightning,Agni), nourishes the world with the milk of the rain, and conducts it by the most direct ways to (the enjoyment of) water, then Mitra,Aryaman,Varuṇaand the circumambient (troop of Maruts) pierce through the (investing) membrane into the womb of the cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: When he comes streaming with the milk of worship, conducting by directest paths of Order Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, Parijman fill the hide full where lies the nether press-stone.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो ।अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ vā́jasya ǀ gó-mataḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ yaho íti ǀasmé íti ǀ dhehi ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, thou who art the lord of wealth in kine, thou Son of Strength, Vouchsafe to us, O Jātavedas, high renown.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, sone of strength, lord of food and of cattle, give us abundant sustenance, you who know all that exists.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, thou who art the lord of wealth in kine, thou Son of Strength, Vouchsafe to us, O Jātavedas, high renown.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इधानो वसुष्कविरग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा ।रेवदस्मभ्यं पुर्वणीक दीदिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ idhānáḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ īḷényaḥ ǀ girā́ ǀrevát ǀ asmábhyam ǀ puru-anīka ǀ dīdihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song: Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the blazing Agni, who is wise, and the granter of dwellings, is to be praised by our hymns; oḥ! you whose mouth (glows) with many (flames), shine (propitiously, so) that food-providing wealth may be ours.
verses.griffith_verse: He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song: Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्षपो राजन्नुत त्मनाग्ने वस्तोरुतोषसः ।स तिग्मजंभ रक्षसो दह प्रति ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣapáḥ ǀ rājan ǀ utá ǀ tmánā ǀ ágne ǀ vástoḥ ǀ utá ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ tigma-jambha ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ daha ǀ práti ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks, Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Rākṣasas.
verses.wilson_translation: Shining Agni, drive off (all disturbers of the rite), either by yourself or (your servants) whether by day or by night; sharp-visaged Agni, destroy therākṣasasentirely.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks, Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Rākṣasas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवा नो अग्न ऊतिभिर्गायत्रस्य प्रभर्मणि ।विश्वासु धीषु वंद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ gāyatrásya ǀ prá-bharmaṇi ǀvíśvāsu ǀ dhīṣú ǀ vandya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adorable in all our rites, favour us, Agni, with thine aid, When the great hymn is chanted forth.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who in all rites are to be praised, guard us with your protection, (propitiated) by the recitation of the metrical hymn.
verses.griffith_verse: Adorable in all our rites, favour us, Agni, with thine aid, When the great hymn is chanted forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो अग्ने रयिं भर सत्रासाहं वरेण्यं ।विश्वासु पृत्सु दुष्टरं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ rayím ǀ bhara ǀ satrā-sáham ǀ váreṇyam ǀvíśvāsu ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ dustáram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring to us ever-conquering wealth, wealth, Agni, worthy of our choice, In all our frays invincible.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant us,Agni, riches that dispel poverty that are desirable (to all), and cannot be taken (from us) in all encounters (with our foes).
verses.griffith_verse: Bring to us ever-conquering wealth, wealth, Agni, worthy of our choice, In all our frays invincible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो अग्ने सुचेतुना रयिं विश्वायुपोषसं ।मार्डीकं धेहि जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ su-cetúnā ǀ rayím ǀ viśvā́yu-poṣasam ǀmārḍīkám ǀ dhehi ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us, O Agni, through thy grace wealth that supporteth all our life, Thy favour so that we may live.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant us,Agni, for our livelihood, wealth, with sound understanding, conferring happiness, and sustaining (us) through life.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us, O Agni, through thy grace wealth that supporteth all our life, Thy favour so that we may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र पूतास्तिग्मशोचिषे वाचो गोतमाग्नये ।भरस्व सुम्नयुर्गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ pūtā́ḥ ǀ tigmá-śociṣe ǀ vā́caḥ ǀ gotama ǀ agnáye ǀbhárasva ǀ sumna-yúḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Gotama, desiring bliss present thy songs composed with care To Agni of the pointed flames.
verses.wilson_translation: Gotama, desirous of wealth, offers to the sharp-flaming Agnipure prayers and praises.
verses.griffith_verse: O Gotama, desiring bliss present thy songs composed with care To Agni of the pointed flames.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो नो अग्नेऽभिदासत्यंति दूरे पदीष्ट सः ।अस्माकमिद्वृधे भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ abhi-dā́sati ǀ ánti ǀ dūré ǀ padīṣṭá ǀ sáḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ ít ǀ vṛdhé ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the man fall, O Agni, who near or afar assaileth us: Do thou increase and prosper us.
verses.wilson_translation: May he,Agni, who annoys us, whether nigh or afar perish; and do you be to us (propitious) for our advancement.
verses.griffith_verse: May the man fall, O Agni, who near or afar assaileth us: Do thou increase and prosper us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्राक्षो विचर्षणिरग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति ।होता गृणीत उक्थ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sahasra-akṣáḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ sedhati ǀhótā ǀ gṛṇīte ǀ ukthyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Keen and swift Agni, thousand-eyed, chaseth the Rākṣasas afar: He singeth, herald meet for lauds.
verses.wilson_translation: The thousand-eyed, all-beholding,Agni, drives away therākṣasas, and (praised by us) with holy hymns, he, the (invoker of the gods) celebrates their praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Keen and swift Agni, thousand-eyed, chaseth the Rākṣasas afar: He singeth, herald meet for lauds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXX. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १६ गोतमो राहूगणः। इन्द्रः, १६ इन्द्रः, (अथर्वा, मनुः दध्यङ् च)। पंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THUS in the Soma, in wild joy the Brahman hath exalted thee:Thou, mightiest thunder-armed, hast driven by force the Dragon from the earth, lauding thine own imperial sway. The mighty flowing Soma-draught, brought by the Hawk, hath gladdened thee,That in thy strength, O Thunderer, thou hast struck down Vṛtra from the floods, lauding thine own imperial sway. Go forward, meet the foe, be bold; thy bolt of thunder is not checked.Manliness, Indra, is thy might: stay Vṛtra, make the waters thine, lauding thine own imperial sway. Thou smotest Vṛtra from the earth, smotest him, Indra, from the sky.Let these life-fostering waters flow attended by the Marut host, lauding thine own imperial sway. The wrathful Indra with his bolt of thunder rushing on the foe,Smote fierce on trembling Vṛtra's back, and loosed the waters free to run, lauding his own imperial sway. With hundred-jointed thunderbolt Indra hath struck him on the back,And, while rejoicing in the juice, seeketh prosperity for friends, lauding his own imperial sway. Indra, unconquered might is thine, Thunderer, Caster of the Stone;For thou with thy surpassing power smotest to death the guileful beast, lauding thine own imperial sway. Far over ninety spacious floods thy thunderbolts were cast abroad:Great, Indra, is thy hero might, and strength is seated in thine arms, lauding thine own imperial sway. Laud him a thousand all at once, shout twenty forth the hymn of praise.Hundreds have sung aloud to him, to Indra hath the prayer been raised, lauding his own imperial sway. Indra hath smitten down the power of Vṛtra,—might with stronger might.This was his manly exploit, he slew Vṛtra and let loose the floods, lauding his own imperial sway. Yea, even this great Pair of Worlds trembled in terror at thy wrath,When, Indra, Thunderer, Marut-girt, thou slewest Vṛtra in thy strength, lauding thine own imperial sway. But Vṛtra scared not Indra with his shaking or his thunder roar.On him that iron thunderbolt fell fiercely with its thousand points, lauding his own imperial sway. When with the thunder thou didst make thy dart and Vṛtra meet in war,Thy might, O Indra, fain to slay the Dragon, was set firm in heaven, lauding thine own imperial sway. When at thy shout, O Thunder-armed, each thing both fixed and moving shook,E’en Tvaṣṭar trembled at thy wrath and quaked with fear because of thee, lauding thine own imperial sway. There is not, in our knowledge, one who passeth Indra in his strength:In him the Deities have stored manliness, insight, power and might, lauding his own imperial sway. Still as of old, whatever rite Atharvan, Manus sire of all,Dadhyach performed, their prayer and praise united in that Indra meet, lauding his own imperial sway.

verses.sanskrit: इत्था हि सोम इन्मदे ब्रह्मा चकार वर्धनं ।शविष्ठ वज्रिन्नोजसा पृथिव्या निः शशा अहिमर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: itthā́ ǀ hí ǀ sóme ǀ ít ǀ máde ǀ brahmā́ ǀ cakā́ra ǀ várdhanam ǀśáviṣṭha ǀ vajrin ǀ ójasā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ śaśāḥ ǀ áhim ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: THUS in the Soma, in wild joy the Brahman hath exalted thee: Thou, mightiest thunder-armed, hast driven by force the Dragon from the earth, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty wielder of the thunderbolt, when the priest had thus exalted you (by praise), and exhilarating Soma(had been drunk), you did expel, by your vigour, Ahi from the earth, manifesting your own soverignty.
verses.griffith_verse: THUS in the Soma, in wild joy the Brahman hath exalted thee: Thou, mightiest thunder-armed, hast driven by force the Dragon from the earth, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वामदद्वृषा मदः सोमः श्येनाभृतः सुतः ।येना वृत्रं निरद्भ्यो जघंथ वज्रिन्नोजसार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ amadat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ mádaḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ śyená-ābhṛtaḥ ǀ sutáḥ ǀyéna ǀ vṛtrám ǀ níḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ jaghántha ǀ vajrin ǀ ójasā ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mighty flowing Soma-draught, brought by the Hawk, hath gladdened thee, That in thy strength, O Thunderer, thou hast struck down Vṛtra from the floods, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: That exceedingly exhilarating Soma, which was brought by the hawk (from heaven), when poured forth, has exhilarated you, so that in your vigour, thunderer, you have struck Vṛtrafrom the sky, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: The mighty flowing Soma-draught, brought by the Hawk, hath gladdened thee, That in thy strength, O Thunderer, thou hast struck down Vṛtra from the floods, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेह्यभीहि धृष्णुहि न ते वज्रो नि यंसते ।इंद्र नृम्णं हि ते शवो हनो वृत्रं जया अपोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ ihi ǀ abhí ǀ ihi ǀ dhṛṣṇuhí ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ vájraḥ ǀ ní ǀ yaṃsate ǀíndra ǀ nṛmṇám ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ śávaḥ ǀ hánaḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jáyāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go forward, meet the foe, be bold; thy bolt of thunder is not checked. Manliness, Indra, is thy might: stay Vṛtra, make the waters thine, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Hasten, assail, subdue; your thunderbolt cannot fail; your vigour,Indra, destroys men; slay Vṛtra, win the waters, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Go forward, meet the foe, be bold; thy bolt of thunder is not checked. Manliness, Indra, is thy might: stay Vṛtra, make the waters thine, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निरिंद्र भूम्या अधि वृत्रं जघंथ निर्दिवः ।सृजा मरुत्वतीरव जीवधन्या इमा अपोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ ǀ indra ǀ bhū́myāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghantha ǀ níḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀsṛjá ǀ marútvatīḥ ǀ áva ǀ jīvá-dhanyāḥ ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou smotest Vṛtra from the earth, smotest him, Indra, from the sky. Let these life-fostering waters flow attended by the Marut host, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Youu have struck Vṛtrafrom off the earth and from heaven; (now) let loose the wind-bound, life-sustaining rain, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou smotest Vṛtra from the earth, smotest him, Indra, from the sky. Let these life-fostering waters flow attended by the Marut host, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो वृत्रस्य दोधतः सानुं वज्रेण हीळितः ।अभिक्रम्याव जिघ्नतेऽपः सर्माय चोदयन्नर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ vṛtrásya ǀ dódhataḥ ǀ sā́num ǀ vájreṇa ǀ hīḷitáḥ ǀabhi-krámya ǀ áva ǀ jighnate ǀ apáḥ ǀ sármāya ǀ codáyan ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wrathful Indra with his bolt of thunder rushing on the foe, Smote fierce on trembling Vṛtra's back, and loosed the waters free to run, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Indignant Indra, encountering him, has struck with his bolt the jaw of the trembling Vṛtra, setting the waters free to flow, and manifesting his own soverignty.
verses.griffith_verse: The wrathful Indra with his bolt of thunder rushing on the foe, Smote fierce on trembling Vṛtra's back, and loosed the waters free to run, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधि सानौ नि जिघ्नते वज्रेण शतपर्वणा ।मंदान इंद्रो अंधसः सखिभ्यो गातुमिच्छत्यर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ sā́nau ǀ ní ǀ jighnate ǀ vájreṇa ǀ śatá-parvaṇā ǀmandānáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ icchati ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: With hundred-jointed thunderbolt Indra hath struck him on the back, And, while rejoicing in the juice, seeketh prosperity for friends, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas struck him on the temple with his hundred-edged thunderbolt, and, exulting, wishes to provide means of sustenance for his friends, manifesting his own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: With hundred-jointed thunderbolt Indra hath struck him on the back, And, while rejoicing in the juice, seeketh prosperity for friends, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र तुभ्यमिदद्रिवोऽनुत्तं वज्रिन्वीर्यं ।यद्ध त्यं मायिनं मृगं तमु त्वं माययावधीरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ túbhyam ǀ ít ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ ánuttam ǀ vajrin ǀ vīryám ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ tyám ǀ māyínam ǀ mṛgám ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvám ǀ māyáyā ǀ avadhīḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, unconquered might is thine, Thunderer, Caster of the Stone; For thou with thy surpassing power smotest to death the guileful beast, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Cloud-borne,Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, verily your prowess is undisputed, since you, with (superior) craft, have slain that deceptive deer, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, unconquered might is thine, Thunderer, Caster of the Stone; For thou with thy surpassing power smotest to death the guileful beast, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि ते वज्रासो अस्थिरन्नवतिं नाव्या अनु ।महत्त इंद्र वीर्यं बाह्वोस्ते बलं हितमर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ te ǀ vájrāsaḥ ǀ asthiran ǀ navatím ǀ nāvyā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀmahát ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ vīryám ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ te ǀ bálam ǀ hitám ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far over ninety spacious floods thy thunderbolts were cast abroad: Great, Indra, is thy hero might, and strength is seated in thine arms, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Your thunderbolts were scattered widely over ninety-and-nine rivers; great is your prowess, strength is deposited in your arms, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Far over ninety spacious floods thy thunderbolts were cast abroad: Great, Indra, is thy hero might, and strength is seated in thine arms, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रं साकमर्चत परि ष्टोभत विंशतिः ।शतैनमन्वनोनवुरिंद्राय ब्रह्मोद्यतमर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: sahásram ǀ sākám ǀ arcata ǀ pári ǀ stobhata ǀ viṃśatíḥ ǀśatā́ ǀ enam ǀ ánu ǀ anonavuḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ bráhma ǀ út-yatam ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Laud him a thousand all at once, shout twenty forth the hymn of praise. Hundreds have sung aloud to him, to Indra hath the prayer been raised, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: A thousand mortals worshipped him together, twenty have hymned (his praise); a hundred (sages) repeatedly glorify him; so,Indra, is the oblation lifted up, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Laud him a thousand all at once, shout twenty forth the hymn of praise. Hundreds have sung aloud to him, to Indra hath the prayer been raised, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो वृत्रस्य तविषीं निरहन्त्सहसा सहः ।महत्तदस्य पौंस्यं वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजदर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ vṛtrásya ǀ táviṣīm ǀ níḥ ǀ ahan ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhaḥ ǀmahát ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ asṛjat ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra hath smitten down the power of Vṛtra,—might with stronger might. This was his manly exploit, he slew Vṛtra and let loose the floods, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraovercame by his strength the strength of Vṛtra; great is his manhood, wherewith, having slain Vṛtra, he lest loose the waters, manifesting his own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra hath smitten down the power of Vṛtra,—might with stronger might. This was his manly exploit, he slew Vṛtra and let loose the floods, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमे चित्तव मन्यवे वेपेते भियसा मही ।यदिंद्र वज्रिन्नोजसा वृत्रं मरुत्वाँ अवधीरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ cit ǀ táva ǀ manyáve ǀ vépete íti ǀ bhiyásā ǀ mahī́ íti ǀyát ǀ indra ǀ vajrin ǀ ójasā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ marútvān ǀ ávadhīḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, even this great Pair of Worlds trembled in terror at thy wrath, When, Indra, Thunderer, Marut-girt, thou slewest Vṛtra in thy strength, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: This heaven and earth trembled, thunderer, at your wrath, when, attended by the Maruts, you slew Vṛtraby your prowess, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, even this great Pair of Worlds trembled in terror at thy wrath, When, Indra, Thunderer, Marut-girt, thou slewest Vṛtra in thy strength, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वेपसा न तन्यतेंद्रं वृत्रो वि बीभयत् ।अभ्येनं वज्र आयसः सहस्रभृष्टिरायतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vépasā ǀ ná ǀ tanyatā́ ǀ índram ǀ vṛtráḥ ǀ ví ǀ bībhayat ǀabhí ǀ enam ǀ vájraḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ sahásra-bhṛṣṭiḥ ǀ āyata ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: But Vṛtra scared not Indra with his shaking or his thunder roar. On him that iron thunderbolt fell fiercely with its thousand points, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: Vṛtradeterred not Indraby his trembling or his clamour; the many-edged iron thunderbolt fell upon him; (Indra) manifesting his own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: But Vṛtra scared not Indra with his shaking or his thunder roar. On him that iron thunderbolt fell fiercely with its thousand points, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वृत्रं तव चाशनिं वज्रेण समयोधयः ।अहिमिंद्र जिघांसतो दिवि ते बद्बधे शवोऽर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vṛtrám ǀ táva ǀ ca ǀ aśánim ǀ vájreṇa ǀ sam-áyodhayaḥ ǀáhim ǀ indra ǀ jíghāṃsataḥ ǀ diví ǀ te ǀ badbadhe ǀ śávaḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When with the thunder thou didst make thy dart and Vṛtra meet in war, Thy might, O Indra, fain to slay the Dragon, was set firm in heaven, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: When you (Indra), did encounter with your bolt Vṛtraand the thunderbolt (which he hurled), then Indra, the strength of you determination to slay Ahi was displayed in the heavens, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: When with the thunder thou didst make thy dart and Vṛtra meet in war, Thy might, O Indra, fain to slay the Dragon, was set firm in heaven, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभिष्टने ते अद्रिवो यत्स्था जगच्च रेजते ।त्वष्टा चित्तव मन्यव इंद्र वेविज्यते भियार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: abhi-stané ǀ te ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ sthā́ḥ ǀ jágat ǀ ca ǀ rejate ǀtváṣṭā ǀ cit ǀ táva ǀ manyáve ǀ índra ǀ vevijyáte ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When at thy shout, O Thunder-armed, each thing both fixed and moving shook, E’en Tvaṣṭar trembled at thy wrath and quaked with fear because of thee, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: At your shout, wielder of the thunderbolt, all things, moveable or immoveable, trembled; even Tvaṣṭāshook with fear,Indra, at your wrath, manifesting your own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: When at thy shout, O Thunder-armed, each thing both fixed and moving shook, E’en Tvaṣṭar trembled at thy wrath and quaked with fear because of thee, lauding thine own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि नु यादधीमसींद्रं को वीर्या परः ।तस्मिन्नृम्णमुत क्रतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ nú ǀ yā́t ǀ adhi-imási ǀ índram ǀ káḥ ǀ vīryā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀtásmin ǀ nṛmṇám ǀ utá ǀ krátum ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ójāṃsi ǀ sám ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: There is not, in our knowledge, one who passeth Indra in his strength: In him the Deities have stored manliness, insight, power and might, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: We know not of a certainty the all-pervading Indra; who (does know him, abiding) afar off in his strength? for in him have the gods concentrated riches, and worship, and power, manifesting his own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: There is not, in our knowledge, one who passeth Indra in his strength: In him the Deities have stored manliness, insight, power and might, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यामथर्वा मनुष्पिता दध्यङ् धियमत्नत ।तस्मिन्ब्रह्माणि पूर्वथेंद्र उक्था समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́m ǀ átharvā ǀ mánuḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ dadhyáṅ ǀ dhíyam ǀ átnata ǀtásmin ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ pūrvá-thā ǀ índre ǀ ukthā́ ǀ sám ǀ agmata ǀ árcan ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Still as of old, whatever rite Atharvan, Manus sire of all, Dadhyach performed, their prayer and praise united in that Indra meet, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as of old, so in whatever act of worship Atharvanor father Manu, or Dadhyañc engaged, their oblations and their hymns were all congregated in that Indra, manifesting his own sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Still as of old, whatever rite Atharvan, Manus sire of all, Dadhyach performed, their prayer and praise united in that Indra meet, lauding his own imperial sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE men have lifted Indra up, the Vṛtra slayer, to joy and strength:Him, verily, we invocate in battles whether great or small: be he our aid in deeds of might. Thou, Hero, art a warrior, thou art giver of abundant spoil.Strengthening e’en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest the offerer ample wealth. When war and battles are on foot, booty is laid before the bold.Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing Bays. Whom wilt thou slay and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich. Mighty through wisdom, as he lists, terrible, he hath waxed in strength.Lord of Bay Steeds, strong-jawed, sublime, he in joined hands for glory's sake hath grasped his iron thunderbolt. He filled the earthly atmosphere and pressed against the lights in heaven.None like thee ever hath been born, none, Indra, will be born like thee. Thou hast waxed mighty over all. May he who to the offerer gives the foeman's man-sustaining food,May Indra lend his aid to us. Deal forth—abundant is thy wealth—that in thy bounty I may share. He, righteous-hearted, at each time of rapture gives us herds of kine.Gather in both thy hands for us treasures of many hundred sorts. Sharpen thou us, and bring us wealth. Refresh thee, Hero, with the juice outpoured for bounty and for strength.We know thee Lord of ample store, to thee have sent our hearts' desires: be therefore our Protector thou. These people, Indra, keep for thee all that is worthy of thy choice.Discover thou, as Lord, the wealth of men who offer up no gifts: bring thou to us this wealth of theirs.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो मदाय वावृधे शवसे वृत्रहा नृभिः ।तमिन्महत्स्वाजिषूतेमर्भे हवामहे स वाजेषु प्र नोऽविषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ mádāya ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ śávase ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ mahát-su ǀ ājíṣu ǀ utá ǀ īm ǀ árbhe ǀ havāmahe ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ aviṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE men have lifted Indra up, the Vṛtra slayer, to joy and strength: Him, verily, we invocate in battles whether great or small: be he our aid in deeds of might.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been augmented in strength and satisfaction by (the adoration of) men; we invoke him in great conflicts as well as in little conflicts; may he defend us in battles.
verses.griffith_verse: THE men have lifted Indra up, the Vṛtra slayer, to joy and strength: Him, verily, we invocate in battles whether great or small: be he our aid in deeds of might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असि हि वीर सेन्योऽसि भूरि पराददिः ।असि दभ्रस्य चिद्वृधो यजमानाय शिक्षसि सुन्वते भूरि ते वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: ási ǀ hí ǀ vīra ǀ sényaḥ ǀ ási ǀ bhū́ri ǀ parā-dadíḥ ǀási ǀ dabhrásya ǀ cit ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śikṣasi ǀ sunvaté ǀ bhū́ri ǀ te ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Hero, art a warrior, thou art giver of abundant spoil. Strengthening e’en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest the offerer ample wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: For you, here,Indra, are a host; you are the giver of much booty; you are the exalter of the humble; you bestow (riches) on the worshipper who offers you oblations, for abundant is your wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Hero, art a warrior, thou art giver of abundant spoil. Strengthening e’en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest the offerer ample wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदुदीरत आजयो धृष्णवे धीयते धना ।युक्ष्वा मदच्युता हरी कं हनः कं वसौ दधोऽस्माँ इंद्र वसौ दधः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ut-ī́rate ǀ ājáyaḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇáve ǀ dhīyate ǀ dhánā ǀyukṣvá ǀ mada-cyútā ǀ hárī íti ǀ kám ǀ hánaḥ ǀ kám ǀ vásau ǀ dadhaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ indra ǀ vásau ǀ dadhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When war and battles are on foot, booty is laid before the bold. Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing Bays. Whom wilt thou slay and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich.
verses.wilson_translation: When battles arise, wealth devolves on the victor; yoke your horses, humblers of the pride (of the foe), that you may destroy one and enrich another; plural ce us,Indra, in affluence.
verses.griffith_verse: When war and battles are on foot, booty is laid before the bold. Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing Bays. Whom wilt thou slay and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्रत्वा महाँ अनुष्वधं भीम आ वावृधे शवः ।श्रिय ऋष्व उपाकयोर्नि शिप्री हरिवांदधे हस्तयोर्वज्रमायसं ॥
verses.transliteration: krátvā ǀ mahā́n ǀ anu-svadhám ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ śávaḥ ǀśriyé ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀ upākáyoḥ ǀ ní ǀ śiprī́ ǀ hári-vān ǀ dadhe ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ vájram ǀ āyasám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty through wisdom, as he lists, terrible, he hath waxed in strength. Lord of Bay Steeds, strong-jawed, sublime, he in joined hands for glory's sake hath grasped his iron thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty through sacrifice, formidable (to foes), partaking of the sacrificial food,Indrahas augmented his strength; plural asing in appearance, having a handsome chin, and possessing (bright) coursers, he grasps the metal thunder-bolt in his contiguoushandsfor (our) prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty through wisdom, as he lists, terrible, he hath waxed in strength. Lord of Bay Steeds, strong-jawed, sublime, he in joined hands for glory's sake hath grasped his iron thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ पप्रौ पार्थिवं रजो बद्बधे रोचना दिवि ।न त्वावाँ इंद्र कश्चन न जातो न जनिष्यतेऽति विश्वं ववक्षिथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ paprau ǀ pā́rthivam ǀ rájaḥ ǀ badbadhé ǀ rocanā́ ǀ diví ǀná ǀ tvā́-vān ǀ indra ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǀ ná ǀ jātáḥ ǀ ná ǀ janiṣyate ǀ áti ǀ víśvam ǀ vavakṣitha ǁ
verses.english_translation: He filled the earthly atmosphere and pressed against the lights in heaven. None like thee ever hath been born, none, Indra, will be born like thee. Thou hast waxed mighty over all.
verses.wilson_translation: He has filled the space of earth and the firmament (with his glory); he has fixed the constellations in the sky; no one has been ever born, now will be born,Indra, like you; you have sustained the universe.
verses.griffith_verse: He filled the earthly atmosphere and pressed against the lights in heaven. None like thee ever hath been born, none, Indra, will be born like thee. Thou hast waxed mighty over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अर्यो मर्तभोजनं पराददाति दाशुषे ।इंद्रो अस्मभ्यं शिक्षतु वि भजा भूरि ते वसु भक्षीय तव राधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ marta-bhójanam ǀ parā-dádāti ǀ dāśúṣe ǀíndraḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ śikṣatu ǀ ví ǀ bhaja ǀ bhū́ri ǀ te ǀ vásu ǀ bhakṣīyá ǀ táva ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he who to the offerer gives the foeman's man-sustaining food, May Indra lend his aid to us. Deal forth—abundant is thy wealth—that in thy bounty I may share.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, the protector, who returns to the giver (of oblations) the food that is fit for mortals, bestow (such food) on us; distribute your wealth, which is abundant, so that I may obtain (a portion) of your riches.
verses.griffith_verse: May he who to the offerer gives the foeman's man-sustaining food, May Indra lend his aid to us. Deal forth—abundant is thy wealth—that in thy bounty I may share.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मदेमदे हि नो ददिर्यूथा गवामृजुक्रतुः ।सं गृभाय पुरू शतोभयाहस्त्या वसु शिशीहि राय आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: máde-made ǀ hí ǀ naḥ ǀ dadíḥ ǀ yūthā́ ǀ gávām ǀ ṛju-krátuḥ ǀsám ǀ gṛbhāya ǀ purú ǀ śatā́ ǀ ubhayāhastyā́ ǀ vásu ǀ śiśīhí ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, righteous-hearted, at each time of rapture gives us herds of kine. Gather in both thy hands for us treasures of many hundred sorts. Sharpen thou us, and bring us wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: The upright performer of (pious) acts is the donor of herds of cattle to us, when receiving frequent enjoyment (from our libations); take up,Indra, with bothhands, many hundred (sorts) of treasure; sharpen (our intellects), bring us wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: He, righteous-hearted, at each time of rapture gives us herds of kine. Gather in both thy hands for us treasures of many hundred sorts. Sharpen thou us, and bring us wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मादयस्व सुते सचा शवसे शूर राधसे ।विद्मा हि त्वा पुरूवसुमुप कामान्त्ससृज्महेऽथा नोऽविता भव ॥
verses.transliteration: mādáyasva ǀ suté ǀ sácā ǀ śávase ǀ śūra ǀ rā́dhase ǀvidmá ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ puru-vásum ǀ úpa ǀ kā́mān ǀ sasṛjmáhe ǀ átha ǀ naḥ ǀ avitā́ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Refresh thee, Hero, with the juice outpoured for bounty and for strength. We know thee Lord of ample store, to thee have sent our hearts' desires: be therefore our Protector thou.
verses.wilson_translation: Enjoy along with us, O hero, the suffused libation for (the increase of our) strength and wealth; we know you (to be) the possessor of vast riches, and address to our desires; be, therefore, our protector.
verses.griffith_verse: Refresh thee, Hero, with the juice outpoured for bounty and for strength. We know thee Lord of ample store, to thee have sent our hearts' desires: be therefore our Protector thou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एते त इंद्र जंतवो विश्वं पुष्यंति वार्यं ।अंतर्हि ख्यो जनानामर्यो वेदो अदाशुषां तेषां नो वेद आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ jantávaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ puṣyanti ǀ vā́ryam ǀantáḥ ǀ hí ǀ khyáḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ aryáḥ ǀ védaḥ ǀ ádāśuṣām ǀ téṣām ǀ naḥ ǀ védaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: These people, Indra, keep for thee all that is worthy of thy choice. Discover thou, as Lord, the wealth of men who offer up no gifts: bring thou to us this wealth of theirs.
verses.wilson_translation: These, your creatures,Indra, cherish (the oblation) that may be partaken of by all; you, lord of all, know what are the riches of those men who make no offerings; bring their wealth to us.
verses.griffith_verse: These people, Indra, keep for thee all that is worthy of thy choice. Discover thou, as Lord, the wealth of men who offer up no gifts: bring thou to us this wealth of theirs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GRACIOUSLY listen to our songs, Maghavan, be not negligent.As thou hast made us full of joy and lettest us solicit thee, now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds. Well have they eaten and rejoiced; the friends have risen and passed away.The sages luminous in themselves have. praised thee with their latest hymn. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds. Maghavan, we will reverence thee who art so fair to look upon.Thus praised, according to our wish come now with richly laden car. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds. He will in very truth ascend the powerful car that finds the kine,Who thinks upon the well-filled bowl, the Tawny Coursers' harnesser. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds. Let, Lord of Hundred Powers, thy Steeds be harnessed on the right and left.Therewith in rapture of the juice, draw near to thy beloved Spouse. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds. With holy prayer I yoke thy long-maned pair of Bays: come hitherward; thou holdest them in both thy hands.The stirring draughts of juice outpoured have made thee glad: thou, Thunderer, hast rejoiced with Pūṣan and thy Spouse.

verses.sanskrit: उपो षु शृणुही गिरो मघवन्मातथा इव ।यदा नः सूनृतावतः कर आदर्थयास इद्योजा न्विंद्र ते हरी ॥
verses.transliteration: úpo íti ǀ sú ǀ śṛṇuhí ǀ gíraḥ ǀ mágha-van ǀ mā́ ǀ átathāḥ-iva ǀyadā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sūnṛ́tā-vataḥ ǀ káraḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ artháyāse ǀ ít ǀ yója ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: GRACIOUSLY listen to our songs, Maghavan, be not negligent. As thou hast made us full of joy and lettest us solicit thee, now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Approach,Maghavan, and listen to our praises; be not different (from what you have hitherto been) since you have inspired us with true speech, you are solicited with it; therefore, quickly yoke your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: GRACIOUSLY listen to our songs, Maghavan, be not negligent. As thou hast made us full of joy and lettest us solicit thee, now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षन्नमीमदंत ह्यव प्रिया अधूषत ।अस्तोषत स्वभानवो विप्रा नविष्ठया मती योजा न्विंद्र ते हरी ॥
verses.transliteration: ákṣan ǀ ámīmadanta ǀ hí ǀ áva ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ adhūṣata ǀástoṣata ǀ svá-bhānavaḥ ǀ víprāḥ ǀ náviṣṭhayā ǀ matī́ ǀ yója ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well have they eaten and rejoiced; the friends have risen and passed away. The sages luminous in themselves have. praised thee with their latest hymn. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: (Your worshippers) have eaten the food which you had given, and have rejoiced, and have trembled through their precious (bodies); self-illuminated sages have glorified you with commendable thoughts; therefore,Indra, quickly yoke your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Well have they eaten and rejoiced; the friends have risen and passed away. The sages luminous in themselves have. praised thee with their latest hymn. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुसंदृशं त्वा वयं मघवन्वंदिषीमहि ।प्र नूनं पूर्णवंधुरः स्तुतो याहि वशाँ अनु योजा न्विंद्र ते हरी ॥
verses.transliteration: su-saṃdṛ́śam ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ mágha-van ǀ vandiṣīmáhi ǀprá ǀ nūnám ǀ pūrṇá-vandhuraḥ ǀ stutáḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ váśān ǀ ánu ǀ yója ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavan, we will reverence thee who art so fair to look upon. Thus praised, according to our wish come now with richly laden car. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: We praise you,Maghavan, who look benignly (upon all); thus praised by us, repair (in your car), filled with treasure, to those who desire your presence;Indra, quickly yoke your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Maghavan, we will reverence thee who art so fair to look upon. Thus praised, according to our wish come now with richly laden car. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स घा तं वृषणं रथमधि तिष्ठाति गोविदं ।यः पात्रं हारियोजनं पूर्णमिंद्र चिकेतति योजा न्विंद्र ते हरी ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ gha ǀ tám ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ rátham ǀ ádhi ǀ tiṣṭhāti ǀ go-vídam ǀyáḥ ǀ pā́tram ǀ hāri-yojanám ǀ pūrṇám ǀ indra ǀ cíketati ǀ yója ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: He will in very truth ascend the powerful car that finds the kine, Who thinks upon the well-filled bowl, the Tawny Coursers' harnesser. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May he ascend that chariot which rains (blessings), and grants cattle, and which provides the vessel filled with the mixture of Somaand grain; quickly,Indra, yoke your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: He will in very truth ascend the powerful car that finds the kine, Who thinks upon the well-filled bowl, the Tawny Coursers' harnesser. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युक्तस्ते अस्तु दक्षिण उत सव्यः शतक्रतो ।तेन जायामुप प्रियां मंदानो याह्यंधसो योजा न्विंद्र ते हरी ॥
verses.transliteration: yuktáḥ ǀ te ǀ astu ǀ dákṣiṇaḥ ǀ utá ǀ savyáḥ ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀténa ǀ jāyā́m ǀ úpa ǀ priyā́m ǀ mandānáḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ yója ǀ nú ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let, Lord of Hundred Powers, thy Steeds be harnessed on the right and left. Therewith in rapture of the juice, draw near to thy beloved Spouse. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Performer of many (holy) acts, let your steeds be harnessed on the right and on the left, and when exhilarated by the (sacrificial) food, repair in your chariot to your beloved wife; quickly,Indra, yoke your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Let, Lord of Hundred Powers, thy Steeds be harnessed on the right and left. Therewith in rapture of the juice, draw near to thy beloved Spouse. Now, Indra, yoke thy two Bay Steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युनज्मि ते ब्रह्मणा केशिना हरी उप प्र याहि दधिषे गभस्त्योः ।उत्त्वा सुतासो रभसा अमंदिषुः पूषण्वान्वज्रिन्त्समु पत्न्यामदः ॥
verses.transliteration: yunájmi ǀ te ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ keśínā ǀ hárī íti ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ dadhiṣé ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀút ǀ tvā ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ rabhasā́ḥ ǀ amandiṣuḥ ǀ pūṣaṇ-vā́n ǀ vajrin ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ pátnyā ǀ amadaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With holy prayer I yoke thy long-maned pair of Bays: come hitherward; thou holdest them in both thy hands. The stirring draughts of juice outpoured have made thee glad: thou, Thunderer, hast rejoiced with Pūṣan and thy Spouse.
verses.wilson_translation: I harness your long-maned steeds wiht (sacred prayers); depart; take the reins in yourhands; the effused and exciting juices have exhilarated you wilder of the thunderbolt; thus filled with nutriment, rejoice with your spouse.
verses.griffith_verse: With holy prayer I yoke thy long-maned pair of Bays: come hitherward; thou holdest them in both thy hands. The stirring draughts of juice outpoured have made thee glad: thou, Thunderer, hast rejoiced with Pūṣan and thy Spouse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INDRA, the mortal man well guarded by thine aid goes foremost in the wealth of horses and of kine.With amplest wealth thou fillest him, as round about the waters clearly seen afar fill Sindhu full. The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread:The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer. Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife.Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts. First the Aṅgirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice.The men together found the Paṇi's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.
