Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun.Uśanā Kāvya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth. When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky.Where the stone rings as ’twere a singer skilled in laud,—Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावति प्रथमो गोषु गच्छति सुप्रावीरिंद्र मर्त्यस्तवोतिभिः ।तमित्पृणक्षि वसुना भवीयसा सिंधुमापो यथाभितो विचेतसः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśva-vati ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ gacchati ǀ supra-avī́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ táva ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ pṛṇakṣi ǀ vásunā ǀ bhávīyasā ǀ síndhum ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ ví-cetasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: INDRA, the mortal man well guarded by thine aid goes foremost in the wealth of horses and of kine. With amplest wealth thou fillest him, as round about the waters clearly seen afar fill Sindhu full.
verses.wilson_translation: The man who is well protected,Indra, by your cares, (and dwells) in a mansion where there are horses, is the first who goes to (that where there are) cows; enrich him with abundant riches, as the unconscious rivers flow in all directions to the ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: INDRA, the mortal man well guarded by thine aid goes foremost in the wealth of horses and of kine. With amplest wealth thou fillest him, as round about the waters clearly seen afar fill Sindhu full.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो न देवीरुप यंति होत्रियमवः पश्यंति विततं यथा रजः ।प्राचैर्देवासः प्र णयंति देवयुं ब्रह्मप्रियं जोषयंते वरा इव ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yanti ǀ hotríyam ǀ aváḥ ǀ paśyanti ǀ ví-tatam ǀ yáthā ǀ rájaḥ ǀprācáiḥ ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ prá ǀ nayanti ǀ deva-yúm ǀ brahma-príyam ǀ joṣayante ǀ varā́ḥ-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread: The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner, as the bright waters flow to the sacrificial ladle, so they (the gods) look down (upon it); as the diffusive light (descends to earth), the gods convey it, desirous of being presented to them by progressive (movements to the altar), and are impatient to enjoy it, filled with the oblation, as bridegrooms (long for their brides).
verses.griffith_verse: The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread: The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधि द्वयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वचो यतस्रुचा मिथुना या सपर्यतः ।असंयत्तो व्रते ते क्षेति पुष्यति भद्रा शक्तिर्यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ dváyoḥ ǀ adadhāḥ ǀ ukthyám ǀ vácaḥ ǀ yatá-srucā ǀ mithunā́ ǀ yā́ ǀ saparyátaḥ ǀásam-yattaḥ ǀ vraté ǀ te ǀ kṣeti ǀ púṣyati ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ śaktíḥ ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife. Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: You have associated,Indra, words of sacred praise with both (the grain and butter of oblation), plural ced together in ladles and jointly presented to you, so that (the sacrificer), undisturbed, remains (engaged) in your worship, and is prosperous; for to the sacrificer pouring out oblations (to you), auspicious power is granted.
verses.griffith_verse: Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife. Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदंगिराः प्रथमं दधिरे वय इद्धाग्नयः शम्या ये सुकृत्यया ।सर्वं पणेः समविंदंत भोजनमश्वावंतं गोमंतमा पशुं नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ áṅgirāḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ dadhire ǀ váyaḥ ǀ iddhá-agnayaḥ ǀ śámyā ǀ yé ǀ su-kṛtyáyā ǀsárvam ǀ paṇéḥ ǀ sám ǀ avindanta ǀ bhójanam ǀ áśva-vantam ǀ gó-mantam ǀ ā́ ǀ paśúm ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: First the Aṅgirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice. The men together found the Paṇi's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.
verses.wilson_translation: The Aṅgirasasfirst prepared (for Indra) the sacrificial food, and then, with kindled fire, (worshipped him) with a most holy rite; they, the instrumental tutors (of the ceremony); acquired all the wealth of Paṇi, comprising horses, and cows, and (other) animals.
verses.griffith_verse: First the Aṅgirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice. The men together found the Paṇi's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमः पथस्तते ततः सूर्यो व्रतपा वेन आजनि ।आ गा आजदुशना काव्यः सचा यमस्य जातममृतं यजामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñáiḥ ǀ átharvā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ patháḥ ǀ tate ǀ tátaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ vrata-pā́ḥ ǀ venáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ajani ǀā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ājat ǀ uśánā ǀ kāvyáḥ ǀ sácā ǀ yamásya ǀ jātám ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ yajāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun. Uśanā Kāvya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth.
verses.wilson_translation: Atharvanfirst by sacrifices discovered the path (of the stolen cattle); then the bright sun, the cherisher of pious acts, was born. Atharvan regained the cattle;Kāvya(Uṣanās) was associated with him. Let us worship the immortal (Indra), who was born to restrain (theasuras).
verses.griffith_verse: Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun. Uśanā Kāvya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बर्हिर्वा यत्स्वपत्याय वृज्यतेऽर्को वा श्लोकमाघोषते दिवि ।ग्रावा यत्र वदति कारुरुक्थ्यस्तस्येदिंद्रो अभिपित्वेषु रण्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: barhíḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ su-apatyā́ya ǀ vṛjyáte ǀ arkáḥ ǀ vā ǀ ślókam ǀ ā-ghóṣate ǀ diví ǀgrā́vā ǀ yátra ǀ vádati ǀ kārúḥ ǀ ukthyáḥ ǀ tásya ǀ ít ǀ índraḥ ǀ abhi-pitvéṣu ǀ raṇyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky. Where the stone rings as ’twere a singer skilled in laud,—Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether the holy grass be cut (for the rite) that brings down blessings, whether the priest repeats (the sacred) verse in the brilliant (sacrifice), whether the stone (that expresses the Soma) sound like the priest who repeats the hymn, on all these occasions Indrarejoices.
verses.griffith_verse: When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky. Where the stone rings as ’twere a singer skilled in laud,—Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come.May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays. His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted mightHither to Ṛṣis’ songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men. Slayer of Vṛtra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer.May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward. This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent.Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law. Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies.The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme. When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer:None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o’ertaken thee. He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts,The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure. When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him?When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise? He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,—Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might. The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink,Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy. Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk.The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy. With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might,They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in theirown supremacy. With bones of Dadhyach for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack,Struck nine-and-ninety Vṛtras dead. He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, foundAt Śaryaṇāvān what he sought. Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvaṣṭar's Bull,Here in the mansion of the Moon. Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit,With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing?Long shall he live who richly pays their service. Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us?Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People? Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons?To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly? Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man.O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee. Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time;And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.

verses.sanskrit: असावि सोम इंद्र ते शविष्ठ धृष्णवा गहि ।आ त्वा पृणक्त्विंद्रियं रजः सूर्यो न रश्मिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ásāvi ǀ sómaḥ ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ śáviṣṭha ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ pṛṇaktu ǀ indriyám ǀ rájaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come. May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays.
verses.wilson_translation: The Somahas been expressed,Indra, for you; potent humber (of your foes), approach; may vigour fill you (by Soma), as the sun fills the firmament with his rays.
verses.griffith_verse: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come. May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रमिद्धरी वहतोऽप्रतिधृष्टशवसं ।ऋषीणां च स्तुतीरुप यज्ञं च मानुषाणां ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ ít ǀ hárī íti ǀ vahataḥ ǀ ápratidhṛṣṭa-śavasam ǀṛ́ṣīṇām ǀ ca ǀ stutī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yajñám ǀ ca ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted might Hither to Ṛṣis’ songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.
verses.wilson_translation: May his horses bear Indra, who is of irresistible prowess, to the praises and sacrifices of sages and of men.
verses.griffith_verse: His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted might Hither to Ṛṣis’ songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तिष्ठ वृत्रहन्रथं युक्ता ते ब्रह्मणा हरी ।अर्वाचीनं सु ते मनो ग्रावा कृणोतु वग्नुना ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ rátham ǀ yuktā́ ǀ te ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ hárī íti ǀarvācī́nam ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ grā́vā ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ vagnúnā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer. May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward.
verses.wilson_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, ascend your chariot, for your horses have been yoked by prayer; may the stone (that bruises the Soma) attract, by its sound, your mind towards us.
verses.griffith_verse: Slayer of Vṛtra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer. May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इममिंद्र सुतं पिब ज्येष्ठममर्त्यं मदं ।शुक्रस्य त्वाभ्यक्षरंधारा ऋतस्य सादने ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ indra ǀ sutám ǀ piba ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ ámartyam ǀ mádam ǀśukrásya ǀ tvā ǀ abhí ǀ akṣaran ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ sádane ǁ
verses.english_translation: This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent. Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indra, this excellent, immortal exhilarating libation, the dropf of which pellucid (beverage) flow towards you in the chamber of sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent. Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राय नूनमर्चतोक्थानि च ब्रवीतन ।सुता अमत्सुरिंदवो ज्येष्ठं नमस्यता सहः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāya ǀ nūnám ǀ arcata ǀ ukthā́ni ǀ ca ǀ bravītana ǀsutā́ḥ ǀ amatsuḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ namasyata ǀ sáhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies. The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer worship quickly to Indra; recite hymns (in his praise); let the effused drops exhilarate him; pay adoration to his superior strength.
verses.griffith_verse: Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies. The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नकिष्ट्वद्रथीतरो हरी यदिंद्र यच्छसे ।नकिष्ट्वानु मज्मना नकिः स्वश्व आनशे ॥
verses.transliteration: nákiḥ ǀ tvát ǀ rathí-taraḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ yácchase ǀnákiḥ ǀ tvā ǀ ánu ǀ majmánā ǀ nákiḥ ǀ su-áśvaḥ ǀ ānaśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer: None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o’ertaken thee.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Indra, you harness your horses, there is no one a better charioteer than you; no one is equal to you in strength; no one, although well-horsed, has overtaken you.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer: None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o’ertaken thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य एक इद्विदयते वसु मर्ताय दाशुषे ।ईशानो अप्रतिष्कुत इंद्रो अंग ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ vi-dáyate ǀ vásu ǀ mártāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀī́śānaḥ ǀ áprati-skutaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ aṅgá ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts, The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure.
verses.wilson_translation: He who alone bestows wealth upon the man who offers him oblations, is the undisputed sovereign,Indra--ho!
verses.griffith_verse: He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts, The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कदा मर्तमराधसं पदा क्षुंपमिव स्फुरत् ।कदा नः शुश्रवद्गिर इंद्रो अंग ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ mártam ǀ arādhásam ǀ padā́ ǀ kṣúmpam-iva ǀ sphurat ǀkadā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ śuśravat ǀ gíraḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ aṅgá ǁ
verses.english_translation: When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him? When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?
verses.wilson_translation: When all he trample with his foot upon the man who offers no oblations, as if upon a coiled-up snake; when will Indralisten to our praises? ho!
verses.griffith_verse: When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him? When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यश्चिद्धि त्वा बहुभ्य आ सुतावाँ आविवासति ।उग्रं तत्पत्यते शव इंद्रो अंग ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ bahú-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sutá-vān ǀ ā-vívāsati ǀugrám ǀ tát ǀ patyate ǀ śávaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ aṅgá ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,— Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, grant formidable strength to him who worships him, having libations prepared--ho!
verses.griffith_verse: He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,— Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वादोरित्था विषूवतो मध्वः पिबंति गौर्यः ।या इंद्रेण सयावरीर्वृष्णा मदंति शोभसे वस्वीरनु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: svādóḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ viṣu-vátaḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ pibanti ǀ gauryáḥ ǀyā́ḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ sa-yā́varīḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣṇā ǀ mádanti ǀ śobháse ǀ vásvīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink, Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
verses.wilson_translation: The white cows drink of the sweet Somathus poured forth, and associated with the bountiful Indra, for the sake of beauty, rejoice; abiding (in their stalls), they are expectant of his sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink, Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता अस्य पृशनायुवः सोमं श्रीणंति पृश्नयः ।प्रिया इंद्रस्य धेनवो वज्रं हिन्वंति सायकं वस्वीरनु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ pṛśana-yúvaḥ ǀ sómam ǀ śrīṇanti ǀ pṛ́śnayaḥ ǀpriyā́ḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ vájram ǀ hinvanti ǀ sā́yakam ǀ vásvīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of his contact, those bridled cows dilute the Somawith their milk; the kine that are loved of Indradirect his destructive thunderbolt against his foes, abiding (in their stalls) expectant of his sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता अस्य नमसा सहः सपर्यंति प्रचेतसः ।व्रतान्यस्य सश्चिरे पुरूणि पूर्वचित्तये वस्वीरनु स्वराज्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ námasā ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ saparyánti ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀvratā́ni ǀ asya ǀ saścire ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ pūrvá-cittaye ǀ vásvīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sva-rā́jyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might, They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
verses.wilson_translation: These intelligent kine reverence his prowess with the adoration (of their milk); they celebrate his manly exploits as an example to later (adversaries); abiding (in their stalls), expectant of his sovereignty.
verses.griffith_verse: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might, They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो दधीचो अस्थभिर्वृत्राण्यप्रतिष्कुतः ।जघान नवतीर्नव ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ dadhīcáḥ ǀ asthá-bhiḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ áprati-skutaḥ ǀjaghā́na ǀ navatī́ḥ ǀ náva ǁ
verses.english_translation: With bones of Dadhyach for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack, Struck nine-and-ninety Vṛtras dead.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, with the bones of Dadhīci, slew ninety times nine Vṛtras.
verses.griffith_verse: With bones of Dadhyach for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack, Struck nine-and-ninety Vṛtras dead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इच्छन्नश्वस्य यच्छिरः पर्वतेष्वपश्रितं ।तद्विदच्छर्यणावति ॥
verses.transliteration: icchán ǀ áśvasya ǀ yát ǀ śíraḥ ǀ párvateṣu ǀ ápa-śritam ǀtát ǀ vidat ǀ śaryaṇā́-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, found At Śaryaṇāvān what he sought.
verses.wilson_translation: Wishing for the horse's head hidden in the mountains, he found is Śaryaṇāvat.
verses.griffith_verse: He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, found At Śaryaṇāvān what he sought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अत्राह गोरमन्वत नाम त्वष्टुरपीच्यं ।इत्था चंद्रमसो गृहे ॥
verses.transliteration: átra ǀ áha ǀ góḥ ǀ amanvata ǀ nā́ma ǀ tváṣṭuḥ ǀ apīcyám ǀitthā́ ǀ candrámasaḥ ǀ gṛhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvaṣṭar's Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
verses.wilson_translation: The (solar rays) found on this occasion the light of Tvaṣṭāverily concealed in the mansion of the moving moon.
verses.griffith_verse: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvaṣṭar's Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को अद्य युंक्ते धुरि गा ऋतस्य शिमीवतो भामिनो दुर्हृणायून् ।आसन्निषून्हृत्स्वसो मयोभून्य एषां भृत्यामृणधत्स जीवात् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ adyá ǀ yuṅkte ǀ dhurí ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ śímī-vataḥ ǀ bhāmínaḥ ǀ duḥ-hṛṇāyū́n ǀāsán-iṣūn ǀ hṛtsu-ásaḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhū́n ǀ yáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ bhṛtyā́m ǀ ṛṇádhat ǀ sáḥ ǀ jīvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit, With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing? Long shall he live who richly pays their service.
verses.wilson_translation: Who yokes todya to the pole of the car (of Indra) his vigorous and radiant steeds, whose fury is unbearable, in whose mouths are arrows, who trample on the hearts (of enemies), who give happiness (to friends). (The sacrificer) who praises their (performance of their) duties obtains (long) life.
verses.griffith_verse: Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit, With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing? Long shall he live who richly pays their service.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क ईषते तुज्यते को बिभाय को मंसते संतमिंद्रं को अंति ।कस्तोकाय क इभायोत रायेऽधि ब्रवत्तन्वे को जनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ īṣate ǀ tujyáte ǀ káḥ ǀ bibhāya ǀ káḥ ǀ maṃsate ǀ sántam ǀ índram ǀ káḥ ǀ ánti ǀkáḥ ǀ tokā́ya ǀ káḥ ǀ íbhāya ǀ utá ǀ rāyé ǀ ádhi ǀ bravat ǀ tanvé ǀ káḥ ǀ jánāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us? Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People?
verses.wilson_translation: Who goes forth, (through dread of foes, when Indrais athand); who is harmed (by his enemies); who is terrified; who is aware that Indra is present, who that he is night? What need is there that any one should importune Indra for his son, his elephant, his property, his person n, or his people?
verses.griffith_verse: Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us? Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को अग्निमीट्टे हविषा घृतेन स्रुचा यजाता ऋतुभिर्ध्रुवेभिः ।कस्मै देवा आ वहानाशु होम को मंसते वीतिहोत्रः सुदेवः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ agním ǀ īṭṭe ǀ havíṣā ǀ ghṛténa ǀ srucā́ ǀ yajātai ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǀ dhruvébhiḥ ǀkásmai ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vahān ǀ āśú ǀ hóma ǀ káḥ ǀ maṃsate ǀ vītí-hotraḥ ǀ su-deváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons? To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly?
verses.wilson_translation: Who praises the (sacrificial) fire, (lighted for Indra), or worships him with the oblation of clarified butter, presented in the ladle, according to the constant seasons? To whom do the gods quickly bring (the wealth) that has been called for? What sacrificer, engaged in offering oblations and favoured by the gods, thoroughly knows Indra?
verses.griffith_verse: Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons? To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमंग प्र शंसिषो देवः शविष्ठ मर्त्यं ।न त्वदन्यो मघवन्नस्ति मर्डितेंद्र ब्रवीमि ते वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ aṅgá ǀ prá ǀ śaṃsiṣaḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ mártyam ǀná ǀ tvát ǀ anyáḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ asti ǀ marḍitā́ ǀ índra ǀ brávīmi ǀ te ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man. O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful,Indra, be present and be favourable to the mortal (who adores you); there is no other giver of felicity,Maghavan, than you; hence, Indra, I recite your praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man. O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा ते राधांसि मा त ऊतयो वसोऽस्मान्कदा चना दभन् ।विश्वा च न उपमिमीहि मानुष वसूनि चर्षणिभ्य आ ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ te ǀ rā́dhāṃsi ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ vaso íti ǀ asmā́n ǀ kádā ǀ caná ǀ dabhan ǀvíśvā ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ upa-mimīhí ǀ mānuṣa ǀ vásūni ǀ carṣaṇí-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time; And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.
verses.wilson_translation: Granter of dwellings, let not your treasury, let not your benefits, ever be detrimental to us. Friend of mankind, bring to us, who are acquainted with prayers, all sorts of riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time; And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXV. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THEY who are glancing forth, like women, on their way, doers of mighty deeds, swift racers, Rudra's Sons,The Maruts have made heaven and earth increase and grow: in sacrifices they delight, the strong and wild. Grown to their perfect strength greatness have they attained; the Rudras have established their abode in heaven.Singing their song of praise and generating might, they have put glory on, the Sons whom Pṛśni bare. When, Children of the Cow, they shine in bright attire, and on their fair limbs lay their golden ornaments,They drive away each adversary from their path, and, following their traces, fatness floweth down, When, mighty Warriors, ye who glitter with your spears, o’erthrowing with your strength e’en what is ne’er o’erthrown,When, O ye Maruts, ye the host that send the rain, had harnessed to your cars the thought-fleet spotted deer. When ye have harnessed to your cars the spotted deer, urging the thunderbolt, O Maruts, to the fray,Forth rush the torrents of the dark red stormy cloud, and moisten, like a skin, the earth with water-floods. Let your swift-gliding coursers bear you hitherward with their fleet pinions. Come ye forward with your arms.Sit on the grass; a wide seat hath been made for you: delight yourselves, O Maruts, in the pleasant food. Strong in their native strength to greatness have they grown, stepped to the firmament and made their dwelling wide.When Viṣṇu saved the Soma bringing wild delight, the Maruts sate like birds on their dear holy grass. In sooth like heroes fain for fight they rush about, like combatants fame-seeking have they striven in war.Before the Maruts every creature is afraid: the men are like to Kings, terrible to behold. When Tvaṣṭar deft of hand had turned the thunderbolt, golden, with thousand edges, fashioned more skilfully,Indra received it to perform heroic deeds. Vṛtra he slew, and forced the flood of water forth. They with their vigorous strength pushed the well up on high, and clove the cloud in twain though it was passing strong.The Maruts, bounteous Givers, sending forth their voice, in the wild joy of Soma wrought their glorious deeds. They drave the cloud transverse directed hitherward, and poured the fountain forth for thirsting Gotama.Shining with varied light they come to him with help: they with their might fulfilled the longing of the sage. The shelters which ye have for him who lauds you, bestow them threefold on the man who offers.Extend the same boons unto us, ye Maruts. Give us, O Heroes, wealth with noble offspring.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ये शुंभंते जनयो न सप्तयो यामन्रुद्रस्य सूनवः सुदंससः ।रोदसी हि मरुतश्चक्रिरे वृधे मदंति वीरा विदथेषु घृष्वयः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ śúmbhante ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sáptayaḥ ǀ yā́man ǀ rudrásya ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ su-dáṃsasaḥ ǀródasī íti ǀ hí ǀ marútaḥ ǀ cakriré ǀ vṛdhé ǀ mádanti ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ ghṛ́ṣvayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THEY who are glancing forth, like women, on their way, doers of mighty deeds, swift racers, Rudra's Sons, The Maruts have made heaven and earth increase and grow: in sacrifices they delight, the strong and wild.
verses.wilson_translation: The Marutswho are going forth decorate themselves like feminine les; they are gliders (through the air), the sons of Rudra, and doers of good works by which they promote the welfare of earth and heaven; heroes, who grind (solid rocks), they delight in sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: THEY who are glancing forth, like women, on their way, doers of mighty deeds, swift racers, Rudra's Sons, The Maruts have made heaven and earth increase and grow: in sacrifices they delight, the strong and wild.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त उक्षितासो महिमानमाशत दिवि रुद्रासो अधि चक्रिरे सदः ।अर्चंतो अर्कं जनयंत इंद्रियमधि श्रियो दधिरे पृश्निमातरः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ukṣitā́saḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ āśata ǀ diví ǀ rudrā́saḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ cakrire ǀ sádaḥ ǀárcantaḥ ǀ arkám ǀ janáyantaḥ ǀ indriyám ǀ ádhi ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grown to their perfect strength greatness have they attained; the Rudras have established their abode in heaven. Singing their song of praise and generating might, they have put glory on, the Sons whom Pṛśni bare.
verses.wilson_translation: They, inaugurated by the gods, have attained majesty; the sons of Rudrahave established their dwelling above the sky; glorify him (Indra) who merits to be glorified, they have inspired him with vigour; the sons of Pṛśnihave acquired dominion.
verses.griffith_verse: Grown to their perfect strength greatness have they attained; the Rudras have established their abode in heaven. Singing their song of praise and generating might, they have put glory on, the Sons whom Pṛśni bare.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गोमातरो यच्छुभयंते अंजिभिस्तनूषु शुभ्रा दधिरे विरुक्मतः ।बाधंते विश्वमभिमातिनमप वर्त्मान्येषामनु रीयते घृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: gó-mātaraḥ ǀ yát ǀ śubháyante ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ śubhrā́ḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ virúkmataḥ ǀbā́dhante ǀ víśvam ǀ abhi-mātínam ǀ ápa ǀ vártmāni ǀ eṣām ǀ ánu ǀ rīyate ǀ ghṛtám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Children of the Cow, they shine in bright attire, and on their fair limbs lay their golden ornaments, They drive away each adversary from their path, and, following their traces, fatness floweth down,
verses.wilson_translation: When the sonf of earth embellish themselves with ornaments, they shine resplendent in their person ns with (brilliant) decorations; they keep aloof every adversary; the waters follow their path.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Children of the Cow, they shine in bright attire, and on their fair limbs lay their golden ornaments, They drive away each adversary from their path, and, following their traces, fatness floweth down,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि ये भ्राजंते सुमखास ऋष्टिभिः प्रच्यावयंतो अच्युता चिदोजसा ।मनोजुवो यन्मरुतो रथेष्वा वृषव्रातासः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yé ǀ bhrā́jante ǀ sú-makhāsaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀ pra-cyaváyantaḥ ǀ ácyutā ǀ cit ǀ ójasā ǀmanaḥ-júvaḥ ǀ yát ǀ marutaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-vrātāsaḥ ǀ pṛ́ṣatīḥ ǀ áyugdhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, mighty Warriors, ye who glitter with your spears, o’erthrowing with your strength e’en what is ne’er o’erthrown, When, O ye Maruts, ye the host that send the rain, had harnessed to your cars the thought-fleet spotted deer.
verses.wilson_translation: They who are worthily worshipped shine with various weapons; incapable of being overthrown, they are the over-throwers (of mountains);Maruts, swift as thought, entrusted with the duty of sending rain, yoke the spotted deer to your cars.
verses.griffith_verse: When, mighty Warriors, ye who glitter with your spears, o’erthrowing with your strength e’en what is ne’er o’erthrown, When, O ye Maruts, ye the host that send the rain, had harnessed to your cars the thought-fleet spotted deer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यद्रथेषु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं वाजे अद्रिं मरुतो रंहयंतः ।उतारुषस्य वि ष्यंति धाराश्चर्मेवोदभिर्व्युंदंति भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ rátheṣu ǀ pṛ́ṣatīḥ ǀ áyugdhvam ǀ vā́je ǀ ádrim ǀ marutaḥ ǀ raṃháyantaḥ ǀutá ǀ aruṣásya ǀ ví ǀ syanti ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ cárma-iva ǀ udá-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ undanti ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: When ye have harnessed to your cars the spotted deer, urging the thunderbolt, O Maruts, to the fray, Forth rush the torrents of the dark red stormy cloud, and moisten, like a skin, the earth with water-floods.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Maruts, urging on the cloud, for the sake of (providing) food, you have yoked the deer to your chariots, the drops fall from the radiant (sun), and moisten the earth, like a hide, with water.
verses.griffith_verse: When ye have harnessed to your cars the spotted deer, urging the thunderbolt, O Maruts, to the fray, Forth rush the torrents of the dark red stormy cloud, and moisten, like a skin, the earth with water-floods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो वहंतु सप्तयो रघुष्यदो रघुपत्वानः प्र जिगात बाहुभिः ।सीदता बर्हिरुरु वः सदस्कृतं मादयध्वं मरुतो मध्वो अंधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ vahantu ǀ sáptayaḥ ǀ raghu-syádaḥ ǀ raghu-pátvānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ jigāta ǀ bāhú-bhiḥ ǀsī́data ǀ ā́ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ urú ǀ vaḥ ǀ sádaḥ ǀ kṛtám ǀ mādáyadhvam ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ándhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let your swift-gliding coursers bear you hitherward with their fleet pinions. Come ye forward with your arms. Sit on the grass; a wide seat hath been made for you: delight yourselves, O Maruts, in the pleasant food.
verses.wilson_translation: Let your quick-paced, smooth-gliding coursers bear you (hither); and moving swiftly, come with yourhands(filled with good things); sit,Maruts, upon the broad seat of sacred grass, and regale yourselves with the sweet sacrificial food.
verses.griffith_verse: Let your swift-gliding coursers bear you hitherward with their fleet pinions. Come ye forward with your arms. Sit on the grass; a wide seat hath been made for you: delight yourselves, O Maruts, in the pleasant food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेऽवर्धंत स्वतवसो महित्वना नाकं तस्थुरुरु चक्रिरे सदः ।विष्णुर्यद्धावद्वृषणं मदच्युतं वयो न सीदन्नधि बर्हिषि प्रिये ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ avardhanta ǀ svá-tavasaḥ ǀ mahi-tvanā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ nā́kam ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ urú ǀ cakrire ǀ sádaḥ ǀvíṣṇuḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ ā́vat ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ mada-cyútam ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sīdan ǀ ádhi ǀ barhíṣi ǀ priyé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong in their native strength to greatness have they grown, stepped to the firmament and made their dwelling wide. When Viṣṇu saved the Soma bringing wild delight, the Maruts sate like birds on their dear holy grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Confiding in their own strength, they have increased in (power); they have attained heaven by their greatness, and have made (for themselves) a spacious abode; may they, for whom Viṣṇudefends (the sacrifice) that bestows all desires and confers delight, come (quickly), like birds, and sit down upon the plural asant and sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong in their native strength to greatness have they grown, stepped to the firmament and made their dwelling wide. When Viṣṇu saved the Soma bringing wild delight, the Maruts sate like birds on their dear holy grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शूरा इवेद्युयुधयो न जग्मयः श्रवस्यवो न पृतनासु येतिरे ।भयंते विश्वा भुवना मरुद्भ्यो राजान इव त्वेषसंदृशो नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: śū́rāḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ yúyudhayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ jágmayaḥ ǀ śravasyávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ yetire ǀbháyante ǀ víśvā ǀ bhu��vanā ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀ rā́jānaḥ-iva ǀ tveṣá-saṃdṛśaḥ ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In sooth like heroes fain for fight they rush about, like combatants fame-seeking have they striven in war. Before the Maruts every creature is afraid: the men are like to Kings, terrible to behold.
verses.wilson_translation: Like heroes, like combatants, like men anxious for food, the swift-moving (Maruts) have engaged in battles; all beings fear the Maruts, who are the leaders (of the rain), and awful of aspect, like princes.
verses.griffith_verse: In sooth like heroes fain for fight they rush about, like combatants fame-seeking have they striven in war. Before the Maruts every creature is afraid: the men are like to Kings, terrible to behold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वष्टा यद्वज्रं सुकृतं हिरण्ययं सहस्रभृष्टिं स्वपा अवर्तयत् ।धत्त इंद्रो नर्यपांसि कर्तवेऽहन्वृत्रं निरपामौब्जदर्णवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tváṣṭā ǀ yát ǀ vájram ǀ sú-kṛtam ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ sahásra-bhṛṣṭim ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ ávartayat ǀdhatté ǀ índraḥ ǀ nári ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ kártave ǀ áhan ǀ vṛtrám ǀ níḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ aubjat ǀ arṇavám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Tvaṣṭar deft of hand had turned the thunderbolt, golden, with thousand edges, fashioned more skilfully, Indra received it to perform heroic deeds. Vṛtra he slew, and forced the flood of water forth.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, wields the well-made, golden, many-bladed thunderbolt, which the skillful Tvaṣṭāhas framed for him, that he may achieve great exploits in war. He has slain Vṛtraand sent forth an ocean of water.
verses.griffith_verse: When Tvaṣṭar deft of hand had turned the thunderbolt, golden, with thousand edges, fashioned more skilfully, Indra received it to perform heroic deeds. Vṛtra he slew, and forced the flood of water forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं नुनुद्रेऽवतं त ओजसा दादृहाणं चिद्बिभिदुर्वि पर्वतं ।धमंतो वाणं मरुतः सुदानवो मदे सोमस्य रण्यानि चक्रिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvám ǀ nunudre ǀ avatám ǀ té ǀ ójasā ǀ dadṛhāṇám ǀ cit ǀ bibhiduḥ ǀ ví ǀ párvatam ǀdhámantaḥ ǀ vāṇám ǀ marútaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ máde ǀ sómasya ǀ ráṇyāni ǀ cakrire ǁ
verses.english_translation: They with their vigorous strength pushed the well up on high, and clove the cloud in twain though it was passing strong. The Maruts, bounteous Givers, sending forth their voice, in the wild joy of Soma wrought their glorious deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: By their power, they bore the well aloft, and clove asunder the mountain that obstructed their path; the munificent Maruts, blowing upon their pipe, have conferred, when exhilarated by the Soma, desirable (gifts upon the sacrificer).
verses.griffith_verse: They with their vigorous strength pushed the well up on high, and clove the cloud in twain though it was passing strong. The Maruts, bounteous Givers, sending forth their voice, in the wild joy of Soma wrought their glorious deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जिह्मं नुनुद्रेऽवतं तया दिशासिंचन्नुत्सं गोतमाय तृष्णजे ।आ गच्छंतीमवसा चित्रभानवः कामं विप्रस्य तर्पयंत धामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: jihmám ǀ nunudre ǀ avatám ǀ táyā ǀ diśā́ ǀ ásiñcan ǀ útsam ǀ gótamāya ǀ tṛṣṇá-je ǀā́ ǀ gacchanti ǀ īm ǀ ávasā ǀ citrá-bhānavaḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ víprasya ǀ tarpayanta ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They drave the cloud transverse directed hitherward, and poured the fountain forth for thirsting Gotama. Shining with varied light they come to him with help: they with their might fulfilled the longing of the sage.
verses.wilson_translation: They brought the crooked well to the plural ce (where the Muniwas), and sprinkled the water upon the thirsty Gotama; the variously-radiant (Maruts) come to his succour, gratifyinng the desire of the sage with life-sustaining (waters).
verses.griffith_verse: They drave the cloud transverse directed hitherward, and poured the fountain forth for thirsting Gotama. Shining with varied light they come to him with help: they with their might fulfilled the longing of the sage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या वः शर्म शशमानाय संति त्रिधातूनि दाशुषे यच्छताधि ।अस्मभ्यं तानि मरुतो वि यंत रयिं नो धत्त वृषणः सुवीरं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ śaśamānā́ya ǀ sánti ǀ tri-dhā́tūni ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ yacchata ǀ ádhi ǀasmábhyam ǀ tā́ni ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ví ǀ yanta ǀ rayím ǀ naḥ ǀ dhatta ǀ vṛṣaṇaḥ ǀ su-vī́ram ǁ
verses.english_translation: The shelters which ye have for him who lauds you, bestow them threefold on the man who offers. Extend the same boons unto us, ye Maruts. Give us, O Heroes, wealth with noble offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever blessings (are diffused) through thethree worlds, and are in your gift, do you bestow upon the donor (of the oblation), who addressed you with praise; bestow them, also,Maruts, upon us, and grant us, bestowers of all good, riches, whence springs prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: The shelters which ye have for him who lauds you, bestow them threefold on the man who offers. Extend the same boons unto us, ye Maruts. Give us, O Heroes, wealth with noble offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVI. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink,O Maruts, giants of the sky. Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages’ hymns,O Maruts, listen to the call. Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall moveInto a stable rich in kine. Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites:Praise and delight are sung aloud. Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be hisThat reaches even to the Sun. For, through the swift Gods’ loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, weHave offered up our sacrifice. Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable,Whose offerings ye bear away. O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise,The heart's desire of him who loves. O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness: strikeThe demon with your thunderbolt. Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend.Create the light for which we long.

verses.sanskrit: मरुतो यस्य हि क्षये पाथा दिवो विमहसः ।स सुगोपातमो जनः ॥
verses.transliteration: márutaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ hí ǀ kṣáye ǀ pāthá ǀ diváḥ ǀ vi-mahasaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ su-gopā́tamaḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink, O Maruts, giants of the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: The man in whose mansion, resplendent Maruts, descending from the sky, you drink (the libation), is provided with most able protectors.
verses.griffith_verse: THE best of guardians hath that man within whose dwelling place ye drink, O Maruts, giants of the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञैर्वा यज्ञवाहसो विप्रस्य वा मतीनां ।मरुतः शृणुता हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñáiḥ ǀ vā ǀ yajña-vāhasaḥ ǀ víprasya ǀ vā ǀ matīnā́m ǀmárutaḥ ǀ śṛṇutá ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages’ hymns, O Maruts, listen to the call.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, bearers of oblations, hear the invocation of the praises of the worshipper with or (without) sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Honoured with sacrifice or with the worship of the sages’ hymns, O Maruts, listen to the call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत वा यस्य वाजिनोऽनु विप्रमतक्षत ।स गंता गोमति व्रजे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vā ǀ yásya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vípram ǀ átakṣata ǀsáḥ ǀ gántā ǀ gó-mati ǀ vrajé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall move Into a stable rich in kine.
verses.wilson_translation: And may he for whom ministrant priests have sharp-ended the sapient (troop of the Maruts), walk among pastures crowded with cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, the strong man to whom ye have vouchsafed to give a sage, shall move Into a stable rich in kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य वीरस्य बर्हिषि सुतः सोमो दिविष्टिषु ।उक्थं मदश्च शस्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ vīrásya ǀ barhíṣi ǀ sutáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀukthám ǀ mádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ śasyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites: Praise and delight are sung aloud.
verses.wilson_translation: The libation is poured out for the hero at the sacrifice, on the appointed days, and the hymn is repeated, and their (is excited).
verses.griffith_verse: Upon this hero's sacred grass Soma is poured in daily rites: Praise and delight are sung aloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य श्रोषंत्वा भुवो विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभि ।सूरं चित्सस्रुषीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ śroṣantu ǀ ā́ ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ carṣaṇī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀsū́ram ǀ cit ǀ sasrúṣīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be his That reaches even to the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, victorious over all men, hear (the praises) of this (their worshipper), and may (abundant) food be obtained by him who praises them.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the strong Maruts hear him, him surpassing all men: strength be his That reaches even to the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वीभिर्हि ददाशिम शरद्भिर्मरुतो वयं ।अवोभिश्चर्षणीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrvī́bhiḥ ǀ hí ǀ dadāśimá ǀ śarát-bhiḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vayám ǀávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, through the swift Gods’ loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, we Have offered up our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Enjoying the protection of you who behold all things, we have offered you,Maruts, (oblations) for many years.
verses.griffith_verse: For, through the swift Gods’ loving help, in many an autumn, Maruts, we Have offered up our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुभगः स प्रयज्यवो मरुतो अस्तु मर्त्यः ।यस्य प्रयांसि पर्षथ ॥
verses.transliteration: su-bhágaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ pra-yajyavaḥ ǀ márutaḥ ǀ astu ǀ mártyaḥ ǀyásya ǀ práyāṃsi ǀ párṣatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable, Whose offerings ye bear away.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, who are to be especially worshipped, may the man whose offering you accept be ever prosperous.
verses.griffith_verse: Fortunate shall that mortal be, O Maruts most adorable, Whose offerings ye bear away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शशमानस्य वा नरः स्वेदस्य सत्यशवसः ।विदा कामस्य वेनतः ॥
verses.transliteration: śaśamānásya ǀ vā ǀ naraḥ ǀ svédasya ǀ satya-śavasaḥ ǀvidá ǀ kā́masya ǀ vénataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise, The heart's desire of him who loves.
verses.wilson_translation: Possessors of true vigour, be cognizant of the wishes of him who praises you, and toils in your service, desirous of (your favour).
verses.griffith_verse: O Heroes truly strong, ye know the toil of him who sings your praise, The heart's desire of him who loves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं तत्सत्यशवस आविष्कर्त महित्वना ।विध्यता विद्युता रक्षः ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ tát ǀ satya-śavasaḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ karta ǀ mahi-tvanā́ ǀvídhyata ǀ vi-dyútā ǀ rákṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness: strike The demon with your thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Possessors of true vigour, you have displayed your might, with the lustre (of which) you have destroyed therākṣasas.
verses.griffith_verse: O ye of true strength, make this thing manifest by your greatness: strike The demon with your thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गूहता गुह्यं तमो वि यात विश्वमत्रिणं ।ज्योतिष्कर्ता यदुश्मसि ॥
verses.transliteration: gū́hata ǀ gúhyam ǀ támaḥ ǀ ví ǀ yāta ǀ víśvam ǀ atríṇam ǀjyótiḥ ǀ karta ǀ yát ǀ uśmási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend. Create the light for which we long.
verses.wilson_translation: Dissipate the concealing darkness; drive away every devouring (foe); show us the light we long for.
verses.griffith_verse: Conceal the horrid darkness, drive far from us each devouring fiend. Create the light for which we long.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LOUD Singers, never humbled, active, full of strength, immovable, impetuous, manliest, best-beloved,They have displayed themselves with glittering ornaments, a few in number only, like the heavens with stars. When, Maruts, on the steeps ye pile the moving cloud, ye are like birds on whatsoever path it be.Clouds everywhere shed forth the rain upon your cars. Drop fatness, honey-hued, for him who sings your praise. Earth at their racings trembles as if weak and worn, when on their ways they yoke their cars for victory.They, sportive, loudly roaring, armed with glittering spears, shakers of all, themselves admire their mightiness. Self-moving is that youthful band, with spotted steeds; thus it hath lordly sway, endued with power and might.Truthful art thou, and blameless, searcher out of sin: so thou, Strong Host, wilt be protector of this prayer. We speak by our descent from our primeval Sire; our tongue, when we behold the Soma, stirs itself.When, shouting, they had joined Indra in toil of fight, then only they obtained their sacrificial names. Splendours they gained for glory, they who wear bright rings; rays they obtained, and men to celebrate their praise.Armed with their swords, impetuous and fearing naught, they have possessed the Maruts’ own beloved home.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्वक्षसः प्रतवसो विरप्शिनोऽनानता अविथुरा ऋजीषिणः ।जुष्टतमासो नृतमासो अंजिभिर्व्यानज्रे के चिदुस्रा इव स्तृभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá-tvakṣasaḥ ǀ prá-tavasaḥ ǀ vi-rapśínaḥ ǀ ánānatāḥ ǀ ávithurāḥ ǀ ṛjīṣíṇaḥ ǀjúṣṭa-tamāsaḥ ǀ nṛ́-tamāsaḥ ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ ānajre ǀ ké ǀ cit ǀ usrā́ḥ-iva ǀ stṛ́-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LOUD Singers, never humbled, active, full of strength, immovable, impetuous, manliest, best-beloved, They have displayed themselves with glittering ornaments, a few in number only, like the heavens with stars.
verses.wilson_translation: Annihilators (of adversaries) endowed with great strength, loud-shouting, unbending inseparable partakers of the evening oblation, constantly worshipped, and leaders (of the clouds), (the Maruts), by their person nal decorations,a re conspicuous (in the sky) like certain rays of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: LOUD Singers, never humbled, active, full of strength, immovable, impetuous, manliest, best-beloved, They have displayed themselves with glittering ornaments, a few in number only, like the heavens with stars.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपह्वरेषु यदचिध्वं ययिं वय इव मरुतः केन चित्पथा ।श्चोतंति कोशा उप वो रथेष्वा घृतमुक्षता मधुवर्णमर्चते ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-hvaréṣu ǀ yát ǀ ácidhvam ǀ yayím ǀ váyaḥ-iva ǀ marutaḥ ǀ kéna ǀ cit ǀ pathā́ ǀścótanti ǀ kóśāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ukṣata ǀ mádhu-varṇam ǀ árcate ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Maruts, on the steeps ye pile the moving cloud, ye are like birds on whatsoever path it be. Clouds everywhere shed forth the rain upon your cars. Drop fatness, honey-hued, for him who sings your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Maruts, flying like birds along a certain path (of the sky), you collect the moving passing (clouds) in the nearest portions (of the firmament), then, coming into collision with your cars, they pour forth (the waters); therefore, do you shower upon your worshipper the honey-coloured rain.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Maruts, on the steeps ye pile the moving cloud, ye are like birds on whatsoever path it be. Clouds everywhere shed forth the rain upon your cars. Drop fatness, honey-hued, for him who sings your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रैषामज्मेषु विथुरेव रेजते भूमिर्यामेषु यद्ध युंजते शुभे ।ते क्रीळयो धुनयो भ्राजदृष्टयः स्वयं महित्वं पनयंत धूतयः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ eṣām ǀ ájmeṣu ǀ vithurā́-iva ǀ rejate ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ yā́meṣu ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ yuñjáte ǀ śubhé ǀté ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ svayám ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ panayanta ǀ dhū́tayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Earth at their racings trembles as if weak and worn, when on their ways they yoke their cars for victory. They, sportive, loudly roaring, armed with glittering spears, shakers of all, themselves admire their mightiness.
verses.wilson_translation: When they assemble (the clouds) for the good work, earth trembles at their impetuous movements, like a wife (whose husband is away); sportive, capricious, armed with bright weapons, and agitating (the solid rocks) they manifest their inherent might.
verses.griffith_verse: Earth at their racings trembles as if weak and worn, when on their ways they yoke their cars for victory. They, sportive, loudly roaring, armed with glittering spears, shakers of all, themselves admire their mightiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि स्वसृत्पृषदश्वो युवा गणोऽया ईशानस्तविषीभिरावृतः ।असि सत्य ऋणयावानेद्योऽस्या धियः प्राविताथा वृषा गणः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ sva-sṛ́t ǀ pṛ́ṣat-aśvaḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ gaṇáḥ ǀ ayā́ ǀ īśānáḥ ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ ā́-vṛtaḥ ǀási ǀ satyáḥ ǀ ṛṇa-yā́vā ǀ ánedyaḥ ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ dhiyáḥ ǀ pra-avitā́ ǀ átha ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ gaṇáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Self-moving is that youthful band, with spotted steeds; thus it hath lordly sway, endued with power and might. Truthful art thou, and blameless, searcher out of sin: so thou, Strong Host, wilt be protector of this prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: The troop of Marutsis self-moving deer-borne, ever young, lords of this (earth), and invested with vigour; you, who are sincere liberators from debt, irreproachable, and shedders of rain, are the protectors of this our rite.
verses.griffith_verse: Self-moving is that youthful band, with spotted steeds; thus it hath lordly sway, endued with power and might. Truthful art thou, and blameless, searcher out of sin: so thou, Strong Host, wilt be protector of this prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पितुः प्रत्नस्य जन्मना वदामसि सोमस्य जिह्वा प्र जिगाति चक्षसा ।यदीमिंद्रं शम्यृक्वाण आशतादिन्नामानि यज्ञियानि दधिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: pitúḥ ǀ pratnásya ǀ jánmanā ǀ vadāmasi ǀ sómasya ǀ jihvā́ ǀ prá ǀ jigāti ǀ cákṣasā ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ índram ǀ śámi ǀ ṛ́kvāṇaḥ ǀ ā́śata ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ nā́māni ǀ yajñíyāni ǀ dadhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: We speak by our descent from our primeval Sire; our tongue, when we behold the Soma, stirs itself. When, shouting, they had joined Indra in toil of fight, then only they obtained their sacrificial names.
verses.wilson_translation: We declare by our birth from our ancient sire, that the tongue (of praise) accompanies the manifesting (invocation of the Maruts) at the libations of the Soma; for, inasmuch as they stood by encouraging Indrain the conflict, they have acquired names that are to be recited at sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: We speak by our descent from our primeval Sire; our tongue, when we behold the Soma, stirs itself. When, shouting, they had joined Indra in toil of fight, then only they obtained their sacrificial names.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रियसे कं भानुभिः सं मिमिक्षिरे ते रश्मिभिस्त ऋक्वभिः सुखादयः ।ते वाशीमंत इष्मिणो अभीरवो विद्रे प्रियस्य मारुतस्य धाम्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: śriyáse ǀ kám ǀ bhānú-bhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ mimikṣire ǀ té ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ té ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ su-khādáyaḥ ǀté ǀ vā́śī-mantaḥ ǀ iṣmíṇaḥ ǀ ábhīravaḥ ǀ vidré ǀ priyásya ǀ mā́rutasya ǀ dhā́mnaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Splendours they gained for glory, they who wear bright rings; rays they obtained, and men to celebrate their praise. Armed with their swords, impetuous and fearing naught, they have possessed the Maruts’ own beloved home.
verses.wilson_translation: Combing with the solar rays, they have willingly poured down (rain) for the welfare (of mankind), and, hymned by the priests, have been plural ased partakers of the (sacrificial food); addressed with praises, moving swiftly, and exempt from fear they have become possessed of a station agreeable and suitable to the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: Splendours they gained for glory, they who wear bright rings; rays they obtained, and men to celebrate their praise. Armed with their swords, impetuous and fearing naught, they have possessed the Maruts’ own beloved home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVIII. Maruts.
hymns.anukramani: ६ गोतमो राहूगणः। मरुतः। त्रिष्टुप्, १, ६ प्रस्तारपंक्तिः, ५ विराड् रुपा।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds.Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power. With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory.Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly. For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits.For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion. The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship.The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water. No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts,What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron. To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth.It rusheth freely from our hands as these libations wont to flow.

verses.sanskrit: आ विद्युन्मद्भिर्मरुतः स्वर्कै रथेभिर्यात ऋष्टिमद्भिरश्वपर्णैः ।आ वर्षिष्ठया न इषा वयो न पप्तता सुमायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vidyúnmat-bhiḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ su-arkáiḥ ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀ yāta ǀ ṛṣṭimát-bhiḥ ǀ áśva-parṇaiḥ ǀā́ ǀ várṣiṣṭhayā ǀ naḥ ǀ iṣā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ paptata ǀ su-māyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds. Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Maruts, with your brilliant light-moving, well-weaponed, steed-harnessed chariots; doers of good deeds, descend like birds, (and bring us) abundant food.
verses.griffith_verse: COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds. Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेऽरुणेभिर्वरमा पिशंगैः शुभे कं यांति रथतूर्भिरश्वैः ।रुक्मो न चित्रः स्वधितीवान्पव्या रथस्य जंघनंत भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ aruṇébhiḥ ǀ váram ǀ ā́ ǀ piśáṅgaiḥ ǀ śubhé ǀ kám ǀ yānti ǀ rathatū́ḥ-bhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀrukmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ citráḥ ǀ svádhiti-vān ǀ pavyā́ ǀ ráthasya ǀ jaṅghananta ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory. Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly.
verses.wilson_translation: To what glorifier (of the gods) do they repair with their ruddy, tawny, car-bearing horses for his advantage? bright as burnished (gold), and armed with the thunderbolt, they furrow the earth with their chariot-wheels.
verses.griffith_verse: With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory. Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रिये कं वो अधि तनूषु वाशीर्मेधा वना न कृणवंत ऊर्ध्वा ।युष्मभ्यं कं मरुतः सुजातास्तुविद्युम्नासो धनयंते अद्रिं ॥
verses.transliteration: śriyé ǀ kám ǀ vaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ vā́śīḥ ǀ medhā́ ǀ vánā ǀ ná ǀ kṛṇavante ǀ ūrdhvā́ ǀyuṣmábhyam ǀ kám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ su-jātāḥ ǀ tuvi-dyumnā́saḥ ǀ dhanayante ǀ ádrim ǁ
verses.english_translation: For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits. For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, the threatening (weapons) are upon your person ns, (able to win) dominion; (to you) they praise lofty sacrifices, like (tall) trees; well-born Maruts, for you do wealthy worshippers enrich the stone (that grinds the Soma)].
verses.griffith_verse: For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits. For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहानि गृध्राः पर्या व आगुरिमां धियं वार्कार्यां च देवीं ।ब्रह्म कृण्वंतो गोतमासो अर्कैरूर्ध्वं नुनुद्र उत्सधिं पिबध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: áhāni ǀ gṛ́dhrāḥ ǀ pári ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aguḥ ǀ imā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ vārkāryā́m ǀ ca ǀ devī́m ǀbráhma ǀ kṛṇvántaḥ ǀ gótamāsaḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ ūrdhvám ǀ nunudre ǀ utsa-dhím ǀ píbadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship. The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water.
verses.wilson_translation: Fortunate days have befallen you, (sons of Gotama), when thirsty, and have given lustre to the rite for which water was essential; the sons of Gotama, (offering) oblations with sacred hymns, have raised aloft the well (provided) for their dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship. The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतत्त्यन्न योजनमचेति सस्वर्ह यन्मरुतो गोतमो वः ।पश्यन्हिरण्यचक्रानयोदंष्ट्रान्विधावतो वराहून् ॥
verses.transliteration: etát ǀ tyát ǀ ná ǀ yójanam ǀ aceti ǀ sasváḥ ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ marutaḥ ǀ gótamaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀpáśyan ǀ híraṇya-cakrān ǀ áyaḥ-daṃṣṭrān ǀ vi-dhā́vataḥ ǀ varā́hūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts, What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron.
verses.wilson_translation: This hymn is known to be the same as that which Gotamarecited Maruts, in your (praise) when he beheld you seated in your chariots with golden wheels, armed with weapons, hurrying hither and thither, and destroying your mightiest foes.
verses.griffith_verse: No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts, What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एषा स्या वो मरुतोऽनुभर्त्री प्रति ष्टोभति वाघतो न वाणी ।अस्तोभयद्वृथासामनु स्वधां गभस्त्योः ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ syā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ anu-bhartrī́ ǀ práti ǀ stobhati ǀ vāghátaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́ṇī ǀástobhayat ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ āsām ǀ ánu ǀ svadhā́m ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth. It rusheth freely from our hands as these libations wont to flow.
verses.wilson_translation: This is that praise,Maruts, which, suited (to your merits) glorifies every one of you. The speech of the priest has now glorified you, without difficulty, with sacred verses, since (you have plural ced) food in ourhands.
verses.griffith_verse: To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth. It rusheth freely from our hands as these libations wont to flow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIX. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious,That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care. May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods.The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live. We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Dakṣa, Mitra, Aditi,Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, auspicious, grant felicity. May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven,And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Aśvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this. Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul,That Pūṣan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good. Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pūṣan prosper us, the Master of all wealth.May Tārkṣya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Bṛhaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity. The Maruts, Sons of Pṛśni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites,Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,—hither let all the Gods for our protection come. Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones.With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods. A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay;Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life. Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son.Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.

verses.sanskrit: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यंतु विश्वतोऽदब्धासो अपरीतास उद्भिदः ।देवा नो यथा सदमिद्वृधे असन्नप्रायुवो रक्षितारो दिवेदिवे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ krátavaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ ádabdhāsaḥ ǀ ápari-itāsaḥ ǀ ut-bhídaḥ ǀdevā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ vṛdhé ǀ ásan ǀ ápra-āyuvaḥ ǀ rakṣitā́raḥ ǀ divé-dive ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious, That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care.
verses.wilson_translation: May auspicious works, unmolested, unimpeded, and subversive (of foes), come to us from every quarter; may the gods, turning not away from us, but granting us protection day by day, be ever with us for our advancement.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious, That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवानां भद्रा सुमतिर्ऋजूयतां देवानां रातिरभि नो नि वर्ततां ।देवानां सख्यमुप सेदिमा वयं देवा न आयुः प्र तिरंतु जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ ṛju-yatā́m ǀ devā́nām ǀ rātíḥ ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ ní ǀ vartatām ǀdevā́nām ǀ sakhyám ǀ úpa ǀ sedima ǀ vayám ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ prá ǀ tirantu ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods. The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.
verses.wilson_translation: May the benevolent favour of the gods (be ours); may the bounty of the gods, ever approving of the upright, light upon us; may we obtain the friendship of the gods, and may the gods extend our days to longevity.
verses.griffith_verse: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods. The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तान्पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधं ।अर्यमणं वरुणं सोममश्विना सरस्वती नः सुभगा मयस्करत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́n ǀ pū́rvayā ǀ ni-vídā ǀ hūmahe ǀ vayám ǀ bhágam ǀ mitrám ǀ áditim ǀ dákṣam ǀ asrídham ǀaryamáṇam ǀ váruṇam ǀ sómam ǀ aśvínā ǀ sárasvatī ǀ naḥ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ máyaḥ ǀ karat ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Dakṣa, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, auspicious, grant felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke them with an ancient text,Bhaga,Mitra,Aditi,Dakṣa, Asridh,Aryaman,Varuṇa,Soma, the Aśvins; and may the gracious Sarasvatīgrant us happiness.
verses.griffith_verse: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Dakṣa, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, auspicious, grant felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत्पिता द्यौः ।तद्ग्रावाणः सोमसुतो मयोभुवस्तदश्विना शृणुतं धिष्ण्या युवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhú ǀ vātu ǀ bheṣajám ǀ tát ǀ mātā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ tát ǀ pitā́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀtát ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ soma-sútaḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀ tát ǀ aśvinā ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ dhiṣṇyā ǀ yuvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven, And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Aśvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.
verses.wilson_translation: May the wind waft to us the grateful medicament; may mother earth, may father heaven, (convey) it (to us); may the stones that express Soma, and are productive of plural asure (bring) it (to us);Aśvins, who are to be meditated upon, hear (our submission).
verses.griffith_verse: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven, And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Aśvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमीशानं जगतस्तस्थुषस्पतिं धियंजिन्वमवसे हूमहे वयं ।पूषा नो यथा वेदसामसद्वृधे रक्षिता पायुरदब्धः स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ī́śānam ǀ jágataḥ ǀ tasthúṣaḥ ǀ pátim ǀ dhiyam-jinvám ǀ ávase ǀ hūmahe ǀ vayám ǀpūṣā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ védasām ǀ ásat ǀ vṛdhé ǀ rakṣitā́ ǀ pāyúḥ ǀ ádabdhaḥ ǀ svastáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul, That Pūṣan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke that lord of living beings, that protector of things immoveable,Indra, who is to be propitiated by pious rites, for our protection; as Pūṣanhas ever been our defender for the increase of our riches, so may he (continue) the unmolested guardian of our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul, That Pūṣan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्ति न इंद्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः ।स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥
verses.transliteration: svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vṛddhá-śravāḥ ǀ svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ viśvá-vedāḥ ǀsvastí ǀ naḥ ǀ tā́rkṣyaḥ ǀ áriṣṭa-nemiḥ ǀ svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ dadhātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pūṣan prosper us, the Master of all wealth. May Tārkṣya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Bṛhaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, who listens to much praise, guard our welfare; may Pūṣan, who knows all things, guard our welfare; may Tārkṣya, with unblemished weapons, guard our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pūṣan prosper us, the Master of all wealth. May Tārkṣya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Bṛhaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पृषदश्वा मरुतः पृश्निमातरः शुभंयावानो विदथेषु जग्मयः ।अग्निजिह्वा मनवः सूरचक्षसो विश्वे नो देवा अवसा गमन्निह ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛ́ṣat-aśvāḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǀ śubham-yā́vānaḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ jágmayaḥ ǀagni-jihvā́ḥ ǀ mánavaḥ ǀ sū́ra-cakṣasaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ naḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gaman ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts, Sons of Pṛśni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites, Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,—hither let all the Gods for our protection come.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, whose coursers are spotted deer, who are the sons of Pṛśni, gracefully-moving frequenters of sacrifices, (seated) on the tongue of Agni, regarders (of all), and radiant as the sun, may all the gods come hither for our preservation.
verses.griffith_verse: The Maruts, Sons of Pṛśni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites, Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,—hither let all the Gods for our protection come.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः ।स्थिरैरंगैस्तुष्टुवांसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ kárṇebhiḥ ǀ śṛṇuyāma ǀ devāḥ ǀ bhadrám ǀ paśyema ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀsthiráiḥ ǀ áṅgaiḥ ǀ tustu-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ tanū́bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśema ǀ devá-hitam ǀ yát ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones. With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us hear, gods, with our ears, what is good; objects of sacrifice, let us see with our eyes what is good; let us, engaged in your praises, enjoy, with firm limb and (sound) bodies, the term of life granted by the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones. With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतमिन्नु शरदो अंति देवा यत्रा नश्चक्रा जरसं तनूनां ।पुत्रासो यत्र पितरो भवंति मा नो मध्या रीरिषतायुर्गंतोः ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ánti ǀ devāḥ ǀ yátra ǀ naḥ ǀ cakrá ǀ jarásam ǀ tanū́nām ǀputrā́saḥ ǀ yátra ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ bhávanti ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ madhyā́ ǀ ririṣata ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ gántoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay; Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.
verses.wilson_translation: Since a hundred years were appointed (for the life of man), interpose not, gods, in the midst of our passing existence, by inflicting infirmity in our bodies so that our sons become our sires (i.e. let us not become so feeble and firm as to be, infants and to require the paternal care of our own sons].
verses.griffith_verse: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay; Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरंतरिक्षमदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः ।विश्वे देवा अदितिः पंच जना अदितिर्जातमदितिर्जनित्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: áditiḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ áditiḥ ǀ mātā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ páñca ǀ jánāḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ jātám ǀ áditiḥ ǀ jáni-tvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son. Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.
verses.wilson_translation: Aditiis heaven; Aditi is the firmament; Aditi is mother, father and son; Aditi is all the gods; Aditi is the five classes of people; Aditi is genitive ration and birth.��
verses.griffith_verse: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son. Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XC. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY Varuṇa with guidance straight, and Mitra lead us, he who knows,And Aryaman in accord with Gods. For they are dealers forth of wealth, and, not deluded, with their mightGuard evermore the holy laws. Shelter may they vouchsafe to us, Immortal Gods to mortal men,Chasing our enemies away. May they mark out our paths to bliss, Indra, the Maruts, Pūṣan,and Bhaga, the Gods to be adored. Yea, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, ye who run your course, enrich our hymns with kine;Bless us with all prosperity. The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the LawSo may the plants be sweet for us. Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere;Sweet be our Father Heaven to us.
