verses.wilson_translation: plural asant is it to you when you are lighted in your own abode, and propitiated by libations, are praised (by the priests); then, much delighted, you give rewards and riches to the worshipper; let us not,Agni, suffer injury through your friendship.
verses.griffith_verse: This is thy grace that, kindled in thine own abode, invoked with Soma thou soundest forth most benign, Thou givest wealth and treasure to the worshipper. Let us not in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै त्वं सुद्रविणो ददाशोऽनागास्त्वमदिते सर्वताता ।यं भद्रेण शवसा चोदयासि प्रजावता राधसा ते स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ tvám ǀ su-draviṇaḥ ǀ dádāśaḥ ǀ anāgāḥ-tvám ǀ adite ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀyám ǀ bhadréṇa ǀ śávasā ǀ codáyāsi ǀ prajā́-vatā ǀ rā́dhasā ǀ té ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: To whom thou, Lord of goodly riches, grantest freedom from every sin with perfect wholeness, Whom with good strength thou quickenest , with children and wealth—may we be they, Eternal Being.
verses.wilson_translation: (Fortunate is the worshipper) to whom, (assiduos) in all pious works, you, possessor of riches, invisible Agni, grant exemption from sin, whom you associate with auspicious strength, may he be (enriched) by you with wealth that comprehends progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: To whom thou, Lord of goodly riches, grantest freedom from every sin with perfect wholeness, Whom with good strength thou quickenest , with children and wealth—may we be they, Eternal Being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमग्ने सौभगत्वस्य विद्वानस्माकमायुः प्र तिरेह देव ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ saubhaga-tvásya ǀ vidvā́n ǀ asmā́kam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ prá ǀ tira ǀ ihá ǀ deva ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such, Agni, thou who knowest all good fortune, God, lengthen here the days of our existence. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, divine Agni, who kno what is good fortune, on this occasion prolong our existence, and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi, ocean, earth and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Such, Agni, thou who knowest all good fortune, God, lengthen here the days of our existence. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCV. Agni
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant.One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour; bright and fair-shining, is he with the other. Tvaṣṭar's ten daughters, vigilant and youthful, produced this Infant borne to sundry quarters.They bear around him whose long flames are pointed, fulgent among mankind with native splendour.. Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters.Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order. Who of you knows this secret One? The Infant by his own nature hath brought forth his Mothers.The germ of many, from the waters' bosom he goes forth, wise and great, of Godlike nature. Visible, fair, he grows in native brightness uplifted in the lap of waving waters.When he was born both Tvaṣṭar's worlds were frightened: they turn to him and reverence the Lion. The Two auspicious Ones, like women, tend him: like lowing cows they seek him in their manner.He is the Lord of Might among the mighty; him, on the right, they balm with their oblations. Like Savitar his arms with might he stretches; awful, he strives grasping the world's two borders.He forces out from all a brilliant vesture, yea, from his Mothers draws he forth new raiment. He makes him a most noble form of splendour, decking him in his home with milk and waters.The Sage adorns the depths of air with wisdom: this is the meeting where the Gods are worshipped. Wide through the firmament spreads forth triumphant the far-resplendent strength of thee the Mighty.Kindled by us do thou preserve us, Agni, with all thy self-bright undiminished succours. In dry spots he makes stream, and course, and torrent, and inundates the earth with floods that glisten.All ancient things within his maw he gathers, and moves among the new fresh-sprouting grasses. Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: द्वे विरूपे चरतः स्वर्थे अन्यान्या वत्समुप धापयेते ।हरिरन्यस्यां भवति स्वधावांछुक्रो अन्यस्यां ददृशे सुवर्चाः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ vírūpe íti ví-rūpe ǀ carataḥ ǀ svárthe íti su-árthe ǀ anyā́-anyā ǀ vatsám ǀ úpa ǀ dhāpayete íti ǀháriḥ ǀ anyásyām ǀ bhávati ǀ svadhā́-vān ǀ śukráḥ ǀ anyásyām ǀ dadṛśe ǀ su-várcāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant. One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour; bright and fair-shining, is he with the other.
verses.wilson_translation: Two periods, of different complexions, revolve for their own purposes, and each in succession severally nourishes a son; in one,Hariis the receiver of oblations, in the other, the brilliant Agniis beheld.
verses.griffith_verse: To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant. One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour; bright and fair-shining, is he with the other.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दशेमं त्वष्टुर्जनयंत गर्भमतंद्रासो युवतयो विभृत्रं ।तिग्मानीकं स्वयशसं जनेषु विरोचमानं परि षीं नयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ imám ǀ tváṣṭuḥ ǀ janayanta ǀ gárbham ǀ átandrāsaḥ ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ ví-bhṛtram ǀtigmá-anīkam ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ jáneṣu ǀ vi-rócamānam ǀ pári ǀ sīm ǀ nayanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tvaṣṭar's ten daughters, vigilant and youthful, produced this Infant borne to sundry quarters. They bear around him whose long flames are pointed, fulgent among mankind with native splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: The vigilant and youthful Ten beget, through the wind, this embryo Agni, inherent (in all beings), sharp-visaged, universally renowned, shining among men; him they conduct (to every dwelling).
verses.griffith_verse: Tvaṣṭar's ten daughters, vigilant and youthful, produced this Infant borne to sundry quarters. They bear around him whose long flames are pointed, fulgent among mankind with native splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रीणि जाना परि भूषंत्यस्य समुद्र एकं दिव्येकमप्सु ।पूर्वामनु प्र दिशं पार्थिवानामृतून्प्रशासद्वि दधावनुष्ठु ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ṇi ǀ jā́nā ǀ pári ǀ bhūṣanti ǀ asya ǀ samudré ǀ ékam ǀ diví ǀ ékam ǀ ap-sú ǀpū́rvām ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ díśam ǀ pā́rthivānām ǀ ṛtū́n ǀ pra-śā́sat ǀ ví ǀ dadhau ǀ anuṣṭhú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
verses.wilson_translation: They contemplate three plural ces of his birth; one in the ocean, one in the heaven, one in the firmament; and, dividing the seasons of the year for the benefit of earthly creatures, he formed, in regular succession, the eastern quarteṛ
verses.griffith_verse: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क इमं वो निण्यमा चिकेत वत्सो मातॄर्जनयत स्वधाभिः ।बह्वीनां गर्भो अपसामुपस्थान्महान्कविर्निश्चरति स्वधावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ imám ǀ vaḥ ǀ niṇyám ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketa ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ mātṝ́ḥ ǀ janayata ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀbahvīnā́m ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ apásām ǀ upá-sthāt ǀ mahā́n ǀ kavíḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ carati ǀ svadhā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who of you knows this secret One? The Infant by his own nature hath brought forth his Mothers. The germ of many, from the waters' bosom he goes forth, wise and great, of Godlike nature.
verses.wilson_translation: Which of you discerns the hidden Agni? a son, he begets his mothers by oblations; the germ of many (waters), he issues from the ocrean, mighty and wise, the recipient of oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Who of you knows this secret One? The Infant by his own nature hath brought forth his Mothers. The germ of many, from the waters' bosom he goes forth, wise and great, of Godlike nature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आविष्ट्यो वर्धते चारुरासु जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः स्वयशा उपस्थे ।उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमानात्प्रतीची सिंहं प्रति जोषयेते ॥
verses.transliteration: āvíḥ-tyaḥ ǀ vardhate ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ āsu ǀ jihmā́nām ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ svá-yaśāḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀubhé íti ǀ tváṣṭuḥ ǀ bibhyatuḥ ǀ jā́yamānāt ǀ pratīcī́ íti ǀ siṃhám ǀ práti ǀ joṣayete íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Visible, fair, he grows in native brightness uplifted in the lap of waving waters. When he was born both Tvaṣṭar's worlds were frightened: they turn to him and reverence the Lion.
verses.wilson_translation: Appearing amongst them (the waters), the bright-shining (Agni) increases, rising above the flanks of the waving waters, spreading his own renown; both (heaven and earth) are alarmed, as the radiant Agni is born, and, approaching the lion, they pay him honour.
verses.griffith_verse: Visible, fair, he grows in native brightness uplifted in the lap of waving waters. When he was born both Tvaṣṭar's worlds were frightened: they turn to him and reverence the Lion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उभे भद्रे जोषयेते न मेने गावो न वाश्रा उप तस्थुरेवैः ।स दक्षाणां दक्षपतिर्बभूवांजंति यं दक्षिणतो हविर्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ bhadré íti ǀ joṣayete íti ǀ ná ǀ méne íti ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vāśrā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ dákṣāṇām ǀ dákṣa-patiḥ ǀ babhūva ǀ añjánti ǀ yám ǀ dakṣiṇatáḥ ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Two auspicious Ones, like women, tend him: like lowing cows they seek him in their manner. He is the Lord of Might among the mighty; him, on the right, they balm with their oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Both the auspicious ones (day and night or two pieces of wood rubbed together to produce flame) wait upon him like two feminine le attendants, as lowing kine (follow their calves) by the paths (that they have gone); he has been the lord of might among the mighty, whom (the priests) on the right (of the altar) anoint.
verses.griffith_verse: The Two auspicious Ones, like women, tend him: like lowing cows they seek him in their manner. He is the Lord of Might among the mighty; him, on the right, they balm with their oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्यंयमीति सवितेव बाहू उभे सिचौ यतते भीम ऋंजन् ।उच्छुक्रमत्कमजते सिमस्मान्नवा मातृभ्यो वसना जहाति ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ yaṃyamīti ǀ savitā́-iva ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ sícau ǀ yatate ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ṛñján ǀút ǀ śukrám ǀ átkam ǀ ajate ǀ simásmāt ǀ návā ǀ mātṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ vásanā ǀ jahāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like Savitar his arms with might he stretches; awful, he strives grasping the world's two borders. He forces out from all a brilliant vesture, yea, from his Mothers draws he forth new raiment.
verses.wilson_translation: Like the sun, he stretches forth his arms, and the formidable Agni, decorating both heaven and earth (with brightness), labours (in his duties); he draws up from everything the essential (moisture), and clothes (the earth) with new vestments (derived) from his maternal (rains).
verses.griffith_verse: Like Savitar his arms with might he stretches; awful, he strives grasping the world's two borders. He forces out from all a brilliant vesture, yea, from his Mothers draws he forth new raiment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वेषं रूपं कृणुत उत्तरं यत्संपृंचानः सदने गोभिरद्भिः ।कविर्बुध्नं परि मर्मृज्यते धीः सा देवताता समितिर्बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: tveṣám ǀ rūpám ǀ kṛṇute ǀ út-taram ǀ yát ǀ sam-pṛñcānáḥ ǀ sádane ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ at-bhíḥ ǀkavíḥ ǀ budhnám ǀ pári ǀ marmṛjyate ǀ dhī́ḥ ǀ sā́ ǀ devá-tātā ǀ sám-itiḥ ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: He makes him a most noble form of splendour, decking him in his home with milk and waters. The Sage adorns the depths of air with wisdom: this is the meeting where the Gods are worshipped.
verses.wilson_translation: Associated in the firmament with the moving waters, he assumes an excellent and lustrous form, and the wise sustainer (of all things) sweeps over the source (of the rains with his radiance), whence a concentration of light is spread abroad by the sportive deity.
verses.griffith_verse: He makes him a most noble form of splendour, decking him in his home with milk and waters. The Sage adorns the depths of air with wisdom: this is the meeting where the Gods are worshipped.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उरु ते ज्रयः पर्येति बुध्नं विरोचमानं महिषस्य धाम ।विश्वेभिरग्ने स्वयशोभिरिद्धोऽदब्धेभिः पायुभिः पाह्यस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: urú ǀ te ǀ jráyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ eti ǀ budhnám ǀ vi-rócamānam ǀ mahiṣásya ǀ dhā́ma ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ sváyaśaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ iddháḥ ǀ ádabdhebhiḥ ǀ pāyú-bhiḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wide through the firmament spreads forth triumphant the far-resplendent strength of thee the Mighty. Kindled by us do thou preserve us, Agni, with all thy self-bright undiminished succours.
verses.wilson_translation: The vast and victorious radiance of you, the mighty one, pervades the firmament;Agni, who have been kindled by us, preserve us with all your undiminished and protecting glories.
verses.griffith_verse: Wide through the firmament spreads forth triumphant the far-resplendent strength of thee the Mighty. Kindled by us do thou preserve us, Agni, with all thy self-bright undiminished succours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: धन्वन्त्स्रोतः कृणुते गातुमूर्मिं शुक्रैरूर्मिभिरभि नक्षति क्षां ।विश्वा सनानि जठरेषु धत्तेऽंतर्नवासु चरति प्रसूषु ॥
verses.transliteration: dhánvan ǀ srótaḥ ǀ kṛṇute ǀ gātúm ǀ ūrmím ǀ śukráiḥ ǀ ūrmí-bhiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ nakṣati ǀ kṣā́m ǀvíśvā ǀ sánāni ǀ jaṭháreṣu ǀ dhatte ǀ antáḥ ǀ návāsu ǀ carati ǀ pra-sū́ṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: In dry spots he makes stream, and course, and torrent, and inundates the earth with floods that glisten. All ancient things within his maw he gathers, and moves among the new fresh-sprouting grasses.
verses.wilson_translation: He causes the waters to flow in a torrent through the sky, and with those pure waves he inundates the earth; he gathers all (articles of) food in the stomach, and for that purpose sojourns in the new-sprung parents (of the gain).
verses.griffith_verse: In dry spots he makes stream, and course, and torrent, and inundates the earth with floods that glisten. All ancient things within his maw he gathers, and moves among the new fresh-sprouting grasses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा नो अग्ने समिधा वृधानो रेवत्पावक श्रवसे वि भाहि ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ revát ǀ pāvaka ǀ śrávase ǀ ví ǀ bhāhi ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are the purifier, growing with the fuel we have supplied, blaze for the sake of (securing) food to us, who are possessed of wealth; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVI. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ९ कुत्स आङ्गिरसः। अग्निः, द्रविणोदा अग्निर्वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE in the ancient way by strength engendered, lo! straight hath taken to himself all wisdom.The waters and the bowl have made him friendly. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni. At Āyu's ancient call he by his wisdom gave all this progeny of men their being,And, by refulgent light, heaven and the waters. The Gods possessed the wealth. bestowing Agni. Praise him, ye Āryan folk, as chief performer of sacrifice adored and ever toiling,Well-tended, Son of Strength, the Constant Giver. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni. That Mātariśvan rich in wealth and treasure, light-winner, finds a pathway for his offspring.Guard of our folk, Father of earth and heaven. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni. Night and Dawn, changing each the other's colour, meeting together suckle one same Infant:Golden between the heaven and earth he shineth. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni. Root of wealth, gathering-place of treasures, banner of sacrifice, who grants the suppliant's wishes:Preserving him as their own life immortal, the Gods possessed the wealth-bestowing Agni. Now and of old the home of wealth, the mansion of what is born and what was born aforetime,Guard of what is and what will be hereafter,—the Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni. May the Wealth-Giver grant us conquering riches; may the Wealth-Giver grant us wealth with heroes.May the Wealth-Giver grant us food with offspring, and length of days may the Wealth-Giver send us. Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: स प्रत्नथा सहसा जायमानः सद्यः काव्यानि बळधत्त विश्वा ।आपश्च मित्रं धिषणा च साधंदेवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ pratná-thā ǀ sáhasā ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ kā́vyāni ǀ báṭ ǀ adhatta ǀ víśvā ǀā́paḥ ǀ ca ǀ mitrám ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ ca ǀ sādhan ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE in the ancient way by strength engendered, lo! straight hath taken to himself all wisdom. The waters and the bowl have made him friendly. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Engendered by force,Agniverily appropriates, as soon as born, the offerings of the sages; the waters and voice make him their friend, and the gods retain him as the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: HE in the ancient way by strength engendered, lo! straight hath taken to himself all wisdom. The waters and the bowl have made him friendly. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोरिमाः प्रजा अजनयन्मनूनां ।विवस्वता चक्षसा द्यामपश्च देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ pū́rvayā ǀ ni-vídā ǀ kavyátā ǀ āyóḥ ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ ajanayat ǀ mánūnām ǀvivásvatā ǀ cákṣasā ǀ dyā́m ǀ apáḥ ǀ ca ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: At Āyu's ancient call he by his wisdom gave all this progeny of men their being, And, by refulgent light, heaven and the waters. The Gods possessed the wealth. bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: (Propitiated) by the primitive laudatory hymn of Āyu, he created the progeny of Manus, and pervades, with his all-investing splendour, the heavens and the firmament; the gods retain Agnias the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: At Āyu's ancient call he by his wisdom gave all this progeny of men their being, And, by refulgent light, heaven and the waters. The Gods possessed the wealth. bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमीळत प्रथमं यज्ञसाधं विश आरीराहुतमृंजसानं ।ऊर्जः पुत्रं भरतं सृप्रदानुं देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ īḷata ǀ prathamám ǀ yajña-sā́dham ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́rīḥ ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ ṛñjasānám ǀūrjáḥ ǀ putrám ǀ bharatám ǀ sṛprá-dānum ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise him, ye Āryan folk, as chief performer of sacrifice adored and ever toiling, Well-tended, Son of Strength, the Constant Giver. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Approachinghim,let all men adore Agni, the chief (of the gods), the accomplisher of sacrifices, who is gratified by oblations and propitiated by praises--the offspring of food, the sustainer of (all men), the giver of continual gifts; the gods retain Agni as the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Praise him, ye Āryan folk, as chief performer of sacrifice adored and ever toiling, Well-tended, Son of Strength, the Constant Giver. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स मातरिश्वा पुरुवारपुष्टिर्विदद्गातुं तनयाय स्वर्वित् ।विशां गोपा जनिता रोदस्योर्देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ puruvā́ra-puṣṭiḥ ǀ vidát ǀ gātúm ǀ tánayāya ǀ svaḥ-vít ǀviśā́m ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ janitā́ ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: That Mātariśvan rich in wealth and treasure, light-winner, finds a pathway for his offspring. Guard of our folk, Father of earth and heaven. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agni, the dweller in the firmament, the nourisher with abundant benefits, the bestower ofsvarga, the protector of mankind, the progenitor of heaven and earth, instrumental uct my sons in the right way; the gods retain Agni as the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: That Mātariśvan rich in wealth and treasure, light-winner, finds a pathway for his offspring. Guard of our folk, Father of earth and heaven. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची ।द्यावाक्षामा रुक्मो अंतर्वि भाति देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: náktoṣásā ǀ várṇam ǀ āmémyāne ítyā-mémyāne ǀ dhāpáyete íti ǀ śíśum ǀ ékam ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀdyā́vākṣā́mā ǀ rukmáḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ ví ǀ bhāti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Night and Dawn, changing each the other's colour, meeting together suckle one same Infant: Golden between the heaven and earth he shineth. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The night and the day, mutually effacing each other's comlexion, give nourishment combined together, to one infant, who, radiant, shines between earth and heaven the gods retain Agnias the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Night and Dawn, changing each the other's colour, meeting together suckle one same Infant: Golden between the heaven and earth he shineth. The Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रायो बुध्नः संगमनो वसूनां यज्ञस्य केतुर्मन्मसाधनो वेः ।अमृतत्वं रक्षमाणास एनं देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyáḥ �� budhnáḥ ǀ sam-gámanaḥ ǀ vásūnām ǀ yajñásya ǀ ketúḥ ǀ manma-sā́dhanaḥ ǀ véríti véḥ ǀamṛta-tvám ǀ rákṣamāṇāsaḥ ǀ enam ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Root of wealth, gathering-place of treasures, banner of sacrifice, who grants the suppliant's wishes: Preserving him as their own life immortal, the Gods possessed the wealth-bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The source of opulence, the bestower of riches, the director of the sacrifice, the accomplisher of the desires (of the man) who has recourse to him; him the gods, preserving their immortality, retain as the giver of (sacrificial) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Root of wealth, gathering-place of treasures, banner of sacrifice, who grants the suppliant's wishes: Preserving him as their own life immortal, the Gods possessed the wealth-bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नू च पुरा च सदनं रयीणां जातस्य च जायमानस्य च क्षां ।सतश्च गोपां भवतश्च भूरेर्देवा अग्निं धारयंद्रविणोदां ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ ca ǀ purā́ ǀ ca ǀ sádanam ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ jātásya ǀ ca ǀ jā́yamānasya ǀ ca ǀ kṣā́m ǀsatáḥ ǀ ca ǀ gopā́m ǀ bhávataḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhārayan ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now and of old the home of wealth, the mansion of what is born and what was born aforetime, Guard of what is and what will be hereafter,—the Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods retain Agnias the giver of (sacrificial) wealth, who now is, and heretofore has been, the abode of riches, the receptacle of all that has been, and all that will be, born, and the preserver of all (that) exists, (as well as of all) that are coming into existence.
verses.griffith_verse: Now and of old the home of wealth, the mansion of what is born and what was born aforetime, Guard of what is and what will be hereafter,—the Gods possessed the wealth bestowing Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्रविणोदा द्रविणसस्तुरस्य द्रविणोदाः सनरस्य प्र यंसत् ।द्रविणोदा वीरवतीमिषं नो द्रविणोदा रासते दीर्घमायुः ॥
verses.transliteration: draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ dráviṇasaḥ ǀ turásya ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ sánarasya ǀ prá ǀ yaṃsat ǀdraviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ vīrá-vatīm ǀ íṣam ǀ naḥ ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ rāsate ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Wealth-Giver grant us conquering riches; may the Wealth-Giver grant us wealth with heroes. May the Wealth-Giver grant us food with offspring, and length of days may the Wealth-Giver send us.
verses.wilson_translation: May Draviṇodā grant us (a portion) of moveable wealth; may Draviṇodā grant us (a portion) of that which is stationary; may Draviṇodā give us food attended byprogeny; may Draviṇodā bestow upon us long life.
verses.griffith_verse: May the Wealth-Giver grant us conquering riches; may the Wealth-Giver grant us wealth with heroes. May the Wealth-Giver grant us food with offspring, and length of days may the Wealth-Giver send us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा नो अग्ने समिधा वृधानो रेवत्पावक श्रवसे वि भाहि ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ revát ǀ pāvaka ǀ śrávase ǀ ví ǀ bhāhi ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus,Agni, who are the purifier gowing with the fuel (we have supplied), blaze for the sake of securing food to us, who are possessed of wealth and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Fed with our fuel, purifying Agni, so blaze to us auspiciously for glory. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . CHASING with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us.May his light chase our sin away. For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee.May his light chase our sin away. Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice.May his light chase our sin away. So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live.May his light chase our sin away. As ever-conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side,May his light chase our sin away. To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere.May his light chase our sin away. O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship.May his light chase our sin away. As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o’er the flood.May his light chase our sin away.

verses.sanskrit: अप नः शोशुचदघमग्ने शुशुग्ध्या रयिं ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǀ ágne ǀ śuśugdhí ǀ ā́ ǀ rayím ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: CHASING with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: May our sin,Agni, be repented of; manifest riches to us; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: CHASING with light our sin away, O Agni, shine thou wealth on us. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुक्षेत्रिया सुगातुया वसूया च यजामहे ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: su-kṣetriyā́ ǀ sugātu-yā́ ǀ vasu-yā́ ǀ ca ǀ yajāmahe ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: We worship you for plural asant fields, for good roads, and for riches; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: For goodly fields, for pleasant homes, for wealth we sacrifice to thee. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यद्भंदिष्ठ एषां प्रास्माकासश्च सूरयः ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ bhándiṣṭhaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ prá ǀ asmā́kāsaḥ ǀ ca ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: (in like manner as, among these your worshippers,Kutsa) is the pre-eminent panegyrist, so are our encomiasts (of you) the most distinguished; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: Best praiser of all these be he; foremost, our chiefs who sacrifice. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यत्ते अग्ने सूरयो जायेमहि प्र ते वयं ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ jā́yemahi ǀ prá ǀ te ǀ vayám ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as your worshippers (are blessed with descentants), so may we, (by repeating your praise), obtain posterity; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: So that thy worshippers and we, thine, Agni, in our sons may live. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यदग्नेः सहस्वतो विश्वतो यंति भानवः ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ agnéḥ ǀ sáhasvataḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ yánti ǀ bhānávaḥ ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ever-conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side, May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: Since the victorious flames of Agnipenetrate universally, may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: As ever-conquering Agni's beams of splendour go to every side, May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि विश्वतोमुख विश्वतः परिभूरसि ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ viśvataḥ-mukha ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ pari-bhū́ḥ ǀ ási ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: You, whose countenance is turned to all sides, are our defender; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: To every side thy face is turned, thou art triumphant everywhere. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्विषो नो विश्वतोमुखाति नावेव पारय ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: dvíṣaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ viśvataḥ-mukha ǀ áti ǀ nāvā́-iva ǀ pāraya ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, whose countenance is turned to all sides, send off our adversaries, as if in a ship, (to the opposite shore); may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: O thou whose face looks every way, bear us past foes as in a ship. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नः सिंधुमिव नावयाति पर्षा स्वस्तये ।अप नः शोशुचदघं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ síndhum-iva ǀ nāváyā ǀ áti ǀ parṣa ǀ svastáye ǀápa ǀ naḥ ǀ śóśucat ǀ aghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o’er the flood. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you convey us in a ship across the sea, for our welfare; may our sin be repented of.
verses.griffith_verse: As in a ship, convey thou us for our advantage o’er the flood. May his light chase our sin away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . STILL in Vaiśvānara's grace may we continue: yea, he is King supreme o’er all things living.Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaiśvānara hath rivalry with Sūrya. Present in heaven, in earth, all-present Agni,—all plants that grow on ground hath he pervaded.May Agni, may Vaiśvānara with vigour, present, preserve us day and night from foemen. Be this thy truth, Vaiśvānara, to us-ward: let wealth in rich abundance gather round us.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः ।इतो जातो विश्वमिदं वि चष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ॥
verses.transliteration: vaiśvānarásya ǀ su-matáu ǀ syāma ǀ rā́jā ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ bhúvanānām ǀ abhi-śrī́ḥ ǀitáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀ vaiśvānaráḥ ǀ yatate ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: STILL in Vaiśvānara's grace may we continue: yea, he is King supreme o’er all things living. Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaiśvānara hath rivalry with Sūrya.
verses.wilson_translation: May we continue in the favour of Vaiśvānara, for verily he is the august sovereign of all beings; as soon as genitive rated from this (wood), he surveys the universe; he accompanies the rising sun.
verses.griffith_verse: STILL in Vaiśvānara's grace may we continue: yea, he is King supreme o’er all things living. Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaiśvānara hath rivalry with Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पृष्टो दिवि पृष्टो अग्निः पृथिव्यां पृष्टो विश्वा ओषधीरा विवेश ।वैश्वानरः सहसा पृष्टो अग्निः स नो दिवा स रिषः पातु नक्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛṣṭáḥ ǀ diví ǀ pṛṣṭáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ pṛṣṭáḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǀvaiśvānaráḥ ǀ sáhasā ǀ pṛṣṭáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dívā ǀ sáḥ ǀ riṣáḥ ǀ pātu ǀ náktam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Present in heaven, in earth, all-present Agni,—all plants that grow on ground hath he pervaded. May Agni, may Vaiśvānara with vigour, present, preserve us day and night from foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who is present in the sky, and present upon earth, and who, present, has pervaded all herbs; may the Agni Vaiśvānara, who is present in vigour, guard us night and day, against our enemies
verses.griffith_verse: Present in heaven, in earth, all-present Agni,—all plants that grow on ground hath he pervaded. May Agni, may Vaiśvānara with vigour, present, preserve us day and night from foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानर तव तत्सत्यमस्त्वस्मान्रायो मघवानः सचंतां ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: váiśvānara ǀ táva ǀ tát ǀ satyám ǀ astu ǀ asmā́n ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ sacantām ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be this thy truth, Vaiśvānara, to us-ward: let wealth in rich abundance gather round us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Vaiśvānara, may this (your adoration be attended) by real (fruit); may precious treasure wait uon us, and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve them to us].
verses.griffith_verse: Be this thy truth, Vaiśvānara, to us-ward: let wealth in rich abundance gather round us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १ कश्यपो मारीचः। अग्निः, जातवेदा अग्निर्वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FOR Jātavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant.May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.

verses.sanskrit: जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः ।स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिंधुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥
verses.transliteration: jātá-vedase ǀ sunavāma ǀ sómam ǀ arāti-yatáḥ ǀ ní ǀ dahāti ǀ védaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ duḥ-gā́ni ǀ víśvā ǀ nāvā́-iva ǀ síndhum ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ áti ǀ agníḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FOR Jātavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant. May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer oblations of Somato Jātavedas, may he consume the wealth of those who feel enmity against us; may he transport us over all difficulties; may Agniconvey us, as in a boat over a river, across all wickedness.
verses.griffith_verse: FOR Jātavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant. May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN C. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY he who hath his home with strength, the Mighty, the King supreme of earth and spacious heaven,Lord of true power, to he invoked in battles,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Whose way is unattainable like Sūrya's: he in each fight is the strong Vṛtra-slayer,Mightiest with his Friends in his own courses. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Whose paths go forth in their great might resistless, forthmilking, as it were, heaven's genial moisture.With manly strength triumphant, foe-subduer,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Among Aṅgirases he was the chiefest, a Friend with friends, mighty amid the mighty.Praiser mid praisers, honoured most of singers. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Strong with the Rudras as with his own children, in manly battle conquering his foemen 'With his close comrades doing deeds of glory,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Humbler of pride, exciter of the conflict, the Lord of heroes, God invoked of many,May he this day gain with our men the sunlight. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. His help hath made him cheerer in the battle, the folk have made him guardian of their comfort.Sole Lord is he of every holy service. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. To him the Hero, on high days of prowess, heroes for help and booty shall betake them.He hath found light even in the blinding darkness. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. He with his left hand checketh even the mighty, and with his right hand gathereth up the booty.Even with the humble he acquireth riches. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. With hosts on foot and cars he winneth treasures: well is he known this day by all the people.With manly might he conquereth those who hate him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. When in his ways with kinsmen or with strangers he speedeth to the fight, invoked of many,For gain of waters, and of sons and grandsons, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Awful and fierce, fiend-slayer, thunder-wielder, with boundless knowledge, hymned by hundreds, mighty,In strength like Soma, guard of the Five Peoples, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Winning the light, hitherward roars his thunder like the terrific mighty voice of Heaven.Rich gifts and treasures evermore attend him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. Whose home eternal through his strength surrounds him on every side, his laud, the earth and heaven,May he, delighted with our service, save us. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour. The limit of whose power not Gods by Godhead, nor mortal men have reached, nor yet the Waters.Both Earth and Heaven in vigour he surpasseth. May Indra, girt by Maruts, he our succour. The red and tawny mare, blaze-marked, high standing, celestial who, to bring Ṛjrāśva riches,Drew at the pole the chariot yoked with stallions, joyous, among the hosts of men was noted. The Vārṣāgiras unto thee, O Indra, the Mighty One, sing forth this laud to please thee,Ṛjrāśva with his fellows, Ambarīṣa, Surādhas, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna. He, much invoked, hath slain Dasyus and Śimyus, after his wont, and laid them low with arrows.The mighty Thunderer with his fair-complexioned friends won the land, the sunlight, and the waters. May Indra evermore be our protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: स यो वृषा वृष्ण्येभिः समोका महो दिवः पृथिव्याश्च सम्राट् ।सतीनसत्वा हव्यो भरेषु मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyebhiḥ ǀ sám-okāḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀsatīná-satvā ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ bháreṣu ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY he who hath his home with strength, the Mighty, the King supreme of earth and spacious heaven, Lord of true power, to he invoked in battles,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who is the showerer of desires, who is co-dweller with (all) energies the supreme ruler over the vast heaven and earth, the sender of water, and to be invoked in battles; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY he who hath his home with strength, the Mighty, the King supreme of earth and spacious heaven, Lord of true power, to he invoked in battles,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्यानाप्तः सूर्यस्येव यामो भरेभरे वृत्रहा शुष्मो अस्ति ।वृषंतमः सखिभिः स्वेभिरेवैर्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ ánāptaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya-iva ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ bháre-bhare ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ śúṣmaḥ ǀ ásti ǀvṛ́ṣan-tamaḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ svébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose way is unattainable like Sūrya's: he in each fight is the strong Vṛtra-slayer, Mightiest with his Friends in his own courses. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: May he whose course, like that of the sun, is not to be overtaken, who in every battle is the slayer of his foes, the witherer (of opponents), who, with his swift-moving friends (the winds), is the most bountiful (of givers); may Indra, associated with the Marutsbe our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Whose way is unattainable like Sūrya's: he in each fight is the strong Vṛtra-slayer, Mightiest with his Friends in his own courses. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवो न यस्य रेतसो दुघानाः पंथासो यंति शवसापरीताः ।तरद्द्वेषाः सासहिः पौंस्येभिर्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ yásya ǀ rétasaḥ ǀ dúghānāḥ ǀ pánthāsaḥ ǀ yánti ǀ śávasā ǀ ápari-itāḥ ǀtarát-dveṣāḥ ǀ sasahíḥ ǀ páuṃsyebhiḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose paths go forth in their great might resistless, forthmilking, as it were, heaven's genial moisture. With manly strength triumphant, foe-subduer,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, whose rays, powerful and unattainable issue forth like those of the sun, milking (the clouds); he who is victorious over his adversaries, triumphant by his manly energies; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Whose paths go forth in their great might resistless, forthmilking, as it were, heaven's genial moisture. With manly strength triumphant, foe-subduer,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो अंगिरोभिरंगिरस्तमो भूद्वृषा वृषभिः सखिभिः सखा सन् ।ऋग्मिभिर्ऋग्मी गातुभिर्ज्येष्ठो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ ǀ bhūt ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ sán ǀṛgmí-bhiḥ ǀ ṛgmī́ ǀ gātú-bhiḥ ǀ jyéṣṭhaḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Among Aṅgirases he was the chiefest, a Friend with friends, mighty amid the mighty. Praiser mid praisers, honoured most of singers. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: He is the swiftest among the swift, most bountiful amongst the bountiful, a friend with friends, venerable among those who claim veneration, and pre-eminent among those deserving of praise; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Among Aṅgirases he was the chiefest, a Friend with friends, mighty amid the mighty. Praiser mid praisers, honoured most of singers. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स सूनुभिर्न रुद्रेभिर्ऋभ्वा नृषाह्ये सासह्वाँ अमित्रान् ।सनीळेभिः श्रवस्यानि तूर्वन्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ sūnú-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀ nṛ-sáhye ǀ sasahvā́n ǀ amítrān ǀsá-nīḷebhiḥ ǀ śravasyā́ni ǀ tū́rvan ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong with the Rudras as with his own children, in manly battle conquering his foemen ' With his close comrades doing deeds of glory,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty with the Rudras, as if with his sons, victorious in battle over his enemies, and sending down with his co-dwellers (the waters which are productive of) food;Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong with the Rudras as with his own children, in manly battle conquering his foemen ' With his close comrades doing deeds of glory,—may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स मन्युमीः समदनस्य कर्तास्माकेभिर्नृभिः सूर्यं सनत् ।अस्मिन्नहन्त्सत्पतिः पुरुहूतो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ manyu-mī́ḥ ǀ sa-mádanasya ǀ kartā́ ǀ asmā́kebhiḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ sanat ǀasmín ǀ áhan ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Humbler of pride, exciter of the conflict, the Lord of heroes, God invoked of many, May he this day gain with our men the sunlight. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, the represser of (hostile) wrath, the author of war, the protector of the good, the invoked of many, share with our people on this day the (light of the) sun; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Humbler of pride, exciter of the conflict, the Lord of heroes, God invoked of many, May he this day gain with our men the sunlight. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमूतयो रणयंछूरसातौ तं क्षेमस्य क्षितयः कृण्वत त्रां ।स विश्वस्य करुणस्येश एको मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ raṇayat ǀ śū́ra-sātau ǀ tám ǀ kṣémasya ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ kṛṇvata ǀ trā́m ǀsáḥ ǀ víśvasya ǀ karúṇasya ǀ īśe ǀ ékaḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: His help hath made him cheerer in the battle, the folk have made him guardian of their comfort. Sole Lord is he of every holy service. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Hi, his allies, the Maruts, animate in battle; him, men regard as the preserver of their property; he alone presides over every act of worship; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: His help hath made him cheerer in the battle, the folk have made him guardian of their comfort. Sole Lord is he of every holy service. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमप्संत शवस उत्सवेषु नरो नरमवसे तं धनाय ।सो अंधे चित्तमसि ज्योतिर्विदन्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ apsanta ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ut-savéṣu ǀ náraḥ ǀ náram ǀ ávase ǀ tám ǀ dhánāya ǀsáḥ ǀ andhé ǀ cit ǀ támasi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ vidat ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the Hero, on high days of prowess, heroes for help and booty shall betake them. He hath found light even in the blinding darkness. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: To him, a leader (to victory), his worshippers apply in contests of strength for protection and for wealth, as he grants them the light (of conquest) in the bewildering darkness (of battle); may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: To him the Hero, on high days of prowess, heroes for help and booty shall betake them. He hath found light even in the blinding darkness. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स सव्येन यमति व्राधतश्चित्स दक्षिणे संगृभीता कृतानि ।स कीरिणा चित्सनिता धनानि मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ savyéna ǀ yamati ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ cit ǀ sáḥ ǀ dakṣiṇé ǀ sám-gṛbhītā ǀ kṛtā́ni ǀsáḥ ǀ kīríṇā ǀ cit ǀ sánitā ǀ dhánāni ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with his left hand checketh even the mighty, and with his right hand gathereth up the booty. Even with the humble he acquireth riches. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: With his lefthandhe restrains the malignant, with his right he receives the (sacrificial) offerings; he is the giver of riches, (when propitiated) by one who celebrates his praise; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: He with his left hand checketh even the mighty, and with his right hand gathereth up the booty. Even with the humble he acquireth riches. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स ग्रामेभिः सनिता स रथेभिर्विदे विश्वाभिः कृष्टिभिर्न्वद्य ।स पौंस्येभिरभिभूरशस्तीर्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ grā́mebhiḥ ǀ sánitā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀ vidé ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ kṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀ nú ǀ adyá ǀsáḥ ǀ páuṃsyebhiḥ ǀ abhi-bhū́ḥ ǀ áśastīḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With hosts on foot and cars he winneth treasures: well is he known this day by all the people. With manly might he conquereth those who hate him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: He, along with his attendants, is a benefactor; he is quickly recognized by all men today, through his chariots; by his manly energies he is victor over unruly (adversaries); may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: With hosts on foot and cars he winneth treasures: well is he known this day by all the people. With manly might he conquereth those who hate him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स जामिभिर्यत्समजाति मीळ्हेऽजामिभिर्वा पुरुहूत एवैः ।अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेषे मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ jāmí-bhiḥ ǀ yát ǀ sam-ájāti ǀ mīḷhé ǀ ájāmi-bhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀapā́m ǀ tokásya ǀ tánayasya ǀ jeṣé ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When in his ways with kinsmen or with strangers he speedeth to the fight, invoked of many, For gain of waters, and of sons and grandsons, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoked by many, he goes to battle with his kinsmen, or with (followers) not of his kindred; he secures the (triumph) of those who trust him, and of their sons and grandsons; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: When in his ways with kinsmen or with strangers he speedeth to the fight, invoked of many, For gain of waters, and of sons and grandsons, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स वज्रभृद्दस्युहा भीम उग्रः सहस्रचेताः शतनीथ ऋभ्वा ।चम्रीषो न शवसा पांचजन्यो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vajra-bhṛ́t ǀ dasyu-hā́ ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ sahásra-cetāḥ ǀ śatá-nīthaḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀcamrīṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ śávasā ǀ pā́ñca-janyaḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Awful and fierce, fiend-slayer, thunder-wielder, with boundless knowledge, hymned by hundreds, mighty, In strength like Soma, guard of the Five Peoples, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: He is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of robbers, fearful and fierce, knowing many things, much eulogized and mighty, and like the Soma, inspiring the five classes of beings with vigour; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Awful and fierce, fiend-slayer, thunder-wielder, with boundless knowledge, hymned by hundreds, mighty, In strength like Soma, guard of the Five Peoples, may Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वज्रः क्रंदति स्मत्स्वर्षा दिवो न त्वेषो रवथः शिमीवान् ।तं सचंते सनयस्तं धनानि मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: tásya ǀ vájraḥ ǀ krandati ǀ smát ǀ svaḥ-sā́ḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ tveṣáḥ ǀ raváthaḥ ǀ śímī-vān ǀtám ǀ sacante ǀ sanáyaḥ ǀ tám ǀ dhánāni ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Winning the light, hitherward roars his thunder like the terrific mighty voice of Heaven. Rich gifts and treasures evermore attend him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: His thunderbolt draws cries (from his enemies), he is the sender of good waters, brilliant as (the luminary) of heaven, the thunderer, the promoter of beneficent acts, upon him do donations and riches attend; may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Winning the light, hitherward roars his thunder like the terrific mighty voice of Heaven. Rich gifts and treasures evermore attend him. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद्रोदसी विश्वतः सीं ।स पारिषत्क्रतुभिर्मंदसानो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ ájasram ǀ śávasā ǀ mā́nam ǀ ukthám ǀ pari-bhuját ǀ ródasī íti ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ sīm ǀsáḥ ǀ pāriṣat ǀ krátu-bhiḥ ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose home eternal through his strength surrounds him on every side, his laud, the earth and heaven, May he, delighted with our service, save us. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, of whom the excellent measure (of all things), through strength, eternally and everywhere cherishes heaven and earth, propitiated by our acts, convey us beyond (evil); may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Whose home eternal through his strength surrounds him on every side, his laud, the earth and heaven, May he, delighted with our service, save us. May Indra, girt by Maruts, be our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अंतमापुः ।स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ devátā ǀ ná ǀ mártāḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ caná ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ántam ǀ āpúḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ pra-ríkvā ǀ tvákṣasā ǀ kṣmáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ca ǀ marútvān ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The limit of whose power not Gods by Godhead, nor mortal men have reached, nor yet the Waters. Both Earth and Heaven in vigour he surpasseth. May Indra, girt by Maruts, he our succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Nor gods, nor men, nor waters, have reached the limit of the strength of that beneficent (divinity) for he surpasses both earth and heaven by his foe-consuming (might); may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: The limit of whose power not Gods by Godhead, nor mortal men have reached, nor yet the Waters. Both Earth and Heaven in vigour he surpasseth. May Indra, girt by Maruts, he our succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रोहिच्छ्यावा सुमदंशुर्ललामीर्द्युक्षा राय ऋज्राश्वस्य ।वृषण्वंतं बिभ्रती धूर्षु रथं मंद्रा चिकेत नाहुषीषु विक्षु ॥
verses.transliteration: rohít ǀ śyāvā́ ǀ sumát-aṃśuḥ ǀ lalāmī́ḥ ǀ dyukṣā́ ǀ rāyé ǀ ṛjrá-aśvasya ǀvṛ́ṣaṇ-vantam ǀ bíbhratī ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ rátham ǀ mandrā́ ǀ ciketa ǀ nā́huṣīṣu ǀ vikṣú ǁ
verses.english_translation: The red and tawny mare, blaze-marked, high standing, celestial who, to bring Ṛjrāśva riches, Drew at the pole the chariot yoked with stallions, joyous, among the hosts of men was noted.
verses.wilson_translation: The red and black coursers, long-limbed, well-caparisoned, and celestial, an dharnessed, well-plural ased, to the yoke of the chariot in which the showerer of benefits is conveyed, for the enrichment ofṚjrāśva, an dis recognized amongst human hosts.
verses.griffith_verse: The red and tawny mare, blaze-marked, high standing, celestial who, to bring Ṛjrāśva riches, Drew at the pole the chariot yoked with stallions, joyous, among the hosts of men was noted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतत्त्यत्त इंद्र वृष्ण उक्थं वार्षागिरा अभि गृणंति राधः ।ऋज्राश्वः प्रष्टिभिरंबरीषः सहदेवो भयमानः सुराधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: etát ǀ tyát ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ ukthám ǀ vārṣāgirā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ gṛṇanti ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀṛjrá-aśvaḥ ǀ práṣṭi-bhiḥ ǀ ambarī́ṣaḥ ǀ sahá-devaḥ ǀ bháyamānaḥ ǀ su-rā́dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Vārṣāgiras unto thee, O Indra, the Mighty One, sing forth this laud to please thee, Ṛjrāśva with his fellows, Ambarīṣa, Surādhas, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, showerer (of benefits), the Vārṣāgirās,Ṛjrāśvaand his companions,Ambariṣa,Sahadeva, Bhayamāna, and Surādhās, address to you this propitiatory praise].
verses.griffith_verse: The Vārṣāgiras unto thee, O Indra, the Mighty One, sing forth this laud to please thee, Ṛjrāśva with his fellows, Ambarīṣa, Surādhas, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दस्यूंछिम्यूंश्च पुरुहूत एवैर्हत्वा पृथिव्यां शर्वा नि बर्हीत् ।सनत्क्षेत्रं सखिभिः श्वित्न्येभिः सनत्सूर्यं सनदपः सुवज्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: dásyūn ǀ śímyūn ǀ ca ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀ hatvā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ śárvā ǀ ní ǀ barhīt ǀsánat ǀ kṣétram ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ śvitnyébhiḥ ǀ sánat ǀ sū́ryam ǀ sánat ǀ apáḥ ǀ su-vájraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, much invoked, hath slain Dasyus and Śimyus, after his wont, and laid them low with arrows. The mighty Thunderer with his fair-complexioned friends won the land, the sunlight, and the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is invoked by many, attended by the moving (Maruts), having attacked the Dasyusand the Śimyus, slew them with his thunderbolt; the thunderer then divided the fields with his white-complexioned friends, and rescued the sun and set free the water.
verses.griffith_verse: He, much invoked, hath slain Dasyus and Śimyus, after his wont, and laid them low with arrows. The mighty Thunderer with his fair-complexioned friends won the land, the sunlight, and the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वाहेंद्रो अधिवक्ता नो अस्त्वपरिह्वृताः सनुयाम वाजं ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvā́hā ǀ índraḥ ǀ adhi-vaktā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ ápari-hvṛtāḥ ǀ sanuyāma ǀ vā́jam ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra evermore be our protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrabe daily our vindicator, and may we, with undiverted course, enjoy (abundant) food; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, preserve it to us].
verses.griffith_verse: May Indra evermore be our protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ११ कुत्स आङ्गिरसः। इन्द्रः (१ गर्भस्रावि ण्युपनिषद्)। जगती, ८-११ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SING, with oblation, praise to him who maketh glad, who with Ṛjiśvan drove the dusky brood away.Fain for help, him the strong whose right hand wields the bolt, him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. Indra, who with triumphant wrath smote Vyaṁsa down, and Śambara, and Pipru the unrighteous one;Who extirpated Śuṣṇa the insatiate,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. He whose great work of manly might is heaven and earth, and Varuṇa and Sūrya keep his holy law;Indra, whose law the rivers follow as they flow,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. He who is Lord and Master of the steeds and kine, honoured—the firm and sure—at every holy act;Stayer even of the strong who pours no offering out,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. He who is Lord of all the world that moves and breathes, who for the Brahman first before all found the Cows;Indra who cast the Dasyus down beneath his feet,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. Whom cowards must invoke and valiant men of war, invoked by those who conquer and by those who flee;Indra, to whom all beings turn their constant thought,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. Refulgent in the Rudras’ region he proceeds, and with the Rudras through the wide space speeds the Dame.The hymn of praise extols Indra the far-renowned: him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend. O girt by Maruts, whether thou delight thee in loftiest gathering-place or lowly dwelling,Come thence unto our rite, true boon-bestower: through love of thee have we prepared oblations. We, fain for thee, strong Indra, have pressed Soma, and, O thou sought with prayer, have made oblations.Now at this sacrifice, with all thy Maruts, on sacred grass, O team-borne God, rejoice thee. Rejoice thee with thine own Bay Steeds, O Indra, unclose thy jaws and let thy lips be open.Thou with the fair cheek, let thy Bay Steeds bring thee: gracious to us, he pleased with our oblation. Guards of the camp whose praisers are the Maruts, may we through Indra, get ourselves the booty.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: प्र मंदिने पितुमदर्चता वचो यः कृष्णगर्भा निरहन्नृजिश्वना ।अवस्यवो वृषणं वज्रदक्षिणं मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ mandíne ǀ pitu-mát ǀ arcata ǀ vácaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ kṛṣṇá-garbhāḥ ǀ niḥ-áhan ǀ ṛjíśvanā ǀavasyávaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vájra-dakṣiṇam ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: SING, with oblation, praise to him who maketh glad, who with Ṛjiśvan drove the dusky brood away. Fain for help, him the strong whose right hand wields the bolt, him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer adoration with oblations to him who is delighted (with praise), who, with Ṛjiśvan, destroyed the pregnant wives of Kṛṣṇa; desirous of protection, we invoke, to become our friend, him, who is the showerer (of benefits), who holds the thunderbolt in his righthand, attended by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: SING, with oblation, praise to him who maketh glad, who with Ṛjiśvan drove the dusky brood away. Fain for help, him the strong whose right hand wields the bolt, him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो व्यंसं जाहृषाणेन मन्युना यः शंबरं यो अहन्पिप्रुमव्रतं ।इंद्रो यः शुष्णमशुषं न्यावृणङ्मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवा���हे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ví-aṃsam ǀ jahṛṣāṇéna ǀ manyúnā ǀ yáḥ ǀ śámbaram ǀ yáḥ ǀ áhan ǀ píprum ǀ avratám ǀíndraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ aśúṣam ǀ ní ǀ ávṛṇak ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who with triumphant wrath smote Vyaṁsa down, and Śambara, and Pipru the unrighteous one; Who extirpated Śuṣṇa the insatiate,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke to be our friend,Indra, who is attended by the Maruts; he who, with increasing wrath, slew the mutilated VṛtraandŚambara, and the unrighteous Pipru, and who extirpated the unabsorbableŚuṣṇa
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, who with triumphant wrath smote Vyaṁsa down, and Śambara, and Pipru the unrighteous one; Who extirpated Śuṣṇa the insatiate,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य द्यावापृथिवी पौंस्यं महद्यस्य व्रते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः ।यस्येंद्रस्य सिंधवः सश्चति व्रतं मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ mahát ǀ yásya ǀ vraté ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀyásya ǀ índrasya ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ sáścati ǀ vratám ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whose great work of manly might is heaven and earth, and Varuṇa and Sūrya keep his holy law; Indra, whose law the rivers follow as they flow,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke to become our friend,Indra, who is attended by the Maruts; whose great power (pervades) heaven and earth, in whose service Varuṇaand Sūryaare steadfast, and whose commadn the rivers obey.
verses.griffith_verse: He whose great work of manly might is heaven and earth, and Varuṇa and Sūrya keep his holy law; Indra, whose law the rivers follow as they flow,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अश्वानां यो गवां गोपतिर्वशी य आरितः कर्मणिकर्मणि स्थिरः ।वीळोश्चिदिंद्रो यो असुन्वतो वधो मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ áśvānām ǀ yáḥ ǀ gávām ǀ gó-patiḥ ǀ vaśī́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ āritáḥ ǀ kármaṇi-karmaṇi ǀ sthiráḥ ǀvīḷóḥ ǀ cit ǀ índraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásunvataḥ ǀ vadháḥ ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is Lord and Master of the steeds and kine, honoured—the firm and sure—at every holy act; Stayer even of the strong who pours no offering out,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Who is th elord over all horses and cattle, who is independent, who, propitiated by praise, is constant in every act, and who is the slayer of the obstinate abstainer from libations; we invoke to become our friend,Indra, attended by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: He who is Lord and Master of the steeds and kine, honoured—the firm and sure—at every holy act; Stayer even of the strong who pours no offering out,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो विश्वस्य जगतः प्राणतस्पतिर्यो ब्रह्मणे प्रथमो गा अविंदत् ।इंद्रो यो दस्यूँरधराँ अवातिरन्मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ víśvasya ǀ jágataḥ ǀ prāṇatáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ brahmáṇe ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ávindat ǀíndraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ dásyūn ǀ ádharān ǀ ava-átirat ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is Lord of all the world that moves and breathes, who for the Brahman first before all found the Cows; Indra who cast the Dasyus down beneath his feet,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Who is the lord of all moving and breathing creatures, who first recovered the (stolen) kine for the Brāhmaṇa, and who slew the humbled Dasyus; we invoke to become our friend,Indra, attended by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: He who is Lord of all the world that moves and breathes, who for the Brahman first before all found the Cows; Indra who cast the Dasyus down beneath his feet,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः शूरेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भीरुभिर्यो धावद्भिर्हूयते यश्च जिग्युभिः ।इंद्रं यं विश्वा भुवनाभि संदधुर्मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ śū́rebhiḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhīrú-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ dhā́vat-bhiḥ ǀ hūyáte ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ jigyúbhiḥ ǀíndram ǀ yám ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhí ǀ sam-dadhúḥ ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom cowards must invoke and valiant men of war, invoked by those who conquer and by those who flee; Indra, to whom all beings turn their constant thought,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, by the vanquished and by victors, and whom all eings plural ce before them (in their ites); we invoke to become our friend,Indra, attended by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: Whom cowards must invoke and valiant men of war, invoked by those who conquer and by those who flee; Indra, to whom all beings turn their constant thought,—him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रुद्राणामेति प्रदिशा विचक्षणो रुद्रेभिर्योषा तनुते पृथु ज्रयः ।इंद्रं मनीषा अभ्यर्चति श्रुतं मरुत्वंतं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: rudrā́ṇām ǀ eti ǀ pra-díśā ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ yóṣā ǀ tanute ǀ pṛthú ǀ jráyaḥ ǀíndram ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ abhí ǀ arcati ǀ śrutám ǀ marútvantam ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Refulgent in the Rudras’ region he proceeds, and with the Rudras through the wide space speeds the Dame. The hymn of praise extols Indra the far-renowned: him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: The radiant Indraproceeds (along the firmament) with the manifestation of the Rudras; through the Rudras, speech spreads with more expansive celerity, and praise glorifies the renowned Indra; him, attended by the Maruts, we invoke to become our friend.
verses.griffith_verse: Refulgent in the Rudras’ region he proceeds, and with the Rudras through the wide space speeds the Dame. The hymn of praise extols Indra the far-renowned: him girt by Maruts we invoke to be our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वा मरुत्वः परमे सधस्थे यद्वावमे वृजने मादयासे ।अत आ याह्यध्वरं नो अच्छा त्वाया हविश्चकृमा सत्यराधः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vā ǀ marutvaḥ ǀ paramé ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ avamé ǀ vṛjáne ǀ mādáyāse ǀátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ adhvarám ǀ naḥ ǀ áccha ǀ tvā-yā́ ǀ havíḥ ǀ cakṛma ǀ satya-rādhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O girt by Maruts, whether thou delight thee in loftiest gathering-place or lowly dwelling, Come thence unto our rite, true boon-bestower: through love of thee have we prepared oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Attended by the winds, giver of true wealth, whether you may be plural ased (to dwell) in a stately mansion or in a lowly dwelling, come to our sacrifice; desirous of your presence, we offer you oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: O girt by Maruts, whether thou delight thee in loftiest gathering-place or lowly dwelling, Come thence unto our rite, true boon-bestower: through love of thee have we prepared oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वायेंद्र सोमं सुषुमा सुदक्ष त्वाया हविश्चकृमा ब्रह्मवाहः ।अधा नियुत्वः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मिन्यज्ञे बर्हिषि मादयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā-yā́ ǀ indra ǀ sómam ǀ susuma ǀ su-dakṣa ǀ tvā-yā́ ǀ havíḥ ǀ cakṛma ǀ brahma-vāhaḥ ǀádha ǀ niyutvaḥ ǀ sá-gaṇaḥ ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ barhíṣi ǀ mādayasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: We, fain for thee, strong Indra, have pressed Soma, and, O thou sought with prayer, have made oblations. Now at this sacrifice, with all thy Maruts, on sacred grass, O team-borne God, rejoice thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of you,Indra, who are possessed of excellent strenghth, we pour forth to you libations desirous of you, who are obtained by prayer, we offer you oblations; therefore, do you, who are possessed of horses, sit down with plural asure upon the sacred grass, attended by the Maruts, at this sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: We, fain for thee, strong Indra, have pressed Soma, and, O thou sought with prayer, have made oblations. Now at this sacrifice, with all thy Maruts, on sacred grass, O team-borne God, rejoice thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इंद्र वि ष्यस्व शिप्रे वि सृजस्व धेने ।आ त्वा सुशिप्र हरयो वहंतूशन्हव्यानि प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: mādáyasva ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ ví ǀ syasva ǀ śípre íti ǀ ví ǀ sṛjasva ǀ dhéne íti ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ su-śipra ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ vahantu ǀ uśán ǀ havyā́ni ǀ práti ǀ naḥ ǀ juṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rejoice thee with thine own Bay Steeds, O Indra, unclose thy jaws and let thy lips be open. Thou with the fair cheek, let thy Bay Steeds bring thee: gracious to us, he pleased with our oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Rejoice,Indra, with the steeds who are of your nature; open your jaws, set wide your throat (to drink Soma); let your horses bring you, who have a handsome chin, (hither), and, benignant towards us, be plural ased by our oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Rejoice thee with thine own Bay Steeds, O Indra, unclose thy jaws and let thy lips be open. Thou with the fair cheek, let thy Bay Steeds bring thee: gracious to us, he pleased with our oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य वृजनस्य गोपा वयमिंद्रेण सनुयाम वाजं ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: marút-stotrasya ǀ vṛjánasya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ vayám ǀ índreṇa ǀ sanuyāma ǀ vā́jam ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Guards of the camp whose praisers are the Maruts, may we through Indra, get ourselves the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Protected by that destroyer (of foes), who is united in praise with the Maruts, we may receive sustenance from Indra; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi-- ocean, earth and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Guards of the camp whose praisers are the Maruts, may we through Indra, get ourselves the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud.In Indra, yea in him victorious through his strength, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed. The Seven Rivers bear his glory far and wide, and heaven and sky and earth display his comely form.The Sun and Moon in change alternate run their course, that we, O Indra, may behold and may have faith. Maghavan, grant us that same car to bring us spoil, thy conquering car in which we joy in shock of fight.Thou, Indra, whom our hearts praise highly in the war, grant shelter, Maghavan, to us who love thee well. Encourage thou our side in every fight: may we, with thee for our ally, conquer the foeman's host.Indra, bestow on us joy and felicity break down, O Maghavan, the vigour of our foes. For here in divers ways these men invoking thee, holder of treasures, sing hymns to win thine aid.Ascend the car that thou mayest bring spoil to us, for, Indra, thy fixt winneth the victory. His arms win kine, his power is boundless in each act best, with a hundred helps, waker of battle's dinIs Indra: none may rival him in mighty strength. Hence, eager for the spoil the people call on him. Thy glory, Maghavan, exceeds a hundred yea, more than a hundred, than a thousand mid the folk,The great bowl hath inspirited thee boundlessly: so mayst thou slay the Vṛtras, breaker-down of forts! Of thy great might there is a three counterpart, the three earths, Lord men and the three realms of light.Above this whole world, Indra, thou hast waxen great: without a foe art thou, nature, from of old. We invocate thee first among the Deities: thou hast become a mighty Conquer in fight.May Indra fill with spirit this our singer's heart, and make our car impetuous, foremost in attack. Thou hast prevailed, and hast not kept the booty back, in trifling battles in those of great account.We make thee keen, the Mighty One, succour us: inspire us, Maghavan, when we defy the foe. May Indra evermore be our Protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: इमां ते धियं प्र भरे महो महीमस्य स्तोत्रे धिषणा यत्त आनजे ।तमुत्सवे च प्रसवे च सासहिमिंद्रं देवासः शवसामदन्ननु ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ te ǀ dhíyam ǀ prá ǀ bhare ǀ maháḥ ǀ mahī́m ǀ asyá ǀ stotré ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ ānajé ǀtám ǀ ut-savé ǀ ca ǀ pra-savé ǀ ca ǀ sasahím ǀ índram ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ amadan ǀ ánu ǁ
verses.english_translation: To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud. In Indra, yea in him victorious through his strength, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed.
verses.wilson_translation: I address to you, who are mighty, this excellent hymn, because your understanding has been gratified by my praise; the gods have successively delighted that victorious Indrawith the power (of praise), for the sake of prosperity and wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud. In Indra, yea in him victorious through his strength, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य श्रवो नद्यः सप्त बिभ्रति द्यावाक्षामा पृथिवी दर्शतं वपुः ।अस्मे सूर्याचंद्रमसाभिचक्षे श्रद्धे कमिंद्र चरतो वितर्तुरं ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ saptá ǀ bibhrati ǀ dyā́vākṣā́mā ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ darśatám ǀ vápuḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ sūryācandramásā ǀ abhi-cákṣe ǀ śraddhé ǀ kám ǀ indra ǀ carataḥ ǀ vi-tarturám ǁ
