verses.english_translation: The Seven Rivers bear his glory far and wide, and heaven and sky and earth display his comely form. The Sun and Moon in change alternate run their course, that we, O Indra, may behold and may have faith.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven rivers display his glory; heaven, and earth, and sky display his visible form; the sun and moon,Indra,perform their revolution, that we may see, and have faith in what we see.
verses.griffith_verse: The Seven Rivers bear his glory far and wide, and heaven and sky and earth display his comely form. The Sun and Moon in change alternate run their course, that we, O Indra, may behold and may have faith.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं स्मा रथं मघवन्प्राव सातये जैत्रं यं ते अनुमदाम संगमे ।आजा न इंद्र मनसा पुरुष्टुत त्वायद्भ्यो मघवंछर्म यच्छ नः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ sma ǀ rátham ǀ magha-van ǀ prá ǀ ava ǀ sātáye ǀ jáitram ǀ yám ǀ te ǀ anu-mádāma ǀ sam-gamé ǀājā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ mánasā ǀ puru-stuta ǀ tvāyát-bhyaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ śárma ǀ yaccha ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavan, grant us that same car to bring us spoil, thy conquering car in which we joy in shock of fight. Thou, Indra, whom our hearts praise highly in the war, grant shelter, Maghavan, to us who love thee well.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavan, despatch your chariot to bring us wealth; that victorious car which,Indra, who are much praised by us in time of war, we rejoice to behold in battle; do you, Maghavan, grant happiness to those who are devoted to you.
verses.griffith_verse: Maghavan, grant us that same car to bring us spoil, thy conquering car in which we joy in shock of fight. Thou, Indra, whom our hearts praise highly in the war, grant shelter, Maghavan, to us who love thee well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयं जयेम त्वया युजा वृतमस्माकमंशमुदवा भरेभरे ।अस्मभ्यमिंद्र वरिवः सुगं कृधि प्र शत्रूणां मघवन्वृष्ण्या रुज ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ jayema ǀ tváyā ǀ yujā́ ǀ vṛ́tam ǀ asmā́kam ǀ áṃśam ǀ út ǀ ava ǀ bháre-bhare ǀasmábhyam ǀ indra ǀ várivaḥ ǀ su-gám ǀ kṛdhi ǀ prá ǀ śátrūṇām ǀ magha-van ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyā ǀ ruja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Encourage thou our side in every fight: may we, with thee for our ally, conquer the foeman's host. Indra, bestow on us joy and felicity break down, O Maghavan, the vigour of our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, having you for our ally, overcome our adversaries in every encounter; defend our portion; render riches easily attained by us; enfeeble Maghavan, the vigour of our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Encourage thou our side in every fight: may we, with thee for our ally, conquer the foeman's host. Indra, bestow on us joy and felicity break down, O Maghavan, the vigour of our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाना हि त्वा हवमाना जना इमे धनानां धर्तरवसा विपन्यवः ।अस्माकं स्मा रथमा तिष्ठ सातये जैत्रं हींद्र निभृतं मनस्तव ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́nā ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ hávamānāḥ ǀ jánāḥ ǀ imé ǀ dhánānām ǀ dhartaḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ vipanyávaḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ sma ǀ rátham ǀ ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ sātáye ǀ jáitram ǀ hí ǀ indra ǀ ní-bhṛtam ǀ mánaḥ ǀ táva ǁ
verses.english_translation: For here in divers ways these men invoking thee, holder of treasures, sing hymns to win thine aid. Ascend the car that thou mayest bring spoil to us, for, Indra, thy fixt winneth the victory.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the men who call upon you for your protection; mount your car to bring wealth to us, for your mind,Indra, is composed, and resolved of victory.
verses.griffith_verse: For here in divers ways these men invoking thee, holder of treasures, sing hymns to win thine aid. Ascend the car that thou mayest bring spoil to us, for, Indra, thy fixt winneth the victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गोजिता बाहू अमितक्रतुः सिमः कर्मन्कर्मंछतमूतिः खजंकरः ।अकल्प इंद्रः प्रतिमानमोजसाथा जना वि ह्वयंते सिषासवः ॥
verses.transliteration: go-jítā ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ ámita-kratuḥ ǀ simáḥ ǀ kárman-karman ǀ śatám-ūtiḥ ǀ khajam-karáḥ ǀakalpáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ ójasā ǀ átha ǀ jánāḥ ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ sisāsávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: His arms win kine, his power is boundless in each act best, with a hundred helps, waker of battle's din Is Indra: none may rival him in mighty strength. Hence, eager for the spoil the people call on him.
verses.wilson_translation: Your arms are the winners of cattle, your wisdom is unbounded, you are most excellent, the granter of a hundred aids in every rite; the author of war,Indrais uncontrolled; the type of strength; wherefore men, who are desirous of wealth, invoke him in various ways.
verses.griffith_verse: His arms win kine, his power is boundless in each act best, with a hundred helps, waker of battle's din Is Indra: none may rival him in mighty strength. Hence, eager for the spoil the people call on him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्ते शतान्मघवन्नुच्च भूयस उत्सहस्राद्रिरिचे कृष्टिषु श्रवः ।अमात्रं त्वा धिषणा तित्विषे मह्यधा वृत्राणि जिघ्नसे पुरंदर ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ te ǀ śatā́t ǀ magha-van ǀ út ǀ ca ǀ bhū́yasaḥ ǀ út ǀ sahásrāt ǀ ririce ǀ kṛṣṭíṣu ǀ śrávaḥ ǀamātrám ǀ tvā ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ titviṣe ǀ mahī́ ǀ ádha ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jighnase ǀ puram-dara ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy glory, Maghavan, exceeds a hundred yea, more than a hundred, than a thousand mid the folk, The great bowl hath inspirited thee boundlessly: so mayst thou slay the Vṛtras, breaker-down of forts!
verses.wilson_translation: The food,Maghavan, (which is to be given by you) to men, may be more than sufficient for a hundred, oor for more, even, than a thousand; great praise has glorified you, who are without limit, whereupon you destroy your enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy glory, Maghavan, exceeds a hundred yea, more than a hundred, than a thousand mid the folk, The great bowl hath inspirited thee boundlessly: so mayst thou slay the Vṛtras, breaker-down of forts!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिविष्टिधातु प्रतिमानमोजसस्तिस्रो भूमीर्नृपते त्रीणि रोचना ।अतीदं विश्वं भुवनं ववक्षिथाशत्रुरिंद्र जनुषा सनादसि ॥
verses.transliteration: triviṣṭi-dhā́tu ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ ójasaḥ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ bhū́mīḥ ǀ nṛ-pate ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ rocanā́ ǀáti ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ vavakṣitha ǀ aśatrúḥ ǀ indra ǀ janúṣā ǀ sanā́t ǀ asi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of thy great might there is a three counterpart, the three earths, Lord men and the three realms of light. Above this whole world, Indra, thou hast waxen great: without a foe art thou, nature, from of old.
verses.wilson_translation: Strong as a twice-twisted rope, you are the type of strength; protector of men, that are more than able to sustain the three spheres, the three luminaries, and all this world of beings,Indra, who have from birth ever been without a rival.
verses.griffith_verse: Of thy great might there is a three counterpart, the three earths, Lord men and the three realms of light. Above this whole world, Indra, thou hast waxen great: without a foe art thou, nature, from of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां देवेषु प्रथमं हवामहे त्वं बभूथ पृतनासु सासहिः ।सेमं नः कारुमुपमन्युमुद्भिदमिंद्रः कृणोतु प्रसवे रथं पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ devéṣu ǀ prathamám ǀ havāmahe ǀ tvám ǀ babhūtha ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ sasahíḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ imám ǀ naḥ ǀ kārúm ǀ upa-manyúm ǀ ut-bhídam ǀ índraḥ ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ pra-savé ǀ rátham ǀ puráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invocate thee first among the Deities: thou hast become a mighty Conquer in fight. May Indra fill with spirit this our singer's heart, and make our car impetuous, foremost in attack.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you,Indra, the first among the gods; you have been the victor in battles; may Indra put foremost in the battle this our chariot, which is efficient, impetuous, and the uprooter (of all impediments).
verses.griffith_verse: We invocate thee first among the Deities: thou hast become a mighty Conquer in fight. May Indra fill with spirit this our singer's heart, and make our car impetuous, foremost in attack.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं जिगेथ न धना रुरोधिथार्भेष्वाजा मघवन्महत्सु च ।त्वामुग्रमवसे सं शिशीमस्यथा न इंद्र हवनेषु चोदय ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ jigetha ǀ ná ǀ dhánā ǀ rurodhitha ǀ árbheṣu ǀ ājā́ ǀ magha-van ǀ mahát-su ǀ ca ǀtvā́m ǀ ugrám ǀ ávase ǀ sám ǀ śiśīmasi ǀ átha ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ hávaneṣu ǀ codaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast prevailed, and hast not kept the booty back, in trifling battles in those of great account. We make thee keen, the Mighty One, succour us: inspire us, Maghavan, when we defy the foe.
verses.wilson_translation: You conquer, and withhold not the booty; in trifling or in serious conflicts, we sharpen you, fierce Maghavan, for our defence; do you, therefore, inspirit us in our defiances.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast prevailed, and hast not kept the booty back, in trifling battles in those of great account. We make thee keen, the Mighty One, succour us: inspire us, Maghavan, when we defy the foe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वाहेंद्रो अधिवक्ता नो अस्त्वपरिह्वृताः सनुयाम वाजं ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvā́hā ǀ índraḥ ǀ adhi-vaktā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ ápari-hvṛtāḥ ǀ sanuyāma ǀ vā́jam ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra evermore be our Protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indradaily be our vindicator, and may we, with undiverted course, enjoy abundant food; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: May Indra evermore be our Protector, and unimperilled may we win the booty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THAT highest Indra-power of thine is distant: that which is here sages possessed aforetime.This one is on the earth, in heaven the other, and both unite as flag with flag in battle. He spread the wide earth out and firmly fixed it, smote with his thunderbolt and loosed the waters.Maghavan with his puissance struck down Ahi, rent Rauhiṇa to death and slaughtered Vyaṁsa. Armed with his bolt and trusting in his prowess he wandered shattering the forts of Dāsas.Cast thy dart, knowing, Thunderer, at the Dasyu; increase the Ārya's might and glory, Indra. For him who thus hath taught these human races, Maghavan, bearing a fame-worthy title,Thunderer, drawing nigh to slay the Dasyus, hath given himself the name of Son for glory. See this abundant wealth that he possesses, and put your trust in Indra's hero vigour.He found the cattle, and he found the horses, he found the plants, the forests and the waters. To him the truly strong, whose deeds are many, to him the strong Bull let us pour the Soma.The Hero, watching like a thief in ambush, goes parting the possessions of the godless. Well didst thou do that hero deed, O Indra, in waking with thy bolt the slumbering Ahi.in thee, delighted, Dames divine rejoiced them, the flying Maruts and all Gods were joyful. As thou hast smitten Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Vṛtra and Kuyava, and Śambara's forts,O Indra.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: तत्त इंद्रियं परमं पराचैरधारयंत कवयः पुरेदं ।क्षमेदमन्यद्दिव्यन्यदस्य समी पृच्यते समनेव केतुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ te ǀ indriyám ǀ paramám ǀ parācáiḥ ǀ ádhārayanta ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ idám ǀkṣamā́ ǀ idám ǀ anyát ǀ diví ǀ anyát ǀ asya ǀ sám ǀ īmíti ǀ pṛcyate ǀ samanā́-iva ǀ ketúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THAT highest Indra-power of thine is distant: that which is here sages possessed aforetime. This one is on the earth, in heaven the other, and both unite as flag with flag in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: The sages have formerly been possessed of this your supreme power,Indra, as if it were present with them, one light of whom shines upon the earth, the other in heaven, and both are in combination with each other, as banner (mingles with banner) in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: THAT highest Indra-power of thine is distant: that which is here sages possessed aforetime. This one is on the earth, in heaven the other, and both unite as flag with flag in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स धारयत्पृथिवीं पप्रथच्च वज्रेण हत्वा निरपः ससर्ज ।अहन्नहिमभिनद्रौहिणं व्यहन्व्यंसं मघवा शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ dhārayat ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ papráthat ǀ ca ǀ vájreṇa ǀ hatvā́ ǀ níḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sasarja ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ ábhinat ǀ rauhiṇám ǀ ví ǀ áhan ǀ ví-aṃsam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He spread the wide earth out and firmly fixed it, smote with his thunderbolt and loosed the waters. Maghavan with his puissance struck down Ahi, rent Rauhiṇa to death and slaughtered Vyaṁsa.
verses.wilson_translation: He upholds, and has spread out, the earth; having struck (the clouds), he has extricated the waters; he has slain Ahi, he has pierced Rauhiṇa, he has destroyed, by his prowess, the mutilated (Vṛtra).
verses.griffith_verse: He spread the wide earth out and firmly fixed it, smote with his thunderbolt and loosed the waters. Maghavan with his puissance struck down Ahi, rent Rauhiṇa to death and slaughtered Vyaṁsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स जातूभर्मा श्रद्दधान ओजः पुरो विभिंदन्नचरद्वि दासीः ।विद्वान्वज्रिंदस्यवे हेतिमस्यार्यं सहो वर्धया द्युम्नमिंद्र ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ jātū́-bharmā ǀ śrat-dádhānaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ vi-bhindán ǀ acarat ǀ ví ǀ dā́sīḥ ǀvidvā́n ǀ vajrin ǀ dásyave ǀ hetím ǀ asya ǀ ā́ryam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ vardhaya ǀ dyumnám ǀ indra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Armed with his bolt and trusting in his prowess he wandered shattering the forts of Dāsas. Cast thy dart, knowing, Thunderer, at the Dasyu; increase the Ārya's might and glory, Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Armed with the thunderbolt, and confident in his strength, he has gone on destroying the cities of the Dasyus. Thunderer, acknowledging (the praises of your worshipper) cast, for his sake, your shaft agains the Dasyu, and augment the strength and glory of theĀrya.
verses.griffith_verse: Armed with his bolt and trusting in his prowess he wandered shattering the forts of Dāsas. Cast thy dart, knowing, Thunderer, at the Dasyu; increase the Ārya's might and glory, Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदूचुषे मानुषेमा युगानि कीर्तेन्यं मघवा नाम बिभ्रत् ।उपप्रयंदस्युहत्याय वज्री यद्ध सूनुः श्रवसे नाम दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ūcúṣe ǀ mā́nuṣā ǀ imā́ ǀ yugā́ni ǀ kīrtényam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ nā́ma ǀ bíbhrat ǀupa-prayán ǀ dasyu-hátyāya ǀ vajrī́ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ śrávase ǀ nā́ma ǀ dadhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: For him who thus hath taught these human races, Maghavan, bearing a fame-worthy title, Thunderer, drawing nigh to slay the Dasyus, hath given himself the name of Son for glory.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavan, possessing a name that is to be glorified, offers to him who celebrates it, these (revolving) ages of man; the thunderer, the scatterer (of his foes), sallying forth to destroy the Dasyus, has obtained a name (renowned for victorious) prowess.
verses.griffith_verse: For him who thus hath taught these human races, Maghavan, bearing a fame-worthy title, Thunderer, drawing nigh to slay the Dasyus, hath given himself the name of Son for glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदस्येदं पश्यता भूरि पुष्टं श्रदिंद्रस्य धत्तन वीर्याय ।स गा अविंदत्सो अविंददश्वान्त्स ओषधीः सो अपः स वनानि ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ asya ǀ idám ǀ paśyata ǀ bhū́ri ǀ puṣṭám ǀ śrát ǀ índrasya ǀ dhattana ǀ vīryā́ya ǀsáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ avindat ǀ sáḥ ǀ avindat ǀ áśvān ǀ sáḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ vánāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: See this abundant wealth that he possesses, and put your trust in Indra's hero vigour. He found the cattle, and he found the horses, he found the plants, the forests and the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Behold this, the vast and extensive (might of Indra); have confidence in his prowess; he has recovered the cattle, he has recovered the horses, the plural nts, the waters, the woods.
verses.griffith_verse: See this abundant wealth that he possesses, and put your trust in Indra's hero vigour. He found the cattle, and he found the horses, he found the plants, the forests and the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरिकर्मणे वृषभाय वृष्णे सत्यशुष्माय सुनवाम सोमं ।य आदृत्या परिपंथीव शूरोऽयज्वनो विभजन्नेति वेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri-karmaṇe ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ satyá-śuṣmāya ǀ sunavāma ǀ sómam ǀyáḥ ǀ ā-dṛ́tya ǀ paripanthī́-iva ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ áyajvanaḥ ǀ vi-bhájan ǀ éti ǀ védaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the truly strong, whose deeds are many, to him the strong Bull let us pour the Soma. The Hero, watching like a thief in ambush, goes parting the possessions of the godless.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer the Somalibation to him who is the performer of many exploits, the best (of the gods), the showerer (of benefits), the possessor of true strength, the hero who, holding respect for wealth, takes it from him who performs no sacrifice, like a foot-pad (from a traveller), and proceeds (to give it) to the sacrificer.
verses.griffith_verse: To him the truly strong, whose deeds are many, to him the strong Bull let us pour the Soma. The Hero, watching like a thief in ambush, goes parting the possessions of the godless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिंद्र प्रेव वीर्यं चकर्थ यत्ससंतं वज्रेणाबोधयोऽहिं ।अनु त्वा पत्नीर्हृषितं वयश्च विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननु त्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ indra ǀ prá-iva ǀ vīryám ǀ cakartha ǀ yát ǀ sasántam ǀ vájreṇa ǀ ábodhayaḥ ǀ áhim ǀánu ǀ tvā ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ hṛṣitám ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ amadan ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well didst thou do that hero deed, O Indra, in waking with thy bolt the slumbering Ahi. in thee, delighted, Dames divine rejoiced them, the flying Maruts and all Gods were joyful.
verses.wilson_translation: You did perform,Indra, a glorious deed, when you did awaken the sleeping Ahi with your thunderbolt; then the wives (of the gods), the Maruts, and all the gods, imitated your exultation.
verses.griffith_verse: Well didst thou do that hero deed, O Indra, in waking with thy bolt the slumbering Ahi. in thee, delighted, Dames divine rejoiced them, the flying Maruts and all Gods were joyful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुष्णं पिप्रुं कुयवं वृत्रमिंद्र यदावधीर्वि पुरः शंबरस्य ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: śúṣṇam ǀ píprum ǀ kúyavam ǀ vṛtrám ǀ indra ǀ yadā́ ǀ ávadhīḥ ǀ ví ǀ púraḥ ǀ śámbarasya ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou hast smitten Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Vṛtra and Kuyava, and Śambara's forts, O Indra. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch,Indra, as you have slainŚuṣṇa, Pipru,Kuyavaand Vṛtra, and destroyed the cities ofŚambara, therefore may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, grant us that (which we desire).
verses.griffith_verse: As thou hast smitten Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Vṛtra and Kuyava, and Śambara's forts, O Indra. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE altar hath been made for thee to rest on: come like a panting courser and be seated.Loosen thy flying Steeds, set free thy Horses who bear thee swiftly nigh at eve and morning. These men have come to Indra for assistance: shall he not quickly come upon these pathways?May the Gods quell the fury of the Dāsa, and may they lead our folk to happy fortune. He who hath only wish as his possession casts on himself, casts foam amid the waters.Both wives of Kuyava in milk have bathed them: may they be drowned within the depth of Śiphā. This hath his kinship checked who lives beside us: with ancient streams forth speeds and rules the Hero,Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Virapatnī, delighting him, bear milk upon their waters. Soon as this Dasyu's traces were discovered, as she who knows her home, he sought the dwelling.Now think thou of us, Maghavan, nor cast us away as doth a profligate his treasure. Indra, as such, give us a share of sunlight, of waters, sinlessness, and reputation.Do thou no harm to our yet unborn offspring: our trust is in thy mighty Indra-power. Now we, I think, in thee as such have trusted: lead us on, Mighty One, to ample riches.In no unready house give us, O Indra invoked of many, food and drink when hungry. Slay us not, Indra; do not thou forsake us: steal not away the joys which we delight in.Rend not our unborn brood, strong Lord of Bounty! our vessels with the life that is within them. Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover: here is the pressed juice. Drink thereof for rapture.Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and, invocated, hear us like a Father.

verses.sanskrit: योनिष्ट इंद्र निषदे अकारि तमा नि षीद स्वानो नार्वा ।विमुच्या वयोऽवसायाश्वांदोषा वस्तोर्वहीयसः प्रपित्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: yóniḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ ni-sáde ǀ akāri ǀ tám ǀ ā́ ǀ ní ǀ sīda ǀ svānáḥ ǀ ná ǀ árvā ǀvi-múcya ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ava-sā́ya ǀ áśvān ǀ doṣā́ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ váhīyasaḥ ǀ pra-pitvé ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE altar hath been made for thee to rest on: come like a panting courser and be seated. Loosen thy flying Steeds, set free thy Horses who bear thee swiftly nigh at eve and morning.
verses.wilson_translation: The altar has been raised,Indra, for your seat; hasten to sit upon it as a neighing horse (hastens to his stable); slackening the reins, and letting your coursers free, who, at the season of sacrifice, bear you night and day.
verses.griffith_verse: THE altar hath been made for thee to rest on: come like a panting courser and be seated. Loosen thy flying Steeds, set free thy Horses who bear thee swiftly nigh at eve and morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओ त्ये नर इंद्रमूतये गुर्नू चित्तान्त्सद्यो अध्वनो जगम्यात् ।देवासो मन्युं दासस्य श्चम्नंते न आ वक्षन्त्सुविताय वर्णं ॥
verses.transliteration: ó íti ǀ tyé ǀ náraḥ ǀ índram ǀ ūtáye ǀ guḥ ǀ nú ǀ cit ǀ tā́n ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ jagamyāt ǀdevā́saḥ ǀ manyúm ǀ dā́sasya ǀ ścamnan ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣan ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ várṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: These men have come to Indra for assistance: shall he not quickly come upon these pathways? May the Gods quell the fury of the Dāsa, and may they lead our folk to happy fortune.
verses.wilson_translation: These person ns have come to Indra(to solicit) his protection; may he quickly direct them on the way; may the gods repress the wrathof the destroyer, and bring to our solemnity the obviator of evil.
verses.griffith_verse: These men have come to Indra for assistance: shall he not quickly come upon these pathways? May the Gods quell the fury of the Dāsa, and may they lead our folk to happy fortune.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव त्मना भरते केतवेदा अव त्मना भरते फेनमुदन् ।क्षीरेण स्नातः कुयवस्य योषे हते ते स्यातां प्रवणे शिफायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ tmánā ǀ bharate ǀ kéta-vedāḥ ǀ áva ǀ tmánā ǀ bharate ǀ phénam ǀ udán ǀkṣīréṇa ǀ snātaḥ ǀ kúyavasya ǀ yóṣe íti ǀ haté íti ǀ té íti ǀ syātām ǀ pravaṇé ǀ śíphāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who hath only wish as his possession casts on himself, casts foam amid the waters. Both wives of Kuyava in milk have bathed them: may they be drowned within the depth of Śiphā.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Asura), knowing the wealth of others, carries it off of himself; present in the water, he carries off, of himself, the foam; the two wives of Kuyavabathe with the water; may they be drowned in the depths of theŚiphāriver.
verses.griffith_verse: He who hath only wish as his possession casts on himself, casts foam amid the waters. Both wives of Kuyava in milk have bathed them: may they be drowned within the depth of Śiphā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युयोप नाभिरुपरस्यायोः प्र पूर्वाभिस्तिरते राष्टि शूरः ।अंजसी कुलिशी वीरपत्नी पयो हिन्वाना उदभिर्भरंते ॥
verses.transliteration: yuyópa ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ úparasya ǀ āyóḥ ǀ prá ǀ pū́rvābhiḥ ǀ tirate ǀ rā́ṣṭi ǀ śū́raḥ ǀañjasī́ ǀ kuliśī́ ǀ vīrá-patnī ǀ páyaḥ ǀ hinvānā́ḥ ǀ udá-bhiḥ ǀ bharante ǁ
verses.english_translation: This hath his kinship checked who lives beside us: with ancient streams forth speeds and rules the Hero, Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Virapatnī, delighting him, bear milk upon their waters.
verses.wilson_translation: The abiding-plural ce of the vagrant (Kuyava) was concealed (in the midst) of the water; the hero increases with the waters formerly (carried off), and is renowned (throughout the world); the Añjasī, kuliśī and Vīrapatni rivers, plural asing him with their substance, sustain him with their waters.
verses.griffith_verse: This hath his kinship checked who lives beside us: with ancient streams forth speeds and rules the Hero, Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Virapatnī, delighting him, bear milk upon their waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति यत्स्या नीथादर्शि दस्योरोको नाच्छा सदनं जानती गात् ।अध स्मा नो मघवंचर्कृतादिन्मा नो मघेव निष्षपी परा दाः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti �� yát ǀ syā́ ǀ nī́thā ǀ ádarśi ǀ dásyoḥ ǀ ókaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áccha ǀ sádanam ǀ jānatī́ ǀ gāt ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ carkṛtā́t ǀ ít ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ maghā́-iva ǀ niṣṣapī́ ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soon as this Dasyu's traces were discovered, as she who knows her home, he sought the dwelling. Now think thou of us, Maghavan, nor cast us away as doth a profligate his treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Since the track that leads to the dwelling of the Dasyuhas been seen by us, as a cow knows the way to her stall, therefore do you,Maghavan, (defend us) from his repeated violence; do not you cast away as a libertine throws away wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Soon as this Dasyu's traces were discovered, as she who knows her home, he sought the dwelling. Now think thou of us, Maghavan, nor cast us away as doth a profligate his treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं न इंद्र सूर्ये सो अप्स्वनागास्त्व आ भज जीवशंसे ।मांतरां भुजमा रीरिषो नः श्रद्धितं ते महत इंद्रियाय ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ sū́rye ǀ sáḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ anāgāḥ-tvé ǀ ā́ ǀ bhaja ǀ jīva-śaṃsé ǀmā́ ǀ ántarām ǀ bhújam ǀ ā́ ǀ ririṣaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ śráddhitam ǀ te ǀ mahaté ǀ indriyā́ya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, as such, give us a share of sunlight, of waters, sinlessness, and reputation. Do thou no harm to our yet unborn offspring: our trust is in thy mighty Indra-power.
verses.wilson_translation: Excite in us,Indra, veneration for the sun, for the waters, and for those who are worthy of the praise of living beings, as exempt from sin; injure not our offspring while yet in the womb, for our trust is in yourmighty power.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, as such, give us a share of sunlight, of waters, sinlessness, and reputation. Do thou no harm to our yet unborn offspring: our trust is in thy mighty Indra-power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा मन्ये श्रत्ते अस्मा अधायि वृषा चोदस्व महते धनाय ।मा नो अकृते पुरुहूत योनाविंद्र क्षुध्यद्भ्यो वय आसुतिं दाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ manye ǀ śrát ǀ te ǀ asmai ǀ adhāyi ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ codasva ǀ mahaté ǀ dhánāya ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ákṛte ǀ puru-hūta ǀ yónau ǀ índra ǀ kṣúdhyat-bhyaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ā-sutím ǀ dāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now we, I think, in thee as such have trusted: lead us on, Mighty One, to ample riches. In no unready house give us, O Indra invoked of many, food and drink when hungry.
verses.wilson_translation: Hence,Indra, I meditate on you; on his (your power) has our trust been plural ced; showerer (of benefits), direct us to great wealth; consign us not, you who are invoked by many, to a destitute dwelling; give, Indra, food and drink to the hungry.
verses.griffith_verse: Now we, I think, in thee as such have trusted: lead us on, Mighty One, to ample riches. In no unready house give us, O Indra invoked of many, food and drink when hungry.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो वधीरिंद्र मा परा दा मा नः प्रिया भोजनानि प्र मोषीः ।आंडा मा नो मघवंछक्र निर्भेन्मा नः पात्रा भेत्सहजानुषाणि ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ indra ǀ mā́ ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ priyā́ ǀ bhójanāni ǀ prá ǀ moṣīḥ ǀāṇḍā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ śakra ǀ níḥ ǀ bhet ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pā́trā ǀ bhet ǀ sahá-jānuṣāṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slay us not, Indra; do not thou forsake us: steal not away the joys which we delight in. Rend not our unborn brood, strong Lord of Bounty! our vessels with the life that is within them.
verses.wilson_translation: Harm us not,Indra, abandon us not; deprive us not of the enjoyments that aare dear to us; injure not, affluentŚakra, our unborn offspring; harm not those who are capable (only of crawling) on their knees.
verses.griffith_verse: Slay us not, Indra; do not thou forsake us: steal not away the joys which we delight in. Rend not our unborn brood, strong Lord of Bounty! our vessels with the life that is within them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वाङेहि सोमकामं त्वाहुरयं सुतस्तस्य पिबा मदाय ।उरुव्यचा जठर आ वृषस्व पितेव नः शृणुहि हूयमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ṅ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ sóma-kāmam ǀ tvā ǀ āhuḥ ǀ ayám ǀ sutáḥ ǀ tásya ǀ piba ǀ mádāya ǀuru-vyácāḥ ǀ jaṭháre ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǀ pitā́-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ śṛṇuhi ǀ hūyámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover: here is the pressed juice. Drink thereof for rapture. Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and, invocated, hear us like a Father.
verses.wilson_translation: Come into our presence; they have called you, fond of the Soma; it is prepared; drink of it for your exhilaration; vast of limb, distend your stomach, and when invoked hear us, as a father (listens to the words of his sons).
verses.griffith_verse: Come to us; they have called thee Soma-lover: here is the pressed juice. Drink thereof for rapture. Widely-capacious, pour it down within thee, and, invocated, hear us like a Father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १९ त्रित आप्त्यः, कुत्स आङ्गिरसो वा। विश्वे देवाः। पंक्तिः, ८ यव मध्य महाबृहती, १९ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITHIN the waters runs the Moon, he with the beauteous wings in heaven.Ye lightnings with your golden wheels, men find not your abiding-place. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Surely men crave and gain their wish. Close to her husband clings the wife.And, in embraces intertwined, both give and take the bliss of love. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. O never may that light, ye Gods, fall from its station in the sky.Ne’er fail us one like Soma sweet, the spring of our felicity. Mark this my woe,ye Earth and Heaven. I ask the last of sacrifice. As envoy he shall tell it forth.Where is the ancient law divine? Who is its new diffuser now? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Ye Gods who yonder have your home in the three lucid realms of heaven,What count ye truth and what untruth? Where is mine ancient call on you? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. What is your firm support of Law? What Varuṇa's observant eye?How may we pass the wicked on the path of mighty Aryaman? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. I am the man who sang of old full many a laud when Soma flowed.Yet torturing cares consume me as the wolf assails the thirsty deer. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Like rival wives on every side enclosing ribs oppress me sore.O Śatakratu, biting cares devour me, singer of thy praise, as rats devour the weaver's threads. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Where those seven rays are shining, thence my home and family extend.This Tṛta Āptya knoweth well, and speaketh out for brotherhood. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. May those five Bulls which stand on high full in the midst of mighty heaven,Having together swiftly borne my praises to the Gods, return. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. High in the mid ascent of heaven those Birds of beauteous pinion sit.Back from his path they drive the wolf as he would cross the restless floods. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Firm is this new-wrought hymn of praise, and meet to be told forth, O Gods.The flowing of the floods is Law, Truth is the Sun's extended light. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Worthy of laud, O Agni, is that kinship which thou hast with Gods.Here seat thee like a man: most wise, bring thou the Gods for sacrifice. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Here seated, man-like as a priest shall wisest Agni to the GodsSpeed onward our oblations, God among the Gods, intelligent. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Varuṇa makes the holy prayer. To him who finds the path we pray.He in the heart reveals his thought. Let sacred worship rise anew. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified,Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Tṛta, when buried in the well, calls on the Gods to succour him.That call of his Bṛhaspati heard and released him from distress. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. A ruddy wolf beheld me once, as I was faring on my path.He, like a carpenter whose back is aching crouched and slunk away. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven. Through this our song may we, allied with Indra, with all our heroes conquer in the battle.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: चंद्रमा अप्स्वंतरा सुपर्णो धावते दिवि ।न वो हिरण्यनेमयः पदं विंदंति विद्युतो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: candrámāḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ dhāvate ǀ diví ǀná ǀ vaḥ ǀ hiraṇya-nemayaḥ ǀ padám ǀ vindanti ǀ vi-dyutaḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITHIN the waters runs the Moon, he with the beauteous wings in heaven. Ye lightnings with your golden wheels, men find not your abiding-place. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The graceful-movingmoonspeeds along the middle region in the sky; bright golden rays (my eyes) behold not your abidding-plural ce. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: WITHIN the waters runs the Moon, he with the beauteous wings in heaven. Ye lightnings with your golden wheels, men find not your abiding-place. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्थमिद्वा उ अर्थिन आ जाया युवते पतिं ।तुंजाते वृष्ण्यं पयः परिदाय रसं दुहे वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: ártham ǀ ít ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ arthínaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ yuvate ǀ pátim ǀtuñjā́te íti ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǀ páyaḥ ǀ pari-dā́ya ǀ rásam ǀ duhe ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Surely men crave and gain their wish. Close to her husband clings the wife. And, in embraces intertwined, both give and take the bliss of love. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who seek for wealth, obtain it; a wife enjoys (the presence of) her husband, and from their union progeny is engendered. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Surely men crave and gain their wish. Close to her husband clings the wife. And, in embraces intertwined, both give and take the bliss of love. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मो षु देवा अदः स्वरव पादि दिवस्परि ।मा सोम्यस्य शंभुवः शूने भूम कदा चन वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ devāḥ ǀ adáḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ áva ǀ pādi ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀmā́ ǀ somyásya ǀ śam-bhúvaḥ ǀ śū́ne ǀ bhūma ǀ kádā ǀ caná ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: O never may that light, ye Gods, fall from its station in the sky. Ne’er fail us one like Soma sweet, the spring of our felicity. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Never, Gods, may this (my ancestry), abiding above in heaven, be excluded (from it); never may we be in want (of a son), the cause of joy (to his progenitors), entitled to libations of the Soma. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: O never may that light, ye Gods, fall from its station in the sky. Ne’er fail us one like Soma sweet, the spring of our felicity. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञं पृच्छाम्यवमं स तद्दूतो वि वोचति ।क्व ऋतं पूर्व्यं गतं कस्तद्बिभर्ति नूतनो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñám ǀ pṛcchāmi ǀ avamám ǀ sáḥ ǀ tát ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ví ǀ vocati ǀkvá ǀ ṛtám ǀ pūrvyám ǀ gatám ǀ káḥ ǀ tát ǀ bibharti ǀ nū́tanaḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I ask the last of sacrifice. As envoy he shall tell it forth. Where is the ancient law divine? Who is its new diffuser now? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: I implore the first (of the gods), the object of sacrifice, that he will become my messenger, and narrate (my condition to the other deities). Where,Agni, is your former benevolence, what new being now possesses it? Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: I ask the last of sacrifice. As envoy he shall tell it forth. Where is the ancient law divine? Who is its new diffuser now? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमी ये देवाः स्थन त्रिष्वा रोचने दिवः ।कद्व ऋतं कदनृतं क्व प्रत्ना व आहुतिर्वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: amī́ íti ǀ yé ǀ devāḥ ǀ sthána ǀ triṣú ǀ ā́ ǀ rocané ǀ diváḥ ǀkát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ kát ǀ ánṛtam ǀ kvá ǀ pratnā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́-hutiḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Gods who yonder have your home in the three lucid realms of heaven, What count ye truth and what untruth? Where is mine ancient call on you? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Gods, who are present in thethree worlds, who abide in the light of the sun, where now is your truth, where your untruth, where the ancient invocation (that I have addressed) to you? Heaven and earth, be conscious of (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Gods who yonder have your home in the three lucid realms of heaven, What count ye truth and what untruth? Where is mine ancient call on you? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कद्व ऋतस्य धर्णसि कद्वरुणस्य चक्षणं ।कदर्यम्णो महस्पथाति क्रामेम दूढ्यो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dharṇasí ǀ kát ǀ váruṇasya ǀ cákṣaṇam ǀkát ǀ aryamṇáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ pathā́ ǀ áti ǀ krāmema ǀ duḥ-dhyáḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: What is your firm support of Law? What Varuṇa's observant eye? How may we pass the wicked on the path of mighty Aryaman? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Where, deities, is your observance of the truth, where the (benignant) regard of Varuṇa, where is the path of the mighty Aryaman, (so that) we may overcome the malevolent? Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: What is your firm support of Law? What Varuṇa's observant eye? How may we pass the wicked on the path of mighty Aryaman? Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं सो अस्मि यः पुरा सुते वदामि कानि चित् ।तं मा व्यंत्याध्यो वृको न तृष्णजं मृगं वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmi ǀ yáḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ suté ǀ vádāmi ǀ kā́ni ǀ cit ǀtám ǀ mā ǀ vyanti ǀ ā-dhyáḥ ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǀ ná ǀ tṛṣṇá-jam ǀ mṛgám ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am the man who sang of old full many a laud when Soma flowed. Yet torturing cares consume me as the wolf assails the thirsty deer. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: I am he, Gods, who formerly recited (your praise) when the libation was poured out; yet sorrows assail me, like a wolf (that falls upon) a thirsty deer. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: I am the man who sang of old full many a laud when Soma flowed. Yet torturing cares consume me as the wolf assails the thirsty deer. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं मा तपंत्यभितः सपत्नीरिव पर्शवः ।मूषो न शिश्ना व्यदंति माध्यः स्तोतारं ते शतक्रतो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ mā ǀ tapanti ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ sapátnīḥ-iva ǀ párśavaḥ ǀmū́ṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śiśnā́ ǀ ví ǀ adanti ǀ mā ǀ ā-dhyáḥ ǀ stotā́ram ǀ te ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like rival wives on every side enclosing ribs oppress me sore. O Śatakratu, biting cares devour me, singer of thy praise, as rats devour the weaver's threads. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The ribs (of the well close) round me, like the rival wives (of one husband); cares consume me,Śatakratu, although your worshipper, as a rat (gnaws a weaver's) threads. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Like rival wives on every side enclosing ribs oppress me sore. O Śatakratu, biting cares devour me, singer of thy praise, as rats devour the weaver's threads. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमी ये सप्त रश्मयस्तत्रा मे नाभिरातता ।त्रितस्तद्वेदाप्त्यः स जामित्वाय रेभति वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: amī́ íti ǀ yé ǀ saptá ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ tátra ǀ me ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ ā́-tatā ǀtritáḥ ǀ tát ǀ veda ǀ āptyáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ jāmi-tvā́ya ǀ rebhati ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where those seven rays are shining, thence my home and family extend. This Tṛta Āptya knoweth well, and speaketh out for brotherhood. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Those which are the seven rays (of the sun), in them is my navel expanded;Trita, the son of the waters, knows that (it is so), and he praises them for his extrication (from the well). Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Where those seven rays are shining, thence my home and family extend. This Tṛta Āptya knoweth well, and speaketh out for brotherhood. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमी ये पंचोक्षणो मध्ये तस्थुर्महो दिवः ।देवत्रा नु प्रवाच्यं सध्रीचीना नि वावृतुर्वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: amī́ íti ǀ yé ǀ páñca ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀdeva-trā́ ǀ nú ǀ pra-vā́cyam ǀ sadhrīcīnā́ḥ ǀ ní ǀ vavṛtuḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those five Bulls which stand on high full in the midst of mighty heaven, Having together swiftly borne my praises to the Gods, return. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May the five shedders (of benefits), who abide in the centre of the expanded heavens, having together conveyed my prayers quickly to the gods, (speedily) return. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: May those five Bulls which stand on high full in the midst of mighty heaven, Having together swiftly borne my praises to the Gods, return. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुपर्णा एत आसते मध्य आरोधने दिवः ।ते सेधंति पथो वृकं तरंतं यह्वतीरपो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ eté ǀ āsate ǀ mádhye ǀ ā-ródhane ǀ diváḥ ǀté ǀ sedhanti ǀ patháḥ ǀ vṛ́kam ǀ tárantam ǀ yahvátīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: High in the mid ascent of heaven those Birds of beauteous pinion sit. Back from his path they drive the wolf as he would cross the restless floods. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The rays of the sun abide in the surrounding centre of heaven; they drive back the wolf crossing the great waters from the path. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: High in the mid ascent of heaven those Birds of beauteous pinion sit. Back from his path they drive the wolf as he would cross the restless floods. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नव्यं तदुक्थ्यं हितं देवासः सुप्रवाचनं ।ऋतमर्षंति सिंधवः सत्यं तातान सूर्यो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: návyam ǀ tát ǀ ukthyám ǀ hitám ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ su-pravācanám ǀṛtám ǀ arṣanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ satyám ǀ tatāna ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Firm is this new-wrought hymn of praise, and meet to be told forth, O Gods. The flowing of the floods is Law, Truth is the Sun's extended light. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: That new praiseworthy and commended (vigour) is seated in you, ye Gods, (by which) the rivers urge on the waters, and the sun diffuses his constant (light). Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Firm is this new-wrought hymn of praise, and meet to be told forth, O Gods. The flowing of the floods is Law, Truth is the Sun's extended light. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने तव त्यदुक्थ्यं देवेष्वस्त्याप्यं ।स नः सत्तो मनुष्वदा देवान्यक्षि विदुष्टरो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ táva ǀ tyát ǀ ukthyám ǀ devéṣu ǀ asti ǀ ā́pyam ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sattáḥ ǀ manuṣvát ǀ ā́ ǀ devā́n ǀ yakṣi ǀ vidúḥ-taraḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worthy of laud, O Agni, is that kinship which thou hast with Gods. Here seat thee like a man: most wise, bring thou the Gods for sacrifice. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Worthy of praise,Agni, is that your relationship 9with the gods), do you, who are most wise, seated at our (solemnity) worship (the gods), as (at the sacrifice of)Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: Worthy of laud, O Agni, is that kinship which thou hast with Gods. Here seat thee like a man: most wise, bring thou the Gods for sacrifice. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सत्तो होता मनुष्वदा देवाँ अच्छा विदुष्टरः ।अग्निर्हव्या सुषूदति देवो देवेषु मेधिरो वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: sattáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ manuṣvát ǀ ā́ ǀ devā́n ǀ áccha ǀ vidúḥ-taraḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ susūdati ǀ deváḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ médhiraḥ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here seated, man-like as a priest shall wisest Agni to the Gods Speed onward our oblations, God among the Gods, intelligent. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May that wise and liberal Agni, a sage amongst the gods, seated at our rite, as at the sacrifice of Manu, be the invoker of the deities, and offer them oblations. Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Here seated, man-like as a priest shall wisest Agni to the Gods Speed onward our oblations, God among the Gods, intelligent. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा कृणोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे ।व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: bráhmā ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ gātu-vídam ǀ tám ǀ īmahe ǀví ǀ ūrṇoti ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ matím ǀ návyaḥ ǀ jāyatām ǀ ṛtám ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa makes the holy prayer. To him who finds the path we pray. He in the heart reveals his thought. Let sacred worship rise anew. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇaperforms the rite of preservation; we desire him as guide of our way; (to him, the repeater of praise) addresses praise with his (whole) heart; may he who is entitled to laudation become our true (support). Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa makes the holy prayer. To him who finds the path we pray. He in the heart reveals his thought. Let sacred worship rise anew. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असौ यः पंथा आदित्यो दिवि प्रवाच्यं कृतः ।न स देवा अतिक्रमे तं मर्तासो न पश्यथ वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: asáu ǀ yáḥ ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ ādityáḥ ǀ diví ǀ pra-vā́cyam ǀ kṛtáḥ ǀná ǀ sáḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ ati-kráme ǀ tám ǀ martāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ paśyatha ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified, Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun, who is avowedly made the path in heaven, is not to be disregarded, Gods, by you; but you, mortals, regard him not. Heaven and earth be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified, Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रितः कूपेऽवहितो देवान्हवत ऊतये ।तच्छुश्राव बृहस्पतिः कृण्वन्नंहूरणादुरु वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: tritáḥ ǀ kū́pe ǀ áva-hitaḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ havate ǀ ūtáye ǀtát ǀ śuśrāva ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ kṛṇván ǀ aṃhūraṇā́t ǀ urú ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tṛta, when buried in the well, calls on the Gods to succour him. That call of his Bṛhaspati heard and released him from distress. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Trita, fallen into the well, invokes the Gods for succour;Bṛhaspati, who liberates many from sin, heard (the submission). Heaven and earth, be conscious of this (my affliction).
verses.griffith_verse: Tṛta, when buried in the well, calls on the Gods to succour him. That call of his Bṛhaspati heard and released him from distress. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अरुणो मा सकृद्वृकः पथा यंतं ददर्श हि ।उज्जिहीते निचाय्या तष्टेव पृष्ट्यामयी वित्तं मे अस्य रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: aruṇáḥ ǀ mā ǀ sakṛ́t ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǀ pathā́ ǀ yántam ǀ dadárśa ǀ hí ǀút ǀ jihīte ǀ ni-cā́yya ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ pṛṣṭi-āmayī́ ǀ vittám ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ rodasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: A ruddy wolf beheld me once, as I was faring on my path. He, like a carpenter whose back is aching crouched and slunk away. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Once, a tawny wolf beheld me faring on my way, and having seen me, rushed upon me, (rearing) as a carpenter, whose back aches (with stooping, standing erect in his work).
verses.griffith_verse: A ruddy wolf beheld me once, as I was faring on my path. He, like a carpenter whose back is aching crouched and slunk away. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एनांगूषेण वयमिंद्रवंतोऽभि ष्याम वृजने सर्ववीराः ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: enā́ ǀ āṅgūṣéṇa ǀ vayám ǀ índra-vantaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ syāma ǀ vṛjáne ǀ sárva-vīrāḥ ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through this our song may we, allied with Indra, with all our heroes conquer in the battle. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: By this recitation, may we, becoming possessed of Indra, and strong with multiplied progeny, overcome our foes in battle; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi---ocean, earth and heaven, be gracious to us in this (request).
verses.griffith_verse: Through this our song may we, allied with Indra, with all our heroes conquer in the battle. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: ७ कुत्स आङ्गिरसः। विश्वे देवाः। जगती, ७ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi.Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. Come ye Ādityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us.Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law.Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. To mighty Narāśaṁsa, strengthening his might, to Pūṣan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns.Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. Bṛhaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir.Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. Sunk in the pit the Ṛṣi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, Lord of power and might.Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress. May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिं हवामहे ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ mitrám ǀ váruṇam ǀ agním ǀ ūtáye ǀ mā́rutam ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ áditim ǀ havāmahe ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke, for our preservation,Indra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Agni, the might of the Maruts, and Aditi; may they, who are bountiful and bestowers of dwellings, extricate us from all sin, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त आदित्या आ गता सर्वतातये भूत देवा वृत्रतूर्येषु शंभुवः ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ādityāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǀ sarvá-tātaye ǀ bhūtá ǀ devāḥ ǀ vṛtra-tū́ryeṣu ǀ śam-bhúvaḥ ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come ye Ādityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: Sons of Aditi, come with all (your hosts) to battle; be to us the cause of happiness in combats, and may they, whoare bountiful and bestowers of dwellings, extricate us from all sin, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: Come ye Ādityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवंतु नः पितरः सुप्रवाचना उत देवी देवपुत्रे ऋतावृधा ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: ávantu ǀ naḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ su-pravācanā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ devī́ íti ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhā ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Pitrṣ, who are easily to be praised protect us; and may the two divinities, heaven and earth, the promoters of sacrifices, and of whom, the gods are progeny, protect us; and may they, who are bountiful and givers of dwellings, extricate us from sin, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नराशंसं वाजिनं वाजयन्निह क्षयद्वीरं पूषणं सुम्नैरीमहे ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: nárāśáṃsam ǀ vājínam ǀ vājáyan ǀ ihá ǀ kṣayát-vīram ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ sumnáiḥ ǀ īmahe ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: To mighty Narāśaṁsa, strengthening his might, to Pūṣan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: Exciting him who is the praised of men and the giver of food, (to be present) at this rite, we solicit (also) with our praises him who is the purifier and destroyer of heroes; may they, who are bountiful and the givers of food, extricate us from sun, as a chariot from a defile
verses.griffith_verse: To mighty Narāśaṁsa, strengthening his might, to Pūṣan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते सदमिन्नः सुगं कृधि शं योर्यत्ते मनुर्हितं तदीमहे ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ naḥ ǀ su-gám ǀ kṛdhi ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ mánuḥ-hitam ǀ tát ǀ īmahe ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir. Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspati, always confer happiness upon us, we solicit that faculty of both (alleviating pain and obvitaing peril) implanted in you by Manu; may they, who are bountiful and the givers of dwellings extricate us from all sins, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: Bṛhaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir. Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं कुत्सो वृत्रहणं शचीपतिं काटे निबाळ्ह ऋषिरह्वदूतये ।रथं न दुर्गाद्वसवः सुदानवो विश्वस्मान्नो अंहसो निष्पिपर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ kútsaḥ ǀ vṛtra-hánam ǀ śacī́-pátim ǀ kāṭé ǀ ní-bāḷhaḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ ahvat ǀ ūtáye ǀrátham ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-gā́t ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ pipartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sunk in the pit the Ṛṣi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, Lord of power and might. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: Kutsa, the ṛṣi, thrown into a well, has invoked to his succour,Indra, the slayer of enemies, the encourager of good works; may they, who are bountiful and the givers of dwellings, extricate us from all sin, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: Sunk in the pit the Ṛṣi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, Lord of power and might. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवैर्नो देव्यदितिर्नि पातु देवस्त्राता त्रायतामप्रयुच्छन् ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: deváiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ní ǀ pātu ǀ deváḥ ǀ trātā́ ǀ trāyatām ǀ ápra-yucchan ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May the goddess,Aditi, with the gods, protect us, and may the radiant guardian, (the sun), be vigilant fo rour protection; and may they, who are bountiful and the givers of dwellings, extricate us from all sin, as a chariot from a defile.
verses.griffith_verse: May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVII. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE sacrifice obtains the Gods’ acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Ādityas.Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble. By praise-songs of Aṅgirases exalted, may the Gods come to us with their protection.May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Ādityas grant us shelter. This laud of ours may Varuṇa and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञो देवानां प्रत्येति सुम्नमादित्यासो भवता मृळयंतः ।आ वोऽर्वाची सुमतिर्ववृत्यादंहोश्चिद्या वरिवोवित्तरासत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ práti ǀ eti ǀ sumnám ǀ ā́dityāsaḥ ǀ bhávata ǀ mṛḷayántaḥ ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ arvā́cī ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ vavṛtyāt ǀ aṃhóḥ ǀ cit ǀ yā́ ǀ varivovít-tarā ǀ ásat ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE sacrifice obtains the Gods’ acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Ādityas. Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble.
verses.wilson_translation: May our sacrifice give satisfaction to the gods;Ādityas, be gracious, and may your good intentions be directed towards us, so as to be abundant source of affliction to the poor.
verses.griffith_verse: THE sacrifice obtains the Gods’ acceptance: be graciously inclined to us, Ādityas. Hitherward let your favour be directed, and be our best deliverer from trouble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप नो देवा अवसा गमंत्वंगिरसां सामभिः स्तूयमानाः ।इंद्र इंद्रियैर्मरुतो मरुद्भिरादित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्म यंसत् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gamantu ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ sā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ stūyámānāḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ indriyáiḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ ādityáiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǁ
verses.english_translation: By praise-songs of Aṅgirases exalted, may the Gods come to us with their protection. May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Ādityas grant us shelter.
verses.wilson_translation: May the gods, who are to be lauded by the hymns of the Aṅgirasas, come hither for our protection; may Indrawith his treasures, the Marutswith the vital airs, and Aditiwith theĀdityas(come and) give us felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: By praise-songs of Aṅgirases exalted, may the Gods come to us with their protection. May Indra with his powers, Maruts with Maruts, Aditi with Ādityas grant us shelter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तन्न इंद्रस्तद्वरुणस्तदग्निस्तदर्यमा तत्सविता चनो धात् ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ tát ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ tát ǀ agníḥ ǀ tát ǀ aryamā́ ǀ tát ǀ savitā́ ǀ cánaḥ ǀ dhāt ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This laud of ours may Varuṇa and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, may Varuṇa, may Agni, may Aryaman, may Savitā, bestow upon us that food (which we solicit); and may Mitra, Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, preserve it (to us).
verses.griffith_verse: This laud of ours may Varuṇa and Indra, Aryaman Agni, Savitar find pleasant. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVIII. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ON that most wondrous car of yours, O Indra and Agni, which looks round on all things living,Take ye your stand and come to us together, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. As vast as all this world is in its compass, deep as it is, with its far-stretching surface,So let this Soma be, Indra and Agni, made for your drinking till your soul be sated. For ye have won a blessed name together: yea, with one aim ye strove, O Vṛtra-slayers.So Indra-Agni, seated here together, pour in, ye Mighty Ones, the mighty Soma. Both stand adorned, when fires are duly kindled, spreading the sacred grass, with lifted ladles.Drawn by strong Soma juice poured forth around us, come, Indra-Agni, and display your favour. The brave deeds ye have done, Indra and Agni, the forms ye have displayed and mighty exploits,The ancient and auspicious bonds of friendship,—for sake of these drink of the flowing Soma. As first I said when choosing you, in battle we must contend with Asuras for this Soma.So came ye unto this my true conviction, and drank libations of the flowing Soma. If in your dwelling, or with prince or Brahman, ye, Indra-Agni, Holy Ones, rejoice you,Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libation of the flowing Soma. If with, the Yadus, Turvaśas, ye sojourn, with Druhyus, Anus, Pūrus, Indra-Agni!Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in lowest earth, in central, or in highest.Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in highest earth, in central, or in lowest,Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. Whether ye be in heaven, O Indra-Agni, on earth, on mountains, in the herbs, or waters,Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. If, when the Sun to the mid-heaven hath mounted, ye take delight in food, O Indra-Agni,Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma. Thus having drunk your fill of our libation, win us all kinds of wealth, Indra and Agni.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: य इंद्राग्नी चित्रतमो रथो वामभि विश्वानि भुवनानि चष्टे ।तेना यातं सरथं तस्थिवांसाथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ���
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ citrá-tamaḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vām ǀ abhí ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ cáṣṭe ǀténa ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ sa-rátham ǀ tasthi-vā́ṃsā ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: ON that most wondrous car of yours, O Indra and Agni, which looks round on all things living, Take ye your stand and come to us together, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, sitting together in your car, that wonderful car which illuminates all beings, approach and drink of the effused Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: ON that most wondrous car of yours, O Indra and Agni, which looks round on all things living, Take ye your stand and come to us together, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यावदिदं भुवनं विश्वमस्त्युरुव्यचा वरिमता गभीरं ।तावाँ अयं पातवे सोमो अस्त्वरमिंद्राग्नी मनसे युवभ्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́vat ǀ idám ǀ bhúvanam ǀ víśvam ǀ ásti ǀ uru-vyácā ǀ varimátā ǀ gabhīrám ǀtā́vān ǀ ayám ǀ pā́tave ǀ sómaḥ ǀ astu ǀ áram ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ mánase ǀ yuvá-bhyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: As vast as all this world is in its compass, deep as it is, with its far-stretching surface, So let this Soma be, Indra and Agni, made for your drinking till your soul be sated.
verses.wilson_translation: Vast as is the whole universe in expanse, and profound indepth, such,Indraand Agni, may this Somabe for you, sufficient for your desires.
verses.griffith_verse: As vast as all this world is in its compass, deep as it is, with its far-stretching surface, So let this Soma be, Indra and Agni, made for your drinking till your soul be sated.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चक्राथे हि सध्र्यङ्नाम भद्रं सध्रीचीना वृत्रहणा उत स्थः ।ताविंद्राग्नी सध्र्यंचा निषद्या वृष्णः सोमस्य वृषणा वृषेथां ॥
verses.transliteration: cakrā́the íti ǀ hí ǀ sadhryák ǀ nā́ma ǀ bhadrám ǀ sadhrīcīnā́ ǀ vṛtra-hanau ǀ utá ǀ sthaḥ ǀtáu ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ sadhryáñcā ǀ ni-sádya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣethām ǁ
verses.english_translation: For ye have won a blessed name together: yea, with one aim ye strove, O Vṛtra-slayers. So Indra-Agni, seated here together, pour in, ye Mighty Ones, the mighty Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: You have made your associated names renowned, since, slayers of Vṛtra, you have been allied (for his death); the showerers of benefits,Indraand Agni, are the two seated together (on the altar); receive (your portion) of the Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: For ye have won a blessed name together: yea, with one aim ye strove, O Vṛtra-slayers. So Indra-Agni, seated here together, pour in, ye Mighty Ones, the mighty Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धेष्वग्निष्वानजाना यतस्रुचा बर्हिरु तिस्तिराणा ।तीव्रैः सोमैः परिषिक्तेभिरर्वागेंद्राग्नी सौमनसाय यातं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddheṣu ǀ agníṣu ǀ ānajānā́ ǀ yatá-srucā ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tistirāṇā́ ǀtīvráiḥ ǀ sómaiḥ ǀ pári-siktebhiḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ ā́ ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ saumanasā́ya ǀ yātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Both stand adorned, when fires are duly kindled, spreading the sacred grass, with lifted ladles. Drawn by strong Soma juice poured forth around us, come, Indra-Agni, and display your favour.
verses.wilson_translation: The first being kindled the two (priests stand by) sprinkling the clarified butter from the ladles, which they raise, and spreading the sacred grass (upon the altar); therefore,Indraand Agni, come before us for our gratification, (attracted) by stimulating Somasprinkled all round.
verses.griffith_verse: Both stand adorned, when fires are duly kindled, spreading the sacred grass, with lifted ladles. Drawn by strong Soma juice poured forth around us, come, Indra-Agni, and display your favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यानींद्राग्नी चक्रथुर्वीर्याणि यानि रूपाण्युत वृष्ण्यानि ।या वां प्रत्नानि सख्या शिवानि तेभिः सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ni ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ cakráthuḥ ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ yā́ni ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ utá ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyāni ǀyā́ ǀ vām ǀ pratnā́ni ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ śivā́ni ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The brave deeds ye have done, Indra and Agni, the forms ye have displayed and mighty exploits, The ancient and auspicious bonds of friendship,—for sake of these drink of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever heroic exploits you ahve achieved whatever forms (you have created), whatever benefits (you have poured down), whatever ancient and fortunate friendships (you have contracted, come with them all), and drink of the effused Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: The brave deeds ye have done, Indra and Agni, the forms ye have displayed and mighty exploits, The ancient and auspicious bonds of friendship,—for sake of these drink of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदब्रवं प्रथमं वां वृणानोऽयं सोमो असुरैर्नो विहव्यः ।तां सत्यां श्रद्धामभ्या हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ábravam ǀ prathamám ǀ vām ǀ vṛṇānáḥ ǀ ayám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ásuraiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vi-hávyaḥ ǀtā́m ǀ satyā́m ǀ śraddhā́m ǀ abhí ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: As first I said when choosing you, in battle we must contend with Asuras for this Soma. So came ye unto this my true conviction, and drank libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Come and witness the sincere faith with which, selecting you two, I first promised (you the libation); drink of the effused libation, for the Somais prepared by the priests.
verses.griffith_verse: As first I said when choosing you, in battle we must contend with Asuras for this Soma. So came ye unto this my true conviction, and drank libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी मदथः स्वे दुरोणे यद्ब्रह्मणि राजनि वा यजत्रा ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ mádathaḥ ǀ své ǀ duroṇé ǀ yát ǀ brahmáṇi ǀ rā́jani ǀ vā ǀ yajatrā ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: If in your dwelling, or with prince or Brahman, ye, Indra-Agni, Holy Ones, rejoice you, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libation of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: If, adorable Indraand Agni, you have ever been delighted (withlibations) in your own dwelling, in tha tof a Brāhmaṇa, or in that of a prince, then, showerers of benefits, come hither from wherever you may be, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: If in your dwelling, or with prince or Brahman, ye, Indra-Agni, Holy Ones, rejoice you, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libation of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी यदुषु तुर्वशेषु यद्द्रुह्युष्वनुषु पूरुषु स्थः ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ yáduṣu ǀ turváśeṣu ǀ yát ǀ druhyúṣu ǀ ánuṣu ǀ pūrúṣu ǀ stháḥ ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: If with, the Yadus, Turvaśas, ye sojourn, with Druhyus, Anus, Pūrus, Indra-Agni! Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: If,Indraand Agni, you are amongst men who are in offensive, malevolent, or tyrannical, or those who live (to fulfil the duties of life), or those who receive the fruits (of good deeds), then, showerers of benefits, come hither from wherever you may be, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: If with, the Yadus, Turvaśas, ye sojourn, with Druhyus, Anus, Pūrus, Indra-Agni! Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी अवमस्यां पृथिव्यां मध्यमस्यां परमस्यामुत स्थः ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ avamásyām ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ madhyamásyām ǀ paramásyām ǀ utá ǀ stháḥ ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in lowest earth, in central, or in highest. Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether,Indraand Agni, you are in the lower, the central, or the upper region of the world, showerers of benefits, come hither from wherever you may be, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in lowest earth, in central, or in highest. Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी परमस्यां पृथिव्यां मध्यमस्यामवमस्यामुत स्थः ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ paramásyām ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ madhyamásyām ǀ avamásyām ǀ utá ǀ stháḥ ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in highest earth, in central, or in lowest, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether,Indraand Agni, you are in the upper, central, or lower region of the world, come,showerers of benefits, hither from wherever you may be, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: Whether, O Indra-Agni, ye be dwelling in highest earth, in central, or in lowest, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी दिवि ष्ठो यत्पृथिव्यां यत्पर्वतेष्वोषधीष्वप्सु ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ diví ǀ stháḥ ǀ yát ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ yát ǀ párvateṣu ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǀ ap-sú ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether ye be in heaven, O Indra-Agni, on earth, on mountains, in the herbs, or waters, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether,Indraand Agni, you are in heaven or upon earth, in the mountains, in the herbs, or in the waters, showerers of benefits, come hither from wherever you may be, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: Whether ye be in heaven, O Indra-Agni, on earth, on mountains, in the herbs, or waters, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी उदिता सूर्यस्य मध्ये दिवः स्वधया मादयेथे ।अतः परि वृषणावा हि यातमथा सोमस्य पिबतं सुतस्य ॥
