verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ út-itā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ mádhye ǀ diváḥ ǀ svadháyā ǀ mādáyethe íti ǀátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ yātám ǀ átha ǀ sómasya ǀ pibatam ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: If, when the Sun to the mid-heaven hath mounted, ye take delight in food, O Indra-Agni, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Although,Indraand Agni, in the midst of the sky, on the rising of the sun, you may be exhilarated by your own splendour, yet, showerers of benefits, come hither from wherever you maybe, and drink of the effused Somalibation.
verses.griffith_verse: If, when the Sun to the mid-heaven hath mounted, ye take delight in food, O Indra-Agni, Even from thence, ye mighty Lords, come hither, and drink libations of the flowing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवेंद्राग्नी पपिवांसा सुतस्य विश्वास्मभ्यं सं जयतं धनानि ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ papi-vā́ṃsā ǀ sutásya ǀ víśvā ǀ asmábhyam ǀ sám ǀ jayatam ǀ dhánāni ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus having drunk your fill of our libation, win us all kinds of wealth, Indra and Agni. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus,Indraand Agni, drinking deep of the libation, grant to us all (kinds of) wealth; and may Mitra,Varuṇaand Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus having drunk your fill of our libation, win us all kinds of wealth, Indra and Agni. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIX. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LONGING for weal I looked around, in spirit, for kinsmen, Indra-Agni, or for brothers.No providence but yours alone is with me so have I wrought for you this hymn for succour. For I have heard that ye give wealth more freely than worthless son-in-law or spouse's brother.So offering to you this draught of Soma, I make you this new hymn, Indra and Agni, Let us not break the cords: with this petition we strive to gain the powers of our forefathers.For Indra-Agni the strong drops are joyful, for here in the bowl's lap are both the press-stones. For you the bowl divine, Indra and Agni, presses the Soma gladly to delight you.With hands auspicious and fair arms, ye Aśvins, haste, sprinkle it with sweetness in the waters. You, I have heard, were mightiest, Indra-Agni, when Vṛtra fell and when the spoil was parted.Sit at this sacrifice, ye ever active, on the strewn grass, and with the juice delight you. Surpassing all men where they shout for battle, ye Twain exceed the earth and heaven in greatness.Greater are ye than rivers and than mountains, O Indra-Agni, and all things beside them. Bring wealth and give it, ye whose arms wield thunder: Indra and Agni, with your powers protect us.Now of a truth these be the very sunbeams wherewith our fathers were of old united. Give, ye who shatter forts, whose hands wield thunder: Indra and Agni, save us in our battles.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: वि ह्यख्यं मनसा वस्य इच्छन्निंद्राग्नी ज्ञास उत वा सजातान् ।नान्या युवत्प्रमतिरस्ति मह्यं स वां धियं वाजयंतीमतक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ hí ǀ ákhyam ǀ mánasā ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ icchán ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ jñāsáḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ sa-jātā́n ǀná ǀ anyā́ ǀ yuvát ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ asti ǀ máhyam ǀ sáḥ ǀ vām ǀ dhíyam ǀ vāja-yántīm ǀ atakṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: LONGING for weal I looked around, in spirit, for kinsmen, Indra-Agni, or for brothers. No providence but yours alone is with me so have I wrought for you this hymn for succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, desirous of wealth, I consider you, in my mind, as kinsmen and relations; the clear understanding you have given me, (is given) by no one else, and (so gifted), I have composed this hymn to you, intimating my wish for sustenance.
verses.griffith_verse: LONGING for weal I looked around, in spirit, for kinsmen, Indra-Agni, or for brothers. No providence but yours alone is with me so have I wrought for you this hymn for succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्रवं हि भूरिदावत्तरा वां विजामातुरुत वा घा स्यालात् ।अथा सोमस्य प्रयती युवभ्यामिंद्राग्नी स्तोमं जनयामि नव्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: áśravam ǀ hí ǀ bhūridā́vat-tarā ǀ vām ǀ ví-jāmātuḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ syālā́t ǀátha ǀ sómasya ǀ prá-yatī ǀ yuvá-bhyām ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ stómam ǀ janayāmi ǀ návyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: For I have heard that ye give wealth more freely than worthless son-in-law or spouse's brother. So offering to you this draught of Soma, I make you this new hymn, Indra and Agni,
verses.wilson_translation: I have heard,Indraand Agni, that you are more munificent givers than an unworthy bridegroom, or the brother of a bride; therefore, as I offer youa Somalibation, I address you, Indra and Agni, with a new hymn.
verses.griffith_verse: For I have heard that ye give wealth more freely than worthless son-in-law or spouse's brother. So offering to you this draught of Soma, I make you this new hymn, Indra and Agni,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा च्छेद्म रश्मीँरिति नाधमानाः पितॄणां शक्तीरनुयच्छमानाः ।इंद्राग्निभ्यां कं वृषणो मदंति ता ह्यद्री धिषणाया उपस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ chedma ǀ raśmī́n ǀ íti ǀ nā́dhamānāḥ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ śaktī́ḥ ǀ anu-yácchamānāḥ ǀindrāgní-bhyām ǀ kám ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ madanti ǀ tā́ ǀ hí ǀ ádrī íti ǀ dhiṣáṇāyāḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us not break the cords: with this petition we strive to gain the powers of our forefathers. For Indra-Agni the strong drops are joyful, for here in the bowl's lap are both the press-stones.
verses.wilson_translation: Never may we cut off the long line (of posterity); thus soliciting and asking for descendants endowed with the vigour of their progenitors, the (worshippers), begetting children, praise Indraand Agnifor their happiness, and they two, destroyers of foes, are nigh (to hear this adoration).
verses.griffith_verse: Let us not break the cords: with this petition we strive to gain the powers of our forefathers. For Indra-Agni the strong drops are joyful, for here in the bowl's lap are both the press-stones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवाभ्यां देवी धिषणा मदायेंद्राग्नी सोममुशती सुनोति ।तावश्विना भद्रहस्ता सुपाणी आ धावतं मधुना पृंक्तमप्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́bhyām ǀ devī́ ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ mádāya ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ sómam ǀ uśatī́ ǀ sunoti ǀtáu ǀ aśvinā ǀ bhadra-hastā ǀ supāṇī íti su-pāṇī ǀ ā́ ǀ dhāvatam ǀ mádhunā ǀ pṛṅktám ǀ ap-sú ǁ
verses.english_translation: For you the bowl divine, Indra and Agni, presses the Soma gladly to delight you. With hands auspicious and fair arms, ye Aśvins, haste, sprinkle it with sweetness in the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: The sacred prayer, desiring your presence, offers to you both,Indraand Agni, for your exhilaration, the Somalibation; do you two, who have horses, handsome arms, and gracefulhands, come quickly and mix (the libation) with sweetness in the waters.
verses.griffith_verse: For you the bowl divine, Indra and Agni, presses the Soma gladly to delight you. With hands auspicious and fair arms, ye Aśvins, haste, sprinkle it with sweetness in the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवामिंद्राग्नी वसुनो विभागे तवस्तमा शुश्रव वृत्रहत्ये ।तावासद्या बर्हिषि यज्ञे अस्मिन्प्र चर्षणी मादयेथां सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ vásunaḥ ǀ vi-bhāgé ǀ taváḥ-tamā ǀ śuśrava ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀtáu ǀ ā-sádya ǀ barhíṣi ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀ prá ǀ carṣaṇī íti ǀ mādayethām ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: You, I have heard, were mightiest, Indra-Agni, when Vṛtra fell and when the spoil was parted. Sit at this sacrifice, ye ever active, on the strewn grass, and with the juice delight you.
verses.wilson_translation: I have heard, (when you were present) at the division of the treasure (among the worshippers), that you two,Indraand Agni, were most vigorous in the destruction of Vṛtra; beholders of all things seated at this sacrifice upon the sacred grass, be exhilarated, (by drinking of the effused libation).
verses.griffith_verse: You, I have heard, were mightiest, Indra-Agni, when Vṛtra fell and when the spoil was parted. Sit at this sacrifice, ye ever active, on the strewn grass, and with the juice delight you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र चर्षणिभ्यः पृतनाहवेषु प्र पृथिव्या रिरिचाथे दिवश्च ।प्र सिंधुभ्यः प्र गिरिभ्यो महित्वा प्रेंद्राग्नी विश्वा भुवनात्यन्या ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ carṣaṇí-bhyaḥ ǀ pṛtanā-háveṣu ǀ prá ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ riricāthe íti ǀ diváḥ ǀ ca ǀprá ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ prá ǀ girí-bhyaḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ prá ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ áti ǀ anyā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Surpassing all men where they shout for battle, ye Twain exceed the earth and heaven in greatness. Greater are ye than rivers and than mountains, O Indra-Agni, and all things beside them.
verses.wilson_translation: Attending to the summons at the time of battle, you surpass all me (in magnitude); you are vaster than the earth, than the sky, than the rivers, than the mountains; you exceed all other existent things.
verses.griffith_verse: Surpassing all men where they shout for battle, ye Twain exceed the earth and heaven in greatness. Greater are ye than rivers and than mountains, O Indra-Agni, and all things beside them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू अस्माँ इंद्राग्नी अवतं शचीभिः ।इमे नु ते रश्मयः सूर्यस्य येभिः सपित्वं पितरो न आसन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ bharatam ǀ śíkṣatam ǀ vajrabāhū íti vajra-bāhū ǀ asmā́n ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ avatam ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀimé ǀ nú ǀ té ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ sa-pitvám ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́san ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring wealth and give it, ye whose arms wield thunder: Indra and Agni, with your powers protect us. Now of a truth these be the very sunbeams wherewith our fathers were of old united.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring wealth, thunderers, and give it to us; protect us,Indraand Agni, by your deeds; may those rays of the sun, by which our forefathers have attained together a hevenly region, shine also upon us.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring wealth and give it, ye whose arms wield thunder: Indra and Agni, with your powers protect us. Now of a truth these be the very sunbeams wherewith our fathers were of old united.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरंदरा शिक्षतं वज्रहस्तास्माँ इंद्राग्नी अवतं भरेषु ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: púram-darā ǀ śíkṣatam ǀ vajra-hastā ǀ asmā́n ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ avatam ǀ bháreṣu ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give, ye who shatter forts, whose hands wield thunder: Indra and Agni, save us in our battles. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, wielders of the thunderbolt, overturners of cities, grant us wealth, defens us in battles; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, be propitious to this (our prayer).
verses.griffith_verse: Give, ye who shatter forts, whose hands wield thunder: Indra and Agni, save us in our battles. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CX. Ṛbhus.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE holy work I wrought before is wrought again: my sweetest hymn is sung to celebrate your praise.Here, O ye Ṛbhus, is this sea for all the Gods: sate you with Soma offered with the hallowing word. When, seeking your enjoyment onward from afar, ye, certain of my kinsmen, wandered on your way,Sons of Sudhanvan, after your long journeying, ye came unto the home of liberal Savitar. Savitar therefore gave you immortality, because ye came proclaiming him whom naught can hide;And this the drinking-chalice of the Asura, which till that time was one, ye made to be fourfold. When they had served with zeal at sacrifice as priests, they, mortal as they were, gained immortality.The Ṛbhus, children of Sudhanvan, bright as suns, were in a year's course made associate with prayers. The Ṛbhus, with a rod measured, as ’twere a field, the single sacrificial chalice. wide of mouth,Lauded of all who saw, praying for what is best, desiring glorious fame among Immortal Gods. As oil in ladles, we through knowledge will present unto the Heroes of the firmament our hymn,—The Ṛbhus who came near with this great Father's speed, and rose to heaven's high sphere to eat the strengthening food. Ṛbhu to us is Indra freshest in his might, Ṛbhu with powers and wealth is giver of rich gifts.Gods, through your favour may we on the happy day quell the attacks of those who pour no offerings forth. Out of a skin, O Ṛbhus, once ye formed a cow, and brought the mother close unto her calf again.Sons of Sudhanvan, Heroes, with surpassing skill ye made your aged Parents youthful as before. Help us with strength where spoil is won, O Indra: joined with the Ṛbhus give us varied bounty.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: ततं मे अपस्तदु तायते पुनः स्वादिष्ठा धीतिरुचथाय शस्यते ।अयं समुद्र इह विश्वदेव्यः स्वाहाकृतस्य समु तृप्णुत ऋभवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tatám ǀ me ǀ ápaḥ ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tāyate ǀ púnaríti ǀ svā́diṣṭhā ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ ucáthāya ǀ śasyate ǀayám ǀ samudráḥ ǀ ihá ǀ viśvá-devyaḥ ǀ svā́hā-kṛtasya ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tṛpṇuta ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE holy work I wrought before is wrought again: my sweetest hymn is sung to celebrate your praise. Here, O ye Ṛbhus, is this sea for all the Gods: sate you with Soma offered with the hallowing word.
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛbhus, the rite formerly celebrated by me is again repeated, and the melodious hymn is recited in your praise; in this ceremony, the Somais sufficient for all the gods; drink of it to your utmost content when offered on the fire.
verses.griffith_verse: THE holy work I wrought before is wrought again: my sweetest hymn is sung to celebrate your praise. Here, O ye Ṛbhus, is this sea for all the Gods: sate you with Soma offered with the hallowing word.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आभोगयं प्र यदिच्छंत ऐतनापाकाः प्रांचो मम के चिदापयः ।सौधन्वनासश्चरितस्य भूमनागच्छत सवितुर्दाशुषो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-bhogáyam ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ icchántaḥ ǀ áitana ǀ ápākāḥ ǀ prā́ñcaḥ ǀ máma ǀ ké ǀ cit ǀ āpáyaḥ ǀsáudhanvanāsaḥ ǀ caritásya ǀ bhūmánā ǀ ágacchata ǀ savitúḥ ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, seeking your enjoyment onward from afar, ye, certain of my kinsmen, wandered on your way, Sons of Sudhanvan, after your long journeying, ye came unto the home of liberal Savitar.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Ṛbhus, you who are amongst my ancestors, yet immature (in wisdom), but desirous of enjoying (the Somalibations), retired to the forest to perform (penance), then, sons of Sudhanvan, throught he plural nitude of your completed (devotions), you came to the (sacrificial) hall of the worshipper Savitā.
verses.griffith_verse: When, seeking your enjoyment onward from afar, ye, certain of my kinsmen, wandered on your way, Sons of Sudhanvan, after your long journeying, ye came unto the home of liberal Savitar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तत्सविता वोऽमृतत्वमासुवदगोह्यं यच्छ्रवयंत ऐतन ।त्यं चिच्चमसमसुरस्य भक्षणमेकं संतमकृणुता चतुर्वयं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ savitā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ā́ ǀ asuvat ǀ ágohyam ǀ yát ǀ śraváyantaḥ ǀ áitana ǀtyám ǀ cit ǀ camasám ǀ ásurasya ǀ bhákṣaṇam ǀ ékam ǀ sántam ǀ akṛṇuta ǀ cátuḥ-vayam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Savitar therefore gave you immortality, because ye came proclaiming him whom naught can hide; And this the drinking-chalice of the Asura, which till that time was one, ye made to be fourfold.
verses.wilson_translation: Then Savitābestowed upon you immortality, when you came to him, who is not to be concealed, and representd (your desire) to partake of the libations; and that ladle for the sacrificial viands which the Asurahad formed single, you made fourfold.
verses.griffith_verse: Savitar therefore gave you immortality, because ye came proclaiming him whom naught can hide; And this the drinking-chalice of the Asura, which till that time was one, ye made to be fourfold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विष्ट्वी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः संतो अमृतत्वमानशुः ।सौधन्वना ऋभवः सूरचक्षसः संवत्सरे समपृच्यंत धीतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: viṣṭvī́ ǀ śámī ǀ taraṇi-tvéna ǀ vāghátaḥ ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ sántaḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśuḥ ǀsaudhanvanā́ḥ ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ sū́ra-cakṣasaḥ ǀ saṃvatsaré ǀ sám ǀ apṛcyanta ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they had served with zeal at sacrifice as priests, they, mortal as they were, gained immortality. The Ṛbhus, children of Sudhanvan, bright as suns, were in a year's course made associate with prayers.
verses.wilson_translation: Associated with the priests, and quickly performing the holy rites, they, being yet mortals, acquired immortality and the son of Sudhanvan, theṚbhus, brilliant as the sun, became connected with the ceremonies (appropriated to the different season) of the year.
verses.griffith_verse: When they had served with zeal at sacrifice as priests, they, mortal as they were, gained immortality. The Ṛbhus, children of Sudhanvan, bright as suns, were in a year's course made associate with prayers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रमिव वि ममुस्तेजनेनँ एकं पात्रमृभवो जेहमानं ।उपस्तुता उपमं नाधमाना अमर्त्येषु श्रव इच्छमानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣétram-iva ǀ ví ǀ mamuḥ ǀ téjanena ǀ ékam ǀ pā́tram ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ jéhamānam ǀúpa-stutāḥ ǀ upa-mám ǀ nā́dhamānāḥ ǀ ámartyeṣu ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ icchámānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Ṛbhus, with a rod measured, as ’twere a field, the single sacrificial chalice. wide of mouth, Lauded of all who saw, praying for what is best, desiring glorious fame among Immortal Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Lauded by the bystanders, theṚbhus, with a sharp weapon, meted outt the single sacrificial ladle, like a field (measured by a rod), soliciting the best (libations) and desiring (to participate of) sacrificial food amongs thte gods.
verses.griffith_verse: The Ṛbhus, with a rod measured, as ’twere a field, the single sacrificial chalice. wide of mouth, Lauded of all who saw, praying for what is best, desiring glorious fame among Immortal Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ मनीषामंतरिक्षस्य नृभ्यः स्रुचेव घृतं जुहवाम विद्मना ।तरणित्वा ये पितुरस्य सश्चिर ऋभवो वाजमरुहंदिवो रजः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ antárikṣasya ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ srucā́-iva ǀ ghṛtám ǀ juhavāma ǀ vidmánā ǀtaraṇi-tvā́ ǀ yé ǀ pitúḥ ǀ asya ǀ saściré ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ aruhan ǀ diváḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As oil in ladles, we through knowledge will present unto the Heroes of the firmament our hymn,— The Ṛbhus who came near with this great Father's speed, and rose to heaven's high sphere to eat the strengthening food.
verses.wilson_translation: To the leaders (of the sacrifice), dwelling in the firmament, we present, as with a ladle, the appointed clarified butter, and praise with knowledge thoseṚbhus, who, having equalled the velocityof the protector (of the universe, the sun), ascended to the region of heaven, through (the offerings) of (sacrificial) food.
verses.griffith_verse: As oil in ladles, we through knowledge will present unto the Heroes of the firmament our hymn,— The Ṛbhus who came near with this great Father's speed, and rose to heaven's high sphere to eat the strengthening food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुर्न इंद्रः शवसा नवीयानृभुर्वाजेभिर्वसुभिर्वसुर्ददिः ।युष्माकं देवा अवसाहनि प्रियेऽभि तिष्ठेम पृत्सुतीरसुन्वतां ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhúḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ návīyān ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ dadíḥ ǀyuṣmā́kam ǀ devāḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ áhani ǀ priyé ǀ abhí ǀ tiṣṭhema ǀ pṛtsutī́ḥ ǀ ásunvatām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ṛbhu to us is Indra freshest in his might, Ṛbhu with powers and wealth is giver of rich gifts. Gods, through your favour may we on the happy day quell the attacks of those who pour no offerings forth.
verses.wilson_translation: The most excellentṚbhuis in strength our defender; Ṛbhu, through gifts of food and of wealth, is our asylum; may he bestow them upon us, Gods, through your protection; may we, upon a favourable occasion, overcome the hosts of those who offer no libations.
verses.griffith_verse: Ṛbhu to us is Indra freshest in his might, Ṛbhu with powers and wealth is giver of rich gifts. Gods, through your favour may we on the happy day quell the attacks of those who pour no offerings forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निश्चर्मण ऋभवो गामपिंशत सं वत्सेनासृजता मातरं पुनः ।सौधन्वनासः स्वपस्यया नरो जिव्री युवाना पितराकृणोतन ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ ǀ cármaṇaḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ gā́m ǀ apiṃśata ǀ sám ǀ vatséna ǀ asṛjata ǀ mātáram ǀ púnaríti ǀsáudhanvanāsaḥ ǀ su-apasyáyā ǀ naraḥ ǀ jívrī íti ǀ yúvānā ǀ pitárā ǀ akṛṇotana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Out of a skin, O Ṛbhus, once ye formed a cow, and brought the mother close unto her calf again. Sons of Sudhanvan, Heroes, with surpassing skill ye made your aged Parents youthful as before.
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛbhus, you covered the cow with a hide, and reunited themother with the calf; sons of Sudhanvan, leaders (of sacrifice), through your good works you rendered your aged parents young.
verses.griffith_verse: Out of a skin, O Ṛbhus, once ye formed a cow, and brought the mother close unto her calf again. Sons of Sudhanvan, Heroes, with surpassing skill ye made your aged Parents youthful as before.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वाजेभिर्नो वाजसातावविड्ढ्यृभुमाँ इंद्र चित्रमा दर्षि राधः ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́jebhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀ aviḍḍhi ǀ ṛbhu-mā́n ǀ indra ǀ citrám ǀ ā́ ǀ darṣi ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Help us with strength where spoil is won, O Indra: joined with the Ṛbhus give us varied bounty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, associated with theṚbhus, supply us, in the distribution of viands, with food, and consent to bestow upon us wonderful riches; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve them fo rus.
verses.griffith_verse: Help us with strength where spoil is won, O Indra: joined with the Ṛbhus give us varied bounty. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXI. Ṛbhus.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WORKING with skill they wrought the lightly rolling car: they wrought the Bays who bear Indra and bring great gifts.The Ṛbhus for their Parents made life young again; and fashioned for the calf a mother by its side. For sacrifice make for us active vital power for skill and wisdom food with noble progeny.Grant to our company this power most excellent, that with a family all-heroic we may dwell. Do ye, O Ṛbhus, make prosperity for us, prosperity for car, ye Heroes, and for steed.Grant us prosperity victorious evermore,conquering foes in battle, strangers or akin. Indra, the Ṛbhus' Lord, I invocate for aid, the Ṛbhus, Vājas, Maruts to the Soma draught.Varuṇa, Mitra, both, yea, and the Aśvins Twain: let them speed us to wealth, wisdom, and victory. May Ṛbhu send prosperity for battle, may Vāja conquering in the fight protect us.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: तक्षन्रथं सुवृतं विद्मनापसस्तक्षन्हरी इंद्रवाहा वृषण्वसू ।तक्षन्पितृभ्यामृभवो युवद्वयस्तक्षन्वत्साय मातरं सचाभुवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tákṣan ǀ rátham ǀ su-vṛ́tam ǀ vidmanā́-apasaḥ ǀ tákṣan ǀ hárī íti ǀ indra-vā́hā ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇvasū íti vṛ́ṣaṇ-vasū ǀtákṣan ǀ pitṛ́-bhyām ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ yúvat ǀ váyaḥ ǀ tákṣan ǀ vatsā́ya ǀ mātáram ǀ sacā-bhúvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: WORKING with skill they wrought the lightly rolling car: they wrought the Bays who bear Indra and bring great gifts. The Ṛbhus for their Parents made life young again; and fashioned for the calf a mother by its side.
verses.wilson_translation: TheṚbhus, possessed of skill in their work, constructed (for the Aśvins) a well-built car; they framed the vigorous horses bearing Indra; they gave youthful existence to their parents; they gave to the calf its accompanying mother.
verses.griffith_verse: WORKING with skill they wrought the lightly rolling car: they wrought the Bays who bear Indra and bring great gifts. The Ṛbhus for their Parents made life young again; and fashioned for the calf a mother by its side.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो यज्ञाय तक्षत ऋभुमद्वयः क्रत्वे दक्षाय सुप्रजावतीमिषं ।यथा क्षयाम सर्ववीरया विशा तन्नः शर्धाय धासथा स्विंद्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñā́ya ǀ takṣata ǀ ṛbhu-mát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ krátve ǀ dákṣāya ǀ su-prajā́vatīm ǀ íṣam ǀyáthā ǀ kṣáyāma ǀ sárva-vīrayā ǀ viśā́ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ śárdhāya ǀ dhāsatha ǀ sú ǀ indriyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: For sacrifice make for us active vital power for skill and wisdom food with noble progeny. Grant to our company this power most excellent, that with a family all-heroic we may dwell.
verses.wilson_translation: Prepare fully for our sacrifice resplendent sacrificial food, and for our rite and for our strength, such nutriments as may be the cause of excellent progeny, so that we may live (surrounded) by vigorous descendants, such wealth do you confer upon us for our benefit.
verses.griffith_verse: For sacrifice make for us active vital power for skill and wisdom food with noble progeny. Grant to our company this power most excellent, that with a family all-heroic we may dwell.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तक्षत सातिमस्मभ्यमृभवः सातिं रथाय सातिमर्वते नरः ।सातिं नो जैत्रीं सं महेत विश्वहा जामिमजामिं पृतनासु सक्षणिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ takṣata ǀ sātím ǀ asmábhyam ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ sātím ǀ ráthāya ǀ sātím ǀ árvate ǀ naraḥ ǀsātím ǀ naḥ ǀ jáitrīm ǀ sám ǀ maheta ǀ viśváhā ǀ jāmím ǀ ájāmim ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ sakṣáṇim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do ye, O Ṛbhus, make prosperity for us, prosperity for car, ye Heroes, and for steed. Grant us prosperity victorious evermore, conquering foes in battle, strangers or akin.
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛbhusconductors (of sacrifice), bestow ample sustenance upon us, upon our chariots, upon our horses; let every one daily acknowledge our victorious wealth, and may we triumph in battle over our foes; whether strangers or kinsmen.
verses.griffith_verse: Do ye, O Ṛbhus, make prosperity for us, prosperity for car, ye Heroes, and for steed. Grant us prosperity victorious evermore, conquering foes in battle, strangers or akin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुक्षणमिंद्रमा हुव ऊतय ऋभून्वाजान्मरुतः सोमपीतये ।उभा मित्रावरुणा नूनमश्विना ते नो हिन्वंतु सातये धिये जिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhukṣáṇam ǀ índram ǀ ā́ ǀ huve ǀ ūtáye ǀ ṛbhū́n ǀ vā́jān ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀubhā́ ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ nūnám ǀ aśvínā ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ hinvantu ǀ sātáye ǀ dhiyé ǀ jiṣé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the Ṛbhus' Lord, I invocate for aid, the Ṛbhus, Vājas, Maruts to the Soma draught. Varuṇa, Mitra, both, yea, and the Aśvins Twain: let them speed us to wealth, wisdom, and victory.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the mighty Indrafor protection, and theṚbhu,Vājasand Marutsto drink the Soma, also both Mitra,Varuṇaand the Aśvins; and may they direct us to opulence, to holy rites, and to victory.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, the Ṛbhus' Lord, I invocate for aid, the Ṛbhus, Vājas, Maruts to the Soma draught. Varuṇa, Mitra, both, yea, and the Aśvins Twain: let them speed us to wealth, wisdom, and victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुर्भराय सं शिशातु सातिं समर्यजिद्वाजो अस्माँ अविष्टु ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhúḥ ǀ bhárāya ǀ sám ǀ śiśātu ǀ sātím ǀ samarya-jít ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ aviṣṭu ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Ṛbhu send prosperity for battle, may Vāja conquering in the fight protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: MayṚbhusupply us with wealth for war; may Vāja, victorious in battle, protect us, and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, be propitious ot this our prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: May Ṛbhu send prosperity for battle, may Vāja conquering in the fight protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXII. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: २५ कुत्स आङ्गिरसः। १(आद्यपादस्य) द्यावापृथिव्यौ, १(द्विती यपादस्य) अग्निः, १ (उत्तरार्धस्य) अश्विनौ, २-२५ अश्विनौ। जगती, २४-२५ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: To give first thought to them, I worship Heaven and Earth, and Agni, fair bright glow, to hasten their approach.Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith in fight ye speed the war-cry to the spoil. Ample, unfailing, they have mounted as it were an eloquent car that ye may think of us and give.Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye help our thoughts to further holy acts. Ye by the might which heavenly nectar giveth you are in supreme dominion Lords of all these folk.Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye, Heroes, made the barren cow give milk. The aids wherewith the Wanderer through his offspring's might, or the Two-Mothered Son shows swiftest mid the swift;Wherewith the sapient one acquired his triple lore,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye raised from waters, prisoned and fast bound, Rebha, and Vandana to look upon the light;Wherewith ye succoured Kaṇva as he strove to win,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye rescued Antaka when languishing deep in the pit, and Bhujyu with unfailing help.And comforted Karkandhu, Vayya, in their woe,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye gave Śucanti wealth and happy home, and made the fiery pit friendly for Atri's sake;Wherewith ye guarded Purukutsa, Pṛśnigu,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvin;, with those aids. Mighty Ones, with what powers ye gave Parāvṛj aid what time ye made the blind and lame to see and walk;Wherewith ye set at liberty the swallowed quail,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye quickened the most sweet exhaustless flood, and comforted Vasiṣṭha, ye who ne’er decay;And to Śrutarya, Kutsa, Narya gave your help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye helped, in battle of a thousand spoils, Viśpalā seeking booty, powerless to move.Wherewith ye guarded friendly Vaśa, Aśva's son,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Whereby the cloud, ye Bounteous Givers, shed sweet rain for Dīrghaśravas, for the merchant Auśija,Wherewith ye helped Kakṣīvān, singer of your praise,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye made Rasā swell full with water-floods, and urged to victory the car without a horse;Wherewith Triśoka drove forth his recovered cows,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye, compass round the Sun when far away, strengthened Mandhātar in his tasks as lord of lands,And to sage Bharadvāja gave protecting help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith, when Śambara was slain, ye guarded well great Atithigva, Divodāsa, Kaśoju,And Trasadasyu when the forts were shattered down,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye honoured the great drinker Vamra, and Upastuta and Kali when he gained his wife,And lent to Vyaśva and to Pṛthi favouring help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith, O Heroes, ye vouchsafed deliverance to Śayu, Atri, and to Manu long ago;Wherewith ye shot your shafts in Syūmaraśmi's cause.—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith Paṭharvā, in his majesty of form, shone in his course like to a gathered kindled fire;Wherewith ye helped Śāryāta in the mighty fray,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith, Aṅgirases! ye triumphed in your heart, and onward went to liberate the flood of milk;Wherewith ye helped the hero Manu with new strength,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye brought a wife for Vimada to wed, wherewith ye freely gave the ruddy cows away;Wherewith ye brought the host of kind Gods to Sudās—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye bring great bliss to him who offers gifts, wherewith ye have protected Bhujyu, Adhrigu,And good and gracious Subharā and Ṛtastup,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye served Kṛśānu where the shafts were shot, and helped the young man's horse to swiftness in the race;Wherewith ye bring delicious honey to the bees,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Wherewith ye speed the hero as he fights for kine in hero battle, in the strife for land and sons,Wherewith ye safely guard his horses and his car,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins with those aids. Wherewith ye, Lords of Hundred Powers, helped Kutsa, son of Ārjuni, gave Turvīti and Dabhīti strength,Favoured Dhvasanti and lent Puruṣanti help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids. Make ye our speech effectual, O ye Aśvins, and this our hymn, ye mighty Wonder-Workers.In luckless game I call on you for succour: strengthen us also on the field of battle. With, undiminished blessings, O ye Aśvins, for evermore both night and day protect us.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: ईळे द्यावापृथिवी पूर्वचित्तयेऽग्निं घर्मं सुरुचं यामन्निष्टये ।याभिर्भरे कारमंशाय जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: ī́ḷe ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ pūrvá-cittaye ǀ agním ǀ gharmám ǀ su-rúcam ǀ yā́man ǀ iṣṭáye ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ bháre ǀ kārám ǀ áṃśāya ǀ jínvathaḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: To give first thought to them, I worship Heaven and Earth, and Agni, fair bright glow, to hasten their approach. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith in fight ye speed the war-cry to the spoil.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise Heaven and Earth for preliminary meditation, (prior to the coming of the Aśvins); I praise the hot and bright-shining Agniupon their approach, (as preparatory) to their worship; with those appliances with which you sound the conch-shell in battle for your share (in the booty), with those aids, Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: To give first thought to them, I worship Heaven and Earth, and Agni, fair bright glow, to hasten their approach. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith in fight ye speed the war-cry to the spoil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवोर्दानाय सुभरा असश्चतो रथमा तस्थुर्वचसं न मंतवे ।याभिर्धियोऽवथः कर्मन्निष्टये ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ dānā́ya ǀ su-bhárāḥ ǀ asaścátaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ ā́ ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ vacasám ǀ ná ǀ mántave ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ávathaḥ ǀ kárman ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ample, unfailing, they have mounted as it were an eloquent car that ye may think of us and give. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye help our thoughts to further holy acts.
verses.wilson_translation: Earnest and exclusive adorers stand,Aśvins, round your car, (to benefit) by your bounty, as (disciples listen) to the words (of a teacher) for instrumental uction; with those aids with which you defend the pious who are engaged in acts of worship, come, Aśvins,wilingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Ample, unfailing, they have mounted as it were an eloquent car that ye may think of us and give. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye help our thoughts to further holy acts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं तासां दिव्यस्य प्रशासने विशां क्षयथो अमृतस्य मज्मना ।याभिर्धेनुमस्वं पिन्वथो नरा ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ tā́sām ǀ divyásya ǀ pra-śā́sane ǀ viśā́m ǀ kṣayathaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ majmánā ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ dhenúm ǀ asvám ǀ pínvathaḥ ǀ narā ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye by the might which heavenly nectar giveth you are in supreme dominion Lords of all these folk. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye, Heroes, made the barren cow give milk.
verses.wilson_translation: By the vigour infused from celestial nectar, you are able, leaders (of sacrifice), to rule over those beings (who people the three worldds); with those aids by which you gave (milk) to the barren cow, come,Aśvins, willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye by the might which heavenly nectar giveth you are in supreme dominion Lords of all these folk. Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids wherewith ye, Heroes, made the barren cow give milk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः परिज्मा तनयस्य मज्मना द्विमाता तूर्षु तरणिर्विभूषति ।याभिस्त्रिमंतुरभवद्विचक्षणस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ tánayasya ǀ majmánā ǀ dvi-mātā́ ǀ tūrṣú ǀ taráṇiḥ ǀ vi-bhū́ṣati ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ tri-mántuḥ ǀ ábhavat ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The aids wherewith the Wanderer through his offspring's might, or the Two-Mothered Son shows swiftest mid the swift; Wherewith the sapient one acquired his triple lore,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which the circumambient (wind), endowed with the vigour of his son, the measurer of the two worlds (of heaven and earth), and swiftest of the swift, beautifies (all things), and by which (Kakṣīvat) became learned in the three kinds of sacrifice; with them come,Aśvins, willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: The aids wherewith the Wanderer through his offspring's might, or the Two-Mothered Son shows swiftest mid the swift; Wherewith the sapient one acquired his triple lore,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभी रेभं निवृतं सितमद्भ्य उद्वंदनमैरयतं स्वर्दृशे ।याभिः कण्वं प्र सिषासंतमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ rebhám ǀ ní-vṛtam ǀ sitám ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ út ǀ vándanam ǀ áirayatam ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛśé ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ káṇvam ǀ prá ǀ sísāsantam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye raised from waters, prisoned and fast bound, Rebha, and Vandana to look upon the light; Wherewith ye succoured Kaṇva as he strove to win,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you raised up from the water, Rebha, who had been cst bound (into a well), and also Vandana(similarly circumstanced), to behold the sky; by which you protected Kaṇva, when longing to see the light; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye raised from waters, prisoned and fast bound, Rebha, and Vandana to look upon the light; Wherewith ye succoured Kaṇva as he strove to win,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिरंतकं जसमानमारणे भुज्युं याभिरव्यथिभिर्जिजिन्वथुः ।याभिः कर्कंधुं वय्यं च जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ ántakam ǀ jásamānam ǀ ā-áraṇe ǀ bhujyúm ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ avyathí-bhiḥ ǀ jijinváthuḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ karkándhum ǀ vayyám ǀ ca ǀ jínvathaḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye rescued Antaka when languishing deep in the pit, and Bhujyu with unfailing help. And comforted Karkandhu, Vayya, in their woe,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you rescued Antaka, (when cast into) a deep (pool), and about to be destroyed; by which, inflicting no distress, you preserved Bhujyu, and by which you relieved Karkandhuand Vayya; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye rescued Antaka when languishing deep in the pit, and Bhujyu with unfailing help. And comforted Karkandhu, Vayya, in their woe,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः शुचंतिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये ।याभिः पृश्निगुं पुरुकुत्समावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ śucantí ǀ dhana-sā́m ǀ su-saṃsádam ǀ taptám ǀ gharmám ǀ omyā́-vantam ǀ átraye ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ pṛ́śni-gum ǀ puru-kútsam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye gave Śucanti wealth and happy home, and made the fiery pit friendly for Atri's sake; Wherewith ye guarded Purukutsa, Pṛśnigu,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvin;, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you enrichedŚucanti, and gave him a handsome habitation, and rendered the scorching heat plural asurable to Atri, and by which you preserved Pṛśnigu and Purukutsa; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye gave Śucanti wealth and happy home, and made the fiery pit friendly for Atri's sake; Wherewith ye guarded Purukutsa, Pṛśnigu,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvin;, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः शचीभिर्वृषणा परावृजं प्रांधं श्रोणं चक्षस एतवे कृथः ।याभिर्वर्तिकां ग्रसिताममुंचतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ parā-vṛ́jam ǀ prá ǀ andhám ǀ śroṇám ǀ cákṣase ǀ étave ǀ kṛtháḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ vártikām ǀ grasitā́m ǀ ámuñcatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty Ones, with what powers ye gave Parāvṛj aid what time ye made the blind and lame to see and walk; Wherewith ye set at liberty the swallowed quail,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerers (of benefits), with those aids by which you enabled (the lame) Parāvṛj (to walk), the blind (Ṛjraśva) to see, and (the cripple)Śroṇato go, and by which you set free the quail when seized (by a wolf); with those aids,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty Ones, with what powers ye gave Parāvṛj aid what time ye made the blind and lame to see and walk; Wherewith ye set at liberty the swallowed quail,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः सिंधुं मधुमंतमसश्चतं वसिष्ठं याभिरजरावजिन्वतं ।याभिः कुत्सं श्रुतर्यं नर्यमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ síndhum ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ásaścatam ǀ vásiṣṭham ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ajarau ǀ ájinvatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ kútsam ǀ śrutáryam ǀ náryam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye quickened the most sweet exhaustless flood, and comforted Vasiṣṭha, ye who ne’er decay; And to Śrutarya, Kutsa, Narya gave your help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you caused the sweet stream to flow, by which you, who are exempt from decay, gratified Vāsiṣṭha, and by which you protected (ṛṣis:)Kutsa,Śrutarya, and Narya; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hitheṛ
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye quickened the most sweet exhaustless flood, and comforted Vasiṣṭha, ye who ne’er decay; And to Śrutarya, Kutsa, Narya gave your help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिर्विश्पलां धनसामथर्व्यं सहस्रमीळ्ह आजावजिन्वतं ।याभिर्वशमश्व्यं प्रेणिमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ viśpálām ǀ dhana-sā́m ǀ atharvyám ǀ sahásra-mīḷhe ǀ ājáu ǀ ájinvatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ váśam ǀ aśvyám ǀ preṇím ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye helped, in battle of a thousand spoils, Viśpalā seeking booty, powerless to move. Wherewith ye guarded friendly Vaśa, Aśva's son,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you enabled the opulent Viśpalā, when she was unable to move, to go to the battle rich in a thousand spoils, and by which you protected the devout Vaśa, the son of Aśva; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye helped, in battle of a thousand spoils, Viśpalā seeking booty, powerless to move. Wherewith ye guarded friendly Vaśa, Aśva's son,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः सुदानू औशिजाय वणिजे दीर्घश्रवसे मधु कोशो अक्षरत् ।कक्षीवंतं स्तोतारं याभिरावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ auśijā́ya ǀ vaṇíje ǀ dīrghá-śravase ǀ mádhu ǀ kóśaḥ ǀ ákṣarat ǀkakṣī́vantam ǀ stotā́ram ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whereby the cloud, ye Bounteous Givers, shed sweet rain for Dīrghaśravas, for the merchant Auśija, Wherewith ye helped Kakṣīvān, singer of your praise,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which, beauteous donors, the cloud (was made to) shed its sweet (water), for the sake of the merchant Dīrghaśravas, the son of Uṣij, and by which you protected the devout Kakṣīvat; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Whereby the cloud, ye Bounteous Givers, shed sweet rain for Dīrghaśravas, for the merchant Auśija, Wherewith ye helped Kakṣīvān, singer of your praise,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभी रसां क्षोदसोद्नः पिपिन्वथुरनश्वं याभी रथमावतं जिषे ।याभिस्त्रिशोक उस्रिया उदाजत ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ rasā́m ǀ kṣódasā ǀ udnáḥ ǀ pipinváthuḥ ǀ anaśvám ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ rátham ǀ ā́vatam ǀ jiṣé ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ tri-śókaḥ ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ ut-ā́jata ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye made Rasā swell full with water-floods, and urged to victory the car without a horse; Wherewith Triśoka drove forth his recovered cows,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you filled the (dry) river-bed
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye made Rasā swell full with water-floods, and urged to victory the car without a horse; Wherewith Triśoka drove forth his recovered cows,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः सूर्यं परियाथः परावति मंधातारं क्षैत्रपत्येष्वावतं ।याभिर्विप्रं प्र भरद्वाजमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ pari-yātháḥ ǀ parā-váti ǀ mandhātā́ram ǀ kṣáitra-patyeṣu ǀ ā́vatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ vípram ǀ prá ǀ bharát-vājam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye, compass round the Sun when far away, strengthened Mandhātar in his tasks as lord of lands, And to sage Bharadvāja gave protecting help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you encompassed the sun, when afar off, (to extricate him from eclipse); by which you defended Mandhātāin (the discharge of) his soverign functions, and by whciḥ you protected the sage Bharadvāja; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye, compass round the Sun when far away, strengthened Mandhātar in his tasks as lord of lands, And to sage Bharadvāja gave protecting help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिर्महामतिथिग्वं कशोजुवं दिवोदासं शंबरहत्य आवतं ।याभिः पूर्भिद्ये त्रसदस्युमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ mahā́m ǀ atithi-gvám ǀ kaśaḥ-júvam ǀ dívaḥ-dāsam ǀ śambara-hátye ǀ ā́vatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ pūḥ-bhídye ǀ trasádasyum ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith, when Śambara was slain, ye guarded well great Atithigva, Divodāsa, Kaśoju, And Trasadasyu when the forts were shattered down,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you defended the mighty and hospitable Divodāsa, (when, having undertaken) the death ofŚambara, he hid himself in the water (through fear of theasuras); by which you protected Trasadasyuin war; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith, when Śambara was slain, ye guarded well great Atithigva, Divodāsa, Kaśoju, And Trasadasyu when the forts were shattered down,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिर्वम्रं विपिपानमुपस्तुतं कलिं याभिर्वित्तजानिं दुवस्यथः ।याभिर्व्यश्वमुत पृथिमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ vamrám ǀ vi-pipānám ǀ upa-stutám ǀ kalím ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ vittá-jānim ǀ duvasyáthaḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ ví-aśvam ǀ utá ǀ pṛ́thim ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye honoured the great drinker Vamra, and Upastuta and Kali when he gained his wife, And lent to Vyaśva and to Pṛthi favouring help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you preserved Vamra, praised by all around him, when drinking (the dews of the earth); by which you protected Kaliwhen he had taken a wife, and Pṛthi,when had lost his horse; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye honoured the great drinker Vamra, and Upastuta and Kali when he gained his wife, And lent to Vyaśva and to Pṛthi favouring help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिर्नरा शयवे याभिरत्रये याभिः पुरा मनवे गातुमीषथुः ।याभिः शारीराजतं स्यूमरश्मये ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ narā ǀ śayáve ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ átraye ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ mánave ǀ gātúm ǀ īṣáthuḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ śā́rīḥ ǀ ā́jatam ǀ syū́ma-raśmaye ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith, O Heroes, ye vouchsafed deliverance to Śayu, Atri, and to Manu long ago; Wherewith ye shot your shafts in Syūmaraśmi's cause.—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids, leaders (of sacrifices), which you afforded toŚayu, to Atri, and formerly to Manu, anxious (to show them) the way (to escape from evil); with those by which you shot arrows (upon the foes) of Syūmaraśmi; with them, Aśvis, willingly come hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith, O Heroes, ye vouchsafed deliverance to Śayu, Atri, and to Manu long ago; Wherewith ye shot your shafts in Syūmaraśmi's cause.—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः पठर्वा जठरस्य मज्मनाग्निर्नादीदेच्चित इद्धो अज्मन्ना ।याभिः शर्यातमवथो महाधने ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ páṭharvā ǀ jáṭharasya ǀ majmánā ǀ agníḥ ǀ ná ǀ ádīdet ǀ citáḥ ǀ iddháḥ ǀ ájman ǀ ā́ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ śáryātam ǀ ávathaḥ ǀ mahā-dhané ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith Paṭharvā, in his majesty of form, shone in his course like to a gathered kindled fire; Wherewith ye helped Śāryāta in the mighty fray,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: WIth those aids by which Paddarvan shone with with strngth of orm in battle, like a blazing fire piled up (with fuel); by which you defendedŚaryātain war; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith Paṭharvā, in his majesty of form, shone in his course like to a gathered kindled fire; Wherewith ye helped Śāryāta in the mighty fray,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिरंगिरो मनसा निरण्यथोऽग्रं गच्छथो विवरे गोअर्णसः ।याभिर्मनुं शूरमिषा समावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ ni-raṇyáthaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ vi-varé ǀ gó-arṇasaḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ mánum ǀ śū́ram ǀ iṣā́ ǀ sam-ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith, Aṅgirases! ye triumphed in your heart, and onward went to liberate the flood of milk; Wherewith ye helped the hero Manu with new strength,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: Aṅgiras, (prise the Aśvins); Aśvins, with those aids by which, with (gratified) minds, you delight (in praise), and thence preceded the gods to the cavern, to recover the stolen cattle; by which you sustained the heroic Manuwith food; with them, Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith, Aṅgirases! ye triumphed in your heart, and onward went to liberate the flood of milk; Wherewith ye helped the hero Manu with new strength,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः पत्नीर्विमदाय न्यूहथुरा घ वा याभिररुणीरशिक्षतं ।याभिः सुदास ऊहथुः सुदेव्यं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ ni-ūháthuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gha ǀ vā ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ aruṇī́ḥ ǀ áśikṣatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ su-dā́se ǀ ūháthuḥ ǀ su-devyám ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye brought a wife for Vimada to wed, wherewith ye freely gave the ruddy cows away; Wherewith ye brought the host of kind Gods to Sudās—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you gave a wife to Vimada, by which you recovered the ruddy kine, by which you conferred excellent wealth upon Sudās; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye brought a wife for Vimada to wed, wherewith ye freely gave the ruddy cows away; Wherewith ye brought the host of kind Gods to Sudās—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः शंताती भवथो ददाशुषे भुज्युं याभिरवथो याभिरध्रिगुं ।ओम्यावतीं सुभरामृतस्तुभं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ śáṃtātī íti śáṃ-tātī ǀ bhávathaḥ ǀ dadāśúṣe ǀ bhujyúm ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ávathaḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ádhri-gum ǀomyā́-vatīm ǀ su-bhárām ǀ ṛta-stúbham ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye bring great bliss to him who offers gifts, wherewith ye have protected Bhujyu, Adhrigu, And good and gracious Subharā and Ṛtastup,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you are bestowers of happiness upon the donor (of oblations), by which you have protected Bhujyuand Adhrigu, and by which you have granted delighting and nourishing (food) to Ritastubh; with them.Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye bring great bliss to him who offers gifts, wherewith ye have protected Bhujyu, Adhrigu, And good and gracious Subharā and Ṛtastup,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः कृशानुमसने दुवस्यथो जवे याभिर्यूनो अर्वंतमावतं ।मधु प्रियं भरथो यत्सरड्भ्यस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ kṛśā́num ǀ ásane ǀ duvasyáthaḥ ǀ javé ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ yū́naḥ ǀ árvantam ǀ ā́vatam ǀmádhu ǀ priyám ǀ bharathaḥ ǀ yát ǀ saráṭ-bhyaḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye served Kṛśānu where the shafts were shot, and helped the young man's horse to swiftness in the race; Wherewith ye bring delicious honey to the bees,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you defended Kṛśānuin battle, with which you succoured the horse of the young Purukutsain speed, and by which you deliver the plural asant honey to the bees; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye served Kṛśānu where the shafts were shot, and helped the young man's horse to swiftness in the race; Wherewith ye bring delicious honey to the bees,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिर्नरं गोषुयुधं नृषाह्ये क्षेत्रस्य साता तनयस्य जिन्वथः ।याभी रथाँ अवथो याभिरर्वतस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ náram ǀ goṣu-yúdham ǀ nṛ-sáhye ǀ kṣétrasya ǀ sātā́ ǀ tánayasya ǀ jínvathaḥ ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ ráthān ǀ ávathaḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ árvataḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye speed the hero as he fights for kine in hero battle, in the strife for land and sons, Wherewith ye safely guard his horses and his car,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you succoured the worshipper contending in war for cattle, by which you assist him in the acquisition of houses and wealth, by which you preserve his chariots and horses; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hitheṛ
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye speed the hero as he fights for kine in hero battle, in the strife for land and sons, Wherewith ye safely guard his horses and his car,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतू प्र तुर्वीतिं प्र च दभीतिमावतं ।याभिर्ध्वसंतिं पुरुषंतिमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ kútsam ǀ ārjuneyám ǀ śatakratū íti śata-kratū ǀ prá ǀ turvī́tim ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ dabhī́tim ǀ ā́vatam ǀyā́bhiḥ ǀ dhvasántim ǀ puru-sántim ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherewith ye, Lords of Hundred Powers, helped Kutsa, son of Ārjuni, gave Turvīti and Dabhīti strength, Favoured Dhvasanti and lent Puruṣanti help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.wilson_translation: With those aids by which you, who are worshipped in many rites, protected Kutsa, the son of Arjuna, as well as Turviti, Dhabhiti, Dhvasant, and Puruśanti; with them,Aśvins, come willingly hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Wherewith ye, Lords of Hundred Powers, helped Kutsa, son of Ārjuni, gave Turvīti and Dabhīti strength, Favoured Dhvasanti and lent Puruṣanti help,—Come hither unto us, O Aśvins, with those aids.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्नस्वतीमश्विना वाचमस्मे कृतं नो दस्रा वृषणा मनीषां ।अद्यूत्येऽवसे नि ह्वये वां वृधे च नो भवतं वाजसातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ápnasvatīm ǀ aśvinā ǀ vā́cam ǀ asmé íti ǀ kṛtám ǀ naḥ ǀ dasrā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ manīṣā́m ǀadyūtyé ǀ ávase ǀ ní ǀ hvaye ǀ vām ǀ vṛdhé ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make ye our speech effectual, O ye Aśvins, and this our hymn, ye mighty Wonder-Workers. In luckless game I call on you for succour: strengthen us also on the field of battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, sanctify our words with works; showerers (of benefits), subduers of foes (invigorate) our understandin g(for the sacred study); we invoke you both, in the last watch of the night, for our preservation; be to us for increase in the provision of food.
verses.griffith_verse: Make ye our speech effectual, O ye Aśvins, and this our hymn, ye mighty Wonder-Workers. In luckless game I call on you for succour: strengthen us also on the field of battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्युभिरक्तुभिः परि पातमस्मानरिष्टेभिरश्विना सौभगेभिः ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: dyú-bhiḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ pári ǀ pātam ǀ asmā́n ǀ áriṣṭebhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ sáubhagebhiḥ ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With, undiminished blessings, O ye Aśvins, for evermore both night and day protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Cherish us,Aśvins, always, by night or day, with undiminished blessings; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, be favourable to this our (prayer).
verses.griffith_verse: With, undiminished blessings, O ye Aśvins, for evermore both night and day protect us. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXIII. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness.Night, sent away for Savitar's uprising, hath yielded up a birth-place for the Morning. The Fair, the Bright is come with her white offspring; to her the Dark One hath resigned her dwelling.Akin, immortal, following each other, changing their colours both the heavens move onward. Common, unending is the Sisters' pathway; taught by the Gods, alternately they travel.Fair-formed, of different hues and yet one-minded, Night and Dawn clash not, neither do they travel. Bright leader of glad sounds, our eyes behold her; splendid in hue she hath unclosed the portals.She, stirring up the world, hath shown us riches: Dawn hath awakened every living creature. Rich Dawn, she sets afoot the coiled-up sleeper, one for enjoyment, one for wealth or worship,Those who saw little for extended vision. All living creatures hath the Dawn awakened. One to high sway, one to exalted glory, one to pursue his gain, and one his labour:All to regard their different vocations, all moving creatures hath the Dawn awakened. We see her there, the Child of Heaven apparent, the young Maid, flushing in her shining raiment.Thou sovran Lady of all earthly treasure, flush on us here, auspicious Dawn, this morning. She first of endless morns to come hereafter, follows the path of morns that have departed.Dawn, at her rising, urges forth the living him who is dead she wakes not from his slumber. As thou, Dawn, hast caused Agni to be kindled, and with the Sun's eye hast revealed creation.And hast awakened men to offer worship, thou hast performed, for Gods, a noble service. How long a time, and they shall be together,—Dawns that have shone and Dawns to shine hereafter?She yearns for former Dawns with eager longing, and goes forth gladly shining with the others. Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning.We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her. Foe-chaser, born of Law, the Law's protectress, joy-giver, waker of all pleasant voices,Auspicious, bringing food for Gods’ enjoyment, shine on us here, most bright, O Dawn, this morning. From days eternal hath Dawn shone, the Goddess, and shows this light to-day, endowed with riches.So will she shine on days to come immortal she moves on in her own strength, undecaying. In the sky's borders hath she shone in splendour: the Goddess hath thrown off the veil of darkness.Awakening the world with purple horses, on her well-harnessed chariot Dawn approaches. Bringing all life-sustaining blessings with her, showing herself she sends forth brilliant lustre.Last of the countless mornings that have vanished, first of bright morns to come hath Dawn arisen. Arise! the breath, the life, again hath reached us: darkness hath passed away and light approacheth.She for the Sun hath left a path to travel we have arrived where men prolong existence. Singing the praises of refulgent Mornings with his hymn's web the priest, the poet rises.Shine then to-day, rich Maid, on him who lauds thee, shine down on us the gift of life and offspring. Dawns giving sons all heroes, kine and horses, shining upon the man who brings oblations,—These let the Soma-presser gain when ending his glad songs louder than the voice of Vāyu. Mother of Gods, Aditi's form of glory, ensign of sacrifice, shine forth exalted.Rise up, bestowing praise on our devotion all-bounteous, make us chief among the people. Whatever splendid wealth the Dawns bring with them to bless the man who offers praise and worship,Even that may Mitra, Varuṇa vouchsafe us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ jyótiṣām ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ citráḥ ǀ pra-ketáḥ ǀ ajaniṣṭa ǀ ví-bhvā ǀyáthā ǀ prá-sūtā ǀ savitúḥ ǀ savā́ya ǀ evá ǀ rā́trī ǀ uṣáse ǀ yónim ǀ araik ǁ
verses.english_translation: This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness. Night, sent away for Savitar's uprising, hath yielded up a birth-place for the Morning.
verses.wilson_translation: This most excellent luminary of all luminaries has arrived; the wonderful and diffusive manifester (of all things) has been born; in like manner as night is the offspring of the sun, so she becomes the birth-plural ce of the dawn.
verses.griffith_verse: This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness. Night, sent away for Savitar's uprising, hath yielded up a birth-place for the Morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ।समानबंधू अमृते अनूची द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ॥
verses.transliteration: rúśat-vatsā ǀ rúśatī ǀ śvetyā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ áraik ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ sádanāni ǀ asyāḥ ǀsamānábandhū íti samāná-bandhū ǀ amṛ́te íti ǀ anūcī́ íti ǀ dyā́vā ǀ várṇam ǀ carataḥ ǀ āmināné ítyā-mināné ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Fair, the Bright is come with her white offspring; to her the Dark One hath resigned her dwelling. Akin, immortal, following each other, changing their colours both the heavens move onward.
verses.wilson_translation: The white-shining dawn, the parent of the sun, has arrived; dark night has sought her own abode; both allied to the same (sun), immortal, succeeding to each other, and mutually effacing each other's complexion, they traverse the heavens.
verses.griffith_verse: The Fair, the Bright is come with her white offspring; to her the Dark One hath resigned her dwelling. Akin, immortal, following each other, changing their colours both the heavens move onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानो अध्वा स्वस्रोरनंतस्तमन्यान्या चरतो देवशिष्टे ।न मेथेते न तस्थतुः सुमेके नक्तोषासा समनसा विरूपे ॥
verses.transliteration: samānáḥ ǀ ádhvā ǀ svásroḥ ǀ anantáḥ ǀ tám ǀ anyā́-anyā ǀ carataḥ ǀ deváśiṣṭe íti devá-śiṣṭe ǀná ǀ methete íti ǀ ná ǀ tasthatuḥ ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀ náktoṣásā ǀ sá-manasā ǀ vírūpe íti ví-rūpe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Common, unending is the Sisters' pathway; taught by the Gods, alternately they travel. Fair-formed, of different hues and yet one-minded, Night and Dawn clash not, neither do they travel.
verses.wilson_translation: The path of the sisters is unending; they travel it alternately, guided by the radiant (sun); combined in purpose, though of different forms, night and dawn, giving birth (to all things), obstruct not eachother, neither do they stand still.
verses.griffith_verse: Common, unending is the Sisters' pathway; taught by the Gods, alternately they travel. Fair-formed, of different hues and yet one-minded, Night and Dawn clash not, neither do they travel.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भास्वती नेत्री सूनृतानामचेति चित्रा वि दुरो न आवः ।प्रार्प्या जगद्व्यु नो रायो अख्यदुषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: bhā́svatī ǀ netrī́ ǀ sūnṛ́tānām ǀ áceti ǀ citrā́ ǀ ví ǀ dúraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ āvarítyāvaḥ ǀpra-árpya ǀ jágat ǀ ví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ akhyat ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ajīgaḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bright leader of glad sounds, our eyes behold her; splendid in hue she hath unclosed the portals. She, stirring up the world, hath shown us riches: Dawn hath awakened every living creature.
verses.wilson_translation: Brilliant guide of the speakers of truth, the many-tinted dawn, is recognized by us; she has opened our doors; having illuminated the world, she has made our riches manifest. Uṣās gives back all the regions (that had been swallowed up by night).
verses.griffith_verse: Bright leader of glad sounds, our eyes behold her; splendid in hue she hath unclosed the portals. She, stirring up the world, hath shown us riches: Dawn hath awakened every living creature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जिह्मश्ये चरितवे मघोन्याभोगय इष्टये राय उ त्वं ।दभ्रं पश्यद्भ्य उर्विया विचक्ष उषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: jihma-śyé ǀ cáritave ǀ maghónī ǀ ā-bhogáye ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ rāyé ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvam ǀdabhrám ǀ páśyat-bhyaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ vi-cákṣe ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ajīgaḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich Dawn, she sets afoot the coiled-up sleeper, one for enjoyment, one for wealth or worship, Those who saw little for extended vision. All living creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.wilson_translation: The opulent (dawn) arouses to exertion the man bowed down in sleep--one man to enjoyments, another to devotion, another to (the acquisition of) wealth; she has enabled those who were almost sightless to see distinctly. The expansive Uṣas has given back all the regions.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich Dawn, she sets afoot the coiled-up sleeper, one for enjoyment, one for wealth or worship, Those who saw little for extended vision. All living creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्षत्राय त्वं श्रवसे त्वं महीया इष्टये त्वमर्थमिव त्वमित्यै ।विसदृशा जीविताभिप्रचक्ष उषा अजीगर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣatrā́ya ǀ tvam ǀ śrávase ǀ tvam ǀ mahīyái ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ tvam ǀ ártham-iva ǀ tvam ǀ ityái ǀví-sadṛśā ǀ jīvitā́ ǀ abhi-pracákṣe ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ajīgaḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: One to high sway, one to exalted glory, one to pursue his gain, and one his labour: All to regard their different vocations, all moving creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.wilson_translation: The dawn rouses one man to acquire wealth, another to earn food, another to achieve greatness, another to sacrifices, another to his own (pursuits), another to activity, and lights all men to their various means of maintaining life. Uṣās has given back all the regions.
verses.griffith_verse: One to high sway, one to exalted glory, one to pursue his gain, and one his labour: All to regard their different vocations, all moving creatures hath the Dawn awakened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि व्युच्छंती युवतिः शुक्रवासाः ।विश्वस्येशाना पार्थिवस्य वस्व उषो अद्येह सुभगे व्युच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ práti ǀ adarśi ǀ vi-ucchántī ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ śukrá-vāsāḥ ǀvíśvasya ǀ ī́śānā ǀ pā́rthivasya ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ ihá ǀ su-bhage ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: We see her there, the Child of Heaven apparent, the young Maid, flushing in her shining raiment. Thou sovran Lady of all earthly treasure, flush on us here, auspicious Dawn, this morning.
verses.wilson_translation: The daughter of heaven, young, white-robed, the mistress of all earthly treasure, is beheld dissipating the darkness. Auspicious Uṣās,shine upon us today in this (hall of sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: We see her there, the Child of Heaven apparent, the young Maid, flushing in her shining raiment. Thou sovran Lady of all earthly treasure, flush on us here, auspicious Dawn, this morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परायतीनामन्वेति पाथ आयतीनां प्रथमा शश्वतीनां ।व्युच्छंती जीवमुदीरयंत्युषा मृतं कं चन बोधयंती ॥
verses.transliteration: parā-yatīnā́m ǀ ánu ǀ eti ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ ā-yatīnā́m ǀ prathamā́ ǀ śáśvatīnām ǀvi-ucchántī ǀ jīvám ǀ ut-īráyantī ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ mṛtám ǀ kám ǀ caná ǀ bodháyantī ǁ
verses.english_translation: She first of endless morns to come hereafter, follows the path of morns that have departed. Dawn, at her rising, urges forth the living him who is dead she wakes not from his slumber.
verses.wilson_translation: Following the path
verses.griffith_verse: She first of endless morns to come hereafter, follows the path of morns that have departed. Dawn, at her rising, urges forth the living him who is dead she wakes not from his slumber.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषो यदग्निं समिधे चकर्थ वि यदावश्चक्षसा सूर्यस्य ।यन्मानुषान्यक्ष्यमाणाँ अजीगस्तद्देवेषु चकृषे भद्रमप्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ yát ǀ agním ǀ sam-ídhe ǀ cakártha ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ ā́vaḥ ǀ cákṣasā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀyát ǀ mā́nuṣān ǀ yakṣyámāṇān ǀ ájīgaríti ǀ tát ǀ devéṣu ǀ cakṛṣe ǀ bhadrám ǀ ápnaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou, Dawn, hast caused Agni to be kindled, and with the Sun's eye hast revealed creation. And hast awakened men to offer worship, thou hast performed, for Gods, a noble service.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣās, inasmuch as you have caused the sacred fire to be kindled, inasmuch as you have lighted the world with the light of the sun, inasmuch as you have wakened men to perform sacrifice, you have done good service to the godṣ
verses.griffith_verse: As thou, Dawn, hast caused Agni to be kindled, and with the Sun's eye hast revealed creation. And hast awakened men to offer worship, thou hast performed, for Gods, a noble service.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कियात्या यत्समया भवाति या व्यूषुर्याश्च नूनं व्युच्छान् ।अनु पूर्वाः कृपते वावशाना प्रदीध्याना जोषमन्याभिरेति ॥
verses.transliteration: kíyati ǀ ā́ ǀ yát ǀ samáyā ǀ bhávāti ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ vi-ūṣúḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ nūnám ǀ vi-ucchā́n ǀánu ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ kṛpate ǀ vāvaśānā́ ǀ pra-dī́dhyānā ǀ jóṣam ǀ anyā́bhiḥ ǀ eti ǁ
verses.english_translation: How long a time, and they shall be together,—Dawns that have shone and Dawns to shine hereafter? She yearns for former Dawns with eager longing, and goes forth gladly shining with the others.
verses.wilson_translation: For how long a period is it that the dawns have risen? for how long a period will they rise? still desirous to bring us light, Uṣās pursues the functions of those that have gone before, and, shining brightly, proceeds with the others (that are to follow).
verses.griffith_verse: How long a time, and they shall be together,—Dawns that have shone and Dawns to shine hereafter? She yearns for former Dawns with eager longing, and goes forth gladly shining with the others.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ईयुष्टे ये पूर्वतरामपश्यन्व्युच्छंतीमुषसं मर्त्यासः ।अस्माभिरू नु प्रतिचक्ष्याभूदो ते यंति ये अपरीषु पश्यान् ॥
verses.transliteration: īyúḥ ǀ té ǀ yé ǀ pū́rva-tarām ǀ ápaśyan ǀ vi-ucchántīm ǀ uṣásam ǀ mártyāsaḥ ǀasmā́bhiḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ prati-cákṣyā ǀ abhūt ǀ ó íti ǀ té ǀ yanti ǀ yé ǀ aparī́ṣu ǀ páśyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning. We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her.
verses.wilson_translation: Those mortals who beheld the pristine Uṣās dawning have passed away; to us she is now visible, and they approach who may behold her in after times.
verses.griffith_verse: Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning. We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यावयद्द्वेषा ऋतपा ऋतेजाः सुम्नावरी सूनृता ईरयंती ।सुमंगलीर्बिभ्रती देववीतिमिहाद्योषः श्रेष्ठतमा व्युच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: yavayát-dveṣāḥ ǀ ṛta-pā́ḥ ǀ ṛte-jā́ḥ ǀ sumna-várī ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ īráyantī ǀsu-maṅgalī́ḥ ǀ bíbhratī ǀ devá-vītim ǀ ihá ǀ adyá ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ śréṣṭha-tamā ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Foe-chaser, born of Law, the Law's protectress, joy-giver, waker of all pleasant voices, Auspicious, bringing food for Gods’ enjoyment, shine on us here, most bright, O Dawn, this morning.
verses.wilson_translation: The beings hostile (to acts of devotion) now withdraw, for she is the protectress of sacred rites, who is manifested for their performance; she is the giver of happiness, the awakener of plural asant voices, the enjoyer of felicity, and provider of food for the gods; most excellent Uṣās dawn today on this (sacrificial hall).
verses.griffith_verse: Foe-chaser, born of Law, the Law's protectress, joy-giver, waker of all pleasant voices, Auspicious, bringing food for Gods’ enjoyment, shine on us here, most bright, O Dawn, this morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी ।अथो व्युच्छादुत्तराँ अनु द्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: śáśvat ǀ purā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ uvāsa ǀ devī́ ǀ átho íti ǀ adyá ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ āvaḥ ǀ maghónī ǀátho íti ǀ ví ǀ ucchāt ǀ út-tarān ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ ajárā ǀ amṛ́tā ǀ carati ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From days eternal hath Dawn shone, the Goddess, and shows this light to-day, endowed with riches. So will she shine on days to come immortal she moves on in her own strength, undecaying.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Uṣās dawned continually in former times; the source of wealth, she still rises on this (world); so will she give light hereafter, through future days, for, exempt from decay or death, she goes on in her splendour.
