verses.griffith_verse: From days eternal hath Dawn shone, the Goddess, and shows this light to-day, endowed with riches. So will she shine on days to come immortal she moves on in her own strength, undecaying.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्यंजिभिर्दिव आतास्वद्यौदप कृष्णां निर्णिजं देव्यावः ।प्रबोधयंत्यरुणेभिरश्वैरोषा याति सुयुजा रथेन ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́tāsu ǀ adyaut ǀ ápa ǀ kṛṣṇā́m ǀ niḥ-níjam ǀ devī́ ǀ āvarítyāvaḥ ǀpra-bodháyantī ǀ aruṇébhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ yāti ǀ su-yújā ǀ ráthena ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the sky's borders hath she shone in splendour: the Goddess hath thrown off the veil of darkness. Awakening the world with purple horses, on her well-harnessed chariot Dawn approaches.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Uṣās lights up with her beams the quarters of the heavens; she has thrown off her gloomy form, and, awaking (those who sleep), comes in her car, drawn by purple steeds.
verses.griffith_verse: In the sky's borders hath she shone in splendour: the Goddess hath thrown off the veil of darkness. Awakening the world with purple horses, on her well-harnessed chariot Dawn approaches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आवहंती पोष्या वार्याणि चित्रं केतुं कृणुते चेकिताना ।ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनां विभातीनां प्रथमोषा व्यश्वैत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-váhantī ǀ póṣyā ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀ citrám ǀ ketúm ǀ kṛṇute ǀ cékitānā ǀīyúṣīṇām ǀ upa-mā́ ǀ śáśvatīnām ǀ vi-bhātīnā́m ǀ prathamā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśvait ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bringing all life-sustaining blessings with her, showing herself she sends forth brilliant lustre. Last of the countless mornings that have vanished, first of bright morns to come hath Dawn arisen.
verses.wilson_translation: Bringing with her life-sustaining blessings, and giving consciousness (to the unconscious), she imparts (to the world) her wonderful radiance. The similitude of numerous dawns that have gone by, the first of the billiant (dawns that are to come), Uṣās has today appeared.
verses.griffith_verse: Bringing all life-sustaining blessings with her, showing herself she sends forth brilliant lustre. Last of the countless mornings that have vanished, first of bright morns to come hath Dawn arisen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीर्ध्वं जीवो असुर्न आगादप प्रागात्तम आ ज्योतिरेति ।आरैक्पंथां यातवे सूर्यायागन्म यत्र प्रतिरंत आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrdhvam ǀ jīváḥ ǀ ásuḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ ápa ǀ prá ǀ agāt ǀ támaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ eti ǀáraik ǀ pánthām ǀ yā́tave ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ áganma ǀ yátra ǀ pra-tiránte ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Arise! the breath, the life, again hath reached us: darkness hath passed away and light approacheth. She for the Sun hath left a path to travel we have arrived where men prolong existence.
verses.wilson_translation: Arise; inspiring life revives; darkness has departed; light approaches. Uṣās has opened the road for the sun to travel; let us repair to where they distribute food.
verses.griffith_verse: Arise! the breath, the life, again hath reached us: darkness hath passed away and light approacheth. She for the Sun hath left a path to travel we have arrived where men prolong existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्यूमना वाच उदियर्ति वह्निः स्तवानो रेभ उषसो विभातीः ।अद्या तदुच्छ गृणते मघोन्यस्मे आयुर्नि दिदीहि प्रजावत् ॥
verses.transliteration: syū́manā ǀ vācáḥ ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ váhniḥ ǀ stávānaḥ ǀ rebháḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀadyá ǀ tát ǀ uccha ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ maghoni ǀ asmé íti ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ní ǀ didīhi ǀ prajā́-vat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Singing the praises of refulgent Mornings with his hymn's web the priest, the poet rises. Shine then to-day, rich Maid, on him who lauds thee, shine down on us the gift of life and offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: The offerer of praise, the reciter of praise, celebrating the brilliant Uṣas, repeats the well-connected words (of the Veda). Possessor of affluence, dawn today upon him who praise you; bestow upon us food, whence progeny may be obtained.
verses.griffith_verse: Singing the praises of refulgent Mornings with his hymn's web the priest, the poet rises. Shine then to-day, rich Maid, on him who lauds thee, shine down on us the gift of life and offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या गोमतीरुषसः सर्ववीरा व्युच्छंति दाशुषे मर्त्याय ।वायोरिव सूनृतानामुदर्के ता अश्वदा अश्नवत्सोमसुत्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sárva-vīrāḥ ǀ vi-ucchánti ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǀvāyóḥ-iva ǀ sūnṛ́tānām ǀ ut-arké ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ aśva-dā́ḥ ǀ aśnavat ǀ soma-sútvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dawns giving sons all heroes, kine and horses, shining upon the man who brings oblations,— These let the Soma-presser gain when ending his glad songs louder than the voice of Vāyu.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who has offered the libation obtain, upon the conclusion of his praises, (enunciated), life the wind, (with speed), (the favour of) those Uṣasas who are givers of horses, and of cattle, and of progeny, and who shed light upon the mortal presenting to them (offerings).
verses.griffith_verse: Dawns giving sons all heroes, kine and horses, shining upon the man who brings oblations,— These let the Soma-presser gain when ending his glad songs louder than the voice of Vāyu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: माता देवानामदितेरनीकं यज्ञस्य केतुर्बृहती वि भाहि ।प्रशस्तिकृद्ब्रह्मणे नो व्युच्छा नो जने जनय विश्ववारे ॥
verses.transliteration: mātā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ánīkam ǀ yajñásya ǀ ketúḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ ǀ ví ǀ bhāhi ǀpraśasti-kṛ́t ǀ bráhmaṇe ǀ naḥ ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ jáne ǀ janaya ǀ viśva-vāre ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mother of Gods, Aditi's form of glory, ensign of sacrifice, shine forth exalted. Rise up, bestowing praise on our devotion all-bounteous, make us chief among the people.
verses.wilson_translation: Mother of the gods, rival of Aditi, illuminator of the sacrificer, mighty Uṣās, shine forth; approving of our prayer, dawn upon us. Do you, who are cherished by all, make us eminent among the people.
verses.griffith_verse: Mother of Gods, Aditi's form of glory, ensign of sacrifice, shine forth exalted. Rise up, bestowing praise on our devotion all-bounteous, make us chief among the people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यच्चित्रमप्न उषसो वहंतीजानाय शशमानाय भद्रं ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ citrám ǀ ápnaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ váhanti ǀ ījānā́ya ǀ śaśamānā́ya ǀ bhadrám ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever splendid wealth the Dawns bring with them to bless the man who offers praise and worship, Even that may Mitra, Varuṇa vouchsafe us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever valuable wealth the Uṣās convey is beneficial to the sacrificer and to the praiser. May Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth, and heaven, be favourable to this our prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: Whatever splendid wealth the Dawns bring with them to bless the man who offers praise and worship, Even that may Mitra, Varuṇa vouchsafe us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXIV. Rudra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes with the braided hair,That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed. Be gracious unto us, O Rudra, bring us joy: thee, Lord of Heroes, thee with reverence will we serve.Whatever health and strength our father Manu won by sacrifice may we, under thy guidance, gain. By worship of the Gods may we, O Bounteous One, O Rudra, gain thy grace, Ruler of valiant men.Come to our families, bringing them bliss: may we, whose heroes are uninjured, bring thee sacred gifts, Hither we call for aid the wise, the wanderer, impetuous Rudra, perfecter of sacrifice.May he repel from us the anger of the Gods: verily we desire his favourable grace. Him with the braided hair we call with reverence down, the wild-boar of the sky, the red, the dazzling shape.May he, his hand filled full of sovran medicines, grant us protection, shelter, and a home secure. To him the Maruts’ Father is this hymn addressed, to strengthen Rudra's might, a song more sweet than sweet.Grant us, Immortal One, the food which mortals eat: be gracious unto me, my seed, my progeny. O Rudra, harm not either great or small of us, harm not the growing boy, harm not the full-grown man.Slay not a sire among us, slay no mother here, and to our own dear bodies, Rudra, do not harm. Harm us not, Rudra, in our seed and progeny, harm us not in the living, nor in cows or steeds,Slay not our heroes in the fury of thy wrath. Bringing oblations evermore we call to thee. Even as a herdsman I have brought thee hymns of praise: O Father of the Maruts, give us happiness,Blessed is thy most favouring benevolence, so, verily, do we desire thy saving help. Far be thy dart that killeth men or cattle: thy bliss be with us, O thou Lord of Heroes.Be gracious unto us, O God, and bless us, and then vouchsafe us doubly-strong protection. We, seeking help, have spoken and adored him: may Rudra, girt by Maruts, hear our calling.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: इमा रुद्राय तवसे कपर्दिने क्षयद्वीराय प्र भरामहे मतीः ।यथा शमसद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे विश्वं पुष्टं ग्रामे अस्मिन्ननातुरं ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ taváse ǀ kapardíne ǀ kṣayát-vīrāya ǀ prá ǀ bharāmahe ǀ matī́ḥ ǀyáthā ǀ śám ǀ ásat ǀ dvi-páde ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǀ víśvam ǀ puṣṭám ǀ grā́me ǀ asmín ǀ anāturám ǁ
verses.english_translation: To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes with the braided hair, That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer these praises to the mighty Rudra, with the braided hair, the destroyer of heroes, in order that health may be enjoyed by bipeds and quadrupeds, and that all being sin this villag may be (well) nourished and exempt from disease.
verses.griffith_verse: To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes with the braided hair, That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मृळा नो रुद्रोत नो मयस्कृधि क्षयद्वीराय नमसा विधेम ते ।यच्छं च योश्च मनुरायेजे पिता तदश्याम तव रुद्र प्रणीतिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: mṛḷá ǀ naḥ ǀ rudra ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ máyaḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ kṣayát-vīrāya ǀ námasā ǀ vidhema ǀ te ǀyát ǀ śám ǀ ca ǀ yóḥ ǀ ca ǀ mánuḥ ǀ ā-yejé ǀ pitā́ ǀ tát ǀ aśyāma ǀ táva ǀ rudra ǀ prá-nītiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be gracious unto us, O Rudra, bring us joy: thee, Lord of Heroes, thee with reverence will we serve. Whatever health and strength our father Manu won by sacrifice may we, under thy guidance, gain.
verses.wilson_translation: Be gracious to us,Rudra; grant us happiness, for we worship the destroyer of heroes with oblations; and, by your directions, Rudra, may we obtain that freedom from disease and exemption from dangers which our progenitor,Manu, bestowed upon us, (having obtained them form the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Be gracious unto us, O Rudra, bring us joy: thee, Lord of Heroes, thee with reverence will we serve. Whatever health and strength our father Manu won by sacrifice may we, under thy guidance, gain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्याम ते सुमतिं देवयज्यया क्षयद्वीरस्य तव रुद्र मीढ्वः ।सुम्नायन्निद्विशो अस्माकमा चरारिष्टवीरा जुहवाम ते हविः ॥
verses.transliteration: aśyā́ma ǀ te ǀ su-matím ǀ deva-yajyáyā ǀ kṣayát-vīrasya ǀ táva ǀ rudra ǀ mīḍhvaḥ ǀsumna-yán ǀ ít ǀ víśaḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ ā́ ǀ cara ǀ áriṣṭa-vīrāḥ ǀ juhavāma ǀ te ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By worship of the Gods may we, O Bounteous One, O Rudra, gain thy grace, Ruler of valiant men. Come to our families, bringing them bliss: may we, whose heroes are uninjured, bring thee sacred gifts,
verses.wilson_translation: Rudra, showerer (of benefits), may we obtain, through our worship of the gods, the favour of you, who are the destroyer of heroes;come to our posterity, purposing to promote their happiness, while we, having our sons in safety, offer you oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: By worship of the Gods may we, O Bounteous One, O Rudra, gain thy grace, Ruler of valiant men. Come to our families, bringing them bliss: may we, whose heroes are uninjured, bring thee sacred gifts,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वेषं वयं रुद्रं यज्ञसाधं वंकुं कविमवसे नि ह्वयामहे ।आरे अस्मद्दैव्यं हेळो अस्यतु सुमतिमिद्वयमस्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tveṣám ǀ vayám ǀ rudrám ǀ yajña-sā́dham ǀ vaṅkúm ǀ kavím ǀ ávase ǀ ní ǀ hvayāmahe ǀāré ǀ asmát ǀ dáivyam ǀ héḷaḥ ǀ asyatu ǀ su-matím ǀ ít ǀ vayám ǀ asya ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither we call for aid the wise, the wanderer, impetuous Rudra, perfecter of sacrifice. May he repel from us the anger of the Gods: verily we desire his favourable grace.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for our preservation the illustrious Rudra, the accomplisher of sacrifices, the tortuous, the wise; may he remove far from us his celestial wrath, for we earnestly solicit his favour.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither we call for aid the wise, the wanderer, impetuous Rudra, perfecter of sacrifice. May he repel from us the anger of the Gods: verily we desire his favourable grace.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवो वराहमरुषं कपर्दिनं त्वेषं रूपं नमसा नि ह्वयामहे ।हस्ते बिभ्रद्भेषजा वार्याणि शर्म वर्म च्छर्दिरस्मभ्यं यंसत् ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ varāhám ǀ aruṣám ǀ kapardínam ǀ tveṣám ǀ rūpám ǀ námasā ǀ ní ǀ hvayāmahe ǀháste ǀ bíbhrat ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀ śárma ǀ várma ǀ chardíḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ yaṃsat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him with the braided hair we call with reverence down, the wild-boar of the sky, the red, the dazzling shape. May he, his hand filled full of sovran medicines, grant us protection, shelter, and a home secure.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke, from heaven, with reverence, him who has excellent food, who is radiant, and has braided hair, who is brilliant, and is to be ascertained (by sacred study), holding in hishandsexcellent medicaments; mayhe grant us health, defensive armour, and a (secure) dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: Him with the braided hair we call with reverence down, the wild-boar of the sky, the red, the dazzling shape. May he, his hand filled full of sovran medicines, grant us protection, shelter, and a home secure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः स्वादोः स्वादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनं ।रास्वा च नो अमृत मर्तभोजनं त्मने तोकाय तनयाय मृळ ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ pitré ǀ marútām ǀ ucyate ǀ vácaḥ ǀ svādóḥ ǀ svā́dīyaḥ ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ várdhanam ǀrā́sva ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ amṛta ǀ marta-bhójanam ǀ tmáne ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ mṛḷa ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the Maruts’ Father is this hymn addressed, to strengthen Rudra's might, a song more sweet than sweet. Grant us, Immortal One, the food which mortals eat: be gracious unto me, my seed, my progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise, the sweetest of the sweet, and cause of increase (to the reciter), is addressed to Rudra, the father of the Maruts; immortal Rudra, grant us food sufficient for mortals, and bestow happiness on me, my son, and my grandson.
verses.griffith_verse: To him the Maruts’ Father is this hymn addressed, to strengthen Rudra's might, a song more sweet than sweet. Grant us, Immortal One, the food which mortals eat: be gracious unto me, my seed, my progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो महांतमुत मा नो अर्भकं मा न उक्षंतमुत मा न उक्षितं ।मा नो वधीः पितरं मोत मातरं मा नः प्रियास्तन्वो रुद्र रीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́ntam ǀ utá ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ arbhakám ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ úkṣantam ǀ utá ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ukṣitám ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ mā́ ǀ utá ǀ mātáram ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ rudra ǀ ririṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Rudra, harm not either great or small of us, harm not the growing boy, harm not the full-grown man. Slay not a sire among us, slay no mother here, and to our own dear bodies, Rudra, do not harm.
verses.wilson_translation: Injure not,Rudra, those amongst us who are old or young, who are capable of begetting, or who are begotten, nor a father, nor a mother, nor afflict our precious person ns.
verses.griffith_verse: O Rudra, harm not either great or small of us, harm not the growing boy, harm not the full-grown man. Slay not a sire among us, slay no mother here, and to our own dear bodies, Rudra, do not harm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयौ मा नो गोषु मा नो अश्वेषु रीरिषः ।वीरान्मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मंतः सदमित्त्वा हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ toké ǀ tánaye ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ āyáu ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ áśveṣu ǀ ririṣaḥ ǀvīrā́n ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rudra ǀ bhāmitáḥ ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ tvā ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harm us not, Rudra, in our seed and progeny, harm us not in the living, nor in cows or steeds, Slay not our heroes in the fury of thy wrath. Bringing oblations evermore we call to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Harm us not,Rudra, in our sons or grandsons, or othermaledescendants, nor in our cattle, nor in our horses; inflamed with anger, kill not our valiant men, for we, presenting clarified butter perpetually invoke you.
verses.griffith_verse: Harm us not, Rudra, in our seed and progeny, harm us not in the living, nor in cows or steeds, Slay not our heroes in the fury of thy wrath. Bringing oblations evermore we call to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप ते स्तोमान्पशुपा इवाकरं रास्वा पितर्मरुतां सुम्नमस्मे ।भद्रा हि ते सुमतिर्मृळयत्तमाथा वयमव इत्ते वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ te ǀ stómān ǀ paśupā́ḥ-iva ǀ ā́ ǀ akaram ǀ rā́sva ǀ pitaḥ ǀ marutām ǀ sumnám ǀ asmé íti ǀbhadrā́ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ mṛḷayát-tamā ǀ átha ǀ vayám ǀ ávaḥ ǀ ít ǀ te ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as a herdsman I have brought thee hymns of praise: O Father of the Maruts, give us happiness, Blessed is thy most favouring benevolence, so, verily, do we desire thy saving help.
verses.wilson_translation: I restore to you the praises (derived from you), as a shepherd (returns his sheep to their owner); father of the Maruts, bestow happiness upon me; your auspicious benignityis the cause of successive delight, therefore we especially solicit your protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Even as a herdsman I have brought thee hymns of praise: O Father of the Maruts, give us happiness, Blessed is thy most favouring benevolence, so, verily, do we desire thy saving help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आरे ते गोघ्नमुत पूरुषघ्नं क्षयद्वीर सुम्नमस्मे ते अस्तु ।मृळा च नो अधि च ब्रूहि देवाधा च नः शर्म यच्छ द्विबर्हाः ॥
verses.transliteration: āré ǀ te ǀ go-ghnám ǀ utá ǀ puruṣa-ghnám ǀ kṣáyat-vīra ǀ sumnám ǀ asmé íti ǀ te ǀ astu ǀmṛḷá ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ca ǀ brūhi ǀ deva ǀ ádha ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaccha ǀ dvi-bárhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far be thy dart that killeth men or cattle: thy bliss be with us, O thou Lord of Heroes. Be gracious unto us, O God, and bless us, and then vouchsafe us doubly-strong protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyer of heroes, may your cow-killing or man-slaying (weapon) be far away, and let the felicity granted by you be ours; favour us; speak, brilliant hero, in our behalf, and grant us, you who are mighty over the two (realms of heaven and earth), prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: Far be thy dart that killeth men or cattle: thy bliss be with us, O thou Lord of Heroes. Be gracious unto us, O God, and bless us, and then vouchsafe us doubly-strong protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवोचाम नमो अस्मा अवस्यवः शृणोतु नो हवं रुद्रो मरुत्वान् ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: ávocāma ǀ námaḥ ǀ asmai ǀ avasyávaḥ ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀ hávam ǀ rudráḥ ǀ marútvān ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We, seeking help, have spoken and adored him: may Rudra, girt by Maruts, hear our calling. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of protection, we have said: reverence be to him; may Rudra, with the Maruts, hear our invocation; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, be favourable to this (our prayer).
verses.griffith_verse: We, seeking help, have spoken and adored him: may Rudra, girt by Maruts, hear our calling. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXV. Sūrya.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni.The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven. Like as a young man followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess:Where pious men extend their generations, before the Auspicious One for happy fortune. Auspicious are the Sun's Bay-coloured Horses, bright, changing hues, meet for our shouts of triumph.Bearing our prayers, the sky's ridge have they mounted, and in a moment speed round earth and heaven. This is the Godhead, this might of Sūrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished.When he hath loosed his Horses from their station, straight over all Night spreadeth out her garment. In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuṇa and Mitra may behold it.His Bay Steeds well maintain his power eternal, at one time bright and darksome at another. This day, O Gods, while Sūrya is ascending, deliver us from trouble and dishonour.This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.

verses.sanskrit: चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः ।आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: citrám ǀ devā́nām ǀ út ǀ agāt ǀ ánīkam ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ agnéḥ ǀā́ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ antárikṣam ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ātmā́ ǀ jágataḥ ǀ tasthúṣaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Thewonderful hostof rays has risen; th eye of Mitra,Varuṇaand Agni; the sun, thesoulof all that moves or is immoveable, has filled (with his glory) the heaven, the earth, and the firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: THE brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूर्यो देवीमुषसं रोचमानां मर्यो न योषामभ्येति पश्चात् ।यत्रा नरो देवयंतो युगानि वितन्वते प्रति भद्राय भद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: sū́ryaḥ ǀ devī́m ǀ uṣásam ǀ rócamānām ǀ máryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóṣām ǀ abhí ǀ eti ǀ paścā́t ǀyátra ǀ náraḥ ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ yugā́ni ǀ vi-tanvaté ǀ práti ǀ bhadrā́ya ǀ bhadrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like as a young man followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess: Where pious men extend their generations, before the Auspicious One for happy fortune.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun follows the divine and brilliant Uṣā, as a man (follows a young and elegant) woman; at which season, pious men perform (the ceremonies established for) ages, worshipping the auspicious (sun), for the sake of good (reward).
verses.griffith_verse: Like as a young man followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess: Where pious men extend their generations, before the Auspicious One for happy fortune.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रा अश्वा हरितः सूर्यस्य चित्रा एतग्वा अनुमाद्यासः ।नमस्यंतो दिव आ पृष्ठमस्थुः परि द्यावापृथिवी यंति सद्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrā́ḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ harítaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ éta-gvāḥ ǀ anu-mā́dyāsaḥ ǀnamasyántaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛṣṭhám ǀ asthuḥ ǀ pári ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ yanti ǀ sadyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious are the Sun's Bay-coloured Horses, bright, changing hues, meet for our shouts of triumph. Bearing our prayers, the sky's ridge have they mounted, and in a moment speed round earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The auspicious, swift horses of the sun, well-limbed, road-traversing, who merit to be plural ased with praise, revernced byus, have ascended to the summit of the sky, and quickly circumambulate earth and heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Auspicious are the Sun's Bay-coloured Horses, bright, changing hues, meet for our shouts of triumph. Bearing our prayers, the sky's ridge have they mounted, and in a moment speed round earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तत्सूर्यस्य देवत्वं तन्महित्वं मध्या कर्तोर्विततं सं जभार ।यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ deva-tvám ǀ tát ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ madhyā́ ǀ kártoḥ ǀ ví-tatam ǀ sám ǀ jabhāra ǀyadā́ ǀ ít ǀ áyukta ǀ harítaḥ ǀ sadhá-sthāt ǀ ā́t ǀ rā́trī ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ tanute ǀ simásmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the Godhead, this might of Sūrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished. When he hath loosed his Horses from their station, straight over all Night spreadeth out her garment.
verses.wilson_translation: Such is the divinity, such is the majesty of the sun, that when he has set, he has withdrawn (into himself) the diffused (light which had been shed) upon the unfinished task; when he has unyoked his coursers from his car, then night extends the veiling darkness over all.
verses.griffith_verse: This is the Godhead, this might of Sūrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished. When he hath loosed his Horses from their station, straight over all Night spreadeth out her garment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याभिचक्षे सूर्यो रूपं कृणुते द्योरुपस्थे ।अनंतमन्यद्रुशदस्य पाजः कृष्णमन्यद्धरितः सं भरंति ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ abhi-cákṣe ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ rūpám ǀ kṛṇute ǀ dyóḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀanantám ǀ anyát ǀ rúśat ǀ asya ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ kṛṣṇám ǀ anyát ǀ harítaḥ ǀ sám ǀ bharanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuṇa and Mitra may behold it. His Bay Steeds well maintain his power eternal, at one time bright and darksome at another.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun, is the sight of Mitraand Varuṇa, displays his form (of brightness) in the middle of the heavens, and his rays extend, on onehand, his infinite and brilliant power, or, on the other, (by their departure), bring on the blackness of night.
verses.griffith_verse: In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuṇa and Mitra may behold it. His Bay Steeds well maintain his power eternal, at one time bright and darksome at another.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्या देवा उदिता सूर्यस्य निरंहसः पिपृता निरवद्यात् ।तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहंतामदितिः सिंधुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: adyá ǀ devāḥ ǀ út-itā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ níḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ pipṛtá ǀ níḥ ǀ avadyā́t ǀtát ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahantām ǀ áditiḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This day, O Gods, while Sūrya is ascending, deliver us from trouble and dishonour. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: This day, gods, with the rising of the sun, deliver us from heinous sin; and may Mitra,Varuṇa,Aditi--ocean, earth and heaven, be favourable to this (our prayer).
verses.griffith_verse: This day, O Gods, while Sūrya is ascending, deliver us from trouble and dishonour. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXVI. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I TRIM like grass my song for the Nāsatyas and send their lauds forth as the wind drives rain-clouds,Who, in a chariot rapid as an arrow, brought to the youthful Vimada a consort. Borne on by rapid steeds of mighty pinion, or proudly trusting in the Gods’ incitements.That stallion ass of yours won, O Nāsatyas, that thousand in the race, in Yama's contest. Yea, Aśvins, as a dead man leaves his riches, Tugra left Bhujyu in the cloud of waters.Ye brought him back in animated vessels, traversing air, unwetted by the billows. Bhujyu ye bore with winged things, Nāsatyas, which for three nights, three days full swiftly travelled,To the sea's farther shore, the strand of ocean, in three cars, hundred-footed, with six horses. Ye wrought that hero exploit in the ocean which giveth no support, or hold or station,What time ye carried Bhujyu to his dwelling, borne in a ship with hundred oars, O Aśvins. The white horse which of old ye gave Aghāśva, Aśvins, a gift to be his wealth for ever,—Still to be praised is that your glorious present, still to be famed is the brave horse of Pedu. O Heroes, ye gave wisdom to Kakṣīvān who sprang from Pajra's line, who sang your praises.Ye poured forth from the hoof of your strong charger a hundred jars of wine as from a strainer. Ye warded off with cold the fire's fierce burning; food very rich in nourishment ye furnished.Atri, cast downward in the cavern, Aśvins ye brought, with all his people, forth to comfort. Ye lifted up the well, O ye Nāsatyas, and set the base on high to open downward.Streams flowed for folk of Gotama who thirsted, like rain to bring forth thousandfold abundance. Ye from the old Cyavāna, O Nāsatyas, stripped, as ’twere mail, the skin uponhis body,Lengthened his life when all had left him helpless, Dasras! and made him lord of youthful maidens. Worthy of praise and worth the winning, Heroes, is that your favouring succour O Nāsatyas,What time ye, knowing well his case, delivered Vandana from the pit like hidden treasure. That mighty deed of yours, for gain, O Heroes, as thunder heraldeth the rain, I publish,When, by the horse's head, Atharvan's offspring Dadhyac made known to you the Soma's sweetness. In the great rite the wise dame called, Nāsatyas, you, Lords of many treasures, to assist her.Ye heard the weakling's wife, as ’twere an order, and gave to her a son Hiraṇyahasta. Ye from the wolf's jaws, as ye stood together, set free the quail, O Heroes, O Nāsatyas.Ye, Lords of many treasures, gave the poet his perfect vision as he mourned his trouble. When in the time of night, in Khela's battle, a leg was severed like a wild bird's pinion,Straight ye gave Viśpalā a leg of iron that she might move what time the conflict opened. His father robbed Ṛjrāśva of his eyesight who for the she-wolf slew a hundred wethers.Ye gave him eyes, Nāsatyas, Wonder-Workers, Physicians, that he saw with sight uninjured. The Daughter of the Sun your car ascended, first reaching as it were the goal with coursers.All Deities within their hearts assented, and ye, Nāsatyas, are close linked with glory. When to his house ye came, to Divodāsa, hasting to Bharadvāja, O ye Aśvins,The car that came with you brought splendid riches: a porpoise and a bull were yoked together. Ye, bringing wealth with rule, and life with offspring, life rich in noble heroes; O Nāsatyas,Accordant came with strength to Jahnu's children who offered you thrice every day your portion. Ye bore away at night by easy pathways Jāhuṣa compassed round on every quarter,And, with your car that cleaves the toe asunder, Nāsatyas never decaying! rent the mountains. One morn ye strengthened Vaśa for the battle, to gather spoils that might be told in thousands.With Indra joined ye drove away misfortunes, yea foes of Pṛthuśravas, O ye mighty. From the deep well ye raised on high the water, so that Ṛcatka's son, Sara, should drink it;And with your might, to help the weary Śayu, ye made the barren cow yield milk, Nāsatyas. To Viśvaka, Nāsatyas! son of Kṛṣṇa, the righteous man who sought your aid and praised you,Ye with your powers restored, like some lost creature, his son Viṣṇāpū for his eyes to look on. Aśvins, ye raised, like Soma in a ladle Rebha, who for ten days and ten nights, fettered.Had lain in cruel bonds, immersed and wounded, suffering sore affliction, in the waters. have declared your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins: may this be mine, and many kine and heroes.May I, enjoying lengthened life, still seeing, enter old age as ’twere the house I live in.

verses.sanskrit: नासत्याभ्यां बर्हिरिव प्र वृंजे स्तोमाँ इयर्म्यभ्रियेव वातः ।यावर्भगाय विमदाय जायां सेनाजुवा न्यूहतू रथेन ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́satyābhyām ǀ barhíḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ vṛñje ǀ stómān ǀ iyarmi ǀ abhríyā-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀyáu ǀ árbhagāya ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ jāyā́m ǀ senā-júvā ǀ ni-ūhátuḥ ǀ ráthena ǁ
verses.english_translation: I TRIM like grass my song for the Nāsatyas and send their lauds forth as the wind drives rain-clouds, Who, in a chariot rapid as an arrow, brought to the youthful Vimada a consort.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as a worshipper strews the sacred grass for the Nāsatyas, so do I urge on their laudations, as the wind drives on the clouds; they, who gave a bride to the youthful Vimada, and bore her away in their car, outstripping the rival host.
verses.griffith_verse: I TRIM like grass my song for the Nāsatyas and send their lauds forth as the wind drives rain-clouds, Who, in a chariot rapid as an arrow, brought to the youthful Vimada a consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वीळुपत्मभिराशुहेमभिर्वा देवानां वा जूतिभिः शाशदाना ।तद्रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय ॥
verses.transliteration: vīḷupátma-bhiḥ ǀ āśuhéma-bhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ devā́nām ǀ vā ǀ jūtí-bhiḥ ǀ śā́śadānā ǀtát ǀ rā́sabhaḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ sahásram ǀ ājā́ ǀ yamásya ǀ pra-dháne ǀ jigāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Borne on by rapid steeds of mighty pinion, or proudly trusting in the Gods’ incitements. That stallion ass of yours won, O Nāsatyas, that thousand in the race, in Yama's contest.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas,borne by strong and rapid (steeds), and (urged) by the encouragements of the gods, the ass of you, thus instrumental gated, overcame a thousand (enemies) in conflict, in the war grateful to Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: Borne on by rapid steeds of mighty pinion, or proudly trusting in the Gods’ incitements. That stallion ass of yours won, O Nāsatyas, that thousand in the race, in Yama's contest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तुग्रो ह भुज्युमश्विनोदमेघे रयिं न कश्चिन्ममृवाँ अवाहाः ।तमूहथुर्नौभिरात्मन्वतीभिरंतरिक्षप्रुद्भिरपोदकाभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: túgraḥ ǀ ha ǀ bhujyúm ǀ aśvinā ǀ uda-meghé ǀ rayím ǀ ná ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ mamṛ-vā́n ǀ áva ǀ ahāḥ ǀtám ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ naubhíḥ ǀ ātman-vátībhiḥ ǀ antarikṣaprút-bhiḥ ǀ ápa-udakābhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, Aśvins, as a dead man leaves his riches, Tugra left Bhujyu in the cloud of waters. Ye brought him back in animated vessels, traversing air, unwetted by the billows.
verses.wilson_translation: Tugra, verily,Aśvins, sent (his son)Bhujyuto sea, as a dying man parts with his riches; but you brought him back in vessels of your own, floating over the ocean, and keeping out the waters.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, Aśvins, as a dead man leaves his riches, Tugra left Bhujyu in the cloud of waters. Ye brought him back in animated vessels, traversing air, unwetted by the billows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रः क्षपस्त्रिरहातिव्रजद्भिर्नासत्या भुज्युमूहथुः पतंगैः ।समुद्रस्य धन्वन्नार्द्रस्य पारे त्रिभी रथैः शतपद्भिः षळश्वैः ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ kṣápaḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ áhā ǀ ativrájat-bhiḥ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ bhujyúm ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ pataṅgáiḥ ǀsamudrásya ǀ dhánvan ǀ ārdrásya ǀ pāré ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ráthaiḥ ǀ śatápat-bhiḥ ǀ ṣáṭ-aśvaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bhujyu ye bore with winged things, Nāsatyas, which for three nights, three days full swiftly travelled, To the sea's farther shore, the strand of ocean, in three cars, hundred-footed, with six horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Threenights, and three days,Nāsatyas, have you conveyed Bhujyuin three rapid, revolving cars, having a hundred wheels, and drawn by six horses, along the dry bed of the ocean to the short of the sea.
verses.griffith_verse: Bhujyu ye bore with winged things, Nāsatyas, which for three nights, three days full swiftly travelled, To the sea's farther shore, the strand of ocean, in three cars, hundred-footed, with six horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनारंभणे तदवीरयेथामनास्थाने अग्रभणे समुद्रे ।यदश्विना ऊहथुर्भुज्युमस्तं शतारित्रां नावमातस्थिवांसं ॥
verses.transliteration: anārambhaṇé ǀ tát ǀ avīrayethām ǀ anāsthāné ǀ agrabhaṇé ǀ samudré ǀyát ǀ aśvinau ǀ ūháthuḥ ǀ bhujyúm ǀ ástam ǀ śatá-aritrān ǀ nā́vam ǀ ātasthi-vā́ṃsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye wrought that hero exploit in the ocean which giveth no support, or hold or station, What time ye carried Bhujyu to his dwelling, borne in a ship with hundred oars, O Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: this exploit you achieved,Aśvins, in the ocean, where there is nothing to give support, nothing to rest upon,nothing to cling to, that you brought Bhujyu, sailing in a hundred-oared ship, to his father's house.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye wrought that hero exploit in the ocean which giveth no support, or hold or station, What time ye carried Bhujyu to his dwelling, borne in a ship with hundred oars, O Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमश्विना ददथुः श्वेतमश्वमघाश्वाय शश्वदित्स्वस्ति ।तद्वां दात्रं महि कीर्तेन्यं भूत्पैद्वो वाजी सदमिद्धव्यो अर्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ aśvinā ǀ dadáthuḥ ǀ śvetám ǀ áśvam ǀ aghá-aśvāya ǀ śáśvat ǀ ít ǀ svastí ǀtát ǀ vām ǀ dātrám ǀ máhi ǀ kīrtényam ǀ bhūt ǀ paidváḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The white horse which of old ye gave Aghāśva, Aśvins, a gift to be his wealth for ever,— Still to be praised is that your glorious present, still to be famed is the brave horse of Pedu.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, the white horse you gave to Pedu, whose horses were indestrucible, was ever to him success; that, your precious gift, is always to be celebrated; the horse of Pedu, the scatterer (of enemies), is always to be invoked.
verses.griffith_verse: The white horse which of old ye gave Aghāśva, Aśvins, a gift to be his wealth for ever,— Still to be praised is that your glorious present, still to be famed is the brave horse of Pedu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं नरा स्तुवते पज्रियाय कक्षीवते अरदतं पुरंधिं ।कारोतराच्छफादश्वस्य वृष्णः शतं कुंभाँ असिंचतं सुरायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ narā ǀ stuvaté ǀ pajriyā́ya ǀ kakṣī́vate ǀ aradatam ǀ púram-dhim ǀkārotarā́t ǀ śaphā́t ǀ áśvasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ śatám ǀ kumbhā́n ǀ asiñcatam ǀ súrāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Heroes, ye gave wisdom to Kakṣīvān who sprang from Pajra's line, who sang your praises. Ye poured forth from the hoof of your strong charger a hundred jars of wine as from a strainer.
verses.wilson_translation: You gave, leaders (of sacrifice), to Kakṣīvat, of the race of Pajra, various knowledge; you filled from the hoof of your vigorous steed, as if from a cask, a hundred jars of wine.
verses.griffith_verse: O Heroes, ye gave wisdom to Kakṣīvān who sprang from Pajra's line, who sang your praises. Ye poured forth from the hoof of your strong charger a hundred jars of wine as from a strainer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिमेनाग्निं घ्रंसमवारयेथां पितुमतीमूर्जमस्मा अधत्तं ।ऋबीसे अत्रिमश्विनावनीतमुन्निन्यथुः सर्वगणं स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: hiména ǀ agním ǀ ghraṃsám ǀ avārayethām ǀ pitu-mátīm ǀ ū́rjam ǀ asmai ǀ adhattam ǀṛbī́se ǀ átrim ǀ aśvinā ǀ áva-nītam ǀ út ǀ ninyathuḥ ǀ sárva-gaṇam ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye warded off with cold the fire's fierce burning; food very rich in nourishment ye furnished. Atri, cast downward in the cavern, Aśvins ye brought, with all his people, forth to comfort.
verses.wilson_translation: You quenched with cold (water) the blazing flames (that encompassed Atri), and supplied him with food-supported strength; you extricated him,Aśvins, from the dark (cavern) into which he had been thrown headlong and restored him to every kind of welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye warded off with cold the fire's fierce burning; food very rich in nourishment ye furnished. Atri, cast downward in the cavern, Aśvins ye brought, with all his people, forth to comfort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परावतं नासत्यानुदेथामुच्चाबुध्नं चक्रथुर्जिह्मबारं ।क्षरन्नापो न पायनाय राये सहस्राय तृष्यते गोतमस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ avatám ǀ nāsatyā ǀ anudethām ǀ uccā́-budhnam ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ jihmá-bāram ǀkṣáran ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ pāyánāya ǀ rāyé ǀ sahásrāya ǀ tṛ́ṣyate ǀ gótamasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye lifted up the well, O ye Nāsatyas, and set the base on high to open downward. Streams flowed for folk of Gotama who thirsted, like rain to bring forth thousandfold abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, you raised up the well, and made th ebase, which had been turned upwards, the curved mouth, so that the water issued for the beverage of the thirsty Gotama, the offerer.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye lifted up the well, O ye Nāsatyas, and set the base on high to open downward. Streams flowed for folk of Gotama who thirsted, like rain to bring forth thousandfold abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वव्रिं प्रामुंचतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् ।प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: jujurúṣaḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ utá ǀ vavrím ǀ prá ǀ amuñcatam ǀ drāpím-iva ǀ cyávānāt ǀprá ǀ atiratam ǀ jahitásya ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ dasrā ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ pátim ǀ akṛṇutam ǀ kanī́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye from the old Cyavāna, O Nāsatyas, stripped, as ’twere mail, the skin upon his body, Lengthened his life when all had left him helpless, Dasras! and made him lord of youthful maidens.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, you stripped off from the aged Cyavanahis entire skin, as if it had been a coat of mail; you reversed,Dasras, the life of the sage who was without kindred, and constituted him the husband of many maidens.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye from the old Cyavāna, O Nāsatyas, stripped, as ’twere mail, the skin upon his body, Lengthened his life when all had left him helpless, Dasras! and made him lord of youthful maidens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वां नरा शंस्यं राध्यं चाभिष्टिमन्नासत्या वरूथं ।यद्विद्वांसा निधिमिवापगूळ्हमुद्दर्शतादूपथुर्वंदनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ śáṃsyam ǀ rā́dhyam ǀ ca ǀ abhiṣṭi-mát ǀ nāsatyā ǀ várūtham ǀyát ǀ vidvā́ṃsā ǀ nidhím-iva ǀ ápa-gūḷham ǀ út ǀ darśatā́t ǀ ūpáthuḥ ǀ vándanāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worthy of praise and worth the winning, Heroes, is that your favouring succour O Nāsatyas, What time ye, knowing well his case, delivered Vandana from the pit like hidden treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, leaders, glorious was that exploit of yours, one to be celebrated, to be adored, to be desired by us, when, becoming aware (of the circumstance), you extricated Vandanā, (hidden), like a concealed treasure, from the (well) that was visible (to travellers).
verses.griffith_verse: Worthy of praise and worth the winning, Heroes, is that your favouring succour O Nāsatyas, What time ye, knowing well his case, delivered Vandana from the pit like hidden treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वां नरा सनये दंस उग्रमाविष्कृणोमि तन्यतुर्न वृष्टिं ।दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ sanáye ǀ dáṃsaḥ ǀ ugrám ǀ āvíḥ ǀ kṛṇomi ǀ tanyatúḥ ǀ ná ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀdadhyáṅ ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ mádhu ǀ ātharvaṇáḥ ǀ vām ǀ áśvasya ǀ śīrṣṇā́ ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ uvā́ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: That mighty deed of yours, for gain, O Heroes, as thunder heraldeth the rain, I publish, When, by the horse's head, Atharvan's offspring Dadhyac made known to you the Soma's sweetness.
verses.wilson_translation: I proclaim, leadeers (of sacriifce), for the skae of acquiring wealth, that inimitable deed which you performed, as the thunder (announces) rain, when provided by you with the head of a horse. Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, taught you the mystic science.
verses.griffith_verse: That mighty deed of yours, for gain, O Heroes, as thunder heraldeth the rain, I publish, When, by the horse's head, Atharvan's offspring Dadhyac made known to you the Soma's sweetness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजोहवीन्नासत्या करा वां महे यामन्पुरुभुजा पुरंधिः ।श्रुतं तच्छासुरिव वध्रिमत्या हिरण्यहस्तमश्विनावदत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: ájohavīt ǀ nāsatyā ǀ karā́ ǀ vām ǀ mahé ǀ yā́man ǀ puru-bhujā ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀśrutám ǀ tát ǀ śā́suḥ-iva ǀ vadhri-matyā́ḥ ǀ híraṇya-hastam ǀ aśvinau ǀ adattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the great rite the wise dame called, Nāsatyas, you, Lords of many treasures, to assist her. Ye heard the weakling's wife, as ’twere an order, and gave to her a son Hiraṇyahasta.
verses.wilson_translation: The intelligent (Vadhrimati) invoked you.Nāsatyas, who are the accom;ishers (of desires) and the protectors of many, with a sacred hymn; her prayer was heard, like (the instrumental uction of) a teacher, and you,Aśvins, gave to the wife of an impotent husband,Hiraṇyahasta, her son.
verses.griffith_verse: In the great rite the wise dame called, Nāsatyas, you, Lords of many treasures, to assist her. Ye heard the weakling's wife, as ’twere an order, and gave to her a son Hiraṇyahasta.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आस्नो वृकस्य वर्तिकामभीके युवं नरा नासत्यामुमुक्तं ।उतो कविं पुरुभुजा युवं ह कृपमाणमकृणुतं विचक्षे ॥
verses.transliteration: āsnáḥ ǀ vṛ́kasya ǀ vártikām ǀ abhī́ke ǀ yuvám ǀ narā ǀ nāsatyā ǀ amumuktam ǀutó íti ǀ kavím ǀ puru-bhujā ǀ yuvám ǀ ha ǀ kṛ́pamāṇam ǀ akṛṇutam ǀ vi-cákṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye from the wolf's jaws, as ye stood together, set free the quail, O Heroes, O Nāsatyas. Ye, Lords of many treasures, gave the poet his perfect vision as he mourned his trouble.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, leaders, you liberated the quail from the mouth of the dog that had seized her, and you, who are the benefactors of many, have granted to the sage who praises you, to behold (true wisdom).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye from the wolf's jaws, as ye stood together, set free the quail, O Heroes, O Nāsatyas. Ye, Lords of many treasures, gave the poet his perfect vision as he mourned his trouble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चरित्रं हि वेरिवाच्छेदि पर्णमाजा खेलस्य परितक्म्यायां ।सद्यो जंघामायसीं विश्पलायै धने हिते सर्तवे प्रत्यधत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: carítram ǀ hí ǀ véḥ-iva ǀ ácchedi ǀ parṇám ǀ ājā́ ǀ khelásya ǀ pári-takmyāyām ǀsadyáḥ ǀ jáṅghām ǀ ā́yasīm ǀ viśpálāyai ǀ dháne ǀ hité ǀ sártave ǀ práti ǀ adhattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When in the time of night, in Khela's battle, a leg was severed like a wild bird's pinion, Straight ye gave Viśpalā a leg of iron that she might move what time the conflict opened.
verses.wilson_translation: The foot of (Vispalā, the wife of) Khela, was cut off, like the wing of a bird, in an engagement by night; immediately you gave her a metallic leg, that she might walk, the hidden treasure (of the enemy being the object of the conflict).
verses.griffith_verse: When in the time of night, in Khela's battle, a leg was severed like a wild bird's pinion, Straight ye gave Viśpalā a leg of iron that she might move what time the conflict opened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं मेषान्वृक्ये चक्षदानमृज्राश्वं तं पितांधं चकार ।तस्मा अक्षी नासत्या विचक्ष आधत्तं दस्रा भिषजावनर्वन् ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ meṣā́n ǀ vṛkyé ǀ cakṣadānám ǀ ṛjrá-aśvam ǀ tám ǀ pitā́ ǀ andhám ǀ cakāra ǀtásmai ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ nāsatyā ǀ vi-cákṣe ǀ ā́ ǀ adhattam ǀ dasrā ǀ bhiṣajau ǀ anarván ǁ
verses.english_translation: His father robbed Ṛjrāśva of his eyesight who for the she-wolf slew a hundred wethers. Ye gave him eyes, Nāsatyas, Wonder-Workers, Physicians, that he saw with sight uninjured.
verses.wilson_translation: When his father caused,Ṛjrāśvā, as he was giving to a she-wolf a hundred sheep cut up in pieces, to become blind, you,Dasras, physicians (of the gods), gave him eyes (that had been) unable to find their way, with which he might see.
verses.griffith_verse: His father robbed Ṛjrāśva of his eyesight who for the she-wolf slew a hundred wethers. Ye gave him eyes, Nāsatyas, Wonder-Workers, Physicians, that he saw with sight uninjured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य कार्ष्मेवातिष्ठदर्वता जयंती ।विश्वे देवा अन्वमन्यंत हृद्भिः समु श्रिया नासत्या सचेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ duhitā́ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ kā́rṣma-iva ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ árvatā ǀ jáyantī ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ amanyanta ǀ hṛt-bhíḥ ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śriyā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Daughter of the Sun your car ascended, first reaching as it were the goal with coursers. All Deities within their hearts assented, and ye, Nāsatyas, are close linked with glory.
verses.wilson_translation: The daughter of the sun ascended your car, (like a runner) to a goal; when you won (the race) with your swift horse, all the gods looked on with (anxious hearts), and you,Nāsatyas, were associated with glory.
verses.griffith_verse: The Daughter of the Sun your car ascended, first reaching as it were the goal with coursers. All Deities within their hearts assented, and ye, Nāsatyas, are close linked with glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदयातं दिवोदासाय वर्तिर्भरद्वाजायाश्विना हयंता ।रेवदुवाह सचनो रथो वां वृषभश्च शिंशुमारश्च युक्ता ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ áyātam ǀ dívaḥ-dāsāya ǀ vartíḥ ǀ bharát-vājāya ǀ aśvinā ǀ háyantā ǀrevát ǀ uvāha ǀ sacanáḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vām ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ca ǀ śiṃśumā́raḥ ǀ ca ǀ yuktā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When to his house ye came, to Divodāsa, hasting to Bharadvāja, O ye Aśvins, The car that came with you brought splendid riches: a porpoise and a bull were yoked together.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Aśvins, being invited, you went to his dwelling (to give due rewards) to Divodāsa, offering oblations, then your helping chariot conveyed (food and) treasure, and the bull and the porpoise were yoked together.
verses.griffith_verse: When to his house ye came, to Divodāsa, hasting to Bharadvāja, O ye Aśvins, The car that came with you brought splendid riches: a porpoise and a bull were yoked together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रयिं सुक्षत्रं स्वपत्यमायुः सुवीर्यं नासत्या वहंता ।आ जह्नावीं समनसोप वाजैस्त्रिरह्नो भागं दधतीमयातं ॥
verses.transliteration: rayím ǀ su-kṣatrám ǀ su-apatyám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ váhantā ǀā́ ǀ jahnā́vīm ǀ sá-manasā ǀ úpa ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ dádhatīm ǀ ayātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, bringing wealth with rule, and life with offspring, life rich in noble heroes; O Nāsatyas, Accordant came with strength to Jahnu's children who offered you thrice every day your portion.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, bearing strength and wealth with posterity and vigour-sustaining food, you came, with one intention, to the family of Jahnu, (provide) with (sacrificial) viands, and possessing a third portion of the daily (offerings).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, bringing wealth with rule, and life with offspring, life rich in noble heroes; O Nāsatyas, Accordant came with strength to Jahnu's children who offered you thrice every day your portion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परिविष्टं जाहुषं विश्वतः सीं सुगेभिर्नक्तमूहथू रजोभिः ।विभिंदुना नासत्या रथेन वि पर्वताँ अजरयू अयातं ॥
verses.transliteration: pári-viṣṭam ǀ jāhuṣám ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ sīm ǀ su-gébhiḥ ǀ náktam ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ rájaḥ-bhiḥ ǀvi-bhindúnā ǀ nāsatyā ǀ ráthena ǀ ví ǀ párvatān ǀ ajarayū́ íti ǀ ayātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye bore away at night by easy pathways Jāhuṣa compassed round on every quarter, And, with your car that cleaves the toe asunder, Nāsatyas never decaying! rent the mountains.
verses.wilson_translation: Undecaying Nāsatyas, you bore away by night, in your foe-overwhelming car,Jāhuṣa, surrounded on every side by (enemies), through practicable roads, and went to (inaccessible) mountains.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye bore away at night by easy pathways Jāhuṣa compassed round on every quarter, And, with your car that cleaves the toe asunder, Nāsatyas never decaying! rent the mountains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एकस्या वस्तोरावतं रणाय वशमश्विना सनये सहस्रा ।निरहतं दुच्छुना इंद्रवंता पृथुश्रवसो वृषणावरातीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ékasyāḥ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ āvatam ǀ ráṇāya ǀ váśam ǀ aśvinā ǀ sanáye ǀ sahásrā ǀníḥ ǀ ahatam ǀ ducchúnāḥ ǀ índra-vantā ǀ pṛthu-śrávasaḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ árātīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: One morn ye strengthened Vaśa for the battle, to gather spoils that might be told in thousands. With Indra joined ye drove away misfortunes, yea foes of Pṛthuśravas, O ye mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: You preserved Vaśa,Aśvins, (that he might obtain) in a single day a thousand acceptable gifts; showerers (of benefits), associated with Indra, you destroyed the malignant enemies of Pṛthuśravas.
verses.griffith_verse: One morn ye strengthened Vaśa for the battle, to gather spoils that might be told in thousands. With Indra joined ye drove away misfortunes, yea foes of Pṛthuśravas, O ye mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शरस्य चिदार्चत्कस्यावतादा नीचादुच्चा चक्रथुः पातवे वाः ।शयवे चिन्नासत्या शचीभिर्जसुरये स्तर्यं पिप्यथुर्गां ॥
verses.transliteration: śarásya ǀ cit ǀ ārcat-kásya ǀ avatā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ nīcā́t ǀ uccā́ ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ pā́tave ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǀśayáve ǀ cit ǀ nāsatyā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ jásuraye ǀ staryám ǀ pipyathuḥ ǀ gā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: From the deep well ye raised on high the water, so that Ṛcatka's son, Sara, should drink it; And with your might, to help the weary Śayu, ye made the barren cow yield milk, Nāsatyas.
verses.wilson_translation: You raised the water from the bottom to the top of the well, for the drinking ofŚara, the son of Ṛcitka, and by your powers,Nāsatyas, you filled, for the sake of the wearyŚayu, the barren cow (with milk).
verses.griffith_verse: From the deep well ye raised on high the water, so that Ṛcatka's son, Sara, should drink it; And with your might, to help the weary Śayu, ye made the barren cow yield milk, Nāsatyas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवस्यते स्तुवते कृष्णियाय ऋजूयते नासत्या शचीभिः ।पशुं न नष्टमिव दर्शनाय विष्णाप्वं ददथुर्विश्वकाय ॥
verses.transliteration: avasyaté ǀ stuvaté ǀ kṛṣṇiyā́ya ǀ ṛju-yaté ǀ nāsatyā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀpaśúm ǀ ná ǀ naṣṭám-iva ǀ dárśanāya ǀ viṣṇāpvám ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ víśvakāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Viśvaka, Nāsatyas! son of Kṛṣṇa, the righteous man who sought your aid and praised you, Ye with your powers restored, like some lost creature, his son Viṣṇāpū for his eyes to look on.
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, by your acts you restored to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, soliciting your protection, adoring you, and a lover of rectitude, hs son Viṣṇāpu, (welcome) to his sight as an animal that has been lost.
verses.griffith_verse: To Viśvaka, Nāsatyas! son of Kṛṣṇa, the righteous man who sought your aid and praised you, Ye with your powers restored, like some lost creature, his son Viṣṇāpū for his eyes to look on.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दश रात्रीरशिवेना नव द्यूनवनद्धं श्नथितमप्स्वंतः ।विप्रुतं रेभमुदनि प्रवृक्तमुन्निन्यथुः सोममिव स्रुवेण ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ rā́trīḥ ǀ áśivena ǀ náva ǀ dyū́n ǀ áva-naddham ǀ śnathitám ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáríti ǀví-prutam ǀ rebhám ǀ udáni ǀ prá-vṛktam ǀ út ǀ ninyathuḥ ǀ sómam-iva ǀ sruvéṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aśvins, ye raised, like Soma in a ladle Rebha, who for ten days and ten nights, fettered. Had lain in cruel bonds, immersed and wounded, suffering sore affliction, in the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, you raised up, like Somain a ladle, Rebha, who for ten nights and nine days, had lain (in a well), bound with tight bonds, wounded, immersed, and suffering distress form the water.
verses.griffith_verse: Aśvins, ye raised, like Soma in a ladle Rebha, who for ten days and ten nights, fettered. Had lain in cruel bonds, immersed and wounded, suffering sore affliction, in the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वां दंसांस्यश्विनाववोचमस्य पतिः स्यां सुगवः सुवीरः ।उत पश्यन्नश्नुवंदीर्घमायुरस्तमिवेज्जरिमाणं जगम्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vām ǀ dáṃsāṃsi ǀ aśvinau ǀ avocam ǀ asyá ǀ pátiḥ ǀ syām ǀ su-gávaḥ ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǀutá ǀ páśyan ǀ aśnuván ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ástam-iva ǀ ít ǀ jarimā́ṇam ǀ jagamyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 have declared your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins: may this be mine, and many kine and heroes. May I, enjoying lengthened life, still seeing, enter old age as ’twere the house I live in.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus,Aśvins, have I declared your exploits; may I become the master (of this plural ce), having abundant cattle and a numerous progeny, and retaining my sight, and enjoying a long life; may I enter into old age, as (a master enters) his house.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 have declared your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins: may this be mine, and many kine and heroes. May I, enjoying lengthened life, still seeing, enter old age as ’twere the house I live in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXVII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AŚVINS, your ancient priest invites you hither to gladden you with draughts of meath of Soma.Our gift is on the grass, our song apportioned: with food and strength come hither, O Nāsatyas. That car of yours, swifter than thought, O Aśvins, which drawn by brave steeds cometh to the people,Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious,—come ye thereon to our abode, O Heroes. Ye freed sage Atri, whom the Five Tribes honoured, from the strait pit, ye Heroes with his people,Baffling the guiles of the malignant Dasyu, repelling them, ye Mighty in succession. Rebha the sage, ye mighty Heroes, Aśvins! whom, like a horse, vile men had sunk in water,—Him, wounded, with your wondrous power ye rescued: your exploits of old time endure for ever. Ye brought forth Vandana, ye Wonder-Workers, for triumph, like fair gold that hath been buried,Like one who slumbered in destruction's bosom, or like the Sun when dwelling in the darkness. Kakṣīvān, Pajra's son, must laud that exploit of yours, Nāsatyas, Heroes, ye who wander!When from the hoof of your strong horse ye showered a hundred jars of honey for the people. To Kṛṣṇa's son, to Viśvaka who praised you, O Heroes, ye restored his son Viṣṇāpū.To Ghoṣā, living in her father's dwelling, stricken in years, ye gave a husband, Aśvins. Ruṣatī, of the mighty people, Aśvins, ye gave to Śyāva of the line of Kaṇva.This deed of yours, ye Strong Ones should be published, that ye gave glory to the son of Nṛṣad. O Aśvins, wearing many forms at pleasure, on Pedu ye bestowed a fleet-foot courser,Strong, winner of a thousand spoils, resistless the serpent slayer, glorious, triumphant. These glorious things are yours, ye Bounteous Givers; prayer, praise in both worlds are your habitation.O Aśvins, when the sons of Pajra call you, send strength with nourishment to him who knoweth. Hymned with the reverence of a son, O Aśvins ye Swift Ones giving booty to the singer,Glorified by Agastya with devotion, established Viśpalā again, Nāsatyas. Ye Sons of Heaven, ye Mighty, whither went ye, sought ye, for his fair praise the home of Kāvya.When, like a pitcher full of gold, O Aśvins, on the tenth day ye lifted up the buried? Ye with the aid of your great powers, O Aśvins, restored to youth the ancient man Cyavāna.The Daughter of the Sun with all her glory, O ye Nāsatyas, chose your car to bear her. Ye, ever-youthful Ones, again remembered Tugra, according to your ancient manner:With horses brown of hue that flew with swift wings ye brought back Bhujyu from the sea of billows. The son of Tugra had invoked you, Aśvins; borne on he went uninjured through the ocean.Ye with your chariot swift as thought, well-harnessed, carried him off, O Mighty Ones, to safety. The quail had invocated you, O Aśvins, when from the wolf's devouring jaws ye freed her.With conquering car ye cleft the mountain's ridges: the offspring of Viśvāc ye killed with poison. He whom for furnishing a hundred wethers to the she-wolf, his wicked father blinded,—To him, Ṛjrāśva, gave ye eyes, O Aśvins; light to the blind ye sent for perfect vision. To bring the blind man joy thus cried the she-wolf: O Aśvins, O ye Mighty Ones, O Heroes,For me Ṛjrāśva, like a youthful lover, hath. cut piecemeal one and a hundred wethers. Great and weal-giving is your aid, O Aśvins, ye, objects of all thought, made whole the cripple.Purandhi also for this cause invoked you, and ye, O mighty, came to her with succours. Ye, Wonder-Workers, filled with milk for Śayu the milkless cow, emaciated, barren;And by your powers the child of Purumitra ye brought to Vimada to be his consort. Ploughing and sowing barley, O ye Aśvins, milking out food for men, ye Wonder-Workers,Blasting away the Dasyu with your trumpet, ye gave far-spreading light unto the Ārya. Ye brought the horse's head, Aśvins, and gave it unto Dadhyac the offspring of Atharvan.True, he revealed to you, O Wonder-Workers, sweet Soma, Tvaṣṭar's secret, as your girdle. O Sages, evermore I crave your favour: be gracious unto all my prayers, O Aśvins.Grant me, Nāsatyas, riches in abundance, wealth famous and accompanied with children. With liberal bounty to the weakling's consorts ye, Heroes, gave a son Hiraṇyahasta;And Śyāva, cut into three several pieces, ye brought to life again, O bounteous Aśvins. These your heroic exploits, O ye Aśvins, done in the days. of old, have men related.May we, addressing prayer to you, ye Mighty, speak with brave sons about us to the synod.

verses.sanskrit: मध्वः सोमस्याश्विना मदाय प्रत्नो होता विवासते वां ।बर्हिष्मती रातिर्विश्रिता गीरिषा यातं नासत्योप वाजैः ॥
verses.transliteration: mádhvaḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ aśvinā ǀ mádāya ǀ pratnáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsate ǀ vām ǀbarhíṣmatī ǀ rātíḥ ǀ ví-śritā ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ iṣā́ ǀ yātam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ úpa ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: AŚVINS, your ancient priest invites you hither to gladden you with draughts of meath of Soma. Our gift is on the grass, our song apportioned: with food and strength come hither, O Nāsatyas.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvinsfor your gratification by the plural asant Soma, your ancient worshipper adores you; the offering is poured upon the sacred gras, thehymn is ready (for repetition); come,Nāsatyas, with food and with vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: AŚVINS, your ancient priest invites you hither to gladden you with draughts of meath of Soma. Our gift is on the grass, our song apportioned: with food and strength come hither, O Nāsatyas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वामश्विना मनसो जवीयान्रथः स्वश्वो विश आजिगाति ।येन गच्छथः सुकृतो दुरोणं तेन नरा वर्तिरस्मभ्यं यातं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ su-áśvaḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā-jígāti ǀyéna ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ duroṇám ǀ téna ǀ narā ǀ vartíḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ yātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: That car of yours, swifter than thought, O Aśvins, which drawn by brave steeds cometh to the people, Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious,—come ye thereon to our abode, O Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: With that car,Aśvins, which, rapid as thought, drawn by good horses, appears before men, and withwhich you repair to the dwelling of the virtuous, come, leaders of (sacrifice), to our abode.
verses.griffith_verse: That car of yours, swifter than thought, O Aśvins, which drawn by brave steeds cometh to the people, Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious,—come ye thereon to our abode, O Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋषिं नरावंहसः पांचजन्यमृबीसादत्रिं मुंचथो गणेन ।मिनंता दस्योरशिवस्य माया अनुपूर्वं वृषणा चोदयंता ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛ́ṣim ǀ narau ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ pā́ñca-janyam ǀ ṛbī́sāt ǀ átrim ǀ muñcathaḥ ǀ gaṇéna ǀminántā ǀ dásyoḥ ǀ áśivasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ anu-pūrvám ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ codáyantā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye freed sage Atri, whom the Five Tribes honoured, from the strait pit, ye Heroes with his people, Baffling the guiles of the malignant Dasyu, repelling them, ye Mighty in succession.
verses.wilson_translation: You liberated, leaders (of rites), the sage Atri, who was venerated by the five classes of men from the wicked prison, together with his troop (of children), destroying his enemies and baffling, showerers (of benefits), the devices of the malignant Dasyus.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye freed sage Atri, whom the Five Tribes honoured, from the strait pit, ye Heroes with his people, Baffling the guiles of the malignant Dasyu, repelling them, ye Mighty in succession.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वं न गूळ्हमश्विना दुरेवैर्ऋषिं नरा वृषणा रेभमप्सु ।सं तं रिणीथो विप्रुतं दंसोभिर्न वां जूर्यंति पूर्व्या कृतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvam ǀ ná ǀ gūḷhám ǀ aśvinā ǀ duḥ-évaiḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ narā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ rebhám ǀ ap-sú ǀsám ǀ tám ǀ riṇīthaḥ ǀ ví-prutam ǀ dáṃsaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ vām ǀ jūryanti ǀ pūrvyā́ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rebha the sage, ye mighty Heroes, Aśvins! whom, like a horse, vile men had sunk in water,— Him, wounded, with your wondrous power ye rescued: your exploits of old time endure for ever.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of sacrifice), showerers (of benefits), you restored Rebha, cast by unassailable (enemies) into the water, and wounded, like a (sick) horse, by your (healing) skill; your ancient exploits do not fade (from recollection).
verses.griffith_verse: Rebha the sage, ye mighty Heroes, Aśvins! whom, like a horse, vile men had sunk in water,— Him, wounded, with your wondrous power ye rescued: your exploits of old time endure for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुषुप्वांसं न निर्ऋतेरुपस्थे सूर्यं न दस्रा तमसि क्षियंतं ।शुभे रुक्मं न दर्शतं निखातमुदूपथुरश्विना वंदनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: susupvā́ṃsam ǀ ná ǀ níḥ-ṛteḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ná ǀ dasrā ǀ támasi ǀ kṣiyántam ǀśubhé ǀ rukmám ǀ ná ǀ darśatám ǀ ní-khātam ǀ út ǀ ūpathuḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ vándanāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye brought forth Vandana, ye Wonder-Workers, for triumph, like fair gold that hath been buried, Like one who slumbered in destruction's bosom, or like the Sun when dwelling in the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: You extricated,Dasras, the sage (Vandanā) cast into a well, like a handsome and splendid ornament designed for embellishment, and (lying)Aśvins, like one sleepin gon the lap of the earth or like the sun disappearing in darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye brought forth Vandana, ye Wonder-Workers, for triumph, like fair gold that hath been buried, Like one who slumbered in destruction's bosom, or like the Sun when dwelling in the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वां नरा शंस्यं पज्रियेण कक्षीवता नासत्या परिज्मन् ।शफादश्वस्य वाजिनो जनाय शतं कुंभाँ असिंचतं मधूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ śáṃsyam ǀ pajriyéṇa ǀ kakṣī́vatā ǀ nāsatyā ǀ pári-jman ǀśaphā́t ǀ áśvasya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ jánāya ǀ śatám ǀ kumbhā́n ǀ asiñcatam ǀ mádhūnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Kakṣīvān, Pajra's son, must laud that exploit of yours, Nāsatyas, Heroes, ye who wander! When from the hoof of your strong horse ye showered a hundred jars of honey for the people.
verses.wilson_translation: That (exploit) of yours, leaders (of sacrifice), is to be celebrated,Nāsatyas, by Kakṣīvat, of the race of Pajra, when you filled for the (expectant) man a hundred vases of sweet (liquors) from the hoof of your fleet horse.
verses.griffith_verse: Kakṣīvān, Pajra's son, must laud that exploit of yours, Nāsatyas, Heroes, ye who wander! When from the hoof of your strong horse ye showered a hundred jars of honey for the people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं नरा स्तुवते कृष्णियाय विष्णाप्वं ददथुर्विश्वकाय ।घोषायै चित्पितृषदे दुरोणे पतिं जूर्यंत्या अश्विनावदत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ narā ǀ stuvaté ǀ kṛṣṇiyā́ya ǀ viṣṇāpvám ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ víśvakāya ǀghóṣāyai ǀ cit ǀ pitṛ-sáde ǀ duroṇé ǀ pátim ǀ jū́ryantyai ǀ aśvinau ǀ adattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Kṛṣṇa's son, to Viśvaka who praised you, O Heroes, ye restored his son Viṣṇāpū. To Ghoṣā, living in her father's dwelling, stricken in years, ye gave a husband, Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: You restored, leaders (of sacrifices), Viṣṇāpu (his lost son) to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, when he praised you; you bestowed,Aśvins, a husband upon Ghoṣā, growing old and tarrying inher father's dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: To Kṛṣṇa's son, to Viśvaka who praised you, O Heroes, ye restored his son Viṣṇāpū. To Ghoṣā, living in her father's dwelling, stricken in years, ye gave a husband, Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं श्यावाय रुशतीमदत्तं महः क्षोणस्याश्विना कण्वाय ।प्रवाच्यं तद्वृषणा कृतं वां यन्नार्षदाय श्रवो अध्यधत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ śyā́vāya ǀ rúśatīm ǀ adattam ǀ maháḥ ǀ kṣoṇásya ǀ aśvinā ǀ káṇvāya ǀpra-vā́cyam ǀ tát ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ kṛtám ǀ vām ǀ yát ǀ nārsadā́ya ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ adhi-ádhattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ruṣatī, of the mighty people, Aśvins, ye gave to Śyāva of the line of Kaṇva. This deed of yours, ye Strong Ones should be published, that ye gave glory to the son of Nṛṣad.
verses.wilson_translation: You gave,Aśvins, a lovely bride to Śyāvā; you gave sight to Kaṇva, unable to see his way; showerers (of benefits), the deed is to be glorified by which you gave hearing to the son of Nṛṣad.
verses.griffith_verse: Ruṣatī, of the mighty people, Aśvins, ye gave to Śyāva of the line of Kaṇva. This deed of yours, ye Strong Ones should be published, that ye gave glory to the son of Nṛṣad.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरू वर्पांस्यश्विना दधाना नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वं ।सहस्रसां वाजिनमप्रतीतमहिहनं श्रवस्यं तरुत्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: purú ǀ várpāṃsi ǀ aśvinā ǀ dádhānā ǀ ní ǀ pedáve ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ āśúm ǀ áśvam ǀsahasra-sā́m ǀ vājínam ǀ áprati-itam ǀ ahi-hánam ǀ śravasyám ǀ tárutram ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, wearing many forms at pleasure, on Pedu ye bestowed a fleet-foot courser, Strong, winner of a thousand spoils, resistless the serpent slayer, glorious, triumphant.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, who assume many forms, you gave to Pedua swift horse, the bringer of a thousand (treasures), powerful, irresistible, the destroyer of foes, the object of praise, the bearer (over dangers).
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, wearing many forms at pleasure, on Pedu ye bestowed a fleet-foot courser, Strong, winner of a thousand spoils, resistless the serpent slayer, glorious, triumphant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतानि वां श्रवस्या सुदानू ब्रह्मांगूषं सदनं रोदस्योः ।यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवंते यातमिषा च विदुषे च वाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ vām ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ bráhma ǀ āṅgūṣám ǀ sádanam ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀyát ǀ vām ǀ pajrā́saḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ hávante ǀ yātám ǀ iṣā́ ǀ ca ǀ vidúṣe ǀ ca ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: These glorious things are yours, ye Bounteous Givers; prayer, praise in both worlds are your habitation. O Aśvins, when the sons of Pajra call you, send strength with nourishment to him who knoweth.
verses.wilson_translation: Liberal givers, these your exploits are to be celebrated, and the resounding prayer propitiates you while abiding in heaven and earth; when the descendants of Pajra invite you,Aśvins, come with food, and grant strength to the sage (who worships you).
verses.griffith_verse: These glorious things are yours, ye Bounteous Givers; prayer, praise in both worlds are your habitation. O Aśvins, when the sons of Pajra call you, send strength with nourishment to him who knoweth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूनोर्मानेनाश्विना गृणाना वाजं विप्राय भुरणा रदंता ।अगस्त्ये ब्रह्मणा वावृधाना सं विश्पलां नासत्यारिणीतं ॥
verses.transliteration: sūnóḥ ǀ mā́nena ǀ aśvinā ǀ gṛṇānā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ víprāya ǀ bhuraṇā ǀ rádantā ǀagástye ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ vavṛdhānā́ ǀ sám ǀ viśpálām ǀ nāsatyā ǀ ariṇītam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hymned with the reverence of a son, O Aśvins ye Swift Ones giving booty to the singer, Glorified by Agastya with devotion, established Viśpalā again, Nāsatyas.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, glorified by the praises of the son (of the jar), and giving food, nourishers (of men), to the sage (Bharadvāja), exalted by Agastyawithprayer, you restored Nāsatyas, Viṣpalā.
verses.griffith_verse: Hymned with the reverence of a son, O Aśvins ye Swift Ones giving booty to the singer, Glorified by Agastya with devotion, established Viśpalā again, Nāsatyas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुह यांता सुष्टुतिं काव्यस्य दिवो नपाता वृषणा शयुत्रा ।हिरण्यस्येव कलशं निखातमुदूपथुर्दशमे अश्विनाहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: kúha ǀ yā́ntā ǀ su-stutím ǀ kāvyásya ǀ dívaḥ ǀ napātā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ śayutrā́ ǀhíraṇyasya-iva ǀ kaláśam ǀ ní-khātam ǀ út ǀ ūpathuḥ ǀ daśamé ǀ aśvinā ǀ áhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Sons of Heaven, ye Mighty, whither went ye, sought ye, for his fair praise the home of Kāvya. When, like a pitcher full of gold, O Aśvins, on the tenth day ye lifted up the buried?
verses.wilson_translation: Wither were you going, sons of heaven, showerers (of benefits), when, on your way to the dwellingof Kāvya, (to receive his) adoration, you raised up (Rebha),Aśvins, on the tenth day, like a buried vessel full of gold?
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Sons of Heaven, ye Mighty, whither went ye, sought ye, for his fair praise the home of Kāvya. When, like a pitcher full of gold, O Aśvins, on the tenth day ye lifted up the buried?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः ।युवो रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य सह श्रिया नासत्यावृणीत ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ cyávānam ǀ aśvinā ǀ járantam ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yúvānam ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ rátham ǀ duhitā́ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ sahá ǀ śriyā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ avṛṇīta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye with the aid of your great powers, O Aśvins, restored to youth the ancient man Cyavāna. The Daughter of the Sun with all her glory, O ye Nāsatyas, chose your car to bear her.
verses.wilson_translation: You rendered, by your power,Aśvins, the aged Cyavanaagain young; the daughter of the sun,Nāsatyas, invested your chariot with beauty.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye with the aid of your great powers, O Aśvins, restored to youth the ancient man Cyavāna. The Daughter of the Sun with all her glory, O ye Nāsatyas, chose your car to bear her.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं तुग्राय पूर्व्येभिरेवैः पुनर्मन्यावभवतं युवाना ।युवं भुज्युमर्णसो निः समुद्राद्विभिरूहथुर्ऋज्रेभिरश्वैः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ túgrāya ǀ pūrvyébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀ punaḥ-manyáu ǀ abhavatam ǀ yuvānā ǀyuvám ǀ bhujyúm ǀ árṇasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ samudrā́t ǀ ví-bhiḥ ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ ṛjrébhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, ever-youthful Ones, again remembered Tugra, according to your ancient manner: With horses brown of hue that flew with swift wings ye brought back Bhujyu from the sea of billows.
verses.wilson_translation: Dissipators of affliction, as you were praised with former praises by Tugra, so were you again adored (by him), when you brought Bhujyusafe from the tossing ocean with swift ships and rapid horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, ever-youthful Ones, again remembered Tugra, according to your ancient manner: With horses brown of hue that flew with swift wings ye brought back Bhujyu from the sea of billows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजोहवीदश्विना तौग्र्यो वां प्रोळ्हः समुद्रमव्यथिर्जगन्वान् ।निष्टमूहथुः सुयुजा रथेन मनोजवसा वृषणा स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: ájohavīt ǀ aśvinā ǀ taugryáḥ ǀ vām ǀ prá-ūḷhaḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ avyathíḥ ǀ jaganvā́n ǀníḥ ǀ tám ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ su-yújā ǀ ráthena ǀ mánaḥ-javasā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: The son of Tugra had invoked you, Aśvins; borne on he went uninjured through the ocean. Ye with your chariot swift as thought, well-harnessed, carried him off, O Mighty Ones, to safety.
verses.wilson_translation: Th sun of Tugra, brought back by you,Aśvins, (to his father), glorified you whenhe ahd crossed the ocean in safety, and you bore him, showerers (of benefits), with your well-harnessed car, swift as thought, to safety.
verses.griffith_verse: The son of Tugra had invoked you, Aśvins; borne on he went uninjured through the ocean. Ye with your chariot swift as thought, well-harnessed, carried him off, O Mighty Ones, to safety.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजोहवीदश्विना वर्तिका वामास्नो यत्सीममुंचतं वृकस्य ।वि जयुषा ययथुः सान्वद्रेर्जातं विष्वाचो अहतं विषेण ॥
verses.transliteration: ájohavīt ǀ aśvinā ǀ vártikā ǀ vām ǀ āsnáḥ ǀ yát ǀ sīm ǀ ámuñcatam ǀ vṛ́kasya ǀví ǀ jayúṣā ǀ yayathuḥ ǀ sā́nu ǀ ádreḥ ǀ jātám ǀ viṣvā́caḥ ǀ ahatam ǀ viṣéṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: The quail had invocated you, O Aśvins, when from the wolf's devouring jaws ye freed her. With conquering car ye cleft the mountain's ridges: the offspring of Viśvāc ye killed with poison.
verses.wilson_translation: The quail glorified you,Aśvins, when you saved her from the mouth of the wolf; you carried off (Jāhuṣa) to the top of the mountain in your triumphant chariot; and slew the son of Viṣvāñc with a poisoned (arrow).
verses.griffith_verse: The quail had invocated you, O Aśvins, when from the wolf's devouring jaws ye freed her. With conquering car ye cleft the mountain's ridges: the offspring of Viśvāc ye killed with poison.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
