verses.sanskrit: शतं मेषान्वृक्ये मामहानं तमः प्रणीतमशिवेन पित्रा ।आक्षी ऋज्राश्वे अश्विनावधत्तं ज्योतिरंधाय चक्रथुर्विचक्षे ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ meṣā́n ǀ vṛkyé ǀ mamahānám ǀ támaḥ ǀ prá-nītam ǀ áśivena ǀ pitrā́ ǀā́ ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ ṛjrá-aśve ǀ aśvinau ǀ adhattam ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ andhā́ya ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ vi-cákṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom for furnishing a hundred wethers to the she-wolf, his wicked father blinded,— To him, Ṛjrāśva, gave ye eyes, O Aśvins; light to the blind ye sent for perfect vision.
verses.wilson_translation: You restored eyes toṚjrāśva, who, on presenting a hundred sheep to the she-wolf, had been condemned to darkness by his indignant father, and gave light to the blind, wherewith to behold all things.
verses.griffith_verse: He whom for furnishing a hundred wethers to the she-wolf, his wicked father blinded,— To him, Ṛjrāśva, gave ye eyes, O Aśvins; light to the blind ye sent for perfect vision.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनमंधाय भरमह्वयत्सा वृकीरश्विना वृषणा नरेति ।जारः कनीन इव चक्षदान ऋज्राश्वः शतमेकं च मेषान् ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ andhā́ya ǀ bháram ǀ ahvayat ǀ sā́ ǀ vṛkī́ḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ nárā ǀ íti ǀjāráḥ ǀ kanī́naḥ-iva ǀ cakṣadānáḥ ǀ ṛjrá-aśvaḥ ǀ śatám ǀ ékam ǀ ca ǀ meṣā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: To bring the blind man joy thus cried the she-wolf: O Aśvins, O ye Mighty Ones, O Heroes, For me Ṛjrāśva, like a youthful lover, hath. cut piecemeal one and a hundred wethers.
verses.wilson_translation: (Desiring) that the enjoyment (arising from the perfection) of the senses (should be restored to the blind), the she-wolf invoked you, (saying), "Aśvins, showerers (of benefits), leaders (of sacrifices),Ṛjrāśva, (lavish) as a youthful gallant, (has given me) a hundred and one sheep, cutting them into fragments".
verses.griffith_verse: To bring the blind man joy thus cried the she-wolf: O Aśvins, O ye Mighty Ones, O Heroes, For me Ṛjrāśva, like a youthful lover, hath. cut piecemeal one and a hundred wethers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मही वामूतिरश्विना मयोभूरुत स्रामं धिष्ण्या सं रिणीथः ।अथा युवामिदह्वयत्पुरंधिरागच्छतं सीं वृषणाववोभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ ǀ vām ǀ ūtíḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ mayaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ srāmám ǀ dhiṣṇyā ǀ sám ǀ riṇīthaḥ ǀátha ǀ yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ ahvayat ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agacchatam ǀ sīm ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Great and weal-giving is your aid, O Aśvins, ye, objects of all thought, made whole the cripple. Purandhi also for this cause invoked you, and ye, O mighty, came to her with succours.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, your powerful protection is the source of happiness; worthy of laudation, you have made whole the maimed; therefore, has the intelligent (Ghoṣā) called upon you; showerers (of benefits) come hither with your succours.
verses.griffith_verse: Great and weal-giving is your aid, O Aśvins, ye, objects of all thought, made whole the cripple. Purandhi also for this cause invoked you, and ye, O mighty, came to her with succours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधेनुं दस्रा स्तर्यं विषक्तामपिन्वतं शयवे अश्विना गां ।युवं शचीभिर्विमदाय जायां न्यूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्य योषां ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhenum ǀ dasrā ǀ staryám ǀ ví-saktām ǀ ápinvatam ǀ śayáve ǀ aśvinā ǀ gā́m ǀyuvám ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ jāyā́m ǀ ní ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ puru-mitrásya ǀ yóṣām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, Wonder-Workers, filled with milk for Śayu the milkless cow, emaciated, barren; And by your powers the child of Purumitra ye brought to Vimada to be his consort.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras, you fille dthe milkless, barren, and emaciated cow ofŚayuwith milk; you brought, by your powers, the daughter of Purumitra, as a wife, of Vimada.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, Wonder-Workers, filled with milk for Śayu the milkless cow, emaciated, barren; And by your powers the child of Purumitra ye brought to Vimada to be his consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यवं वृकेणाश्विना वपंतेषं दुहंता मनुषाय दस्रा ।अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमंतोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: yávam ǀ vṛ́keṇa ǀ aśvinā ǀ vápantā ǀ íṣam ǀ duhántā ǀ mánuṣāya ǀ dasrā ǀabhí ǀ dásyum ǀ bákureṇa ǀ dhámantā ǀ urú ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ ā́ryāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ploughing and sowing barley, O ye Aśvins, milking out food for men, ye Wonder-Workers, Blasting away the Dasyu with your trumpet, ye gave far-spreading light unto the Ārya.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, causing the barley to be sown (in the fields that had been prepared) by the plural ugh; milking (the clouds) for the sake of Manu; destroying the Dasyuwith the thunderbolt; you have bestowed brilliant light upon theĀrya.
verses.griffith_verse: Ploughing and sowing barley, O ye Aśvins, milking out food for men, ye Wonder-Workers, Blasting away the Dasyu with your trumpet, ye gave far-spreading light unto the Ārya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आथर्वणायाश्विना दधीचेऽश्व्यं शिरः प्रत्यैरयतं ।स वां मधु प्र वोचदृतायंत्वाष्ट्रं यद्दस्रावपिकक्ष्यं वां ॥
verses.transliteration: ātharvaṇā́ya ǀ aśvinā ǀ dadhīcé ǀ áśvyam ǀ śíraḥ ǀ práti ǀ airayatam ǀsáḥ ǀ vām ǀ mádhu ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ ṛta-yán ǀ tvāṣṭrám ǀ yát ǀ dasrau ǀ api-kakṣyám ǀ vām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye brought the horse's head, Aśvins, and gave it unto Dadhyac the offspring of Atharvan. True, he revealed to you, O Wonder-Workers, sweet Soma, Tvaṣṭar's secret, as your girdle.
verses.wilson_translation: You replaced,Aśvins, with the head of a horse, (the head of) Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, and, true to his promise, he revealed to you the mystic knowledge which he had learned from Tvaṣṭā, and which was as a ligature of the waist to you.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye brought the horse's head, Aśvins, and gave it unto Dadhyac the offspring of Atharvan. True, he revealed to you, O Wonder-Workers, sweet Soma, Tvaṣṭar's secret, as your girdle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सदा कवी सुमतिमा चके वां विश्वा धियो अश्विना प्रावतं मे ।अस्मे रयिं नासत्या बृहंतमपत्यसाचं श्रुत्यं रराथां ॥
verses.transliteration: sádā ǀ kavī íti ǀ su-matím ǀ ā́ ǀ cake ǀ vām ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ prá ǀ avatam ǀ me ǀasmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ nāsatyā ǀ bṛhántam ǀ apatya-sā́cam ǀ śrútyam ǀ rarāthām ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Sages, evermore I crave your favour: be gracious unto all my prayers, O Aśvins. Grant me, Nāsatyas, riches in abundance, wealth famous and accompanied with children.
verses.wilson_translation: Sapient Aśvins, I ever solicit your favour; protect all my religious duties, and grant,Nāsatyas, abundant and excellent wealth, together with offsprings.
verses.griffith_verse: O Sages, evermore I crave your favour: be gracious unto all my prayers, O Aśvins. Grant me, Nāsatyas, riches in abundance, wealth famous and accompanied with children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यहस्तमश्विना रराणा पुत्रं नरा वध्रिमत्या अदत्तं ।त्रिधा ह श्यावमश्विना विकस्तमुज्जीवस ऐरयतं सुदानू ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-hastam ǀ aśvinā ǀ rárāṇā ǀ putrám ǀ narā ǀ vadhri-matyā́ḥ ǀ adattam ǀtrídhā ǀ ha ǀ śyā́vam ǀ aśvinā ǀ ví-kastam ǀ út ǀ jīváse ǀ airayatam ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǁ
verses.english_translation: With liberal bounty to the weakling's consorts ye, Heroes, gave a son Hiraṇyahasta; And Śyāva, cut into three several pieces, ye brought to life again, O bounteous Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: Liberal Aśvins, leaders (of sacrifices), you gave to Vadhṛmati her son Hiraṇyahasta; bounteous Aśvins, you restored to life the triply-mutilatedŚyāva.
verses.griffith_verse: With liberal bounty to the weakling's consorts ye, Heroes, gave a son Hiraṇyahasta; And Śyāva, cut into three several pieces, ye brought to life again, O bounteous Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतानि वामश्विना वीर्याणि प्र पूर्व्याण्यायवोऽवोचन् ।ब्रह्म कृण्वंतो वृषणा युवभ्यां सुवीरासो विदथमा वदेम ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ prá ǀ pūrvyā́ṇi ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ avocan ǀbráhma ǀ kṛṇvántaḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ yuvá-bhyām ǀ su-vī́rāsaḥ ǀ vidátham ǀ ā́ ǀ vadema ǁ
verses.english_translation: These your heroic exploits, O ye Aśvins, done in the days. of old, have men related. May we, addressing prayer to you, ye Mighty, speak with brave sons about us to the synod.
verses.wilson_translation: These, your ancient exploits,Aśvins, our forefathers have celebrated, and we offer adoration to you, showerers (of benefits) repeating your praises, accompanied by our dependants.
verses.griffith_verse: These your heroic exploits, O ye Aśvins, done in the days. of old, have men related. May we, addressing prayer to you, ye Mighty, speak with brave sons about us to the synod.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXVIII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FLYING, with falcons, may your chariot, Aśvins, most gracious, bringing friendlyhelp, come hither,—Your chariot, swifter than the mind of mortal, fleet as the wind, three-seated O ye Mighty. Come to us with your chariot triple seated, three-wheeled, of triple form, that rolleth lightly.Fill full our cows, give mettle to our horses, and make each hero son grow strong, O Aśvins. With your well-rolling car, descending swiftly, hear this the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers.How then have ancient sages said, O Aśvins, that ye most swiftly come to stay affliction? O Aśvins, let your falcons bear you hither, yoked to your chariot, swift, with flying pinions,Which, ever active, like the airy eagles, carry you, O Nāsatyas, to the banquet. The youthful Daughter of the Sun, delighting in you, ascended there your chariot, Heroes.Borne on their swift wings let your beauteous horses, your birds of ruddy hue, convey you near us. Ye raised up Vandana, strong Wonder-Workers! with great might, and with power ye rescued Rebha.From out the sea ye saved the son of Tugra, and gave his youth again unto Cyavāna. To Atri, cast down to the fire that scorched him, ye gave, O Aśvins, strengthening food and favour.Accepting his fair praises with approval, ye gave his eyes again to blinded Kaṇva. For ancient Śayu in his sore affliction ye caused his cow to swell with milk, O Aśvins.The quail from her great misery ye delivered, and a new leg for Viśpalā provided. A white horse, Aśvins, ye bestowed on Pedu, a serpent-slaying steed sent down by Indra,Loud-neighing, conquering the foe, high-mettled, firm-limbed and vigorous, winning thousand treasures. Such as ye are, O nobly born, O Heroes, we in our trouble call on you for succour.Accepting these our songs, for our wellbeing come to us on your chariot treasure-laden. Come unto us combined in love, Nāsatyas come with the fresh swift vigour of the falcon.Bearing oblations I invoke you, Aśvins, at the first break of everlasting morning.

verses.sanskrit: आ वां रथो अश्विना श्येनपत्वा सुमृळीकः स्ववाँ यात्वर्वाङ् ।यो मर्त्यस्य मनसो जवीयांत्रिवंधुरो वृषणा वातरंहाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ śyená-patvā ǀ su-mṛḷīkáḥ ǀ svá-vān ǀ yātu ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀyáḥ ǀ mártyasya ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ tri-vandhuráḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ vā́ta-raṃhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FLYING, with falcons, may your chariot, Aśvins, most gracious, bringing friendly help, come hither,— Your chariot, swifter than the mind of mortal, fleet as the wind, three-seated O ye Mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: May your elegant and rich car, swift as a hawk, come,Aśvins, to our presence, fo rit as quick as the mind of man, surmounted, showerers (of benefits) by three columns, and rapid as the wind.
verses.griffith_verse: FLYING, with falcons, may your chariot, Aśvins, most gracious, bringing friendly help, come hither,— Your chariot, swifter than the mind of mortal, fleet as the wind, three-seated O ye Mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिवंधुरेण त्रिवृता रथेन त्रिचक्रेण सुवृता यातमर्वाक् ।पिन्वतं गा जिन्वतमर्वतो नो वर्धयतमश्विना वीरमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-vandhuréṇa ǀ tri-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀ tri-cakréṇa ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ arvā́k ǀpínvatam ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ jínvatam ǀ árvataḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vardháyatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ vīrám ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us with your chariot triple seated, three-wheeled, of triple form, that rolleth lightly. Fill full our cows, give mettle to our horses, and make each hero son grow strong, O Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us with your tri-columnar, triangular, three-wheeled, and well-constructed car; replenish our cows (with milk), give spirit to our horses, and augment,Aśvins, our posterity.
verses.griffith_verse: Come to us with your chariot triple seated, three-wheeled, of triple form, that rolleth lightly. Fill full our cows, give mettle to our horses, and make each hero son grow strong, O Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रवद्यामना सुवृता रथेन दस्राविमं शृणुतं श्लोकमद्रेः ।किमंग वां प्रत्यवर्तिं गमिष्ठाहुर्विप्रासो अश्विना पुराजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: pravát-yāmanā ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀ dásrau ǀ imám ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ ślókam ǀ ádreḥ ǀkím ǀ aṅgá ǀ vām ǀ práti ǀ ávartim ǀ gámiṣṭhā ǀ āhúḥ ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ purā-jā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With your well-rolling car, descending swiftly, hear this the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers. How then have ancient sages said, O Aśvins, that ye most swiftly come to stay affliction?
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras(having come) with your quick-moving well-constructed car, hear this hymn, (recited by one) who reveres you; do not the ancient sages say that you are most prompt,Aśvins, (to avert) poverty from the worshipper?
verses.griffith_verse: With your well-rolling car, descending swiftly, hear this the press-stone's song, ye Wonder-Workers. How then have ancient sages said, O Aśvins, that ye most swiftly come to stay affliction?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां श्येनासो अश्विना वहंतु रथे युक्तास आशवः पतंगाः ।ये अप्तुरो दिव्यासो न गृध्रा अभि प्रयो नासत्या वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ śyenā́saḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ vahantu ǀ ráthe ǀ yuktā́saḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ pataṅgā́ḥ ǀyé ǀ ap-túraḥ ǀ divyā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ gṛ́dhrāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ práyaḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ váhanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, let your falcons bear you hither, yoked to your chariot, swift, with flying pinions, Which, ever active, like the airy eagles, carry you, O Nāsatyas, to the banquet.
verses.wilson_translation: May your quick-moving, prancing steeds, rapid as hawks, yoked to your car, bear you,Aśvins, (hither), who, quick as (falling) water, like vultures flying through the air, convey you,Nāsatyas, to the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, let your falcons bear you hither, yoked to your chariot, swift, with flying pinions, Which, ever active, like the airy eagles, carry you, O Nāsatyas, to the banquet.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां रथं युवतिस्तिष्ठदत्र जुष्ट्वी नरा दुहिता सूर्यस्य ।परि वामश्वा वपुषः पतंगा वयो वहंत्वरुषा अभीके ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ tiṣṭhat ǀ átra ǀ juṣṭvī́ ǀ narā ǀ duhitā́ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀpári ǀ vām ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ vápuṣaḥ ǀ pataṅgā́ḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ vahantu ǀ aruṣā́ḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǁ
verses.english_translation: The youthful Daughter of the Sun, delighting in you, ascended there your chariot, Heroes. Borne on their swift wings let your beauteous horses, your birds of ruddy hue, convey you near us.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of sacrifice), the youthful daughter of Sūryaascended, delighted, this your car; may your strong-bodied prancing, fleet, and shining horses, bring you near uṣ
verses.griffith_verse: The youthful Daughter of the Sun, delighting in you, ascended there your chariot, Heroes. Borne on their swift wings let your beauteous horses, your birds of ruddy hue, convey you near us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्वंदनमैरतं दंसनाभिरुद्रेभं दस्रा वृषणा शचीभिः ।निष्टौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात्पुनश्च्यवानं चक्रथुर्युवानं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ vándanam ǀ airatam ǀ daṃsánābhiḥ ǀ út ǀ rebhám ǀ dasrā ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀníḥ ǀ taugryám ǀ pārayathaḥ ǀ samudrā́t ǀ púnaríti ǀ cyávānam ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ yúvānam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye raised up Vandana, strong Wonder-Workers! with great might, and with power ye rescued Rebha. From out the sea ye saved the son of Tugra, and gave his youth again unto Cyavāna.
verses.wilson_translation: By your deeds,Dasras, you raised up Vandanā, and, showerers (of benefits), Rebha; you bore the son of Tugraover the sea, and made Cyavanayoung.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye raised up Vandana, strong Wonder-Workers! with great might, and with power ye rescued Rebha. From out the sea ye saved the son of Tugra, and gave his youth again unto Cyavāna.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवमत्रयेऽवनीताय तप्तमूर्जमोमानमश्विनावधत्तं ।युवं कण्वायापिरिप्ताय चक्षुः प्रत्यधत्तं सुष्टुतिं जुजुषाणा ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ átraye ǀ áva-nītāya ǀ taptám ǀ ū́rjam ǀ omā́nam ǀ aśvinau ǀ adhattam ǀyuvám ǀ káṇvāya ǀ ápi-riptāya ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ práti ǀ adhattam ǀ su-stutím ǀ jujuṣāṇā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Atri, cast down to the fire that scorched him, ye gave, O Aśvins, strengthening food and favour. Accepting his fair praises with approval, ye gave his eyes again to blinded Kaṇva.
verses.wilson_translation: You (gave relief) to the imprisoned Atri, (quenching the) scorching heat, and fed him with grateful food; solicitous of worthy praise, you gave sight of Kaṇva, blinded (by darkness).
verses.griffith_verse: To Atri, cast down to the fire that scorched him, ye gave, O Aśvins, strengthening food and favour. Accepting his fair praises with approval, ye gave his eyes again to blinded Kaṇva.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं धेनुं शयवे नाधितायापिन्वतमश्विना पूर्व्याय ।अमुंचतं वर्तिकामंहसो निः प्रति जंघां विश्पलाया अधत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ dhenúm ǀ śayáve ǀ nādhitā́ya ǀ ápinvatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀámuñcatam ǀ vártikām ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ práti ǀ jáṅghām ǀ viśpálāyāḥ ǀ adhattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: For ancient Śayu in his sore affliction ye caused his cow to swell with milk, O Aśvins. The quail from her great misery ye delivered, and a new leg for Viśpalā provided.
verses.wilson_translation: You filled his cow with milk,Aśvins, for the ancientŚayu, when imploring (yoru aid); you liberated the quail from danger; you gave a leg to Viśpalā.
verses.griffith_verse: For ancient Śayu in his sore affliction ye caused his cow to swell with milk, O Aśvins. The quail from her great misery ye delivered, and a new leg for Viśpalā provided.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं श्वेतं पेदव इंद्रजूतमहिहनमश्विनादत्तमश्वं ।जोहूत्रमर्यो अभिभूतिमुग्रं सहस्रसां वृषणं वीड्वंगं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ śvetám ǀ pedáve ǀ índra-jūtam ǀ ahi-hánam ǀ aśvinā ǀ adattam ǀ áśvam ǀjohū́tram ǀ aryáḥ ǀ abhí-bhūtim ǀ ugrám ǀ sahasra-sā́m ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vīḷú-aṅgam ǁ
verses.english_translation: A white horse, Aśvins, ye bestowed on Pedu, a serpent-slaying steed sent down by Indra, Loud-neighing, conquering the foe, high-mettled, firm-limbed and vigorous, winning thousand treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: You gave to Pedu,Aśvins, the white and foe-trampling steed which you had received from Indra, loud-neighing (in battle), defying enemies, high-spirited, the acquirer of a thousand tresures, vigorous, and firm in body.
verses.griffith_verse: A white horse, Aśvins, ye bestowed on Pedu, a serpent-slaying steed sent down by Indra, Loud-neighing, conquering the foe, high-mettled, firm-limbed and vigorous, winning thousand treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता वां नरा स्ववसे सुजाता हवामहे अश्विना नाधमानाः ।आ न उप वसुमता रथेन गिरो जुषाणा सुविताय यातं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ sú ǀ ávase ǀ su-jātā́ ǀ hávāmahe ǀ aśvinā ǀ nā́dhamānāḥ ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vásu-matā ǀ ráthena ǀ gíraḥ ǀ juṣāṇā́ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ yātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such as ye are, O nobly born, O Heroes, we in our trouble call on you for succour. Accepting these our songs, for our wellbeing come to us on your chariot treasure-laden.
verses.wilson_translation: Earnestly we call you, leaders (of the sacrifice), such (as you have been described), and who are well born, to our succour, soliciting,Aśvins, wealth; contented with our laudations, come to us with your wealthy car, to brign us felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Such as ye are, O nobly born, O Heroes, we in our trouble call on you for succour. Accepting these our songs, for our wellbeing come to us on your chariot treasure-laden.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः ।हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमाया उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ śyenásya ǀ jávasā ǀ nū́tanena ǀ asmé íti ǀ yātam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀháve ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ śaśvat-tamā́yāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come unto us combined in love, Nāsatyas come with the fresh swift vigour of the falcon. Bearing oblations I invoke you, Aśvins, at the first break of everlasting morning.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us, auspicious Nāsatyas, with the fresh velocity of a hawk; bearing an oblation, I invoke you,Aśvins, at the rising of the ever constant dawn.
verses.griffith_verse: Come unto us combined in love, Nāsatyas come with the fresh swift vigour of the falcon. Bearing oblations I invoke you, Aśvins, at the first break of everlasting morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXIX. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HITHER, that I may live, I call unto the feast your wondrous car, thought-swift, borne on by rapid steeds.With thousand banners, hundred treasures, pouring gifts, promptly obedient, bestowing ample room. Even as it moveth near my hymn is lifted up, and all the regions come together to sing praise.I sweeten the oblations; now the helpers come. Ūrjānī hath, O Aśvins, mounted on your car. When striving man with man for glory they have met, brisk, measureless, eager for victory in fight,Then verily your car is seen upon the slope when ye, O Aśvins, bring some choice boon to the prince. Ye came to Bhujyu while he struggled in the flood, with flying birds, self-yoked, ye bore him to his sires.Ye went to the far-distant home, O Mighty Ones; and famed is your great aid to Divodāsa given. Aśvins, the car which you had yoked for glorious show your own two voices urged directed to its goal.Then she who came for friendship, Maid of noble birth, elected you as Husbands, you to be her Lords. Rebha ye saved from tyranny; for Atri's sake ye quenched with cold the fiery pit that compassed him.Ye made the cow of Śayu stream refreshing milk, and Vandana was holpen to extended life. Doers of marvels, skilful workers, ye restored Vandana, like a car, worn out with length of days.From earth ye brought the sage to life in wondrous mode; be your great deeds done here for him who honours you. Ye went to him who mourned in a far distant place, him who was left forlorn by treachery of his sire.Rich with the light of heaven was then the help ye gave, and marvellous your succour when ye stood by him. To you in praise of sweetness sang the honey-bee: Auśija calleth you in Soma's rapturous joy.Ye drew unto yourselves the spirit of Dadhyac, and then the horse's head uttered his words to you. A horse did ye provide for Pedu, excellent, white, O ye Aśvins, conqueror of combatants,Invincible in war by arrows, seeking heaven worthy of fame, like Indra, vanquisher of men.

verses.sanskrit: आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञियं जीवसे हुवे ।सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टीवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ puru-māyám ǀ manaḥ-júvam ǀ jīrá-aśvam ǀ yajñíyam ǀ jīváse ǀ huve ǀsahásra-ketum ǀ vanínam ǀ śatát-vasum ǀ śruṣṭī-vā́nam ǀ varivaḥ-dhā́m ǀ abhí ǀ práyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: HITHER, that I may live, I call unto the feast your wondrous car, thought-swift, borne on by rapid steeds. With thousand banners, hundred treasures, pouring gifts, promptly obedient, bestowing ample room.
verses.wilson_translation: Desiringfood, I invoke, (Aśvins), to support my life, your wonderful car, swift as thought, drawn by fleet horses, worthy of veneration, many-bannered, bringing rain, containing wealth, abundantly yielding delight, and conferring riches.
verses.griffith_verse: HITHER, that I may live, I call unto the feast your wondrous car, thought-swift, borne on by rapid steeds. With thousand banners, hundred treasures, pouring gifts, promptly obedient, bestowing ample room.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वा धीतिः प्रत्यस्य प्रयामन्यधायि शस्मन्त्समयंत आ दिशः ।स्वदामि घर्मं प्रति यंत्यूतय आ वामूर्जानी रथमश्विनारुहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvā́ ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ práti ǀ asya ǀ prá-yāmani ǀ ádhāyi ǀ śásman ǀ sám ǀ ayante ǀ ā́ ǀ díśaḥ ǀsvádāmi ǀ gharmám ǀ práti ǀ yanti ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vām ǀ ūrjā́nī ǀ rátham ǀ aśvinā ǀ aruhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as it moveth near my hymn is lifted up, and all the regions come together to sing praise. I sweeten the oblations; now the helpers come. Ūrjānī hath, O Aśvins, mounted on your car.
verses.wilson_translation: Upon its moving, our minds have been raised on high in praise; our hymns reach (the Aśvins). I sweeten the oblation; the assistants come nigh; Ūrjāni, (the daughter of the sun), has ascended, Aśvins, your car.
verses.griffith_verse: Even as it moveth near my hymn is lifted up, and all the regions come together to sing praise. I sweeten the oblations; now the helpers come. Ūrjānī hath, O Aśvins, mounted on your car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं यन्मिथः पस्पृधानासो अग्मत शुभे मखा अमिता जायवो रणे ।युवोरह प्रवणे चेकिते रथो यदश्विना वहथः सूरिमा वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ yát ǀ mitháḥ ǀ paspṛdhānā́saḥ ǀ ágmata ǀ śubhé ǀ makhā́ḥ ǀ ámitāḥ ǀ jāyávaḥ ǀ ráṇe ǀyuvóḥ ǀ áha ǀ pravaṇé ǀ cekite ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ yát ǀ aśvinā ǀ váhathaḥ ǀ sūrím ǀ ā́ ǀ váram ǁ
verses.english_translation: When striving man with man for glory they have met, brisk, measureless, eager for victory in fight, Then verily your car is seen upon the slope when ye, O Aśvins, bring some choice boon to the prince.
verses.wilson_translation: When devout and unnumbered (men), victorious in battle, mutually contending for wealth, come together, your car,Aśvins, is perceived on its downward course, in which you bear excellent (treasure) to the worshipper.
verses.griffith_verse: When striving man with man for glory they have met, brisk, measureless, eager for victory in fight, Then verily your car is seen upon the slope when ye, O Aśvins, bring some choice boon to the prince.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं भुज्युं भुरमाणं विभिर्गतं स्वयुक्तिभिर्निवहंता पितृभ्य आ ।यासिष्टं वर्तिर्वृषणा विजेन्यं दिवोदासाय महि चेति वामवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ bhujyúm ǀ bhurámāṇam ǀ ví-bhiḥ ǀ gatám ǀ sváyukti-bhiḥ ǀ ni-váhantā ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀyāsiṣṭám ǀ vartíḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ vi-jenyám ǀ dívaḥ-dāsāya ǀ máhi ǀ ceti ǀ vām ǀ ávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye came to Bhujyu while he struggled in the flood, with flying birds, self-yoked, ye bore him to his sires. Ye went to the far-distant home, O Mighty Ones; and famed is your great aid to Divodāsa given.
verses.wilson_translation: You brought back to his ancestor (Bhujyu, who, borne by his own steeds, had perished), (but that you rescued him) with your self-harnessed horses, and sent showerers (o fbenefits), to his distant dwellign; and great was the succour whichit is know you rendered to Divodāsa.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye came to Bhujyu while he struggled in the flood, with flying birds, self-yoked, ye bore him to his sires. Ye went to the far-distant home, O Mighty Ones; and famed is your great aid to Divodāsa given.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवोरश्विना वपुषे युवायुजं रथं वाणी येमतुरस्य शर्ध्यं ।आ वां पतित्वं सख्याय जग्मुषी योषावृणीत जेन्या युवां पती ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ vápuṣe ǀ yuvā-yújam ǀ rátham ǀ vā́ṇī íti ǀ yematuḥ ǀ asya ǀ śárdhyam ǀā́ ǀ vām ǀ pati-tvám ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ jagmúṣī ǀ yóṣā ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ jényā ǀ yuvā́m ǀ pátī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aśvins, the car which you had yoked for glorious show your own two voices urged directed to its goal. Then she who came for friendship, Maid of noble birth, elected you as Husbands, you to be her Lords.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, your admirable (horses) bore the car which you had carnessed, (first) to the goal, for the sake of honour, and the damsel, who was the prize, came through  affection, to you, and acknowledged your (husbandship), saying, "you are (my) lords".
verses.griffith_verse: Aśvins, the car which you had yoked for glorious show your own two voices urged directed to its goal. Then she who came for friendship, Maid of noble birth, elected you as Husbands, you to be her Lords.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं रेभं परिषूतेरुरुष्यथो हिमेन घर्मं परितप्तमत्रये ।युवं शयोरवसं पिप्यथुर्गवि प्र दीर्घेण वंदनस्तार्यायुषा ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ rebhám ǀ pári-sūteḥ ǀ uruṣyathaḥ ǀ hiména ǀ gharmám ǀ pári-taptam ǀ átraye ǀyuvám ǀ śayóḥ ǀ avasám ǀ pipyathuḥ ǀ gávi ǀ prá ǀ dīrghéṇa ǀ vándanaḥ ǀ tāri ǀ ā́yuṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rebha ye saved from tyranny; for Atri's sake ye quenched with cold the fiery pit that compassed him. Ye made the cow of Śayu stream refreshing milk, and Vandana was holpen to extended life.
verses.wilson_translation: You preserved Rebha from the violence around him; you quenched with snow, for Atri, the scorching heat; you genitive rated milk in the cow ofŚayu; and (by you) was Vandanāendowed with prolonged life.
verses.griffith_verse: Rebha ye saved from tyranny; for Atri's sake ye quenched with cold the fiery pit that compassed him. Ye made the cow of Śayu stream refreshing milk, and Vandana was holpen to extended life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं वंदनं निर्ऋतं जरण्यया रथं न दस्रा करणा समिन्वथः ।क्षेत्रादा विप्रं जनथो विपन्यया प्र वामत्र विधते दंसना भुवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ vándanam ǀ níḥ-ṛtam ǀ jaraṇyáyā ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ dasrā ǀ karaṇā́ ǀ sám ǀ invathaḥ ǀkṣétrāt ǀ ā́ ǀ vípram ǀ janathaḥ ǀ vipanyáyā ǀ prá ǀ vām ǀ átra ǀ vidhaté ǀ daṃsánā ǀ bhuvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Doers of marvels, skilful workers, ye restored Vandana, like a car, worn out with length of days. From earth ye brought the sage to life in wondrous mode; be your great deeds done here for him who honours you.
verses.wilson_translation: Skillful Dasras, you restored Vandanā, when debilitated by old age, as a (wheelwright repairs a worn-out) car; (moved) by his praises, you brought forth the sage (Vāmadeva) from the womb; may your (glorious) deeds be (displayed) for him who in this plural ce offers you worship.
verses.griffith_verse: Doers of marvels, skilful workers, ye restored Vandana, like a car, worn out with length of days. From earth ye brought the sage to life in wondrous mode; be your great deeds done here for him who honours you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अगच्छतं कृपमाणं परावति पितुः स्वस्य त्यजसा निबाधितं ।स्वर्वतीरित ऊतीर्युवोरह चित्रा अभीके अभवन्नभिष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágacchatam ǀ kṛ́pamāṇam ǀ parā-váti ǀ pitúḥ ǀ svásya ǀ tyájasā ǀ ní-bādhitam ǀsváḥ-vatīḥ ǀ itáḥ ǀ ūtī́ḥ ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ áha ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀ abhavan ǀ abhíṣṭayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye went to him who mourned in a far distant place, him who was left forlorn by treachery of his sire. Rich with the light of heaven was then the help ye gave, and marvellous your succour when ye stood by him.
verses.wilson_translation: You repaired to him who, aflicted by the abandonment of his own father, praised you from afar; hence your prompt and wonderful succours have been wished to be athand(by all).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye went to him who mourned in a far distant place, him who was left forlorn by treachery of his sire. Rich with the light of heaven was then the help ye gave, and marvellous your succour when ye stood by him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्या वां मधुमन्मक्षिकारपन्मदे सोमस्यौशिजो हुवन्यति ।युवं दधीचो मन आ विवासथोऽथा शिरः प्रति वामश्व्यं वदत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syā�� ǀ vām ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ mákṣikā ǀ arapat ǀ máde ǀ sómasya ǀ auśijáḥ ǀ huvanyati ǀyuvám ǀ dadhīcáḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsathaḥ ǀ átha ǀ śíraḥ ǀ práti ǀ vām ǀ áśvyam ǀ vadat ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you in praise of sweetness sang the honey-bee: Auśija calleth you in Soma's rapturous joy. Ye drew unto yourselves the spirit of Dadhyac, and then the horse's head uttered his words to you.
verses.wilson_translation: That honey-seeking bee also murmured your praise; the son of Us;ij invokes you to the exhilaratin of Soma; you conciliated the mind of Dadhyañc, so that, provided with the head of a horse, he taught you (the mystic science).
verses.griffith_verse: To you in praise of sweetness sang the honey-bee: Auśija calleth you in Soma's rapturous joy. Ye drew unto yourselves the spirit of Dadhyac, and then the horse's head uttered his words to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं पेदवे पुरुवारमश्विना स्पृधां श्वेतं तरुतारं दुवस्यथः ।शर्यैरभिद्युं पृतनासु दुष्टरं चर्कृत्यमिंद्रमिव चर्षणीसहं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ pedáve ǀ puru-vā́ram ǀ aśvinā ǀ spṛdhā́m ǀ śvetám ǀ tarutā́ram ǀ duvasyathaḥ ǀśáryaiḥ ǀ abhí-dyum ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ dustáram ǀ carkṛ́tyam ǀ índram-iva ǀ carṣaṇi-sáham ǁ
verses.english_translation: A horse did ye provide for Pedu, excellent, white, O ye Aśvins, conqueror of combatants, Invincible in war by arrows, seeking heaven worthy of fame, like Indra, vanquisher of men.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, you gave to Peduthe white (horse) desired by many, the breaker-through of combatants, shining, unconquerable by foes in battle, fit for every work; like Indra, the conquerer of men.
verses.griffith_verse: A horse did ye provide for Pedu, excellent, white, O ye Aśvins, conqueror of combatants, Invincible in war by arrows, seeking heaven worthy of fame, like Indra, vanquisher of men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXX. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: १२ कक्षीवान् दैर्घतमस औशिजः। अश्विनौ। (१२ दुःस्वप्ननाशनम्) ।१ गायत्री, २ ककुप्, ३ का- विराट्, ४ नष्टरूपी, ५ तनुशिरा, ६ उष्णिक्, ७ विष्टार-बृहती, ८ कृतिः, ९ विराट्, १०-१२ गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AŚVINS, what praise may win your grace? Who may be pleasing to you both?How shall the ignorant worship you? Here let the ignorant ask the means of you who know—for none beside you knoweth aught—Not of a spiritless mortal man. Such as ye: are, all-wise, we call you. Ye wise, declare to us this day accepted prayer.Loving you well your servant lauds you. Simply, ye Mighty Ones, I ask the Gods of that wondrous oblation hallowed by the mystic word.Save us from what is stronger, fiercer than ourselves. Forth go the hymn that shone in Ghoṣā Bhṛgu's like, the song wherewith the son of Pajra worships you,Like some wise minister. Hear ye the song of him who hastens speedily. O Aśvins, I am he who sang your praise.Hither, ye Lords of Splendour, hither turn your eyes. For ye were ever nigh to deal forth ample wealth, to give the wealth that ye had gathered up.As such, ye Vasus, guard us well, and keep us safely from the wicked wolf. Give us not up to any man who hateth us, nor let our milch-cows stray, whose udders give us food,Far from our homes without their calves. May they who love you gain you for their Friends. Prepare ye us for opulence with strengthening food,Prepare us for the food that floweth from our cows I have obtained the horseless car of Aśvins rich in sacrifice,And I am well content therewith. May it convey me evermore: may the light chariot pass from menTo men unto the Soma draught. It holdeth slumber in contempt. and the rich who enjoyeth not:Both vanish quickly and are lost.

verses.sanskrit: का राधद्धोत्राश्विना वां को वां जोष उभयोः ।कथा विधात्यप्रचेताः ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ rādhat ǀ hótrā ǀ aśvinā ǀ vām ǀ káḥ ǀ vām ǀ jóṣe ǀ ubháyoḥ ǀkathā́ ǀ vidhāti ǀ ápra-cetāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: AŚVINS, what praise may win your grace? Who may be pleasing to you both? How shall the ignorant worship you?
verses.wilson_translation: What praise may propitiate you,Aśvins? who may give satisfaction to you both? how may an ignorant (man) pay fitting homage?
verses.griffith_verse: AŚVINS, what praise may win your grace? Who may be pleasing to you both? How shall the ignorant worship you?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विद्वांसाविद्दुरः पृच्छेदविद्वानित्थापरो अचेताः ।नू चिन्नु मर्ते अक्रौ ॥
verses.transliteration: vidvā́ṃsau ǀ ít ǀ dúraḥ ǀ pṛcchet ǀ ávidvān ǀ itthā́ ǀ áparaḥ ǀ acetā́ḥ ǀnú ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ márte ǀ ákrau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here let the ignorant ask the means of you who know—for none beside you knoweth aught— Not of a spiritless mortal man.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus may an ignorant man inquire the means of worshipping the all-wise, for every (one) other (than the Aśvins) is unknowing; they, the unconquered, quickly(show favour) to the man (who worships them).
verses.griffith_verse: Here let the ignorant ask the means of you who know—for none beside you knoweth aught— Not of a spiritless mortal man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता विद्वांसा हवामहे वां ता नो विद्वांसा मन्म वोचेतमद्य ।प्रार्चद्दयमानो युवाकुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vidvā́ṃsā ǀ havāmahe ǀ vām ǀ tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vidvā́ṃsā ǀ mánma ǀ vocetam ǀ adyá ǀprá ǀ ārcat ǀ dáyamānaḥ ǀ yuvā́kuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such as ye: are, all-wise, we call you. Ye wise, declare to us this day accepted prayer. Loving you well your servant lauds you.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you, who know all things; may you, who are omniscient, declare to us today the praise tha tis acceptable; desirous of your presence, I reverence you, offering (oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Such as ye: are, all-wise, we call you. Ye wise, declare to us this day accepted prayer. Loving you well your servant lauds you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि पृच्छामि पाक्या न देवान्वषट्कृतस्याद्भुतस्य दस्रा ।पातं च सह्यसो युवं च रभ्यसो नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ pṛcchāmi ǀ pākyā́ ǀ ná ǀ devā́n ǀ váṣaṭ-kṛtasya ǀ adbhutásya ǀ dasrā ǀpātám ǀ ca ǀ sáhyasaḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ ca ǀ rábhyasaḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Simply, ye Mighty Ones, I ask the Gods of that wondrous oblation hallowed by the mystic word. Save us from what is stronger, fiercer than ourselves.
verses.wilson_translation: I invite not the gods immature (in wisdom), but you,Dasras; drink of the wonderful and strength-giving burnt-offering, and make us vigorous.
verses.griffith_verse: Simply, ye Mighty Ones, I ask the Gods of that wondrous oblation hallowed by the mystic word. Save us from what is stronger, fiercer than ourselves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र या घोषे भृगवाणे न शोभे यया वाचा यजति पज्रियो वां ।प्रैषयुर्न विद्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yā́ ǀ ghóṣe ǀ bhṛ́gavāṇe ǀ ná ǀ śóbhe ǀ yáyā ǀ vācā́ ǀ yájati ǀ pajriyáḥ ǀ vām ǀprá ǀ iṣa-yúḥ ǀ ná ǀ vidvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forth go the hymn that shone in Ghoṣā Bhṛgu's like, the song wherewith the son of Pajra worships you, Like some wise minister.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful is the hymn that was repeated by the son of Ghoṣā, and by Bhṛgu, and with which hymn the Aṅgirasasadore you; may the sage (kakṣīvat), desirous (of food), obtain it abundantly.
verses.griffith_verse: Forth go the hymn that shone in Ghoṣā Bhṛgu's like, the song wherewith the son of Pajra worships you, Like some wise minister.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतं गायत्रं तकवानस्याहं चिद्धि रिरेभाश्विना वां ।आक्षी शुभस्पती दन् ॥
verses.transliteration: śrutám ǀ gāyatrám ǀ tákavānasya ǀ ahám ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ rirébha ǀ aśvinā ǀ vām ǀā́ ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ dán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear ye the song of him who hastens speedily. O Aśvins, I am he who sang your praise. Hither, ye Lords of Splendour, hither turn your eyes.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear the song of the stumbling (blind man), for verily,Aśvins, I glorify you, recovering my eyes (through you), who are protectors of good works
verses.griffith_verse: Hear ye the song of him who hastens speedily. O Aśvins, I am he who sang your praise. Hither, ye Lords of Splendour, hither turn your eyes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह्यास्तं महो रन्युवं वा यन्निरततंसतं ।ता नो वसू सुगोपा स्यातं पातं नो वृकादघायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ hí ǀ ā́stam ǀ maháḥ ǀ rán ǀ yuvám ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ niḥ-átataṃsatam ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vasū íti ǀ su-gopā́ ǀ syātam ǀ pātám ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛ́kāt ǀ agha-yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For ye were ever nigh to deal forth ample wealth, to give the wealth that ye had gathered up. As such, ye Vasus, guard us well, and keep us safely from the wicked wolf.
verses.wilson_translation: You have been givers of great riches; you have again caused them to disappear; do you, who are donors of dwellings, become our preservers; protect us from the felonous robber.
verses.griffith_verse: For ye were ever nigh to deal forth ample wealth, to give the wealth that ye had gathered up. As such, ye Vasus, guard us well, and keep us safely from the wicked wolf.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा कस्मै धातमभ्यमित्रिणे नो माकुत्रा नो गृहेभ्यो धेनवो गुः ।स्तनाभुजो अशिश्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ kásmai ǀ dhātam ǀ abhí ǀ amitríṇe ǀ naḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ akútra ǀ naḥ ǀ gṛhébhyaḥ ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ guḥ ǀstana-bhújaḥ ǀ áśiśvīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us not up to any man who hateth us, nor let our milch-cows stray, whose udders give us food, Far from our homes without their calves.
verses.wilson_translation: deliver us not,Aśvins, to our enemies; never may our cows, who nourish us with their udders, stray from our houses, separated from their calves.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us not up to any man who hateth us, nor let our milch-cows stray, whose udders give us food, Far from our homes without their calves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दुहीयन्मित्रधितये युवाकु राये च नो मिमीतं वाजवत्यै ।इषे च नो मिमीतं धेनुमत्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: duhīyán ǀ mitrá-dhitaye ǀ yuvā́ku ǀ rāyé ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ mimītám ǀ vā́ja-vatyai ǀiṣé ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ mimītam ǀ dhénu-mátyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: May they who love you gain you for their Friends. Prepare ye us for opulence with strengthening food, Prepare us for the food that floweth from our cows
verses.wilson_translation: Those who adore you obtain (wealth) for the support of their friends; direct us to opulence, bestowing food; direct us to food, associated with kine.
verses.griffith_verse: May they who love you gain you for their Friends. Prepare ye us for opulence with strengthening food, Prepare us for the food that floweth from our cows
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्विनोरसनं रथमनश्वं वाजिनीवतोः ।तेनाहं भूरि चाकन ॥
verses.transliteration: aśvínoḥ ǀ asanam ǀ rátham ǀ anaśvám ǀ vājínī-vatoḥ ǀténa ǀ ahám ǀ bhū́ri ǀ cākana ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have obtained the horseless car of Aśvins rich in sacrifice, And I am well content therewith.
verses.wilson_translation: I have obtained, without horses, the car of the food-bestowing Aśvins, and expect (to gain) by it much (wealth).
verses.griffith_verse: I have obtained the horseless car of Aśvins rich in sacrifice, And I am well content therewith.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं समह मा तनूह्याते जनाँ अनु ।सोमपेयं सुखो रथः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ samaha ǀ mā ǀ tanu ǀ ūhyā́te ǀ jánān ǀ ánu ǀsoma-péyam ǀ su-kháḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May it convey me evermore: may the light chariot pass from men To men unto the Soma draught.
verses.wilson_translation: This (is he who has obtained you), wealth- bearing (car); augment (my prosperity); may the delightful car bear the Somabeverage (to the Aśvins).
verses.griffith_verse: May it convey me evermore: may the light chariot pass from men To men unto the Soma draught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध स्वप्नस्य निर्विदेऽभुंजतश्च रेवतः ।उभा ता बस्रि नश्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ svápnasya ǀ níḥ ǀ vide ǀ ábhuñjataḥ ǀ ca ǀ revátaḥ ǀubhā́ ǀ tā́ ǀ básri ǀ naśyataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: It holdeth slumber in contempt. and the rich who enjoyeth not: Both vanish quickly and are lost.
verses.wilson_translation: Now am I disdainful of sleep, and of the rich man who benefits not others, for both (the morning sleep and the selfish rich man) quickly perish.
verses.griffith_verse: It holdeth slumber in contempt. and the rich who enjoyeth not: Both vanish quickly and are lost.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १५ कक्षीवान् दैर्घतमस औशिजः। इन्द्रो विश्वे देवा वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHEN Will men's guardians hasting hear with favour the song of Aṅgiras's piouschildren?When to the people of the home he cometh he strideth to the sacrifice, the Holy. He stablished heaven; he poured forth, skilful worker, the wealth of kine, for strength, that nurtures heroes.The Mighty One his self-born host regarded, the horse's mate, the mother of the heifer. Lord of red dawns, he came victorious, daily to the Aṅgirases' former invocation.His bolt and team hath he prepared, and stablished the heaven for quadrupeds and men two-footed. In joy of this thou didst restore, for worship, the lowing company of hidden cattle.When the three-pointed one descends with onslaught he opens wide the doors that cause man trouble. Thine is that milk which thy swift-moving Parents brought down, a strengthening genial gift for conquest;When the pure treasure unto thee they offered, the milk shed from the cow who streameth nectar. There is he born. May the Swift give us rapture, and like the Sun shine forth from yonder dawning,Indu, even us who drank, whose toils are offerings, poured from the spoon, with praise, upon the altar. When the wood-pile, made of good logs, is ready, at the Sun's worship to bind fast the Bullock,Then when thou shinest forth through days of action for the Car-borne, the Swift, the Cattle-seeker. Eight steeds thou broughtest down from mighty heaven, when fighting for the well that giveth splendour,That men might press with stones the gladdening yellow, strengthened with milk, fermenting, to exalt thee. Thou hurledst forth from heaven the iron missile, brought by the Skilful, from the sling of leather,When thou, O Much-invoked, assisting Kutsa with endless deadly darts didst compass Śuṣṇa. Bolt-armed, ere darkness overtook the sunlight, thou castest at the veiling cloud thy weapon,Thou rentest, out of heaven, though firmly knotted, the might of Śuṣṇa that was thrown around him. The mighty Heaven and Earth, those bright expanses that have no wheels, joyed, Indra, at thine exploit.Vṛtra, the boar who lay amid the waters, to sleep thou sentest with thy mighty thunder. Mount Indra, lover of the men thou guardest, the well-yoked horses of the wind, best bearers.The bolt which Kāvya Uśanā erst gave thee, strong, gladdening, Vṛtra-slaying, hath he fashioned. The strong Bay Horses of the Sun thou stayedst: this Etaśa drew not the wheel, O Indra.Casting them forth beyond the ninety rivers thou dravest down into the pit the godless. Indra, preserve thou us from this affliction Thunder-armed, save us from the misery near us.Vouchsafe us affluence in chariots, founded on horses, for our food and fame and gladness. Never may this thy loving-kindness fail us; mighty in strength, may plenteous food surround us.Maghavan, make us share the foeman's cattle: may we be thy most liberal feast companions.

verses.sanskrit: कदित्था नॄँः पात्रं देवयतां श्रवद्गिरो अंगिरसां तुरण्यन् ।प्र यदानड्विश आ हर्म्यस्योरु क्रंसते अध्वरे यजत्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ itthā́ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ pā́tram ǀ deva-yatā́m ǀ śrávat ǀ gíraḥ ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ turaṇyán ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ harmyásya ǀ urú ǀ kraṃsate ǀ adhvaré ǀ yájatraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHEN Will men's guardians hasting hear with favour the song of Aṅgiras's pious children ? When to the people of the home he cometh he strideth to the sacrifice, the Holy.
verses.wilson_translation: When will Indra, the protector of men and granter of riches, listen to the praises thus (recited) of the Aṅgirasas, who are devoted to the gods? When he perceives the ministers of the master of the mansion, and is to be the object of worship in the sacrifice, he greatly exults.
verses.griffith_verse: WHEN Will men's guardians hasting hear with favour the song of Aṅgiras's pious children ? When to the people of the home he cometh he strideth to the sacrifice, the Holy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तंभीद्ध द्यां स धरुणं प्रुषायदृभुर्वाजाय द्रविणं नरो गोः ।अनु स्वजां महिषश्चक्षत व्रां मेनामश्वस्य परि मातरं गोः ॥
verses.transliteration: stámbhīt ǀ ha ǀ dyā́m ǀ sáḥ ǀ dharúṇam ǀ pruṣāyat ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ vā́jāya ǀ dráviṇam ǀ náraḥ ǀ góḥ ǀánu ǀ sva-jā́m ǀ mahiṣáḥ ǀ cakṣata ǀ vrā́m ǀ ménām ǀ áśvasya ǀ pári ǀ mātáram ǀ góḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He stablished heaven; he poured forth, skilful worker, the wealth of kine, for strength, that nurtures heroes. The Mighty One his self-born host regarded, the horse's mate, the mother of the heifer.
verses.wilson_translation: He verily upholds the heaven; he, the brilliant, the leader of the (stolen) herd, pours forth the flowing (water), for the sake of food; the mighty Indramanifests himself after his own daughter (the dawn); he made the feminine le of the horse unnaturally the mother of the cow.
verses.griffith_verse: He stablished heaven; he poured forth, skilful worker, the wealth of kine, for strength, that nurtures heroes. The Mighty One his self-born host regarded, the horse's mate, the mother of the heifer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नक्षद्धवमरुणीः पूर्व्यं राट् तुरो विशामंगिरसामनु द्यून् ।तक्षद्वज्रं नियुतं तस्तंभद्द्यां चतुष्पदे नर्याय द्विपादे ॥
verses.transliteration: nákṣat ǀ hávam ǀ aruṇī́ḥ ǀ pūrvyám ǀ rā́ṭ ǀ turáḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀtákṣat ǀ vájram ǀ ní-yutam ǀ tastámbhat ǀ dyā́m ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǀ náryāya ǀ dvi-pā́de ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of red dawns, he came victorious, daily to the Aṅgirases' former invocation. His bolt and team hath he prepared, and stablished the heaven for quadrupeds and men two-footed.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, illuminating the purple (dawn), listen to the invocation (addressed to him) of old, daily besowing wealth upon the race of Aṅgiras; he has sharpened his fatal shaft; he has supported the heaven for the good of men, of quadrupeds, andbipeds.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of red dawns, he came victorious, daily to the Aṅgirases' former invocation. His bolt and team hath he prepared, and stablished the heaven for quadrupeds and men two-footed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य मदे स्वर्यं दा ऋतायापीवृतमुस्रियाणामनीकं ।यद्ध प्रसर्गे त्रिककुम्निवर्तदप द्रुहो मानुषस्य दुरो वः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ máde ǀ svaryám ǀ dāḥ ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ ápi-vṛtam ǀ usríyāṇām ǀ ánīkam ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ pra-sárge ǀ tri-kakúp ǀ ni-vártat ǀ ápa ǀ drúhaḥ ǀ mā́nuṣasya ǀ dúraḥ ǀ varíti vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In joy of this thou didst restore, for worship, the lowing company of hidden cattle. When the three-pointed one descends with onslaught he opens wide the doors that cause man trouble.
verses.wilson_translation: In the exhilaration of the Soma, you have restored the celebrated herd of cattle, hidden (in the cave), for the sake of sacrifice, (to the Aṅgirasas); when,Indra, the threefold crest engages in combat, he opens the doors of the tyrannical descendants of Manu
verses.griffith_verse: In joy of this thou didst restore, for worship, the lowing company of hidden cattle. When the three-pointed one descends with onslaught he opens wide the doors that cause man trouble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं पयो यत्पितरावनीतां राधः सुरेतस्तुरणे भुरण्यू ।शुचि यत्ते रेक्ण आयजंत सबर्दुघायाः पय उस्रियायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ páyaḥ ǀ yát ǀ pitárau ǀ ánītām ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ su-rétaḥ ǀ turáṇe ǀ bhuraṇyū́ íti ǀśúci ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ áyajanta ǀ sabaḥ-dúghāyāḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ usríyāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine is that milk which thy swift-moving Parents brought down, a strengthening genial gift for conquest; When the pure treasure unto thee they offered, the milk shed from the cow who streameth nectar.
verses.wilson_translation: When your parents, (heaven and earth), theprotectors (of the world), brought the nutritious and invigorating oblation to you, who are quick in act, and when they offered you the pure and precious milk of the cow.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine is that milk which thy swift-moving Parents brought down, a strengthening genial gift for conquest; When the pure treasure unto thee they offered, the milk shed from the cow who streameth nectar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध प्र जज्ञे तरणिर्ममत्तु प्र रोच्यस्या उषसो न सूरः ।इंदुर्येभिराष्ट स्वेदुहव्यैः स्रुवेण सिंचंजरणाभि धाम ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ prá ǀ jajñe ǀ taráṇiḥ ǀ mamattu ǀ prá ǀ roci ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sū́raḥ ǀínduḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ ā́ṣṭa ǀ svá-íduhavyaiḥ ǀ sruvéṇa ǀ siñcán ǀ jaráṇā ǀ abhí ǀ dhā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: There is he born. May the Swift give us rapture, and like the Sun shine forth from yonder dawning, Indu, even us who drank, whose toils are offerings, poured from the spoon, with praise, upon the altar.
verses.wilson_translation: Now is Indramanifested; may he, the over-comer (of his foes), grant us happiness,he, who shines brightly, like the sun of this dawn; may the excellent Soma, being sprinklled upon the plural ceof sacrifice with a ladle, (exhilarate us), by whom, presenting the oblations we had prepared, it was imbibed.
verses.griffith_verse: There is he born. May the Swift give us rapture, and like the Sun shine forth from yonder dawning, Indu, even us who drank, whose toils are offerings, poured from the spoon, with praise, upon the altar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्विध्मा यद्वनधितिरपस्यात्सूरो अध्वरे परि रोधना गोः ।यद्ध प्रभासि कृत्व्याँ अनु द्यूननर्विशे पश्विषे तुराय ॥
verses.transliteration: su-idhmā́ ǀ yát ǀ vaná-dhitiḥ ǀ apasyā́t ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ pári ǀ ródhanā ǀ góḥ ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ pra-bhā́si ǀ kṛ́tvyān ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ ánarviśe ǀ paśu-íṣe ǀ turā́ya ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the wood-pile, made of good logs, is ready, at the Sun's worship to bind fast the Bullock, Then when thou shinest forth through days of action for the Car-borne, the Swift, the Cattle-seeker.
verses.wilson_translation: When the bright-edged hatchet is ready for its work, the directing priest is able to have the victim bound in the sacrifice; when Indra, you shine upon the days that are appropriated to sacred rites, then (success attends) upon the man who goes with his cart (for fuel), the driver (of cattle), or the active (shepherd).
verses.griffith_verse: When the wood-pile, made of good logs, is ready, at the Sun's worship to bind fast the Bullock, Then when thou shinest forth through days of action for the Car-borne, the Swift, the Cattle-seeker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अष्टा महो दिव आदो हरी इह द्युम्नासाहमभि योधान उत्सं ।हरिं यत्ते मंदिनं दुक्षन्वृधे गोरभसमद्रिभिर्वाताप्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: aṣṭā́ ǀ maháḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́daḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ ihá ǀ dyumna-sáham ǀ abhí ǀ yodhānáḥ ǀ útsam ǀhárim ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ mandínam ǀ dhukṣán ǀ vṛdhé ǀ gó-rabhasam ǀ ádri-bhiḥ ǀ vātā́pyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eight steeds thou broughtest down from mighty heaven, when fighting for the well that giveth splendour, That men might press with stones the gladdening yellow, strengthened with milk, fermenting, to exalt thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Send hither your horses, the quaffers of the exhilarating libation; overcome, warrior, the adversary plural ndering us of our treasure; when they express with stones, for the increase (of your strength), the delightful, exhilarating, invigorating (Soma), to be overtaken by you, who are swifter than the wind.
verses.griffith_verse: Eight steeds thou broughtest down from mighty heaven, when fighting for the well that giveth splendour, That men might press with stones the gladdening yellow, strengthened with milk, fermenting, to exalt thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमायसं प्रति वर्तयो गोर्दिवो अश्मानमुपनीतमृभ्वा ।कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वंछुष्णमनंतैः परियासि वधैः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ āyasám ǀ práti ǀ vartayaḥ ǀ góḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ áśmānam ǀ úpa-nītam ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀkútsāya ǀ yátra ǀ puru-hūta ǀ vanván ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ anantáiḥ ǀ pari-yā́si ǀ vadháiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hurledst forth from heaven the iron missile, brought by the Skilful, from the sling of leather, When thou, O Much-invoked, assisting Kutsa with endless deadly darts didst compass Śuṣṇa.
verses.wilson_translation: You did hurl your metal bolt upon the quick-moving (asura), the swift destroyer of foes, that was brought (to you) byṚbhufrom heaven; when you, who are worshipped by many, strikingŚuṣṇa, for the sake of Kutsa, did encompass him with numberless fatal (weapons).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hurledst forth from heaven the iron missile, brought by the Skilful, from the sling of leather, When thou, O Much-invoked, assisting Kutsa with endless deadly darts didst compass Śuṣṇa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरा यत्सूरस्तमसो अपीतेस्तमद्रिवः फलिगं हेतिमस्य ।शुष्णस्य चित्परिहितं यदोजो दिवस्परि सुग्रथितं तदादः ॥
verses.transliteration: purā́ ǀ yát ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ támasaḥ ǀ ápi-iteḥ ǀ tám ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ phali-gám ǀ hetím ǀ asya ǀśúṣṇasya ǀ cit ǀ pári-hitam ǀ yát ǀ ójaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ sú-grathitam ǀ tát ǀ ā́ ǀ adarítyadaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bolt-armed, ere darkness overtook the sunlight, thou castest at the veiling cloud thy weapon, Thou rentest, out of heaven, though firmly knotted, the might of Śuṣṇa that was thrown around him.
verses.wilson_translation: When the sun (had emerged) from the struggle with darkness, you did break, wielder of the thunderbolt, the cloud that had been his annoyance, and did under the well-fastened covering in whichŚuṣṇahad enveloped him.
verses.griffith_verse: Bolt-armed, ere darkness overtook the sunlight, thou castest at the veiling cloud thy weapon, Thou rentest, out of heaven, though firmly knotted, the might of Śuṣṇa that was thrown around him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनु त्वा मही पाजसी अचक्रे द्यावाक्षामा मदतामिंद्र कर्मन् ।त्वं वृत्रमाशयानं सिरासु महो वज्रेण सिष्वपो वराहुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ tvā ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ pā́jasī íti ǀ acakré íti ǀ dyā́vākṣā́mā ǀ madatām ǀ indra ǀ kárman ǀtvám ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ā-śáyānam ǀ sirā́su ǀ maháḥ ǀ vájreṇa ǀ sisvapaḥ ǀ varā́hum ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mighty Heaven and Earth, those bright expanses that have no wheels, joyed, Indra, at thine exploit. Vṛtra, the boar who lay amid the waters, to sleep thou sentest with thy mighty thunder.
verses.wilson_translation: Then the vast, powerful, and immoveable earth and heaven animated you,Indra, to glorious needs, and you did hurl down into the waters, with your mightythunderbolt, the everywhere-spreading and destroying Vṛtra.
verses.griffith_verse: The mighty Heaven and Earth, those bright expanses that have no wheels, joyed, Indra, at thine exploit. Vṛtra, the boar who lay amid the waters, to sleep thou sentest with thy mighty thunder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमिंद्र नर्यो याँ अवो नॄंतिष्ठा वातस्य सुयुजो वहिष्ठान् ।यं ते काव्य उशना मंदिनं दाद्वृत्रहणं पार्यं ततक्ष वज्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ indra ǀ náryaḥ ǀ yā́n ǀ ávaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ vā́tasya ǀ su-yújaḥ ǀ váhiṣṭhān ǀyám ǀ te ǀ kāvyáḥ ǀ uśánā ǀ mandínam ǀ dā́t ǀ vṛtra-hánam ǀ pā́ryam ǀ tatakṣa ǀ vájram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mount Indra, lover of the men thou guardest, the well-yoked horses of the wind, best bearers. The bolt which Kāvya Uśanā erst gave thee, strong, gladdening, Vṛtra-slaying, hath he fashioned.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, friend of man, mount the horses whom you cherish, who are fleet as the wind, are easily yoked, and who bear (theri burden) well; you have sharpened the foe-destroying thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra, which inspiring (weapon)Uśanas, the son of Kavi, gave you.
verses.griffith_verse: Mount Indra, lover of the men thou guardest, the well-yoked horses of the wind, best bearers. The bolt which Kāvya Uśanā erst gave thee, strong, gladdening, Vṛtra-slaying, hath he fashioned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं सूरो हरितो रामयो नॄन्भरच्चक्रमेतशो नायमिंद्र ।प्रास्य पारं नवतिं नाव्यानामपि कर्तमवर्तयोऽयज्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ harítaḥ ǀ ramayaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ bhárat ǀ cakrám ǀ étaśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ayám ǀ indra ǀpra-ásya ǀ pārám ǀ navatím ǀ nāvyā́nām ǀ ápi ǀ kartám ǀ avartayaḥ ǀ áyajyūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: The strong Bay Horses of the Sun thou stayedst: this Etaśa drew not the wheel, O Indra. Casting them forth beyond the ninety rivers thou dravest down into the pit the godless.
verses.wilson_translation: Stop,Sūra, your yellow horses, for this Etaśa,Indra, drags the wheel; having driven those who offer no sacrifices to the opposite bank of the ninety rivers, you compel them (to do) what is to be done.
verses.griffith_verse: The strong Bay Horses of the Sun thou stayedst: this Etaśa drew not the wheel, O Indra. Casting them forth beyond the ninety rivers thou dravest down into the pit the godless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो अस्या इंद्र दुर्हणायाः पाहि वज्रिवो दुरितादभीके ।प्र नो वाजान्रथ्यो अश्वबुध्यानिषे यंधि श्रवसे सूनृतायै ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ duḥ-hánāyāḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀ duḥ-itā́t ǀ abhī́ke ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́jān ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ áśva-budhyān ǀ iṣé ǀ yandhi ǀ śrávase ǀ sūnṛ́tāyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, preserve thou us from this affliction Thunder-armed, save us from the misery near us. Vouchsafe us affluence in chariots, founded on horses, for our food and fame and gladness.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, preserve us from this (poverty), that is so difficult to be destroyed, and from misfortune in war; grant us riches, conspicuous for chariots, remarkable for horses, for the sake of food, of fame, and of truth.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, preserve thou us from this affliction Thunder-armed, save us from the misery near us. Vouchsafe us affluence in chariots, founded on horses, for our food and fame and gladness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा सा ते अस्मत्सुमतिर्वि दसद्वाजप्रमहः समिषो वरंत ।आ नो भज मघवन्गोष्वर्यो मंहिष्ठास्ते सधमादः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ sā́ ǀ te ǀ asmát ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ ví ǀ dasat ǀ vā́ja-pramahaḥ ǀ sám ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ varanta ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhaja ǀ magha-van ǀ góṣu ǀ aryáḥ ǀ máṃhiṣṭhāḥ ǀ te ǀ sadha-mā́daḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never may this thy loving-kindness fail us; mighty in strength, may plenteous food surround us. Maghavan, make us share the foeman's cattle: may we be thy most liberal feast companions.
verses.wilson_translation: Famous for affluence,Indra, never may your favour be withdrawn from us; may food ever sustain us; opulent Maghavan, make us possessors of cattle, and may we, most assiduous in your adoration, be happy, together (with our families).
verses.griffith_verse: Never may this thy loving-kindness fail us; mighty in strength, may plenteous food surround us. Maghavan, make us share the foeman's cattle: may we be thy most liberal feast companions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXII Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १५ कक्षीवान् दैर्घतमस औशिजः। विश्वे देवाः । त्रिष्टुप्,- ५-६ विराड् रूपा।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SAY, bringing sacrifice to bounteous Rudra, This juice for drink to you whose wrath is fleeting!With Dyaus the Asura's Heroes I have lauded the Maruts as with prayer to Earth and Heaven. Strong to exalt the early invocation are Night and Dawn who show with varied aspect.The Barren clothes her in wide-woven raiment, and fair Morn shines with Sūrya's golden splendour. Cheer us the Roamer round, who strikes at morning, the Wind delight us, pourer forth of waters!Sharpen our wits, O Parvata and Indra. May all the Gods vouchsafe to us this favour. And Auśija shall call for me that famous Pair who enjoy and drink, who come to brighten.Set ye the Offspring of the Floods before you; both Mothers of the Living One who beameth. For you shall Auśija call him who thunders, as, to win Arjuna's assent, cried Ghoṣā.I will invoke, that Pūṣan may be bounteous to you, the rich munificence of Agni. Hear, Mitra-Varuṇa, these mine invocations, hear them from all men in the hall of worship.Giver of famous gifts, kind hearer, Sindhu who gives fair fields, listen with all his waters! Praised, Mitra, Varuṇa! is your gift, a hundred cows to the Pṛkṣayāmas and the Pajra.Presented by car-famous Priyaratha, supplying nourishment, they came directly. Praised is the gift of him the very wealthy: may we enjoy it, men with hero children:His who hath many gifts to give the Pajras, a chief who makes me rich in cars and horses. The folk, O Mitra-Varuṇa, who hate you, who sinfully hating pour you no libations,Lay in their hearts, themselves, a wasting sickness, whereas the righteous gaineth all by worship. That man, most puissant, wondrously urged onward, famed among heroes, liberal in giving,Moveth a warrior, evermore undaunted in all encounters even with the mighty. Come to the man's, the sacrificer's calling: hear, Kings of Immortality, joy-givers!While ye who speed through clouds decree your bounty largely, for fame, to him the chariot rider. Vigour will we bestow on that adorer whose tenfold draught we come to taste, so spake they.May all in whom rest splendour and great riches obtain refreshment in these sacrifices. We will rejoice to drink the tenfold present when the twicefive come bearing sacred viands.What can he do whose steeds and reins are choicest? These, the all-potent, urge brave men to conquest. The sea and all the Deities shall give us him with the golden ear and neck bejewelled.Dawns, hasting to the praises of the pious, be pleased with us, both offerers and singers. Four youthful sons of Maśarśāra vex me, three, of the king, the conquering Ayavasa.Now like the Sun, O Varuṇa and Mitra, your car hath shone, long-shaped and reined with splendour.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वः पांतं रघुमन्यवोऽंधो यज्ञं रुद्राय मीळ्हुषे भरध्वं ।दिवो अस्तोष्यसुरस्य वीरैरिषुध्येव मरुतो रोदस्योः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pā́ntam ǀ raghu-manyavaḥ ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ mīḷhúṣe ǀ bharadhvam ǀdiváḥ ǀ astoṣi ǀ ásurasya ǀ vīráiḥ ǀ iṣudhyā́-iva ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ródasyoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SAY, bringing sacrifice to bounteous Rudra, This juice for drink to you whose wrath is fleeting! With Dyaus the Asura's Heroes I have lauded the Maruts as with prayer to Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Present, mild-tempered (priests), the sacrificial viands which you have prepared, to there warm-showering Rudra. I praise him who, with his heroid (followers) as (with shafts) from a quiver, expelled (theasuras) from heaven; and (I praise) the Maruts, (who abide) between heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: SAY, bringing sacrifice to bounteous Rudra, This juice for drink to you whose wrath is fleeting! With Dyaus the Asura's Heroes I have lauded the Maruts as with prayer to Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पत्नीव पूर्वहूतिं वावृधध्या उषासानक्ता पुरुधा विदाने ।स्तरीर्नात्कं व्युतं वसाना सूर्यस्य श्रिया सुदृशी हिरण्यैः ॥
verses.transliteration: pátnī-iva ǀ pūrvá-hūtim ǀ vavṛdhádhyai ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ purudhā́ ǀ vídāne íti ǀstarī́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ átkam ǀ ví-utam ǀ vásānā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ śriyā́ ǀ su-dṛ́śī ǀ híraṇyaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong to exalt the early invocation are Night and Dawn who show with varied aspect. The Barren clothes her in wide-woven raiment, and fair Morn shines with Sūrya's golden splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: Animated by our diversified praise, hasten, Morning and Night, to attend to our first invocation, as a wife (to the first call of her husband); and may the--Dawn, beautiful with the lustre of the (rising) Sun, and robbing like the Sun (her) vast expanse with golden rays, (come to our early rite).
verses.griffith_verse: Strong to exalt the early invocation are Night and Dawn who show with varied aspect. The Barren clothes her in wide-woven raiment, and fair Morn shines with Sūrya's golden splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ममत्तु नः परिज्मा वसर्हा ममत्तु वातो अपां वृषण्वान् ।शिशीतमिंद्रापर्वता युवं नस्तन्नो विश्वे वरिवस्यंतु देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: mamáttu ǀ naḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ vasarhā́ ǀ mamáttu ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇ-vān ǀśiśītám ǀ indrāparvatā ǀ yuvám ǀ naḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ varivasyantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cheer us the Roamer round, who strikes at morning, the Wind delight us, pourer forth of waters! Sharpen our wits, O Parvata and Indra. May all the Gods vouchsafe to us this favour.
verses.wilson_translation: May the circumambient divinity, the wearer of various forms, grant us delight; may the wind, the shedder of rain, grant us delight; do you,Indraand Parvata, sharpen our (intellects), and may all the gods show us favour.
verses.griffith_verse: Cheer us the Roamer round, who strikes at morning, the Wind delight us, pourer forth of waters! Sharpen our wits, O Parvata and Indra. May all the Gods vouchsafe to us this favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्या मे यशसा श्वेतनायै व्यंता पांतौशिजो हुवध्यै ।प्र वो नपातमपां कृणुध्वं प्र मातरा रास्पिनस्यायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tyā́ ǀ me ǀ yaśásā ǀ śvetanā́yai ǀ vyántā ǀ pā́ntā ǀ auśijáḥ ǀ huvádhyai ǀprá ǀ vaḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ apā́m ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ prá ǀ mātárā ǀ rāspinásya ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: And Auśija shall call for me that famous Pair who enjoy and drink, who come to brighten. Set ye the Offspring of the Floods before you; both Mothers of the Living One who beameth.
verses.wilson_translation: Whenever I, the son of Uśij, worship with my offerings (of food) those two (Aśvins) who eat and drink (of oblations and libations) at (the season) of the world-whitening (dawn); do you, Priests, glorify the grandson of the waters (Agni), and render (the divinities of the day and night) the mothers (as it were) of the man who repeats their praise.
verses.griffith_verse: And Auśija shall call for me that famous Pair who enjoy and drink, who come to brighten. Set ye the Offspring of the Floods before you; both Mothers of the Living One who beameth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो रुवण्युमौशिजो हुवध्यै घोषेव शंसमर्जुनस्य नंशे ।प्र वः पूष्णे दावन आँ अच्छा वोचेय वसुतातिमग्नेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ruvaṇyúm ǀ auśijáḥ ǀ huvádhyai ǀ ghóṣā-iva ǀ śáṃsam ǀ árjunasya ǀ náṃśe ǀprá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pūṣṇé ǀ dāváne ǀ ā́ ǀ áccha ǀ voceya ǀ vasú-tātim ǀ agnéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For you shall Auśija call him who thunders, as, to win Arjuna's assent, cried Ghoṣā. I will invoke, that Pūṣan may be bounteous to you, the rich munificence of Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: I, the son of Uśij, address to you (Aśvins) audible praises, in like manner as Ghoṣāpraised you for the removal of her white-tinted (skin); I glorify (gods) the bountiful Pūṣan(associated) with you, and I proclaim the munificence of Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: For you shall Auśija call him who thunders, as, to win Arjuna's assent, cried Ghoṣā. I will invoke, that Pūṣan may be bounteous to you, the rich munificence of Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमोत श्रुतं सदने विश्वतः सीं ।श्रोतु नः श्रोतुरातिः सुश्रोतुः सुक्षेत्रा सिंधुरद्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrutám ǀ me ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ hávā ǀ imā́ ǀ utá ǀ śrutam ǀ sádane ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ sīm ǀśrótu ǀ naḥ ǀ śrótu-rātiḥ ǀ su-śrótuḥ ǀ su-kṣétrā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ at-bhíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear, Mitra-Varuṇa, these mine invocations, hear them from all men in the hall of worship. Giver of famous gifts, kind hearer, Sindhu who gives fair fields, listen with all his waters!
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, hear these my invocations, and moreover listen to those (that are) everywhere (uttered) in the chamber of sacrifice; and may Sindhu, the renowned bestower of wealth, hear us, (fertilizing our) broad fields with water.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear, Mitra-Varuṇa, these mine invocations, hear them from all men in the hall of worship. Giver of famous gifts, kind hearer, Sindhu who gives fair fields, listen with all his waters!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तुषे सा वां वरुण मित्र रातिर्गवां शता पृक्षयामेषु पज्रे ।श्रुतरथे प्रियरथे दधानाः सद्यः पुष्टिं निरुंधानासो अग्मन् ॥
verses.transliteration: stuṣé ǀ sā́ ǀ vām ǀ varuṇa ǀ mitra ǀ rātíḥ ǀ gávām ǀ śatā́ ǀ pṛkṣá-yāmeṣu ǀ pajré ǀśrutá-rathe ǀ priyá-rathe ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ puṣṭím ǀ ni-rundhānā́saḥ ǀ agman ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised, Mitra, Varuṇa! is your gift, a hundred cows to the Pṛkṣayāmas and the Pajra. Presented by car-famous Priyaratha, supplying nourishment, they came directly.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise you,Mitraand Varuṇa, for your gift of numerous cattle to the Pajra, and (from those praises) may abundant food (proceed). May (the gods), bestowing nourishment on me, come quickly unimpeded, (each) in his famous and favourite car.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised, Mitra, Varuṇa! is your gift, a hundred cows to the Pṛkṣayāmas and the Pajra. Presented by car-famous Priyaratha, supplying nourishment, they came directly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य स्तुषे महिमघस्य राधः सचा सनेम नहुषः सुवीराः ।जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ stuṣe ǀ máhi-maghasya ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ sácā ǀ sanema ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǀjánaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pajrébhyaḥ ǀ vājínī-vān ǀ áśva-vataḥ ǀ rathínaḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ sūríḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised is the gift of him the very wealthy: may we enjoy it, men with hero children: His who hath many gifts to give the Pajras, a chief who makes me rich in cars and horses.
verses.wilson_translation: I laud the treasures of that opulent (assemblyof the gods); may we, men who (are blessed) with excellent descendants, partake of them together; the assembly conferring upon the Pajras abundant food, has been my benefactor, and has made me the master of horses and chariots.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised is the gift of him the very wealthy: may we enjoy it, men with hero children: His who hath many gifts to give the Pajras, a chief who makes me rich in cars and horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जनो यो मित्रावरुणावभिध्रुगपो न वां सुनोत्यक्ष्णयाध्रुक् ।स्वयं स यक्ष्मं हृदये नि धत्त आप यदीं होत्राभिर्ऋतावा ॥
verses.transliteration: jánaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇau ǀ abhi-dhrúk ǀ apáḥ ǀ ná ǀ vām ǀ sunóti ǀ akṣṇayā-dhrúk ǀsvayám ǀ sáḥ ǀ yákṣmam ǀ hṛ́daye ǀ ní ǀ dhatte ǀ ā́pa ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ hótrābhiḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The folk, O Mitra-Varuṇa, who hate you, who sinfully hating pour you no libations, Lay in their hearts, themselves, a wasting sickness, whereas the righteous gaineth all by worship.
verses.wilson_translation: The mman who does you wrong,Mitraand Varuṇa, who injures you in any way, who does not present you with oblations, contracts for himself sickness in his heart; but he who, performing worship, (celebrates it) with praises.
verses.griffith_verse: The folk, O Mitra-Varuṇa, who hate you, who sinfully hating pour you no libations, Lay in their hearts, themselves, a wasting sickness, whereas the righteous gaineth all by worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः ।विसृष्टरातिर्याति बाळ्हसृत्वा विश्वासु पृत्सु सदमिच्छूरः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ dáṃ-sujūtaḥ ǀ śárdhaḥ-taraḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ gūrtá-śravāḥ ǀvísṛṣṭa-rātiḥ ǀ yāti ǀ bāḷha-sṛ́tvā ǀ víśvāsu ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ śū́raḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That man, most puissant, wondrously urged onward, famed among heroes, liberal in giving, Moveth a warrior, evermore undaunted in all encounters even with the mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: He, borne by well-trained horses, endowed with surpassing strength, renowned above men, munificent in gifts, moves a hero, ever undaunted in all combats, (even) against mightymen.
verses.griffith_verse: That man, most puissant, wondrously urged onward, famed among heroes, liberal in giving, Moveth a warrior, evermore undaunted in all encounters even with the mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध ग्मंता नहुषो हवं सूरेः श्रोता राजानो अमृतस्य मंद्राः ।नभोजुवो यन्निरवस्य राधः प्रशस्तये महिना रथवते ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ gmánta ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ hávam ǀ sūréḥ ǀ śróta ǀ rājānaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ mandrāḥ ǀnabhaḥ-júvaḥ ǀ yát ǀ niravásya ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ prá-śastaye ǀ mahinā́ ǀ rátha-vate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to the man's, the sacrificer's calling: hear, Kings of Immortality, joy-givers! While ye who speed through clouds decree your bounty largely, for fame, to him the chariot rider.
verses.wilson_translation: Royal bestowers of delight, listen to the invocation of (your) undying worshipper, and then come hither, that you who traverse the sky may be propitiated by the greatness of the (sacrificial) wealth presented to you by the sacrificer, who acknowledges no other protector.
verses.griffith_verse: Come to the man's, the sacrificer's calling: hear, Kings of Immortality, joy-givers! While ye who speed through clouds decree your bounty largely, for fame, to him the chariot rider.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतं शर्धं धाम यस्य सूरेरित्यवोचन्दशतयस्य नंशे ।द्युम्नानि येषु वसुताती रारन्विश्वे सन्वंतु प्रभृथेषु वाजं ॥
