verses.transliteration: etám ǀ śárdham ǀ dhāma ǀ yásya ǀ sūréḥ ǀ íti ǀ avocan ǀ dáśa-tayasya ǀ náṃśe ǀdyumnā́ni ǀ yéṣu ǀ vasú-tātiḥ ǀ rarán ǀ víśve ǀ sanvantu ǀ pra-bhṛthéṣu ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vigour will we bestow on that adorer whose tenfold draught we come to taste, so spake they. May all in whom rest splendour and great riches obtain refreshment in these sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have declared: we confer present vigour upon the worshipper (who invokes us) to partake of the (ibation). May all (the gods) in whom splendour and riches abound, bestow (abundant) food at (solemn) sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Vigour will we bestow on that adorer whose tenfold draught we come to taste, so spake they. May all in whom rest splendour and great riches obtain refreshment in these sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंदामहे दशतयस्य धासेर्द्विर्यत्पंच बिभ्रतो यंत्यन्ना ।किमिष्टाश्व इष्टरश्मिरेत ईशानासस्तरुष ऋंजते नॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: mándāmahe ǀ dáśa-tayasya ǀ dhāséḥ ǀ dvíḥ ǀ yát ǀ páñca ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ yánti ǀ ánnā ǀkím ǀ iṣṭá-aśvaḥ ǀ iṣṭá-raśmiḥ ǀ eté ǀ īśānā́saḥ ǀ táruṣaḥ ǀ ṛñjate ǀ nṝ́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: We will rejoice to drink the tenfold present when the twicefive come bearing sacred viands. What can he do whose steeds and reins are choicest? These, the all-potent, urge brave men to conquest.
verses.wilson_translation: We rejoice tha tfor the satisfaction of the ten (organs of sense), the (priests) bearing the twice five (ladles of) sacrificial food, proceed (to the altar). What can Iṣṭaśva, (what can)Iṣṭaraśmi, (what can) those who are now lords of the earth, achieve (with respect) to the leaders of men, the conquerors of their foes?
verses.griffith_verse: We will rejoice to drink the tenfold present when the twicefive come bearing sacred viands. What can he do whose steeds and reins are choicest? These, the all-potent, urge brave men to conquest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यकर्णं मणिग्रीवमर्णस्तन्नो विश्वे वरिवस्यंतु देवाः ।अर्यो गिरः सद्य आ जग्मुषीरोस्राश्चाकंतूभयेष्वस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-karṇam ǀ maṇi-grīvam ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ tám ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ varivasyantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǀaryáḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jagmúṣīḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ cākantu ǀ ubháyeṣu ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sea and all the Deities shall give us him with the golden ear and neck bejewelled. Dawns, hasting to the praises of the pious, be pleased with us, both offerers and singers.
verses.wilson_translation: May all the gods favour us with a person n decorated with golden earrings and jewel necklace; may the venerable (company of the deities) be propitiated by the praises issuing (from the mouth of the worshipper); may our offerings be acceptable to them, and (may they be plural ased) with both (our praises and offerings).
verses.griffith_verse: The sea and all the Deities shall give us him with the golden ear and neck bejewelled. Dawns, hasting to the praises of the pious, be pleased with us, both offerers and singers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारो मा मशर्शारस्य शिश्वस्त्रयो राज्ञ आयवसस्य जिष्णोः ।रथो वां मित्रावरुणा दीर्घाप्साः स्यूमगभस्तिः सूरो नाद्यौत् ॥
verses.transliteration: catvā́raḥ ǀ mā ǀ maśarśā́rasya ǀ śíśvaḥ ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ ā́yavasasya ǀ jiṣṇóḥ ǀráthaḥ ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ dīrghá-apsāḥ ǀ syū́ma-gabhastiḥ ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ adyaut ǁ
verses.english_translation: Four youthful sons of Maśarśāra vex me, three, of the king, the conquering Ayavasa. Now like the Sun, O Varuṇa and Mitra, your car hath shone, long-shaped and reined with splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: The four (silly) sons of Maśar'śāra, the three of the victorious monarchĀyavasa(annoy) me. Let your spacious and bright-rayed chariot,Mitraand Varuṇa, blaze (before them) like the sun (filling them with fear).
verses.griffith_verse: Four youthful sons of Maśarśāra vex me, three, of the king, the conquering Ayavasa. Now like the Sun, O Varuṇa and Mitra, your car hath shone, long-shaped and reined with splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXIII. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Dakṣiṇā's broad chariot hath been harnessed: this car the Gods Immortal have ascended.Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness. She before all the living world hath wakened, the Lofty One who wins and gathers treasure.Revived and ever young on high she glances. Dawn hath come first unto our morning worship. If, Dawn, thou Goddess nobly born, thou dealest fortune this day to all the race of mortals,May Savitar the God, Friend of the homestead, declare before the Sun that we are sinless. Showing her wonted form each day that passeth, spreading the light she visiteth each dwelling.Eager for conquest, with bright sheen she cometh. Her portion is the best of goodly treasures. Sister of Varuṇa, sister of Bhaga, first among all sing forth, O joyous Morning.Weak be the strength of him who worketh evil: may we subdue him with our car the guerdon. Let our glad hymns and holy thoughts rise upward, for the flames brightly burning have ascended.The far-refulgent Mornings make apparent the lovely treasures which the darkness covered. The one departeth and the other cometh: unlike in hue day's, halves march on successive.One hides the gloom of the surrounding Parents. Dawn on her shining chariot is resplendent. The same in form to-day, the same tomorrow, they still keep Varuṇa's eternal statute.Blameless, in turn they traverse thirty regions, and dart across the spirit in a moment. She who hath knowledge Of the first day's nature is born refulgent white from out the darkness.The Maiden breaketh not the law of Order, day by day coming to the place appointed. In pride of beauty like a maid thou goest, O Goddess, to the God who longs to win thee,And smiling youthful, as thou shinest brightly, before him thou discoverest thy bosom. Fair as a bride embellished by her mother thou showest forth thy form that all may see it.Blessed art thou O Dawn. Shine yet more widely. No other Dawns have reached what thou attainest. Rich in kine, horses, and all goodly treasures, in constant operation with the sunbeams,The Dawns depart and come again assuming their wonted forms that promise happy fortune. Obedient to the rein of Law Eternal give us each thought that more and more shall bless us.Shine thou on us to-day, Dawn, swift to listen. With us be riches and with chiefs who worship.

verses.sanskrit: पृथू रथो दक्षिणाया अयोज्यैनं देवासो अमृतासो अस्थुः ।कृष्णादुदस्थादर्या विहायाश्चिकित्संती मानुषाय क्षयाय ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛthúḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀ ayoji ǀ ā́ ǀ enam ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ amṛ́tāsaḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀkṛṣṇā́t ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǀ aryā́ ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ cíkitsantī ǀ mā́nuṣāya ǀ kṣáyāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Dakṣiṇā's broad chariot hath been harnessed: this car the Gods Immortal have ascended. Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The spacious chariot of the graceful (dawn) has been harnessed; the immortal gods have ascended it; the noble and all-pervading Uṣā has risen up from the darkness, bringing health to human habitations.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Dakṣiṇā's broad chariot hath been harnessed: this car the Gods Immortal have ascended. Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वा विश्वस्माद्भुवनादबोधि जयंती वाजं बृहती सनुत्री ।उच्चा व्यख्यद्युवतिः पुनर्भूरोषा अगन्प्रथमा पूर्वहूतौ ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́rvā ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ bhúvanāt ǀ abodhi ǀ jáyantī ǀ vā́jam ǀ bṛhatī́ ǀ sánutrī ǀuccā́ ǀ ví ǀ akhyat ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ punaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ agan ǀ prathamā́ ǀ pūrvá-hūtau ǁ
verses.english_translation: She before all the living world hath wakened, the Lofty One who wins and gathers treasure. Revived and ever young on high she glances. Dawn hath come first unto our morning worship.
verses.wilson_translation: First of all the world is she awake, triumphing over transitory (darkness); the mighty, the giver (of light) from on high, she beholds (all things); ever youthful, ever reviving, she comes first to the invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: She before all the living world hath wakened, the Lofty One who wins and gathers treasure. Revived and ever young on high she glances. Dawn hath come first unto our morning worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदद्य भागं विभजासि नृभ्य उषो देवि मर्त्यत्रा सुजाते ।देवो नो अत्र सविता दमूना अनागसो वोचति सूर्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ adyá ǀ bhāgám ǀ vi-bhájāsi ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ devi ǀ martya-trā́ ǀ su-jāte ǀdeváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ savitā́ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀ vocati ǀ sū́ryāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: If, Dawn, thou Goddess nobly born, thou dealest fortune this day to all the race of mortals, May Savitar the God, Friend of the homestead, declare before the Sun that we are sinless.
verses.wilson_translation: Well-born and divine Uṣā, who are the protectress of mortals; whatever share (of light) you apportion today to men, may the radiant Savitābedisposed (to confirm) the gift, and declar us free from sin; so that (he) the sun (may come to our sacrificial hall).
verses.griffith_verse: If, Dawn, thou Goddess nobly born, thou dealest fortune this day to all the race of mortals, May Savitar the God, Friend of the homestead, declare before the Sun that we are sinless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गृहंगृहमहना यात्यच्छा दिवेदिवे अधि नामा दधाना ।सिषासंती द्योतना शश्वदागादग्रमग्रमिद्भजते वसूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: gṛhám-gṛham ǀ ahanā́ ǀ yāti ǀ áccha ǀ divé-dive ǀ ádhi ǀ nā́ma ǀ dádhānā ǀsísāsantī ǀ dyotanā́ ǀ śáśvat ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ ágram-agram ǀ ít ǀ bhajate ǀ vásūnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Showing her wonted form each day that passeth, spreading the light she visiteth each dwelling. Eager for conquest, with bright sheen she cometh. Her portion is the best of goodly treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: Ahana, charged with downward-bending (light), goes daily from house to house; she comes, perpetually diffusing light, and desirous of bestowing (benefits), and accepts the choicest portions of (the sacrificial) treasures.
verses.griffith_verse: Showing her wonted form each day that passeth, spreading the light she visiteth each dwelling. Eager for conquest, with bright sheen she cometh. Her portion is the best of goodly treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व ।पश्चा स दघ्या यो अघस्य धाता जयेम तं दक्षिणया रथेन ॥
verses.transliteration: bhágasya ǀ svásā ǀ váruṇasya ǀ jāmíḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ sūnṛte ǀ prathamā́ ǀ jarasva ǀpaścā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ daghyāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ aghásya ǀ dhātā́ ǀ jáyema ǀ tám ǀ dákṣiṇayā ǀ ráthena ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sister of Varuṇa, sister of Bhaga, first among all sing forth, O joyous Morning. Weak be the strength of him who worketh evil: may we subdue him with our car the guerdon.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣā, endowed with truth, who are the sister of Bhaga, the sister of Varuṇa, be you hymned first (of the gods); then let the worker of iniquity depart, for we shall overcome him with our chariot, through your assistance.
verses.griffith_verse: Sister of Varuṇa, sister of Bhaga, first among all sing forth, O joyous Morning. Weak be the strength of him who worketh evil: may we subdue him with our car the guerdon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीरतां सूनृता उत्पुरंधीरुदग्नयः शुशुचानासो अस्थुः ।स्पार्हा वसूनि तमसापगूळ्हाविष्कृण्वंत्युषसो विभातीः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īratām ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ út ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ út ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ śuśucānā́saḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀspārhā́ ǀ vásūni ǀ támasā ǀ ápa-gūḷhā ǀ āvíḥ ǀ kṛṇvanti ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let our glad hymns and holy thoughts rise upward, for the flames brightly burning have ascended. The far-refulgent Mornings make apparent the lovely treasures which the darkness covered.
verses.wilson_translation: Let words of truth be spoken; let works of wisdom (be performed); let the blazing fires rise up, so that the many radiant Uṣā may make manifest the desirable treasures hidden by the darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Let our glad hymns and holy thoughts rise upward, for the flames brightly burning have ascended. The far-refulgent Mornings make apparent the lovely treasures which the darkness covered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपान्यदेत्यभ्यन्यदेति विषुरूपे अहनी सं चरेते ।परिक्षितोस्तमो अन्या गुहाकरद्यौदुषाः शोशुचता रथेन ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ anyát ǀ éti ǀ abhí ǀ anyát ǀ eti ǀ víṣurūpe íti víṣu-rūpe ǀ áhanī íti ǀ sám ǀ carete íti ǀpari-kṣítoḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ anyā́ ǀ gúhā ǀ akaḥ ǀ ádyaut ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ śóśucatā ǀ ráthena ǁ
verses.english_translation: The one departeth and the other cometh: unlike in hue day's, halves march on successive. One hides the gloom of the surrounding Parents. Dawn on her shining chariot is resplendent.
verses.wilson_translation: The twofold day proceeds unseparated; one (part going) forward, one backward; one of these two alternating (periods) effects the concealment (of things); the dawn illumines them with her radiant chariot.
verses.griffith_verse: The one departeth and the other cometh: unlike in hue day's, halves march on successive. One hides the gloom of the surrounding Parents. Dawn on her shining chariot is resplendent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सदृशीरद्य सदृशीरिदु श्वो दीर्घं सचंते वरुणस्य धाम ।अनवद्यास्त्रिंशतं योजनान्येकैका क्रतुं परि यंति सद्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ adyá ǀ sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śváḥ ǀ dīrghám ǀ sacante ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǀanavadyā́ḥ ǀ triṃśátam ǀ yójanāni ǀ ékā-ekā ǀ krátum ǀ pári ǀ yanti ǀ sadyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The same in form to-day, the same tomorrow, they still keep Varuṇa's eternal statute. Blameless, in turn they traverse thirty regions, and dart across the spirit in a moment.
verses.wilson_translation: The same today, the same tomorrow, the irreproachable (dawn) precede the distant course of Varuṇaby thirtyyojanas, and each in succession revolves in its (appointed) office.
verses.griffith_verse: The same in form to-day, the same tomorrow, they still keep Varuṇa's eternal statute. Blameless, in turn they traverse thirty regions, and dart across the spirit in a moment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जानत्यह्नः प्रथमस्य नाम शुक्रा कृष्णादजनिष्ट श्वितीची ।ऋतस्य योषा न मिनाति धामाहरहर्निष्कृतमाचरंती ॥
verses.transliteration: jānatī́ ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ prathamásya ǀ nā́ma ǀ śukrā́ ǀ kṛṣṇā́t ǀ ajaniṣṭa ǀ śvitīcī́ ǀṛtásya ǀ yóṣā ǀ ná ǀ mināti ǀ dhā́ma ǀ áhaḥ-ahaḥ ǀ niḥ-kṛtám ǀ ā-cárantī ǁ
verses.english_translation: She who hath knowledge Of the first day's nature is born refulgent white from out the darkness. The Maiden breaketh not the law of Order, day by day coming to the place appointed.
verses.wilson_translation: The self-illumined dawn, announcing the declination of the first (portion) of the day, is born white-shining out of the gloom; cleansing (with the radiance) of the sun, she impairs not his splendour, but daily adds embellishment (to his lustre).
verses.griffith_verse: She who hath knowledge Of the first day's nature is born refulgent white from out the darkness. The Maiden breaketh not the law of Order, day by day coming to the place appointed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कन्येव तन्वा शाशदानाँ एषि देवि देवमियक्षमाणं ।संस्मयमाना युवतिः पुरस्तादाविर्वक्षांसि कृणुषे विभाती ॥
verses.transliteration: kanyā́-iva ǀ tanvā́ ǀ śā́śadānā ǀ éṣi ǀ devi ǀ devám ǀ íyakṣamāṇam ǀsam-smáyamānā ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ āvíḥ ǀ vákṣāṃsi ǀ kṛṇuṣe ǀ vi-bhātī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In pride of beauty like a maid thou goest, O Goddess, to the God who longs to win thee, And smiling youthful, as thou shinest brightly, before him thou discoverest thy bosom.
verses.wilson_translation: Goddess, manifest in person n like a maiden, you go to the resplendent and munificent (sun), and, like a youthful bride (beforeher husband), you uncover, smiling, yor bosom in his presence.
verses.griffith_verse: In pride of beauty like a maid thou goest, O Goddess, to the God who longs to win thee, And smiling youthful, as thou shinest brightly, before him thou discoverest thy bosom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुसंकाशा मातृमृष्टेव योषाविस्तन्वं कृणुषे दृशे कं ।भद्रा त्वमुषो वितरं व्युच्छ न तत्ते अन्या उषसो नशंत ॥
verses.transliteration: su-saṃkāśā́ ǀ mātṛ́mṛṣṭā-iva ǀ yóṣā ǀ āvíḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ kṛṇuṣe ǀ dṛśé ǀ kám ǀbhadrā́ ǀ tvám ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ vi-tarám ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǀ ná ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ anyā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ naśanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fair as a bride embellished by her mother thou showest forth thy form that all may see it. Blessed art thou O Dawn. Shine yet more widely. No other Dawns have reached what thou attainest.
verses.wilson_translation: Radiant as a bride decorated by her mother, you willingly display your person n to the view. Do you, auspicious Uṣā, remove the investing (gloom), for, other dawns than you do not disperse it.
verses.griffith_verse: Fair as a bride embellished by her mother thou showest forth thy form that all may see it. Blessed art thou O Dawn. Shine yet more widely. No other Dawns have reached what thou attainest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्विश्ववारा यतमाना रश्मिभिः सूर्यस्य ।परा च यंति पुनरा च यंति भद्रा नाम वहमाना उषासः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśva-vatīḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ viśvá-vārāḥ ǀ yátamānāḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀpárā ǀ ca ǀ yánti ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ yanti ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ nā́ma ǀ váhamānāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich in kine, horses, and all goodly treasures, in constant operation with the sunbeams, The Dawns depart and come again assuming their wonted forms that promise happy fortune.
verses.wilson_translation: Possessed of horses, possessed of cows, existing through all time, vying with the rays of the sun (in dissipating darkness), auspicious dawns, sending down benefits (on mankind), pass away and again return.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich in kine, horses, and all goodly treasures, in constant operation with the sunbeams, The Dawns depart and come again assuming their wonted forms that promise happy fortune.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य रश्मिमनुयच्छमाना भद्रंभद्रं क्रतुमस्मासु धेहि ।उषो नो अद्य सुहवा व्युच्छास्मासु रायो मघवत्सु च स्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ raśmím ǀ anu-yácchamānā ǀ bhadrám-bhadram ǀ krátum ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhehi ǀúṣaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ su-hávā ǀ ví ǀ uccha ǀ asmā́su ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ maghávat-su ǀ ca ǀ syuríti syuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Obedient to the rein of Law Eternal give us each thought that more and more shall bless us. Shine thou on us to-day, Dawn, swift to listen. With us be riches and with chiefs who worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Co-operating with the rays of the true (sun), confirm in us every propitious act; earnestly invoked byus today, disperse, Uṣā, (the darkness), that wealth may devolve upon us, (already) affluent (in sacrificial treasures).
verses.griffith_verse: Obedient to the rein of Law Eternal give us each thought that more and more shall bless us. Shine thou on us to-day, Dawn, swift to listen. With us be riches and with chiefs who worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXIV. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Dawn refulgent when the fire is kindled, and the Sun rising, far diffuse their brightness.Savitar, God, hath sent us forth to labour, each quadruped, each biped, to be active. Not interrupting heavenly ordinances, although she minisheth human generations.The last of endless morns that have departed, the first of those that come, Dawn brightly shineth. There in the eastern region she, Heaven's Daughter, arrayed in garments all of light, appeareth.Truly she followeth the path of Order, nor faileth, knowing well, the heavenly quarters. Near is she seen, as ’twere the Bright One's bosom: she showeth sweet things like a new song-singer.She cometh like a fly awaking sleepers, of all returning dames most true and constant. There in the east half of the watery region the Mother of the Cows hath shown her ensign.Wider and wider still she spreadeth onward, and filleth full the laps of both heir Parents. She, verily, exceeding vast to look on debarreth from her light nor kin nor stranger.Proud of her spotless form she, brightly shining, turneth not from the high nor from the humble. She seeketh men, as she who hath no brother, mounting her car, as ’twere to gather riches.Dawn, like a loving matron for her husband, smiling and well attired, unmasks her beauty. The Sister quitteth, for the elder Sister, her place, and having looked on her departeth.She decks her beauty, shining forth with sunbeams, like women trooping to the festal meeting. To all these Sisters who ere now have vanished a later one each day in course succeedeth.So, like the past, with days of happy fortune, may the new Dawns shine forth on us with riches. Rouse up, O Wealthy One, the liberal givers; let niggard traffickers sleep on unwakened:Shine richly, Wealthy One, on those who worship, richly, glad.Dawn while wasting, on the singer. This young Maid from the east hath shone upon us; she harnesseth her team of bright red oxen.She will beam forth, the light will hasten hither, and Agni will be present in each dwelling. As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning.Yea, to the liberal mortal who remaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest. Praised through my prayer be ye who should be lauded. Ye have increased our wealth, ye Dawns who love us.Goddesses, may we win by your good favour wealth to be told by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.sanskrit: उषा उच्छंती समिधाने अग्ना उद्यन्त्सूर्य उर्विया ज्योतिरश्रेत् ।देवो नो अत्र सविता न्वर्थं प्रासावीद्द्विपत्प्र चतुष्पदित्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchántī ǀ sam-idhāné ǀ agnáu ǀ ut-yán ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ aśret ǀdeváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ savitā́ ǀ nú ǀ ártham ǀ prá ǀ asāvīt ǀ dvi-pát ǀ prá ǀ cátuḥ-pat ǀ ityái ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Dawn refulgent when the fire is kindled, and the Sun rising, far diffuse their brightness. Savitar, God, hath sent us forth to labour, each quadruped, each biped, to be active.
verses.wilson_translation: When the (sacred) fire is kindled, Uṣā sheds abundant light, dispersing (the darkness) like the rising sun; may the divine Savitābestow upon usfor our use, wealth of both bipeds and quadrupeds.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Dawn refulgent when the fire is kindled, and the Sun rising, far diffuse their brightness. Savitar, God, hath sent us forth to labour, each quadruped, each biped, to be active.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि ।ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनामायतीनां प्रथमोषा व्यद्यौत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áminatī ǀ dáivyāni ǀ vratā́ni ǀ pra-minatī́ ǀ manuṣyā́ ǀ yugā́ni ǀīyúṣīṇām ǀ upamā́ ǀ śáśvatīnām ǀ ā-yatīnā́m ǀ prathamā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ adyaut ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not interrupting heavenly ordinances, although she minisheth human generations. The last of endless morns that have departed, the first of those that come, Dawn brightly shineth.
verses.wilson_translation: Unimpeding divine rites, although wearing away the ages of mankind, the dawn shines the similitude of the (mornings) that have passed, or that are to be forever, the first of those that are to come.
verses.griffith_verse: Not interrupting heavenly ordinances, although she minisheth human generations. The last of endless morns that have departed, the first of those that come, Dawn brightly shineth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि ज्योतिर्वसाना समना पुरस्तात् ।ऋतस्य पंथामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ práti ǀ adarśi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ vásānā ǀ samanā́ ǀ purástāt ǀṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǀ ánu ǀ eti ǀ sādhú ǀ prajānatī́-iva ǀ ná ǀ díśaḥ ǀ mināti ǁ
verses.english_translation: There in the eastern region she, Heaven's Daughter, arrayed in garments all of light, appeareth. Truly she followeth the path of Order, nor faileth, knowing well, the heavenly quarters.
verses.wilson_translation: She, the daughter of heaven, is beheld in the east, gracious and arrayed in light; she travels steadily along the path of the sun, as if cognizant (of his plural asure), and damages not the quarters (of the horizon).
verses.griffith_verse: There in the eastern region she, Heaven's Daughter, arrayed in garments all of light, appeareth. Truly she followeth the path of Order, nor faileth, knowing well, the heavenly quarters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपो अदर्शि शुंध्युवो न वक्षो नोधा इवाविरकृत प्रियाणि ।अद्मसन्न ससतो बोधयंती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: úpo íti ǀ adarśi ǀ śundhyúvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vákṣaḥ ǀ nodhā́ḥ-iva ǀ āvíḥ ǀ akṛta ǀ priyā́ṇi ǀadma-sát ǀ ná ǀ sasatáḥ ǀ bodháyantī ǀ śaśvat-tamā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ā-īyúṣīṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Near is she seen, as ’twere the Bright One's bosom: she showeth sweet things like a new song-singer. She cometh like a fly awaking sleepers, of all returning dames most true and constant.
verses.wilson_translation: She is beheld nigh athand, (radiant) as the breast of the illuminator (the sun); and, like Nodhas, has made manifest many plural asing (objects); like a matron she awakens (her) sleeping (children), and of all (feminine les who are) stirring betimes, she, the most unvarying, repeatedly appears.
verses.griffith_verse: Near is she seen, as ’twere the Bright One's bosom: she showeth sweet things like a new song-singer. She cometh like a fly awaking sleepers, of all returning dames most true and constant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो अप्त्यस्य गवां जनित्र्यकृत प्र केतुं ।व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीय ओभा पृणंती पित्रोरुपस्था ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́rve ǀ árdhe ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ aptyásya ǀ gávām ǀ jánitrī ǀ akṛta ǀ prá ǀ ketúm ǀví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prathate ǀ vi-tarám ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ubhā́ ǀ pṛṇántī ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthā ǁ
verses.english_translation: There in the east half of the watery region the Mother of the Cows hath shown her ensign. Wider and wider still she spreadeth onward, and filleth full the laps of both heir Parents.
verses.wilson_translation: Born in the eastern quarter of the spacious firmament, she displays a banner of rays of light. plural ced on the lap of both parents (heaven and earth), filling them (with radiance), she enjoys vast and wide-spread renown.
verses.griffith_verse: There in the east half of the watery region the Mother of the Cows hath shown her ensign. Wider and wider still she spreadeth onward, and filleth full the laps of both heir Parents.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवेदेषा पुरुतमा दृशे कं नाजामिं न परि वृणक्ति जामिं ।अरेपसा तन्वा शाशदाना नार्भादीषते न महो विभाती ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ ít ǀ eṣā́ ǀ puru-támā ǀ dṛśé ǀ kám ǀ ná ǀ ájāmim ǀ ná ǀ pári ǀ vṛṇakti ǀ jāmím ǀarepásā ǀ tanvā́ ǀ śā́śadānā ǀ ná ǀ árbhāt ǀ ī́ṣate ǀ ná ǀ maháḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: She, verily, exceeding vast to look on debarreth from her light nor kin nor stranger. Proud of her spotless form she, brightly shining, turneth not from the high nor from the humble.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily she, the wide-expanded Uṣā, neglects not (to give) the joy of sight to those of her own or of a different nature; visible in her faultless person n, and brightly shining, she passes not by the littleror the great.
verses.griffith_verse: She, verily, exceeding vast to look on debarreth from her light nor kin nor stranger. Proud of her spotless form she, brightly shining, turneth not from the high nor from the humble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभ्रातेव पुंस एति प्रतीची गर्तारुगिव सनये धनानां ।जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासा उषा हस्रेव नि रिणीते अप्सः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhrātā́-iva ǀ puṃsáḥ ǀ eti ǀ pratīcī́ ǀ garta-ārúgiva ǀ sanáye ǀ dhánānām ǀjāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ uśatī́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ hasrā́-iva ǀ ní ǀ riṇīte ǀ ápsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: She seeketh men, as she who hath no brother, mounting her car, as ’twere to gather riches. Dawn, like a loving matron for her husband, smiling and well attired, unmasks her beauty.
verses.wilson_translation: She goes to the west, as (a woman who has) no brother (repairs) to hermale(relatives); and like one ascending the hall (of justice) for the recovery of property, (she mounts in the sky to claim her lustre); and like a wife desirous to plural ase her husband, Uṣā puts on becoming attire, and smiling as it were, displays her charms.
verses.griffith_verse: She seeketh men, as she who hath no brother, mounting her car, as ’twere to gather riches. Dawn, like a loving matron for her husband, smiling and well attired, unmasks her beauty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वसा स्वस्रे ज्यायस्यै योनिमारैगपैत्यस्याः प्रतिचक्ष्येव ।व्युच्छंती रश्मिभिः सूर्यस्यांज्यंक्ते समनगा इव व्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: svásā ǀ svásre ǀ jyā́yasyai ǀ yónim ǀ araik ǀ ápa ǀ eti ǀ asyāḥ ǀ praticákṣya-iva ǀvi-ucchántī ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ añjí ǀ aṅkte ǀ samanagā́ḥ-iva ǀ vrā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Sister quitteth, for the elder Sister, her place, and having looked on her departeth. She decks her beauty, shining forth with sunbeams, like women trooping to the festal meeting.
verses.wilson_translation: The sister (night) has prepared a birth-plural ce for her elder sister (day), and having amde it known to her, departs. Uṣā, dispersing the darkness with the rays of the sun, illumines the world, like congregated lightnings.
verses.griffith_verse: The Sister quitteth, for the elder Sister, her place, and having looked on her departeth. She decks her beauty, shining forth with sunbeams, like women trooping to the festal meeting.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आसां पूर्वासामहसु स्वसॄणामपरा पूर्वामभ्येति पश्चात् ।ताः प्रत्नवन्नव्यसीर्नूनमस्मे रेवदुच्छंतु सुदिना उषासः ॥
verses.transliteration: āsā́m ǀ pū́rvāsām ǀ áha-su ǀ svásṝṇām ǀ áparā ǀ pū́rvām ǀ abhí ǀ eti ǀ paścā́t ǀtā́ḥ ǀ pratna-vát ǀ návyasīḥ ǀ nūnám ǀ asmé íti ǀ revát ǀ ucchantu ǀ su-dínāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To all these Sisters who ere now have vanished a later one each day in course succeedeth. So, like the past, with days of happy fortune, may the new Dawns shine forth on us with riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Of all these sisters who have gone before, a successor daily follows the one that has preceded. So may new dawns, like the old, bringing fortunate days, shine upon us blessed with affluence.
verses.griffith_verse: To all these Sisters who ere now have vanished a later one each day in course succeedeth. So, like the past, with days of happy fortune, may the new Dawns shine forth on us with riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र बोधयोषः पृणतो मघोन्यबुध्यमानाः पणयः ससंतु ।रेवदुच्छ मघवद्भ्यो मघोनि रेवत्स्तोत्रे सूनृते जारयंती ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ bodhaya ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ pṛṇatáḥ ǀ maghoni ǀ ábudhyamānāḥ ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ sasantu ǀrevát ǀ uccha ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ maghoni ǀ revát ǀ stotré ǀ sūnṛte ǀ jaráyantī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rouse up, O Wealthy One, the liberal givers; let niggard traffickers sleep on unwakened: Shine richly, Wealthy One, on those who worship, richly, glad. Dawn while wasting, on the singer.
verses.wilson_translation: Awaken, wealth-abounding, Uṣā, those whose delight (in holy offerings); let the (niggard) traders, reluctant wake (for such a purpose), sleep on. Arise, opulent Uṣā, bearing wealth to the liberal (worshipper); speaker of truth, who are the waster away (of living creatures), arise, bearing wealth to him who praises you.
verses.griffith_verse: Rouse up, O Wealthy One, the liberal givers; let niggard traffickers sleep on unwakened: Shine richly, Wealthy One, on those who worship, richly, glad. Dawn while wasting, on the singer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवेयमश्वैद्युवतिः पुरस्ताद्युंक्ते गवामरुणानामनीकं ।वि नूनमुच्छादसति प्र केतुर्गृहंगृहमुप तिष्ठाते अग्निः ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ iyám ǀ aśvait ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ yuṅkté ǀ gávām ǀ aruṇā́nām ǀ ánīkam ǀví ǀ nūnám ǀ ucchāt ǀ ásati ǀ prá ǀ ketúḥ ǀ gṛhám-gṛham ǀ úpa ǀ tiṣṭhāte ǀ agníḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This young Maid from the east hath shone upon us; she harnesseth her team of bright red oxen. She will beam forth, the light will hasten hither, and Agni will be present in each dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: This youthful Uṣā, approached from the east; she harnesses her team of purple oxen. Assuredly she will disperse the darkness, a manifest sign (of day) in the firmament; the (sacred) fire is kindled in every dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: This young Maid from the east hath shone upon us; she harnesseth her team of bright red oxen. She will beam forth, the light will hasten hither, and Agni will be present in each dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्ते वयश्चिद्वसतेरपप्तन्नरश्च ये पितुभाजो व्युष्टौ ।अमा सते वहसि भूरि वाममुषो देवि दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ te ǀ váyaḥ ǀ cit ǀ vasatéḥ ǀ apaptan ǀ náraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǀ pitu-bhā́jaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀamā́ ǀ saté ǀ vahasi ǀ bhū́ri ǀ vāmám ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ devi ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning. Yea, to the liberal mortal who remaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest.
verses.wilson_translation: At your dawning, (Uṣā), the various birds rise up from their nests, and men who have to earn their bread (quit their homes). You bring, divine (Uṣā), much wealth to the liberal mortal who is present in the chamber (of sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning. Yea, to the liberal mortal who remaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्तोढ्वं स्तोम्या ब्रह्मणा मेऽवीवृधध्वमुशतीरुषासः ।युष्माकं देवीरवसा सनेम सहस्रिणं च शतिनं च वाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ástoḍhvam ǀ stomyāḥ ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ me ǀ ávīvṛdhadhvam ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ uṣasaḥ ǀyuṣmā́kam ǀ devīḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ sanema ǀ sahasríṇam ǀ ca ǀ śatínam ǀ ca ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised through my prayer be ye who should be lauded. Ye have increased our wealth, ye Dawns who love us. Goddesses, may we win by your good favour wealth to be told by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.wilson_translation: Praiseworthy Uṣās, be glorified by this (my hymn); graciously disposed towards us, augment (our prosperity); and may we obtain, goddesses, through your favour, wealth; a hundred and a thousand fold.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised through my prayer be ye who should be lauded. Ye have increased our wealth, ye Dawns who love us. Goddesses, may we win by your good favour wealth to be told by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXV. Svanaya.
hymns.anukramani: ७ कक्षीवान् दैर्घतमस औशिजः। स्वनयस्य दानस्तुतिः। त्रिष्टुप्, ४-५ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COMING at early morn he gives his treasure; the prudent one receives and entertains him.Thereby increasing still his life and offspring, he comes with brave sons to abundant riches. Rich shall he be in gold and kine and horses. Indra bestows on him great vital power,Who stays thee, as thou comest, with his treasure, like game caught in the net, O early comer. Longing, I came this morning to the pious, the son of sacrifice, with car wealth-laden.Give him to drink juice of the stalk that gladdens; prosper with pleasant hymns the Lord of Heroes. Health-bringing streams, as milch-cows, flow to profit him who hath worshipped, him who now will worship.To him who freely gives and fills on all sides full streams of fatness flow and make him famous. On the high ridge of heaven he stands exalted, yea, to the Gods he goes, the liberal giver.The streams, the waters flow for him with fatness: to him this guerdon ever yields abundance. For those who give rich meeds are all these splendours, for those who give rich meeds suns shine in heaven.The givers of rich meeds are made immortal; the givers of rich fees prolong their lifetime. Let not the liberal sink to sin and sorrow, never decay the pious chiefs who worship!Let every man besides be their protection, and let affliction fall upon the niggard.

verses.sanskrit: प्राता रत्नं प्रातरित्वा दधाति तं चिकित्वान्प्रतिगृह्या नि धत्ते ।तेन प्रजां वर्धयमान आयू रायस्पोषेण सचते सुवीरः ॥
verses.transliteration: prātáríti ǀ rátnam ǀ prātaḥ-ítvā ǀ dadhāti ǀ tám ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ prati-gṛ́hya ǀ ní ǀ dhatte ǀténa ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ vardháyamānaḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣeṇa ǀ sacate ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: COMING at early morn he gives his treasure; the prudent one receives and entertains him. Thereby increasing still his life and offspring, he comes with brave sons to abundant riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Having come in the early morning, (Svanaya) presents precious (wealth), knowing it (to be worthy of acceptance); and having, (therefore), accepted it, (Kakṣīvat) brings it (to his father); wherewith the parent of excellent sons, maintaining his progeny, passes his life in the enjoyment of affluence.
verses.griffith_verse: COMING at early morn he gives his treasure; the prudent one receives and entertains him. Thereby increasing still his life and offspring, he comes with brave sons to abundant riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मै वय इंद्रो दधाति ।यस्त्वायंतं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥
verses.transliteration: su-gúḥ ǀ asat ǀ su-hiraṇyáḥ ǀ su-áśvaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ asmai ǀ váyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ dadhāti ǀyáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ ā-yántam ǀ vásunā ǀ prātaḥ-itvaḥ ǀ mukṣī́jayā-iva ǀ pádim ǀ ut-sinā́ti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich shall he be in gold and kine and horses. Indra bestows on him great vital power, Who stays thee, as thou comest, with his treasure, like game caught in the net, O early comer.
verses.wilson_translation: May he (the Rājā) be rich in kine, in gold, in horses; may Indragrant abundant food to him who delays you, returning home in the early morning, by costly gifts, as (a hunter arrests the) wandering (animals) by his snares.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich shall he be in gold and kine and horses. Indra bestows on him great vital power, Who stays thee, as thou comest, with his treasure, like game caught in the net, O early comer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आयमद्य सुकृतं प्रातरिच्छन्निष्टेः पुत्रं वसुमता रथेन ।अंशोः सुतं पायय मत्सरस्य क्षयद्वीरं वर्धय सूनृताभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́yam ǀ adyá ǀ su-kṛ́tam ǀ prātáḥ ǀ icchán ǀ iṣṭéḥ ǀ putrám ǀ vásu-matā ǀ ráthena ǀaṃśóḥ ǀ sutám ǀ pāyaya ǀ matsarásya ǀ kṣayát-vīram ǀ vardhaya ǀ sūnṛ́tābhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Longing, I came this morning to the pious, the son of sacrifice, with car wealth-laden. Give him to drink juice of the stalk that gladdens; prosper with pleasant hymns the Lord of Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous (of again beholding you), I have this day obtained you, who have done in the morning a good deed; the performer of a sacrifice with a wealth-laden car, refresh yoursel fwiththe effused libation of the exhilarating (Soma), and augment with sincere prayers (the prosperity) of the chief of the flourishing race.
verses.griffith_verse: Longing, I came this morning to the pious, the son of sacrifice, with car wealth-laden. Give him to drink juice of the stalk that gladdens; prosper with pleasant hymns the Lord of Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप क्षरंति सिंधवो मयो���ुव ईजानं च यक्ष्यमाणं च धेनवः ।पृणंतं च पपुरिं च श्रवस्यवो घृतस्य धारा उप यंति विश्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ kṣaranti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀ ījānám ǀ ca ǀ yakṣyámāṇam ǀ ca ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀpṛṇántam ǀ ca ǀ pápurim ǀ ca ǀ śravasyávaḥ ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yanti ǀ viśvátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Health-bringing streams, as milch-cows, flow to profit him who hath worshipped, him who now will worship. To him who freely gives and fills on all sides full streams of fatness flow and make him famous.
verses.wilson_translation: The copiously-yielding and joy-conferringkine, distil (their milk) for the celebration of the (Soma) sacrifice; and for him who has undertaken its celebration; the nutritious streams of butter coverage from every quarter towards him, who both propitiates (his progenitors), and benefits (mankind).
verses.griffith_verse: Health-bringing streams, as milch-cows, flow to profit him who hath worshipped, him who now will worship. To him who freely gives and fills on all sides full streams of fatness flow and make him famous.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाकस्य पृष्ठे अधि तिष्ठति श्रितो यः पृणाति स ह देवेषु गच्छति ।तस्मा आपो घृतमर्षंति सिंधवस्तस्मा इयं दक्षिणा पिन्वते सदा ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́kasya ǀ pṛṣṭhé ǀ ádhi ǀ tiṣṭhati ǀ śritáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pṛṇā́ti ǀ sáḥ ǀ ha ǀ devéṣu ǀ gacchati ǀtásmai ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ arṣanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ tásmai ǀ iyám ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ pinvate ǀ sádā ǁ
verses.english_translation: On the high ridge of heaven he stands exalted, yea, to the Gods he goes, the liberal giver. The streams, the waters flow for him with fatness: to him this guerdon ever yields abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: He who propitiates (the gods), gives to the gods, and sits at ease upon the summit of heaven; to him the flowing waters bear their essence; to him this fertile (earth) ever yields abundance.
verses.griffith_verse: On the high ridge of heaven he stands exalted, yea, to the Gods he goes, the liberal giver. The streams, the waters flow for him with fatness: to him this guerdon ever yields abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दक्षिणावतामिदिमानि चित्रा दक्षिणावतां दिवि सूर्यासः ।दक्षिणावंतो अमृतं भजंते दक्षिणावंतः प्र तिरंत आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: dákṣiṇā-vatām ǀ ít ǀ imā́ni ǀ citrā́ ǀ dákṣiṇā-vatām ǀ diví ǀ sū́ryāsaḥ ǀdákṣiṇā-vantaḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ bhajante ǀ dákṣiṇā-vantaḥ ǀ prá ǀ tirante ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For those who give rich meeds are all these splendours, for those who give rich meeds suns shine in heaven. The givers of rich meeds are made immortal; the givers of rich fees prolong their lifetime.
verses.wilson_translation: These wonderful (rewards) verily are for those who give (pious) donations; for the donors of (pious) gifts the suns shine in heaven; the givers of (pious) donations attain immortality; the givers of (pious) gifts prolong their (worldly) existence.
verses.griffith_verse: For those who give rich meeds are all these splendours, for those who give rich meeds suns shine in heaven. The givers of rich meeds are made immortal; the givers of rich fees prolong their lifetime.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा पृणंतो दुरितमेन आरन्मा जारिषुः सूरयः सुव्रतासः ।अन्यस्तेषां परिधिरस्तु कश्चिदपृणंतमभि सं यंतु शोकाः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ pṛṇántaḥ ǀ dúḥ-itam ǀ énaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aran ǀ mā́ ǀ jāriṣuḥ ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ su-vratā́saḥ ǀanyáḥ ǀ téṣām ǀ pari-dhíḥ ǀ astu ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ ápṛṇantam ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ yantu ǀ śókāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the liberal sink to sin and sorrow, never decay the pious chiefs who worship! Let every man besides be their protection, and let affliction fall upon the niggard.
verses.wilson_translation: May those who propitiate (the gods), never commit degrading sin; may those who praise the gods and observe holy vows, never experience decay; may some (honourable) individual ever be their defence; and may afflictions fall upon him who does not propitiate (the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Let not the liberal sink to sin and sorrow, never decay the pious chiefs who worship! Let every man besides be their protection, and let affliction fall upon the niggard.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVI. Bhāvayavya.
hymns.anukramani: ७ कक्षीवान् दैर्घतमस औशिजः। (६) स्वनयो भावयव्यः, (७) रोमशा। १-५ स्वनयो भावयव्यः, ६ रोमशा, ७ स्वनयो भावयव्यः। त्रिष्टुप्, ६-७ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH wisdom I present these lively praises of Bhāvya dweller on the bank of Sindhu;For he, unconquered King, desiring glory, hath furnished me a thousand sacrifices. A hundred necklets from the King, beseeching, a hundred gift-steeds I at once accepted;Of the lord's cows a thousand, I Kakṣīvān. His deathless glory hath he spread to heaven. Horses of dusky colour stood beside me, ten chariots, Svanaya's gift, with mares to draw them.Kine numbering sixty thousand followed after. Kakṣīvān gained them when the days were closing. Forty bay horses of the ten cars' master before a thousand lead the long procession.Reeling in joy Kakṣīvān's sons and Pajra's have grounded the coursers decked with pearly trappings. An earlier gift for you have I accepted eight cows, good milkers, and three harnessed horses,Pajras, who with your wains with your great kinsman, like troops of subjects, have been fain for glory. [Ille loquitur]. Adhaerens, arcte adhaerens, illa quae mustelae similis se abdidit, multum humorem effundens, dat mihi complexuum centum gaudia.. [Ille loquitur]. Prope, prope accede; molliter me tange. Ne putes pilos corporis mei-paucos esse: tota sum villosa sicut Gandharium ovis.

verses.sanskrit: अमंदान्त्स्तोमान्प्र भरे मनीषा सिंधावधि क्षियतो भाव्यस्य ।यो मे सहस्रममिमीत सवानतूर्तो राजा श्रव इच्छमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ámandān ǀ stómān ǀ prá ǀ bhare ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ síndhau ǀ ádhi ǀ kṣiyatáḥ ǀ bhāvyásya ǀyáḥ ǀ me ǀ sahásram ǀ ámimīta ǀ savā́n ǀ atū́rtaḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ icchámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH wisdom I present these lively praises of Bhāvya dweller on the bank of Sindhu; For he, unconquered King, desiring glory, hath furnished me a thousand sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: I repeat with a (willing) mind, the unreluctant praises of Bhavya, dwellingon th ebanks of the Sindhu; a prince of unequalled (might), desirous of renown, who has enabled me to celebrate a thousand sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH wisdom I present these lively praises of Bhāvya dweller on the bank of Sindhu; For he, unconquered King, desiring glory, hath furnished me a thousand sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं राज्ञो नाधमानस्य निष्काञ्छतमश्वान्प्रयतान्त्सद्य आदं ।शतं कक्षीवाँ असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवोऽजरमा ततान ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ nā́dhamānasya ǀ niṣkā́n ǀ śatám ǀ áśvān ǀ prá-yatān ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ā́dam ǀśatám ǀ kakṣī́vān ǀ ásurasya ǀ gónām ǀ diví ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ajáram ǀ ā́ ǀ tatāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred necklets from the King, beseeching, a hundred gift-steeds I at once accepted; Of the lord's cows a thousand, I Kakṣīvān. His deathless glory hath he spread to heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: From which genitive rous prince, soliciting (my acceptance), I,Kakṣīvat, unhesitatingly accepted a hundredniṣkas, a hundred vigorous steeds, and a hundred bulls, whereby he has spread his imperishable fame through heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: A hundred necklets from the King, beseeching, a hundred gift-steeds I at once accepted; Of the lord's cows a thousand, I Kakṣīvān. His deathless glory hath he spread to heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप मा श्यावाः स्वनयेन दत्ता वधूमंतो दश रथासो अस्थुः ।षष्टिः सहस्रमनु गव्यमागात्सनत्कक्षीवाँ अभिपित्वे अह्नां ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ mā ǀ śyāvā́ḥ ǀ svanáyena ǀ dattā́ḥ ǀ vadhū́-mantaḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ ráthāsaḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ ánu ǀ gávyam ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ sánat ǀ kakṣī́vān ǀ abhi-pitvé ǀ áhnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Horses of dusky colour stood beside me, ten chariots, Svanaya's gift, with mares to draw them. Kine numbering sixty thousand followed after. Kakṣīvān gained them when the days were closing.
verses.wilson_translation: Ten chariots drawn by bay steeds, and carrying my wives, stood near me, given meby Svanaya; and a thousand and sixty cows followed; these, after a short interval of time, did Kakṣīvatdeliver (to his father).
verses.griffith_verse: Horses of dusky colour stood beside me, ten chariots, Svanaya's gift, with mares to draw them. Kine numbering sixty thousand followed after. Kakṣīvān gained them when the days were closing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारिंशद्दशरथस्य शोणाः सहस्रस्याग्रे श्रेणिं नयंति ।मदच्युतः कृशनावतो अत्यान्कक्षीवंत उदमृक्षंत पज्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: catvāriṃśát ǀ dáśa-rathasya ǀ śóṇāḥ ǀ sahásrasya ǀ ágre ǀ śréṇim ǀ nayanti ǀmada-cyútaḥ ǀ kṛśaná-vataḥ ǀ átyān ǀ kakṣī́vantaḥ ǀ út ǀ amṛkṣanta ǀ pajrā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forty bay horses of the ten cars' master before a thousand lead the long procession. Reeling in joy Kakṣīvān's sons and Pajra's have grounded the coursers decked with pearly trappings.
verses.wilson_translation: Forty bay horses, (harnessed) to the chariots, lead the procession in front of a thousand (followers). The Pajras, the kinsmen of Kakṣīvat, rub down the high-spirited steeds, decorated with golden trappings.
verses.griffith_verse: Forty bay horses of the ten cars' master before a thousand lead the long procession. Reeling in joy Kakṣīvān's sons and Pajra's have grounded the coursers decked with pearly trappings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वामनु प्रयतिमा ददे वस्त्रीन्युक्ताँ अष्टावरिधायसो गाः ।सुबंधवो ये विश्या इव व्रा अनस्वंतः श्रव ऐषंत पज्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́rvām ǀ ánu ǀ prá-yatim ǀ ā́ ǀ dade ǀ vaḥ ǀ trī́n ǀ yuktā́n ǀ aṣṭáu ǀ arí-dhāyasaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀsu-bándhavaḥ ǀ yé ǀ viśyā́ḥ-iva ǀ vrā́ḥ ǀ ánasvantaḥ ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ áiṣanta ǀ pajrā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: An earlier gift for you have I accepted eight cows, good milkers, and three harnessed horses, Pajras, who with your wains with your great kinsman, like troops of subjects, have been fain for glory.
verses.wilson_translation: I have accepted a prior grant, (kinsmen), for you; three and eight harnessed chariots and cattle of incalculable value; may the kindred Pajras, like well-disposed relations, be desirous of acquiring renown by their abundant offerings.
verses.griffith_verse: An earlier gift for you have I accepted eight cows, good milkers, and three harnessed horses, Pajras, who with your wains with your great kinsman, like troops of subjects, have been fain for glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आगधिता परिगधिता या कशीकेव जंगहे ।ददाति मह्यं यादुरी याशूनां भोज्या शता ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́-gadhitā ǀ pári-gadhitā ǀ yā́ ǀ kaśīkā́-iva ǀ jáṅgahe ǀdádāti ǀ máhyam ǀ yā́durī ǀ yā́śūnām ǀ bhojyā́ ǀ śatā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [Ille loquitur]. Adhaerens, arcte adhaerens, illa quae mustelae similis se abdidit, multum humorem effundens, dat mihi complexuum centum gaudia.
verses.wilson_translation: She, who, when her desires are assented to, clings as tenaciously as a feminine le weasel, and who is ripe for enjoyment, yields me infinite delight.
verses.griffith_verse: [Ille loquitur]. Adhaerens, arcte adhaerens, illa quae mustelae similis se abdidit, multum humorem effundens, dat mihi complexuum centum gaudia.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपोप मे परा मृश मा मे दभ्राणि मन्यथाः ।सर्वाहमस्मि रोमशा गंधारीणामिवाविका ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa-upa ǀ me ǀ párā ǀ mṛśa ǀ mā́ ǀ me ǀ dabhrā́ṇi ǀ manyathāḥ ǀsárvā ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǀ romaśā́ ǀ gandhā́rīṇām-iva ǀ avikā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [Ille loquitur]. Prope, prope accede; molliter me tange. Ne putes pilos corporis mei-paucos esse: tota sum villosa sicut Gandharium ovis.
verses.wilson_translation: Approach me, (husband); deem me not immature; I am covered with down like a eve of the gandhārins.
verses.griffith_verse: [Ille loquitur]. Prope, prope accede; molliter me tange. Ne putes pilos corporis mei-paucos esse: tota sum villosa sicut Gandharium ovis.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVII Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI I hold as herald, the munificent, the gracious, Son of Strength, who knoweth all that live, as holy Singer, knowing all,Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected turning to the Gods,He, when the flame hath sprung forth from the holy oil, the offered fatness, longeth for it with his glow. We, sacrificing, call on thee best worshipper, the eldest of Aṅgirases, Singer, with hymns, thee, brilliant One! with singers’ hymns;Thee, wandering round as ’t were the sky, who art the invoking Priest of men,Whom, Bull with hair of flame the people must observe, the people that he speed them on. He with his shining glory blazing far and wide, he verily it is who slayeth demon foes, slayeth the demons like an axe:At whose close touch things solid shake, and what is stable yields like trees.Subduing all, he keeps his ground and flinches not, from the skilled archer flinches not. To him, as one who knows, even things solid yield: unrough fire-sticks heated hot he gives his gifts to aid. Men offer Agni gifts for aid.He deeply piercing many a thing hews it like wood with fervent glow.Even hard and solid food he crunches with his might, yea, hard and solid food with might. Here near we place the sacrificial food for him who shines forth fairer in the night than in the day, with life then stronger than by day.His life gives sure and firm defence as that one giveth to a son.The during fires enjoy things given and things not given, the during fires enjoy as food. He, roaring very loudly like the Maruts’ host, in fertile cultivated fields adorable, in desert spots adorable,Accepts and eats our offered gifts, ensign of sacrifice by desert;So let all, joying, love his path when he is glad, as men pursue a path for bliss. Even as they who sang forth hymns, addressed to heaven, the Bhṛgus with their prayer and praise invited him, the Bhṛgus rubbing, offering gifts.For radiant Agni, Lord of all these treasures, is exceeding strong.May he, the wise, accept the grateful coverings, the wise accept the coverings. Thee we invoke, the Lord of all our settled homes, common to all, the household's guardian, to enjoy, bearer of true hymns, to enjoy.Thee we invoke, the guest of men, by whose mouth, even as a sire's,All these Immortals come to gain their food of life, oblations come to Gods as food. Thou, Agni, most victorious with thy conquering strength, most Mighty One, art born for service of the Gods, like wealth for service of the Gods.Most mighty is thine ecstasy, most splendid is thy mental power.Therefore men wait upon thee, undecaying One, like vassals, undecaying One. To him the mighty, conquering with victorious strength, to Agni walking with the dawn, who sendeth kine, be sung your laud, to Agni sung;As he who with oblation comes calls him aloud in every place.Before the brands of fire he shouteth singerlike, the herald, kindler of the brands. Agni, beheld by us in nearest neighbourhood, accordant with the Gods, bring us, with gracious love, great riches with thy gracious love.Give us O Mightiest, what is great, to see and to enjoy the earth.As one of awful power, stir up heroic might for those who praise thee, Bounteous Lord!

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं होतारं मन्ये दास्वंतं वसुं सूनुं सहसो जातवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसं ।य ऊर्ध्वया स्वध्वरो देवो देवाच्या कृपा ।घृतस्य विभ्राष्टिमनु वष्टि शोचिषाजुह्वानस्य सर्पिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ hótāram ǀ manye ǀ dā́svantam ǀ vásum ǀ sūnúm ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ vípram ǀ ná ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀyá ǀ ūrdhváyā ǀ su-adhvaráḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ devā́cyā ǀ kṛpā́ ǀghṛtásya ǀ ví-bhrāṣṭim ǀ ánu ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ śocíṣā ǀ ā-júhvānasya ǀ sarpíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI I hold as herald, the munificent, the gracious, Son of Strength, who knoweth all that live, as holy Singer, knowing all, Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected turning to the Gods, He, when the flame hath sprung forth from the holy oil, the offered fatness, longeth for it with his glow.
verses.wilson_translation: I venerate Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the munificent, the giver of dwellings, the son of strength; he who knows all that exists, like a sage who is endowed with knowledge; who, the divine regenerator of sacrifices, through his lofty and reverntial devotion, covets for the gods the blaze of the liquefied butter which is offered in oblation with his flames.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI I hold as herald, the munificent, the gracious, Son of Strength, who knoweth all that live, as holy Singer, knowing all, Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected turning to the Gods, He, when the flame hath sprung forth from the holy oil, the offered fatness, longeth for it with his glow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यजिष्ठं त्वा यजमाना हुवेम ज्येष्ठमंगिरसां विप्र मन्मभिर्विप्रेभिः शुक्र मन्मभिः ।परिज्मानमिव द्यां होतारं चर्षणीनां ।शोचिष्केशं वृषणं यमिमा विशः प्रावंतु जूतये विशः ॥
verses.transliteration: yájiṣṭham ǀ tvā ǀ yájamānāḥ ǀ huvema ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ vipra ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀ víprebhiḥ ǀ śukra ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀpárijmānam-iva ǀ dyā́m ǀ hótāram ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀśocíḥ-keśam ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ yám ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ prá ǀ avantu ǀ jūtáye ǀ víśaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We, sacrificing, call on thee best worshipper, the eldest of Aṅgirases, Singer, with hymns, thee, brilliant One! with singers’ hymns; Thee, wandering round as ’t were the sky, who art the invoking Priest of men, Whom, Bull with hair of flame the people must observe, the people that he speed them on.
verses.wilson_translation: We, the instrumental tutors of the ceremony, invoke you,Agni, who are most deserving of worship, and are the eldest of the Aṅgirasas, with (acceptable) prayers; and with prayers (recited) by the priests, (we adore) you, who, like the traverser of the sky, (the sun), are the invoker (of the gods on behalf) of men, and whom, the bright-haired showeree (of blessings), many people approaching propitiate for the attainment of felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: We, sacrificing, call on thee best worshipper, the eldest of Aṅgirases, Singer, with hymns, thee, brilliant One! with singers’ hymns; Thee, wandering round as ’t were the sky, who art the invoking Priest of men, Whom, Bull with hair of flame the people must observe, the people that he speed them on.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि पुरू चिदोजसा विरुक्मता दीद्यानो भवति द्रुहंतरः परशुर्न द्रुहंतरः ।वीळु चिद्यस्य समृतौ श्रुवद्वनेव यत्स्थिरं ।निष्षहमाणो यमते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ purú ǀ cit ǀ ójasā ǀ virúkmatā ǀ dī́dyānaḥ ǀ bhávati ǀ druham-taráḥ ǀ paraśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ druham-taráḥ ǀvīḷú ǀ cit ǀ yásya ǀ sám-ṛtau ǀ śrúvat ǀ vánā-iva ǀ yát ǀ sthirám ǀniḥ-sáhamānaḥ ǀ yamate ǀ ná ǀ ayate ǀ dhanva-sáhā ǀ ná ǀ ayate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with his shining glory blazing far and wide, he verily it is who slayeth demon foes, slayeth the demons like an axe: At whose close touch things solid shake, and what is stable yields like trees. Subduing all, he keeps his ground and flinches not, from the skilled archer flinches not.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily, that Agni, far shining with brilliant vigour, is the destroyer of foes, like a hatchet that cuts down trees; whatever is most solid and stable dissolves like water at his contact; unsparing, he sports (amidst enemies), nor desists (from their destruction), like an archer who retreats not (frombattle).
verses.griffith_verse: He with his shining glory blazing far and wide, he verily it is who slayeth demon foes, slayeth the demons like an axe: At whose close touch things solid shake, and what is stable yields like trees. Subduing all, he keeps his ground and flinches not, from the skilled archer flinches not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दृळ्हा चिदस्मा अनु दुर्यथा विदे तेजिष्ठाभिररणिभिर्दाष्ट्यवसेऽग्नये दाष्ट्यवसे ।प्र यः पुरूणि गाहते तक्षद्वनेव शोचिषा ।स्थिरा चिदन्ना नि रिणात्योजसा नि स्थिराणि चिदोजसा ॥
verses.transliteration: dṛḷhā́ ǀ cit ǀ asmai ǀ ánu ǀ duḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ vidé ǀ téjiṣṭhābhiḥ ǀ aráṇi-bhiḥ ǀ dāṣṭi ǀ ávase ǀ agnáye ǀ dāṣṭi ǀ ávase ǀprá ǀ yáḥ ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ gā́hate ǀ tákṣat ǀ vánā-iva ǀ śocíṣā ǀsthirā́ ǀ cit ǀ ánnā ǀ ní ǀ riṇāti ǀ ójasā ǀ ní ǀ sthirā́ṇi ǀ cit ǀ ójasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him, as one who knows, even things solid yield: unrough fire-sticks heated hot he gives his gifts to aid. Men offer Agni gifts for aid. He deeply piercing many a thing hews it like wood with fervent glow. Even hard and solid food he crunches with his might, yea, hard and solid food with might.
verses.wilson_translation: They have presented substantial donations to him, as (they give riches) to a sage, and by resplendent means he grants us (grace) for our preservation; (the worshipper) presents (gifts) to Agnifor preservation; he who pervades the (many offerings made to him) consumes them (as rapidly) as (he consumes) forests; he matures the standing corn by his potency; he destroys whatever (things) are stationary by his potency.
verses.griffith_verse: To him, as one who knows, even things solid yield: unrough fire-sticks heated hot he gives his gifts to aid. Men offer Agni gifts for aid. He deeply piercing many a thing hews it like wood with fervent glow. Even hard and solid food he crunches with his might, yea, hard and solid food with might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमस्य पृक्षमुपरासु धीमहि नक्तं यः सुदर्शतरो दिवातरादप्रायुषे दिवातरात् ।आदस्यायुर्ग्रभणवद्वीळु शर्म न सूनवे ।भक्तमभक्तमवो व्यंतो अजरा अग्नयो व्यंतो अजराः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ asya ǀ pṛkṣám ǀ úparāsu ǀ dhīmahi ǀ náktam ǀ yáḥ ǀ sudárśa-taraḥ ǀ dívā-tarāt ǀ ápra-āyuṣe ǀ dívā-tarāt ǀā́t ǀ asya ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ grábhaṇa-vat ǀ vīḷú ǀ śárma ǀ ná ǀ sūnáve ǀbhaktám ǀ ábhaktam ǀ ávaḥ ǀ vyántaḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ vyántaḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here near we place the sacrificial food for him who shines forth fairer in the night than in the day, with life then stronger than by day. His life gives sure and firm defence as that one giveth to a son. The during fires enjoy things given and things not given, the during fires enjoy as food.
verses.wilson_translation: We plural ce near the altar the (sacrificial) food of him who is more conspicuous by night than by day; (we offer it) to him who is scarcely alive by day; hence his (sacrificial) food finds prompt acceptance, like dwelling (given by a father) to a son; these undecaying fires, (although) discriminating between the devout and the undevout, grant (both) protection, and accepting (the offerings of the pious), they are exempt from decay.
verses.griffith_verse: Here near we place the sacrificial food for him who shines forth fairer in the night than in the day, with life then stronger than by day. His life gives sure and firm defence as that one giveth to a son. The during fires enjoy things given and things not given, the during fires enjoy as food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि शर्धो न मारुतं तुविष्वणिरप्नस्वतीषूर्वरास्विष्टनिरार्तनास्विष्टनिः ।आदद्धव्यान्याददिर्यज्ञस्य केतुरर्हणा ।अध स्मास्य हर्षतो हृषीवतो विश्वे जुषंत पंथां नरः शुभे न पंथां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́rutam ǀ tuvi-svániḥ ǀ ápnasvatīṣu ǀ urvárāsu ǀ iṣṭániḥ ǀ ā́rtanāsu ǀ iṣṭániḥ ǀā́dat ǀ havyā́ni ǀ ā-dadíḥ ǀ yajñásya ǀ ketúḥ ǀ arháṇā ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ hárṣataḥ ǀ hṛ́ṣīvataḥ ǀ víśve ǀ juṣanta ǀ pánthām ǀ náraḥ ǀ śubhé ǀ ná ǀ pánthām ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, roaring very loudly like the Maruts’ host, in fertile cultivated fields adorable, in desert spots adorable, Accepts and eats our offered gifts, ensign of sacrifice by desert; So let all, joying, love his path when he is glad, as men pursue a path for bliss.
verses.wilson_translation: He roars aloud, like the roaring of the winds, amidst the sanctified and selected (rites of sacred) solemnities; he who is to be worshipped, who is to be adored (for victory) over hosts (of enemies); he, the receiver 9of oblations), the manifester of the sacrifice; he, who is deserving of veneration, devours the oblations; hence, all men for their good pursue the path of Agni, who gives plural asure (to his worshipper), being plural ased (himself), in like manner as men follow a path (that leads) to happiness.
verses.griffith_verse: He, roaring very loudly like the Maruts’ host, in fertile cultivated fields adorable, in desert spots adorable, Accepts and eats our offered gifts, ensign of sacrifice by desert; So let all, joying, love his path when he is glad, as men pursue a path for bliss.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्विता यदीं कीस्तासो अभिद्यवो नमस्यंत उपवोचंत भृगवो मथ्नंतो दाशा भृगवः ।अग्निरीशे वसूनां शुचिर्यो धर्णिरेषां ।प्रियाँ अपिधीँर्वनिषीष्ट मेधिर आ वनिषीष्ट मेधिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvitā́ ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ kīstā́saḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǀ namasyántaḥ ǀ upa-vócanta ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ mathnántaḥ ǀ dāśā́ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ īśe ǀ vásūnām ǀ śúciḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ dharṇíḥ ǀ eṣām ǀpriyā́n ǀ api-dhī́n ǀ vaniṣīṣṭa ǀ médhiraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaniṣīṣṭa ǀ médhiraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as they who sang forth hymns, addressed to heaven, the Bhṛgus with their prayer and praise invited him, the Bhṛgus rubbing, offering gifts. For radiant Agni, Lord of all these treasures, is exceeding strong. May he, the wise, accept the grateful coverings, the wise accept the coverings.
verses.wilson_translation: The descendants of Bhṛgu, celebrating him (Agni) in both his forms, glorifying him, and payig him homage, proclaim his praises; the descendants of Bhṛgu, rubbing (the flame) for the oblation. For the radiant Agni, who is the guardian of all these treasures, has power (to distribute them). Mayhe, the receier of sacrifices, partake of the agreeable (offerings) given to satiety; may he, the receiver of sacrifices, partake (of the oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Even as they who sang forth hymns, addressed to heaven, the Bhṛgus with their prayer and praise invited him, the Bhṛgus rubbing, offering gifts. For radiant Agni, Lord of all these treasures, is exceeding strong. May he, the wise, accept the grateful coverings, the wise accept the coverings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वासां त्वा विशां पतिं हवामहे सर्वासां समानं दंपतिं भुजे सत्यगिर्वाहसं भुजे ।अतिथिं मानुषाणां पितुर्न यस्यासया ।अमी च विश्वे अमृतास आ वयो हव्या देवेष्वा वयः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvāsām ǀ tvā ǀ viśā́m ǀ pátim ǀ havāmahe ǀ sárvāsām ǀ samānám ǀ dám-patim ǀ bhujé ǀ satyá-girvāhasam ǀ bhujé ǀátithim ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǀ pitúḥ ǀ ná ǀ yásya ǀ āsayā́ ǀamī́ íti ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tāsaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee we invoke, the Lord of all our settled homes, common to all, the household's guardian, to enjoy, bearer of true hymns, to enjoy. Thee we invoke, the guest of men, by whose mouth, even as a sire's, All these Immortals come to gain their food of life, oblations come to Gods as food.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you, the protector of all people, the same alike to all, the preserver of the house, to enjoy (the oblation); you, who are the wafter of our infallible prayer, to enjoy (the oblation); we invoke you, who are the guest of men, to whom all these immortals apply for their sustenance, as (a son) to a father; you, to whom the priests offer oblations amongst the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee we invoke, the Lord of all our settled homes, common to all, the household's guardian, to enjoy, bearer of true hymns, to enjoy. Thee we invoke, the guest of men, by whose mouth, even as a sire's, All these Immortals come to gain their food of life, oblations come to Gods as food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने सहसा सहंतमः शुष्मिंतमो जायसे देवतातये रयिर्न देवतातये ।शुष्मिंतमो हि ते मदो द्युम्निंतम उत क्रतुः ।अध स्मा ते परि चरंत्यजर श्रुष्टीवानो नाजर ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhan-tamaḥ ǀ śuṣmín-tamaḥ ǀ jāyase ǀ devá-tātaye ǀ rayíḥ ǀ ná ǀ devá-tātaye ǀśuṣmín-tamaḥ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ dyumnín-tamaḥ ǀ utá ǀ krátuḥ ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ te ǀ pári ǀ caranti ǀ ajara ǀ śruṣṭī-vā́naḥ ǀ ná ǀ ajara ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni, most victorious with thy conquering strength, most Mighty One, art born for service of the Gods, like wealth for service of the Gods. Most mighty is thine ecstasy, most splendid is thy mental power. Therefore men wait upon thee, undecaying One, like vassals, undecaying One.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, the destroyer (of enemies) by your strength, the possessor of great splendour, as born for the sake of sacrificing to the gods, as riches (are genitive rated) for the sake of sacrificing to the gods; verily your exhilaration is most brilliant, your worship is most productive of renown; hence, undecaying Agni, (sacrificers) wait upon you, like envoys (upon a prince; upon you), who preserve (your votaries) from decay.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni, most victorious with thy conquering strength, most Mighty One, art born for service of the Gods, like wealth for service of the Gods. Most mighty is thine ecstasy, most splendid is thy mental power. Therefore men wait upon thee, undecaying One, like vassals, undecaying One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो महे सहसा सहस्वत उषर्बुधे पशुषे नाग्नये स्तोमो बभूत्वग्नये ।प्रति यदीं हविष्मान्विश्वासु क्षासु जोगुवे ।अग्रे रेभो न जरत ऋषूणां जूर्णिर्होत ऋषूणां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ mahé ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhasvate ǀ uṣaḥ-búdhe ǀ paśu-sé ǀ ná ǀ agnáye ǀ stómaḥ ǀ babhūtu ǀ agnáye ǀpráti ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ havíṣmān ǀ víśvāsu ǀ kṣā́su ǀ jóguve ǀágre ǀ rebháḥ ǀ ná ǀ jarate ǀ ṛṣūṇā́m ǀ jū́rṇiḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ṛṣūṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him the mighty, conquering with victorious strength, to Agni walking with the dawn, who sendeth kine, be sung your laud, to Agni sung; As he who with oblation comes calls him aloud in every place. Before the brands of fire he shouteth singerlike, the herald, kindler of the brands.
verses.wilson_translation: May your praise, (oḥ priests), become grateful to Agni, who is desrving of laudation, who is of strength to overcome the strong, who is awakened at the dawn; to Agni, as if to a giver of cattle. Inasmuch as the presenter of the oblation repairs assiduously to every altar, the invoking priest, well-skilled in (pious) praise, glorifies him (Agni) as the first of the attaining (divinities), as a herald (recites the praises) of illustrious (men).
verses.griffith_verse: To him the mighty, conquering with victorious strength, to Agni walking with the dawn, who sendeth kine, be sung your laud, to Agni sung; As he who with oblation comes calls him aloud in every place. Before the brands of fire he shouteth singerlike, the herald, kindler of the brands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नो नेदिष्ठं ददृशान आ भराग्ने देवेभिः सचनाः सुचेतुना महो रायः सुचेतुना ।महि शविष्ठ नस्कृधि संचक्षे भुजे अस्यै ।महि स्तोतृभ्यो मघवन्त्सुवीर्यं मथीरुग्रो न शवसा ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ nédiṣṭham ǀ dádṛśānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ ágne ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ sá-canāḥ ǀ su-cetúnā ǀ maháḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ su-cetúnā ǀmáhi ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ sam-cákṣe ǀ bhujé ǀ asyái ǀmáhi ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ máthīḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śávasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, beheld by us in nearest neighbourhood, accordant with the Gods, bring us, with gracious love, great riches with thy gracious love. Give us O Mightiest, what is great, to see and to enjoy the earth. As one of awful power, stir up heroic might for those who praise thee, Bounteous Lord!
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, do youur becoming visible close to us, and partaking with benignant intent of (the sacrificial) food along with the gods, bestow upon us abundant riches, with benignant intent. Most mighty Agni, render us illustrious, that we may behold and enjoy (this earth); and grant greatness with excellent progeny to those who praise you, possessor of wealth, destroyer of foes, like a fierce (giant) in strength.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, beheld by us in nearest neighbourhood, accordant with the Gods, bring us, with gracious love, great riches with thy gracious love. Give us O Mightiest, what is great, to see and to enjoy the earth. As one of awful power, stir up heroic might for those who praise thee, Bounteous Lord!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . By Manu's law was born this Agni, Priest most skilled, born for the holy work of those who yearn therefore, yea, born for his own holy work.All ear to him who seeks his love and wealth to him who strives for fame,Priest ne’er deceived, he sits in Iḷā's holy place, girt round in Iḷā's holy place. We call that perfecter of worship by the path or sacrifice; with reverence rich in offerings, with worship rich in offerings.Through presentation of our food he grows not old in this his from;The God whom Mātariśvan brought from far away, for Manu brought from far away. In ordered course forthwith he traverses the earth, swift-swallowing, bellowing Steer, bearing the genial seed, bearing the seed and bellowing.Observant with a hundred eyes the God is conqueror in the wood:Agni, who hath his seat in broad plains here below, and in the high lands far away. That Agni, wise High-Priest, in every house takes thought for sacrifice and holy service, yea, takes thought, with mental power, for sacrifice.Disposer, he with mental power shows all things unto him who strives;Whence he was born a guest enriched with holy oil, born as Ordainer and as Priest. When through his power and in his strong prevailing flames the Maruts’ gladdening boons mingle with Agni's roar, boons gladdening for the active One,Then he accelerates the gift, and by the greatness of his wealth,Shall rescue us from overwhelming misery, from curse and overwhelming woe. Vast, universal, good he was made messenger; the speeder with his right hand hath not loosed his hold, through love of fame not loosed his hold.He bears oblations to the Gods for whosoever supplicates.Agni bestows a blessing on each pious man, and opens wide the doors for him. That Agni hath been set most kind in camp of men, in sacrifice like a Lord victorious, like a dear Lord in sacred rites.His are the oblations of mankind when offered up at Iḷā's place.He shall preserve us from Varuṇa's chastisement, yea, from the great God's chastisement. Agni the Priest they supplicate to grant them wealth: him, dear, most thoughtful, have they made their messenger, him, offering-bearer have they made,Beloved of all, who knoweth all, the Priest, the Holy one, the Sage—Him, Friend, for help, the Gods when they are fain for wealth, him, Friend, with hymns, when fain for wealth.

verses.sanskrit: अयं जायत मनुषो धरीमणि होता यजिष्ठ उशिजामनु व्रतमग्निः स्वमनु व्रतं ।विश्वश्रुष्टिः सखीयते रयिरिव श्रवस्यते ।अदब्धो होता नि षददिळस्पदे परिवीत इळस्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ jāyata ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ dhárīmaṇi ǀ hótā ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ uśíjām ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ agníḥ ǀ svám ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀviśvá-śruṣṭiḥ ǀ sakhi-yaté ǀ rayíḥ-iva ǀ śravasyaté ǀádabdhaḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ sadat ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀ pári-vītaḥ ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǁ
verses.english_translation: By Manu's law was born this Agni, Priest most skilled, born for the holy work of those who yearn therefore, yea, born for his own holy work. All ear to him who seeks his love and wealth to him who strives for fame, Priest ne’er deceived, he sits in Iḷā's holy place, girt round in Iḷā's holy place.
verses.wilson_translation: This Agni, the invoker of the gods, the assiduous offerer of sacrifices, is genitive rated of man, (for the fulfilment of the) duty of those who desire (the fruit of) pious rites as well as for (the discharge of) his own duty; he is the bestower of all blessings on him who desires his friendship, and is wealth to (such a  one) seeking for food; the unobstructed offerer of oblations, he sits down, surrounded (by ministering priests), on the most sacred spot of earth upon the footmark of Iḷa.
verses.griffith_verse: By Manu's law was born this Agni, Priest most skilled, born for the holy work of those who yearn therefore, yea, born for his own holy work. All ear to him who seeks his love and wealth to him who strives for fame, Priest ne’er deceived, he sits in Iḷā's holy place, girt round in Iḷā's holy place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं यज्ञसाधमपि वातयामस्यृतस्य पथा नमसा हविष्मता देवताता हविष्मता ।स न ऊर्जामुपाभृत्यया कृपा न जूर्यति ।यं मातरिश्वा मनवे परावतो देवं भाः परावतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ yajña-sā́dham ǀ ápi ǀ vātayāmasi ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pathā́ ǀ námasā ǀ havíṣmatā ǀ devá-tātā ǀ havíṣmatā ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūrjā́m ǀ upa-ā́bhṛti ǀ ayā́ ǀ kṛpā́ ǀ ná ǀ jūryati ǀyám ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ mánave ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ devám ǀ bhā́ríti bhā́ḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call that perfecter of worship by the path or sacrifice; with reverence rich in offerings, with worship rich in offerings. Through presentation of our food he grows not old in this his from; The God whom Mātariśvan brought from far away, for Manu brought from far away.
verses.wilson_translation: We propitiate that instrumental ument of sacrifice by the path of sacrifice, by reverential salutation, and by oblations of clarified butter; by oblations (offered) to the gods and he accepts our offerings, and through his benignity quits not (the rite until its close), the divinity whom the wind brought from afar for the service of Manu; (may he come) from afar (to our sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: We call that perfecter of worship by the path or sacrifice; with reverence rich in offerings, with worship rich in offerings. Through presentation of our food he grows not old in this his from; The God whom Mātariśvan brought from far away, for Manu brought from far away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवेन सद्यः पर्येति पार्थिवं मुहुर्गी रेतो वृषभः कनिक्रदद्दधद्रेतः कनिक्रदत् ।शतं चक्षाणो अक्षभिर्देवो वनेषु तुर्वणिः ।सदो दधान उपरेषु सानुष्वग्निः परेषु सानुषु ॥
verses.transliteration: évena ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ pári ǀ eti ǀ pā́rthivam ǀ muhuḥ-gī́ḥ ǀ rétaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ kánikradat ǀ dádhat ǀ rétaḥ ǀ kánikradat ǀśatám ǀ cákṣāṇaḥ ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ váneṣu ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀsádaḥ ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ úpareṣu ǀ sā́nuṣu ǀ agníḥ ǀ páreṣu ǀ sā́nuṣu ǁ
