verses.english_translation: Dispelling on their way the horror of black gloom, making a glorious show these flames of his fly forth, When o’er the spacious tract he spreads himself abroad, and rushes panting on with thunder and with roar.
verses.wilson_translation: Thereupon those (flames of Agni) extend together in all directions, dispersing gloom, and spreading great light along the path of darkness; when (Agni) illumines repeatedly the whole earth, and proceeds panting thundering, and roaring aloud.
verses.griffith_verse: Dispelling on their way the horror of black gloom, making a glorious show these flames of his fly forth, When o’er the spacious tract he spreads himself abroad, and rushes panting on with thunder and with roar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूषन्न योऽधि बभ्रूषु नम्नते वृषेव पत्नीरभ्येति रोरुवत् ।ओजायमानस्तन्वश्च शुंभते भीमो न शृंगा दविधाव दुर्गृभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ṣan ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ babhrū́ṣu ǀ námnate ǀ vṛ́ṣā-iva ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ abhí ǀ eti ǀ róruvat ǀojāyámānaḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ ca ǀ śumbhate ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ śṛ́ṅgā ǀ davidhāva ǀ duḥ-gṛ́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Amid brown plants he stoops as if adorning them, and rushes bellowing like a bull upon his wives. Proving his might, he decks the glory of his form, and shakes his horns like one terrific, hard to stay.
verses.wilson_translation: He stoops down among the bushes as if embellishing them (with his lustre), and rushes roaring like a bull amongst (a herd of) cows; thence increasing in intensity, he enhances (the fierceness) of his form, and is difficult to be arrested as a formidable (animal), when he brandishes his horns. Like a bull amongst: vṛṣeva pantir abhyeti; patnir = pālayitrīḥ, those who cherish him,Agni, i.e., bushes, timber; patnī = a cow].
verses.griffith_verse: Amid brown plants he stoops as if adorning them, and rushes bellowing like a bull upon his wives. Proving his might, he decks the glory of his form, and shakes his horns like one terrific, hard to stay.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स संस्तिरो विष्टिरः सं गृभायति जानन्नेव जानतीर्नित्य आ शये ।पुनर्वर्धंते अपि यंति देव्यमन्यद्वर्पः पित्रोः कृण्वते सचा ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ sam-stíraḥ ǀ vi-stíraḥ ǀ sám ǀ gṛbhāyati ǀ jānán ǀ evá ǀ jānatī́ḥ ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ śaye ǀpúnaḥ ǀ vardhante ǀ ápi ǀ yanti ǀ devyám ǀ anyát ǀ várpaḥ ǀ pitróḥ ǀ kṛṇvate ǀ sácā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now covered, now displayed he grasps as one who knows his resting-place in those who know him well. A second time they wax and gather Godlike power, and blending both together change their Parents' form.
verses.wilson_translation: Now hidden, now displayed, he seizes (on the fuel), as if understanding (the purpose of the worshipper), and even reposes amidst the conscious (flames); again they break forth, and repair to the divine (fire of sacrifice), blending with which they give a different (luminous)form to their parents, (heaven and earth).
verses.griffith_verse: Now covered, now displayed he grasps as one who knows his resting-place in those who know him well. A second time they wax and gather Godlike power, and blending both together change their Parents' form.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमग्रुवः केशिनीः सं हि रेभिर ऊर्ध्वास्तस्थुर्मम्रुषीः प्रायवे पुनः ।तासां जरां प्रमुंचन्नेति नानददसुं परं जनयञ्जीवमस्तृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ keśínīḥ ǀ sám ǀ hí ǀ rebhiré ǀ ūrdhvā́ḥ ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ mamrúṣīḥ ǀ prá ǀ āyáve ǀ púnaríti ǀtā́sām ǀ jarā́m ǀ prá-muñcán ǀ eti ǀ nā́nadat ǀ ásum ǀ páram ǀ janáyan ǀ jīvám ǀ ástṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The maidens with long, tresses hold him in embrace; dead, they rise up again to meet the Living One. Releasing them from age with a loud roar he comes, filling them with new spirit, living, unsubdued.
verses.wilson_translation: The curving tresses (of the flames) embrace him, (Agni), and when expiring spring aloft again to (greet) their coming (lord); rescuing them from decrepitude, he comes sounding aloud, genitive rating (in them) intenser animation and unimpaired vitality.
verses.griffith_verse: The maidens with long, tresses hold him in embrace; dead, they rise up again to meet the Living One. Releasing them from age with a loud roar he comes, filling them with new spirit, living, unsubdued.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधीवासं परि मातू रिहन्नह तुविग्रेभिः सत्वभिर्याति वि ज्रयः ।वयो दधत्पद्वते रेरिहत्सदानु श्येनी सचते वर्तनीरह ॥
verses.transliteration: adhīvāsám ǀ pári ǀ mātúḥ ǀ rihán ǀ áha ǀ tuvi-grébhiḥ ǀ sátva-bhiḥ ǀ yāti ǀ ví ǀ jráyaḥ ǀváyaḥ ǀ dádhat ǀ pat-váte ǀ rérihat ǀ sádā ǀ ánu ǀ śyénī ǀ sacate ǀ vartaníḥ ǀ áha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Licking the mantle of the Mother, far and wide he wanders over fields with beasts that flee apace. Strengthening all that walk, licking up all around, a blackened path, forsooth, he leaves where’er he goes.
verses.wilson_translation: Licking up the (verdant) vesture of the mother (of all things, earth), the rapid (Agni) proceeds with resounding existences; granting sustenance to (every) footed (creature); ever consuming (fuel), so that a blackened track follows (hispath).
verses.griffith_verse: Licking the mantle of the Mother, far and wide he wanders over fields with beasts that flee apace. Strengthening all that walk, licking up all around, a blackened path, forsooth, he leaves where’er he goes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमग्ने मघवत्सु दीदिह्यध श्वसीवान्वृषभो दमूनाः ।अवास्या शिशुमतीरदीदेर्वर्मेव युत्सु परिजर्भुराणः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ agne ǀ maghávat-su ǀ dīdihi ǀ ádha ǀ śvásīvān ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀava-ásya ǀ śíśu-matīḥ ǀ adīdeḥ ǀ várma-iva ǀ yut-sú ǀ pari-járbhurāṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, shine resplendent with our wealthy chiefs, like a loud-snorting bull, accustomed to the house. Thou casting off thine infant wrappings blazest forth as though thou hadst put on a coat of mail for war.
verses.wilson_translation: Shine,Agni, in our opulent (abodes), vivifying, showering (blessings), bounteous, casting off infantine (glimmerings); blaze (fiercely), repelling repeatedly, like a coat of mail, (our enemies) in combats.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, shine resplendent with our wealthy chiefs, like a loud-snorting bull, accustomed to the house. Thou casting off thine infant wrappings blazest forth as though thou hadst put on a coat of mail for war.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदमग्ने सुधितं दुर्धितादधि प्रियादु चिन्मन्मनः प्रेयो अस्तु ते ।यत्ते शुक्रं तन्वो रोचते शुचि तेनास्मभ्यं वनसे रत्नमा त्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ agne ǀ sú-dhitam ǀ dúḥ-dhitāt ǀ ádhi ǀ priyā́t ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ cit ǀ mánmanaḥ ǀ préyaḥ ǀ astu ǀ te ǀyát ǀ te ǀ śukrám ǀ tanváḥ ǀ rócate ǀ śúci ǀ téna ǀ asmábhyam ǀ vanase ǀ rátnam ǀ ā́ ǀ tvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this our perfect prayer be dearer unto thee than an imperfect prayer although it please thee well. With the pure brilliancy that radiates from thy form, mayest thou grant to us abundant store of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: May this oblation,Agni, carefully plural ced upon the rugged but agreeable (pile of fuel), be most acceptable to you, so that the pure radiance of your person n may shine brightly, and you may grant us wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: May this our perfect prayer be dearer unto thee than an imperfect prayer although it please thee well. With the pure brilliancy that radiates from thy form, mayest thou grant to us abundant store of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रथाय नावमुत नो गृहाय नित्यारित्रां पद्वतीं रास्यग्ने ।अस्माकं वीराँ उत नो मघोनो जनांश्च या पारयाच्छर्म या च ॥
verses.transliteration: ráthāya ǀ nā́vam ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ gṛhā́ya ǀ nítya-aritrām ǀ pat-vátīm ǀ rāsi ǀ agne ǀasmā́kam ǀ vīrā́n ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ jánān ǀ ca ǀ yā́ ǀ pāráyāt ǀ śárma ǀ yā́ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant to our chariot, to our house, O Agni, a boat with moving feet and constant oarage, One that may further well our wealthy princes and all the folk, and be our certain refuge.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow,Agni, upon our exfellent patron a boat ever fitted with oars and feet, (one that may render) our posterity prosperous, and may bear mankind across (the ocean of life) to felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Grant to our chariot, to our house, O Agni, a boat with moving feet and constant oarage, One that may further well our wealthy princes and all the folk, and be our certain refuge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभी नो अग्न उक्थमिज्जुगुर्या द्यावाक्षामा सिंधवश्च स्वगूर्ताः ।गव्यं यव्यं यंतो दीर्घाहेषं वरमरुण्यो वरंत ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ ukthám ǀ ít ǀ juguryāḥ ǀ dyā́vākṣā́mā ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ca ǀ svá-gūrtāḥ ǀgávyam ǀ yávyam ǀ yántaḥ ǀ dīrghā́ ǀ áhā ǀ íṣam ǀ váram ǀ aruṇyáḥ ǀ varanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Welcome our laud with thine approval, Agni. May earth and heaven and freely flowing rivers Yield us long life and food and corn and cattle, and may the red Dawns choose for us their choicest.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, be propitiated by this our earnest praise, and may heaven and earth, and the spontaneously-flowing (streams), provide for us the produce of the herd, and of the field; and may the purple coursers (of the dawn) bestow upon us abundant food through a length of days.
verses.griffith_verse: Welcome our laud with thine approval, Agni. May earth and heaven and freely flowing rivers Yield us long life and food and corn and cattle, and may the red Dawns choose for us their choicest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YEA, verily, the fair effulgence of the God for glory was established, since he sprang from strength.When he inclines thereto successful is the hymn: the songs of sacrifice have brought him as they flow Wonderful, rich in nourishment, he dwells in food; next, in the seven auspicious Mothers is his home.Thirdly, that they might drain the treasures of the Bull, the maidens brought forth him for whom the ten provide. What time from out the deep, from the Steer's wondrous form, the Chiefs who had the power produced him with their strength;When Mātariśvan rubbed forth him who lay concealed, for mixture of the sweet drink, in the days of old. When from the Highest Father he is brought to us, amid the plants he rises hungry, wondrously.As both together join to expedite his birth, most youthful he is born resplendent in his light. Then also entered he the Mothers, and in them pure and uninjured he increased in magnitude.As to the first he rose, the vigorous from of old, so now he runs among the younger lowest ones. Therefore they choose him Herald at the morning rites, pressing to him as unto Bhaga, pouring gifts,When, much-praised, by the power and will of Gods, he goes at all times to his mortal worshipper to drink. What time the Holy One, wind-urged, hath risen up, serpent-like winding through the dry grass unrestrained,Dust lies upon the way of him who burneth all, black-winged and pure of birth who follows sundry paths. Like a swift chariot made by men who know their art, he with his red limbs lifts himself aloft to heaven.Thy worshippers become by burning black of hue: their strength flies as before a hero's violence. By thee, O Agni, Varuṇa who guards the Law, Mitra and Aryaman, the Bounteous, are made strong;For, as the felly holds the spokes, thou with thy might pervading hast been born encompassing them round. Agni, to him who toils and pours libations, thou, Most Youthful! sendest wealth and all the host of Gods.Thee, therefore, even as Bhaga, will we set anew, young Child of Strength, most wealthy! in our battle-song. Vouchsafe us riches turned to worthy ends, good luck abiding in the house, and strong capacity,Wealth that directs both worlds as they were guiding-reins, and, very Wise, the Gods’ assent in sacrifice. May he, the Priest resplendent, joyful, hear us, he with the radiant car and rapid horses.May Agni, ever wise, with best directions to bliss and highest happiness conduct us. With hymns of might hath Agni now been lauded, advanced to height of universal kingship.Now may these wealthy chiefs and we together spread forth as spreads the Sun above the rain-clouds.

verses.sanskrit: बळित्था तद्वपुषे धायि दर्शतं देवस्य भर्गः सहसो यतो जनि ।यदीमुप ह्वरते साधते मतिर्ऋतस्य धेना अनयंत सस्रुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: báṭ ǀ itthā́ ǀ tát ǀ vápuṣe ǀ dhāyi ǀ darśatám ǀ devásya ǀ bhárgaḥ ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ jáni ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ úpa ǀ hvárate ǀ sā́dhate ǀ matíḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhénāḥ ǀ anayanta ǀ sa-srútaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: YEA, verily, the fair effulgence of the God for glory was established, since he sprang from strength. When he inclines thereto successful is the hymn: the songs of sacrifice have brought him as they flow
verses.wilson_translation: Verily, that visible radiance of the divine (Agni) has been so apprehended (by all, that it may be) for (the support of) the body, for which end it has been genitive rated by (bodily) strength; and that my mind may apprehend and apply (that radiance), they address the sacred prayers associated with oblations (to Agni).
verses.griffith_verse: YEA, verily, the fair effulgence of the God for glory was established, since he sprang from strength. When he inclines thereto successful is the hymn: the songs of sacrifice have brought him as they flow
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पृक्षो वपुः पितुमान्नित्य आ शये द्वितीयमा सप्तशिवासु मातृषु ।तृतीयमस्य वृषभस्य दोहसे दशप्रमतिं जनयंत योषणः ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛkṣáḥ ǀ vápuḥ ǀ pitu-mā́n ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ śaye ǀ dvitī́yam ǀ ā́ ǀ saptá-śivāsu ǀ mātṛ́ṣu ǀtṛtī́yam ǀ asya ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ doháse ǀ dáśa-pramatim ǀ janayanta ǀ yóṣaṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wonderful, rich in nourishment, he dwells in food; next, in the seven auspicious Mothers is his home. Thirdly, that they might drain the treasures of the Bull, the maidens brought forth him for whom the ten provide.
verses.wilson_translation: First, he reposes (on the earth) as the digestive (faculty), the embodied, the accepter of food, the eternal secondly, (he dwells) among the seven auspicious mothers (of fertility); thirdly, the associated (regions) genitive rate him, delighting in the ten (quarters) of space, for the sake of milking this showerer (of rain).
verses.griffith_verse: Wonderful, rich in nourishment, he dwells in food; next, in the seven auspicious Mothers is his home. Thirdly, that they might drain the treasures of the Bull, the maidens brought forth him for whom the ten provide.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निर्यदीं बुध्नान्महिषस्य वर्पस ईशानासः शवसा क्रंत सूरयः ।यदीमनु प्रदिवो मध्व आधवे गुहा संतं मातरिश्वा मथायति ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ budhnā́t ǀ mahiṣásya ǀ várpasaḥ ǀ īśānā́saḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ kránta ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ ánu ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ā-dhavé ǀ gúhā ǀ sántam ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ mathāyáti ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time from out the deep, from the Steer's wondrous form, the Chiefs who had the power produced him with their strength; When Mātariśvan rubbed forth him who lay concealed, for mixture of the sweet drink, in the days of old.
verses.wilson_translation: As powerful priests extract by force (of prayer) this Agnifrom his primitive seat, (for the evolution) of his mighty form; as the wind arouses him lurking in the hiding-plural ce (of the altar), for the sake of offering oblations now as of old.
verses.griffith_verse: What time from out the deep, from the Steer's wondrous form, the Chiefs who had the power produced him with their strength; When Mātariśvan rubbed forth him who lay concealed, for mixture of the sweet drink, in the days of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यत्पितुः परमान्नीयते पर्या पृक्षुधो वीरुधो दंसु रोहति ।उभा यदस्य जनुषं यदिन्वत आदिद्यविष्ठो अभवद्घृणा शुचिः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ pitúḥ ǀ paramā́t ǀ nīyáte ǀ pári ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛkṣúdhaḥ ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ dáṃ-su ǀ rohati ǀubhā́ ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ janúṣam ǀ yát ǀ ínvataḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ yáviṣṭhaḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ ghṛṇā́ ǀ śúciḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When from the Highest Father he is brought to us, amid the plants he rises hungry, wondrously. As both together join to expedite his birth, most youthful he is born resplendent in his light.
verses.wilson_translation: As from the excellence of the nutritious (offering) be, (Agni), is brought forth and the consumable branches rise amidst (the flames); and as both (the instrumental tutor of the rite and the priest) combine for his genitive ration, therefore has he been genitive rated, pure, youthful, and radiant.
verses.griffith_verse: When from the Highest Father he is brought to us, amid the plants he rises hungry, wondrously. As both together join to expedite his birth, most youthful he is born resplendent in his light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदिन्मातॄराविशद्यास्वा शुचिरहिंस्यमान उर्विया वि वावृधे ।अनु यत्पूर्वा अरुहत्सनाजुवो नि नव्यसीष्ववरासु धावते ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ mātṝ́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aviśat ǀ yā́su ǀ ā́ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ áhiṃsyamānaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ vavṛdhe ǀánu ǀ yát ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ áruhat ǀ sanā-júvaḥ ǀ ní ǀ návyasīṣu ǀ ávarāsu ǀ dhāvate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then also entered he the Mothers, and in them pure and uninjured he increased in magnitude. As to the first he rose, the vigorous from of old, so now he runs among the younger lowest ones.
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore has the brilliant Agnientered the maternal (quarters of space), amidst which pure, and unharmed, he had evolved into magnitude, so that he mounted (the bushes) plural ced before him, as he had (consumed others) prior to them, and runs rapidly among the more recent and inferior branches.
verses.griffith_verse: Then also entered he the Mothers, and in them pure and uninjured he increased in magnitude. As to the first he rose, the vigorous from of old, so now he runs among the younger lowest ones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदिद्धोतारं वृणते दिविष्टिषु भगमिव पपृचानास ऋंजते ।देवान्यत्क्रत्वा मज्मना पुरुष्टुतो मर्तं शंसं विश्वधा वेति धायसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ hótāram ǀ vṛṇate ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀ bhágam-iva ǀ papṛcānā́saḥ ǀ ṛñjate ǀdevā́n ǀ yát ǀ krátvā ǀ majmánā ǀ puru-stutáḥ ǀ mártam ǀ śáṃsam ǀ viśvádhā ǀ véti ǀ dhā́yase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore they choose him Herald at the morning rites, pressing to him as unto Bhaga, pouring gifts, When, much-praised, by the power and will of Gods, he goes at all times to his mortal worshipper to drink.
verses.wilson_translation: Pious worshippers then adore the invoker (of the gods), for (the propitiation of) the dwellers in heaven, as (such men) adore a powerful prince, since the many-lauded, and all upholding (Agni) knows how by (holy) act and (bodily) strength to bring together the gods and their mortal worshipper for the sake of obtaining (mutual) sustenance.
verses.griffith_verse: Therefore they choose him Herald at the morning rites, pressing to him as unto Bhaga, pouring gifts, When, much-praised, by the power and will of Gods, he goes at all times to his mortal worshipper to drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि यदस्थाद्यजतो वातचोदितो ह्वारो न वक्वा जरणा अनाकृतः ।तस्य पत्मन्दक्षुषः कृष्णजंहसः शुचिजन्मनो रज आ व्यध्वनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yát ǀ ásthāt ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ vā́ta-coditaḥ ǀ hvāráḥ ǀ ná ǀ vákvā ǀ jaráṇāḥ ǀ ánākṛtaḥ ǀtásya ǀ pátman ǀ dhakṣúṣaḥ ǀ kṛṣṇá-jaṃhasaḥ ǀ śúci-janmanaḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ví-adhvanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time the Holy One, wind-urged, hath risen up, serpent-like winding through the dry grass unrestrained, Dust lies upon the way of him who burneth all, black-winged and pure of birth who follows sundry paths.
verses.wilson_translation: Since the adorable (Agni), impelled by the wind, spreads in various directions, like an insincere and unrestrained chatterer, (who utters indiscriminate) praises, therefore the world is assiduous in the worship of him, the consumer of all, whose way is dark, who is pure of birth and follows various paths.
verses.griffith_verse: What time the Holy One, wind-urged, hath risen up, serpent-like winding through the dry grass unrestrained, Dust lies upon the way of him who burneth all, black-winged and pure of birth who follows sundry paths.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रथो न यातः शिक्वभिः कृतो द्यामंगेभिररुषेभिरीयते ।आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ráthaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yātáḥ ǀ śíkva-bhiḥ ǀ kṛtáḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ áṅgebhiḥ ǀ aruṣébhiḥ ǀ īyate ǀā́t ǀ asya ǀ té ǀ kṛṣṇā́saḥ ǀ dhakṣi ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ śū́rasya-iva ǀ tveṣáthāt ǀ īṣate ǀ váyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a swift chariot made by men who know their art, he with his red limbs lifts himself aloft to heaven. Thy worshippers become by burning black of hue: their strength flies as before a hero's violence.
verses.wilson_translation: Like a chariot drawn by ropes,Agni, set in movement by his own revolving members (his flames), proceeds to the heavens; the paths he traverses are blackened by smoke, as he consumes (the fuel), and (beasts and) birds fly from his radiance as (enemies fly from the prowess) of a hero.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a swift chariot made by men who know their art, he with his red limbs lifts himself aloft to heaven. Thy worshippers become by burning black of hue: their strength flies as before a hero's violence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वया ह्यग्ने वरुणो धृतव्रतो मित्रः शाशद्रे अर्यमा सुदानवः ।यत्सीमनु क्रतुना विश्वथा विभुररान्न नेमिः परिभूरजायथाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tváyā ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ śāśadré ǀ aryamā́ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ánu ǀ krátunā ǀ viśvá-thā ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ arā́n ǀ ná ǀ nemíḥ ǀ pari-bhū́ḥ ǀ ájāyathāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By thee, O Agni, Varuṇa who guards the Law, Mitra and Aryaman, the Bounteous, are made strong; For, as the felly holds the spokes, thou with thy might pervading hast been born encompassing them round.
verses.wilson_translation: By you,Agni;Varuṇa, observant of his duties and Mitraand Aryaman, bountiful divinities, are animated, so that yo have been born comprehending them all universally in all (their) functions, and encompassing (them all) as the circumference (encompasses) the spokes (of a wheel).
verses.griffith_verse: By thee, O Agni, Varuṇa who guards the Law, Mitra and Aryaman, the Bounteous, are made strong; For, as the felly holds the spokes, thou with thy might pervading hast been born encompassing them round.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने शशमानाय सुन्वते रत्नं यविष्ठ देवतातिमिन्वसि ।तं त्वा नु नव्यं सहसो युवन्वयं भगं न कारे महिरत्न धीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ śaśamānā́ya ǀ sunvaté ǀ rátnam ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ devá-tātim ǀ invasi ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ nú ǀ návyam ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ yuvan ǀ vayám ǀ bhágam ǀ ná ǀ kāré ǀ mahi-ratna ǀ dhīmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, to him who toils and pours libations, thou, Most Youthful! sendest wealth and all the host of Gods. Thee, therefore, even as Bhaga, will we set anew, young Child of Strength, most wealthy! in our battle-song.
verses.wilson_translation: Most youthful Agni, for the good of him who praises you and offers you libations, you make the precious (offering) acceptable to the gods; new-born of strength we glorify you who are to be lauded; to whom rich offerings (are to be presented); (we glorify you) in (our) hymn as (men eulogize) a powerful prince.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, to him who toils and pours libations, thou, Most Youthful! sendest wealth and all the host of Gods. Thee, therefore, even as Bhaga, will we set anew, young Child of Strength, most wealthy! in our battle-song.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे रयिं न स्वर्थं दमूनसं भगं दक्षं न पपृचासि धर्णसिं ।रश्मीँरिव यो यमति जन्मनी उभे देवानां शंसमृत आ च सुक्रतुः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ ná ǀ su-ártham ǀ dámūnasam ǀ bhágam ǀ dákṣam ǀ ná ǀ papṛcāsi ǀ dharṇasím ǀraśmī́n-iva ǀ yáḥ ǀ yámati ǀ jánmanī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ devā́nām ǀ śáṃsam ǀ ṛté ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ su-krátuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vouchsafe us riches turned to worthy ends, good luck abiding in the house, and strong capacity, Wealth that directs both worlds as they were guiding-reins, and, very Wise, the Gods’ assent in sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as you confer upon us riches, (so you bestow upon us) a well-disposed, docile, and energetic (son); the receptacle (of learning and other merits), one who is the performer of holy rites,Agni, who regulates as it were his own rays, (and the condition) both (his) births, (or heaven and earth), he regulates at (our) sacrifice the adoration of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Vouchsafe us riches turned to worthy ends, good luck abiding in the house, and strong capacity, Wealth that directs both worlds as they were guiding-reins, and, very Wise, the Gods’ assent in sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत नः सुद्योत्मा जीराश्वो होता मंद्रः शृणवच्चंद्ररथः ।स नो नेषन्नेषतमैरमूरोऽग्निर्वामं सुवितं वस्यो अच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ su-dyótmā ǀ jīrá-aśvaḥ ǀ hótā ǀ mandráḥ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ candrá-rathaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ neṣat ǀ néṣa-tamaiḥ ǀ ámūraḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ vāmám ǀ suvitám ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he, the Priest resplendent, joyful, hear us, he with the radiant car and rapid horses. May Agni, ever wise, with best directions to bliss and highest happiness conduct us.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who is one with light, who has fleet horses, the invoker (of the gods), full of joy, and borne in a golden chariot, listen to us; may that irresistible, yet plural cable Agni, conduct us, by the most efficacious (means), to that desirable and accessible (heaven).
verses.griffith_verse: May he, the Priest resplendent, joyful, hear us, he with the radiant car and rapid horses. May Agni, ever wise, with best directions to bliss and highest happiness conduct us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्ताव्यग्निः शिमीवद्भिरर्कैः साम्राज्याय प्रतरं दधानः ।अमी च ये मघवानो वयं च मिहं न सूरो अति निष्टतन्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: ástāvi ǀ agníḥ ǀ śímīvat-bhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ sā́m-rājyāya ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀamī́ íti ǀ ca ǀ yé ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ ca ǀ míham ǀ ná ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ áti ǀ níḥ ǀ tatanyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With hymns of might hath Agni now been lauded, advanced to height of universal kingship. Now may these wealthy chiefs and we together spread forth as spreads the Sun above the rain-clouds.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, possessing eminent (fitness) for supreme sovereignty, has been glorified by us, with holy rites (śimīśaktiḥ:Nirukta2.1.24), and with hymns. Let all who are presen1, as well as we ourselves, enriched (by his favour), shout aloud (the praise of Agni), as (loudly as) the sun (causes) the rain-cloud (to thunder).
verses.griffith_verse: With hymns of might hath Agni now been lauded, advanced to height of universal kingship. Now may these wealthy chiefs and we together spread forth as spreads the Sun above the rain-clouds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLII. Āprīs.
hymns.anukramani: १३ दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः। (आप्रीसूक्तं)-१ इध्मः समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा, २ तनून पात्, ३ नराशंसः, ४ इळः, ५ बर्हिः, ६ देवीः द्वारः, ७ उषासानक्ता ८ दैव्यो होतारौ प्रचेतसौ, ९ तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळा भारत्यः, १० त्वष्टा, ११ वनस्पतिः, १२ स्वाहा कृतयः, १३ इन्द्रः। अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . KINDLED, bring, Agni, Gods to-day for him who lifts the ladle up.Spin out the ancient thread for him who sheds, with gifts, the Soma juice. Thou dealest forth, Tanūnapāt, sweet sacrifice enriched with oil,Brought by a singer such as I who offers gifts and toils for thee. He wondrous, sanctifying, bright, sprinkles the sacrifice with mead,Thrice, Narāśaṁsa from the heavens, a God mid Gods adorable. Agni, besought, bring hitherward Indra the Friend, the Wonderful,For this my hymn of praise, O sweet of tongue, is chanted forth to thee. The ladle-holders strew trimmed grass at this well-ordered sacrifice;A home for Indra is adorned, wide, fittest to receive the Gods. Thrown open be the Doors Divine, unfailing, that assist the rite,High, purifying, much-desired, so that the Gods may enter in. May Night and Morning, hymned with lauds, united, fair to look upon,Strong Mothers of the sacrifice, seat them together on the grass. May the two Priests Divine, the sage, the sweet-voiced lovers of the hymn,Complete this sacrifice of ours, effectual, reaching heaven to-day. Let Hotrā pure, set among Gods, amid the Maruts Bhāratī, Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī, rest on the grass, adorable. May Tvaṣṭar send us genial dew abundant, wondrous, rich in gifts,For increase and for growth of wealth, Tvaṣṭar our kinsman and our Friend. Vanaspati, give forth, thyself, and call the Gods to sacrifice.May Agni, God intelligent, speed our oblation to the Gods. To Vāyu joined with Pūṣan, with the Maruts, and the host of Gods,To Indra who inspires the hymn cry Glory! and present the gift. Come hither to enjoy the gifts prepared with cry of Glory! Come,O Indra, hear their calling; they invite thee to the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धो अग्न आ वह देवाँ अद्य यतस्रुचे ।तंतुं तनुष्व पूर्व्यं सुतसोमाय दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ devā́n ǀ adyá ǀ yatá-sruce ǀtántum ǀ tanuṣva ǀ pūrvyám ǀ sutá-somāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: KINDLED, bring, Agni, Gods to-day for him who lifts the ladle up. Spin out the ancient thread for him who sheds, with gifts, the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are samiddha, bring the gods today (to the worshipper), whose ladle is uplifted; extent (the merit of) former sacrificer to the giver (of the offering), by whom the Somais poured forth.
verses.griffith_verse: KINDLED, bring, Agni, Gods to-day for him who lifts the ladle up. Spin out the ancient thread for him who sheds, with gifts, the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृतवंतमुप मासि मधुमंतं तनूनपात् ।यज्ञं विप्रस्य मावतः शशमानस्य दाशुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛtá-vantam ǀ úpa ǀ māsi ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ tanū-napāt ǀyajñám ǀ víprasya ǀ mā́-vataḥ ǀ śaśamānásya ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou dealest forth, Tanūnapāt, sweet sacrifice enriched with oil, Brought by a singer such as I who offers gifts and toils for thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Tanūnapāt, be present at this well-flavoured and cutter-fed sacrifice, (the offering) of a pious offerer (of oblations); glorifying you.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou dealest forth, Tanūnapāt, sweet sacrifice enriched with oil, Brought by a singer such as I who offers gifts and toils for thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुचिः पावको अद्भुतो मध्वा यज्ञं मिमिक्षति ।नराशंसस्त्रिरा दिवो देवो देवेषु यज्ञियः ॥
verses.transliteration: śúciḥ ǀ pāvakáḥ ǀ ádbhutaḥ ǀ mádhvā ǀ yajñám ǀ mimikṣati ǀnárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He wondrous, sanctifying, bright, sprinkles the sacrifice with mead, Thrice, Narāśaṁsa from the heavens, a God mid Gods adorable.
verses.wilson_translation: The pure, purifying, wonderful Narāśaṃsa, an adorable god among gods, (having come) from heaven, thrice mixes the sacrifice with the sweet (Soma).
verses.griffith_verse: He wondrous, sanctifying, bright, sprinkles the sacrifice with mead, Thrice, Narāśaṁsa from the heavens, a God mid Gods adorable.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ईळितो अग्न आ वहेंद्रं चित्रमिह प्रियं ।इयं हि त्वा मतिर्ममाच्छा सुजिह्व वच्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: īḷitáḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ índram ǀ citrám ǀ ihá ǀ priyám ǀiyám ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ matíḥ ǀ máma ǀ áccha ǀ su-jihva ǀ vacyáte ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, besought, bring hitherward Indra the Friend, the Wonderful, For this my hymn of praise, O sweet of tongue, is chanted forth to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are Iḷita, bring hither Indra, the wonderful, the beloved; this my praise is recited, bright-tongued, before you.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, besought, bring hitherward Indra the Friend, the Wonderful, For this my hymn of praise, O sweet of tongue, is chanted forth to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तृणानासो यतस्रुचो बर्हिर्यज्ञे स्वध्वरे ।वृंजे देवव्यचस्तममिंद्राय शर्म सप्रथः ॥
verses.transliteration: stṛṇānā́saḥ ǀ yatá-srucaḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ yajñé ǀ su-adhvaré ǀvṛñjé ǀ devávyacaḥ-tamam ǀ índrāya ǀ śárma ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ladle-holders strew trimmed grass at this well-ordered sacrifice; A home for Indra is adorned, wide, fittest to receive the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The priests, bearing ladles, are strewing the sacred grass in this holy sacrifice, to prepare a god-frequented and well-spread abode for Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: The ladle-holders strew trimmed grass at this well-ordered sacrifice; A home for Indra is adorned, wide, fittest to receive the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि श्रयंतामृतावृधः प्रयै देवेभ्यो महीः ।पावकासः पुरुस्पृहो द्वारो देवीरसश्चतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ śrayantām ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ pra-yái ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀpāvakā́saḥ ǀ puru-spṛ́haḥ ǀ dvā́raḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ asaścátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrown open be the Doors Divine, unfailing, that assist the rite, High, purifying, much-desired, so that the Gods may enter in.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the bright, separable doors, the augmenters of sacrifice, the purifiers of rites, the desired of many, be set open for the gods to enter.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrown open be the Doors Divine, unfailing, that assist the rite, High, purifying, much-desired, so that the Gods may enter in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ भंदमाने उपाके नक्तोषासा सुपेशसा ।यह्वी ऋतस्य मातरा सीदतां बर्हिरा सुमत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ bhándamāne íti ǀ úpāke íti ǀ náktoṣásā ǀ su-péśasā ǀyahvī́ íti ǀ ṛtásya ǀ mātárā ǀ sī́datām ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ su-mát ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Night and Morning, hymned with lauds, united, fair to look upon, Strong Mothers of the sacrifice, seat them together on the grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful night and morning, ever hymned, ever associated, progeny (yahuḥsunuḥ--Nirukta2.2.11) (of time), parents of sacrifice, sit down of your own good will on the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: May Night and Morning, hymned with lauds, united, fair to look upon, Strong Mothers of the sacrifice, seat them together on the grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंद्रजिह्वा जुगुर्वणी होतारा दैव्या कवी ।यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृशं ॥
verses.transliteration: mandrá-jihvā ǀ jugurváṇī íti ǀ hótārā ǀ dáivyā ǀ kavī́ íti ǀyajñám ǀ naḥ ǀ yakṣatām ǀ imám ǀ sidhrám ǀ adyá ǀ divi-spṛ́śam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the two Priests Divine, the sage, the sweet-voiced lovers of the hymn, Complete this sacrifice of ours, effectual, reaching heaven to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: May the two plural asing-tongued receivers of praise, the divine and sage invokers (of the gods), officiate today at this our sacrifice, which confers (rewards) and attains heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: May the two Priests Divine, the sage, the sweet-voiced lovers of the hymn, Complete this sacrifice of ours, effectual, reaching heaven to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुचिर्देवेष्वर्पिता होत्रा मरुत्सु भारती ।इळा सरस्वती मही बर्हिः सीदंतु यज्ञियाः ॥
verses.transliteration: śúciḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ árpitā ǀ hótrā ǀ marút-su ǀ bhā́ratī ǀíḷā ǀ sárasvatī ǀ mahī́ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sīdantu ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Hotrā pure, set among Gods, amid the Maruts Bhāratī, Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī, rest on the grass, adorable.
verses.wilson_translation: May the purehotā, plural ced among the gods, and Bhāratī, among the Maruts, and may the adorable Iḷā,Sarasvatī,Mahī, sit down upon the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Let Hotrā pure, set among Gods, amid the Maruts Bhāratī, Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī, rest on the grass, adorable.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तन्नस्तुरीपमद्भुतं पुरु वारं पुरु त्मना ।त्वष्टा पो��ाय वि ष्यतु राये नाभा नो अस्मयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ naḥ ǀ turī́pam ǀ ádbhutam ǀ purú ǀ vā ǀ áram ǀ purú ǀ tmánā ǀtváṣṭā ǀ póṣāya ǀ ví ǀ syatu ǀ rāyé ǀ nā́bhā ǀ naḥ ǀ asma-yúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Tvaṣṭar send us genial dew abundant, wondrous, rich in gifts, For increase and for growth of wealth, Tvaṣṭar our kinsman and our Friend.
verses.wilson_translation: May Tvaṣṭā, favourably disposed towards us, send to us, for our nourishment and prosperity, the quick (falling), wonderful, abundant (water), in the centre (of the cloud, effecting), of itself much (good).
verses.griffith_verse: May Tvaṣṭar send us genial dew abundant, wondrous, rich in gifts, For increase and for growth of wealth, Tvaṣṭar our kinsman and our Friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवसृजन्नुप त्मना देवान्यक्षि वनस्पते ।अग्निर्हव्या सुषूदति देवो देवेषु मेधिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ava-sṛján ǀ úpa ǀ tmánā ǀ devā́n ǀ yakṣi ǀ vanaspate ǀagníḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ susūdati ǀ deváḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ médhiraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vanaspati, give forth, thyself, and call the Gods to sacrifice. May Agni, God intelligent, speed our oblation to the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Vanaspati, here present of your own accord, convey our offerings to the gods; the divine and intelligent Agniaccepts (the oblations) for the deities.
verses.griffith_verse: Vanaspati, give forth, thyself, and call the Gods to sacrifice. May Agni, God intelligent, speed our oblation to the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूषण्वते मरुत्वते विश्वदेवाय वायवे ।स्वाहा गायत्रवेपसे हव्यमिंद्राय कर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣaṇ-váte ǀ marútvate ǀ viśvá-devāya ǀ vāyáve ǀsvā́hā ǀ gāyatrá-vepase ǀ havyám ǀ índrāya ǀ kartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Vāyu joined with Pūṣan, with the Maruts, and the host of Gods, To Indra who inspires the hymn cry Glory! and present the gift.
verses.wilson_translation: (Priests), present the oblation withsvāhāto Indra, in the form of Gāyatra, along with Pūṣanand the Maruts; also to the assembled gods, and the Vāyu.
verses.griffith_verse: To Vāyu joined with Pūṣan, with the Maruts, and the host of Gods, To Indra who inspires the hymn cry Glory! and present the gift.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वाहाकृतान्या गह्युप हव्यानि वीतये ।इंद्रा गहि श्रुधी हवं त्वां हवंते अध्वरे ॥
verses.transliteration: svā́hā-kṛtāni ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ úpa ǀ havyā́ni ǀ vītáye ǀíndra ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ śrudhí ǀ hávam ǀ tvā́m ǀ havante ǀ adhvaré ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither to enjoy the gifts prepared with cry of Glory! Come, O Indra, hear their calling; they invite thee to the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Approach,Indra, to partake of the oblations consecrated withsvāhā; approach and hear the invocation, as they invoke you to the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither to enjoy the gifts prepared with cry of Glory! Come, O Indra, hear their calling; they invite thee to the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To Agni I present a newer mightier hymn, I bring my words and song unto the Son of Strength,Who, Offspring of the Waters, bearing precious things sits on the earth, in season, dear Invoking Priest. Soon as he sprang to birth that Agni was shown forth to Mātariśvan in the highest firmament.When he was kindled, through his power and majesty his fiery splendour made the heavens and earth to shine. His flames that wax not old, beams fair to look upon of him whose face is lovely, shine with beauteous sheen.The rays of Agni, him whose active force is light, through the nights glimmer sleepless, ageless, like the floods. Send thou with hymns that Agni to his own abode, who rules, one Sovran Lord of wealth, like Varuṇa,Him, All-possessor, whom the Bhṛgus with their might brought to earth's central point, the centre of the world. He whom no force can stay, even as the Maruts’ roar, like to a dart sent forth, even as the bolt from heaven,Agni with sharpened jaws chews up and eats the trees, and conquers them as when the warrior smites his foes. And will not Agni find enjoyment in our praise, will not the Vasu grant our wish with gifts of wealth?Will not the Inspirer speed our prayers to gain their end? Him with the radiant glance I laud with this my song. The kindler of the flame wins Agni as a Friend, promoter of the Law, whose face is bright with oil.Inflamed and keen, refulgent in our gatherings, he lifts our hymn on high clad in his radiant hues. Keep us incessantly with guards that cease not, Agni, with guards auspicious, very mighty.With guards that never slumber, never heedless, never beguiled. O Helper, keep our children.

verses.sanskrit: प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीं धीतिमग्नये वाचो मतिं सहसः सूनवे भरे ।अपां नपाद्यो वसुभिः सह प्रियो होता पृथिव्यां न्यसीददृत्वियः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ távyasīm ǀ návyasīm ǀ dhītím ǀ agnáye ǀ vācáḥ ǀ matím ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ sūnáve ǀ bhare ǀapā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ yáḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sahá ǀ priyáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ ní ǀ ásīdat ǀ ṛtvíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Agni I present a newer mightier hymn, I bring my words and song unto the Son of Strength, Who, Offspring of the Waters, bearing precious things sits on the earth, in season, dear Invoking Priest.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer devoutly to Agni, the son of strength, an invigorating and most new sacrifice, with words of adoration; (that Agni), the grandson of the waters, who, (present) in due season, the friend and ministering priest (of the sacrificer), sits upon the altar with (many) good things.
verses.griffith_verse: To Agni I present a newer mightier hymn, I bring my words and song unto the Son of Strength, Who, Offspring of the Waters, bearing precious things sits on the earth, in season, dear Invoking Priest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स जायमानः परमे व्योमन्याविरग्निरभवन्मातरिश्वने ।अस्य क्रत्वा समिधानस्य मज्मना प्र द्यावा शोचिः पृथिवी अरोचयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ paramé ǀ ví-omani ǀ āvíḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ mātaríśvane ǀasyá ǀ krátvā ǀ sam-idhānásya ǀ majmánā ǀ prá ǀ dyā́vā ǀ śocíḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ arocayat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soon as he sprang to birth that Agni was shown forth to Mātariśvan in the highest firmament. When he was kindled, through his power and majesty his fiery splendour made the heavens and earth to shine.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as born, what that (Agni) manifested to Matariśvan in the highest atmosphere, and his radiance, kindled by vigorous effort, spread through heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Soon as he sprang to birth that Agni was shown forth to Mātariśvan in the highest firmament. When he was kindled, through his power and majesty his fiery splendour made the heavens and earth to shine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य त्वेषा अजरा अस्य भानवः सुसंदृशः सुप्रतीकस्य सुद्युतः ।भात्वक्षसो अत्यक्तुर्न सिंधवोऽग्ने रेजंते अससंतो अजराः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ tveṣā́ḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǀ asyá ǀ bhānávaḥ ǀ su-saṃdṛ́śaḥ ǀ su-prátīkasya ǀ su-dyútaḥ ǀbhā́-tvakṣasaḥ ǀ áti ǀ aktúḥ ǀ ná ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ rejante ǀ ásasantaḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: His flames that wax not old, beams fair to look upon of him whose face is lovely, shine with beauteous sheen. The rays of Agni, him whose active force is light, through the nights glimmer sleepless, ageless, like the floods.
verses.wilson_translation: His radiance is undecaying; the rays of him who is of plural asing aspect, are everywhere visible and bright; the intensely shining, all-pervading, unceasing, undecaying (rays) of Agni, desist not (from their functions).
verses.griffith_verse: His flames that wax not old, beams fair to look upon of him whose face is lovely, shine with beauteous sheen. The rays of Agni, him whose active force is light, through the nights glimmer sleepless, ageless, like the floods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमेरिरे भृगवो विश्ववेदसं नाभा पृथिव्या भुवनस्य मज्मना ।अग्निं तं गीर्भिर्हिनुहि स्व आ दमे य एको वस्वो वरुणो न राजति ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ ā-īriré ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ viśvá-vedasam ǀ nā́bhā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ majmánā ǀagním ǀ tám ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ hinuhi ǀ své ǀ ā́ ǀ dáme ǀ yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́jati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send thou with hymns that Agni to his own abode, who rules, one Sovran Lord of wealth, like Varuṇa, Him, All-possessor, whom the Bhṛgus with their might brought to earth's central point, the centre of the world.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring to his own abode with hymns that Agni, the possessor of all riches, whom the descendants of Bhṛguplural ced by the strength of all beings upon the navel of the earth; for, like Varuṇa, he reigns sole (monarch) over (all) treasure.
verses.griffith_verse: Send thou with hymns that Agni to his own abode, who rules, one Sovran Lord of wealth, like Varuṇa, Him, All-possessor, whom the Bhṛgus with their might brought to earth's central point, the centre of the world.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यो वराय मरुतामिव स्वनः सेनेव सृष्टा दिव्या यथाशनिः ।अग्निर्जंभैस्तिगितैरत्ति भर्वति योधो न शत्रून्त्स वना न्यृंजते ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ várāya ǀ marútām-iva ǀ svanáḥ ǀ sénā-iva ǀ sṛṣṭā́ ǀ divyā́ ǀ yáthā ǀ aśániḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ jámbhaiḥ ǀ tigitáiḥ ǀ atti ǀ bhárvati ǀ yodháḥ ǀ ná ǀ śátrūn ǀ sáḥ ǀ vánā ǀ ní ǀ ṛñjate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom no force can stay, even as the Maruts’ roar, like to a dart sent forth, even as the bolt from heaven, Agni with sharpened jaws chews up and eats the trees, and conquers them as when the warrior smites his foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who, like the roaring of the winds, like a victorious host, like the thunderbolt in heaven, is not to be arrested, devours and destroys (our foes) with sharpened teeth (bharva hiṃsāyām; bharvatirattikarmā:Nirukta9.23), and, as a warrior (annihilates his enemies), he, (Agni), lays waste the woods.
verses.griffith_verse: He whom no force can stay, even as the Maruts’ roar, like to a dart sent forth, even as the bolt from heaven, Agni with sharpened jaws chews up and eats the trees, and conquers them as when the warrior smites his foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुविन्नो अग्निरुचथस्य वीरसद्वसुष्कुविद्वसुभिः काममावरत् ।चोदः कुवित्तुतुज्यात्सातये धियः शुचिप्रतीकं तमया धिया गृणे ॥
verses.transliteration: kuvít ǀ naḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ucáthasya ǀ vī́ḥ ǀ ásat ǀ vásuḥ ǀ kuvít ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ ā-várat ǀcodáḥ ǀ kuvít ǀ tutujyā́t ǀ sātáye ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ śúci-pratīkam ǀ tám ǀ ayā́ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ gṛṇe ǁ
verses.english_translation: And will not Agni find enjoyment in our praise, will not the Vasu grant our wish with gifts of wealth? Will not the Inspirer speed our prayers to gain their end? Him with the radiant glance I laud with this my song.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agnibe ever desirous of our praise; may the giver of wealth satisfy our utmost expectation with riches; may the inspirer (of our devotion) hasten our rites to fruition. I glorify him, the radiant-limbed (Agni), with this laudation.
verses.griffith_verse: And will not Agni find enjoyment in our praise, will not the Vasu grant our wish with gifts of wealth? Will not the Inspirer speed our prayers to gain their end? Him with the radiant glance I laud with this my song.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृतप्रतीकं व ऋतस्य धूर्षदमग्निं मित्रं न समिधान ऋंजते ।इंधानो अक्रो विदथेषु दीद्यच्छुक्रवर्णामुदु नो यंसते धियं ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛtá-pratīkam ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhūḥ-sádam ǀ agním ǀ mitrám ǀ ná ǀ sam-idhānáḥ ǀ ṛñjate ǀíndhānaḥ ǀ akráḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ dī́dyat ǀ śukrá-varṇām ǀ út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ yaṃsate ǀ dhíyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The kindler of the flame wins Agni as a Friend, promoter of the Law, whose face is bright with oil. Inflamed and keen, refulgent in our gatherings, he lifts our hymn on high clad in his radiant hues.
verses.wilson_translation: The kindler (of the sacrificial fire) propitiates Agni, of glistening form; the upholder of your ceremony, like a friend; well kindled and well supplied (with fuel); blazing brightly at holy rites, he illumines our pure and pious observances.
verses.griffith_verse: The kindler of the flame wins Agni as a Friend, promoter of the Law, whose face is bright with oil. Inflamed and keen, refulgent in our gatherings, he lifts our hymn on high clad in his radiant hues.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्रयुच्छन्नप्रयुच्छद्भिरग्ने शिवेभिर्नः पायुभिः पाहि शग्मैः ।अदब्धेभिरदृपितेभिरिष्टेऽनिमिषद्भिः परि पाहि नो जाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápra-yucchan ǀ áprayucchat-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ śivébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pāyú-bhiḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ śagmáiḥ ǀádabdhebhiḥ ǀ ádṛpitebhiḥ ǀ iṣṭe ǀ ánimiṣat-bhiḥ ǀ pári ǀ pāhi ǀ naḥ ǀ jā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Keep us incessantly with guards that cease not, Agni, with guards auspicious, very mighty. With guards that never slumber, never heedless, never beguiled. O Helper, keep our children.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, never heedless (of us), guard us with never heedless, auspicious, and joy-bestowing cares; do you, who are desired (by all), protect us, and those born of us, with unobstructed unovercome, and never slumbering (vigilance).
verses.griffith_verse: Keep us incessantly with guards that cease not, Agni, with guards auspicious, very mighty. With guards that never slumber, never heedless, never beguiled. O Helper, keep our children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLIV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Priest goes forth to sacrifice, with wondrous power sending aloft the hymn of glorious brilliancy.He moves to meet the ladles turning to the right, which are the first to kiss the place where he abides. To him sang forth the flowing streams of Holy Law, encompassed in the home and birth-place of the God.He, when he dwelt extended in the waters’ lap, absorbed those Godlike powers for which he is adored. Seeking in course altern to reach the selfsame end the two copartners strive to win this beauteous form.Like Bhaga must he be duly invoked by us, as he who drives the car holds fast the horse's reins. He whom the two copartners with observance tend, the pair who dwell together in the same abode,By night as in the day the grey one was born young, passing untouched by eld through many an age of man. Him the ten fingers, the devotions, animate: we mortals call on him a God to give us help.He speeds over the sloping surface of the land: new deeds hath he performed with those who gird him round. For, Agni, like a herdsman, thou by thine own might rulest o’er all that is in heaven and on the earth;And these two Mighty Ones, bright, golden closely joined, rolling them round are come unto thy sacred grass. Agni, accept with joy, be glad in this our prayer, joy-giver, self-sustained, strong, born of Holy Law!For fair to see art thou turning to every side, pleasant to look on as a dwelling filled with food.

verses.sanskrit: एति प्र होता व्रतमस्य माययोर्ध्वां दधानः शुचिपेशसं धियं ।अभि स्रुचः क्रमते दक्षिणावृतो या अस्य धाम प्रथमं ह निंसते ॥
verses.transliteration: éti ǀ prá ǀ hótā ǀ vratám ǀ asya ǀ māyáyā ǀ ūrdhvā́m ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ śúci-peśasam ǀ dhíyam ǀabhí ǀ srúcaḥ ǀ kramate ǀ dakṣiṇā-āvṛ́taḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ prathamám ǀ ha ǀ níṃsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Priest goes forth to sacrifice, with wondrous power sending aloft the hymn of glorious brilliancy. He moves to meet the ladles turning to the right, which are the first to kiss the place where he abides.
verses.wilson_translation: The ministering priest, (qualified) by experience, and possessing exalted and graceful devotion,proceeds (to celebrate) his, (Agni's), worship, having circumambulated (the altar), he takes up the ladles which are first to present theoblations.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Priest goes forth to sacrifice, with wondrous power sending aloft the hymn of glorious brilliancy. He moves to meet the ladles turning to the right, which are the first to kiss the place where he abides.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभीमृतस्य दोहना अनूषत योनौ देवस्य सदने परीवृताः ।अपामुपस्थे विभृतो यदावसदध स्वधा अधयद्याभिरीयते ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ īm ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dohánāḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀ yónau ǀ devásya ǀ sádane ǀ pári-vṛtāḥ ǀapā́m ǀ upá-sthe ǀ ví-bhṛtaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ā́ ǀ ávasat ǀ ádha ǀ svadhā́ḥ ǀ adhayat ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ī́yate ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him sang forth the flowing streams of Holy Law, encompassed in the home and birth-place of the God. He, when he dwelt extended in the waters’ lap, absorbed those Godlike powers for which he is adored.
verses.wilson_translation: The drops of rain, enveloped (by the solar rays), are renewed in the dwelling of the divine (sun), their birth-plural ce; when he, (Agni), abides cherished on the lap of the waters, then (the world) drinks the nectareous (rain), with which he, (as the lightning), associates.
verses.griffith_verse: To him sang forth the flowing streams of Holy Law, encompassed in the home and birth-place of the God. He, when he dwelt extended in the waters’ lap, absorbed those Godlike powers for which he is adored.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युयूषतः सवयसा तदिद्वपुः समानमर्थं वितरित्रता मिथः ।आदीं भगो न हव्यः समस्मदा वोळ्हुर्न रश्मीन्त्समयंस्त सारथिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yúyūṣataḥ ǀ sá-vayasā ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ vápuḥ ǀ samānám ǀ ártham ǀ vi-táritratā ǀ mitháḥ ǀā́t ǀ īm ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ vóḷhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmī́n ǀ sám ǀ ayaṃsta ǀ sā́rathiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seeking in course altern to reach the selfsame end the two copartners strive to win this beauteous form. Like Bhaga must he be duly invoked by us, as he who drives the car holds fast the horse's reins.
verses.wilson_translation: The two (priests, the hotī andadhvaryu), of equal honour, and alike assiduous, labouring mutually for a common object, combine the form of Agni(with their respective functions); whereupon he to whom the oblation is to be offered, collects the drops (of clarified butter), as Bhaga(accepts the worship of all), or as a charioteer (gathers the reins of the horses) that draw (the car).
verses.griffith_verse: Seeking in course altern to reach the selfsame end the two copartners strive to win this beauteous form. Like Bhaga must he be duly invoked by us, as he who drives the car holds fast the horse's reins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमीं द्वा सवयसा सपर्यतः समाने योना मिथुना समोकसा ।दिवा न नक्तं पलितो युवाजनि पुरू चरन्नजरो मानुषा युगा ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ īm ǀ dvā́ ǀ sá-vayasā ǀ saparyátaḥ ǀ samāné ǀ yónā ǀ mithunā́ ǀ sám-okasā ǀdívā ǀ ná ǀ náktam ǀ palitáḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ ajani ǀ purú ǀ cáran ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ mā́nuṣā ǀ yugā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom the two copartners with observance tend, the pair who dwell together in the same abode, By night as in the day the grey one was born young, passing untouched by eld through many an age of man.
verses.wilson_translation: He, whom the two, a pair of equal power, dwelling in the same plural ce, and engaged in the same ceremony, worship night and day; he, whether old or young, has been engendered for the sake of mortal couples, accepting many (oblations), and exempt from decay.
verses.griffith_verse: He whom the two copartners with observance tend, the pair who dwell together in the same abode, By night as in the day the grey one was born young, passing untouched by eld through many an age of man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमीं हिन्वंति धीतयो दश व्रिशो देवं मर्तास ऊतये हवामहे ।धनोरधि प्रवत आ स ऋण्वत्यभिव्रजद्भिर्वयुना नवाधित ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ īm ǀ hinvanti ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ vríśaḥ ǀ devám ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ havāmahe ǀdhánoḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛṇvati ǀ abhivrájat-bhiḥ ǀ vayúnā ǀ návā ǀ adhita ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him the ten fingers, the devotions, animate: we mortals call on him a God to give us help. He speeds over the sloping surface of the land: new deeds hath he performed with those who gird him round.
verses.wilson_translation: The ten fingers intertwined propitiate that divine (Agni), whom we mortals invoke for protection; he darts (his rays) like swift (arrows) from a bow, and accepts the new praises (uttered) by those who crowd round the altar.
verses.griffith_verse: Him the ten fingers, the devotions, animate: we mortals call on him a God to give us help. He speeds over the sloping surface of the land: new deeds hath he performed with those who gird him round.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह्यग्ने दिव्यस्य राजसि त्वं पार्थिवस्य पशुपा इव त्मना ।एनी त एते बृहती अभिश्रिया हिरण्ययी वक्वरी बर्हिराशाते ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ divyásya ǀ rā́jasi ǀ tvám ǀ pā́rthivasya ǀ paśupā́ḥ-iva ǀ tmánā ǀénī íti ǀ te ǀ eté íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ abhi-śríyā ǀ hiraṇyáyī íti ǀ vákvarī íti ǀ barhíḥ ǀ āśāte íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, Agni, like a herdsman, thou by thine own might rulest o’er all that is in heaven and on the earth; And these two Mighty Ones, bright, golden closely joined, rolling them round are come unto thy sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, reign over (the dweller in) heaven, and over those of earth, according to thine own (will), as a herdsman over his (herd), and those two, (heaven and earth), bright, vast, adorable, beneficent, and sounding (agreeably), partake of the oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: For, Agni, like a herdsman, thou by thine own might rulest o’er all that is in heaven and on the earth; And these two Mighty Ones, bright, golden closely joined, rolling them round are come unto thy sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने जुषस्व प्रति हर्य तद्वचो मंद्र स्वधाव ऋतजात सुक्रतो ।यो विश्वतः प्रत्यङ्ङसि दर्शतो रण्वः संदृष्टौ पितुमाँ इव क्षयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ juṣásva ǀ práti ǀ harya ǀ tát ǀ vácaḥ ǀ mándra ǀ svádhā-vaḥ ǀ ṛ́ta-jāta ǀ súkrato íti sú-krato ǀyáḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ ási ǀ darśatáḥ ǀ raṇváḥ ǀ sám-dṛṣṭau ǀ pitumā́n-iva ǀ kṣáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, accept with joy, be glad in this our prayer, joy-giver, self-sustained, strong, born of Holy Law! For fair to see art thou turning to every side, pleasant to look on as a dwelling filled with food.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who confers happiness, who accepts oblations, who was born for sacrifice, and are the performer of good works, be plural ased (with this rite), attend to this prayer; for you are in presence of all (the world), are visible (to all), are plural asant in their sight, and are their refuge, like a (bountiful) distributor of food.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, accept with joy, be glad in this our prayer, joy-giver, self-sustained, strong, born of Holy Law! For fair to see art thou turning to every side, pleasant to look on as a dwelling filled with food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Ask ye of him for he is come, he knoweth it; he, full of wisdom, is implored, is now implored.With him are admonitions and with him commands: he is the Lord of Strength, the Lord of Power and Might. They ask of him: not all learn by their questioning what he, the Sage, hath grasped, as ’twere, with his own mind.Forgetting not the former nor the later word, he goeth on, not careless, in his mental power. To him these ladles go, to him these racing mares: he only will give ear to all the words I speak.All-speeding, victor, perfecter of sacrifice, the Babe with flawless help hath mustered vigorous might. Whate’er he meets he grasps and then runs farther on, and straightway, newly born, creeps forward with his kin.He stirs the wearied man to pleasure and great joy what time the longing gifts approach him as he comes. He is a wild thing of the flood and forest: he hath been laid upon the highest surface.He hath declared the lore of works to mortals, Agni the Wise, for he knows Law, the Truthful.

verses.sanskrit: तं पृच्छता स जगामा स वेद स चिकित्वाँ ईयते सा न्वीयते ।तस्मिन्त्संति प्रशिषस्तस्मिन्निष्टयः स वाजस्य शवसः शुष्मिणस्पतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ pṛcchata ǀ sáḥ ǀ jagāma ǀ sáḥ ǀ veda ǀ sáḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ īyate ǀ sáḥ ǀ nú ǀ īyate ǀtásmin ǀ santi ǀ pra-śíṣaḥ ǀ tásmin ǀ iṣṭáyaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ śuṣmíṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ask ye of him for he is come, he knoweth it; he, full of wisdom, is implored, is now implored. With him are admonitions and with him commands: he is the Lord of Strength, the Lord of Power and Might.
verses.wilson_translation: Ask (of Agniwhat you desire), for he goes (everywhere), he knows (all things); possessed of intelligence, he proceeds (to ascertain what is to be done), and is had recourse to (by his worshippers); for in him is the power of restraining (unreasonable desires) in him (is the power of granting) enjoyment; he is the giver of food and of strength; the protector of the mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Ask ye of him for he is come, he knoweth it; he, full of wisdom, is implored, is now implored. With him are admonitions and with him commands: he is the Lord of Strength, the Lord of Power and Might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमित्पृच्छंति न सिमो वि पृच्छति स्वेनेव धीरो मनसा यदग्रभीत् ।न मृष्यते प्रथमं नापरं वचोऽस्य क्रत्वा सचते अप्रदृपितः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ pṛcchanti ǀ ná ǀ simáḥ ǀ ví ǀ pṛcchati ǀ svéna-iva ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ yát ǀ ágrabhīt ǀná ǀ mṛṣyate ǀ prathamám ǀ ná ǀ áparam ǀ vácaḥ ǀ asyá ǀ krátvā ǀ sacate ǀ ápra-dṛpitaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They ask of him: not all learn by their questioning what he, the Sage, hath grasped, as ’twere, with his own mind. Forgetting not the former nor the later word, he goeth on, not careless, in his mental power.
verses.wilson_translation: They ask of Agni, but no one asks improperly; for a sensible man (replies to solicitation) as he has determined in his own mind; Agni tolerates not a speech that anticipates (his reply), nor endures a rejoinder; he who is devoid of arrogance is favoured by his protection.
verses.griffith_verse: They ask of him: not all learn by their questioning what he, the Sage, hath grasped, as ’twere, with his own mind. Forgetting not the former nor the later word, he goeth on, not careless, in his mental power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमिद्गच्छंति जुह्वस्तमर्वतीर्विश्वान्येकः शृणवद्वचांसि मे ।पुरुप्रैषस्ततुरिर्यज्ञसाधनोऽच्छिद्रोतिः शिशुरादत्त सं रभः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ gacchanti ǀ juhváḥ ǀ tám ǀ árvatīḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ ékaḥ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ me ǀpuru-praiṣáḥ ǀ táturiḥ ǀ yajña-sā́dhanaḥ ǀ ácchidra-ūtiḥ ǀ śíśuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ adatta ǀ sám ǀ rábhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him these ladles go, to him these racing mares: he only will give ear to all the words I speak. All-speeding, victor, perfecter of sacrifice, the Babe with flawless help hath mustered vigorous might.
verses.wilson_translation: To him the (sacrificial) ladles are directed; to him (our) praises are addressed; he alone hears all my prayers; be is the instrumental gator of many, the transporter (across the world), the instrumental ument of sacrifice, the unintermitting preserver (of mankind), and (genitive le as) an infant; provided with the preparations (of sacrifice), he accepts libations.
verses.griffith_verse: To him these ladles go, to him these racing mares: he only will give ear to all the words I speak. All-speeding, victor, perfecter of sacrifice, the Babe with flawless help hath mustered vigorous might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपस्थायं चरति यत्समारत सद्यो जातस्तत्सार युज्येभिः ।अभि श्वांतं मृशते नांद्ये मुदे यदीं गच्छंत्युशतीरपिष्ठितं ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-sthā́yam ǀ carati ǀ yát ǀ sam-ā́rata ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ tatsāra ǀ yújyebhiḥ ǀabhí ǀ śvāntám ǀ mṛśate ǀ nāndyé ǀ mudé ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ gácchanti ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ api-sthitám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whate’er he meets he grasps and then runs farther on, and straightway, newly born, creeps forward with his kin. He stirs the wearied man to pleasure and great joy what time the longing gifts approach him as he comes.
verses.wilson_translation: When (the priest) proceeds to effect his development, he is (at once) manifested; and as soon as engendered, is associated with his objects; he provides for the gratification (of his worshipper), plural cidly engaged in the agreeable (rite), when the (oblations) that desire (his acceptance) reach him present (at the sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: Whate’er he meets he grasps and then runs farther on, and straightway, newly born, creeps forward with his kin. He stirs the wearied man to pleasure and great joy what time the longing gifts approach him as he comes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स ईं मृगो अप्यो वनर्गुरुप त्वच्युपमस्यां नि धायि ।व्यब्रवीद्वयुना मर्त्येभ्योऽग्निर्विद्वाँ ऋतचिद्धि सत्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ápyaḥ ǀ vanargúḥ ǀ úpa ǀ tvací ǀ upa-másyām ǀ ní ǀ dhāyi ǀví ǀ abravīt ǀ vayúnā ǀ mártyebhyaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ṛta-cít ǀ hí ǀ satyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is a wild thing of the flood and forest: he hath been laid upon the highest surface. He hath declared the lore of works to mortals, Agni the Wise, for he knows Law, the Truthful.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the searcher, the accessible, the dweller in woods, has been plural ced (amidst the fuel), as in the similitude of (an enveloping) skin; the wise Agni, the appreciater of sacrifice, the veracious, has declared to mortals (the knowledge of) their religious duties.
verses.griffith_verse: He is a wild thing of the flood and forest: he hath been laid upon the highest surface. He hath declared the lore of works to mortals, Agni the Wise, for he knows Law, the Truthful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I LAUD the seven-rayed, the triple-headed, Agni all-perfect in his Parents’ bosom,Sunk in the lap of all that moves and moves not, him who hath filled all luminous realms of heaven. As a great Steer he grew to these his Parents; sublime he stands, untouched by eld, far-reaching.He plants his footsteps on the lofty ridges of the broad earth: his red flames lick the udder. Coming together to their common youngling both Cows, fairshaped, spread forth in all directions,Measuring out the paths that must be travelled, entrusting all desires to him the Mighty. The prudent sages lead him to his dwelling, guarding with varied skill the Ever-Youthful.Longing, they turned their eyes unto the River: to these the Sun of men was manifested. Born noble in the regions, aim of all mens’ eyes to be implored for life by great and small alike,Far as the Wealthy One hath spread himself abroad, he is the Sire all-visible of this progeny.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिमूर्धानं सप्तरश्मिं गृणीषेऽनूनमग्निं पित्रोरुपस्थे ।निषत्तमस्य चरतो ध्रुवस्य विश्वा दिवो रोचनापप्रिवांसं ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-mūrdhā́nam ǀ saptá-raśmim ǀ gṛṇīṣe ǀ ánūnam ǀ agním ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀni-sattám ǀ asya ǀ cárataḥ ǀ dhruvásya ǀ víśvā ǀ diváḥ ǀ rocanā́ ǀ āpapri-vā́ṃsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I LAUD the seven-rayed, the triple-headed, Agni all-perfect in his Parents’ bosom, Sunk in the lap of all that moves and moves not, him who hath filled all luminous realms of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify the three-headed, seven-rayed Agni, who is sibject to no diminution, seated on the lap of his parents, (heaven and earth); and gratifying all (desires); as the universal radiance of the divine (Agni), whether moving or stationary, (spreads around).
verses.griffith_verse: I LAUD the seven-rayed, the triple-headed, Agni all-perfect in his Parents’ bosom, Sunk in the lap of all that moves and moves not, him who hath filled all luminous realms of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उक्षा महाँ अभि ववक्ष एने अजरस्तस्थावितऊतिर्ऋष्वः ।उर्व्याः पदो नि दधाति सानौ रिहंत्यूधो अरुषासो अस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ukṣā́ ǀ mahā́n ǀ abhí ǀ vavakṣe ǀ ene íti ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ tasthau ǀ itáḥ-ūtiḥ ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀurvyā́ḥ ǀ padáḥ ǀ ní ǀ dadhāti ǀ sā́nau ǀ rihánti ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: As a great Steer he grew to these his Parents; sublime he stands, untouched by eld, far-reaching. He plants his footsteps on the lofty ridges of the broad earth: his red flames lick the udder.
verses.wilson_translation: The great showerer (of benefits) has pervaded these two (worlds); undecaying and adorable, he is (ever) present, bestowing protection; he plural ces his foot on the summit of the earth, and his radiant (flames) lick the udder (of the firmament).
verses.griffith_verse: As a great Steer he grew to these his Parents; sublime he stands, untouched by eld, far-reaching. He plants his footsteps on the lofty ridges of the broad earth: his red flames lick the udder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानं वत्समभि संचरंती विष्वग्धेनू वि चरतः सुमेके ।अनपवृज्याँ अध्वनो मिमाने विश्वान्केताँ अधि महो दधाने ॥
verses.transliteration: samānám ǀ vatsám ǀ abhí ǀ saṃcárantī íti saṃ-cárantī ǀ víṣvak ǀ dhenū́ íti ǀ ví ǀ carataḥ ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀanapa-vṛjyā́n ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ mímāne íti ǀ víśvān ǀ kétān ǀ ádhi ǀ maháḥ ǀ dádhāne íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Coming together to their common youngling both Cows, fairshaped, spread forth in all directions, Measuring out the paths that must be travelled, entrusting all desires to him the Mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: (there are) two well-disposed cows together approaching their common progeny, and fully nourishing (him); pointingout the paths that are free from all that is to be avoided, and possessing more than the great intelligence (necessary for his development).
verses.griffith_verse: Coming together to their common youngling both Cows, fairshaped, spread forth in all directions, Measuring out the paths that must be travelled, entrusting all desires to him the Mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: धीरासः पदं कवयो नयंति नाना हृदा रक्षमाणा अजुर्यं ।सिषासंतः पर्यपश्यंत सिंधुमाविरेभ्यो अभवत्सूर्यो नॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: dhī́rāsaḥ ǀ padám ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ nayanti ǀ nā́nā ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ rákṣamāṇāḥ ǀ ajuryám ǀsísāsantaḥ ǀ pári ǀ apaśyanta ǀ síndhum ǀ āvíḥ ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: The prudent sages lead him to his dwelling, guarding with varied skill the Ever-Youthful. Longing, they turned their eyes unto the River: to these the Sun of men was manifested.
verses.wilson_translation: Experienced sages (kavayaḥ: ye vā anūcāste kavayaḥ--Aitareya Brāhmaṇa2.2) bring the invincible (Agni), to his station (onthe altar); cherishing him in manifold (ways) in their hearts; desirous of propitiating him, they worshipthe (boon) shedding (Agni); and to those men he is manifest as the Sun.
verses.griffith_verse: The prudent sages lead him to his dwelling, guarding with varied skill the Ever-Youthful. Longing, they turned their eyes unto the River: to these the Sun of men was manifested.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिदृक्षेण्यः परि काष्ठासु जेन्य ईळेन्यो महो अर्भाय जीवसे ।पुरुत्रा यदभवत्सूरहैभ्यो गर्भेभ्यो मघवा विश्वदर्शतः ॥
verses.transliteration: didṛkṣéṇyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ kā́ṣṭhāsu ǀ jényaḥ ǀ īḷényaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ árbhāya ǀ jīváse ǀpuru-trā́ ǀ yát ǀ ábhavat ǀ sū́ḥ ǀ áha ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ gárbhebhyaḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ viśvá-darśataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Born noble in the regions, aim of all mens’ eyes to be implored for life by great and small alike, Far as the Wealthy One hath spread himself abroad, he is the Sire all-visible of this progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: He is willing to be seen in the (ten) regions (of space); the victorious, the adorable, the source of life to great and small; inasmuch as in many plural ces the opulent (possessor of sacrificial food), who is visible to all, is the parent of that (pious) progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: Born noble in the regions, aim of all mens’ eyes to be implored for life by great and small alike, Far as the Wealthy One hath spread himself abroad, he is the Sire all-visible of this progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . How, Agni, have the radiant ones, aspiring, endued thee with the vigour of the living,So that on both sides fostering seed and offspring, the Gods may joy in Holy Law's fulfilment? Mark this my speech, Divine One, thou, Most Youthful! offered to thee by him who gives most freely.One hates thee, and another sings thy praises: I thine adorer laud thy form, O Agni. Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Māmateya from affliction.Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious the foes who fain would harm them did no mischief. The sinful man who worships not, O Agni, who, offering not, harms us with double-dealing,—Be this in turn to him a heavy sentence: may he distress himself by his revilings. Yea, when a mortal knowingly, O Victor, injures with double tongue a fellow-mortal,From him, praised Agni! save thou him that lauds thee: bring us not into trouble and affliction.

verses.sanskrit: कथा ते अग्ने शुचयंत आयोर्ददाशुर्वाजेभिराशुषाणाः ।उभे यत्तोके तनये दधाना ऋतस्य सामन्रणयंत देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ śucáyantaḥ ǀ āyóḥ ǀ dadāśúḥ ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ āśuṣāṇā́ḥ ǀubhé íti ǀ yát ǀ toké íti ǀ tánaye ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ sā́man ǀ raṇáyanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: How, Agni, have the radiant ones, aspiring, endued thee with the vigour of the living, So that on both sides fostering seed and offspring, the Gods may joy in Holy Law's fulfilment?
verses.wilson_translation: How have your shining and evaporating (rays),Agni, supported life (and supplied) food; so that, enjoying both, the devout (worshippers), possessing sons and grandsons, may repeat the hymns of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: How, Agni, have the radiant ones, aspiring, endued thee with the vigour of the living, So that on both sides fostering seed and offspring, the Gods may joy in Holy Law's fulfilment?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बोधा मे अस्य वचसो यविष्ठ मंहिष्ठस्य प्रभृतस्य स्वधावः ।पीयति त्वो अनु त्वो गृणाति वंदारुस्ते तन्वं वंदे अग्ने ॥
verses.transliteration: bódha ǀ me ǀ asyá ǀ vácasaḥ ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ máṃhiṣṭhasya ǀ prá-bhṛtasya ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀpī́yati ǀ tvaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ tvaḥ ǀ gṛṇāti ǀ vandā́ruḥ ǀ te ǀ tanvám ǀ vande ǀ agne ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mark this my speech, Divine One, thou, Most Youthful! offered to thee by him who gives most freely. One hates thee, and another sings thy praises: I thine adorer laud thy form, O Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Youthful (Agni), to whom oblations are due, appreciate this my reverential and earnest praise; one man reviles (you), another propitiates (you); I, your worshipper, glorify, your person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Mark this my speech, Divine One, thou, Most Youthful! offered to thee by him who gives most freely. One hates thee, and another sings thy praises: I thine adorer laud thy form, O Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये पायवो मामतेयं ते अग्ने पश्यंतो अंधं दुरितादरक्षन् ।ररक्ष तान्त्सुकृतो विश्ववेदा दिप्संत इद्रिपवो नाह देभुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ pāyávaḥ ǀ māmateyám ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ páśyantaḥ ǀ andhám ǀ duḥ-itā́t ǀ árakṣan ǀrarákṣa ǀ tā́n ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ viśvá-vedāḥ ǀ dípsantaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áha ǀ debhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Māmateya from affliction. Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious the foes who fain would harm them did no mischief.
verses.wilson_translation: Your fostering (rays),Agni, beholding the blind son of Mamatā, relieved him of the affliction; he who knows all things protect the pious, and (their) malevolent enemies are unable to do them harm.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy guardian rays, O Agni, when they saw him, preserved blind Māmateya from affliction. Lord of all riches, he preserved the pious the foes who fain would harm them did no mischief.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो नो अग्ने अररिवाँ अघायुररातीवा मर्चयति द्वयेन ।मंत्रो गुरुः पुनरस्तु सो अस्मा अनु मृक्षीष्ट तन्वं दुरुक्तैः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ árari-vān ǀ agha-yúḥ ǀ arāti-vā́ ǀ marcáyati ǀ dvayéna ǀmántraḥ ǀ gurúḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ astu ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ ánu ǀ mṛkṣīṣṭa ǀ tanvám ǀ duḥ-uktáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sinful man who worships not, O Agni, who, offering not, harms us with double-dealing,— Be this in turn to him a heavy sentence: may he distress himself by his revilings.
verses.wilson_translation: When a wicked (man), with twofold (malignity of thought and speech), obstructing our offerings, and refraining from gifts (himself), reviles us, may his prayer be heavy on him, and involve his person n (in the consequences of) his evil words.
verses.griffith_verse: The sinful man who worships not, O Agni, who, offering not, harms us with double-dealing,— Be this in turn to him a heavy sentence: may he distress himself by his revilings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत वा यः सहस्य प्रविद्वान्मर्तो मर्तं मर्चयति द्वयेन ।अतः पाहि स्तवमान स्तुवंतमग्ने माकिर्नो दुरिताय धायीः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ sahasya ǀ pra-vidvā́n ǀ mártaḥ ǀ mártam ǀ marcáyati ǀ dvayéna ǀátaḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ stavamāna ǀ stuvántam ǀ ágne ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-itā́ya ǀ dhāyīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, when a mortal knowingly, O Victor, injures with double tongue a fellow-mortal, From him, praised Agni! save thou him that lauds thee: bring us not into trouble and affliction.
verses.wilson_translation: When, Son of Strength, a man skilful (in deception) assails another man with a doubly (malignant prayer), do you,Agni, duly propitiated, protect him who worships you (from its effects); consign us not to misfortune.
