verses.griffith_verse: Yea, when a mortal knowingly, O Victor, injures with double tongue a fellow-mortal, From him, praised Agni! save thou him that lauds thee: bring us not into trouble and affliction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT Mātariśvan, piercing, formed by friction, Herald of all the Gods. in varied figure,Is he whom they have set mid human houses, gay-hued as light and shining forth for beauty. They shall not harm the man who brings thee praises: such as I am, Agni my help approves me.All acts of mine shall they accept with pleasure, laudation from the singer who presents it. Him in his constant seat men skilled in worship have taken and with praises have established.As, harnessed to a chariot fleet-foot horses, at his command let bearers lead him forward. Wondrous, full many a thing he chews and crunches: he shines amid the wood with spreading brightness.Upon his glowing flames the wind blows daily, driving them like the keen shaft of an archer. Him, whom while yet in embryo the hostile, both skilled and fain to harm, may never injure,Men blind and sightless through his splendour hurt not: his never-failing lovers have preserved him.

verses.sanskrit: मथीद्यदीं विष्टो मातरिश्वा होतारं विश्वाप्सुं विश्वदेव्यं ।नि यं दधुर्मनुष्यासु विक्षु स्वर्ण चित्रं वपुषे विभावं ॥
verses.transliteration: máthīt ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ viṣṭáḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ hótāram ǀ viśvá-apsum ǀ viśvá-devyam ǀní ǀ yám ǀ dadhúḥ ǀ manuṣyā́su ǀ vikṣú ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrám ǀ vápuṣe ǀ vibhā́-vam ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT Mātariśvan, piercing, formed by friction, Herald of all the Gods. in varied figure, Is he whom they have set mid human houses, gay-hued as light and shining forth for beauty.
verses.wilson_translation: The wind, penetrating (amidst the fuel), has excited (Agni), the invoker (of the gods), the multiform, the minister of all the deities, whom they have established amongst mortal worshippers for the accomplishment of sacrifice, like the wonderful and variously radiant sun.
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT Mātariśvan, piercing, formed by friction, Herald of all the Gods. in varied figure, Is he whom they have set mid human houses, gay-hued as light and shining forth for beauty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ददानमिन्न ददभंत मन्माग्निर्वरूथं मम तस्य चाकन् ।जुषंत विश्वान्यस्य कर्मोपस्तुतिं भरमाणस्य कारोः ॥
verses.transliteration: dadānám ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ dadabhanta ǀ mánma ǀ agníḥ ǀ várūtham ǀ máma ǀ tásya ǀ cākan ǀjuṣánta ǀ víśvāni ǀ asya ǀ kárma ǀ úpa-stutim ǀ bháramāṇasya ǀ kāróḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They shall not harm the man who brings thee praises: such as I am, Agni my help approves me. All acts of mine shall they accept with pleasure, laudation from the singer who presents it.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not (my enemies) prevail against me, when presenting acceptable (oblations), for (Agni) is desirous of my so offered adoration, and all they (the gods) are gratified by the (pious) acts of me, the reciter of their praise, and the celebrator (of the sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: They shall not harm the man who brings thee praises: such as I am, Agni my help approves me. All acts of mine shall they accept with pleasure, laudation from the singer who presents it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नित्ये चिन्नु यं सदने जगृभ्रे प्रशस्तिभिर्दधिरे यज्ञियासः ।प्र सू नयंत गृभयंत इष्टावश्वासो न रथ्यो रारहाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nítye ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ yám ǀ sádane ǀ jagṛbhré ǀ práśasti-bhiḥ ǀ dadhiré ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀprá ǀ sú ǀ nayanta ǀ gṛbháyantaḥ ǀ iṣṭáu ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ rarahāṇā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him in his constant seat men skilled in worship have taken and with praises have established. As, harnessed to a chariot fleet-foot horses, at his command let bearers lead him forward.
verses.wilson_translation: Him, whom the worshippers lay hold of in his perpetual abode, they detain by their praises, and the holders convey him diligently to the sacrifice, as rapid coursers, harnessed to a car, (bear the rider to his destination).
verses.griffith_verse: Him in his constant seat men skilled in worship have taken and with praises have established. As, harnessed to a chariot fleet-foot horses, at his command let bearers lead him forward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जंभैराद्रोचते वन आ विभावा ।आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरस्तुर्न शर्यामसनामनु द्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: purū́ṇi ǀ dasmáḥ ǀ ní ǀ riṇāti ǀ jámbhaiḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ rocate ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀā́t ǀ asya ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vāti ǀ śocíḥ ǀ ástuḥ ǀ ná ǀ śáryām ǀ asanā́m ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wondrous, full many a thing he chews and crunches: he shines amid the wood with spreading brightness. Upon his glowing flames the wind blows daily, driving them like the keen shaft of an archer.
verses.wilson_translation: The destroyer, (Agni), consumes numerous (trees) by his flames, and shares with manifold radiance in the forest; the favouring wind blows (the flames) onwards day by day, like the swift arrows (śaryāiṣavaḥ śaramayyaḥ--Nirukta5.4) of an archer.
verses.griffith_verse: Wondrous, full many a thing he chews and crunches: he shines amid the wood with spreading brightness. Upon his glowing flames the wind blows daily, driving them like the keen shaft of an archer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यं रिपवो न रिषण्यवो गर्भे संतं रेषणा रेषयंति ।अंधा अपश्या न दभन्नभिख्या नित्यास ईं प्रेतारो अरक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yám ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ riṣaṇyávaḥ ǀ gárbhe ǀ sántam ǀ reṣaṇā́ḥ ǀ reṣáyanti ǀandhā́ḥ ǀ apaśyā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ dabhan ǀ abhi-khyā́ ǀ nítyāsaḥ ǀ īm ǀ pretā́raḥ ǀ arakṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, whom while yet in embryo the hostile, both skilled and fain to harm, may never injure, Men blind and sightless through his splendour hurt not: his never-failing lovers have preserved him.
verses.wilson_translation: The blind (of intellect), or those who see not (physically), detract not from his glory, whom no enemies no malevolent adversaries, harm, even whilst yet in (his) embryo (condition), for his constant encouragers defend him.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, whom while yet in embryo the hostile, both skilled and fain to harm, may never injure, Men blind and sightless through his splendour hurt not: his never-failing lovers have preserved him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HITHER he hastens to give, Lord of great riches, King of the mighty, to the place of treasure.The pressing-stones shall serve him speeding near us. As Steer of men so Steer of earth and heaven by glory, he whose streams all life hath drunken,Who hasting forward rests upon the altar. He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise Courser like the Steed of cloudy heaven,Bright like the Sun, with hundredfold existence. He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions,Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather. Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing,The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.

verses.sanskrit: महः स राय एषते पतिर्दन्निन इनस्य वसुनः पद आ ।उप ध्रजंतमद्रयो विधन्नित् ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣate ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ ináḥ ǀ inásya ǀ vásunaḥ ǀ padé ǀ ā́ ǀúpa ǀ dhrájantam ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ vidhán ǀ ít ǁ
verses.english_translation: HITHER he hastens to give, Lord of great riches, King of the mighty, to the place of treasure. The pressing-stones shall serve him speeding near us.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the lord of great wealth, the granter (of desires) comes (to the plural ce of sacrifice); he, the lord of lords, comes to the plural ce of affluence, (the altar); the stones prepare (the libation fo rhim) as he approaches.
verses.griffith_verse: HITHER he hastens to give, Lord of great riches, King of the mighty, to the place of treasure. The pressing-stones shall serve him speeding near us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स यो वृषा नरां न रोदस्योः श्रवोभिरस्ति जीवपीतसर्गः ।प्र यः सस्राणः शिश्रीत योनौ ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ásti ǀ jīvápīta-sargaḥ ǀprá ǀ yáḥ ǀ sasrāṇáḥ ǀ śiśrītá ǀ yónau ǁ
verses.english_translation: As Steer of men so Steer of earth and heaven by glory, he whose streams all life hath drunken, Who hasting forward rests upon the altar.
verses.wilson_translation: He, who is, as it were, the genitive rator of men as well as of heaven and earth, of whom creation has imbibed life, abides with his glories; he it is who, entering into the womb (of being), procreates (all living creatures).
verses.griffith_verse: As Steer of men so Steer of earth and heaven by glory, he whose streams all life hath drunken, Who hasting forward rests upon the altar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यः पुरं नार्मिणीमदीदेदत्यः कविर्नभन्यो नार्वा ।सूरो न रुरुक्वाञ्छतात्मा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ púram ǀ nā́rmiṇīm ǀ ádīdet ǀ átyaḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ nabhanyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ árvā ǀsū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ rurukvā́n ǀ śatá-ātmā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise Courser like the Steed of cloudy heaven, Bright like the Sun, with hundredfold existence.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is wise, and goes (wheresoever he will), like the rapid ethereal (wind), has lighted up the delightful spot, (the altar), and, identical with many forms, is radiant as the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise Courser like the Steed of cloudy heaven, Bright like the Sun, with hundredfold existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि द्विजन्मा त्री रोचनानि विश्वा रजांसि शुशुचानो अस्थात् ।होता यजिष्ठो अपां सधस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ dvi-jánmā ǀ trī́ ǀ rocanā́ni ǀ víśvā ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ śuśucānáḥ ǀ asthāt ǀhótā ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ sadhá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions, Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather.
verses.wilson_translation: He the twice-born, illuminating the three bright (regions), and shining over all the lustrous spheres, the adorable invoker of the gods, is present at the plural ce where the waters are collected.
verses.griffith_verse: He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions, Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं स होता यो द्विजन्मा विश्वा दधे वार्याणि श्रवस्या ।मर्तो यो अस्मै सुतुको ददाश ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ sáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ yáḥ ǀ dvi-jánmā ǀ víśvā ǀ dadhé ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀ śravasyā́ ǀmártaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ su-túkaḥ ǀ dadā́śa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing, The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: He is the offerer of oblations, who is of twofold birth; and, through desire of (sacrificial) food, has in his keeping all good things; the man who presents offerings to him is the parent of excellent offspring.
verses.griffith_verse: Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing, The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CL. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, thy faithful servant I call upon thee with many a gift,As in the keeping of the great inciting God; Thou who ne’er movest thee to aid the indolent, the godless man,Him who though wealthy never brings an offering. Splendid, O Singer, is that man, mightiest of the great in heaven.Agni, may we be foremost, we thy worshippers.

verses.sanskrit: पुरु त्वा दाश्वान्वोचेऽरिरग्ने तव स्विदा ।तोदस्येव शरण आ महस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: purú ǀ tvā ǀ dāśvā́n ǀ voce ǀ aríḥ ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ svit ǀ ā́ ǀtodásya-iva ǀ śaraṇé ǀ ā́ ǀ mahásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI, thy faithful servant I call upon thee with many a gift, As in the keeping of the great inciting God;
verses.wilson_translation: Presenting many offerings, I address you,Agni, ever coming into your presence (like a servant) in the dwelling of a mighty master.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI, thy faithful servant I call upon thee with many a gift, As in the keeping of the great inciting God;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्यनिनस्य धनिनः प्रहोषे चिदररुषः ।कदा चन प्रजिगतो अदेवयोः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ aninásya ǀ dhanínaḥ ǀ pra-hoṣé ǀ cit ǀ áraruṣaḥ ǀkadā́ ǀ caná ǀ pra-jígataḥ ǀ ádeva-yoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou who ne’er movest thee to aid the indolent, the godless man, Him who though wealthy never brings an offering.
verses.wilson_translation: (I ask you also to withhold your favour) from (those) two godless (person ns), from the rich man, who acknowledging you not as his lord, is chary of gifts at sacred rites, and from him who rarely praises (the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou who ne’er movest thee to aid the indolent, the godless man, Him who though wealthy never brings an offering.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स चंद्रो विप्र मर्त्यो महो व्राधंतमो दिवि ।प्रप्रेत्ते अग्ने वनुषः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ candráḥ ǀ vipra ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ vrā́dhan-tamaḥ ǀ diví ǀprá-pra ǀ ít ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Splendid, O Singer, is that man, mightiest of the great in heaven. Agni, may we be foremost, we thy worshippers.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Agni, the mortal (who propitiates you) becomes a moon in heaven, the most eminent of the great (deities); may we, therefore, ever be in an especial manner your worshippers.
verses.griffith_verse: Splendid, O Singer, is that man, mightiest of the great in heaven. Agni, may we be foremost, we thy worshippers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLI. Mitra and Varuṇa
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HEAVEN and earth trembled at the might and voice of him, whom, loved and Holy One, helper of all mankind,The wise who longed for spoil in fight for kine brought forth with power, a Friend, mid waters, at the sacrifice. As these, like friends, have done this work for you, these prompt servants of Purumīlha Soma-offerer,Give mental power to him who sings the sacred song, and hearken, Strong Ones, to the master of the house. The folk have glorified your birth from Earth and Heaven, to be extolled, ye Strong Ones, for your mighty power.Ye, when ye bring to singer and the rite, enjoy the sacrifice performed with holy praise and strength. The people prospers, Asuras! whom ye dearly love: ye, Righteous Ones, proclaim aloud the Holy Law.That efficacious power that comes from lofty heaven, ye bind unto the work, as to the pole an ox. On this great earth ye send your treasure down with might: unstained by dust, the crowding kine are in the stalls.Here in the neighbourhood they cry unto the Sun at morning and at evening, like swift birds of prey. The flames with curling tresses serve your sacrifice, whereto ye sing the song, Mitra and Varuṇa.Send down of your free will, prosper our holy songs: ye are sole Masters of the singer's hymn of praise. Whoso with sacrifices toiling brings you gifts, and worships, sage and priest, fulfilling your desire,—To him do ye draw nigh and taste his sacrifice. Come well-inclined to us unto our songs and prayer. With sacrifices and with milk they deck you first, ye Righteous Ones, as if through stirrings of the mind.To you they bring their hymns with their collected thought, while ye with earnest soul come to us gloriously. Rich strength of life is yours: ye, Heroes, have obtained through your surpassing powers rich far-extending might.Not the past days conjoined with nights, not rivers, not the Paṇis have attained your Godhead and your wealth.

verses.sanskrit: मित्रं न यं शिम्या गोषु गव्यवः स्वाध्यो विदथे अप्सु जीजनन् ।अरेजेतां रोदसी पाजसा गिरा प्रति प्रियं यजतं जनुषामवः ॥
verses.transliteration: mitrám ǀ ná ǀ yám ǀ śímyā ǀ góṣu ǀ gavyávaḥ ǀ su-ādhyáḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ ap-sú ǀ jī́janan ǀárejetām ǀ ródasī íti ǀ pā́jasā ǀ girā́ ǀ práti ǀ priyám ǀ yajatám ǀ janúṣām ǀ ávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: HEAVEN and earth trembled at the might and voice of him, whom, loved and Holy One, helper of all mankind, The wise who longed for spoil in fight for kine brought forth with power, a Friend, mid waters, at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth have been terrified by the strength and the noise (of him), whom pious worshippers, desirous of acquiring cattle, have genitive rated by their (sacred) acts, amidst the waters (of the firmament), at the sacrifice, as a friend for the preservation of living beings, the benefactor (of man), and entitled to adoration.
verses.griffith_verse: HEAVEN and earth trembled at the might and voice of him, whom, loved and Holy One, helper of all mankind, The wise who longed for spoil in fight for kine brought forth with power, a Friend, mid waters, at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्ध त्यद्वां पुरुमीळ्हस्य सोमिनः प्र मित्रासो न दधिरे स्वाभुवः ।अध क्रतुं विदतं गातुमर्चत उत श्रुतं वृषणा पस्त्यावतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ vām ǀ puru-mīḷhásya ǀ somínaḥ ǀ prá ǀ mitrā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ dadhiré ǀ su-ābhúvaḥ ǀádha ǀ krátum ǀ vidatam ǀ gātúm ǀ árcate ǀ utá ǀ śrutam ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ pastyá-vataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As these, like friends, have done this work for you, these prompt servants of Purumīlha Soma-offerer, Give mental power to him who sings the sacred song, and hearken, Strong Ones, to the master of the house.
verses.wilson_translation: Since they, (the priests), like friends, have prepared for you both, (Mitraand Varuṇaa libation) of the abundantly-flowing and spontaneous Soma, therefore do you consent to come to the rite of the worshipper, and listen, showerers (of blessings), to the (prayers of the) householdeṛ
verses.griffith_verse: As these, like friends, have done this work for you, these prompt servants of Purumīlha Soma-offerer, Give mental power to him who sings the sacred song, and hearken, Strong Ones, to the master of the house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां भूषन्क्षितयो जन्म रोदस्योः प्रवाच्यं वृषणा दक्षसे महे ।यदीमृताय भरथो यदर्वते प्र होत्रया शिम्या वीथो अध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ bhūṣan ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ jánma ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀ pra-vā́cyam ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ dákṣase ǀ mahé ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ bhárathaḥ ǀ yát ǀ árvate ǀ prá ǀ hótrayā ǀ śímyā ǀ vīthaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The folk have glorified your birth from Earth and Heaven, to be extolled, ye Strong Ones, for your mighty power. Ye, when ye bring to singer and the rite, enjoy the sacrifice performed with holy praise and strength.
verses.wilson_translation: For the sake (of obtaining) great vigour, showerers (of benefits), men glorify your birth from heaven and earth, which is to be extolled, inasmuch as you bestow (his desires) upon the worshipper (as the reward) of his sacrifice, and accept the rite (that is solemnized) with praise and oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: The folk have glorified your birth from Earth and Heaven, to be extolled, ye Strong Ones, for your mighty power. Ye, when ye bring to singer and the rite, enjoy the sacrifice performed with holy praise and strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सा क्षितिरसुर या महि प्रिय ऋतावानावृतमा घोषथो बृहत् ।युवं दिवो बृहतो दक्षमाभुवं गां न धुर्युप युंजाथे अपः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sā́ ǀ kṣitíḥ ǀ asurā ǀ yā́ ǀ máhi ǀ priyā́ ǀ ṛ́ta-vānau ǀ ṛtám ǀ ā́ ǀ ghoṣathaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀyuvám ǀ diváḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ dákṣam ǀ ā-bhúvam ǀ gā́m ǀ ná ǀ dhurí ǀ úpa ǀ yuñjāthe íti ǀ apáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The people prospers, Asuras! whom ye dearly love: ye, Righteous Ones, proclaim aloud the Holy Law. That efficacious power that comes from lofty heaven, ye bind unto the work, as to the pole an ox.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful divinities, most acceptable to you both is that spot, (where you are worshipped); accepters of sacrifice, proclaim the great ceremony (as duly performed); for you two connect the efficacious and comprehensive rise with the vast heaven, like a cow with a burden.
verses.griffith_verse: The people prospers, Asuras! whom ye dearly love: ye, Righteous Ones, proclaim aloud the Holy Law. That efficacious power that comes from lofty heaven, ye bind unto the work, as to the pole an ox.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मही अत्र महिना वारमृण्वथोऽरेणवस्तुज आ सद्मन्धेनवः ।स्वरंति ता उपरताति सूर्यमा निम्रुच उषसस्तक्ववीरिव ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ íti ǀ átra ǀ mahinā́ ǀ vā́ram ǀ ṛṇvathaḥ ǀ areṇávaḥ ǀ tújaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sádman ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀsváranti ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ upará-tāti ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ā́ ǀ ni-mrúcaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ takvavī́ḥ-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: On this great earth ye send your treasure down with might: unstained by dust, the crowding kine are in the stalls. Here in the neighbourhood they cry unto the Sun at morning and at evening, like swift birds of prey.
verses.wilson_translation: You bring (the cattle) to their acceptable (pasture) upon earth, whence the milk-yielding cows, protected by your power, return unharmed to their stalls; they cry to the sun (in heaven) above, both at evening and at dawn, as one (cries aloud) who detects a thief.
verses.griffith_verse: On this great earth ye send your treasure down with might: unstained by dust, the crowding kine are in the stalls. Here in the neighbourhood they cry unto the Sun at morning and at evening, like swift birds of prey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वामृताय केशिनीरनूषत मित्र यत्र वरुण गातुमर्चथः ।अव त्मना सृजतं पिन्वतं धियो युवं विप्रस्य मन्मनामिरज्यथः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ keśínīḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀ mítra ǀ yátra ǀ váruṇa ǀ gātúm ǀ árcathaḥ ǀáva ǀ tmánā ǀ sṛjátam ǀ pínvatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ víprasya ǀ mánmanām ǀ irajyathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The flames with curling tresses serve your sacrifice, whereto ye sing the song, Mitra and Varuṇa. Send down of your free will, prosper our holy songs: ye are sole Masters of the singer's hymn of praise.
verses.wilson_translation: The tresses of Agniminister,Mitraand Varuṇa, to your sacrifice, when you honour (with your presence) the sacrificial chamber; send down of your own accord (the rain), and prosper our offerings, for you have command over the praise of the pious men.
verses.griffith_verse: The flames with curling tresses serve your sacrifice, whereto ye sing the song, Mitra and Varuṇa. Send down of your free will, prosper our holy songs: ye are sole Masters of the singer's hymn of praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वां यज्ञैः शशमानो ह दाशति कविर्होता यजति मन्मसाधनः ।उपाह तं गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरमच्छा गिरः सुमतिं गंतमस्मयू ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ śaśamānáḥ ǀ ha ǀ dā́śati ǀ kavíḥ ǀ hótā ǀ yájati ǀ manma-sā́dhanaḥ ǀúpa ǀ áha ǀ tám ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ vītháḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ áccha ǀ gíraḥ ǀ su-matím ǀ gantam ǀ asmayū́ ítyasma-yū́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whoso with sacrifices toiling brings you gifts, and worships, sage and priest, fulfilling your desire,— To him do ye draw nigh and taste his sacrifice. Come well-inclined to us unto our songs and prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to the devout (worshipper), who, glorifying you, and providing (all that is) acceptable, presents you with oblations; (to him), the sage, the invoker, who offers you worship; accept his sacrifice; favourably disposed towards us, (accept) our praises.
verses.griffith_verse: Whoso with sacrifices toiling brings you gifts, and worships, sage and priest, fulfilling your desire,— To him do ye draw nigh and taste his sacrifice. Come well-inclined to us unto our songs and prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां यज्ञैः प्रथमा गोभिरंजत ऋतावाना मनसो न प्रयुक्तिषु ।भरंति वां मन्मना संयता गिरोऽदृप्यता मनसा रेवदाशाथे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ añjate ǀ ṛ́ta-vānā ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ prá-yuktiṣu ǀbháranti ǀ vām ǀ mánmanā ǀ sam-yátā ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ádṛpyatā ǀ mánasā ǀ revát ǀ āśāthe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: With sacrifices and with milk they deck you first, ye Righteous Ones, as if through stirrings of the mind. To you they bring their hymns with their collected thought, while ye with earnest soul come to us gloriously.
verses.wilson_translation: Accepter of sacrifices, you are the first whom (worshippers) propitiate with offerings, the produce of the cow; like (the application) of the mind (in the first instrumental nce) to the results (of the senses); hymns (prompted) by thoughts wholly intent upon you, celebrate (your praise); do you, with humble minds, bestow upon us wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: With sacrifices and with milk they deck you first, ye Righteous Ones, as if through stirrings of the mind. To you they bring their hymns with their collected thought, while ye with earnest soul come to us gloriously.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रेवद्वयो दधाथे रेवदाशाथे नरा मायाभिरितऊति माहिनं ।न वां द्यावोऽहभिर्नोत सिंधवो न देवत्वं पणयो नानशुर्मघं ॥
verses.transliteration: revát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhāthe íti ǀ revát ǀ āśāthe íti ǀ nárā ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ itá-ūti ǀ mā́hinam ǀná ǀ vām ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ utá ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ deva-tvám ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ānaśuḥ ǀ maghám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich strength of life is yours: ye, Heroes, have obtained through your surpassing powers rich far-extending might. Not the past days conjoined with nights, not rivers, not the Paṇis have attained your Godhead and your wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: You distribute food, accompanied by riches; you bestow upon us, leaders (of sacrifice), wealth, ample, and defended by your wise provisions; the days with the nights have not attained your divinity; neither have the rivers, nor have theasuras, and they have not obtained (your) wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich strength of life is yours: ye, Heroes, have obtained through your surpassing powers rich far-extending might. Not the past days conjoined with nights, not rivers, not the Paṇis have attained your Godhead and your wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLII. Mitra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE robes which ye put on abound with fatness: uninterrupted courses are your counsels.All falsehood, Mitra-Varuṇa! ye conquer, and closely cleave unto the Law Eternal. This might of theirs hath no one comprehended. True is the crushing word the sage hath uttered,The fearful four-edged bolt smites down the three-edged, and those who hate the Gods first fall and perish. The Footless Maid precedeth footed creatures. Who marketh, Mitra-Varuṇa, this your doing?The Babe Unborn supporteth this world's burthen, fulfilleth Law and overcometh falsehood. We look on him the darling of the Maidens, always advancing, never falling downward,Wearing inseparable, wide-spread raiment, Mitra's and Varuṇa's delightful glory. Unbridled Courser, born but not of horses, neighing he flieth on with back uplifted.The youthful love mystery thought-surpassing, praising in Mitra-Varuṇa, its glory. May the milch-kine who favour Māmateya prosper in this world him who loves devotion.May he, well skilled in rites, be food, and calling Aditi with his lips give us assistance. Gods, Mitra-Varuṇa, with love and worship, let me make you delight in this oblation.May our prayer be victorious in battles, may we have rain from heaven to make us prosper.

verses.sanskrit: युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे युवोरच्छिद्रा मंतवो ह सर्गाः ।अवातिरतमनृतानि विश्व ऋतेन मित्रावरुणा सचेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ vástrāṇi ǀ pīvasā́ ǀ vasāthe íti ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ ácchidrāḥ ǀ mántavaḥ ǀ ha ǀ sárgāḥ ǀáva ǀ atiratam ǀ ánṛtāni ǀ víśvā ǀ ṛténa ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE robes which ye put on abound with fatness: uninterrupted courses are your counsels. All falsehood, Mitra-Varuṇa! ye conquer, and closely cleave unto the Law Eternal.
verses.wilson_translation: Robust Mitraand Varuṇa, you wear vestments (of light); your natures are to be regarded as without defect; you annihilate all untruths; you associate (us) with sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: THE robes which ye put on abound with fatness: uninterrupted courses are your counsels. All falsehood, Mitra-Varuṇa! ye conquer, and closely cleave unto the Law Eternal.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतच्चन त्वो वि चिकेतदेषां सत्यो मंत्रः कविशस्त ऋघावान् ।त्रिरश्रिं हंति चतुरश्रिरुग्रो देवनिदो ह प्रथमा अजूर्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: etát ǀ caná ǀ tvaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ciketat ǀ eṣām ǀ satyáḥ ǀ mántraḥ ǀ kavi-śastáḥ ǀ ṛ́ghāvān ǀtriḥ-áśrim ǀ hanti ǀ cátuḥ-aśriḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ deva-nídaḥ ǀ ha ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ ajūryan ǁ
verses.english_translation: This might of theirs hath no one comprehended. True is the crushing word the sage hath uttered, The fearful four-edged bolt smites down the three-edged, and those who hate the Gods first fall and perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He amongst those (who are your followers), who observes truth, who is considerate, who is commended by the wise, who is able to (inflict) harm, carefully weighs (the means whereby), fierce and well-armed, he slays (a foe) less efficiently accoutred, and (by which) the revilers of the gods, however mighty, may perish.
verses.griffith_verse: This might of theirs hath no one comprehended. True is the crushing word the sage hath uttered, The fearful four-edged bolt smites down the three-edged, and those who hate the Gods first fall and perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपादेति प्रथमा पद्वतीनां कस्तद्वां मित्रावरुणा चिकेत ।गर्भो भारं भरत्या चिदस्य ऋतं पिपर्त्यनृतं नि तारीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́t ǀ eti ǀ prathamā́ ǀ pat-vátīnām ǀ káḥ ǀ tát ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketa ǀgárbhaḥ ǀ bhārám ǀ bharati ǀ ā́ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ ṛtám ǀ píparti ǀ ánṛtam ǀ ní ǀ tārīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Footless Maid precedeth footed creatures. Who marketh, Mitra-Varuṇa, this your doing? The Babe Unborn supporteth this world's burthen, fulfilleth Law and overcometh falsehood.
verses.wilson_translation: Who knows,Mitraand Varuṇa, that it is your doing, that the footless dawn is the precursor of footed beings; and that your infant (progeny, the sun), sustains the burden of this (world); he diffuses (the) truth (of light), and disperses the falsehood (of darkness).
verses.griffith_verse: The Footless Maid precedeth footed creatures. Who marketh, Mitra-Varuṇa, this your doing? The Babe Unborn supporteth this world's burthen, fulfilleth Law and overcometh falsehood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रयंतमित्परि जारं कनीनां पश्यामसि नोपनिपद्यमानं ।अनवपृग्णा वितता वसानं प्रियं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम ॥
verses.transliteration: pra-yántam ǀ ít ǀ pári ǀ jārám ǀ kanī́nām ǀ páśyāmasi ǀ ná ǀ upa-nipádyamānam ǀánava-pṛgṇā ǀ ví-tatā ǀ vásānam ǀ priyám ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: We look on him the darling of the Maidens, always advancing, never falling downward, Wearing inseparable, wide-spread raiment, Mitra's and Varuṇa's delightful glory.
verses.wilson_translation: We behold the lover of the maiden (dawns), ever in movement, never resting for an instrumental nt, wearing inseparable and diffusive (radiance), the beloved abode of Mitraand Varuṇa
verses.griffith_verse: We look on him the darling of the Maidens, always advancing, never falling downward, Wearing inseparable, wide-spread raiment, Mitra's and Varuṇa's delightful glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुरर्वा कनिक्रदत्पतयदूर्ध्वसानुः ।अचित्तं ब्रह्म जुजुषुर्युवानः प्र मित्रे धाम वरुणे गृणंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: anaśváḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ anabhīśúḥ ǀ árvā ǀ kánikradat ǀ patayat ǀ ūrdhvá-sānuḥ ǀacíttam ǀ bráhma ǀ jujuṣuḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ mitré ǀ dhā́ma ǀ váruṇe ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unbridled Courser, born but not of horses, neighing he flieth on with back uplifted. The youthful love mystery thought-surpassing, praising in Mitra-Varuṇa, its glory.
verses.wilson_translation: Without steeds, without stay, (he is nevertheless) borne swift-moving and loud-sounding; he travels, ascending higher and higher, connecting the inconceivable mystery (of sacred rites) with the radiance (abiding) in Mitraand Varuṇa, (which men), eulogizing, glorify.
verses.griffith_verse: Unbridled Courser, born but not of horses, neighing he flieth on with back uplifted. The youthful love mystery thought-surpassing, praising in Mitra-Varuṇa, its glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ धेनवो मामतेयमवंतीर्ब्रह्मप्रियं पीपयन्त्सस्मिन्नूधन् ।पित्वो भिक्षेत वयुनानि विद्वानासाविवासन्नदितिमुरुष्येत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ māmateyám ǀ ávantīḥ ǀ brahma-príyam ǀ pīpayan ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǀpitváḥ ǀ bhikṣeta ǀ vayúnāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ āsā́ ǀ ā-vívāsan ǀ áditim ǀ uruṣyet ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the milch-kine who favour Māmateya prosper in this world him who loves devotion. May he, well skilled in rites, be food, and calling Aditi with his lips give us assistance.
verses.wilson_translation: May the cow, propitious to the devout son of Mamatā, be possessed of well-filled udders; knowing the rites (necessary to be performed), let him beg (the residue) of the offerings for his eating, and worshipping (you both) complete the perfect (ceremony).
verses.griffith_verse: May the milch-kine who favour Māmateya prosper in this world him who loves devotion. May he, well skilled in rites, be food, and calling Aditi with his lips give us assistance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं नमसा देवाववसा ववृत्यां ।अस्माकं ब्रह्म पृतनासु सह्या अस्माकं वृष्टिर्दिव्या सुपारा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ havyá-juṣṭim ǀ námasā ǀ devau ǀ ávasā ǀ vavṛtyām ǀasmā́kam ǀ bráhma ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ sahyāḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ ǀ divyā́ ǀ su-pārā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, Mitra-Varuṇa, with love and worship, let me make you delight in this oblation. May our prayer be victorious in battles, may we have rain from heaven to make us prosper.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Mitraand Varuṇa, may I render the oblation acceptable to you with reverence and prayer; may the sacred rite enable us (to overcome) in battles, and may the heavenly rain be to us the means of satisfying our wants.
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, Mitra-Varuṇa, with love and worship, let me make you delight in this oblation. May our prayer be victorious in battles, may we have rain from heaven to make us prosper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLIII. Mitra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WE worship with our reverence and oblations you, Mitra Varuṇa, accordant, mighty,So that with us, ye Twain whose backs are sprinkled with oil, the priests with oil and hymns support you. Your praise is like a mighty power, an impulse: to you, Twain Gods, a well-formed hymn is offered,As the priest decks yon, Strong Ones, in assemblies, and the prince fain to worship you for blessings. O Mitra-Varuṇa, Aditi the Milch-cow streams for the rite, for folk who bring oblation,When in the assembly he who worships moves you, like to a human priest, with gifts presented. So may the kine and heavenly Waters pour you sweet drink in families that make you joyful.Of this may he, the ancient House-Lord, give us. Enjoy, drink of the milk the cow provideth.

verses.sanskrit: यजामहे वां महः सजोषा हव्येभिर्मित्रावरुणा नमोभिः ।घृतैर्घृतस्नू अध यद्वामस्मे अध्वर्यवो न धीतिभिर्भरंति ॥
verses.transliteration: yájāmahe ǀ vām ǀ maháḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀghṛtáiḥ ǀ ghṛtasnū íti ghṛta-snū ǀ ádha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ asmé íti ǀ adhvaryávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ bháranti ǁ
verses.english_translation: WE worship with our reverence and oblations you, Mitra Varuṇa, accordant, mighty, So that with us, ye Twain whose backs are sprinkled with oil, the priests with oil and hymns support you.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty Mitraand Varuṇa, dispensers of butter, we worship you, rejoicing, with oblations; with reverential homage, and with (offerings of) water; so that our ministrant priests may propitiate you by (our) devotions.
verses.griffith_verse: WE worship with our reverence and oblations you, Mitra Varuṇa, accordant, mighty, So that with us, ye Twain whose backs are sprinkled with oil, the priests with oil and hymns support you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रस्तुतिर्वां धाम न प्रयुक्तिरयामि मित्रावरुणा सुवृक्तिः ।अनक्ति यद्वां विदथेषु होता सुम्नं वां सूरिर्वृषणावियक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá-stutiḥ ǀ vām ǀ dhā́ma ǀ ná ǀ prá-yuktiḥ ǀ áyāmi ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ su-vṛktíḥ ǀanákti ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ hótā ǀ sumnám ǀ vām ǀ sūríḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ íyakṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your praise is like a mighty power, an impulse: to you, Twain Gods, a well-formed hymn is offered, As the priest decks yon, Strong Ones, in assemblies, and the prince fain to worship you for blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: The purpose of worshipping you,Mitraand Varuṇa, is not the performance, but (even by so much) I may attain to your glory, and there is acquittance (of my duty); for when the priest offers you oblations in sacrifices, then the pious man, showerers (of benefits), being desirous of worshipping you, (obtains) felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Your praise is like a mighty power, an impulse: to you, Twain Gods, a well-formed hymn is offered, As the priest decks yon, Strong Ones, in assemblies, and the prince fain to worship you for blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पीपाय धेनुरदितिर्ऋताय जनाय मित्रावरुणा हविर्दे ।हिनोति यद्वां विदथे सपर्यन्त्स रातहव्यो मानुषो न होता ॥
verses.transliteration: pīpā́ya ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ jánāya ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ haviḥ-dé ǀhinóti ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ vidáthe ǀ saparyán ǀ sáḥ ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Mitra-Varuṇa, Aditi the Milch-cow streams for the rite, for folk who bring oblation, When in the assembly he who worships moves you, like to a human priest, with gifts presented.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the productive cow,Mitraand Varuṇa, furnish abundant nutriment to the pious man who presents you with oblations, as when Rātahavya, glorifying you, propitiates you in the solemnity, like the ministrant priest of a man (who instrumental tutes the rite).
verses.griffith_verse: O Mitra-Varuṇa, Aditi the Milch-cow streams for the rite, for folk who bring oblation, When in the assembly he who worships moves you, like to a human priest, with gifts presented.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वंधो गाव आपश्च पीपयंत देवीः ।उतो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पतिर्दन्वीतं पातं पयस उस्रियायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vām ǀ vikṣú ǀ mádyāsu ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ca ǀ pīpayanta ǀ devī́ḥ ǀutó íti ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pūrvyáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ vītám ǀ pātám ǀ páyasaḥ ǀ usríyāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may the kine and heavenly Waters pour you sweet drink in families that make you joyful. Of this may he, the ancient House-Lord, give us. Enjoy, drink of the milk the cow provideth.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine cows, and the waters, supply you with (sacrificial) food, for the prosperity of the people whom you favour; or may (Agni), the former protector of this (our patron), be the donor (of the oblation); eat (of the butter and curds), drink of the milk of the kine.
verses.griffith_verse: So may the kine and heavenly Waters pour you sweet drink in families that make you joyful. Of this may he, the ancient House-Lord, give us. Enjoy, drink of the milk the cow provideth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLIV. Viṣṇu
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I WILL declare the mighty deeds of Viṣṇu, of him who measured out the earthly regions,Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely striding. For this his mighty deed is Viṣṇu lauded, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming;He within whose three wide-extended paces all living creatures have their habitation. Let the hymn lift itself as strength to Viṣṇu, the Bull far-striding, dwelling on the mountains,Him who alone with triple step hath measured this common dwelling-place, long, far extended. Him whose three places that are filled with sweetness, imperishable, joy as it may list them,Who verily alone upholds the threefold, the earth, the heaven, and all living creatures. May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy.For there springs, close akin to the Wide-Strider, the well of meath in Viṣṇu's highest footstep. Fain would we go unto your dwelling-places where there are many-horned and nimble oxen,For mightily, there, shineth down upon us the widely-striding Bull's sublimest mansion.

verses.sanskrit: विष्णोर्नु कं वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यः पार्थिवानि विममे रजांसि ।यो अस्कभायदुत्तरं सधस्थं विचक्रमाणस्त्रेधोरुगायः ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣṇoḥ ǀ nú ǀ kam ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ prá ǀ vocam ǀ yáḥ ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ vi-mamé ǀ rájāṃsi ǀyáḥ ǀ áskabhāyat ǀ út-taram ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ vi-cakramāṇáḥ ǀ tredhā́ ǀ uru-gāyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I WILL declare the mighty deeds of Viṣṇu, of him who measured out the earthly regions, Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely striding.
verses.wilson_translation: Earnetly I glorify the exploits of Viṣṇu, who made thethree worlds; who sustained the lofty aggregate site (of the spheres); thrice traversing (the whole); who is praised by the exalted.
verses.griffith_verse: I WILL declare the mighty deeds of Viṣṇu, of him who measured out the earthly regions, Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely striding.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः ।यस्योरुषु त्रिषु विक्रमणेष्वधिक्षियंति भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tát ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ stavate ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ kucaráḥ ǀ giri-sthā́ḥ ǀyásya ǀ urúṣu ǀ triṣú ǀ vi-krámaṇeṣu ǀ adhi-kṣiyánti ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: For this his mighty deed is Viṣṇu lauded, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming; He within whose three wide-extended paces all living creatures have their habitation.
verses.wilson_translation: Viṣṇuis therefore glorified, that by his prowess he is like a fearful, ravenous, and mountain-haunting wild beast, and because of that in his three paces all worlds abide.
verses.griffith_verse: For this his mighty deed is Viṣṇu lauded, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming; He within whose three wide-extended paces all living creatures have their habitation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र विष्णवे शूषमेतु मन्म गिरिक्षित उरुगायाय वृष्णे ।य इदं दीर्घं प्रयतं सधस्थमेको विममे त्रिभिरित्पदेभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ víṣṇave ǀ śūṣám ǀ etu ǀ mánma ǀ giri-kṣíte ǀ uru-gāyā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀyáḥ ǀ idám ǀ dīrghám ǀ prá-yatam ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ ékaḥ ǀ vi-mamé ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ít ǀ padébhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the hymn lift itself as strength to Viṣṇu, the Bull far-striding, dwelling on the mountains, Him who alone with triple step hath measured this common dwelling-place, long, far extended.
verses.wilson_translation: May acceptable vigour attend Viṣṇu, who abides in prayer, the hymned of many, the showerer (of benefits), who alone made, by three steps, this spacious and durable aggregate (of thethree worlds).
verses.griffith_verse: Let the hymn lift itself as strength to Viṣṇu, the Bull far-striding, dwelling on the mountains, Him who alone with triple step hath measured this common dwelling-place, long, far extended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य त्री पूर्णा मधुना पदान्यक्षीयमाणा स्वधया मदंति ।य उ त्रिधातु पृथिवीमुत द्यामेको दाधार भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ trī́ ǀ pūrṇā́ ǀ mádhunā ǀ padā́ni ǀ ákṣīyamāṇā ǀ svadháyā ǀ mádanti ǀyáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǀ ékaḥ ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him whose three places that are filled with sweetness, imperishable, joy as it may list them, Who verily alone upholds the threefold, the earth, the heaven, and all living creatures.
verses.wilson_translation: Whose three imperishable paces, filled with ambrosia, delight (mankind) with sacred food; who verily alone upholds the three elements, and earth and heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Him whose three places that are filled with sweetness, imperishable, joy as it may list them, Who verily alone upholds the threefold, the earth, the heaven, and all living creatures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्यां नरो यत्र देवयवो मदंति ।उरुक्रमस्य स हि बंधुरित्था विष्णोः पदे परमे मध्व उत्सः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ asya ǀ priyám ǀ abhí ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ aśyām ǀ náraḥ ǀ yátra ǀ deva-yávaḥ ǀ mádanti ǀuru-kramásya ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ bándhuḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ padé ǀ paramé ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ útsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy. For there springs, close akin to the Wide-Strider, the well of meath in Viṣṇu's highest footstep.
verses.wilson_translation: May I attain his favourite path, in which god-seeking men delight; (the path) of that wide-stepping Viṣṇu, in whose exalted station there is a (perpetual) flow of felicity; for to such a degree is he the friend (of the pious).
verses.griffith_verse: May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy. For there springs, close akin to the Wide-Strider, the well of meath in Viṣṇu's highest footstep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता वां वास्तून्युश्मसि गमध्यै यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगा अयासः ।अत्राह तदुरुगायस्य वृष्णः परमं पदमव भाति भूरि ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ vā́stūni ǀ uśmasi ǀ gámadhyai ǀ yátra ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ bhū́ri-śṛṅgāḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ tát ǀ uru-gāyásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ paramám ǀ padám ǀ áva ǀ bhāti ǀ bhū́ri ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fain would we go unto your dwelling-places where there are many-horned and nimble oxen, For mightily, there, shineth down upon us the widely-striding Bull's sublimest mansion.
verses.wilson_translation: We pary (to Viṣṇu) that you may both go to those regions where the many-pointed and wide-spreading rays (of light expand); for here the supreme station of the many-hymned, the showerer (of benefits), shines (with) great (splendour).
verses.griffith_verse: Fain would we go unto your dwelling-places where there are many-horned and nimble oxen, For mightily, there, shineth down upon us the widely-striding Bull's sublimest mansion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLV. Viṣṇu-Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To the great Hero, him who sets his mind thereon, and Viṣṇu, praise aloud in song your draught of juice,—Gods ne’er beguiled, who borne as ’twere by noble steed, have stood upon the lofty ridges of the hills. Your Soma-drinker keeps afar your furious rush, Indra and Viṣṇu, when ye come with all your might.That which hath been directed well at mortal man, bow-armed Kṛśānu's arrow, ye turn far aside. These offerings increase his mighty manly strength: he brings both Parents down to share the genial flow.He lowers, though a son, the Father's highest name; the third is that which is high in the light of heaven. We laud this manly power of him the Mighty One, preserver, inoffensive, bounteous and benign;His who strode, widely pacing, with three steppings forth over the realms of earth for freedom and for life. A mortal man, when he beholds two steps of him who looks upon the light, is restless with amaze.But his third step doth no one venture to approach, no, nor the feathered birds of air who fly with wings. He, like a rounded wheel, hath in swift motion set his ninety racing steeds together with the four.Developed, vast in form, with those who sing forth praise, a youth, no more a child, he cometh to our call.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वः पांतमंधसो धियायते महे शूराय विष्णवे चार्चत ।या सानुनि पर्वतानामदाभ्या महस्तस्थतुरर्वतेव साधुना ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pā́ntam ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ dhiyā-yaté ǀ mahé ǀ śū́rāya ǀ víṣṇave ǀ ca ǀ arcata ǀyā́ ǀ sā́nuni ǀ párvatānām ǀ ádābhyā ǀ maháḥ ǀ tasthátuḥ ǀ árvatā-iva ǀ sādhúnā ǁ
verses.english_translation: To the great Hero, him who sets his mind thereon, and Viṣṇu, praise aloud in song your draught of juice,— Gods ne’er beguiled, who borne as ’twere by noble steed, have stood upon the lofty ridges of the hills.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer your nutritious viands to the great hero, (Indra), who is plural ased by praise, and to Viṣṇu, the two invincible deities who ride upon the radiant summit of the clouds as upon a well-trained steed.
verses.griffith_verse: To the great Hero, him who sets his mind thereon, and Viṣṇu, praise aloud in song your draught of juice,— Gods ne’er beguiled, who borne as ’twere by noble steed, have stood upon the lofty ridges of the hills.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमीवतोरिंद्राविष्णू सुतपा वामुरुष्यति ।या मर्त्याय प्रतिधीयमानमित्कृशानोरस्तुरसनामुरुष्यथः ॥
verses.transliteration: tveṣám ǀ itthā́ ǀ sam-áraṇam ǀ śímī-vatoḥ ǀ índrāviṣṇū íti ǀ suta-pā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ uruṣyati ǀyā́ ǀ mártyāya ǀ prati-dhīyámānam ǀ ít ǀ kṛśā́noḥ ǀ ástuḥ ǀ asanā́m ǀ uruṣyáthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your Soma-drinker keeps afar your furious rush, Indra and Viṣṇu, when ye come with all your might. That which hath been directed well at mortal man, bow-armed Kṛśānu's arrow, ye turn far aside.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Viṣṇu, the devout worshipper glorifies the radiant approach of you two, who are the granters of desires, and who bestow upon the mortal who worships you an immediately-receivable (reward), through the distribution of that fire which is the scatterer (of desired blessings).
verses.griffith_verse: Your Soma-drinker keeps afar your furious rush, Indra and Viṣṇu, when ye come with all your might. That which hath been directed well at mortal man, bow-armed Kṛśānu's arrow, ye turn far aside.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता ईं वर्धंति मह्यस्य पौंस्यं नि मातरा नयति रेतसे भुजे ।दधाति पुत्रोऽवरं परं पितुर्नाम तृतीयमधि रोचने दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ īm ǀ vardhanti ǀ máhi ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ ní ǀ mātárā ǀ nayati ǀ rétase ǀ bhujé ǀdádhāti ǀ putráḥ ǀ ávaram ǀ páram ǀ pitúḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ tṛtī́yam ǀ ádhi ǀ rocané ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These offerings increase his mighty manly strength: he brings both Parents down to share the genial flow. He lowers, though a son, the Father's highest name; the third is that which is high in the light of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: These (oblations) augment his (Indra's), mighty manhood, by which he fits the parents (of all creatures heaven and earth), for genitive ration and enjoyment; whereby, in the upper region of the sky, the son has an inferior and superior appellation, and a third (name) of father.
verses.griffith_verse: These offerings increase his mighty manly strength: he brings both Parents down to share the genial flow. He lowers, though a son, the Father's highest name; the third is that which is high in the light of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तत्तदिदस्य पौंस्यं गृणीमसीनस्य त्रातुरवृकस्य मीळ्हुषः ।यः पार्थिवानि त्रिभिरिद्विगामभिरुरु क्रमिष्टोरुगायाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tát-tat ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀ inásya ǀ trātúḥ ǀ avṛkásya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ ít ǀ vígāma-bhiḥ ǀ urú ǀ krámiṣṭa ǀ uru-gāyā́ya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: We laud this manly power of him the Mighty One, preserver, inoffensive, bounteous and benign; His who strode, widely pacing, with three steppings forth over the realms of earth for freedom and for life.
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore, verily, we celebrate the manhood of that lord (of all), the preserver, the innocuous, the vigorous who traversed the three regions with three wide steps in different directions for the many-praised (preservation of) existence.
verses.griffith_verse: We laud this manly power of him the Mighty One, preserver, inoffensive, bounteous and benign; His who strode, widely pacing, with three steppings forth over the realms of earth for freedom and for life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वे इदस्य क्रमणे स्वर्दृशोऽभिख्याय मर्त्यो भुरण्यति ।तृतीयमस्य नकिरा दधर्षति वयश्चन पतयंतः पतत्रिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ krámaṇe íti ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ abhi-khyā́ya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ bhuraṇyati ǀtṛtī́yam ǀ asya ǀ nákiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dadharṣati ǀ váyaḥ ǀ caná ǀ patáyantaḥ ǀ patatríṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A mortal man, when he beholds two steps of him who looks upon the light, is restless with amaze. But his third step doth no one venture to approach, no, nor the feathered birds of air who fly with wings.
verses.wilson_translation: Man glorifying (Viṣṇu), tracks two steps of that heaven-beholding (deity), but he apprehends not the third; nor can the soaring-winged birds (pursue it).
verses.griffith_verse: A mortal man, when he beholds two steps of him who looks upon the light, is restless with amaze. But his third step doth no one venture to approach, no, nor the feathered birds of air who fly with wings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्भिः साकं नवतिं च नामभिश्चक्रं न वृत्तं व्यतीँरवीविपत् ।बृहच्छरीरो विमिमान ऋक्वभिर्युवाकुमारः प्रत्येत्याहवं ॥
verses.transliteration: catúḥ-bhiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ nā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ ná ǀ vṛttám ǀ vyátīn ǀ avīvipat ǀbṛhát-śarīraḥ ǀ vi-mímānaḥ ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ ákumāraḥ ǀ práti ǀ eti ǀ ā-havám ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, like a rounded wheel, hath in swift motion set his ninety racing steeds together with the four. Developed, vast in form, with those who sing forth praise, a youth, no more a child, he cometh to our call.
verses.wilson_translation: He causes, by his gyrations, ninety and four periodical revolutions, like a circular wheel, vast of body, and evolving in many forms, through the praises (addressed to him); ever young, though not infantine, he comes at our invocations.
verses.griffith_verse: He, like a rounded wheel, hath in swift motion set his ninety racing steeds together with the four. Developed, vast in form, with those who sing forth praise, a youth, no more a child, he cometh to our call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLVI. Viṣṇu
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FAR-SHINING, widely famed, going thy wonted way, fed with the oil, be helpful. Mitra-like, to us.So, Viṣṇu, e’en the wise must swell thy song of praise, and he who hath oblations pay thee solemn rites. He who brings gifts to him the Ancient and the Last, to Viṣṇu who ordains, together with his Spouse,Who tells the lofty birth of him the Lofty One, shall verily surpass in glory e’en his peer. Him have ye satisfied, singers, as well as ye know, primeval germ of Order even from his birth.Ye, knowing e’en his name, have told it forth: may we, Viṣṇu, enjoy the grace of thee the Mighty One. The Sovran Varuṇa and both the Aśvins wait on this the will of him who guides the Marut host.Viṣṇu hath power supreme and might that finds the day, and with his Friend unbars the stable of the kine. Even he the Heavenly One who came for fellowship, Viṣṇu to Indra, godly to the godlier,Who Maker, throned in three worlds, helps the Āryan man, and gives the worshipper his share of Holy Law.

verses.sanskrit: भवा मित्रो न शेव्यो घृतासुतिर्विभूतद्युम्न एवया उ सप्रथाः ।अधा ते विष्णो विदुषा चिदर्ध्यः स्तोमो यज्ञश्च राध्यो हविष्मता ॥
verses.transliteration: bháva ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śévyaḥ ǀ ghṛtá-āsutiḥ ǀ víbhūta-dyumnaḥ ǀ eva-yā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sa-práthāḥ ǀádha ǀ te ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ vidúṣā ǀ cit ǀ árdhyaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ca ǀ rā́dhyaḥ ǀ havíṣmatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: FAR-SHINING, widely famed, going thy wonted way, fed with the oil, be helpful. Mitra-like, to us. So, Viṣṇu, e’en the wise must swell thy song of praise, and he who hath oblations pay thee solemn rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Be (to us),Viṣṇu, like a friend, the giver of happiness, the acepter of oblations, abounding with food, the granter of protection, and every way accessible; on which account your praise is to be repeatedly recited by the wise, and your worship to be celebrated by the offerer of oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: FAR-SHINING, widely famed, going thy wonted way, fed with the oil, be helpful. Mitra-like, to us. So, Viṣṇu, e’en the wise must swell thy song of praise, and he who hath oblations pay thee solemn rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः पूर्व्याय वेधसे नवीयसे सुमज्जानये विष्णवे ददाशति ।यो जातमस्य महतो महि ब्रवत्सेदु श्रवोभिर्युज्यं चिदभ्यसत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀ vedháse ǀ návīyase ǀ sumát-jānaye ǀ víṣṇave ǀ dádāśati ǀyáḥ ǀ jātám ǀ asya ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ máhi ǀ brávat ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ yújyam ǀ cit ǀ abhí ǀ asat ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who brings gifts to him the Ancient and the Last, to Viṣṇu who ordains, together with his Spouse, Who tells the lofty birth of him the Lofty One, shall verily surpass in glory e’en his peer.
verses.wilson_translation: He who presents (offerings) to Viṣṇu, the ancient, the creator, the recent, the self-born; he who celebrates the great birth of that mighty one; he verily possessed of abundance, attains (the station) that is to be sought (by all).
verses.griffith_verse: He who brings gifts to him the Ancient and the Last, to Viṣṇu who ordains, together with his Spouse, Who tells the lofty birth of him the Lofty One, shall verily surpass in glory e’en his peer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमु स्तोतारः पूर्व्यं यथा विद ऋतस्य गर्भं जनुषा पिपर्तन ।आस्य जानंतो नाम चिद्विवक्तन महस्ते विष्णो सुमतिं भजामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stotāraḥ ǀ pūrvyám ǀ yáthā ǀ vidá ǀ ṛtásya ǀ gárbham ǀ janúṣā ǀ pipartana ǀā́ ǀ asya ǀ jānántaḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ cit ǀ vivaktana ǀ maháḥ ǀ te ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ su-matím ǀ bhajāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him have ye satisfied, singers, as well as ye know, primeval germ of Order even from his birth. Ye, knowing e’en his name, have told it forth: may we, Viṣṇu, enjoy the grace of thee the Mighty One.
verses.wilson_translation: Hymners, propitiate of your own accord that ancient Viṣṇu, since you know him as the germ of sacrifice, cognizant of his greatness, celebrate his name; may we, Viṣṇu, enjoy your favour.
verses.griffith_verse: Him have ye satisfied, singers, as well as ye know, primeval germ of Order even from his birth. Ye, knowing e’en his name, have told it forth: may we, Viṣṇu, enjoy the grace of thee the Mighty One.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विना क्रतुं सचंत मारुतस्य वेधसः ।दाधार दक्षमुत्तममहर्विदं व्रजं च विष्णुः सखिवाँ अपोर्णुते ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ asya ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ tám ǀ aśvínā ǀ krátum ǀ sacanta ǀ mā́rutasya ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀdādhā́ra ǀ dákṣam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ ahaḥ-vídam ǀ vrajám ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ sákhi-vān ǀ apa-ūrṇuté ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Sovran Varuṇa and both the Aśvins wait on this the will of him who guides the Marut host. Viṣṇu hath power supreme and might that finds the day, and with his Friend unbars the stable of the kine.
verses.wilson_translation: The royal Varuṇaassociates (himself) with the sacrifice of the pious worshipper, assisted by the company of the priests; the Aśvins(unite with it);Viṣṇu, with his friend (Indra), possesses supreme heaven-conferring power, and sits upon the clouds.
verses.griffith_verse: The Sovran Varuṇa and both the Aśvins wait on this the will of him who guides the Marut host. Viṣṇu hath power supreme and might that finds the day, and with his Friend unbars the stable of the kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यो विवाय सचथाय दैव्य इंद्राय विष्णुः सुकृते सुकृत्तरः ।वेधा अजिन्वत्त्रिषधस्थ आर्यमृतस्य भागे यजमानमाभजत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vivā́ya ǀ sacáthāya ǀ dáivyaḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ sukṛ́t-taraḥ ǀvedhā́ḥ ǀ ajinvat ǀ tri-sadhastháḥ ǀ ā́ryam ǀ ṛtásya ǀ bhāgé ǀ yájamānam ǀ ā́ ǀ abhajat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even he the Heavenly One who came for fellowship, Viṣṇu to Indra, godly to the godlier, Who Maker, throned in three worlds, helps the Āryan man, and gives the worshipper his share of Holy Law.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Viṣṇu, the best of the doers of good deeds, who came to the pious instrumental tutor of the rite, to assist (at its celebration), knowing (the desire of the worshipper), and present at the three connected periods (of worship), shows favour to te Arya, and admits the author if the ceremony to a share of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Even he the Heavenly One who came for fellowship, Viṣṇu to Indra, godly to the godlier, Who Maker, throned in three worlds, helps the Āryan man, and gives the worshipper his share of Holy Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLVII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI is wakened: Sūrya riseth from the earth. Mighty, refulgent Dawn hath shone with all her light.The Aśvins have equipped their chariot for the course. God Savitar hath moved the folk in sundry ways. When, Aśvins, ye equip your very mighty car, bedew, ye Twain, our power with honey and with oil.To our devotion give victorious strength in war: may we win riches in the heroes' strife for spoil. Nigh to us come the Aśvins' lauded three-wheeled car, the car laden with meath and drawn by fleet-foot steeds,Three-seated, opulent, bestowing all delight. may it bring weal to us, to cattle and to men. Bring hither nourishment for us, ye Aśvins Twain; sprinkle us with your whip that drops with honey-dew.Prolong our days of life, wipe out our trespasses; destroy our foes, be our companions and our Friends. Ye store the germ of life in female creatures, ye lay it up within all living beings.Ye have sent forth, O Aśvins passing mighty, the fire, the sovrans of the wood, the waters, Leeches are ye with medicines to heal us, and charioteers are ye with skill in driving.Ye Strong, give sway to him who brings oblation and with his heart pours out his gift before you.

verses.sanskrit: अबोध्यग्निर्ज्म उदेति सूर्यो व्युषाश्चंद्रा मह्यावो अर्चिषा ।आयुक्षातामश्विना यातवे रथं प्रासावीद्देवः सविता जगत्पृथक् ॥
verses.transliteration: ábodhi ǀ agníḥ ǀ jmáḥ ǀ út ǀ eti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ví ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ candrā́ ǀ mahī́ ǀ āvaḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀáyukṣātām ǀ aśvínā ǀ yā́tave ǀ rátham ǀ prá ǀ asāvīt ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ jágat ǀ pṛ́thak ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI is wakened: Sūrya riseth from the earth. Mighty, refulgent Dawn hath shone with all her light. The Aśvins have equipped their chariot for the course. God Savitar hath moved the folk in sundry ways.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis awakened upon earth; the Sun rises; the spreading dawn, exhilarating (all) by her radiance, has dispersed (the darkness); harness, (therefore),Aśvinsyour chariot, to come (to the sacrifice), that the divine Savitāmay animate allbeings to (the performance of) their several (duties).
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI is wakened: Sūrya riseth from the earth. Mighty, refulgent Dawn hath shone with all her light. The Aśvins have equipped their chariot for the course. God Savitar hath moved the folk in sundry ways.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्युंजाथे वृषणमश्विना रथं घृतेन नो मधुना क्षत्रमुक्षतं ।अस्माकं ब्रह्म पृतनासु जिन्वतं वयं धना शूरसाता भजेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ yuñjā́the íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ aśvinā ǀ rátham ǀ ghṛténa ǀ naḥ ǀ mádhunā ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ukṣatam ǀasmā́kam ǀ bráhma ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ jinvatam ǀ vayám ǀ dhánā ǀ śū́ra-sātā ǀ bhajemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Aśvins, ye equip your very mighty car, bedew, ye Twain, our power with honey and with oil. To our devotion give victorious strength in war: may we win riches in the heroes' strife for spoil.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Aśvins, you harness your bounty-shedding chariot, refresh our strength with trickling honey; bestow (abundant) food upon our people; may we acquire riches in the strife of heroes.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Aśvins, ye equip your very mighty car, bedew, ye Twain, our power with honey and with oil. To our devotion give victorious strength in war: may we win riches in the heroes' strife for spoil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वाङ् त्रिचक्रो मधुवाहनो रथो जीराश्वो अश्विनोर्यातु सुष्टुतः ।त्रिवंधुरो मघवा विश्वसौभगः शं न आ वक्षद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ṅ ǀ tri-cakráḥ ǀ madhu-vā́hanaḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ jīrá-aśvaḥ ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ yātu ǀ sú-stutaḥ ǀtri-vandhuráḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ viśvá-saubhagaḥ ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣat ǀ dvi-páde ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nigh to us come the Aśvins' lauded three-wheeled car, the car laden with meath and drawn by fleet-foot steeds, Three-seated, opulent, bestowing all delight. may it bring weal to us, to cattle and to men.
verses.wilson_translation: May the three-wheeled car of the Aśvins, drawn by swift horses, laden with honey, three-canopied, filled with treasure, and every way auspicious, come to our presence, and bring prosperity to our people and our cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Nigh to us come the Aśvins' lauded three-wheeled car, the car laden with meath and drawn by fleet-foot steeds, Three-seated, opulent, bestowing all delight. may it bring weal to us, to cattle and to men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ न ऊर्जं वहतमश्विना युवं मधुमत्या नः कशया मिमिक्षतं ।प्रायुस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ū́rjam ǀ vahatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuvám ǀ mádhu-matyā ǀ naḥ ǀ káśayā ǀ mimikṣatam ǀprá ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ tā́riṣṭam ǀ níḥ ǀ rápāṃsi ǀ mṛkṣatam ǀ sédhatam ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ bhávatam ǀ sacā-bhúvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring hither nourishment for us, ye Aśvins Twain; sprinkle us with your whip that drops with honey-dew. Prolong our days of life, wipe out our trespasses; destroy our foes, be our companions and our Friends.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring us,Aśvins, vigour; animate us with your honied speech; prolong our existence; wipe away our sins; destroy our foes; be ever our associates.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring hither nourishment for us, ye Aśvins Twain; sprinkle us with your whip that drops with honey-dew. Prolong our days of life, wipe out our trespasses; destroy our foes, be our companions and our Friends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह गर्भं जगतीषु धत्थो युवं विश्वेषु भुवनेष्वंतः ।युवमग्निं च वृषणावपश्च वनस्पतीँरश्विनावैरयेथां ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ gárbham ǀ jágatīṣu ǀ dhatthaḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ víśveṣu ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ antáríti ǀyuvám ǀ agním ǀ ca ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ apáḥ ǀ ca ǀ vánaspátīn ǀ aśvinau ǀ áirayethām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye store the germ of life in female creatures, ye lay it up within all living beings. Ye have sent forth, O Aśvins passing mighty, the fire, the sovrans of the wood, the waters,
verses.wilson_translation: You,Aśvins, sustain the germ in all moving creatures; you are in the interior of all beings; do you, showerers of benefits, supply (for our own use) fire and water and the trees of the forest.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye store the germ of life in female creatures, ye lay it up within all living beings. Ye have sent forth, O Aśvins passing mighty, the fire, the sovrans of the wood, the waters,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह स्थो भिषजा भेषजेभिरथो ह स्थो रथ्या राथ्येभिः ।अथो ह क्षत्रमधि धत्थ उग्रा यो वां हविष्मान्मनसा ददाश ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ sthaḥ ǀ bhiṣájā ǀ bheṣajébhiḥ ǀ átho íti ǀ ha ǀ sthaḥ ǀ rathyā́ ǀ ráthyebhiríti ráthyebhiḥ ǀátho íti ǀ ha ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ádhi ǀ dhattha ǀ ugrā ǀ yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ havíṣmān ǀ mánasā ǀ dadā́śa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leeches are ye with medicines to heal us, and charioteers are ye with skill in driving. Ye Strong, give sway to him who brings oblation and with his heart pours out his gift before you.
verses.wilson_translation: You two are physicians, (conversant) with (all) medicaments; you ride in a chariot (drawn by) well-trained steeds; therefore, mighty (divinities), resolutely uphold (the worshipper), who, with a mind (devoted to you), offers you oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Leeches are ye with medicines to heal us, and charioteers are ye with skill in driving. Ye Strong, give sway to him who brings oblation and with his heart pours out his gift before you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLVIII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE Vasus Twain, ye Rudras full of counsel, grant us, Strong Strengtheners, when ye stand beside us,What wealth Aucathya craves of you, great Helpers when ye come forward with no niggard succour. Who may give you aught, Vasus, for your favour, for what, at the Cow's place, ye grant through worship?Wake for us understanding full of riches, come with a heart that will fulfil our longing. As erst for Tugra's son your car, sea-crossing, strong, was equipped and set amid the waters,So may I gain your shelter and protection as with winged course a hero seeks his army. May this my praise preserve Ucathya's offspring: let not these Twain who fly with wings exhaust me.Let not the wood ten times up-piled consume me, when fixed for you it bites the ground it stands on. The most maternal streams, wherein the Dāsas cast me securely bound, have not devoured me.When Traitana would cleave my head asunder, the Dāsa wounded his own breast and shoulders. Dīrghatamas the son of Mamatā hath come to length of days in the tenth age of human kind.He is the Brahman of the waters as they strive to reach their end and aim: their charioteer is he.

verses.sanskrit: वसू रुद्रा पुरुमंतू वृधंता दशस्यतं नो वृषणावभिष्टौ ।दस्रा ह यद्रेक्ण औचथ्यो वां प्र यत्सस्राथे अकवाभिरूती ॥
verses.transliteration: vásū íti ǀ rudrā́ ǀ purumántū íti puru-mántū ǀ vṛdhántā ǀ daśasyátam ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ abhíṣṭau ǀdásrā ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ aucathyáḥ ǀ vām ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ sasrā́the íti ǀ ákavābhiḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: YE Vasus Twain, ye Rudras full of counsel, grant us, Strong Strengtheners, when ye stand beside us, What wealth Aucathya craves of you, great Helpers when ye come forward with no niggard succour.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras, showerers (of benefits), granters of dwellings, dispellers of sin, cognizant of many (things), increasing (through praise), and fulfillers (of desires), inasmuch as Aucatthya offer you (sacrificial) wealth, and you protect (your worshippers) with unobjectionable aids, bestow uponus (our prayers).
verses.griffith_verse: YE Vasus Twain, ye Rudras full of counsel, grant us, Strong Strengtheners, when ye stand beside us, What wealth Aucathya craves of you, great Helpers when ye come forward with no niggard succour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को वां दाशत्सुमतये चिदस्यै वसू यद्धेथे नमसा पदे गोः ।जिगृतमस्मे रेवतीः पुरंधीः कामप्रेणेव मनसा चरंता ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vām ǀ dāśat ǀ su-matáye ǀ cit ǀ asyái ǀ vásū íti ǀ yát ǀ dhéthe íti ǀ námasā ǀ padé ǀ góḥ ǀjigṛtám ǀ asmé íti ǀ revátīḥ ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ kāmapréṇa-iva ǀ mánasā ǀ cárantā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who may give you aught, Vasus, for your favour, for what, at the Cow's place, ye grant through worship? Wake for us understanding full of riches, come with a heart that will fulfil our longing.
verses.wilson_translation: Granters of dwellings, who may make you offerings so propitiatory of that your good will, that (invoked) by our adoration, to the site of the altar, you may entertain (favourable intentions towards us), and grant us kine rich in milk, coming with minds made up to grant the desires (of the worshipper).
verses.griffith_verse: Who may give you aught, Vasus, for your favour, for what, at the Cow's place, ye grant through worship? Wake for us understanding full of riches, come with a heart that will fulfil our longing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युक्तो ह यद्वां तौग्र्याय पेरुर्वि मध्ये अर्णसो धायि पज्रः ।उप वामवः शरणं गमेयं शूरो नाज्म पतयद्भिरेवैः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuktáḥ ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ taugryā́ya ǀ perúḥ ǀ ví ǀ mádhye ǀ árṇasaḥ ǀ dhā́yi ǀ pajráḥ ǀúpa ǀ vām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ śaraṇám ǀ gameyam ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ ájma ǀ patáyat-bhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As erst for Tugra's son your car, sea-crossing, strong, was equipped and set amid the waters, So may I gain your shelter and protection as with winged course a hero seeks his army.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner,Aśvins, as your strong-drawn (car), able to cross (the sea), was plural ced,harnessed, in the middle of the water, for (the rescue of) the son of Tugra, so may I attain to your preserving protection (with the same alacrity) as a victorious hero (returns home) with bounding steeds.
verses.griffith_verse: As erst for Tugra's son your car, sea-crossing, strong, was equipped and set amid the waters, So may I gain your shelter and protection as with winged course a hero seeks his army.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपस्तुतिरौचथ्यमुरुष्येन्मा मामिमे पतत्रिणी वि दुग्धां ।मा मामेधो दशतयश्चितो धाक् प्र यद्वां बद्धस्त्मनि खादति क्षां ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa-stutiḥ ǀ aucathyám ǀ uruṣyet ǀ mā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ imé íti ǀ patatríṇī íti ǀ ví ǀ dugdhām ǀmā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ édhaḥ ǀ dáśa-tayaḥ ǀ citáḥ ǀ dhāk ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ baddháḥ ǀ tmáni ǀ khā́dati ǀ kṣā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this my praise preserve Ucathya's offspring: let not these Twain who fly with wings exhaust me. Let not the wood ten times up-piled consume me, when fixed for you it bites the ground it stands on.
verses.wilson_translation: May the praise addressed to you,Aśvins, preserve the son of Ucatthya; let not those revolving (days and nights) exhaust me; let not the ten times kindled fire consume me; let it not be, that one who is your, (dependant), bound (with bonds), should of himself bite the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: May this my praise preserve Ucathya's offspring: let not these Twain who fly with wings exhaust me. Let not the wood ten times up-piled consume me, when fixed for you it bites the ground it stands on.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न मा गरन्नद्यो मातृतमा दासा यदीं सुसमुब्धमवाधुः ।शिरो यदस्य त्रैतनो वितक्षत्स्वयं दास उरो अंसावपि ग्ध ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ mā ǀ garan ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ mātṛ́-tamāḥ ǀ dāsā́ḥ ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ sú-samubdham ǀ ava-ádhuḥ ǀśíraḥ ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ traitanáḥ ǀ vi-tákṣat ǀ svayám ǀ dāsáḥ ǀ úraḥ ǀ áṃsau ǀ ápi ǀ gdhéti gdha ǁ
verses.english_translation: The most maternal streams, wherein the Dāsas cast me securely bound, have not devoured me. When Traitana would cleave my head asunder, the Dāsa wounded his own breast and shoulders.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the maternal waters swallow me, since the slaves hurled down this decrepit (old man); in like manner as Traitana wounded his head, so has the slave wounded his own, and has struck his breast and shoulders.
verses.griffith_verse: The most maternal streams, wherein the Dāsas cast me securely bound, have not devoured me. When Traitana would cleave my head asunder, the Dāsa wounded his own breast and shoulders.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घतमा मामतेयो जुजुर्वान्दशमे युगे ।अपामर्थं यतीनां ब्रह्मा भवति सारथिः ॥
verses.transliteration: dīrghá-tamāḥ ǀ māmateyáḥ ǀ jujurvā́n ǀ daśamé ǀ yugé ǀapā́m ǀ ártham ǀ yatī́nām ǀ brahmā́ ǀ bhavati ǀ sā́rathiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dīrghatamas the son of Mamatā hath come to length of days in the tenth age of human kind. He is the Brahman of the waters as they strive to reach their end and aim: their charioteer is he.
verses.wilson_translation: Dīrghatamas, the son of Mamatā, has grown old after the tenthyuga(has passed); he is the Brahmāof those who seek to obtain the object of their (pious) works; he is their charioteer.
verses.griffith_verse: Dīrghatamas the son of Mamatā hath come to length of days in the tenth age of human kind. He is the Brahman of the waters as they strive to reach their end and aim: their charioteer is he.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLIX. Heaven and Earth.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I PRAISE with sacrifices mighty Heaven and Earth at festivals, the wise, the Strengtheners of Law.Who, having Gods for progeny, conjoined with Gods, through wonder-working wisdom bring forth choicest boons. With invocations, on the gracious Father's mind, and on the Mother's great inherent power I muse.Prolific Parents, they have made the world of life, and for their brood all round wide immortality. These Sons of yours well skilled in work, of wondrous power, brought forth to life the two great Mothers first of all.To keep the truth of all that stands and all that moves, ye guard the station of your Son who knows no guile. They with surpassing skill, most wise, have measured out the Twins united in their birth and in their home.They, the refulgent Sages, weave within the sky, yea, in the depths of sea, a web for ever new. This is to-day the goodliest gift of Savitar: this thought we have when now the God is furthering us.On us with loving-kindness Heaven and Earth bestow riches and various wealth and treasure hundredfold!

verses.sanskrit: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी ऋतावृधा मही स्तुषे विदथेषु प्रचेतसा ।देवेभिर्ये देवपुत्रे सुदंससेत्था धिया वार्याणि प्रभूषतः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ dyā́vā ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhā ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ stuṣe ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ prá-cetasā ǀdevébhiḥ ǀ yé íti ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀ su-dáṃsasā ǀ itthā́ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀ pra-bhū́ṣataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I PRAISE with sacrifices mighty Heaven and Earth at festivals, the wise, the Strengtheners of Law. Who, having Gods for progeny, conjoined with Gods, through wonder-working wisdom bring forth choicest boons.
