Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother.Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place: the Father laid the Daughter's germ within it. I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee.I ask thee of the Stallion's seed prolific, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth. This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre.The Stallion's seed prolific is the Soma; this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth. Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Viṣṇu's ordinance.Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, they compass us about present on every side. What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander.When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this speech I first obtain a portion. Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortalCeaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one, and fail to mark the other. Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,—Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-song? But they who know it well sit here assembled.Fortunatemayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy.Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and coming hitherward drink limpid water. Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she,Who hath become eight-footed or hath got nine feet, the thousand-syllabled in the sublimest heaven. From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being,Thence flows the imperishable flood and thence the universe hath life. I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it.The Mighty Men have dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days aforetime, Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended.One with his powers the universe regardeth: Of one, the sweep is seen, but his figure. Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them.Three kept in close concealment cause no motion; of speech, men speak only the fourth division. They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān.To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan. Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters.Again descend they from the seat of Order, and all the earth is moistened with their fatness. Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it?Therein are set together spokes three hundred and sixty, which in nowise can be loosened. That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest,Wealth-giver, treasure. finder, free bestower,—bring that, Sarasvatī, that we may drain it. By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances.These Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling. Uniform, with the passing days, this water mounts and fails again.The tempest-clouds give life to earth, and fires re-animate the heaven. The Bird Celestial, vast with noble pinion, the lovely germ of plants, the germ of waters,Him who delighteth us with rain in season, Sarasvān I invoke that he may help us.

verses.sanskrit: अस्य वामस्य पलितस्य होतुस्तस्य भ्राता मध्यमो अस्त्यश्नः ।तृतीयो भ्राता घृतपृष्ठो अस्यात्रापश्यं विश्पतिं सप्तपुत्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ vāmásya ǀ palitásya ǀ hótuḥ ǀ tásya ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ madhyamáḥ ǀ asti ǀ áśnaḥ ǀtṛtī́yaḥ ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ ghṛtá-pṛṣṭhaḥ ǀ asya ǀ átra ǀ apaśyam ǀ viśpátim ǀ saptá-putram ǁ
verses.english_translation: OF this benignant Priest, with eld grey-coloured, the brother midmost of the three is lightning. The third is he whose back with oil is sprinkled. Here I behold the Chief with seven male children.
verses.wilson_translation: I have beheld the Lord of men with seven sons; of which delightful and benevolent (deity), who is the object of our invocation, there is an all-pervadingmiddlebrother, and a third brother, well fed with (oblationsof)ghee.
verses.griffith_verse: OF this benignant Priest, with eld grey-coloured, the brother midmost of the three is lightning. The third is he whose back with oil is sprinkled. Here I behold the Chief with seven male children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्त युंजंति रथमेकचक्रमेको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा ।त्रिनाभि चक्रमजरमनर्वं यत्रेमा विश्वा भुवनाधि तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ yuñjanti ǀ rátham ǀ éka-cakram ǀ ékaḥ ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ vahati ǀ saptá-nāmā ǀtri-nā́bhi ǀ cakrám ǀ ajáram ǀ anarvám ǀ yátra ǀ imā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ ádhi ǀ tasthúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven to the one-wheeled chariot yoke the Courser; bearing seven names the single Courser draws it. Three-naved the wheel is, sound and undecaying, whereon are resting all these worlds of being.
verses.wilson_translation: They yoke the seven (horses) to the one-wheeled car; one horse, named seven, bears it along; the three-axled wheel is undecaying, never loosened, and in it all these regions of the universe abide.
verses.griffith_verse: Seven to the one-wheeled chariot yoke the Courser; bearing seven names the single Courser draws it. Three-naved the wheel is, sound and undecaying, whereon are resting all these worlds of being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं रथमधि ये सप्त तस्थुः सप्तचक्रं सप्त वहंत्यश्वाः ।सप्त स्वसारो अभि सं नवंते यत्र गवां निहिता सप्त नाम ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ rátham ǀ ádhi ǀ yé ǀ saptá ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ saptá-cakram ǀ saptá ǀ vahanti ǀ áśvāḥ ǀsaptá ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ navante ǀ yátra ǀ gávām ǀ ní-hitā ǀ saptá ǀ nā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven who on the seven-wheeled car are mounted have horses, seven in tale, who draw them onward. Seven Sisters utter songs of praise together, in whom the names of the seven Cows are treasured.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven who preside over this sevenpwheeled chariot (are) the seven horses who draw it; seven sisters ride in it together, and in are deposited the seven forms of utterance.
verses.griffith_verse: The seven who on the seven-wheeled car are mounted have horses, seven in tale, who draw them onward. Seven Sisters utter songs of praise together, in whom the names of the seven Cows are treasured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को ददर्श प्रथमं जायमानमस्थन्वंतं यदनस्था बिभर्ति ।भूम्या असुरसृगात्मा क्व स्वित्को विद्वांसमुप गात्प्रष्टुमेतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ dadarśa ǀ prathamám ǀ jā́yamānam ǀ asthan-vántam ǀ yát ǀ anasthā́ ǀ bíbharti ǀbhū́myāḥ ǀ ásuḥ ǀ ásṛk ǀ ātmā́ ǀ kvá ǀ svit ǀ káḥ ǀ vidvā́ṃsam ǀ úpa ǀ gāt ǀ práṣṭum ǀ etát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who hath beheld him as he sprang to being, seen how the boneless One supports the bony? Where is the blood of earth, the life, the spirit? Who may approach the man who knows, to ask it?
verses.wilson_translation: Who has seen the primeval (being) at the time of his being born; what is that endowed with substance which the unsubstantial sustains; from earth are the breath and blood; but where is thesoul; who may repair to the sage to ask this?
verses.griffith_verse: Who hath beheld him as he sprang to being, seen how the boneless One supports the bony? Where is the blood of earth, the life, the spirit? Who may approach the man who knows, to ask it?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पाकः पृच्छामि मनसाविजानन्देवानामेना निहिता पदानि ।वत्से बष्कयेऽधि सप्त तंतून्वि तत्निरे कवय ओतवा उ ॥
verses.transliteration: pā́kaḥ ǀ pṛcchāmi ǀ mánasā ǀ ávi-jānan ǀ devā́nām ǀ enā́ ǀ ní-hitā ǀ padā́ni ǀvatsé ǀ baṣkáye ǀ ádhi ǀ saptá ǀ tántūn ǀ ví ǀ tatnire ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ ótavai ǀ ūṃ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unripe in mind, in spirit undiscerning, I ask of these the Gods’ established places; For up above the yearling Calf the sages, to form a web, their own seven threads have woven.
verses.wilson_translation: Immature (in understanding) undiscerning in mind, I inquire of those things which are hidden (even) from the gods; (what are) the seven threads which the sages have spread to envelop the sun, in whom all abide?
verses.griffith_verse: Unripe in mind, in spirit undiscerning, I ask of these the Gods’ established places; For up above the yearling Calf the sages, to form a web, their own seven threads have woven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अचिकित्वाञ्चिकितुषश्चिदत्र कवीन्पृच्छामि विद्मने न विद्वान् ।वि यस्तस्तंभ षळिमा रजांस्यजस्य रूपे किमपि स्विदेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ácikitvān ǀ cikitúṣaḥ ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀ kavī́n ǀ pṛcchāmi ǀ vidmáne ǀ ná ǀ vidvā́n ǀví ǀ yáḥ ǀ tastámbha ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ imā́ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ ajásya ǀ rūpé ǀ kím ǀ ápi ǀ svit ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I ask, unknowing, those who know, the sages, as one all ignorant for sake of knowledge, What was that ONE who in the Unborn's image hath stablished and fixed firm these worlds' six regions.
verses.wilson_translation: Ignorant, I inquire of the sages who know (the truth); not as one knowing (do I inquire), for the sake of (gaining) knowledge; what is that one alone, who has upheld these six spheres in the form of the unborn?
verses.griffith_verse: I ask, unknowing, those who know, the sages, as one all ignorant for sake of knowledge, What was that ONE who in the Unborn's image hath stablished and fixed firm these worlds' six regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इह ब्रवीतु य ईमंग वेदास्य वामस्य निहितं पदं वेः ।शीर्ष्णः क्षीरं दुह्रते गावो अस्य वव्रिं वसाना उदकं पदापुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ bravītu ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ aṅgá ǀ véda ǀ asyá ǀ vāmásya ǀ ní-hitam ǀ padám ǀ véríti véḥ ǀśīrṣṇáḥ ǀ kṣīrám ǀ duhrate ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ asya ǀ vavrím ǀ vásānāḥ ǀ udakám ǀ padā́ ǀ apuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let him who knoweth presently declare it, this lovely Bird's securely founded station. Forth from his head the Cows draw milk, and, wearing his vesture, with their foot have drunk the water.
verses.wilson_translation: Let him who knows this (truth) quickly declare it; the mysterious condition of the beautiful ever-moving (sun); the rays shed (their) milk from his (exalted) head investing his form with radiance; they have drunk up the water by the paths (by which they were poured forth).
verses.griffith_verse: Let him who knoweth presently declare it, this lovely Bird's securely founded station. Forth from his head the Cows draw milk, and, wearing his vesture, with their foot have drunk the water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: माता पितरमृत आ बभाज धीत्यग्रे मनसा सं हि जग्मे ।सा बीभत्सुर्गर्भरसा निविद्धा नमस्वंत इदुपवाकमीयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: mātā́ ǀ pitáram ǀ ṛté ǀ ā́ ǀ babhāja ǀ dhītī́ ǀ ágre ǀ mánasā ǀ sám ǀ hí ǀ jagmé ǀsā́ ǀ bībhatsúḥ ǀ gárbha-rasā ǀ ní-viddhā ǀ námasvantaḥ ǀ ít ǀ upa-vākám ǀ īyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Mother gave the Sire his share of Order: with thought, at first, she wedded him in spirit. She, the coy Dame, was filled with dew prolific: with adoration men approached to praise her.
verses.wilson_translation: The mother, (earth), worships the father, (sun), with holy rites, for the sake of water; but he has anticipated (her wants) in his mind; whereupon desirous of progeny, she is penetrated by the dews of impregnation, and, (all) expectant of abundance, exchange words (of congratulation).
verses.griffith_verse: The Mother gave the Sire his share of Order: with thought, at first, she wedded him in spirit. She, the coy Dame, was filled with dew prolific: with adoration men approached to praise her.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युक्ता मातासीद्धुरि दक्षिणाया अतिष्ठद्गर्भो वृजनीष्वंतः ।अमीमेद्वत्सो अनु गामपश्यद्विश्वरूप्यं त्रिषु योजनेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: yuktā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ āsīt ǀ dhurí ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀ átiṣṭhat ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ vṛjanī́ṣu ǀ antáríti ǀámīmet ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ gā́m ǀ apaśyat ǀ viśva-rūpyám ǀ triṣú ǀ yójaneṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yoked was the Mother to the boon Cow's car-pole: in the dank rows of cloud the Infant rested. Then the Calf lowed, and looked upon the Mother, the Cow who wears all shapes in three directions.
verses.wilson_translation: The mother, (sky), was associated in (sustaining) the burden of the fulfiller of desires, (the earth); the embryo (water) rested within the (womb of the) clouds; thereupon the calf bellowed, and beheld the omniform cow in the three combinations.
verses.griffith_verse: Yoked was the Mother to the boon Cow's car-pole: in the dank rows of cloud the Infant rested. Then the Calf lowed, and looked upon the Mother, the Cow who wears all shapes in three directions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो मातॄस्त्रीन्पितॄन्बिभ्रदेक ऊर्ध्वस्तस्थौ नेमव ग्लापयंति ।मंत्रयंते दिवो अमुष्य पृष्ठे विश्वविदं वाचमविश्वमिन्वां ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ mātṝ́ḥ ǀ trī́n ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ bíbhrat ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ tasthau ǀ ná ǀ īm ǀ áva ǀ glapayanti ǀmantráyante ǀ diváḥ ǀ amúṣya ǀ pṛṣṭhé ǀ viśva-vídam ǀ vā́cam ǀ áviśva-minvām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bearing three Mothers and three Fathers, single he stood erect: they never make him weary. There on the pitch of heaven they speak together in speech all-knowing but not all-impelling.
verses.wilson_translation: The one sole (sun), having three mothers and three fathers, stood on high; none ever over-weary him; the (gods) on the summit of the sky take counsel respecting him in language all-comprehending (but) not extending to all.
verses.griffith_verse: Bearing three Mothers and three Fathers, single he stood erect: they never make him weary. There on the pitch of heaven they speak together in speech all-knowing but not all-impelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य ।आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvā́daśa-aram ǀ nahí ǀ tát ǀ járāya ǀ várvarti ǀ cakrám ǀ pári ǀ dyā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀā́ ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ mithunā́saḥ ǀ átra ǀ saptá ǀ śatā́ni ǀ viṃśatíḥ ǀ ca ǀ tasthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Formed with twelve spokes, by length of time, unweakened, rolls round the heaven this wheel of during Order. Herein established, joined in pairs together, seven hundred Sons and twenty stand, O Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The twelve-spoked wheel, of the true (sun) revolves round the heavens, and never (tends) to decay; seven hundred and twenty children in pais,Agni, abide in it.
verses.griffith_verse: Formed with twelve spokes, by length of time, unweakened, rolls round the heaven this wheel of during Order. Herein established, joined in pairs together, seven hundred Sons and twenty stand, O Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पंचपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं दिव आहुः परे अर्धे पुरीषिणं ।अथेमे अन्य उपरे विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षळर आहुरर्पितं ॥
verses.transliteration: páñca-pādam ǀ pitáram ǀ dvā́daśa-ākṛtim ǀ diváḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ páre ǀ árdhe ǀ purīṣíṇam ǀátha ǀ imé ǀ anyé ǀ úpare ǀ vi-cakṣaṇám ǀ saptá-cakre ǀ ṣáṭ-are ǀ āhuḥ ǀ árpitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: They call him in the farther half of heaven the Sire five-footed, of twelve forms, wealthy in watery store. These others say that he, God with far-seeing eyes, is mounted on the lower seven-wheeled, six-spoked car.
verses.wilson_translation: They have termed the five-footed, twelve-formed parent, Puriṣin, when in the further hemisphere of the sky; and others have termed in Arpita, when in the hither (portion of the sky); shining in his seven-wheeled car), each (wheel) having six spokes.
verses.griffith_verse: They call him in the farther half of heaven the Sire five-footed, of twelve forms, wealthy in watery store. These others say that he, God with far-seeing eyes, is mounted on the lower seven-wheeled, six-spoked car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पंचारे चक्रे परिवर्तमाने तस्मिन्ना तस्थुर्भुवनानि विश्वा ।तस्य नाक्षस्तप्यते भूरिभारः सनादेव न शीर्यते सनाभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: páñca-are ǀ cakré ǀ pari-vártamāne ǀ tásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀtásya ǀ ná ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ tapyate ǀ bhū́ri-bhāraḥ ǀ sanā́t ǀ evá ǀ ná ǀ śīryate ǀ sá-nābhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon this five-spoked wheel revolving ever all living creatures rest and are dependent. Its axle, heavy-laden, is not heated: the nave from ancient time remains unbroken.
verses.wilson_translation: All beings abide in this five-spoked revolving wheel; the heavily-loaded axle is never heated; its eternal compact nave is never worn away.
verses.griffith_verse: Upon this five-spoked wheel revolving ever all living creatures rest and are dependent. Its axle, heavy-laden, is not heated: the nave from ancient time remains unbroken.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनेमि चक्रमजरं वि वावृत उत्तानायां दश युक्ता वहंति ।सूर्यस्य चक्षू रजसैत्यावृतं तस्मिन्नार्पिता भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: sá-nemi ǀ cakrám ǀ ajáram ǀ ví ǀ vavṛte ǀ uttānā́yām ǀ dáśa ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ vahanti ǀsū́ryasya ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ rájasā ǀ eti ǀ ā́-vṛtam ǀ tásmin ǀ ā́rpitā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wheel revolves, unwasting, with its felly: ten draw it, yoked to the far-stretching car-pole. The Sun's eye moves encompassed by the region: on him dependent rest all living creatures.
verses.wilson_translation: The even-fellied, undecaying wheel, repeatedly revolves; ten, united on the upper surface, bear (the world); the orb of the sun proceeds, invested with water, and in it are all beings deposited.
verses.griffith_verse: The wheel revolves, unwasting, with its felly: ten draw it, yoked to the far-stretching car-pole. The Sun's eye moves encompassed by the region: on him dependent rest all living creatures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: साकंजानां सप्तथमाहुरेकजं षळिद्यमा ऋषयो देवजा इति ।तेषामिष्टानि विहितानि धामशः स्थात्रे रेजंते विकृतानि रूपशः ॥
verses.transliteration: sākam-jā́nām ǀ saptátham ǀ āhuḥ ǀ eka-jám ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ ít ǀ yamā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ deva-jā́ḥ ǀ íti ǀtéṣām ǀ iṣṭā́ni ǀ ví-hitāni ǀ dhāma-śáḥ ǀ sthātré ǀ rejante ǀ ví-kṛtāni ǀ rūpa-śáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of the co-born they call the seventh single-born; the six twin pairs are called Ṛṣis, Children of Gods. Their good gifts sought of men are ranged in order due, and various in their form move for the Lord who guides.
verses.wilson_translation: Of those that are born together, sages have called the seventh single-born; for six are twins, and are moveable, and born of the gods; their desirable (properties), plural ced severally in their proper abode, are various (also) in form, and revolve for (the benefit of) that which is stationary.
verses.griffith_verse: Of the co-born they call the seventh single-born; the six twin pairs are called Ṛṣis, Children of Gods. Their good gifts sought of men are ranged in order due, and various in their form move for the Lord who guides.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रियः सतीस्ताँ उ मे पुंस आहुः पश्यदक्षण्वान्न वि चेतदंधः ।कविर्यः पुत्रः स ईमा चिकेत यस्ता विजानात्स पितुष्पितासत् ॥
verses.transliteration: stríyaḥ ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ me ǀ puṃsáḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ páśyat ǀ akṣaṇ-vā́n ǀ ná ǀ ví ǀ cetat ǀ andháḥ ǀkavíḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketa ǀ yáḥ ǀ tā́ ǀ vi-jānā́t ǀ sáḥ ǀ pitúḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ asat ǁ
verses.english_translation: They told me these were males, though truly females: he who hath eyes sees this, the blind discerns not. The son who is a sage hath comprehended: who knows this rightly is his father's father.
verses.wilson_translation: They have called thes, my virtuous feminine les,males; he who has eyes beholds; the blind man sees not; he whois a sage son understands this, and he who discriminates is the father of the father.
verses.griffith_verse: They told me these were males, though truly females: he who hath eyes sees this, the blind discerns not. The son who is a sage hath comprehended: who knows this rightly is his father's father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवः परेण पर एनावरेण पदा वत्सं बिभ्रती गौरुदस्थात् ।सा कद्रीची कं स्विदर्धं परागात्क्व स्वित्सूते नहि यूथे अंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: aváḥ ǀ páreṇa ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ ávareṇa ǀ padā́ ǀ vatsám ǀ bíbhratī ǀ gáuḥ ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǀsā́ ǀ kadrī́cī ǀ kám ǀ svit ǀ árdham ǀ párā ǀ agāt ǀ kvá ǀ svit ǀ sūte ǀ nahí ǀ yūthé ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her calf at foot the Cow hath risen. Witherward, to what place hath she departed? Where calves she? Not amid this herd of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: The cow, holding her calf underneath with her fore-feet, and then above with her hind-feet, has risen up; whither is she gone; to whom has she turned back when half-way; where does she bear young; it is not amidst the herd.
verses.griffith_verse: Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her calf at foot the Cow hath risen. Witherward, to what place hath she departed? Where calves she? Not amid this herd of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवः परेण पितरं यो अस्यानुवेद पर एनावरेण ।कवीयमानः क इह प्र वोचद्देवं मनः कुतो अधि प्रजातं ॥
verses.transliteration: aváḥ ǀ páreṇa ǀ pitáram ǀ yáḥ ǀ asya ǀ anu-véda ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ ávareṇa ǀkavi-yámānaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ devám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ prá-jātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, that the father of this Calf discerneth beneath the upper realm, above the lower, Showing himself a sage, may here declare it? Whence hath the Godlike spirit had its rising?
verses.wilson_translation: He who knows the protector of this (world) as the inferior associated with the superior, and the superior associated with the inferior, he is, as it were, a sage; but who in this world can expound (it); whence is the divine mind in its supremacy engendereḍ
verses.griffith_verse: Who, that the father of this Calf discerneth beneath the upper realm, above the lower, Showing himself a sage, may here declare it? Whence hath the Godlike spirit had its rising?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये अर्वांचस्ताँ उ पराच आहुर्ये परांचस्ताँ उ अर्वाच आहुः ।इंद्रश्च या चक्रथुः सोम तानि धुरा न युक्ता रजसो वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ arvā́ñcaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ párācaḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ yé ǀ párāñcaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ arvā́caḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́ ǀ cakráthuḥ ǀ soma ǀ tā́ni ǀ dhurā́ ǀ ná ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vahanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those that come hitherward they call departing, those that depart they call directed hither. And what so ye have made, Indra and Soma, steeds bear as ’twere yoked to the region's car-pole.
verses.wilson_translation: Those which (the sages) have termed descending, they have also termed ascending; and those they have termed ascending, they have also called descending; and those (orbits) which your,Somaand Indra, have made, bear along the worlds like (oxen) yoked to a twain.
verses.griffith_verse: Those that come hitherward they call departing, those that depart they call directed hither. And what so ye have made, Indra and Soma, steeds bear as ’twere yoked to the region's car-pole.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परि षस्वजाते ।तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभि चाकशीति ॥
verses.transliteration: dvā́ ǀ su-parṇā́ ǀ sa-yújā ǀ sákhāyā ǀ samānám ǀ vṛkṣám ǀ pári ǀ sasvajāte íti ǀtáyoḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ píppalam ǀ svādú ǀ átti ǀ ánaśnan ǀ anyáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cākaśīti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Two Birds with fair wings, knit with bonds of friendship, in the same sheltering tree have found a refuge. One of the twain eats the sweet Fig-tree's fruitage; the other eating not regardeth only.
verses.wilson_translation: Two birds associated together, and mutual friends, take refuge in the same tree; one of them eats the sweet fig; the other abstaining from food, merely looks on.
verses.griffith_verse: Two Birds with fair wings, knit with bonds of friendship, in the same sheltering tree have found a refuge. One of the twain eats the sweet Fig-tree's fruitage; the other eating not regardeth only.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्रा सुपर्णा अमृतस्य भागमनिमेषं विदथाभिस्वरंति ।इनो विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपाः स मा धीरः पाकमत्रा विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ su-parṇā́ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ bhāgám ǀ áni-meṣam ǀ vidáthā ǀ abhi-sváranti ǀináḥ ǀ víśvasya ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ mā ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ pā́kam ǀ átra ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where those fine Birds hymn ceaselessly their portion of life eternal, and the sacred synods, There is the Universe's mighty Keeper, who, wise, hath entered into me the simple.
verses.wilson_translation: Where the smooth-gliding (rays), cognizant (of their duty), distil the perpetual portion of ambrosia (water); there has the lord and steadfast protector all beings consigned me, (though) immature (in wisdom).
verses.griffith_verse: Where those fine Birds hymn ceaselessly their portion of life eternal, and the sacred synods, There is the Universe's mighty Keeper, who, wise, hath entered into me the simple.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्वृक्षे मध्वदः सुपर्णा निविशंते सुवते चाधि विश्वे ।तस्येदाहुः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वग्रे तन्नोन्नशद्यः पितरं न वेद ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ vṛkṣé ǀ madhu-ádaḥ ǀ su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ ni-viśánte ǀ súvate ǀ ca ǀ ádhi ǀ víśve ǀtásya ǀ ít ǀ āhuḥ ǀ píppalam ǀ svādú ǀ ágre ǀ tát ǀ ná ǀ út ǀ naśat ǀ yáḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ ná ǀ véda ǁ
verses.english_translation: The, tree whereon the fine Birds eat the sweetness, where they all rest and procreate their offspring,— Upon its top they say the fig is luscious: none gaineth it who knoweth not the Father.
verses.wilson_translation: In the tree into which the smooth-gliding (rays) feeders on the sweet (produce), enter, and again bring forth (light) over all, they have called the fruit sweet, but he partakes not of it who knows not the protector (of the universe).
verses.griffith_verse: The, tree whereon the fine Birds eat the sweetness, where they all rest and procreate their offspring,— Upon its top they say the fig is luscious: none gaineth it who knoweth not the Father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्गायत्रे अधि गायत्रमाहितं त्रैष्टुभाद्वा त्रैष्टुभं निरतक्षत ।यद्वा जगज्जगत्याहितं पदं य इत्तद्विदुस्ते अमृतत्वमानशुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ gāyatré ǀ ádhi ǀ gāyatrám ǀ ā́-hitam ǀ tráistubhāt ǀ vā ǀ tráistubham ǀ niḥ-átakṣata ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ jágat ǀ jágati ǀ ā́-hitam ǀ padám ǀ yé ǀ ít ǀ tát ǀ vidúḥ ǀ té ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: How on the Gāyatrī the Gāyatrī was based, how from the Triṣṭup they fashioned the Triṣṭup forth, How on the Jagatī was based the Jagatī,—they who know this have won themselves immortal life.
verses.wilson_translation: They who know the station of Agniupon the earth; the station of Vāyuthat was fabricated from the firmament; and that station of the Sun which is plural ced in heaven, obtain immortality.
verses.griffith_verse: How on the Gāyatrī the Gāyatrī was based, how from the Triṣṭup they fashioned the Triṣṭup forth, How on the Jagatī was based the Jagatī,—they who know this have won themselves immortal life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गायत्रेण प्रति मिमीते अर्कमर्केण साम त्रैष्टुभेन वाकं ।वाकेन वाकं द्विपदा चतुष्पदाक्षरेण मिमते सप्त वाणीः ॥
verses.transliteration: gāyatréṇa ǀ práti ǀ mimīte ǀ arkám ǀ arkéṇa ǀ sā́ma ǀ tráistubhena ǀ vākám ǀvākéna ǀ vākám ǀ dvi-pádā ǀ cátuḥ-padā ǀ akṣáreṇa ǀ mimate ǀ saptá ǀ vā́ṇīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Gāyatrī he measures out the praise-song, Sāma with praise-song, triplet with the Triṣṭup. The triplet with the two or four-foot measure, and with the syllable they form seven metres.
verses.wilson_translation: He constructs the prayer with thegāyatrīmetre; with the prayer (he constructs) the Soma, and with thetriṣṭubhmetre the couplet (or triplet); with the couplet (or triplet) he constructs the hymn with (verses of) two or four distichs; and with the syllable they construct the seven metres.
verses.griffith_verse: With Gāyatrī he measures out the praise-song, Sāma with praise-song, triplet with the Triṣṭup. The triplet with the two or four-foot measure, and with the syllable they form seven metres.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जगता सिंधुं दिव्यस्तभायद्रथंतरे सूर्यं पर्यपश्यत् ।गायत्रस्य समिधस्तिस्र आहुस्ततो मह्ना प्र रिरिचे महित्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: jágatā ǀ síndhum ǀ diví ǀ astabhāyat ǀ ratham-taré ǀ sū́ryam ǀ pári ǀ apaśyat ǀgāyatrásya ǀ sam-ídhaḥ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ āhuḥ ǀ tátaḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ prá ǀ ririce ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Jagatī the flood in heaven he stablished, and saw the Sun in the Rathantara Sāman. Gāyatrī hath, they say, three brands for kindling: hence it excels in majesty and vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: With the hymns in thejagatīmetre he fixed the rain in heaven, and surveyed the Sun in therathantara. They have declared three divisions of thegāyatrīmetre, whence it surpasses (all the rest) in force and majesty.
verses.griffith_verse: With Jagatī the flood in heaven he stablished, and saw the Sun in the Rathantara Sāman. Gāyatrī hath, they say, three brands for kindling: hence it excels in majesty and vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप ह्वये सुदुघां धेनुमेतां सुहस्तो गोधुगुत दोहदेनां ।श्रेष्ठं सवं सविता साविषन्नोऽभीद्धो घर्मस्तदु षु प्र वोचं ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ hvaye ǀ su-dúghām ǀ dhenúm ǀ etā́m ǀ su-hástaḥ ǀ go-dhúk ǀ utá ǀ dohat ǀ enām ǀśréṣṭham ǀ savám ǀ savitā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ naḥ ǀ abhí-iddhaḥ ǀ gharmáḥ ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ prá ǀ vocam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invocate the milch-cow good for milking so that the milker, deft of hand, may drain her. May Savitar give goodliest stimulation. The caldron is made hot; I will proclaim it.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the cow that is easily milked, that the handy milker may milk her; may Savitāaccept this our excellent libation, that his heat may (thereby) increase; it is for this, verily, that I earnestly invoke him.
verses.griffith_verse: I invocate the milch-cow good for milking so that the milker, deft of hand, may drain her. May Savitar give goodliest stimulation. The caldron is made hot; I will proclaim it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिंकृण्वती वसुपत्नी वसूनां वत्समिच्छंती मनसाभ्यागात् ।दुहामश्विभ्यां पयो अघ्न्येयं सा वर्धतां महते सौभगाय ॥
verses.transliteration: hiṅ-kṛṇvatī́ ǀ vasu-pátnī ǀ vásūnām ǀ vatsám ǀ icchántī ǀ mánasā ǀ abhí ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀduhā́m ǀ aśví-bhyām ǀ páyaḥ ǀ aghnyā́ ǀ iyám ǀ sā́ ǀ vardhatām ǀ mahaté ǀ sáubhagāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: She, lady of all treasure, is come hither yearning in spirit for her calf and lowing. May this cow yield her milk for both the Aśvins, and may she prosper to our high advantage.
verses.wilson_translation: She comes lowing, abounding in rich (products), desiring her calf in her mind;may this cow grant her milk to the Aśvins; may she thrive for our great advantage.
verses.griffith_verse: She, lady of all treasure, is come hither yearning in spirit for her calf and lowing. May this cow yield her milk for both the Aśvins, and may she prosper to our high advantage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गौरमीमेदनु वत्सं मिषंतं मूर्धानं हिङ्ङकृणोन्मातवा उ ।सृक्वाणं घर्ममभि वावशाना मिमाति मायुं पयते पयोभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: gáuḥ ǀ amīmet ǀ ánu ǀ vatsám ǀ miṣántam ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ híṅ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ mā́tavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀsṛ́kvāṇam ǀ gharmám ǀ abhí ǀ vāvaśānā́ ǀ mímāti ǀ māyúm ǀ páyate ǀ páyaḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The cow hath lowed after her blinking youngling; she licks his forehead, as she lows, to form it. His mouth she fondly calls to her warm udder, and suckles him with milk while gently lowing.
verses.wilson_translation: The cow bellows for her calf, (who stands) with winking eyes, and lows as (she proceeds to lick his forehead; she utters a cry, as, anxious, she sees the moisture in the corners of his mouth, and nourishes him with her milk.
verses.griffith_verse: The cow hath lowed after her blinking youngling; she licks his forehead, as she lows, to form it. His mouth she fondly calls to her warm udder, and suckles him with milk while gently lowing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं स शिंक्ते येन गौरभीवृता मिमाति मायुं ध्वसनावधि श्रिता ।सा चित्तिभिर्नि हि चकार मर्त्यं विद्युद्भवंती प्रति वव्रिमौहत ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ sáḥ ǀ śiṅkte ǀ yéna ǀ gáuḥ ǀ abhí-vṛtā ǀ mímāti ǀ māyúm ǀ dhvasánau ǀ ádhi ǀ śritā́ ǀsā́ ǀ cittí-bhiḥ ǀ ní ǀ hí ǀ cakā́ra ǀ mártyam ǀ vi-dyút ǀ bhávantī ǀ práti ǀ vavrím ǀ auhata ǁ
verses.english_translation: He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow laws as she clings unto the shedder of the rain. She with her shrilling cries hath humbled mortal man, and, turned to lightning, hath stripped off her covering robe.
verses.wilson_translation: He, too, bellows, and the cow utters inarticulate sounds, as, encompassed by him, she repairs to her stall; (influenced) by her instrumental ncts, she acts like a human being, and, radiant, manifests her nature.
verses.griffith_verse: He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow laws as she clings unto the shedder of the rain. She with her shrilling cries hath humbled mortal man, and, turned to lightning, hath stripped off her covering robe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनच्छये तुरगातु जीवमेजद्ध्रुवं मध्य आ पस्त्यानां ।जीवो मृतस्य चरति स्वधाभिरमर्त्यो मर्त्येना सयोनिः ॥
verses.transliteration: anát ǀ śaye ǀ turá-gātu ǀ jīvám ǀ éjat ǀ dhruvám ǀ mádhye ǀ ā́ ǀ pastyā́nām ǀjīváḥ ǀ mṛtásya ǀ carati ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀ mártyena ǀ sá-yoniḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That which hath breath and speed and life and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses. Living, by offerings to the Dead he moveth Immortal One, the brother of the mortal.
verses.wilson_translation: Life endowed with breath, eager (in discharge of its functions), reposes, steady, in the midst of its (proper) abodes; the life of the mortal body, cognate with the mortal frame, endures immortal (sustained) by (obsequial) offerings.
verses.griffith_verse: That which hath breath and speed and life and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses. Living, by offerings to the Dead he moveth Immortal One, the brother of the mortal.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानमा च परा च पथिभिश्चरंतं ।स सध्रीचीः स विषूचीर्वसान आ वरीवर्ति भुवनेष्वंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ gopā́m ǀ áni-padyamānam ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ párā ǀ ca ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ cárantam ǀsáḥ ǀ sadhrī́cīḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ víṣūcīḥ ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ varīvarti ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing. He, clothed with gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.wilson_translation: I have beheld the unwearied protector of the universe, the sun, travelling upwards, the downwards by various paths;invested with aggregative and diffusive radiance, he revolves in the midst of the regions.
verses.griffith_verse: I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing. He, clothed with gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य ईं चकार न सो अस्य वेद य ईं ददर्श हिरुगिन्नु तस्मात् ।स मातुर्योना परिवीतो अंतर्बहुप्रजा निर्ऋतिमा विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ cakā́ra ǀ ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ asyá ǀ veda ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ dadárśa ǀ híruk ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ tásmāt ǀsáḥ ǀ mātúḥ ǀ yónā ǀ pári-vītaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ bahu-prajā́ḥ ǀ níḥ-ṛtim ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who hath made him cloth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely is he hidden. He, yet enveloped in his Mother's bosom, source of much life, hath sunk into destruction.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has made (this state of things) does not comprehend it; he who has beheld it, has it also verily hidden (from him); he, whilst yet enveloped in his mother's womb, is subject to many births, and has entered upon evil.
verses.griffith_verse: He who hath made him cloth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely is he hidden. He, yet enveloped in his Mother's bosom, source of much life, hath sunk into destruction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्यौर्मे पिता जनिता नाभिरत्र बंधुर्मे माता पृथिवी महीयं ।उत्तानयोश्चम्वोर्योनिरंतरत्रा पिता दुहितुर्गर्भमाधात् ॥
verses.transliteration: dyáuḥ ǀ me ǀ pitā́ ǀ janitā́ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ átra ǀ bándhuḥ ǀ me ǀ mātā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ mahī́ ǀ iyám ǀuttānáyoḥ ǀ camvóḥ ǀ yóniḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ átra ǀ pitā́ ǀ duhitúḥ ǀ gárbham ǀ ā́ ǀ adhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother. Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place: the Father laid the Daughter's germ within it.
verses.wilson_translation: The heaven is my parent and progenitor; the navel (of the earth) is my kinsman; the spacious earth is my mother. The womb (of all beings) lies between the two uplifted ladles, and in it the parent has deposited the germ (of the fruitfulness) of the daughter.
verses.griffith_verse: Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother. Between the wide-spread world-halves is the birth-place: the Father laid the Daughter's germ within it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पृच्छामि त्वा परमंतं पृथिव्याः पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः ।पृच्छामि त्वा वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतः पृच्छामि वाचः परमं व्योम ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛcchā́mi ǀ tvā ǀ páram ǀ ántam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ yátra ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀpṛcchā́mi ǀ tvā ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ rétaḥ ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ vācáḥ ǀ paramám ǀ ví-oma ǁ
verses.english_translation: I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee. I ask thee of the Stallion's seed prolific, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.wilson_translation: I ask you, (instrumental tutor of the rite), what is the uttermost end of the earth; I ask you, where is the navel of the world. I ask you, what is the fecundating power of the rain-shedding steed; I ask you, what is the supreme heaven of (holy) speech.
verses.griffith_verse: I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee. I ask thee of the Stallion's seed prolific, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं वेदिः परो अंतः पृथिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः ।अयं सोमो वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतो ब्रह्मायं वाचः परमं व्योम ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ védiḥ ǀ páraḥ ǀ ántaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ayám ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀayám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ rétaḥ ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ayám ǀ vācáḥ ǀ paramám ǀ ví-oma ǁ
verses.english_translation: This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre. The Stallion's seed prolific is the Soma; this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.wilson_translation: This altar is the uttermost end of the earth; this sacrifice is the navel of the world; this Somais the fecundating power of the rain-shedding steed; this Brahmāis the supreme heavn of (holy) speech.
verses.griffith_verse: This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre. The Stallion's seed prolific is the Soma; this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्तार्धगर्भा भुवनस्य रेतो विष्णोस्तिष्ठंति प्रदिशा विधर्मणि ।ते धीतिभिर्मनसा ते विपश्चितः परिभुवः परि भवंति विश्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ ardha-garbhā́ḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ rétaḥ ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ tiṣṭhanti ǀ pra-díśā ǀ ví-dharmaṇi ǀté ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ té ǀ vipaḥ-cítaḥ ǀ pari-bhúvaḥ ǀ pári ǀ bhavanti ǀ viśvátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Viṣṇu's ordinance. Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, they compass us about present on every side.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven (sustaining), the embryo (rain) for half a year, the fecundating (element) of the world, abide, by appointment, in the various functions of Viṣṇu. By their intelligence they pervade in thought all around (them), for they are intelligent and diffusive.
verses.griffith_verse: Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Viṣṇu's ordinance. Endued with wisdom through intelligence and thought, they compass us about present on every side.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वि जानामि यदिवेदमस्मि निण्यः संनद्धो मनसा चरामि ।यदा मागन्प्रथमजा ऋतस्यादिद्वाचो अश्नुवे भागमस्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ví ǀ jānāmi ǀ yát-iva ǀ idám ǀ ásmi ǀ niṇyáḥ ǀ sám-naddhaḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ carāmi ǀyadā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ ágan ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ vācáḥ ǀ aśnuve ǀ bhāgám ǀ asyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander. When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this speech I first obtain a portion.
verses.wilson_translation: I distinguish not if I am this all; for I go perplexed, and bound in mind; when the first-born (perceptions) of the truth reach me, then immediately shall I obtain a portion (of the meaning) of that (sacred) word.
verses.griffith_verse: What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander. When the first-born of holy Law approached me, then of this speech I first obtain a portion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपाङ् प्राङेति स्वधया गृभीतोऽमर्त्यो मर्त्येना सयोनिः ।ता शश्वंता विषूचीना वियंता न्यन्यं चिक्युर्न नि चिक्युरन्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ápāṅ ǀ prā́ṅ ǀ eti ǀ svadháyā ǀ gṛbhītáḥ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀ mártyena ǀ sá-yoniḥ ǀtā́ ǀ śáśvantā ǀ viṣūcī́nā ǀ vi-yántā ǀ ní ǀ anyám ǀ cikyúḥ ǀ ná ǀ ní ǀ cikyuḥ ǀ anyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortal Ceaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one, and fail to mark the other.
verses.wilson_translation: The immortal cognate with the mortal, affected by (desire of) enjoyment, goes to the lower or the upper (sphere); but (men beholding them) associated, going everywhere (in this world together); going everywhere (in other worlds together); have comprehended the one, but have not comprehended the other.
verses.griffith_verse: Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortal Ceaseless they move in opposite directions: men mark the one, and fail to mark the other.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋचो अक्षरे परमे व्योमन्यस्मिन्देवा अधि विश्वे निषेदुः ।यस्तन्न वेद किमृचा करिष्यति य इत्तद्विदुस्त इमे समासते ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛcáḥ ǀ akṣáre ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀ yásmin ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ víśve ǀ ni-sedúḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ tát ǀ ná ǀ véda ǀ kím ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ kariṣyati ǀ yé ǀ ít ǀ tát ǀ vidúḥ ǀ té ǀ imé ǀ sám ǀ āsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,— Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-song? But they who know it well sit here assembled.
verses.wilson_translation: All the gods have taken their seats upon this supreme heaven, the imperishable (text) of  the Veda; what will he, who knows not this, do with the Veda? but they who do know it, they are perfect.
verses.griffith_verse: Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,— Who knows not this, what will he do with praise-song? But they who know it well sit here assembled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूयवसाद्भगवती हि भूया अथो वयं भगवंतः स्याम ।अद्धि तृणमघ्न्ये विश्वदानीं पिब शुद्धमुदकमाचरंती ॥
verses.transliteration: suyavasa-át ǀ bhága-vatī ǀ hí ǀ bhūyā́ḥ ǀ átho íti ǀ vayám ǀ bhága-vantaḥ ǀ syāma ǀaddhí ǀ tṛ́ṇam ǀ aghnye ǀ viśva-dā́nīm ǀ píba ǀ śuddhám ǀ udakám ǀ ā-cárantī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fortunate mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy. Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and coming hitherward drink limpid water.
verses.wilson_translation: Cow, may you be rich in milk through abundant fodder; that we also may be rich (in abundance); eat grass at all seasons, and, roaming (at will), drink pure water.
verses.griffith_verse: Fortunate mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy. Feed on the grass, O Cow, at every season, and coming hitherward drink limpid water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गौरीर्मिमाय सलिलानि तक्षत्येकपदी द्विपदी सा चतुष्पदी ।अष्टापदी नवपदी बभूवुषी सहस्राक्षरा परमे व्योमन् ॥
verses.transliteration: gaurī́ḥ ǀ mimāya ǀ salilā́ni ǀ tákṣatī ǀ éka-padī ǀ dvi-pádī ǀ sā́ ǀ cátuḥ-padī ǀaṣṭā́-padī ǀ náva-padī ǀ babhūvúṣī ǀ sahásra-akṣarā ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she, Who hath become eight-footed or hath got nine feet, the thousand-syllabled in the sublimest heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The sound (of the clouds) has been uttered, fabricating the waters, and being one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed, or infinite in the highest heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she, Who hath become eight-footed or hath got nine feet, the thousand-syllabled in the sublimest heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्याः समुद्रा अधि वि क्षरंति तेन जीवंति प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ।ततः क्षरत्यक्षरं तद्विश्वमुप जीवति ॥
verses.transliteration: tásyāḥ ǀ samudrā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ví ǀ kṣaranti ǀ téna ǀ jīvanti ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǀtátaḥ ǀ kṣarati ǀ akṣáram ǀ tát ǀ víśvam ǀ úpa ǀ jīvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being, Thence flows the imperishable flood and thence the universe hath life.
verses.wilson_translation: From her the clouds shed abundant rain, and thence (the people of) the four quarters live; thence the moisture spreads (to the grain), and the universe exists.
verses.griffith_verse: From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being, Thence flows the imperishable flood and thence the universe hath life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शकमयं धूममारादपश्यं विषूवता पर एनावरेण ।उक्षाणं पृश्निमपचंत वीरास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् ॥
verses.transliteration: śaka-máyam ǀ dhūmám ǀ ārā́t ǀ apaśyam ǀ viṣu-vátā ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ ávareṇa ǀukṣā́ṇam ǀ pṛ́śnim ǀ apacanta ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ tā́ni ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ āsan ǁ
verses.english_translation: I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it. The Mighty Men have dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days aforetime,
verses.wilson_translation: I beheld near (me) the smoke of burning cow-dung; and by that tall-pervading mean (effect, discovered the cause (fire); the priests have the Somaox, for such are their first duties.
verses.griffith_verse: I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it. The Mighty Men have dressed the spotted bullock. These were the customs in the days aforetime,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रयः केशिन ऋतुथा वि चक्षते संवत्सरे वपत एक एषां ।विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्ध्राजिरेकस्य ददृशे न रूपं ॥
verses.transliteration: tráyaḥ ǀ keśínaḥ ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ ví ǀ cakṣate ǀ saṃvatsaré ǀ vapate ǀ ékaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀvíśvam ǀ ékaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ caṣṭe ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ dhrā́jiḥ ǀ ékasya ǀ dadṛśe ǀ ná ǀ rūpám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended. One with his powers the universe regardeth: Of one, the sweep is seen, but his figure.
verses.wilson_translation: The three, with beautiful tresses, look down in their several seasons upon the earth; one of them, when the year is ended, shears (the ground); one, by his acts, overlooks the universe; the course of one is visible, though not his form.
verses.griffith_verse: Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended. One with his powers the universe regardeth: Of one, the sweep is seen, but his figure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारि वाक्परिमिता पदानि तानि विदुर्ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः ।गुहा त्रीणि निहिता नेंगयंति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदंति ॥
verses.transliteration: catvā́ri ǀ vā́k ǀ pári-mitā ǀ padā́ni ǀ tā́ni ǀ viduḥ ǀ brāhmaṇā́ḥ ǀ yé ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀgúhā ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ ní-hitā ǀ ná ǀ iṅgayanti ǀ turī́yam ǀ vācáḥ ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ vadanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them. Three kept in close concealment cause no motion; of speech, men speak only the fourth division.
verses.wilson_translation: Four are the definite grades of spech; those Brahmaṇaswho are wise know them; three, deposited in secret, indicate no meaning; men speak the fourth grade of speech.
verses.griffith_verse: Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them. Three kept in close concealment cause no motion; of speech, men speak only the fourth division.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् ।एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंत्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ mitrám ǀ váruṇam ǀ agním ǀ āhuḥ ǀ átho íti ǀ divyáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ garútmān ǀékam ǀ sát ǀ víprāḥ ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ vadanti ǀ agním ǀ yamám ǀ mātaríśvānam ǀ āhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān. To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan.
verses.wilson_translation: They have styled (him, the Sun),Indra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Agni, and he is the celestial, well-winged Garutmat, for learned priests call one by many names as they speak of Agni,Yama,Mātariśvan.
verses.griffith_verse: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān. To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतंति ।त आववृत्रन्त्सदनादृतस्यादिद्घृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇám ǀ ni-yā́nam ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ vásānāḥ ǀ dívam ǀ út ǀ patanti ǀté ǀ ā́ ǀ avavṛtran ǀ sádanāt ǀ ṛtásya ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ ghṛténa ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ví ǀ udyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters. Again descend they from the seat of Order, and all the earth is moistened with their fatness.
verses.wilson_translation: The smooth-gliding wafters (of the rain, the solar rays), clothing the waters with a dark cloud, ascend to heaven; they come down again from the dwelling of the rain, and immediately the earth is moistened with water.
verses.griffith_verse: Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters. Again descend they from the seat of Order, and all the earth is moistened with their fatness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वादश प्रधयश्चक्रमेकं त्रीणि नभ्यानि क उ तच्चिकेत ।तस्मिन्त्साकं त्रिशता न शंकवोऽर्पिताः षष्टिर्न चलाचलासः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvā́daśa ǀ pra-dháyaḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ ékam ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ nábhyāni ǀ káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tát ǀ ciketa ǀtásmin ǀ sākám ǀ tri-śatā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ śaṅkávaḥ ǀ arpitā́ḥ ǀ ṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ ná ǀ calācalā́saḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it? Therein are set together spokes three hundred and sixty, which in nowise can be loosened.
verses.wilson_translation: The fellies are twelve; the wheel is one; three are the axles; but who knows it? within it are collected 360 (spokes), which are, as it were, moveable and immoveable.
verses.griffith_verse: Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it? Therein are set together spokes three hundred and sixty, which in nowise can be loosened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूर्येन विश्वा पुष्यसि वार्याणि ।यो रत्नधा वसुविद्यः सुदत्रः सरस्वति तमिह धातवे कः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ stánaḥ ǀ śaśayáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ yéna ǀ víśvā ǀ púṣyasi ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀyáḥ ǀ ratna-dhā́ḥ ǀ vasu-vít ǀ yáḥ ǀ su-dátraḥ ǀ sárasvati ǀ tám ǀ ihá ǀ dhā́tave ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest, Wealth-giver, treasure. finder, free bestower,—bring that, Sarasvatī, that we may drain it.
verses.wilson_translation: Sarasvatī, that retiring breast, which is the source of delight, with which you bestow all good things, which is the container of wealth, the distributor of riches, the giver of good (fortune); that (bodom) do you lay open at this season for our nourishment.
verses.griffith_verse: That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest, Wealth-giver, treasure. finder, free bestower,—bring that, Sarasvatī, that we may drain it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् ।ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñéna ǀ yajñám ǀ ayajanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ tā́ni ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ āsan ǀté ǀ ha ǀ nā́kam ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ sacanta ǀ yátra ǀ pū́rve ǀ sādhyā́ḥ ǀ sánti ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances. These Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods sacrifice with sacrifice, for such are their first duties; those mighty ones assemble in heaven, where the divinities who are to be propitiated (by sacred rites) abide.
verses.griffith_verse: By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances. These Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXV. Indra. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH what bright beauty are the Maruts jointly invested, peers in age, who dwell together?From what place have they come? With what intention? Sing they their strength through love of wealth, these Heroes? Whose prayers have they, the Youthful Ones, accepted? Who to his sacrifice hath turned the Maruts?We will delay them on their journey sweeping—with what high spirit!—through the air like eagles. Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose?Thou greetest us when meeting us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us. Mine are devotions, hymns; sweet are libations. Strength stirs, and hurled forth is my bolt of thunder.They call for me, their lauds are longing for me. These my Bay Steeds bear me to these oblations. Therefore together with our strong companions, having adorned our bodies, now we harness,Our spotted deer with might, for thou, O Indra, hast learnt and understood our Godlike nature. Where was that nature then of yours, O Maruts, that ye charged me alone to slay the Dragon?For I in truth am fierce and strong and mighty. I bent away from every foeman's weapons. Yea, much hast thou achieved with us for comrades, with manly valour like thine own, thou Hero.Much may we too achieve, O mightiest Indra, with our great power, we Maruts, when we will it. Vṛtra I slew by mine own strength, O Maruts, having waxed mighty in mine indignation.I with the thunder in my hand created for man these lucid softly flowing waters. Nothing, O Maghavan, stands firm before thee; among the Gods not one is found thine equal.None born or springing into life comes nigh thee. Do what thou hast to do, exceeding mighty? Mine only be transcendent power, whatever I, daring in my spirit, may accomplish.For I am known as terrible, O Maruts I, Indra, am the Lord of what I ruined. Now, O ye Maruts, hath your praise rejoiced me, the glorious hymn which ye have made me, Heroes!For me, for Indra, champion strong in battle, for me, yourselves, as lovers for a lover. Here, truly, they send forth their sheen to meet me, wearing their blameless glory and their vigour.When I have seen you, Maruts, in gay splendour, ye have delighted me, so now delight me. Who here hath magnified you, O ye Maruts? speed forward, O ye lovers, to your lovers.Ye Radiant Ones, assisting their devotions, of these my holy rites he ye regardful. To this hath Mānya's wisdom brought us, so as to aid, as aids the poet him who worships.Bring hither quick! On to the sage, ye Maruts! These prayers for you the singer hath recited. May this your praise, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance!

verses.sanskrit: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीळाः समान्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ।कया मती कुत एतास एतेऽर्चंति शुष्मं वृषणो वसूया ॥
verses.transliteration: káyā ǀ śubhā́ ǀ sá-vayasaḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀ samānyā́ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sám ǀ mimikṣuḥ ǀkáyā ǀ matī́ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ ā́-itāsaḥ ǀ eté ǀ árcanti ǀ śúṣmam ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vasu-yā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH what bright beauty are the Maruts jointly invested, peers in age, who dwell together? From what place have they come? With what intention? Sing they their strength through love of wealth, these Heroes?
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks): With what auspicious fortune have the Maruts, who are of one age, one residence, one dignity, watered (the earth) together; with what intention; whence have they come; showerers of rain, they venerate through desire of wealth, the energy (that is genitive rated in the world by rain).
verses.griffith_verse: WITH what bright beauty are the Maruts jointly invested, peers in age, who dwell together? From what place have they come? With what intention? Sing they their strength through love of wealth, these Heroes?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कस्य ब्रह्माणि जुजुषुर्युवानः को अध्वरे मरुत आ ववर्त ।श्येनाँ इव ध्रजतो अंतरिक्षे केन महा मनसा रीरमाम ॥
verses.transliteration: kásya ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ jujuṣuḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vavarta ǀśyenā́n-iva ǀ dhrájataḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀ kéna ǀ mahā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ rīramāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose prayers have they, the Youthful Ones, accepted? Who to his sacrifice hath turned the Maruts? We will delay them on their journey sweeping—with what high spirit!—through the air like eagles.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whose oblations do the youthful (Maruts) approve; who attracts them to his (own) sacrifice (from the rites of others); with what powerful praise may we propitiate (them), wandering like kites in the mid-air?
verses.griffith_verse: Whose prayers have they, the Youthful Ones, accepted? Who to his sacrifice hath turned the Maruts? We will delay them on their journey sweeping—with what high spirit!—through the air like eagles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुतस्त्वमिंद्र माहिनः सन्नेको यासि सत्पते किं त इत्था ।सं पृच्छसे समराणः शुभानैर्वोचेस्तन्नो हरिवो यत्ते अस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: kútaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ mā́hinaḥ ǀ sán ǀ ékaḥ ǀ yāsi ǀ sat-pate ǀ kím ǀ te ǀ itthā́ ǀsám ǀ pṛcchase ǀ sam-arāṇáḥ ǀ śubhānáiḥ ǀ vocéḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose? Thou greetest us when meeting us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts):Indra, lord of the good, whither do you, who are entitled to honour, proceed alone; what means this (absence of attendance); when followed (by us), you require (what is right); lord of fleet horses say to us, with plural asant words, that which you (have to say) to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose? Thou greetest us when meeting us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्माणि मे मतयः शं सुतासः शुष्म इयर्ति प्रभृतो मे अद्रिः ।आ शासते प्रति हर्यंत्युक्थेमा हरी वहतस्ता नो अच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: bráhmāṇi ǀ me ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ śám ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ śúṣmaḥ ǀ iyarti ǀ prá-bhṛtaḥ ǀ me ǀ ádriḥ ǀā́ ǀ śāsate ǀ práti ǀ haryanti ǀ ukthā́ ǀ imā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀ vahataḥ ǀ tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mine are devotions, hymns; sweet are libations. Strength stirs, and hurled forth is my bolt of thunder. They call for me, their lauds are longing for me. These my Bay Steeds bear me to these oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra): Sacred rites are mine; (holy) praises give me plural asure; libations are for me; my vigorous thunderbolt, hurled (against my foes), goes (to its mark); me, do (pious worshippers) proptiate; hymns are addressed tome; these horses bear us to the presence (ofwhose worshippers, and worship).
verses.griffith_verse: Mine are devotions, hymns; sweet are libations. Strength stirs, and hurled forth is my bolt of thunder. They call for me, their lauds are longing for me. These my Bay Steeds bear me to these oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतो वयमंतमेभिर्युजानाः स्वक्षत्रेभिस्तन्वः शुंभमानाः ।महोभिरेताँ उप युज्महे न्विंद्र स्वधामनु हि नो बभूथ ॥
verses.transliteration: átaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ antamébhiḥ ǀ yujānā́ḥ ǀ svá-kṣatrebhiḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śúmbhamānāḥ ǀmáhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ étān ǀ úpa ǀ yujmahe ǀ nú ǀ índra ǀ svadhā́m ǀ ánu ǀ hí ǀ naḥ ǀ babhū́tha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore together with our strong companions, having adorned our bodies, now we harness, Our spotted deer with might, for thou, O Indra, hast learnt and understood our Godlike nature.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts): Therefore we also, decorating our person ns, are ready, with our docile and night-standing steeds, (to attend) you, with all our splendour, to those rites; verily,Indra, you appropriate our (sacrificial) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Therefore together with our strong companions, having adorned our bodies, now we harness, Our spotted deer with might, for thou, O Indra, hast learnt and understood our Godlike nature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व स्या वो मरुतः स्वधासीद्यन्मामेकं समधत्ताहिहत्ये ।अहं ह्यूग्रस्तविषस्तुविष्मान्विश्वस्य शत्रोरनमं वधस्नैः ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ syā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ svadhā́ ǀ āsīt ǀ yát ǀ mā́m ǀ ékam ǀ sam-ádhatta ǀ ahi-hátye ǀahám ǀ hí ǀ ugráḥ ǀ taviṣáḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǀ víśvasya ǀ śátroḥ ǀ ánamam ǀ vadha-snáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where was that nature then of yours, O Maruts, that ye charged me alone to slay the Dragon? For I in truth am fierce and strong and mighty. I bent away from every foeman's weapons.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra): Where,Maruts, has that (sacrificial) food been assigned to you, which, for the destruction of Ahi was appropriated to me alone; for I indeed am fierce and strong, and mighty, and have bowed down all mine enemies with death-dealing shafts.
verses.griffith_verse: Where was that nature then of yours, O Maruts, that ye charged me alone to slay the Dragon? For I in truth am fierce and strong and mighty. I bent away from every foeman's weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः ।भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेंद्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ cakartha ǀ yújyebhiḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ samānébhiḥ ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ páuṃsyebhiḥ ǀbhū́rīṇi ǀ hí ǀ kṛṇávāma ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ índra ǀ krátvā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yát ǀ váśāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, much hast thou achieved with us for comrades, with manly valour like thine own, thou Hero. Much may we too achieve, O mightiest Indra, with our great power, we Maruts, when we will it.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts): Showerer (of benefits), you have done much; but it has been without united equal energies; for we, too, most powerful Indra, have done many things, and by our deeds (we are, as) we desire to be, Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, much hast thou achieved with us for comrades, with manly valour like thine own, thou Hero. Much may we too achieve, O mightiest Indra, with our great power, we Maruts, when we will it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वधीं वृत्रं मरुत इंद्रियेण स्वेन भामेन तविषो बभूवान् ।अहमेता मनवे विश्वश्चंद्राः सुगा अपश्चकर वज्रबाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: vádhīm ǀ vṛtrám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ indriyéṇa ǀ svéna ǀ bhā́mena ǀ taviṣáḥ ǀ babhūvā́n ǀahám ǀ etā́ḥ ǀ mánave ǀ viśvá-candrāḥ ǀ su-gā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ cakara ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vṛtra I slew by mine own strength, O Maruts, having waxed mighty in mine indignation. I with the thunder in my hand created for man these lucid softly flowing waters.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra): By my own prowess,Maruts, I, mighty in my wrath, slew Vṛtra; armed with my thunderbolt, I created all these pellucid genitive ly-flowing waters for (the good of) man.
verses.griffith_verse: Vṛtra I slew by mine own strength, O Maruts, having waxed mighty in mine indignation. I with the thunder in my hand created for man these lucid softly flowing waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनुत्तमा ते मघवन्नकिर्नु न त्वावाँ अस्ति देवता विदानः ।न जायमानो नशते न जातो यानि करिष्या कृणुहि प्रवृद्ध ॥
verses.transliteration: ánuttam ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ nákiḥ ǀ nú ǀ ná ǀ tvā́-vān ǀ asti ǀ devátā ǀ vídānaḥ ǀná ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ náśate ǀ ná ǀ jātáḥ ǀ yā́ni ǀ kariṣyā́ ǀ kṛṇuhí ǀ pra-vṛddha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nothing, O Maghavan, stands firm before thee; among the Gods not one is found thine equal. None born or springing into life comes nigh thee. Do what thou hast to do, exceeding mighty?
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts): Verily, Maghvan, nothing (done) by you is unavailing; there is no divinity as wise as you; no one being born, or that has been born, ever surpasses the glorious deeds which you, mighty (Indra), have achieved.
verses.griffith_verse: Nothing, O Maghavan, stands firm before thee; among the Gods not one is found thine equal. None born or springing into life comes nigh thee. Do what thou hast to do, exceeding mighty?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एकस्य चिन्मे विभ्वस्त्वोजो या नु दधृष्वान्कृणवै मनीषा ।अहं ह्यूग्रो मरुतो विदानो यानि च्यवमिंद्र इदीश एषां ॥
verses.transliteration: ékasya ǀ cit ǀ me ǀ vi-bhú ǀ astu ǀ ójaḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ nú ǀ dadhṛṣvā́n ǀ kṛṇávai ǀ manīṣā́ ǀahám ǀ hí ǀ ugráḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vídānaḥ ǀ yā́ni ǀ cyávam ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ īśe ǀ eṣām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mine only be transcendent power, whatever I, daring in my spirit, may accomplish. For I am known as terrible, O Maruts I, Indra, am the Lord of what I ruined.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra): May the prowes of me alone be irresistible; may I quickly accomplish whatever I contemplate in my mind; for verily,Maruts, I am fierce and sagacious and to whatever (objects) I direct (my thoughts), of them I am the lord, and rule (over them).
verses.griffith_verse: Mine only be transcendent power, whatever I, daring in my spirit, may accomplish. For I am known as terrible, O Maruts I, Indra, am the Lord of what I ruined.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमंदन्मा मरुतः स्तोमो अत्र यन्मे नरः श्रुत्यं ब्रह्म चक्र ।इंद्राय वृष्णे सुमखाय मह्यं सख्ये सखायस्तन्वे तनूभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ámandat ǀ mā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ átra ǀ yát ǀ me ǀ naraḥ ǀ śrútyam ǀ bráhma ǀ cakrá ǀíndrāya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ sú-makhāya ǀ máhyam ǀ sákhye ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ tanvé ǀ tanū́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now, O ye Maruts, hath your praise rejoiced me, the glorious hymn which ye have made me, Heroes! For me, for Indra, champion strong in battle, for me, yourselves, as lovers for a lover.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, on this occasion praise delights me; that prise which is to be heard (by all), which men have offered me. To Indra, the showerer (of benefits), the object of pious sacrifice; to me, (endowed) with many forms (do you) my friends (offer sacrifices) for (the nourishment of my) person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Now, O ye Maruts, hath your praise rejoiced me, the glorious hymn which ye have made me, Heroes! For me, for Indra, champion strong in battle, for me, yourselves, as lovers for a lover.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवेदेते प्रति मा रोचमाना अनेद्यः श्रव एषो दधानाः ।संचक्ष्या मरुतश्चंद्रवर्णा अच्छांत मे छदयाथा च नूनं ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ ít ǀ eté ǀ práti ǀ mā ǀ rócamānāḥ ǀ ánedyaḥ ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀsam-cákṣya ǀ marutaḥ ǀ candrá-varṇāḥ ǀ ácchānta ǀ me ǀ chadáyātha ǀ ca ǀ nūnám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here, truly, they send forth their sheen to meet me, wearing their blameless glory and their vigour. When I have seen you, Maruts, in gay splendour, ye have delighted me, so now delight me.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, verily, glorifying me, and enjoying boundless fame and food (through my favour), edo you, of golden colour, and invested with glory, cover me in requital verily, (with renown).
verses.griffith_verse: Here, truly, they send forth their sheen to meet me, wearing their blameless glory and their vigour. When I have seen you, Maruts, in gay splendour, ye have delighted me, so now delight me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को न्वत्र मरुतो मामहे वः प्र यातन सखीँरच्छा सखायः ।मन्मानि चित्रा अपिवातयंत एषां भूत नवेदा म ऋतानां ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ nú ǀ átra ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mamahe ǀ vaḥ ǀ prá ǀ yātana ǀ sákhīn ǀ áccha ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀmánmāni ǀ citrāḥ ǀ api-vātáyantaḥ ǀ eṣā́m ǀ bhūta ǀ návedāḥ ǀ me ǀ ṛtā́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who here hath magnified you, O ye Maruts? speed forward, O ye lovers, to your lovers. Ye Radiant Ones, assisting their devotions, of these my holy rites he ye regardful.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agastya): What mortal,Maruts, worships you in this world; hasten, friends, to the presence of your friends; wonderful (divinities), be to them the means of acquiring riches, and be not uncognizant of my merits.
verses.griffith_verse: Who here hath magnified you, O ye Maruts? speed forward, O ye lovers, to your lovers. Ye Radiant Ones, assisting their devotions, of these my holy rites he ye regardful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यद्दुवस्याद्दुवसे न कारुरस्माञ्चक्रे मान्यस्य मेधा ।ओ षु वर्त्त मरुतो विप्रमच्छेमा ब्रह्माणि जरिता वो अर्चत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yát ǀ duvasyā́t ǀ duváse ǀ ná ǀ kārúḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ cakré ǀ mānyásya ǀ medhā́ ǀó íti ǀ sú ǀ vartta ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vípram ǀ áccha ǀ imā́ ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ jaritā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ arcat ǁ
verses.english_translation: To this hath Mānya's wisdom brought us, so as to aid, as aids the poet him who worships. Bring hither quick! On to the sage, ye Maruts! These prayers for you the singer hath recited.
verses.wilson_translation: Since the experienced intellect of a venerable (sage), competent to bestow praise upon (you), who deserve praise, has been exerted for us; do you,Maruts, come to the presence of the devout (worshipper), who, glorifying (you), worships you with these holy rites.
verses.griffith_verse: To this hath Mānya's wisdom brought us, so as to aid, as aids the poet him who worships. Bring hither quick! On to the sage, ye Maruts! These prayers for you the singer hath recited.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ māndāryásya ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀā́ ǀ iṣā́ ǀ yāsīṣṭa ǀ tanvé ǀ vayā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this your praise, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance!
verses.wilson_translation: This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations). May the praise reach you, for (the good of your) person ns, so that we may (thence) obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: May this your praise, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVI. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now let us publish, for the vigorous company the herald of the Strong One, their primeval might.With fire upon your way, O Maruts loud of voice, with battle, Mighty Ones, achieve your deeds of strength. Bringing the pleasant meath as ’twere their own dear son, they sport in sportive wise gay at their gatherings.The Rudras come with succour to the worshipper; self-strong they fail not him who offers sacrifice. To whomsoever, bringer of oblations, they immortal guardians, have given plenteous wealth,For him, like loving friends, the Maruts bringing bliss bedew the regions round with milk abundantly. Ye who with mighty powers have stirred the regions up, your coursers have sped forth directed by themselves.All creatures of the earth, all dwellings are afraid, for brilliant is your coming with your spears advanced. When they in dazzling rush have made the mountains roar, and shaken heaven's high back in their heroic strength,Each sovran of the forest fears as ye drive near, aid the shrubs fly before you swift as whirling wheels. Terrible Maruts, ye with ne’er-diminished host, with great benevolence fulfil our heart's desire.Where’er your lightning bites armed with its gory teeth it crunches up the cattle like a well-aimed dart. Givers of during gifts whose bounties never fail, free from ill-will, at sacrifices glorified,They sing their song aloud that they may drink sweet juice: well do they know the Hero's first heroic deeds. With castles hundredfold, O Maruts, guard ye well the man whom ye have loved from ruin and from sin,—The man whom ye the fierce, the Mighty ones who roar, preserve from calumny by cherishing his seed. O Maruts, in your cars are all things that are good: great powers are set as ’twere in rivalry therein.Rings are upon your shoulders when ye journey forth: your axle turns together both the chariot wheels. Held in your manly arms are many goodly things, gold chains are on your chests, and glistering ornaments,Deer-skins are on their shoulders, on their fellies knives: they spread their glory out as birds spread out their wings. Mighty in mightiness, pervading, passing strong, visible from afar as ’twere with stars of heaven,Lovely with pleasant tongues, sweet singers with their mouths, the Maruts, joined with Indra, shout forth all around. This is your majesty, ye Maruts nobly born, far as the sway of Aditi your bounty spreads.Even Indra by desertion never disannuls the boon bestowed by you upon the pious man. This is your kinship, Maruts, that, Immortals, ye were oft in olden time regardful of our call,Having vouchsafed to man a hearing through this prayer, by wondrous deeds the Heroes have displayed their might. That, O ye Maruts, we may long time flourish through your abundant riches, O swift movers,And that our men may spread in the encampment, let me complete the rite with these oblations. May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: तन्नु वोचाम रभसाय जन्मने पूर्वं महित्वं वृषभस्य केतवे ।ऐधेव यामन्मरुतस्तुविष्वणो युधेव शक्रास्तविषाणि कर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ nú ǀ vocāma ǀ rabhasā́ya ǀ jánmane ǀ pū́rvam ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ ketáve ǀaidhā́-iva ǀ yā́man ǀ marutaḥ ǀ tuvi-svanaḥ ǀ yudhā́-iva ǀ śakrāḥ ǀ taviṣā́ṇi ǀ kartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now let us publish, for the vigorous company the herald of the Strong One, their primeval might. With fire upon your way, O Maruts loud of voice, with battle, Mighty Ones, achieve your deeds of strength.
verses.wilson_translation: We proclaim eagerly,Maruts, your ancient greatness, for (the sake of inducing) your prompt appearance, as the indication of (the approach of) the showerer (of benefits). Loud-roaring and mighty Maruts, you exert your vigorous energies for the advance (to the sacrifice), as if it was to battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Now let us publish, for the vigorous company the herald of the Strong One, their primeval might. With fire upon your way, O Maruts loud of voice, with battle, Mighty Ones, achieve your deeds of strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नित्यं न सूनुं मधु बिभ्रत उप क्रीळंति क्रीळा विदथेषु घृष्वयः ।नक्षंति रुद्रा अवसा नमस्विनं न मर्धंति स्वतवसो हविष्कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: nítyam ǀ ná ǀ sūnúm ǀ mádhu ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ úpa ǀ krī́ḷanti ǀ krīḷā́ḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ ghṛ́ṣvayaḥ ǀnákṣanti ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ namasvínam ǀ ná ǀ mardhanti ǀ svá-tavasaḥ ǀ haviḥ-kṛ́tam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bringing the pleasant meath as ’twere their own dear son, they sport in sportive wise gay at their gatherings. The Rudras come with succour to the worshipper; self-strong they fail not him who offers sacrifice.
