verses.wilson_translation: Ever accepting the sweet (libation), as (they would) a son, they sport plural yfully at sacrifices, demolishing (all intruders); the Rudrascome to the offerer of prayers and oblations, for his protection, and powerul as they are, do him no harm.
verses.griffith_verse: Bringing the pleasant meath as ’twere their own dear son, they sport in sportive wise gay at their gatherings. The Rudras come with succour to the worshipper; self-strong they fail not him who offers sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मा ऊमासो अमृता अरासत रायस्पोषं च हविषा ददाशुषे ।उक्षंत्यस्मै मरुतो हिता इव पुरू रजांसि पयसा मयोभुवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ ū́māsaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ árāsata ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ ca ǀ havíṣā ǀ dadāśúṣe ǀukṣánti ǀ asmai ǀ marútaḥ ǀ hitā́ḥ-iva ǀ purú ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ páyasā ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To whomsoever, bringer of oblations, they immortal guardians, have given plenteous wealth, For him, like loving friends, the Maruts bringing bliss bedew the regions round with milk abundantly.
verses.wilson_translation: To him, the presenter (of offerings), the protecting and immortal Maruts, (gratified) by the oblation, have given abundance of riches; they, the bestowers of happiness, becoming, as it were, the friends (of the worshipper), sprinkle the regions plural ntifully with water.
verses.griffith_verse: To whomsoever, bringer of oblations, they immortal guardians, have given plenteous wealth, For him, like loving friends, the Maruts bringing bliss bedew the regions round with milk abundantly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ ये रजांसि तविषीभिरव्यत प्र व एवासः स्वयतासो अध्रजन् ।भयंते विश्वा भुवनानि हर्म्या चित्रो वो यामः प्रयतास्वृष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yé ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ ávyata ǀ prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ évāsaḥ ǀ svá-yatāsaḥ ǀ adhrajan ǀbháyante ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ harmyā́ ǀ citráḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ prá-yatāsu ǀ ṛṣṭíṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye who with mighty powers have stirred the regions up, your coursers have sped forth directed by themselves. All creatures of the earth, all dwellings are afraid, for brilliant is your coming with your spears advanced.
verses.wilson_translation: Those, your coursers, which traverse the regions in their speed, proceed, self-guided; all worlds, all dwellings, are alarmed, for marvellous is your coming; (such fear as is felt) when spears are thrust forth (in battle).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye who with mighty powers have stirred the regions up, your coursers have sped forth directed by themselves. All creatures of the earth, all dwellings are afraid, for brilliant is your coming with your spears advanced.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्त्वेषयामा नदयंत पर्वतान्दिवो वा पृष्ठं नर्या अचुच्यवुः ।विश्वो वो अज्मन्भयते वनस्पती रथीयंतीव प्र जिहीत ओषधिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ tveṣá-yāmāḥ ǀ nadáyanta ǀ párvatān ǀ diváḥ ǀ vā ǀ pṛṣṭhám ǀ náryāḥ ǀ ácucyavuḥ ǀvíśvaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ájman ǀ bhayate ǀ vánaspátiḥ ǀ rathiyántī-iva ǀ prá ǀ jihīte ǀ óṣadhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they in dazzling rush have made the mountains roar, and shaken heaven's high back in their heroic strength, Each sovran of the forest fears as ye drive near, aid the shrubs fly before you swift as whirling wheels.
verses.wilson_translation: When your brilliant coursers make the mountains echo; and, friendly to man, traverse the summit of the firmament; then all the forest lords are alarmed at your approach, and the bushes wave to and fro, as a woman in a chariot.
verses.griffith_verse: When they in dazzling rush have made the mountains roar, and shaken heaven's high back in their heroic strength, Each sovran of the forest fears as ye drive near, aid the shrubs fly before you swift as whirling wheels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं न उग्रा मरुतः सुचेतुनारिष्टग्रामाः सुमतिं पिपर्तन ।यत्रा वो दिद्युद्रदति क्रिविर्दती रिणाति पश्वः सुधितेव बर्हणा ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ naḥ ǀ ugrāḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ su-cetúnā ǀ áriṣṭa-grāmāḥ ǀ su-matím ǀ pipartana ǀyátra ǀ vaḥ ǀ didyút ǀ rádati ǀ kríviḥ-datī ǀ riṇā́ti ǀ paśváḥ ǀ súdhitā-iva ǀ barháṇā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Terrible Maruts, ye with ne’er-diminished host, with great benevolence fulfil our heart's desire. Where’er your lightning bites armed with its gory teeth it crunches up the cattle like a well-aimed dart.
verses.wilson_translation: Fierce Maruts, free from malevolence in your kindly thoughts, fulfil towards us your good purposes; when your missile lightning rends (the clouds), as a well-hurled weapon wound the deer.
verses.griffith_verse: Terrible Maruts, ye with ne’er-diminished host, with great benevolence fulfil our heart's desire. Where’er your lightning bites armed with its gory teeth it crunches up the cattle like a well-aimed dart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र स्कंभदेष्णा अनवभ्रराधसोऽलातृणासो विदथेषु सुष्टुताः ।अर्चंत्यर्कं मदिरस्य पीतये विदुर्वीरस्य प्रथमानि पौंस्या ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ skambhá-deṣṇāḥ ǀ anavabhrá-rādhasaḥ ǀ alātṛṇā́saḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ sú-stutāḥ ǀárcanti ǀ arkám ǀ madirásya ǀ pītáye ǀ vidúḥ ǀ vīrásya ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ páuṃsyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Givers of during gifts whose bounties never fail, free from ill-will, at sacrifices glorified, They sing their song aloud that they may drink sweet juice: well do they know the Hero's first heroic deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Givers without stint, possessors of inexhaustible riches, devoid of malevolence, ever glorified at sacrifices, they worship the adorable (Indra), for (the sake of) drinking (the Soma) wine; for they know the first manly exploits of the hero.
verses.griffith_verse: Givers of during gifts whose bounties never fail, free from ill-will, at sacrifices glorified, They sing their song aloud that they may drink sweet juice: well do they know the Hero's first heroic deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतभुजिभिस्तमभिह्रुतेरघात्पूर्भी रक्षता मरुतो यमावत ।जनं यमुग्रास्तवसो विरप्शिनः पाथना शंसात्तनयस्य पुष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: śatábhuji-bhiḥ ǀ tám ǀ abhí-hruteḥ ǀ aghā́t ǀ pūḥ-bhíḥ ǀ rakṣata ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ā́vata ǀjánam ǀ yám ǀ ugrāḥ ǀ tavasaḥ ǀ vi-rapśinaḥ ǀ pāthána ǀ śáṃsāt ǀ tánayasya ǀ puṣṭíṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: With castles hundredfold, O Maruts, guard ye well the man whom ye have loved from ruin and from sin,— The man whom ye the fierce, the Mighty ones who roar, preserve from calumny by cherishing his seed.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, gratify, with infinite and complete enjoyments, him, whom you proect from degrading sin; that man whom, fierce and mighty, and glorified (as you are), you defend from calumny, by (providing for) the nourishment of his descendants.
verses.griffith_verse: With castles hundredfold, O Maruts, guard ye well the man whom ye have loved from ruin and from sin,— The man whom ye the fierce, the Mighty ones who roar, preserve from calumny by cherishing his seed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वानि भद्रा मरुतो रथेषु वो मिथस्पृध्येव तविषाण्याहिता ।अंसेष्वा वः प्रपथेषु खादयोऽक्षो वश्चक्रा समया वि वावृते ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvāni ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀ vaḥ ǀ mithaspṛ́dhyā-iva ǀ taviṣā́ṇi ǀ ā́-hitā ǀáṃseṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ prá-patheṣu ǀ khādáyaḥ ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ cakrā́ ǀ samáyā ǀ ví ǀ vavṛte ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Maruts, in your cars are all things that are good: great powers are set as ’twere in rivalry therein. Rings are upon your shoulders when ye journey forth: your axle turns together both the chariot wheels.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, all good things are in your cars; on your shoulders abides emulous strength; at your resting-plural ces on the road refreshments (are ready); the axle of your (chariot) wheels holds them firmly together.
verses.griffith_verse: O Maruts, in your cars are all things that are good: great powers are set as ’twere in rivalry therein. Rings are upon your shoulders when ye journey forth: your axle turns together both the chariot wheels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरीणि भद्रा नर्येषु बाहुषु वक्षःसु रुक्मा रभसासो अंजयः ।अंसेष्वेताः पविषु क्षुरा अधि वयो न पक्षान्व्यनु श्रियो धिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́rīṇi ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ náryeṣu ǀ bāhúṣu ǀ vákṣaḥ-su ǀ rukmā́ḥ ǀ rabhasā́saḥ ǀ añjáyaḥ ǀáṃseṣu ǀ étāḥ ǀ pavíṣu ǀ kṣurā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pakṣā́n ǀ ví ǀ ánu ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ dhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Held in your manly arms are many goodly things, gold chains are on your chests, and glistering ornaments, Deer-skins are on their shoulders, on their fellies knives: they spread their glory out as birds spread out their wings.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, in your arms, propitious to man, are many good things; on your breasts are golden (ornaments) brilliant and conspicuous; while garlands (hang) on your shoulders; sharp are (the edges of) your weapons; the Maruts have various decorations, as birds have (many-coloured) wings.
verses.griffith_verse: Held in your manly arms are many goodly things, gold chains are on your chests, and glistering ornaments, Deer-skins are on their shoulders, on their fellies knives: they spread their glory out as birds spread out their wings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महांतो मह्ना विभ्वो विभूतयो दूरेदृशो ये दिव्या इव स्तृभिः ।मंद्राः सुजिह्वाः स्वरितार आसभिः संमिश्ला इंद्रे मरुतः परिष्टुभः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahā́ntaḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ vi-bhváḥ ǀ ví-bhūtayaḥ ǀ dūre-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ yé ǀ divyā́ḥ-iva ǀ stṛ́-bhiḥ ǀmandrā́ḥ ǀ su-jihvā́ḥ ǀ sváritāraḥ ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǀ sám-miślāḥ ǀ índre ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pari-stúbhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty in mightiness, pervading, passing strong, visible from afar as ’twere with stars of heaven, Lovely with pleasant tongues, sweet singers with their mouths, the Maruts, joined with Indra, shout forth all around.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, mighty with mighty power, all-pervading, manifest afar off, as the gods (are made manifest) by the constellations; exhilarating, soft-tongued, speaking genitive ly with your mouths, associated with Indra, glorified by praise; (come to our sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty in mightiness, pervading, passing strong, visible from afar as ’twere with stars of heaven, Lovely with pleasant tongues, sweet singers with their mouths, the Maruts, joined with Indra, shout forth all around.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वः सुजाता मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं वो दात्रमदितेरिव व्रतं ।इंद्रश्चन त्यजसा वि ह्रुणाति तज्जनाय यस्मै सुकृते अराध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ su-jātāḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mahi-tvanám ǀ dīrghám ǀ vaḥ ǀ dātrám ǀ áditeḥ-iva ǀ vratám ǀíndraḥ ǀ caná ǀ tyájasā ǀ ví ǀ hruṇāti ǀ tát ǀ jánāya ǀ yásmai ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ árādhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is your majesty, ye Maruts nobly born, far as the sway of Aditi your bounty spreads. Even Indra by desertion never disannuls the boon bestowed by you upon the pious man.
verses.wilson_translation: Such, well-born Maruts, is your greatness, that your munificence is as long (continued) as the function of Aditi; and Indradoes not exceed, by his own liberality, (the value of) that which you have bestowed upon the devout man (who worships you).
verses.griffith_verse: This is your majesty, ye Maruts nobly born, far as the sway of Aditi your bounty spreads. Even Indra by desertion never disannuls the boon bestowed by you upon the pious man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वो जामित्वं मरुतः परे युगे पुरू यच्छंसममृतास आवत ।अया धिया मनवे श्रुष्टिमाव्या साकं नरो दंसनैरा चिकित्रिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ jāmi-tvám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ páre ǀ yugé ǀ purú ǀ yát ǀ śáṃsam ǀ amṛtāsaḥ ǀ ā́vata ǀayā́ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ mánave ǀ śruṣṭím ǀ ā́vya ǀ sākám ǀ náraḥ ǀ daṃsánaiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cikitrire ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is your kinship, Maruts, that, Immortals, ye were oft in olden time regardful of our call, Having vouchsafed to man a hearing through this prayer, by wondrous deeds the Heroes have displayed their might.
verses.wilson_translation: Your alliance with us,Maruts, is of a long duration on which account, immortals, accept our ample praise and, having accepted ourlaudation, be gratified, leaders (of sacrifice), by our holy acts, through this (your) favourable disposition towards mankind.
verses.griffith_verse: This is your kinship, Maruts, that, Immortals, ye were oft in olden time regardful of our call, Having vouchsafed to man a hearing through this prayer, by wondrous deeds the Heroes have displayed their might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येन दीर्घं मरुतः शूशवाम युष्माकेन परीणसा तुरासः ।आ यत्ततनन्वृजने जनास एभिर्यज्ञेभिस्तदभीष्टिमश्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ dīrghám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ śūśávāma ǀ yuṣmā́kena ǀ párīṇasā ǀ turāsaḥ ǀā́ ǀ yát ǀ tatánan ǀ vṛjáne ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ ebhíḥ ǀ yajñébhiḥ ǀ tát ǀ abhí ǀ íṣṭim ǀ aśyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: That, O ye Maruts, we may long time flourish through your abundant riches, O swift movers, And that our men may spread in the encampment, let me complete the rite with these oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Quick-moving Maruts, we augment the long (offered ceremony) upon your mighty (approach), whereby men triumph in war; may we obtain, by these our sacrifices, your wished-for (presence).
verses.griffith_verse: That, O ye Maruts, we may long time flourish through your abundant riches, O swift movers, And that our men may spread in the encampment, let me complete the rite with these oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ māndāryásya ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀā́ ǀ íṣā́ ǀ yāsīṣṭa ǀ tanvé ǀ vayā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you; (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring (by his laudations); may the praise reach you (for the good of your) person ns, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVII. Indra. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . A THOUSAND are thy helps for us, O Indra: a thousand, Lord of Bays, thy choice refreshments.Wealth of a thousand sorts hast thou to cheer us: may precious goods come nigh to us in thousands. May the most sapient Maruts, with protection, with best boons brought from lofty heaven, approach us,Now when their team of the most noble horses speeds even on the sea's extremest limit. Close to them clings one moving in seclusion, like a man's wife, like a spear carried rearward,Well grasped, bright, decked with gold there is Vāk also, like to a courtly, eloquent dame, among them. Far off the brilliant, never-weary Maruts cling to the young Maid as a joint possession.The fierce Gods drave not Rodasī before them, but wished for her to grow their friend and fellow. When chose immortal Rodasī to follow—she with loose tresses and heroic spirit—She climbed her servant's chariot, she like Sūrya with cloud-like motion and refulgent aspect. Upon their car the young men set the Maiden wedded to glory, mighty in assemblies,When your song, Maruts, rose, and, with oblation, the Soma-pourer sang his hymn in worship. I will declare the greatness of these Maruts, their real greatness, worthy to be lauded,How, with them, she though firm, strong-minded, haughty, travels to women happy in their fortune. Mitra and Varuṇa they guard from censure: Aryaman too, discovers worthless sinners Firm things are overthrown that ne’er were shaken: he prospers, Maruts, who gives choice oblations. None of us, Maruts, near or at a distance, hath ever reached the limit of your vigour.They in courageous might still waxing boldly have compassed round their foemen like an ocean. May we this day be dearest friends of Indra, and let us call on him in fight to-morrow.So were we erst. New might attend us daily! So be with us! Ṛbhukṣan of the Heroes! May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya,Bring offspring for ourselves with. food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रं त इंद्रोतयो नः सहस्रमिषो हरिवो गूर्ततमाः ।सहस्रं रायो मादयध्यै सहस्रिण उप नो यंतु वाजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sahásram ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ gūrtá-tamāḥ ǀsahásram ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ mādayádhyai ǀ sahasríṇaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ yantu ǀ vā́jāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A THOUSAND are thy helps for us, O Indra: a thousand, Lord of Bays, thy choice refreshments. Wealth of a thousand sorts hast thou to cheer us: may precious goods come nigh to us in thousands.
verses.wilson_translation: May your thousand benefits,Indra, come to us; may a thousand kinds of abundant food come to us, lord of horses; may a thousand (sorts of wealth) come to exhilarate us; may thousands of horses be ours.
verses.griffith_verse: A THOUSAND are thy helps for us, O Indra: a thousand, Lord of Bays, thy choice refreshments. Wealth of a thousand sorts hast thou to cheer us: may precious goods come nigh to us in thousands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नोऽवोभिर्मरुतो यांत्वच्छा ज्येष्ठेभिर्वा बृहद्दिवैः सुमायाः ।अध यदेषां नियुतः परमाः समुद्रस्य चिद्धनयंत पारे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ yāntu ǀ áccha ǀ jyéṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ bṛhát-divaiḥ ǀ su-māyā́ḥ ǀádha ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ paramā́ḥ ǀ samudrásya ǀ cit ǀ dhanáyanta ǀ pāré ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the most sapient Maruts, with protection, with best boons brought from lofty heaven, approach us, Now when their team of the most noble horses speeds even on the sea's extremest limit.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Marutscome to our presence with benefaction; may they who are possessed of knowledge (come) with most excellent and brilliant (treasures), since their glorious horses, the Niyutas, gather wealth even on the farther shore of the sea.
verses.griffith_verse: May the most sapient Maruts, with protection, with best boons brought from lofty heaven, approach us, Now when their team of the most noble horses speeds even on the sea's extremest limit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मिम्यक्ष येषु सुधिता घृताची हिरण्यनिर्णिगुपरा न ऋष्टिः ।गुहा चरंती मनुषो न योषा सभावती विदथ्येव सं वाक् ॥
verses.transliteration: mimyákṣa ǀ yéṣu ǀ sú-dhitā ǀ ghṛtā́cī ǀ híraṇya-nirnik ǀ úparā ǀ ná ǀ ṛṣṭíḥ ǀgúhā ǀ cárantī ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóṣā ǀ sabhā́-vatī ǀ vidathyā́-iva ǀ sám ǀ vā́k ǁ
verses.english_translation: Close to them clings one moving in seclusion, like a man's wife, like a spear carried rearward, Well grasped, bright, decked with gold there is Vāk also, like to a courtly, eloquent dame, among them.
verses.wilson_translation: In whom the water-shedding, golden-coloured lighting, is fitly deposited like a chaplet (of clouds) moving in the firmament like the (splendidly-attired) wife of a man (of rank), and distinguished in assemblies like a sacrificial hymn.
verses.griffith_verse: Close to them clings one moving in seclusion, like a man's wife, like a spear carried rearward, Well grasped, bright, decked with gold there is Vāk also, like to a courtly, eloquent dame, among them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः ।न रोदसी अप नुदंत घोरा जुषंत वृधं सख्याय देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ śubhrā́ḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀ yavyā́ ǀ sādhāraṇyā́-iva ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mimikṣuḥ ǀná ǀ rodasī́ íti ǀ ápa ǀ nudanta ǀ ghorā́ḥ ǀ juṣánta ǀ vṛ́dham ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far off the brilliant, never-weary Maruts cling to the young Maid as a joint possession. The fierce Gods drave not Rodasī before them, but wished for her to grow their friend and fellow.
verses.wilson_translation: The radiant, ever-moving Maruts, have mingled with (their) associate, (lightning), like (youths) with common women; the formidable divinities do not overwhelm heaven and earth (with rain), but promote their prosperity through (friendly) regard.
verses.griffith_verse: Far off the brilliant, never-weary Maruts cling to the young Maid as a joint possession. The fierce Gods drave not Rodasī before them, but wished for her to grow their friend and fellow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जोषद्यदीमसुर्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नृमणाः ।आ सूर्येव विधतो रथं गात्त्वेषप्रतीका नभसो नेत्या ॥
verses.transliteration: jóṣat ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ asuryā́ ǀ sacádhyai ǀ vísita-stukā ǀ rodasī́ ǀ nṛ-mánāḥ ǀā́ ǀ sūryā́-iva ǀ vidhatáḥ ǀ rátham ǀ gāt ǀ tveṣá-pratīkā ǀ nábhasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ityā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When chose immortal Rodasī to follow—she with loose tresses and heroic spirit— She climbed her servant's chariot, she like Sūrya with cloud-like motion and refulgent aspect.
verses.wilson_translation: Rodasī, the associate of the scatterers (of the clouds), with dishevelled tresses, and mind devoted to her lords, woos them to associate (with her); radiant in form, she has ascended the car of the restless (Maruts) as Sūrya(ascended the car of the Aśvins), and comes hither (with the celerity) of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: When chose immortal Rodasī to follow—she with loose tresses and heroic spirit— She climbed her servant's chariot, she like Sūrya with cloud-like motion and refulgent aspect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आस्थापयंत युवतिं युवानः शुभे निमिश्लां विदथेषु पज्रां ।अर्को यद्वो मरुतो हविष्मान्गायद्गाथं सुतसोमो दुवस्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ asthāpayanta ǀ yuvatím ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ śubhé ǀ ní-miślām ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ pajrā́m ǀarkáḥ ǀ yát ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ havíṣmān ǀ gā́yat ǀ gāthám ǀ sutá-somaḥ ǀ duvasyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon their car the young men set the Maiden wedded to glory, mighty in assemblies, When your song, Maruts, rose, and, with oblation, the Soma-pourer sang his hymn in worship.
verses.wilson_translation: The youthful (Maruts) have plural ced the young (lightning) in (their) brilliant (car), commingling (with them), and vigorous (in yielding rain) on sacrifices (being solemnized); when, Maruts, your worshipper, presenting oblations, pouring out the Soma, and offering adoration, chants the sacred song.
verses.griffith_verse: Upon their car the young men set the Maiden wedded to glory, mighty in assemblies, When your song, Maruts, rose, and, with oblation, the Soma-pourer sang his hymn in worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र तं विवक्मि वक्म्यो य एषां मरुतां महिमा सत���यो अस्ति ।सचा यदीं वृषमणा अहंयुः स्थिरा चिज्जनीर्वहते सुभागाः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tám ǀ vivakmi ǀ vákmyaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ marútām ǀ mahimā́ ǀ satyáḥ ǀ ásti ǀsácā ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ vṛ́ṣa-manāḥ ǀ aham-yúḥ ǀ sthirā́ ǀ cit ǀ jánīḥ ǀ váhate ǀ su-bhāgā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will declare the greatness of these Maruts, their real greatness, worthy to be lauded, How, with them, she though firm, strong-minded, haughty, travels to women happy in their fortune.
verses.wilson_translation: I celebrate that greatness of the Maruts, which is true, and worthy of celebration, inasmuch as their high-minded,haughty, and ever-enduring (bride), supports a flourishing progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: I will declare the greatness of these Maruts, their real greatness, worthy to be lauded, How, with them, she though firm, strong-minded, haughty, travels to women happy in their fortune.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पांति मित्रावरुणाववद्याच्चयत ईमर्यमो अप्रशस्तान् ।उत च्यवंते अच्युता ध्रुवाणि वावृध ईं मरुतो दातिवारः ॥
verses.transliteration: pā́nti ǀ mitrā́váruṇau ǀ avadyā́t ǀ cáyate ǀ īm ǀ aryamó íti ǀ ápra-śastān ǀutá ǀ cyavante ǀ ácyutā ǀ dhruvā́ṇi ǀ vavṛdhé ǀ īm ǀ marutaḥ ǀ dā́ti-vāraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitra and Varuṇa they guard from censure: Aryaman too, discovers worthless sinners Firm things are overthrown that ne’er were shaken: he prospers, Maruts, who gives choice oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, and Aryaman, defend (this) sacrifice from (all that is) reprehensible, and destroy (all that are) unworthy. They cause the yet unfallen and showering (rains) to descend, when,Maruts, the water-yielding (season) gives increase to this (world).
verses.griffith_verse: Mitra and Varuṇa they guard from censure: Aryaman too, discovers worthless sinners Firm things are overthrown that ne’er were shaken: he prospers, Maruts, who gives choice oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नही नु वो मरुतो अंत्यस्मे आरात्ताच्चिच्छवसो अंतमापुः ।ते धृष्णुना शवसा शूशुवांसोऽर्णो न द्वेषो धृषता परि ष्ठुः ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ nú ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ánti ǀ asmé íti ǀ ārā́ttāt ǀ cit ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ántam ǀ āpúḥ ǀté ǀ dhṛṣṇúnā ǀ śávasā ǀ śūśu-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ pári ǀ sthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: None of us, Maruts, near or at a distance, hath ever reached the limit of your vigour. They in courageous might still waxing boldly have compassed round their foemen like an ocean.
verses.wilson_translation: None of us,Maruts, have attained, either nearly or remotely, the limit of your strength; those (Maruts), increasing in energy and vigour, overwhelm their enemies like an ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: None of us, Maruts, near or at a distance, hath ever reached the limit of your vigour. They in courageous might still waxing boldly have compassed round their foemen like an ocean.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयमद्येंद्रस्य प्रेष्ठा वयं श्वो वोचेमहि समर्ये ।वयं पुरा महि च नो अनु द्यून्तन्न ऋभुक्षा नरामनु ष्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ adyá ǀ índrasya ǀ préṣṭhāḥ ǀ vayám ǀ śváḥ ǀ vocemahi ǀ sa-maryé ǀvayám ǀ purā́ ǀ máhi ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ ánu ǀ syāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we this day be dearest friends of Indra, and let us call on him in fight to-morrow. So were we erst. New might attend us daily! So be with us! Ṛbhukṣan of the Heroes!
verses.wilson_translation: Let us, who are beloved of Indra, glorify him today; let us glorify him tomorrow, at the sacred rite; let us glorify him for our great (good), in future days as of old, so thatṚbhukṣinmay ever be favourable to us amongst men.
verses.griffith_verse: May we this day be dearest friends of Indra, and let us call on him in fight to-morrow. So were we erst. New might attend us daily! So be with us! Ṛbhukṣan of the Heroes!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ māndāryásya ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀā́ ǀ íṣā́ ǀ yāsīṣṭa ǀ tanvé ǀ vayā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with. food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise,Maruts, is for you, this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations); may the praise reach you for (the good of your) person ns, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: May this your laud, may this your song, O Maruts, sung by the poet, Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with. food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVIII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SWIFT gain is his who hath you near at every rite: ye welcome every song of him who serves the Gods.So may I turn you hither with fair hymns of praise to give great succour for the weal of both the worlds. Surrounding, as it were, self-born, self-powerful, they spring to life the shakers-down of food and light;Like as the countess undulations of the floods, worthy of praise when near, like bullocks and like kine. They who, like Somas with their well-grown stalks pressed out, imbibed within the heart, dwell there in friendly wise.Upon their shoulders rests as ’twere a warrior's spear and in their hand they hold a dagger and a ring. Self-yoked they have descended lightly from the sky. With your own lash, Immortals, urge yourselves to speed.Unstained by dust the Maruts, mighty in their strength, have cast down e’en firm things, armed with their shining spears. Who among you, O Maruts armed with lightning-spears, moveth you by himself, as with the tongue his jaws?Ye rush from heaven's floor as though ye sought for food, on many errands like the Sun's diurnal Steed. Say where, then, is this mighty region's farthest bound, where, Maruts, is the lowest depth that ye have reached,When ye cast down like chaff the firmly stablished pile, and from the mountain send the glittering water-flood? Your winning is with strength, dazzling, with heavenly light, with fruit mature, O Maruts, fall of plenteousness.Auspicious is your gift like a free giver's meed, victorious, spreading far, as of immortal Gods. The rivers roar before your chariot fellies when they are uttering the voice of rain-clouds.The lightnings laugh upon the earth beneath them, what time the Maruts scatter forth their fatness. Pṛśni brought forth, to fight the mighty battle, the glittering army of the restless Maruts.Nurtured together they begat the monster, and then looked round them for the food that strengthens. May this your laud, may this your song O Maruts, sung by the poet Māna's son, Māndārya,Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञायज्ञा वः समना तुतुर्वणिर्धियंधियं वो देवया उ दधिध्वे ।आ वोऽर्वाचः सुविताय रोदस्योर्महे ववृत्यामवसे सुवृक्तिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñā́-yajñā ǀ vaḥ ǀ samanā́ ǀ tuturváṇiḥ ǀ dhíyam-dhiyam ǀ vaḥ ǀ deva-yā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dadhidhve ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ arvā́caḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀ mahé ǀ vavṛtyām ǀ ávase ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SWIFT gain is his who hath you near at every rite: ye welcome every song of him who serves the Gods. So may I turn you hither with fair hymns of praise to give great succour for the weal of both the worlds.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, at every sacrifice your alacrity is uniform; you, verily, discharge your every function for the benefit of the gods; therefore, do I invite you to come hither, by sacred hymns, for (the sake of) your powerful protection of heaven and earth, and your benevolent praise.
verses.griffith_verse: SWIFT gain is his who hath you near at every rite: ye welcome every song of him who serves the Gods. So may I turn you hither with fair hymns of praise to give great succour for the weal of both the worlds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वव्रासो न ये स्वजाः स्वतवस इषं स्वरभिजायंत धूतयः ।सहस्रियासो अपां नोर्मय आसा गावो वंद्यासो नोक्षणः ॥
verses.transliteration: vavrā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ sva-jā́ḥ ǀ svá-tavasaḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ sváḥ ǀ abhi-jā́yanta ǀ dhū́tayaḥ ǀsahasríyāsaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ ná ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ āsā́ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ vándyāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Surrounding, as it were, self-born, self-powerful, they spring to life the shakers-down of food and light; Like as the countess undulations of the floods, worthy of praise when near, like bullocks and like kine.
verses.wilson_translation: They who are as if embodied, self-born, self-invigorated, and (ever) tremulous (in movement), are genitive rated (to confer) abundant food and heaven; they are numerous as the undulations of the waters; they are to be praised when present, shedding water, like cows (yielding milk).
verses.griffith_verse: Surrounding, as it were, self-born, self-powerful, they spring to life the shakers-down of food and light; Like as the countess undulations of the floods, worthy of praise when near, like bullocks and like kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमासो न ये सुतास्तृप्तांशवो हृत्सु पीतासो दुवसो नासते ।ऐषामंसेषु रंभिणीव रारभे हस्तेषु खादिश्च कृतिश्च सं दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: sómāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ sutā́ḥ ǀ tṛptá-aṃśavaḥ ǀ hṛt-sú ǀ pītā́saḥ ǀ duvásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ā́sate ǀā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ áṃseṣu ǀ rambhíṇī-iva ǀ rarabhe ǀ hásteṣu ǀ khādíḥ ǀ ca ǀ kṛtíḥ ǀ ca ǀ sám ǀ dadhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who, like Somas with their well-grown stalks pressed out, imbibed within the heart, dwell there in friendly wise. Upon their shoulders rests as ’twere a warrior's spear and in their hand they hold a dagger and a ring.
verses.wilson_translation: They, who are like the Soma, with well-nourished shoots, and then poured out (in libations), are imbibed; they abide, like devoted adherents, in the hearts (of men); upon their shoulders hangs (a lance) like a youthful feminine le, and in theirhandsa guard and sword are wielded.
verses.griffith_verse: They who, like Somas with their well-grown stalks pressed out, imbibed within the heart, dwell there in friendly wise. Upon their shoulders rests as ’twere a warrior's spear and in their hand they hold a dagger and a ring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव स्वयुक्ता दिव आ वृथा ययुरमर्त्याः कशया चोदत त्मना ।अरेणवस्तुविजाता अचुच्यवुर्दृळ्हानि चिन्मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ svá-yuktāḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ yayuḥ ǀ ámartyāḥ ǀ káśayā ǀ codata ǀ tmánā ǀareṇávaḥ ǀ tuvi-jātā́ḥ ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀ dṛḷhā́ni ǀ cit ǀ marútaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Self-yoked they have descended lightly from the sky. With your own lash, Immortals, urge yourselves to speed. Unstained by dust the Maruts, mighty in their strength, have cast down e’en firm things, armed with their shining spears.
verses.wilson_translation: Mutually supported, they descend readily from the sky; immortal Maruts, animate us by your own words (to praise you); exempt from toil, present at many (sacrifices), brilliant-eyed, the Maruts ahve shaken the firmest mountains.
verses.griffith_verse: Self-yoked they have descended lightly from the sky. With your own lash, Immortals, urge yourselves to speed. Unstained by dust the Maruts, mighty in their strength, have cast down e’en firm things, armed with their shining spears.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को वोऽंतर्मरुत ऋष्टिविद्युतो रेजति त्मना हन्वेव जिह्वया ।धन्वच्युत इषां न यामनि पुरुप्रैषा अहन्यो नैतशः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭi-vidyutaḥ ǀ réjati ǀ tmánā ǀ hánvā-iva ǀ jihváyā ǀdhanva-cyútaḥ ǀ iṣā́m ǀ ná ǀ yā́mani ǀ puru-práiṣāḥ ǀ ahanyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ étaśaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who among you, O Maruts armed with lightning-spears, moveth you by himself, as with the tongue his jaws? Ye rush from heaven's floor as though ye sought for food, on many errands like the Sun's diurnal Steed.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, lightning-armed, who, (standing) amongst you, sets you of yourselves in motion, as the jaws are (set in motion) by the tongue; as falling rains(are essential) for the obtaining of food, so (those, desirous of sustenance), excite you in various ways, like a horse in (his) daily (training).
verses.griffith_verse: Who among you, O Maruts armed with lightning-spears, moveth you by himself, as with the tongue his jaws? Ye rush from heaven's floor as though ye sought for food, on many errands like the Sun's diurnal Steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व स्विदस्य रजसो महस्परं क्वावरं मरुतो यस्मिन्नायय ।यच्च्यावयथ विथुरेव संहितं व्यद्रिणा पतथ त्वेषमर्णवं ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ svit ǀ asyá ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ páram ǀ kvá ǀ ávaram ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yásmin ǀ ā-yayá ǀyát ǀ cyaváyatha ǀ vithurā́-iva ǀ sám-hitam ǀ ví ǀ ádriṇā ǀ patatha ǀ tveṣám ǀ arṇavám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Say where, then, is this mighty region's farthest bound, where, Maruts, is the lowest depth that ye have reached, When ye cast down like chaff the firmly stablished pile, and from the mountain send the glittering water-flood?
verses.wilson_translation: Where,Maruts, is the limit of the vast region (whence you come); where is the beginning of that to which you proceed; when you scatter the dense vapour like light grass, and hurl down the brilliant rain-cloud by the thunderbolt.
verses.griffith_verse: Say where, then, is this mighty region's farthest bound, where, Maruts, is the lowest depth that ye have reached, When ye cast down like chaff the firmly stablished pile, and from the mountain send the glittering water-flood?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सातिर्न वोऽमवती स्वर्वती त्वेषा विपाका मरुतः पिपिष्वती ।भद्रा वो रातिः पृणतो न दक्षिणा पृथुज्रयी असुर्येव जंजती ॥
verses.transliteration: sātíḥ ǀ ná ǀ vaḥ ǀ áma-vatī ǀ sváḥ-vatī ǀ tveṣā́ ǀ ví-pākā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ pípiṣvatī ǀbhadrā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ rātíḥ ǀ pṛṇatáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ pṛthu-jráyī ǀ ásuryā-iva ǀ jáñjatī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your winning is with strength, dazzling, with heavenly light, with fruit mature, O Maruts, fall of plenteousness. Auspicious is your gift like a free giver's meed, victorious, spreading far, as of immortal Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Like your possession of treasure,Maruts, is your liberality; ministerial (of Indra's bounty), heaven-bestowing, brilliant, fruitful, favourable to the husbandman, propitious; it is like the donation of a wealthy (donor), prompt (of distribution), and like the all-subduing force of theasuras.
verses.griffith_verse: Your winning is with strength, dazzling, with heavenly light, with fruit mature, O Maruts, fall of plenteousness. Auspicious is your gift like a free giver's meed, victorious, spreading far, as of immortal Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति ष्टोभंति सिंधवः पविभ्यो यदभ्रियां वाचमुदीरयंति ।अव स्मयंत विद्युतः पृथिव्यां यदी घृतं मरुतः प्रुष्णुवंति ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ stobhanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ paví-bhyaḥ ǀ yát ǀ abhríyām ǀ vā́cam ǀ ut-īráyanti ǀáva ǀ smayanta ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ yádi ǀ ghṛtám ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pruṣṇuvánti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The rivers roar before your chariot fellies when they are uttering the voice of rain-clouds. The lightnings laugh upon the earth beneath them, what time the Maruts scatter forth their fatness.
verses.wilson_translation: The rivers are arrested by the thunderbolts when they utter the voice of the clouds; but the lightnings smile in the firmament when the Marutssprinkle water on the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: The rivers roar before your chariot fellies when they are uttering the voice of rain-clouds. The lightnings laugh upon the earth beneath them, what time the Maruts scatter forth their fatness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असूत पृश्निर्महते रणाय त्वेषमयासां मरुतामनीकं ।ते सप्सरासोऽजनयंताभ्वमादित्स्वधामिषिरां पर्यपश्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ásūta ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ mahaté ǀ ráṇāya ǀ tveṣám ǀ ayā́sām ǀ marútām ǀ ánīkam ǀté ǀ sapsarā́saḥ ǀ ajanayanta ǀ ábhvam ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ svadhā́m ǀ iṣirā́m ǀ pári ǀ apaśyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pṛśni brought forth, to fight the mighty battle, the glittering army of the restless Maruts. Nurtured together they begat the monster, and then looked round them for the food that strengthens.
verses.wilson_translation: Pṛśnibore the brilliant troop of the quick-moving Marutsfor the great combat (with the clouds), whereupon (mankind) immediately beheld the desiderated food.
verses.griffith_verse: Pṛśni brought forth, to fight the mighty battle, the glittering army of the restless Maruts. Nurtured together they begat the monster, and then looked round them for the food that strengthens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ māndāryásya ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀā́ ǀ iṣā́ ǀ yāsīṣṭa ǀ tanvé ǀ vayā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this your laud, may this your song O Maruts, sung by the poet Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise,Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations); may the praise reach you for (the good of your) person ns, so that we may thence obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: May this your laud, may this your song O Maruts, sung by the poet Māna's son, Māndārya, Bring offspring for ourselves with food to feed us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXIX. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ८ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणः। इन्द्रः। त्रिष्टुप्, २ चतुष्पदा विराट्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As, Indra, from great treason thou protectest, yea, from great treachery these who approach us,So, marking well, Controller of the Maruts grant us their blessings, for they are thy dearest. The various doings of all mortal people by thee are ordered, in thy wisdom, Indra.The host of Maruts goeth forth exulting to win the light-bestowing spoil of battle. That spear of thine sat firm for us, O Indra: the Maruts set their whole dread power in motion.E’en Agni shines resplendent in the brush-wood: the viands hold him as floods hold an island. Vouchsafe us now that opulence, O Indra, as guerdon won by mightiest donation.May hymns that please thee cause the breast of Vāyu to swell as with the mead's refreshing sweetness. With thee, O Indra, are most bounteous riches that further every one who lives uprightly.Now may these Maruts show us loving-kindness, Gods who of old were ever prompt to help us. Bring forth the Men who rain down boons, O Indra: exert thee in the great terrestrial region;For their broad-chested speckled deer are standing like a King's armies on the field of battle. Heard is the roar of the advancing Maruts, terrific, glittering, and swiftly moving,Who with their rush o’erthrow as ’twere a sinner the mortal who would fight with those who love him Give to the Mānas, Indra with Maruts, gifts universal, gifts of cattle foremost.Thou, God, art praised with Gods who must be lauded. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: महश्चित्त्वमिंद्र यत एतान्महश्चिदसि त्यजसो वरूता ।स नो वेधो मरुतां चिकित्वान्त्सुम्ना वनुष्व तव हि प्रेष्ठा ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ cit ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ yatáḥ ǀ etā́n ǀ maháḥ ǀ cit ǀ asi ǀ tyájasaḥ ǀ varūtā́ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vedhaḥ ǀ marútām ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ sumnā́ ǀ vanuṣva ǀ táva ǀ hí ǀ préṣṭhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As, Indra, from great treason thou protectest, yea, from great treachery these who approach us, So, marking well, Controller of the Maruts grant us their blessings, for they are thy dearest.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are mighty from the might of those of whom you are the protector against abandonment therefore, creator of the Maruts, favourably-minded towards us, grant us those blessings which are most dear to you.
verses.griffith_verse: As, Indra, from great treason thou protectest, yea, from great treachery these who approach us, So, marking well, Controller of the Maruts grant us their blessings, for they are thy dearest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयुज्रंत इंद्र विश्वकृष्टीर्विदानासो निष्षिधो मर्त्यत्रा ।मरुतां पृत्सुतिर्हासमाना स्वर्मीळ्हस्य प्रधनस्य सातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: áyujran ǀ té ǀ indra ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭīḥ ǀ vidānā́saḥ ǀ niḥ-sídhaḥ ǀ martya-trā́ ǀmarútām ǀ pṛtsutíḥ ǀ hā́samānā ǀ sváḥ-mīḷhasya ǀ pra-dhánasya ǀ sātáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The various doings of all mortal people by thee are ordered, in thy wisdom, Indra. The host of Maruts goeth forth exulting to win the light-bestowing spoil of battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Rulers over all men, and impelling towards man the water-shedding clouds, they are united,Indra, (with you); the host of Marutsis delighted by (your) acquisition of heaven-bestowing wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: The various doings of all mortal people by thee are ordered, in thy wisdom, Indra. The host of Maruts goeth forth exulting to win the light-bestowing spoil of battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अम्यक्सा त इंद्र ऋष्टिरस्मे सनेम्यभ्वं मरुतो जुनंति ।अग्निश्चिद्धि ष्मातसे शुशुक्वानापो न द्वीपं दधति प्रयांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: ámyak ǀ sā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ ṛṣṭíḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ sánemi ǀ ábhvam ǀ marútaḥ ǀ junanti ǀagníḥ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ atasé ǀ śuśukvā́n ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ dvīpám ǀ dádhati ǀ práyāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: That spear of thine sat firm for us, O Indra: the Maruts set their whole dread power in motion. E’en Agni shines resplendent in the brush-wood: the viands hold him as floods hold an island.
verses.wilson_translation: Your weapon,Indra, is athandfor our (good); the Marutssend down the long-accusative ulated rain;Agniis blazing for the ceremony; the oblations encompass him as the waters (surround) an island.
verses.griffith_verse: That spear of thine sat firm for us, O Indra: the Maruts set their whole dread power in motion. E’en Agni shines resplendent in the brush-wood: the viands hold him as floods hold an island.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तू न इंद्र तं रयिं दा ओजिष्ठया दक्षिणयेव रातिं ।स्तुतश्च यास्ते चकनंत वायोः स्तनं न मध्वः पीपयंत वाजैः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ tám ǀ rayím ǀ dāḥ ǀ ójiṣṭhayā ǀ dákṣiṇayā-iva ǀ rātím ǀstútaḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ cakánanta ǀ vāyóḥ ǀ stánam ǀ ná ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ pīpayanta ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vouchsafe us now that opulence, O Indra, as guerdon won by mightiest donation. May hymns that please thee cause the breast of Vāyu to swell as with the mead's refreshing sweetness.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, quickly grant us that wealth (which you possess, for we gratify) the donor with a most worthy present; we, your praisers, offer to you, the ready giver of boons, the laudations that would propitiate you; (and the priests) nourish you with sacrificial food, as they cherish the bosom (of a feminine le for the sakeof replenishing it) with sweet (milk).
verses.griffith_verse: Vouchsafe us now that opulence, O Indra, as guerdon won by mightiest donation. May hymns that please thee cause the breast of Vāyu to swell as with the mead's refreshing sweetness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे राय इंद्र तोशतमाः प्रणेतारः कस्य चिदृतायोः ।ते षु णो मरुतो मृळयंतु ये स्मा पुरा गातूयंतीव देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ indra ǀ tośá-tamāḥ ǀ pra-netā́raḥ ǀ kásya ǀ cit ǀ ṛta-yóḥ ǀté ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mṛḷayantu ǀ yé ǀ sma ǀ purā́ ǀ gātuyánti-iva ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With thee, O Indra, are most bounteous riches that further every one who lives uprightly. Now may these Maruts show us loving-kindness, Gods who of old were ever prompt to help us.
verses.wilson_translation: Your riches,Indra, are most delighting; the exciters of any one desirous to sacrifice; may those Marutsbe propitious to us; the divine beings who were anxious to go first to the ceremony.
verses.griffith_verse: With thee, O Indra, are most bounteous riches that further every one who lives uprightly. Now may these Maruts show us loving-kindness, Gods who of old were ever prompt to help us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति प्र याहींद्र मीळ्हुषो नॄन्महः पार्थिवे सदने यतस्व ।अध यदेषां पृथुबुध्नास एतास्तीर्थे नार्यः पौंस्यानि तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ indra ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ maháḥ ǀ pā́rthive ǀ sádane ǀ yatasva ǀádha ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ pṛthu-budhnā́saḥ ǀ étāḥ ǀ tīrthé ǀ ná ǀ aryáḥ ǀ páuṃsyāni ǀ tasthúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring forth the Men who rain down boons, O Indra: exert thee in the great terrestrial region; For their broad-chested speckled deer are standing like a King's armies on the field of battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Go,Indra, to the mighty rain-shedding leaders (of the clouds), and exert yourself in (thine) aerial dwelling; for their broad-footed steeds stand (firm), like the manly energies of an enemy in the field of battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring forth the Men who rain down boons, O Indra: exert thee in the great terrestrial region; For their broad-chested speckled deer are standing like a King's armies on the field of battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति घोराणामेतानामयासां मरुतां शृण्व आयतामुपब्दिः ।ये मर्त्यं पृतनायंतमूमैर्ऋणावानं न पतयंत सर्गैः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ ghorā́ṇām ǀ étānām ǀ ayā́sām ǀ marútām ǀ śṛṇve ǀ ā-yatā́m ǀ upabdíḥ ǀyé ǀ mártyam ǀ pṛtanā-yántam ǀ ū́maiḥ ǀ ṛṇa-vā́nam ǀ ná ǀ patáyanta ǀ sárgaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heard is the roar of the advancing Maruts, terrific, glittering, and swiftly moving, Who with their rush o’erthrow as ’twere a sinner the mortal who would fight with those who love him
verses.wilson_translation: The noise of the formidable, dark-coloured, swift-moving and advancing Maruts, is everywhere echoed; (the noise) of them who strike down their mortal (foes) gathering in a host against them, by their self-defending blows, as (they strike down) a contemptible enemy.
verses.griffith_verse: Heard is the roar of the advancing Maruts, terrific, glittering, and swiftly moving, Who with their rush o’erthrow as ’twere a sinner the mortal who would fight with those who love him
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं मानेभ्य इंद्र विश्वजन्या रदा मरुद्भिः शुरुधो गोअग्राः ।स्तवानेभिः स्तवसे देव देवैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ mā́nebhyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ viśvá-janyā ǀ ráda ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ gó-agrāḥ ǀstávānebhiḥ ǀ stavase ǀ deva ǀ deváiḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give to the Mānas, Indra with Maruts, gifts universal, gifts of cattle foremost. Thou, God, art praised with Gods who must be lauded. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Associated with the Maruts, do you,Indra, for your own honour and the good of all, pierce the exhilarating receptacles of the waters, for you, Indra, are glorified by the lauded divinities; may we obtain for you food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Give to the Mānas, Indra with Maruts, gifts universal, gifts of cattle foremost. Thou, God, art praised with Gods who must be lauded. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXX. Indra. Maruts.
hymns.anukramani: (५) १,३,४ इन्द्रः, (४अगस्त्यो वा,) २,५ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः । इन्द्रः। १बृहती, २-४ अनुष्टुप्, ५ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery?We must address ourselves unto another's thought, and lost is then the hope we formed. The Maruts are thy brothers. Why, O Indra, wouldst thou take our lives?Agree with them in friendly wise, and do not slay us in the fight. Agastya, brother, why dost thou neglect us, thou who art our friend?We know the nature of thy mind. Verity thou wilt give us naught. Let them prepare the altar, let them kindle fire in front: we twoHere will spread sacrifice for thee, that the Immortal may observe. Thou, Lord of Wealth, art Master of all treasures, thou, Lord of friends, art thy friends' best supporter.O Indra, speak thou kindly with the Maruts, and taste oblations in their proper season.

verses.sanskrit: न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं ।अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ nūnám ǀ ásti ǀ nó íti ǀ śváḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ tát ǀ veda ǀ yát ǀ ádbhutam ǀanyásya ǀ cittám ǀ abhí ǀ sam-caréṇyam ǀ utá ǀ ā́-dhītam ǀ ví ǀ naśyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery? We must address ourselves unto another's thought, and lost is then the hope we formed.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks): It is not certain what today or what tomorrow will yield to us; who comprehends this mystery; verily, the mind of any other (being) is of an unsteady (nature), and even that which has been profoundly studied, is (in time) forgotten.
verses.griffith_verse: NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery? We must address ourselves unto another's thought, and lost is then the hope we formed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं न इंद्र जिघांससि भ्रातरो मरुतस्तव ।तेभिः कल्पस्व साधुया मा नः समरणे वधीः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ jighāṃsasi ǀ bhrā́taraḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ táva ǀtébhiḥ ǀ kalpasva ǀ sādhu-yā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sam-áraṇe ǀ vadhīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts are thy brothers. Why, O Indra, wouldst thou take our lives? Agree with them in friendly wise, and do not slay us in the fight.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agstya): Why,Indra, do you purpose to slay us; the Marutsare your brothers; share with them (the offering) in peace; destroy us not in enmity.
verses.griffith_verse: The Maruts are thy brothers. Why, O Indra, wouldst thou take our lives? Agree with them in friendly wise, and do not slay us in the fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं नो भ्रातरगस्त्य सखा सन्नति मन्यसे ।विद्मा हि ते यथा मनोऽस्मभ्यमिन्न दित्ससि ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ naḥ ǀ bhrātaḥ ǀ agastya ǀ sákhā ǀ sán ǀ áti ǀ manyase ǀvidmá ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ yáthā ǀ mánaḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ ditsasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agastya, brother, why dost thou neglect us, thou who art our friend? We know the nature of thy mind. Verity thou wilt give us naught.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra): Wherefore, brother Agastya, do you, who are my friend, treat me with regard; verily, we know what is in your mind; you do not intend to give us anything.
verses.griffith_verse: Agastya, brother, why dost thou neglect us, thou who art our friend? We know the nature of thy mind. Verity thou wilt give us naught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अरं कृण्वंतु वेदिं समग्निमिंधतां पुरः ।तत्रामृतस्य चेतनं यज्ञं ते तनवावहै ॥
verses.transliteration: áram ǀ kṛṇvantu ǀ védim ǀ sám ǀ agním ǀ indhatām ǀ puráḥ ǀtátra ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ cétanam ǀ yajñám ǀ te ǀ tanavāvahai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let them prepare the altar, let them kindle fire in front: we two Here will spread sacrifice for thee, that the Immortal may observe.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agastya): Let the priests decorate the altar; let them kindle the fire to the east; and then let us both consummate the sacrifice, the inspirerof immortal (wisdom).
verses.griffith_verse: Let them prepare the altar, let them kindle fire in front: we two Here will spread sacrifice for thee, that the Immortal may observe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमीशिषे वसुपते वसूनां त्वं मित्राणां मित्रपते धेष्ठः ।इंद्र त्वं मरुद्भिः सं वदस्वाध प्राशान ऋतुथा हवींषि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ īśiṣe ǀ vasu-pate ǀ vásūnām ǀ tvám ǀ mitrā́ṇām ǀ mitra-pate ǀ dhéṣṭhaḥ ǀíndra ǀ tvám ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ vadasva ǀ ádha ǀ prá ǀ aśāna ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Lord of Wealth, art Master of all treasures, thou, Lord of friends, art thy friends' best supporter. O Indra, speak thou kindly with the Maruts, and taste oblations in their proper season.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agastya); You, Vasupati, are the lord of riches; you, Mitrapati, are the firm stay (of us), your friends; declare,Indra, along with the Maruts, (your approval of our acts), and partake of the oblation offered in due season.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Lord of Wealth, art Master of all treasures, thou, Lord of friends, art thy friends' best supporter. O Indra, speak thou kindly with the Maruts, and taste oblations in their proper season.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXI. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To you I come with this mine adoration, and with a hymn I crave the Strong Ones' favourA hymn that truly makes you joyful, Maruts. Suppress your anger and unyoke your horses. Maruts, to you this laud with prayer and worship, formed in the mind and heart, ye Gods, is offered.Come ye to us, rejoicing in your spirit, for ye are they who make our prayer effective. The Maruts, praised by us, shall show us favour; Maghavan, lauded, shall be most propitious.Maruts,, may all our days that are to follow be very pleasant, lovely and triumphant. I fled interrorfrom this mighty Indra, my body trembling in alarm, O Maruts.Oblations meant for you had been made ready; these have we set aside: for this forgive us. By whom the Mānas recognize the day-springs, by whose strength at the dawn of endless mornings,Give us, thou Mighty, glory with Maruts. fierce with the fierce, the Strong who givest triumph. Do thou, O Indra, guard the conquering Heroes, and rid thee of thy wrath against the Maruts,With them, the wise, victorious and bestowing. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: प्रति व एना नमसाहमेमि सूक्तेन भिक्षे सुमतिं तुराणां ।रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ vaḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ námasā ǀ ahám ǀ emi ǀ su-ukténa ǀ bhikṣe ǀ su-matím ǀ turā́ṇām ǀrarāṇátā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vedyā́bhiḥ ǀ ní ǀ héḷaḥ ǀ dhattá ǀ ví ǀ mucadhvam ǀ áśvān ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you I come with this mine adoration, and with a hymn I crave the Strong Ones' favour A hymn that truly makes you joyful, Maruts. Suppress your anger and unyoke your horses.
verses.wilson_translation: I approach you,Maruts, with this reverential homage, and with a hymn implore your favour against eager (foes); with minds pacified by our praises, suppress your anger, and let loose your horses.
verses.griffith_verse: To you I come with this mine adoration, and with a hymn I crave the Strong Ones' favour A hymn that truly makes you joyful, Maruts. Suppress your anger and unyoke your horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वः स्तोमो मरुतो नमस्वान्हृदा तष्टो मनसा धायि देवाः ।उपेमा यात मनसा जुषाणा यूयं हि ष्ठा नमस इद्वृधासः ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ námasvān ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ taṣṭáḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ dhāyi ǀ devāḥ ǀúpa ǀ īm ǀ ā́ ǀ yāta ǀ mánasā ǀ juṣāṇā́ḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ hí ǀ sthá ǀ námasaḥ ǀ ít ǀ vṛdhā́saḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, to you this laud with prayer and worship, formed in the mind and heart, ye Gods, is offered. Come ye to us, rejoicing in your spirit, for ye are they who make our prayer effective.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise, accompanied by offerings,Maruts, is for you, offered from the heart; accept it, divinities, with favour, and come with willing minds (to receive) these (laudations), for you are the augmenters of sacrificial food.
verses.griffith_verse: Maruts, to you this laud with prayer and worship, formed in the mind and heart, ye Gods, is offered. Come ye to us, rejoicing in your spirit, for ye are they who make our prayer effective.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तुतासो नो मरुतो मृळयंतूत स्तुतो मघवा शंभविष्ठः ।ऊर्ध्वा नः संतु कोम्या वनान्यहानि विश्वा मरुतो जिगीषा ॥
verses.transliteration: stutā́saḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mṛḷayantu ǀ utá ǀ stutáḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhaḥ ǀūrdhvā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ santu ǀ komyā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ áhāni ǀ víśvā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ jigīṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts, praised by us, shall show us favour; Maghavan, lauded, shall be most propitious. Maruts,, may all our days that are to follow be very pleasant, lovely and triumphant.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, now hymned, bestow happiness upon us; may Maghavan, now glorified, be propitious to us; Maruts, may all the ensuing days that may be expected by us prove gratifying and full of enjoyment.
verses.griffith_verse: The Maruts, praised by us, shall show us favour; Maghavan, lauded, shall be most propitious. Maruts,, may all our days that are to follow be very pleasant, lovely and triumphant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मादहं तविषादीषमाण इंद्राद्भिया मरुतो रेजमानः ।युष्मभ्यं हव्या निशितान्यासन्तान्यारे चकृमा मृळता नः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́t ǀ ahám ǀ taviṣā́t ǀ ī́ṣamāṇaḥ ǀ índrāt ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ réjamānaḥ ǀyuṣmábhyam ǀ havyā́ ǀ ní-śitāni ǀ āsan ǀ tā́ni ǀ āré ǀ cakṛma ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I fled in terror from this mighty Indra, my body trembling in alarm, O Maruts. Oblations meant for you had been made ready; these have we set aside: for this forgive us.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, through fear of that violent Indra, I fly, trembling, (from his presence); the oblations that had been prepared for you have been put away; nevertheless, have patience with us.
verses.griffith_verse: I fled in terror from this mighty Indra, my body trembling in alarm, O Maruts. Oblations meant for you had been made ready; these have we set aside: for this forgive us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येन मानासश्चितयंत उस्रा व्युष्टिषु शवसा शश्वतीनां ।स नो मरुद्भिर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ mā́nāsaḥ ǀ citáyante ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ śávasā ǀ śáśvatīnām ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ ugrébhiḥ ǀ stháviraḥ ǀ sahaḥ-dā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By whom the Mānas recognize the day-springs, by whose strength at the dawn of endless mornings, Give us, thou Mighty, glory with Maruts. fierce with the fierce, the Strong who givest triumph.
verses.wilson_translation: The rays of the ever-recurring mornings, favoured,Indra, by your vigour, confer consciousness as they shine; showerer of benefits, ancient (of days), bestower of strength, fierce, (and attended), by the fierce Maruts, grant us (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: By whom the Mānas recognize the day-springs, by whose strength at the dawn of endless mornings, Give us, thou Mighty, glory with Maruts. fierce with the fierce, the Strong who givest triumph.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं पाहींद्र सहीयसो नॄन्भवा मरुद्भिरवयातहेळाः ।सुप्रकेतेभिः सासहिर्दधानो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ pāhi ǀ indra ǀ sáhīyasaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ bháva ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ ávayāta-heḷāḥ ǀsu-praketébhiḥ ǀ sasahíḥ ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do thou, O Indra, guard the conquering Heroes, and rid thee of thy wrath against the Maruts, With them, the wise, victorious and bestowing. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, cherish the vigorous leaders (of the rains), be free from displeasure against the Maruts; overcoming (our) enemies along with the intelligent (Maruts), support us (so that) we may obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Do thou, O Indra, guard the conquering Heroes, and rid thee of thy wrath against the Maruts, With them, the wise, victorious and bestowing. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones,Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam. Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft;Far from us be the stone ye hurl. O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Tṛṇskanda's folk;Lift ye us up that we may live.

verses.sanskrit: चित्रो वोऽस्तु य��मश्चित्र ऊती सुदानवः ।मरुतो अहिभानवः ॥
verses.transliteration: citráḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ astu ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ citráḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀmárutaḥ ǀ áhi-bhānavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones, Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, of inseparable splendour, may your coming be marvellous, liberal benefactors, for our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones, Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आरे सा वः सुदानवो मरुत ऋंजती शरुः ।आरे अश्मा यमस्यथ ॥
verses.transliteration: āré ǀ sā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ márutaḥ ǀ ṛñjatī́ ǀ śáruḥ ǀāré ǀ áśmā ǀ yám ǀ ásyatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft; Far from us be the stone ye hurl.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, liberal benefactors, may your bright destructive (shaft) be far from us; may the stone which you hurl be far from us.
verses.griffith_verse: Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft; Far from us be the stone ye hurl.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तृणस्कंदस्य नु विशः परि वृंक्त सुदानवः ।ऊर्ध्वान्नः कर्त जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛṇa-skandásya ǀ nú ǀ víśaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṅkta ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀūrdhvā́n ǀ naḥ ǀ karta ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Tṛṇskanda's folk; Lift ye us up that we may live.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, liberal benefactors, protect my people, (although I be) as insignificant as grass; lift us up, that we may live.
verses.griffith_verse: O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Tṛṇskanda's folk; Lift ye us up that we may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १३ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः । इन्द्रः। त्रिष्टुप्, ४ विराट् स्थाना, विषमपदा वा।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE praise-song let him sing forth bursting bird-like: sing we that hymn which like heaven's light expandeth,That the milk-giving cows may, unimpeded call to the sacred grass the Gods’ assembly. Let the Bull sing with Bulls whose toil is worship, with a loud roar like some wild beast that hungers.Praised God! the glad priest brings his heart's devotion; the holy youth presents twofold oblation. May the Priest come circling the measured stations, and with him bring the earth's autumnal fruitage.Let the Horse neigh led near, let the Steer bellow: let the Voice go between both worlds as herald, To him we offer welcomest oblations, the pious bring their strength-inspiring praises.May Indra, wondrous in his might, accept them, car-borne and swift to move like the Nāsatyas. Praise thou that Indra who is truly mighty, the car-borne Warrior, Maghavan the Hero;Stronger in war than those who fight against him, borne by strong steeds, who kills enclosing darkness; Him who surpasses heroes in his greatness: the earth and heavens suffice not for his girdles.Indra endues the earth to be his garment, and, God-like, wears the heaven as ’twere a frontlet, Thee, Hero, guardian of the brave in battles, who roamest in the van,—to draw thee hither,Indra, the hosts agree beside the Soma, and joy, for his great actions, in the Chieftain. Libations in the sea to thee are pleasant, when thy divine Floods come to cheer these people.To thee the Cow is sum of all things grateful when with the wish thou seekest men and princes. So may we in this One be well befriended, well aided as it were through praise of chieftains,That Indra still may linger at our worship, as one led swift to work, to hear our praises. Like men in rivalry extolling princes, our Friend be Indra, wielder of the thunder.Like true friends of some city's lord within them held in good rule with sacrifice they help him. For every sacrifice makes Indra stronger, yea, when he goes around angry in spirit;As pleasure at the ford invites the thirsty, as the long way brings him who gains his object. Let us not here contend with Gods, O Indra, for here, O Mighty One, is thine own portion,The Great, whose Friends the bounteous Maruts honour, as with a stream, his song who pours oblations. Addressed to thee is this our praise, O Indra: Lord of Bay Steeds, find us hereby advancement.So mayst thou lead us on, O God, to comfort. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: गायत्साम नभन्यं यथा वेरर्चाम तद्वावृधानं स्वर्वत् ।गावो धेनवो बर्हिष्यदब्धा आ यत्सद्मानं दिव्यं विवासान् ॥
verses.transliteration: gā́yat ǀ sā́ma ǀ nabhanyám ǀ yáthā ǀ véḥ ǀ árcāma ǀ tát ǀ vavṛdhānám ǀ sváḥ-vat ǀgā́vaḥ ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ barhíṣi ǀ ádabdhāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yát ǀ sadmā́nam ǀ divyám ǀ vívāsān ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE praise-song let him sing forth bursting bird-like: sing we that hymn which like heaven's light expandeth, That the milk-giving cows may, unimpeded call to the sacred grass the Gods’ assembly.
verses.wilson_translation: The priests chant the heaven-ascendingsāma, as you know (it), for such (praise) do we venerate as the cause of increase and conferrer of heaven, whence the kine, unimpeded, do honour to the divine (Indra), who is seated on the sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: THE praise-song let him sing forth bursting bird-like: sing we that hymn which like heaven's light expandeth, That the milk-giving cows may, unimpeded call to the sacred grass the Gods’ assembly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्चद्वृषा वृषभिः स्वेदुहव्यैर्मृगो नाश्नो अति यज्जुगुर्यात् ।प्र मंदयुर्मनां गूर्त होता भरते मर्यो मिथुना यजत्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: árcat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ svá-íduhavyaiḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ áśnaḥ ǀ áti ǀ yát ǀ juguryā́t ǀprá ǀ mandayúḥ ǀ manā́m ǀ gūrta ǀ hótā ǀ bhárate ǀ máryaḥ ǀ mithunā́ ǀ yájatraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the Bull sing with Bulls whose toil is worship, with a loud roar like some wild beast that hungers. Praised God! the glad priest brings his heart's devotion; the holy youth presents twofold oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: The showerer (of the oblation, the offerer of the sacrifice, assisted) by (the priests), presenting the oblations which have been provided by himself, adores (Indra), in order that he may hasten (to the rite), as a (thirsty) deer to the water. The mortal invoker (of the gods), O mighty Indra, whilst glorifying them who are desirous of praise, presents a twofold offering (to you).
verses.griffith_verse: Let the Bull sing with Bulls whose toil is worship, with a loud roar like some wild beast that hungers. Praised God! the glad priest brings his heart's devotion; the holy youth presents twofold oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नक्षद्धोता परि सद्म मिता यन्भरद्गर्भमा शरदः पृथिव्याः ।क्रंददश्वो नयमानो रुवद्गौरंतर्दूतो न रोदसी चरद्वाक् ॥
verses.transliteration: nákṣat ǀ hótā ǀ pári ǀ sádma ǀ mitā́ ǀ yán ǀ bhárat ǀ gárbham ǀ ā́ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀkrándat ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ náyamānaḥ ǀ ruvát ǀ gáuḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ná ǀ ródasī íti ǀ carat ǀ vā́k ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Priest come circling the measured stations, and with him bring the earth's autumnal fruitage. Let the Horse neigh led near, let the Steer bellow: let the Voice go between both worlds as herald,
verses.wilson_translation: The invoker (of the gods,Agni), pervades the measured stations (of the altars), and accepts that (oblation), which is the germ of the year of the earth; as a horse neighs when bringing (the offering to Indra), as a bull bellows like a messenger proclaiming (his message) between heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: May the Priest come circling the measured stations, and with him bring the earth's autumnal fruitage. Let the Horse neigh led near, let the Steer bellow: let the Voice go between both worlds as herald,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता कर्माषतरास्मै प्र च्यौत्नानि देवयंतो भरंते ।जुजोषदिंद्रो दस्मवर्चा नासत्येव सुग्म्यो रथेष्ठाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ karma ǀ áṣa-tarā ǀ asmai ǀ prá ǀ cyautnā́ni ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ bharante ǀjújoṣat ǀ índraḥ ǀ dasmá-varcāḥ ǀ nā́satyā-iva ǀ súgmyaḥ ǀ rathe-sthā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him we offer welcomest oblations, the pious bring their strength-inspiring praises. May Indra, wondrous in his might, accept them, car-borne and swift to move like the Nāsatyas.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer to him, (Indra), the most pious (oblations); the worshippers of the gods present to him substantial (adorations); may he, of conspicuous lustre, standing in his car, and light-moving like the Aśvins, be gratified (by our worship).
verses.griffith_verse: To him we offer welcomest oblations, the pious bring their strength-inspiring praises. May Indra, wondrous in his might, accept them, car-borne and swift to move like the Nāsatyas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमु ष्टुहींद्रं यो ह सत्वा यः शूरो मघवा यो रथेष्ठाः ।प्रतीचश्चिद्योधीयान्वृषण्वान्ववव्रुषश्चित्तमसो विहंता ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stuhi ǀ índram ǀ yáḥ ǀ ha ǀ sátvā ǀ yáḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ rathe-sthā́ḥ ǀpratīcáḥ ǀ cit ǀ yódhīyān ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇ-vān ǀ vavavrúṣaḥ ǀ cit ǀ támasaḥ ǀ vi-hantā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise thou that Indra who is truly mighty, the car-borne Warrior, Maghavan the Hero; Stronger in war than those who fight against him, borne by strong steeds, who kills enclosing darkness;
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify that Indrawho is mighty, who is a hero, possessing abundant wealth, standing in his car, a valiant combatant against adversaries, the wilder of the thunderbolt, the dispenser of all-enveloping gloom.
verses.griffith_verse: Praise thou that Indra who is truly mighty, the car-borne Warrior, Maghavan the Hero; Stronger in war than those who fight against him, borne by strong steeds, who kills enclosing darkness;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यदित्था महिना नृभ्यो अस्त्यरं रोदसी कक्ष्ये नास्मै ।सं विव्य इंद्रो वृजनं न भूमा भर्ति स्वधावाँ ओपशमिव द्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ itthā́ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ áram ǀ ródasī íti ǀ kakṣyé íti ǀ ná ǀ asmai ǀsám ǀ vivye ǀ índraḥ ǀ vṛjánam ǀ ná ǀ bhū́ma ǀ bhárti ǀ svadhā́-vān ǀ opaśám-iva ǀ dyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him who surpasses heroes in his greatness: the earth and heavens suffice not for his girdles. Indra endues the earth to be his garment, and, God-like, wears the heaven as ’twere a frontlet,
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth are insufficient for the girth of that Indra, who, with his greatness, rules over the leaders (of sacrifice); as the atmosphere encompasses the earth, so he encompasses (thethree worlds), and, being the master of the rain, he upholds the sky as well as the firmament and the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Him who surpasses heroes in his greatness: the earth and heavens suffice not for his girdles. Indra endues the earth to be his garment, and, God-like, wears the heaven as ’twere a frontlet,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समत्सु त्वा शूर सतामुराणं प्रपथिंतमं परितंसयध्यै ।सजोषस इंद्रं मदे क्षोणीः सूरिं चिद्ये अनुमदंति वाजैः ॥
verses.transliteration: samát-su ǀ tvā ǀ śūra ǀ satā́m ǀ urāṇám ǀ prapathín-tamam ǀ pari-taṃsayádhyai ǀsa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ índram ǀ máde ǀ kṣoṇī́ḥ ǀ sūrím ǀ cit ǀ yé ǀ anu-mádanti ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thee, Hero, guardian of the brave in battles, who roamest in the van,—to draw thee hither, Indra, the hosts agree beside the Soma, and joy, for his great actions, in the Chieftain.
verses.wilson_translation: Those people, who, jointly worshipping Indra, diligently endeavour, O hero, to propitiate you, the invigorator in combats, the guide in the right way; provide, for his gratification, with sacrificial viands.
verses.griffith_verse: Thee, Hero, guardian of the brave in battles, who roamest in the van,—to draw thee hither, Indra, the hosts agree beside the Soma, and joy, for his great actions, in the Chieftain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा हि ते शं सवना समुद्र आपो यत्त आसु मदंति देवीः ।विश्वा ते अनु जोष्या भूद्गौः सूरींश्चिद्यदि धिषा वेषि जनान् ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ śám ǀ sávanā ǀ samudré ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ āsú ǀ mádanti ǀ devī́ḥ ǀvíśvā ǀ te ǀ ánu ǀ jóṣyā ǀ bhūt ǀ gáuḥ ǀ sūrī́n ǀ cit ǀ yádi ǀ dhiṣā́ ǀ véṣi ǀ jánān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Libations in the sea to thee are pleasant, when thy divine Floods come to cheer these people. To thee the Cow is sum of all things grateful when with the wish thou seekest men and princes.
verses.wilson_translation: The libations (offered) to you are, verily, the cause of happiness, since the divine waters (effused) in the firmament for the benefit of mankind afford you satisfaction. All praise,Indra, is acceptable to you, and you reward with understanding those who praise you.
verses.griffith_verse: Libations in the sea to thee are pleasant, when thy divine Floods come to cheer these people. To thee the Cow is sum of all things grateful when with the wish thou seekest men and princes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असाम यथा सुषखाय एन स्वभिष्टयो नरां न शंसैः ।असद्यथा न इंद्रो वंदनेष्ठास्तुरो न कर्म नयमान उक्था ॥
verses.transliteration: ásāma ǀ yáthā ǀ su-sakhā́yaḥ ǀ ena ǀ su-abhiṣṭáyaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsaiḥ ǀásat ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vandane-sthā́ḥ ǀ turáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kárma ǀ náyamānaḥ ǀ ukthā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may we in this One be well befriended, well aided as it were through praise of chieftains, That Indra still may linger at our worship, as one led swift to work, to hear our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be, as it were, your valued friends, O Lord, and obtain our desires, like those (who gain their objects) by the praise of princes. May Indra, propitiated by our eulogies, be brought to the sacrifice by our hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: So may we in this One be well befriended, well aided as it were through praise of chieftains, That Indra still may linger at our worship, as one led swift to work, to hear our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विष्पर्धसो नरां न शंसैरस्माकासदिंद्रो वज्रहस्तः ।मित्रायुवो न पूर्पतिं सुशिष्टौ मध्यायुव उप शिक्षंति यज्ञैः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví-spardhasaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsaiḥ ǀ asmā́ka ǀ asat ǀ índraḥ ǀ vájra-hastaḥ ǀmitra-yúvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pū́ḥ-patim ǀ sú-śiṣṭau ǀ madhya-yúvaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣanti ǀ yajñáiḥ ǁ
