verses.english_translation: Like men in rivalry extolling princes, our Friend be Indra, wielder of the thunder. Like true friends of some city's lord within them held in good rule with sacrifice they help him.
verses.wilson_translation: Emulous in commendation, like (those contending for the favour) of men, may Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, be equally (a friend) to us; like those who, desirous of his friendship, (conciliate) the lord of a city (ruling) with good government, so do our intermediate (representatives) propitiate (Indra) with sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Like men in rivalry extolling princes, our Friend be Indra, wielder of the thunder. Like true friends of some city's lord within them held in good rule with sacrifice they help him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञो हि ष्मेंद्रं कश्चिदृंधञ्जुहुराणश्चिन्मनसा परियन् ।तीर्थे नाच्छा तातृषाणमोको दीर्घो न सिध्रमा कृणोत्यध्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñáḥ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ índram ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ ṛndhán ǀ juhurāṇáḥ ǀ cit ǀ mánasā ǀ pari-yán ǀtīrthé ǀ ná ǀ áccha ǀ tatṛṣāṇám ǀ ókaḥ ǀ dīrgháḥ ǀ ná ǀ sidhrám ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ ádhvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: For every sacrifice makes Indra stronger, yea, when he goes around angry in spirit; As pleasure at the ford invites the thirsty, as the long way brings him who gains his object.
verses.wilson_translation: One man propitiates Indra, augmenting (his vigour) by sacrifice; another, who is insincere, worships (him), with mind averted, (to worldly thoughts); (to the first he is) like a lake to a thirsty (pilgrim) near a sacred spot; (to the other) like a long road, which retards the end (of the journey).
verses.griffith_verse: For every sacrifice makes Indra stronger, yea, when he goes around angry in spirit; As pleasure at the ford invites the thirsty, as the long way brings him who gains his object.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मो षू ण इंद्रात्र पृत्सु देवैरस्ति हि ष्मा ते शुष्मिन्नवयाः ।महश्चिद्यस्य मीळ्हुषो यव्या हविष्मतो मरुतो वंदते गीः ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ átra ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ásti ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ te ǀ śuṣmin ǀ ava-yā́ḥ ǀmaháḥ ǀ cit ǀ yásya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀ yavyā́ ǀ havíṣmataḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ vándate ǀ gī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us not here contend with Gods, O Indra, for here, O Mighty One, is thine own portion, The Great, whose Friends the bounteous Maruts honour, as with a stream, his song who pours oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, associated with the Marutsin battles (with the clouds), abandon us not; for a share of the offering is set apart, mighty one, for you, for whom, the shedder of rain and accepter of oblations, the worship is offered with oblations, whilst the hymn glorifies the Marutṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Let us not here contend with Gods, O Indra, for here, O Mighty One, is thine own portion, The Great, whose Friends the bounteous Maruts honour, as with a stream, his song who pours oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष स्तोम इंद्र तुभ्यमस्मे एतेन गातुं हरिवो विदो नः ।आ नो ववृत्याः सुविताय देव विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ asmé íti ǀ eténa ǀ gātúm ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ vidaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vavṛtyāḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ deva ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Addressed to thee is this our praise, O Indra: Lord of Bay Steeds, find us hereby advancement. So mayst thou lead us on, O God, to comfort. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: This hymn,Indra, is addressed to you. Lord of steeds, learn by it the way to our sacrifice, and come hither for our good, that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Addressed to thee is this our praise, O Indra: Lord of Bay Steeds, find us hereby advancement. So mayst thou lead us on, O God, to comfort. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU art the King of all the Gods, O Indra: protect the men, O Asura, preserve us.Thou Lord of Heroes, Maghavan, our saver, art faithful, very rich, the victory-giver. Indra, thou humbledst tribes that spake with insult by breaking down seven autumn forts, their refuge.Thou stirredst, Blameless! billowy floods, and gavest his foe a prey to youthful Purukutsa. With whom thou drivest troops whose lords are heroes, and bringest daylight now, much worshipped Indra,With them guard lion-like wasting active Agni to dwell in our tilled fields and in our homestead. They through the greatness of thy spear, O Indra, shall, to thy praise, rest in this earthly station.To loose the floods, to seek, for kine, the battle, his Bays he mounted boldly seized the booty. Indra, bear Kutsa, him in whom thou joyest: the dark-red horses of the Wind are docile.Let the Sun roll his chariot wheel anear us, and let the Thunderer go to meet the foemen. Thou Indra, Lord of Bays, made strong by impulse, hast slain the vexers of thy friends, who give not.They who beheld the Friend beside the living were cast aside by thee as they rode onward. Indra, the bard sang forth in inspiration: thou madest earth a covering for the Dāsa.Maghavan made the three that gleam with moisture, and to his home brought Kuyavāc to slay him. These thine old deeds new bards have sung, O Indra. Thou conqueredst, boundest many tribes for ever.Like castles thou hast crushed the godless races, and bowed the godless scorner's deadly weapon. A Stormer thou hast made the stormy waters flow down, O Indra, like the running rivers.When o’er the flood thou broughtest them, O Hero, thou keptest Turvaśa and Yadu safely. Indra, mayst thou be ours in all occasions, protector of the men, most gentle-hearted,Giving us victory over all our rivals. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं राजेंद्र ये च देवा रक्षा नॄन्पाह्यसुर त्वमस्मान् ।त्वं सत्पतिर्मघवा नस्तरुत्रस्त्वं सत्यो वसवानः सहोदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ rā́jā ǀ indra ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rákṣa ǀ nṝ́n ǀ pāhí ǀ asura ǀ tvám ǀ asmā́n ǀtvám ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ naḥ ǀ tárutraḥ ǀ tvám ǀ satyáḥ ǀ vásavānaḥ ǀ sahaḥ-dā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOU art the King of all the Gods, O Indra: protect the men, O Asura, preserve us. Thou Lord of Heroes, Maghavan, our saver, art faithful, very rich, the victory-giver.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are king; they who are gods (are subject) to you; therefore, scatterer (of foes), do you protect and cherish us men; you are the protector of the good, the possessor of wealth, the extricator of us (from sin); you are true, the invester (of all with your lustre) the giver of strength.
verses.griffith_verse: THOU art the King of all the Gods, O Indra: protect the men, O Asura, preserve us. Thou Lord of Heroes, Maghavan, our saver, art faithful, very rich, the victory-giver.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दनो विश इंद्र मृध्रवाचः सप्त यत्पुरः शर्म शारदीर्��र्त् ।ऋणोरपो अनवद्यार्णा यूने वृत्रं पुरुकुत्साय रंधीः ॥
verses.transliteration: dánaḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ indra ǀ mṛdhrá-vācaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yát ǀ púraḥ ǀ śárma ǀ śā́radīḥ ǀ dárt ǀṛṇóḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ anavadya ǀ árṇāḥ ǀ yū́ne ǀ vṛtrám ǀ puru-kútsāya ǀ randhīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, thou humbledst tribes that spake with insult by breaking down seven autumn forts, their refuge. Thou stirredst, Blameless! billowy floods, and gavest his foe a prey to youthful Purukutsa.
verses.wilson_translation: You have humbled the people, suing for pardon when you have destroyed their seven new cities; you the irrproachable have dispersed the flowing waters; you have destroyed Vṛtrafor the sake of the youthful Purukutsa.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, thou humbledst tribes that spake with insult by breaking down seven autumn forts, their refuge. Thou stirredst, Blameless! billowy floods, and gavest his foe a prey to youthful Purukutsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजा वृत इंद्र शूरपत्नीर्द्यां च येभिः पुरुहूत नूनं ।रक्षो अग्निमशुषं तूर्वयाणं सिंहो न दमे अपांसि वस्तोः ॥
verses.transliteration: ája ǀ vṛ́taḥ ǀ indra ǀ śū́ra-patnīḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ca ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ nūnám ǀrákṣo íti ǀ agním ǀ aśúṣam ǀ tū́rvayāṇam ǀ siṃháḥ ǀ ná ǀ dáme ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ vástoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With whom thou drivest troops whose lords are heroes, and bringest daylight now, much worshipped Indra, With them guard lion-like wasting active Agni to dwell in our tilled fields and in our homestead.
verses.wilson_translation: Go the cities inhabited by therākṣasas, and thence to heaven (attended), receiver of many sacrifices by those who (attend you). Defend, like a lion, the untamed, quick-moving Agni, that he may abide in his dwelling, fulfilling his functions.
verses.griffith_verse: With whom thou drivest troops whose lords are heroes, and bringest daylight now, much worshipped Indra, With them guard lion-like wasting active Agni to dwell in our tilled fields and in our homestead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शेषन्नु त इंद्र सस्मिन्योनौ प्रशस्तये पवीरवस्य मह्ना ।सृजदर्णांस्यव यद्युधा गास्तिष्ठद्धरी धृषता मृष्ट वाजान् ॥
verses.transliteration: śéṣan ǀ nú ǀ té ǀ indra ǀ sásmin ǀ yónau ǀ prá-śastaye ǀ pávīravasya ǀ mahnā́ ǀsṛját ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ áva ǀ yát ǀ yudhā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ tíṣṭhat ǀ hárī íti ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ mṛṣṭa ǀ vā́jān ǁ
verses.english_translation: They through the greatness of thy spear, O Indra, shall, to thy praise, rest in this earthly station. To loose the floods, to seek, for kine, the battle, his Bays he mounted boldly seized the booty.
verses.wilson_translation: Let (your foes,Indra), humbled by the might of your thunderbolt rest in their own station, for your glory; when you move, (armed) with your weapons, you send down the waters; arresting your horses, increase, by your power, (the abundance of) food.
verses.griffith_verse: They through the greatness of thy spear, O Indra, shall, to thy praise, rest in this earthly station. To loose the floods, to seek, for kine, the battle, his Bays he mounted boldly seized the booty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वह कुत्समिंद्र यस्मिञ्चाकन्त्स्यूमन्यू ऋज्रा वातस्याश्वा ।प्र सूरश्चक्रं वृहतादभीकेऽभि स्पृधो यासिषद्वज्रबाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: váha ǀ kútsam ǀ indra ǀ yásmin ǀ cākán ǀ syūmanyū́ íti ǀ ṛjrā́ ǀ vā́tasya ǀ áśvā ǀprá ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ vṛhatāt ǀ abhī́ke ǀ abhí ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ yāsiṣat ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, bear Kutsa, him in whom thou joyest: the dark-red horses of the Wind are docile. Let the Sun roll his chariot wheel anear us, and let the Thunderer go to meet the foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: Bear,Indra, with your obedient horses, as swift as the wind, (the sage)Kutsa, to that ceremony (to which) you desire (to convey him); let the sun bring near the wheel of his chariot, and let the thunder-armed advance against his opponents.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, bear Kutsa, him in whom thou joyest: the dark-red horses of the Wind are docile. Let the Sun roll his chariot wheel anear us, and let the Thunderer go to meet the foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जघन्वाँ इंद्र मित्रेरूञ्चोदप्रवृद्धो हरिवो अदाशून् ।प्र ये पश्यन्नर्यमणं सचायोस्त्वया शूर्ता वहमाना अपत्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: jaghanvā́n ǀ indra ǀ mitrérūn ǀ codá-pravṛddhaḥ ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ ádāśūn ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ páśyan ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ śūrtā́ḥ ǀ váhamānāḥ ǀ ápatyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou Indra, Lord of Bays, made strong by impulse, hast slain the vexers of thy friends, who give not. They who beheld the Friend beside the living were cast aside by thee as they rode onward.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, lord of steeds, invigorated by our animating praise, you have slain those who make you no offerings and disturb your worshippers; but they who look upon you as (their) protector, and are associated for (the presentation of sacrificial) food, obtain from the posterity.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou Indra, Lord of Bays, made strong by impulse, hast slain the vexers of thy friends, who give not. They who beheld the Friend beside the living were cast aside by thee as they rode onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रपत्कविरिंद्रार्कसातौ क्षां दासायोपबर्हणीं कः ।करत्तिस्रो मघवा दानुचित्रा नि दुर्योणे कुयवाचं मृधि श्रेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: rápat ǀ kavíḥ ǀ indra ǀ arká-sātau ǀ kṣā́m ǀ dāsā́ya ǀ upa-bárhaṇīm ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀkárat ǀ tisráḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ dā́nu-citrāḥ ǀ ní ǀ duryoṇé ǀ kúyavācam ǀ mṛdhí ǀ śret ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the bard sang forth in inspiration: thou madest earth a covering for the Dāsa. Maghavan made the three that gleam with moisture, and to his home brought Kuyavāc to slay him.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage praises you,Indra, for the grant of desirable (food), since you have made the earth the bed of theasura;Maghavanhas made the three (regions) marvellous by his gifts, and has destroyed for (the prince) Duryoṇi (the asura), Kuyavāca, in combat.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, the bard sang forth in inspiration: thou madest earth a covering for the Dāsa. Maghavan made the three that gleam with moisture, and to his home brought Kuyavāc to slay him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सना ता त इंद्र नव्या आगुः सहो नभोऽविरणाय पूर्वीः ।भिनत्पुरो न भिदो अदेवीर्ननमो वधरदेवस्य पीयोः ॥
verses.transliteration: sánā ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ návyāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aguḥ ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ nábhaḥ ǀ ávi-raṇāya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀbhinát ǀ púraḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhídaḥ ǀ ádevīḥ ǀ nanámaḥ ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ ádevasya ǀ pīyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These thine old deeds new bards have sung, O Indra. Thou conqueredst, boundest many tribes for ever. Like castles thou hast crushed the godless races, and bowed the godless scorner's deadly weapon.
verses.wilson_translation: The sages have celebrated your everlasting (as well as your) recent (exploits, in achieving which) you have endured many injuries in putting an end to war; verily, you have demolished hostile and undivine cities; you have bowed down the thunderbolt of the undivineasura.
verses.griffith_verse: These thine old deeds new bards have sung, O Indra. Thou conqueredst, boundest many tribes for ever. Like castles thou hast crushed the godless races, and bowed the godless scorner's deadly weapon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं धुनिरिंद्र धुनिमतीर्ऋणोरपः सीरा न स्रवंतीः ।प्र यत्समुद्रमति शूर पर्षि पारया तुर्वशं यदुं स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ dhúniḥ ǀ indra ǀ dhúni-matīḥ ǀ ṛṇóḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sīrā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ srávantīḥ ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ samudrám ǀ áti ǀ śūra ǀ párṣi ǀ pāráya ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: A Stormer thou hast made the stormy waters flow down, O Indra, like the running rivers. When o’er the flood thou broughtest them, O Hero, thou keptest Turvaśa and Yadu safely.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are the terrifier (of your foes); you have made the trembling waters overspread (the earth) like flowing rivers; but, hero, when you fill the ocean you have protected in their well-being Turvaśaand Yadu.
verses.griffith_verse: A Stormer thou hast made the stormy waters flow down, O Indra, like the running rivers. When o’er the flood thou broughtest them, O Hero, thou keptest Turvaśa and Yadu safely.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमस्माकमिंद्र विश्वध स्या अवृकतमो नरां नृपाता ।स नो विश्वासां स्पृधां सहोदा विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ indra ǀ viśvádha ǀ syāḥ ǀ avṛká-tamaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ nṛ-pātā́ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāsām ǀ spṛdhā́m ǀ sahaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, mayst thou be ours in all occasions, protector of the men, most gentle-hearted, Giving us victory over all our rivals. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Be you,Indra, at all times our especial defender; the preserver of our people, the bestower of strength upon all these our emulous (followers); that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, mayst thou be ours in all occasions, protector of the men, most gentle-hearted, Giving us victory over all our rivals. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ६ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः । इन्द्रः। १ स्कंधोग्रीवी बृहती, २-५ अनुष्टुप्, ६ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GLAD thee: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of Bay Steeds, as ’twere the bowl's enlivening mead.For thee the Strong there is strong drink, mighty, omnipotent to win. Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee,Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight, Thou, Hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man.Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the lawless Dasyu, Conqueror! Empowered by thine own might, O Sage, thou stolest Sūrya's chariot wheel.Thou barest Kutsa with the steeds of Wind to Śuṣṇa as his death. Most mighty is thy rapturous joy, most splendid is thine active power,Wherewith, foe-slaying, sending bliss, thou art supreme in gaining steeds. As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, as water to the thirsty,So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: मत्स्यपायि ते महः पात्रस्येव हरिवो मत्सरो मदः ।वृषा ते वृष्ण इंदुर्वाजी सहस्रसातमः ॥
verses.transliteration: mátsi ǀ ápāyi ǀ te ǀ máhaḥ ǀ pā́trasya-iva ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ matsaráḥ ǀ mádaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ te ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ índuḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ sahasra-sā́tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: GLAD thee: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of Bay Steeds, as ’twere the bowl's enlivening mead. For thee the Strong there is strong drink, mighty, omnipotent to win.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of steeds, you are exhilarated when the sacred (Soma) has been imbibed by you as by its (appropriate) vessel; for to you, showerer (of benefits), it is exhilarating, inebriating, invigorating, the yielder of delight, (satisfying as) food, and the giver of a thousand (plural asures).
verses.griffith_verse: GLAD thee: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of Bay Steeds, as ’twere the bowl's enlivening mead. For thee the Strong there is strong drink, mighty, omnipotent to win.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नस्ते गंतु मत्सरो वृषा मदो वरेण्यः ।सहावाँ इंद्र सानसिः पृतनाषाळमर्त्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ te ǀ gantu ǀ matsaráḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ mádaḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀsahá-vān ǀ indra ǀ sānasíḥ ǀ pṛtanāṣā́ṭ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee, Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight,
verses.wilson_translation: May oursomalibation reach you, (for it is) exhilarating, invigorating, inebriating, most precious; it is companionable,Indra, enjoyable, the over-thrower of hosts, immortal.
verses.griffith_verse: Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee, Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि शूरः सनिता चोदयो मनुषो रथं ।सहावान्दस्युमव्रतमोषः पात्रं न शोचिषा ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ sánitā ǀ codáyaḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ rátham ǀsahá-vān ǀ dásyum ǀ avratám ǀ óṣaḥ ǀ pā́tram ǀ ná ǀ śocíṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man. Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the lawless Dasyu, Conqueror!
verses.wilson_translation: You are a hero, a benefactor, accelerate the vehicle of man (that bears him to heaven); consume, mightyone, the irreligious Dasyu, as a (woode) vessel is burnt by fire.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man. Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the lawless Dasyu, Conqueror!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मुषाय सूर्यं कवे चक्रमीशान ओजसा ।वह शुष्णाय वधं कुत्सं वातस्याश्वैः ॥
verses.transliteration: muṣāyá ǀ sū́ryam ǀ kave ǀ cakrám ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ ójasā ǀváha ǀ śúṣṇāya ǀ vadhám ǀ kútsam ǀ vā́tasya ǀ áśvaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Empowered by thine own might, O Sage, thou stolest Sūrya's chariot wheel. Thou barest Kutsa with the steeds of Wind to Śuṣṇa as his death.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Indra, who are the lord, you have carried off by your strength one wheel of (the chariot of) the sun. Take up your bolt for the death ofŚuṣṇa, and proceed with your horses, swift as the wind, to Kutsa.
verses.griffith_verse: Empowered by thine own might, O Sage, thou stolest Sūrya's chariot wheel. Thou barest Kutsa with the steeds of Wind to Śuṣṇa as his death.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुष्मिंतमो हि ते मदो द्युम्निंतम उत क्रतुः ।वृत्रघ्ना वरिवोविदा मंसीष्ठा अश्वसातमः ॥
verses.transliteration: śuṣmín-tamaḥ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ dyumnín-tamaḥ ǀ utá ǀ krátuḥ ǀvṛtra-ghnā́ ǀ varivaḥ-vídā ǀ maṃsīṣṭhā́ḥ ǀ aśva-sā́tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most mighty is thy rapturous joy, most splendid is thine active power, Wherewith, foe-slaying, sending bliss, thou art supreme in gaining steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Your inebriety is most intense; nevertheless, your acts (for our good) are most beneficent. You desire, bountiful giver of horses, that (both your inebriety and your beneficence should be the means of) destroying enemies and distributing riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Most mighty is thy rapturous joy, most splendid is thine active power, Wherewith, foe-slaying, sending bliss, thou art supreme in gaining steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा पूर्वेभ्यो जरितृभ्य इंद्र मय इवापो न तृष्यते बभूथ ।तामनु त्वा निविदं जोहवीमि विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ pū́rvebhyaḥ ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ máyaḥ-iva ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ tṛ́ṣyate ǀ babhū́tha ǀtā́m ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǀ ni-vídam ǀ johavīmi ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, as water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch Indra, as you have been the (giver of) happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, as water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . CHEER thee with draughts to win us bliss: Soma, pierce Indra in thy strength.Thou stormest trembling in thy rage, and findest not a foeman nigh. Make our songs penetrate to him who is the Only One of men;For whom the sacred food is spread, as the steer ploughs the barley in. Within whose hands deposited all the Five Peoples’ treasures rest.Mark thou the man who injures us and kill him like the heavenly bolt. Slay everyone who pours no gift, who, hard to reach, delights thee not.Bestow on us what wealth he hath: this even the worshipper awaits. Thou helpest him the doubly strong whose hymns were sung unceasingly.When Indra fought, O Soma, thou helpest the mighty in the fray. As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, like water to the thirsty,So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: मत्सि नो वस्यइष्टय इंद्रमिंदो वृषा विश ।ऋघायमाण इन्वसि शत्रुमंति न विंदसि ॥
verses.transliteration: mátsi ǀ naḥ ǀ vásyaḥ-iṣṭaye ǀ índram ǀ indo íti ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ā́ ǀ viśa ǀṛghāyámāṇaḥ ǀ invasi ǀ śátrum ǀ ánti ǀ ná ǀ vindasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: CHEER thee with draughts to win us bliss: Soma, pierce Indra in thy strength. Thou stormest trembling in thy rage, and findest not a foeman nigh.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, exhilarate Indra(at the sacrifice we offer), for the sake of obtaining wealth; pervade him, showerer (ofbenefits), for when imbibed you are the annihilator (of enemies), and suffer not a foe to be nigh.
verses.griffith_verse: CHEER thee with draughts to win us bliss: Soma, pierce Indra in thy strength. Thou stormest trembling in thy rage, and findest not a foeman nigh.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्ना वेशया गिरो य एकश्चर्षणीनां ।अनु स्वधा यमुप्यते यवं न चर्कृषद्वृषा ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ veśaya ǀ gíraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀánu ǀ svadhā́ ǀ yám ǀ upyáte ǀ yávam ǀ ná ǀ cárkṛṣat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make our songs penetrate to him who is the Only One of men; For whom the sacred food is spread, as the steer ploughs the barley in.
verses.wilson_translation: Pervade with our praise him who is the sole sustainer of men, to whom the oblation is presented and who, the showerer (of benefits), causes (every desire) to bud like barley.
verses.griffith_verse: Make our songs penetrate to him who is the Only One of men; For whom the sacred food is spread, as the steer ploughs the barley in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोः पंच क्षितीनां वसु ।स्पाशयस्व यो अस्मध्रुग्दिव्येवाशनिर्जहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ víśvāni ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ páñca ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ vásu ǀspāśáyasva ǀ yáḥ ǀ asma-dhrúk ǀ divyā́-iva ǀ aśániḥ ǀ jahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Within whose hands deposited all the Five Peoples’ treasures rest. Mark thou the man who injures us and kill him like the heavenly bolt.
verses.wilson_translation: In whosehands are all the treasures (that are desired by) the five classes of beings; destroy,Indra, him who oppresses us; slay him, (as if you were yourself) the heavenly thunderbolt.
verses.griffith_verse: Within whose hands deposited all the Five Peoples’ treasures rest. Mark thou the man who injures us and kill him like the heavenly bolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असुन्वंतं समं जहि दूणाशं यो न ते मयः ।अस्मभ्यमस्य वेदनं दद्धि सूरिश्चिदोहते ॥
verses.transliteration: ásunvantam ǀ samam ǀ jahi ǀ duḥ-náśam ǀ yáḥ ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ máyaḥ ǀasmábhyam ǀ asya ǀ védanam ǀ daddhí ǀ sūríḥ ǀ cit ǀ ohate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slay everyone who pours no gift, who, hard to reach, delights thee not. Bestow on us what wealth he hath: this even the worshipper awaits.
verses.wilson_translation: Slay every one who offers not libations, however difficult to be destroyed; slay every one who is no delight to you; bestow upon us his wealth, for the pious (worshipper) deserves it.
verses.griffith_verse: Slay everyone who pours no gift, who, hard to reach, delights thee not. Bestow on us what wealth he hath: this even the worshipper awaits.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आवो यस्य द्विबर्हसोऽर्केषु सानुषगसत् ।आजाविंद्रस्येंदो प्रावो वाजेषु वाजिनं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́vaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ dvi-bárhasaḥ ǀ arkéṣu ǀ sānuṣák ǀ ásat ǀājáu ǀ índrasya ǀ indo íti ǀ prá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ vājínam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou helpest him the doubly strong whose hymns were sung unceasingly. When Indra fought, O Soma, thou helpest the mighty in the fray.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, you protect him in whose prayers, doubly devout, there is the combination (of praise and oblation); protect, especially,Indrain war; protect the vigorous Indra in battles.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou helpest him the doubly strong whose hymns were sung unceasingly. When Indra fought, O Soma, thou helpest the mighty in the fray.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा पूर्वेभ्यो जरितृभ्य इंद्र मय इवापो न तृष्यते बभूथ ।तामनु त्वा निविदं जोहवीमि विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ pū́rvebhyaḥ ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ máyaḥ-iva ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ tṛ́ṣyate ǀ babhū́tha ǀtā́m ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǀ ni-vídam ǀ johavīmi ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, like water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch Indra, as you have been the giver of happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: As thou, O Indra, to the ancient singers wast ever joy, like water to the thirsty, So unto thee I sing this invocation. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Bull of men, who cherishes all people, King of the Races, Indra, called of many,Fame-loving, praised, hither to me with succour turn having yoked both vigorous Bay Horses! Thy mighty Stallions, yoked by prayer, O Indra, thy. Coursers to thy mighty chariot harnessed,—Ascend thou these, and borne by them come hither: with Soma juice outpoured, Indra, we call thee. Ascend thy mighty car: the mighty Soma is poured for thee and sweets are sprinkled round us.Come down to us-ward, Bull of human races, come, having harnessed them, with strong Bay Horses. Here is God-reaching sacrifice, here the victim; here, Indra, are the prayers, here is the Soma.Strewn is the sacred grass: come hither, Śakra; seat thee and drink: unyoke thy two Bay Coursers. Come to us, Indra, come thou highly lauded to the devotions of the singer Māna.Singing, may we find early through thy succour, may we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: आ चर्षणिप्रा वृषभो जनानां राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इंद्रः ।स्तुतः श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग्युक्त्वा हरी वृषणा याह्यर्वाङ् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ carṣaṇi-prā́ḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ rā́jā ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀstutáḥ ǀ śravasyán ǀ ávasā ǀ úpa ǀ madrík ǀ yuktvā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Bull of men, who cherishes all people, King of the Races, Indra, called of many, Fame-loving, praised, hither to me with succour turn having yoked both vigorous Bay Horses!
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, who is the cherisher of men, the benefactor of mankind,t he lord of men, the adored of many, (come to us), Indra, who are praised (by us), and are desirous of the oblation, harness your vigorous steeds, and come down to me for (my preservation).
verses.griffith_verse: THE Bull of men, who cherishes all people, King of the Races, Indra, called of many, Fame-loving, praised, hither to me with succour turn having yoked both vigorous Bay Horses!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये ते वृषणो वृषभास इंद्र ब्रह्मयुजो वृषरथासो अत्याः ।ताँ आ तिष्ठ तेभिरा याह्यर्वाङ् हवामहे त्वा सुत इंद्र सोमे ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ te ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vṛṣabhā́saḥ ǀ indra ǀ brahma-yújaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-rathāsaḥ ǀ átyāḥ ǀtā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ hávāmahe ǀ tvā ǀ suté ǀ indra ǀ sóme ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy mighty Stallions, yoked by prayer, O Indra, thy. Coursers to thy mighty chariot harnessed,— Ascend thou these, and borne by them come hither: with Soma juice outpoured, Indra, we call thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Mount,Indra, your steeds, who are young and vigorous, tractable to prayer, and harnessed to a bounty-shedding car; come down with them to us. We invoke you, Indra, the libation being poured out.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy mighty Stallions, yoked by prayer, O Indra, thy. Coursers to thy mighty chariot harnessed,— Ascend thou these, and borne by them come hither: with Soma juice outpoured, Indra, we call thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तिष्ठ रथं वृषणं वृषा ते सुतः सोमः परिषिक्ता मधूनि ।युक्त्वा वृषभ्यां वृषभ क्षितीनां हरिभ्यां याहि प्रवतोप मद्रिक् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ rátham ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ te ǀ sutáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ pári-siktā ǀ mádhūni ǀyuktvā́ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhyām ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ yāhi ǀ pra-vátā ǀ úpa ǀ madrík ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ascend thy mighty car: the mighty Soma is poured for thee and sweets are sprinkled round us. Come down to us-ward, Bull of human races, come, having harnessed them, with strong Bay Horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend your bounty-shedding car, for you the Soma, the showerer of benefits, is effused, the sweet libations are prepared. Bounty-shedding Indra, having harnessed them, come with your vigorous steeds for (the good of) mankind; come with your rapid (car) to my presence.
verses.griffith_verse: Ascend thy mighty car: the mighty Soma is poured for thee and sweets are sprinkled round us. Come down to us-ward, Bull of human races, come, having harnessed them, with strong Bay Horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं यज्ञो देवया अयं मियेध इमा ब्रह्माण्ययमिंद्र सोमः ।स्तीर्णं बर्हिरा तु शक्र प्र याहि पिबा निषद्य वि मुचा हरी इह ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ deva-yā́ḥ ǀ ayám ǀ miyédhaḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ ayám ǀ indra ǀ sómaḥ ǀstīrṇám ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tú ǀ śakra ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ píba ǀ ni-sádya ǀ ví ǀ muca ǀ hárī íti ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here is God-reaching sacrifice, here the victim; here, Indra, are the prayers, here is the Soma. Strewn is the sacred grass: come hither, Śakra; seat thee and drink: unyoke thy two Bay Coursers.
verses.wilson_translation: This is the sacrifice offered to the gods; this is the offering of the victim; these are the prayers; this,Indra, is the Soma; the sacred grass is ready strewn; come, therefore, Indra, quickly, sit down, drink (the libation); here let loose your steeds.
verses.griffith_verse: Here is God-reaching sacrifice, here the victim; here, Indra, are the prayers, here is the Soma. Strewn is the sacred grass: come hither, Śakra; seat thee and drink: unyoke thy two Bay Coursers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओ सुष्टुत इंद्र याह्यर्वाङुप ब्रह्माणि मान्यस्य कारोः ।विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गृणंतो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ó íti ǀ sú-stutaḥ ǀ indra ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ úpa ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀvidyā́ma ǀ vástoḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us, Indra, come thou highly lauded to the devotions of the singer Māna. Singing, may we find early through thy succour, may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified by us,Indra, come to (our) presence to accept the prayers of the venerable offerer (of the oblation); so that we may ever enjoy prosperity through your protection, and thence obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Come to us, Indra, come thou highly lauded to the devotions of the singer Māna. Singing, may we find early through thy succour, may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IF, Indra, thou hast given that gracious hearing where with thou helpest those who sang thy praises.Blast not the wish that would exalt us may I gain all from thee, and pay all man's devotions. Let not the Sovran Indra disappoint us in what shall bring both Sisters to our dwelling.To him have run the quickly flowing waters. May Indra come to us with life and friendship. Victorious with the men, Hero in battles, Indra, who hears the singer's supplication,Will bring his car nigh to the man who offers, if he himself upholds the songs that praise him. Yea, Indra, with the men, through love of glory consumes the sacred food which friends have offered.The ever-strengthening song of him who worships is sung in fight amid the clash of voices. Aided by thee, O Maghavan, O Indra, may we subdue our foes who count them mighty.Be our protector, strengthen and increase us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: यद्ध स्या त इंद्र श्रुष्टिरस्ति यया बभूथ जरितृभ्य ऊती ।मा नः कामं महयंतमा धग्विश्वा ते अश्यां पर्याप आयोः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ha ǀ syā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ śruṣṭíḥ ǀ ásti ǀ yáyā ǀ babhū́tha ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ maháyantam ǀ ā́ ǀ dhak ǀ víśvā ǀ te ǀ aśyām ǀ pári ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: IF, Indra, thou hast given that gracious hearing where with thou helpest those who sang thy praises. Blast not the wish that would exalt us may I gain all from thee, and pay all man's devotions.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch,Indra, as the praise by which you are (induced to bestow) protection on your adorers is heard (by all), therefore disappoint not the desire (that would raise us) to greatness; may I obtain, through your (favour), all things that are obtainable by man.
verses.griffith_verse: IF, Indra, thou hast given that gracious hearing where with thou helpest those who sang thy praises. Blast not the wish that would exalt us may I gain all from thee, and pay all man's devotions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न घा राजेंद्र आ दभन्नो या नु स्वसारा कृणवंत योनौ ।आपश्चिदस्मै सुतुका अवेषन्गमन्न इंद्रः सख्या वयश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ gha ǀ rā́jā ǀ índraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dabhat ǀ naḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ nú ǀ svásārā ǀ kṛṇávanta ǀ yónau ǀā́paḥ ǀ cit ǀ asmai ǀ su-túkāḥ ǀ aveṣan ǀ gámat ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the Sovran Indra disappoint us in what shall bring both Sisters to our dwelling. To him have run the quickly flowing waters. May Indra come to us with life and friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the royal Indrafrustrate those our actions, which the sisters, (Day and Night), are directing to their object. May these invigorating offerings propitiate hi, so that he may bestow upon us friendly (regard), and (abundant) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not the Sovran Indra disappoint us in what shall bring both Sisters to our dwelling. To him have run the quickly flowing waters. May Indra come to us with life and friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जेता नृभिरिंद्रः पृत्सु शूरः श्रोता हवं नाधमानस्य कारोः ।प्रभर्ता रथं दाशुष उपाक उद्यंता गिरो यदि च त्मना भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: jétā ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ śrótā ǀ hávam ǀ nā́dhamānasya ǀ kāróḥ ǀprá-bhartā ǀ rátham ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ upāké ǀ út-yantā ǀ gíraḥ ǀ yádi ǀ ca ǀ tmánā ǀ bhū́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: Victorious with the men, Hero in battles, Indra, who hears the singer's supplication, Will bring his car nigh to the man who offers, if he himself upholds the songs that praise him.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the hero, the victor in battles, along with the leaders (of his hosts, the Maruts), will hear the invocation of his supplicating worshipper, and when disposed to accept his praises, will, of his own accord, drive his chariot close to the donor (of the oblation).
verses.griffith_verse: Victorious with the men, Hero in battles, Indra, who hears the singer's supplication, Will bring his car nigh to the man who offers, if he himself upholds the songs that praise him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा नृभिरिंद्रः सुश्रवस्या प्रखादः पृक्षो अभि मित्रिणो भूत् ।समर्य इषः स्तवते विवाचि सत्राकरो यजमानस्य शंसः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-śravasyā́ ǀ pra-khādáḥ ǀ pṛkṣáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ mitríṇaḥ ǀ bhūt ǀsa-maryé ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ stavate ǀ ví-vāci ǀ satrā-karáḥ ǀ yájamānasya ǀ śáṃsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, Indra, with the men, through love of glory consumes the sacred food which friends have offered. The ever-strengthening song of him who worships is sung in fight amid the clash of voices.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily,Indrathrough desire of (sacrificial) food, is the devourer (of that which is presented) by (his) worshippers, and overcomes (the adversaries) of his friend; in the many-voiced assembly (of men), Indra, the faithful (performer of his promise), commending (the piety) of his worshipper, approves of the (offered) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, Indra, with the men, through love of glory consumes the sacred food which friends have offered. The ever-strengthening song of him who worships is sung in fight amid the clash of voices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वया वयं मघवन्निंद्र शत्रूनभि ष्याम महतो मन्यमानान् ।त्वं त्राता त्वमु नो वृधे भूर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tváyā ǀ vayám ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ śátrūn ǀ abhí ǀ syāma ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ mányamānān ǀtvám ǀ trātā́ ǀ tvám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǀ bhūḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aided by thee, O Maghavan, O Indra, may we subdue our foes who count them mighty. Be our protector, strengthen and increase us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: By you, opulent Indra, may we overcome our mighty and formidable enemies; you are our protector; may you be propitious to our prosperity, that we may thence obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Aided by thee, O Maghavan, O Indra, may we subdue our foes who count them mighty. Be our protector, strengthen and increase us. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIX. Rati.
hymns.anukramani: (६) १-२ लोपामुद्रा, ३-४ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः, ५-६ अगस्त्यशिष्यो ब्रह्मचारी। रतिः। त्रिष्टुप्, ५ बृहती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: Through many autumns have I toiled and laboured, at night and morn, through age-inducing dawnings.Old age impairs the beauty of our bodies. Let husbands still come near unto their spouses.For even the men aforetime, law-fulfillers, who with the Gods declared eternal statutes,—They have decided, but have not accomplished: so now let Wives come near unto their husbands.Non inutilis est labor cui Dii favent: nos omnes aemulos et aemulas vincamus.Superemus in hac centum artium pugna in qua duas partes convenientes utrinque commovemus.Cupido me cepit illius tauri [viri] qui me despicit, utrum hinc utrum illinc ab aliqua parte nata sit.Lopamudra taurum [maritum suum] ad se detrahit: insipiens illa sapientem anhelantem absorbet.This Soma I address that is most near us, that which hath been imbibed within the spirit,To pardon any sins we have committed. Verily mortal man is full of longings.Agastya thus, toiling with strong endeavour, wishing for children, progeny and power,Cherished—a sage of mighty strength—both classes, and with the Gods obtained his prayer's fulfilment.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वीरहं शरदः शश्रमाणा दोषा वस्तोरुषसो जरयंतीः ।मिनाति श्रियं जरिमा तनूनामप्यू नु पत्नीर्वृषणो जगम्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrvī́ḥ ǀ ahám ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ śaśramāṇā́ ǀ doṣā́ḥ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jaráyantīḥ ǀminā́ti ǀ śríyam ǀ jarimā́ ǀ tanū́nām ǀ ápi ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ jagamyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: 'Through many autumns have I toiled and laboured, at night and morn, through age-inducing dawnings. Old age impairs the beauty of our bodies. Let husbands still come near unto their spouses.
verses.wilson_translation: (Lopāmudrā): Many years have I been serving you diligently, both day and night, and through mornings, bringing on old age; decay now impairs the beauty of my limbs; what, therefore, is now (to be done); let husbands approach their wives.
verses.griffith_verse: 'Through many autumns have I toiled and laboured, at night and morn, through age-inducing dawnings. Old age impairs the beauty of our bodies. Let husbands still come near unto their spouses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये चिद्धि पूर्व ऋतसाप आसन्त्साकं देवेभिरवदन्नृतानि ।ते चिदवासुर्नह्यंतमापुः समू नु पत्नीर्वृषभिर्जगम्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛta-sā́paḥ ǀ ā́san ǀ sākám ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ ávadan ǀ ṛtā́ni ǀté ǀ cit ǀ áva ǀ asuḥ ǀ nahí ǀ ántam ǀ āpúḥ ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ jagamyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For even the men aforetime, law-fulfillers, who with the Gods declared eternal statutes,— They have decided, but have not accomplished: so now let Wives come near unto their husbands.
verses.wilson_translation: The ancient sages, disseminators of truth, who, verily, conversed of tuths with the gods, begot (progeny), nor thereby violated (their vow of continence), therefore should wives be approached by their husbands.
verses.griffith_verse: For even the men aforetime, law-fulfillers, who with the Gods declared eternal statutes,— They have decided, but have not accomplished: so now let Wives come near unto their husbands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न मृषा श्रांतं यदवंति देवा विश्वा इत्स्पृधो अभ्यश्नवाव ।जयावेदत्र शतनीथमाजिं यत्सम्यंचा मिथुनावभ्यजाव ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ mṛ́ṣā ǀ śrāntám ǀ yát ǀ ávanti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ít ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ aśnavāva ǀjáyāva ǀ ít ǀ átra ǀ śatá-nītham ǀ ājím ǀ yát ǀ samyáñcā ǀ mithunáu ǀ abhí ǀ ájāva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Non inutilis est labor cui Dii favent: nos omnes aemulos et aemulas vincamus. Superemus in hac centum artium pugna in qua duas partes convenientes utrinque commovemus.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agastya): Penance has not been practised in vain; since the gods protect us, we may indulge all our desires; in this world we may triumph in many conflicts, if we exert ourselves mutually together.
verses.griffith_verse: Non inutilis est labor cui Dii favent: nos omnes aemulos et aemulas vincamus. Superemus in hac centum artium pugna in qua duas partes convenientes utrinque commovemus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नदस्य मा रुधतः काम आगन्नित आजातो अमुतः कुतश्चित् ।लोपामुद्रा वृषणं नी रिणाति धीरमधीरा धयति श्वसंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: nadásya ǀ mā ǀ rudhatáḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agan ǀ itáḥ ǀ ā́-jātaḥ ǀ amútaḥ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ cit ǀlópāmudrā ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ níḥ ǀ riṇāti ǀ dhī́ram ǀ ádhīrā ǀ dhayati ǀ śvasántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cupido me cepit illius tauri [viri] qui me despicit, utrum hinc utrum illinc ab aliqua parte nata sit. Lopamudra taurum [maritum suum] ad se detrahit: insipiens illa sapientem anhelantem absorbet.
verses.wilson_translation: Desire, either from this cause or from that, has come upon me whilst engaged in prayer and suppressing (passion); let Lopāmudrāapproach her husband; the unsteady feminine le beguiles the firm and resolute man.
verses.griffith_verse: Cupido me cepit illius tauri [viri] qui me despicit, utrum hinc utrum illinc ab aliqua parte nata sit. Lopamudra taurum [maritum suum] ad se detrahit: insipiens illa sapientem anhelantem absorbet.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं नु सोममंतितो हृत्सु पीतमुप ब्रुवे ।यत्सीमागश्चकृमा तत्सु मृळतु पुलुकामो हि मर्त्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ nú ǀ sómam ǀ ántitaḥ ǀ hṛt-sú ǀ pītám ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ cakṛmá ǀ tát ǀ sú ǀ mṛḷatu ǀ pulu-kā́maḥ ǀ hí ǀ mártyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Soma I address that is most near us, that which hath been imbibed within the spirit, To pardon any sins we have committed. Verily mortal man is full of longings.
verses.wilson_translation: (Pupil): I beseech the Soma, which has been drunk in my heart, that it may fully expiate the sin we have committed; man is subject to many desires.
verses.griffith_verse: This Soma I address that is most near us, that which hath been imbibed within the spirit, To pardon any sins we have committed. Verily mortal man is full of longings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अगस्त्यः खनमानः खनित्रैः प्रजामपत्यं बलमिच्छमानः ।उभौ वर्णावृषिरुग्रः पुपोष सत्या देवेष्वाशिषो जगाम ॥
verses.transliteration: agástyaḥ ǀ khánamānaḥ ǀ khanítraiḥ ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ ápatyam ǀ bálam ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀubháu ǀ várṇau ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ pupoṣa ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ ā-śíṣaḥ ǀ jagāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agastya thus, toiling with strong endeavour, wishing for children, progeny and power, Cherished—a sage of mighty strength—both classes, and with the Gods obtained his prayer's fulfilment. By 'both classes' probably priests and princes, or institutors of sacrifices, are meant. M. Bergaigne understands the expression to mean the two forms or essences of Soma, the celestial and the terrestrial.
verses.wilson_translation: Agastya, a venerable sage, working with (fit) implements, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength, practised both classes (of obligations), and received true benedictions from the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Agastya thus, toiling with strong endeavour, wishing for children, progeny and power, Cherished—a sage of mighty strength—both classes, and with the Gods obtained his prayer's fulfilment. By 'both classes' probably priests and princes, or institutors of sacrifices, are meant. M. Bergaigne understands the expression to mean the two forms or essences of Soma, the celestial and the terrestrial.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXX. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIGHTLY your coursers travel through the regions when round the sea of air your car is flying.Your golden fellies scatter drops of moisture: drinking the sweetness yeattendthe Mornings. Ye as ye travel overtake the Courser who flies apart, the Friend of man, most holy.The prayer is that the Sister may convey you, all praised, meath-drinkers! to support and strengthen. Ye have deposited, matured within her, in the raw cow the first milk of the milch-cow,Which the bright offerer, shining like a serpent mid trees, presents to you whose form is perfect. Ye made the fierce heat to be full of sweetness for Atri at his wish, like streaming water.Fire-offering thence is yours, O Aśvins, Heroes: your car-wheels speed to us like springs of honey. Like Tugra's ancient son may I, ye Mighty, bring you to give your gifts with milk-oblations.Your greatness compasseth Earth, Heaven, and Waters: decayed for you is sorrow's net, ye Holy. When, Bounteous Ones, ye drive your yoked team downward, ye send, by your own natures, understanding.Swift as the wind let the prince please and feast you: he, like a pious man, gains strength for increase. For verily we truthful singers praise you the niggard trafficker is here excluded.Now, even now do ye O blameless Aśvins, ye Mighty, guard the man whose God is near him. You of a truth day after day, O Aśvins, that he might win the very plenteous torrent,Agastya, famous among mortal heroes, roused with a thousand lauds like sounds of music. When with the glory of your car ye travel, when we go speeding like the priest of mortals,And give good horses to sacrificers, may we, Nāsatyas! gain our share of riches. With songs of praise we call to-day, O Aśvins, that your new chariot, for our own well-being,That circles heaven with never-injured fellies. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: युवो रजांसि सुयमासो अश्वा रथो यद्वां पर्यर्णांसि दीयत् ।हिरण्यया वां पवयः प्रुषायन्मध्वः पिबंता उषसः सचेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ su-yámāsaḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ pári ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ dī́yat ǀhiraṇyáyāḥ ǀ vām ǀ paváyaḥ ǀ pruṣāyan ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ píbantau ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: LIGHTLY your coursers travel through the regions when round the sea of air your car is flying. Your golden fellies scatter drops of moisture: drinking the sweetness ye attend the Mornings.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, your horses are traversers of the (three) regions, when your chariot proceeds to (its desired) quarters; the golden fellies of your wheels grant (whatever is wished for); drinking the Soma, you participate in the morning (rite).
verses.griffith_verse: LIGHTLY your coursers travel through the regions when round the sea of air your car is flying. Your golden fellies scatter drops of moisture: drinking the sweetness ye attend the Mornings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवमत्यस्याव नक्षथो यद्विपत्मनो नर्यस्य प्रयज्योः ।स्वसा यद्वां विश्वगूर्ती भराति वाजायेट्टे मधुपाविषे च ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ átyasya ǀ áva ǀ nakṣathaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ví-patmanaḥ ǀ náryasya ǀ prá-yajyoḥ ǀsvásā ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ viśvagūrtī íti viśva-gūrtī ǀ bhárāti ǀ vā́jāya ǀ ī́ṭṭe ǀ madhu-pau ǀ iṣé ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye as ye travel overtake the Courser who flies apart, the Friend of man, most holy. The prayer is that the Sister may convey you, all praised, meath-drinkers! to support and strengthen.
verses.wilson_translation: Direct downwards (the course) of your (car) swift moving, variously going, friendly to man, and to be especially venerated, when all adorable, your sister (dawn) prepares (for your approach), and (the instrumental tutor of the ceremony) worships you, drinkers of the Soma, for the sake (of obtaining) strength and food.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye as ye travel overtake the Courser who flies apart, the Friend of man, most holy. The prayer is that the Sister may convey you, all praised, meath-drinkers! to support and strengthen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं पय उस्रियायामधत्तं पक्वमामायामव पूर्व्यं गोः ।अंतर्यद्वनिनो वामृतप्सू ह्वारो न शुचिर्यजते हविष्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ páyaḥ ǀ usríyāyām ǀ adhattam ǀ pakvám ǀ āmā́yām ǀ áva ǀ pū́rvyam ǀ góḥ ǀantáḥ ǀ yát ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ vām ǀ ṛtapsū ítyṛta-psū ǀ hvāráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śúciḥ ǀ yájate ǀ havíṣmān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye have deposited, matured within her, in the raw cow the first milk of the milch-cow, Which the bright offerer, shining like a serpent mid trees, presents to you whose form is perfect.
verses.wilson_translation: Youhave restored milk to the cow; you have (brought) down the prior mature (secretion) into the unripe (or barren udder) of the cow; the devout offerer of the oblation worships you, whose forms are truth, (as vigilant in the midst of the ceremony), as a thief (in the midst) of a thicket.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye have deposited, matured within her, in the raw cow the first milk of the milch-cow, Which the bright offerer, shining like a serpent mid trees, presents to you whose form is perfect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह घर्मं मधुमंतमत्रयेऽपो न क्षोदोऽवृणीतमेषे ।तद्वां नरावश्विना पश्वइष्टी रथ्येव चक्रा प्रति यंति मध्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ gharmám ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ átraye ǀ apáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ avṛṇītam ǀ eṣé ǀtát ǀ vām ǀ narau ǀ aśvinā ǀ páśvaḥ-iṣṭiḥ ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǀ práti ǀ yanti ǀ mádhvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye made the fierce heat to be full of sweetness for Atri at his wish, like streaming water. Fire-offering thence is yours, O Aśvins, Heroes: your car-wheels speed to us like springs of honey.
verses.wilson_translation: You rendered the heat as soothing as sweet butter to Atri; wishing (for relief), and invested it with coolness,like water; therefore, for you,Aśvins, leaders (of rites) the fire-offering (is made); to you the Soma(drips) run like chariot wheels (down a declivity).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye made the fierce heat to be full of sweetness for Atri at his wish, like streaming water. Fire-offering thence is yours, O Aśvins, Heroes: your car-wheels speed to us like springs of honey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां दानाय ववृतीय दस्रा गोरोहेण तौग्र्यो न जिव्रिः ।अपः क्षोणी सचते माहिना वां जूर्णो वामक्षुरंहसो यजत्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ dānā́ya ǀ vavṛtīya ǀ dasrā ǀ góḥ ǀ óhena ǀ taugryáḥ ǀ ná ǀ jívriḥ ǀapáḥ ǀ kṣoṇī́ íti ǀ sacate ǀ mā́hinā ǀ vām ǀ jūrṇáḥ ǀ vām ǀ ákṣuḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ yajatrā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like Tugra's ancient son may I, ye Mighty, bring you to give your gifts with milk-oblations. Your greatness compasseth Earth, Heaven, and Waters: decayed for you is sorrow's net, ye Holy.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras, may I bring you, by the vehicle of my prayers, (hither), to bestow (upon me your aid), like the infirm son of Tugra; heaven and earth combine (to worship you) through your greatness; may this, your aged (worshipper), adorable (Aśvins), enjoy long life, (exempt) from sin.
verses.griffith_verse: Like Tugra's ancient son may I, ye Mighty, bring you to give your gifts with milk-oblations. Your greatness compasseth Earth, Heaven, and Waters: decayed for you is sorrow's net, ye Holy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि यद्युवेथे नियुतः सुदानू उप स्वधाभिः सृजथः पुरंधिं ।प्रेषद्वेषद्वातो न सूरिरा महे ददे सुव्रतो न वाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ yát ǀ yuvéthe íti ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ úpa ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ sṛjathaḥ ǀ púram-dhim ǀpréṣat ǀ véṣat ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūríḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ mahé ǀ dade ǀ su-vratáḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Bounteous Ones, ye drive your yoked team downward, ye send, by your own natures, understanding. Swift as the wind let the prince please and feast you: he, like a pious man, gains strength for increase.
verses.wilson_translation: Bountiful givers, when you yoke your horses you replenish the earth with viands; may this your worshipper be (swift) as the wind to propitiate and plural ase you, that, through your great (favour), he may, like a pious man, obtain food.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Bounteous Ones, ye drive your yoked team downward, ye send, by your own natures, understanding. Swift as the wind let the prince please and feast you: he, like a pious man, gains strength for increase.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयं चिद्धि वां जरितारः सत्या विपन्यामहे वि पणिर्हितावान् ।अधा चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनिंद्या पाथो हि ष्मा वृषणावंतिदेवं ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ vipanyā́mahe ǀ ví ǀ paṇíḥ ǀ hitá-vān ǀádha ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ aśvinau ǀ anindyā ǀ pātháḥ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ vṛṣaṇau ǀ ánti-devam ǁ
verses.english_translation: For verily we truthful singers praise you the niggard trafficker is here excluded. Now, even now do ye O blameless Aśvins, ye Mighty, guard the man whose God is near him.
verses.wilson_translation: Your sincere adorers, we verily praise you in various ways. The pitcher has been plural ced (ready for the Soma). Irreproachable Aśvins, showerers (of benefits) drink freely of the juice in the presence of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: For verily we truthful singers praise you the niggard trafficker is here excluded. Now, even now do ye O blameless Aśvins, ye Mighty, guard the man whose God is near him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनु द्यून्विरुद्रस्य प्रस्रवणस्य सातौ ।अगस्त्यो नरां नृषु प्रशस्तः काराधुनीव चितयत्सहस्रैः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ aśvinau ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ ví-rudrasya ǀ pra-srávaṇasya ǀ sātáu ǀagástyaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ nṛ́ṣu ǀ prá-śastaḥ ǀ kā́rādhunī-iva ǀ citayat ǀ sahásraiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You of a truth day after day, O Aśvins, that he might win the very plenteous torrent, Agastya, famous among mortal heroes, roused with a thousand lauds like sounds of music.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins,Agastya, eminent among the leader of men, arouses you daily with numerous (invocations) like an instrumental ument of sound, for the sake of obtaining a manifold (flow) of a torrent (of rain).
verses.griffith_verse: You of a truth day after day, O Aśvins, that he might win the very plenteous torrent, Agastya, famous among mortal heroes, roused with a thousand lauds like sounds of music.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यद्वहेथे महिना रथस्य प्र स्यंद्रा याथो मनुषो न होता ।धत्तं सूरिभ्य उत वा स्वश्व्यं नासत्या रयिषाचः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ váhethe íti ǀ mahinā́ ǀ ráthasya ǀ prá ǀ syandrā ǀ yāthaḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǀdhattám ǀ sūrí-bhyaḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ su-áśvyam ǀ nā́satyā ǀ rayi-sā́caḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: When with the glory of your car ye travel, when we go speeding like the priest of mortals, And give good horses to sacrificers, may we, Nāsatyas! gain our share of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: When, by the virtue of your chariot, you come (to the sacrifice), and when, like the ministering priest (after discharging his rfunction), you depart, gliding away, you give to the devout (worshippers a reward), thogh it be store of good horses; may we be enriched,Nāsatyās(by your favour).
verses.griffith_verse: When with the glory of your car ye travel, when we go speeding like the priest of mortals, And give good horses to sacrificers, may we, Nāsatyas! gain our share of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम स्तोमैरश्विना सुविताय नव्यं ।अरिष्टनेमिं परि द्यामियानं विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ vayám ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ návyam ǀáriṣṭa-nemim ǀ pári ǀ dyā́m ǀ iyānám ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: With songs of praise we call to-day, O Aśvins, that your new chariot, for our own well-being, That circles heaven with never-injured fellies. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke today,Aśvins, with hymns, for the sake of good things, your praiseworthy chariot of undamaged wheels, and traversing the sky, that we may obtain (from it) food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: With songs of praise we call to-day, O Aśvins, that your new chariot, for our own well-being, That circles heaven with never-injured fellies. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXI. Aśvins
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT, dearest Pair, is this in strength and riches that ye as Priests are bring from the waters?This sacrifice is your glorification, ye who protect mankind and give them treasures. May your pure steeds, rain-drinkers, bring you hither, swift as the tempest, your celestial coursers,Rapid as thought, with fair backs, full of vigour, resplendent in their native light, O Aśvins. Your car is like a torrent rushing downward: may it come nigh, broad-seated, for our welfare,—Car holy, strong, that ever would be foremost, thought-swift, which ye, for whom we long, have mounted. Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them;One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven's auspicious offspring. May your car-seat, down-gliding, golden-coloured, according to your wish approach our dwellings.Men shall feed full the bay steeds of the other, and, Aśvins they with roars shall stir the regions. Forth comes your strong Bull like a cloud of autumn, sending abundant food of liquid sweetness.Let them feed with the other's ways and vigour: the upper streams have come and do us service. Your constant song hath been sent forth, Disposers! that flows threefold in mighty strength, O Aśvins.Thus lauded, give the suppliant protection moving or resting hear mine invocation. This song of bright contents for you is swelling in the men's hall where three-fold grass is ready.Your strong rain-cloud, ye Mighty Ones, hath swollen, honouring men as ’twere with milk's outpouring. The prudent worshipper, like Pūṣan, Aśvins! praises you as he praises Dawn and Agni,When, singing with devotion, he invokes you. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: कदु प्रेष्ठाविषां रयीणामध्वर्यंता यदुन्निनीथो अपां ।अयं वां यज्ञो अकृत प्रशस्तिं वसुधिती अवितारा जनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ préṣṭhau ǀ iṣā́m ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ adhvaryántā ǀ yát ǀ ut-ninītháḥ ǀ apā́m ǀayám ǀ vām ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ akṛta ǀ prá-śastim ǀ vásudhitī íti vásu-dhitī ǀ ávitārā ǀ janānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT, dearest Pair, is this in strength and riches that ye as Priests are bring from the waters? This sacrifice is your glorification, ye who protect mankind and give them treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: When, beloved (Aśvins), do you bear aloft (the materials) of food and riches, that, desirous of the sacrifice, you may send down the rain; this sacrifice offers you adoration, givers of riches, protectors of men.
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT, dearest Pair, is this in strength and riches that ye as Priests are bring from the waters? This sacrifice is your glorification, ye who protect mankind and give them treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वामश्वासः शुचयः पयस्पा वातरंहसो दिव्यासो अत्याः ।मनोजुवो वृषणो वीतपृष्ठा एह स्वराजो अश्विना वहंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ payaḥ-pā́ḥ ǀ vā́ta-raṃhasaḥ ǀ divyā́saḥ ǀ átyāḥ ǀmanaḥ-júvaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vītá-pṛṣṭhāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ sva-rā́jaḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ vahantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your pure steeds, rain-drinkers, bring you hither, swift as the tempest, your celestial coursers, Rapid as thought, with fair backs, full of vigour, resplendent in their native light, O Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, may your horses, pure, rain-drinking, swift as the wind, heaven-born, quick-moving, fleet as thought, vigorous, well-backed, and self-irradiating, bring you hither.
verses.griffith_verse: May your pure steeds, rain-drinkers, bring you hither, swift as the tempest, your celestial coursers, Rapid as thought, with fair backs, full of vigour, resplendent in their native light, O Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां रथोऽवनिर्न प्रवत्वान्त्सृप्रवंधुरः सुविताय गम्याः ।वृष्णः स्थातारा मनसो जवीयानहंपूर्वो यजतो धिष्ण्या यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ avániḥ ǀ ná ǀ pravátvān ǀ sṛprá-vandhuraḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ gamyāḥ ǀvṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ sthātārā ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ aham-pūrváḥ ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dhiṣṇyā ǀ yáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your car is like a torrent rushing downward: may it come nigh, broad-seated, for our welfare,— Car holy, strong, that ever would be foremost, thought-swift, which ye, for whom we long, have mounted.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, excellent and steady, may your chariot, vast as the earth, broad-fronted, rapid as the rain (fleet) as thought, cumulative and adorable, come hither for (our) good.
verses.griffith_verse: Your car is like a torrent rushing downward: may it come nigh, broad-seated, for our welfare,— Car holy, strong, that ever would be foremost, thought-swift, which ye, for whom we long, have mounted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः स्वैः ।जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá-iha ǀ jātā́ ǀ sám ǀ avāvaśītām ǀ arepásā ǀ tanvā́ ǀ nā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ sváiḥ ǀjiṣṇúḥ ǀ vām ǀ anyáḥ ǀ sú-makhasya ǀ sūríḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ su-bhágaḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀ ūhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them; One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven's auspicious offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Born here (in the middle region) and here (in the upper region), you are glorified together, as faultless in your forms and (perfect in) your own many excellences; one (of you) the victorious son (of the firmament), the devout (promoter) of sacred sacrifice, the other, the auspicious son of heaven, (each) upholds (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them; One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven's auspicious offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वां निचेरुः ककुहो वशाँ अनु पिशंगरूपः सदनानि गम्याः ।हरी अन्यस्य पीपयंत वाजैर्मथ्ना रजांस्यश्विना वि घोषैः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vām ǀ ni-cerúḥ ǀ kakuháḥ ǀ váśān ǀ ánu ǀ piśáṅga-rūpaḥ ǀ sádanāni ǀ gamyāḥ ǀhárī íti ǀ anyásya ǀ pīpáyanta ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ mathnā́ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ aśvinā ǀ ví ǀ ghóṣaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your car-seat, down-gliding, golden-coloured, according to your wish approach our dwellings. Men shall feed full the bay steeds of the other, and, Aśvins they with roars shall stir the regions.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, may the golden-coloured (car of one of you), traversing at will the quarters of space, come to our dwellings; may mankind encourage the horses of the other by food, by friction, and by shouts.
verses.griffith_verse: May your car-seat, down-gliding, golden-coloured, according to your wish approach our dwellings. Men shall feed full the bay steeds of the other, and, Aśvins they with roars shall stir the regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वां शरद्वान्वृषभो न निष्षाट् पूर्वीरिषश्चरति मध्व इष्णन् ।एवैरन्यस्य पीपयंत वाजैर्वेषंतीरूर्ध्वा नद्यो न आगुः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vām ǀ śarát-vān ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ niṣṣā́ṭ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ carati ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ iṣṇán ǀévaiḥ ǀ anyásya ǀ pīpáyanta ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ véṣantīḥ ǀ ūrdhvā́ḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aguḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forth comes your strong Bull like a cloud of autumn, sending abundant food of liquid sweetness. Let them feed with the other's ways and vigour: the upper streams have come and do us service.
verses.wilson_translation: (One of you), the disperser (of the clouds), like Indra, the annihilator (of his foes), desirous of the oblation, proceeds (bestowing) abundant food. (Devout worshippers) cherish with (sacrificial) viands, (the faculties) of the other, for the sake of favours, which flow upon us like swelling rivers.
verses.griffith_verse: Forth comes your strong Bull like a cloud of autumn, sending abundant food of liquid sweetness. Let them feed with the other's ways and vigour: the upper streams have come and do us service.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असर्जि वां स्थविरा वेधसा गीर्बाळ्हे अश्विना त्रेधा क्षरंती ।उपस्तुताववतं नाधमानं यामन्नयामञ्छृणुतं हवं मे ॥
verses.transliteration: ásarji ǀ vām ǀ sthávirā ǀ vedhasā ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ bāḷhé ǀ aśvinā ǀ tredhā́ ǀ kṣárantī ǀúpa-stutau ǀ avatam ǀ nā́dhamānam ǀ yā́man ǀ áyāman ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ hávam ǀ me ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your constant song hath been sent forth, Disposers! that flows threefold in mighty strength, O Aśvins. Thus lauded, give the suppliant protection moving or resting hear mine invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, creators, the perpetual threefold hymn addressed to you, has been uttered, (to secure) your steady (favour); thus glorified protect him who solicits (your bounty), and whether moving or resting, hear his invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: Your constant song hath been sent forth, Disposers! that flows threefold in mighty strength, O Aśvins. Thus lauded, give the suppliant protection moving or resting hear mine invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्या वां रुशतो वप्ससो गीस्त्रिबर्हिषि सदसि पिन्वते नॄन् ।वृषा वां मेघो वृषणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषो दशस्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syā́ ǀ vām ǀ rúśataḥ ǀ vápsasaḥ ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ tri-barhíṣi ǀ sádasi ǀ pinvate ǀ nṝ́n ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ vām ǀ megháḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ pīpāya ǀ góḥ ǀ ná ǀ séke ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ daśasyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: This song of bright contents for you is swelling in the men's hall where three-fold grass is ready. Your strong rain-cloud, ye Mighty Ones, hath swollen, honouring men as ’twere with milk's outpouring.
verses.wilson_translation: May the praise of your resplendent forms, (uttered) in the hall of sacrifice, thrice strewn with sacred grass, bring prosperity to the conductors (of the sacrifice). Showerers (of benefits), may the raining-cloud, proceeding to man, nourish him lik a a sprinkling of water.
verses.griffith_verse: This song of bright contents for you is swelling in the men's hall where three-fold grass is ready. Your strong rain-cloud, ye Mighty Ones, hath swollen, honouring men as ’twere with milk's outpouring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां पूषेवाश्विना पुरंधिरग्निमुषां न जरते हविष्मान् ।हुवे यद्वां वरिवस्या गृणानो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ pūṣā́-iva ǀ aśvinā ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ agním ǀ uṣā́m ǀ ná ǀ jarate ǀ havíṣmān ǀhuvé ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ varivasyā́ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: The prudent worshipper, like Pūṣan, Aśvins! praises you as he praises Dawn and Agni, When, singing with devotion, he invokes you. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise offerer of oblations, like Pūṣan, praises you,Aśvins, as (he would praise)Agniand Uṣā, (at the season) at which I invoke you praising with devotion that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: The prudent worshipper, like Pūṣan, Aśvins! praises you as he praises Dawn and Agni, When, singing with devotion, he invokes you. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS was the task. Appear promptly, ye prudent Ones. Here is the chariot drawn by strong steeds: be ye glad.Heart-stirring, longed for, succourers of Viśpalā, here are Heaven's Sons whose sway blesses the pious man. Longed for, most Indra-like, mighty, most Marut-like, most wonderful in deed, car-borne, best charioteers,Bring your full chariot hither heaped with liquid sweet: thereon, ye Aśvins, come to him who offers gifts. What make ye there, ye Mighty? Wherefore linger ye with folk who, offering not, are held in high esteem?Pass over them; make ye the niggard's life decay: give light unto the singer eloquent in praise. Crunch up on. every side the dogs who bark at us: slay ye our foes, O Aśvins this ye understand.Make wealthy every word of him who praises you: accept with favour, both Nāsatyas, this my laud. Ye made for Tugra's son amid the water-floods that animated ship with wings to fly withal,Whereon with God-devoted mind ye brought him forth, and fled with easy flight from out the mighty surge. Four ships most welcome in the midst of ocean, urged by the Aśvins, save the son of Tugra,Him who was cast down headlong in the waters, plunged in the thick inevitable darkness. What tree was that which stood fixed in surrounding sea to which the son of Tugra supplicating clung?Like twigs, of which some winged creature may take hold, ye, Aśvins, bore him off safely to your renown. Welcome to you be this the hymn of praises uttered by Mānas, O Nāsatyas, Heroes,From this our gathering where we offer Soma. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: अभूदिदं वयुनमो षु भूषता रथो वृषण्वान्मदता मनीषिणः ।धियंजिन्वा धिष्ण्या विश्पलावसू दिवो नपाता सुकृते शुचिव्रता ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūt ǀ idám ǀ vayúnam ǀ ó íti ǀ sú ǀ bhūṣata ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇ-vān ǀ mádata ǀ manīṣiṇaḥ ǀdhiyam-jinvā́ ǀ dhíṣṇyā ǀ viśpálāvasū íti ǀ diváḥ ǀ nápātā ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ śúci-vratā ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS was the task. Appear promptly, ye prudent Ones. Here is the chariot drawn by strong steeds: be ye glad. Heart-stirring, longed for, succourers of Viśpalā, here are Heaven's Sons whose sway blesses the pious man.
verses.wilson_translation: The information, sage (priests), has been received; be ready with your praises, for the (benefit) showering car (of the Aśvinshas arrived); propitiate (the divinities), for they show favour to the doer of good works; they are entitled to praise, rich in benevolence to mankind the grandsons of heaven, and observers of holy rites.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS was the task. Appear promptly, ye prudent Ones. Here is the chariot drawn by strong steeds: be ye glad. Heart-stirring, longed for, succourers of Viśpalā, here are Heaven's Sons whose sway blesses the pious man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रतमा हि धिष्ण्या मरुत्तमा दस्रा दंसिष्ठा रथ्या रथीतमा ।पूर्णं रथं वहेथे मध्व आचितं तेन दाश्वांसमुप याथो अश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: índra-tamā ǀ hí ǀ dhíṣṇyā ǀ marút-tamā ǀ dasrā́ ǀ dáṃsiṣṭhā ǀ rathyā́ ǀ rathí-tamā ǀpūrṇám ǀ rátham ǀ vahethe íti ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ā́-citam ǀ téna ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ úpa ǀ yāthaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Longed for, most Indra-like, mighty, most Marut-like, most wonderful in deed, car-borne, best charioteers, Bring your full chariot hither heaped with liquid sweet: thereon, ye Aśvins, come to him who offers gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras, in truth most imperial, adorable, swifter than the winds, and eminent in good works, riders in a car, and most distinguished charioteers, bring hither your car, full heaped up with ambrosia, and with it come,Aśvins, to the donor (of the offering).
verses.griffith_verse: Longed for, most Indra-like, mighty, most Marut-like, most wonderful in deed, car-borne, best charioteers, Bring your full chariot hither heaped with liquid sweet: thereon, ye Aśvins, come to him who offers gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किमत्र दस्रा कृणुथः किमासाथे जनो यः कश्चिदहविर्महीयते ।अति क्रमिष्टं जुरतं पणेरसुं ज्योतिर्विप्राय कृणुतं वचस्यवे ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ átra ǀ dasrā ǀ kṛṇuthaḥ ǀ kím ǀ āsāthe íti ǀ jánaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ áhaviḥ ǀ mahīyáte ǀáti ǀ kramiṣṭam ǀ jurátam ǀ paṇéḥ ǀ ásum ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ víprāya ǀ kṛṇutam ǀ vacasyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: What make ye there, ye Mighty? Wherefore linger ye with folk who, offering not, are held in high esteem? Pass over them; make ye the niggard's life decay: give light unto the singer eloquent in praise.
verses.wilson_translation: What makes you here,Aśvins; why do you tarry, (where) any man who makes no oblation is respected; humble him; take away the life of the niggard; grant light to the pious man striving to speak your praise.
verses.griffith_verse: What make ye there, ye Mighty? Wherefore linger ye with folk who, offering not, are held in high esteem? Pass over them; make ye the niggard's life decay: give light unto the singer eloquent in praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जंभयतमभितो रायतः शुनो हतं मृधो विदथुस्तान्यश्विना ।वाचंवाचं जरितू रत्निनीं कृतमुभा शंसं नासत्यावतं मम ॥
verses.transliteration: jambháyatam ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ rā́yataḥ ǀ śúnaḥ ǀ hatám ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ vidáthuḥ ǀ tā́ni ǀ aśvinā ǀvā́cam-vācam ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ ratnínīm ǀ kṛtam ǀ ubhā́ ǀ śáṃsam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ avatam ǀ máma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Crunch up on. every side the dogs who bark at us: slay ye our foes, O Aśvins this ye understand. Make wealthy every word of him who praises you: accept with favour, both Nāsatyas, this my laud.
verses.wilson_translation: Annihilate,Aśvins, the dogs who bark at us; slay them warring (against us); you know their (means of harm); render every word of him who praises you affluent in precious (rewards); accept Nāsatyas, both of you, may praise.
