verses.griffith_verse: Crunch up on. every side the dogs who bark at us: slay ye our foes, O Aśvins this ye understand. Make wealthy every word of him who praises you: accept with favour, both Nāsatyas, this my laud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवमेतं चक्रथुः सिंधुषु प्लवमात्मन्वंतं पक्षिणं तौग्र्याय कं ।येन देवत्रा मनसा निरूहथुः सुपप्तनी पेतथुः क्षोदसो महः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ etám ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ síndhuṣu ǀ plavám ǀ ātman-vántam ǀ pakṣíṇam ǀ taugryā́ya ǀ kám ǀyéna ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ niḥ-ūháthuḥ ǀ su-paptaní ǀ petathuḥ ǀ kṣódasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye made for Tugra's son amid the water-floods that animated ship with wings to fly withal, Whereon with God-devoted mind ye brought him forth, and fled with easy flight from out the mighty surge.
verses.wilson_translation: You constructed a plural asant, substantial winged bark, borne on the ocean waters for the son of Tugra, by which, with minddevoted to the gods, you bore him up, and quickly descending (from the sky), you made a path for him across the great waters.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye made for Tugra's son amid the water-floods that animated ship with wings to fly withal, Whereon with God-devoted mind ye brought him forth, and fled with easy flight from out the mighty surge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवविद्धं तौग्र्यमप्स्वंतरनारंभणे तमसि प्रविद्धं ।चतस्रो नावो जठलस्य जुष्टा उदश्विभ्यामिषिताः पारयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: áva-viddham ǀ taugryám ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáḥ ǀ anārambhaṇé ǀ támasi ǀ prá-viddham ǀcátasraḥ ǀ nā́vaḥ ǀ jáṭhalasya ǀ júṣṭāḥ ǀ út ǀ aśví-bhyām ǀ iṣitā́ḥ ǀ pārayanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Four ships most welcome in the midst of ocean, urged by the Aśvins, save the son of Tugra, Him who was cast down headlong in the waters, plunged in the thick inevitable darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Four ships launched into the midst of the receptable (of the waters), sent by the Aśvins, brought safe to shore the son of Tugra, who had been cast headlong into the waters (by his foes), and plural nged in extricable darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Four ships most welcome in the midst of ocean, urged by the Aśvins, save the son of Tugra, Him who was cast down headlong in the waters, plunged in the thick inevitable darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कः स्विद्वृक्षो निष्ठितो मध्ये अर्णसो यं तौग्र्यो नाधितः पर्यषस्वजत् ।पर्णा मृगस्य पतरोरिवारभ उदश्विना ऊहथुः श्रोमताय कं ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ svit ǀ vṛkṣáḥ ǀ níḥ-sthitaḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ árṇasaḥ ǀ yám ǀ taugryáḥ ǀ nādhitáḥ ǀ pari-ásasvajat ǀparṇā́ ǀ mṛgásya ǀ patároḥ-iva ǀ ā-rábhe ǀ út ǀ aśvinā ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ śrómatāya ǀ kám ǁ
verses.english_translation: What tree was that which stood fixed in surrounding sea to which the son of Tugra supplicating clung? Like twigs, of which some winged creature may take hold, ye, Aśvins, bore him off safely to your renown.
verses.wilson_translation: What was the tree that was stationed in the midst of the ocean, to which the supplicating son of Tugraclung; as leaves (are caught hold of) for the support of a falling animal; you,Aśvins, bore him up to safety, to your great renown.
verses.griffith_verse: What tree was that which stood fixed in surrounding sea to which the son of Tugra supplicating clung? Like twigs, of which some winged creature may take hold, ye, Aśvins, bore him off safely to your renown.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वां नरा नासत्यावनु ष्याद्यद्वां मानास उचथमवोचन् ।अस्मादद्य सदसः सोम्यादा विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ nāsatyau ǀ ánu ǀ syāt ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ mā́nāsaḥ ǀ ucátham ǀ ávocan ǀasmā́t ǀ adyá ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ somyā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Welcome to you be this the hymn of praises uttered by Mānas, O Nāsatyas, Heroes, From this our gathering where we offer Soma. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: May the praise which your devout adorers have uttered be acceptable to you,Nāsatyas, leaders (in pious rites); be propitiated today by the libations of our assembly, that we may obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Welcome to you be this the hymn of praises uttered by Mānas, O Nāsatyas, Heroes, From this our gathering where we offer Soma. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAKE ready that which passes thought in swiftness, that hath three wheels and triple seat, ye Mighty,Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious, whereon, threefold, ye fly like birds with pinions. Light rolls your easy chariot faring earthward, what time, for food, ye, full of wisdom, mount it.May this song, wondrous fair, attend your glory: ye, as ye travel, wait on Dawn Heaven's Daughter. Ascend your lightly rolling car, approaching the worshipper who turns him to his duties,—Whereon ye come unto the house to quicken man and his offspring, O Nāsatyas, Heroes. Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf harm you. Forsake me not, nor pass me by or others.Here stands your share, here is your hymn, ye Mighty: yours are these vessels, full of pleasant juices. Gotama, Purumīlha, Atri bringing oblations all invoke you for protection.Like one who goes straight to the point directed, ye Nāsatyas, to mine invocation. We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins.Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: तं युंजाथां मनसो यो जवीयान् त्रिवंधुरो वृषणा यस्त्रिचक्रः ।येनोपयाथः सुकृतो दुरोणं त्रिधातुना पतथो विर्न पर्णैः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ yuñjāthām ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ tri-vandhuráḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ yáḥ ǀ tri-cakráḥ ǀyéna ǀ upa-yātháḥ ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ duroṇám ǀ tri-dhā́tunā ǀ patathaḥ ǀ víḥ ǀ ná ǀ parṇáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAKE ready that which passes thought in swiftness, that hath three wheels and triple seat, ye Mighty, Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious, whereon, threefold, ye fly like birds with pinions.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerers of benefits, harness the car which has three benches, three wheels, and is as quick as thought; with which, embellished with three metals, you come to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper), and in which you travel like a bird with wings.
verses.griffith_verse: MAKE ready that which passes thought in swiftness, that hath three wheels and triple seat, ye Mighty, Whereon ye seek the dwelling of the pious, whereon, threefold, ye fly like birds with pinions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुवृद्रथो वर्तते यन्नभि क्षां यत्तिष्ठथः क्रतुमंतानु पृक्षे ।वपुर्वपुष्या सचतामियं गीर्दिवो दुहित्रोषसा सचेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: su-vṛ́t ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vartate ǀ yán ǀ abhí ǀ kṣā́m ǀ yát ǀ tíṣṭhathaḥ ǀ krátu-mantā ǀ ánu ǀ pṛkṣé ǀvápuḥ ǀ vapuṣyā́ ǀ sacatām ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitrā́ ǀ uṣásā ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Light rolls your easy chariot faring earthward, what time, for food, ye, full of wisdom, mount it. May this song, wondrous fair, attend your glory: ye, as ye travel, wait on Dawn Heaven's Daughter.
verses.wilson_translation: Your easy-rolling car alights upon the earth, where favourable to the sacred rite, you stop for the sake of the (sacrificial) food; may this hymn, promotive of your person nal (welfare), be associated with your forms, and do you unite with the dawn, the daughter of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Light rolls your easy chariot faring earthward, what time, for food, ye, full of wisdom, mount it. May this song, wondrous fair, attend your glory: ye, as ye travel, wait on Dawn Heaven's Daughter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तिष्ठतं सुवृतं यो रथो वामनु व्रतानि वर्तते हविष्मान् ।येन नरा नासत्येषयध्यै वर्तिर्याथस्तनयाय त्मने च ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tiṣṭhatam ǀ su-vṛ́tam ǀ yáḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vām ǀ ánu ǀ vratā́ni ǀ vártate ǀ havíṣmān ǀyéna ǀ narā ǀ nāsatyā ǀ iṣayádhyai ǀ vartíḥ ǀ yātháḥ ǀ tánayāya ǀ tmáne ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ascend your lightly rolling car, approaching the worshipper who turns him to his duties,— Whereon ye come unto the house to quicken man and his offspring, O Nāsatyas, Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend your rolling car, which approaches the sacred rite of the offerer of the oblation; the car in which,Nāsatyas, leaders, you purpose to come to the sacrifice, and proceed to the dwelling (of the worshipper), for (bestowing upon him) offspring, and for his own (good).
verses.griffith_verse: Ascend your lightly rolling car, approaching the worshipper who turns him to his duties,— Whereon ye come unto the house to quicken man and his offspring, O Nāsatyas, Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा वां वृको मा वृकीरा दधर्षीन्मा परि वर्क्तमुत माति धक्तं ।अयं वां भागो निहित इयं गीर्दस्राविमे वां निधयो मधूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vām ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ vṛkī́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dadharṣīt ǀ mā́ ǀ pári ǀ varktam ǀ utá ǀ mā́ ǀ áti ǀ dhaktam ǀayám ǀ vām ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ ní-hitaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ dásrau ǀ imé ǀ vām ǀ ni-dháyaḥ ǀ mádhūnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf harm you. Forsake me not, nor pass me by or others. Here stands your share, here is your hymn, ye Mighty: yours are these vessels, full of pleasant juices.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf, harm me safe (in your protection); abandon me not, nor deliver me (to another). This your share (of the offering) is prepared; this prayer,Dasras, (is addressed) to you; these treasures of Somaare for you.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not the wolf, let not the she-wolf harm you. Forsake me not, nor pass me by or others. Here stands your share, here is your hymn, ye Mighty: yours are these vessels, full of pleasant juices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां गोतमः पुरुमीळ्हो अत्रिर्दस्रा हवतेऽवसे हविष्मान् ।दिशं न दिष्टामृजूयेव यंता मे हवं नासत्योप यातं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ gótamaḥ ǀ puru-mīḷháḥ ǀ átriḥ ǀ dásrā ǀ hávate ǀ ávase ǀ havíṣmān ǀdíśam ǀ ná ǀ diṣṭā́m ǀ ṛjuyā́-iva ǀ yántā ǀ ā́ ǀ me ǀ hávam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gotama, Purumīlha, Atri bringing oblations all invoke you for protection. Like one who goes straight to the point directed, ye Nāsatyas, to mine invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Gotama, Purimiḷha,Atri, (each) offering oblations, invokes you for his protection; like unto a wayfarer, who (makes for his intended direction) by a straight (path) do you,Dasras, come (direct) to my invocation).
verses.griffith_verse: Gotama, Purumīlha, Atri bringing oblations all invoke you for protection. Like one who goes straight to the point directed, ye Nāsatyas, to mine invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतारिष्म तमसस्पारमस्य प्रति वां स्तोमो अश्विनावधायि ।एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयानैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: átāriṣma ǀ támasaḥ ǀ pārám ǀ asyá ǀ práti ǀ vām ǀ stómaḥ ǀ aśvinau ǀ adhāyi ǀā́ ǀ ihá ǀ yātam ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ deva-yā́naiḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: (Through your aid)Aśvins, we cross over this (limit of) darkness; to you this (our) hymn has been addressed; come hither by the paths traversed by the gods, that we may obtain food, and strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIV. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET us invoke you both this day and after the priest is here with lauds when morn is breaking:Nāsatyas, wheresoe’er ye be, Heaven's Children, for him who is more liberal than the godless. With us, ye Mighty, let yourselves be joyful, glad in our stream of Soma slay the niggards.Graciously hear my hymns and invitations, marking, O Heroes, with your cars my longing. Nāsatyas, Pūṣans, ye as Gods for glory arranged and set in order Sūrya's bridal.Your giant steeds move on, sprung from the waters, like ancient times of Varuṇa the Mighty. Your grace be with us, ye who love sweet juices: further the hymn sung by the poet Māna,When men are joyful in your glorious actions, to win heroic strength, ye Bounteous Givers. This praise was made, O liberal Lords, O Aśvins, for you with fair adornment by the Mānas.Come to our house for us and for our children, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, in Agastya. We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins.Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. may we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: ता वामद्य तावपरं हुवेमोच्छंत्यामुषसि वह्निरुक्थैः ।नासत्या कुह चित्संतावर्यो दिवो नपाता सुदास्तराय ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ adyá ǀ táu ǀ aparám ǀ huvema ǀ ucchántyām ǀ uṣási ǀ váhniḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀnā́satyā ǀ kúha ǀ cit ǀ sántau ǀ aryáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ nápātā ǀ sudā́ḥ-tarāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: LET us invoke you both this day and after the priest is here with lauds when morn is breaking: Nāsatyas, wheresoe’er ye be, Heaven's Children, for him who is more liberal than the godless.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you two, (Aśvins), today; the same two on any other day; when the morning dawns.Nāsatyas, grandsons of heaven, wherever you may be, the pious reciter (of the hymn) invokes you with praises on behalf of the liberal donor (of the offering).
verses.griffith_verse: LET us invoke you both this day and after the priest is here with lauds when morn is breaking: Nāsatyas, wheresoe’er ye be, Heaven's Children, for him who is more liberal than the godless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे ऊ षु वृषणा मादयेथामुत्पणीँर्हतमूर्म्या मदंता ।श्रुतं मे अच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनामेष्टा नरा निचेतारा च कर्णैः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ mādayethām ǀ út ǀ paṇī́n ǀ hatam ǀ ūrmyā́ ǀ mádantā ǀśrutám ǀ me ǀ ácchokti-bhiḥ ǀ matīnā́m ǀ éṣṭā ǀ narā ǀ ní-cetārā ǀ ca ǀ kárṇaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With us, ye Mighty, let yourselves be joyful, glad in our stream of Soma slay the niggards. Graciously hear my hymns and invitations, marking, O Heroes, with your cars my longing.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerers (of benefits), rejoicing in (our) libations), make us happy, and destroy the niggard (withholder) of offerings; hear, leaders, with your ears, my praises addressed to you with pure words, for you are seekers (after praise), you are retentive (of laudation).
verses.griffith_verse: With us, ye Mighty, let yourselves be joyful, glad in our stream of Soma slay the niggards. Graciously hear my hymns and invitations, marking, O Heroes, with your cars my longing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रिये पूषन्निषुकृतेव देवा नासत्या वहतुं सूर्यायाः ।वच्यंते वां ककुहा अप्सु जाता युगा जूर्णेव वरुणस्य भूरेः ॥
verses.transliteration: śriyé ǀ pūṣan ǀ iṣukṛ́tā-iva ǀ devā́ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ vahatúm ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǀvacyánte ǀ vām ǀ kakuhā́ḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ yugā́ ǀ jūrṇā́-iva ǀ váruṇasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nāsatyas, Pūṣans, ye as Gods for glory arranged and set in order Sūrya's bridal. Your giant steeds move on, sprung from the waters, like ancient times of Varuṇa the Mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Aśvins, in whom is no untruth, (darting) like arrows to acquire glory, and to carry off Sūrya, to you are addressed the prayers that are recited at holy rites, for (the completion of) the uninterrupted, sin-removing (sacrifice), as ancient ages (offered them).
verses.griffith_verse: Nāsatyas, Pūṣans, ye as Gods for glory arranged and set in order Sūrya's bridal. Your giant steeds move on, sprung from the waters, like ancient times of Varuṇa the Mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे सा वां माध्वी रातिरस्तु स्तोमं हिनोतं मान्यस्य कारोः ।अनु यद्वां श्रवस्या सुदानू सुवीर्याय चर्षणयो मदंति ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ sā́ ǀ vām ǀ mādhvī íti ǀ rātíḥ ǀ astu ǀ stómam ǀ hinotam ǀ mānyásya ǀ kāróḥ ǀánu ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀ su-vī́ryāya ǀ carṣaṇáyaḥ ǀ mádanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your grace be with us, ye who love sweet juices: further the hymn sung by the poet Māna, When men are joyful in your glorious actions, to win heroic strength, ye Bounteous Givers.
verses.wilson_translation: Receivers of the oblation, may your liberality be displayed towards us; be plural ased with the hymn of the venerable author, so that men may honour the instrumental tutor of the ceremony, as (they honour) you, liberal donors, for the sake of renown.
verses.griffith_verse: Your grace be with us, ye who love sweet juices: further the hymn sung by the poet Māna, When men are joyful in your glorious actions, to win heroic strength, ye Bounteous Givers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एष वां स्तोमो अश्विनावकारि मानेभिर्मघवाना सुवृक्ति ।यातं वर्तिस्तनयाय त्मने चागस्त्ये नासत्या मदंता ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vām ǀ stómaḥ ǀ aśvinau ǀ akāri ǀ mā́nebhiḥ ǀ magha-vānā ǀ su-vṛktí ǀyātám ǀ vartíḥ ǀ tánayāya ǀ tmáne ǀ ca ǀ agástye ǀ nāsatyā ǀ mádantā ǁ
verses.english_translation: This praise was made, O liberal Lords, O Aśvins, for you with fair adornment by the Mānas. Come to our house for us and for our children, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, in Agastya.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, possessors of wealth, this sin-removing hymn has been addressed to you, together with respectful (oblations);Nāsatyasbe favourable to Agastya; come to his dwelling for (conferring on him) progeny, and for his own (good).
verses.griffith_verse: This praise was made, O liberal Lords, O Aśvins, for you with fair adornment by the Mānas. Come to our house for us and for our children, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, in Agastya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतारिष्म तमसस्पारमस्य प्रति वां स्तोमो अश्विनावधायि ।एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयानैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: átāriṣma ǀ támasaḥ ǀ pārám ǀ asyá ǀ práti ǀ vām ǀ stómaḥ ǀ aśvinau ǀ adhāyi ǀā́ ǀ ihá ǀ yātam ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ deva-yā́naiḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: (Through your aid),Aśvins, we cross over the limit of darkness; to you this (our hymn) has been addressed; come hither by the path traversed by thd gods, thatwe may obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: We have passed o’er the limit of this darkness: our praise hath been bestowed on you, O Aśvins. Come hitherward by paths which Gods have travelled. may we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXV. Heaven and Earth.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHETHER of these is elder, whether later? How were they born? Who knoweth it, ye sages?These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward. The Twain uphold, though motionless and footless, a widespread offspring having feet and moving.Like your own son upon his parents’ bosom, protect us, Heaven and earth, from fearful danger. I call for Aditi's unrivalled bounty, perfect, celestial, deathless, meet for worship.Produce this, ye Twain Worlds, for him who lauds you. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. May we be close to both the Worlds who suffer no pain, Parents of Gods, who aid with favour,Both mid the Gods, with Day and Night alternate. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. Faring together, young, with meeting limits, Twin Sisters lying in their Parents’ bosom,Kissing the centre of the world together. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. Duly I call the two wide seats, the mighty, the general Parents, with the God's protection.Who, beautiful to look on, make the nectar. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. Wide, vast, and manifold, whose bounds are distant,—these, reverent, I address at this our worship,The blessed Pair, victorious, all-sustaining. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. What sin we have at any time committed against the Gods, our friend, our house's chieftain,Thereof may this our hymn be expiation. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger. May both these Friends of man, who bless, preserve me, may they attend me with their help and favour.Enrich the man more liberal than the godless. May we, ye Gods, be strong with food rejoicing. Endowed with understanding, I have uttered this truth, for all to hear, to Earth and Heaven.Be near us, keep us from reproach and trouble. Father and Mother, with your help preserve us. Be this my prayer fulfilled, O Earth and Heaven, wherewith, Father and Mother, I address you.Nearest of Gods be ye with your protection. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोः कथा जाते कवयः को वि वेद ।विश्वं त्मना बिभृतो यद्ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ॥
verses.transliteration: katarā́ ǀ pū́rvā ǀ katarā́ ǀ áparā ǀ ayóḥ ǀ kathā́ ǀ jāté íti ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ ví ǀ veda ǀvíśvam ǀ tmánā ǀ bibhṛtaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ nā́ma ǀ ví ǀ vartete íti ǀ áhanī íti ǀ cakríyā-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHETHER of these is elder, whether later? How were they born? Who knoweth it, ye sages? These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward.
verses.wilson_translation: Which of these two, (Heaven and Earth), is prior which posterior; how were they engendered; (declare), sages, who knows this? verily, you uphold the universe of itself, and the days (and nights) revolve as if they had wheels.
verses.griffith_verse: WHETHER of these is elder, whether later? How were they born? Who knoweth it, ye sages? These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरिं द्वे अचरंती चरंतं पद्वंतं गर्भमपदी दधाते ।नित्यं न सूनुं पित्रोरुपस्थे द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́rim ǀ dvé íti ǀ ácarantī íti ǀ cárantam ǀ pat-vántam ǀ gárbham ǀ apádī íti ǀ dadhāte íti ǀnítyam ǀ ná ǀ sūnúm ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Twain uphold, though motionless and footless, a widespread offspring having feet and moving. Like your own son upon his parents’ bosom, protect us, Heaven and earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: Footless and motionless, they sustain numerous moving and footed races, as a son is even (nursed) on the lap of his parents; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).
verses.griffith_verse: The Twain uphold, though motionless and footless, a widespread offspring having feet and moving. Like your own son upon his parents’ bosom, protect us, Heaven and earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनेहो दात्रमदितेरनर्वं हुवे स्वर्वदवधं नमस्वत् ।तद्रोदसी जनयतं जरित्रे द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: aneháḥ ǀ dātrám ǀ áditeḥ ǀ anarvám ǀ huvé ǀ sváḥ-vat ǀ avadhám ǀ námasvat ǀtát ǀ rodasī íti ǀ janayatam ǀ jaritré ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: I call for Aditi's unrivalled bounty, perfect, celestial, deathless, meet for worship. Produce this, ye Twain Worlds, for him who lauds you. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: I solicit of Aditi, wealth, without pain or decay, like heaven (in fullness of enjoyment), exempt from injury, and abounding in food; grant, Heaven and Earth, such wealth to him who praises you; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).
verses.griffith_verse: I call for Aditi's unrivalled bounty, perfect, celestial, deathless, meet for worship. Produce this, ye Twain Worlds, for him who lauds you. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अतप्यमाने अवसावंती अनु ष्याम रोदसी देवपुत्रे ।उभे देवानामुभयेभिरह्नां द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: átapyamāne íti ǀ ávasā ǀ ávantī íti ǀ ánu ǀ syāma ǀ ródasī íti ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀubhé íti ǀ devā́nām ǀ ubháyebhiḥ ǀ áhnām ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we be close to both the Worlds who suffer no pain, Parents of Gods, who aid with favour, Both mid the Gods, with Day and Night alternate. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: May we ever be (devoted to) that Heaven and Earth, who are not subject to annoyance, who satisfy (all beings) with food, who have the gods (and men) for sons, and who are both endowed with the double (condition) of the divine days (and nights); defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).
verses.griffith_verse: May we be close to both the Worlds who suffer no pain, Parents of Gods, who aid with favour, Both mid the Gods, with Day and Night alternate. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: संगच्छमाने युवती समंते स्वसारा जामी पित्रोरुपस्थे ।अभिजिघ्रंती भुवनस्य नाभिं द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: saṃgácchamāne íti sam-gácchamāne ǀ yuvatī́ íti ǀ sámante íti sám-ante ǀ svásārā ǀ jāmī́ íti ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀabhijíghrantī ítyabhi-jíghrantī ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ nā́bhim ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Faring together, young, with meeting limits, Twin Sisters lying in their Parents’ bosom, Kissing the centre of the world together. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: Going always together, equally young, and of the like termination, sisters, and kindred, and scenting the navel of the world, plural ced on their lap as its parents; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.
verses.griffith_verse: Faring together, young, with meeting limits, Twin Sisters lying in their Parents’ bosom, Kissing the centre of the world together. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उर्वी सद्मनी बृहती ऋतेन हुवे देवानामवसा जनित्री ।दधाते ये अमृतं सुप्रतीके द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: urvī́ íti ǀ sádmanī íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ ṛténa ǀ huvé ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávasā ǀ jánitrī íti ǀdadhā́te íti ǀ yé íti ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ suprátīke íti su-prátīke ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Duly I call the two wide seats, the mighty, the general Parents, with the God's protection. Who, beautiful to look on, make the nectar. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke to the sacrifice, for the preservation of gods (and men), the two vast, all-supporting, and mighty parents (of the rain and corn); who, beautiful in form, sustain ambrosial (showers); defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.
verses.griffith_verse: Duly I call the two wide seats, the mighty, the general Parents, with the God's protection. Who, beautiful to look on, make the nectar. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उर्वी पृथ्वी बहुले दूरेअंते उप ब्रुवे नमसा यज्ञे अस्मिन् ।दधाते ये सुभगे सुप्रतूर्ती द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: urvī́ íti ǀ pṛthvī́ íti ǀ bahulé íti ǀ dūréante íti dūré-ante ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀ námasā ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀdadhā́te íti ǀ yé íti ǀ subháge íti su-bháge ǀ suprátūrtī íti su-prátūrtī ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wide, vast, and manifold, whose bounds are distant,—these, reverent, I address at this our worship, The blessed Pair, victorious, all-sustaining. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify with reverence, at this sacrifice, (the two), who are vast, expansive, multiform, infinite, auspicious;who support (all beings) by their bounty; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.
verses.griffith_verse: Wide, vast, and manifold, whose bounds are distant,—these, reverent, I address at this our worship, The blessed Pair, victorious, all-sustaining. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवान्वा यच्चकृमा कच्चिदागः सखायं वा सदमिज्जास्पतिं वा ।इयं धीर्भूया अवयानमेषां द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́n ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ cakṛmá ǀ kát ǀ cit ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ sákhāyam ǀ vā ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ jā́ḥ-patim ǀ vā ǀiyám ǀ dhī́ḥ ǀ bhūyāḥ ǀ ava-yā́nam ǀ eṣām ǀ dyā́vā ǀ rákṣatam ǀ pṛthivī íti ǀ naḥ ǀ ábhvāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: What sin we have at any time committed against the Gods, our friend, our house's chieftain, Thereof may this our hymn be expiation. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.wilson_translation: May this sacrifice be the means of expiating those offences which we may have committed against the gods, against a friend at any time, against a son-in-law; defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.
verses.griffith_verse: What sin we have at any time committed against the Gods, our friend, our house's chieftain, Thereof may this our hymn be expiation. Protect us, Heaven and Earth, from fearful danger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उभा शंसा नर्या मामविष्टामुभे मामूती अवसा सचेतां ।भूरि चिदर्यः सुदास्तरायेषा मदंत इषयेम देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhā́ ǀ śáṃsā ǀ náryā ǀ mā́m ǀ aviṣṭām ǀ ubhé íti ǀ mā́m ǀ ūtī́ íti ǀ ávasā ǀ sacetām ǀbhū́ri ǀ cit ǀ aryáḥ ǀ sudā́ḥ-tarāya ǀ iṣā́ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ iṣayema ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May both these Friends of man, who bless, preserve me, may they attend me with their help and favour. Enrich the man more liberal than the godless. May we, ye Gods, be strong with food rejoicing.
verses.wilson_translation: May both these, accepting praise, and friendly to man, be favourable to me; may they both be associated as guardians for my protection; deities, we your adorers, propitiating you with (sacrificial) food, desire ample (wealth), for the sake of makign liberal donations.
verses.griffith_verse: May both these Friends of man, who bless, preserve me, may they attend me with their help and favour. Enrich the man more liberal than the godless. May we, ye Gods, be strong with food rejoicing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतं दिवे तदवोचं पृथिव्या अभिश्रावाय प्रथमं सुमेधाः ।पातामवद्याद्दुरितादभीके पिता माता च रक्षतामवोभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtám ǀ divé ǀ tát ǀ avocam ǀ pṛthivyái ǀ abhi-śrāvā́ya ǀ prathamám ǀ su-medhā́ḥ ǀpātā́m ǀ avadyā́t ǀ duḥ-itā́t ǀ abhī́ke ǀ pitā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ ca ǀ rakṣatām ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Endowed with understanding, I have uttered this truth, for all to hear, to Earth and Heaven. Be near us, keep us from reproach and trouble. Father and Mother, with your help preserve us.
verses.wilson_translation: Endowed with understanding, I repeat to Heaven and Earth this initial praise, to be heard around; may paternal (heaven) and maternal (earth) preserve us from reprehensible iniquity; and ever nigh defend us with their protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Endowed with understanding, I have uttered this truth, for all to hear, to Earth and Heaven. Be near us, keep us from reproach and trouble. Father and Mother, with your help preserve us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं द्यावापृथिवी सत्यमस्तु पितर्मातर्यदिहोपब्रुवे वां ।भूतं देवानामवमे अवोभिर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ satyám ǀ astu ǀ pítaḥ ǀ mā́taḥ ǀ yát ǀ ihá ǀ upa-bruvé ǀ vām ǀbhūtám ǀ devā́nām ǀ avamé íti ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be this my prayer fulfilled, O Earth and Heaven, wherewith, Father and Mother, I address you. Nearest of Gods be ye with your protection. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: May this (hymn), Heaven and Earth,be successful; (the hymn) which, Father and Mother, I repeat to you both on this occasion; be ever with your protection in the proximity of those who praise you; that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Be this my prayer fulfilled, O Earth and Heaven, wherewith, Father and Mother, I address you. Nearest of Gods be ye with your protection. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LOVED of all men, may Savitar, through praises offered as sacred food, come to our synod,That you too, through-our hymn, ye ever-youthful, may gladden, at your visit, all our people. To us may all the Gods come trooped together, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa concordant,That all may be promoters of our welfare, and with great might preserve our strength from slackness. Agni I sing, the guest you love most dearly: the Conqueror through our lauds is friendly-minded.That he may be our Varuṇa rich in glory and send food like a prince praised by the godly. To you I seek with reverence, Night and Morning, like a cow good to milk, with hope to conquer,Preparing on a common day the praise. song with milk of various hues within this udder. May the great Dragon of the Deep rejoice us: as one who nourishes her young comes Sindhu,With whom we will incite the Child of Waters whom vigorous course swift as thought bring hither. Moreover Tvaṣṭar also shall approach us, one-minded with the princes at his visit.Hither shall come the Vṛtra-slayer Indra, Ruler of men, as strongest of the Heroes. Him too our hymns delight, that yoke swift horses, like mother cows who lick their tender youngling.To him our songs shall yield themselves like spouses, to him the most delightful of the Heroes. So may the Maruts, armed with mighty weapons, rest here on heaven and earth with hearts in concord,As Gods whose cars have dappled steeds like torrents, destroyers of the foe allies of Mitra. They hasten on to happy termination their orders when they are made known byglory.As on a fair bright day the arrow flieth o’er all the barren soil their missiles sparkle. Incline the Aśvins to show grace, and Pūṣan, for power and might have they, their own possession.Friendly are Viṣṇu, Vāta, and Ṛbhukṣan so may I bring the Gods to make us happy. This is my reverent thought of you, ye Holy; may it inspire you, make you dwell among us,—Thought, toiling for the Gods and seeking treasure. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: आ न इळाभिर्विदथे सुशस्ति विश्वानरः सविता देव एतु ।अपि यथा युवानो मत्सथा नो विश्वं जगदभिपित्वे मनीषा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ íḷābhiḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ su-śastí ǀ viśvā́naraḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ etu ǀápi ǀ yáthā ǀ yuvānaḥ ǀ mátsatha ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ jágat ǀ abhi-pitvé ǀ manīṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LOVED of all men, may Savitar, through praises offered as sacred food, come to our synod, That you too, through-our hymn, ye ever-youthful, may gladden, at your visit, all our people.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitā, the benefactor of all men, come benignantly to our solemnity, together with the divinities of earth, and do you, who are (always) young, willingly present at our sacrifice, exhilarate us, as (you exhilarate) the whole world.
verses.griffith_verse: LOVED of all men, may Savitar, through praises offered as sacred food, come to our synod, That you too, through-our hymn, ye ever-youthful, may gladden, at your visit, all our people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो विश्व आस्क्रा गमंतु देवा मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणः सजोषाः ।भुवन्यथा नो विश्वे वृधासः करन्त्सुषाहा विथुरं न शवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ā́skrāḥ ǀ gamantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀbhúvan ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ vṛdhā́saḥ ǀ káran ǀ su-sáhā ǀ vithurám ǀ ná ǀ śávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To us may all the Gods come trooped together, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa concordant, That all may be promoters of our welfare, and with great might preserve our strength from slackness.
verses.wilson_translation: May all the triumphant gods,Mitra,Aryaman,Varuṇaequally well plural ased, come (to our rite); may they all be propitious to us; may they not leave us in want of food, after overcoming (our foes).
verses.griffith_verse: To us may all the Gods come trooped together, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa concordant, That all may be promoters of our welfare, and with great might preserve our strength from slackness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेष्ठं वो अतिथिं गृणीषेऽग्निं शस्तिभिस्तुर्वणिः सजोषाः ।असद्यथा नो वरुणः सुकीर्तिरिषश्च पर्षदरिगूर्तः सूरिः ॥
verses.transliteration: préṣṭham ǀ vaḥ ǀ átithim ǀ gṛṇīṣe ǀ agním ǀ śastí-bhiḥ ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀásat ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ su-kīrtíḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ ca ǀ parṣat ǀ ari-gūrtáḥ ǀ sūríḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni I sing, the guest you love most dearly: the Conqueror through our lauds is friendly-minded. That he may be our Varuṇa rich in glory and send food like a prince praised by the godly.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise with hymns, (O gods), your best beloved guest,Agni, who is prompt (to partake of the oblation) and who is well plural ased along (with you); so that (thereby)Varuṇa, the possessor of renown, the subduer of foes, the animator (of men), may fill us with food.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni I sing, the guest you love most dearly: the Conqueror through our lauds is friendly-minded. That he may be our Varuṇa rich in glory and send food like a prince praised by the godly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप व एषे नमसा जिगीषोषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः ।समाने अहन्विमिमानो अर्कं विषुरूपे पयसि सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣe ǀ námasā ǀ jigīṣā́ ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ sudúghā-iva ǀ dhenúḥ ǀsamāné ǀ áhan ǀ vi-mímānaḥ ǀ arkám ǀ víṣu-rūpe ǀ páyasi ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you I seek with reverence, Night and Morning, like a cow good to milk, with hope to conquer, Preparing on a common day the praise. song with milk of various hues within this udder.
verses.wilson_translation: I approach you, (deities), with reverence, night and day, in the hope of overcoming (sin), as (willingly), as a genitive tle cow (comes to be milked), mixing (for you) on the appropriate day the (sacrificial) food, (consisting) of multiform (preparations) of milk (genitive rated) from the same udder.
verses.griffith_verse: To you I seek with reverence, Night and Morning, like a cow good to milk, with hope to conquer, Preparing on a common day the praise. song with milk of various hues within this udder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो मयस्कः शिशुं न पिप्युषीव वेति सिंधुः ।येन नपातमपां जुनाम मनोजुवो वृषणो यं वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ áhiḥ ǀ budhnyáḥ ǀ máyaḥ ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀ śíśum ǀ ná ǀ pipyúṣī-iva ǀ veti ǀ síndhuḥ ǀyéna ǀ nápātam ǀ apā́m ǀ junā́ma ǀ manaḥ-júvaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ yám ǀ váhanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the great Dragon of the Deep rejoice us: as one who nourishes her young comes Sindhu, With whom we will incite the Child of Waters whom vigorous course swift as thought bring hither.
verses.wilson_translation: May,Ahirbudhnyagrant us happiness; may Sindhucome, nourishing us as a (cow her) calf, whereby we may propitiate the grandson of the waters, (Agni), whom the clouds, swift as thought, convey.
verses.griffith_verse: May the great Dragon of the Deep rejoice us: as one who nourishes her young comes Sindhu, With whom we will incite the Child of Waters whom vigorous course swift as thought bring hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत न ईं त्वष्टा गंत्वच्छा स्मत्सूरिभिरभिपित्वे सजोषाः ।आ वृत्रहेंद्रश्चर्षणिप्रास्तुविष्टमो नरां न इह गम्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ īm ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ ā́ ǀ gantu ǀ áccha ǀ smát ǀ sūrí-bhiḥ ǀ abhi-pitvé ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ carṣaṇi-prā́ḥ ǀ tuvíḥ-tamaḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ naḥ ǀ ihá ǀ gámyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Moreover Tvaṣṭar also shall approach us, one-minded with the princes at his visit. Hither shall come the Vṛtra-slayer Indra, Ruler of men, as strongest of the Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Or may Tvaṣṭācome to this sacrifice, equally well plural ased with those who praise (him) at the excellent (rite) at which he is present; may the most potent Indra, the protector of man, the destroyer of Vṛtra, come to the (solemnity) of our leaders.
verses.griffith_verse: Moreover Tvaṣṭar also shall approach us, one-minded with the princes at his visit. Hither shall come the Vṛtra-slayer Indra, Ruler of men, as strongest of the Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत न ईं मतयोऽश्वयोगाः शिशुं न गावस्तरुणं रिहंति ।तमीं गिरो जनयो न पत्नीः सुरभिष्टमं नरां नसंत ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ īm ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ áśva-yogāḥ ǀ śíśum ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ táruṇam ǀ rihanti ǀtám ǀ īm ǀ gíraḥ ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ surabhíḥ-tamam ǀ narā́m ǀ nasanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him too our hymns delight, that yoke swift horses, like mother cows who lick their tender youngling. To him our songs shall yield themselves like spouses, to him the most delightful of the Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: For our minds, yoked together like horses tend to the ever youthful Indra, as cows to their calves; and the praises of men, (addressed) to him, are genitive rating most fragrant (fruit), as wives bear (children to their husbands).
verses.griffith_verse: Him too our hymns delight, that yoke swift horses, like mother cows who lick their tender youngling. To him our songs shall yield themselves like spouses, to him the most delightful of the Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत न ईं मरुतो वृद्धसेनाः स्मद्रोदसी समनसः सदंतु ।पृषदश्वासोऽवनयो न रथा रिशादसो मित्रयुजो न देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ īm ǀ marútaḥ ǀ vṛddhá-senāḥ ǀ smát ǀ ródasī íti ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ sadantu ǀpṛ́ṣat-aśvāsaḥ ǀ avánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ mitra-yújaḥ ǀ ná ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may the Maruts, armed with mighty weapons, rest here on heaven and earth with hearts in concord, As Gods whose cars have dappled steeds like torrents, destroyers of the foe allies of Mitra.
verses.wilson_translation: Or may the Maruts, being of one mind, come from heaven and earth (to the sacrifice); they who are a mighty host, who have parti-coloured steeds, who are like protecting chariots, and who are devourers of foes may they come like friendly deities.
verses.griffith_verse: So may the Maruts, armed with mighty weapons, rest here on heaven and earth with hearts in concord, As Gods whose cars have dappled steeds like torrents, destroyers of the foe allies of Mitra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नु यदेषां महिना चिकित्रे प्र युंजते प्रयुजस्ते सुवृक्ति ।अध यदेषां सुदिने न शरुर्विश्वमेरिणं प्रुषायंत सेनाः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ mahinā́ ǀ cikitré ǀ prá ǀ yuñjate ǀ pra-yújaḥ ǀ té ǀ su-vṛktí ǀádha ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ su-díne ǀ ná ǀ śáruḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ íriṇam ǀ pruṣāyánta ǀ sénāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They hasten on to happy termination their orders when they are made known by glory. As on a fair bright day the arrow flieth o’er all the barren soil their missiles sparkle.
verses.wilson_translation: For, verily, their greatness is well known, (as) they diligently discharge their functions; by which their spot pours rain upon every arid soil, as light spreads (universally) on a fine day.
verses.griffith_verse: They hasten on to happy termination their orders when they are made known by glory. As on a fair bright day the arrow flieth o’er all the barren soil their missiles sparkle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रो अश्विनाववसे कृणुध्वं प्र पूषणं स्वतवसो हि संति ।अद्वेषो विष्णुर्वात ऋभुक्षा अच्छा सुम्नाय ववृतीय देवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: pró íti ǀ aśvínau ǀ ávase ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ prá ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ svá-tavasaḥ ǀ hí ǀ sánti ǀadveṣáḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ áccha ǀ sumnā́ya ǀ vavṛtīya ǀ devā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Incline the Aśvins to show grace, and Pūṣan, for power and might have they, their own possession. Friendly are Viṣṇu, Vāta, and Ṛbhukṣan so may I bring the Gods to make us happy.
verses.wilson_translation: Propitiate the Aśvinsand Pūṣan, for my protection; (propitiate) those (deities), who are of independent powers, as Viṣṇu, devoid of hatred,VāyuandṚbhukṣin, and may I influence the gods to be present for my felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Incline the Aśvins to show grace, and Pūṣan, for power and might have they, their own possession. Friendly are Viṣṇu, Vāta, and Ṛbhukṣan so may I bring the Gods to make us happy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं सा वो अस्मे दीधितिर्यजत्रा अपिप्राणी च सदनी च भूयाः ।नि या देवेषु यतते वसूयुर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ sā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ dī́dhitiḥ ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀ api-prā́ṇī ǀ ca ǀ sádanī ǀ ca ǀ bhūyāḥ ǀní ǀ yā́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ yátate ǀ vasu-yúḥ ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is my reverent thought of you, ye Holy; may it inspire you, make you dwell among us,— Thought, toiling for the Gods and seeking treasure. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: Objects of admiration, may that wealth-abounding effulgence which manifests itself amongst the gods, give animation to our existence, and (permanence to) our dwellings; that we may (thence) obtain food, strength, and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: This is my reverent thought of you, ye Holy; may it inspire you, make you dwell among us,— Thought, toiling for the Gods and seeking treasure. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVII. Praise of Food.
hymns.anukramani: ११ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः । अन्नं। १अनुष्टुब्गर्भा उष्णिक्, ३, ५-७, ११ अनुष्टुप्,११ बृहती वा, २, ४, ८-१० गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now will I glorify Food that upholds great strength,By whose invigorating power Trita rent Vṛtra limb from limb. O pleasant Food, O Food of meath, thee have we chosen for our own,So be our kind protector thou. Come hitherward to us, O Food, auspicious with auspicious help,Health-bringing, not unkind, a dear and guileless friend. These juices which, O Food, are thine throughout the regions are diffused.like winds they have their place in heaven. These gifts of thine, O Food, O Food most sweet to taste,These savours of thy juices work like creatures that have mighty necks. In thee, O Food, is set the spirit of great Gods.Under thy flag brave deeds were done he slew the Dragon with thy help. If thou be gone unto the splendour of the clouds,Even from thence, O Food of meath, prepared for our enjoyment, come. Whatever morsel we consume from waters or from plants of earth, O Soma, wax thou fat thereby. What Soma, we enjoy from thee in milky food or barley-brew, Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby. O Vegetable, Cake of meal, he wholesome, firm, and strengthening: Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby. O Food, from thee as such have we drawn forth with lauds, like cows, our sacrificial gifts,From thee who banquetest with Gods, from thee who banquetest with us.

verses.sanskrit: पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीं ।यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: pitúm ǀ nú ǀ stoṣam ǀ maháḥ ǀ dharmā́ṇam ǀ táviṣīm ǀyásya ǀ tritáḥ ǀ ví ǀ ójasā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ví-parvam ǀ ardáyat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now will I glorify Food that upholds great strength, By whose invigorating power Trita rent Vṛtra limb from limb.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify Pitu, the great, the upholder, the strong, by whose invigorating power Tritaslew themutilated Vṛtra.
verses.griffith_verse: Now will I glorify Food that upholds great strength, By whose invigorating power Trita rent Vṛtra limb from limb.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वादो पितो मधो पितो वयं त्वा ववृमहे ।अस्माकमविता भव ॥
verses.transliteration: svā́do íti ǀ pito íti ǀ mádho íti ǀ pito íti ǀ vayám ǀ tvā ǀ vavṛmahe ǀasmā́kam ǀ avitā́ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: O pleasant Food, O Food of meath, thee have we chosen for our own, So be our kind protector thou.
verses.wilson_translation: Savoury Pitā; sweet pitā; we worship you; become our protector.
verses.griffith_verse: O pleasant Food, O Food of meath, thee have we chosen for our own, So be our kind protector thou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप नः पितवा चर शिवः शिवाभिरूतिभिः ।मयोभुरद्विषेण्यः सखा सुशेवो अद्वयाः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ pito íti ǀ ā́ ǀ cara ǀ śiváḥ ǀ śivā́bhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀmayaḥ-bhúḥ ǀ adviṣeṇyáḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ su-śévaḥ ǀ ádvayāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hitherward to us, O Food, auspicious with auspicious help, Health-bringing, not unkind, a dear and guileless friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us,Pitā, auspicious with auspicious aids; a source of delight;not unpalatable; a friend well respected, and having none (but agreeable properties).
verses.griffith_verse: Come hitherward to us, O Food, auspicious with auspicious help, Health-bringing, not unkind, a dear and guileless friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तव त्ये पितो रसा रजांस्यनु विष्ठिताः ।दिवि वाता इव श्रिताः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tyé ǀ pito íti ǀ rásāḥ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ ánu ǀ ví-sthitāḥ ǀdiví ǀ vā́tāḥ-iva ǀ śritā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These juices which, O Food, are thine throughout the regions are diffused. like winds they have their place in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Your flavours,Pitā, are diffused through the regions, as the winds are spread through the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: These juices which, O Food, are thine throughout the regions are diffused. like winds they have their place in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तव त्ये पितो ददतस्तव स्वादिष्ठ ते पितो ।प्र स्वाद्मानो रसानां तुविग्रीवा इवेरते ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tyé ǀ pito íti ǀ dádataḥ ǀ táva ǀ svādiṣṭha ǀ té ǀ pito íti ǀprá ǀ svādmā́naḥ ǀ rásānām ǀ tuvigrī́vāḥ-iva ǀ īrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: These gifts of thine, O Food, O Food most sweet to taste, These savours of thy juices work like creatures that have mighty necks.
verses.wilson_translation: Those (men),Pitā, (are the enjoyers of your bounty), who are your distributors, most sweet Pitā, (to others); they who are the relishers of your flavours, are as if they had stiff necks.
verses.griffith_verse: These gifts of thine, O Food, O Food most sweet to taste, These savours of thy juices work like creatures that have mighty necks.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे पितो महानां देवानां मनो हितं ।अकारि चारु केतुना तवाहिमवसावधीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ pito íti ǀ mahā́nām ǀ devā́nām ǀ mánaḥ ǀ hitám ǀákāri ǀ cā́ru ǀ ketúnā ǀ táva ǀ áhim ǀ ávasā ǀ avadhīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: In thee, O Food, is set the spirit of great Gods. Under thy flag brave deeds were done he slew the Dragon with thy help.
verses.wilson_translation: The thoughts of the mighty gods are fixed,Pitā, upon you; by your kind and intelligent assistance, (Indra) slew Ahi.
verses.griffith_verse: In thee, O Food, is set the spirit of great Gods. Under thy flag brave deeds were done he slew the Dragon with thy help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यददो पितो अजगन्विवस्व पर्वतानां ।अत्रा चिन्नो मधो पितोऽरं भक्षाय गम्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ adáḥ ǀ pito íti ǀ ájagan ǀ vivásva ǀ párvatānām ǀátra ǀ cit ǀ naḥ ǀ madho íti ǀ pito íti ǀ áram ǀ bhakṣā́ya ǀ gamyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: If thou be gone unto the splendour of the clouds, Even from thence, O Food of meath, prepared for our enjoyment, come.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Pitā, this (product) of the water-wealthy clouds, (the rain), arrives; then do you, sweet Pitā, be athandwith sufficiency for our eating.
verses.griffith_verse: If thou be gone unto the splendour of the clouds, Even from thence, O Food of meath, prepared for our enjoyment, come.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदपामोषधीनां परिंशमारिशामहे ।वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ apā́m ǀ óṣadhīnām ǀ pariṃśám ǀ ā-riśā́mahe ǀvā́tāpe ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever morsel we consume from waters or from plants of earth, O Soma, wax thou fat thereby.
verses.wilson_translation: And since we enjoy the abundance of the waters and the plural nts; therefore, Body, do you grow fat.
verses.griffith_verse: Whatever morsel we consume from waters or from plants of earth, O Soma, wax thou fat thereby.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते सोम गवाशिरो यवाशिरो भजामहे ।वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ soma ǀ gó-āśiraḥ ǀ yáva-āśiraḥ ǀ bhájāmahe ǀvā́tāpe ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: What Soma, we enjoy from thee in milky food or barley-brew, Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.wilson_translation: And since we enjoy,Soma, your mixture with boiled milk or boiled barley; therefore, Body, do you grow fat.
verses.griffith_verse: What Soma, we enjoy from thee in milky food or barley-brew, Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: करंभ ओषधे भव पीवो वृक्क उदारथिः ।वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥
verses.transliteration: karambháḥ ǀ oṣadhe ǀ bhava ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ vṛkkáḥ ǀ udārathíḥ ǀvā́tāpe ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Vegetable, Cake of meal, he wholesome, firm, and strengthening: Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.wilson_translation: Vegetable cake of fried meal, do you be substantial, wholesome, and invigorating; and, Body, do you grow fat.
verses.griffith_verse: O Vegetable, Cake of meal, he wholesome, firm, and strengthening: Vātāpi, grow thou fat thereby.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा वयं पितो वचोभिर्गावो न हव्या सुषूदिम ।देवेभ्यस्त्वा सधमादमस्मभ्यं त्वा सधमादं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ pito íti ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ havyā́ ǀ susūdima ǀdevébhyaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǀ asmábhyam ǀ tvā ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Food, from thee as such have we drawn forth with lauds, like cows, our sacrificial gifts, From thee who banquetest with Gods, from thee who banquetest with us.
verses.wilson_translation: We extract from you,Pitā, by our praises, (the sacrificial food), as cows yield butter for oblation; from you, who are exhilarating to the gods; exhilarating also to us.
verses.griffith_verse: O Food, from thee as such have we drawn forth with lauds, like cows, our sacrificial gifts, From thee who banquetest with Gods, from thee who banquetest with us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVIII. Āprīs.
hymns.anukramani: ११ अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः । आप्रीसूक्तं-(१ इध्मः समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा, २ तनूनपात् ३ इळः, ४ बर्हिः, ५ देवीर्द्वारः, ६ उषा सानक्ता, ७ दैव्यौ होतारौ प्रचेतसौ, ८ तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः, ९ त्वष्टा, १० वनस्पतिः, ११ स्वाहाकृतयः)। गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WINNER of thousands, kindled, thou shinest a God with Gods to-day.Bear out oblations, envoy, Sage. Child of Thyself the sacrifice is for the righteous blent with meath,Presenting viands thousandfold. Invoked and worthy of our praise bring Gods whose due is sacrifice:Thou, Agni, givest countless gifts. To seat a thousand Heroes they eastward have strewn the grass with might,Whereon, Ādityas, ye shine forth. The sovran all-imperial Doors, wide, good, many and manifold,Have poured their streams of holy oil. With gay adornment, fair to see, in glorious beauty shine they forth:Let Night and Morning rest them here. Let these two Sages first of all, heralds divine and eloquent,Perform for us this sacrifice. You I address, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī, and Iḷā, all:Urge ye us on to glorious fame. Tvaṣṭar the Lord hath made all forms and all the cattle of the fieldCause them to multiply for us. Send to the Gods, Vanaspati, thyself, the sacrificial draught:Let Agni make the oblations sweet. Agni, preceder of the Gods, is honoured with the sacred song:He glows at offerings blest with Hail!

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धो अद्य राजसि देवो देवैः सहस्रजित् ।दूतो हव्या कविर्वह ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ rājasi ǀ deváḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ sahasra-jit ǀdūtáḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ vaha ǁ
verses.english_translation: WINNER of thousands, kindled, thou shinest a God with Gods to-day. Bear out oblations, envoy, Sage.
verses.wilson_translation: You shine today, divine conqueror of thousands, kindled by the priests; do you, who are the sapient messenger (of the gods), convey (to them) our oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: WINNER of thousands, kindled, thou shinest a God with Gods to-day. Bear out oblations, envoy, Sage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तनूनपादृतं यते मध्वा यज्ञः समज्यते ।दधत्सहस्रिणीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: tánū-napāt ǀ ṛtám ǀ yaté ǀ mádhvā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ sám ǀ ajyate ǀdádhat ǀ sahasríṇīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Child of Thyself the sacrifice is for the righteous blent with meath, Presenting viands thousandfold.
verses.wilson_translation: The adorable Tanūnapātproceeds to the rite and combines with the oblation, bearing (for the sacrificer) infinite (abundance of) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Child of Thyself the sacrifice is for the righteous blent with meath, Presenting viands thousandfold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आजुह्वानो न ईड्यो देवाँ आ वक्षि यज्ञियान् ।अग्ने सहस्रसा असि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-júhvānaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣi ǀ yajñíyān ǀágne ǀ sahasra-sā́ḥ ǀ asi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invoked and worthy of our praise bring Gods whose due is sacrifice: Thou, Agni, givest countless gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are to be glorified, bring hither, being invoked by us, the adorable gods, for you are the donor of thousands.
verses.griffith_verse: Invoked and worthy of our praise bring Gods whose due is sacrifice: Thou, Agni, givest countless gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्तृणन् ।यत्रादित्या विराजथ ॥
verses.transliteration: prācī́nam ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ sahásra-vīram ǀ astṛṇan ǀyátra ǀ ādityāḥ ǀ vi-rā́jatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: To seat a thousand Heroes they eastward have strewn the grass with might, Whereon, Ādityas, ye shine forth.
verses.wilson_translation: By the power (of their prayers) they have strewn the sacred grass, the seat of numerous heroes, pointing to the east; on which,Ādityas, you are manifest.
verses.griffith_verse: To seat a thousand Heroes they eastward have strewn the grass with might, Whereon, Ādityas, ye shine forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विराट् सम्राड्विभ्वीः प्रभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च याः ।दुरो घृतान्यक्षरन् ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-rā́ṭ ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ vi-bhvī́ḥ ǀ pra-bhvī́ḥ ǀ bahvī́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhū́yasīḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́ḥ ǀdúraḥ ǀ ghṛtā́ni ǀ akṣaran ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sovran all-imperial Doors, wide, good, many and manifold, Have poured their streams of holy oil.
verses.wilson_translation: They have sprinkled water on the doors (of the hall of sacrifice), which are variously and perfectly radiant, manifold, excellent, many, and numerous.
verses.griffith_verse: The sovran all-imperial Doors, wide, good, many and manifold, Have poured their streams of holy oil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुरुक्मे हि सुपेशसाधि श्रिया विराजतः ।उषासावेह सीदतां ॥
verses.transliteration: surukmé íti su-rukmé ǀ hí ǀ su-péśasā ǀ ádhi ǀ śriyā́ ǀ vi-rā́jataḥ ǀuṣásau ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ sīdatām ǁ
verses.english_translation: With gay adornment, fair to see, in glorious beauty shine they forth: Let Night and Morning rest them here.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the brilliant and beautiful Day and Night, who shine with surpassing lustre, sit down here (upon the sacred grass).
verses.griffith_verse: With gay adornment, fair to see, in glorious beauty shine they forth: Let Night and Morning rest them here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रथमा हि सुवाचसा होतारा दैव्या कवी ।यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं ॥
verses.transliteration: prathamā́ ǀ hí ǀ su-vā́casā ǀ hótārā ǀ dáivyā ǀ kavī́ íti ǀyajñám ǀ naḥ ǀ yakṣatām ǀ imám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let these two Sages first of all, heralds divine and eloquent, Perform for us this sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Let these two chief, well-spoken, divine sages, the invokers (of the gods), perform this our sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Let these two Sages first of all, heralds divine and eloquent, Perform for us this sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भारतीळे सरस्वति या वः सर्वा उपब्रुवे ।ता नश्चोदयत श्रिये ॥
verses.transliteration: bhā́rati ǀ íḷe ǀ sárasvati ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ upa-bruvé ǀtā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ codayata ǀ śriyé ǁ
verses.english_translation: You I address, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī, and Iḷā, all: Urge ye us on to glorious fame.
verses.wilson_translation: Bhāratī, Iḷā,Sarasvatī, I invoke you all, that you may direct us to prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: You I address, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī, and Iḷā, all: Urge ye us on to glorious fame.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्त्समानजे ।तेषां नः स्फातिमा यज ॥
verses.transliteration: tváṣṭā ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ hí ǀ pra-bhúḥ ǀ paśū́n ǀ víśvān ǀ sam-ānajé ǀtéṣām ǀ naḥ ǀ sphātím ǀ ā́ ǀ yaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tvaṣṭar the Lord hath made all forms and all the cattle of the field Cause them to multiply for us.
verses.wilson_translation: Tvaṣṭā, who is the master (in fashioning) the forms (of beings), has made all animals distinct; grant us, (Tvaṣṭa), their increase.
verses.griffith_verse: Tvaṣṭar the Lord hath made all forms and all the cattle of the field Cause them to multiply for us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप त्मन्या वनस्पते पाथो देवेभ्यः सृज ।अग्निर्हव्यानि सिष्वदत् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ tmányā ǀ vanaspate ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ sṛja ǀagníḥ ǀ havyā́ni ǀ sisvadat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send to the Gods, Vanaspati, thyself, the sacrificial draught: Let Agni make the oblations sweet.
verses.wilson_translation: Vanaspati, deliver of yourself the victim to the gods, so that Agnimay taste the oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: Send to the Gods, Vanaspati, thyself, the sacrificial draught: Let Agni make the oblations sweet.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोगा अग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते ।स्वाहाकृतीषु रोचते ॥
verses.transliteration: puraḥ-gā́ḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ gāyatréṇa ǀ sám ǀ ajyate ǀsvā́hā-kṛtīṣu ǀ rocate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, preceder of the Gods, is honoured with the sacred song: He glows at offerings blest with Hail!
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the preceder of the gods
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, preceder of the Gods, is honoured with the sacred song: He glows at offerings blest with Hail!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BY goodly paths lead us to riches, Agni, God who knowest every sacred duty.Remove the sin that makes us stray and wander. most ample adoration will we bring thee. Lead us anew to happiness, O Agni; lead us beyond all danger and affliction.Be unto us a wide broad ample castle bless, prosper on their way our sons and offspring. Far from us, Agni, put thou all diseases let them strike lauds that have no saving Agni.God, make our home again to be a blessing, with all the Immortal Deities, O Holy. Preserve us, Agni, with perpetual succour, refulgent in the dwelling which thou lovest.O Conqueror, most youthful, let no danger touch him who praises thee to-day or after. Give not us up a prey to sin, O Agni, the greedy enemy that brings us trouble;Not to the fanged that bites, not to the toothless: give not us up, thou Conqueror, to the spoiler. Such as thou art, born after Law, O Agni when lauded give protection to our bodies,From whosoever would reproach or injure: for thou, God, rescuest from all oppression. Thou, well discerning both these classes, comest to men at early morn, O holy Agni.Be thou obedient unto man at evening, to be adorned, as keen, by eager suitors. To him have we addressed our pious speeches, I, Māna's son, to him victorious Agni.May we gain countless riches with the sages. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ।युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमउक्तिं विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ náya ǀ su-páthā ǀ rāyé ǀ asmā́n ǀ víśvāni ǀ deva ǀ vayúnāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀyuyodhí ǀ asmát ǀ juhurāṇám ǀ énaḥ ǀ bhū́yiṣṭhām ǀ te ǀ námaḥ-uktim ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: BY goodly paths lead us to riches, Agni, God who knowest every sacred duty. Remove the sin that makes us stray and wander. most ample adoration will we bring thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, knowing all kinds of knowledge, lead us by good ways to wealth; remove from from us the sun that would force us astray, that we may offer to you most ample adoratioṇ
verses.griffith_verse: BY goodly paths lead us to riches, Agni, God who knowest every sacred duty. Remove the sin that makes us stray and wander. most ample adoration will we bring thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने त्वं पारया नव्यो अस्मान्त्स्वस्तिभिरति दुर्गाणि विश्वा ।पूश्च पृथ्वी बहुला न उर्वी भवा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ tvám ǀ pāraya ǀ návyaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ áti ǀ duḥ-gā́ni ǀ víśvā ǀpū́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ pṛthvī́ ǀ bahulā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ urvī́ ǀ bháva ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lead us anew to happiness, O Agni; lead us beyond all danger and affliction. Be unto us a wide broad ample castle bless, prosper on their way our sons and offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Agni, convey us by the sacred sets (of worship), beyond all evil ways; may our city be spacious; our land be extensive; be the bestower of happiness upon our offspring, upon our sons.
verses.griffith_verse: Lead us anew to happiness, O Agni; lead us beyond all danger and affliction. Be unto us a wide broad ample castle bless, prosper on their way our sons and offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने त्वमस्मद्युयोध्यमीवा अनग्नित्रा अभ्यमंत कृष्टीः ।पुनरस्मभ्यं सुविताय देव क्षां विश्वेभिरमृतेभिर्यजत्र ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ tvám ǀ asmát ǀ yuyodhi ǀ ámīvāḥ ǀ ánagni-trāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ámanta ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀpúnaḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ deva ǀ kṣā́m ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ amṛ́tebhiḥ ǀ yajatra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far from us, Agni, put thou all diseases let them strike lauds that have no saving Agni. God, make our home again to be a blessing, with all the Immortal Deities, O Holy.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, do you remove from us disease, and those men who, unprotected by Agni, are adverse to us; and, adorable divinity (visit) the earth, with all the immortals, for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Far from us, Agni, put thou all diseases let them strike lauds that have no saving Agni. God, make our home again to be a blessing, with all the Immortal Deities, O Holy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरुत प्रिये सदन आ शुशुक्वान् ।मा ते भयं जरितारं यविष्ठ नूनं विदन्मापरं सहस्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: pāhí ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ pāyú-bhiḥ ǀ ájasraiḥ ǀ utá ǀ priyé ǀ sádane ǀ ā́ ǀ śuśukvā́n ǀmā́ ǀ te ǀ bhayám ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ nūnám ǀ vidat ǀ mā́ ǀ aparám ǀ sahasvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Preserve us, Agni, with perpetual succour, refulgent in the dwelling which thou lovest. O Conqueror, most youthful, let no danger touch him who praises thee to-day or after.
verses.wilson_translation: Cherish us,Agni, with incessant bounties; shine always in your favourite abode; let no danger, youngest (of the gods), assails your worshipper today; nor, mighty one, let t assail him any other season.
verses.griffith_verse: Preserve us, Agni, with perpetual succour, refulgent in the dwelling which thou lovest. O Conqueror, most youthful, let no danger touch him who praises thee to-day or after.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो अग्नेऽव सृजो अघायाविष्यवे रिपवे दुच्छुनायै ।मा दत्वते दशते मादते नो मा रीषते सहसावन्परा दाः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ áva ǀ sṛjaḥ ǀ aghā́ya ǀ aviṣyáve ǀ ripáve ǀ ducchúnāyai ǀmā́ ǀ datváte ǀ dáśate ǀ mā́ ǀ adáte ǀ naḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ríṣate ǀ sahasā-van ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give not us up a prey to sin, O Agni, the greedy enemy that brings us trouble; Not to the fanged that bites, not to the toothless: give not us up, thou Conqueror, to the spoiler.
verses.wilson_translation: Abandon us not,Agni, to a wicked, voracious, malevolent foe; (abandon us) not to one who has fangs, and who bites; nor to one without teeth; nor to the malignant; nor give us up, powerful Agni, to disgrace.
verses.griffith_verse: Give not us up a prey to sin, O Agni, the greedy enemy that brings us trouble; Not to the fanged that bites, not to the toothless: give not us up, thou Conqueror, to the spoiler.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि घ त्वावाँ ऋतजात यंसद्गृणानो अग्ने तन्वे वरूथं ।विश्वाद्रिरिक्षोरुत वा निनित्सोरभिह्रुतामसि हि देव विष्पट् ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ gha ǀ tvā́-vān ǀ ṛta-jāta ǀ yaṃsat ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ agne ǀ tanvé ǀ várūtham ǀvíśvāt ǀ ririkṣóḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ ninitsóḥ ǀ abhi-hrútām ǀ ási ǀ hí ǀ deva ǀ viṣpáṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such as thou art, born after Law, O Agni when lauded give protection to our bodies, From whosoever would reproach or injure: for thou, God, rescuest from all oppression.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, born for sacrifice, (a man) praising you, who are excellent, for (the sake of cherishing) his body, becomes such as you are; exempts himself from all who are inclined to harm or revile him; for you, Agni, are the especial adversary of those who do wrong.
verses.griffith_verse: Such as thou art, born after Law, O Agni when lauded give protection to our bodies, From whosoever would reproach or injure: for thou, God, rescuest from all oppression.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ताँ अग्न उभयान्वि विद्वान्वेषि प्रपित्वे मनुषो यजत्र ।अभिपित्वे मनवे शास्यो भूर्मर्मृजेन्य उशिग्भिर्नाक्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tā́m ǀ agne ǀ ubháyān ǀ ví ǀ vidvā́n ǀ véṣi ǀ pra-pitvé ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ yajatra ǀabhi-pitvé ǀ mánave ǀ śā́syaḥ ǀ bhūḥ ǀ marmṛjényaḥ ǀ uśík-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ akráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, well discerning both these classes, comest to men at early morn, O holy Agni. Be thou obedient unto man at evening, to be adorned, as keen, by eager suitors.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Agni, you are sagacious, and in a short time discriminate between both those men (who do and do not worshhip you); approach the worshipper at the proper time, and be compliant (with his wishes); like an instrumental tutor of the rite, (who is directed) by the desires (of the priests).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, well discerning both these classes, comest to men at early morn, O holy Agni. Be thou obedient unto man at evening, to be adorned, as keen, by eager suitors.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवोचाम निवचनान्यस्मिन्मानस्य सूनुः सहसाने अग्नौ ।वयं सहस्रमृषिभिः सनेम विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ávocāma ǀ ni-vácanāni ǀ asmin ǀ mā́nasya ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ sahasāné ǀ agnáu ǀvayám ǀ sahásram ǀ ṛ́ṣi-bhiḥ ǀ sanema ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ iṣám ǀ vṛjánam ǀ jīrá-dānum ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him have we addressed our pious speeches, I, Māna's son, to him victorious Agni. May we gain countless riches with the sages. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: We address our pious prayers to you,Agni, the son of prayer, the subduer of foes; may we procure, by these sacred supplications, infinite wealth, that we may thence obtain food, strength and long life.
verses.griffith_verse: To him have we addressed our pious speeches, I, Māna's son, to him victorious Agni. May we gain countless riches with the sages. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXC. Bṛhaspati.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GLORIFY thou Bṛhaspati, the scatheless, who must be praised with hymns, sweet-tongued and mighty,To whom as leader of the song, resplendent, worthy of lauds, both Gods and mortals listen. On him wait songs according to the season even as a stream of pious men set moving.Bṛhaspati—for he laid out the expanses—was, at the sacrifice, vast Mātariśvan. The praise, the verse that offers adoration, may he bring forth, as the Sun sends his arms out,He who gives daily light through this God's wisdom, strong as a dread wild beast, and inoffensive. His song of praise pervades the earth and heaven: let the wise worshipper draw it, like a courser.These of Bṛhaspati, like hunters' arrows, go to the skies that change their hue like serpents. Those, God, who count thee as a worthless bullock, and, wealthy sinners, live on thee the Bounteous,—On fools like these no blessing thou bestowest: Bṛhaspati, thou punishest the spiteful. Like a fair path is he, where grass is pleasant, though hard to win, a Friend beloved most early.Those who unharmed by enemies behold us, while they would make them bare, stood closely compassed. He to whom songs of praise go forth like torrents, as rivers eddying under banks flow sea-ward—Bṛhaspati the wise, the eager, closely looks upon both, the waters and the vessel. So hath Bṛhaspati, great, strong and mighty, the God exceeding powerful, been brought hither.May he thus lauded give us kine and horses. May we find strengthening food in full abundance.

verses.sanskrit: अनर्वाणं वृषभं मंद्रजिह्वं बृहस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः ।गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आशृण्वंति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ॥
verses.transliteration: anarvā́ṇam ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ mandrá-jihvam ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ vardhaya ǀ návyam ǀ arkáiḥ ǀgāthānyáḥ ǀ su-rúcaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ā-śṛṇvánti ǀ návamānasya ǀ mártāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: GLORIFY thou Bṛhaspati, the scatheless, who must be praised with hymns, sweet-tongued and mighty, To whom as leader of the song, resplendent, worthy of lauds, both Gods and mortals listen.
verses.wilson_translation: (Priests), augment by your hymns Bṛhaspati, who deserts not (his worshipper); the showerer (of benefits) the plural asant-tongued, the adorable; of whom resplendent gods and men, (the ministers) of the instrumental tutor of the sacrifice, emulous in sacred songs, proclaim (the praise).
verses.griffith_verse: GLORIFY thou Bṛhaspati, the scatheless, who must be praised with hymns, sweet-tongued and mighty, To whom as leader of the song, resplendent, worthy of lauds, both Gods and mortals listen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमृत्विया उप वाचः सचंते सर्गो न यो देवयतामसर्जि ।बृहस्पतिः स ह्यंजो वरांसि विभ्वाभवत्समृते मातरिश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ṛtvíyāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vā́caḥ ǀ sacante ǀ sárgaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ deva-yatā́m ǀ ásarji ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ áñjaḥ ǀ várāṃsi ǀ ví-bhvā ǀ ábhavat ǀ sám ǀ ṛté ǀ mātaríśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: On him wait songs according to the season even as a stream of pious men set moving. Bṛhaspati—for he laid out the expanses—was, at the sacrifice, vast Mātariśvan.
verses.wilson_translation: The hymns of the (rainy) season are addressed to him, who is verily the creator (of the rain), and has granted it (to the prayers) of the devout; for that Bṛhaspatiis the manifester (of all), the expansive wind that (dispensing) blessings has been produced for (the diffusion of) water.
verses.griffith_verse: On him wait songs according to the season even as a stream of pious men set moving. Bṛhaspati—for he laid out the expanses—was, at the sacrifice, vast Mātariśvan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपस्तुतिं नमस उद्यतिं च श्लोकं यंसत्सवितेव प्र बाहू ।अस्य क्रत्वाहन्यो यो अस्ति मृगो न भीमो अरक्षसस्तुविष्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa-stutim ǀ námasaḥ ǀ út-yatim ǀ ca ǀ ślókam ǀ yaṃsat ǀ savitā́-iva ǀ prá ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀasyá ǀ krátvā ǀ ahanyáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásti ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ arakṣásaḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǁ
verses.english_translation: The praise, the verse that offers adoration, may he bring forth, as the Sun sends his arms out, He who gives daily light through this God's wisdom, strong as a dread wild beast, and inoffensive.
verses.wilson_translation: He is ready (to accept) the offered praise, the presentation of the homage, the hymn, as the sun (is ready) to put forth his rays; by the acts of him whom therākṣasas(oppose not), the daily (revolving sun) exists, and he is strong as a fearful beast of prey.
verses.griffith_verse: The praise, the verse that offers adoration, may he bring forth, as the Sun sends his arms out, He who gives daily light through this God's wisdom, strong as a dread wild beast, and inoffensive.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः ।मृगाणां न हेतयो यंति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमायाँ अभि द्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ślókaḥ ǀ diví ǀ īyate ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yaṃsat ǀ yakṣa-bhṛ́t ǀ ví-cetāḥ ǀmṛgā́ṇām ǀ ná ǀ hetáyaḥ ǀ yánti ǀ ca ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ bṛ́haspáteḥ ǀ áhi-māyān ǀ abhí ǀ dyū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: His song of praise pervades the earth and heaven: let the wise worshipper draw it, like a courser. These of Bṛhaspati, like hunters' arrows, go to the skies that change their hue like serpents.
