verses.english_translation: Maruts, granters of dwellings, protect us from the malignity of the man who cherishes wolf-like enmity against us; encompass him with your burning diseases; ward off the murderous (weapon) of the devourer.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, granters of dwellings, protect us from the malignity of the man who cherishes wolf-like enmity against us; encompass him with your burning diseases; ward off the murderous (weapon) of the devourer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चित्रं तद्वो मरुतो याम चेकिते पृश्न्या यदूधरप्यापयो दुहुः ।यद्वा निदे नवमानस्य रुद्रियास्त्रितं जराय जुरतामदाभ्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: citrám ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yā́ma ǀ cekite ǀ pṛ́śnyāḥ ǀ yát ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ ápi ǀ āpáyaḥ ǀ duhúḥ ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ nidé ǀ návamānasya ǀ rudriyāḥ ǀ tritám ǀ járāya ǀ juratā́m ǀ adābhyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, your marvellous energy is well known, whereby, seizing the udder of heaven, you milked it (of the rain, destroyed) the reviler of your worshipper, and (came), irresistible sons of Rudra, to Tritafor the destruction of enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, your marvellous energy is well known, whereby, seizing the udder of heaven, you milked it (of the rain, destroyed) the reviler of your worshipper, and (came), irresistible sons of Rudra, to Tritafor the destruction of enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तान्वो महो मरुत एवयाव्नो विष्णोरेषस्य प्रभृथे हवामहे ।हिरण्यवर्णान्ककुहान्यतस्रुचो ब्रह्मण्यंतः शंस्यं राध ईमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́n ǀ vaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ eva-yā́vnaḥ ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ eṣásya ǀ pra-bhṛthé ǀ havāmahe ǀhíraṇya-varṇān ǀ kakuhā́n ǀ yatá-srucaḥ ǀ brahmaṇyántaḥ ǀ śáṃsyam ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you, mighty Maruts, who frequent such sacrifices (as this, to be present) at the offering of the diffusive and desirable (libation); lifting up our ladles, and reciting their praise, we solicit the golden-hued and lofty Maruts for excellent wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you, mighty Maruts, who frequent such sacrifices (as this, to be present) at the offering of the diffusive and desirable (libation); lifting up our ladles, and reciting their praise, we solicit the golden-hued and lofty Maruts for excellent wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते दशग्वाः प्रथमा यज्ञमूहिरे ते नो हिन्वंतूषसो व्युष्टिषु ।उषा न रामीररुणैरपोर्णुते महो ज्योतिषा शुचता गोअर्णसा ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ dáśa-gvāḥ ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ ūhire ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ hinvantu ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀuṣā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ rāmī́ḥ ǀ aruṇáiḥ ǀ ápa ǀ ūrṇute ǀ maháḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ śucatā́ ǀ gó-arṇasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: May they, who, the first celebrators of the ten-months' rite, accomplished this sacrifice, reanimate us at the rising dawn; for as the dawn with purple rays drives away the night, so (do they scatter the darkness) with great, and pure, and mist-dispelling radiance.
verses.wilson_translation: May they, who, the first celebrators of the ten-months' rite, accomplished this sacrifice, reanimate us at the rising dawn; for as the dawn with purple rays drives away the night, so (do they scatter the darkness) with great, and pure, and mist-dispelling radiance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते क्षोणीभिररुणेभिर्नांजिभी रुद्रा ऋतस्य सदनेषु वावृधुः ।निमेघमाना अत्येन पाजसा सुश्चंद्रं वर्णं दधिरे सुपेशसं ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ kṣoṇī́bhiḥ ǀ aruṇébhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ sádaneṣu ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀni-méghamānāḥ ǀ átyena ǀ pā́jasā ǀ su-candrám ǀ várṇam ǀ dadhire ǀ su-péśasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: They, the Rudras, (equipped) with melodious (lutes), and decorated with purple ornaments, exult in the dwellings of the waters; and scattering the clouds with rappid vigour, they are endowed with delightful and beautiful forms.
verses.wilson_translation: They, the Rudras, (equipped) with melodious (lutes), and decorated with purple ornaments, exult in the dwellings of the waters; and scattering the clouds with rappid vigour, they are endowed with delightful and beautiful forms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ताँ इयानो महि वरूथमूतय उप घेदेना नमसा गृणीमसि ।त्रितो न यान्पंच हो��ॄनभिष्टय आववर्तदवरांचक्रियावसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́n ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ máhi ǀ várūtham ǀ ūtáye ǀ úpa ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ enā́ ǀ námasā ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀtritáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́n ǀ páñca ǀ hótṝn ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀ ā-vavártat ǀ ávarān ǀ cakríyā ǀ ávase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Imploring them for ample wealth, and (having recourse to him) for protection, we glorify them with this praise; like the five chief priests whom Tritadetained for the (performance of) the sacrifice, and to protect it with their weapons.
verses.wilson_translation: Imploring them for ample wealth, and (having recourse to him) for protection, we glorify them with this praise; like the five chief priests whom Tritadetained for the (performance of) the sacrifice, and to protect it with their weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यया रध्रं पारयथात्यंहो यया निदो मुंचथ वंदितारं ।अर्वाची सा मरुतो या व ऊतिरो षु वाश्रेव सुमतिर्जिगातु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáyā ǀ radhrám ǀ pāráyatha ǀ áti ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ yáyā ǀ nidáḥ ǀ muñcátha ǀ vanditā́ram ǀarvā́cī ǀ sā́ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ūtíḥ ǀ ó íti ǀ sú ǀ vāśrā́-iva ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ jigātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, may that protection wherewith you convey the worshipper beyond sin, wherewith you rescue the reciter of your praise from the scoffer, be present with us; may your benign disposition tend towards us, like a lowing (cow towards her calf).
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, may that protection wherewith you convey the worshipper beyond sin, wherewith you rescue the reciter of your praise from the scoffer, be present with us; may your benign disposition tend towards us, like a lowing (cow towards her calf).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXV. Son of Waters.
hymns.anukramani: १५ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। अपांनपात्। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . EAGER for spoil my flow of speech I utter: may the Floods' Child accept my songs with favour.Will not the rapid Son of Waters make them lovely, for he it is who shall enjoy them? To him let us address the song well-fashioned, forth from the heart. Shall he not understand it'The friendly Son of Waters by the greatness of Godhead hath produced all things existing. Some floods unite themselves and others join them: die sounding rivers fill one common storehouse.On every side the bright Floods have encompassed the bright resplendent Offspring of the Waters. The never-sullen waters, youthful Maidens, carefully decking, wait on him the youthful.He with bright rays shines forth in splendid beauty, unfed with wood, in waters, oil-enveloped. To him three Dames are offering food to feed him, Goddesses to the God whom none may injure.Within the waters hath he pressed, as hollows, and drinks their milk who now are first made mothers. Here was the horse's birth; his was the sunlight. Save thou our princes from the oppressor's onslaught.Him, indestructible, dwelling at a distance in forts unwrought lies and ill spirits reach not. He, in whose mansion is the teeming Milch-cow, swells the Gods’ nectar and cats noble viands.The Son of Waters, gathering strength in waters, shines for his worshipper to give him treasures. He who in waters with his own pure Godhead shines widely, law-abiding, everlasting—The other worlds are verily his branches, and plants are born of him with all their offspring. The Waters’ Son hath risen, and clothed in lightning ascended up unto the curled cloud's bosom;And bearing with them his supremest glory the Youthful Ones, gold-coloured, move around him. Golden in form is he, like gold to look on, his colour is like gold, the Son of Waters.When he is seated fresh from golden birthplace those who present their gold give food to feed him. This the fair name and this the lovely aspect of him the Waters’ Son increase in secret.Whom here the youthful Maids together kindle, his food is sacred oil of golden colour. Him, nearest Friend of many, will we worship with sacrifice. and reverence and oblation.I make his back to shine, with chips provide him; I offer food and with my songs exalt him. The Bull hath laid his own life-germ Within them. He sucks them as an infant, and they kiss him.He, Son of Waters, of unfading colour, hath entered here as in another's body. While here he dwelleth in sublimest station, resplendent with the rays that never perish,The Waters, bearing oil to feed their offspring, flow, Youthful Ones, in wanderings about him. Agni, I gave good shelter to the people, and to the princes goodly preparation.Blessed is all that Gods regard with favour. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

verses.sanskrit: उपेमसृक्षि वाजयुर्वचस्यां चनो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे ।अपां नपादाशुहेमा कुवित्स सुपेशसस्करति जोषिषद्धि ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ īm ǀ asṛkṣi ǀ vāja-yúḥ ǀ vacasyā́m ǀ cánaḥ ǀ dadhīta ǀ nādyáḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ me ǀapā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ āśu-hémā ǀ kuvít ǀ sáḥ ǀ su-péśasaḥ ǀ karati ǀ jóṣiṣat ǀ hí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desiring food, I put forth this laudatory hymn; may the sounding and swift-moving grandson of the waters bestow abundant food upon me his worshipper; may he make us of goodly appearance, for verily he is propitiated by praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Desiring food, I put forth this laudatory hymn; may the sounding and swift-moving grandson of the waters bestow abundant food upon me his worshipper; may he make us of goodly appearance, for verily he is propitiated by praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं स्वस्मै हृद आ सुतष्टं मंत्रं वोचेम कुविदस्य वेदत् ।अपां नपादसुर्यस्य मह्ना विश्वान्यर्यो भुवना जजान ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ sú ǀ asmai ǀ hṛdáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sú-taṣṭam ǀ mántram ǀ vocema ǀ kuvít ǀ asya ǀ védat ǀapā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ asuryásya ǀ mahnā́ ǀ víśvāni ǀ aryáḥ ǀ bhúvanā ǀ jajāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us address to him the prayer that is conceived in our hearts, and may he fully understand (its purport); for he, the lord, the grandson of the waters, has genitive rated all beings by the greatness of his might.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us address to him the prayer that is conceived in our hearts, and may he fully understand (its purport); for he, the lord, the grandson of the waters, has genitive rated all beings by the greatness of his might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समन्या यंत्युप यंत्यन्याः समानमूर्वं नद्यः पृणंति ।तमू शुचिं शुचयो दीदिवांसमपां नपातं परि तस्थुरापः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ anyā́ḥ ǀ yánti ǀ úpa ǀ yanti ǀ anyā́ḥ ǀ samānám ǀ ūrvám ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ pṛṇanti ǀtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śúcim ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ apā́m ǀ nápātam ǀ pári ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Some waters collect together (from the rain); others, (already collected on earth), unite with them; as rivers, they flow together to propitiate the ocean-fire; the pure waters are gathered round the pure and brilliant grandsons of the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Some waters collect together (from the rain); others, (already collected on earth), unite with them; as rivers, they flow together to propitiate the ocean-fire; the pure waters are gathered round the pure and brilliant grandsons of the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमस्मेरा युवतयो युवानं मर्मृज्यमानाः परि यंत्यापः ।स शुक्रेभिः शिक्वभी रेवदस्मे दीदायानिध्मो घृतनिर्णिगप्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ásmerāḥ ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ yúvānam ǀ marmṛjyámānāḥ ǀ pári ǀ yanti ǀ ā́paḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ śukrébhiḥ ǀ śíkva-bhiḥ ǀ revát ǀ asmé íti ǀ dīdā́ya ǀ anidhmáḥ ǀ ghṛtá-nirnik ǀ ap-sú ǁ
verses.english_translation: The young and modest (waters) wait upon the youth, assiduous in bathing him, and he, although unfed with fuel, yet cleansed with clarified butter, shines with bright rays amidst the waters, the abundance (may be) to us.
verses.wilson_translation: The young and modest (waters) wait upon the youth, assiduous in bathing him, and he, although unfed with fuel, yet cleansed with clarified butter, shines with bright rays amidst the waters, the abundance (may be) to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मै तिस्रो अव्यथ्याय नारीर्देवाय देवीर्दिधिषंत्यन्नं ।कृता इवोप हि प्रसर्स्रे अप्सु स पीयूषं धयति पूर्वसूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ tisráḥ ǀ avyathyā́ya ǀ nā́rīḥ ǀ devā́ya ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ didhiṣanti ǀ ánnam ǀkṛ́tāḥ-iva ǀ úpa ǀ hí ǀ pra-sarsré ǀ ap-sú ǀ sáḥ ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ dhayati ǀ pūrva-sū́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: THree divine feminine les present food to that uninjurable divinity; as if formed in the waters they spread abroad, and he drinks the ambrosia of the first-created (elements).
verses.wilson_translation: THree divine feminine les present food to that uninjurable divinity; as if formed in the waters they spread abroad, and he drinks the ambrosia of the first-created (elements).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वस्यात्र जनिमास्य च स्वर्द्रुहो रिषः संपृचः पाहि सूरीन् ।आमासु पूर्षु परो अप्रमृष्यं नारातयो वि नशन्नानृतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvasya ǀ átra ǀ jánima ǀ asyá ǀ ca ǀ sváḥ ǀ druháḥ ǀ riṣáḥ ǀ sam-pṛ́caḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ sūrī́n ǀāmā́su ǀ pūrṣú ǀ paráḥ ǀ apra-mṛṣyám ǀ ná ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ ví ǀ naśan ǀ ná ǀ ánṛtāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: In him is the birth of the horse, of him is (the origin of) the world; do you, grandson of the (waters), protect the pious worshippers from the malevolence of the oppressor; those who give no offerings, those who practise untruths, attain not the inconceivable deity, whether abiding in the  immature or the perfect waters.
verses.wilson_translation: In him is the birth of the horse, of him is (the origin of) the world; do you, grandson of the (waters), protect the pious worshippers from the malevolence of the oppressor; those who give no offerings, those who practise untruths, attain not the inconceivable deity, whether abiding in the  immature or the perfect waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्व आ दमे सुदुघा यस्य धेनुः स्वधां पीपाय सुभ्वन्नमत्ति ।सो अपां नपादूर्जयन्नप्स्वंतर्वसुदेयाय विधते वि भाति ॥
verses.transliteration: své ǀ ā́ ǀ dáme ǀ su-dúghā ǀ yásya ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ svadhā́m ǀ pīpāya ǀ su-bhú ǀ ánnam ǀ atti ǀsáḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ ūrjáyan ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáḥ ǀ vasu-déyāya ǀ vidhaté ǀ ví ǀ bhāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, the grandson of the waters, who abides in his own dwelling; of whom is the readily-milked cow; who augments the nectar (of the skies), and (thence) eats the sacrificial food; he, gathering strength in the midst of the waters, shines for the sake of conferring wealth upon his worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the grandson of the waters, who abides in his own dwelling; of whom is the readily-milked cow; who augments the nectar (of the skies), and (thence) eats the sacrificial food; he, gathering strength in the midst of the waters, shines for the sake of conferring wealth upon his worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो अप्स्वा शुचिना दैव्येन ऋतावाजस्र उर्विया विभाति ।वया इदन्या भुवनान्यस्य प्र जायंते वीरुधश्च प्रजाभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ ā́ ǀ śúcinā ǀ dáivyena ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ ájasraḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ vi-bhā́ti ǀvayā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ anyā́ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ asya ǀ prá ǀ jāyante ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pra-jā́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All other beings are, as it were, branches of him, who, truthful, eternal, and vast, shines amid the waters with pure and divine (radiance); and the shrubs, with their products, are born (of him).
verses.wilson_translation: All other beings are, as it were, branches of him, who, truthful, eternal, and vast, shines amid the waters with pure and divine (radiance); and the shrubs, with their products, are born (of him).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपां नपादा ह्यस्थादुपस्थं जिह्मानामूर्ध्वो विद्युतं वसानः ।तस्य ज्येष्ठं महिमानं वहंतीर्हिरण्यवर्णाः परि यंति यह्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ ásthāt ǀ upá-stham ǀ jihmā́nām ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ vi-dyútam ǀ vásānaḥ ǀtásya ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ váhantīḥ ǀ híraṇya-varṇāḥ ǀ pári ǀ yanti ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The grandson of the waters has ascended the firmament above (the region) of the tortuously-moving (clouds), arrayed in lightning; the broad and golden-coloured (rivers) spread around, bearing (to all quarters) his exceeding glory.
verses.wilson_translation: The grandson of the waters has ascended the firmament above (the region) of the tortuously-moving (clouds), arrayed in lightning; the broad and golden-coloured (rivers) spread around, bearing (to all quarters) his exceeding glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यरूपः स हिरण्यसंदृगपां नपात्सेदु हिरण्यवर्णः ।हिरण्ययात्परि योनेर्निषद्या हिरण्यदा ददत्यन्नमस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-rūpaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ híraṇya-sandṛk ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ híraṇya-varṇaḥ ǀhiraṇyáyāt ǀ pári ǀ yóneḥ ǀ ni-sádya ǀ hiraṇya-dā́ḥ ǀ dadati ǀ ánnam ǀ asmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: The grandson of the waters is of olden form, of golden aspect, of golden hue, and (shines) seated upon a seat of gold; the givers of gold (at solemn rites) present to him (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: The grandson of the waters is of olden form, of golden aspect, of golden hue, and (shines) seated upon a seat of gold; the givers of gold (at solemn rites) present to him (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तदस्यानीकमुत चारु नामापीच्यं वर्धते नप्तुरपां ।यमिंधते युवतयः समित्था हिरण्यवर्णं घृतमन्नमस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ asya ǀ ánīkam ǀ utá ǀ cā́ru ǀ nā́ma ǀ apīcyám ǀ vardhate ǀ náptuḥ ǀ apā́m ǀyám ǀ indháte ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ itthā́ ǀ híraṇya-varṇam ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ánnam ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Beautiful is his form (of aggregated lustre, beautiful) is the name of the grandson of the waters; (both) flourish, though  hidden (by the clouds); the youthful w2aters collectively kindle the golden-coloured divinity in the firmament, for water is his food.
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful is his form (of aggregated lustre, beautiful) is the name of the grandson of the waters; (both) flourish, though  hidden (by the clouds); the youthful w2aters collectively kindle the golden-coloured divinity in the firmament, for water is his food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मै बहूनामवमाय सख्ये यज्ञैर्विधेम नमसा हविर्भिः ।सं सानु मार्ज्मि दिधिषामि बिल्मैर्दधाम्यन्नैः परि वंद ऋग्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ bahūnā́m ǀ avamā́ya ǀ sákhye ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ námasā ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀsám ǀ sā́nu ǀ mā́rjmi ǀ dídhiṣāmi ǀ bílmaiḥ ǀ dádhāmi ǀ ánnaiḥ ǀ pári ǀ vande ǀ ṛk-bhíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him our friend, the first of many (deities), we offer worship with sacrifices, oblations, and prostration; I decorate the high plural ce (of his presence); I nourish him with fuel; I sustain him with (sacrificial) viands; I glorify him with hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: To him our friend, the first of many (deities), we offer worship with sacrifices, oblations, and prostration; I decorate the high plural ce (of his presence); I nourish him with fuel; I sustain him with (sacrificial) viands; I glorify him with hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स ईं वृषाजनयत्तासु गर्भं स ईं शिशुर्धयति तं रिहंति ।सो अपां नपादनभिम्लातवर्णोऽन्यस्येवेह तन्वा विवेष ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ajanayat ǀ tā́su ǀ gárbham ǀ sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ śíśuḥ ǀ dhayati ǀ tám ǀ rihanti ǀsáḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ ánabhimlāta-varṇaḥ ǀ anyásya-iva ǀ ihá ǀ tanvā́ ǀ viveṣa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vigorous, he has genitive rated himself as an embryo in those (waters); he is their infant; he sucks them; they bedew him (with moisture); the grandson of the waters of untarnished splendour has descended to this (earth) in the form of a different (fire).
verses.wilson_translation: Vigorous, he has genitive rated himself as an embryo in those (waters); he is their infant; he sucks them; they bedew him (with moisture); the grandson of the waters of untarnished splendour has descended to this (earth) in the form of a different (fire).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मिन्पदे परमे तस्थिवांसमध्वस्मभिर्विश्वहा दीदिवांसं ।आपो नप्त्रे घृतमन्नं वहंतीः स्वयमत्कैः परि दीयंति यह्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmín ǀ padé ǀ paramé ǀ tasthi-vā́ṃsam ǀ adhvasmá-bhiḥ ǀ viśváhā ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀā́paḥ ǀ náptre ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ánnam ǀ váhantīḥ ǀ svayám ǀ átkaiḥ ǀ pári ǀ dīyanti ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The abundant waters, bearing sustenance to their grandson, flow round him with spontaneous movements; when abiding in his supreme sphere, and shining daily with imperishable (rays).
verses.wilson_translation: The abundant waters, bearing sustenance to their grandson, flow round him with spontaneous movements; when abiding in his supreme sphere, and shining daily with imperishable (rays).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयांसमग्ने सुक्षितिं जनायायांसमु मघवद्भ्यः सुवृक्तिं ।विश्वं तद्भद्रं यदवंति देवा बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥
verses.transliteration: áyāṃsam ǀ agne ǀ su-kṣitím ǀ jánāya ǀ áyāṃsam ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ su-vṛktím ǀvíśvam ǀ tát ǀ bhadrám ǀ yát ǀ ávanti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ vadema ǀ vidáthe ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have come,Agni, to you, (the giver) of good dwellings, for the sake of offspring; I have come with a propitiatory hymn for the sake of the opulent (offerers of oblations); may all the good which the gods defend (be ours); that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: I have come,Agni, to you, (the giver) of good dwellings, for the sake of offspring; I have come with a propitiatory hymn for the sake of the opulent (offerers of oblations); may all the good which the gods defend (be ours); that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVI Various Gods.
hymns.anukramani: ६ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। ऋतुदेवताः- १ इन्द्रो मधुश्च, २मरुतो माधवश्च, ३ त्वष्टा शुक्रश्च, ४ अग्निः शचिश्च, ५ इन्द्रो नभश्च, ६ मित्रावरुणौ नभस्यश्च। जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WATER and milk hath he endued, sent forth to thee: the men have drained him with the filters and the stones.Drink, Indra, from the Hotar's bowl—first right is thine—Soma hallowed and poured with Vaṣaṭ and Svāhā. Busied with sacrifice, with spotted deer and spears, gleaming upon your way with ornaments, yea, our Friends,Sitting on sacred grass, ye Sons of Bhārata, drink Soma from the Potar's bowl, O Men of heaven. Come unto us, ye swift to listen: as at home upon the sacred grass sit and enjoy yourselves.And, Tvaṣṭar, well-content be joyful in the juice with Gods and Goddesses in gladsome company. Bring the Gods hither, Sage, and offer sacrifice: at the three altars seat thee willingly, O Priest.Accept for thy delight the proffered Soma meath: drink from the Kindler's bowl and fill thee with thy share. This is the strengthener of thy body's manly might: strength, victory for all time are placed within thine arms.Pressed for thee, Maghavan, it is offered unto thee: drink from the chalice of this Brahman, drink thy fill. Accept the sacrifice; mark both of you, my call: the Priest hath seated him after the ancient texts.My prayer that bids them come goes forth to both the Kings: drink ye the Soma meath from the Director's bowl.

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं हिन्वानो वसिष्ट गा अपोऽधुक्षन्त्सीमविभिरद्रिभिर्नरः ।पिबेंद्र स्वाहा प्रहुतं वषट्कृतं होत्रादा सोमं प्रथमो य ईशिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ hinvānáḥ ǀ vasiṣṭa ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ádhukṣan ǀ sīm ǀ ávi-bhiḥ ǀ ádri-bhiḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀpíba ǀ indra ǀ svā́hā ǀ prá-hutam ǀ váṣaṭ-kṛtam ǀ hotrā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ sómam ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ī́śiṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: (The libation) that is being presented,Indra, to you, comprises the (products of the) cow, and he (consecrated) water; and the leaders (of the rite) have expressed it with stones, and strained it through woollen (filters); do you, Indra, who are the first (of the gods), and rule (over the world), drink the Somaoffered by the Hotā, and sanctified by the exclamationssvāhāand vaṣat.
verses.wilson_translation: (The libation) that is being presented,Indra, to you, comprises the (products of the) cow, and he (consecrated) water; and the leaders (of the rite) have expressed it with stones, and strained it through woollen (filters); do you, Indra, who are the first (of the gods), and rule (over the world), drink the Somaoffered by the Hotā, and sanctified by the exclamationssvāhāand vaṣat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञैः सम्मिश्लाः पृषतीभिर्ऋष्टिभिर्यामञ्छुभ्रासो अंजिषु प्रिया उत ।आसद्या बर्हिर्भरतस्य सूनवः पोत्रादा सोमं पिबता दिवो नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñáiḥ ǀ sám-miślāḥ ǀ pṛ́ṣatībhiḥ ǀ ṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀ yā́man ǀ śubhrā́saḥ ǀ añjíṣu ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀā-sádya ǀ barhíḥ ǀ bharatasya ǀ sūnavaḥ ǀ potrā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ sómam ǀ pibata ǀ divaḥ ǀ naraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, together worshipped with sacrifices, standing in the car drawn by spotted mares, radiant with lances, and delighted by ornaments, sons of Bharata, leaders in the firmament, seated on the sacred grass, drink the Somapresented by the Potā.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, together worshipped with sacrifices, standing in the car drawn by spotted mares, radiant with lances, and delighted by ornaments, sons of Bharata, leaders in the firmament, seated on the sacred grass, drink the Somapresented by the Potā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अमेव नः सुहवा आ हि गंतन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन ।अथा मंदस्व जुजुषाणो अंधसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ॥
verses.transliteration: amā́-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ su-havāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ gántana ǀ ní ǀ barhíṣi ǀ sadatana ǀ ráṇiṣṭana ǀátha ǀ mandasva ǀ jujuṣāṇáḥ ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ tváṣṭaḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ jáni-bhiḥ ǀ sumát-gaṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you, who are devoutly invoked, come to us together, and, seated on the sacrificial grass, enjoy your rest; and then,Tvaṣṭā, who head a brilliant cohort (come) with the gods and their wives, and rejoice being plural ased with the (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, who are devoutly invoked, come to us together, and, seated on the sacrificial grass, enjoy your rest; and then,Tvaṣṭā, who head a brilliant cohort (come) with the gods and their wives, and rejoice being plural ased with the (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वक्षि देवाँ इह विप्र यक्षि चोशन्होतर्नि षदा योनिषु त्रिषु ।प्रति वीहि प्रस्थितं सोम्यं मधु पिबाग्नीध्रात्तव भागस्य तृप्णुहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vakṣi ǀ devā́n ǀ ihá ǀ vipra ǀ yákṣi ǀ ca ǀ uśán ǀ hotaḥ ǀ ní ǀ sada ǀ yóniṣu ǀ triṣú ǀpráti ǀ vīhi ǀ prá-sthitam ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǀ píba ǀ ā́gnīdhrāt ǀ táva ǀ bhāgásya ǀ tṛpṇuhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sage Agni, bring hither the gods, and sacrifice to them; invoker of the gods, propitious to us, sit down in the three altars; accept the libation of Somathat is offered to you, from the Agnidhraand be satisfied with your portion.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Agni, bring hither the gods, and sacrifice to them; invoker of the gods, propitious to us, sit down in the three altars; accept the libation of Somathat is offered to you, from the Agnidhraand be satisfied with your portion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एष स्य ते तन्वो नृम्णवर्धनः सह ओजः प्रदिवि बाह्वोर्हितः ।तुभ्यं सुतो मघवंतुभ्यमाभृतस्त्वमस्य ब्राह्मणादा तृपत्पिब ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ syáḥ ǀ te ǀ tanváḥ ǀ nṛmṇa-várdhanaḥ ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ pra-dívi ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǀtúbhyam ǀ sutáḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ túbhyam ǀ ā́-bhṛtaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ asya ǀ brā́hmaṇāt ǀ ā́ ǀ tṛpát ǀ piba ǁ
verses.english_translation: This (libation),Indra, is the augmenter of your bodily (vigour), favourable of old to the resistless strength of (your) arms; it is effused,Maghavan, for you; it is brought to you from the Brāhmaṇa; do you drink and be satisfied.
verses.wilson_translation: This (libation),Indra, is the augmenter of your bodily (vigour), favourable of old to the resistless strength of (your) arms; it is effused,Maghavan, for you; it is brought to you from the Brāhmaṇa; do you drink and be satisfied.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु ।अच्छा राजाना नम एत्यावृतं प्रशास्त्रादा पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣéthām ǀ yajñám ǀ bódhatam ǀ hávasya ǀ me ǀ sattáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ni-vídaḥ ǀ pūrvyā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀáccha ǀ rā́jānā ǀ námaḥ ǀ eti ǀ ā-vṛ́tam ǀ pra-śāstrā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ pibatam ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, both be gratified with the sacrifice; hear my invocation as the seated Hotārepeats in succession the ancient praises; the (sacrificial) food encompassed (by the priests), attends the royal pair drink, both of you, the sweet Somalibation, offered by the Praśāstā.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, both be gratified with the sacrifice; hear my invocation as the seated Hotārepeats in succession the ancient praises; the (sacrificial) food encompassed (by the priests), attends the royal pair drink, both of you, the sweet Somalibation, offered by the Praśāstā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVII. Various Gods.
hymns.anukramani: ६ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। ऋतुदेवताः- १-४ द्रविणोदा ऋतवश्च, ५ अश्विनौ ऋतवश्च, ६ अग्निः ऋतुश्च। जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Enjoy thy fill of meath out of the Hotar's cup: Adhvaryus he desires a full draught poured for him.Bring it him: seeking this he gives. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Hotar's cup. He whom of old I called on, him I call on now. He is to be invoked; his name is He who Gives,Here brought by priests is Soma meath. Granter of Wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Potar's cup. Fat may the horses be wherewith thou speedest on: Lord of the Wood, unharming, strengthen thou thyself.Drawing and seizing, Bold One, thou who grantest wealth, drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Neṣṭar's cup. From Hotar's cup and Potar's he hath drunk and joyed: the proffered food hath pleased him from the Neṣṭar's bowl.The fourth cup undisturbed, immortal, let him drink who giveth wealth, the cup of the wealth-giving God. Yoke, O ye Twain, to-day your hero-bearing car, swift-moving hitherward: your loosing-place is here.Mix the oblations, then come hither with the meath, and drink the Soma, ye rich in abundant strength. Agni, accept the fuel and our offered gift: accept the prayer of man, accept our eulogy,Do thou with all, with Ṛtu, O thou Excellent, fain, make the great Gods all fain taste the gift we bring.

verses.sanskrit: मंदस्व होत्रादनु जोषमंधसोऽध्वर्यवः स पूर्णां वष्ट्यासिचं ।तस्मा एतं भरत तद्वशो ददिर्होत्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: mándasva ǀ hotrā́t ǀ ánu ǀ jóṣam ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ ádhvaryavaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ pūrṇā́m ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ ā-sícam ǀtásmai ǀ etám ǀ bharata ǀ tat-vaśáḥ ǀ dadíḥ ǀ hotrā́t ǀ sómam ǀ draviṇaḥ-daḥ ǀ píba ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be gratified, Draviṇodas, by the sacrificial food presented as the offering of the Hotā; he desires, priests, a fall libation; present it to him, and influenced (by it, he will be your) benefactor; drink, Draviṇodas, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Hotā.
verses.wilson_translation: Be gratified, Draviṇodas, by the sacrificial food presented as the offering of the Hotā; he desires, priests, a fall libation; present it to him, and influenced (by it, he will be your) benefactor; drink, Draviṇodas, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Hotā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यमु पूर्वमहुवे तमिदं हुवे सेदु हव्यो ददिर्यो नाम पत्यते ।अध्वर्युभिः प्रस्थितं सोम्यं मधु पोत्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ pū́rvam ǀ áhuve ǀ tám ǀ idám ǀ huve ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ dadíḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ pátyate ǀadhvaryú-bhiḥ ǀ prá-sthitam ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǀ potrā́t ǀ sómam ǀ draviṇaḥ-daḥ ǀ píba ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, whom I formerly invoked and whom I now invoke, is verily worthy of invocation, for he is renowned as a benefactor; the Somalibation has been brought by the priests; drink, Draviṇodās, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Potā.
verses.wilson_translation: He, whom I formerly invoked and whom I now invoke, is verily worthy of invocation, for he is renowned as a benefactor; the Somalibation has been brought by the priests; drink, Draviṇodās, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Potā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मेद्यंतु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसेऽरिषण्यन्वीळयस्वा वनस्पते ।आयूया धृष्णो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्ट्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: médyantu ǀ te ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ ī́yase ǀ áriṣaṇyan ǀ vīḷayasva ǀ vanaspate ǀā-yū́ya ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ abhi-gū́rya ǀ tvám ǀ neṣṭrā́t ǀ sómam ǀ draviṇaḥ-daḥ ǀ píba ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May these your bearers, by whom you are borne along, be satisfied; lord of the forest, be firm, doing no injury, steadfast of resolve; come and being gracious, drink, Draviṇodas, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Neṣṭā.
verses.wilson_translation: May these your bearers, by whom you are borne along, be satisfied; lord of the forest, be firm, doing no injury, steadfast of resolve; come and being gracious, drink, Draviṇodas, along with the Ṛtus, the Soma, the offering of the Neṣṭā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपाद्धोत्रादुत पोत्रादमत्तोत नेष्ट्रादजुषत प्रयो हितं ।तुरीयं पात्रममृक्तममर्त्यं द्रविणोदाः पिबतु द्राविणोदसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápāt ǀ hotrā́t ǀ utá ǀ potrā́t ǀ amatta ǀ utá ǀ neṣṭrā́t ǀ ajuṣata ǀ práyaḥ ǀ hitám ǀturī́yam ǀ pā́tram ǀ ámṛktam ǀ ámartyam ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ pibatu ǀ drāviṇaḥ-dasáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether he has drunk the Somafrom the offering of the Hotā; whether he has been exhilarated by the offering of the Potā; whether he has been plural ased with the (sacrificial) food presented as the act of the Neṣṭā; still let Draviṇodās quaff the unstrained ambrosial cup, the fourth offered by the priest.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether he has drunk the Somafrom the offering of the Hotā; whether he has been exhilarated by the offering of the Potā; whether he has been plural ased with the (sacrificial) food presented as the act of the Neṣṭā; still let Draviṇodās quaff the unstrained ambrosial cup, the fourth offered by the priest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वांचमद्य यय्यं नृवाहणं रथं युंजाथामिह वां विमोचनं ।पृंक्तं हवींषि मधुना हि कं गतमथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ñcam ǀ adyá ǀ yayyám ǀ nṛ-vā́hanam ǀ rátham ǀ yuñjāthām ǀ ihá ǀ vām ǀ vi-mócanam ǀpṛṅktám ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ mádhunā ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ gatám ǀ átha ǀ sómam ǀ pibatam ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yoke today,Aśvins, your rolling car conveying (you), the leaders (of the rite); and setting yu down before us; mix the oblations with the sweet juice; come you are affluent with (abundant) food, and drink the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Yoke today,Aśvins, your rolling car conveying (you), the leaders (of the rite); and setting yu down before us; mix the oblations with the sweet juice; come you are affluent with (abundant) food, and drink the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जोष्यग्ने समिधं जोष्याहुतिं जोषि ब्रह्म जन्यं जोषि सुष्टुतिं ।विश्वेभिर्विश्वाँ ऋतुना वसो मह उशंदेवाँ उशतः पायया हविः ॥
verses.transliteration: jóṣi ǀ agne ǀ sam-ídham ǀ jóṣi ǀ ā́-hutim ǀ jóṣi ǀ bráhma ǀ jányam ǀ jóṣi ǀ su-stutím ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ víśvān ǀ ṛtúnā ǀ vaso íti ǀ maháḥ ǀ uśán ǀ devā́n ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ pāyaya ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be plural ased,Agni, with the fuel; be plural ased with the oblation; be plural ased with the sacred prayer that is good for man; be plural ased with holy praise, asylum of all; Agni, willing (to accept oblations), render all the great gods desirous (of the same), and with them all, and with the Ṛtu drink the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Be plural ased,Agni, with the fuel; be plural ased with the oblation; be plural ased with the sacred prayer that is good for man; be plural ased with holy praise, asylum of all; Agni, willing (to accept oblations), render all the great gods desirous (of the same), and with them all, and with the Ṛtu drink the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVIII. Savitar.
hymns.anukramani: ११ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। सविता।त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . UPRISEN is Savitar, this God, to quicken, Priest who neglects not this most constant duty.To the Gods, verily, he gives rich treasure, and blesses him who calls them to the banquet. Having gone up on high, the God broad-handed spreads his arms widely forth that all may mark him.Even the waters bend them to his service: even this wind rests in the circling region. Though borne by swift steeds he will yet unyoke them: e’en the fleet chariot hath he stayed from going.He hath checked e’en their haste who glide like serpents. Night closely followed Savitar's dominion. What was spread out she weaves afresh, re-weaving: the skilful leaves his labour half-completed.He hath arisen from rest, and parted seasons: Savitar hath approached, God, holy-minded. Through various dwellings, through entire existence, spreads, manifest, the household light of Agni.The Mother gives her Son the goodliest portion, and Savitar hath sped to meet his summons. He comes again, unfolded, fain for conquest: at home was he, the love of all things moving.Each man hath come leaving his evil doings, after the Godlike Savitar's commandment. The wild beasts spread through desert places seeking their watery share which thou hast set in waters.The woods are given to the birds. These statutes of the God Savitar none disobeyeth. With utmost speed, in restless haste at sunset Varuṇa seeks his watery habitation.Then seeks each bird his nest, each beast his lodging. In due place Savitar hath set each creature. Him whose high law not Varuṇa nor Indra, not Mitra, Aryaman, nor Rudra breaketh,Nor evil-hearted fiends, here for my welfare him I invoke, God Savitar, with worship. May they who strengthen bliss, and thought and wisdom, and the Dames’ Lord and Narāśaṁsa aid us.That good may come to us and wealth be gathered, may we be Savitar the God's beloved. So come to us our hearts' desire, the bounty bestowed by thee, from heaven and earth and waters,That it be well with friends and those who praise thee, and, Savitar, with the loud-lauding singer.

verses.sanskrit: उदु ष्य देवः सविता सवाय शश्वत्तमं तदपा वह्निरस्थात् ।नूनं देवेभ्यो वि हि धाति रत्नमथाभजद्वीतिहोत्रं स्वस्तौ ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ syáḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ savā́ya ǀ śaśvat-tamám ǀ tát-apāḥ ǀ váhniḥ ǀ asthāt ǀnūnám ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ hí ǀ dhā́ti ǀ rátnam ǀ átha ǀ ā́ ǀ abhajat ǀ vītí-hotram ǀ svastáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: In truth, the divine Savitā, the bearer (of the world), has perpetually been present for the genitive ration (of mankind), for such is his office; verily he grants wealth to the pious (worshippers); may he, therefore, bestow upon the offerer of the oblation (sufficient) for his well-being.
verses.wilson_translation: In truth, the divine Savitā, the bearer (of the world), has perpetually been present for the genitive ration (of mankind), for such is his office; verily he grants wealth to the pious (worshippers); may he, therefore, bestow upon the offerer of the oblation (sufficient) for his well-being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्य हि श्रुष्टये देव ऊर्ध्वः प्र बाहवा पृथुपाणिः सिसर्ति ।आपश्चिदस्य व्रत आ निमृग्रा अयं चिद्वातो रमते परिज्मन् ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasya ǀ hí ǀ śruṣṭáye ǀ deváḥ ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ prá ǀ bāhávā ǀ pṛthú-pāṇiḥ ǀ sísarti ǀā́paḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ vraté ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-mṛgrāḥ ǀ ayám ǀ cit ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ramate ǀ pári-jman ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine, vast-handed (Savitā), having risen, stretches forth his arms for the delight of all; the purifying waters (flow) for (the fulfilment of) his rites, and this circumambient air sports (in the firmament).
verses.wilson_translation: The divine, vast-handed (Savitā), having risen, stretches forth his arms for the delight of all; the purifying waters (flow) for (the fulfilment of) his rites, and this circumambient air sports (in the firmament).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आशुभिश्चिद्यान्वि मुचाति नूनमरीरमदतमानं चिदेतोः ।अह्यर्षूणां चिन्न्ययाँ अविष्यामनु व्रतं सवितुर्मोक्यागात् ॥
verses.transliteration: āśú-bhiḥ ǀ cit ǀ yā́n ǀ ví ǀ mucāti ǀ nūnám ǀ árīramat ǀ átamānam ǀ cit ǀ étoḥ ǀahyárṣūṇām ǀ cit ǀ ní ǀ ayān ǀ aviṣyā́m ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ savitúḥ ǀ mókī ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: The moving (Sun) is liberated by his rapid rays; verily he has stopped the traveller from his journey; he restraisn the desire of warriors for combat, for night follows (the cessation of) the function of Savitā.
verses.wilson_translation: The moving (Sun) is liberated by his rapid rays; verily he has stopped the traveller from his journey; he restraisn the desire of warriors for combat, for night follows (the cessation of) the function of Savitā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुनः समव्यद्विततं वयंती मध्या कर्तोर्न्यधाच्छक्म धीरः ।उत्संहायास्थाद्व्यृतूँरदर्धररमतिः सविता देव आगात् ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaríti ǀ sám ǀ avyat ǀ ví-tatam ǀ váyantī ǀ madhyā́ ǀ kártoḥ ǀ ní ǀ adhāt ǀ śákma ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀút ǀ sam-hā́ya ǀ asthāt ǀ ví ǀ ṛtū́n ǀ adardhaḥ ǀ arámatiḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: She, (Night), enwraps the extended (world) like (a woman) weaving (a garment); the prudent man lays aside the work he is able (to execute) in the midst (of his labour); but all spring up (from repose) when the divine, unwearied Sun, who has divided the seasons, again appears.
verses.wilson_translation: She, (Night), enwraps the extended (world) like (a woman) weaving (a garment); the prudent man lays aside the work he is able (to execute) in the midst (of his labour); but all spring up (from repose) when the divine, unwearied Sun, who has divided the seasons, again appears.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नानौकांसि दुर्यो विश्वमायुर्वि तिष्ठते प्रभवः शोको अग्नेः ।ज्येष्ठं माता सूनवे भागमाधादन्वस्य केतमिषितं सवित्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́nā ǀ ókāṃsi ǀ dúryaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ví ǀ tiṣṭhate ǀ pra-bhaváḥ ǀ śókaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀjyéṣṭham ǀ mātā́ ǀ sūnáve ǀ bhāgám ǀ ā́ ǀ adhāt ǀ ánu ǀ asya ǀ kétam ǀ iṣitám ǀ savitrā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The engendered domestic radiance of Agnispreads through various dwellings, and presides over all (sorts of sacrificial) food; the mother, (Dawn), has assigned to her son, (Agni), the best portion (at sacrifices), which is the manifestation of him imparted by Savitā.
verses.wilson_translation: The engendered domestic radiance of Agnispreads through various dwellings, and presides over all (sorts of sacrificial) food; the mother, (Dawn), has assigned to her son, (Agni), the best portion (at sacrifices), which is the manifestation of him imparted by Savitā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समाववर्ति विष्ठितो जिगीषुर्विश्वेषां कामश्चरताममाभूत् ।शश्वाँ अपो विकृतं हित्व्यागादनु व्रतं सवितुर्दैव्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-ā́vavarti ǀ ví-sthitaḥ ǀ jigīṣúḥ ǀ víśveṣām ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ cáratām ǀ amā́ ǀ abhūt ǀśáśvān ǀ ápaḥ ǀ ví-kṛtam ǀ hitvī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ savitúḥ ǀ dáivyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The warrior, eager for victory, who has gone forth (to battle), turns back; (for) home is the desire of  moving beiings; abandoning his half-wrought toil, the labourer returns (home) when the function of the divine Savitā(is suspended).
verses.wilson_translation: The warrior, eager for victory, who has gone forth (to battle), turns back; (for) home is the desire of  moving beiings; abandoning his half-wrought toil, the labourer returns (home) when the function of the divine Savitā(is suspended).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वया हितमप्यमप्सु भागं धन्वान्वा मृगयसो वि तस्थुः ।वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनंति ॥
verses.transliteration: tváyā ǀ hitám ǀ ápyam ǀ ap-sú ǀ bhāgám ǀ dhánva ǀ ánu ǀ ā́ ǀ mṛgayásaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tasthuḥ ǀvánāni ǀ ví-bhyaḥ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ asya ǀ tā́ni ǀ vratā́ ǀ devásya ǀ savitúḥ ǀ minanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The animals search in dry plural ces for the water element which has been collected in the firmament by you; the woods are assigned (by you) to the birds; no one obstructs these functions of the divine Savitā.
verses.wilson_translation: The animals search in dry plural ces for the water element which has been collected in the firmament by you; the woods are assigned (by you) to the birds; no one obstructs these functions of the divine Savitā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: याद्राध्यं वरुणो योनिमप्यमनिशितं निमिषि जर्भुराणः ।विश्वो मार्तांडो व्रजमा पशुर्गात्स्थशो जन्मानि सविता व्याकः ॥
verses.transliteration: yāt-rādhyám ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yónim ǀ ápyam ǀ áni-śitam ǀ ni-míṣi ǀ járbhurāṇaḥ ǀvíśvaḥ ǀ mārtāṇḍáḥ ǀ vrajám ǀ ā́ ǀ paśúḥ ǀ gāt ǀ stha-śáḥ ǀ jánmāni ǀ savitā́ ǀ ví ǀ ā́ ǀ akarítyakaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ever-going Varuṇagrants a cool, accessible and agreeable plural ce (of rest), to all moving (creatures) on the closing of the eyes (of Savitā), and every bird and every beast repairs to its lair when Savitā has dispersed (all) beings in various directions.
verses.wilson_translation: The ever-going Varuṇagrants a cool, accessible and agreeable plural ce (of rest), to all moving (creatures) on the closing of the eyes (of Savitā), and every bird and every beast repairs to its lair when Savitā has dispersed (all) beings in various directions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्येंद्रो वरुणो न मित्रो व्रतमर्यमा न मिनंति रुद्रः ।नारातयस्तमिदं स्वस्ति हुवे देवं सवितारं नमोभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vratám ǀ aryamā́ ǀ ná ǀ minánti ǀ rudráḥ ǀná ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ tám ǀ idám ǀ svastí ǀ huvé ǀ devám ǀ savitā́ram ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invite to this plural ce, with reverential salutations, for my good, that divine Savitā, whose functions neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitranor Aryamannor Rudranor the enemies (of the gods), impede.
verses.wilson_translation: I invite to this plural ce, with reverential salutations, for my good, that divine Savitā, whose functions neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitranor Aryamannor Rudranor the enemies (of the gods), impede.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भगं धियं वाजयंतः पुरंधिं नराशंसो ग्नास्पतिर्नो अव्याः ।आये वामस्य संगथे रयीणां प्रिया देवस्य सवितुः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: bhágam ǀ dhíyam ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǀ púram-dhim ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ gnā́ḥpátiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ avyāḥ ǀā-ayé ǀ vāmásya ǀ sam-gathé ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ devásya ǀ savitúḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he, who is adored by men, the protector of the wives (of the gods), preserve us; when worshipping his, who is auspicious, the object of meditation, and the all wise; may we be the beloved of the divine Savitā, that we may (thence be successful) in the accusative ulation of wealth and the acquisition of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, who is adored by men, the protector of the wives (of the gods), preserve us; when worshipping his, who is auspicious, the object of meditation, and the all wise; may we be the beloved of the divine Savitā, that we may (thence be successful) in the accusative ulation of wealth and the acquisition of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मभ्यं तद्दिवो अद्भ्यः पृथिव्यास्त्वया दत्तं काम्यं राध आ गात् ।शं यत्स्तोतृभ्य आपये भवात्युरुशंसाय सवितर्जरित्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: asmábhyam ǀ tát ǀ diváḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ dattám ǀ kā́myam ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gāt ǀśám ǀ yát ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ āpáye ǀ bhávāti ǀ uru-śáṃsāya ǀ savitaḥ ǀ jaritré ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that desirable wealth which is granted to us,Savitā, by you, proceed from the sky, from the waters from the earth; and may the happiness (which belongs) to the race of those who eulogise you, devolve upon me, repeating diligently your praises.
verses.wilson_translation: May that desirable wealth which is granted to us,Savitā, by you, proceed from the sky, from the waters from the earth; and may the happiness (which belongs) to the race of those who eulogise you, devolve upon me, repeating diligently your praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIX. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: ८ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। अश्विनौ। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SING like the two press-stones for this same purpose; come like two misers to the tree of treasure;Like two laud-singing Brahmans in the assembly, like the folk's envoys called in many places. Moving at morning like two car-borne heroes, like to a pair of goats ye come electing;Like two fair dames embellishing their bodies, like a wise married pair among the people. Like to a pair of horns come first to us-ward, like to a pair of hoofs with rapid motion;Come like two Cakavās in the grey of morning, come like two chariot wheels at dawn, ye Mighty. Bear us across the rivers like two vessels, save us as ye were yokes, naves, spokes and fellies.Be like two dogs that injure not our bodies; preserve us, like two crutches, that we fall not. Like two winds ageing not, two confluent rivers, come with quick vision like two eyes before us.Come like two hands most helpful to the body, and guide us like two feet to what is precious. Even as two lips that with the mouth speak honey, even as two breasts that nourish our existence,Like the two nostrils that protect our being, be to us as our ears that hear distinctly. Like two hands give ye us increasing vigour; like heaven and earth constrain the airy regions.Aśvins, these hymns that struggle to approach you, sharpen ye like an axe upon a whetstone. These prayers of ours exalting you, O Aśvins, have the Gṛtsamadas, for a laud, made ready.Welcome them, O ye Heroes, and come hither. Loud may we speak. with brave men, in assembly.

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावाणेव तदिदर्थं जरेथे गृध्रेव वृक्षं निधिमंतमच्छ ।ब्रह्माणेव विदथ उक्थशासा दूतेव हव्या जन्या पुरुत्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vāṇā-iva ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ ártham ǀ jarethe íti ǀ gṛ́dhrā-iva ǀ vṛkṣám ǀ nidhi-mántam ǀ áccha ǀbrahmā́ṇā-iva ǀ vidáthe ǀ uktha-śásā ǀ dūtā́-iva ǀ hávyā ǀ jányā ǀ puru-trā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Descend,Aśvins, like falling stones, for the purpose (of destroying our foes); hasten to the presence of the wealth-possessing (worshippers), like vultures to a tree; like two Brāhmaṇasrepeating hymns, (be present) at the sacrifice, and come like (royal) messengers in the land, welcomed by many people.
verses.wilson_translation: Descend,Aśvins, like falling stones, for the purpose (of destroying our foes); hasten to the presence of the wealth-possessing (worshippers), like vultures to a tree; like two Brāhmaṇasrepeating hymns, (be present) at the sacrifice, and come like (royal) messengers in the land, welcomed by many people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्यावाणा रथ्येव वीराजेव यमा वरमा सचेथे ।मेने इव तन्वा शुंभमाने दंपतीव क्रतुविदा जनेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-yā́vānā ǀ rathyā́-iva ǀ vīrā́ ǀ ajā́-iva ǀ yamā́ ǀ váram ǀ ā́ ǀ sacethe íti ǀméne ivéti méne-iva ǀ tanvā́ ǀ śúmbhamāne íti ǀ dámpatī ivéti dámpatī-iva ǀ kratu-vídā ǀ jáneṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Moving at dawn like two heroes in a cr; like a pair of goats; like two women lovely inform, or like husband and wife; come together, knowing (how sacred) ites (are to be celebrated) amongst men, (to bestow) happiness (on the worshipper).
verses.wilson_translation: Moving at dawn like two heroes in a cr; like a pair of goats; like two women lovely inform, or like husband and wife; come together, knowing (how sacred) ites (are to be celebrated) amongst men, (to bestow) happiness (on the worshipper).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शृंगेव नः प्रथमा गंतमर्वाक् छफाविव जर्भुराणा तरोभिः ।चक्रवाकेव प्रति वस्तोरुस्रार्वांचा यातं रथ्येव शक्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛ́ṅgā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ gantam ǀ arvā́k ǀ śapháu-iva ǀ járbhurāṇā ǀ táraḥ-bhiḥ ǀcakravākā́-iva ǀ práti ǀ vástoḥ ǀ usrā ǀ arvā́ñcā ǀ yātam ǀ rathyā́-iva ǀ śakrā ǁ
verses.english_translation: COme to us, the first (before other gods), like a pair of horns, or like two hoofs, travelling with rapid (steps); like a pair ofcakravākas, awaiting day; overthrower of foes, like warriors in cars, able (to perform all things), come to our presence.
verses.wilson_translation: COme to us, the first (before other gods), like a pair of horns, or like two hoofs, travelling with rapid (steps); like a pair ofcakravākas, awaiting day; overthrower of foes, like warriors in cars, able (to perform all things), come to our presence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नावेव नः पारयतं युगेव नभ्येव न उपधीव प्रधीव ।श्वानेव नो अरिषण्या तनूनां खृगलेव विस्रसः पातमस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: nāvā́-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ pārayatam ǀ yugā́-iva ǀ nábhyā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ upadhī́ ivétyupadhī́-iva ǀ pradhī́ ivéti pradhī́-iva ǀśvā́nā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ áriṣaṇyā ǀ tanū́nām ǀ khṛ́galā-iva ǀ vi-srásaḥ ǀ pātam ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bear us across (the sea of life), like two vessels, or (over difficult plural ces), like the poles of a car, the axles, the spokes, the fellies (of two wheels). Be like two dogs, warding off injury to our person ns, and, like two coats of mail, defend us from decay.
verses.wilson_translation: Bear us across (the sea of life), like two vessels, or (over difficult plural ces), like the poles of a car, the axles, the spokes, the fellies (of two wheels). Be like two dogs, warding off injury to our person ns, and, like two coats of mail, defend us from decay.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वातेवाजुर्या नद्येव रीतिरक्षी इव चक्षुषा यातमर्वाक् ।हस्ताविव तन्वेशंभविष्ठा पादेव नो नयतं वस्यो अच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́tā-iva ǀ ajuryā́ ǀ nadyā́-iva ǀ rītíḥ ǀ akṣī́ ivétyakṣī́-iva ǀ cákṣuṣā ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ arvā́k ǀhástau-iva ǀ tanvé ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhā ǀ pā́dā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ nayatam ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Irresistible as two winds, rapid as two rivers; and quick of sight, come like two eyes before us; like twohands; like two feet; subservient to the well-being of our bodies, conduct us to (the acquisition) of excellent (wealth).
verses.wilson_translation: Irresistible as two winds, rapid as two rivers; and quick of sight, come like two eyes before us; like twohands; like two feet; subservient to the well-being of our bodies, conduct us to (the acquisition) of excellent (wealth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ओष्ठाविव मध्वास्ने वदंता स्तनाविव पिप्यतं जीवसे नः ।नासेव नस्तन्वो रक्षितारा कर्णाविव सुश्रुता भूतमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: óṣṭhau-iva ǀ mádhu ǀ āsné ǀ vádantā ǀ stánau-iva ǀ pipyatam ǀ jīváse ǀ naḥ ǀnā́sā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ rakṣitā́rā ǀ kárṇau-iva ǀ su-śrútā ǀ bhūtam ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like two lips uttering sweet words, like two breasts yielding nourishment for our existence; be to us like two noses, preserving our person ns, and like two ears for the hearing of agreeable (sounds).
verses.wilson_translation: Like two lips uttering sweet words, like two breasts yielding nourishment for our existence; be to us like two noses, preserving our person ns, and like two ears for the hearing of agreeable (sounds).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हस्तेव शक्तिमभि संददी नः क्षामेव नः समजतं रजांसि ।इमा गिरो अश्विना युष्मयंतीः क्ष्णोत्रेणेव स्वधितिं सं शिशीतं ॥
verses.transliteration: hástā-iva ǀ śaktím ǀ abhí ǀ sandadī́ íti sam-dadī́ ǀ naḥ ǀ kṣā́mā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ sám ǀ ajatam ǀ rájāṃsi ǀimā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuṣma-yántīḥ ǀ kṣṇótreṇa-iva ǀ svá-dhitim ǀ sám ǀ śiśītam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like twohands,Aśvins, be ever investing us with vigour; like heaven and earth, bestow upon us rain; give sharpness to the praises that are addressed to you, as they whet an axe upon a grindstone.
verses.wilson_translation: Like twohands,Aśvins, be ever investing us with vigour; like heaven and earth, bestow upon us rain; give sharpness to the praises that are addressed to you, as they whet an axe upon a grindstone.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एतानि वामश्विना वर्धनानि ब्रह्म स्तोमं गृत्समदासो अक्रन् ।तानि नरा जुजुषाणोप यातं बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ várdhanāni ǀ bráhma ǀ stómam ǀ gṛtsa-madā́saḥ ǀ akran ǀtā́ni ǀ narā ǀ jujuṣāṇā́ ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǀ bṛhát ǀ vadema ǀ vidáthe ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gṛtsamadashave composed this prayer, these praises,Aśvins, for your exaltation; be propitiated by them, leaders of ceremonies, and come hither; that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: The Gṛtsamadashave composed this prayer, these praises,Aśvins, for your exaltation; be propitiated by them, leaders of ceremonies, and come hither; that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XL. Soma and Pūṣan.
hymns.anukramani: ६ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। सोमापूषणौ, ६(अन्त्यार्धर्चस्य) अदितिः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: SOMA and Pūṣan, Parents of all riches, Parents of earth and Parents of high heaven,You Twain, brought forth as the whole world's protectors, the Gods have made centre of life eternal. At birth of these two Gods all Gods are joyful: they have caused darkness, which we hate, to vanish.With these, with Soma and with Pūṣan, India generates ripe warm milk in the raw milch-cows. Soma and Pūṣan, urge your chariot hither, the seven-wheeled car that measures out the region,That stirs not all, that moves to every quarter, five-reined and harnessed by the thought, ye Mighty. One in the heaven on high hath made his dwelling, on earth and in the firmament the other.May they disclose to us great store of treasure, much-longed for, rich in food, source of enjoyment. One of you Twain is Parent of all creatures, the other journeys onward all-beholding.Soma and Pūṣan, aid my thought with favour: with you may we o’ercome in all encounters. May Pūṣan stir our thought, the all-impelling, may Soma Lord of riches grant us riches.May Aditi the perfect Goddess aid us. Loud may we speak, with heroes, in assembly.

verses.sanskrit: सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां जनना दिवो जनना पृथिव्याः ।जातौ विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपौ देवा अकृण्वन्नमृतस्य नाभिं ॥
verses.transliteration: sómāpūṣaṇā ǀ jánanā ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ jánanā ǀ diváḥ ǀ jánanā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀjātáu ǀ víśvasya ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gopáu ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ akṛṇvan ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ nā́bhim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Somaand Pūṣaṇ, you two are the genitive rators of riches, the genitive rators of heaven, the genitive rators of earth; as soon as born you are the guardians of the whole world; the gods have made you the source of immortality.
verses.wilson_translation: Somaand Pūṣaṇ, you two are the genitive rators of riches, the genitive rators of heaven, the genitive rators of earth; as soon as born you are the guardians of the whole world; the gods have made you the source of immortality.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमौ देवौ जायमानौ जुषंतेमौ तमांसि गूहतामजुष्टा ।आभ्यामिंद्रः पक्वमामास्वंतः सोमापूषभ्यां जनदुस्रियासु ॥
verses.transliteration: imáu ǀ deváu ǀ jā́yamānau ǀ juṣanta ǀ imáu ǀ támāṃsi ǀ gūhatām ǀ ájuṣṭā ǀābhyā́m ǀ índraḥ ǀ pakvám ǀ āmā́su ǀ antáríti ǀ somāpūṣá-bhyām ǀ janat ǀ usríyāsu ǁ
verses.english_translation: (The gods) propitiate these two divinities at the moment of the ir birth, for they drive away the disagreeable glooms; with these two,Somaand Pūṣaṇ,Indragenitive rates the mature (milk) in the immature heifers.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods) propitiate these two divinities at the moment of the ir birth, for they drive away the disagreeable glooms; with these two,Somaand Pūṣaṇ,Indragenitive rates the mature (milk) in the immature heifers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सोमापूषणा रजसो विमानं सप्तचक्रं रथमविश्वमिन्वं ।विषूवृतं मनसा युज्यमानं तं जिन्वथो वृषणा पंचरश्मिं ॥
verses.transliteration: sómāpūṣaṇā ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́nam ǀ saptá-cakram ǀ rátham ǀ áviśva-minvam ǀviṣu-vṛ́tam ǀ mánasā ǀ yujyámānam ǀ tám ǀ jinvathaḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ páñca-raśmim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Somaand Pūṣaṇ, showerers (of benefits)m direct towards us the seven-wheeled car, the measure of the spheres, undistinguishable from the universe, everywhere existing, (guided) by five reins, and to be harnessed by the mind.
verses.wilson_translation: Somaand Pūṣaṇ, showerers (of benefits)m direct towards us the seven-wheeled car, the measure of the spheres, undistinguishable from the universe, everywhere existing, (guided) by five reins, and to be harnessed by the mind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिव्यन्यः सदनं चक्र उच्चा पृथिव्यामन्यो अध्यंतरिक्षे ।तावस्मभ्यं पुरुवारं पुरुक्षुं रायस्पोषं वि ष्यतां नाभिमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: diví ǀ anyáḥ ǀ sádanam ǀ cakré ǀ uccā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ antárikṣe ǀtáu ǀ asmábhyam ǀ puru-vā́ram ǀ puru-kṣúm ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ ví ǀ syatām ǀ nā́bhim ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of them, (Pūṣaṇ), has made his dwelling above in the heaven; the other (Soma), upon earth, and in the firmament; may they both grant us much-desired and much-commended abundant wealth of cattle, the source to us (of enjoyment).
verses.wilson_translation: One of them, (Pūṣaṇ), has made his dwelling above in the heaven; the other (Soma), upon earth, and in the firmament; may they both grant us much-desired and much-commended abundant wealth of cattle, the source to us (of enjoyment).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वान्यन्यो भुवना जजान विश्वमन्यो अभिचक्षाण एति ।सोमापूषणाववतं धियं मे युवाभ्यां विश्वाः पृतना जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvāni ǀ anyáḥ ǀ bhúvanā ǀ jajā́na ǀ víśvam ǀ anyáḥ ǀ abhi-cákṣāṇaḥ ǀ eti ǀsómāpūṣaṇau ǀ ávatam ǀ dhíyam ǀ me ǀ yuvā́bhyām ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of you, (Soma) has genitive rated all beings; the other proceeds looking upon the universe: Soma and Pūṣaṇ, protect my (pious) rite; through you, may we overcome all the hosts of our enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: One of you, (Soma) has genitive rated all beings; the other proceeds looking upon the universe: Soma and Pūṣaṇ, protect my (pious) rite; through you, may we overcome all the hosts of our enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धियं पूषा जिन्वतु विश्वमिन्वो रयिं सोमो रयिपतिर्दधातु ।अवतु देव्यदितिरनर्वा बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhíyam ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ jinvatu ǀ viśvam-inváḥ ǀ rayím ǀ sómaḥ ǀ rayi-pátiḥ ǀ dadhātu ǀávatu ǀ devī́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ anarvā́ ǀ bṛhát ǀ vadema ǀ vidáthe ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Pūṣaṇ, who is the benefactor of all, be propitious to (this pious) rite; may Soma, the lord of wealth, grant us affluence; may Aditi, who is without an adversary, protect us, so that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify (you) at this sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣaṇ, who is the benefactor of all, be propitious to (this pious) rite; may Soma, the lord of wealth, grant us affluence; may Aditi, who is without an adversary, protect us, so that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify (you) at this sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Various Deities.
hymns.anukramani: २१ गृत्समद (आङ्गिरसः शौनहोत्रः पश्चाद्) भार्गवः शौनकः। १-२ वायुः, ३ इंद्रवायू, ४-६ मित्रावरुणौ, ७-९ अश्विनौ, १०-१२ इन्द्रः, १३-१५ विश्वेदेवाः,  १६-१८ सरस्वती, १९-२१ द्यावापृथिव्यौ हविर्धाने वाः (१९ तृतीयपादस्य अग्निर्वा)।गायत्री, १६-१७ अनुष्टुप्, १८ बृहती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O VĀYU, come to us with all the thousand chariots that are thine,Team-borne, to drink the Soma juice. Drawn by thy team, O Vāyu, come; to thee is offered this, the pure.Thou visitest the presser's house. Indra and Vāyu, drawn by teams, ye Heroes, come today and drink.Of the bright juice when blent with milk. This Soma hath been shed for you, Law-strengtheners, Mitra-Varuṇa!Listen ye here to this my call. Both Kings who never injure aught seat them in their supremest home,The thousand-pillared, firmly-based. Fed with oblation, Sovran Kings, Ādityas, Lords of liberal gifts.They wait on him whose life is true. With kine, Nāsatyas, and with steeds, come, Aśvins, Rudras, to the houseThat will protect its heroes well; Such, wealthy Gods! as none afar nor standing nigh to us may harm,Yea, no malicious mortal foe. As such, O longed-far Aśvins, lead us on to wealth of varied sort,Wealth that shall bring us room and rest. Verily Indra, conquering all, driveth e’en mighty fear away,For firm is he and swift to act. Indra be gracious unto us: sin shall not reach us afterward,And good shall be before us still. From all the regions of the world let Indra send security,The foe-subduer, swift to act. O all ye Gods, come hitherward: hear this mine invocation, seatYourselves upon this sacred grass. Among the Śunahotras strong for you is this sweet gladdening draught.Drink ye of this delightsome juice. YeMarutsled by Indra, Gods with Pūṣan for your bounteousest,Hear all of you this call of mine. Best Mother, best of Rivers, best of Goddesses, Sarasvatī, We are, as ’twere, of no repute and dear Mother, give thou us renown. In thee, Sarasvatī, divine, all generations have their stay.Be, glad with Śunahotra's sons: O Goddess grant us progeny. Enriched with sacrifice, accept Sarasvatī, these prayers of ours,Thoughts which Gṛtsamadas beloved of Gods bring, Holy One, to thee. Ye who bless sacrifice, go forth, for verily we choose you both,And Agni who conveys our gifts. This our effectual sacrifice, reaching the sky, shall Heaven and EarthPresent unto the Gods to-day. In both your laps, ye guileless Ones, the Holy Gods shall sit them downTo-day to drink the Soma here.

verses.sanskrit: वायो ये ते सहस्रिणो रथासस्तेभिरा गहि ।नियुत्वान्त्सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́yo íti ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ sahasríṇaḥ ǀ ráthāsaḥ ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀniyútvān ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāyu, whose are a thousand chariots, and the Niyutsteeds, come to drink the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāyu, whose are a thousand chariots, and the Niyutsteeds, come to drink the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नियुत्वान्वायवा गह्ययं शुक्रो अयामि ते ।गंतासि सुन्वतो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: niyútvān ǀ vāyo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ ayám ǀ śukráḥ ǀ ayāmi ǀ te ǀgántā ǀ asi ǀ sunvatáḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāyu,of the Niyutsteds, approach; this bright (juice) has been accepted by you, for you go to the dwelling of the offerer of the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāyu,of the Niyutsteds, approach; this bright (juice) has been accepted by you, for you go to the dwelling of the offerer of the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुक्रस्याद्य गवाशिर इंद्रवायू नियुत्वतः ।आ यातं पिबतं नरा ॥
verses.transliteration: śukrásya ǀ adyá ǀ gó-āśiraḥ ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ niyútvataḥ ǀā́ ǀ yātam ǀ píbatam ǀ narā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leaders (of rites),Indraand Vāyu, lords of the Niyutsteeds, come and drink today the mixture of milk and of the pure Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of rites),Indraand Vāyu, lords of the Niyutsteeds, come and drink today the mixture of milk and of the pure Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं वां मित्रावरुणा सुतः सोम ऋतावृधा ।ममेदिह श्रुतं हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ sutáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛdhā ǀmáma ǀ ít ǀ ihá ǀ śrutam ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This libation is offered to you,Mitraand Varuṇa, cherishers of truth; hear, verily, this my present invocatioṇ
verses.wilson_translation: This libation is offered to you,Mitraand Varuṇa, cherishers of truth; hear, verily, this my present invocatioṇ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: राजानावनभिद्रुहा ध्रुवे सदस्युत्तमे ।सहस्रस्थूण आसाते ॥
verses.transliteration: rā́jānau ǀ ánabhi-druhā ǀ dhruvé ǀ sádasi ǀ ut-tamé ǀsahásra-sthūṇe ǀ āsāte íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sovereigns, exercising no oppression, sit down in this substantial and elegant hall, (built) with a thousand columns.
verses.wilson_translation: Sovereigns, exercising no oppression, sit down in this substantial and elegant hall, (built) with a thousand columns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता सम्राजा घृतासुती आदित्या दानुनस्पती ।सचेते अनवह्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ sam-rā́jā ǀ ghṛtā́sutī íti ghṛtá-āsutī ǀ ādityā́ ǀ dā́nunaḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀsácete íti ǀ ánava-hvaram ǁ
verses.english_translation: May these two universal monarchs, fed with clarified butter, sons of Aditi, lords of liberality, show favour to their sincere (worshipper).
verses.wilson_translation: May these two universal monarchs, fed with clarified butter, sons of Aditi, lords of liberality, show favour to their sincere (worshipper).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गोमदू षु नासत्याश्वावद्यातमश्विना ।वर्ती रुद्रा नृपाय्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: gó-mat ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ nāsatyā ǀ áśva-vat ǀ yātam ǀ aśvinā ǀvartíḥ ǀ rudrā ǀ nṛ-pā́yyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aśvins, in whom there is no untruth;Rudras, go by the (direct) road to (the sacrifice at which the libation) is to be drunk by the leaders (of sacred rite), for which (the offerer may receive the reward of) cows and horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, in whom there is no untruth;Rudras, go by the (direct) road to (the sacrifice at which the libation) is to be drunk by the leaders (of sacred rite), for which (the offerer may receive the reward of) cows and horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न यत्परो नांतर आदधर्षद्वृषण्वसू ।दुःशंसो मर्त्यो रिपुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yát ǀ páraḥ ǀ ná ǀ ántaraḥ ǀ ā-dadhárṣat ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀduḥ-śáṃsaḥ ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ ripúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Showerers of wealth, (bring to us) such (riches) that the malevolent man, or foe, whether he be far off or nigh, may not take (it) away.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerers of wealth, (bring to us) such (riches) that the malevolent man, or foe, whether he be far off or nigh, may not take (it) away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता न आ वोळ्हमश्विना रयिं पिशंगसंदृशं ।धिष्ण्या वरिवोविदं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ voḷham ǀ aśvinā ǀ rayím ǀ piśáṅga-sandṛśam ǀdhíṣṇyā ǀ varivaḥ-vídam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resolute Aśvins, bring to us riches of various sorts, and wealth begetting wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Resolute Aśvins, bring to us riches of various sorts, and wealth begetting wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो अंग महद्भयमभी षदप चुच्यवत् ।स हि स्थिरो विचर्षणिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ aṅgá ǀ mahát ǀ bhayám ǀ abhí ǀ sát ǀ ápa ǀ cucyavat ǀsáḥ ǀ hí ǀ sthiráḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra, dissipate all great and overpowering danger, for he is resolute, and the beholder of all.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, dissipate all great and overpowering danger, for he is resolute, and the beholder of all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रश्च मृळयाति नो न नः पश्चादघं नशत् ।भद्रं भवाति नः पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ mṛḷáyāti ǀ naḥ ǀ ná ǀ naḥ ǀ paścā́t ǀ aghám ǀ naśat ǀbhadrám ǀ bhavāti ǀ naḥ ǀ puráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: If Indraprovide for our happiness, evil will not come behidn us, good will be before us.
verses.wilson_translation: If Indraprovide for our happiness, evil will not come behidn us, good will be before us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र आशाभ्यस्परि सर्वाभ्यो अभयं करत् ।जेता शत्रून्विचर्षणिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ā́śābhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ sárvābhyaḥ ǀ ábhayam ǀ karat ǀjétā ǀ śátrūn ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Indra, the beholder of all, the conqueror of foes, send us security from all quarters.
verses.wilson_translation: Let Indra, the beholder of all, the conqueror of foes, send us security from all quarters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवास आ गत शृणुता म इमं हवं ।एदं बर्हिर्नि षीदत ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǀ śṛṇutá ǀ me ǀ imám ǀ hávam ǀā́ ǀ idám ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ní ǀ sīdata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Universal gods, come hither; hear this my invocation; sit down upon this sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Universal gods, come hither; hear this my invocation; sit down upon this sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तीव्रो वो मधुमाँ अयं शुनहोत्रेषु मत्सरः ।एतं पिबत काम्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: tīvráḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ ayám ǀ śuná-hotreṣu ǀ matsaráḥ ǀetám ǀ pibata ǀ kā́myam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This sharp, savoury, exhilarating (beverage), is (prepared) for you by the Śunahotras; drink of it at your plural asure.
verses.wilson_translation: This sharp, savoury, exhilarating (beverage), is (prepared) for you by the Śunahotras; drink of it at your plural asure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रज्येष्ठा मरुद्गणा देवासः पूषरातयः ।विश्वे मम श्रुता हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra-jyeṣṭhāḥ ǀ márut-gaṇāḥ ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ pū́ṣa-rātayaḥ ǀvíśve ǀ máma ǀ śruta ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, of whom Indrais the chief; divinities, of whom Pūṣan. is benefactor; do you all hear my invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, of whom Indrais the chief; divinities, of whom Pūṣan. is benefactor; do you all hear my invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अंबितमे नदीतमे देवितमे सरस्वति ।अप्रशस्ता इव स्मसि प्रशस्तिमंब नस्कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: ámbi-tame ǀ nádī-tame ǀ dévi-tame ǀ sárasvati ǀapraśastā́ḥ-iva ǀ smasi ǀ prá-śastim ǀ amba ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sarasvatī, best of mothers, best of rivers, best of goddesses, we are, as it were, of no repute; grant us, mother, distinction.
verses.wilson_translation: Sarasvatī, best of mothers, best of rivers, best of goddesses, we are, as it were, of no repute; grant us, mother, distinction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे विश्वा सरस्वति श्रितायूंषि देव्यां ।शुनहोत्रेषु मत्स्व प्रजां देवि दिदिड्ढि नः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ víśvā ǀ sarasvati ǀ śritā́ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ devyā́m ǀśuná-hotreṣu ǀ matsva ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ devi ǀ didiḍḍhi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In you,Sarasvatī, who are divine, all existences are collected; rejoice, goddess, among the Śunahotras, grant us, goddess, progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: In you,Sarasvatī, who are divine, all existences are collected; rejoice, goddess, among the Śunahotras, grant us, goddess, progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा ब्रह्म सरस्वति जुषस्व वाजिनी��ति ।या ते मन्म गृत्समदा ऋतावरि प्रिया देवेषु जुह्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ ǀ bráhma ǀ sarasvati ǀ juṣásva ǀ vājinī-vati ǀyā́ ǀ te ǀ mánma ǀ gṛtsa-madā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-vari ǀ priyā́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ júhvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sarasvatī, abounding in food, abounding in water, be propitiated by these oblations, which the Gṛtsamadasoffer as acceptable to you, and precious of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Sarasvatī, abounding in food, abounding in water, be propitiated by these oblations, which the Gṛtsamadasoffer as acceptable to you, and precious of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शंभुवा युवामिदा वृणीमहे ।अग्निं च हव्यवाहनं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ itām ǀ yajñásya ǀ śam-bhúvā ǀ yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀagním ǀ ca ǀ havya-vā́hanam ǁ
