verses.english_translation: He who has been made by the sacred rite, the choice (of the worshipper), who comprehends (within himself) the germ of all creatures, and whom the daughter of Dakṣa(receives) as the parent of the world.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has been made by the sacred rite, the choice (of the worshipper), who comprehends (within himself) the germ of all creatures, and whom the daughter of Dakṣa(receives) as the parent of the world.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि त्वा दधे वरेण्यं दक्षस्येळा सहस्कृत ।अग्ने सुदीतिमुशिजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tvā ǀ dadhe ǀ váreṇyam ǀ dákṣasya ǀ iḷā́ ǀ sahaḥ-kṛta ǀágne ǀ su-dītím ǀ uśíjam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, strength-engendered, Iḷā (the daughter) of Dakṣahas sustained you, the desirable, the resplendent, and longing (for the oblation).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, strength-engendered, Iḷā (the daughter) of Dakṣahas sustained you, the desirable, the resplendent, and longing (for the oblation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं यंतुरमप्तुरमृतस्य योगे वनुषः ।विप्रा वाजैः समिंधते ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ yantúram ǀ ap-túram ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yóge ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀvíprāḥ ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ sám ǀ indhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wise (priests) performers (of the ceremony) kindle with oblations for the due celebration of the rite,Agni, the regulator (of all), the sender of the rain.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise (priests) performers (of the ceremony) kindle with oblations for the due celebration of the rite,Agni, the regulator (of all), the sender of the rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्जो नपातमध्वरे दीदिवांसमुप द्यवि ।अग्निमीळे कविक्रतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrjáḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ adhvaré ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀagním ǀ īḷe ǀ kaví-kratum ǁ
verses.english_translation: I adore at this sacrifice Agnithe grandson of (sacrificial) food, shining above in the firmament, the creation of the wise.
verses.wilson_translation: I adore at this sacrifice Agnithe grandson of (sacrificial) food, shining above in the firmament, the creation of the wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईळेन्यो नमस्यस्तिरस्तमांसि दर्शतः ।समग्निरिध्यते वृषा ॥
verses.transliteration: īḷényaḥ ǀ namasyáḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ támāṃsi ǀ darśatáḥ ǀsám ǀ agníḥ ǀ idhyate ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who is to be worshipped with praise and with prostration, the dispeller of darkness, the beautiful, the showerer (of benefits) is kindled.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who is to be worshipped with praise and with prostration, the dispeller of darkness, the beautiful, the showerer (of benefits) is kindled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृषो अग्निः समिध्यतेऽश्वो न देववाहनः ।तं हविष्मंत ईळते ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣo íti ǀ agníḥ ǀ sám ǀ idhyate ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ deva-vā́hanaḥ ǀtám ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ īḷate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The offerers of oblations glorify that Agniwho is the showerer (of benefits) and is the bearer of the offerings to the gods as a horse (bears his rider to his home).
verses.wilson_translation: The offerers of oblations glorify that Agniwho is the showerer (of benefits) and is the bearer of the offerings to the gods as a horse (bears his rider to his home).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृषणं त्वा वयं वृषन्वृषणः समिधीमहि ।अग्ने दीद्यतं बृहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ vṛṣan ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ idhīmahi ǀágne ǀ dī́dyatam ǀ bṛhát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Showerer (of benefits) we profusely offering (oblations) kindle you mighty and resplendent Agni, who is the sender of showers.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerer (of benefits) we profusely offering (oblations) kindle you mighty and resplendent Agni, who is the sender of showers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVIII. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ६ गाथिनो विश्वामित्रः। अग्निः।१-२, ६ गायत्री, ३ उष्णिक्, ४ त्रिष्टुप्, ५ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI who knowest all, accept our offering and the cake of meal,At dawn's libation, rich in prayer! Agni, the sacrificial cake hath been prepared and dressed for thee:Accept it, O Most Youthful God. Agni, enjoy the cake of meal and our oblation three days old:Thou, Son of Strength, art stablished at our sacrifice. Here at the midday sacrifice enjoy thou the sacrificial cake, wise, Jātavedas!Agni, the sages in assemblies never minish the portion due to thee the Mighty. O Agni, at the third libation takewith joy the offered cake of sacrifice, thou, Son of Strength.Through skill in song bear to the Gods our sacrifice, watchful and fraught with riches, to Immortal God. O waxing Agni, knower, thou, of all, accept our gifts, the cake,And that prepared ere yesterday.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः पुरोळाशं जातवेदः ।प्रातःसावे धियावसो ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ juṣásva ǀ naḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀprātaḥ-sāvé ǀ dhiyāvaso íti dhiyā-vaso ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, by whom all is known, who rewards pious acts with wealth, accept our cakes offered with butter at the morning worships.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, by whom all is known, who rewards pious acts with wealth, accept our cakes offered with butter at the morning worships.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोळा अग्ने पचतस्तुभ्यं वा घा परिष्कृतः ।तं जुषस्व यविष्ठ्य ॥
verses.transliteration: puroḷā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ pacatáḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ pári-kṛtaḥ ǀtám ǀ juṣasva ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The cakes and butter are dressed,Agni, and verily prepared for you; accept them youngest (of the gods).
verses.wilson_translation: The cakes and butter are dressed,Agni, and verily prepared for you; accept them youngest (of the gods).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने वीहि पुरोळाशमाहुतं तिरोअह्न्यं ।सहसः सूनुरस्यध्वरे हितः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ vīhí ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ tiráḥ-ahnyam ǀsáhasaḥ ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ asi ǀ adhvaré ǀ hitáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eat,Agni, the cakes and butter offered as the day disappears; you, son of strength, are stationed (by us) at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Eat,Agni, the cakes and butter offered as the day disappears; you, son of strength, are stationed (by us) at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: माध्यंदिने सवने जातवेदः पुरोळाशमिह कवे जुषस्व ।अग्ने यह्वस्य तव भागधेयं न प्र मिनंति विदथेषु धीराः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́dhyandine ǀ sávane ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ ihá ǀ kave ǀ juṣasva ǀágne ǀ yahvásya ǀ táva ǀ bhāga-dhéyam ǀ ná ǀ prá ǀ minanti ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise Jātavedasaccept the cakes and butter offered in this sacrifice at the mid-day rite; prudent (worshippers), withhold not at solemn ceremonies the portion of you who are mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: Wise Jātavedasaccept the cakes and butter offered in this sacrifice at the mid-day rite; prudent (worshippers), withhold not at solemn ceremonies the portion of you who are mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने तृतीये सवने हि कानिषः पुरोळाशं सहसः सूनवाहुतं ।अथा देवेष्वध्वरं विपन्यया धा रत्नवंतममृतेषु जागृविं ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ tṛtī́ye ǀ sávane ǀ hí ǀ kā́niṣaḥ ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ ā́-hutam ǀátha ǀ devéṣu ǀ adhvarám ǀ vipanyáyā ǀ dhā́ḥ ǀ rátna-vantam ǀ amṛ́teṣu ǀ jā́gṛvim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be plural ased,Agni, son of strength, with the cakes and butter offered at the third (daily sacrifice), and do you (propitiated) by praise convey the precious imperishable and awakening (oblation) to the immortal gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Be plural ased,Agni, son of strength, with the cakes and butter offered at the third (daily sacrifice), and do you (propitiated) by praise convey the precious imperishable and awakening (oblation) to the immortal gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने वृधान आहुतिं पुरोळाशं जातवेदः ।जुषस्व तिरोअह्न्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ ā́-hutim ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀjuṣásva ǀ tiráḥ-ahnyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniwho is Jātavedasand is thriving upon oblations accept the cakes the butter as the day disappears.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniwho is Jātavedasand is thriving upon oblations accept the cakes the butter as the day disappears.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HERE is the gear for friction, here tinder made ready for the spark.Bring thou the Matron: we will rub Agni in ancient fashion forth.n the two fire-sticks Jātavedas lieth, even as the well-set germ in pregnant women,Agni who day by day must be exalted by men who watch and worship with oblations. Lay this with care on that which lies extended: straight hath she borne the Steer when made prolific.With his red pillar—radiant is his splendour—in our skilled task is born the Son of Iḷā. In Iḷā's place we set thee down, upon the central point of earth,That, Agni Jātavedas, thou mayst bear our offerings to the Gods. Rub into life, ye men, the Sage, the guileless, Immortal, very wise and fair to look on.O men, bring forth the most propitious Agni, first ensign of the sacrifice to eastward. When with their arms they rub him straight he shineth forth like a strong courser, red in colour, in the wood.Bright, checkless, as it were upon the Aśvins' path, he passeth by the stones and burneth up the grass. Agni shines forth when born, observant, mighty, the bountiful, the Singer praised by sages;Whom, as adorable and knowing all things, Gods set at solemn rites as offering-bearer. Set thee, O Priest, in, thine own place, observant: lay down the sacrifice in the home of worship.Thou, dear to Gods, shalt serve them with oblation: Agni, give long life to the sacrificer. Raise ye a mighty smoke, my fellow-workers! Ye shall attain to wealth without obstruction.This Agni is the battle-winning Hero by whom the Gods have overcome the Dasyus. This is thine ordered place of birth whence sprung to life thou shonest forth.Knowing this, Agni, sit thee down, and prosper thou the songs we sing. As Germ Celestial he is called Tanūnapāt, and Narāśaṁsa born diffused in varied shape.Formed in his Mother he is Mātariśvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind. With strong attrition rubbed to life, laid down with careful hand, a Sage,Agni, make sacrifices good, and for the pious bring the Gods. Mortals have brought to life the God Immortal, the Conqueror with mighty jaws, unfailing.The sisters ten, unwedded and united, together grasp the Babe, the new-born Infant. Served by the seven priests, he shone forth from ancient time, when in his Mother's bosom, in her lap, he glowed.Giving delight each day he closeth not his eye, since from the Asura's body hewas brought to life. Even as the Maruts, onslaughts who attack the foe, those born the first of all knew the full power of prayer.The Kuśikas have made the glorious hymn ascend, and, each one singly in his home, have kindled fire. As we, O Priest observant, have elected thee this day, what time the solemn sacrifice began,So surely hast thou worshipped, surely hast thou toiled: come thou unto the Soma, wise and knowing all.

verses.sanskrit: अस्तीदमधिमंथनमस्ति प्रजननं कृतं ।एतां विश्पत्नीमा भराग्निं मंथाम पूर्वथा ॥
verses.transliteration: ásti ǀ idám ǀ adhi-mánthanam ǀ ásti ǀ pra-jánanam ǀ kṛtám ǀetā́m ǀ viśpátnīm ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ agním ǀ manthāma ǀ pūrvá-thā ǁ
verses.english_translation: This, the apparatus of attrition is ready; the genitive ration (of the flame) is ready; take up this (stick) the protectress of mankind, and let us churn the fire as has been done of old.
verses.wilson_translation: This, the apparatus of attrition is ready; the genitive ration (of the flame) is ready; take up this (stick) the protectress of mankind, and let us churn the fire as has been done of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुधितो गर्भिणीषु ।दिवेदिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ॥
verses.transliteration: aráṇyoḥ ǀ ní-hitaḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ gárbhaḥ-iva ǀ sú-dhitaḥ ǀ garbhíṇīṣu ǀdivé-dive ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ jāgṛvát-bhiḥ ǀ havíṣmat-bhiḥ ǀ manuṣyébhiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Jātavedashas been deposited in the two sticks as the embryo is deposited in pregnant women;Agniis to be adored day by day by vigilant men laden with oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Jātavedashas been deposited in the two sticks as the embryo is deposited in pregnant women;Agniis to be adored day by day by vigilant men laden with oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्त्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान ।अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट ॥
verses.transliteration: uttānā́yām ǀ áva ǀ bhara ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ prá-vītā ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ jajāna ǀaruṣá-stūpaḥ ǀ rúśat ǀ asya ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ íḷāyāḥ ǀ putráḥ ǀ vayúne ǀ ajaniṣṭa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the intelligent priest plural ce the lower of the sticks with the face upwards, the upper (with the surface) downwards, so that quickly impregnated it may genitive rate the showerer (of benefits)Agni; then the bright blazing son of Iḷā whose light dissipates the darkness is born of the wood of attrition.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the intelligent priest plural ce the lower of the sticks with the face upwards, the upper (with the surface) downwards, so that quickly impregnated it may genitive rate the showerer (of benefits)Agni; then the bright blazing son of Iḷā whose light dissipates the darkness is born of the wood of attrition.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इळायास्त्वा पदे वयं नाभा पृथिव्या अधि ।जातवेदो नि धीमह्यग्ने हव्याय वोळ्हवे ॥
verses.transliteration: íḷāyāḥ ǀ tvā ǀ padé ǀ vayám ǀ nā́bhā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀjā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ ní ǀ dhīmahi ǀ ágne ǀ havyā́ya ǀ vóḷhave ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniwho is Jātavedas, we plural ce you upon the earth in the centre, in the plural ce of Iḷā, for the purpose of receiving the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniwho is Jātavedas, we plural ce you upon the earth in the centre, in the plural ce of Iḷā, for the purpose of receiving the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मंथता नरः कविमद्वयंतं प्रचेतसममृतं सुप्रतीकं ।यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं पुरस्तादग्निं नरो जनयता सुशेवं ॥
verses.transliteration: mánthata ǀ naraḥ ǀ kavím ǀ ádvayantam ǀ prá-cetasam ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ su-prátīkam ǀyajñásya ǀ ketúm ǀ prathamám ǀ purástāt ǀ agním ǀ naraḥ ǀ janayata ǀ su-śévam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Conductors of the rite, produce by attrition the far-seeing, single-minded, intelligent, immortal, radiant-limbed Agni; genitive rate him, leaders (of the solemnity), in the first plural ce the chief standard of the sacrifice, who is the source of felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Conductors of the rite, produce by attrition the far-seeing, single-minded, intelligent, immortal, radiant-limbed Agni; genitive rate him, leaders (of the solemnity), in the first plural ce the chief standard of the sacrifice, who is the source of felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदी मंथंति बाहुभिर्वि रोचतेऽश्वो न वाज्यरुषो वनेष्वा ।चित्रो न यामन्नश्विनोरनिवृतः परि वृणक्त्यश्मनस्तृणा दहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: yádi ǀ mánthanti ǀ bāhú-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ rocate ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vājī́ ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ váneṣu ǀ ā́ ǀcitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́man ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ áni-vṛtaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vṛṇakti ǀ áśmanaḥ ǀ tṛ́ṇā ǀ dáhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they rub (the sticks) with their arms the radiant Agnibursts forth from the wood like a fleet courser, and like the many-coloured car of the Aśvinsunresisted in its course, Agni spreads wide around consuming stones and trees.
verses.wilson_translation: When they rub (the sticks) with their arms the radiant Agnibursts forth from the wood like a fleet courser, and like the many-coloured car of the Aśvinsunresisted in its course, Agni spreads wide around consuming stones and trees.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जातो अग्नी रोचते चेकितानो वाजी विप्रः कविशस्तः सुदानुः ।यं देवास ईड्यं विश्वविदं हव्यवाहमदधुरध्वरेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: jātáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ rocate ǀ cékitānaḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ kavi-śastáḥ ǀ su-dā́nuḥ ǀyám ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ī́ḍyam ǀ viśva-vídam ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: As soon as born Agni, shines intelligent, swift-moving, skilled in rites, praised by the wise, and liberal in gifts; (and it is he) whom the gods have held as the bearer of oblations at sacrifices, adorable and all-knowing.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as born Agni, shines intelligent, swift-moving, skilled in rites, praised by the wise, and liberal in gifts; (and it is he) whom the gods have held as the bearer of oblations at sacrifices, adorable and all-knowing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान्त्सादया यज्ञं सुकृतस्य योनौ ।देवावीर्देवान्हविषा यजास्यग्ने बृहद्यजमाने वयो धाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sī́da ǀ hotaríti ǀ své ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ loké ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ sādáya ǀ yajñám ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ yónau ǀdeva-avī́ḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ havíṣā ǀ yajāsi ǀ ágne ǀ bṛhát ǀ yájamāne ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offerer of oblations sit down in your own sphere, for you are cognizant (of holy acts), and station the instrumental tutor of the ceremony in the chief plural ce of the sacred rite; cherisher of the gods, worship the gods,Agni, and bestow abundant food on the founder of the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Offerer of oblations sit down in your own sphere, for you are cognizant (of holy acts), and station the instrumental tutor of the ceremony in the chief plural ce of the sacred rite; cherisher of the gods, worship the gods,Agni, and bestow abundant food on the founder of the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृणोत धूमं वृषणं सखायोऽस्रेधंत इतन वाजमच्छ ।अयमग्निः पृतनाषाट् सुवीरो येन देवासो असहंत दस्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṇóta ǀ dhūmám ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ ásredhantaḥ ǀ itana ǀ vā́jam ǀ áccha ǀayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ pṛtanāṣā́ṭ ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǀ yéna ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ásahanta ǀ dásyūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: Produce, friends, smoke, the showerer (of benefits); indefatigable person st in the contest with (Agni); the heroic Agni is able to encounter hosts, and by him the gods overcome their foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Produce, friends, smoke, the showerer (of benefits); indefatigable person st in the contest with (Agni); the heroic Agni is able to encounter hosts, and by him the gods overcome their foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं ते योनिर्ऋत्वियो यतो जातो अरोचथाः ।तं जानन्नग्न आ सीदाथा नो वर्धया गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ te ǀ yóniḥ ǀ ṛtvíyaḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ árocathāḥ ǀtám ǀ jānán ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ sīda ǀ átha ǀ naḥ ǀ vardhaya ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This in every season,Agni, is your plural ce, whence, as soon as genitive rated, you have ever shone; knowing that to be so, Agni, there abide, and thrive by our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: This in every season,Agni, is your plural ce, whence, as soon as genitive rated, you have ever shone; knowing that to be so, Agni, there abide, and thrive by our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तनूनपादुच्यते गर्भ आसुरो नराशंसो भवति यद्विजायते ।मातरिश्वा यदमिमीत मातरि वातस्य सर्गो अभवत्सरीमणि ॥
verses.transliteration: tanū́-nápāt ǀ ucyate ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ āsuráḥ ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ yát ǀ vi-jā́yate ǀmātaríśvā ǀ yát ǀ ámimīta ǀ mātári ǀ vā́tasya ǀ sárgaḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ sárīmaṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: When (existing) as an embryo (in the wood),Agniis called Tanunapāt; when he is genitive rated (he is called) theasura-destroying narāśam,sa; when he has displayed (his energy) in the material firmament,Mātariśvan; and the creation of the wind is in his rapid motion.
verses.wilson_translation: When (existing) as an embryo (in the wood),Agniis called Tanunapāt; when he is genitive rated (he is called) theasura-destroying narāśam,sa; when he has displayed (his energy) in the material firmament,Mātariśvan; and the creation of the wind is in his rapid motion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुनिर्मथा निर्मथितः सुनिधा निहितः कविः ।अग्ने स्वध्वरा कृणु देवांदेवयते यज ॥
verses.transliteration: suniḥ-máthā ǀ níḥ-mathitaḥ ǀ su-nidhā́ ǀ ní-hitaḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀágne ǀ su-adhvarā́ ǀ kṛṇu ǀ devā́n ǀ deva-yaté ǀ yaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who is pronounced by reverential attrition, and deposited with reverential care, and who are far-seeing, render our rites (exempt from defects), and worship the gods (on behalf) of the devout worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who is pronounced by reverential attrition, and deposited with reverential care, and who are far-seeing, render our rites (exempt from defects), and worship the gods (on behalf) of the devout worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अजीजनन्नमृतं मर्त्यासोऽस्रेमाणं तरणिं वीळुजंभं ।दश स्वसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमांसं जातमभि सं रभंते ॥
verses.transliteration: ájījanan ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ mártyāsaḥ ǀ asremā́ṇam ǀ taráṇim ǀ vīḷú-jambham ǀdáśa ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ sam-īcī́ḥ ǀ púmāṃsam ǀ jātám ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ rabhante ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mortals have begotten the immortals, the undecaying (Agni), the devourer of oblations, the conveyance (by which they cross over sin), the ten sister fingers intertwined proclaim him born as if it was amale(infant).
verses.wilson_translation: Mortals have begotten the immortals, the undecaying (Agni), the devourer of oblations, the conveyance (by which they cross over sin), the ten sister fingers intertwined proclaim him born as if it was amale(infant).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सप्तहोता सनकादरोचत मातुरुपस्थे यदशोचदूधनि ।न नि मिषति सुरणो दिवेदिवे यदसुरस्य जठरादजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ saptá-hotā ǀ sanakā́t ǀ arocata ǀ mātúḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ yát ǀ áśocat ǀ ū́dhani ǀná ǀ ní ǀ miṣati ǀ su-ráṇaḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ yát ǀ ásurasya ǀ jaṭhárāt ǀ ájāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who has seven ministering priests, shines eternally; when he has blazed upon the bosom and lap of his mother (earth), he is vociferous (with delight); day by day he never slumbers after he is born from the interior of the (spark) emitting wood.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who has seven ministering priests, shines eternally; when he has blazed upon the bosom and lap of his mother (earth), he is vociferous (with delight); day by day he never slumbers after he is born from the interior of the (spark) emitting wood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अमित्रायुधो मरुतामिव प्रयाः प्रथमजा ब्रह्मणो विश्वमिद्विदुः ।द्युम्नवद्ब्रह्म कुशिकास एरिर एकएको दमे अग्निं समीधिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: amitra-yúdhaḥ ǀ marútām-iva ǀ pra-yā́ḥ ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ít ǀ viduḥ ǀdyumná-vat ǀ bráhma ǀ kuśikā́saḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īrire ǀ ékaḥ-ekaḥ ǀ dáme ǀ agním ǀ sám ǀ īdhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Kuśikas, the first-born of Brahmā, armed against enemies like the energies of the Maruts, comprehend the universe; they have uttered the prayer accompanied by the oblation; they have one by one lighted Agniin this dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: The Kuśikas, the first-born of Brahmā, armed against enemies like the energies of the Maruts, comprehend the universe; they have uttered the prayer accompanied by the oblation; they have one by one lighted Agniin this dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदद्य त्वा प्रयति यज्ञे अस्मिन्होतश्चिकित्वोऽवृणीमहीह ।ध्रुवमया ध्रुवमुताशमिष्ठाः प्रजानन्विद्वाँ उप याहि सोमं ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ adyá ǀ tvā ǀ pra-yatí ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀ hótaríti ǀ cikitvaḥ ǀ ávṛṇīmahi ǀ ihá ǀdhruvám ǀ ayāḥ ǀ dhruvám ǀ utá ǀ aśamiṣṭhāḥ ǀ pra-jānán ǀ vidvā́n ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ sómam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, offerer of oblations, cognizant of rites, inasmuch as we have recourse to you today in this progressing sacrifice, therefore do you steadily convey (the offering to the gods), or tranquilly be at rest, and knowing (the purport of our acts), and wise (in all respects), approach (and accept) the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, offerer of oblations, cognizant of rites, inasmuch as we have recourse to you today in this progressing sacrifice, therefore do you steadily convey (the offering to the gods), or tranquilly be at rest, and knowing (the purport of our acts), and wise (in all respects), approach (and accept) the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE friends who offer Soma long to find thee: they pour forth Soma and present their viands.They bear unmoved the cursing of the people, for all our wisdom comes from thee, O Indra. Not far for thee are mid-air's loftiest regions: start hither, Lord of Bays, with thy Bay Horses.Made for the Firm and Strong are these libations. The pressing-stones are set and fire is kindled. Fair cheeks hath Indra, Maghavan, the Victor, Lord of a great host, Stormer, strong in action.What once thou didst in might when mortals vexed thee,—where now, O Bull, are those thy hero exploits? For, overthrowing what hath ne’er been shaken, thou goest forth alone destroying Vṛtras.For him who followeth thy Law the mountains and heaven and earth stand as if firmly stablished. Yea, Much-invoked! in safety through thy glories alone thou speakest truth as Vṛtra's slayer.E’en these two boundless worlds to thee, O Indra, what time thou graspest them, are but a handful. Forthwith thy Bay steeds down the steep, O Indra, forth, crushing foemen, go thy bolt of thunder!Slay those who meet thee, those who flee, who follow: make all thy promise true; be all completed. The man to whom thou givest as Provider enjoys domestic plenty undivided.Blest, Indra, is thy favour dropping fatness: thy worship, Much-invoked! brings gifts in thousands. Thou, Indra, Much-invoked! didst crush to pieces Kunaru handless fiend who dwelt with Danu.Thou with might, Indra, smotest dead the scorner, the footless Vṛtra as he waxed in vigour. Thou hast established in her seat, O Indra, the level earth, vast, vigorous, unbounded.The Bull hath propped the heaven and air's mid-region. By thee sent onward let the floods flow hither. He who withheld the kine, in silence I yielded in fear before thy blow, O Indra.He made paths easy to drive forth the cattle. Loud-breathing praises helped the Much-invoked One. Indra alone filled full the earth and heaven, the Pair who meet together, rich in treasures.Yea, bring thou near us from the air's mid-region strength, on thy car, and wholesome food, O Hero. Sūrya transgresses not the ordered limits set daily by the Lord of Tawny Coursers.When to the goal he comes, his journey ended, his Steeds he looses: this is Indra's doing. Men gladly in the course of night would look on the broad bright front of the refulgent Morning;And all acknowledge, when she comes in glory, the manifold and goodly works of Indra. A mighty splendour rests upon her bosom: bearing ripe milk the Cow, unripe, advances.All sweetness is collected in the Heifer, sweetness which Indra made for our enjoyment. Barring the way they come. Be firm, O Indra; aid friends to sacrifice and him who singeth.These must be slain by thee, malignant mortals, armed with ill arts, our quiverbearing foemen. A cry is beard from enemies most near us: against them send thy fiercest-flaming weapon.Rend them from under, crush them and subdue them. Slay, Maghavan, and make the fiends our booty. Root up the race of Rākṣasas, O Indra rend it in front and crush it in the middle.How long hast thou bebaved as one who wavers? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion: When borne by strong Steeds for our weal, O Leader, thou seatest thee at many noble viands.May we be winners of abundant riches. May Indra be our wealth with store of children. Bestow on us resplendent wealth. O Indra let us enjoy thine overflow of bounty.Wide as a sea our longing hath expanded, fulfil it, O thou Treasure-Lord of treasures. With kine and horses satisfy this longing with very splendid bounty skill extend it.Seeking the light, with hymns to thee, O Indra, Kuśikas have brought their gift, the singers. Lord of the kine, burst the kine's stable open: cows shall be ours, and strength that wins the booty.Hero, whose might is true, thy home is heaven: to us, O Maghavan, grant gifts of cattle. Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

verses.sanskrit: इच्छंति त्वा सोम्यासः सखायः सुन्वंति सोमं दधति प्रयांसि ।तितिक्षंते अभिशस्तिं जनानामिंद्र त्वदा कश्चन हि प्रकेतः ॥
verses.transliteration: icchánti ǀ tvā ǀ somyā́saḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ sunvánti ǀ sómam ǀ dádhati ǀ práyāṃsi ǀtítikṣante ǀ abhí-śastim ǀ jánānām ǀ índra ǀ tvát ǀ ā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǀ hí ǀ pra-ketáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bearers of the libations desire you; your friends pour forth the Soma; they offer copious oblations; (supported by) you they endure patiently the calumny of men, for who is so renowned as you are.
verses.wilson_translation: The bearers of the libations desire you; your friends pour forth the Soma; they offer copious oblations; (supported by) you they endure patiently the calumny of men, for who is so renowned as you are.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न ते दूरे परमा चिद्रजांस्या तु प्र याहि हरिवो हरिभ्यां ।स्थिराय वृष्णे सवना कृतेमा युक्ता ग्रावाणः समिधाने अग्नौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ te ǀ dūré ǀ paramā́ ǀ cit ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ ā́ ǀ tú ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀsthirā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ sávanā ǀ kṛtā́ ǀ imā́ ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ sam-idhāné ǀ agnáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Master of tawny steeds, the remotest regions are not remote for you; then come quickly with your horses; to you the steady showerer (of benefits), these sacrifices are presented; the stones (for bruising the Soma) are ready, as the fire is being kindled.
verses.wilson_translation: Master of tawny steeds, the remotest regions are not remote for you; then come quickly with your horses; to you the steady showerer (of benefits), these sacrifices are presented; the stones (for bruising the Soma) are ready, as the fire is being kindled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रः सुशिप्रो मघवा तरुत्रो महाव्रातस्तुविकूर्मिर्ऋघावान् ।यदुग्रो धा बाधितो मर्त्येषु क्व त्या ते वृषभ वीर्याणि ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ su-śípraḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ tárutraḥ ǀ mahā́-vrātaḥ ǀ tuvi-kūrmíḥ ǀ ṛ́ghāvān ǀyát ǀ ugráḥ ǀ dhā́ḥ ǀ bādhitáḥ ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ kvá ǀ tyā́ ǀ te ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Showerer (of benefits), who are Indra, the wearer of the helmet, the professor of opulence, the conveyor (of men beyond the evil), the leader of the numerous troops (of the Maruts), the achiever of many great deeds, the devastation of hostile (regions), the terror of your foes, where are those heroic deeds (which you have performed) against the mortal (asuras) when opposed (by them in battle).
verses.wilson_translation: Showerer (of benefits), who are Indra, the wearer of the helmet, the professor of opulence, the conveyor (of men beyond the evil), the leader of the numerous troops (of the Maruts), the achiever of many great deeds, the devastation of hostile (regions), the terror of your foes, where are those heroic deeds (which you have performed) against the mortal (asuras) when opposed (by them in battle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि ष्मा च्यावयन्नच्युतान्येको वृत्रा चरसि जिघ्नमानः ।तव द्यावापृथिवी पर्वतासोऽनु व्रताय निमितेव तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ cyaváyan ǀ ácyutāni ǀ ékaḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ cárasi ǀ jíghnamānaḥ ǀtáva ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vratā́ya ǀ nímitā-iva ǀ tasthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You alone casting down the firmly-footed (asuras) proceed, destroying the Vṛtras, and obedient to your command the heaven and earth and the mountains stood as if immoveable.
verses.wilson_translation: You alone casting down the firmly-footed (asuras) proceed, destroying the Vṛtras, and obedient to your command the heaven and earth and the mountains stood as if immoveable.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् ।इमे चिदिंद्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन्काशिरित्ते ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ ábhaye ǀ puru-hūta ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ dṛḷhám ǀ avadaḥ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ sán ǀimé ǀ cit ǀ indra ǀ ródasī íti ǀ apāré íti ǀ yát ǀ sam-gṛbhṇā́ḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ kāśíḥ ǀ ít ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: You alone, when invoked by many, and the slayer of Vṛtra, by your prowess, did say firmly (to the gods), fear not!Indra, endowed with opulence, vast is your grasp, wherewith you have seized these unbounded regions, heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: You alone, when invoked by many, and the slayer of Vṛtra, by your prowess, did say firmly (to the gods), fear not!Indra, endowed with opulence, vast is your grasp, wherewith you have seized these unbounded regions, heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सू त इंद्र प्रवता हरिभ्यां प्र ते वज्रः प्रमृणन्नेतु शत्रून् ।जहि प्रतीचो अनूचः पराचो विश्वं सत्यं कृणुहि विष्टमस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ pra-vátā ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ prá ǀ te ǀ vájraḥ ǀ pra-mṛṇán ǀ etu ǀ śátrūn ǀjahí ǀ pratīcáḥ ǀ anūcáḥ ǀ párācaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ satyám ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ viṣṭám ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let (your car),Indra, drawn by your horses (rush) downwards (upon theasuras); let your destroying thunder-bolt fall upon your enemies; slay those that assail in front or in rear, or that fly (from the combat); make the universe (the abode of) truth; (let such power) be concentrated in you.
verses.wilson_translation: Let (your car),Indra, drawn by your horses (rush) downwards (upon theasuras); let your destroying thunder-bolt fall upon your enemies; slay those that assail in front or in rear, or that fly (from the combat); make the universe (the abode of) truth; (let such power) be concentrated in you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै धायुरदधा मर्त्यायाभक्तं चिद्भजते गेह्यं सः ।भद्रा त इंद्र सुमतिर्घृताची सहस्रदाना पुरुहूत रातिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ dhā́yuḥ ǀ ádadhāḥ ǀ mártyāya ǀ ábhaktam ǀ cit ǀ bhajate ǀ gehyám ǀ sáḥ ǀbhadrā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ ghṛtā́cī ǀ sahásra-dānā ǀ puru-hūta ǀ rātíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man to whom you grant, lord of power, (your good-will), enjoys unprecedented domestic (prosperity);Indra, who are invoked by many, your auspicous favour, which is obtained by oblations, is the giver of unbounded wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: The man to whom you grant, lord of power, (your good-will), enjoys unprecedented domestic (prosperity);Indra, who are invoked by many, your auspicous favour, which is obtained by oblations, is the giver of unbounded wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियंतमहस्तमिंद्र सं पिणक्कुणारुं ।अभि वृत्रं वर्धमानं पियारुमपादमिंद्र तवसा जघंथ ॥
verses.transliteration: sahá-dānum ǀ puru-hūta ǀ kṣiyántam ǀ ahastám ǀ indra ǀ sám ǀ piṇak ǀ kúṇārum ǀabhí ǀ vṛtrám ǀ várdhamānam ǀ píyārum ǀ apā́dam ǀ indra ǀ tavásā ǀ jaghantha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who is invoked by many, grind to dust the reviling malevolent Vṛtraopposing you, dwelling with the mother of the Dānavas, and increasing in might, until having deprived him ofhandand foot, you have destroyed him by your strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is invoked by many, grind to dust the reviling malevolent Vṛtraopposing you, dwelling with the mother of the Dānavas, and increasing in might, until having deprived him ofhandand foot, you have destroyed him by your strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि सामनामिषिरामिंद्र भूमिं महीमपारां सदने ससत्थ ।अस्तभ्नाद्द्यां वृषभो अंतरिक्षमर्षंत्वापस्त्वयेह प्रसूताः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ sāmanā́m ǀ iṣirā́m ǀ indra ǀ bhū́mim ǀ mahī́m ǀ apārā́m ǀ sádane ǀ sasattha ǀástabhnāt ǀ dyā́m ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ árṣantu ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ ihá ǀ prá-sūtāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have fixed tranquil in its position the vast unbounded and wandering earth; the showerer (of benefits) has upheld the heaven and the firmament; let the waters engendered by you here descend.
verses.wilson_translation: You have fixed tranquil in its position the vast unbounded and wandering earth; the showerer (of benefits) has upheld the heaven and the firmament; let the waters engendered by you here descend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अलातृणो वल इंद्र व्रजो गोः पुरा हंतोर्भयमानो व्यार ।सुगान्पथो अकृणोन्निरजे गाः प्रावन्वाणीः पुरुहूतं धमंतीः ॥
verses.transliteration: alātṛṇáḥ ǀ valáḥ ǀ indra ǀ vrajáḥ ǀ góḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ hántoḥ ǀ bháyamānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ āra ǀsu-gā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ niḥ-áje ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvan ǀ vā́ṇīḥ ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ dhámantīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The heavy cloud, the receptacle of water, dreading you its destroyer, opened out before (you had cast your bolt); then Indramade easily-traversed paths for the waters to issue, and desirable and loud sounding they proceeded to the (waters of the earth) invoked of many.
verses.wilson_translation: The heavy cloud, the receptacle of water, dreading you its destroyer, opened out before (you had cast your bolt); then Indramade easily-traversed paths for the waters to issue, and desirable and loud sounding they proceeded to the (waters of the earth) invoked of many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एको द्वे वसुमती समीची इंद्र आ पप्रौ पृथिवीमुत द्यां ।उतांतरिक्षादभि नः समीक इषो रथीः सयुजः शूर वाजान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ékaḥ ǀ dvé íti ǀ vásumatī íti vásu-matī ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ paprau ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǀutá ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ sam-īké ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ rathī́ḥ ǀ sa-yújaḥ ǀ śūra ǀ vā́jān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraalone has filled the two,both earth and heaven mutually combined, and abounding with wealth; do you hero, mounted in your car, come with your harnessed horses from the firmament, impatient to be near us.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraalone has filled the two,both earth and heaven mutually combined, and abounding with wealth; do you hero, mounted in your car, come with your harnessed horses from the firmament, impatient to be near us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिशः सूर्यो न मिनाति प्रदिष्टा दिवेदिवे हर्यश्वप्रसूताः ।सं यदानळध्वन आदिदश्वैर्विमोचनं कृणुते तत्त्वस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: díśaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mināti ǀ prá-diṣṭāḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ háryaśva-prasūtāḥ ǀsám ǀ yát ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ vi-mócanam ǀ kṛṇute ǀ tát ǀ tú ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sūryaharms not the quarters (of the horizon), set open daily (for his journey), the progeny of Haryaśva; when he has traversed the roads (he is to travel), then he lets loose his horses, for such is his office.
verses.wilson_translation: Sūryaharms not the quarters (of the horizon), set open daily (for his journey), the progeny of Haryaśva; when he has traversed the roads (he is to travel), then he lets loose his horses, for such is his office.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिदृक्षंत उषसो यामन्नक्तोर्विवस्वत्या महि चित्रमनीकं ।विश्वे जानंति महिना यदागादिंद्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि ॥
verses.transliteration: dídṛkṣante ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ yā́man ǀ aktóḥ ǀ vivásvatyāḥ ǀ máhi ǀ citrám ǀ ánīkam ǀvíśve ǀ jānanti ǀ mahinā́ ǀ yát ǀ ā́ ǀ ágāt ǀ índrasya ǀ kárma ǀ sú-kṛtā ǀ purū́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Al,l me are anxious to behold the great and variegated host (of the solar rays) at the issuing of the dawn after the night has been displaced; and when the morning has come, they recognize the many great and glorious acts of Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Al,l me are anxious to behold the great and variegated host (of the solar rays) at the issuing of the dawn after the night has been displaced; and when the morning has come, they recognize the many great and glorious acts of Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महि ज्योतिर्निहितं वक्षणास्वामा पक्वं चरति बिभ्रती गौः ।विश्वं स्वाद्म संभृतमुस्रियायां यत्सीमिंद्रो अदधाद्भोजनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ní-hitam ǀ vakṣáṇāsu ǀ āmā́ ǀ pakvám ǀ carati ǀ bíbhratī ǀ gáuḥ ǀvíśvam ǀ svā́dma ǀ sám-bhṛtam ǀ usríyāyām ǀ yát ǀ sīm ǀ índraḥ ǀ ádadhāt ǀ bhójanāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: A great light has been shed upon the rivers; the cow yet immature grazes, charged with the ripe (milk), for Indrahas plural ced in the cow all this collected sweetness for food.
verses.wilson_translation: A great light has been shed upon the rivers; the cow yet immature grazes, charged with the ripe (milk), for Indrahas plural ced in the cow all this collected sweetness for food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र दृह्य यामकोशा अभूवन्यज्ञाय शिक्ष गृणते सखिभ्यः ।दुर्मायवो दुरेवा मर्त्यासो निषंगिणो रिपवो हंत्वासः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ dṛ́hya ǀ yāma-kośā́ḥ ǀ abhūvan ǀ yajñā́ya ǀ śikṣa ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀduḥ-māyávaḥ ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǀ mártyāsaḥ ǀ niṣaṅgíṇaḥ ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ hántvāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, be firm, for there are obstructors of your path; secure to the worshipper and his friends (the means of completing) the sacrifice; mortal enemies bearing bows, armed with mischievous weapons, and coming with evil intent, must be destroyed (by you).
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, be firm, for there are obstructors of your path; secure to the worshipper and his friends (the means of completing) the sacrifice; mortal enemies bearing bows, armed with mischievous weapons, and coming with evil intent, must be destroyed (by you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सं घोषः शृण्वेऽवमैरमित्रैर्जही न्येष्वशनिं तपिष्ठां ।वृश्चेमधस्ताद्वि रुजा सहस्व जहि रक्षो मघवन्रंधयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀ śṛṇve ǀ avamáiḥ ǀ amítraiḥ ǀ jahí ǀ ní ǀ eṣu ǀ aśánim ǀ tápiṣṭhām ǀvṛścá ǀ īm ǀ adhástāt ǀ ví ǀ ruja ǀ sáhasva ǀ jahí ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ randháyasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sound (of your bolt) has been heard by the approaching foes; hurl upon them the consuming thunder-bolt, cut them up by the root, oppose;Maghavan, overcome, slay therākṣasas, complete (the sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: The sound (of your bolt) has been heard by the approaching foes; hurl upon them the consuming thunder-bolt, cut them up by the root, oppose;Maghavan, overcome, slay therākṣasas, complete (the sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उद्वृह रक्षः सहमूलमिंद्र वृश्चा मध्यं प्रत्यग्रं शृणीहि ।आ कीवतः सललूकं चकर्थ ब्रह्मद्विषे तपुषिं हेतिमस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ vṛha ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ sahá-mūlam ǀ indra ǀ vṛścá ǀ mádhyam ǀ práti ǀ ágram ǀ śṛṇīhi ǀā́ ǀ kī́vataḥ ǀ salalū́kam ǀ cakartha ǀ brahma-dvíṣe ǀ tápuṣim ǀ hetím ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: plural ck therākṣasas,Indra, by the root; cut as under the middle, blight the summit; to whatever remote (regions) you have driven the sinner, cast upon the enemy of the Vedayour consuming weapon.
verses.wilson_translation: plural ck therākṣasas,Indra, by the root; cut as under the middle, blight the summit; to whatever remote (regions) you have driven the sinner, cast upon the enemy of the Vedayour consuming weapon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्तये वाजिभिश्च प्रणेतः सं यन्महीरिष आसत्सि पूर्वीः ।रायो वंतारो बृहतः स्यामास्मे अस्तु भग इंद्र प्रजावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: svastáye ǀ vājí-bhiḥ ǀ ca ǀ pranetaríti pra-netaḥ ǀ sám ǀ yát ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ ā-sátsi ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀrāyáḥ ǀ vantā́raḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ syāma ǀ asmé íti ǀ astu ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ indra ǀ prajā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Regulator (of the world, provide us) with horses for our welfare, and when you are seated near to us may we become mighty, enjoying abundant food, and ample riches, and may there be to us wealth accompanied by progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: Regulator (of the world, provide us) with horses for our welfare, and when you are seated near to us may we become mighty, enjoying abundant food, and ample riches, and may there be to us wealth accompanied by progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो भर भगमिंद्र द्युमंतं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके ।ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhara ǀ bhágam ǀ indra ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ ní ǀ te ǀ deṣṇásya ǀ dhīmahi ǀ pra-reké ǀūrváḥ-iva ǀ paprathe ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ tám ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛṇa ǀ vasu-pate ǀ vásūnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring to us,Indra, splendid affluence; we rely on the bounty of you who are fond of giving; our desire is as insatiable as the fire of the ocean; appease it, lord of infinite riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring to us,Indra, splendid affluence; we rely on the bounty of you who are fond of giving; our desire is as insatiable as the fire of the ocean; appease it, lord of infinite riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं कामं मंदया गोभिरश्वैश्चंद्रवता राधसा पप्रथश्च ।स्वर्यवो मतिभिस्तुभ्यं विप्रा इंद्राय वाहः कुशिकासो अक्रन् ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ kā́mam ǀ mandaya ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ candrá-vatā ǀ rā́dhasā ǀ papráthaḥ ǀ ca ǀsvaḥ-yávaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ víprāḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ vā́haḥ ǀ kuśikā́saḥ ǀ akran ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gratify this our desire (of wealth) with cows, with horses, with shining treasure, and make us renowned; the wise Kuśikas, desirous of heaven, offer praise to you Indra, with pious (prayers).
verses.wilson_translation: Gratify this our desire (of wealth) with cows, with horses, with shining treasure, and make us renowned; the wise Kuśikas, desirous of heaven, offer praise to you Indra, with pious (prayers).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो गोत्रा दर्दृहि गोपते गाः समस्मभ्यं सनयो यंतु वाजाः ।दिवक्षा असि वृषभ सत्यशुष्मोऽस्मभ्यं सु मघवन्बोधि गोदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ gotrā́ ǀ dardṛhi ǀ go-pate ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ sanáyaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ vā́jāḥ ǀdivákṣāḥ ǀ asi ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ satyá-śuṣmaḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ sú ǀ magha-van ǀ bodhi ǀ go-dā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, lord of cattle, (divide the clouds and send us) rain, whence nutritious food may come to us; showerer (of benefits), you are spread through the sky, and powerful through truth;Maghavan, consider yourself as our protector.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, lord of cattle, (divide the clouds and send us) rain, whence nutritious food may come to us; showerer (of benefits), you are spread through the sky, and powerful through truth;Maghavan, consider yourself as our protector.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke for our protection the opulent Indradistinguished in this combat; the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for our protection the opulent Indradistinguished in this combat; the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: २२ कुशिक ऐषीरथिः, गाथिनो विश्वामित्रो वा। इन्द्रः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WISE, teaching, following the thought of Order, the sonless gained a grandson from his daughter.Fain, as a sire, to see his child prolific, he sped to meet her with an eager spirit. The Son left not his portion to the brother, he made a home to hold him who should gain, it.What time his Parents gave the Priest his being, of the good pair one acted, one promoted. Agni was born trembling with tongue that flickered, so that the Red's great children should be honoured.Great is their germ, that born of them is mighty, great the Bays' Lord's approach through sacrifices. Conquering bands upon the Warrior waited: they recognized great light from out the darkness.The conscious Dawns went forth to meet his coming, and the sole Master of the kine was Indra. The sages freed them from their firmbuilt prison: the seven priests drove them forward with their spirit.All holy Order's pathway they discovered he, full of knowledge, shared these deeds through worship. When Saramā had found the mountain's fissure, that vast and ancient place she plundered thoroughly.In the floods' van she led them forth, light-footed: she who well knew came first unto their lowing. Longing for friendship came the noblest singer: the hill poured forth its treasure for the pious.The Hero with young followers fought and conquered, and straightway Aṅgiras was singing praises, Peer of each noble thing, yea, all excelling, all creatures doth he know, he slayeth Śuṣṇa.Our leader, fain for war, singing from heaven, as Friend he saved his lovers from dishonour. They sate them down with spirit fain for booty, making with hymns a way to life eternal.And this is still their place of frequent session, whereby they sought to gain the months through Order. Drawing the milk of ancient seed prolific, they joyed as they beheld their own possession.Their shout of triumph heated earth and heaven. When the kine showed, they bade the heroes rouse them. Indra drove forth the kine, that Vṛtra-slayer, while hymns of praise rose up and gifts were offered.For him the Cow, noble and far-extending, poured pleasant juices, bringing oil and sweetness. They made a mansion for their Father, deftly provided him a great and glorious dwelling;With firm support parted and stayed the Parents, and, sitting, fixed him there erected, mighty. What time the ample chalice had impelled him, swift waxing, vast, to pierce the earth and heaven,—Him in whom blameless songs are all united: all powers invincible belong to Indra. I crave thy powers, I crave thy mighty friendship: full many a team goes to the Vṛtra-slayer.Great is the laud, we seek the Princes' favour. Be thou, O Maghavan, our guard and keeper. He, having found great, splendid, rich dominion, sent life and motion to his friends and lovers.Indra who shone together with the Heroes begot the song, the fire, and Sun and Morning. Vast, the House-Friend, he set the waters flowing, all-lucid, widely spread, that move together.By the wise cleansings of the meath made holy, through days, and nights they speed the swift streams onward. To thee proceed the dark, the treasure-holders, both of them sanctified by Sūrya's bounty.The while thy ovely storming Friends, O Indra, fail to attain the measure of thy greatness. Be Lord of joyous songs, O Vṛtra-slayer, Bull dear to all, who gives the power of living.Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, hastening, Mighty One, with mighty succours. Like Aṅgiras I honour him with worship, and renovate old song for him the Ancient.Chase thou the many godless evil creatures, and give us, Maghavan, heaven's light to help m. Far forth are spread the purifying waters convey thou us across them unto safety.Save us, our Charioteer, from harm, O Indra, soon, very soon, make us win spoil of cattle. His kine their Lord hath shown, e’en Vṛtra's slayer, through the black hosts he passed with red attendants.Teaching us pleasant things by holy Order, to, us hath he thrown open all his portals. Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered.The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

verses.sanskrit: शासद्वह्निर्दुहितुर्नप्त्यं गाद्विद्वाँ ऋतस्य दीधितिं सपर्यन् ।पिता यत्र दुहितुः सेकमृंजन्त्सं शग्म्येन मनसा दधन्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: śā́sat ǀ váhniḥ ǀ duhitúḥ ǀ naptyám ǀ gāt ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dī́dhitim ǀ saparyán ǀpitā́ ǀ yátra ǀ duhitúḥ ǀ sékam ǀ ṛñján ǀ sám ǀ śagmyéna ǀ mánasā ǀ dadhanvé ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sonless father, regulating (the contract), refers to his grandson, (the son) of his daughter, and relying on the efficiency of the rite, honours (his son-in-law) with valuable gifts; the father, trusting to the impregnation of the daughter, supports himself with a tranquil mind.
verses.wilson_translation: The sonless father, regulating (the contract), refers to his grandson, (the son) of his daughter, and relying on the efficiency of the rite, honours (his son-in-law) with valuable gifts; the father, trusting to the impregnation of the daughter, supports himself with a tranquil mind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानं ।यदी मातरो जनयंत वह्निमन्यः कर्ता सुकृतोर��्य ऋंधन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ jāmáye ǀ tā́nvaḥ ǀ rikthám ǀ araik ǀ cakā́ra ǀ gárbham ǀ sanitúḥ ǀ ni-dhā́nam ǀyádi ǀ mātáraḥ ǀ janáyanta ǀ váhnim ǀ anyáḥ ǀ kartā́ ǀ su-kṛ́toḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ṛndhán ǁ
verses.english_translation: (A son) born of the body, does not transfer (paternal) wealth to a sister; he has made (her) the recptacle of the embryo of the husband; if the parents procreate children (of either sex), one is the performer of holy acts, the other is to be enriched (with gifts).
verses.wilson_translation: (A son) born of the body, does not transfer (paternal) wealth to a sister; he has made (her) the recptacle of the embryo of the husband; if the parents procreate children (of either sex), one is the performer of holy acts, the other is to be enriched (with gifts).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्जज्ञे जुह्वा रेजमानो महस्पुत्राँ अरुषस्य प्रयक्षे ।महान्गर्भो मह्या जातमेषां मही प्रवृद्धर्यश्वस्य यज्ञैः ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ jajñe ǀ juhvā́ ǀ réjamānaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ putrā́n ǀ aruṣásya ǀ pra-yákṣe ǀmahā́n ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ ā́ ǀ jātám ǀ eṣām ǀ mahī́ ǀ pra-vṛ́t ǀ hári-aśvasya ǀ yajñáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For the worship of the resplendent (Indra),Agni, glowing with flame, has begotten mighty sons; great was the germ, and great was their birth, and great was their efficacy, for the worship of Haryaśva.
verses.wilson_translation: For the worship of the resplendent (Indra),Agni, glowing with flame, has begotten mighty sons; great was the germ, and great was their birth, and great was their efficacy, for the worship of Haryaśva.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि जैत्रीरसचंत स्पृधानं महि ज्योतिस्तमसो निरजानन् ।तं जानतीः प्रत्युदायन्नुषासः पतिर्गवामभवदेक इंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ jáitrīḥ ǀ asacanta ǀ spṛdhānám ǀ máhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ támasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ ajānan ǀtám ǀ jānatī́ḥ ǀ práti ǀ út ǀ āyan ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ gávām ǀ abhavat ǀ ékaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The victorious (Maruts) associated (with Indrawhen contending with Vṛtra) perceived a great light issuing from the darkness. The dawns recognizing him (as the sun) arose, and Indra was the sole sovereign of the rays (of light).
verses.wilson_translation: The victorious (Maruts) associated (with Indrawhen contending with Vṛtra) perceived a great light issuing from the darkness. The dawns recognizing him (as the sun) arose, and Indra was the sole sovereign of the rays (of light).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अतृंदन्प्राचाहिन्वन्मनसा सप्त विप्राः ।विश्वामविंदन्पथ्यामृतस्य प्रजानन्नित्ता नमसा विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: vīḷáu ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ atṛndan ǀ prācā́ ǀ ahinvan ǀ mánasā ǀ saptá ǀ víprāḥ ǀvíśvām ǀ avindan ǀ pathyā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pra-jānán ǀ ít ǀ tā́ ǀ námasā ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven intelligent ages (theaṅgirasas) having ascertained that (the cows) were concealed in the strong (cavern), propitiated (Indra) by mental devotion; they recovered them all by the path of sacrifice; for Indra, knowing (their pious acts), and offering them homage, entered (the cave).
verses.wilson_translation: The seven intelligent ages (theaṅgirasas) having ascertained that (the cows) were concealed in the strong (cavern), propitiated (Indra) by mental devotion; they recovered them all by the path of sacrifice; for Indra, knowing (their pious acts), and offering them homage, entered (the cave).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक्कः ।अग्रं नयत्सुपद्यक्षराणामच्छा रवं प्रथमा जानती गात् ॥
verses.transliteration: vidát ǀ yádi ǀ sarámā ǀ rugṇám ǀ ádreḥ ǀ máhi ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ pūrvyám ǀ sadhryák ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀágram ǀ nayat ǀ su-pádī ǀ ákṣarāṇām ǀ áccha ǀ rávam ǀ prathamā́ ǀ jānatī́ ǀ gāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Saramādiscovered the broken (entrance) of the mountain, then Indramade great and ample (provision) for her young, as previously (promised); then the sure-footed (animal), forest recognizing their lowing, proceeded, and came to the presence of the imperishable kine.
verses.wilson_translation: When Saramādiscovered the broken (entrance) of the mountain, then Indramade great and ample (provision) for her young, as previously (promised); then the sure-footed (animal), forest recognizing their lowing, proceeded, and came to the presence of the imperishable kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अगच्छदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत्सुकृते गर्भमद्रिः ।ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदंगिराः सद्यो अर्चन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ágacchat ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vípra-tamaḥ ǀ sakhi-yán ǀ ásūdayat ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ gárbham ǀ ádriḥ ǀsasā́na ǀ máryaḥ ǀ yúva-bhiḥ ǀ makhasyán ǀ átha ǀ abhavat ǀ áṅgirāḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ árcan ǁ
verses.english_translation: The most sage (Indra), desirous of the friendship of the (aṅgirasas), went to the cave, and the mountain yielded its contents to the valiant (deity), aided by the youthful Maruts, equally wishing (to conciliate the sages); the destroyer (of theasuras) recovered (the cattle), and immediately aṅgirasas became his worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: The most sage (Indra), desirous of the friendship of the (aṅgirasas), went to the cave, and the mountain yielded its contents to the valiant (deity), aided by the youthful Maruts, equally wishing (to conciliate the sages); the destroyer (of theasuras) recovered (the cattle), and immediately aṅgirasas became his worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सतःसतः प्रतिमानं पुरोभूर्विश्वा वेद जनिमा हंति शुष्णं ।प्र णो दिवः पदवीर्गव्युरर्चन्त्सखा सखीँरमुंचन्निरवद्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: satáḥ-sataḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ puraḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ veda ǀ jánima ǀ hánti ǀ śúṣṇam ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ pada-vī́ḥ ǀ gavyúḥ ǀ árcan ǀ sákhā ǀ sákhīn ǀ amuñcat ǀ níḥ ǀ avadyā́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he who is the type of all that is excellent the anticipator (of his foes), he who knows all that is born, who destroysŚuṣṇa, the far-seeing, the restorer of cattle may he, a friend coming from heaven, honouring us as his friends, be free from all reproach.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who is the type of all that is excellent the anticipator (of his foes), he who knows all that is born, who destroysŚuṣṇa, the far-seeing, the restorer of cattle may he, a friend coming from heaven, honouring us as his friends, be free from all reproach.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि गव्यता मनसा सेदुरर्कैः कृण्वानासो अमृतत्वाय गातुं ।इदं चिन्नु सदनं भूर्येषां येन मासाँ असिषासन्नृतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ gavyatā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ seduḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ kṛṇvānā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvā́ya ǀ gātúm ǀidám ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ sádanam ǀ bhū́ri ǀ eṣām ǀ yéna ǀ mā́sān ǀ ásisāsan ǀ ṛténa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Theaṅgirasas, with minds intent on their cattle, (sat down to worship Indra) with hymns, following the road to immortality; great was their person verance by which they sought for months to accomplish (their ends).
verses.wilson_translation: Theaṅgirasas, with minds intent on their cattle, (sat down to worship Indra) with hymns, following the road to immortality; great was their person verance by which they sought for months to accomplish (their ends).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: संपश्यमाना अमदन्नभि स्वं पयः प्रत्नस्य रेतसो दुघानाः ।वि रोदसी अतपद्घोष एषां जाते निष्ठामदधुर्गोषु वीरान् ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-páśyamānāḥ ǀ amadan ǀ abhí ǀ svám ǀ páyaḥ ǀ pratnásya ǀ rétasaḥ ǀ dúghānāḥ ǀví ǀ ródasī íti ǀ atapat ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ jāté ǀ niḥ-sthā́m ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ vīrā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Contemplating their own (cattle) giving milk to their former progeny (theaṅgirasas) were delighted; their shouts spread through heaven and earth; they replaced the recovered kine in their plural ces, and stationed guards over the cows.
verses.wilson_translation: Contemplating their own (cattle) giving milk to their former progeny (theaṅgirasas) were delighted; their shouts spread through heaven and earth; they replaced the recovered kine in their plural ces, and stationed guards over the cows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स जातेभिर्वृत्रहा सेदु हव्यैरुदुस्रिया असृजदिंद्रो अर्कैः ।उरूच्यस्मै घृतवद्भरंती मधु स्वाद्म दुदुहे जेन्या गौः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ jātébhiḥ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ havyáiḥ ǀ út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ índraḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀurūcī́ ǀ asmai ǀ ghṛtá-vat ǀ bhárantī ǀ mádhu ǀ svā́dma ǀ duduhe ǀ jényā ǀ gáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra,let loose the milch kine, assisted by the Maruts, born for his aid, and entitled to praises and oblations, and the excellent (cows) contributing abundantly to sacred offerings, and yielding the butter of libation, milked for him sweet (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra,let loose the milch kine, assisted by the Maruts, born for his aid, and entitled to praises and oblations, and the excellent (cows) contributing abundantly to sacred offerings, and yielding the butter of libation, milked for him sweet (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पित्रे चिच्चक्रुः सदनं समस्मै महि त्विषीमत्सुकृतो वि हि ख्यन् ।विष्कभ्नंतः स्कंभनेना जनित्री आसीना ऊर्ध्वं रभसं वि मिन्वन् ॥
verses.transliteration: pitré ǀ cit ǀ cakruḥ ǀ sádanam ǀ sám ǀ asmai ǀ máhi ǀ tvíṣi-mat ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ ví ǀ hí ǀ khyán ǀvi-skabhnántaḥ ǀ skámbhanena ǀ jánitrī íti ǀ ā́sīnāḥ ǀ ūrdhvám ǀ rabhasám ǀ ví ǀ minvan ǁ
verses.english_translation: They (theaṅgirasas) performing pious acts made for their protector a spacious and splendid abode which they celebrated; seated (at the sacrifice) and supporting with the pillar (of the firmament) the parents (of all things heaven and earth), they established the rapid Indraon high (in heaven).
verses.wilson_translation: They (theaṅgirasas) performing pious acts made for their protector a spacious and splendid abode which they celebrated; seated (at the sacrifice) and supporting with the pillar (of the firmament) the parents (of all things heaven and earth), they established the rapid Indraon high (in heaven).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मही यदि धिषणा शिश्नथे धात्सद्योवृधं विभ्वं रोदस्योः ।गिरो यस्मिन्ननवद्याः समीचीर्विश्वा इंद्राय तविषीरनुत्ताः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ ǀ yádi ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ śiśnáthe ǀ dhā́t ǀ sadyaḥ-vṛ́dham ǀ vi-bhvám ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀgíraḥ ǀ yásmin ǀ anavadyā́ḥ ǀ sam-īcī́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ ánuttāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inasmuch as our devout praise has appointed a thiriving ruler for the regulation of heaven and earth, to whom faultless and appropriate commendations (are due), therefore are all the energies of Indraspontaneously exerted.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as our devout praise has appointed a thiriving ruler for the regulation of heaven and earth, to whom faultless and appropriate commendations (are due), therefore are all the energies of Indraspontaneously exerted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मह्या ते सख्यं वश्मि शक्तीरा वृत्रघ्ने नियुतो यंति पूर्वीः ।महि स्तोत्रमव आगन्म सूरेरस्माकं सु मघवन्बोधि गोपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ sakhyám ǀ vaśmi ǀ śaktī́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛtra-ghné ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ yanti ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀmáhi ǀ stotrám ǀ ávaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aganma ǀ sūréḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sú ǀ magha-van ǀ bodhi ǀ gopā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I wish,Indra, for your friendship, and (the exercise of) your powers;many heroes come to the slayer of Vṛtra; we offer to you, sage, great praise and oblations; consider yourself,Maghavan, as our protector.
verses.wilson_translation: I wish,Indra, for your friendship, and (the exercise of) your powers;many heroes come to the slayer of Vṛtra; we offer to you, sage, great praise and oblations; consider yourself,Maghavan, as our protector.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महि क्षेत्रं पुरु श्चंद्रं विविद्वानादित्सखिभ्यश्चरथं समैरत् ।इंद्रो नृभिरजनद्दीद्यानः साकं सूर्यमुषसं गातुमग्निं ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ kṣétram ǀ purú ǀ candrám ǀ vividvā́n ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ carátham ǀ sám ǀ airát ǀíndraḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ ajanat ǀ dī́dyānaḥ ǀ sākám ǀ sū́ryam ǀ uṣásam ǀ gātúm ǀ agním ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wide fields, vast treasure, (spacious) pastures has the much-knowing (Indra) bestowed upon his friends; the radiant Indra with the leaders (of rites, the Maruts) genitive rated the sun, the dawn, the earth and fire.
verses.wilson_translation: Wide fields, vast treasure, (spacious) pastures has the much-knowing (Indra) bestowed upon his friends; the radiant Indra with the leaders (of rites, the Maruts) genitive rated the sun, the dawn, the earth and fire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपश्चिदेष विभ्वो दमूनाः प्र सध्रीचीरसृजद्विश्वश्चंद्राः ।मध्वः पुनानाः कविभिः पवित्रैर्द्युभिर्हिन्वंत्यक्तुभिर्धनुत्रीः ॥
verses.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ cit ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ vi-bhváḥ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ prá ǀ sadhrī́cīḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ viśvá-candrāḥ ǀmádhvaḥ ǀ punānā́ḥ ǀ kaví-bhiḥ ǀ pavítraiḥ ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀ hinvanti ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ dhánutrīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This lowly-minded Indrahas created the wide-spread, commingled, all-delighting waters; and they, purifying the sweet (libations) with the sage purifiers, and being benevolent (to all), proceed with (the revolutions) of days and nights.
verses.wilson_translation: This lowly-minded Indrahas created the wide-spread, commingled, all-delighting waters; and they, purifying the sweet (libations) with the sage purifiers, and being benevolent (to all), proceed with (the revolutions) of days and nights.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनु कृष्णे वसुधिती जिहाते उभे सूर्यस्य मंहना यजत्रे ।परि यत्ते महिमानं वृजध्यै सखाय इंद्र काम्या ऋजिप्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ kṛṣṇé íti ǀ vásudhitī íti vásu-dhitī ǀ jihāte íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ maṃhánā ǀ yájatre íti ǀpári ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ vṛjádhyai ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ kā́myāḥ ǀ ṛjipyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The two adorable (alternations of) day and night, upholding (all things) by the might of the sun, successively revolve; your sincere and acceptable friends (the Maruts) are ready to encounter (your foes) and maintain your greatness.
verses.wilson_translation: The two adorable (alternations of) day and night, upholding (all things) by the might of the sun, successively revolve; your sincere and acceptable friends (the Maruts) are ready to encounter (your foes) and maintain your greatness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पतिर्भव वृत्रहन्त्सूनृतानां गिरां विश्वायुर्वृषभो वयोधाः ।आ नो गहि सख्येभिः शिवेभिर्महान्महीभिरूतिभिः सरण्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: pátiḥ ǀ bhava ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ sūnṛ́tānām ǀ girā́m ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ gahi ǀ sakhyébhiḥ ǀ śivébhiḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ mahī́bhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ saraṇyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, do you, who is long lived the showerer (of benefits), the giver of food, be the lord of our true praises, repairing (to the sacrifice), come to us great, with great, friendly, and auspicious protections.
verses.wilson_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, do you, who is long lived the showerer (of benefits), the giver of food, be the lord of our true praises, repairing (to the sacrifice), come to us great, with great, friendly, and auspicious protections.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमंगिरस्वन्नमसा सपर्यन्नव्यं कृणोमि सन्यसे पुराजां ।द्रुहो वि याहि बहुला अदेवीः स्वश्च नो मघवन्त्सातये धाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ aṅgirasvát ǀ námasā ǀ saparyán ǀ návyam ǀ kṛṇomi ǀ sányase ǀ purā-jā́m ǀdrúhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ yāhi ǀ bahulā́ḥ ǀ ádevīḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ sātáye ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worshipping him with reverence, like anaṅgiras, I make the ancient (Indra) renovate to accept the oblation; destroy the many impious oppressors (of your worshippers) and bestow upon us,Maghavan, yours own (wealth) for our acceptance.
verses.wilson_translation: Worshipping him with reverence, like anaṅgiras, I make the ancient (Indra) renovate to accept the oblation; destroy the many impious oppressors (of your worshippers) and bestow upon us,Maghavan, yours own (wealth) for our acceptance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मिहः पावकाः प्रतता अभूवन्त्स्वस्ति नः पिपृहि पारमासां ।इंद्र त्वं रथिरः पाहि नो रिषो मक्षूमक्षू कृणुहि गोजितो नः ॥
verses.transliteration: míhaḥ ǀ pāvakā́ḥ ǀ prá-tatāḥ ǀ abhūvan ǀ svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ pipṛhi ǀ pārám ǀ āsām ǀíndra ǀ tvám ǀ rathiráḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ naḥ ǀ riṣáḥ ǀ makṣú-makṣu ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ go-jítaḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You purifying water have been spread abroad; fill their beds for our welfare; riding on the car, defend us from the malevolent, and make us quickly the conquerors of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: You purifying water have been spread abroad; fill their beds for our welfare; riding on the car, defend us from the malevolent, and make us quickly the conquerors of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अदेदिष्ट वृत्रहा गोपतिर्गा अंतः कृष्णाँ अरुषैर्धामभिर्गात् ।प्र सूनृता दिशमान ऋतेन दुरश्च विश्वा अवृणोदप स्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádediṣṭa ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ gó-patiḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ antáríti ǀ kṛṣṇā́n ǀ aruṣáiḥ ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ gāt ǀprá ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ diśámānaḥ ǀ ṛténa ǀ dúraḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ avṛṇot ǀ ápa ǀ svā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of herds, has discovered the cattle, and by his radiant effulgence driven away the black (asuras), and indicating with veracity (to theaṅgirasas) the honest (kine), heshutthe gate uon all their own cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of herds, has discovered the cattle, and by his radiant effulgence driven away the black (asuras), and indicating with veracity (to theaṅgirasas) the honest (kine), heshutthe gate uon all their own cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praise), terriblein battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praise), terriblein battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXII. Indra
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRINK thou this Soma, Indra, Lord of Soma; drink thou the draught of noonday which thou Iovest.Puffing thy cheeks, impetuous, liberal Giver, here loose thy two Bay Horses and rejoice thee. Quaff it pure, meal-blent, mixt with milk, O Indra; we have poured forth the Soma for thy rapture.Knit with the prayer-fulfilling band of Maruts, yea, with the Rudras, drink till thou art sated; Those who gave increase to thy strength and vigour; the Maruts singing forth thy might, O Indra.Drink thou, O fair of cheek, whose hand wields thunder, with Rudras banded, at our noon libation. They, even the Maruts who were there, excited with song the meath-created strength of Indra.By them impelled to act he reached the vitals Of Vṛtra, though he deemed that none might wound him. Pleased, like a man, with our libation, Indra, drink, for enduring hero might, the Soma.Lord of Bays, moved by sacrifice come hither: thou with the Swift Ones stirrest floods and waters. When thou didst loose the streams to run like racers in the swift contest, having smitten VṛtraWith flying weapon where he lay, O Indra, and, godless, kept the Goddesses encompassed. With reverence let us worship mighty Indra, great and sublime, eternal, everyouthful,Whose greatness the dear world-halves have not measured, no, nor conceived the might of him the Holy. Many are Indra's nobly wrought achievements, and none of all the Gods transgress his statutes.He beareth up this earth and heaven, and, doer of marvels, he begot the Sun and Morning. Herein, O Guileless One, is thy true greatness, that soon as born thou drankest up the Soma.Days may not check the power of thee the Mighty, nor the nights, Indra, nor the months, nor autumns. As soon as thou wast born in highest heaven thou drankest Soma to delight thee, Indra;And when thou hadst pervaded earth and heaven thou wast the first supporter of the singer. Thou, puissant God, more mighty, slewest. Ahi showing his strength when couched around the waters.The heaven itself attained not to thy greatness when with one hip of thine the earth was shadowed. Sacrifice, Indra, made thee wax so mighty, the dear oblation with the flowing Soma.O Worshipful, with worship help our worship, for worship helped thy bolt when slaying Ahi. With sacrifice and wish have I brought Indra; still for new blessings may I turn him hither,Him magnified by ancient songs and praises, by lauds of later time and days yet recent. I have brought forth a song when longing seized me: ere the decisive day will I laud Indra;Then may he safely bear us over trouble, as in a ship, when both sides invocate him. Full is his chalice: Glory! Like a pourer I have filled up the vessel for his drinking.Presented on the right, dear Soma juices have brought us Indra, to rejoice him, hither. Not the deep-flowing flood, O Much-invoked One! not hills that compass thee about restrain thee,Since here incited, for thy friends, O Indra, thou breakest e’en the firm built stall of cattle. Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र सोमं सोमपते पिबेमं माध्यंदिनं सवनं चारु यत्ते ।प्रप्रुथ्या शिप्रे मघवन्नृजीषिन्विमुच्या हरी इह मादयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ sómam ǀ soma-pate ǀ píba ǀ imám ǀ mā́dhyandinam ǀ sávanam ǀ cā́ru ǀ yát ǀ te ǀpra-prúthya ǀ śípre íti ǀ magha-van ǀ ṛjīṣin ǀ vi-múcya ǀ hárī íti ǀ ihá ǀ mādayasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, lord of the Soma, drink this Soma which is grateful to you at noon-day sacrifice,Maghavan, partake of the spiritless Soma, unyoke your horses, and filling their jaws (with fodder), exhilarate them at this ceremony.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, lord of the Soma, drink this Soma which is grateful to you at noon-day sacrifice,Maghavan, partake of the spiritless Soma, unyoke your horses, and filling their jaws (with fodder), exhilarate them at this ceremony.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गवाशिरं मंथिनमिंद्र शुक्रं पिबा सोमं ररिमा ते मदाय ।ब्रह्मकृता मारुतेना गणेन सजोषा रुद्रैस्तृपदा वृषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: gó-āśiram ǀ manthínam ǀ indra ǀ śukrám ǀ píba ǀ sómam ǀ rarimá ǀ te ǀ mádāya ǀbrahma-kṛ́tā ǀ mā́rutena ǀ gaṇéna ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ rudráiḥ ǀ tṛpát ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, drink the Somamixed with milk, with butter-milk, or fresh; we offer it for your exhilaration, associated with the devout company of the Marutsand the Rudras; drink it till you are satisfied.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, drink the Somamixed with milk, with butter-milk, or fresh; we offer it for your exhilaration, associated with the devout company of the Marutsand the Rudras; drink it till you are satisfied.
