verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वीरस्य निष्षिधो मर्त्येषु पुरू वसूनि पृथिवी बिभर्ति ।इंद्राय द्याव ओषधीरुतापो रयिं रक्षंति जीरयो वनानि ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrvī́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ niḥ-sídhaḥ ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ purú ǀ vásūni ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ bibharti ǀíndrāya ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ utá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ rayím ǀ rakṣanti ǀ jīráyaḥ ǀ vánāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are his prohibitions (against evil enjoined) to men; many are the treasures that the earth enshrines; for Indrathe heavens, the plural nts, the waters, men and priests, preserve their riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are his prohibitions (against evil enjoined) to men; many are the treasures that the earth enshrines; for Indrathe heavens, the plural nts, the waters, men and priests, preserve their riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि गिर इंद्र तुभ्यं सत्रा दधिरे हरिवो जुषस्व ।बोध्यापिरवसो नूतनस्य सखे वसो जरितृभ्यो वयो धाः ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ gíraḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ satrā́ ǀ dadhire ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ juṣásva ǀbodhí ǀ āpíḥ ǀ ávasaḥ ǀ nū́tanasya ǀ sákhe ǀ vaso íti ǀ jaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you,Indra, (the pious) address prayers, and praises, and sacrifices; accept them, lord of horses; give all things, partake of this present oblation, and grant food to the worshippers.
verses.wilson_translation: To you,Indra, (the pious) address prayers, and praises, and sacrifices; accept them, lord of horses; give all things, partake of this present oblation, and grant food to the worshippers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं यथा शार्याते अपिबः सुतस्य ।तव प्रणीती तव शूर शर्मन्ना विवासंति कवयः सुयज्ञाः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ marutvaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ pāhi ǀ sómam ǀ yáthā ǀ śāryāté ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ sutásya ǀtáva ǀ prá-nītī ǀ táva ǀ śūra ǀ śárman ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsanti ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ su-yajñā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, accompanied, by the Maruts, drink the Somaat this ceremony as you have drunk of this libation of the son ofŚāryāti; your far-reaching and devout worshippers, being in security, adore you through their offerings.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, accompanied, by the Maruts, drink the Somaat this ceremony as you have drunk of this libation of the son ofŚāryāti; your far-reaching and devout worshippers, being in security, adore you through their offerings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स वावशान इह पाहि सोमं मरुद्भिरिंद्र सखिभिः सुतं नः ।जातं यत्त्वा परि देवा अभूषन्महे भराय पुरुहूत विश्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vāvaśānáḥ ǀ ihá ǀ pāhi ǀ sómam ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ sutám ǀ naḥ ǀjātám ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ pári ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ábhūṣan ǀ mahé ǀ bhárāya ǀ puru-hūta ǀ víśve ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you,Indra, who is gratified by the Soma, drink the Soma that has been effused by us, together with your friends, the Maruts, at this ceremony; you who is invoked of many, and whom all the gods equipped as soon as born for the great battle (with theasuras).
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, who is gratified by the Soma, drink the Soma that has been effused by us, together with your friends, the Maruts, at this ceremony; you who is invoked of many, and whom all the gods equipped as soon as born for the great battle (with theasuras).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अप्तूर्ये मरुत आपिरेषोऽमंदन्निंद्रमनु दातिवाराः ।तेभिः साकं पिबतु वृत्रखादः सुतं सोमं दाशुषः स्वे सधस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-tū́rye ǀ marutaḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ ámandan ǀ índram ǀ ánu ǀ dā́ti-vārāḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ pibatu ǀ vṛtra-khādáḥ ǀ sutám ǀ sómam ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ své ǀ sadhá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, this is your friend for sending of the waters; they (the Maruts), the givers of strength, have yielded Indragratification; may the devourer of Vṛtradrink with them the libation offered by the worshipper in his abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, this is your friend for sending of the waters; they (the Maruts), the givers of strength, have yielded Indragratification; may the devourer of Vṛtradrink with them the libation offered by the worshipper in his abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इदं ह्यन्वोजसा सुतं राधानां पते ।पिबा त्वस्य गिर्वणः ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ hí ǀ ánu ǀ ójasā ǀ sutám ǀ rādhānām ǀ pate ǀpíba ǀ tú ǀ asyá ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of riches, entitled to praise, this libation has been effused agreeably to (our) strength; do you drink of it quickly.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of riches, entitled to praise, this libation has been effused agreeably to (our) strength; do you drink of it quickly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते अनु स्वधामसत्सुते नि यच्छ तन्वं ।स त्वा ममत्तु सोम्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ ánu ǀ svadhā́m ǀ ásat ǀ suté ǀ ní ǀ yaccha ǀ tanvám ǀsáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ mamattu ǀ somyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invigorate your body with the Somathat has been poured out as food for you; may it exhilarate you, delighting in the Soma draught.
verses.wilson_translation: Invigorate your body with the Somathat has been poured out as food for you; may it exhilarate you, delighting in the Soma draught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते अश्नोतु कुक्ष्योः प्रेंद्र ब्रह्मणा शिरः ।प्र बाहू शूर राधसे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ aśnotu ǀ kukṣyóḥ ǀ prá ǀ indra ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ śíraḥ ǀprá ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ śūra ǀ rā́dhase ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this libation,Indra, penetrate to your flanks; may it, (aided) by prayer, reach your head; may it spread, hero, through your arms, (that they may distribute) wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: May this libation,Indra, penetrate to your flanks; may it, (aided) by prayer, reach your head; may it spread, hero, through your arms, (that they may distribute) wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INDRA, accept at break of day our Soma mixt with roasted corn,With groats with cake, with eulogies. Accept, O Indra, and enjoy the well-dressed sacrificial cake: Oblations are poured forth to thee. Consume our sacrificial cake, accept the songs of praise we sing,As he who woes accepts his bride. Famed from of old, accept the cake at our libation poured at dawn,Forgreat, O Indra, is thy power. Let roasted corn of our midday libation, and sacrificial cake here please thee, Indra,What time the lauding singer, keen of purpose and eager as a bull, with hymns implores thee. At the third sacrifice, O thou whom many praise, give glory to the roasted corn and holy cake.With offered viands and with songs may we assist thee, Sage, whom Vāja and the Ṛbhus wait upon. The groats have we prepared for thee with Pūṣan, corn for thee, Lord of Bay Steeds, with thy horses.Eat thou the meal-cake, banded with the Maruts, wise Hero, Vṛtra-slayer, drink the Soma. Bring forth the roasted corn to meet him quickly, cake for the bravest Hero mid the heroes.Indra, may hymns accordant with thee daily strengthen thee, Bold One, for the draught of Soma.

verses.sanskrit: धानावंतं करंभिणमपूपवंतमुक्थिनं ।इंद्र प्रातर्जुषस्व नः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhānā́-vantam ǀ karambhíṇam ǀ apūpá-vantam ǀ ukthínam ǀíndra ǀ prātáḥ ǀ juṣasva ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Accept,Indra, at our morning sacrifice, this libation, combined with fresh barley, with parched grain and curds, and with cakes, and sanctified by holy prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Indra, at our morning sacrifice, this libation, combined with fresh barley, with parched grain and curds, and with cakes, and sanctified by holy prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोळाशं पचत्यं जुषस्वेंद्रा गुरस्व च ।तुभ्यं हव्यानि सिस्रते ॥
verses.transliteration: puroḷā́śam ǀ pacatyám ǀ juṣásva ǀ indra ǀ ā́ ǀ gurasva ǀ ca ǀtúbhyam ǀ havyā́ni ǀ sisrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Accept,Indra, the prepared cakes and butter; eat them eagerly; the oblations flow for you.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Indra, the prepared cakes and butter; eat them eagerly; the oblations flow for you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोळाशं च नो घसो जोषयासे गिरश्च नः ।वधूयुरिव योषणां ॥
verses.transliteration: puroḷā́śam ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ ghásaḥ ǀ joṣáyāse ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀvadhūyúḥ-iva ǀ yóṣaṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eat,Indra, our (offered) cakes and butter, derive enjoyment from our praises, as a lover from his mistress.
verses.wilson_translation: Eat,Indra, our (offered) cakes and butter, derive enjoyment from our praises, as a lover from his mistress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोळाशं सनश्रुत प्रातःसावे जुषस्व नः ।इंद्र क्रतुर्हि ते बृहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: puroḷā́śam ǀ sana-śruta ǀ prātaḥ-sāvé ǀ juṣasva ǀ naḥ ǀíndra ǀ krátuḥ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ bṛhán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, renowned of old, accept our cakes and butter, offered at dawn; for great are your deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, renowned of old, accept our cakes and butter, offered at dawn; for great are your deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धानाः पुरोळाशमिंद्र कृष्वेह चारुं ।प्र यत्स्तोता जरिता तूर्ण्यर्थो वृषायमाण उप गीर्भिरीट्टे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́dhyandinasya ǀ sávanasya ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ indra ǀ kṛṣva ǀ ihá ǀ cā́rum ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ stotā́ ǀ jaritā́ ǀ tū́rṇi-arthaḥ ǀ vṛṣa-yámāṇaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ ī́ṭṭe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Partake,Indra, of the barley and the delicious cakes and butter of the midday sacrifice, when your zealous worshipper, hastening to adore you, and eager as a bull, is present, and celebrates (yo) with hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: Partake,Indra, of the barley and the delicious cakes and butter of the midday sacrifice, when your zealous worshipper, hastening to adore you, and eager as a bull, is present, and celebrates (yo) with hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तृतीये धानाः सवने पुरुष्टुत पुरोळाशमाहुतं मामहस्व नः ।ऋभुमंतं वाजवंतं त्वा कवे प्रयस्वंत उप शिक्षेम धीतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛtī́ye ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀ sávane ǀ puru-stuta ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ mamahasva ǀ naḥ ǀṛbhu-mántam ǀ vā́ja-vantam ǀ tvā ǀ kave ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣema ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who is praised of many, accept readily from our friend of barley, and cakes, and butter, offered at the third (or evening) sacrifice; ladenwith sacrificial viands, we approach with praises to your sage Indra, who is accompanied by theṛbhusand by Vāja.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is praised of many, accept readily from our friend of barley, and cakes, and butter, offered at the third (or evening) sacrifice; ladenwith sacrificial viands, we approach with praises to your sage Indra, who is accompanied by theṛbhusand by Vāja.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषण्वते ते चकृमा करंभं हरिवते हर्यश्वाय धानाः ।अपूपमद्धि सगणो मरुद्भिः सोमं पिब वृत्रहा शूर विद्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣaṇ-váte ǀ te ǀ cakṛma ǀ karambhám ǀ hári-vate ǀ hári-aśvāya ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀapūpám ǀ addhi ǀ sá-gaṇaḥ ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ sómam ǀ piba ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ śūra ǀ vidvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have prepared the parched grain and curds for you, associated with Pūṣan; the fried barley for you, lord of the tawny horses, associated with your steeds; attend by the troop of Maruts, eat the cakes; hero, who is wise, and the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: We have prepared the parched grain and curds for you, associated with Pūṣan; the fried barley for you, lord of the tawny horses, associated with your steeds; attend by the troop of Maruts, eat the cakes; hero, who is wise, and the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति धाना भरत तूयमस्मै पुरोळाशं वीरतमाय नृणां ।दिवेदिवे सदृशीरिंद्र तुभ्यं वर्धंतु त्वा सोमपेयाय धृष्णो ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀ bharata ǀ tū́yam ǀ asmai ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ vīrá-tamāya ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀdivé-dive ǀ sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ várdhantu ǀ tvā ǀ soma-péyāya ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer to him quickly (priests) the fried barley; offer to the most heroic of leaders the cakes and butter; may the like offerings, victorious Indra, presented to you daily, augment your vigour for the drinking of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer to him quickly (priests) the fried barley; offer to the most heroic of leaders the cakes and butter; may the like offerings, victorious Indra, presented to you daily, augment your vigour for the drinking of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Indra, Parvata, Etc.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ON a high car, O Parvata and Indra, bring pleasant viands, with brave heroes, hither.Enjoy the gifts, Gods, at our sacrifices wax strong by hymns, rejoice in our oblation. Stay still, O Maghavan, advance no farther. a draught of well-pressed Soma will I give thee.With sweetest song I grasp, O Mighty Indra, thy garment's hem as a child grasps his father's. Adhvaryu, sing we both; sing thou in answer: make we a laud acceptable to Indra.Upon this sacrificer's grass he seated: to Indra shall our eulogy be uttered. A wife, O Maghavan is home and dwelling: so let thy Bay Steeds yoked convey thee hither.Whenever we press out for thee the Soma, let Agni as our Herald speed to call thee. Depart, O Maghavan;again come hither: both there and here thy goat is Indra, Brother,Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and where thqu loosest thy loud-neighing Courser. Thou hast drunk Soma, Indra, turn thee homeward; thy joy is in thy home, thy racious Consort;Where thy tall chariot hath a place to rest in, and thy strong Courser is set free with guerdon. Bounteous are these, Aṅgirases, Virupas: the Asura's Heroes and the Sons of Heaven.They, giving store of wealth to Viśvāmitra, prolong his life through countless Soma-pressings. Maghavan weareth every shape at pleasure, effecting magic changes in his body,Holy One, drinker out of season, coming thrice, in a moment, through fit prayers, from heaven. The mighty sage, God-born and God-incited, who looks on men, restrained the billowy river.When Viśvāmitra was Sudās's escort, then Indra through the Kuśikas grew friendly. Like swans, prepare a song of praise with pressing-stones, glad in your hymns with juice poured forth in sacrifice.Ye singers, with the Gods, sages who look on men, ye Kutikas drink up the Soma's savoury meath. Come forward, Kuśikas, and be attentive; let loose Sudās's horse to win him riches.East, west, and north, let the King slay the foeman, then at earth's choicest place perform his worship. Praises to Indra have I sung, sustainer of this earth and heaven. This prayer of Viśvāmitra keeps secure the race of Bharatas. The Viśvāmitras have sung forth this prayer to Indra Thunder-aimed:So let him make us prosperous. Among the Kikatas what do thy cattle? They pour no milky draught, they heat no caldron.Bring thou to us the wealth of Pramaganda;give up to us, O Maghavan, the low-born. Sasarpari, the gift of Jamadagnis, hath lowed with mighty voice dispelling famine.The Daughter of the Sun hath spread our glory among the Gods, imperishable, deathless. Sasarpari brought glory speedily to these, over the generations of the Fivefold Race;Daughter of Paksa, she bestows new vital power, she whom the ancient Jamadagnis gave to me. Strong be the pair of oxen, firm the axles, let not the pole slip nor the yoke be broken.May Indra, keep the yoke-pins from decaying: attend us, thou whose fellies are uninjured. O Indra, give our bodies strength, strength to the bulls who draw the wains,Strength to our seed and progeny that they may live, for thou art he who giveth strength. Enclose thee in the heart of Khayar timber, in the car wrought of Sinsapa put firmness.Show thyself strong, O Axle, fixed and strengthened: throw us not from the car whereon we travel. Let not this sovran of the wood leave us forlorn or injure us.Safe may we be until we reach our homes and rest us and unyoke. With various aids this day come to us, Indra, with best aids speed us, Maghavan, thou Hero.Let him who hatcth us fall headlong downward: him whom we hate let vital breath abandon. He heats his very axe, and then cuts a mere Semal blossom off.O Indra, like a caldron cracked and seething, so he pours out foam. Men notice not the arrow, O ye people; they bring the red beast deeming it a bullock.A sluggish steed men run not with the courser, nor ever lead an ass before a charger. These men, the sons of Bhārata, O Indra, regard not severance or close connexion.They urge their own steed as it were another's, and take him, swift as the bow's string, to battle.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः ।वीतं हव्यान्यध्वरेषु देवा वर्धेथां गीर्भिरिळया मदंता ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāparvatā ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ vāmī́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vahatam ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǀvītám ǀ havyā́ni ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ devā ǀ várdhethām ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ íḷayā ǀ mádantā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Parvata, bring hither, in a spacious car, delightful viands (genitive rative of) good progeny; partake, deities, of the oblations (offered)at (our) sacrifices, and gratified by the (sacrificial) food, be elevated by our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Parvata, bring hither, in a spacious car, delightful viands (genitive rative of) good progeny; partake, deities, of the oblations (offered)at (our) sacrifices, and gratified by the (sacrificial) food, be elevated by our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठा सु कं मघवन्मा परा गाः सोमस्य नु त्वा सुषुतस्य यक्षि ।पितुर्न पुत्रः सिचमा रभे त इंद्र स्वादिष्ठया गिरा शचीवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tíṣṭha ǀ sú ǀ kam ǀ magha-van ǀ mā́ ǀ párā ǀ gāḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ nú ǀ tvā ǀ sú-sutasya ǀ yakṣi ǀpitúḥ ǀ ná ǀ putráḥ ǀ sícam ǀ ā́ ǀ rabhe ǀ te ǀ índra ǀ svā́diṣṭhayā ǀ girā́ ǀ śacī-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tarry a while contentedly,Maghavan(at our rite); go not away; for I offer to you (the libation) of the copiously-effused Soma; powerful Indra, I lay hold of the skirts (of your robe) with sweet-flavoured commendations, as a son (clings to the garment) of a father.
verses.wilson_translation: Tarry a while contentedly,Maghavan(at our rite); go not away; for I offer to you (the libation) of the copiously-effused Soma; powerful Indra, I lay hold of the skirts (of your robe) with sweet-flavoured commendations, as a son (clings to the garment) of a father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शंसावाध्वर्यो प्रति मे गृणीहींद्राय वाहः कृणवाव जुष्टं ।एदं बर्हिर्यजमानस्य सीदाथा च भूदुक्थमिंद्राय शस्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: śáṃsāva ǀ adhvaryo íti ǀ práti ǀ me ǀ gṛṇīhi ǀ índrāya ǀ vā́haḥ ǀ kṛṇavāva ǀ júṣṭam ǀā́ ǀ idám ǀ barhíḥ ǀ yájamānasya ǀ sīda ǀ átha ǀ ca ǀ bhūt ǀ ukthám ǀ índrāya ǀ śastám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adhvaryu, let us two offer praise; do you concur with me; let us address plural asing praise to Indra; sit down, Indra, on the sacred grass (prepared by) the instrumental tutor of the rite; and may our commendations be most acceptable to Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Adhvaryu, let us two offer praise; do you concur with me; let us address plural asing praise to Indra; sit down, Indra, on the sacred grass (prepared by) the instrumental tutor of the rite; and may our commendations be most acceptable to Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जायेदस्तं मघवन्त्सेदु योनिस्तदित्त्वा युक्ता हरयो वहंतु ।यदा कदा च सुनवाम सोममग्निष्ट्वा दूतो धन्वात्यच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: jāyā́ ǀ ít ǀ ástam ǀ magha-van ǀ sā́ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ yóniḥ ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ tvā ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ vahantu ǀyadā́ ǀ kadā́ ǀ ca ǀ sunávāma ǀ sómam ǀ agníḥ ǀ tvā ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ dhanvāti ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: A man's wife,Maghavan, is hiw dwelling; verily she is his plural ce of birth; thither let your horses, harnessed (to your car), convey you; we prepare the Somaat the fit season; may Agnicome as our messenger befor eyou.
verses.wilson_translation: A man's wife,Maghavan, is hiw dwelling; verily she is his plural ce of birth; thither let your horses, harnessed (to your car), convey you; we prepare the Somaat the fit season; may Agnicome as our messenger befor eyou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परा याहि मघवन्ना च याहींद्र भ्रातरुभयत्रा ते अर्थं ।यत्रा रथस्य बृहतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो रासभस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ yāhi ǀ magha-van ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ yāhi ǀ índra ǀ bhrātaḥ ǀ ubhayátra ǀ te ǀ ártham ǀyátra ǀ ráthasya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ ni-dhā́nam ǀ vi-mócanam ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ rā́sabhasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Depart,Maghavan; come Indra; both ways, protector, there is a motive for you whether it be standing in your vast chariot, or liberating your neighing steed.
verses.wilson_translation: Depart,Maghavan; come Indra; both ways, protector, there is a motive for you whether it be standing in your vast chariot, or liberating your neighing steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपाः सोममस्तमिंद्र प्र याहि कल्याणीर्जाया सुरणं गृहे ते ।यत्रा रथस्य बृहतो निधानं विमोचनं वाजिनो दक्षिणावत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ápāḥ ǀ sómam ǀ ástam ǀ indra ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ kalyāṇī́ḥ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ su-ráṇam ǀ gṛhé ǀ te ǀyátra ǀ ráthasya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ ni-dhā́nam ǀ vi-mócanam ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā-vat ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you have drunk the Soma, then,Indra, go home; an auspicious life (abides) plural asantly in your dwelling; in either (case) there is the standing in your car or liberating the steeds for provender.
verses.wilson_translation: When you have drunk the Soma, then,Indra, go home; an auspicious life (abides) plural asantly in your dwelling; in either (case) there is the standing in your car or liberating the steeds for provender.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमे भोजा अंगिरसो विरूपा दिवस्पुत्रासो असुरस्य वीराः ।विश्वामित्राय ददतो मघानि सहस्रसावे प्र तिरंत आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ví-rūpāḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀviśvā́mitrāya ǀ dádataḥ ǀ maghā́ni ǀ sahasra-sāvé ǀ prá ǀ tirante ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These (sacrificers) are the Bhojas, of whom the diversified Aṅgirasas(are the priests); and the heroic sons of the expeller (of the foes of the gods) from heaven, bestowing riches upon Viśvāmitraat the sacrifice of a thousand (victims), prolong (his) life.
verses.wilson_translation: These (sacrificers) are the Bhojas, of whom the diversified Aṅgirasas(are the priests); and the heroic sons of the expeller (of the foes of the gods) from heaven, bestowing riches upon Viśvāmitraat the sacrifice of a thousand (victims), prolong (his) life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रूपंरूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं परि स्वां ।त्रिर्यद्दिवः परि मुहूर्तमागात्स्वैर्मंत्रैरनृतुपा ऋतावा ॥
verses.transliteration: rūpám-rūpam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ bobhavīti ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ pári ǀ svā́m ǀtríḥ ǀ yát ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ muhūrtám ǀ ā́ ǀ ágāt ǀ sváiḥ ǀ mántraiḥ ǀ ánṛtu-pāḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavanbecomes repeatedly (manifest) in various forms, practising delusions with respect to his own peculiar person n; and invoked by his appropriate prayers, he comes in a moment from heaven to the three (daily rites), and, although observant of seasons, is the drinker (of the Soma) irrespective of season.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavanbecomes repeatedly (manifest) in various forms, practising delusions with respect to his own peculiar person n; and invoked by his appropriate prayers, he comes in a moment from heaven to the three (daily rites), and, although observant of seasons, is the drinker (of the Soma) irrespective of season.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महाँ ऋषिर्देवजा देवजूतोऽस्तभ्नात्सिंधुमर्णवं नृचक्षाः ।विश्वामित्रो यदवहत्सुदासमप्रियायत कुशिकेभिरिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahā́n ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ deva-jā́ḥ ǀ devá-jūtaḥ ǀ ástabhnāt ǀ síndhum ǀ arṇavám ǀ nṛ-cákṣāḥ ǀviśvā́mitraḥ ǀ yát ǀ ávahat ǀ su-dā́sam ǀ ápriyāyata ǀ kuśikébhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The great ṛṣi the genitive rator of the gods, the attracted by the deities, the overlooker of the leaders (at holy rites),Viśvāmitraattested the watery stream when he sacrificed for Sudās;Indra, with the Kuśikaswas plural ased.
verses.wilson_translation: The great ṛṣi the genitive rator of the gods, the attracted by the deities, the overlooker of the leaders (at holy rites),Viśvāmitraattested the watery stream when he sacrificed for Sudās;Indra, with the Kuśikaswas plural ased.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हंसा इव कृणुथ श्लोकमद्रिभिर्मदंतो गीर्भिरध्वरे सुते सचा ।देवेभिर्विप्रा ऋषयो नृचक्षसो वि पिबध्वं कुशिकाः सोम्यं मधु ॥
verses.transliteration: haṃsā́ḥ-iva ǀ kṛṇutha ǀ ślókam ǀ ádri-bhiḥ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ suté ǀ sácā ǀdevébhiḥ ǀ viprāḥ ǀ ṛṣayaḥ ǀ nṛ-cakṣasaḥ ǀ ví ǀ pibadhvam ǀ kuśikāḥ ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sages and saints overlookers of the leaders (of sacred rites),Kuśikas, when the Somais expresssed with stones at the sacrifice, then exhilarating (the gods) with praises, sing the holy strain (aloud) like (screaming) swans, and, together with the gods, drink the sweet juice of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Sages and saints overlookers of the leaders (of sacred rites),Kuśikas, when the Somais expresssed with stones at the sacrifice, then exhilarating (the gods) with praises, sing the holy strain (aloud) like (screaming) swans, and, together with the gods, drink the sweet juice of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उप प्रेत कुशिकाश्चेतयध्वमश्वं राये प्र मुंचता सुदासः ।राजा वृत्रं जंघनत्प्रागपागुदगथा यजाते वर आ पृथिव्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ prá ǀ ita ǀ kuśikāḥ ǀ cetáyadhvam ǀ áśvam ǀ rāyé ǀ prá ǀ muñcata ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀrā́jā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaṅghanat ǀ prā́k ǀ ápāk ǀ údak ǀ átha ǀ yajāte ǀ váre ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Approach,Kuśikas, the steed of Sudās; animate (him), and let him loose to (win) riches (for theraja); for the king (of the gods) has slain Vṛtrain the East, in the West, in the North, therefore let (Sudās) worship him in the best (regions) of the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Approach,Kuśikas, the steed of Sudās; animate (him), and let him loose to (win) riches (for theraja); for the king (of the gods) has slain Vṛtrain the East, in the West, in the North, therefore let (Sudās) worship him in the best (regions) of the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इमे रोदसी उभे अहमिंद्रमतुष्टवं ।विश्वामित्रस्य रक्षति ब्रह्मेदं भारतं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imé íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ahám ǀ índram ǀ átustavam ǀviśvā́mitrasya ǀ rakṣati ǀ bráhma ǀ idám ǀ bhā́ratam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have made Indraglorified by these two, heaven and earth, and this prayer of Viśvāmitraprotects the race of Bharata.
verses.wilson_translation: I have made Indraglorified by these two, heaven and earth, and this prayer of Viśvāmitraprotects the race of Bharata.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वामित्रा अरासत ब्रह्मेंद्राय वज्रिणे ।करदिन्नः सुराधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvā́mitrāḥ ǀ arāsata ǀ bráhma ǀ índrāya ǀ vajríṇe ǀkárat ǀ ít ǀ naḥ ǀ su-rā́dhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Viśvāmitrashave addressed the prayer to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt; may he therefore render us very opulent.
verses.wilson_translation: The Viśvāmitrashave addressed the prayer to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt; may he therefore render us very opulent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किं ते कृण्वंति कीकटेषु गावो नाशिरं दुह्रे न तपंति घर्मं ।आ नो भर प्रमगंदस्य वेदो नैचाशाखं मघवन्रंधया नः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ te ǀ kṛṇvanti ǀ kī́kaṭeṣu ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ā-śíram ǀ duhré ǀ ná ǀ tapanti ǀ gharmám ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhara ǀ prá-magandasya ǀ védaḥ ǀ naicā-śākhám ǀ magha-van ǀ randhaya ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What do the cattle for you among the Kīkaṭas; they yield no milk to mix with the Soma, they need not the vessel (for the libation); bring them to us; (bring also) the wealth of the son of the usurer, and give us Maghavan, (the possessions) of the low branches (of the community).
verses.wilson_translation: What do the cattle for you among the Kīkaṭas; they yield no milk to mix with the Soma, they need not the vessel (for the libation); bring them to us; (bring also) the wealth of the son of the usurer, and give us Maghavan, (the possessions) of the low branches (of the community).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ससर्परीरमतिं बाधमाना बृहन्मिमाय जमदग्निदत्ता ।आ सूर्यस्य दुहिता ततान श्रवो देवेष्वमृतमजुर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: sasarparī́ḥ ǀ ámatim ǀ bā́dhamānā ǀ bṛhát ǀ mimāya ǀ jamádagni-dattā ǀā́ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ duhitā́ ǀ tatāna ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ajuryám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The daughter of Sūryagiven by Jamadagnigliding everywhere and dissipating ignorance, has emitted a mighty (sound), and has diffused ambrosial imperishable food among the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The daughter of Sūryagiven by Jamadagnigliding everywhere and dissipating ignorance, has emitted a mighty (sound), and has diffused ambrosial imperishable food among the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ससर्परीरभरत्तूयमेभ्योऽधि श्रवः पांचजन्यासु कृष्टिषु ।सा पक्ष्या नव्यमायुर्दधाना यां मे पलस्तिजमदग्नयो ददुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sasarparī́ḥ ǀ abharat ǀ tū́yam ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ pā́ñca-janyāsu ǀ kṛṣṭíṣu ǀsā́ ǀ pakṣyā́ ǀ návyam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ dádhānā ǀ yā́m ǀ me ǀ palasti-jamadagnáyaḥ ǀ dadúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May she, gliding everywhere, quickly bring us food (suited) to the five races of men; may she, the daughter of the sun whom the grey-hairedjamadagnisgave to me, (be) the bestower of new life.
verses.wilson_translation: May she, gliding everywhere, quickly bring us food (suited) to the five races of men; may she, the daughter of the sun whom the grey-hairedjamadagnisgave to me, (be) the bestower of new life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्थिरौ गावौ भवतां वीळुरक्षो मेषा वि वर्हि मा युगं वि शारि ।इंद्रः पातल्ये ददतां शरीतोररिष्टनेमे अभि नः सचस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: sthiráu ǀ gā́vau ǀ bhavatām ǀ vīḷúḥ ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ īṣā́ ǀ ví ǀ varhi ǀ mā́ ǀ yugám ǀ ví ǀ śāri ǀíndraḥ ǀ pātalyé íti ǀ dadatām ǀ śárītoḥ ǀ áriṣṭa-neme ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ sacasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the horse be steady, the axle be strong, the pole be not defective, the yoke not be rotten; may Indrapreserve the two yoke-pins from decay; car with uninjured felloes, be ready for us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the horse be steady, the axle be strong, the pole be not defective, the yoke not be rotten; may Indrapreserve the two yoke-pins from decay; car with uninjured felloes, be ready for us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बलं धेहि तनूषु नो बलमिंद्रानळुत्सु नः ।बलं तोकाय तनयाय जीवसे त्वं हि बलदा असि ॥
verses.transliteration: bálam ǀ dhehi ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ naḥ ǀ bálam ǀ indra ǀ anaḷút-su ǀ naḥ ǀbálam ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ jīváse ǀ tvám ǀ hí ǀ bala-dā́ḥ ǀ ási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give strength,Indra, to our bodies; give strength to our vehicles; (give) strength to our sons and grandsons; that they may live (long); for you are giver of strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Give strength,Indra, to our bodies; give strength to our vehicles; (give) strength to our sons and grandsons; that they may live (long); for you are giver of strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि व्ययस्व खदिरस्य सारमोजो धेहि स्पंदने शिंशपायां ।अक्ष वीळो वीळित वीळयस्व मा यामादस्मादव जीहिपो नः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ vyayasva ǀ khadirásya ǀ sā́ram ǀ ójaḥ ǀ dhehi ǀ spandané ǀ śiṃśápāyām ǀákṣa ǀ vīḷo íti ǀ vīḷita ǀ vīḷáyasva ǀ mā́ ǀ yā́māt ǀ asmā́t ǀ áva ǀ jīhipaḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fix firmly the substance of the khayar (axle), give solidity to theśiśu(floor) of the car; strong axle, strongly fixed by us, be strong; cast us not from out of our conveyance.
verses.wilson_translation: Fix firmly the substance of the khayar (axle), give solidity to theśiśu(floor) of the car; strong axle, strongly fixed by us, be strong; cast us not from out of our conveyance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमस्मान्वनस्पतिर्मा च हा मा च रीरिषत् ।स्वस्त्या गृहेभ्य आवसा आ विमोचनात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ asmā́n ǀ vánaspátiḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ca ǀ hā́ḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ca ǀ ririṣat ǀsvastí ǀ ā́ ǀ gṛhébhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ avasái ǀ ā́ ǀ vi-mócanāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this lord of the forest never desert us nor do us harm; may we travel prosperously home until the stopping (of the car), until the unharnessing (of the steeds).
verses.wilson_translation: May this lord of the forest never desert us nor do us harm; may we travel prosperously home until the stopping (of the car), until the unharnessing (of the steeds).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रोतिभिर्बहुलाभिर्नो अद्य याच्छ्रेष्ठाभिर्मघवंछूर जिन्व ।यो नो द्वेष्ट्यधरः सस्पदीष्ट यमु द्विष्मस्तमु प्राणो जहातु ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ bahulā́bhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ yāt-śreṣṭhā́bhiḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ śūra ǀ jinva ǀyáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dvéṣṭi ǀ ádharaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ padīṣṭa ǀ yám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dviṣmáḥ ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prāṇáḥ ǀ jahātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, hero,possessor of wealth, protect us this day against our foes with many and excellent defences; may the vile wretch who hates us fall (before us); may the breath of life depart from him whom we hate.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, hero,possessor of wealth, protect us this day against our foes with many and excellent defences; may the vile wretch who hates us fall (before us); may the breath of life depart from him whom we hate.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परशुं चिद्वि तपति शिंबलं चिद्वि वृश्चति ।उखा चिदिंद्र येषंती प्रयस्ता फेनमस्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: paraśúm ǀ cit ǀ ví ǀ tapati ǀ śimbalám ǀ cit ǀ ví ǀ vṛścati ǀukhā́ ǀ cit ǀ indra ǀ yéṣantī ǀ prá-yastā ǀ phénam ǀ asyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: As (the tree) suffers pain from the axe, as the śimbal flower is (easily) cut off, as the injured cauldron leaking scatters foam, so may mine enemy perish.
verses.wilson_translation: As (the tree) suffers pain from the axe, as the śimbal flower is (easily) cut off, as the injured cauldron leaking scatters foam, so may mine enemy perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न सायकस्य चिकिते जनासो लोधं नयंति पशु मन्यमानाः ।नावाजिनं वाजिना हासयंति न गर्दभं पुरो अश्वान्नयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sā́yakasya ǀ cikite ǀ janāsaḥ ǀ lodhám ǀ nayanti ǀ páśu ǀ mányamānāḥ ǀná ǀ ávājinam ǀ vājínā ǀ hāsayanti ǀ ná ǀ gardabhám ǀ puráḥ ǀ áśvāt ǀ nayanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men, (the might) of the destroyer is not known toyou; regarding him as a mere animal, they lead him away desirous (silently to complete his devotions); the wise condescend not to turn the foolish into ridicule, they do not lead the ass before the horse.
verses.wilson_translation: Men, (the might) of the destroyer is not known toyou; regarding him as a mere animal, they lead him away desirous (silently to complete his devotions); the wise condescend not to turn the foolish into ridicule, they do not lead the ass before the horse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इम इंद्र भरतस्य पुत्रा अपपित्वं चिकितुर्न प्रपित्वं ।हिन्वंत्यश्वमरणं न नित्यं ज्यावाजं परि णयंत्याजौ ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ indra ǀ bharatásya ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ apa-pitvám ǀ cikituḥ ǀ ná ǀ pra-pitvám ǀhinvánti ǀ áśvam ǀ áraṇam ǀ ná ǀ nítyam ǀ jyā-vā́jam ǀ pári ǀ nayanti ǀ ājáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: These sons of Bharata,Indra, understand severance (from the Vasiṣṭhas), not association (with them); they urge their steeds (against them) as against a constant foe; they bear a stout bow (for their destruction) in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: These sons of Bharata,Indra, understand severance (from the Vasiṣṭhas), not association (with them); they urge their steeds (against them) as against a constant foe; they bear a stout bow (for their destruction) in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: २२ प्रजापतिर्वैश्वामित्रः, प्रजापतिर्वाच्यो वा। विश्वे देवाः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To him adorable, mighty, meet for synods, this strengthening hymn, unceasing, have they offered.May Agni hear us with his homely splendours, hear us, Eternal One, with heavenly lustre. To mighty Heaven and Earth I sing forth loudly: my wish goes out desirous and well knowingBoth, at whose laud in synods, showing favour, the Gods rejoice them with the living mortal. O Heaven and Earth, may your great law he faithful: he ye our leaders for our high advantage.To Heaven and Earth I offer this my homage, with food, O Agni, as I pray for riches. Yea, holy Heaven and Earth, the ancient sages whose word was ever true had power to find you;And brave men in the fightwhere heroes conquer, O Earth, have known you well and paid you honour. What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it?Seen are their lowest dwelling-places only, but they are in remote and secret regions. The Sage who looketh on mankind hath viewed them bedewed, rejoicing in the seat of Order.They make a home as for a bird, though parted, with one same will finding themselves together. Partners though parted, with far-distant limits, on one firm place both stand for ever watchful,And, being young for evermore, as sisters, speak to each other names that are united. All living things they part and keep asunder; though bearing up the mighty Gods they reel not.One All is Lord of what is fixed and moving, that walks, that flies, this multiform creation. Afar the Ancient from of old I ponder, our kinship with our mighty Sire and Father,—Singing the praise whereof the Gods by custom stand on the spacious far-extended pathway. This laud, O Heaven and Earth, to you I utter: let the kind-hearted hear, whose tongue is Agni,Young, Sovran Rulers, Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise and very glorious Ādityas. The fair-tongued Savitar, the golden-handed, comes thrice from heaven as Lord in our assembly.Bear to the Gods this song of praise, and send us, then, Savitar, complete and perfect safety. Deft worker, skiful-handed, helpful, holy, may Tvaṣṭar, God, give us these things to aid us,Take your delight, Ye Ṛbhus joined with Pūṣan: ye have prepared the rite with stones adjusted. Borne on their flashing car, the spear-armed Maruts, the nimble Youths of Heaven, the Sons of Order,The Holy, and Sarasvatī, shall hear us: ye Mighty, give us wealth with noble offspring. To Viṣṇu rich in marvels, songs And praises shall go as singers on the road of Bhaga,—The Chieftain of the Mighty Stride, whose Mothers, the many young Dames, never disregard him. Indra, who rules through all his powers heroic, hath with his majesty filled earth and heaven.Lord of brave hosts, Fort-crusher, Vṛtra-slayer, gather thou up and bring us store of cattle. My Sires are the Nāsatyas, kind tokinsmen: the Aśvins' kinship is a glorious title.For ye are they who give us store of riches: ye guard your gift uncheated by the bounteous. This is, ye Wise, your great and glorious title, that all ye Deities abide in Indra.Friend, Much-invoked! art thou with thy dear Ṛbhus: fashion ye this our hymn for our advantage. Aryaman, Aditi deserve our worship: the laws of Varuṇa remain unbroken.The lot of childlessness remove ye from us, and let our course be rich in kine and offspring. May the Gods’ envoy, sent to many a quarter, proclaim us sinless for our perfect safety.May Earth and Heaven, the Sun, the waters, hear us, and the wide firmament and constellations. Hear us the mouatains which distil the rain-drops, and, resting firm, rejoice in freshening moisture.May Aditi with the Ādityas hear us, and Maruts grant us their auspicious shelter. Soft be our path for ever, well-provisioned: with pleasant meath, O Gods, the herbs besprinkle.Safe be my bliss, O Agni, in thy friendship: may I attain the seat of foodful. riches, Enjoy the offering: beam thou strength upon us; combine thou for our good all kinds of glory.Conquer in battle, Agni, all those foemen, and light us every day with loving kindness.

verses.sanskrit: इमं महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुः ।शृणोतु नो दम्येभिरनीकैः शृणोत्वग्निर्दिव्यैरजस्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ mahé ǀ vidathyā́ya ǀ śūṣám ǀ śáśvat ǀ kṛ́tvaḥ ǀ ī́ḍyāya ǀ prá ǀ jabhruḥ ǀśṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀ dámyebhiḥ ǀ ánīkaiḥ ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ agníḥ ǀ divyáiḥ ǀ ájasraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They recite repeatedly this gratifying praise to the great product of sacrifice (Agni); may he who is (endowed) with domestic radiance hear us; may the imperishable Agni, (endowed) with divine radiance, hear us.
verses.wilson_translation: They recite repeatedly this gratifying praise to the great product of sacrifice (Agni); may he who is (endowed) with domestic radiance hear us; may the imperishable Agni, (endowed) with divine radiance, hear us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महि महे दिवे अर्चा पृथिव्यै कामो म इच्छंचरति प्रजानन् ।ययोर्ह स्तोमे विदथेषु देवाः सपर्यवो मादयंते सचायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ mahé ǀ divé ǀ arca ǀ pṛthivyái ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ me ǀ icchán ǀ carati ǀ pra-jānán ǀyáyoḥ ǀ ha ǀ stóme ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ saparyávaḥ ǀ mādáyante ǀ sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing their greatness, offer worship to the vast heaven and to the earth; my desire, wishing (for felicity) proceed (to them), in whose praise the gods,desirous of adoration, delight together with their worshippers at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Knowing their greatness, offer worship to the vast heaven and to the earth; my desire, wishing (for felicity) proceed (to them), in whose praise the gods,desirous of adoration, delight together with their worshippers at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवोर्ऋतं रोदसी सत्यमस्तु महे षु णः सुविताय प्र भूतं ।इदं दिवे नमो अग्ने पृथिव्यै सपर्यामि प्रयसा यामि रत्नं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ rodasī íti ǀ satyám ǀ astu ǀ mahé ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ prá ǀ bhūtam ǀidám ǀ divé ǀ námaḥ ǀ agne ǀ pṛthivyái ǀ saparyā́mi ǀ práyasā ǀ yā́mi ǀ rátnam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heaven and earth, may your truth be ever inviolable; be propitious to us for the due completion of the rite; this adoration (Agni) is offered to heaven and earth; I worship (them) with (sacrificial) food; I solicit of them precious (wealth).
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth, may your truth be ever inviolable; be propitious to us for the due completion of the rite; this adoration (Agni) is offered to heaven and earth; I worship (them) with (sacrificial) food; I solicit of them precious (wealth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उतो हि वां पूर्व्या आविविद्र ऋतावरी रोदसी सत्यवाचः ।नरश्चिद्वां समिथे शूरसातौ ववंदिरे पृथिवि वेविदानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: utó íti ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ pūrvyā́ḥ ǀ ā-vividré ǀ ṛ́tavarī ítyṛta-varī ǀ rodasī íti ǀ satya-vā́caḥ ǀnáraḥ ǀ cit ǀ vām ǀ sam-ithé ǀ śū́ra-sātau ǀ vavandiré ǀ pṛthivi ǀ vévidānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heaven and earth, endowed with truth, they who are the ancient declarers of the truth, have obtained from you (what they desired); and so, earth, men cognizant (of the greaness of you both) have worshipped you for the sake of triumphing over (hostile) heroes in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth, endowed with truth, they who are the ancient declarers of the truth, have obtained from you (what they desired); and so, earth, men cognizant (of the greaness of you both) have worshipped you for the sake of triumphing over (hostile) heroes in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को अद्धा वेद क इह प्र वोचद्देवाँ अच्छा पथ्या का समेति ।ददृश्र एषामवमा सदांसि परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ addhā́ ǀ veda ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ devā́n ǀ áccha ǀ pathyā́ ǀ kā́ ǀ sám ǀ eti ǀdádṛśre ǀ eṣām ǀ avamā́ ǀ sádāṃsi ǀ páreṣu ǀ yā́ ǀ gúhyeṣu ǀ vratéṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who knows what is the truth, or who may here declare it? What is the proper path that leads to the gods? Their inferior abiding plural ces are beheld, as are those which (are situated) in superior mysterious rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Who knows what is the truth, or who may here declare it? What is the proper path that leads to the gods? Their inferior abiding plural ces are beheld, as are those which (are situated) in superior mysterious rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कविर्नृचक्षा अभि षीमचष्ट ऋतस्य योना विघृते मदंती ।नाना चक्राते सदनं यथा वेः समानेन क्रतुना संविदाने ॥
verses.transliteration: kavíḥ ǀ nṛ-cákṣāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sīm ǀ acaṣṭa ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónā ǀ víghṛte íti ví-ghṛte ǀ mádantī íti ǀnā́nā ǀ cakrāte íti ǀ sádanam ǀ yáthā ǀ véḥ ǀ samānéna ǀ krátunā ǀ saṃvidāné íti sam-vidāné ǁ
verses.english_translation: The far-seeing beholder of mankind (the sun), surveys this heaven and earth, rejoicing when deficient in moisture in the womb of the waters (the firmament), both concurring in community (of function), although they occupy various dwellings, like the diversified nests of a bird.
verses.wilson_translation: The far-seeing beholder of mankind (the sun), surveys this heaven and earth, rejoicing when deficient in moisture in the womb of the waters (the firmament), both concurring in community (of function), although they occupy various dwellings, like the diversified nests of a bird.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समान्या वियुते दूरेअंते ध्रुवे पदे तस्थतुर्जागरूके ।उत स्वसारा युवती भवंती आदु ब्रुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ॥
verses.transliteration: samānyā́ ǀ víyute íti ví-yute ǀ dūréante íti dūré-ante ǀ dhruvé ǀ padé ǀ tasthatuḥ ǀ jāgarū́ke íti ǀutá ǀ svásārā ǀ yuvatī́ íti ǀ bhávantī íti ǀ ā́t ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bruvāte íti ǀ mithunā́ni ǀ nā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Common (in function), disjoined, of distant termination, they remain vigilant in a permanent station; being, as it were, sisters, and ever young; they therefore address each other by twin appellations.
verses.wilson_translation: Common (in function), disjoined, of distant termination, they remain vigilant in a permanent station; being, as it were, sisters, and ever young; they therefore address each other by twin appellations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वेदेते जनिमा सं विविक्तो महो देवान्बिभ्रती न व्यथेते ।एजद्ध्रुवं पत्यते विश्वमेकं चरत्पतत्रि विषुणं वि जातं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvā ǀ ít ǀ eté íti ǀ jánima ǀ sám ǀ viviktaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ bíbhratī íti ǀ ná ǀ vyathete íti ǀéjat ǀ dhruvám ǀ patyate ǀ víśvam ǀ ékam ǀ cárat ǀ patatrí ǀ víṣuṇam ǀ ví ǀ jātám ǁ
verses.english_translation: These two keep all born things discrete, and, although comprehending the great divinities, are not distressed; all moving and stationary beings rest upon one (basis), whether animals, or birds, or creatures of various kinds.
verses.wilson_translation: These two keep all born things discrete, and, although comprehending the great divinities, are not distressed; all moving and stationary beings rest upon one (basis), whether animals, or birds, or creatures of various kinds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सना पुराणमध्येम्यारान्महः पितुर्जनितुर्जामि तन्नः ।देवासो यत्र पनितार एवैरुरौ पथि व्युते तस्थुरंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: sánā ǀ purāṇám ǀ ádhi ǀ emi ǀ ārā́t ǀ maháḥ ǀ pitúḥ ǀ janitúḥ ǀ jāmí ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀdevā́saḥ ǀ yátra ǀ panitā́raḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀ uráu ǀ pathí ǀ ví-ute ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I consider at present the eternal and ancient sisterhood to us of you, our great protectress and progenitrix, within whose vast and separated path your eulogists, the gods, travel in their chariots.
verses.wilson_translation: I consider at present the eternal and ancient sisterhood to us of you, our great protectress and progenitrix, within whose vast and separated path your eulogists, the gods, travel in their chariots.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं स्तोमं रोदसी प्र ब्रवीम्यृदूदराः शृणवन्नग्निजिह्वाः ।मित्रः सम्राजो वरुणो युवान आदित्यासः कवयः पप्रथानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ stómam ǀ rodasī íti ǀ prá ǀ bravīmi ǀ ṛdūdárāḥ ǀ śṛṇavan ǀ agni-jihvā́ḥ ǀmitráḥ ǀ sam-rā́jaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ ādityā́saḥ ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ paprathānā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I repeat this hymn, heaven and earth, to you; and may the soft-bellied, fire-tongued Mitra, royal Varuṇa, the youthfulĀdityas, all cognizant of the past, and proclaiming (their own acts), hear it.
verses.wilson_translation: I repeat this hymn, heaven and earth, to you; and may the soft-bellied, fire-tongued Mitra, royal Varuṇa, the youthfulĀdityas, all cognizant of the past, and proclaiming (their own acts), hear it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यपाणिः सविता सुजिह्वस्त्रिरा दिवो विदथे पत्यमानः ।देवेषु च सवितः श्लोकमश्रेरादस्मभ्यमा सुव सर्वतातिं ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-pāṇiḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ su-jihváḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ pátyamānaḥ ǀdevéṣu ǀ ca ǀ savitaríti ǀ ślókam ǀ áśreḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ asmábhyam ǀ ā́ ǀ suva ǀ sarvá-tātim ǁ
verses.english_translation: The golden-handed, soft-tongued Savitāis descending from heaven (to be present) thrice (daily) at the sacrifice; accept, Savitā, the praise (recited) by the worshippers, and thereupon grant to us all our desires.
verses.wilson_translation: The golden-handed, soft-tongued Savitāis descending from heaven (to be present) thrice (daily) at the sacrifice; accept, Savitā, the praise (recited) by the worshippers, and thereupon grant to us all our desires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुकृत्सुपाणिः स्ववाँ ऋतावा देवस्त्वष्टावसे तानि नो धात् ।पूषण्वंत ऋभवो मादयध्वमूर्ध्वग्रावाणो अध्वरमतष्ट ॥
verses.transliteration: su-kṛ́t ǀ su-pāṇíḥ ǀ svá-vān ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ deváḥ ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ ávase ǀ tā́ni ǀ naḥ ǀ dhāt ǀpūṣaṇ-vántaḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ mādayadhvam ǀ ūrdhvá-grāvāṇaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ ataṣṭa ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine Tvaṣṭā, the able artificer, the dextrous-handed, the possessor of wealth, the observer of truth, bestow upon us those things (which are necessary) for our preservation;ṛbhus, associated with Pūṣan, make us joyful, as they (the priests), with uplifted stones, prepare the sacred libation.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Tvaṣṭā, the able artificer, the dextrous-handed, the possessor of wealth, the observer of truth, bestow upon us those things (which are necessary) for our preservation;ṛbhus, associated with Pūṣan, make us joyful, as they (the priests), with uplifted stones, prepare the sacred libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विद्युद्रथा मरुत ऋष्टिमंतो दिवो मर्या ऋतजाता अयासः ।सरस्वती शृणवन्यज्ञियासो धाता रयिं सहवीरं तुरासः ॥
verses.transliteration: vidyút-rathāḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭi-mántaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ máryāḥ ǀ ṛtá-jātāḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀsárasvatī ǀ śṛṇavan ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ dhā́ta ǀ rayím ǀ sahá-vīram ǀ turāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Maruts, whose cars are the lightning, who are armed with spears, resplendent, destroyers of foes, from whom the waters proceed, (who are) unresting and adorable, and may Sarasvatīhear (my prayer); and may you (maruts), speedy in your liberality, bestow (upon us) riches and good offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, whose cars are the lightning, who are armed with spears, resplendent, destroyers of foes, from whom the waters proceed, (who are) unresting and adorable, and may Sarasvatīhear (my prayer); and may you (maruts), speedy in your liberality, bestow (upon us) riches and good offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विष्णुं स्तोमासः पुरुदस्ममर्का भगस्येव कारिणो यामनि ग्मन् ।उरुक्रमः ककुहो यस्य पूर्वीर्न मर्धंति युवतयो जनित्रीः ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣṇum ǀ stómāsaḥ ǀ puru-dasmám ǀ arkā́ḥ ǀ bhágasya-iva ǀ kāríṇaḥ ǀ yā́mani ǀ gman ǀuru-kramáḥ ǀ kakuháḥ ǀ yásya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ mardhanti ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ jánitrīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May (our) praises and prayers, the causes of good fortune, attain at this sacrifice Viṣṇu, the object of many rites; he, the wide-stepping; whose commands the many-blending regions of space, the genitive rators (of all beings), do not disobey.
verses.wilson_translation: May (our) praises and prayers, the causes of good fortune, attain at this sacrifice Viṣṇu, the object of many rites; he, the wide-stepping; whose commands the many-blending regions of space, the genitive rators (of all beings), do not disobey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो विश्वैर्वीर्यैः पत्यमान उभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा ।पुरंदरो वृत्रहा धृष्णुषेणः संगृभ्या न आ भरा भूरि पश्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ víśvaiḥ ǀ vīryáiḥ ǀ pátyamānaḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ paprau ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀpuram-daráḥ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ dhṛṣṇú-seṇaḥ ǀ sam-gṛ́bhya ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ bhū́ri ǀ paśváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, invested with all energies, has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness; do you, who are the destroyer of cities, the slayer of Vṛtra, the leader of a conquering host, collect cattle and bestow them abundantly upon us.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, invested with all energies, has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness; do you, who are the destroyer of cities, the slayer of Vṛtra, the leader of a conquering host, collect cattle and bestow them abundantly upon us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नासत्या मे पितरा बंधुपृच्छा सजात्यमश्विनोश्चारु नाम ।युवं हि स्थो रयिदौ नो रयीणां दात्रं रक्षेथे अकवैरदब्धा ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́satyā ǀ me ǀ pitárā ǀ bandhu-pṛ́cchā ǀ sa-jātyám ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ cā́ru ǀ nā́ma ǀyuvám ǀ hí ǀ stháḥ ǀ rayi-dáu ǀ naḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ dātrám ǀ rakṣethe íti ǀ ákavaiḥ ǀ ádabdhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nāsatyas, my protectors, inquirers (after the wishes) of your kinsman, beautiful is your cognate appellation of Aśvins; be to us the liberal donors of riches; do you, who are irresistible, protect the offerer (of the oblation) with unblameable (defences).]
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, my protectors, inquirers (after the wishes) of your kinsman, beautiful is your cognate appellation of Aśvins; be to us the liberal donors of riches; do you, who are irresistible, protect the offerer (of the oblation) with unblameable (defences).]
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महत्तद्वः कवयश्चारु नाम यद्ध देवा भवथ विश्व इंद्रे ।सख ऋभुभिः पुरुहूत प्रियेभिरिमां धियं सातये तक्षता नः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahát ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ cā́ru ǀ nā́ma ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ devāḥ ǀ bhávatha ǀ víśve ǀ índre ǀsákhā ǀ ṛbhú-bhiḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ priyébhiḥ ǀ imā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ sātáye ǀ takṣata ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sages acquainted with the past, excellent is that beautiful appellation under which you have both become gods in (the sphere of)Indra; do you, Indra, the invoked of many, a friend, (associated) with the belovedṛbhus, shape this prayer for our benefit.
verses.wilson_translation: Sages acquainted with the past, excellent is that beautiful appellation under which you have both become gods in (the sphere of)Indra; do you, Indra, the invoked of many, a friend, (associated) with the belovedṛbhus, shape this prayer for our benefit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्यमा णो अदितिर्यज्ञियासोऽदब्धानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि ।युयोत नो अनपत्यानि गंतोः प्रजावान्नः पशुमाँ अस्तु गातुः ॥
verses.transliteration: aryamā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ ádabdhāni ǀ váruṇasya ǀ vratā́ni ǀyuyóta ǀ naḥ ǀ anapatyā́ni ǀ gántoḥ ǀ prajā́-vān ǀ naḥ ǀ paśu-mā́n ǀ astu ǀ gātúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Aryaman,Aditi, the adorable (gods), and the unimpeded functions of Varuṇa(protect) us; keep us from (following) the course unpropitious to offspring, and may our dwelling be abundant in progeny and cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: May Aryaman,Aditi, the adorable (gods), and the unimpeded functions of Varuṇa(protect) us; keep us from (following) the course unpropitious to offspring, and may our dwelling be abundant in progeny and cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवानां दूतः पुरुध प्रसूतोऽनागान्नो वोचतु सर्वताता ।शृणोतु नः पृथिवी द्यौरुतापः सूर्यो नक्षत्रैरुर्वंतरिक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ purudhá ǀ prá-sūtaḥ ǀ ánāgān ǀ naḥ ǀ vocatu ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀśṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ utá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ nákṣatraiḥ ǀ urú ǀ antárikṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the messenger of the gods, engendered in many plural ces, everywhere proclaim us void of offence; may earth and heaven, the waters, the sun, and the vast firmament, with the constellation, hear us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the messenger of the gods, engendered in many plural ces, everywhere proclaim us void of offence; may earth and heaven, the waters, the sun, and the vast firmament, with the constellation, hear us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शृण्वंतु नो वृषणः पर्वतासो ध्रुवक्षेमास इळया मदंतः ।आदित्यैर्नो अदितिः शृणोतु यच्छंतु नो मरुतः शर्म भद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛṇvántu ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀ dhruvá-kṣemāsaḥ ǀ íḷayā ǀ mádantaḥ ǀādityáiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śṛṇotu ǀ yácchantu ǀ naḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ bhadrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the (divine) showerers (of benefits), the deities of the mountains, and those abiding in fixed habitations, propitiated by the sacrificial food, hear us; may Aditi, with theĀdityas, heqar us; may the Marutsgrant us auspicious felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the (divine) showerers (of benefits), the deities of the mountains, and those abiding in fixed habitations, propitiated by the sacrificial food, hear us; may Aditi, with theĀdityas, heqar us; may the Marutsgrant us auspicious felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सदा सुगः पितुमाँ अस्तु पंथा मध्वा देवा ओषधीः सं पिपृक्त ।भगो मे अग्ने सख्ये न मृध्या उद्रायो अश्यां सदनं पुरुक्षोः ॥
verses.transliteration: sádā ǀ su-gáḥ ǀ pitu-mā́n ǀ astu ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ mádhvā ǀ devāḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sám ǀ pipṛkta ǀbhágaḥ ǀ me ǀ agne ǀ sakhyé ǀ ná ǀ mṛdhyāḥ ǀ út ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ aśyām ǀ sádanam ǀ puru-kṣóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May our path ever be easy of going, and provided with food; sprinkle, gods, the plural nts with sweet water; (safe) in your friendship,Agni, may my fortune never be impaired, but may I occupy a dwelling (abounding) with riches and ample food.
verses.wilson_translation: May our path ever be easy of going, and provided with food; sprinkle, gods, the plural nts with sweet water; (safe) in your friendship,Agni, may my fortune never be impaired, but may I occupy a dwelling (abounding) with riches and ample food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीह्यस्मद्र्यक्सं मिमीहि श्रवांसि ।विश्वाँ अग्ने पृत्सु तांजेषि शत्रूनहा विश्वा सुमना दीदिही नः ॥
verses.transliteration: svádasva ǀ havyā́ ǀ sám ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ didīhi ǀ asmadryák ǀ sám ǀ mimīhi ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀvíśvān ǀ agne ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ tā́n ǀ jeṣi ǀ śátrūn ǀ áhā ǀ víśvā ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ dīdihi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Taste (Agni) the oblations, make manifest (for us) abundant food measure out the viands before us; you overcome all those (who are) our enemies in conflict;  favourably inclined towards us lighten up all our (ceremonies) day by day.
verses.wilson_translation: Taste (Agni) the oblations, make manifest (for us) abundant food measure out the viands before us; you overcome all those (who are) our enemies in conflict;  favourably inclined towards us lighten up all our (ceremonies) day by day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: २२ प्रजापतिर्वैश्वामित्रः, प्रजापतिर्वाच्यो वा। विश्वे देवाः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AT the first shining of the earliest Mornings, in the Cow's home was born the Great Eternal.Now shall the statutes of the Gods be valid. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion - Let not the Gods here injure us, O Agni, nor Fathers of old time who know the region,Nor the sign set between two ancient dwellings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. My wishes fly abroad to many places: I glance back to the ancient sacrifices.Let us declare the truth when fire is kindled. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. King Universal, born to sundry quarters, extended through the wood be lies on couches.One Mother rests: another feeds the Infant. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Lodged in old plants, he grows again in younger, swiftly within the newly-born and tender.Though they are unimpregned, he makes them fruitful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Now lying far away, Child of two Mothers, he wanders unrestrained, the single youngling.These are the laws of Varuṇa and Mitra. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Child of two Mothers, Priest, sole Lord in synods, he still precedes while resting as foundation.They who speak sweetly bring him sweet addresses. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. As to a friendly warrior when he battles, each thing that comes anear is seen to meet him.The hymn commingles with the cow's oblation. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Deep within these the hoary envoy pierceth; mighty, he goeth to the realm of splendour,And looketh on us, clad in wondrous beauty. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Viṣṇu, the guardian, keeps the loftiest station, upholding dear, immortal dwelling-places.Agni knows well all these created beings. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Ye, variant Pair, have made yourselves twin beauties: one of the Twain is dark, bright shines the other;And yet these two, the dark, the red, are Sisters. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Where the two Cows, the Mother and the Daughter, meet and give suck yielding their lordly nectar,I praise them at the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Loud hath she lowed, licking the other's youngling. On what world hath the Milch-cow laid her udder?This Iḷā streameth with the milk of Order. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Earth weareth beauties manifold: uplifted, licking her Calf of eighteen months, she standeth.Well-skilled I seek the seat of law eternal. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Within a wondrous place the Twain are treasured: the one is manifest, the other hidden.One common pathway leads in two directions. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Let the milch-kine that have no calves storm downward, yielding rich nectar, streaming, unexhausted,These who are ever new and fresh and youthful. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. What time the Bull bellows in other regions, another herd receives the genial moisture;For he is Bhaga, King, the earth's Protector. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Let us declare the Hero's wealth in horses, O all ye folk: of this the Gods have knowledge.Sixfold they bear him, or by fives are harnessed. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Tvaṣṭar the God, the omniform. Creator, begets and feeds mankind in various manner.His, verily, arc all these living creatures. Great is the Gods’ supreme dominion. The two great meeting Bowls hath he united: each of the Pair is laden with histreasure.The Hero is renowned for gathering riches. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion. Yea, and on this our earth the All-Sustainer dwells like a King with noble friends about him.In his protection heroes rest in safety. Great is the Cods' supreme and sole dominion. Rich in their gifts for thee are herbs and waters, and earth brings all her wealth for thee, O Indra.May we as friends of thine share goodly treasures. Great is the Gods’ supreme and sole dominion.

verses.sanskrit: उषसः पूर्वा अध यद्व्यूषुर्महद्वि जज्ञे अक्षरं पदे गोः ।व्रता देवानामुप नु प्रभूषन्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣásaḥ ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ ádha ǀ yát ǀ vi-ūṣúḥ ǀ mahát ǀ ví ǀ jajñe ǀ akṣáram ǀ padé ǀ góḥ ǀvratā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ úpa ǀ nú ǀ pra-bhū́ṣan ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the preceding dawns appear, the great imperishable (light) is engendered in the (firmament, the) sphere of the waters, and then the worshipper is alert to perform the rites (due to) the gods, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: When the preceding dawns appear, the great imperishable (light) is engendered in the (firmament, the) sphere of the waters, and then the worshipper is alert to perform the rites (due to) the gods, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मो षू णो अत्र जुहुरंत देवा मा पूर्वे अग्ने पितरः पदज्ञाः ।पुराण्योः सद्मनोः केतुरंतर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ juhuranta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ pū́rve ǀ agne ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ pada-jñā́ḥ ǀpurāṇyóḥ ǀ sádmanoḥ ǀ ketúḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the gods,Agni, now do us harm, nor the ancient progenitors, who have come to know the degree (of divinity); nor the manifester of light between the two ancient dwellings (earth and heaven, the sun); for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the gods,Agni, now do us harm, nor the ancient progenitors, who have come to know the degree (of divinity); nor the manifester of light between the two ancient dwellings (earth and heaven, the sun); for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि मे पुरुत्रा पतयंति कामाः शम्यच्छा दीद्ये पूर्व्याणि ।समिद्धे अग्नावृतमिद्वदेम महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ me ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ patayanti ǀ kā́māḥ ǀ śámi ǀ áccha ǀ dīdye ǀ pūrvyā́ṇi ǀsám-iddhe ǀ agnáu ǀ ṛtám ǀ ít ǀ vadema ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Variously do my manifold desires alight; present at the solemnity,  I recite ancient (hymns); when the fire is kindled we speak indeed the truth, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Variously do my manifold desires alight; present at the solemnity,  I recite ancient (hymns); when the fire is kindled we speak indeed the truth, for great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समानो राजा विभृतः पुरुत्रा शये शयासु प्रयुतो वनानु ।अन्या वत्सं भरति क्षेति माता महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: samānáḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ ví-bhṛtaḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ śáye ǀ śayā́su ǀ prá-yutaḥ ǀ vánā ǀ ánu ǀanyā́ ǀ vatsám ǀ bhárati ǀ kṣéti ǀ mātā́ ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The universal sovereign is conveyed to many directions; he sleeps in the plural ces of repose; he is connected with the forests; one mother (heaven) nourishes the child; the other (earth) gives him a dwelling; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The universal sovereign is conveyed to many directions; he sleeps in the plural ces of repose; he is connected with the forests; one mother (heaven) nourishes the child; the other (earth) gives him a dwelling; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आक्षित्पूर्वास्वपरा अनूरुत्सद्यो जातासु तरुणीष्वंतः ।अंतर्वतीः सुवते अप्रवीता महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-kṣít ǀ pū́rvāsu ǀ áparāḥ ǀ anūrút ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ jātā́su ǀ táruṇīṣu ǀ antáríti ǀantáḥ-vatīḥ ǀ suvate ǀ ápra-vītāḥ ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Existing in ancient plural nts, abiding afterwards in new, he enters into the young (herbs) as soon as they are produced; unimpregnated they become pregnant and bear fruit; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Existing in ancient plural nts, abiding afterwards in new, he enters into the young (herbs) as soon as they are produced; unimpregnated they become pregnant and bear fruit; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शयुः परस्तादध नु द्विमाताबंधनश्चरति वत्स एकः ।मित्रस्य ता वरुणस्य व्रतानि महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: śayúḥ ǀ parástāt ǀ ádha ǀ nú ǀ dvi-mātā́ ǀ abandhanáḥ ǀ carati ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀmitrásya ǀ tā́ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ vratā́ni ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The child of two mothers sleeps in the west, but (in the morning) the single infant proceeds unobstructed (through the sky); these are the functions of Mitraand Varuṇa; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The child of two mothers sleeps in the west, but (in the morning) the single infant proceeds unobstructed (through the sky); these are the functions of Mitraand Varuṇa; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: द्विमाता होता विदथेषु सम्राळन्वग्रं चरति क्षेति बुध्नः ।प्र रण्यानि रण्यवाचो भरंते महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: dvi-mātā́ ǀ hótā ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ ánu ǀ ágram ǀ cárati ǀ kṣéti ǀ budhnáḥ ǀprá ǀ ráṇyāni ǀ raṇya-vā́caḥ ǀ bharante ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The child of two mothers, the invoker of the gods at sacrifices, the universal sovereign, proceeds thenceforward (in the sky); the root (of all), he abides (in the houses of the pious); the reciters of plural asant (words) offer him agreeable (praises); great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The child of two mothers, the invoker of the gods at sacrifices, the universal sovereign, proceeds thenceforward (in the sky); the root (of all), he abides (in the houses of the pious); the reciters of plural asant (words) offer him agreeable (praises); great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शूरस्येव युध्यतो अंतमस्य प्रतीचीनं ददृशे विश्वमायत् ।अंतर्मतिश्चरति निष्षिधं गोर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: śū́rasya-iva ǀ yúdhyataḥ ǀ antamásya ǀ pratīcī́nam ǀ dadṛśe ǀ víśvam ǀ ā-yát ǀantáḥ ǀ matíḥ ǀ carati ǀ niḥ-sídham ǀ góḥ ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: All (creatures) approaching too near his confines are beheld with their faces turned away as (an enemy) flies from a combatant; obvious (to all), he penetrates the water for its destruction; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: All (creatures) approaching too near his confines are beheld with their faces turned away as (an enemy) flies from a combatant; obvious (to all), he penetrates the water for its destruction; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि वेवेति पलितो दूत आस्वंतर्महांश्चरति रोचनेन ।वपूंषि बिभ्रदभि नो वि चष्टे महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ veveti ǀ palitáḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ āsu ǀ antáḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ carati ǀ rocanéna ǀvápūṃṣi ǀ bíbhrat ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: In those (plural nts) the aged messenger (of the gods) constantly abides; mighty, he presses with the radiant (sun) through the region of space; assuming various forms, he looks (complacently) upon us; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: In those (plural nts) the aged messenger (of the gods) constantly abides; mighty, he presses with the radiant (sun) through the region of space; assuming various forms, he looks (complacently) upon us; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विष्णुर्गोपाः परमं पाति पाथः प्रिया धामान्यमृता दधानः ।अग्निष्टा विश्वा भुवनानि वेद महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣṇuḥ ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ paramám ǀ pāti ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ priyā́ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ amṛ́tā ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ tā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ veda ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pervading and protecting (all), possessing grateful and immortal radiance, he preserves the supreme path (or the rains), for Agniknows all these worlds; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Pervading and protecting (all), possessing grateful and immortal radiance, he preserves the supreme path (or the rains), for Agniknows all these worlds; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नाना चक्राते यम्या वपूंषि तयोरन्यद्रोचते कृष्णमन्यत् ।श्यावी च यदरुषी च स्वसारौ महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́nā ǀ cakrāte íti ǀ yamyā́ ǀ vápūṃṣi ǀ táyoḥ ǀ anyát ǀ rócate ǀ kṛṣṇám ǀ anyát ǀśyā́vī ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ áruṣī ǀ ca ǀ svásārau ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The twin pair (day and night) adopt various forms; one of them shines brightly, the other is black; twin sisters are they, one black and the other white; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The twin pair (day and night) adopt various forms; one of them shines brightly, the other is black; twin sisters are they, one black and the other white; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: माता च यत्र दुहिता च धेनू सबर्दुघे धापयेते समीची ।ऋतस्य ते सदसीळे अंतर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: mātā́ ǀ ca ǀ yátra ǀ duhitā́ ǀ ca ǀ dhenū́ íti ǀ sabardúghe íti sabaḥ-dúghe ǀ dhāpáyete íti ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀṛtásya ǀ té íti ǀ sádasi ǀ īḷe ǀ antáḥ ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where the mother and daughter, two productive kine, unite, they nourish each other; I worship them both in (the firmament), the dwelling of the waters great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Where the mother and daughter, two productive kine, unite, they nourish each other; I worship them both in (the firmament), the dwelling of the waters great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा नि दधे धेनुरूधः ।ऋतस्य सा पयसापिन्वतेळा महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: anyásyāḥ ǀ vatsám ǀ rihatī́ ǀ mimāya ǀ káyā ǀ bhuvā́ ǀ ní ǀ dadhe ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ sā́ ǀ páyasā ǀ apinvata ǀ íḷā ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Licking the calf of the other, one of them lows aloud; the cow offers her udder for the one that is without mosture (the earth), and she (the earth) is refreshed by the milk of the rain; great and unequalles is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Licking the calf of the other, one of them lows aloud; the cow offers her udder for the one that is without mosture (the earth), and she (the earth) is refreshed by the milk of the rain; great and unequalles is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पद्या वस्ते पुरुरूपा वपूंष्यूर्ध्वा तस्थौ त्र्यविं रेरिहाणा ।ऋतस्य सद्म वि चरामि विद्वान्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: pádyā ǀ vaste ǀ puru-rū́pā ǀ vápūṃṣi ǀ ūrdhvā́ ǀ tasthau ǀ tri-ávim ǀ rérihāṇā ǀṛtásya ǀ sádma ǀ ví ǀ carāmi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The earth wears bodies of many forms; she abides on high cherishing her year and a half old (calf); knowing the abode of the truth (the sun), I offer worship; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The earth wears bodies of many forms; she abides on high cherishing her year and a half old (calf); knowing the abode of the truth (the sun), I offer worship; great and unequalled is the might of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पदे इव निहिते दस्मे अंतस्तयोरन्यद्गुह्यमाविरन्यत् ।सध्रीचीना पथ्या सा विषूची महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: padé ivéti padé-iva ǀ níhite íti ní-hite ǀ dasmé ǀ antáríti ǀ táyoḥ ǀ anyát ǀ gúhyam ǀ āvíḥ ǀ anyát ǀsadhrīcīnā́ ǀ pathyā́ ǀ sā́ ǀ víṣūcī ǀ mahát ǀ devā́nām ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
