verses.wilson_translation: Interrogated with respect, I declare the truth, that this (wealth is acquired),Jātavedas, by the praise of you; you rule over it, (over) all that (it may be), the wealth that is in heaven or on earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किं नो अस्य द्रविणं कद्ध रत्नं वि नो वोचो जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् ।गुहाध्वनः परमं यन्नो अस्य रेकु पदं न निदाना अगन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ dráviṇam ǀ kát ǀ ha ǀ rátnam ǀ ví ǀ naḥ ǀ vocaḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀgúhā ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ paramám ǀ yát ǀ naḥ ǀ asyá ǀ réku ǀ padám ǀ ná ǀ nidānā́ḥ ǀ áganma ǁ
verses.english_translation: What is the value of this (wealth) to us? what is its advantage? inform us,Jātavedas, for you know; (tell us) what is the best (course) for us on this secret path, so that we may follow unreproached the direct road.
verses.wilson_translation: What is the value of this (wealth) to us? what is its advantage? inform us,Jātavedas, for you know; (tell us) what is the best (course) for us on this secret path, so that we may follow unreproached the direct road.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: का मर्यादा वयुना कद्ध वाममच्छा गमेम रघवो न वाजं ।कदा नो देवीरमृतस्य पत्नीः सूरो वर्णेन ततनन्नुषासः ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ maryā́dā ǀ vayúnā ǀ kát ǀ ha ǀ vāmám ǀ áccha ǀ gamema ǀ raghávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǀkadā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ várṇena ǀ tatanan ǀ uṣásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wha tis the limit, what are the objects, which is the desirable (end) to which we rush like swift (chargers) to the battle? when for us will the divine dawns, the brides of the immortal (sun), overspread (the world) with light.
verses.wilson_translation: Wha tis the limit, what are the objects, which is the desirable (end) to which we rush like swift (chargers) to the battle? when for us will the divine dawns, the brides of the immortal (sun), overspread (the world) with light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनिरेण वचसा फल्ग्वेन प्रतीत्येन कृधुनातृपासः ।अधा ते अग्ने किमिहा वदंत्यनायुधास आसता सचंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: aniréṇa ǀ vácasā ǀ phalgvéna ǀ pratī́tyena ǀ kṛdhúnā ǀ atṛpā́saḥ ǀádha ǀ té ǀ agne ǀ kím ǀ ihá ǀ vadanti ǀ anāyudhā́saḥ ǀ ásatā ǀ sacantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Men are) not satisfied by unproductive, frivolous, inconclusive, scanty speech; then what,Agni, do they here say to you? devoid of the implements (of worship), let them suffer from distress.
verses.wilson_translation: (Men are) not satisfied by unproductive, frivolous, inconclusive, scanty speech; then what,Agni, do they here say to you? devoid of the implements (of worship), let them suffer from distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य श्रिये समिधानस्य वृष्णो वसोरनीकं दम आ रुरोच ।रुशद्वसानः सुदृशीकरूपः क्षितिर्न राया पुरुवारो अद्यौत् ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ śriyé ǀ sam-idhānásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ vásoḥ ǀ ánīkam ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ ruroca ǀrúśat ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ sudṛ́śīka-rūpaḥ ǀ kṣitíḥ ǀ ná ǀ rāyā́ ǀ puru-vā́raḥ ǀ adyaut ǁ
verses.english_translation: For the prosperity of this (instrumental tutor of the rite), the host (of the flames) of the kindled (Agni), the showerer (of benefits), the giver of dwellings, has blazed in the hall (of sacrifice); clothed in radiance, beautiful in semblance, and glorified by many, he shines like a man with opulence.
verses.wilson_translation: For the prosperity of this (instrumental tutor of the rite), the host (of the flames) of the kindled (Agni), the showerer (of benefits), the giver of dwellings, has blazed in the hall (of sacrifice); clothed in radiance, beautiful in semblance, and glorified by many, he shines like a man with opulence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PRIEST of our rite, stand up erect, O Agni, in the Gods’ service best of sacrificers,For over evei y thought thou art the Ruler: thou furtherest e’en the wisdom of the pious. He was set down mid men as Priest unerring, Agni, wise, welcome in our holy synods.Like Savitar he hath lifted up his splendour, and like a builder raised his smoke to heaven. The glowing ladle, filled with oil, is lifted; choosing Gods’ service to the right he circles.Eager he rises like the new-wrought pillar which, firmly set and fixed, anoints the victims. When sacred grass is strewn and Agni kindled, the Adhvaryu rises to, his task rejoicing.Agni the Priest, like one who tends the cattle, goes three times round, as from of old he wills it. Agni himself, the Priest, with measured motion, goes round, with sweet speech, cheerful, true to Order.His fulgent flames run forth like vigorous horses; all creatures are affrighted when he blazes. Beautiful and auspicious is thine aspect, O lovely Agni, terrible when spreading.Thy splendours are not covered by the darkness: detraction leaves no stain upon thy body. Naught hindered his production, Bounteous Giver: his Mother and his Sire were free to send him.Then as Friend benevolent, refulgent, Agni shone forth in human habitations. He, Agni, whom the twice-five sisters, dwelling together, in the homes of men engendered,Bright like a spear's tooth, wakened in the morning, with powerful mouth and like an axe well-sharpened. These thy Bay Coursers, Agni, dropping fatness, ruddy vigorous, speeding straightly forward,And red steeds, wonderful, of mighty muscle, are to this service of the Gods invited: These brightly-shining games of thine, O Agni, that move for ever restless, all-subduing,Like falcons hasting eagerly to the quarry, roar loudly like the army of the Maruts. To thee, O flaming God, hath prayer been offered. Let the priest laud thee: give to him who worships.Men have established Agni as Invoker, fain to adore the glory of the living.

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णो अध्वरस्य होतरग्ने तिष्ठ देवताता यजीयान् ।त्वं हि विश्वमभ्यसि मन्म प्र वेधसश्चित्तिरसि मनीषां ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ adhvarasya ǀ hotaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ devá-tātā ǀ yájīyān ǀtvám ǀ hí ǀ víśvam ǀ abhí ǀ ási ǀ mánma ǀ prá ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀ cit ǀ tirasi ǀ manīṣā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, ministrant of the sacrifice, do you who are entitled to worship, be above usin this offering to the gods; for you prevail over all that is desirable; you inspire the praise of the worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, ministrant of the sacrifice, do you who are entitled to worship, be above usin this offering to the gods; for you prevail over all that is desirable; you inspire the praise of the worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अमूरो होता न्यसादि विक्ष्वग्निर्मंद्रो विदथेषु प्रचेताः ।ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सवितेवाश्रेन्मेतेव धूमं स्तभायदुप द्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: ámūraḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ asādi ǀ vikṣú ǀ agníḥ ǀ mandráḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǀūrdhvám ǀ bhānúm ǀ savitā́-iva ǀ aśret ǀ métā-iva ǀ dhūmám ǀ stabhāyat ǀ úpa ǀ dyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: The unperplexed, the sagacious, exhilarating Agni, the ministrant priest, has been plural ced among men for (the celebration of) sacrifices; like the sun, he spreads light above, and props the smoke above the sky like a pillar.
verses.wilson_translation: The unperplexed, the sagacious, exhilarating Agni, the ministrant priest, has been plural ced among men for (the celebration of) sacrifices; like the sun, he spreads light above, and props the smoke above the sky like a pillar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यता सुजूर्णी रातिनी घृताची प्रदक्षिणिद्देवतातिमुराणः ।उदु स्वरुर्नवजा नाक्रः पश्वो अनक्ति सुधितः सुमेकः ॥
verses.transliteration: yatā́ ǀ su-jūrṇíḥ ǀ rātínī ǀ ghṛtā́cī ǀ pra-dakṣiṇít ǀ devá-tātim ǀ urāṇáḥ ǀút ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sváruḥ ǀ nava-jā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ akráḥ ǀ paśváḥ ǀ anakti ǀ sú-dhitaḥ ǀ su-mékaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ladle filled (with butter) is prepared; prompt (in act), opulent (with the oblation), the multiplying (priest), conducting (the worship) of the gods, circumambulates (the fire); the newly-trimmedpostis set up, the impending shining axe falls upon the victims.
verses.wilson_translation: The ladle filled (with butter) is prepared; prompt (in act), opulent (with the oblation), the multiplying (priest), conducting (the worship) of the gods, circumambulates (the fire); the newly-trimmedpostis set up, the impending shining axe falls upon the victims.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि समिधाने अग्ना ऊर्ध्वो अध्वर्युर्जुजुषाणो अस्थात् ।पर्यग्निः पशुपा न होता त्रिविष्ट्येति प्रदिव उराणः ॥
verses.transliteration: stīrṇé ǀ barhíṣi ǀ sam-idhāné ǀ agnáu ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ adhvaryúḥ ǀ jujuṣāṇáḥ ǀ asthāt ǀpári ǀ agníḥ ǀ paśu-pā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǀ tri-viṣṭí ǀ eti ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ urāṇáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the sacred grass is strewn and the fire is kindled, the Adhvaryurises, propitiating (the gods), and Agni, the offerer of the oblation, ancient and multiplying (the offering), thrice circumambulates (the victim) like a keeper of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: When the sacred grass is strewn and the fire is kindled, the Adhvaryurises, propitiating (the gods), and Agni, the offerer of the oblation, ancient and multiplying (the offering), thrice circumambulates (the victim) like a keeper of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि त्मना मितद्रुरेति होताग्निर्मंद्रो मधुवचा ऋतावा ।द्रवंत्यस्य वाजिनो न शोका भयंते विश्वा भुवना यदभ्राट् ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ tmánā ǀ mitá-druḥ ǀ eti ǀ hótā ǀ agníḥ ǀ mandráḥ ǀ mádhu-vacāḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀdrávanti ǀ asya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śókāḥ ǀ bháyante ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ yát ǀ ábhrāṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the sacrificer, the exhilarator, the sweet-spoken, the object of sacrifice, moving measuredly, circumambulates (the victim) of his own (accord); the bright (rays) of him (fed) with (sacrificial) food, spread around; all the regions are alarmed when he blazes.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the sacrificer, the exhilarator, the sweet-spoken, the object of sacrifice, moving measuredly, circumambulates (the victim) of his own (accord); the bright (rays) of him (fed) with (sacrificial) food, spread around; all the regions are alarmed when he blazes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रा ते अग्ने स्वनीक संदृग्घोरस्य सतो विषुणस्य चारुः ।न यत्ते शोचिस्तमसा वरंत न ध्वस्मानस्तन्वी रेप आ धुः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ su-anīka ǀ sam-dṛ́k ǀ ghorásya ǀ satáḥ ǀ víṣuṇasya ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀná ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ śocíḥ ǀ támasā ǀ váranta ǀ ná ǀ dhvasmā́naḥ ǀ tanví ǀ répaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dhuríti dhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bright-shining,Agni, beautiful and auspicious is the semblance of you who are terrible and wide-spreading, for (the nights) hide not your splendour with darkness, nor do the malignant (spirits) inflict any injury on your person n.
verses.wilson_translation: Bright-shining,Agni, beautiful and auspicious is the semblance of you who are terrible and wide-spreading, for (the nights) hide not your splendour with darkness, nor do the malignant (spirits) inflict any injury on your person n.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्य सातुर्जनितोरवारि न मातरापितरा नू चिदिष्टौ ।अधा मित्रो न सुधितः पावकोऽग्निर्दीदाय मानुषीषु विक्षु ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ sā́tuḥ ǀ jánitoḥ ǀ ávāri ǀ ná ǀ mātárāpitárā ǀ nú ǀ cit ǀ iṣṭáu ǀádha ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ sú-dhitaḥ ǀ pāvakáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ dīdāya ǀ mā́nuṣīṣu ǀ vikṣú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of whom, progenitor (of mankind), the benevolence is never checked; whose parents need not urge him to exertion; so that the well-satisfied, purifying Agnishines like a friend among men, the descendants of Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom, progenitor (of mankind), the benevolence is never checked; whose parents need not urge him to exertion; so that the well-satisfied, purifying Agnishines like a friend among men, the descendants of Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: द्विर्यं पंच जीजनन्त्संवसानाः स्वसारो अग्निं मानुषीषु विक्षु ।उषर्बुधमथर्यो न दंतं शुक्रं स्वासं परशुं न तिग्मं ॥
verses.transliteration: dvíḥ ǀ yám ǀ páñca ǀ jī́janan ǀ sam-vásānāḥ ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ agním ǀ mā́nuṣīṣu ǀ vikṣú ǀuṣaḥ-búdham ǀ atharyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dántam ǀ śukrám ǀ su-ā́sam ǀ paraśúm ǀ ná ǀ tigmám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, whom the twice five sisters dwelling among men, the descendants of Manu, have engendered, like feminine les, (awaking) him at dawn, feeding on oblations, brilliant of goodly aspect, and shharp as an axe.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, whom the twice five sisters dwelling among men, the descendants of Manu, have engendered, like feminine les, (awaking) him at dawn, feeding on oblations, brilliant of goodly aspect, and shharp as an axe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव त्ये अग्ने हरितो घृतस्ना रोहितास ऋज्वंचः स्वंचः ।अरुषासो वृषण ऋजुमुष्का आ देवतातिमह्वंत दस्माः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tyé ǀ agne ǀ harítaḥ ǀ ghṛta-snā́ḥ ǀ róhitāsaḥ ǀ ṛju-áñcaḥ ǀ su-áñcaḥ ǀaruṣā́saḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ ṛju-muṣkā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ devá-tātim ǀ ahvanta ǀ dasmā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your horses,Agni, breathing foam, red-coloured, straight-going well-plural ced, bright-shining, vigorous, well-membered, and of graceful form, are summoned to the worthy of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Your horses,Agni, breathing foam, red-coloured, straight-going well-plural ced, bright-shining, vigorous, well-membered, and of graceful form, are summoned to the worthy of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये ह त्ये ते सहमाना अयासस्त्वेषासो अग्ने अर्चयश्चरंति ।श्येनासो न दुवसनासो अर्थं तुविष्वणसो मारुतं न शर्धः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ha ǀ tyé ǀ te ǀ sáhamānāḥ ǀ ayā́saḥ ǀ tveṣā́saḥ ǀ agne ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ cáranti ǀśyenā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ duvasanā́saḥ ǀ ártham ǀ tuvi-svanásaḥ ǀ mā́rutam ǀ ná ǀ śárdhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those, your rays,Agni, triumphant, wide-spreading, radiant, adorable, go like hawk-faced horses (to their  goal), loud-sounding like the company of the Maruts.
verses.wilson_translation: Those, your rays,Agni, triumphant, wide-spreading, radiant, adorable, go like hawk-faced horses (to their  goal), loud-sounding like the company of the Maruts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अकारि ब्रह्म समिधान तुभ्यं शंसात्युक्थं यजते व्यू धाः ।होतारमग्निं मनुषो नि षेदुर्नमस्यंत उशिजः शंसमायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: ákāri ǀ bráhma ǀ sam-idhāna ǀ túbhyam ǀ śáṃsāti ǀ ukthám ǀ yájate ǀ ví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dhāḥ ǀhótāram ǀ agním ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ní ǀ seduḥ ǀ namasyántaḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ śáṃsam ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well-kindled Agni, for you the prayer has been composed; may (the priest) propitiate (you) by (his) praise; the (sacrificer) offers worship; bestow upon us manifold (wealth); desiring (riches), men sit down adoring Agni, the invoker of the gods, the glorifier of mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: Well-kindled Agni, for you the prayer has been composed; may (the priest) propitiate (you) by (his) praise; the (sacrificer) offers worship; bestow upon us manifold (wealth); desiring (riches), men sit down adoring Agni, the invoker of the gods, the glorifier of mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HERE by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites:Whom Apnavāna, and the Bhṛgus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading from home to home. When shall thy glory as a God, Agni, be suddenly shown forth.For mortal men have held thee fast, adorable in all their homes, Seeing thee faithful to the Law, most sapient, like the starry heaven,Illumining with cheerful ray each solemn rite in every house. Vivasvān's envoy living men have taken as their ensign, swift,The ruler over all mankind, moving like Bhṛgu in each home. Him the intelligent have they placed duly as Invoking Priest,Welcome, with sanctifying flame, best worshipper, with sevenfold might; In his Eternal Mothers, in the wood, concealed and unapproached,Kept secret though his flames are bright seeking on all sides, quickly found. That as food spreads forth in this earthly udder, Gods may rejoice them in the home of Order,Great Agni, served with reverence and oblation, flies ever to the sacrifice, the Faithful. Bird of each rite, skilled in an envoy's duties, knowing both worlds and that which lies between them,Thou goest from of old a willing Herald, knowing full well heaven's innermost recesses. Bright God, thy path is black: light is before thee: thy moving splendour is the chief of wonders.When she, yet unimpregnate, hath conceived thee, even when newly born thou art an envoy. Yet newly born, his vigour is apparent when the wind blows upon his fiery splendour,His sharpened tongue he layeth on the brushwood, and with his teeth e’en solid food consumeth. When he hath borne off food with swift flame swiftly, strong Agni makes himself a speedy envoy,Follows the rustling of the wind, consuming, and courser-like, speeds, drives the swift horse onward.

verses.sanskrit: अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यः ।यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ ihá ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ dhāyi ǀ dhātṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ hótā ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀyám ǀ ápnavānaḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ vi-rurucúḥ ǀ váneṣu ǀ citrám ǀ vi-bhvám ǀ viśé-viśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: This invoker of the gods and minister of frequent worship, who is to be glorified at sacrifices, has been plural ced first (of the gods) by the performers of the rite; the Agniwhom Apnavāna and other Bhṛguslighted in the woods for the sake of all men, marvellous (in his acts), and soverign (over all).
verses.wilson_translation: This invoker of the gods and minister of frequent worship, who is to be glorified at sacrifices, has been plural ced first (of the gods) by the performers of the rite; the Agniwhom Apnavāna and other Bhṛguslighted in the woods for the sake of all men, marvellous (in his acts), and soverign (over all).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने कदा त आनुषग्भुवद्देवस्य चेतनं ।अधा हि त्वा जगृभ्रिरे मर्तासो विक्ष्वीड्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ kadā́ ǀ te ǀ ānuṣák ǀ bhúvat ǀ devásya ǀ cétanam ǀádha ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ jagṛbhriré ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ ī́ḍyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When,Agni, is the light of you, bright-shining, to be manifested; for therefore have mortals accepted you as to be worshipped among mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Agni, is the light of you, bright-shining, to be manifested; for therefore have mortals accepted you as to be worshipped among mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतावानं विचेतसं पश्यंतो द्यामिव स्तृभिः ।विश्वेषामध्वराणां हस्कर्तारं दमेदमे ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtá-vānam ǀ ví-cetasam ǀ páśyantaḥ ǀ dyā́m-iva ǀ stṛ́-bhiḥ ǀvíśveṣām ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǀ haskartā́ram ǀ dáme-dame ǁ
verses.english_translation: Contemplating you in every dwelling, truthful intelligent, (brilliant with sparks) like the sky with stars, the perfecter of all sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: Contemplating you in every dwelling, truthful intelligent, (brilliant with sparks) like the sky with stars, the perfecter of all sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आशुं दूतं विवस्वतो विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभि ।आ जभ्रुः केतुमायवो भृगवाणं विशेविशे ॥
verses.transliteration: āśúm ǀ dūtám ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ carṣaṇī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀā́ ǀ jabhruḥ ǀ ketúm ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavāṇam ǀ viśé-viśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men have brought, for the sake of all people, the swift messenger of the worshipper (to the gods), who (rules) over all mankind, the manifester, the resplendent.
verses.wilson_translation: Men have brought, for the sake of all people, the swift messenger of the worshipper (to the gods), who (rules) over all mankind, the manifester, the resplendent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमीं होतारमानुषक्चिकित्वांसं नि षेदिरे ।रण्वं पावकशोचिषं यजिष्ठं सप्त धामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ īm ǀ hótāram ǀ ānuṣák ǀ cikitvā́ṃsam ǀ ní ǀ sedire ǀraṇvám ǀ pāvaká-śociṣam ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ saptá ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They (the worshippers) have seated him in his due order, the invoker (of the gods), the intelligent, the agreeable, the purifyingly-radiant, the performer of frequent sacrifice, (brilliant) with seven flames.
verses.wilson_translation: They (the worshippers) have seated him in his due order, the invoker (of the gods), the intelligent, the agreeable, the purifyingly-radiant, the performer of frequent sacrifice, (brilliant) with seven flames.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं शश्वतीषु मातृषु वन आ वीतं अश्रितं ।चित्रं संतं गुहा हितं सुवेदं कूचिदर्थिनं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ śáśvatīṣu ǀ mātṛ́ṣu ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ vītám ǀ áśritam ǀcitrám ǀ sántam ǀ gúhā ǀ hitám ǀ su-védam ǀ kūcit-arthínam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, abiding in the maternal (waters) and in the woods, loved, yet unapproached, wonderful, hidden in a cave, endowed with knowledge, seeking (oblations) from any quarter.
verses.wilson_translation: Him, abiding in the maternal (waters) and in the woods, loved, yet unapproached, wonderful, hidden in a cave, endowed with knowledge, seeking (oblations) from any quarter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ससस्य यद्वियुता सस्मिन्नूधन्नृतस्य धामन्रणयंत देवाः ।महाँ अग्निर्नमसा रातहव्यो वेरध्वराय सदमिदृतावा ॥
verses.transliteration: sasásya ǀ yát ǀ ví-yutā ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhā́man ǀ raṇáyanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀmahā́n ǀ agníḥ ǀ námasā ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ véḥ ǀ adhvarā́ya ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ ṛtá-vā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom, when they desist from slumber, the devout propitiate in the abode of water at every sacrifice; the mighty Agni, to whom oblations are to be offered with reverence, who truthful always, accepts the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Whom, when they desist from slumber, the devout propitiate in the abode of water at every sacrifice; the mighty Agni, to whom oblations are to be offered with reverence, who truthful always, accepts the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वेरध्वरस्य दूत्यानि विद्वानुभे अंता रोदसी संचिकित्वान् ।दूत ईयसे प्रदिव उराणो विदुष्टरो दिव आरोधनानि ॥
verses.transliteration: véḥ ǀ adhvarásya ǀ dūtyā́ni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ubhé íti ǀ antáríti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ sam-cikitvā́n ǀdūtáḥ ǀ īyase ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ urāṇáḥ ǀ vidúḥ-taraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā-ródhanāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: You who are all-knowing understand the functions of a messenger (of the gods) at the sacrifice; well informed of both heaven and earth and the intermediate (firmament), and a most intelligent, ancient, and amplifying envoy, you go up the ascents of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: You who are all-knowing understand the functions of a messenger (of the gods) at the sacrifice; well informed of both heaven and earth and the intermediate (firmament), and a most intelligent, ancient, and amplifying envoy, you go up the ascents of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णं त एम रुशतः पुरो भाश्चरिष्ण्वर्चिर्वपुषामिदेकं ।यदप्रवीता दधते ह गर्भं सद्यश्चिज्जातो भवसीदु दूतः ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇám ǀ te ǀ éma ǀ rúśataḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ bhā́ḥ ǀ cariṣṇú ǀ arcíḥ ǀ vápuṣām ǀ ít ǀ ékam ǀyát ǀ ápra-vītā ǀ dádhate ǀ ha ǀ gárbham ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ cit ǀ jātáḥ ǀ bhávasi ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dūtáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dark is the path of you wo are bright; the light is before you; your moving radiance is the chief of (all luminous) bodies; when the present (worshippers) take up the germ (in the sticks of attrition) you are speedily genitive rated, and become indeed the messenger (of the sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: Dark is the path of you wo are bright; the light is before you; your moving radiance is the chief of (all luminous) bodies; when the present (worshippers) take up the germ (in the sticks of attrition) you are speedily genitive rated, and become indeed the messenger (of the sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सद्यो जातस्य ददृशानमोजो यदस्य वातो अनुवाति शोचिः ।वृणक्ति तिग्मामतसेषु जिह्वां स्थिरा चिदन्ना दयते वि जंभैः ॥
verses.transliteration: sadyáḥ ǀ jātásya ǀ dádṛśānam ǀ ójaḥ ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ anu-vā́ti ǀ śocíḥ ǀvṛṇákti ǀ tigmā́m ǀ ataséṣu ǀ jihvā́m ǀ sthirā́ ǀ cit ǀ ánnā ǀ dayate ǀ ví ǀ jámbhaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The light of the speedily-genitive rated is visible, and when the win fans the flame, he (Agni) spreads his blazing tongue among the trees, and with his (glowing) teeth consumes the standing (fuel, his) food.
verses.wilson_translation: The light of the speedily-genitive rated is visible, and when the win fans the flame, he (Agni) spreads his blazing tongue among the trees, and with his (glowing) teeth consumes the standing (fuel, his) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तृषु यदन्ना तृषुणा ववक्ष तृषुं दूतं कृणुते यह्वो अग्निः ।वातस्य मेळिं सचते निजूर्वन्नाशुं न वाजयते हिन्वे अर्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛṣú ǀ yát ǀ ánnā ǀ tṛṣúṇā ǀ vavákṣa ǀ tṛ���úm ǀ dūtám ǀ kṛṇute ǀ yahváḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀvā́tasya ǀ meḷím ǀ sacate ǀ ni-jū́rvan ǀ āśúm ǀ ná ǀ vājayate ǀ hinvé ǀ árvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When quickly, with rapid (radiance), he has carried off his food, the mighty Agnimakes (himself) the fleet messenger (of the worshipper); consuming (the fuel), he allies himself with the force of the wind, and as (a horseman) urges his fast steed, so the rapid going Agni, invigorates and urges (his flames).
verses.wilson_translation: When quickly, with rapid (radiance), he has carried off his food, the mighty Agnimakes (himself) the fleet messenger (of the worshipper); consuming (the fuel), he allies himself with the force of the wind, and as (a horseman) urges his fast steed, so the rapid going Agni, invigorates and urges (his flames).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YOUR envoy who possesses all, Immortal, bearer of your gifts,Best worshipper, I woo with song. He, Mighty, knows the gift of wealth, he knows the deep recess of heaven:He shall bring hitherward the Gods. He knows, a God himself, to guide Gods to the righteous in his home:He gives e’en treasures that we love. He is the Herald: well-informed, he doth his errand to and fro,Knowing the deep recess of heaven. May we be they who gratify Agni with sacrificial gifts,Who cherish and enkindle him. Illustrious for wealth are they, and hero deeds, victorious,Who have served Agni reverently. So unto us, day after day, may riches craved by many come,And power and might spring up for us. That holy Singer in his strength shoots forth his arrows swifter thanThe swift shafts of the tribes of men.

verses.sanskrit: दूतं वो विश्ववेदसं हव्यवाहममर्त्यं ।यजिष्ठमृंजसे गिरा ॥
verses.transliteration: dūtám ǀ vaḥ ǀ viśvá-vedasam ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ ámartyam ǀyájiṣṭham ǀ ṛñjase ǀ girā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I propitiate you with praise, the messenger (of the gods), the omniscient, the bearer of oblations, the immortal, the chief sacrificer.
verses.wilson_translation: I propitiate you with praise, the messenger (of the gods), the omniscient, the bearer of oblations, the immortal, the chief sacrificer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि वेदा वसुधितिं महाँ आरोधनं दिवः ।स देवाँ एह वक्षति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ véda ǀ vásu-dhitim ǀ mahā́n ǀ ā-ródhanam ǀ diváḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ vakṣati ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mighty one knows how to bestow the (desired) wealth (upon the worshipper); he knows the ascents of heaven; may he bring the gods hither.
verses.wilson_translation: The mighty one knows how to bestow the (desired) wealth (upon the worshipper); he knows the ascents of heaven; may he bring the gods hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स वेद देव आनमं देवाँ ऋतायते दमे ।दाति प्रियाणि चिद्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ veda ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā-námam ǀ devā́n ǀ ṛta-yaté ǀ dáme ǀdā́ti ǀ priyā́ṇi ǀ cit ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, the divine (Agni), knows how the gods are to be reverenced; to the sincere (worshipper) in his dwelling he gives wealth that is desired.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the divine (Agni), knows how the gods are to be reverenced; to the sincere (worshipper) in his dwelling he gives wealth that is desired.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स होता सेदु दूत्यं चिकित्वाँ अंतरीयते ।विद्वाँ आरोधनं दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dūtyám ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ antáḥ ǀ īyate ǀvidvā́n ǀ ā-ródhanam ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is the invoker (of the gods), comprehending the deity of (their) messenger; and, knowing the ascent of the sky, he travels between earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: He is the invoker (of the gods), comprehending the deity of (their) messenger; and, knowing the ascent of the sky, he travels between earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते स्याम ये अग्नये ददाशुर्हव्यदातिभिः ।य ईं पुष्यंत इंधते ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ syāma ǀ yé ǀ agnáye ǀ dadāśúḥ ǀ havyádāti-bhiḥ ǀyé ǀ īm ǀ púṣyantaḥ ǀ indhaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we be they who propitiate Agniwith gifts of oblations, and who, cherishing him, feed him with fuel.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be they who propitiate Agniwith gifts of oblations, and who, cherishing him, feed him with fuel.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते राया ते सुवीर्यैः ससवांसो वि शृण्विरे ।ये अग्ना दधिरे दुवः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ rāyā́ ǀ té ǀ su-vī́ryaiḥ ǀ sasa-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ ví ǀ śṛṇvire ǀyé ǀ agnā́ ǀ dadhiré ǀ dúvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They are renowned for riches and for progeny, who, venerating Agni, offer him oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: They are renowned for riches and for progeny, who, venerating Agni, offer him oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे रायो दिवेदिवे सं चरंतु पुरुस्पृहः ।अस्मे वाजास ईरतां ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ sám ǀ carantu ǀ puru-spṛ́haḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ vā́jāsaḥ ǀ īratām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many riches, envied by many, devolve upon us day by day, and (abundant) food await us.
verses.wilson_translation: Many riches, envied by many, devolve upon us day by day, and (abundant) food await us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स विप्रश्चर्षणीनां शवसा मानुषाणां ।अति क्षिप्रेव विध्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ śávasā ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǀáti ǀ kṣiprā́-iva ǀ vidhyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the wise Agnientirely obviate, by his powe,r the removable (ills) of men the descendants of Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: May the wise Agnientirely obviate, by his powe,r the removable (ills) of men the descendants of Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN IX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, show favour: great art thou who to this pious man art come,To seat thee on the sacred grass. May he the Immortal, Helper, bard to be deceived among mankind,Become the messenger of all. Around the altar is he led, welcome Chief Priest at solemn rites,Or as the Potar sits him down. Agni in fire at sacrifice, and in the house as Lord thereof,And as a Brahman takes his seat. Thou comest as the guide of folk who celebrate a sacrifice,And to oblations brought by men. Thou servest as his messenger whose sacrifice thou lovest well,To bear the mortal's gifts to heaven. Accept our solemn rite; be pleased, Aṅgiras, with our sacrifice:Give ear and listen to our call. May thine inviolable car, wherewith thou guardest those who give,Come near to us from every side.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने मृळ महाँ असि य ईमा देवयुं जनं ।इयेथ बर्हिरासदं ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ mṛḷá ǀ mahā́n ǀ asi ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ ā́ ǀ deva-yúm ǀ jánam ǀiyétha ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā-sádam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, make us happy, for you are mighty, (you) who come to this devout man to sit down on the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, make us happy, for you are mighty, (you) who come to this devout man to sit down on the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स मानुषीषु दूळभो विक्षु प्रावीरमर्त्यः ।दूतो विश्वेषां भुवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ mā́nuṣīṣu ǀ duḥ-dábhaḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ pra-avī́ḥ ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀdūtáḥ ǀ víśveṣām ǀ bhuvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that Agni, who is difficult to overcome, who is immortal, who is pre-eminent among men the descendants of Manu, becomes the messenger of all the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: May that Agni, who is difficult to overcome, who is immortal, who is pre-eminent among men the descendants of Manu, becomes the messenger of all the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स सद्म परि णीयते होता मंद्रो दिविष्टिषु ।उत पोता नि षीदति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ sádma ǀ pári ǀ nīyate ǀ hótā ǀ mandráḥ ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀutá ǀ pótā ǀ ní ǀ sīdati ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is conveyed into the sacrificial hall as the Hotāto be adored at sacrifices, or as the Potāhe sits down (on the sacred grass).
verses.wilson_translation: He is conveyed into the sacrificial hall as the Hotāto be adored at sacrifices, or as the Potāhe sits down (on the sacred grass).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत ग्ना अग्निरध्वर उतो गृहपतिर्दमे ।उत ब्रह्मा नि षीदति ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ utó íti ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ dáme ǀutá ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ní ǀ sīdati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agnimay be the officiating priest at the sacrifice, or the master of the house in the sacrificial chamber, or he sits down as the Brahman.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnimay be the officiating priest at the sacrifice, or the master of the house in the sacrificial chamber, or he sits down as the Brahman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वेषि ह्यध्वरीयतामुपवक्ता जनानां ।हव्या च मानुषाणां ॥
verses.transliteration: véṣi ǀ hí ǀ adhvari-yatā́m ǀ upa-vaktā́ ǀ jánānām ǀhavyā́ ǀ ca ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: You, who are the director (of the ceremonial), accept the oblations of devoutly-worshipping men the descendants of Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: You, who are the director (of the ceremonial), accept the oblations of devoutly-worshipping men the descendants of Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वेषीद्वस्य दूत्यं यस्य जुजोषो अध्वरं ।हव्यं मर्तस्य वोळ्हवे ॥
verses.transliteration: véṣi ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ asya ǀ dūtyám ǀ yásya ǀ jújoṣaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀhavyám ǀ mártasya ǀ vóḷhave ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are willing (to fulfil) the office of messenger for the mortal whose oblations at the sacrifice you are plural ased to convey.
verses.wilson_translation: You are willing (to fulfil) the office of messenger for the mortal whose oblations at the sacrifice you are plural ased to convey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं जोष्यध्वरमस्माकं यज्ञमंगिरः ।अस्माकं शृणुधी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ joṣi ǀ adhvarám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yajñám ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ śṛṇudhi ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be plural ased by our sacrifice; (be plural ased)Aṅgiras, by our offering hear our invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Be plural ased by our sacrifice; (be plural ased)Aṅgiras, by our offering hear our invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि ते दूळभो रथोऽस्माँ अश्नोतु विश्वतः ।येन रक्षसि दाशुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ te ǀ duḥ-dábhaḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ aśnotu ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀyéna ǀ rákṣasi ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your inviolable car, whereby you defend the donors of oblations, be everywhere around us.
verses.wilson_translation: May your inviolable car, whereby you defend the donors of oblations, be everywhere around us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN X. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ८ वामदेवो गौतमः। अग्निः। पादपंक्तिः, ४, ६, ७, उष्णिग्वा, ५ महापदपंक्तिः, ८ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . This day with praises, Agni, we bring thee that which thou lovest.Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions. For thou hast ever been the Car-driver, Agni, of nobleStrength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment. Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight,O Agni, well disposed, with all thine aspects. Now may we serve thee singing these lauds this day to thee, Agni.Loud as the voice of Heaven thy blasts are roaring. Just at this time of the day and the night thy look is the sweetest:It shineth near us even as gold for glory. Spotless thy body, brilliant as gold, like clarified butter:This gleams like gold on thee, O Self. dependent. All hate and mischief, yea, if committed, Agni, thou turnest,Holy One, from the man who rightly worships. Agni, with you Gods, prosperous be our friendships and kinships.Be this our bond here by this place, thine altar.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने तमद्याश्वं न स्तोमैः क्रतुं न भद्रं हृदिस्पृशं ।ऋध्यामा त ओहैः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ tám ǀ adyá ǀ áśvam ǀ ná ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ krátum ǀ ná ǀ bhadrám ǀ hṛdi-spṛ́śam ǀṛdhyā́ma ǀ te ǀ óhaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We celebrate you today,Agni, who are like a horse (in conveying our burden) with your praises, conveying (our wishes to the gods), and (who are) like a benefactor, propitious and affectionate.
verses.wilson_translation: We celebrate you today,Agni, who are like a horse (in conveying our burden) with your praises, conveying (our wishes to the gods), and (who are) like a benefactor, propitious and affectionate.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अधा ह्यग्ने क्रतोर्भद्रस्य दक्षस्य साधोः ।रथीर्ऋतस्य बृहतो बभूथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ krátoḥ ǀ bhadrásya ǀ dákṣasya ǀ sādhóḥ ǀrathī́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ babhū́tha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be now the conveyer,Agni, of our auspicious, powerful, efficacious, truthful, and great sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Be now the conveyer,Agni, of our auspicious, powerful, efficacious, truthful, and great sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एभिर्नो अर्कैर्भवा नो अर्वाङ् स्वर्ण ज्योतिः ।अग्ने विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः ॥
verses.transliteration: ebhíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ bháva ǀ naḥ ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyótiḥ ǀágne ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ánīkaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who like the sun are light, propitiated by these our hymns, come to our presence with all your hosts (of radiance).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who like the sun are light, propitiated by these our hymns, come to our presence with all your hosts (of radiance).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आभिष्टे अद्य गीर्भिर्गृणंतोऽग्ने दाशेम ।प्र ते दिवो न स्तनयंति शुष्माः ॥
verses.transliteration: ābhíḥ ǀ te ǀ adyá ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ dā́śema ǀprá ǀ te ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ stanayanti ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorifying you,Agni, today, with these our praises, may we offer you (oblations); your (flames), bright as those of the sun, roar aloud.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorifying you,Agni, today, with these our praises, may we offer you (oblations); your (flames), bright as those of the sun, roar aloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव स्वादिष्ठाग्ने संदृष्टिरिदा चिदह्न इदा चिदक्तोः ।श्रिये रुक्मो न रोचत उपाके ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ svā́diṣṭhā ǀ ágne ǀ sám-dṛṣṭiḥ ǀ idā́ ǀ cit ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ idā́ ǀ cit ǀ aktóḥ ǀśriyé ǀ rukmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ rocate ǀ upāké ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your lovely radiance,Agni, whether by day or by night, shines upon (all objects) like an ornament (to give them) beauty.
verses.wilson_translation: Your lovely radiance,Agni, whether by day or by night, shines upon (all objects) like an ornament (to give them) beauty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: घृतं न पूतं तनूररेपाः शुचि हिरण्यं ।तत्ते रुक्मो न रोचत स्वधावः ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ pūtám ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ arepā́ḥ ǀ śúci ǀ híraṇyam ǀtát ǀ te ǀ rukmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ rocata ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Giver of sustenance, (Agni), your favour is free from fault, like clarified butter; your pure and golden lustre shines like an ornament.
verses.wilson_translation: Giver of sustenance, (Agni), your favour is free from fault, like clarified butter; your pure and golden lustre shines like an ornament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृतं चिद्धि ष्मा सनेमि द्वेषोऽग्न इनोषि मर्तात् ।इत्था यजमानादृतावः ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛtám ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ sánemi ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ágne ǀ inóṣi ǀ mártāt ǀitthā́ ǀ yájamānāt ǀ ṛta-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Truthful,Agni, verily you remove from the mortal who instrumental tutes (your) worship, whatever sin has been committed (by him) of old.
verses.wilson_translation: Truthful,Agni, verily you remove from the mortal who instrumental tutes (your) worship, whatever sin has been committed (by him) of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शिवा नः सख्या संतु भ्रात्राग्ने देवेषु युष्मे ।सा नो नाभिः सदने सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥
verses.transliteration: śivā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ sántu ǀ bhrātrā́ ǀ ágne ǀ devéṣu ǀ yuṣmé íti ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ sádane ǀ sásmin ǀ ū́dhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: May our friendly and fraternal attentions to your deities prove fortunate; for such (attentions shown) in every sacrifice (form) our security in the sphere (of the gods).
verses.wilson_translation: May our friendly and fraternal attentions to your deities prove fortunate; for such (attentions shown) in every sacrifice (form) our security in the sphere (of the gods).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THY blessed majesty, victorious Agni, shines brightly in the neighbourhood of Sūrya.Splendid to see, it shows even at nighttime, and food is fair to look on in thy beauty. Agni, disclose his thought for him who singeth, the well, Strong God! while thou art praised with fervour.Vouchsafe to us that powerful hymn, O Mighty, which, Radiant One! with all the Gods thou lovest. From thee, O Agni, springs poetic wisdom, from thee come thoughts and hymns of praise that prosper;From thee flows wealth, with heroes to adorn it, to the true-hearted man who gives oblation. From thee the hero springs who wins the booty, bringer of help, mighty, of real courage.From thee comes wealth, sent by the Gods, bliss-giving; Agni, from thee the fleet impetuous charger. Immortal Agni, thee whose voice is pleasant, as first in rank, as God, religious mortalsInvite with hymns; thee who removest hatred, Friend of the Home, the household's Lord, unerring. Far from us thou removest want and sorrow, far from us all ill-will when thou protectest.Son of Strength, Agni, blest is he at evening, whom thou as God attendest for his welfare.

verses.sanskrit: भद्रं ते अग्ने स���सिन्ननीकमुपाक आ रोचते सूर्यस्य ।रुशद्दृशे ददृशे नक्तया चिदरूक्षितं दृश आ रूपे अन्नं ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ sahasin ǀ ánīkam ǀ upāké ǀ ā́ ǀ rocate ǀ sū́ryasya ǀrúśat ǀ dṛśé ǀ dadṛśe ǀ nakta-yā́ ǀ cit ǀ árūkṣitam ǀ dṛśé ǀ ā́ ǀ rūpé ǀ ánnam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Powerful Agni, your auspicious radiance shines upon the proximity of the sun (by day); your bright and visible (lustre) is conspicuous by night, as the bland and plural asing food (of sacrifice, the oblation) becomes manifest in your form.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Agni, your auspicious radiance shines upon the proximity of the sun (by day); your bright and visible (lustre) is conspicuous by night, as the bland and plural asing food (of sacrifice, the oblation) becomes manifest in your form.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि षाह्यग्ने गृणते मनीषां खं वेपसा तुविजात स्तवानः ।विश्वेभिर्यद्वावनः शुक्र देवैस्तन्नो रास्व सुमहो भूरि मन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sāhi ǀ agne ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ khám ǀ vépasā ǀ tuvi-jāta ǀ stávānaḥ ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ yát ǀ vavánaḥ ǀ śukra ǀ deváiḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ rāsva ǀ su-mahaḥ ǀ bhū́ri ǀ mánma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who are engendered repeatedly, and glorified by sacrifice, set open heaven to him who offers you adoration; resplendent (Agni), bestow upon us that ample and acceptable (wealth), which, radiant (deity), you with all the gods, have given (to other worshippers).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are engendered repeatedly, and glorified by sacrifice, set open heaven to him who offers you adoration; resplendent (Agni), bestow upon us that ample and acceptable (wealth), which, radiant (deity), you with all the gods, have given (to other worshippers).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वदग्ने काव्या त्वन्मनीषास्त्वदुक्था जायंते राध्यानि ।त्वदेति द्रविणं वीरपेशा इत्थाधिये दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: tvát ǀ agne ǀ kā́vyā ǀ tvám ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǀ tvát ǀ ukthā́ ǀ jāyante ǀ rā́dhyāni ǀtvát ǀ eti ǀ dráviṇam ǀ vīrá-peśāḥ ǀ itthā́-dhiye ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The offerings (to the gods) are engendered,Agni, of you; from you (proceed) praises; from you effective prayers; from you come a vigorous frame and wealth to man who worships with sincerity and offers oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: The offerings (to the gods) are engendered,Agni, of you; from you (proceed) praises; from you effective prayers; from you come a vigorous frame and wealth to man who worships with sincerity and offers oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वद्वाजी वाजंभरो विहाया अभिष्टिकृज्जायते सत्यशुष्मः ।त्वद्रयिर्देवजूतो मयोभुस्त्वदाशुर्जूजुवाँ अग्ने अर्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: tvát ǀ vājī́ ǀ vājam-bharáḥ ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ abhiṣṭi-kṛ́t ǀ jāyate ǀ satyá-śuṣmaḥ ǀtvát ǀ rayíḥ ǀ devá-jūtaḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhúḥ ǀ tvát ǀ āśúḥ ǀ jūju-vā́n ǀ agne ǀ árvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: From you, who are vigorous, to conveyer of oblations, the vast, the granter of what is desired, is born (a son) of real strength; from you comes wealth approved of by the gods, the source of happiness; from you,Agni, (is obtained) a swift unarrested horse.
verses.wilson_translation: From you, who are vigorous, to conveyer of oblations, the vast, the granter of what is desired, is born (a son) of real strength; from you comes wealth approved of by the gods, the source of happiness; from you,Agni, (is obtained) a swift unarrested horse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामग्ने प्रथमं देवयंतो देवं मर्ता अमृत मंद्रजिह्वं ।द्वेषोयुतमा विवासंति धीभिर्दमूनसं गृहपतिममूरं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ devám ǀ bhártā ǀ amṛta ǀ mandrá-jihvam ǀdveṣaḥ-yútam ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsanti ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ dámūnasam ǀ gṛhá-patim ǀ ámūram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Immortal Agni, devout mortals worship with holy rites you the first deity (of the gods), whose tongue exhilarates (them), the dissipator of sin, the humiliator (of the demons) the lord of the mansion, the unperplexed.
verses.wilson_translation: Immortal Agni, devout mortals worship with holy rites you the first deity (of the gods), whose tongue exhilarates (them), the dissipator of sin, the humiliator (of the demons) the lord of the mansion, the unperplexed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आरे अस्मदमतिमारे अंह आरे विश्वां दुर्मतिं यन्निपासि ।दोषा शिवः सहसः सूनो अग्ने यं देव आ चित्सचसे स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: āré ǀ asmát ǀ ámatim ǀ āré ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ āré ǀ víśvām ǀ duḥ-matím ǀ yát ǀ ni-pā́si ǀdoṣā́ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ agne ǀ yám ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cit ǀ sácase ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, son of strength, since you protect (your worshippers), far (remove) from us all iniquity; far (remove from us) sin; far (from us) all evil thoughts; for proeperous is he of whom you who are radiant by night promote the well-being.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, son of strength, since you protect (your worshippers), far (remove) from us all iniquity; far (remove from us) sin; far (from us) all evil thoughts; for proeperous is he of whom you who are radiant by night promote the well-being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHOSO enkindles thee, with lifted ladle, and thrice this day offers thee food, O Agni,May he excel, triumphant through thy splendours, wise through thy mental power, O Jātavedas. Whoso with toil and trouble brings thee fuel, serving the majesty of mighty Agni,He, kindling thee at evening and at morning, prospers, and comes to wealth, and slays his foemen. Agni is Master of sublime dominion, Agni is Lord of strength and lofty riches.Straightway the self-reliant God, Most Youthful, gives treasures to the mortal who adores him. Most Youthful God, whatever sin, through folly, we here, as human beings, have committed,In sight of Aditi make thou us sinless remit, entirely, Agni, our offences. Even in the presence of great sin, O Agni, free us from prison of the Gods or mortals.Never may we who are thy friends be injured: grant health and strength unto our seed and offspring. Even as ye here, Gods Excellent and Holy, have loosed the cow that by the foot was tethered,So also set us free from this affliction long let our life, O Agni, be extended.

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वामग्न इनधते यतस्रुक्त्रिस्ते अन्नं कृणवत्सस्मिन्नहन् ।स सु द्युम्नैरभ्यस्तु प्रसक्षत्तव क्रत्वा जातवेदश्चिकित्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ inádhate ǀ yatá-sruk ǀ tríḥ ǀ te ǀ ánnam ǀ kṛṇávat ǀ sásmin ǀ áhan ǀsáḥ ǀ sú ǀ dyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ astu ǀ pra-sákṣat ǀ táva ǀ krátvā ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he who with uplifted ladle kindles you, and thrice every day presents to you the (sacrificial) food, knowing your glory,Jātavedas, to be invigorated by the act, surpass (all others) in riches.
verses.wilson_translation: May he who with uplifted ladle kindles you, and thrice every day presents to you the (sacrificial) food, knowing your glory,Jātavedas, to be invigorated by the act, surpass (all others) in riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इध्मं यस्ते जभरच्छश्रमाणो महो अग्ने अनीकमा सपर्यन् ।स इधानः प्रति दोषामुषासं पुष्यन्रयिं सचते घ्नन्नमित्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: idhmám ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ jabhárat ǀ śaśramāṇáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ agne ǀ ánīkam ǀ ā́ ǀ saparyán ǀsáḥ ǀ idhānáḥ ǀ práti ǀ doṣā́m ǀ uṣásam ǀ púṣyan ǀ rayím ǀ sacate ǀ ghnán ǀ amítrān ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who, labouring diligently, brings you fuel, honouring,Agni, your great glory; he who kindles you in the evening and at dawn; he, prosperous and destroying his enemies, acquires riches.
verses.wilson_translation: He who, labouring diligently, brings you fuel, honouring,Agni, your great glory; he who kindles you in the evening and at dawn; he, prosperous and destroying his enemies, acquires riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निरीशे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्याग्निर्वाजस्य परमस्य रायः ।दधाति रत्नं विधते यविष्ठो व्यानुषङ्मर्त्याय स्वधावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ īśe ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ kṣatríyasya ǀ agníḥ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ paramásya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀdádhāti ǀ rátnam ǀ vidhaté ǀ yáviṣṭhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ānuṣák ǀ mártyāya ǀ svadhā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniis the possessor of great strength of excellent food of riches, the young (of the gods); abounding in sustenance, he gives to the mortal who worships him precious (wealth) according to (his devotion).
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis the possessor of great strength of excellent food of riches, the young (of the gods); abounding in sustenance, he gives to the mortal who worships him precious (wealth) according to (his devotion).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि ते पुरुषत्रा यविष्ठाचित्तिभिश्चकृमा कच्चिदागः ।कृधी ष्वस्माँ अदितेरनागान्व्येनांसि शिश्रथो विष्वगग्ने ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ puruṣa-trā́ ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ ácitti-bhiḥ ǀ cakṛmá ǀ kát ǀ cit ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀkṛdhí ǀ sú ǀ asmā́n ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ánāgān ǀ ví ǀ énāṃsi ǀ śiśrathaḥ ǀ víṣvak ǀ agne ǁ
verses.english_translation: If, young (of the gods), with the inconsiderateness common to men, we have ever committed any offence against you, make us free from the defects of earth efface entirely,Agniour offences.
verses.wilson_translation: If, young (of the gods), with the inconsiderateness common to men, we have ever committed any offence against you, make us free from the defects of earth efface entirely,Agniour offences.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महश्चिदग्न एनसो अभीक ऊर्वाद्देवानामुत मर्त्यानां ।मा ते सखायः सदमिद्रिषाम यच्छा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ cit ǀ agne ǀ énasaḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀ ūrvā́t ǀ devā́nām ǀ utá ǀ mártyānām ǀmā́ ǀ te ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ riṣāma ǀ yáccha ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not us,Agni, who are your friends, ever suffer harm from any great or comprehensive offence against either gods or men; bestow forgiveness upon our sons and grandsons, the reward of what has been well done.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not us,Agni, who are your friends, ever suffer harm from any great or comprehensive offence against either gods or men; bestow forgiveness upon our sons and grandsons, the reward of what has been well done.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा ह त्यद्वसवो गौर्यं चित्पदि षिताममुंचता यजत्राः ।एवो ष्वस्मन्मुंचता व्यंहः प्र तार्यग्ने प्रतरं न आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ gauryám ǀ cit ǀ padí ǀ sitā́m ǀ ámuñcata ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀevó íti ǀ sú ǀ asmát ǀ muñcata ǀ ví ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ tāri ǀ agne ǀ pra-tarám ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adorable Vasus, in like manner as you have liberated the cow bound by the foot, so set us free entirely from sin; and may our existence,Agni, be prolonged.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Vasus, in like manner as you have liberated the cow bound by the foot, so set us free entirely from sin; and may our existence,Agni, be prolonged.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI hath looked, benevolently-minded, on the wealth-giving spring of radiant Mornings.Come, Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious: Sūrya the God is rising with his splendour. Savitar, God, hath spread on high his lustre, waving his flag like a spoil-seeking hero.Their stablished way go Varuṇa and Mitra, what time they make the Sun ascend the heaven. Him whom they made to drive away the darkness, Lords of sure mansions, constant to their object,Him who beholds the universe, the Sun-God, seven strong and youthful Coursers carry onward. Spreading thy web with mightiest Steeds thou comest, rending apart, thou God, the black-hued mantle.The rays of Sūrya tremulously shining sink, like a hide, the darkness in the waters. How is it that, unbound and not supported, he falleth not although directed downward?By what self power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यद्विभातीनां सुमना रत्नधेयं ।यातमश्विना सुकृतो दुरोणमुत्सूर्यो ज्योतिषा देव एति ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ agníḥ ǀ uṣásām ǀ ágram ǀ akhyat ǀ vi-bhātīnā́m ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ratna-dhéyam ǀyātám ǀ aśvinā ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ duroṇám ǀ út ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ deváḥ ǀ eti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Favourably-minded,Agnihas manifested (his might) in regard to the wealth-bestowing procession of the resplendent dawns; proceed,Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper); the divine sun rises with splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: Favourably-minded,Agnihas manifested (his might) in regard to the wealth-bestowing procession of the resplendent dawns; proceed,Aśvins, to the dwelling of the pious (worshipper); the divine sun rises with splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्द्रप्सं दविध्वद्गविषो न सत्वा ।अनु व्रतं वरुणो यंति मित्रो यत्सूर्यं दिव्यारोहयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvám ǀ bhānúm ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aśret ǀ drapsám ǀ dávidhvat ǀ go-iṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sátvā ǀánu ǀ vratám ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yanti ǀ mitráḥ ǀ yát ǀ sū́ryam ǀ diví ǀ ā-roháyanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Savitādiffuses his light on high, dispersing the dew, and like a vigorous (bull) ardent for the cow; then Varuṇa, and Mitra, and other (divinities), hasten to (fulfil) their offices when they elevate the sun in the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitādiffuses his light on high, dispersing the dew, and like a vigorous (bull) ardent for the cow; then Varuṇa, and Mitra, and other (divinities), hasten to (fulfil) their offices when they elevate the sun in the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यं सीमकृण्वंतमसे विपृचे ध्रुवक्षेमा अनवस्यंतो अर्थं ।तं सूर्यं हरितः सप्त यह्वीः स्पशं विश्वस्य जगतो वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ sīm ǀ ákṛṇvan ǀ támase ǀ vi-pṛ́ce ǀ dhruvá-kṣemāḥ ǀ ánava-syantaḥ ǀ ártham ǀtám ǀ sū́ryam ǀ harítaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǀ spáśam ǀ víśvasya ǀ jágataḥ ǀ vahanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven great courses convey that sun, whom the (deities), occupants of enduring mansions, and not heedless (of their offices), have formed for the driving away of darkness, (and who is) the animator of the whole world.
verses.wilson_translation: Seven great courses convey that sun, whom the (deities), occupants of enduring mansions, and not heedless (of their offices), have formed for the driving away of darkness, (and who is) the animator of the whole world.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वहिष्ठेभिर्विहरन्यासि तंतुमवव्ययन्नसितं देव वस्म ।दविध्वतो रश्मयः सूर्यस्य चर्मेवावाधुस्तमो अप्स्वंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: váhiṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ vi-háran ǀ yāsi ǀ tántum ǀ ava-vyáyan ǀ ásitam ǀ deva ǀ vásma ǀdávidhvataḥ ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ cárma-iva ǀ áva ǀ adhuḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine (sun), you proceed with most powerful (horses), spreading your web (or rays), and cutting down the black abode (of night); the tremulous rays of the sun throw off the darknes which is spread like a skin over the firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine (sun), you proceed with most powerful (horses), spreading your web (or rays), and cutting down the black abode (of night); the tremulous rays of the sun throw off the darknes which is spread like a skin over the firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं न्यङ्ङुत्तानोऽव पद्यते न ।कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कंभः समृतः पाति नाकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ánāyataḥ ǀ áni-baddhaḥ ǀ kathā́ ǀ ayám ǀ nyáṅ ǀ uttānáḥ ǀ áva ǀ padyate ǀ ná ǀkáyā ǀ yāti ǀ svadháyā ǀ káḥ ǀ dadarśa ǀ diváḥ ǀ skambháḥ ǀ sám-ṛtaḥ ǀ pāti ǀ nā́kam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This sun, not far removed, and unobstructed, whether (looking) downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky?
verses.wilson_translation: This sun, not far removed, and unobstructed, whether (looking) downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XIV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE God hath looked, even Agni Jātavedas, to meet the Dawns refulgent in their glories.Come on your chariot, ye who travel widely, come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas. Producing light for all the world of creatures, God Savitar hath raised aloft his banner.Making his presence known by sunbeams, Sūrya hath filled the firmament and earth and heaven. Red Dawn is come, riding with brightness onward, distinguished by her beams, gay-hued and mighty.Dawn on her nobly-harnessed car, the Goddess, awaking men to happiness, approacheth. May those most powerful steeds and chariot bring you, O Aśvins, hither at the break of morning.Here for your draught of meath are Soma juices: at this our sacrifice rejoice, ye Mighty. How is it that, unbound and unsupported, he falleth not although directed downward?By what self-power moves he? Who hath seen it? He guards the vault of heaven, a close-set pillar?

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यग्निरुषसो जातवेदा अख्यद्देवो रोचमाना महोभिः ।आ नासत्योरुगाया रथेनेमं यज्ञमुप नो यातमच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ agníḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ ákhyat ǀ deváḥ ǀ rócamānāḥ ǀ máhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ uru-gāyā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ yātam ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: The resplendent Agni, by whom all is known, has manifested (his might) in regard to the dawns radiant with lustre; far-going Nāsatyas, come with your car to this our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: The resplendent Agni, by whom all is known, has manifested (his might) in regard to the dawns radiant with lustre; far-going Nāsatyas, come with your car to this our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं केतुं सविता देवो अश्रेज्ज्योतिर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय कृण्वन् ।आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं वि सूर्यो रश्मिभिश्चेकितानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvám ǀ ketúm ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aśret ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ víśvasmai ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ kṛṇván ǀā́ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ví ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ cékitānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Savitādisplays his banner on high, diffusing light through all worlds; contemplating (all things), the sun has filled heaven and earth and the firmament with his rays.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitādisplays his banner on high, diffusing light through all worlds; contemplating (all things), the sun has filled heaven and earth and the firmament with his rays.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आवहंत्यरुणीर्ज्योतिषागान्मही चित्रा रश्मिभिश्चेकिताना ।प्रबोधयंती सुविताय देव्युषा ईयते सुयुजा रथेन ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-váhantī ǀ aruṇī́ḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ mahī́ ǀ citrā́ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ cékitānā ǀpra-bodháyantī ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ devī́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ īyate ǀ su-yújā ǀ ráthena ǁ
verses.english_translation: The great and intelligent dawn, variegated with (many-coloured) rays of purple tint, bringing opulence, has come with (her) lustre; the divine Uṣas, arousing (the sleepers), proceeds with her well-harnessed car (to distribute) felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: The great and intelligent dawn, variegated with (many-coloured) rays of purple tint, bringing opulence, has come with (her) lustre; the divine Uṣas, arousing (the sleepers), proceeds with her well-harnessed car (to distribute) felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां वहिष्ठा इह ते वहंतु रथा अश्वास उषसो व्युष्टौ ।इमे हि वां मधुपेयाय सोमा अस्मिन्यज्ञे वृषणा मादयेथां ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ váhiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ihá ǀ té ǀ vahantu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀimé ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ madhu-péyāya ǀ sómāḥ ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ mādayethām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those robust and active horses bring you, (Aśvins), hither at the breaking of the dawn, and may these Somajuices prepared, showerers (of benefits), for your drinking, exhilarate you at this (our sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: May those robust and active horses bring you, (Aśvins), hither at the breaking of the dawn, and may these Somajuices prepared, showerers (of benefits), for your drinking, exhilarate you at this (our sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनायतो अनिबद्धः कथायं न्यङ्ङुत्तानोऽव पद्यते न ।कया याति स्वधया को ददर्श दिवः स्कंभः समृतः पाति नाकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ánāyataḥ ǀ áni-baddhaḥ ǀ kathā́ ǀ ayám ǀ nyáṅ ǀ uttānáḥ ǀ áva ǀ padyate ǀ ná ǀkáyā ǀ yāti ǀ svadháyā ǀ káḥ ǀ dadarśa ǀ diváḥ ǀ skambháḥ ǀ sám-ṛtaḥ ǀ pāti ǀ nā́kam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This sun, not far removed and unobstructed, whether looking downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: This sun, not far removed and unobstructed, whether looking downwards or looking upwards, is harmed by no one; what is the power by which he travels? who has (truly) beheld him who, as the collective pillar of heaven, sustains the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XV. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १० वामदेवो गौतमः। अग्निः, ७-८ सोमकः साहदेव्यः, ९-१० अश्विनौ। गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI the Herald, like a horse, is led forth at our solemn rite,God among Gods adorable. Three times unto our solemn rite comes Agni like a charioteer,Bearing the viands to the Gods. Round the oblations hath he paced, Agni the Wise, the Lord of Strength,Giving the offerer precious boons. He who is kindled eastward for Sṛñjaya, Devāvata's son,Resplendent, tamer of the foe. So mighty be the Agni whom the mortal hero shall command,With sharpened teeth and bountiful. Day after day they dress him, as they clean a horse who wins the prize.Dress the red Scion of the Sky. When Sahadeva's princely son with two bay horses thought of me,Summoned by him I drew not back. And truly those two noble bays I straightway took when offered me,From Sahadeva's princely son. Long, O ye Aśvins, may he live, your care, ye Gods, the princely son.Of Sahadeva, Somaka. Cause him the youthful prince, the son of Sahadeva, to enjoyLong life, O Aśvins, O ye Gods.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्होता नो अध्वरे वाजी सन्परि णीयते ।देवो देवेषु यज्ञियः ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ naḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ vājī́ ǀ sán ǀ pári ǀ nīyate ǀdeváḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the invoker (of the gods), like a horse (that bears a burden), is brought to our sacrifice; a deity adorable among deities.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the invoker (of the gods), like a horse (that bears a burden), is brought to our sacrifice; a deity adorable among deities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि त्रिविष्ट्यध्वरं यात्यग्नी रथीरिव ।आ देवेषु प्रयो दधत् ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ tri-viṣṭí ǀ adhvarám ǀ yā́ti ǀ agníḥ ǀ rathī́ḥ-iva ǀā́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ práyaḥ ǀ dádhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, thrice (a day), comes to our sacrifice like charioteer, bearing the sacrificial food to the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, thrice (a day), comes to our sacrifice like charioteer, bearing the sacrificial food to the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि वाजपतिः कविरग्निर्हव्यान्यक्रमीत् ।दधद्रत्नानि दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ vā́ja-patiḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ havyā́ni ǀ akramīt ǀdádhat ǀ rátnāni ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sage,Agni, the lord of food, has encompassed the oblation, giving precious things to the donor.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage,Agni, the lord of food, has encompassed the oblation, giving precious things to the donor.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं यः सृंजये पुरो दैववाते समिध्यते ।द्युमाँ अमित्रदंभनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ yáḥ ǀ sṛ́ñjaye ǀ puráḥ ǀ daiva-vāté ǀ sam-idhyáte ǀdyu-mā́n ǀ amitra-dámbhanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Radiant as this Agni, the subduer of foes, who is kindled on the (altar) of the cast as (he was kindled) for Sṛñjaya, the son of Devavāta.
verses.wilson_translation: Radiant as this Agni, the subduer of foes, who is kindled on the (altar) of the cast as (he was kindled) for Sṛñjaya, the son of Devavāta.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य घा वीर ईवतोऽग्नेरीशीत मर्त्यः ।तिग्मजंभस्य मीळ्हुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ásya ǀ gha ǀ vīráḥ ǀ ī́vataḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ īśīta ǀ mártyaḥ ǀtigmá-jambhasya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the mortal who is strenuous (in worship) acquire authority over this Agni, the sharp-rayed, the showerer (of benefits).
verses.wilson_translation: May the mortal who is strenuous (in worship) acquire authority over this Agni, the sharp-rayed, the showerer (of benefits).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमर्वंतं न सानसिमरुषं न दिवः शिशुं ।मर्मृज्यंते दिवेदिवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ árvantam ǀ ná ǀ sānasím ǀ aruṣám ǀ ná ǀ diváḥ ǀ śíśum ǀmarmṛjyánte ǀ divé-dive ǁ
verses.english_translation: They diligently worship him daily who is like a horse (to convey oblations), who is liberal and resplendent as the son of heaven, (the sun).
verses.wilson_translation: They diligently worship him daily who is like a horse (to convey oblations), who is liberal and resplendent as the son of heaven, (the sun).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बोधद्यन्मा हरिभ्यां कुमारः साहदेव्यः ।अच्छा न हूत उदरं ॥
verses.transliteration: bódhat ǀ yát ǀ mā ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ sāha-devyáḥ ǀáccha ǀ ná ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ út ǀ aram ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the prince, the son of Sahadeva, promised (to present) me with two horses, I withdrew not when called before him.
verses.wilson_translation: When the prince, the son of Sahadeva, promised (to present) me with two horses, I withdrew not when called before him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्या यजता हरी कुमारात्साहदेव्यात् ।प्रयता सद्य आ ददे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tyā́ ǀ yajatā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀ kumārā́t ǀ sāha-devyā́t ǀprá-yatā ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dade ǁ
verses.english_translation: But immediately accepted those two excellent and well-trained horses from the prince, the son of Sahadeva.
verses.wilson_translation: But immediately accepted those two excellent and well-trained horses from the prince, the son of Sahadeva.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एष वां देवावश्विना कुमारः साहदेव्यः ।दीर्घायुरस्तु सोमकः ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ vām ǀ devau ǀ aśvinā ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ sāha-devyáḥ ǀdīrghá-āyuḥ ǀ astu ǀ sómakaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Aśvins, may this prince,Somaka, the son of Sahadeva, your (worshipper), enjoy long life.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Aśvins, may this prince,Somaka, the son of Sahadeva, your (worshipper), enjoy long life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं युवं देवावश्विना कुमारं साहदेव्यं ।दीर्घायुषं कृणोतन ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ yuvám ǀ devau ǀ aśvinā ǀ kumārám ǀ sāha-devyám ǀdīrghá-āyuṣam ǀ kṛṇotana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Aśvins, do you two make the prince, the son of Sahadeva, long-lived.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Aśvins, do you two make the prince, the son of Sahadeva, long-lived.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XVI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IMPETUOUS, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his Tawny Coursers speed to reach us.For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit. Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee today at this libation.Like Uśanā, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest. When the Bull, quaffing, praises our libation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret,Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e’en by day have wrought their works while singing. When heaven's fair light by hymns was made apparent (they made great splendour shine at break of morning),He with his succour, best of Heroes, scattered the blinding darkness so that men saw clearly. Indra, Impetuous One, hath waxed immensely: he with his vastness hath filled earth and heaven.E’en beyond this his majesty extendeth who hath exceeded all the worlds in greatness. Śakra who knoweth well all human actions hath with his eager Friends let loose the waters.They with their songs cleft e’en the mountain open and willingly disclosed the stall of cattle. He smote away the floods' obstructer, Vṛtra; Earth, conscious, lent her aid to speed thy thunder.Thou sentest forth the waters of the ocean, as Lord through power and might, O daring Hero. When, Much-invoked! the water's rock thou cleftest, Saramā showed herself and went before thee.Hymned by Aṅgirases, bursting the cow-stalls, much strength thou foundest for us as our leader. Come, Maghavan, Friend of Man, to aid the singer imploring thee in battle for the sunlight.Speed him with help in his inspired invokings: down sink the sorcerer, the prayerless Dasyu. Come to our home resolved to slay the Dasyu: Kutsa longed eagerly to win thy friendship.Alike in form ye both sate in his dwelling the faithful Lady was in doubt between you. Thou comest, fain to succour him, with Kutsa,—a goad that masters both the Wind-God's horses,That, holding the brown steeds like spoil for capture, the sage may on the final day be present. For Kutsa, with thy thousand, thou at day-break didst hurl down greedy Śuṣṇa, foe of harvest.Quickly with Kutsa's friend destroy the Dasyus, and roll the chariot-wheel of Sūrya near us. Thou to the son of Vidathin, Ṛjiśvan, gavest up mighty Mṛgaya and Pipru.Thou smotest down the swarthy fifty thousand, and rentest forts as age consumes a garment. What time thou settest near the Sun thy body, thy form, Immortal One, is seen expanding:Thou a wild elephant with might invested. like a dread lion as thou wieldest weapons. Wishes for wealth have gone to Indra, longing for him in war for light and at libation,Eager for glory, labouring with praisesongs: he is like home, like sweet and fair nutrition. Call we for you that Indra, prompt to listen, him who hath done so much for men's advantage;Who, Lord of envied bounty, to a singer like me brings quickly booty worth the capture. When the sharp-pointed arrow, O thou Hero, flieth mid any conflict of the people,When, Faithful One, the dread encounter cometh, then be thou the Protector of our body. Further the holy thoughts of Vamadeva be thou a guileless Friend in fight for booty.We come to thee whose providence protects us: wide be thy sway for ever for thy singer. O Indra, with these men who love thee truly, free givers, Maghavan, in every battle,May we rejoice through many autumns, quelling our foes, as days subdue the nights with splendour. Now, as the Bhṛgus wrought a car, for Indra the Strong, the Mighty, we our prayer have fashioned,That he may, ne’er withdraw from us his friendship, but be our bodies' guard and strong defender. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell. high like rivers for the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: आ सत्यो यातु मघवाँ ऋजीषी द्रवंत्वस्य हरय उप नः ।तस्मा इदंधः सुषुमा सुदक्षमिहाभिपित्वं करते गृणानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ satyáḥ ǀ yātu ǀ maghá-vān ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀ drávantu ǀ asya ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀtásmai ǀ ít ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ susuma ǀ su-dákṣam ǀ ihá ǀ abhi-pitvám ǀ karate ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the truthful Maghavanthe accepter of the spiritless Soma, come to us; may his horses hasten to us; to him we offer this sacrifice, the very potent beverage; may he grant the fulfilment of our desires.
verses.wilson_translation: May the truthful Maghavanthe accepter of the spiritless Soma, come to us; may his horses hasten to us; to him we offer this sacrifice, the very potent beverage; may he grant the fulfilment of our desires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव स्य शूराध्वनो नांतेऽस्मिन्नो अद्य सवने मंदध्यै ।शंसात्युक्थमुशनेव वेधाश्चिकितुषे असुर्याय मन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ sya ǀ śūra ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ánte ǀ asmín ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ sávane ǀ mandádhyai ǀśáṃsāti ǀ ukthám ǀ uśánā-iva ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ cikitúṣe ǀ asuryā́ya ǀ mánma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero,Indra, set us free today to give you exhilaration at this sacrifice, as (they let loose a horse) at the end of the road; may the worshipper, like Uśanās, repeat an acceptable prayer to you, the knower (of all things), the destroyer of theasuras.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, set us free today to give you exhilaration at this sacrifice, as (they let loose a horse) at the end of the road; may the worshipper, like Uśanās, repeat an acceptable prayer to you, the knower (of all things), the destroyer of theasuras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कविर्न निण्यं विदथानि साधन्वृषा यत्सेकं विपिपानो अर्चात् ।दिव इत्था जीजनत्सप्त कारूनह्ना चिच्चक्रुर्वयुना गृणंतः ॥
