verses.transliteration: kavíḥ ǀ ná ǀ niṇyám ǀ vidáthāni ǀ sā́dhan ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ yát ǀ sékam ǀ vi-pipānáḥ ǀ árcāt ǀdiváḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ jījanat ǀ saptá ǀ kārū́n ǀ áhnā ǀ cit ǀ cakruḥ ǀ vayúnā ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a sage (knowing) what is hidden, and fulfilling sacred rites, so the showerer (of benefits), quaffing copiously the effused (libation), exults (in the draught), and he genitive rates the seven efficient (rays) from heaven, which, being glorified, have made (manifest) the objects of (human) perception by day.
verses.wilson_translation: Like a sage (knowing) what is hidden, and fulfilling sacred rites, so the showerer (of benefits), quaffing copiously the effused (libation), exults (in the draught), and he genitive rates the seven efficient (rays) from heaven, which, being glorified, have made (manifest) the objects of (human) perception by day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्यद्वेदि सुदृशीकमर्कैर्महि ज्योती रुरुचुर्यद्ध वस्तोः ।अंधा तमांसि दुधिता विचक्षे नृभ्यश्चकार नृतमो अभिष्टौ ॥
verses.transliteration: sváḥ ǀ yát ǀ védi ǀ su-dṛ́śīkam ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ máhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ rurucuḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vástoḥ ǀandhā́ ǀ támāṃsi ǀ dúdhitā ǀ vi-cákṣe ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ cakāra ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ abhíṣṭau ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the vast luminous heaven manifested by the rays (of light) is displayed, then are (the deities) resplendent according to (their heavenly) abode; the chief of leaders, (Indra), in his approach has scattered the thick glooms so that men may see.
verses.wilson_translation: When the vast luminous heaven manifested by the rays (of light) is displayed, then are (the deities) resplendent according to (their heavenly) abode; the chief of leaders, (Indra), in his approach has scattered the thick glooms so that men may see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ववक्ष इंद्रो अमितमृजीष्युभे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा ।अतश्चिदस्य महिमा वि रेच्यभि यो विश्वा भुवना बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: vavakṣé ǀ índraḥ ǀ ámitam ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ paprau ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ ví ǀ reci ǀ abhí ǀ yáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ babhū́va ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, as the accepter of the stale Soma, sustains infinite greatness, and has filled both heaven and earth by his magnitude; therefore has the vastness of him who has surpassed all the regions, exceeded (the world).
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, as the accepter of the stale Soma, sustains infinite greatness, and has filled both heaven and earth by his magnitude; therefore has the vastness of him who has surpassed all the regions, exceeded (the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वानि शक्रो नर्याणि विद्वानपो रिरेच सखिभिर्निकामैः ।अश्मानं चिद्ये बिभिदुर्वचोभिर्व्रजं गोमंतमुशिजो वि वव्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvāni ǀ śakráḥ ǀ náryāṇi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ apáḥ ǀ rireca ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ ní-kāmaiḥ ǀáśmānam ǀ cit ǀ yé ǀ bibhidúḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vrajám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vavruríti vavruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing all things profitable for men,Śakrahas, with his willing friends (the Maruts), sent forth the waters, for they, with (loud) shouts, divided the clouds, and, desiring (to fulfil) their office, set open the pasturage of the cows (of the Aṅgirasas).
verses.wilson_translation: Knowing all things profitable for men,Śakrahas, with his willing friends (the Maruts), sent forth the waters, for they, with (loud) shouts, divided the clouds, and, desiring (to fulfil) their office, set open the pasturage of the cows (of the Aṅgirasas).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपो वृत्रं वव्रिवांसं पराहन्प्रावत्ते वज्रं पृथिवी सचेताः ।प्रार्णांसि समुद्रियाण्यैनोः पतिर्भवञ्छवसा शूर धृष्णो ॥
verses.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vavri-vā́ṃsam ǀ párā ǀ ahan ǀ prá ǀ āvat ǀ te ǀ vájram ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ sá-cetāḥ ǀprá ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ samudríyāṇi ǀ ainoḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ bhávan ǀ śávasā ǀ śūra ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your protecting thunderbolt has slain Vṛtraobstructing the (issue of the waters), the conscious earth (co-operating) with you; valiant hero, preserver (of the regions), send down by your strength the waters of the firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: Your protecting thunderbolt has slain Vṛtraobstructing the (issue of the waters), the conscious earth (co-operating) with you; valiant hero, preserver (of the regions), send down by your strength the waters of the firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपो यदद्रिं पुरुहूत दर्दराविर्भुवत्सरमा पूर्व्यं ते ।स नो नेता वाजमा दर्षि भूरिं गोत्रा रुजन्नंगिरोभिर्गृणानः ॥
verses.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ yát ǀ ádrim ǀ puru-hūta ǀ dárdaḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ sarámā ǀ pūrvyám ǀ te ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ netā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ā́ ǀ darṣi ǀ bhū́rim ǀ gotrā́ ǀ ruján ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invoked of many, when you had divided the cloud for (the escape of) the waters,Saramāappeared before you; and you, the bringer of abundant food, have shown us favour, dividing the clouds and glorified by the Aṅgirasas.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoked of many, when you had divided the cloud for (the escape of) the waters,Saramāappeared before you; and you, the bringer of abundant food, have shown us favour, dividing the clouds and glorified by the Aṅgirasas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा कविं नृमणो गा अभिष्टौ स्वर्षाता मघवन्नाधमानं ।ऊतिभिस्तमिषणो द्युम्नहूतौ नि मायावानब्रह्मा दस्युरर्त ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ kavím ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ gāḥ ǀ abhíṣṭau ǀ sváḥ-sātā ǀ magha-van ǀ nā́dhamānam ǀūtí-bhiḥ ǀ tám ǀ iṣaṇaḥ ǀ dyumná-hūtau ǀ ní ǀ māyā́-vān ǀ ábrahmā ǀ dásyuḥ ǀ arta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavan, who are honoured by men, you have repaired to the presence of the sage for (the sake of) bestowing (upon him) wealth, and when soliciting (you) in his need (for aid); defending (him) with your protection, the guileful, impious Dasyuhas been destroyed in the contest for the spoil.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavan, who are honoured by men, you have repaired to the presence of the sage for (the sake of) bestowing (upon him) wealth, and when soliciting (you) in his need (for aid); defending (him) with your protection, the guileful, impious Dasyuhas been destroyed in the contest for the spoil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ दस्युघ्ना मनसा याह्यस्तं भुवत्ते कुत्सः सख्ये निकामः ।स्वे योनौ नि षदतं सरूपा वि वां चिकित्सदृतचिद्ध नारी ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dasyu-ghnā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ yāhi ǀ ástam ǀ bhúvat ǀ te ǀ kútsaḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ ní-kāmaḥ ǀsvé ǀ yónau ǀ ní ǀ sadatam ǀ sá-rūpā ǀ ví ǀ vām ǀ cikitsat ǀ ṛta-cít ǀ ha ǀ nā́rī ǁ
verses.english_translation: With a mind resolved on killing the Dasyu, you came (to his dwelling), and Kutsawas eager for your friendship; now have you two alighted in his, (Indra's), habitation, and being entirely similar in form the truthful woman has been perplexed (to discriminate between you).
verses.wilson_translation: With a mind resolved on killing the Dasyu, you came (to his dwelling), and Kutsawas eager for your friendship; now have you two alighted in his, (Indra's), habitation, and being entirely similar in form the truthful woman has been perplexed (to discriminate between you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यासि कुत्सेन सरथमवस्युस्तोदो वातस्य हर्योरीशानः ।ऋज्रा वाजं न गध्यं युयूषन्कविर्यदहन्पार्याय भूषात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́si ǀ kútsena ǀ sa-rátham ǀ avasyúḥ ǀ todáḥ ǀ vā́tasya ǀ háryoḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀṛjrā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ná ǀ gádhyam ǀ yúyūṣan ǀ kavíḥ ǀ yát ǀ áhan ǀ pā́ryāya ǀ bhū́ṣāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: You go with Kutsain the same chariot, determined to defend him; (you) who are the tormentor (of foes), the lord of horses (of the speech) of the wind; on the same day wherein, yoking (to the car) the straight-going steeds, as if to receive food, the sage (Kutsa) has been enabled to cross over (the sea) of calamity.
verses.wilson_translation: You go with Kutsain the same chariot, determined to defend him; (you) who are the tormentor (of foes), the lord of horses (of the speech) of the wind; on the same day wherein, yoking (to the car) the straight-going steeds, as if to receive food, the sage (Kutsa) has been enabled to cross over (the sea) of calamity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कुत्साय शुष्णमशुषं नि बर्हीः प्रपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहस्रा ।सद्यो दस्यून्प्र मृण कुत्स्येन प्र सूरश्चक्रं वृहतादभीके ॥
verses.transliteration: kútsāya ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ aśúṣam ǀ ní ǀ barhīḥ ǀ pra-pitvé ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ kúyavam ǀ sahásrā ǀsadyáḥ ǀ dásyūn ǀ prá ǀ mṛṇa ǀ kutsyéna ǀ prá ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ vṛhatāt ǀ abhī́ke ǁ
verses.english_translation: For Kutsa, you have slain the unhappyŚuṣṇaand in the forepart of the day, attended by thousands (you have slain)Kuyavawith the thunderbolt; you have swiftly destroyed the Dasyus, and you have cut them to pieces in the battle, with the wheel (of the chariot of) the sun.
verses.wilson_translation: For Kutsa, you have slain the unhappyŚuṣṇaand in the forepart of the day, attended by thousands (you have slain)Kuyavawith the thunderbolt; you have swiftly destroyed the Dasyus, and you have cut them to pieces in the battle, with the wheel (of the chariot of) the sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं पिप्रुं मृगयं शूशुवांसमृजिश्वने वैदथिनाय रंधीः ।पंचाशत्कृष्णा नि वपः सहस्रात्कं न पुरो जरिमा वि दर्दः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ píprum ǀ mṛ́gayam ǀ śūśu-vā́ṃsam ǀ ṛjíśvane ǀ vaidathinā́ya ǀ randhīḥ ǀpañcāśát ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ ní ǀ vapaḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ átkam ǀ ná ǀ púraḥ ǀ jarimā́ ǀ ví ǀ dardaríti dardaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have subjugated Pipru and the mighty Mṛgayāfor the sake of Ṛjiṣvan, the son of Vidathin, you have slain the fifty thousand Kṛṣṇas; and, as old age (destroys) life, you have demolished the cities (ofŚambara).
verses.wilson_translation: You have subjugated Pipru and the mighty Mṛgayāfor the sake of Ṛjiṣvan, the son of Vidathin, you have slain the fifty thousand Kṛṣṇas; and, as old age (destroys) life, you have demolished the cities (ofŚambara).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सूर उपाके तन्वं दधानो वि यत्ते चेत्यमृतस्य वर्पः ।मृगो न हस्ती तविषीमुषाणः सिंहो न भीम आयुधानि बिभ्रत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sū́raḥ ǀ upāké ǀ tanvám ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ céti ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ várpaḥ ǀmṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ hastī́ ǀ táviṣīm ǀ uṣāṇáḥ ǀ siṃháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ bíbhrat ǁ
verses.english_translation: While having (your) person n in the proximity of the sun, your form becomes redolent of ambrosia, and you are like the deer-like elephant, consuming the strength (of the strong), and are like a terrible lion when wielding your weapons.
verses.wilson_translation: While having (your) person n in the proximity of the sun, your form becomes redolent of ambrosia, and you are like the deer-like elephant, consuming the strength (of the strong), and are like a terrible lion when wielding your weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं कामा वसूयंतो अग्मन्त्स्वर्मीळ्हे न सवने चकानाः ।श्रवस्यवः शशमानास उक्थैरोको न रण्वा सुदृशीव पुष्टिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ kā́māḥ ǀ vasu-yántaḥ ǀ agman ǀ sváḥ-mīḷhe ǀ ná ǀ sávane ǀ cakānā́ḥ ǀśravasyávaḥ ǀ śaśamānā́saḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ ókaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raṇvā́ ǀ sudṛ́śī-iva ǀ puṣṭíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Relying (upon Indra) for protection, and desirous of riches, (pious men) repair to him soliciting his presence in the sacrifice, as if in the battle, asking for food, celebrating his praise with hymns, for he is the refuge (of his worshippers), and resembles the grateful and lovely (goddess) of nutrition.
verses.wilson_translation: Relying (upon Indra) for protection, and desirous of riches, (pious men) repair to him soliciting his presence in the sacrifice, as if in the battle, asking for food, celebrating his praise with hymns, for he is the refuge (of his worshippers), and resembles the grateful and lovely (goddess) of nutrition.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमिद्व इंद्रं सुहवं हुवेम यस्ता चकार नर्या पुरूणि ।यो मावते जरित्रे गध्यं चिन्मक्षू वाजं भरति स्पार्हराधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ vaḥ ǀ índram ǀ su-hávam ǀ huvema ǀ yáḥ ǀ tā́ ǀ cakā́ra ǀ náryā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀyáḥ ǀ mā́-vate ǀ jaritré ǀ gádhyam ǀ cit ǀ makṣú ǀ vā́jam ǀ bhárati ǀ spārhá-rādhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us invoke that gracious Indrawho has made so many things good for man; who, bestowing enviable opulence, quickly brings acceptable food to a worshipper like me.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us invoke that gracious Indrawho has made so many things good for man; who, bestowing enviable opulence, quickly brings acceptable food to a worshipper like me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तिग्मा यदंतरशनिः पताति कस्मिंचिच्छूर मुहुके जनानां ।घोरा यदर्य समृतिर्भवात्यध स्मा नस्तन्वो बोधि गोपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tigmā́ ǀ yát ǀ antáḥ ǀ aśániḥ ǀ pátāti ǀ kásmin ǀ cit ǀ śūra ǀ muhuké ǀ jánānām ǀghorā́ ǀ yát ǀ arya ǀ sám-ṛtiḥ ǀ bhávāti ǀ ádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ gopā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero,indra, when in any conflict of men the sharp thunderbolt falls in the midst (of them), and when, lord there is a terrible battle, then the defender of our person ns is made known.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,indra, when in any conflict of men the sharp thunderbolt falls in the midst (of them), and when, lord there is a terrible battle, then the defender of our person ns is made known.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भुवोऽविता वामदेवस्य धीनां भुवः सखावृको वाजसातौ ।त्वामनु प्रमतिमा जगन्मोरुशंसो जरित्रे विश्वध स्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhúvaḥ ǀ avitā́ ǀ vāmá-devasya ǀ dhīnā́m ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ avṛkáḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀtvā́m ǀ ánu ǀ prá-matim ǀ ā́ ǀ jaganma ǀ uru-śáṃsaḥ ǀ jaritré ǀ viśvádha ǀ syāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be you the protector of the pious acts of Vāmadeva; be you in battle an unfailing friend; we come to you, eminent in wisdom; may you be ever benignant to your praiser.
verses.wilson_translation: Be you the protector of the pious acts of Vāmadeva; be you in battle an unfailing friend; we come to you, eminent in wisdom; may you be ever benignant to your praiser.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एभिर्नृभिरिंद्र त्वायुभिष्ट्वा मघवद्भिर्मघवन्विश्व आजौ ।द्यावो न द्युम्नैरभि संतो अर्यः क्षपो मदेम शरदश्च पूर्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ebhíḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ tvāyú-bhiḥ ǀ tvā ǀ maghávat-bhiḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ víśve ǀ ājáu ǀdyā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sántaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ kṣapáḥ ǀ madema ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In every battle,Maghavan, may we, along with those men who trust in you and offer rich gifts, like those who are resplendent with riches, triumphing over their foes, glorify you many nights and years.
verses.wilson_translation: In every battle,Maghavan, may we, along with those men who trust in you and offer rich gifts, like those who are resplendent with riches, triumphing over their foes, glorify you many nights and years.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवेदिंद्राय वृषभाय वृष्णे ब्रह्माकर्म भृगवो न रथं ।नू चिद्यथा नः सख्या वियोषदसन्न उग्रोऽविता तनूपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ ít ǀ índrāya ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ bráhma ǀ akarma ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rátham ǀnú ǀ cit ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ vi-yóṣat ǀ ásat ǀ naḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ avitā́ ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore we offer to the vigorous Indra, the showerer (of benefits), holy adoration, that he may never withdraw his friendly (actions) from us, and that he may be our powerful protector, the defender of (our) person ns, as the Bhṛgus(fabricate) a car (for use).
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore we offer to the vigorous Indra, the showerer (of benefits), holy adoration, that he may never withdraw his friendly (actions) from us, and that he may be our powerful protector, the defender of (our) person ns, as the Bhṛgus(fabricate) a car (for use).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in (your) praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in (your) praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XVII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: २१ वामदेवो गौतमः। इन्द्रः। त्रिष्टुप्, १५ एकपदा विराट्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GREAT art thou, Indra; yea, the earth, with gladness, and heaven confess to thee thine high dominion.Thou in thy vigour having slaughtered Vṛtra didst free the floods arrested by the Dragon. Heaven trembled at the birth of thine effulgence; Earth trembled at the fear of thy displeasure.The stedfast mountains shook in agitation . the waters flowed, and desert spots were flooded. Hurling his bolt with might he cleft the mountain, while, putting forth his strength, he showed his vigour.He slaughtered Vṛtra with his bolt, exulting, and, their lord slain, forth flowed the waters swiftly. Thy Father Dyaus esteemed himself a hero: most noble was the work of Indra's Maker,His who begat the strong bolt's Lord who roareth, immovable like earth from her foundation. He who alone o’erthrows the world of creatures, Indra the peoples' King, invoked of many-Verily all rejoice in him, extolling the boons which Maghavan the God hath sent them. All Soma juices are his own for ever, most gladdening draughts are ever his, the Mighty,Thou ever wast the Treasure-Lord of treasures: Indra, thou lettest all folk share thy bounty. Moreover, when thou first wast born, O Indra, thou struckest terror into all the people.Thou, Maghavan, rentest with thy bolt the Dragon who lay against the waterfloods of heaven. The ever-slaying, bold and furious Indra, the bright bolt's Lord, infinite, strong and mighty,Who slayeth Vṛtra and acquireth booty, giver of blessings, Maghavan the bounteous: Alone renowned as Maghavan in battles, he frighteneth away assembled armies.He bringeth us the booty that he winneth may we, well-loved, continue in his friendship. Renowned is he when conquering and when slaying: 'fis he who winneth cattle in the combat.When Indra hardeneth his indignation all that is fixed and all that moveth fear him. Indra hath won all kine, all gold, all horses,—Maghavan, he who breaketh forts in pieces;Most manly with these men of his who help him, dealing out wealth and gathering the treasure. What is the care of Indra for his Mother, what cares he for the Father who begat him?His care is that which speeds his might in conflicts, like wind borne onward by the clouds that thunder. Maghavan makes the settled man unsettled: he scatters dust that he hath swept together,Breaking in pieces like Heaven armed with lightning: Maghavan shall enrich the man who lauds h;m. He urged the chariot-wheel of Sūrya forward: Etaśa, speeding on his way, he rested.Him the black undulating cloud bedeweth, in this mid-air's depth, at the base of darkness, As in the night the sacrificing priest. Eager for booty, craving strength and horses, we-singers stir Indra, the strong, for friendship,Who gives the wives we seek, whose succour fails not, to hasten, like a pitcher to the fountain. Be thou our guardian, show thyself our kinsman, watching and blessing those who pour the Soma;As Friend, as Sire, most fatherly of fathers giving the suppliant vital strength and freedom. Be helping Friend of those who seek thy friendship . give life, when lauded, Indra, to the singer.For, Indra, we the priests have paid thee worship, exalting thee with these our sacrifices. Alone, when Indra Maghavan is lauded, he slayeth many ne’er-resisted Vṛtras.Him in whose keeping is the well-loved singer never do Gods or mortals stay or hinder. E’en so let Maghavan, the loud-voiced Indra, give us true blessings, foeless, men's upholder.King of all creatures, give us glory amply, exalted glory due to him who lauds thee. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers for the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं महाँ इंद्र तुभ्यं ह क्षा अनु क्षत्रं मंहना मन्यत द्यौः ।त्वं वृत्रं शवसा जघन्वान्त्सृजः सिंधूँरहिना जग्रसानान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ mahā́n ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ ha ǀ kṣā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ kṣatrám ǀ maṃhánā ǀ manyata ǀ dyáuḥ ǀtvám ǀ vṛtrám ǀ śávasā ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ sṛjáḥ ǀ síndhūn ǀ áhinā ǀ jagrasānā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Indra, are mighty; the vast earth confesses to you (your) strength, as does the heaven; you have slain Vṛtraby your vigour, you have set free the rivers arrested by Ahi.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are mighty; the vast earth confesses to you (your) strength, as does the heaven; you have slain Vṛtraby your vigour, you have set free the rivers arrested by Ahi.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव त्विषो जनिमन्रेजत द्यौ रेजद्भूमिर्भियसा स्वस्य मन्योः ।ऋघायंत सुभ्वः पर्वतास आर्दंधन्वानि सरयंत आपः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tviṣáḥ ǀ jániman ǀ rejata ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ réjat ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ bhiyásā ǀ svásya ǀ manyóḥ ǀṛghāyánta ǀ su-bhváḥ ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀ ā́rdan ǀ dhánvāni ǀ saráyante ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: At the birth of you who are resplendent, trembled the heaven (and) trembled the earth through fear of your wrath; the mighty clouds were confined; they destroyed (the distress of drought), spreading the waters over the dry plural ces.
verses.wilson_translation: At the birth of you who are resplendent, trembled the heaven (and) trembled the earth through fear of your wrath; the mighty clouds were confined; they destroyed (the distress of drought), spreading the waters over the dry plural ces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भिनद्गिरिं शवसा वज्रमिष्णन्नाविष्कृण्वानः सहसान ओजः ।वधीद्वृत्रं वज्रेण मंदसानः सरन्नापो जवसा हतवृष्णीः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhinát ǀ girím ǀ śávasā ǀ vájram ǀ iṣṇán ǀ āviḥ-kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ sahasānáḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀvádhīt ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vájreṇa ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀ sáran ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ jávasā ǀ hatá-vṛṣṇīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The subduer of foes, manifesting his energy and hurling his thunderbolt, shattered the mountain by his strength; he slew Vṛtrawith the thunderbolt, exulting, and the waters whose obstructor was destroyed rushed forth with rapidity.
verses.wilson_translation: The subduer of foes, manifesting his energy and hurling his thunderbolt, shattered the mountain by his strength; he slew Vṛtrawith the thunderbolt, exulting, and the waters whose obstructor was destroyed rushed forth with rapidity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुवीरस्ते जनिता मन्यत द्यौरिंद्रस्य कर्ता स्वपस्तमो भूत् ।य ईं जजान स्वर्यं सुवज्रमनपच्युतं सदसो न भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: su-vī́raḥ ǀ te ǀ janitā́ ǀ manyata ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ kartā́ ǀ svápaḥ-tamaḥ ǀ bhūt ǀyáḥ ǀ īm ǀ jajā́na ǀ svaryám ǀ su-vájram ǀ ánapa-cyutam ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heaven, your progenitor, conceived (I have obtained) a worthy son; the maker of Indrawas the accomplisher of a most excellent work; he who begot the adorable (Indra), armed with the thunderbolt, irremovable from his station, and endowed with greatness.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven, your progenitor, conceived (I have obtained) a worthy son; the maker of Indrawas the accomplisher of a most excellent work; he who begot the adorable (Indra), armed with the thunderbolt, irremovable from his station, and endowed with greatness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य एक इच्च्यावयति प्र भूमा राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इंद्रः ।सत्यमेनमनु विश्वे मदंति रातिं देवस्य गृणतो मघोनः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ cyaváyati ǀ prá ǀ bhū́ma ǀ rā́jā ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀsatyám ǀ enam ǀ ánu ǀ víśve ǀ madanti ǀ rātím ǀ devásya ǀ gṛṇatáḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All men, praising the munificence of the divine Maghavan, verily glorify him who alone casts downmany,Indra, the king of men, the adored of many.
verses.wilson_translation: All men, praising the munificence of the divine Maghavan, verily glorify him who alone casts downmany,Indra, the king of men, the adored of many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्रा सोमा अभवन्नस्य विश्वे सत्रा मदासो बृहतो मदिष्ठाः ।सत्राभवो वसुपतिर्वसूनां दत्रे विश्वा अधिथा इंद्र कृष्टीः ॥
verses.transliteration: satrā́ ǀ sómāḥ ǀ abhavan ǀ asya ǀ víśve ǀ satrā́ ǀ mádāsaḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ mádiṣṭhāḥ ǀsatrā́ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ vásu-patiḥ ǀ vásūnām ǀ dátre ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ adhithāḥ ǀ indra ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Truly are all libations his, the inebriating draughts are truly most exhilarating to the mighty Indra; truly are you the lord of wealth, of (all sorts of) treasures; you, Indra, support all people by the gift (of riches).
verses.wilson_translation: Truly are all libations his, the inebriating draughts are truly most exhilarating to the mighty Indra; truly are you the lord of wealth, of (all sorts of) treasures; you, Indra, support all people by the gift (of riches).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमध प्रथमं जायमानोऽमे विश्वा अधिथा इंद्र कृष्टीः ।त्वं प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण मघवन्वि वृश्चः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ádha ǀ prathamám ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ áme ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ adhithāḥ ǀ indra ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀtvám ǀ práti ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ā-śáyānam ǀ áhim ǀ vájreṇa ǀ magha-van ǀ ví ǀ vṛścaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [7-8] (We praise) the slayer of many foes, the courageous, the discomfiter (of enemies), the great, the unbounded, the showerer (of benefits), the wielder of the bright thunderbolt, him who is the destroyer of Vṛtra, the bestower of food, the giver of wealth,Maghavan, the possessor of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: [7-8] (We praise) the slayer of many foes, the courageous, the discomfiter (of enemies), the great, the unbounded, the showerer (of benefits), the wielder of the bright thunderbolt, him who is the destroyer of Vṛtra, the bestower of food, the giver of wealth,Maghavan, the possessor of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्राहणं दाधृषिं तुम्रमिंद्रं महामपारं वृषभं सुवज्रं ।हंता यो वृत्रं सनितोत वाजं दाता मघानि मघवा सुराधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: satrā-hánan ǀ dádhṛṣim ǀ túmram ǀ índram ǀ mahā́m ǀ apārám ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ su-vájram ǀhántā ǀ yáḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ sánitā ǀ utá ǀ vā́jam ǀ dā́tā ǀ maghā́ni ǀ maghá-vā ǀ su-rā́dhāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं वृतश्चातयते समीचीर्य आजिषु मघवा शृण्व एकः ।अयं वाजं भरति यं सनोत्यस्य प्रियासः सख्ये स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vṛ́taḥ ǀ cātayate ǀ sam-īcī́ḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ājíṣu ǀ maghá-vā ǀ śṛṇvé ǀ ékaḥ ǀayám ǀ vā́jam ǀ bharati ǀ yám ǀ sanóti ǀ asyá ǀ priyā́saḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Maghavan, who destroys assembled hosts, is he who is renowned as chief in battles; he brings the food which he bestows (upon the worshipper); may we be held dear in his friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: This Maghavan, who destroys assembled hosts, is he who is renowned as chief in battles; he brings the food which he bestows (upon the worshipper); may we be held dear in his friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं शृण्वे अध जयन्नुत घ्नन्नयमुत प्र कृणुते युधा गाः ।यदा सत्यं कृणुते मन्युमिंद्रो विश्वं दृळ्हं भयत एजदस्मात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ śṛṇve ǀ ádha ǀ jáyan ǀ utá ǀ ghnán ǀ ayám ǀ utá ǀ prá ǀ kṛṇute ǀ yudhā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀyadā́ ǀ satyám ǀ kṛṇuté ǀ manyúm ǀ índraḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ dṛḷhám ǀ bhayate ǀ éjat ǀ asmāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: This (Indra), is renowned, whether conquering or slaying (his foes), or whether in conflict he recovers the cattle; when Indra truly entertains anger all that is stationary or moveable is in fear of him.
verses.wilson_translation: This (Indra), is renowned, whether conquering or slaying (his foes), or whether in conflict he recovers the cattle; when Indra truly entertains anger all that is stationary or moveable is in fear of him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिंद्रो गा अजयत्सं हिरण्या समश्विया मघवा यो ह पूर्वीः ।एभिर्नृभिर्नृतमो अस्य शाकै रायो विभक्ता संभरश्च वस्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ índraḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ajayat ǀ sám ǀ híraṇyā ǀ sám ǀ aśviyā́ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ha ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀebhíḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ asya ǀ śākáiḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ vi-bhaktā́ ǀ sam-bharáḥ ǀ ca ǀ vásvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the lord of opulence, who has overcomemany (enemies), has completely won (their) cattle, (their) gold, (their) horses; chief leader by his energies, praised by these his worshippers, he is the distributor of riches, the bestower of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the lord of opulence, who has overcomemany (enemies), has completely won (their) cattle, (their) gold, (their) horses; chief leader by his energies, praised by these his worshippers, he is the distributor of riches, the bestower of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कियत्स्विदिंद्रो अध्येति मातुः कियत्पितुर्जनितुर्यो जजान ।यो अस्य शुष्मं मुहुकैरियर्ति वातो न जूतः स्तनयद्भिरभ्रैः ॥
verses.transliteration: kíyat ǀ svit ǀ índraḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ eti ǀ mātúḥ ǀ kíyat ǀ pitúḥ ǀ janitúḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ jajā́na ǀyáḥ ǀ asya ǀ śúṣmam ǀ muhukáiḥ ǀ íyarti ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ jūtáḥ ǀ stanáyat-bhiḥ ǀ abhráiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Some portion (of his strength)Indraderives from his mother, some portion from his father; he who, though his progenitor, has begotten (the world), and animates its vigour repeatedly, as the wind is driven by thundering clouds.
verses.wilson_translation: Some portion (of his strength)Indraderives from his mother, some portion from his father; he who, though his progenitor, has begotten (the world), and animates its vigour repeatedly, as the wind is driven by thundering clouds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्षियंतं त्वमक्षियंतं कृणोतीयर्ति रेणुं मघवा समोहं ।विभंजनुरशनिमाँ इव द्यौरुत स्तोतारं मघवा वसौ धात् ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣiyántam ǀ tvam ǀ ákṣiyantam ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ íyarti ǀ reṇúm ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sam-óham ǀvi-bhañjanúḥ ǀ aśánimān-iva ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ utá ǀ stotā́ram ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vásau ǀ dhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are the Maghavanwho makes one man destitute, another prosperous, who (scatters from his worshipper) the accusative ulated dust (of sin), the destroyer (of foes), like the heaven with the thunderbolt, Maghavan conducts his worshipper to wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the Maghavanwho makes one man destitute, another prosperous, who (scatters from his worshipper) the accusative ulated dust (of sin), the destroyer (of foes), like the heaven with the thunderbolt, Maghavan conducts his worshipper to wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं चक्रमिषणत्सूर्यस्य न्येतशं रीरमत्ससृमाणं ।आ कृष्ण ईं जुहुराणो जिघर्ति त्वचो बुध्ने रजसो अस्य योनौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ cakrám ǀ iṣaṇat ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ ní ǀ étaśam ǀ rīramat ǀ sasṛmāṇám ǀā́ ǀ kṛṣṇáḥ ǀ īm ǀ juhurāṇáḥ ǀ jigharti ǀ tvacáḥ ǀ budhné ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ asyá ǀ yónau ǁ
verses.english_translation: He has hurled the wheel (of the chariot) of the sun, and has stopped Etaśagoing forth to (battle); the dark undulating cloud bedews him, (staying) at the root of radiance in the regions of its waters.
verses.wilson_translation: He has hurled the wheel (of the chariot) of the sun, and has stopped Etaśagoing forth to (battle); the dark undulating cloud bedews him, (staying) at the root of radiance in the regions of its waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: असिक्न्यां यजमानो न होता ॥
verses.transliteration: ásiknyām ǀ yájamānaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the sacrificer (pours the oblation) at night upon the fire.
verses.wilson_translation: As the sacrificer (pours the oblation) at night upon the fire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गव्यंत इंद्रं सख्याय विप्रा अश्वायंतो वृषणं वाजयंतः ।जनीयंतो जनिदामक्षितोतिमा च्यावयामोऽवते न कोशं ॥
verses.transliteration: gavyántaḥ ǀ índram ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ víprāḥ ǀ aśva-yántaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǀjani-yántaḥ ǀ jani-dā́m ǀ ákṣita-ūtim ǀ ā́ ǀ cyavayāmaḥ ǀ avaté ǀ ná ǀ kóśam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we (who are) wishing for cattle, for horses, for food, for wives, through his friendship induce Indra, the showerer (of benefits), the giver of wives, the unwearied granter of protection, to come down, as a bucket (is lowered) into a well.
verses.wilson_translation: May we (who are) wishing for cattle, for horses, for food, for wives, through his friendship induce Indra, the showerer (of benefits), the giver of wives, the unwearied granter of protection, to come down, as a bucket (is lowered) into a well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्राता नो बोधि ददृशान आपिरभिख्याता मर्डिता सोम्यानां ।सखा पिता पितृतमः पितॄणां कर्तेमु लोकमुशते वयोधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: trātā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ dádṛśānaḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ abhi-khyātā́ ǀ marḍitā́ ǀ somyā́nām ǀsákhā ǀ pitā́ ǀ pitṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ kártā ǀ īm ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ uśaté ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be our preserver, you who are looking (benevolently upon) all; a kinsman (to us); a supervisor (of all things), a bestower of felicity on those who are worthy (to offer) libations; a friend, a protector, a defender in the highest degree among defenders, a creator; (be you, who bestows) the world of heaven upon him who desires it, the giver to us of food.
verses.wilson_translation: Be our preserver, you who are looking (benevolently upon) all; a kinsman (to us); a supervisor (of all things), a bestower of felicity on those who are worthy (to offer) libations; a friend, a protector, a defender in the highest degree among defenders, a creator; (be you, who bestows) the world of heaven upon him who desires it, the giver to us of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सखीयतामविता बोधि सखा गृणान इंद्र स्तुवते वयो धाः ।वयं ह्या ते चकृमा सबाध आभिः शमीभिर्महयंत इंद्र ॥
verses.transliteration: sakhi-yatā́m ǀ avitā́ ǀ bodhi ǀ sákhā ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ indra ǀ stuvaté ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǀvayám ǀ hí ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ cakṛmá ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ ābhíḥ ǀ śámībhiḥ ǀ maháyantaḥ ǀ indra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Regard yourself as a protector of those who desire your friendship; be a friend deserving of commendation; grant,Indra, food to him who praises (you); suffering difficulties, we make our suppications to you, worshipping you with these holy rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Regard yourself as a protector of those who desire your friendship; be a friend deserving of commendation; grant,Indra, food to him who praises (you); suffering difficulties, we make our suppications to you, worshipping you with these holy rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तुत इंद्रो मघवा यद्ध वृत्रा भूरीण्येको अप्रतीनि हंति ।अस्य प्रियो जरिता यस्य शर��मन्नकिर्देवा वारयंते न मर्ताः ॥
verses.transliteration: stutáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ bhū́rīṇi ǀ ékaḥ ǀ apratī́ni ǀ hanti ǀasyá ǀ priyáḥ ǀ jaritā́ ǀ yásya ǀ śárman ǀ nákiḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vāráyante ǀ ná ǀ mártāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Indra, the possessor of opulence, is glorified, he singly destroys many unyielding foes; the worshipper is dear to him (who relies) on his protection, and neither gods nor men molest him.
verses.wilson_translation: When Indra, the possessor of opulence, is glorified, he singly destroys many unyielding foes; the worshipper is dear to him (who relies) on his protection, and neither gods nor men molest him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा न इंद्रो मघवा विरप्शी करत्सत्या चर्षणीधृदनर्वा ।त्वं राजा जनुषां धेह्यस्मे अधि श्रवो माहिनं यज्जरित्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vi-rapśī́ ǀ kárat ǀ satyā́ ǀ carṣaṇi-dhṛ́t ǀ anarvā́ ǀtvám ǀ rā́jā ǀ janúṣām ǀ dhehi ǀ asmé íti ǀ ádhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ mā́hinam ǀ yát ǀ jaritré ǁ
verses.english_translation: The many-voiced Indra, the possessor of opulence, the supporter of men, the irresistible bestows upon us, when praised by us, assured (rewards); you, (Indra), are the king of men; grant to us abundantly that great fame which (is due) to (your) worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: The many-voiced Indra, the possessor of opulence, the supporter of men, the irresistible bestows upon us, when praised by us, assured (rewards); you, (Indra), are the king of men; grant to us abundantly that great fame which (is due) to (your) worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XVIII. Indra and Others.
hymns.anukramani: १३ वामदेवो गौतमः, १ इन्द्रः,४ (उत्तरार्धर्चस्य), ७ अदितिः। १ वामदेवः, २-४ (पूर्वार्धर्चस्य), ८-१३ इन्द्रः,(उत्तरार्धर्चस्य), ७ वामदेवः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS is the ancient and accepted pathway by which all Gods have come into existence.Hereby could one be born though waxen mighty. Let him not, otherwise, destroy his Mother. Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue.Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question. He bent his eye upon the dying Mother: My word I now withdraw. That way I follow.In Tvaṣṭar's dwelling India drank the Soma, a hundredworth of juice pressed from the mortar. What strange act shall he do, he whom his Mother bore for a thousand months and many autumns?No peer hath he among those born already, nor among those who shall be born hereafter. Deeming him a reproach, his mother hid him, Indra, endowed with all heroic valour.Then up he sprang himself, assumed his vesture, and filled, as soon as born, the earth and heaven. With lively motion onward flow these waters, the Holy Ones, shouting, as ’twere, together.Ask them to. tell thee what the floods are saying, what girdling rock the waters burst asunder. Are they addressing him with words of welcome? Will the floods take on them the shame of Indra?With his great thunderbolt my Son hath slaughtered Vṛtra, and set these rivers free to wander. I cast thee from me, mine,—thy youthful mother: thee, mine own offspring, Kusava hath swallowed.To him, mine infant, were the waters gracious. Indra, my Son, rose up in conquering vigour. Thou art mine own, O Maghavan, whom Vyaṁsa struck to the ground and smote thy jaws in pieces.But, smitten through, the mastery thou wonnest, and with thy bolt the Dāsa's head thou crushedst. The Heifer hath brought forth the Strong, the Mighty, the unconquerable Bull, the furious Indra.The Mother left her unlicked Calf to wander, seeking himself, the path that he would follow. Then to her mighty Child the Mother turned her, saying, My son, these Deities forsake thee.Then Indra said, about to slaughter Vṛtra, O my friend Vṛtra, stride full boldly forward. Who was he then who made thy Mother widow? Who sought to stay thee lying still or moving?What God, when by the foot thy Sire thou tookest and slewest, was at hand to give thee comfort? In deep distress I cooked a dog's intestines. Among the Gods I found not one to comfort.My consort I beheld in degradation. The Falcon then brought me the pleasant Soma.

verses.sanskrit: अयं पंथा अनुवित्तः पुराणो यतो देवा उदजायंत विश्वे ।अतश्चिदा जनिषीष्ट प्रवृद्धो मा मातरममुया पत्तवे कः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ ánu-vittaḥ ǀ purāṇáḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ut-ájāyanta ǀ víśve ǀátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ janiṣīṣṭa ǀ prá-vṛddhaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ mātáram ǀ amuyā́ ǀ páttave ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraspeaks: This is the old and recognized path by which all the gods are born; so, when full-grown, let him be born in the same manner; let him not cause the loss of this his mother.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraspeaks: This is the old and recognized path by which all the gods are born; so, when full-grown, let him be born in the same manner; let him not cause the loss of this his mother.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नाहमतो निरया दुर्गहैतत्तिरश्चता पार्श्वान्निर्गमाणि ।बहूनि मे अकृता कर्त्वानि युध्यै त्वेन सं त्वेन पृच्छै ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ átaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ aya ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǀ etát ǀ tiraścátā ǀ pārśvā́t ǀ níḥ ǀ gamāni ǀbahū́ni ǀ me ǀ ákṛtā ǀ kártvāni ǀ yúdhyai ǀ tvena ǀ sám ǀ tvena ǀ pṛcchai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāmadevaspeaks: Let me not come forth by this path, for it is difficult (of issue); let me come forth obliquely from the side; many acts unperformed by others are to be accomplished by me; let me contend (in war) with one (enemy), in controversy with one opponent.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāmadevaspeaks: Let me not come forth by this path, for it is difficult (of issue); let me come forth obliquely from the side; many acts unperformed by others are to be accomplished by me; let me contend (in war) with one (enemy), in controversy with one opponent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परायतीं मातरमन्वचष्ट न नानु गान्यनु नू गमानि ।त्वष्टुर्गृहे अपिबत्सोममिंद्रः शतधन्यं चम्वोः सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: parā-yatī́m ǀ mātáram ǀ ánu ǀ acaṣṭa ǀ ná ǀ ná ǀ ánu ǀ gāni ǀ ánu ǀ nú ǀ gamāni ǀtváṣṭuḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀ apibat ǀ sómam ǀ índraḥ ǀ śata-dhanyám ǀ camvóḥ ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, (Indra), has asserted (that it will) cause the death of my mother; let me not proceed by the usual way, but proceed quickly, according (to my will); in the dwelling of TvaṣṭāIndra drank the costly Somafrom the vessels of the offerers.
verses.wilson_translation: He, (Indra), has asserted (that it will) cause the death of my mother; let me not proceed by the usual way, but proceed quickly, according (to my will); in the dwelling of TvaṣṭāIndra drank the costly Somafrom the vessels of the offerers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किं स ऋधक्कृणवद्यं सहस्रं मासो जभार शरदश्च पूर्वीः ।नही न्वस्य प्रतिमानमस्त्यंतर्जातेषूत ये जनित्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ kṛṇavat ǀ yám ǀ sahásram ǀ māsáḥ ǀ jabhā́ra ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀnahí ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ ásti ǀ antáḥ ǀ jātéṣu ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ jáni-tvāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aditispeaks: What irregular act has he committed whom (I, his mother), bore for a thousand months and for many years? there is no analogy between him and those who have been or will be born.
verses.wilson_translation: Aditispeaks: What irregular act has he committed whom (I, his mother), bore for a thousand months and for many years? there is no analogy between him and those who have been or will be born.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवद्यमिव मन्यमाना गुहाकरिंद्रं माता वीर्येणा न्यृष्टं ।अथोदस्थात्स्वयमत्कं वसान आ रोदसी अपृणाज्जायमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: avadyám-iva ǀ mányamānā ǀ gúhā ǀ akaḥ ǀ índram ǀ mātā́ ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ ní-ṛṣṭam ǀátha ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǀ svayám ǀ átkam ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ apṛṇāt ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Deeming it disreputable (that he should be brought forth) in secret, his mother endowed (Indra) with (extraordinary) vigour; therefore, as soon as born he sprung up of his own accord, invested with splendour, and filled both heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Deeming it disreputable (that he should be brought forth) in secret, his mother endowed (Indra) with (extraordinary) vigour; therefore, as soon as born he sprung up of his own accord, invested with splendour, and filled both heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एता अर्षंत्यललाभवंतीर्ऋतावरीरिव संक्रोशमानाः ।एता वि पृच्छ किमिदं भनंति कमापो अद्रिं परिधिं रुजंति ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ḥ ǀ arṣanti ǀ alalā-bhávantīḥ ǀ ṛtávarīḥ-iva ǀ sam-króśamānāḥ ǀetā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ pṛccha ǀ kím ǀ idám ǀ bhananti ǀ kám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ádrim ǀ pari-dhím ǀ rujanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: These (rivers) flew murmuring as if, being filled with water, they were uttering sounds (of joy); ask them what is this they say; what is the encompassing cloud that the waters break through?
verses.wilson_translation: These (rivers) flew murmuring as if, being filled with water, they were uttering sounds (of joy); ask them what is this they say; what is the encompassing cloud that the waters break through?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किमु ष्विदस्मै निविदो भनंतेंद्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषंत आपः ।ममैतान्पुत्रो महता वधेन वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजद्वि सिंधून् ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svit ǀ asmai ǀ ni-vídaḥ ǀ bhananta ǀ índrasya ǀ avadyám ǀ didhiṣante ǀ ā́paḥ ǀmáma ǀ etā́n ǀ putráḥ ǀ mahatā́ ǀ vadhéna ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ asṛjat ǀ ví ǀ síndhūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: What do the sacred expiatory strains declare to me? the waters reeive the reproach of Indra; my son has slain Vṛtrawith the mighty thunderbolt; he has set those rivers free.
verses.wilson_translation: What do the sacred expiatory strains declare to me? the waters reeive the reproach of Indra; my son has slain Vṛtrawith the mighty thunderbolt; he has set those rivers free.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ममच्चन त्वा युवतिः परास ममच्चन त्वा कुषवा जगार ।ममच्चिदापः शिशवे ममृड्युर्ममच्चिदिंद्रः सहसोदतिष्ठत् ॥
verses.transliteration: mámat ǀ caná ǀ tvā ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ parā-ā́sa ǀ mámat ǀ caná ǀ tvā ǀ kuṣávā ǀ jagā́ra ǀmámat ǀ cit ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ śíśave ǀ mamṛḍyuḥ ǀ mámat ǀ cit ǀ índraḥ ǀ sáhasā ǀ út ǀ atiṣṭhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāmadevaspeaks: exulting one youthful mother brought you forth; exulting, Kuṣavā swallowed you; exulting, the waters gave delight to the infant;Indra, exulting, rose up by his strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāmadevaspeaks: exulting one youthful mother brought you forth; exulting, Kuṣavā swallowed you; exulting, the waters gave delight to the infant;Indra, exulting, rose up by his strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ममच्चन ते मघवन्व्यंसो निविविध्वाँ अप हनू जघान ।अधा निविद्ध उत्तरो बभूवाञ्छिरो दासस्य सं पिणग्वधेन ॥
verses.transliteration: mámat ǀ caná ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ ví-aṃsaḥ ǀ ni-vividhvā́n ǀ ápa ǀ hánū íti ǀ jaghā́na ǀádha ǀ ní-viddhaḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǀ babhūvā́n ǀ śíraḥ ǀ dāsásya ǀ sám ǀ piṇak ǀ vadhéna ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vyaṃsa, exulting and striking (hard blows), smote you,Maghavan, upon the jaw; whereupon, being so smitten, you proved the stronger, and did crush the head of the slave with the thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Vyaṃsa, exulting and striking (hard blows), smote you,Maghavan, upon the jaw; whereupon, being so smitten, you proved the stronger, and did crush the head of the slave with the thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गृष्टिः ससूव स्थविरं तवागामनाधृष्यं वृषभं तुम्रमिंद्रं ।अरीळ्हं वत्सं चरथाय माता स्वयं गातुं तन्व इच्छमानं ॥
verses.transliteration: gṛṣṭíḥ ǀ sasūva ǀ stháviram ǀ tavāgā́m ǀ anādhṛṣyám ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ túmram ǀ índram ǀárīḷham ǀ vatsám ǀ caráthāya ǀ mātā́ ǀ svayám ǀ gātúm ǀ tanvé ǀ icchámānam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As a helper bears a calf, his mother, (Aditi), bore Indra, mature (in years), strong, irresisitble, vigorous, energetic, invincible, (destined) to follow his own course, heedful of his person n.
verses.wilson_translation: As a helper bears a calf, his mother, (Aditi), bore Indra, mature (in years), strong, irresisitble, vigorous, energetic, invincible, (destined) to follow his own course, heedful of his person n.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत माता महिषमन्ववेनदमी त्वा जहति पुत्र देवाः ।अथाब्रवीद्वृत्रमिंद्रो हनिष्यन्त्सखे विष्णो वितरं वि क्रमस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ mātā́ ǀ mahiṣám ǀ ánu ǀ avenat ǀ amī́ íti ǀ tvā ǀ jahati ǀ putra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀátha ǀ abravīt ǀ vṛtrám ǀ índraḥ ǀ haniṣyán ǀ sákhe ǀ viṣṇo íti ǀ vi-tarám ǀ ví ǀ kramasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: His mother inquired of the mighty Indra, have these deities deserted you, my son? then Indra and Viṣṇu, my friend (if you) purpose slaying Vṛtraexert your greatest prowess.
verses.wilson_translation: His mother inquired of the mighty Indra, have these deities deserted you, my son? then Indra and Viṣṇu, my friend (if you) purpose slaying Vṛtraexert your greatest prowess.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कस्ते मातरं विधवामचक्रच्छयुं कस्त्वामजिघांसच्चरंतं ।कस्ते देवो अधि मार्डीक आसीद्यत्प्राक्षिणाः पितरं पादगृह्य ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ te ǀ mātáram ǀ vidhávām ǀ acakrat ǀ śayúm ǀ káḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ ajighāṃsat ǀ cárantam ǀkáḥ ǀ te ǀ deváḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ mārḍīké ǀ āsīt ǀ yát ǀ prá ǀ ákṣiṇāḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ pāda-gṛ́hya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who has made your mother a widow? who has sought to slay the sleeping and the walking? what deity has been more gracious than you since you have slain the father, having seized him by the foot?
verses.wilson_translation: Who has made your mother a widow? who has sought to slay the sleeping and the walking? what deity has been more gracious than you since you have slain the father, having seized him by the foot?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवर्त्या शुन आंत्राणि पेचे न देवेषु विविदे मर्डितारं ।अपश्यं जायाममहीयमानामधा मे श्येनो मध्वा जभार ॥
verses.transliteration: ávartyā ǀ śúnaḥ ǀ āntrā́ṇi ǀ pece ǀ ná ǀ devéṣu ǀ vivide ǀ marḍitā́ram ǀápaśyam ǀ jāyā́m ǀ ámahīyamānām ǀ ádha ǀ me ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́ ǀ jabhāra ǁ
verses.english_translation: In extreme destitution I have cooked the entrails of a dog; I have not found a comforter among the gods; I have beheld my wife disrsepected; then the falcon, (Indra), has brought to me sweet water.
verses.wilson_translation: In extreme destitution I have cooked the entrails of a dog; I have not found a comforter among the gods; I have beheld my wife disrsepected; then the falcon, (Indra), has brought to me sweet water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THEE, verily, O Thunder-wielding Indra, all the Gods here, the Helpers swift to listen,And both the worlds elected, thee the Mighty, High, waxen strong, alone to slaughter Vṛtra. The Gods, as worn witheld, relaxed their efforts: thou, Indra, born of truth, wast Sovran Ruler.Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and duggest out their all-supporting channels. The insatiate one, extended, hard to waken, who slumbered in perpetual sleep, O Indra,—The Dragon stretched against the seven prone rivers, where no joint was, thou rentest with thy thunder. Indra with might shook earth and her foundation as the wind stirs the water with its fury.Striving, with strength he burst the firm asunder, and tore away the summits of the mountains. They ran to thee as mothers to their offspring: the clouds, like chariots, hastened forth together.Thou didst refresh the streams and force the billows: thou, Indra, settest free obstructed rivers. Thou for the sake of Vayya and Turvīti didst stay the great stream, flowing, all-sustaining:Yea, at their prayer didst check the rushing river and make the floods easy to cross, O Indra. He let the young Maids skilled in Law, unwedded, like fountains, bubbling, flow forth streaming onward.He inundated thirsty plains and deserts, and milked the dry Cows of the mighty master. Through many a morn and many a lovely autumn, having slain Vṛtra, he set free the rivers.Indra hath set at liberty to wander on earth the streams encompassed pressed together. Lord of Bay Steeds, thou broughtest from the ant-hill the unwedded damsel's son whom ants were eating.The blind saw clearly, as he grasped the serpent, rose, brake the jar: his joints again united. To the wise man, O Sage and Sovran Ruler, the man who knoweth all thine ancient exploits.Hath told these deeds of might as thou hast wrought them, great acts, spontaneous, and to man's advantage. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let powers swell high, like rivers, for the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: एवा त्वामिंद्र वज्रिन्नत्र विश्वे देवासः सुहवास ऊमाः ।महामुभे रोदसी वृद्धमृष्वं निरेकमिद्वृणते वृत्रहत्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ vajrin ǀ átra ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ su-hávāsaḥ ǀ ū́māḥ ǀmahā́m ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vṛddhám ǀ ṛṣvám ǀ níḥ ǀ ékam ǀ ít ǀ gṛṇate ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, wielder of the thuderbolt, all the protecting deities who are reverently invoked, and both the heaven and the earth, glorify you who are verily one alone, mighty, vast, and plural asing of aspect, for the destruction of Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, wielder of the thuderbolt, all the protecting deities who are reverently invoked, and both the heaven and the earth, glorify you who are verily one alone, mighty, vast, and plural asing of aspect, for the destruction of Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवासृजंत जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळिंद्र सत्ययोनिः ।अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्णः प्र वर्तनीररदो विश्वधेनाः ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ asṛjanta ǀ jívrayaḥ ǀ ná �� devā́ḥ ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ indra ǀ satyá-yoniḥ ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ pari-śáyānam ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ vartanī́ḥ ǀ aradaḥ ǀ viśvá-dhenāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As elders (send forth their young), so the gods have sent you (against Vṛtra); thence you became,Indrawho is the abode of truth, the soverign of the world; you have slain the slumbering Ahi for (the release of) the water and have marked out (the channels of) all the delighting rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: As elders (send forth their young), so the gods have sent you (against Vṛtra); thence you became,Indrawho is the abode of truth, the soverign of the world; you have slain the slumbering Ahi for (the release of) the water and have marked out (the channels of) all the delighting rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अतृप्णुवंतं वियतमबुध्यमबुध्यमानं सुषुपाणमिंद्र ।सप्त प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण वि रिणा अपर्वन् ॥
verses.transliteration: átṛpṇuvantam ǀ ví-yatam ǀ abudhyám ǀ ábudhyamānam ǀ susupānám ǀ indra ǀsaptá ǀ práti ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ā-śáyānam ǀ áhim ǀ vájreṇa ǀ ví ǀ riṇāḥ ǀ aparván ǁ
verses.english_translation: On the day of full moon you have slain with the thunderbolt the insatiable, unnerved, ignorant, unapprehending, slumbering Ahi, obstructing the gliding-downward-flowing (streams).
verses.wilson_translation: On the day of full moon you have slain with the thunderbolt the insatiable, unnerved, ignorant, unapprehending, slumbering Ahi, obstructing the gliding-downward-flowing (streams).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षोदयच्छवसा क्षाम बुध्नं वार्ण वातस्तविषीभिरिंद्रः ।दृळ्हान्यौभ्नादुशमान ओजोऽवाभिनत्ककुभः पर्वतानां ॥
verses.transliteration: ákṣodayat ǀ śávasā ǀ kṣā́ma ǀ budhnám ǀ vā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀdṛḷhā́ni ǀ aubhnāt ǀ uśámānaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ áva ǀ abhinat ǀ kakúbhaḥ ǀ párvatānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, by his strength, has agitated the exhausted firmament, as wind, by its violent (gusts, agitates) the water; exulting in his strength, he has divided the solid (clouds), and has shattered the peaks of the mountains.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, by his strength, has agitated the exhausted firmament, as wind, by its violent (gusts, agitates) the water; exulting in his strength, he has divided the solid (clouds), and has shattered the peaks of the mountains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि प्र दद्रुर्जनयो न गर्भं रथा इव प्र ययुः साकमद्रयः ।अतर्पयो विसृत उब्ज ऊर्मींत्वं वृताँ अरिणा इंद्र सिंधून् ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ prá ǀ dadruḥ ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ gárbham ǀ ráthāḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ yayuḥ ǀ sākám ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀátarpayaḥ ǀ vi-sṛ́taḥ ǀ ubjáḥ ǀ ūrmī́n ǀ tvám ǀ vṛtā́n ǀ ariṇāḥ ǀ indra ǀ síndhūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Marutshave hastened to you like mother to their young; like chariots they have rushed in along (with you); you,Indra, have satisfied the following streams; you have shattered the clouds; you have set free the obstructed rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: The Marutshave hastened to you like mother to their young; like chariots they have rushed in along (with you); you,Indra, have satisfied the following streams; you have shattered the clouds; you have set free the obstructed rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं महीमवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय क्षरंतीं ।अरमयो नमसैजदर्णः सुतरणाँ अकृणोरिंद्र सिंधून् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ mahī́m ǀ avánim ǀ viśvá-dhenām ǀ turvī́taye ǀ vayyā́ya ǀ kṣárantīm ǀáramayaḥ ǀ námasā ǀ éjat ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ su-taraṇā́n ǀ akṛṇoḥ ǀ indra ǀ síndhūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have made the vast, all-cherishing, and exuberant earth, delighted with (abundant) food, and tremulous water, for (the sake of)Turvītiand Vayyā; you have made the rivers easy to be crosseḍ
verses.wilson_translation: You have made the vast, all-cherishing, and exuberant earth, delighted with (abundant) food, and tremulous water, for (the sake of)Turvītiand Vayyā; you have made the rivers easy to be crosseḍ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्राग्रुवो नभन्वो न वक्वा ध्वस्रा अपिन्वद्युवतीर्ऋतज्ञाः ।धन्वान्यज्राँ अपृणक्तृषाणाँ अधोगिंद्रः स्तर्यो दंसुपत्नीः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ nabhanváḥ ǀ ná ǀ vákvāḥ ǀ dhvasrā́ḥ ǀ apinvat ǀ yuvatī́ḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀdhánvāni ǀ ájrān ǀ apṛṇak ǀ tṛṣāṇā́n ǀ ádhok ǀ índraḥ ǀ staryáḥ ǀ dáṃ-supatnīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrahas filled the youthful rivers, the parents of plural nty, the corroders (of their banks), like  armies destructive (of their foes); he has inundated the dry lands, and (satisfied) the thirsty travellers; he has milked the barren cows whom theasurashad become the lords of.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas filled the youthful rivers, the parents of plural nty, the corroders (of their banks), like  armies destructive (of their foes); he has inundated the dry lands, and (satisfied) the thirsty travellers; he has milked the barren cows whom theasurashad become the lords of.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वीरुषसः शरदश्च गूर्ता वृत्रं जघन्वाँ असृजद्वि सिंधून् ।परिष्ठिता अतृणद्बद्बधानाः सीरा इंद्रः स्रवितवे पृथिव्या ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrvī́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ gūrtā́ḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ asṛjat ǀ ví ǀ síndhūn ǀpári-sthitāḥ ǀ atṛṇat ǀ badbadhānā́ḥ ǀ sīrā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ srávitave ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Having slain Vṛtra, he has liberated many mornings and years (that had been) swallowed up by darkness, and has set the rivers free;Indrahas released the imprisoned rivers, encompassed (by the cloud), to flow upon the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Having slain Vṛtra, he has liberated many mornings and years (that had been) swallowed up by darkness, and has set the rivers free;Indrahas released the imprisoned rivers, encompassed (by the cloud), to flow upon the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वम्रीभिः पुत्रमग्रुवो अदानं निवेशनाद्धरिव आ जभर्थ ।व्यंधो अख्यदहिमाददानो निर्भूदुखच्छित्समरंत पर्व ॥
verses.transliteration: vamrī́bhiḥ ǀ putrám ǀ agrúvaḥ ǀ adānám ǀ ni-véśanāt ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jabhartha ǀví ǀ andháḥ ǀ akhyat ǀ áhim ǀ ā-dadānáḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ bhūt ǀ ukha-chít ǀ sám ǀ aranta ǀ párva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of horses, you have brought the son of Agru from his dwelling, where he was being devoured by the ants; when extricated, although blind, he distinguished the serpent; and when he came forth the joints that had been sundered in the ant-hill were restrung.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of horses, you have brought the son of Agru from his dwelling, where he was being devoured by the ants; when extricated, although blind, he distinguished the serpent; and when he came forth the joints that had been sundered in the ant-hill were restrung.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते पूर्वाणि करणानि विप्राविद्वाँ आह विदुषे करांसि ।यथायथा वृष्ण्यानि स्वगूर्तापांसि राजन्नर्याविवेषीः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ pū́rvāṇi ǀ káraṇāni ǀ vipra ǀ ā-vidvā́n ǀ āha ǀ vidúṣe ǀ kárāṃsi ǀyáthā-yathā ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyāni ǀ svá-gūrtā ǀ ápāṃsi ǀ rājan ǀ náryā ǀ áviveṣīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sage, (Vāmadeva), knowing, royal Indra, the ancient deeds of you who are all wise, has proclaimed the actions, such as you ahve performed them, genitive rative of rain, self-evolved, and beneficial to man.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage, (Vāmadeva), knowing, royal Indra, the ancient deeds of you who are all wise, has proclaimed the actions, such as you ahve performed them, genitive rative of rain, self-evolved, and beneficial to man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FROM near or far away may mighty Indra giver of succour, come for our protectionLord of men, armed with thunder, with the Strongest, slaying his foes in conflict, in the battles. May Indra come to us with Tawny Coursers, inclined to us, to favour and enrich us.May Maghavan, loud-voiced and wielding thunder, stand by us at this sacrifice, in combat. Thou, honouring this our sacrifice, O Indra, shalt give us strength and fill us full of courage.To win the booty, Thunder-armed! like hunters may we with thee subdue in fight our foemen. Loving us well, benevolent, close beside us, drink, Godlike Indra, of the well-pressed Soma.Drink of the meath we offer, and delight thee with food that cometh from the mountain ridges. Him who is sung aloud by recent sages, like a ripe-fruited tree, a scythe-armed victor,—I, like a bridegroom thinking of his consort, call hither Indra, him invoked of many; Him who in native strength is like a mountain, the lofty Indra born or old for conquest,Terrific wielder of the ancient thunder. filled full with splendour as a jar with water. Whom from of old there is not one to hinder, none to curtail the riches of his bounty.Pouring forth freely, O thou Strong and Mighty, vouchsafe us riches, God invoked of many! Of wealth and homes of men thou art the ruler, and opener of the stable of the cattle.Helper of men, winner of spoil in combats, thou leadest to an ample heap of riches. By what great might is he renowned as strongest, wherewith the Lofty One stirs up wild battles?Best soother of the worshipper's great sorrow, he gives possessions to the man who lauds him. Slay us not; bring, bestow onus the ample gift which thou hast to give to him who offers.At this new gift, with this laud sung before thee, extolling thee, we, Indra, will declare it. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.A new hymn, Lord of Bays! for thee is fashioned. May we, car-born, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: आ न इंद्रो दूरादा न आसादभिष्टिकृदवसे यासदुग्रः ।ओजिष्ठेभिर्नृपतिर्वज्रबाहुः संगे समत्सु तुर्वणिः पृतन्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ dūrā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ āsā́t ǀ abhiṣṭi-kṛ́t ǀ ávase ǀ yāsat ǀ ugráḥ ǀójiṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ nṛ-pátiḥ ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǀ sam-gé ǀ samát-su ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀ pṛtanyū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the illustrious Indra, the granter of desires, come to us, whether from afar or nigh, for our protection; he who is the lord of men, armed with the thunderbolt, overcoming his foes in conflict and in combats, (attended) by the most illustrious (Maruts).
verses.wilson_translation: May the illustrious Indra, the granter of desires, come to us, whether from afar or nigh, for our protection; he who is the lord of men, armed with the thunderbolt, overcoming his foes in conflict and in combats, (attended) by the most illustrious (Maruts).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ न इंद्रो हरिभिर्यात्वच्छार्वाचीनोऽवसे राधसे च ।तिष्ठाति वज्री मघवा विरप्शीमं यज्ञमनु नो वाजसातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ yātu ǀ áccha ǀ arvācīnáḥ ǀ ávase ǀ rā́dhase ǀ ca ǀtíṣṭhāti ǀ vajrī́ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vi-rapśī́ ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ ánu ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra, looking down upon us, come with his steeds to our presence for our protection and enrichment; may the mighty thunderer, the possessor of wealth, (aiding us) in battle, be present at this our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, looking down upon us, come with his steeds to our presence for our protection and enrichment; may the mighty thunderer, the possessor of wealth, (aiding us) in battle, be present at this our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं यज्ञं त्वमस्माकमिंद्र पुरो दधत्सनिष्यसि क्रतुं नः ।श्वघ्नीव वज्रिन्त्सनये धनानां त्वया वयमर्य आजिं जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ yajñám ǀ tvám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ indra ǀ puráḥ ǀ dádhat ǀ saniṣyasi ǀ krátum ǀ naḥ ǀśvaghnī́-iva ǀ vajrin ǀ sanáye ǀ dhánānām ǀ tváyā ǀ vayám ǀ aryáḥ ǀ ājím ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Indra, plural cing us before you, shall receive this sacrifice, our holy offering; and as the huntsman (kills his game), may we, your worshippers, holder of the thunderbolt, for the acquisition of riches through you to be victorious in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, plural cing us before you, shall receive this sacrifice, our holy offering; and as the huntsman (kills his game), may we, your worshippers, holder of the thunderbolt, for the acquisition of riches through you to be victorious in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उशन्नु षु णः सुमना उपाके सोमस्य नु सुषुतस्य स्वधावः ।पा इंद्र प्रतिभृतस्य मध्वः समंधसा ममदः पृष्ठ्येन ॥
verses.transliteration: uśán ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ upāké ǀ sómasya ǀ nú ǀ sú-sutasya ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀpā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ práti-bhṛtasya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ándhasā ǀ mamadaḥ ǀ pṛṣṭhyéna ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the giver of food, be near to us, favourably disposed; and anxious for our (good), drink of the effused, prepared, exhilarating Soma, and be plural ased by the (sacrificial) food (offered with the noon-day hymn.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the giver of food, be near to us, favourably disposed; and anxious for our (good), drink of the effused, prepared, exhilarating Soma, and be plural ased by the (sacrificial) food (offered with the noon-day hymn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि यो ररप्श ऋषिभिर्नवेभिर्वृक्षो न पक्वः सृण्यो न जेता ।मर्यो न योषामभि मन्यमानोऽच्छा विवक्मि पुरुहूतमिंद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yáḥ ǀ rarápśé ǀ ṛ́ṣi-bhiḥ ǀ návebhiḥ ǀ vṛkṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pakváḥ ǀ sṛ́ṇyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ jétā ǀmáryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóṣām ǀ abhí ǀ mányamānaḥ ǀ áccha ǀ vivakmi ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ índram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a man boasting of his wife, I glorify that Indrawho is invoked of many, who is hymned by recent sages (who is) like a tree with ripe fruit, like a victorious (warrior), skilful in arms.
verses.wilson_translation: Like a man boasting of his wife, I glorify that Indrawho is invoked of many, who is hymned by recent sages (who is) like a tree with ripe fruit, like a victorious (warrior), skilful in arms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गिरिर्न यः स्वतवाँ ऋष्व इंद्रः सनादेव सहसे जात उग्रः ।आदर्ता वज्रं स्थविरं न भीम उद्नेव कोशं वसुना न्यृष्टं ॥
verses.transliteration: giríḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ svá-tavān ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ sanā́t ǀ evá ǀ sáhase ǀ jātáḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀā́-dartā ǀ vájram ǀ stháviram ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ udnā́-iva ǀ kóśam ǀ vásunā ǀ ní-ṛṣṭam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is vast and self-sustained like a mountain, the radiant and formidable Indra, born of old for the destruction (of the foes of the gods), the wielder of the ancient thunderbolt, charged with splendour, like a jar (filled) with water.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is vast and self-sustained like a mountain, the radiant and formidable Indra, born of old for the destruction (of the foes of the gods), the wielder of the ancient thunderbolt, charged with splendour, like a jar (filled) with water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्य वर्ता जनुषा न्वस्ति न राधस आमरीता मघस्य ।उद्वावृषाणस्तविषीव उग्रास्मभ्यं दद्धि पुरुहूत रायः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ vartā́ ǀ janúṣā ǀ nú ǀ ásti ǀ ná ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ ā-marītā́ ǀ maghásya ǀut-vavṛṣāṇáḥ ǀ taviṣī-vaḥ ǀ ugra ǀ asmábhyam ǀ daddhi ǀ puru-hūta ǀ rāyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of whom there is no opposer by (reason of) his birth nor any destroyer of the wealth that accomplishes (pious works); powerful and resplendent (Indra), the invoked of many, do you who are the showerer (of benefits) bestow upon us riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom there is no opposer by (reason of) his birth nor any destroyer of the wealth that accomplishes (pious works); powerful and resplendent (Indra), the invoked of many, do you who are the showerer (of benefits) bestow upon us riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईक्षे रायः क्षयस्य चर्षणीनामुत व��रजमपवर्तासि गोनां ।शिक्षानरः समिथेषु प्रहावान्वस्वो राशिमभिनेतासि भूरिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ī́kṣe ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ kṣáyasya ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ utá ǀ vrajám ǀ apa-vartā́ ǀ asi ǀ gónām ǀśikṣā-naráḥ ǀ sam-ithéṣu ǀ prahā́-vān ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ rāśím ǀ abhi-netā́ ǀ asi ǀ bhū́rim ǁ
verses.english_translation: You rule over the riches and the dwellings of men; you are the rescuer of the herd of cattle; you are the giver of the instrumental uction, the smiter in battles, and the distributor of great heaps of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: You rule over the riches and the dwellings of men; you are the rescuer of the herd of cattle; you are the giver of the instrumental uction, the smiter in battles, and the distributor of great heaps of riches.

verses.sanskrit: कया तच्छृण्वे शच्या शचिष्ठो यया कृणोति मुहु का चिदृष्वः ।पुरु दाशुषे विचयिष्ठो अंहोऽथा दधाति द्रविणं जरित्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: káyā ǀ tát ǀ śṛṇve ǀ śácyā ǀ śáciṣṭhaḥ ǀ yáyā ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ múhu ǀ kā́ ǀ cit ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀpurú ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ ví-cayiṣṭhaḥ ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ átha ǀ dadhāti ǀ dráviṇam ǀ jaritré ǁ
verses.english_translation: By what wisdom is he who is most wise renowned by that wherewith the mighty Indrarepeatedly does (great things); he is the especial effacer of the manifold sin of the worshipper, and bestows wealth upon his adorer.
verses.wilson_translation: By what wisdom is he who is most wise renowned by that wherewith the mighty Indrarepeatedly does (great things); he is the especial effacer of the manifold sin of the worshipper, and bestows wealth upon his adorer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो मर्धीरा भरा दद्धि तन्नः प्र दाशुषे दातवे भूरि यत्ते ।नव्ये देष्णे शस्ते अस्मिंत उक्थे प्र ब्रवाम वयमिंद्र स्तुवंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mardhīḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ daddhí ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ prá ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ dā́tave ǀ bhū́ri ǀ yát ǀ te ǀnávye ǀ deṣṇé ǀ śasté ǀ asmín ǀ te ǀ ukthé ǀ prá ǀ bravāma ǀ vayám ǀ indra ǀ stuvántaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harm us not, but cherish us,Indra; bestow upon us that abundant wealth which it is yours to give to the donor (of the oblation); praising you, we celebrate you at this sacred rite, which is new and excellent, and (at which the oblation) is proper to be presented.
verses.wilson_translation: Harm us not, but cherish us,Indra; bestow upon us that abundant wealth which it is yours to give to the donor (of the oblation); praising you, we celebrate you at this sacred rite, which is new and excellent, and (at which the oblation) is proper to be presented.
