hymns.title: HYMN XXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY Indra come to us for our protection; here be the Hero, praised, our feast-companion.May he whose powers are many, waxen mighty, cherish, like Dyaus, his own supreme dominion. Here magnify his great heroic exploits, most glorious One, enriching men with bounties,Whose will is like a Sovran in assembly, who rules the people, Conqueror, all-surpassing. Hither let Indra come from earth or heaven, hither with speech from firmament or ocean;With Maruts, from the realm of light to aid us, or from a distance, from the seat of Order. That Indra will we laud in our assemblies, him who is Lord of great and lasting riches,Victor with Vāyu where the herds are gathered, who leads with boldness on to higher fortune. May the Priest, Lord of many blessings, striving,—who fixing reverence on reverence, givingVent to his voice, inciteth men to worship—with lauds bring Indra hither to our dwellings. When sitting pondering in deep devotion in Auśija's abode they ply the press-stone,May he whose wrath is fierce, the mighty bearer, come as the house-lord's priest within our chambers. Surely the power of Bhārvara the mighty for ever helpeth to support the singer;That which in Auśija's abode lies hidden, to come forth for delight and for devotion. When he unbars the spaces of the mountains, and quickens with his floods the water-torrents,He finds in lair the buffalo and wild-ox when the wise lead him on to vigorous exploit. Auspicious are thy hands, thine arms well-fashioned which proffer bounty, Indra, to thy praiser.What sloth is this? Why dost thou not rejoice thee? Why dost thou not delight thyself with giving? So Indra is the truthful Lord of treasure. Freedom he gave to man by slaying Vṛtra.Much-lauded! help us with thy power to riches: may I be sharer of thy Godlike favour. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let power swell high, like rivers, for the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays! is fashioned. May we, care-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: आ यात्विंद्रोऽवस उप न इह स्तुतः सधमादस्तु शूरः ।वावृधानस्तविषीर्यस्य पूर्वीर्द्यौर्न क्षत्रमभिभूति पुष्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yātu ǀ índraḥ ǀ ávase ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ ihá ǀ stutáḥ ǀ sadha-mā́t ǀ astu ǀ śū́raḥ ǀvavṛdhānáḥ ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ yásya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣatrám ǀ abhí-bhūti ǀ púṣyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indracome to us for protection, and being praised (by us), may the mighty hero be exhilarated along with (us) at this rite; he whose energies are many; may he, like the radiant sun, recruit his own overpowering vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indracome to us for protection, and being praised (by us), may the mighty hero be exhilarated along with (us) at this rite; he whose energies are many; may he, like the radiant sun, recruit his own overpowering vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तस्येदिह स्तवथ वृष्ण्यानि तुविद्युम्नस्य तुविराधसो नॄन् ।यस्य क्रतुर्विदथ्यो न सम्राट् साह्वाँ तरुत्रो अभ्यस्ति कृष्टीः ॥
verses.transliteration: tásya ǀ ít ǀ ihá ǀ stavatha ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyāni ǀ tuvi-dyumnásya ǀ tuvi-rā́dhasaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀyásya ǀ krátuḥ ǀ vidathyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ sahvā́n ǀ tárutraḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ásti ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorify the powerful leaders of that renowned and opulent (Indra), whose victorious and protecting energy rules over men, like a universal sovereign entitled to veneration.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify the powerful leaders of that renowned and opulent (Indra), whose victorious and protecting energy rules over men, like a universal sovereign entitled to veneration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ यात्विंद्रो दिव आ पृथिव्या मक्षू समुद्रादुत वा पुरीषात् ।स्वर्णरादवसे नो मरुत्वान्परावतो वा सदनादृतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yātu ǀ índraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ makṣú ǀ samudrā́t ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ púrīṣāt ǀsváḥ-narāt ǀ ávase ǀ naḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ vā ǀ sádanāt ǀ ṛtásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra, accompanied by the Marutscome quickly for our protection, from the heaven, from the earth, from the firmament, or from the waters; from the sphere of the sun, from (any) distant region, from the abode of the rains.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, accompanied by the Marutscome quickly for our protection, from the heaven, from the earth, from the firmament, or from the waters; from the sphere of the sun, from (any) distant region, from the abode of the rains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्थूरस्य रायो बृहतो य ईशे तमु ष्टवाम विदथेष्विंद्रं ।यो वायुना जयति गोमतीषु प्र धृष्णुया नयति वस्यो अच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: sthūrásya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ī́śe ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stavāma ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ índram ǀyáḥ ǀ vāyúnā ǀ jáyati ǀ gó-matīṣu ǀ prá ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀ náyati ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: We glorify, in solemn rites, this Indrawho rules over substantial, abundant riches; who by his prowess is victor over (hostile) hosts; who by his munificence brings excellent (wealth) to the presence (of his worshippers).
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify, in solemn rites, this Indrawho rules over substantial, abundant riches; who by his prowess is victor over (hostile) hosts; who by his munificence brings excellent (wealth) to the presence (of his worshippers).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उप यो नमो नमसि स्तभायन्नियर्ति वाचं जनयन्यजध्यै ।ऋंजसानः पुरुवार उक्थैरेंद्रं कृण्वीत सदनेषु होता ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ yáḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ námasi ǀ stabhāyán ǀ íyarti ǀ vā́cam ǀ janáyan ǀ yájadhyai ǀṛñjasānáḥ ǀ puru-vā́raḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ índram ǀ kṛṇvīta ǀ sádaneṣu ǀ hótā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the invoking priest bring to our dwellings that (Indra) who, firmly fixing the (world) returns food for (sacrificial food), and (utters) a voice enjoining (men) to worship; he who is to be propitiated by praises, who is adored by many.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the invoking priest bring to our dwellings that (Indra) who, firmly fixing the (world) returns food for (sacrificial food), and (utters) a voice enjoining (men) to worship; he who is to be propitiated by praises, who is adored by many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धिषा यदि धिषण्यंतः सरण्यान्त्सदंतो अद्रिमौशिजस्य गोहे ।आ दुरोषाः पास्त्यस्य होता यो नो महान्त्संवरणेषु वह्निः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhiṣā́ ǀ yádi ǀ dhiṣaṇyántaḥ ǀ saraṇyā́n ǀ sádantaḥ ǀ ádrim ǀ auśijásya ǀ góhe ǀā́ ǀ duróṣāḥ ǀ pāstyásya ǀ hótā ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ sam-váraṇeṣu ǀ váhniḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the repeaters of (his) commendations, abiding in the dwelling of the worshipper, approach Indrawith praise, may he who is our (great) sustainer in conflicts, whose wrath is difficult to be (appeased), becomes the ministering priest of the master of the house.
verses.wilson_translation: When the repeaters of (his) commendations, abiding in the dwelling of the worshipper, approach Indrawith praise, may he who is our (great) sustainer in conflicts, whose wrath is difficult to be (appeased), becomes the ministering priest of the master of the house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्रा यदीं भार्वरस्य वृष्णः सिषक्ति शुष्मः स्तुवते भराय ।गुहा यदीमौशिजस्य गोहे प्र यद्धिये प्रायसे मदाय ॥
verses.transliteration: satrā́ ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ bhārvarásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ sísakti ǀ śúṣmaḥ ǀ stuvaté ǀ bhárāya ǀgúhā ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ auśijásya ǀ góhe ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ dhiyé ǀ prá ǀ áyase ǀ mádāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: True it is that this might of the son of the protector of the world, the showerer (of benefits), affects for his advantage the offerer of praise; it (prevails) in the secret (thoughts) of the worshipper, and in his dwelling, for (the accomplishment of his) pious acts, (the attainment of his) desires, and his delight.
verses.wilson_translation: True it is that this might of the son of the protector of the world, the showerer (of benefits), affects for his advantage the offerer of praise; it (prevails) in the secret (thoughts) of the worshipper, and in his dwelling, for (the accomplishment of his) pious acts, (the attainment of his) desires, and his delight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि यद्वरांसि पर्वतस्य वृण्वे पयोभिर्जिन्वे अपां जवांसि ।विदद्गौरस्य गवयस्य गोहे यदी वाजाय सुध्यो वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yát ǀ várāṃsi ǀ párvatasya ǀ vṛṇvé ǀ páyaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ jinvé ǀ apā́m ǀ jávāṃsi ǀvidát ǀ gaurásya ǀ gavayásya ǀ góhe ǀ yádi ǀ vā́jāya ǀ su-dhyáḥ ǀ váhanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inasmuch as he has opened the doors of the cloud, and has supplied the rapid courses of the waters with (additional) torrents, so when the pious have recourse to Indrafor food, he finds (it) in the haunt of the Gauraand Gavaya.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as he has opened the doors of the cloud, and has supplied the rapid courses of the waters with (additional) torrents, so when the pious have recourse to Indrafor food, he finds (it) in the haunt of the Gauraand Gavaya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रा ते हस्ता सुकृतोत पाणी प्रयंतारा स्तुवते राध इंद्र ।का ते निषत्तिः किमु नो ममत्सि किं नोदुदु हर्षसे दातवा उ ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrā́ ǀ te ǀ hástā ǀ sú-kṛtā ǀ utá ǀ pāṇī́ íti ǀ pra-yantā́rā ǀ stuvaté ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ indra ǀkā́ ǀ te ǀ ní-sattiḥ ǀ kím ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ mamatsi ǀ kím ǀ ná ǀ út-ut ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ harṣase ǀ dā́tavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your auspicioushands,Indra, are the doers of good deeds; your two hands, Indra, are the extenders of wealth to him who praises you; what, Indra, is this delay? why do you not exhilarate us? why are you not delighted to make us gifts?
verses.wilson_translation: Your auspicioushands,Indra, are the doers of good deeds; your two hands, Indra, are the extenders of wealth to him who praises you; what, Indra, is this delay? why do you not exhilarate us? why are you not delighted to make us gifts?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा वस्व इंद्रः सत्यः सम्राड्ढंता वृत्रं वरिवः पूरवे कः ।पुरुष्टुत क्रत्वा नः शग्धि रायो भक्षीय तेऽवसो दैव्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ satyáḥ ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ hántā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ várivaḥ ǀ pūráve ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀpúru-stuta ǀ krátvā ǀ naḥ ǀ śagdhi ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ bhakṣīyá ǀ te ǀ ávasaḥ ǀ dáivyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus (glorified),Indra, who is faithful (to his word), the lord of wealth, the slayer of Vṛtra, bestows rihes on man; so you, the praised of many, give us riches for our pious acts, that I may eat of your divine food.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus (glorified),Indra, who is faithful (to his word), the lord of wealth, the slayer of Vṛtra, bestows rihes on man; so you, the praised of many, give us riches for our pious acts, that I may eat of your divine food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever delighted in your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THAT gift of ours which Indra loves and welcomes, even that he makes for us, the Great and Strong One.He who comes wielding in his might the thunder, Maghavan, gives prayer, praise, and laud, and Soma. Bull, hurler of the four-edged rain-producer with both his arms, strong, mighty, most heroic;Wearing as wool Paruṣṇī for adornment, whose joints for sake of friendship he hath covered. God who of all the Gods was born divinest, endowed with ample strength and mighty powers,And bearing in his arms the yearning thunder, with violent rush caused heaven and earth to tremble. Before the High God, at his birth, heaven trembled, earth, many floods and all the precipices.The Strong One bringeth nigh the Bull's two Parents: loud sing the winds, like men, in air's mid-region. These are thy great deeds, Indra, thine, the Mighty, deeds to be told aloud at all libations,That thou, O Hero, bold and boldly daring, didst with thy bolt, by strength, destroy the Dragon. True are all these thy deeds, O Most Heroic. The Milch-kine issued from the streaming udder.In fear of thee, O thou of manly spirit, the rivers swiftly set themselves in motion. With joy, O Indra, Lord of Tawny Coursers, the Sisters then, these Goddesses, extolled thee,When thou didst give the prisoned ones their freedom to wander at their will in long succession. Pressed is the gladdening stalk as ’twere a river: so let the rite, the toiler's power, attract theeTo us-ward, of the Bright One, as the courser strains his. exceedingly strong leather bridle. Ever by us perform thy most heroic, thine highest, best victorious deeds, O Victor.For us make Vṛtras easy to be conquered: destroy the weapon of our mortal foeman. Graciously listen to our prayer, O Indra, and strength of varied sort bestow thou on us.Send to us all intelligence arid wisdom O Maghavan, be he who gives us cattle. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers to the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: यन्न इंद्रो जुजुषे यच्च वष्टि तन्नो महान्करति शुष्म्या चित् ।ब्रह्म स्तोमं मघवा सोममुक्था यो अश्मानं शवसा बिभ्रदेति ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ jujuṣé ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ váṣṭi ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ karati ǀ śuṣmī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ cit ǀbráhma ǀ stómam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sómam ǀ ukthā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ áśmānam ǀ śávasā ǀ bíbhrat ǀ éti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Since the great and mighty Indrais propitiated by our (oblations), since he desires (them) from us, may he, the possessor of opulence, who comes wielding the thunderbolt of his strength, accept the (sacrificial) food, the hymn, the Somalibation, and the prayers.
verses.wilson_translation: Since the great and mighty Indrais propitiated by our (oblations), since he desires (them) from us, may he, the possessor of opulence, who comes wielding the thunderbolt of his strength, accept the (sacrificial) food, the hymn, the Somalibation, and the prayers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृषा वृषंधिं चतुरश्रिमस्यन्नुग्रो बाहुभ्यां नृतमः शचीवान् ।श्रिये परुष्णीमुषमाण ऊर्णां यस्याः पर्वाणि सख्याय विव्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛ́ṣandhim ǀ cátuḥ-aśrim ǀ ásyan ǀ ugráḥ ǀ bāhú-bhyām ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ śácī-vān ǀśriyé ǀ páruṣṇīm ǀ uṣámāṇaḥ ǀ ū́rṇām ǀ yásyāḥ ǀ párvāṇi ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ vivyé ǁ
verses.english_translation: The showerer (of benefits), casting with hishandsthe quadrangular bolt that causes rain, fierce, the chief of leaders, the achiever of (glorious) acts, is desirous of the prosperity of the investing Paruṣṇi (river), whose (bordering) districts he has frequented through regard.
verses.wilson_translation: The showerer (of benefits), casting with hishandsthe quadrangular bolt that causes rain, fierce, the chief of leaders, the achiever of (glorious) acts, is desirous of the prosperity of the investing Paruṣṇi (river), whose (bordering) districts he has frequented through regard.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो देवो देवतमो जायमानो महो वाजेभिर्महद्भिश्च शुष्मैः ।दधानो वज्रं बाह्वोरुशंतं द्याममेन रेजयत्प्र भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ devá-tamaḥ ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ ca ǀ śúṣmaiḥ ǀdádhānaḥ ǀ vájram ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ uśántam ǀ dyā́m ǀ ámena ǀ rejayat ǀ prá ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who diine, most divine, as soon as born (was endowed) with abundant viands, and great energies, holding in his arms the willing thunderbolt, and causing by his strength (both) heaven and earth to tremble.
verses.wilson_translation: Who diine, most divine, as soon as born (was endowed) with abundant viands, and great energies, holding in his arms the willing thunderbolt, and causing by his strength (both) heaven and earth to tremble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वा रोधांसि प्रवतश्च पूर्वीर्द्यौर्ऋष्वाज्जनिमन्रेजत क्षाः ।आ मातरा भरति शुष्म्या गोर्नृवत्परिज्मन्नोनुवंत वाताः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvā ǀ ródhāṃsi ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ṛṣvā́t ǀ jániman ǀ rejata ǀ kṣā́ḥ ǀā́ ǀ mātárā ǀ bhárati ǀ śuṣmī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ góḥ ǀ nṛ-vát ǀ pári-jman ǀ nonuvanta ǀ vā́tāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All the high plural ces, and the many low paces, the heaven and the earth, trembled (through fear) of the mighty (Indra) at his birth; the strong (Indra) cherishes the parents of the moving (Sun), and the winds, like men, make a noise in their peregrination.
verses.wilson_translation: All the high plural ces, and the many low paces, the heaven and the earth, trembled (through fear) of the mighty (Indra) at his birth; the strong (Indra) cherishes the parents of the moving (Sun), and the winds, like men, make a noise in their peregrination.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता तू त इंद्र महतो महानि विश्वेष्वित्सवनेषु प्रवाच्या ।यच्छूर धृष्णो धृषता दधृष्वानहिं वज्रेण शवसाविवेषीः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ tú ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ mahā́ni ǀ víśveṣu ǀ ít ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ pra-vā́cyā ǀyát ǀ śūra ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ dadhṛṣvā́n ǀ áhim ǀ vájreṇa ǀ śávasā ǀ áviveṣīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of you,Indra, who are mighty, great are deeds, and to be proclaimed at all sacrifices, inasmuch as, high-minded hero, you, sustaining (the world), have by your strength slain Ahi with the resistless thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Of you,Indra, who are mighty, great are deeds, and to be proclaimed at all sacrifices, inasmuch as, high-minded hero, you, sustaining (the world), have by your strength slain Ahi with the resistless thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता तू ते सत्या तुविनृम्ण विश्वा प्र धेनवः सिस्रते वृष्ण ऊध्नः ।अधा ह त्वद्वृषमणो भियानाः प्र सिंधवो जवसा चक्रमंत ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ tú ǀ te ǀ satyā́ ǀ tuvi-nṛmṇa ǀ víśvā ǀ prá ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ sisrate ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ ū́dhnaḥ ǀádha ǀ ha ǀ tvát ǀ vṛṣa-manaḥ ǀ bhiyānā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ jávasā ǀ cakramanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most powerful Indra, all these, your exploits, are verily true: (through fear of you), the showerer (of benefits), the cows shed (milk) from their udders; then, benevolent-minded (Indra), the rivers, fearing you, flow with rapidity.
verses.wilson_translation: Most powerful Indra, all these, your exploits, are verily true: (through fear of you), the showerer (of benefits), the cows shed (milk) from their udders; then, benevolent-minded (Indra), the rivers, fearing you, flow with rapidity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अत्राह ते हरिवस्ता उ देवीरवोभिरिंद्र स्तवंत स्वसारः ।यत्सीमनु प्र मुचो बद्बधाना दीर्घामनु प्रसितिं स्यंदयध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: átra ǀ áha ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ stavanta ǀ svásāraḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ mucáḥ ǀ badbadhānā́ḥ ǀ dīrghā́m ǀ ánu ǀ prá-sitim ǀ syandayádhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then,Indra, lord of horses, the divine sister (rivers) praise (you) for your protection when you did set them free to flow, after having been impeded (by Vṛtra) through a long confinement.
verses.wilson_translation: Then,Indra, lord of horses, the divine sister (rivers) praise (you) for your protection when you did set them free to flow, after having been impeded (by Vṛtra) through a long confinement.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पिपीळे अंशुर्मद्यो न सिंधुरा त्वा शमी शशमानस्य शक्तिः ।अस्मद्र्यक्शुशुचानस्य यम्या आशुर्न रश्मिं तुव्योजसं गोः ॥
verses.transliteration: pipīḷé ǀ aṃśúḥ ǀ mádyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ śámī ǀ śaśamānásya ǀ śaktíḥ ǀasmadryák ǀ śuśucānásya ǀ yamyāḥ ǀ āśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmím ǀ tuvi-ójasam ǀ góḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The exhilarating Somajuice has been expressed; now may the curren flow to you, and may the expiatory power of the illustrious utterer of praise be directed towards us, as the quick rider holds firmly the reins of the steed.
verses.wilson_translation: The exhilarating Somajuice has been expressed; now may the curren flow to you, and may the expiatory power of the illustrious utterer of praise be directed towards us, as the quick rider holds firmly the reins of the steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे वर्षिष्ठा कृणुहि ज्येष्ठा नृम्णानि सत्रा सहुरे सहांसि ।अस्मभ्यं वृत्रा सुहनानि रंधि जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ várṣiṣṭhā ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ jyéṣṭhā ǀ nṛmṇā́ni ǀ satrā́ ǀ sahure ǀ sáhāṃsi ǀasmábhyam ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ su-hánāni ǀ randhi ǀ jahí ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀ mártyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Enduring Indra, bestow upon us energies, excellent, superior, powerful; bring under subjection to us enemies deserving of death; demolish the weapon of the malevolent man.
verses.wilson_translation: Enduring Indra, bestow upon us energies, excellent, superior, powerful; bring under subjection to us enemies deserving of death; demolish the weapon of the malevolent man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमित्सु शृणुहि त्वमिंद्रास्मभ्यं चित्राँ उप माहि वाजान् ।अस्मभ्यं विश्वा इषणः पुरंधीरस्माकं सु मघवन्बोधि गोदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ ít ǀ sú ǀ śṛṇuhi ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ asmábhyam ǀ citrā́n ǀ úpa ǀ māhi ǀ vā́jān ǀasmábhyam ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ iṣaṇaḥ ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sú ǀ magha-van ǀ bodhi ǀ go-dā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear our praises,Indra, and bestow upon us many kinds of food; fulfil all our desires, and know yourself,Maghavan, to be to us the donor of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear our praises,Indra, and bestow upon us many kinds of food; fulfil all our desires, and know yourself,Maghavan, to be to us the donor of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in (your) praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in (your) praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ११ वामदेवो गौतमः। इन्द्रः, ८-१० ऋतं वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . How, what priest's sacrifice hath he made mighty, rejoicing in the Soma and its fountain?Delighting in juice, eagerly drinking, the Lofty One hath waxed for splendid riches. What hero hath been made his feast-companion? Who hath been partner in his loving-kindness?What know we of his wondrous acts? How often comes he to aid and speed the pious toiler? How heareth Indra offered invocation? How, hearing, marketh he the invoker's wishes?What are his ancient acts of bounty? Wherefore call they him One who filleth full the singer? How doth the priest who laboureth, ever longing, win for himself the wealth which he possesseth?May he, the God, mark well my truthful praises, having received the homage which he loveth. How, and what bond of friendship with a mortal hath the God chosen as this morn is breaking?How, and what love hath he for those who love him, who have entwined in him their firm affection? Is then thy friendship with thy friends most mighty? Thy brotherhood with us,—when may we tell it?The streams of milk move, as most wondrous sunlight, the beauty of the Lovely One for glory. About to stay the Indra-less destructive spirit he sharpens his keen arms to strike her.Whereby the Strong, although our debts’ exactor, drives in the distant mornings that we know not. Eternal Law hath varied food that strengthens; thought of eternal Law, removes transgressions.The praise-hymn of eternal Law, arousing, glowing, hath oped the deaf ears of the living. Firm-seated are eternal Law's foundations in its fair form are many splendid beauties.By holy Law long lasting food they bring us; by holy Law have cows come to our worship. Fixing eternal Law he, too, upholds it swift moves the might of Law and wins the booty.To Law belong the vast deep Earth and Heaven: Milch-kine supreme, to Law their milk they render. Now, Indra! lauded,—glorified with praises, let power swell high like rivers to the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: कथा महामवृधत्कस्य होतुर्यज्ञं जुषाणो अभि सोममूधः ।पिबन्नुशानो जुषमाणो अंधो ववक्ष ऋष्वः शुचते धनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ mahā́m ǀ avṛdhat ǀ kásya ǀ hótuḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ juṣāṇáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sómam ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀpíban ǀ uśānáḥ ǀ juṣámāṇaḥ ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ vavakṣé ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀ śucaté ǀ dhánāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: In what manner may (any one) extol the mighty Indra? at the sacrifice of what worshipper may he, propitiated, be present, drinking the sacrificial Somabeverage, desirous of the (sacred) food, and plural ased (by the oblation)? the mighty Indra is borne (to the rite) for the purpose of bestowing brilliant wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: In what manner may (any one) extol the mighty Indra? at the sacrifice of what worshipper may he, propitiated, be present, drinking the sacrificial Somabeverage, desirous of the (sacred) food, and plural ased (by the oblation)? the mighty Indra is borne (to the rite) for the purpose of bestowing brilliant wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को अस्य वीरः सधमादमाप समानंश सुमतिभिः को अस्य ।कदस्य चित्रं चिकिते कदूती वृधे भुवच्छशमानस्य यज्योः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ asya ǀ vīráḥ ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǀ āpa ǀ sám ǀ ānaṃśa ǀ sumatí-bhiḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ asya ǀkát ǀ asya ǀ citrám ǀ cikite ǀ kát ǀ ūtī́ ǀ vṛdhé ǀ bhuvat ǀ śaśamānásya ǀ yájyoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What hero has enjoyed his fellowship (in battle)? who has been a sharer in his benevolent thoughts? when does any one appreciate his wonderful bounty? when is he (presen) for the promotion of the prosperity of the man who glorifies and worships him?
verses.wilson_translation: What hero has enjoyed his fellowship (in battle)? who has been a sharer in his benevolent thoughts? when does any one appreciate his wonderful bounty? when is he (presen) for the promotion of the prosperity of the man who glorifies and worships him?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कथा शृणोति हूयमानमिंद्रः कथा शृण्वन्नवसामस्य वेद ।का अस्य पूर्वीरुपमातयो ह कथैनमाहुः पपुरिं जरित्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ śṛṇoti ǀ hūyámānam ǀ índraḥ ǀ kathā́ ǀ śṛṇván ǀ ávasām ǀ asya ǀ veda ǀkā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ úpa-mātayaḥ ǀ ha ǀ kathā́ ǀ enam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ pápurim ǀ jaritré ǁ
verses.english_translation: How is that Indrahears (the worshipper) who invokes him? and, hearing, how does he know his necessities? what are his gifts of old; why have they termed him the fulfiller (of the desires) of him who offers praise?
verses.wilson_translation: How is that Indrahears (the worshipper) who invokes him? and, hearing, how does he know his necessities? what are his gifts of old; why have they termed him the fulfiller (of the desires) of him who offers praise?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कथा सबाधः शशमानो अस्य नशदभि द्रविणं दीध्यानः ।देवो भुवन्नवेदा म ऋतानां नमो जगृभ्वाँ अभि यज्जुजोषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ śaśamānáḥ ǀ asya ǀ náśat ǀ abhí ǀ dráviṇam ǀ dī́dhyānaḥ ǀdeváḥ ǀ bhuvat ǀ návedāḥ ǀ me ǀ ṛtā́nām ǀ námaḥ ǀ jagṛbhvā́n ǀ abhí ǀ yát ǀ jújoṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: How does he who glorifies Indra, and is diligent in his worship, although encountering opposition, obtain from him wealth? may the divine Indra be the appreciation of my praises, when accepting the sacrificial food he is propitiated towards me.
verses.wilson_translation: How does he who glorifies Indra, and is diligent in his worship, although encountering opposition, obtain from him wealth? may the divine Indra be the appreciation of my praises, when accepting the sacrificial food he is propitiated towards me.

verses.sanskrit: कथा कदस्या उषसो व्युष्टौ देवो मर्तस्य सख्यं जुजोष ।कथा कदस्य सख्यं सखिभ्यो ये अस्मिन्कामं सुयुजं ततस्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ kát ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ deváḥ ǀ mártasya ǀ sakhyám ǀ jujoṣa ǀkathā́ ǀ kát ǀ asya ǀ sakhyám ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ yé ǀ asmin ǀ kā́mam ǀ su-yújam ǀ tatasré ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, in what manner, at the dawning of this morning, has the divine Indraaccepted the friendship of a mortal? when and in what manner, (is) his friendship (manifested) to the friends who have spread out the desirable and suitable (offering) before him?
verses.wilson_translation: When, in what manner, at the dawning of this morning, has the divine Indraaccepted the friendship of a mortal? when and in what manner, (is) his friendship (manifested) to the friends who have spread out the desirable and suitable (offering) before him?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किमादमत्रं सख्यं सखिभ्यः कदा नु ते भ्रात्रं प्र ब्रवाम ।श्रिये सुदृशो वपुरस्य सर्गाः स्वर्ण चित्रतममिष आ गोः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ ā́t ǀ ámatram ǀ sakhyám ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ kadā́ ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ bhrātrám ǀ prá ǀ bravāma ǀśriyé ǀ su-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ vápuḥ ǀ asya ǀ sárgāḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrá-tamam ǀ iṣe ǀ ā́ ǀ góḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we in any manner proclaim your friendship for your friends? when may (we make known) your fraternal regard? the efforts of the well-looking Indraare for the happiness of all; the wonderful form of the moving (Indra) is, like the sun, ever wished for.
verses.wilson_translation: May we in any manner proclaim your friendship for your friends? when may (we make known) your fraternal regard? the efforts of the well-looking Indraare for the happiness of all; the wonderful form of the moving (Indra) is, like the sun, ever wished for.

verses.sanskrit: द्रुहं जिघांसंध्वरसमनिंद्रां तेतिक्ते तिग्मा तुजसे अनीका ।ऋणा चिद्यत्र ऋणया न उग्रो दूरे अज्ञाता उषसो बबाधे ॥
verses.transliteration: drúham ǀ jíghāṃsan ǀ dhvarásam ǀ anindrā́m ǀ tétikte ǀ tigmā́ ǀ tujáse ǀ ánīkā ǀṛṇā́ ǀ cit ǀ yátra ǀ ṛṇa-yā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ dūré ǀ ájñātāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ babādhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resolving to kil the oppressing, malevolent (rākṣasi), not acknowledging Indra, he sharpened his sharp weapons for (her) destruction, and the fierce (Indra) the canceller of debts, has kept afar the unknown dawns in which the debts (are to be paid).
verses.wilson_translation: Resolving to kil the oppressing, malevolent (rākṣasi), not acknowledging Indra, he sharpened his sharp weapons for (her) destruction, and the fierce (Indra) the canceller of debts, has kept afar the unknown dawns in which the debts (are to be paid).

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः संति पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हंति ।ऋतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ sánti ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ vṛjinā́ni ǀ hanti ǀṛtásya ǀ ślókaḥ ǀ badhirā́ ǀ tatarda ǀ kárṇā ǀ budhānáḥ ǀ śucámānaḥ ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are the waters of ṛta; the adoration of ṛta destroys iniquities; the intelligent and brilliant praise of ṛta has opened the deaf (ears) of man.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the waters of ṛta; the adoration of ṛta destroys iniquities; the intelligent and brilliant praise of ṛta has opened the deaf (ears) of man.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य दृळ्हा धरुणानि संति पुरूणि चंद्रा वपुषे वपूंषि ।ऋतेन दीर्घमिषणंत पृक्ष ऋतेन गाव ऋतमा विवेशुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ dṛḷhā́ ǀ dharúṇāni ǀ santi ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ candrā́ ǀ vápuṣe ǀ vápūṃṣi ǀṛténa ǀ dīrghám ǀ iṣaṇanta ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ ṛténa ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are the stable, sustaining, delightful forms of the embodied ṛta; the ṛta are (the pious) expectant of food; by ṛta have the kine entered into the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the stable, sustaining, delightful forms of the embodied ṛta; the ṛta are (the pious) expectant of food; by ṛta have the kine entered into the sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतं येमान ऋतमिद्वनोत्यृतस्य शुष्मस्तुरया उ गव्युः ।ऋताय पृथ्वी बहुले गभीरे ऋताय धेनू परमे दुहाते ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtám ǀ yemānáḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ ít ǀ vanoti ǀ ṛtásya ǀ śúṣmaḥ ǀ tura-yā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ gavyúḥ ǀṛtā́ya ǀ pṛthvī́ íti ǀ bahulé íti ǀ gabhīré íti ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ dhenū́ íti ǀ paramé íti ǀ duhāte íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The (worshipper) subjecting ṛta (to his will) verily enjoys ṛta; the strength ṛta is (developed) with speed, and is desirous of (possessing) water; to ṛta belong the wide and profound heaven and earth; supreme kine, they yield their milk to ṛta.

hymns.title: HYMN XXIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT worthy praise will bring before us Indra, the Son of Strength, that he may grant us riches;For he the Hero, gives the singer treasures: he is the Lord who sends us gifts, ye people. To be invoked and hymned in fight with Vṛtra, that well-praised Indra gives us real bounties.That Maghavan brings comfort in the foray to the religious man who pours libations. Him, verily, the men invoke in combat; risking their lives they make him their protector,When heroes, foe to foe, give up their bodies, fighting, each side, for children and their offspring. Strong God! the folk at need put forth their vigour, striving together in the whirl of battle.When warrior bands encounter one another some in the grapple quit themselves like Indra. Hence many a one worships the might of Indra: hence let the brew succeed the meal-oblation.Hence let the Soma banish those who pour not: even hence I joy to pay the Strong One worship. Indra gives comfort to the man who truly presses, for him who longsforit, the Soma,Not disaffected, with devoted spirit this man he takes to be his friend in battles. He who this day for Indra presses Soma, prepares the brew and fries the grains of barley—Loving the hymns of that devoted servant, to him may Indra give heroic vigour. When the impetuous chief hath sought theconflict, and the lord looked upon the long-drawn battle,The matron calls to the Strong God whom pressers of Soma have encouraged in the dwelling. He bid a small price for a thing of value: I was content, returning, still unpurchased.He heightened not his insufficient offer. Simple and clever, both milk out the udder. Who for ten milch-kine purchaseth from me this Indra who is mine?When he hath slain the Vṛtras let the buyer give him back to me. Now, Indra! lauded, glorified with praises, let wealth swell high like rivers for the singer.For thee a new hymn, Lord of Bays, is fashioned. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever.

verses.sanskrit: का सुष्टुतिः शवसः सूनुमिंद्रमर्वाचीनं राधस आ ववर्तत् ।ददिर्हि वीरो गृणते वसूनि स गोपतिर्निष्षिधां नो जनासः ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ su-stutíḥ ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ sūnúm ǀ índram ǀ arvācīnám ǀ rā́dhase ǀ ā́ ǀ vavartat ǀdadíḥ ǀ hí ǀ vīráḥ ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ vásūni ǀ sáḥ ǀ gó-patiḥ ǀ niḥ-sídhām ǀ naḥ ǀ janāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What suitable praise may bring the son of strength,Indra, before us, to give us wealth; the hero, the lord of cattle, is the donor, oḥ man, of the wealth of his adversaries to him who glorifies him.
verses.wilson_translation: What suitable praise may bring the son of strength,Indra, before us, to give us wealth; the hero, the lord of cattle, is the donor, oḥ man, of the wealth of his adversaries to him who glorifies him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स वृत्रहत्ये हव्यः स ईड्यः स सुष्टुत इंद्रः सत्यराधाः ।स यामन्ना मघवा मर्त्याय ब्रह्मण्यते सुष्वये वरिवो धात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ sú-stutaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ satyá-rādhāḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ yā́man ǀ ā́ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ mártyāya ǀ brahmaṇyaté ǀ súsvaye ǀ várivaḥ ǀ dhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: He,Indra, is to be invoked for the destruction of Vṛtra; he, the deservedly praised, is to be worshipped; the real donor of wealth, he,Maghavan, gives wealth, (acquired) in battle, to the mortal offers him prayer and libations.
verses.wilson_translation: He,Indra, is to be invoked for the destruction of Vṛtra; he, the deservedly praised, is to be worshipped; the real donor of wealth, he,Maghavan, gives wealth, (acquired) in battle, to the mortal offers him prayer and libations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमिन्नरो वि ह्वयंते समीके रिरिक्वांसस्तन्वः कृण्वत त्रां ।मिथो यत्त्यागमुभयासो अग्मन्नरस्तोकस्य तनयस्य सातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ náraḥ ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ sam-īké ǀ ririkvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ kṛṇvata ǀ trā́m ǀmitháḥ ǀ yát ǀ tyāgám ǀ ubháyāsaḥ ǀ ágman ǀ náraḥ ǀ tokásya ǀ tánayasya ǀ sātáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men verily call upon him in battle; the (devout) inflicters of austerity upon their person ns constitute him their preserver; when both (the worshipper and the priest) approach together the bountiful Indra, men (succeed) in (obtaining) the gift of sons and grandsons.
verses.wilson_translation: Men verily call upon him in battle; the (devout) inflicters of austerity upon their person ns constitute him their preserver; when both (the worshipper and the priest) approach together the bountiful Indra, men (succeed) in (obtaining) the gift of sons and grandsons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्रतूयंति क्षितयो योग उग्राशुषाणासो मिथो अर्णसातौ ।सं यद्विशोऽववृत्रंत युध्मा आदिन्नेम इंद्रयंते अभीके ॥
verses.transliteration: kratu-yánti ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ yóge ǀ ugra ǀ āśuṣāṇā́saḥ ǀ mitháḥ ǀ árṇa-sātau ǀsám ǀ yát ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ávavṛtranta ǀ yudhmā́ḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ néme ǀ indrayante ǀ abhī́ke ǁ
verses.english_translation: Powerful Indra, men variously dispersed, come mutually together to celebrate sacred rites for the sake of obtaining rain; when men who are combatants assemble in battle, there are some of them who rely upon Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Indra, men variously dispersed, come mutually together to celebrate sacred rites for the sake of obtaining rain; when men who are combatants assemble in battle, there are some of them who rely upon Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदिद्ध नेम इंद्रियं यजंत आदित्पक्तिः पुरोळाशं रिरिच्यात् ।आदित्सोमो वि पपृच्यादसुष्वीनादिज्जुजोष वृषभं यजध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ ha ǀ néme ǀ indriyám ǀ yajante ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ paktíḥ ǀ puroḷā́śam ǀ riricyāt ǀā́t ǀ ít ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ví ǀ papṛcyāt ǀ ásusvīn ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ jujoṣa ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ yájadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thereupon some verily worship the powerful (Indra); thereupon one man prepares the buttered cake that he may offer it to (Indra); thereupon the offerer of the Somahe distinguishes from him who presents no libation; thereupon some one rejoices to worship the showerer (of benefits).
verses.wilson_translation: Thereupon some verily worship the powerful (Indra); thereupon one man prepares the buttered cake that he may offer it to (Indra); thereupon the offerer of the Somahe distinguishes from him who presents no libation; thereupon some one rejoices to worship the showerer (of benefits).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृणोत्यस्मै वरिवो य इत्थेंद्राय सोममुशते सुनोति ।सध्रीचीनेन मनसाविवेनंतमित्सखायं कृणुते समत्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṇóti ǀ asmai ǀ várivaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ índrāya ǀ sómam ǀ uśaté ǀ sunóti ǀsadhrīcī́nena ǀ mánasā ǀ ávi-venan ǀ tám ǀ ít ǀ sákhāyam ǀ kṛṇute ǀ samát-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrabestows wealth upon him who offers a libation to him, desiring it, though in another sphere; and, with a humble mind, makes him who is devoted to him his friend in combats.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrabestows wealth upon him who offers a libation to him, desiring it, though in another sphere; and, with a humble mind, makes him who is devoted to him his friend in combats.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इंद्राय सुनवत्सोममद्य पचात्पक्तीरुत भृज्जाति धानाः ।प्रति मनायोरुचथानि हर्यंतस्मिंदधद्वृषणं शुष्ममिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ sunávat ǀ sómam ǀ adyá ǀ pácāt ǀ paktī́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ bhṛjjā́ti ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀpráti ǀ manāyóḥ ǀ ucáthāni ǀ háryan ǀ tásmin ǀ dadhat ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ śúṣmam ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraaccepting graciously the praises of his devoted (worshipper), who today pours out the libation to him who toasts the buttered cakes, or fries barley for Indra, exercises towards him the power that grants his desires.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraaccepting graciously the praises of his devoted (worshipper), who today pours out the libation to him who toasts the buttered cakes, or fries barley for Indra, exercises towards him the power that grants his desires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदा समर्यं व्यचेदृघावा दीर्घं यदाजिमभ्यख्यदर्यः ।अचिक्रदद्वृषणं पत्न्यच्छा दुरोण आ निशितं सोमसुद्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ sa-maryám ǀ ví ǀ ácet ǀ ṛ́ghāvā ǀ dīrghám ǀ yát ǀ ājím ǀ abhí ǀ ákhyat ǀ aryáḥ ǀácikradat ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ pátnī ǀ áccha ǀ duroṇé ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-śitam ǀ somasút-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the destroyer (of enemies) distinguishes a mortal foe; when the lord is engaged in the long (continued) battle, (his) bride summons to the dwelling the showerer (of benefits), encompassed by the offerers of the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: When the destroyer (of enemies) distinguishes a mortal foe; when the lord is engaged in the long (continued) battle, (his) bride summons to the dwelling the showerer (of benefits), encompassed by the offerers of the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भूयसा वस्नमचरत्कनीयोऽविक्रीतो अकानिषं पुनर्यन् ।स भूयसा कनीयो नारिरेचीद्दीना दक्षा वि दुहंति प्र वाणं ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́yasā ǀ vasnám ǀ acarat ǀ kánīyaḥ ǀ ávi-krītaḥ ǀ akāniṣam ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yán ǀsáḥ ǀ bhū́yasā ǀ kánīyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ arirecīt ǀ dīnā́ḥ ǀ dákṣāḥ ǀ ví ǀ duhanti ǀ prá ǀ vāṇám ǁ
verses.english_translation: A man has realized a small price for an article of great value, and again coming (to the buyer he says) this has not been sold; I require the full price; but he does not recover a small price by a large (equivalent); whether helpless or clever they adhere to their bargain.
verses.wilson_translation: A man has realized a small price for an article of great value, and again coming (to the buyer he says) this has not been sold; I require the full price; but he does not recover a small price by a large (equivalent); whether helpless or clever they adhere to their bargain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क इमं दशभिर्ममेंद्रं क्रीणाति धेनुभिः ।यदा वृत्राणि जंघनदथैनं मे पुनर्ददत् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ imám ǀ daśá-bhiḥ ǀ máma ǀ índram ǀ krīṇāti ǀ dhenú-bhiḥ ǀyadā́ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jáṅghanat ǀ átha ǀ enam ǀ me ǀ púnaḥ ǀ dadat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who buys him, my Indra, with ten kine? when he shall have slain (your) foes, then let (the purchaser) give him again to me.
verses.wilson_translation: Who buys him, my Indra, with ten kine? when he shall have slain (your) foes, then let (the purchaser) give him again to me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू ष्टुत इंद्र नू गृणान इषं जरित्रे नद्यो न पीपेः ।अकारि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म नव्यं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ stutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ nú ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ jaritré ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ pīperíti pīpeḥ ǀákāri ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorified (in the past), glorified,Indra, at present, satisfy your worshipper with food, as rivers (are filled with water); lord of horses, a new hymn has been made for you; may we, possessed of chariots, be ever diligent in your praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT friend of man, God-loving, hath delighted, yearning therefor, this day in Indra's friendship?Who with enkindled flame and flowing Soma laudeth him for his great protecting favour? Who hath with prayer bowed to the Soma-lover? What pious man endues the beams of morning?Who seeks bond, friendship, brotherhood with Indra? Who hath recourse unto the Sage for succour? Who claims to-day the Deities' protection, asks Aditi for light, or the Ādityas?Of whose pressed stalk of Soma drink the Aśvins, Indra, and Agni, well-inclined in spirit? To him shall Agni Bhārata give shelter: long shall he look upon the Sun up-rising,Who sayeth, Let us press the juice for Indra, man's Friend, the Hero manliest of heroes. Him neither few men overcome, nor many to him shall Aditi give spacious shelter.Dear is the pious, the devout, to Indra dear is the zealous, dear the Soma-bringer. This Hero curbs the mighty for the zealous: the presser's brew Indra possesses solely:No brother, kin, or friend to him who pours not, destroyer of the dumb who would resist him. Not with the wealthy churl who pours no Soma doth Indra, Soma-drinker, bind alliance.He draws away his wealth and slays him naked, own Friend to him who offers, for oblation. Highest and lowest, men who stand between diem, going, returning, dwelling in contentment,Those who show forth their strength when urged to battle-these are the men who call for aid on Indra.

verses.sanskrit: को अद्य नर्यो देवकाम उशन्निंद्रस्य सख्यं जुजोष ।को वा महेऽवसे पार्याय समिद्धे अग्नौ सुतसोम ईट्टे ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ adyá ǀ náryaḥ ǀ devá-kāmaḥ ǀ uśán ǀ índrasya ǀ sakhyám ǀ jujoṣa ǀkáḥ ǀ vā ǀ mahé ǀ ávase ǀ pā́ryāya ǀ sám-iddhe ǀ agnáu ǀ sutá-somaḥ ǀ īṭṭe ǁ
verses.english_translation: What friend of man, or worshipper of the gods, deserving the friendship of Indra, has today enjoyed (it)? or what offerer of the libation on the kindled fire praises him (sufficiently) for his great and unbounded protection?
verses.wilson_translation: What friend of man, or worshipper of the gods, deserving the friendship of Indra, has today enjoyed (it)? or what offerer of the libation on the kindled fire praises him (sufficiently) for his great and unbounded protection?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को नानाम वचसा सोम्याय मनायुर्वा भवति वस्त उस्राः ।क इंद्रस्य युज्यं कः सखित्वं को भ्रात्रं वष्टि कवये क ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ nanāma ǀ vácasā ǀ somyā́ya ǀ manāyúḥ ǀ vā ǀ bhavati ǀ váste ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀkáḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ yújyam ǀ káḥ ǀ sakhi-tvám ǀ káḥ ǀ bhrātrám ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ kaváye ǀ káḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who has reverenced with (suitable) words the (deity) worthy of the libation? who is devoted (to him)? who supports the cattle (given by him)? who desires the society of Indra? who his friendship? who his fraternity? who (has recourse) to the sage Indra for protection?
verses.wilson_translation: Who has reverenced with (suitable) words the (deity) worthy of the libation? who is devoted (to him)? who supports the cattle (given by him)? who desires the society of Indra? who his friendship? who his fraternity? who (has recourse) to the sage Indra for protection?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को देवानामवो अद्या वृणीते क आदित्याँ अदितिं ज्योतिरीट्टे ।कस्याश्विनाविंद्रो अग्निः सुतस्यांशोः पिबंति मनसाविवेनं ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīté ǀ káḥ ǀ ādityā́n ǀ áditim ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ īṭṭe ǀkásya ǀ aśvínau ǀ índraḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sutásya ǀ aṃśóḥ ǀ pibanti ǀ mánasā ǀ ávi-venam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who solicits today the protection of the gods? who glorifies theĀdityas,Aditi, light? of whose effused libation to the Aśvins,Indra,Agni, drink at will propitiated by his praise?
verses.wilson_translation: Who solicits today the protection of the gods? who glorifies theĀdityas,Aditi, light? of whose effused libation to the Aśvins,Indra,Agni, drink at will propitiated by his praise?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं ।य इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणां ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmai ǀ agníḥ ǀ bhā́rataḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǀ jyók ǀ paśyāt ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ut-cárantam ǀyáḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ sunávāma ǀ íti ǀ ā́ha ǀ náre ǀ náryāya ǀ nṛ́-tamāya ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Agni, the bearer of oblations, grant him felicity, and long behold the rising sun (in the dwelling of him) who says, let us offer libations to Indra, leader (of rites) the friend of man, the chief leader among leaders.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agni, the bearer of oblations, grant him felicity, and long behold the rising sun (in the dwelling of him) who says, let us offer libations to Indra, leader (of rites) the friend of man, the chief leader among leaders.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न तं जिनंति बहवो न दभ्रा उर्वस्मा अदितिः शर्म यंसत् ।प्रियः सुकृत्प्रिय इंद्रे मनायुः प्रियः सुप्रावीः प्रियो अस्य सोमी ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ jinanti ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dabhrā́ḥ ǀ urú ǀ asmai ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǀpriyáḥ ǀ su-kṛ́t ǀ priyáḥ ǀ índre ǀ manāyúḥ ǀ priyáḥ ǀ supra-avī́ḥ ǀ priyáḥ ǀ asya ǀ somī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him neither many nor few can molest; may Aditigrant him infinite happiness; the performer of pious acts is dear (to Indra); dear to Indra is he whose mind is intent upon him; dear is he who approaches him with homage; dear to him is the offerer of the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: Him neither many nor few can molest; may Aditigrant him infinite happiness; the performer of pious acts is dear (to Indra); dear to Indra is he whose mind is intent upon him; dear is he who approaches him with homage; dear to him is the offerer of the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुप्राव्यः प्राशुषाळेष वीरः सुष्वेः पक्तिं कृणुते केवलेंद्रः ।नासुष्वेरापिर्न सखा न जामिर्दुष्प्राव्योऽवहंतेदवाचः ॥
verses.transliteration: supra-avyáḥ ǀ prāśuṣā́ṭ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ vīráḥ ǀ súsveḥ ǀ paktím ǀ kṛṇute ǀ kévalā ǀ índraḥ ǀná ǀ ásusveḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ ná ǀ sákhā ǀ ná ǀ jāmíḥ ǀ duḥpra-avyáḥ ǀ ava-hantā́ ǀ ít ǀ ávācaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This hero,Indra, the prompt discomfiter (of foes), who is to be approached with homage, grants special maturity to the presenter of the libation; he is not the kinsman, nor friend, nor relative, of him who offers no libation (to him); he is difficult of access, and the punisher of him who repeats not (his) praise.
verses.wilson_translation: This hero,Indra, the prompt discomfiter (of foes), who is to be approached with homage, grants special maturity to the presenter of the libation; he is not the kinsman, nor friend, nor relative, of him who offers no libation (to him); he is difficult of access, and the punisher of him who repeats not (his) praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न रेवता पणिना सख्यमिंद्रोऽसुन्वता सुतपाः सं गृणीते ।आस्य वेदः खिदति हंति नग्नं वि सुष्वये पक्तये केवलो भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ revátā ǀ paṇínā ǀ sakhyám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ásunvatā ǀ suta-pā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ gṛṇīte ǀā́ ǀ asya ǀ védaḥ ǀ khidáti ǀ hánti ǀ nagnám ǀ ví ǀ súsvaye ǀ paktáye ǀ kévalaḥ ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Indra), the drinker of the effused Soma, contract no friendship with the wealthy trader who offers not any libation; he takes away his wealth; destroys him when destitute; but he is a special (friend) to him who presents the libation and oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra), the drinker of the effused Soma, contract no friendship with the wealthy trader who offers not any libation; he takes away his wealth; destroys him when destitute; but he is a special (friend) to him who presents the libation and oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं परेऽवरे मध्यमास इंद्रं यांतोऽवसितास इंद्रं ।इंद्रं क्षियंत उत युध्यमाना इंद्रं नरो वाजयंतो हवंते ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ páre ǀ ávare ǀ madhyamā́saḥ ǀ índram ǀ yā́ntaḥ ǀ áva-sitāsaḥ ǀ índram ǀíndram ǀ kṣiyántaḥ ǀ utá ǀ yúdhyamānāḥ ǀ índram ǀ náraḥ ǀ vājayántaḥ ǀ havante ǁ
verses.english_translation: The most exalted, the most humble, (invoke)Indra; the middle (classes) invoke Indra; those going, those stopping, (invoke) Indra; those dwelling at home, those going in battle, (invoke) Indra; men needing food invoke Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: The most exalted, the most humble, (invoke)Indra; the middle (classes) invoke Indra; those going, those stopping, (invoke) Indra; those dwelling at home, those going in battle, (invoke) Indra; men needing food invoke Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ७ वामदेवो गौतमः, १-३ इन्द्रो वा। १-३ इन्द्रः, आत्मा वा, ४-७ श्येनः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Sūrya: I am the sage Kakṣīvān, holy singer.Kutsa the son of Ārjuni I master. I am the sapient Uśanā behold me. I have bestowed the earth upon the Ārya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation.I guided forth the loudly-roaring waters, and the Gods moved according to my pleasure. In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Śambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together;And, utterly, the hundredth habitation, when helping Divodāsa Atithigva. Before all birds be ranked this Bird, O Maruts; supreme of falcons be this fleet-winged Falcon,Because, strong- pinioned, with no car to bear him, he brought to Manu the Godloved oblation. When the Bird brought it, hence in rapid motion sent on the wide path fleet as thought he hurried.Swift he returned with sweetness of the Soma, and hence the Falcon hath acquired his glory. Bearing the stalk, the Falcon speeding onward, Bird bringing from afar the draught that gladdens,Friend of the Gods, brought, grasping fast, the Soma which be bad taken from yon loftiest heaven. The Falcon took and brought the Soma, bearing thousand libations with him, yea, ten thousand.The Bold One left Malignities behind him, wise, in wild joy of Soma, left the foolish.

verses.sanskrit: अहं मनुरभवं सूर्यश्चाहं कक्षीवाँ ऋषिरस्मि विप्रः ।अहं कुत्समार्जुनेयं न्यृंजेऽहं कविरुशना पश्यता मा ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ mánuḥ ǀ abhavam ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ahám ǀ kakṣī́vān ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ asmi ǀ vípraḥ ǀahám ǀ kútsam ǀ ārjuneyám ǀ ní ǀ ṛñje ǀ ahám ǀ kavíḥ ǀ uśánā ǀ páśyata ǀ mā ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have been Manuand Sūrya; I am the wise ṛṣi:Kakṣīvat; I have befriended Kutsa, the son of Arjuni; I am the far-seeing Uśanās; so behold me.
verses.wilson_translation: I have been Manuand Sūrya; I am the wise ṛṣi:Kakṣīvat; I have befriended Kutsa, the son of Arjuni; I am the far-seeing Uśanās; so behold me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं भूमिमददामार्यायाहं वृष्टिं दाशुषे मर्त्याय ।अहमपो अनयं वावशाना मम देवासो अनु केतमायन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ bhū́mim ǀ adadām ǀ ā́ryāya ǀ ahám ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǀahám ǀ apáḥ ǀ anayam ǀ vāvaśānā́ḥ ǀ máma ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ánu ǀ kétam ǀ āyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: I gave the earth to the venerable (Manu); I have bestowed rain upon the mortal who presents (oblations); I have let forth the sounding waters; the gods obey my will.
verses.wilson_translation: I gave the earth to the venerable (Manu); I have bestowed rain upon the mortal who presents (oblations); I have let forth the sounding waters; the gods obey my will.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं पुरो मंदसानो व्यैरं नव साकं नवतीः शंबरस्य ।शततमं वेश्यं सर्वताता दिवोदासमतिथिग्वं यदावं ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ púraḥ ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀ ví ǀ airam ǀ náva ǀ sākám ǀ navatī́ḥ ǀ śámbarasya ǀśata-tamám ǀ veśyám ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀ dívaḥ-dāsam ǀ atithi-gvám ǀ yát ǀ ā́vam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Exhilarated (by the Somabeverage) I have destroyed the ninety and nine cities ofŚambara, the hundredth I gave to be occupied by Divodāsawhen I protected him,Atithigva, at his sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Exhilarated (by the Somabeverage) I have destroyed the ninety and nine cities ofŚambara, the hundredth I gave to be occupied by Divodāsawhen I protected him,Atithigva, at his sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विरस्तु प्र श्येनः श्येनेभ्य आशुपत्वा ।अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ sáḥ ǀ ví-bhyaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ víḥ ǀ astu ǀ prá ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ śyenébhyaḥ ǀ āśu-pátvā ǀacakráyā ǀ yát ǀ svadháyā ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ havyám ǀ bhárat ǀ mánave ǀ devá-juṣṭam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this bird,Maruts, be pre-eminent over (other) hawks, since with a wheelless car the swift-winged bore the Soma, accepted by the gods, to Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: May this bird,Maruts, be pre-eminent over (other) hawks, since with a wheelless car the swift-winged bore the Soma, accepted by the gods, to Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भरद्यदि विरतो वेविजानः पथोरुणा मनोजवा असर्जि ।तूयं ययौ मधुना सोम्येनोत श्रवो विविदे श्येनो अत्र ॥
verses.transliteration: bhárat ǀ yádi ǀ víḥ ǀ átaḥ ǀ vévijānaḥ ǀ pathā́ ǀ urúṇā ǀ mánaḥ-javāḥ ǀ asarji ǀtū́yam ǀ yayau ǀ mádhunā ǀ somyéna ǀ utá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ vivide ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ átra ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the bird, intimidating (its guardians), carried off from hence (the Soma) it was at large; (flying) swift as thought along the vast path (of the firmament), it went rapidly with the sweet Soma, and the hawks thence acquired the celebrity in this world.
verses.wilson_translation: When the bird, intimidating (its guardians), carried off from hence (the Soma) it was at large; (flying) swift as thought along the vast path (of the firmament), it went rapidly with the sweet Soma, and the hawks thence acquired the celebrity in this world.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋजीपी श्येनो ददमानो अंशुं परावतः शकुनो मंद्रं मदं ।सोमं भरद्दादृहाणो देवावांदिवो अमुष्मादुत्तरादादाय ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛjīpī́ ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ dádamānaḥ ǀ aṃśúm ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ śakunáḥ ǀ mandrám ǀ mádam ǀsómam ǀ bharat ǀ dadṛhāṇáḥ ǀ devá-vān ǀ diváḥ ǀ amúṣmāt ǀ út-tarāt ǀ ā-dā́ya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The straight-flying hawk, conveying the Somafrom afar; the bird, attended by the gods, brought, resolute of purpose, the adorable exhilarating Soma, having taken it from that lofty heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The straight-flying hawk, conveying the Somafrom afar; the bird, attended by the gods, brought, resolute of purpose, the adorable exhilarating Soma, having taken it from that lofty heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवाँ अयुतं च साकं ।अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-dā́ya ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ abharat ǀ sómam ǀ sahásram ǀ savā́n ǀ ayútam ǀ ca ǀ sākám ǀátra ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ ajahāt ǀ árātīḥ ǀ máde ǀ sómasya ǀ mūrā́ḥ ǀ ámūraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Having taken it, the hawk brought the Somawith him to a thousand and ten thousand sacrifices, and this being provided, the performer of many (great) deeds, the unbewildered (Indra) destroyed, in the exhilaration of the Soma, (his) bewildered foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Having taken it, the hawk brought the Somawith him to a thousand and ten thousand sacrifices, and this being provided, the performer of many (great) deeds, the unbewildered (Indra) destroyed, in the exhilaration of the Soma, (his) bewildered foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVII. The Falcon.
hymns.anukramani: ५ वामदेवो गौतमः। श्येनः, ५ इन्द्रो वा। त्रिष्टुप्, ५ शक्वरी।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order.A hundred iron fortresses confined me but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon. Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage.Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty. When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One.Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kṛśānu aimed and loosed the string to strike him. The Falcon bore him from heaven's lofty summit as the swift car of Indra's Friend bore Bhujyu.Then downward hither fell a flying feather of the Bird hasting forward in his journey. And now let Maghavan accept the beaker, white, filled with milk, filled with the shining liquid;The best of sweet meath which the priests have offered: that Indra to his joy may drink, the Hero, that he may take and drink it to his rapture.

verses.sanskrit: गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा ।शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नध श्येनो जवसा निरदीयं ॥
verses.transliteration: gárbhe ǀ nú ǀ sán ǀ ánu ǀ eṣām ǀ avedam ǀ ahám ǀ devā́nām ǀ jánimāni ǀ víśvā ǀśatám ǀ mā ǀ púraḥ ǀ ā́yasīḥ ǀ arakṣan ǀ ádha ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ javásā ǀ níḥ ǀ adīyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Being still in the germ, I have known all the births of these divinities in their order; a hundred bodies of metal confined me, but as a hawk I came forth with speed.
verses.wilson_translation: Being still in the germ, I have known all the births of these divinities in their order; a hundred bodies of metal confined me, but as a hawk I came forth with speed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न घा स मामप जोषं जभाराभीमास त्वक्षसा वीर्येण ।ईर्मा पुरंधिरजहादरातीरुत वाताँ अतरच्छूशुवानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ gha ǀ sáḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ ápa ǀ jóṣam ǀ jabhāra ǀ abhí ǀ īm ǀ āsa ǀ tvákṣasā ǀ vīryéṇa ǀīrmā́ ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ ajahāt ǀ árātīḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā́tān ǀ atarat ǀ śū́śuvānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That embryo did not beguile me into satisfaction, but by the keen energy (of divine wisdom), I triumphed over it; the impeller of all, the sustainer of many, abandoned the foes (of knowledge), and, expanding, passed beyond the winds (of worldly troubles).
verses.wilson_translation: That embryo did not beguile me into satisfaction, but by the keen energy (of divine wisdom), I triumphed over it; the impeller of all, the sustainer of many, abandoned the foes (of knowledge), and, expanding, passed beyond the winds (of worldly troubles).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव यच्छ्येनो अस्वनीदध द्योर्वि यद्यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिं ।सृजद्यदस्मा अव ह क्षिपज्ज्यां कृशानुरस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ yát ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ ásvanīt ǀ ádha ǀ dyóḥ ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ yádi ǀ vā ǀ átaḥ ǀ ūhúḥ ǀ púram-dhim ǀsṛját ǀ yát ǀ asmai ǀ áva ǀ ha ǀ kṣipát ǀ jyā́m ǀ kṛśā́nuḥ ǀ ástā ǀ mánasā ǀ bhuraṇyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the hawk screamed (with exultation) on his descent from heaven, and (the guardians of the Soma) perceived that the Soma was (carried away) by it then, the archer of Kṛśānu, pursuing with the speed of thought, and stringing his bow, let fly an arrow against it.
verses.wilson_translation: When the hawk screamed (with exultation) on his descent from heaven, and (the guardians of the Soma) perceived that the Soma was (carried away) by it then, the archer of Kṛśānu, pursuing with the speed of thought, and stringing his bow, let fly an arrow against it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋजिप्य ईमिंद्रावतो न भुज्युं श्येनो जभार बृहतो अधि ष्णोः ।अंतः पतत्पतत्र्यस्य पर्णमध यामनि प्रसितस्य तद्वेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛjipyáḥ ǀ īm ǀ índra-vataḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhujyúm ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ jabhāra ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ snóḥ ǀantáríti ǀ patat ǀ patatrí ǀ asya ǀ parṇám ǀ ádha ǀ yā́mani ǀ prá-sitasya ǀ tát ǀ véríti véḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The straight-flying hawk carried off the Somafrom above the vast heaven, as (the Aśvinscarried off)Bhujyufrom the region of Indra, and a falling feather from the middle of the bird dropped from him wounded in the conflict.
verses.wilson_translation: The straight-flying hawk carried off the Somafrom above the vast heaven, as (the Aśvinscarried off)Bhujyufrom the region of Indra, and a falling feather from the middle of the bird dropped from him wounded in the conflict.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध श्वेतं कलशं गोभिरक्तमापिप्यानं मघवा शुक्रमंधः ।अध्वर्युभिः प्रयतं मध्वो अग्रमिंद्रो मदाय प्रति धत्पिबध्यै शूरो मदाय प्रति धत्पिबध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ śvetám ǀ kaláśam ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ aktám ǀ ā-pipyānám ǀ maghá-vā ǀ śukrám ǀ ándhaḥ ǀadhvaryú-bhiḥ ǀ prá-yatam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ índraḥ ǀ mádāya ǀ práti ǀ dhat ǀ píbadhyai ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ mádāya ǀ práti ǀ dhat ǀ píbadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now may Maghavanaccept the pure nutitious (sacrificial) food in a white pitcher, mixed with milk and curds, offered by the priests; the upper part of the sweet (beverage) to drink for his exhilaration; may the hero accept (it) to drink for (his) exhilaration.
verses.wilson_translation: Now may Maghavanaccept the pure nutitious (sacrificial) food in a white pitcher, mixed with milk and curds, offered by the priests; the upper part of the sweet (beverage) to drink for his exhilaration; may the hero accept (it) to drink for (his) exhilaration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVIII. Indra-Soma.
hymns.anukramani: ५ वामदेवो गौतमः। इन्द्रः, इन्द्रासोमौ वा। त्रिष्��ुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ALLIED with thee, in this thy friendship, Soma, Indra for man made waters flow together,Slew Ahi, and sent forth the Seven Rivers, and opened as it were obstructed fountains. Indu, with thee for his confederate, Indra swiftly with might pressed down the wheel of Sūrya.What rolled, all life's support, on heaven's high summit was separated from the great oppressor. Indra smote down, Agni consumed, O Indu, the Dasyus ere the noontide in the conflict.Of those who gladly sought a hard-won dwelling he cast down many a thousand with his arrow. Lower than all besides hast thou, O Indra, cast down the Dasyus, abject tribes of Dāsas.Ye drave away, ye put to death the foemen, and took great vengeance with your murdering weapons. So, of a truth, Indra and Soma, Heroes, ye burst the stable of the kine and horses,The stable which the bar or stone obstructed; and piercing through set free the habitations.

verses.sanskrit: त्वा युजा तव तत्सोम सख्य इंद्रो अपो मनवे सस्रुतस्कः ।अहन्नहिमरिणात्सप्त सिंधूनपावृणोदपिहितेव खानि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́ ǀ yujā́ ǀ táva ǀ tát ǀ soma ǀ sakhyé ǀ índraḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ mánave ǀ sa-srútaḥ ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ áriṇāt ǀ saptá ǀ síndhūn ǀ ápa ǀ avṛṇot ǀ ápihitā-iva ǀ khā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through that friendship,Soma, which has united you with your (friend)Indra, he has made the waters flow for man; he has slain Ahi; he has sent forth the seven rivers, and has opened theshut-up sources (of the streams).
verses.wilson_translation: Through that friendship,Soma, which has united you with your (friend)Indra, he has made the waters flow for man; he has slain Ahi; he has sent forth the seven rivers, and has opened theshut-up sources (of the streams).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वा युजा नि खिदत्सूर्यस्येंद्रश्चक्रं सहसा सद्य इंदो ।अधि ष्णुना बृहता वर्तमानं महो द्रुहो अप विश्वायु धायि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́ ǀ yujā́ ǀ ní ǀ khidat ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ índraḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ sáhasā ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ indo íti ǀádhi ǀ snúnā ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ vártamānam ǀ maháḥ ǀ druháḥ ǀ ápa ǀ viśvá-āyu ǀ dhāyi ǁ
verses.english_translation: With you,Soma, for his ally,Indrahas quickly taken off by force the wheel of the chariot of the sun, abiding above with the vast and stationary (firmament); the everywhere going wheel (of the car) of the great oppressor has been taken away.
verses.wilson_translation: With you,Soma, for his ally,Indrahas quickly taken off by force the wheel of the chariot of the sun, abiding above with the vast and stationary (firmament); the everywhere going wheel (of the car) of the great oppressor has been taken away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहन्निंद्रो अदहदग्निरिंदो पुरा दस्यून्मध्यंदिनादभीके ।दुर्गे दुरोणे क्रत्वा न यातां पुरू सहस्रा शर्वा नि बर्हीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áhan ǀ índraḥ ǀ ádahat ǀ agníḥ ǀ indo íti ǀ purā́ ǀ dásyūn ǀ madhyándināt ǀ abhī́ke ǀduḥ-gé ǀ duroṇé ǀ krátvā ǀ ná ǀ yātā́m ǀ purú ǀ sahásrā ǀ śárvā ǀ ní ǀ barhīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrahas slain the Dasyus,Soma, in battle;Agnihas consumed them before the noon; he (Indra) has destroyed the whole of many thosands, as (robbers are the destroyers of those) going upon (their own) business, in a difficult and dangerous (plural ce).
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas slain the Dasyus,Soma, in battle;Agnihas consumed them before the noon; he (Indra) has destroyed the whole of many thosands, as (robbers are the destroyers of those) going upon (their own) business, in a difficult and dangerous (plural ce).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्मात्सीमधमाँ इंद्र दस्यून्विशो दासीरकृणोरप्रशस्ताः ।अबाधेथाममृणतं नि शत्रूनविंदेथामपचितिं वधत्रैः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasmāt ǀ sīm ǀ adhamā́n ǀ indra ǀ dásyūn ǀ víśaḥ ǀ dā́sīḥ ǀ akṛṇoḥ ǀ apra-śastā́ḥ ǀábādhethām ǀ ámṛṇatam ǀ ní ǀ śátrūn ǀ ávindethām ǀ ápa-citim ǀ vádhatraiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, you have made these Dasyusdevoid of all (good qualities); you have made the races without rites abject; may you, (Somaand Indra), repel (and) destroy (your) enemies; accept (our) homage for their destruction.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, you have made these Dasyusdevoid of all (good qualities); you have made the races without rites abject; may you, (Somaand Indra), repel (and) destroy (your) enemies; accept (our) homage for their destruction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा सत्यं मघवाना युवं तदिंद्रश्च सोमोर्वमश्व्यं गोः ।आदर्दृतमपिहितान्यश्ना रिरिचथुः क्षाश्चित्ततृदाना ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ satyám ǀ magha-vānā ǀ yuvám ǀ tát ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ soma ǀ ūrvám ǀ áśvyam ǀ góḥ ǀā́ ǀ adardṛtam ǀ ápi-hitāni ǀ áśnā ǀ riricáthuḥ ǀ kṣā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ tatṛdānā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Possessors of wealth, destroyers of foes,Indraand Soma, it is indeed true that you have distributed great numbers of horses, and of the cattle which had been concealed and the land which you had recovered by your strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Possessors of wealth, destroyers of foes,Indraand Soma, it is indeed true that you have distributed great numbers of horses, and of the cattle which had been concealed and the land which you had recovered by your strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COME, lauded, unto us with powers and succours, O Indra, with thy Tawny Steeds; exulting,Past even the foeman's manifold libations, glorified with our hymns, true Wealth-bestower. Man's Friend, to this our sacrifice he cometh marking how he is called by Soma-pressers.Fearless, and conscious that his Steeds are noble, he joyeth with the Soma-pouring heroes. Make his cars hear, that he may show his vigour and may be joyful in the way he loveth.May mighty Indra pouring forth in bounty bestow on us good roads and perfect safety; He who with succour comes to his implorer, the singer here who with his song invites him;He who himself sets to the pole swift Coursers, he who hath hundreds, thousands, Thunder-wielder. O Indra Maghavan, by thee protected may we be thine, princes and priests and singers,Sharing the riches sent from lofty heaven which yields much food, and all desire its bounty.

verses.sanskrit: आ नः स्तुत उप वाजेभिरूती इंद्र याहि हरिभिर्मंदसानः ।तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना पुरूण्यांगूषेभिर्गृणानः सत्यराधाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ stutáḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ índra ǀ yāhí ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀtiráḥ ǀ cit ǀ aryáḥ ǀ sávanā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ āṅgūṣébhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ satyá-rādhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Honoured with accepted (sacrificial) viands, come,Indra, exulting, with your steeds, to our many rites, for our protection; you who are the lord, glorified by hymns, whose wealth is truth.
verses.wilson_translation: Honoured with accepted (sacrificial) viands, come,Indra, exulting, with your steeds, to our many rites, for our protection; you who are the lord, glorified by hymns, whose wealth is truth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ हि ष्मा याति नर्यश्चिकित्वान्हूयमानः सोतृभिरुप यज्ञं ।स्वश्वो यो अभीरुर्मन्यमानः सुष्वाणेभिर्मदति सं ह वीरैः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ yā́ti ǀ náryaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ hūyámānaḥ ǀ sotṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yajñám ǀsu-áśvaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ábhīruḥ ǀ mányamānaḥ ǀ su-svānébhiḥ ǀ mádati ǀ sám ǀ ha ǀ vīráiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then her shattered wagon reposed (on the bank) of the Vipās' (river), and she departed from afar.
verses.wilson_translation: Then her shattered wagon reposed (on the bank) of the Vipās' (river), and she departed from afar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: श्रावयेदस्य कर्णा वाजयध्यै जुष्टामनु प्र दिशं मंदयध्यै ।उद्वावृषाणो राधसे तुविष्मान्करन्न इंद्रः सुतीर्थाभयं च ॥
verses.transliteration: śraváya ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ kárṇā ǀ vājayádhyai ǀ júṣṭām ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ díśam ǀ mandayádhyai ǀut-vavṛṣāṇáḥ ǀ rā́dhase ǀ túviṣmān ǀ kárat ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-tīrthā́ ǀ ábhayam ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have spread abroad upon the earth, by your contrivance, the swollen Sindhuwhen arrested (on its course).
verses.wilson_translation: You have spread abroad upon the earth, by your contrivance, the swollen Sindhuwhen arrested (on its course).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा यो गंता नाधमानमूती इत्था विप्रं हवमानं गृणंतं ।उप त्मनि दधानो धुर्याशून्त्सहस्राणि शतानि वज्रबाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ yáḥ ǀ gántā ǀ nā́dhamānam ǀ ūtī́ ǀ itthā́ ǀ vípram ǀ hávamānam ǀ gṛṇántam ǀúpa ǀ tmáni ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ dhurí ǀ āśū́n ǀ sahásrāṇi ǀ śatā́ni ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By valour you have carried off the wealth ofŚuṣṇa, when you had demolished his cities.
verses.wilson_translation: By valour you have carried off the wealth ofŚuṣṇa, when you had demolished his cities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वोतासो मघवन्निंद्र विप्रा वयं ते स्याम सूरयो गृणंतः ।भेजानासो बृहद्दिवस्य राय आकाय्यस्य दावने पुरुक्षोः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́-ūtāsaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ víprāḥ ǀ vayám ǀ te ǀ syāma ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀbhejānā́saḥ ǀ bṛhát-divasya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā-kāyyásya ǀ dāváne ǀ puru-kṣóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have slain the slaveŚambara, the son Kulitara hurling him off the huge mountain.
verses.wilson_translation: You have slain the slaveŚambara, the son Kulitara hurling him off the huge mountain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: You have slain the five hundreds and thousands (of the followers) of the slave Varin, (surrounding) him like the fellies (round the spokes of the wheel).
verses.wilson_translation: You have slain the five hundreds and thousands (of the followers) of the slave Varin, (surrounding) him like the fellies (round the spokes of the wheel).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: You,Indra, who areŚatakratu, have made Parāvṛj, the son of Agru, participant in sacred hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, who areŚatakratu, have made Parāvṛj, the son of Agru, participant in sacred hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: The lord of acts, the wise Indra, has borne across (their difficulties),Turvaśasand Yadu, when denied inauguration.
verses.wilson_translation: The lord of acts, the wise Indra, has borne across (their difficulties),Turvaśasand Yadu, when denied inauguration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: You have slain at once those twoĀryas,Arṇaand Citraratha, (dwellig) on the opposite (bank) of the Sarayu.
verses.wilson_translation: You have slain at once those twoĀryas,Arṇaand Citraratha, (dwellig) on the opposite (bank) of the Sarayu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)
