verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ yé ǀ cakrúḥ ǀ su-vṛ́tam ǀ su-cétasaḥ ǀ ávi-hvarantam ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ pári ǀ dhyáyā ǀtā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ asyá ǀ sávanasya ǀ pītáye ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ vedayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you respectfully,VājasandṚbhus, to drink of this libation, for you are the wise sages, who, by mental meditation, made the well-constructed undeviating car (of the Aśvins).
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you respectfully,VājasandṚbhus, to drink of this libation, for you are the wise sages, who, by mental meditation, made the well-constructed undeviating car (of the Aśvins).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वो वाजा ऋभवः सुप्रवाचनं देवेषु विभ्वो अभवन्महित्वनं ।जिव्री यत्संता पितरा सनाजुरा पुनर्युवाना चरथाय तक्षथ ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ su-pravācanám ǀ devéṣu ǀ vi-bhvaḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ mahi-tvanám ǀjívrī íti ǀ yát ǀ sántā ǀ pitárā ǀ sanā-júrā ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yúvānā ǀ caráthāya ǀ tákṣatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore,Vāja,Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, was your greatness proclaimed among the gods, that you made your aged and inform parents young (and able) to go (withere they would).
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore,Vāja,Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, was your greatness proclaimed among the gods, that you made your aged and inform parents young (and able) to go (withere they would).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एकं वि चक्र चमसं चतुर्वयं निश्चर्मणो गामरिणीत धीतिभिः ।अथा देवेष्वमृतत्वमानश श्रुष्टी वाजा ऋभवस्तद्व उक्थ्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ékam ǀ ví ǀ cakra ǀ camasám ǀ cátuḥ-vayam ǀ níḥ ǀ cármaṇaḥ ǀ gā́m ǀ ariṇīta ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀátha ǀ devéṣu ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśa ǀ śruṣṭī́ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ukthyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have made the single ladle fourfold; by your (marvellous) acts you have clothed the cow with a (new) hide; therefore you have obtained immortality among the gods; such acts,VājasandṚbhus, are to be eagerly glorified.
verses.wilson_translation: You have made the single ladle fourfold; by your (marvellous) acts you have clothed the cow with a (new) hide; therefore you have obtained immortality among the gods; such acts,VājasandṚbhus, are to be eagerly glorified.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुतो रयिः प्रथमश्रवस्तमो वाजश्रुतासो यमजीजनन्नरः ।विभ्वतष्टो विदथेषु प्रवाच्यो यं देवासोऽवथा स विचर्षणिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhutáḥ ǀ rayíḥ ǀ prathamáśravaḥ-tamaḥ ǀ vā́ja-śrutāsaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ájījanan ǀ náraḥ ǀvibhva-taṣṭáḥ ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ pra-vā́cyaḥ ǀ yám ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ávatha ǀ sáḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From theṚbhusmay wealth, the best and most productive of food, (come to me); that which the leaders of rites renowned together with the Vājas, have engendered; that which has been fabricated by Vibhvan and is to be celebrated at sacrifice; that which, deities you protect, that is to be beheld.
verses.wilson_translation: From theṚbhusmay wealth, the best and most productive of food, (come to me); that which the leaders of rites renowned together with the Vājas, have engendered; that which has been fabricated by Vibhvan and is to be celebrated at sacrifice; that which, deities you protect, that is to be beheld.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स वाज्यर्वा स ऋषिर्वचस्यया स शूरो अस्ता पृतनासु दुष्टरः ।स रायस्पोषं स सुवीर्यं दधे यं वाजो विभ्वाँ ऋभवो यमाविषुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ árvā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ vacasyáyā ǀ sáḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ ástā ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ dustáraḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ sáḥ ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ dadhe ǀ yám ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ví-bhvā ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ā́viṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is vigorous and skilled in war, he is a ṛṣi worthy of homage, he is a hero, the discomfiter of foes, invincible in battles, he is possessed of ample wealth, and (is blessed) with excellent posterity, whom Vājaand Vibhvan, whom theṚbhusprotect.
verses.wilson_translation: He is vigorous and skilled in war, he is a ṛṣi worthy of homage, he is a hero, the discomfiter of foes, invincible in battles, he is possessed of ample wealth, and (is blessed) with excellent posterity, whom Vājaand Vibhvan, whom theṚbhusprotect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: श्रेष्ठं वः पेशो अधि धायि दर्शत��� स्तोमो वाजा ऋभवस्तं जुजुष्टन ।धीरासो हि ष्ठा कवयो विपश्चितस्तान्व एना ब्रह्मणा वेदयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: śréṣṭham ǀ vaḥ ǀ péśaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhāyi ǀ darśatám ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ tám ǀ jujuṣṭana ǀdhī́rāsaḥ ǀ hí ǀ sthá ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ vipaḥ-cítaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ vaḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ ā́ ǀ vedayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: An excellent and agreeable form has been assumed by you; (this is our own) praise;VājasandṚbhusbe gratified (thereby), for you are wise, experienced, and intelligent; such we make you known (to be) by this (our) prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: An excellent and agreeable form has been assumed by you; (this is our own) praise;VājasandṚbhusbe gratified (thereby), for you are wise, experienced, and intelligent; such we make you known (to be) by this (our) prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयमस्मभ्यं धिषणाभ्यस्परि विद्वांसो विश्वा नर्याणि भोजना ।द्युमंतं वाजं वृषशुष्ममुत्तममा नो रयिमृभवस्तक्षता वयः ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dhiṣáṇābhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vidvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ náryāṇi ǀ bhójanā ǀdyu-mántam ǀ vā́jam ǀ vṛ́ṣa-śuṣmam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ takṣata ǀ ā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you who are wise, (bestow) upon us, in requital of our praises, all enjoyments that are good for man and fabricate for us,Ṛbhus, riches and food, resplendent invigorating, overpowering (foes), and most excellent.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you who are wise, (bestow) upon us, in requital of our praises, all enjoyments that are good for man and fabricate for us,Ṛbhus, riches and food, resplendent invigorating, overpowering (foes), and most excellent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इह प्रजामिह रयिं रराणा इह श्रवो वीरवत्तक्षता नः ।येन वयं चितयेमात्यन्यांतं वाजं चित्रमृभवो ददा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ ihá ǀ rayím ǀ rárāṇāḥ ǀ ihá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ vīrá-vat ǀ takṣata ǀ naḥ ǀyéna ǀ vayám ǀ citáyema ǀ áti ǀ anyā́n ǀ tám ǀ vā́jam ǀ citrám ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ dada ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gratified (by your worship), fabricate for us, on this occasion, progeny and wealth, and reputation, with numerous adherents; grant to us,Ṛbhus, abundant sustenance wherewith we may greatly excel others.
verses.wilson_translation: Gratified (by your worship), fabricate for us, on this occasion, progeny and wealth, and reputation, with numerous adherents; grant to us,Ṛbhus, abundant sustenance wherewith we may greatly excel others.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVII. Ṛbhus.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COME to our sacrifice, Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans, Gods, by the paths which Gods are wont to travel,As ye, gay Gods, accept in splendid weather the sacrifice among these folk of Manus. May these rites please you in your heart and spirit; may the drops clothed in oil this day approach you.May the abundant juices bear you onward to power and strength, and, when imbibed, delight you. Your threefold going near is God-appointed, so praise is given you, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans.So, Manus-like, mid younger folk I offer, to you who are aloft in heaven, the Soma. Strong, with fair chains of gold and jaws of iron, ye have a splendid car and well-fed horses.Ye Sons of Strength, ye progeny of Indra, to you the best is offered to delight you. Ṛbhukṣans! him, for handy wealth, the mightiest comrade in the fight,Him, Indra's equal, we invoke, most bounteous ever, rich in steeds. The mortal man whom, Ṛbhus, ye and Indra favour with your help,Must be successful, by his thoughts, at sacrifice and with the steed. O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, free for us the paths to sacrifice,Ye Princes, lauded, that we may press forward to each point of heaven. O Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, ye Nāsatyas, Indra, bless this wealth,And, before other men's, the steed, that ample riches may be won.

verses.sanskrit: उप नो वाजा अध्वरमृभुक्षा देवा यात पथिभिर्देवयानैः ।यथा यज्ञं मनुषो विक्ष्वासु दधिध्वे रण्वाः सुदिनेष्वह्नां ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ ṛbhukṣāḥ ǀ dévāḥ ǀ yātá ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ deva-yā́naiḥ ǀyáthā ǀ yajñám ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ vikṣú ǀ āsú ǀ dadhidhvé ǀ raṇvāḥ ǀ su-díneṣu ǀ áhnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Vājas,Ṛbhus, come to our sacrifice by the path travelled by the gods, inasmuch as you, gracious (Ṛbhus), have maintained sacrifice among the people, (the progeny) of Manu, for (the sake of) securing the prosperous course of days.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Vājas,Ṛbhus, come to our sacrifice by the path travelled by the gods, inasmuch as you, gracious (Ṛbhus), have maintained sacrifice among the people, (the progeny) of Manu, for (the sake of) securing the prosperous course of days.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते वो हृदे मनसे संतु यज्ञा जुष्टासो अद्य घृतनिर्णिजो गुः ।प्र वः सुतासो हरयंत पूर्णाः क्रत्वे दक्षाय हर्षयंत पीताः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ vaḥ ǀ hṛdé ǀ mánase ǀ santu ǀ yajñā́ḥ ǀ júṣṭāsaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ ghṛtá-nirnijaḥ ǀ guḥ ǀprá ǀ vaḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ harayanta ǀ pūrṇā́ḥ ǀ krátve ǀ dákṣāya ǀ harṣayanta ǀ pītā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May these sacrifices be (acceptable) to you in heart and mind; may today the sufficient (juices) mixed with butter to you; the full libations are prepared for you; may they, when drunk, animate you for glorious deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May these sacrifices be (acceptable) to you in heart and mind; may today the sufficient (juices) mixed with butter to you; the full libations are prepared for you; may they, when drunk, animate you for glorious deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्र्युदायं देवहितं यथा वः स्तोमो वाजा ऋभुक्षणो ददे वः ।जुह्वे मनुष्वदुपरासु विक्षु युष्मे सचा बृहद्दिवेषु सोमं ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-udāyám ǀ devá-hitam ǀ yáthā ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ dadé ǀ vaḥ ǀjuhvé ǀ manuṣvát ǀ úparāsu ǀ vikṣú ǀ yuṣmé íti ǀ sácā ǀ bṛhát-diveṣu ǀ sómam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the offering suited to the gods at the third (daily) sacrifice supports, you,Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans; as the praise (then recited supports you); therefore, like Manu, I offer you the Somajuice, along with the very radiant (deities) among the people assembled at the solemnity.
verses.wilson_translation: As the offering suited to the gods at the third (daily) sacrifice supports, you,Vājas, Ṛbhukṣans; as the praise (then recited supports you); therefore, like Manu, I offer you the Somajuice, along with the very radiant (deities) among the people assembled at the solemnity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पीवोअश्वाः शुचद्रथा हि भूतायःशिप्रा वाजिनः सुनिष्काः ।इंद्रस्य सूनो शवसो नपातोऽनु वश्चेत्यग्रियं मदाय ॥
verses.transliteration: pī́vaḥ-aśvāḥ ǀ śucát-rathāḥ ǀ hí ǀ bhūtá ǀ áyaḥ-śiprāḥ ǀ vājinaḥ ǀ su-niṣkā́ḥ ǀíndrasya ǀ sūno íti ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ napātaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vaḥ ǀ ceti ǀ agriyám ǀ mádāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vājins, you are borne by stout horses mounted on a brilliant car, have jaws of metal and are possessed of treasures; sons of Indra, grandsons of strength, this last sacrifice is for your exhilaration.
verses.wilson_translation: Vājins, you are borne by stout horses mounted on a brilliant car, have jaws of metal and are possessed of treasures; sons of Indra, grandsons of strength, this last sacrifice is for your exhilaration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुमृभुक्षणो रयिं वाजे वाजिंतमं युजं ।इंद्रस्वंतं हवामहे सदासातममश्विनं ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhúm ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ rayím ǀ vā́je ǀ vājín-tamam ǀ yújam ǀíndrasvantam ǀ havāmahe ǀ sadā-sā́tamam ǀ aśvínam ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you, Ṛbhukṣans, for splendid wealth, mutually co-operating, most invigorating in war, affecting the senses, ever munificent, and comprehending horses.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you, Ṛbhukṣans, for splendid wealth, mutually co-operating, most invigorating in war, affecting the senses, ever munificent, and comprehending horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सेदृभवो यमवथ यूयमिंद्रश्च मर्त्यं ।स धीभिरस्तु सनिता मेधसाता सो अर्वता ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ yám ǀ ávatha ǀ yūyám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ mártyam ǀsáḥ ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ astu ǀ sánitā ǀ medhá-sātā ǀ sáḥ ǀ árvatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the man whom you,Ṛbhusand Indra, favour, be ever liberal by his acts, and possessed of a horse at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May the man whom you,Ṛbhusand Indra, favour, be ever liberal by his acts, and possessed of a horse at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि नो वाजा ऋभुक्षणः पथश्चितन यष्टवे ।अस्मभ्यं सूरयः स्तुता विश्वा आशास्तरीषणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ patháḥ ǀ citana ǀ yáṣṭave ǀasmábhyam ǀ sūrayaḥ ǀ stutā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ tarīṣáṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs, direct us in the way to sacrifice; for you, who are intelligent, being glorified (by us), are able to traverse all the quarters (of space).
verses.wilson_translation: Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs, direct us in the way to sacrifice; for you, who are intelligent, being glorified (by us), are able to traverse all the quarters (of space).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं नो वाजा ऋभुक्षण इंद्र नासत्या रयिं ।समश्वं चर्षणिभ्य आ पुरु शस्त मघत्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ naḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ índra ǀ nā́satyā ǀ rayím ǀsám ǀ áśvam ǀ carṣaṇí-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ purú ǀ śasta ǀ magháttaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs,Indra,Nāsatyas, command that ample wealth with horses be sent to men for their enrichment.
verses.wilson_translation: Vājas, Ṛbhukṣaṇs,Indra,Nāsatyas, command that ample wealth with horses be sent to men for their enrichment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVIII. Dadhikris.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FROM you two came the gifts in days aforetime which Trasadasyu granted to the Pūrus.Ye gave the winner of our fields and plough-lands, and the strong smiter who subdued the Dasyus. And ye gave mighty Dadhikrās, the giver of many gifts, who visiteth all people,Impetuous hawk, swift and of varied colour, like a brave King whom each true man must honour. Whom, as ’twere down a precipice, swift rushing, each Pūru praises and his heart rejoices,—Springing forth like a hero fain for battle, whirling the car and flying like the tempest. Who gaineth precious booty in the combats and moveth, winning spoil, among the cattle;Shown in bright colour, looking on the assemblies, beyond the churl, to worship of the living. Loudly the folk cry after him in battles, as ’twere a thief who steals away a garment;Speeding to glory, or a herd of cattle, even as a hungry falcon swooping downward. And, fain to come forth first amid these armies, this way and that with rows of cars he rushes,Gay like a bridesman, making him a garland, tossing the dust, champing the rein that holds him. And that strong Steed, victorious and faithful, obedient with his body in the combat,Speeding straight on amid the swiftly pressing, casts o’er his brows the dust he tosses upward. And at his thunder, like the roar of heaven, those who attack tremble and are affrighted;For when he fights against embattled thousands, dread is he in his striving; none may stay him. The people praise the overpowering swiftness of this fleet Steed who giveth men abundance.Of him they say when drawing back from battle. Dadhikrās hath sped forward with his thousands. Dadhikrās hath o’erspread the Fivefold People with vigour, as the Sun lightens the waters.May the strong Steed who winneth hundreds, thousands, requite with sweetness these my words and praises.

verses.sanskrit: उतो हि वां दात्रा संति पूर्वा या पूरुभ्यस्त्रसदस्युर्नितोशे ।क्षेत्रासां ददथुरुर्वरासां घनं दस्युभ्यो अभिभूतिमुग्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: utó íti ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ dātrā́ ǀ sánti ǀ pū́rvā ǀ yā́ ǀ pūrú-bhyaḥ ǀ trasádasyuḥ ǀ ni-tośé ǀkṣetra-sā́m ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ urvarā-sā́m ǀ ghanám ǀ dásyu-bhyaḥ ǀ abhí-bhūtim ǀ ugrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Trasadasyuhas bestowed upon many the ancient (gifts) which were obtained by the liberal (prince) through your (favour, Heaven and Earth) you two have given a horse, a son, a weapon (for the destruction) of the Dasyus, fierce and foe-subduing.
verses.wilson_translation: Trasadasyuhas bestowed upon many the ancient (gifts) which were obtained by the liberal (prince) through your (favour, Heaven and Earth) you two have given a horse, a son, a weapon (for the destruction) of the Dasyus, fierce and foe-subduing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत वाजिनं पुरुनिष्षिध्वानं दधिक्रामु ददथुर्विश्वकृष्टिं ।ऋजिप्यं श्येनं प्रुषितप्सुमाशुं चर्कृत्यमर्यो नृपतिं न शूरं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vājínam ǀ puruniḥ-sídhvānam ǀ dadhi-krā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭim ǀṛjipyám ǀ śyenám ǀ pruṣitá-psum ǀ āśúm ǀ carkṛ́tyam ǀ aryáḥ ǀ nṛ-pátim ǀ ná ǀ śū́ram ǁ
verses.english_translation: And you two have given the swift Dadhikrā, the repeller of many (foes), the defender of all men, the straight-going, the graceful-moving, the resplendent, the rapid, the destroyer of enemies like a heroic prince.
verses.wilson_translation: And you two have given the swift Dadhikrā, the repeller of many (foes), the defender of all men, the straight-going, the graceful-moving, the resplendent, the rapid, the destroyer of enemies like a heroic prince.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यं सीमनु प्रवतेव द्रवंतं विश्वः पूरुर्मदति हर्षमाणः ।पड्भिर्गृध्यंतं मेधयुं न शूरं रथतुरं वातमिव ध्रजंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ sīm ǀ ánu ǀ pravátā-iva ǀ drávantam ǀ víśvaḥ ǀ pūrúḥ ǀ mádati ǀ hárṣamāṇaḥ ǀpaṭ-bhíḥ ǀ gṛ́dhyantam ǀ medha-yúm ǀ ná ǀ śū́ram ǀ ratha-túram ǀ vā́tam-iva ǀ dhrájantam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom all men, rejoicing, praise, rushing everywhere, as if down a precipice, springing with his feet like a hero eager for war, drawing a car, and going as swift as the wind.
verses.wilson_translation: Whom all men, rejoicing, praise, rushing everywhere, as if down a precipice, springing with his feet like a hero eager for war, drawing a car, and going as swift as the wind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यः स्मारुंधानो गध्या समत्सु सनुतरश्चरति गोषु गच्छन् ।आविर्ऋजीको विदथा निचिक्यत्तिरो अरतिं पर्याप आयोः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ sma ǀ ā-rundhānáḥ ǀ gádhyā ǀ samát-su ǀ sánu-taraḥ ǀ cárati ǀ góṣu ǀ gácchan ǀāvíḥ-ṛjīkaḥ ǀ vidáthā ǀ ni-cíkyat ǀ tiráḥ ǀ aratím ǀ pári ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, opposing the mingled multitude in battles, rushes eager, passing through the regions, whose vigour is manifestl, who, understanding what is to be known, puts to shame the adversary of the (pious) man.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, opposing the mingled multitude in battles, rushes eager, passing through the regions, whose vigour is manifestl, who, understanding what is to be known, puts to shame the adversary of the (pious) man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्मैनं वस्त्रमथिं न तायुमनु क्रोशंति क्षितयो भरेषु ।नीचायमानं जसुरिं न श्येनं श्रवश्चाच्छा पशुमच्च यूथं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ enam ǀ vastra-máthim ǀ ná ǀ tāyúm ǀ ánu ǀ krośanti ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ bháreṣu ǀnīcā́ ǀ áyamānam ǀ jásurim ǀ ná ǀ śyenám ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ áccha ǀ paśu-mát ǀ ca ǀ yūthám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom men call after in battles, as after a thief carrying off a garment, or as (after) a hungry hawk pouncing (upon his prey); they call after him, hastening to obtain food, or a herd of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Whom men call after in battles, as after a thief carrying off a garment, or as (after) a hungry hawk pouncing (upon his prey); they call after him, hastening to obtain food, or a herd of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्मासु प्रथमः सरिष्यन्नि वेवेति श्रेणिभी रथानां ।स्रजं कृण्वानो जन्यो न शुभ्वा रेणुं रेरिहत्किरणं ददश्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ āsu ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ sariṣyán ǀ ní ǀ veveti ǀ śréṇi-bhiḥ ǀ ráthānām ǀsrájam ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ jányaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śúbhvā ǀ reṇúm ǀ rérihat ǀ kiráṇam ǀ dadaśvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: And who, issuing forth the first in those encounters, rushes in various directions with rows of chariots; like an elegant (courser), friendly to man, decorated with a garland, raising the dust, and champing his bit.
verses.wilson_translation: And who, issuing forth the first in those encounters, rushes in various directions with rows of chariots; like an elegant (courser), friendly to man, decorated with a garland, raising the dust, and champing his bit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्य वाजी सहुरिर्ऋतावा शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये ।तुरं यतीषु तुरयन्नृजिप्योऽधि भ्रुवोः किरते रेणुमृंजन् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ śúśrūṣamāṇaḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ sa-maryé ǀtúram ǀ yatī́ṣu ǀ turáyan ǀ ṛjipyáḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ bhruvóḥ ǀ kirate ǀ reṇúm ǀ ṛñján ǁ
verses.english_translation: And that swift (horse) enduring in battle, bestowing food, and doing service with his limbs, rushing swiftly upon the quick-moving (host of the enemy), going straight onward, and tossing up the dust, throws it above his brows.
verses.wilson_translation: And that swift (horse) enduring in battle, bestowing food, and doing service with his limbs, rushing swiftly upon the quick-moving (host of the enemy), going straight onward, and tossing up the dust, throws it above his brows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्मास्य तन्यतोरिव द्योर्ऋघायतो अभियुजो भयंते ।यदा सहस्रमभि षीमयोधीद्दुर्वर्तुः स्मा भवति भीम ऋंजन् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ tanyatóḥ-iva ǀ dyóḥ ǀ ṛghāyatáḥ ǀ abhi-yújaḥ ǀ bhayante ǀyadā́ ǀ sahásram ǀ abhí ǀ sīm ǀ áyodhīt ǀ duḥ-vártuḥ ǀ sma ǀ bhavati ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ṛñján ǁ
verses.english_translation: And the adversaries of that foe-destroying steed, like (those) of the brilliant thunderbolt, are alarmed; for when he contends, even against thousands on every side, then, rousing (his spirit), he is fearful and irresistible.
verses.wilson_translation: And the adversaries of that foe-destroying steed, like (those) of the brilliant thunderbolt, are alarmed; for when he contends, even against thousands on every side, then, rousing (his spirit), he is fearful and irresistible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्मास्य पनयंति जना जूतिं कृष्टिप्रो अभिभूतिमाशोः ।उतैनमाहुः समिथे वियंतः परा दधिक्रा असरत्सहस्रैः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ panayanti ǀ jánāḥ ǀ jūtím ǀ kṛṣṭi-práḥ ǀ abhí-bhūtim ǀ āśóḥ ǀutá ǀ enam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ sam-ithé ǀ vi-yántaḥ ǀ párā ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ asarat ǀ sahásraiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men praise the overpowering rapidty of that fleet (steed), who is the accomplisher (of the desires) of mankind, and following him to battle, they have said, Dadhikrā with (his) thousands has gone forth against the foe.
verses.wilson_translation: Men praise the overpowering rapidty of that fleet (steed), who is the accomplisher (of the desires) of mankind, and following him to battle, they have said, Dadhikrā with (his) thousands has gone forth against the foe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ दधिक्राः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान ।सहस्रसाः शतसा वाज्यर्वा पृणक्तु मध्वा समिमा वचांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ páñca ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ apáḥ ǀ tatāna ǀsahasra-sā́ḥ ǀ śata-sā́ḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ árvā ǀ pṛṇáktu ǀ mádhvā ǀ sám ǀ imā́ ǀ vácāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dadhikrā has spread abroad the five classes of beings by his strength, as the sun (diffuses) the waters by his radiance; may he, the giver of hundreds and thousands, associate these praises with agreeable (rewards).
verses.wilson_translation: Dadhikrā has spread abroad the five classes of beings by his strength, as the sun (diffuses) the waters by his radiance; may he, the giver of hundreds and thousands, associate these praises with agreeable (rewards).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIX Dadhikrās.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now give we praise to Dadhikrās the rapid, and mention in our laud the Earth and Heaven.May the Dawns flushing move me to exertion, and bear me safely over every trouble. I praise the mighty Steed who fills my spirit, the Stallion Dadhikrāvan rich in bounties,Whom, swift of foot and shining bright as Agni, ye, Varuṇa and Mitra, gave to Pūrus. Him who hath honoured, when the flame is kindled at break of dawn, the Courser Dadhikrāvan,Him, of one mind with Varuṇa and Mitra may Aditi make free from all transgression. When we remember mighty Dadhikrāvan our food and strength, then the blest name of Maruts,Varuṇa, Mitra, we invoke for welfare, and Agni, and the thunder-wielding Indra. Both sides invoke him as they call on Indra when they stir forth and turn to sacrificing.To us have Varuṇa and Mitra granted the Courser Dadhikrās, a guide for mortals. So have I glorified with praise strong Dadhikrāvan, conquering Steed.Sweet may he make our mouths; may he prolong the days we have to live.

verses.sanskrit: आशुं दधिक्रां तमु नु ष्टवाम दिवस्पृथिव्या उत चर्किराम ।उच्छंतीर्मामुषसः सूदयंत्वति विश्वानि दुरितानि पर्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: āśúm ǀ dadhi-krā́m ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ stavāma ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ carkirāma ǀucchántīḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sūdayantu ǀ áti ǀ víśvāni ǀ duḥ-itā́ni ǀ parṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Verily we praise that swift Dadhikrā and scatter (proved before him) from heaven and earth; may the gloom-dispelling dawns preserve for me (all good things), and bear me beyond all evils.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily we praise that swift Dadhikrā and scatter (proved before him) from heaven and earth; may the gloom-dispelling dawns preserve for me (all good things), and bear me beyond all evils.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महश्चर्कर्म्यर्वतः क्रतुप्रा दधिक्राव्णः पुरुवारस्य वृष्णः ।यं पूरुभ्यो दीदिवांसं नाग्निं ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा ततुरिं ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ carkarmi ǀ árvataḥ ǀ kratu-prā́ḥ ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ puru-vā́rasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀyám ǀ pūrú-bhyaḥ ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ ná ǀ agním ǀ dadáthuḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ táturim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fulfiller of religious rites, I reiterate the praise of the great Dadhikrā, the liberal, many-honoured showerer (of benefits), whom Mitraand Varuṇagave for the good of many, the transporter (beyond calamity), as brilliant as Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Fulfiller of religious rites, I reiterate the praise of the great Dadhikrā, the liberal, many-honoured showerer (of benefits), whom Mitraand Varuṇagave for the good of many, the transporter (beyond calamity), as brilliant as Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो अश्वस्य दधिक्राव्णो अकारीत्समिद्धे अग्ना उषसो व्युष्टौ ।अनागसं तमदितिः कृणोतु स मित्रेण वरुणेना सजोषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ ákārīt ǀ sám-iddhe ǀ agnáu ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀánāgasam ǀ tám ǀ áditiḥ ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ sáḥ ǀ mitréṇa ǀ váruṇena ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Aditi, consentient with Mitraand Varuṇarender him free from sin who has performed the worship of the steed Dadhikrā, when the fire has been kindled at the opening of the dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: May Aditi, consentient with Mitraand Varuṇarender him free from sin who has performed the worship of the steed Dadhikrā, when the fire has been kindled at the opening of the dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्राव्ण इष ऊर्जो महो यदमन्महि मरुतां नाम भद्रं ।स्वस्तये वरुणं मित्रमग्निं हवामह इंद्रं वज्रबाहुं ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ ūrjáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ yát ǀ ámanmahi ǀ marútām ǀ nā́ma ǀ bhadrám ǀsvastáye ǀ váruṇam ǀ mitrám ǀ agním ǀ hávāmahe ǀ índram ǀ vájra-bāhum ǁ
verses.english_translation: While we glorify the name of the great Dadhikrā the means of sustenance and of strength, the prosperity of those who praise (him), let us invoke (also) for our welfare Varuṇa,Mitra,Agni, and Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: While we glorify the name of the great Dadhikrā the means of sustenance and of strength, the prosperity of those who praise (him), let us invoke (also) for our welfare Varuṇa,Mitra,Agni, and Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रमिवेदुभये वि ह्वयंत उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयंतः ।दधिक्रामु सूदनं मर्त्याय ददथुर्मित्रावरुणा नो अश्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: índram-iva ǀ ít ǀ ubháye ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ ut-ī́rāṇāḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ upa-prayántaḥ ǀdadhi-krā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sū́danam ǀ mártyāya ǀ dadáthuḥ ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ naḥ ǀ áśvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those who are preparing for battle, those who are proceeding to sacrifice, both invoke (Dadhikra) as if (he was)Indra;Mitraand Varuṇahave given to us the horse Dadhikrā as an encourager to man.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who are preparing for battle, those who are proceeding to sacrifice, both invoke (Dadhikra) as if (he was)Indra;Mitraand Varuṇahave given to us the horse Dadhikrā as an encourager to man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषं जिष्णोरश्वस्य वाजिनः ।सुरभि नो मुखा करत्प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ akāriṣam ǀ jiṣṇóḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀsurabhí ǀ naḥ ǀ múkhā ǀ karat ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ tāriṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have celebrated the praise of Dadhikrā, the rapid and victorious stee; may he make our mouths fragrant, may he prolong our lives.
verses.wilson_translation: I have celebrated the praise of Dadhikrā, the rapid and victorious stee; may he make our mouths fragrant, may he prolong our lives.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XL. Dadhikrāvan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET us recite the praise of Dadhikrāvan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion;Praise of the Lord of Waters, Dawn, and Agni, Bṛhaspati Son of Aṅgiras, and Sūrya. Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn.May he the true, the fleet, the lover of the course, the bird-like Dadhikrāvan, bring food, strength, and light. His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim,And, as it were a falcon's gliding through the air, strikes Dadhikrāvan's side as he speeds on with might. Bound by the neck and by the flanks and by the mouth, the vigorous Courser lends new swiftness to his speed.Drawing himself together, as his strength allows, Dadhikrās springs along the windings of the paths. The Haṁsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest,Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law.

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्राव्ण इदु नु चर्किराम विश्वा इन्मामुषसः सूदयंतु ।अपामग्नेरुषसः सूर्यस्य बृहस्पतेरांगिरसस्य जिष्णोः ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ carkirāma ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ mā́m ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sūdayantu ǀapā́m ǀ agnéḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ bṛ́haspáteḥ ǀ āṅgirasásya ǀ jiṣṇóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we repeatedly recite (the praise) of Dadhikrāvaṇ; may all rising dawns excite me (to the adoration) of the waters, of Agni, of Uṣas, of Sūrya, of Bṛhaspati, and of Jiṣṇu, the son of Aṅgiras.
verses.wilson_translation: May we repeatedly recite (the praise) of Dadhikrāvaṇ; may all rising dawns excite me (to the adoration) of the waters, of Agni, of Uṣas, of Sūrya, of Bṛhaspati, and of Jiṣṇu, the son of Aṅgiras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्वा भरिषो गविषो दुवन्यसच्छ्रवस्यादिष उषसस्तुरण्यसत् ।सत्यो द्रवो द्रवरः पतंगरो दधिक्रावेषमूर्जं स्वर्जनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sátvā ǀ bhariṣáḥ ǀ go-iṣáḥ ǀ duvanya-sát ǀ śravasyā́t ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ turaṇya-sát ǀsatyáḥ ǀ draváḥ ǀ dravaráḥ ǀ pataṅgaráḥ ǀ dadhi-krā́vā ǀ íṣam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ sváḥ ǀ janat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Dadhikrāvaṇ, the active, the cherisher, the giver of cattle, who abides with the devout, the swift-going, be willing to accept (the sacrificial) food at the time of the desirable dawn; may he who is true, moving, rapid, and leaping like a grasshopper, produce (for us) food, strength and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May Dadhikrāvaṇ, the active, the cherisher, the giver of cattle, who abides with the devout, the swift-going, be willing to accept (the sacrificial) food at the time of the desirable dawn; may he who is true, moving, rapid, and leaping like a grasshopper, produce (for us) food, strength and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्मास्य द्रवतस्तुरण्यतः पर्णं न वेरनु वाति प्रगर्धिनः ।श्येनस्येव ध्रजतो अंकसं परि दधिक्राव्णः सहोर्जा तरित्रतः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ asya ǀ drávataḥ ǀ turaṇyatáḥ ǀ parṇám ǀ ná ǀ véḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vāti ǀ pra-gardhínaḥ ǀśyenásya-iva ǀ dhrájataḥ ǀ aṅkasám ǀ pári ǀ dadhi-krā́vṇaḥ ǀ sahá ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ táritrataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: And after him who is quick-going, hastening, eager (to arrive at his goald, men) follow (as other birds pursue) the flight of a swift (bird) striving together to keep up by the side of Dadhikrāvan. the transporter (of others) as swift as a hawk.
verses.wilson_translation: And after him who is quick-going, hastening, eager (to arrive at his goald, men) follow (as other birds pursue) the flight of a swift (bird) striving together to keep up by the side of Dadhikrāvan. the transporter (of others) as swift as a hawk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि ।क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामंकांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ kṣipaṇím ǀ turaṇyati ǀ grīvā́yām ǀ baddháḥ ǀ api-kakṣé ǀ āsáni ǀkrátum ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sam-távītvat ǀ pathā́m ǀ áṅkāṃsi ǀ ánu ǀ ā-pánīphaṇat ǁ
verses.english_translation: And that horse bound by his neck, his flanks, his mouth, accelerates his paces; Dadhikrā increasing in vigour after the (sacred rite), following the windings of the roads, goes still more rapidly.
verses.wilson_translation: And that horse bound by his neck, his flanks, his mouth, accelerates his paces; Dadhikrā increasing in vigour after the (sacred rite), following the windings of the roads, goes still more rapidly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरंतरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं ॥
verses.transliteration: haṃsáḥ ǀ śuci-sát ǀ vásuḥ ǀ antarikṣa-sát ǀ hótā ǀ vedi-sát ǀ átithiḥ ǀ duroṇa-sát ǀnṛ-sát ǀ vara-sát ǀ ṛta-sát ǀ vyoma-sát ǀ ap-jā́ḥ ǀ go-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-jā́ḥ ǀ adri-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛtám ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is the Haṃsa, (the sun), dwelling;Vasu(the wind), dwelling in the firmament; the invoker of the gods (Agni), dwelling on the altar; the guest (of the worshipper), dweling in the house (as the culinary fire); the dweller among men, (as consciousness), the dweller in the most excellent (orbl, the sun), the dweller in truth, the dweller in the sky (the air), born in the waters, in the rays of light, in the verity (of manifestation) in the (eastern) mountain, the truth (itself).
verses.wilson_translation: He is the Haṃsa, (the sun), dwelling;Vasu(the wind), dwelling in the firmament; the invoker of the gods (Agni), dwelling on the altar; the guest (of the worshipper), dweling in the house (as the culinary fire); the dweller among men, (as consciousness), the dweller in the most excellent (orbl, the sun), the dweller in truth, the dweller in the sky (the air), born in the waters, in the rays of light, in the verity (of manifestation) in the (eastern) mountain, the truth (itself).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Indra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT laud, O Indra-Varuṇa, with oblation, hath like the Immortal Priest obtained your favour?Hath our effectual laud, addressed with homage, touched you, O Indra-Varuṇa, in spirit? He who with dainty food hath won you, Indra and Varuṇa, Gods, as his allies to friendship,Slayeth the Vṛtras and his foes in battles, and through your mighty favours is made famous. Indra and Varuṇa are most liberal givers of treasure to the men who toil to serve them,When they, as Friends inclined to friendship, honoured with dainty food, delight in flowing Soma. Indra and Varuṇa, ye hurl, O Mighty, on him your strongest flashing bolt of thunderWho treats us ill, the robber and oppressor: measure on him your overwhelming vigour. O Indra-Varuṇa, be ye the lovers of this my song, as steers who love the milch-Cow.Milk may it yield us as, gone forth to pasture, the great Cow pouring out her thousand rivers. For fertile fields, for worthy sons and grandsons, for the Sun's beauty and for steer-like vigour,May Indra-Varuṇa with gracious favours work marvels for us in the stress of battle. For you, as Princes, for your ancient kindness, good comrades of the man who seeks for booty,We choose to us for the dear bond of friendship, most liberal Heroes bringing bliss like parents. Showing their strength, these hymns for grace, Free-givers I have gone to you, devoted, as to battle.For glory have they gone, as milk to Soma, to Indra-Varuṇa my thoughts and praises. To Indra and to Varuṇa, desirous of gaining wealth have these my thoughts proceeded.They have come nigh to you as treasure-lovers, like mares, fleet-footed, eager for the glory. May we ourselves be lords of during riches, of ample sustenance for car and hones.So may the Twain who work with newest succours bring yoked teams hitherward to us and riches. Come with your mighty succours, O ye Mighty; come, Indra-Varuṇa, to us in battle.What time the flashing arrows play in combat, may we through you be winners in the contest.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा को वां वरुणा सुम्नमाप स्तोमो हविष्माँ अमृतो न होता ।यो वां हृदि क्रतुमाँ अस्मदुक्तः पस्पर्शदिंद्रावरुणा नमस्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ káḥ ǀ vām ǀ varuṇā ǀ sumnám ǀ āpa ǀ stómaḥ ǀ havíṣmān ǀ amṛ́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ hótā ǀyáḥ ǀ vām ǀ hṛdí ǀ krátu-mān ǀ asmát ǀ uktáḥ ǀ paspárśat ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ námasvān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra(and Varuṇa), Varuṇa (and Indra), what praise of you accompanied by oblations may obtain for us felicity, (such as) the immortal invoker of the gods, (Agni, may bestow); may (the praise) which is addressed by us to you both, Indra and Varuṇa, sanctified by acts and prompted by veneration, touch your heartṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Indra(and Varuṇa), Varuṇa (and Indra), what praise of you accompanied by oblations may obtain for us felicity, (such as) the immortal invoker of the gods, (Agni, may bestow); may (the praise) which is addressed by us to you both, Indra and Varuṇa, sanctified by acts and prompted by veneration, touch your heartṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा ह यो वरुणा चक्र आपी देवौ मर्तः सख्याय प्रयस्वान् ।स हंति वृत्रा समिथेषु शत्रूनवोभिर्वा महद्भिः स प्र शृण्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ ha ǀ yáḥ ǀ váruṇā ǀ cakré ǀ āpī́ íti ǀ deváu ǀ mártaḥ ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ práyasvān ǀsáḥ ǀ hanti ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ sam-ithéṣu ǀ śátrūn ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vā ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá ǀ śṛṇve ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Indraand Varuṇa, the mortal diligent in offering (you) sacrificial food, who has through friendship made you his kinsmen, destroys (his own) sins, and his enemies in battle; and by your great favours he becomes renowned.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Indraand Varuṇa, the mortal diligent in offering (you) sacrificial food, who has through friendship made you his kinsmen, destroys (his own) sins, and his enemies in battle; and by your great favours he becomes renowned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा ह रत्नं वरुणा धेष्ठेत्था नृभ्यः शशमानेभ्यस्ता ।यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादयैते ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ ha ǀ rátnam ǀ váruṇā ǀ dhéṣṭhā ǀ itthā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ śaśamānébhyaḥ ǀ tā́ ǀyádi ǀ sákhāyā ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ sómaiḥ ǀ sutébhiḥ ǀ su-prayásā ǀ mādáyaite íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa(you are) most liberal givers of wealth to men praising you in various ways, when as friends well plural ed with (sacrificial) food, you are exhilarated by the Somajuice effused through friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa(you are) most liberal givers of wealth to men praising you in various ways, when as friends well plural ed with (sacrificial) food, you are exhilarated by the Somajuice effused through friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा युवं वरुणा दिद्युमस्मिन्नोजिष्ठमुग्रा नि वधिष्टं वज्रं ।यो नो दुरेवो वृकतिर्दभीतिस्तस्मिन्मिमाथामभिभूत्योजः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ yuvám ǀ varuṇā ǀ didyúm ǀ asmin ǀ ójiṣṭham ǀ ugrā ǀ ní ǀ vadhiṣṭam ǀ vájram ǀyáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-évaḥ ǀ vṛkátiḥ ǀ dabhī́tiḥ ǀ tásmin ǀ mimāthām ǀ abhí-bhūti ǀ ójaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce Indraand Varuṇayou hurled the bright-shining and most mighty thunderbolt against this (our foe), who is difficult ot be resisted by us; (who is) rapacious, malevolent; grant us strength to overcome him.
verses.wilson_translation: Fierce Indraand Varuṇayou hurled the bright-shining and most mighty thunderbolt against this (our foe), who is difficult ot be resisted by us; (who is) rapacious, malevolent; grant us strength to overcome him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा युवं वरुणा भूतमस्या धियः प्रेतारा वृषभेव धेनोः ।सा नो दुहीयद्यवसेव गत्वी सहस्रधारा पयसा मही गौः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ yuvám ǀ varuṇā ǀ bhūtám ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ dhiyáḥ ǀ pretā́rā ǀ vṛṣabhā́-iva ǀ dhenóḥ ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duhīyat ǀ yávasā-iva ǀ gatvī́ ǀ sahásra-dhārā ǀ páyasā ǀ mahī́ ǀ gáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, be the exciters of this our praise, as the bull is of the cows; may that cow (of praise) yield us (reward), like a large cow that has gone forth to pasture, whose thousand channels (are filled) with milk.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, be the exciters of this our praise, as the bull is of the cows; may that cow (of praise) yield us (reward), like a large cow that has gone forth to pasture, whose thousand channels (are filled) with milk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तोके हिते तनय उर्वरासु सूरो दृशीके वृषणश्च पौंस्ये ।इंद्रा नो अत्र वरुणा स्यातामवोभिर्दस्मा परितक्म्यायां ॥
verses.transliteration: toké ǀ hité ǀ tánaye ǀ urvárāsu ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ dṛ́śīke ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ páuṃsye ǀíndrā ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ váruṇā ǀ syātām ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ dasmā́ ǀ pári-takmyāyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indraand Varuṇa, the overthrowers (of foes), be around us with (their) protections; (that thereby we may have) good sons and grandsons, and fertile lands, and long life, and virility.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indraand Varuṇa, the overthrowers (of foes), be around us with (their) protections; (that thereby we may have) good sons and grandsons, and fertile lands, and long life, and virility.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवामिद्ध्यवसे पूर्व्याय परि प्रभूती गविषः स्वापी ।वृणीमहे सख्याय प्रियाय शूरा मंहिष्ठा पितरेव शंभू ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ ávase ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀ pári ǀ prábhūtī íti prá-bhūtī ǀ go-íṣaḥ ǀ svāpī íti su-āpī ǀvṛṇīmáhe ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ priyā́ya ǀ śū́rā ǀ máṃhiṣṭhā ǀ pitárā-iva ǀ śambhū́ íti śam-bhū́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desirous of (possessing) cattlle, we have recourse to you,Indraand Varuṇa, for full protection, you who are powerful and kind as (kinsmen); we have recourse to you, adorable heroes, for (your) friendship and affection, (to you who are), like parents, givers of happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of (possessing) cattlle, we have recourse to you,Indraand Varuṇa, for full protection, you who are powerful and kind as (kinsmen); we have recourse to you, adorable heroes, for (your) friendship and affection, (to you who are), like parents, givers of happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता वां धियोऽवसे वाजयंतीराजिं न जग्मुर्युवयूः सुदानू ।श्रिये न गाव उप सोममस्थुरिंद्रं गिरो वरुणं मे मनीषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ávase ǀ vāja-yántīḥ ǀ ājím ǀ ná ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ yuva-yū́ḥ ǀ sudānū íti su-dānū ǀśriyé ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sómam ǀ asthuḥ ǀ índram ǀ gíraḥ ǀ váruṇam ǀ me ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Liberal givers, those (our) praises soliciting (abundant) food have proceeded to you for (your) protection; longing for you as (soldiers long) for battle, and as cattle approach the Somafor (its) advantage, so my heartfelt hymns (approach)Indraand Varuṇa.
verses.wilson_translation: Liberal givers, those (our) praises soliciting (abundant) food have proceeded to you for (your) protection; longing for you as (soldiers long) for battle, and as cattle approach the Somafor (its) advantage, so my heartfelt hymns (approach)Indraand Varuṇa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा इंद्रं वरुणं मे मनीषा अग्मन्नुप द्रविणमिच्छमानाः ।उपेमस्थुर्जोष्टार इव वस्वो रघ्वीरिव श्रवसो भिक्षमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ índram ǀ váruṇam ǀ me ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǀ ágman ǀ úpa ǀ dráviṇam ǀ icchámānāḥ ǀúpa ǀ īm ǀ asthuḥ ǀ joṣṭā́raḥ-iva ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ raghvī́ḥ-iva ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These my earnest praises approach Indraand Varuṇa, desirous to obtain wealth, as dependants attend (upon an opulent man) for the sake of riches, like humble (feminine les) begging for food.
verses.wilson_translation: These my earnest praises approach Indraand Varuṇa, desirous to obtain wealth, as dependants attend (upon an opulent man) for the sake of riches, like humble (feminine les) begging for food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्व्यस्य त्मना रथ्यस्य पुष्टेर्नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम ।ता चक्राणा ऊतिभिर्नव्यसीभिरस्मत्रा रायो नियुतः सचंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvyasya ǀ tmánā ǀ ráthyasya ǀ puṣṭéḥ ǀ nítyasya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ syāma ǀtā́ ǀ cakrāṇáu ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ návyasībhiḥ ǀ asma-trā́ ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ sacantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we of our own (right) be the masters of permanent riches, comprising horses, chariots, and nourishment; may those two, traversing (the regions), direct their Niyutsteeds towards us, associating (them) with riches and with recent protections.
verses.wilson_translation: May we of our own (right) be the masters of permanent riches, comprising horses, chariots, and nourishment; may those two, traversing (the regions), direct their Niyutsteeds towards us, associating (them) with riches and with recent protections.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो बृहंता बृहतीभिरूती इंद्र यातं वरुण वाजसातौ ।यद्दिद्यवः पृतनासु प्रक्रीळांतस्य वां स्याम सनितार आजेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bṛhantā ǀ bṛhatī́bhiḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ índra ǀ yātám ǀ varuṇa ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀyát ǀ didyávaḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ pra-krī́ḷān ǀ tásya ǀ vām ǀ syāma ǀ sanitā́raḥ ǀ ājéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty Indraand Varuṇa, come to us in battle with (your) powerful protections, and where the bright (weapons) plural y amidst the (hostile) hosts, may we triumph in that conflict (through) your (favour).
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty Indraand Varuṇa, come to us in battle with (your) powerful protections, and where the bright (weapons) plural y amidst the (hostile) hosts, may we triumph in that conflict (through) your (favour).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIL Indra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I AM the royal Ruler, mine is empire, as mine who sway all life are all Immortals.Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover. I am King Varuṇa. To me were given these first existing high celestial powers.Varuṇa's will the Gods obey and follow. I am the King of men's most lofty cover. I Varuṇa am Indra: in their greatness, these the two wide deep fairly-fashioned regions,These the two world-halves have I, even as Tvaṣṭar knowing all beings, joined and held together. I made to flow the moisture-shedding waters, and set the heaven firm in the scat of Order.By Law the Son of Aditi, Law Observer, hath spread abroad the world in threefold measure. Heroes with noble horses, fain for battle, selected warriors, call on me in combat.I Indra Maghavan, excite the conflict; I stir the dust, Lord of surpassing vigour. All this I did. The Gods’ own conquering power never impedeth me whom none opposeth.When lauds and Soma juice have made me joyful, both the unbounded regions are affrighted. All beings know these deeds of thine thou tellest this unto Varuṇa, thou great Disposer!Thou art renowned as having slain the Vṛtras. Thou madest flow the floods that were obstructed. Our fathers then were these, the Seven his, what time the son of Durgaha was captive.For her they gained by sacrifice Trasadasyu, a demi-god, like Indra, conquering foemen. The spouse of Purukutsa gave oblations to you, O Indra-Varuṇa, with homage.Then unto her ye gave King Trasadasyu, the demi-god, the slayer of the foeman. May we, possessing much, delight in riches, Gods in oblations and the kine in pasture;And that Milch-cow who shrinks not from the milking, O Indra-Varuṇa, give to us daily.

verses.sanskrit: मम द्विता राष्ट्रं क्षत्रियस्य विश्वायोर्विश्वे अमृता यथा नः ।क्रतुं सचंते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥
verses.transliteration: máma ǀ dvitā́ ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ kṣatríyasya ǀ viśvá-āyoḥ ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀkrátum ǀ sacante ǀ váruṇasya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rā́jāmi ǀ kṛṣṭéḥ ǀ upamásya ǀ vavréḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Twofold is my empire, that of the wholekṣatriyarace, and all the immortals are ours; the gods associate me with the acts of Varuṇa; I rule over (those) of the proximate form of man.
verses.wilson_translation: Twofold is my empire, that of the wholekṣatriyarace, and all the immortals are ours; the gods associate me with the acts of Varuṇa; I rule over (those) of the proximate form of man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं राजा वरुणो मह्यं तान्यसुर्याणि प्रथमा धारयंत ।क्रतुं सचंते वरुणस्य देवा राजामि कृष्टेरुपमस्य वव्रेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ tā́ni ǀ asuryā́ṇi ǀ prathamā́ ǀ dhārayanta ǀkrátum ǀ sacante ǀ váruṇasya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ rā́jāmi ǀ kṛṣṭéḥ ǀ upamásya ǀ vavréḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am the king Varuṇa; on me (the gods) bestow those principal energies (that are) destructive of theasuras; (they) associate me with the worship of Varuṇa; I rule over (the nets) of the proximate form of man.
verses.wilson_translation: I am the king Varuṇa; on me (the gods) bestow those principal energies (that are) destructive of theasuras; (they) associate me with the worship of Varuṇa; I rule over (the nets) of the proximate form of man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहमिंद्रो वरुणस्ते महित्वोर्वी गभीरे रजसी सुमेके ।त्वष्टेव विश्वा भुवनानि विद्वान्त्समैरयं रोदसी धारयं च ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ té íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ gabhīré íti ǀ rájasī íti ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀtváṣṭā-iva ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ sám ǀ airayam ǀ ródasī íti ǀ dhāráyam ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am Indra, I am Varuṇa, I am those two in greatness; (I am) the vast, profound, beautiful, heaven and earth; intelligent, I give Tvaṣṭā-like animation to all beings; I uphold earth and heaven].
verses.wilson_translation: I am Indra, I am Varuṇa, I am those two in greatness; (I am) the vast, profound, beautiful, heaven and earth; intelligent, I give Tvaṣṭā-like animation to all beings; I uphold earth and heaven].
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहमपो अपिन्वमुक्षमाणा धारयं दिवं सदन ऋतस्य ।ऋतेन पुत्रो अदितेर्ऋतावोत त्रिधातु प्रथयद्वि भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ apáḥ ǀ apinvam ǀ ukṣámāṇāḥ ǀ dhāráyam ǀ dívam ǀ sádane ǀ ṛtásya ǀṛténa ǀ putráḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ utá ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ prathayat ǀ ví ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have distributed the moisture-shedding waters; I have upheld the sky as the abode of the water; by the water I have become the preserver of the water, the son of Aditi, illustrating the threefold elementary space.
verses.wilson_translation: I have distributed the moisture-shedding waters; I have upheld the sky as the abode of the water; by the water I have become the preserver of the water, the son of Aditi, illustrating the threefold elementary space.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मां नरः स्वश्वा वाजयंतो मां वृताः समरणे हवंते ।कृणोम्याजिं मघवाहमिंद्र इयर्मि रेणुमभिभूत्योजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́m ǀ náraḥ ǀ su-áśvāḥ ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ vṛtā́ḥ ǀ sam-áraṇe ǀ havante ǀkṛṇómi ǀ ājím ǀ maghá-vā ǀ ahám ǀ índraḥ ǀ íyarmi ǀ reṇúm ǀ abhíbhūti-ojāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Warriors well mounted, ardent for contest invoke me; selected (combatants invoke) me in battle; I, the affluent Indra, instrumental gate the conflict, and, endowed with victorious prowess, I raise up the dust (in the battle).
verses.wilson_translation: Warriors well mounted, ardent for contest invoke me; selected (combatants invoke) me in battle; I, the affluent Indra, instrumental gate the conflict, and, endowed with victorious prowess, I raise up the dust (in the battle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं ता विश्वा चकरं नकिर्मा दैव्यं सहो वरते अप्रतीतं ।यन्मा सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्थोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ tā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ cakaram ǀ nákiḥ ǀ mā ǀ dáivyam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ varate ǀ áprati-itam ǀyát ǀ mā ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ mamádan ǀ yát ǀ ukthā́ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ bhayete íti ǀ rájasī íti ǀ apāré íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have done all these (deeds); no one resists my divine, unsurpassed vigour; and when the Somajuices, when sacred songs, exhilarate me, then the unbounded heaven and earth are both alarmed.
verses.wilson_translation: I have done all these (deeds); no one resists my divine, unsurpassed vigour; and when the Somajuices, when sacred songs, exhilarate me, then the unbounded heaven and earth are both alarmed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विदुष्टे विश्वा भुवनानि तस्य ता प्र ब्रवीषि वरुणाय वेधः ।त्वं वृत्राणि शृण्विषे जघन्वांत्वं वृताँ अरिणा इंद्र सिंधून् ॥
verses.transliteration: vidúḥ ǀ te ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tásya ǀ tā́ ǀ prá ǀ bravīṣi ǀ váruṇāya ǀ vedhaḥ ǀtvám ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ śṛṇviṣe ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ tvám ǀ vṛtā́n ǀ ariṇāḥ ǀ indra ǀ síndhūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: All beings recognize you (Varuṇa), and your, worshipper, address these (encomiums) to Varuṇa; you,Indra, are renowned as slaying Vṛtra; you have set the obstructed rivers free to flow.
verses.wilson_translation: All beings recognize you (Varuṇa), and your, worshipper, address these (encomiums) to Varuṇa; you,Indra, are renowned as slaying Vṛtra; you have set the obstructed rivers free to flow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमत्र पितरस्त आसन्त्सप्त ऋषयो दौर्गहे बध्यमाने ।त आयजंत त्रसदस्युमस्या इंद्रं न वृत्रतुरमर्धदेवं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ átra ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ té ǀ āsan ǀ saptá ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ dauḥ-gahé ǀ badhyámāne ǀté ǀ ā́ ǀ ayajanta ǀ trasádasyum ǀ asyāḥ ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ vṛtra-túram ǀ ardha-devám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven ṛṣis were the protectors of this our (kingdom) when the son of Durgaha was in bonds; performing worship they obtained for (hisqueen) from the favour of Indraand Varuṇa,Trasadasyu, like Indra the slayer of foes, dwelling near the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven ṛṣis were the protectors of this our (kingdom) when the son of Durgaha was in bonds; performing worship they obtained for (hisqueen) from the favour of Indraand Varuṇa,Trasadasyu, like Indra the slayer of foes, dwelling near the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुकुत्सानी हि वामदाशद्धव्येभिरिंद्रावरुणा नमोभिः ।अथा राजानं त्रस���स्युमस्या वृत्रहणं ददथुरर्धदेवं ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-kútsānī ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ ádāśat ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀátha ǀ rā́jānam ǀ trasádasyum ǀ asyāḥ ǀ vṛtra-hánam ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ ardha-devám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wife of Purukutsapropitiated you two,Indraand Varuṇa, with oblations and prostrations, and therefore you gave her the king Trasadasyu, the slayer of foes dwelling near the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The wife of Purukutsapropitiated you two,Indraand Varuṇa, with oblations and prostrations, and therefore you gave her the king Trasadasyu, the slayer of foes dwelling near the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: राया वयं ससवांसो मदेम हव्येन देवा यवसेन गावः ।तां धेनुमिंद्रावरुणा युवं नो विश्वाहा धत्तमनपस्फुरंतीं ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyā́ ǀ vayám ǀ sasa-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ madema ǀ havyéna ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yávasena ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀtā́m ǀ dhenúm ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ yuvám ǀ naḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ dhattam ǀ ánapa-sphurantīm ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, glorifying you both, be delighted by riches; may the gods be plural ased by oblations, the cows by pasture; and do you,Indraand Varuṇa, daily grant us that same cow, (riches) free from any imperfection.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, glorifying you both, be delighted by riches; may the gods be plural ased by oblations, the cows by pasture; and do you,Indraand Varuṇa, daily grant us that same cow, (riches) free from any imperfection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHO will hear, who of those who merit worship, which of all Gods take pleasure in our homage?On whose heart shall we lay this laud celestial, rich with fair offerings, dearest to Immortals? Who will be gracious? Who will come most quickly of all the Gods? Who willbring bliss most largely?What car do they call swift with rapid coursers? That which the Daughter of the Sun elected. So many days do ye come swiftly hither, as Indra to give help in stress of battle.Descended from the sky, divine, strong-pinioned, by which of all your powers are ye most mighty? What is the prayer that we should bring you, Aśvins, whereby ye come to us when invocated?Whether of you confronts e’en great betrayal? Lovers of sweetness, Dasras, help and save us. In the wide space your chariot reacheth heaven, what time it turneth hither from the ocean.Sweets from your sweet shall drop, lovers of sweetness! These have they dressed for you as dainty viands. Let Sindhu with his wave bedew your horses: in fiery glow have the red birds come hither.Observed of all was that your rapid going, whereby ye were the Lords of Sūrya's Daughter. Whene’er I gratified you here together, your grace was given us, O ye rich in booty.Protect, ye Twain, the singer of your praises: to you, Nāsatyas, is my wish directed.

verses.sanskrit: क उ श्रवत्कतमो यज्ञियानां वंदारु देवः कतमो जुषाते ।कस्येमां देवीममृतेषु प्रेष्ठां हृदि श्रेषाम सुष्टुतिं सुहव्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śravat ǀ katamáḥ ǀ yajñíyānām ǀ vandā́ru ǀ deváḥ ǀ katamáḥ ǀ juṣāte ǀkásya ǀ imā́m ǀ devī́m ǀ amṛ́teṣu ǀ préṣṭhām ǀ hṛdí ǀ śreṣāma ǀ su-stutím ǀ su-havyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Which of those who are entitled to sacrifice will listen (to our prayers)? which of the gods will hear our praise? which will be propitiated (by it)? upon the heart of whom among the immortals may we impress the devout affectionate adoration, accompanied by sacred oblations?
verses.wilson_translation: Which of those who are entitled to sacrifice will listen (to our prayers)? which of the gods will hear our praise? which will be propitiated (by it)? upon the heart of whom among the immortals may we impress the devout affectionate adoration, accompanied by sacred oblations?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को मृळाति कतम आगमिष्ठो देवानामु कतमः शंभविष्ठः ।रथं कमाहुर्द्रवदश्वमाशुं यं सूर्यस्य दुहितावृणीत ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ mṛḷāti ǀ katamáḥ ǀ ā́-gamiṣṭhaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ katamáḥ ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhaḥ ǀrátham ǀ kám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ dravát-aśvam ǀ āśúm ǀ yám ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ duhitā́ ǀ ávṛṇīta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who will make us happy? which of the gods is the most prompt to come to our sacrifice? which is the most willing to grant us felicity? what chariot do they say is quick and drawn by rapid steeds? That which the daughter of Sūryaselected.
verses.wilson_translation: Who will make us happy? which of the gods is the most prompt to come to our sacrifice? which is the most willing to grant us felicity? what chariot do they say is quick and drawn by rapid steeds? That which the daughter of Sūryaselected.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मक्षू हि ष्मा गच्छथ ईवतो द्यूनिंद्रो न शक्तिं परितक्म्यायां ।दिव आजाता दिव्या सुपर्णा कया शचीनां भवथः शचिष्ठा ॥
verses.transliteration: makṣú ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ ī́vataḥ ǀ dyū́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ ná ǀ śaktím ǀ pári-takmyāyām ǀdiváḥ ǀ ā́-jātā ǀ divyā́ ǀ su-parṇā́ ǀ káyā ǀ śácīnām ǀ bhavathaḥ ǀ śáciṣṭhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Moving, you proceed rapidly by day, as Indra, at the end of the night, (manifests his) power; descended from heaven, divine, of graceful motion, (Aśvins), by which of (your) acts are you most distinguished?
verses.wilson_translation: Moving, you proceed rapidly by day, as Indra, at the end of the night, (manifests his) power; descended from heaven, divine, of graceful motion, (Aśvins), by which of (your) acts are you most distinguished?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: का वां भूदुपमातिः कया न आश्विना गमथो हूयमाना ।को वां महश्चित्त्यजसो अभीक उरुष्यतं माध्वी दस्रा न ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ vām ǀ bhūt ǀ úpa-mātiḥ ǀ káyā ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aśvinā ǀ gamathaḥ ǀ hūyámānā ǀkáḥ ǀ vām ǀ maháḥ ǀ cit ǀ tyájasaḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀ uruṣyátam ǀ mādhvī íti ǀ dasrā ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What may be the fit measure (of your merits)? invoked by what praises do you come to us? who (can exist as) the object of your great wrath?Dasras, dispensers of sweet (water), defend us with your protection.
verses.wilson_translation: What may be the fit measure (of your merits)? invoked by what praises do you come to us? who (can exist as) the object of your great wrath?Dasras, dispensers of sweet (water), defend us with your protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उरु वां रथः परि नक्षति द्यामा यत्समुद्रादभि वर्तते वां ।मध्वा माध्वी मधु वां प्रुषायन्यत्सीं वां पृक्षो भुरजंत पक्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: urú ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ pári ǀ nakṣati ǀ dyā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ yát ǀ samudrā́t ǀ abhí ǀ vártate ǀ vām ǀmádhvā ǀ mādhvī íti ǀ mádhu ǀ vām ǀ pruṣāyan ǀ yát ǀ sīm ǀ vām ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ bhurájanta ǀ pakvā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your chariot travels widely round the heaven until it plural ces you beyond the firmament; dispensers of sweet (water, the priests) are diluting the Somajuice with milk, that the boiled (barley) may be united with the libation offered to you.
verses.wilson_translation: Your chariot travels widely round the heaven until it plural ces you beyond the firmament; dispensers of sweet (water, the priests) are diluting the Somajuice with milk, that the boiled (barley) may be united with the libation offered to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सिंधुर्ह वां रसया सिंचदश्वान्घृणा वयोऽरुषासः परि ग्मन् ।तदू षु वामजिरं चेति यानं येन पती भवथः सूर्यायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: síndhuḥ ǀ ha ǀ vām ǀ rasáyā ǀ siñcat ǀ áśvān ǀ ghṛṇā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ pári ǀ gman ǀtát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ vām ǀ ajirám ǀ ceti ǀ yā́nam ǀ yéna ǀ pátī íti ǀ bhávathaḥ ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The flowing (stream) has sprinkled your steeds with moisture; the radiant horses (like) birds (in swiftness) pass on, bright with lustre; well known as that quick-moving chariot, whereby you became the lords of Sūrya.
verses.wilson_translation: The flowing (stream) has sprinkled your steeds with moisture; the radiant horses (like) birds (in swiftness) pass on, bright with lustre; well known as that quick-moving chariot, whereby you became the lords of Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इहेह यद्वां समना पपृक्षे सेयमस्मे सुमतिर्वाजरत्ना ।उरुष्यतं जरितारं युवं ह श्रितः कामो नासत्या युवद्रिक् ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá-iha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ samanā́ ǀ papṛkṣé ǀ sā́ ǀ iyám ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ vāja-ratnā ǀuruṣyátam ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yuvám ǀ ha ǀ śritáḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ yuvadrík ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the earnest praise, distributors of food, wherewith I associate you both like-minded at this sacrifice, be (beneficial) to us; do you protect your worshipper; my desire,Nāsatyas, directed towards you is gratified.
verses.wilson_translation: May the earnest praise, distributors of food, wherewith I associate you both like-minded at this sacrifice, be (beneficial) to us; do you protect your worshipper; my desire,Nāsatyas, directed towards you is gratified.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIV. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WE will invoke this day your car, far-spreading, O Aśvins, even the gathering, of the sunlight,—Car praised in hymns, most ample, rich in treasure, fitted with seats, the car that beareth Sūrya. Aśvins, ye gained that glory by your Godhead, ye Sons of Heaven, by your own might and power.Food followeth close upon your bright appearing when stately horses in your chariot draw you. Who bringeth you to-day for help with offered oblation, or with hymns to drink the juices?Who, for the sacrifice's ancient lover, turneth you hither, Aśvins, offering homage? Borne on your golden car, ye omnipresent! come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas.Drink of the pleasant liquor of the Soma give riches to the people who adore you. Come hitherward to us from earth, from heaven, borne on your golden chariot rolling lightly.Suffer not other worshippers to stay you here are ye bound by earlier bonds of friendship. Now for us both, mete out, O Wonder-Workers, riches exceeding great with store of heroes,Because the men have sent you praise, O Aśvins, and Ajamīlhas come to the laudation. Whene’er I gratified you here together, your grace was given us, O ye rich in booty.Protect, ye Twain, the singer of your praises: to you, Nāsatyas, is my wish directed.

verses.sanskrit: तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम पृथुज्रयमश्विना संगतिं गोः ।यः सूर्यां वहति वंधुरायुर्गिर्वाहसं पुरुतमं वसूयुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vām ǀ rátham ǀ vayám ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀ pṛthu-jráyam ǀ aśvinā ǀ sám-gatim ǀ góḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ sūryā́m ǀ váhati ǀ vandhura-yúḥ ǀ gírvāhasam ǀ puru-támam ǀ vasu-yúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke,Aśvins, today, your rapid car, the associator of the solar ray; the banked car which bears Sūrya, vast, wealthy, and laden with praises.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke,Aśvins, today, your rapid car, the associator of the solar ray; the banked car which bears Sūrya, vast, wealthy, and laden with praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवं श्रियमश्विना देवता तां दिवो नपाता वनथः शचीभिः ।युवोर्वपुरभि पृक्षः सचंते वहंति यत्ककुहासो रथे वां ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ śríyam ǀ aśvinā ǀ devátā ǀ tā́n ǀ dívaḥ ǀ napātā ǀ vanathaḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ vápuḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ sacante ǀ váhanti ǀ yát ǀ kakuhā́saḥ ǀ ráthe ǀ vām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aśvins, grandsons of heaven, divinities, you enjoy that glory of your actions, that (sacrificial) food is administered to your person ns, and powerul horses draw you in your chariot.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, grandsons of heaven, divinities, you enjoy that glory of your actions, that (sacrificial) food is administered to your person ns, and powerul horses draw you in your chariot.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को वामद्या करते रातहव्य ऊतये वा सुतपेयाय वार्कैः ।ऋतस्य वा वनुषे पूर्व्याय नमो येमानो अश्विना ववर्तत् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vām ǀ adyá ǀ karate ǀ rātá-havyaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ vā ǀ suta-péyāya ǀ vā ǀ arkáiḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ vā ǀ vanúṣe ǀ pūrvyā́ya ǀ námaḥ ǀ yemānáḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ vavartat ǁ
verses.english_translation: What offer of oblations addresses you today with hymns for the sake (of obtaining) protection, for the drinking of the Soma, or for the ancient fulfilment of the sacrifice? what offer of adoration may bring you Aśvinsmay bring you Aśvins (to this rite)?
verses.wilson_translation: What offer of oblations addresses you today with hymns for the sake (of obtaining) protection, for the drinking of the Soma, or for the ancient fulfilment of the sacrifice? what offer of adoration may bring you Aśvinsmay bring you Aśvins (to this rite)?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्ययेन पुरुभू रथेनेमं यज्ञं नासत्योप यातं ।पिबाथ इन्मधुनः सोम्यस्य दधथो रत्नं विधते जनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyáyena ǀ purubhū íti puru-bhū ǀ ráthena ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ nāsatyā ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǀpíbāthaḥ ǀ ít ǀ mádhunaḥ ǀ somyásya ǀ dádhathaḥ ǀ rátnam ǀ vidhaté ǀ jánāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nāsatyas, who are manifold, come with your golden chariot to this sacrifice; drink of the sweet Somabeverage, and give precious things to the man who celebrates (your worship).
verses.wilson_translation: Nāsatyas, who are manifold, come with your golden chariot to this sacrifice; drink of the sweet Somabeverage, and give precious things to the man who celebrates (your worship).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो यातं दिवो अच्छा पृथिव्या हिरण्ययेन सुवृता रथेन ।मा वामन्ये नि यमंदेवयंतः सं यद्ददे नाभिः पूर्व्या वां ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yātam ǀ diváḥ ǀ áccha ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ hiraṇyáyena ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀmā́ ǀ vām ǀ anyé ǀ ní ǀ yaman ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ sám ǀ yát ǀ dadé ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ pūrvyā́ ǀ vām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to our presence, whether from heaven or earth, with your well-constructed golden chariot; let not other devout worshippers detain yhou, for a prior attraction awaits you (here).
verses.wilson_translation: Come to our presence, whether from heaven or earth, with your well-constructed golden chariot; let not other devout worshippers detain yhou, for a prior attraction awaits you (here).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू नो रयिं पुरुवीरं बृहंतं दस्रा मिमाथामुभयेष्वस्मे ।नरो यद्वामश्विना स्तोममावन्त्सधस्तुतिमाजमीळ्हासो अग्मन् ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ puru-vī́ram ǀ bṛhántam ǀ dásrā ǀ mímāthām ǀ ubháyeṣu ǀ asmé íti ǀnáraḥ ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ aśvinā ǀ stómam ǀ ā́van ǀ sadhá-stutim ǀ āja-mīḷhā́saḥ ǀ agman ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dasras, mete out for us both great opulence, comprising many descendants, since the leaders of the rite (the Purumīḷhas), have addressed to you,Aśvins, their praise, and the Ajamīḷhas have united with it their laudation.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasras, mete out for us both great opulence, comprising many descendants, since the leaders of the rite (the Purumīḷhas), have addressed to you,Aśvins, their praise, and the Ajamīḷhas have united with it their laudation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इहेह यद्वां समना पपृक्षे सेयमस्मे सुमतिर्वाजरत्ना ।उरुष्यतं जरितारं युवं ह श्रितः कामो नासत्या युवद्रिक् ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá-iha ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ samanā́ ǀ papṛkṣé ǀ sā́ ǀ iyám ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ vāja-ratnā ǀuruṣyátam ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yuvám ǀ ha ǀ śritáḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ yuvadrík ǁ
verses.english_translation: May you earn praise wherewith, distributors of food, I associate you both like-minded at this sacrifice, be (beneficial) to us; do you protect your worshipper; my desire,Nāsatyas, directed towards you is gratified.
verses.wilson_translation: May you earn praise wherewith, distributors of food, I associate you both like-minded at this sacrifice, be (beneficial) to us; do you protect your worshipper; my desire,Nāsatyas, directed towards you is gratified.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLV. Aśvins
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YONDER goes up that light: your chariot is yoked that travels round upon the summit of this heaven.Within this car are stored three kindred shares of food, and a skin filled with meath is rustling as the fourth. Forth come your viands rich with store of pleasant meath, and cars and horses at the flushing of the dawn,Stripping the covering from the surrounded gloom, and spreading through mid-air bright radiance like the Sun. Drink of the meath with lips accustomed to the draught; harness for the meath's sake the chariot that ye love.Refresh the way ye go, refresh the paths with meath: hither, O Aśvins, bring the skin that holds the meath. The swans ye have are friendly, rich in store of meath, gold-pinioned, strong to draw, awake at early morn,Swimming the flood, exultant, fain for draughts that cheer: ye come like flies to our libations of the meath. Well knowing solemn rites and rich in meath, the fires sing to the morning Aśvins at the break of day,When with pure hands the prudent energetic priest hath with the stones pressed out the Soma rich in meath. The rays advancing nigh, chasing with day the gloom, spread through the firmament bright radiance like the Sun;And the Sun harnessing his horses goeth forth: ye through your Godlike nature let his paths be known. Devout in thought I have declared, O Aśvins, your chariot with good steeds, which lasts for ever,Wherewith ye travel swiftly through the regions to the prompt worshipper who brings oblation.

verses.sanskrit: एष स्य भानुरुदियर्ति युज्यते रथः परिज्मा दिवो अस्य सानवि ।पृक्षासो अस्मिन्मिथुना अधि त्रयो दृतिस्तुरीयो मधुनो वि रप्शते ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ syáḥ ǀ bhānúḥ ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ yujyáte ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ diváḥ ǀ asyá ǀ sā́navi ǀpṛkṣā́saḥ ǀ asmin ǀ mithunā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ dṛ́tiḥ ǀ turī́yaḥ ǀ mádhunaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rapśate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sun rises; your chariot, (Aśvins), traversing (the regions), is associated with the divine (orb) on the summit (of the eastern mountain in it are three analogous kinds of food, and the leather vessel of the sweet Somajuice appears as the fourth.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun rises; your chariot, (Aśvins), traversing (the regions), is associated with the divine (orb) on the summit (of the eastern mountain in it are three analogous kinds of food, and the leather vessel of the sweet Somajuice appears as the fourth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उद्वां पृक्षासो मधुमंत ईरते रथा अश्वास उषसो व्युष्टिषु ।अपोर्णुवंतस्तम आ प���ीवृतं स्वर्ण शुक्रं तन्वंत आ रजः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ vām ǀ pṛkṣā́saḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ īrate ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀapa-ūrṇuvántaḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pári-vṛtam ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ śukrám ǀ tanvántaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ rájaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your food-bearing,Soma-laden, well-horsed chariots, appearing at the opening of the dawn, scattering the surrounding darkness like the sun, and spreading bright radiance over the firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: Your food-bearing,Soma-laden, well-horsed chariots, appearing at the opening of the dawn, scattering the surrounding darkness like the sun, and spreading bright radiance over the firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मध्वः पिबतं मधुपेभिरासभिरुत प्रियं मधुने युंजाथां रथं ।आ वर्तनिं मधुना जिन्वथस्पथो दृतिं वहेथे मधुमंतमश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: mádhvaḥ ǀ pibatam ǀ madhu-pébhiḥ ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ priyám ǀ mádhune ǀ yuñjāthām ǀ rátham ǀā́ ǀ vartaním ǀ mádhunā ǀ jinvathaḥ ǀ patháḥ ǀ dṛ́tim ǀ vahethe íti ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink of the Somajuice, with mouths (fit for) imbibing the beverage; harness your beloved chariot for the Soma juice; (come to the dwelling) of the sacrifice; enliven the path with the Soma; bring,Aśvins, the leather vessels filled with the Soma-juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink of the Somajuice, with mouths (fit for) imbibing the beverage; harness your beloved chariot for the Soma juice; (come to the dwelling) of the sacrifice; enliven the path with the Soma; bring,Aśvins, the leather vessels filled with the Soma-juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हंसासो ये वां मधुमंतो अस्रिधो हिरण्यपर्णा उहुव उषर्बुधः ।उदप्रुतो मंदिनो मंदिनिस्पृशो मध्वो न मक्षः सवनानि गच्छथः ॥
verses.transliteration: haṃsā́saḥ ǀ yé ǀ vām ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ asrídhaḥ ǀ híraṇya-parṇāḥ ǀ uhúvaḥ ǀ uṣaḥ-búdhaḥ ǀuda-prútaḥ ǀ mandínaḥ ǀ mandi-nispṛ́śaḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mákṣaḥ ǀ sávanāni ǀ gacchathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to sacrifices as flies to honey, (with those horses) that are swift of speed, genitive le, unrefractory, golden-winged, bearers (of burden), wakers at dawn, dispensers of water, exulting and sipping the Somajuice.
