verses.wilson_translation: Come to sacrifices as flies to honey, (with those horses) that are swift of speed, genitive le, unrefractory, golden-winged, bearers (of burden), wakers at dawn, dispensers of water, exulting and sipping the Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वध्वरासो मधुमंतो अग्नय उस्रा जरंते प्रति वस्तोरश्विना ।यन्निक्तहस्तस्तरणिर्विचक्षणः सोमं सुषाव मधुमंतमद्रिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-adhvarā́saḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ usrā́ ǀ jarante ǀ práti ǀ vástoḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀyát ǀ niktá-hastaḥ ǀ taráṇiḥ ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ sómam ǀ susā́va ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ádri-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ssacred fires, the instrumental uments of holy sacrifice the conveyers of libations, praise the associated Aśvinsat the break of day, when the observant (priest) the conductor of the rite, with washedhandshas expressed by the (grinding) stones the sweet-flavoured Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: The ssacred fires, the instrumental uments of holy sacrifice the conveyers of libations, praise the associated Aśvinsat the break of day, when the observant (priest) the conductor of the rite, with washedhandshas expressed by the (grinding) stones the sweet-flavoured Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आकेनिपासो अहभिर्दविध्वतः स्वर्ण शुक्रं तन्वंत आ रजः ।सूरश्चिदश्वान्युयुजान ईयते विश्वाँ अनु स्वधया चेतथस्पथः ॥
verses.transliteration: āke-nipā́saḥ ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ dávidhvataḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ śukrám ǀ tanvántaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ rájaḥ ǀsū́raḥ ǀ cit ǀ áśvān ǀ yuyujānáḥ ǀ īyate ǀ víśvān ǀ ánu ǀ svadháyā ǀ cetathaḥ ǀ patháḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The near-advancing (rays), dispersing (the darkness) by the (light of day), are overspreading the firmament with lustre like the sun; the sun, harnessing his horses, (proceeds on his way); do you make known all his paths by (following) after (him) with sacrificial food.
verses.wilson_translation: The near-advancing (rays), dispersing (the darkness) by the (light of day), are overspreading the firmament with lustre like the sun; the sun, harnessing his horses, (proceeds on his way); do you make known all his paths by (following) after (him) with sacrificial food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वामवोचमश्विना धियंधा रथः स्वश्वो अजरो यो अस्ति ।येन सद्यः परि रजांसि याथो हविष्मंतं तरणिं भोजमच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vām ǀ avocam ǀ aśvinā ǀ dhiyam-dhā́ḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ su-áśvaḥ ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásti ǀyéna ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ pári ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ yātháḥ ǀ havíṣmantam ǀ taráṇim ǀ bhojám ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Celebrating (sacred) rites, I glorify you,Aśvins; well-horsed and undecaying is that chariot, whereby you quickly traverse the regions (of space), and come to (our sacrifice) abounding in oblations, promptly passing away, and the yielder of enjoyment.
verses.wilson_translation: Celebrating (sacred) rites, I glorify you,Aśvins; well-horsed and undecaying is that chariot, whereby you quickly traverse the regions (of space), and come to (our sacrifice) abounding in oblations, promptly passing away, and the yielder of enjoyment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVI. Vāyu. Indra-Vāyu
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRINK the best draught of Soma-juice, O Vāyu, at our holy rites:For thou art he who drinketh first. Come, team-drawn, with thy hundred helps, with Indra, seated in the car,Vāyu, and drink your fill of juice. May steeds a thousand bring you both, Indra. and Vāyu, hitherwardTo drink the Soma, to the feast. For ye, O Indra-Vāyu, mount the golden-seated car that aidsThe sacrifice, that reaches heaven. On far-refulgent chariot come unto the man who offers gifts:Come, Indra-Vāyu, hitherward. Here, Indra-Vāyu, is the juice: drink it, accordant with the Gods,Within the giver's dwelling-place. Hither, O Indra-Vāyu, be your journey here unyoke your steeds,Here for your draught of Soma juice.

verses.sanskrit: अग्रं पिबा मधूनां सुतं वायो दिविष्टिषु ।त्वं हि पूर्वपा असि ॥
verses.transliteration: ágram ǀ piba ǀ mádhūnām ǀ sutám ǀ vāyo íti ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀtvám ǀ hí ǀ pūrva-pā́ḥ ǀ ási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink first,Vāyu, the effused libation of the Somaat the rites that secure heaven, for you verily are the first drinker.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink first,Vāyu, the effused libation of the Somaat the rites that secure heaven, for you verily are the first drinker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वाँ इंद्रसारथिः ।वायो सुतस्य तृंपतं ॥
verses.transliteration: śaténa ǀ naḥ ǀ abhíṣṭi-bhiḥ ǀ niyútvān ǀ índra-sārathiḥ ǀvā́yo íti ǀ sutásya ǀ tṛmpatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāyu, who are drawn by the Niyuts, and have Indrafor charioteer, come (for the fulfilment) of our numerous wishes, and do you (and Indra) drink of the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāyu, who are drawn by the Niyuts, and have Indrafor charioteer, come (for the fulfilment) of our numerous wishes, and do you (and Indra) drink of the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां सहस्रं हरय इंद्रवायू अभि प्रयः ।वहंतु सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ sahásram ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ abhí ǀ práyaḥ ǀváhantu ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Vāyu, may a thousand steeds, eager for food, bring you to drink the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Vāyu, may a thousand steeds, eager for food, bring you to drink the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथं हिरण्यवंधुरमिंद्रवायू स्वध्वरं ।आ हि स्थाथो दिविस्पृशं ॥
verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ híraṇya-vandhuram ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ su-adhvarám ǀā́ ǀ hí ǀ sthā́thaḥ ǀ divi-spṛ́śam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mount,Indraand Vāyu, the golden-seated chariot, propitious to sacrifice, soaring to heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Mount,Indraand Vāyu, the golden-seated chariot, propitious to sacrifice, soaring to heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथेन पृथुपाजसा दाश्वांसमुप गच्छतं ।इंद्रवायू इहा गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: ráthena ǀ pṛthu-pā́jasā ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ úpa ǀ gacchatam ǀíndravāyū íti ǀ ihá ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Vāyu, come with your very strong chariot to the sacrifice; come hither.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Vāyu, come with your very strong chariot to the sacrifice; come hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रवायू अयं सुतस्तं देवेभिः सजोषसा ।पिबतं दाशुषो गृहे ॥
verses.transliteration: índravāyū íti ǀ ayám ǀ sutáḥ ǀ tám ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣasā ǀpíbatam ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ gṛhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Vāyu, this (libation) is poured out sympathizing with the gods, drink it in the dwelling of the donor.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Vāyu, this (libation) is poured out sympathizing with the gods, drink it in the dwelling of the donor.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इह प्रयाणमस्तु वामिंद्रवायू विमोचनं ।इह वां सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ pra-yā́nam ǀ astu ǀ vām ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ vi-mócanam ǀihá ǀ vām ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither be your course; here,Indraand Vāyu, be the letting of your horses loose, for your drinking of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Hither be your course; here,Indraand Vāyu, be the letting of your horses loose, for your drinking of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVIL Vāyu. Indra-Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Vāyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites.Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God, longed-for, on thy team-drawn car. O Vāyu, thou and Indra are meet drinkers of these Soma-draughts,For unto you the drops proceed as waters gather to the vale. O Indra-Vāyu, mighty Twain, speeding together, Lords of Strength,Come to our succour with your team, that ye may drink the Soma juice. The longed-for teams which ye possess, O Heroes, for the worshipper,Turn to us, Indra-Vāyu, ye to whom the sacrifice is paid.

verses.sanskrit: वायो शुक्रो अयामि ते मध्वो अग्रं दिविष्टिषु ।आ याहि सोमपीतये स्पार्हो देव नियुत्वता ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́yo íti ǀ śukráḥ ǀ ayāmi ǀ te ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ spārháḥ ǀ deva ǀ niyútvatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Purified (by holy acts) I bring to you,Vāyu, the Soma, first (offered to you at sacrifices) that seek to gain heaven; deity, who are ever longed over, come with your Niyutsteeds to drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Purified (by holy acts) I bring to you,Vāyu, the Soma, first (offered to you at sacrifices) that seek to gain heaven; deity, who are ever longed over, come with your Niyutsteeds to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रश्च वायवेषां सोमानां पीतिमर्हथः ।युवां हि यंतींदवो निम्नमापो न सध्र्यक् ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ vāyo íti ǀ eṣām ǀ sómānām ǀ pītím ǀ arhathaḥ ǀyuvā́m ǀ hí ǀ yánti ǀ índavaḥ ǀ nimnám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ sadhryák ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Vāyu, you are fit for the drinking of these Somalibations, for the drops flow towards you as waters (run) together in a deep plural ce.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Vāyu, you are fit for the drinking of these Somalibations, for the drops flow towards you as waters (run) together in a deep plural ce.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वायविंद्रश्च शुष्मिणा सरथं शवसस्पती ।नियुत्वंता न ऊतय आ यातं सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́yo íti ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ śuṣmíṇā ǀ sa-rátham ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀniyútvantā ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Vāyu, who are lords of strength, vigorous and drawn by the Niyutsteeds, come (riding in) the same car; drink the Somafor our protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Vāyu, who are lords of strength, vigorous and drawn by the Niyutsteeds, come (riding in) the same car; drink the Somafor our protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या वां संति पुरुस्पृहो नियुतो दाशुषे नरा ।अस्मे ता यज्ञवाहसेंद्रवायू नि यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ sánti ǀ puru-spṛ́haḥ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ narā ǀasmé íti ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ yajña-vāhasā ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ ní ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leaders (of rites), conveyers of sacrifices,Indraand Vāyu, give to us for the offer (of the oblation), those Niyutswho are your (steeds), and are desired of many.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of rites), conveyers of sacrifices,Indraand Vāyu, give to us for the offer (of the oblation), those Niyutswho are your (steeds), and are desired of many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVIII. Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . TASTE offerings never tasted yet, as bards enjoy the foeman's wealth.O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice. Removing curses, drawn by teams, with Indra, seated by thy side,O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice. The two dark treasuries of wealth that wearall beauties wait on thee.O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice. May nine-and-ninety harnessed steeds who yoke them at thy will bring thee.O Vāyu, on refulgent car come to the drinking of the juice. Harness, O Vāyu, to thy car a hundred well-fed tawny steeds,Yea, or a thousand steeds, and let thy chariot come to us with might.

verses.sanskrit: विहि होत्रा अवीता विपो न रायो अर्यः ।वायवा चंद्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: vihí ǀ hótrā ǀ ávītāḥ ǀ vípaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀvā́yo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ candréṇa ǀ ráthena ǀ yāhí ǀ sutásya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink,Vāyu, the oblations yet untested, like (a prince) the terrifier of foes; (bestow) upon the worshipper wealth; come with your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Vāyu, the oblations yet untested, like (a prince) the terrifier of foes; (bestow) upon the worshipper wealth; come with your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: निर्युवाणो अशस्तीर्नियुत्वाँ इंद्रसारथिः ।वायवा चंद्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: niḥ-yuvānáḥ ǀ áśastīḥ ǀ niyútvān ǀ índra-sārathiḥ ǀvā́yo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ candréṇa ǀ ráthena ǀ yāhí ǀ sutásya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāyu, who are the represser of calumnies, who are drawn by the Niyuts, and have Indrafor your charioteer come with your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāyu, who are the represser of calumnies, who are drawn by the Niyuts, and have Indrafor your charioteer come with your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनु कृष्णे वसुधिती येमाते विश्वपेशसा ।वायवा चंद्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ kṛṣṇé íti ǀ vásudhitī íti vásu-dhitī ǀ yemā́te íti ǀ viśvá-peśasā ǀvā́yo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ candréṇa ǀ ráthena ǀ yāhí ǀ sutásya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: The dark nurses of wealth, the universal forms (heaven and earth), attend upon you; come Vāyuwith your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: The dark nurses of wealth, the universal forms (heaven and earth), attend upon you; come Vāyuwith your brilliant car to drink the Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वहंतु त्वा मनोयुजो युक्तासो नवतिर्नव ।वायवा चंद्रेण रथेन याहि सुतस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: váhantu ǀ tvā ǀ manaḥ-yújaḥ ǀ yuktā́saḥ ǀ navatíḥ ǀ náva ǀvā́yo íti ǀ ā́ ǀ candréṇa ǀ ráthena ǀ yāhí ǀ sutásya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the ninety-nine steeds harnessed together, that are as swift as thought, convey you; come,Vāyu, with your brilliant car, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: May the ninety-nine steeds harnessed together, that are as swift as thought, convey you; come,Vāyu, with your brilliant car, to drink the Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वायो शतं हरीणां युवस्व पोष्याणां ।उत वा ते सहस्रिणो रथ आ यातु पाजसा ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́yo íti ǀ śatám ǀ hárīṇām ǀ yuvásva ǀ póṣyāṇām ǀutá ǀ vā ǀ te ǀ sahasríṇaḥ ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yātu ǀ pā́jasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harness,Vāyu, a hundred plural mp steeds, or even a thousand, and let your chariot come with rapidity (hither).
verses.wilson_translation: Harness,Vāyu, a hundred plural mp steeds, or even a thousand, and let your chariot come with rapidity (hither).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIX. Indra-Bṛhaspati.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DEAR is this offering in your mouth, O Indra and Bṛhaspati:Famed is the laud, the gladdening draught. This lovely Soma is effused, O Indra and Bṛhaspati,For you, to drink it and rejoice. As Soma-drinkers to our house come, Indra and Bṛhaspati-and Indra-to drink Soma juice. Vouchsafe us riches hundredfold, O Indra, and Bṛhaspati,With store of horses, thousandfold. O Indra. and Bṛhaspati, we call you when the meath is shed,With songs, to drink the Soma juice. Drink, Indra and Bṛhaspati, the Soma in the giver's house:Delight yourselves abiding there.

verses.sanskrit: इदं वामास्ये हविः प्रियमिंद्राबृहस्पती ।उक्थं मदश्च शस्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ vām ǀ āsyé ǀ havíḥ ǀ priyám ǀ indrābṛhaspatī íti ǀukthám ǀ mádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ śasyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: (I present) the agreeable oblation to your mouths,Indraand Bṛhaspati, and the hymn and the exhilarating beverage are offered.
verses.wilson_translation: (I present) the agreeable oblation to your mouths,Indraand Bṛhaspati, and the hymn and the exhilarating beverage are offered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं वां परि षिच्यते सोम इंद्राबृहस्पती ।चारुर्मदाय पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vām ǀ pári ǀ sicyate ǀ sómaḥ ǀ indrābṛhaspatī íti ǀcā́ruḥ ǀ mádāya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: This delicious Somais effused,Indraand Bṛhaspati, for you, (your) drinking and exhilaration.
verses.wilson_translation: This delicious Somais effused,Indraand Bṛhaspati, for you, (your) drinking and exhilaration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ न इंद्राबृहस्पती गृहमिंद्रश्च गच्छतं ।सोमपा सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ indrābṛhaspatī íti ǀ gṛhám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ gacchatam ǀsoma-pā́ ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Bṛhaspati, come to our dwelling, drinkers of Soma, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Bṛhaspati, come to our dwelling, drinkers of Soma, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे इंद्राबृहस्पती रयिं धत्तं शतग्विनं ।अश्वावंतं सहस्रिणं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ indrābṛhaspatī íti ǀ rayím ǀ dhattam ǀ śata-gvínam ǀáśva-vantam ǀ sahasríṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant to us,Indraand Bṛhaspatiriches comprising a hundred (cattle), a thousand horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant to us,Indraand Bṛhaspatiriches comprising a hundred (cattle), a thousand horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राबृहस्पती वयं सुते गीर्भिर्हवामहे ।अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: índrābṛ́haspátī íti ǀ vayám ǀ suté ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ havāmahe ǀasyá ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Bṛhaspati, we invoke you with praises, when the libation is effused, to drink of this Somajuice.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Bṛhaspati, we invoke you with praises, when the libation is effused, to drink of this Somajuice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सोममिंद्राबृहस्पती पिबतं दाशुषो गृहे ।मादयेथां तदोकसा ॥
verses.transliteration: sómam ǀ indrābṛhaspatī íti ǀ píbatam ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀmādáyethām ǀ tát-okasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink,Indraand Bṛhaspati, the Soma; in the dwelling of the donor, and be exhilarated in his abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indraand Bṛhaspati, the Soma; in the dwelling of the donor, and be exhilarated in his abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN L. Bṛhaspati.
hymns.anukramani: ११ वामदेवो गौतमः। बृहस्पतिः, १०-११ इन्द्राबृहस्पती । त्रिष्टुप्, १० जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Him who with might hath propped earth's ends, who sitteth in threefold seat, Bṛhaspati, with thunder,Him of the pleasant tongue have ancient sages, deep-thinking, holy singers, set before them. Wild in their course, in well-marked wise rejoicing were they, Bṛhaspati, who pressed around us.Preserve Bṛhaspati, the stall uninjured, this company's raining, ever-moving birthplace. Bṛhaspati, from thy remotest distance have they sat down who love the law eternal.For thee were dug wells springing from the mountain, which murmuring round about pour streams of sweetness. Bṛhaspati, when first he had his being from mighty splendour in supremest heaven,Strong, with his sevenfold mouth, with noise of thunder, with his seven rays, blew and dispersed the darkness. With the loud-shouting band who sang his praises, with thunder, he destroyed obstructive Vala.Bṛhaspati thundering drave forth the cattle, the lowing cows who make oblations ready. Serve we with sacrifices, gifts, and homage even thus the Steer of all the Gods, the Father.Bṛhaspati, may we be lords of riches, with noble progeny and store of heroes. Surely that King by power and might heroic hath made him lord of all his foes' posses-ions,Who cherishes Bṛhaspati well-tended, adorns and worships him as foremost sharer. In his own house he dwells in peace and comfort: to him for ever holy food flows richly.To him the people with free will pay homage-the King with whom the Brahman hath precedence. He, unopposed, is master of the riches of his own subjects and of hostile people.The Gods uphold that King with their protection who helps the Brahman when he seeks his favour. Indra, Bṛhaspati, rainers of treasure, rejoicing at this sacrifice drink the Soma.Let the abundant drops sink deep within you: vouchsafe us riches with full store of heroes. Bṛhaspati and Indra, make us prosper may this be your benevolence to us-ward.Assist our holy thoughts, wake up our spirit: weaken the hatred of our foe and rivals.

verses.sanskrit: यस्तस्तंभ सहसा वि ज्मो अंतान्बृहस्पतिस्त्रिषधस्थो रवेण ।तं प्रत्नास ऋषयो दीध्यानाः पुरो विप्रा दधिरे मंद्रजिह्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tastámbha ǀ sáhasā ǀ ví ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántān ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ tri-sadhastháḥ ǀ ráveṇa ǀtám ǀ pratnā́saḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ víprāḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ mandrá-jihvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ancient sages, illustrious, intelligent, have plural ced before (them) the plural asing-tongued Bṛhaspati, who propped up by (his) strength the ends of the earth, and who abides with noise in the three regions.
verses.wilson_translation: The ancient sages, illustrious, intelligent, have plural ced before (them) the plural asing-tongued Bṛhaspati, who propped up by (his) strength the ends of the earth, and who abides with noise in the three regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धुनेतयः सुप्रकेतं मदंतो बृहस्पते अभि ये नस्ततस्रे ।पृषंतं सृप्रमदब्धमूर्वं बृहस्पते रक्षतादस्य योनिं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhuná-itayaḥ ǀ su-praketám ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ naḥ ǀ tatasré ǀpṛ́ṣantam ǀ sṛprám ǀ ádabdham ǀ ūrvám ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ rákṣatāt ǀ asya ǀ yónim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, protect the fruit-yielding, progressive, uninjured ample sacrifice of this (your worshipp0er, at which) they who are the terrifiers (of foes), the delighters of you who are possessed of great wisdom, glorify (you) in our behalf.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspati, protect the fruit-yielding, progressive, uninjured ample sacrifice of this (your worshipp0er, at which) they who are the terrifiers (of foes), the delighters of you who are possessed of great wisdom, glorify (you) in our behalf.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते या परमा परावदत आ त ऋतस्पृशो नि षेदुः ।तुभ्यं खाता अवता अद्रिदुग्धा मध्वः श्चोतंत्यभितो विरप्शं ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ yā́ ǀ paramā́ ǀ parā-vát ǀ átaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ ṛta-spṛ́śaḥ ǀ ní ǀ seduḥ ǀtúbhyam ǀ khātā́ḥ ǀ avatā́ḥ ǀ ádri-dugdhāḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ścotanti ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ vi-rapśám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those (steeds),Bṛhaspati, which had come from that distant (region), the best (of all), have sat down in connection with the ceremony, and to you the Somajuices expressed by the stones flow copiously, (accompanied) by the sounds of praise, like deep wells that supply water.
verses.wilson_translation: Those (steeds),Bṛhaspati, which had come from that distant (region), the best (of all), have sat down in connection with the ceremony, and to you the Somajuices expressed by the stones flow copiously, (accompanied) by the sounds of praise, like deep wells that supply water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पतिः प्रथमं जायमानो महो ज्योतिषः परमे व्योमन् ।सप्तास्यस्तुविजातो रवेण वि सप्तरश्मिरधमत्तमांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ jyótiṣaḥ ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀsaptá-āsyaḥ ǀ tuvi-jātáḥ ǀ ráveṇa ǀ ví ǀ saptá-raśmiḥ ǀ adhamat ǀ támāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, when first being born in the highest heaven of supreme light, seven-mouthed, multiform, (combined) with sound, and seven-rayed, has subdued the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspati, when first being born in the highest heaven of supreme light, seven-mouthed, multiform, (combined) with sound, and seven-rayed, has subdued the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स सुष्टुभा स ऋक्वता गणेन वलं रुरोज फलिगं रवेण ।बृहस्पतिरुस्रिया हव्यसूदः कनिक्रदद्वावशतीरुदाजत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ su-stúbhā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛ́kvatā ǀ gaṇéna ǀ valám ǀ ruroja ǀ phali-gám ǀ ráveṇa ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ havya-sū́daḥ ǀ kánikradat ǀ vā́vaśatīḥ ǀ út ǀ ājat ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Aided) by the praised and brilliant troop (of the Aṅgirasas), he destroyed with sound the mischievous Bala,Bṛhaspati, shouting aloud, set free the boon-bestowing, oblation-supplying kine.
verses.wilson_translation: (Aided) by the praised and brilliant troop (of the Aṅgirasas), he destroyed with sound the mischievous Bala,Bṛhaspati, shouting aloud, set free the boon-bestowing, oblation-supplying kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा पित्रे विश्वदेवाय वृष्णे यज्ञैर्विधेम नमसा हविर्भिः ।बृहस्पते सुप्रजा वीरवंतो वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ pitré ǀ viśvá-devāya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ námasā ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀbṛ́haspate ǀ su-prajā́ḥ ǀ vīrá-vantaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ syāma ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus may we offer worship with sacrifices, with oblations, with praise, to the paternal, universal deity, the showerer (of benefits); and may we,Bṛhaspati, become possessed of riches, and be blessed with excellent progeny and valiant descendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus may we offer worship with sacrifices, with oblations, with praise, to the paternal, universal deity, the showerer (of benefits); and may we,Bṛhaspati, become possessed of riches, and be blessed with excellent progeny and valiant descendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स इद्राजा प्रतिजन्यानि विश्वा शुष्मेण तस्थावभि वीर्येण ।बृहस्पतिं यः सुभृतं बिभर्ति वल्गूयति वंदते पूर्वभाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ rā́jā ǀ práti-janyāni ǀ víśvā ǀ śúṣmeṇa ǀ tasthau ǀ abhí ǀ vīryéṇa ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ yáḥ ǀ sú-bhṛtam ǀ bibhárti ǀ valgu-yáti ǀ vándate ǀ pūrva-bhā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: That prince overcomes by his strength and prowess, all hostile people, who cherishes liberally Bṛhaspati, and glorifies and honours him as the first sharer (of the offering).
verses.wilson_translation: That prince overcomes by his strength and prowess, all hostile people, who cherishes liberally Bṛhaspati, and glorifies and honours him as the first sharer (of the offering).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स इत्क्षेति सुधित ओकसि स्वे तस्मा इळा पिन्वते विश्वदानीं ।तस्मै विशः स्वयमेवा नमंते यस्मिन्ब्रह्मा राजनि पूर्व एति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ kṣeti ǀ sú-dhitaḥ ǀ ókasi ǀ své ǀ tásmai ǀ íḷā ǀ pinvate ǀ viśva-dā́nīm ǀtásmai ǀ víśaḥ ǀ svayám ǀ evá ǀ namante ǀ yásmin ǀ brahmā́ ǀ rā́jani ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ éti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Verily he abides prosperous in his own abode; for him the earth bears fruit at all seasons; to him (his) subjects willingly pay homage, the prince, to whom the Brāhmaṇafirst, (duly reverenced), repairs.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily he abides prosperous in his own abode; for him the earth bears fruit at all seasons; to him (his) subjects willingly pay homage, the prince, to whom the Brāhmaṇafirst, (duly reverenced), repairs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अप्रतीतो जयति सं धनानि प्रतिजन्यान्युत या सजन्या ।अवस्यवे यो वरिवः कृणोति ब्रह्मणे राजा तमवंति देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: áprati-itaḥ ǀ jayati ǀ sám ǀ dhánāni ǀ práti-janyāni ǀ utá ǀ yā́ ǀ sá-janyā ǀavasyáve ǀ yáḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ brahmáṇe ǀ rā́jā ǀ tám ǀ avanti ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unopposed he is the master of the riches of hostile people, and of his own subjects; the Rājāwho bestows riches upon the Brāhmaṇaseeking his protection him the gods protect.
verses.wilson_translation: Unopposed he is the master of the riches of hostile people, and of his own subjects; the Rājāwho bestows riches upon the Brāhmaṇaseeking his protection him the gods protect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पतेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे मंदसाना वृषण्वसू ।आ वां विशंत्विंदवः स्वाभुवोऽस्मे रयिं सर्ववीरं नि यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ sómam ǀ pibatam ǀ bṛhaspate ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ mandasānā́ ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀā́ ǀ vām ǀ viśantu ǀ índavaḥ ǀ su-ābhúvaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ sárva-vīram ǀ ní ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, do you and Indra, both exulting and showering riches, drink the Somaat this sacrifice; may the all-pervading drops enter you; bestow upon us riches, comprising allmaledescendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspati, do you and Indra, both exulting and showering riches, drink the Somaat this sacrifice; may the all-pervading drops enter you; bestow upon us riches, comprising allmaledescendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पत इंद्र वर्धतं नः सचा सा वां सुमतिर्भूत्वस्मे ।अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्जजस्तमर्यो वनुषामरातीः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ indra ǀ várdhatam ǀ naḥ ǀ sácā ǀ sā́ ǀ vām ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ bhūtu ǀ asmé íti ǀaviṣṭám ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ jigṛtám ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ jajastám ǀ aryáḥ ǀ vanúṣām ǀ árātīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati,Indra, elevate us; may the favourable disposition of you both be combined for us; protect our rites; be awake to our laudations, confound the arrogant (foes) of us who are the donors (of oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspati,Indra, elevate us; may the favourable disposition of you both be combined for us; protect our rites; be awake to our laudations, confound the arrogant (foes) of us who are the donors (of oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LI. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FORTH from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant splendid light hatb mounted.Now verily the far-refulgent Mornings, Daughters of Heaven, bring welfare to the people. The richly-coloured Dawns have mounted eastward, like pillars planted at our sacrifices,And, flushing far, splendid and purifying, unbarred the portals of the fold of darkness. Dispelling gloom this day the wealthy Mornings urge liberal givers to present their treasures.In the unlightened depth of darkness round them let niggard traffickers sleep unawakened. O Goddesses, is this your car, I ask you, ancient this day, or is it new, ye Mornings,Wherewith, rich Dawns, ye seek with wealth Navagva, Daśagva Aṅgira, the seven-toned singer? With horses harnessed by eternal Order, Goddesses, swiftly round the worlds ye travel,Arousing from their rest, O Dawns, the sleeping, and all that lives, man, bird, and beast, to motion. Which among these is eldest, and where is she through whom they fixed the Ṛbhus' regulations?What time the splendid Dawns go forth for splendour, they are not known apart, alike, unwasting. Blest were these Dawns of old, shining with succour, true with the truth that springs from holy Order;With whom the toiling worshipper, by praises, hymning and lauding, soon attained to riches. Hither from eastward all at once they travel, from one place spreading in the selfsame manner.Awaking, from the seat of holy Order the Godlike Dawns come nigh like troops of cattle. Thus they go forth with undiminished colours, these Mornings similar, in self-same fashion,Concealing the gigantic might of darkness with radiant bodies bright and pure and shining. O Goddesses, O Heaven's refulgent Daughters, bestow upon us wealth with store of children.As from our pleasant place of rest ye rouse us may we be masters of heroic vigour. Well-skilled in lore of sacrifice, ye Daughters of Heaven, refulgent Dawns, I thus address you.May we be glorious among the people. May Heaven vouchsafe us this, and Earth the Goddess,

verses.sanskrit: इदमु त्यत्पुरुतमं पुरस्ताज्ज्योतिस्तमसो वयुनावदस्थात् ।नूनं दिवो दुहितरो विभातीर्गातुं कृणवन्नुषसो जनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyát ǀ puru-támam ǀ purástāt ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ támasaḥ ǀ vayúna-vat ǀ asthāt ǀnūnám ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitáraḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ kṛṇavan ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jánāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: This widely-spread and sense-bestowing light has sprung up in the east from out of the darkness; verily the brilliant Dawns, the daughters of heaven, are giving to man (the faculty to act).
verses.wilson_translation: This widely-spread and sense-bestowing light has sprung up in the east from out of the darkness; verily the brilliant Dawns, the daughters of heaven, are giving to man (the faculty to act).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्थुरु चित्रा उषसः पुरस्तान्मिता इव स्वरवोऽध्वरेषु ।व्यू व्रजस्य तमसो द्वारोच्छंतीरव्रंछुचयः पावकाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ásthuḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ mitā́ḥ-iva ǀ sváravaḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vrajásya ǀ támasaḥ ǀ dvā́rā ǀ ucchántīḥ ǀ avran ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ pāvakā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The many-limbed Dawns rise up in the east, like the pillars plural nted at sacrifices (round the altar); radiant and purifying, they are manifested, opening the gates of the obstructing gloom.
verses.wilson_translation: The many-limbed Dawns rise up in the east, like the pillars plural nted at sacrifices (round the altar); radiant and purifying, they are manifested, opening the gates of the obstructing gloom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छंतीरद्य चितयंत भोजान्राधोदेयायोषसो मघोनीः ।अचित्रे अंतः पणयः ससंत्वबुध्यमानास्तमसो विमध्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: ucchántīḥ ǀ adyá ǀ citayanta ǀ bhojā́n ǀ rādhaḥ-déyāya ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ maghónīḥ ǀacitré ǀ antáríti ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ sasantu ǀ ábudhyamānāḥ ǀ támasaḥ ǀ ví-madhye ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gloom-dispelling, affluent Dawns animate the pious worshippers to offer (sacrificial) treasure; may the churlish (traffickers) sleep on unawakened, in the unlovely depth of darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The gloom-dispelling, affluent Dawns animate the pious worshippers to offer (sacrificial) treasure; may the churlish (traffickers) sleep on unawakened, in the unlovely depth of darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कुवित्स देवीः सनयो नवो वा यामो बभूयादुषसो वो अद्य ।येना नवग्वे अंगिरे दशग्वे सप्तास्ये रेवती रेवदूष ॥
verses.transliteration: kuvít ǀ sáḥ ǀ devīḥ ǀ sanáyaḥ ǀ návaḥ ǀ vā ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ babhūyā́t ǀ uṣasaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ adyá ǀyéna ǀ náva-gve ǀ áṅgire ǀ dáśa-gve ǀ saptá-āsye ǀ revatīḥ ǀ revát ǀ ūṣá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Dawns, may your chariot, whether old or new, be frequent at this day's (worship), wherewith, affluent Dawns, possessing riches, (you shine) upon the seven-mouthed (troop of the)Aṅgirasas, the observers of the nine or ten days' rite.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Dawns, may your chariot, whether old or new, be frequent at this day's (worship), wherewith, affluent Dawns, possessing riches, (you shine) upon the seven-mouthed (troop of the)Aṅgirasas, the observers of the nine or ten days' rite.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं हि देवीर्ऋतयुग्भिरश्वैः परिप्रयाथ भुवनानि सद्यः ।प्रबोधयंतीरुषसः ससंतं द्विपाच्चतुष्पाच्चरथाय जीवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ hí ǀ devīḥ ǀ ṛtayúk-bhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ pari-prayāthá ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ sadyáḥ ǀpra-bodháyantīḥ ǀ uṣasaḥ ǀ sasántam ǀ dvi-pā́t ǀ cátuḥ-pāt ǀ caráthāya ǀ jīvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Dawns, with horses that frequent sacrifices you quickly travel round the regions (of space); awake the sleeping being, whether biped or quadruped, to pursue (his functions).
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Dawns, with horses that frequent sacrifices you quickly travel round the regions (of space); awake the sleeping being, whether biped or quadruped, to pursue (his functions).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्व स्विदासां कतमा पुराणी यया विधाना विदधुर्ऋभूणां ।शुभं यच्छुभ्रा उषसश्चरंति न वि ज्ञायंते सदृशीरजुर्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ svit ǀ āsām ǀ katamā́ ǀ purāṇī́ ǀ yáyā ǀ vi-dhā́nā ǀ vi-dadhúḥ ǀ ṛbhūṇā́m ǀśúbham ǀ yát ǀ śubhrā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ cáranti ǀ ná ǀ ví ǀ jñāyante ǀ sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ ajuryā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where is that ancient one of those (Dawns), through whom the works of theṚbhuswere accomplished? For as the bright Dawns happily proceed, they are not distinguished, being alike and undecaying.
verses.wilson_translation: Where is that ancient one of those (Dawns), through whom the works of theṚbhuswere accomplished? For as the bright Dawns happily proceed, they are not distinguished, being alike and undecaying.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता घा ता भद्रा उषसः पुरासुरभिष्टिद्युम्ना ऋतजातसत्याः ।यास्वीजानः शशमान उक्थैः स्तुवंछंसंद्रविणं सद्य आप ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ gha ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ āsuḥ ǀ abhiṣṭí-dyumnāḥ ǀ ṛtájāta-satyāḥ ǀyā́su ǀ ījānáḥ ǀ śaśamānáḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ stuván ǀ śáṃsan ǀ dráviṇam ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ā́pa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Verily those auspicious Dawns have been of old, rich with desired blessings, truthful (bestowers) of the results of sacrifice; at which the sacrificer, adoring with (silent) praise, glorifying (with hymns), has quickly obtained wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily those auspicious Dawns have been of old, rich with desired blessings, truthful (bestowers) of the results of sacrifice; at which the sacrificer, adoring with (silent) praise, glorifying (with hymns), has quickly obtained wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता आ चरंति समना पुरस्तात्समानतः समना पप्रथानाः ।ऋतस्य देवीः सदसो बुधाना गवां न सर्गा उषसो जरंते ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ caranti ǀ samanā́ ǀ purástāt ǀ samānátaḥ ǀ samanā́ ǀ paprathānā́ḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ budhānā́ḥ ǀ gávām ǀ ná ǀ sárgāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jarante ǁ
verses.english_translation: They spread around of smilar form, (coming) from the east, (coming) from the same region alike renowned; the divine Dawns, arousing the assembly of the sacrifice are glorified like the (rays) creative of the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: They spread around of smilar form, (coming) from the east, (coming) from the same region alike renowned; the divine Dawns, arousing the assembly of the sacrifice are glorified like the (rays) creative of the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता इन्न्वेव समना समानीरमीतवर्णा उषसश्चरंति ।गूहंतीरभ्वमसितं रुशद्भिः शुक्रास्तनूभिः शुचयो रुचानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ evá ǀ samanā́ ǀ samānī́ḥ ǀ ámīta-varṇāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ caranti ǀgū́hantīḥ ǀ ábhvam ǀ ásitam ǀ rúśat-bhiḥ ǀ śukrā́ḥ ǀ tanū́bhiḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ rucānā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those Dawns proceed verily all alike, of similar form, of infinite hues, pure, bright, illumining, concealing by their radiant person ns the very great gloom.
verses.wilson_translation: Those Dawns proceed verily all alike, of similar form, of infinite hues, pure, bright, illumining, concealing by their radiant person ns the very great gloom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रयिं दिवो दुहितरो विभातीः प्रजावंतं यच्छतास्मासु देवीः ।स्योनादा वः प्रतिबुध्यमानाः सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: rayím ǀ divaḥ ǀ duhitaraḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ prajā́-vantam ǀ yacchata ǀ asmā́su ǀ devīḥ ǀsyonā́t ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ prati-búdhyamānāḥ ǀ su-vī́ryasya ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine, resplendent daughters of heaven, bestow upon us wealth, comprehending progeny; awaking you for our benefit, may we be the lords of excellent descendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine, resplendent daughters of heaven, bestow upon us wealth, comprehending progeny; awaking you for our benefit, may we be the lords of excellent descendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वो दिवो दुहितरो विभातीरुप ब्रुव उषसो यज्ञकेतुः ।वयं स्याम यशसो जनेषु तद्द्यौश्च धत्तां पृथिवी च देवी ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀ duhitaraḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀ uṣasaḥ ǀ yajñá-ketuḥ ǀvayám ǀ syāma ǀ yaśásaḥ ǀ jáneṣu ǀ tát ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ca ǀ dhattā́m ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ca ǀ devī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Daughters of heaven, resplendent Dawns, I address you (as) the announcer of the sacrificer; may we be (the possessors) of celebrity among men, and may heaven and the divine earth perpetuate (it).
verses.wilson_translation: Daughters of heaven, resplendent Dawns, I address you (as) the announcer of the sacrificer; may we be (the possessors) of celebrity among men, and may heaven and the divine earth perpetuate (it).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS Lady, giver of delight, after her Sister shining forth, Daughter of Heaven, hath shown herself.- Unfailing, Mother of the Kine, in colour like a bright red mare,The Dawn became the Aśvins' Friend. Yea, and thou art the Aśvins' Friend, the Mother of the Kine art thou:O Dawn thou rulest over wealth. Thinking of thee, O joyous One, as her who driveth hate away,We woke to meet thee with our lauds. Our eyes behold thy blessed rays like troops of cattle loosed to feed.Dawn hath filled full the wide expanse. When thou hast filled it, Fulgent One! thou layest bare the gloom with light.After thy nature aid us, Dawn. Thou overspreadest heaven with rays, the dear wide region of mid-air.With thy bright shining lustre, Dawn.

verses.sanskrit: प्रति ष्या सूनरी जनी व्युच्छंती परि स्वसुः ।दिवो अदर्शि दुहिता ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ syā́ ǀ sūnárī ǀ jánī ǀ vi-ucchántī ǀ pári ǀ svásuḥ ǀdiváḥ ǀ adarśi ǀ duhitā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The daughter of heaven has been seen; the kind conductress (of men), the parent (of benefits) shedding radiance upon (the departure of her) sister nighṭ
verses.wilson_translation: The daughter of heaven has been seen; the kind conductress (of men), the parent (of benefits) shedding radiance upon (the departure of her) sister nighṭ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वेव चित्रारुषी माता गवामृतावरी ।सखाभूदश्विनोरुषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvā-iva ǀ citrā́ ǀ áruṣī ǀ mātā́ ǀ gávām ǀ ṛtá-varī ǀsákhā ǀ abhūt ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a beautiful mare, the radiant mother of the rays of light, the object of sacrifice, (she) is the friend of the Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: Like a beautiful mare, the radiant mother of the rays of light, the object of sacrifice, (she) is the friend of the Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत सखास्यश्विनोरुत माता गवामसि ।उतोषो वस्व ईशिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sákhā ǀ asi ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ utá ǀ mātā́ ǀ gávām ǀ asi ǀutá ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ īśiṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are the friend of the Aśvins; you are the mother of the rays of light; you, Uṣas, rule over riches.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the friend of the Aśvins; you are the mother of the rays of light; you, Uṣas, rule over riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यावयद्द्वेषसं त्वा चिकित्वित्सूनृतावरि ।प्रति स्तोमैरभुत्स्महि ॥
verses.transliteration: yavayát-dveṣasam ǀ tvā ǀ cikitvít ǀ sūnṛtā-vari ǀpráti ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ abhutsmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: With praises we awaken you, you who are endowed with truth; you, baffler of animosities, the restorer of consciousness.
verses.wilson_translation: With praises we awaken you, you who are endowed with truth; you, baffler of animosities, the restorer of consciousness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति भद्रा अदृक्षत गवां सर्गा न रश्मयः ।ओषा अप्रा उरु ज्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ adṛkṣata ǀ gávām ǀ sárgāḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀā́ ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ urú ǀ jráyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The auspicious rays are visible like showers of rain, the dawn has filled (the world) with ample light.
verses.wilson_translation: The auspicious rays are visible like showers of rain, the dawn has filled (the world) with ample light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आपप्रुषी विभावरि व्यावर्ज्योतिषा तमः ।उषो अनु स्वधामव ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-paprúṣī ǀ vibhā-vari ǀ ví ǀ āvaḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ támaḥ ǀúṣaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ svadhā́m ǀ ava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brilliant Uṣas, filling (the world with light), you disperse the darkness with radiance; thereafter protect the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Brilliant Uṣas, filling (the world with light), you disperse the darkness with radiance; thereafter protect the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ द्यां तनोषि रश्मिभिरांतरिक्षमुरु प्रियं ।उषः शुक्रेण शोचिषा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ tanoṣi ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ urú ǀ priyám ǀúṣaḥ ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: You overspread, Uṣas, the heaven with rays, as well as the vast and beloved firmament with pure lustre.
verses.wilson_translation: You overspread, Uṣas, the heaven with rays, as well as the vast and beloved firmament with pure lustre.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Savitar.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . OF Savitar the God, the sapient Asura, we crave this great gift which is worthy of our choice,Wherewith he freely grants his worshiper defence. This with his rays the Great God hath vouchsafed to us. Sustainer of the heaven, Lord of the whole world's life, the Sage, he putteth on his golden-coloured mail.Clear-sighted, spreading far, filling the spacious realm, Savitar hath brought forth bliss that deserveth laud. He hath filled full the regions of the heaven and earth: the God for his own strengthening waketh up the hymn.Savitar hath stretched out his arms to cherish life, producing with his rays and lulling all that moves. Lighting all living creatures, ne’er to be deceived, Savitar, God, protects each holy ordinance.He hath stretched out his arms to all the folk of earth, and, with his laws observed, rules his own mighty course. Savitar thrice surrounding with his mightiness mid-air, three regions, and the triple sphere of light,Sets the three heavens in motion and the threefold earth, and willingly protects us with his triple law. Most gracious God, who brings to life and lulls to rest, he who controls the world, what moves not and what moves,May he vouchsafe us shelter,—Savitar the God,—for tranquil life, with triple bar against distress. With the year's seasons hath Savitar, God, come nigh: may he prosper our home, give food and noble sons.May he invigorate us through the days and nights, and may he send us opulence with progeny.

verses.sanskrit: तद्देवस्य सवितुर्वार्यं महद्वृणीमहे असुरस्य प्रचेतसः ।छर्दिर्येन दाशुषे यच्छति त्मना तन्नो महाँ उदयांदेवो अक्तुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ devásya ǀ savitúḥ ǀ vā́ryam ǀ mahát ǀ vṛṇīmáhe ǀ ásurasya ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀchardíḥ ǀ yéna ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ yácchati ǀ tmánā ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ út ǀ ayān ǀ deváḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit of the divine, powerful, and intelligen Savitāthat desirable and ample (wealth), along with which he grants a dwelling to the offerer of the oblation of his own accord; may the great deity grant us such every day.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit of the divine, powerful, and intelligen Savitāthat desirable and ample (wealth), along with which he grants a dwelling to the offerer of the oblation of his own accord; may the great deity grant us such every day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिवो धर्ता भुवनस्य प्रजापतिः पिशंगं द्रापिं प्रति मुंचते कविः ।विचक्षणः प्रथयन्नापृणन्नुर्वजीजनत्सविता सुम्नमुक्थ्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ dhartā́ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ prajā́-patiḥ ǀ piśáṅgam ǀ drāpím ǀ práti ǀ muñcate ǀ kavíḥ ǀvi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ pratháyan ǀ ā-pṛṇán ǀ urú ǀ ájījanat ǀ savitā́ ǀ sumnám ǀ ukthyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The supporter of heaven, the protector of the world, the wise (Savitā) puts on his golden armour discrimiator (of objects), filling (the world with light) Savitā has engendered great and laudable felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: The supporter of heaven, the protector of the world, the wise (Savitā) puts on his golden armour discrimiator (of objects), filling (the world with light) Savitā has engendered great and laudable felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आप्रा रजांसि दिव्यानि पार्थिवा श्लोकं देवः कृणुते स्वाय धर्मणे ।प्र बाहू अस्राक्सविता सवीमनि निवेशयन्प्रसुवन्नक्तुभिर्जगत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ aprāḥ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ divyā́ni ǀ pā́rthivā ǀ ślókam ǀ deváḥ ǀ kṛṇute ǀ svā́ya ǀ dhármaṇe ǀprá ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ asrāk ǀ savitā́ ǀ sávīmani ǀ ni-veśáyan ǀ pra-suván ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ jágat ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine (Savitā) fills (with radiance) the celestial and terrestrial regions, and boasts of his own function; Savitā puts forth his arms or (the work of) production, regulating the world, and animating it with light.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine (Savitā) fills (with radiance) the celestial and terrestrial regions, and boasts of his own function; Savitā puts forth his arms or (the work of) production, regulating the world, and animating it with light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अदाभ्यो भुवनानि प्रचाकशद्व्रतानि देवः सविताभि रक्षते ।प्रास्राग्बाहू भुवनस्य प्रजाभ्यो धृतव्रतो महो अज्मस्य राजति ॥
verses.transliteration: ádābhyaḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ pra-cā́kaśat ǀ vratā́ni ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ abhí ǀ rakṣate ǀprá ǀ asrāk ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ pra-jā́bhyaḥ ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ ájmasya ǀ rājati ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Savitāunrestrained, illumining the regions, protects the righteous acts (of men); he extends his arms for (the direction of) the people of the earth; observant of obligations, he rules over the wide world.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitāunrestrained, illumining the regions, protects the righteous acts (of men); he extends his arms for (the direction of) the people of the earth; observant of obligations, he rules over the wide world.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिरंतरिक्षं सविता महित्वना त्री रजांसि परिभुस्त्रीणि रोचना ।तिस्रो दिवः पृथिवीस्तिस्र इन्वति त्रिभिर्व्रतैरभि नो रक्षति त्मना ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ savitā́ ǀ mahi-tvanā́ ǀ trī́ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ pari-bhū́ḥ ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ rocanā́ ǀtisráḥ ǀ dívaḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ḥ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ invati ǀ tri-bhíḥ ǀ vratáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ rakṣati ǀ tmánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Savitā, encompassing them by his magnitude, pervades th three (divisions of the) firmament, thethree worlds, the three brilliant sphere, the three heavens, the threefold earth may he, by his three functions, of his own (plural asure) protect us.
verses.wilson_translation: Savitā, encompassing them by his magnitude, pervades th three (divisions of the) firmament, thethree worlds, the three brilliant sphere, the three heavens, the threefold earth may he, by his three functions, of his own (plural asure) protect us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहत्सुम्नः प्रसवीता निवेशनो जगतः स्थातुरुभयस्य यो वशी ।स नो देवः सविता शर्म यच्छत्वस्मे क्षयाय त्रिवरूथमंहसः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhát-sumnaḥ ǀ pra-savitā́ ǀ ni-véśanaḥ ǀ jágataḥ ǀ sthātúḥ ǀ ubháyasya ǀ yáḥ ǀ vaśī́ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatu ǀ asmé íti ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that divine Savitā, who is the source of great happiness, the engenderer (of good works), the comprehender (of all beings), the regulator of both the moveable and the stationary, grant us happiness in thethree worlds, and (be) to us for the destruction of sin.
verses.wilson_translation: May that divine Savitā, who is the source of great happiness, the engenderer (of good works), the comprehender (of all beings), the regulator of both the moveable and the stationary, grant us happiness in thethree worlds, and (be) to us for the destruction of sin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आगंदेव ऋतुभिर्वर्धतु क्षयं दधातु नः सविता सुप्रजामिषं ।स नः क्षपाभिरहभिश्च जिन्वतु प्रजावंतं रयिमस्मे समिन्वतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ agan ǀ deváḥ ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǀ várdhatu ǀ kṣáyam ǀ dádhātu ǀ naḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ su-prajā́m ǀ íṣam ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ kṣapā́bhiḥ ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ ca ǀ jinvatu ǀ prajā́-vantam ǀ rayím ǀ asmé íti ǀ sám ǀ invatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine Savitāapproach along with the Ṛtus, prosper our dwelling, and bestow upon us good progeny and food; may he be favourable to us by night and by day; may he heap upon us wealth comprehending offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitāapproach along with the Ṛtus, prosper our dwelling, and bestow upon us good progeny and food; may he be favourable to us by night and by day; may he heap upon us wealth comprehending offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Savitar.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now must we praise and honour Savitar the God: at this time of the day the men must call to him,Him who distributes wealth to Manu's progeny, that he may grant us here riches most excellent. For thou at first producest for the holy Gods the noblest of all portions, immortality:Thereafter as a gift to men, O Savitar, thou openest existence, life succeeding life. If we, men as we are, have sinned against the Gods through want of thought, in weakness, or through insolence,Absolve us from the guilt and make us free from sin, O Savitar, alike among both Gods and men. None may impede that power of Savitar the God whereby he will maintain the universal world.What the fair-fingered God brings forth on earth's expanse or in the height of heaven, that work of his stands sure. To lofty hills thou sendest those whom Indra leads, and givest fixed abodes with houses unto these.However they may fly and draw themselves apart, still, Savitar, they stand obeying thy behest. May the libations poured to thee thrice daily, day after day, O Savitar, bring us blessing.May Indra, Heaven, Earth, Sindhu with the Waters, Aditi with Ādityas, give us shelter.

verses.sanskrit: अभूद्देवः सविता वंद्यो नु न इदानीमह्न उपवाच्यो नृभिः ।वि यो रत्ना भजति मानवेभ्यः श्रेष्ठं नो अत्र द्रविणं यथा दधत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūt ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ vándyaḥ ǀ nú ǀ naḥ ǀ idā́nīm ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ upa-vā́cyaḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀví ǀ yáḥ ǀ rátnā ǀ bhájati ǀ mānavébhyaḥ ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ dráviṇam ǀ yáthā ǀ dádhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Savitāhas been manifested; he is at once to be glorified by us; he is to be praised by the priests at the present (rite), and at the close (of the day), in order that he who apportions precious things to be descendants of Manumay bestow upon us, on this occasion, most excellent wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitāhas been manifested; he is at once to be glorified by us; he is to be praised by the priests at the present (rite), and at the close (of the day), in order that he who apportions precious things to be descendants of Manumay bestow upon us, on this occasion, most excellent wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवेभ्यो हि प्रथमं यज्ञियेभ्योऽमृतत्वं सुवसि भागमुत्तमं ।आदिद्दामानं सवितर्व्यूर्णुषेऽनूचीना जीविता मानुषेभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: devébhyaḥ ǀ hí ǀ prathamám ǀ yajñíyebhyaḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ suvási ǀ bhāgám ǀ ut-tamám ǀā́t ǀ ít ǀ dāmā́nam ǀ savitaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ūrṇuṣe ǀ anūcīnā́ ǀ jīvitā́ ǀ mā́nuṣebhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: First you engender for the adorable gods the best portion, immortality; then,Savitā, you set open (the day) to the donor (of the oblation), and (grant) successive existences to men.
verses.wilson_translation: First you engender for the adorable gods the best portion, immortality; then,Savitā, you set open (the day) to the donor (of the oblation), and (grant) successive existences to men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अचित्ती यच्चकृमा दैव्ये जने दीनैर्दक्षैः प्रभूती पूरुषत्वता ।देवेषु च सवितर्मानुषेषु च त्वं नो अत्र सुवतादनागसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ácittī ǀ yát ǀ cakṛmá ǀ dáivye ǀ jáne ǀ dīnáiḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ prá-bhūtī ǀ puruṣatvátā ǀdevéṣu ǀ ca ǀ savitaḥ ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ ca ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ suvatāt ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: If,Savitā, through ignorance, through pride in feeble or powerful (dependants), or through human infirmity, we have committed (offence) against your divine person n, or against gods or men, do you on this occasion hold us to be unoffending.
verses.wilson_translation: If,Savitā, through ignorance, through pride in feeble or powerful (dependants), or through human infirmity, we have committed (offence) against your divine person n, or against gods or men, do you on this occasion hold us to be unoffending.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न प्रमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तद्यथा विश्वं भुवनं धारयिष्यति ।यत्पृथिव्या वरिमन्ना स्वंगुरिर्वर्ष्मंदिवः सुवति सत्यमस्य तत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ pra-míye ǀ savitúḥ ǀ dáivyasya ǀ tát ǀ yáthā ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ dhārayiṣyáti ǀyát ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ váriman ǀ ā́ ǀ su-aṅguríḥ ǀ várṣman ǀ diváḥ ǀ suváti ǀ satyám ǀ asya ǀ tát ǁ
verses.english_translation: (It is) not (fit) to obstruct (the acts) of the divine Savitā, since by them he upholds the whole world, wheeby his gracioushandspreads fertility over the extent of the earth, and the magnitude of the heaven; such is his true (power).
verses.wilson_translation: (It is) not (fit) to obstruct (the acts) of the divine Savitā, since by them he upholds the whole world, wheeby his gracioushandspreads fertility over the extent of the earth, and the magnitude of the heaven; such is his true (power).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रज्येष्ठान्बृहद्भ्यः पर्वतेभ्यः क्षयाँ एभ्यः सुवसि पस्त्यावतः ।यथायथा पतयंतो वियेमिर एवैव तस्थुः सवितः सवाय ते ॥
verses.transliteration: índra-jyeṣṭhān ǀ bṛhát-bhyaḥ ǀ párvatebhyaḥ ǀ kṣáyān ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ suvasi ǀ pastyá-vataḥ ǀyáthā-yathā ǀ patáyantaḥ ǀ vi-yemiré ǀ evá ǀ evá ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ savitaríti ǀ savā́ya ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: You elevate those, of whom Indrais chief, above the vast clouds; for these, (your worshippers), you provide dwelling (plural ces) filled in habitations; as when advancing they detained you, so in like manner at your command they stayed.
verses.wilson_translation: You elevate those, of whom Indrais chief, above the vast clouds; for these, (your worshippers), you provide dwelling (plural ces) filled in habitations; as when advancing they detained you, so in like manner at your command they stayed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये ते त्रिरहन्त्सवितः सवासो दिवेदिवे सौभगमासुवंति ।इंद्रो द्यावापृथिवी सिंधुरद्भिरादित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्म यंसत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ te ǀ tríḥ ǀ áhan ǀ savitaríti ǀ savā́saḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ sáubhagam ǀ ā-suvánti ǀíndraḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ at-bhíḥ ǀ ādityáiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra, heaven and earth,Sindhuwith the waters, and Aditiwith theĀdityas, bestow happiness upon us, who, offering libations,Savitā, pour out the auspicious Soma, day by day, thrice a day.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, heaven and earth,Sindhuwith the waters, and Aditiwith theĀdityas, bestow happiness upon us, who, offering libations,Savitā, pour out the auspicious Soma, day by day, thrice a day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १० वामदेवो गौतमः। विश्वे देवाः। त्रिष्टुप् ८-१० गायत्री ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHO of you, Vasus, saveth? who protecteth? O Heaven and Earth and Aditi, preserve us,Varuṇa., Mitra, from the stronger mortal. Gods, which of you at sacrifice giveth comfort? They who with laud extol the ancient statutes, when they shine forth infallible dividers,Have ordered as perpetual Ordainers, and beamed as holy-thoughted Wonder-Workers. The Housewife Goddess, Aditi, and Sindhu, the Goddess Svasti I implore for friendship:And may the unobstructed Night and Morning both, day and night, provide for our protection. Aryaman, Varuṇa have disclosed the pathway, Agni as Lord of Strength the road to welfare.Lauded in manly mode may Indra-Viṣṇu grant us their powerful defence and shelter. I have besought the favour of the Maruts, of Parvata, of Bhaga God who rescues.From trouble caused by man the Lord preserve us; from woe sent by his friend let Mitra save us. Agree, through these our watery oblations, Goddesses, Heaven and Earth, with Ahibudhnya.As if to win the sea, the Gharma-heaters have opened, as they come anear, the rivers. May Goddess Aditi with Gods defend us, save us the saviour God with care unceasing.We dare not stint the sacred food of Mitra and Varuṇa upon the back of Agni. Agni is Sovran Lord of wealth, Agni of great prosperity:May he bestow these gifts on us. Hither to us, rich pleasant Dawn, bring many things to be desired,Thou who hast ample store of wealth. So then may Bhaga, Savitar, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Indra, with bounty come to us.

verses.sanskrit: को वस्त्राता वसवः को वरूता द्यावाभूमी अदिते त्रासीथां नः ।सहीयसो वरुण मित्र मर्तात्को वोऽध्वरे वरिवो धाति देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ trātā́ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ varūtā́ ǀ dyā́vābhūmī íti ǀ adite ǀ trā́sīthām ǀ naḥ ǀsáhīyasaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ mitra ǀ mártāt ǀ káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀ várivaḥ ǀ dhāti ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Which of you,Vasus, is a defender? Which is a protector? Heaven and earth and Aditipreserve us; defend us,Mitraand Varuṇa, from the strong man; who is it, gods, that offers you wealth at the sacrifice?
verses.wilson_translation: Which of you,Vasus, is a defender? Which is a protector? Heaven and earth and Aditipreserve us; defend us,Mitraand Varuṇa, from the strong man; who is it, gods, that offers you wealth at the sacrifice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ये धामानि पूर्व्याण्यर्चान्वि यदुच्छान्वियोतारो अमूराः ।विधातारो वि ते दधुरजस्रा ऋतधीतयो रुरुचंत दस्माः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ dhā́māni ǀ pūrvyā́ṇi ǀ árcān ǀ ví ǀ yát ǀ ucchā́n ǀ vi-yotā́raḥ ǀ ámūrāḥ ǀvi-dhātā́raḥ ǀ ví ǀ té ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ ájasrāḥ ǀ ṛtá-dhītayaḥ ǀ rurucanta ǀ dasmā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The (deities) who bestow ancient plural ces (of enjoyment on their worshippers), and (with minds) unperplexed, are the separators of light (from darkness); they, the eternal distributors (of rewards), grant (what is desired), and shine of plural asing aspect, the true (recompensers) of pious actṣ
verses.wilson_translation: The (deities) who bestow ancient plural ces (of enjoyment on their worshippers), and (with minds) unperplexed, are the separators of light (from darkness); they, the eternal distributors (of rewards), grant (what is desired), and shine of plural asing aspect, the true (recompensers) of pious actṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र पस्त्यामदितिं सिंधुमर्कैः स्वस्तिमीळे सख्याय देवीं ।उभे यथा नो अहनी निपात उषासानक्ता करतामदब्धे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ pastyā́m ǀ áditim ǀ síndhum ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ svastím ǀ īḷe ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ devī́m ǀubhé íti ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ áhanī íti ǀ ni-pā́taḥ ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ karatām ǀ ádabdhe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I adore the venerated Aditi, the Sindhuand the divine Svastifor their friendship; (I praise you) both, Day and Night, that you may protect us unimpeded; night and morning do (what we desire).
verses.wilson_translation: I adore the venerated Aditi, the Sindhuand the divine Svastifor their friendship; (I praise you) both, Day and Night, that you may protect us unimpeded; night and morning do (what we desire).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: व्यर्यमा वरुणश्चेति पंथामिषस्पतिः सुवितं गातुमग्निः ।इंद्राविष्णू नृवदु षु स्तवाना शर्म नो यंतममवद्वरूथं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ceti ǀ pánthām ǀ iṣáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ suvitám ǀ gātúm ǀ agníḥ ǀíndrāviṣṇū íti ǀ nṛ-vát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ stávānā ǀ śárma ǀ naḥ ǀ yantam ǀ áma-vat ǀ várūtham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aryamanand Varuṇainstrumental uct us in the path (of worship);Agni, the lord of food points out the way to happiness;Indraand Viṣṇu, being glorified, bestow upon us desirable prosperity comprehending descendants and strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Aryamanand Varuṇainstrumental uct us in the path (of worship);Agni, the lord of food points out the way to happiness;Indraand Viṣṇu, being glorified, bestow upon us desirable prosperity comprehending descendants and strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ पर्वतस्य मरुतामवांसि देवस्य त्रातुरव्रि भगस्य ।पात्पतिर्जन्यादंहसो नो मित्रो मित्रियादुत न उरुष्येत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ párvatasya ǀ marútām ǀ ávāṃsi ǀ devásya ǀ trātúḥ ǀ avri ǀ bhágasya ǀpā́t ǀ pátiḥ ǀ jányāt ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ mitríyāt ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ uruṣyet ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have recourse to the protection of Parvata, of the Maruts, and of the divine protector,Bhaga; may the lord (Varuṇa) preserve us from human wretchedness, and may Mitradefend us with a friendly regard.
verses.wilson_translation: I have recourse to the protection of Parvata, of the Maruts, and of the divine protector,Bhaga; may the lord (Varuṇa) preserve us from human wretchedness, and may Mitradefend us with a friendly regard.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू रोदसी अहिना बुध्न्येन स्तुवीत देवी अप्येभिरिष्टैः ।समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवो घर्मस्वरसो नद्यो अप व्रन् ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ rodasī íti ǀ áhinā ǀ budhnyéna ǀ stuvītá ǀ devī íti ǀ ápyebhiḥ ǀ iṣṭáiḥ ǀsamudrám ǀ ná ǀ sam-cáraṇe ǀ saniṣyávaḥ ǀ gharmá-svarasaḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ ápa ǀ vran ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Heaven and Earth, I praise you together with Ahirbudhnyafor those (good things that are) desired, as those desirous of acquiring (riches) praise the ocean on traversing it (in which) the sounding rivers disappear.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Heaven and Earth, I praise you together with Ahirbudhnyafor those (good things that are) desired, as those desirous of acquiring (riches) praise the ocean on traversing it (in which) the sounding rivers disappear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवैर्नो देव्यदितिर्नि पातु देवस्त्राता त्रायतामप्रयुच्छन् ।नहि मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धासिमर्हामसि प्रमियं सान्वग्नेः ॥
verses.transliteration: deváiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ní ǀ pātu ǀ deváḥ ǀ trātā́ ǀ trāyatām ǀ ápra-yucchan ǀnahí ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhāsím ǀ árhāmasi ǀ pra-míyam ǀ sā́nu ǀ agnéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine Aditi, with the gods, preserve us; may the ever-attentive protecting (deity,Indra), protect us; we are not able to withhold the elevated (sacrificial) food of Mitra, of Varuṇa, of Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Aditi, with the gods, preserve us; may the ever-attentive protecting (deity,Indra), protect us; we are not able to withhold the elevated (sacrificial) food of Mitra, of Varuṇa, of Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निरीशे वसव्यस्याग्निर्महः सौभगस्य ।तान्यस्मभ्यं रासते ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ īśe ǀ vasavyásya ǀ agníḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ sáubhagasya ǀtā́ni ǀ asmábhyam ǀ rāsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniis lord over treasure; Agni (is lord) over great good fortune; may he bestow them upon us.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis lord over treasure; Agni (is lord) over great good fortune; may he bestow them upon us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उषो मघोन्या वह सूनृते वार्या पुरु ।अस्मभ्यं वाजिनीवति ॥
verses.transliteration: úṣaḥ ǀ maghoni ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ sū́nṛte ǀ vā́ryā ǀ purú ǀasmábhyam ǀ vājinī-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Opulent, Uṣas, truth-speaking, food-abounding, bestow upon us many good things.
verses.wilson_translation: Opulent, Uṣas, truth-speaking, food-abounding, bestow upon us many good things.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तत्सु नः सविता भगो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।इंद्रो नो राधसा गमत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀíndraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ rā́dhasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gamat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Savitā,Bhaga,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman,Indra, come to us with the wealth (that each bestow).
verses.wilson_translation: May Savitā,Bhaga,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman,Indra, come to us with the wealth (that each bestow).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Heaven and Earth.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY mighty Heaven and Earth, most meet for honour, be present here with light and gleaming splendours;When, fixing them apart, vast, most extensive, the Steer roars loudly in far-reaching courses. The Goddesses with Gods, holy with holy, the Two stand pouring out their rain, exhaustless:Faithful and guileless, having Gods for children, leaders of sacrifice with shining splendours. Sure in the worlds he was a skilful Craftsman, he who produced these Twain the Earth and Heaven.Wise, with his power he brought both realms, together spacious and deep, well-fashioned, unsupported. O Heaven and Earth, with one accord promoting, with high protection as of Queens, our welfare,Far-reaching, universal, holy, guard us. May we, car-borne, through song be victors ever. To both of you, O Heaven and Earth, we bring our lofty song of praise,Pure Ones! to glorify you both. Ye sanctify each other's form, by your own proper might ye rule,And from of old observe the Law. Furthering and fulfilling, ye, O Mighty, perfect Mitra's Law.Ye sit around our sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: मही द्यावापृथिवी इह ज्येष्ठे रुचा भवतां शुचयद्भिरर्कैः ।यत्सीं वरिष्ठे बृहती विमिन्वन्रुवद्धोक्षा पप्रथानेभिरेवैः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ihá ǀ jyéṣṭhe íti ǀ rucā́ ǀ bhavatām ǀ śucáyat-bhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ váriṣṭhe íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ vi-minván ǀ ruvát ǀ ha ǀ ukṣā́ ǀ paprathānébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vast and most excellent Heaven and Earth, be present with splendour at this (sacrifice, attracted) by sanctifying hymns; since that the showerer sounds everywhere with (his) heralds, the rapid (winds), passing through the two spacious and mighty (regions).
verses.wilson_translation: Vast and most excellent Heaven and Earth, be present with splendour at this (sacrifice, attracted) by sanctifying hymns; since that the showerer sounds everywhere with (his) heralds, the rapid (winds), passing through the two spacious and mighty (regions).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवी देवेभिर्यजते यजत्रैरमिनती तस्थतुरुक्षमाणे ।ऋतावरी अद्रुहा देवपुत्रे यज्ञस्य नेत्री शुचयद्भिरर्कैः ॥
verses.transliteration: devī́ íti ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ yajaté íti ǀ yájatraiḥ ǀ áminatī íti ǀ tasthatuḥ ǀ ukṣámāṇe íti ǀṛtávarī ítyṛtá-varī ǀ adrúhā ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀ yajñásya ǀ netrī́ íti ǀ śucáyat-bhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine, adorable, benevolent, fertilizing, truthful, unoppressive Heaven and Earth, the leaders of sacrifice, whose sons are the gods, be present with the adorable gods, (attracted) by sanctifying hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine, adorable, benevolent, fertilizing, truthful, unoppressive Heaven and Earth, the leaders of sacrifice, whose sons are the gods, be present with the adorable gods, (attracted) by sanctifying hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स इत्स्वपा भुवनेष्वास य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जजान ।उर्वी गभीरे रजसी सुमेके अवंशे धीरः शच्या समैरत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ āsa ǀ yáḥ ǀ imé íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ jajā́na ǀurvī́ íti ǀ gabhīré íti ǀ rájasī íti ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀ avaṃśé ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ śácyā ǀ sám ǀ airat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Verily he was the doer of a good work in the regions, who genitive rated these two, Heaven and Earth, and firm of purpose, gave an impulse by his deed to the two vast immoveable, beautiful, unsupported worlds.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily he was the doer of a good work in the regions, who genitive rated these two, Heaven and Earth, and firm of purpose, gave an impulse by his deed to the two vast immoveable, beautiful, unsupported worlds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू रोदसी बृहद्भिर्नो वरूथैः पत्नीवद्भिरिषयंती सजोषाः ।उरूची विश्वे यजते नि पातं धिया स्याम रथ्यः सदासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ rodasī íti ǀ bṛhát-bhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ várūthaiḥ ǀ pátnīvat-bhiḥ ǀ iṣáyantī íti ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀurūcī́ íti ǀ víśve íti ǀ yajaté íti ǀ ní ǀ pātam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ sadā-sā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Heaven and Earth, vast, universal, adorable, united in satisfaction and disposed to give us food, protect us with our spacious dwelings, inhabited by our wives, and may we for our (pious) acts be possessed of chariots and slaves.
verses.wilson_translation: May Heaven and Earth, vast, universal, adorable, united in satisfaction and disposed to give us food, protect us with our spacious dwelings, inhabited by our wives, and may we for our (pious) acts be possessed of chariots and slaves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वां महि द्यवी अभ्युपस्तुतिं भरामहे ।शुची उप प्रशस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vām ǀ máhi ǀ dyávī íti ǀ abhí ǀ úpa-stutim ǀ bharāmahe ǀśúcī íti ǀ úpa ǀ prá-śastaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: We offer earnest praise you both resplendent (Heaven and Earth); we approach you who are pure to offer adoration.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer earnest praise you both resplendent (Heaven and Earth); we approach you who are pure to offer adoration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुनाने तन्वा मिथः स्वेन दक्षेण राजथः ।ऊह्याथे सनादृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: punāné íti ǀ tanvā́ ǀ mitháḥ ǀ svéna ǀ dákṣeṇa ǀ rājathaḥ ǀūhyā́the íti ǀ sanā́t ǀ ṛtám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mutually sanctifying (each other) of your own substance you shine by your own power, and ever beat away the offering.
verses.wilson_translation: Mutually sanctifying (each other) of your own substance you shine by your own power, and ever beat away the offering.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मही मित्रस्य साधथस्तरंती पिप्रती ऋतं ।परि यज्ञं नि षेदथुः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ íti ǀ mitrásya ǀ sādhathaḥ ǀ tárantī íti ǀ pípratī íti ǀ ṛtám ǀpári ǀ yajñám ǀ ní ǀ sedathuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty (Heaven and Earth), you fulfil the desires of your friend; distributing food and giving sustenance you have sat down at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty (Heaven and Earth), you fulfil the desires of your friend; distributing food and giving sustenance you have sat down at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVII. Ksetrapati, Etc.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WE through the Master of the Field, even as through a friend, obtainWhat nourisheth our kine and steeds. In such may he be good to us. As the cow yieldeth milk, pour for us freely, Lord of the Field, the wave that beareth sweetness,Distilling meath, well-purified like butter, and let the. Lords of holy Law be gracious. Sweet be the plants for us. the heavens, the waters, and full of sweets for us be air's mid-region.May the Field's Lord for us be full of sweetness, and may we follow after him uninjured. Happily work our steers and men, may the plough furrow happily.Happily be the traces bound; happily may he ply the goad. Śuna and Sīra, welcome ye this laud, and with the milk which ye have made in heavenBedew ye both this earth of ours. Auspicious Sītā, come thou near: we venerate and worship theeThat thou mayst bless and prosper us and bring us fruits abundantly. May Indra press the furrow down, may Pūṣan guide its course aright.May she, as rich in milk, be drained for us through each succeeding year. Happily let the shares turn up the plough-land, happily go the ploughers with the oxen.With meath and milk Parjanya make us happy. Grant us prosperity, Śuna and Sīra.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रस्य पतिना वयं हितेनेव जयामसि ।गामश्वं पोषयित्न्वा स नो मृळातीदृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣétrasya ǀ pátinā ǀ vayám ǀ hiténa-iva ǀ jayāmasi ǀgā́m ǀ áśvam ǀ poṣayitnú ǀ ā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mṛḷāti ǀ īdṛ́śe ǁ
verses.english_translation: With the master of the field, our friend, we triumph; may he bestow upon us cattle, horses, nourishment, for by such (gifts) he makes us happy.
verses.wilson_translation: With the master of the field, our friend, we triumph; may he bestow upon us cattle, horses, nourishment, for by such (gifts) he makes us happy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रस्य पते मधुमंतमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व ।मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣétrasya ǀ pate ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ūrmím ǀ dhenúḥ-iva ǀ páyaḥ ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhukṣva ǀmadhu-ścútam ǀ ghṛtám-iva ǀ sú-pūtam ǀ ṛtásya ǀ naḥ ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ mṛḷayantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the field, bestow upon us sweet abundant, (water), as the cow (yields her) milk, dropping like honey, blend as butter; may the lords of the water make us happy.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of the field, bestow upon us sweet abundant, (water), as the cow (yields her) milk, dropping like honey, blend as butter; may the lords of the water make us happy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)
