verses.sanskrit: मधुमतीरोषधीर्द्याव आपो मधुमन्नो भवत्वंतरिक्षं ।क्षेत्रस्य पतिर्मधुमान्नो अस्त्वरिष्यंतो अन्वेनं चरेम ॥
verses.transliteration: mádhu-matīḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ antárikṣam ǀkṣétrasya ǀ pátiḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ áriṣyantaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ enam ǀ carema ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the herbs (of the field) be sweet for us; may the heavens, the waters, the firmament, be kind to us; may the lord of the field be gracious to us; let us, undeterred (by foes), have recourse to him.
verses.wilson_translation: May the herbs (of the field) be sweet for us; may the heavens, the waters, the firmament, be kind to us; may the lord of the field be gracious to us; let us, undeterred (by foes), have recourse to him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं वाहाः शुनं नरः शुनं कृषतु लांगलं ।शुनं वरत्रा बध्यंतां शुनमष्ट्रामुदिंगय ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ vāhā́ḥ ǀ śunám ǀ náraḥ ǀ śunám ǀ kṛṣatu ǀ lā́ṅgalam ǀśunám ǀ varatrā́ḥ ǀ badhyantām ǀ śunám ǀ áṣṭrām ǀ út ǀ iṅgaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the oxen (draw) happily, the men (labour) happily; the plural ugh furrows happily; may the traces bind happily; wield the goad happily.
verses.wilson_translation: May the oxen (draw) happily, the men (labour) happily; the plural ugh furrows happily; may the traces bind happily; wield the goad happily.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनासीराविमां वाचं जुषेथां यद्दिवि चक्रथुः पयः ।तेनेमामुप सिंचतं ॥
verses.transliteration: śúnāsīrau ǀ imā́m ǀ vā́cam ǀ juṣethām ǀ yát ǀ diví ǀ cakráthuḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀténa ǀ imā́m ǀ úpa ǀ siñcatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Śunaand Sīrabe plural ased by this our praise, and consequently sprinkle this (earth) with the water which you have reated in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Śunaand Sīrabe plural ased by this our praise, and consequently sprinkle this (earth) with the water which you have reated in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वाची सुभगे भव सीते वंदामहे त्वा ।यथा नः सुभगाससि यथा नः सुफलाससि ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́cī ǀ su-bhage ǀ bhava ǀ sī́te ǀ vándāmahe ǀ tvā ǀyáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ ásasi ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ su-phálā ǀ ásasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious Sītā, be present, we glorify you; that you may be propitious to us, that you may yield us abundant fruit.
verses.wilson_translation: Auspicious Sītā, be present, we glorify you; that you may be propitious to us, that you may yield us abundant fruit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रः सीतां नि गृह्णातु तां पूषानु यच्छतु ।सा नः पयस्वती दुहामुत्तरामुत्तरां समां ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ sī́tām ǀ ní ǀ gṛhṇātu ǀ tā́m ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ ánu ǀ yacchatu ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ páyasvatī ǀ duhām ǀ úttarām-uttarām ǀ sámām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indratake hold of Sītā; may Pūṣanguide her; may she, well stored with water, yield it as milk, year after year.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indratake hold of Sītā; may Pūṣanguide her; may she, well stored with water, yield it as milk, year after year.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं नः फाला वि कृषंतु भूमिं शुनं कीनाशा अभि यंतु वाहैः ।शुनं पर्जन्यो मधुना पयोभिः शुनासीरा शुनमस्मासु धत्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ naḥ ǀ phā́lāḥ ǀ ví ǀ kṛṣantu ǀ bhū́mim ǀ śunám ǀ kīnā́śāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ yantu ǀ vāháiḥ ǀśunám ǀ parjányaḥ ǀ mádhunā ǀ páyaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ śúnāsīrā ǀ śunám ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhattam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the plural ugh shares break up our land happily; may the plural ughman go happily with the oxen; may Parjanya(water the earth) with sweet showers happily; grant,Śunaand Sīra, prosperity to us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the plural ugh shares break up our land happily; may the plural ughman go happily with the oxen; may Parjanya(water the earth) with sweet showers happily; grant,Śunaand Sīra, prosperity to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Ghṛta.
hymns.anukramani: ११ वामदेवो गौतमः। अग्निः, सूर्यो वाऽऽपो वा गावो वा घृतस्तुतिर्वा। त्रिष्टुप्, ११ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FORTH from the ocean sprang the wave of sweetness: together with the stalk it turned to Amṛta,That which is holy oil's mysterious title: but the Gods’ tongue is truly Amṛta's centre. Let us declare aloud the name of Ghṛta, and at this sacrifice hold it up with homage.So let the Brahman hear the praise we utter. This hath the four-horned Buffalo emitted. Four are his horns, three are the feet that bear him; his heads are two, his hands are seven in number.Bound with a triple bond the Steer roars loudly: the mighty God hath entered in to mortals. That oil in triple shape the Gods discovered laid down within the Cow, concealed by Paṇis.Indra produced one shape, Sūrya another: by their own power they formed the third from Vena. From inmost reservoir in countless channels flow down these rivers which the foe beholds not.I look upon the streams of oil descending, and lo! the Golden Reed is there among them. Like rivers our libations flow together, cleansing themselves in inmost heart and spirit.The streams of holy oil pour swiftly downward like the wild beasts that fly before the bowman. As rushing down the rapids of a river, flow swifter than the wind the vigorous currents,The streams of oil in swelling fluctuation like a red courser bursting through the fences. Like women at a gathering fair to look on and gently smiling, they incline to Agni.The streams of holy oil attain the fuel, and Jātavedas joyfully receives them. As maidens dock themselves with gay adornment to join the bridal feast, I now behold them.Where Soma flows and sacrifice is ready, thither the streams of holy oil are running. Send to our eulogy a herd of cattle bestow upon us excellent possessions.Bear to the Gods the sacrifice we offer the streams of oil flow pure and full of sweetness. The universe depends upon thy power and might within the sea, within the heart, within all life.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रादूर्मिर्मधुमाँ उदारदुपांशुना सममृतत्वमानट् ।घृतस्य नाम गुह्यं यदस्ति जिह्वा देवानाममृतस्य नाभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: samudrā́t ǀ ūrmíḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ út ǀ ārat ǀ úpa ǀ aṃśúnā ǀ sám ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaṭ ǀghṛtásya ǀ nā́ma ǀ gúhyam ǀ yát ǀ ásti ǀ jihvā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sweet water swells up from the firmament; by the (solar) ray (man) obtains immortality; that which is he secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods, the navel of ambrosia.
verses.wilson_translation: The sweet water swells up from the firmament; by the (solar) ray (man) obtains immortality; that which is he secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods, the navel of ambrosia.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वयं नाम प्र ब्रवामा घृतस्यास्मिन्यज्ञे धारयामा नमोभिः ।उप ब्रह्मा शृणवच्छस्यमानं चतुःशृंगोऽवमीद्गौर एतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ nā́ma ǀ prá ǀ bravāma ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ dhārayāma ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀúpa ǀ brahmā́ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ śasyámānam ǀ cátuḥ-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ avamīt ǀ gauráḥ ǀ etát ǁ
verses.english_translation: We celebrate the name Ghṛtaat this sacrifice, we offer it with adoration; may the four-horned Brahmālisten to its being glorified; the fair-complexioned-deity perfect this rite.
verses.wilson_translation: We celebrate the name Ghṛtaat this sacrifice, we offer it with adoration; may the four-horned Brahmālisten to its being glorified; the fair-complexioned-deity perfect this rite.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारि शृंगा त्रयो अस्य पादा द्वे शीर्षे सप्त हस्तासो अस्य ।त्रिधा बद्धो वृषभो रोरवीति महो देवो मर्त्याँ आ विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: catvā́ri ǀ śṛ́ṅgā ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ asya ǀ pā́dāḥ ǀ dvé íti ǀ śīrṣé íti ǀ saptá ǀ hástāsaḥ ǀ asya ǀtrídhā ǀ baddháḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ roravīti ǀ maháḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ mártyān ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Four are his horns; three are his feet; his heads are two, hishandsare seven; the triple-bound showerer (of benefits) roars aloud; the mighty deity has entered among men.
verses.wilson_translation: Four are his horns; three are his feet; his heads are two, hishandsare seven; the triple-bound showerer (of benefits) roars aloud; the mighty deity has entered among men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिधा हितं पणिभिर्गुह्यमानं गवि देवासो घृतमन्वविंदन् ।इंद्र एकं सूर्य एकं जजान वेनादेकं स्वधया निष्टतक्षुः ॥
verses.transliteration: trídhā ǀ hitám ǀ paṇí-bhiḥ ǀ guhyámānam ǀ gávi ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ánu ǀ avindan ǀíndraḥ ǀ ékam ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ékam ǀ jajāna ǀ venā́t ǀ ékam ǀ svadháyā ǀ níḥ ǀ tatakṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gods discovered the Ghī concealed by the Paṇis, plural ced three-fold in the cow;Indragenitive rated one (portion),Sūryaanother, the (other gods) fabricated one from the resplendent (Agni), for the sake of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods discovered the Ghī concealed by the Paṇis, plural ced three-fold in the cow;Indragenitive rated one (portion),Sūryaanother, the (other gods) fabricated one from the resplendent (Agni), for the sake of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एता अर्षंति हृद्यात्समुद्राच्छतव्रजा रिपुणा नावचक्षे ।घृतस्य धारा अभि चाकशीमि हिरण्ययो वेतसो मध्य आसां ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ḥ ǀ arṣanti ǀ hṛ́dyāt ǀ samudrā́t ǀ śatá-vrajāḥ ǀ ripúṇā ǀ ná ǀ ava-cákṣe ǀghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cākaśīmi ǀ hiraṇyáyaḥ ǀ vetasáḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ āsām ǁ
verses.english_translation: These hundred-channeled showers fall from the heart-delighting firmament, unobserved by the hostile (cloud); I look upon these showers of Ghī, (and behold) the golden Vetasain the midst of them.
verses.wilson_translation: These hundred-channeled showers fall from the heart-delighting firmament, unobserved by the hostile (cloud); I look upon these showers of Ghī, (and behold) the golden Vetasain the midst of them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सम्यक्स्रवंति सरितो न धेना अंतर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः ।एते अर्षंत्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: samyák ǀ sravanti ǀ sarítaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhénāḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ pūyámānāḥ ǀeté ǀ arṣanti ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ mṛgā́ḥ-iva ǀ kṣipaṇóḥ ǀ ī́ṣamāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They flow uninterruptedly like plural asing rivers, purified by the mind that is seated in the heart; these streams of Ghī descend (upon the fire), like deer flying from the hunter.
verses.wilson_translation: They flow uninterruptedly like plural asing rivers, purified by the mind that is seated in the heart; these streams of Ghī descend (upon the fire), like deer flying from the hunter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सिंधोरिव प्राध्वने शूघनासो वातप्रमियः पतयंति यह्वाः ।घृतस्य धारा अरुषो न वाजी काष्ठा भिंदन्नूर्मिभिः पिन्वमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: síndhoḥ-iva ǀ pra-adhvané ǀ śūghanā́saḥ ǀ vā́ta-pramiyaḥ ǀ patayanti ǀ yahvā́ḥ ǀghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ ná ǀ vājī́ ǀ kā́ṣṭhāḥ ǀ bhindán ǀ ūrmíbhiḥ ǀ pínvamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The stream of Ghī fall copious, swift as the wind, and rapid as the waters of a river down a declivity, breaking through the confining banks, and hurrying on with their waves, like a high-spirited steed.
verses.wilson_translation: The stream of Ghī fall copious, swift as the wind, and rapid as the waters of a river down a declivity, breaking through the confining banks, and hurrying on with their waves, like a high-spirited steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि प्रवंत समनेव योषाः कल्याण्यः स्मयमानासो अग्निं ।घृतस्य धाराः समिधो नसंत ता जुषाणो हर्यति जातवेदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ pravanta ǀ sámanā-iva ǀ yóṣāḥ ǀ kalyāṇyáḥ ǀ smáyamānāsaḥ ǀ agním ǀghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ sam-ídhaḥ ǀ nasanta ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ juṣāṇáḥ ǀ haryati ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The streams of Ghī incline to Agnias devoted wives, auspicious and smiling, to a husband; they feed (the flame) like fuel, and Jātavedas, propitiated, accepts them.
verses.wilson_translation: The streams of Ghī incline to Agnias devoted wives, auspicious and smiling, to a husband; they feed (the flame) like fuel, and Jātavedas, propitiated, accepts them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कन्या इव वहतुमेतवा उ अंज्यंजाना अभि चाकशीमि ।यत्र सोमः सूयते यत्र यज्ञो घृतस्य धारा अभि तत्पवंते ॥
verses.transliteration: kanyā́ḥ-iva ǀ vahatúm ǀ étavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ añjí ǀ añjānā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cākaśīmi ǀyátra ǀ sómaḥ ǀ sūyáte ǀ yátra ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ tát ǀ pavante ǁ
verses.english_translation: I contemplate these streams of Ghī as they flow from where the Somais effused, where the sacrifice (is solemnized), as maidens decorating themselves with unguents to go to the bridegroom.
verses.wilson_translation: I contemplate these streams of Ghī as they flow from where the Somais effused, where the sacrifice (is solemnized), as maidens decorating themselves with unguents to go to the bridegroom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यर्षत सुष्टुतिं गव्यमाजिमस्मासु भद्रा द्रविणानि धत्त ।इमं यज्ञं नयत देवता नो घृतस्य धारा मधुमत्पवंते ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ arṣata ǀ su-stutím ǀ gávyam ǀ ājím ǀ asmā́su ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ dráviṇāni ǀ dhatta ǀimám ǀ yajñám ǀ nayata ǀ devátā ǀ naḥ ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ pavante ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Priests) address the pious praise, (the source) of herds of cattle; bestow upon us auspicious riches; convey this our sacrifice to the gods, (where at) the streams of Ghī with sweetness descend.
verses.wilson_translation: (Priests) address the pious praise, (the source) of herds of cattle; bestow upon us auspicious riches; convey this our sacrifice to the gods, (where at) the streams of Ghī with sweetness descend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धामंते विश्वं भुवनमधि श्रितमंतः समुद्रे हृद्यंतरायुषि ।अपामनीके समिथे य आभृतस्तमश्याम मधुमंतं त ऊर्मिं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhā́man ǀ te ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ ádhi ǀ śritám ǀ antáríti ǀ samudré ǀ hṛdí ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́yuṣi ǀapā́m ǀ ánīke ǀ sam-ithé ǀ yáḥ ǀ ā́-bhṛtaḥ ǀ tám ǀ aśyāma ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ te ǀ ūrmím ǁ
verses.english_translation: The whole world, (Agni), finds an asylum in your effulgence, whether it be in the ocean, in the heart (of man), in the life (of living beings), in the assemblage of the waters, or in warfare; may we attain the sweet-flavoured wave which is established in your (essence).
verses.wilson_translation: The whole world, (Agni), finds an asylum in your effulgence, whether it be in the ocean, in the heart (of man), in the life (of living beings), in the assemblage of the waters, or in warfare; may we attain the sweet-flavoured wave which is established in your (essence).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN I. Agni
hymns.anukramani: १२ बुधगविष्ठिरावात्रेयौ। अग्निः। त्रिष्टुप्।अबो॑ध्य॒ग्निः स॒मिधा॒ जना॑नां॒ प्रति॑ धे॒नुमि॑वाय॒तीमु॒षास॑म् । य॒ह्वा इ॑व॒ प्र व॒यामु॒ज्जिहा॑ना॒: प्र भा॒नव॑: सिस्रते॒ नाक॒मच्छ॑ ॥१॥अबो॑धि॒ होता॑ य॒जथा॑य दे॒वानू॒र्ध्वो अ॒ग्निः सु॒मना॑: प्रा॒तर॑स्थात् । समि॑द्धस्य॒ रुश॑ददर्शि॒ पाजो॑ म॒हान् दे॒वस्तम॑सो॒ निर॑मोचि ॥२॥यदीं॑ ग॒णस्य॑ रश॒नामजी॑ग॒: शुचि॑रङ्क्ते॒ शुचि॑भि॒र्गोभि॑र॒ग्निः । आद् दक्षि॑णा युज्यते वाज॒यन्त्यु॑त्ता॒नामू॒र्ध्वो अ॑धयज्जु॒हूभि॑: ॥३॥अ॒ग्निमच्छा॑ देवय॒तां मनां॑सि॒ चक्षूं॑षीव॒ सूर्ये॒ सं च॑रन्ति । यदीं॒ सुवा॑ते उ॒षसा॒ विरू॑पे श्वे॒तो वा॒जी जा॑यते॒ अग्रे॒ अह्ना॑म् ॥४॥जनि॑ष्ट॒ हि जेन्यो॒ अग्रे॒ अह्नां॑ हि॒तो हि॒तेष्व॑रु॒षो वने॑षु । दमे॑दमे स॒प्त रत्ना॒ दधा॑नो॒ऽग्निर्होता॒ नि ष॑सादा॒ यजी॑यान् ॥५॥अ॒ग्निर्होता॒ न्य॑सीद॒द् यजी॑यानु॒पस्थे॑ मा॒तुः सु॑र॒भा उ॑ लो॒के । युवा॑ क॒विः पु॑रुनि॒ष्ठ ऋ॒तावा॑ ध॒र्ता कृ॑ष्टी॒नामु॒त मध्य॑ इ॒द्धः ॥६॥प्र णु त्यं विप्र॑मध्व॒रेषु॑ सा॒धुम॒ग्निं होता॑रमीळते॒ नमो॑भिः । आ यस्त॒तान॒ रोद॑सी ऋ॒तेन॒ नित्यं॑ मृजन्ति वा॒जिनं॑ घृ॒तेन॑ ॥७॥मा॒र्जा॒ल्यो॑ मृज्यते॒ स्वे दमू॑नाः कविप्रश॒स्तो अति॑थिः शि॒वो न॑: । स॒हस्र॑शृङ्गो वृष॒भस्तदो॑जा॒ विश्वाँ॑ अग्ने॒ सह॑सा॒ प्रास्य॒न्यान् ॥८॥प्र स॒द्यो अ॑ग्ने॒ अत्ये॑ष्य॒न्याना॒विर्यस्मै॒ चारु॑तमो ब॒भूथ॑ । ई॒ळेन्यो॑ वपु॒ष्यो॑ वि॒भावा॑ प्रि॒यो वि॒शामति॑थि॒र्मानु॑षीणाम् ॥९॥तुभ्यं॑ भरन्ति क्षि॒तयो॑ यविष्ठ ब॒लिम॑ग्ने॒ अन्ति॑त॒ ओत दू॒रात् । आ भन्दि॑ष्ठस्य सुम॒तिं चि॑किद्धि बृ॒हत् ते॑ अग्ने॒ महि॒ शर्म॑ भ॒द्रम् ॥१०॥आद्य रथं॑ भानुमो भानु॒मन्त॒मग्ने॒ तिष्ठ॑ यज॒तेभि॒: सम॑न्तम् । वि॒द्वान् प॑थी॒नामु॒र्व१न्तरि॑क्ष॒मेह दे॒वान् ह॑वि॒रद्या॑य वक्षि ॥११॥अवो॑चाम क॒वये॒ मेध्या॑य॒ वचो॑ व॒न्दारु॑ वृष॒भाय॒ वृष्णे॑ । गवि॑ष्ठिरो॒ नम॑सा॒ स्तोम॑म॒ग्नौ दि॒वी॑व रु॒क्ममु॑रु॒व्यञ्च॑मश्रेत् ॥१२॥
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Agni is wakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow.Like young trees shooting up on high their branches, his flames are rising to the vault of heaven. For worship of the Gods the Priest was wakened: at morning gracious Agni hath arisen.Kindled, his radiant might is made apparent, and the great Deity set free from darkness. When he hath stirred the line of his attendants, with the pure milk pure Agni is anointed.The strength-bestowing gift is then made ready, which spread in front, with tongues, erect, he drinketh. The spirits of the pious turn together to Agni, as the eyes of all to Sūrya.He, when both Dawns of different hues have borne him, springs up at daybreak as a strong white charger. The noble One was born at days' beginning, laid red in colour mid the well-laid fuel.Yielding in every house his seven rich treasures, Agni is seated, Priest most skilled in worship. Agni hath sat him down, a Priest most skilful, on a sweet-smelling place, his Mother's bosom.Young, faithful, sage, preeminent o’er many, kindled among the folk whom he sustaineth. This Singer excellent at sacrifices, Agni the Priest, they glorify with homage.Him who spread out both worlds by Law Eternal they balm with oil, strong Steed who never faileth.. He, worshipful House-Friend, in his home is worshipped, our own auspicious guest, lauded by sages.That strength the Bull with thousand horns possesses. In might, O Agni, thou excellest others. Thou quickly passest by all others, Agni, for him to whom thou hast appeared most lovely,Wondrously fair, adorable, effulgent, the guest of men, the darling of the people. To thee, Most Youthful God! to thee, O Agni from near and far the people bring their tribute.Mark well the prayer of him who best extols thee. Great, high, auspicious, Agni, is thy shelter. Ascend to-day thy splendid car, O Agni, in splendour, with the Holy Ones around it.Knowing the paths by mid-air's spacious region bring hither Gods to feast on our oblation. To him adorable, sage, strong and mighty we have sung forth our song of praise and homage.Gavisthira hath raised with prayer to Agni this laud far-reaching, like gold light to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: अबोध्यग्निः समिधा जनानां प्रति धेनुमिवायतीमुषासं ।यह्वा इव प्र वयामुज्जिहानाः प्र भानवः सिस्रते नाकमच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: ábodhi ǀ agníḥ ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ jánānām ǀ práti ǀ dhenúm-iva ǀ ā-yatī́m ǀ uṣásam ǀyahvā́ḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ vayā́m ǀ ut-jíhānāḥ ǀ prá ǀ bhānávaḥ ǀ sisrate ǀ nā́kam ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniis awakened by the fuel (supplied) by the priests at the dawn, approaching like a cow (to pasture); his flames rise up to the sky like stately (trees) throwing aloft their branches.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis awakened by the fuel (supplied) by the priests at the dawn, approaching like a cow (to pasture); his flames rise up to the sky like stately (trees) throwing aloft their branches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अबोधि होता यजथाय देवानूर्ध्वो अग्निः सुमनाः प्रातरस्थात् ।समिद्धस्य रुशददर्शि पाजो महांदेवस्तमसो निरमोचि ॥
verses.transliteration: ábodhi ǀ hótā ǀ yajáthāya ǀ devā́n ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ prātáḥ ǀ asthāt ǀsám-iddhasya ǀ rúśat ǀ adarśi ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ deváḥ ǀ támasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ amoci ǁ
verses.english_translation: The offer of the oblation is awakened for the worship of the gods; favourably minded,Agnihas rise up with the dawn; the radiant vigour of the kindled (fire) is manifested; the great deity has been liberated from the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The offer of the oblation is awakened for the worship of the gods; favourably minded,Agnihas rise up with the dawn; the radiant vigour of the kindled (fire) is manifested; the great deity has been liberated from the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदीं गणस्य रशनामजीगः शुचिरंक्ते शुचिभिर्गोभिरग्निः ।आद्दक्षिणा युज्यते वाजयंत्युत्तानामूर्ध्वो अधयज्जुहूभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ īm ǀ gaṇásya ǀ raśanā́m ǀ ájīgaríti ǀ śúciḥ ǀ aṅkte ǀ śúci-bhiḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀā́t ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ yujyate ǀ vāja-yántī ǀ uttānā́m ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ adhayat ǀ juhū́bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Agnihas seized upon the (confining) girdle of the aggregated (world), then, bright-shining, he makes all manifest with brilliant rays; thereupon the precious food-desiring (oblations) is added (to the flame), and Agni, soaring aloft, drinks it as it is (spread out) recumbent by the ladles.
verses.wilson_translation: When Agnihas seized upon the (confining) girdle of the aggregated (world), then, bright-shining, he makes all manifest with brilliant rays; thereupon the precious food-desiring (oblations) is added (to the flame), and Agni, soaring aloft, drinks it as it is (spread out) recumbent by the ladles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निमच्छा देवयतां मनांसि चक्षूंषीव सूर्ये सं चरंति ।यदीं सुवाते उषसा विरूपे श्वेतो वाजी जायते अग्रे अह्नां ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ áccha ǀ deva-yatā́m ǀ mánāṃsi ǀ cákṣūṃṣi-iva ǀ sū́rye ǀ sám ǀ caranti ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ súvāte íti ǀ uṣásā ǀ vírūpe íti ví-rūpe ǀ śvetáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ jāyate ǀ ágre ǀ áhnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: The minds of the devout turn to Agni, as the eyes (of men) look towards the sun; when the multiform (heaven and earth) bring him forth along with the dawn, he is born as a white courser in the beginning of the days.
verses.wilson_translation: The minds of the devout turn to Agni, as the eyes (of men) look towards the sun; when the multiform (heaven and earth) bring him forth along with the dawn, he is born as a white courser in the beginning of the days.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जनिष्ट हि जेन्यो अग्रे अह्नां हितो हितेष्वरुषो वनेषु ।दमेदमे सप्त रत्ना दधानोऽग्निर्होता नि षसादा यजीयान् ॥
verses.transliteration: jániṣṭa ǀ hí ǀ jényaḥ ǀ ágre ǀ áhnām ǀ hitáḥ ǀ hitéṣu ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ váneṣu ǀdáme-dame ǀ saptá ǀ rátnā ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ sasāda ǀ yájīyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Agni), capable of birth, is born in the beginning of the days; radiant, he is deposited in the friendly woods, and then the adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation, displaying seven precious (rays), is seated in every house.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agni), capable of birth, is born in the beginning of the days; radiant, he is deposited in the friendly woods, and then the adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation, displaying seven precious (rays), is seated in every house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्होता न्यसीदद्यजीयानुपस्थे मातुः सुरभा उ लोके ।युवा कविः पुरुनिष्ठ ऋतावा धर्ता कृष्टीनामुत मध्य इद्धः ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ asīdat ǀ yájīyān ǀ upá-sthe ǀ mātúḥ ǀ surabháu ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ loké ǀyúvā ǀ kavíḥ ǀ puruniḥ-stháḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ dhartā́ ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ utá ǀ mádhye ǀ iddháḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation, has sat down in a fragrant plural ce on the top of his mother (earth); youthful, wise, many-stationed, the celebrator of sacrifice, the sustainer (of all), kindled (he abides) among men.
verses.wilson_translation: The adorable Agni, the offerer of the oblation, has sat down in a fragrant plural ce on the top of his mother (earth); youthful, wise, many-stationed, the celebrator of sacrifice, the sustainer (of all), kindled (he abides) among men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र णु त्यं विप्रमध्वरेषु साधुमग्निं होतारमीळते नमोभिः ।आ यस्ततान रोदसी ऋतेन नित्यं मृजंति वाजिनं घृतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ tyám ǀ vípram ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ sādhúm ǀ agním ǀ hótāram ǀ īḷate ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ tatā́na ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ṛténa ǀ nítyam ǀ mṛjanti ǀ vājínam ǀ ghṛténa ǁ
verses.english_translation: They glorify at present withhymns that Agniwho is intelligent, the fulfiller (of desires) at sacrifices, the offer of oblations, who has charged heaven and earth with water, and whom they always worship with clarified butter as the bestower of food.
verses.wilson_translation: They glorify at present withhymns that Agniwho is intelligent, the fulfiller (of desires) at sacrifices, the offer of oblations, who has charged heaven and earth with water, and whom they always worship with clarified butter as the bestower of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मार्जाल्यो मृज्यते स्वे दमूनाः कविप्रशस्तो अतिथिः शिवो नः ।सहस्रशृंगो वृषभस्तदोजा विश्वाँ अग्ने सहसा प्रास्यन्यान् ॥
verses.transliteration: mārjālyáḥ ǀ mṛjyate ǀ své ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ kavi-praśastáḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀsahásra-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ tát-ojāḥ ǀ víśvān ǀ agne ǀ sáhasā ǀ prá ǀ asi ǀ anyā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Entitled to worship, he is worshipped in his own (abode); humble-minded, eminent among sages, our auspicious guest, the thousand-rayed, the showerer (of benefits), of well-known might, you,Agni, surpass all others in strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Entitled to worship, he is worshipped in his own (abode); humble-minded, eminent among sages, our auspicious guest, the thousand-rayed, the showerer (of benefits), of well-known might, you,Agni, surpass all others in strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सद्यो ��ग्ने अत्येष्यन्यानाविर्यस्मै चारुतमो बभूथ ।ईळेन्यो वपुष्यो विभावा प्रियो विशामतिथिर्मानुषीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ agne ǀ áti ǀ eṣi ǀ anyā́n ǀ āvíḥ ǀ yásmai ǀ cā́ru-tamaḥ ǀ babhū́tha ǀīḷényaḥ ǀ vapuṣyáḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ priyáḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ átithiḥ ǀ mā́nuṣīṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Too) quickly,Agni, do you pass to others from him to whom you have been manifest; most beautiful, adorable, radiant, many-shining, the loved of people, the guest of men.
verses.wilson_translation: (Too) quickly,Agni, do you pass to others from him to whom you have been manifest; most beautiful, adorable, radiant, many-shining, the loved of people, the guest of men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं भरंति क्षितयो यविष्ठ बलिमग्ने अंतित ओत दूरात् ।आ भंदिष्ठस्य सुमतिं चिकिद्धि बृहत्ते अग्ने महि शर्म भद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ bharanti ǀ kṣitáyaḥ ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ balím ǀ agne ǀ ántitaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ utá ǀ dūrā́t ǀā́ ǀ bhándiṣṭhasya ǀ su-matím ǀ cikiddhi ǀ bṛhát ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ bhadrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you, young (of the gods), men present oblations, whether nigh or from far; accept the praise of him who most extols you; for the felicity (which you confer).Agniis great, vast, auspicious.
verses.wilson_translation: To you, young (of the gods), men present oblations, whether nigh or from far; accept the praise of him who most extols you; for the felicity (which you confer).Agniis great, vast, auspicious.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आद्य रथं भानुमो भानुमंतमग्ने तिष्ठ यजतेभिः समंतं ।विद्वान्पथीनामुर्वंतरिक्षमेह देवान्हविरद्याय वक्षि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ adyá ǀ rátham ǀ bhānu-maḥ ǀ bhānu-mántam ǀ ágne ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ yajatébhiḥ ǀ sám-antam ǀvidvā́n ǀ pathīnā́m ǀ urú ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ devā́n ǀ haviḥ-ádyāya ǀ vakṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ascend today, radiant Agni, your resplendent, well-conducted chariot, together with the adorable (gods), cognizant of the ways (of worship), bring hither, by the vast firmament, the gods to partake of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend today, radiant Agni, your resplendent, well-conducted chariot, together with the adorable (gods), cognizant of the ways (of worship), bring hither, by the vast firmament, the gods to partake of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवोचाम कवये मेध्याय वचो वंदारु वृषभाय वृष्णे ।गविष्ठिरो नमसा स्तोममग्नौ दिवीव रुक्ममुरुव्यंचमश्रेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ávocāma ǀ kaváye ǀ médhyāya ǀ vácaḥ ǀ vandā́ru ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀgáviṣṭhiraḥ ǀ námasā ǀ stómam ǀ agnáu ǀ diví-iva ǀ rukmám ǀ uru-vyáñcam ǀ aśret ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have uttered aloud this encomiastic praise to the wise, holy, vigorous (Agni), the showerer (of benefits);Gaviṣṭhiraoffers with reverence (this) praise to Agni like the wide-sojourning (sun), effulgent in the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: We have uttered aloud this encomiastic praise to the wise, holy, vigorous (Agni), the showerer (of benefits);Gaviṣṭhiraoffers with reverence (this) praise to Agni like the wide-sojourning (sun), effulgent in the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN II. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १२ कुमार आत्रेयः, वृशो वा जानः, उभौ वा, २, ९ वृशो जानः। अग्निः। त्रिष्टुप्, १२ शक्वरी।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE youthful Mother keeps the Boy in secret pressed to her close, nor yields him to the Father.But, when he lies upon the arm, the people see his unfading countenance before them. What child is this thou carriest as handmaid, O Youthful One? The Consort-Queen hath borne him.The Babe unborn increased through many autumns. I saw him born what time his Mother bare him. I saw him from afar gold-toothed, bright-coloured, hurling his weapons from his habitation,What time I gave him Amṛta free from mixture. How can the Indraless, the hymnless harm me? I saw him moving from the place he dwells in, even as with a herd, brilliantly shining.These seized him not: he had been born already. They who were grey with age again grow youthful. Who separate my young bull from the cattle, they whose protector was in truth no stranger?Let those whose hands have seized upon them free them. May he, observant, drive the herd to us-ward. Mid mortal men godless have secreted the King of all who live, home of the people.So may the prayers of Atri give him freedom. Reproached in turn be those who now reproach him. Thou from the stake didst loose e’en Śunaḥśepa bound for a thousand; for he prayed with fervour.So, Agni, loose from us the bonds that bind us, when thou art seated here, O Priest who knowest. Thou hast sped from me, Agni, in thine anger: this the protector of Gods’ Laws hath told me.Indra who knoweth bent his eye upon thee: by him instructed am I come, O Agni. Agni shines far and wide with lofty splendour, and by his greatness makes all things apparent.He conquers godless and malign enchantments, and sharpens both his horns to gore the Rakṣas. Loud in the heaven above be Agni's roarings with keen-edged weapons to destroy the demons.Forth burst his splendours in the Soma's rapture. The godless bands press round but cannot stay him. As a skilled craftsman makes a car, a singer I, Mighty One! this hymn for thee have fashioned.If thou, O Agni, God, accept it gladly, may we obtain thereby the heavenly Waters. May he, the strong-necked Steer, waxing in vigour, gather the foeman's wealth with none to check him.Thus to this Agni have the Immortals spoken. To man who spreads the grass may he grant shelter, grant shelter to the man who brings oblation.

verses.sanskrit: कुमारं माता युवतिः समुब्धं गुहा बिभर्ति न ददाति पित्रे ।अनीकमस्य न मिनज्जनासः पुरः पश्यंति निहितमरतौ ॥
verses.transliteration: kumārám ǀ mātā́ ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ sám-ubdham ǀ gúhā ǀ bibharti ǀ ná ǀ dadāti ǀ pitré ǀánīkam ǀ asya ǀ ná ǀ minát ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ paśyanti ǀ ní-hitam ǀ aratáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The young mother cherishes her mutilated boy in secret, and gives him not up to the father; men behold not his mutilated form, but (see him) when plural ced before (them) in an unresting (position).
verses.wilson_translation: The young mother cherishes her mutilated boy in secret, and gives him not up to the father; men behold not his mutilated form, but (see him) when plural ced before (them) in an unresting (position).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कमेतं त्वं युवते कुमारं पेषी बिभर्षि महिषी जजान ।पूर्वीर्हि गर्भः शरदो ववर्धापश्यं जातं यदसूत माता ॥
verses.transliteration: kám ǀ etám ǀ tvám ǀ yuvate ǀ kumārám ǀ péṣī ǀ bibharṣi ǀ máhiṣī ǀ jajāna ǀpūrvī́ḥ ǀ hí ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ vavárdha ǀ ápaśyam ǀ jātám ǀ yát ǀ ásūta ǀ mātā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Young mother, what boy is this whom you, (become) a malevolent spirit, foster? The mighty (queen) has given him birth; the embryo has thrived through many years; I have seen him born as the mother brought him forth.
verses.wilson_translation: Young mother, what boy is this whom you, (become) a malevolent spirit, foster? The mighty (queen) has given him birth; the embryo has thrived through many years; I have seen him born as the mother brought him forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यदंतं शुचिवर्णमारात्क्षेत्रादपश्यमायुधा मिमानं ।ददानो अस्मा अमृतं विपृक्वत्किं मामनिंद्राः कृणवन्ननुक्थाः ॥
verses.transliteration: híraṇya-dantam ǀ śúci-varṇam ǀ ārā́t ǀ kṣétrāt ǀ apaśyam ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ mímānam ǀdadānáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ vipṛ́kvat ǀ kím ǀ mā́m ǀ anindrā́ḥ ǀ kṛṇavan ǀ anukthā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have seen him from a near plural ce, golden-toothed, bright-coloured, wielding (flames like) weapons, (when) offering to him the ambrosial, all-diffusing (oblation); what can those who acknowledge not Indra, who repeat not his praise, do unto me.
verses.wilson_translation: I have seen him from a near plural ce, golden-toothed, bright-coloured, wielding (flames like) weapons, (when) offering to him the ambrosial, all-diffusing (oblation); what can those who acknowledge not Indra, who repeat not his praise, do unto me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रादपश्यं सनुतश्चरंतं सुमद्यूथं न पुरु शोभमानं ।न ता अगृभ्रन्नजनिष्ट हि षः पलिक्नीरिद्युवतयो भवंति ॥
verses.transliteration: kṣétrāt ǀ apaśyam ǀ sanutáríti ǀ cárantam ǀ su-mát ǀ yūthám ǀ ná ǀ purú ǀ śóbhamānam ǀná ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ agṛbhran ǀ ájaniṣṭa ǀ hí ǀ sáḥ ǀ páliknīḥ ǀ ít ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ bhavanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have seen him passing secretly from plural ce (to plural ce) like a herd (of cattle), shining brightly of his own accord; they apprehended not those (flames of his), but he has (again) been born, and they who had become grey-haired are (once more) young.
verses.wilson_translation: I have seen him passing secretly from plural ce (to plural ce) like a herd (of cattle), shining brightly of his own accord; they apprehended not those (flames of his), but he has (again) been born, and they who had become grey-haired are (once more) young.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: के मे मर्यकं वि यवंत गोभिर्न येषां गोपा अरणश्चिदास ।य ईं जगृभुरव ते सृजंत्वाजाति पश्व उप नश्चिकित्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ké ǀ me ǀ maryakám ǀ ví ǀ yavanta ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ yéṣām ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ áraṇaḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́sa ǀyé ǀ īm ǀ jagṛbhúḥ ǀ áva ǀ té ǀ sṛjantú ǀ ā́ ǀ ajāti ǀ paśváḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who have disunited my people from the cattle? was there not for them an invincible protector? may they who have seized upon that (people) perish, for he who knows (our wishes) approaches to (protect) the cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Who have disunited my people from the cattle? was there not for them an invincible protector? may they who have seized upon that (people) perish, for he who knows (our wishes) approaches to (protect) the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वसां राजानं वसतिं जनानामरातयो नि दधुर्मर्त्येषु ।ब्रह्माण्यत्रेरव तं सृजंतु निंदितारो निंद्यासो भवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: vasā́m ǀ rā́jānam ǀ vasatím ǀ jánānām ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ ní ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ mártyeṣu ǀbráhmāṇi ǀ átreḥ ǀ áva ǀ tám ǀ sṛjantu ǀ ninditā́raḥ ǀ níndyāsaḥ ǀ bhavantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Enemies have secreted amongmortals, the king of living beings, the asylum of men; may the prayers of Atriset him free; may those who revile be reviled.
verses.wilson_translation: Enemies have secreted amongmortals, the king of living beings, the asylum of men; may the prayers of Atriset him free; may those who revile be reviled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्राद्यूपादमुंचो अशमिष्ट हि षः ।एवास्मदग्ने वि मुमुग्धि पाशान्होतश्चिकित्व इह तू निषद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: śúnaḥ-śépam ǀ cit ǀ ní-ditam ǀ sahásrāt ǀ yū́pāt ǀ amuñcaḥ ǀ áśamiṣṭa ǀ hí ǀ sáḥ ǀevá ǀ asmát ǀ agne ǀ ví ǀ mumugdhi ǀ pā́śān ǀ hótaríti ǀ cikitvaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ tú ǀ ni-sádya ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have liberated the fettered Śunahśepa from a thousand stakes, for he was patient in endurance; so Agni, free us from our bonds, having sat down here (at our sacrifice), intelligent offerer of oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: You have liberated the fettered Śunahśepa from a thousand stakes, for he was patient in endurance; so Agni, free us from our bonds, having sat down here (at our sacrifice), intelligent offerer of oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हृणीयमानो अप हि मदैयेः प्र मे देवानां व्रतपा उवाच ।इंद्रो विद्वाँ अनु हि त्वा चचक्ष तेनाहमग्ने अनुशिष्ट आगां ॥
verses.transliteration: hṛṇīyámānaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ hí ǀ mát ǀ áiyeḥ ǀ prá ǀ me ǀ devā́nām ǀ vrata-pā́ḥ ǀ uvāca ǀíndraḥ ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ánu ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ cacákṣa ǀ téna ǀ ahám ǀ agne ǀ ánu-śiṣṭaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agām ǁ
verses.english_translation: When angered, (Agni), depart from me; the protector of the worship of the gods, (Indra), has spoken to me; the wise Indra has looked upon you, and instrumental ucted by him, I have come, Agni, to you.
verses.wilson_translation: When angered, (Agni), depart from me; the protector of the worship of the gods, (Indra), has spoken to me; the wise Indra has looked upon you, and instrumental ucted by him, I have come, Agni, to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि ज्योतिषा बृहता भात्यग्निराविर्विश्वानि कृणुते महित्वा ।प्रादेवीर्मायाः सहते दुरेवाः शिशीते शृंगे रक्षसे विनिक्षे ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ bhāti ǀ agníḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ kṛṇute ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀprá ǀ ádevīḥ ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ sahate ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǀ śíśīte ǀ śṛ́ṅge íti ǀ rákṣase ǀ vi-níkṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, shines with great and varied radiance; he makes all things manifest by his might; he overcomes undivine malignant delusions; he sharpens his horns for the destruction of therākṣasas.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, shines with great and varied radiance; he makes all things manifest by his might; he overcomes undivine malignant delusions; he sharpens his horns for the destruction of therākṣasas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्वानासो दिवि षंत्वग्नेस्तिग्मायुधा रक्षसे हंतवा उ ।मदे चिदस्य प्र रुजंति भामा न वरंते परिबाधो अदेवीः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ svānā́saḥ ǀ diví ǀ santu ǀ agnéḥ ǀ tigmá-āyudhāḥ ǀ rákṣase ǀ hántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀmáde ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ prá ǀ rujanti ǀ bhā́māḥ ǀ ná ǀ varante ǀ pari-bā́dhaḥ ǀ ádevīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: My roaring (flames),Agni, be manifest in the sky as sharp weapons wherewith to slay therākṣasas; in his exhilaration his shining (rays) inflict (destruction), and undivine opposing (hosts) arrest him not.
verses.wilson_translation: My roaring (flames),Agni, be manifest in the sky as sharp weapons wherewith to slay therākṣasas; in his exhilaration his shining (rays) inflict (destruction), and undivine opposing (hosts) arrest him not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एतं ते स्तोमं तुविजात विप्रो रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षं ।यदीदग्ने प्रति त्वं देव हर्याः स्वर्वतीरप एना जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: etám ǀ te ǀ stómam ǀ tuvi-jāta ǀ vípraḥ ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ atakṣam ǀyádi ǀ ít ǀ agne ǀ práti ǀ tvám ǀ deva ǀ háryāḥ ǀ sváḥ-vatīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ena ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: This praise have I, a devout worshipper, composed for you, (Agni), who are born with many (faculties), as a steady dexterous (artisan fabricates) a car; if, divine Agni, you approve of it, then may we obtain abundant flowing water.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise have I, a devout worshipper, composed for you, (Agni), who are born with many (faculties), as a steady dexterous (artisan fabricates) a car; if, divine Agni, you approve of it, then may we obtain abundant flowing water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुविग्रीवो वृषभो वावृधानोऽशत्र्वर्यः समजाति वेदः ।इतीममग्निममृता अवोचन्बर्हिष्मते मनवे शर्म यंसद्धविष्मते मनवे शर्म यंसत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tuvi-grī́vaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ aśatrú ǀ aryáḥ ǀ sám ǀ ajāti ǀ védaḥ ǀíti ǀ imám ǀ agním ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ avocan ǀ barhíṣmate ǀ mánave ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǀ havíṣmate ǀ mánave ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǁ
verses.english_translation: The many-necked, the showerer (of benefits), ever increasing, collects together the wealth of the enemy without opposition; the immortals have enjoined Agnithat he will bestow happiness on the man who offers sacrifice; that he will bestow happiness on the man who offers oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: The many-necked, the showerer (of benefits), ever increasing, collects together the wealth of the enemy without opposition; the immortals have enjoined Agnithat he will bestow happiness on the man who offers sacrifice; that he will bestow happiness on the man who offers oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN III. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १२ वसुश्रुत आत्रेयः। अग्निः, ३ मरुद्रुद्रविष्णवः। त्रिष्टुप्, १ विराट्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU at thy birth art Varuṇa, O Agni; when thou art kindled thou becomest Mitra.In thee, O Son of Strength, all Gods are centred. Indra art thou to man who brings oblation. Aryaman art thou as regardeth maidens mysterious, is thy name, O Self-sustainer.As a kind friend with streams of milk they balm thee what time thou makest wife and lord one-minded. The Maruts deck their beauty for thy glory, yea, Rudra! for thy birth fair, brightly-coloured.That which was fixed as Viṣṇu's loftiest station—therewith the secret of the Cows thou guardest. Gods through thy glory, God who art so lovely! granting abundant gifts gained life immortal.As their own Priest have men established Agni; and serve him fain for praise from him who liveth. There is no priest more skilled than thou in worship; none Self-sustainer pass thee in wisdom.The man within whose house as guest thou dwellest, O God, by sacrifice shall conquer mortals. Aided by thee, O Agni may we conquer through our oblation, fain for wealth, awakened:May we in battle, in the days’ assemblies, O Son of Strength, by riches conquer mortals. He shall bring evil on the evil-plotter whoever turns against us sin and outrage.Destroy this calumny of him, O Agni, whoever injures us with double-dealing. At this dawn's flushing, God! our ancient fathers served thee with offerings, making thee their envoy,When, Agni, to the store of wealth thou goest, a God enkindled with good things by mortals. Save, thou who knowest, draw thy father near thee, who counts as thine own son, O Child of Power.O sapient Agni, when wilt thou regard us? When, skilled in holy Law, wilt thou direct us? Adoring thee he gives thee many a title, when thou, Good Lord! acceptest this as Father.And doth not Agni, glad in strength of Godhead, gain splendid bliss when he hath waxen mighty? Most Youthful Agni, verily thou bearest thy praiser safely over all his troubles.Thieves have been seen by us and open foemen: unknown have been the plottings of the wicked. To thee these eulogies have been directed: or to the Vasu hath this sin been spoken.But this our Agni, flaming high, shall never yield us to calumny, to him who wrongs us.

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः ।त्वे विश्वे सहसस्पुत्र देवास्त्वमिंद्रो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ jā́yase ǀ yát ǀ tvám ǀ mitráḥ ǀ bhavasi ǀ yát ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀtvé íti ǀ víśve ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ putra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ tvám ǀ índraḥ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Agni, are born Varuṇa, you become Mitrawhen kindled; in you, son of strength, are all the gods; you are Indra, son of strength, to the mortal who presents (oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are born Varuṇa, you become Mitrawhen kindled; in you, son of strength, are all the gods; you are Indra, son of strength, to the mortal who presents (oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्���नीनां नाम स्वधावन्गुह्यं बिभर्षि ।अंजंति मित्रं सुधितं न गोभिर्यद्दंपती समनसा कृणोषि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ aryamā́ ǀ bhavasi ǀ yát ǀ kanī́nām ǀ nā́ma ǀ svadhā-van ǀ gúhyam ǀ bibharṣi ǀañjánti ǀ mitrám ǀ sú-dhitam ǀ ná ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ yát ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ sá-manasā ǀ kṛṇóṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are Aryamanin relation to maidens; you bear, enjoy of sacrificial food, a mysterious name; they anoint you, like a welcome friend, with milk and butter, when you make husband and wife of one mind.
verses.wilson_translation: You are Aryamanin relation to maidens; you bear, enjoy of sacrificial food, a mysterious name; they anoint you, like a welcome friend, with milk and butter, when you make husband and wife of one mind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव श्रिये मरुतो मर्जयंत रुद्र यत्ते जनिम चारु चित्रं ।पदं यद्विष्णोरुपमं निधायि तेन पासि गुह्यं नाम गोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ śriyé ǀ marútaḥ ǀ marjayanta ǀ rúdra ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ jánima ǀ cā́ru ǀ citrám ǀpadám ǀ yát ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ upa-mám ǀ ni-dhā́yi ǀ téna ǀ pāsi ǀ gúhyam ǀ nā́ma ǀ gónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: For your glory the Marutssweep (the firmament), when your birth,Rudra, is beautiful and wonderful; the middle step of Viṣṇuhas been plural ced, so you cherish the mysterious name of the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: For your glory the Marutssweep (the firmament), when your birth,Rudra, is beautiful and wonderful; the middle step of Viṣṇuhas been plural ced, so you cherish the mysterious name of the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव श्रिया सुदृशो देव देवाः पुरू दधाना अमृतं सपंत ।होतारमग्निं मनुषो नि षेदुर्दशस्यंत उशिजः शंसमायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ śriyā́ ǀ su-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ deva ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ purú ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ sapanta ǀhótāram ǀ agním ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ní ǀ seduḥ ǀ daśasyántaḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ śáṃsam ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine (Agni), gods, (made) comely by your glory, and bearing (the) great (affection), sip the ambrosia; men adore Agni, the conveyer of theburnt-offering, presenting oblations on behalfof the instrumental tutor of the rite, desirous of (its) reward.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine (Agni), gods, (made) comely by your glory, and bearing (the) great (affection), sip the ambrosia; men adore Agni, the conveyer of theburnt-offering, presenting oblations on behalfof the instrumental tutor of the rite, desirous of (its) reward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न त्वद्धोता पूर्वो अग्ने यजीयान्न काव्यैः परो अस्ति स्वधावः ।विशश्च यस्या अतिथिर्भवासि स यज्ञेन वनवद्देव मर्तान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tvát ǀ hótā ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ agne ǀ yájīyān ǀ ná ǀ kā́vyaiḥ ǀ paráḥ ǀ asti ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀviśáḥ ǀ ca ǀ yásyāḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ bhávāsi ǀ sáḥ ǀ yajñéna ǀ vanavat ǀ deva ǀ mártān ǁ
verses.english_translation: There is no more venerable offerer of oblation,Agni, than you, nor (one) prior to you; neither, giver of food, is any one subsequent (tobe more glorified by hymns); the man of whom you are the guest destroys hostile men by sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: There is no more venerable offerer of oblation,Agni, than you, nor (one) prior to you; neither, giver of food, is any one subsequent (tobe more glorified by hymns); the man of whom you are the guest destroys hostile men by sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वयमग्ने वनुयाम त्वोता वसूयवो हविषा बुध्यमानाः ।वयं समर्ये विदथेष्वह्नां वयं राया सहसस्पुत्र मर्तान् ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ agne ǀ vanuyāma ǀ tvā́-ūtāḥ ǀ vasu-yávaḥ ǀ havíṣā ǀ búdhyamānāḥ ǀvayám ǀ sa-maryé ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ áhnām ǀ vayám ǀ rāyā́ ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ putra ǀ mártān ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, desirous of wealth,Agni,and arousing you by oblations, secure in your protection, acquire (riches); may we (be victorious) in battle, (successful) in sacrifices every day; and may we, son of strength, obtain with richesmale(descendants).
verses.wilson_translation: May we, desirous of wealth,Agni,and arousing you by oblations, secure in your protection, acquire (riches); may we (be victorious) in battle, (successful) in sacrifices every day; and may we, son of strength, obtain with richesmale(descendants).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो न आगो अभ्येनो भरात्यधीदघमघशंसे दधात ।जही चिकित्वो अभिशस्तिमेतामग्ने यो नो मर्चयति द्वयेन ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ énaḥ ǀ bhárāti ǀ ádhi ǀ ít ǀ aghám ǀ aghá-śaṃse ǀ dadhāta ǀjahí ǀ cikitvaḥ ǀ abhí-śastim ǀ etā́m ǀ agne ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ marcáyati ǀ dvayéna ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Agniinflict (evil) upon the evil-doer, who commits offence, or wickedness against us; destroy, sagacious Agni, the calumniator who injures us in these two ways.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agniinflict (evil) upon the evil-doer, who commits offence, or wickedness against us; destroy, sagacious Agni, the calumniator who injures us in these two ways.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामस्या व्युषि देव पूर्वे दूतं कृण्वाना अयजंत हव्यैः ।संस्थे यदग्न ईयसे रयीणां देवो मर्तैर्वसुभिरिध्यमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ vi-úṣi ǀ deva ǀ pū́rve ǀ dūtám ǀ kṛṇvānā́ḥ ǀ ayajanta ǀ havyáiḥ ǀsam-sthé ǀ yát ǀ agne ǀ ī́yase ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ deváḥ ǀ mártaiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ idhyámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Former (worshippers) constituting you, divine (Agni), the messenger (of the gods), have worshipped you with oblations at the dawn of day; when you proceed to the plural ce (of the aggregation) of the wealth (of sacrifice), bright-shining, kindled by the mortals who have given you an abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Former (worshippers) constituting you, divine (Agni), the messenger (of the gods), have worshipped you with oblations at the dawn of day; when you proceed to the plural ce (of the aggregation) of the wealth (of sacrifice), bright-shining, kindled by the mortals who have given you an abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव स्पृधि पितरं योधि विद्वान्पुत्रो यस्ते सहसः सून ऊहे ।कदा चिकित्वो अभि चक्षसे नोऽग्ने कदाँ ऋतचिद्यातयासे ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ spṛdhi ǀ pitáram ǀ yódhi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ putráḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ ūhé ǀkadā́ ǀ cikitvaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cakṣase ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ kadā́ ǀ ṛta-cít ǀ yātayāse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Convey him (to safety) in war, son of strength, who like a wise son offers to you (reverence) as to a father; when, sagacious Agnido you look upon us; when, director of sacrifice, do you direct us (to good ways).
verses.wilson_translation: Convey him (to safety) in war, son of strength, who like a wise son offers to you (reverence) as to a father; when, sagacious Agnido you look upon us; when, director of sacrifice, do you direct us (to good ways).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भूरि नाम वंदमानो दधाति पिता वसो यदि तज्जोषयासे ।कुविद्देवस्य सहसा चकानः सुम्नमग्निर्वनते वावृधानः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ nā́ma ǀ vándamānaḥ ǀ dadhāti ǀ pitā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ yádi ǀ tát ǀ joṣáyāse ǀkuvít ǀ devásya ǀ sáhasā ǀ cakānáḥ ǀ sumnám ǀ agníḥ ǀ vanate ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorifying you, he offers the copious oblation, if, bestower of dwellings, you as a father are plural ased to accept it;Agni, ever augmenting, and desirous (to be friend), by hismight, the devout (worshipper, offering) copious oblations, bestows upon him happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorifying you, he offers the copious oblation, if, bestower of dwellings, you as a father are plural ased to accept it;Agni, ever augmenting, and desirous (to be friend), by hismight, the devout (worshipper, offering) copious oblations, bestows upon him happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमंग जरितारं यविष्ठ विश्वान्यग्ने दुरिताति पर्षि ।स्तेना अदृश्रन्रिपवो जनासोऽज्ञातकेता वृजिना अभूवन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ aṅgá ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ víśvāni ǀ agne ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ áti ǀ parṣi ǀstenā́ḥ ǀ adṛśran ǀ ripávaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ ájñāta-ketāḥ ǀ vṛjinā́ḥ ǀ abhūvan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, young (of the gods), verily you bear your adorer (safe) beyond all calamities; thieves have been detected, and hostile men with cover evil intentions, have been avoided (by us).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, young (of the gods), verily you bear your adorer (safe) beyond all calamities; thieves have been detected, and hostile men with cover evil intentions, have been avoided (by us).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमे यामासस्त्वद्रिगभूवन्वसवे वा तदिदागो अवाचि ।नाहायमग्निरभिशस्तये नो न रीषते वावृधानः परा दात् ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ yā́māsaḥ ǀ tvadrík ǀ abhūvan ǀ vásave ǀ vā ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ avāci ǀná ǀ áha ǀ ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ abhí-śastaye ǀ naḥ ǀ ná ǀ ríṣate ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ párā ǀ dāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: These (encomiums) are directed towards you, but perhaps an offence has thereby been uttered to (you), the giver of dwellings;may Agni,augmenting (by our praise), yield us not up to the maligner or the malevolent.
verses.wilson_translation: These (encomiums) are directed towards you, but perhaps an offence has thereby been uttered to (you), the giver of dwellings;may Agni,augmenting (by our praise), yield us not up to the maligner or the malevolent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN IV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O AGNI, King and Lord of wealth and treasures, in thee is my delight at sacrifices.Through thee may we obtain the strength we long for, and overcome the fierce attacks of mortals. Agni, Eternal Father, offering-bearer, fair to behold, far-reaching, far-refulgent,From well-kept household fire beam food to feed us, and measure out to us abundant glory. The Sage of men, the Lord of human races, pure, purifying Agni, balmed with butter,Him the Omniscient as your Priest ye stablish: he wins among the Gods things worth the choosing. Agni, enjoy, of one accord with Iḷā, striving in rivalry with beams of Sūrya,Enjoy, O Jātavedas, this our fuel, and bring the Gods to us to taste oblations. As dear House-Friend, guest welcome in the dwelling, to this our sacrifice come thou who knowest.And, Agni, having scattered all assailants, bring to us the possessions of our foemen. Drive thou away the Dasyu with thy weapon. As, gaining vital power for thine own body,O Son of Strength, the Gods thou satisfiest, so in fight save us, most heroic Agni. May we, O Agni, with our lauds adore thee, and with our gifts, fair-beaming Purifier!Send to us wealth containing all things precious: bestow upon us every sort of riches. Son of Strength, Agni, dweller in three regions, accept our sacrifice and our oblation.Among the Gods may we be counted pious: protect us with a triply-guarding shelter. Over all woes and dangers, Jātavedas, bear us as in a boat across a river.Praised with our homage even as Atri praised thee, O Agni, be the guardian of our bodies. As I, remembering thee with grateful spirit, a mortal, call with might on thee Immortal,Vouchsafe us high renown, O Jātavedas, and may I be immortal by my children. The pious man, O Jātavedas Agni, to whom thou grantest ample room and pleasure,Gaineth abundant wealth with sons and horses, with heroes and with kine for his well-being.

verses.sanskrit: त्वामग्ने वसुपतिं वसूनामभि प्र मंदे अध्वरेषु राजन् ।त्वया वाजं वाजयंतो जयेमाभि ष्याम पृत्सुतीर्मर्त्यानां ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ vásu-patim ǀ vásūnām ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ mande ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ rājan ǀtváyā ǀ vā́jam ǀ vāja-yántaḥ ǀ jayema ǀ abhí ǀ syāma ǀ pṛtsutī́ḥ ǀ mártyānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Royal Agni, I glorify at sacrifices you who are the lord of vast riches; may we who are in want of food obtain food through you, and (through you) may we overcome hosts of (hostile) men.
verses.wilson_translation: Royal Agni, I glorify at sacrifices you who are the lord of vast riches; may we who are in want of food obtain food through you, and (through you) may we overcome hosts of (hostile) men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हव्यवाळग्निरजरः पिता नो विभुर्विभावा सुदृशीको अस्मे ।सुगार्हपत्याः समिषो दिदीह्यस्मद्र्यक्सं मिमीहि श्रवांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: havya-vā́ṭ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ su-dṛ́śīkaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀsu-gārhapatyā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ didīhi ǀ asmadryák ǀ sám ǀ mimīhi ǀ śrávāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the undecaying Agni, the bearer of oblations, be a father to us, all-pervading and resplendent (may he be) to us of plural asing aspect; supply us plural ntifully with food in return for our well-maintained household fire grant us viand abundantly.
verses.wilson_translation: May the undecaying Agni, the bearer of oblations, be a father to us, all-pervading and resplendent (may he be) to us of plural asing aspect; supply us plural ntifully with food in return for our well-maintained household fire grant us viand abundantly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विशां कविं विश्पतिं मानुषीणां शुचिं पावकं घृतपृष्ठमग्निं ।नि होतारं विश्वविदं दधिध्वे स देवेषु वनते वार्याणि ॥
verses.transliteration: viśā́m ǀ kavím ǀ viśpátim ǀ mā́nuṣīṇām ǀ śúcim ǀ pāvakám ǀ ghṛtá-pṛṣṭham ǀ agním ǀní ǀ hótāram ǀ viśva-vídam ǀ dadhidhve ǀ sáḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ vanate ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: You (priests) possess the wise lord of human beings, the pure, the purifying,Agni, cherished with oblations of butter, the offer of the burnt-offering, the all-knowing; he among the gods bestows desirable (riches).
verses.wilson_translation: You (priests) possess the wise lord of human beings, the pure, the purifying,Agni, cherished with oblations of butter, the offer of the burnt-offering, the all-knowing; he among the gods bestows desirable (riches).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जुषस्वाग्न इळया सजोषा यतमानो रश्मिभिः सूर्यस्य ।जुषस्व नः समिधं जातवेद आ च देवान्हविरद्याय वक्षि ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣásva ǀ agne ǀ íḷayā ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ yátamānaḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀjuṣásva ǀ naḥ ǀ sam-ídham ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ devā́n ǀ haviḥ-ádyāya ǀ vakṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be propitiated,Agni, sharing in satisfaction with Iḷā, viewing with the rays of the sun; be gratified,Jātavedas, by our fuel, and bring the gods to partake of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Be propitiated,Agni, sharing in satisfaction with Iḷā, viewing with the rays of the sun; be gratified,Jātavedas, by our fuel, and bring the gods to partake of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जुष्टो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् ।विश्वा अग्ने अभियुजो विहत्या शत्रूयतामा भरा भोजनानि ॥
verses.transliteration: júṣṭaḥ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ imám ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ vidvā́n ǀvíśvā ǀ agne ǀ abhi-yújaḥ ǀ vi-hátya ǀ śatru-yatā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ bhójanāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Proppitiated, lowly-minded, a guest in the dwelling, come, you who are wise, to this our sacrifice; having destroyed Agni, all our adversaries, bring off the possessions of those who bear us enmity.
verses.wilson_translation: Proppitiated, lowly-minded, a guest in the dwelling, come, you who are wise, to this our sacrifice; having destroyed Agni, all our adversaries, bring off the possessions of those who bear us enmity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वधेन दस्युं प्र हि चातयस्व वयः कृण्वानस्तन्वे स्वायै ।पिपर्षि यत्सहसस्पुत्र देवान्त्सो अग्ने पाहि नृतम वाजे अस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: vedhéna ǀ dásyum ǀ prá ǀ hí ǀ cātáyasva ǀ váyaḥ ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ tanvé ǀ svā́yai ǀpíparṣi ǀ yát ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ putra ǀ devā́n ǀ sáḥ ǀ agne ǀ pāhi ǀ nṛ-tama ǀ vā́je ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Demolish,Agni, with your weapon, the Dasyu, appropriating the sustenance to your own person n; and inasmuch, son of strength, as you satisfy the gods, so do you, Agni, chief of leaders, protect us in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Demolish,Agni, with your weapon, the Dasyu, appropriating the sustenance to your own person n; and inasmuch, son of strength, as you satisfy the gods, so do you, Agni, chief of leaders, protect us in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वयं ते अग्न उक्थैर्विधेम वयं हव्यैः पावक भद्रशोचे ।अस्मे रयिं विश्ववारं समिन्वास्���े विश्वानि द्रविणानि धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ vayám ǀ havyáiḥ ǀ pāvaka ǀ bhadra-śoce ǀasmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ viśvá-vāram ǀ sám ǀ inva ǀ asmé íti ǀ víśvāni ǀ dráviṇāni ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We worship you,Agni, with hymns; we (worship you), purifier, and of auspicious lustre, with oblations; bestow upon us all desired riches; bestow upon us all sorts of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We worship you,Agni, with hymns; we (worship you), purifier, and of auspicious lustre, with oblations; bestow upon us all desired riches; bestow upon us all sorts of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व सहसः सूनो त्रिषधस्थ हव्यं ।वयं देवेषु सुकृतः स्याम शर्मणा नस्त्रिवरूथेन पाहि ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ agne ǀ adhvarám ǀ juṣasva ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ tri-sadhastha ǀ havyám ǀvayám ǀ devéṣu ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ syāma ǀ śármaṇā ǀ naḥ ǀ tri-várūthena ǀ pāhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Accept,Agni, our sacrifice; son of strength, the abider in the three regions, (accept our) oblation; may we be (regarded) among the goddess doers of good; cherish us with triply-protected felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Agni, our sacrifice; son of strength, the abider in the three regions, (accept our) oblation; may we be (regarded) among the goddess doers of good; cherish us with triply-protected felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वानि नो दुर्गहा जातवेदः सिंधुं न नावा दुरिताति पर्षि ।अग्ने अत्रिवन्नमसा गृणानोऽस्माकं बोध्यविता तनूनां ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvāni ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ síndhum ǀ ná ǀ nāvā́ ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ áti ǀ parṣi ǀágne ǀ atri-vát ǀ námasā ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ bodhi ǀ avitā́ ǀ tanū́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: You convey us,Jātavedas, across all intolerable evils, as (people are carried) over a river by a boat;Agni, who are glorified by us with reverence, such as (that shown) by Atri, know yourself the protector of our person ns.
verses.wilson_translation: You convey us,Jātavedas, across all intolerable evils, as (people are carried) over a river by a boat;Agni, who are glorified by us with reverence, such as (that shown) by Atri, know yourself the protector of our person ns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वा हृदा कीरिणा मन्यमानोऽमर्त्यं मर्त्यो जोहवीमि ।जातवेदो यशो अस्मासु धेहि प्रजाभिरग्ने अमृतत्वमश्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ kīríṇā ǀ mányamānaḥ ǀ ámartyam ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ jóhavīmi ǀjā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ yáśaḥ ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhehi ǀ pra-jā́bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ aśyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inasmuch as I who am a mortal earnestly invoke you who are an immortal, praising you with a devoted heart; therefore,Jātavedas, grant us food, and may I obtain immortality through my posterity.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as I who am a mortal earnestly invoke you who are an immortal, praising you with a devoted heart; therefore,Jātavedas, grant us food, and may I obtain immortality through my posterity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै त्वं सुकृते जातवेद उ लोकमग्ने कृणवः स्योनं ।अश्विनं स पुत्रिणं वीरवंतं गोमंतं रयिं नशते स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ tvám ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ agne ǀ kṛṇávaḥ ǀ syonám ǀaśvínam ǀ sáḥ ǀ putríṇam ǀ vīrá-vantam ǀ gó-mantam ǀ rayím ǀ naśate ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon whatsoever performer of good works you,Agni, who are Jātavedas, cast a favourable regard, he enjoys welfare, and riches, comprehending horses, cattle, sons andmaledescendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Upon whatsoever performer of good works you,Agni, who are Jātavedas, cast a favourable regard, he enjoys welfare, and riches, comprehending horses, cattle, sons andmaledescendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN V. Āprīs.
hymns.anukramani: ११ वसुश्रुत आत्रेयः। आप्रीसूक्तं- (१ इध्मः समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा, २ नराशंसः, ३ इळः, ४ बर्हिः, ५ देवीर्द्वारः, ६ उषासाक्ता, ७दैव्यो होतारौ प्रचेतसौ, ८ तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः, ९त्वष्टा, १० वनस्पतिः, ११ स्वाहाकृतयः )।गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To Agni, Jātavedas, to the flame, the well-enkindled God,Offer thick sacrificial oil. He, Narāśaṁsa, ne’er beguiled, inspiriteth this sacrifice:For sage is he, with sweets in hand. Adored, O Agni, hither bring Indra the Wonderful, the Friend,On lightly-rolling car to aid. Spread thyself out, thou soft as wool The holy hymns have sung to thee.Bring gain to us, O beautiful! Open yourselves, ye Doors Divine, easy of access for our aid:Fill, more and more, the sacrifice. Fair strengtheners of vital power, young Mothers of eternal Law,Morning and Night we supplicate. On the wind's flight come, glorified, ye two celestial Priests of manCome ye to this our sacrifice. Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī, three Goddesses who bring us weal,Be seated harmless on the grass. Rich in all plenty, Tvaṣṭar, come auspicious of thine own accordHelp us in every sacrifice. Vanaspati, wherever thou knowest the Gods’ mysterious names,Send our oblations thitherward. To Agni and to Varuṇa, Indra, the Maruts, and the Gods,With Svāhā be oblation brought.

verses.sanskrit: सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे घृतं तीव्रं जुहोतन ।अग्नये जातवेदसे ॥
verses.transliteration: sú-samiddhāya ǀ śocíṣe ǀ ghṛtám ǀ tīvrám ǀ juhotana ǀagnáye ǀ jātá-vedase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer abundant butter to the replendent Susamiddha, to Agni, to Jātavedas.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer abundant butter to the replendent Susamiddha, to Agni, to Jātavedas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नराशंसः सुषूदतीमं यज्ञमदाभ्यः ।कविर्हि मधुहस्त्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ susūdati ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǀkavíḥ ǀ hí ǀ mádhu-hastyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Narāśaṃsa animates this sacrifice he who is uninjurable, who verily is wise and sweet-handed.
verses.wilson_translation: Narāśaṃsa animates this sacrifice he who is uninjurable, who verily is wise and sweet-handed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईळितो अग्न आ वहेंद्रं चित्रमिह प्रियं ।सुखै रथेभिरूतये ॥
verses.transliteration: īḷitáḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ índram ǀ citrám ǀ ihá ǀ priyám ǀsu-kháiḥ ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀ ūtáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agno, who are Īḷita, bring hither the wonderful and friendly Indra, with his easy going chariots for our protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Agno, who are Īḷita, bring hither the wonderful and friendly Indra, with his easy going chariots for our protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्णम्रदा वि प्रथस्वाभ्यर्का अनूषत ।भवा नः शुभ्र सातये ॥
verses.transliteration: ū́rṇa-mradāḥ ǀ ví ǀ prathasva ǀ abhí ǀ arkā́ḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀbháva ǀ naḥ ǀ śubhra ǀ sātáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Grass), soft aswool, be spread; the worshippers praise you; be to us radiant (grass the source of) liberality.
verses.wilson_translation: (Grass), soft aswool, be spread; the worshippers praise you; be to us radiant (grass the source of) liberality.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवीर्द्वारो वि श्रयध्वं सुप्रायणा न ऊतये ।प्रप्र यज्ञं पृणीतन ॥
verses.transliteration: dévīḥ ǀ dvāraḥ ǀ ví ǀ śrayadhvam ǀ supra-ayanā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀprá-pra ǀ yajñám ǀ pṛṇītana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Open divine doors, our passages to preservation; fill full the sacrifice (with its rewards).
verses.wilson_translation: Open divine doors, our passages to preservation; fill full the sacrifice (with its rewards).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुप्रतीके वयोवृधा यह्वी ऋतस्य मातरा ।दोषामुषासमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: suprátīke íti su-prátīke ǀ vayaḥ-vṛ́dhā ǀ yahvī́ íti ǀ ṛtásya ǀ mātárā ǀdoṣā́m ǀ uṣásam ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We glorify the evening and the morning lovely, food-bestowing, mighty, the mothers of sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify the evening and the morning lovely, food-bestowing, mighty, the mothers of sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वातस्य पत्मन्नीळिता दैव्या होतारा मनुषः ।इमं नो यज्ञमा गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́tasya ǀ pátman ǀ īḷitā́ ǀ dáivyā ǀ hótārā ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀimám ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised (by us), divine invokers of the gods, come moving on the path of the wind, to this sacrifice of our patron.
verses.wilson_translation: Praised (by us), divine invokers of the gods, come moving on the path of the wind, to this sacrifice of our patron.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः ।बर्हिः सीदंत्वस्रिधः ॥
verses.transliteration: íḷā ǀ sárasvatī ǀ mahī́ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀbarhíḥ ǀ sīdantu ǀ asrídhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Iḷā,Sarasvatī,Mahī, the three goddesses who are the sources of happiness, sit down, benevolent, upon the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: May Iḷā,Sarasvatī,Mahī, the three goddesses who are the sources of happiness, sit down, benevolent, upon the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शिवस्त्वष्टरिहा गहि विभुः पोष उत त्मना ।यज्ञेयज्ञे न उदव ॥
verses.transliteration: śiváḥ ǀ tvaṣṭaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ póṣe ǀ utá ǀ tmánā ǀyajñé-yajñe ǀ naḥ ǀ út ǀ ava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tvaṣṭā, being propitious, you who are diffusive in kindness, come to your own accord protect us in repeated sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: Tvaṣṭā, being propitious, you who are diffusive in kindness, come to your own accord protect us in repeated sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्र वेत्थ वनस्पते देवानां गुह्या नामानि ।तत्र हव्यानि गामय ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ véttha ǀ vanaspate ǀ devā́nām ǀ gúhyā ǀ nā́māni ǀtátra ǀ havyā́ni ǀ gamaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wherever you know,Vanaspati, the secret forms of the gods to be, thither convey the oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Wherever you know,Vanaspati, the secret forms of the gods to be, thither convey the oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वाहाग्नये वरुणाय स्वाहेंद्राय मरुद्भ्यः ।स्वाहा देवेभ्यो हविः ॥
verses.transliteration: svā́hā ǀ agnáye ǀ váruṇāya ǀ svā́hā ǀ índrāya ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀsvā́hā ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The oblation is offered with reverence to Agni, to Varuṇa; with reverence to Indra, to the Maruts; with reverence to the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The oblation is offered with reverence to Agni, to Varuṇa; with reverence to Indra, to the Maruts; with reverence to the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I VALUE Agni that good Lord, the home to which the kine return:Whom fleet-foot coursers seek as home, and strong enduring steeds as home. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. ’Tis Agni whom we laud as good, to whom the milch-kine come in herds,To whom the chargers swift of foot, to whom our well-born princes come. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. Agni the God of all mankind, gives, verily, a steed to man.Agni gives precious gear for wealth, treasure he gives when he is pleased. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. God, Agni, we will kindle thee, rich in thy splendour, fading not,So that this glorious fuel may send forth by day its light for thee. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. To thee the splendid, Lord of flame, bright, wondrous, Prince of men, is brought.Oblation with the holy verse, O Agni, bearer of our gifts.Bring food to those who sing thy praise. These Agnis in the seats of the fire nourish each thing most excellent.They give delight, they spread abroad, they move themselves continually. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. Agni, these brilliant flames of thine wax like strong chargers mightily,Who with the treadings of their hoofs go swiftly to the stalls of kine. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. To us who laud thee, Agni, bring fresh food and safe and happy homes.May we who have sung hymns to thee have thee for envoy in each house. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. Thou, brilliant God, within thy mouth warmest both ladles of the oil.So fill us also, in our hymns, abundantly, O Lord of Strength. Bring food to those who sing thy praise. Thus Agni have we duly served with sacrifices and with hymns.So may he give us what we crave, store of brave sons and fleet-foot steeds. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं तं मन्ये यो वसुरस्तं यं यंति धेनवः ।अस्तमर्वंत आशवोऽस्तं नित्यासो वाजिन इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ tám ǀ manye ǀ yáḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ ástam ǀ yám ǀ yánti ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀástam ǀ árvantaḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ nítyāsaḥ ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: I glorify that Agniwho is the giver of dwellings; to whom, as to their home, the kine, the light-faced steeds, the constant offers of oblations, repair; do you, (Agni), bring food to your adorers.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify that Agniwho is the giver of dwellings; to whom, as to their home, the kine, the light-faced steeds, the constant offers of oblations, repair; do you, (Agni), bring food to your adorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सो अग्निर्यो वसुर्गृणे सं यमायंति धेनवः ।समर्वंतो रघुद्रुवः सं सुजातासः सूरय इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ gṛṇé ǀ sám ǀ yám ǀ ā-yánti ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀsám ǀ árvantaḥ ǀ raghu-drúvaḥ ǀ sám ǀ su-jātā́saḥ ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is Agni, who is praised as the giver of dwellings, to whom the kine, the light-faced steeds, the well-born, devout worshippers repair; do you Agni, bring food to your adorers.
verses.wilson_translation: He is Agni, who is praised as the giver of dwellings, to whom the kine, the light-faced steeds, the well-born, devout worshippers repair; do you Agni, bring food to your adorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्हि वाजिनं विशे ददाति विश्वचर्षणिः ।अग्नी राये स्वाभुवं स प्रीतो याति वार्यमिषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ hí ǀ vājínam ǀ viśé ǀ dádāti ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇiḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ rāyé ǀ su-ābhúvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ prītáḥ ǀ yāti ǀ vā́ryam ǀ íṣam ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the all-beholding, gives, verily, to the man (who worships him, a son) possessing abundant food; Agni, when propitiated proceeds (to bestow) that wealth which is of its own nature precious; do you, Agni, bring food to your adorers.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the all-beholding, gives, verily, to the man (who worships him, a son) possessing abundant food; Agni, when propitiated proceeds (to bestow) that wealth which is of its own nature precious; do you, Agni, bring food to your adorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते अग्न इधीमहि द्युमंतं देवाजरं ।यद्ध स्या ते पनीयसी समिद्दीदयति द्यवीषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ idhīmahi ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ deva ǀ ajáram ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ syā́ ǀ te ǀ pánīyasī ǀ sam-ít ǀ dīdáyati ǀ dyávi ǀ íṣam ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: We kindle you, divine Agni, bright, undecaying so that your glorious blaze shines in heaven; do you bring food to your adorers.
verses.wilson_translation: We kindle you, divine Agni, bright, undecaying so that your glorious blaze shines in heaven; do you bring food to your adorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते अग्न ऋचा हविः शुक्रस्य शोचिषस्पते ।सुश्चंद्र दस्म विश्पते हव्यवाट् तुभ्यं हूयत इषं स्तोतृभ्य आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ havíḥ ǀ śúkrasya ǀ śociṣaḥ ǀ pate ǀsú-candra ǀ dásma ǀ víśpate ǀ hávya-vāṭ ǀ túbhyam ǀ hūyate ǀ íṣam ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
