Thee, Agni, would we choose as Priest, the perfecter of strength and skill;We who bring sacred food invoke with song thee Chief at holy rites. Here as is needful for thine aid we toil, O Conqueror, day by day,For wealth, for Law. May we rejoice, Most Wise One! at the feast, with kine, rejoice, with heroes, at the feast.

verses.sanskrit: यमग्ने वाजसातम त्वं चिन्मन्यसे रयिं ।तं नो गीर्भिः श्रवाय्यं देवत्रा पनया युजं ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ agne ǀ vāja-sātama ǀ tvám ǀ cit ǀ mányase ǀ rayím ǀtám ǀ naḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ śravā́yyam ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ panaya ǀ yújam ǁ
verses.english_translation: That (sacrificial) wealth,Agni, bounteous giver of food, of which you approve, and which deserves to be commanded by our praises, do you convey to the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: That (sacrificial) wealth,Agni, bounteous giver of food, of which you approve, and which deserves to be commanded by our praises, do you convey to the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये अग्ने नेरयंति ते वृद्धा उग्रस्य शवसः ।अप द्वेषो अप ह्वरोऽन्यव्रतस्य सश्चिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ agne ǀ ná ǀ īráyanti ǀ te ǀ vṛddhā́ḥ ǀ ugrásya ǀ śávasaḥ ǀápa ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ hváraḥ ǀ anyá-vratasya ǀ saścire ǁ
verses.english_translation: may those prosperous men who do not offer oblations to you become destitute of great strength, and may (the followers) of other (than Vaidika) observances incur (your) enmity and punishment.
verses.wilson_translation: may those prosperous men who do not offer oblations to you become destitute of great strength, and may (the followers) of other (than Vaidika) observances incur (your) enmity and punishment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: होतारं त्वा वृणीमहेऽग्ने दक्षस्य साधनं ।यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यं गिरा प्रयस्वंतो हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: hótāram ǀ tvā ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ ágne ǀ dákṣasya ǀ sā́dhanam ǀyajñéṣu ǀ pūrvyám ǀ girā́ ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We, Prayasvats, have recourse to you, the invoker (of the gods), the means of strength; we glorify you first at sacrifices with praise.
verses.wilson_translation: We, Prayasvats, have recourse to you, the invoker (of the gods), the means of strength; we glorify you first at sacrifices with praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इत्था यथा त ऊतये सहसावंदिवेदिवे ।राय ऋताय सुक्रतो गोभिः ष्याम सधमादो वीरैः स्याम सधमादः ॥
verses.transliteration: itthā́ ǀ yáthā ǀ te ǀ ūtáye ǀ sáhasā-van ǀ divé-dive ǀrāyé ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ syāma ǀ sadha-mā́daḥ ǀ vīráiḥ ǀ syāma ǀ sadha-mā́daḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Possessor of strength, day by day so (provide) that we may enjoy your protection; doer of good deeds, may we (be deserving) of wealth through sacrifice, and may we be happy with cattle, happy withmaledescendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Possessor of strength, day by day so (provide) that we may enjoy your protection; doer of good deeds, may we (be deserving) of wealth through sacrifice, and may we be happy with cattle, happy withmaledescendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WE stablish thee as Manus used, as Manus used we kindle thee.Like Manus, for the pious man , Aṅgiras, Agni, worship Gods. For well, O Agni, art thou pleased when thou art kindled mid mankind.Straight go the ladles unto thee, thou highborn God whose food is oil. Thee have all Gods of one accord established as their messenger.Serving at sacrifices men adore thee as a God, O Sage. Let mortal man adore your God, Agni, with worship due to Gods.Shine forth enkindled, Radiant One. Sit in the chamber of the Law, sit in the chamber of the food.

verses.sanskrit: मनुष्वत्त्वा नि धीमहि मनुष्वत्समिधीमहि ।अग्ने मनुष्वदंगिरो देवांदेवयते यज ॥
verses.transliteration: manuṣvát ǀ tvā ǀ ní ǀ dhīmahi ǀ manuṣvát ǀ sám ǀ idhīmahi ǀágne ǀ manuṣvát ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ deva-yaté ǀ yaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like Manu, we meditate,Agni, upon you; like Manu, we kindle you; worship the gods on behalf of the (worshipper), devout as Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: Like Manu, we meditate,Agni, upon you; like Manu, we kindle you; worship the gods on behalf of the (worshipper), devout as Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि मानुषे जनेऽग्ने सुप्रीत इध्यसे ।स्रुचस्त्वा यंत्यानुषक्सुजात सर्पिरासुते ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ mā́nuṣe ǀ jáne ǀ ágne ǀ sú-prītaḥ ǀ idhyáse ǀsrúcaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ yanti ǀ ānuṣák ǀ sú-jāta ǀ sárpiḥ-āsute ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you are plural ased,Agni, you shine upon the human race; well-born, feeder upon clarified butter, the ladles are constantly uplifted to you.
verses.wilson_translation: When you are plural ased,Agni, you shine upon the human race; well-born, feeder upon clarified butter, the ladles are constantly uplifted to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो दूतमक्रत ।सपर्यंतस्त्वा कवे यज्ञेषु देवमीळते ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ víśve ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ dūtám ǀ akrata ǀsaparyántaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ kave ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ devám ǀ īḷate ǁ
verses.english_translation: All the consentient divinities have made you their messenger; therefore the pious worship you who are divine, wise Agni, at sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: All the consentient divinities have made you their messenger; therefore the pious worship you who are divine, wise Agni, at sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवं वो देवयज्ययाग्निमीळीत मर्त्यः ।समिद्धः शुक्र दीदिह्यृतस्य योनिमासदः ससस्य योनिमासदः ॥
verses.transliteration: devám ǀ vaḥ ǀ deva-yajyáyā ǀ agním ǀ īḷīta ǀ mártyaḥ ǀsám-iddhaḥ ǀ śukra ǀ dīdihi ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónim ǀ ā́ ǀ asadaḥ ǀ sasásya ǀ yónim ǀ ā́ ǀ asadaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Man praises you, divine Agni, to convey his offerings to the gods; bright Agni, blaze when kindled; take your seat in the chamber (of sacrifice), in the chamber of the sincere Sasa.
verses.wilson_translation: Man praises you, divine Agni, to convey his offerings to the gods; bright Agni, blaze when kindled; take your seat in the chamber (of sacrifice), in the chamber of the sincere Sasa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIKE Atri, Viśvasāman! sing to him of purifying light,Who must be praised in holy rites, the Priest most welcome in the house. Set Jātavedas in his place, Agni the God and Minister.Let sacrifice proceed to-day duly, comprising all the Gods. All mortals come to thee for aid, the God of most observant mind.Of thine excelling favour we bethink us as we long for it. Mark with attention this our speech, O Agni, thou victorious One.Thee, Strong-jawed! as the homestead's Lord, the Atris with their lauds exalt, the Atris beautify with songs.

verses.sanskrit: प्र विश्वसामन्नत्रिवदर्चा पावकशोचिषे ।यो अध्वरेष्वीड्यो होता मंद्रतमो विशि ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ viśva-sāman ǀ atri-vát ǀ árca ǀ pāvaká-śociṣe ǀyáḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ hótā ǀ mandrá-tamaḥ ǀ viśí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing, Viśvasāman, like Atri, (a hymn) to the dispenser of purifying light; (to him) who is to be praised at sacrifices, the invoker of the gods, the most adorable by man.
verses.wilson_translation: Sing, Viśvasāman, like Atri, (a hymn) to the dispenser of purifying light; (to him) who is to be praised at sacrifices, the invoker of the gods, the most adorable by man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न्यग्निं जातवेदसं दधाता देवमृत्विजं ।प्र यज्ञ एत्वानुषगद्या देवव्यचस्तमः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ agním ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ dádhāta ǀ devám ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀprá ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ etu ǀ ānuṣák ǀ adyá ǀ devávyacaḥ-tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cherish the divine Agni, by whom all that exists is known, the priest (of the rite); may the sacrifice most suitable for the gods duly this day proceed to them.
verses.wilson_translation: Cherish the divine Agni, by whom all that exists is known, the priest (of the rite); may the sacrifice most suitable for the gods duly this day proceed to them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चिकित्विन्मनसं त्वा देवं मर्तास ऊतये ।वरेण्यस्य तेऽवस इयानासो अमन्महि ॥
verses.transliteration: cikitvít-manasam ǀ tvā ǀ devám ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀváreṇyasya ǀ te ǀ ávasaḥ ǀ iyānā́saḥ ǀ amanmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men have recourse to you, divine Agni, who are of intelligent mind, for security; we praise you who are most excellent, seeking your protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Men have recourse to you, divine Agni, who are of intelligent mind, for security; we praise you who are most excellent, seeking your protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने चिकिद्ध्यस्य न इदं वचः सहस्य ।तं त्वा सुशिप्र दंपते स्तोमैर्वर्धंत्यत्रयो गीर्भिः शुंभंत्यत्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ cikiddhí ǀ asyá ǀ naḥ ǀ idám ǀ vácaḥ ǀ sahasya ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ su-śipra ǀ dam-pate ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ vardhanti ǀ átrayaḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ śumbhanti ǀ átrayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, son of strength, recognize the words of this our (laudation); handsome-chinned, lord of the dwelling, the sons of Atriexalt you, such (as you are), by thei rpraise; they embellish you by their hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, son of strength, recognize the words of this our (laudation); handsome-chinned, lord of the dwelling, the sons of Atriexalt you, such (as you are), by thei rpraise; they embellish you by their hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . By thy fair splendour's mighty power, O Agni, bring victorious wealth,Wealth that o’ercometh all mankind, and, near us, conquereth in fight. Victorious Agni, bring to us the wealth that vanquisheth in war;For thou art wonderful and true, giver of strength in herds of kine. For all the folk with one accord, whose sacred grass is trimmed and strewn,Invite thee to their worship-halls, as a dear Priest, for choicest wealth. For he, the God of all men, hath gotten him might that quelleth foes.O Agni, in these homes shine forth, bright God! for our prosperity, shine, Purifier! splendidly.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने सहंतमा भर द्युम्नस्य प्रासहा रयिं ।विश्वा यश्चर्षणीरभ्यासा वाजेषु सासहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ sáhantam ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ dyumnásya ǀ pra-sáhā ǀ rayím ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ carṣaṇī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ āsā́ ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ sasáhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestow,Agni, upon Dyumna, a son, overcoming foes by his prowess; one who may with glory subdue all men in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow,Agni, upon Dyumna, a son, overcoming foes by his prowess; one who may with glory subdue all men in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमग्ने पृतनाषहं रयिं सहस्व आ भर ।त्वं हि सत्यो अद्भुतो दाता वाजस्य गोमतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ agne ǀ pṛtanā-sáham ǀ rayím ǀ sahasvaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀtvám ǀ hí ǀ satyáḥ ǀ ádbhutaḥ ǀ dātā́ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ gó-mataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty Agni, grant us a son able to encounter hosts; for you are true and wonderful, and the giver of food with cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty Agni, grant us a son able to encounter hosts; for you are true and wonderful, and the giver of food with cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे हि त्वा सजोषसो जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषः ।होतारं सद्मसु प्रियं व्यंति वार्या पुरु ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣaḥ ǀhótāram ǀ sádma-su ǀ priyám ǀ vyánti ǀ vā́ryā ǀ purú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Allmen concurring in satisfaction, bearing the clipped sacred grass, solicit you, as the kind invoker of the gods, to the chambers (of sacrifice) for infinite wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Allmen concurring in satisfaction, bearing the clipped sacred grass, solicit you, as the kind invoker of the gods, to the chambers (of sacrifice) for infinite wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि ष्मा विश्वचर्षणिरभिमाति सहो दधे ।अग्न एषु क्षयेष्वा रेवन्नः शुक्र दीदिहि द्युमत्पावक दीदिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ abhí-māti ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ dadhé ǀágne ǀ eṣú ǀ kṣáyeṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ revát ǀ naḥ ǀ śukra ǀ dīdihi ǀ dyu-mát ǀ pāvaka ǀ dīdihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the (sage) on whom all men rely possess foe-subduing strength; radiant Agni, so shine in our habitation that they may abound in riches; shine, purifying Agni, dispensing light.
verses.wilson_translation: May the (sage) on whom all men rely possess foe-subduing strength; radiant Agni, so shine in our habitation that they may abound in riches; shine, purifying Agni, dispensing light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIV. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ४ गौपायना लौपायना वा बन्धुः सुबन्धुः श्रुतबन्धुर्विप्रबन्धुश्च। अग्निः । द्विपदा विराट्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O AGNI, be our nearest Friend, be thou a kind deliverer and a gracious Friend. Excellent Agni, come thou nigh to us, and give us wealth most splendidly renowned. So hear us, listen to this call of ours, and keep us far from every sinful man. To thee then, O Most Bright, O Radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने त्वं नो अंतम उत त्राता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀ utá ǀ trātā́ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ varūthyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [1-2]Agni, who are to be adored, be ever nigh to us, our protector and benefactor; do you, who are the giver of dwellings and dispenser of food, be present with us; bestow upon us most brilliant wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: [1-2]Agni, who are to be adored, be ever nigh to us, our protector and benefactor; do you, who are the giver of dwellings and dispenser of food, be present with us; bestow upon us most brilliant wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वसुरग्निर्वसुश्रवा अच्छा नक्षि द्युमत्तमं रयिं दाः ॥
verses.transliteration: vásuḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ vásu-śravāḥ ǀ áccha ǀ nakṣi ǀ dyumát-tamam ǀ rayím ǀ dāḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स नो बोधि श्रुधी हवमुरुष्या णो अघायतः समस्मात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ śrudhí ǀ hávam ǀ uruṣyá ǀ naḥ ǀ agha-yatáḥ ǀ samasmāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: [3-4] Understand us,Agni; hear our invocation; defend us from all malevolent (people); most bright and resplendent Agni, we earnestly solicit you for the happiness (of ourselves) and our friends.
verses.wilson_translation: [3-4] Understand us,Agni; hear our invocation; defend us from all malevolent (people); most bright and resplendent Agni, we earnestly solicit you for the happiness (of ourselves) and our friends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनमीमहे सखिभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ śociṣṭha ǀ dīdi-vaḥ ǀ sumnā́ya ǀ nūnám ǀ īmahe ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I WILL sing near, for grace, your God Agni, for he is good to us.Son of the Brands, may he give gifts, and, righteous, save us from the foe. For he is true, whom men of old enkindled, and the Gods themselves,The Priest with the delicious tongue, rich with the light of glorious beams. With wisdom that surpasseth all, with gracious will most excellent,O Agni, worthy of our choice, shine wealth on us through hymns of praise. Agni is King, for he extends to mortals and to Gods alike.Agni is bearer of our gifts. Worship ye Agni with your thoughts. Agni gives to the worshipper a son, the best, of mightiest fame,Of deep devotion, ne’er subdued, bringer of glory to his sire. Agni bestows the hero-lord who conquers with the men in fight.Agni bestows the fleet-foot steed, the victor never overcome. The mightiest song is Agni's: shine on high, thou who art rich in light.Like the Chief Consort of a King, riches and strength proceed from thee. Resplendent are thy rays of light: loud is thy voice like pressing-stones.Yea, of itself thy thunder goes forth like the roaring of the heaven. Thus, seeking riches, have we paid homage to Agni Conqueror.May he, most wise, as with a ship, carry us over all our foes.

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा वो अग्निमवसे देवं गासि स नो वसुः ।रासत्पुत्र ऋषूणामृतावा पर्षति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ vaḥ ǀ agním ǀ ávase ǀ devám ǀ gāsi ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀrā́sat ǀ putráḥ ǀ ṛṣūṇā́m ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ parṣati ǀ dviṣáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Celebrate the divine Agnifor his protection; may he who presides over dwellings grant (our desires); may the son of the ṛṣis, the observers of truth, save us from those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: Celebrate the divine Agnifor his protection; may he who presides over dwellings grant (our desires); may the son of the ṛṣis, the observers of truth, save us from those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि सत्यो यं पूर्वे चिद्देवासश्चिद्यमीधिरे ।होतारं मंद्रजिह्वमित्सुदीतिभिर्विभावसुं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ satyáḥ ǀ yám ǀ pū́rve ǀ cit ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ cit ǀ yám ǀ īdhiré ǀhótāram ǀ mandrá-jihvam ǀ ít ǀ sudītí-bhiḥ ǀ vibhā́-vasum ǁ
verses.english_translation: That Agniis true whom ancients, whom the gods have kindled, as the bright-tongued invoker of the gods, radiant with holy splendours.
verses.wilson_translation: That Agniis true whom ancients, whom the gods have kindled, as the bright-tongued invoker of the gods, radiant with holy splendours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स नो धीती वरिष्ठया श्रेष्ठया च सुमत्या ।अग्ने रायो दिदीहि नः सुवृक्तिभिर्वरेण्य ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dhītī́ ǀ váriṣṭhayā ǀ śréṣṭhayā ǀ ca ǀ su-matyā́ ǀágne ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ didīhi ǀ naḥ ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ vareṇya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, to be propitiated by praises, (gratified) by our choice and most excellent adoration and hymns, bestow upon us riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, to be propitiated by praises, (gratified) by our choice and most excellent adoration and hymns, bestow upon us riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्देवेषु राजत्यग्निर्मर्तेष्वाविशन् ।अग्निर्नो हव्यवाहनोऽग्निं धीभिः सपर्यत ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ rājati ǀ agníḥ ǀ márteṣu ǀ ā-viśán ǀagníḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ havya-vā́hanaḥ ǀ agním ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ saparyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agnishines among the gods; Agni is present among mortals; Agni is the bearer of our oblations glorify Agni with praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnishines among the gods; Agni is present among mortals; Agni is the bearer of our oblations glorify Agni with praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निस्तुविश्रवस्तमं तुविब्रह्माणमुत्तमं ।अतूर्तं श्रावयत्पतिं पुत्रं ददाति दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ tuvíśravaḥ-tamam ǀ tuví-brahmāṇam ǀ ut-tamám ǀatū́rtam ǀ śravayát-patim ǀ putrám ǀ dadāti ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Agnibestow upon the donor (of the oblation) son, abounding in food, abounding in devotion, excellent, unharmed, conferring honour upon his progenitors.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agnibestow upon the donor (of the oblation) son, abounding in food, abounding in devotion, excellent, unharmed, conferring honour upon his progenitors.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्ददाति सत्पतिं सासाह यो युधा नृभिः ।अग्निरत्यं रघुष्यदं जेतारमपराजितं ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ dadāti ǀ sát-patim ǀ sasā́ha ǀ yáḥ ǀ yudhā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ átyam ǀ raghu-syádam ǀ jétāram ǀ áparā-jitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Agnibestow a son, the protector of the good, who, with his followers, may be victorious in battle; may he bestow a swift-footed steed, conquering, unconquered.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agnibestow a son, the protector of the good, who, with his followers, may be victorious in battle; may he bestow a swift-footed steed, conquering, unconquered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नये बृहदर्च विभावसो ।महिषीव त्वद्रयिस्त्वद्वाजा उदीरते ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vā́hiṣṭham ǀ tát ǀ agnáye ǀ bṛhát ǀ arca ǀ vibhāvaso íti vibhā-vaso ǀmáhiṣī-iva ǀ tvát ǀ rayíḥ ǀ tvát ǀ vā́jāḥ ǀ út ǀ īrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: That (praise) which best conveys (our veneration, is due) to Agni; affluent in splendour, grant us, (Agni), great (wealth), for from you vast riches and ample food proceed.
verses.wilson_translation: That (praise) which best conveys (our veneration, is due) to Agni; affluent in splendour, grant us, (Agni), great (wealth), for from you vast riches and ample food proceed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव द्युमंतो अर्चयो ग्रावेवोच्यते बृहत् ।उतो ते तन्यतुर्यथा स्वानो अर्त त्मना दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ dyu-mántaḥ ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ grā́vā-iva ǀ ucyate ǀ bṛhát ǀutó íti ǀ te ǀ tanyatúḥ ǀ yathā ǀ svānáḥ ǀ arta ǀ tmánā ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brilliant,Agni, are your rays; mighty are you termed, like the stone (that bruises the Soma), and your voice spontaneously spreads through the sky like thundeṛ
verses.wilson_translation: Brilliant,Agni, are your rays; mighty are you termed, like the stone (that bruises the Soma), and your voice spontaneously spreads through the sky like thundeṛ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवाँ अग्निं वसूयवः सहसानं ववंदिम ।स नो विश्वा अति द्विषः पर्षन्नावेव सुक्रतुः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ agním ǀ vasu-yávaḥ ǀ sahasānám ǀ vavandima ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ párṣat ǀ nāvā́-iva ǀ su-krátuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus, we Vasuyus, glorify the vigorous Agni; may he, the performer of great deeds, enable us to pass over all our enemies as (we cross a river) with a boat.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus, we Vasuyus, glorify the vigorous Agni; may he, the performer of great deeds, enable us to pass over all our enemies as (we cross a river) with a boat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O AGNI, Holy and Divine, with splendour and thy pleasant tongueBring hither and adore the Gods. We pray thee, thou who droppest oil, bright-rayed! who lookest on the Sun,Bring the Gods hither to the feast. We have enkindled thee, O Sage, bright caller of the Gods to feast.O Agni, great in Sacrifice. O Agni, come with all the Gods, come to our sacrificial gift:We choose thee as Invoking Priest. Bring, Agni, to the worshipper who pours the juice, heroic strength:Sit with the Gods upon the grass. Victor of thousands, Agni, thou, enkindled, cherishest the laws,Laud-worthy, envoy of the Gods. Set Agni Jātavedas down, the bearer of our sacred gifts,MostYouthful, God and Minister. Duly proceed our sacrifice, comprising all the Gods, to-day:Strew holy grass to be their seat. So may the Maruts sit thereon, the Aśvins, Mitra, Varuṇa:The Gods with all their company.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने पावक रोचिषा मंद्रया देव जिह्वया ।आ देवान्वक्षि यक्षि च ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ pāvaka ǀ rocíṣā ǀ mandráyā ǀ deva ǀ jihváyā ǀā́ ǀ devā́n ǀ vakṣi ǀ yákṣi ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine purifier,Agni, with your radiant and plural asing tongue, bring hither and worship the gods
verses.wilson_translation: Divine purifier,Agni, with your radiant and plural asing tongue, bring hither and worship the gods
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा घृतस्नवीमहे चित्रभानो स्वर्दृशं ।देवाँ आ वीतये वह ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ ghṛtasno íti ghṛta-sno ǀ īmahe ǀ cítrabhāno íti cítra-bhāno ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śam ǀdevā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vītáye ǀ vaha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Feeder upon butter, bright and variegated radiance we solicit you, the beholder of heaven, to (partake of) the (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: Feeder upon butter, bright and variegated radiance we solicit you, the beholder of heaven, to (partake of) the (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वीतिहोत्रं त्वा कवे द्युमंतं समिधीमहि ।अग्ने बृहंतमध्वरे ॥
verses.transliteration: vītí-hotram ǀ tvā ǀ kave ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ sám ǀ idhīmahi ǀágne ǀ bṛhántam ǀ adhvaré ǁ
verses.english_translation: We kindle you at the sacrifice, wise Agni, whose food is the oblation, who are brilliant and vast.
verses.wilson_translation: We kindle you at the sacrifice, wise Agni, whose food is the oblation, who are brilliant and vast.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने विश्वेभिरा गहि देवेभिर्हव्यदातये ।होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ havyá-dātaye ǀhótāram ǀ tvā ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come,Agni, with all the gods, to the donor (of the oblation); we have recourse to you as their invoker.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Agni, with all the gods, to the donor (of the oblation); we have recourse to you as their invoker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यजमानाय सुन्वत आग्ने सुवीर्यं वह ।देवैरा सत्सि बर्हिषि ॥
verses.transliteration: yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǀ ā́ ǀ agne ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ vaha ǀdeváiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ satsi ǀ barhíṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: To the instrumental tutor of the rite, pouring out the libation, bring excellent vigour; sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: To the instrumental tutor of the rite, pouring out the libation, bring excellent vigour; sit down with the gods upon the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिधानः सहस्रजिदग्ने धर्माणि पुष्यसि ।देवानां दूत उक्थ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-idhānáḥ ǀ sahasra-jit ǀ ágne ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ puṣyasi ǀdevā́nām ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ukthyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Victor over thousands, you favour, when kindled our holy rites, the honoured messenger of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Victor over thousands, you favour, when kindled our holy rites, the honoured messenger of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न्यग्निं जातवेदसं होत्रवाहं यविष्ठ्यं ।दधाता देवमृत्विजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ agním ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ hotra-vā́ham ǀ yáviṣṭhyam ǀdádhāta ǀ devám ǀ ṛtvíjam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Reverence Agni, by whom all that is, is known, the bearer of oblations, the young of the gods, the divine, the ministrant priest.
verses.wilson_translation: Reverence Agni, by whom all that is, is known, the bearer of oblations, the young of the gods, the divine, the ministrant priest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यज्ञ एत्वानुषगद्या देवव्यचस्तमः ।स्तृणीत बर्हिरासदे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ etu ǀ ānuṣák ǀ adyá ǀ devávyacaḥ-tamaḥ ǀstṛṇītá ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā-sáde ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the sacrifice most solemnly offered by the devout duly proceed today (to the gods); spread the sacred grass for their seat.
verses.wilson_translation: May the sacrifice most solemnly offered by the devout duly proceed today (to the gods); spread the sacred grass for their seat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एदं मरुतो अश्विना मित्रः सीदंतु वरुणः ।देवासः सर्वया विशा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ idám ǀ marútaḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ mitráḥ ǀ sīdantu ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀdevā́saḥ ǀ sárvayā ǀ viśā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Maruts, the Aśvins,Mitra,Varuṇa, the gods, with all their attendants, sit down upon this grass.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Maruts, the Aśvins,Mitra,Varuṇa, the gods, with all their attendants, sit down upon this grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVII. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ६ त्रैवृष्णस्त्र्यरुणः, पौरुकुत्सस्रसदस्युः भारतोऽश्वमेधश्च राजानः, (अत्रिर्भौम इति केचित्)। अग्निः ६ इन्द्राग्नी।त्रिष्टुप्, ४-६ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Godlike hero, famousest of nobles, hath granted me two oxen with a wagon.Trvrsan's son Tryaruna hath distinguished himself, Vaiśvānara Agni! with ten thousands. Protect Tryaruna, as thou art waxing strong and art highly praised, Vaiśvānara Agni!Who granteth me a hundred kine and twenty, and two bay horses, good at draught, and harnessed. So Trasadasyu served thee, God Most Youthful, craving thy favour for the ninth time, Agni;Tryaruya who with attentive spirit accepteth many a song from me the mighty. He who declares his wish to me, to Asvamedha, to the Prince,Pays him who with his verse seeks gain, gives power to him who keeps the Law. From whom a hundred oxen, all of speckled hue, delight my heart,The gifts of Asvamedha, like thrice-mingled draughts of Soma juice. To Asvamedha who bestows a hundred gifts grant hero power,O Indra-Agni! lofty rule like the unwasting Sun in heaven.

verses.sanskrit: अनस्वंता सत्पतिर्मामहे मे गावा चेतिष्ठो असुरो मघोनः ।त्रैवृष्णो अग्ने दशभिः सहस्रैर्वैश्वानर त्र्यरुणश्चिकेत ॥
verses.transliteration: ánasvantā ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ mamahe ǀ me ǀ gā́vā ǀ cétiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀtraivṛṣṇáḥ ǀ agne ǀ daśá-bhiḥ ǀ sahásraiḥ ǀ váiśvānara ǀ trí-aruṇaḥ ǀ ciketa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniwho are the protector of the good, most wise, powerful and opulent; Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivṛṣṇa, has become renowned,Vaiśvānara, in that he has bestowed upon me a pair of cattle with a wagon, and with them thousands of treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniwho are the protector of the good, most wise, powerful and opulent; Tryaruṇa, the son of Trivṛṣṇa, has become renowned,Vaiśvānara, in that he has bestowed upon me a pair of cattle with a wagon, and with them thousands of treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो मे शता च विंशतिं च गोनां हरी च युक्ता सुधुरा ददाति ।वैश्वानर सुष्टुतो वावृधानोऽग्ने यच्छ त्र्यरुणाय शर्म ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ me ǀ śatā́ ǀ ca ǀ viṃśatím ǀ ca ǀ gónām ǀ hárī íti ǀ ca ǀ yuktā́ ǀ su-dhúrā ǀ dádāti ǀváiśvānara ǀ sú-stutaḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ ágne ǀ yáccha ǀ trí-aruṇāya ǀ śárma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni,Vaiśvānara, who are deservedly praised and exaulted (by us), bestow happiness upon Tryaruṇa, who gives me hundreds (of Suvarṇas), twenty cattle and a pair of burden-bearing horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni,Vaiśvānara, who are deservedly praised and exaulted (by us), bestow happiness upon Tryaruṇa, who gives me hundreds (of Suvarṇas), twenty cattle and a pair of burden-bearing horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा ते अग्ने सुमतिं चकानो नविष्ठाय नवमं त्रसदस्युः ।यो मे गिरस्तुविजातस्य पूर्वीर्युक्तेनाभि त्र्यरुणो गृणाति ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ su-matím ǀ cakānáḥ ǀ náviṣṭhāya ǀ navamám ǀ trasádasyuḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ me ǀ gíraḥ ǀ tuvi-jātásya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ yukténa ǀ abhí ǀ trí-aruṇaḥ ǀ gṛṇā́ti ǁ
verses.english_translation: As Tryaruṇa, plural ased by the eulogies of me who has many children, presses with earnest (mind, gifts upon me), so does Trasadsyu, desirous Agni, of your valued favour through your exceeding praise.
verses.wilson_translation: As Tryaruṇa, plural ased by the eulogies of me who has many children, presses with earnest (mind, gifts upon me), so does Trasadsyu, desirous Agni, of your valued favour through your exceeding praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो म इति प्रवोचत्यश्वमेधाय सूरये ।दददृचा सनिं यते ददन्मेधामृतायते ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ me ǀ íti ǀ pra-vócati ǀ áśva-medhāya ǀ sūráye ǀdádat ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ saním ǀ yaté ǀ dádat ǀ medhā́m ǀ ṛta-yaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Aśvamedhagives to him who solicits of him as a benefactor, saying (bestow wealth) upon me, and comes (to him) with a verse (in your praise), do you,Agni, grant intelligence to (the Rājā) who wishes to offer sacrifice (to you).
verses.wilson_translation: When Aśvamedhagives to him who solicits of him as a benefactor, saying (bestow wealth) upon me, and comes (to him) with a verse (in your praise), do you,Agni, grant intelligence to (the Rājā) who wishes to offer sacrifice (to you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य मा परुषाः शतमुद्धर्षयंत्युक्षणः ।अश्वमेधस्य दानाः सोमा इव त्र्याशिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ mā ǀ paruṣā́ḥ ǀ śatám ǀ ut-harṣáyanti ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀáśva-medhasya ǀ dā́nāḥ ǀ sómāḥ-iva ǀ trí-āśiraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose hundred robust oxen yield me delight, as triple-mixed Soma, the offering of Aśvamedha(gratifies you).
verses.wilson_translation: Whose hundred robust oxen yield me delight, as triple-mixed Soma, the offering of Aśvamedha(gratifies you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी शतदाव्न्यश्वमेधे सुवीर्यं ।क्षत्रं धारयतं बृहद्दिवि सूर्यमिवाजरं ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ śata-dā́vni ǀ áśva-medhe ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀkṣatrám ǀ dhārayatam ǀ bṛhát ǀ diví ǀ sū́ryam-iva ǀ ajáram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, bestow upon the munificent Aśvamedhainfinite wealth with excellent posterity, undecaying as the sun in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, bestow upon the munificent Aśvamedhainfinite wealth with excellent posterity, undecaying as the sun in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI inflamed hath sent to heaven his lustre: he shines forth widely turning unto Morning.Eastward the ladle goes that brings all blessing, praising the Godswith homage and oblation. Enkindled, thou art King of the immortal world: him who brings offerings thou attendest for his weal.He whom thou urgest on makes all possessions his: he sets before thee, Agni, gifts that guests may claim. Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours.Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us. Thy glory, Agni, I adore, kindled, exalted in thy strength.A Steer of brilliant splendour, thou art lighted well at sacred rites. Agni, invoked and kindled, serve the Gods, thou skilled in sacrifice:For thou art bearer of our gifts. Invoke and worship Agni while the sacrificial rite proceeds:For offering-bearer choose ye him.

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धो अग्निर्दिवि शोचिरश्रेत्प्रत्यङ्ङुषसमुर्विया वि भाति ।एति प्राची विश्ववारा नमोभिर्देवाँ ईळाना हविषा घृताची ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ diví ǀ śocíḥ ǀ aśret ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ uṣásam ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ bhāti ǀéti ǀ prā́cī ǀ viśvá-vārā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ ī́ḷānā ǀ havíṣā ǀ ghṛtā́cī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, when kindled, spreads lustre through the firmament, and shines widely in the presence of the dawn; Viśvavārā, facing the east, glorifying the gods with praises, and bearing the ladle with the oblation, proceeds (to the sacred fire).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, when kindled, spreads lustre through the firmament, and shines widely in the presence of the dawn; Viśvavārā, facing the east, glorifying the gods with praises, and bearing the ladle with the oblation, proceeds (to the sacred fire).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिध्यमानो अमृतस्य राजसि हविष्कृण्वंतं सचसे स्वस्तये ।विश्वं स धत्ते द्रविणं यमिन्वस्यातिथ्यमग्ने नि च धत्त इत्पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-idhyámānaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ rājasi ǀ havíḥ ǀ kṛṇvántam ǀ sacase ǀ svastáye ǀvíśvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ dhatte ǀ dráviṇam ǀ yám ǀ ínvasi ǀ ātithyám ǀ agne ǀ ní ǀ ca ǀ dhatte ǀ ít ǀ puráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When about to be kindled,Agni, you rule over ambrosial (water); you are present with the offerer of the oblation for his welfare; he to whom you repair acquires universal wealth; he plural ces you, Agni the dues of hospitality.
verses.wilson_translation: When about to be kindled,Agni, you rule over ambrosial (water); you are present with the offerer of the oblation for his welfare; he to whom you repair acquires universal wealth; he plural ces you, Agni the dues of hospitality.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगाय तव द्युम्नान्युत्तमानि संतु ।सं जास्पत्यं सुयममा कृणुष्व शत्रूयतामभि तिष्ठा महांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ śárdha ǀ mahaté ǀ sáubhagāya ǀ táva ǀ dyumnā́ni ǀ ut-tamā́ni ǀ santu ǀsám ǀ jaḥ-patyám ǀ su-yámam ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǀ śatru-yatā́m ǀ abhí ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ máhāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Repress,Agni, (our foes to ensure our) exceeding prosperity; may your riches ever be excellent; preserve in concord the relation of man and wife, and overpower the energies of the hostile.
verses.wilson_translation: Repress,Agni, (our foes to ensure our) exceeding prosperity; may your riches ever be excellent; preserve in concord the relation of man and wife, and overpower the energies of the hostile.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धस्य प्रमहसोऽग्ने वंदे तव श्रियं ।वृषभो द्युम्नवाँ असि समध्वरेष्विध्यसे ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhasya ǀ prá-mahasaḥ ǀ agne ǀ vánde ǀ táva ǀ śríyam ǀvṛṣabháḥ ǀ dyumná-vān ǀ asi ǀ sám ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ idhyase ǁ
verses.english_translation: I praise the glory,Agni, of you when kindled and blazing fiercely; you are the affluent showerer (of benefits), you are fitly lighted at sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise the glory,Agni, of you when kindled and blazing fiercely; you are the affluent showerer (of benefits), you are fitly lighted at sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धो अग्न आहुत देवान्यक्षि स्वध्वर ।त्वं हि हव्यवाळसि ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā-huta ǀ devā́n ǀ yakṣi ǀ su-adhvara ǀtvám ǀ hí ǀ havya-vā́ṭ ǀ ási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, who are kindled and invoked, worship the gods at the holy rite, for you are the bearer of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are kindled and invoked, worship the gods at the holy rite, for you are the bearer of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ जुहोता दुवस्यताग्निं प्रयत्यध्वरे ।वृणीध्वं हव्यवाहनं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ juhota ǀ duvasyáta ǀ agním ǀ pra-yatí ǀ adhvaré ǀvṛṇīdhvám ǀ havya-vā́hanam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer worship and adoration to Agniwhen the sacrifice is solemnized; select the bearer of the oblation to the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer worship and adoration to Agniwhen the sacrifice is solemnized; select the bearer of the oblation to the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १५ गौरिवीतिः शाक्त्यः। इन्द्रः, ९(प्रथमपादस्य) उशना वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAN'S worship of the Gods hath three great lustres, and three celestial lights have they establishedThe Maruts gifted with pure strength adore thee, for thou, O Indra, art their sapient Ṛṣi. What time the Maruts sang their song to Indra, joyous when he had drunk of Soma juices,He grasped his thunderbolt to slay the Dragon, and loosed, that they might flow, the youthful Waters. And, O ye Brahmans, Maruts, so may Indra drink draughts of this my carefully pressed Soma;For this oblation found for man the cattle, and Indra, having quaffed it, slew the Dragon. Then heaven and earth he sundered and supported: wrapped even in these he struck the Beast with terror.So Indra forced the Engulfer to disgorgement, and slew the Dānava. panting against him. Thus all the Gods, O Maghavan, delivered to thee of their free will the draught of Soma;When thou for Etaśa didst cause to tarry the flying mares of Sūrya racing forward. When Maghavan with the thunderbolt demolished his nine-and-ninety castles all together,The Maruts, where they met, glorified Indra: ye with the Tṛṣṭup hymn obstructed heaven. As friend to aid a friend, Agni dressed quickly three hundred buffaloes, even as he willed it.And Indra, from man's gift, for Vṛtra's slaughter, drank ofr at once three lakes of pressed-out Soma. When thou three hundred buffaloes' flesh hadst eaten, and drunk, as Maghavan, three lakes of Soma,All the Gods raised as ’twere a shout of triumph to Indra praise because he slew the Dragon. What time ye came with strong steeds swiftly speeding, O Uśanā and Indra, to the dwelling,Thou camest thither -conquering together with Kutsa and the Gods: thou slewest Śuṣṇa. One car-wheel of the Sun thou rolledst forward, and one thou settest free to move for Kutsa.Thou slewest noseless Dasyus with thy weapon, and in their home o’erthrewest hostile speakers. The lauds of Gauriviti made thee mighty to Vidathin's son, as prey, thou gavest Pipru.Rjisivan drew thee into friendship dressing the sacred food, and thou hast drunk his Soma. Navagvas and Dasgvas with libations of Soma juice sing hymns of praise to Indra.Labouring at their task the men laid open the stall of Kine though firmly closed and fastened. How shall I serve thee, Maghavan, though knowing full well what hero deeds thou hast accomplished?And the fresh deeds which thou wilt do, Most Mighty! these, too, will we tell forth in sacred synods. Resistless from of old through hero courage, thou hast done all these many acts, O Indra.What thou wilt do in bravery, Thunder-wielder! none is there who may hinder this thy prowess. Indra, accept the prayers which now are offered, accept the new prayers, Mightiest! which we utter.Like fair and well-made robes, I, seeking riches, as a deft craftsman makes a car, have wrought them.

verses.sanskrit: त्र्यर्यमा मनुषो देवताता त्री रोचना दिव्या धारयंत ।अर्चंति त्वा मरुतः पूतदक्षास्त्वमेषामृषिरिंद्रासि धीरः ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ devá-tātā ǀ trī́ ǀ rocanā́ ǀ divyā́ ǀ dhārayanta ǀárcanti ǀ tvā ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pūtá-dakṣāḥ ǀ tvám ǀ eṣām ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ indra ǀ asi ǀ dhī́raḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the adoration of the gods by Manuthere are three effulgences, and they, (the Maruts), uphold three luminaries in heaven; the Maruts of pure energy worship you, for you,Indra, are their intelligent ṛṣi
verses.wilson_translation: In the adoration of the gods by Manuthere are three effulgences, and they, (the Maruts), uphold three luminaries in heaven; the Maruts of pure energy worship you, for you,Indra, are their intelligent ṛṣi
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनु यदीं मरुतो मंदसानमार्चन्निंद्रं पपिवांसं सुतस्य ।आदत्त वज्रमभि यदहिं हन्नपो यह्वीरसृजत्सर्तवा उ ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mandasānám ǀ ā́rcan ǀ índram ǀ papi-vā́ṃsam ǀ sutásya ǀā́ ǀ adatta ǀ vájram ǀ abhí ǀ yát ǀ áhim ǀ hán ǀ apáḥ ǀ yahvī́ḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ sártavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the Marutsworship Indra, exulting and drinking of the effused libation, he grasps the thunderbolt wherewith he destroys Ahi, and sets the abundant waters free to flow.
verses.wilson_translation: When the Marutsworship Indra, exulting and drinking of the effused libation, he grasps the thunderbolt wherewith he destroys Ahi, and sets the abundant waters free to flow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत ब्रह्माणो मरुतो मे अस्येंद्रः सोमस्य सुषुतस्य पेयाः ।तद्धि हव्यं मनुषे गा अविंददहन्नहिं पपिवाँ इंद्रो अस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ brahmāṇaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ me ǀ asya ǀ índraḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ sú-sutasya ǀ peyāḥ ǀtát ǀ hí ǀ havyám ǀ mánuṣe ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ávindat ǀ áhan ǀ áhim ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Or,mighty Maruts, and you also,Indra, drink of this my copiously-effused libation; then the offered libation obtains cattle for the offerer, and Indra, drinking of it, kills Ahi.
verses.wilson_translation: Or,mighty Maruts, and you also,Indra, drink of this my copiously-effused libation; then the offered libation obtains cattle for the offerer, and Indra, drinking of it, kills Ahi.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आद्रोदसी वितरं वि ष्कभायत्संविव्यानश्चिद्भियसे मृगं कः ।जिगर्तिमिंद्रो अपजर्गुराणः प्रति श्वसंतमव दानवं हन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vi-tarám ǀ ví ǀ skabhāyat ǀ sam-vivyānáḥ ǀ cit ǀ bhiyáse ǀ mṛgám ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀjígartim ǀ índraḥ ǀ apa-járgurāṇaḥ ǀ práti ǀ śvasántam ǀ áva ǀ dānavám ǀ hanníti han ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thereupon he fixed firmly heaven and earth, and resolutely advancing, filled (Vṛtra), like a deer, with terror, stripping off his covering,Indra, slew the Dānava, endeavouring to hide, and panting with affright.
verses.wilson_translation: Thereupon he fixed firmly heaven and earth, and resolutely advancing, filled (Vṛtra), like a deer, with terror, stripping off his covering,Indra, slew the Dānava, endeavouring to hide, and panting with affright.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध क्रत्वा मघवंतुभ्यं देवा अनु विश्वे अददुः सोमपेयं ।यत्सूर्यस्य हरितः पतंतीः पुरः सतीरुपरा एतशे कः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ krátvā ǀ magha-van ǀ túbhyam ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ víśve ǀ adaduḥ ǀ soma-péyam ǀyát ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ harítaḥ ǀ pátantīḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ úparāḥ ǀ étaśe ǀ káríti káḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then, for this exploit, all the gods gave you Maghavan, in succession, the Somabeverage; whence you have retarded, for the sake of Etaśa, the advancing horses of the sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Then, for this exploit, all the gods gave you Maghavan, in succession, the Somabeverage; whence you have retarded, for the sake of Etaśa, the advancing horses of the sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नव यदस्य नवतिं च भोगान्त्साकं वज्रेण मघवा विवृश्चत् ।अर्चंतींद्रं मरुतः सधस्थे त्रैष्टुभेन वचसा बाधत द्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: náva ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ bhogā́n ǀ sākám ǀ vájreṇa ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vi-vṛścát ǀárcanti ǀ índram ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ tráistubhena ǀ vácasā ǀ bādhata ǀ dyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whereupon Maghavanhas destroyed with his thunderbolt at once his (Śambara's) ninety and nine cities; the Marutsglorifying Indrain a common dwelling with the Triṣṭubhhymn, he destroyed the bright (city of theasura).
verses.wilson_translation: Whereupon Maghavanhas destroyed with his thunderbolt at once his (Śambara's) ninety and nine cities; the Marutsglorifying Indrain a common dwelling with the Triṣṭubhhymn, he destroyed the bright (city of theasura).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सखा सख्ये अपचत्तूयमग्निरस्य क्रत्वा महिषा त्री शतानि ।त्री साकमिंद्रो मनुषः सरांसि सुतं पिबद्वृत्रहत्याय सोमं ॥
verses.transliteration: sákhā ǀ sákhye ǀ apacat ǀ tū́yam ǀ agníḥ ǀ asyá ǀ krátvā ǀ mahiṣā́ ǀ trī́ ǀ śatā́ni ǀtrī́ ǀ sākám ǀ índraḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ sárāṃsi ǀ sutám ǀ pibat ǀ vṛtra-hátyāya ǀ sómam ǁ
verses.english_translation: To aid (the undertaking of) his friend,Agni, the friend (of Indra) has quickly consumed three hundred buffaloes; and Indra, for the destruction of Vṛtra, has at once quaffed vessels of Soma, offered by Manu.
verses.wilson_translation: To aid (the undertaking of) his friend,Agni, the friend (of Indra) has quickly consumed three hundred buffaloes; and Indra, for the destruction of Vṛtra, has at once quaffed vessels of Soma, offered by Manu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्री यच्छता महिषाणामघो मास्त्री सरांसि मघवा सोम���यापाः ।कारं न विश्वे अह्वंत देवा भरमिंद्राय यदहिं जघान ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ ǀ yát ǀ śatā́ ǀ mahiṣā́ṇām ǀ ághaḥ ǀ mā́ḥ ǀ trī́ ǀ sárāṃsi ǀ maghá-vā ǀ somyā́ ǀ ápāḥ ǀkārám ǀ ná ǀ víśve ǀ ahvanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ bháram ǀ índrāya ǀ yát ǀ áhim ǀ jaghā́na ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you had eaten the flesh of the three hundred buffaloes, when you who are Maghavanhad drunk the three vessels of Soma, when he had slain Ahi, then all the gods summoned Indra, full of food, as if he had been a servant, to the battle.
verses.wilson_translation: When you had eaten the flesh of the three hundred buffaloes, when you who are Maghavanhad drunk the three vessels of Soma, when he had slain Ahi, then all the gods summoned Indra, full of food, as if he had been a servant, to the battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उशना यत्सहस्यैरयातं गृहमिंद्र जूजुवानेभिरश्वैः ।वन्वानो अत्र सरथं ययाथ कुत्सेन देवैरवनोर्ह शुष्णं ॥
verses.transliteration: uśánā ǀ yát ǀ sahasyáiḥ ǀ áyātam ǀ gṛhám ǀ indra ǀ jūjuvānébhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀvanvānáḥ ǀ átra ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yayātha ǀ kútsena ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ávanoḥ ǀ ha ǀ śúṣṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When,Indra, you and Uśanas, with vigorous and rapid courses went to the dwelling of Kutsa, then destroying his foes, you went in one chariot with Kutsa and the gods, and verily you have slainŚuṣṇa
verses.wilson_translation: When,Indra, you and Uśanas, with vigorous and rapid courses went to the dwelling of Kutsa, then destroying his foes, you went in one chariot with Kutsa and the gods, and verily you have slainŚuṣṇa
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यद्वरिवो यातवेऽकः ।अनासो दस्यूँरमृणो वधेन नि दुर्योण आवृणङ्मृध्रवाचः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ anyát ǀ cakrám ǀ avṛhaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ kútsāya ǀ anyát ǀ várivaḥ ǀ yā́tave ǀ akarítyakaḥ ǀanā́saḥ ǀ dásyūn ǀ amṛṇaḥ ǀ vadhéna ǀ ní ǀ duryoṇé ǀ avṛṇak ǀ mṛdhrá-vācaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have formerly detached one wheel (of the car) of Sūrya; another you have given to Kutsawherewith to acquire wealth; with the thunderbolt you have confounded the voiceless Dasyus, you have destroyed in battle the speech-bereft (foes).
verses.wilson_translation: You have formerly detached one wheel (of the car) of Sūrya; another you have given to Kutsawherewith to acquire wealth; with the thunderbolt you have confounded the voiceless Dasyus, you have destroyed in battle the speech-bereft (foes).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोमासस्त्वा गौरिवीतेरवर्धन्नरंधयो वैदथिनाय पिप्रुं ।आ त्वामृजिश्वा सख्याय चक्रे पचन्पक्तीरपिबः सोममस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: stómāsaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ gáuri-vīteḥ ǀ avardhan ǀ árandhayaḥ ǀ vaidathinā́ya ǀ píprum ǀā́ ǀ tvā́m ǀ ṛjíśvā ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ cakre ǀ pácan ǀ paktī́ḥ ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ sómam ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the praises of Gaurivīti exalt you; you have humbled Pipru for the son of Vidathin; Ṛjiśvan preparing dressed viands, has, through your friendship brought you (to his presence), and you have drunk of his libation.
verses.wilson_translation: May the praises of Gaurivīti exalt you; you have humbled Pipru for the son of Vidathin; Ṛjiśvan preparing dressed viands, has, through your friendship brought you (to his presence), and you have drunk of his libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इंद्रं दशग्वासो अभ्यर्चंत्यर्कैः ।गव्यं चिदूर्वमपिधानवंतं तं चिन्नरः शशमाना अप व्रन् ॥
verses.transliteration: náva-gvāsaḥ ǀ sutá-somāsaḥ ǀ índram ǀ dáśa-gvāsaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ arcanti ǀ arkáiḥ ǀgávyam ǀ cit ǀ ūrvám ǀ apidhā́na-vantam ǀ tám ǀ cit ǀ náraḥ ǀ śaśamānā́ḥ ǀ ápa ǀ vran ǁ
verses.english_translation: The observers of the nine month's celebration, those of the ten months, pouring out libations, worship Indrawith hymns; the leaders (of rites), glorifying him, have set open the cave (concealing the cattle).
verses.wilson_translation: The observers of the nine month's celebration, those of the ten months, pouring out libations, worship Indrawith hymns; the leaders (of rites), glorifying him, have set open the cave (concealing the cattle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कथो नु ते परि चराणि विद्वान्वीर्या मघवन्या चकर्थ ।या चो नु नव्या कृणवः शविष्ठ प्रेदु ता ते विदथेषु ब्रवाम ॥
verses.transliteration: kathó íti ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ pári ǀ carāṇi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ vīryā́ ǀ magha-van ǀ yā́ ǀ cakártha ǀyā́ ǀ co íti ǀ nú ǀ návyā ǀ kṛṇávaḥ ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ prá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ bravāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Although, knowing the heroic acts which,Maghavan, you have performed, how may I adequately offer you adoration; most mighty Indra, we ever celebrate sacred rites the recent exploits which you have achieved.
verses.wilson_translation: Although, knowing the heroic acts which,Maghavan, you have performed, how may I adequately offer you adoration; most mighty Indra, we ever celebrate sacred rites the recent exploits which you have achieved.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एता विश्वा चकृवाँ इंद्र भूर्यपरीतो जनुषा वीर्येण ।या चिन्नु वज्रिन्कृणवो दधृष्वान्न ते वर्ता तविष्या अस्ति तस्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ cakṛ-vā́n ǀ indra ǀ bhū́ri ǀ ápari-itaḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ vīryéṇa ǀyā́ ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ vajrin ǀ kṛṇávaḥ ǀ dadhṛṣvā́n ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ vartā́ ǀ táviṣyāḥ ǀ asti ǀ tásyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unmatched (by any), you have done,Indra, all these many (deeds) by your innate energy; wielder of the thunderbolt, whatever you, the humbler of (foes), have undertaken, there is no one the arrester of this your prowess.
verses.wilson_translation: Unmatched (by any), you have done,Indra, all these many (deeds) by your innate energy; wielder of the thunderbolt, whatever you, the humbler of (foes), have undertaken, there is no one the arrester of this your prowess.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र ब्रह्म क्रियमाणा जुषस्व या ते शविष्ठ नव्या अकर्म ।वस्त्रेव भद्रा सुकृता वसूयू रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ bráhma ǀ kriyámāṇā ǀ juṣasva ǀ yā́ ǀ te ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ návyāḥ ǀ ákarma ǀvástrā-iva ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ sú-kṛtā ǀ vasu-yúḥ ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ atakṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most mighty Indra, be plural ased to accept the prayers which we are about to offer, and the present praises which we repeat; firm, doing pious acts, and desirous of wealth; I have fabricated acceptable and pious works like (rich) garments, and like a chariot.
verses.wilson_translation: Most mighty Indra, be plural ased to accept the prayers which we are about to offer, and the present praises which we repeat; firm, doing pious acts, and desirous of wealth; I have fabricated acceptable and pious works like (rich) garments, and like a chariot.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHERE is that Hero? Who hath looked on Indra borne on light-rolling car by Tawny Coursers,Who, Thunderer, seeks with wealth the Soma-presser, and to his house goes, much-invoked, to aid him? I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder's habitation.I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra. We will tell, Indra, when we pour libation, what mighty deeds thou hast performed to please us.Let him who knows not learn, who knows them listen: hither rides Maghavan with all his army. Indra, when born, thou madest firm thy spirit: alone thou seekest war to fight with many.With might thou clavest e’en the rock asunder, and foundest out the stable of the Milch-kine. When thou wast born supremest at a distance, bearing a name renowned in far-off regions,Since then e’en Gods have been afraid of Indra: he conquered all the floods which served the Dāsa. These blissful Maruts sing their psalm to praise thee, and pour to thee libation of the Soma.Indra with wondrous powers subdued the Dragon, the guileful lurker who beset the waters. Thou, Maghavan, from the first didst scatter foemen, speeding, while joying in the milk, the Giver.There, seeking man's prosperity, thou torest away the head of Namuci the Dāsa. Pounding the head of Namuci the Dāsa, me, too thou madest thine associate, Indra!Yea, and the rolling stone that is in heaven both worlds, as on a car, brought to the Maruts. Women for weapons hath the Dāsa taken, What injury can his feeble armies To me?Well he distinguished his two different voices, and Indra then advanced to fight the Dasyu. Divided from their calves the Cows went lowing around, on every side, hither and thither.These Indra re-united with his helpers, what time the well-pressed Soma made him joyful. What time the Somas mixed by Babhru cheered him, loud the Steer bellowed in his habitations.So Indra drank thereof, the Fort-destroyer, and gave him guerdon, in return, of milch-kine. This good deed have the Rusamas done, Agni! that they have granted me four thousand cattle.We have received Rnancaya's wealth, of heroes the most heroic, which was freely offered. The Rusamas, O Agni, sent me homeward with fair adornment and with kine in thousands.The strong libations have made Indra joyful, when night, whose course was ending, changed to morning. Night, well-nigh ended, at Rnancaya's coming, King of the Rusamas, was changed to morning.Like a strong courser, fleet of foot, urged onward, Babhru hath gained four thousand as his guerdon. We have received four thousand head of cattle presented by the Rusamas, O Agni.And we, the singers, have received the caldron of metal which was heated for Pravargya.

verses.sanskrit: क्व स्य वीरः को अपश्यदिंद्रं सुखरथमीयमानं हरिभ्यां ।यो राया वज्री सुतसोममिच्छंतदोको गंता पुरुहूत ऊती ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ syáḥ ǀ vīráḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ apaśyat ǀ índram ǀ sukhá-ratham ǀ ī́yamānam ǀ hári-bhyām ǀyáḥ ǀ rāyā́ ǀ vajrī́ ǀ sutá-somam ǀ icchán ǀ tát ǀ ókaḥ ǀ gántā ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where is that hero? who has seen Indraseated in his easy chariot travelling with his horses, the thunder, the invoked of many, who, desirous of the libation is proceeding with riches to the habitation (of his worshipper) for his preservation?
verses.wilson_translation: Where is that hero? who has seen Indraseated in his easy chariot travelling with his horses, the thunder, the invoked of many, who, desirous of the libation is proceeding with riches to the habitation (of his worshipper) for his preservation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवाचचक्षं पदमस्य सस्वरुग्रं निधातुरन्वायमिच्छन् ।अपृच्छमन्याँ उत ते म आहुरिंद्रं नरो बुबुधाना अशेम ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ acacakṣam ǀ padám ǀ asya ǀ sasváḥ ǀ ugrám ǀ ni-dhātúḥ ǀ ánu ǀ āyam ǀ icchán ǀápṛccham ǀ anyā́n ǀ utá ǀ té ǀ me ǀ āhuḥ ǀ índram ǀ náraḥ ǀ bubudhānā́ḥ ǀ aśema ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have looked down upon the secret and fearful plural ce of his abiding; I have repaired, desiring him, (to the plural ce of) the self-sustainer; I have inquired (of him) from others; they, the leaders (of rites), the search after wisdom, have said to me, let us have recourse to Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: I have looked down upon the secret and fearful plural ce of his abiding; I have repaired, desiring him, (to the plural ce of) the self-sustainer; I have inquired (of him) from others; they, the leaders (of rites), the search after wisdom, have said to me, let us have recourse to Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नु वयं सुते या ते कृतानींद्र ब्रवाम यानि नो जुजोषः ।वेददविद्वांछृणवच्च विद्वान्वहतेऽयं मघवा सर्वसेनः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ vayám ǀ suté ǀ yā́ ǀ te ǀ kṛtā́ni ǀ índra ǀ brávāma ǀ yā́ni ǀ naḥ ǀ jújoṣaḥ ǀvédat ǀ ávidvān ǀ śṛṇávat ǀ ca ǀ vidvā́n ǀ váhate ǀ ayám ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sárva-senaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the libation is offered,Indra, we celebrate your exploits; those (exploits) which you have been praised (to achieve) for us; let him who is ignorant acquire knowledge (of them); let him who is acquainted (with them) make them known; this Maghavan(is) the lord of hosts.
verses.wilson_translation: When the libation is offered,Indra, we celebrate your exploits; those (exploits) which you have been praised (to achieve) for us; let him who is ignorant acquire knowledge (of them); let him who is acquainted (with them) make them known; this Maghavan(is) the lord of hosts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्थिरं मनश्चकृषे जात इंद्र वेषीदेको युधये भूयसश्चित् ।अश्मानं चिच्छवसा दिद्युतो वि विदो गवामूर्वमुस्रियाणां ॥
verses.transliteration: sthirám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ cakṛṣe ǀ jātáḥ ǀ indra ǀ véṣi ǀ ít ǀ ékaḥ ǀ yudháye ǀ bhū́yasaḥ ǀ cit ǀáśmānam ǀ cit ǀ śávasā ǀ didyutaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vidáḥ ǀ gávām ǀ ūrvám ǀ usríyāṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: As soon as genitive rated,Indra, you have made your mind resolved; you have gone alone to contend against numerous (foes); you have rent asunder the rock by your strength; you have rescued the herd of milk-yielding kine.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as genitive rated,Indra, you have made your mind resolved; you have gone alone to contend against numerous (foes); you have rent asunder the rock by your strength; you have rescued the herd of milk-yielding kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परो यत्त्वं परम आजनिष्ठाः परावति श्रुत्यं नाम बिभ्रत् ।अतश्चिदिंद्रादभयंत देवा विश्वा अपो अजयद्दासपत्नीः ॥
verses.transliteration: paráḥ ǀ yát ǀ tvám ǀ paramáḥ ǀ ā-jániṣṭhāḥ ǀ parā-váti ǀ śrútyam ǀ nā́ma ǀ bíbhrat ǀátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ índrāt ǀ abhayanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ajayat ǀ dāsá-patnīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you have been born most excellent and supreme, bearing a name widely renowned, then the gods have been in dread of Indra, and he has subjugated all the waters, the brides of the slave (Vṛtra).
verses.wilson_translation: When you have been born most excellent and supreme, bearing a name widely renowned, then the gods have been in dread of Indra, and he has subjugated all the waters, the brides of the slave (Vṛtra).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्येदेते मरुतः सुशेवा अर्चंत्यर्कं सुन्वंत्यंधः ।अहिमोहानमप आशयानं प्र मायाभिर्मायिनं सक्षदिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhya ǀ ít ǀ eté ǀ marútaḥ ǀ su-śévāḥ ǀ árcanti ǀ arkám ǀ sunvánti ǀ ándhaḥ ǀáhim ǀ ohānám ǀ apáḥ ǀ ā-śáyānam ǀ prá ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ māyínam ǀ sakṣat ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These devoted Marutseulogise you with pious praise, and pour out to you the sacrificial food;Indrahas overcome by his device the guileful Ahi, harassing the gods and arresting the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: These devoted Marutseulogise you with pious praise, and pour out to you the sacrificial food;Indrahas overcome by his device the guileful Ahi, harassing the gods and arresting the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि षू मृधो जनुषा दानमिन्वन्नहन्गवा मघवन्त्संचकानः ।अत्रा दासस्य नमुचेः शिरो यदवर्तयो मनवे गातुमिच्छन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sú ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ dā́nam ǀ ínvan ǀ áhan ǀ gávā ǀ magha-van ǀ sam-cakānáḥ ǀátra ǀ dāsásya ǀ námuceḥ ǀ śíraḥ ǀ yát ǀ ávartayaḥ ǀ mánave ǀ gātúm ǀ icchán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavan, who are glorified by us, assailing with the thunderbolt the antagonist (of the gods), you have slain those who were ever hostile (to you) from your birth; desiring to do good to Manu, you have bruised the head of the slave Namuci.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavan, who are glorified by us, assailing with the thunderbolt the antagonist (of the gods), you have slain those who were ever hostile (to you) from your birth; desiring to do good to Manu, you have bruised the head of the slave Namuci.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युजं हि मामकृथा आदिदिंद्र शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् ।अश्मानं चित्स्वर्यं वर्तमानं प्र चक्रियेव रोदसी मरुद्भ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: yújam ǀ hí ǀ mā́m ǀ ákṛthāḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ śíraḥ ǀ dāsásya ǀ námuceḥ ǀ mathāyán ǀáśmānam ǀ cit ǀ svaryám ǀ vártamānam ǀ prá ǀ cakríyā-iva ǀ ródasī íti ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Verily you have made me,Indra, your associate when grinding the head of the slave Namucilike a sounding and rolling cloud; and the heaven and earth (have been caused) by the Maruts(to revolve like a wheel).
verses.wilson_translation: Verily you have made me,Indra, your associate when grinding the head of the slave Namucilike a sounding and rolling cloud; and the heaven and earth (have been caused) by the Maruts(to revolve like a wheel).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रियो हि दास आयुधानि चक्रे किं मा करन्नबला अस्य सेनाः ।अंतर्ह्यख्यदुभे अस्य धेने अथोप प्रैद्युधये दस्युमिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: stríyaḥ ǀ hí ǀ dāsáḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ cakré ǀ kím ǀ mā ǀ karan ǀ abalā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ sénāḥ ǀantáḥ ǀ hí ǀ ákhyat ǀ ubhé íti ǀ asya ǀ dhéne íti ǀ átha ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ ait ǀ yudháye ǀ dásyum ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The slave (Namuci) made women his weapons what will his feminine le hosts do unto me? The two his best beloved, (Indra) confined in the inner apartments, and then went forth to combat against the Dasyus.
verses.wilson_translation: The slave (Namuci) made women his weapons what will his feminine le hosts do unto me? The two his best beloved, (Indra) confined in the inner apartments, and then went forth to combat against the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समत्र गावोऽभितोऽनवंतेहेह वत्सैर्वियुता यदासन् ।सं ता इंद्रो असृजदस्य शाकैर्यदीं सोमासः सुषुता अमंदन् ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ átra ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ anavanta ǀ ihá-iha ǀ vatsáiḥ ǀ ví-yutāḥ ǀ yát ǀ ā́san ǀsám ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ asya ǀ śākáiḥ ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ sú-sutāḥ ǀ ámandan ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the cows were separated from their calves, they wandered about hither and thither; but when the well-offered libations had exhilarated hi, then Indra, with his vigorous (maruts), reunited them (with their calves).
verses.wilson_translation: When the cows were separated from their calves, they wandered about hither and thither; but when the well-offered libations had exhilarated hi, then Indra, with his vigorous (maruts), reunited them (with their calves).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदीं सोमा बभ्रुधूता अमंदन्नरोरवीद्वृषभः सादनेषु ।पुरंदरः पपिवाँ इंद्रो अस्य पुनर्गवामददादुस्रियाणां ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ īm ǀ sómāḥ ǀ babhrú-dhūtāḥ ǀ ámandan ǀ ároravīt ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ sádaneṣu ǀpuram-daráḥ ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ asya ǀ púnaḥ ǀ gávām ǀ adadāt ǀ usríyāṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the libations effused by Babhruhad exhilarated him, the showerer (of benefits) shouted aloud in the combats;Indra, the destroyer fo cities, quaffing (the Soma), restored to him his milk-yielding cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: When the libations effused by Babhruhad exhilarated him, the showerer (of benefits) shouted aloud in the combats;Indra, the destroyer fo cities, quaffing (the Soma), restored to him his milk-yielding cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रमिदं रुशमा अग्ने अक्रन्गवां चत्वारि ददतः सहस्रा ।ऋणंचयस्य प्रयता मघानि प्रत्यग्रभीष्म नृतमस्य नृणां ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ idám ǀ ruśámāḥ ǀ agne ǀ akran ǀ gávām ǀ catvā́ri ǀ dádataḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀṛṇam-cayásya ǀ prá-yatā ǀ maghā́ni ǀ práti ǀ agrabhīṣma ǀ nṛ́-tamasya ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Suśamās giving me four thousand cows,Agni, have done well; we have accepted the wealth, the donation of the leader of leaders rṇañcaya.
verses.wilson_translation: The Suśamās giving me four thousand cows,Agni, have done well; we have accepted the wealth, the donation of the leader of leaders rṇañcaya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुपेशसं माव सृजंत्यस्तं गवां सहस्रै रुशमासो अग्ने ।तीव्रा इंद्रमममंदुः सुतासोऽक्तोर्व्युष्टौ परितक्म्यायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-péśasam ǀ mā ǀ áva ǀ sṛjanti ǀ ástam ǀ gávām ǀ sahásraiḥ ǀ ruśámāsaḥ ǀ agne ǀtīvrā́ḥ ǀ índram ǀ amamanduḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ aktóḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ pári-takmyāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Ruśamās,Agni, have presented to me a beautiful abode, with thousands of cattle; the sharp libations have exhilarated Indraupon the breaking up of the (gloom-) investing night.
verses.wilson_translation: The Ruśamās,Agni, have presented to me a beautiful abode, with thousands of cattle; the sharp libations have exhilarated Indraupon the breaking up of the (gloom-) investing night.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: औच्छत्सा रात्री परितक्म्या याँ ऋणंचये राजनि रुशमानां ।अत्यो न वाजी रघुरज्यमानो बभ्रुश्चत्वार्यसनत्सहस्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: áucchat ǀ sā́ ǀ rā́trī ǀ pári-takmyā ǀ yā́ ǀ ṛṇam-cayé ǀ rā́jani ǀ ruśámānām ǀátyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vājī́ ǀ raghúḥ ǀ ajyámānaḥ ǀ babhrúḥ ǀ catvā́ri ǀ asanat ǀ sahásrā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The (gloom-) investing night has dispersed with the dawn (upon the appearance of) Ṛṇañcaya, therājāof theruśamās;Babhrubeing summoned, going like a fleet courser, has received the four thousand (cattle).
verses.wilson_translation: The (gloom-) investing night has dispersed with the dawn (upon the appearance of) Ṛṇañcaya, therājāof theruśamās;Babhrubeing summoned, going like a fleet courser, has received the four thousand (cattle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चतुःसहस्रं गव्यस्य पश्वः प्रत्यग्रभीष्म रुशमेष्वग्ने ।घर्मश्चित्तप्तः प्रवृजे य आसीदयस्मयस्तम्वादाम विप्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: cátuḥ-sahasram ǀ gávyasya ǀ paśváḥ ǀ práti ǀ agrabhīṣma ǀ ruśámeṣu ǀ agne ǀgharmáḥ ǀ cit ǀ taptáḥ ǀ pra-vṛ́je ǀ yáḥ ǀ ā́sīt ǀ ayasmáyaḥ ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ā́dāma ǀ víprāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have accepted,Agni, the four thousand cattle from the Ruśamās; and the glowing, the golden ewer prepared for the solemnity, we who are wise have accepted it.
verses.wilson_translation: We have accepted,Agni, the four thousand cattle from the Ruśamās; and the glowing, the golden ewer prepared for the solemnity, we who are wise have accepted it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १३ अवस्युरात्रेयः। इन्द्रः, ८ तृतीयपादस्य कुत्सो वा, चतुर्थपादस्य उशना वा, ९ इन्द्राकुत्सौ। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAGHAVAN Indra turns his chariot downward, the strength-displaying car which he hath mounted.Even as a herdsman driveth forth his cattle, he goeth, first, uninjured, fain for treasure.. Haste to us, Lord of Bays; be not ungracious: visit us, lover of gold-hued oblation.There is naught else better than thou art, Indra: e’en to the wifeless hast thou given spouses. When out of strength arose the strength that conquers, Indra displayed all powers that he possesses.Forth from the cave he drove the milky mothers, and with the light laid bare investing darkness.. Anus have wrought a chariot for thy Courser, and Tvaṣṭar, Much-invoked! thy bolt that glitters.The Brahmans with their songs exalting Indra increased his strength that he might slaughter Ahi. When heroes sang their laud to thee the Hero, Indra! and stones and Aditi accordant,Without or steed or chariot were the fellies which, sped by Indra, rolled upon the Dasytis. I will declare thine exploits wrought aforetime, and, Maghavan, thy deeds of late achievement,When, Lord of Might, thou sunderedst earth and heaven, winning for man the moistly-gleaming waters. This is thy deed, e’en this, Wonderful! Singer! that, slaying Ahi, here thy strength thou showedst,Didst check and stay e’en gusna's wiles and magic, and, drawing nigh, didst chase away the Dasytis. Thou, Indra, on the farther bank forYadu and Turvaga didst stay the gushing waters.Ye both assailed the fierce: thou barest Kutsa: when Gods and Uśanā came to you together. Let the steeds bring you both, Indra and Kutsa, borne on the chariot within hearing-distance.Ye blew him from the waters, from his dwelling, and chased the darkness from the noble's spirit. Even this sage hath come looking for succour even to Vāta's docile harnessed horses.Here are the Maruts, all, thy dear companions: prayers have increased thy power and might, O Indra. When night was near its close he carried forward e’en the Sun's chariot backward in its running.Etaga brought his wheel and firmly stays it: setting it eastward he shall give us courage. This Indra, O ye men, hath come to see you, seeking a friend who hath expressed the Soma.The creaking stone is laid upon the altar, and the Adhvaryus come to turn it quickly. Let mortals who were happy still be happy; let them not come to sorrow, O Immortal.Love thou the pious, and to these thy people-with whom may we be numbered-give thou vigour.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो रथाय प्रवतं कृणोति यमध्यस्थान्मघवा वाजयंतं ।यूथेव पश्वो व्युनोति गोपा अरिष्टो याति प्रथमः सिषासन् ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ráthāya ǀ pra-vátam ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ yám ǀ adhi-ásthāt ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vāja-yántam ǀyūthā́-iva ǀ paśváḥ ǀ ví ǀ unoti ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ áriṣṭaḥ ǀ yāti ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ sísāsan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the possessor of opulence, directs downwards the car over which, intended (to receive sacrificial) viands, he presides; he proceeds unimpeded, the first of the gods, driving (his enemies before him), as a herdsman drives the herds of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the possessor of opulence, directs downwards the car over which, intended (to receive sacrificial) viands, he presides; he proceeds unimpeded, the first of the gods, driving (his enemies before him), as a herdsman drives the herds of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ प्र द्रव हरिवो मा वि वेनः पिशंगराते अभि नः सचस्व ।नहि त्वदिंद्र वस्यो अन्यदस्त्यमेनांश्चिज्जनिवतश्चकर्थ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ prá ǀ drava ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ venaḥ ǀ píśaṅga-rāte ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ sacasva ǀnahí ǀ tvát ǀ indra ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ anyát ǀ ásti ǀ amenā́n ǀ cit ǀ jáni-vataḥ ǀ cakartha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hasten to us, lord of horses; be not indifferent to us; distributor of manifold wealth, befriend us; for there is nothing else that is better,Indra, than you; you have given wives to those who were without women.
verses.wilson_translation: Hasten to us, lord of horses; be not indifferent to us; distributor of manifold wealth, befriend us; for there is nothing else that is better,Indra, than you; you have given wives to those who were without women.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उद्यत्सहः सहस आजनिष्ट देदिष्ट इंद्र इंद्रियाणि विश्वा ।प्राचोदयत्सुदुघा वव्रे अंतर्वि ज्योतिषा संववृत्वत्तमोऽवः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ yát ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ájaniṣṭa ǀ dédiṣṭe ǀ índraḥ ǀ indriyā́ṇi ǀ víśvā ǀprá ǀ acodayat ǀ su-dúghāḥ ǀ vavré ǀ antáḥ ǀ ví ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ sam-vavṛtvát ǀ támaḥ ǀ avarítyavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the light (of the sun) overpowers the light (of the dawn)Indragrants all (sorts of) wealth (to the worshipper); he has liberated the kine from the interior of the obstructing (mountain); he dissipates the enveloping darkness with light.
verses.wilson_translation: When the light (of the sun) overpowers the light (of the dawn)Indragrants all (sorts of) wealth (to the worshipper); he has liberated the kine from the interior of the obstructing (mountain); he dissipates the enveloping darkness with light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनवस्ते रथमश्वाय तक्षंत्वष्टा वज्रं पुरुहूत द्युमंतं ।ब्रह्माण इंद्रं महयंतो अर्कैरवर्धयन्नहये हंतवा उ ॥
verses.transliteration: ánavaḥ ǀ te ǀ rátham ǀ áśvāya ǀ takṣan ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ vájram ǀ puru-hūta ǀ dyu-mántam ǀbrahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ índram ǀ maháyantaḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ ávardhayan ǀ áhaye ǀ hántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: TheṚbhushave fabricated your car,Indra, the invoked of many, adapted to its horses;Tvaṣṭā(had made) your radiant thunderbolt; the venerable (Aṅgirasas), praising Indra with hymns, have given him vigour for the destruction of Ahi.
verses.wilson_translation: TheṚbhushave fabricated your car,Indra, the invoked of many, adapted to its horses;Tvaṣṭā(had made) your radiant thunderbolt; the venerable (Aṅgirasas), praising Indra with hymns, have given him vigour for the destruction of Ahi.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृष्णे यत्ते वृषणो अर्कमर्चानिंद्र ग्रावाणो अदितिः सजोषाः ।अनश्वासो ये पवयोऽरथा इंद्रेषिता अभ्यवर्तंत दस्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ arkám ǀ árcān ǀ índra ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀanaśvā́saḥ ǀ yé ǀ paváyaḥ ǀ arathā́ḥ ǀ índra-iṣitāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ávartanta ǀ dásyūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the Maruts, the showerers (of benefits), glorify you,Indra, the showerer (of desires), with praises, and the exulting stones delight (to bruise the Soma), then, without horses, without chariots, they, the purifying (Maruts), dispatched by Indra, have overcome the Dasyus.
verses.wilson_translation: When the Maruts, the showerers (of benefits), glorify you,Indra, the showerer (of desires), with praises, and the exulting stones delight (to bruise the Soma), then, without horses, without chariots, they, the purifying (Maruts), dispatched by Indra, have overcome the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते पूर्वाणि करणानि वोचं प्र नूतना मघवन्या चकर्थ ।शक्तीवो यद्विभरा रोदसी उभे जयन्नपो मनवे दानुचित्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ pū́rvāṇi ǀ káraṇāni ǀ vocam ǀ prá ǀ nū́tanā ǀ magha-van ǀ yā́ ǀ cakártha ǀśákti-vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ vi-bhárāḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ jáyan ǀ apáḥ ǀ mánave ǀ dā́nu-citrāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I celebrate,Maghavan, your ancient exploits, and those which you have newly achieved; wielder of the thunderbolt, subjugating both heaven and earth, you have distributed the wonderfully bountiful waters to man.
