verses.english_translation: Offer praise to the company of the Maruts, the self-irradiating, the precipitators of mountains; present liberal oblations to the assuagers of heat, to those who come from the sky, to whom solemn rites are familiar, to the givers of abundant food.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer praise to the company of the Maruts, the self-irradiating, the precipitators of mountains; present liberal oblations to the assuagers of heat, to those who come from the sky, to whom solemn rites are familiar, to the givers of abundant food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो मरुतस्तविषा उदन्यवो वयोवृधो अश्वयुजः परिज्रयः ।सं विद्युता दधति वाशति त्रितः स्वरंत्यापोऽवना परिज्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ taviṣā́ḥ ǀ udanyávaḥ ǀ vayaḥ-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ aśva-yújaḥ ǀ pári-jrayaḥ ǀsám ǀ vi-dyútā ǀ dádhati ǀ vā́śati ǀ tritáḥ ǀ sváranti ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ avánā ǀ pári-jrayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your (cohort),Maruts, is conspicous, mighty shedding water and augmenting food; yoking your horse (to your cars), spreading everywhere, and combined with the lightning, the triple-stationed company roars aloud, and the circumambient waters fall upon the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Your (cohort),Maruts, is conspicous, mighty shedding water and augmenting food; yoking your horse (to your cars), spreading everywhere, and combined with the lightning, the triple-stationed company roars aloud, and the circumambient waters fall upon the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विद्युन्महसो नरो अश्मदिद्यवो वातत्विषो मरुतः पर्वतच्युतः ।अब्दया चिन्मुहुरा ह्रादुनीवृतः स्तनयदमा रभसा उदोजसः ॥
verses.transliteration: vidyút-mahasaḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ áśma-didyavaḥ ǀ vā́ta-tviṣaḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ parvata-cyútaḥ ǀabda-yā́ ǀ cit ǀ múhuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hrāduni-vṛ́taḥ ǀ stanáyat-amāḥ ǀ rabhasā́ḥ ǀ út-ojasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts(appear) radiant with lightning, leaders (of the rain), armed with weapons of adamant, blazing with the wind, the precipitators of mountains, the repeated distributors of water, wielders of the thunderbolt, roaring in concert, combining (to send rain), and of exceeding strength.
verses.wilson_translation: The Maruts(appear) radiant with lightning, leaders (of the rain), armed with weapons of adamant, blazing with the wind, the precipitators of mountains, the repeated distributors of water, wielders of the thunderbolt, roaring in concert, combining (to send rain), and of exceeding strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: व्यक्तून्रुद्रा व्यहानि शिक्वसो व्यंतरिक्षं वि रजांसि धूतयः ।वि यदज्राँ अजथ नाव ईं यथा वि दुर्गाणि मरुतो नाह रिष्यथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ aktū́n ǀ rudrāḥ ǀ ví ǀ áhāni ǀ śikvasaḥ ǀ ví ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ví ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ dhūtayaḥ ǀví ǀ yát ǀ ájrān ǀ ájatha ǀ nā́vaḥ ǀ īm ǀ yathā ǀ ví ǀ duḥ-gā́ni ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áha ǀ riṣyatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Powerful Rudras, you urge on the nights and days the firmament and the worlds; agitators (of all things), you toss the clouds like ships (in the sea), so (you throw down) the strong plural ces (of the enemy); but,Marutsyou do no harm.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Rudras, you urge on the nights and days the firmament and the worlds; agitators (of all things), you toss the clouds like ships (in the sea), so (you throw down) the strong plural ces (of the enemy); but,Marutsyou do no harm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वीर्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं ततान सूर्यो न योजनं ।एता न यामे अगृभीतशोचिषोऽनश्वदां यन्न्ययातना गिरिं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vīryám ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mahi-tvanám ǀ dīrghám ǀ tatāna ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yójanam ǀétāḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́me ǀ ágṛbhīta-śociṣaḥ ǀ ánaśva-dām ǀ yát ǀ ní ǀ áyātana ǀ girím ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your prowess,Maruts, has spread wide your glory as the sun (sends afar his) radiance, or the white (horses of the gods travel far) in their course; of unbounded lustre, you close the cloud withholding the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Your prowess,Maruts, has spread wide your glory as the sun (sends afar his) radiance, or the white (horses of the gods travel far) in their course; of unbounded lustre, you close the cloud withholding the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभ्राजि शर्धो मरुतो यदर्णसं मोषथा वृक्षं कपनेव वेधसः ।अध स्मा नो अरमतिं सजोषसश्चक्षुरिव यंतमनु नेषथा सुगं ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhrāji ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yát ǀ arṇasám ǀ móṣatha ǀ vṛkṣám ǀ kapanā́-iva ǀ vedhasaḥ ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ arámatim ǀ sa-joṣasaḥ ǀ cákṣuḥ-iva ǀ yántam ǀ ánu ǀ neṣatha ǀ su-gám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, dispensers of rain, your strength is manifested when, shaking the water-laden cloud, you let loose the shower; conjointly propitiated, conduct us by an easy path leading to prosperity, as the eye (shows the way).
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, dispensers of rain, your strength is manifested when, shaking the water-laden cloud, you let loose the shower; conjointly propitiated, conduct us by an easy path leading to prosperity, as the eye (shows the way).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न स जीयते मरुतो न हन्यते न स्रेधति न व्यथते न रिष्यति ।नास्य राय उप दस्यंति नोतय ऋषिं वा यं राजानं वा सुषूदथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ jīyate ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hanyate ǀ ná ǀ sredhati ǀ ná ǀ vyathate ǀ ná ǀ riṣyati ǀná ǀ asya ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dasyanti ǀ ná ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ vā ǀ yám ǀ rā́jānam ǀ vā ǀ súsūdatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sage, or the sovereign, whom you,Maruts, direct, is never overcome nor slain; he perishes not, nor suffers pain, nor undergoes injury, nor are his riches or his safety imperilled.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage, or the sovereign, whom you,Maruts, direct, is never overcome nor slain; he perishes not, nor suffers pain, nor undergoes injury, nor are his riches or his safety imperilled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नियुत्वंतो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽर्यमणो न मरुतः कबंधिनः ।पिन्वंत्युत्सं यदिनासो अस्वरन्व्युंदंति पृथिवीं मध्वो अंधसा ॥
verses.transliteration: niyútvantaḥ ǀ grāma-jítaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ náraḥ ǀ aryamáṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ marútaḥ ǀ kabandhínaḥ ǀpínvanti ǀ útsam ǀ yát ǀ inā́saḥ ǀ ásvaran ǀ ví ǀ undanti ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ándhasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lords of the Niyutsteeds, overcomers of multitudes leaders (of rites), radiant as theĀdityas, are the dispensers of water; when sovereign lords, they fill the clouds, and, loud sounding, moisten the earth with sweet (watery) sustenance.
verses.wilson_translation: Lords of the Niyutsteeds, overcomers of multitudes leaders (of rites), radiant as theĀdityas, are the dispensers of water; when sovereign lords, they fill the clouds, and, loud sounding, moisten the earth with sweet (watery) sustenance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रवत्वतीयं पृथिवी मरुद्भ्यः प्रवत्वती द्यौर्भवति प्रयद्भ्यः ।प्रवत्वतीः पथ्या अंतरिक्ष्याः प्रवत्वंतः पर्वता जीरदानवः ॥
verses.transliteration: pravátvatī ǀ iyám �� pṛthivī́ ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀ pravátvatī ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ prayát-bhyaḥ ǀpravátvatīḥ ǀ pathyā́ḥ ǀ antárikṣyāḥ ǀ pravátvantaḥ ǀ párvatāḥ ǀ jīrá-dānavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This wide-extended earth is for the Maruts; the spacious heaven is for the spreading winds; the paths of the firmament are provided (for their course); for them the expanding clouds quickly bestow (their gifts).
verses.wilson_translation: This wide-extended earth is for the Maruts; the spacious heaven is for the spreading winds; the paths of the firmament are provided (for their course); for them the expanding clouds quickly bestow (their gifts).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यन्मरुतः सभरसः स्वर्णरः सूर्य उदिते मदथा दिवो नरः ।न वोऽश्वाः श्रथयंताह सिस्रतः सद्यो अस्याध्वनः पारमश्नुथ ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ marutaḥ ǀ sa-bharasaḥ ǀ svaḥ-naraḥ ǀ sū́rye ǀ út-ite ǀ mádatha ǀ divaḥ ǀ naraḥ ǀná ǀ vaḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ śrathayanta ǀ áha ǀ sísrataḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ asyá ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ pārám ǀ aśnutha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Marutsof combined strength, leaders of the universe, guides of heaven, when the sun has risen you rejoice (in the Somabeverage), then your rapid steeds know no relaxation, but quickly you reach the limits of this road (to the sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: Marutsof combined strength, leaders of the universe, guides of heaven, when the sun has risen you rejoice (in the Somabeverage), then your rapid steeds know no relaxation, but quickly you reach the limits of this road (to the sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः ।अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ॥
verses.transliteration: áṃseṣu ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ pat-sú ǀ khādáyaḥ ǀ vákṣaḥ-su ǀ rukmā́ḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ráthe ǀ śúbhaḥ ǀagní-bhrājasaḥ ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀ śíprāḥ ǀ śīrṣá-su ǀ ví-tatāḥ ǀ hiraṇyáyīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lances (gleam),Maruts, upon your shoulders, anklets on your feet, golden cuirasses on your breasts, and pure (waters shine) in your chariots; lightning blazing with fire in yourhands, and golden tiarsa are towering on your heads.
verses.wilson_translation: Lances (gleam),Maruts, upon your shoulders, anklets on your feet, golden cuirasses on your breasts, and pure (waters shine) in your chariots; lightning blazing with fire in yourhands, and golden tiarsa are towering on your heads.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं नाकमर्यो अगृभीतशोचिषं रुशत्पिप्पलं मरुतो वि धूनुथ ।समच्यंत वृजनातित्विषंत यत्स्वरंति घोषं विततमृतायवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ nā́kam ǀ aryáḥ ǀ ágṛbhīta-śociṣam ǀ rúśat ǀ píppalam ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ví ǀ dhūnutha ǀsám ǀ acyanta ǀ vṛjánā ǀ átitviṣanta ǀ yát ǀ sváranti ǀ ghóṣam ǀ ví-tatam ǀ ṛta-yávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, when moving, you agitate the heaven of unchecked radiance, and (stir) the bright water; when you combine your energies and are shining brilliantly, and when purposing to send down rain, you utter a loud shout.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, when moving, you agitate the heaven of unchecked radiance, and (stir) the bright water; when you combine your energies and are shining brilliantly, and when purposing to send down rain, you utter a loud shout.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युष्मादत्तस्य मरुतो विचेतसो रायः स्याम रथ्यो वयस्वतः ।न यो युच्छति तिष्यो यथा दिवोऽस्मे रारंत मरुतः सहस्रिणं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuṣmā́-dattasya ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vi-cetasaḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ syāma ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ váyasvataḥ ǀná ǀ yáḥ ǀ yúcchati ǀ tiṣyáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ diváḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ raranta ǀ marutaḥ ǀ sahasríṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, who are possessed of chariots, intelligent Maruts, become (proprietors) of wealth, comprising food bestowed by you; of wealth that vanishes not, as Tiṣya(declines not) from the sky; therefore, Maruts, gratify us with infinite (riches).
verses.wilson_translation: May we, who are possessed of chariots, intelligent Maruts, become (proprietors) of wealth, comprising food bestowed by you; of wealth that vanishes not, as Tiṣya(declines not) from the sky; therefore, Maruts, gratify us with infinite (riches).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं रयिं मरुतः स्पार्हवीरं यूयमृषिमवथ सामविप्रं ।यूयमर्वंतं भरताय वाजं यूयं धत्थ राजानं श्रुष्टिमंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ rayím ǀ marutaḥ ǀ spārhá-vīram ǀ yūyám ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ avatha ǀ sā́ma-vipram ǀyūyám ǀ árvantam ǀ bharatā́ya ǀ vā́jam ǀ yūyám ǀ dhattha ǀ rā́jānam ǀ śruṣṭi-mántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: You bestow,Maruts, wealth and enviable posterity; you protect the sage learned in the Sāma; you grant horses and food to (me) the ministrant priest; you render a prince prosperous.
verses.wilson_translation: You bestow,Maruts, wealth and enviable posterity; you protect the sage learned in the Sāma; you grant horses and food to (me) the ministrant priest; you render a prince prosperous.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वो यामि द्रविणं सद्यऊतयो येना स्वर्ण ततनाम नॄँरभि ।इदं सु मे मरुतो हर्यता वचो यस्य तरेम तरसा शतं हिमाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ yāmi ǀ dráviṇam ǀ sadyaḥ-ūtayaḥ ǀ yéna ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ tatánāma ǀ nṝ́n ǀ abhí ǀidám ǀ sú ǀ me ǀ marutaḥ ǀ haryata ǀ vácaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ tárema ǀ tárasā ǀ śatám ǀ hímāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore do I solicit wealth of you, who are prompt to grant protection, whereby we may multiply our descendants, as the sun (spreads wide his rays); be propitiated,Maruts, by this my praise, by the efficacy whereof may we pass over a hundred winters.
verses.wilson_translation: Therefore do I solicit wealth of you, who are prompt to grant protection, whereby we may multiply our descendants, as the sun (spreads wide his rays); be propitiated,Maruts, by this my praise, by the efficacy whereof may we pass over a hundred winters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH gleaming lances, with their breasts adorned with gold, the Maruts, rushing onward, hold high power of life.They hasten with swift steeds easy to be controlled. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Ye, as ye wist, have gained of your own selves your power: high, O ye Mighty Ones, and wide ye shine abroad.They with their strength have even measured out the sky.Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Strong, born together, they together have waxed great: the Heroes more and more have grown to majestyResplendent as the Sun's beams in their light are they. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Maruts, your mightiness deserves to be adored, sight to be longed for like the shining of the Sun.So lead us with your aid to immortality.Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. O Maruts, from the Ocean ye uplift the rain, and fraught with vaporous moisture pour the torrents down.Never, ye Wonder-Workers, are your Milch-kine dry. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. When to your car-poles ye have yoked your spotted deer to be your steeds, and put your golden mantles on,O Maruts, ye disperse all enemies abroad. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Neither the mountains nor the rivers keep you back: whither ye have resolved thither ye, Maruts, go.Ye compass round about even the heaven and earth. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.Whate’er is ancient, Maruts, what of recent time, whate’er is spoken, Vasus, what is chanted forth,They who take cognizance of all of this are ye. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. Be gracious unto us, ye Maruts, slay us not extend ye unto us shelter of many a sort.Pay due regard unto our friendship and our praise. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory. O Maruts, lead us on to higher fortune deliver us, when lauded, from afflictions.Accept, ye Holy Ones, the gifts we bring you. May we be masters of abundant riches.

verses.sanskrit: प्रयज्यवो मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयो बृहद्वयो दधिरे रुक्मवक्षसः ।ईयंते अश्वैः सुयमेभिराशुभिः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: prá-yajyavaḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ rukmá-vakṣasaḥ ǀī́yante ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ su-yámebhiḥ ǀ āśú-bhiḥ ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The adorable Maruts, armed with bright lances and cuirassed with golden breast-plural tes, enjoy vigorous existence; may the ears of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: The adorable Maruts, armed with bright lances and cuirassed with golden breast-plural tes, enjoy vigorous existence; may the ears of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वयं दधिध्वे तविषीं यथा विद बृहन्महांत उर्विया वि राजथ ।उतांतरिक्षं ममिरे व्योजसा शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: svayám ǀ dadhidhve ǀ táviṣīm ǀ yáthā ǀ vidá ǀ bṛhát ǀ mahāntaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ rājatha ǀutá ǀ antárikṣam ǀ mamire ǀ ví ǀ ójasā ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, you have of yourselves maintained your vigour according as you judge (fit); you shine most mighty and vast, and you pervade the firmament with your power; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, you have of yourselves maintained your vigour according as you judge (fit); you shine most mighty and vast, and you pervade the firmament with your power; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: साकं जाताः सुभ्वः साकमुक्षिताः श्रिये चिदा प्रतरं वावृधुर्नरः ।विरोकिणः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: sākám ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ su-bhváḥ ǀ sākám ǀ ukṣitā́ḥ ǀ śriyé ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀvi-rokíṇaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya-iva ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Born simultaneously, mighty, co-dispensers of moisture, they have grown exceedingly in glory; leaders (of rites), and radiant (are they) as the rays of the sun; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Born simultaneously, mighty, co-dispensers of moisture, they have grown exceedingly in glory; leaders (of rites), and radiant (are they) as the rays of the sun; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आभूषेण्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दिदृक्षेण्यं सूर्यस्येव चक्षणं ।उतो अस्माँ अमृतत्वे दधातन शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-bhūṣéṇyam ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mahi-tvanám ǀ didṛkṣéṇyam ǀ sū́ryasya-iva ǀ cákṣaṇam ǀutó íti ǀ asmā́n ǀ amṛta-tvé ǀ dadhātana ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your might,Maruts, is to be glorified; it is to be contemplated like the orb of the sun; sustain us ever in immortality; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Your might,Maruts, is to be glorified; it is to be contemplated like the orb of the sun; sustain us ever in immortality; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतो यूयं वृष्टिं वर्षयथा पुरीषिणः ।न वो दस्रा उप दस्यंति धेनवः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrayatha ǀ marutaḥ ǀ samudratáḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ varṣayatha ǀ purīṣiṇaḥ ǀná ǀ vaḥ ǀ dasrāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dasyanti ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: You send (the rain),Maruts, from the firmament; charged with the waters you shower down the rain; destroyers of foes, your kine are never dry; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: You send (the rain),Maruts, from the firmament; charged with the waters you shower down the rain; destroyers of foes, your kine are never dry; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदश्वांधूर्षु पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं हिरण्ययान्प्रत्यत्काँ अमुग्ध्वं ।विश्वा इत्स्पृधो मरुतो व्यस्यथ शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ áśvān ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ pṛ́ṣatīḥ ǀ áyugdhvam ǀ hiraṇyáyān ǀ práti ǀ átkān ǀ ámugdhvam ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ ít ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ví ǀ asyatha ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you yoke your spotted mares to the poles (of your chariots), you lay aside your golden breast-plural tes, for you dissipate all hostility; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: When you yoke your spotted mares to the poles (of your chariots), you lay aside your golden breast-plural tes, for you dissipate all hostility; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न पर्वता न नद्यो वरंत वो यत्राचिध्वं मरुतो गच्छथेदु तत् ।उत द्यावापृथिवी याथना परि शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ párvatāḥ ǀ ná ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ varanta ǀ vaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ ácidhvam ǀ marutaḥ ǀ gácchatha ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tát ǀutá ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ yāthana ǀ pári ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the mountains, let not the rivers, arrest you; whither you purpose, (Maruts), thither repair, and compass heaven and earth; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the mountains, let not the rivers, arrest you; whither you purpose, (Maruts), thither repair, and compass heaven and earth; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्पूर्व्यं मरुतो यच्च नूतनं यदुद्यते वसवो यच्च शस्यते ।विश्वस्य तस्य भवथा नवेदसः शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ pūrvyám ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ nū́tanam ǀ yát ǀ udyáte ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ śasyáte ǀvíśvasya ǀ tásya ǀ bhavatha ǀ návedasaḥ ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever (rite has been addressed to you),Maruts, of old; whatever is recent; whatever (hymn) is recited,Vasus, whatever prayer is repeated, do you be cognizant of all; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever (rite has been addressed to you),Maruts, of old; whatever is recent; whatever (hymn) is recited,Vasus, whatever prayer is repeated, do you be cognizant of all; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मृळत नो मरुतो मा वधिष्टनास्मभ्यं शर्म बहुलं वि यंतन ।अधि स्तोत्रस्य सख्यस्य गातन शुभं यातामनु रथा अवृत्सत ॥
verses.transliteration: mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ vadhiṣṭana ǀ asmábhyam ǀ śárma ǀ bahulám ǀ ví ǀ yantana ǀádhi ǀ stotrásya ǀ sakhyásya ǀ gātana ǀ śúbham ǀ yātā́m ǀ ánu ǀ ráthāḥ ǀ avṛtsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send us felicity,Maruts, harm us not; bestow upon us exceeding happiness; reward our adoration by your friendship; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Send us felicity,Maruts, harm us not; bestow upon us exceeding happiness; reward our adoration by your friendship; may the cars of the quick-moving (Maruts) arrive for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयमस्मान्नयत वस्यो अच्छा निरंहतिभ्यो मरुतो गृणानाः ।जुषध्वं नो हव्यदातिं यजत्रा वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ asmā́n ǀ nayata ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ áccha ǀ níḥ ǀ aṃhatí-bhyaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ gṛṇānā́ḥ ǀjuṣádhvam ǀ naḥ ǀ havyá-dātim ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀ vayám ǀ syāma ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you,Maruts, conduct us to opulence; propitiated by our praises, extricate us from sin; accept, adorable (Maruts), our offered oblation, and may we be the possessors of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Maruts, conduct us to opulence; propitiated by our praises, extricate us from sin; accept, adorable (Maruts), our offered oblation, and may we be the possessors of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, that valorous company adorned with ornaments of gold,The people of the Maruts, I call down to-day even from the luminous realm of heaven. Even as thou thinkest in thy heart, thither my wishes also tend.Those who have come most near to thine invoking calls, strengthen them fearful to behold. Earth, like a bounteous lady, liberal of her gifts, struck down and shaken, yet exultant, comes to us.Impetuous as a bear, O Maruts, is youi rush terrible as a dreadful bull.. They who with mighty strength o’erthrow like oxen difficult to yoke,Cause e’en the heavenly stone to shake ' yea, shake the rocky mountain as they race along. Rise up! even now with lauds I call the very numerous company,Unequalled, of these Maruts, like a herd of kine, grown up together in their strength. Bind to your car the bright red mares, yoke the red coursers to your car.Bind to the pole, to draw, the fleet-foot tawny steeds, the best at drawing, to the pole. Yea, and this loudly-neighing bright red vigorous horse who hath been sutioned, fair to see,Let him not cause delay, O Maruts,, in your course, urge ye him onward in your cars. The Maruts’ chariot, ever fain to gather glory, we invoke,Which Rodasī hath mounted, bringing pleasant gifts, with Maruts in her company. I call that brilliant band of yours, adorable, rapid on the carWhereon the bounteous Dame, auspicious, nobly born, shows glorious with the Marut host.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने शर्धंतमा गणं पिष्टं रुक्मेभ���रंजिभिः ।विशो अद्य मरुतामव ह्वये दिवश्चिद्रोचनादधि ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ śárdhantam ǀ ā́ ǀ gaṇám ǀ piṣṭám ǀ rukmébhiḥ ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀvíśaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ marútām ǀ áva ǀ hvaye ǀ diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ rocanā́t ǀ ádhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke,Agni, the victorious company (of the Maruts) decorated with brilliant ornaments; (I invoke them), the people of the Maruts, to descend today from above the shining heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke,Agni, the victorious company (of the Maruts) decorated with brilliant ornaments; (I invoke them), the people of the Maruts, to descend today from above the shining heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा चिन्मन्यसे हृदा तदिन्मे जग्मुराशसः ।ये ते नेदिष्ठं हवनान्यागमंतान्वर्ध भीमसंदृशः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ cit ǀ mányase ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ me ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ ā-śásaḥ ǀyé ǀ te ǀ nédiṣṭham ǀ hávanāni ǀ ā-gáman ǀ tā́n ǀ vardha ǀ bhīmá-sandṛśaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In whatever manner you honour the (Maruts,Agni) in your heart, may they come to me as benefactors; gratify, (by oblations), those fierce-looking Maruts, who most promptly come to your invocations.
verses.wilson_translation: In whatever manner you honour the (Maruts,Agni) in your heart, may they come to me as benefactors; gratify, (by oblations), those fierce-looking Maruts, who most promptly come to your invocations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मीळ्हुष्मतीव पृथिवी पराहता मदंत्येत्यस्मदा ।ऋक्षो न वो मरुतः शिमीवाँ अमो दुध्रो गौरिव भीमयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: mīḷhúṣmatī-iva ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ párā-hatā ǀ mádantī ǀ eti ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ śímī-vān ǀ ámaḥ ǀ dudhráḥ ǀ gáuḥ-iva ǀ bhīma-yúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the (people of the) earth having a powerful lord have recourse to him when oppressed (by others), so comes (the host of the Maruts) exulting to us; your company, Maruts, active as fire, is as difficult to be resisted as a formidable ox.
verses.wilson_translation: As the (people of the) earth having a powerful lord have recourse to him when oppressed (by others), so comes (the host of the Maruts) exulting to us; your company, Maruts, active as fire, is as difficult to be resisted as a formidable ox.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि ये रिणंत्योजसा वृथा गावो न दुर्धुरः ।अश्मानं चित्स्वर्यं पर्वतं गिरिं प्र च्यावयंति यामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ yé ǀ riṇánti ǀ ójasā ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-dhúraḥ ǀáśmānam ǀ cit ǀ svaryám ǀ párvatam ǀ girím ǀ prá ǀ cyavayanti ǀ yā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who with ease destroy (their foes) by their prowess, like horses difficult to be restrained, they send down by their movements the vast and sounding water-laden cloud.
verses.wilson_translation: They who with ease destroy (their foes) by their prowess, like horses difficult to be restrained, they send down by their movements the vast and sounding water-laden cloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ नूनमेषां स्तोमैः समुक्षितानां ।मरुतां पुरुतममपूर्व्यं गवां सर्गमिव ह्वये ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ nūnám ǀ eṣām ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ sám-ukṣitānām ǀmarútām ǀ puru-támam ǀ ápūrvyam ǀ gávām ǀ sárgam-iva ǀ hvaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rise up (Maruts); verily by my praises I invoke the mighty and unpreceded (troop) of these exalted (maruts) like a heap of waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise up (Maruts); verily by my praises I invoke the mighty and unpreceded (troop) of these exalted (maruts) like a heap of waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युंग्ध्वं ह्यरुषी रथे युंग्ध्वं रथेषु रोहितः ।युंग्ध्वं हरी अजिरा धुरि वोळ्हवे वहिष्ठा धुरि वोळ्हवे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuṅgdhvám ǀ hí ǀ áruṣīḥ ǀ ráthe ǀ yuṅgdhvám ǀ rátheṣu ǀ rohítaḥ ǀyuṅgdhvám ǀ hárī íti ǀ ajirā́ ǀ dhurí ǀ vóḷhave ǀ váhiṣṭhā ǀ dhurí ǀ vóḷhave ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yoke the bright steeds to the car, yoke the red steeds to the cars; yoke the swift pair of horses to bear the burden; the strong bearing to bear the burden.
verses.wilson_translation: Yoke the bright steeds to the car, yoke the red steeds to the cars; yoke the swift pair of horses to bear the burden; the strong bearing to bear the burden.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्य वाज्यरुषस्तुविष्वणिरिह स्म धायि दर्शतः ।मा वो यामेषु मरुतश्चिरं करत्प्र तं रथेषु चोदत ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ tuvi-svániḥ ǀ ihá ǀ sma ǀ dhāyi ǀ darśatáḥ ǀmā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ yā́meṣu ǀ marutaḥ ǀ cirám ǀ karat ǀ prá ǀ tám ǀ rátheṣu ǀ codata ǁ
verses.english_translation: And let not that horse, bright-shining, loud-neighing, of graceful form, who has been plural ced (in harness), delay you,Maruts, on your journey; urge him on in the car.
verses.wilson_translation: And let not that horse, bright-shining, loud-neighing, of graceful form, who has been plural ced (in harness), delay you,Maruts, on your journey; urge him on in the car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे ।आ यस्मिंतस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ nú ǀ mā́rutam ǀ vayám ǀ śravasyúm ǀ ā́ ǀ huvāmahe ǀā́ ǀ yásmin ǀ tastháu ǀ suráṇāni ǀ bíbhratī ǀ sácā ǀ marút-su ǀ rodasī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke the food-laden chariot of the Maruts, in which Rodasistood with the Maruts, bearing the delicious (waters).
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke the food-laden chariot of the Maruts, in which Rodasistood with the Maruts, bearing the delicious (waters).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं वः शर्धं रथेशुभं त्वेषं पनस्युमा हुवे ।यस्मिन्त्सुजाता सुभगा महीयते सचा मरुत्सु मीळ्हुषी ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárdham ǀ rathe-śúbham ǀ tveṣám ǀ panasyúm ǀ ā́ ǀ huve ǀyásmin ǀ sú-jātā ǀ su-bhágā ǀ mahīyáte ǀ sácā ǀ marút-su ǀ mīḷhuṣī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke that, your cohort, gracing the chariot, brilliant and adorable, amidst which the rain-bestowing (goddess), of goodly origin and auspicious, is worshipped together with the Maruts.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke that, your cohort, gracing the chariot, brilliant and adorable, amidst which the rain-bestowing (goddess), of goodly origin and auspicious, is worshipped together with the Maruts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . OF one accord, with Indra, O ye Rudras, come borne on your golden car for our prosperity.An offering from us, this hymn is brought to you, as, unto one who th irsts for water, heavenly springs. Armed with your daggers, full of wisdom, armed with spears, armed with your quivers, armed with arrows, with good bows,Good horses and good cars have ye, O Pṛśni's Sons: ye, Maruts, with good weapons go to victory. From hills and heaven ye shake wealth for the worshipper: in terror at your coming low the woods bow down.Ye make the earth to tremble, Sons of Pṛśni, when for victory ye have yoked, fierce Ones! your spotted deer. Bright with the blasts of wind, wrapped in their robes of rain, like twins of noble aspect and of lovely form,The Maruts, spotless, with steeds tawnyhued and red, strong in their mightiness and spreading wide like heaven. Rich in adornment, rich in drops, munificent, bright in their aspect, yielding bounties that endure,Noble by birth, adorned with gold upon their breasts, the Singers of the sky have won immortal fame. Borne on both shoulders, O ye Maruts, are your spears: within your arms is laid your energy and trength.Bold thoughts are in your heads, your weapons in your cars, all glorious majesty is moulded on your forms. Vouchsafe to us, O Maruts, splendid bounty in cattle and in steeds, in cars and heroes.Children of Rudra, give us high distinction: may I enjoy your Godlike help and favour. Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

verses.sanskrit: आ रुद्रास इंद्रवंतः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गंतन ।इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ rudrāsaḥ ǀ índra-vantaḥ ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ híraṇya-rathāḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ gantana ǀiyám ǀ vaḥ ǀ asmát ǀ práti ǀ haryate ǀ matíḥ ǀ tṛṣṇá-je ǀ ná ǀ diváḥ ǀ útsāḥ ǀ udanyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rudras, servants of Indra, mutually kind, riding in golden cars, come to the accessible (sacrifice); this our praise is addressed to you; (come to us as you came) from heaven, (bringing) oozing water to the thirsty (Gotama) longing for moisture.
verses.wilson_translation: Rudras, servants of Indra, mutually kind, riding in golden cars, come to the accessible (sacrifice); this our praise is addressed to you; (come to us as you came) from heaven, (bringing) oozing water to the thirsty (Gotama) longing for moisture.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वाशीमंत ऋष्टिमंतो मनीषिणः सुधन्वान इषुमंतो निषंगिणः ।स्वश्वाः स्थ सुरथाः पृश्निमातरः स्वायुधा मरुतो याथना शुभं ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́śī-mantaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭi-mántaḥ ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀ su-dhánvānaḥ ǀ íṣu-mantaḥ ǀ niṣaṅgíṇaḥ ǀsu-áśvāḥ ǀ stha ǀ su-ráthāḥ ǀ pṛśni-mātaraḥ ǀ su-āyudhā́ḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ yāthana ǀ śúbham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Intelligent Maruts, you are armed with swords, with lances, with bows with arrows, with quivers; you are well mounted and have handsome chariots; sons of Pṛṣṇiyou are well armed; come for our good.
verses.wilson_translation: Intelligent Maruts, you are armed with swords, with lances, with bows with arrows, with quivers; you are well mounted and have handsome chariots; sons of Pṛṣṇiyou are well armed; come for our good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धूनुथ द्यां पर्वतांदाशुषे वसु नि वो वना जिहते यामनो भिया ।कोपयथ पृथिवीं पृश्निमातरः शुभे यदुग्राः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhūnuthá ǀ dyā́m ǀ párvatān ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vásu ǀ ní ǀ vaḥ ǀ vánā ǀ jihate ǀ yā́manaḥ ǀ bhiyā́ ǀkopáyatha ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ pṛśni-mātaraḥ ǀ śubhé ǀ yát ǀ ugrāḥ ǀ pṛ́ṣatīḥ ǀ áyugdhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: You agitate the clouds in the sky; (you give) wealth to the donor (of oblations); through fear of your approach the forests bow down; sons of Pṛṣṇi, you incense the earth when, for the purpose of (sending) water, you, fierce (Maruts), yoke your spotted steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: You agitate the clouds in the sky; (you give) wealth to the donor (of oblations); through fear of your approach the forests bow down; sons of Pṛṣṇi, you incense the earth when, for the purpose of (sending) water, you, fierce (Maruts), yoke your spotted steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वातत्विषो मरुतो वर्षनिर्णिजो यमा इव सुसदृशः सुपेशसः ।पिशंगाश्वा अरुणाश्वा अरेपसः प्रत्वक्षसो महिना द्यौरिवोरवः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́ta-tviṣaḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ varṣá-nirnijaḥ ǀ yamā́ḥ-iva ǀ sú-sadṛśaḥ ǀ su-péśasaḥ ǀpiśáṅga-aśvāḥ ǀ aruṇá-aśvāḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǀ prá-tvakṣasaḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ dyáuḥ-iva ǀ urávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Maruts, radiant with light, purifiers of the rain, like twins of goodly aspect and graceful form, masters of tawny and of ruddy steeds, devoid of guile, thinners (of foes) and vast in magnitude as the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: The Maruts, radiant with light, purifiers of the rain, like twins of goodly aspect and graceful form, masters of tawny and of ruddy steeds, devoid of guile, thinners (of foes) and vast in magnitude as the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुद्रप्सा अंजिमंतः सुदानवस्त्वेषसंदृशो अनवभ्रराधसः ।सुजातासो जनुषा रुक्मवक्षसो दिवो अर्का अमृतं नाम भेजिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-drapsā́ḥ ǀ añji-mántaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ tveṣá-sandṛśaḥ ǀ anavabhrá-rādhasaḥ ǀsu-jātā́saḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ rukmá-vakṣasaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ arkā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ nā́ma ǀ bhejire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shedders of abundant showers, wearers of ornaments, munificent, of brilliant aspect, of inexhaustible wealth well descendent by birth, wearing golden breast-plural tes, entitled to adoration, (coming) from heaven, accept teḥ ambrosial oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Shedders of abundant showers, wearers of ornaments, munificent, of brilliant aspect, of inexhaustible wealth well descendent by birth, wearing golden breast-plural tes, entitled to adoration, (coming) from heaven, accept teḥ ambrosial oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋष्टयो वो मरुतो अंसयोरधि सह ओजो बाह्वोर्वो बलं हितं ।नृम्णा शीर्षस्वायुधा रथेषु वो विश्वा वः श्रीरधि तनूषु पिपिशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ áṃsayoḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ bálam ǀ hitám ǀnṛmṇā́ ǀ śīrṣá-su ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ rátheṣu ǀ vaḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ vaḥ ǀ śrī́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ pipiśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lances rest,Maruts, upon your shoulders; strength (of) foes-destroying power is seated in your arms; golden (tiaras) are on your heads, weapons are plural ced in your chariots, all glory is assembled in your limbs.
verses.wilson_translation: Lances rest,Maruts, upon your shoulders; strength (of) foes-destroying power is seated in your arms; golden (tiaras) are on your heads, weapons are plural ced in your chariots, all glory is assembled in your limbs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गोमदश्वावद्रथवत्सुवीरं चंद्रवद्राधो मरुतो ददा नः ।प्रशस्तिं नः कृणुत रुद्रियासो भक्षीय वोऽवसो दैव्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: gó-mat ǀ áśva-vat ǀ rátha-vat ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ candrá-vat ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ dada ǀ naḥ ǀprá-śastim ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ rudriyāsaḥ ǀ bhakṣīyá ǀ vaḥ ǀ ávasaḥ ǀ dáivyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, bestow upon us affluence, comprehending cattle, horses, cars, treasure, andmaledescendants; sons of Rudra, grant us distinction; may I ever enjoy your divine protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, bestow upon us affluence, comprehending cattle, horses, cars, treasure, andmaledescendants; sons of Rudra, grant us distinction; may I ever enjoy your divine protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तुवीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः ।सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बृहद्गिरयो बृहदुक्षमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: hayé ǀ náraḥ ǀ márutaḥ ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǀ túvi-maghāsaḥ ǀ ámṛtāḥ ǀ ṛ́ta-jñāḥ ǀsátya-śrutaḥ ǀ kávayaḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ bṛ́hat-girayaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ ukṣámāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ho,Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified, and worshipped with copious oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Ho,Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified, and worshipped with copious oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now do I glorify their mighty cohort, the company of these the youthful Maruts,Who ride impetuous on with rapid horses, and radiant in themselves, are Lords of Amṛta. The mighty glittering band, arm-bound with bracelets, givers of bliss, unmeasured in their greatness,With magical powers, bountiful, ever-roaring,—these, liberal Heroes, venerate thou singer. This day may all your water-bringers, Maruts, they who impel the falling rain, approach us.This fire, O Maruts, hath been duly kindled; let it find favour with you, youthful Sages. Ye raise up for the folk an active ruler whom, Holy Ones! a Master's hand hath fashioned.Ye send the fighter hand to hand, armmighty, and the brave hero, Maruts with good horses. They spring forth more and more, strong in their glories, like days, like spokes where none are last in order.Highest and mightiest are the Sons of Pṛśni. Firm to their own intention cling the Maruts. When ye have hastened on with spotted coursers, O Maruts, on your cars with strong-wrought fellies,The waters are disturbed, the woods are shattered. Let Dyaus the Red Steer send his thunder downward. Even Earth hath spread herself wide at their coming, and they as husbands have with power impregned her.They to the pole have yoked the winds for coursers: their sweat have they made rain, these Sons of Rudra. Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

verses.sanskrit: तमु नूनं तविषीमंतमेषां स्तुषे गणं मारुतं नव्यसीनां ।य आश्वश्वा अमवद्वहंत उतेशिरे अमृतस्य स्वराजः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nūnám ǀ táviṣī-mantam ǀ eṣām ǀ stuṣé ǀ gaṇám ǀ mā́rutam ǀ návyasīnām ǀyé ǀ āśú-aśvāḥ ǀ áma-vat ǀ váhante ǀ utá ǀ īśire ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ sva-rā́jaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I praise today that brilliant company of the adorable Maruts, lords of swift horses, who pass along in strength, who, self-radiant, preside over the ambrosial rain.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise today that brilliant company of the adorable Maruts, lords of swift horses, who pass along in strength, who, self-radiant, preside over the ambrosial rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वेषं गणं तवसं खादिहस्तं धुनिव्रतं मायिनं दा���िवारं ।मयोभुवो ये अमिता महित्वा वंदस्व विप्र तुविराधसो नॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tveṣám ǀ gaṇám ǀ tavásam ǀ khā́di-hastam ǀ dhúni-vratam ǀ māyínam ǀ dā́ti-vāram ǀmayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ámitāḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ vándasva ǀ vipra ǀ tuvi-rā́dhasaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adore, priest, the resplendent and powerful company, whose arms (are decorated) with bracelets, whose function is the agitation (of the trees), who are wise, and by whom wealth is conferred; they who are bestowers of felicity, whose greatness is unbounded; glorify the opulent leaders (of rites).
verses.wilson_translation: Adore, priest, the resplendent and powerful company, whose arms (are decorated) with bracelets, whose function is the agitation (of the trees), who are wise, and by whom wealth is conferred; they who are bestowers of felicity, whose greatness is unbounded; glorify the opulent leaders (of rites).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो यंतूदवाहासो अद्य वृष्टिं ये विश्वे मरुतो जुनंति ।अयं यो अग्निर्मरुतः समिद्ध एतं जुषध्वं कवयो युवानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ uda-vāhā́saḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ yé ǀ víśve ǀ marútaḥ ǀ junánti ǀayám ǀ yáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ etám ǀ juṣadhvam ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ yuvānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the universal Maruts, who urge on the rain, come to you today laden with water; Maruts, who are wise and young, be plural ased by this fire which is kindled for you.
verses.wilson_translation: May the universal Maruts, who urge on the rain, come to you today laden with water; Maruts, who are wise and young, be plural ased by this fire which is kindled for you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं राजानमिर्यं जनाय विभ्वतष्टं जनयथा यजत्राः ।युष्मदेति मुष्टिहा बाहुजूतो युष्मत्सदश्वो मरुतः सुवीरः ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ rā́jānam ǀ íryam ǀ jánāya ǀ vibhva-taṣṭám ǀ janayatha ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀyuṣmát ǀ eti ǀ muṣṭi-hā́ ǀ bāhú-jūtaḥ ǀ yuṣmát ǀ sát-aśvaḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adorable Maruts, you cause (a son) to be born to the man (who worships you), a ruler, an over-comer of foes, and modelled by Vibhvan; from you, Maruts, comes a valiant descendant, strong-fisted, mighty armed; from you (he acquires) an excellent steed.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Maruts, you cause (a son) to be born to the man (who worships you), a ruler, an over-comer of foes, and modelled by Vibhvan; from you, Maruts, comes a valiant descendant, strong-fisted, mighty armed; from you (he acquires) an excellent steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अरा इवेदचरमा अहेव प्रप्र जायंते अकवा महोभिः ।पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ॥
verses.transliteration: arā́ḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ ácaramāḥ ǀ áhā-iva ǀ prá-pra ǀ jāyante ǀ ákavāḥ ǀ máhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀpṛ́śneḥ ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ upa-mā́saḥ ǀ rábhiṣṭhāḥ ǀ sváyā ǀ matyā́ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sám ǀ mimikṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like the spokes of a wheel, none (of you) are inferior (to the rest), but equal as days (of like duration); the sons of Pṛṣṇiare born all alike, none inferior in splendour; rapid in speed, the Maruts, of their own free favour send down (the rains).
verses.wilson_translation: Like the spokes of a wheel, none (of you) are inferior (to the rest), but equal as days (of like duration); the sons of Pṛṣṇiare born all alike, none inferior in splendour; rapid in speed, the Maruts, of their own free favour send down (the rains).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्प्रायासिष्ट पृषतीभिरश्वैर्वीळुपविभिर्मरुतो रथेभिः ।क्षोदंत आपो रिणते वनान्यवोस्रियो वृषभः क्रंदतु द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ prá ǀ áyāsiṣṭa ǀ pṛ́ṣatībhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ vīḷupaví-bhiḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ráthebhiḥ ǀkṣódante ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ riṇaté ǀ vánāni ǀ áva ǀ usríyaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ krandatu ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When,Maruts, you come with stout-axled cars drawn by spotted steeds, then the waters descend, the forests are damaged,a nd the bright showerer (of the rain), influenced by the solar rays, may emit a downward sound.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Maruts, you come with stout-axled cars drawn by spotted steeds, then the waters descend, the forests are damaged,a nd the bright showerer (of the rain), influenced by the solar rays, may emit a downward sound.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रथिष्ट यामन्पृथिवी चिदेषां भर्तेव गर्भं स्वमिच्छवो धुः ।वातान्ह्यश्वांधुर्यायुयुज्रे वर्षं स्वेदं चक्रिरे रुद्रियासः ॥
verses.transliteration: práthiṣṭa ǀ yā́man ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ cit ǀ eṣām ǀ bhártā-iva ǀ gárbham ǀ svám ǀ ít ǀ śávaḥ ǀ dhuḥ ǀvā́tān ǀ hí ǀ áśvān ǀ dhurí ǀ ā-yuyujré ǀ varṣám ǀ svédam ǀ cakrire ǀ rudríyāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: On their approach the earth becomes capable of fertility, and they deposit in her water as their germ, as the husband genitive rates the embryo of the child; they have harnessed their horses fleet as the wind; the sons of Rudrahave emitted their person iration, (the rain).
verses.wilson_translation: On their approach the earth becomes capable of fertility, and they deposit in her water as their germ, as the husband genitive rates the embryo of the child; they have harnessed their horses fleet as the wind; the sons of Rudrahave emitted their person iration, (the rain).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हये नरो मरुतो मृळता नस्तुवीमघासो अमृता ऋतज्ञाः ।सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बृहद्गिरयो बृहदुक्षमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: hayé ǀ náraḥ ǀ márutaḥ ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǀ túvi-maghāsaḥ ǀ ámṛtāḥ ǀ ṛ́ta-jñāḥ ǀsátya-śrutaḥ ǀ kávayaḥ ǀ yúvānaḥ ǀ bṛ́hat-girayaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ ukṣámāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ho,Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified, and worshipped with copious oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Ho,Maruts, leaders (of rites), be propitious to us, you who are infinitely opulent, immortal, shedders of rain, renowned for truth, wise, young, greatly glorified, and worshipped with copious oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIX. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YOUR spy hath called to you to give prosperity. I sing to Heaven and Earth and offer sacrifice.They bathe their steeds and hasten through the firmament: they spread abroad their radiance through the sea of cloud. Earth shakes and reels in terror at their onward rush, like a full ship which, quivering, lets the water in.Marked on their ways are they, visible from afar: the Heroes press between in mighty armament. As the exalted horn of bulls for splendid might, as the Sun's eye set in the firmament's expanse,Like vigorous horses ye are beauteous to behold, and for your glory show like bridegrooms, O ye Men. Who, O ye Maruts, may attain the mighty lore of you the mighty, who may reach your manly deeds?Ye, verily, make earth tremble like a ray of light what time ye bring your boons to give prosperity, Like steeds of ruddy colour, scions of one race, as foremost champions they have battled in the van.The Heroes have waxed strong like we.grown manly youths; with floods of rain they make the Sun's eye fade away, Having no eldest and no youngest in their band, no middlomost, preeminent they have waxed in might,These Sons of Pṛśni, sprung of noble ancestry: come hitberward to us, ye bridegrooms of the sky. Like birds of air they flew with might in lengthened lines from heaven's high ridges to the borders of the sky.The steeds who carry them, as Gods and mortals know, have caused the waters of the mounuains to desGend. May Dyaus, the Infinite, roar for our banquet: may Dawns toil for us, glittering with moisture.Lauded by thee, these Maruts, Sons o Rudra, O Ṛṣi, have sent down the heavenly treasure.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वः स्पळक्रन्त्सुविताय दावनेऽर्चा दिवे प्र पृथिव्या ऋतं भरे ।उक्षंते अश्वांतरुषंत आ रजोऽनु स्वं भानुं श्रथयंते अर्णवैः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ spáṭ ǀ akran ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ dāváne ǀ árca ǀ divé ǀ prá ǀ pṛthivyái ǀ ṛtám ǀ bhare ǀukṣánte ǀ áśvān ǀ táruṣante ǀ ā́ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ svám ǀ bhānúm ǀ śrathayante ǀ arṇaváiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The priest glorifies you,Maruts, for the good of the donor of the oblation; offer worship to the shining (heaven); I bring offerings to the earth; they, the Maruts, scatter the rapid (rain); they traverse the firmament; they combine their own radiance with (that of) the clouds.
verses.wilson_translation: The priest glorifies you,Maruts, for the good of the donor of the oblation; offer worship to the shining (heaven); I bring offerings to the earth; they, the Maruts, scatter the rapid (rain); they traverse the firmament; they combine their own radiance with (that of) the clouds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अमादेषां भियसा भूमिरेजति नौर्न पूर्णा क्षरति व्यथिर्यती ।दूरेदृशो ये चितयंत एमभिरंतर्महे विदथे येतिरे नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ámāt ǀ eṣām ǀ bhiyásā ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ ejati ǀ náuḥ ǀ ná ǀ pūrṇā́ ǀ kṣarati ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀ yatī́ ǀdūre-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ yé ǀ citáyante ǀ éma-bhiḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ mahé ǀ vidáthe ǀ yetire ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From their approach, the earth trembles with fear as a crowded boat goes quivering (through the water) visible from afar, they are recognized by their movements; the Maruts, leaders (of rites), pass between (heaven and earth) to the solemn sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: From their approach, the earth trembles with fear as a crowded boat goes quivering (through the water) visible from afar, they are recognized by their movements; the Maruts, leaders (of rites), pass between (heaven and earth) to the solemn sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गवामिव श्रियसे शृंगमुत्तमं सूर्यो न चक्षू रजसो विसर्जने ।अत्या इव सुभ्वश्चारवः स्थन मर्या इव श्रियसे चेतथा नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: gávām-iva ǀ śriyáse ǀ śṛ́ṅgam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-sárjane ǀátyāḥ-iva ǀ su-bhváḥ ǀ cā́ravaḥ ǀ sthana ǀ máryāḥ-iva ǀ śriyáse ǀ cetatha ǀ naraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You bear, for your decoration, an excellent (diadem) like the horn of cattle; as the sun, the eye (of day, dispenses light), so (are you diligent) in the distribution of the rains; graceful are you, and rapid as horses, and like (pious) mortals, you, leaders (of rites), consider (holy ceremonies) for their glory.
verses.wilson_translation: You bear, for your decoration, an excellent (diadem) like the horn of cattle; as the sun, the eye (of day, dispenses light), so (are you diligent) in the distribution of the rains; graceful are you, and rapid as horses, and like (pious) mortals, you, leaders (of rites), consider (holy ceremonies) for their glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को वो महांति महतामुदश्नवत्कस्काव्या मरुतः को ह पौंस्या ।यूयं ह भूमिं किरणं न रेजथ प्र यद्भरध्वे सुविताय दावने ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ mahā́nti ǀ mahatā́m ǀ út ǀ aśnavat ǀ káḥ ǀ kā́vyā ǀ marutaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ ha ǀ páuṃsyā ǀyūyám ǀ ha ǀ bhū́mim ǀ kiráṇam ǀ ná ǀ rejatha ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ bháradhve ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ dāváne ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who may exalt the great excellences of you who are adorable? who may (offer you fitting) praises? who (glorify your) manly (deeds)? For you make the earth tremble like a ray (of light) when you confer the gift (of rain) for (the diffusion of) fertility.
verses.wilson_translation: Who may exalt the great excellences of you who are adorable? who may (offer you fitting) praises? who (glorify your) manly (deeds)? For you make the earth tremble like a ray (of light) when you confer the gift (of rain) for (the diffusion of) fertility.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वा इवेदरुषासः सबंधवः शूरा इव प्रयुधः प्रोत युयुधुः ।मर्या इव सुवृधो वावृधुर्नरः सूर्यस्य चक्षुः प्र मिनंति वृष्टिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvāḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ sá-bandhavaḥ ǀ śū́rāḥ-iva ǀ pra-yúdhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ utá ǀ yuyudhuḥ ǀmáryāḥ-iva ǀ su-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ prá ǀ minanti ǀ vṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent as steeds, of one kindred, they engage in combat like valiant heroes; like (prosperous) men, they, the leaders (of rites), have increased (in power), and cover the eye of the sun with showers.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent as steeds, of one kindred, they engage in combat like valiant heroes; like (prosperous) men, they, the leaders (of rites), have increased (in power), and cover the eye of the sun with showers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते अज्येष्ठा अकनिष्ठास उद्भिदोऽमध्यमासो महसा वि वावृधुः ।सुजातासो जनुषा पृश्निमातरो दिवो मर्या आ नो अच्छा जिगातन ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ajyeṣṭhā́ḥ ǀ ákaniṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ ut-bhídaḥ ǀ ámadhyamāsaḥ ǀ máhasā ǀ ví ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀsu-jātā́saḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ máryāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ áccha ǀ jigātana ǁ
verses.english_translation: None of them are older, none younger (than the others); the destroyers of (foes), none hold a middle (rank), but all excel in glory; honourable by birth having Pṛṣṇifor your mother, do you,Maruts, favourable to man, come from heaven to our presence.
verses.wilson_translation: None of them are older, none younger (than the others); the destroyers of (foes), none hold a middle (rank), but all excel in glory; honourable by birth having Pṛṣṇifor your mother, do you,Maruts, favourable to man, come from heaven to our presence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वयो न ये श्रेणीः पप्तुरोजसांतांदिवो बृहतः सानुनस्परि ।अश्वास एषामुभये यथा विदुः प्र पर्वतस्य नभनूँरचुच्यवुः ॥
verses.transliteration: váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ śréṇīḥ ǀ paptúḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ ántān ǀ diváḥ ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ sā́nunaḥ ǀ pári ǀáśvāsaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ ubháye ǀ yáthā ǀ vidúḥ ǀ prá ǀ párvatasya ǀ nabhanū́n ǀ acucyavuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like birds (that fly) in rows they pass along in their strength above the vast summit (of the sky) to the ends of the firmament; their horses have caused the waters of the cloud to descend, as both (gods and mortals) know.
verses.wilson_translation: Like birds (that fly) in rows they pass along in their strength above the vast summit (of the sky) to the ends of the firmament; their horses have caused the waters of the cloud to descend, as both (gods and mortals) know.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मिमातु द्यौरदितिर्वीतये नः सं दानुचित्रा उषसो यतंतां ।आचुच्यवुर्दिव्यं कोशमेत ऋषे रुद्रस्य मरुतो गृणानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: mímātu ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ vītáye ǀ naḥ ǀ sám ǀ dā́nu-citrāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ yatantām ǀā́ ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀ divyám ǀ kóśam ǀ eté ǀ ṛ́ṣe ǀ rudrásya ǀ marútaḥ ǀ gṛṇānā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the heaven and the earth yield (rain) for our sustenance; may the wonderfully bounteous dawns exert themselves (for our good); may these sons of Rudra, lauded, Ṛṣi, (by you), send down the celestial rain.
verses.wilson_translation: May the heaven and the earth yield (rain) for our sustenance; may the wonderfully bounteous dawns exert themselves (for our good); may these sons of Rudra, lauded, Ṛṣi, (by you), send down the celestial rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LX. Maruts.
hymns.anukramani: ८ श्यावाश्व आत्रेयः। मरुतोऽग्नामरुतौ वा। त्रिष्टुप्, ७- ८ जगती ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I LAUD with reverence the gracious Agni: here may he sit and part our meed among us.As with spoil-seeking cars I bring oblation: turned rightward I will swell the Marut's, praise-song. The Maruts, yea, the Rudras, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and cars swift-moving,—Before you, fierce Ones! woods bow down in terror: Earth, even the mountain, trembles at your coming. Though vast and tall, the mountain is affrighted, the height of heaven is shaken at your roaringWhen, armed with lances, ye are sporting, Maruts, and rush along together like the waters. They, like young suitors, sons of wealthy houses, have with their golden natures decked their bodies.Strong on their cars, the lordly Ones, for glory, have set their splendours on their forms for ever. None being eldest, none among them youngest, as brothers they have grown to happy fortune.May their Sire Rudra, young and deft, and Pṛśni pouring much milk, bring fair days to the Maruts. Whether, O blessed Maruts, ye be dwelling in highest, midmost, or in lowest heaven,Thence, O ye Rudras, and thou also, Agni, notice the sacrificial food we offer. O Maruts, Lords of all, when Agni and when ye drive downward from sublimest heaven along the heights,Shakers of all, rejoicing, slayers of the foe, give riches to the Soma-pressing worshipper. O Agni, with the Maruts as they gleam and sing, gathered in troop, rejoicing drink the Soma juice;With these the living ones who cleanse and further all, joined with thy banner, O Vaiśvānara, from of old.

verses.sanskrit: ईळे अग्निं स्ववसं नमोभिरिह प्रसत्तो वि चयत्कृतं नः ।रथैरिव प्र भरे वाजयद्भिः प्रदक्षिणिन्मरुतां स्तोममृध्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: ī́ḷe ǀ agním ǀ su-ávasam ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ pra-sattáḥ ǀ ví ǀ cayat ǀ kṛtám ǀ naḥ ǀráthaiḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ bhare ǀ vājayát-bhiḥ ǀ pra-dakṣiṇít ǀ marútām ǀ stómam ǀ ṛdhyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: I adore the protecting Agniwith hymns; may he, propitiated on this occasion, approve of our acts; offer (worship with praises), intended to obtain food; as if (proceeding) with cars (to the goal), circumambulating (the fire); may I exalt the praise of themaruts.
verses.wilson_translation: I adore the protecting Agniwith hymns; may he, propitiated on this occasion, approve of our acts; offer (worship with praises), intended to obtain food; as if (proceeding) with cars (to the goal), circumambulating (the fire); may I exalt the praise of themaruts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ ये तस्थुः पृषतीषु श्रुतासु सुखेषु रुद्रा मरुतो रथेषु ।वना चिदुग्रा जिहते नि वो भिया पृथिवी चिद्रेजते पर्वतश्चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yé ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ pṛ́ṣatīṣu ǀ śrutā́su ǀ su-khéṣu ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀvánā ǀ cit ǀ ugrāḥ ǀ jihate ǀ ní ǀ vaḥ ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ cit ǀ rejate ǀ párvataḥ ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce Maruts, sons of Rudra, who ride in easy chariots (drawn by) celebrated steeds, (at your coming) the woods bow down with fear, the earth tremles, and the mountains (shake).
verses.wilson_translation: Fierce Maruts, sons of Rudra, who ride in easy chariots (drawn by) celebrated steeds, (at your coming) the woods bow down with fear, the earth tremles, and the mountains (shake).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पर्वतश्चिन्महि वृद्धो बिभाय दिवश्चित्सानु रेजत स्वने वः ।यत्क्रीळथ मरुत ऋष्टिमंत आप इव सध्र्यंचो धवध्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: párvataḥ ǀ cit ǀ máhi ǀ vṛddháḥ ǀ bibhāya ǀ diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ sā́nu ǀ rejata ǀ svané ǀ vaḥ ǀyát ǀ krī́ḷatha ǀ marutaḥ ǀ ṛṣṭi-mántaḥ ǀ ā́paḥ-iva ǀ sadhryáñcaḥ ǀ dhavadhve ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mountain, vast and lofty (though it be), is alarmed at your noise, and the summit of the firmament trembles when, lance-armed Maruts, you are sporting; you rush along together like waters.
verses.wilson_translation: The mountain, vast and lofty (though it be), is alarmed at your noise, and the summit of the firmament trembles when, lance-armed Maruts, you are sporting; you rush along together like waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वरा इवेद्रैवतासो हिरण्यैरभि स्वधाभिस्तन्वः पिपिश्रे ।श्रिये श्रेयांसस्तवसो रथेषु सत्रा महांसि चक्रिरे तनूषु ॥
verses.transliteration: varā́ḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ raivatā́saḥ ǀ híraṇyaiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ pipiśre ǀśriyé ǀ śréyāṃsaḥ ǀ tavásaḥ ǀ rátheṣu ǀ satrā́ ǀ máhāṃsi ǀ cakrire ǀ tanū́ṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like wealthy bridegrooms who have decorated their person ns with golden (ornaments) and purifying waters, so the noble and powerful Maruts, associated together in their chariots, have made great (preparation) in their several person ns for their embellishment.
verses.wilson_translation: Like wealthy bridegrooms who have decorated their person ns with golden (ornaments) and purifying waters, so the noble and powerful Maruts, associated together in their chariots, have made great (preparation) in their several person ns for their embellishment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अज्येष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते सं भ्रातरो वावृधुः सौभगाय ।युवा पिता स्वपा रुद्र एषां सुदुघा पृश्निः सुदिना मरुद्भ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ajyeṣṭhā́saḥ ǀ ákaniṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ eté ǀ sám ǀ bhrā́taraḥ ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ sáubhagāya ǀyúvā ǀ pitā́ ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ rudráḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ su-dúghā ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ su-dínā ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They are brothers, of whom no one is the elder, no one the younger, but who grew up together for their mutual prosperity; may their father,Rudra, ever youthful, the doer of good deeds, and Pṛṣṇi, (their mother), easy to be milked, grant favourable days for (the sake of) the Maruts.
verses.wilson_translation: They are brothers, of whom no one is the elder, no one the younger, but who grew up together for their mutual prosperity; may their father,Rudra, ever youthful, the doer of good deeds, and Pṛṣṇi, (their mother), easy to be milked, grant favourable days for (the sake of) the Maruts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदुत्तमे मरुतो मध्यमे वा यद्वावमे सुभगासो दिवि ष्ठ ।अतो नो रुद्रा उत वा न्वस्याग्ने वित्ताद्धविषो यद्यजाम ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ut-tamé ǀ marutaḥ ǀ madhyamé ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ avamé ǀ su-bhagāsaḥ ǀ diví ǀ sthá ǀátaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ rudrāḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ ágne ǀ vittā́t ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ yát ǀ yájāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious Maruts, whether you abide in the upper, the middle, or \the lower heaven, (come),Rudras, to us from thence; and do you,Agni, accept the oblation which this day we offer.
verses.wilson_translation: Auspicious Maruts, whether you abide in the upper, the middle, or \the lower heaven, (come),Rudras, to us from thence; and do you,Agni, accept the oblation which this day we offer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निश्च यन्मरुतो विश्ववेदसो दिवो वहध्व उत्तरादधि ष्णुभिः ।ते मंदसाना धुनयो रिशादसो वामं धत्त यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ marutaḥ ǀ viśva-vedasaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ váhadhve ǀ út-tarāt ǀ ádhi ǀ snú-bhiḥ ǀté ǀ mandasānā́ḥ ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǀ riśādasaḥ ǀ vāmám ǀ dhatta ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, who are omniscient, since you and Agniabide above the summits of the upper (region) of the sky, do you who cause (your enemies) to tremble, and are the consumers of (our) foes, do you, being plural ased, bestow upon the sacrificer who offers you oblations desirable wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, who are omniscient, since you and Agniabide above the summits of the upper (region) of the sky, do you who cause (your enemies) to tremble, and are the consumers of (our) foes, do you, being plural ased, bestow upon the sacrificer who offers you oblations desirable wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने मरुद्भिः शुभयद्भिर्ऋक्वभिः सोमं पिब मंदसानो गणश्रिभिः ।पावकेभिर्विश्वमिन्वेभिरायुभिर्वैश्वानर प्रदिवा केतुना सजूः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ śubháyat-bhiḥ ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ sómam ǀ piba ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀ gaṇaśrí-bhiḥ ǀpāvakébhiḥ ǀ viśvam-invébhiḥ ǀ āyú-bhiḥ ǀ váiśvānara ǀ pra-dívā ǀ ketúnā ǀ sa-jū́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, drink the Soma-juice, rejoicing, along with the Maruts, resplendent, adorable, associated in troops, purifying all, animating and long-lived; drink,Vaiśvānara, who are identified with the ancient emblem (of flame).
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, drink the Soma-juice, rejoicing, along with the Maruts, resplendent, adorable, associated in troops, purifying all, animating and long-lived; drink,Vaiśvānara, who are identified with the ancient emblem (of flame).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXI. Maruts.
hymns.anukramani: १९ श्यावाश्व आत्रेयः। १-४, ११-१६ मरुतः, ५-८ तरन्तमहिषी शशीयसी, ९ वैददश्विः पुरुमीळहः, १० वैददश्विस्तरन्तः, १७-१९ दार्भ्यो रथवीतिः। गायत्री, ३ निचृत्, ५ अनुष्टुप्, ९ सतोबृहती ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O HEROES lordliest of all, who are ye that have singly comeForth from a region most remote?. Where are your horses, where the reins? How came ye? how had ye the power?Rein was on nose and seat on back. The whip is laid upon the flank. The heroes stretch their thighs apart,Like women when the babe is born. Go ye, O Heroes, far away, ye bridegrooms with a lovely SpouseThat ye may warm you at the fire. May she gain cattle for her meed, hundreds of sheep and steeds and kine,Who threw embracing arms around the hero whom gyavaiva praised. Yea, many a woman is more firm and better than the man who turnsAway from Gods, andoffers not. She who discerns the weak and worn, the man who thirsts and is in wantShe sets her mind upon the Gods. And yet full many a one, unpraised, mean niggard, is entitled man:Only in weregild is he such. And she, the young, the joyous-spirited, divulged the path to Śyāva, yea, to me.Two red steeds carried me to Purumīlha's side, that sage of far-extended fame, Him who, like Vaidadasvi, like Taranta, hath bestowed on meA hundred cows in liberal gift. They who are borne by rapid steeds, drinking the meath that gives delight,They have attained high glories here. They by whose splendour both the worlds are over-spread they shine on carsAs the gold gleams above in heaven. That Marut band is ever young, borne on bright cars, unblamable,Moving to victory, checked by none. Who knoweth, verily, of these where the All-shakers take delight,Born, spotless, after sacred Law? Guides are ye, lovers of the song to mortal man through holy hymn,And hearers when he cries for help. Do ye, destroyers of the foe, worshipful and exceeding bright,Send down the treasures that we crave. OUrmya, bear thou far away to Darbhya this my hymn of praise,Songs, Goddess, as if chariot-borne. From me to Rathaviti say, when he hath pressed the Soma juice,The wish I had departeth not. This wealthy Rathaviti dwells among the people rich in kine,Among the mountains, far withdrawn.

verses.sanskrit: के ष्ठा नरः श्रेष्ठतमा य एकएक आयय ।परमस्याः परावतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ké ǀ stha ǀ naraḥ ǀ śréṣṭha-tamāḥ ǀ yé ǀ ékaḥ-ekaḥ ǀ ā-yayá ǀparamásyāḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who are you, most excellent leadeers (of rites), who come one by one from a region exceedingly remote?
verses.wilson_translation: Who are you, most excellent leadeers (of rites), who come one by one from a region exceedingly remote?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्व वोऽश्वाः क्वाभीशवः कथं शेक कथा यय ।पृष्ठे सदो नसोर्यमः ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ vaḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ kvá ǀ abhī́śavaḥ ǀ kathám ǀ śeka ǀ kathā́ ǀ yaya ǀpṛṣṭhé ǀ sádaḥ ǀ nasóḥ ǀ yámaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where are your horses? where your reins? what is your capability? where are you going? The saddle is on the back (of the steeds), the bridle in their nostrils.
verses.wilson_translation: Where are your horses? where your reins? what is your capability? where are you going? The saddle is on the back (of the steeds), the bridle in their nostrils.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जघने चोद एषां वि सक्थानि नरो यमुः ।पुत्रकृथे न जनयः ॥
verses.transliteration: jagháne ǀ códaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ ví ǀ sakthā́ni ǀ náraḥ ǀ yamuḥ ǀputra-kṛthé ǀ ná ǀ jánayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The goad is (applied) to their flanks; the drivers force them to spread their thighs apart, like women in bringing forth children.
verses.wilson_translation: The goad is (applied) to their flanks; the drivers force them to spread their thighs apart, like women in bringing forth children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परा वीरास एतन मर्यासो भद्रजानयः ।अग्नितपो यथासथ ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ vīrāsaḥ ǀ itana ǀ máryāsaḥ ǀ bhádra-jānayaḥ ǀagni-tápaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heroes, friendly to man, of honourable birth, you are as if blazing with fire.
verses.wilson_translation: Heroes, friendly to man, of honourable birth, you are as if blazing with fire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सनत्साश्व्यं पशुमुत गव्यं शतावयं ।श्यावाश्वस्तुताय या दोर्वीरायोपबर्बृहत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sánat ǀ sā́ ǀ áśvyam ǀ paśúm ǀ utá ǀ gávyam ǀ śatá-avayam ǀśyāvā́śva-stutāya ǀ yā́ ǀ dóḥ ǀ vīrā́ya ǀ upa-bárbṛhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: She, (Śaśiyasī), who has thrown her arms round the hero Taranta, who was eulogized byŚyāvāśva, has given me cattle comprising horses, and cows, and hundreds of sheep.
verses.wilson_translation: She, (Śaśiyasī), who has thrown her arms round the hero Taranta, who was eulogized byŚyāvāśva, has given me cattle comprising horses, and cows, and hundreds of sheep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वा स्त्री शशीयसी पुंसो भवति वस्यसी ।अदेवत्रादराधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ strī́ ǀ śáśīyasī ǀ puṃsáḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ vásyasī ǀádeva-trāt ǀ arādhásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Śaśīyasi, though a feminine le, is more excellent than a man who reverences not the gods, nor bestows wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Śaśīyasi, though a feminine le, is more excellent than a man who reverences not the gods, nor bestows wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि या जानाति जसुरिं वि तृष्यंतं वि कामिनं ।देवत्रा कृणुते मनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yā́ ǀ jānā́ti ǀ jásurim ǀ ví ǀ tṛ́ṣyantam ǀ ví ǀ kāmínam ǀdeva-trā́ ǀ kṛṇuté ǀ mánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For she discerns one who suffers pain, one who is in want, or one desirous (of any thing), and directs her mind towards the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: For she discerns one who suffers pain, one who is in want, or one desirous (of any thing), and directs her mind towards the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत घा नेमो अस्तुतः पुमाँ इति ब्रुवे पणिः ।स वैरदेय इत्समः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ gha ǀ némaḥ ǀ ástutaḥ ǀ púmān ǀ íti ǀ bruve ǀ paṇíḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ váira-deye ǀ ít ǀ samáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: And, eulogizing (him), I proclaim that the man, her (other) half is, (as it were), uncommended, for he is ever the same in munificent donations.
verses.wilson_translation: And, eulogizing (him), I proclaim that the man, her (other) half is, (as it were), uncommended, for he is ever the same in munificent donations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत मेऽरपद्युवतिर्ममंदुषी प्रति श्यावाय वर्तनिं ।वि रोहिता पुरुमीळ्हाय येमतुर्विप्राय दीर्घयशसे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ me ǀ arapat ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ mamandúṣī ǀ práti ǀ śyāvā́ya ǀ vartaním ǀví ǀ róhitā ǀ puru-mīḷhā́ya ǀ yematuḥ ǀ víprāya ǀ dīrghá-yaśase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Young and affable, she has explained to me,Śyāvāśva, the road, and two ruddy horses have borne me to the valiant and renowned Purumīḷha.
verses.wilson_translation: Young and affable, she has explained to me,Śyāvāśva, the road, and two ruddy horses have borne me to the valiant and renowned Purumīḷha.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो मे धेनूनां शतं वैददश्विर्यथा ददत् ।तरंत इव मंहना ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ me ǀ dhenūnā́m ǀ śatám ǀ váidat-aśviḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ dádat ǀtarantáḥ-iva ǀ maṃhánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, the son of Vidadaśva, has given me a hundred (head) of cattle, and, like Taranta, many precious gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, the son of Vidadaśva, has given me a hundred (head) of cattle, and, like Taranta, many precious gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य ईं वहंत आशुभिः पिबंतो मदिरं मधु ।अत्र श्रवांसि दधिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ īm ǀ váhante ǀ āśú-bhiḥ ǀ píbantaḥ ǀ madirám ǀ mádhu ǀátra ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀ dadhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those (Maruts) who are brought hither by swift horses, drinking the inembriating juice, receive here gratification.
verses.wilson_translation: Those (Maruts) who are brought hither by swift horses, drinking the inembriating juice, receive here gratification.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: येषां श्रियाधि रोदसी विभ्राजंते रथेष्वा ।दिवि रुक्म इवोपरि ॥
verses.transliteration: yéṣām ǀ śriyā́ ǀ ádhi ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vi-bhrā́jante ǀ rátheṣu ǀ ā́ ǀdiví ǀ rukmáḥ-iva ǀ upári ǁ
verses.english_translation: They by whose glory heaven and earth are surpassed; who shine splendid in their chariots like the radiant (sun) in the heaven above.
verses.wilson_translation: They by whose glory heaven and earth are surpassed; who shine splendid in their chariots like the radiant (sun) in the heaven above.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवा स मारुतो गणस्त्वेषरथो अनेद्यः ।शुभंयावाप्रतिष्कुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yúvā ǀ sáḥ ǀ mā́rutaḥ ǀ gaṇáḥ ǀ tveṣá-rathaḥ ǀ ánedyaḥ ǀśubham-yā́vā ǀ áprati-skutaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That company of Maruts, ever young, riding in bright chariots, irreproachable, auspicious, motive, unobstructed.
verses.wilson_translation: That company of Maruts, ever young, riding in bright chariots, irreproachable, auspicious, motive, unobstructed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: को वेद नूनमेषां यत्रा मदंति धूतयः ।ऋतजाता अरेपसः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ veda ǀ nūnám ǀ eṣām ǀ yátra ǀ mádanti ǀ dhū́tayaḥ ǀṛtá-jātāḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who knows of a certainty their (abode), where the intimidators (of their foes) rejoice? born for (the distribution of) water, exempt from defects.
verses.wilson_translation: Who knows of a certainty their (abode), where the intimidators (of their foes) rejoice? born for (the distribution of) water, exempt from defects.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं मर्तं विपन्यवः प्रणेतार इत्था धिया ।श्रोतारो यामहूतिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ mártam ǀ vipanyavaḥ ǀ pra-netā́raḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀśrótāraḥ ǀ yā́ma-hūtiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desirous of praise, you are the guides (to happiness) of the man who propitiates (you) by this pious rite; you are bearers of invocations to the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of praise, you are the guides (to happiness) of the man who propitiates (you) by this pious rite; you are bearers of invocations to the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते नो वसूनि काम्या पुरुश्चंद्रा रिशादसः ।आ यज्ञियासो ववृत्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ naḥ ǀ vásūni ǀ kā́myā ǀ puru-candrā́ḥ ǀ riśādasaḥ ǀā́ ǀ yajñiyāsaḥ ǀ vavṛttana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you, who are destroyers of themaleviolent, abounding in wealth, and entitled to adoration, bestow upon us desirable riches.
