verses.transliteration: ávidat ǀ dákṣam ǀ mitráḥ ǀ návīyān ǀ papānáḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ acait ǀsasa-vā́n ǀ staulā́bhiḥ ǀ dhautárībhiḥ ǀ uruṣyā́ ǀ pāyúḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, appreciates him who is skilled (in holy rites); a recent friend, quaffing (the libation), he heaps excellent (wealth) upon the devout; partaking of (the sacrificial) food, (and brought) by his robust agitators (of the earth, his steeds), he, through his benevolence, is a protector to his friends.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, appreciates him who is skilled (in holy rites); a recent friend, quaffing (the libation), he heaps excellent (wealth) upon the devout; partaking of (the sacrificial) food, (and brought) by his robust agitators (of the earth, his steeds), he, through his benevolence, is a protector to his friends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य पथि वेधा अपायि श्रिये मनांसि देवासो अक्रन् ।दधानो नाम महो वचोभिर्वपुर्दृशये वेन्यो व्यावः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ pathí ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ apāyi ǀ śriyé ǀ mánāṃsi ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ akran ǀdádhānaḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ maháḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ vápuḥ ǀ dṛśáye ǀ venyáḥ ǀ ví ǀ āvarítyāvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Soma, creator (of all), on the path of sacrifice, has been drunk; the worshippers have presented it to gratify the mind (of Indra); may he, the humiliator (of his foes), possessing a vast body, propitiated by our praises, become manifest to our view.
verses.wilson_translation: The Soma, creator (of all), on the path of sacrifice, has been drunk; the worshippers have presented it to gratify the mind (of Indra); may he, the humiliator (of his foes), possessing a vast body, propitiated by our praises, become manifest to our view.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: द्युमत्तमं दक्षं धेह्यस्मे सेधा जनानां पूर्वीररातीः ।वर्षीयो वयः कृणुहि शचीभिर्धनस्य सातावस्माँ अविड्ढि ॥
verses.transliteration: dyumát-tamam ǀ dákṣam ǀ dhehi ǀ asmé íti ǀ sédha ǀ jánānām ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ árātīḥ ǀvárṣīyaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ dhánasya ǀ sātáu ǀ asmā́n ǀ aviḍḍhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestow upon us most brilliant vigour; oppose the numerous enemies of your worshippers; gran us, for our pious acts, abundant food; secure us in the enjoyment of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow upon us most brilliant vigour; oppose the numerous enemies of your worshippers; gran us, for our pious acts, abundant food; secure us in the enjoyment of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र तुभ्यमिन्मघवन्नभूम वयं दात्रे हरिवो मा वि वेनः ।नकिरापिर्ददृशे मर्त्यत्रा किमंग रध्रचोदनं त्वाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ túbhyam ǀ ít ǀ magha-van ǀ abhūma ǀ vayám ǀ dātré ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ venaḥ ǀnákiḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ dadṛśe ǀ martya-trā́ ǀ kím ǀ aṅgá ǀ radhra-códanam ǀ tvā ǀ āhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, possessor of affluence, we have recourse to you, the bountiful, lord of steeds, be not unfavourable to us; no other kinsman is beheld (by us) among men; who else have they called yo the bestower of wealth?
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, possessor of affluence, we have recourse to you, the bountiful, lord of steeds, be not unfavourable to us; no other kinsman is beheld (by us) among men; who else have they called yo the bestower of wealth?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा जस्वने वृषभ नो ररीथा मा ते रेवतः सख्ये रिषाम ।पूर्वीष्ट इंद्र निष्षिधो जनेषु जह्यसुष्वीन्प्र वृहापृणतः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ jásvane ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ naḥ ǀ rarīthāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ revátaḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ riṣāma ǀpūrvī́ḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ niḥ-sídhaḥ ǀ jáneṣu ǀ jahí ǀ ásusvīn ǀ prá ǀ vṛha ǀ ápṛṇataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us not up, showerer (of benefits), to the obstructor (of our rites); relying upon the friendship of you, lord of riches, may we be unharmed; many are the hindrances (opposed) to you among men; slay those who make no libations, root out those who present no offerings.
verses.wilson_translation: Give us not up, showerer (of benefits), to the obstructor (of our rites); relying upon the friendship of you, lord of riches, may we be unharmed; many are the hindrances (opposed) to you among men; slay those who make no libations, root out those who present no offerings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदभ्राणीव स्तनयन्नियर्तींद्रो राधांस्यश्व्यानि गव्या ।त्वमसि प्रदिवः कारुधाया मा त्वादामान आ दभन्मघोनः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ abhrā́ṇi-iva ǀ stanáyan ǀ iyarti ǀ índraḥ ǀ rā́dhāṃsi ǀ áśvyāni ǀ gávyā ǀtvám ǀ asi ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ kārú-dhāyāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ adāmā́naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dabhan ǀ maghónaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As Indra, when thundering rases the clouds, so he (heaps upon his worshippers) riches of horses and cattle; yo, Indra, are he ancient upholder of the sacrificer; let not the opulent wrong you, not presenting (oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: As Indra, when thundering rases the clouds, so he (heaps upon his worshippers) riches of horses and cattle; yo, Indra, are he ancient upholder of the sacrificer; let not the opulent wrong you, not presenting (oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्यो वीर प्र महे सुतानामिंद्राय भर स ह्यस्य राजा ।यः पूर्व्याभिरुत नूतनाभिर्गीर्भिर्वावृधे गृणतामृषीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhvaryo íti ǀ vīra ǀ prá ǀ mahé ǀ sutā́nām ǀ índrāya ǀ bhara ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ rā́jā ǀyáḥ ǀ pūrvyā́bhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ nū́tanābhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ vavṛdhé ǀ gṛṇatā́m ǀ ṛ́ṣīṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ministrant priests offer libations to the mighty Indra, for he is their king, he who has been exalted by the ancient and recent hymns of adoring sages.
verses.wilson_translation: Ministrant priests offer libations to the mighty Indra, for he is their king, he who has been exalted by the ancient and recent hymns of adoring sages.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य मदे पुरु वर्पांसि विद्वानिंद्रो वृत्राण्यप्रती जघान ।तमु प्र होषि मधुमंतमस्मै सोमं वीराय शिप्रिणे पिबध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ máde ǀ purú ǀ várpāṃsi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ apratí ǀ jaghāna ǀtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ hoṣi ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ asmai ǀ sómam ǀ vīrā́ya ǀ śipríṇe ǀ píbadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the exhilaration of this Soma, the wise Indra, irresistible, has destroyed numerous opposing enemies; offer the sweet-flavoured beverage to that hero, the handsome-chinned, to drink.
verses.wilson_translation: In the exhilaration of this Soma, the wise Indra, irresistible, has destroyed numerous opposing enemies; offer the sweet-flavoured beverage to that hero, the handsome-chinned, to drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पाता सुतमिंद्रो अस्तु सोमं हंता वृत्रं वज्रेण मंदसानः ।गंता यज्ञं परावतश्चिदच्छा वसुर्धीनामविता कारुधायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: pā́tā ǀ sutám ǀ índraḥ ǀ astu ǀ sómam ǀ hántā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vájreṇa ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀgántā ǀ yajñám ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ áccha ǀ vásuḥ ǀ dhīnā́m ǀ avitā́ ǀ kārú-dhāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indrabe the drinker of this effused Soma, and, exhilarated by it, become the destroyer of Vṛtraby the thunderbolt; may he come, although from afar, to our sacrifice, (he who is) the giver of dwellings, the upholder of the celebrator (of religious).
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrabe the drinker of this effused Soma, and, exhilarated by it, become the destroyer of Vṛtraby the thunderbolt; may he come, although from afar, to our sacrifice, (he who is) the giver of dwellings, the upholder of the celebrator (of religious).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिंद्रस्य प्रियममृतमपायि ।मत्सद्यथा सौमनसाय देवं व्यस्मद्द्वेषो युयवद्व्यंहः ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ tyát ǀ pā́tram ǀ indra-pā́nam ǀ índrasya ǀ priyám ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ apāyi ǀmátsat ǀ yáthā ǀ saumanasā́ya ǀ devám ǀ ví ǀ asmát ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ yuyávat ǀ ví ǀ áṃhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this ambrosia, the appropriate beverage of Indra, of which is fond, be quaffed (by him), so that it may inspire the divinity with favourable feelings (towards us), and that he may remove from us our adversaries, and (all) iniquity.
verses.wilson_translation: May this ambrosia, the appropriate beverage of Indra, of which is fond, be quaffed (by him), so that it may inspire the divinity with favourable feelings (towards us), and that he may remove from us our adversaries, and (all) iniquity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एना मंदानो जहि शूर शत्रूंजामिमजामिं मघवन्नमित्रान् ।अभिषेणाँ अभ्यादेदिशानान्पराच इंद्र प्र मृणा जही च ॥
verses.transliteration: enā́ ǀ mandānáḥ ǀ jahí ǀ śūra ǀ śátrūn ǀ jāmím ǀ ájāmim ǀ magha-van ǀ amítrān ǀabhi-senā́n ǀ abhí ǀ ā-dédiśānān ǀ párācaḥ ǀ indra ǀ prá ǀ mṛṇa ǀ jahí ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Exhilarated by it, valiant Maghavan, slay our unfriendly adversaries, whether kinsman or unrelated (to us); put to flight,Indra, hostile armies menacing us (with their weapons), and slay them.
verses.wilson_translation: Exhilarated by it, valiant Maghavan, slay our unfriendly adversaries, whether kinsman or unrelated (to us); put to flight,Indra, hostile armies menacing us (with their weapons), and slay them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आसु ष्मा णो मघवन्निंद्र पृत्स्वस्मभ्यं महि वरिवः सुगं कः ।अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेष इंद्र सूरीन्कृणुहि स्मा नो अर्धं ॥
verses.transliteration: āsú ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ asmábhyam ǀ máhi ǀ várivaḥ ǀ su-gám ǀ karíti kaḥ ǀapā́m ǀ tokásya ǀ tánayasya ǀ jeṣé ǀ índra ǀ sūrī́n ǀ kṛṇuhí ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ ardhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent Indra, facilitate to us (the acquisition of) vast riches in these our battles; (enable us) to gain the victory; make us prosperous with rain, and with sons and grandsons.
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent Indra, facilitate to us (the acquisition of) vast riches in these our battles; (enable us) to gain the victory; make us prosperous with rain, and with sons and grandsons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वा हरयो वृषणो युजाना वृषरथासो वृषरश्मयोऽत्याः ।अस्मत्रांचो वृषणो वज्रवाहो वृष्णे मदाय सुयुजो वहंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ yujānā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-rathāsaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-raśmayaḥ ǀ átyāḥ ǀasmatrā́ñcaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vajra-vā́haḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ mádāya ǀ su-yújaḥ ǀ vahantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let your vigorous steeds, harnessed of their own will, drawing your wish-bestowing chariot, guided by shower-yielding reins, quick-moving, hastening towards us, youthful, thunder-bearing, well-yoked, bring you to the hountiful, exhilarating (libation).
verses.wilson_translation: Let your vigorous steeds, harnessed of their own will, drawing your wish-bestowing chariot, guided by shower-yielding reins, quick-moving, hastening towards us, youthful, thunder-bearing, well-yoked, bring you to the hountiful, exhilarating (libation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते वृषन्वृषणो द्रोणमस्थुर्घृतप्रुषो नोर्मयो मदंतः ।इंद्र प्र तुभ्यं वृषभिः सुतानां वृष्णे भरंति वृषभाय सोमं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ vṛṣan ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ dróṇam ǀ asthuḥ ǀ ghṛta-prúṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀíndra ǀ prá ǀ túbhyam ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ sutā́nām ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ bharanti ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ sómam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Showerer (of benefits), your vigorous water-shedding steeds, like the waves (of the sea), exulting, are harnessed to your car; for they, (the priests), offer to you, the showerer (of benefits), ever youthful, the libation of the Somaexpressed by the stones.
verses.wilson_translation: Showerer (of benefits), your vigorous water-shedding steeds, like the waves (of the sea), exulting, are harnessed to your car; for they, (the priests), offer to you, the showerer (of benefits), ever youthful, the libation of the Somaexpressed by the stones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृषासि दिवो वृषभः पृथिव्या वृषा सिंधूनां वृषभः स्तियानां ।वृष्णे त इंदुर्वृषभ पीपाय स्वादू रसो मधुपेयो वराय ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ asi ǀ diváḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ síndhūnām ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ stíyānām ǀvṛ́ṣṇe ǀ te ǀ índuḥ ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ pīpāya ǀ svādúḥ ǀ rásaḥ ǀ madhu-péyaḥ ǀ várāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Indra, are the showerer of heaven, the bearer of earth, the feeder of the rivers, the supplier of the aggregated (waters); for you, showerer (of benefits), who are the most excellent shedder of rain, the sweet Soma, the honey-flavoured, is ready to be quaffed.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are the showerer of heaven, the bearer of earth, the feeder of the rivers, the supplier of the aggregated (waters); for you, showerer (of benefits), who are the most excellent shedder of rain, the sweet Soma, the honey-flavoured, is ready to be quaffed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं देवः सहसा जायमान इंद्रेण युजा पणिमस्तभायत् ।अयं स्वस्य पितुरायुधानींदुरमुष्णादशिवस्य मायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ deváḥ ǀ sáhasā ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ yujā́ ǀ paṇím ǀ astabhāyat ǀayám ǀ svásya ǀ pitúḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ índuḥ ǀ amuṣṇāt ǀ áśivasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This divine Soma, with Indrafor its ally, crushed, as soon as genitive rated,Paṇiby force; this Soma baffled the devices and the weapons of the malignant secreter of (the stolen) wealth, (the cattle).
verses.wilson_translation: This divine Soma, with Indrafor its ally, crushed, as soon as genitive rated,Paṇiby force; this Soma baffled the devices and the weapons of the malignant secreter of (the stolen) wealth, (the cattle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमकृणोदुषसः सुपत्नीरयं सूर्ये अदधाज्ज्योतिरंतः ।अयं त्रिधातु दिवि रोचनेषु त्रितेषु विंददमृतं निगूळ्हं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ akṛṇot ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ su-pátnīḥ ǀ ayám ǀ sū́rye ǀ adadhāt ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ antáríti ǀayám ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ diví ǀ rocanéṣu ǀ tritéṣu ǀ vindat ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ní-gūḷham ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Somamade the dawns happily wedded to the sun; this Soma plural ced the light within the solar orb; this (Soma) has found the threefold ambrosia hidden in heaven in the three bright regions.
verses.wilson_translation: This Somamade the dawns happily wedded to the sun; this Soma plural ced the light within the solar orb; this (Soma) has found the threefold ambrosia hidden in heaven in the three bright regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं द्यावापृथिवी वि ष्कभायदयं रथमयुनक्सप्तरश्मिं ।अयं गोषु शच्या पक्वमंतः सोमो दाधार दशयंत्रमुत्सं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ví ǀ skabhāyat ǀ ayám ǀ rátham ǀ ayunak ǀ saptá-raśmim ǀayám ǀ góṣu ǀ śácyā ǀ pakvám ǀ antáríti ǀ sómaḥ ǀ dādhāra ǀ dáśa-yantram ǀ útsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This (Soma) has been fixed heaven and earth; this has harnessed the seven-rayed chariot (of the sun); this Soma has developed of its own will the mature deeply-organized secretion in the kind.
verses.wilson_translation: This (Soma) has been fixed heaven and earth; this has harnessed the seven-rayed chariot (of the sun); this Soma has developed of its own will the mature deeply-organized secretion in the kind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ३३ शंयुर्बार्हस्पत्य:। इन्द्र:, ३१-३३ बृबुस्तक्षा । गायत्री, २९ अतिनिचृत, ३१ पादनिचृत, ३३ अनुष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THAT Indra is our youthful Friend, who with his trusty guidance ledTurvaśa, Yadu from afar. Even to the dull and uninspired Indra, gives vital power, and winsEven with slow steed the offered prize. Great are his ways of guiding us, andṅanilbld are Ins eulogies:His kind protections never fail. Friends, sing your psalm and offer praise to him to whom the prayer is brought:For our great Providence is he. Thou, Slaughterer of Vṛtra, art Guardian and Friend of one and two,Yea, of a man like one of us. Beyond men's hate thou leadest us, and givest cause to sing thy praise:Good hero art thou called by men. I call with hymns, as ’twere a cow to milk, the Friend who merits praise,The Brahman who accepts the prayer. Him in whose hands they say are stored all treasures from the days of old,The Hero, conquering in the fight. Lord of Strength, Caster of the Stone, destroy the firm forts built by men,And foil their arts, unbending God! Thee, thee as such, O Lord of Power, O Indra, Soma-drinker, true,We, fain for glory, have invoked. Such as thou wast of old, and art now to be called on when the prizelies ready, listen to our call. With hymns and coursers we will gain, Indra, through thee, both steeds and spoilMost glorious, and the proffered prize. Thou, Indra, Lover of the Song, whom men must stir to help, hast beenGreat in the contest for the prize. Slayer of foes, whatever aid of thine imparts the swiftest course,With that impel our car to speed. As skilfullest of those who drive the chariot, with our art and aim,O Conqueror, win the proffered prize. Praise him who, Matchless and Alone, was born the Lord of living men,Most active, with heroic soul. Thou who hast been the singers' Friend, a Friend auspicious with thine aid,As such, O Indra, favour us. Grasp in thine arms the thunderbolt, O Thunder-armed, to slay the fiends:Mayst thou subdue the foemen's host. I call the ancient Friend, allied with wealth, who speeds the lowly man,Him to whom chiefly prayer is brought. For he alone is Lord of all the treasures of the earth: he speedsHither, chief Lover of the Song. So with thy yoked teams satisfy our wish with power and wealth in steedsAnd cattle, boldly, Lord of kine! Sing this, what time the ' juice is pressed, to him your Hero, Much-invoked,To please him as a mighty Steer. He, Excellent, withholdeth not his gift of power and wealth in kine,When he hath listened to our songs. May he with might unclose for us the cow's stall, whosesoe’er it be,To which the Dasyu-slayer goes. O Indra Śatakratu, these our songs have called aloud to thee,Like mother cows to meet their calves. Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers:Be to one craving steeds a Steed. Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence:Yield not thy singer to reproach. These songs with every draught we pour come, Lover of the Song, to thee,As milch-kine hasten to their young To thee most oft invoked, amid the many singers' rivalryWho beg with all their might for wealth. Nearest and most attractive may our laud, O Indra come to thee.Urge thou us on to ample wealth. Brbu hath set himself above the Paṇis, o’er their highest head,Like the wide bush on Gan!gā's bank. He whose good bounty, thousandfold, swift as the rushing of the wind,Suddenly offers as a gift. So all our singers ever praise the pious Brbu's noble deed,Chief, best to give his thousands, best to give a thousand liberal gifts.

verses.sanskrit: य आनयत्परावतः सुनीती तुर्वशं यदुं ।इंद्रः स नो युवा सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ánayat ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ sú-nītī ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀíndraḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that youthful Indra, who, by good guidance, brought Turvaśaand Yadufrom afar, (be) our friend.
verses.wilson_translation: May that youthful Indra, who, by good guidance, brought Turvaśaand Yadufrom afar, (be) our friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अविप्रे चिद्वयो दधदनाशुना चिदर्वता ।इंद्रो जेता हितं धनं ॥
verses.transliteration: avipré ǀ cit ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dádhat ǀ anāśúnā ǀ cit ǀ árvatā ǀíndraḥ ǀ jétā ǀ hitám ǀ dhánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indragives sustenance, even to the undevout he is the conqueror of wealh accusative ulated (by enemies) though (going against) them with a slow-paced steed.
verses.wilson_translation: Indragives sustenance, even to the undevout he is the conqueror of wealh accusative ulated (by enemies) though (going against) them with a slow-paced steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महीरस्य प्रणीतयः पूर्वीरुत प्रशस्तयः ।नास्य क्षीयंत ऊतयः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahī́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ prá-nītayaḥ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ prá-śastayaḥ ǀná ǀ asya ǀ kṣīyante ǀ ūtáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vast are his designs, manifold are his praises, his protections are never withdrawn.
verses.wilson_translation: Vast are his designs, manifold are his praises, his protections are never withdrawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सखायो ब्रह्मवाहसेऽर्चत प्र च गायत ।स हि नः प्रमतिर्मही ॥
verses.transliteration: sákhāyaḥ ǀ bráhma-vāhase ǀ árcata ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ gāyata ǀsáḥ ǀ hí ǀ naḥ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ mahī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer worship and praises, friends, to him who is to be attracted by prayers; for he verily is our great intelligence.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer worship and praises, friends, to him who is to be attracted by prayers; for he verily is our great intelligence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमेकस्य वृत्रहन्नविता द्वयोरसि ।उतेदृशे यथा वयं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ékasya ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ avitā́ ǀ dváyoḥ ǀ asi ǀutá ǀ īdṛ́śe ǀ yáthā ǀ vayám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, you are the protector of one (adorer), or of two, and of such as we are.
verses.wilson_translation: Slayer of Vṛtra, you are the protector of one (adorer), or of two, and of such as we are.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नयसीद्वति द्विषः कृणोष्युक्थशंसिनः ।नृभिः सुवीर उच्यसे ॥
verses.transliteration: náyasi ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ kṛṇóṣi ǀ uktha-śaṃsínaḥ ǀnṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǀ ucyase ǁ
verses.english_translation: You remove (far from us) those who hate us; you prosper hose who repeat your praise; bestower of excellentmaledescendants, you are glorified by man
verses.wilson_translation: You remove (far from us) those who hate us; you prosper hose who repeat your praise; bestower of excellentmaledescendants, you are glorified by man
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्माणं ब्रह्मवाहसं गीर्भिः सखायमृग्मियं ।गां न दोहसे हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: brahmā́ṇam ǀ bráhma-vāhasam ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ sákhāyam ǀ ṛgmíyam ǀgā́m ǀ ná ǀ doháse ǀ huve ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke with hymns Indra, our friends, who is Brahma, who is attracted by prayer and entitled to adoration, to milk him as a cow.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke with hymns Indra, our friends, who is Brahma, who is attracted by prayer and entitled to adoration, to milk him as a cow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोरूचुर्वसूनि नि द्विता ।वीरस्य पृतनाषहः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ víśvāni ǀ hástayoḥ ǀ ūcúḥ ǀ vásūni ǀ ní ǀ dvitā́ ǀvīrásya ǀ pṛtanā-sáhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In thehandsof whom, the eroic subduer of hostile armies, (the sages) have declared, are all the treasures in both (heaven and earth).
verses.wilson_translation: In thehandsof whom, the eroic subduer of hostile armies, (the sages) have declared, are all the treasures in both (heaven and earth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि दृळ्हानि चिदद्रिवो जनानां शचीपते ।वृह माया अनानत ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ dṛḷhā́ni ǀ cit ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ śacī-pate ǀvṛhá ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ anānata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, lord ofŚaci, demolish the strong (cities) of men; (battle), unbending (Indra) their devices.
verses.wilson_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, lord ofŚaci, demolish the strong (cities) of men; (battle), unbending (Indra) their devices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमु त्वा सत्य सोमपा इंद्र वाजानां पते ।अहूमहि श्रवस्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ satya ǀ soma-pāḥ ǀ índra ǀ vājānām ǀ pate ǀáhūmahi ǀ śravasyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Veracious Indra, drinker of the Soma, provider of sustenance, we, desirous of food, invoke such as you are.
verses.wilson_translation: Veracious Indra, drinker of the Soma, provider of sustenance, we, desirous of food, invoke such as you are.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमु त्वा यः पुरासिथ यो वा नूनं हिते धने ।हव्यः स श्रुधी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ yáḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ ā́sitha ǀ yáḥ ǀ vā ǀ nūnám ǀ hité ǀ dháne ǀhávyaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ śrudhi ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: (We invoke) you, such as you are, you who have been invocable of old, and who are now to be invoked for the wealth held (by the foe); hear our invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: (We invoke) you, such as you are, you who have been invocable of old, and who are now to be invoked for the wealth held (by the foe); hear our invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धीभिरर्वद्भिरर्वतो वाजाँ इंद्र श्रवाय्यान् ।त्वया जेष्म हितं धनं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhībhíḥ ǀ árvat-bhiḥ ǀ árvataḥ ǀ vā́jān ǀ indra ǀ śravā́yyān ǀtváyā ǀ jeṣma ǀ hitám ǀ dhánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Favoured) by you,Indra, (who are propitiated), by our hymns, (we ovecome) with our steeds the steeds (of the enemy), and we conquer abundant food, and the wealth held (by the foes).
verses.wilson_translation: (Favoured) by you,Indra, (who are propitiated), by our hymns, (we ovecome) with our steeds the steeds (of the enemy), and we conquer abundant food, and the wealth held (by the foes).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभूरु वीर गिर्वणो महाँ इंद्र धने हिते ।भरे वितंतसाय्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vīra ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ indra ǀ dháne ǀ hité ǀbháre ǀ vitantasā́yyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heroic and adorable Indra, verily you are mighty in battle, and victor of the wealth held (by the enemy).
verses.wilson_translation: Heroic and adorable Indra, verily you are mighty in battle, and victor of the wealth held (by the enemy).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या त ऊतिरमित्रहन्मक्षूजवस्तमासति ।तया नो हिनुही रथं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ te ǀ ūtíḥ ǀ amitra-han ǀ makṣújavaḥ-tamā ǀ ásati ǀtáyā ǀ naḥ ǀ hinuhi ǀ rátham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroyer of enemies with that your velocity, which is of exceeding swiftness, impel our chariots (against the foe).
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyer of enemies with that your velocity, which is of exceeding swiftness, impel our chariots (against the foe).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स रथेन रथीतमोऽस्माकेनाभियुग्वना ।जेषि जिष्णो हितं धनं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ráthena ǀ rathí-tamaḥ ǀ asmā́kena ǀ abhi-yúgvanā ǀjéṣi ǀ jiṣṇo íti ǀ hitám ǀ dhánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Victorious Indra, who are the chief off charioteers, conquer the wealth that is held (by the enemy) with our assailing car.
verses.wilson_translation: Victorious Indra, who are the chief off charioteers, conquer the wealth that is held (by the enemy) with our assailing car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य एक इत्तमु ष्टुहि कृष्टीनां विचर्षणिः ।पतिर्जज्ञे वृषक्रतुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ stuhi ǀ kṛṣṭīnā́m ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǀpátiḥ ǀ jajñé ǀ vṛ́ṣa-kratuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise that Indrawho alone has been born the supervisor (of all), the lord of men, the giver of rain.
verses.wilson_translation: Praise that Indrawho alone has been born the supervisor (of all), the lord of men, the giver of rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो गृणतामिदासिथापिरूती शिवः सखा ।स त्वं न इंद्र मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ gṛṇatā́m ǀ ít ǀ ā́sitha ǀ āpíḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ sákhā ǀsáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ mṛḷaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who has ever been the friend of those who praise you, and the insurer of their happiness by your protection, grant us felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who has ever been the friend of those who praise you, and the insurer of their happiness by your protection, grant us felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धिष्व वज्रं गभस्त्यो रक्षोहत्याय वज्रिवः ।सासहीष्ठा अभि स्पृधः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhiṣvá ǀ vájram ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀ rakṣaḥ-hátyāya ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀsasahīṣṭhā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, take the bolt in yourhandsfor the destruction ofrākṣasas, and uttely overthrow those who defy you.
verses.wilson_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, take the bolt in yourhandsfor the destruction ofrākṣasas, and uttely overthrow those who defy you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्नं रयीणां युजं सखायं कीरिचोदनं ।ब्रह्मवाहस्तमं हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: pratnám ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ yújam ǀ sákhāyam ǀ kīri-códanam ǀbráhma-vāhaḥ-tamam ǀ huve ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke the ancient Indra, the giver of iches, (our) friend, the encourager of his adorers, who is to be propitiated by prayer.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the ancient Indra, the giver of iches, (our) friend, the encourager of his adorers, who is to be propitiated by prayer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि विश्वानि पार्थिवाँ एको वसूनि पत्यते ।गिर्वणस्तमो अध्रिगुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ víśvāni ǀ pā́rthivā ǀ ékaḥ ǀ vásūni ǀ pátyate ǀgírvaṇaḥ-tamaḥ ǀ ádhri-guḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He alone rules over all terrestrial riches, he who is entitled to especial praise, he who is irresistible.
verses.wilson_translation: He alone rules over all terrestrial riches, he who is entitled to especial praise, he who is irresistible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स नो नियुद्भिरा पृण कामं वाजेभिरश्विभिः ।गोमद्भिर्गोपते धृषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ niyút-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛṇa ǀ kā́mam ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ aśví-bhiḥ ǀgómat-bhiḥ ǀ go-pate ǀ dhṛṣát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of cattle, (coming) with your mares, saisfy our desires completely with (abundant) food, with horses, and with kine.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of cattle, (coming) with your mares, saisfy our desires completely with (abundant) food, with horses, and with kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वो गाय सुते सचा पुरुहूताय सत्वने ।शं यद्गवे न शाकिने ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ gāya ǀ suté ǀ sácā ǀ puru-hūtā́ya ǀ sátvane ǀśám ǀ yát ǀ gáve ǀ ná ǀ śākíne ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing praises, when your libation is poured out, to him who is the invoked of many, the subduer (of foes), giving him gratification, like (fresh pasture) to cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Sing praises, when your libation is poured out, to him who is the invoked of many, the subduer (of foes), giving him gratification, like (fresh pasture) to cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न घा वसुर्नि यमते दानं वाजस्य गोमतः ।यत्सीमुप श्रवद्गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ gha ǀ vásuḥ ǀ ní ǀ yamate ǀ dānám ǀ vā́jasya ǀ gó-mataḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ úpa ǀ śrávat ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The giver of dwellings verily withholds not the gift of food conjoined with cattle, when he hears our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: The giver of dwellings verily withholds not the gift of food conjoined with cattle, when he hears our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमंतं दस्युहा गमत् ।शचीभिरप नो वरत् ॥
verses.transliteration: kuvít-sasya ǀ prá ǀ hí ǀ vrajám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ dasyu-hā́ ǀ gámat ǀśácībhiḥ ǀ ápa ǀ naḥ ǀ varat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then the desroyer of the Dasyus, proceeds to the cattl-crowded folds of Kuvitsa, and by his acts opens them for us.
verses.wilson_translation: Then the desroyer of the Dasyus, proceeds to the cattl-crowded folds of Kuvitsa, and by his acts opens them for us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा उ त्वा शतक्रतोऽभि प्र णोनुवुर्गिरः ।इंद्र वत्सं न मातरः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonuvuḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀíndra ǀ vatsám ǀ ná ǀ mātáraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, performer of many exploits, these our praises repeatedly recur to you as parent (cows) to their young.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, performer of many exploits, these our praises repeatedly recur to you as parent (cows) to their young.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दूणाशं सख्यं तव गौरसि वीर गव्यते ।अश्वो अश्वायते भव ॥
verses.transliteration: duḥ-náśam ǀ sakhyám ǀ táva ǀ gáuḥ ǀ asi ǀ vīra ǀ gavyaté ǀáśvaḥ ǀ aśva-yaté ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your friendship,Indra, is not easily lost; you, hero are (the giver of) cattle to him who desires cattle (of) horses him who desires horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Your friendship,Indra, is not easily lost; you, hero are (the giver of) cattle to him who desires cattle (of) horses him who desires horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स मंदस्वा ह्यंधसो राधसे तन्वा महे ।न स्तोतारं निदे करः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ mandasva ǀ hí ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ rā́dhase ǀ tanvā́ ǀ mahé ǀná ǀ stotā́ram ǀ nidé ǀ karaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Delight your person n with the libation (offered) for the sake of treasure; subject not your worshipper to his reviler.
verses.wilson_translation: Delight your person n with the libation (offered) for the sake of treasure; subject not your worshipper to his reviler.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा उ त्वा सुतेसुते नक्षंते गिर्वणो गिरः ।वत्सं गावो न धेनवः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ suté-sute ǀ nákṣante ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀvatsám ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These our praises tend, as the libationsa are repeatedly poured out, eagerly to you who are gratified by praise, as the milch kine (hasten) to their calves.
verses.wilson_translation: These our praises tend, as the libationsa are repeatedly poured out, eagerly to you who are gratified by praise, as the milch kine (hasten) to their calves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरूतमं पुरूणां स्तोतॄणां विवाचि ।वाजेभिर्वाजयतां ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-támam ǀ purūṇā́m ǀ stotṝṇā́m ǀ ví-vāci ǀvā́jebhiḥ ǀ vāja-yatā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the praises of many worshippers offered at the sacrifice, (accompanied) by (sacrificial) viands, invigorate you, destroyer of multitudes.
verses.wilson_translation: May the praises of many worshippers offered at the sacrifice, (accompanied) by (sacrificial) viands, invigorate you, destroyer of multitudes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमिंद्र भूतु ते स्तोमो वाहिष्ठो अंतमः ।अस्मान्राये महे हिनु ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ indra ǀ bhūtu ǀ te ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vā́hiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀasmā́n ǀ rāyé ǀ mahé ǀ hinu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May our most elevating praise be near,Indra, to you, and urge us to (the acquisition of) great riches.
verses.wilson_translation: May our most elevating praise be near,Indra, to you, and urge us to (the acquisition of) great riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अधि बृबुः पणीनां वर्षिष्ठे मूर्धन्नस्थात् ।उरुः कक्षो न गांग्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ bṛbúḥ ǀ paṇīnā́m ǀ várṣiṣṭhe ǀ mūrdhán ǀ asthāt ǀurúḥ ǀ kákṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ gāṅgyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛbu presided over the high plural ces of the Paṇis, like the elevated bank of the Ganges.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛbu presided over the high plural ces of the Paṇis, like the elevated bank of the Ganges.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य वायोरिव द्रवद्भद्रा रातिः सहस्रिणी ।सद्यो दानाय मंहते ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ vāyóḥ-iva ǀ dravát ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ rātíḥ ǀ sahasríṇī ǀsadyáḥ ǀ dānā́ya ǀ máṃhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of whom, prompt as the wind, the liberal donation of thousands (of cattle) has been quickly given to (me) soliciting a gift.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom, prompt as the wind, the liberal donation of thousands (of cattle) has been quickly given to (me) soliciting a gift.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तत्सु नो विश्वे अर्य आ सदा गृणंति कारवः ।बृबुं सहस्रदातमं सूरिं सहस्रसातमं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ aryáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sádā ǀ gṛṇanti ǀ kārávaḥ ǀbṛbúm ǀ sahasra-dā́tamam ǀ sūrím ǀ sahasra-sā́tamam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom, therefore, we all, who are the profferers and bestowers of praise ever commend, as the pious Bṛbu, the donor of thousands (of cattle), the receiver of thousands (of laudations).
verses.wilson_translation: Whom, therefore, we all, who are the profferers and bestowers of praise ever commend, as the pious Bṛbu, the donor of thousands (of cattle), the receiver of thousands (of laudations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १४ शंयुर्बार्हस्पत्य:। इन्द्र: प्रगाथ: [= विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ] ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THAT we may win us wealth and power we poets, verily, call on thee:In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's race-course call on thee. As such, O Wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone!Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariotsteeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength. We call upon that Indra, who, most active, ever slays the foe:Lord of the brave, Most Manly, with a thousand powers, help thou and prosper us in fight. Rcisama, thou forcest men as with a bull, with anger, in the furious fray.Be thou our Helper in the mighty battle fought for sunlight, water, and for life. O Indra, bring us name and fame, enriching, mightiest, excellent,Wherewith, O Wondrous God, fair-visored, thunder-armed, thou hast filled full this earth and heaven. We call on thee, O King, Mighty amid the Gods, Ruler of men, to succour us.All that is weak in us, Excellent God, make firm: make our foes easy to subdue. All strength and valour that is found, Indra, in tribes of Nahusas, and all the splendid fame that the Five Tribes enjoyBring, yea, all manly powers at once. Or, Maghavan, what vigorous strength in Trksi lay, in Druhyus or in Paru's folk,Fully bestow on us, that, in the conquering fray, we may subdue our foes in fight. O Indra, grant a happy home, a triple refuge triply strong.Bestow a dwelling-place on the rich lords and me, and keep thy dart afar from these. They who with minds intent on spoil subdue the foe, boldly attack and smite him down,—From these, O Indra Maghavan who lovest song, be closest guardian of our lives. And now, O Indra, strengthen us: come near and aid us in the fight,What time the feathered shafts are flying in the air, the arrows with their sharpened points. Give us, where heroes strain their bodies in the fight, the shelter that our fathers loved.To us and to our sons give refuge: keep afar all unobserved hostility. When, Indra, in the mighty fray thou urgest chargers to their speed,On the uneven road and on a toilsome path, like falcons, eager for renown, Speeding like rivers rushing down a steep descent, responsive to the urging call,That come like birds attracted to the bait, held in by reins in both the driver's hands.

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिद्धि हवामहे साता वाजस्य कारवः ।त्वां वृत्रेष्विंद्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ hávāmahe ǀ sātā́ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ kārávaḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ vṛtréṣu ǀ indra ǀ sát-patim ǀ náraḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ kā́ṣṭhāsu ǀ árvataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We worshippers invoke you for the acquisition of food; you,Indra, the protector of the good, (do) men (invoke for aid) against enemies, and in plural ces where horses (encounter).
verses.wilson_translation: We worshippers invoke you for the acquisition of food; you,Indra, the protector of the good, (do) men (invoke for aid) against enemies, and in plural ces where horses (encounter).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं नश्चित्र वज्रहस्त धृष्णुया महः स्तवानो अद्रिवः ।गामश्वं रथ्यमिंद्र सं किर सत्रा वाजं न जिग्युषे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ citra ǀ vajra-hasta ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀ maháḥ ǀ stavānáḥ ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀgā́m ǀ áśvam ǀ rathyám ǀ indra ǀ sám ǀ kira ǀ satrā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ná ǀ jigyúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt,Indra, the lord of clouds, mighty in resolution, being glorified by us, grant us cattle, and horses fit for chariots, as (you grant) abundant food to him who is victorious (in battle).
verses.wilson_translation: Wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt,Indra, the lord of clouds, mighty in resolution, being glorified by us, grant us cattle, and horses fit for chariots, as (you grant) abundant food to him who is victorious (in battle).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिंद्रं तं हूमहे वयं ।सहस्रमुष्क तुविनृम्ण सत्पते भवा समत्सु नो वृधे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ satrā-hā́ ǀ ví-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ índram ǀ tám ǀ hūmahe ǀ vayám ǀsáhasra-muṣka ǀ túvi-nṛmṇa ǀ sát-pate ǀ bháva ǀ samát-su ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke that Indrawho is the desroyer of mighty foes, the supervisor (of all things); do you, the many organed, the protector of the good, the distributor of wealth, be unto us (the insurer of) success in combats.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke that Indrawho is the desroyer of mighty foes, the supervisor (of all things); do you, the many organed, the protector of the good, the distributor of wealth, be unto us (the insurer of) success in combats.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बाधसे जनान्वृषभेव मन्युना घृषौ मीळ्ह ऋचीषम ।अस्माकं बोध्यविता महाधने तनूष्वप्सु सूर्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: bā́dhase ǀ jánān ǀ vṛṣabhā́-iva ǀ manyúnā ǀ ghṛ́ṣau ǀ mīḷhé ǀ ṛcīṣama ǀasmā́kam ǀ bodhi ǀ avitā́ ǀ mahā-dhané ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ ap-sú ǀ sū́rye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such,Indra, as you are represented in holy texts, assail (our) adversaries with fierceness like (that of) a bull in close conflict; regard yourself as our defender in war, (that we may long enjoy) posterity, water, and the sight of the) sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Such,Indra, as you are represented in holy texts, assail (our) adversaries with fierceness like (that of) a bull in close conflict; regard yourself as our defender in war, (that we may long enjoy) posterity, water, and the sight of the) sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरँ ओजिष्ठं पपुरि श्रवः ।येनेमे चित्र वज्रहस्त रोदसी ओभे सुशिप्र प्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ ójiṣṭham ǀ pápuri ǀ śrávaḥ ǀyéna ǀ imé íti ǀ citra ǀ vajra-hasta ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ su-śipra ǀ prā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, bring to us most excellent, most invigorating and nutritious food, wherewith, wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt, the handsome-chinned, you sustain both heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, bring to us most excellent, most invigorating and nutritious food, wherewith, wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt, the handsome-chinned, you sustain both heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामुग्रमवसे चर्षणीसहं राजंदेवेषु हूमहे ।विश्वा सु नो विथुरा पिब्दना वसोऽमित्रान्त्सुषहान्कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ugrám ǀ ávase ǀ carṣaṇi-sáham ǀ rā́jan ǀ devéṣu ǀ hūmahe ǀvíśvā ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ vithurā́ ǀ pibdanā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ amítrān ǀ su-sáhān ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke for protection you, royal Indra, who are mighty among the gods, tthe subduer of men; granter of dwellings, repel all evil spirits, and render our enemies easy of discomfiture.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for protection you, royal Indra, who are mighty among the gods, tthe subduer of men; granter of dwellings, repel all evil spirits, and render our enemies easy of discomfiture.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्र नाहुषीष्वाँ ओजो नृम्णं च कृष्टिषु ।यद्वा पंच क्षितीनां द्युम्नमा भर सत्रा विश्वानि पौंस्या ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ nā́huṣīṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ nṛmṇám ǀ ca ǀ kṛṣṭíṣu ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ páñca ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ dyumnám ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ satrā́ ǀ víśvāni ǀ páuṃsyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever strength and opulence (exist) among human beings, whatever be the sustenance of the five classes of men, bring Indrato us, as well (as) all great manly energies.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever strength and opulence (exist) among human beings, whatever be the sustenance of the five classes of men, bring Indrato us, as well (as) all great manly energies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वा तृक्षौ मघवंद्रुह्यावा जने यत्पूरौ कच्च वृष्ण्यं ।अस्मभ्यं तद्रिरीहि सं नृषाह्येऽमित्रान्पृत्सु तुर्वणे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vā ǀ tṛkṣáu ǀ magha-van ǀ druhyáu ǀ ā́ ǀ jáne ǀ yát ǀ pūráu ǀ kát ǀ ca ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǀasmábhyam ǀ tát ǀ rirīhi ǀ sám ǀ nṛ-sáhye ǀ amítrān ǀ pṛt-sú ǀ turváṇe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever vigour,Maghavan, (existed) in Tṛkṣu, in Druhyu, in Puru, bestow fully upon us in conflicts with foes, so that we may destroy our enemies in war.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever vigour,Maghavan, (existed) in Tṛkṣu, in Druhyu, in Puru, bestow fully upon us in conflicts with foes, so that we may destroy our enemies in war.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्रिवरूथं स्वस्तिमत् ।छर्दिर्यच्छ मघवद्भ्यश्च मह्यं च यावया दिद्युमेभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ tri-dhā́tu ǀ śaraṇám ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ svasti-mát ǀchardíḥ ǀ yaccha ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ máhyam ǀ ca ǀ yaváya ǀ didyúm ǀ ebhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give,Indra, to the affluent, and to me also, a sheltering and prosperous dwelling combining three elements, and defending in three ways and keep from them the blazing (weapon of our foes).
verses.wilson_translation: Give,Indra, to the affluent, and to me also, a sheltering and prosperous dwelling combining three elements, and defending in three ways and keep from them the blazing (weapon of our foes).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये गव्यता मनसा शत्रुमादभुरभिप्रघ्नंति धृष्णुया ।अध स्मा नो मघवन्निंद्र गिर्वणस्तनूपा अंतमो भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ gavyatā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ śátrum ǀ ā-dabhúḥ ǀ abhi-praghnánti ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent Indra, propitiated by praise, be nigh o us, as the defender of our person ns (against those) who assail (us as) enemies, with a mind bent upon carrying off (our) cattle, or who assault us with arrogance.
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent Indra, propitiated by praise, be nigh o us, as the defender of our person ns (against those) who assail (us as) enemies, with a mind bent upon carrying off (our) cattle, or who assault us with arrogance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध स्मा नो वृधे भवेंद्र नायमवा युधि ।यदंतरिक्षे पतयंति पर्णिनो दिद्यवस्तिग्ममूर्धानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǀ bhava ǀ índra ǀ nāyám ǀ ava ǀ yudhí ǀyát ǀ antárikṣe ǀ patáyanti ǀ parṇínaḥ ǀ didyávaḥ ǀ tigmá-mūrdhānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, be (favourable) at present to our success; protect our leader in battle when the feathered, sharp-pointed, shining shafts fall from the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, be (favourable) at present to our success; protect our leader in battle when the feathered, sharp-pointed, shining shafts fall from the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्र शूरासस्तन्वो वितन्वते प्रिया शर्म पितॄणां ।अध स्मा यच्छ तन्वे तने च छर्दिरचित्तं यावय द्वेषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ śū́rāsaḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ vi-tanvaté ǀ priyā́ ǀ śárma ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀádha ǀ sma ǀ yaccha ǀ tanvé ǀ táne ǀ ca ǀ chardíḥ ǀ acíttam ǀ yaváya ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When heroes rest their person ns (until abandoning) the plural asant abodes of their progenitors; grant us, for ourselves and our posterity, an unsuspected defence, and scatter our enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: When heroes rest their person ns (until abandoning) the plural asant abodes of their progenitors; grant us, for ourselves and our posterity, an unsuspected defence, and scatter our enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्र सर्गे अर्वतश्चोदयासे महाधने ।असमने अध्वनि वृजिने पथि श्येनाँ इव श्रवस्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ sárge ǀ árvataḥ ǀ codáyāse ǀ mahā-dhané ǀasamané ǀ ádhvani ǀ vṛjiné ǀ pathí ǀ śyenā́n-iva ǀ śravasyatáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: (At the time) when, in the effort (made) in an arduous conflict, you urge our horses over an uneven road, like falcons darting upon their food through the difficult path (of the firmament).
verses.wilson_translation: (At the time) when, in the effort (made) in an arduous conflict, you urge our horses over an uneven road, like falcons darting upon their food through the difficult path (of the firmament).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सिंधूँरिव प्रवण आशुया यतो यदि क्लोशमनु ष्वणि ।आ ये वयो न वर्वृतत्यामिषि गृभीता बाह्वोर्गवि ॥
verses.transliteration: síndhūn-iva ǀ pravaṇé ǀ āśu-yā́ ǀ yatáḥ ǀ yádi ǀ klóśam ǀ ánu ǀ sváni ǀā́ ǀ yé ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ várvṛtati ǀ ā́miṣi ǀ gṛbhītā́ḥ ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ gávi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rushing rapidly like rivers in their downward course and although neighing loudly through trro, they yet, tight-girthed, return repeatedly (to the conflict) for cattle, like birds darting on their prey.
verses.wilson_translation: Rushing rapidly like rivers in their downward course and although neighing loudly through trro, they yet, tight-girthed, return repeatedly (to the conflict) for cattle, like birds darting on their prey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVII. Indra, Etc.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YEA, this is good to taste and full of. sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour.No one may conquer Indra in the battle when he hath drunken of the draught we offer. This sweet juice here had mightiest power to gladden: it boldened Indra when he siaughtered Vṛtra,When he defeated Śambara's many onslaughts, and battered down his nineand ninety ramparts. This stirreth up my voice when I have drunk it: this hath aroused from sleep my yearning spirit.This Sage hath measured out the six expanses from which no single creature is excluded. This, even this, is he who hath created the breadth of earth, the lofty height of heaven.He formed the nectar in three headlong rivers. Soma supports the wide mid-air above us. He found the wavy sea of brilliant colours in forefront of the Dawns who dwell in brightness.This Mighty One, the Steer begirt by Maruts, hath propped the heavens up with a mighty pillar. Drink Soma boldly from the beaker, Indra, in war for treasures, Hero, Vṛtra-slayer!Fill thyself full at the mid-day libation, and give us wealth, thou Treasury of riches. Look out for us, O Indra, as our Leader, and guide us on to gain yet goodlier treasure.Excellent Guardian, bear us well through peril, and lead us on to wealth with careful guidance. Lead us to ample room, O thou who knowest, to happiness, security, and sunlight.High, Indra, are the arms of thee the Mighty: may we betake. us to their lofty shelter. Set us on widest chariot-seat, O Indra, with two steeds best to draw, O Lord of Hundreds!Bring us the best among all sorts of viands: let not the foe's wealth, Maghavan, subdue us. Be gracious, Indra, let my days be lengthened: sharpen my thought as ’twere a blade of ironApprove whatever words I speak, dependent on thee, and grant me thy divine protection. Indra the Rescuer, Indra the Helper, Hero who listens at each invocation,Śakra I call, Indra invoked of many. May Indra Maghavan prosper and bless us. May helpful Indra as our good Protector, Lord of all treasures, favour us with succour,Baffle our foes, and give us rest and safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour. May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, may we dwell in his auspicious favour.May helpful Indra as our good Preserver drive from us, even from afar, our foemen. Like rivers rushing down a slope, O Indra, to thee haste songs and prayers and linked verses.Thou gatherest, Thunderer! like widespread bounty, kine, water, drops, and manifold libations. Who lauds him, satisfies him, pays him worship? E’en the rich noble still hath found him mighty.With power, as when one moves his feet alternate, he makes the last precede, the foremost follow. Famed is the Hero as each strong man's tamer, ever advancing one and then another.King of both worlds, hating the high and haughty, Indra protects the men who are his people. He loves no more the men he loved aforetime: he turns and moves away allied with others.Rejecting those who disregard his worship, Indra victorious lives through many autumns. In every figure he hath been the mode: this is his only form for us to look on.Indra moves multiform by his illusions; for his Bay Steeds are yoked, ten times a hundred. Here Tvaṣṭar, yoking to the car the Bay Steeds, hath extended sway.Who will for ever stand upon the foeman's side, even when our princes sit at ease? Gods, we have reached a country void of pasture the land, though spacious, was too small to hold us.Bṛhaspati, provide in war for cattle; find a path, Indra, for this faithful singer. Day after day far from their seat he drove them, alike, from place to place, those darksome creatures.The Hero slew the meanly-huckstering Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, where the waters gather. Out of thy bounty, Indra, hath Prastoka bestowed ten coffers and ten mettled horses.We have received in turn from Divodāsa Śambara's wealth, the gift of Atithigva. Ten horses and ten treasure-chests, ten garments as an added gift,These and ten lumps of gold have I received from Divodāsa's hand. Ten cars with extra steed to each, for the Atharvans hundred cows,Hath Asvatha to Payu given. Thus Sṛñjaya's son honoured the Bharadvājas, recipients of all noble gifts and bounty. Lord of the wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious heroShow forth thy strength, compact with straps of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle. Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood.Honour with holy gifts the Car like Indra's bolt, the Car bound round with straps, the vigour of the floods. Thou Bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuṇa and Child of Mitra,—As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O Godlike Chariot, these oblations. Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee;O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen. Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers.Drive hence, O War-drum, drive away misfortune: thou art the Fist of Indra: show thy firmness. Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle's signal.Our heroes, winged with horses, come together. Let our car-warriors, Indra, be triumphant.

verses.sanskrit: स्वादुष्किलायं मधुमाँ उतायं तीव्रः किलायं रसवाँ उतायं ।उतो न्वस्य पपिवांसमिंद्रं न कश्चन सहत आहवेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: svādúḥ ǀ kíla ǀ ayám ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ utá ǀ ayám ǀ tīvráḥ ǀ kíla ǀ ayám ǀ rása-vān ǀ utá ǀ ayám ǀutó íti ǀ nú ǀ asyá ǀ papi-vā́ṃsam ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǀ sahate ǀ ā-havéṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Savoury indeed is this (Soma); sweet is it, sharp, and full of flavour; no one is able to encounter Indrain battles after he has been quaffing this (Soma).
verses.wilson_translation: Savoury indeed is this (Soma); sweet is it, sharp, and full of flavour; no one is able to encounter Indrain battles after he has been quaffing this (Soma).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं स्वादुरिह मदिष्ठ आस यस्येंद्रो वृत्रहत्ये ममाद ।पुरूणि यश्च्यौत्ना शंबरस्य वि नवतिं नव च देह्यो हन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ svādúḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mádiṣṭhaḥ ǀ āsa ǀ yásya ǀ índraḥ ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀ mamā́da ǀpurū́ṇi ǀ yáḥ ǀ cyautnā́ ǀ śámbarasya ǀ ví ǀ navatím ǀ náva ǀ ca ǀ dehyáḥ ǀ hán ǁ
verses.english_translation: The savoury Soma, drunk on this occasion, has been most exhilarating; by drinking of it Indrahas been elevated to the slaying of Vṛtra, and it has destroyed the numerous hosts ofŚambaraand the ninetynine cities.
verses.wilson_translation: The savoury Soma, drunk on this occasion, has been most exhilarating; by drinking of it Indrahas been elevated to the slaying of Vṛtra, and it has destroyed the numerous hosts ofŚambaraand the ninetynine cities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं मे पीत उदियर्ति वाचमयं मनीषामुशतीमजीगः ।अयं षळुर्वीरमिमीत धीरो न याभ्यो भुवनं कच्चनारे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ me ǀ pītáḥ ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ vā́cam ǀ ayám ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ uśatī́m ǀ ajīgaríti ǀayám ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ urvī́ḥ ǀ amimīta ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́bhyaḥ ǀ bhúvanam ǀ kát ǀ caná ǀ āré ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Somainspires my speech; this develops the desired intelligence; this sagacious (Soma) has created the six vast conditions, from which no creature is distinct.
verses.wilson_translation: This Somainspires my speech; this develops the desired intelligence; this sagacious (Soma) has created the six vast conditions, from which no creature is distinct.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं स यो वरिमाणं पृथिव्या वर्ष्माणं दिवो अकृणोदयं सः ।अयं पीयूषं तिसृषु प्रवत्सु सोमो दाधारोर्वंतरिक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ sáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ varimā́ṇam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ varṣmā́ṇam ǀ diváḥ ǀ ákṛṇot ǀ ayám ǀ sáḥ ǀayám ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ tisṛ́ṣu ǀ pravát-su ǀ sómaḥ ǀ dādhāra ǀ urú ǀ antárikṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This it is which formed the expanse of the earth, the compactness of the heaven; this Somahas deposited the ambrosia in its three principal (receptacles), and has upheld the spacious firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: This it is which formed the expanse of the earth, the compactness of the heaven; this Somahas deposited the ambrosia in its three principal (receptacles), and has upheld the spacious firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं विदच्चित्रदृशीकमर्णः शुक्रसद्मनामुषसामनीके ।अयं महान्महता स्कंभनेनोद्द्यामस्तभ्नाद्वृषभो मरुत्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vidat ǀ citra-dṛ́śīkam ǀ árṇaḥ ǀ śukrá-sadmanām ǀ uṣásām ǀ ánīke ǀayám ǀ mahā́n ǀ mahatā́ ǀ skámbhanena ǀ út ǀ dyā́m ǀ astabhnāt ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ marútvān ǁ
verses.english_translation: This makes known the wonderfully beautiful and inspiring (solar) radiance) at the appearance of the dawns, whose dwelling is the firmament; this mighty (Soma) has sustained the heaven with a powerful support, th sender of rain, the leader of the winds.
verses.wilson_translation: This makes known the wonderfully beautiful and inspiring (solar) radiance) at the appearance of the dawns, whose dwelling is the firmament; this mighty (Soma) has sustained the heaven with a powerful support, th sender of rain, the leader of the winds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धृषत्पिब कलशे सोममिंद्र वृत्रहा शूर समरे वसूनां ।माध्यंदिने सवन आ वृषस्व रयिस्थानो रयिमस्मासु धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: dhṛṣát ǀ piba ǀ kaláśe ǀ sómam ǀ indra ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ śūra ǀ sam-aré ǀ vásūnām ǀmā́dhyandine ǀ sávane ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǀ rayi-sthā́naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero,Indra, who are the slayer of foes in contests for (the acquisition of) treasures, drink boldly from the pitcher; drink copiously at the noonday rite; receptacle of rices, bestow riches upon us.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, who are the slayer of foes in contests for (the acquisition of) treasures, drink boldly from the pitcher; drink copiously at the noonday rite; receptacle of rices, bestow riches upon us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र प्र णः पुरएतेव पश्य प्र नो नय प्रतरं वस्यो अच्छ ।भवा सुपारो अतिपारयो नो भवा सुनीतिरुत वामनीतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ puraetā́-iva ǀ páśya ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ naya ǀ pra-tarám ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ áccha ǀbháva ǀ su-pāráḥ ǀ ati-pārayáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ bháva ǀ sú-nītiḥ ǀ utá ǀ vāmá-nītiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like one who goes before us,Indra, (on the road), look out, bring before us infinite wealth; be our conductor beyond the bounds (of want), convey us safely over (peril); be our careful guide, our gude to desirable (affluence).
verses.wilson_translation: Like one who goes before us,Indra, (on the road), look out, bring before us infinite wealth; be our conductor beyond the bounds (of want), convey us safely over (peril); be our careful guide, our gude to desirable (affluence).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उरुं नो लोकमनु नेषि विद्वान्त्स्वर्वज्ज्योतिरभयं स्वस्ति ।ऋष्वा त इंद्र स्थविरस्य बाहू उप स्थेयाम शरणा बृहंता ॥
verses.transliteration: urúm ǀ naḥ ǀ lokám ǀ ánu ǀ neṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǀ sváḥ-vat ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ábhayam ǀ svastí ǀṛṣvā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ sthávirasya ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ úpa ǀ stheyāma ǀ śaraṇā́ ǀ bṛhántā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make me happy,Indra; be plural ased to prolong my life; shapen my intellect like the edge of a metal sword; whatsoever, desirous (of propitiating) you, I may utter, be plural ased by it; render me the object of divine protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Make me happy,Indra; be plural ased to prolong my life; shapen my intellect like the edge of a metal sword; whatsoever, desirous (of propitiating) you, I may utter, be plural ased by it; render me the object of divine protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वरिष्ठे न इंद्र वंधुरे धा वहिष्ठयोः शतावन्नश्वयोरा ।इषमा वक्षीषां वर्षिष्ठां मा नस्तारीन्मघवन्रायो अर्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: váriṣṭhe ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ vandhúre ǀ dhāḥ ǀ váhiṣṭhayoḥ ǀ śata-van ǀ áśvayoḥ ǀ ā́ ǀíṣam ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣi ǀ iṣā́m ǀ várṣiṣṭhām ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ tārīt ǀ magha-van ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke, at repeated sacrifice,Indra, the preserver, the protector, the hero, who is easily propitiated, Indra, the powerful, the invoked of many; may Indra, the lord of affluence, bestow upon us prosperity.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke, at repeated sacrifice,Indra, the preserver, the protector, the hero, who is easily propitiated, Indra, the powerful, the invoked of many; may Indra, the lord of affluence, bestow upon us prosperity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र मृळ मह्यं जीवातुमिच्छ चोदय धियमयसो न धारां ।यत्किं चाहं त्वायुरिदं वदामि तज्जुषस्व कृधि मा देववंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ mṛḷá ǀ máhyam ǀ jīvā́tum ǀ iccha ǀ codáya ǀ dhíyam ǀ áyasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhā́rām ǀyát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ ahám ǀ tvā-yúḥ ǀ idám ǀ vádāmi ǀ tát ǀ juṣasva ǀ kṛdhí ǀ mā ǀ devá-vantam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the protecting, opulent Indrabe the bestower of felicity by his protections; may he, who is all-knower of felicity by his protections; may he, who is all-knowing, foil our adversaries; may he keep us out of danger, and may we be the possessors of excellent posterity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the protecting, opulent Indrabe the bestower of felicity by his protections; may he, who is all-knower of felicity by his protections; may he, who is all-knowing, foil our adversaries; may he keep us out of danger, and may we be the possessors of excellent posterity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रातारमिंद्रमवितारमिंद्रं हवेहवे सुहवं शूरमिंद्रं ।ह्वयामि शक्रं पुरुहूतमिंद्रं स्वस्ति नो मघवा धात्विंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: trātā́ram ǀ índram ǀ avitā́ram ǀ índram ǀ háve-have ǀ su-hávam ǀ śū́ram ǀ índram ǀhváyāmi ǀ śakrám ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ índram ǀ svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ dhātu ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we continue in the favour of that adorable (deity) even in his auspicious good-will; may that protecting and opulent Indradrive far from us, into extinction, all those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: May we continue in the favour of that adorable (deity) even in his auspicious good-will; may that protecting and opulent Indradrive far from us, into extinction, all those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रः सुत्रामा स्ववाँ अवोभिः सुमृळीको भवतु विश्ववेदाः ।बाधतां द्वेषो अभयं कृणोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ su-trā́mā ǀ svá-vān ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ su-mṛḷīkáḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ viśvá-vedāḥ ǀbā́dhatām ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ábhayam ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ su-vī́ryasya ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you the praises and prayers of the worshipper hasten like a torrent down a declivity; and you thunderer, aggregate the immense wealth (of sacrificial offerings), copious libations, and milk, and the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: To you the praises and prayers of the worshipper hasten like a torrent down a declivity; and you thunderer, aggregate the immense wealth (of sacrificial offerings), copious libations, and milk, and the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ।स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इंद्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥
verses.transliteration: tásya ǀ vayám ǀ su-matáu ǀ yajñíyasya ǀ ápi ǀ bhadré ǀ saumanasé ǀ syāma ǀsáḥ ǀ su-trā́mā ǀ svá-vān ǀ índraḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ ārā́t ǀ cit ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyotu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who may (adequately) praise him? Who may satisfy him? Who offer worthy adoration? Since Maghava is daily conscious of his own terrible (power); by his acts he makes first one and then the other precede and follow, as (a man) throws out his feet (alternately in walking).
verses.wilson_translation: Who may (adequately) praise him? Who may satisfy him? Who offer worthy adoration? Since Maghava is daily conscious of his own terrible (power); by his acts he makes first one and then the other precede and follow, as (a man) throws out his feet (alternately in walking).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव त्वे इंद्र प्रवतो नोर्मिर्गिरो ब्रह्माणि नियुतो धवंते ।उरू न राधः सवना पुरूण्यपो गा वज्रिन्युवसे समिंदून् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ tvé íti ǀ indra ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ūrmíḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ dhavante ǀurú ǀ ná ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ sávanā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ apáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ vajrin ǀ yuvase ǀ sám ǀ índūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hero Indrais renowned; humiliating every formidable (foe), and repeatedly changing the plural ce of one (worshipper) with that of another; Indra, the enemy of the arrogant, the soverign of both (heaven and earth), calls again and again (to encourage) the men who are his worshippers.
verses.wilson_translation: The hero Indrais renowned; humiliating every formidable (foe), and repeatedly changing the plural ce of one (worshipper) with that of another; Indra, the enemy of the arrogant, the soverign of both (heaven and earth), calls again and again (to encourage) the men who are his worshippers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क ईं स्तवत्कः पृणात्को यजाते यदुग्रमिन्मघवा विश्वहावेत् ।पादाविव प्रहरन्नन्यमन्यं कृणोति पूर्वमपरं शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ īm ǀ stavat ǀ káḥ ǀ pṛṇāt ǀ káḥ ǀ yajāte ǀ yát ǀ ugrám ǀ ít ǀ maghá-vā ǀ viśváhā ǀ ávet ǀpā́dau-iva ǀ pra-háran ǀ anyám-anyam ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ pū́rvam ǀ áparam ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrarejects the friendship of those who are formost (in pious acts), and, depositing them, associates with (their) inferiors; or (again) shaking off those who neglect his worship, Indra abides many years with those who serve him.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrarejects the friendship of those who are formost (in pious acts), and, depositing them, associates with (their) inferiors; or (again) shaking off those who neglect his worship, Indra abides many years with those who serve him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शृण्वे वीर उग्रमुग्रं दमायन्नन्यमन्यमतिनेनीयमानः ।एधमानद्विळुभयस्य राजा चोष्कूयते विश इंद्रो मनुष्यान् ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛṇvé ǀ vīráḥ ǀ ugrám-ugram ǀ dama-yán ǀ anyám-anyam ǀ ati-nenīyámānaḥ ǀedhamāna-dvíṭ ǀ ubháyasya ǀ rā́jā ǀ coṣkūyáte ǀ víśaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ manuṣyā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the prototype, has assumed various forms, and such is his form as that which (he adopts) for his manifestation; Indra, multiform by his illusion, proceeds (to his many worshippers), for the horses, yoked to his car are a thousand.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the prototype, has assumed various forms, and such is his form as that which (he adopts) for his manifestation; Indra, multiform by his illusion, proceeds (to his many worshippers), for the horses, yoked to his car are a thousand.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परा पूर्वेषां सख्या वृणक्ति वितर्तुराणो अपरेभिरेति ।अनानुभूतीरवधून्वानः पूर्वीरिंद्रः शरदस्तर्तरीति ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ pū́rveṣām ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ vṛṇakti ǀ vi-tárturāṇaḥ ǀ áparebhiḥ ǀ eti ǀánanu-bhūtīḥ ǀ ava-dhūnvānáḥ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ tartarīti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yoking his horses to his car,Tvaṣṭāshines in many plural ces here in thethree worlds; who (else), sojourning daily among his present worshippers, is their proector against adversaries?
verses.wilson_translation: Yoking his horses to his car,Tvaṣṭāshines in many plural ces here in thethree worlds; who (else), sojourning daily among his present worshippers, is their proector against adversaries?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय ।इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥
verses.transliteration: rūpám-rūpam ǀ práti-rūpaḥ ǀ babhūva ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ rūpám ǀ prati-cákṣaṇāya ǀíndraḥ ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ puru-rū́paḥ ǀ īyate ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ śatā́ ǀ dáśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have wandered, gods, into a desert where there is no track of cattle; the vast extant earth has become the protectress of murderers; direct us,Bṛhaspati, in our search for cattle; show the path,Indra, to your votary being astray.
verses.wilson_translation: We have wandered, gods, into a desert where there is no track of cattle; the vast extant earth has become the protectress of murderers; direct us,Bṛhaspati, in our search for cattle; show the path,Indra, to your votary being astray.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युजानो हरिता रथे भूरि त्वष्टेह राजति ।को विश्वाहा द्विषतः पक्ष आसत उतासीनेषु सूरिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: yujānáḥ ǀ harítā ǀ ráthe ǀ bhū́ri ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ ihá ǀ rājati ǀkáḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ dviṣatáḥ ǀ pákṣaḥ ǀ āsate ǀ utá ǀ ā́sīneṣu ǀ sūríṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, becoming manifest from his abode (in the firmament), dissipates, day by day, the resembling glooms, (so that he may distinguish) the other portion, (or the day); and the showerer has slain the two wealth-seeking slaves, Varcin andŚambara, in (the country of) Udavraja.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, becoming manifest from his abode (in the firmament), dissipates, day by day, the resembling glooms, (so that he may distinguish) the other portion, (or the day); and the showerer has slain the two wealth-seeking slaves, Varcin andŚambara, in (the country of) Udavraja.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अगव्यूति क्षेत्रमागन्म देवा उर्वी सती भूमिरंहूरणाभूत् ।बृहस्पते प्र चिकित्सा गविष्टावित्था सते जरित्र इंद्र पंथां ॥
verses.transliteration: agavyūtí ǀ kṣétram ǀ ā́ ǀ aganma ǀ devāḥ ǀ urvī́ ǀ satī́ ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ aṃhūraṇā́ ǀ abhūt ǀbṛ́haspate ǀ prá ǀ cikitsa ǀ gó-iṣṭau ǀ itthā́ ǀ saté ǀ jaritré ǀ indra ǀ pánthām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prastoka has given to your worshipper,Indra, ten purses of gold, and ten horses, and we have accepted this treasure from Divodāsa, the spoil won by AtithigvafromŚambara.
verses.wilson_translation: Prastoka has given to your worshipper,Indra, ten purses of gold, and ten horses, and we have accepted this treasure from Divodāsa, the spoil won by AtithigvafromŚambara.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिवेदिवे सदृशीरन्यमर्धं कृष्णा असेधदप सद्मनो जाः ।अहंदासा वृषभो वस्नयंतोदव्रजे वर्चिनं शंबरं च ॥
verses.transliteration: divé-dive ǀ sa-dṛ́śīḥ ǀ anyám ǀ árdham ǀ kṛṣṇā́ḥ ǀ asedhat ǀ ápa ǀ sádmanaḥ ǀ jā́ḥ ǀáhan ǀ dāsā́ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ vasnayántā ǀ udá-vraje ǀ varcínam ǀ śámbaram ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have received ten horses, ten purses, clothes, and ample food and ten lumps of gold from Divodāsa.
verses.wilson_translation: I have received ten horses, ten purses, clothes, and ample food and ten lumps of gold from Divodāsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रस्तोक इन्नु राधसस्त इंद्र दश कोशयीर्दश वाजिनोऽदात् ।दिवोदासादतिथिग्वस्य राधः शांबरं वसु प्रत्यग्रभीष्म ॥
verses.transliteration: prastokáḥ ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ dáśa ǀ kóśayīḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ adāt ǀdívaḥ-dāsāt ǀ atithi-gvásya ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ śāmbarám ǀ vásu ǀ práti ǀ agrabhīṣma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aśvatthahas given to Pāyuten chariots with their horses, and a hundred cows to the priests.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvatthahas given to Pāyuten chariots with their horses, and a hundred cows to the priests.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दशाश्वांदश कोशांदश वस्त्राधिभोजना ।दशो हिरण्यपिंडांदिवोदासादसानिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ áśvān ǀ dáśa ǀ kóśān ǀ dáśa ǀ vástrā ǀ ádhi-bhojanā ǀdáśo íti ǀ hiraṇya-piṇḍā́n ǀ dívaḥ-dāsāt ǀ asāniṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The son of Sṛñjayahas reverenced the Bharadvājaswho have accepted such great wealth for the good of all men.
verses.wilson_translation: The son of Sṛñjayahas reverenced the Bharadvājaswho have accepted such great wealth for the good of all men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दश रथान्प्रष्टिमतः शतं गा अथर्वभ्यः ।अश्वथः पायवेऽदात् ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ ráthān ǀ práṣṭi-mataḥ ǀ śatám ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ átharva-bhyaḥ ǀaśvatháḥ ǀ pāyáve ǀ adāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Chariot made of the) forest lord, be strong of fabric; be our friend; be our protector, and be manned by warriors; you are wrapped with cow-hides; keep us steady; and may he who rides in you be victorious over conquered (foes).
verses.wilson_translation: (Chariot made of the) forest lord, be strong of fabric; be our friend; be our protector, and be manned by warriors; you are wrapped with cow-hides; keep us steady; and may he who rides in you be victorious over conquered (foes).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महि राधो विश्वजन्यं दधानान्भरद्वाजान्त्सार्ञ्जयो अभ्ययष्ट ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ viśvá-janyam ǀ dádhānān ǀ bharát-vājān ǀ sārñjayáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ayaṣṭa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worship with oblations the chariot constructed of the substance of heaven and earth, the extracted essence of the forest lords; the velocity of the waters; the encompassed with the cow-hide; the thunderbolt (of Indra).
verses.wilson_translation: Worship with oblations the chariot constructed of the substance of heaven and earth, the extracted essence of the forest lords; the velocity of the waters; the encompassed with the cow-hide; the thunderbolt (of Indra).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वनस्पते वीड्वंगो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः ।गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥
verses.transliteration: vánaspate ǀ vīḷú-aṅgaḥ ǀ hí ǀ bhūyā́ḥ ǀ asmát-sakhā ǀ pra-táraṇaḥ ǀ su-vī́raḥ ǀgóbhiḥ ǀ sám-naddhaḥ ǀ asi ǀ vīḷáyasva ǀ ā-sthātā́ ǀ te ǀ jayatu ǀ jétvāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you, divine chariot, who are the thunderbolt of Indra, the precursor of the Maruts, the embryo of Mitra, the navel of Varuṇa, propitiated by this our sacrifice, accept the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, divine chariot, who are the thunderbolt of Indra, the precursor of the Maruts, the embryo of Mitra, the navel of Varuṇa, propitiated by this our sacrifice, accept the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दिवस्पृथिव्याः पर्योज उद्भृतं वनस्पतिभ्यः पर्याभृतं सहः ।अपामोज्मानं परि गोभिरावृतमिंद्रस्य वज्रं हविषा रथं यज ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ pári ǀ ójaḥ ǀ út-bhṛtam ǀ vánaspáti-bhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ ā́-bhṛtam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀapā́m ǀ ojmā́nam ǀ pári ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ ā́-vṛtam ǀ índrasya ǀ vájram ǀ havíṣā ǀ rátham ǀ yaja ǁ
verses.english_translation: War-drum, fill with your sound both heaven and earth; and let all things, fixed or moveable, be aware of it; do you, who are associated with Indraand the gods, drive away our foes to the remotest distance.
