verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ śṛṇvántu ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ yé ǀsu-mṛḷīkā́ḥ ǀ bhavantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Universal gods, augmenters of sacrifice, listening to praises (uttered) at due seasons, accept your appropriate milk-offering.
verses.wilson_translation: Universal gods, augmenters of sacrifice, listening to praises (uttered) at due seasons, accept your appropriate milk-offering.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवा ऋतावृध ऋतुभिर्हवनश्रुतः ।जुषंतां युज्यं पयः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǀ havana-śrútaḥ ǀjuṣántām ǀ yújyam ǀ páyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, with the company of the Maruts,Mitra, with Tvaṣṭāand Aryaman, accept our praise and these our oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, with the company of the Maruts,Mitra, with Tvaṣṭāand Aryaman, accept our praise and these our oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोत्रमिंद्रो मरुद्गणस्त्वष्टृमान्मित्रो अर्यमा ।इमा हव्या जुषंत नः ॥
verses.transliteration: stotrám ǀ índraḥ ǀ marút-gaṇaḥ ǀ tváṣṭṛ-mān ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀimā́ ǀ havyā́ ǀ juṣanta ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, invoker of the gods, cognizant (which of) the divine assembly (is he honoured), offer this our sacrifice according to the proper order.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, invoker of the gods, cognizant (which of) the divine assembly (is he honoured), offer this our sacrifice according to the proper order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं होतर्वयुनशो यज ।चिकित्वांदैव्यं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ adhvarám ǀ hótaḥ ǀ vayuna-śáḥ ǀ yaja ǀcikitvā́n ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Universal gods, hear this my invocation, whether you be in the firmament or in the heaven; you who (receive oblations) by the tongue of Agni, or are to be (otherwise) worshipped; seated on this sacred grass, be exhilarated (by the Soma).
verses.wilson_translation: Universal gods, hear this my invocation, whether you be in the firmament or in the heaven; you who (receive oblations) by the tongue of Agni, or are to be (otherwise) worshipped; seated on this sacred grass, be exhilarated (by the Soma).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं मे ये अंतरिक्षे य उप द्यवि ष्ठ ।ये अग्निजिह्वा उत वा यजत्रा आसद्यास्मिन्बर्हिषि मादयध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devāḥ ǀ śṛṇutá ǀ imám ǀ hávam ǀ me ǀ yé ǀ antárikṣe ǀ yé ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀ sthá ǀyé ǀ agni-jihvā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ yájatrāḥ ǀ ā-sádya ǀ asmín ǀ barhíṣi ǀ mādayadhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the adorable, universal deities, and both heaven and earth, and the grandson, of the waters, hear my praise; let me not utter words to be disregarded, but let us, (brought) most nigh unto you, rejoice in the happiness (you bestow).
verses.wilson_translation: May the adorable, universal deities, and both heaven and earth, and the grandson, of the waters, hear my praise; let me not utter words to be disregarded, but let us, (brought) most nigh unto you, rejoice in the happiness (you bestow).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवा मम शृण्वंतु यज्ञिया उभे रोदसी अपां नपाच्च मन्म ।मा वो वचांसि परिचक्ष्याणि वोचं सुम्नेष्विद्वो अंतमा मदेम ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ máma ǀ śṛṇvantu ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ ca ǀ mánma ǀmā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ pari-cákṣyāṇi ǀ vocam ǀ sumnéṣu ǀ ít ǀ vaḥ ǀ ántamāḥ ǀ madema ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those mighty deities, having power to destroy, whether they have been manifested upon earth or in heaven, or in the abode of the waters, bestow upon us and our posterity abundant sustenance both by night and day.
verses.wilson_translation: May those mighty deities, having power to destroy, whether they have been manifested upon earth or in heaven, or in the abode of the waters, bestow upon us and our posterity abundant sustenance both by night and day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमाया दिवो जज्ञिरे अपां सधस्थे ।ते अस्मभ्यमिषये विश्वमायुः क्षप उस्रा वरिवस्यंतु देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ké ǀ ca ǀ jmā́ ǀ mahínaḥ ǀ áhi-māyāḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ jajñiré ǀ apā́m ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀté ǀ asmábhyam ǀ iṣáye ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ kṣápaḥ ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ varivasyantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniand Parjanya, prosper my pious acts; (accept), you who are reverently invoked, our praise at this sacrifice; one of you genitive rates food, the other posterity; grant us, therefore, food productive of descendants.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniand Parjanya, prosper my pious acts; (accept), you who are reverently invoked, our praise at this sacrifice; one of you genitive rates food, the other posterity; grant us, therefore, food productive of descendants.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नीपर्जन्याववतं धियं मेऽस्मिन्हवे सुहवा सुष्टुतिं नः ।इळामन्यो जनयद्गर्भमन्यः प्रजावतीरिष आ धत्तमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágnīparjanyau ǀ ávatam ǀ dhíyam ǀ me ǀ asmín ǀ háve ǀ su-havā ǀ su-stutím ǀ naḥ ǀíḷām ǀ anyáḥ ǀ janáyat ǀ gárbham ǀ anyáḥ ǀ prajā́-vatīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dhattam ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the sacred grass is strewn, when the fire is kindled, and when I worship (you) with a hymn, and with profound veneration, then, adorable universal gods, rejoice in the oblation (offered) today at this our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: When the sacred grass is strewn, when the fire is kindled, and when I worship (you) with a hymn, and with profound veneration, then, adorable universal gods, rejoice in the oblation (offered) today at this our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LORD of the path, O Pūṣan, we have yoked and bound thee to our hymn,Even as a car, to win the prize. Bring us the wealth that men require, a manly master of a house,Free-handed with the liberal meed. Even him who would not give, do thou,O glowing Pūṣan, urge to give,And make the niggard's soul grow soft. Clear paths that we may win the prize; scatter our enemies afar.Strong God, be all our thoughts fulfilled. Penetrate with an awl, O Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,And make them subject to our will. Thrust with thine awl, O Pūṣan: seek that which the niggard's heart holds dear,And make him subject to our will. Tear up and read in pieces, Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,And make them subject to our will. Thou, glowing Pūṣan, carriest an awl that urges men to prayer;Therewith do thou tear up and rend to shreds the heart of every one. Thou bearest, glowing Lord! a goad with horny point that guides the cowsThence do we seek thy gift of bliss. And make this hymn of ours produce kine, horses, and a store of wealthFor our delight and use as men.

verses.sanskrit: वयमु त्वा पथस्पते रथं न वाजसातये ।धिये पूषन्नयुज्महि ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ pathaḥ ǀ pate ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀdhiyé ǀ pūṣan ǀ ayujmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣan, lord of paths, we attach you to us like a chariot, for (the sake of) bringing food, and of (accomplishing our) solemnity.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣan, lord of paths, we attach you to us like a chariot, for (the sake of) bringing food, and of (accomplishing our) solemnity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि नो नर्यं वसु वीरं प्रयतदक्षिणं ।वामं गृहपतिं नय ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ náryam ǀ vásu ǀ vīrám ǀ práyata-dakṣiṇam ǀvāmám ǀ gṛhá-patim ǀ naya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Conduct us to a gracious householder, friendly to men, liberal in (bestowing) wealth, the giver of pious donations.
verses.wilson_translation: Conduct us to a gracious householder, friendly to men, liberal in (bestowing) wealth, the giver of pious donations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अदित्संतं चिदाघृणे पूषंदानाय चोदय ।पणेश्चिद्वि म्रदा मनः ॥
verses.transliteration: áditsantam ǀ cit ǀ āghṛṇe ǀ pū́ṣan ǀ dā́nāya ǀ codaya ǀpaṇéḥ ǀ cit ǀ ví ǀ mrada ǀ mánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, instrumental gate the niggard to liberality, soften the heart of the miser.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, instrumental gate the niggard to liberality, soften the heart of the miser.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि पथो वाजसातये चिनुहि वि मृधो जहि ।साधंतामुग्र नो धियः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ patháḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀ cinuhí ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ jahi ǀsā́dhantām ǀ ugra ǀ naḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pierce Pūṣan, select (fit) roads for the passage of provisions; drive away all obstructors, (thieves, or the like), so that our holy rites may be accomplished.
verses.wilson_translation: Pierce Pūṣan, select (fit) roads for the passage of provisions; drive away all obstructors, (thieves, or the like), so that our holy rites may be accomplished.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि तृंधि पणीनामारया हृदया कवे ।अथेमस्मभ्यं रंधय ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ tṛndhi ǀ paṇīnā́m ǀ ā́rayā ǀ hṛ́dayā ǀ kave ǀátha ǀ īm ǀ asmábhyam ǀ randhaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pierce with a goad the hearts of the avaricious, wise Pūṣan, and so render them complacent towards us.
verses.wilson_translation: Pierce with a goad the hearts of the avaricious, wise Pūṣan, and so render them complacent towards us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि पूषन्नारया तुद पणेरिच्छ हृदि प्रियं ।अथेमस्मभ्यं रंधय ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ pūṣan ǀ ā́rayā ǀ tuda ǀ paṇéḥ ǀ iccha ǀ hṛdí ǀ priyám ǀátha ǀ īm ǀ asmábhyam ǀ randhaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pierce with a goad,Pūṣan, the heart of the avaricious; genitive rate genitive rosity in his heart, and so render him complacent towards us.
verses.wilson_translation: Pierce with a goad,Pūṣan, the heart of the avaricious; genitive rate genitive rosity in his heart, and so render him complacent towards us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ रिख किकिरा कृणु पणीनां हृदया कवे ।अथेमस्मभ्यं रंधय ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ rikha ǀ kikirā́ ǀ kṛṇu ǀ paṇīnā́m ǀ hṛ́dayā ǀ kave ǀátha ǀ īm ǀ asmábhyam ǀ randhaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Abrade, wise Pūṣan, the hearts of the avaricious; relax (their hardness), and so render them complacent towards us.
verses.wilson_translation: Abrade, wise Pūṣan, the hearts of the avaricious; relax (their hardness), and so render them complacent towards us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यां पूषन्ब्रह्मचोदनीमारां बिभर्ष्याघृणे ।तया समस्य हृदयमा रिख किकिरा कृणु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́m ǀ pūṣan ǀ brahma-códanīm ǀ ā́rām ǀ bíbharṣi ǀ āghṛṇe ǀtáyā ǀ samasya ǀ hṛ́dayam ǀ ā́ ǀ rikha ǀ kikirā́ ǀ kṛṇu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, with that food-propelling goad which you bear, abrade the heart of every miser, and render it relaxed.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, with that food-propelling goad which you bear, abrade the heart of every miser, and render it relaxed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या ते अष्ट्रा गोओपशाघृणे पशुसाधनी ।तस्यास्ते सुम्नमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ te ǀ áṣṭrā ǀ gó-opaśā ǀ ā́ghṛṇe ǀ paśu-sā́dhanī ǀtásyāḥ ǀ te ǀ sumnám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, we ask of you the service of that your weapon, which is the guide of cows, the director of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, we ask of you the service of that your weapon, which is the guide of cows, the director of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो गोषणिं धियमश्वसां वाजसामुत ।नृवत्कृणुहि वीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ go-sánim ǀ dhíyam ǀ aśvasā́m ǀ vāja-sā́m ǀ utá ǀnṛ-vát ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ vītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make our pious worship productive of cows, of horses, of food, of dependants, for our enjoyment.
verses.wilson_translation: Make our pious worship productive of cows, of horses, of food, of dependants, for our enjoyment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O PUSAN, bring us to the man who knows, who shall direct us straight,And say unto us, It is here. May we go forth with Pūṣan who shall point the houses out to us,And say to us, These same are they. Unharmed is Pūṣan's chariot wheel; the box ne’er falleth to the ground,Nor doth the loosened felIy shake. Pūṣan forgetteth not the man who serveth him with offered gift:That man is first to gather wealth. May Pūṣan follow near our kine; may Pūṣan keep our horses safe:May Pūṣan gather gear for us. Follow the kine of him who pours libations out and worships thee;And ours who sing thee songs of praise. Let none be lost, none injured, none sink in a pit and break a limb.Return with these all safe and sound. Pūṣan who listens to our prayers, the Strong whose wealth is never lost,The Lord of riches, we implore. Secure in thy protecting care, O Pūṣan, never may we fail.We here are they who sing thy praise. From out the distance, far and wide, may Pūṣan stretch his right hand forth,And drive our lost again to us.

verses.sanskrit: सं पूषन्विदुषा नय यो अंजसानुशासति ।य एवेदमिति ब्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ pūṣan ǀ vidúṣā ǀ naya ǀ yáḥ ǀ áñjasā ǀ anu-śā́sati ǀyáḥ ǀ evá ǀ idám ǀ íti ǀ brávat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring us,Pūṣan, into communication with a wise man who may rightly direct us, who may even say, this is so.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring us,Pūṣan, into communication with a wise man who may rightly direct us, who may even say, this is so.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समु पूष्णा गमेमहि यो गृहाँ अभिशासति ।इम एवेति च ब्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ pūṣṇā́ ǀ gamemahi ǀ yáḥ ǀ gṛhā́n ǀ abhi-śā́sati ǀimé ǀ evá ǀ íti ǀ ca ǀ brávat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, by the favour of Pūṣan, come in communication with (the man) who may direct us to the houses (where our goods are secreted), and may say, verily these are they.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, by the favour of Pūṣan, come in communication with (the man) who may direct us to the houses (where our goods are secreted), and may say, verily these are they.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूष्णश्चक्रं न रिष्यति न कोशोऽव पद्यते ।नो अस्य व्यथते पविः ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣṇáḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ ná ǀ riṣyati ǀ ná ǀ kóśaḥ ǀ áva ǀ padyate ǀnó íti ǀ asya ǀ vyathate ǀ pavíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The discus of Pūṣandoes not destroy; its sheath is not discarded, its edge harms not us.���
verses.wilson_translation: The discus of Pūṣandoes not destroy; its sheath is not discarded, its edge harms not us.���
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो अस्मै हविषाविधन्न तं पूषापि मृष्यते ।प्रथमो विंदते वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ havíṣā ǀ ávidhat ǀ ná ǀ tám ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ ápi ǀ mṛṣyate ǀprathamáḥ ǀ vindate ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣaninflicts not the least injury on the man who propitiates him by oblations; he is the first who acquires wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣaninflicts not the least injury on the man who propitiates him by oblations; he is the first who acquires wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा गा अन्वेतु नः पूषा रक्षत्वर्वतः ।पूषा वाजं सनोतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ etu ǀ naḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ rakṣatu ǀ árvataḥ ǀpūṣā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ sanotu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Pūṣancome to (guard) our cattle, ma Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan give us food.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣancome to (guard) our cattle, ma Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan give us food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषन्ननु प्र गा इहि यजमानस्य सुन्वतः ।अस्माकं स्तुवतामुत ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́ṣan ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ihi ǀ yájamānasya ǀ sunvatáḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ stuvatā́m ǀ utá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come,Pūṣan, to (guard) the cattle of the instrumental tutor of the rite presenting libations, and also of us repeating (your) praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Pūṣan, to (guard) the cattle of the instrumental tutor of the rite presenting libations, and also of us repeating (your) praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: माकिर्नेशन्माकीं रिषन्माकीं सं शारि केवटे ।अथारिष्टाभिरा गहि ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́kiḥ ǀ neśat ǀ mā́kīm ǀ riṣat ǀ mā́kīm ǀ sám ǀ śāri ǀ kévaṭe ǀátha ǀ áriṣṭābhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not,Pūṣan, our cattle perish; let them not be injured; let them not be hurt by falling into a well; come, therefore, along with them unharmed.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not,Pūṣan, our cattle perish; let them not be injured; let them not be hurt by falling into a well; come, therefore, along with them unharmed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शृण्वंतं पूषणं वयमिर्यमनष्टवेदसं ।ईशानं राय ईमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛṇvántam ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ vayám ǀ íryam ǀ ánaṣṭa-vedasam ǀī́śānam ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit Pūṣan, who hears (our eulogies); who is the averter (of poverty); the preserver of that which is not lost, the ruler (over all).
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit Pūṣan, who hears (our eulogies); who is the averter (of poverty); the preserver of that which is not lost, the ruler (over all).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषंतव व्रते वयं न रिष्येम कदा चन ।स्तोतारस्त इह स्मसि ॥
verses.transliteration: pū́ṣan ǀ táva ǀ vraté ǀ vayám ǀ ná ǀ riṣyema ǀ kádā ǀ caná ǀstotā́raḥ ǀ te ǀ ihá ǀ smasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we never suffer detriment when engaged,Pūṣan, in your worship; we are at this time your adorers.
verses.wilson_translation: May we never suffer detriment when engaged,Pūṣan, in your worship; we are at this time your adorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि पूषा परस्ताद्धस्तं दधातु दक्षिणं ।पुनर्नो नष्टमाजतु ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ parástāt ǀ hástam ǀ dadhātu ǀ dákṣiṇam ǀpúnaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ naṣṭám ǀ ā́ ǀ ajatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Pūṣanput forth his righthand(to restrain our cattle) from going astray; may we bring again to us that which has been lost.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣanput forth his righthand(to restrain our cattle) from going astray; may we bring again to us that which has been lost.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SON of Deliverance, come, bright God!Let us twain go together: be our charioteer of sacrifice. We pray for wealth to thee most skilled of charioteers, with braided hair,Lord of great riches, and our Friend. Bright God whose steeds are goats, thou art a stream of wealth, a treasure-heap,The Friend of every pious man. Pūṣan, who driveth goats for steeds, the strong and Mighty, who is calledHis Sister's lover, will we laud. His Mother's suitor I address. May he who loves his Sister hear,Brother of Indra, and my Friend. May the sure-footed goats come nigh, conveying Pūṣan on his car,The God who visiteth mankind.

verses.sanskrit: एहि वां विमुचो नपादाघृणे सं सचावहै ।रथीर्ऋतस्य नो भव ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ vā́m ǀ vi-mucaḥ ǀ napāt ǀ ā́ghṛṇe ǀ sám ǀ sacāvahai ǀrathī́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come illusrious grandson of Prajāpatito (me your) worshipper); let us two be associated; become the conveyer of our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Come illusrious grandson of Prajāpatito (me your) worshipper); let us two be associated; become the conveyer of our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथीतमं कपर्दिनमीशानं राधसो महः ।रायः सखायमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: rathí-tamam ǀ kapardínam ǀ ī́śānam ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀrāyáḥ ǀ sákhāyam ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit riches of our friend, (Pūṣan), the chief of charioteers, the wearer of a braid (of hair), the lord of infinite wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit riches of our friend, (Pūṣan), the chief of charioteers, the wearer of a braid (of hair), the lord of infinite wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रायो धारास्याघृणे वसो राशिरजाश्व ।धीवतोधीवतः सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyáḥ ǀ dhā́rā ǀ asi ǀ āghṛṇe ǀ vásoḥ ǀ rāśíḥ ǀ aja-aśva ǀdhī́vataḥ-dhīvataḥ ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Illustrious Pūṣan, you are a torrent of riches; you, who have a goat for your steed, are a heap of wealth; the friend of every worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Illustrious Pūṣan, you are a torrent of riches; you, who have a goat for your steed, are a heap of wealth; the friend of every worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषणं न्वजाश्वमुप स्तोषाम वाजिनं ।स्वसुर्यो जार उच्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣáṇam ǀ nú ǀ ajá-aśvam ǀ úpa ǀ stoṣāma ǀ vājínam ǀsvásuḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ jāráḥ ǀ ucyáte ǁ
verses.english_translation: We glorify Pūṣan, the rider of the goat, the giver of food, him who is called the gallant of his sister.
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify Pūṣan, the rider of the goat, the giver of food, him who is called the gallant of his sister.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मातुर्दिधिषुमब्रवं स्वसुर्जारः शृणोतु नः ।भ्रातेंद्रस्य सखा मम ॥
verses.transliteration: mātúḥ ǀ didhiṣúm ǀ abravam ǀ svásuḥ ǀ jāráḥ ǀ śṛṇotu ǀ naḥ ǀbhrā́tā ǀ índrasya ǀ sákhā ǀ máma ǁ
verses.english_translation: I glorify Pūṣan, the husband of his mother; may the gallant of his sister hear us; may the brother of Indrabe our friend.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify Pūṣan, the husband of his mother; may the gallant of his sister hear us; may the brother of Indrabe our friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आजासः पूषणं रथे निशृंभास्ते जनश्रियं ।देवं वहंतु बिभ्रतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ajā́saḥ ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ ráthe ǀ ni-śṛmbhā́ḥ ǀ té ǀ jana-śríyam ǀdevám ǀ vahantu ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the harnessed goats, drawing the deity in his car, bring hither Pūṣan, the benefactor of man.
verses.wilson_translation: May the harnessed goats, drawing the deity in his car, bring hither Pūṣan, the benefactor of man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI, Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHOSO remembers Pūṣan as cater of mingled curd and mealNeed think no more upon the God. And he is best of charioteers. Indra, the hero's Lord, alliedWith him as Friend, destroys the foes. And there the best of charioteers hath guided through the speckled cloudThe golden wheel of Sūra's car. Whate’er we speak this day to thee, Wise, Wondrous God whom many praise,Give thou fulfilment of our thought. Lead on this company of ours, that longs for kine, to win the spoil:Thou, Pūṣan, art renowned afar. Prosperity we crave from thee, afar from sin and near to wealth,Tending to perfect happiness both for to. morrow and to-day.

verses.sanskrit: य एनमादिदेशति करंभादिति पूषणं ।न तेन देव आदिशे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ enam ǀ ā-dídeśati ǀ karambha-át ǀ íti ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀná ǀ téna ǀ deváḥ ǀ ā-díśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: No (other) deity is indicated by him who declares the offering of mixed meal and butter to be intended for Pūṣan.
verses.wilson_translation: No (other) deity is indicated by him who declares the offering of mixed meal and butter to be intended for Pūṣan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत घा स रथीतमः सख्या सत्पतिर्युजा ।इंद्रो वृत्राणि जिघ्नते ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ gha ǀ sáḥ ǀ rathí-tamaḥ ǀ sákhyā ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ yujā́ ǀíndraḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jighnate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, the chief of charioteers, the protector of the virtuous,Indra, destroys his foes, with his friend Pūṣanfor his ally.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the chief of charioteers, the protector of the virtuous,Indra, destroys his foes, with his friend Pūṣanfor his ally.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उतादः परुषे गवि सूरश्चक्रं हिरण्ययं ।न्यैरयद्रथीतमः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ adáḥ ǀ paruṣé ǀ gávi ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cakrám ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀní ǀ airayat ǀ rathí-tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, the impeller, the chief of charioteers, (Pūṣan) ever urges on that golden wheel (of his car) for the radiant sun.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the impeller, the chief of charioteers, (Pūṣan) ever urges on that golden wheel (of his car) for the radiant sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदद्य त्वा पुरुष्टुत ब्रवाम दस्र मंतुमः ।तत्सु नो मन्म साधय ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ adyá ǀ tvā ǀ puru-stuta ǀ brávāma ǀ dasra ǀ mantu-maḥ ǀtát ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ mánma ǀ sādhaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Since, intelligent Pūṣan, of godly aspect, the praised of many, we celebrate you today, therefore grant us the desired wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Since, intelligent Pūṣan, of godly aspect, the praised of many, we celebrate you today, therefore grant us the desired wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं च नो गवेषणं सातये सीषधो गणं ।आरात्पूषन्नसि श्रुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ go-éṣaṇam ǀ sātáye ǀ sīsadhaḥ ǀ gaṇám ǀārā́t ǀ pūṣan ǀ asi ǀ śrutáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gratify this our assembly, desirous of cattle, by their acquisition; you,Pūṣan, are renowned afar.
verses.wilson_translation: Gratify this our assembly, desirous of cattle, by their acquisition; you,Pūṣan, are renowned afar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते स्वस्तिमीमह आरेअघामुपावसुं ।अद्या च सर्वतातये श्वश्च सर्वतातये ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ svastím ǀ īmahe ǀ āré-aghām ǀ úpa-vasum ǀadyá ǀ ca ǀ sarvá-tātaye ǀ śváḥ ǀ ca ǀ sarvá-tātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: We deserve of your well-being, remote from evil, approximate to wealth, both for the sake of genitive ral sacrifice today, for the sake of genitive ral sacrifice tomorrow.
verses.wilson_translation: We deserve of your well-being, remote from evil, approximate to wealth, both for the sake of genitive ral sacrifice today, for the sake of genitive ral sacrifice tomorrow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVII. Indra and Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INDRA and Pūṣan will we call for friend ship and prosperityAnd for the winning of the spoil. One by the Soma sits to drink juice which the mortar hath expressed:The other longs for curd and meal. Goats are the team that draws the one: the other hath Bay Steeds at hand;With both of these he slays the fiends. When Indra, wondrous strong, brought down the streams, the mighty waterfloods,Pūṣan was standing by his side. To this, to Pūṣan's favouring love, and Indra's, may we closely cling,As to a tree's extended bough. As one who drives a car draws in his reins, may we draw Pūṣan near,And Indra, for our great success.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रा नु पूषणा वयं सख्याय स्वस्तये ।हुवेम वाजसातये ॥
verses.transliteration: índrā ǀ nú ǀ pūṣáṇā ǀ vayám ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ svastáye ǀhuvéma ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you,Indraand Pūṣan, for your friendship, for our well-being, and for the obtaining of food.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you,Indraand Pūṣan, for your friendship, for our well-being, and for the obtaining of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सोममन्य उपासदत्पातवे चम्वोः सुतं ।करंभमन्य इच्छति ॥
verses.transliteration: sómam ǀ anyáḥ ǀ úpa ǀ asadat ǀ pā́tave ǀ camvóḥ ǀ sutám ǀkarambhám ǀ anyáḥ ǀ icchati ǁ
verses.english_translation: One (of you) approaches to drink the Somapoured out into ladles, the other desires the buttered meal.
verses.wilson_translation: One (of you) approaches to drink the Somapoured out into ladles, the other desires the buttered meal.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अजा अन्यस्य वह्नयो हरी अन्यस्य संभृता ।ताभ्यां वृत्राणि जिघ्नते ॥
verses.transliteration: ajā́ḥ ǀ anyásya ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ anyásya ǀ sám-bhṛtā ǀtā́bhyām ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jighnate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Goats are the bearers of the one, two well-fed horses of the other, and with them he destroys his foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Goats are the bearers of the one, two well-fed horses of the other, and with them he destroys his foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्रो अनयद्रितो महीरपो वृषंतमः ।तत्र पूषाभवत्सचा ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ índraḥ ǀ ánayat ǀ rítaḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣan-tamaḥ ǀtátra ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ abhavat ǀ sácā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the showerer Indrasends down the falling and mighty waters, there is Pūṣanalong with him.
verses.wilson_translation: When the showerer Indrasends down the falling and mighty waters, there is Pūṣanalong with him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तां पूष्णः सुमतिं वयं वृक्षस्य प्र वयामिव ।इंद्रस्य चा रभामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́m ǀ pūṣṇáḥ ǀ su-matím ǀ vayám ǀ vṛkṣásya ǀ prá ǀ vayā́m-iva ǀíndrasya ǀ ca ǀ ā́ ǀ rabhāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We depend upon the good-will of Pūṣan, and of Indra, as (we cling) to the branches of a tree.
verses.wilson_translation: We depend upon the good-will of Pūṣan, and of Indra, as (we cling) to the branches of a tree.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत्पूषणं युवामहेऽभीशूँरिव सारथिः ।मह्या इंद्रं स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ yuvāmahe ǀ abhī́śūn-iva ǀ sā́rathiḥ ǀmahyái ǀ índram ǀ svastáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: We draw to us, for our great welfare,Pūṣanand Indra, as a charioteer (pulls tight) his reins.
verses.wilson_translation: We draw to us, for our great welfare,Pūṣanand Indra, as a charioteer (pulls tight) his reins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Pūṣan.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIKE heaven art thou: one form is bright, one holy, like Day and Night dissimilar in colour.All magic powers thou aidest, self-depen. dent! Auspicious be thy bounty here, O Pūṣan. Goat-borne, the guard of cattle, he whose home is strength, inspirer of the hymn, set over all the world;Brandishing here and there his lightly. moving goad, beholding every creature, Pūṣan, God, goes forth. O Pūṣan, with thy golden ships that travel across the ocean, in the air's mid-region,Thou goest on an embassy to Sūrya, subdued by love, desirous of the glory. Near kinsman of the heaven and earth is Pūṣan, liberal, Lord of food, of wondrous iustre,Whom strong and vigorous and swiftlymoving, subdued by love, the Deities gave to Sūrya.

verses.sanskrit: शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि ।विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: śukrám ǀ te ǀ anyát ǀ yajatám ǀ te ǀ anyát ǀ víṣurūpe íti víṣu-rūpe ǀ áhanī íti ǀ dyáuḥ-iva ǀ asi ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ hí ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ ávasi ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ te ǀ pūṣan ǀ ihá ǀ rātíḥ ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of your forms, (Pūṣan), is luminous, one is venerable; so that the day is variously complexioned; for you are like the sun; verily, bestower of food, you protect all intelligence; may your auspicious liberality be manifested on this occasion.
verses.wilson_translation: One of your forms, (Pūṣan), is luminous, one is venerable; so that the day is variously complexioned; for you are like the sun; verily, bestower of food, you protect all intelligence; may your auspicious liberality be manifested on this occasion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अजाश्वः पशुपा वाजपस्त्यो धियंजिन्वो भुवने विश्वे अर्पितः ।अष्ट्रां पूषा शिथिरामुद्वरीवृजत्संचक्षाणो भुवना देव ईयते ॥
verses.transliteration: ajá-aśvaḥ ǀ paśu-pā́ḥ ǀ vā́ja-pastyaḥ ǀ dhiyam-jinváḥ ǀ bhúvane ǀ víśve ǀ árpitaḥ ǀáṣṭrām ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ śithirā́m ǀ ut-várīvṛjat ǀ sam-cákṣāṇaḥ ǀ bhúvanā ǀ deváḥ ǀ īyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The rider of the goat, the protector of animals, in whose dwelling good is abundant, the propitiated by sacred rites, who has been plural ced over the whole (world), the divine Pūṣan, brandishing his loosened goad, proceeds (in the sky), contemplating all beings.
verses.wilson_translation: The rider of the goat, the protector of animals, in whose dwelling good is abundant, the propitiated by sacred rites, who has been plural ced over the whole (world), the divine Pūṣan, brandishing his loosened goad, proceeds (in the sky), contemplating all beings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यास्ते पूषन्नावो अंतः समुद्रे हिरण्ययीरंतरिक्षे चरंति ।ताभिर्यासि दूत्यां सूर्यस्य कामेन कृत श्रव इच्छमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ pūṣan ǀ nā́vaḥ ǀ antáríti ǀ samudré ǀ hiraṇyáyīḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀ cáranti ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ yāsi ǀ dūtyā́m ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ kā́mena ǀ kṛta ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ icchámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With thos your golden vessels, which navigate within the ocean-firmament, you discharge the office of messenger of the sun; desirous of the sacrificial food, you are propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.
verses.wilson_translation: With thos your golden vessels, which navigate within the ocean-firmament, you discharge the office of messenger of the sun; desirous of the sacrificial food, you are propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा सुबंधुर्दिव आ पृथिव्या इळस्पतिर्मघवा दस्मवर्चाः ।यं देवासो अददुः सूर्यायै कामेन कृतं तवसं स्वंचं ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ su-bándhuḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ dasmá-varcāḥ ǀyám ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ádaduḥ ǀ sūryā́yai ǀ kā́mena ǀ kṛtám ǀ tavásam ǀ su-áñcam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣanis the kind kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of food, the possessor of opulence, of goodly form; whom the gods gave to Sūrya, vigorous, well-moving, propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣanis the kind kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of food, the possessor of opulence, of goodly form; whom the gods gave to Sūrya, vigorous, well-moving, propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIX. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I WILL declare, while juices flow, the manly deeds that ye have done:Your Fathers, enemies of Gods, were smitten down, and, Indra-Agni, ye survive. Thus, Indra-Agnip verily your greatness merits loftiest praise,Sprung from one common Father, brothers, twins are ye; your Mother is in every place. These who delight in flowing juice, like fellow horses at their food,Indra and Agni, Gods armed with the thunderbolt, we call this day to come with help. Indra and Agni, Friends of Law, served with rich gifts, your speech is kindTo him who praises you while these libations flow: that man, O Gods, ye ne’er consume. What mortal understands, O Gods, Indra and Agni, this your way?One of you, yoking Steeds that move to every side, advances in your common car. First, Indra-Agni, hath this Maid come footless unto those with feet.Stretching her head and speaking loudly with her tongue, she hath gone downward thirty steps. E’en now, O Indra-Agni, men hold in their arms and stretch their bows.Desert us not in this great fray, in battles for the sake of kine. The foeman's sinful enmities, Indra and Agni, vex me sore.Drive those who hate me far away, and keep them distant from the Sun. Indra and Agni, yours are all the treasures of the heavens and earth.Here give ye us the opulence that prospers every living man. O Indra-Agni, who accept the laud, and hear us for our praise,Come near us, drawn by all our songs, to drink of this our Soma juice.

verses.sanskrit: प्र नु वोचा सुतेषु वां वीर्या यानि चक्रथुः ।हतासो वां पितरो देवशत्रव इंद्राग्नी जीवथो युवं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nú ǀ voca ǀ sutéṣu ǀ vām ǀ vīryā́ ǀ yā́ni ǀ cakráthuḥ ǀhatā́saḥ ǀ vām ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ devá-śatravaḥ ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ jī́vathaḥ ǀ yuvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the libation is effused I celebrate,Indraand Agni, your heroic exploits; the Pitaras, the enemies of the gods, have been slain by you, and you survive.
verses.wilson_translation: When the libation is effused I celebrate,Indraand Agni, your heroic exploits; the Pitaras, the enemies of the gods, have been slain by you, and you survive.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बळित्था महिमा वामिंद्राग्नी पनिष्ठ आ ।समानो वां जनिता भ्रातरा युवं यमाविहेहमातरा ॥
verses.transliteration: báṭ ǀ itthā́ ǀ mahimā́ ǀ vām ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ pániṣṭhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀsamānáḥ ǀ vām ǀ janitā́ ǀ bhrā́tarā ǀ yuvám ǀ yamáu ǀ ihéha-mātarā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your greatness,Indraand Agni, is after this fashion, and is most deserving of praise; the same is your progenitor; twin brethren are you, having a mother everywhere present.
verses.wilson_translation: Your greatness,Indraand Agni, is after this fashion, and is most deserving of praise; the same is your progenitor; twin brethren are you, having a mother everywhere present.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ओकिवांसा सुते सचाँ अश्वा सप्ती इवादने ।इंद्रा न्वग्नी अवसेह वज्रिणा वयं देवा हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: oki-vā́ṃsā ǀ suté ǀ sácā ǀ áśvā ǀ sáptī ivéti sáptī-iva ǀ ā́dane ǀíndrā ǀ nú ǀ agnī́ íti ǀ ávasā ǀ ihá ǀ vajríṇā ǀ vayám ǀ devā́ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: You approach together, when the libation is effused, like two fleet coursers to their forage; we invoke today Indraand Agni, deities armed with the thunderbolt, to this ceremony for our preservation.
verses.wilson_translation: You approach together, when the libation is effused, like two fleet coursers to their forage; we invoke today Indraand Agni, deities armed with the thunderbolt, to this ceremony for our preservation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्वृतावृधा ।जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ sutéṣu ǀ vām ǀ stávat ǀ téṣu ǀ ṛta-vṛdhā ǀjoṣa-vākám ǀ vádataḥ ǀ pajra-hoṣiṇā ǀ ná ǀ devā ǀ bhasáthaḥ ǀ caná ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Indraand Agni, augmenters of sacrifice by whom the acclamation (of praise) is received, you partake not of the (Soma) of him who, when the libation is effused, praises you (improperly), uttering unacceptable eulogies.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Indraand Agni, augmenters of sacrifice by whom the acclamation (of praise) is received, you partake not of the (Soma) of him who, when the libation is effused, praises you (improperly), uttering unacceptable eulogies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी को अस्य वां देवौ मर्तश्चिकेतति ।विषूचो अश्वान्युयुजान ईयत एकः समान आ रथे ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ káḥ ǀ asyá ǀ vām ǀ dévau ǀ mártaḥ ǀ ciketati ǀvíṣūcaḥ ǀ áśvān ǀ yuyujānáḥ ǀ īyate ǀ ékaḥ ǀ samāné ǀ ā́ ǀ ráthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: What mortal, divine Indraand Agni, is a judge of that (your act), when one of you, harnessing his diversely-going horses, proceeds in the common car.
verses.wilson_translation: What mortal, divine Indraand Agni, is a judge of that (your act), when one of you, harnessing his diversely-going horses, proceeds in the common car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी अपादियं पूर्वागात्पद्वतीभ्यः ।हित्वी शिरो जिह्वया वावदच्चरत्त्रिंशत्पदा न्यक्रमीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ apā́t ǀ iyám ǀ pū́rvā ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ pat-vátībhyaḥ ǀhitvī́ ǀ śíraḥ ǀ jihváyā ǀ vā́vadat ǀ cárat ǀ triṃśát ǀ padā́ ǀ ní ǀ akramīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: This footless (dawn),Indraand Agni, comes before the footed sleepers, animating the head (of living beings with consciousness), causing them to utter loud sounds with their tongues, and passing onwards she traverses thirty steps.
verses.wilson_translation: This footless (dawn),Indraand Agni, comes before the footed sleepers, animating the head (of living beings with consciousness), causing them to utter loud sounds with their tongues, and passing onwards she traverses thirty steps.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी आ हि तन्वते नरो धन्वानि बाह्वोः ।मा नो अस्मिन्महाधने परा वर्क्तं गविष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ tanvaté ǀ náraḥ ǀ dhánvāni ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ asmín ǀ mahā-dhané ǀ párā ǀ varktam ǀ gó-iṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, men verily stretch their bows with their arms, but do not you desert us contending for cattle in the great combat.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, men verily stretch their bows with their arms, but do not you desert us contending for cattle in the great combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी तपंति माघा अर्यो अरातयः ।अप द्वेषांस्या कृतं युयुतं सूर्यादधि ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ tápanti ǀ mā ǀ aghā́ḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ árātayaḥ ǀápa ǀ dvéṣāṃsi ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛtam ǀ yuyutám ǀ sū́ryāt ǀ ádhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, murderous, aggressive enemies harasss us; drive away mine adversaries; separate them from (sight of) the sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, murderous, aggressive enemies harasss us; drive away mine adversaries; separate them from (sight of) the sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी युवोरपि वसु दिव्यानि पार्थिवा ।आ न इह प्र यच्छतं रयिं विश्वायुपोषसं ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ ápi ǀ vásu ǀ divyā́ni ǀ pā́rthivā ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ yacchatam ǀ rayím ǀ viśvā́yu-poṣasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, yours are both celestial and terrestrial treasures; bestow upon us, on this occasion, life-sustaining riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, yours are both celestial and terrestrial treasures; bestow upon us, on this occasion, life-sustaining riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी उक्थवाहसा स्तोमेभिर्हवनश्रुता ।विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरा गतमस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ uktha-vāhasā ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ havana-śrutā ǀvíśvābhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ asyá ǀ sómasya ǀ pītáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, who are to be attracted by hymns; you, who hear our invocation (accompanied) by praise and by all adorations, come hither to drink of this Somalibation.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, who are to be attracted by hymns; you, who hear our invocation (accompanied) by praise and by all adorations, come hither to drink of this Somalibation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LX. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE slays the foe and wins the spoil who worships Indra and Agni, strong and mighty Heroes,Who rule as Sovrans over ample riches, victorious, showing forth their power in conquest. So battle now, O Indra and thou, Agni, for cows and waters, sunlight, stolen Mornings.Team-borne, thou makest kine thine own, O Agni: thou, Indra, light, Dawns, regions, wondrous waters. With Vṛtra-slaying might, Indra and Agni, come, drawn by homage, O ye Vṛtra-slayers.Indra and Agni, show yourselves among us with your supreme and unrestricted bounties. I call the Twain whose deeds of old have all been famed in ancient daysO Indra-Agni, harm us not. The Strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni, we invoke;May they be kind to one like me. They slay our Ārya foes, these Lords of heroes, slay our Dasyu foesAnd drive our enemies away. Indra and Agni, these our songs of praise have sounded forth to you:Ye who bring blessings! drink the juice. Come, Indra-Agni, with those teams, desired of many, which ye have,O Heroes, for the worshipper. With those to this libation poured, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, come:Come ye to drink the Soma juice. Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing flame,And leaves them blackened with his tongue. He who gains Indra's bliss with fire enkindled finds an easy wayOver the floods to happiness. Give us fleet coursers to convey Indra and Agni, and bestowAbundant strengthening food on us. Indra and Agni, I will call you hither and make you joyful with the gifts I offer.Ye Twain are givers both of food and riches: to win me strength and vigour I invoke you. Come unto us with riches, come with wealth in horses and in kine.Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, the Gods, as Friends for friendship, bringing bliss. Indra and Agni, hear his call who worships. with libations poured.Come and enjoy the offerings, drink the sweetly-flavoured Soma juice.

verses.sanskrit: श्नथद्वृत्रमुत सनोति वाजमिंद्रा यो अग्नी सहुरी सपर्यात् ।इरज्यंता वसव्यस्य भूरेः सहस्तमा सहसा वाजयंता ॥
verses.transliteration: śnáthat ǀ vṛtrám ǀ utá ǀ sanoti ǀ vā́jam ǀ índrā ǀ yáḥ ǀ agnī́ íti ǀ sáhurī íti ǀ saparyā́t ǀirajyántā ǀ vasavyásya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ sáhaḥ-tamā ǀ sáhasā ǀ vāja-yántā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He ovecomes his enemy, and acquires food, who worships the victorious Indraand Agni, the lords of infinite opulence, most powerful in strength, desirous of (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: He ovecomes his enemy, and acquires food, who worships the victorious Indraand Agni, the lords of infinite opulence, most powerful in strength, desirous of (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता योधिष्टमभि गा इंद्र नूनमपः स्वरुषसो अग्न ऊळ्हाः ।दिशः स्वरुषस इंद्र चित्रा अपो गा अग्ने युवसे नियुत्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ yodhiṣṭam ǀ abhí ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ nūnám ǀ apáḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ agne ǀ ūḷhā́ḥ ǀdíśaḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ indra ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ yuvase ǀ niyútvān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, verily you have combated for (the recovery of) the cows, the waters, the sun, the dawns that had been carried away (by theasuras); you reunite, Indra (with the world), the quarters of the horizon, the sun, the wonderful waters, the dawns, the cattle and so do you, Agni, who have the Niyutsteeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, verily you have combated for (the recovery of) the cows, the waters, the sun, the dawns that had been carried away (by theasuras); you reunite, Indra (with the world), the quarters of the horizon, the sun, the wonderful waters, the dawns, the cattle and so do you, Agni, who have the Niyutsteeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरिंद्र यातं नमोभिरग्ने अर्वाक् ।युवं राधोभिरकवेभिरिंद्राग्ने अस्मे भवतमुत्तमेभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vṛtra-hanā ǀ vṛtrahá-bhiḥ ǀ śúṣmaiḥ ǀ índra ǀ yātám ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ arvā́k ǀyuvám ǀ rā́dhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ákavebhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ ágne ǀ asmé íti ǀ bhavatam ǀ ut-tamébhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayers of Vṛtra,Indraand Agni, come down with foe-subduing energies, (to be invigorated) by (our) offerings; be manifest to us, Indra and Agni, with unblameable and most excellent riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Slayers of Vṛtra,Indraand Agni, come down with foe-subduing energies, (to be invigorated) by (our) offerings; be manifest to us, Indra and Agni, with unblameable and most excellent riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता हुवे ययोरिदं पप्ने विश्वं पुरा कृतं ।इंद्राग्नी न मर्धतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ huve ǀ yáyoḥ ǀ idám ǀ papné ǀ víśvam ǀ purā́ ǀ kṛtám ǀindrāgnī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ mardhataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke those two, the whole of whose deeds of old have been celebrated;Indraand Agniharm us not.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke those two, the whole of whose deeds of old have been celebrated;Indraand Agniharm us not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उग्रा विघनिना मृध इंद्राग्नी हवामहे ।ता नो मृळात ईदृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ugrā́ ǀ vi-ghanínā ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ havāmahe ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mṛḷātaḥ ǀ īdṛ́śe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke the fierce Indraand Agni, the slayers of enemies; may they give us success in similar warfare.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke the fierce Indraand Agni, the slayers of enemies; may they give us success in similar warfare.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हतो वृत्राण्यार्या हतो दासानि सत्पती ।हतो विश्वा अप द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: hatáḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ ā́ryā ǀ hatáḥ ǀ dā́sāni ǀ sátpatī íti sát-patī ǀhatáḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ápa ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Counteract all oppressions (committed) by the pious; counteract all oppressions (committed) by the impious; protectors of the virtuous, destroy all those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: Counteract all oppressions (committed) by the pious; counteract all oppressions (committed) by the impious; protectors of the virtuous, destroy all those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी युवामिमेऽभि स्तोमा अनूषत ।पिबतं शंभुवा सुतं ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ yuvā́m ǀ imé ǀ abhí ǀ stómāḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀpíbatam ǀ śam-bhuvā ǀ sutám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, these hymns glorify you both; drink, bestowers of happiness, the libation.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, these hymns glorify you both; drink, bestowers of happiness, the libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या वां संति पुरुस्पृहो नियुतो दाशुषे नरा ।इंद्राग्नी ताभिरा गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ sánti ǀ puru-spṛ́haḥ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ narā ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Agni, leaders (of rites), whose Niyutsteeds are desired by many, come with them to the donor (of the libation).
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Agni, leaders (of rites), whose Niyutsteeds are desired by many, come with them to the donor (of the libation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ताभिरा गच्छतं नरोपेदं सवनं सुतं ।इंद्राग्नी सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gacchatam ǀ narā ǀ úpa ǀ idám ǀ sávanam ǀ sutám ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come with them, leaders (of rites),
verses.wilson_translation: Come with them, leaders (of rites),
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमीळिष्व यो अर्चिषा वना विश्वा परिष्वजत् ।कृष्णा कृणोति जिह्वया ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ īḷiṣva ǀ yáḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀ vánā ǀ víśvā ǀ pari-svájat ǀkṛṣṇā́ ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ jihváyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorify that Agniwho envelopes all the forest with flame, who blackens them with (his) tongue.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify that Agniwho envelopes all the forest with flame, who blackens them with (his) tongue.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इद्ध आविवासति सुम्नमिंद्रस्य मर्त्यः ।द्युम्नाय सुतरा अपः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ iddhé ǀ ā-vívāsati ǀ sumnám ǀ índrasya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀdyumnā́ya ǀ su-tárāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mortal who presents the gratifying (oblation) to Indrain the kindled (fire), to him (Indra grants) acceptable waters for his sustenance.
verses.wilson_translation: The mortal who presents the gratifying (oblation) to Indrain the kindled (fire), to him (Indra grants) acceptable waters for his sustenance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता नो वाजवतीरिष आशून्पिपृतमर्वतः ।इंद्रमग्निं च वोळ्हवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́ja-vatīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ āśū́n ǀ pipṛtam ǀ árvataḥ ǀíndram ǀ agním ǀ ca ǀ vóḷhave ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those two grant us strengthening food, and swift horses to convey (our offerings).
verses.wilson_translation: May those two grant us strengthening food, and swift horses to convey (our offerings).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उभा वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्या उभा राधसः सह मादयध्यै ।उभा दाताराविषां रयीणामुभा वाजस्य सातये हुवे वां ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhā́ ǀ vām ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ ā-huvádhyai ǀ ubhā́ ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ sahá ǀ mādayádhyai ǀubhā́ ǀ dātā́rau ǀ iṣā́m ǀ rayīṇā́m ǀ ubhā́ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ sātáye ǀ huve ǀ vām ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke you both,Indraand Agni, to be present at the sacrifice; and both together to be exhilarated by the (sacrificial) food; for you are both donors of food and riches, and therefore I invoke you both for the obtaining of sustenance.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke you both,Indraand Agni, to be present at the sacrifice; and both together to be exhilarated by the (sacrificial) food; for you are both donors of food and riches, and therefore I invoke you both for the obtaining of sustenance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो गव्येभिरश्व्यैर्वसव्यैरुप गच्छतं ।सखायौ देवौ सख्याय शंभुवेंद्राग्नी ता हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ gávyebhiḥ ǀ áśvyaiḥ ǀ vasavyáiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ gacchatam ǀsákhāyau ǀ deváu ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ śam-bhúvā ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ tā́ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us with herds of cattle, with troops of horses, with ample treasures, divine friends,Indraand Agni; givers of happiness, we invoke you as such for your friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us with herds of cattle, with troops of horses, with ample treasures, divine friends,Indraand Agni; givers of happiness, we invoke you as such for your friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी शृणुतं हवं यजमानस्य सुन्वतः ।वीतं हव्यान्या गतं पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ śṛṇutám ǀ hávam ǀ yájamānasya ǀ sunvatáḥ ǀvītám ǀ havyā́ni ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ píbatam ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear,Indraand Agni, the instrumental tutor of the rite as he offers the libation; partake of the offering; come, quaff the sweet Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear,Indraand Agni, the instrumental tutor of the rite as he offers the libation; partake of the offering; come, quaff the sweet Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXI. Sarasvatī.
hymns.anukramani: १४ बार्हस्पत्यो भरद्वाज: । सरस्वती। गायत्री; १-३, १३ जगती; १४ त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To Vadhryasva when. be worshipped her with gifts she gave fierce Divodāsa, canceller of debts.Consumer of the churlish niggard, one and all, thine, O Sarasvatī, are these effectual boons. She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.Let us invite with songs and holy hymns for help Sarasvatī who slayeth the Paravatas. Thou castest down, Sarasvatī, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Bṛsaya skilled in magic arts.Thou hast discovered rivers for the tribes of men, and, rich in wealth! made poison flow away from them. May the divine Sarasvatī, rich in her wealth, protect us well,Furthering all our thoughts with might Whoso, divine Sarasvatī, invokes thee where the prize is set,Like Indra when he smites the foe. Aid us, divine Sarasvad, thou who art strong in wealth and powerLike Pūṣan, give us opulence. Yea, this divine Sarasvatī, terrible with her golden path,Foe-slayer, claims our eulogy. Whose limitless unbroken flood, swift-moving with a rapid rush,Comes onward with tempestuous roar. She hath spread us beyond all foes, beyond her Sisters, Holy One,As Sūrya spreadeth out the days. Yea, she most dear amid dear stream, Seven-sistered, graciously inclined,Sarasvatī hath earned our praise. Guard us from hate Sarasvatī, she who hath filled the realms of earth,And that wide tract, the firmament! Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must beInvoked in every deed of might. Marked out by majesty among the Mighty Ones, in glory swifter than the other rapid Streams,Created vast for victory like a chariot, Sarasvatī must be extolled by every sage. Guide us, Sarasvatī, to glorious treasure: refuse us not thy milk, nor spurn us from thee.Gladly accept our friendship and obedience: let us not go from thee to distant countries.

verses.sanskrit: इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतं दिवोदासं वध्र्यश्वाय दाशुषे ।या शश्वंतमाचखादावसं पणिं ता ते दात्राणि तविषा सरस्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ adadāt ǀ rabhasám ǀ ṛṇa-cyútam ǀ dívaḥ-dāsam ǀ vadhri-aśvā́ya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀyā́ ǀ śáśvantam ǀ ā-cakhā́da ǀ avasám ǀ paṇím ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ dātrā́ṇi ǀ taviṣā́ ǀ sarasvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: She gave to the donor of the oblations, Vadhryaśva, a son Divodāsaendowed with speed, and acquitting the debt (due to gods and progenitors), she who destroyed the churlis niggard, (thinking) only of himself, such are your bounties,Sarasvatī.
verses.wilson_translation: She gave to the donor of the oblations, Vadhryaśva, a son Divodāsaendowed with speed, and acquitting the debt (due to gods and progenitors), she who destroyed the churlis niggard, (thinking) only of himself, such are your bounties,Sarasvatī.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः ।पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ śúṣmebhiḥ ǀ bisakhā́ḥ-iva ǀ arujat ǀ sā́nu ǀ girīṇā́m ǀ taviṣébhiḥ ǀ ūrmí-bhiḥ ǀpārāvata-ghnī́m ǀ ávase ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ sárasvatīm ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsema ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With impetuous and mighty waves she breaks down the precipices of the mountains, like a digger for the lotus fibres; we adore for our protection, the praises and with sacred rites,Sarasvatīthe underminer of both her banks.
verses.wilson_translation: With impetuous and mighty waves she breaks down the precipices of the mountains, like a digger for the lotus fibres; we adore for our protection, the praises and with sacred rites,Sarasvatīthe underminer of both her banks.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वति देवनिदो नि बर्हय प्रजां विश्वस्य बृसयस्य मायिनः ।उत क्षितिभ्योऽवनीरविंदो विषमेभ्यो अस्रवो वाजिनीवति ॥
verses.transliteration: sárasvati ǀ deva-nídaḥ ǀ ní ǀ barhaya ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ víśvasya ǀ bṛ́sayasya ǀ māyínaḥ ǀutá ǀ kṣití-bhyaḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ avindaḥ ǀ viṣám ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ asravaḥ ǀ vājinī-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroy,Sarasvatī, the revilers of the gods, the offspring of the universal deluder,Bṛsaya; giver of sustenance, you have acquired for men the lands (seized by theasuras), and have showered water upon them.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroy,Sarasvatī, the revilers of the gods, the offspring of the universal deluder,Bṛsaya; giver of sustenance, you have acquired for men the lands (seized by theasuras), and have showered water upon them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र णो देवी सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती ।धीनामवित्र्यवतु ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ vā́jebhiḥ ǀ vājínī-vatī ǀdhīnā́m ǀ avitrī́ ǀ avatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine Sarasvatī, the acceptress of (sacrificial) food, the protectress o her worshippers, sustain us with (abundant) viands.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Sarasvatī, the acceptress of (sacrificial) food, the protectress o her worshippers, sustain us with (abundant) viands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वा देवि सरस्वत्युपब्रूते धने हिते ।इंद्रं न वृत्रतूर्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ devi ǀ sarasvati ǀ upa-brūté ǀ dháne ǀ hité ǀíndram ǀ ná ǀ vṛtra-tū́rye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Sarasvatī, protect him engaged in conflict for the sake of wealth, who glorifies you like Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Sarasvatī, protect him engaged in conflict for the sake of wealth, who glorifies you like Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं देवि सरस्वत्यवा वाजेषु वाजिनि ।रदा पूषेव नः सनिं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ devi ǀ sarasvati ǀ áva ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ vājini ǀráda ǀ pūṣā́-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ saním ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Sarasvatī, abounding in food, protect us in combat, and, like Pūṣan, give us gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Sarasvatī, abounding in food, protect us in combat, and, like Pūṣan, give us gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्या नः सरस्वती घोरा हिरण्यवर्तनिः ।वृत्रघ्नी वष्टि सुष्टुतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ ghorā́ ǀ híraṇya-vartaniḥ ǀvṛtra-ghnī́ ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ su-stutím ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the fierce Sarasvatī, riding in a golden chariot, the destructress of enemies, be plural ased by our earnest laudation.
verses.wilson_translation: May the fierce Sarasvatī, riding in a golden chariot, the destructress of enemies, be plural ased by our earnest laudation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्या अनंतो अह्रुतस्त्वेषश्चरिष्णुरर्णवः ।अमश्चरति रोरुवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yásyāḥ ǀ anantáḥ ǀ áhrutaḥ ǀ tveṣáḥ ǀ cariṣṇúḥ ǀ arṇaváḥ ǀámaḥ ǀ cárati ǀ róruvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May she whose might, infinite, undeviating, splendid, progressive, water-shedding, proceeds loud-sounding.
verses.wilson_translation: May she whose might, infinite, undeviating, splendid, progressive, water-shedding, proceeds loud-sounding.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सा नो विश्वा अति द्विषः स्वसॄरन्या ऋतावरी ।अतन्नहेव सूर्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ svásṝḥ ǀ anyā́ḥ ǀ ṛtá-varī ǀátan ǀ áhā-iva ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Overcome all our adversaries, and bring to us her other water-laden sisters, as the ever-rolling sun (leads on) the days.
verses.wilson_translation: Overcome all our adversaries, and bring to us her other water-laden sisters, as the ever-rolling sun (leads on) the days.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत नः प्रिया प्रियासु सप्तस्वसा सुजुष्टा ।सरस्वती स्तोम्या भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ priyā́ ǀ priyā́su ǀ saptá-svasā ǀ sú-juṣṭā ǀsárasvatī ǀ stómyā ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Sarasvatī, who has seven sisters, who is dearest among those dear to us, and is fully propitiated, be ever adorable.
verses.wilson_translation: May Sarasvatī, who has seven sisters, who is dearest among those dear to us, and is fully propitiated, be ever adorable.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आपप्रुषी पार्थिवान्युरु रजो अंतरिक्षं ।सरस्वती निदस्पातु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-paprúṣī ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ urú ǀ rájaḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀsárasvatī ǀ nidáḥ ǀ pātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Sarasvatī, filing (with radiance) the expanse of earth and heaven, defend us from the reviled.
verses.wilson_translation: May Sarasvatī, filing (with radiance) the expanse of earth and heaven, defend us from the reviled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिषधस्था सप्तधातुः पंच जाता वर्धयंती ।वाजेवाजे हव्या भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-sadhásthā ǀ saptá-dhātuḥ ǀ páñca ǀ jātā́ ǀ vardháyantī ǀvā́je-vāje ǀ hávyā ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Abiding in thethree worlds, comprising seven elements, cherishing the five races (of beings), she is ever to be invoked in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Abiding in thethree worlds, comprising seven elements, cherishing the five races (of beings), she is ever to be invoked in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र या महिम्ना महिनासु चेकिते द्युम्नेभिरन्या अपसामपस्तमा ।रथ इव बृहती विभ्वने कृतोपस्तुत्या चिकितुषा सरस्वती ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yā́ ǀ mahimnā́ ǀ mahínā ǀ āsu ǀ cékite ǀ dyumnébhiḥ ǀ anyā́ḥ ǀ apásām ǀ apáḥ-tamā ǀráthaḥ-iva ǀ bṛhatī́ ǀ vi-bhváne ǀ kṛtā́ ǀ upa-stútyā ǀ cikitúṣā ǀ sárasvatī ǁ
verses.english_translation: She who is disinguished among them as eminent in greatness and in her glories; she who is the most impetuous of all other streams; she who as been created vast in capacity as a chariot, she,Sarasvatī, is to be glorified by the discree (worshippers)
verses.wilson_translation: She who is disinguished among them as eminent in greatness and in her glories; she who is the most impetuous of all other streams; she who as been created vast in capacity as a chariot, she,Sarasvatī, is to be glorified by the discree (worshippers)
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यो माप स्फरीः पयसा मा न आ धक् ।जुषस्व नः सख्या वेश्या च मा त्वत्क्षेत्राण्यरणानि गन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: sárasvati ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ neṣi ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ápa ǀ spharīḥ ǀ páyasā ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dhak ǀjuṣásva ǀ naḥ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ veśyā́ ǀ ca ǀ mā́ ǀ tvát ǀ kṣétrāṇi ǀ áraṇāni ǀ ganma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Guide us,Sarasvatī, to precious wealth; reduce us no to insignificance; overwhelm us not with (excess of) water; be plural ased by our friendly (services) and access to our habitations, and let us not repair to plural ces unacceptable to you.
verses.wilson_translation: Guide us,Sarasvatī, to precious wealth; reduce us no to insignificance; overwhelm us not with (excess of) water; be plural ased by our friendly (services) and access to our habitations, and let us not repair to plural ces unacceptable to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I LAUD the Heroes Twain, this heaven's Controllers: singing with songs of praise I call the Aśvins,Fain in a moment, when the morns are breaking, to part the earth's ends and the spacious regions. Moving to sacrifice through realms of lustre they light the radiance of the car that bears them.Traversing many wide unmeasured spaces, over the wastes ye pass, and fields, and waters. Ye to that bounteous path of yours, ye mighty, have ever borne away our thoughts with horses,Mind-swift and full of vigour, that the trouble of man who offers gifts might cease and slumber. So ye, when ye have yoked your chariothorses, come to the hymn of the most recent singer.Our true and ancient Herald Priest shall bring you, the Youthful, bearing splendour, food, and vigour. With newest hymn I call those Wonder-Workers, ancient and brilliant, and exceeding mighty,Bringers of bliss to him who lauds and praises, bestowing varied bounties on the singer. So ye, with birds, out of the sea and waters bore Bhujyu, son of Tugra, through the regions.Speeding with winged steeds through dustless spaces, out of the bosom of the flood they bore him. Victors, car-borne, ye rent the rock asunder: Bulls, heard the calling of the eunuch's consort.Bounteous, ye filled the cow with milk for Śayu: thus, swift and zealous Ones, ye showed your favour. Whate’er from olden time, Heaven, Earth! existeth great object of the wrath of Gods and mortals,Make that, Ādityas, Vasus, sons of Rudra, an evil brand to one allied with demons. May he who knows, as Varuṇa and Mitra, air's realm, appointing both the Kings in season,Against the secret fiend cast forth his weapon, against the lying words that strangers utter. Come to our home with friendly wheels, for offipring; come on your radiant chariot rich in heroes.Strike off, ye Twain, the heads of our assailants who with man's treacherous attack approach us. Come hitherward to us with teams of horses, the highest and the midmost and the lowest.Bountiful Lords, throw open to the singer doors e’en of the firm-closed stall of cattle.

verses.sanskrit: स्तुषे नरा दिवो अस्य प्रसंताश्विना हुवे जरमाणो अर्कैः ।या सद्य उस्रा व्युषि ज्मो अंतान्युयूषतः पर्युरू वरांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: stuṣé ǀ nárā ǀ diváḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pra-sántā ǀ aśvínā ǀ huve ǀ járamāṇaḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀyā́ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ usrā́ ǀ vi-úṣi ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántān ǀ yúyūṣataḥ ǀ pári ǀ urú ǀ várāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: I praise the two leaders of heaven, the presiders over this world; I invoke the Aśvins, glorifying them with sacred hymns, them, who are ever the discomfiture (of foes), who at dawn scatter the investing glooms to the ends of the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise the two leaders of heaven, the presiders over this world; I invoke the Aśvins, glorifying them with sacred hymns, them, who are ever the discomfiture (of foes), who at dawn scatter the investing glooms to the ends of the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता यज्ञमा शुचिभिश्चक्रमाणा रथस्य भानुं रुरुचू रजोभिः ।पुरू वरांस्यमिता मिमानापो धन्वान्यति याथो अज्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ śúci-bhiḥ ǀ cakramāṇā́ ǀ ráthasya ǀ bhānúm ǀ rurucuḥ ǀ rájaḥ-bhiḥ ǀpurú ǀ várāṃsi ǀ ámitā ǀ mímānā ǀ apáḥ ǀ dhánvāni ǀ áti ǀ yāthaḥ ǀ ájrān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Coming to the sacrifice with their bright splendours, they light up the lustre of (their) car; emitting vast and infinite radiance; they drive their horses over deserts (refreshing them) with water.
verses.wilson_translation: Coming to the sacrifice with their bright splendours, they light up the lustre of (their) car; emitting vast and infinite radiance; they drive their horses over deserts (refreshing them) with water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता ह त्यद्वर्तिर्यदरध्रमुग्रेत्था धिय ऊहथुः शश्वदश्वैः ।मनोजवेभिरिषिरैः शयध्यै परि व्यथिर्दाशुषो मर्त्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ vartíḥ ǀ yát ǀ áradhram ǀ ugrā ǀ itthā́ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ śáśvat ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀmánaḥ-javebhiḥ ǀ iṣiráiḥ ǀ śayádhyai ǀ pári ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ mártyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce Aśvins, from thhat humble mansion to which (you have repaired), you have ever borne with your desirable horses, as swift as thought, the pious worshippers in some manner (to heaven); let the injurer of the liberal man (be consigned by you) to (final) repose.
verses.wilson_translation: Fierce Aśvins, from thhat humble mansion to which (you have repaired), you have ever borne with your desirable horses, as swift as thought, the pious worshippers in some manner (to heaven); let the injurer of the liberal man (be consigned by you) to (final) repose.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता नव्यसो जरमाणस्य मन्मोप भूषतो युयुजानसप्ती ।शुभं पृक्षमिषमूर्जं वहंता होता यक्षत्प्रत्नो अध्रुग्युवाना ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ návyasaḥ ǀ járamāṇasya ǀ mánma ǀ úpa ǀ bhūṣataḥ ǀ yuyujānásaptī íti yuyujāná-saptī ǀśúbham ǀ pṛ́kṣam ǀ íṣam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ váhantā ǀ hótā ǀ yakṣat ǀ pratnáḥ ǀ adhrúk ǀ yúvānā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harnessing their horses, bringing excellent food, nourishment, and strength, they approach (to receive) the adoration of their recent worshipper; and may the benevolent ancient invoker of the gods (Agni) sacrifice to the ever youthful (deities).
verses.wilson_translation: Harnessing their horses, bringing excellent food, nourishment, and strength, they approach (to receive) the adoration of their recent worshipper; and may the benevolent ancient invoker of the gods (Agni) sacrifice to the ever youthful (deities).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता वल्गू दस्रा पुरुशाकतमा प्रत्ना नव्यसा वचसा विवासे ।या शंसते स्तुवते शंभविष्ठा बभूवतुर्गृणते चित्रराती ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ valgū́ íti ǀ dasrā́ ǀ puruśā́ka-tamā ǀ pratnā́ ǀ návyasā ǀ vácasā ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāse ǀyā́ ǀ śáṃsate ǀ stuvaté ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhā ǀ babhūvátuḥ ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ citrárātī íti citrá-rātī ǁ
verses.english_translation: I worship with a new hymn those two quick-moving good-looking ancient (Aśvins), the achievers of many exploits, who are the givers of great felicity to him who prays to (them), or praises (them); the bestowers of wondrous gifts on him who adores (them).
verses.wilson_translation: I worship with a new hymn those two quick-moving good-looking ancient (Aśvins), the achievers of many exploits, who are the givers of great felicity to him who prays to (them), or praises (them); the bestowers of wondrous gifts on him who adores (them).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता भुज्युं विभिरद्भ्यः समुद्रात्तुग्रस्य सूनुमूहथू रजोभिः ।अरेणुभिर्योजनेभिर्भुजंता पतत्रिभिरर्णसो निरुपस्थात् ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ bhujyúm ǀ ví-bhiḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ samudrā́t ǀ túgrasya ǀ sūnúm ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ rájaḥ-bhiḥ ǀareṇú-bhiḥ ǀ yójanebhiḥ ǀ bhujántā ǀ patatrí-bhiḥ ǀ árṇasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ upá-sthāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: They bore up from te waters, from the ocean, by the winged horses attached to their car, (passing) by roads unsoiled by dust,Bhujyu, the son of Tugra; they (bore them) from out of the lap of the water.
verses.wilson_translation: They bore up from te waters, from the ocean, by the winged horses attached to their car, (passing) by roads unsoiled by dust,Bhujyu, the son of Tugra; they (bore them) from out of the lap of the water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि जयुषा रथ्या यातमद्रिं श्रुतं हवं वृषणा वध्रिमत्याः ।दशस्यंता शयवे पिप्यथुर्गामिति च्यवाना सुमतिं भुरण्यू ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ jayúṣā ǀ rathyā ǀ yātam ǀ ádrim ǀ śrutám ǀ hávam ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ vadhri-matyā́ḥ ǀdaśasyántā ǀ śayáve ǀ pipyathuḥ ǀ gā́m ǀ íti ǀ cyavānā ǀ su-matím ǀ bhuraṇyū íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Riders in your car, you have penetrated the mountain by your triumphant chariot; showerers (of benefits) you heard the invocation of Vadhrimatī; you have nourished, bountiful givers, the cow ofŚayu-- and in this manner displaying benevolence are you everywhere present.
verses.wilson_translation: Riders in your car, you have penetrated the mountain by your triumphant chariot; showerers (of benefits) you heard the invocation of Vadhrimatī; you have nourished, bountiful givers, the cow ofŚayu-- and in this manner displaying benevolence are you everywhere present.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्रोदसी प्रदिवो अस्ति भूमा हेळो देवानामुत मर्त्यत्रा ।तदादित्या वसवो रुद्रियासो रक्षोयुजे तपुरघं दधात ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ rodasī íti ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ bhū́ma ǀ héḷaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ utá ǀ martya-trā́ ǀtát ǀ ādityāḥ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ rudriyāsaḥ ǀ rakṣaḥ-yúje ǀ tápuḥ ǀ aghám ǀ dadhāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heaven and Earth, Ādiyas,Vasus,Maruts, rende that dread ange of the gods which (has) of old (been directed) against mortals, destructive and fatal to him who is associated with therākṣasas.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and Earth, Ādiyas,Vasus,Maruts, rende that dread ange of the gods which (has) of old (been directed) against mortals, destructive and fatal to him who is associated with therākṣasas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य ईं राजानावृतुथा विदधद्रजसो मित्रो वरुणश्चिकेतत् ।गंभीराय रक्षसे हेतिमस्य द्रोघाय चिद्वचस आनवाय ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ rā́jānau ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ vi-dádhat ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ cíketat ǀgambhīrā́ya ǀ rákṣase ǀ hetím ǀ asya ǀ dróghāya ǀ cit ǀ vácase ǀ ā́navāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitraand Varuṇarecognize him who of all the world worships the royal (Aśvins) in due season; he hurls his weapon against the strongrākṣasa, against the malignant menaces of man.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇarecognize him who of all the world worships the royal (Aśvins) in due season; he hurls his weapon against the strongrākṣasa, against the malignant menaces of man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अंतरैश्चक्रैस्तनयाय वर्तिर्द्युमता यातं नृवता रथेन ।सनुत्येन त्यजसा मर्त्यस्य वनुष्यतामपि शीर्षा ववृक्तं ॥
verses.transliteration: ántaraiḥ ǀ cakráiḥ ǀ tánayāya ǀ vartíḥ ǀ dyu-mátā ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ nṛ-vátā ǀ ráthena ǀsánutyena ǀ tyájasā ǀ mártyasya ǀ vanuṣyatā́m ǀ ápi ǀ śīrṣā́ ǀ vavṛktam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come with your shining and well-guided chariot, (fitted) with excellen wheels, to our dwelling, (to bestow upon us)maleoffspring; cut off with secret indignation the heads of those obstructing (the adoration) of the mortal (who worships you).
verses.wilson_translation: Come with your shining and well-guided chariot, (fitted) with excellen wheels, to our dwelling, (to bestow upon us)maleoffspring; cut off with secret indignation the heads of those obstructing (the adoration) of the mortal (who worships you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ परमाभिरुत मध्यमाभिर्नियुद्भिर्यातमवमाभिरर्वाक् ।दृळ्हस्य चिद्गोमतो वि व्रजस्य दुरो वर्तं गृणते चित्रराती ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ paramā́bhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ madhyamā́bhiḥ ǀ niyút-bhiḥ ǀ yātam ǀ avamā́bhiḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀdṛḷhásya ǀ cit ǀ gó-mataḥ ǀ ví ǀ vrajásya ǀ dúraḥ ǀ vartam ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ citrarātī íti citra-rātī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come down, whether with the most excellent, or middling, or inferior Niyutsteeds; set upon the doors of the fast-shutstall of the cattle; eb bountiful to him who praises you.
verses.wilson_translation: Come down, whether with the most excellent, or middling, or inferior Niyutsteeds; set upon the doors of the fast-shutstall of the cattle; eb bountiful to him who praises you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIII. Aśvins.
