verses.english_translation: I invoke for you with this hymn,Agni, the son of strength, the kind, the most knowing, the unobstructed;the fit object of sacred rites, the messenger of all the immortals.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke for you with this hymn,Agni, the son of strength, the kind, the most knowing, the unobstructed;the fit object of sacred rites, the messenger of all the immortals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स योजते अरुषा विश्वभोजसा स दुद्रवत्स्वाहुतः ।सुब्रह्मा यज्ञः सुशमी वसूनां देवं राधो जनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ yojate ǀ aruṣā́ ǀ viśvá-bhojasā ǀ sáḥ ǀ dudravat ǀ sú-āhutaḥ ǀsu-bráhmā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ su-śámī ǀ vásūnām ǀ devám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ jánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he harness his brilliant protecting (steeds to his car), when earnestly invoked; may he hasten (tobring the gods); may the sacrificial wealth of the worshippers (proceed to) that deity who is the giver of abundantfood, the adorable, the doer of great deeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May he harness his brilliant protecting (steeds to his car), when earnestly invoked; may he hasten (tobring the gods); may the sacrificial wealth of the worshippers (proceed to) that deity who is the giver of abundantfood, the adorable, the doer of great deeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदस्य शोचिरस्थादाजुह्वानस्य मीळ्हुषः ।उद्धूमासो अरुषासो दिविस्पृशः समग्निमिंधते नरः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ asya ǀ śocíḥ ǀ asthāt ǀ ā-júhvānasya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀút ǀ dhūmā́saḥ ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ divi-spṛ́śaḥ ǀ sám ǀ agním ǀ indhate ǀ náraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The radiance of that showerer (of benefits), repeatedly invoked, rises up, as does the fiery sky-lambentsmoke when men kindle Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The radiance of that showerer (of benefits), repeatedly invoked, rises up, as does the fiery sky-lambentsmoke when men kindle Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा दूतं कृण्महे यशस्तमं देवाँ आ वीतये वह ।विश्वा सूनो सहसो मर्तभोजना रास्व तद्यत्त्वेमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ dūtám ǀ kṛṇmahe ǀ yaśáḥ-tamam ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vītáye ǀ vaha ǀvíśvā ǀ sūno íti ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ marta-bhójanā ǀ rā́sva ǀ tát ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ ī́mahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We constitute you our most renowned messenger; bring the gods to partake (of the oblations); bestowupon us, son of strength, all human blessings; whatsoever we solicit of you.
verses.wilson_translation: We constitute you our most renowned messenger; bring the gods to partake (of the oblations); bestowupon us, son of strength, all human blessings; whatsoever we solicit of you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्ने गृहपतिस्त्वं होता नो अध्वरे ।त्वं पोता विश्ववार प्रचेता यक्षि वेषि च वार्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ tvám ǀ hótā ǀ naḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀtvám ǀ pótā ǀ viśva-vāra ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǀ yákṣi ǀ véṣi ǀ ca ǀ vā́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: All-desired Agni, you are the lord of the mansion; you are the invoker of the gods; you are the assistantpriest; do you, who are wise, present (the oblation to the gods), and partake (of it yourself).
verses.wilson_translation: All-desired Agni, you are the lord of the mansion; you are the invoker of the gods; you are the assistantpriest; do you, who are wise, present (the oblation to the gods), and partake (of it yourself).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृधि रत्नं यजमानाय सुक्रतो त्वं हि रत्नधा असि ।आ न ऋते शिशीहि विश्वमृत्विजं सुशंसो यश्च दक्षते ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛdhí ǀ rátnam ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ tvám ǀ hí ǀ ratna-dhā́ḥ ǀ ási ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ṛté ǀ śiśīhi ǀ víśvam ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀ su-śáṃsaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ dákṣate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Doer of good deeds, bestow treasure upon the instrumental tutor of the solemnity, for you are the bestower oftreasure; inspire all the priests at our sacrifice; (prosper him) who, offering worthy praise, is prosperouṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Doer of good deeds, bestow treasure upon the instrumental tutor of the solemnity, for you are the bestower oftreasure; inspire all the priests at our sacrifice; (prosper him) who, offering worthy praise, is prosperouṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे अग्ने स्वाहुत प्रियासः संतु सूरयः ।यंतारो ये मघवानो जनानामूर्वांदयंत गोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ agne ǀ su-āhuta ǀ priyā́saḥ ǀ santu ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀyantā́raḥ ǀ yé ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ūrvā́n ǀ dáyanta ǀ gónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, piously invoked, may those devout worshippers be dear to you, who are liberal, opulent, and thebestowers upon man of herds of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, piously invoked, may those devout worshippers be dear to you, who are liberal, opulent, and thebestowers upon man of herds of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: येषामिळा घृतहस्ता दुरोण आँ अपि प्राता निषीदति ।तांस्त्रायस्व सहस्य द्रुहो निदो यच्छा नः शर्म दीर्घश्रुत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yéṣām ǀ íḷā ǀ ghṛtá-hastā ǀ duroṇé ǀ ā́ ǀ ápi ǀ prātā́ ǀ ni-sī́dati ǀtā́n ǀ trāyasva ǀ sahasya ǀ druháḥ ǀ nidáḥ ǀ yáccha ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ dīrgha-śrút ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strength-bestowing Agni, protect from the oppressor and the revilers those in whose dwelling Iḷā,butter-handed, sits down satisfied, and grant to us felicity long renowned; Iḷā, butter-handed: iḷā ghṛtahastā= annarūpa havirlakṣaṇādevī, a goddess, the impersonation of food, that is, of sacrificial food, or theoblation person nified].
verses.wilson_translation: Strength-bestowing Agni, protect from the oppressor and the revilers those in whose dwelling Iḷā,butter-handed, sits down satisfied, and grant to us felicity long renowned; Iḷā, butter-handed: iḷā ghṛtahastā= annarūpa havirlakṣaṇādevī, a goddess, the impersonation of food, that is, of sacrificial food, or theoblation person nified].
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स मंद्रया च जिह्वया वह्निरासा विदुष्टरः ।अग्ने रयिं मघवद्भ्यो न आ वह हव्यदातिं च सूदय ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ mandráyā ǀ ca ǀ jihváyā ǀ váhniḥ ǀ āsā́ ǀ vidúḥ-taraḥ ǀágne ǀ rayím ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ havyá-dātim ǀ ca ǀ sūdaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The most wise Agniis the bearer (of oblations), as the mouth of the gods with his graceful tongue (offlame); bring riches, Agni, to the affluent (in sacrifices); encourage the donor of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: The most wise Agniis the bearer (of oblations), as the mouth of the gods with his graceful tongue (offlame); bring riches, Agni, to the affluent (in sacrifices); encourage the donor of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये राधांसि ददत्यश्व्या मघा कामेन श्रवसो महः ।ताँ अंहसः पिपृहि पर्तृभिष्ट्वं शतं पूर्भिर्यविष्ठ्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ rā́dhāṃsi ǀ dádati ǀ áśvyā ǀ maghā́ ǀ kā́mena ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀtā́n ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ pipṛhi ǀ partṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ tvám ǀ śatám ǀ pūḥ-bhíḥ ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Youngest (of the gods), protect with your protections from iniquity, (and reward) with numerous citiesthose who, through the desire of extended fame, bestow riches, comprehending horses and treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Youngest (of the gods), protect with your protections from iniquity, (and reward) with numerous citiesthose who, through the desire of extended fame, bestow riches, comprehending horses and treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवो वो द्रविणोदाः पूर्णां विवष्ट्यासिचं ।उद्वा सिंचध्वमुप वा पृणध्वमादिद्वो देव ओहते ॥
verses.transliteration: deváḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ pūrṇā́m ǀ vivaṣṭi ǀ ā-sícam ǀút ǀ vā ǀ siñcádhvam ǀ úpa ǀ vā ǀ pṛṇadhvam ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ vaḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ ohate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Agni, the giver of wealth, desires the ladle filled full. Pour out (the contents), and replenish(the vessel), and then the deity bears (your oblations to the gods).
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Agni, the giver of wealth, desires the ladle filled full. Pour out (the contents), and replenish(the vessel), and then the deity bears (your oblations to the gods).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं होतारमध्वरस्य प्रचेतसं वह्निं देवा अकृण्वत ।दधाति रत्नं विधते सुवीर्यमग्निर्जनाय दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ hótāram ǀ adhvarásya ǀ prá-cetasam ǀ váhnim ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ akṛṇvata ǀdádhāti ǀ rátnam ǀ vidhaté ǀ su-vī́ryam ǀ agníḥ ǀ jánāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gods have made the wise (Agni) the ministrant priest, and bearer of the sacrifice. Agni giives to theman who performs the prescribed rite and presents (the offering), wealth, with virtuousmaleposterity.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have made the wise (Agni) the ministrant priest, and bearer of the sacrifice. Agni giives to theman who performs the prescribed rite and presents (the offering), wealth, with virtuousmaleposterity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, be kindled well with proper fuel, and let the grass be scattered wide about thee. Let the impatient Portals be thrown open bring thou the Gods impatient to come hither. Taste, Agni: serve the Gods with our oblation. Offer good sacrifices, Jātavedas! Let Jātavedas pay fair sacrifices, worship andgratify the Gods Immortal. Wise God, win for us things that are all-goodly, and let the prayers, we pray today be fruitful. Thee, even thee, the Son of Strength, O Agni, those Gods have made the bearer of oblations. To thee the God may we perform our worship: do thou, besought, grant us abundant riches.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने भव सुषमिधा समिद्ध उत बर्हिरुर्विया वि स्तृणीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ bháva ǀ su-samídhā ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ utá ǀ barhíḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ stṛṇītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be kindled,Agni, with suitable fuel; let the (priest) strew the plural ntiful sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Be kindled,Agni, with suitable fuel; let the (priest) strew the plural ntiful sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत द्वार उशतीर्वि श्रयंतामुत देवाँ उशत आ वहेह ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ dvā́raḥ ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ śrayantām ǀ utá ǀ devā́n ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the willing doors and the chamber of sacrifice be thrown open; bring hither the willing gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the willing doors and the chamber of sacrifice be thrown open; bring hither the willing gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने वीहि हविषा यक्षि देवान्त्स्वध्वरा कृणुहि जातवेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ vīhí ǀ havíṣā ǀ yákṣi ǀ devā́n ǀ su-adhvarā́ ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni Jātavedas, repair to the gods, worship them with the oblation, render them plural ased by thesacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni Jātavedas, repair to the gods, worship them with the oblation, render them plural ased by thesacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वध्वरा करति जातवेदा यक्षद्देवाँ अमृतान्पिप्रयच्च ॥
verses.transliteration: su-adhvarā́ ǀ karati ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ yákṣat ǀ devā́n ǀ amṛ́tān ǀ pipráyat ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Jātavedasrender the immortal gods, plural ased by the sacrifice; let him sacrifice (to them), andgratify them (with praise).
verses.wilson_translation: May Jātavedasrender the immortal gods, plural ased by the sacrifice; let him sacrifice (to them), andgratify them (with praise).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वंस्व विश्वा वार्याणि प्रचेतः सत्या भवंत्वाशिषो नो अद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: váṃsva ǀ víśvā ǀ vā́ryāṇi ǀ praceta íti pra-cetaḥ ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ bhavantu ǀ ā-śíṣaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestow upon us, sage,Agni, all desirable (riches); may the blessings (vouchsafed) to us this day besacrificed.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow upon us, sage,Agni, all desirable (riches); may the blessings (vouchsafed) to us this day besacrificed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामु ते दधिरे हव्यवाहं देवासो अग्न ऊर्ज आ नपातं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ té ǀ dadhire ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ agne ǀ ūrjáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ nápātam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gods have made you,Agni, who are the son of strength, the bearer of the oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have made you,Agni, who are the son of strength, the bearer of the oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते ते देवाय दाशतः स्याम महो नो रत्ना वि दध इयानः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ te ǀ devā́ya ǀ dā́śataḥ ǀ syāma ǀ maháḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ rátnā ǀ ví ǀ dadhaḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we be the presenters (of offerings) to you who are divine; and you, the mighty one, being solicited,bestow upon us treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be the presenters (of offerings) to you who are divine; and you, the mighty one, being solicited,bestow upon us treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XVIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ALL is with thee, O Indra, all the treasures which erst our fathers won who sang thy praises.With thee are milch-kine good to milk, and horses: best winner thou of riches for the pious. For like a King among his wives thou dwellest: with glories, as a Sage, surround and help us.Make us, thy servants, strong for wealth, and honour our songs wirth kine and steeds and decoration. Here these our holy hymns with joy and gladness in pious emulation have approached thee.Hitherward come thy path that leads to riches: may we find shelter in thy favour, Indra. Vasiṣṭha hath poured forth his prayers, desiring to milk thee like a cow in goodly pasture.All these my people call thee Lord of cattle: may Indra. come unto the prayer we offer. What though the floods spread widely, Indra made them shallow and easy for Sudās to traverse.He, worthy of our praises, caused the Simyu, foe of our hymn, to curse the rivers' fury. Eager for spoil was Turvaśa Purodas, fain to win wealth, like fishes urged by hunger.The Bhṛgus and the Druhyus quickly listened: friend rescued friend mid the two distant peoples. Together came the Pakthas, the Bhalanas, the Alinas, the Sivas, the Visanins.Yet to the Trtsus came the Ārya's Comrade, through love of spoil and heroes' war, to lead them. Fools, in their folly fain to waste her waters, they parted inexhaustible Paruṣṇī.Lord of the Earth, he with his might repressed them: still lay the herd and the affrighted herdsman. As to their goal they sped to their destruetion: they sought Paruṣṇī; e’en the swift returned not.Indra abandoned, to Sudās the manly, the swiftly flying foes, unmanly babblers. They went like kine unherded from the pasture, each clinging to a friend as chance directed.They who drive spotted steeds, sent down by Pṛśni, gave ear, the Warriors and the harnessed horses. The King who scattered one-and-twenty people of both Vaikarna tribes through lust of glory-As the skilled priest clips grass within the chamber, so hath the Hero Indra, wrought their downfall. Thou, thunder-armed, o’erwhelmedst in the waters famed ancient Kavasa and then the Druhyu.Others here claiming friendship to their friendship, devoted unto thee, in thee were joyful. Indra at once with conquering might demolished all their strong places and their seven castles.The goods of Anu's son he gave to Trtsu. May we in sacrifice conquer scorned Pūru. The Anavas and Druhyus, seeking booty, have slept, the sixty hundred, yea, six thousand,And six-and-sixty heroes. For the pious were all these mighty exploits done by Indra. These Trtsus under Indra's careful guidance came speeding like loosed waters rushing downward.The foemen, measuring exceeding closely, abandoned to Sudās all their provisions. The hero's side who drank the dressed oblation, Indra's denier, far o’er earth he scattered.Indra brought down the fierce destroyer's fury. He gave them various roads, the path's Controller. E’en with the weak he wrought this matchless exploit: e’en with a goat he did to death a lion.He pared the pillar's angles with a needle. Thus to Sudās Indra gave all provisions. To thee have all thine enemies submitted: e’en the fierce Bheda hast thou made thy subject.Cast down thy sharpened thunderbolt, O Indra, on him who harms the men who sing thy praises. Yamuna and the Trtsus aided Indra. There he stripped Bheda bare of all his treasures.The Ajas and the Sigrus and the Yaksus brought in to him as tribute heads of horses. Not to be scorned, but like Dawns past and recent, O Indra, are thy favours and thy riches.Devaka, Mānyamana's son, thou slewest, and smotest Śambara from the lofty mountain. They who, from home, have gladdened thee, thy servants Parasara, Vasiṣṭha, Satayatu,Will not forget thy friendship, liberal Giver. So shall the days dawn prosperous for the princes. Priest-like, with praise, I move around the altar, earning Paijavana's reward, O Agni,Two hundred cows from Devavan's descendant, two chariots from Sudās with mares to draw them. Gift of Paijavana, four horses bear me in foremost place, trained steeds with pearl to deck them.Sudās's brown steeds, firmly-stepping, carry me and my son for progeny and glory. Him whose fame spreads between wide earth and heaven, who, as dispenser, gives each chief his portion,Seven flowing Rivers glorify like Indra. He slew Yudhyamadhi in close encounter. Attend on him O ye heroic Maruts as on Sudās's father Divodāsa.Further Paijavana's desire with favour. Guard faithfully his lasting firm dominion.

verses.sanskrit: त्वे ह यत्पितरश्चिन्न इंद्र विश्वा वामा जरितारो असन्वन् ।त्वे गावः सुदुघास्त्वे ह्यश्वास्त्वं वसु देवयते वनिष्ठः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ cit ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ víśvā ǀ vāmā́ ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ ásanvan ǀtvé íti ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ su-dúghāḥ ǀ tvé íti ǀ hí ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ tvám ǀ vásu ǀ deva-yaté ǀ vániṣṭhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our forefathers,Indra, glorifying you, have obtained all desirable (riches); in your gift are cows easy tobe milked, and horses, and you are the liberal donor of wealth to the devout.
verses.wilson_translation: Our forefathers,Indra, glorifying you, have obtained all desirable (riches); in your gift are cows easy tobe milked, and horses, and you are the liberal donor of wealth to the devout.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: राजेव हि जनिभिः क्षेष्येवाव द्युभिरभि विदुष्कविः सन् ।पिशा गिरो मघवन्गोभिरश्वैस्त्वायतः शिशीहि राये अस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: rā́jā-iva ǀ hí ǀ jáni-bhiḥ ǀ kṣéṣi ǀ evá ǀ áva ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vidúḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ sán ǀpiśā́ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ tvā-yatáḥ ǀ śiśīhi ǀ rāyé ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: You dwell with your glories like arājāwith his wives;Maghavan, who are wise and experienced,(reward our) praises with the precious metals, with cows, with horses; conduct us who are dependent on yourriches.
verses.wilson_translation: You dwell with your glories like arājāwith his wives;Maghavan, who are wise and experienced,(reward our) praises with the precious metals, with cows, with horses; conduct us who are dependent on yourriches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा उ त्वा पस्पृधानासो अत्र मंद्रा गिरो देवयंतीरुप स्थुः ।अर्वाची ते पथ्या राय एतु स्याम ते सुमताविंद्र शर्मन् ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ paspṛdhānā́saḥ ǀ átra ǀ mandrā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ deva-yántīḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sthuḥ ǀarvā́cī ǀ te ǀ pathyā́ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ etu ǀ syā́ma ǀ te ǀ su-matáu ǀ indra ǀ śárman ǁ
verses.english_translation: These gratifying and pious hymns, emulous (in earnestness), are addressed on this occasion to you,may the path of your riches lead downwards; may we,Indra, (diligent) in your praise, enjoy felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: These gratifying and pious hymns, emulous (in earnestness), are addressed on this occasion to you,may the path of your riches lead downwards; may we,Indra, (diligent) in your praise, enjoy felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धेनुं न त्वा सूयवसे दुदुक्षन्नुप ब्रह्माणि ससृजे वसिष्ठः ।त्वामिन्मे गोपतिं विश्व आहा न इंद्रः सुमतिं गंत्वच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: dhenúm ǀ ná ǀ tvā ǀ su-yávase ǀ dúdhukṣan ǀ úpa ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ sasṛje ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ ít ǀ me ǀ gó-patim ǀ víśvaḥ ǀ āha ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-matím ǀ gantu ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desirous of milking you like a milch cow at pasture,Vasiṣṭhahas let loose his prayers to you; everyone of my people proclaims you the lord of cattle; may Indrabe present at our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of milking you like a milch cow at pasture,Vasiṣṭhahas let loose his prayers to you; everyone of my people proclaims you the lord of cattle; may Indrabe present at our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्णांसि चित्पप्रथाना सुदास इंद्रो गाधान्यकृणोत्सुपारा ।शर्धंतं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शापं सिंधूनामकृणोदशस्तीः ॥
verses.transliteration: árṇāṃsi ǀ cit ǀ paprathānā́ ǀ su-dā́se ǀ índraḥ ǀ gādhā́ni ǀ akṛṇot ǀ su-pārā́ ǀśárdhantam ǀ śimyúm ǀ ucáthasya ǀ návyaḥ ǀ śā́pam ǀ síndhūnām ǀ akṛṇot ǀ áśastīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The adorable Indramade the well-known deep waters (of the Paruṣṇi) fordable for Sudāsa, andconverted the vehement awakening imprecation of the sacrificer into the calumnation of the rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: The adorable Indramade the well-known deep waters (of the Paruṣṇi) fordable for Sudāsa, andconverted the vehement awakening imprecation of the sacrificer into the calumnation of the rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरोळा इत्तुर्वशो यक्षुरासीद्राये मत्स्यासो निशिता अपीव ।श्रुष्टिं चक्रुर्भृगवो द्रुह्यवश्च सखा सखायमतरद्विषूचोः ॥
verses.transliteration: puroḷā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ turváśaḥ ǀ yákṣuḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ rāyé ǀ mátsyāsaḥ ǀ ní-śitāḥ ǀ ápi-iva ǀśruṣṭím ǀ cakruḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ druhyávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ sákhā ǀ sákhāyam ǀ atarat ǀ víṣūcoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Turvaśa, who was presiding (at solemn rites), diligent in sacrifice, (went to Sudāsa) for wealth; but likefishes restricted (to the element of water), the Bhrigusand Druhyusquickly assailed them; of these twoeverywhere going the friend (of Sudāsa,Indra) rescued his friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Turvaśa, who was presiding (at solemn rites), diligent in sacrifice, (went to Sudāsa) for wealth; but likefishes restricted (to the element of water), the Bhrigusand Druhyusquickly assailed them; of these twoeverywhere going the friend (of Sudāsa,Indra) rescued his friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ पक्थासो भलानसो भनंतालिनासो विषाणिनः शिवासः ।आ योऽनयत्सधमा आर्यस्य गव्या तृत्सुभ्यो अजगन्युधा नॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ pakthā́saḥ ǀ bhalānásaḥ ǀ bhananta ǀ ā́ ǀ álināsaḥ ǀ viṣāṇínaḥ ǀ śivā́saḥ ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ánayat ǀ sadha-mā́ḥ ǀ ā́ryasya ǀ gavyā́ ǀ tṛ́tsu-bhyaḥ ǀ ajagan ǀ yudhā́ ǀ nṝ́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those who dress the oblation, those who pronounce auspicious words, those who abstain frompenance, those who bear horns (in theirhands), those who bestow happiness (on the world by sacrifice), glorifythat Indra, who recovered the cattle of the Aryafrom the plural nderers, who slew the enemies in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who dress the oblation, those who pronounce auspicious words, those who abstain frompenance, those who bear horns (in theirhands), those who bestow happiness (on the world by sacrifice), glorifythat Indra, who recovered the cattle of the Aryafrom the plural nderers, who slew the enemies in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दुराध्यो अदितिं स्रेवयंतोऽचेतसो वि जगृभ्रे परुष्णीं ।मह्नाविव्यक्पृथिवीं पत्यमानः पशुष्कविरशयच्चायमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: duḥ-ādhyáḥ ǀ áditim ǀ sreváyantaḥ ǀ acetásaḥ ǀ ví ǀ jagṛbhre ǀ páruṣṇīm ǀmahnā́ ǀ avivyak ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ pátyamānaḥ ǀ paśúḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ aśayat ǀ cā́yamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The evil-disposed and stupid (enemies of Sudāsa), crossing the humble Paruṣṇi river, have brokendown its banks; but he by his greatness pervades the earth, and Kavi, the son of Cāyamana, like a fallingvictim, sleeps (in death).
verses.wilson_translation: The evil-disposed and stupid (enemies of Sudāsa), crossing the humble Paruṣṇi river, have brokendown its banks; but he by his greatness pervades the earth, and Kavi, the son of Cāyamana, like a fallingvictim, sleeps (in death).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईयुरर्थं न न्यर्थं परुष्णीमाशुश्चनेदभिपित्वं जगाम ।सुदास इंद्रः सुतुकाँ अमित्रानरंधयन्मानुषे वध्रिवाचः ॥
verses.transliteration: īyúḥ ǀ ártham ǀ ná ǀ ni-arthám ǀ páruṣṇīm ǀ āśúḥ ǀ caná ǀ ít ǀ abhi-pitvám ǀ jagāma ǀsu-dā́se ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-túkān ǀ amítrān ǀ árandhayat ǀ mā́nuṣe ǀ vádhri-vācaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The waters followed their regular course to the Paruṣṇi, nor (wandered) beyond it; the quick courser(of the king) came to the accessible plural ces, and Indramade the idly-talking enemies, with their numerousprogeny, subject among men (to Sudāsa).
verses.wilson_translation: The waters followed their regular course to the Paruṣṇi, nor (wandered) beyond it; the quick courser(of the king) came to the accessible plural ces, and Indramade the idly-talking enemies, with their numerousprogeny, subject among men (to Sudāsa).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईयुर्गावो न यवसादगोपा यथाकृतमभि मित्रं चितासः ।पृश्निगावः पृश्निनिप्रेषितासः श्रुष्टिं चक्रुर्नियुतो रंतयश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: īyúḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yávasāt ǀ ágopāḥ ǀ yathā-kṛtám ǀ abhí ǀ mitrám ǀ citā́saḥ ǀpṛ́śni-gāvaḥ ǀ pṛ́śni-nipreṣitāsaḥ ǀ śruṣṭím ǀ cakruḥ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ rántayaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who ride on particoloured cattle, (the Maruts), despatched by Pṛṣṇiand recalling theengagement made by them with their friend (Indra), came like cattle from the pasturage, when left without aherdsman; the exulting Niyutsteeds brought them quickly (against the foe).
verses.wilson_translation: They who ride on particoloured cattle, (the Maruts), despatched by Pṛṣṇiand recalling theengagement made by them with their friend (Indra), came like cattle from the pasturage, when left without aherdsman; the exulting Niyutsteeds brought them quickly (against the foe).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एकं च यो विंशतिं च श्रवस्या वैकर्णयोर्जनान्राजा न्यस्तः ।दस्मो न सद्मन्नि शिशाति बर्हिः शूरः सर्गमकृणोदिंद्र एषां ॥
verses.transliteration: ékam ǀ ca ǀ yáḥ ǀ viṃśatím ǀ ca ǀ śravasyā́ ǀ vaikarṇáyoḥ ǀ jánān ǀ rā́jā ǀ ní ǀ ástarityástaḥ ǀdasmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ sádman ǀ ní ǀ śiśāti ǀ barhíḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ sárgam ǀ akṛṇot ǀ índraḥ ǀ eṣām ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hero Indracreated the Maruts(for the assistance of therājā), who, ambitious of fame, slewone-and-twenty of the men on the two banks (of the Paruṣṇi), as a well-looking priest lops the sacred grass inthe chamber of sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: The hero Indracreated the Maruts(for the assistance of therājā), who, ambitious of fame, slewone-and-twenty of the men on the two banks (of the Paruṣṇi), as a well-looking priest lops the sacred grass inthe chamber of sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध श्रुतं कवषं वृद्धमप्स्वनु द्रुह्युं नि वृणग्वज्रबाहुः ।वृणाना अत्र सख्याय सख्यं त्वायंतो ये अमदन्ननु त्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ śrutám ǀ kaváṣam ǀ vṛddhám ǀ ap-sú ǀ ánu ǀ druhyúm ǀ ní ǀ vṛṇak ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǀvṛṇānā́ḥ ǀ átra ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ sakhyám ǀ tvā-yántaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ámadan ǀ ánu ǀ tvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: You, the bearer of the thunderbolt, did drownŚruta,Kavaṣa,Vṛddhaand afterwards Druhyu, in thewaters; for they,Indra, who are devoted to you, and glorify you, preferring your friendship, enjoy it.
verses.wilson_translation: You, the bearer of the thunderbolt, did drownŚruta,Kavaṣa,Vṛddhaand afterwards Druhyu, in thewaters; for they,Indra, who are devoted to you, and glorify you, preferring your friendship, enjoy it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि सद्यो विश्वा दृंहितान्येषामिंद्रः पुरः सहसा सप्त दर्दः ।व्यानवस्य तृत्सवे गयं भाग्जेष्म पूरुं विदथे मृध्रवाचं ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ dṛṃhitā́ni ǀ eṣām ǀ índraḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ sáhasā ǀ saptá ǀ dardaríti dardaḥ ǀví ǀ ā́navasya ǀ tṛ́tsave ǀ gáyam ǀ bhāk ǀ jéṣma ǀ pūrúm ǀ vidáthe ǀ mṛdhrá-vācam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, in his might, quickly demolished all their strongholds, and their seven (kinds of) cities; he hasgiven the dwelling of the son of Anu to Tṛtsu; may we, (by propitiating Indra), conquer in battle the ill-speakingman.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, in his might, quickly demolished all their strongholds, and their seven (kinds of) cities; he hasgiven the dwelling of the son of Anu to Tṛtsu; may we, (by propitiating Indra), conquer in battle the ill-speakingman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि गव्यवोऽनवो द्रुह्यवश्च षष्टिः शता सुषुपुः षट् सहस्रा ।षष्टिर्वीरासो अधि षड्दुवोयु विश्वेदिंद्रस्य वीर्या कृतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ gavyávaḥ ǀ ánavaḥ ǀ druhyávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ śatā́ ǀ susupuḥ ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ sahásrā ǀṣaṣṭíḥ ǀ vīrā́saḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ duvaḥ-yú ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ índrasya ǀ vīryā́ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: The warriors of the Anus and Druhyus, intending (to carry off the) cattle, (hostile) to the pious(Sudāsa) perished to the number of sixty-six thousand six hundred and sixty; such are all the glorious acts of Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: The warriors of the Anus and Druhyus, intending (to carry off the) cattle, (hostile) to the pious(Sudāsa) perished to the number of sixty-six thousand six hundred and sixty; such are all the glorious acts of Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रेणैते तृत्सवो वेविषाणा आपो न सृष्टा अधवंत नीचीः ।दुर्मित्रासः प्रकलविन्मिमाना जहुर्विश्वानि भोजना सुदासे ॥
verses.transliteration: índreṇa ǀ eté ǀ tṛ́tsavaḥ ǀ véviṣāṇāḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ sṛṣṭā́ḥ ǀ adhavanta ǀ nī́cīḥ ǀduḥ-mitrā́saḥ ǀ prakala-vít ǀ mímānāḥ ǀ jahúḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhójanā ǀ su-dā́se ǁ
verses.english_translation: These hostile, Tṛtsus, ignorantly contending with Indra, fled routed as rapidly as rivers on a downwardcourse, and being discomfited, abandoned all their possessions to Sudāsa.
verses.wilson_translation: These hostile, Tṛtsus, ignorantly contending with Indra, fled routed as rapidly as rivers on a downwardcourse, and being discomfited, abandoned all their possessions to Sudāsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्धं वीरस्य शृतपामनिंद्रं परा शर्धंतं नुनुदे अभि क्षां ।इंद्रो मन्युं मन्युम्यो मिमाय भेजे पथो वर्तनिं पत्यमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ardhám ǀ vīrásya ǀ śṛta-pā́m ǀ anindrám ǀ párā ǀ śárdhantam ǀ nunude ǀ abhí ǀ kṣā́m ǀíndraḥ ǀ manyúm ǀ manyu-bhyáḥ ǀ mimāya ǀ bhejé ǀ patháḥ ǀ vartaním ǀ pátyamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrahas scattered over the earth the hostile rival of the hero (Sudāsa), the senior of Indra, theappropriator of the oblation; Indra has baffled the wrath of the wratfhful enemy, and the (foe) advancing on theway (against Sudāsa) has taken the path of flight.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas scattered over the earth the hostile rival of the hero (Sudāsa), the senior of Indra, theappropriator of the oblation; Indra has baffled the wrath of the wratfhful enemy, and the (foe) advancing on theway (against Sudāsa) has taken the path of flight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आध्रेण चित्तद्वेकं चकार सिंह्यं चित्पेत्वेना जघान ।अव स्रक्तीर्वेश्यावृश्चदिंद्रः प्रायच्छद्विश्वा भोजना सुदासे ॥
verses.transliteration: ādhréṇa ǀ cit ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ékam ǀ cakāra ǀ siṃhyám ǀ cit ǀ pétvena ǀ jaghāna ǀáva ǀ sraktī́ḥ ǀ veśyā́ ǀ avṛścat ǀ índraḥ ǀ prá ǀ ayacchat ǀ víśvā ǀ bhójanā ǀ su-dā́se ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, has effected a valuable (donation) by a pauper; he has slain an old lion by a goat; he has cut theangles of the sacrificialpostwith a needle; he has given all the spoils (of the enemy) to Sudāsa.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, has effected a valuable (donation) by a pauper; he has slain an old lion by a goat; he has cut theangles of the sacrificialpostwith a needle; he has given all the spoils (of the enemy) to Sudāsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शश्वंतो हि शत्रवो रारधुष्टे भेदस्य चिच्छर्धतो विंद रंधिं ।मर्ताँ एनः स्तुवतो यः कृणोति तिग्मं तस्मिन्नि जहि वज्रमिंद्र ॥
verses.transliteration: śáśvantaḥ ǀ hí ǀ śátravaḥ ǀ raradhúḥ ǀ te ǀ bhedásya ǀ cit ǀ śárdhataḥ ǀ vinda ǀ rándhim ǀmártān ǀ énaḥ ǀ stuvatáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ tigmám ǀ tásmin ǀ ní ǀ jahi ǀ vájram ǀ indra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your numerous enemies,Indra, have been reduced to subjection, effect at some time or other thesubjugation of the turbulent Bheda, who holds men praising you as guilty of wickedness; hurl, Indra, your sharpthuderbolt against him.
verses.wilson_translation: Your numerous enemies,Indra, have been reduced to subjection, effect at some time or other thesubjugation of the turbulent Bheda, who holds men praising you as guilty of wickedness; hurl, Indra, your sharpthuderbolt against him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आवदिंद्रं यमुना तृत्सवश्च प्रात्र भेदं सर्वताता मुषायत् ।अजासश्च शिग्रवो यक्षवश्च बलिं शीर्षाणि जभ्रुरश्व्यानि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́vat ǀ índram ǀ yamúnā ǀ tṛ́tsavaḥ ǀ ca ǀ prá ǀ átra ǀ bhedám ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀ muṣāyat ǀajā́saḥ ǀ ca ǀ śígravaḥ ǀ yákṣavaḥ ǀ ca ǀ balím ǀ śīrṣā́ṇi ǀ jabhruḥ ǀ áśvyāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: The dwellers on the Yamunaand the Tṛtsus glorified Indrawhen he killed Bhedain battle; the Ajas, theŚigrus, the Yakṣas, offered him as a sacrifice the heads of the horses (killed in the combat).
verses.wilson_translation: The dwellers on the Yamunaand the Tṛtsus glorified Indrawhen he killed Bhedain battle; the Ajas, theŚigrus, the Yakṣas, offered him as a sacrifice the heads of the horses (killed in the combat).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न त इंद्र सुमतयो न रायः संचक्षे पूर्वा उषसो न नूत्नाः ।देवकं चिन्मान्यमानं जघंथाव त्मना बृहतः शंबरं भेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ su-matáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ sam-cákṣe ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ nū́tnāḥ ǀdévakam ǀ cit ǀ mānyamānám ǀ jaghantha ǀ áva ǀ tmánā ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ śámbaram ǀ bhet ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your favours,Indra, and your bounties, whether old or new, cannot be counted like the (recurring)dawn; you have slain Devaka, the son of Mānyamāna, and of thine own will, has cast downŚambarafrom thevast (mountain).
verses.wilson_translation: Your favours,Indra, and your bounties, whether old or new, cannot be counted like the (recurring)dawn; you have slain Devaka, the son of Mānyamāna, and of thine own will, has cast downŚambarafrom thevast (mountain).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ये गृहादममदुस्त्वाया पराशरः शतयातुर्वसिष्ठः ।न ते भोजस्य सख्यं मृषंताधा सूरिभ्यः सुदिना व्युच्छान् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ gṛhā́t ǀ ámamaduḥ ǀ tvā-yā́ ǀ parā-śaráḥ ǀ śatá-yātuḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀná ǀ te ǀ bhojásya ǀ sakhyám ǀ mṛṣanta ǀ ádha ǀ sūrí-bhyaḥ ǀ su-dínā ǀ ví ǀ ucchān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Parāśara, the destroyer of hundreds (ofrākṣasas), and Vasiṣṭhathey who, devoted to you, haveglorified you in every dwelling, neglect not the friendship of you (their) benefactor; therefore prosperous daysdawn upon the pious.
verses.wilson_translation: Parāśara, the destroyer of hundreds (ofrākṣasas), and Vasiṣṭhathey who, devoted to you, haveglorified you in every dwelling, neglect not the friendship of you (their) benefactor; therefore prosperous daysdawn upon the pious.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: द्वे नप्तुर्देववतः शते गोर्द्वा रथा वधूमंता सुदासः ।अर्हन्नग्ने पैजवनस्य दानं होतेव सद्म पर्येमि रेभन् ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ náptuḥ ǀ devá-vataḥ ǀ śaté íti ǀ góḥ ǀ dvā́ ǀ ráthā ǀ vadhū́-mantā ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀárhan ǀ agne ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ dā́nam ǀ hótā-iva ǀ sádma ǀ pári ǀ emi ǀ rébhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praising the liberality of Sudāsa, the grandson of Devavat, the son of Paijavana, the donor of twohundred cows, and of two chariots with two wives, I, worthy (of the gift), circumambulate you,Agni, like theministrant priest in the chamber (of sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: Praising the liberality of Sudāsa, the grandson of Devavat, the son of Paijavana, the donor of twohundred cows, and of two chariots with two wives, I, worthy (of the gift), circumambulate you,Agni, like theministrant priest in the chamber (of sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारो मा पैजवनस्य दानाः स्मद्दिष्टयः कृशनिनो निरेके ।ऋज्रासो मा पृथिव���ष्ठाः सुदासस्तोकं तोकाय श्रवसे वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: catvā́raḥ ǀ mā ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ dā́nāḥ ǀ smát-diṣṭayaḥ ǀ kṛśanínaḥ ǀ nireké ǀṛjrā́saḥ ǀ mā ǀ pṛthivi-sthā́ḥ ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀ tokám ǀ tokā́ya ǀ śrávase ǀ vahanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Four (horses), having golden trappings, going steadily on a difficult road, celebrated on the earth, theexcellent and acceptable gifts (made) to me by Sudāsa, the son of Paijavana, bear me as a son (to obtain) foodand progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: Four (horses), having golden trappings, going steadily on a difficult road, celebrated on the earth, theexcellent and acceptable gifts (made) to me by Sudāsa, the son of Paijavana, bear me as a son (to obtain) foodand progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य श्रवो रोदसी अंतरुर्वी शीर्ष्णेशीर्ष्णे विबभाजा विभक्ता ।सप्तेदिंद्रं न स्रवतो गृणंति नि युध्यामधिमशिशादभीके ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antáḥ ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ śīrṣṇé-śīrṣṇe ǀ vi-babhā́ja ǀ vi-bhaktā́ ǀsaptá ǀ ít ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ sravátaḥ ǀ gṛṇanti ǀ ní ǀ yudhyāmadhím ǀ aśiśāt ǀ abhī́ke ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven worlds praise (Sudāsa) as if he were Indra; him whose fame (spreads) through thespacious heaven and earth; who, munificent, has distributed (wealth) on every eminent person n, and (for him) theflowing (rivers) have destroyed Yudhyamadhi in war.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven worlds praise (Sudāsa) as if he were Indra; him whose fame (spreads) through thespacious heaven and earth; who, munificent, has distributed (wealth) on every eminent person n, and (for him) theflowing (rivers) have destroyed Yudhyamadhi in war.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चतानु दिवोदासं न पितरं सुदासः ।अविष्टना पैजवनस्य केतं दूणाशं क्षत्रमजरं दुवोयु ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ naraḥ ǀ marutaḥ ǀ saścata ǀ ánu ǀ dívaḥ-dāsam ǀ ná ǀ pitáram ǀ su-dā́saḥ ǀaviṣṭána ǀ paija-vanásya ǀ kétam ǀ duḥ-náśam ǀ kṣatrám ǀ ajáram ǀ duvaḥ-yú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, leaders (of rites), attend upon this (prince) as you did upon Divodāsa, the father of Sudāsa;favour the prayers of the devout son of Pijavana, and may his strength be unimpaired, undecaying].
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, leaders (of rites), attend upon this (prince) as you did upon Divodāsa, the father of Sudāsa;favour the prayers of the devout son of Pijavana, and may his strength be unimpaired, undecaying].
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE like a bull with sharpened horns, terrific, singly excites and agitates all the people:Thou givest him who largely pours libations his goods who pours not, for his own possession. Thou, verily, Indra, gavest help to Kutsa, willingly giving car to him in battle,When, aiding Ārjuneya, thou subduedst to him both Kuyava and the Dāsa Śuṣṇa. O Bold One, thou with all thine aids hast boldly holpen Sudās whose offerings were accepted,Pūru in winning land and slaying foemen, and Trasadasyu son of Purukutsa. At the Gods’ banquet, hero-souled! with Heroes, Lord of Bay Steeds, thou slewest many foemen.Thou sentest in swift death to sleep the Dasyu, both Cumuri and Dhuni, for Dabhīti. These were thy mighty powers that, Thunder-wielder, thou swiftly crushedst nine-and-ninety castles:Thou capturedst the hundredth in thine onslaught; thou slewest Namuci, thou slewest Vṛtra. Old are the blessings, Indra, which thou gavest Sudās the worshipper who brought oblations.For thee, the Strong, I yoke thy strong Bay Horses: may our prayers reach thee and win strength, Most Mighty! Give us not up, Lord of Bay Horses, Victor, in this thine own assembly, to the wicked.Deliver us with true and faithful succours: dear may we be to thee among the princes. May we men, Maghavan, the friends thou lovest, near thee be joyful under thy protection.Fain to fulfil the wish of Atithigva humble. the pride of Turvaśa and Yadva. Swiftly, in truth, O Maghavan, about thee men skilled in hymning sing their songs and praises. 'Elect us also into their assembly who by their calls on thee despoiled the niggards. Thine are these lauds, O manliest of heroes, lauds which revert to us and give us riches.Favour these, Indra, when they fight with faemen, as Friend and Hero and the heroes' Helper. Now, lauded for thine aid, Heroic Indra, sped by our prayer, wax mighty in thy body.Apportion to us strength and habitations. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: यस्तिग्मशृंगो वृषभो न भीम एकः कृष्टीश्च्यावयति प्र विश्वाः ।यः शश्वतो अदाशुषो गयस्य प्रयंतासि सुष्वितराय वेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tigmá-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ cyaváyati ǀ prá ǀ víśvāḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ śáśvataḥ ǀ ádāśuṣaḥ ǀ gáyasya ǀ pra-yantā́ ǀ asi ǀ susví-tarāya ǀ védaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who is formidable as a sharp-horned bull, singly expels all men (from their stations); you who arethe despoiler of the ample wealth of him who makes no offerings are the giver of riches to the presenter offrequent oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is formidable as a sharp-horned bull, singly expels all men (from their stations); you who arethe despoiler of the ample wealth of him who makes no offerings are the giver of riches to the presenter offrequent oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह त्यदिंद्र कुत्समावः शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये ।दासं यच्छुष्णं कुयवं न्यस्मा अरंधय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ indra ǀ kútsam ǀ āvaḥ ǀ śúśrūṣamāṇaḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ sa-maryé ǀdā́sam ǀ yát ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ kúyavam ǀ ní ǀ asmai ǀ árandhayaḥ ǀ ārjuneyā́ya ǀ śíkṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aiding him with your person n,Indra, you had defended Kutsain combat when you had subjugated Dāsa,Śuṣṇaand Kuyava, giving (their spoil) to that son of Arjuni.
verses.wilson_translation: Aiding him with your person n,Indra, you had defended Kutsain combat when you had subjugated Dāsa,Śuṣṇaand Kuyava, giving (their spoil) to that son of Arjuni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं धृष्णो धृषता वीतहव्यं प्रावो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सुदासं ।प्र पौरुकुत्सिं त्रसदस्युमावः क्षेत्रसाता वृत्रहत्येषु पूरुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ vītá-havyam ǀ prá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ su-dā́sam ǀprá ǀ páuru-kutsim ǀ trasádasyum ǀ āvaḥ ǀ kṣétra-sātā ǀ vṛtra-hátyeṣu ǀ pūrúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Undaunted (Indra), you had protected with all your protections Sudāsa, the offerer of oblations; youhave protected in battles with enemies for the possession of the earth Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and Puru.
verses.wilson_translation: Undaunted (Indra), you had protected with all your protections Sudāsa, the offerer of oblations; youhave protected in battles with enemies for the possession of the earth Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and Puru.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नृभिर्नृमणो देववीतौ भूरीणि वृत्रा हर्यश्व हंसि ।त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ nṛ-manaḥ ǀ devá-vītau ǀ bhū́rīṇi ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ hari-aśva ǀ haṃsi ǀtvám ǀ ní ǀ dásyum ǀ cúmurim ǀ dhúnim ǀ ca ǀ ásvāpayaḥ ǀ dabhī́taye ǀ su-hántu ǁ
verses.english_translation: You, the lord of horses, who are honoured by men, have destroyed, along with the Maruts, numerousenemies at the sacrifice of the gods; you have put to sleep with the thunderbolt the Dasyus, Chumuri, and Dhuni,on behalf of Dabhīti.
verses.wilson_translation: You, the lord of horses, who are honoured by men, have destroyed, along with the Maruts, numerousenemies at the sacrifice of the gods; you have put to sleep with the thunderbolt the Dasyus, Chumuri, and Dhuni,on behalf of Dabhīti.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तव च्यौत्नानि वज्रहस्त तानि नव यत्पुरो नवतिं च सद्यः ।निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहंच वृत्रं नमुचिमुताहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ cyautnā́ni ǀ vajra-hasta ǀ tā́ni ǀ náva ǀ yát ǀ púraḥ ǀ navatím ǀ ca ǀ sadyáḥ ǀni-véśane ǀ śata-tamā́ ǀ aviveṣīḥ ǀ áhan ǀ ca ǀ vṛtrám ǀ námucim ǀ utá ǀ ahan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Such, wielder of the thunderbolt, are your mighty powers, that when you had quickly destroyed ninetyand nine cities, you have occupied the hundredth as a plural ce of abode; you have slain Vṛtra, you have also slain Namuci.
verses.wilson_translation: Such, wielder of the thunderbolt, are your mighty powers, that when you had quickly destroyed ninetyand nine cities, you have occupied the hundredth as a plural ce of abode; you have slain Vṛtra, you have also slain Namuci.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सना ता त इंद्र भोजनानि रातहव्याय दाशुषे सुदासे ।वृष्णे ते हरी वृषणा युनज्मि व्यंतु ब्रह्माणि पुरुशाक वाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: sánā ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ bhójanāni ǀ rātá-havyāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ su-dā́se ǀvṛ́ṣṇe ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ yunajmi ǀ vyántu ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ puru-śāka ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your favours,Indra, to Sudāsa, the donor (of offerings), the presenter of oblations, are infinite;showerer (of benefits), I yoke for you (your vigorous) steeds; may our prayers reach you who are mighty, towhom many rites are addressed.
verses.wilson_translation: Your favours,Indra, to Sudāsa, the donor (of offerings), the presenter of oblations, are infinite;showerer (of benefits), I yoke for you (your vigorous) steeds; may our prayers reach you who are mighty, towhom many rites are addressed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा ते अस्यां सहसावन्परिष्टावघाय भूम हरिवः परादै ।त्रायस्व नोऽवृकेभिर्वरूथैस्तव प्रियासः सूरिषु स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ te ǀ asyā́m ǀ sahasā-van ǀ páriṣṭau ǀ aghā́ya ǀ bhūma ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ parā-dái ǀtrā́yasva ǀ naḥ ǀ avṛkébhiḥ ǀ várūthaiḥ ǀ táva ǀ priyā́saḥ ǀ sūríṣu ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Powerful Indra, lord of horses, let us not be exposed at this ceremony, addressed to you, to themurderous despoiler; protect us with impregnable defences; may we be held dear among your worshippers.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Indra, lord of horses, let us not be exposed at this ceremony, addressed to you, to themurderous despoiler; protect us with impregnable defences; may we be held dear among your worshippers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रियास इत्ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरो मदेम शरणे सखायः ।नि तुर्वशं नि याद्वं शिशीह्यतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: priyā́saḥ ǀ ít ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ abhíṣṭau ǀ náraḥ ǀ madema ǀ śaraṇé ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀní ǀ turváśam ǀ ní ǀ yā́dvam ǀ śiśīhi ǀ atithi-gvā́ya ǀ śáṃsyam ǀ kariṣyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we,Maghavan, leaders in your adoration, regarded as dear friends, be happy in our homes; aboutto bestow felicity upon Atithigvan, humiliate Turvaśa; (humiliate) the son of Yadu.
verses.wilson_translation: May we,Maghavan, leaders in your adoration, regarded as dear friends, be happy in our homes; aboutto bestow felicity upon Atithigvan, humiliate Turvaśa; (humiliate) the son of Yadu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सद्यश्चिन्नु ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरः शंसंत्युक्थशास उक्था ।ये ते हवेभिर्वि पणीँरदाशन्नस्मान्वृणीष्व युज्याय तस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: sadyáḥ ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ abhíṣṭau ǀ náraḥ ǀ śaṃsanti ǀ uktha-śā́saḥ ǀ ukthā́ ǀyé ǀ te ǀ hávebhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ paṇī́n ǀ ádāśan ǀ asmā́n ǀ vṛṇīṣva ǀ yújyāya ǀ tásmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: The leader (of rites), reciters of prayers, offer,Maghavan, prayers devoutly for your adoration; they bytheir praises have appropriated the wealth of the niggards; select us (as the objects) of your friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: The leader (of rites), reciters of prayers, offer,Maghavan, prayers devoutly for your adoration; they bytheir praises have appropriated the wealth of the niggards; select us (as the objects) of your friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एते स्तोमा नरां नृतम तुभ्यमस्मद्र्यंचो ददतो मघानि ।तेषामिंद्र वृत्रहत्ये शिवो भूः सखा च शूरोऽविता च नृणां ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ stómāḥ ǀ narā́m ǀ nṛ-tama ǀ túbhyam ǀ asmadryáñcaḥ ǀ dádataḥ ǀ maghā́ni ǀtéṣām ǀ indra ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀ śiváḥ ǀ bhūḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ ca ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ avitā́ ǀ ca ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Chief leader (of rites), these praises of man addressed to you revert to us, who are the offerers of(sacrificial) riches; do you be propitious to such men, (Indra), in conflicts with enemies; be their friend, their hero,and protector.
verses.wilson_translation: Chief leader (of rites), these praises of man addressed to you revert to us, who are the offerers of(sacrificial) riches; do you be propitious to such men, (Indra), in conflicts with enemies; be their friend, their hero,and protector.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू इंद्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व ।उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्तीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ indra ǀ śūra ǀ stávamānaḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ bráhma-jūtaḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ vavṛdhasva ǀúpa ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́jān ǀ mimīhi ǀ úpa ǀ stī́n ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero,Indra, glorified on the present occasion, and propitiated by praise, be amplified in your person n forour protection; bestow upon us food and habitations; and do you ever cherish us wiht blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, glorified on the present occasion, and propitiated by praise, be amplified in your person n forour protection; bestow upon us food and habitations; and do you ever cherish us wiht blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . STRONG, Godly-natured, born for hero exploit, man's Friend, hedoth whatever deed he willeth.Saving us e’en from great transgression, Indra, the Youthful, visiteth man's home with favour. Waxing greatness Indra slayeth Vṛtra: the Hero with his aid hath helped the singer.He gave Sudās wide room and space, and often hath granted wealth to him who brought oblations. Soldier unchecked, war-rousing, battling Hero, unconquered from of old, victorious ever,Indra the very strong hath scattered armies; yea, he hath slain each foe who fought against him. Thou with thy greatness hast filled full, O Indra, even both the worlds with might, O thou Most Mighty.Lord of Bays, Indra, brandishing his thunder, is gratified with Soma at the banquet. A Bull begat the Bull for joy of battle, and a strong Mother brought forth him the manly.He who is Chief of men, their armies' Leader, is strong Hero, bold, and fain for booty. The people falter not, nor suffer sorrow, who win themselves this God's terrific spirit.He who with sacrifices worships Indra is lord of wealth, law-born and law's protector. Whene’er the elder fain would help the younger the greater cometh to the lesser's present.Shall the Immortal sit aloof' inactive? O Wondrous Indra, bring us wondrous riches. Thy dear folk, Indra, who present oblations, are, in chief place, thy friends, O Thunder-wielder.May we be best content in this thy favour, sheltered by One who slays not, but preserves us. To thee the mighty hymn hath clamoured loudly, and, Maghavan, the eloquent hath besought thee.Desire of wealth hath come upon thy singer: help us then, gakra, to our share of riches. Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: उग्रो जज्ञे वीर्याय स्वधावांचक्रिरपो नर्यो यत्करिष्यन् ।जग्मिर्युवा नृषदनमवोभिस्त्राता न इंद्र एनसो महश्चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: ugráḥ ǀ jajñe ǀ vīryā́ya ǀ svadhā́-vān ǀ cákriḥ ǀ ápaḥ ǀ náryaḥ ǀ yát ǀ kariṣyán ǀjágmiḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ nṛ-sádanam ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ trātā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ énasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: The fierce and powerful (Indra) has been born for heroic (deeds); friendly to man, he is theaccomplisher of whatever act he undertakes to perform; ever youthful, he invests the (sacrificial) hall withdefences (against interruption); be our preserver, Indra, from heinous sin.
verses.wilson_translation: The fierce and powerful (Indra) has been born for heroic (deeds); friendly to man, he is theaccomplisher of whatever act he undertakes to perform; ever youthful, he invests the (sacrificial) hall withdefences (against interruption); be our preserver, Indra, from heinous sin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हंता वृत्रमिंद्रः शूशुवानः प्रावीन्नु वीरो जरितारमूती ।कर्ता सुदासे अह वा उ लोकं दाता वसु मुहुरा दाशुषे भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: hántā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ índraḥ ǀ śū́śuvānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvīt ǀ nú ǀ vīráḥ ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ ūtī́ ǀkártā ǀ su-dā́se ǀ áha ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ dā́tā ǀ vásu ǀ múhuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ bhūt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, dilating in bulk, is the slayer of Vṛtra; the hero defends his worshipper promptly with hisprotection, whether he be the giver of dominion to Sudāsa, or the donor repeatedly of wealth to the offerer (ofoblations).
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, dilating in bulk, is the slayer of Vṛtra; the hero defends his worshipper promptly with hisprotection, whether he be the giver of dominion to Sudāsa, or the donor repeatedly of wealth to the offerer (ofoblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युध्मो अनर्वा खजकृत्समद्वा शूरः सत्राषाड् जनुषेमषाळ्हः ।व्यास इंद्रः पृतनाः स्वोजा अधा विश्वं शत्रूयंतं जघान ॥
verses.transliteration: yudhmáḥ ǀ anarvā́ ǀ khaja-kṛ́t ǀ samát-vā ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ satrāṣā́ṭ ǀ janúṣā ǀ īm ǀ áṣāḷhaḥ ǀví ǀ āse ǀ índraḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ su-ójāḥ ǀ ádha ǀ víśvam ǀ śatru-yántam ǀ jaghāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: A warrior who turns not back in battle, a combatant, one engaged in tumults, a hero, victorious over(his) foes from birth, invincible, of great vigour, this Indrascatters (hostile) hosts and slays all (his) adversaries.
verses.wilson_translation: A warrior who turns not back in battle, a combatant, one engaged in tumults, a hero, victorious over(his) foes from birth, invincible, of great vigour, this Indrascatters (hostile) hosts and slays all (his) adversaries.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उभे चिदिंद्र रोदसी महित्वा पप्राथ तविषीभिस्तुविष्मः ।नि वज्रमिंद्रो हरिवान्मिमिक्षन्त्समंधसा मदेषु वा उवोच ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ cit ǀ indra ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ paprātha ǀ táviṣībhiḥ ǀ tuviṣmaḥ ǀní ǀ vájram ǀ índraḥ ǀ hári-vān ǀ mímikṣan ǀ sám ǀ ándhasā ǀ mádeṣu ǀ vái ǀ uvoca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Opulent Indra, you have filled both heaven and earth with your magnitutde, your energies; Indra, thelord of horses, brandishing the thunderbolt, is gratified at sacrifices by the (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: Opulent Indra, you have filled both heaven and earth with your magnitutde, your energies; Indra, thelord of horses, brandishing the thunderbolt, is gratified at sacrifices by the (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृषा जजान वृषणं रणाय तमु चिन्नारी नर्यं ससूव ।प्र यः सेनानीरध नृभ्यो अस्तीनः सत्वा गवेषणः स धृष्णुः ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ jajāna ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ ráṇāya ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ cit ǀ nā́rī ǀ náryam ǀ sasūva ǀprá ǀ yáḥ ǀ senā-nī́ḥ ǀ ádha ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ ináḥ ǀ sátvā ǀ go-éṣaṇaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: (His) progenitor begot Indra, the showerer (of benefits) for (the purpose of) war; his mother brought himforth the benefactor of man; the leader of armies who is chief over men, he is the lord, the conqueror, therecoverer of the kine, the subduer of foes.
verses.wilson_translation: (His) progenitor begot Indra, the showerer (of benefits) for (the purpose of) war; his mother brought himforth the benefactor of man; the leader of armies who is chief over men, he is the lord, the conqueror, therecoverer of the kine, the subduer of foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू चित्स भ्रेषते जनो न रेषन्मनो यो अस्य घोरमाविवासात् ।यज्ञैर्य इंद्रे दधते दुवांसि क्षयत्स राय ऋतपा ऋतेजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ cit ǀ sáḥ ǀ bhreṣate ǀ jánaḥ ǀ ná ǀ reṣat ǀ mánaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ asya ǀ ghorám ǀ ā-vívāsāt ǀyajñáiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ índre ǀ dádhate ǀ dúvāṃsi ǀ kṣáyat ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyé ǀ ṛta-pā́ḥ ǀ ṛte-jā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who devotes his mind to the terrible Indranever falls (from his condition), nor will he perish; theprotector of sacred rites, the progeny of sacrifice, bestows riches on him who offers to Indra praises and prayerswith sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: He who devotes his mind to the terrible Indranever falls (from his condition), nor will he perish; theprotector of sacred rites, the progeny of sacrifice, bestows riches on him who offers to Indra praises and prayerswith sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्र पूर्वो अपराय शिक्षन्नयज्ज्यायान्कनीयसो देष्णं ।अमृत इत्पर्यासीत दूरमा चित्र चित्र्यं भरा रयिं नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ áparāya ǀ śíkṣan ǀ áyat ǀ jyā́yān ǀ kánīyasaḥ ǀ deṣṇám ǀamṛ́taḥ ǀ ít ǀ pári ǀ āsīta ǀ dūrám ǀ ā́ ǀ citra ǀ cítryam ǀ bhara ǀ rayím ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That (wealth)Indra, which the prior has given to the posterior; which the elder may accept from theyounger; with which (the son) yet living dwells far away (separated from his father), confer, wonderful Indra, suchprecious riches upon us.
verses.wilson_translation: That (wealth)Indra, which the prior has given to the posterior; which the elder may accept from theyounger; with which (the son) yet living dwells far away (separated from his father), confer, wonderful Indra, suchprecious riches upon us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्त इंद्र प्रियो जनो ददाशदसन्निरेके अद्रिवः सखा ते ।वयं ते अस्यां सुमतौ चनिष्ठाः स्याम वरूथे अघ्नतो नृपीतौ ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ priyáḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǀ dádāśat ǀ ásat ǀ nireké ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ te ǀvayám ǀ te ǀ asyā́m ǀ su-matáu ǀ cániṣṭhāḥ ǀ syā́ma ǀ várūthe ǀ ághnataḥ ǀ nṛ́-pītau ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the man who is dear to you,Indra, present (oblations); may he be your friend, wielder of thethunderbolt, he (assiduous) in donations; may we be abounding in food through this favour of you who aredevoid of cruelty, (may we be in the enjoyment of) a dwelling giving shelter to men.
verses.wilson_translation: May the man who is dear to you,Indra, present (oblations); may he be your friend, wielder of thethunderbolt, he (assiduous) in donations; may we be abounding in food through this favour of you who aredevoid of cruelty, (may we be in the enjoyment of) a dwelling giving shelter to men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एष स्तोमो अचिक्रदद्वृषा त उत स्तामुर्मघवन्नक्रपिष्ट ।रायस्कामो जरितारं त आगंत्वमंग शक्र वस्व आ शको नः ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣáḥ ǀ stómaḥ ǀ acikradat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ te ǀ utá ǀ stāmúḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ akrapiṣṭa ǀrāyáḥ ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ agan ǀ tvám ǀ aṅgá ǀ śakra ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ śakaḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For you,Maghavan, this showering Soma(libation) cries aloud; to you the worshipper has recitedpraises; the desire of riches has fallen upon thine adorer, do you, therefore,Śakra, bestow quickly upon uswealth.
verses.wilson_translation: For you,Maghavan, this showering Soma(libation) cries aloud; to you the worshipper has recitedpraises; the desire of riches has fallen upon thine adorer, do you, therefore,Śakra, bestow quickly upon uswealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स न इंद्र त्वयताया इषे धास्त्मना च ये मघवानो जुनंति ।वस्वी षु ते जरित्रे अस्तु शक्तिर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ tvá-yatāyai ǀ iṣé ǀ dhāḥ ǀ tmánā ǀ ca ǀ yé ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ junánti ǀvásvī ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ jaritré ǀ astu ǀ śaktíḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer (you oblations); may there be power in thine adorer (to repeat) manylaudations; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer (you oblations); may there be power in thine adorer (to repeat) manylaudations; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PRESSED is the juice divine with milk commingled: thereto hath Indra ever been accustomed.We wake thee, Lord of Bays, with sacrifices: mark this our laud in the wild joy of Soma. On to the rite they move, the grass they scatter, these Soma-drinkers eloquent in synod.Hither, for men to grasp, are brought the press-stones, far-thundering, famous, strong, that wait on heroes. Indra, thou settest free the many waters that were encompassed, Hero, by the Dragon.Down rolled, as if on chariots borne, the rivers: through fear of thee all things created tremble. Skilled in all manly deeds the God terrific hath with his weapons mastered these opponents.Indra in rapturous joy shook down their castles he slew them in his might, the Thunder-wielder. No evil spirits have impelled us, Indra, nor fiends, O Mightiest God, with their devices.Let our true God subdue the hostile rabble: let not the lewd approach our holy worship. Thou in thy strength surpassest Earth and Heaven: the regions comprehend not all thy greatness.With thine own power and might thou slewest Vṛtra: no foe hath found the end of thee in battle. Even the earlier Deities submitted their powers to thy supreme divine dominion.Indra wins wealth and deals it out to other's: men in the strife for booty call on Indra. The humble hath invoked thee for protection, thee, Lord of great felicity, O Indra.Thou with a hundred aids hast been our Helper: one who brings gifts like thee hath his defender. May we, O Indra, be thy friends for ever, eagerly, Conqueror, yielding greater homage.May, through thy grace, the strength of us who battle quell in the shock the onset of the foeman. Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

verses.english_translation: Bright sacrificial food mixed with curds and milk has been poured out;Indradelights in it from his birth;lord of bay horses, we wake you up with sacrifices, acknowledge our praises in the exhilaration of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Bright sacrificial food mixed with curds and milk has been poured out;Indradelights in it from his birth;lord of bay horses, we wake you up with sacrifices, acknowledge our praises in the exhilaration of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: They repair to the sacrifice, they strew the sacred grass; the (grinding) stones at the ceremony are ofdifficulty suppressed noise; famous priests, whose voices are heard far off, bring the stones from the interior ofthe dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: They repair to the sacrifice, they strew the sacred grass; the (grinding) stones at the ceremony are ofdifficulty suppressed noise; famous priests, whose voices are heard far off, bring the stones from the interior ofthe dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: You, hero, have enabled the many waters arrested by Ahi to flow; by you the rivers rushed forth likecharioteers; all created worlds trembled through fear of you.
verses.wilson_translation: You, hero, have enabled the many waters arrested by Ahi to flow; by you the rivers rushed forth likecharioteers; all created worlds trembled through fear of you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: The formidable (Indra), knowing all actions beneficial to man, intimidated those (asuras) by hisweapons; Indra, exuling shook their cities; armed with his thunderbolt he slew them in his might.
verses.wilson_translation: The formidable (Indra), knowing all actions beneficial to man, intimidated those (asuras) by hisweapons; Indra, exuling shook their cities; armed with his thunderbolt he slew them in his might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: Let not thrākṣasas,Indra, do us harm; let not the evil spirits do harm to our progeny, most powerful(Indra); let the sovereign lord, (Indra), exert himself (in the restraint) of disorderly beings, so that the unchastemay not disturb our rite.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not thrākṣasas,Indra, do us harm; let not the evil spirits do harm to our progeny, most powerful(Indra); let the sovereign lord, (Indra), exert himself (in the restraint) of disorderly beings, so that the unchastemay not disturb our rite.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: You,Indra, by your function, preside over the beings (of earth); all the regions (of the world) do notsurpass your magnitude; by thine own strength you have slain Vṛtra; no enemy has effected your destruction inbattle.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, by your function, preside over the beings (of earth); all the regions (of the world) do notsurpass your magnitude; by thine own strength you have slain Vṛtra; no enemy has effected your destruction inbattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: The older deities have confessed your vigour superior to their destructive strength,Indrahavingsubdued his foes, gives the rich spoils (to his worshippers); they invoke Indra to obtain food.
verses.wilson_translation: The older deities have confessed your vigour superior to their destructive strength,Indrahavingsubdued his foes, gives the rich spoils (to his worshippers); they invoke Indra to obtain food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: The worshipper has invoked you the sovereign Indra, for protection; protector of many, you have beento us the guardian of great fortune; be our defender against every overpowering (assailant).
verses.wilson_translation: The worshipper has invoked you the sovereign Indra, for protection; protector of many, you have beento us the guardian of great fortune; be our defender against every overpowering (assailant).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: May we, daily increasing in reverence, be (regarded),Indra, (as) your friends; through the protection ofyou, surpasser in greatness, may (your worshippers) repulse the attack of the foe in battle, the strength of themalevolent.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, daily increasing in reverence, be (regarded),Indra, (as) your friends; through the protection ofyou, surpasser in greatness, may (your worshippers) repulse the attack of the foe in battle, the strength of themalevolent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.english_translation: Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer the (oblations); may there be ability in thine adorer (to repeat) my laudations;and do you ever cherish us wiḥ blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Enable us,Indra, (to partake of) food granted by you, as well as those who, opulent (in sacrificialpresentations), spontaneously offer the (oblations); may there be ability in thine adorer (to repeat) my laudations;and do you ever cherish us wiḥ blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXII Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRINK Soma, Lord of Bays, and let it cheer thee: Indra, the stone, like a well guided courser,Directed by the presser's arms hath pressed it. So let the draught of joy, thy dear companion, by which, O Lord of Bays, thou slayest foemen,Delight thee, Indra, Lord of princely treasures. Mark closely, Maghavan, the words I utter, this eulogy recited by Vasiṣṭha:Accept the prayers I offer at thy banquet. Hear thou the call of the juice-drinking press-stone: hear thou the Brahman's hymn who sings and lauds thee.Take to thine inmost self these adorations. I know and ne’er forget the hymns and praises of thee, the Conqueror, and thy strength immortal.Thy name I ever utter. Self-Refulgent Among mankind many are thy libations, and many a time the pious sageinvokes thee.O Maghavan, be not long distant from us. All these libations are for thee, O Hero: to thee I offer these my prayers. that strengthen.Ever, in every place, must men invoke thee. Never do men attain, O Wonder-Worker, thy greatness, Mighty One, who must be lauded,Nor, Indra, thine heroic power and bounty. Among all Ṛṣis, Indra, old and recent, who have engendered hymns as sacred singers,Even with us be thine auspicious friendships. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: पिबा सोममिंद्र मंदतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः ।सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: píba ǀ sómam ǀ indra ǀ mándatu ǀ tvā ǀ yám ǀ te ǀ susā́va ǀ hari-aśva ǀ ádriḥ ǀsotúḥ ǀ bāhú-bhyām ǀ sú-yataḥ ǀ ná ǀ árvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink,Indra, the Soma; may it exhilarate you, that which the stone tightly held like a horse (by thereins), by the arms of the grinder, has expressed, lord of bay horses for you.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indra, the Soma; may it exhilarate you, that which the stone tightly held like a horse (by thereins), by the arms of the grinder, has expressed, lord of bay horses for you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते मदो युज्यश्चारुरस्ति येन वृत्राणि हर्यश्व हंसि ।स त्वामिंद्र प्रभूवसो ममत्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ yújyaḥ ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ ásti ǀ yéna ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ hari-aśva ǀ háṃsi ǀsáḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ prabhuvaso íti prabhu-vaso ǀ mamattu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the exhilarating Somawhich is fit for and suitable to you, by which, lord of bay horses, you slay Vṛtra, exhilarate you,Indra, abounding in riches.
verses.wilson_translation: May the exhilarating Somawhich is fit for and suitable to you, by which, lord of bay horses, you slay Vṛtra, exhilarate you,Indra, abounding in riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बोधा सु मे मघवन्वाचमेमां यां ते वसिष्ठो अर्चति प्रशस्तिं ।इमा ब्रह्म सधमादे जुषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: bódha ǀ sú ǀ me ǀ magha-van ǀ vā́cam ǀ ā́ ǀ imā́m ǀ yā́m ǀ te ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ árcati ǀ prá-śastim ǀimā́ ǀ bráhma ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ juṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Understand thoroughly,Maghavan, this my speech, this praise of you, which Vasiṣṭharecites; bepleased by these prayers at the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Understand thoroughly,Maghavan, this my speech, this praise of you, which Vasiṣṭharecites; bepleased by these prayers at the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुधी हवं विपिपानस्याद्रेर्बोधा विप्रस्यार्चतो मनीषां ।कृष्वा दुवांस्यंतमा सचेमा ॥
verses.transliteration: śrudhí ǀ hávam ǀ vi-pipānásya ǀ ádreḥ ǀ bódha ǀ víprasya ǀ árcataḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀkṛṣvá ǀ dúvāṃsi ǀ ántamā ǀ sácā ǀ imā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear the invocation of the (grinding) stone, (of me) repeatedly drinking (the Soma), comprehend thehymn of the adoring sage, and, friendly (with us), take to your near consideration these adorations.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear the invocation of the (grinding) stone, (of me) repeatedly drinking (the Soma), comprehend thehymn of the adoring sage, and, friendly (with us), take to your near consideration these adorations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न ते गिरो अपि मृष्ये तुरस्य न सुष्टुतिमसुर्यस्य विद्वान् ।सदा ते नाम स्वयशो विवक्मि ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ te ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ápi ǀ mṛṣye ǀ turásya ǀ ná ǀ su-stutím ǀ asuryásya ǀ vidvā́n ǀsádā ǀ te ǀ nā́ma ǀ sva-yaśaḥ ǀ vivakmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing of your strength, I refrain not from the praise nor from the glorification of you, the destroyer (offoes), but ever proclaim your especial care.
verses.wilson_translation: Knowing of your strength, I refrain not from the praise nor from the glorification of you, the destroyer (offoes), but ever proclaim your especial care.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भूरि हि ते सवना मानुषेषु भूरि मनीषी हवते त्वामित् ।मारे अस्मन्मघवंज्योक्कः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ sávanā ǀ mā́nuṣeṣu ǀ bhū́ri ǀ manīṣī́ ǀ havate ǀ tvā́m ǀ ít ǀmā́ ǀ āré ǀ asmát ǀ magha-van ǀ jyók ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are the sacrifices offered,Maghavan, to you among mankind; constantly does worshipper indeedinvoke you; therefore be not far nor be a long time from us.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the sacrifices offered,Maghavan, to you among mankind; constantly does worshipper indeedinvoke you; therefore be not far nor be a long time from us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्येदिमा सवना शूर विश्वा तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि वर्धना कृणोमि ।त्वं नृभिर्हव्यो विश्वधासि ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhya ǀ ít ǀ imā́ ǀ sávanā ǀ śūra ǀ víśvā ǀ túbhyam ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ várdhanā ǀ kṛṇomi ǀtvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ viśvádhā ǀ asi ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you, hero, I indeed offer these sacrifices, to you I address these elevating praises; you are to be inall ways invoked by the leaders (of rites).
verses.wilson_translation: To you, hero, I indeed offer these sacrifices, to you I address these elevating praises; you are to be inall ways invoked by the leaders (of rites).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू चिन्नु ते मन्यमानस्य दस्मोदश्नुवंति महिमानमुग्र ।न वीर्यमिंद्र ते न राधः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ mányamānasya ǀ dasma ǀ út ǀ aśnuvanti ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ugra ǀná ǀ vīryám ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ ná ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, of goodly aspect, none attain the greatness of you who are to be honoured, nor, fierce Indra, yourheroism, nor your wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, of goodly aspect, none attain the greatness of you who are to be honoured, nor, fierce Indra, yourheroism, nor your wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये च पूर्व ऋषयो ये च नूत्ना इंद्र ब्रह्माणि जनयंत विप्राः ।अस्मे ते संतु सख्या शिवानि यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ca ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ nū́tnāḥ ǀ índra ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ janáyanta ǀ víprāḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ te ǀ santu ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ śivā́ni ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your auspicious regards,Indra, be directed towards us, as they have been to those pious sages,ancient or recent, who have originated (your) praises, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May your auspicious regards,Indra, be directed towards us, as they have been to those pious sages,ancient or recent, who have originated (your) praises, and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PRAYERS have been offered up through love of glory: Vasiṣṭha, honour Indra in the battle.He who with might extends through all existence hears words which I, his faithful servant, utter. A cry was raised which reached the Gods, O Indra, a cry to them to send us strength in combat.None among men knows his own life's duration: bear us in safety over these our troubles. The Bays, the booty-seeking car I harness: my prayers have reached him who accepts them gladly.Indra, when he had slain resistless foemen, forced with his might the two world-halves asunder. Like barren cows, moreover, swelled the waters: the singen sought thy holy rite, O Indra.Come unto us as with his team comes Vāyu: thou, through our solemn hymns bestowest booty. So may these gladdening draughts rejoice thee, Indra, the Mighty, very bounteous to the singer.Alone among the Gods thou pitiest mortals: O Hero, make thee glad at this libation.
