verses.english_translation: Heaven and earth are now glorified by the Vasiṣṭhas, as are Varuṇa, the objec of worship, and Mitraand Agni; may they, the conferrers of joy, bestow upon us excellent food; and do you (all) ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth are now glorified by the Vasiṣṭhas, as are Varuṇa, the objec of worship, and Mitraand Agni; may they, the conferrers of joy, bestow upon us excellent food; and do you (all) ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XL. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BE gathered all the audience of the synod: let us begin their praise whose course is rapid.Whate’er God Savitar this day produces, may we be where the Wealthy One distributes. This, dealt from heaven ' may both the Worlds vouchsafe us, and Varuṇa, Indra, Aryaman, and Mitra.May Goddess Aditi assign us riches, Vāyu and Bhaga make them ours for ever. Strong be the man and full of power, O Maruts, whom ye, borne on by spotted coursers, favour.Him, too, Sarasvatī and Agni further, and there is none to rob him of his riches. This Varuṇa is guide of Law, he, Mitra, and Aryaman, the Kings, our work have finished.Divine and foeless Aditi quickly listens. May these deliver us unharmed from trouble. With offerings I propitiate the branches of this swift-moving God, the bounteous Viṣṇu.Hence Rudra gained his Rudra-strength: O Aśvins, ye sought the house that hath celestial viands. Be not thou angry here, O glowing Pūṣan, for what Varūtrī and the Bounteous gave us.May the swift-moving Gods protect and bless us, and Vāta send us rain, wha wanders round us. Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasisthas, and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: ओ श्रुष्टिर्विदथ्या समेतु प्रति स्तोमं दधीमहि तुराणां ।यदद्य देवः सविता सुवाति स्यामास्य रत्निनो विभागे ॥
verses.transliteration: ó íti ǀ śruṣṭíḥ ǀ vidathyā́ ǀ sám ǀ etu ǀ práti ǀ stómam ǀ dadhīmahi ǀ turā́ṇām ǀyát ǀ adyá ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ suvā́ti ǀ syā́ma ǀ asya ǀ ratnínaḥ ǀ vi-bhāgé ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the satisfaction derived from pious rites come to us as we contemplate the glorification of the swiftmoving (divinities); may we be included in the apportionment by that wealth-bestowing deity (of the riches) whichthe divine Savitāgoday distributes.
verses.wilson_translation: May the satisfaction derived from pious rites come to us as we contemplate the glorification of the swiftmoving (divinities); may we be included in the apportionment by that wealth-bestowing deity (of the riches) whichthe divine Savitāgoday distributes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो रोदसी च द्युभक्तमिंद्रो अर्यमा ददातु ।दिदेष्टु देव्यदिती रेक्णो वायुश्च यन्नियुवैते भगश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: mitráḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ca ǀ dyú-bhaktam ǀ índraḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ dadātu ǀdídeṣṭu ǀ devī́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ niyuváite íti ni-yuváite ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Mitraand Varuṇa, heaven and earth,IndraandĀryaman, give us that (wealth) which is meritedby brilliant (laudations); may the divine Aditibe disposed to give us riches, which Vāyuand Bhagamay preserveever in our keeping.
verses.wilson_translation: May Mitraand Varuṇa, heaven and earth,IndraandĀryaman, give us that (wealth) which is meritedby brilliant (laudations); may the divine Aditibe disposed to give us riches, which Vāyuand Bhagamay preserveever in our keeping.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सेदुग्रो अस्तु मरुतः स शुष्मी यं मर्त्यं पृषदश्वा अवाथ ।उतेमग्निः सरस्वती जुनंति न तस्य रायः पर्येतास्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ ugráḥ ǀ astu ǀ marutaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ śuṣmī́ ǀ yám ǀ mártyam ǀ pṛṣat-aśvāḥ ǀ ávātha ǀutá ǀ īm ǀ agníḥ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ junánti ǀ ná ǀ tásya ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ pari-etā́ ǀ asti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maruts, whose steeds are the spotted deer, may the mortal whom you protect the resolute, be strong,for him Agniand Sarasvatīalso defend, and there be no despoiler of his riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Maruts, whose steeds are the spotted deer, may the mortal whom you protect the resolute, be strong,for him Agniand Sarasvatīalso defend, and there be no despoiler of his riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं हि नेता वरुण ऋतस्य मित्रो राजानो अर्यमापो धुः ।सुहवा देव्यदितिरनर्वा ते नो अंहो अति पर्षन्नरिष्टान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ hí ǀ netā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ mitráḥ ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ ápaḥ ǀ dhúríti dhúḥ ǀsu-hávā ǀ devī́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ anarvā́ ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ áti ǀ parṣan ǀ áriṣṭān ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Varuṇa, the leader of the rite, and the royal MitraandĀryaman, uphold my acts, and the divineunopposed Aditi, earnestly invoked; may they convey us safe beyond evil.
verses.wilson_translation: This Varuṇa, the leader of the rite, and the royal MitraandĀryaman, uphold my acts, and the divineunopposed Aditi, earnestly invoked; may they convey us safe beyond evil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य देवस्य मीळ्हुषो वया विष्णोरेषस्य प्रभृथे हविर्भिः ।विदे हि रुद्रो रुद्रियं महित्वं यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत् ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ devásya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀ vayā́ḥ ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ eṣásya ǀ pra-bhṛthé ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀvidé ǀ hí ǀ rudráḥ ǀ rudríyam ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ yāsiṣṭám ǀ vartíḥ ǀ aśvinau ǀ írā-vat ǁ
verses.english_translation: I propitiate with oblations the ramifications of that divine attainable Viṣṇu, the showerer of benefits;Rudra, bestow upon us the magnificence of his nature; the Aśvinshave come to our dwelling abond with(sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: I propitiate with oblations the ramifications of that divine attainable Viṣṇu, the showerer of benefits;Rudra, bestow upon us the magnificence of his nature; the Aśvinshave come to our dwelling abond with(sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मात्र पूषन्नाघृण इरस्यो वरूत्री यद्रातिषाचश्च रासन् ।मयोभुवो नो अर्वंतो नि पांतु वृष्टिं परिज्मा वातो ददातु ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ átra ǀ pūṣan ǀ āghṛṇe ǀ irasyaḥ ǀ várūtrī ǀ yát ǀ rāti-sā́caḥ ǀ ca ǀ rā́san ǀmayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ árvantaḥ ǀ ní ǀ pāntu ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ pári-jmā ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ dadātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, oppose not (hindrance) on this occasion; may the protectress, (Sarasvatī) andthe liberal (wives of the gods), grant us wealth; may the ever-moving deities, the sources of happiness, protectus; may the circumambient Vātasend us rain.
verses.wilson_translation: Resplendent Pūṣan, oppose not (hindrance) on this occasion; may the protectress, (Sarasvatī) andthe liberal (wives of the gods), grant us wealth; may the ever-moving deities, the sources of happiness, protectus; may the circumambient Vātasend us rain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू रोदसी अभिष्टुते वसिष्ठैर्ऋतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः ।यच्छंतु चंद्रा उपमं नो अर्कं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ ródasī íti ǀ abhístute ítyabhí-stute ǀ vásiṣṭhaiḥ ǀ ṛtá-vānaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀyácchantu ǀ candrā́ḥ ǀ upa-mám ǀ naḥ ǀ arkám ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heaven and earth are now glorified by the Vasiṣṭhas, as are Varuṇathe object of worship, and Mitraand Agni; may they, the conferrers of joy, bestow upon us excellent food; and do you (all) ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth are now glorified by the Vasiṣṭhas, as are Varuṇathe object of worship, and Mitraand Agni; may they, the conferrers of joy, bestow upon us excellent food; and do you (all) ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Bhaga.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI at dawn, and Indra we invoke at dawn, and Varuṇa and Mitra, and the Aśvins twain.Bhaga at dawn, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati, Soma at dawn, Rudra we will invoke at dawn. We will invoke strong, early-conquering Bhaga, the Son of Aditi, the great supporter:Thinking of whom, the poor, yea, even the mighty, even the King himself says, Give me Bhaga. Bhaga our guide, Bhaga whose gifts are faithful, favour this song, and give us wealth, O Bhaga.Bhaga, augment our store of kine and horses, Bhaga, may we be rich in men and heroes. So may felicity be ours at present, and when the day approaches, and at noontide;And may we still, O Bounteous One, at sunset be happy in the Deities' loving-kindness. May Bhaga verily be bliss-bestower, and through him, Gods! may happiness attend us.As such, O Bhaga, all with might invoke thee: as such be thou our Champion here, O Bhaga. To this our worship may all Dawns incline them, and come to the pure place like Dadhikrāvan.As strong steeds draw a chariot may they bring us hitherward Bhaga who discovers treasure. May blessed Mornings dawn on us for ever, with wealth of kine, of horses, and of heroes,Streaming with all abundance, pouring fatness. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्रातरग्निं प्रातरिंद्रं हवामहे प्रातर्मित्रावरुणा प्रातरश्विना ।प्रातर्भगं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं प्रातः सोममुत रुद्रं हुवेम ॥
verses.transliteration: prātáḥ ǀ agním ǀ pratáḥ ǀ índram ǀ havāmahe ǀ pratáḥ ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ prātáḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀpratáḥ ǀ bhágam ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátim ǀ pratáḥ ǀ sómam ǀ utá ǀ rudrám ǀ huvema ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke at dawn Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitraand Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn Bhaga,Pūṣan,Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn Somaand Rudra.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke at dawn Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitraand Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn Bhaga,Pūṣan,Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn Somaand Rudra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता ।आध्रश्चिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-jítam ǀ bhágam ǀ ugrám ǀ huvema ǀ vayám ǀ putrám ǀ áditeḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vi-dhartā́ ǀādhráḥ ǀ cit ǀ yám ǀ mányamānaḥ ǀ turáḥ ǀ cit ǀ rā́jā ǀ cit ǀ yám ǀ bhágam ǀ bhakṣi ǀ íti ǀ ā́ha ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke at dawn fierce Bhaga, the son of Aditi, who is the sustainer (of the world), to whom the poorman praising him applies, saying, give (me wealth), to whom the opulent prince (addresses the same prayer).
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke at dawn fierce Bhaga, the son of Aditi, who is the sustainer (of the world), to whom the poorman praising him applies, saying, give (me wealth), to whom the opulent prince (addresses the same prayer).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भग प्रणेतर्भग सत्यराधो भगेमां धियमुदवा ददन्नः ।भग प्र णो जनय गोभिरश्वैर्भग प्र नृभिर्नृवंतः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: bhága ǀ pránetaríti prá-netaḥ ǀ bhága ǀ sátya-rādhaḥ ǀ bhága ǀ imā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ út ǀ ava ǀ dádat ǀ naḥ ǀbhága ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ janaya ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ bhága ǀ prá ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ nṛ-vántaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bhaga, chief leader of rites, Bhaga, faithful granting (our wishes), fructify ceremony, enrich us withcattle and horses; may we Bhaga, be eminent withmaledescendants and followers.
verses.wilson_translation: Bhaga, chief leader of rites, Bhaga, faithful granting (our wishes), fructify ceremony, enrich us withcattle and horses; may we Bhaga, be eminent withmaledescendants and followers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उतेदानीं भगवंतः स्यामोत प्रपित्व उत मध्ये अह्नां ।उतोदिता मघवन्त्सूर्यस्य वयं देवानां सुमतौ स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ idā́nīm ǀ bhága-vantaḥ ǀ syāma ǀ utá ǀ pra-pitvé ǀ utá ǀ mádhye ǀ áhnām ǀutá ǀ út-itā ǀ magha-van ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ vayám ǀ devā́nām ǀ su-matáu ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we now have Bhaga(for our lord), whether in the forenoon or mid- day, or at sun-rise; may we,Maghavan, enjoy the favour of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: May we now have Bhaga(for our lord), whether in the forenoon or mid- day, or at sun-rise; may we,Maghavan, enjoy the favour of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भग एव भगवाँ अस्तु देवास्तेन वयं भगवंतः स्याम ।तं त्वा भग सर्व इज्जोहवीति स नो भग पुरएता भवेह ॥
verses.transliteration: bhágaḥ ǀ evá ǀ bhága-vān ǀ astu ǀ devāḥ ǀ téna ǀ vayám ǀ bhága-vantaḥ ǀ syāma ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ bhaga ǀ sárvaḥ ǀ ít ǀ johavīti ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhaga ǀ puraḥ-etā́ ǀ bhava ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Bhaga, gods, be the possessor of opulence, and, through him, may we be possessed of wealth,every one verily repeatedly invokes you, Bhaga; do you, Bhaga, be our preceder at this solemnity.
verses.wilson_translation: May Bhaga, gods, be the possessor of opulence, and, through him, may we be possessed of wealth,every one verily repeatedly invokes you, Bhaga; do you, Bhaga, be our preceder at this solemnity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समध्वरायोषसो नमंत दधिक्रावेव शुचये पदाय ।अर्वाचीनं वसुविदं भगं नो रथमिवाश्वा वाजिन आ वहंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ adhvarā́ya ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ namanta ǀ dadhikrā́vā-iva ǀ śúcaye ǀ padā́ya ǀarvācīnám ǀ vasu-vídam ǀ bhágam ǀ naḥ ǀ rátham-iva ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vahantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the dawn come to our sacrifice as a horse to a suitable station; as rapid steeds convey a chariot,so may the dawns bring to us Bhaga, down- descending, charged with riches.
verses.wilson_translation: May the dawn come to our sacrifice as a horse to a suitable station; as rapid steeds convey a chariot,so may the dawns bring to us Bhaga, down- descending, charged with riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्न उषासो वीरवतीः सदमुच्छंतु भद्राः ।घृतं दुहाना विश्वतः प्रपीता यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśva-vatīḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vīrá-vatīḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ucchantu ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀghṛtám ǀ dúhānāḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ prá-pītāḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: {Text is missing}
verses.wilson_translation: {Text is missing}
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLII Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET Brahmans and Aṅgirases come forward, and let the roar of cloudy heaven surround us.Loud low the Milch-kine swimming in the waters: set be the stones that grace our holy service. Fair, Agni, is thy long-known path to travel: yoke for the juice tfiy bay, thy ruddy horses,Or red steeds, Hero-bearing, for the chamber. Seated, I call the Deities' generations. They glorify your sacrifice with worship, yet the glad Priest near them is left unequalled.Bring the Gods hither, thou of many aspects: turn hitherward Aramati the Holy. What time the Guest hath made himself apparent, at ease reclining in the rich man's dwelling,Agni, well-pleased, well-placed within the chamber gives to a house like this wealth worth the choosing. Accept this sacrifice of ours, O Agni; glorify it with Indra and the Maruts.Here on our grass let Night and Dawn be seated: bring longing Varuṇa and Mitra hither. Thus hath Vasiṣṭha praised victorious Agni, yearning for wealth that giveth all subsistence.May he bestow on us food, strength, and riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ब्रह्माणो अंगिरसो नक्षंत प्र क्रंदनुर्नभन्यस्य वेतु ।प्र धेनव उदप्रुतो नवंत युज्यातामद्री अध्वरस्य पेशः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ brahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ nakṣanta ǀ prá ǀ krandanúḥ ǀ nabhanyásya ǀ vetu ǀprá ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ uda-prútaḥ ǀ navanta ǀ yujyā́tām ǀ ádrī íti ǀ adhvarásya ǀ péśaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May thebrāhmaṇas, the Aṅgirasas, be everywhere present; may Krandanu be conscious of (our)adoration; may the rivers glide along, distributing water; may the pious couple (theyajamānaand his wife),conjointly appreciate the beauty of the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May thebrāhmaṇas, the Aṅgirasas, be everywhere present; may Krandanu be conscious of (our)adoration; may the rivers glide along, distributing water; may the pious couple (theyajamānaand his wife),conjointly appreciate the beauty of the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुगस्ते अग्ने सनवित्तो अध्वा युंक्ष्वा सुते हरितो रोहितश्च ।ये वा सद्मन्नरुषा वीरवाहो हुवे देवानां जनिमानि सत्तः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-gáḥ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ sána-vittaḥ ǀ ádhvā ǀ yuṅkṣvá ǀ suté ǀ harítaḥ ǀ rohítaḥ ǀ ca ǀyé ǀ vā ǀ sádman ǀ aruṣā́ḥ ǀ vīra-vā́haḥ ǀ huvé ǀ devā́nām ǀ jánimāni ǀ sattáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: plural asant,Agni, by your long-familiar path, invoke the libation; the bay, the ruddy horses, who, brilliantshining, are the conveyers of (you), the hero, to the hall of sacrifice, where seated, I invoke the companies of thegods.
verses.wilson_translation: plural asant,Agni, by your long-familiar path, invoke the libation; the bay, the ruddy horses, who, brilliantshining, are the conveyers of (you), the hero, to the hall of sacrifice, where seated, I invoke the companies of thegods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समु वो यज्ञं महयन्नमोभिः प्र होता मंद्रो रिरिच उपाके ।यजस्व सु पुर्वणीक देवाना यज्ञियामरमतिं ववृत्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vaḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ mahayan ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ prá ǀ hótā ǀ mandráḥ ǀ ririce ǀ upāké ǀyájasva ǀ sú ǀ puru-anīka ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ yajñíyām ǀ arámatim ǀ vavṛtyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The (worshippers) offer you, (gods), this sacrifice, with prostrations; the ministrant priest, who is nearus repeating pious praise, excels (all others); worship well the gods; resplendent (Agni), make the venerableearth revolve.
verses.wilson_translation: The (worshippers) offer you, (gods), this sacrifice, with prostrations; the ministrant priest, who is nearus repeating pious praise, excels (all others); worship well the gods; resplendent (Agni), make the venerableearth revolve.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदा वीरस्य रेवतो दुरोणे स्योनशीरतिथिराचिकेतत् ।सुप्रीतो अग्निः सुधितो दम आ स विशे दाति वार्यमियत्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ vīrásya ǀ revátaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ syona-śī́ḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ ā-cíketat ǀsú-prītaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sú-dhitaḥ ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ viśé ǀ dāti ǀ vā́ryam ǀ íyatyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Agni, reposing at his ease in the dwelling of the liberal worshipper, is welcomed as a guest, thussuitable plural ced in the hall of sacrifice, he gives well-plural ased, desirable (wealth) to the people who approach him.
verses.wilson_translation: When Agni, reposing at his ease in the dwelling of the liberal worshipper, is welcomed as a guest, thussuitable plural ced in the hall of sacrifice, he gives well-plural ased, desirable (wealth) to the people who approach him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व मरुत्स्विंद्रे यशसं कृधी नः ।आ नक्ता बर्हिः सदतामुषासोशंता मित्रावरुणा यजेह ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ adhvarám ǀ juṣasva ǀ marút-su ǀ índre ǀ yaśásam ǀ kṛdhi ǀ naḥ ǀā́ ǀ náktā ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sadatām ǀ uṣásā ǀ uśántā ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ yaja ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be gratified,Agni, by this our sacrifice; render our (worship) renowned among Indraand the Maruts; letthe days and nights sit down on the sacred grass; worship (Agni), at this rite,Mitraand Varuṇa, desiring (theoblation).
verses.wilson_translation: Be gratified,Agni, by this our sacrifice; render our (worship) renowned among Indraand the Maruts; letthe days and nights sit down on the sacred grass; worship (Agni), at this rite,Mitraand Varuṇa, desiring (theoblation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवाग्निं सहस्यं वसिष्ठो रायस्कामो विश्वप्स्न्यस्य स्तौत् ।इषं रयिं पप्रथद्वाजमस्मे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ agním ǀ sahasyám ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ rāyáḥ-kāmaḥ ǀ viśvá-psnyasya ǀ staut ǀíṣam ǀ rayím ǀ paprathat ǀ vā́jam ǀ asmé íti ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus has Vasiṣṭhawishing for riches, glorified the vigorous Agnifor the sake of every sort of wealth;may he bestow upon us food, rices, strength; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus has Vasiṣṭhawishing for riches, glorified the vigorous Agnifor the sake of every sort of wealth;may he bestow upon us food, rices, strength; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIII Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SING out the pious at your sacrifices to move with adorations Earth and Heaven-The Holy Singers, whose unmatched devotions, like a tree's branches, part in all directions. Let sacrifice proceed like some fleet courser: with one accord lift ye on high the ladles.Strew sacred grass meet for the solenm service: bright flames that love the Gods have mounted upward. Like babes in arms reposing on their mother, let the Gods sit upon the grass's summit.Let general fire make bright the flame of worship: scorn us not, Agni, in the Gods’ assembly. Gladly the Gods have let themselves be honoured, milking the copious streams of holy Order.The highest might to-day is yours, the Vasits': come ye, as many as ye are, one-minded. So, Agni, send us wealth among the people: may we be closely knit to thee, O Victor,Unharmed, and rich, and taking joy together. Preserve us evermore, ye ods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो यज्ञेषु देवयंतो अर्चंद्यावा नमोभिः पृथिवी इषध्यै ।येषां ब्रह्माण्यसमानि विप्रा विष्वग्वियंति वनिनो न शाखाः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ arcan ǀ dyā́vā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ iṣádhyai ǀyéṣām ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ ásamāni ǀ víprā ǀ víṣvak ǀ vi-yánti ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śā́khāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Devout worshippers seek to attain you, gods, by praises at sacrifices; they (worship) the heaven andearth, they of whom the divesified adorations spread everywhere like th ebranches of trees.
verses.wilson_translation: Devout worshippers seek to attain you, gods, by praises at sacrifices; they (worship) the heaven andearth, they of whom the divesified adorations spread everywhere like th ebranches of trees.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यज्ञ एतु हेत्वो न सप्तिरुद्यच्छध्वं समनसो घृताचीः ।स्तृणीत बर्हिरध्वराय साधूर्ध्वा शोचींषि देवयून्यस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ etu ǀ hétvaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sáptiḥ ǀ út ǀ yacchadhvam ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ ghṛtā́cīḥ ǀstṛṇītá ǀ barhíḥ ǀ adhvarā́ya ǀ sādhú ǀ ūrdhvā́ ǀ śocī́ṃṣi ǀ deva-yū́ni ǀ asthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift course (tot he gods); elevate, (priests), with one occurred, yourladles, charged with butter; spread for the solemnity the sacred grass;le the flames (of the burnt-offering) to thegods ascend on high.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift course (tot he gods); elevate, (priests), with one occurred, yourladles, charged with butter; spread for the solemnity the sacred grass;le the flames (of the burnt-offering) to thegods ascend on high.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ पुत्रासो न मातरं विभृत्राः सानौ देवासो बर्हिषः सदंतु ।आ विश्वाची विदथ्यामनक्त्वग्ने मा नो देवताता मृधस्कः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ mātáram ǀ ví-bhṛtrāḥ ǀ sā́nau ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ barhíṣaḥ ǀ sadantu ǀā́ ǀ viśvā́cī ǀ vidathyā́m ǀ anaktu ǀ ágne ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ devá-tātā ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ karíti kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the gods sit down on the summit of the sacred grass, like children nursed on the (lap of the) mother;let the full ladle,Agni, pour (the oblaion) on the sacrificial flame; give us not up to your adversaries in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the gods sit down on the summit of the sacred grass, like children nursed on the (lap of the) mother;let the full ladle,Agni, pour (the oblaion) on the sacrificial flame; give us not up to your adversaries in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते सीषपंत जोषमा यजत्रा ऋतस्य धाराः सुदुघा दुहानाः ।ज्येष्ठं वो अद्य मह आ वसूनामा गंतन समनसो यति ष्ठ ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ sīṣapanta ǀ jóṣam ǀ ā́ ǀ yájatrāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhā́rāḥ ǀ su-dúghāḥ ǀ dúhānāḥ ǀjyéṣṭham ǀ vaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ máhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vásūnām ǀ ā́ ǀ gantana ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ yáti ǀ sthá ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the adorable deities, who are the bestowers of water, the shedders of showers, be fully propitiated(by our praises); may the most precious and commendable of your treasure (be ours) today; and do you with oneaccord come hither.
verses.wilson_translation: May the adorable deities, who are the bestowers of water, the shedders of showers, be fully propitiated(by our praises); may the most precious and commendable of your treasure (be ours) today; and do you with oneaccord come hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा नो अग्ने विक्ष्वा दशस्य त्वया वयं सहसावन्नास्क्राः ।राया युजा सधमादो अरिष्टा यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ vikṣú ǀ ā́ ǀ daśasya ǀ tváyā ǀ vayám ǀ sahasā-van ǀ ā́skrāḥ ǀrāyā́ ǀ yujā́ ǀ sadha-mā́daḥ ǀ áriṣṭāḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be glorified Agni; grant us (wealth) among the people; may we, vigorous Agni, ever be undeserted byyou, but always be rejoicing and unmolested in the possession of riches; and do you, (gods), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Be glorified Agni; grant us (wealth) among the people; may we, vigorous Agni, ever be undeserted byyou, but always be rejoicing and unmolested in the possession of riches; and do you, (gods), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIV. Dadhikrās.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I CALL on Dadhikrās, the first, to give you aid, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Dawn, and Agni kindled well,Indra, and Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Light. When, rising, to the sacrifice we hasten, awaking Dadhikrās with adorations.Seating on sacred grass the Goddess Iḷā. let us invoke the sage swift-hearing Aśvins. While I am thus arousing Dadhikrāvan I speak to Agni, Earth, and Dawn, and Sūrya,The red, the brown of Varuṇa ever mindful: may they ward off from us all grief and trouble. Foremost is Dadhikrāvan, vigorous courser; in forefront of the cars, his way he knoweth,Closely allied with Sūrya and with Morning, Ādityas, and Aṅgirases, and Vasus. May Dadhikrās prepare the way we travel that we may pass along the path of Order.May Agni bear us, and the Heavenly Army: hear us all Mighty Ones whom none deceiveth.

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्रां वः प्रथममश्विनोषसमग्निं समिद्धं भगमूतये हुवे ।इंद्रं विष्णुं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिमादित्यांद्यावापृथिवी अपः स्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́m ǀ vaḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ aśvínā ǀ uṣásam ǀ agním ǀ sám-iddham ǀ bhágam ǀ ūtáye ǀ huve ǀíndram ǀ víṣṇum ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátim ǀ ādityā́n ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ sváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For your preservation, (worshippers), I invoke, first, Dadhikrā, then the Aśvins, the Dawn, the kindled Agni,Bhaga,Indra,Viṣṇu,Pūṣan,Brahmaṇaspati, theĀdityas, heaven and earth, the waters, the sun.
verses.wilson_translation: For your preservation, (worshippers), I invoke, first, Dadhikrā, then the Aśvins, the Dawn, the kindled Agni,Bhaga,Indra,Viṣṇu,Pūṣan,Brahmaṇaspati, theĀdityas, heaven and earth, the waters, the sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्रामु नमसा बोधयंत उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयंतः ।इळां देवीं बर्हिषि सादयंतोऽश्विना विप्रा सुहवा हुवेम ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ námasā ǀ bodháyantaḥ ǀ ut-ī́rāṇāḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ upa-prayántaḥ ǀíḷām ǀ devī́m ǀ barhíṣi ǀ sādáyantaḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ víprāḥ ǀ su-hávā ǀ huvema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Arousing and animating Dadhikrā, proceeding diligently with the sacrifice; seating the divine Iḷā onthe sacred grass, let us invoke the intelligent and worthily-invoked Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: Arousing and animating Dadhikrā, proceeding diligently with the sacrifice; seating the divine Iḷā onthe sacred grass, let us invoke the intelligent and worthily-invoked Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्रावाणं बुबुधानो अग्निमुप ब्रुव उषसं सूर्यं गां ।ब्रध्नं मांश्चतोर्वरुणस्य बभ्रुं ते विश्वास्मद्दुरिता यावयंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́vāṇam ǀ bubudhānáḥ ǀ agním ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀ uṣásam ǀ sū́ryam ǀ gā́m ǀbradhnám ǀ máṃścatóḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ babhrúm ǀ té ǀ víśvā ǀ asmát ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ yavayantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Propitiating Dadhikrāvan, I glorify Agni, Uṣas, the sun, the earth, the great brown horse of Varuṇa,who is mindful of his adorers; may they put far away from us iniquities.
verses.wilson_translation: Propitiating Dadhikrāvan, I glorify Agni, Uṣas, the sun, the earth, the great brown horse of Varuṇa,who is mindful of his adorers; may they put far away from us iniquities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दधिक्रावा प्रथमो वाज्यर्वाग्रे रथानां भवति प्रजानन् ।संविदान उषसा सूर्येणादित्येभिर्वसुभिरंगिरोभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: dadhi-krā́vā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ vājī́ ǀ árvā ǀ ágre ǀ ráthānām ǀ bhavati ǀ pra-jānán ǀsam-vidānáḥ ǀ uṣásā ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ ādityébhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dadhikrāvan, the swift steed, the first (of horses), knowing (his office), is in the front of the chariots (ofthe gods), consentient with Uṣas, with Sūrya, wiḥ theĀdityas, with the Vasus, with the Aṅgirasas.
verses.wilson_translation: Dadhikrāvan, the swift steed, the first (of horses), knowing (his office), is in the front of the chariots (ofthe gods), consentient with Uṣas, with Sūrya, wiḥ theĀdityas, with the Vasus, with the Aṅgirasas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो दधिक्राः पथ्यामनक्त्वृतस्य पंथामन्वेतवा उ ।शृणोतु नो दैव्यं शर्धो अग्निः शृण्वंतु विश्वे महिषा अमूराः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ dadhi-krā́ḥ ǀ pathyā́m ǀ anaktu ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǀ ánu-etavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀśṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀ dáivyam ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ śṛṇvántu ǀ víśve ǀ mahiṣā́ḥ ǀ ámūrāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Dadhikrā sprinkle our path (with water), that we may follow the road of sacrifice; may Agni, thestrength of the gods, here our (invocation); may the mighty, unperplexed, universal deities hear it.
verses.wilson_translation: May Dadhikrā sprinkle our path (with water), that we may follow the road of sacrifice; may Agni, thestrength of the gods, here our (invocation); may the mighty, unperplexed, universal deities hear it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLV. Savitar.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY the God Savitar, rich in goodly treasures, filling the region, borne by steeds, come hither,In his hand holding much that makes men happy, lulling to slumber and arousing creatures. Golden, sublime, and easy in their motion, his arms extend unto the bounds of heaven.Now shall that mightiness of his he lauded: even Sūrya yields to him in active vigour. May this God Savitar, the Strong and Mighty, the Lord of precious wealth, vouchsafe us treasures.May he, advancing his far-spreading lustre, bestow on us the food that feedeth mortals. These songs praise Savitar whose tongue is pleasant, praise him whose arms are full, whose hands are lovely.High vital strength, and manifold, may he grant us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: आ देवो यातु सविता सुरत्नोऽंतरिक्षप्रा वहमानो अश्वैः ।हस्ते दधानो नर्या पुरूणि निवेशयंच प्रसुवंच भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ yātu ǀ savitā́ ǀ su-rátnaḥ ǀ antarikṣa-prā́ḥ ǀ váhamānaḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀháste ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ náryā ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ ni-veśáyan ǀ ca ǀ pra-suván ǀ ca ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Borne by his steeds, may the divine Savitā, who is possessed of precious treasure, and filling thefirmament (with radiance), come hither, holding in hishandsmany things good for man, and (both) tranquilizingand animating living beings.
verses.wilson_translation: Borne by his steeds, may the divine Savitā, who is possessed of precious treasure, and filling thefirmament (with radiance), come hither, holding in hishandsmany things good for man, and (both) tranquilizingand animating living beings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदस्य बाहू शिथिरा बृहंता हिरण्यया दिवो अंताँ अनष्टां ।नूनं सो अस्य महिमा पनिष्ट सूरश्चिदस्मा अनु दादपस्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ asya ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ śithirā́ ǀ bṛhántā ǀ hiraṇyáyā ǀ diváḥ ǀ ántān ǀ anaṣṭām ǀnūnám ǀ sáḥ ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ paniṣṭa ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ cit ǀ asmai ǀ ánu ǀ dāt ǀ apasyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the outspread, vast, and golden arms of Savitāextend to the ends of the sky; verily his greatnessis glorified (by us); may the sun impart energy unto him.
verses.wilson_translation: May the outspread, vast, and golden arms of Savitāextend to the ends of the sky; verily his greatnessis glorified (by us); may the sun impart energy unto him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स घा नो देवः सविता सहावा साविषद्वसुपतिर्वसूनि ।विश्रयमाणो अमतिमुरूचीं मर्तभोजनमध रासते नः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ gha ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ sahá-vā ǀ ā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ vásu-patiḥ ǀ vásūni ǀvi-śráyamāṇaḥ ǀ amátim ǀ urūcī́m ǀ marta-bhójanam ǀ ádha ǀ rāsate ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine Savitā, who is endowed with energy, the lord of treasure, bestow treasures upon usconcentrating infinite lustre; may he bestow upon us wealh, the source of the enjoyment of mortals.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitā, who is endowed with energy, the lord of treasure, bestow treasures upon usconcentrating infinite lustre; may he bestow upon us wealh, the source of the enjoyment of mortals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा गिरः सवितारं सुजिह्वं पूर्णगभस्तिमीळते सुपाणिं ।चित्रं वयो बृहदस्मे दधातु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ savitā́ram ǀ su-jihvám ǀ pūrṇá-gabhastim ǀ īḷate ǀ su-pāṇím ǀcitrám ǀ váyaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ asmé íti ǀ dadhātu ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These praises glorify the eloquent-tongued, dextrous-handed, whosehandsare full (of wealth); may hebestow upon us manifold and abundant food; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: These praises glorify the eloquent-tongued, dextrous-handed, whosehandsare full (of wealth); may hebestow upon us manifold and abundant food; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVI. Rudra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To Rudra bring these songs, whose bow is firm and strong, the self-dependent God with swiftly-flying shafts,The Wise, the Conqueror whom none may overcome, armed with sharp-pointed weapons: may he hear our call. He through his lordship thinks on beings of the earth, on heavenly beings through his high imperial sway.Come willingly to our doors that gladly welcome thee, and heal all sickness, Rudra., in our families. May thy bright arrow which, shot down by thee from heaven, flieth upon the earth, pass us uninjured by.Thou, very gracious God, hast thousand medicines: inflict no evil on our sons or progeny. Slay us not, nor abandon us, O Rudra let not thy noose, when thou art angry, seize us.Give us trimmed grass and fame among the living. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधाव्ने ।अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता श��णोतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ sthirá-dhanvane ǀ gíraḥ ǀ kṣiprá-iṣave ǀ devā́ya ǀ svadhā́-vne ǀáṣāḷhāya ǀ sáhamānāya ǀ vedháse ǀ tigmá-āyudhāya ǀ bharata ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer these praises to the divine Rudra, armed with the strong bow and fast-flying arrows, the bestowerof food, the invincible, the conqueror, the creator, the wielder of sharp weapons; may he hear our (praises).
verses.wilson_translation: Offer these praises to the divine Rudra, armed with the strong bow and fast-flying arrows, the bestowerof food, the invincible, the conqueror, the creator, the wielder of sharp weapons; may he hear our (praises).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि क्षयेण क्षम्यस्य जन्मनः साम्राज्येन दिव्यस्य चेतति ।अवन्नवंतीरुप नो दुरश्चरानमीवो रुद्र जासु नो भव ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ kṣáyeṇa ǀ kṣámyasya ǀ jánmanaḥ ǀ sā́m-rājyena ǀ divyásya ǀ cétati ǀávan ǀ ávantīḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ dúraḥ ǀ cara ǀ anamīváḥ ǀ rudra ǀ jā́su ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is known by his rule over those of terrestrial birth, by his sovereignty over those of celestial (origin);protecting our progeny,Rudra, propitiating you (by praise), come to our dwellings, and be to them a guardianagainst disease.
verses.wilson_translation: He is known by his rule over those of terrestrial birth, by his sovereignty over those of celestial (origin);protecting our progeny,Rudra, propitiating you (by praise), come to our dwellings, and be to them a guardianagainst disease.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या ते दिद्युदवसृष्टा दिवस्परि क्ष्मया चरति परि सा वृणक्तु नः ।सहस्रं ते स्वपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषु तनयेषु रीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ te ǀ didyút ǀ áva-sṛṣṭā ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ cárati ǀ pári ǀ sā́ ǀ vṛṇaktu ǀ naḥ ǀsahásram ǀ te ǀ su-apivāta ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ tokéṣu ǀ tánayeṣu ǀ ririṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your blazing (weapon), which, discharged from heaven, traverses the earth, avoid us; thine,appeaser of the wind, are a thousand medicaments; inflict not evil upon our sons and grandsons.
verses.wilson_translation: May your blazing (weapon), which, discharged from heaven, traverses the earth, avoid us; thine,appeaser of the wind, are a thousand medicaments; inflict not evil upon our sons and grandsons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो वधी रुद्र मा परा दा मा ते भूम प्रसितौ हीळितस्य ।आ नो भज बर्हिषि जीवशंसे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vadhīḥ ǀ rudra ǀ mā́ ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ bhūma ǀ prá-sitau ǀ hīḷitásya ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhaja ǀ barhíṣi ǀ jīva-śaṃsé ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harm us not,Rudra; abandon us not; let us not fall under the bondage of you when displeased; makeus partakers of the life-promotion sacrifice; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Harm us not,Rudra; abandon us not; let us not fall under the bondage of you when displeased; makeus partakers of the life-promotion sacrifice; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVII. Waters.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY we obtain this day from you, O Waters, that wave of pure refreshment, which the piousMade erst the special beverage of Indra, bright, stainless, rich in sweets and dropping fatness. May the Floods' Offspring, he whose course is rapid, protect that wave most rich in sweets, O Waters,That shall make Indra and the Vasus joyful. This may we gain from you to-day, we pious. All-purifying, joying in their nature, to paths of Gods the Goddesses move onward.They never violate the laws of Indra. Present the oil-rich offering to the Rivers. Whom Sūrya with his bright beams hath attracted, and Indra dug the path for them to travel,May these Streams give us ample room and freedom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: आपो यं वः प्रथमं देवयंत इंद्रपानमूर्मिमकृण्वतेळः ।तं वो ��यं शुचिमरिप्रमद्य घृतप्रुषं मधुमंतं वनेम ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ yám ǀ vaḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ indra-pā́nam ǀ ūrmím ǀ ákṛṇvata ǀ iḷáḥ ǀtám ǀ vaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ śúcim ǀ ariprám ǀ adyá ǀ ghṛta-prúṣam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ vanema ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit from you, Waters, today, that pure, faultless, rain- shedding, sweet essence of the earth,which devout have first consecrated as the Somafor Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit from you, Waters, today, that pure, faultless, rain- shedding, sweet essence of the earth,which devout have first consecrated as the Somafor Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमूर्मिमापो मधुमत्तमं वोऽपां नपादवत्वाशुहेमा ।यस्मिन्निंद्रो वसुभिर्मादयाते तमश्याम देवयंतो वो अद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūrmím ǀ āpaḥ ǀ mádhumat-tamam ǀ vaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ avatu ǀ āśu-hémā ǀyásmin ǀ índraḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ mādáyāte ǀ tám ǀ aśyāma ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ adyá ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the swift-moving grandson of the Waters protect, Waters, your most sweet essence, wherewiḥ may Indra and the Vasusbe delighted; and may we, devoted to the gods, partake (of it).
verses.wilson_translation: May the swift-moving grandson of the Waters protect, Waters, your most sweet essence, wherewiḥ may Indra and the Vasusbe delighted; and may we, devoted to the gods, partake (of it).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतपवित्राः स्वधया मदंतीर्देवीर्देवानामपि यंति पाथः ।ता इंद्रस्य न मिनंति व्रतानि सिंधुभ्यो हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥
verses.transliteration: śatá-pavitrāḥ ǀ svadháyā ǀ mádantīḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ápi ǀ yanti ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ ná ǀ minanti ǀ vratā́ni ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ havyám ǀ ghṛtá-vat ǀ juhota ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Waters, the purifiers of many, gratifying men with food, pursue the paths of the gods; theyimpede not the sacred rites of Indra; offer, (priests), the butter-charged oblation to the rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Waters, the purifiers of many, gratifying men with food, pursue the paths of the gods; theyimpede not the sacred rites of Indra; offer, (priests), the butter-charged oblation to the rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: याः सूर्यो रश्मिभिराततान याभ्य इंद्रो अरदद्गातुमूर्मिं ।ते सिंधवो वरिवो धातना नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ ā-tatā́na ǀ yā́bhyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ áradat ǀ gātúm ǀ ūrmím ǀté ǀ sindhavaḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ dhātana ǀ naḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Waters, whom the sun has evaporized by his rays, for whom Indrahas opened a path by which toissue, bestow upon us wealth; and do you (also) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, whom the sun has evaporized by his rays, for whom Indrahas opened a path by which toissue, bestow upon us wealth; and do you (also) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLVIII. Ṛbhus.
hymns.anukramani: ४ मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठ:। ऋभव:, ४ विश्वे देवा वा । त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE liberal Heroes, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, come and delight you with our flowing Soma.May your strength, Vibhus, as ye come to meet us, turn hitherward your car that brings men profit. May we as Ṛbhu with your Ṛbhus conquer strength with our strength, as Vibhus with the Vibhus.May Vāja aid us in the fight for booty, and helped by Indra may we quell the foeman. For they rule many tribes with high dominion, and conquer all their foes in close encounter.May Indra, Vibhvan, Vāja, and Ṛbhukṣan destroy by turns the wicked foeman's valour. Now, Deities, give us ample room and freedom: be all of you, one-minded, our protection.So let the Vasus grant us strength and vigour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुक्षणो वाजा मादयध्वमस्मे नरो मघवानः सुतस्य ।आ वोऽर्वाचः क्रतवो न यातां विभ्वो रथं नर्यं वर्तयंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛ́bhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ vājāḥ ǀ mādáyadhvam ǀ asmé íti ǀ naraḥ ǀ magha-vānaḥ ǀ sutásya ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ arvā́caḥ ǀ krátavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yātā́m ǀ ví-bhvaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ náryam ǀ vartayantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ṛbhu, (Vibhu), and Vāja, leaders of rites, possessors of opulence, be exhilarated by our effused(libation); may your active and powerful (horses) bring to our presence your chariot, beneficial to mankiṇḍ
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛbhu, (Vibhu), and Vāja, leaders of rites, possessors of opulence, be exhilarated by our effused(libation); may your active and powerful (horses) bring to our presence your chariot, beneficial to mankiṇḍ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुर्ऋभुभिरभि वः स्याम विभ्वो विभुभिः शवसा शवांसि ।वाजो अस्माँ अवतु वाजसाताविंद्रेण युजा तरुषेम वृत्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhúḥ ǀ ṛbhú-bhiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vaḥ ǀ syāma ǀ ví-bhvaḥ ǀ vibhú-bhiḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ śávāṃsi ǀvā́jaḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ avatu ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀ índreṇa ǀ yujā́ ǀ taruṣema ǀ vṛtrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty with theṚbhus, opulent with the Vibhus, may we overcome by strength, the strength (of ourfoes); may Vājadefend us in battle; with Indra, our ally, may we destroy the enemy.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty with theṚbhus, opulent with the Vibhus, may we overcome by strength, the strength (of ourfoes); may Vājadefend us in battle; with Indra, our ally, may we destroy the enemy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते चिद्धि पूर्वीरभि संति शासा विश्वाँ अर्य उपरताति वन्वन् ।इंद्रो विभ्वाँ ऋभुक्षा वाजो अर्यः शत्रोर्मिथत्या कृणवन्वि नृम्णं ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sánti ǀ śāsā́ ǀ víśvān ǀ aryáḥ ǀ upará-tāti ǀ vanvan ǀíndraḥ ǀ ví-bhvā ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ śátroḥ ǀ mithatyā́ ǀ kṛṇavan ǀ ví ǀ nṛmṇám ǁ
verses.english_translation: They verily, (IndraandṚbhus), overcome multitudes by their prowess; they overcome all enemies inthe missile conflict; may Indra, Vibhvan,Ṛbhukṣinand Vāja, the subduers of foes, annihilate by their wrath thestrength of the enemy.
verses.wilson_translation: They verily, (IndraandṚbhus), overcome multitudes by their prowess; they overcome all enemies inthe missile conflict; may Indra, Vibhvan,Ṛbhukṣinand Vāja, the subduers of foes, annihilate by their wrath thestrength of the enemy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू देवासो वरिवः कर्तना नो भूत नो विश्वेऽवसे सजोषाः ।समस्मे इषं वसवो ददीरन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ kartana ǀ naḥ ǀ bhūtá ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ávase ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀsám ǀ asmé íti ǀ íṣam ǀ vásavaḥ ǀ dadīran ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant us, deities, this day opulence; may you all, may you all, well- plural ased alike, be (ready) for ourprotection; may the exalted (Ṛbhus) bestow upon us food; and do you (all) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Grant us, deities, this day opulence; may you all, may you all, well- plural ased alike, be (ready) for ourprotection; may the exalted (Ṛbhus) bestow upon us food; and do you (all) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIX. Waters.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FORTH from the middle of the flood the Waters-their chief the Sea-flow cleansing, never sleeping.Indra, the Bull, the Thunderer, dug their channels: here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me. Waters which come from heaven, or those that wander dug from the earth, or flowing free by nature,Bright, purifying, speeding to the Ocean, here let those Waters. Goddesses, protect me. Those amid whom goes Varuṇa the Sovran, he who discriminates men's truth and falsehood-Distilling meath, the bright, the purifying, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me. They from whom Varuṇa the King, and Soma, and all the Deities drink strength and vigour,They into whom Vaiśvānara Agni entered, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect Me.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रज्येष्ठाः सलिलस्य मध्यात्पुनाना यंत्यनिविशमानाः ।इंद्रो या वज्री वृषभो रराद ता आपो देवीरिह मामवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: samudrá-jyeṣṭhāḥ ǀ salilásya ǀ mádhyāt ǀ punānā́ḥ ǀ yanti ǀ áni-viśamānāḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ vajrī́ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ rarā́da ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mā́m ǀ avantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The waters, with their ocen-chief, proceed from the midst of the firmament, purifying (all things), flowingunceasingly; may the divine waters, whom the thunder-bearing Indra, the showerer, sent forth, protect me here(on earth).
verses.wilson_translation: The waters, with their ocen-chief, proceed from the midst of the firmament, purifying (all things), flowingunceasingly; may the divine waters, whom the thunder-bearing Indra, the showerer, sent forth, protect me here(on earth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या आपो दिव्या उत वा स्रवंति खनित्रिमा उत वा याः स्वयंजाः ।समुद्रार्था याः शुचयः पावकास्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ divyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ srávanti ǀ khanítrimāḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ svayam-jā́ḥ ǀsamudrá-arthāḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ pāvakā́ḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mā́m ǀ avantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the waters that are in the sky, or those that flow (on the earth), those (whose channels) have beendug, or those that have sprung up spontaneously, and those that seek the ocean. All pure and purifying, maythose divine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.wilson_translation: May the waters that are in the sky, or those that flow (on the earth), those (whose channels) have beendug, or those that have sprung up spontaneously, and those that seek the ocean. All pure and purifying, maythose divine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यासां राजा वरुणो याति मध्ये सत्यानृते अवपश्यंजनानां ।मधुश्चुतः शुचयो याः पावकास्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́sām ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yā́ti ǀ mádhye ǀ satyānṛté íti ǀ ava-páśyan ǀ jánānām ǀmadhu-ścútaḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ pāvakā́ḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mā́m ǀ avantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those whose sovereign,Varuṇa, passes in the middle sphere, discriminating the truth and falsehod ofmankind; those shedding sweet showers, pure and purifying; may those divine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.wilson_translation: Those whose sovereign,Varuṇa, passes in the middle sphere, discriminating the truth and falsehod ofmankind; those shedding sweet showers, pure and purifying; may those divine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यासु राजा वरुणो यासु सोमो विश्वे देवा यासूर्जं मदंति ।वैश्वानरो यास्वग्निः प्रविष्टस्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́su ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yā́su ǀ sómaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yā́su ǀ ū́rjam ǀ mádanti ǀvaiśvānaráḥ ǀ yā́su ǀ agníḥ ǀ prá-viṣṭaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mā́m ǀ avantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May they in which their king,Varuṇa, in which Soma, abides, in which the gods delight (to receive) thesacrificial food, into which Agni Vaiśvānaraentered, may those diine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.wilson_translation: May they in which their king,Varuṇa, in which Soma, abides, in which the gods delight (to receive) thesacrificial food, into which Agni Vaiśvānaraentered, may those diine waters protect me here (on earth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN L. Various Deities.
hymns.anukramani: ४ मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठ:।१ मित्रावरुणौ,२ अग्नि:, ३ विश्वे देवा:, ४नद्य: ।  जगती ,४ अतिजगती शक्व्वरी वा ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O MITRA-VARUNA, guard and protect me here: let not that come to me which nests within and swells.I drive afar the scorpion hateful to the sight: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot. Eruption that appears upon the twofold joints, and that which overspreads the ankles and the knees,May the refulgent Agni banish far away let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot. The poison that is formed upon the Salmali, that which is found in streams, that which the plants produce,All this may all the Gods banish and drive away: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot. The steep declivities, the valleys, and the heights, the channels full of water, and the waterless-May those who swell with water, gracious Goddesses, never afflict us with the Sipada disease, may all the rivers keep us free from Simida.

verses.sanskrit: आ मां मित्रावरुणेह रक्षतं कुलाययद्विश्वयन्मा न आ गन् ।अजकावं दुर्दृशीकं तिरो दधे मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ ihá ǀ rakṣatam ǀ kulāyáyat ǀ vi-śváyat ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gan ǀajakā-vám ǀ duḥ-dṛ́śīkam ǀ tiráḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ mā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ pádyena ǀ rápasā ǀ vidat ǀ tsáruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, protect me here (in this world) let not the insidious and spreading (poison) reach me;may the equally malignant and undiscernible (venom) disappear; let not the tortuous (snake) recognize me by thesound of my footsteps.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, protect me here (in this world) let not the insidious and spreading (poison) reach me;may the equally malignant and undiscernible (venom) disappear; let not the tortuous (snake) recognize me by thesound of my footsteps.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्विजामन्परुषि वंदनं भुवदष्ठीवंतौ परि कुल्फौ च देहत् ।अग्निष्टच्छोचन्नप बाधतामितो मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vi-jā́man ǀ páruṣi ǀ vándanam ǀ bhúvat ǀ aṣṭhīvántau ǀ pári ǀ kulpháu ǀ ca ǀ déhat ǀagníḥ ǀ tát ǀ śócan ǀ ápa ǀ bādhatām ǀ itáḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ pádyena ǀ rápasā ǀ vidat ǀ tsáruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the brilliant Agnicounteract that poison which is genitive rated in the manifold knots (of trees) and thelike, or which is smeared upon the knees of ankles; let not the tortuous snake recognize me by the sound of myfootsteps.
verses.wilson_translation: May the brilliant Agnicounteract that poison which is genitive rated in the manifold knots (of trees) and thelike, or which is smeared upon the knees of ankles; let not the tortuous snake recognize me by the sound of myfootsteps.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यच्छल्मलौ भवति यन्नदीषु यदोषधीभ्यः परि जायते विषं ।विश्वे देवा निरितस्तत्सुवंतु मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ śalmaláu ǀ bhávati ǀ yát ǀ nadī́ṣu ǀ yát ǀ óṣadhībhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ jā́yate ǀ viṣám ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ itáḥ ǀ tát ǀ suvantu ǀ mā́ ǀ mā́m ǀ pádyena ǀ rápasā ǀ vidat ǀ tsáruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The poison that is in theŚalmalītree, in the rivers, or which is genitive rated from plural nts, may theuniversal gods remove from hence; let not the tortuous (snake) recognize me by the sound of my footsteps.
verses.wilson_translation: The poison that is in theŚalmalītree, in the rivers, or which is genitive rated from plural nts, may theuniversal gods remove from hence; let not the tortuous (snake) recognize me by the sound of my footsteps.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: याः प्रवतो निवत उद्वत उदन्वतीरनुदकाश्च याः ।ता अस्मभ्यं पयसा पिन्वमानाः शिवा देवीरशिपदा भवंतु सर्वा नद्यो अशिमिदा भवंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ ni-vátaḥ ǀ ut-vátaḥ ǀ udan-vátīḥ ǀ anudakā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́ḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ páyasā ǀ pínvamānāḥ ǀ śivā́ḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ aśipadā́ḥ ǀ bhavantu ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ aśimidā́ḥ ǀ bhavantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the divine rivers, whether flowing down declivities, in hollow plural ces, or upwards, whether filled withwater or dry, nourishing all with their water, be auspicious to us communicating not disease; may all the rivers beunproductive of harm.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine rivers, whether flowing down declivities, in hollow plural ces, or upwards, whether filled withwater or dry, nourishing all with their water, be auspicious to us communicating not disease; may all the rivers beunproductive of harm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LI. Ādityas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: THROUGH the Ādityas’ most auspicious shelter, through their most recent succour may we conquer.May they, the Mighty, giving ear, establish this sacrifice, to make us free and sinless. Let Aditi rejoice and the Ādityas, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, most righteous.May they, the Guardians of the world, protect us, and, to show favour, drink this day our Soma. All Universal Deities, the Maruts, all the Ādityas, yea, and all the Ṛbhus,Indra, and Agni, and the Aśvins, lauded. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्यानामवसा नूतनेन सक्षीमहि शर्मणा शंतमेन ।अनागास्त्वे अदितित्वे तुरास इमं यज्ञं दधतु श्रोषमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ādityā́nām ǀ ávasā ǀ nū́tanena ǀ sakṣīmáhi ǀ śármaṇā ǀ śám-tamena ǀanāgā́ḥ-tvé ǀ aditi-tvé ǀ turā́saḥ ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ dadhatu ǀ śróṣamāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, through the protection of theĀdityas, be in the enjoyment of a new and comfortable dwelling;may the swift-moving Ādityas, listening to our praises, preserve this their worshipper in sinlessness andindependence.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, through the protection of theĀdityas, be in the enjoyment of a new and comfortable dwelling;may the swift-moving Ādityas, listening to our praises, preserve this their worshipper in sinlessness andindependence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्यासो अदितिर्मादयंतां मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो रजिष्ठाः ।अस्माकं संतु भुवनस्य गोपाः पिबंतु सोममवसे नो अद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ādityā́saḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ mādayantām ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ rájiṣṭhāḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ santu ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ píbantu ǀ sómam ǀ ávase ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǁ
verses.english_translation: May theĀdityasand Aditi, and the upright Mitra,Āryaman, and Varuṇa, be exhilarated (by thelibation); may the guardians of the world be ours also; may they drink the Somatoday for our preservation.
verses.wilson_translation: May theĀdityasand Aditi, and the upright Mitra,Āryaman, and Varuṇa, be exhilarated (by thelibation); may the guardians of the world be ours also; may they drink the Somatoday for our preservation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्या विश्वे मरुतश्च विश्वे देवाश्च विश्व ऋभवश्च विश्वे ।इंद्रो अग्निरश्विना तुष्टुवाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ādityā́ḥ ǀ víśve ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśve ǀíndraḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ tustuvānā́ḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All theĀdityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, all theṚbhus,Indra,Agni, and the Aśvins, (have been)glorified (by us), do you all ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: All theĀdityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, all theṚbhus,Indra,Agni, and the Aśvins, (have been)glorified (by us), do you all ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Ādityas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY we be free from every bond, Ādityas! a castle among Gods and men, ye Vasus.Winning, may we win Varuṇa and Mitra, and, being, may we be, O Earth and Heaven. May Varuṇa and Mitra grant this blessing, our Guardians, shelter to our seed and offspring.Let us not suffer for another's trespass. nor do the thing that ye, O Vasus, punish. The ever-prompt Aṅgirases, imploring riches from Savitar the God, obtained them.So may our Father who is great and holy, and all the Gods, accordant, grant this favour.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्यासो अदितयः स्याम पूर्देवत्रा वसवो मर्त्यत्रा ।सनेम मित्रावरुणा सनंतो भवेम द्यावापृथिवी भवंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ādityā́saḥ ǀ áditayaḥ ǀ syāma ǀ pū́ḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ martya-trā́ ǀsánema ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ sánantaḥ ǀ bhávema ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ bhávantaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ādityas, may we be independent;Vasus, (dwelling) among the gods, may your protection (extend) tomortals; offering (oblations to you),Mitraand Varuṇa, may we partake (of your bounty); may we, heaven andearth exist (through your favour).
verses.wilson_translation: Ādityas, may we be independent;Vasus, (dwelling) among the gods, may your protection (extend) tomortals; offering (oblations to you),Mitraand Varuṇa, may we partake (of your bounty); may we, heaven andearth exist (through your favour).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो मामहंत शर्म तोकाय तनयाय गोपाः ।मा वो भुजेमान्यजातमेनो मा तत्कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: mitráḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mamahanta ǀ śárma ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀmā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ bhujema ǀ anyá-jātam ǀ énaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tát ǀ karma ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ yát ǀ cáyadhve ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Mitraand Varuṇabestow upon us felicity; (may they), the guardians (of all men, bestow felicity)upon our sons and grandsons; let us not suffer (gods), for offences committed by another; let us not,Vasus, doany act by which you may be offended.
verses.wilson_translation: May Mitraand Varuṇabestow upon us felicity; (may they), the guardians (of all men, bestow felicity)upon our sons and grandsons; let us not suffer (gods), for offences committed by another; let us not,Vasus, doany act by which you may be offended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुरण्यवोऽंगिरसो नक्षंत रत्नं देवस्य सवितुरियानाः ।पिता च तन्नो महान्यजत्रो विश्वे देवाः समनसो जुषंत ॥
verses.transliteration: turaṇyávaḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ nakṣanta ǀ rátnam ǀ devásya ǀ savitúḥ ǀ iyānā́ḥ ǀpitā́ ǀ ca ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ mahā́n ǀ yájatraḥ ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ juṣanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Aṅgirasas, prompt (in worship), soliciting him obtain preious (wealth) from Savitā; may the mightyadorable parent, and the universal god alike favourable minded, approve (of the donation).
verses.wilson_translation: The Aṅgirasas, prompt (in worship), soliciting him obtain preious (wealth) from Savitā; may the mightyadorable parent, and the universal god alike favourable minded, approve (of the donation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Heaven and Earth.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AS priest with solemn rites and adorations I worship Heaven and Earth, the High and Holy.To them, great Parents of the Gods, have sages of ancient time, singing, assigned precedence. With newest hymns set in the seat of Order, those the Two Parents, born before all others,Come, Heaven and Earth, with the Celestial People, hither to us, for strong is your protection. Yea, Heaven and Earth, ye hold in your possession full many a treasure for the liberal giver.Grant us that wealth which comes in free abundance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी नमोभिः सबाध ईळे बृहती यजत्रे ।ते चिद्धि पूर्वे कवयो गृणंतः पुरो मही दधिरे देवपुत्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ dyā́vā ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ īḷe ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ yájatre íti ǀté íti ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ pū́rve ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ dadhiré ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǁ
verses.english_translation: Attended by a concourse (of priests) I worship the adorable and mighty Heaven and Earth withsacrifices and praises, those wo great ones of whom the gods are the sons, whom ancient sages glorifying haveformerly detained.
verses.wilson_translation: Attended by a concourse (of priests) I worship the adorable and mighty Heaven and Earth withsacrifices and praises, those wo great ones of whom the gods are the sons, whom ancient sages glorifying haveformerly detained.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र पूर्वजे पितरा नव्यसीभिर्गीर्भिः कृणुध्वं सदने ऋतस्य ।आ नो द्यावापृथिवी दैव्येन जनेन यातं महि वां वरूथं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ pūrvajé íti pūrva-jé ǀ pitárā ǀ návyasībhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ sádane íti ǀ ṛtásya ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ dáivyena ǀ jánena ǀ yātam ǀ máhi ǀ vām ǀ várūtham ǁ
verses.english_translation: plural ce before (us) in the hall of sacrifice, with new songs, the ancient parents (of all beings); come to us,Heaven and Earth, with the celestial people, for vast is your protecting (wealth).
verses.wilson_translation: plural ce before (us) in the hall of sacrifice, with new songs, the ancient parents (of all beings); come to us,Heaven and Earth, with the celestial people, for vast is your protecting (wealth).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उतो हि वां रत्नधेयानि संति पुरूणि द्यावापृथिवी सुदासे ।अस्मे धत्तं यदसदस्कृधोयु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: utó íti ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ ratna-dhéyāni ǀ sánti ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ su-dā́se ǀasmé íti ǀ dhattam ǀ yát ǀ ásat ǀ áskṛdhoyu ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many, Heavan and Earth, are the treasures fit to be given to the pious donor (of the oblation); give to usthat wealth which is unlimited; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Many, Heavan and Earth, are the treasures fit to be given to the pious donor (of the oblation); give to usthat wealth which is unlimited; and do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Vastospati.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ACKNOWLEDGE us, O Guardian of the Homestead: bring no disease, and give us happy entrance.Whate’er we ask of thee, be pleased to grant it, and prosper thou quadrupeds and bipeds. Protector of the Home, be our promoter: increase our wealth in kine and steeds, O Indu.May we be ever-youthful in thy friendship: be pleased in us as in his sons a father. Through thy dear fellowship that bringeth welfare, may we be victors, Guardian of the Dwelling!Protect our happiness in rest and labour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: वास्तोष्पते प्रति जानीह्यस्मान्त्स्वावेशो अनमीवो भवा नः ।यत्त्वेमहे प्रति तन्नो जुषस्व शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́stoḥ ǀ pate ǀ práti ǀ jānīhi ǀ asmā́n ǀ su-āveśáḥ ǀ anamīváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ naḥ ǀyát ǀ tvā ǀ ī́mahe ǀ práti ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ juṣasva ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
verses.english_translation: Protector of the dwelling, recognize us; be to us an excellent abode the non-inflicter of disease;whatever we ask of you, be plural ased to grant; be the bestower of happiness on our bipeds and quadrupedṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Protector of the dwelling, recognize us; be to us an excellent abode the non-inflicter of disease;whatever we ask of you, be plural ased to grant; be the bestower of happiness on our bipeds and quadrupedṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वास्तोष्पते प्रतरणो न एधि गयस्फानो गोभिरश्वेभिरिंदो ।अजरासस्ते सख्ये स्याम पितेव पुत्रान्प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́stoḥ ǀ pate ǀ pra-táraṇaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ edhi ǀ gaya-sphā́naḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvebhiḥ ǀ indo íti ǀajárāsaḥ ǀ te ǀ sakhyé ǀ syāma ǀ pitā́-iva ǀ putrā́n ǀ práti ǀ naḥ ǀ juṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Protector of the dwelling, be our preserver and the augmenter of our wealth; possessed of catle andhorses,Indra, may we, through your friendship, be exempt from decay; be favourable to us, like a father to hissons.
verses.wilson_translation: Protector of the dwelling, be our preserver and the augmenter of our wealth; possessed of catle andhorses,Indra, may we, through your friendship, be exempt from decay; be favourable to us, like a father to hissons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वास्तोष्पते शग्मया संसदा ते सक्षीमहि रण्वया गातुमत्या ।पाहि क्षेम उत योगे वरं नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́stoḥ ǀ pate ǀ śagmáyā ǀ sam-sádā ǀ te ǀ sakṣīmáhi ǀ raṇváyā ǀ gātu-mátyā ǀpāhí ǀ kṣéme ǀ utá ǀ yóge ǀ váram ǀ naḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Protector of the dwelling, may we be possessed of a comfortable, delightful, opulent abode, bestowedby you; protect our wealth, whether in possession or expectaion; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Protector of the dwelling, may we be possessed of a comfortable, delightful, opulent abode, bestowedby you; protect our wealth, whether in possession or expectaion; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Vastospati.
hymns.anukramani: ८ मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठ:। वास्तोष्पति:, २- ८ इन्द्र:( २-८ प्रस्वापिनी उपनिषद् ) ।१ गायत्री, २-४ उपरिष्टाद्बृहती, ५-८ अनुष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . VASTOSPATI, who killest all disease and wearest every form,Be an auspicious Friend to us. When, O bright Son of Saramā, thou showest, tawny-hued! thy teeth,They gleam like lances' points within thy mouth when thou wouldst bite; go thou to steep. Saramā's Son, retrace thy way: bark at the robber and the thief.At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dust thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep. Be on thy guard against the boar, and let the boar beware of thee.At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dost thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep. Sleep mother, let the father sleep, sleep dog and master of the house.Let all the kinsmen sleep, sleep all the people who are round about. The man who sits, the man who walks, and whosoever looks on us,Of these we closely shut the eyes, even as we closely shut this house. The Bull who hath a thousand horns, who rises up from out the sea,—By him the Strong and Mighty One we lull and make the people sleep. The women sleeping in the court, lying without, or stretched on beds,The matrons with their odorous sweetsthese, one and all, we lull to sleep.

verses.sanskrit: अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन् ।सखा सुशेव एधि नः ॥
verses.transliteration: amīva-hā́ ǀ vāstoḥ ǀ pate ǀ víśvā ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ ā-viśán ǀsákhā ǀ su-śévaḥ ǀ edhi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Protector of the dwelling, remover of disease, assuming all (kinds of) forms, be to us a friend, thegranter of happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Protector of the dwelling, remover of disease, assuming all (kinds of) forms, be to us a friend, thegranter of happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदर्जुन सारमेय दतः पिशंग यच्छसे ।वीव भ्राजंत ऋष्टय उप स्रक्वेषु बप्सतो नि षु स्वप ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ arjuna ǀ sārameya ǀ datáḥ ǀ piśaṅga ǀ yácchase ǀví-iva ǀ bhrājante ǀ ṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ srákveṣu ǀ bápsataḥ ǀ ní ǀ sú ǀ svapa ǁ
verses.english_translation: White offspring of Saramā, with tawny limbs, althogh barking you display your teeth against me,bristling like lances in your gums, nevertheless, to quietly to sleep.
verses.wilson_translation: White offspring of Saramā, with tawny limbs, althogh barking you display your teeth against me,bristling like lances in your gums, nevertheless, to quietly to sleep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तेनं राय सारमेय तस्करं वा पुनःसर ।स्तोतॄनिंद्रस्य रायसि किमस्मांदुच्छुनायसे नि षु स्वप ॥
verses.transliteration: stenám ǀ rāya ǀ sārameya ǀ táskaram ǀ vā ǀ punaḥ-sara ǀstotṝ́n ǀ índrasya ǀ rāyasi ǀ kím ǀ asmā́n ǀ ducchuna-yase ǀ ní ǀ sú ǀ svapa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offspring of Saramā, returning (to the charge), attack the pilferer or the thief; why do you assail theworshippers of Indra? Why do you intimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.
verses.wilson_translation: Offspring of Saramā, returning (to the charge), attack the pilferer or the thief; why do you assail theworshippers of Indra? Why do you intimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं सूकरस्य दर्दृहि तव दर्दर्तु सूकरः ।स्तोतॄनिंद्रस्य रायसि किमस्मांदुच्छुनायसे नि षु स्वप ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ sūkarásya ǀ dardṛhi ǀ táva ǀ dardartu ǀ sūkaráḥ ǀstotṝ́n ǀ índrasya ǀ rāyasi ǀ kím ǀ asmā́n ǀ ducchuna-yase ǀ ní ǀ sú ǀ svapa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you rend the hog; let the hog rend you; why do you assail the worshippers of Indra? Why do youintimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you rend the hog; let the hog rend you; why do you assail the worshippers of Indra? Why do youintimidate us? Go quietly to sleep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सस्तु माता सस्तु पिता सस्तु श्वा सस्तु विश्पतिः ।ससंतु सर्वे ज्ञातयः सस्त्वयमभितो जनः ॥
verses.transliteration: sástu ǀ mātā́ ǀ sástu ǀ pitā́ ǀ sástu ǀ śvā́ ǀ sástu ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀsasántu ǀ sárve ǀ jñātáyaḥ ǀ sástu ǀ ayám ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the mother sleep let the father sleep, let the dog sleep, let the son-in-law sleep, let all the kindredsleep, let the people (who are stationed) around sleep.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the mother sleep let the father sleep, let the dog sleep, let the son-in-law sleep, let all the kindredsleep, let the people (who are stationed) around sleep.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य आस्ते यश्च चरति यश्च पश्यति नो जनः ।तेषां सं हन्मो अक्षाणि यथेदं हर्म्यं तथा ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ā́ste ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ cárati ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ páśyati ǀ naḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǀtéṣām ǀ sám ǀ hanmaḥ ǀ akṣā́ṇi ǀ yáthā ǀ idám ǀ harmyám ǀ táthā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man who sits, or he who walks, or he who sees us, of these weshutup the eyes, so that they maybe as unconscious as the mansion.
verses.wilson_translation: The man who sits, or he who walks, or he who sees us, of these weshutup the eyes, so that they maybe as unconscious as the mansion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रशृंगो वृषभो यः समुद्रादुदाचरत् ।तेना सहस्येना वयं नि जनान्त्स्वापयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: sahásra-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ samudrā́t ǀ ut-ā́carat ǀténa ǀ sahasyéna ǀ vayám ǀ ní ǀ jánān ǀ svāpayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We put men to sleep through the irresisible might or the bull with a thousand horns, who rises out of theocean.
verses.wilson_translation: We put men to sleep through the irresisible might or the bull with a thousand horns, who rises out of theocean.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रोष्ठेशया वह्येशया नारीर्यास्तल्पशीवरीः ।स्त्रियो याः पुण्यगंधास्ताः सर्वाः स्वापयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: proṣṭhe-śayā́ḥ ǀ vahye-śayā́ḥ ǀ nā́rīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ talpa-śī́varīḥ ǀstríyaḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ púṇya-gandhāḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ svāpayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We put to sleep all those women are lying in the courtyard in litter on the bed, the wom who aredecorated with holiday perfumes.
verses.wilson_translation: We put to sleep all those women are lying in the courtyard in litter on the bed, the wom who aredecorated with holiday perfumes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Wno are these radiant men in serried rank, Rudra's young heroes borne by noble steeds? Verily no one knoweth whence they sprang: they, and they only, know each other's birth. They strew each other with their blasts, these Hawks: they strove together, roaring like the wind. A sage was he who knew these mysteries, what in her udder mighty Pṛśni bore. Ever victorious, through the Maruts, be this band of Heroes, nursing manly strength, Most bright in splendour, flectest on their way, close-knit to glory, strong with varied power. Yea, mighty is your power and firm your strength: so, potent, with the Maruts, be the band. Bright is your spirit, wrathful are your minds: your bold troop's minstrel is like one inspired. Ever avert your blazing shaft from us, and let not your displeasure reach us here Your dear names, conquering Maruts, we invoke, calling aloud till we are satisfied. Well-armed, impetuous in their haste, they deck themselves, their forms, with oblations: to you, the pure, ornaments made of gold. Pure, Maruts, pure yourselves, are your oblations: to you, the pure, pure sacrifice I offer.By Law they came to truth, the Law's observers, bright by their birth, and pure, and sanctifying. Your rings, O Maruts, rest upon your shoulders, and chains of gold are twined upon your bosoms.Gleaming with drops of rain, like lightning-flashes, after your wont ye whirl about your weapons. Wide in the depth of air spread forth your glories, far, most adorable, ye bear your titles.Maruts, accept this thousandfold allotment of household sacrifice and household treasure. If, Maruts, ye regard the praise recited here at this mighty singer invocation,Vouchsafe us quickly wealth with noble heroes, wealth which no man uho hateth us may injure. The Maruts, fleet as coursers, while they deck them like youths spectators of a festal meeting,Linger, like beauteous colts, about the dwelling, like frisking calves, these who pour down the water. So may the Maruts help us and be gracious, bringing free room to lovely Earth and Heaven.Far be your bolt that slayeth men and cattle. Ye Vasus, turn yourselves to us with blessings. The priest, when seated, loudly calls you, Maruts, praising in song your universal bounty.He, Bulls! who hath so much in his possession, free from duplicity, with hymns invokes you. These Maruts bring the swift man to a stand-still, and strength with mightier strength they break and humbleThese guard the singer from the man who hates him and lay their sore displeasure on the wicked. These Maruts rouse even the poor and needy: the Vasus love him as an active champion.Drive to a distance, O ye Bulls, the darkness: give us full store of children and descendants.
