verses.transliteration: mahé ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ bodhi ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ mahé ǀ sáubhagāya ǀ prá ǀ yandhi ǀcitrám ǀ rayím ǀ yaśásam ǀ dhehi ǀ asmé íti ǀ dévi ǀ márteṣu ǀ mānuṣi ǀ śravasyúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be unto us today the cause of great felicity; bestow, Uṣas, (what is promotive) of great prosperity; giveus wonderful riches and reputation; grant, divine benefactrss of men, to mortals flourishingmaleposterity.
verses.wilson_translation: Be unto us today the cause of great felicity; bestow, Uṣas, (what is promotive) of great prosperity; giveus wonderful riches and reputation; grant, divine benefactrss of men, to mortals flourishingmaleposterity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एते त्ये भानवो दर्शतायाश्चित्रा उषसो अमृतास आगुः ।जनयंतो दैव्यानि व्रतान्यापृणंतो अंतरिक्षा व्यस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ tyé ǀ bhānávaḥ ǀ darśatā́yāḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāsaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aguḥ ǀjanáyantaḥ ǀ dáivyāni ǀ vratā́ni ǀ ā-pṛṇántaḥ ǀ antárikṣā ǀ ví ǀ asthuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These wonderful, immortal rays of the beautifu Dawn appear, giving birth to the pious rites of divineworship, and filling the firmament, they spread around.
verses.wilson_translation: These wonderful, immortal rays of the beautifu Dawn appear, giving birth to the pious rites of divineworship, and filling the firmament, they spread around.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एषा स्या युजाना पराकात्पंच क्षितीः परि सद्यो जिगाति ।अभिपश्यंती वयुना जनानां दिवो दुहिता भुवनस्य पत्नी ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ syā́ ǀ yujānā́ ǀ parākā́t ǀ páñca ǀ kṣitī́ḥ ǀ pári ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ jigāti ǀabhi-páśyantī ǀ vayúnā ǀ jánānām ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ pátnī ǁ
verses.english_translation: Exerting herself, she approaches rapidly from afar (to give light) to the five classes of men, witnessingthe thoughts of men, the daughter of heaven, the benefactress of living beings.
verses.wilson_translation: Exerting herself, she approaches rapidly from afar (to give light) to the five classes of men, witnessingthe thoughts of men, the daughter of heaven, the benefactress of living beings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वाजिनीवती सूर्यस्य योषा चित्रामघा राय ईशे वसूनां ।ऋषिष्टुता जरयंती मघोन्युषा उच्छति वह्निभिर्गृणाना ॥
verses.transliteration: vājínī-vatī ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ yóṣā ǀ citrá-maghā ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ īśe ǀ vásūnām ǀṛ́ṣi-stutā ǀ jaráyantī ǀ maghónī ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchati ǀ váhni-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bride Sūrya, the distributress (of food), the possessor of wonderful wealth, she rules overtreasures (of every kind) of riches; hymned by the ṛṣis, the waster away of life, the mistress of opulence, sherises glorified by the offerers (of oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: The bride Sūrya, the distributress (of food), the possessor of wonderful wealth, she rules overtreasures (of every kind) of riches; hymned by the ṛṣis, the waster away of life, the mistress of opulence, sherises glorified by the offerers (of oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति द्युतानामरुषासो अश्वाश्चित्रा अदृश्रन्नुषसं वहंतः ।याति शुभ्रा विश्वपिशा रथेन दधाति रत्नं विधते जनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ dyutānā́m ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ adṛśran ǀ uṣásam ǀ váhantaḥ ǀyā́ti ǀ śubhrā́ ǀ viśva-píśā ǀ ráthena ǀ dádhāti ǀ rátnam ǀ vidhaté ǀ jánāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bright and wondrous steeds, conveying the resplendent Uṣas, are visible; she advances, radiantin her every-way-moving chariot; she bestows wealth upon the man who practises sacred rites.
verses.wilson_translation: The bright and wondrous steeds, conveying the resplendent Uṣas, are visible; she advances, radiantin her every-way-moving chariot; she bestows wealth upon the man who practises sacred rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्या सत्येभिर्महती महद्भिर्देवी देवेभिर्यजता यजत्रैः ।रुजद्दृळ्हानि दददुस्रियाणां प्रति गाव उषसं वावशंत ॥
verses.transliteration: satyā́ ǀ satyébhiḥ ǀ mahatī́ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ yajatā́ ǀ yájatraiḥ ǀruját ǀ dṛḷhā́ni ǀ dádat ǀ usríyāṇām ǀ práti ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ uṣásam ǀ vāvaśanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: True with the truthful, great with the great, divine with the deities, adorable with adorable, she dispersesthe solid (glooms), she displays (the pastures) of the cattle; all creatures, the cattle especially, are longing for the Dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: True with the truthful, great with the great, divine with the deities, adorable with adorable, she dispersesthe solid (glooms), she displays (the pastures) of the cattle; all creatures, the cattle especially, are longing for the Dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नू नो गोमद्वीरवद्धेहि रत्नमुषो अश्वावत्पुरुभोजो अस्मे ।मा नो बर्हिः पुरुषता निदे कर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: nú ǀ naḥ ǀ gó-mat ǀ vīrá-vat ǀ dhehi ǀ rátnam ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ áśva-vat ǀ puru-bhójaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ puruṣátā ǀ nidé ǀ kaḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestow upon us, Uṣas, wealth, comprising cattle horses, abundant food, andmaleoffspring; let not oursacrifice incur reproach among men; and do you (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow upon us, Uṣas, wealth, comprising cattle horses, abundant food, andmaleoffspring; let not oursacrifice incur reproach among men; and do you (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVI. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SAVITAR God of all men hath sent upward his light, designed for all mankind, immortal.Through the Gods’ power that Eye was first created. Dawn hath made all the universe apparent. I see the paths which Gods are wont to travel, innocuous paths made ready by the Vasus.Eastward the flag of Dawn hath been uplifted; she hath come hither o’er the tops of houses. Great is, in truth, the number of the Mornings which were aforetime at the Sun's uprising.Since thou, O Dawn, hast been beheld repairing as to thy love, as one no more to leave him. They were the Gods’ companions at the banquet, the ancient sages true to Law Eternal.The Fathers found the light that lay in darkness, and with effectual words begat the Morning. Meeting together in the same enclosure, they strive not, ofone mind, one with another.They never break the Gods’ eternal statutes, and injure none, in rivalry with Vasus. Extolling thee, Blest Goddess, the Vasisthas, awake at early mom, with lauds implore thee.Leader of kine and Queen of all that strengthens, shine, come as first to us, O high-born Morning. She bringeth bounty and sweet charm of voices. The flushing Dawn is sung by the Vasisthas,Giving us riches famed to distant places. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: उदु ज्योतिरमृतं विश्वजन्यं विश्वानरः सविता देवो अश्रेत् ।क्रत्वा देवानामजनिष्ट चक्षुराविरकर्भुवनं विश्वमुषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ viśvá-janyam ǀ viśvā́naraḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aśret ǀkrátvā ǀ devā́nām ǀ ajaniṣṭa ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ akaḥ ǀ bhúvanam ǀ víśvam ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Savitā, the leader of all, sends upwards the immortal, all- benefiting light; the eye of thegods has been manifested for (the celebration of) religious rites; the Dawn has made all creatures visible.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Savitā, the leader of all, sends upwards the immortal, all- benefiting light; the eye of thegods has been manifested for (the celebration of) religious rites; the Dawn has made all creatures visible.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र मे पंथा देवयाना अदृश्रन्नमर्धंतो वसुभिरिष्कृतासः ।अभूदु केतुरुषसः पुरस्तात्प्रतीच्यागादधि हर्म्येभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ me ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ deva-yā́nāḥ ǀ adṛśran ǀ ámardhantaḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ íṣkṛtāsaḥ ǀábhūt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ketúḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ pratīcī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ ádhi ǀ harmyébhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The paths that lead to the gods are beheld by me, innocuous and glorious with light; the banner of Uṣas is displayed in the east, she comes to the west, rising above high plural ces.
verses.wilson_translation: The paths that lead to the gods are beheld by me, innocuous and glorious with light; the banner of Uṣas is displayed in the east, she comes to the west, rising above high plural ces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तानीदहानि बहुलान्यासन्या प्राचीनमुदिता सूर्यस्य ।यतः परि जार इवाचरंत्युषो ददृक्षे न पुनर्यतीव ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ni ǀ ít ǀ áhāni ǀ bahulā́ni ǀ āsan ǀ yā́ ǀ prācī́nam ǀ út-itā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀyátaḥ ǀ pári ǀ jāráḥ-iva ǀ ā-cárantī ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ dadṛkṣé ǀ ná ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yatī́-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are the days that have dawned before the rising of the sun, on which you, Uṣas, have beenbeheld like a wife going to an inconstant husband, and not like one deserting him.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the days that have dawned before the rising of the sun, on which you, Uṣas, have beenbeheld like a wife going to an inconstant husband, and not like one deserting him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन्नृतावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः ।गूळ्हं ज्योतिः पितरो अन्वविंदन्त्सत्यमंत्रा अजनयन्नुषासं ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ít ǀ devā́nām ǀ sadha-mā́daḥ ǀ āsan ǀ ṛtá-vānaḥ ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ pūrvyā́saḥ ǀgūḷhám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ ánu ǀ avindan ǀ satyá-mantrāḥ ǀ ajanayan ǀ uṣásam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those ancient sages, our ancestors, observant of truth, rejoicing together with the gods, discovered thehidden ligh, and, reciters of sincere prayers, they genitive rated the Dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: Those ancient sages, our ancestors, observant of truth, rejoicing together with the gods, discovered thehidden ligh, and, reciters of sincere prayers, they genitive rated the Dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समान ऊर्वे अधि संगतासः सं जानते न यतंते मिथस्ते ।ते देवानां न मिनंति व्रतान्यमर्धंतो वसुभिर्यादमानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: samāné ǀ ūrvé ǀ ádhi ǀ sám-gatāsaḥ ǀ sám ǀ jānate ǀ ná ǀ yatante ǀ mitháḥ ǀ té ǀté ǀ devā́nām ǀ ná ǀ minanti ǀ vratā́ni ǀ ámardhantaḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ yā́damānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the common herd (of cattle had been stolen) then, associating, they concurred, nor mutuallycontended; they obstructed not the sacrifices of the gods, but, unoffending, proceeded with the light (they hadrecovered).
verses.wilson_translation: When the common herd (of cattle had been stolen) then, associating, they concurred, nor mutuallycontended; they obstructed not the sacrifices of the gods, but, unoffending, proceeded with the light (they hadrecovered).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति त्वा स्तोमैरीळते वसिष्ठा उषर्बुधः सुभगे तुष्टुवांसः ।गवां नेत्री वाजपत्नी न उच्छोषः सुजाते प्रथमा जरस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ tvā ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀ uṣaḥ-búdhaḥ ǀ su-bhage ǀ tustu-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀgávām ǀ netrī́ ǀ vā́ja-patnī ǀ naḥ ǀ uccha ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ su-jāte ǀ prathamā́ ǀ jarasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious Uṣas, the Vasiṣṭhas, waking at dawn; and praising you, glorify you, glorify you with hymns;Uṣas, who are the conductress of the cattle (to pasture), the bestower of food, dawn upon us; shine, well-born Uṣas, the first (of the gods).
verses.wilson_translation: Auspicious Uṣas, the Vasiṣṭhas, waking at dawn; and praising you, glorify you, glorify you with hymns;Uṣas, who are the conductress of the cattle (to pasture), the bestower of food, dawn upon us; shine, well-born Uṣas, the first (of the gods).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एषा नेत्री राधसः सूनृतानामुषा उच्छंती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः ।दीर्घश्रुतं रयिमस्मे दधाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ netrī́ ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ sūnṛ́tānām ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchántī ǀ ribhyate ǀ vásiṣṭhaiḥ ǀdīrgha-śrútam ǀ rayím ǀ asmé íti ǀ dádhānā ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uṣas, the object of the sincere praises of the worshipper, is glorified when dawning, by the Vasiṣṭhasbestowing upon us far-famed riches; do you (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas, the object of the sincere praises of the worshipper, is glorified when dawning, by the Vasiṣṭhasbestowing upon us far-famed riches; do you (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVIT. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SHE hath shone brightly like a youthful woman, stirring to motion every living creature.Agni hath come to feed on mortal? fuel. She hath made light and chased away the darkness. Turned to this All, far-spreading, she hath risen and shone in brightness with white robes about her.She hath beamed forth lovely with golden colours, Mother of kine, Guide of the days she bringeth. Bearing the Gods’ own Eye, auspicious Lady, leading her Courser white and fair to look on,Distinguished by her bean-is Dawn shines apparent, come forth to all the world with wondrous treasure. Draw nigh with wealth and dawn away the foeman: prepare for us wide pasture free from danger.Drive away those who hate us, bring us riches: pour bounty, opulent Lady, on the singer. Send thy most excellent beams to shine and light us, giving us lengthened days, O Dawn, O Goddess,Granting us food, thou who hast all things precious, and bounty rich in chariots, kine, and horses. O Uṣas, nobly-born, Daughter of Heaven, whom the Vasisthas with their hymns make mighty,Bestow thou on us vast and glorious riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: उपो रुरुचे युवतिर्न योषा विश्वं जीवं प्रसुवंती चरायै ।अभूदग्निः समिधे मानुषाणामकर्ज्योतिर्बाधमाना तमांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: úpo íti ǀ ruruce ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóṣā ǀ víśvam ǀ jīvám ǀ pra-suvántī ǀ carā́yai ǀábhūt ǀ agníḥ ǀ sam-ídhe ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǀ ákaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ bā́dhamānā ǀ támāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uṣas shines radiant in the proximity (of the sun), like a youthful wife (in the presence of her husband),animating all existence to activity;Agniis to be kindled for the good of men; the light disperses the obstructingdarkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas shines radiant in the proximity (of the sun), like a youthful wife (in the presence of her husband),animating all existence to activity;Agniis to be kindled for the good of men; the light disperses the obstructingdarkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वं प्रतीची सप्रथा उदस्थाद्रुशद्वासो बिभ्रती शुक्रमश्वैत् ।हिरण्यवर्णा सुदृशीकसंदृग्गवां माता नेत्र्यह्नामरोचि ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvam ǀ pratīcī́ ǀ sa-práthāḥ ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǀ rúśat ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ bíbhratī ǀ śukrám ǀ aśvait ǀhíraṇya-varṇā ǀ sudṛ́śīka-sandṛk ǀ gávām ǀ mātā́ ǀ netrī́ ǀ áhnām ǀ aroci ǁ
verses.english_translation: Advancing towards all, and spreading widely, the Dawn has risen; clothed in pure and brilliant vesture,she expands; of golden colour and of lovely radiance, she shines the parent of sounds, the leader of days.
verses.wilson_translation: Advancing towards all, and spreading widely, the Dawn has risen; clothed in pure and brilliant vesture,she expands; of golden colour and of lovely radiance, she shines the parent of sounds, the leader of days.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवानां चक्षुः सुभगा वहंती श्वेतं नयंती सुदृशीकमश्वं ।उषा अदर्शि रश्मिभिर्व्यक्ता चित्रामघा विश्वमनु प्रभूता ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ váhantī ǀ śvetám ǀ náyantī ǀ su-dṛ́śīkam ǀ áśvam ǀuṣā́ḥ ǀ adarśi ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ ví-aktā ǀ citrá-maghā ǀ víśvam ǀ ánu ǀ prá-bhūtā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The auspicious Uṣas, bearing the eye of the gods (the light), leading her white and beautiful courser(the sun), is belied, manifested by her rays, disributress of wonderful wealth, mighty over all.
verses.wilson_translation: The auspicious Uṣas, bearing the eye of the gods (the light), leading her white and beautiful courser(the sun), is belied, manifested by her rays, disributress of wonderful wealth, mighty over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अंतिवामा दूरे अमित्रमुच्छोर्वीं गव्यूतिमभयं कृधी नः ।यावय द्वेष आ भरा वसूनि चोदय राधो गृणते मघोनि ॥
verses.transliteration: ánti-vāmā ǀ dūré ǀ amítram ǀ uccha ǀ urvī́m ǀ gávyūtim ǀ ábhayam ǀ kṛdhi ǀ naḥ ǀyaváya ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ vásūni ǀ codáya ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ maghoni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dawn, Uṣas, who are the bearer to us of desirable (wealth), and keep our adversary from us; renderthe wide earth free from peril; drive away those who hate us; bring to us treasures; bestow, opulent goddesswealth upon him who praises you.
verses.wilson_translation: Dawn, Uṣas, who are the bearer to us of desirable (wealth), and keep our adversary from us; renderthe wide earth free from peril; drive away those who hate us; bring to us treasures; bestow, opulent goddesswealth upon him who praises you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे श्रेष्ठेभिर्भानुभिर्वि भाह्युषो देवि प्रतिरंती न आयुः ।इषं च नो दधती विश्ववारे गोमदश्वावद्रथवच्च राधः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ śréṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ bhānú-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ bhāhi ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ devi ǀ pra-tirántī ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀíṣam ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ dádhatī ǀ viśva-vāre ǀ gó-mat ǀ áśva-vat ǀ rátha-vat ǀ ca ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Uṣas, illumine us with your brightest rays, prolonging our existence, bestowing upon us food,(and granting us), you who are adored by all, affluence, comprising cattle, horses, and chariots.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Uṣas, illumine us with your brightest rays, prolonging our existence, bestowing upon us food,(and granting us), you who are adored by all, affluence, comprising cattle, horses, and chariots.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यां त्वा दिवो दुहितर्वर्धयंत्युषः सुजाते मतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः ।सास्मासु धा रयिमृष्वं बृहंतं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́n ǀ tvā ǀ divaḥ ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ vardháyanti ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ su-jāte ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀsā́ ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhāḥ ǀ rayím ǀ ṛṣvám ǀ bṛhántam ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well-manifested Uṣas, daughter of heaven, do you, whom the Vasiṣṭhasmagnify with praises, bestowupon us brillian and infinite wealth; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Well-manifested Uṣas, daughter of heaven, do you, whom the Vasiṣṭhasmagnify with praises, bestowupon us brillian and infinite wealth; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVIII. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WE have beheld her earliest lights approaching: her many glories part, on high, asunder.On car sublime, refulgent, wending hither, O Uṣas, bring the Wealth that makes us happy. The fire well-kindIed sings aloud to greet her, and with their hymns the priests are chaming welcome.Uṣas approaches in her splendour, driving all evil darkness far away, the Goddess. Apparent eastward are those lights of Morning, sending out lustre, as they rise, around them.She hath brought forth Sun, sacrifice, and Agni, and far away hath fled detested darkness. Rich Daughter of the Sky, we all behold her, yea, all men look on Dawn as she is breaking.fler car that moves self-harnessed hath she mounted, the car drawn onward by her well-yoked horses. Inspired with loving thoughts this day to greet thee, we and our wealthy nobles have awakened.Show yourselves fruitful, Dawns, as ye are rising. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्रति केतवः प्रथमा अदृश्रन्नूर्ध्वा अस्या अंजयो वि श्रयंते ।उषो अर्वाचा बृहता रथेन ज्योतिष्मता वाममस्मभ्यं वक्षि ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ adṛśran ǀ ūrdhvā́ḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ añjáyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ śrayante ǀúṣaḥ ǀ arvā́cā ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ jyótiṣmatā ǀ vāmám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ vakṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The first signs of the Dawn are visible, her rays are spreading not high; you bring us, Uṣas, desirable(riches) in your vast, descending and resplendent chariot.
verses.wilson_translation: The first signs of the Dawn are visible, her rays are spreading not high; you bring us, Uṣas, desirable(riches) in your vast, descending and resplendent chariot.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति षीमग्निर्जरते समिद्धः प्रति विप्रासो मतिभिर्गृणंतः ।उषा याति ज्योतिषा बाधमाना विश्वा तमांसि दुरिताप देवी ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ sīm ǀ agníḥ ǀ jarate ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ práti ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀuṣā́ḥ ǀ yāti ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ bā́dhamānā ǀ víśvā ǀ támāṃsi ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ ápa ǀ devī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The kindled fire increases everywhere, (and) the priests, glorifying (the dawn) with hymns; the divine Uṣas comes, driving away all the evil glooms by her lustre.
verses.wilson_translation: The kindled fire increases everywhere, (and) the priests, glorifying (the dawn) with hymns; the divine Uṣas comes, driving away all the evil glooms by her lustre.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एता उ त्याः प्रत्यदृश्रन्पुरस्ताज्ज्योतिर्यच्छंतीरुषसो विभातीः ।अजीजनन्त्सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निमपाचीनं तमो अगादजुष्टं ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyā́ḥ ǀ práti ǀ adṛśran ǀ purástāt ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ yácchantīḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀájījanan ǀ sū́ryam ǀ yajñám ǀ agním ǀ apācī́nam ǀ támaḥ ǀ agāt ǀ ájuṣṭam ǁ
verses.english_translation: These luminous (beams of the) dawn are beheld in the east diffusing light; (the dawn) enger sacrifice,fire; the odious glooms, descending, disappear.
verses.wilson_translation: These luminous (beams of the) dawn are beheld in the east diffusing light; (the dawn) enger sacrifice,fire; the odious glooms, descending, disappear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अचेति दिवो दुहिता मघोनी विश्वे पश्यंत्युषसं विभातीं ।आस्थाद्रथं स्वधया युज्यमानमा यमश्वासः सुयुजो वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: áceti ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ maghónī ǀ víśve ǀ paśyanti ǀ uṣásam ǀ vi-bhātī́m ǀā́ ǀ asthāt ǀ rátham ǀ svadháyā ǀ yujyámānam ǀ ā́ ǀ yám ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ su-yújaḥ ǀ váhanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The affluent daughter of heaven is perceived; all creatures behold the luminous dawn; she ascends herchariot laden with sustenance, which her easily- yoked horses draw.
verses.wilson_translation: The affluent daughter of heaven is perceived; all creatures behold the luminous dawn; she ascends herchariot laden with sustenance, which her easily- yoked horses draw.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति त्वाद्य सुमनसो बुधंतास्माकासो मघवानो वयं च ।तिल्विलायध्वमुषसो विभातीर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ tvā ǀ adyá ǀ su-mánasaḥ ǀ budhanta ǀ asmā́kāsaḥ ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ ca ǀtilvilāyádhvam ǀ uṣasaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent (in sacrificial offerings), actuated by one mind, we and ours awaken you, (Uṣas), today;luminous dawns, soften (the earth) with unctuous (dews) and do you, (gods) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent (in sacrificial offerings), actuated by one mind, we and ours awaken you, (Uṣas), today;luminous dawns, soften (the earth) with unctuous (dews) and do you, (gods) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIX. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ROUSING the lands where men's Five Tribes are settled, Dawn hath disclosed the pathways of the people.She hath sent out her sheen with beauteous oxen. The Sun with light hath opened earth and heaven. They paint their bright rays on the sky's far limits. the Dawns come on like tribes arrayed for battle.Thy cattle, closely shutting up the darkness, as Savitar spreads his arms, give forth their lustre. Wealthy, most like to Indra, Dawn hath risen, and brought forth lauds that shall promote our welfare.Daughter of Heaven, a Goddess, she distributes, best of Aṅgirases, treasures to the pious. Bestow on us, O Dawn, that ample bounty which thou didst send to those who sang thy praises;Thou whom with bellowings of a bull they quickened: thou didst unbar the firm-set mountain's portals. Impelling every God to grant his bounty sending to us the charm of pleasant voices,Vouchsafe us thoughts, for profit, as thou breakest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: व्युषा आवः पथ्या जनानां पंच क्षितीर्मानुषीर्बोधयंती ।सुसंदृग्भिरुक्षभिर्भानुमश्रेद्वि सूर्यो रोदसी चक्षसावः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ āvaḥ ǀ pathyā́ ǀ jánānām ǀ páñca ǀ kṣitī́ḥ ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ bodháyantī ǀsusandṛ́k-bhiḥ ǀ ukṣá-bhiḥ ǀ bhānúm ǀ aśret ǀ ví ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ cákṣasā ǀ āvarítyāvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uṣas has dawned upon the paths of men, awaking the five classes of human beings; she has shedlight with her lustrous oxen; the sun makes heaven and earth manifest with radiance.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas has dawned upon the paths of men, awaking the five classes of human beings; she has shedlight with her lustrous oxen; the sun makes heaven and earth manifest with radiance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: व्यंजते दिवो अंतेष्वक्तून्विशो न युक्ता उषसो यतंते ।सं ते गावस्तम आ वर्तयंति ज्योतिर्यच्छंति सवितेव बाहू ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ añjate ǀ diváḥ ǀ ánteṣu ǀ aktū́n ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ yatante ǀsám ǀ te ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayanti ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ yacchanti ǀ savitā́-iva ǀ bāhū́ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The dawns send their rays to the ends of the sky. They advance like people arrayed like people (inmartial order); your rays, Uṣas, annihilate the darkness; they diffuse light as Savitā(spreads out) his arms.
verses.wilson_translation: The dawns send their rays to the ends of the sky. They advance like people arrayed like people (inmartial order); your rays, Uṣas, annihilate the darkness; they diffuse light as Savitā(spreads out) his arms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभूदुषा इंद्रतमा मघोन्यजीजनत्सुविताय श्रवांसि ।वि दिवो देवी दुहिता दधात्यंगिरस्तमा सुकृते वसूनि ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūt ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ índra-tamā ǀ maghónī ǀ ájījanat ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀví ǀ diváḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ dadhāti ǀ áṅgiraḥ-tamā ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ vásūni ǁ
verses.english_translation: The supreme sovereign, the opulent uṣas, has risen; she has engendered food for our welfare; thedivine daughter of heaven, most prompt in movement, bestows treasures upon the pious worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: The supreme sovereign, the opulent uṣas, has risen; she has engendered food for our welfare; thedivine daughter of heaven, most prompt in movement, bestows treasures upon the pious worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तावदुषो राधो अस्मभ्यं रास्व यावत्स्तोतृभ्यो अरदो गृणाना ।यां त्वा जज्ञुर्वृषभस्या रवेण वि दृळ्हस्य दुरो अद्रेरौर्णोः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́vat ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ rāsva ǀ yā́vat ǀ stotṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ áradaḥ ǀ gṛṇānā́ ǀyā́m ǀ tvā ǀ jajñúḥ ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ ráveṇa ǀ ví ǀ dṛḷhásya ǀ dúraḥ ǀ ádreḥ ǀ aurṇoḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant us as much wealth as you have bestowed upon thine adorers when (formerly) praised by them;you whom (your worshippers) welcomed with clamour, (loud as the bellowing) of a bull, when you had set openthe doors of the mountains (where the stolen cattle were confined).
verses.wilson_translation: Grant us as much wealth as you have bestowed upon thine adorers when (formerly) praised by them;you whom (your worshippers) welcomed with clamour, (loud as the bellowing) of a bull, when you had set openthe doors of the mountains (where the stolen cattle were confined).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवंदेवं राधसे चोदयंत्यस्मद्र्यक्सूनृता ईरयंती ।व्युच्छंती नः सनये धियो धा यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: devám-devam ǀ rā́dhase ǀ codáyantī ǀ asmadryák ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ īráyantī ǀvi-ucchántī ǀ naḥ ǀ sanáye ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inspiring every individual devout (worshipper) with a desire for wealth, addressing to us the words oftruth, diffusing the light of morning, bestow upon us understanding (fit) for the acquisition of riches; and do you,(gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Inspiring every individual devout (worshipper) with a desire for wealth, addressing to us the words oftruth, diffusing the light of morning, bestow upon us understanding (fit) for the acquisition of riches; and do you,(gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXX. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: THE priests, Vasisthas, are the first awakened to welcome Uṣas with their songs and praises,Who makes surrounding regions part asunder,and shows apparent all existing creatures. Giving fresh life when she hath hid the darkness, this Dawn hath wakened there with new-born lustre.Youthful and unrestrained she cometh forward: she hath turned thoughts to Sun and fire and worship. May blessed Mornings shine on us for ever, with wealth of kine, of horses, and of heroes,Streaming with all abundance, pouring fatness. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्रति स्तोमेभिरुषसं वसिष्ठा गीर्भिर्विप्रासः प्रथमा अबुध्रन् ।विवर्तयंतीं रजसी समंते आविष्कृण्वतीं भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ uṣásam ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ abudhran ǀvi-vartáyantīm ǀ rájasī íti ǀ sámante íti sám-ante ǀ āviḥ-kṛṇvatī́m ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The pious Vasiṣṭhas, first (of all worshippers) awaken with prayers and praises (each succeeding)dawn spreading over the like-bounded earth and heaven making all the regions manifest.
verses.wilson_translation: The pious Vasiṣṭhas, first (of all worshippers) awaken with prayers and praises (each succeeding)dawn spreading over the like-bounded earth and heaven making all the regions manifest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एषा स्या नव्यमायुर्दधाना गूढ्वी तमो ज्योतिषोषा अबोधि ।अग्र एति युवतिरह्रयाणा प्राचिकितत्सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निं ॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā́ ǀ syā́ ǀ návyam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ dádhānā ǀ gūḍhvī́ ǀ támaḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ abodhi ǀágre ǀ eti ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ áhrayāṇā ǀ prá ǀ acikitat ǀ sū́ryam ǀ yajñám ǀ agním ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestowing new existence, dispersing the thick darkness by her radiance, the Dawn is awakened andlike an immodest dame, she comes before (the sun), and makes manifest Sūrya, sacrifice and Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestowing new existence, dispersing the thick darkness by her radiance, the Dawn is awakened andlike an immodest dame, she comes before (the sun), and makes manifest Sūrya, sacrifice and Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्न उषासो वीरवतीः सदमुच्छंतु भद्राः ।घृतं दुहाना विश्वतः प्रपीता यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśva-vatīḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vīrá-vatīḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ucchantu ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀghṛtám ǀ dúhānāḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ prá-pītāḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the auspicious dawns ever break upon us redolen of horses, of cattle, ofmaleposterity, sheddingmoisture, yielding everywhere abundance; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May the auspicious dawns ever break upon us redolen of horses, of cattle, ofmaleposterity, sheddingmoisture, yielding everywhere abundance; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXI. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ADVANCING, sending forth her rays, the Daughter of the Sky is seen.Uncovering, that we may see, the mighty gloom, the friendly Lady makes the light. The Sun ascending, the refulgent Star, pours down his beams together with the Dawn.O Dawn, at thine arising, and the Sun's, may we attain the share allotted us. Promptly we woke to welcome thee, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,Thee, Bounteous One, who bringest all we long to have, and to the offerer health and wealth. Thou, dawning, workest fain to light the great world, yea, heaven, Goddess! that it may be seen.We yearn to be thine own, Dealer of Wealth: may we be to this Mother like her sons. Bring us that wondrous bounty, Dawn, that shall be famed most far away.What, Child of Heaven, thou hast of nourishment for man, bestow thou on us to enjoy. Give to our princes opulence and immortal fame, and strength in herds of kine to us.May she who prompts the wealthy, Lady of sweet strains, may Uṣas dawn our foes away.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यु अदर्श्यायत्युच्छंती दुहिता दिवः ।अपो महि व्ययति चक्षसे तमो ज्योतिष्कृणोति सूनरी ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ adarśi ǀ ā-yatī́ ǀ ucchántī ǀ duhitā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀápo íti ǀ máhi ǀ vyayati ǀ cákṣase ǀ támaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ sūnárī ǁ
verses.english_translation: The daughter of heaven is everywhere beheld advancing and shedding light; she drives away the deepdarkness that objects may meet the eye; the kind guide of man, she diffuses light.
verses.wilson_translation: The daughter of heaven is everywhere beheld advancing and shedding light; she drives away the deepdarkness that objects may meet the eye; the kind guide of man, she diffuses light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदुस्रियाः सृजते सूर्यः सचाँ उद्यन्नक्षत्रमर्चिवत् ।तवेदुषो व्युषि सूर्यस्य च सं भक्तेन गमेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ sṛjate ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ sácā ǀ ut-yát ǀ nákṣatram ǀ arci-vát ǀtáva ǀ ít ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ vi-úṣi ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ ca ǀ sám ǀ bhakténa ǀ gamemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: At the same time the sun sends forth his rays, and, rising, renders the plural nets luminous; so, Uṣas,upon your manifestation, and that of Sūrya, may we become possessed of sustenance.
verses.wilson_translation: At the same time the sun sends forth his rays, and, rising, renders the plural nets luminous; so, Uṣas,upon your manifestation, and that of Sūrya, may we become possessed of sustenance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति त्वा दुहितर्दिव उषो जीरा अभुत्स्महि ।या वहसि पुरु स्पार्हं वनन्वति रत्नं न दाशुषे मयः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ tvā ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ jīrā́ḥ ǀ abhutsmahi ǀyā́ ǀ váhasi ǀ purú ǀ spārhám ǀ vanan-vati ǀ rátnam ǀ ná ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ máyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, prompt adorers, awaken you, Uṣas, daughter of heaven, bountiful divinity, who bring ampleand desirable (wealth) and happiness, like riches, to the donor (of the oblation).
verses.wilson_translation: May we, prompt adorers, awaken you, Uṣas, daughter of heaven, bountiful divinity, who bring ampleand desirable (wealth) and happiness, like riches, to the donor (of the oblation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छंती या कृणोषि मंहना महि प्रख्यै देवि स्वर्दृशे ।तस्यास्ते रत्नभाज ईमहे वयं स्याम मातुर्न सूनवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ucchántī ǀ yā́ ǀ kṛṇóṣi ǀ maṃhánā ǀ mahi ǀ pra-khyái ǀ devi ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛśé ǀtásyāḥ ǀ te ǀ ratna-bhā́jaḥ ǀ īmahe ǀ vayám ǀ syā́ma ǀ mātúḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūnávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty goddess, who, scattering darkness, are endowed with power to arouse the world and make itvisible, we pray that we may be dear to you, the distributress of wealth, as sons are to a mother.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty goddess, who, scattering darkness, are endowed with power to arouse the world and make itvisible, we pray that we may be dear to you, the distributress of wealth, as sons are to a mother.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तच्चित्रं राध आ भरोषो यद्दीर्घश्रुत्तमं ।यत्ते दिवो दुहितर्मर्तभोजनं तद्रास्व भुनजामहै ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ citrám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ yát ǀ dīrghaśrút-tamam ǀyát ǀ te ǀ divaḥ ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ marta-bhójanam ǀ tát ǀ rāsva ǀ bhunájāmahai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring Uṣas, such wondrous wealth as may be long renowned; bestow, daughter of heaven, thatsustenance which is fit for mortals, such as we may enjoy.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring Uṣas, such wondrous wealth as may be long renowned; bestow, daughter of heaven, thatsustenance which is fit for mortals, such as we may enjoy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: श्रवः सूरिभ्यो अमृतं वसुत्वनं वाजाँ अस्मभ्यं गोमतः ।चोदयित्री मघोनः सूनृतावत्युषा उच्छदप स्रिधः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrávaḥ ǀ sūrí-bhyaḥ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ vasu-tvanám ǀ vā́jān ǀ asmábhyam ǀ gó-mataḥ ǀcodayitrī́ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ sūnṛ́tā-vatī ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchat ǀ ápa ǀ srídhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant to the pious immortal fame, conjoined with affluence; grant to us food and cattle; and may Uṣas,the encourager of the wealthy (sacrificer) the speaker of truth, drive away our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant to the pious immortal fame, conjoined with affluence; grant to us food and cattle; and may Uṣas,the encourager of the wealthy (sacrificer) the speaker of truth, drive away our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIT. Indra-Varuṇa
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GRANT us your strong protection, IndraVaruṇa, our people, and our family, for sacrifice.May we subdue in fight our evil-hearted foes, him who attacks the man steadfast in lengthened rites. O Indra-Varuṇa, mighty and very rich One of you is called Monarch and One Autocrat.All Gods in the most lofty region of the air have, O ye Steers, combined all power and might in you. Ye with your strength have pierced the fountains of the floods: the Sun have ye brought forward as the Lord in heaven.Cheered by this magic draught ye, Indra-Varuṇa, made the dry places stream, made songs of praise flow forth. In battels and in frays we ministering priests, kneeling upon our knees for furtherance of our weal,Invoke you, only you, the Lords of twofold wealth, you prompt to hear, we bards, O Indra-Varuṇa. O Indra-Varuṇa, as ye created all these creatures of the world by your surpassing might,In peace and quiet Mitra waits on Varuṇa, the Other, awful, with the Maruis seeks renown. That Varuṇa's high worth may shine preeminent, these Twain have measured each his proper power and might.The One subdueth the destructive enemy; the Other with a few furthereth many a man. No trouble, no misfortune, Indra-Varuṇa, no woe from any side assails the mortal manWhose sacrifice, O Gods, ye visit and enjoy: ne’er doth the crafty guile of mortal injure him. With your divine protection, Heroes, come to us: mine invncation hear, if ye be pleased therewith.Bestow ye upon us, O Indra-Varuṇa, your friendship and your kinship and your favouring grace. In battle after battle, Indra-Varuṇa, be ye our Champions, ye who are the peoples' strength,When both opposing bands invoke you for the fight, and men that they may gain offspring and progeny. May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman vouchsafe us glory and great shelter spreading far.We think of the beneficent light of Aditi, and Savitar's song of praise, the God who strengthens Law.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतं ।दीर्घप्रयज्युमति यो वनुष्यति वयं जयेम पृतनासु दूढ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇā ǀ yuvám ǀ adhvarā́ya ǀ naḥ ǀ viśé ǀ jánāya ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatam ǀdīrghá-prayajyum ǀ áti ǀ yáḥ ǀ vanuṣyáti ǀ vayám ǀ jayema ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ duḥ-dhyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, bestow upon this man, our employer, a spacious chamber for (the celebration of) thesacrifice; and may we subdue in conflicts such evil-minded person ns as may seek to injure him who has been longengaged (in your adoration).
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, bestow upon this man, our employer, a spacious chamber for (the celebration of) thesacrifice; and may we subdue in conflicts such evil-minded person ns as may seek to injure him who has been longengaged (in your adoration).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सम्राळन्यः स्वराळन्य उच्यते वां महांताविंद्रावरुणा महावसू ।विश्वे देवासः परमे व्योमनि सं वामोजो वृषणा सं बलं दधुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-rā́ṭ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ sva-rā́ṭ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ucyate ǀ vām ǀ mahā́ntau ǀ índrāváruṇā ǀ mahā́vasū íti mahā́-vasū ǀvíśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ paramé ǀ ví-omani ǀ sám ǀ vām ǀ ójaḥ ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ sám ǀ bálam ǀ dadhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of you it titled supreme monarch, so is the other; mighty and most opulent are you,Indraand all thegods in the highest heaven, showerers (of benefits), have combined your united strength, (your) maid vigouṛ
verses.wilson_translation: One of you it titled supreme monarch, so is the other; mighty and most opulent are you,Indraand all thegods in the highest heaven, showerers (of benefits), have combined your united strength, (your) maid vigouṛ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अन्वपां खान्यतृंतमोजसा सूर्यमैरयतं दिवि प्रभुं ।इंद्रावरुणा मदे अस्य मायिनोऽपिन्वतमपितः पिन्वतं धियः ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ apā́m ǀ khā́ni ǀ atṛntam ǀ ójasā ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ airayatam ǀ diví ǀ pra-bhúm ǀíndrāvaruṇā ǀ máde ǀ asya ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ ápinvatam ǀ apítaḥ ǀ pínvatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, you have forced open by your strength the barriers of the waters; you haveestablished Sūryaas the lord in heaven; in the exhilaration of the inspiring (Soma) you have replenished the dry(beds of the rivers); do you also fulfil the objects of our sacred rite.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, you have forced open by your strength the barriers of the waters; you haveestablished Sūryaas the lord in heaven; in the exhilaration of the inspiring (Soma) you have replenished the dry(beds of the rivers); do you also fulfil the objects of our sacred rite.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवामिद्युत्सु पृतनासु वह्नयो युवां क्षेमस्य प्रसवे मितज्ञवः ।ईशाना वस्व उभयस्य कारव इंद्रावरुणा सुहवा हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ yut-sú ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀ yuvā́m ǀ kṣémasya ǀ pra-savé ǀ mitá-jñavaḥ ǀīśānā́ ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ ubháyasya ǀ kārávaḥ ǀ índrāvaruṇā ǀ su-hávā ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bearers (of offerings) invoke you,Indraand Varuṇa, in wars, in battles; on banded knees (the Aṅgirasas invoke you) for the begetting of prosperity; and we, your worshippers, invoke you, who are entitled torespectful homage, the lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: The bearers (of offerings) invoke you,Indraand Varuṇa, in wars, in battles; on banded knees (the Aṅgirasas invoke you) for the begetting of prosperity; and we, your worshippers, invoke you, who are entitled torespectful homage, the lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणा यदिमानि चक्रथुर्विश्वा जातानि भुवनस्य मज्मना ।क्षेमेण मित्रो वरुणं दुवस्यति मरुद्भिरुग्रः शुभमन्य ईयते ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇā ǀ yát ǀ imā́ni ǀ cakráthuḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ jātā́ni ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ majmánā ǀkṣémeṇa ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇam ǀ duvasyáti ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ śúbham ǀ anyáḥ ǀ īyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, inasmuch as you have created by your might all these beings of the world, therefore Mitra worships Varuṇa for prosperity, while the other, the fierce Indra, associated with the Maruts, acquiresglory.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, inasmuch as you have created by your might all these beings of the world, therefore Mitra worships Varuṇa for prosperity, while the other, the fierce Indra, associated with the Maruts, acquiresglory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: महे शुल्काय वरुणस्य नु त्विष ओजो मिमाते ध्रुवमस्य यत्स्वं ।अजामिमन्यः श्नथयंतमातिरद्दभ्रेभिरन्यः प्र वृणोति भूयसः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahé ǀ śulkā́ya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ nú ǀ tviṣé ǀ ójaḥ ǀ mimāte íti ǀ dhruvám ǀ asya ǀ yát ǀ svám ǀájāmim ǀ anyáḥ ǀ śnatháyantam ǀ ā́ ǀ átirat ǀ dabhrébhiḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ prá ǀ vṛṇoti ǀ bhū́yasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In honour of (Indraand Varuṇa) the sacrificer and his wife for (the obtaining of) great wealth, confer (bytheir praises) that strength which is peculiar to each of them, and ever-enduring; one of them, (Varuṇa), destroysthe unfriendly man neglecting (his worship); the other, (Indra), with scanty (means), discomfits numerous(enemies).
verses.wilson_translation: In honour of (Indraand Varuṇa) the sacrificer and his wife for (the obtaining of) great wealth, confer (bytheir praises) that strength which is peculiar to each of them, and ever-enduring; one of them, (Varuṇa), destroysthe unfriendly man neglecting (his worship); the other, (Indra), with scanty (means), discomfits numerous(enemies).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न तमंहो न दुरितानि मर्त्यमिंद्रावरुणा न तपः कुतश्चन ।यस्य देवा गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरं न तं मर्तस्य नशते परिह्वृतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-itā́ni ǀ mártyam ǀ índrāvaruṇā ǀ ná ǀ tápaḥ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ caná ǀyásya ǀ devā ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ vītháḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ ná ǀ tám ǀ mártasya ǀ naśate ǀ pári-hvṛtiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sin contaminates not, difficulties assail not, nor distress at any time afflicts the mortal,Indraand Varuṇa, to whose sacrifices you, deities, go, and of which you approve; such a man ruin never destroyṣ
verses.wilson_translation: Sin contaminates not, difficulties assail not, nor distress at any time afflicts the mortal,Indraand Varuṇa, to whose sacrifices you, deities, go, and of which you approve; such a man ruin never destroyṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वाङ्नरा दैव्येनावसा गतं शृणुतं हवं यदि मे जुजोषथः ।युवोर्हि सख्यमुत वा यदाप्यं मार्डीकमिंद्रावरुणा नि यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́k ǀ narā ǀ dáivyena ǀ ávasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ śṛṇutám ǀ hávam ǀ yádi ǀ me ǀ jújoṣathaḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ hí ǀ sakhyám ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ ā́pyam ǀ mārḍīkám ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ní ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leaders of rites, come to our presence with divine protection; if you have any regard for me, hear myinvocation; verily your friendship, your affinity, is the source of happiness; grant them,Indraand Varuṇa(untous).
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders of rites, come to our presence with divine protection; if you have any regard for me, hear myinvocation; verily your friendship, your affinity, is the source of happiness; grant them,Indraand Varuṇa(untous).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमिंद्रावरुणा भरेभरे पुरोयोधा भवतं कृष्ट्योजसा ।यद्वां हवंत उभये अध स्पृधि नरस्तोकस्य तनयस्य सातिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ bháre-bhare ǀ puraḥ-yodhā́ ǀ bhavatam ǀ kṛṣṭi-ojasā ǀyát ǀ vām ǀ hávante ǀ ubháye ǀ ádha ǀ spṛdhí ǀ náraḥ ǀ tokásya ǀ tánayasya ǀ sātíṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, of irresistible strength, be our preceders in every encounter, for both (past andpresent) worshippers invoke you to defend them iin war, or for the acquisition of sons and grandsons.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, of irresistible strength, be our preceders in every encounter, for both (past andpresent) worshippers invoke you to defend them iin war, or for the acquisition of sons and grandsons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे इंद्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा द्युम्नं यच्छंतु महि शर्म सप्रथः ।अवध्रं ज्योतिरदितेर्ऋतावृधो देवस्य श्लोकं सवितुर्मनामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ dyumnám ǀ yacchantu ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀavadhrám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ devásya ǀ ślókam ǀ savitúḥ ǀ manāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra,Varuṇa,Mitraand Aryamangrant us wealth and a large and spacious habitation; may thelustre of Aditi, the augmentress of sacrifice, be innoxious to us; we recite the praise of the divine Savitā.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra,Varuṇa,Mitraand Aryamangrant us wealth and a large and spacious habitation; may thelustre of Aditi, the augmentress of sacrifice, be innoxious to us; we recite the praise of the divine Savitā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIII. Indra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LOOKING to you and your alliance, O ye Men, armed with broad axes they went forward, fain for spoil.Ye smote and slew his Dāsa and his Āryan enemies, and helped Sudās with favour, Indra-Varuṇa. Where heroes come together with their banners raised, in the encounter where is naught for us to love,Where all things that behold the light are terrified, there did ye comfort us, O Indra-Varuṇa. The boundaries of earth were seen all dark with dust: O Indra-Varuṇa, the shout went up to heaven.The enmities of the people compassed me about. Ye heard my calling and ye came to me with help. With your resistless weapons, Indra-Varuṇa, ye conquered Bheda and ye gave Sudās your aid.Ye heard the prayers of these amid the cries of war: effectual was the service of the Trtsus' priest. O Indra-Varuṇa, the wickedness of foes and mine assailants' hatred sorely trouble me.Ye Twain are Lords of riches both of earth and heaven: so grant to us your aid on the decisive day. The men of both the hosts invoked you in the fight, Indra and Varuṇa, that they might win the wealth,What time ye helped Sudās, with all the Trtsu folk, when the Ten Kings had pressed him down in their attack. Ten Kings who worshipped not, O Indra-Varuṇa, confederate, in war prevailed not o’er Sudās.True was the boast of heroes sitting at the feast: so at their invocations Gods were on their side. O Indra-Varuṇa, ye gave Sudās your aid when the Ten Kings in battle compassed him about,There where the white-robed Trtsus with their braided hair, skilled in song worshipped you with homage and with hymn. One of you Twain destroys the Vṛtras in the fight, the Other evermore maintains his holy Laws.We call on you, ye Mighty, with our hymns of praise. Vouchsafe us your protection, Indra-Varuṇa. May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman vouchsafe us glory and great shelter spreading far.We think of the beneficent light of Aditi, and Savitar's song of praise, the God who strengthens Law.

verses.sanskrit: युवां नरा पश्यमानास आप्यं प्राचा गव्यंतः पृथुपर्शवो ययुः ।दासा च वृत्रा हतमार्याणि च सुदासमिंद्रावरुणावसावतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ narā ǀ páśyamānāsaḥ ǀ ā́pyam ǀ prācā́ ǀ gavyántaḥ ǀ pṛthu-párśavaḥ ǀ yayuḥ ǀdā́sā ǀ ca ǀ vṛtrā́ ǀ hatám ǀ ā́ryāṇi ǀ ca ǀ su-dā́sam ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ávasā ǀ avatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, leaders (of rites), contemplating your affinity, and desirous of cattle, the worshippers,armed with large sickles, have proceeded to the east (to cut the sacred grass); destroy, Indra and Varuṇa, yourenemies, whether Dāsās orĀryāsand defend Sudāsawith yor protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, leaders (of rites), contemplating your affinity, and desirous of cattle, the worshippers,armed with large sickles, have proceeded to the east (to cut the sacred grass); destroy, Indra and Varuṇa, yourenemies, whether Dāsās orĀryāsand defend Sudāsawith yor protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्रा नरः समयंते कृतध्वजो यस्मिन्नाजा भवति किं चन प्रियं ।यत्रा भयंते भुवना स्वर्दृशस्तत्रा न इंद्रावरुणाधि वोचतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ náraḥ ǀ sam-áyante ǀ kṛtá-dhvajaḥ ǀ yásmin ǀ ājā́ ǀ bhávati ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ priyám ǀyátra ǀ bháyante ǀ bhúvanā ǀ svaḥ-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ tátra ǀ naḥ ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ádhi ǀ vocatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where men assemble with uplifted banners, in whatever conflict, there is something unfavourable;where living beings, looking to heaven, are in fear, there,Indraand Varuṇa, speak tous (encouragement).
verses.wilson_translation: Where men assemble with uplifted banners, in whatever conflict, there is something unfavourable;where living beings, looking to heaven, are in fear, there,Indraand Varuṇa, speak tous (encouragement).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सं भूम्या अंता ध्वसिरा अदृक्षतेंद्रावरुणा दिवि घोष आ��ुहत् ।अस्थुर्जनानामुप मामरातयोऽर्वागवसा हवनश्रुता गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ bhū́myāḥ ǀ ántāḥ ǀ dhvasirā́ḥ ǀ adṛkṣata ǀ índrāvaruṇā ǀ diví ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aruhat ǀásthuḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ úpa ǀ mā́m ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ ávasā ǀ havana-śrutā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ends of the earth are beheld laid waste; the clamour has ascended,Indraand Varuṇa, to heaven;the adversaries of my people approach me; having heard my invocation, come for my defence.
verses.wilson_translation: The ends of the earth are beheld laid waste; the clamour has ascended,Indraand Varuṇa, to heaven;the adversaries of my people approach me; having heard my invocation, come for my defence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणा वधनाभिरप्रति भेदं वन्वंता प्र सुदासमावतं ।ब्रह्माण्येषां शृणुतं हवीमनि सत्या तृत्सूनामभवत्पुरोहितिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇā ǀ vadhánābhiḥ ǀ apratí ǀ bhedám ǀ vanvántā ǀ prá ǀ su-dā́sam ǀ āvatam ǀbráhmāṇi ǀ eṣām ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ hávīmani ǀ satyā́ ǀ tṛ́tsūnām ǀ abhavat ǀ puráḥ-hitiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, you protected Sudāsa, overwhelming the yet unassailed Bhedawith your fatalweapons; here the prayers of threse Tṛtsus in time of battle, so that my ministration may have borne them fruit.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, you protected Sudāsa, overwhelming the yet unassailed Bhedawith your fatalweapons; here the prayers of threse Tṛtsus in time of battle, so that my ministration may have borne them fruit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणावभ्या तपंति माघान्यर्यो वनुषामरातयः ।युवं हि वस्व उभयस्य राजथोऽध स्मा नोऽवतं पार्ये दिवि ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇau ǀ abhí ǀ ā́ ǀ tapanti ǀ mā ǀ aghā́ni ǀ aryáḥ ǀ vanúṣām ǀ árātayaḥ ǀyuvám ǀ hí ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ ubháyasya ǀ rā́jathaḥ ǀ ádha ǀ sma ǀ naḥ ǀ avatam ǀ pā́rye ǀ diví ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, the murderous (weapons) of my enemy distressme; foes among the malignant(assail me); you two are sovereigns over both (celestial and terrestrial) wealth; protect us therefore, onthe day ofbattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraand Varuṇa, the murderous (weapons) of my enemy distressme; foes among the malignant(assail me); you two are sovereigns over both (celestial and terrestrial) wealth; protect us therefore, onthe day ofbattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवां हवंत उभयास आजिष्विंद्रं च वस्वो वरुणं च सातये ।यत्र राजभिर्दशभिर्निबाधितं प्र सुदासमावतं तृत्सुभिः सह ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ havante ǀ ubháyāsaḥ ǀ ājíṣu ǀ índram ǀ ca ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ váruṇam ǀ ca ǀ sātáye ǀyátra ǀ rā́ja-bhiḥ ǀ daśá-bhiḥ ǀ ní-bādhitam ǀ prá ǀ su-dā́sam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ tṛ́tsu-bhiḥ ǀ sahá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Both (Sudāsaand the Tṛtsus) call upon you two (Indraand Varuṇa), in combats for the acquisition ofwealth, when you defend Sudāsa, together with Tṛtsus, when attacked bythe tenrājās.
verses.wilson_translation: Both (Sudāsaand the Tṛtsus) call upon you two (Indraand Varuṇa), in combats for the acquisition ofwealth, when you defend Sudāsa, together with Tṛtsus, when attacked bythe tenrājās.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दश राजानः समिता अयज्यवः सुदासमिंद्रावरुणा न युयुधुः ।सत्या नृणामद्मसदामुपस्तुतिर्देवा एषामभवंदेवहूतिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ sám-itāḥ ǀ áyajyavaḥ ǀ su-dā́sam ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ná ǀ yuyudhuḥ ǀsatyā́ ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀ adma-sádām ǀ úpa-stutiḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ abhavan ǀ devá-hūtiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ten confederated irreligiousrājāsdid not prevail,Indraand Varuṇa, against Sudāsa; the praiseof the leaders (of rites), the offerers of sacrificial food, was fruitful; the gods were present at their sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: The ten confederated irreligiousrājāsdid not prevail,Indraand Varuṇa, against Sudāsa; the praiseof the leaders (of rites), the offerers of sacrificial food, was fruitful; the gods were present at their sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दाशराज्ञे परियत्ताय विश्वतः सुदास इंद्रावरुणावशिक्षतं ।श्वित्यंचो यत्र नमसा कपर्दिनो धिया धीवंतो असपंत तृत्सवः ॥
verses.transliteration: dāśa-rājñé ǀ pári-yattāya ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ su-dā́se ǀ indrāvaruṇau ǀ aśikṣatam ǀśvityáñcaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ námasā ǀ kapardínaḥ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ dhī́-vantaḥ ǀ ásapanta ǀ tṛ́tsavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You gave vigour,Indraand Varuṇa, to Sudāsawhen surrounded on all sides by the tenrājās(inthe country) where the pious Tṛtsus, walking in whiteness, and wearing braided hair, worshipped with oblationsand praise.
verses.wilson_translation: You gave vigour,Indraand Varuṇa, to Sudāsawhen surrounded on all sides by the tenrājās(inthe country) where the pious Tṛtsus, walking in whiteness, and wearing braided hair, worshipped with oblationsand praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृत्राण्यन्यः समिथेषु जिघ्नते व्रतान्यन्यो अभि रक्षते सदा ।हवामहे वां वृषणा सुवृक्तिभिरस्मे इंद्रावरुणा शर्म यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ anyáḥ ǀ sam-ithéṣu ǀ jíghnate ǀ vratā́ni ǀ anyáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ rakṣate ǀ sádā ǀhávāmahe ǀ vām ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of you destroys enemies inbattle, the other ever protects religious observances; we invoke you,showerers (of benefits), with praises; bestow upon us,Indraand Varuṇa, felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: One of you destroys enemies inbattle, the other ever protects religious observances; we invoke you,showerers (of benefits), with praises; bestow upon us,Indraand Varuṇa, felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे इंद्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा द्युम्नं यच्छंतु महि शर्म सप्रथः ।अवध्रं ज्योतिरदितेर्ऋतावृधो देवस्य श्लोकं सवितुर्मनामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ índraḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ dyumnám ǀ yacchantu ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀavadhrám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ devásya ǀ ślókam ǀ savitúḥ ǀ manāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryamangrant us wealth and a large and spacious mansion; may the lustreof Aditi, the augmentress (of sacrifice), be innoxious to us; we recite the praise of the divine Savitā.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryamangrant us wealth and a large and spacious mansion; may the lustreof Aditi, the augmentress (of sacrifice), be innoxious to us; we recite the praise of the divine Savitā.

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIV. Indra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . KINGS, Indra-Varuṇa, I would turn you hither to this our sacrifice with gifts and homage.Held in both arms the ladle, dropping fatness, goes of itself to you whose forms are varied. Dyaus quickens and promotes your high dominion who bind with bonds not wrought of rope or cordage.Far from us still be Varuṇa's displeasure may Indra give us spacious room to dwell in. Make ye our sacrifice fair amid the assemblies: make ye our prayers approved among our princes.May God-sent riches come for our possession: further ye us with your delightful succours. O Indra-Varuṇa, vouchsafe us riches with store of treasure, food, and every blessing;For the Āditya, banisher of falsehood, the Hero, dealeth wealth in boundless plenty. May this my song reach Varuṇa and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring.To the Gods’ banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: आ वां राजानावध्वरे ववृत्यां हव्येभिरिंद्रावरुणा नमोभिः ।प्र वां घृताची बाह्वोर्दधाना परि त्मना विषुरूपा जिगाति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ rājānau ǀ adhvaré ǀ vavṛtyām ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀprá ǀ vām ǀ ghṛtā́cī ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ dádhānā ǀ pári ǀ tmánā ǀ víṣu-rūpā ǀ jigāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Royal Indraand Varuṇa, I invite you to the sacrifice with oblations and with praise; the butter-dropping(ladle), held in ourhands, offers spontaneously (the oblation) to you who are of many forms.
verses.wilson_translation: Royal Indraand Varuṇa, I invite you to the sacrifice with oblations and with praise; the butter-dropping(ladle), held in ourhands, offers spontaneously (the oblation) to you who are of many forms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभिररज्जुभिः सिनीथः ।परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ bṛhát ǀ invati ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ yáu ǀ setṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ arajjú-bhiḥ ǀ sinītháḥ ǀpári ǀ naḥ ǀ héḷaḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ vṛjyāḥ ǀ urúm ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ kṛṇavat ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your vast kingdom of heaven gratifies (the world with rain), you who bind (the sinner) with bonds notmade of rope; may the wrath of Varuṇapass away from us; may Indraprepare for us a spacious region.
verses.wilson_translation: Your vast kingdom of heaven gratifies (the world with rain), you who bind (the sinner) with bonds notmade of rope; may the wrath of Varuṇapass away from us; may Indraprepare for us a spacious region.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृतं नो यज्ञं विदथेषु चारुं कृतं ब्रह्माणि सूरिषु प्रशस्ता ।उपो रयिर्देवजूतो न एतु प्र णः स्पार्हाभिरूतिभिस्तिरेतं ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛtám ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ cā́rum ǀ kṛtám ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ sūríṣu ǀ pra-śastā́ ǀúpo íti ǀ rayíḥ ǀ devá-jūtaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ etu ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ spārhā́bhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ tiretam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Render the sacrifices offered inour dwelling fruitful, the prayers uttered by the worshippers successful;may riches come to us sent by the gods; do you two give us increase by you desirable protections.
verses.wilson_translation: Render the sacrifices offered inour dwelling fruitful, the prayers uttered by the worshippers successful;may riches come to us sent by the gods; do you two give us increase by you desirable protections.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे इंद्रावरुणा विश्ववारं रयिं धत्तं वसुमंतं पुरुक्षुं ।प्र य आदित्यो अनृता मिनात्यमिता शूरो दयते वसूनि ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ viśvá-vāram ǀ rayím ǀ dhattam ǀ vásu-mantam ǀ puru-kṣúm ǀprá ǀ yáḥ ǀ ādityáḥ ǀ ánṛtā ǀ minā́ti ǀ ámitā ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ dayate ǀ vásūni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bestow upon us,Indraand Varuṇa, riches desirable to all, together with a dwelling and abundant food,for the hero,Āditya, who punishes beings devoid of truth, gives (to the devout) unbounded treasures.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow upon us,Indraand Varuṇa, riches desirable to all, together with a dwelling and abundant food,for the hero,Āditya, who punishes beings devoid of truth, gives (to the devout) unbounded treasures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इयमिंद्रं वरुणमष्ट मे गीः प्रावत्तोके तनये तूतुजाना ।सुरत्नासो देववीतिं गमेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ índram ǀ váruṇam ǀ aṣṭa ǀ me ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvat ǀ toké ǀ tánaye ǀ tū́tujānā ǀsu-rátnāsaḥ ǀ devá-vītim ǀ gamema ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this my praise reach Indraand Varuṇa, and, earnestly offered (by me), preserve sons andgrandsons; let us, possessed of affluence, present (their) food to the gods; and do you, (duties), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May this my praise reach Indraand Varuṇa, and, earnestly offered (by me), preserve sons andgrandsons; let us, possessed of affluence, present (their) food to the gods; and do you, (duties), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXV. Indra-Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FOR you I deck a harmless hymn, presenting the Soma juice to Varuṇa and Indra-A hymn that shines like heavenly Dawn with fatness. May they be near us on the march and guard us. Here where the arrows fall amid the banners both hosts invoke the Gods in emulation.O Indra-Varuṇa, smite back those-our foemen,yea, smite them withyour shaft to every quarter. Self-lucid in their seats, e’en heavenly Waters endowed with Godhead Varuṇa and Indra.One of these holds the folk distinct and sundered, the Other smites and slays resistless foemen. Wise be the priest and skilled in Law Eternal, who with his sacred gifts and oration.Brings you to aid us with your might, Ādityas: let him have viands to promote his welfare. May this my song reach Varuṇa and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring.To the Gods’ banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: पुनीषे वामरक्षसं मनीषां सोममिंद्राय वरुणाय जुह्वत् ।घृतप्रतीकामुषसं न देवीं ता नो यामन्नुरुष्यतामभीके ॥
verses.transliteration: punīṣé ǀ vām ǀ arakṣásam ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ sómam ǀ índrāya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ júhvat ǀghṛtá-pratīkām ǀ uṣásam ǀ ná ǀ devī́m ǀ tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yā́man ǀ uruṣyatām ǀ abhī́ke ǁ
verses.english_translation: I offer to you both adoration, uninterrupted byrākṣasas, presenting the Somato Indraand to Varuṇa,-- (adoration), of which the members are radiant as the celestial dawn; may these two protect us at the time ofgoing to battle.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer to you both adoration, uninterrupted byrākṣasas, presenting the Somato Indraand to Varuṇa,-- (adoration), of which the members are radiant as the celestial dawn; may these two protect us at the time ofgoing to battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्पर्धंते वा उ देवहूये अत्र येषु ध्वजेषु दिद्यवः पतंति ।युवं ताँ इंद्रावरुणावमित्रान्हतं पराचः शर्वा विषूचः ॥
verses.transliteration: spárdhante ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ deva-hū́ye ǀ átra ǀ yéṣu ǀ dhvajéṣu ǀ didyávaḥ ǀ pátanti ǀyuvám ǀ tā́n ǀ indrāvaruṇau ǀ amítrān ǀ hatám ǀ párācaḥ ǀ śárvā ǀ víṣūcaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the conflict where (combatants) strive against us, in those (contests) in which bright (weapons) fallupon the banners, do you two,Indraand Varuṇa, slay with your shaft those enemies who have been routed, andare scattered in various directions.
verses.wilson_translation: In the conflict where (combatants) strive against us, in those (contests) in which bright (weapons) fallupon the banners, do you two,Indraand Varuṇa, slay with your shaft those enemies who have been routed, andare scattered in various directions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आपश्चिद्धि स्वयशसः सदस्सु देवीरिंद्रं वरुणं देवता धुः ।कृष्टीरन्यो धारयति प्रविक्ता वृत्राण्यन्यो अप्रतीनि हंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ svá-yaśasaḥ ǀ sádaḥ-su ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ índram ǀ váruṇam ǀ devátā ǀ dhúríti dhúḥ ǀkṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ dhāráyati ǀ prá-viktāḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ anyáḥ ǀ apratī́ni ǀ hanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine Soma, flowing like water, self-renowned, (offered) at religious assemblies, supoort Indraand Varuṇa; of whom one regulates mankind, distinguished (as good or bad), and the other slays unresisted foeṣ
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Soma, flowing like water, self-renowned, (offered) at religious assemblies, supoort Indraand Varuṇa; of whom one regulates mankind, distinguished (as good or bad), and the other slays unresisted foeṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स सुक्रतुर्ऋतचिदस्तु होता य आदित्य शवसा वां नमस्वान् ।आववर्तदवसे वां हविष्मानसदित्स सुविताय प्रयस्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ ṛta-cít ǀ astu ǀ hótā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ādityā ǀ śávasā ǀ vām ǀ námasvān ǀā-vavártat ǀ ávase ǀ vām ǀ havíṣmān ǀ ásat ǀ ít ǀ sáḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ práyasvān ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the devout worshipper derive benefit from sacrifice when offering adoration to you both, sons of Aditi (involved) with strength; he who, liberal of oblations invites you for your satisfaction, may he, possessingabundance, be in the enjoyment of happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: May the devout worshipper derive benefit from sacrifice when offering adoration to you both, sons of Aditi (involved) with strength; he who, liberal of oblations invites you for your satisfaction, may he, possessingabundance, be in the enjoyment of happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इयमिंद्रं वरुणमष्ट मे गीः प्रावत्तोके तनये तूतुजाना ।सुरत्नासो देववीतिं गमेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ índram ǀ váruṇam ǀ aṣṭa ǀ me ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ āvat ǀ toké ǀ tánaye ǀ tū́tujānā ǀsu-rátnāsaḥ ǀ devá-vītim ǀ gamema ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this my praise reach Indraand Varuṇa; and earnestly offered (by me), preserve sons andgrandsons; let us, possessed of affluence, present (their) food to the gods; and do you, (deities), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May this my praise reach Indraand Varuṇa; and earnestly offered (by me), preserve sons andgrandsons; let us, possessed of affluence, present (their) food to the gods; and do you, (deities), ever cherish uswith blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVI. Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WISE, verily, are creatures through his greatness who stayed ever, spacious heaven and earth asunder;Who urged the high and mighty sky to motion, the Star of old, and spread the earth before him. With mine own heart I commune on the question how Varuṇa and I may be united.What gift of mine will he accept unangered? When may I calmly look and find him gracious? Fain to know this is my sin I question others: I seek the wise, O Varuṇa, and ask them.This one same answer even the sages gave me, "Surely this Varuṇa is angry with thee." What, Varuṇa, hath been my chief transgression, that thou wouldst slay the friend who sings thy praises?Tell me, Unconquerable Lord, and quickly sinless will I approach thee with mine homage. Free us from sins committed by our fathers, from those wherein we have ourselves offended.O King, loose, like a thief who feeds the cattle, as from the cord a calf, set free Vasiṣṭha. Not our own will betrayed us, but seduction, thoughtlessness, Varuṇa wine, dice, or anger.The old is near to lead astray the younger: even sleep removeth not all evil-doing. Slavelike may I do service to the Bounteous, serve, free from sin, the God inclined to anger.This gentle Lord gives wisdom to the simple: the wiser God leads on the wise to riches. O Lord, O Varuṇa, may this laudation come close to thee and lie within thy spirit.May it be well with us in rest and labour. Preserve us ever-more, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: धीरा त्वस्य महिना जनूंषि वि यस्तस्तंभ रोदसी चिदुर्वी ।प्र नाकमृष्वं नुनुदे बृहंतं द्विता नक्षत्रं पप्रथच्च भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: dhī́rā ǀ tú ǀ asya ǀ mahinā́ ǀ janū́ṃṣi ǀ ví ǀ yáḥ ǀ tastámbha ǀ ródasī íti ǀ cit ǀ urvī́ íti ǀprá ǀ nā́kam ǀ ṛṣvám ǀ nunude ǀ bṛhántam ǀ dvitā́ ǀ nákṣatram ǀ papráthat ǀ ca ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Permanent in greatness are the births of that Varuṇawho propped up the vast heaven and earth, whoappointed to (their) two-fold (task) the glorious sun and beautiful constellations, who spread out the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Permanent in greatness are the births of that Varuṇawho propped up the vast heaven and earth, whoappointed to (their) two-fold (task) the glorious sun and beautiful constellations, who spread out the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्वया तन्वा सं वदे तत्कदा न्वंतर्वरुणे भुवानि ।किं मे हव्यमहृणानो जुषेत कदा मृळीकं सुमना अभि ख्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sváyā ǀ tanvā́ ǀ sám ǀ vade ǀ tát ǀ kadā́ ǀ nú ǀ antáḥ ǀ váruṇe ǀ bhuvāni ǀkím ǀ me ǀ havyám ǀ áhṛṇānaḥ ǀ juṣeta ǀ kadā́ ǀ mṛḷīkám ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ khyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When may I in my person n converse with the deity? When may I (be admitted) to the heart of Varuṇa?By what means may he, without displeasure, accept my oblation? When may I, rejoicing in mind, behold thatgiver of felicity?
verses.wilson_translation: When may I in my person n converse with the deity? When may I (be admitted) to the heart of Varuṇa?By what means may he, without displeasure, accept my oblation? When may I, rejoicing in mind, behold thatgiver of felicity?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पृच्छे तदेनो वरुण दिदृक्षूपो एमि चिकितुषो विपृच्छं ।समानमिन्मे कवयश्चिदाहुरयं ह तुभ्यं वरुणो हृणीते ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛcché ǀ tát ǀ énaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ didṛ́kṣu ǀ úpo íti ǀ emi ǀ cikitúṣaḥ ǀ vi-pṛ́ccham ǀsamānám ǀ ít ǀ me ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ cit ǀ āhuḥ ǀ ayám ǀ ha ǀ túbhyam ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ hṛṇīte ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desirous of beholding you,Varuṇa, I inquire what is my offence; I have gone to make inquiry of thewise; the sages verily have said the same thing to me: -- this Varuṇa is displeased with you.
verses.wilson_translation: Desirous of beholding you,Varuṇa, I inquire what is my offence; I have gone to make inquiry of thewise; the sages verily have said the same thing to me: -- this Varuṇa is displeased with you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: किमाग आस वरुण ज्येष्ठं यत्स्तोतारं जिघांससि सखायं ।प्र तन्मे वोचो दूळभ स्वधावोऽव त्वानेना नमसा तुर इयां ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ āsa ǀ varuṇa ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ yát ǀ stotā́ram ǀ jíghāṃsasi ǀ sákhāyam ǀprá ǀ tát ǀ me ǀ vocaḥ ǀ duḥ-dabha ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ áva ǀ tvā ǀ anenā́ḥ ǀ námasā ǀ turáḥ ǀ iyām ǁ
verses.english_translation: What has that great wickedness been,Varuṇa, that you should seek to destroy the worshiper, yourfriend? Insuperable, resplendent Varuṇa, declare it to me, so that, freed from sin, I may quick approach you withveneration.
verses.wilson_translation: What has that great wickedness been,Varuṇa, that you should seek to destroy the worshiper, yourfriend? Insuperable, resplendent Varuṇa, declare it to me, so that, freed from sin, I may quick approach you withveneration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव द्रुग्धानि पित्र्या सृजा नोऽव या वयं चकृमा तनूभिः ।अव राजन्पशुतृपं न तायुं सृजा वत्सं न दाम्नो वसिष्ठं ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ drugdhā́ni ǀ pítryā ǀ sṛja ǀ naḥ ǀ áva ǀ yā́ ǀ vayám ǀ cakṛmá ǀ tanū́bhiḥ ǀáva ǀ rājan ǀ paśu-tṛ́pam ǀ ná ǀ tāyúm ǀ sṛjá ǀ vatsám ǀ ná ǀ dā́mnaḥ ǀ vásiṣṭham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Relax (the bonds) imosed by all the ill deeds of our fore-fathers, and those incurred (by the sins) whichwe have committed in our person ns; liberate, royal Varuṇa, like a calf from its tether,Vasiṣṭhalike a thiefnourishing the animal (he has stolen).
verses.wilson_translation: Relax (the bonds) imosed by all the ill deeds of our fore-fathers, and those incurred (by the sins) whichwe have committed in our person ns; liberate, royal Varuṇa, like a calf from its tether,Vasiṣṭhalike a thiefnourishing the animal (he has stolen).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न स स्वो दक्षो वरुण ध्रुतिः सा सुरा मन्युर्विभीदको अचित्तिः ।अस्ति ज्यायान्कनीयस उपारे स्वप्नश्चनेदनृतस्य प्रयोता ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ dhrútiḥ ǀ sā́ ǀ súrā ǀ manyúḥ ǀ vi-bhī́dakaḥ ǀ ácittiḥ ǀásti ǀ jyā́yān ǀ kánīyasaḥ ǀ upa-aré ǀ svápnaḥ ǀ caná ǀ ít ǀ ánṛtasya ǀ pra-yotā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: It is not our own choice,Varuṇa, not our condition, (that is the cause of our sinning); it is that which isintoxication, wrath, gambling, ignorance; there is a senior in the proximity of the junior; even a dream is aprovocation to sin.
verses.wilson_translation: It is not our own choice,Varuṇa, not our condition, (that is the cause of our sinning); it is that which isintoxication, wrath, gambling, ignorance; there is a senior in the proximity of the junior; even a dream is aprovocation to sin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अरं दासो न मीळ्हुषे कराण्यहं देवाय भूर्णयेऽनागाः ।अचेतयदचितो देवो अर्यो गृत्सं राये कवितरो जुनाति ॥
verses.transliteration: áram ǀ dāsáḥ ǀ ná ǀ mīḷhúṣe ǀ karāṇi ǀ ahám ǀ devā́ya ǀ bhū́rṇaye ǀ ánāgāḥ ǀácetayat ǀ acítaḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ gṛ́tsam ǀ rāyé ǀ kaví-taraḥ ǀ junāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Liberated from sin, I may perform diligent service, like a slave, to the divine showerer (of benefits), thesustainer of the world; may he, the divine lord, give intelligence to us who are devoid of understanding; may hewho is most wise, guide the worshipper to wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Liberated from sin, I may perform diligent service, like a slave, to the divine showerer (of benefits), thesustainer of the world; may he, the divine lord, give intelligence to us who are devoid of understanding; may hewho is most wise, guide the worshipper to wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधावो हृदि स्तोम उपश्रितश्चिदस्तु ।शं नः क्षेमे शमु योगे नो अस्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ sú ǀ túbhyam ǀ varuṇa ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ hṛdí ǀ stómaḥ ǀ úpa-śritaḥ ǀ cit ǀ astu ǀśám ǀ naḥ ǀ kṣéme ǀ śám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ yóge ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
