verses.english_translation: May this laudation, food-conferring Varuṇa, be taken to your heart; may success be ours in retainingwhat we have, and in acquiring more; and do you, (deities), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May this laudation, food-conferring Varuṇa, be taken to your heart; may success be ours in retainingwhat we have, and in acquiring more; and do you, (deities), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVII. Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . VARUNA cut a pathway out for Sūrya, and led the watery floods of rivers onward.The Mares, as in a race, speed on in order. He made great channels for the days to follow. The wind, thy breath, hath sounded through the region like a wild beast that seeks his food in pastures.Within these two, exalted Earth and Heaven, O Varuṇa, are all the forms thou lovest. Varuṇa's spies, sent forth upon their errand, survey the two world-halves well formed and fashioned.Wise are they, holy, skilled in sacrifices, the furtherers of the praise-songs of the prudent. To me who understand hath Varuṇa spoken, the names borne by the Cow are three times seven.The sapient God, knowing the place's secret, shall speak as ’twere to teach the race that cometh. On him three heavens rest and are supported, and the three earths are there in sixfold order.The wise King Varuṇa hath made in heaven that Golden Swing to cover it with glory. Like Varuṇa from heaven he sinks in Sindhu, like a white-shining spark, a strong wild creature.Ruling in depths and meting out the region, great saving power hath he, this world's Controller. Before this Varuṇa may we be sinless him who shows mercy even to the sinner-While we are keeping Aditi's ordinances. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: रदत्पथो वरुणः सूर्याय प्रार्णांसि समुद्रिया नदीनां ।सर्गो न सृष्टो अर्वतीर्ऋतायंचकार महीरवनीरहभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: rádat ǀ patháḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ prá ǀ árṇāṃsi ǀ samudríyā ǀ nadī́nām ǀsárgaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sṛṣṭáḥ ǀ árvatīḥ ǀ ṛta-yán ǀ cakā́ra ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ áha-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇaprepared a path for the sun; he set free the waters of the rivers genitive rated in the firmament;hastening (to his task), as a horse let loose rushes to (a flock of) mares, he divided the great nights from thedays.
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇaprepared a path for the sun; he set free the waters of the rivers genitive rated in the firmament;hastening (to his task), as a horse let loose rushes to (a flock of) mares, he divided the great nights from thedays.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आत्मा ते वातो रज आ नवीनोत्पशुर्न भूर्णिर्यवसे ससवान् ।अंतर्मही बृहती रोदसीमे विश्वा ते धाम वरुण प्रियाणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ātmā́ ǀ te ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ navīnot ǀ paśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhū́rṇiḥ ǀ yávase ǀ sasa-vā́n ǀantáḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ imé íti ǀ víśvā ǀ te ǀ dhā́ma ǀ varuṇa ǀ priyā́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your spirit is the wind; he sends abroad the waters; he, the cherisher of the world, is the feeder on(ssacrificial) food, like an animal upon fodder; all your glories,Varuṇa, manifested between the vast andspacious heaven and earth, give delight (to all).
verses.wilson_translation: Your spirit is the wind; he sends abroad the waters; he, the cherisher of the world, is the feeder on(ssacrificial) food, like an animal upon fodder; all your glories,Varuṇa, manifested between the vast andspacious heaven and earth, give delight (to all).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परि स्पशो वरुणस्य स्मदिष्टा उभे पश्यंति रोदसी सुमेके ।ऋतावानः कवयो यज्ञधीराः प्रचेतसो य इषयंत मन्म ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ smát-iṣṭāḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ paśyanti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ suméke íti su-méke ǀṛtá-vānaḥ ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ yajñá-dhīrāḥ ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ yé ǀ iṣáyanta ǀ mánma ǁ
verses.english_translation: The excellent spies of Varuṇabehold the beautiful heaven and earth, as well as those (men) who, thecelebrators of rites, constant in sacrifice, wise and intelligent address (to him their) praise.
verses.wilson_translation: The excellent spies of Varuṇabehold the beautiful heaven and earth, as well as those (men) who, thecelebrators of rites, constant in sacrifice, wise and intelligent address (to him their) praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उवाच मे वरुणो मेधिराय त्रिः सप्त नामाघ्न्या बिभर्ति ।विद्वान्पदस्य गुह्या न वोचद्युगाय विप्र उपराय शिक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: uvā́ca ǀ me ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ médhirāya ǀ tríḥ ǀ saptá ǀ nā́ma ǀ ághnyā ǀ bibharti ǀvidvā́n ǀ padásya ǀ gúhyā ǀ ná ǀ vocat ǀ yugā́ya ǀ vípraḥ ǀ úparāya ǀ śíkṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇathus spoke to me, possessed of understanding; the cow (speech) has thrice sevenappellations; the wise and intelligent Varuṇa, giving instrumental uction to me, his worthy disciple, had declared themysteries of the plural ce (of Brahma).
verses.wilson_translation: Varuṇathus spoke to me, possessed of understanding; the cow (speech) has thrice sevenappellations; the wise and intelligent Varuṇa, giving instrumental uction to me, his worthy disciple, had declared themysteries of the plural ce (of Brahma).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिंतिस्रो भूमीरुपराः षड्विधानाः ।गृत्सो राजा वरुणश्चक्र एतं दिवि प्रेंखं हिरण्ययं शुभे कं ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ ní-hitāḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ asmin ǀ tisráḥ ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ úparāḥ ǀ ṣáṭ-vidhānāḥ ǀgṛ́tsaḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ cakre ǀ etám ǀ diví ǀ pra-īṅkhám ǀ hiraṇyáyam ǀ śubhé ǀ kám ǁ
verses.english_translation: In him are deposited the three heavens, the three earths with their six seasons are shown in him; themost adorable, royal Varuṇahas made this golden sun undulating in the sky, he has made it to diffuse light.
verses.wilson_translation: In him are deposited the three heavens, the three earths with their six seasons are shown in him; themost adorable, royal Varuṇahas made this golden sun undulating in the sky, he has made it to diffuse light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अव सिंधुं वरुणो द्यौरिव स्थाद्द्रप्सो न श्वेतो मृगस्तुविष्मान् ।गंभीरशंसो रजसो विमानः सुपारक्षत्रः सतो अस्य राजा ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ síndhum ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ dyáuḥ-iva ǀ sthāt ǀ drapsáḥ ǀ ná ǀ śvetáḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǀgambhīrá-śaṃsaḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́naḥ ǀ supārá-kṣatraḥ ǀ satáḥ ǀ asyá ǀ rā́jā ǁ
verses.english_translation: (Radiant) as the sun,Varuṇaplural ced the ocean (in its bed) white as a drop (of water), vigorous as anantelope, objects of profound praise, distributor of water, the powerful transporter beyond sin, the ruler of thisexisting (world).
verses.wilson_translation: (Radiant) as the sun,Varuṇaplural ced the ocean (in its bed) white as a drop (of water), vigorous as anantelope, objects of profound praise, distributor of water, the powerful transporter beyond sin, the ruler of thisexisting (world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो मृळयाति चक्रुषे चिदागो वयं स्याम वरुणे अनागाः ।अनु व्रतान्यदितेर्ऋधंतो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ mṛḷáyāti ǀ cakrúṣe ǀ cit ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ vayám ǀ syāma ǀ váruṇe ǀ ánāgāḥ ǀánu ǀ vratā́ni ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ṛdhántaḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we be free from sin against that Varuṇa, who has compassion upon him who commits offence, wewho are duly observing the rites of the son Aditi; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be free from sin against that Varuṇa, who has compassion upon him who commits offence, wewho are duly observing the rites of the son Aditi; and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVIII. Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PRESENT to Varuṇa thine hymn, Vasiṣṭha, bright, most delightful to the Bounteous Giver,Who bringeth on to us the Bull, the lofty, the Holy, laden with a thousand treasures. And now, as I am come before his presence, I take the face of Varuṇa for Agni's.So might he bring-Lord also of the darkness-the light in heaven that I may see its beauty! When Varuṇa and I embark together and urge our boat into the midst of ocean,We, when we ride o’er ridges of the waters, will swing within that swing and there be happy. Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha in the vessel, and deftly with his niight made him a Ṛṣi.When days shone bright the Sage made him a singer, while the heavens broadened and the Dawns were lengthened. What hath become of those our ancient friendships, when without enmity we walked together?I, Varuṇa, thou glorious Lord, have entered thy lofty home, thine house with thousand portals. If he, thy true ally, hath sinned against thee, still, Varuṇa, he is the friend thou lovedst.Let us not, Living One, as sinners I know thee: give shelter, as a Sage, to him who lauds thee. While we abide in these fixed habitations, and from the lap of Aditi win favour,May Varuṇa untie the bond that binds us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र शुंध्युवं वरुणाय प्रेष्ठां मतिं वसिष्ठ मीळ्हुषे भरस्व ।य ईमर्वांचं करते यजत्रं सहस्रामघं वृषणं बृहंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ śundhyúvam ǀ váruṇāya ǀ préṣṭhām ǀ matím ǀ vasiṣṭha ǀ mīḷhúṣe ǀ bharasva ǀyáḥ ǀ īm ǀ arvā́ñcam ǀ kárate ǀ yájatram ǀ sahásra-magham ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ bṛhántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer pure and acceptable praise,Vasiṣṭhato the showerer,Varuṇa, he who makes the adorable(sun), the donor of thousands, the showerer (of benefits), the vast, manifest before (us).
verses.wilson_translation: Offer pure and acceptable praise,Vasiṣṭhato the showerer,Varuṇa, he who makes the adorable(sun), the donor of thousands, the showerer (of benefits), the vast, manifest before (us).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अधा न्वस्य संदृशं जगन्वानग्नेरनीकं वरुणस्य मंसि ।स्वर्यदश्मन्नधिपा उ अंधोऽभि मा वपुर्दृशये निनीयात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ sam-dṛ́śam ǀ jaganvā́n ǀ agnéḥ ǀ ánīkam ǀ váruṇasya ǀ maṃsi ǀsváḥ ǀ yát ǀ áśman ǀ adhi-pā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ mā ǀ vápuḥ ǀ dṛśáye ǀ ninīyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hastening into his sight, may I (worthily) glorify the aggregated radiance of Varuṇa, when he is theimbiber of the exhilarating beverage (expressed) by the stones; may he render my person n of goodly aspect.
verses.wilson_translation: Hastening into his sight, may I (worthily) glorify the aggregated radiance of Varuṇa, when he is theimbiber of the exhilarating beverage (expressed) by the stones; may he render my person n of goodly aspect.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ यद्रुहाव वरुणश्च नावं प्र यत्समुद्रमीरयाव मध्यं ।अधि यदपां स्नुभिश्चराव प्र प्रेंख ईंखयावहै शुभे कं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yát ǀ ruhā́va ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ nā́vam ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ samudrám ǀ īráyāva ǀ mádhyam ǀádhi ǀ yát ǀ apā́m ǀ snú-bhiḥ ǀ cárāva ǀ prá ǀ pra-īṅkhé ǀ īṅkhayāvahai ǀ śubhé ǀ kám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When (I,Vasiṣṭha) and Varuṇaascend the ship together when we send it forth into the midst of theocean, when we proceed over the waters with swift (sailing vessels), then may we both undulate happily in theprosperous swing.
verses.wilson_translation: When (I,Vasiṣṭha) and Varuṇaascend the ship together when we send it forth into the midst of theocean, when we proceed over the waters with swift (sailing vessels), then may we both undulate happily in theprosperous swing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वसिष्ठं ह वरुणो नाव्याधादृषिं चकार स्वपा महोभिः ।स्तोतारं विप्रः सुदिनत्वे अह्नां यान्नु द्यावस्ततनन्यादुषासः ॥
verses.transliteration: vásiṣṭham ǀ ha ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ nāví ǀ ā́ ǀ adhāt ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ cakāra ǀ su-ápāḥ ǀ máhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀstotā́ram ǀ vípraḥ ǀ sudina-tvé ǀ áhnām ǀ yā́t ǀ nú ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ tatánan ǀ yā́t ǀ uṣásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So Varuṇaplural ced Vasiṣṭhain the ship, and by his mighty protection made the ṛṣi a doer of goodworks; the wise Varuṇa plural ced his worshipper in a fortunate day of days, he extended the passing days, thepassing nights.
verses.wilson_translation: So Varuṇaplural ced Vasiṣṭhain the ship, and by his mighty protection made the ṛṣi a doer of goodworks; the wise Varuṇa plural ced his worshipper in a fortunate day of days, he extended the passing days, thepassing nights.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्व त्यानि नौ सख्या बभूवुः सचावहे यदवृकं पुरा चित् ।बृहंतं मानं वरुण स्वधावः सहस्रद्वारं जगमा गृहं ते ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ tyā́ni ǀ nau ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ babhūvuḥ ǀ sácāvahe íti ǀ yát ǀ avṛkám ǀ purā́ ǀ cit ǀbṛhántam ǀ mā́nam ǀ varuṇa ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ sahásra-dvāram ǀ jagama ǀ gṛhám ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: What has become of those our ancient friendships? Let us preserve them unimpaired as of old;food-bestowing Varuṇa, may I go to your vast comprehensive thousand-doored dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: What has become of those our ancient friendships? Let us preserve them unimpaired as of old;food-bestowing Varuṇa, may I go to your vast comprehensive thousand-doored dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य आपिर्नित्यो वरुण प्रियः संत्वामागांसि कृणवत्सखा ते ।मा त एनस्वंतो यक्षिन्भुजेम यंधि ष्मा विप्रः स्तुवते वरूथं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ varuṇa ǀ priyáḥ ǀ sán ǀ tvā́m ǀ ā́gāṃsi ǀ kṛṇávat ǀ sákhā ǀ te ǀmā́ ǀ te ǀ énasvantaḥ ǀ yakṣin ǀ bhujema ǀ yandhí ǀ sma ǀ vípraḥ ǀ stuvaté ǀ várūtham ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he your unvarying kin, who was ever dear, though committing offences against you, still be yourfriend; adorable Varuṇa, offending you, let us not enjoy (happiness); but do you, who are wise, bestow on yourworshipper a secure abode.
verses.wilson_translation: May he your unvarying kin, who was ever dear, though committing offences against you, still be yourfriend; adorable Varuṇa, offending you, let us not enjoy (happiness); but do you, who are wise, bestow on yourworshipper a secure abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ध्रुवासु त्वासु क्षितिषु क्षियंतो व्यस्मत्पाशं वरुणो मुमोचत् ।अवो वन्वाना अदितेरुपस्थाद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhruvā́su ǀ tvā ǀ āsú ǀ kṣitíṣu ǀ kṣiyántaḥ ǀ ví ǀ asmát ǀ pā́śam ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mumocat ǀávaḥ ǀ vanvānā́ḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ upá-sthāt ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: While dwelling in these durable worlds, may Varuṇaloose our bonds; may we be enjoyers of theprotection (which has been given by him) from the lap of Aditi, and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.wilson_translation: While dwelling in these durable worlds, may Varuṇaloose our bonds; may we be enjoyers of theprotection (which has been given by him) from the lap of Aditi, and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessingṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIX Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET me not yet, King Varuṇa, enter into the house of clay:Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord. When, Thunderer! I move along tremulous like a wind-blown skin,Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord. O Bright and Powerful God, through want of strength I erred and went astrayHave mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord. Thirst found thy worshipper though he stood in the midst of water-fijods:Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord. O Varuṇa, whatever the offence may be which we as men commit against the heavenly host,When through our want of thought we violate thy laws, punish us not, O God, for that iniquity.

verses.sanskrit: मो षु वरुण मृन्मयं गृहं राजन्नहं गमं ।मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ varuṇa ǀ mṛt-máyam ǀ gṛhám ǀ rājan ǀ ahám ǀ gamam ǀmṛḷá ǀ su-kṣatra ǀ mṛḷáya ǁ
verses.english_translation: May I never go, royal Varuṇa, to a house made of clay; grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grantme happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: May I never go, royal Varuṇa, to a house made of clay; grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grantme happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदेमि प्रस्फुरन्निव दृतिर्न ध्मातो अद्रिवः ।मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ émi ǀ prasphurán-iva ǀ dṛ́tiḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhmātáḥ ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀmṛḷá ǀ su-kṣatra ǀ mṛḷáya ǁ
verses.english_translation: When,Varuṇa, I am throbbing as if (with awe) like an inflated skin, grant me happiness, possessor ofwealth, grant me happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Varuṇa, I am throbbing as if (with awe) like an inflated skin, grant me happiness, possessor ofwealth, grant me happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्रत्वः समह दीनता प्रतीपं जगमा शुचे ।मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: krátvaḥ ǀ samaha ǀ dīnátā ǀ prati-īpám ǀ jagama ǀ śuce ǀmṛḷá ǀ su-kṣatra ǀ mṛḷáya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Opulent and pure (Varuṇa), if through infirmity I have done what is contrary (to the law), yet grant mehappiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Opulent and pure (Varuṇa), if through infirmity I have done what is contrary (to the law), yet grant mehappiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपां मध्ये तस्थिवांसं तृष्णाविदज्जरितारं ।मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ mádhye ǀ tasthi-vā́ṃsam ǀ tṛ́ṣṇā ǀ avidat ǀ jaritā́ram ǀmṛḷá ǀ su-kṣatra ǀ mṛḷáya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thirst distresses (me) your worshipper in the midst of the waters; grant me happiness, possessor ofwealth, grant me happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Thirst distresses (me) your worshipper in the midst of the waters; grant me happiness, possessor ofwealth, grant me happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्किं चेदं वरुण दैव्ये जनेऽभिद्रोहं मनुष्याश्चरामसि ।अचित्ती यत्तव धर्मा युयोपिम मा नस्तस्मादेनसो देव रीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ idám ǀ varuṇa ǀ dáivye ǀ jáne ǀ abhi-drohám ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ cárāmasi ǀácittī ǀ yát ǀ táva ǀ dhárma ǀ yuyopimá ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ tásmāt ǀ énasaḥ ǀ deva ǀ ririṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever the offence which we men commit Varuṇaagainst divine beings, whatever law of yours wemay through ignorance violate, do not you, divine Varuṇa, punish us on account of that iniquity.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever the offence which we men commit Varuṇaagainst divine beings, whatever law of yours wemay through ignorance violate, do not you, divine Varuṇa, punish us on account of that iniquity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XC. Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To you pure juice, rich in meath, are offered by priest: through longing for the Pair of Heroes.Drive, Vāyu, bring thine harnessed horses hither: drink the pressed Soma till it make thee joyful. Whoso to thee, the Mighty, brings oblation, pure Soma unto thee, pure-drinking Vāyu,That man thou makest famous among mortals: to him strong sons are born in quick succession. The God whom both these worlds brought forth for riches, whom heavenly Dhiṣaṇā for our wealth appointeth,His team of harnessed horses waits on Vāyu, and, foremost, on the radiant Treasure-bearer. The spotless Dawns with fair bright days have broken; they found the spacious light when they were shining.Eagerly they disclosed the stall of cattle: floods streamed for them as in the days aforetime. These with their truthful spirit, shining brightly, move on provided with their natural insight.Viands attend the car that beareth Heroes, your car, ye Sovran Pair, Indra and Vāyu. May these who give us heavenly light, these rulers, with gifts of kine and horses, gold and treasures.These princes, through full life, Indra and Vāyu! o’ercome in battle with their steeds and heroes. Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vāyu, with our fair laudations.Exerting all our power call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वीरया शुचयो दद्रिरे वामध्वर्युभिर्मधुमंतः सुतासः ।वह वायो नियुतो याह्यच्छा पिबा सुतस्यांधसो मदाय ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vīra-yā́ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ dadrire ǀ vām ǀ adhvaryú-bhiḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀváha ǀ vāyo íti ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ áccha ǀ píba ǀ sutásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ mádāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sweet and pure Somais offered to you, the hero Vāyu, by the priests; therefore, harness your Niyut steeds, come hither and drink of effused Soma for your exhilaration.
verses.wilson_translation: The sweet and pure Somais offered to you, the hero Vāyu, by the priests; therefore, harness your Niyut steeds, come hither and drink of effused Soma for your exhilaration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त आनट् छुचिं सोमं शुचिपास्तुभ्यं वायो ।कृणोषि तं मर्त्येषु प्रशस्तं जातोजातो जायते वाज्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: īśānā́ya ǀ prá-hutim ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ śúcim ǀ sómam ǀ śuci-pāḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ vāyo íti ǀkṛṇóṣi ǀ tám ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ pra-śastám ǀ jātáḥ-jātaḥ ǀ jāyate ǀ vājī́ ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drinker of the Soma,Vāyu, you elevate him who among mortals offers to you who are the lord anexcellent oblation, the pure Soma; repeatedly born, he is born for the acquisition of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Drinker of the Soma,Vāyu, you elevate him who among mortals offers to you who are the lord anexcellent oblation, the pure Soma; repeatedly born, he is born for the acquisition of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे राये देवी धिषणा धाति देवं ।अध वायुं नियुतः सश्चत स्वा उत श्वेतं वसुधितिं निरेके ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyé ǀ nú ǀ yám ǀ jajñátuḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ imé íti ǀ rāyé ǀ devī́ ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ dhāti ǀ devám ǀádha ǀ vāyúm ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ saścata ǀ svā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ śvetám ǀ vásu-dhitim ǀ nireké ǁ
verses.english_translation: His own Niyutsteeds bear to the plural ce of poverty the white- complexioned dispenser of wealth,Vāyu,whom heaven and earth bore for the sake of riches, whom the divine language of praise sustains as a deity forthe sake of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: His own Niyutsteeds bear to the plural ce of poverty the white- complexioned dispenser of wealth,Vāyu,whom heaven and earth bore for the sake of riches, whom the divine language of praise sustains as a deity forthe sake of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्रा उरु ज्योतिर्विविदुर्दीध्यानाः ।गव्यं चिदूर्वमुशिजो वि वव्रुस्तेषामनु प्रदिवः सस्रुरापः ॥
verses.transliteration: ucchán ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ su-dínāḥ ǀ ariprā́ḥ ǀ urú ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ vividuḥ ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀgávyam ǀ cit ǀ ūrvám ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vavruḥ ǀ téṣām ǀ ánu ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ sasruḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The blameless dawns (ushering) bright days have broken, and, shining radiantly, (the Aṅgirasas) haveobtained the vast light (the sun); desirous (to recover it) they have obtained their wealth of cattle and the ancientwaters have subsequently issued for their good.
verses.wilson_translation: The blameless dawns (ushering) bright days have broken, and, shining radiantly, (the Aṅgirasas) haveobtained the vast light (the sun); desirous (to recover it) they have obtained their wealth of cattle and the ancientwaters have subsequently issued for their good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः स्वेन युक्तासः क्रतुना वहंति ।इंद्रवायू वीरवाहं रथं वामीशानयोरभि पृक्षः सचंते ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ satyéna ǀ mánasā ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀ svéna ǀ yuktā́saḥ ǀ krátunā ǀ vahanti ǀíndravāyū íti ǀ vīra-vā́ham ǀ rátham ǀ vām ǀ īśānáyoḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ sacante ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those (worshippers) illustrious by sincere adoration, assiduous in the discharge of their own duties,bring to you,Indraand Vāyu, a hero-bearing chariot, and present to you, two soverigns, (sacrificial) fooḍ
verses.wilson_translation: Those (worshippers) illustrious by sincere adoration, assiduous in the discharge of their own duties,bring to you,Indraand Vāyu, a hero-bearing chariot, and present to you, two soverigns, (sacrificial) fooḍ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईशानासो ये दधते स्वर्णो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्हिरण्यैः ।इंद्रवायू सूरयो विश्वमायुरर्वद्भिर्वीरैः पृतनासु सह्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: īśānā́saḥ ǀ yé ǀ dádhate ǀ sváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvebhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ híraṇyaiḥ ǀíndravāyū íti ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ árvat-bhiḥ ǀ vīráiḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ sahyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those munificent princes who confer upon us prosperity by gifts of cattle, horses, treasure, gold,overcome,Indraand Vāyu, the entire existence (of their enemies) in contests with horses and with heroeṣ
verses.wilson_translation: May those munificent princes who confer upon us prosperity by gifts of cattle, horses, treasure, gold,overcome,Indraand Vāyu, the entire existence (of their enemies) in contests with horses and with heroeṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वंतो न श्रवसो भिक्षमाणा इंद्रवायू सुष्टुतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः ।वाजयंतः स्ववसे हुवेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: árvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀ indravāyū́ íti ǀ sustutí-bhiḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀvāja-yántaḥ ǀ sú ǀ ávase ǀ huvema ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We,Vasiṣṭha, (bearing oblation) like horses (bearing burdens), soliciting food, desiring strength,invoke with praises Indraand Vāyufor (our) sure defence; do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: We,Vasiṣṭha, (bearing oblation) like horses (bearing burdens), soliciting food, desiring strength,invoke with praises Indraand Vāyufor (our) sure defence; do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCI. Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WERE not in sooth, the Gods aforetime blameless, whose pleasure was increased by adoration?For Vāyu and for man in his affliction they caused the Morning to arise with Sūrya. Guardians infallible, eager as envoys' preserve us safe through many months and autumns.Addressed to you, our fair praise, Indra-Vāyu, implores your favour and renewed well-being. Wise, bright, arranger of his teams, he. seeketh men with rich food whose treasures are abundant.They have arranged them of one mind with Vāyu: the men have wrought all noble operations. So far as native power and strength permit you, so far as men behold whose eyes have vision,O ye pure-drinkers, drink with us pure Soma: sit on this sacred grass, Indra and Vāyu. Driving down teams that bear the lovely Heroes, hitherward, Indra-Vāyu, come together.To you this prime of savoury juice is offered: here loose your horses and be friendly-minded. Your hundred and your thousand teams, O Indra and Vāyu, all-munificent, which attend you,With these most gracious-minded come ye hither, and drink, O Heroes of the meath we offer. Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vāyu, with our fair laudations,Exerting all our powe-,, call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: कुविदंग नमसा ये वृधासः पुरा देवा अनवद्यास आसन् ।ते वायवे मनवे बाधितायावासयन्नुषसं सूर्येण ॥
verses.transliteration: kuvít ǀ aṅgá ǀ námasā ǀ yé ǀ vṛdhā́saḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ anavadyā́saḥ ǀ ā́san ǀté ǀ vāyáve ǀ mánave ǀ bādhitā́ya ǀ ávāsayan ǀ uṣásam ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those venerable worshippers, who by prompted and frequently (adoring Vāyu) with reverence wereformerly free from reproach, have now illumined Uṣas and the sun for sacrificing to Vāyu and (the preservationof) embarrassed mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: Those venerable worshippers, who by prompted and frequently (adoring Vāyu) with reverence wereformerly free from reproach, have now illumined Uṣas and the sun for sacrificing to Vāyu and (the preservationof) embarrassed mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उशंता दूता न दभाय गोपा मासश्च पाथः शरदश्च पूर्वीः ।इंद्रवायू सुष्टुतिर्वामियाना मार्डीकमीट्टे सुवितं च नव्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: uśántā ǀ dūtā́ ǀ ná ǀ dábhāya ǀ gopā́ ǀ māsáḥ ǀ ca ǀ pātháḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀíndravāyū íti ǀ su-stutíḥ ǀ vām ǀ iyānā́ ǀ mārḍīkám ǀ īṭṭe ǀ suvitám ǀ ca ǀ návyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desiring (adoration), proceeding (in the sky), preservers of mankind, be not disposed,Indraand Vāyu,to do us harm; protect us through many months and years; our sincere praise, addressed to you both, solicitshappiness and excellent wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Desiring (adoration), proceeding (in the sky), preservers of mankind, be not disposed,Indraand Vāyu,to do us harm; protect us through many months and years; our sincere praise, addressed to you both, solicitshappiness and excellent wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पीवोअन्नान्रयिवृधः सुमेधाः श्वेतः सिषक्ति नियुतामभिश्रीः ।ते वायवे समनसो वि तस्थुर्विश्वेन्नरः स्वपत्यानि चक्रुः ॥
verses.transliteration: pī́vaḥ-annān ǀ rayi-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ su-medhā́ḥ ǀ śvetáḥ ǀ sisakti ǀ ni-yútām ǀ abhi-śrī́ḥ ǀté ǀ vāyáve ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tasthuḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ náraḥ ǀ su-apatyā́ni ǀ cakruḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The white-complexioned Vāyu, intelligent, glorious with the Niyutsteeds, favours those men who arewell fed, abounding in riches, for they with one mind stand everywhere, ready to (worship) him, and leaders ofrites, they perform all the ceremonies, that are productive of excellent offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: The white-complexioned Vāyu, intelligent, glorious with the Niyutsteeds, favours those men who arewell fed, abounding in riches, for they with one mind stand everywhere, ready to (worship) him, and leaders ofrites, they perform all the ceremonies, that are productive of excellent offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यावत्तरस्तन्वो यावदोजो यावन्नरश्चक्षसा दीध्यानाः ।शुचिं सोमं शुचिपा पातमस्मे इंद्रवायू सदतं बर्हिरेदं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́vat ǀ táraḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ yā́vat ǀ ójaḥ ǀ yā́vat ǀ náraḥ ǀ cákṣasā ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀśúcim ǀ sómam ǀ śuci-pā ǀ pātam ǀ asmé íti ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ sádatam ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ idám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As much as is your rapidity of body, as much as is your vigour, as much as the leaders (of rites) areilluminated by wisdom, (to such extent), drinkers of the pure (Soma)Indraand Varuṇa., drink this our pure Soma,and sit down upon this sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: As much as is your rapidity of body, as much as is your vigour, as much as the leaders (of rites) areilluminated by wisdom, (to such extent), drinkers of the pure (Soma)Indraand Varuṇa., drink this our pure Soma,and sit down upon this sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नियुवाना नियुतः स्पार्हवीरा इंद्रवायू सरथं यातमर्वाक् ।इदं हि वां प्रभृतं मध्वो अग्रमध प्रीणाना वि मुमुक्तमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: ni-yuvānā́ ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ spārhá-vīrāḥ ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yātam ǀ arvā́k ǀidám ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ prá-bhṛtam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ ádha ǀ prīṇānā́ ǀ ví ǀ mumuktam ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harnessing the Niyuts, whom the devout (worshippers) desire, to your common car, come,Indraand Vāyu, hither; this the first (cup) of the sweet Somais prepared for you; and then, delighted (by the draught),liberate us (from sin).
verses.wilson_translation: Harnessing the Niyuts, whom the devout (worshippers) desire, to your common car, come,Indraand Vāyu, hither; this the first (cup) of the sweet Somais prepared for you; and then, delighted (by the draught),liberate us (from sin).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या वां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रमिंद्रवायू विश्ववाराः सचंते ।आभिर्यातं सुविदत्राभिरर्वाक्पातं नरा प्रतिभृतस्य मध्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ vām ǀ śatám ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ índravāyū íti ǀ viśvá-vārāḥ ǀ sácante ǀā́ ǀ ābhiḥ ǀ yātam ǀ su-vidátrābhiḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ pātám ǀ narā ǀ práti-bhṛtasya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to our presence,Indraand Vāyu, with those munificent Niyutsteeds, who, the desired of all,wait upon you both by hundreds and thousands; drink, leaders (of rites), of the sweet Somaplural ced near (thealtar).
verses.wilson_translation: Come to our presence,Indraand Vāyu, with those munificent Niyutsteeds, who, the desired of all,wait upon you both by hundreds and thousands; drink, leaders (of rites), of the sweet Somaplural ced near (thealtar).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वंतो न श्रवसो भिक्षमाणा इंद्रवायू सुष्टुतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः ।वाजयंतः स्ववसे हुवेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: árvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀ indravāyū́ íti ǀ sustutí-bhiḥ ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀvāja-yántaḥ ǀ sú ǀ ávase ǀ huvema ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We,Vasiṣṭhas(bearing oblations) like horses (bearing burdens), soliciting food, desiring strength,invoke with praises Indraand Vāyufor our sure defence; do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: We,Vasiṣṭhas(bearing oblations) like horses (bearing burdens), soliciting food, desiring strength,invoke with praises Indraand Vāyufor our sure defence; do you ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCII. Vāyu
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O VĀYU, drinker of the pure, be near us: a thousand teams are thine, Allbounteous Giver.To thee the rapture-bringing juice is offered, whose first draught, God, thou takest as thy portion. Prompt at the holy rites forth came the presser with Soma-draughts for Indra and for Vāyu,When ministering priests with strong devotion bring to you Twain the first taste of the Soma. The teams wherewith thou seekest him who offers, within his home, O Viyu, to direct him,Therewith send wealth: to us with full enjoyment, a hero son and gifts of kine and horses. Near to the Gods and making Indra joyful, devout and ofFering precious gifts to Vāyu,Allied with princes, smiting down the hostile, may we with heroes conquer foes in battle. With thy yoked teams in hundreds and in thousands come to our sacrifice and solemn worship.Come, Vāyu, make thee glad at this libation. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार ।उपो ते अंधो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vāyo íti ǀ bhūṣa ǀ śuci-pāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ te ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀ viśva-vāra ǀúpo íti ǀ te ǀ ándhaḥ ǀ mádyam ǀ ayāmi ǀ yásya ǀ deva ǀ dadhiṣé ǀ pūrva-péyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drinker of the pure (Soma),Vāyu, come to us as your Niyutare thousands; oḥ, you who are desired ofall, I offer you, the exhilarating (sacrificial) food, of which you, deity, have the prior drinking.
verses.wilson_translation: Drinker of the pure (Soma),Vāyu, come to us as your Niyutare thousands; oḥ, you who are desired ofall, I offer you, the exhilarating (sacrificial) food, of which you, deity, have the prior drinking.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेष्वस्थात्सोममिंद्राय वायवे पिबध्यै ।प्र यद्वां मध्वो अग्रियं भरंत्यध्वर्यवो देवयंतः शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sótā ǀ jīráḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ asthāt ǀ sómam ǀ índrāya ǀ vāyáve ǀ píbadhyai ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ agriyám ǀ bháranti ǀ adhvaryávaḥ ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The prompt effuser of the libation offers the Somato Indraand to Vāyuto drink at the sacrifices, atwhich devout priests, according to their functions, bring to you two the first (portion) of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: The prompt effuser of the libation offers the Somato Indraand to Vāyuto drink at the sacrifices, atwhich devout priests, according to their functions, bring to you two the first (portion) of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा नियुद्भिर्वायविष्टये दुरोणे ।नि नो रयिं सुभोजसं युवस्व नि वीरं गव्यमश्व्यं च राधः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ yā́si ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ áccha ǀ niyút-bhiḥ ǀ vāyo íti ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ duroṇé ǀní ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ su-bhójasam ǀ yuvasva ǀ ní ǀ vīrám ǀ gávyam ǀ áśvyam ǀ ca ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With those Niyutsteeds, with which you go,Vāyu, to the donor (of the libation), waiting in this hall tooffer sacrifice, (come to us), and bestow upon us enjoyable riches, bestowmaleprogeny, and wealth,comprehending cattle, and horses.
verses.wilson_translation: With those Niyutsteeds, with which you go,Vāyu, to the donor (of the libation), waiting in this hall tooffer sacrifice, (come to us), and bestow upon us enjoyable riches, bestowmaleprogeny, and wealth,comprehending cattle, and horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये वायव इंद्रमादनास आदेवासो नितोशनासो अर्यः ।घ्नंतो वृत्राणि सूरिभिः ष्याम सासह्वांसो युधा नृभिरमित्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ vāyáve ǀ indra-mā́danāsaḥ ǀ ā́-devāsaḥ ǀ ni-tóśanāsaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀghnántaḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sūrí-bhiḥ ǀ syāma ǀ sasahvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ yudhā́ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ amítrān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Overcoming our enemies in war by our warriors, may we be the slayers of foes, through the pious(worshippers) who are the exhilarators of Indraand Vāyu, the reciters of divine hymns, the destroyers of theadversary.
verses.wilson_translation: Overcoming our enemies in war by our warriors, may we be the slayers of foes, through the pious(worshippers) who are the exhilarators of Indraand Vāyu, the reciters of divine hymns, the destroyers of theadversary.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं सहस्रिणीभिरुप याहि यज्ञं ।वायो अस्मिन्त्सवने मादयस्व यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ niyút-bhiḥ ǀ śatínībhiḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ sahasríṇībhiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ yajñám ǀvā́yo íti ǀ asmín ǀ sávane ǀ mādayasva ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come Vāyu, to our imperishable sacrifice, with hundreds and thousands of Niyutsteeds, and beexhilarated at this ceremony; do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Come Vāyu, to our imperishable sacrifice, with hundreds and thousands of Niyutsteeds, and beexhilarated at this ceremony; do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIII. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SLAYERS of enemies, Indra and Agni, accept this day our new-born pure laudation.Again, again I call you prompt to listen, best to give quickly strength to him who craves it. For ye were strong to gain, exceeding mighty, growing together, waxing in your vigour.Lords of the pasture filled with ample riches, bestow upon us strength both fresh and lasting. Yea when the strong have entered our assembly, and singers seeking with their hymns your favour,They are like steeds who come into the race-course, those men who call aloud on Indra-Agni. The singer, seeking with his hymns your favour, begs splendid riches of their first possessor.Further us with new bounties, Indra-Agni, armed with strong thunder, slayers of the foeman. When two great hosts, arrayed against each other, meet clothed with brightness, in the fierce encounterStand ye beside the godly, smite the godless; and still assist the men who press the Soma. To this our Soma-pressing, Indra-Agni, come ye prepared to show your loving-kindness,For not at any time have ye despised us. So may I draw you with all strengthenings hither. So Agni, kindled mid this adoration, invite thou Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra.Forgive whatever sin we have committed may Aryaman and Aditi remove it. While we accelerate these our sacrifices, may we win strength from both of you, O Agni:Ne’er may the Maruts, Indra, Viṣṇu slight us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्येंद्राग्नी वृत्रहणा जुषेथां ।उभा हि वां सुहवा जोहवीमि ता वाजं सद्य उशते धेष्ठा ॥
verses.transliteration: śúcim ǀ nú ǀ stómam ǀ náva-jātam ǀ adyá ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ vṛtra-hanā ǀ juṣéthām ǀubhā́ ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ su-hávā ǀ jóhavīmi ǀ tā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ uśaté ǀ dhéṣṭhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayers of enemies,Indraand Agni, be plural ased today by this pious and newly recited praise; repeatedlydo we invoke you both, who are worthy of invocation; you are the chief bestowers of food promptly upon him whosolicits (it of you).
verses.wilson_translation: Slayers of enemies,Indraand Agni, be plural ased today by this pious and newly recited praise; repeatedlydo we invoke you both, who are worthy of invocation; you are the chief bestowers of food promptly upon him whosolicits (it of you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता सानसी शवसाना हि भूतं साकंवृधा शवसा शूशुवांसा ।क्षयंतौ रायो यवसस्य भूरेः पृंक्तं वाजस्य स्थविरस्य घृष्वेः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ sānasī́ íti ǀ śavasānā ǀ hí ǀ bhūtám ǀ sākam-vṛ́dhā ǀ śávasā ǀ śūśu-vā́ṃsā ǀkṣáyantau ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ yávasasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ pṛṅktám ǀ vā́jasya ǀ sthávirasya ǀ ghṛ́ṣveḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You two are desired of all, the demolishers of (hostile) strength, augmenting together, increasing invigour, lords of the wealth of corn; do you grant us substantial invigorating food.
verses.wilson_translation: You two are desired of all, the demolishers of (hostile) strength, augmenting together, increasing invigour, lords of the wealth of corn; do you grant us substantial invigorating food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उपो ह यद्विदथं वाजिनो गुर्धीभिर्विप्राः प्रमतिमिच्छमानाः ।अर्वंतो न काष्ठां नक्षमाणा इंद्राग्नी जोहुवतो नरस्ते ॥
verses.transliteration: úpo íti ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ vidátham ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ gúḥ ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ víprāḥ ǀ prá-matim ǀ icchámānāḥ ǀárvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ kā́ṣṭhām ǀ nákṣamāṇāḥ ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ jóhuvataḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ té ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those sage offerers of oblations, who, desiring your favour, celebrate the sacrifice with holy rites,hasten to worship you, like horse to battle, repeatedly invoking Indraand Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: Those sage offerers of oblations, who, desiring your favour, celebrate the sacrifice with holy rites,hasten to worship you, like horse to battle, repeatedly invoking Indraand Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमान ईट्टे रयिं यशसं पूर्वभाजं ।इंद्राग्नी वृत्रहणा सुवज्रा प्र नो नव्येभिस्तिरतं देष्णैः ॥
verses.transliteration: gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ prá-matim ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ ī́ṭṭe ǀ rayím ǀ yaśásam ǀ pūrva-bhā́jam ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ vṛtra-hanā ǀ su-vajrā ǀ prá ǀ naḥ ǀ návyebhiḥ ǀ tiratam ǀ deṣṇáiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The pious sage, desiring your favour, glorifies you with praises for the sake of formerly enjoyed riches,accompanied by celebrity;Indraand Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, bearers of the thunderbolt, exalt us with preciousdonations.
verses.wilson_translation: The pious sage, desiring your favour, glorifies you with praises for the sake of formerly enjoyed riches,accompanied by celebrity;Indraand Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, bearers of the thunderbolt, exalt us with preciousdonations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सं यन्मही मिथती स्पर्धमाने तनूरुचा शूरसाता यतैते ।अदेवयुं विदथे देवयुभिः सत्रा हतं सोमसुता जनेन ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ yát ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ mithatī́ íti ǀ spárdhamāne íti ǀ tanū-rúcā ǀ śū́ra-sātā ǀ yátaite íti ǀádeva-yum ǀ vidáthe ǀ devayú-bhiḥ ǀ satrā́ ǀ hatam ǀ soma-sútā ǀ jánena ǁ
verses.english_translation: As two large, mutually defiant (armies), emulous in corporal vigour, may contend in war, so do youdestroy, by the devout, those who are not devoted to the gods in sacrifice, and, by the man who presentslibations, (him who does not offer).
verses.wilson_translation: As two large, mutually defiant (armies), emulous in corporal vigour, may contend in war, so do youdestroy, by the devout, those who are not devoted to the gods in sacrifice, and, by the man who presentslibations, (him who does not offer).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमामु षु सोमसुतिमुप न एंद्राग्नी सौमनसाय यातं ।नू चिद्धि परिमम्नाथे अस्माना वां शश्वद्भिर्ववृतीय वाजैः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ sóma-sutim ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ indrāgnī íti ǀ saumanasā́ya ǀ yātam ǀnú ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ parimamnā́the íti pari-mamnā́the ǀ asmā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vām ǀ śáśvat-bhiḥ ǀ vavṛtīya ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come with gracious minds,Indraand Agni, to this our Somalibation; you are never regardless of us,therefore, I propitiate you with constant (sacrificial) viands.
verses.wilson_translation: Come with gracious minds,Indraand Agni, to this our Somalibation; you are never regardless of us,therefore, I propitiate you with constant (sacrificial) viands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सो अग्न एना नमसा समिद्धोऽच्छा मित्रं वरुणमिंद्रं वोचेः ।यत्सीमागश्चकृमा तत्सु मृळ तदर्यमादितिः शिश्रथंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ agne ǀ enā́ ǀ námasā ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ áccha ǀ mitrám ǀ váruṇam ǀ índram ǀ voceḥ ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ cakṛmá ǀ tát ǀ sú ǀ mṛḷa ǀ tát ǀ aryamā́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śiśrathantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Kindled,Agni, by this adoration, do you recommend us to Mitra,Varuṇa, and Indra; whatever sin wemay have committed, do you expiate, and may Aryaman,Aditi(and Mitra) remove it (from us).
verses.wilson_translation: Kindled,Agni, by this adoration, do you recommend us to Mitra,Varuṇa, and Indra; whatever sin wemay have committed, do you expiate, and may Aryaman,Aditi(and Mitra) remove it (from us).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एता अग्न आशुषाणास इष्टीर्युवोः सचाभ्यश्याम वाजान् ।मेंद्रो नो विष्णुर्मरुतः परि ख्यन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ āśuṣāṇā́saḥ ǀ iṣṭī́ḥ ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ sácā ǀ abhí ǀ aśyāma ǀ vā́jān ǀmā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pári ǀ khyan ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Diligently celebrating these rites, may we,Agni, (and Indra), at once arrive at your food; let not Indra,Viṣ.u, the Maruts, abandon us; and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Diligently celebrating these rites, may we,Agni, (and Indra), at once arrive at your food; let not Indra,Viṣ.u, the Maruts, abandon us; and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIV. Indra-Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As rain from out the cloud, for you, Indra and Agni, from my soulThis noblest praise hath been produced. Do ye, O Indra-Agni, hear the singer's call: accept his songs.Ye Rulers, grant his heart's desire. Give us not up to poverty, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, norTo slander and reproach of men. To Indra and to Agni we bring reverence, high and holy hymn,And, craving help, softwords with prayer. For all these holy singers here implore these Twain to succour them,And priests that they may win them strength. Eager to laudyou, we with songs invoke you, bearing sacred food,Fain for success in sacrifice. Indra and Agni, come to us with favour, ye who conquer men:Let not the wicked master us. At no time let the injurious blow of hostile mortal fall on us:O Indra-Agni, shelter us. Whatever wealth we crave of you, in gold, in cattle, or in steeds,That, Indra-Agni, let us gain; When heroes prompt in worship call Indra and Agni, Lords of steeds,Beside the Soma juice effused. Call hither with the song and lauds those who best slay the foemen, thoseWho take delight in hymns of praise. Slay ye the wicked man whose thought is evil of the demon kind.Slay him who stays the waters, slay the Serpent with your deadly dart.

verses.sanskrit: इयं वामस्य मन्मन इंद्राग्नी पूर्व्यस्तुतिः ।अभ्राद्वृष्टिरिवाजनि ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ vām ǀ asyá ǀ mánmanaḥ ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ pūrvyá-stutiḥ ǀabhrā́t ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ-iva ǀ ajani ǁ
verses.english_translation: This chief praise,Indraand Agni, proceeds (copiously) from me your worshipper, like rain from a cloud.
verses.wilson_translation: This chief praise,Indraand Agni, proceeds (copiously) from me your worshipper, like rain from a cloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शृणुतं जरितुर्हवमिंद्राग्नी वनतं गिरः ।ईशाना पिप्यतं धियः ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛṇutám ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ hávam ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ vánatam ǀ gíraḥ ǀīśānā́ ǀ pipyatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear,Indraand Agni, the invocation of the worshipper; accept his adoration. Recompense, lords, hispious acts.
verses.wilson_translation: Hear,Indraand Agni, the invocation of the worshipper; accept his adoration. Recompense, lords, hispious acts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा पापत्वाय नो नरेंद्राग्नी माभिशस्तये ।मा नो रीरधतं निदे ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ pāpa-tvā́ya ǀ naḥ ǀ narā ǀ índrāgnī íti ǀ mā́ ǀ abhí-śastaye ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rīradhatam ǀ nidé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leaders of (rites),Indraand Agni, subject us not to wickedness, nor to calumny, nor to the reviler.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders of (rites),Indraand Agni, subject us not to wickedness, nor to calumny, nor to the reviler.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रे अग्ना नमो बृहत्सुवृक्तिमेरयामहे ।धिया धेना अवस्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: índre ǀ agnā́ ǀ námaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ su-vṛktím ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayāmahe ǀdhiyā́ ǀ dhénāḥ ǀ avasyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desiring protection, we offer copious oblations and praise to Indraand Agni, and prayers with holy rites.
verses.wilson_translation: Desiring protection, we offer copious oblations and praise to Indraand Agni, and prayers with holy rites.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता हि शश्वंत ईळत इत्था विप्रास ऊतये ।सबाधो वाजसातये ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ hí ǀ śáśvantaḥ ǀ ī́ḷate ǀ itthā́ ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀsa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Many are the sages who propitiate (Indraand Agni) in this manner for (their) protection, mutuallystriving for the acquisition of food.
verses.wilson_translation: Many are the sages who propitiate (Indraand Agni) in this manner for (their) protection, mutuallystriving for the acquisition of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता वां गीर्भिर्विपन्यवः प्रयस्वंतो हवामहे ।मेधसाता सनिष्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ vipanyávaḥ ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ havāmahe ǀmedhá-sātā ǀ saniṣyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eager to offer praise, bearing (sacrificial) food, desirous of wealth, we invoke you,Indraand Agni, withpraises, in the celebration of holy acts.
verses.wilson_translation: Eager to offer praise, bearing (sacrificial) food, desirous of wealth, we invoke you,Indraand Agni, withpraises, in the celebration of holy acts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतमस्मभ्यं चर्षणीसहा ।मा नो दुःशंस ईशत ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāgnī íti ǀ ávasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ asmábhyam ǀ carṣaṇi-sahā ǀmā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-śáṃsaḥ ǀ īśata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Overcomers of (hostile) men,Indraand Agni, come wiḥ food (to be bestowed) upon us; let not themalevolent have power over us.
verses.wilson_translation: Overcomers of (hostile) men,Indraand Agni, come wiḥ food (to be bestowed) upon us; let not themalevolent have power over us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा कस्य नो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्यस्य ।इंद्राग्नी शर्म यच्छतं ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ kásya ǀ naḥ ǀ áraruṣaḥ ǀ dhūrtíḥ ǀ práṇak ǀ mártyasya ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the malice of any hostile mortal reach us; gran us,Indraand Agni, felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the malice of any hostile mortal reach us; gran us,Indraand Agni, felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गोमद्धिरण्यवद्वसु यद्वामश्वावदीमहे ।इंद्राग्नी तद्वनेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: gó-mat ǀ híraṇya-vat ǀ vásu ǀ yát ǀ vām ǀ áśva-vat ǀ ī́mahe ǀíndrāgnī íti ǀ tát ǀ vanemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit you both for wealth, comprising cattle, gold and horses; may we obtain it for you,Indraand Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit you both for wealth, comprising cattle, gold and horses; may we obtain it for you,Indraand Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यत्सोम आ सुते नर इंद्राग्नी अजोहवुः ।सप्तीवंता सपर्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ sóme ǀ ā́ ǀ suté ǀ náraḥ ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ ájohavuḥ ǀsápti-vantā ǀ saparyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When adoring leaders (of rites), invoke you two, lords of horses, on the Somabeing offered, (comehither).
verses.wilson_translation: When adoring leaders (of rites), invoke you two, lords of horses, on the Somabeing offered, (comehither).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उक्थेभिर्वृत्रहंतमा या मंदाना चिदा गिरा ।आंगूषैराविवासतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ukthébhiḥ ǀ vṛtrahán-tamā ǀ yā́ ǀ mandānā́ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ girā́ ǀāṅgūṣáiḥ ǀ ā-vívāsataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Utter destroyers of Vṛtra, exhilarated (by the Soma), you who are worshipped with prayers and hymnsand songs, (come hither).
verses.wilson_translation: Utter destroyers of Vṛtra, exhilarated (by the Soma), you who are worshipped with prayers and hymnsand songs, (come hither).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ताविद्दुःशंसं मर्त्यं दुर्विद्वांसं रक्षस्विनं ।आभोगं हन्मना हतमुदधिं हन्मना हतं ॥
verses.transliteration: táu ǀ ít ǀ duḥ-śáṃsam ǀ mártyam ǀ dúḥ-vidvāṃsam ǀ rakṣasvínam ǀā-bhogám ǀ hánmanā ǀ hatam ǀ uda-dhím ǀ hánmanā ǀ hatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroy with your fatal (weapons) the mortal who is malignant, ignorant, strong, rapacious; destroy himlike a water jar, with your weapons.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroy with your fatal (weapons) the mortal who is malignant, ignorant, strong, rapacious; destroy himlike a water jar, with your weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCV. Sarasvatī.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS stream Sarasvatī with fostering current comes forth, our sure defence, our fort of iron.As on a car, the flood flows on, surpassing in majesty and might all other waters. Pure in her course from mountains to the ocean, alone of streams Sarasvatī hath listened.Thinking of wealth and the great world of creatures, she poured for Nahuṣa her milk and fatness. Friendly to man he grew among the women, a strong young Steer amid the Holy Ladies.He gives the fleet steed to our wealthy princes, and decks their bodies for success in battle. May this Sarasvatī be pleased and listen at this our sacrifice, auspicious Lady,When we with reverence, on our knees, implore her close-knit to wealth, most kind to those she loveth. These offerings have ye made with adoration: say this, Sarasvatī, and accept our praises;And, placing us under thy dear protection, may we approach thee, as a tree, for shelter. For thee, O Blest Sarasvatī, Vasiṣṭha hath here unbarred the doors d sacred Order.Wax, Bright One, and give strength to him who lauds thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषा सरस्वती धरुणमायसी पूः ।प्रबाबधाना रथ्येव याति विश्वा अपो महिना सिंधुरन्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ kṣódasā ǀ dhā́yasā ǀ sasre ǀ eṣā́ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ dharúṇam ǀ ā́yasī ǀ pū́ḥ ǀpra-bā́badhānā ǀ rathyā́-iva ǀ yāti ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ anyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Sarasvatī, firm as a city made of metal, flows rapidly with all sustaining water, sweeping away inits might all other waters, as a charioteer (clears the road).
verses.wilson_translation: This Sarasvatī, firm as a city made of metal, flows rapidly with all sustaining water, sweeping away inits might all other waters, as a charioteer (clears the road).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एकाचेतत्सरस्वती नदीनां शुचिर्यती गिरिभ्य आ समुद्रात् ।रायश्चेतंती भुवनस्य भूरेर्घृतं पयो दुदुहे नाहुषाय ॥
verses.transliteration: ékā ǀ acetat ǀ sárasvatī ǀ nadī́nām ǀ śúciḥ ǀ yatī́ ǀ girí-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ samudrā́t ǀrāyáḥ ǀ cétantī ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ bhū́reḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ páyaḥ ǀ duduhe ǀ nā́huṣāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sarasvatī, chief and pure of rivers, flowing from the mountains to the ocean, understood the request of Nahuṣa, and distributing riches among the many existing beings, milked for him butter and water.
verses.wilson_translation: Sarasvatī, chief and pure of rivers, flowing from the mountains to the ocean, understood the request of Nahuṣa, and distributing riches among the many existing beings, milked for him butter and water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स वावृधे नर्यो योषणासु वृषा शिशुर्वृषभो यज्ञियासु ।स वाजिनं मघवद्भ्यो दधाति वि सातये तन्वं मामृजीत ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ náryaḥ ǀ yóṣaṇāsu ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ śíśuḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ yajñíyāsu ǀsáḥ ǀ vājínam ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ dadhāti ǀ ví ǀ sātáye ǀ tanvám ǀ mamṛjīta ǁ
verses.english_translation: The showerer Sarasvat, the friend of man, a showerer (of benefits), even while yet a child, continuallyincreases among his adorable wives (the rains); he bestows upon the affluent (worshippers) a vigorous son; hepurifies their person ns (to fit them) for the reception (of his bounties).
verses.wilson_translation: The showerer Sarasvat, the friend of man, a showerer (of benefits), even while yet a child, continuallyincreases among his adorable wives (the rains); he bestows upon the affluent (worshippers) a vigorous son; hepurifies their person ns (to fit them) for the reception (of his bounties).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणोप श्रवत्सुभगा यज्णे अस्मिन् ।मितज्ञुभिर्नमस्यैरियाना राया युजा चिदुत्तरा सखिभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ juṣāṇā́ ǀ úpa ǀ śravat ǀ su-bhágā ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀmitájñu-bhiḥ ǀ namasyáiḥ ǀ iyānā́ ǀ rāyā́ ǀ yujā́ ǀ cit ǀ út-tarā ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the auspicious and gracious Sarasvatīhear (our praises) at this sacrifice, approached as she iswith reverence and with bended knees, and most liberal to her friends with the riches she possesses.
verses.wilson_translation: May the auspicious and gracious Sarasvatīhear (our praises) at this sacrifice, approached as she iswith reverence and with bended knees, and most liberal to her friends with the riches she possesses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिः प्रति स्तोमं सरस्वति जुषस्व ।तव शर्मन्प्रियतमे दधाना उप स्थेयाम शरणं न वृक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ ǀ júhvānāḥ ǀ yuṣmát ǀ ā́ ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ práti ǀ stómam ǀ sarasvati ǀ juṣasva ǀtáva ǀ śárman ǀ priyá-tame ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ stheyāma ǀ śaraṇám ǀ ná ǀ vṛkṣám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Presenting to you,Sarasvatī, these oblations with reverence (may we receive from you affluence); begratified by our praise and may we, being retained in your dearest felicity, ever recline upon you, as on asheltering tree.
verses.wilson_translation: Presenting to you,Sarasvatī, these oblations with reverence (may we receive from you affluence); begratified by our praise and may we, being retained in your dearest felicity, ever recline upon you, as on asheltering tree.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमु ते सरस्वति वसिष्ठो द्वारावृतस्य सुभगे व्यावः ।वर्ध शुभ्रे स्तुवते रासि वाजान्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ te ǀ sarasvati ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ dvā́rau ǀ ṛtásya ǀ su-bhage ǀ ví ǀ āvarítyāvaḥ ǀvárdha ǀ śubhre ǀ stuvaté ǀ rāsi ǀ vā́jān ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious Sarasvatī, for you Vasiṣṭhahas set open the two doors (the east and west) of sacrifice;white-complexioned (goddess), be magnified; bestow food on him who glorifies you; and do you (gods) evercherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Auspicious Sarasvatī, for you Vasiṣṭhahas set open the two doors (the east and west) of sacrifice;white-complexioned (goddess), be magnified; bestow food on him who glorifies you; and do you (gods) evercherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVI. Sarasvatī.
hymns.anukramani: ६  मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठ:। सरस्वती, ४-६ सरस्वान्  । १-२= प्रगाथ: (१ बृहती, २ सतोबृहती ), ३ प्रस्तारपंक्ति:, ४-६ गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I SING a lofty song, for she is mightiest, most divine of Streams.Sarasvatī will I exalt with hymns and lauds, and, O Vasiṣṭha, Heaven and Earth. When in the fulness of their strength the Pūrus dwell, Beauteous One, on thy two grassy banks,Favour us thou who hast the Maruts for thy friends: stir up the bounty of our chiefs. So may Sarasvatī auspicious send good luck; she, rich in spoil, is never niggardly in thought,When praised in jamadagni's way and lauded as Vasiṣṭha lauds. We call upon Sarasvān, as unmarried men who long for wives,As liberal men who yearn for sons. Be thou our kind protector, O Sarasvān, with those waves of thineLaden with sweets and dropping oil. May we enjoy Sarasvān's breast, all-beautiful, that swells with streams,May we gain food and progeny.

verses.sanskrit: बृहदु गायिषे वचोऽसुर्या नदीनां ।सरस्वतीमिन्महया सुवृक्तिभिः स्तोमैर्वसिष्ठ रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ gāyiṣe ǀ vácaḥ ǀ asuryā́ ǀ nadī́nām ǀsárasvatīm ǀ ít ǀ mahaya ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ vasiṣṭha ǀ ródasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: You chant,Vasiṣṭhaa powerful hymn to her who is the most mighty of rivers; worship, Vasiṣṭha withwell-selected praises,Sarasvatī, who is both in heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: You chant,Vasiṣṭhaa powerful hymn to her who is the most mighty of rivers; worship, Vasiṣṭha withwell-selected praises,Sarasvatī, who is both in heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उभे यत्ते महिना शुभ्रे अंधसी अधिक्षियंति पूरवः ।सा नो बोध्यवित्री मरुत्सखा चोद राधो मघोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ mahinā́ ǀ śubhre ǀ ándhasī íti ǀ adhi-kṣiyánti ǀ pūrávaḥ ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ avitrī́ ǀ marút-sakhā ǀ códa ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ maghónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Beautiful Sarasvatī, inasmuch as by your might men obtain both kinds of food, do you, our protectress,regard us; do you, the friend of the Maruts, bestow riches upon those who are affluent (in oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: Beautiful Sarasvatī, inasmuch as by your might men obtain both kinds of food, do you, our protectress,regard us; do you, the friend of the Maruts, bestow riches upon those who are affluent (in oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रमिद्भद्रा कृणवत्सरस्वत्यकवारी चेतति वाजिनीवती ।गृणाना जमदग्निवत्स्तुवाना च वसिष्ठवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ ít ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ kṛṇavat ǀ sárasvatī ǀ ákava-arī ǀ cetati ǀ vājínī-vatī ǀgṛṇānā́ ǀ jamadagni-vát ǀ stuvānā́ ǀ ca ǀ vasiṣṭha-vát ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the auspicious Sarasvatībestow auspicious fortune upon us; may the faultless-movingfood-conferring (goddess) think of us; glorified (as you have been) by Jamadagnī, (be now) glorified by Vasiṣṭha.
verses.wilson_translation: May the auspicious Sarasvatībestow auspicious fortune upon us; may the faultless-movingfood-conferring (goddess) think of us; glorified (as you have been) by Jamadagnī, (be now) glorified by Vasiṣṭha.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जनीयंतो न्वग्रवः पुत्रीयंतः सुदानवः ।सरस्वंतं हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: jani-yántaḥ ǀ nú ǀ ágravaḥ ǀ putri-yántaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀsárasvantam ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Desiring wives, desiring sons, liberal of donations, approaching him, now worship Sarasvat.
verses.wilson_translation: Desiring wives, desiring sons, liberal of donations, approaching him, now worship Sarasvat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये ते सरस्व ऊर्मयो मधुमंतो घृतश्चुतः ।तेभिर्नोऽविता भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ te ǀ sarasvaḥ ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ ghṛta-ścútaḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ avitā́ ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: With those your waves Sarasvat, which are sweet-tasted, the distributors of water, be our protector.
verses.wilson_translation: With those your waves Sarasvat, which are sweet-tasted, the distributors of water, be our protector.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः स्तनं यो विश्वदर्शतः ।भक्षीमहि प्रजामिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: pīpi-vā́ṃsam ǀ sárasvataḥ ǀ stánam ǀ yáḥ ǀ viśvá-darśataḥ ǀbhakṣīmáhi ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ íṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we recline upon the protuberant breast of Sarasvati. Which is visible to all; that we may possessprogeny and food.
verses.wilson_translation: May we recline upon the protuberant breast of Sarasvati. Which is visible to all; that we may possessprogeny and food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVIL Bṛhaspati.
hymns.anukramani: १०  मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठ:। १ इन्द्र:, २,४-८ बृहस्पति:, ३,९ इन्द्राब्रह्मणस्पती, १० इन्द्राबृहस्पती । त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHERE Heaven and Earth combine in men's assembly, and ttose who love the Gods delight in worship,Where the libations are effused for Indra, may he come first to drink and make him stronger. We crave the heavenly grace of Gods to guard us-so may Bṛhaspati, O friends, exalt us-That he, the Bounteous God, may find us sintess, who giveth from a distance like a father. That Brahmaṇaspati, most High and Gracious, I glorify with offerings and with homage.May the great song of praise divine, reach Indra who is the King of prayer the Gods’ creation. May that Bṛhaspati who brings all blessings, most dearly loved, be seated by our altar.Heroes and wealth we crave; may he bestow them, and bear us safe beyond the men who vex us. To us these Deathless Ones, erst born, have granted this laud of ours which gives the Immortal pleasure.Let us invoke Bṛhaspati, the foeless, the clear-voiced God, the Holy One of households Him, this Bṛhaspati, his red-hued horses, drawing together, full of strength, bring hither.Robed in red colour like the cloud, they carry the Lord of Might whose friendship gives a dwelling. For he is pure, with hundred wings, refulgent, with sword of gold, impetuous, winning sunlight.Sublime Bṛhaspati, easy of access granteth his friends most bountiful refreshment. Both Heaven and Earth, divine, the Deity's Parents, have made Bṛhaspati increase in grandeur.Glorify him, O friends, who merits glory: may he give prayer fair way and easy passage. This, Brahmaṇaspati, is your laudation prayer hath been made to thunderwielding Indra.Favour our songs, wake up our thought and spirit: destroy the godless and our foemen's malice. Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Bṛhaspati, and thou, O Indra.Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञे दिवो नृषदने पृथिव्या नरो यत्र देवयवो मदंति ।इंद्राय यत्र सवनानि सुन्वे गमन्मदाय प्रथमं वयश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñé ǀ diváḥ ǀ nṛ-sádane ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ yátra ǀ deva-yávaḥ ǀ mádanti ǀíndrāya ǀ yátra ǀ sávanāni ǀ sunvé ǀ gámat ǀ mádāya ǀ prathamám ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: At the sacrifice in the dwellings of man upon earth, where the devout leaders of (rites) rejoice, wherethe libations to Indraare poured out, there may he descend before (other gods) from heaven for his exhilaration;(may his) swift (horses approach).
verses.wilson_translation: At the sacrifice in the dwellings of man upon earth, where the devout leaders of (rites) rejoice, wherethe libations to Indraare poured out, there may he descend before (other gods) from heaven for his exhilaration;(may his) swift (horses approach).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ दैव्या वृणीमहेऽवांसि बृहस्पतिर्नो मह आ सखायः ।यथा भवेम मीळ्हुषे अनागा यो नो दाता परावतः पितेव ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dáivyā ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ ávāṃsi ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahe ǀ ā́ ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀyáthā ǀ bhávema ǀ mīḷhúṣe ǀ ánāgāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dātā́ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ pitā́-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us solicit, friends divine protections, for Bṛhaspatiaccepts our (oblations); so may we be withoutoffence towards that showerer (of benefits) whois our benefactor from afar, as a father (of a son).
verses.wilson_translation: Let us solicit, friends divine protections, for Bṛhaspatiaccepts our (oblations); so may we be withoutoffence towards that showerer (of benefits) whois our benefactor from afar, as a father (of a son).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमु ज्येष्ठं नमसा हविर्भिः सुशेवं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं गृणीषे ।इंद्रं श्लोको महि दैव्यः सिषक्तु यो ब्रह्मणो देवकृतस्य राजा ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ námasā ǀ havíḥ-bhiḥ ǀ su-śévam ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátim ǀ gṛṇīṣe ǀíndram ǀ ślókaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ dáivyaḥ ǀ sisaktu ǀ yáḥ ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ devá-kṛtasya ǀ rā́jā ǁ
verses.english_translation: I glorify with homage and with oblations that most excellent and beneficent Brahmaṇaspati; may mypraise worthy of the deity, attain to the mighty Indra, who is the lord of the prayers offered by the devout.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify with homage and with oblations that most excellent and beneficent Brahmaṇaspati; may mypraise worthy of the deity, attain to the mighty Indra, who is the lord of the prayers offered by the devout.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स आ नो योनिं सदतु प्रेष्ठो बृहस्पतिर्विश्ववारो यो अस्ति ।कामो रायः सुवीर्यस्य तं दात्पर्षन्नो अति सश्चतो अरिष्टान् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yónim ǀ sadatu ǀ préṣṭhaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ viśvá-vāraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásti ǀkā́maḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ su-vī́ryasya ǀ tám ǀ dāt ǀ párṣat ǀ naḥ ǀ áti ǀ saścátaḥ ǀ áriṣṭān ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that best beloved Bṛhaspati, who is the desired of all sit down in our hall of sacrifice; may hegratify our desire of riches and ofmaleposterity. Transporting us (at present) embarrassed uninjured beyond(the assaults of enemies).
verses.wilson_translation: May that best beloved Bṛhaspati, who is the desired of all sit down in our hall of sacrifice; may hegratify our desire of riches and ofmaleposterity. Transporting us (at present) embarrassed uninjured beyond(the assaults of enemies).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमा नो अर्कममृताय जुष्टमिमे धासुरमृतासः पुराजाः ।शुचिक्रंदं यजतं पस्त्यानां बृहस्पतिमनर्वाणं हुवेम ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ arkám ǀ amṛ́tāya ǀ júṣṭam ǀ imé ǀ dhāsuḥ ǀ amṛ́tāsaḥ ǀ purā-jā́ḥ ǀśúci-krandam ǀ yajatám ǀ pastyā́nām ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ anarvā́ṇam ǀ huvema ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the first-born immortals (by his command) bestow upon us the food that is necessary for existence;let us invoke the unresisted Bṛhaspati, to whom pure praises are addressed, he adored of householder.
verses.wilson_translation: May the first-born immortals (by his command) bestow upon us the food that is necessary for existence;let us invoke the unresisted Bṛhaspati, to whom pure praises are addressed, he adored of householder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं शग्मासो अरुषासो अश्वा बृहस्पतिं सहवाहो वहंति ।सहश्चिद्यस्य नीलवत्सधस्थं नभो न रूपमरुषं वसानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ śagmā́saḥ ǀ aruṣā́saḥ ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ saha-vā́haḥ ǀ vahanti ǀsáhaḥ ǀ cit ǀ yásya ǀ nī́la-vat ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ nábhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rūpám ǀ aruṣám ǀ vásānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May his powerful brilliant horses, wearing a lustrous form like (that of) the sun, acting together, bring(hither) that Bṛhaspai, in whom strength abides like that of a substantial mansion.
verses.wilson_translation: May his powerful brilliant horses, wearing a lustrous form like (that of) the sun, acting together, bring(hither) that Bṛhaspai, in whom strength abides like that of a substantial mansion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स हि शुचिः शतपत्रः स शुंध्युर्हिरण्यवाशीरिषिरः स्वर्षाः ।बृहस्पतिः स स्वावेश ऋष्वः पुरू सखिभ्य आसुतिं करिष्ठः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ śúciḥ ǀ śatá-patraḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ śundhyúḥ ǀ híraṇya-vāśīḥ ǀ iṣiráḥ ǀ svaḥ-sā́ḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ su-āveśáḥ ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀ purú ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ ā-sutím ǀ káriṣṭhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He verily is pure, borne by numerous conveyances, he is the purifier armed with golden weapons, theobject of desire, the enjoyer of heaven; he,Bṛhaspatiis well domiciled, of goodly aspect, a most bountiful giverof ample food to his friend.
verses.wilson_translation: He verily is pure, borne by numerous conveyances, he is the purifier armed with golden weapons, theobject of desire, the enjoyer of heaven; he,Bṛhaspatiis well domiciled, of goodly aspect, a most bountiful giverof ample food to his friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: देवी देवस्य रोदसी जनित्री बृहस्पतिं वावृधतुर्महित्वा ।दक्षाय्याय दक्षता सखायः करद्ब्रह्मणे सुतरा सुगाधा ॥
verses.transliteration: devī́ íti ǀ devásya ǀ ródasī íti ǀ jánitrī íti ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ vavṛdhatuḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀdakṣā́yyāya ǀ dakṣata ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ kárat ǀ bráhmaṇe ǀ su-tárā ǀ su-gādhā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The divine heaven and earth, the genitive ratrices of the deity have by their might, given growth to Bṛhaspati; magnify, friends, the magnifiable, and may he render (the waters) easy to be crossed and forded for(the attainment of) food.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine heaven and earth, the genitive ratrices of the deity have by their might, given growth to Bṛhaspati; magnify, friends, the magnifiable, and may he render (the waters) easy to be crossed and forded for(the attainment of) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इयं वां ब्रह्मणस्पते सुवृक्तिर्ब्रह्मेंद्राय वज्रिणे अकारि ।अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्जजस्तमर्यो वनुषामरातीः ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ vām ǀ brahmaṇaḥ ǀ pate ǀ su-vṛktíḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ índrāya ǀ vajríṇe ǀ akāri ǀaviṣṭám ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ jigṛtám ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ jajastám ǀ aryáḥ ǀ vanúṣām ǀ árātīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This praise has been offered as prayer to you both,Brahmaṇaspatiand Indra, the wielder of thethunderbolt; protect our ceremonies; hear our manifold praise; annihilate the assailing adversaries of yourworshippers.
verses.wilson_translation: This praise has been offered as prayer to you both,Brahmaṇaspatiand Indra, the wielder of thethunderbolt; protect our ceremonies; hear our manifold praise; annihilate the assailing adversaries of yourworshippers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्वो दिव्यस्येशाथे उत पार्थिवस्य ।धत्तं रयिं स्तुवते कीरये चिद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ yuvám ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ divyásya ǀ īśāthe íti ǀ utá ǀ pā́rthivasya ǀdhattám ǀ rayím ǀ stuvaté ǀ kīráye ǀ cit ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You two,Bṛhaspatiand Indraare lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasure; grant riches to theworshipper who praises you; and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: You two,Bṛhaspatiand Indraare lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasure; grant riches to theworshipper who praises you; and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PRIESTS, offer to the Lord of all the people the milked-out stalk of Soma, radiant-coloured.No wild-bull knows his drinking-place like Indra who ever seeks him who hath pressed the Soma, Thou dost desire to drink, each day that passes, the pleasant food which thou hast had aforetime,O Indra, gratified in heart and spirit, drink eagerly the Soma set before thee. Thou, newly-born, for strength didst drink the Soma; the Mother told thee of thy future greatness.O Indra, thou hast filled mid-air's wide region, and given the Gods by battle room and freedom. When thou hast urged the arrocrant to combat, proud in their strength of arm, we will subdue them.Or, Indra, when thou fightest girt by heroes, we in the glorious fray with thee will conquer. I will declare the earliest deeds of Indra, and recent acts which Maghavan hath accomplished.When he had conquered godless wiles and magic, Soma became his own entire possession. Thine is this world of flocks and herds around thee, which with the eye of Sūrya thou beholdest.Thou, Indra, art alone the Lord of cattle; may we enjoy the treasure which thou givest. Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Bṛhaspati, and thou, O Indra.Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्यवोऽरुणं दुग्धमंशुं जुहोतन वृषभाय क्षितीनां ।गौराद्वेदीयाँ अवपानमिंद्रो विश्वाहेद्याति सुतसोममिच्छन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhvaryavaḥ ǀ aruṇám ǀ dugdhám ǀ aṃśúm ǀ juhótana ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀgaurā́t ǀ védīyān ǀ ava-pā́nam ǀ índraḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ ít ǀ yāti ǀ sutá-somam ǀ icchán ǁ
