verses.english_translation: Come like a thirsty deer to the watering plural ce, drink at will of the Soma, whence, daily driving down theclouds, you sustain,Maghavan, most vigorous strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Come like a thirsty deer to the watering plural ce, drink at will of the Soma, whence, daily driving down theclouds, you sustain,Maghavan, most vigorous strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्यो द्रावया त्वं सोममिंद्रः पिपासति ।उप नूनं युयुजे वृषणा हरी आ च जगाम वृत्रहा ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhvaryo íti ǀ draváya ǀ tvám ǀ sómam ǀ índraḥ ǀ pipāsati ǀúpa ǀ nūnám ǀ yuyuje ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ hárī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ jagāma ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Quickly, priest, pour forth the Soma, for Indrais thirsty; verily he has harnessed his vigorous steeds, theslayer of Vṛtra hasarrived.
verses.wilson_translation: Quickly, priest, pour forth the Soma, for Indrais thirsty; verily he has harnessed his vigorous steeds, theslayer of Vṛtra hasarrived.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्वयं चित्स मन्यते दाशुरिर्जनो यत्रा सोमस्य तृंपसि ।इदं ते अन्नं युज्यं समुक्षितं तस्येहि प्र द्रवा पिब ॥
verses.transliteration: svayám ǀ cit ǀ sáḥ ǀ manyate ǀ dā́śuriḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ sómasya ǀ tṛmpási ǀidám ǀ te ǀ ánnam ǀ yújyam ǀ sám-ukṣitam ǀ tásya ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ prá ǀ drava ǀ píba ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man who is the donor (of the oblation), he with (the gift of whose) libation you are satisfied,possesses of himself understanding; this your appropriate food is ready; come, hasten, drink of it.
verses.wilson_translation: The man who is the donor (of the oblation), he with (the gift of whose) libation you are satisfied,possesses of himself understanding; this your appropriate food is ready; come, hasten, drink of it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथेष्ठायाध्वर्यवः सोममिंद्राय सोतन ।अधि ब्रध्नस्याद्रयो वि चक्षते सुन्वंतो दाश्वध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: rathe-sthā́ya ǀ adhvaryavaḥ ǀ sómam ǀ índrāya ǀ sotana ǀádhi ǀ bradhnásya ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakṣate ǀ sunvántaḥ ǀ dāśú-adhvaram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pour our, priests, the Somalibation to Indrain his chariot; the stones, plural ced upon their bases, arebeheld effusing the Soma for the sacrifice of the offerer.
verses.wilson_translation: Pour our, priests, the Somalibation to Indrain his chariot; the stones, plural ced upon their bases, arebeheld effusing the Soma for the sacrifice of the offerer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उप ब्रध्नं वावाता वृषणा हरी इंद्रमपसु वक्षतः ।अर्वांचं त्वा सप्तयोऽध्वरश्रियो वहंतु सवनेदुप ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ bradhnám ǀ vavā́tā ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ hárī íti ǀ índram ǀ apá-su ǀ vakṣataḥ ǀarvā́ñcam ǀ tvā ǀ sáptayaḥ ǀ adhvara-śríyaḥ ǀ váhantu ǀ sávanā ǀ ít ǀ úpa ǁ
verses.english_translation: May his vigorous horses, repeatedly traversing the firmament, bring Indrato our rites; may your steeds,glorious through sacrifice, bring you indeed to the (daily) ceremonials.
verses.wilson_translation: May his vigorous horses, repeatedly traversing the firmament, bring Indrato our rites; may your steeds,glorious through sacrifice, bring you indeed to the (daily) ceremonials.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र पूषणं वृणीमहे युज्याय पुरूवसुं ।स शक्र शिक्ष पुरुहूत नो धिया तुजे राये विमोचन ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ yújyāya ǀ puru-vásum ǀsáḥ ǀ śakra ǀ śikṣa ǀ puru-hūta ǀ naḥ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ túje ǀ rāyé ǀ vi-mocana ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have recourse to the opulent Pūṣanfor his alliance; do you,Śakra, the adored of many, theliberator (from iniquity), enable us to acquire by our intelligence, wealth and victory.
verses.wilson_translation: We have recourse to the opulent Pūṣanfor his alliance; do you,Śakra, the adored of many, theliberator (from iniquity), enable us to acquire by our intelligence, wealth and victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सं नः शिशीहि भुरिजोरिव क्षुरं रास्व रायो विमोचन ।त्वे तन्नः सुवेदमुस्रियं वसु यं त्वं हिनोषि मर्त्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ naḥ ǀ śiśīhi ǀ bhuríjoḥ-iva ǀ kṣurám ǀ rā́sva ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ vi-mocana ǀtvé íti ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ su-védam ǀ usríyam ǀ vásu ǀ yám ǀ tvám ǀ hinóṣi ǀ mártyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sharpen us like a razor in thehands(of a barber); grant us riches, liberator (from iniquity), the wealth ofcattle easily obtained by us from you, such wealth as you bestow upon the (pious) mortal.
verses.wilson_translation: Sharpen us like a razor in thehands(of a barber); grant us riches, liberator (from iniquity), the wealth ofcattle easily obtained by us from you, such wealth as you bestow upon the (pious) mortal.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वेमि त्वा पूषन्नृंजसे वेमि स्तोतव आघृणे ।न तस्य वेम्यरणं हि तद्वसो स्तुषे पज्राय साम्ने ॥
verses.transliteration: vémi ǀ tvā ǀ pūṣan ǀ ṛñjáse ǀ vémi ǀ stótave ǀ āghṛṇe ǀná ǀ tásya ǀ vemi ǀ áraṇam ǀ hí ǀ tát ǀ vaso íti ǀ stuṣé ǀ pajrā́ya ǀ sā́mne ǁ
verses.english_translation: I desire,Pūṣan, to propitiate you; I desire, illustrious deity, to glorify you; I desire not (to offer)ungracious praise to any other; (grant riches), bestower of wealth, to him who praises, eulogizes, and glorifiesyou.
verses.wilson_translation: I desire,Pūṣan, to propitiate you; I desire, illustrious deity, to glorify you; I desire not (to offer)ungracious praise to any other; (grant riches), bestower of wealth, to him who praises, eulogizes, and glorifiesyou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: परा गावो यवसं कच्चिदाघृणे नित्यं रेक्णो अमर्त्य ।अस्माकं पूषन्नविता शिवो भव मंहिष्ठो वाजसातये ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ yávasam ǀ kát ǀ cit ǀ āghṛṇe ǀ nítyam ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ amartya ǀasmā́kam ǀ pūṣan ǀ avitā́ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ máṃhiṣṭhaḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Illustrious (Pūṣan), my cattle go forth occasionally to pasture, may that wealth (of herds), immortaldeity, be permanent; being my protector, Pūṣan, be the granter of felicity, be most bountiful in bestowing food.
verses.wilson_translation: Illustrious (Pūṣan), my cattle go forth occasionally to pasture, may that wealth (of herds), immortaldeity, be permanent; being my protector, Pūṣan, be the granter of felicity, be most bountiful in bestowing food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्थूरं राधः शताश्वं कुरुंगस्य दिविष्टिषु ।राज्ञस्त्वेषस्य सुभगस्य रातिषु तुर्वशेष्वमन्महि ॥
verses.transliteration: sthūrám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ śatá-aśvam ǀ kuruṅgásya ǀ díviṣṭiṣu ǀrā́jñaḥ ǀ tveṣásya ǀ su-bhágasya ǀ rātíṣu ǀ turváśeṣu ǀ amanmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We acknowledge the substantial wealth (of the gift) of a hundred horses, the donation made to usamong men at the holy solemnities of the illustrious and auspicious RājāKuruṅga.
verses.wilson_translation: We acknowledge the substantial wealth (of the gift) of a hundred horses, the donation made to usamong men at the holy solemnities of the illustrious and auspicious RājāKuruṅga.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धीभिः सातानि काण्वस्य वाजिनः प्रियमेधैरभिद्युभिः ।षष्टिं सहस्रानु निर्मजामजे निर्यूथानि गवामृषिः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhībhíḥ ǀ sātā́ni ǀ kāṇvásya ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ priyá-medhaiḥ ǀ abhídyu-bhiḥ ǀṣaṣṭím ǀ sahásrā ǀ ánu ǀ níḥ-majām ǀ aje ǀ níḥ ǀ yūthā́ni ǀ gávām ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I, the Ṛṣi (Devātithi), have received subsequently the complete donation; the sixty thousand herds ofpure cattle merited by the devotions of the pious son of Kaṇva, and by the illustrious Priyamedhas.
verses.wilson_translation: I, the Ṛṣi (Devātithi), have received subsequently the complete donation; the sixty thousand herds ofpure cattle merited by the devotions of the pious son of Kaṇva, and by the illustrious Priyamedhas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृक्षाश्चिन्मे अभिपित्वे अरारणुः ।गां भजंत मेहनाश्वं भजंत मेहना ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛkṣā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ me ǀ abhi-pitvé ǀ araraṇuḥ ǀgā́m ǀ bhajanta ǀ mehánā ǀ áśvam ǀ bhajanta ǀ mehánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Upon the acceptance of this donation to me, the very trees have exclaimed; (see these ṛṣis) haveacquired excellent cows excellent horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Upon the acceptance of this donation to me, the very trees have exclaimed; (see these ṛṣis) haveacquired excellent cows excellent horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN V. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: ३९ ब्रह्मातिथि: काण्व: ।अश्विनौ, ३७ ( उत्तरार्धस्य ) – ३९ चैद्य: कशु: । गायत्री, ३७ -३८  बृहती , ३९ अनुष्टुप्  ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHEN, even as she were present here, red Dawn hath shone from far away,She spreadeth light on every side. Like Heroes on your will-yoked car farshining, Wonder-Workers! yeAttend, O Aśvins, on the Dawn. By you, O Lords of ample wealth our songs of praise have been observed:As envoy have I brought the prayer. Kaṇvas must praise the Aśvins dear to many, making many glad,Most rich, that they may succour us. Most liberal, best at winning strength, inciters, Lords of splendour whoVisit the worshipper's abode. So for devout Sudeva dew with fatness his unfailing mead,And make it rich for sacrifice. Hitherward running speedily with horses, as with rapid hawks,Come, Aśvins, to our song of praise Wherewith the three wide distances, and all the lights that are in heaven.Ye traverse, and three times of night. O Finders of the Day, that we may win us food of kine and wealth,Open the paths for us to tread. O Aśvins, bring us wealth in kine, in noble heroes, and in cars:Bring us the strength that horses give. Ye Lords of splendour, glorified, ye Wonder-Workers borne on pathsOf gold, drink sweets with Somajuice. To us, ye Lords of ample wealth, and to our wealth chiefs extendWide shelter, ne’er to be assailed. Come quickly downward to the prayer of people whom ye favour most:Approach not unto other folk. Ye Aśvins whom our minds perceive, drink of this lovely gladdening draught,The mcath which we present to you. Bring riches hither unto us in hundreds and in thousands, sourceOf plenteous food, sustaining all. Verily sages call on you, ye Heroes, in full many a place.Moved by the priests, O Aśvins, conic. Men who have trimmed the sacred grass, bringing oblations and prepared,O Aśvins, are invoking you. May this our hymn of praise to-day, most powerful to bring you, be,O Aśvins, nearest to your hearts. The skin filled full of savoury meath, laid in the pathway of your car-O Aśvins, drink ye both therefrom. For this, ye Lords of ample wealth, bring blessing for our herd, our kine,Our progeny, and plenteous food. Ye too unclose to us like doors the strengthening waters of the sky,And rivers, ye who find the day. When did the son of Tugra serve you, Men? Abandoned in the sea,That with winged steeds your car might fly. Ye, O Nāsatyas, ministered to Kaṇva with repeated aid,When cast into the heated pit. Come near with those most recent aids of yours which merit eulogy,When I invoke you, Wealthy Gods. As ye protected Kaṇva erst, Priyamedha and Upastuta,Atri, Sinjara, Aśvins Twain And Amsu in decisive fight, Agastya in the fray for kine.And, in his battles, Sobhari. For so much bliss, or even more, O Aśvins, Wealthy Gods, than this,We pray white singing hymns to you. Ascend your car with golden seat, O Aśvins, and with reins of gold,That reaches even to the sky. Golden is its supporting shaft, the axle also is of gold,And both the wheels are made of gold. Thereon, ye Lords of ample wealth, come to us even from afar,Come ye to this mine eulogy. From far away ye come to us, Aśvins, enjoying plenteous foodOf Dāsas, O Immortal Ones. With splendour, riches, and renown, O Aśvins, hither come to us,Nāsatyas, shining brilliantly. May dappled horses, steeds who fly with pinions, bring you hitherwardTo people skilled in sacrifice. The whcel delayeth not that car of yours accompanied by song,That cometh with a store of food. Borne on that chariot wrought of gold, with coursers very fleet of foot,Come, O Nāsatyas, swift as thought. O Wealthy Gods, ye taste and find the brisk and watchful wild beast good.Associate wealth with food for us. As such, O Aśvins, find for me my share of new-presented gifts,As Kasu, Cedi's son, gave me a hundred head of buffaloes, and ten thousand kine. He who hath given me for mine own ten Kings like gold to look upon.At Caidya's feet are all the people round about, all those who think upon the shield. No man, not any, goes upon the path on which the Cedis walk.No other prince, no folk is held more liberal of gifts than they.

verses.sanskrit: दूरादिहेव यत्सत्यरुणप्सुरशिश्वितत् ।वि भानुं विश्वधातनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: dūrā́t ǀ ihá-iva ǀ yát ǀ satī́ ǀ aruṇá-psuḥ ǀ áśiśvitat ǀví ǀ bhānúm ǀ viśvádhā ǀ atanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the shining dawn, advancing hither from afar, whitens (all things), she spreads the light on allsides.
verses.wilson_translation: When the shining dawn, advancing hither from afar, whitens (all things), she spreads the light on allsides.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नृवद्दस्रा मनोयुजा रथेन पृथुपाजसा ।सचेथे अश्विनोषसं ॥
verses.transliteration: nṛ-vát ǀ dasrā ǀ manaḥ-yújā ǀ ráthena ǀ pṛthu-pā́jasā ǀsácethe íti ǀ aśvinā ǀ uṣásam ǁ
verses.english_translation: And you,Aśvins, of goodly aspect, accompany the dawn like leader with your mighty chariot harnessedat a thought.
verses.wilson_translation: And you,Aśvins, of goodly aspect, accompany the dawn like leader with your mighty chariot harnessedat a thought.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवाभ्यां वाजिनीवसू प्रति स्तोमा अदृक्षत ।वाचं दूतो यथोहिषे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́bhyām ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǀ práti ǀ stómāḥ ǀ adṛkṣata ǀvā́cam ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ohiṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: By you, affluent in sacrifices, may our praises be severally accepted; I bear the words (of theworshipper) like a messenger (to you).
verses.wilson_translation: By you, affluent in sacrifices, may our praises be severally accepted; I bear the words (of theworshipper) like a messenger (to you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुप्रिया ण ऊतये पुरुमंद्रा पुरूवसू ।स्तुषे कण्वासो अश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-priyā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ puru-mandrā́ ǀ puruvásū íti puru-vásū ǀstuṣé ǀ káṇvāsaḥ ǀ aśvínā ǁ
verses.english_translation: We,Kaṇvas, praise for our protection the many-loved, the many- delighting Aśvins, abounding inwealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We,Kaṇvas, praise for our protection the many-loved, the many- delighting Aśvins, abounding inwealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मंहिष्ठा वाजसातमेषयंता शुभस्पती ।गंतारा दाशुषो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: máṃhiṣṭhā ǀ vāja-sā́tamā ǀ iṣáyantā ǀ śubháḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀgántārā ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most adorable bestowwers of strength, distributors of food, lords of opulence, repairers to the dwellingof the donor (of the oblation).
verses.wilson_translation: Most adorable bestowwers of strength, distributors of food, lords of opulence, repairers to the dwellingof the donor (of the oblation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता सुदेवाय दाशुषे सुमेधामवितारिणीं ।घृतैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ su-devā́ya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ su-medhā́m ǀ ávi-tāriṇīm ǀghṛtáiḥ ǀ gávyūtim ǀ ukṣatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sprinkle well with water the pure unfailing pasturage (of his cattle) for the devout donor (of theoblation).
verses.wilson_translation: Sprinkle well with water the pure unfailing pasturage (of his cattle) for the devout donor (of theoblation).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नः स्तोममुप द्रवत्तूयं श्येनेभिराशुभिः ।यातमश्वेभिरश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ stómam ǀ úpa ǀ dravát ǀ tū́yam ǀ śyenébhiḥ ǀ āśú-bhiḥ ǀyātám ǀ áśvebhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come,Aśvins, to our adoration, hastening quickly with your rapid falcon-like horses.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Aśvins, to our adoration, hastening quickly with your rapid falcon-like horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: येभिस्तिस्रः परावतो दिवो विश्वानि रोचना ।त्रीँरक्तून्परिदीयथः ॥
verses.transliteration: yébhiḥ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ rocanā́ ǀtrī́n ǀ aktū́n ǀ pari-dī́yathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With which in three days and three nights you traverse from afar all the brilliant (constellations).
verses.wilson_translation: With which in three days and three nights you traverse from afar all the brilliant (constellations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो गोमतीरिष उत सातीरहर्विदा ।वि पथः सातये सितं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ gó-matīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ utá ǀ sātī́ḥ ǀ ahaḥ-vidā ǀví ǀ patháḥ ǀ sātáye ǀ sitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bringers of the day, (bestow) upon us food with cattle, or donations of wealth, and close the path(against aggression) upon our gains.
verses.wilson_translation: Bringers of the day, (bestow) upon us food with cattle, or donations of wealth, and close the path(against aggression) upon our gains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो गोमंतमश्विना सुवीरं सुरथं रयिं ।वोळ्हमश्वावतीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ gó-mantam ǀ aśvinā ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ su-rátham ǀ rayím ǀvoḷhám ǀ áśva-vatīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring to us,Aśvins, riches comprising cattle,maleoffspring, chariots, horses, food.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring to us,Aśvins, riches comprising cattle,maleoffspring, chariots, horses, food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वावृधाना शुभस्पती दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी ।पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
verses.transliteration: vavṛdhānā́ ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ dásrā ǀ híraṇyavartanī íti híraṇya-vartanī ǀpíbatam ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Magnificent lords of good fortune, handsome Aśvins, riding in a golden chariot, drink the sweet Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Magnificent lords of good fortune, handsome Aśvins, riding in a golden chariot, drink the sweet Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मभ्यं वाजिनीवसू मघवद्भ्यश्च सप्रथः ।छर्दिर्यंतमदाभ्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmábhyam ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǀ maghávat-bhyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀchardíḥ ǀ yantam ǀ ádābhyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent i sacrifices, grant to us who are opulent (in oblations) a spacious unassailable dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent i sacrifices, grant to us who are opulent (in oblations) a spacious unassailable dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि षु ब्रह्म जनानां याविष्टं तूयमा गतं ।मो ष्वन्याँ उपारतं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ sú ǀ bráhma ǀ jánānām ǀ yā́ ǀ áviṣṭam ǀ tū́yam ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀmó íti ǀ sú ǀ anyā́n ǀ úpa ǀ aratam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you ever carefully protect the Brahmanamong men, come quickly; tarry not with other(worshippers).
verses.wilson_translation: Do you ever carefully protect the Brahmanamong men, come quickly; tarry not with other(worshippers).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य पिबतमश्विना युवं मदस्य चारुणः ।मध्वो रातस्य धिष्ण्या ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ pibatam ǀ aśvinā ǀ yuvám ǀ mádasya ǀ cā́ruṇaḥ ǀmádhvaḥ ǀ rātásya ǀ dhiṣṇyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adorable Aśvins, drink of this exhilarating, delightful, sweet Soma, presented by us.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable Aśvins, drink of this exhilarating, delightful, sweet Soma, presented by us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे आ वहतं रयिं शतवंतं सहस्रिणं ।पुरुक्षुं विश्वधायसं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ vahatam ǀ rayím ǀ śatá-vantam ǀ sahasríṇam ǀpuru-kṣúm ǀ viśvá-dhāyasam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring unto us riches by hundreds and by thousands, desired by many, sustaining all.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring unto us riches by hundreds and by thousands, desired by many, sustaining all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुत्रा चिद्धि वां नरा विह्वयंते मनीषिणः ।वाघद्भिरश्विना गतं ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-trā́ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ vi-hváyante ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀvāghát-bhiḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Leaders (of rites), wise men worship you in many plural ces; come to us with your steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of rites), wise men worship you in many plural ces; come to us with your steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषो हविष्मंतो अरंकृतः ।युवां हवंते अश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: jánāsaḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣaḥ ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ aram-kṛ́taḥ ǀyuvā́m ǀ havante ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men bearing the clipped sacred grass, presenting oblations, and completely fulfilling (their functions),worship you,Aśvin.
verses.wilson_translation: Men bearing the clipped sacred grass, presenting oblations, and completely fulfilling (their functions),worship you,Aśvin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमद्य वामयं स्तोमो वाहिष्ठो अंतमः ।युवाभ्यां भूत्वश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ adyá ǀ vām ǀ ayám ǀ stómaḥ ǀ vā́hiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀyuvā́bhyām ǀ bhūtu ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this our praise today be conveyed successfully to you,Aśvins, and be most near to you.
verses.wilson_translation: May this our praise today be conveyed successfully to you,Aśvins, and be most near to you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो ह वां मधुनो दृतिराहितो रथचर्षणे ।ततः पिबतमश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ha ǀ vām ǀ mádhunaḥ ǀ dṛ́tiḥ ǀ ā́-hitaḥ ǀ ratha-cárṣaṇe ǀtátaḥ ǀ pibatam ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink,Aśvins, from the skin (filled) with the sweet (Soma) which is suspended in view of your car.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Aśvins, from the skin (filled) with the sweet (Soma) which is suspended in view of your car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तेन नो वाजिनीवसू पश्वे तोकाय शं गवे ।वहतं पीवरीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: téna ǀ naḥ ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǀ páśve ǀ tokā́ya ǀ śám ǀ gáve ǀváhatam ǀ pī́varīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent in oblations, bring to us with that (chariot) abundant food, so that there may be prosperity inhorses, progeny, and cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent in oblations, bring to us with that (chariot) abundant food, so that there may be prosperity inhorses, progeny, and cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो दिव्या इष उत सिंधूँरहर्विदा ।अप द्वारेव वर्षथः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ divyā́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ utá ǀ síndhūn ǀ ahaḥ-vidā ǀápa ǀ dvā́rā-iva ǀ varṣathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bringers of the day, you rain upon us by the (open) door (of the clouds) the waters of heaven, or (withthem fill) the rivers.
verses.wilson_translation: Bringers of the day, you rain upon us by the (open) door (of the clouds) the waters of heaven, or (withthem fill) the rivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कदा वां तौग्र्यो विधत्समुद्रे जहितो नरा ।यद्वां रथो विभिष्पतात् ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ vām ǀ taugryáḥ ǀ vidhat ǀ samudré ǀ jahitáḥ ǀ narā ǀyát ǀ vām ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ ví-bhiḥ ǀ pátāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: When did the son of Tugra, thrown into the ocean, glorify you, leaders (of rites)? then when yourchariot and horses descended.
verses.wilson_translation: When did the son of Tugra, thrown into the ocean, glorify you, leaders (of rites)? then when yourchariot and horses descended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवं कण्वाय नासत्या ऋपिरिप्ताय हर्म्ये ।शश्वदूतीर्दशस्यथः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ káṇvāya ǀ nāsatyā ǀ ápi-riptāya ǀ harmyé ǀśáśvat ǀ ūtī́ḥ ǀ daśasyathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: to Kaṇvawhen blinded (by the Asuras) in his dwelling, you rendered, Na-satyās, effectual aiḍ
verses.wilson_translation: to Kaṇvawhen blinded (by the Asuras) in his dwelling, you rendered, Na-satyās, effectual aiḍ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ताभिरा यातमूतिभिर्नव्यसीभिः सुशस्तिभिः ।यद्वां वृषण्वसू हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ návyasībhiḥ ǀ suśastí-bhiḥ ǀyát ǀ vām ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀ huvé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich in showers, come with your newest and most excellent protections when I call upon you.
verses.wilson_translation: Rich in showers, come with your newest and most excellent protections when I call upon you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा चित्कण्वमावतं प्रियमेधमुपस्तुतं ।अत्रिं शिंजारमश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ cit ǀ káṇvam ǀ ā́vatam ǀ priyá-medham ǀ upa-stutám ǀátrim ǀ śiñjā́ram ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: In like manner as you protected Kaṇva,Priyamedha, Upastuta, and the praise-repeating Atri.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as you protected Kaṇva,Priyamedha, Upastuta, and the praise-repeating Atri.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथोत कृत्व्ये धनेऽंशुं गोष्वगस्त्यं ।यथा वाजेषु सोभरिं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ utá ǀ kṛ́tvye ǀ dháne ǀ aṃśúm ǀ góṣu ǀ agástyam ǀyáthā ǀ vā́jeṣu ǀ sóbharim ǁ
verses.english_translation: And in like manner as (you protected) Anshu when wealth was to be bestowed, and Agastyawhen hiscattle (were to be recovered), and Sobhari when food (was to be supplied to him).
verses.wilson_translation: And in like manner as (you protected) Anshu when wealth was to be bestowed, and Agastyawhen hiscattle (were to be recovered), and Sobhari when food (was to be supplied to him).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एतावद्वां वृषण्वसू अतो वा भूयो अश्विना ।गृणंतः सुम्नमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́vat ǀ vām ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀ átaḥ ǀ vā ǀ bhū́yaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀgṛṇántaḥ ǀ sumnám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: So pariasing you,Aśvins, rich in showers, we solicit of you happiness as great or greater than that(which they obtained).
verses.wilson_translation: So pariasing you,Aśvins, rich in showers, we solicit of you happiness as great or greater than that(which they obtained).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथं हिरण्यवंधुरं हिरण्याभीशुमश्विना ।आ हि स्थाथो दिविस्पृशं ॥
verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ híraṇya-vandhuram ǀ híraṇya-abhīśum ǀ aśvinā ǀā́ ǀ hí ǀ sthā́thaḥ ǀ divi-spṛ́śam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ascend,Aśvins, your sky-touching chariot with a golden seat and golden reins.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend,Aśvins, your sky-touching chariot with a golden seat and golden reins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्ययी वां रभिरीषा अक्षो हिरण्ययः ।उभा चक्रा हिरण्यया ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyáyīm ǀ vām ǀ rábhiḥ ǀ īṣā́ ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ hiraṇyáyaḥ ǀubhā́ ǀ cakrā́ ǀ hiraṇyáyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Golden is its supporting shaft, golden the axle, golden both the wheels.
verses.wilson_translation: Golden is its supporting shaft, golden the axle, golden both the wheels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तेन नो वाजिनीवसू परावतश्चिदा गतं ।उपेमां सुष्टुतिं मम ॥
verses.transliteration: téna ǀ naḥ ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀúpa ǀ imā́m ǀ su-stutím ǀ máma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us, affluent in sacrifices, from afar, come to this mine adoration.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us, affluent in sacrifices, from afar, come to this mine adoration.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वहेथे पराकात्पूर्वीरश्नंतावश्विना ।इषो दासीरमर्त्या ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vahethe íti ǀ parākā́t ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ aśnántau ǀ aśvinā ǀíṣaḥ ǀ dā́sīḥ ǀ amartyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Immortal Aśvins, destroyers of the cities of the Dāsas, you bring to us food from afar.
verses.wilson_translation: Immortal Aśvins, destroyers of the cities of the Dāsas, you bring to us food from afar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो द्युम्नैरा श्रवोभिरा राया यातमश्विना ।पुरुश्चंद्रा नासत्या ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ dyumnáiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ śrávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ rāyā́ ǀ yātam ǀ aśvinā ǀpúru-candrā ǀ nā́satyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us,Aśvins, with food, with fame, with riches,Nāsatyās, delighters of many.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us,Aśvins, with food, with fame, with riches,Nāsatyās, delighters of many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एह वां प्रुषितप्सवो वयो वहंतु पर्णिनः ।अच्छा स्वध्वरं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ vām ǀ pruṣitá-psavaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ vahantu ǀ parṇínaḥ ǀáccha ǀ su-adhvarám ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let your sleek, winged, rapid (horses) bring you to the presence of the man offering holy sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Let your sleek, winged, rapid (horses) bring you to the presence of the man offering holy sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथं वामनुगायसं य इषा वर्तते सह ।न चक्रमभि बाधते ॥
verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ vām ǀ ánu-gāyasam ǀ yáḥ ǀ iṣā́ ǀ vártate ǀ sahá ǀná ǀ cakrám ǀ abhí ǀ bādhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: No hostile force arrests that car of yours which is hymned (by the devout), and which is laden with food.
verses.wilson_translation: No hostile force arrests that car of yours which is hymned (by the devout), and which is laden with food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्ययेन रथेन द्रवत्पाणिभिरश्वैः ।धीजवना नासत्या ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyáyena ǀ ráthena ǀ dravátpāṇi-bhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀdhī́-javanā ǀ nā́satyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rapid as thought,Nāsatyās, (come) with your golden chariot drawn by quick-footed steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Rapid as thought,Nāsatyās, (come) with your golden chariot drawn by quick-footed steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवं मृगं जागृवांसं स्वदथो वा वृषण्वसू ।ता नः पृंक्तमिषा रयिं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ mṛgám ǀ jāgṛ-vā́ṃsám ǀ svádathaḥ ǀ vā ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pṛṅktam ǀ iṣā́ ǀ rayím ǁ
verses.english_translation: Affluent in showers, taste the wakeful desirable Soma; combine for us riches with food.
verses.wilson_translation: Affluent in showers, taste the wakeful desirable Soma; combine for us riches with food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ता मे अश्विना सनीनां विद्यातं नवानां ।यथा चिच्चैद्यः कशुः शतमुष्ट्रानां ददत्सहस्रा दश गोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ me ǀ aśvinā ǀ sanīnā́m ǀ vidyā́tam ǀ návānām ǀyáthā ǀ cit ǀ caidyáḥ ǀ kaśúḥ ǀ śatám ǀ úṣṭrānām ǀ dádat ǀ sahásrā ǀ dáśa ǀ gónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Become appraised,Aśvins, of my recent gifts, how that Kaśu, the son of Cedi, has presented me with ahundred camels and ten thousand cows.
verses.wilson_translation: Become appraised,Aśvins, of my recent gifts, how that Kaśu, the son of Cedi, has presented me with ahundred camels and ten thousand cows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो मे हिरण्यसंदृशो दश राज्ञो अमंहत ।अधस्पदा इच्चैद्यस्य कृष्टयश्चर्मम्ना अभितो जनाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ me ǀ híraṇya-sandṛśaḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ ámaṃhata ǀadhaḥ-padā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ caidyásya ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ carma-mnā́ḥ ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ jánāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The son of Cedi, who has given me for servants ten Rājās, bright as gold, for all men are beneath hisfeet; all those around him wear cuirasses of leather.
verses.wilson_translation: The son of Cedi, who has given me for servants ten Rājās, bright as gold, for all men are beneath hisfeet; all those around him wear cuirasses of leather.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: माकिरेना पथा गाद्येनेमे यंति चेदयः ।अन्यो नेत्सूरिरोहते भूरिदावत्तरो जनः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́kiḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ pathā́ ǀ gāt ǀ yéna ǀ imé ǀ yánti ǀ cedáyaḥ ǀanyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ ít ǀ sūríḥ ǀ óhate ǀ bhūridā́vat-taraḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: No one proceeds by that path which the Cedisfollow, no other proud man as a more liberal benefactorconfers (favour on those who praise him).
verses.wilson_translation: No one proceeds by that path which the Cedisfollow, no other proud man as a more liberal benefactorconfers (favour on those who praise him).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VI Indra
hymns.anukramani: ४८ वत्स:  काण्व । इन्द्र:, ४६ -४८  तिरिन्दिर: पार्शव्य: । गायत्री  ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INDRA, great in his power and might, and like Parjanya rich in rain,Is magnified by Vatsa's lauds. When the priests, strengthening the Son of Holy Law, present their gifts,Singers with Order's hymn of praiser. Since Kaṇvas with their lauds have made Indra complete the sacrifice.Words are their own appropriate arms. Before his hot displeasure all the peoples, all the men, bow down,As rivers bow them to the sea. This power of his shone brightly forth when Indra brought together, likeA skin, the worlds of heaven and earth. The fiercely-moving Vṛtra's head he severed with his thunderbolt,His mighty hundred-knotted bolt. Here are-we sing them loudly forth-our thoughts among-the best of songs.Even lightnings like the blaze of fire. When bidden thoughts, spontaneously advancing, glow, and with the streamOf sacrifice the Kaṇvas shine. Indra, may we obtain that wealth in horses and in herds of cows,And prayer that may be noticed first. I from my Father have received deep knowledge of the Holy LawI was born like unto the Sun. After the lore of ancient time I make, like Kaṇva, beauteous songs,And Indra's selfgains strength thereby. Whatever Ṛṣis have not praised thee, Indra, or have lauded thee,By me exalted wax thou strong. When his wrath thundered, when he rent Vṛtra to pieces, limb by limb,He sent the waters to the sea. Against the Dasyu gusna thou, Indra, didst hurl thy during bolt:Thou, Dread one, hast a hero's fame. Neither the heavens nor firmaments nor regions of the earth containIndra, the Thunderer with his might. O Indra him who lay at length staying thy copious waters thou,In his own footsteps, smotest down Thou hiddest deep in darkness itim, O Indra, who had set his graspOn spacious heaven and earth conjoined. Indra, whatever Yatis and Bhṛgus have offered praise to thee,Listen, thou Mighty, to my call. Indra, these spotted cows yield thee their butter and the milky draught;Aiders, thereby, of sacrifice; Which, teeming, have received thee as a life-germ, Indra, with their mouth,Like Sūrya who sustaineth all. O Lord of Might, with hymns of praise the Kaṇvas have increased thy power,The drops poured forth have strengthened thee. Under thy guidance, Indra, mid thy praises, Lord of Thunder, shallThe sacrifice be soon performed. Indra, disclose much food for us, like a stronghold with store of kine:Give progeny and heroic strength. And, Indra, grant us all that wealth of fleet steeds which shone bright of oldAmong the tribes of Nahusas. Hither thou seemest to attract heaven's fold which shines before our eyes,When, Indra, thou art kind to us. Yea, when thou puttest forth thy power, Indra, thou governest the folk.Mighty, unlimited in strength. The tribes who bring oblations call to thee, to thee to give them help,With drops to thee who spreadest far. There where the mountains downward slope, there by the meeting of the streamsThe Sage was manifest with song. Thence, marking, from his lofty place downward he looks upon the sea,And thence with rapid stir he moves. Then, verify, they see the light refulgent of primeval seed,Kindled on yonder side of heaven. Indra, the Kaṇvas all exalt thy wisdom and thy manly power,And, Mightiest! thine heroic strength. Accept this eulogy of mine, Indra, and guard me carefully:Strengthen my thought and prosper it. For thee, O Mighty, Thunder-armed, we singers through devotionhaveFashioned the hymn that we may live. To Indra have the Kaṇvas sung, like waters speeding down a slope:The song is fain to go to him. As rivers swell the ocean, so our hymns of praise make Indra strong,Eternal, of resistIess wrath. Come with thy lovely Bay Steeds, come to us from regions far awayO Indra, drink this Soma juice. Best slayer of Vṛtras, men whose sacred grass is ready trimmedInvoke thee for the gain of spoil. The heavens and earth come after thee as the wheel follows Etaśa:To thee flow Soma-drops effused. Rejoice, O Indra, in the light, rejoice in Saryandyan, be Glad in the sacrificer's hymn. Grown strong in heaven, the Thunder-armed hath bellowed, Vṛtra-slayer, Bull,Chief drinker of the Soma juice. Thou art a Ṛṣi born of old, sole Ruler over all by might:Thou, Indra, guardest well our wealth. May thy Bay Steeds with beauteous backs, a hundred, bring thee to the feast,Bring thee to these our Soma-draughts. The Kaṇvas with their hymns of praise have magnified this ancient thoughtThat swells with streams of meath and oil. Mid mightiest Gods let mortal man choose Indra at the sacrifice,Indra, whoe’er would win, for help. Thy steeds, by Priyamedhas praised, shall bring thee, God whom all invoke,Hither to drink the Somajuice. A hundred thousand have I gained from Parsu, from Tirindira,And presents of the Yadavas. Ten thousand head of kine, and steeds three times a hundred they bestowedOn Pajra for the Sāma-song. Kakuha hath reached up to heaven, bestowing buffaloes yoked in fours,And matched in fame the Yadavas.

verses.sanskrit: महाँ इंद्रो य ओजसा पर्जन्यो वृष्टिमाँ इव ।स्तोमैर्वत्सस्य वावृधे ॥
verses.transliteration: mahā́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ parjányaḥ ǀ vṛṣṭimā́n-iva ǀstómaiḥ ǀ vatsásya ǀ vavṛdhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, who is great in might like Parjanyathe disributor of rain, is magnified by the praises o Vatsa.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is great in might like Parjanyathe disributor of rain, is magnified by the praises o Vatsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रजामृतस्य पिप्रतः प्र यद्भरंत वह्नयः ।विप्रा ऋतस्य वाहसा ॥
verses.transliteration: pra-jā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ píprataḥ ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ bháranta ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀvíprāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vā́hasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When his steeds filling (the heavens) bear onwards the progeny of the sacrifice, then the pious(magnify him) with the hymns of the rite.
verses.wilson_translation: When his steeds filling (the heavens) bear onwards the progeny of the sacrifice, then the pious(magnify him) with the hymns of the rite.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कण्वा इंद्रं यदक्रत स्तोमैर्यज्ञस्य साधनं ।जामि ब्रुवत आयुधं ॥
verses.transliteration: káṇvāḥ ǀ índram ǀ yát ǀ ákrata ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ yajñásya ǀ sā́dhanam ǀjāmí ǀ bruvate ǀ ā́yudham ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the Kaṇvasby their praises have made Indrathe accomplisher of the sacrifice, they declare allweapons needless.
verses.wilson_translation: When the Kaṇvasby their praises have made Indrathe accomplisher of the sacrifice, they declare allweapons needless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समस्य मन्यवे विशो विश्वा नमंत कृष्टयः ।समुद्रायेव सिंधवः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ asya ǀ manyáve ǀ víśaḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ namanta ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀsamudrā́ya-iva ǀ síndhavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All people, (all) men bow down before his anger, as rivers (decline) towards the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: All people, (all) men bow down before his anger, as rivers (decline) towards the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ओजस्तदस्य तित्विष उभे यत्समवर्तयत् ।इंद्रश्चर्मेव रोदसी ॥
verses.transliteration: ójaḥ ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ titviṣe ǀ ubhé íti ǀ yát ǀ sam-ávartayat ǀíndraḥ ǀ cárma-iva ǀ ródasī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: His might is manifest, for Indrafolds and unfolds both heaven and earth, as (one spreads or rolls up) askin.
verses.wilson_translation: His might is manifest, for Indrafolds and unfolds both heaven and earth, as (one spreads or rolls up) askin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि चिद्वृत्रस्य दोधतो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा ।शिरो बिभेद वृष्णिना ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ cit ǀ vṛtrásya ǀ dódhataḥ ǀ vájreṇa ǀ śatá-parvaṇā ǀśíraḥ ǀ bibheda ǀ vṛṣṇínā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He has cloven with the powerful hundred-edged thunderbolt the head of the turbulent Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: He has cloven with the powerful hundred-edged thunderbolt the head of the turbulent Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा अभि प्र णोनुमो विपामग्रेषु धीतयः ।अग्नेः शोचिर्न दिद्युतः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ nonumaḥ ǀ vipā́m ǀ ágreṣu ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀagnéḥ ǀ śocíḥ ǀ ná ǀ didyútaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In front of one worshipper we repeatedly utter our praises, radiant as the flame of fire.
verses.wilson_translation: In front of one worshipper we repeatedly utter our praises, radiant as the flame of fire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: गुहा सतीरुप त्मना प्र यच्छोचंत धीतयः ।कण्वा ऋतस्य धारया ॥
verses.transliteration: gúhā ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ tmánā ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ śócanta ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀkáṇvāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhā́rayā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The praises that are offered in secret shine brightly when approaching (Indra) of their own will; the Kaṇvas (combine them) with the stream of the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: The praises that are offered in secret shine brightly when approaching (Indra) of their own will; the Kaṇvas (combine them) with the stream of the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र तमिंद्र नशीमहि रयिं गोमंतमश्विनं ।प्र ब्रह्म पूर्वचित्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tám ǀ indra ǀ naśīmahi ǀ rayím ǀ gó-mantam ǀ aśvínam ǀprá ǀ bráhma ǀ pūrvá-cittaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we obtain,Indra, that wealth which comprises cattle, horses, and food, before it be known toothers.
verses.wilson_translation: May we obtain,Indra, that wealth which comprises cattle, horses, and food, before it be known toothers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहमिद्धि पितुष्परि मेधामृतस्य जग्रभ ।अहं सूर्य इवाजनि ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ pitúḥ ǀ pári ǀ medhā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ jagrábha ǀahám ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ ajani ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have verily acquired the favour of the true protector (Indra); I have become (bright) as the sun.
verses.wilson_translation: I have verily acquired the favour of the true protector (Indra); I have become (bright) as the sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं प्रत्नेन मन्मना गिरः शुंभामि कण्ववत् ।येनेंद्रः शुष्ममिद्दधे ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ pratnéna ǀ mánmanā ǀ gíraḥ ǀ śumbhāmi ǀ kaṇva-vát ǀyéna ǀ índraḥ ǀ śúṣmam ǀ ít ǀ dadhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: I grace my words with ancient praise, like Kaṇva; whereby Indraassuredly enjoys vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: I grace my words with ancient praise, like Kaṇva; whereby Indraassuredly enjoys vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वामिंद्र न तुष्टुवुर्ऋषयो ये च तुष्टुवुः ।ममेद्वर्धस्व सुष्टुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ ná ǀ tustuvúḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ tustuvúḥ ǀmáma ǀ ít ǀ vardhasva ǀ sú-stutaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Amid those who do not praise you,Indra, amid the Ṛṣis who do praise you, by my praise beingglorified, do you increase.
verses.wilson_translation: Amid those who do not praise you,Indra, amid the Ṛṣis who do praise you, by my praise beingglorified, do you increase.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदस्य मन्युरध्वनीद्वि वृत्रं पर्वशो रुजन् ।अपः समुद्रमैरयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ asya ǀ manyúḥ ǀ ádhvanīt ǀ ví ǀ vṛtrám ǀ parva-śáḥ ǀ ruján ǀapáḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ áirayat ǁ
verses.english_translation: When his wrath thundered, dividing Vṛtrajoint by joint, then he drove the waters to the ocean.
verses.wilson_translation: When his wrath thundered, dividing Vṛtrajoint by joint, then he drove the waters to the ocean.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि शुष्ण इंद्र धर्णसिं वज्रं जघंथ दस्यवि ।वृषा ह्युग्र शृण्विषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ śúṣṇe ǀ indra ǀ dharṇasím ǀ vájram ǀ jaghantha ǀ dásyavi ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ hí ǀ ugra ǀ śṛṇviṣé ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have hurled your wielded thunderbolt upon the impiousŚuṣṇa; you are renowned, fierce Indra,as the showerer (of benefits).
verses.wilson_translation: You have hurled your wielded thunderbolt upon the impiousŚuṣṇa; you are renowned, fierce Indra,as the showerer (of benefits).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न द्याव इंद्रमोजसा नांतरिक्षाणि वज्रिणं ।न विव्यचंत भूमयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ índram ǀ ójasā ǀ ná ǀ antárikṣāṇi ǀ vajríṇam ǀná ǀ vivyacanta ǀ bhū́mayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Neither the heavens, nor the realms of the firmament, nor the regions of the earth, equal the thunderer Indra in strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Neither the heavens, nor the realms of the firmament, nor the regions of the earth, equal the thunderer Indra in strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्त इंद्र महीरपः स्तभूयमान आशयत् ।नि तं पद्यासु शिश्नथः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ stabhu-yámānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ áśayat ǀní ǀ tám ǀ pádyāsu ǀ śiśnathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Indra, have cast into the rushing streams him who lay obstructing your copious waters.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, have cast into the rushing streams him who lay obstructing your copious waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इमे रोदसी मही समीची समजग्रभीत् ।तमोभिरिंद्र तं गुहः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imé íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ sam-ájagrabhīt ǀtámaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ tám ǀ guhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have enveloped with darkness,Indra, him who had seized upon these spacious aggregated(realms of) heaven and earth.
verses.wilson_translation: You have enveloped with darkness,Indra, him who had seized upon these spacious aggregated(realms of) heaven and earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य इंद्र यतयस्त्वा भृगवो ये च तुष्टुवुः ।ममेदुग्र श्रुधी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ indra ǀ yátayaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ tustuvúḥ ǀmáma ǀ ít ǀ ugra ǀ śrudhi ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Amid those pious sages, amid those Bhṛgus, who have glorified you, hear also, fierce Indra, myinvocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Amid those pious sages, amid those Bhṛgus, who have glorified you, hear also, fierce Indra, myinvocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमास्त इंद्र पृश्नयो घृतं दुहत आशिरं ।एनामृतस्य पिप्युषीः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ pṛ́śnayaḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ duhate ǀ ā-śíram ǀenā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pipyúṣīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These, your spotted cows, the nourishers of the sacrifice, yields,Indra, their butter, and this mixture (ofmilk and curds).
verses.wilson_translation: These, your spotted cows, the nourishers of the sacrifice, yields,Indra, their butter, and this mixture (ofmilk and curds).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या इंद्र प्रस्वस्त्वासा गर्भमचक्रिरन् ।परि धर्मेव सूर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ pra-sváḥ ǀ tvā ǀ āsā́ ǀ gárbham ǀ ácakriran ǀpári ǀ dhárma-iva ǀ sū́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: These prolific cattle became pregnant, having taken into their mouths,Indra, (the products of yourvigour) like the all-sustaining sun.
verses.wilson_translation: These prolific cattle became pregnant, having taken into their mouths,Indra, (the products of yourvigour) like the all-sustaining sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिच्छवसस्पते कण्वा उक्थेन वावृधुः ।त्वां सुतास इंदवः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ pate ǀ káṇvāḥ ǀ ukthéna ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of strength, the Kaṇvasverily invigorate you by praise; the effused Soma(invigorates) you.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of strength, the Kaṇvasverily invigorate you by praise; the effused Soma(invigorates) you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तवेदिंद्र प्रणीतिषूत प्रशस्तिरद्रिवः ।यज्ञो वितंतसाय्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ prá-nītiṣu ǀ utá ǀ prá-śastiḥ ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀyajñáḥ ǀ vitantasā́yyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, excellent praise (is addressed to you) on account of your goodguidance, as is a most extended sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, excellent praise (is addressed to you) on account of your goodguidance, as is a most extended sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ न इंद्र महीमिषं पुरं न दर्षि गोमतीं ।उत प्रजां सुवीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ mahī́m ǀ íṣam ǀ púram ǀ ná ǀ darṣi ǀ gó-matīm ǀutá ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be willing to grant us abundant food with cattle; (to grant us) protection, progeny, and vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Be willing to grant us abundant food with cattle; (to grant us) protection, progeny, and vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्यदाश्वश्व्यं यदिंद्र नाहुषीष्वा ।अग्रे विक्षु प्रदीदयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tyát ǀ āśu-áśvyam ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ nā́huṣīṣu ǀ ā́ ǀágre ǀ vikṣú ǀ pra-dī́dayat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May that herd of swift horses, which formerly shone among the people ofnahuṣa, (be granted),Indra,to us.
verses.wilson_translation: May that herd of swift horses, which formerly shone among the people ofnahuṣa, (be granted),Indra,to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि व्रजं न तत्निषे सूर उपाकचक्षसं ।यदिंद्र मृळयासि नः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ vrajám ǀ ná ǀ tatniṣe ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ upāká-cakṣasam ǀyát ǀ indra ǀ mṛḷáyāsi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sage Indra, you spread (the cattle) over the adjacent pastures when you are favourably inclined towardus.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Indra, you spread (the cattle) over the adjacent pastures when you are favourably inclined towardus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदंग तविषीयस इंद्र प्रराजसि क्षितीः ।महाँ अपार ओजसा ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ aṅgá ǀ taviṣī-yáse ǀ índra ǀ pra-rā́jasi ǀ kṣitī́ḥ ǀmahā́n ǀ apāráḥ ǀ ójasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When you put forth your might, you reign,Indra, over mankind; surpassing are you, and unlimited instrumental ength.
verses.wilson_translation: When you put forth your might, you reign,Indra, over mankind; surpassing are you, and unlimited instrumental ength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा हविष्मतीर्विश उप ब्रुवत ऊतये ।उरुज्रयसमिंदुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ havíṣmatīḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ bruvate ǀ ūtáye ǀuru-jráyasam ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The people offering oblations call upon you, the pervader of space, with libations for protection.
verses.wilson_translation: The people offering oblations call upon you, the pervader of space, with libations for protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उपह्वरे गिरीणां संगथे च नदीनां ।धिया विप्रो अजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-hvaré ǀ girīṇā́m ǀ sam-gathé ǀ ca ǀ nadī́nām ǀdhiyā́ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wise (Indra) has been engendered by holy rites on the skirts of the mountains, at the confluence ofrivers.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise (Indra) has been engendered by holy rites on the skirts of the mountains, at the confluence ofrivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अतः समुद्रमुद्वतश्चिकित्वाँ अव पश्यति ।यतो विपान एजति ॥
verses.transliteration: átaḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ ut-vátaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ áva ǀ paśyati ǀyátaḥ ǀ vipānáḥ ǀ éjati ǁ
verses.english_translation: From the lofty region in which pervading he abides,Indrathe intelligent looks down upon the offeredlibation.
verses.wilson_translation: From the lofty region in which pervading he abides,Indrathe intelligent looks down upon the offeredlibation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्प्रत्नस्य रेतसो ज्योतिष्पश्यंति वासरं ।परो यदिध्यते दिवा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ pratnásya ǀ rétasaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ paśyanti ǀ vāsarám ǀparáḥ ǀ yát ǀ idhyáte ǀ divā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then (men) behold the daily light of the ancient shedder of water, when he shines above the heaveṇ
verses.wilson_translation: Then (men) behold the daily light of the ancient shedder of water, when he shines above the heaveṇ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कण्वास इंद्र ते मतिं विश्वे वर्धंति पौंस्यं ।उतो शविष्ठ वृष्ण्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: káṇvāsaḥ ǀ indra ǀ te ǀ matím ǀ víśve ǀ vardhanti ǀ páuṃsyam ǀutó íti ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: All the Kaṇvas,Indra, magnify your wisdom, your manhood, and, most mighty one, your strength.
verses.wilson_translation: All the Kaṇvas,Indra, magnify your wisdom, your manhood, and, most mighty one, your strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमां म इंद्र सुष्टुतिं ज���षस्व प्र सु मामव ।उत प्र वर्धया मतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ me ǀ indra ǀ su-stutím ǀ juṣásva ǀ prá ǀ sú ǀ mā́m ǀ ava ǀutá ǀ prá ǀ vardhaya ǀ matím ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be propitiated,Indra, by this my praise; carefully protect me, and give increase to my understanding.
verses.wilson_translation: Be propitiated,Indra, by this my praise; carefully protect me, and give increase to my understanding.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत ब्रह्मण्या वयं तुभ्यं प्रवृद्ध वज्रिवः ।विप्रा अतक्ष्म जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ brahmaṇyā́ ǀ vayám ǀ túbhyam ǀ pra-vṛddha ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀvíprāḥ ǀ atakṣma ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, magnified (by our praises), we your worshippers have offered to you theseprayers for our existence.
verses.wilson_translation: Wielder of the thunderbolt, magnified (by our praises), we your worshippers have offered to you theseprayers for our existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि कण्वा अनूषतापो न प्रवता यतीः ।इंद्रं वनन्वती मतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ káṇvāḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ pra-vátā ǀ yatī́ḥ ǀíndram ǀ vánan-vatī ǀ matíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Kaṇvasglorify Indra; like waters rushing down a declivity, praise spontaneously seeks Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: The Kaṇvasglorify Indra; like waters rushing down a declivity, praise spontaneously seeks Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रमुक्थानि वावृधुः समुद्रमिव सिंधवः ।अनुत्तमन्युमजरं ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ ukthā́ni ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ samudrám-iva ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀánutta-manyum ǀ ajáram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Holy praises magnify Indra, the imperishable, the implacable, as rivers (swell) the ocean.
verses.wilson_translation: Holy praises magnify Indra, the imperishable, the implacable, as rivers (swell) the ocean.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो याहि परावतो हरिभ्यां हर्यताभ्यां ।इममिंद्र सुतं पिब ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ haryatā́bhyām ǀimám ǀ indra ǀ sutám ǀ piba ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us from afar with your beloved horses; drink,Indra, this libation.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us from afar with your beloved horses; drink,Indra, this libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिद्वृत्रहंतम जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषः ।हवंते वाजसातये ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ vṛtrahan-tama ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣaḥ ǀhávante ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroyer of Vṛtra, men strewing the clipped sacred grass invoke you for the obtaining of food.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyer of Vṛtra, men strewing the clipped sacred grass invoke you for the obtaining of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनु त्वा रोदसी उभे चक्रं न वर्त्येतशं ।अनु सुवानास इंदवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ tvā ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ cakrám ǀ ná ǀ varti ǀ étaśam ǀánu ǀ suvānā́saḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Both heaven and earth follow you as the wheels (of a car follow) the horse; the streams of the Somapoured forth (by the priests) follow (you).
verses.wilson_translation: Both heaven and earth follow you as the wheels (of a car follow) the horse; the streams of the Somapoured forth (by the priests) follow (you).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मंदस्वा सु स्वर्णर उतेंद्र शर्यणावति ।मत्स्वा विवस्वतो मती ॥
verses.transliteration: mándasva ǀ sú ǀ sváḥ-nare ǀ utá ǀ indra ǀ śaryaṇā́-vati ǀmátsva ǀ vívasvataḥ ǀ matī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rejoice,Indra, at the heaven-guiding sacrifice as Śaryaṇāvat; be exhilarated by the praise of theworshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Rejoice,Indra, at the heaven-guiding sacrifice as Śaryaṇāvat; be exhilarated by the praise of theworshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वावृधान उप द्यवि वृषा वज्र्यरोरवीत् ।वृत्रहा सोमपातमः ॥
verses.transliteration: vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vajrī́ ǀ aroravīt ǀvṛtra-hā́ ǀ soma-pā́tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The vast wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra, the deep quaffer of the Soma, the showerer,roars near athandin the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: The vast wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra, the deep quaffer of the Soma, the showerer,roars near athandin the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऋषिर्हि पूर्वजा अस्येक ईशान ओजसा ।इंद्र चोष्कूयसे वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ hí ǀ pūrva-jā́ḥ ǀ ási ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ ójasā ǀíndra ǀ coṣkūyáse ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are a Ṛṣi, the first-born (of the gods), the chief, the ruler (over all) by your strength; you giverepeatedly,Indra, wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: You are a Ṛṣi, the first-born (of the gods), the chief, the ruler (over all) by your strength; you giverepeatedly,Indra, wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं त्वा सुताँ उप वीतपृष्ठा अभि प्रयः ।शतं वहंतु हरयः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ tvā ǀ sutā́n ǀ úpa ǀ vītá-pṛṣṭhāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ práyaḥ ǀśatám ǀ vahantu ǀ hárayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your hundred sleek-backed horses bring you to our libations, to our (sacrificial) food.
verses.wilson_translation: May your hundred sleek-backed horses bring you to our libations, to our (sacrificial) food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमां सु पूर्व्यां धियं मधोर्घृतस्य पिप्युषीं ।कण्वा उक्थेन वावृधुः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ sú ǀ pūrvyā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ mádhoḥ ǀ ghṛtásya ǀ pipyúṣīm ǀkáṇvāḥ ǀ ukthéna ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Kaṇvasaugment by praise this ancient rite intended (to obtain) an abundance of sweet water.
verses.wilson_translation: The Kaṇvasaugment by praise this ancient rite intended (to obtain) an abundance of sweet water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रमिद्विमहीनां मेधे वृणीत मर्त्यः ।इंद्रं सनिष्युरूतये ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ ít ǀ ví-mahīnām ǀ médhe ǀ vṛṇīta ǀ mártyaḥ ǀíndram ǀ saniṣyúḥ ǀ ūtáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mortal (adorer) selects at the sacrifice Indrafrom among the mighty (gods); he who is desirous ofwealth (worships) Indra for protection.
verses.wilson_translation: The mortal (adorer) selects at the sacrifice Indrafrom among the mighty (gods); he who is desirous ofwealth (worships) Indra for protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अर्वांचं त्वा पुरुष्टुत प्रियमेधस्तुता हरी ।सोमपेयाय वक्षतः ॥
verses.transliteration: arvā́ñcam ǀ tvā ǀ puru-stuta ǀ priyámedha-stutā ǀ hárī íti ǀsoma-péyāya ǀ vakṣataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May your horses, praised by the pious priests, bring you, who are the praised of many, down to drinkthe Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: May your horses, praised by the pious priests, bring you, who are the praised of many, down to drinkthe Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतमहं तिरिंदिरे सहस्रं पर्शावा ददे ।राधांसि याद्वानां ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ ahám ǀ tiríndire ǀ sahásram ǀ párśau ǀ ā́ ǀ dade ǀrā́dhāṃsi ǀ yā́dvānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have accepted from Tirindira, the son of Paraśu, hundreds and thousands of the treasures of meṇ
verses.wilson_translation: I have accepted from Tirindira, the son of Paraśu, hundreds and thousands of the treasures of meṇ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रीणि शतान्यर्वतां सहस्रा दश गोनां ।ददुष्पज्राय साम्ने ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ṇi ǀ śatā́ni ǀ árvatām ǀ sahásrā ǀ dáśa ǀ gónām ǀdadúḥ ǀ pajrā́ya ǀ sā́mne ǁ
verses.english_translation: (These princes) have given to the chanter Pajra three hundred horses, ten thousand cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: (These princes) have given to the chanter Pajra three hundred horses, ten thousand cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदानट् ककुहो दिवमुष्ट्रांचतुर्युजो ददत् ।श्रवसा याद्वं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ānaṭ ǀ kakuháḥ ǀ dívam ǀ úṣṭrān ǀ catuḥ-yújaḥ ǀ dádat ǀśrávasā ǀ yā́dvam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The exalted (prince) has been raised by fame to heaven, for he has given camels laden with four (loadsof gold), and Yādva people (as slaves).
verses.wilson_translation: The exalted (prince) has been raised by fame to heaven, for he has given camels laden with four (loadsof gold), and Yādva people (as slaves).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN VII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O MARUTS, when the sage hath poured the Tṛṣṭup forth as food for you,Ye shine amid the mountain-clouds. When, Bright Ones, fain to show your might ye have determined on your course,The mountain-clouds have bent them down. Loud roaring with the winds the Sons of Pṛśni have upraised themselves:They have poured out the streaming food. The Maruts spread the mist abroad and make mountains rock and reel,When with the winds they go their way What time the rivers and the hills before your coming bowed them down,So to sustain your mighty force. We call on you for aid by night, on you for succour in the day,On you while sacrifice proceeds. These, verily, wondrous, red of hue, speed on their courses with a roarOver the ridges of the sky. With might they drop the loosened rein so that the Sun may run his course,And spread themselves with beams of light. Accept, ye Maruts, this my song, accept ye this mine hymn of praise,Accept, Ṛbhukṣans, this my call. The dappled Cows have poured three lakes, meath for the Thunder-wielding God,From the great cask, the watery cloud. O Maruts, quickly come to us when, longing for felicity,We call you hither from the sky. For, Rudras and Ṛbhukṣans, ye, Most Bountiful, are in the house,Wise when the gladdening draught is drunk. O Maruts, send us down from heaven riches distilling rapturous joy,With plenteous food, sustaining all. When, Bright Ones, hither from the hills ye have resolved to take your way,Ye revel in the drops effused. Man should solicit with his lauds happiness which belongs to them,So great a band invincible. They who like fiery sparks with showers of rain blow through the heaven and earth,Milking the spring that never fails. With chariots and tumultuous roar, with tempests and with hymns of praiseThe Sons of Pṛśni hurry forth. For wealth, we think of that whereby ye aided Yadu, Turvaśa,And KanVa who obtained the spoil. May these our viands Bounteous Ones I that flow in streams like holy oil,With Kaṇva's hymns, increase your might. Where, Bounteous Lords for whom the grass is trimmed, are ye rejoicing now?What Brahman is adoring you? Is it not there where ye of old, supplied with sacred grass, for laudsInspired the strong in sacrifice? They brought together both the worlds, the mighty waters, and the Sun,And, joint by joint, the thunderbolt. They sundered Vṛtra limb from limb and split the gloomy mountain-clouds,Performing a heroic deed. They reinforced the power and strength of Trita as he fought, and helpedIndra in battle with the foe. They deck themselves for glory, bright, celestial, lightning in their hands,And helms of gold upon their heads. When eagerly ye from far away came to the cavern of the Bull,He bellowed in his fear like Heaven. Borne by your golden-footed steeds, O Gods, come hither to receiveThe sacrifice we offer you. When the red leader draws along their spotted deer yoked to the car.The Bright Ones come, and shed the rain. Susoma, Saryakiavan, and Arjika full of homes, have they.These Heroes, sought with downward car. When, Maruts, ye come to him, the singer who invokes you thus,With favours to your suppliant? What now? where have ye still a friend since ye left Indra all alone?Who counteth on your friendship now? The Kaṇvas sing forth Agni's praise together with our Maruts’ whoWield thunder and wear swords of gold. Hither for new felicity may I attract the Impetuous Ones,The Heroes with their wondrous strength Before them sink the very hills deerning themseives abysses: yea,Even the mountains bend them down. Steeds flying on their tortuous path through mid-air carry them, and giveThe man who lauds them strength and life. Agni was born the first of all, like Sūrya lovely with his light:With lustre these have spread abroad.

verses.sanskrit: प्र यद्वस्त्रिष्टुभमिषं मरुतो विप्रो अक्षरत् ।वि पर्वतेषु राजथ ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ vaḥ ǀ tri-stúbham ǀ íṣam ǀ márutaḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ ákṣarat ǀví ǀ párvateṣu ǀ rājatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the pious worshipper offers you,Maruts, food at the three diurnal rites, then you havesovereignty over the mountains.
verses.wilson_translation: When the pious worshipper offers you,Maruts, food at the three diurnal rites, then you havesovereignty over the mountains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदंग तविषीयवो यामं शुभ्रा अचिध्वं ।नि पर्वता अहासत ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ aṅgá ǀ taviṣī-yavaḥ ǀ yā́mam ǀ śubhrāḥ ǀ ácidhvam ǀní ǀ párvatāḥ ǀ ahāsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, glorious and powerful (Maruts), you fit out your chariot, the mountains depart (from their plural ces).
verses.wilson_translation: When, glorious and powerful (Maruts), you fit out your chariot, the mountains depart (from their plural ces).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदीरयंत वायुभिर्वाश्रासः पृश्निमातरः ।धुक्षंत पिप्युषीमिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrayanta ǀ vāyú-bhiḥ ǀ vāśrā́saḥ ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǀdhukṣánta ǀ pipyúṣīm ǀ íṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The loud-sounding sons of Pṛśnidrive with their breezes (the clouds), they milk forth nutritioussustenance.
verses.wilson_translation: The loud-sounding sons of Pṛśnidrive with their breezes (the clouds), they milk forth nutritioussustenance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वपंति मरुतो मिहं प्र वेपयंति पर्वतान् ।यद्यामं यांति वायुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: vápanti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ míham ǀ prá ǀ vepayanti ǀ párvatān ǀyát ǀ yā́mam ǀ yā́nti ǀ vāyú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Marutsscatter the rain, they shake the mountains, when they mount their chariot, with the winds.
verses.wilson_translation: The Marutsscatter the rain, they shake the mountains, when they mount their chariot, with the winds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नि यद्यामाय वो गिरिर्नि सिंधवो विधर्मणे ।महे शुष्माय येमिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ yát ǀ yā́māya ǀ vaḥ ǀ giríḥ ǀ ní ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ ví-dharmaṇe ǀmahé ǀ śúṣmāya ǀ yemiré ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mountains are curbed, the rivers are restrained at your coming, for the upholding of your greatstrength.
verses.wilson_translation: The mountains are curbed, the rivers are restrained at your coming, for the upholding of your greatstrength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युष्माँ उ नक्तमूतये युष्मांदिवा हवामहे ।युष्मान्प्रयत्यध्वरे ॥
verses.transliteration: yuṣmā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ náktam ǀ ūtáye ǀ yuṣmā́n ǀ dívā ǀ havāmahe ǀyuṣmā́n ǀ pra-yatí ǀ adhvaré ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you for protection by night, (we invoke) you by day, (we invoke) you when the sacrifice is inprogress.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you for protection by night, (we invoke) you by day, (we invoke) you when the sacrifice is inprogress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदु त्ये अरुणप्सवश्चित्रा यामेभिरीरते ।वाश्रा अधि ष्णुना दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyé ǀ aruṇá-psavaḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ yā́mebhiḥ ǀ īrate ǀvāśrā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ snúnā ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Truly these purple-hued, wonderful, clamorous Marutsproceed with their chariots in the height aove thesky.
verses.wilson_translation: Truly these purple-hued, wonderful, clamorous Marutsproceed with their chariots in the height aove thesky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सृजंति रश्मिमोजसा पंथां सूर्याय यातवे ।ते भानुभिर्वि तस्थिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: sṛjánti ǀ raśmím ǀ ójasā ǀ pánthām ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ yā́tave ǀté ǀ bhānú-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ tasthire ǁ
verses.english_translation: They, who by their might open a radiant path for the sun to travel, they pervade (the world) with lustre.
verses.wilson_translation: They, who by their might open a radiant path for the sun to travel, they pervade (the world) with lustre.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमां मे मरुतो गिरमिमं स्तोममृभुक्षणः ।इमं मे वनता हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ me ǀ marutaḥ ǀ gíram ǀ imám ǀ stómam ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀimám ǀ me ǀ vanata ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Accept,Maruts, this my praise, (accept), mighty ones, this my adoration, (accept) this my invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Maruts, this my praise, (accept), mighty ones, this my adoration, (accept) this my invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्रीणि सरांसि पृश्नयो दुदुह्रे वज्रिणे मधु ।उत्सं कवंधमुद्रिणं ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ṇi ǀ sárāṃsi ǀ pṛ́śnayaḥ ǀ duduhré ǀ vajríṇe ǀ mádhu ǀútsam ǀ kávandham ǀ udríṇam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The kine have filled for the thunderer three lakes of the sweet (Soma) from the dripping water-bearingcloud.
verses.wilson_translation: The kine have filled for the thunderer three lakes of the sweet (Soma) from the dripping water-bearingcloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मरुतो यद्ध वो दिवः सुम्नायंतो हवामहे ।आ तू न उप गंतन ॥
verses.transliteration: márutaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ sumna-yántaḥ ǀ hávāmahe ǀā́ ǀ tú ǀ naḥ ǀ úpa ǀ gantana ǁ
verses.english_translation: When,Maruts, desirous of felicity, we invoke you from heaven, come unto us quickly.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Maruts, desirous of felicity, we invoke you from heaven, come unto us quickly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं हि ष्ठा सुदानवो रुद्रा ऋभुक्षणो दमे ।उत प्रचेतसो मदे ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ hí ǀ sthá ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ rúdrāḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ dáme ǀutá ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ máde ǁ
verses.english_translation: Munificent, mighty Rudras, you in the sacrificial hall are wise (even) in the exhilaration (of the Soma).
verses.wilson_translation: Munificent, mighty Rudras, you in the sacrificial hall are wise (even) in the exhilaration (of the Soma).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो रयिं मदच्युतं पुरुक्षुं विश्वधायसं ।इयर्ता मरुतो दिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ mada-cyútam ǀ puru-kṣúm ǀ viśvá-dhāyasam ǀíyarta ǀ marutaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send us,Maruts, from heaven exhilarating, many lauded, all-sustaining riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Send us,Maruts, from heaven exhilarating, many lauded, all-sustaining riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अधीव यद्गिरीणां यामं शुभ्रा अचिध्वं ।सुवानैर्मंदध्व इंदुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi-iva ǀ yát ǀ girīṇā́m ǀ yā́mam ǀ śubhrāḥ ǀ ácidhvam ǀsuvānáiḥ ǀ mandadhve ǀ índu-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, bright (Maruts), you harness your car over the mountains, then you exhilarate (yourselves) withthe effusing Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: When, bright (Maruts), you harness your car over the mountains, then you exhilarate (yourselves) withthe effusing Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एतावतश्चिदेषां सुम्नं भिक्षेत मर्त्यः ।अदाभ्यस्य मन्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́vataḥ ǀ cit ǀ eṣām ǀ sumnám ǀ bhikṣeta ǀ mártyaḥ ǀádābhyasya ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A man should solicit happiness of them with praises of such an unconquerable (company).
verses.wilson_translation: A man should solicit happiness of them with praises of such an unconquerable (company).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ये द्रप्सा इव रोदसी धमंत्यनु वृष्टिभिः ।उत्सं दुहंतो अक्षितं ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ drapsā́ḥ-iva ǀ ródasī íti ǀ dhámanti ǀ ánu ǀ vṛṣṭí-bhiḥ ǀútsam ǀ duhántaḥ ǀ ákṣitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who, like dropping showers, inflate heaven and earth with rain, milking the inexhaustible cloud.
verses.wilson_translation: They who, like dropping showers, inflate heaven and earth with rain, milking the inexhaustible cloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदु स्वानेभिरीरत उद्रथैरुदु वायुभिः ।उत्स्तोमैः पृश्निमातरः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svānébhiḥ ǀ īrate ǀ út ǀ ráthaiḥ ǀ út ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vāyú-bhiḥ ǀút ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ pṛ́śni-mātaraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sons of Pṛśnirise up with shouts, with chariots, with winds, with praises.
verses.wilson_translation: The sons of Pṛśnirise up with shouts, with chariots, with winds, with praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: येनाव तुर्वशं यदुं येन कण्वं धनस्पृतं ।राये सु तस्य धीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ āvá ǀ turváśam ǀ yádum ǀ yéna ǀ káṇvam ǀ dhana-spṛ́tam ǀrāyé ǀ sú ǀ tásya ǀ dhīmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We meditate on that (genitive rosity) whereby for (the sake of granting them) riches you have protected Turvaśa and Yaduand the wealth-desiring Kaṇva.
verses.wilson_translation: We meditate on that (genitive rosity) whereby for (the sake of granting them) riches you have protected Turvaśa and Yaduand the wealth-desiring Kaṇva.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमा उ वः सुदानवो घृतं न पिप्युषीरिषः ।वर्धान्काण्वस्य मन्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vaḥ ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ pipyúṣīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀvárdhān ǀ kāṇvásya ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Munificent (Maruts), may these (sacrificial) viands, nutritious as butter, together with the praises of thedescendant of Kaṇva, afford you augmentation.
verses.wilson_translation: Munificent (Maruts), may these (sacrificial) viands, nutritious as butter, together with the praises of thedescendant of Kaṇva, afford you augmentation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: क्व नूनं सुदानवो मदथा वृक्तबर्हिषः ।ब्रह्मा को वः सपर्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ nūnám ǀ su-dānavaḥ ǀ mádatha ǀ vṛkta-barhiṣaḥ ǀbrahmā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ saparyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Munificent (Maruts), for whom the sacred grass has been trimmed, where now are you beingexhilarated? What pious worshipper detains you as he) adores you?
verses.wilson_translation: Munificent (Maruts), for whom the sacred grass has been trimmed, where now are you beingexhilarated? What pious worshipper detains you as he) adores you?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नहि ष्म यद्ध वः पुरा स्तोमेभिर्वृक्तबर्हिषः ।शर्धाँ ऋतस्य जिन्वथ ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ sma ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ vaḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ vṛkta-barhiṣaḥ ǀśárdhān ǀ ṛtásya ǀ jínvatha ǁ
