verses.transliteration: prá ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ nabhāka-vát ǀ indrāgní-bhyām ǀ irajyata ǀyā́ ǀ saptá-budhnam ǀ arṇavám ǀ jihmá-bāram ǀ apa-ūrṇutáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Address like Nabhākayour praises to Indraand Agni, who overspread (with their lustre) theseven-rooted ocean whose gates are hidden, and of whom Indra by his might is the lord; may all our adversariesperish.
verses.wilson_translation: Address like Nabhākayour praises to Indraand Agni, who overspread (with their lustre) theseven-rooted ocean whose gates are hidden, and of whom Indra by his might is the lord; may all our adversariesperish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अपि वृश्च पुराणवद्व्रततेरिव गुष्पितमोजो दासस्य दंभय ।वयं तदस्य संभृतं वस्विंद्रेण वि भजेमहि नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: ápi ǀ vṛśca ǀ purāṇa-vát ǀ vratáteḥ-iva ǀ guṣpitám ǀ ójaḥ ǀ dāsásya ǀ dambhaya ǀvayám ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ sám-bhṛtam ǀ vásu ǀ índreṇa ǀ ví ǀ bhajemahi ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cut off (the foe),Indra, as and old (pruner) the protruding (branch) of a creeper, humble the strength ofthe Dāsa; may we divide his accusative ulated treasure (despoiled) by Indra; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Cut off (the foe),Indra, as and old (pruner) the protruding (branch) of a creeper, humble the strength ofthe Dāsa; may we divide his accusative ulated treasure (despoiled) by Indra; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्राग्नी जना इमे विह्वयंते तना गिरा ।अस्माकेभिर्नृभिर्वयं सासह्याम पृतन्यतो वनुयाम वनुष्यतो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ jánāḥ ǀ imé ǀ vi-hváyante ǀ tánā ǀ girā́ ǀasmā́kebhiḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ vayám ǀ sasahyā́ma ǀ pṛtanyatáḥ ǀ vanuyā́ma ǀ vanuṣyatáḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inasmuch as these people honour Indraand Agniwith gifts and with praises, so may we, defying hosts,overcome (our foes) with our warriors; let us praise those seeking praise; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as these people honour Indraand Agniwith gifts and with praises, so may we, defying hosts,overcome (our foes) with our warriors; let us praise those seeking praise; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: या नु श्वेताववो दिव उच्चरात उप द्युभिः ।इंद्राग्न्योरनु व्रतमुहाना यंति सिंधवो यान्त्सीं बंधादमुंचतां नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ nú ǀ śvetáu ǀ aváḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ut-cárātaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀindrāgnyóḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ úhānāḥ ǀ yanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ yā́n ǀ sīm ǀ bandhā́t ǀ ámuñcatām ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offering oblations, (the worshippers) approach to the worship of Indraand Agni, who are of a whitecomplexion, and rise from below with bright rays to heaven; they verily have liberated the waters from bondage;may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Offering oblations, (the worshippers) approach to the worship of Indraand Agni, who are of a whitecomplexion, and rise from below with bright rays to heaven; they verily have liberated the waters from bondage;may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वीष्ट इंद्रोपमातयः पूर्वीरुत प्रशस्तयः सूनो हिन्वस्य हरिवः ।वस्वो वीरस्यापृचो या नु साधंत नो धियो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrvī́ḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ úpa-mātayaḥ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ prá-śastayaḥ ǀ sū́no íti ǀ hinvásya ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀvásvaḥ ǀ vīrásya ǀ ā-pṛ́caḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ nú ǀ sā́dhanta ǀ naḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, instrumental gator (of acts), may the numerous merits, the many excellences ofyou, who are the bestower of affluence and ofmaleoffspring, perfect our understandings; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, instrumental gator (of acts), may the numerous merits, the many excellences ofyou, who are the bestower of affluence and ofmaleoffspring, perfect our understandings; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं शिशीता सुवृक्तिभिस्त्वेषं सत्वानमृग्मियं ।उतो नु चिद्य ओजसा शुष्णस्यांडानि भेदति जेषत्स्वर्वतीरपो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ śiśīta ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ tveṣám ǀ sátvānam ǀ ṛgmíyam ǀutó íti ǀ nú ǀ cit ǀ yáḥ ǀ ójasā ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ āṇḍā́ni ǀ bhédati ǀ jéṣat ǀ sváḥ-vatīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Animate with praises that brilliant adorable Indra, the distributor (of riches), who by hismight breaks theeggs ofŚuṣṇa; may he conquer the celestial waters; may all our enemies perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Animate with praises that brilliant adorable Indra, the distributor (of riches), who by hismight breaks theeggs ofŚuṣṇa; may he conquer the celestial waters; may all our enemies perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं शिशीता स्वध्वरं सत्यं सत्वानमृत्वियं ।उतो नु चिद्य ओहत आंडा शुष्णस्य भेदत्यजैः स्वर्वतीरपो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ śiśīta ǀ su-adhvarám ǀ satyám ǀ sátvānam ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀutó íti ǀ nú ǀ cit ǀ yáḥ ǀ óhate ǀ āṇḍā́ ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ bhédati ǀ ájaiḥ ǀ sváḥ-vatīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Animate that Indrato whom sacrifice is due-- sincere, bountiful, adorable; him who frequents sacrifices,who breaks the eggs ofŚuṣṇa; you have conquered the celestial waters; may all our enemies perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Animate that Indrato whom sacrifice is due-- sincere, bountiful, adorable; him who frequents sacrifices,who breaks the eggs ofŚuṣṇa; you have conquered the celestial waters; may all our enemies perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवेंद्राग्निभ्यां पितृवन्नवीयो मंधातृवदंगिरस्वदवाचि ।त्रिधातुना शर्मणा पातमस्मान्वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ indrāgní-bhyām ǀ pitṛ-vát ǀ návīyaḥ ǀ mandhātṛ-vát ǀ aṅgirasvát ǀ avāci ǀtri-dhā́tunā ǀ śármaṇā ǀ pātam ǀ asmā́n ǀ vayám ǀ syāma ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus has a new hymn been addressed to Indraand Agni, as was done by my father, by Mandhātā,by Aṅgirasa; cherish us with a triply defended dwelling; may we be the lords of riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus has a new hymn been addressed to Indraand Agni, as was done by my father, by Mandhātā,by Aṅgirasa; cherish us with a triply defended dwelling; may we be the lords of riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Varuṇa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To make this Varuṇa come forth sing thou a song unto the band of Maruts wiser than thyself,—This Varuṇa who guardeth well the thoughts of men like herds of kine.Let all the others die away. Him altogether praise I with the song and hymns our fathers sang, and with Nabhāka's eulogies,—Him dwelling at the rivers’ source, surrounded by his Sisters Seven. The nights he hath encompassed, and stablished the morns with magic art visible over all is he.His dear Ones, following his Law, have prospered the Three Dawns for him. He, visible o’er all the earth, stablished the quarters of the sky:He measured out the eastern place, that is the fold of Varuṇa: like a strong herdsman is the God. He who supports the worlds of life, he who well knows the hidden names mysterious of the morning beams,He cherishes much wisdom, Sage, as heaven brings forth each varied form. In whom all wisdom centres, as the nave is set within the wheel.Haste ye to honour Trita, as kine haste to gather in the fold, even as they muster steeds to yoke. He wraps these regions as a robe; he contemplates the tribes of Gods and all the works of mortal men.Before the home of Varuṇa all the Gods follow his decree. He is an Ocean far-removed, yet through the heaven to him ascends the worship which these realms possess.With his bright foot he overthrew their magic, and went up to heaven. Ruler, whose bright far-seeing rays, pervading all three earths, have filled the three superior realms of heaven.Firm is the seat of Varuṇa: over the Seven he rules as King. Who, after his decree, o’erspread the Dark Ones with a robe of light;Who measured out the ancient seat, who pillared both the worlds apart as the Unborn supported heaven. Let all the others die away.

verses.sanskrit: अस्मा ऊ षु प्रभूतये वरुणाय मरुद्भ्योऽर्चा विदुष्टरेभ्यः ।यो धीता मानुषाणां पश्वो गा इव रक्षति नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: asmái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ prá-bhūtaye ǀ váruṇāya ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀ árca ǀ vidúḥ-tarebhyaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ dhītā́ ǀ mā́nuṣāṇām ǀ paśváḥ ǀ gā́ḥ-iva ǀ rákṣati ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer praise to that opulent Varuṇa, and to the most sage Maruts; (Varuṇa) who protects men by hisacts, as (the herdsman guards) the cattle; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer praise to that opulent Varuṇa, and to the most sage Maruts; (Varuṇa) who protects men by hisacts, as (the herdsman guards) the cattle; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमू षु समना गिरा पितॄणां च मन्मभिः ।नाभाकस्य प्रशस्तिभिर्यः सिंधूनामुपोदये सप्तस्वसा स मध्यमो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ samanā́ ǀ girā́ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ca ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀnābhākásya ǀ práśasti-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ síndhūnām ǀ úpa ǀ ut-ayé ǀ saptá-svasā ǀ sáḥ ǀ madhyamáḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: (I praise) with a like praise, with the praises of (my) progenitors, with the eulogies of Nabhāka, that Varuṇa who rises up in the vicinity of the rivers, and in the midst (of them) has seven sisters; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: (I praise) with a like praise, with the praises of (my) progenitors, with the eulogies of Nabhāka, that Varuṇa who rises up in the vicinity of the rivers, and in the midst (of them) has seven sisters; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स क्षपः परि षस्वजे न्युस्रो मायया दधे स विश्वं परि दर्शतः ।तस्य वेनीरनु व्रतमुषस्तिस्रो अवर्धयन्नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ kṣápa�� ǀ pári ǀ sasvaje ǀ ní ǀ usráḥ ǀ māyáyā ǀ dadhe ǀ sáḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ pári ǀ darśatáḥ ǀtásya ǀ vénīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ uṣáḥ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ avardhayan ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He embraces the nights; of goodly aspect, and quick of movement, he encompasses the universe byhis acts; all who are desirous (of his favour) diligently offer him worship at the three diurnal rites; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He embraces the nights; of goodly aspect, and quick of movement, he encompasses the universe byhis acts; all who are desirous (of his favour) diligently offer him worship at the three diurnal rites; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यः ककुभो निधारयः पृथिव्यामधि दर्शतः ।स माता पूर्व्यं पदं तद्वरुणस्य सप्त्यं स हि गोपा इवेर्यो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ kakúbhaḥ ǀ ni-dhārayáḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ ádhi ǀ darśatáḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ mā́tā ǀ pūrvyám ǀ padám ǀ tát ǀ váruṇasya ǀ sáptyam ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ gopā́ḥ-iva ǀ íryaḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, who visible above the earth sustains the points of the horizon, is the measurer (of the universe);that is the ancient abode of Varuṇa, to which we have access; he is our lord, like the keeper of cattle; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He, who visible above the earth sustains the points of the horizon, is the measurer (of the universe);that is the ancient abode of Varuṇa, to which we have access; he is our lord, like the keeper of cattle; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो धर्ता भुवनानां य उस्राणामपीच्या वेद नामानि गुह्या ।स कविः काव्या पुरु रूपं द्यौरिव पुष्यति नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ dhartā́ ǀ bhúvanānām ǀ yáḥ ǀ usrā́ṇām ǀ apīcyā́ ǀ véda ǀ nā́māni ǀ gúhyā ǀsáḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ kā́vyā ǀ purú ǀ rūpám ǀ dyáuḥ-iva ǀ puṣyati ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is the sustainer of the worlds, who knows the hidden and secret names of the (solar) rays, he isthe sage who cherishes the acts of sages, as the heaven cherishes numerous forms; may all our adversariesperish.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is the sustainer of the worlds, who knows the hidden and secret names of the (solar) rays, he isthe sage who cherishes the acts of sages, as the heaven cherishes numerous forms; may all our adversariesperish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्विश्वानि काव्या चक्रे नाभिरिव श्रिता ।त्रितं जूती सपर्यत व्रजे गावो न संयुजे युजे अश्वाँ अयुक्षत नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ víśvāni ǀ kā́vyā ǀ cakré ǀ nā́bhiḥ-iva ǀ śritā́ ǀtritám ǀ jūtī́ ǀ saparyata ǀ vrajé ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sam-yúje ǀ yujé ǀ áśvān ǀ ayukṣata ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: In whom all pious acts are concentrated, like the nave in the (centre of the) wheel, worship him quicklywho abides in thethree worlds; as men assemble the cattle in their pasture, so do (our foes) collect their horses(to assail us); may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: In whom all pious acts are concentrated, like the nave in the (centre of the) wheel, worship him quicklywho abides in thethree worlds; as men assemble the cattle in their pasture, so do (our foes) collect their horses(to assail us); may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य आस्वत्क आशये विश्वा जातान्येषां ।परि धामानि मर्मृशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वे देवा अनु व्रतं नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ āsu ǀ átkaḥ ǀ ā-śáye ǀ víśvā ǀ jātā́ni ǀ eṣām ǀpári ǀ dhā́māni ǀ mármṛśat ǀ váruṇasya ǀ puráḥ ǀ gáye ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who, passing amid those (regions of the firmament), given refuge to all their races, and all thedeities precede the chariot of Varuṇa, when manifesting his glories to perform his worship; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He who, passing amid those (regions of the firmament), given refuge to all their races, and all thedeities precede the chariot of Varuṇa, when manifesting his glories to perform his worship; may all ouradversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स समुद्रो अपीच्यस्तुरो द्यामिव रोहति नि यदासु यजुर्दधे ।स माया अर्चिना पदास्तृणान्नाकमारुहन्नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ samudráḥ ǀ apīcyáḥ ǀ turáḥ ǀ dyā́m-iva ǀ rohati ǀ ní ǀ yát ǀ āsu ǀ yájuḥ ǀ dadhé ǀsáḥ ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ arcínā ǀ padā́ ǀ ástṛṇāt ǀ nā́kam ǀ ā́ ǀ aruhat ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He is the hidden ocean; swift he mounts (the heaven) as (the sun) the sky; when he has plural ced thesacrifice in those (regions of the firmament), he demolishes with his brilliant radiance the devices (of theasuras);he ascends to heaven; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He is the hidden ocean; swift he mounts (the heaven) as (the sun) the sky; when he has plural ced thesacrifice in those (regions of the firmament), he demolishes with his brilliant radiance the devices (of theasuras);he ascends to heaven; may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य श्वेता विचक्षणा तिस्रो भूमीरधिक्षितः ।त्रिरुत्तराणि पप्रतुर्वरुणस्य ध्रुवं सदः स सप्तानामिरज्यति नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ śvetā́ ǀ vi-cakṣaṇā́ ǀ tisráḥ ǀ bhū́mīḥ ǀ adhi-kṣitáḥ ǀtríḥ ǀ út-tarāṇi ǀ paprátuḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhruvám ǀ sádaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ saptānā́m ǀ irajyati ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of whom, present in thethree worlds, the brilliant rays pervade the three realms beyond, the eternaldwelling of Varuṇa, he is lord of the seven (rivers); may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom, present in thethree worlds, the brilliant rays pervade the three realms beyond, the eternaldwelling of Varuṇa, he is lord of the seven (rivers); may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यः श्वेताँ अधिनिर्णिजश्चक्रे कृष्णाँ अनु व्रता ।स धाम पूर्व्यं ममे यः स्कंभेन वि रोदसी अजो न द्यामधारयन्नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ śvetā́n ǀ ádhi-nirnijaḥ ǀ cakré ǀ kṛṣṇā́n ǀ ánu ǀ vratā́ ǀsáḥ ǀ dhā́ma ǀ pūrvyám ǀ mame ǀ yáḥ ǀ skambhéna ǀ ví ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ajáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dyā́m ǀ ádhārayat ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who in his successive functions emits his bright rays or turns them dark, first made his residence (inthe firmament), and as the unborn sun the sky, supports with the pillar (of the firmament) both heaven and earth;may all our adversaries perish.
verses.wilson_translation: He who in his successive functions emits his bright rays or turns them dark, first made his residence (inthe firmament), and as the unborn sun the sky, supports with the pillar (of the firmament) both heaven and earth;may all our adversaries perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLII Varuṇa.
hymns.anukramani: ६ नाभाक: काण्व:, अर्चनाना आत्रेयो  वा ।१-३ वरुण:, ४-६ अश्विनौ ।१-३ त्रिष्टुप् , ४-६ अनुष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LORD of all wealth, the Asura propped the heavens, and measured out the broad earth's wide expanses.He, King supreme, approached all living creatures. All these are Varuṇa's holy operations. So humbly worship Varuṇa the Mighty revere the wise Guard of World Immortal.May he vouchsafe us triply-barred protection. O Earth and Heaven, within your lap preserve us. Sharpen this song of him who strives his utmost, sharpen, God Varuṇa, his strength and insight;May we ascend the ship that bears us safely, whereby we may pass over all misfortune. Aśvins, with songs the singer stones have made you hasten hitherward,Nāsatyas, to the Soma-draught. Let all the others die away. As the sage Atri with his hymns, O Aśvins, called you eagerly,Nāsatyas, to the Soma-draught. Let all the others die away. So have I called you to our aid, even as the wise have called of old,Nāsatyas, to the Soma-draught. Let all the others die away.

verses.sanskrit: अस्तभ्नाद्द्यामसुरो विश्ववेदा अमिमीत वरिमाणं पृथिव्याः ।आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि सम्राड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: ástabhnāt ǀ dyā́m ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ viśvá-vedāḥ ǀ ámimīta ǀ varimā́ṇam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀā́ ǀ asīdat ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ sam-rā́ṭ ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ tā́ni ǀ váruṇasya ǀ vratā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: The possessor of all wealth, the powerful Varuṇa, has fixed the heaven; he has meted the measure ofthe earth; he presides as supreme monarch over all worlds; these all are the functions of Varuṇa
verses.wilson_translation: The possessor of all wealth, the powerful Varuṇa, has fixed the heaven; he has meted the measure ofthe earth; he presides as supreme monarch over all worlds; these all are the functions of Varuṇa
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं नमस्या धीरममृतस्य गोपां ।स नः शर्म त्रिवरूथं वि यंसत्पातं नो द्यावापृथिवी उपस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ vandasva ǀ váruṇam ǀ bṛhántam ǀ namasyá ǀ dhī́ram ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ gopā́m ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ ví ǀ yaṃsat ǀ pātám ǀ naḥ ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ upá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorify then the mighty Varuṇa; reverence the wise guardian of the ambrosia; may he bestow upon usa thrice sheltering habitation; may heaven and earth preserve us abiding in their proximity.
verses.wilson_translation: Glorify then the mighty Varuṇa; reverence the wise guardian of the ambrosia; may he bestow upon usa thrice sheltering habitation; may heaven and earth preserve us abiding in their proximity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इमां धियं शिक्षमाणस्य देव क्रतुं दक्षं वरुण सं शिशाधि ।ययाति विश्वा दुरिता तरेम सुतर्माणमधि नावं रुहेम ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ śíkṣamāṇasya ǀ deva ǀ krátum ǀ dákṣam ǀ varuṇa ǀ sám ǀ śiśādhi ǀyáyā ǀ áti ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ tárema ǀ su-tármāṇam ǀ ádhi ǀ nā́vam ǀ ruhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Varuṇa, animate the sacred acts of me engaging in this your worship; may we ascend thesafe-bearing vessel by which we may cross all difficulties.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Varuṇa, animate the sacred acts of me engaging in this your worship; may we ascend thesafe-bearing vessel by which we may cross all difficulties.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां ग्रावाणो अश्विना धीभिर्विप्रा अचुच्यवुः ।नासत्या सोमपीतये नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ víprāḥ ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀnā́satyā ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: The sacred stones,Aśvins, the pious worshipers,Nāsatyās, have fallen upon their sacred functions,(to induce you) to drink the Soma; may all our enemies perish.
verses.wilson_translation: The sacred stones,Aśvins, the pious worshipers,Nāsatyās, have fallen upon their sacred functions,(to induce you) to drink the Soma; may all our enemies perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा वामत्रिरश्विना गीर्भिर्विप्रो अजोहवीत् ।नासत्या सोमपीतये नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ vām ǀ átriḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ ájohavīt ǀnā́satyā ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: In like manner as the pious Atri,Aśvins, invoked you with hymns, so (I invoke you),Nāsatyās, todrink the Soma; may all our enemies perish.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as the pious Atri,Aśvins, invoked you with hymns, so (I invoke you),Nāsatyās, todrink the Soma; may all our enemies perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एवा वामह्व ऊतये यथाहुवंत मेधिराः ।नासत्या सोमपीतये नभंतामन्यके समे ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ vām ǀ ahve ǀ ūtáye ǀ yáthā ǀ áhuvanta ǀ médhirāḥ ǀnā́satyā ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyaké ǀ same ǁ
verses.english_translation: In like manner as the wise invoke you for protection, so do I invoke you,Nāsatyās, to drink the Soma;may all our enemies perish.
verses.wilson_translation: In like manner as the wise invoke you for protection, so do I invoke you,Nāsatyās, to drink the Soma;may all our enemies perish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THESE songs of mine go forth as lauds of Agni, the disposing Sage,Whose worshipper is ne’er o’erthrown. Wise Agni Jātavedas, I beget a song of praise for thee.Who willingly receivest it. Thy sharpened flames, O Agni, like the gleams of light that glitter through,Devour the forests with their teeth. Gold-coloured, bannered with the smoke, urged by the wind, aloft to heavenRise, lightly borne, the flames of fire. These lightly kindled fiery flames are all around made visible,Even as the gleanings of the Dawns. As Jātavedas speeds along, the dust is black beneath his feet,When Agni spreads upon the earth. Making the plants his nourishment, Agni devours and wearies not,Seeking the tender shrubs again. Bending him down with all his tongues, he flickers with his fiery glowSplendid is Agni in the woods. Agni, thine home is in the floods: into the plants thou forcest way,And as their Child art born anew. Worshipped with offerings shines thy flame, O Agni, from the sacred oil,With kisses on the ladle's mouth. Let us serve Agni with our hymns, Disposer, fed on ox and cow,Who bears the Soma on his back. Yea, thee, O Agni, do we seek with homage and with fuel, PriestWhose wisdom is most excellent. O worshipped with oblations, pure Agni, we call on thee as erst,Did Bhṛgu, Manus, Aṅgiras. For thou, O Agni, by the fire, Sage by the Sage, Good by the Good,Friend by the Friend, art lighted up. So wealth in thousands, food with store of heroes give thou to the sage,O Agni, to the worshipper. O Agni, Brother, made by strength, Lord of red steeds and brilliant sway,Take pleasure in this laud of mine. My praises, Agni, go to thee, as the cows seek the stall to meet,The lowing calf that longs for milk. Agni, best Aṅgiras, to thee all people who have pleasant homes,Apart, have turned as to their wish. The sages skilled in holy song and thinkers with their thoughts have urgedAgni to share the sacred feast. So, Agni, unto thee the Priest, Invoker, strong in forays, prayThose who spin out the sacrifice. In many a place, the same in look art thou, a Prince o’er all the tribesIn battles we invoke thine aid. Pray thou to Agni, pray to him who blazes served with sacred oil:Let him give ear to this our call. We call on thee as such, as one who hears, as Jātavedas, one,Agni! who beats away our foes. I pray to Agni, King of men, the Wonderful, the PresidentOf holy Laws: may he give ear. Him like a bridegroom, him who stirs all people, like a noble horse,Like a fleet steed, we instigate. Slaying things deadly, burning up foes, Rākṣasas, on every side,Shine, Agni, with thy sharpened flame. Thou whom the people kindle even as Manus did, best Aṅgiras!O Agni, mark thou this my speech. O Agni, made by strength! be thou born in the heavens or born in floods,As such we call on thee with songs. Yea, all the people, all the folk who have good dwellings, each apart,Send food for thee to eat thereof. O Agni, so may we, devout, gazed at by men, throughout our days,Pass lightly over all distress. We venerate with cheerful hearts the cheerful Agni, dear to all,Burning, with purifying flame. So thou, O Agni rich in light, beaming like Sūrya with thy raysBoldly demolishest the gloom, We pray to thee for this thy gift, Victor the gift that faileth not,O Agni, choicest wealth from thee.

verses.sanskrit: इमे विप्रस्य वेधसोऽग्नेरस्तृतयज्वनः ।गिरः स्तोमास ईरते ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ víprasya ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ ástṛta-yajvanaḥ ǀgíraḥ ǀ stómāsaḥ ǀ īrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: These repeaters of laudations recite the praises of the wise creative Agni, the uninterrupted sacrificeṛ
verses.wilson_translation: These repeaters of laudations recite the praises of the wise creative Agni, the uninterrupted sacrificeṛ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मै ते प्रतिहर्यते जातवेदो विचर्षणे ।अग्ने जनामि सुष्टुतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ásmai ǀ te ǀ prati-háryate ǀ jā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ ví-carṣaṇe ǀágne ǀ jánāmi ǀ su-stutím ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni,Jātavedas, to you, the liberal offerer (of the oblation), the all-beholding, I repeat earnest praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni,Jātavedas, to you, the liberal offerer (of the oblation), the all-beholding, I repeat earnest praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आरोका इव घेदह तिग्मा अग्ने तव त्विषः ।दद्भिर्वनानि बप्सति ॥
verses.transliteration: ārokā́ḥ-iva ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ áha ǀ tigmā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ tvíṣaḥ ǀdat-bhíḥ ǀ vánāni ǀ bapsati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your fierce flames,Agni, consume the forest, as wild animals destroy (the plural nts) with their teeth.
verses.wilson_translation: Your fierce flames,Agni, consume the forest, as wild animals destroy (the plural nts) with their teeth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: हरयो धूमकेतवो वातजूता उप द्यवि ।यतंते वृथगग्नयः ॥
verses.transliteration: hárayaḥ ǀ dhūmá-ketavaḥ ǀ vā́ta-jūtāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀyátante ǀ vṛ́thak ǀ agnáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The consuming smoke-bannered fires, borne by the wind, spread diversely in the firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: The consuming smoke-bannered fires, borne by the wind, spread diversely in the firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एते त्ये वृथगग्नय इद्धासः समदृक्षत ।उषसामिव केतवः ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ tyé ǀ vṛ́thak ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ iddhā́saḥ ǀ sám ǀ adṛkṣata ǀuṣásām-iva ǀ ketávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These fires separately kindled are beheld like the tokens of the dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: These fires separately kindled are beheld like the tokens of the dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णा रजांसि पत्सुतः प्रयाणे जातवेदसः ।अग्निर्यद्रोधति क्षमि ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇā́ ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ patsutáḥ ǀ pra-yā́ne ǀ jātá-vedasaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ yát ǀ ródhati ǀ kṣámi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Black dust is raised by the feet of Jātavedaswhen he moves, when Agnispreads on the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Black dust is raised by the feet of Jātavedaswhen he moves, when Agnispreads on the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धासिं कृण्वा�� ओषधीर्बप्सदग्निर्न वायति ।पुनर्यंतरुणीरपि ॥
verses.transliteration: dhāsím ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ bápsat ǀ agníḥ ǀ ná ǀ vāyati ǀpúnaḥ ǀ yán ǀ táruṇīḥ ǀ ápi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Making the plural nts his food,Agnidevouring them is never satiated, but falls again upon the young(shrubs).
verses.wilson_translation: Making the plural nts his food,Agnidevouring them is never satiated, but falls again upon the young(shrubs).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जिह्वाभिरह नन्नमदर्चिषा जंजणाभवन् ।अग्निर्वनेषु रोचते ॥
verses.transliteration: jihvā́bhiḥ ǀ áha ǀ nánnamat ǀ arcíṣā ǀ jañjaṇā-bhávan ǀagníḥ ǀ váneṣu ǀ rocate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bowing down (the trees) with his tongues (of flame), and blazing with splendour,Agnishines in theforests.
verses.wilson_translation: Bowing down (the trees) with his tongues (of flame), and blazing with splendour,Agnishines in theforests.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अप्स्वग्ने सधिष्टव सौषधीरनु रुध्यसे ।गर्भे संजायसे पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ agne ǀ sádhiḥ ǀ táva ǀ sáḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ rudhyase ǀgárbhe ǀ sán ǀ jāyase ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your station,Agni, is in the waters; you cling to the plural nts, and becoming their embryo, are born again.
verses.wilson_translation: Your station,Agni, is in the waters; you cling to the plural nts, and becoming their embryo, are born again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदग्ने तव तद्घृतादर्ची रोचत आहुतं ।निंसानं जुह्वो मुखे ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ tát ǀ ghṛtā́t ǀ arcíḥ ǀ rocate ǀ ā́-hutam ǀníṃsānam ǀ juhváḥ ǀ múkhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your lustre,Agni, lambent in the mouth of the ladle, shines when offered from (the oblation of) butter.
verses.wilson_translation: Your lustre,Agni, lambent in the mouth of the ladle, shines when offered from (the oblation of) butter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उक्षान्नाय वशान्नाय सोमपृष्ठाय वेधसे ।स्तोमैर्विधेमाग्नये ॥
verses.transliteration: ukṣá-annāya ǀ vaśā́-annāya ǀ sóma-pṛṣṭhāya ǀ vedháse ǀstómaiḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ agnáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us adore with hymns Agni, the granter (of desires), the eater of the ox, the eater of the marrow, onwhose back the libation is poured.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us adore with hymns Agni, the granter (of desires), the eater of the ox, the eater of the marrow, onwhose back the libation is poured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वा नमसा वयं होतर्वरेण्यक्रतो ।अग्ने समिद्भिरीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ námasā ǀ vayám ǀ hótaḥ ǀ váreṇyakrato íti váreṇya-krato ǀágne ǀ samít-bhiḥ ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit you,Agni, invoker of the gods, performer of sacred rites, with oblations and with fueḷ
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit you,Agni, invoker of the gods, performer of sacred rites, with oblations and with fueḷ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वा भृगुवच्छुचे मनुष्वदग्न आहुत ।अंगिरस्वद्धवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ bhṛgu-vát ǀ śuce ǀ manuṣvát ǀ agne ǀ ā-huta ǀaṅgirasvát ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Holy Agni, to whom oblations are offered, we worship you in like manner (as you have beenworshipped) by Bhṛgu, by Manus, by Aṅgirasa.
verses.wilson_translation: Holy Agni, to whom oblations are offered, we worship you in like manner (as you have beenworshipped) by Bhṛgu, by Manus, by Aṅgirasa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सता ।सखा सख्या समिध्यसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ agnínā ǀ vípraḥ ǀ vípreṇa ǀ sán ǀ satā́ ǀsákhā ǀ sákhyā ǀ sam-idhyáse ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Agni, are kindled by Agni; a sage by a sage, saint by a saint, a friend by a friend.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are kindled by Agni; a sage by a sage, saint by a saint, a friend by a friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं विप्राय दाशुषे रयिं देहि सहस्रिणं ।अग्ने वीरवतीमिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ víprāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ rayím ǀ dehi ǀ sahasríṇam ǀágne ǀ vīrá-vatīm ǀ íṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do you,Agni, bestow upon the pious donor (of the oblation) infinite riches and food withmaleprogeny.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Agni, bestow upon the pious donor (of the oblation) infinite riches and food withmaleprogeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने भ्रातः सहस्कृत रोहिदश्व शुचिव्रत ।इमं स्तोमं जुषस्व मे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ bhrā́taríti ǀ sáhaḥ-kṛta ǀ róhit-aśva ǀ śúci-vrata ǀimám ǀ stómam ǀ juṣasva ǀ me ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, (our) brother, who are elicited by strength, who have red horses, and are (the performer) of purerites, be propitiated by this my praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, (our) brother, who are elicited by strength, who have red horses, and are (the performer) of purerites, be propitiated by this my praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वाग्ने मम स्तुतो वाश्राय प्रतिहर्यते ।गोष्ठं गाव इवाशत ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ agne ǀ máma ǀ stútaḥ ǀ vāśrā́ya ǀ prati-háryate ǀgo-sthám ǀ gā́vaḥ-iva ǀ āśata ǁ
verses.english_translation: My praises hasten to you,Agni, as cows enter their stalls (to give milk) to the thirsting calves.
verses.wilson_translation: My praises hasten to you,Agni, as cows enter their stalls (to give milk) to the thirsting calves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तम विश्वाः सुक्षितयः पृथक् ।अग्ने कामाय येमिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ aṅgiraḥ-tama ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ su-kṣitáyaḥ ǀ pṛ́thak ǀágne ǀ kā́māya ǀ yemire ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you,Agni, who are the chief of the Aṅgirasas, all people have severally recourse for the attainemntof their desires.
verses.wilson_translation: To you,Agni, who are the chief of the Aṅgirasas, all people have severally recourse for the attainemntof their desires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं धीभिर्मनीषिणो मेधिरासो विपश्चितः ।अद्मसद्याय हिन्विरे ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀ médhirāsaḥ ǀ vipaḥ-cítaḥ ǀadma-sádyāya ǀ hinvire ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wise, the intelligent, the sagacious, propitiate Agniwith sacrifices for the attainment of food.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise, the intelligent, the sagacious, propitiate Agniwith sacrifices for the attainment of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वामज्मेषु वाजिनं तन्वाना अग्ने अध्वरं ।वह्निं होतारमीळते ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā́m ǀ ájmeṣu ǀ vājínam ǀ tanvānā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ adhvarám ǀváhnim ǀ hótāram ǀ īḷate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Preparing the sacrifice in their mansions, (the worshippers) adore you,Agni, the powerful, the bearer(of the oblation), the invoker of the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Preparing the sacrifice in their mansions, (the worshippers) adore you,Agni, the powerful, the bearer(of the oblation), the invoker of the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुत्रा हि सदृङ्ङसि विशो विश्वा अनु प्रभुः ।समत्सु त्वा हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: puru-trā́ ǀ hí ǀ sa-dṛ́ṅ ǀ ási ǀ víśaḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ pra-bhúḥ ǀsamát-su ǀ tvā ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are the lord, you behold all people alike in many plural ces; we therefore invoke you in battles.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the lord, you behold all people alike in many plural ces; we therefore invoke you in battles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तमीळिष्व य आहुतोऽग्निर्विभ्राजते घृतैः ।इमं नः शृणवद्धवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ īḷiṣva ǀ yáḥ ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ vi-bhrā́jate ǀ ghṛtáiḥ ǀimám ǀ naḥ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adore that Agniwho shines brightly when fed with offerings of butter, who hears this our invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Adore that Agniwho shines brightly when fed with offerings of butter, who hears this our invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा वयं हवामहे शृण्वंतं जातवेदसं ।अग्ने घ्नंतमप द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ havāmahe ǀ śṛṇvántam ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀágne ǀ ghnántam ǀ ápa ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you,Agni, who are Jātavedas, listening (to our praises), exterminating our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you,Agni, who are Jātavedas, listening (to our praises), exterminating our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विशां राजानमद्भुतमध्यक्षं धर्मणामिमं ।अग्निमीळे स उ श्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: viśā́m ǀ rā́jānam ǀ ádbhutam ǀ ádhi-akṣam ǀ dhármaṇām ǀ imám ǀagním ǀ īḷe ǀ sáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śravat ǁ
verses.english_translation: I praise this Agni, the sovereign of men, the wonderful, the superintendent of holy acts; may he hearme.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise this Agni, the sovereign of men, the wonderful, the superintendent of holy acts; may he hearme.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं विश्वायुवेपसं मर्यं न वाजिनं हितं ।सप्तिं न वाजयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ viśvā́yu-vepasam ǀ máryam ǀ ná ǀ vājínam ǀ hitám ǀsáptim ǀ ná ǀ vājayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invigorate like a horse that (Agni) whose might is everywhere present; who is noble, strong, andbenevolent.
verses.wilson_translation: We invigorate like a horse that (Agni) whose might is everywhere present; who is noble, strong, andbenevolent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: घ्नन्मृध्राण्यप द्विषो दहन्रक्षांसि विश्वहा ।अग्ने तिग्मेन दीदिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ghnán ǀ mṛdhrā́ṇi ǀ ápa ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ dáhan ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ viśváhā ǀágne ǀ tigména ǀ dīdihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slaying the malignant (driving away) our enemies everywhere consuming therākṣasas, do you, Agniblaze forth with bright (radiance).
verses.wilson_translation: Slaying the malignant (driving away) our enemies everywhere consuming therākṣasas, do you, Agniblaze forth with bright (radiance).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यं त्वा जनास इंधते मनुष्वदंगिरस्तम ।अग्ने स बोधि मे वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ indhaté ǀ manuṣvát ǀ aṅgiraḥ-tama ǀágne ǀ sáḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ me ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Chief of the Aṅgirasas, whose men kindle as did Manus;Agni, hear my words.
verses.wilson_translation: Chief of the Aṅgirasas, whose men kindle as did Manus;Agni, hear my words.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदग्ने दिविजा अस्यप्सुजा वा सहस्कृत ।तं त्वा गीर्भिर्हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ agne ǀ divi-jā́ḥ ǀ ási ǀ apsu-jā́ḥ ǀ vā ǀ sahaḥ-kṛta ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We worship with praises you,Agni, who are born in heaven or in the waters, elicited by strength.
verses.wilson_translation: We worship with praises you,Agni, who are born in heaven or in the waters, elicited by strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यं घेत्ते जना इमे विश्वाः सुक्षितयः पृथक् ।धासिं हिन्वंत्यत्तवे ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ té ǀ jánāḥ ǀ imé ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ su-kṣitáyaḥ ǀ pṛ́thak ǀdhāsím ǀ hinvanti ǀ áttave ǁ
verses.english_translation: All these people, the inhabitants (of the earth), offer severally to you (sacrificial) food for your eatingand enjoyment.
verses.wilson_translation: All these people, the inhabitants (of the earth), offer severally to you (sacrificial) food for your eatingand enjoyment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ते घेदग्ने स्वाध्योऽहा विश्वा नृचक्षसः ।तरंतः स्याम दुर्गहा ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ agne ǀ su-ādhyáḥ ǀ áhā ǀ víśvā ǀ nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǀtárantaḥ ǀ syāma ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, through you, may we, skilled in sacrifices and beholding men all our days, pass through (all)difficulties.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, through you, may we, skilled in sacrifices and beholding men all our days, pass through (all)difficulties.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं मंद्रं पुरुप्रियं शीरं पावकशोचिषं ।हृद्भिर्मंद्रेभिरीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ mandrám ǀ puru-priyám ǀ śīrám ǀ pāvaká-śociṣam ǀhṛt-bhíḥ ǀ mandrébhiḥ ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke with cheerful and delightful (hymns) the gladdening Agni, dear to many, who abides in thesacrifice with purifying brilliance.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke with cheerful and delightful (hymns) the gladdening Agni, dear to many, who abides in thesacrifice with purifying brilliance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमग्ने विभावसुः सृजन्त्सूर्यो न रश्मिभिः ।शर्धंतमांसि जिघ्नसे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ vibhā́-vasuḥ ǀ sṛján ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀśárdhan ǀ támāṃsi ǀ jighnase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shining forth,Agni, like the rising sun, displaying your strength by your beams, you destroy thedarkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Shining forth,Agni, like the rising sun, displaying your strength by your beams, you destroy thedarkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तत्ते सहस्व ईमहे दात्रं यन्नोपदस्यति ।त्वदग्ने वार्यं वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ te ǀ sahasvaḥ ǀ īmahe ǀ dātrám ǀ yát ǀ ná ǀ upa-dásyati ǀtvát ǀ agne ǀ vā́ryam ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit from you, strong Agni, that desirable wealth which is in your gift and which decays not.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit from you, strong Agni, that desirable wealth which is in your gift and which decays not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . PAY service unto Agni with your fuel, rouse your Guest with oil:In him present your offerings. Agni, do thou accept my laud, be magnified by this my song:Welcome my sweetly-spoken words. Agni, envoy, I place in front; the oblation-bearer I address:Here let him seat the Deities. Agni, the lofty flames of thee enkindled have gone up on high,Thy bright flames, thou Refulgent One. Beloved! let my ladles full of sacred oil come near to thee:Agni, accept our offerings. I worship Agni—may he hear!—the cheerful, the Invoker, Priest,Of varied splendour, rich in light. Ancient Invoker, meet for praise, beloved Agni, wise and strong,The visitant of solemn rites. Agni, best Aṅgiras, accept straightway these offerings, and guideThe seasonable sacrifice. Excellent God, with brilliant flames, enkindled bring thou hitherward,Knowing the way, the Heavenly Host. Him, Sage and Herald, void of guile, ensign of sacrifices, himSmoke-bannered, rich in light, we seek. O Agni, be our Guardian thou, God, against those who injure us:Destroy our foes, thou Son of Strength. Making his body beautiful, Agni the Sage hath waxen byThe singer and his ancient hymn. I invocate the Child of Strength, Agni with purifying flame,At this well-ordered sacrifice. So Agni, rich in many friends, with fiery splendour, seat thyselfWith Gods upon our sacred grass. The mortal man who serves the God Agni within his own abode,For him he causes wealth to shine. Agni is head and height of heaven, the Master of the earth is he:He quickeneth the waters’ seed. Upward, O Agni, rise thy flames, pure and resplendent, blazing high,Thy lustres, fair effulgences. For, Agni, thou as Lord of Light rulest o’er choicest gifts: may I,Thy singer, find defence in thee. O Agni, they who understand stir thee to action with their thoughts:So let our songs enhance thy might. We ever claim the friendship of Agni, the singing messenger,Of God-like nature, void of guile. Agni who bears most holy sway, the holy Singer, holy Sage,Shines holy when we worship him. Yea, let my meditations, let my songs exalt thee evermore.Think, Agni, of our friendly bond, If I were thou and thou wert I, O Agni, every prayer of thineShould have its due fulfilment here. For Excellent and Lord of wealth. art thou O Agni, rich in light:May we enjoy thy favouring grace. Agni, to thee whose laws stand fast our resonant songs of praise speed forth,As rivers hasten to the sea. Agni, the Youthful Lord of men, who stirreth much and eateth all,The Sage, I glorify with hymns. To Agni let us haste with lauds, the Guide of sacrificial rites,Armed with sharp teeth, the Mighty One. And let this man, good Agni, be with thee the singer of thy praise:Be gracious, Holy One, to him. For thou art sharer of our feast, wise, ever watchful as a Sage:Agni, thou shinest in the sky. O Agni, Sage, before our foes, before misfortunes fall on us,Excellent Lord, prolong our lives.

verses.sanskrit: समिधाग्निं दुवस्यत घृतैर्बोधयतातिथिं ।आस्मिन्हव्या जुहोतन ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-ídhā ǀ agním ǀ duvasyata ǀ ghṛtáiḥ ǀ bodhayata ǀ átithim ǀā́ ǀ asmin ǀ havyā́ ǀ juhotana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Honour Agniwith fuel, awaken him, the guest, with (libations of) butter; offer the oblations in him.
verses.wilson_translation: Honour Agniwith fuel, awaken him, the guest, with (libations of) butter; offer the oblations in him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने स्तोमं जुषस्व मे वर्धस्वानेन मन्मना ।प्रति सूक्तानि हर्य नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ stómam ǀ juṣasva ǀ me ǀ várdhasva ǀ anéna ǀ mánmanā ǀpráti ǀ su-uktā́ni ǀ harya ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, accept my praise, be invigorated by this prayer; be favourable to our hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, accept my praise, be invigorated by this prayer; be favourable to our hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं दूतं पुरो दधे हव्यवाहमुप ब्रुवे ।देवाँ आ सादयादिह ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ dūtám ǀ puráḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀdevā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ sādayāt ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: I set Agniin the front as the messenger, I adore him as the bearer of the oblations; may he cause thegods to sit down here.
verses.wilson_translation: I set Agniin the front as the messenger, I adore him as the bearer of the oblations; may he cause thegods to sit down here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत्ते बृहंतो अर्चयः समिधानस्य दीदिवः ।अग्ने शुक्रास ईरते ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ te ǀ bṛhántaḥ ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ sam-idhānásya ǀ dīdi-vaḥ ǀágne ǀ śukrā́saḥ ǀ īrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brilliant Agni, as you are kindled, your great flames start blazing up.
verses.wilson_translation: Brilliant Agni, as you are kindled, your great flames start blazing up.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उप त्वा जुह्वो मम घृताचीर्यंतु हर्यत ।अग्ने हव्या जुषस्व नः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ tvā ǀ juhváḥ ǀ máma ǀ ghṛtā́cīḥ ǀ yantu ǀ haryata ǀágne ǀ havyā́ ǀ juṣasva ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let my ladles, filled with butter, come near you, O propitious one;Agni, receive our oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: Let my ladles, filled with butter, come near you, O propitious one;Agni, receive our oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मंद्रं होतारमृत्विजं चित्रभानुं विभावसुं ।अग्निमीळे स उ श्रवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: mandrám ǀ hótāram ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀ citrá-bhānum ǀ vibhā́-vasum ǀagním ǀ īḷe ǀ sáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śravat ǁ
verses.english_translation: I worship Agni, the exhilarating invoker (of the gods), the priest, him who shines forth with various lustre,and is rich in brilliance, may he give car.
verses.wilson_translation: I worship Agni, the exhilarating invoker (of the gods), the priest, him who shines forth with various lustre,and is rich in brilliance, may he give car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्नं होतारमीड्यं जुष्टमग्निं कविक्रतुं ।अध्वराणामभिश्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: pratnám ǀ hótāram ǀ ī́ḍyam ǀ júṣṭam ǀ agním ǀ kaví-kratum ǀadhvarā́ṇām ǀ abhi-śríyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: (I worship) the beloved Agni, the ancient adorable invoker (of the gods), the wise, the frequenter ofsacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: (I worship) the beloved Agni, the ancient adorable invoker (of the gods), the wise, the frequenter ofsacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: जुषाणो अंगिरस्तमेमा हव्यान्यानुषक् ।अग्ने यज्ञं नय ऋतुथा ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣāṇáḥ ǀ aṅgiraḥ-tama ǀ imā́ ǀ havyā́ni ǀ ānuṣák ǀágne ǀ yajñám ǀ naya ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, best of the Aṅgirasas, do you, continually accepting these our oblations, conduct the sacrifice atthe due seasons.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, best of the Aṅgirasas, do you, continually accepting these our oblations, conduct the sacrifice atthe due seasons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिधान उ संत्य शुक्रशोच इहा वह ।चिकित्वांदैव्यं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-idhānáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ santya ǀ śúkra-śoce ǀ ihá ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀcikitvā́n ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brilliant-flames giver of food, do you, the knower, when kindled, bring the host of the gods here.
verses.wilson_translation: Brilliant-flames giver of food, do you, the knower, when kindled, bring the host of the gods here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विप्रं होतारमद्रुहं धूमकेतुं विभावसुं ।यज्ञानां केतुमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: vípram ǀ hótāram ǀ adrúham ǀ dhūmá-ketum ǀ vibhā́-vasum ǀyajñā́nām ǀ ketúm ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We solicit the wise invoker (of the gods), the beneficent, the smoke- bannered, the resplendent, thebanner of the sacrifices.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit the wise invoker (of the gods), the beneficent, the smoke- bannered, the resplendent, thebanner of the sacrifices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने नि पाहि नस्त्वं प्रति ष्म देव रीषतः ।भिंधि द्वेषः सहस्कृत ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ ní ǀ pāhi ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ práti ǀ sma ǀ deva ǀ ríṣataḥ ǀbhindhí ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ sahaḥ-kṛta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divine Agni, produced by strength, do you protect us from the injurer, tear asunder our enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Agni, produced by strength, do you protect us from the injurer, tear asunder our enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निः प्रत्नेन मन्मना शुंभानस्तन्वं स्वां ।कविर्विप्रेण वावृधे ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ pratnéna ǀ mánmanā ǀ śúmbhānaḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ svā́m ǀkavíḥ ǀ vípreṇa ǀ vavṛdhe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wise Agni, beautifying his body with the ancient hymn, has grown in might through the intelligenthymner.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise Agni, beautifying his body with the ancient hymn, has grown in might through the intelligenthymner.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्जो नपातमा हुवेऽग्निं पावकशोचिषं ।अस्मिन्यज्ञे स्वध्वरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrjáḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ ā́ ǀ huve ǀ agním ǀ pāvaká-śociṣam ǀasmín ǀ yajñé ǀ su-adhvaré ǁ
verses.english_translation: I invoke Agniof purifying lustre, the son of (sacrificial) food, in this inviolable sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke Agniof purifying lustre, the son of (sacrificial) food, in this inviolable sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स नो मित्रमहस्त्वमग्ने शुक्रेण शोचिषा ।देवैरा सत्सि बर्हिषि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ ágne ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀdeváiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ satsi ǀ barhíṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: OAgni, adorable to your friends, sit down with the gods on our sacred grass with your resplendentradiance.
verses.wilson_translation: OAgni, adorable to your friends, sit down with the gods on our sacred grass with your resplendentradiance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो अग्निं तन्वो दमे देवं मर्तः सपर्यति ।तस्मा इद्दीदयद्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ agním ǀ tanváḥ ǀ dáme ǀ devám ǀ mártaḥ ǀ saparyáti ǀtásmai ǀ ít ǀ dīdayat ǀ vásu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatsoever mortal worships the divine Agniin his house (for the attainment) of wealth, to him he givesriches.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatsoever mortal worships the divine Agniin his house (for the attainment) of wealth, to him he givesriches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्मूर्धा दिवः ककुत्पतिः पृथिव्या अयं ।अपां रेतांसि जिन्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ mūrdhā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ kakút ǀ pátiḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ayám ǀapā́m ǀ rétāṃsi ǀ jinvati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the head (of the gods), the summit of heaven-- he the lord of the earth-- gladdens the seed of thewaters.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the head (of the gods), the summit of heaven-- he the lord of the earth-- gladdens the seed of thewaters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उदग्ने शुचयस्तव शुक्रा भ्राजंत ईरते ।तव ज्योतींष्यर्चयः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ agne ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ táva ǀ śukrā́ḥ ǀ bhrā́jantaḥ ǀ īrate ǀtáva ǀ jyótīṃṣi ǀ arcáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, your pure, bright, shining flames send forth your splendours.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, your pure, bright, shining flames send forth your splendours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ईशिषे वार्यस्य हि दात्रस्याग्ने स्वर्पतिः ।स्तोता स्यां तव शर्मणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ī́śiṣe ǀ vā́ryasya ǀ hí ǀ dātrásya ǀ agne ǀ sváḥ-patiḥ ǀstotā́ ǀ syām ǀ táva ǀ śármaṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, lord of heaven, you preside over (all) that is to be desired or given; may I be your eulogist forhappiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, lord of heaven, you preside over (all) that is to be desired or given; may I be your eulogist forhappiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामग्ने मनीषिणस्त्वां हिन्वंति चित्तिभिः ।त्वां वर्धंतु नो गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ manīṣíṇaḥ ǀ tvā́m ǀ hinvanti ǀ cítti-bhiḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ vardhantu ǀ naḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You,Agni, the wise (praise), you they rejoice with (pious) rites; may our praises invigorate you.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, the wise (praise), you they rejoice with (pious) rites; may our praises invigorate you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अदब्धस्य स्वधावतो दूतस्य रेभतः सदा ।अग्नेः सख्यं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ádabdhasya ǀ svadhā́-vataḥ ǀ dūtásya ǀ rébhataḥ ǀ sádā ǀagnéḥ ǀ sakhyám ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We ever choose the friendship of Agni, the unharmed, the strong, the messenger, the praiser (of thegods).
verses.wilson_translation: We ever choose the friendship of Agni, the unharmed, the strong, the messenger, the praiser (of thegods).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निः शुचिव्रततमः शुचिर्विप्रः शुचिः कविः ।शुची रोचत आहुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ śúcivrata-tamaḥ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀśúciḥ ǀ rocate ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The pure Agnishines forth when worshipped the purest offerer, the pure priest, the pure sage.
verses.wilson_translation: The pure Agnishines forth when worshipped the purest offerer, the pure priest, the pure sage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वा धीतयो मम गिरो वर्धंतु विश्वहा ।अग्ने सख्यस्य बोधि नः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀ máma ǀ gíraḥ ǀ vardhantu ǀ viśváhā ǀágne ǀ sakhyásya ǀ bodhi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May my rites also and my praises ever invigorate you Agni, take thought of our friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: May my rites also and my praises ever invigorate you Agni, take thought of our friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदग्ने स्यामहं त्वं त्वं वा घा स्या अहं ।स्युष्टे सत्या इहाशिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ agne ǀ syā́m ǀ ahám ǀ tvám ǀ tvám ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ syā́ḥ ǀ ahám ǀsyúḥ ǀ te ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ ihá ǀ ā-śíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, if I were you or you were I, your wishes here should come true.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, if I were you or you were I, your wishes here should come true.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वसुर्वसुपतिर्हि कमस्यग्ने विभावसुः ।स्याम ते सुमतावपि ॥
verses.transliteration: vásuḥ ǀ vásu-patiḥ ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ ási ǀ agne ǀ vibhā́-vasuḥ ǀsyā́ma ǀ te ǀ su-matáu ǀ ápi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, you are rich in splendour, the lord of wealth, and the giver of dwellings; may we too abide in yourfavour.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, you are rich in splendour, the lord of wealth, and the giver of dwellings; may we too abide in yourfavour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने धृतव्रताय ते समुद्रायेव सिंधवः ।गिरो वाश्रास ईरते ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ dhṛtá-vratāya ǀ te ǀ samudrā́ya-iva ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀgíraḥ ǀ vāśrā́saḥ ǀ īrate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, my loud praises proceed to you, observant of pious rites, as rivers to the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, my loud praises proceed to you, observant of pious rites, as rivers to the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवानं विश्पतिं कविं विश्वादं पुरुवेपसं ।अग्निं शुंभामि मन्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yúvānam ǀ viśpátim ǀ kavím ǀ viśva-ádam ǀ puru-vépasam ǀagním ǀ śumbhāmi ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I glorify with hymns the ever-young Agni, the lord of men, the wise, the all-devouring, the performer ofmany acts.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify with hymns the ever-young Agni, the lord of men, the wise, the all-devouring, the performer ofmany acts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञानां रथ्ये वयं तिग्मजंभाय वीळवे ।स्तोमैरिषेमाग्नये ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñā́nām ǀ rathyé ǀ vayám ǀ tigmá-jambhāya ǀ vīḷáve ǀstómaiḥ ǀ iṣema ǀ agnáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us seek with our hymns Agni, the conductor of the sacrifices, the mighty, the sharp-jawed.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us seek with our hymns Agni, the conductor of the sacrifices, the mighty, the sharp-jawed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमग्ने त्वे अपि जरिता भूतु संत्य ।तस्मै पावक मृळय ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ agne ǀ tvé íti ǀ ápi ǀ jaritā́ ǀ bhūtu ǀ santya ǀtásmai ǀ pāvaka ǀ mṛḷaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this (my family) also be your worshippers, adorable Agni; O purifier, give them happinesṣ
verses.wilson_translation: May this (my family) also be your worshippers, adorable Agni; O purifier, give them happinesṣ
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धीरो ह्यस्यद्मसद्विप्रो न जागृविः सदा ।अग्ने दीदयसि द्यवि ॥
verses.transliteration: dhī́raḥ ǀ hí ǀ ási ǀ adma-sát ǀ vípraḥ ǀ ná ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀ sádā ǀágne ǀ dīdáyasi ǀ dyávi ǁ
verses.english_translation: You verily are wise, seated at the oblation, wakeful as the seer (for the welfare of living beings);Agni,you ever shine in the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: You verily are wise, seated at the oblation, wakeful as the seer (for the welfare of living beings);Agni,you ever shine in the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुराग्ने दुरितेभ्यः पुरा मृध्रेभ्यः कवे ।प्र ण आयुर्वसो तिर ॥
verses.transliteration: purā́ ǀ agne ǀ duḥ-itébhyaḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ mṛdhrébhyaḥ ǀ kave ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ vaso íti ǀ tira ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise Agni, giver of dwellings, extend our lives,before sins or assailants (destroy us).
verses.wilson_translation: Wise Agni, giver of dwellings, extend our lives,before sins or assailants (destroy us).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN XLV. Indra
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HITHERWARD! they who light flame and straightway trim the sacred grass.Whose Friend is Indra ever young. High is their fuel, great their laud, wide is their splinter from the stake,Whose Friend is Indra ever young.Unequalledin fight the hero leads his army with the warrior chiefs.Whose Friend is Indra ever young. The new-born Vṛtra-slayer asked his Mother, as he seized his shaft,Who are the fierce? Who are renowned? Śavasī answered, He who seeks thine enmity will battle likeA stately elephant on a hill. And hear, O Maghavan; to him who craves of thee thou grantest allWhate’er thou makest firm is firm. What time the Warrior Indra goes to battle, borne by noble steeds,Best of all charioteers is he. Repel, O Thunder-armed, in all directions all attacks on us:And be our own most glorious God. May Indra set our car in front, in foremost Place to win the spoil,He whom the wicked injure not. Thine enmity may we escape, and, Śakra, for thy bounty, richIn kine, may we come near to thee Softly approaching, Thunder-armed wealthy by hundreds, rich in steeds,Unrivalled, ready with our gifts. For thine exalted excellence gives to thy worshippers each dayHundreds and thousands of thy boons. Indra, we know thee breaker-down even of strong forts, winner of spoil,As one who conquers wealth for us. Though thou art highest, Sage and Bold! let the drops cheer thee when we comeTo thee as to a trafficker. Bring unto us the treasure of the opulent man who, loth to give,Hath slighted thee for gain of wealth. Indra, these friends of ours, supplied with Soma, wait and look to thee,As men with fodder to the herd. And thee who art not deaf, whose cars are quick to listen, for our aid,We call to us from far away. When thou hast listened, make our call one which thou never wilt forget,And be our very nearest Friend. When even now, when we have been in trouble, we have thought of thee,O Indra, give us gifts of kine. O Lord of Strength, we rest on thee, as old men rest upon a staff:We long to have. thee dwell with us. To Indra sing a song of praise, Hero of mighty valour, himWhom no one challenges to war. Hero, the Soma being shed, I pour the juice for thee to drink:Sate thee and finish thy carouse. Let not the fools, or those who mock beguile thee when they seek thine aidLove not the enemies of prayer. Here let them with rich milky draught cheer thee to great munificence:Drink as the wild-bull drinks the lake. Proclaim in our assemblies what deeds, new and ancient, far away,The Vṛtra-slayer hath achieved. In battle of a thousand arms Indra drank Kadrū's Soma juice:There he displayed his manly might. True undeniable strength he found in Yadu and in Turvaśa,And conquered through the sacrifice. Him have I magnified, our Lord in, common, Guardian of your folk,Discloser of great wealth in kine; Ṛbhukṣan, not to be restrained, who strengthened Tugra's son in lauds,Indra beside the flowing juice; Who for Triśoka clave the hill that formed a wide receptacle,So that the cows might issue forth. Whate’er thy plan or purpose be, whate’er, in transport, thou wouldst do,Do it not, Indra, but be kind. But little hath been heard of done upon the earth by one like thee iLet thine heart, Indra, turn to us. Thine then shall be this high renown, thine shall these lofty praises be,When, Indra, thou art kind to us. Not for one trespass, not for two, O Hero, slay us, nor for three,Nor yet for many trespasses. I fear one powerful like thee, the crusher-down of enemies,Mighty, repelling all attacks. O wealthy God, ne’er may I live to see my friend or son in need:Hitherward let thy heart be turned. What friend, O people, unprovoked, hath ever said unto a friend,He turns and leaves us in distress? Hero, insatiate enjoy this Soma juice so near to thee,Even as a hunter rushing down. Hither I draw those Bays of thine yokedby our hymn, with splendid car,That thou mayst give unto the priests. Drive all our enemies away, smite down the foes who press around,And bring the wealth for which we long: O Indra, that which is concealed in strong firm place precipitous:Bring us the wealth for which we long Great riches which the world of men shall recognize as sent by thee:Bring us the wealth for which we long.

verses.sanskrit: आ घा ये अग्निमिंधते स्तृणंति बर्हिरानुषक् ।येषामिंद्रो युवा सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gha ǀ yé ǀ agním ǀ indhaté ǀ stṛṇánti ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ānuṣák ǀyéṣām ǀ índraḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those (sages) who kindle Agni, those of whom the ever-young Indrais the friend, continually spreadthe sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Those (sages) who kindle Agni, those of whom the ever-young Indrais the friend, continually spreadthe sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: बृहन्निदिध्म एषां भूरि शस्तं पृथुः स्वरुः ।येषामिंद्रो युवा सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhán ǀ ít ǀ idhmáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ bhū́ri ǀ śastám ǀ pṛthú ǀ sváruḥ ǀyéṣām ǀ índraḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ample is their fuel, many their hymns, broad their sacred shaving-- whose friend is the ever-young Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Ample is their fuel, many their hymns, broad their sacred shaving-- whose friend is the ever-young Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयुद्ध इद्युधा वृतं शूर आजति सत्वभिः ।येषामिंद्रो युवा सखा ॥
verses.transliteration: áyuddhaḥ ǀ ít ǀ yudhā́ ǀ vṛ́tam ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ajati ǀ sátva-bhiḥ ǀyéṣām ǀ índraḥ ǀ yúvā ǀ sákhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Though before powerless to combat, the hero by his might now subdues one surrounded by allies, (ifhelped by those) of whom the ever-young Indrais the friend.
verses.wilson_translation: Though before powerless to combat, the hero by his might now subdues one surrounded by allies, (ifhelped by those) of whom the ever-young Indrais the friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ बुंदं वृत्रहा ददे जातः पृच्छद्वि मातरं ।क उग्राः के ह शृण्विरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ bundám ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ dade ǀ jātáḥ ǀ pṛcchat ǀ ví ǀ mātáram ǀké ǀ ugrā́ḥ ǀ ké ǀ ha ǀ śṛṇvire ǁ
verses.english_translation: The slayer of Vṛtra, as soon as he was born, seized his arrow, and asked his mother, "who are theterrible, who are renowned?"
verses.wilson_translation: The slayer of Vṛtra, as soon as he was born, seized his arrow, and asked his mother, "who are theterrible, who are renowned?"
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति त्वा शवसी वदद्गिरावप्सो न योधिषत् ।यस्ते शत्रुत्वमाचके ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ tvā ǀ śavasī́ ǀ vadat ǀ giráu ǀ ápsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yodhiṣat ǀyáḥ ǀ te ǀ śatru-tvám ǀ ā-caké ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your strong mother answered you, "he who wishes your enmity fights as the elephant in the mountain".
verses.wilson_translation: Your strong mother answered you, "he who wishes your enmity fights as the elephant in the mountain".
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वं मघवंछृणु यस्ते वष्टि ववक्षि तत् ।यद्वीळयासि वीळु तत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvám ǀ magha-van ǀ śṛṇu ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ váṣṭi ǀ vavákṣi ǀ tát ǀyát ǀ vīḷáyāsi ǀ vīḷú ǀ tát ǁ
verses.english_translation: OMaghavan, do you hear (our praise); whosoever desires of you, you bear to him his request, whatyou fix is sure.
verses.wilson_translation: OMaghavan, do you hear (our praise); whosoever desires of you, you bear to him his request, whatyou fix is sure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदाजिं यात्याजिकृदिंद्रः स्वश्वयुरुप ।रथीतमो रथीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ājím ǀ yā́ti ǀ āji-kṛ́t ǀ índraḥ ǀ svaśva-yúḥ ǀ úpa ǀrathí-tamaḥ ǀ rathínām ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Indra, the warrior, goes to battle, desirous of gallant steeds, he is the foremost of the lords ofchariots.
verses.wilson_translation: When Indra, the warrior, goes to battle, desirous of gallant steeds, he is the foremost of the lords ofchariots.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वि षु विश्वा अभियुजो वज्रिन्विष्वग्यथा वृह ।भवा नः सुश्रवस्तमः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sú ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ abhi-yújaḥ ǀ vájrin ǀ víṣvak ǀ yáthā ǀ vṛha ǀbháva ǀ naḥ ǀ suśrávaḥ-tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thunderer, smite all your enemies that you may be scattered-- be to us a most abundant benefactor.
verses.wilson_translation: Thunderer, smite all your enemies that you may be scattered-- be to us a most abundant benefactor.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं सु रथं पुर इंद्रः कृणोतु सातये ।न यं धूर्वंति धूर्तयः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ sú ǀ rátham ǀ puráḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ sātáye ǀná ǀ yám ǀ dhū́rvanti ǀ dhūrtáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra, whom no foes can harm, send before us a beautiful chariot for the acquisition (of ourdesires).
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, whom no foes can harm, send before us a beautiful chariot for the acquisition (of ourdesires).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वृज्याम ते परि द्विषोऽरं ते शक्र दावने ।गमेमेदिंद्र गोमतः ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛjyā́ma ǀ te ǀ pári ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǀ áram ǀ te ǀ śakra ǀ dāváne ǀgaméma ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ gó-mataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Surround Indra, may we escape your enemies; may we come to you abundantly for your gifts, rich incattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Surround Indra, may we escape your enemies; may we come to you abundantly for your gifts, rich incattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शनैश्चिद्यंतो अद्रिवोऽश्वावंतः शतग्विनः ।विवक्षणा अनेहसः ॥
verses.transliteration: śánaiḥ ǀ cit ǀ yántaḥ ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ áśva-vantaḥ ǀ śata-gvínaḥ ǀvivákṣaṇāḥ ǀ anehásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: (May we come), thunderer, slowly approaching you-- may we be rich in horses, possessed of abundanttreasure, ready to offer, and unharmed (by calamity).
verses.wilson_translation: (May we come), thunderer, slowly approaching you-- may we be rich in horses, possessed of abundanttreasure, ready to offer, and unharmed (by calamity).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वा हि ते दिवेदिवे सहस्रा सूनृता शता ।जरितृभ्यो विमंहते ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvā́ ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ divé-dive ǀ sahásrā ǀ sūnṛ́tā ǀ śatā́ ǀjaritṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ vi-máṃhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: (The sacrificer) gives to your praisers day by day hundreds and thousands of excellent and auspiciousgifts.
verses.wilson_translation: (The sacrificer) gives to your praisers day by day hundreds and thousands of excellent and auspiciousgifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विद्मा हि त्वा धनंजयमिंद्र दृळ्हा चिदारुजं ।आदारिणं यथा गयं ॥
verses.transliteration: vidmá ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ dhanam-jayám ǀ índra ǀ dṛḷhā́ ǀ cit ǀ ā-rujám ǀādāríṇam ǀ yáthā ǀ gáyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: We know you,Indra, as the conqueror of wealth, the breaker of firm obstacles, the opener, and(guarding from harm) as a house.
verses.wilson_translation: We know you,Indra, as the conqueror of wealth, the breaker of firm obstacles, the opener, and(guarding from harm) as a house.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ककुहं चित्त्वा कवे मंदंतु धृष्णविंदवः ।आ त्वा पणिं यदीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: kakuhám ǀ cit ǀ tvā ǀ kave ǀ mándantu ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ índavaḥ ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ paṇím ǀ yát ǀ ī́mahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise (Indra) overcomer of enemies, when we solicit you the barterer, may the drops of the Somaexhilarate you the exalted one.
verses.wilson_translation: Wise (Indra) overcomer of enemies, when we solicit you the barterer, may the drops of the Somaexhilarate you the exalted one.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते रेवाँ अदाशुरिः प्रममर्ष मघत्तये ।तस्य नो वेद आ भर ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ revā́n ǀ ádāśuriḥ ǀ pra-mamárṣa ǀ magháttaye ǀtásya ǀ naḥ ǀ védaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant to us the possessions of that rich man who, through his niggardliness, reviles you as to yourbestowal of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant to us the possessions of that rich man who, through his niggardliness, reviles you as to yourbestowal of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इम उ त्वा वि चक्षते सखाय इंद्र सोमिनः ।पुष्टावंतो यथा पशुं ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā ǀ ví ǀ cakṣate ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ indra ǀ somínaḥ ǀpuṣṭá-vantaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ paśúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: These friends, effusing the Soma, look on you,Indra, as men with their fodder ready (look) on theircattle.
verses.wilson_translation: These friends, effusing the Soma, look on you,Indra, as men with their fodder ready (look) on theircattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वाबधिरं वयं श्रुत्कर्णं संतमूतये ।दूरादिह हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvā ǀ ábadhiram ǀ vayám ǀ śrút-karṇam ǀ sántam ǀ ūtáye ǀdūrā́t ǀ ihá ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke you here from afar for our protection, who are never deaf, and whose ears are always opento hear.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you here from afar for our protection, who are never deaf, and whose ears are always opento hear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यच्छुश्रूया इमं हवं दुर्मर्षं चक्रिया उत ।भवेरापिर्नो अंतमः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ śuśruyā́ḥ ǀ imám ǀ hávam ǀ duḥ-márṣam ǀ cakriyāḥ ǀ utá ǀbháveḥ ǀ āpíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: If you hear this our prayer, then display your invincible power and be our nearest kinsman.
verses.wilson_translation: If you hear this our prayer, then display your invincible power and be our nearest kinsman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यच्चिद्धि ते अपि व्यथिर्जगन्वांसो अमन्महि ।गोदा इदिंद्र बोधि नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ ápi ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀ jaganvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ ámanmahi ǀgo-dā́ḥ ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ bodhi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whenever, repairing to you in our distress, we offer our praises, attend to us,Indra, as a giver of cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Whenever, repairing to you in our distress, we offer our praises, attend to us,Indra, as a giver of cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वा रंभं न जिव्रयो ररभ्मा शवसस्पते ।उश्मसि त्वा सधस्थ आ ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ rambhám ǀ ná ǀ jívrayaḥ ǀ rarabhmá ǀ śavasaḥ ǀ pate ǀuśmási ǀ tvā ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of might, we lean on you as the aged on a staff; we long for you in the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of might, we lean on you as the aged on a staff; we long for you in the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोत्रमिंद्राय गायत पुरुनृम्णाय सत्वने ।नकिर्यं वृण्वते युधि ॥
verses.transliteration: stotrám ǀ índrāya ǀ gāyata ǀ puru-nṛmṇā́ya ǀ sátvane ǀnákiḥ ǀ yám ǀ vṛṇvaté ǀ yudhí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing the praise to Indra, who is rich in wealth and bountiful, whom none can slay in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Sing the praise to Indra, who is rich in wealth and bountiful, whom none can slay in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्वा वृषभा सुते सुतं सृजामि पीतये ।तृंपा व्यश्नुही मदं ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ suté ǀ sutám ǀ sṛjāmi ǀ pītáye ǀtṛmpá ǀ ví ǀ aśnuhi ǀ mádam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the Somais effused, I pour the libation to you, showerer (of blessings), for your drinking; satiateyourself, enjoy the exhilarating draught.
verses.wilson_translation: When the Somais effused, I pour the libation to you, showerer (of blessings), for your drinking; satiateyourself, enjoy the exhilarating draught.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा त्वा मूरा अविष्यवो मोपहस्वान आ दभन् ।माकीं ब्रह्मद्विषो वनः ॥
