verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा कण्वे मघवंत्रसदस्यवि यथा पक्थे दशव्रजे ।यथा गोशर्ये असनोर्ऋजिश्वनींद्र गोमद्धिरण्यवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ káṇve ǀ magha-van ǀ trasádasyavi ǀ yáthā ǀ pakthé ǀ dáśa-vraje ǀyáthā ǀ gó-śarye ǀ ásanoḥ ǀ ṛjíśvani ǀ índra ǀ gó-mat ǀ híraṇya-vat ǁ
verses.english_translation: As you, Mahavan, did give abundant kine and gold to Kaṇvaand Trasadasyu, to Pakthaand Daśavraja; as you did give them to Gośarya and Ṛjiśvan.
verses.wilson_translation: As you, Mahavan, did give abundant kine and gold to Kaṇvaand Trasadasyu, to Pakthaand Daśavraja; as you did give them to Gośarya and Ṛjiśvan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN L. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १० पुष्टिगु: काण्व:। इन्द्र: । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BOTH boons,—may Indra, hitherward turned, listen to this prayer of ours,And mightiest Maghavan with thought inclined to us come near to drink the Soma juice. For him, strong, independent Ruler, Heaven and Earth have fashioned forth for power and might.Thou seatest thee as first among thy peers in place, for thy soul longs for Soma juice. Fill thyself full, O Lord of wealth, O Indra, with the juice we shed.We know thee, Lord of Bay Steeds victor in the fight, vanquishing e’en the invincible. Changeless in truth, O Maghavan Indra, let it be as thou in wisdom willest it.May we, O fair of check, win booty with thine aid, O Thunderer, swiftly seeking it. Indra, with all thy saving helps give us assistance, Lord of power.For after thee we follow even as glorious bliss, thee, Hero, finder-out of wealth. Increaser of our steeds and multiplying kine, a golden well, O God, art thou,For no one may impair the gifts laid up in thee. Bring me whatever thing I ask. For thou,—come to the worshipper!—wilt find great wealth to make us rich.Fill thyself full, O Maghavan, for gain of kine, full, Indra, for the gain of steeds. Thou as thy gift bestowest many hundred herds, yea, many thousands dost thou give.With singers' hymns have we brought the Fort-render near, singing to Indra for his grace. Whether the simple or the sage, Indra, have offered praise to thee,He Śatakratu! by his love hath gladdened thee, ambitious! ever pressing on! If he the Strong of arm, the breaker-down of forts, the great Destroyer, hear my call,We, seeking riches cry to Indra, Lord of wealth, to Śatakratu with our lauds. We count not then as sinners, nor as niggardly or foolish men,When with the Soma juice which we have shed we make Indra, the Mighty One, our Friend. Him have we yoked in fight, the powerful Conqueror, debt-claimer, not to be deceived.Best charioteer, the Victor marks each fault, he knows the strong to whom he will come near. Indra, give us security from that whereof we are afraid.Help us, O Maghavan, let thy succour give us this: drive away foes and enemies. For thou, O liberal Lord of bounty, strengthenest his ample home who worships thee.So Indra, Maghavan, thou Lover of the Song, we with pressed Soma call on thee, Indra is Vṛtra-slayer, guard, our best defender from the foe.May he preserve our last and middlemost, and keep watch from behind us and before. Defend us from behind, below, above, in front, on all sides, Indra, shield us well.Keep far away from us the terror sent from heaven: keep impious weapons far away. Protect us, Indra, each to-day, each morrow, and each following day.Our singers, through all days, shalt thou, Lord of the brave, keep safely both by day and night. A crushing Warrior, passing rich is Maghavan, endowed with all heroic might.Thine arms, O Śatakratu, are exceeding strong, arms which have grasped the thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit: प्र सु श्रुतं सुराधसमर्चा शक्रमभिष्टये ।यः सुन्वते स्तुवते काम्यं वसु सहस्रेणेव मंहते ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ śrutám ǀ su-rā́dhasam ǀ árca ǀ śakrám ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀyáḥ ǀ sunvaté ǀ stuvaté ǀ kā́myam ǀ vásu ǀ sahásreṇa-iva ǀ máṃhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: I would praise the far-famed, the bounteousŚakra, for the sake of his protection, who gives desirablewealth by thousands to the presser of the Somaand the offerer of hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: I would praise the far-famed, the bounteousŚakra, for the sake of his protection, who gives desirablewealth by thousands to the presser of the Somaand the offerer of hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतानीका हेतयो अस्य दुष्टरा इंद्रस्य समिषो महीः ।गिरिर्न भुज्मा मघवत्सु पिन्वते यदीं सुता अमंदिषुः ॥
verses.transliteration: śatá-anīkāḥ ǀ hetáyaḥ ǀ asya ǀ dustárāḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ sam-íṣaḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀgiríḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhujmā́ ǀ maghávat-su ǀ pinvate ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ sutā́ḥ ǀ ámandiṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invincible are his hundred-edged weapons, he mighty arrows of Indra; he pours forth blessings on hisliberal worshippers like a mountain rich in springs, when the effused Somahas exhilarated him.
verses.wilson_translation: Invincible are his hundred-edged weapons, he mighty arrows of Indra; he pours forth blessings on hisliberal worshippers like a mountain rich in springs, when the effused Somahas exhilarated him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदीं सुतास इंदवोऽभि प्रियममंदिषुः ।आपो न धायि सवनं म आ वसो दुघा इवोप दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ īm ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ priyám ǀ ámandiṣuḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhāyi ǀ sávanam ǀ me ǀ ā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ dúghāḥ-iva ǀ úpa ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the effused Soma-drops have exhilarated the beloved one, my oblation is offered abundantly likethe waters, O gracious Indra-- it is like the kine to the worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: When the effused Soma-drops have exhilarated the beloved one, my oblation is offered abundantly likethe waters, O gracious Indra-- it is like the kine to the worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अनेहसं वो हवमानमूतये मध्वः क्षरंति धीतयः ।आ त्वा वसो हवमानास इंदव उप स्तोत्रेषु दधिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: anehásam ǀ vaḥ ǀ hávamānam ǀ ūtáye ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ kṣaranti ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ vaso íti ǀ hávamānāsaḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ stotréṣu ǀ dadhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: The prayers which consecrate the Somaflow forth to the incomparable one who calls you for hisfavour, the Soma-drops which invoke you, O gracious one, have set you in the midst of the hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: The prayers which consecrate the Somaflow forth to the incomparable one who calls you for hisfavour, the Soma-drops which invoke you, O gracious one, have set you in the midst of the hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नः सोमे स्वध्वर इयानो अत्यो न तोशते ।यं ते स्वदावन्त्स्वदंति गूर्तयः पौरे छंदयसे हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ sóme ǀ su-adhvaré ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ tośate ǀyám ǀ te ǀ svadā-van ǀ svádanti ǀ gūrtáyaḥ ǀ pauré ǀ chandayase ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He rushes hurrying like a horse to the Somaoffered in our festival, which the hymns make sweet toyou, O you that love sweet viands, you approve the summons to the satisfying Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: He rushes hurrying like a horse to the Somaoffered in our festival, which the hymns make sweet toyou, O you that love sweet viands, you approve the summons to the satisfying Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वीरमुग्रं विविचिं धनस्पृतं विभूतिं राधसो महः ।उद्रीव वज्रिन्नवतो वसुत्वना सदा पीपेथ दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vīrám ǀ ugrám ǀ vívicim ǀ dhana-spṛ́tam ǀ ví-bhūtim ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀudrī́-iva ǀ vajrin ǀ avatáḥ ǀ vasu-tvanā́ ǀ sádā ǀ pīpetha ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise the mighty hero, wide-grasping, spoil-harrying, who has control over vast treasure; you, Othunderer ever pour forth wealth to the worshipper like an abundan fountain.
verses.wilson_translation: Praise the mighty hero, wide-grasping, spoil-harrying, who has control over vast treasure; you, Othunderer ever pour forth wealth to the worshipper like an abundan fountain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यद्ध नूनं परावति यद्वा पृथिव्यां दिवि ।युजान इंद्र हरिभिर्महेमत ऋष्व ऋष्वेभिरा गहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ha ǀ nūnám ǀ parā-váti ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ diví ǀyujānáḥ ǀ indra ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ mahe-mate ǀ ṛṣváḥ ǀ ṛṣvébhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whether you are in the far distance or in the earth or in heaven, OIndra, god of lofty counsel, yoke yoursteeds, come here, lofty one, with the lofty.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether you are in the far distance or in the earth or in heaven, OIndra, god of lofty counsel, yoke yoursteeds, come here, lofty one, with the lofty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: रथिरासो हरयो ये ते अस्रिध ओजो वातस्य पिप्रति ।येभिर्नि दस्युं मनुषो निघोषयो येभिः स्वः परीयसे ॥
verses.transliteration: rathirā́saḥ ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ asrídhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ vā́tasya ǀ píprati ǀyébhiḥ ǀ ní ǀ dásyum ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ni-ghóṣayaḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ pari-ī́yase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your harmless steeds which draw your chariot, which surpass the strength of the wind, with which yousilence the enemy of man and with which you go round the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: Your harmless steeds which draw your chariot, which surpass the strength of the wind, with which yousilence the enemy of man and with which you go round the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एतावतस्ते वसो विद्याम शूर नव्यसः ।यथा प्राव एतशं कृत्व्ये धने यथा वशं दशव्रजे ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́vataḥ ǀ te ǀ vaso íti ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ śūra ǀ návyasaḥ ǀyáthā ǀ pra-ā́vaḥ ǀ étaśam ǀ kṛ́tvye ǀ dháne ǀ yáthā ǀ váśam ǀ dáśa-vraje ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we once more know you as such, O gracious hero, as when you did aid Etaśain the decisivebattle, or Vaśaagainst Daśavraja.
verses.wilson_translation: May we once more know you as such, O gracious hero, as when you did aid Etaśain the decisivebattle, or Vaśaagainst Daśavraja.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा कण्वे मघवन्मेधे अध्वरे दीर्घनीथे दमूनसि ।यथा गोशर्ये असिषासो अद्रिवो मयि गोत्रं हरिश्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ káṇve ǀ magha-van ǀ médhe ǀ adhvaré ǀ dīrghá-nīthe ǀ dámūnasi ǀyáthā ǀ gó-śarye ǀ ásisāsaḥ ǀ adri-vaḥ ǀ máyi ǀ gotrám ǀ hari-śríyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As you were willing to give, OMaghavan, to Kaṇvain the sacrificial feast, or to Dīrghanītha thefriend of the house, as you were willing to give, O slinger, to Gośarya, so give to me a herd of kine shining likegold.
verses.wilson_translation: As you were willing to give, OMaghavan, to Kaṇvain the sacrificial feast, or to Dīrghanītha thefriend of the house, as you were willing to give, O slinger, to Gośarya, so give to me a herd of kine shining likegold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १० श्रुष्टिगु: काण्व:। इन्द्र: । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . OFFER ye up as praise to him that wherein Indra takes delight.The Soma-bringers magnify Indra's great energy with hymns. Good are the gifts that Indra gives. Sole among chiefs, companionless, impetuous, and peerless, heHath waxen great o’er many folk, yea., over all things born, in might. Lord of swift bounty, he will win e’en with a steed of worthless sort.This, Indra, must be told of thee who wilt perform heroic deeds. Come to us hither: let us pay devotions that enhance thy might,For which, Most Potent! thou wouldst fain bless the man here who strives for fame. For thou, O Indra, makest yet more bold the spirit of the boldWho with strong Soma serveth thee, still ready with his reverent prayers. Worthy of song, he looketh down as a man looketh into wells.Pleased with the Soma-bringer's skill he maketh him his mate and friend. In strength and wisdom all the Gods, Indra, have yielded unto thee.Be thou the Guard of all, O thou whom many praise. Praised, Indra, is this might of thine, best for the service of the Gods,That thou with power dost slay Vṛtra, O Lord of Strength. He makes the races of mankind like synods of the Beauteous One.Indra knows this his manifest deed, and is renowned. Thy might, O Indra, at its birth, thee also, and thy mental power,In thy care, Maghavan rich in kine! they have increased exceedingly. O Vṛtra-slayer, thou and I will both combine for winning spoil.Even malignity will consent, O Bolt-armed Hero, unto us. Let us extol this Indra as truthful and never as untrue.Dire is his death who pours no gifts great light hath he who offers them. Good are the gifts that Indra gives.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मनौ सांवरणौ सोममिंद्रापिबः सुतं ।नीपातिथौ मघवन्मेध्यातिथौ पुष्टिगौ श्रुष्टिगौ सचा ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ mánau ǀ sā́m-varaṇau ǀ sómam ǀ indra ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ sutám ǀnī́pa-atithau ǀ magha-van ǀ médhya-atithau ǀ púṣṭi-gau ǀ śrúṣṭi-gau ǀ sácā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As you did drink, OIndra, the effused Somabeside Manu, the descendant of Saṃvaraṇa, by Nīpātithi and Medhyātithi, by Puṣṭigu and Śruṣṭigu, OMaghavan(so do you drink it here).
verses.wilson_translation: As you did drink, OIndra, the effused Somabeside Manu, the descendant of Saṃvaraṇa, by Nīpātithi and Medhyātithi, by Puṣṭigu and Śruṣṭigu, OMaghavan(so do you drink it here).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पार्षद्वाणः प्रस्कण्वं समसादयच्छयानं जिव्रिमुद्धितं ।सहस्राण्यसिषासद्गवामृषिस्त्वोतो दस्यवे वृकः ॥
verses.transliteration: pārṣadvāṇáḥ ǀ práskaṇvam ǀ sám ǀ asādayat ǀ śáyānam ǀ jívrim ǀ úddhitam ǀsahásrāṇi ǀ asisāsat ǀ gávām ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ tvā́-ūtaḥ ǀ dásyave ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The descendant of Pṛṣadvana entertained the aged Praskaṇvawho lay rejected (by his kindred);aided by you the seer Dasyave-vṛkadesired to obtain thousands of cows.
verses.wilson_translation: The descendant of Pṛṣadvana entertained the aged Praskaṇvawho lay rejected (by his kindred);aided by you the seer Dasyave-vṛkadesired to obtain thousands of cows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य उक्थेभिर्न विंधते चिकिद्य ऋषिचोदनः ।इंद्रं तमच्छा वद नव्यस्या मत्यविष्यंतं न भोजसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ukthébhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ vindháte ǀ cikít ǀ yáḥ ǀ ṛṣi-códanaḥ ǀíndram ǀ tám ǀ áccha ǀ vada ǀ návyasyā ǀ matī́ ǀ áviṣyantam ǀ ná ǀ bhójase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sing that Indrawith the new hymn who has no lack of praises, who is wise and the inspirer of seers,who is as it were eager to enjoy.
verses.wilson_translation: Sing that Indrawith the new hymn who has no lack of praises, who is wise and the inspirer of seers,who is as it were eager to enjoy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मा अर्कं सप्तशीर्षाणमानृचुस्त्रिधातुमुत्तमे पदे ।स त्विमा विश्वा भुवनानि चिक्रददादिज्जनिष्ट पौंस्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ arkám ǀ saptá-śīrṣāṇam ǀ ānṛcúḥ ǀ tri-dhā́tum ǀ ut-tamé ǀ padé ǀsáḥ ǀ tú ǀ imā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ cikradat ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ janiṣṭa ǀ páuṃsyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He to whom theysangthe seven-headed hymn with its three parts in the highest region, he has madeall these worlds tremble, and has thus brought forth his power.
verses.wilson_translation: He to whom theysangthe seven-headed hymn with its three parts in the highest region, he has madeall these worlds tremble, and has thus brought forth his power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो नो दाता वसूनामिंद्रं तं हूमहे वयं ।विद्मा ह्यस्य सुमतिं नवीयसीं गमेम गोमति व्रजे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dātā́ ǀ vásūnām ǀ índram ǀ tám ǀ hūmahe ǀ vayám ǀvidmá ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ su-matím ǀ návīyasīm ǀ gaméma ǀ gó-mati ǀ vrajé ǁ
verses.english_translation: We invoke that Indrawho gives us wealth; for we know his new favour; may we obtain a stall rich incows.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke that Indrawho gives us wealth; for we know his new favour; may we obtain a stall rich incows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै त्वं वसो दानाय शिक्षसि स रायस्पोषमश्नुते ।तं त्वा वयं मघवन्निंद्र गिर्वणः सुतावंतो हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ tvám ǀ vaso íti ǀ dānā́ya ǀ śíkṣasi ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ aśnute ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ sutá-vantaḥ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom you help, O gracious one, to give, obtains abundance of wealth; bringing the Somawe invokeyou,Indra,Maghavan, you that love hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: He whom you help, O gracious one, to give, obtains abundance of wealth; bringing the Somawe invokeyou,Indra,Maghavan, you that love hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कदा चन स्तरीरसि नेंद्र सश्चसि दाशुषे ।उपोपेन्नु मघवन्भूय इन्नु ते दानं देवस्य पृच्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ caná ǀ starī́ḥ ǀ asi ǀ ná ǀ indra ǀ saścasi ǀ dāśúṣe ǀúpa-upa ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ magha-van ǀ bhū́yaḥ ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ dā́nam ǀ devásya ǀ pṛcyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never are you niggardly,Indra, and give not to the worshipper; but your godlike gifts, OMaghavan, arepoured forth more and more.
verses.wilson_translation: Never are you niggardly,Indra, and give not to the worshipper; but your godlike gifts, OMaghavan, arepoured forth more and more.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यो ननक्षे अभ्योजसा क्रिविं वधैः शुष्णं निघोषयन् ।यदेदस्तंभीत्प्रथयन्नमूं दिवमादिज्जनिष्ट पार्थिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yáḥ ǀ nanakṣé ǀ abhí ǀ ójasā ǀ krívim ǀ vadháiḥ ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ ni-ghoṣáyan ǀyadā́ ǀ ít ǀ ástambhīt ǀ pratháyan ǀ amū́m ǀ dívam ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ janiṣṭa ǀ pā́rthivaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who overpowered Krivi by his might and silences Suṣṇa with his weapons, when he spread abroadyonder sky and propped it up, then first the dweller on earth was born.
verses.wilson_translation: He who overpowered Krivi by his might and silences Suṣṇa with his weapons, when he spread abroadyonder sky and propped it up, then first the dweller on earth was born.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्यायं विश्व आर्यो दासः शेवधिपा अरिः ।तिरश्चिदर्ये रुशमे परीरवि तुभ्येत्सो अज्यते रयिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ ayám ǀ víśvaḥ ǀ ā́ryaḥ ǀ dā́saḥ ǀ śevadhi-pā́ḥ ǀ aríḥ ǀtiráḥ ǀ cit ǀ aryé ǀ rúśame ǀ pávīravi ǀ túbhya ǀ ít ǀ sáḥ ǀ ajyate ǀ rayíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That wealth, which everyĀryahere covets and every miserly Dāsa, is sent direct to yo, the pious Ruśama Paviru.
verses.wilson_translation: That wealth, which everyĀryahere covets and every miserly Dāsa, is sent direct to yo, the pious Ruśama Paviru.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तुरण्यवो मधुमंतं घृतश्चुतं विप्रासो अर्कमानृचुः ।अस्मे रयिः पप्रथे वृष्ण्यं शवोऽस्मे सुवानास इंदवः ॥
verses.transliteration: turaṇyávaḥ ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ghṛta-ścútam ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ arkám ǀ ānṛcuḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ rayíḥ ǀ paprathe ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǀ śávaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ suvānā́saḥ ǀ índavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The zealous seers have sung a hymn, sweet with Somaand dropping ghī; wealth and manly strengthhav espread themselves among us, and so too the expressed Soma drops.
verses.wilson_translation: The zealous seers have sung a hymn, sweet with Somaand dropping ghī; wealth and manly strengthhav espread themselves among us, and so too the expressed Soma drops.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १० आयु: काण्व:। इन्द्र: । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH powers of Mighty Ones hath he, Ancient, Beloved, been equipped,Through whom the Father Manu made prayers efficacious with the Gods. Him, Maker of the sky, let stones wet with the Soma ne’er forsake,Nor hymns and prayer that must be said. Indra who knew full well disclosed the kine to the Aṅgirases.This his great deed must be extolled. Indra, promoter of the song, the sage's Strengthener as of old,Shall come to bless and succour us at presentation of this laud. Now after their desire's intent the pious singers with the cryOf Hail! have sung loud hymns to thee, Indra, to gain a stall of kine. With Indra rest all deeds of might, deeds done and yet to be performed,Whom singers know devoid of guile. When the Five Tribes with all their men to Indra have sent out their voice,And when the priest hath strewn much grass, this is the Friend's own dwelling-place. This praise is verily thine own: thou hast performed these manly deeds,And sped the wheel upon its way. At the o’erflowing of this Steer, boldly he strode for life, and tookSoma as cattle take their corn. Receiving this and craving help, we, who with you are Dakṣa's sons,Would fain exalt the Maruts’ Lord. Yea, Hero, with the singers we sing to the duly-coming Band.Allied with thee may we prevail. With us are raining Rudras, clouds accordant in call to battle, at the death of Vṛtra,

verses.sanskrit: यथा मनौ विवस्वति सोमं शक्रापिबः सुतं ।यथा त्रिते छंद इंद्र जुजोषस्यायौ मादयसे सचा ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ mánau ǀ vívasvati ǀ sómam ǀ śakra ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ sutám ǀyáthā ǀ trité ǀ chándaḥ ǀ indra ǀ jújoṣasi ǀ āyáu ǀ mādayase ǀ sácā ǁ
verses.english_translation: As you,Śakra, did drink the effused Somafrom Manu Vivasvat, as you did accept the hymn from Trita,so do you gladden yourself with Āyu.
verses.wilson_translation: As you,Śakra, did drink the effused Somafrom Manu Vivasvat, as you did accept the hymn from Trita,so do you gladden yourself with Āyu.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पृषध्रे मेध्ये मातरिश्वनींद्र सुवाने अमंदथाः ।यथा सोमं दशशिप्रे दशोण्ये स्यूमरश्मावृजूनसि ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛ́ṣadhre ǀ médhye ǀ mātaríśvani ǀ índra ǀ suvāné ǀ ámandathāḥ ǀyáthā ǀ sómam ǀ dáśa-śipre ǀ dáśa-oṇye ǀ syū́ma-raśmau ǀ ṛ́jūnasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: You did enjoy,Indra, the effused drink with Pṛṣadhra,Medhyaand Mātariśvan, just as you did drinkthe Somawith Daśaśipra, Daśoṇya, Syumaraśmi, and Ṛjunas.
verses.wilson_translation: You did enjoy,Indra, the effused drink with Pṛṣadhra,Medhyaand Mātariśvan, just as you did drinkthe Somawith Daśaśipra, Daśoṇya, Syumaraśmi, and Ṛjunas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य उक्था केवला दधे यः सोमं धृषितापिबत् ।यस्मै विष्णुस्त्रीणि पदा विचक्रम उप मित्रस्य धर्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ukthā́ ǀ kévalā ǀ dadhé ǀ yáḥ ǀ sómam ǀ dhṛṣitā́ ǀ ápibat ǀyásmai ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ padā́ ǀ vi-cakramé ǀ úpa ǀ mitrásya ǀ dhárma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: (It is Indra) who has appropriated the hymns for himself, who has bravely drunk the Soma, for whom Viṣṇu strode the three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra.
verses.wilson_translation: (It is Indra) who has appropriated the hymns for himself, who has bravely drunk the Soma, for whom Viṣṇu strode the three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य त्वमिंद्र स्तोमेषु चाकनो वाजे वाजिंछतक्रतो ।तं त्वा वयं सुदुघामिव गोदुहो जुहूमसि श्रवस्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ stómeṣu ǀ cākánaḥ ǀ vā́je ǀ vājin ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ sudúghām-iva ǀ go-dúhaḥ ǀ juhūmási ǀ śravasyávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: OŚatakratu, you who are bountiful to him whose praises and oblations you delight in, we, desiringwealth, invoke you, as the milkers call a cow which bears abundant milk.
verses.wilson_translation: OŚatakratu, you who are bountiful to him whose praises and oblations you delight in, we, desiringwealth, invoke you, as the milkers call a cow which bears abundant milk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यो नो दाता स नः पिता महाँ उग्र ईशानकृत् ।अयामन्नुग्रो मघवा पुरूवसुर्गोरश्वस्य प्र दातु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dātā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ mahā́n ǀ ugráḥ ǀ īśāna-kṛ́t ǀáyāman ǀ ugráḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ puru-vásuḥ ǀ góḥ ǀ áśvasya ǀ prá ǀ dātu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who gives to us is our father, the mighty, the strong, he who acts as the sovereign, may he, thestrong rich Maghavan, give us kine and horses, even without our asking for it.
verses.wilson_translation: He who gives to us is our father, the mighty, the strong, he who acts as the sovereign, may he, thestrong rich Maghavan, give us kine and horses, even without our asking for it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै त्वं वसो दानाय मंहसे स रायस्पोषमिन्वति ।वसूयवो वसुपतिं शतक्रतुं स्तोमैरिंद्रं हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ tvám ǀ vaso íti ǀ dānā́ya ǀ máṃhase ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ invati ǀvasu-yávaḥ ǀ vásu-patim ǀ śatá-kratum ǀ stómaiḥ ǀ índram ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: He to whom you give a present that he may obtain abundance of wealth; we, desiring wealth, invokewith our praises IndraŚatakratu, the lord of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: He to whom you give a present that he may obtain abundance of wealth; we, desiring wealth, invokewith our praises IndraŚatakratu, the lord of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: कदा चन प्र युच्छस्युभे नि पासि जन्मनी ।तुरीयादित्य हवनं त इंद्रियमा तस्थावमृतं दिवि ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ caná ǀ prá ǀ yucchasi ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ní ǀ pāsi ǀ jánmanī íti ǀtúrīya ǀ āditya ǀ hávanam ǀ te ǀ indriyám ǀ ā́ ǀ tasthau ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ diví ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never are you heedless, you guard both races, (gods and men); O fourthĀditya, to you belongs the Indra invocation, the ambrosia has risen to heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Never are you heedless, you guard both races, (gods and men); O fourthĀditya, to you belongs the Indra invocation, the ambrosia has risen to heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै त्वं मघवन्निंद्र गिर्वणः शिक्षो शिक्षसि दाशुषे ।अस्माकं गिर उत सुष्टुतिं वसो कण्ववच्छृणुधी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ tvám ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ girvaṇaḥ ǀ śíkṣo íti ǀ śíkṣasi ǀ dāśúṣe ǀasmā́kam ǀ gíraḥ ǀ utá ǀ su-stutím ǀ vaso íti ǀ kaṇva-vát ǀ śṛṇudhi ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: (As you hear) the worshipper who you favour, OIndra,Maghavan, liberal one, you that love hymns, so,gracious one, hear our hymns and our invocation of praise, like Kaṇva's.
verses.wilson_translation: (As you hear) the worshipper who you favour, OIndra,Maghavan, liberal one, you that love hymns, so,gracious one, hear our hymns and our invocation of praise, like Kaṇva's.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अस्तावि मन्म पूर्व्यं ब्रह्मेंद्राय वोचत ।पूर्वीर्ऋतस्य बृहतीरनूषत स्तोतुर्मेधा असृक्षत ॥
verses.transliteration: ástāvi ǀ mánma ǀ pūrvyám ǀ bráhma ǀ índrāya ǀ vocata ǀpūrvī́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀ stotúḥ ǀ medhā́ḥ ǀ asṛkṣata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The old hymn has been sun, you have uttered the prayer to Indra; they have shouted many bṛhatīverses of the rite, many hymns of the worshipper have they poured forth.
verses.wilson_translation: The old hymn has been sun, you have uttered the prayer to Indra; they have shouted many bṛhatīverses of the rite, many hymns of the worshipper have they poured forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: समिंद्रो रायो बृहतीरधूनुत सं क्षोणी समु सूर्यं ।सं शुक्रासः शुचयः सं गवाशिरः सोमा इंद्रममंदिषुः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ índraḥ ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ adhūnuta ǀ sám ǀ kṣoṇī́ íti ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sū́ryam ǀsám ǀ śukrā́saḥ ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ sám ǀ gó-āśiraḥ ǀ sómāḥ ǀ índram ǀ amandiṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indrahas heaped together vast stores of wealth, the two worlds and the sun; the bright pure Soma-drink mixed with milk, has exhilarated Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrahas heaped together vast stores of wealth, the two worlds and the sun; the bright pure Soma-drink mixed with milk, has exhilarated Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ८  मध्य: काण्व:। इन्द्र: । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY our hymns give thee great delight. Display thy bounty, Thunderer.Drive off the enemies of prayer. Crush with thy foot the niggard churls who bring no gifts. Mighty art thouThere is not one to equal thee. Thou art the Lord of Soma pressed, Soma impressed is also thine.Thou art the Sovran of the folk. Come, go thou forth, dwelling in heaven and listening to the prayers of men:Thou fillest both the heavens and earth. Even that hill with rocky heights, with hundreds, thousands, held within.Thou for thy worshippers brakest through. We call on thee both night and day to taste the flowing Soma juice:Do thou fulfil our heart's desire. Where is that ever-youthful Steer, strong. necked and never yet bent down?What Brahman ministers to him? To whose libation doth the Steer, betake him with delight therein?Who takes delight in Indra now? Whom, Vṛtra-slayer, have thy gift and hero powers accompanied?Who is thy dearest in the laud? For thee among mankind, among the Pūrus is this Soma shed.Hasten thou hither: drink thereof. This, growing by Soma and by Śaryaṇāvān, dear to thee,In Ārjīkīya, cheers thee best. Hasten thou hitherward, and drink this for munificence to-day,Delightful for thine eager draught.

verses.sanskrit: उपमं त्वा मघोनां ज्येष्ठं च वृषभाणां ।पूर्भित्तमं मघवन्निंद्र गोविदमीशानं राय ईमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-mám ǀ tvā ǀ maghónām ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ ca ǀ vṛṣabhā́ṇām ǀpūrbhít-tamam ǀ magha-van ǀ indra ǀ go-vídam ǀ ī́śānam ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We come to you, OMaghavan Indra, the highest of Maghavans, the strong of bulls, the mightiestbreakere of forts, the provider of kine, the lord of wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: We come to you, OMaghavan Indra, the highest of Maghavans, the strong of bulls, the mightiestbreakere of forts, the provider of kine, the lord of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवेदिवे ।तं त्वा वयं हर्यश्वं शतक्रतुं वाजयंतो हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ āyúm ǀ kútsam ǀ atithi-gvám ǀ árdayaḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ hári-aśvam ǀ śatá-kratum ǀ vāja-yántaḥ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: You who, waxing in might day by day, did destroy Āyu,Kutsa, and Atithigva, we invoke you,Śatakratu, with your bay horses, rousing you by our offerings.
verses.wilson_translation: You who, waxing in might day by day, did destroy Āyu,Kutsa, and Atithigva, we invoke you,Śatakratu, with your bay horses, rousing you by our offerings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो विश्वेषां रसं मध्वः सिंचंत्वद्रयः ।ये परावति सुन्विरे जनेष्वा ये अर्वावतींदवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśveṣām ǀ rásam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ siñcantu ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀyé ǀ parā-váti ǀ sunviré ǀ jáneṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ yé ǀ arvā-váti ǀ índavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the stones our forth the Somafor us all, the Soma-drops which have been pressed by men afar ornear.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the stones our forth the Somafor us all, the Soma-drops which have been pressed by men afar ornear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वा द्वेषांसि जहि चाव चा कृधि विश्वे सन्वंत्वा वसु ।शीष्टेषु चित्ते मदिरासो अंशवो यत्रा सोमस्य तृंपसि ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvā ǀ dvéṣāṃsi ǀ jahí ǀ ca ǀ áva ǀ ca ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ víśve ǀ sanvantu ǀ ā́ ǀ vásu ǀśī́ṣṭeṣu ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ madirā́saḥ ǀ aṃśávaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ sómasya ǀ tṛmpási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Smite all our enemies and drive them away, may we all obtain their wealth; even amont the Śīṣṭasare you exhilarating Soma-stalks, where you fill yourself with the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Smite all our enemies and drive them away, may we all obtain their wealth; even amont the Śīṣṭasare you exhilarating Soma-stalks, where you fill yourself with the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र नेदीय एदिहि मितमेधाभिरूतिभिः ।आ शंतम शंतमाभिरभिष्टिभिरा स्वापे स्वापिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ nédīyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ít ǀ ihi ǀ mitá-medhābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ śam-tama ǀ śám-tamābhiḥ ǀ abhíṣṭi-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ su-āpe ǀ svāpí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, come very near with your firmly-wise protections; come, O most healthful, with your mos healthfulaid, come, good kinsma, with your good kinsmen.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, come very near with your firmly-wise protections; come, O most healthful, with your mos healthfulaid, come, good kinsma, with your good kinsmen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आजितुरं सत्पतिं विश्वचर्षणिं कृधि प्रजास्वाभगं ।प्र सू तिरा शचीभिर्ये त उक्थिनः क्रतुं पुनत आनुषक् ॥
verses.transliteration: āji-túram ǀ sát-patim ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇim ǀ kṛdhí ǀ pra-jā́su ǀ ā́-bhagam ǀprá ǀ sú ǀ tira ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ ukthínaḥ ǀ krátum ǀ punaté ǀ ānuṣák ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make rich in children that chief of all me, who is victorious in battle and a strong protector; properthoroughly with your powers your singers who cintinually purify their minds.
verses.wilson_translation: Make rich in children that chief of all me, who is victorious in battle and a strong protector; properthoroughly with your powers your singers who cintinually purify their minds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते साधिष्ठोऽवसे ते स्याम भरेषु ते ।वयं होत्राभिरुत देवहूतिभिः ससवांसो मनामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ sā́dhiṣṭhaḥ ǀ ávase ǀ té ǀ syāma ǀ bháreṣu ǀ te ǀvayám ǀ hótrābhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ deváhūti-bhiḥ ǀ sasa-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ manāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we be in battle as one who is the sure to gain your protection; we worship you with invocationsand prayers wen we obtain our desire.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be in battle as one who is the sure to gain your protection; we worship you with invocationsand prayers wen we obtain our desire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अहं हि ते हरिवो ब्रह्म वाजयुराजिं यामि सदोतिभिः ।त्वामिदेव तममे समश्वयुर्गव्युरग्रे मथीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ vāja-yúḥ ǀ ājím ǀ yā́mi ǀ sádā ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ ít ǀ evá ǀ tám ǀ áme ǀ sám ǀ aśva-yúḥ ǀ gavyúḥ ǀ ágre ǀ mathīnā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: With your help, O lord of bay steeds, I always go into prayer and into battle, seeking spoil; it is youwhom I insist upon, when I go, longing for horses and kine, at the head of plural nders.
verses.wilson_translation: With your help, O lord of bay steeds, I always go into prayer and into battle, seeking spoil; it is youwhom I insist upon, when I go, longing for horses and kine, at the head of plural nders.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ८  मातरिश्वा काण्व:। इन्द्र:, ३-४  विश्वे देवा : । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOUGH, Indra, thou art called by men from east and west, from north and south,Come hither quickly with fleet steeds If in the effluence of heaven, rich in its light, thou takest joy,Or in the sea in Soma juice. With songs I call thee, Great and Wide, even as a cow to profit us,Indra, to drink the Soma-draught. Hither, O Indra, let thy Bays bear up and, bring upon thy carThy glory, God! and majesty. Thou, Indra, wouldst be sung and praised as great, strong, lordly in thy deedsCome hither, drink our Soma juice. We who have shed the Soma and prepared the feast are calling thee.To sit on this our sacred grass. As, Indra, thou art evermore the common Lord of all alike,As such we invocate thee now. The men with stones have milked for thee this nectar of the Soma juice:Indra, be pleased with it, and drink. Neglect all pious men with skill in sacred song: come hitherward,With speed, and give us high renown. Gods, may the mighty rest unharmed, the King who gives me spotted kine,Kine decked with golden ornaments. Beside a thousand spotted kine I have received a gift of gold,Pure, brilliant, and exceeding great. Durgaha's grandsons, giving me a thousand kine, munificent,Have won renown among the Gods.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्त इंद्र वीर्यं गीर्भिर्गृणंति कारवः ।ते स्तोभंत ऊर्जमावन्घृतश्चुतं पौरासो नक्षंधीतिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: etát ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ vīryám ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ gṛṇánti ǀ kārávaḥ ǀté ǀ stóbhantaḥ ǀ ū́rjam ǀ āvan ǀ ghṛta-ścútam ǀ paurā́saḥ ǀ nakṣan ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The singers with their hymns, OIndra, this might of yours; singing loudly, they have brought you sacredviands dropping with Soma; the offerers have drawn near with their prayers.
verses.wilson_translation: The singers with their hymns, OIndra, this might of yours; singing loudly, they have brought you sacredviands dropping with Soma; the offerers have drawn near with their prayers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: नक्षंत इंद्रमवसे सुकृत्यया येषां सुतेषु मंदसे ।यथा संवर्ते अमदो यथा कृश एवास्मे इंद्र मत्स्व ॥
verses.transliteration: nákṣante ǀ índram ǀ ávase ǀ su-kṛtyáyā ǀ yéṣām ǀ sutéṣu ǀ mándase ǀyáthā ǀ sam-varté ǀ ámadaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ kṛśé ǀ evá ǀ asmé íti ǀ indra ǀ matsva ǁ
verses.english_translation: They have drawn near Indrawith holy rites for his protection, they in whose libations you rejoice; as youdid rejoice in Samvaraand Kṛśa, so now, Indra, do you rejoice in us.
verses.wilson_translation: They have drawn near Indrawith holy rites for his protection, they in whose libations you rejoice; as youdid rejoice in Samvaraand Kṛśa, so now, Indra, do you rejoice in us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो गंतनोप नः ।वसवो रुद्रा अवसे न आ गमंछृण्वंतु मरुतो हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśve ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ gántana ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀvásavaḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ ávase ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gaman ǀ śṛṇvántu ǀ marútaḥ ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: You gods, come all with one accord to us; let the Vasusand Rudrascome for our protection, let the Maruts hear our call.
verses.wilson_translation: You gods, come all with one accord to us; let the Vasusand Rudrascome for our protection, let the Maruts hear our call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा विष्णुर्हवनं मे सरस्वत्यवंतु सप्त सिंधवः ।आपो वातः पर्वतासो वनस्पतिः शृणोतु पृथिवी हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ hávanam ǀ me ǀ sárasvatī ǀ ávantu ǀ saptá ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀ vánaspátiḥ ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Pūṣan,Viṣṇu, Sarsvatī, and the seven rivers, favour my call; may the waters, the wind, themountains, the trees, the earth, hear my call.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣan,Viṣṇu, Sarsvatī, and the seven rivers, favour my call; may the waters, the wind, themountains, the trees, the earth, hear my call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्र राधो अस्ति ते माघोनं मघवत्तम ।तेन नो बोधि सधमाद्यो वृधे भगो दानाय वृत्रहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ ásti ǀ te ǀ mā́ghonam ǀ maghavat-tama ǀténa ǀ naḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ sadha-mā́dyaḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ dānā́ya ǀ vṛtra-han ǁ
verses.english_translation: With yours own special gift, OIndra, best of Maghavans, be you our boon-companion for good, ourliberal benefactor, O slayer of Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: With yours own special gift, OIndra, best of Maghavans, be you our boon-companion for good, ourliberal benefactor, O slayer of Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आजिपते नृपते त्वमिद्धि नो वाज आ वक्षि सुक्रतो ।वीती होत्राभिरुत देववीतिभिः ससवांसो वि शृण्विरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ji-pate ǀ nṛ-pate ǀ tvám ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́je ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣi ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀvītī́ ǀ hótrābhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ devávīti-bhiḥ ǀ sasa-vā́ṃsaḥ ǀ ví ǀ śṛṇvire ǁ
verses.english_translation: O lord of battle, lord of men, mighty in action, do you guide us in the conflict; far-famed are those whoobtain their desires by sacrificial feasts, by invocations, and by entertaining the gods.
verses.wilson_translation: O lord of battle, lord of men, mighty in action, do you guide us in the conflict; far-famed are those whoobtain their desires by sacrificial feasts, by invocations, and by entertaining the gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: संति ह्यर्य आशिष इंद्र आयुर्जनानां ।अस्मान्नक्षस्व मघवन्नुपावसे धुक्षस्व पिप्युषीमिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: sánti ǀ hí ǀ aryé ǀ ā-śíṣaḥ ǀ índre ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ jánānām ǀasmā́n ǀ nakṣasva ǀ magha-van ǀ úpa ǀ ávase ǀ dhukṣásva ǀ pipyúṣīm ǀ íṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our prayers abide in the true one, in Indrais the life of men; draw near to us,Maghavan, for ourprotection; milk for the streaming drink.
verses.wilson_translation: Our prayers abide in the true one, in Indrais the life of men; draw near to us,Maghavan, for ourprotection; milk for the streaming drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: वयं त इंद्र स्तोमेभिर्विधेम त्वमस्माकं शतक्रतो ।महि स्थूरं शशयं राधो अह्रयं प्रस्कण्वाय नि तोशय ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ vidhema ǀ tvám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀmáhi ǀ sthūrám ǀ śaśayám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ áhrayam ǀ práskaṇvāya ǀ ní ǀ tośaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: OIndra, we would worship you with hymns; OŚatakratu, you are ours; pour down upon Praśkaṇvagreat, solid, inexhaustible, exuberant abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: OIndra, we would worship you with hymns; OŚatakratu, you are ours; pour down upon Praśkaṇvagreat, solid, inexhaustible, exuberant abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ५ कृश: काण्व:। इन्द्र:, प्रस्कण्वश्च । गायत्री , ३, ५ अनुष्टुप्  ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LOUD singing at the sacred rite where Soma flows we priests invokeWith haste, that he may help, as the bard's Cherisher, Indra who findeth wealth for you.. Whom with fair helm, in rapture of the juice, the firm resistless slayers hinder not:Giver of glorious wealth to him who sing a his praise, honouring him who toils and pours: Śakra, who like a curry-comb for horses or a golden goad,Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, urges eagerly the opening of the stall of kine: Who for the worshipper scatters forth ample wealth, even though buried, piled in heaps:May Indra, Lord of Bay Steeds, fair-helmed Thunderer, act at his pleasure, as he lists. Hero whom many praise, what thou hast longed for, oven of old, from men.All that we offer unto thee, O Indra, now, sacrifice, laud, effectual speech. To Soma, Much-invoked, Bolt-armed! for thy carouse, Celestial, Soma-drinker come.Thou to the man who- prays and pours the juice hast been best giver of delightful wealth. Here, verily, yesterday we let the Thunder-wielder drink his fill.So in like manner offer him the juice today. Now range you by the Glorious One. Even the wolf, the savage beast that rends the sheep, follows the path of his decrees.So graciously accepting, Indra, this our praise, with wondrous thought come forth to us. What manly deed of vigour now remains that Indra hath not done?Who hath not heard his glorious title and his fame, the Vṛtra-slayer from his birth? 'How great his power resistless! how invincible the Vṛtra-slayer's matchless might!Indra excels all usurers who see the day, excels all traffickers in strength. O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, we, thy very constant worshippers,Bring prayers ne’er heard before to thee, O Much-invoked, O Thunder-armed, to be thy meed. O thou of mighty acts, the aids that are in thee call forward many an eager hope.Past the drink-offerings, Vasu, even of the good, hear my call, Strongest God, and come. Verily, Indra, we are thine, we worshippers depend on thee.For there is none but only thou to show us race, O Maghavan, thou much invoked. From this our misery and famine set us free, from this dire curse deliver us.Succour us with thine help and with thy wondrous thought. Most Mighty, finder of the way. Now let your Soma juice be poured; be not afraid, O Kali's sons.This darkening sorrow goes away; yea, of itself it vanishes.

verses.sanskrit: भूरीदिंद्रस्य वीर्यं व्यख्यमभ्यायति ।राधस्ते दस्यवे वृक ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ ít ǀ índrasya ǀ vīryám ǀ ví ǀ ákhyam ǀ abhí ǀ ā́ ǀ ayati ǀrā́dhaḥ ǀ te ǀ dasyave ǀ vṛka ǁ
verses.english_translation: Great indeed is Indra's might; I have beheld it; your gift approaches, O Dasyaavevṛka
verses.wilson_translation: Great indeed is Indra's might; I have beheld it; your gift approaches, O Dasyaavevṛka
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतं श्वेतास उक्षणो दिवि तारो न रोचंते ।मह्ना दिवं न तस्तभुः ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ śvetā́saḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ diví ǀ tā́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ rocante ǀmahnā́ ǀ dívam ǀ ná ǀ tastabhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred white oxen shine like stars in the heaven, by their size they have almost held up theheavens.
verses.wilson_translation: A hundred white oxen shine like stars in the heaven, by their size they have almost held up theheavens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतं वेणूंछतं शुनः शतं चर्माणि म्लातानि ।शतं मे बल्बजस्तुका अरुषीणां चतुःशतं ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ veṇū́n ǀ śatám ǀ śúnaḥ ǀ śatám ǀ cármāṇi ǀ mlātā́ni ǀśatám ǀ me ǀ balbaja-stukā́ḥ ǀ áruṣīṇām ǀ cátuḥ-śatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, a hundred dressed hides, a hundred bunches ofbalbajagrass,and four hundred red mares are mine.
verses.wilson_translation: A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, a hundred dressed hides, a hundred bunches ofbalbajagrass,and four hundred red mares are mine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सुदेवाः स्थ काण्वायना वयोवयो विचरंतः ।अश्वासो न चंक्रमत ॥
verses.transliteration: su-devā́ḥ ǀ stha ǀ kāṇvāyanāḥ ǀ váyaḥ-vayaḥ ǀ vi-carántaḥ ǀáśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ caṅkramata ǁ
verses.english_translation: May youu have the gods propitious to you, O descendants of Kaṇva, living through youth on youth;step out vigorously like steed.
verses.wilson_translation: May youu have the gods propitious to you, O descendants of Kaṇva, living through youth on youth;step out vigorously like steed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्साप्तस्य चर्किरन्नानूनस्य महि श्रवः ।श्यावीरतिध्वसन्पथश्चक्षुषा चन संनशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ ít ǀ sāptásya ǀ carkiran ǀ ná ǀ ánūnasya ǀ máhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀśyā́vīḥ ǀ ati-dhvasán ǀ patháḥ ǀ cákṣuṣā ǀ caná ǀ sam-náśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let them praise the seven-yoked team, great is the strength of that which is not yet full-grown; thedark-brown mares have rushed along the paths so that no eye can follow them.
verses.wilson_translation: Let them praise the seven-yoked team, great is the strength of that which is not yet full-grown; thedark-brown mares have rushed along the paths so that no eye can follow them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Ādityas.
hymns.anukramani: ५ पृषध्र: काण्व:। इन्द्र:, प्रस्कण्वश्च ५  अग्निसूर्यौ । गायत्री , ५ पंक्ति:।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now pray we to these Ksatriyas, to the Ādityas for their aid,These who are gracious to assist. May Mitra bear us o’er distress, and Varuṇa and Aryaman,Yea, the Ādityas, as they know. For wonderful and meet for praise is these Ādityas’ saving helpTo him who offers and prepares. The mighty aid of you, the Great, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,We claim to be our sure defence. Guard us, Ādityas, still alive, before the deadly weapon strike:Are yc not they who hear our call? What sheltering defence ye have for him who toils in pouring gifts,Graciously bless ye us therewith. Ādityas, Gods, from sorrow there is freedom; for the sinless, wealth,O ye in whom no fault is seen. Let not this fetter bind us fast: may he release us for success;For strong is Indra and renowned. O Gods who fain would lend your aid, destroy not us as ye destroyYour enemies who go astray. And thee too, O Great Aditi, thee also, Goddess, I address,Thee very gracious to assist. Save us in depth and shallow from the foe, thou Mother of Strong SonsLet no one of our seed be harmed. Far-spread! wide-ruling! grant that we, unharmed by envy, may expandGrant that our progeny may live. Those who, the Princes of the folk, in native glory, ne’er deceived,Maintain their statutes, void of guile— As such, from mouth of ravening wolves, O ye Ādityas, rescue us,Like a bound thief, O Aditi. Ādityas, let this arrow, yea, let this malignity departFrom us or e’er it strike us dead. For, Bountiful Ādityas, we have evermore enjoyed your help,Both now and in die days of old. To every one, O ye Most Wise, who turneth even from sin to you,Ye Gods vouchsafe that he may live. May this new mercy profit us, which, ye Ādityas, frees like one,Bound from his bonds, O Aditi. O ye Ādityas, this your might is not to be despised by us:So be ye graciously inclined. Let not Vivasvān's weapon nor the shaft, Ādityas, wrought with skill,Destroy us ere old age be nigh. On every side dispel all sin, Ādityas, all hostility,Indigence, and combined attack.

verses.sanskrit: प्रति ते दस्यवे वृक राधो अदर्श्यह्रयं ।द्यौर्न प्रथिना शवः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ te ǀ dasyave ǀ vṛka ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ adarśi ǀ áhrayam ǀdyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ prathinā́ ǀ śávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your inexhaustible gift has appeared, O Dasyavevṛka, its fullness is in extent like the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: Your inexhaustible gift has appeared, O Dasyavevṛka, its fullness is in extent like the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: दश मह्यं पौतक्रतः सहस्रा दस्यवे वृकः ।नित्याद्रायो अमंहत ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśa ǀ máhyam ǀ pauta-kratáḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ dásyave ǀ vṛ́kaḥ ǀnítyāt ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ amaṃhata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dasyave-vṛka, the son of Putakrata, has given to me ten thousand from his own store.
verses.wilson_translation: Dasyave-vṛka, the son of Putakrata, has given to me ten thousand from his own store.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शतं मे गर्दभानां शतमूर्णावतीनां ।शतं दासाँ अति स्रजः ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ me ǀ gardabhā́nām ǀ śatám ǀ ū́rṇā-vatīnām ǀśatám ǀ dāsā́n ǀ áti ǀ srájaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A hundred asses a hundred woolly sheep, a hundred slaves, beside garlands.
verses.wilson_translation: A hundred asses a hundred woolly sheep, a hundred slaves, beside garlands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: तत्रो अपि प्राणीयत पूतक्रतायै व्यक्ता ।अश्वानामिन्न यूथ्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: tátro íti ǀ ápi ǀ prá ǀ anīyata ǀ pūtá-kratāyai ǀ ví-aktā ǀáśvānām ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ yūthyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: There too has been brought for Putakrata a well-adorned mare, which is not one of the common horsesof the herd.
verses.wilson_translation: There too has been brought for Putakrata a well-adorned mare, which is not one of the common horsesof the herd.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अचेत्यग्निश्चिकितुर्हव्यवाट् स सुमद्रथः ।अग्निः शुक्रेण शोचिषा बृहत्सूरो अरोचत दिवि सूर्यो अरोचत ॥
verses.transliteration: áceti ǀ agníḥ ǀ cikitúḥ ǀ havya-vā́ṭ ǀ sáḥ ǀ sumát-rathaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀ bṛhát ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ arocata ǀ diví ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ arocata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The shining Agnihas appeared, the bearer of the oblation, with his chariot; Agni has gleamed forthbrilliantly with his bright flame as Sura, he has gleamed forth in heaven as Sūrya.
verses.wilson_translation: The shining Agnihas appeared, the bearer of the oblation, with his chariot; Agni has gleamed forthbrilliantly with his bright flame as Sura, he has gleamed forth in heaven as Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . EVEN as a car to give us aid, we draw thee hither for our bliss,Strong in thy deeds, checking assault, Lord, Mightiest Indra, of the brave! Great in thy power and wisdom, Strong, with thought that comprehendeth allThou hast filled full with majesty. Thou very Mighty One, whose hands by virtue of thy greatness grasp,The golden bolt that breaks its way. Your Lord of might that ne’er hath bent, that ruleth over all mankind,I call, that he, as he is wont, may aid the chariots and the men. Whom, ever furthering, in frays that win the light, in both the hostsMen call to succour and to help. Indra, the Strong, the measureless, worthy of praise, Most Bountiful,Sole Ruler even over wealth. Him, for his ample bounty, him, this Indra do I urge to drink,Who, as his praise was sung of old, the Dancer, is the Lord of men. Thou Mighty One, whose friendship none of mortals ever hath obtainedNone will attain unto thy might. Aided by thee, with thee allied, in frays for water and for sun,Bolt-armed! may we win ample spoil. So seek we thee with sacrifice and songs, chief Lover of the Song,As, in our battles Indra, thou to Purumayya gavest help. O Thunderer, thou whose friendship and whose onward guidance both are sweet,Thy sacrifice must be prepared. To us, ourselves, give ample room, give for our dwelling ample roomGive ample room to us to live. We count the banquet of the Gods a spacious pathway for the men,And for the cattle, and the car. Six men, yea, two and two, made glad with Soma juice, come near to meWith offerings pleasant to the taste. Two brown-hued steeds, Indrota's gift, two bays from Rksa's son were mine,From Asvamedha's son two red. From Atithigva good car-steeds; from Arksa rein-obeying steeds,From Asvamedha beauteous ones. Indrota, Atithigva's son, gave me six horses matched with maresAnd Patakratu gave besides. Marked above all, amid the brown, is the red mare Vṛṣanvati,Obedient to the rein and whip. O bound to me by deeds of might, not even the man who loves to blame.Hath found a single fault in you.

verses.sanskrit: युवं देवा क्रतुना पूर्व्येण युक्ता रथेन तविषं यजत्रा ।आगच्छतं नासत्या शचीभिरिदं तृतीयं सवनं पिबाथः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ devā ǀ krátunā ǀ pūrvyéṇa ǀ yuktā́ ǀ ráthena ǀ taviṣám ǀ yajatrā ǀā́ ǀ agacchatam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ idám ǀ tṛtī́yam ǀ sávanam ǀ pibāthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: You have come quickly, you two gods, with your car, endowed with ancient might, O sacred Aśvins,truthful ones, with your powers, drink this third libation.
verses.wilson_translation: You have come quickly, you two gods, with your car, endowed with ancient might, O sacred Aśvins,truthful ones, with your powers, drink this third libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवां देवास्त्रय एकादशासः सत्याः सत्यस्य ददृशे पुरस्तात् ।अस्माकं यज्ञं सवनं जुषाणा पातं सोममश्विना दीद्यग्नी ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ tráyaḥ ǀ ekādaśā́saḥ ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ satyásya ǀ dadṛśe ǀ purástāt ǀasmā́kam ǀ yajñám ǀ sávanam ǀ juṣāṇā́ ǀ pātám ǀ sómam ǀ aśvinā ǀ dī́dyagnī íti dī́di-agnī ǁ
verses.english_translation: The three-and-thirty truthful gods saw you before the truthful one; OAśvins, gleaming with fire, drinkthe Soma, enjoying our offering, our libation.
verses.wilson_translation: The three-and-thirty truthful gods saw you before the truthful one; OAśvins, gleaming with fire, drinkthe Soma, enjoying our offering, our libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पनाय्यं तदश्विना कृतं वां वृषभो दिवो रजसः पृथिव्याः ।सहस्रं शंसा उत ये गविष्टौ सर्वाँ इत्ताँ उप याता पिबध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: panā́yyam ǀ tát ǀ aśvinā ǀ kṛtám ǀ vām ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀsahásram ǀ śáṃsāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ gó-iṣṭau ǀ sárvān ǀ ít ǀ tā́n ǀ úpa ǀ yāta ǀ píbadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: That work of yours, OAśvins, is worthy of wonder, the bull of the heavens, the firmament and the earth;and your thousand blessings in battle, for all these come here to drink.
verses.wilson_translation: That work of yours, OAśvins, is worthy of wonder, the bull of the heavens, the firmament and the earth;and your thousand blessings in battle, for all these come here to drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयं वां भागो निहितो यजत्रेमा गिरो नासत्योप यातं ।पिबतं सोमं मधुमंतमस्मे प्र दाश्वांसमवतं शचीभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ vām ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ ní-hitaḥ ǀ yajatrā ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ nāsatyā ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǀpíbatam ǀ sómam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ asmé íti ǀ prá ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ avatam ǀ śácībhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O sacred ones, this your portion has been plural ced for you, O truthful ones, come to these your praises;drink among us the sweet Soma, succour your worshipper with your powers.
verses.wilson_translation: O sacred ones, this your portion has been plural ced for you, O truthful ones, come to these your praises;drink among us the sweet Soma, succour your worshipper with your powers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ३ मेध्य: काण्व:। विश्वे   देवा:, १ ऋत्विजो  वा । त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I SEND you forth the song of praise for Indu, hero-gladdener.With hymn and plenty he invites you to complete the sacrifice. Thou wishest for thy kine a bull, for those who long for his approach,For those who turn away from him, lord of thy cows whom none may kill. The dappled kine who stream with milk prepare his draught of Soma juice:Clans in the birth-place of the Gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven. Praise, even as he is known, with song Indra the guardian of the kine,The Son of Truth, Lord of the brave. Hither his Bay Steeds have been sent, red Steeds are on the sacred grass,,Where we in concert sing our songs. For Indra Thunder-armed the kine have yielded mingled milk and meath,What time he found them in the vault. When I and Indra mount on high up to the Bright One's place and home,We, having drunk of meath, will reach his seat whose Friends are three times seven. Sing, sing ye forth your songs of praise, ye Briyamedhas, sing your songs:Yea, let young children sing their lauds as a strong castle praise ye him. Now loudly let the viol sound, the lute send out its voice with might,Shrill be, the music of the string. To Indra. is the hymn up-raised. When hither speed the dappled cows, unflinching, easy to be milked,Seize quickly, as it bursts away, the Soma juice for Indra's drink. Indra hath drunk, Agni hath drunk. all Deities have drunk their fill.Here Varuṇa shall have his home, to whom the floods have sung aloud as mother-kine unto their calves. Thou, Varuṇa, to whom belong Seven Rivers, art a glorious God.The waters flow into thy throat as ’twere a pipe with ample mouth. He who hath made the fleet steeds spring, well-harnessed, to the worshipper,He, the swift Guide, is that fair form that loosed the horses near at hand. Indra, the very Mighty, holds his enemies in utter scorn.He, far away, and yet a child, cleft the cloud smitten by his voice. He, yet a boy exceeding small, mounted his newly-fashioned car.He for his Mother and his Sire cooked the wild mighty buffalo. Lord of the home, fair-helmeted, ascend thy chariot wrought of gold.We will attend the Heavenly One, the thousand-footed, red of hue, matchless, who blesses where he goes. With reverence they come hitherward to him as to. a Sovran lord,That they may bring him near for this man's good success, to prosper and bestow his gifts. The Priyamedhas have observed the offering of the men of old,Of ancient custom, while they strewed the sacred grass, and spread their sacrificial food.

verses.sanskrit: यमृत्विजो बहुधा कल्पयंतः सचेतसो यज्ञमिमं वहंति ।यो अनूचानो ब्राह्मणो युक्त आसीत्का स्वित्तत्र यजमानस्य संवित् ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ ṛtvíjaḥ ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ kalpáyantaḥ ǀ sá-cetasaḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ imám ǀ váhanti ǀyáḥ ǀ anūcānáḥ ǀ brāhmaṇáḥ ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ kā́ ǀ svit ǀ tátra ǀ yájamānasya ǀ sam-vít ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom the wise priests bring, when they arrange the offering in many ways, who was employed as alearnedbrāhmaṇa, what is the offerer's knowledge regarding him?
verses.wilson_translation: He whom the wise priests bring, when they arrange the offering in many ways, who was employed as alearnedbrāhmaṇa, what is the offerer's knowledge regarding him?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: एक एवाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूर्यो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः ।एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं वि भात्येकं वा इदं वि बभूव सर्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: ékaḥ ǀ evá ǀ agníḥ ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ánu ǀ prá-bhūtaḥ ǀékā ǀ evá ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ sárvam ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ bhāti ǀ ékam ǀ vái ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ babhūva ǀ sárvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agniis one, though kindled in various ways; one is the Sun, pre- eminent over all; one Dawn illuminesthis all; one is that which has become this all.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis one, though kindled in various ways; one is the Sun, pre- eminent over all; one Dawn illuminesthis all; one is that which has become this all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: ज्योतिष्मंतं केतुमंतं त्रिचक्रं सुखं रथं सुषदं भूरिवारं ।चित्रामघा यस्य योगेऽधिजज्ञे तं वां हुवे अति रिक्तं पिबध्यै ॥
verses.transliteration: jyótiṣmantam ǀ ketu-mántam ǀ tri-cakrám ǀ su-khám ǀ rátham ǀ su-sádam ǀ bhū́ri-vāram ǀcitrá-maghā ǀ yásya ǀ yóge ǀ adhi-jajñe ǀ tám ǀ vām ǀ huvé ǀ áti ǀ riktam ǀ píbadhyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: The brilliant chariot, diffusing splendour, rolling lightly on its three wheels, offering an easy seat, and fullof many gifts, at whose yoking the Dawn was born, rich in marvellous treasures, I invoke that your chariot (OAśvins), come you here to drink.
verses.wilson_translation: The brilliant chariot, diffusing splendour, rolling lightly on its three wheels, offering an easy seat, and fullof many gifts, at whose yoking the Dawn was born, rich in marvellous treasures, I invoke that your chariot (OAśvins), come you here to drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE who, as Sovran Lord of men, moves with his chariots unrestrained,The Vṛtra-slayer vanquisher, of fighting hosts, preeminent, is praised with song. Honour that Indra, Puruhanman! for his aid, in whose sustaining hand of old,The splendid bolt of thunder was deposited, as the great Sun was set in heaven. No one by deed attains to him who works and strengthens evermore:No, not by sacrifice, to Indra. praised o all, resistless, daring, bold in might. The potent Conqueror, invincible in war, him at whose birth the Mighty Ones,The Kine who spreadafar, sent their loud voices out, heavens, earths seat their loud voices out, O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were thine—No, not a thousand Suns could match thee at thy birth, not both the worlds, O Thunderer. Thou, Hero, hast performed thy hero deeds with might, yea, all with strength, O Strongest One.Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with wondrous aids. Let not a godless mortal gain this food, O thou whose life is long!But one who yokes the bright-hued steeds, the Etasas, even Indra yoker of the Bays. Urge ye the Conqueror to give, your Indra greatly to be praised,To be invoked in shallow waters and in depths, to be invoked in deeds of might. O Vasu, O thou Hero, raise us up to ample opulence.Raise us to gain of mighty wealth, O Maghavan, O Indra, to sublime renown. Indra, thou justifiest us, and tramplest down thy slanderers.Guard thyself, valiant Hero, in thy vital parts: strike down the Dāsa with thy blows. The man who brings no sacrifice, inhuman, godless, infidel,Him let his friend the mountain cast to rapid death, the mountain cast the Dasyu down. O Mightiest Indra, loving us, gather thou up, as grains of corn,Within thine hand, of these their kine, to give away, yea, gather twice as loving us. O my companions, wish for power. How may we perfect Sara's praise,The liberal princely patron, never to be harmed? By many a sage whose grass is trimmed thou art continually praised,That thou, O Sara, hast bestowed here one and here another calf. The noble, Suradeva's son, hath brought a calf, led by the car to three of us.As a chief brings a goat to milk.

verses.sanskrit: इमानि वां भागधेयानि सिस्रत इंद्रावरुणा प्र महे सुतेषु वां ।यज्ञेयज्ञे ह सवना भुरण्यथो यत्सुन्वते यजमानाय शिक्षथः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ni ǀ vām ǀ bhāga-dhéyāni ǀ sisrate ǀ índrāvaruṇā ǀ prá ǀ mahé ǀ sutéṣu ǀ vām ǀyajñé-yajñe ǀ ha ǀ sávanā ǀ bhuraṇyáthaḥ ǀ yát ǀ sunvaté ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śíkṣathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These your offered portions stream forth, OIndraand Varuṇa, to your honour in the oblations; at everysacrifice you hasten to the oblations, when you help the offerer who presses out the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: These your offered portions stream forth, OIndraand Varuṇa, to your honour in the oblations; at everysacrifice you hasten to the oblations, when you help the offerer who presses out the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: निष्षिध्वरीरोषधीराप आस्तामिंद्रावरुणा महिमानमाशत ।या सिस्रतू रजसः पारे अध्वनो ययोः शत्रुर्नकिरादेव ओहते ॥
verses.transliteration: niḥ-sídhvarīḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ āstām ǀ índrāvaruṇā ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ āśata ǀyā́ ǀ sísratuḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ pāré ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ yáyoḥ ǀ śátruḥ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ ádevaḥ ǀ óhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The plural nts and the waters were efficacious, they have attained their power, Oindraand Varuṇa, youwho have gone beyond the path of the firmament, no godless man is worth being called your enemy.
verses.wilson_translation: The plural nts and the waters were efficacious, they have attained their power, Oindraand Varuṇa, youwho have gone beyond the path of the firmament, no godless man is worth being called your enemy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं तदिंद्रावरुणा कृशस्य वां मध्व ऊर्मिं दुहते सप्त वाणीः ।ताभिर्दाश्वांसमवतं शुभस्पती यो वामदब्धो अभि पाति चित्तिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: satyám ǀ tát ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ kṛśásya ǀ vām ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ūrmím ǀ duhate ǀ saptá ǀ vā́ṇīḥ ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ dāśvā́ṃsam ǀ avatam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ ádabdhaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pā́ti ǀ cítti-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: True, OIndraand Varuṇa, is that saying of Kṛsa's, 'the seven sacred voices distil a stream of honey',for their sake help the worshipper, O you lords of splendour, who reverence you devoutly in his thoughts.
verses.wilson_translation: True, OIndraand Varuṇa, is that saying of Kṛsa's, 'the seven sacred voices distil a stream of honey',for their sake help the worshipper, O you lords of splendour, who reverence you devoutly in his thoughts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: घृतप्रुषः सौम्या जीरदानवः सप्त स्वसारः सदन ऋतस्य ।या ह वामिंद्रावरुणा घृतश्चुतस्ताभिर्धत्तं यजमानाय शिक्षतं ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛta-prúṣaḥ ǀ sáumyāḥ ǀ jīrá-dānavaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ svásāraḥ ǀ sádane ǀ ṛtásya ǀyā́ḥ ǀ ha ǀ vām ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ghṛta-ścútaḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ dhattam ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śikṣatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven sister-streams of the Soma, in the hot the offering, pour forth ghī-dripping streams of yours,OIndra Varuṇa, provide for and help the offerer.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven sister-streams of the Soma, in the hot the offering, pour forth ghī-dripping streams of yours,OIndra Varuṇa, provide for and help the offerer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अवोचाम महते सौभगाय सत्यं त्वेषाभ्यां महिमानमिंद्रियं ।अस्मान्त्स्विंद्रावरुणा घृतश्चुतस्त्रिभिः साप्तेभिरवतं शुभस्पती ॥
verses.transliteration: ávocāma ǀ mahaté ǀ sáubhagāya ǀ satyám ǀ tveṣā́bhyām ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ indriyám ǀasmā́n ǀ sú ǀ indrāvaruṇā ǀ ghṛta-ścútaḥ ǀ trí-bhiḥ ǀ sāptébhiḥ ǀ avatam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: To our great happiness we hae declared to these two brilliant ones the true might of Indra; O indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendour, help us, the offerers of ghī, with the company of thrice seven.
verses.wilson_translation: To our great happiness we hae declared to these two brilliant ones the true might of Indra; O indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendour, help us, the offerers of ghī, with the company of thrice seven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणा यदृषिभ्यो मनीषां वाचो मतिं श्रुतमदत्तमग्रे ।यानि स्थानान्यसृजंत धीरा यज्ञं तन्वानास्तपसाभ्यपश्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇā ǀ yát ǀ ṛṣí-bhyaḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ vācáḥ ǀ matím ǀ śrutám ǀ adattam ǀ ágre ǀyā́ni ǀ sthā́nāni ǀ asṛjanta ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ tanvānā́ḥ ǀ tápasā ǀ abhí ǀ apaśyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: OIndraand Varuṇa, I have seen what you formerly gave to the seers, wisdom, power of song, andfame, and the plural ces which the wise have prepared for themselves, as they spread the web of the sacrifice withholy austerities.
verses.wilson_translation: OIndraand Varuṇa, I have seen what you formerly gave to the seers, wisdom, power of song, andfame, and the plural ces which the wise have prepared for themselves, as they spread the web of the sacrifice withholy austerities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रावरुणा सौमनसमदृप्तं रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धत्तं ।प्रजां पुष्टिं भूतिमस्मासु धत्तं दीर्घायुत्वाय प्र तिरतं न आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāvaruṇā ǀ saumanasám ǀ ádṛptam ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ yájamāneṣu ǀ dhattam ǀpra-jā́m ǀ puṣṭím ǀ bhūtim ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhattam ǀ dīrghāyu-tvā́ya ǀ prá ǀ tiratam ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: OIndraand Varuṇa, give to the offerers cheerfulness without levity, and abundance of wealth; give tous offspring, food, prosperity; prolong our lives to length of days.
verses.wilson_translation: OIndraand Varuṇa, give to the offerers cheerfulness without levity, and abundance of wealth; give tous offspring, food, prosperity; prolong our lives to length of days.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN LX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: २०  भर्ग: प्रागाथ: । अग्नि: । प्रगाथ:= ( विषमा बृहती, समा सतोबृहती ) ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O AGNI, with thy mighty wealth guard us from all malignity,Yea, from all hate of mortal man. For over thee, O Friend from birth, the wrath of man hath no control:Nay, Guardian of the earth art thou. As such, with all the Gods, O Son of Strength, auspicious in thy flame.Give us wealth bringing all things good. Malignities stay not from wealth the mortal man whom, Agni, thouProtectest while he offers gifts. Sage Agni, be whom thou dost urge, in worship of the Gods, to wealth,With thine assistance winneth kine. Riches with many heroes thou hast for the man who offers gifts:Lead thou us on to higher bliss. Save us, O Jātavedas, nor abandon us to him who sins,Unto the evil-hearted man. O Agni, let no godless man avert thy bounty as a God:Over all treasures thou art Lord. So, Son of Strength, thou aidest us to what is great and excellent.Those, Vasu! Friend! who sing thy praise. Let our songs come anear to him beauteous and bright with piercing flameOur offerings, with our homage, to theLord of wealth, to him whom many praise, for help: To Agni Jātavedas, to the Son of Strength, that he may give us precious gifts,Immortal, from of old Priest among mortal men, the most delightful in the house. Agni, made yours by sacrifice, Agni, while holy rites advance;Agni, the first in songs, first with the warrior steed; Agni to win the land for us. May Agni who is Lord of wealth vouchsafe us food for friendship sake.Agni we ever seek for seed and progeny, the Vasu who protects our lives. Solicit with your chants, for help, Agni the God with piercing flame,For riches famous Agni, Purumīlha and ye men! Agni to light our dwelling well. Agni we laud that he may keep our foes afar, Agni to give us health and strength.Let him as Guardian be invoked in all the tribes, the lighter-up of glowing brands.

verses.sanskrit: अग्न आ याह्यग्निभिर्होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे ।आ त्वामनक्तु प्रयता हविष्मती यजिष्ठं बर्हिरासदे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ agní-bhiḥ ǀ hótāram ǀ tvā ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀā́ ǀ tvā́m ǀ anaktu ǀ prá-yatā ǀ havíṣmatī ǀ yájiṣṭham ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā-sáde ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, come here with the fires, we choose you as our invoking priest; let the presented offering anointyou, the chief sacrificer, to sit down on the sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, come here with the fires, we choose you as our invoking priest; let the presented offering anointyou, the chief sacrificer, to sit down on the sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा हि त्वा सहसः सूनो अंगिरः स्रुचश्चरंत्यध्वरे ।ऊर्जो नपातं घृतकेशमीमहेऽग्निं यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ aṅgiraḥ ǀ srúcaḥ ǀ cáranti ǀ adhvaré ǀūrjáḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ ghṛtá-keśam ǀ īmahe ǀ agním ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ pūrvyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aṅgirasa, son of strength, the ladles go to find you in the sacrifice; we praise the ancient Agniin ourofferings, the grandson of food, butter-haired.
verses.wilson_translation: Aṅgirasa, son of strength, the ladles go to find you in the sacrifice; we praise the ancient Agniin ourofferings, the grandson of food, butter-haired.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने कविर्वेधा असि होता पावक यक्ष्यः ।मंद्रो यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यो विप्रेभिः शुक्र मन्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ kavíḥ ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ asi ǀ hótā ǀ pāvaka ǀ yákṣyaḥ ǀmandráḥ ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ víprebhiḥ ǀ śukra ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, you, wise, are the creator (of consequences); O purifier, you are the involving priest, worthy ofworship; bright one, you are to be praised in our sacrifices by the priests with hymns, yourself the chief ministrantworthy to be rejoiced in.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, you, wise, are the creator (of consequences); O purifier, you are the involving priest, worthy ofworship; bright one, you are to be praised in our sacrifices by the priests with hymns, yourself the chief ministrantworthy to be rejoiced in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अद्रोघमा वहोशतो यविष्ठ्य देवाँ अजस्र वीतये ।अभि प्रयांसि सुधिता वसो गहि मंदस्व धीतिभिर्हितः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádrogham ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǀ devā́n ǀ ajasra ǀ vītáye ǀabhí ǀ práyāṃsi ǀ sú-dhitā ǀ ā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ gahi ǀ mándasva ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most youthful, eternal one, bring the longing gods to me guileless, to eat (the oblation); giver ofdwellings, approach the well-plural ced food; rejoice, being set in your plural ce with praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Most youthful, eternal one, bring the longing gods to me guileless, to eat (the oblation); giver ofdwellings, approach the well-plural ced food; rejoice, being set in your plural ce with praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमित्सप्रथा अस्यग्ने त्रातर्ऋतस्कविः ।त्वां विप्रासः समिधान दीदिव आ विवासंति वेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ít ǀ sa-práthāḥ ǀ asi ǀ ágne ǀ trātaḥ ǀ ṛtáḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ sam-idhāna ǀ dīdi-vaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsanti ǀ vedhásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Deliverer Agni, you, the truthful and the seer, are widely spread; O kindled blazing one, the wisepraisers wait on you.
verses.wilson_translation: Deliverer Agni, you, the truthful and the seer, are widely spread; O kindled blazing one, the wisepraisers wait on you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: शोचा शोचिष्ठ दीदिहि विशे मयो रास्व स्तोत्रे महाँ असि ।देवानां शर्मन्मम संतु सूरयः शत्रूषाहः स्वग्नयः ॥
verses.transliteration: śóca ǀ śociṣṭha ǀ dīdihí ǀ viśé ǀ máyaḥ ǀ rā́sva ǀ stotré ǀ mahā́n ǀ asi ǀdevā́nām ǀ śárman ǀ máma ǀ santu ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ śatru-sáhaḥ ǀ su-agnáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most resplendent (Agni), shine forth and illuminate (us); give happiness to your people, to yourworshipper, for you are great; may my priests abide in the bliss of the gods, subduing their enemies, possessingbright fires.
verses.wilson_translation: Most resplendent (Agni), shine forth and illuminate (us); give happiness to your people, to yourworshipper, for you are great; may my priests abide in the bliss of the gods, subduing their enemies, possessingbright fires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यथा चिद्वृद्धमतसमग्ने संजूर्वसि क्षमि ।एवा दह मित्रमहो यो अस्मध्रुग्दुर्मन्मा कश्च वेनति ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ cit ǀ vṛddhám ǀ atasám ǀ ágne ǀ sam-jū́rvasi ǀ kṣámi ǀevá ǀ daha ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ asma-dhrúk ǀ duḥ-mánmā ǀ káḥ ǀ ca ǀ vénati ǁ
verses.english_translation: As,Agni, you consume old timber on the earth, so, cherisher of friends, do you burn our injurer,whosoever evil-minded wishes (our ill).
verses.wilson_translation: As,Agni, you consume old timber on the earth, so, cherisher of friends, do you burn our injurer,whosoever evil-minded wishes (our ill).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो मर्ताय रिपवे रक्षस्विने माघशंसाय रीरधः ।अस्रेधद्भिस्तरणिभिर्यविष्ठ्य शिवेभिः पाहि पायुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mártāya ǀ ripáve ǀ rakṣasvíne ǀ mā́ ǀ aghá-śaṃsāya ǀ rīradhaḥ ǀásredhat-bhiḥ ǀ taráṇi-bhiḥ ǀ yaviṣṭhya ǀ śivébhiḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ pāyú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Subject us not to a strong mortal enemy, nor to the malevolent; O most youthful, guard us with yourunharming delivering auspicious protections.
verses.wilson_translation: Subject us not to a strong mortal enemy, nor to the malevolent; O most youthful, guard us with yourunharming delivering auspicious protections.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)
