verses.griffith_verse: He who is Lord of all divine oblation, shared by all living men at break of morning, Agni to whom our offerings are devoted, in whom rests he whose car, through might, is scatheless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शूषेभिर्वृधो जुषाणो अर्कैर्देवाँ अच्छा रघुपत्वा जिगाति ।मंद्रो होता स जुह्वा यजिष्ठः सम्मिश्लो अग्निरा जिघर्ति देवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: śūṣébhiḥ ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ juṣāṇáḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ áccha ǀ raghu-pátvā ǀ jigāti ǀmandráḥ ǀ hótā ǀ sáḥ ǀ juhvā́ ǀ yájiṣṭhaḥ ǀ sám-miślaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jigharti ǀ devā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Increasing by his strength. while lauds content him, with easy flight unto the Gods he travels. Agni the cheerful Priest, best Sacrificer, balms with his tongue the Gods with whom he mingles.
verses.wilson_translation: Magnified by our oblations, propitiated by our praises, swift-moving, he proceeds to the presence ofthe gods; the adorable invoker of the deities, most entitled to worship, associated (with the gods).Agnipresentsto them (the oblation) with the sacrificial ladle.
verses.griffith_verse: Increasing by his strength. while lauds content him, with easy flight unto the Gods he travels. Agni the cheerful Priest, best Sacrificer, balms with his tongue the Gods with whom he mingles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमुस्रामिंद्रं न रेजमानमग्निं गीर्भिर्नमोभिरा कृणुध्वं ।आ यं विप्रासो मतिभिर्गृणंति जातवेदसं जुह्वं सहानां ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ usrā́m ǀ índram ǀ ná ǀ réjamānam ǀ agním ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀā́ ǀ yám ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇánti ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ juhvám ǀ sahā́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: With songs and adorations bring ye hither Agni who stirs himself at dawn like Indra, Whom sages laud with hymns as Jātavedas of those who wield the sacrificial ladle.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring before us with praises, and with adorations, the brilliant Agni, the bestower of enjoyments, as ifhe were Indra, him, whom wise worshippers praise with hymns as Jātavedas, the sacrificer of the victorious Gods.
verses.griffith_verse: With songs and adorations bring ye hither Agni who stirs himself at dawn like Indra, Whom sages laud with hymns as Jātavedas of those who wield the sacrificial ladle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं यस्मिन्विश्वा वसूनि जग्मुर्वाजे नाश्वाः सप्तीवंत एवैः ।अस्मे ऊतीरिंद्रवाततमा अर्वाचीना अग्न आ कृणुष्व ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ yásmin ǀ víśvā ǀ vásūni ǀ jagmúḥ ǀ vā́je ǀ ná ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ sápti-vantaḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀasmé íti ǀ ūtī́ḥ ǀ índravāta-tamāḥ ǀ arvācīnā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǁ
verses.english_translation: In whom all goodly treasures meet together, even as steeds and riders for the booty. Inclining hither bring us help, O Agni, even assistance most desired by Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: OAgni, in whom all treasures are brought together as fleet horses are brought together in battle;bestow upon us protections even more effective than those of Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: In whom all goodly treasures meet together, even as steeds and riders for the booty. Inclining hither bring us help, O Agni, even assistance most desired by Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा ह्यग्ने मह्ना निषद्या सद्यो जज्ञानो हव्यो बभूथ ।तं ते देवासो अनु केतमायन्नधावर्धंत प्रथमास ऊमाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ hí ǀ agne ǀ mahnā́ ǀ ni-sádya ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ jajñānáḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ babhū́tha ǀtám ǀ te ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ánu ǀ kétam ǀ āyan ǀ ádha ǀ avardhanta ǀ prathamā́saḥ ǀ ū́māḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, at thy birth, when thou hadst sat in glory, thou, Agni, wast the aim of invocations. The Gods came near, obedient to thy sunimons, and thus attained their rank as chief Protectors.
verses.wilson_translation: Since you,Agni, born in your glory and having sat down (on the altar), are immediately entitled to theoblation; therefore, the holy (priests) come to that your ensign and the mos worthy (worshippers) prosperprotected (by you).
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, at thy birth, when thou hadst sat in glory, thou, Agni, wast the aim of invocations. The Gods came near, obedient to thy sunimons, and thus attained their rank as chief Protectors.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN VII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O AGNI, shared by all men living bring us good luck for sacrifice from earth and heaven.With us be thine intelligence, WonderWorker! Protect us, God, with thy far-reaching blessings. These hymns brought forth for thee, O Agni, laud thee for bounteous gifts, with cattle and with horses.Good Lord, when man from thee hath gained enjoyment, by hymns, O noblyborn, hath he obtained it. Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever.I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Sūrya. Effectual, Agni, are our prayers for profit. He whom, at home thou, Priest for ever, guardestIs rich in food, drawn by red steeds, and holy: by day and night to him shall all be pleasant. Men with their arms have generated Agni, helpful as some kind friend, adorned with splendours,And stablished as Invoker mid the people the ancient Priest the sacrifice's lover. Worship, thyself, O God, the Gods in heaven: what, void of knowledge, shall the fool avail thee?As thou, O God, hast worshipped Gods by seasons, so, nobly-born! to thine own self pay worship. Agni, be thou our Guardian and Protector bestow upon us life and vital vigour.Accept, O Mighty One, the gifts we offer, and with unceasing care protect our bodies.

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्ति नो दिवो अग्ने पृथिव्या विश्वायुर्धेहि यजथाय देव ।सचेमहि तव दस्म प्रकेतैरुरुष्या ण उरुभिर्देव शंसैः ॥
verses.transliteration: svastí ǀ naḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ agne ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ dhehi ǀ yajáthāya ǀ deva ǀsácemahi ǀ táva ǀ dasma ǀ pra-ketáiḥ ǀ uruṣyá ǀ naḥ ǀ urú-bhiḥ ǀ deva ǀ śáṃsaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O AGNI, shared by all men living bring us good luck for sacrifice from earth and heaven. With us be thine intelligence, WonderWorker! Protect us, God, with thy far-reaching blessings.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Agni, bestow upon us from earth and heaven prosperity and abundant food, that we may beable to offer sacrifices. May we be associated, beautiful (Agni), with your indications (of favour); protect us, divine Agni, on account of our many hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: O AGNI, shared by all men living bring us good luck for sacrifice from earth and heaven. With us be thine intelligence, WonderWorker! Protect us, God, with thy far-reaching blessings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमा अग्ने मतयस्तुभ्यं जाता गोभिरश्वैरभि गृणंति राधः ।यदा ते मर्तो अनु भोगमानड्वसो दधानो मतिभिः सुजात ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ gṛṇanti ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀyadā́ ǀ te ǀ mártaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ bhógam ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ váso íti ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ su-jāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: These hymns brought forth for thee, O Agni, laud thee for bounteous gifts, with cattle and with horses. Good Lord, when man from thee hath gained enjoyment, by hymns, O noblyborn, hath he obtained it.
verses.wilson_translation: These hymns, addressed,Agni, to you, praise you for wealth, together with cattle and horses; when amortal obtains the means of enjoyment from the, (then), opulent and well-born Agni, you, who are the granter ofbenefits, (are celebrated) by our praises.
verses.griffith_verse: These hymns brought forth for thee, O Agni, laud thee for bounteous gifts, with cattle and with horses. Good Lord, when man from thee hath gained enjoyment, by hymns, O noblyborn, hath he obtained it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं मन्ये पितरमग्निमापिमग्निं भ्रातरं सदमित्सखायं ।अग्नेरनीकं बृहतः सपर्यं दिवि शुक्रं यजतं सूर्यस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ manye ǀ pitáram ǀ agním ǀ āpím ǀ agním ǀ bhrā́taram ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ sákhāyam ǀagnéḥ ǀ ánīkam ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ saparyam ǀ diví ǀ śukrám ǀ yajatám ǀ sū́ryasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever. I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Sūrya.
verses.wilson_translation: I regard Agnias a father, as a kinsman, as a brother, as a constant friend. I reverence the face of themighty Agni, radiant in heaven, adorable as the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever. I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सिध्रा अग्ने धियो अस्मे सनुत्रीर्यं त्रायसे दम आ नित्यहोता ।ऋतावा स रोहिदश्वः पुरुक्षुर्द्युभिरस्मा अहभिर्वाममस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: sidhrā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ sánutrīḥ ǀ yám ǀ trā́yase ǀ dáme ǀ ā́ ǀ nítya-hotā ǀṛtá-vā ǀ sáḥ ǀ rohít-aśvaḥ ǀ puru-kṣúḥ ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǀ asmai ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ vāmám ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Effectual, Agni, are our prayers for profit. He whom, at home thou, Priest for ever, guardest Is rich in food, drawn by red steeds, and holy: by day and night to him shall all be pleasant.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, our earnest praises have been composed for you. May he whom you, the perpetual invoker ofthe gods, protect in the sacrificial chamber, be rich in sacrifices, the master of red steeds, the possessor ofabundant food; may the desirable (oblation) be granted him on shining days.
verses.griffith_verse: Effectual, Agni, are our prayers for profit. He whom, at home thou, Priest for ever, guardest Is rich in food, drawn by red steeds, and holy: by day and night to him shall all be pleasant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्युभिर्हितं मित्रमिव प्रयोगं प्रत्नमृत्विजमध्वरस्य जारं ।बाहुभ्यामग्निमायवोऽजनंत विक्षु होतारं न्यसादयंत ॥
verses.transliteration: dyú-bhiḥ ǀ hitám ǀ mitrám-iva ǀ pra-yógam ǀ pratnám ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀ adhvarásya ǀ jārám ǀbāhú-bhyām ǀ agním ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ ajananta ǀ vikṣú ǀ hótāram ǀ ní ǀ asādayanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men with their arms have generated Agni, helpful as some kind friend, adorned with splendours, And stablished as Invoker mid the people the ancient Priest the sacrifice's lover.
verses.wilson_translation: Men have genitive rated with their arms Agni, who is decorated with rays of light, selected as a friend, theancient priest, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, and they have appointed him among people, the invoker of thegods.
verses.griffith_verse: Men with their arms have generated Agni, helpful as some kind friend, adorned with splendours, And stablished as Invoker mid the people the ancient Priest the sacrifice's lover.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वयं यजस्व दिवि देव देवान्किं ते पाकः कृणवदप्रचेताः ।यथायज ऋतुभिर्देव देवानेवा यजस्व तन्वं सुजात ॥
verses.transliteration: svayám ǀ yajasva ǀ diví ǀ deva ǀ devā́n ǀ kím ǀ te ǀ pā́kaḥ ǀ kṛṇavat ǀ ápra-cetāḥ ǀyáthā ǀ áyajaḥ ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǀ deva ǀ devā́n ǀ evá ǀ yajasva ǀ tanvám ǀ su-jāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worship, thyself, O God, the Gods in heaven: what, void of knowledge, shall the fool avail thee? As thou, O God, hast worshipped Gods by seasons, so, nobly-born! to thine own self pay worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer sacrifice thyself, divine (Agni), to the gods in heaven; what can one who is ignorant and ofimmature understanding effect for you? As in due seasons, divine (Agni), you have sacrificed to the gods, so doyou, well- engendered (Agni), sacrifice to your won person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Worship, thyself, O God, the Gods in heaven: what, void of knowledge, shall the fool avail thee? As thou, O God, hast worshipped Gods by seasons, so, nobly-born! to thine own self pay worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भवा नो अग्नेऽवितोत गोपा भवा वयस्कृदुत नो वयोधाः ।रास्वा च नः सुमहो हव्यदातिं त्रास्वोत नस्तन्वो अप्रयुच्छन् ॥
verses.transliteration: bháva ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ avitā́ ǀ utá ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ bháva ǀ vayaḥ-kṛ́t ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ vayaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀrā́sva ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ su-mahaḥ ǀ havyá-dātim ǀ trā́sva ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ ápra-yucchan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, be thou our Guardian and Protector bestow upon us life and vital vigour. Accept, O Mighty One, the gifts we offer, and with unceasing care protect our bodies.
verses.wilson_translation: Be our protector,Agni, (in obvious peril); be our preserver (in unseen danger), be the provider andgiver of sustenance; bestow upon us, nightly Agni, the donation of oblations, and ever attentive, protect ourpersons.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, be thou our Guardian and Protector bestow upon us life and vital vigour. Accept, O Mighty One, the gifts we offer, and with unceasing care protect our bodies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN VIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI advances with his lofty banner: the Bull is bellowing to the earth and heavens.He hath attained the sky's supremest limits. the Steer hath waxen in the lap of waters. The Bull, the youngling with the hump, hath frolicked, the strong and never-ceasing Calf hath bellowed.Bringing our offerings to the God's assembly, he moves as Chief in his own dwelling-places. Him who hath grasped his Parents' head, they stablished at sacrifice a wave of heavenly lustre.In his swift flight the red Dawns borne by horses refresh their bodies in the home of Order. For, Vasu thou precedest every Morning, and still hast been the Twins' illuminator.For sacrifice, seven places thou retainest while for thine own self thou engenderest Mitra. Thou art the Eye and Guard of mighty Order, and Varuṇa when to sacrifice thou comest.Thou art the Waters’ Child O Jātavedas, envoy of him whose offering thou acceptest. Thou art the Leader of the rite and region, to which with thine auspicious teams thou teadest,Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue the oblationbearer, Agni. Through his wise insight Trita in the cavern, seeking as ever the Chief Sire's intention,Carefully tended in his Parents' bosom, calling the weapons kin, goes forth to combat. Well-skilled to use the weapons of his Father, Āptya, urged on by Indra, fought the battle.Then Trita slew the foe seven-rayed, three-headed, and freed the cattle of the Son of Tvaṣṭar. Lord of the brave, Indra cleft him in pieces who sought to gain much strength and deemed him mighty.He smote his three heads from his body, seizing the cattle of the oniniform Son of Tvaṣṭar.

verses.sanskrit: प्र केतुना बृहता यात्यग्निरा रोदसी वृषभो रोरवीति ।दिवश्चिदंताँ उपमाँ उदानळपामुपस्थे महिषो ववर्ध ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ ketúnā ǀ bṛhatā́ ǀ yāti ǀ agníḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ roravīti ǀdiváḥ ǀ cit ǀ ántān ǀ upa-mā́n ǀ út ǀ ānaṭ ǀ apā́m ǀ upá-sthe ǀ mahiṣáḥ ǀ vavardha ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI advances with his lofty banner: the Bull is bellowing to the earth and heavens. He hath attained the sky's supremest limits. the Steer hath waxen in the lap of waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnitraverses heaven and earth with a vast banner; he roars (like) a bull; he spreads aloft over theremote and proximate (regions) of the sky; mighty, he increases in the lap of the water.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI advances with his lofty banner: the Bull is bellowing to the earth and heavens. He hath attained the sky's supremest limits. the Steer hath waxen in the lap of waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मुमोद गर्भो वृषभः ककुद्मानस्रेमा वत्सः शिमीवाँ अरावीत् ।स देवतात्युद्यतानि कृण्वन्त्स्वेषु क्षयेषु प्रथमो जिगाति ॥
verses.transliteration: mumóda ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ kakút-mān ǀ asremā́ ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ śímī-vān ǀ arāvīt ǀsáḥ ǀ devá-tāti ǀ út-yatāni ǀ kṛṇván ǀ svéṣu ǀ kṣáyeṣu ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ jigāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Bull, the youngling with the hump, hath frolicked, the strong and never-ceasing Calf hath bellowed. Bringing our offerings to the God's assembly, he moves as Chief in his own dwelling-places.
verses.wilson_translation: THe embryo (of heaven and earth), the showerer (of benefits), the glorious, rejoices; the excellentchild (of morn and eve), the celebrator of holy rites calls aloud; assiduous in exertions at the worship of the gods,he moves chief in his own abodes.
verses.griffith_verse: The Bull, the youngling with the hump, hath frolicked, the strong and never-ceasing Calf hath bellowed. Bringing our offerings to the God's assembly, he moves as Chief in his own dwelling-places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ यो मूर्धानं पित्रोररब्ध न्यध्वरे दधिरे सूरो अर्णः ।अस्य पत्मन्नरुषीरश्वबुध्ना ऋतस्य योनौ तन्वो जुषंत ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ pitróḥ ǀ árabdha ǀ ní ǀ adhvaré ǀ dadhire ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ árṇaḥ ǀásya ǀ pátman ǀ áruṣīḥ ǀ áśva-budhnāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónau ǀ tanváḥ ǀ juṣanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him who hath grasped his Parents' head, they stablished at sacrifice a wave of heavenly lustre. In his swift flight the red Dawns borne by horses refresh their bodies in the home of Order.
verses.wilson_translation: They have plural ced in the sacrifice the radiance of the powerful Agni, who seizes hold of the forehead ofhis parents, gratifying his cherished, radiant, and expanding limbs, in their course, in their chamber of sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Him who hath grasped his Parents' head, they stablished at sacrifice a wave of heavenly lustre. In his swift flight the red Dawns borne by horses refresh their bodies in the home of Order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषौषो हि वसो अग्रमेषि त्वं यमयोरभवो विभावा ।ऋताय सप्त दधिषे पदानि जनयन्मित्रं तन्वे स्वायै ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣáḥ-uṣaḥ ǀ hí ǀ vaso íti ǀ ágram ǀ éṣi ǀ tvám ǀ yamáyoḥ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀṛtā́ya ǀ saptá ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ padā́ni ǀ janáyan ǀ mitrám ǀ tanvé ǀ svā́yai ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, Vasu thou precedest every Morning, and still hast been the Twins' illuminator. For sacrifice, seven places thou retainest while for thine own self thou engenderest Mitra.
verses.wilson_translation: Opulent Agni, you precede dawn after dawn. You are the illuminator of the twin (day and night);engendering Mitrafrom your own person n, you retain seven plural ces for sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: For, Vasu thou precedest every Morning, and still hast been the Twins' illuminator. For sacrifice, seven places thou retainest while for thine own self thou engenderest Mitra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भुवश्चक्षुर्मह ऋतस्य गोपा भुवो वरुणो यदृताय वेषि ।भुवो अपां नपाज्जातवेदो भुवो दूतो यस्य हव्यं जुजोषः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhúvaḥ ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ṛtā́ya ǀ véṣi ǀbhúvaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ yásya ǀ havyám ǀ jújoṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou art the Eye and Guard of mighty Order, and Varuṇa when to sacrifice thou comest. Thou art the Waters’ Child O Jātavedas, envoy of him whose offering thou acceptest.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the eye, the protector of the great sacrifice; when you proceed to the rite, you are Varuṇa;you are the grandson of the waters,Jātavedas; you are the messenger (of him) whose oblation you enjoy.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou art the Eye and Guard of mighty Order, and Varuṇa when to sacrifice thou comest. Thou art the Waters’ Child O Jātavedas, envoy of him whose offering thou acceptest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश्च नेता यत्रा नियुद्भिः सचसे शिवाभिः ।दिवि मूर्धानं दधिषे स्वर्षां जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहं ॥
verses.transliteration: bhúvaḥ ǀ yajñásya ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ ca ǀ netā́ ǀ yátra ǀ niyút-bhiḥ ǀ sácase ǀ śivā́bhiḥ ǀdiví ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ svaḥ-sā́m ǀ jihvā́m ǀ agne ǀ cakṛṣe ǀ havya-vā́ham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou art the Leader of the rite and region, to which with thine auspicious teams thou teadest, Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue the oblationbearer, Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the leader of the sacrifice and sacrificial water to the plural ce in which you are associated withthe auspicious steeds of the wind; you sustain the all-enjoying (sun) as chief in heaven; you,Agni, make yourtongue the bearer of the oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou art the Leader of the rite and region, to which with thine auspicious teams thou teadest, Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue the oblationbearer, Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य त्रितः क्रतुना वव्रे अंतरिच्छंधीतिं पितुरेवैः परस्य ।सचस्यमानः पित्रोरुपस्थे जामि ब्रुवाण आयुधानि वेति ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ tritáḥ ǀ krátunā ǀ vavré ǀ antáḥ ǀ icchán ǀ dhītím ǀ pitúḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀ párasya ǀsacasyámānaḥ ǀ pitróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ jāmí ǀ bruvāṇáḥ ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ veti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through his wise insight Trita in the cavern, seeking as ever the Chief Sire's intention, Carefully tended in his Parents' bosom, calling the weapons kin, goes forth to combat.
verses.wilson_translation: Tritaby (his own), desiring a share (of the sacrifice), for the sake of taking part in the exploit of thesupreme protector (of the world), chose (Indraas his friend); attended (by the priests) in the proximity of theparental heaven and earth, and reciting appropriate praise, he takes up his weapons.
verses.griffith_verse: Through his wise insight Trita in the cavern, seeking as ever the Chief Sire's intention, Carefully tended in his Parents' bosom, calling the weapons kin, goes forth to combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स पित्र्याण्यायुधानि विद्वानिंद्रेषित आप्त्यो अभ्ययुध्यत् ।त्रिशीर्षाणं सप्तरश्मिं जघन्वांत्वाष्ट्रस्य चिन्निः ससृजे त्रितो गाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ pítryāṇi ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ índra-iṣitaḥ ǀ āptyáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ayudhyat ǀtri-śīrṣā́ṇam ǀ saptá-raśmim ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ tvāṣṭrásya ǀ cit ǀ níḥ ǀ sasṛje ǀ tritáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well-skilled to use the weapons of his Father, Āptya, urged on by Indra, fought the battle. Then Trita slew the foe seven-rayed, three-headed, and freed the cattle of the Son of Tvaṣṭar.
verses.wilson_translation: He, the son of the waters, incited by Indra, skilled in his paternal weapons, fought against (the enemy),and slew the seven-rayed, three-headed (asura); then Tritaset free the cows of the son of Tvaṣṭā.
verses.griffith_verse: Well-skilled to use the weapons of his Father, Āptya, urged on by Indra, fought the battle. Then Trita slew the foe seven-rayed, three-headed, and freed the cattle of the Son of Tvaṣṭar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरीदिंद्र उदिनक्षंतमोजोऽवाभिनत्सत्पतिर्मन्यमानं ।त्वाष्ट्रस्य चिद्विश्वरूपस्य गोनामाचक्राणस्त्रीणि शीर्षा परा वर्क् ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ ít ǀ índraḥ ǀ ut-ínakṣantam ǀ ójaḥ ǀ áva ǀ abhinat ǀ sát-patiḥ ǀ mányamānam ǀtvāṣṭrásya ǀ cit ǀ viśvá-rūpasya ǀ gónām ǀ ā-cakrāṇáḥ ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ śīrṣā́ ǀ párā ǀ vargíti várk ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the brave, Indra cleft him in pieces who sought to gain much strength and deemed him mighty. He smote his three heads from his body, seizing the cattle of the oniniform Son of Tvaṣṭar.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the protector of the virtuous, crushed the arrogant (foe), attaining vast strenth; shouting, he cutoff the three heads of the multiform son of Tvaṣṭā(the lord) of cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of the brave, Indra cleft him in pieces who sought to gain much strength and deemed him mighty. He smote his three heads from his body, seizing the cattle of the oniniform Son of Tvaṣṭar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN IX. Waters.
hymns.anukramani: ९ त्रिशिरास्त्वाष्ट्रः,सिन्धुद्वीप आम्बरीषो वा। आपः। गायत्री,५ वर्धमाना गायत्री, ७ प्रतिष्ठा गायत्री, ८ -९ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE, Waters, are beneficent: so help ye us to energyThat we may look on great delight. Give us a portion of the sap, the most auspicious that ye have,Like mothers in their longing love. To you we gladly come for him to whose abode ye send us on;And, Waters, give us procreant strength. The Waters. be to us for drink, Goddesses for our aid and bliss:Let them stream to us health and strength. beg the Floods to give us balm, these Queens who rule o’er precious things,And have supreme control of men. Within the Waters-Soma thus hath told me-dwell all balms that heal,And Agni, he who blesseth all. O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm,So that I long may see the Sun. Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought,If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me. The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come:O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.

verses.sanskrit: आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवस्ता न ऊर्जे दधातन ।महे रणाय चक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ hí ǀ sthá ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūrjé ǀ dadhātana ǀmahé ǀ ráṇāya ǀ cákṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: YE, Waters, are beneficent: so help ye us to energy That we may look on great delight.
verses.wilson_translation: Since, waters, you are the sources of happiness, grant to us to enjoy abundance, and great anddelightful perception.
verses.griffith_verse: YE, Waters, are beneficent: so help ye us to energy That we may look on great delight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वः शिवतमो रसस्तस्य भाजयतेह नः ।उशतीरिव मातरः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ śivá-tamaḥ ǀ rásaḥ ǀ tásya ǀ bhājayata ǀ ihá ǀ naḥ ǀuśatī́ḥ-iva ǀ mātáraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us a portion of the sap, the most auspicious that ye have, Like mothers in their longing love.
verses.wilson_translation: Give us to partake in this world of your most auspicious Soma, like affectionate mothers.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us a portion of the sap, the most auspicious that ye have, Like mothers in their longing love.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्मा अरं गमाम वो यस्य क्षयाय जिन्वथ ।आपो जनयथा च नः ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmai ǀ áram ǀ gamāma ǀ vaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jínvatha ǀā́paḥ ǀ janáyatha ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you we gladly come for him to whose abode ye send us on; And, Waters, give us procreant strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us quickly have recourse to you, for that your (faculty) of removing (sin) by which you gladden us;waters, bestow upon us progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: To you we gladly come for him to whose abode ye send us on; And, Waters, give us procreant strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शं नो देवीरभिष्टय आपो भवंतु पीतये ।शं योरभि स्रवंतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: śám ǀ naḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ bhavantu ǀ pītáye ǀśám ǀ yóḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sravantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Waters. be to us for drink, Goddesses for our aid and bliss: Let them stream to us health and strength.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine water be propitious to our worship, (may they be good) for our drinking; may they flowround us, and be our health and safety.
verses.griffith_verse: The Waters. be to us for drink, Goddesses for our aid and bliss: Let them stream to us health and strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ईशाना वार्याणां क्षयंतीश्चर्षणीनां ।अपो याचामि भेषजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ī́śānāḥ ǀ vā́ryāṇām ǀ kṣáyantīḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀapáḥ ǀ yācāmi ǀ bheṣajám ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 beg the Floods to give us balm, these Queens who rule o’er precious things, And have supreme control of men.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, sovereigns of precious (treasures), granters of habitations to men, I solicit of youmedicine(formy infirmities).
verses.griffith_verse: 1 beg the Floods to give us balm, these Queens who rule o’er precious things, And have supreme control of men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीदंतर्विश्वानि भेषजा ।अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवं ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ me ǀ sómaḥ ǀ abravīt ǀ antáḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀagním ǀ ca ǀ viśvá-śambhuvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Within the Waters-Soma thus hath told me-dwell all balms that heal, And Agni, he who blesseth all.
verses.wilson_translation: Somahas declared to me; all medicaments, as well as Agni, the benefactor of the universe, are in thewaters.
verses.griffith_verse: Within the Waters-Soma thus hath told me-dwell all balms that heal, And Agni, he who blesseth all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपः पृणीत भेषजं वरूथं तन्वे मम ।ज्योक्च सूर्यं दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ pṛṇītá ǀ bheṣajám ǀ várūtham ǀ tanvé ǀ máma ǀjyók ǀ ca ǀ sū́ryam ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm, So that I long may see the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, bring to perfection, all disease-dispelling medicaments for the good of my body, that I maybehold the Sun.
verses.griffith_verse: O Waters, teem with medicine to keep my body safe from harm, So that I long may see the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदमापः प्र वहत यत्किं च दुरितं मयि ।यद्वाहमभिदुद्रोह यद्वा शेप उतानृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ āpaḥ ǀ prá ǀ vahata ǀ yát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ duḥ-itám ǀ máyi ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ ahám ǀ abhi-dudróha ǀ yát ǀ vā ǀ śepé ǀ utá ǀ ánṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought, If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, take away whatever sin has been (found) in me, whether I have (knowingly) done wrong, orhave pronounced imprecations (against holy men), or have spoken untruth.
verses.griffith_verse: Whatever sin is found in me, whatever evil I have wrought, If I have lied or falsely sworn, Waters, remove it far from me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं रसेन समगस्महि ।पयस्वानग्न आ गहि तं मा सं सृज वर्चसा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ adyá ǀ ánu ǀ acāriṣam ǀ rásena ǀ sám ǀ agasmahi ǀpáyasvān ǀ agne ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ tám ǀ mā ǀ sám ǀ sṛja ǀ várcasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come: O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.
verses.wilson_translation: I have this day entered into the waters; we have mingled with their essence.Agni, abiding in thewaters approach, and fill me (thus bathed) with vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: The Waters I this day have sought, and to their moisture have we come: O Agni, rich in milk, come thou, and with thy splendour cover me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN X.Yama Yami.
hymns.anukramani: १४ नवमीवर्ज्यानामयुजां षष्ठ्याश्च वैवस्वती यमी ऋषिका। यमः। षष्ठीवर्ज्यानां युजां नवम्याश्च वैवस्वतो यमः ऋषिः। यमी। त्रिष्टुप्, १३विराट्स्थाना।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FAIN would I win my friend to kindly friendship. So may the Sage, come through the air's wide ocean,Remembering the earth and days to follow, obtain a son, the issue of his father. Thy friend loves not the friendship which considers her who is near in kindred as stranger.Sons of the mighty Asura, the Heroes, supporters of the heavens, see far around them. Yea, this the Immortals seek of thee with longing, progeny of the sole existing mortal.Then let thy soul and mine be knit together, and as a loving husband take thy consort. Shall we do now what we ne’er did aforetime? we who spake righteously now talk impurely?Gandharva in the floods, the Dame of Waters-such is our bond, such our most lofty kinship. Even in the womb God Tvaṣṭar, Vivifier, shaping all forms, Creator, made us consorts.None violates his holy ordinances: that we are his the heavens and earth acknowledge. Who knows that earliest day whereof thou speakest? Who hatb beheld it? Who can here declare it?Great is the Law of Varuṇa and Mitra. What, wanton! wilt thou say to men to tempt them? I, Yami, am possessed by love of Yama, that I may rest on the same couch beside him.I as a wife would yield me to my husband. Like car-wheels let us speed to meet each other. They stand not still, they never close their eyelids, those sentinels of Gods who wander round us.Not me-go quickly, wanton, with another, and hasten like a chariot wheel to meet him. May Sūrya's eye with days and nights endow him, and ever may his light spread out before him.In heaven and earth the kindred Pair commingle. On Yam! be the unbrotherly act of Yama. Sure there will come succeeding times when brothers and sisters will do acts unmeet for kinsfolk.Not me, O fair one,—seek another husband, and make thine arm a pillow for thy consort. Is he a brother when no lord is left her? Is she a sister when Destruction cometh?Forced by my love these many words I utter. Come near, and hold me in thy close embraces. I will not fold mine arms about thy body: they call it sin when one comes near his sister.Not me,—prepare thy pleasures with another: thy brother seeks not this from thee, O fair one. Alas! thou art indeed a weakling, Yama we find in thee no trace of heart or spirit.As round the tree the woodbine clings, another will cling albout thee girt as with a girdle. Embrace another, Yami; let another, even as the woodbine rings the tree, enfold thee.Win thou his heart and let him win thy fancy, and he shall form with thee a blest alliance.

verses.sanskrit: ओ चित्सखायं सख्या ववृत्यां तिरः पुरू चिदर्णवं जगन्वान् ।पितुर्नपातमा दधीत वेधा अधि क्षमि प्रतरं दीध्यानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ó íti ǀ cit ǀ sákhāyam ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ vavṛtyām ǀ tiráḥ ǀ purú ǀ cit ǀ arṇavám ǀ jaganvā́n ǀpitúḥ ǀ nápātam ǀ ā́ ǀ dadhīta ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ kṣámi ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dī́dhyānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FAIN would I win my friend to kindly friendship. So may the Sage, come through the air's wide ocean, Remembering the earth and days to follow, obtain a son, the issue of his father.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). I invite my friend to friendship, having come over the vast and desert ocean; may Vedhas, after reflecting, plural ce in the earth the offsprig (of you) the father, edowed with excellent qualities.
verses.griffith_verse: FAIN would I win my friend to kindly friendship. So may the Sage, come through the air's wide ocean, Remembering the earth and days to follow, obtain a son, the issue of his father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न ते सखा सख्यं वष्ट्येतत्सलक्ष्मा यद्विषुरूपा भवाति ।महस्पुत्रासो असुरस्य वीरा दिवो धर्तार उर्विया परि ख्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ te ǀ sákhā ǀ sakhyám ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ etát ǀ sá-lakṣmā ǀ yát ǀ víṣu-rūpā ǀ bhávāti ǀmaháḥ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ dhartā́raḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ pári ǀ khyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy friend loves not the friendship which considers her who is near in kindred as stranger. Sons of the mighty Asura, the Heroes, supporters of the heavens, see far around them.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). Your friend desires not this friendship, for although of one origin, she is of differentform; the hero sons of the greatasura(are) the upholders of heaven, enjoying vast renown.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy friend loves not the friendship which considers her who is near in kindred as stranger. Sons of the mighty Asura, the Heroes, supporters of the heavens, see far around them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उशंति घा ते अमृतास एतदेकस्य चित्त्यजसं मर्त्यस्य ।नि ते मनो मनसि धाय्यस्मे जन्युः पतिस्तन्वमा विविश्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: uśánti ǀ gha ǀ té ǀ amṛ́tāsaḥ ǀ etát ǀ ékasya ǀ cit ǀ tyajásam ǀ mártyasya ǀní ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ mánasi ǀ dhāyi ǀ asmé íti ǀ jányuḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ ā́ ǀ viviśyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, this the Immortals seek of thee with longing, progeny of the sole existing mortal. Then let thy soul and mine be knit together, and as a loving husband take thy consort.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). The immortals take plural asure in (a union) like this which is forbidden to every mortal; letyour mind then concur with mine, and as the progenitor (of all) was the husband (of his daughter), do you enjoymy person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, this the Immortals seek of thee with longing, progeny of the sole existing mortal. Then let thy soul and mine be knit together, and as a loving husband take thy consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यत्पुरा चकृमा कद्ध नूनमृता वदंतो अनृतं रपेम ।गंधर्वो अप्स्वप्या च योषा सा नो नाभिः परमं जामि तन्नौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yát ǀ purā́ ǀ cakṛmá ǀ kát ǀ ha ǀ nūnám ǀ ṛtā́ ǀ vádantaḥ ǀ ánṛtam ǀ rapema ǀgandharváḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ ápyā ǀ ca ǀ yóṣā ǀ sā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ paramám ǀ jāmí ǀ tát ǀ nau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shall we do now what we ne’er did aforetime? we who spake righteously now talk impurely? Gandharva in the floods, the Dame of Waters-such is our bond, such our most lofty kinship.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeak). We have not done what was done formerly; for how can we who speak truth, utter nowthat which is untrue?Gandharva(the sun) was in the watery (firmament), and the water was his bride. She is ourcommon hence our near affinity.
verses.griffith_verse: Shall we do now what we ne’er did aforetime? we who spake righteously now talk impurely? Gandharva in the floods, the Dame of Waters-such is our bond, such our most lofty kinship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गर्भे नु नौ जनिता दंपती क��्देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः ।नकिरस्य प्र मिनंति व्रतानि वेद नावस्य पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥
verses.transliteration: gárbhe ǀ nú ǀ nau ǀ janitā́ ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ kaḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ savitā́ ǀ viśvá-rūpaḥ ǀnákiḥ ǀ asya ǀ prá ǀ minanti ǀ vratā́ni ǀ véda ǀ nau ǀ asyá ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ utá ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even in the womb God Tvaṣṭar, Vivifier, shaping all forms, Creator, made us consorts. None violates his holy ordinances: that we are his the heavens and earth acknowledge.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). The divine omniform genitive rator Tvaṣṭā, the progenitor, made us two husband andwife, even in the womb: none frustrate his undertaking; earth and heaven are conscious of this our (union).
verses.griffith_verse: Even in the womb God Tvaṣṭar, Vivifier, shaping all forms, Creator, made us consorts. None violates his holy ordinances: that we are his the heavens and earth acknowledge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को अस्य वेद प्रथमस्याह्नः क ईं ददर्श क इह प्र वोचत् ।बृहन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम कदु ब्रव आहनो वीच्या नॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ asyá ǀ veda ǀ prathamásya ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ īm ǀ dadarśa ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀbṛhát ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ kát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bravaḥ ǀ āhanaḥ ǀ vī́cyā ǀ nṝ́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who knows that earliest day whereof thou speakest? Who hatb beheld it? Who can here declare it? Great is the Law of Varuṇa and Mitra. What, wanton! wilt thou say to men to tempt them?
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). Who knows anything of this (his) first day (of existence)? Who has beheld it? Whohas here revealed it? The dwelling of Mitraand of Varuṇais vast. What say you, who punishes men with hell?
verses.griffith_verse: Who knows that earliest day whereof thou speakest? Who hatb beheld it? Who can here declare it? Great is the Law of Varuṇa and Mitra. What, wanton! wilt thou say to men to tempt them?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमस्य मा यम्यं काम आगन्त्समाने योनौ सहशेय्याय ।जायेव पत्ये तन्वं रिरिच्यां वि चिद्वृहेव रथ्येव चक्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: yamásya ǀ mā ǀ yamyám ǀ kā́maḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agan ǀ samāné ǀ yónau ǀ saha-śéyyāya ǀjāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ tanvám ǀ riricyām ǀ ví ǀ cit ǀ vṛheva ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I, Yami, am possessed by love of Yama, that I may rest on the same couch beside him. I as a wife would yield me to my husband. Like car-wheels let us speed to meet each other.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). The desire of Yamahas approached me Yamī, to lie with him in the same bed; I willabandon my person n as a wife to her husband; let us exert ourselves in union like the two wheels of a wagon.
verses.griffith_verse: I, Yami, am possessed by love of Yama, that I may rest on the same couch beside him. I as a wife would yield me to my husband. Like car-wheels let us speed to meet each other.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न तिष्ठंति न नि मिषंत्येते देवानां स्पश इह ये चरंति ।अन्येन मदाहनो याहि तूयं तेन वि वृह रथ्येव चक्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tiṣṭhanti ǀ ná ǀ ní ǀ miṣanti ǀ eté ǀ devā́nām ǀ spáśaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ yé ǀ cáranti ǀanyéna ǀ mát ǀ āhanaḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ tū́yam ǀ téna ǀ ví ǀ vṛheva ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They stand not still, they never close their eyelids, those sentinels of Gods who wander round us. Not me-go quickly, wanton, with another, and hasten like a chariot wheel to meet him.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). The spies of the gods, which wander upon earth, never stop, never close their eyeṣAssociate quickly, destructress, with some other than with me, and exert yourselves in union, like the two wheelsof a wagon.
verses.griffith_verse: They stand not still, they never close their eyelids, those sentinels of Gods who wander round us. Not me-go quickly, wanton, with another, and hasten like a chariot wheel to meet him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रात्रीभिरस्मा अहभिर्दशस्येत्सूर्यस्य चक्षुर्मुहुरुन्मिमीयात् ।दिवा पृथिव्या मिथुना सबंधू यमीर्यमस्य बिभृयादजामि ॥
verses.transliteration: rā́trībhiḥ ǀ asmai ǀ áha-bhiḥ ǀ daśasyet ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ múhuḥ ǀ út ǀ mimīyāt ǀdivā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ mithunā́ ǀ sábandhū íti sá-bandhū ǀ yamī́ḥ ǀ yamásya ǀ bibhṛyāt ǀ ájāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Sūrya's eye with days and nights endow him, and ever may his light spread out before him. In heaven and earth the kindred Pair commingle. On Yam! be the unbrotherly act of Yama.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). To him (Yam) let every worshipper sacrifice both day and night, on him let the eye ofthe Sun repeatedly rise; (for him may) the kindred pair (day and night unite) with heaven and earth.Yamawilladhere to the non- affinity of Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: May Sūrya's eye with days and nights endow him, and ever may his light spread out before him. In heaven and earth the kindred Pair commingle. On Yam! be the unbrotherly act of Yama.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ घा ता गच्छानुत्तरा युगानि यत्र जामयः कृणवन्नजामि ।उप बर्बृहि वृषभाय बाहुमन्यमिच्छस्व सुभगे पतिं मत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ gha ǀ tā́ ǀ gacchān ǀ út-tarā ǀ yugā́ni ǀ yátra ǀ jāmáyaḥ ǀ kṛṇávan ǀ ájāmi ǀúpa ǀ barbṛhi ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ bāhúm ǀ anyám ǀ icchasva ǀ su-bhage ǀ pátim ǀ mát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sure there will come succeeding times when brothers and sisters will do acts unmeet for kinsfolk. Not me, O fair one,—seek another husband, and make thine arm a pillow for thy consort.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). The subsequent ages will come, when sisters will choose one who is not a brother (asa husband); therefore, auspicious one, choose another husband than me, and make your arm a pillow for yourmate.
verses.griffith_verse: Sure there will come succeeding times when brothers and sisters will do acts unmeet for kinsfolk. Not me, O fair one,—seek another husband, and make thine arm a pillow for thy consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं भ्रातासद्यदनाथं भवाति किमु स्वसा यन्निर्ऋतिर्निगच्छात् ।काममूता बह्वेतद्रपामि तन्वा मे तन्वं सं पिपृग्धि ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ asat ǀ yát ǀ anāthám ǀ bhávāti ǀ kím ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svásā ǀ yát ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ ni-gácchāt ǀkā́ma-mūtā ǀ bahú ǀ etát ǀ rapāmi ǀ tanvā́ ǀ me ǀ tanvám ǀ sám ǀ pipṛgdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Is he a brother when no lord is left her? Is she a sister when Destruction cometh? Forced by my love these many words I utter. Come near, and hold me in thy close embraces.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). Is he a brother whose sister has no lord? Is she a sister (whose brother) misfortuneapproaches? Overcome by desire, I strongly urge this one request; unite your person n with mine.
verses.griffith_verse: Is he a brother when no lord is left her? Is she a sister when Destruction cometh? Forced by my love these many words I utter. Come near, and hold me in thy close embraces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वा उ ते तन्वा तन्वं सं पपृच्यां पापमाहुर्यः स्वसारं निगच्छात् ।अन्येन मत्प्रमुदः कल्पयस्व न ते भ्राता सुभगे वष्ट्येतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ te ǀ tanvā́ ǀ tanvám ǀ sám ǀ papṛcyām ǀ pāpám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ svásāram ǀ ni-gácchāt ǀanyéna ǀ mát ǀ pra-múdaḥ ǀ kalpayasva ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ su-bhage ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ etát ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will not fold mine arms about thy body: they call it sin when one comes near his sister. Not me,—prepare thy pleasures with another: thy brother seeks not this from thee, O fair one.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). I will not unite my person n with yours; they call him who approaches a sister, a sinneṛEnjoy plural asure with some other than me; your brother, auspicious one, has no such desire.
verses.griffith_verse: I will not fold mine arms about thy body: they call it sin when one comes near his sister. Not me,—prepare thy pleasures with another: thy brother seeks not this from thee, O fair one.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बतो बतासि यम नैव ते मनो हृदयं चाविदाम ।अन्या किल त्वां कक्ष्येव युक्तं परि ष्वजाते लिबुजेव वृक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: batáḥ ǀ bata ǀ asi ǀ yama ǀ ná ǀ evá ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ hṛ́dayam ǀ ca ǀ avidāma ǀanyā́ ǀ kíla ǀ tvā́m ǀ kakṣyā́-iva ǀ yuktám ǀ pári ǀ svajāte ǀ líbujā-iva ǀ vṛkṣám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Alas! thou art indeed a weakling, Yama we find in thee no trace of heart or spirit. As round the tree the woodbine clings, another will cling albout thee girt as with a girdle.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamispeaks). Alas,Yama, you are feeble; we understand not your mind or your heart. Some otherfemale embraces you as a girth a horse, or as a creeper a tree.
verses.griffith_verse: Alas! thou art indeed a weakling, Yama we find in thee no trace of heart or spirit. As round the tree the woodbine clings, another will cling albout thee girt as with a girdle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अन्यमू षु त्वं यम्यन्य उ त्वां परि ष्वजाते लिबुजेव वृक्षं ।तस्य वा त्वं मन इच्छा स वा तवाधा कृणुष्व संविदं सुभद्रां ॥
verses.transliteration: anyám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ tvám ǀ yami ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā́m ǀ pári ǀ svajāte ǀ líbujā-iva ǀ vṛkṣám ǀtásya ǀ vā ǀ tvám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ icchá ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā ǀ táva ǀ ádha ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǀ sam-vídam ǀ sú-bhadrām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Embrace another, Yami; let another, even as the woodbine rings the tree, enfold thee. Win thou his heart and let him win thy fancy, and he shall form with thee a blest alliance.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yamaspeaks). Do you,Yamī, embrace another; and let another embrace you as a creeper a tree;seek his affection, let him seek you; and make a happy union.
verses.griffith_verse: Embrace another, Yami; let another, even as the woodbine rings the tree, enfold thee. Win thou his heart and let him win thy fancy, and he shall form with thee a blest alliance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XI. Agni
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Bull hath yielded for the Bull the milk of heaven: the Son of Aditi can never be deceived.According to his wisdom Varuṇa knoweth all: may he, the Holy, hallow times for sacrifice. Gandharvi spake: may she, the Lady of the flood, amid the river's roaring leave my heart untouched.May Aditi accomplish all that we desire, and may our eldest Brother tell us this as Chief. Yea, even this blessed Morning, rich in store of food, splendid, with heavenly lustre, hath shone out for man,Since they, as was the wish of yearning Gods, brought forth that yearning Agni for the assembly as the Priest. And the fleet Falcon brought for sacrifice from afar this flowing Drop most excellent and keen of sight,Then when the Āryan tribes chose as Invoking Priest Agni the Wonder-Worker, and the hymn rose up. Still art thou kind to him who feeds thee as with grass, and, skilled in sacrifice, offers thee holy gifts.When thou, having received the sage's strengthening food with lauds, after long toil, cornest with many more. Urge thou thy Parents, as a lover ' to delight: the Lovely One desires and craves it from his heart.The priest calls out, the sacrificer shows his skill, the Asura tries his strength, and with the hymn is stirred. Far-famed is he, the mortal man, O Agni, thou Son of Strength, who hath obtained thy favour.He, gathering power, borne onward by his horses, makes his days lovely in his might and splendour. When, Holy Agni, the divine assembly, the sacred synod mid the Gods, is gathered,And when thou, Godlike One, dealest forth treasures, vouchsafe us, too, our portion of the riches. Hear us, O Agni, in your common dwelling: harness thy rapid car of Amṛta.Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.

verses.sanskrit: वृषा वृष्णे दुदुहे दोहसा दिवः पयांसि यह्वो अदितेरदाभ्यः ।विश्वं स वेद वरुणो यथा धिया स यज्ञियो यजतु यज्ञियाँ ऋतून् ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ duduhe ǀ dóhasā ǀ diváḥ ǀ páyāṃsi ǀ yahváḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǀvíśvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ veda ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǀ yajatu ǀ yajñíyān ǀ ṛtū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Bull hath yielded for the Bull the milk of heaven: the Son of Aditi can never be deceived. According to his wisdom Varuṇa knoweth all: may he, the Holy, hallow times for sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: The great, the unconquerable (Agni), the showerer, milks openly with a (great) milking the streams (ofprosperity) from heaven for the unwearying sacrificer; like Varuṇa, he knows everything by his understanding;may he who is skilled in sacrifice observe the sacrificial seasona.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Bull hath yielded for the Bull the milk of heaven: the Son of Aditi can never be deceived. According to his wisdom Varuṇa knoweth all: may he, the Holy, hallow times for sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रपद्गंधर्वीरप्या च योषणा नदस्य नादे परि पातु मे मनः ।इष्टस्य मध्ये अदितिर्नि धातु नो भ्राता नो ज्येष्ठः प्रथमो वि वोचति ॥
verses.transliteration: rápat ǀ gandharvī́ḥ ǀ ápyā ǀ ca ǀ yóṣaṇā ǀ nadásya ǀ nādé ǀ pári ǀ pātu ǀ me ǀ mánaḥ ǀiṣṭásya ǀ mádhye ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ní ǀ dhātu ǀ naḥ ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ naḥ ǀ jyeṣṭháḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ ví ǀ vocati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gandharvi spake: may she, the Lady of the flood, amid the river's roaring leave my heart untouched. May Aditi accomplish all that we desire, and may our eldest Brother tell us this as Chief.
verses.wilson_translation: The Gandharvīand the water-consecrated feminine nine oblation praise Agni; may he be favourable tothe thought of me, raising my voice in his praise; may Agni plural ce us in the midst of the sacrifice; the chief (of theworshipers), our elder brother, repeats his various laudations.
verses.griffith_verse: Gandharvi spake: may she, the Lady of the flood, amid the river's roaring leave my heart untouched. May Aditi accomplish all that we desire, and may our eldest Brother tell us this as Chief.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो चिन्नु भद्रा क्षुमती यशस्वत्युषा उवास मनवे स्वर्वती ।यदीमुशंतमुशतामनु क्रतुमग्निं होतारं विदथाय जीजनन् ॥
verses.transliteration: só íti ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ kṣu-mátī ǀ yáśasvatī ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ uvāsa ǀ mánave ǀ sváḥ-vatī ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ uśántam ǀ uśatā́m ǀ ánu ǀ krátum ǀ agním ǀ hótāram ǀ vidáthāya ǀ jī́janan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, even this blessed Morning, rich in store of food, splendid, with heavenly lustre, hath shone out for man, Since they, as was the wish of yearning Gods, brought forth that yearning Agni for the assembly as the Priest.
verses.wilson_translation: The very auspicious, resounding, famous Dawn, ascends bringing the sun to man; when for thesacrifice after the worship they give birth to that Agni, the desirer, the invoker of the desiring (gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, even this blessed Morning, rich in store of food, splendid, with heavenly lustre, hath shone out for man, Since they, as was the wish of yearning Gods, brought forth that yearning Agni for the assembly as the Priest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध त्यं द्रप्सं विभ्वं विचक्षणं विराभरदिषितः श्येनो अध्वरे ।यदी विशो वृणते दस्ममार्या अग्निं होतारमध धीरजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ tyám ǀ drapsám ǀ vi-bhvám ǀ vi-cakṣaṇám ǀ víḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ abharat ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ adhvaré ǀyádi ǀ víśaḥ ǀ vṛṇáte ǀ dasmám ǀ ā́ryāḥ ǀ agním ǀ hótāram ǀ ádha ǀ dhī́ḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: And the fleet Falcon brought for sacrifice from afar this flowing Drop most excellent and keen of sight, Then when the Āryan tribes chose as Invoking Priest Agni the Wonder-Worker, and the hymn rose up.
verses.wilson_translation: The hawk sent (by Agni) to the sacrifice has brought the dripping copious all-seeing (Soma) libatioṇWhen the Aryapeople choose the victorious Agni as the ministrant priest, then the sacred rite is celebrateḍ
verses.griffith_verse: And the fleet Falcon brought for sacrifice from afar this flowing Drop most excellent and keen of sight, Then when the Āryan tribes chose as Invoking Priest Agni the Wonder-Worker, and the hymn rose up.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सदासि रण्वो यवसेव पुष्यते होत्राभिरग्ने मनुषः स्वध्वरः ।विप्रस्य वा यच्छशमान उक्थ्यं वाजं ससवाँ उपयासि भूरिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: sádā ǀ asi ǀ raṇváḥ ǀ yávasā-iva ǀ púṣyate ǀ hótrābhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ su-adhvaráḥ ǀvíprasya ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ śaśamānáḥ ǀ ukthyám ǀ vā́jam ǀ sasa-vā́n ǀ upa-yā́si ǀ bhū́ri-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Still art thou kind to him who feeds thee as with grass, and, skilled in sacrifice, offers thee holy gifts. When thou, having received the sage's strengthening food with lauds, after long toil, cornest with many more.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are ever plural asing (to your worshippers), as pasture satisfies (the herds); bewell-worshipped with man's sacrifices; if commending the praise of the wise, and partaking of the (sacrificial)food, you come with many (divinities of the rite).
verses.griffith_verse: Still art thou kind to him who feeds thee as with grass, and, skilled in sacrifice, offers thee holy gifts. When thou, having received the sage's strengthening food with lauds, after long toil, cornest with many more.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीरय पितरा जार आ भगमियक्षति हर्यतो हृत्त इष्यति ।विवक्ति वह्निः स्वपस्यते मखस्तविष्यते असुरो वेपते मती ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īraya ǀ pitárā ǀ jāráḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhágam ǀ íyakṣati ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ hṛttáḥ ǀ iṣyati ǀvívakti ǀ váhniḥ ǀ su-apasyáte ǀ makháḥ ǀ taviṣyáte ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ vépate ǀ matī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Urge thou thy Parents, as a lover ' to delight: the Lovely One desires and craves it from his heart. The priest calls out, the sacrificer shows his skill, the Asura tries his strength, and with the hymn is stirred.
verses.wilson_translation: Wake up the parents, as the Sun his splendour; (the worshipper) desires to offer worship to (thedeities) who are plural ased by it; with all his heart he wishes (to do so); he desires to repeat (your praise); thebearer (of the oblation) is anxious to effect the good work; the sacrifice longs for augmentation, the prudent(sacrificer) trembles in his thoughts.
verses.griffith_verse: Urge thou thy Parents, as a lover ' to delight: the Lovely One desires and craves it from his heart. The priest calls out, the sacrificer shows his skill, the Asura tries his strength, and with the hymn is stirred.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते अग्ने सुमतिं मर्तो अक्षत्सहसः सूनो अति स प्र शृण्वे ।इषं दधानो वहमानो अश्वैरा स द्युमाँ अमवान्भूषति द्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ su-matím ǀ mártaḥ ǀ ákṣat ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ áti ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá ǀ śṛṇve ǀíṣam ǀ dádhānaḥ ǀ váhamānaḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ dyu-mā́n ǀ áma-vān ǀ bh��ṣati ǀ dyū́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far-famed is he, the mortal man, O Agni, thou Son of Strength, who hath obtained thy favour. He, gathering power, borne onward by his horses, makes his days lovely in his might and splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, son of strength, the mortal who obtains your favour is widely celebrated; possessing abundantfood, and being conveyed by horses, illustrious and vigorous he graces the days of his existence.
verses.griffith_verse: Far-famed is he, the mortal man, O Agni, thou Son of Strength, who hath obtained thy favour. He, gathering power, borne onward by his horses, makes his days lovely in his might and splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदग्न एषा समितिर्भवाति देवी देवेषु यजता यजत्र ।रत्ना च यद्विभजासि स्वधावो भागं नो अत्र वसुमंतं वीतात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ agne ǀ eṣā́ ǀ sám-itiḥ ǀ bhávāti ǀ devī́ ǀ devéṣu ǀ yajatā́ ǀ yajatra ǀrátnā ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ vi-bhájāsi ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ vásu-mantam ǀ vītāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Holy Agni, the divine assembly, the sacred synod mid the Gods, is gathered, And when thou, Godlike One, dealest forth treasures, vouchsafe us, too, our portion of the riches.
verses.wilson_translation: When, adorable Agni, this united praise is resplendent among the adorable gods, and when you,bearer of the oblatio, apportion the precious (treasures), then allot to us a valuable share. bring to us the heaven and earth, the daughters of the divine (Prajāpati), let none of the gods be absent, and doyou yourself be present.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Holy Agni, the divine assembly, the sacred synod mid the Gods, is gathered, And when thou, Godlike One, dealest forth treasures, vouchsafe us, too, our portion of the riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुधी नो अग्ने सदने सधस्थे युक्ष्वा रथममृतस्य द्रवित्नुं ।आ नो वह रोदसी देवपुत्रे माकिर्देवानामप भूरिह स्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrudhí ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sádane ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ yukṣvá ǀ rátham ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ dravitnúm ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vaha ǀ ródasī íti ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ápa ǀ bhūḥ ǀ ihá ǀ syāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear us, O Agni, in your common dwelling: harness thy rapid car of Amṛta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear us, O Agni, in your common dwelling: harness thy rapid car of Amṛta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XII. Agni
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HEAVEN and Earth, first by everlasting Order, speakers of truth, are near enough to hear us,When the God, urging men to worship. sitteth as Priest, assuming all his vital vigour. As God comprising Gods by Law Eternal, bear, as the Chief who knoweth, our oblation,Smoke-bannered with the fuel, radiant, joyous, better to praise and worship, Priest for ever. When the cow's nectar wins the God completely, men here below are heaven's sustainers.All the Gods came to this thy heavenly Yajus which from the motley Pair milked oil and water. praise your work that ye may make me prosper: hear, Heaven and Earth, Twain Worlds that drop with fatness.While days and nights go to the world of spirits, here let the Parents with sweet meath refresh us Hath the King siezed us? How have we offended against his holy ordinance? Who knoweth?For even Mitra mid the Gods is angry there are both song and strength for those who come not. ’Tis hard to understand the Immortal's nature, where she who is akin becomes astranger.Guard ceaselessly, great Agni, him who ponders Yama's name, easy to be comprehended. They in the synod where the Gods rejoice them, where they are seated in Vivasvān's dwelling,Have given the Moon his beams, the Sun his splendour-the Two unweariedly maintain their brightness. The counsel which the Gods meet to consider, their secret plan,—of that we have no knowledge.There let God Savitar, Aditi, and Mitra proclaim to Varuṇa that we are sinless. Hear us, O Agni, in your comninn dwell ing: harness thy rapid car, the car of Amṛta.Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.

verses.sanskrit: द्यावा ह क्षामा प्रथमे ऋतेनाभिश्रावे भवतः सत्यवाचा ।देवो यन्मर्तान्यजथाय कृण्वन् सीदद्धोता प्रत्यङ्स्वमसुं यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: dyā́vā ǀ ha ǀ kṣā́mā ǀ prathamé íti ǀ ṛténa ǀ abhi-śrāvé ǀ bhavataḥ ǀ satya-vā́cā ǀdeváḥ ǀ yát ǀ mártān ǀ yajáthāya ǀ kṛṇván ǀ sī́dat ǀ hótā ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ svám ǀ ásum ǀ yán ǁ
verses.english_translation: HEAVEN and Earth, first by everlasting Order, speakers of truth, are near enough to hear us, When the God, urging men to worship. sitteth as Priest, assuming all his vital vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth, declarers of truth, principal (of things), be present at the invocation, associatedwith the rite, when the divine (Agni), exciting mortals to sacrifice, sits down in their presence as the invoker (ofthe gods) putting forth his flame.
verses.griffith_verse: HEAVEN and Earth, first by everlasting Order, speakers of truth, are near enough to hear us, When the God, urging men to worship. sitteth as Priest, assuming all his vital vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवो देवान्परिभूर्ऋतेन वहा नो हव्यं प्रथमश्चिकित्वान् ।धूमकेतुः समिधा भाऋजीको मंद्रो होता नित्यो वाचा यजीयान् ॥
verses.transliteration: deváḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ pari-bhū́ḥ ǀ ṛténa ǀ váha ǀ naḥ ǀ havyám ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀdhūmá-ketuḥ ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ bhā́ḥ-ṛjīkaḥ ǀ mandráḥ ǀ hótā ǀ nítyaḥ ǀ vācā́ ǀ yájīyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: As God comprising Gods by Law Eternal, bear, as the Chief who knoweth, our oblation, Smoke-bannered with the fuel, radiant, joyous, better to praise and worship, Priest for ever.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you, bright (Agni), surrounding the gods, carry our oblation with due rites; you, who are the chief(of the deities), the wise, the smoke-bannered, fuel-kindled, straight-flaming, adorable, the invoker, the constantsacrificer with prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: As God comprising Gods by Law Eternal, bear, as the Chief who knoweth, our oblation, Smoke-bannered with the fuel, radiant, joyous, better to praise and worship, Priest for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वावृग्देवस्यामृतं यदी गोरतो जातासो धारयंत उर्वी ।विश्वे देवा अनु तत्ते यजुर्गुर्दुहे यदेनी दिव्यं घृतं वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: svā́vṛk ǀ devásya ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ yádi ǀ góḥ ǀ átaḥ ǀ jātā́saḥ ǀ dhārayante ǀ urvī́ íti ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ yájuḥ ǀ guḥ ǀ duhé ǀ yát ǀ énī ǀ divyám ǀ ghṛtám ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the cow's nectar wins the God completely, men here below are heaven's sustainers. All the Gods came to this thy heavenly Yajus which from the motley Pair milked oil and water.
verses.wilson_translation: When the self-aggregated ambrosia of the divine Agniis genitive rated fromhis radiance, then theproducts from it sustain both heaven and earth, all the worshippers glorify this your oblation, the celestial nutriouswater which your white lustre milks forth.
verses.griffith_verse: When the cow's nectar wins the God completely, men here below are heaven's sustainers. All the Gods came to this thy heavenly Yajus which from the motley Pair milked oil and water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्चामि वां वर्धायापो घृतस्नू द्यावाभूमी शृणुतं रोदसी मे ।अहा यद्द्यावोऽसुनीतिमयन्मध्वा नो अत्र पितरा शिशीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: árcāmi ǀ vām ǀ várdhāya ǀ ápaḥ ǀ ghṛtasnū íti ghṛta-snū ǀ dyā́vābhūmī íti ǀ śṛṇutám ǀ rodasī íti ǀ me ǀáhā ǀ yát ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ ásu-nītim ǀ áyan ǀ mádhvā ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ pitárā ǀ śiśītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 praise your work that ye may make me prosper: hear, Heaven and Earth, Twain Worlds that drop with fatness. While days and nights go to the world of spirits, here let the Parents with sweet meath refresh us
verses.wilson_translation: I worship you, waters that pour forth ghī, and you, heaven and earth, for your increase; hear me, youworlds; when worshippers at the daily or nightly rite proceed to their pious purpose, then may the parents (of all)sanctify us with ambrosia.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 praise your work that ye may make me prosper: hear, Heaven and Earth, Twain Worlds that drop with fatness. While days and nights go to the world of spirits, here let the Parents with sweet meath refresh us
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं स्विन्नो राजा जगृहे कदस्याति व्रतं चकृमा को वि वेद ।मित्रश्चिद्धि ष्मा जुहुराणो देवांछ्लोको न यातामपि वाजो अस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ naḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ jagṛhe ǀ kát ǀ asya ǀ áti ǀ vratám ǀ cakṛma ǀ káḥ ǀ ví ǀ veda ǀmitráḥ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ sma ǀ juhurāṇáḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ ślókaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yātā́m ǀ ápi ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ásti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hath the King siezed us? How have we offended against his holy ordinance? Who knoweth? For even Mitra mid the Gods is angry there are both song and strength for those who come not.
verses.wilson_translation: But will the royal Agniaccept our oblation? Have we duly performed our vows to him? Who decides?As a friend affectionately invited, so let our praise now proceed to the gods; together with the sacrificial food thatis left over.
verses.griffith_verse: Hath the King siezed us? How have we offended against his holy ordinance? Who knoweth? For even Mitra mid the Gods is angry there are both song and strength for those who come not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दुर्मंत्वत्रामृतस्य नाम सलक्ष्मा यद्विषुरूपा भवाति ।यमस्य यो मनवते सुमंत्वग्ने तमृष्व पाह्यप्रयुच्छन् ॥
verses.transliteration: duḥ-mántu ǀ átra ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ nā́ma ǀ sá-lakṣmā ǀ yát ǀ víṣu-rūpā ǀ bhávāti ǀyamásya ǀ yáḥ ǀ manávate ǀ su-mántu ǀ ágne ǀ tám ǀ ṛṣva ǀ pāhi ǀ ápra-yucchan ǁ
verses.english_translation: ’Tis hard to understand the Immortal's nature, where she who is akin becomes astranger. Guard ceaselessly, great Agni, him who ponders Yama's name, easy to be comprehended.
verses.wilson_translation: Hard to understand is the nature of the immortal, for although of one origin, she is of a different form;cherish him diligently, great Agni, who understands Yama's nature easy to be understood.
verses.griffith_verse: ’Tis hard to understand the Immortal's nature, where she who is akin becomes astranger. Guard ceaselessly, great Agni, him who ponders Yama's name, easy to be comprehended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिंदेवा विदथे मादयंते विवस्वतः सदने धारयंते ।सूर्ये ज्योतिरदधुर्मास्यक्तून्परि द्योतनिं चरतो अजस्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vidáthe ǀ mādáyante ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀ sádane ǀ dhāráyante ǀsū́rye ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ māsí ǀ aktū́n ǀ pári ǀ dyotaním ǀ carataḥ ǀ ájasrā ǁ
verses.english_translation: They in the synod where the Gods rejoice them, where they are seated in Vivasvān's dwelling, Have given the Moon his beams, the Sun his splendour-the Two unweariedly maintain their brightness.
verses.wilson_translation: In him the gods find plural asure at the sacrifice; they seat themselves on the altar of the sacrificer. Theyplaced light in the sun; beams in the moon; and these untiring shed their light around.
verses.griffith_verse: They in the synod where the Gods rejoice them, where they are seated in Vivasvān's dwelling, Have given the Moon his beams, the Sun his splendour-the Two unweariedly maintain their brightness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिंदेवा मन्मनि संचरंत्यपीच्ये न वयमस्य विद्म ।मित्रो नो अत्रादितिरनागान्त्सविता देवो वरुणाय वोचत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ mánmani ǀ sam-cáranti ǀ apīcyé ǀ ná ǀ vayám ǀ asya ǀ vidma ǀmitráḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ átra ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ánāgān ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ váruṇāya ǀ vocat ǁ
verses.english_translation: The counsel which the Gods meet to consider, their secret plan,—of that we have no knowledge. There let God Savitar, Aditi, and Mitra proclaim to Varuṇa that we are sinless.
verses.wilson_translation: When he, the all-illumining, is there, the gods assemble; but when he is concealed, we know not (hisabode); so at this sacrifice, let Mitraand Aditiand Savitāproclaim us to Varuṇaas free from sin.
verses.griffith_verse: The counsel which the Gods meet to consider, their secret plan,—of that we have no knowledge. There let God Savitar, Aditi, and Mitra proclaim to Varuṇa that we are sinless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रुधी नो अग्ने सदने सधस्थे युक्ष्वा रथममृतस्य द्रवित्नुं ।आ नो वह रोदसी देवपुत्रे माकिर्देवानामप भूरिह स्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrudhí ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ sádane ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ yukṣvá ǀ rátham ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ dravitnúm ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vaha ǀ ródasī íti ǀ deváputre íti devá-putre ǀ mā́kiḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ápa ǀ bhūḥ ǀ ihá ǀ syāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear us, O Agni, in your comninn dwell ing: harness thy rapid car, the car of Amṛta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear us, O Agni, in your comninn dwell ing: harness thy rapid car, the car of Amṛta. Bring Heaven and Earth, the Deities' Parents, hither: stay with us here, nor from the Gods be distant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XIII Havirdhanas.
hymns.anukramani: ५ आङ्गिर्हविर्धानः। विवस्वानादित्यो वा। हविर्धाने। त्रिष्टुप्, ५ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I YOKE with prayer your ancient inspiration: may the laud rise as on the prince's pathway.All Sons of Immortality shall hear it, all the possessors of celestial natures. When speeding ye came nigh us like twin sisters, religious-hearted votaries brought you forward.Take your place, ye who know your proper station: be near, be very near unto our Soma. Five paces have I risen from Earth. I follow her who hath four feet with devout observance.This by the Sacred Syllable have I measured: I purify in the central place of Order, He, for God's sake, chose death to be his portion. He chose not, for men's good, a life eternalThey sacrificed Bṛhaspati the Ṛṣi. Yama delivered up his own dear body. The Seven flow to the Youth on whom the Maruts wait: the Sons unto the Father brought the sacrifice.Both these are his, as his they are the Lords of both: both toil; belonging unto both they prosper well.

verses.sanskrit: युजे वां ब्रह्म पूर्व्यं नमोभिर्वि श्लोक एतु पथ्येव सूरेः ।शृण्वंतु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्रा आ ये धामानि दिव्यानि तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yujé ǀ vām ǀ bráhma ǀ pūrvyám ǀ námaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ ślókaḥ ǀ etu ǀ pathyā́-iva ǀ sūréḥ ǀśṛṇvántu ǀ víśve ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yé ǀ dhā́māni ǀ divyā́ni ǀ tasthúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I YOKE with prayer your ancient inspiration: may the laud rise as on the prince's pathway. All Sons of Immortality shall hear it, all the possessors of celestial natures.
verses.wilson_translation: I load you two with sacred offerings, repeating an ancient prayer; may the sound (of your approach)reach (the gods) like the path of the worshipper, may all the sons of the immortal (Prajāpati) who inhabit thecelestial regions hear (the sound).
verses.griffith_verse: I YOKE with prayer your ancient inspiration: may the laud rise as on the prince's pathway. All Sons of Immortality shall hear it, all the possessors of celestial natures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमे इव यतमाने यदैतं प्र वां भरन्मानुषा देवयंतः ।आ सीदतं स्वमु लोकं विदाने स्वासस्थे भवतमिंदवे नः ॥
verses.transliteration: yamé ivéti yamé-iva ǀ yátamāne íti ǀ yát ǀ áitam ǀ prá ǀ vām ǀ bharan ǀ mā́nuṣāḥ ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀā́ ǀ sīdatam ǀ svám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ vídāne íti ǀ svāsasthé íti su-āsasthé ǀ bhavatam ǀ índave ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When speeding ye came nigh us like twin sisters, religious-hearted votaries brought you forward. Take your place, ye who know your proper station: be near, be very near unto our Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: When you two came, like twins, busily engaged, then devout worshipper brought you forward;knowing your plural ce there abide and be fair storehouses for our Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: When speeding ye came nigh us like twin sisters, religious-hearted votaries brought you forward. Take your place, ye who know your proper station: be near, be very near unto our Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पंच पदानि रुपो अन्वरोहं चतुष्पदीमन्वेमि व्रतेन ।अक्षरेण प्रति मिम एतामृतस्य नाभावधि सं पुनामि ॥
verses.transliteration: páñca ǀ padā́ni ǀ rupáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ aroham ǀ cátuḥ-padīm ǀ ánu ǀ emi ǀ vraténa ǀakṣáreṇa ǀ práti ǀ mime ǀ etā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ nā́bhau ǀ ádhi ǀ sám ǀ punāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Five paces have I risen from Earth. I follow her who hath four feet with devout observance. This by the Sacred Syllable have I measured: I purify in the central place of Order,
verses.wilson_translation: I make the five stages of the sacrifice ascend; I take four steps by pious observances; with the sacredsyllable, I perfect this (adoration); I purify (the Soma) on the navel of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Five paces have I risen from Earth. I follow her who hath four feet with devout observance. This by the Sacred Syllable have I measured: I purify in the central place of Order,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवेभ्यः कमवृणीत मृत्युं प्रजायै कममृतं नावृणीत ।बृहस्पतिं यज्ञमकृण्वत ऋषिं प्रियां यमस्तन्वं प्रारिरेचीत् ॥
verses.transliteration: devébhyaḥ ǀ kám ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ mṛtyúm ǀ pra-jā́yai ǀ kám ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ná ǀ avṛṇīta ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ yajñám ǀ akṛṇvata ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ priyā́m ǀ yamáḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ prá ǀ arirecīt ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, for God's sake, chose death to be his portion. He chose not, for men's good, a life eternal They sacrificed Bṛhaspati the Ṛṣi. Yama delivered up his own dear body.
verses.wilson_translation: Whom has he selected as the slayer of the gods? Whom has he not selected as non-slayer of theabove mentioned are necessarily present while the business of the bringing of the oblation is in progress, yamadoes not send any of hie men as the destroyer. Another translation: What death did he choose for the gods, whatimmortality did he not choose for men? i.e.,Yamaordained that gods should not die, and that men should receiveimmortality; Yama preserves our loved bodies: prārirecit = takes away (from death), mṛtyoḥsaka- śātpariharati; 'ric' is here used in the sense of taking away; the meaning is: he does not take our life away as aconsequence of a fault arising from a defect in our worship].
verses.griffith_verse: He, for God's sake, chose death to be his portion. He chose not, for men's good, a life eternal They sacrificed Bṛhaspati the Ṛṣi. Yama delivered up his own dear body.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्त क्षरंति शिशवे मरुत्वते पित्रे पुत्रासो अप्यवीवतन्नृतं ।उभे इदस्योभयस्य राजत उभे यतेते उभयस्य पुष्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ kṣaranti ǀ śíśave ǀ marútvate ǀ pitré ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ ápi ǀ avīvatan ǀ ṛtám ǀubhé íti ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ ubháyasya ǀ rājataḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ yatete íti ǀ ubháyasya ǀ puṣyataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Seven flow to the Youth on whom the Maruts wait: the Sons unto the Father brought the sacrifice. Both these are his, as his they are the Lords of both: both toil; belonging unto both they prosper well.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven (metres) offer laudation to the glorious, the adorable parent, (the Soma), his sons (thepriests) utter his true (praise); you both are lords of both (men and gods), you both exert yourselves and are thenourishers of both (men and gods).
verses.griffith_verse: The Seven flow to the Youth on whom the Maruts wait: the Sons unto the Father brought the sacrifice. Both these are his, as his they are the Lords of both: both toil; belonging unto both they prosper well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XIV. Yama.
hymns.anukramani: १६ वैवस्वतो यमः। यमः,६ अङ्गिरःपित्रथर्वभृगुसोमाः,७-९ लिङ्गोक्तदेवताः पितरो वा,१०-१२ श्वानौ। त्रिष्टुप्,१३,१४,१६, अनुष्टुप्,१५बृहती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HONOUR the King with thine oblations, Yama, Vivasvān's Son, who gathers men together,Who travelled to the lofty heights above us, who searcbes out and shows the path to many. Yama first found for us a place to dwell in: this pasture never can be taken fromUs.Men born on earth tread their own paths that lead them whither our ancient Fathers have departed. Mitali prospers there with Kavyas, Yama with Aṅgiras' sons, Bṛhaspati with Rkvans:Exalters of the Gods, by Gods exalted, some joy in praise and some in our oblation. Come, seat thee on this bed of grass, O Yama, in company with Aṅgirases and Fathers.Let texts recited by the sages bring thee O King, let this oblation make thee joyful. Come, Yama, with the Aṅgirases the Holy, rejoice thee here with children of Virūpa.To sit on sacred grass at this our worship, I call Vivasvān, too, thy Father hither. Our Fathers are Aṅgirases, Navagvas, Atharvans, Bhṛgus who deserve the Soma.May these, the Holy, look on us with favour, may we enjoy their gracious loving-kindness. Go forth, go forth upon the ancient pathways whereon our sires of old have gone before us.'Mere shalt thou look on both the Kings enjoying their sacred food, God Varuṇa and Yama. Meet Yama, meet the Fathers, meet the merit of free or ordered acts, in highest heaven.Leave sin and evil, seek anew thy dwelling, and bright with glory wear another body. Go hence, depart ye, fly in all directions: this place for him the Fathers have provided.Yama bestows on him a place to rest in adorned with days and beams of light and waters. Run and outspeed the two dogs, Saramā's offspring, brindled, four-eyed, upon thy happy pathway.Draw nigh then to the gracious-minded Fathers where they rejoice in company with Yama. And those two dogs of thine, Yama, the watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway,—Entrust this man, O King, to their protection, and with prosperity and health endow him. Dark-hued, insatiate, with distended nostrils, Yama's two envoys roam among the People;May they restore to us a fair existence here and to-day, that we may see the sunlight.
