To Yama pour the Soma, bring to Yama consecrated gifts:To Yama sacrifice prepared and heralded by Agni goes. Offer to Yama holy gifts enriched with butter, and draw near:So may he grant that we may live long days of life among the Gods. Offer to Yama, to the King, oblation very rich in meath:Bow down before the Ṛṣis of the ancient times, who made this path in days of old. Into the six Expanses flies the Great One in Trkadrukas.The Gāyatrī, the Tṛṣṭup, all metres in Yama are contained.

verses.sanskrit: परेयिवांसं प्रवतो महीरनु बहुभ्यः पंथामनुपस्पशानं ।वैवस्वतं संगमनं जनानां यमं राजानं हविषा दुवस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: pareyi-vā́ṃsam ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ bahú-bhyaḥ ǀ pánthām ǀ anu-paspaśānám ǀvaivasvatám ǀ sam-gámanam ǀ jánānām ǀ yamám ǀ rā́jānam ǀ havíṣā ǀ duvasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: HONOUR the King with thine oblations, Yama, Vivasvān's Son, who gathers men together, Who travelled to the lofty heights above us, who searcbes out and shows the path to many.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship with oblations from Yama, king (of the Pitṛs), son of Vivasvat, the aggregation of mankind,who conducts those who are virtuous over the earth, and opens to many the path (of heaven).
verses.griffith_verse: HONOUR the King with thine oblations, Yama, Vivasvān's Son, who gathers men together, Who travelled to the lofty heights above us, who searcbes out and shows the path to many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमो नो गातुं प्रथमो विवेद नैषा गव्यूतिरपभर्तवा उ ।यत्रा नः पूर्वे पितरः परेयुरेना जज्ञानाः पथ्या अनु स्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yamáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ viveda ǀ ná ǀ eṣā́ ǀ gávyūtiḥ ǀ ápa-bhartavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀyátra ǀ naḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ parā-īyúḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ jajñānā́ḥ ǀ pathyā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ svā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yama first found for us a place to dwell in: this pasture never can be taken from Us. Men born on earth tread their own paths that lead them whither our ancient Fathers have departed.
verses.wilson_translation: Yama, the chief (of all), knows our well-being; this pasture no one can take from us; by the road bywhich our forefathers have gone, all who are born (proceed) along the paths they have made for themselveṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Yama first found for us a place to dwell in: this pasture never can be taken from Us. Men born on earth tread their own paths that lead them whither our ancient Fathers have departed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मातली कव्यैर्यमो अंगिरोभिर्बृहस्पतिर्ऋक्वभिर्वावृधानः ।यांश्च देवा वावृधुर्ये च देवान्त्स्वाहान्ये स्वधयान्ये मदंति ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́talī ǀ kavyáiḥ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀyā́n ǀ ca ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vavṛdhúḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ devā́n ǀ svā́hā ǀ anyé ǀ svadháyā ǀ anyé ǀ madanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mitali prospers there with Kavyas, Yama with Aṅgiras' sons, Bṛhaspati with Rkvans: Exalters of the Gods, by Gods exalted, some joy in praise and some in our oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Mātalin prospers with the Kavyas;Yamawith the Aṅgirasas;Bṛhaspatiwith the Ṛkvans; they whomthe gods augment, and they who augment the gods, these rejoice in Svāhā, those in the Svadhā.
verses.griffith_verse: Mitali prospers there with Kavyas, Yama with Aṅgiras' sons, Bṛhaspati with Rkvans: Exalters of the Gods, by Gods exalted, some joy in praise and some in our oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं यम प्रस्तरमा हि सीदांगिरोभिः पितृभिः संविदानः ।आ त्वा मंत्राः कविशस्ता वहंत्वेना राजन्हविषा मादयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ yama ǀ pra-starám ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ sī́da ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sam-vidānáḥ ǀā́ ǀ tvā ǀ mántrāḥ ǀ kavi-śastā́ḥ ǀ vahantu ǀ enā́ ǀ rājan ǀ havíṣā ǀ mādayasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, seat thee on this bed of grass, O Yama, in company with Aṅgirases and Fathers. Let texts recited by the sages bring thee O King, let this oblation make thee joyful.
verses.wilson_translation: Yama, who are associated with the Aṅgirasa Pitṛs, sit down at this sacrifice; may the prayers recitedby the priests bring you here; be exhilarated, Sovereign, (Yam), by this oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, seat thee on this bed of grass, O Yama, in company with Aṅgirases and Fathers. Let texts recited by the sages bring thee O King, let this oblation make thee joyful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंगिरोभिरा गहि यज्ञियेभिर्यम वैरूपैरिह मादयस्व ।विवस्वंतं हुवे यः पिता तेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे बर्हिष्या निषद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ yajñíyebhiḥ ǀ yáma ǀ vairūpáiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mādayasva ǀvívasvantam ǀ huve ǀ yáḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ te ǀ asmín ǀ yajñé ǀ barhíṣi ǀ ā́ ǀ ni-sádya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, Yama, with the Aṅgirases the Holy, rejoice thee here with children of Virūpa. To sit on sacred grass at this our worship, I call Vivasvān, too, thy Father hither.
verses.wilson_translation: Come here,Yama, with the venerable multiform Aṅgirasas, and be exhilarated; I summon Vivasvat,who is your father, to this sacrifice; be seated on the sacred grass (delight the sacrificer).
verses.griffith_verse: Come, Yama, with the Aṅgirases the Holy, rejoice thee here with children of Virūpa. To sit on sacred grass at this our worship, I call Vivasvān, too, thy Father hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंगिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्यासः ।तेषां वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियानामपि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: áṅgirasaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ náva-gvāḥ ǀ átharvāṇaḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ somyā́saḥ ǀtéṣām ǀ vayám ǀ su-matáu ǀ yajñíyānām ǀ ápi ǀ bhadré ǀ saumanasé ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our Fathers are Aṅgirases, Navagvas, Atharvans, Bhṛgus who deserve the Soma. May these, the Holy, look on us with favour, may we enjoy their gracious loving-kindness.
verses.wilson_translation: The Aṅgirasas, the Atharvas, the Bhṛgus, who are entitled to the Soma, are our recent progenitors;may we ever have a plural ce in the favour of these venerable (pitrṣ); may we be ever held in their auspiciousregard.
verses.griffith_verse: Our Fathers are Aṅgirases, Navagvas, Atharvans, Bhṛgus who deserve the Soma. May these, the Holy, look on us with favour, may we enjoy their gracious loving-kindness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेहि प्रेहि पथिभिः पूर्व्येभिर्यत्रा नः पूर्वे पितरः परेयुः ।उभा राजाना स्वधया मदंता यमं पश्यासि वरुणं च देवं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ ihi ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ pūrvyébhiḥ ǀ yátra ǀ naḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ parā-īyúḥ ǀubhā́ ǀ rā́jānā ǀ svadháyā ǀ mádantā ǀ yamám ǀ paśyāsi ǀ váruṇam ǀ ca ǀ devám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go forth, go forth upon the ancient pathways whereon our sires of old have gone before us. 'Mere shalt thou look on both the Kings enjoying their sacred food, God Varuṇa and Yama.
verses.wilson_translation: Depart, depart, by the former paths by which our forefathers have departed; there shall you behold thetwo monarchs Yamaand the divine Varuṇarejoicing in the Svadhā.
verses.griffith_verse: Go forth, go forth upon the ancient pathways whereon our sires of old have gone before us. 'Mere shalt thou look on both the Kings enjoying their sacred food, God Varuṇa and Yama.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं गच्छस्व पितृभिः सं यमेनेष्टापूर्तेन परमे व्योमन् ।हित्वायावद्यं पुनरस्तमेहि सं गच्छस्व तन्वा सुवर्चाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ gacchasva ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ yaména ǀ iṣṭāpūrténa ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀhitvā́ya ǀ avadyám ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ sám ǀ gacchasva ǀ tanvā́ ǀ su-várcāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Meet Yama, meet the Fathers, meet the merit of free or ordered acts, in highest heaven. Leave sin and evil, seek anew thy dwelling, and bright with glory wear another body.
verses.wilson_translation: Be united with the Pitṛs, with Yama, and with the fulfilment of your wishes in the highest heaven;discarding iniquity, return to your abode, and unite yourself to a luminous body.
verses.griffith_verse: Meet Yama, meet the Fathers, meet the merit of free or ordered acts, in highest heaven. Leave sin and evil, seek anew thy dwelling, and bright with glory wear another body.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपेत वीत वि च सर्पतातोऽस्मा एतं पितरो लोकमक्रन् ।अहोभिरद्भिरक्तुभिर्व्यक्तं यमो ददात्यवसानमस्मै ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ ita ǀ ví ǀ ita ǀ ví ǀ ca ǀ sarpata ǀ átaḥ ǀ asmái ǀ etám ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ lokám ǀ akran ǀáhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ at-bhíḥ ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀ ví-aktam ǀ yamáḥ ǀ dadāti ǀ ava-sā́nam ǀ asmai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go hence, depart ye, fly in all directions: this place for him the Fathers have provided. Yama bestows on him a place to rest in adorned with days and beams of light and waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Depart from hence, begone, go far off, (evil spirits); the Pitṛshave assigned this plural ce to him, yamahas given him a plural ce of cremation consecrated by days, streams and nights. To him-- (the departedworshipper].
verses.griffith_verse: Go hence, depart ye, fly in all directions: this place for him the Fathers have provided. Yama bestows on him a place to rest in adorned with days and beams of light and waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ चतुरक्षौ शबलौ साधुना पथा ।अथा पितॄन्त्सुविदत्राँ उपेहि यमेन ये सधमादं मदंति ॥
verses.transliteration: áti ǀ drava ǀ sārameyáu ǀ śvā́nau ǀ catuḥ-akṣáu ǀ śabálau ǀ sādhúnā ǀ pathā́ ǀátha ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ su-vidátrān ǀ úpa ǀ ihi ǀ yaména ǀ yé ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǀ mádanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Run and outspeed the two dogs, Saramā's offspring, brindled, four-eyed, upon thy happy pathway. Draw nigh then to the gracious-minded Fathers where they rejoice in company with Yama.
verses.wilson_translation: Pass by a secure path beyond the two spotted four-eyed dogs, the progeny of Saramā, and join thewise Pitṛswho rejoice joyfully with Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: Run and outspeed the two dogs, Saramā's offspring, brindled, four-eyed, upon thy happy pathway. Draw nigh then to the gracious-minded Fathers where they rejoice in company with Yama.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यौ ते श्वानौ यम रक्षितारौ चतुरक्षौ पथिरक्षी नृचक्षसौ ।ताभ्यामेनं परि देहि राजन्त्स्वस्ति चास्मा अनमीवं च धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáu ǀ te ǀ śvā́nau ǀ yama ǀ rakṣitā́rau ǀ catuḥ-akṣáu ǀ pathirákṣī íti pathi-rákṣī ǀ nṛ-cákṣasau ǀtā́bhyām ǀ enam ǀ pári ǀ dehi ǀ rājan ǀ svastí ǀ ca ǀ asmai ǀ anamīvám ǀ ca ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: And those two dogs of thine, Yama, the watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway,— Entrust this man, O King, to their protection, and with prosperity and health endow him.
verses.wilson_translation: Entrust him, O king, to your two dogs, which are your protectors,Yama, the four-eyed guardians of theroad, renowned by men, and grant him prosperity and health.
verses.griffith_verse: And those two dogs of thine, Yama, the watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway,— Entrust this man, O King, to their protection, and with prosperity and health endow him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उरूणसावसुतृपा उदुंबलौ यमस्य दूतौ चरतो जनाँ अनु ।तावस्मभ्यं दृशये सूर्याय पुनर्दातामसुमद्येह भद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: uru-nasáu ǀ asu-tṛ́pau ǀ udumbaláu ǀ yamásya ǀ dūtáu ǀ carataḥ ǀ jánān ǀ ánu ǀtáu ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dṛśáye ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ púnaḥ ǀ dātām ǀ ásum ǀ adyá ǀ ihá ǀ bhadrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dark-hued, insatiate, with distended nostrils, Yama's two envoys roam among the People; May they restore to us a fair existence here and to-day, that we may see the sunlight.
verses.wilson_translation: The messengers of Yama, broad-nosed, and of exceeding strength, and satiating themselves with thelife (of mortals), hunt mankind; may they allow us this day a prosperous existence here, that we may look uponthe sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Dark-hued, insatiate, with distended nostrils, Yama's two envoys roam among the People; May they restore to us a fair existence here and to-day, that we may see the sunlight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमाय सोमं सुनुत यमाय जुहुता हविः ।यमं ह यज्ञो गच्छत्यग्निदूतो अरंकृतः ॥
verses.transliteration: yamā́ya ǀ sómam ǀ sunuta ǀ yamā́ya ǀ juhuta ǀ havíḥ ǀyamám ǀ ha ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ gacchati ǀ agní-dūtaḥ ǀ áram-kṛtaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Yama pour the Soma, bring to Yama consecrated gifts: To Yama sacrifice prepared and heralded by Agni goes.
verses.wilson_translation: Pour out the Somafor Yama; to Yama offer the oblation, the decorated sacrifice of which Agniis themessenger proceeds to Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: To Yama pour the Soma, bring to Yama consecrated gifts: To Yama sacrifice prepared and heralded by Agni goes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमाय घृतवद्धविर्जुहोत प्र च तिष्ठत ।स नो देवेष्वा यमद्दीर्घमायुः प्र जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yamā́ya ǀ ghṛtá-vat ǀ havíḥ ǀ juhóta ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ tiṣṭhata ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ yamat ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ prá ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer to Yama holy gifts enriched with butter, and draw near: So may he grant that we may live long days of life among the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer the oblation of clarified butter to Yama, and stand near (to the altar); it is he who among the godsgives us a long life to live.
verses.griffith_verse: Offer to Yama holy gifts enriched with butter, and draw near: So may he grant that we may live long days of life among the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमाय मधुमत्तमं राज्ञे हव्यं जुहोतन ।इदं नम ऋषिभ्यः पूर्वजेभ्यः पूर्वेभ्यः पथिकृद्भ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: yamā́ya ǀ mádhumat-tamam ǀ rā́jñe ǀ havyám ǀ juhotana ǀidám ǀ námaḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣi-bhyaḥ ǀ pūrva-jébhyaḥ ǀ pū́rvebhyaḥ ǀ pathikṛ́t-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Offer to Yama, to the King, oblation very rich in meath: Bow down before the Ṛṣis of the ancient times, who made this path in days of old.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer to the royal Yamathis most sweet oblation; (let) this our adoration (be addressed) to the ancientsages, the first followers of (virtuous) paths.
verses.griffith_verse: Offer to Yama, to the King, oblation very rich in meath: Bow down before the Ṛṣis of the ancient times, who made this path in days of old.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिकद्रुकेभिः पतति षळुर्वीरेकमिद्बृहत् ।त्रिष्टुब्गायत्री छंदांसि सर्वा ता यम आहिता ॥
verses.transliteration: trí-kadrukebhiḥ ǀ patati ǀ ṣáṭ ǀ urvī́ḥ ǀ ékam ǀ ít ǀ bṛhát ǀtri-stúp ǀ gāyatrī́ ǀ chándāṃsi ǀ sárvā ǀ tā́ ǀ yamé ǀ ā́-hitā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Into the six Expanses flies the Great One in Trkadrukas. The Gāyatrī, the Tṛṣṭup, all metres in Yama are contained.
verses.wilson_translation: (Yama) acquires the three trikadruka saacrifices; the six earths, the one great (moving world); thetriṣṭubh,gāyatrī, all the sacred metres converge in Yama.
verses.griffith_verse: Into the six Expanses flies the Great One in Trkadrukas. The Gāyatrī, the Tṛṣṭup, all metres in Yama are contained.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XV. Fathers.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY they ascend, the lowest, highest, midmost, the Fathers who deserve a share of Soma-May they who have attained the life of spirits, gentle and righteous, aid us when we call them. Now let us pay this homage to the Fathers, to those who passed of old and those who followed,Those who have rested in the earthly region, and those who dwell among the Mighty Races. have attained the gracious-minded Fathers, I have gained son and progeny from Viṣṇu.They who enjoy pressed juices with oblation seated on sacred grass, come oftenest hither. Fathers who sit on sacred grass, come, help us: these offerings have we made for you; accept them.So come to us with most auspicious favour, and give us health and strength without a trouble. May they, the Fathers, worthy of the Soma, invited to their favourite oblations.Laid on the sacred grass, come nigh and listen: may they be gracious unto us and bless us. Bowing your bended knees and seated southward, accept this sacrifice of ours with favour.Punish us not for any sin, O Fathers, which we through human frailty have committed. Lapped in the bosom of the purple Mornings, give riches to the man who brings oblations.Grant to your sons a portion of that treasure, and, present, give them energy, ye Fathers. Our ancient Fathers who deserve the Soma, who came, most noble, to our Soma banquet,—With these let Yama, yearning with the yearning, rejoicing eat our offerings at his pleasure. Come to us, Agni, with the gracioug Fathers who dwell in glowing light, the very Kavyas,Who thirsted mid the Gods, who hasten hither, oblation winners, theme of singers' praises. Come, Agni, come with countless ancient Fathers, dwellers in light, primeval, God-adorers,Eaters and drinkers of oblations, truthful, who travel with the Deities and Indra. Fathers whom Agni's flames have tasted, come ye nigh: ye kindly leaders, take ye each your proper place.Eat sacrificial food presented on the grass: grant riches with a multitude of hero sons. Thou, Agni Jātavedas, when entreated, didst bear the offerings which thou madest fragrant,And give them to the Fathers who did cat them with Svadha. Eat, thou God, the gifts we bring thee. Thou, Jātavedas, knowest well the number of Fathers who are here and who are absent,Of Fathers whom we know and whom we know not: accept the sacrifice wellprepared with portions. They who, consumed by fire or not cremated, joy in their offering in the midst of heaven,—Grant them, O Sovran Lord, the world of spirits and their own body, as thy pleasure wills it.

verses.sanskrit: उदीरतामवर उत्परास उन्मध्यमाः पितरः सोम्यासः ।असुं य ईयुरवृका ऋतज्ञास्ते नोऽवंतु पितरो हवेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īratām ǀ ávare ǀ út ǀ párāsaḥ ǀ út ǀ madhyamā́ḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ somyā́saḥ ǀásum ǀ yé ǀ īyúḥ ǀ avṛkā́ḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ avantu ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ háveṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY they ascend, the lowest, highest, midmost, the Fathers who deserve a share of Soma- May they who have attained the life of spirits, gentle and righteous, aid us when we call them.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the lower, the upper, the intermediate Pitṛs, rise up, accepting the Somalibation; may thoseprogenitors who, unlike wolves, acknowledging our offerings, have come to preserve our lives, protect us uponour invocations.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY they ascend, the lowest, highest, midmost, the Fathers who deserve a share of Soma- May they who have attained the life of spirits, gentle and righteous, aid us when we call them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं पितृभ्यो नमो अस्त्वद्य ये पूर्वासो य उपरास ईयुः ।ये पार्थिवे रजस्या निषत्ता ये वा नूनं सुवृजनासु विक्षु ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ astu ǀ adyá ǀ yé ǀ pū́rvāsaḥ ǀ yé ǀ úparāsaḥ ǀ īyúḥ ǀyé ǀ pā́rthive ǀ rájasi ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-sattāḥ ǀ yé ǀ vā ǀ nūnám ǀ su-vṛjánāsu ǀ vikṣú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now let us pay this homage to the Fathers, to those who passed of old and those who followed, Those who have rested in the earthly region, and those who dwell among the Mighty Races.
verses.wilson_translation: Let this our adoration be today addressed to those Pitṛsour predecessors, to those our successors,who have departed (to the world of the manes); to those who are seated in the terrestrial sphere, to those whoare present among opulent people.
verses.griffith_verse: Now let us pay this homage to the Fathers, to those who passed of old and those who followed, Those who have rested in the earthly region, and those who dwell among the Mighty Races.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आहं पितॄन्त्सुविदत्राँ अवित्सि नपातं च विक्रमणं च विष्णोः ।बर्हिषदो ये स्वधया सुतस्य भजंत पित्वस्त इहागमिष्ठाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ahám ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ su-vidátrān ǀ avitsi ǀ nápātam ǀ ca ǀ vi-krámaṇam ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀbarhi-sádaḥ ǀ yé ǀ svadháyā ǀ sutásya ǀ bhájanta ǀ pitváḥ ǀ té ǀ ihá ǀ ā́-gamiṣṭhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 have attained the gracious-minded Fathers, I have gained son and progeny from Viṣṇu. They who enjoy pressed juices with oblation seated on sacred grass, come oftenest hither.
verses.wilson_translation: I have brought to my presence the Pitṛswho are well cognizant (of my worship), the infallibility, andfood of the effused (Soma) with the sacrificial cake.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 have attained the gracious-minded Fathers, I have gained son and progeny from Viṣṇu. They who enjoy pressed juices with oblation seated on sacred grass, come oftenest hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बर्हिषदः पितर ऊत्यर्वागिमा वो हव्या चकृमा जुषध्वं ।त आ गतावसा शंतमेनाथा नः शं योररपो दधात ॥
verses.transliteration: bárhi-sadaḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ ūtī́ ǀ arvā́k ǀ imā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ cakṛma ǀ juṣádhvam ǀté ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǀ ávasā ǀ śám-tamena ǀ átha ǀ naḥ ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǀ arapáḥ ǀ dadhāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fathers who sit on sacred grass, come, help us: these offerings have we made for you; accept them. So come to us with most auspicious favour, and give us health and strength without a trouble.
verses.wilson_translation: Pitṛs,Barhiṣads, protect (us who are) in your presence; we have made these oblations for you,accept them; come with your most felicitous protection, and bestow upon us health and happiness; and pardonfrom sin.
verses.griffith_verse: Fathers who sit on sacred grass, come, help us: these offerings have we made for you; accept them. So come to us with most auspicious favour, and give us health and strength without a trouble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपहूताः पितरः सोम्यासो बर्हिष्येषु निधिषु प्रियेषु ।त आ गमंतु त इह श्रुवंत्वधि ब्रुवंतु तेऽवंत्वस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa-hūtāḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ somyā́saḥ ǀ barhiṣyéṣu ǀ ni-dhíṣu ǀ priyéṣu ǀté ǀ ā́ ǀ gamantu ǀ té ǀ ihá ǀ śruvantu ǀ ádhi ǀ bruvantu ǀ té ǀ avantu ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May they, the Fathers, worthy of the Soma, invited to their favourite oblations. Laid on the sacred grass, come nigh and listen: may they be gracious unto us and bless us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the Pitṛswho are entitled to the Somacome, when invoked by us, to the agreeable treasuresconnected with the sacred grass; let them here listen (to our praises), let them speak (their approbation in reply);let them protect us.
verses.griffith_verse: May they, the Fathers, worthy of the Soma, invited to their favourite oblations. Laid on the sacred grass, come nigh and listen: may they be gracious unto us and bless us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आच्या जानु दक्षिणतो निषद्येमं यज्ञमभि गृणीत विश्वे ।मा हिंसिष्ट पितरः केन चिन्नो यद्व आगः पुरुषता कराम ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-ácya ǀ jā́nu ǀ dakṣiṇatáḥ ǀ ni-sádya ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ abhí ǀ gṛṇīta ǀ víśve ǀmā́ ǀ hiṃsiṣṭa ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ kéna ǀ cit ǀ naḥ ǀ yát ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ puruṣátā ǀ kárāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bowing your bended knees and seated southward, accept this sacrifice of ours with favour. Punish us not for any sin, O Fathers, which we through human frailty have committed.
verses.wilson_translation: Having sat down on the right side withbended knee, do you all accept this sacrifice. Harm us not Pitṛs, for any offence which through human (infirmity) we may have committed towards you.
verses.griffith_verse: Bowing your bended knees and seated southward, accept this sacrifice of ours with favour. Punish us not for any sin, O Fathers, which we through human frailty have committed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आसीनासो अरुणीनामुपस्थे रयिं धत्त दाशुषे मर्त्याय ।पुत्रेभ्यः पितरस्तस्य वस्वः प्र यच्छत त इहोर्जं दधात ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́sīnāsaḥ ǀ aruṇī́nām ǀ upá-sthe ǀ rayím ǀ dhatta ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ mártyāya ǀputrébhyaḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ tásya ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ prá ǀ yacchata ǀ té ǀ ihá ǀ ū́rjam ǀ dadhāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lapped in the bosom of the purple Mornings, give riches to the man who brings oblations. Grant to your sons a portion of that treasure, and, present, give them energy, ye Fathers.
verses.wilson_translation: Seated in the proximity of the radiant (flames of the altar), bestow riches on the mortal donor (of theoblation); give wealth,Pitṛs, to his sons; do you who are present grant us vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: Lapped in the bosom of the purple Mornings, give riches to the man who brings oblations. Grant to your sons a portion of that treasure, and, present, give them energy, ye Fathers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये नः पूर्वे पितरः सोम्यासोऽनूहिरे सोमपीथं वसिष्ठाः ।तेभिर्यमः संरराणो हवींष्युशन्नुशद्भिः प्रतिकाममत्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ naḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ somyā́saḥ ǀ anu-ūhiré ǀ soma-pīthám ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ sam-rarāṇáḥ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ uśán ǀ uśát-bhiḥ ǀ prati-kāmám ǀ attu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our ancient Fathers who deserve the Soma, who came, most noble, to our Soma banquet,— With these let Yama, yearning with the yearning, rejoicing eat our offerings at his pleasure.
verses.wilson_translation: May Yama, being propitiated, desirous (of the offering), partake at plural asure of the oblations along withthose our ancient progenitors of the Saumyas, the possessors of great wealth, who also desire it, and whoconveyed the Soma(to the gods and to the Pitṛs) in order.
verses.griffith_verse: Our ancient Fathers who deserve the Soma, who came, most noble, to our Soma banquet,— With these let Yama, yearning with the yearning, rejoicing eat our offerings at his pleasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये तातृषुर्देवत्रा जेहमाना होत्राविदः स्तोमतष्टासो अर्कैः ।आग्ने याहि सुविदत्रेभिरर्वाङ्सत्यैः कव्यैः पितृभिर्घर्मसद्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ tatṛṣúḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ jéhamānāḥ ǀ hotrā-vídaḥ ǀ stóma-taṣṭāsaḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀā́ ǀ agne ǀ yāhi ǀ su-vidátrebhiḥ ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ satyáiḥ ǀ kavyáiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ gharmasát-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come to us, Agni, with the gracioug Fathers who dwell in glowing light, the very Kavyas, Who thirsted mid the Gods, who hasten hither, oblation winners, theme of singers' praises.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Agni, to our presence with the Pitṛs, who are possessed of knowledge, who having attained aseat among the gods, thirst (for the Soma), skilled in sacrifices, reciters of praises with hymns, truth-speaking,seers, frequenters of sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Come to us, Agni, with the gracioug Fathers who dwell in glowing light, the very Kavyas, Who thirsted mid the Gods, who hasten hither, oblation winners, theme of singers' praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये सत्यासो हविरदो हविष्पा इंद्रेण देवैः सरथं दधानाः ।आग्ने याहि सहस्रं देववंदैः परैः पूर्वैः पितृभिर्घर्मसद्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ satyā́saḥ ǀ haviḥ-ádaḥ ǀ haviḥ-pā́ḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ deváiḥ ǀ sa-rátham ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀā́ ǀ agne ǀ yāhi ǀ sahásram ǀ deva-vandáiḥ ǀ páraiḥ ǀ pū́rvaiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ gharmasát-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, Agni, come with countless ancient Fathers, dwellers in light, primeval, God-adorers, Eaters and drinkers of oblations, truthful, who travel with the Deities and Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Agni, with thousands of Pitṛs, of both past and future (time), frequenters of sacrifices, eulogistsof the gods; those who are true, who feed on oblations, and drink oblations, possessing equality with Indraandthe gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, Agni, come with countless ancient Fathers, dwellers in light, primeval, God-adorers, Eaters and drinkers of oblations, truthful, who travel with the Deities and Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निष्वात्ताः पितर एह गच्छत सदःसदः सदत सुप्रणीतयः ।अत्ता हवींषि प्रयतानि बर्हिष्यथा रयिं सर्ववीरं दधातन ॥
verses.transliteration: ágni-svāttāḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ gacchata ǀ sádaḥ-sadaḥ ǀ sadata ǀ su-pranītayaḥ ǀattá ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ prá-yatāni ǀ barhíṣi ǀ átha ǀ rayím ǀ sárva-vīram ǀ dadhātana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fathers whom Agni's flames have tasted, come ye nigh: ye kindly leaders, take ye each your proper place. Eat sacrificial food presented on the grass: grant riches with a multitude of hero sons.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, come to this solemnity; sit down, directors in the right way, in your appropriateplaces; eat the oblations spread on the grass, and grant us riches andmaleposterity.
verses.griffith_verse: Fathers whom Agni's flames have tasted, come ye nigh: ye kindly leaders, take ye each your proper place. Eat sacrificial food presented on the grass: grant riches with a multitude of hero sons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमग्न ईळितो जातवेदोऽवाड्ढव्यानि सुरभीणि कृत्वी ।प्रादाः पितृभ्यः स्वधया ते अक्षन्नद्धि त्वं देव प्रयता हवींषि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ agne ǀ īḷitáḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ ávāṭ ǀ havyā́ni ǀ surabhī́ṇi ǀ kṛtvī́ ǀprá ǀ adāḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ svadháyā ǀ té ǀ akṣan ǀ addhí ǀ tvám ǀ deva ǀ prá-yatā ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Agni Jātavedas, when entreated, didst bear the offerings which thou madest fragrant, And give them to the Fathers who did cat them with Svadha. Eat, thou God, the gifts we bring thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni Jātavedas, who are glorified (by us), having made our oblations fragrant, you have borne themoff, and have presented them to the Pitṛs; may they partake of them with the Svadhā; and do you also, divine Agni, feed upon the offered oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Agni Jātavedas, when entreated, didst bear the offerings which thou madest fragrant, And give them to the Fathers who did cat them with Svadha. Eat, thou God, the gifts we bring thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये चेह पितरो ये च नेह यांश्च विद्म याँ उ च न प्रविद्म ।त्वं वेत्थ यति ते जातवेदः स्वधाभिर्यज्ञं सुकृतं जुषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ca ǀ ihá ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ yé ǀ ca ǀ ná ǀ ihá ǀ yā́n ǀ ca ǀ vidmá ǀ yā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ca ǀ ná ǀ pra-vidmá ǀtvám ǀ vettha ǀ yáti ǀ té ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ sú-kṛtam ǀ juṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Jātavedas, knowest well the number of Fathers who are here and who are absent, Of Fathers whom we know and whom we know not: accept the sacrifice wellprepared with portions.
verses.wilson_translation: You know,Jātavedas, those Pitṛs, how many they may be, who are not in this world, those whom weknow, and those whom we do not fully know; enjoy this pious sacrifice offered together withsvadhās.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Jātavedas, knowest well the number of Fathers who are here and who are absent, Of Fathers whom we know and whom we know not: accept the sacrifice wellprepared with portions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये अग्निदग्धा ये अनग्निदग्धा मध्ये दिवः स्वधया मादयंते ।तेभिः स्वराळसुनीतिमेतां यथावशं तन्वं कल्पयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ agni-dagdhā́ḥ ǀ yé ǀ ánagni-dagdhāḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ diváḥ ǀ svadháyā ǀ mādáyante ǀtébhiḥ ǀ sva-rā́ṭ ǀ ásu-nītim ǀ etā́m ǀ yathā-vaśám ǀ tanvám ǀ kalpayasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who, consumed by fire or not cremated, joy in their offering in the midst of heaven,— Grant them, O Sovran Lord, the world of spirits and their own body, as thy pleasure wills it.
verses.wilson_translation: May those who are agnidagdhas, and those who are not, be satisfied withsvadhāin the midst ofheaven; and do you supreme lord, associated with them, construct at your plural asure that body that is endowedwith breath.
verses.griffith_verse: They who, consumed by fire or not cremated, joy in their offering in the midst of heaven,— Grant them, O Sovran Lord, the world of spirits and their own body, as thy pleasure wills it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Burn him not up, nor quite consume him, Agni: let not his body or his skin be scattered.O Jātavedas, when thou hast matured him, then send him on his way unto the Fathers. When thou hast made him ready, Jātavedas, then do thou give him over to the Fathers.When he attains unto the life that waits him, he shall become the Deities' controller. The Sun receive thine eye, tne Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven.Go, if it be thy lot, unto the waters; go, make thine home in plants with all thy members. Thy portion is the goat: with heat consume him: let thy fierce flame, thy glowing splendour, burn himWith thine auspicious forms, o Jātavedas, bear this man to the region of the pious. Again, O Agni, to the Fathers send him who, offered in thee, goes with our oblations.Wearing new life let him increase his offspring: let him rejoin a body, Jātavedas. What wound soe’er the dark bird hath inflicted, the emmet, or the serpent, or the jackal,May Agni who devoureth all things heal it and Soma who hath passed into the Brahmans. Shield thee with flesh against the flames of Agni, encompass thee about with fat and marrow,So will the Bold One, eager to attack thee with fierce glow fail to girdle and consume thee. Forbear, O Agni, to upset this ladle: the Gods and they who merit Soma love it.This ladle, this which serves the Gods to drink from, in this the Immortal Deities rejoice them. send afar flesh eating Agni, bearing off stains may he depart to Yama's subjects.But let this other Jātavedas carry oblation to the Gods, for he is skilful. I choose as God for Father-worship Agni, flesh-eater, who hath past within your dwelling,While looking on this other Jātavedas. Let him light flames in the supreme assembly. With offerings meet let Agni bring the Fathers who support the Law.Let him announce oblations paid to Fathers and to Deities. Right gladly would we set thee down, right gladly make thee burn and glow.Gladly bring yearning Fathers nigh to cat the food of sacrifice. Cool, Agni, and again refresh the spot which thou hast scorched and burnt.Here let the water-lily grow, and tender grass and leafy herb. O full of coolness, thou cool Plant, full of fresh moisture, freshening Herb,Come hither with the female frog: fill with delight this Agni here.

verses.sanskrit: मैनमग्ने वि दहो माभि शोचो मास्य त्वचं चिक्षिपो मा शरीरं ।यदा शृतं कृणवो जातवेदोऽथेमेनं प्र हिणुतात्पितृभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ enam ǀ agne ǀ ví ǀ dahaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ abhí ǀ śocaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ asya ǀ tvácam ǀ cikṣipaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ śárīram ǀyadā́ ǀ śṛtám ǀ kṛṇávaḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ átha ǀ īm ǀ enam ǀ prá ǀ hiṇutāt ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Burn him not up, nor quite consume him, Agni: let not his body or his skin be scattered. O Jātavedas, when thou hast matured him, then send him on his way unto the Fathers.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, consume him not entirely; afflict him not; scatter not (here and there) his skin nor his body; when Jātavedas, you have rendered him mature, then send him to the Pitṛs.
verses.griffith_verse: Burn him not up, nor quite consume him, Agni: let not his body or his skin be scattered. O Jātavedas, when thou hast matured him, then send him on his way unto the Fathers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शृतं यदा करसि जातवेदोऽथेमेनं परि दत्तात्पितृभ्यः ।यदा गच्छात्यसुनीतिमेतामथा देवानां वशनीर्भवाति ॥
verses.transliteration: śṛtám ǀ yadā́ ǀ kárasi ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ átha ǀ īm ǀ enam ǀ pári ǀ dattāt ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀyadā́ ǀ gácchāti ǀ ásu-nītim ǀ etā́m ǀ átha ǀ devā́nām ǀ vaśa-nī́ḥ ǀ bhavāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When thou hast made him ready, Jātavedas, then do thou give him over to the Fathers. When he attains unto the life that waits him, he shall become the Deities' controller.
verses.wilson_translation: When you have rendered him mature, then give him up,Jātavedas, to the Pitṛs; when he proceedsto that world of spirits, then he becomes subject to the will of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: When thou hast made him ready, Jātavedas, then do thou give him over to the Fathers. When he attains unto the life that waits him, he shall become the Deities' controller.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूर्यं चक्षुर्गच्छतु वातमात्मा द्यां च गच्छ पृथिवीं च धर्मणा ।अपो वा गच्छ यदि तत्र ते हितमोषधीषु प्रति तिष्ठा शरीरैः ॥
verses.transliteration: sū́ryam ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ gacchatu ǀ vā́tam ǀ ātmā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ca ǀ gaccha ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ ca ǀ dhármaṇā ǀapáḥ ǀ vā ǀ gaccha ǀ yádi ǀ tátra ǀ te ǀ hitám ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǀ práti ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ śárīraiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Sun receive thine eye, tne Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven. Go, if it be thy lot, unto the waters; go, make thine home in plants with all thy members.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the eye repair to the sun; the breath to the wind; go you to the heaven or to the earth, according toyour merit; or go to the waters it it suits you (to be) there, or abide with your members in the plural nts.
verses.griffith_verse: The Sun receive thine eye, tne Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven. Go, if it be thy lot, unto the waters; go, make thine home in plants with all thy members.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजो भागस्तपसा तं तपस्व तं ते शोचिस्तपतु तं ते अर्चिः ।यास्ते शिवास्तन्वो जातवेदस्ताभिर्वहैनं सुकृतामु लोकं ॥
verses.transliteration: ajáḥ ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ tápasā ǀ tám ǀ tapasva ǀ tám ǀ te ǀ śocíḥ ǀ tapatu ǀ tám ǀ te ǀ arcíḥ ǀyā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ śivā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ vaha ǀ enam ǀ su-kṛ́tām ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy portion is the goat: with heat consume him: let thy fierce flame, thy glowing splendour, burn him With thine auspicious forms, o Jātavedas, bear this man to the region of the pious.
verses.wilson_translation: The unborn portion; burn that,Agni, with your heat; let your flame, your splendour, consume it; withthose glorious members which you have given him,Jātavedas, bear him to the world (of the virtuous).
verses.griffith_verse: Thy portion is the goat: with heat consume him: let thy fierce flame, thy glowing splendour, burn him With thine auspicious forms, o Jātavedas, bear this man to the region of the pious.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव सृज पुनरग्ने पितृभ्यो यस्त आहुतश्चरति स्वधाभिः ।आयुर्वसान उप वेतु शेषः सं गच्छतां तन्वा जातवेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ sṛja ǀ púnaḥ ǀ agne ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ cárati ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀā́yuḥ ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vetu ǀ śéṣaḥ ǀ sám ǀ gacchatām ǀ tanvā́ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Again, O Agni, to the Fathers send him who, offered in thee, goes with our oblations. Wearing new life let him increase his offspring: let him rejoin a body, Jātavedas.
verses.wilson_translation: Dismiss again to the Pitṛs,Agni, him who offered on you, comes with thesvadhās; putting on(celestial) life, let the remains (of bodily life) depart; let him,Jātavedas, be associated with a body.
verses.griffith_verse: Again, O Agni, to the Fathers send him who, offered in thee, goes with our oblations. Wearing new life let him increase his offspring: let him rejoin a body, Jātavedas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते कृष्णः शकुन आतुतोद पिपीलः सर्प उत वा श्वापदः ।अग्निष्टद्विश्वादगदं कृणोतु सोमश्च यो ब्राह्मणाँ आविवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ kṛṣṇáḥ ǀ śakunáḥ ǀ ā-tutóda ǀ pipīláḥ ǀ sarpáḥ ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ śvā́padaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ tát ǀ viśva-át ǀ agadám ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ca ǀ yáḥ ǀ brāhmaṇā́n ǀ ā-vivéśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: What wound soe’er the dark bird hath inflicted, the emmet, or the serpent, or the jackal, May Agni who devoureth all things heal it and Soma who hath passed into the Brahmans.
verses.wilson_translation: Should the black crow, the ant, the snake, the wild beast, harm (a limb) of you, may Agnitheall-devourer, and the Somathat has pervaded thebrāhmaṇas, make it whole.
verses.griffith_verse: What wound soe’er the dark bird hath inflicted, the emmet, or the serpent, or the jackal, May Agni who devoureth all things heal it and Soma who hath passed into the Brahmans.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नेर्वर्म परि गोभिर्व्ययस्व सं प्रोर्णुष्व पीवसा मेदसा च ।नेत्त्वा धृष्णुर्हरसा जर्हृषाणो दधृग्विधक्ष्यन्पर्यंखयाते ॥
verses.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ várma ǀ pári ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ vyayasva ǀ sám ǀ prá ǀ ūrṇuṣva ǀ pī́vasā ǀ médasā ǀ ca ǀná ǀ ít ǀ tvā ǀ dhṛṣṇúḥ ǀ hárasā ǀ járhṛṣāṇaḥ ǀ dadhṛ́k ǀ vi-dhakṣyán ǀ pari-aṅkháyāte ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shield thee with flesh against the flames of Agni, encompass thee about with fat and marrow, So will the Bold One, eager to attack thee with fierce glow fail to girdle and consume thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Enclose the mail of Agniwith the (hide of the) cow; cover it with the fat and marrow; then will not(Agni), bold, exulting in his fierce heat, proud, embrace you roundabout to consume you (toashes).
verses.griffith_verse: Shield thee with flesh against the flames of Agni, encompass thee about with fat and marrow, So will the Bold One, eager to attack thee with fierce glow fail to girdle and consume thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इममग्ने चमसं मा वि जिह्वरः प्रियो देवानामुत सोम्यानां ।एष यश्चमसो देवपानस्तस्मिंदेवा अमृता मादयंते ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ agne ǀ camasám ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ jihvaraḥ ǀ priyáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ utá ǀ somyā́nām ǀeṣáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ camasáḥ ǀ deva-pā́naḥ ǀ tásmin ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ mādayante ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forbear, O Agni, to upset this ladle: the Gods and they who merit Soma love it. This ladle, this which serves the Gods to drink from, in this the Immortal Deities rejoice them.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, shake not this ladle, for it is dear to the gods and to the (Pitṛs) who are worthy of the Soma; thiswhich is the drinking ladle of the ogds, in this immortal gods delight.
verses.griffith_verse: Forbear, O Agni, to upset this ladle: the Gods and they who merit Soma love it. This ladle, this which serves the Gods to drink from, in this the Immortal Deities rejoice them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्रव्यादमग्निं प्र हिणोमि दूरं यमराज्ञो गच्छतु रिप्रवाहः ।इहैवायमितरो जातवेदा देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहतु प्रजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: kravya-ádam ǀ agním ǀ prá ǀ hiṇomi ǀ dūrám ǀ yamá-rājñaḥ ǀ gacchatu ǀ ripra-vāháḥ ǀihá ǀ evá ǀ ayám ǀ ítaraḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ havyám ǀ vahatu ǀ pra-jānán ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 send afar flesh eating Agni, bearing off stains may he depart to Yama's subjects. But let this other Jātavedas carry oblation to the Gods, for he is skilful.
verses.wilson_translation: I send the flesh-devouring Agnito a distance; let him bearing away sin repair to (the realm of) king Yama; but let this other Jātavedaswho is known (by all) convey the oblation to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 send afar flesh eating Agni, bearing off stains may he depart to Yama's subjects. But let this other Jātavedas carry oblation to the Gods, for he is skilful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अग्निः क्रव्यात्प्रविवेश वो गृहमिमं पश्यन्नितरं जातवेदसं ।तं हरामि पितृयज्ञाय देवं स घर्ममिन्वात्परमे सधस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ kravya-át ǀ pra-vivéśa ǀ vaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǀ imám ǀ páśyan ǀ ítaram ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀtám ǀ harāmi ǀ pitṛ-yajñā́ya ǀ devám ǀ sáḥ ǀ gharmám ǀ invāt ǀ paramé ǀ sadhá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: I choose as God for Father-worship Agni, flesh-eater, who hath past within your dwelling, While looking on this other Jātavedas. Let him light flames in the supreme assembly.
verses.wilson_translation: The flesh-devouring deity Agni, who has entered your dwelling, I turn him out, for the worship of the Pitṛs, upon beholding this other (Agni)Jātavedas; let him celebrate the sacrifice (to the Pitṛs) in the mostexcellent assembly.
verses.griffith_verse: I choose as God for Father-worship Agni, flesh-eater, who hath past within your dwelling, While looking on this other Jātavedas. Let him light flames in the supreme assembly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अग्निः क्रव्यवाहनः पितॄन्यक्षदृतावृधः ।प्रेदु हव्यानि वोचति देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्य आ ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ kravya-vā́hanaḥ ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ yákṣat ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀprá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ havyā́ni ǀ vocati ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With offerings meet let Agni bring the Fathers who support the Law. Let him announce oblations paid to Fathers and to Deities.
verses.wilson_translation: Let Agnithe bearer of the Kavyaworship the Pitṛs, who are magnified by truth, let him declare whichare the offerings to the gods, which to the Pitṛs.
verses.griffith_verse: With offerings meet let Agni bring the Fathers who support the Law. Let him announce oblations paid to Fathers and to Deities.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उशंतस्त्वा नि धीमह्युशंतः समिधीमहि ।उशन्नुशत आ वह पितॄन्हविषे अत्तवे ॥
verses.transliteration: uśántaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ ní ǀ dhīmahi ǀ uśántaḥ ǀ sám ǀ idhīmahi ǀuśán ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaha ǀ pitṝ́n ǀ havíṣe ǀ áttave ǁ
verses.english_translation: Right gladly would we set thee down, right gladly make thee burn and glow. Gladly bring yearning Fathers nigh to cat the food of sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Longing we set you down; longing we kindle you; do you longing bring the longing Pitṛsto eat of the(sacrificial) viands.
verses.griffith_verse: Right gladly would we set thee down, right gladly make thee burn and glow. Gladly bring yearning Fathers nigh to cat the food of sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं त्वमग्ने समदहस्तमु निर्वापया पुनः ।कियांब्वत्र रोहतु पाकदूर्वा व्यल्कशा ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ sam-ádahaḥ ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ níḥ ǀ vāpaya ǀ púnaríti ǀkiyā́mbu ǀ átra ǀ rohatu ǀ pāka-dūrvā́ ǀ ví-alkaśā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cool, Agni, and again refresh the spot which thou hast scorched and burnt. Here let the water-lily grow, and tender grass and leafy herb.
verses.wilson_translation: Cool again,Agni, the spot which you have burned, there let thewater- lilygrow, and the ripe Durvawith its many stalks.
verses.griffith_verse: Cool, Agni, and again refresh the spot which thou hast scorched and burnt. Here let the water-lily grow, and tender grass and leafy herb.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शीतिके शीतिकावति ह्लादिके ह्लादिकावति ।मंडूक्या सु सं गम इमं स्वग्निं हर्षय ॥
verses.transliteration: śī́tike ǀ śī́tikā-vati ǀ hlā́dike ǀ hlā́dikā-vati ǀmaṇḍūkyā́ ǀ sú ǀ sám ǀ gamaḥ ǀ imám ǀ sú ǀ agním ǀ harṣaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: O full of coolness, thou cool Plant, full of fresh moisture, freshening Herb, Come hither with the female frog: fill with delight this Agni here.
verses.wilson_translation: (Oh earth), cool and filled with cool (herbs), gladsome and filled with gladsome (trees), be throngedwith feminine le frogs and give joy to this Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: O full of coolness, thou cool Plant, full of fresh moisture, freshening Herb, Come hither with the female frog: fill with delight this Agni here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XVII. Various Deities.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . TVASTAR prepares the bridal of his Daughter: all the world hears the tidings and assembles.But Yama's Mother, Spouse of great Vivasvān, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling. From mortal men they hid the Immortal Lady, made one like her and gave her to Vivasvān.Saranyu brought to him the Aśvin brothers, and then deserted both twinned pairs of children. Guard of the world, whose cattle ne’er are injured, may Pūṣan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge.May he consign thee to these Fathers' keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee. May Āyu, giver of all life, protect thee, and bear thee forward on the distant pathway.Thither let Savitar the God transport thee, where dwell the pious who have passed-before thee. Pūṣan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and danger.Giver of blessings, glowing, all-heroic, may he, thewise and watchful, go before us. Pūṣan was born to move on distant pathways, on the road far from earth and far from heaven.To both most wonted places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge. The pious call Sarasvatī, they worship Sarasvatī while sacrifice proceedeth.The pious called Sarasvatī aforetime. Sarasvatī send bliss to him who giveth. Sarasvatī, who camest with the Fathers, with them rejoicing thee in our oblations,Seated upon this sacred grass be joyful, and give us strengthening food that brings no sickness. Thou, called on as Sarasvatī by Fathers who come right forward to our solemn service,Give food and wealth to present sacrificers, a portion, worth a thousand, of refreshment. The Mother Floods shall make us bright and shining, cleansers of holy oil, with oil shall cleanse us:For, Goddesses, they bear off all defilement: I, rise up from them purified and brightened. Through days of earliest date the Drop descended on this place and on that which was before it.I offer up, throughout the seven oblations, the Drop which still to one same place is moving. The Drop that falls, thy stalk which arms have shaken, which from the bosom of the press hath fallen,Or from the Adhvaryu's purifying filter, I offer thee with heart and cry of Vaṣaṭ! That fallen Drop of thine, the stalk which from the ladle fell away,This present God Bṛhaspati shall pour it forth to make us rich. The plants of earth are rich in milk, and rich in milk is this my speech;And rich in milk the essence of the Waters: make me pure therewith.

verses.sanskrit: त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति ।यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥
verses.transliteration: tváṣṭā ǀ duhitré ǀ vahatúm ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ íti ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ sám ǀ eti ǀyamásya ǀ mātā́ ǀ pari-uhyámānā ǀ maháḥ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ vívasvataḥ ǀ nanāśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: TVASTAR prepares the bridal of his Daughter: all the world hears the tidings and assembles. But Yama's Mother, Spouse of great Vivasvān, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: Tvaṣṭācelebrates the marriage of his daughter; therefore, the whole world is assembled; but themother of Yama, the newly-married wife of the mighty Vivasvat, disappeared.
verses.griffith_verse: TVASTAR prepares the bridal of his Daughter: all the world hears the tidings and assembles. But Yama's Mother, Spouse of great Vivasvān, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते ।उताश्विनावभरद्यत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ agūhan ǀ amṛ́tām ǀ mártyebhyaḥ ǀ kṛtvī́ ǀ sá-varṇām ǀ adaduḥ ǀ vívasvate ǀutá ǀ aśvínau ǀ abharat ǀ yát ǀ tát ǀ ā́sīt ǀ ájahāt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dvā́ ǀ mithunā́ ǀ saraṇyū́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From mortal men they hid the Immortal Lady, made one like her and gave her to Vivasvān. Saranyu brought to him the Aśvin brothers, and then deserted both twinned pairs of children.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods concealing the immortal (Sarṇyū) for th esake of mortals and having formed her, gave herto Vivasvat. She bore the two Aśvinswhen this had happened and then Saraṇyūgave birth to two twins.
verses.griffith_verse: From mortal men they hid the Immortal Lady, made one like her and gave her to Vivasvān. Saranyu brought to him the Aśvin brothers, and then deserted both twinned pairs of children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा त्वेतश्च्यावयतु प्र विद्वाननष्टपशुर्भुवनस्य गोपाः ।स त्वैतेभ्यः परि ददत्पितृभ्योऽग्निर्देवेभ्यः सुविदत्रियेभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ tvā ǀ itáḥ ǀ cyavayatu ǀ prá ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ánaṣṭa-paśuḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ tvā ǀ etébhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀ dadat ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ su-vidatríyebhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Guard of the world, whose cattle ne’er are injured, may Pūṣan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge. May he consign thee to these Fathers' keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee.
verses.wilson_translation: May the discriminating Pūṣan, whose cattle are never lost, the protector of all beings, transfer youhence (to a better world); may he give you to these Pitṛs; may Agni(give) you to the beneficent gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Guard of the world, whose cattle ne’er are injured, may Pūṣan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge. May he consign thee to these Fathers' keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आयुर्विश्वायुः परि पासति त्वा पूषा त्वा पातु प्रपथे पुरस्तात् ।यत्रासते सुकृतो यत्र ते ययुस्तत्र त्वा देवः सविता दधातु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́yuḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ pári ǀ pāsati ǀ tvā ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ tvā ǀ pātu ǀ prá-pathe ǀ purástāt ǀyátra ǀ ā́sate ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ yátra ǀ té ǀ yayúḥ ǀ tátra ǀ tvā ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ dadhātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Āyu, giver of all life, protect thee, and bear thee forward on the distant pathway. Thither let Savitar the God transport thee, where dwell the pious who have passed-before thee.
verses.wilson_translation: May the all-pervading Vāyuprotect you, may Pūṣan(preserve) you, (going) first on the excellentpath (to heaven); may the divine Savitāplural ce you, where the virtuous abide, whither they have gone.
verses.griffith_verse: May Āyu, giver of all life, protect thee, and bear thee forward on the distant pathway. Thither let Savitar the God transport thee, where dwell the pious who have passed-before thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूषेमा आशा अनु वेद सर्वाः सो अस्माँ अभयतमेन नेषत् ।स्वस्तिदा आघृणिः सर्ववीरोऽप्रयुच्छन्पुर एतु प्रजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ veda ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ ábhaya-tamena ǀ neṣat ǀsvasti-dā́ḥ ǀ ā́ghṛṇiḥ ǀ sárva-vīraḥ ǀ ápra-yucchan ǀ puráḥ ǀ etu ǀ pra-jānán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and danger. Giver of blessings, glowing, all-heroic, may he, thewise and watchful, go before us.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣanknows all these regions severally; met him conduct us by (the path) that is most free fromperil; let him precede us, who is the giver of prosperity, endowed with radiance, accompanied by all pious men,ever vigilant, and knowing our (deserts).
verses.griffith_verse: Pūṣan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and danger. Giver of blessings, glowing, all-heroic, may he, thewise and watchful, go before us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा प्रपथे दिवः प्रपथे पृथिव्याः ।उभे अभि प्रियतमे सधस्थे आ च परा च चरति प्रजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá-pathe ǀ pathā́m ǀ ajaniṣṭa ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ prá-pathe ǀ diváḥ ǀ prá-pathe ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀubhé íti ǀ abhí ǀ priyátame íti priyá-tame ǀ sadhásthe íti sadhá-sthe ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ párā ǀ ca ǀ carati ǀ pra-jānán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣan was born to move on distant pathways, on the road far from earth and far from heaven. To both most wonted places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣanhas been born on the best path of paths, on the best path of heaven on the best path ofearth, he goes forward and backward over both (worlds), the assemblies longed for by all, discriminating (themerits of the dead).
verses.griffith_verse: Pūṣan was born to move on distant pathways, on the road far from earth and far from heaven. To both most wonted places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वतीं देवयंतो हवंते सरस्वतीमध्वरे तायमाने ।सरस्वतीं सुकृतो अह्वयंत सरस्वती दाशुषे वार्यं दात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sárasvatīm ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ havante ǀ sárasvatīm ǀ adhvaré ǀ tāyámāne ǀsárasvatīm ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ ahvayanta ǀ sárasvatī ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vā́ryam ǀ dāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: The pious call Sarasvatī, they worship Sarasvatī while sacrifice proceedeth. The pious called Sarasvatī aforetime. Sarasvatī send bliss to him who giveth.
verses.wilson_translation: The devout invoke Sarasvatī; they worship Sarasvatī at the strewn sacrifice; the virtuous call upon Sarasvatī; may Sarasvatī bestow blessings upon the donor (of the oblation).
verses.griffith_verse: The pious call Sarasvatī, they worship Sarasvatī while sacrifice proceedeth. The pious called Sarasvatī aforetime. Sarasvatī send bliss to him who giveth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वति या सरथं ययाथ स्वधाभिर्देवि पितृभिर्मदंती ।आसद्यास्मिन्बर्हिषि मादयस्वानमीवा इष आ धेह्यस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: sárasvati ǀ yā́ ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yayā́tha ǀ svadhā́bhiḥ ǀ devi ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ mádantī ǀā-sádya ǀ asmín ǀ barhíṣi ǀ mādayasva ǀ anamīvā́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dhehi ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sarasvatī, who camest with the Fathers, with them rejoicing thee in our oblations, Seated upon this sacred grass be joyful, and give us strengthening food that brings no sickness.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Sarasvatī, who rides in the same chariot with the Pitṛs, and delighted (along with them) by the(sacrificial) viands, seated on the sacred grass gratified (by our offering, and grant us wholesome food. worshippers at this sacrifice a portion of food fit for thousands, and increase of riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Sarasvatī, who camest with the Fathers, with them rejoicing thee in our oblations, Seated upon this sacred grass be joyful, and give us strengthening food that brings no sickness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वतीं यां पितरो हवंते दक्षिणा यज्ञमभिनक्षमाणाः ।सहस्रार्घमिळो अत्र भागं रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: sárasvatīm ǀ yā́m ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ hávante ǀ dakṣiṇā́ ǀ yajñám ǀ abhi-nákṣamāṇāḥ ǀsahasra-arghám ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ átra ǀ bhāgám ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ yájamāneṣu ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, called on as Sarasvatī by Fathers who come right forward to our solemn service, Give food and wealth to present sacrificers, a portion, worth a thousand, of refreshment.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, called on as Sarasvatī by Fathers who come right forward to our solemn service, Give food and wealth to present sacrificers, a portion, worth a thousand, of refreshment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो अस्मान्मातरः शुंधयंतु घृतेन नो घृतप्वः पुनंतु ।विश्वं हि रिप्रं प्रवहंति देवीरुदिदाभ्यः शुचिरा पूत एमि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ mātáraḥ ǀ śundhayantu ǀ ghṛténa ǀ naḥ ǀ ghṛta-pváḥ ǀ punantu ǀvíśvam ǀ hí ǀ riprám ǀ pra-váhanti ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ út ǀ ít ǀ ābhyaḥ ǀ śúciḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pūtáḥ ǀ emi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Mother Floods shall make us bright and shining, cleansers of holy oil, with oil shall cleanse us: For, Goddesses, they bear off all defilement: I, rise up from them purified and brightened.
verses.wilson_translation: May the maternal waters, purify us; may the shedders of water purify us with the effusion; for thedivine (waters) bear away all sin; I come away from them purified (to heaven).
verses.griffith_verse: The Mother Floods shall make us bright and shining, cleansers of holy oil, with oil shall cleanse us: For, Goddesses, they bear off all defilement: I, rise up from them purified and brightened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्रप्सश्चस्कंद प्रथमाँ अनु द्यूनिमं च योनिमनु यश्च पूर्वः ।समानं योनिमनु संचरंतं द्रप्सं जुहोम्यनु सप्त होत्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: drapsáḥ ǀ caskanda ǀ prathamā́n ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ imám ǀ ca ǀ yónim ǀ ánu ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀsamānám ǀ yónim ǀ ánu ǀ sam-cárantam ǀ drapsám ǀ juhomi ǀ ánu ǀ saptá ǀ hótrāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through days of earliest date the Drop descended on this place and on that which was before it. I offer up, throughout the seven oblations, the Drop which still to one same place is moving.
verses.wilson_translation: The Somahas risen to the earthly and heavenly (worlds), both this visible world, and that which(existed) before (it); I offer that Soma flowing through the common region (of heaven and earth) after the sacrifice(offered by the) seven (officiating priests).
verses.griffith_verse: Through days of earliest date the Drop descended on this place and on that which was before it. I offer up, throughout the seven oblations, the Drop which still to one same place is moving.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते द्रप्सः स्कंदति यस्ते अंशुर्बाहुच्युतो धिषणाया उपस्थात् ।अध्वर्योर्वा परि वा यः पवित्रात्तं ते जुहोमि मनसा वषट्कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ drapsáḥ ǀ skándati ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ aṃśúḥ ǀ bāhú-cyutaḥ ǀ dhiṣáṇāyāḥ ǀ upá-sthāt ǀadhvaryóḥ ǀ vā ǀ pári ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ pavítrāt ǀ tám ǀ te ǀ juhomi ǀ mánasā ǀ váṣaṭ-kṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Drop that falls, thy stalk which arms have shaken, which from the bosom of the press hath fallen, Or from the Adhvaryu's purifying filter, I offer thee with heart and cry of Vaṣaṭ!
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, which escapes (from the hide), your filaments which let fall from thehands(of the priestescape) from the vicinity of the plural nks (of the press), or (from thehand) of the Adhvaryu, or from the filter; I offer itall with my mind (to Agni) with the word vaṣat.
verses.griffith_verse: The Drop that falls, thy stalk which arms have shaken, which from the bosom of the press hath fallen, Or from the Adhvaryu's purifying filter, I offer thee with heart and cry of Vaṣaṭ!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते द्रप्सः स्कन्नो यस्ते अंशुरवश्च यः परः स्रुचा ।अयं देवो बृहस्पतिः सं तं सिंचतु राधसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ drapsáḥ ǀ skannáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ aṃśúḥ ǀ aváḥ ǀ ca ǀ yáḥ ǀ paráḥ ǀ srucā́ ǀayám ǀ deváḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sám ǀ tám ǀ siñcatu ǀ rā́dhase ǁ
verses.english_translation: That fallen Drop of thine, the stalk which from the ladle fell away, This present God Bṛhaspati shall pour it forth to make us rich.
verses.wilson_translation: Your juice and your filaments, (Soma), which escape, and which fall from the ladle on this side or onthat; may this divine Bṛhaspatisprinkle it for our enrichment.
verses.griffith_verse: That fallen Drop of thine, the stalk which from the ladle fell away, This present God Bṛhaspati shall pour it forth to make us rich.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पयस्वतीरोषधयः पयस्वन्मामकं वचः ।अपां पयस्वदित्पयस्तेन मा सह शुंधत ॥
verses.transliteration: páyasvatīḥ ǀ óṣadhayaḥ ǀ páyasvat ǀ māmakám ǀ vácaḥ ǀapā́m ǀ páyasvat ǀ ít ǀ páyaḥ ǀ téna ǀ mā ǀ sahá ǀ śundhata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The plants of earth are rich in milk, and rich in milk is this my speech; And rich in milk the essence of the Waters: make me pure therewith.
verses.wilson_translation: (Waters)! the plural nts flourish by means of water my prayer is effectual through water; the essence ofwater is vigorous through water; purify me with it.
verses.griffith_verse: The plants of earth are rich in milk, and rich in milk is this my speech; And rich in milk the essence of the Waters: make me pure therewith.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XVIII. Various Deities.
hymns.anukramani: १४ संकुसुको यामायनः। १-४ मृत्युः,५ धाता, ६ त्वष्टा,७-१४ पितृमेधः,१४ प्रजापतिर्वा। त्रिष्टुप् , ११ प्रस्तारपंक्तिः, १३ जगती १४ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel.To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes. As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence,May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing. Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful.We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, tofurther times prolonging our existence. Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit.May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain. As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons,As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer. Live your full lives ap! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other.May Tvaṣṭar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence. Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent.Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth. Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest.Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover. From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory.There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o’ercome all hosts that fight against us. Betake thee to the Iap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious.Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdongiver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom. Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him.Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth. Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,—let a thousand clods remain above him.Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge. I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury.Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place. Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day.The fit word have I caught and held as ’twere a courser with the rein.

verses.sanskrit: परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पंथां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् ।चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान् ॥
verses.transliteration: páram ǀ mṛtyo íti ǀ ánu ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ pánthām ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ sváḥ ǀ ítaraḥ ǀ deva-yā́nāt ǀcákṣuṣmate ǀ śṛṇvaté ǀ te ǀ bravīmi ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ ririṣaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ utá ǀ vīrā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel. To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Depart,Mṛtyu, by a different path; by that which is your own, and distinct from the path of the gods; Ispeak to you who have eyes, who have ears; do no harm to our offspring, nor to ourmaleprogeny.
verses.griffith_verse: Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel. To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मृत्योः पदं योपयंतो यदैत द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ।आप्यायमानाः प्रजया धनेन शुद्धाः पूता भवत यज्ञियासः ॥
verses.transliteration: mṛtyóḥ ǀ padám ǀ yopáyantaḥ ǀ yát ǀ áita ǀ drā́ghīyaḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀāpyā́yamānāḥ ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ dhánena ǀ śuddhā́ḥ ǀ pūtā́ḥ ǀ bhavata ǀ yajñiyāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence, May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing.
verses.wilson_translation: If, avoiding the path of death, you go (on the path of he gods), assuming a longer and better life, (myfriends), then may you, (O sacrificers), diligent in sacrifice, enriched with progeny and affluence, be cleansed andpure.
verses.griffith_verse: As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence, May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमे जीवा वि मृतैराववृत्रन्नभूद्भद्रा देवहूतिर्नो अद्य ।प्रांचो अगाम नृतये हसाय द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ jīvā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ mṛtáiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ avavṛtran ǀ ábhūt ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ devá-hūtiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀprā́ñcaḥ ǀ agāma ǀ nṛtáye ǀ hásāya ǀ drā́ghīyaḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful. We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, tofurther times prolonging our existence.
verses.wilson_translation: May those who are living remain separate from the dead; may our invocation of the gods today besuccessful; let us go forward to dancing and laughter, assuming a longer and better life.
verses.griffith_verse: Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful. We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, tofurther times prolonging our existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि मैषां नु गादपरो अर्थमेतं ।शतं जीवंतु शरदः पुरूचीरंतर्मृत्युं दधतां पर्वतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ jīvébhyaḥ ǀ pari-dhím ǀ dadhāmi ǀ mā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ nú ǀ gāt ǀ áparaḥ ǀ ártham ǀ etám ǀśatám ǀ jīvantu ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ purūcī́ḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ mṛtyúm ǀ dadhatām ǀ párvatena ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit. May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain.
verses.wilson_translation: I erect this circle (of stones) for (the protection of) the living, that none other of them may approach thislimit; may they live a hundred years, occupied by many holy works, and keep death hidden by this mound.
verses.griffith_verse: Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit. May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथाहान्यनुपूर्वं भवंति यथ ऋतव ऋतुभिर्यंति साधु ।यथा न पूर्वमपरो जहात्येवा धातरायूंषि कल्पयैषां ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ áhāni ǀ anu-pūrvám ǀ bhávanti ǀ yáthā ǀ ṛtávaḥ ǀ ṛtú-bhiḥ ǀ yánti ǀ sādhú ǀyáthā ǀ ná ǀ pū́rvam ǀ áparaḥ ǀ jáhāti ǀ evá ǀ dhātaḥ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ kalpaya ǀ eṣā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
verses.wilson_translation: As days pass along in succession; as season are duly followed by seasons; as the successor doesnot abandon his predecessor, so,Dhātā, support the lives of these (my kinsmen).
verses.griffith_verse: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ रोहतायुर्जरसं वृणाना अनुपूर्वं यतमाना यति ष्ठ ।इह त्वष्टा सुजनिमा सजोषा दीर्घमायुः करति जीवसे वः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ rohata ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ jarásam ǀ vṛṇānā́ḥ ǀ anu-pūrvám ǀ yátamānāḥ ǀ yáti ǀ sthá ǀihá ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ su-jánimā ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ karati ǀ jīváse ǀ vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Live your full lives ap! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other. May Tvaṣṭar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence.
verses.wilson_translation: (You kinsmen of the dead man), choosing old age, attain length of life, striving one after the other, howmany soever you may be; may Tvaṣṭā, the creator.
verses.griffith_verse: Live your full lives ap! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other. May Tvaṣṭar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमा नारीरविधवाः सुपत्नीरांजनेन सर्पिषा सं विशंतु ।अनश्रवोऽनमीवाः सुरत्ना आ रोहंतु जनयो योनिमग्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ nā́rīḥ ǀ avidhavā́ḥ ǀ su-pátnīḥ ǀ ā-áñjanena ǀ sarpíṣā ǀ sám ǀ viśantu ǀanaśrávaḥ ǀ anamīvā́ḥ ǀ su-rátnāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ rohantu ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ yónim ǀ ágre ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent. Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth.
verses.wilson_translation: Let these women who are not widows, who have good husbands, enter (anointed) with unguent andbutter. Let women without tears, without sorrow, and decorated with jewels, first proceed to the house.
verses.griffith_verse: Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent. Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीर्ष्व नार्यभि जीवलोकं गतासुमेतमुप शेष एहि ।हस्तग्राभस्य दिधिषोस्तवेदं पत्युर्जनित्वमभि सं बभूथ ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrṣva ǀ nāri ǀ abhí ǀ jīva-lokám ǀ gatá-asum ǀ etám ǀ úpa ǀ śeṣe ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀhasta-grābhásya ǀ didhiṣóḥ ǀ táva ǀ idám ǀ pátyuḥ ǀ jani-tvám ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ babhūtha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest. Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise, woman, (and go) to the world of living beings; come, this man near whom you sleep is lifeless;you have enjoyed this state of being the wife of your husband, the suitor who took you by the band.
verses.griffith_verse: Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest. Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मृतस्यास्मे क्षत्राय वर्चसे बलाय ।अत्रैव त्वमिह वयं सुवीरा विश्वाः स्पृधो अभिमातीर्जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: dhánuḥ ǀ hástāt ǀ ā-dádānaḥ ǀ mṛtásya ǀ asmé íti ǀ kṣatrā́ya ǀ várcase ǀ bálāya ǀátra ǀ evá ǀ tvám ǀ ihá ǀ vayám ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ abhí-mātīḥ ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory. There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o’ercome all hosts that fight against us.
verses.wilson_translation: Taking his bow from thehandof the dead man, for the sake of our vigour, energy and strength, (I say)you are there; may we (who are) here, blessed withmaleoffspring, overcome all the enemies who assail us.
verses.griffith_verse: From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory. There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o’ercome all hosts that fight against us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पृथिवीं सुशेवां ।ऊर्णम्रदा युवतिर्दक्षिणावत एषा त्वा पातु निर्ऋतेरुपस्थात् ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ sarpa ǀ mātáram ǀ bhū́mim ǀ etā́m ǀ uru-vyácasam ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ su-śévām ǀū́rṇa-mradāḥ ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā-vate ǀ eṣā́ ǀ tvā ǀ pātu ǀ níḥ-ṛteḥ ǀ upá-sthāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Betake thee to the Iap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious. Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdongiver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom.
verses.wilson_translation: Go to this your mother-earth, the wide-spread, delightful earth; this virgin (earth is) as soft aswool, tothe liberal (worshipper) may she protect you from the proximity of Nirṛti.
verses.griffith_verse: Betake thee to the Iap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious. Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdongiver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छ्वंचस्व पृथिवि मा नि बाधथाः सूपायनास्मै भव सूपवंचना ।माता पुत्रं यथा सिचाभ्येनं भूम ऊर्णुहि ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ śvañcasva ǀ pṛthivi ǀ mā́ ǀ ní ǀ bādhathāḥ ǀ su-upāyanā́ ǀ asmai ǀ bhava ǀ su-upavañcanā́ ǀmātā́ ǀ putrám ǀ yáthā ǀ sicā́ ǀ abhí ǀ enam ǀ bhūme ǀ ūrṇuhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him. Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Earth, rise up above him; oppress him not; be attentive to him (and) comfortable; cover him up, earth,as a mother covers her child with the skirt of her garment.
verses.griffith_verse: Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him. Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छ्वंचमाना पृथिवी सु तिष्ठतु सहस्रं मित उप हि श्रयंतां ।ते गृहासो घृतश्चुतो भवंतु विश्वाहास्मै शरणाः संत्वत्र ॥
verses.transliteration: ut-śváñcamānā ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ sú ǀ tiṣṭhatu ǀ sahásram ǀ mítaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ hí ǀ śráyantām ǀté ǀ gṛhā́saḥ ǀ ghṛta-ścútaḥ ǀ bhavantu ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ asmai ǀ śaraṇā́ḥ ǀ santu ǀ átra ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,—let a thousand clods remain above him. Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring them back again, render them obedient; may Indrarestor ethem; may Agnibring them near.
verses.griffith_verse: Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,—let a thousand clods remain above him. Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्ते स्तभ्नामि पृथिवीं त्वत्परीमं लोगं निदधन्मो अहं रिषं ।एतां स्थूणां पितरो धारयंतु तेऽत्रा यमः सादना ते मिनोतु ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ te ǀ stabhnāmi ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ tvát ǀ pári ǀ imám ǀ logám ǀ ni-dádhat ǀ mó íti ǀ ahám ǀ riṣam ǀetā́m ǀ sthū́ṇām ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ dhārayantu ǀ te ǀ átra ǀ yamáḥ ǀ sádanā ǀ te ǀ minotu ǁ
verses.english_translation: I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury. Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place.
verses.wilson_translation: May they come back to me and be fostered under this (their) protector; do you Agni, keep them here;may whatever wealth (there is) remain here.
verses.griffith_verse: I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury. Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
