verses.sanskrit: प्रतीचीने मामहनीष्वाः पर्णमिवा दधुः ।प्रतीचीं जग्रभा वाचमश्वं रशनया यथा ॥
verses.transliteration: pratīcī́ne ǀ mā́m ǀ áhani ǀ íṣvāḥ ǀ parṇám-iva ǀ ā́ ǀ dadhuḥ ǀpratī́cīm ǀ jagrabha ǀ vā́cam ǀ áśvam ǀ raśanáyā ǀ yathā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day. The fit word have I caught and held as ’twere a courser with the rein.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the knowledge of the plural ce, of their going, of their coming, of their departure, of theirwandering, of their returning; (I invoke) him who is their keeper.
verses.griffith_verse: Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day. The fit word have I caught and held as ’twere a courser with the rein.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XIX. Waters or Cows.
hymns.anukramani: ८ मथितो यामायनः भृगुर्वारुणिर्वा, भार्गवश्च्यवनो वा। आपः गावो वा, १ उत्तरार्धर्चस्य अग्नीषोमौ। अनुष्टुप्, ६ गायत्री ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . TURN, go not farther on your way: visit us, O ye Wealthy Ones.Agni and Soma, ye who bring riches again, secure us wealth. Make these return to us again, bring them beside us once again.May. Indra give them back to us, and Agni drive them hither-ward. Let them return to us again: under this herdsman let them feed.Do thou, O Agni, keep them here, and let the wealth we have remain. call upon their herdsman, him who knoweth well their coming nigh,Their parting and their home-return, and watcheth their approach and rest. Yea, let the herdsman, too, return, who marketh well their driving-forth;Marketh their wandering away, their turning back and coming home. Home-leader, lead them home to us; Indra, restore to us our kine:We will rejoice in them alive. offer you on every side butter and milk and strengthening food.May all the Holy Deities pour down on us a flood of wealth. O thou Home-leader, lead them home, restore them thou who bringest home.Four are the quarters of the earth; from these bring back to us our kine,

verses.sanskrit: नि वर्तध्वं मानु गातास्मान्त्सिषक्त रेवतीः ।अग्नीषोमा पुनर्वसू अस्मे धारयतं रयिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ vartadhvam ǀ mā́ ǀ ánu ǀ gāta ǀ asmā́n ǀ sisakta ǀ revatīḥ ǀágnīṣomā ǀ punarvasū íti punaḥ-vasū ǀ asmé íti ǀ dhārayatam ǀ rayím ǁ
verses.english_translation: TURN, go not farther on your way: visit us, O ye Wealthy Ones. Agni and Soma, ye who bring riches again, secure us wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Come back; go not elsewhere; abounding in wealth, sprinkle us;Agniand Soma, you who clothe (yourworshippers) again, bestow upon us riches.
verses.griffith_verse: TURN, go not farther on your way: visit us, O ye Wealthy Ones. Agni and Soma, ye who bring riches again, secure us wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनरेना नि वर्तय पुनरेना न्या कुरु ।इंद्र एणा नि यच्छत्वग्निरेना उपाजतु ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ enāḥ ǀ ní ǀ vartaya ǀ púnaḥ ǀ enāḥ ǀ ní ǀ ā́ ǀ kuru ǀíndraḥ ǀ enāḥ ǀ ní ǀ yacchatu ǀ agníḥ ǀ enāḥ ǀ upa-ā́jatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make these return to us again, bring them beside us once again. May. Indra give them back to us, and Agni drive them hither-ward.
verses.griffith_verse: Make these return to us again, bring them beside us once again. May. Indra give them back to us, and Agni drive them hither-ward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनरेता नि वर्तंतामस्मिन्पुष्यंतु गोपतौ ।इहैवाग्ने नि धारयेह तिष्ठतु या रयिः ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ etā́ḥ ǀ ní ǀ vartantām ǀ asmín ǀ puṣyantu ǀ gó-patau ǀihá ǀ evá ǀ agne ǀ ní ǀ dhāraya ǀ ihá ǀ tiṣṭhatu ǀ yā́ ǀ rayíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let them return to us again: under this herdsman let them feed. Do thou, O Agni, keep them here, and let the wealth we have remain.
verses.griffith_verse: Let them return to us again: under this herdsman let them feed. Do thou, O Agni, keep them here, and let the wealth we have remain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यन्नियानं न्ययनं संज्ञानं यत्परायणं ।आवर्तनं निवर्तनं यो गोपा अपि तं हुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ni-yā́nam ǀ ni-áyanam ǀ sam-jñā́nam ǀ yát ǀ parā-áyanam ǀā-vártanam ǀ ni-vártanam ǀ yáḥ ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ápi ǀ tám ǀ huve ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 call upon their herdsman, him who knoweth well their coming nigh, Their parting and their home-return, and watcheth their approach and rest.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 call upon their herdsman, him who knoweth well their coming nigh, Their parting and their home-return, and watcheth their approach and rest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य उदानड्व्ययनं य उदानट् परायणं ।आवर्तनं निवर्तनमपि गोपा नि वर्ततां ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ut-ā́naṭ ǀ vi-áyanam ǀ yáḥ ǀ ut-ā́naṭ ǀ parā-áyanam ǀā-vártanam ǀ ni-vártanam ǀ ápi ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ní ǀ vartatām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, let the herdsman, too, return, who marketh well their driving-forth; Marketh their wandering away, their turning back and coming home.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, let the herdsman, too, return, who marketh well their driving-forth; Marketh their wandering away, their turning back and coming home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ निवर्त नि वर्तय पुनर्न इंद्र गा देहि ।जीवाभिर्भुनजामहै ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ni-varta ǀ ní ǀ vartaya ǀ púnaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ dehi ǀjīvā́bhiḥ ǀ bhunajāmahai ǁ
verses.english_translation: Home-leader, lead them home to us; Indra, restore to us our kine: We will rejoice in them alive.
verses.griffith_verse: Home-leader, lead them home to us; Indra, restore to us our kine: We will rejoice in them alive.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परि वो विश्वतो दध ऊर्जा घृतेन पयसा ।ये देवाः के च यज्ञियास्ते रय्या सं सृजंतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ vaḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ ghṛténa ǀ páyasā ǀyé ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ké ǀ ca ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ té ǀ rayyā́ ǀ sám ǀ sṛjantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 offer you on every side butter and milk and strengthening food. May all the Holy Deities pour down on us a flood of wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 offer you on every side butter and milk and strengthening food. May all the Holy Deities pour down on us a flood of wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ निवर्तन वर्तय नि निवर्तन वर्तय ।भूम्याश्चतस्रः प्रदिशस्ताभ्य एना नि वर्तय ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ni-vartana ǀ vartaya ǀ ní ǀ ni-vartana ǀ vartaya ǀbhū́myāḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ tā́bhyaḥ ǀ enāḥ ǀ ní ǀ vartaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: O thou Home-leader, lead them home, restore them thou who bringest home. Four are the quarters of the earth; from these bring back to us our kine,
verses.griffith_verse: O thou Home-leader, lead them home, restore them thou who bringest home. Four are the quarters of the earth; from these bring back to us our kine,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १० ऐन्द्रो विमदः प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा। अग्निः। गायत्री, १ एकपदा विराट् (एष मन्त्र: शान्त्यर्थः) २अनुष्टुप्,९ विराट् १० त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SEND unto us a good and happy mind. worship Agni, Youthfullest of Gods, resistless, Friend of laws;Under whose guard and heavenly light the Spotted seek the Mother's breast: Whom with their mouth they magnify, bannered with flame and homed in light.He glitters with his row of teeth. Kind, Furtherer of men, he comes, when he hath reached the ends of heaven,Sage, giving splendour to the clouds. To taste man's offerings, he, the Strong, hath risen erect at sacrifice:Fixing his dwelling he proceeds. Here are oblation, worship, rest: rapidly comes his furtherance.To sword-armed Agni come the Gods. With service for chief bliss I seek the Lord of Sacrifice, Agni, whomThey call the Living, Son of Cloud. Blest evermore be all the men who come from us, who magnifyAgni with sacrificial gifts. The path he treads is black and white and red, and striped, and brown, crimson, and glorious.His sire begat him bright with hues of gold. Thus with his thoughts, O Son of Strength, O Agni, hath Vimada, accordant with the Immortals,Offered thee hymns, soliciting thy favour. Thou hast brought all food, strength, a prosperous dwelling.

verses.sanskrit: भद्रं नो अपि वातय मनः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ naḥ ǀ ápi ǀ vātaya ǀ mánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SEND unto us a good and happy mind.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agni), manifest towards us a favourable mind.
verses.griffith_verse: SEND unto us a good and happy mind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निमीळे भुजां यविष्ठं शासा मित्रं दुर्धरीतुं ।यस्य धर्मन्त्स्वरेनीः सपर्यंति मातुरूधः ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ īḷe ǀ bhujā́m ǀ yáviṣṭham ǀ śāsā́ ǀ mitrám ǀ duḥ-dhárītum ǀyásya ǀ dhárman ǀ sváḥ ǀ énīḥ ǀ saparyánti ǀ mātúḥ ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1 worship Agni, Youthfullest of Gods, resistless, Friend of laws; Under whose guard and heavenly light the Spotted seek the Mother's breast:
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify Agni, the youngest of the feeders (on oblations), friendly in counsel, difficult to resist, at whoserite the oblations seek heaven, as (calves) the udder of the mother cow.
verses.griffith_verse: 1 worship Agni, Youthfullest of Gods, resistless, Friend of laws; Under whose guard and heavenly light the Spotted seek the Mother's breast:
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमासा कृपनीळं भासाकेतुं वर्धयंति ।भ्राजते श्रेणिदन् ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ āsā́ ǀ kṛpá-nīḷam ǀ bhāsā́-ketum ǀ vardháyanti ǀbhrā́jate ǀ śréṇi-dan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whom with their mouth they magnify, bannered with flame and homed in light. He glitters with his row of teeth.
verses.wilson_translation: He whom (the worshippers) magnify with their mouth, the sustainer of pious works; whose banner isthe light, he shines, bestowing upon them all their desires.
verses.griffith_verse: Whom with their mouth they magnify, bannered with flame and homed in light. He glitters with his row of teeth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्यो विशां गातुरेति प्र यदानड्दिवो अंतान् ।कविरभ्रं दीद्यानः ॥
verses.transliteration: aryáḥ ǀ viśā́m ǀ gātúḥ ǀ eti ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ántān ǀkavíḥ ǀ abhrám ǀ dī́dyānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Kind, Furtherer of men, he comes, when he hath reached the ends of heaven, Sage, giving splendour to the clouds.
verses.wilson_translation: The refuge of the people, the mover, who, when he moves, penetrates to the ends of the sky; thesage illumining the firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: Kind, Furtherer of men, he comes, when he hath reached the ends of heaven, Sage, giving splendour to the clouds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जुषद्धव्या मानुषस्योर्ध्वस्तस्थावृभ्वा यज्ञे ।मिन्वन्त्सद्म पुर एति ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣát ǀ havyā́ ǀ mā́nuṣasya ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ tasthau ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀ yajñé ǀminván ǀ sádma ǀ puráḥ ǀ eti ǁ
verses.english_translation: To taste man's offerings, he, the Strong, hath risen erect at sacrifice: Fixing his dwelling he proceeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Accepting the oblations (offered) at the sacrifice of the worshipper, he blazes up, with a mighty flame;fixing his abode, he advances.
verses.griffith_verse: To taste man's offerings, he, the Strong, hath risen erect at sacrifice: Fixing his dwelling he proceeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि क्षेमो हविर्यज्ञः श्रुष्टीदस्य गातुरेति ।अग्निं देवा वाशीमंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ kṣémaḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ śruṣṭī́ ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ gātúḥ ǀ eti ǀagním ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vā́śī-mantam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here are oblation, worship, rest: rapidly comes his furtherance. To sword-armed Agni come the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis capable (of protecting all men), he is himself the oblation, and the sacrifice; rapidly indeed doeshis spirit move, the gods come to Agni, who bears the praises.
verses.griffith_verse: Here are oblation, worship, rest: rapidly comes his furtherance. To sword-armed Agni come the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञासाहं दुव इषेऽग्निं पूर्वस्य शेवस्य ।अद्रेः सूनुमायुमाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yajña-sáham ǀ dúvaḥ ǀ iṣe ǀ agním ǀ pū́rvasya ǀ śévasya ǀádreḥ ǀ sūnúm ǀ āyúm ǀ āhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With service for chief bliss I seek the Lord of Sacrifice, Agni, whom They call the Living, Son of Cloud.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who goes to (summon the gods), the bearer of the oblation, whom men call the sow of the stone;him I desire to worship (for the sake) of supreme felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: With service for chief bliss I seek the Lord of Sacrifice, Agni, whom They call the Living, Son of Cloud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नरो ये के चास्मदा विश्वेत्ते वाम आ स्युः ।अग्निं हविषा वर्धंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: náraḥ ǀ yé ǀ ké ǀ ca ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ té ǀ vāmé ǀ ā́ ǀ syuríti syuḥ ǀagním ǀ havíṣā ǀ várdhantaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Blest evermore be all the men who come from us, who magnify Agni with sacrificial gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: May all the men who belong to us be (gratified) in all that is desirable, augmenting Agniwith oblationṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Blest evermore be all the men who come from us, who magnify Agni with sacrificial gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णः श्वेतोऽरुषो यामो अस्य ब्रध्न ऋज्र उत शोणो यशस्वान् ।हिरण्यरूपं जनिता जजान ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇáḥ ǀ śvetáḥ ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ yā́maḥ ǀ asya ǀ bradhnáḥ ǀ ṛjráḥ ǀ utá ǀ śóṇaḥ ǀ yáśasvān ǀhíraṇya-rūpam ǀ jánitā ǀ jajāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: The path he treads is black and white and red, and striped, and brown, crimson, and glorious. His sire begat him bright with hues of gold.
verses.wilson_translation: His chariot is black, white, red, tawny, dark red, crimson, and glorious; the progenitor of all has givenhim a chariot of gold.
verses.griffith_verse: The path he treads is black and white and red, and striped, and brown, crimson, and glorious. His sire begat him bright with hues of gold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा ते अग्ने विमदो मनीषामूर्जो नपादमृतेभिः सजोषाः ।गिर आ वक्षत्सुमतीरियान इषमूर्जं सुक्षितिं विश्वमाभाः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ vi-madáḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ ū́rjaḥ ǀ napāt ǀ amṛ́tebhiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀgíraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vakṣat ǀ su-matī́ḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ íṣam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ su-kṣitím ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ abhārítyabhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus with his thoughts, O Son of Strength, O Agni, hath Vimada, accordant with the Immortals, Offered thee hymns, soliciting thy favour. Thou hast brought all food, strength, a prosperous dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: Grandson of strength,Agni, who are gratified by the ambrosial (Viands),Vimada, (desirous of) wisdom,has recited your praises; do you, approaching with a kind intention, bestow upon us food, strength, and aprosperous abode.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus with his thoughts, O Son of Strength, O Agni, hath Vimada, accordant with the Immortals, Offered thee hymns, soliciting thy favour. Thou hast brought all food, strength, a prosperous dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXI. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ८ ऐन्द्रो विमदः, प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा। अग्निः। आस्तारपंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH offerings of our own we choose thee, Agni, as Invoking Priest,For sacrifice with trimmed grass,—at your glad carouse-piercing and brightly shining. Thou art waxing great. The wealthy ones adorn thee, they who bring us horses as their gift:The sprinkling ladle, Agni,—at your glad carouse -and glowing offering taste thee. Thou art waxing great. The holy statutes rest by thee, as ’twere with ladles that o’erflow.Black and white-gleaming colours,—at your glad carouse-all glories thou assurnest. Thou art waxing great. O Agni, what thou deemest wealth, Victorious and Immortal One!Bring thou to give us vigour,—at your glad carouse -splendid at sacrifices. Thou art waxing great. Skilled in all lore is Agni, he whom erst Atharvan brought to life.He was Vivasvān's envoy, at your glad carouse-the weIl-loved friend of Yama, Thou art waxing great. At sacrifices they adore thee, Agni, when the rite proceeds.All fair and lovely treasures-at your glad carouse-thou givest him who offers. Thou art waxing great. Men, Agni, have established thee as welcome Priest at holy rites,Thee whose face shines with butter,—at your glad carouse-bright, with eyes most observant. Thou art waxing great. Wide and aloft thou spreadest thee, O Agni, with thy brilliant flame.A Bull art thou when bellowing,—at your glad carouse-thou dost impregn the Sisters. Thou art waxing great.

verses.sanskrit: आग्निं न स्ववृक्तिभिर्होतारं त्वा वृणीमहे ।यज्ञाय स्तीर्णबर्हिषे वि वो मदे शीरं पावकशोचिषं विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ agním ǀ ná ǀ svávṛkti-bhiḥ ǀ hótāram ǀ tvā ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀyajñā́ya ǀ stīrṇá-barhiṣe ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ śīrám ǀ pāvaká-śociṣam ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH offerings of our own we choose thee, Agni, as Invoking Priest, For sacrifice with trimmed grass,—at your glad carouse-piercing and brightly shining. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke you now,Agni, invoker (of the gods), with our voluntary (praises) for the sacrifice, at whichthe sacred grass is spread; you, who underlying (all things), who (diffuses) purifying radiance, (we invoke) foryour exhilaration; you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH offerings of our own we choose thee, Agni, as Invoking Priest, For sacrifice with trimmed grass,—at your glad carouse-piercing and brightly shining. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामु ते स्वाभुवः शुंभंत्यश्वराधसः ।वेति त्वामुपसेचनी वि वो मद ऋजीतिरग्न आहुतिर्विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ té ǀ su-ābhúvaḥ ǀ śumbhánti ǀ áśva-rādhasaḥ ǀvéti ǀ tvā́m ǀ upa-sécanī ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ ṛ́jītiḥ ǀ agne ǀ ā́-hutiḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wealthy ones adorn thee, they who bring us horses as their gift: The sprinkling ladle, Agni,—at your glad carouse -and glowing offering taste thee. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Self-radiant, opulent in horses, they glorify you; the oblation poured out over (you) proceeds in astraight course,Agni, to you for your exhilaration; you are mighy.
verses.griffith_verse: The wealthy ones adorn thee, they who bring us horses as their gift: The sprinkling ladle, Agni,—at your glad carouse -and glowing offering taste thee. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे धर्माण आसते जुहूभिः सिंचतीरिव ।कृष्णा रूपाण्यर्जुना वि वो मदे विश्वा अधि श्रियो धिषे विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ dharmā́ṇaḥ ǀ āsate ǀ juhū́bhiḥ ǀ siñcatī́ḥ-iva ǀkṛṣṇā́ ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ árjunā ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ dhiṣe ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: The holy statutes rest by thee, as ’twere with ladles that o’erflow. Black and white-gleaming colours,—at your glad carouse-all glories thou assurnest. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: The establishers (of the rite) worship you with their ladles (filled with the oblation), like (earth)sprinkling (showers); you sustain exceedingly black forms and white and all beauties for your exhilaration; youare mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: The holy statutes rest by thee, as ’twere with ladles that o’erflow. Black and white-gleaming colours,—at your glad carouse-all glories thou assurnest. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमग्ने मन्यसे रयिं सहसावन्नमर्त्य ।तमा नो वाजसातये वि वो मदे यज्ञेषु चित्रमा भरा विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ agne ǀ mányase ǀ rayím ǀ sáhasā-van ǀ amartya ǀtám ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀ ví ǀ va��� ǀ máde ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ citrám ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, what thou deemest wealth, Victorious and Immortal One! Bring thou to give us vigour,—at your glad carouse -splendid at sacrifices. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful and immortal Agni, bring to us, for our sustenance, the precious wealth which you think best;(bring it) for your exhilaration at the sacrifices; you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, what thou deemest wealth, Victorious and Immortal One! Bring thou to give us vigour,—at your glad carouse -splendid at sacrifices. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्जातो अथर्वणा विदद्विश्वानि काव्या ।भुवद्दूतो विवस्वतो वि वो मदे प्रियो यमस्य काम्यो विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ átharvaṇā ǀ vidát ǀ víśvāni ǀ kā́vyā ǀbhúvat ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ priyáḥ ǀ yamásya ǀ kā́myaḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Skilled in all lore is Agni, he whom erst Atharvan brought to life. He was Vivasvān's envoy, at your glad carouse-the weIl-loved friend of Yama, Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, genitive rated by Atharvan, is cognizant of all praises; he is the messenger of Vivasvat, the belovedfriend of Yama, for your exhilaration; you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Skilled in all lore is Agni, he whom erst Atharvan brought to life. He was Vivasvān's envoy, at your glad carouse-the weIl-loved friend of Yama, Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां यज्ञेष्वीळतेऽग्ने प्रयत्यध्वरे ।त्वं वसूनि काम्या वि वो मदे विश्वा दधासि दाशुषे विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ īḷate ǀ ágne ǀ pra-yatí ǀ adhvaré ǀtvám ǀ vásūni ǀ kā́myā ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ víśvā ǀ dadhāsi ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: At sacrifices they adore thee, Agni, when the rite proceeds. All fair and lovely treasures-at your glad carouse-thou givest him who offers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: The men establish you,Agni, at sacrifices, the ministrant priest, graceful, whose face shines withbutter, radiant, most intelligent with your eyes, for your exhilaration; (hence) you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: At sacrifices they adore thee, Agni, when the rite proceeds. All fair and lovely treasures-at your glad carouse-thou givest him who offers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां यज्ञेष्वृत्विजं चारुमग्ने नि षेदिरे ।घृतप्रतीकं मनुषो वि वो मदे शुक्रं चेतिष्ठमक्षभिर्विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ ṛtvíjam ǀ cā́rum ǀ agne ǀ ní ǀ sedire ǀghṛtá-pratīkam ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ śukrám ǀ cétiṣṭham ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men, Agni, have established thee as welcome Priest at holy rites, Thee whose face shines with butter,—at your glad carouse-bright, with eyes most observant. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, you, the mighty one, are known far and wide by your radiant lustre; bellowing, you rush like abull, you impregnate the sister (plural nts) in your exhilaration; you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Men, Agni, have established thee as welcome Priest at holy rites, Thee whose face shines with butter,—at your glad carouse-bright, with eyes most observant. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने शुक्रेण शोचिषोरु प्रथयसे बृहत् ।अभिक्रंदन्वृषायसे वि वो मदे गर्भं दधासि जामिषु विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀ urú ǀ prathayase ǀ bṛhát ǀabhi-krándan ǀ vṛṣa-yase ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ gárbham ǀ dadhāsi ǀ jāmíṣu ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wide and aloft thou spreadest thee, O Agni, with thy brilliant flame. A Bull art thou when bellowing,—at your glad carouse-thou dost impregn the Sisters. Thou art waxing great.
verses.griffith_verse: Wide and aloft thou spreadest thee, O Agni, with thy brilliant flame. A Bull art thou when bellowing,—at your glad carouse-thou dost impregn the Sisters. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १५ ऐन्द्रो विमदः प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा। इन्द्रः। पुरस्ताद्बृहती ५,७,९ अनुष्टुप्, १५ त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHERE is famed Indra heard of? With what folk is he renowned to-day as Mitra is,—Who in the home of Ṛṣis and in secret is extolled with song? Even here is Indra famed, and among us this day the glorious Thunderer is praised,He who like Mitra mid the folk hath won complete and full renown. He who is Sovran Lord of great and perfect strength, exerter of heroic might,Who bears the fearless thunder as a father bears his darling son. Harnessing to thy car, as God, two blustering Steeds Of the Wind-God, O Thunderer,That speed along the shining path, thou making ways art glorified. Even to these dark Steeds of Wind thou of thyself hast come to ride,Of which no driver may be found, none, be he God or mortal man. When ye approach, men ask you, thee and Uśanā: Why come ye to our dwelling-place?Why are ye come to mortal man from distant realms of eapth and heaven? O Indra, thou shalt speak us fair: our holy prayer is offered up.We pray to thee for help as thou didst strike the monster Śuṣṇa dead. Around us is the Dasyu, riteless, void of sense, inhuman, keeping alien laws.Baffle, thou Slayer of the foe, the weapon which this Dāsa wields. Hero with Heroes, thou art ours: yea, strong are they whom thou dost help.In many a place are thy full gifts, and men, like vassals, sing thy praise. Urge thou these heroes on to slay the enemy, brave Thunderer! in the fight with swords.Even when hid among the tribes of Sages numerous as stars. Swift come those gifts of thine whose hand is prompt to rend and burn, O Hero Thunder-armed:As thou with thy Companions didst destroy the whole of SuSnia's brood. Let not thine excellent assistance come to us, O Hero Indra, profitless.May we, may we enjoy the bliss of these thy favours, Thunderer! May those soft impulses of thine, O Indra, be fruitful and innocent to us.May we know these whose treasures are like those of milch-kine, Thunderer! That Earth, through power of knowing things that may be known, handless and footless yet might thrive,Thou slewest, turning to the right, gu;na for every living man. Drink, drink the Soma, Hero Indra; be not withheld as thou art good, O Treasure-giver.Preserve the singers and our liberal princes, and make us wealthy with abundant riches.

verses.sanskrit: कुह श्रुत इंद्रः कस्मिन्नद्य जने मित्रो न श्रूयते ।ऋषीणां वा यः क्षये गुहा वा चर्कृषे गिरा ॥
verses.transliteration: kúha ǀ śrutáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ kásmin ǀ adyá ǀ jáne ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ śrūyate ǀṛ́ṣīṇām ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ kṣáye ǀ gúhā ǀ vā ǀ cárkṛṣe ǀ girā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHERE is famed Indra heard of? With what folk is he renowned to-day as Mitra is,— Who in the home of Ṛṣis and in secret is extolled with song?
verses.wilson_translation: In what plural ce today is Indrarenowned? In what nation is he famed like Mitra? (Indra), who isworshipper; or in secret = or, in the forest].
verses.griffith_verse: WHERE is famed Indra heard of? With what folk is he renowned to-day as Mitra is,— Who in the home of Ṛṣis and in secret is extolled with song?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इह श्रुत इंद्रो अस्मे अद्य स्तवे वज्र्यृचीषमः ।मित्रो न यो जनेष्वा यशश्चक्रे असाम्या ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ śrutáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ adyá ǀ stáve ǀ vajrī́ ǀ ṛ́cīṣamaḥ ǀmitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ jáneṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ yáśaḥ ǀ cakré ǀ ásāmi ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even here is Indra famed, and among us this day the glorious Thunderer is praised, He who like Mitra mid the folk hath won complete and full renown.
verses.wilson_translation: Here is Indrarenowned; today he is praised by us, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the deserving ofpraise; he who, like Mitra, bestows upon men unequalled abundance.
verses.griffith_verse: Even here is Indra famed, and among us this day the glorious Thunderer is praised, He who like Mitra mid the folk hath won complete and full renown.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महो यस्पतिः शवसो असाम्या महो नृम्णस्य तूतुजिः ।भर्ता वज्रस्य धृष्णोः पिता पुत्रमिव प्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ásāmi ǀ ā́ ǀ maháḥ ǀ nṛmṇásya ǀ tūtujíḥ ǀbhartā́ ǀ vájrasya ǀ dhṛṣṇóḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ putrám-iva ǀ priyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who is Sovran Lord of great and perfect strength, exerter of heroic might, Who bears the fearless thunder as a father bears his darling son.
verses.wilson_translation: (May Indraprotect us) who is the lord of great strenght, of unequalled (power), the distributor of greatwealth, the cherisher of the dreadful thunderbolt as a father (cherishes) a dear son.
verses.griffith_verse: He who is Sovran Lord of great and perfect strength, exerter of heroic might, Who bears the fearless thunder as a father bears his darling son.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युजानो अश्वा वातस्य धुनी देवो देवस्य वज्रिवः ।स्यंता पथा विरुक्मता सृजानः स्तोष्यध्वनः ॥
verses.transliteration: yujānáḥ ǀ áśvā ǀ vā́tasya ǀ dhúnī íti ǀ deváḥ ǀ devásya ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀsyántā ǀ pathā́ ǀ virúkmatā ǀ sṛjānáḥ ǀ stoṣi ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Harnessing to thy car, as God, two blustering Steeds Of the Wind-God, O Thunderer, That speed along the shining path, thou making ways art glorified.
verses.wilson_translation: Thunderer, you who are divine, yoking your horses which are swifter than the divine wind, and glidingalong the resplendent road, you, opening out the way (to battle), are glorified.
verses.griffith_verse: Harnessing to thy car, as God, two blustering Steeds Of the Wind-God, O Thunderer, That speed along the shining path, thou making ways art glorified.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्या चिद्वातस्याश्वागा ऋज्रा त्मना वहध्यै ।ययोर्देवो न मर्त्यो यंता नकिर्विदाय्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyā́ ǀ cit ǀ vā́tasya ǀ áśvā ǀ ā́ ǀ agāḥ ǀ ṛjrā́ ǀ tmánā ǀ váhadhyai ǀyáyoḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ ná ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ yantā́ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ vidā́yyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even to these dark Steeds of Wind thou of thyself hast come to ride, Of which no driver may be found, none, be he God or mortal man.
verses.wilson_translation: You have come to these two horses (which have the speed) of the wind, straight-going, for them todraw you of themselves, whom no deity, no mortal is able to restrain; whose fleetness no one comprehends.
verses.griffith_verse: Even to these dark Steeds of Wind thou of thyself hast come to ride, Of which no driver may be found, none, be he God or mortal man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध ग्मंतोशना पृच्छते वां कदर्था न आ गृहं ।आ जग्मथुः पराकाद्दिवश्च ग्मश्च मर्त्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ gmántā ǀ uśánā ǀ pṛcchate ǀ vām ǀ kát-arthā ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gṛhám ǀā́ ǀ jagmathuḥ ǀ parākā́t ǀ diváḥ ǀ ca ǀ gmáḥ ǀ ca ǀ mártyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: When ye approach, men ask you, thee and Uśanā: Why come ye to our dwelling-place? Why are ye come to mortal man from distant realms of eapth and heaven?
verses.wilson_translation: Uśanasinquires of youu two as you pass, "(Why) have you come to (our dwelling) from a distance;from heaven and earth to a mortal?"
verses.griffith_verse: When ye approach, men ask you, thee and Uśanā: Why come ye to our dwelling-place? Why are ye come to mortal man from distant realms of eapth and heaven?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ न इंद्र पृक्षसेऽस्माकं ब्रह्मोद्यतं ।तत्त्वा याचामहेऽवः शुष्णं यद्धन्नमानुषं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ pṛkṣase ǀ asmā́kam ǀ bráhma ǀ út-yatam ǀtát ǀ tvā ǀ yācāmahe ǀ ávaḥ ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ yát ǀ hán ǀ ámānuṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, thou shalt speak us fair: our holy prayer is offered up. We pray to thee for help as thou didst strike the monster Śuṣṇa dead.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Indra, the oblation upraised by us; we solicit of you that protection by which you did slay thenon-human Suṣṇa.
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, thou shalt speak us fair: our holy prayer is offered up. We pray to thee for help as thou didst strike the monster Śuṣṇa dead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अकर्मा दस्युरभि नो अमंतुरन्यव्रतो अमानुषः ।त्वं तस्यामित्रहन्वधर्दासस्य दंभय ॥
verses.transliteration: akarmā́ ǀ dásyuḥ ǀ abhí ǀ naḥ ǀ amantúḥ ǀ anyá-vrataḥ ǀ ámānuṣaḥ ǀtvám ǀ tásya ǀ amitra-han ǀ vádhaḥ ǀ dāsásya ǀ dambhaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Around us is the Dasyu, riteless, void of sense, inhuman, keeping alien laws. Baffle, thou Slayer of the foe, the weapon which this Dāsa wields.
verses.wilson_translation: The Dasyupractising no religious rites, not knowing as thoroughly, following other observances,obeying no human laws, baffle, destroyer of enemies, the weapon of that slave.
verses.griffith_verse: Around us is the Dasyu, riteless, void of sense, inhuman, keeping alien laws. Baffle, thou Slayer of the foe, the weapon which this Dāsa wields.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं न इंद्र शूर शूरैरुत त्वोतासो बर्हणा ।पुरुत्रा ते वि पूर्तयो नवंत क्षोणयो यथा ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ śūra ǀ śū́raiḥ ǀ utá ǀ tvā́-ūtāsaḥ ǀ barháṇā ǀpuru-trā́ ǀ te ǀ ví ǀ pūrtáyaḥ ǀ návanta ǀ kṣoṇáyaḥ ǀ yathā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hero with Heroes, thou art ours: yea, strong are they whom thou dost help. In many a place are thy full gifts, and men, like vassals, sing thy praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, withh the hero (Marutsdefend) us; that protected by you (we may be able) to overcome(our enemies); your blessings are diffused among many (praisers), as men (repair to their lord).
verses.griffith_verse: Hero with Heroes, thou art ours: yea, strong are they whom thou dost help. In many a place are thy full gifts, and men, like vassals, sing thy praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं तान्वृत्रहत्ये चोदयो नॄन्कार्पाणे शूर वज्रिवः ।गुहा यदी कवीनां विशां नक्षत्रशवसां ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tā́n ǀ vṛtra-hátye ǀ codayaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ kārpāṇé ǀ śūra ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀgúhā ǀ yádi ǀ kavīnā́m ǀ viśā́m ǀ nákṣatra-śavasām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Urge thou these heroes on to slay the enemy, brave Thunderer! in the fight with swords. Even when hid among the tribes of Sages numerous as stars.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you have animated those chiefs (the Maruts) to the slaughterof Vṛtrain battle, when (you hear) the mystical (praises) of the sages, the worshippers praising the might of theconstellations.
verses.griffith_verse: Urge thou these heroes on to slay the enemy, brave Thunderer! in the fight with swords. Even when hid among the tribes of Sages numerous as stars.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मक्षू ता त इंद्र दानाप्नस आक्षाणे शूर वज्रिवः ।यद्ध शुष्णस्य दंभयो जातं विश्वं सयावभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: makṣú ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ dāná-apnasaḥ ǀ ākṣāṇé ǀ śūra ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǀyát ǀ ha ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ dambháyaḥ ǀ jātám ǀ víśvam ǀ sayā́va-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Swift come those gifts of thine whose hand is prompt to rend and burn, O Hero Thunder-armed: As thou with thy Companions didst destroy the whole of SuSnia's brood.
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, (your worshippers glorify) those prompt exploits performed by you in battle, (by you whoare) ever bountiful, when with your associate (Maruts) you destroyed the whole race oŚuṣṇa.
verses.griffith_verse: Swift come those gifts of thine whose hand is prompt to rend and burn, O Hero Thunder-armed: As thou with thy Companions didst destroy the whole of SuSnia's brood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: माकुध्र्यगिंद्र शूर वस्वीरस्मे भूवन्नभिष्टयः ।वयंवयं त आसां सुम्ने स्याम वज्रिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ akudhryák ǀ indra ǀ śūra ǀ vásvīḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ bhūvan ǀ abhíṣṭayaḥ ǀvayám-vayam ǀ te ǀ āsām ǀ sumné ǀ syāma ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not thine excellent assistance come to us, O Hero Indra, profitless. May we, may we enjoy the bliss of these thy favours, Thunderer!
verses.wilson_translation: Hero,Indra, let not our manifold sacrifices be unavailing, but may we all, thunderer, (through) your(favour) continue in the fruiton of these (our desires).
verses.griffith_verse: Let not thine excellent assistance come to us, O Hero Indra, profitless. May we, may we enjoy the bliss of these thy favours, Thunderer!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे ता त इंद्र संतु सत्याहिंसंतीरुपस्पृशः ।विद्याम यासां भुजो धेनूनां न वज्रिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ santu ǀ satyā́ ǀ áhiṃsantīḥ ǀ upa-spṛ́śaḥ ǀvidyā́ma ǀ yā́sām ǀ bhújaḥ ǀ dhenūnā́m ǀ ná ǀ vajri-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May those soft impulses of thine, O Indra, be fruitful and innocent to us. May we know these whose treasures are like those of milch-kine, Thunderer!
verses.wilson_translation: May these our (praises) reaching you,Indra, be successful, doing no detriment (to you), so that,thunderer, we may obtain the benefits derivable from them, as (a cowherd enjoys those) from the kine.
verses.griffith_verse: May those soft impulses of thine, O Indra, be fruitful and innocent to us. May we know these whose treasures are like those of milch-kine, Thunderer!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहस्ता यदपदी वर्धत क्षाः शचीभिर्वेद्यानां ।शुष्णं परि प्रदक्षिणिद्विश्वायवे नि शिश्नथः ॥
verses.transliteration: ahastā́ ǀ yát ǀ apádī ǀ várdhata ǀ kṣā́ḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ vedyā́nām ǀśúṣṇam ǀ pári ǀ pra-dakṣiṇít ǀ viśvá-āyave ǀ ní ǀ śiśnathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That Earth, through power of knowing things that may be known, handless and footless yet might thrive, Thou slewest, turning to the right, gu;na for every living man.
verses.wilson_translation: When the earth which has neitherhandsnor feet flourished throught the acts of (devotion paid to) theadorable (deities), then you did smite downŚuṣṇa, circumambulating it on the right, for the sake of Viśvāyu.
verses.griffith_verse: That Earth, through power of knowing things that may be known, handless and footless yet might thrive, Thou slewest, turning to the right, gu;na for every living man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पिबापिबेदिंद्र शूर सोमं मा रिषण्यो वसवान वसुः सन् ।उत त्रायस्व गृणतो मघोनो महश्च रायो रेवतस्कृधी नः ॥
verses.transliteration: píba-piba ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ śūra ǀ sómam ǀ mā́ ǀ riṣaṇyaḥ ǀ vasavāna ǀ vásuḥ ǀ sán ǀutá ǀ trāyasva ǀ gṛṇatáḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ ca ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ revátaḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink, drink the Soma, Hero Indra; be not withheld as thou art good, O Treasure-giver. Preserve the singers and our liberal princes, and make us wealthy with abundant riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink, hero Indra, drink the Soma; being excellent, harm (us) not, possessor of opulence; preservethose who praise you, and are affluent (in offerings), and render us rich with great riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Drink, drink the Soma, Hero Indra; be not withheld as thou art good, O Treasure-giver. Preserve the singers and our liberal princes, and make us wealthy with abundant riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ७ ऐन्द्रो विमदः प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा।इन्द्रः। जगतीः १,७ त्रिष्टुप् ,५ अभिसारिणी।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INDRA, whose right hand wields the bolt, we worship, driver of Bay Steeds seeking sundered courses.Shaking his beard with might he hath arisen, casting his weapons forth and dealing bounties. The treasure which his Bay Steeds found at sacrifice,—this wealth made opulent Indra slayer of the foe.Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja-he is Lord of Might. The Dāsa's very name I utterly destroy. When, with the Princes, Maghavari, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold, and the Controller's carWhich his two Tawny Coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose glory spreads afar. With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard.When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as wind disturbs the wood. We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, fatherlike, with power hath made us stronger;Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manners with contemptuous cries. Indra, the Vimadas have formed for thee a laud, copious, unparalleled, for thee Most Bountiful.We know the good we gain from him the Mighty One when we attract him as a herdsman calls the kine. Ne’er may this bond of friendship be dissevered, the Ṛṣi Vimada's and thine, O Indra.We know thou carest for us as a brother with us, O God, be thine auspicious friendship.

verses.sanskrit: यजामह इंद्रं वज्रदक्षिणं हरीणां रथ्यं विव्रता���ां ।प्र श्मश्रु दोधुवदूर्ध्वथा भूद्वि सेनाभिर्दयमानो वि राधसा ॥
verses.transliteration: yájāmahe ǀ índram ǀ vájra-dakṣiṇam ǀ hárīṇām ǀ rathyám ǀ ví-vratānām ǀprá ǀ śmáśru ǀ dódhuvat ǀ ūrdhvá-thā ǀ bhūt ǀ ví ǀ sénābhiḥ ǀ dáyamānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rā́dhasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: INDRA, whose right hand wields the bolt, we worship, driver of Bay Steeds seeking sundered courses. Shaking his beard with might he hath arisen, casting his weapons forth and dealing bounties.
verses.wilson_translation: We worship Indra, being in his righthandthe thunderbolt, the driver of the bay horses which havemany functions; shaking his beard, he mounts on high, destroying (his enemies) by his armies he gives wealth (tohis worshippers).
verses.griffith_verse: INDRA, whose right hand wields the bolt, we worship, driver of Bay Steeds seeking sundered courses. Shaking his beard with might he hath arisen, casting his weapons forth and dealing bounties.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हरी न्वस्य या वने विदे वस्विंद्रो मघैर्मघवा वृत्रहा भुवत् ।ऋभुर्वाज ऋभुक्षाः पत्यते शवोऽव क्ष्णौमि दासस्य नाम चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: hárī íti ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ yā́ ǀ váne ǀ vidé ǀ vásu ǀ índraḥ ǀ magháiḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ bhuvat ǀṛbhúḥ ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ patyate ǀ śávaḥ ǀ áva ǀ kṣṇaumi ǀ dā́sasya ǀ nā́ma ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: The treasure which his Bay Steeds found at sacrifice,—this wealth made opulent Indra slayer of the foe. Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja-he is Lord of Might. The Dāsa's very name I utterly destroy.
verses.wilson_translation: With his two bay horses which bestow riches at the sacrifice,Indra, wealthy with wealth, is the slayerof Vṛtra; the brilliant, powerful, mighty Indra is the lord of strength; (through him) I cut off the head of the Dāsa.
verses.griffith_verse: The treasure which his Bay Steeds found at sacrifice,—this wealth made opulent Indra slayer of the foe. Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja-he is Lord of Might. The Dāsa's very name I utterly destroy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदा वज्रं हिरण्यमिदथा रथं हरी यमस्य वहतो वि सूरिभिः ।आ तिष्ठति मघवा सनश्रुत इंद्रो वाजस्य दीर्घश्रवसस्पतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ vájram ǀ híraṇyam ǀ ít ǀ átha ǀ rátham ǀ hárī íti ǀ yám ǀ asya ǀ váhataḥ ǀ ví ǀ sūrí-bhiḥ ǀā́ ǀ tiṣṭhati ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sána-śrutaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vā́jasya ǀ dīrghá-śravasaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, with the Princes, Maghavari, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold, and the Controller's car Which his two Tawny Coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose glory spreads afar.
verses.wilson_translation: When he grasps his golden thunderbolt, then the opulent Indraascends with his praisers, the chariotwhich his two bay horses draw, (Indra) the lord of long-celebrated and widely-renowned food.
verses.griffith_verse: When, with the Princes, Maghavari, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold, and the Controller's car Which his two Tawny Coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose glory spreads afar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो चिन्नु वृष्टिर्यूथ्या स्वा सचाँ इंद्रः श्मश्रूणि हरिताभि प्रुष्णुते ।अव वेति सुक्षयं सुते मधूदिद्धूनोति वातो यथा वनं ॥
verses.transliteration: só íti ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ ǀ yūthyā́ ǀ svā́ ǀ sácā ǀ índraḥ ǀ śmáśrūṇi ǀ háritā ǀ abhí ǀ pruṣṇute ǀáva ǀ veti ǀ su-kṣáyam ǀ suté ǀ mádhu ǀ út ǀ ít ǀ dhūnoti ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ vánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard. When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as wind disturbs the wood.
verses.wilson_translation: As the rain (bedews all), so,Indra, accompanied by his troops (of the Maruts), sprinkles their beards,with the green (Soma); he repairs to the plural asant chamber (of sacrifice); (the Soma) beign effused, the sweet Soma agitates (his frame), as the breeze (shakes) the forest.
verses.griffith_verse: With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard. When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as wind disturbs the wood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वाचा विवाचो मृध्रवाचः पुरू सहस्राशिवा जघान ।तत्तदिदस्य पौंस्यं गृणीमसि पितेव यस्तविषीं वावृधे शवः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vācā́ ǀ ví-vācaḥ ǀ mṛdhrá-vācaḥ ǀ purú ǀ sahásrā ǀ áśivā ǀ jaghā́na ǀtát-tat ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀ pitā́-iva ǀ yáḥ ǀ táviṣīm ǀ vavṛdhé ǀ śávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, fatherlike, with power hath made us stronger; Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manners with contemptuous cries.
verses.wilson_translation: We praise his manhood, who, having by his voice alone made the many- tongued speechless has slainmany thousand enemies, who supports the strength (of the world) as a father the strength (of his son).
verses.griffith_verse: We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, fatherlike, with power hath made us stronger; Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manners with contemptuous cries.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोमं त इंद्र विमदा अजीजनन्नपूर्व्यं पुरुतमं सुदानवे ।विद्मा ह्यस्य भोजनमिनस्य यदा पशुं न गोपाः करामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: stómam ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ vi-madā́ḥ ǀ ajījanan ǀ ápūrvyam ǀ puru-támam ǀ su-dā́nave ǀvidmá ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ bhójanam ǀ inásya ǀ yát ǀ ā́ ǀ paśúm ǀ ná ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ karāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the Vimadas have formed for thee a laud, copious, unparalleled, for thee Most Bountiful. We know the good we gain from him the Mighty One when we attract him as a herdsman calls the kine.
verses.wilson_translation: We Vimadas, have genitive rated this your unprecedented, and most varied praise,Indra, to obtain yourbounty; as we know what the opulence of that lord is, (therefore) we call it (before us), as a cowherd (calls) hiscattle. attachment, divine (Indra), to be like that of a sister (to a brother) so may the friendship between us and youprosper.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, the Vimadas have formed for thee a laud, copious, unparalleled, for thee Most Bountiful. We know the good we gain from him the Mighty One when we attract him as a herdsman calls the kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: माकिर्न एना सख्या वि यौषुस्तव चेंद्र विमदस्य च ऋषेः ।विद्मा हि ते प्रमतिं देव जामिवदस्मे ते संतु सख्या शिवानि ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ ví ǀ yauṣuḥ ǀ táva ǀ ca ǀ indra ǀ vi-madásya ǀ ca ǀ ṛ́ṣeḥ ǀvidmá ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ prá-matim ǀ deva ǀ jāmi-vát ǀ asmé íti ǀ te ǀ santu ǀ sakhyā́ ǀ śivā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ne’er may this bond of friendship be dissevered, the Ṛṣi Vimada's and thine, O Indra. We know thou carest for us as a brother with us, O God, be thine auspicious friendship.
verses.griffith_verse: Ne’er may this bond of friendship be dissevered, the Ṛṣi Vimada's and thine, O Indra. We know thou carest for us as a brother with us, O God, be thine auspicious friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIV. Indra. Aśvins.
hymns.anukramani: ६ ऐन्द्रो विमदः, प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा। इन्द्रः। ४-६ अश्विनौ। आस्तारपंक्तिः, ४-६ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets.Send down to us great riches,—at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great. To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come.Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choiceworthy treasure. Thou art waxing great. Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl.Guardian of singers, Indra,—at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great. Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart,When ye, implored by Vimada, Nāsatyas, forced apart the pair. When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained.The Gods to the Nāsatyas cried, Bring these together once again. Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home.So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र सोममिमं पिब मधुमंतं चमू सुतं ।अस्मे रयिं नि धारय वि वो मदे सहस्रिणं पुरूवसो विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ sómam ǀ imám ǀ piba ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ camū́ íti ǀ sutám ǀasmé íti ǀ rayím ǀ ní ǀ dhāraya ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ sahasríṇam ǀ puruvaso íti puru-vaso ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets. Send down to us great riches,—at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indra, this most sweet Soma, expressed by the plural nks (of the Soma-press), then bestow uponus riches in your exhilaration; thousandfold (riches), lord of infinite wealth; you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets. Send down to us great riches,—at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां यज्ञेभिरुक्थैरुप हव्येभिरीमहे ।शचीपते शचीनां वि वो मदे श्रेष्ठं नो धेहि वार्यं विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ yajñébhiḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ havyébhiḥ ǀ īmahe ǀśácī-pate ǀ śacīnām ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ naḥ ǀ dhehi ǀ vā́ryam ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come. Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choiceworthy treasure. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit you with sacrifices, with prayers, with oblations; lord of all pious acts, grant us in yourexhilaration, excellent and desirable (affluence); you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come. Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choiceworthy treasure. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्पतिर्वार्याणामसि रध्रस्य चोदिता ।इंद्र स्तोतॄणामविता वि वो मदे द्विषो नः पाह्यंहसो विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ pátim ǀ vā́ryāṇām ǀ ási ǀ radhrásya ǀ coditā́ ǀíndra ǀ stotṝṇā́m ǀ avitā́ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ dviṣáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl. Guardian of singers, Indra,—at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who are the lord of desirable (riches), the encourager of the worshipper, the protector of theeulogists, defend us, in your exhilaration, from adversaries, (guard us) from sin, you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl. Guardian of singers, Indra,—at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं शक्रा मायाविना समीची निरमंथतं ।विमदेन यदीळिता नासत्या निरमंथतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ śakrā ǀ māyā-vínā ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ níḥ ǀ amanthatam ǀvi-madéna ǀ yát ǀ īḷitā́ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ niḥ-ámanthatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart, When ye, implored by Vimada, Nāsatyas, forced apart the pair.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful and sagacious (Aśvins) mutually associated, you have churned forth (the fire); when you,Nāsatyās, glorified by Vimada, have churned it forth.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart, When ye, implored by Vimada, Nāsatyas, forced apart the pair.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवा अकृपंत समीच्योर्निष्पतंत्योः ।नासत्यावब्रुवंदेवाः पुनरा वहतादिति ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ akṛpanta ǀ sam-īcyóḥ ǀ niḥ-pátantyoḥ ǀnā́satyau ǀ abruvan ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vahatāt ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained. The Gods to the Nāsatyas cried, Bring these together once again.
verses.wilson_translation: All the gods praised you as you were mutually associated, and caused (the sparks) to fly up; the godshave said to the two Nāsatyās, "let the fire again bear (us oblations)"].
verses.griffith_verse: When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained. The Gods to the Nāsatyas cried, Bring these together once again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मधुमन्मे परायणं मधुमत्पुनरायनं ।ता नो देवा देवतया युवं मधुमतस्कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: mádhu-mat ǀ me ǀ parā-áyanam ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ā́-áyanam ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ devā ǀ devátayā ǀ yuvám ǀ mádhu-mataḥ ǀ kṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home. So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.
verses.wilson_translation: May my going forth be plural asant, may my coming back be plural asant, you two divine Aśvins, render us,through your divine power, possessed of plural asure.
verses.griffith_verse: Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home. So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXV. Soma.
hymns.anukramani: ११ ऐन्द्रो विमदः प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा। सोमः। आस्तारपंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power.Then-at your glad carouse-let men joy in thy love, Sweet juice! as kine in pasture. Thou. art waxing great. rn all thy forms, O Soma, rest thy powers that influence the heart.So also these my longings-at your glad carouse-spread themselves seeking riches. Thou art waxing great. Even if, O Soma, I neglect thy laws through my simplicity,Be gracious-at your glad carouse-as sire to son. Preserve us even from slaughter. T'hou. art waxing great. Our songs in concert go to thee as streams of water to the wells.Soma, that we may live, grant-at your glad carouse-full powers of mind, like beakers. Thou art waxing great. O Soma, through thy might who art skilful and strong, these longing men,These sages, have thrown open-at your glad carouse-the stall of kine and horses. Thou art waxing great Our herds thou guardest, Soma, and the moving world spread far and wide.Thou fittest them for living,—at your glad carouse-looking upon all beings. Thou art waxing great. On all sides, Soma, be to us a Guardian ne’er to be deceived.King, drive away our foemen-at your glad carouse:—let not the wicked rule us. Thou art waxing great. Be watchful, Soma, passing wise, to give us store of vital strength.More skilled than man to guide us,—at your glad carouse-save us from harm and sorrow. Thou art waxing great. Chief slayer of our foemen, thou, Indu, art Indra's gracious Friend,When warriors invoke him-at your glad carouse -in fight, to win them offspring. Thou art waxing great. Victorious is this gladdening drink: to Indra dear it grows in strength.This-at your glad carouse -enhanced the mighty hymn of the great sage Kakṣīvān. Thou art waxing great. This to the sage who offers gifts brings power that comes from wealth in kine.This, better than the seven, hath-at your glad carouse-furthered the blind, the cripple. Thou art waxing great.

verses.sanskrit: भद्रं नो अपि वातय मनो दक्षमुत क्रतुं ।अधा ते सख्ये अंधसो वि वो मदे रणन्गावो न यवसे विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ naḥ ǀ ápi ǀ vātaya ǀ mánaḥ ǀ dákṣam ǀ utá ǀ krátum ǀádha ǀ te ǀ sakhyé ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ ráṇan ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yávase ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power. Then-at your glad carouse-let men joy in thy love, Sweet juice! as kine in pasture. Thou. art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Sanctify (Soma) our mind, our heart, our intellect; and may (your worshippers) delight in yourfriendship, like cattle in fresh pasture, in your exhilaration (produced) by the (sacrificial) food; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power. Then-at your glad carouse-let men joy in thy love, Sweet juice! as kine in pasture. Thou. art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हृदिस्पृशस्त आसते विश्वेषु सोम धामसु ।अधा कामा इमे मम वि वो मदे वि तिष्ठंते वसूयवो विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: hṛdi-spṛ́śaḥ ǀ te ǀ āsate ǀ víśveṣu ǀ soma ǀ dhā́ma-su ǀádha ǀ kā́māḥ ǀ imé ǀ máma ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ ví ǀ tiṣṭhante ǀ vasu-yávaḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: rn all thy forms, O Soma, rest thy powers that influence the heart. So also these my longings-at your glad carouse-spread themselves seeking riches. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: They who seek to touch your heart,Soma, worship you in all plural ces; and these desires for wealth risefrom my heart at your exhilaration; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: rn all thy forms, O Soma, rest thy powers that influence the heart. So also these my longings-at your glad carouse-spread themselves seeking riches. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत व्रतानि सोम ते प्राहं मिनामि पाक्या ।अधा पितेव सूनवे वि वो मदे मृळा नो अभि चिद्वधाद्विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vratā́ni ǀ soma ǀ te ǀ prá ǀ ahám ǀ mināmi ǀ pākyā́ ǀádha ǀ pitā́-iva ǀ sūnáve ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ mṛḷá ǀ naḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cit ǀ vadhā́t ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even if, O Soma, I neglect thy laws through my simplicity, Be gracious-at your glad carouse-as sire to son. Preserve us even from slaughter. T'hou. art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily,Soma, I practise all your observances with fullness; and as a father to his son, so do you inyour exhilaration make us happy; protect us from being killed (by our enemies); for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Even if, O Soma, I neglect thy laws through my simplicity, Be gracious-at your glad carouse-as sire to son. Preserve us even from slaughter. T'hou. art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समु प्र यंति धीतयः सर्गासोऽवताँ इव ।क्रतुं नः सोम जीवसे वि वो मदे धारया चमसाँ इव विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ yanti ǀ dhītáyaḥ ǀ sárgāsaḥ ǀ avatā́n-iva ǀkrátum ǀ naḥ ǀ soma ǀ jīváse ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ dhāráya ǀ camasā́n-iva ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our songs in concert go to thee as streams of water to the wells. Soma, that we may live, grant-at your glad carouse-full powers of mind, like beakers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Our praises converge (Soma) towards you, as herds towards a well; establish our pious acts, Soma,for us to live (long), as (the priest sets up) the cups for your exhilaration; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Our songs in concert go to thee as streams of water to the wells. Soma, that we may live, grant-at your glad carouse-full powers of mind, like beakers. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तव त्ये सोम शक्तिभिर्निकामासो व्यृण्विरे ।गृत्सस्य धीरास्तवसो वि वो मदे व्रजं गोमंतमश्विनं विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tyé ǀ soma ǀ śákti-bhiḥ ǀ ní-kāmāsaḥ ǀ ví ǀ ṛṇvire ǀgṛ́tsasya ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ tavásaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ vrajám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ aśvínam ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Soma, through thy might who art skilful and strong, these longing men, These sages, have thrown open-at your glad carouse-the stall of kine and horses. Thou art waxing great
verses.wilson_translation: The intelligent (priests), whose desires are fixed (on the fruit of good works), with sacred rites showforth (the praises) of you,Soma, who are wise and powerful; do you, in your exhilaration, (grant us) pastures,abounding with cattle, and with horses; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: O Soma, through thy might who art skilful and strong, these longing men, These sages, have thrown open-at your glad carouse-the stall of kine and horses. Thou art waxing great
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पशुं नः सोम रक्षसि पुरुत्रा विष्ठितं जगत् ।समाकृणोषि जीवसे वि वो मदे विश्वा संपश्यन्भुवन�� विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: paśúm ǀ naḥ ǀ soma ǀ rakṣasi ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ ví-sthitam ǀ jágat ǀsam-ā́kṛṇoṣi ǀ jīváse ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ víśvā ǀ sam-páśyan ǀ bhúvanā ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Our herds thou guardest, Soma, and the moving world spread far and wide. Thou fittest them for living,—at your glad carouse-looking upon all beings. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: You protect our cattle,Soma, and the variously occupied world, contemplating all existing beings; youprepare (the world) for them to live in for your exhilaration; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Our herds thou guardest, Soma, and the moving world spread far and wide. Thou fittest them for living,—at your glad carouse-looking upon all beings. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नः सोम विश्वतो गोपा अदाभ्यो भव ।सेध राजन्नप स्रिधो वि वो मदे मा नो दुःशंस ईशता विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ soma ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǀ bhava ǀsédha ǀ rājan ǀ ápa ǀ srídhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duḥ-śáṃsaḥ ǀ īśata ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: On all sides, Soma, be to us a Guardian ne’er to be deceived. King, drive away our foemen-at your glad carouse:—let not the wicked rule us. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Be on all sides our preserver,Soma, you, who are unassailable; drive away, monarch, our adversariesin your exhilaration, and let no calumniator rule over us; for you are mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: On all sides, Soma, be to us a Guardian ne’er to be deceived. King, drive away our foemen-at your glad carouse:—let not the wicked rule us. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नः सोम सुक्रतुर्वयोधेयाय जागृहि ।क्षेत्रवित्तरो मनुषो वि वो मदे द्रुहो नः पाह्यंहसो विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ soma ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ vayaḥ-dhéyāya ǀ jāgṛhi ǀkṣetravít-taraḥ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ druháḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pāhi ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be watchful, Soma, passing wise, to give us store of vital strength. More skilled than man to guide us,—at your glad carouse-save us from harm and sorrow. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, author of good works, liberal granter of fields, be vigilant in supplying us with food; and in your
verses.griffith_verse: Be watchful, Soma, passing wise, to give us store of vital strength. More skilled than man to guide us,—at your glad carouse-save us from harm and sorrow. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो वृत्रहंतमेंद्रस्येंदो शिवः सखा ।यत्सीं हवंते समिथे वि वो मदे युध्यमानास्तोकसातौ विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛtrahan-tama ǀ índrasya ǀ indo íti ǀ śiváḥ ǀ sákhā ǀyát ǀ sīm ǀ hávante ǀ sam-ithé ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ yúdhyamānāḥ ǀ toká-sātau ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Chief slayer of our foemen, thou, Indu, art Indra's gracious Friend, When warriors invoke him-at your glad carouse -in fight, to win them offspring. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Utter destroyer of enemies,Soma, who are the auspicious friend of Indra, (protect us), when hostilewarriors everywhere call us to the combat that bestows offsprin; by your exhilration (preserve us); for you aremighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Chief slayer of our foemen, thou, Indu, art Indra's gracious Friend, When warriors invoke him-at your glad carouse -in fight, to win them offspring. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं घ स तुरो मद इंद्रस्य वर्धत प्रियः ।अयं कक्षीवतो महो वि वो मदे मतिं विप्रस्य वर्धयद्विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ gha ǀ sáḥ ǀ turáḥ ǀ mádaḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ vardhata ǀ priyáḥ ǀayám ǀ kakṣī́vataḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ matím ǀ víprasya ǀ vardhayat ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Victorious is this gladdening drink: to Indra dear it grows in strength. This-at your glad carouse -enhanced the mighty hymn of the great sage Kakṣīvān. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: Such is the Somawhich, swiftly moving, exhilarating, acceptable to Indra, has given increase (to ourunderstanding); it has increased the intelligence of the great and pious Kakṣīvatin your exhilaration; for youare mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Victorious is this gladdening drink: to Indra dear it grows in strength. This-at your glad carouse -enhanced the mighty hymn of the great sage Kakṣīvān. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं विप्राय दाशुषे वाजाँ इयर्ति गोमतः ।अयं सप्तभ्य आ वरं वि वो मदे प्रांधं श्रोणं च तारिषद्विवक्षसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ víprāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vā́jān ǀ iyarti ǀ gó-mataḥ ǀayám ǀ saptá-bhyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ váram ǀ ví ǀ vaḥ ǀ máde ǀ prá ǀ andhám ǀ śroṇám ǀ ca ǀ tāriṣat ǀ vívakṣase ǁ
verses.english_translation: This to the sage who offers gifts brings power that comes from wealth in kine. This, better than the seven, hath-at your glad carouse-furthered the blind, the cripple. Thou art waxing great.
verses.wilson_translation: This Somabestows, upon the pious donor of the libation, food with cattle; it gives wealth to the seven(priests) in the manifold exhilaration; it has restored (their faculties) to the blind, and the lame.
verses.griffith_verse: This to the sage who offers gifts brings power that comes from wealth in kine. This, better than the seven, hath-at your glad carouse-furthered the blind, the cripple. Thou art waxing great.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVI. Pūṣan.
hymns.anukramani: ९ ऐन्द्रो विमदः, प्राजापत्यो वा, वासुक्रो वसुकृद्वा।पूषा। अनुष्टुप् ,१,४ उष्णिक्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FORWARD upon their way proceed the ready teams, the lovely songs.Further them glorious Pūṣan with yoked chariot, and the Mighty Twain! With sacred hymns let this man here, this singer, win the God to whomBelong this majesty and might. He hath observed our eulogies. Pūṣan the Strong hath knowledge of sweet praises even as Indu hath.He dews our corn with moisture, he bedews the pasture of our kine. We will bethink ourselves of thee, O Pūṣan, O thou God, as One.Who brings fulfilment of our hymns, and stirs the singer and the sage. joint-sharer of each sacrifice, the driver of the chariot steeds;The Ṛṣi who is good to man, the singer's Friend and faithful Guard. One who is Lord of Suca, Lord of Suca caring for herself:Weaving the raiment of the sheep and making raiment beautiful. The mighty Lord of spoil and wealth, Strong Friend of all prosperity;He with light movement shakes his beard, lovely and ne’er to be deceived. O Pūṣan, may those goats of thine turn hitherward thy chariot-pole.Friend of all suppliants; art thou, born in old time, and arm and sure. May the majestic Pūṣan speed our chariot with his power and might.May he increase our store of wealth and listen to this call of ours.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ह्यच्छा मनीषा स्पार्हा यंति नियुतः ।प्र दस्रा नियुद्रथः पूषा अविष्टु माहिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ hí ǀ áccha ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǀ spārhā́ḥ ǀ yánti ǀ ni-yútaḥ ǀprá ǀ dasrā́ ǀ niyút-rathaḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ aviṣṭu ǀ mā́hinaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FORWARD upon their way proceed the ready teams, the lovely songs. Further them glorious Pūṣan with yoked chariot, and the Mighty Twain!
verses.wilson_translation: Since our appointed and acceptable prayers proceed to him, may the mighty Pūṣan, of plural asingaspect, whose care is ever harnessed, protect us.
verses.griffith_verse: FORWARD upon their way proceed the ready teams, the lovely songs. Further them glorious Pūṣan with yoked chariot, and the Mighty Twain!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य त्यन्महित्वं वाताप्यमयं जनः ।विप्र आ वंसद्धीतिभिश्चिकेत सुष्टुतीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ tyát ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ vātā́pyam ǀ ayám ǀ jánaḥ ǀvípraḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaṃsat ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ cíketa ǀ su-stutīnā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: With sacred hymns let this man here, this singer, win the God to whom Belong this majesty and might. He hath observed our eulogies.
verses.wilson_translation: (May e) whose greatness (manifested as) the matured rain, this pious man celebrates with piousrites-- may he be cognizant of such excellent praises.
verses.griffith_verse: With sacred hymns let this man here, this singer, win the God to whom Belong this majesty and might. He hath observed our eulogies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स वेद सुष्टुतीनामिंदुर्न पूषा वृषा ।अभि प्सुरः प्रुषायति व्रजं न आ प्रुषायति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ veda ǀ su-stutīnā́m ǀ índuḥ ǀ ná ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀabhí ǀ psúraḥ ǀ pruṣāyati ǀ vrajám ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pruṣāyati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pūṣan the Strong hath knowledge of sweet praises even as Indu hath. He dews our corn with moisture, he bedews the pasture of our kine.
verses.wilson_translation: He,Pūṣan, is cognizant of such excellent praises; like Somahe is the showerer (of benefits); thegraceful deity rains down upon us, he rains upon our cow-pastures.
verses.griffith_verse: Pūṣan the Strong hath knowledge of sweet praises even as Indu hath. He dews our corn with moisture, he bedews the pasture of our kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंसीमहि त्वा वयमस्माकं देव पूषन् ।मतीनां च साधनं विप्राणां चाधवं ॥
verses.transliteration: maṃsīmáhi ǀ tvā ǀ vayám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ deva ǀ pūṣan ǀmatīnā́m ǀ ca ǀ sā́dhanam ǀ víprāṇām ǀ ca ǀ ā-dhavám ǁ
verses.english_translation: We will bethink ourselves of thee, O Pūṣan, O thou God, as One. Who brings fulfilment of our hymns, and stirs the singer and the sage.
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify you, divine Pūṣan, the accomplisher of our desires, who make the pious to quake.
verses.griffith_verse: We will bethink ourselves of thee, O Pūṣan, O thou God, as One. Who brings fulfilment of our hymns, and stirs the singer and the sage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यर्धिर्यज्ञानामश्वहयो रथानां ।ऋषिः स यो मनुर्हितो विप्रस्य यावयत्सखः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti-ardhiḥ ǀ yajñā́nām ǀ aśva-hayáḥ ǀ ráthānām ǀṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mánuḥ-hitaḥ ǀ víprasya ǀ yavayat-sakháḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: joint-sharer of each sacrifice, the driver of the chariot steeds; The Ṛṣi who is good to man, the singer's Friend and faithful Guard.
verses.griffith_verse: joint-sharer of each sacrifice, the driver of the chariot steeds; The Ṛṣi who is good to man, the singer's Friend and faithful Guard.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आधीषमाणायाः पतिः शुचायाश्च शुचस्य च ।वासोवायोऽवीनामा वासांसि मर्मृजत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-dhī́ṣamāṇāyāḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ śucā́yāḥ ǀ ca ǀ śucásya ǀ ca ǀvāsaḥ-vāyáḥ ǀ ávīnām ǀ ā́ ǀ vā́sāṃsi ǀ mármṛjat ǁ
verses.english_translation: One who is Lord of Suca, Lord of Suca caring for herself: Weaving the raiment of the sheep and making raiment beautiful.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord both of the pure desirable (she-goat), and of the pure (he-goat); weave3r of the cloth (of thewool) of the sheep; he has cleansed the vestments.
verses.griffith_verse: One who is Lord of Suca, Lord of Suca caring for herself: Weaving the raiment of the sheep and making raiment beautiful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इनो वाजानां पतिरिनः पुष्टीनां सखा ।प्र श्मश्रु हर्यतो दूधोद्वि वृथा यो अदाभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: ináḥ ǀ vā́jānām ǀ pátiḥ ǀ ináḥ ǀ puṣṭīnā́m ǀ sákhā ǀprá ǀ śmáśru ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ dūdhot ǀ ví ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ádābhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The mighty Lord of spoil and wealth, Strong Friend of all prosperity; He with light movement shakes his beard, lovely and ne’er to be deceived.
verses.wilson_translation: The ruler, the lord of viands, the soverign, the friend of the contentment (of all); he who isunassailable, genitive ly shakes his beard (when drinking the Somaof the sacrificer), desiring (his favour).
verses.griffith_verse: The mighty Lord of spoil and wealth, Strong Friend of all prosperity; He with light movement shakes his beard, lovely and ne’er to be deceived.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ ते रथस्य पूषन्नजा धुरं ववृत्युः ।विश्वस्यार्थिनः सखा सनोजा अनपच्युतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ ráthasya ǀ pūṣan ǀ ajā́ḥ ǀ dhúram ǀ vavṛtyuḥ ǀvíśvasya ǀ arthínaḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ sanaḥ-jā́ḥ ǀ ánapa-cyutaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Pūṣan, may those goats of thine turn hitherward thy chariot-pole. Friend of all suppliants; art thou, born in old time, and arm and sure.
verses.wilson_translation: THe goats,Pūṣan, bear the burden of your car, who are the friend of every suppliant, born long ago,never-failing (in your duty).
verses.griffith_verse: O Pūṣan, may those goats of thine turn hitherward thy chariot-pole. Friend of all suppliants; art thou, born in old time, and arm and sure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमूर्जा रथं पूषा अविष्टु माहिनः ।भुवद्वाजानां वृध इमं नः शृणवद्धवं ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ rátham ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ aviṣṭu ǀ mā́hinaḥ ǀbhúvat ǀ vā́jānām ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ imám ǀ naḥ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the majestic Pūṣan speed our chariot with his power and might. May he increase our store of wealth and listen to this call of ours.
verses.wilson_translation: May the mighty Pūṣanprotect our chariot by his might; may he be to us the augmenter of food; mayhe hear this our invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: May the majestic Pūṣan speed our chariot with his power and might. May he increase our store of wealth and listen to this call of ours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma.I slay the man who brings no milkoblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter. Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless,Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices. I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle.Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses. While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed.The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain. None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose.Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated. To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o’ertaken by destruction!Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him. Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee.Two canopies, as ’twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region. The freed kine eat the barley of the pious.  saw them as they wandered with the herdsman.The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner? When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land.There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him. There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds.I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women. When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness?Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her? How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches?If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people. His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter.Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him. High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding.Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder? Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together.Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o’er the rock's high ridges. One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose.The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not. The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted wether: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming.Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying. Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other.To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter. I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature.The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings. These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger.The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.
