This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Sūrya.Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow. Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying,Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Ṛṣi, is affrighted. In the Gods’ mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later.Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture. This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle.He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.

verses.sanskrit: असत्सु मे जरितः साभिवेगो यत्सुन्वते यजमानाय शिक्षं ।अनाशीर्दामहमस्मि प्रहंता सत्यध्वृतं वृजिनायंतमाभुं ॥
verses.transliteration: ásat ǀ sú ǀ me ǀ jaritaríti ǀ sáḥ ǀ abhi-vegáḥ ǀ yát ǀ sunvaté ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śíkṣam ǀánāśīḥ-dām ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǀ pra-hantā́ ǀ satya-dhvṛ́tam ǀ vṛjina-yántam ǀ ābhúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma. I slay the man who brings no milkoblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks). Such is my plural asant disposition, worshipper, that I help the instrumental tutor of the rite, whooffers libation; but I am the punisher of him who offers not libations, who disregards the truth, the perpetrator ofsin, the malignant.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma. I slay the man who brings no milkoblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदीदहं युधये संनयान्यदेवयूंतन्वा शूशुजानान् ।अमा ते तुम्रं वृषभं पचानि तीव्रं सुतं पंचदशं नि षिंचं ॥
verses.transliteration: yádi ǀ ít ǀ ahám ǀ yudháye ǀ sam-náyāni ǀ ádeva-yūn ǀ tanvā́ ǀ śū́śujānān ǀamā́ ǀ te ǀ túmram ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ pacāni ǀ tīvrám ǀ sutám ǀ pañca-daśám ǀ ní ǀ siñcam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless, Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices.
verses.wilson_translation: If I encounter in combat the undevout, resplendent in their bodies, then will I cook a vigorous bull forthem, and will sprinkle (upon the fire) the exhilarating Somathe fifteen-fold (Soma).
verses.griffith_verse: Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless, Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाहं तं वेद य इति ब्रवीत्यदेवयून्त्समरणे जघन्वान् ।यदावाख्यत्समरणमृघावदादिद्ध मे वृषभा प्र ब्रुवंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ tám ǀ veda ǀ yáḥ ǀ íti ǀ brávīti ǀ ádeva-yūn ǀ sam-áraṇe ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀyadā́ ǀ ava-ákhyat ǀ sam-áraṇam ǀ ṛ́ghāvat ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ ha ǀ me ǀ vṛṣabhā́ ǀ prá ǀ bruvanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle. Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses.
verses.wilson_translation: I know not that man who says that he is the slayer in battle of those who do not reverence the gods;but when (I behold) the fierce war commenced, then (my enemies) proclaim my prowess.
verses.griffith_verse: I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle. Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदज्ञातेषु वृजनेष्वासं विश्वे सतो मघवानो म आसन् ।जिनामि वेत्क्षेम आ संतमाभुं प्र तं क्षिणां पर्वते पादगृह्य ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ájñāteṣu ǀ vṛjáneṣu ǀ ā́sam ǀ víśve ǀ satáḥ ǀ maghá-vānaḥ ǀ me ǀ āsan ǀjinā́mi ǀ vā ǀ ít ǀ kṣéme ǀ ā́ ǀ sántam ǀ ābhúm ǀ prá ǀ tám ǀ kṣiṇām ǀ párvate ǀ pāda-gṛ́hya ǁ
verses.english_translation: While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed. The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain.
verses.wilson_translation: When I enter upon unprecedented combats, then all those who are affluent in oblations approach meso engaged; I destroy the mighty and overpowering foe for the protection of the world, and, seizing him by thefeet, throw him down from the mountain.
verses.griffith_verse: While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed. The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वा उ मां वृजने वारयंते न पर्वतासो यदहं मनस्ये ।मम स्वनात्कृधुकर्णो भयात एवेदनु द्यून्किरणः समेजात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ mā́m ǀ vṛjáne ǀ vārayante ǀ ná ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ahám ǀ manasyé ǀmáma ǀ svanā́t ǀ kṛdhu-kárṇaḥ ǀ bhayāte ǀ evá ǀ ít ǀ ánu ǀ dyū́n ǀ kiráṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ejāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose. Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated.
verses.wilson_translation: None resist me (engaged) in combat, not even the mountains when I am resolved; at my shout the dullof hearing is alarmed, and so too even the bright- rayed (sun) trembles day by day.
verses.griffith_verse: None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose. Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दर्शन्न्वत्र शृतपाँ अनिंद्रान्बाहुक्षदः शरवे पत्यमानान् ।घृषुं वा ये निनिदुः सखायमध्यू न्वेषु पवयो ववृत्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: dárśan ǀ nú ǀ átra ǀ śṛta-pā́n ǀ anindrā́n ǀ bāhu-kṣádaḥ ǀ śárave ǀ pátyamānān ǀghṛ́ṣum ǀ vā ǀ yé ǀ ninidúḥ ǀ sákhāyam ǀ ádhi ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ eṣu ǀ paváyaḥ ǀ vavṛtyuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o’ertaken by destruction! Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him.
verses.wilson_translation: Beholding here the drinkers of the libations who serve not Indra, who cut (the worshippers) to pieceswith theirhands, assailing them to do them harm; my shafts quickly fall upon them, as well as on those who revile(your) powerful friend. all existence; the ancient Indra verily destroys (his foe), the other does not destroy (Indra). The united two(heaven and earth) surpass not him who extends beyond the confines of the universe.
verses.griffith_verse: To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o’ertaken by destruction! Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभूर्वौक्षीर्व्यु आयुरानड्दर्षन्नु पूर्वो अपरो नु दर्षत् ।द्वे पवस्ते परि तं न भूतो यो अस्य पारे रजसो विवेष ॥
verses.transliteration: ábhūḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ áukṣīḥ ǀ ví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ānaṭ ǀ dárṣat ǀ nú ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ áparaḥ ǀ nú ǀ darṣat ǀdvé íti ǀ paváste íti ǀ pári ǀ tám ǀ ná ǀ bhūtaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pāré ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vivéṣa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee. Two canopies, as ’twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee. Two canopies, as ’twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गावो यवं प्रयुता अर्यो अक्षंता अपश्यं सहगोपाश्चरंतीः ।हवा इदर्यो अभितः समायन्कियदासु स्वपतिश्छंदयाते ॥
verses.transliteration: gā́vaḥ ǀ yávam ǀ prá-yutāḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ akṣan ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ apaśyam ǀ sahá-gopāḥ ǀ cárantīḥ ǀhávāḥ ǀ ít ǀ aryáḥ ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ sám ǀ āyan ǀ kíyat ǀ āsu ǀ svá-patiḥ ǀ chandayāte ǁ
verses.english_translation: The freed kine eat the barley of the pious. 1 saw them as they wandered with the herdsman. The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner?
verses.wilson_translation: The assembled cattle feed upon the barley; I their master have beheld them grazing, tended by theherdsman; when called, they collect around their lord; when they approach, how much milk does he desire (totake)?
verses.griffith_verse: The freed kine eat the barley of the pious. 1 saw them as they wandered with the herdsman. The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं यद्वयं यवसादो जनानामहं यवाद उर्वज्रे अंतः ।अत्रा युक्तोऽवसातारमिच्छादथो अयुक्तं युनजद्ववन्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ yát ǀ váyam ǀ yavasa-ádaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ahám ǀ yava-ádaḥ ǀ uru-ájre ǀ antáríti ǀátra ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ ava-sātā́ram ǀ icchāt ǀ átho íti ǀ áyuktam ǀ yunajat ǀ vavanvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land. There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him.
verses.wilson_translation: When we, the grass-eaters of men, (are) together, I (am) among the barley-eaters in the wide field;here he who is yoked would like one to unloose him, and the assailant would yoke him who is unyoked.
verses.griffith_verse: When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land. There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अत्रेदु मे मंससे सत्यमुक्तं द्विपाच्च यच्चतुष्पात्संसृजानि ।स्त्रीभिर्यो अत्र वृषणं पृतन्यादयुद्धो अस्य वि भजानि वेदः ॥
verses.transliteration: átra ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ me ǀ maṃsase ǀ satyám ǀ uktám ǀ dvi-pā́t ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ cátuḥ-pāt ǀ sam-sṛjā́ni ǀstrībhíḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ átra ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ pṛtanyā́t ǀ áyuddhaḥ ǀ asya ǀ ví ǀ bhajāni ǀ védaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds. I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks). You know that what is said by me at this time is the truth, that I may create both bipedsand quadrupeds. I distribute without conflict (among my worshippers) the wealth (that I have taken from him), who(neglecting me), the showerer of desires), wishes to contend with women.
verses.griffith_verse: There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds. I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्यानक्षा दुहिता जात्वास कस्तां विद्वाँ अभि मन्याते अंधां ।कतरो मेनिं प्रति तं मुचाते य ईं वहाते य ईं वा वरेयात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ anakṣā́ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ jā́tu ǀ ā́sa ǀ káḥ ǀ tā́m ǀ vidvā́n ǀ abhí ǀ manyāte ǀ andhā́m ǀkataráḥ ǀ mením ǀ práti ǀ tám ǀ mucāte ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ váhāte ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ vā ǀ vare-yā́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness? Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her?
verses.wilson_translation: What (other god but me) whose eyeless daughter is ever present knows her and honours (her) theblind one; which of the two (deities) lets loose that bolt against (a foe)-- he who assails, (or) he who protects hiṃ
verses.griffith_verse: When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness? Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कियती योषा मर्यतो वधूयोः परिप्रीता पन्यसा वार्येण ।भद्रा वधूर्भवति यत्सुपेशाः स्वयं सा मित्रं वनुते जने चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: kíyatī ǀ yóṣā ǀ maryatáḥ ǀ vadhū-yóḥ ǀ pári-prītā ǀ pányasā ǀ vā́ryeṇa ǀbhadrā́ ǀ vadhū́ḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ yát ǀ su-péśāḥ ǀ svayám ǀ sā́ ǀ mitrám ǀ vanute ǀ jáne ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches? If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people.
verses.wilson_translation: How many a woman has been gratified by the flattering praise of man's desire, when the bride isfortunate and beautiful, she of herself chooses her husband among men.
verses.griffith_verse: How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches? If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पत्तो जगार प्रत्यंचमत्ति शीर्ष्णा शिरः प्रति दधौ वरूथं ।आसीन ऊर्ध्वामुपसि क्षिणाति न्यङ्ङुत्तानामन्वेति भूमिं ॥
verses.transliteration: pattáḥ ǀ jagāra ǀ pratyáñcam ǀ atti ǀ śīrṣṇā́ ǀ śíraḥ ǀ práti ǀ dadhau ǀ várūtham ǀā́sīnaḥ ǀ ūrdhvā́m ǀ upási ǀ kṣiṇāti ǀ nyáṅ ǀ uttānā́m ǀ ánu ǀ eti ǀ bhū́mim ǁ
verses.english_translation: His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter. Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him.
verses.wilson_translation: He seizes (it) with his feet, he swallows it when it approaches him, he plural ces the head (of heaven) asa guard around his head; seated (above) he sends (his rays) upwards to the proximate heaven; he send themdownwards, on the outspread earth.
verses.griffith_verse: His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter. Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहन्नच्छायो अपलाशो अर्वा तस्थौ माता विषितो अत्ति गर्भः ।अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा नि दधे धेनुरूधः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhán ǀ acchāyáḥ ǀ apalāśáḥ ǀ árvā ǀ tastháu ǀ mātā́ ǀ ví-sitaḥ ǀ atti ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀanyásyāḥ ǀ vatsám ǀ rihatī́ ǀ mimāya ǀ káyā ǀ bhuvā́ ǀ ní ǀ dadhe ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding. Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder?
verses.wilson_translation: The great (sun), shadeless, undecaying, ever-moving, abides; the builder (of the world), who isliberated, the germ (of thethree worlds), eats (the oblations), fondling the offspring of another (mother), heconstructs (the quarters of the world); with what design has the cow offered her udder?
verses.griffith_verse: High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding. Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्त वीरासो अधरादुदायन्नष्टोत्तरात्तात्समजग्मिरंते ।नव पश्चातात्स्थिविमंत आयंदश प्राक्सानु वि तिरंत्यश्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ vīrā́saḥ ǀ adharā́t ǀ út ǀ āyan ǀ aṣṭá ǀ uttarā́ttāt ǀ sám ǀ ajagmiran ǀ té ǀnáva ǀ paścā́tāt ǀ sthivi-mántaḥ ǀ āyan ǀ dáśa ǀ prā́k ǀ sā́nu ǀ ví ǀ tiranti ǀ áśnaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together. Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o’er the rock's high ridges.
verses.wilson_translation: Seven sages sprang from the lower portion (of Indraas Prajāpati); eight were born from the upperportion; nine occupants of stations came from behind, and ten, genitive rated in the front, partaking of food,eightvālakhilyas; ninebhṛgus; tenaṅgirasas; or, seven Marutson Indra's right, eight on his left, nine behindhim, and ten in front].
verses.griffith_verse: Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together. Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o’er the rock's high ridges.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दशानामेकं कपिलं समानं तं हिन्वंति क्रतवे पार्याय ।गर्भं माता सुधितं वक्षणास्ववेनंतं तुषयंती बिभर्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: daśānā́m ǀ ékam ǀ kapilám ǀ samānám ǀ tám ǀ hinvanti ǀ krátave ǀ pā́ryāya ǀgárbham ǀ mātā́ ǀ sú-dhitam ǀ vakṣáṇāsu ǀ ávenantam ǀ tuṣáyantī ǀ bibharti ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose. The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not.
verses.wilson_translation: (The otheraṅgirasas) despatched one of the ten,Kapila, as equal (to the task) for the completion ofthe sacrifice; the gratified mother cherishes the embryo well-deposited in the waters, and not desirous of anabiding plural ce.
verses.griffith_verse: One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose. The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पीवानं मेषमपचंत वीरा न्युप्ता अक्षा अनु दीव आसन् ।द्वा धनुं बृहतीमप्स्वंतः पवित्रवंता चरतः पुनंता ॥
verses.transliteration: pī́vānam ǀ meṣám ǀ apacanta ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ ní-uptāḥ ǀ akṣā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ dīvé ǀ āsan ǀdvā́ ǀ dhánum ǀ bṛhatī́m ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáríti ǀ pavítra-vantā ǀ carataḥ ǀ punántā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted wether: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming. Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying.
verses.wilson_translation: The sages cooked a fat ram; they followed (prajāpati) in succession like dice thrown in gambling; two(of them), having the means of purification and becoming purified, proceed in the midst of the waters to (Prakṛti)the augmenter, to (Kapila) the implement of destruction.
verses.griffith_verse: The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted wether: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming. Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि क्रोशनासो विष्वंच आयन्पचाति नेमो नहि पक्षदर्धः ।अयं मे देवः सविता तदाह द्र्वन्न इद्वनवत्सर्पिरन्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ krośanā́saḥ ǀ víṣvañcaḥ ǀ āyan ǀ pácāti ǀ némaḥ ǀ nahí ǀ pákṣat ǀ ardháḥ ǀayám ǀ me ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ tát ǀ āha ǀ drú-annaḥ ǀ ít ǀ vanavat ǀ sarpíḥ-annaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other. To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter.
verses.wilson_translation: They (the Aṅgirasas) go in all directions calling (upon Prajāpati), half of them cook (their oblations),the other half cook not; this divine Savitāhas told me this-- (Agni), whose food is wood and ghī, serves(Prajāpati by means of oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other. To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानं ।सिषक्त्यर्यः प्र युगा जनानां सद्यः शिश्ना प्रमिनानो नवीयान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ grā́mam ǀ váhamānam ǀ ārā́t ǀ acakráyā ǀ svadháyā ǀ vártamānam ǀsísakti ǀ aryáḥ ǀ prá ǀ yugā́ ǀ jánānām ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ śiśnā́ ǀ pra-minānáḥ ǀ návīyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature. The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings.
verses.wilson_translation: I beheld the crowd coming from afar, moving of themselves without wheels; the lord of all, (Indra),regulates the seasons (worship of men), younger in vigour, destroying at once the herds of evil beings.
verses.griffith_verse: I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature. The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतौ मे गावौ प्रमरस्य युक्तौ मो षु प्र सेधीर्मुहुरिन्ममंधि ।आपश्चिदस्य वि नशंत्यर्थं सूरश्च मर्क उपरो बभूवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: etáu ǀ me ǀ gā́vau ǀ pra-marásya ǀ yuktáu ǀ mó íti ǀ sú ǀ prá ǀ sedhīḥ ǀ múhuḥ ǀ ít ǀ mamandhi ǀā́paḥ ǀ cit ǀ asya ǀ ví ǀ naśanti ǀ ártham ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ca ǀ markáḥ ǀ úparaḥ ǀ babhūvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger. The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.
verses.wilson_translation: Turn not back, but repeatedly praise these two yoked (steeds) of me the destroyer, which advance (tothe foe and to the sacrifice); the waters fulfil Indra's purpose and (so does) the all-cleansing sun, being (swift as)a cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger. The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं यो वज्रः पुरुधा विवृत्तोऽवः सूर्यस्य बृहतः पुरीषात् ।श्रव इदेना परो अन्यदस्ति तदव्यथी जरिमाणस्तरंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ yáḥ ǀ vájraḥ ǀ purudhā́ ǀ ví-vṛttaḥ ǀ aváḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ púrīṣāt ǀśrávaḥ ǀ ít ǀ enā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ anyát ǀ asti ǀ tát ǀ avyathī́ ǀ jarimā́ṇaḥ ǀ taranti ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Sūrya. Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow.
verses.wilson_translation: This is the thunderbolt which repeatedly falls (on those who are) below the orb of the vast sun; theworshippers easily cause this water (in the sun's orb) above which is differnet form that (in the clouds) to passthrough (the firmament).
verses.griffith_verse: This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Sūrya. Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृक्षेवृक्षे नियता मीमयद्गौस्ततो वयः प्र पतान्पूरुषादः ।अथेदं विश्वं भुवनं भयात इंद्राय सुन्वदृषये च शिक्षत् ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛkṣé-vṛkṣe ǀ ní-yatā ǀ mīmayat ǀ gáuḥ ǀ tátaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ prá ǀ patān ǀ puruṣa-ádaḥ ǀátha ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ bhayāte ǀ índrāya ǀ sunvát ǀ ṛ́ṣaye ǀ ca ǀ śíkṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying, Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Ṛṣi, is affrighted.
verses.wilson_translation: The bowstring fixed to each bow clangs loudly; then the man-destroying (shafts like) birds fall upon(the foes); and the whole of this world is alarmed, presentinglibations to Indra, and donations to the Ṛṣis.
verses.griffith_verse: Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying, Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Ṛṣi, is affrighted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवानां माने प्रथमा अतिष्ठन्कृंतत्रादेषामुपरा उदायन् ।त्रयस्तपंति पृथिवीमनूपा द्वा बृबूकं वहतः पुरीषं ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ mā́ne ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ atiṣṭhan ǀ kṛntátrāt ǀ eṣām ǀ úparāḥ ǀ út ǀ āyan ǀtráyaḥ ǀ tapanti ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ anūpā́ḥ ǀ dvā́ ǀ bṛ́būkam ǀ vahataḥ ǀ púrīṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the Gods’ mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later. Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture.
verses.wilson_translation: At the creation of the gods, the (clouds) stood first; from their division, the waters (of the rain) cameforth; the three divinities (Parjanya,VāyuandĀditya). Sowing in succession, warm the earth; two of them(Vāyu and Āditya) convey all-delighting water (to the sun's sphere).
verses.griffith_verse: In the Gods’ mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later. Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सा ते जीवातुरुत तस्य विद्धि मा स्मैतादृगप गूहः समर्ये ।आविः स्वः कृणुते गूहते बुसं स पादुरस्य निर्णिजो न मुच्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́ ǀ te ǀ jīvā́tuḥ ǀ utá ǀ tásya ǀ viddhi ǀ mā́ ǀ sma ǀ etādṛ́k ǀ ápa ǀ gūhaḥ ǀ sa-maryé ǀāvíḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ kṛṇuté ǀ gū́hate ǀ busám ǀ sáḥ ǀ pādúḥ ǀ asya ǀ niḥ-níjaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mucyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle. He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.
verses.wilson_translation: That your (divine) nature identified with the (sun) is the cause of life; and know such (solar form) of his(to be worthy of adoration) at the sacrifice; conceal nothing; that motion of him the all-cleansing (sun) makesmanifest the universe; it absorbs the moisture; it is never discontinued.
verses.griffith_verse: This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle. He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXVIII. Indra. Vasukra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither.So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling. Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth.That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma. Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest.Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited. Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward:The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood. How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty?Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing? Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole.I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me. Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit.Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vṛtra, and for the offerer oped with might the cow-stall. The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants.They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing. The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain.The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock. There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him.Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled. So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman.They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour. They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma.Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.

verses.sanskrit: विश्वो ह्यन्यो अरिराजगाम ममेदह श्वशुरो ना जगाम ।जक्षीयाद्धाना उत सोमं पपीयात्स्वाशितः पुनरस्तं जगायात् ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvaḥ ǀ hí ǀ anyáḥ ǀ aríḥ ǀ ā-jagā́ma ǀ máma ǀ ít ǀ áha ǀ śváśuraḥ ǀ ná ǀ ā́ ǀ jagāma ǀjakṣīyā́t ǀ dhānā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ sómam ǀ papīyāt ǀ sú-āśitaḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ jagāyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither. So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: (The wife of Vasukra speaks). Every other (divine) lord has come, but my father-in-law has notcome;may he eat the parched grain; and drink the Soma; when he is well-satisfied, may he return home.
verses.griffith_verse: Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither. So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स रोरुवद्वृषभस्तिग्मशृंगो वर्ष्मंतस्थौ वरिमन्ना पृथिव्याः ।विश्वेष्वेनं वृजनेषु पामि यो मे कुक्षी सुतसोमः पृणाति ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ róruvat ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ tigmá-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ várṣman ǀ tasthau ǀ váriman ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀvíśveṣu ǀ enam ǀ vṛjáneṣu ǀ pāmi ǀ yáḥ ǀ me ǀ kukṣī́ íti ǀ sutá-somaḥ ǀ pṛṇā́ti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth. That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks). (Indra) the showerer (of blessings), having not rays, abides roaring in the resoundingexpanse of the firmament; in all conflicts I defend him, (Vasukra), who, having effused the libation, fills my flanks.
verses.griffith_verse: Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth. That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्रिणा ते मंदिन इंद्र तूयान्त्सुन्वंति सोमान्पिबसि त्वमेषां ।पचंति ते वृषभाँ अत्सि तेषां पृक्षेण यन्मघवन्हूयमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádriṇā ǀ te ǀ mandínaḥ ǀ indra ǀ tū́yān ǀ sunvánti ǀ sómān ǀ píbasi ǀ tvám ǀ eṣām ǀpácanti ǀ te ǀ vṛṣabhā́n ǀ átsi ǀ téṣām ǀ pṛkṣéṇa ǀ yát ǀ magha-van ǀ hūyámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest. Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited.
verses.wilson_translation: (Vasukra speaks). Your worshippers express with the stone fast flowing exhilarating Somafor you, youdrink them; they roast bulls for you, you eat them, when you are invoked,Maghavan, to the sacrificial food.
verses.griffith_verse: Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest. Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं सु मे जरितरा चिकिद्धि प्रतीपं शापं नद्यो वहंति ।लोपाशः सिंहं प्रत्यंचमत्साः क्रोष्टा वराहं निरतक्त कक्षात् ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ sú ǀ me ǀ jaritaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cikiddhi ǀ prati-īpám ǀ śā́pam ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ vahanti ǀlopāśáḥ ǀ siṃhám ǀ pratyáñcam ǀ atsāríti ǀ kroṣṭā́ ǀ varāhám ǀ níḥ ǀ atakta ǀ kákṣāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward: The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood.
verses.wilson_translation: Overcomer of foes, (Indra) be cognizant of this my (power, whereby) rivers bear their waterbackwards, and the eater of cut (grass) confronts the lion, the jackal drives the wild boar from his lair.
verses.griffith_verse: Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward: The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कथा त एतदहमा चिकेतं गृत्सस्य पाकस्तवसो मनीषां ।त्वं नो विद्वाँ ऋतुथा वि वोचो यमर्धं ते मघवन्क्षेम्या धूः ॥
verses.transliteration: kathā́ ǀ te ǀ etát ǀ ahám ǀ ā́ ǀ ciketam ǀ gṛ́tsasya ǀ pā́kaḥ ǀ tavásaḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀtvám ǀ naḥ ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ ví ǀ vocaḥ ǀ yám ǀ árdham ǀ te ǀ magha-van ǀ kṣemyā́ ǀ dhū́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty? Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing?
verses.wilson_translation: How,Indra, should I yet immature (in understanding), be capable of comprehending this (your power,so as to render fitting) praise to those who are wise and powerful? Therefore, do you who are all-knowinginstruct us in fit season; the portion of your (praise) OMaghavan, which (we offer) is a burden easy to be bornṣ
verses.griffith_verse: How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty? Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा हि मां तवसं वर्धयंति दिवश्चिन्मे बृहत उत्तरा धूः ।पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशामि साकमशत्रुं हि मा जनिता जजान ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ hí ǀ mā́m ǀ tavásam ǀ vardháyanti ǀ diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ me ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ út-tarā ǀ dhū́ḥ ǀpurú ǀ sahásrā ǀ ní ǀ śiśāmi ǀ sākám ǀ aśatrúm ǀ hí ǀ mā ǀ jánitā ǀ jajā́na ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole. I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks). Since (your laudations) thus increase my strength, (let the praise of me) who ammighty, (rise) even higher than the heavens. I destroy at once many thousand (of foes), for the genitive rator (of all)has engendered me without an enemy.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole. I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा हि मां तवसं जज्ञुरुग्रं कर्मन्कर्मन्वृषणमिंद्र देवाः ।वधीं वृत्रं वज्रेण मंदसानोऽप व्रजं महिना दाशुषे वं ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ hí ǀ mā́m ǀ tavásam ǀ jajñúḥ ǀ ugrám ǀ kárman-karman ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ indra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀvádhīm ǀ vṛtrám ǀ vájreṇa ǀ mandasānáḥ ǀ ápa ǀ vrajám ǀ mahinā́ ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ vam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit. Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vṛtra, and for the offerer oped with might the cow-stall.
verses.wilson_translation: Since,Indra, the gods have known me to be powerful, fierce in every act, the showerer (of oblations);exulting I have slain Vṛtrawith your thunderbolt, and by my might have opened the clouds for the donor (ofoblations).
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit. Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vṛtra, and for the offerer oped with might the cow-stall.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवास आयन्परशूँरबिभ्रन्वना वृश्चंतो अभि विड्भिरायन् ।नि सुद्र्वं दधतो वक्षणासु यत्रा कृपीटमनु तद्दहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́saḥ ǀ āyan ǀ paraśū́n ǀ abibhran ǀ vánā ǀ vṛścántaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ viṭ-bhíḥ ǀ āyan ǀní ǀ su-drvám ǀ dádhataḥ ǀ vakṣáṇāsu ǀ yátra ǀ kṛ́pīṭam ǀ ánu ǀ tát ǀ dahanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants. They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods came, they bare their axes, clearing the woods, they came with men in front of the waters;depositing (the tree) of good wood in the belly (of the river); where the underwood (is), they burnt it up.
verses.griffith_verse: The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants. They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शशः क्षुरं प्रत्यंचं जगाराद्रिं लोगेन व्यभेदमारात् ।बृहंतं चिदृहते रंधयानि वयद्वत्सो वृषभं शूशुवानः ॥
verses.transliteration: śaśáḥ ǀ kṣurám ǀ pratyáñcam ǀ jagāra ǀ ádrim ǀ logéna ǀ ví ǀ abhedam ǀ ārā́t ǀbṛhántam ǀ cit ǀ ṛhaté ǀ randhayāni ǀ váyat ǀ vatsáḥ ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ śū́śuvānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain. The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock.
verses.wilson_translation: (Vasukra speaks). The hare graps the assailing beast of prey; with a clod of clay I cleave the distant(mountain); I can compel the great to submit to the small; swelling (with courage) the calf attacks the bulḷ
verses.griffith_verse: The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain. The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुपर्ण इत्था नखमा सिषायावरुद्धः परिपदं न सिंहः ।निरुद्धश्चिन्महिषस्तर्ष्यावान्गोधा तस्मा अयथं कर्षदेतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: su-parṇáḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ nakhám ǀ ā́ ǀ sisāya ǀ áva-ruddhaḥ ǀ pari-pádam ǀ ná ǀ siṃháḥ ǀni-ruddháḥ ǀ cit ǀ mahiṣáḥ ǀ tarṣyā́-vān ǀ godhā́ ǀ tásmai ǀ ayátham ǀ karṣat ǀ etát ǁ
verses.english_translation: There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him. Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled.
verses.wilson_translation: The hawk has fastened her claw in heaven; a lion confined (in a cage) plural ces one foot over the otheṛAs a captive buffalo (is) thirsty, (so)Indrathirsted for the Soma, Ga-yatrī brought it to him easily (from heaven).
verses.griffith_verse: There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him. Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेभ्यो गोधा अयथं कर्षदेतद्ये ब्रह्मणः प्रतिपीयंत्यन्नैः ।सिम उक्ष्णोऽवसृष्टाँ अदंति स्वयं बलानि तन्वः शृणानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tébhyaḥ ǀ godhā́ḥ ǀ ayátham ǀ karṣat ǀ etát ǀ yé ǀ brahmáṇaḥ ǀ prati-pī́yanti ǀ ánnaiḥ ǀsimáḥ ǀ ukṣṇáḥ ǀ ava-sṛṣṭā́n ǀ adanti ǀ svayám ǀ bálāni ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śṛṇānā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman. They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Gāyatrīdrew it away without difficulty, for the good of those (gods) who, (satisfied) with the viandsof Indra, retaliate the injuries (of the enemies of the gods); they devour all the sprinkling (Somalibations) left (by Indra), spontaneously destroying the armies and bodies (of the enemy).
verses.griffith_verse: So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman. They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एते शमीभिः सुशमी अभूवन्ये हिन्विरे तन्वः सोम उक्थैः ।नृवद्वदन्नुप नो माहि वाजांदिवि श्रवो दधिषे नाम वीरः ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ śámībhiḥ ǀ su-śámī ǀ abhūvan ǀ yé ǀ hinviré ǀ tanváḥ ǀ sóme ǀ uktháiḥ ǀnṛ-vát ǀ vádan ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ māhi ǀ vā́jān ǀ diví ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ nā́ma ǀ vīráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma. Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.
verses.wilson_translation: They have been sanctified by holy rites, who have fostered their bodies with prayers, at the Soma(sacrifice); speaking like a man, grant us food, you possess in heaven name and fame as a hero.
verses.griffith_verse: They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma. Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift Pair, have been roused by clear laudation,Whose Herald-Priest through many days is Indra, earth's Guardian, Friend of men, the best of Heroes. May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero!Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa. What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed through our doors to songs, for thou art mighty.Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer. Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us?As a true Friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us. Speed happily those, as Sūrya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses;Men who present, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises. Thine are two measures, Indra, wide-wellmeted, heaven for thy majesty, earth for thy wisdom.Here for thy choice are Somas mixed with butter: may the sweet meath be pleasant for thy drinking. They have poured out a bowl to him, to Indra, full of sweet juice, for faithful is his bounty.O'er earth's expanse hath he grown great by wisdom, the Friend of man, and by heroic exploits. Indra hath conquered in his wars, the Mighty: men strive in multitudes to win his friendship.Ascend thy chariot as it were in battle, which thou shalt drive to us with gracious favour.

verses.sanskrit: वने न वा यो न्यधायि चाकंछुचिर्वां स्तोमो भुरणावजीगः ।यस्येदिंद्रः पुरुदिनेषु होता नृणां नर्यो नृतमः क्षपावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: váne ǀ ná ǀ vā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ní ǀ adhāyi ǀ cākán ǀ śúciḥ ǀ vām ǀ stómaḥ ǀ bhuraṇau ǀ ajīgaríti ǀyásya ǀ ít ǀ índraḥ ǀ puru-díneṣu ǀ hótā ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀ náryaḥ ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ kṣapā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift Pair, have been roused by clear laudation, Whose Herald-Priest through many days is Indra, earth's Guardian, Friend of men, the best of Heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: As (the bird) who deposits its young (in its nest) in the tree (is) eagerly looking around, so you bearers(Aśvins) your pure praise (ever) keeps you awake; (that praise) of which Indrahas for many days been theinvoker, (Indra) the friend of man, the manliest of men, (to whom the Soma) is offered at night.
verses.griffith_verse: As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift Pair, have been roused by clear laudation, Whose Herald-Priest through many days is Indra, earth's Guardian, Friend of men, the best of Heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते अस्या उषसः प्रापरस्या नृतौ स्याम नृतमस्य नृणां ।अनु त्रिशोकः शतमावहन्नॄन्कुत्सेन रथो यो असत्ससवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ prá ǀ áparasyāḥ ǀ nṛtáu ǀ syāma ǀ nṛ́-tamasya ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀánu ǀ tri-śókaḥ ǀ śatám ǀ ā́ ǀ avahat ǀ nṝ́n ǀ kútsena ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásat ǀ sasa-vā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero! Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be prosperous at the coming of the present or of any future dawn, (through the adoration) ofyou, the chief leader of men; through your favour Triśokaobtained a hundred followers; the chariot which wascommon to him and you was acquired by Kutsa.
verses.griffith_verse: May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero! Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कस्ते मद इंद्र रंत्यो भूद्दुरो गिरो अभ्युग्रो वि धाव ।कद्वाहो अर्वागुप मा मनीषा आ त्वा शक्यामुपमं राधो अन्नैः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ te ǀ mádaḥ ǀ indra ǀ rántyaḥ ǀ bhūt ǀ dúraḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ugráḥ ǀ ví ǀ dhāva ǀkát ǀ vā́haḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ úpa ǀ mā ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ śakyām ǀ upa-mám ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ ánnaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed through our doors to songs, for thou art mighty. Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer.
verses.wilson_translation: What sort of exhilaration,Indra, is agreeable to you? You who are powerful hasten to the doors (of thesacrificial chamber) to our praises; when will the Somabe present? (When will) intelligence (come) to me? When,having propitiated you, may I acquire wealth and food?
verses.griffith_verse: What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed through our doors to songs, for thou art mighty. Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कदु द्युम्नमिंद्र त्वावतो नॄन्कया धिया करसे कन्न आगन् ।मित्रो न सत्य उरुगाय भृत्या अन्ने समस्य यदसन्मनीषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: kát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dyumnám ǀ indra ǀ tvā́-vataḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ káyā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ karase ǀ kát ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agan ǀmitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ satyáḥ ǀ uru-gāya ǀ bhṛtyái ǀ ánne ǀ samasya ǀ yát ǀ ásan ǀ manīṣā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us? As a true Friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Indra, (having partaken of) our oblation, and by what sacred rite, will you render menresembling you? When will you bring them to us? You, who are widely renowned, are to us like a true friend,(attentive) for our support, when the minds of all were (anxious) for food.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us? As a true Friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेरय सूरो अर्थं न पारं ये अस्य कामं जनिधा इव ग्मन् ।गिरश्च ये ते तुविजात पूर्वीर्नर इंद्र प्रतिशिक्षंत्यन्नैः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ īraya ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ártham ǀ ná ǀ pārám ǀ yé ǀ asya ǀ kā́mam ǀ janidhā́ḥ-iva ǀ gmán ǀgíraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ tuvi-jāta ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀ indra ǀ prati-śíkṣanti ǀ ánnaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Speed happily those, as Sūrya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses; Men who present, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises.
verses.wilson_translation: As the sun (brings) the ascetic, do you bring to the end (of existence) (your worshippers), who satisfyyour desire (fo the Soma), as husbands (the desire of their wives); and who (being) leaders of rites, multiform Indra, offer to you ancient praises with (sacrificial) viands.
verses.griffith_verse: Speed happily those, as Sūrya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses; Men who present, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मात्रे नु ते सुमिते इंद्र पूर्वी द्यौर्मज्मना पृथिवी काव्येन ।वराय ते घृतवंतः सुतासः स्वाद्मन्भवंतु पीतये मधूनि ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́tre íti ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ súmite íti sú-mite ǀ indra ǀ pūrvī́ íti ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ majmánā ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ kā́vyena ǀvárāya ǀ te ǀ ghṛtá-vantaḥ ǀ sutā́saḥ ǀ svā́dman ǀ bhavantu ǀ pītáye ǀ mádhūni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine are two measures, Indra, wide-wellmeted, heaven for thy majesty, earth for thy wisdom. Here for thy choice are Somas mixed with butter: may the sweet meath be pleasant for thy drinking.
verses.wilson_translation: By your overwhelming energy,Indra, the vast heaven and earth, the measurers (of all), have beenquickly constructed; may the Soma-libations mixed with ghī be acceptable (to you) who are most excellent; (maythe oblations be) sweet for your drinking.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine are two measures, Indra, wide-wellmeted, heaven for thy majesty, earth for thy wisdom. Here for thy choice are Somas mixed with butter: may the sweet meath be pleasant for thy drinking.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ मध्वो अस्मा असिचन्नमत्रमिंद्राय पूर्णं स हि सत्यराधाः ।स वावृधे वरिमन्ना पृथिव्या अभि क्रत्वा नर्यः पौंस्यैश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ asmai ǀ asican ǀ ámatram ǀ índrāya ǀ pūrṇám ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ satyá-rādhāḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ váriman ǀ ā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ krátvā ǀ náryaḥ ǀ páuṃsyaiḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: They have poured out a bowl to him, to Indra, full of sweet juice, for faithful is his bounty. O'er earth's expanse hath he grown great by wisdom, the Friend of man, and by heroic exploits.
verses.wilson_translation: (The worshippers) have poured out the vessel full of the sweet (Soma) (into the fire) for that Indra, forhe is true (to his promises) of wealth; Indra, the friend of man, (distinguished) by his actions, and his prowess, ismagnified throughout the expanse of the firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: They have poured out a bowl to him, to Indra, full of sweet juice, for faithful is his bounty. O'er earth's expanse hath he grown great by wisdom, the Friend of man, and by heroic exploits.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्यानळिंद्रः पृतनाः स्वोजा आस्मै यतंते सख्याय पूर्वीः ।आ स्मा रथं न पृतनासु तिष्ठ यं भद्रया सुमत्या चोदयासे ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ ānaṭ ǀ índraḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ su-ójāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ asmai ǀ yatante ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀā́ ǀ sma ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ yám ǀ bhadráyā ǀ su-matyā́ ǀ codáyāse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra hath conquered in his wars, the Mighty: men strive in multitudes to win his friendship. Ascend thy chariot as it were in battle, which thou shalt drive to us with gracious favour.
verses.wilson_translation: The powerful Indrareaches the hosts (of the enemy), the mightiest (hosts) exert themselves to obtainhis friendship; ascend, Indra, that chariot which you direct with favourable intent (to our sacrifice), as a chariot(which you mount) against the armies (of the foe).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra hath conquered in his wars, the Mighty: men strive in multitudes to win his friendship. Ascend thy chariot as it were in battle, which thou shalt drive to us with gracious favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXX. Waters.
hymns.anukramani: १५ कवष ऐलूषः।आपः, अपां न पात् वा। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As ’twere with swift exertion of the spirit, let the priest speed to the celestial Waters,The glorious food of Varuṇa and Mitra. To him who spreadeth far this laud I offer. Adhvaryus, he ye ready with oblations,, and come with longing to the longing Waters,Down on which looks the. purple-tinted Eagle. Pour ye that flowing wave this day, deft-handed. Go to the reservoir, O ye Adhvaryus worship the Waters’ Child with your oblations.A consecrated wave he now will give you, so press for him the Soma rich in sweetness. He who shines bright in floods, unfed with fuel, whom sages worship at their sacrifices:Give waters rich in sweets, Child of the Waters, even those which gave heroic might to Indra: Those in which Soma joys and is delighted, as a young man with fair and pleasant damsels.Go thou unto those Waters, O Adhvaryu, and purify with herbs what thou infusest. So maidens bow before the youthful gallant who comes with love to them who yearn to meet him.In heart accordant and in wish one-minded are the Adhvaryus and the heavenly Waters. He who made room for you when fast imprisoned, who freed you from the mighty imprecation,—Even to that Indra send the meath-rich current, the wave that gratifies the Gods, O Waters. Send forth to him the meath-rich wave, O Rivers, which is your offspring and a well of sweetness,Oil-balmed, to be implored at sacrifices. Ye wealthy Waters, hear mine invocation. Send forth the rapture-giving wave, O Rivers, which Indra drinks, which sets the Twain in motion;The well that springeth from the clouds, desirous, that wandereth triple-formed, distilling transport. These winding Streams which with their double current, like cattle-raiders, seek the lower pastures,—Waters which dwell together, thrive together, Queens, Mothers of the world, these, Ṛṣi, honour. Send forth our sacrifice with holy worship send forth the hymn and prayer for gain of riches.For need of sacrifice disclose the udder. Give gracious hearing to our call, O Waters. For, wealthy Waters, ye control all treasures: ye bring auspicious intellect and Amṛta.Ye are the Queens of independent riches Sarasvatī give full life to the singer! When I behold the Waters coming hither, carrying with them milk and mcath and butter,Bearing the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra, they harmonize in spirit with Adhvaryus. Rich, they are come with wealth for living beings, O friends, Adhvaryus, seat them in their places.Seat them on holy grass, ye Soma-bringers in harmony with the Offspring of the Waters. Now to this grass are come the longing Waters: the Pious Ones are seated at our worship.Adbvaryus, press the Soma juice for Indra so will the service of the Gods be easy.

verses.sanskrit: प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुरेत्वपो अच्छा मनसो न प्रयुक्ति ।महीं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धासिं पृथुज्रयसे रीरधा सुवृक्तिं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ bráhmaṇe ǀ gātúḥ ǀ etu ǀ apáḥ ǀ áccha ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ prá-yukti ǀmahī́m ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhāsím ǀ pṛthu-jráyase ǀ rīradha ǀ su-vṛktím ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ’twere with swift exertion of the spirit, let the priest speed to the celestial Waters, The glorious food of Varuṇa and Mitra. To him who spreadeth far this laud I offer.
verses.wilson_translation: (Honoured) by adoration, let the advancing Somaapproach the celestial waters like the celerity of themind; offer abundant (sacrificial) food, and perfect praise for the sake of Mitraand Varuṇa, and for (Indra) therapid mover.
verses.griffith_verse: As ’twere with swift exertion of the spirit, let the priest speed to the celestial Waters, The glorious food of Varuṇa and Mitra. To him who spreadeth far this laud I offer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्यवो हविष्मंतो हि भूताच्छाप इतोशतीरुशंतः ।अव याश्चष्टे अरुणः सुपर्णस्तमास्यध्वमूर्मिमद्या सुहस्ताः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhvaryavaḥ ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ hí ǀ bhūtá ǀ áccha ǀ apáḥ ǀ ita ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ uśantaḥ ǀáva ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ cáṣṭe ǀ aruṇáḥ ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ tám ǀ ā́ ǀ asyadhvam ǀ ūrmím ǀ adyá ǀ su-hastāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Adhvaryus, he ye ready with oblations,, and come with longing to the longing Waters, Down on which looks the. purple-tinted Eagle. Pour ye that flowing wave this day, deft-handed.
verses.wilson_translation: Priests, since you are charged with the libation, desiring (to present it), proceed to the waters desiring(to receive it), to those (waters) which the red hawk beholds descending (from the clouds); do you,dextrous-handed (priests), cast today that flood (of Soma) into (the consecrated water).
verses.griffith_verse: Adhvaryus, he ye ready with oblations,, and come with longing to the longing Waters, Down on which looks the. purple-tinted Eagle. Pour ye that flowing wave this day, deft-handed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्यवोऽप इता समुद्रमपां नपातं हविषा यजध्वं ।स वो दददूर्मिमद्या सुपूतं तस्मै सोमं मधुमंतं सुनोत ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhvaryavaḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ita ǀ samudrám ǀ apā́m ǀ nápātam ǀ havíṣā ǀ yajadhvam ǀsáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ dadat ǀ ūrmím ǀ adyá ǀ sú-pūtam ǀ tásmai ǀ sómam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ sunota ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go to the reservoir, O ye Adhvaryus worship the Waters’ Child with your oblations. A consecrated wave he now will give you, so press for him the Soma rich in sweetness.
verses.wilson_translation: Go, priests, to the water, to the reservoir; worship the grandson of the waters with oblations; may hetoday give you the consecrated water, and do you pour forth to him the sweet-flavoured Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Go to the reservoir, O ye Adhvaryus worship the Waters’ Child with your oblations. A consecrated wave he now will give you, so press for him the Soma rich in sweetness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्स्वंतर्यं विप्रास ईळते अध्वरेषु ।अपां नपान्मधुमतीरपो दा याभिरिंद्रो वावृधे वीर्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ anidhmáḥ ǀ dī́dayat ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáḥ ǀ yám ǀ víprāsaḥ ǀ ī́ḷate ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀápām ǀ napāt ǀ mádhu-matīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ dāḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vavṛdhé ǀ vīryā́ya ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who shines bright in floods, unfed with fuel, whom sages worship at their sacrifices: Give waters rich in sweets, Child of the Waters, even those which gave heroic might to Indra:
verses.wilson_translation: (He) who shines, without fuel, in the midst of the waters, he whom the pious worship at sacrifices,grandson of the waters, give us those sweet waters by which (mixed with the Soma),Indrais elevated toheroism.
verses.griffith_verse: He who shines bright in floods, unfed with fuel, whom sages worship at their sacrifices: Give waters rich in sweets, Child of the Waters, even those which gave heroic might to Indra:
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याभिः सोमो मोदते हर्षते च कल्याणीभिर्युवतिभिर्न मर्यः ।ता अध्वर्यो अपो अच्छा परेहि यदासिंचा ओषधीभिः पुनीतात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́bhiḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ módate ǀ hárṣate ǀ ca ǀ kalyāṇī́bhiḥ ǀ yuvatí-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ máryaḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ adhvaryo íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ áccha ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ yát ǀ ā-siñcā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhībhiḥ ǀ punītāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those in which Soma joys and is delighted, as a young man with fair and pleasant damsels. Go thou unto those Waters, O Adhvaryu, and purify with herbs what thou infusest.
verses.wilson_translation: Those waters with which Somasports and delights as a man (sports) with elegant young damsels; doyou, priest, approach to obtain them; when you sprinkle them (in libation), purify (them with the filter) along withthe plural nts.
verses.griffith_verse: Those in which Soma joys and is delighted, as a young man with fair and pleasant damsels. Go thou unto those Waters, O Adhvaryu, and purify with herbs what thou infusest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवेद्यूने युवतयो नमंत यदीमुशन्नुशतीरेत्यच्छ ।सं जानते मनसा सं चिकित्रेऽध्वर्यवो धिषणापश्च देवीः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ ít ǀ yū́ne ǀ yuvatáyaḥ ǀ namanta ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ uśán ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ éti ǀ áccha ǀsám ǀ jānate ǀ mánasā ǀ sám ǀ cikitre ǀ adhvaryávaḥ ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ca ǀ devī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So maidens bow before the youthful gallant who comes with love to them who yearn to meet him. In heart accordant and in wish one-minded are the Adhvaryus and the heavenly Waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily as young damsels welcome a youth when desiring (them), he comes to them desiring (him), sothe priests and their praise and the divine waters agree in mind and contemplate (their mutual assistance).
verses.griffith_verse: So maidens bow before the youthful gallant who comes with love to them who yearn to meet him. In heart accordant and in wish one-minded are the Adhvaryus and the heavenly Waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वो वृताभ्यो अकृणोदु लोकं यो वो मह्या अभिशस्तेरमुंचत् ।तस्मा इंद्राय मधुमंतमूर्मिं देवमादनं प्र हिणोतनापः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ vṛtā́bhyaḥ ǀ ákṛṇot ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ mahyā́ḥ ǀ abhí-śasteḥ ǀ ámuñcat ǀtásmai ǀ índrāya ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ūrmím ǀ deva-mā́danam ǀ prá ǀ hiṇotana ǀ āpaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who made room for you when fast imprisoned, who freed you from the mighty imprecation,— Even to that Indra send the meath-rich current, the wave that gratifies the Gods, O Waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Present, waters, the sweet-flavoured god-exhilarating mixture to that Indrawho has made an issue foryou when enveloped (by the clouds); who has liberated you from a great calamity.
verses.griffith_verse: He who made room for you when fast imprisoned, who freed you from the mighty imprecation,— Even to that Indra send the meath-rich current, the wave that gratifies the Gods, O Waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रास्मै हिनोत मधुमंतमूर्मिं गर्भो यो वः सिंधवो मध्व उत्सः ।घृतपृष्ठमीड्यमध्वरेष्वापो रेवतीः शृणुता हवं मे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ asmai ǀ hinota ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ ūrmím ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ sindhavaḥ ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ útsaḥ ǀghṛtá-pṛṣṭham ǀ ī́ḍyam ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ revatīḥ ǀ śṛṇutá ǀ hávam ǀ me ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send forth to him the meath-rich wave, O Rivers, which is your offspring and a well of sweetness, Oil-balmed, to be implored at sacrifices. Ye wealthy Waters, hear mine invocation.
verses.wilson_translation: Send forth, rivers, the sweet-flavoured beverage to him who is your germ, a well of the sweet (Soma),the Soma which is mixed with butter adorable at sacrifices; hear, opulent waters my invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: Send forth to him the meath-rich wave, O Rivers, which is your offspring and a well of sweetness, Oil-balmed, to be implored at sacrifices. Ye wealthy Waters, hear mine invocation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं सिंधवो मत्सरमिंद्रपानमूर्मिं प्र हेत य उभे इयर्ति ।मदच्युतमौशानं नभोजां परि त्रितंतुं विचरंतमुत्सं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ sindhavaḥ ǀ matsarám ǀ indra-pā́nam ǀ ūrmím ǀ prá ǀ heta ǀ yáḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ íyarti ǀmada-cyútam ǀ auśānám ǀ nabhaḥ-jā́m ǀ pári ǀ tri-tántum ǀ vi-cárantam ǀ útsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send forth the rapture-giving wave, O Rivers, which Indra drinks, which sets the Twain in motion; The well that springeth from the clouds, desirous, that wandereth triple-formed, distilling transport.
verses.wilson_translation: Send, rivers, (to our sacrifice), that exhilarating wave the Somaof Indra, which sends us both (kinds offruit), exciting exhilaration, desirous (of mixing with the Soma). genitive rated in the firmament, spreading through thethree (worlds), flowing (amidst the vessels of sacrifices), a well (of satisfaction to the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Send forth the rapture-giving wave, O Rivers, which Indra drinks, which sets the Twain in motion; The well that springeth from the clouds, desirous, that wandereth triple-formed, distilling transport.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आवर्वृततीरध नु द्विधारा गोषुयुधो न नियवं चरंतीः ।ऋषे जनित्रीर्भुवनस्य पत्नीरपो वंदस्व सवृधः सयोनीः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-várvṛtatīḥ ǀ ádha ǀ nú ǀ dvi-dhā́rāḥ ǀ goṣu-yúdhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ni-yavám ǀ cárantīḥ ǀṛ́ṣe ǀ jánitrīḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ vandasva ǀ sa-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ sá-yonīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These winding Streams which with their double current, like cattle-raiders, seek the lower pastures,— Waters which dwell together, thrive together, Queens, Mothers of the world, these, Ṛṣi, honour.
verses.griffith_verse: These winding Streams which with their double current, like cattle-raiders, seek the lower pastures,— Waters which dwell together, thrive together, Queens, Mothers of the world, these, Ṛṣi, honour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयज्या हिनोत ब्रह्म सनये धनानां ।ऋतस्य योग�� वि ष्यध्वमूधः श्रुष्टीवरीर्भूतनास्मभ्यमापः ॥
verses.transliteration: hinóta ǀ naḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǀ hinóta ǀ bráhma ǀ sanáye ǀ dhánānām ǀṛtásya ǀ yóge ǀ ví ǀ syadhvam ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ śruṣṭī-várīḥ ǀ bhūtana ǀ asmábhyam ǀ āpaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send forth our sacrifice with holy worship send forth the hymn and prayer for gain of riches. For need of sacrifice disclose the udder. Give gracious hearing to our call, O Waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Direct our sacrifice to the worship of the gods; direct our adoration to the acquisition of wealth; openthe udder on the occasion of (this) rite; be to us, waters, the givers of felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: Send forth our sacrifice with holy worship send forth the hymn and prayer for gain of riches. For need of sacrifice disclose the udder. Give gracious hearing to our call, O Waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्वः क्रतुं च भद्रं बिभृथामृतं च ।रायश्च स्थ स्वपत्यस्य पत्नीः सरस्वती तद्गृणते वयो धात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ revatīḥ ǀ kṣáyatha ǀ hí ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ krátum ǀ ca ǀ bhadrám ǀ bibhṛthá ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ca ǀrāyáḥ ǀ ca ǀ sthá ǀ su-apatyásya ǀ pátnīḥ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ tát ǀ gṛṇaté ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, wealthy Waters, ye control all treasures: ye bring auspicious intellect and Amṛta. Ye are the Queens of independent riches Sarasvatī give full life to the singer!
verses.wilson_translation: Opulent waters, you rule over riches; you support good fortune, pious rites, and immortality; you arethe protectresses of wealth and of offspring; may Sarasvatībestow all this opulence on him who praises you.
verses.griffith_verse: For, wealthy Waters, ye control all treasures: ye bring auspicious intellect and Amṛta. Ye are the Queens of independent riches Sarasvatī give full life to the singer!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति यदापो अदृश्रमायतीर्घृतं पयांसि बिभ्रतीर्मधूनि ।अध्वर्युभिर्मनसा संविदाना इंद्राय सोमं सुषुतं भरंतीः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ yát ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ádṛśram ǀ ā-yatī́ḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ páyāṃsi ǀ bíbhratīḥ ǀ mádhūni ǀadhvaryú-bhiḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ sam-vidānā́ḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ sómam ǀ sú-sutam ǀ bhárantīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When I behold the Waters coming hither, carrying with them milk and mcath and butter, Bearing the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra, they harmonize in spirit with Adhvaryus.
verses.wilson_translation: I behold you, waters, coming to (the sacrifice), conveying the butter, the water, the sweet (Soma);conversing mentally with the priests, and bringing the well-effused Soma for Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: When I behold the Waters coming hither, carrying with them milk and mcath and butter, Bearing the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra, they harmonize in spirit with Adhvaryus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एमा अग्मन्रेवतीर्जीवधन्या अध्वर्यवः सादयता सखायः ।नि बर्हिषि धत्तन सोम्यासोऽपां नप्त्रा संविदानास एनाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ agman ǀ revátīḥ ǀ jīvá-dhanyāḥ ǀ ádhvaryavaḥ ǀ sādáyata ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀní ǀ barhíṣi ǀ dhattana ǀ somyāsaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ náptrā ǀ sam-vidānā́saḥ ǀ enāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich, they are come with wealth for living beings, O friends, Adhvaryus, seat them in their places. Seat them on holy grass, ye Soma-bringers in harmony with the Offspring of the Waters.
verses.wilson_translation: These opulent and life-sustaining (waters) have come (to my sacrifice); friendly priests, make them sitdown; plural ce them on the sacred grass, you offerers of the Soma, conversing with the grandson of the waters.
verses.griffith_verse: Rich, they are come with wealth for living beings, O friends, Adhvaryus, seat them in their places. Seat them on holy grass, ye Soma-bringers in harmony with the Offspring of the Waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आग्मन्नाप उशतीर्बर्हिरेदं न्यध्वरे असदंदेवयंतीः ।अध्वर्यवः सुनुतेंद्राय सोममभूदु वः सुशका देवयज्या ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ agman ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ idám ǀ ní ǀ adhvaré ǀ asadan ǀ deva-yántīḥ ǀádhvaryavaḥ ǀ sunutá ǀ índrāya ǀ sómam ǀ ábhūt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vaḥ ǀ su-śákā ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now to this grass are come the longing Waters: the Pious Ones are seated at our worship. Adbvaryus, press the Soma juice for Indra so will the service of the Gods be easy.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters desiring (it) have come to this sacred grass, and wishing to satisfy the gods, have satdown at our sacrifice; express priests, the Somafor Indrra; for you the worship of the gods is easy.
verses.griffith_verse: Now to this grass are come the longing Waters: the Pious Ones are seated at our worship. Adbvaryus, press the Soma juice for Indra so will the service of the Gods be easy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY benediction of the Gods approach us, holy, to aid us with all rapid succours.Therewith may we be happily befriended, and pass triumphant over all our troubles. A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order,Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit. The hymn is formed, poured are the allotted portions: as to a ford friends come unto the Wondrous.We have obtained the power of case and comfort, we haVe become acquainted, with Immortals. Pleased be the Eternal Lord who loves the household with this man whom God Savitar created.May Bhaga Aryaman grace him with cattle: may he appear to him, and be, delightful. Like the Dawns' dwelling-place be this assembly, where in their might men rich in food have gathered.Striving to share the praises of this singer. To us come strengthening and effectual riches! This Bull's most gracious far-extended favour existed first of all in full abundance.By his support they are maintained in common who in the Asura's mansion dwell together. What was the tree, what wood, in sooth, produced it, from which they fashioned forth the Earth and Heaven?These Twain stand fast and wax not old for ever: these have sung praise to many a day and morning. Not only here is this: more is beyond us. He is the Bull, the Heaven's and Earth's supporter.With power divine he makes his skin a filter, when the Bay Coursers bear him on as Sūrya. He passes o’er the broad earth like a Stega: he penetrates the world as Wind the mist-cloud.He, balmed with oil, near Varuṇa and Mitra, like Agni in the wood, hath shot forth splendour. When suddenly called the cow that erst was barren, she, self-protected, ended all her troubles.Earth, when the first son sprang from sire and mother, cast up the gami, that which men were seeking. To Nṛṣad's son they gave the name of Kainva, and he the brown-hued courser won the treasure.For him dark-coloured streamed the shining udder: none made it swell for him. Thus Order willed it.

verses.sanskrit: आ नो देवानामुप वेतु शंसो विश्वेभिस्तुरैरवसे यजत्रः ।तेभिर्वयं सुषखायो भवेम तरंतो विश्वा दुरिता स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ úpa ǀ vetu ǀ śáṃsaḥ ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ turáiḥ ǀ ávase ǀ yájatraḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ vayám ǀ su-sakhā́yaḥ ǀ bhavema ǀ tárantaḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY benediction of the Gods approach us, holy, to aid us with all rapid succours. Therewith may we be happily befriended, and pass triumphant over all our troubles.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, who is to be praised by us, his worshippers, and to be adored, (Indra), come with all his swift(Maruts), for our protection, may we be excellent friends with them; may we be freed from all sins.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY benediction of the Gods approach us, holy, to aid us with all rapid succours. Therewith may we be happily befriended, and pass triumphant over all our troubles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परि चिन्मर्तो द्रविणं ममन्यादृतस्य पथा नमसा विवासेत् ।उत स्वेन क्रतुना सं वदेत श्रेयांसं दक्षं मनसा जगृभ्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: pári ǀ cit ǀ mártaḥ ǀ dráviṇam ǀ mamanyāt ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pathā́ ǀ námasā ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāset ǀutá ǀ svéna ǀ krátunā ǀ sám ǀ vadeta ǀ śréyāṃsam ǀ dákṣam ǀ mánasā ǀ jagṛbhyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order, Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: Let a mortal be ever desirous of affluence, (having acquired it), let him worship with oblations on thepath of the sacrifice; and let him with his own intellect meditate upon (the gods); let him grasp with his mind thebest and most mighty (of the universal deities).
verses.griffith_verse: A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order, Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधायि धीतिरससृग्रमंशास्तीर्थे न दस्ममुप यंत्यूमाः ।अभ्यानश्म सुवितस्य शूषं नवेदसो अमृतानामभूम ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhāyi ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ ásasṛgram ǀ áṃśāḥ ǀ tīrthé ǀ ná ǀ dasmám ǀ úpa ǀ yanti ǀ ū́māḥ ǀabhí ǀ ānaśma ǀ suvitásya ǀ śūṣám ǀ návedasaḥ ǀ amṛ́tānām ǀ abhūma ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hymn is formed, poured are the allotted portions: as to a ford friends come unto the Wondrous. We have obtained the power of case and comfort, we haVe become acquainted, with Immortals.
verses.wilson_translation: The sacrifice has been prepared; the invigorating portions (of thhe oblation) approach the beautiful(god) of excellent birth, as (the waters) at a holy spot (approach the gods); may we obtain the happiness ofheaven; may we have a real knowledge of the immortals.
verses.griffith_verse: The hymn is formed, poured are the allotted portions: as to a ford friends come unto the Wondrous. We have obtained the power of case and comfort, we haVe become acquainted, with Immortals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नित्यश्चाकन्यात्स्वपतिर्दमूना यस्मा उ देवः सविता जजान ।भगो वा गोभिरर्यमेमनज्यात्सो अस्मै चारुश्छदयदुत स्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: nítyaḥ ǀ cākanyāt ǀ svá-patiḥ ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ yásmai ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ jajā́na ǀbhágaḥ ǀ vā ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ īm ǀ anajyāt ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ chadayat ǀ utá ǀ syāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pleased be the Eternal Lord who loves the household with this man whom God Savitar created. May Bhaga Aryaman grace him with cattle: may he appear to him, and be, delightful.
verses.wilson_translation: May the eternal (Prajāpati), the lord of wealth, of genitive rous mind, be willing to bestow (benefits onhim) to whom the divine Savitāhas given birth; may Bhaga(induced) by (our) praises, and the divine Aryamanunfold (future rewards); or may some (other) gracious (divinity) be inclined to favour this (instrumental tutor of the rite).
verses.griffith_verse: Pleased be the Eternal Lord who loves the household with this man whom God Savitar created. May Bhaga Aryaman grace him with cattle: may he appear to him, and be, delightful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं सा भूया उषसामिव क्षा यद्ध क्षुमंतः शवसा समायन् ।अस्य स्तुतिं जरितुर्भिक्षमाणा आ नः शग्मास उप यंतु वाजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ sā́ ǀ bhūyāḥ ǀ uṣásām-iva ǀ kṣā́ḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ kṣu-mántaḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ sam-ā́yan ǀasyá ǀ stutím ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ bhíkṣamāṇāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ śagmā́saḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yantu ǀ vā́jāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like the Dawns' dwelling-place be this assembly, where in their might men rich in food have gathered. Striving to share the praises of this singer. To us come strengthening and effectual riches!
verses.wilson_translation: May this (our praise) be accessible like the earth at dawn, when the glorious (gods) assemble in theirmight; may the Vājas, the dispensers of happiness, come to us, soliciting the laudation of this (their) adorer.
verses.griffith_verse: Like the Dawns' dwelling-place be this assembly, where in their might men rich in food have gathered. Striving to share the praises of this singer. To us come strengthening and effectual riches!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्येदेषा सुमतिः पप्रथानाभवत्पूर्व्या भूमना गौः ।अस्य सनीळा असुरस्य योनौ समान आ भरणे बिभ्रमाणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ ít ǀ eṣā́ ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ paprathānā́ ǀ ábhavat ǀ pūrvyā́ ǀ bhū́manā ǀ gáuḥ ǀasyá ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ yónau ǀ samāné ǀ ā́ ǀ bháraṇe ǀ bíbhramāṇāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Bull's most gracious far-extended favour existed first of all in full abundance. By his support they are maintained in common who in the Asura's mansion dwell together.
verses.wilson_translation: May this glorification, of this (assemly of the gods), ancient and frequent, approaching (the deities), bewidely diffused, (may the universal gods), collected together, bearing (future rewards, come) to the commonplace (of sacrifice) of this one who is mighty, which nourishes (them).
verses.griffith_verse: This Bull's most gracious far-extended favour existed first of all in full abundance. By his support they are maintained in common who in the Asura's mansion dwell together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं स्विद्वनं क उ स वृक्ष आस यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः ।संतस्थाने अजरे इतऊती अहानि पूर्वीरुषसो जरंत ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ vánam ǀ káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ vṛkṣáḥ ǀ āsa ǀ yátaḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ niḥ-tatakṣúḥ ǀsantasthāné íti sam-tasthāné ǀ ajáre íti ǀ itáūtī ítītáḥ-ūtī ǀ áhāni ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ jaranta ǁ
verses.english_translation: What was the tree, what wood, in sooth, produced it, from which they fashioned forth the Earth and Heaven? These Twain stand fast and wax not old for ever: these have sung praise to many a day and morning.
verses.wilson_translation: What is the forest, which is the tree, out of which (the gods) have fabricated heaven and earth,ever-stationary and undecaying, giving protection to the deities; through numerous days and dawns (men)praises (the gods for this).
verses.griffith_verse: What was the tree, what wood, in sooth, produced it, from which they fashioned forth the Earth and Heaven? These Twain stand fast and wax not old for ever: these have sung praise to many a day and morning.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नैतावदेना परो अन्यदस्त्युक्षा स द्यावापृथिवी बिभर्ति ।त्वचं पवित्रं कृणुत स्वधावान्यदीं सूर्यं न हरितो वहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ etā́vat ǀ enā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ anyát ǀ asti ǀ ukṣā́ ǀ sáḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ bibharti ǀtvácam ǀ pavítram ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ svadhā́-vān ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ná ǀ harítaḥ ǀ váhanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not only here is this: more is beyond us. He is the Bull, the Heaven's and Earth's supporter. With power divine he makes his skin a filter, when the Bay Coursers bear him on as Sūrya.
