verses.wilson_translation: Not such (is their power); there is another greater than they; the creator, he sustains heaven andearth; possessed of might, he makes a pure skin, before his horses bear it to the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Not only here is this: more is beyond us. He is the Bull, the Heaven's and Earth's supporter. With power divine he makes his skin a filter, when the Bay Coursers bear him on as Sūrya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तेगो न क्षामत्येति पृथ्वीं मिहं न वातो वि ह वाति भूम ।मित्रो यत्र वरुणो अज्यमानोऽग्निर्वने न व्यसृष्ट शोकं ॥
verses.transliteration: stegáḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣā́m ǀ áti ǀ eti ǀ pṛthvī́m ǀ míham ǀ ná ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ví ǀ ha ǀ vāti ǀ bhū́ma ǀmitráḥ ǀ yátra ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ajyámānaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ váne ǀ ná ǀ ví ǀ ásṛṣṭa ǀ śókam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He passes o’er the broad earth like a Stega: he penetrates the world as Wind the mist-cloud. He, balmed with oil, near Varuṇa and Mitra, like Agni in the wood, hath shot forth splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun does not pass beyond the broad earth, the wind does not drive the rain from off the earth; (Iglorify Prajāpati) in whom Mitraand Varuṇabeing manifested, disperse their radiance, as Agni(spreads hisflames) in a forest.
verses.griffith_verse: He passes o’er the broad earth like a Stega: he penetrates the world as Wind the mist-cloud. He, balmed with oil, near Varuṇa and Mitra, like Agni in the wood, hath shot forth splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तरीर्यत्सूत सद्यो अज्यमाना व्यथिरव्यथीः कृणुत स्वगोपा ।पुत्रो यत्पूर्वः पित्रोर्जनिष्ट शम्यां गौर्जगार यद्ध पृच्छान् ॥
verses.transliteration: starī́ḥ ǀ yát ǀ sū́ta ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ ajyámānā ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀ avyathī́ḥ ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ svá-gopā ǀputráḥ ǀ yát ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ pitróḥ ǀ jániṣṭa ǀ śamyā́m ǀ gáuḥ ǀ jagāra ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ pṛcchā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: When suddenly called the cow that erst was barren, she, self-protected, ended all her troubles. Earth, when the first son sprang from sire and mother, cast up the gami, that which men were seeking.
verses.wilson_translation: When a barren cow being suddenly impregnated bears (a calf), she the repeller of evils, free frompain, self-protected, produces (offspring); when (Agni), the ancient son, is genitive rated by his two parents, earthejects theŚamīwhich the priests are seeking.
verses.griffith_verse: When suddenly called the cow that erst was barren, she, self-protected, ended all her troubles. Earth, when the first son sprang from sire and mother, cast up the gami, that which men were seeking.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत कण्वं नृषदः पुत्रमाहुरुत श्यावो धनमादत्त वाजी ।प्र कृष्णाय रुशदपिन्वतोधर्ऋतमत्र नकिरस्मा अपीपेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ káṇvam ǀ nṛ-sádaḥ ǀ putrám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ utá ǀ śyāváḥ ǀ dhánam ǀ ā́ ǀ adatta ǀ vājī́ ǀprá ǀ kṛṣṇā́ya ǀ rúśat ǀ apinvata ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ átra ǀ nákiḥ ǀ asmai ǀ apīpet ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Nṛṣad's son they gave the name of Kainva, and he the brown-hued courser won the treasure. For him dark-coloured streamed the shining udder: none made it swell for him. Thus Order willed it.
verses.wilson_translation: (The expounders of the Vedas) spoke to Kaṇva, the son of Nṛṣad, and he the dark-tinted, havingfood, acquired wealth; (Agni) sprinkled (the milk of the brilliant udder for the dark (complexioned sage); no otherdivinity so favours the sacrifice for him].
verses.griffith_verse: To Nṛṣad's son they gave the name of Kainva, and he the brown-hued courser won the treasure. For him dark-coloured streamed the shining udder: none made it swell for him. Thus Order willed it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FORTH speed the Pair to bring the meditating God, benevolent with boons sent in return for boons.May Indra graciously accept both gifts from us, when he hath knowledge of the flowing Soma juice. Thou wanderest far, O Indra, through the spheres of light and realms of earth, the region, thou whom many praise!Let those who often bring their solemn rites conquer the noisy babblers who present no gifts. More beautiful than beauty must this seem to me, when the son duly careth for his parents' line.The wife attracts the husband: with a shout of joy the man's auspicious marriage is performed aright. This beauteous place of meeting have I looked upon, where, like milch-cows, the kine order the marriage train;Where the Herd's Mother counts as first and best of all, and round her are the seven-toned people of the choir. The Pious One hath reached your place before the rest: One only moves victorious with the Rudras' band.To these your helpers pour our meath, Immortal Gods, with whom your song of praise hath power to win their gifts. He who maintains the Laws of God informed me that thou wast lying hidden in the waters.Indra, who knoweth well, beheld and showed thee. By him instructed am I come, O Agni. The stranger asks the way of him who knows it: taught by the skilful guide he travels onward.This is, in truth, the blessing of instruction: he finds the path that leads directly forward. Even now he breathed: these days hath he remembered. Concealed, he sucked the bosom of his Mother.Yet in his youth old age hath come upon him: he hath grown gracious, good, and free from anger. O Kalasa, all these blessings will we bring them, O Kurusravana, who give rich presents.May he, O wealthy princes, and this Soma which I am bearing in my heart, reward you.

verses.sanskrit: प्र सु ग्मंता धियसानस्य सक्षणि वरेभिर्वराँ अभि षु प्रसीदतः ।अस्माकमिंद्र उभयं जुजोषति यत्सोम्यस्यांधसो बुबोधति ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ gmántā ǀ dhiyasānásya ǀ sakṣáṇi ǀ varébhiḥ ǀ varā́n ǀ abhí ǀ sú ǀ pra-sī́dataḥ ǀasmā́kam ǀ índraḥ ǀ ubháyam ǀ jujoṣati ǀ yát ǀ somyásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ búbodhati ǁ
verses.english_translation: FORTH speed the Pair to bring the meditating God, benevolent with boons sent in return for boons. May Indra graciously accept both gifts from us, when he hath knowledge of the flowing Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrasends his quick-going horses to the service of the (worshipper) expectant (of his arrival); may hecome to the excellent (adorations) of the (worshipper), propitiating him by suitable means; Indra is gratified byboth our (oblations and praises), when he recognizes (the taste) of the food presented by the offerer of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: FORTH speed the Pair to bring the meditating God, benevolent with boons sent in return for boons. May Indra graciously accept both gifts from us, when he hath knowledge of the flowing Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वींद्र यासि दिव्यानि रोचना वि पार्थिवानि रजसा पुरुष्टुत ।ये त्वा वहंति मुहुरध्वराँ उप ते सु वन्वंतु वग्वनाँ अराधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ indra ǀ yāsi ǀ divyā́ni ǀ rocanā́ ǀ ví ǀ pā́rthivāni ǀ rájasā ǀ puru-stuta ǀyé ǀ tvā ǀ váhanti ǀ múhuḥ ǀ adhvarā́n ǀ úpa ǀ té ǀ sú ǀ vanvantu ǀ vagvanā́n ǀ arādhásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou wanderest far, O Indra, through the spheres of light and realms of earth, the region, thou whom many praise! Let those who often bring their solemn rites conquer the noisy babblers who present no gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, who is praised by many, you pervade the luminaries of heaven and earth with your lustre; maythe horses that repeatedly bring you to our sacrifices, plural ased by our praise, bring affluence to us who are poor.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou wanderest far, O Indra, through the spheres of light and realms of earth, the region, thou whom many praise! Let those who often bring their solemn rites conquer the noisy babblers who present no gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिन्मे छंत्सद्वपुषो वपुष्टरं पुत्रो यज्जानं पित्रोरधीयति ।जाया पतिं वहति वग्नुना सुमत्पुंस इद्भद्रो वहतुः परिष्कृतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ me ǀ chantsat ǀ vápuṣaḥ ǀ vápuḥ-taram ǀ putráḥ ǀ yát ǀ jā́nam ǀ pitróḥ ǀ adhi-íyati ǀjāyā́ ǀ pátim ǀ vahati ǀ vagnúnā ǀ su-mát ǀ puṃsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhadráḥ ǀ vahatúḥ ǀ pári-kṛtaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: More beautiful than beauty must this seem to me, when the son duly careth for his parents' line. The wife attracts the husband: with a shout of joy the man's auspicious marriage is performed aright.
verses.wilson_translation: May (Indra) desire for me this (act of sacrifice). The most beautiful of beautiful things, (as) when a sonproclaims his birth from his parents. The wife brings her husband (to her side) with genitive le words; the goodfortune of the husband is perfected only as marriage.
verses.griffith_verse: More beautiful than beauty must this seem to me, when the son duly careth for his parents' line. The wife attracts the husband: with a shout of joy the man's auspicious marriage is performed aright.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदित्सधस्थमभि चारु दीधय गावो यच्छासन्वहतुं न धेनवः ।माता यन्मंतुर्यूथस्य पूर्व्याभि वाणस्य सप्तधातुरिज्जनः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ abhí ǀ cā́ru ǀ dīdhaya ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ śā́san ǀ vahatúm ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀmātā́ ǀ yát ǀ mántuḥ ǀ yūthásya ǀ pūrvyā́ ǀ abhí ǀ vāṇásya ǀ saptá-dhātuḥ ǀ ít ǀ jánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This beauteous place of meeting have I looked upon, where, like milch-cows, the kine order the marriage train; Where the Herd's Mother counts as first and best of all, and round her are the seven-toned people of the choir.
verses.wilson_translation: Shine,Indra, upon this elegant chamber of sacrifice when our praises desire (your approach) as kine(desire) their stalls; since the praise of (me) the worshipper precedes (the adoration) of the company, and thisperson accompanied by the seven officiating priests is the offerer of praise.
verses.griffith_verse: This beauteous place of meeting have I looked upon, where, like milch-cows, the kine order the marriage train; Where the Herd's Mother counts as first and best of all, and round her are the seven-toned people of the choir.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वोऽच्छा रिरिचे देवयुष्पदमेको रुद्रेभिर्याति तुर्वणिः ।जरा वा येष्वमृतेषु दावने परि व ऊमेभ्यः सिंचता मधु ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ áccha ǀ ririce ǀ deva-yúḥ ǀ padám ǀ ékaḥ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ yāti ǀ turváṇiḥ ǀjarā́ ǀ vā ǀ yéṣu ǀ amṛ́teṣu ǀ dāváne ǀ pári ǀ vaḥ ǀ ū́mebhyaḥ ǀ siñcata ǀ mádhu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Pious One hath reached your place before the rest: One only moves victorious with the Rudras' band. To these your helpers pour our meath, Immortal Gods, with whom your song of praise hath power to win their gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: The devout (priest) excels (going) towards your plural ce of worship; the quick-moving (Indra), the chief(of the priests), proceeds with the Rudras, (the Maruts); sprinkle the exhilarating (Somawith water) for theprotecting (deities), the immortals among whom praise is (able) to procure wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: The Pious One hath reached your place before the rest: One only moves victorious with the Rudras' band. To these your helpers pour our meath, Immortal Gods, with whom your song of praise hath power to win their gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निधीयमानमपगूळ्हमप्सु प्र मे देवानां व्रतपा उवाच ।इंद्रो विद्वाँ अनु हि त्वा चचक्ष तेनाहमग्ने अनुशिष्ट आगां ॥
verses.transliteration: ni-dhīyámānam ǀ ápa-gūḷham ǀ ap-sú ǀ prá ǀ me ǀ devā́nām ǀ vrata-pā́ḥ ǀ uvāca ǀíndraḥ ǀ vidvā́n ǀ ánu ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ cacákṣa ǀ téna ǀ ahám ǀ agne ǀ ánu-śiṣṭaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agām ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who maintains the Laws of God informed me that thou wast lying hidden in the waters. Indra, who knoweth well, beheld and showed thee. By him instructed am I come, O Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The guardian of the sacred rites of the gods,Indra, said to me, (Agni), who had been deposited in thewaters; the sagacious Indra, following you, Agni, has discovered you, therefore, admonished by him may I, Agni,proceed to heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: He who maintains the Laws of God informed me that thou wast lying hidden in the waters. Indra, who knoweth well, beheld and showed thee. By him instructed am I come, O Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षेत्रवित्क्षेत्रविदं ह्यप्राट् स प्रैति क्षेत्रविदानुशिष्टः ।एतद्वै भद्रमनुशासनस्योत स्रुतिं विंदत्यंजसीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: ákṣetra-vit ǀ kṣetra-vídam ǀ hí ǀ áprāṭ ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá ǀ eti ǀ kṣetra-vídā ǀ ánu-śiṣṭaḥ ǀetát ǀ vái ǀ bhadrám ǀ anu-śā́sanasya ǀ utá ǀ srutím ǀ vindati ǀ añjasī́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: The stranger asks the way of him who knows it: taught by the skilful guide he travels onward. This is, in truth, the blessing of instruction: he finds the path that leads directly forward.
verses.griffith_verse: The stranger asks the way of him who knows it: taught by the skilful guide he travels onward. This is, in truth, the blessing of instruction: he finds the path that leads directly forward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्येदु प्राणीदममन्निमाहापीवृतो अधयन्मातुरूधः ।एमेनमाप जरिमा युवानमहेळन्वसुः सुमना बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: adyá ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prá ǀ ānīt ǀ ámaman ǀ imā́ ǀ áhā ǀ ápi-vṛtaḥ ǀ adhayat ǀ mātúḥ ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀā́ ǀ īm ǀ enam ǀ āpa ǀ jarimā́ ǀ yúvānam ǀ áheḷan ǀ vásuḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even now he breathed: these days hath he remembered. Concealed, he sucked the bosom of his Mother. Yet in his youth old age hath come upon him: he hath grown gracious, good, and free from anger.
verses.wilson_translation: Today (Agni) breathed; he purposed (to conduct) these days surrounded (by lustre), and drank thesap of his mother (earth); the praise of his (worshippers) reaches the over-youthful (Agni), and he has becomegentle, genitive rous, and well-disposed.
verses.griffith_verse: Even now he breathed: these days hath he remembered. Concealed, he sucked the bosom of his Mother. Yet in his youth old age hath come upon him: he hath grown gracious, good, and free from anger.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतानि भद्रा कलश क्रियाम कुरुश्रवण ददतो मघानि ।दान इद्वो मघवानः सो अस्त्वयं च सोमो हृदि यं बिभर्मि ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ kalaśa ǀ kriyāma ǀ kúru-śravaṇa ǀ dádataḥ ǀ maghā́ni ǀdānáḥ ǀ ít ǀ vaḥ ǀ magha-vānaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ astu ǀ ayám ǀ ca ǀ sómaḥ ǀ hṛdí ǀ yám ǀ bíbharmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Kalasa, all these blessings will we bring them, O Kurusravana, who give rich presents. May he, O wealthy princes, and this Soma which I am bearing in my heart, reward you.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra), the possessor of the pitchers, the bearer of the praise of the Kurus, let us celebrate theseauspicious adorations of you, the giver of riches; may he, (Indra), be the donor (of affluence) to you who areopulent, (in pious offering), and (so may) this Somawhich I cherish in my heart.
verses.griffith_verse: O Kalasa, all these blessings will we bring them, O Kurusravana, who give rich presents. May he, O wealthy princes, and this Soma which I am bearing in my heart, reward you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIII. Various Deities.
hymns.anukramani: ९कवष ऐलूषः। १ विश्वेदेवाः, २-३ इन्द्रः, ४-५ कुरुश्रवणस्त्रासदस्यवः, ६-९ उपमश्रवा मैत्रातिथिः। १ त्रिष्टुप् , प्रगाथः = ( २ बृहती, ३ सतोबृहती ),४-९ गायत्री ।

None lives, even had he hundred lives, beyond the statute of the GodsSo am I parted from my friend.

verses.english_translation: THE urgings of the people have impelled me, and by,the nearest way I bring you Pūṣan. The Universal Gods have brought me safely. The cry was heard, Behold, Dubsasu cometh!
verses.wilson_translation: The (divinities, the) appointers of men, have appointed me to Kuruśravaṇa; I have borne Pūṣanonthe way; the universal gods are my protectors; the cry is: "duhśāsu comes"
verses.griffith_verse: THE urgings of the people have impelled me, and by,the nearest way I bring you Pūṣan. The Universal Gods have brought me safely. The cry was heard, Behold, Dubsasu cometh!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: The ribs that compass me give pain and trouble me like rival wives. Indigence, nakedness, exhaustion press me sore: my mind is fluttering like a bird's.
verses.wilson_translation: My ribs pain me on both sides, like rival wives; disease, nakedness, hunger, afflict me; my mindflutters like a bird.
verses.griffith_verse: The ribs that compass me give pain and trouble me like rival wives. Indigence, nakedness, exhaustion press me sore: my mind is fluttering like a bird's.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: As rats eat weavers' threads, cares are consuming me, thy singer, gatakratu, me. Have mercy on us once, O Indra, Bounteous Lord: be thou a Father unto us.
verses.wilson_translation: Afflictions consume me, your worshipperŚatakratu, as mice (eat) threads, for once,Indra, possessorof opulence, grant us felicity; be to us as a father.
verses.griffith_verse: As rats eat weavers' threads, cares are consuming me, thy singer, gatakratu, me. Have mercy on us once, O Indra, Bounteous Lord: be thou a Father unto us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: I the priests' Ṛṣi chose as prince most liberal Kurusravana, The son of Trasadasyu's son,
verses.griffith_verse: I the priests' Ṛṣi chose as prince most liberal Kurusravana, The son of Trasadasyu's son,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Whose three bays harnessed to the car bear me straight onward: I will laud The giver of a thousand meeds,
verses.wilson_translation: Whose three horses bear me plural asantly in the chariot; I praise him at the ceremony in which hepresents thousands.
verses.griffith_verse: Whose three bays harnessed to the car bear me straight onward: I will laud The giver of a thousand meeds,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: The sire of Upamasravas, even him whose words were passing sweet, As a fair field is to its lord.
verses.wilson_translation: Upamaśravas, the words of whose father were sweet, like a plural asant field given to a beggar.
verses.griffith_verse: The sire of Upamasravas, even him whose words were passing sweet, As a fair field is to its lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Mark, Upamasravas, his son, mark, grandson of Mitratithi: I am thy father's eulogist.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to me, my son, grandson of Mitrātithi; I am the eulogist of your father.
verses.griffith_verse: Mark, Upamasravas, his son, mark, grandson of Mitratithi: I am thy father's eulogist.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: If I controlled Immortal Gods, yea, even were I Lord of men, My liberal prince were living still.
verses.wilson_translation: If I were lord oover immortals and mortals, then should my munificent (benefactor) live.
verses.griffith_verse: If I controlled Immortal Gods, yea, even were I Lord of men, My liberal prince were living still.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: None lives, even had he hundred lives, beyond the statute of the Gods So am I parted from my friend.
verses.wilson_translation: No one lives hundred years passing the limit fixed by the gods; so he is separated from his friendṣ
verses.griffith_verse: None lives, even had he hundred lives, beyond the statute of the Gods So am I parted from my friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIV. Dice, Etc.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SPRUNG from tall trees on windy heights, these rollers transport me as they turn upon the table.Dearer to me the die that never slumbers than the deep draught of Mujavan's own Soma. She never vexed me nor was angry with me, but to my friends and me was ever gracious.For the die's sake, whose single point is final, mine own devoted wife I alienated. My wife holds me aloof, her mother hates me: the wretched man finds none to give him comfort.As of a costly horse grown old and feeble, I find not any profit of the gamester. Others caress the wife of him whose riches the die hath coveted, that rapid courser:Of him speak father, mother, brothers saying, We know him not: bind him and take him with you. When I resolve to play with these no longer, my friends depart from me and leave me lonely.When the brown dice, thrown on the board, have rattled, like a fond girl I seek the place of meeting. The gamester seeks the gambling-house, and wonders, his body all afire, Shall I be lucky?Still do the dice extend his eager longing, staking his gains against his adversary. Dice, verily, are armed with goads and driving-hooks, deceiving and tormenting, causing grievous woe.They give frail gifts and then destroy the man who wins, thickly anointed with the player's fairest good. Merrily sports their troop, the three-and-fifty, like Savitar the God whose ways are faithful.They bend not even to the mighty's anger: the King himself pays homage and reveres them. Downward they roll, and then spring quickly upward, and, handless, force the man with hands to serve them.Cast on the board, like lumps of magic charcoal, though cold themselves they burn the heart to ashes. The gambler's wife is left forlorn and wretched: the mother mourns the son who wanders homeless.In constant fear, in debt, and seeking riches, he goes by night unto the home of others. Sad is the gambler when he sees a matron, another's wife, and his well-ordered dwelling.He yokes the brown steeds in the early morning, and when the fire is cold sinks down an outcast. To the great captain of your mighty army, who hath become the host's imperial leader,To him I show my ten extended fingers: I speak the truth. No wealth am I withholding. Play not with dice: no, cultivate thy corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient.There are thy cattle there thy wife, O gambler. So this good Savitar himself hath told me. Make me your friend: show us some little mercy. Assail us not with your terrific fierceness.Appeased be your malignity and anger, and let the brown dice snare some other captive.

verses.sanskrit: प्रावेपा मा बृहतो मादयंति प्रवातेजा इरिणे वर्वृतानाः ।सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जागृविर्मह्यमच्छान् ॥
verses.transliteration: prāvepā́ḥ ǀ mā ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ mādayanti ǀ pravāte-jā́ḥ ǀ íriṇe ǀ várvṛtānāḥ ǀsómasya-iva ǀ mauja-vatásya ǀ bhakṣáḥ ǀ vi-bhī́dakaḥ ǀ jā́gṛviḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ acchān ǁ
verses.english_translation: SPRUNG from tall trees on windy heights, these rollers transport me as they turn upon the table. Dearer to me the die that never slumbers than the deep draught of Mujavan's own Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: The large rattling dice exhilarate me as torrents borne on a precipice flowing in a desert; the excitingdice animate me as the taste of the Somaof Maujavat (delights the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: SPRUNG from tall trees on windy heights, these rollers transport me as they turn upon the table. Dearer to me the die that never slumbers than the deep draught of Mujavan's own Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न मा मिमेथ न जिहीळ एषा शिवा सखिभ्य उत मह्यमासीत् ।अक्षस्याहमेकपरस्य हेतोरनुव्रतामप जायामरोधं ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ mā ǀ mimetha ǀ ná ǀ jihīḷe ǀ eṣā́ ǀ śivā́ ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ utá ǀ máhyam ǀ āsīt ǀakṣásya ǀ ahám ǀ eka-parásya ǀ hetóḥ ǀ ánu-vratām ǀ ápa ǀ jāyā́m ǀ arodham ǁ
verses.english_translation: She never vexed me nor was angry with me, but to my friends and me was ever gracious. For the die's sake, whose single point is final, mine own devoted wife I alienated.
verses.wilson_translation: This (my wife) has not been angry (with me), nor was she overcome withsham; kind was she to meand to my friends; yet for the sake of one or other die, I have deserted this affectionate spouse.
verses.griffith_verse: She never vexed me nor was angry with me, but to my friends and me was ever gracious. For the die's sake, whose single point is final, mine own devoted wife I alienated.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वेष्टि श्वश्रूरप जाया रुणद्धि न नाथितो विंदते मर्डितारं ।अश्वस्येव जरतो वस्न्यस्य नाहं विंदामि कितवस्य भोगं ॥
verses.transliteration: dvéṣṭi ǀ śvaśrū́ḥ ǀ ápa ǀ jāyā́ ǀ ruṇaddhi ǀ ná ǀ nāthitáḥ ǀ vindate ǀ marḍitā́ram ǀáśvasya-iva ǀ járataḥ ǀ vásnyasya ǀ ná ǀ ahám ǀ vindāmi ǀ kitavásya ǀ bhógam ǁ
verses.english_translation: My wife holds me aloof, her mother hates me: the wretched man finds none to give him comfort. As of a costly horse grown old and feeble, I find not any profit of the gamester.
verses.wilson_translation: My mother-in-law reviles me, my wife opposes me; the beggar meets no compassionate (benefactor); Ido not realize the enjoyment of the gamester any more than that of a valuable horse grown old.
verses.griffith_verse: My wife holds me aloof, her mother hates me: the wretched man finds none to give him comfort. As of a costly horse grown old and feeble, I find not any profit of the gamester.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अन्ये जायां परि मृशंत्यस्य यस्यागृधद्वेदने वाज्यक्षः ।पिता माता भ्रातर एनमाहुर्न जानीमो नयता बद्धमेतं ॥
verses.transliteration: anyé ǀ jāyā́m ǀ pári ǀ mṛśanti ǀ asya ǀ yásya ǀ ágṛdhat ǀ védane ǀ vājī́ ǀ akṣáḥ ǀpitā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ bhrā́taraḥ ǀ enam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ jānīmaḥ ǀ náyata ǀ baddhám ǀ etám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Others caress the wife of him whose riches the die hath coveted, that rapid courser: Of him speak father, mother, brothers saying, We know him not: bind him and take him with you.
verses.wilson_translation: Others touch the wife of him whose wealth the potent dice covet; his mother, father, brothers say, "weknow him not, take him away bound (where you will)".
verses.griffith_verse: Others caress the wife of him whose riches the die hath coveted, that rapid courser: Of him speak father, mother, brothers saying, We know him not: bind him and take him with you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदादीध्ये न दविषाण्येभिः परायद्भ्योऽव हीये सखिभ्यः ।न्युप्ताश्च बभ्रवो वाचमक्रतँ एमीदेषां निष्कृतं जारिणीव ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ā-dī́dhye ǀ ná ǀ daviṣāṇi ǀ ebhiḥ ǀ parāyát-bhyaḥ ǀ áva ǀ hīye ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀní-uptāḥ ǀ ca ǀ babhrávaḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ ákrata ǀ émi ǀ ít ǀ eṣām ǀ niḥ-kṛtám ǀ jāríṇī-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: When I resolve to play with these no longer, my friends depart from me and leave me lonely. When the brown dice, thrown on the board, have rattled, like a fond girl I seek the place of meeting.
verses.wilson_translation: When I relect, (then I say), "I will plural y no more with them". I pay attention to my friends who desert(me); and the tawny dice rattle as they are thrown; I hasten to their accusative tomed plural ce as a harlot (to anassignation).
verses.griffith_verse: When I resolve to play with these no longer, my friends depart from me and leave me lonely. When the brown dice, thrown on the board, have rattled, like a fond girl I seek the place of meeting.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सभामेति कितवः पृच्छमानो जेष्यामीति तन्वा शूशुजानः ।अक्षासो अस्य वि तिरंति कामं प्रति���ीव्ने दधत आ कृतानि ॥
verses.transliteration: sabhā́m ǀ eti ǀ kitaváḥ ǀ pṛcchámānaḥ ǀ jeṣyā́mi ǀ íti ǀ tanvā́ ǀ śū́śujānaḥ ǀakṣā́saḥ ǀ asya ǀ ví ǀ tiranti ǀ kā́mam ǀ prati-dī́vne ǀ dádhataḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gamester seeks the gambling-house, and wonders, his body all afire, Shall I be lucky? Still do the dice extend his eager longing, staking his gains against his adversary.
verses.wilson_translation: The gamester goes to the gambling table, radiant in person n, and asking himself, "Shall I win?" Thedice increase his passion for plural y as he practises the arts of (gambling) with his adversary.
verses.griffith_verse: The gamester seeks the gambling-house, and wonders, his body all afire, Shall I be lucky? Still do the dice extend his eager longing, staking his gains against his adversary.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षास इदंकुशिनो नितोदिनो निकृत्वानस्तपनास्तापयिष्णवः ।कुमारदेष्णा जयतः पुनर्हणो मध्वा संपृक्ताः कितवस्य बर्हणा ॥
verses.transliteration: akṣā́saḥ ǀ ít ǀ aṅkuśínaḥ ǀ ni-todínaḥ ǀ ni-kṛ́tvānaḥ ǀ tápanāḥ ǀ tāpayiṣṇávaḥ ǀkumārá-deṣṇāḥ ǀ jáyataḥ ǀ punaḥ-hánaḥ ǀ mádhvā ǀ sám-pṛktāḥ ǀ kitavásya ǀ barháṇā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dice, verily, are armed with goads and driving-hooks, deceiving and tormenting, causing grievous woe. They give frail gifts and then destroy the man who wins, thickly anointed with the player's fairest good.
verses.wilson_translation: Dice verily are armed with hooks, with goads, pricking, paining and torturing (the gamester); to thewinning (plural yer) they are the givers of sons, they are tipped with honey; slaying him in return by taking away thegambler's (all).
verses.griffith_verse: Dice, verily, are armed with goads and driving-hooks, deceiving and tormenting, causing grievous woe. They give frail gifts and then destroy the man who wins, thickly anointed with the player's fairest good.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिपंचाशः क्रीळति व्रात एषां देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मा ।उग्रस्य चिन्मन्यवे ना नमंते राजा चिदेभ्यो नम इत्कृणोति ॥
verses.transliteration: tri-pañcāśáḥ ǀ krīḷati ǀ vrā́taḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ deváḥ-iva ǀ savitā́ ǀ satyá-dharmā ǀugrásya ǀ cit ǀ manyáve ǀ ná ǀ namante ǀ rā́jā ǀ cit ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ ít ǀ kṛṇoti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Merrily sports their troop, the three-and-fifty, like Savitar the God whose ways are faithful. They bend not even to the mighty's anger: the King himself pays homage and reveres them.
verses.wilson_translation: The aggregate fifty-three of them are plural yed as the divine truth, observant Savitā, (travels); the dicebow not before the wrath of any, however violent; a king himself pays them homage.
verses.griffith_verse: Merrily sports their troop, the three-and-fifty, like Savitar the God whose ways are faithful. They bend not even to the mighty's anger: the King himself pays homage and reveres them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नीचा वर्तंत उपरि स्फुरंत्यहस्तासो हस्तवंतं सहंते ।दिव्या अंगारा इरिणे न्युप्ताः शीताः संतो हृदयं निर्दहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: nīcā́ ǀ vartante ǀ upári ǀ sphuranti ǀ ahastā́saḥ ǀ hásta-vantam ǀ sahante ǀdivyā́ḥ ǀ áṅgārāḥ ǀ íriṇe ǀ ní-uptāḥ ǀ śītā́ḥ ǀ sántaḥ ǀ hṛ́dayam ǀ níḥ ǀ dahanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Downward they roll, and then spring quickly upward, and, handless, force the man with hands to serve them. Cast on the board, like lumps of magic charcoal, though cold themselves they burn the heart to ashes.
verses.wilson_translation: Now they abide below; now they palpitate on high handless, they overpower him who hashands; castupon the dice-board like coals from the sky, even though cold they burn the heart.
verses.griffith_verse: Downward they roll, and then spring quickly upward, and, handless, force the man with hands to serve them. Cast on the board, like lumps of magic charcoal, though cold themselves they burn the heart to ashes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जाया तप्यते कितवस्य हीना माता पुत्रस्य चरतः क्व स्वित् ।ऋणावा बिभ्यद्धनमिच्छमानोऽन्येषामस्तमुप नक्तमेति ॥
verses.transliteration: jāyā́ ǀ tapyate ǀ kitavásya ǀ hīnā́ ǀ mātā́ ǀ putrásya ǀ cárataḥ ǀ kvá ǀ svit ǀṛṇa-vā́ ǀ bíbhyat ǀ dhánam ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ anyéṣām ǀ ástam ǀ úpa ǀ náktam ǀ eti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The gambler's wife is left forlorn and wretched: the mother mourns the son who wanders homeless. In constant fear, in debt, and seeking riches, he goes by night unto the home of others.
verses.wilson_translation: The deserted wife of the gamester is afflicted; the mother (grieves) for the son wandering wherever helikes; involved in debt, ever in fear, anxious for wealth, (the gambler) goes forth by night to the dwellings of others(to plural nder).
verses.griffith_verse: The gambler's wife is left forlorn and wretched: the mother mourns the son who wanders homeless. In constant fear, in debt, and seeking riches, he goes by night unto the home of others.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वाय कितवं ततापान्येषां जायां सुकृतं च योनिं ।पूर्वाह्णे अश्वान्युयुजे हि बभ्रून्त्सो अग्नेरंते वृषलः पपाद ॥
verses.transliteration: stríyam ǀ dṛṣṭvā́ya ǀ kitavám ǀ tatāpa ǀ anyéṣām ǀ jāyā́m ǀ sú-kṛtam ǀ ca ǀ yónim ǀpūrvāhṇé ǀ áśvān ǀ yuyujé ǀ hí ǀ babhrū́n ǀ sáḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ ánte ǀ vṛṣaláḥ ǀ papāda ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sad is the gambler when he sees a matron, another's wife, and his well-ordered dwelling. He yokes the brown steeds in the early morning, and when the fire is cold sinks down an outcast.
verses.wilson_translation: The gamester, having observed the happy wife and well-ordered home of others, suffers regret; yet inthe forenoon he puts to the tawny steeds, and at night the sinner lies down by the fire.
verses.griffith_verse: Sad is the gambler when he sees a matron, another's wife, and his well-ordered dwelling. He yokes the brown steeds in the early morning, and when the fire is cold sinks down an outcast.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो वः सेनानीर्महतो गणस्य राजा व्रातस्य प्रथमो बभूव ।तस्मै कृणोमि न धना रुणध्मि दशाहं प्राचीस्तदृतं वदामि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ senā-nī́ḥ ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ gaṇásya ǀ rā́jā ǀ vrā́tasya ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ babhū́va ǀtásmai ǀ kṛṇomi ǀ ná ǀ dhánā ǀ ruṇadhmi ǀ dáśa ǀ ahám ǀ prā́cīḥ ǀ tát ǀ ṛtám ǀ vadāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: To the great captain of your mighty army, who hath become the host's imperial leader, To him I show my ten extended fingers: I speak the truth. No wealth am I withholding.
verses.wilson_translation: Dice, I offer salutation to him who has been the genitive ral of your great army, the chief lord of your host;I do not provide him with wealth; I raise my ten (fingers) to the east; that (which) I speak (is) the truth.
verses.griffith_verse: To the great captain of your mighty army, who hath become the host's imperial leader, To him I show my ten extended fingers: I speak the truth. No wealth am I withholding.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षैर्मा दीव्यः कृषिमित्कृषस्व वित्ते रमस्व बहु मन्यमानः ।तत्र गावः कितव तत्र जाया तन्मे वि चष्टे सवितायमर्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: akṣáiḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ dīvyaḥ ǀ kṛṣím ǀ ít ǀ kṛṣasva ǀ vitté ǀ ramasva ǀ bahú ǀ mányamānaḥ ǀtátra ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ kitava ǀ tátra ǀ jāyā́ ǀ tát ǀ me ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀ savitā́ ǀ ayám ǀ aryáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Play not with dice: no, cultivate thy corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient. There are thy cattle there thy wife, O gambler. So this good Savitar himself hath told me.
verses.wilson_translation: Giving serious attention (to my advie), plural y not with dice; pursue agriculture; delight in wealth (soacquired); there, gambler, are cows; there is a wife; so has this (visible) sovereign Savitādeclared to me.
verses.griffith_verse: Play not with dice: no, cultivate thy corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient. There are thy cattle there thy wife, O gambler. So this good Savitar himself hath told me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मित्रं कृणुध्वं खलु मृळता नो मा नो घोरेण चरताभि धृष्णु ।नि वो नु मन्युर्विशतामरातिरन्यो बभ्रूणां प्रसितौ न्वस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: mitrám ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ khálu ǀ mṛḷáta ǀ naḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ghoréṇa ǀ carata ǀ abhí ǀ dhṛṣṇú ǀní ǀ vaḥ ǀ nú ǀ manyúḥ ǀ viśatām ǀ árātiḥ ǀ anyáḥ ǀ babhrūṇā́m ǀ prá-sitau ǀ nú ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make me your friend: show us some little mercy. Assail us not with your terrific fierceness. Appeased be your malignity and anger, and let the brown dice snare some other captive.
verses.wilson_translation: Be friends with us (dice); bestow upon us happiness; approach us not in terrible wrath; let your angerlight upon our enemies; let our enemy fall under the bondage of the tawny (dice).
verses.griffith_verse: Make me your friend: show us some little mercy. Assail us not with your terrific fierceness. Appeased be your malignity and anger, and let the brown dice snare some other captive.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THESE fires associate with Indra are awake, bringing their light when first the Dawn begins to shine.May Heaven and Earth, great Pair, observe our holy work. We claim for us this day the favour of the Gods. Yea, for ourselves we claim the grace of Heaven and Earth, of Śaryaṇāvān, of the Hills and Mother Streams.For innocence we pray to Sūrya and to Dawn. So may the flowing Soma bring us bliss to-day. May the great Twain, the Mothers, Heaven and Earth, this day preserve us free from sin for peace and happiness.May Morning sending forth her light drive sin afar. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. May this first Dawn bring us the host of gracious Gods: rich, may it richly shine for us who strive for wealth.The wrath of the malignant may we keep afar. We pray to kindled Agni for feilicity. Dawns, who come forward with the bright beams of the Sun, and at your earliest flushing bring to us the light,Shine ye on us to-day auspicious, for renown. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. Free from all sickness may the Mornings come to us, and let our fires mount upward with a lofty blaze.The Aśvin Pair have harnessed their swift-moving car. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. Send us to-day a portion choice and excellent, O Savitar, for thou art he who dealeth wealth.I cry to Dhiṣaṇā, Mother of opulence. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. Further me this declaring of Eternal Law, the Law of Gods, as we mortals acknowledge it!The Sun goes up beholding all the rays of morn. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. This day we pray with innocence in strewing grass, adjusting pressing-stones, and perfecting the hymn.Thou in the Ādityas’ keeping movest restlessly. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. To our great holy grass I bid the Gods at morn to banquet, and will seat them as the seven priests,—Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra, Bhaga for our gain. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. Come hither, O Ādityas, for our perfect weal: accordant help our sacrifice that we may thrive.Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and enkindled Agni we implore for happiness. Ādityas, Gods, vouchsafe that this our home may be praise-worthy, prosperous, our heroes' sure defence,For cattle, for our sons, for progeny, for life. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity. This day may all the Maruts, all he near us with aid: may all our fires be well enkindled.May all Gods come to us with gracious favour. May spoil and wealth he ours, and all possessions. He whom ye aid, O Deities, in battle, whom ye protect and rescue from affliction,Who fears no danger at your milk-libation, -such may we be to feast the Gods, ye Mighty.

verses.sanskrit: अबुध्रमु त्य इंद्रवंतो अग्नयो ज्योतिर्भरंत उषसो व्युष्टिषु ।मही द्यावापृथिवी चेततामपोऽद्या देवानामव आ वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ábudhram ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyé ǀ índra-vantaḥ ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ bhárantaḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀmahī́ íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ cetatām ǀ ápaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: THESE fires associate with Indra are awake, bringing their light when first the Dawn begins to shine. May Heaven and Earth, great Pair, observe our holy work. We claim for us this day the favour of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The fires that are connected with Indraare awake, bringing light at the opening of the dawn; let thegreat heaven and earth be cognizant of that office; to-day we solicit the protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: THESE fires associate with Indra are awake, bringing their light when first the Dawn begins to shine. May Heaven and Earth, great Pair, observe our holy work. We claim for us this day the favour of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवस्पृथिव्योरव आ वृणीमहे मातॄन्त्सिंधून्पर्वतांछर्यणावतः ।अनागास्त्वं सूर्यमुषासमीमहे भद्रं सोमः सुवानो अद्या कृणोतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥpṛthivyóḥ ǀ ávaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ mātṝ́n ǀ síndhūn ǀ párvatān ǀ śaryaṇā́-vataḥ ǀanāgāḥ-tvám ǀ sū́ryam ǀ uṣásam ǀ īmahe ǀ bhadrám ǀ sómaḥ ǀ suvānáḥ ǀ adyá ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, for ourselves we claim the grace of Heaven and Earth, of Śaryaṇāvān, of the Hills and Mother Streams. For innocence we pray to Sūrya and to Dawn. So may the flowing Soma bring us bliss to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: We solicit the protection of heaven and earth; (we solicit) the maternal rivers, the mountains with theirlakes, the sun and the dawn, for freedom from sin; may the Somathat is now effused secure to us today goodfortune.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, for ourselves we claim the grace of Heaven and Earth, of Śaryaṇāvān, of the Hills and Mother Streams. For innocence we pray to Sūrya and to Dawn. So may the flowing Soma bring us bliss to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्यावा नो अद्य पृथिवी अनागसो मही त्रायेतां सुविताय मातरा ।उषा उच्छंत्यप बाधतामघं स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: dyā́vā ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ trāyetām ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ mātárā ǀuṣā́ḥ ǀ ucchántī ǀ ápa ǀ bādhatām ǀ aghám ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the great Twain, the Mothers, Heaven and Earth, this day preserve us free from sin for peace and happiness. May Morning sending forth her light drive sin afar. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the vast maternal heaven and earth this day preserve us for our happiness, free from sin; may theopening dawn drive away our sin; we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: May the great Twain, the Mothers, Heaven and Earth, this day preserve us free from sin for peace and happiness. May Morning sending forth her light drive sin afar. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं न उस्रा प्रथमा सुदेव्यं रेवत्सनिभ्यो रेवती व्युच्छतु ।आरे मन्युं दुर्विदत्रस्य धीमहि स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ naḥ ǀ usrā́ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ su-devyám ǀ revát ǀ saní-bhyaḥ ǀ revátī ǀ ví ǀ ucchatu ǀāré ǀ manyúm ǀ duḥ-vidátrasya ǀ dhīmahi ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this first Dawn bring us the host of gracious Gods: rich, may it richly shine for us who strive for wealth. The wrath of the malignant may we keep afar. We pray to kindled Agni for feilicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May this first dawn, the possessor of wealth, open; bringing to us who are liberal (a season) fit for thegods, abounding with riches; we consider the anger of the malevolent (to be) remote; we solicit the kindled firefor our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: May this first Dawn bring us the host of gracious Gods: rich, may it richly shine for us who strive for wealth. The wrath of the malignant may we keep afar. We pray to kindled Agni for feilicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र याः सिस्रते सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्ज्योतिर्भरंतीरुषसो व्युष्टिषु ।भद्रा नो अद्य श्रवसे व्युच्छत स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ sísrate ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ bhárantīḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀbhadrā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ śrávase ǀ ví ǀ ucchata ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dawns, who come forward with the bright beams of the Sun, and at your earliest flushing bring to us the light, Shine ye on us to-day auspicious, for renown. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Dawns, who are associated with the rays of the sun, bringing light at the opening (of the day), shineupon us today, propitious, for our subsistence; we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Dawns, who come forward with the bright beams of the Sun, and at your earliest flushing bring to us the light, Shine ye on us to-day auspicious, for renown. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनमीवा उषस आ चरंतु न उदग्नयो जिहतां ज्योतिषा बृहत् ।आयुक्षातामश्विना तूतुजिं रथं स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: anamīvā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ carantu ǀ naḥ ǀ út ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ jihatām ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ bṛhát ǀáyukṣātām ǀ aśvínā ǀ tū́tujim ǀ rátham ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Free from all sickness may the Mornings come to us, and let our fires mount upward with a lofty blaze. The Aśvin Pair have harnessed their swift-moving car. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the salutary dawns hasten to us; may the fires blaze up with great lustre, and may the Aśvinsharness their quick-going chariot; we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Free from all sickness may the Mornings come to us, and let our fires mount upward with a lofty blaze. The Aśvin Pair have harnessed their swift-moving car. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रेष्ठं नो अद्य सवितर्वरेण्यं भागमा सुव स हि रत्नधा असि ।रायो जनित्रीं धिषणामुप ब्रुवे स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: śréṣṭham ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ savitaḥ ǀ váreṇyam ǀ bhāgám ǀ ā́ ǀ suva ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ ratna-dhā́ḥ ǀ ási ǀrāyáḥ ǀ jánitrīn ǀ dhiṣáṇām ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send us to-day a portion choice and excellent, O Savitar, for thou art he who dealeth wealth. I cry to Dhiṣaṇā, Mother of opulence. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Savitā, this day bestow upon us excellent and eligible portion, for you verily are the dispenser ofwealth; I recite the praise (of the gods) which is the progenitress of riches; we solicit the kindled fire for ourwelfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Send us to-day a portion choice and excellent, O Savitar, for thou art he who dealeth wealth. I cry to Dhiṣaṇā, Mother of opulence. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पिपर्तु मा तदृतस्य प्रवाचनं देवानां यन्मनुष्या अमन्महि ।विश्वा इदुस्राः स्पळुदेति सूर्यः स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: pípartu ǀ mā ǀ tát ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pra-vā́canam ǀ devā́nām ǀ yát ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ ámanmahi ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ ít ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ spáṭ ǀ út ǀ eti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Further me this declaring of Eternal Law, the Law of Gods, as we mortals acknowledge it! The Sun goes up beholding all the rays of morn. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May that glorification of the gods which men repeat in connection with the rite preserve me; the sunrises visiting all the lustre of the dawn; we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Further me this declaring of Eternal Law, the Law of Gods, as we mortals acknowledge it! The Sun goes up beholding all the rays of morn. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्वेषो अद्य बर्हिषः स्तरीमणि ग्राव्णां योगे मन्मनः साध ईमहे ।आदित्यानां शर्मणि स्था भुरण्यसि स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: adveṣáḥ ǀ adyá ǀ barhíṣaḥ ǀ stárīmaṇi ǀ grā́vṇām ǀ yóge ǀ mánmanaḥ ǀ sā́dhe ǀ īmahe ǀādityā́nām ǀ śármaṇi ǀ sthā́ḥ ǀ bhuraṇyasi ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: This day we pray with innocence in strewing grass, adjusting pressing-stones, and perfecting the hymn. Thou in the Ādityas’ keeping movest restlessly. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: On strewing the sacred grass, and bringing the stones into contact (with the Soma), whereby ourwishes are accomplished, we solicit today the benevolent (Ādityas); abiding in the happiness of those Ādityas,you discharged, worshipper, your duties, we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: This day we pray with innocence in strewing grass, adjusting pressing-stones, and perfecting the hymn. Thou in the Ādityas’ keeping movest restlessly. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो बर्हिः सधमादे बृहद्दिवि देवाँ ईळे सादया सप्त होतॄन् ।इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणं सातये भगं स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ bṛhát ǀ diví ǀ devā́n ǀ īḷe ǀ sādáya ǀ saptá ǀ hótṝn ǀíndram ǀ mitrám ǀ váruṇam ǀ sātáye ǀ bhágam ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: To our great holy grass I bid the Gods at morn to banquet, and will seat them as the seven priests,— Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra, Bhaga for our gain. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: On this our sacred grass, spacious and bright where the gods delight together, do you (Agni) seat theseven ministrant priests,Indra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Bhaga, I praise the gods for their bounty; we solicit the kindled firefor our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: To our great holy grass I bid the Gods at morn to banquet, and will seat them as the seven priests,— Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra, Bhaga for our gain. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त आदित्या आ गता सर्वतातये वृधे नो यज्ञमवता सजोषसः ।बृहस्पतिं पूषणमश्विना भगं स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ādityāḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǀ sarvátātaye ǀ vṛdhé ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ avata ǀ sa-joṣasaḥ ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ aśvínā ǀ bhágam ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither, O Ādityas, for our perfect weal: accordant help our sacrifice that we may thrive. Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and enkindled Agni we implore for happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: Ādityas, come to our ceremony, being well-plural ased protect the sacrifice for our growth; we solicit forour welfare Bṛhaspati,Pūṣan, the Aśvins,Bhaga, and the kindled fire.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither, O Ādityas, for our perfect weal: accordant help our sacrifice that we may thrive. Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and enkindled Agni we implore for happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तन्नो देवा यच्छत सुप्रवाचनं छर्दिरादित्याः सुभरं नृपाय्यं ।पश्वे तोकाय तनयाय जीवसे स्वस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ naḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ yacchata ǀ su-pravācanám ǀ chardíḥ ǀ ādityāḥ ǀ su-bháram ǀ nṛ-pā́yyam ǀpáśve ǀ tokā́ya ǀ tánayāya ǀ jīváse ǀ svastí ǀ agním ǀ sam-idhānám ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ādityas, Gods, vouchsafe that this our home may be praise-worthy, prosperous, our heroes' sure defence, For cattle, for our sons, for progeny, for life. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Aśvins, bestow upon us an excellent, spacious, man-protecting dwelling, for our cattle, oursons and our grandsons to exist; we solicit the kindled fire for our welfare.
verses.griffith_verse: Ādityas, Gods, vouchsafe that this our home may be praise-worthy, prosperous, our heroes' sure defence, For cattle, for our sons, for progeny, for life. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे अद्य मरुतो विश्व ऊती विश्वे भवंत्वग्नयः समिद्धाः ।विश्वे नो देवा अवसा गमंतु विश्वमस्तु द्रविणं वाजो अस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ adyá ǀ marútaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ūtī́ ǀ víśve ǀ bhavantu ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ sám-iddhāḥ ǀvíśve ǀ naḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ ā́ ǀ gamantu ǀ víśvam ǀ astu ǀ dráviṇam ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: This day may all the Maruts, all he near us with aid: may all our fires be well enkindled. May all Gods come to us with gracious favour. May spoil and wealth he ours, and all possessions.
verses.wilson_translation: This day, may all the Maruts, all the (deities), be for our protection; and may all the fires be kindleḍMay all the gods come for our preservation, and may all wealth and food be ours.
verses.griffith_verse: This day may all the Maruts, all he near us with aid: may all our fires be well enkindled. May all Gods come to us with gracious favour. May spoil and wealth he ours, and all possessions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं देवासोऽवथ वाजसातौ यं त्रायध्वे यं पिपृथात्यंहः ।यो वो गोपीथे न भयस्य वेद ते स्याम देववीतये तुरासः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ávatha ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀ yám ǀ trā́yadhve ǀ yám ǀ pipṛthá ǀ áti ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ go-pīthé ǀ ná ǀ bhayásya ǀ véda ǀ té ǀ syāma ǀ devá-vītaye ǀ turāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whom ye aid, O Deities, in battle, whom ye protect and rescue from affliction, Who fears no danger at your milk-libation, -such may we be to feast the Gods, ye Mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: Gods, who are prompt (to grant our desires), may he, whom you guard in battle, whom you defend(from his enemies), whom having extricated from sin, you gratify (in all his wishes), who (secure) in yourprotection; knows not of fear, may we (who are all this) be assiduous in offering sacrifice to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: He whom ye aid, O Deities, in battle, whom ye protect and rescue from affliction, Who fears no danger at your milk-libation, -such may we be to feast the Gods, ye Mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THERE are the Dawn and Night, the grand and beauteous Pair, Earth, Heaven, and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.Indra I call, the Maruts, Mountains, and the Floods, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sky. May Dyaus and Prthivi, wise, true to Holy Law, keep us in safety from distress and injury.Let not malignant Nirrti rule over us. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods. Mother of Mitra and of opulent Varuṇa, may Aditi preserve us safe from all distress.May we obtain the light of heaven without a foe. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. May ringing press-stones keep the Rākṣasas afar, ill dream, and Nirrti, and each voracious fiend.May the Ādityas and the Maruts shelter us. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. Full flow libations; on our grass let Indra sit; Bṛhaspati the singer laud with Sāma hymns!Wise be our hearts' imaginings that we may live. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. Ye Aśvins, make our sacrifice ascend to heaven, and animate the rite that it may send us bliss,Offered with holy oil, with forward-speeding rein. We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day. Hither I call the band of Maruts, swift to hear, great, purifying, bringing bliss, to he our Friends.May we increase our wealth to glorify our name. We crave this graciousfavour of the Gods to-day. We bring the Stay of Life, who makes the waters swell, swift-hearing, Friend of Gods, who waits on sacrifice.May we control that Power, Soma whose rays are bright. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. Alive ourselves, with living sons, devoid of guilt, may we win this with winners by fair means to win.Let the prayer-haters bear our sin to every side. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. Hear us, O ye who claim the worship of mankind, and give us, O ye Gods, the gift for which we pray,Victorious wisdom, fame with heroes and with wealth. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods. We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day, great favour of great Gods, sublime and free from foes,That we may gain rich treasure sprung from hero sons. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. In great enkindled Agni's keeping, and, for bliss, free from all sin before Mitra and Varuṇa.May we share Savitar's best animating help. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. All ye, the Gods whom Savitar the Father of truth, and Varuṇa and Mitra govern,Give us prosperity with hero children, and opulence in kine and various treasure. Savitar, Savitar from cast and westward, Savitar, Savitar from north and southward,Savitar send us perfect health and comfort, Savitar let our days of life be lengthened!

verses.sanskrit: उषासानक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा द्यावाक्षामा वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।इंद्रं हुवे मरुतः पर्वताँ अप आदित्यांद्यावापृथिवी अपः स्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣásānáktā ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ su-péśasā ǀ dyā́vākṣā́mā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀíndram ǀ huve ǀ marútaḥ ǀ párvatān ǀ apáḥ ǀ ādityā́n ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THERE are the Dawn and Night, the grand and beauteous Pair, Earth, Heaven, and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman. Indra I call, the Maruts, Mountains, and the Floods, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sky.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke the vast and beautiful day and night, heaven and earth,Mitraand Varuṇawith Aryaman,Indra, the Maruts, the mountains, the waters, theĀdityas, heaven and earth, the waters (of the firmament), thewhole (host of the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: THERE are the Dawn and Night, the grand and beauteous Pair, Earth, Heaven, and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman. Indra I call, the Maruts, Mountains, and the Floods, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्यौश्च नः पृथिवी च प्रचेतस ऋतावरी रक्षतामंहसो रिषः ।मा दुर्विदत्रा निर्ऋतिर्न ईशत तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: dyáuḥ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ca ǀ prá-cetasā ǀ ṛtávarī ítyṛtá-varī ǀ rakṣatām ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ riṣáḥ ǀmā́ ǀ duḥ-vidátrā ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ īśata ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Dyaus and Prthivi, wise, true to Holy Law, keep us in safety from distress and injury. Let not malignant Nirrti rule over us. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: May the intelligent and truthful heaven and earth defend us from sin, and from malignant; let not themalevolent Nirṛtihave power over us; we solicit today this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: May Dyaus and Prthivi, wise, true to Holy Law, keep us in safety from distress and injury. Let not malignant Nirrti rule over us. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्मान्नो अदितिः पात्वंहसो माता मित्रस्य वरुणस्य रेवतः ।स्वर्वज्ज्योतिरवृकं नशीमहि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasmāt ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ pātu ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ mātā́ ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ revátaḥ ǀsváḥ-vat ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ avṛkám ǀ naśīmahi ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mother of Mitra and of opulent Varuṇa, may Aditi preserve us safe from all distress. May we obtain the light of heaven without a foe. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: May Aditi, the mother of the opulent Mitraand Varuṇa, preserve us from all sin, may we hasten tocelestial light, which is free from oppressors; we solicit today this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Mother of Mitra and of opulent Varuṇa, may Aditi preserve us safe from all distress. May we obtain the light of heaven without a foe. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावा वदन्नप रक्षांसि सेधतु दुष्ष्वप्न्यं निर्ऋतिं विश्वमत्रिणं ।आदित्यं शर्म मरुतामशीमहि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vā ǀ vádan ǀ ápa ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ sedhatu ǀ duḥ-svápnyam ǀ níḥ-ṛtim ǀ víśvam ǀ atríṇam ǀādityám ǀ śárma ǀ marútām ǀ aśīmahi ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May ringing press-stones keep the Rākṣasas afar, ill dream, and Nirrti, and each voracious fiend. May the Ādityas and the Maruts shelter us. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: May the sounding stone drive awayrākṣasas, evil dreams,Nirṛti, and every spirit of ill; may weobtain the happiness of theĀdityasand the Maruts; we solicit today this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: May ringing press-stones keep the Rākṣasas afar, ill dream, and Nirrti, and each voracious fiend. May the Ādityas and the Maruts shelter us. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एंद्रो बर्हिः सीदतु पिन्वतामिळा बृहस्पतिः सामभिर्ऋक्वो अर्चतु ।सुप्रकेतं जीवसे मन्म धीमहि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ sī́datu ǀ pínvatām ǀ íḷā ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ ṛkváḥ ǀ arcatu ǀsu-praketám ǀ jīváse ǀ mánma ǀ dhīmahi ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Full flow libations; on our grass let Indra sit; Bṛhaspati the singer laud with Sāma hymns! Wise be our hearts' imaginings that we may live. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrasit down upon the sacred grass; may Iḷā be propitious; may Bṛhaspatithe singer hymnedwith Sāmanshonour us; we offer an intelligent prayer for life; we solcit today this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Full flow libations; on our grass let Indra sit; Bṛhaspati the singer laud with Sāma hymns! Wise be our hearts' imaginings that we may live. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिविस्पृशं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कृणुतं सुम्नमिष्टये ।प्राचीनरश्मिमाहुतं घृतेन तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: divi-spṛ́śam ǀ yajñám ǀ asmā́kam ǀ aśvinā ǀ jīrá-adhvaram ǀ kṛṇutam ǀ sumnám ǀ iṣṭáye ǀprācī́na-raśmim ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ ghṛténa ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Aśvins, make our sacrifice ascend to heaven, and animate the rite that it may send us bliss, Offered with holy oil, with forward-speeding rein. We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, make our sacriice ascend to heaven free from injury, happy for the attainment of our desires;make the fire to which she is offered blaze up towards (the gods); we solicit today this protection of our gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Aśvins, make our sacrifice ascend to heaven, and animate the rite that it may send us bliss, Offered with holy oil, with forward-speeding rein. We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप ह्वये सुहवं मारुतं गणं पावकमृष्वं सख्याय शंभुवं ।रायस्पोषं सौश्रवसाय धीमहि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ hvaye ǀ su-hávam ǀ mā́rutam ǀ gaṇám ǀ pāvakám ǀ ṛṣvám ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ śam-bhúvam ǀrāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ sauśravasā́ya ǀ dhīmahi ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither I call the band of Maruts, swift to hear, great, purifying, bringing bliss, to he our Friends. May we increase our wealth to glorify our name. We crave this graciousfavour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: I invoke for their friendship, the deservedly invoked, purifying, beautiful troops of the Maruts, the giversof felicity, the dispensers of riches; we meditate upon them for the attainemtn of abundant food; we solicit todaythis protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither I call the band of Maruts, swift to hear, great, purifying, bringing bliss, to he our Friends. May we increase our wealth to glorify our name. We crave this graciousfavour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपां पेरुं जीवधन्यं भरामहे देवाव्यं सुहवमध्वरश्रियं ।सुरश्मिं सोममिंद्रियं यमीमहि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ pérum ǀ jīvá-dhanyam ǀ bharāmahe ǀ deva-avyám ǀ su-hávam ǀ adhvara-śríyam ǀsu-raśmím ǀ sómam ǀ indriyám ǀ yamīmahi ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We bring the Stay of Life, who makes the waters swell, swift-hearing, Friend of Gods, who waits on sacrifice. May we control that Power, Soma whose rays are bright. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: We offer the Soma, the protector of the waters, affluent in life, the delighter of the gods, who iswell-praised, the glory of sacrifice, the brilliant-rayed, the vigour which we desire; we solicit today this protectionof the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: We bring the Stay of Life, who makes the waters swell, swift-hearing, Friend of Gods, who waits on sacrifice. May we control that Power, Soma whose rays are bright. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनेम तत्सुसनिता सनित्वभिर्वयं जीवा जीवपुत्रा अनागसः ।ब्रह्मद्विषो विष्वगेनो भरेरत तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: sanéma ǀ tát ǀ su-sanítā ǀ sanítva-bhiḥ ǀ vayám ǀ jīvā́ḥ ǀ jīvá-putrāḥ ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀbrahma-dvíṣaḥ ǀ víṣvak ǀ énaḥ ǀ bharerata ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Alive ourselves, with living sons, devoid of guilt, may we win this with winners by fair means to win. Let the prayer-haters bear our sin to every side. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: Living with living offspring, and free from fault, let us make offerings (to the gods), sharing with thosewho share with us; may those who hate thebrāhmaṇas, carry off our iniquity in different directions; we solicittoday this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Alive ourselves, with living sons, devoid of guilt, may we win this with winners by fair means to win. Let the prayer-haters bear our sin to every side. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये स्था मनोर्यज्ञियास्ते शृणोतन यद्वो देवा ईमहे तद्ददातन ।जैत्रं क्रतुं रयिमद्वीरवद्यशस्तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ sthā́ḥ ǀ mánoḥ ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ té ǀ śṛṇotana ǀ yát ǀ vaḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ ī́mahe ǀ tát ǀ dadātana ǀjáitram ǀ krátum ǀ rayimát ǀ vīrá-vat ǀ yáśaḥ ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hear us, O ye who claim the worship of mankind, and give us, O ye Gods, the gift for which we pray, Victorious wisdom, fame with heroes and with wealth. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Gods, who are entitled to the worship of men, hear (our prayers), and grant us that which we request;(bestow upon us) the intelligence requisite for victory, and fame with wealth, andmaleprogeny; we solicit todaythis protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Hear us, O ye who claim the worship of mankind, and give us, O ye Gods, the gift for which we pray, Victorious wisdom, fame with heroes and with wealth. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महदद्य महतामा वृणीमहेऽवो देवानां बृहतामनर्वणां ।यथा वसु वीरजातं नशामहै तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: mahát ǀ adyá ǀ mahatā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǀ áva��� ǀ devā́nām ǀ bṛhatā́m ǀ anarváṇām ǀyáthā ǀ vásu ǀ vīrá-jātam ǀ náśāmahai ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day, great favour of great Gods, sublime and free from foes, That we may gain rich treasure sprung from hero sons. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: We impolore today the especial protection of the mighty, the great, the irresistible, gods, that we mayobtain riches, andmaleprogeny; we solicit today this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day, great favour of great Gods, sublime and free from foes, That we may gain rich treasure sprung from hero sons. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महो अग्नेः समिधानस्य शर्मण्यनागा मित्रे वरुणे स्वस्तये ।श्रेष्ठे स्याम सवितुः सवीमनि तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: maháḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ sam-idhānásya ǀ śármaṇi ǀ ánāgāḥ ǀ mitré ǀ váruṇe ǀ svastáye ǀśréṣṭhe ǀ syāma ǀ savitúḥ ǀ sávīmani ǀ tát ǀ devā́nām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: In great enkindled Agni's keeping, and, for bliss, free from all sin before Mitra and Varuṇa. May we share Savitar's best animating help. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.wilson_translation: May we free from sin be in the (enjoyment of the) happiness of the mighty kindled Agni; and in (thekeeping of)Mitraand Varuṇafor our welfare; may we be among the excellent progeny of Savitā; we solicittoday this protection of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: In great enkindled Agni's keeping, and, for bliss, free from all sin before Mitra and Varuṇa. May we share Savitar's best animating help. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये सवितुः सत्यसवस्य विश्वे मित्रस्य व्रते वरुणस्य देवाः ।ते सौभगं वीरवद्गोमदप्नो दधातन द्रविणं चित्रमस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ savitúḥ ǀ satyá-savasya ǀ víśve ǀ mitrásya ǀ vraté ǀ váruṇasya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀté ǀ sáubhagam ǀ vīrá-vat ǀ gó-mat ǀ ápnaḥ ǀ dádhātana ǀ dráviṇam ǀ citrám ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: All ye, the Gods whom Savitar the Father of truth, and Varuṇa and Mitra govern, Give us prosperity with hero children, and opulence in kine and various treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Universal gods, who (take part) in the functions of Savitā, the parent of truth, of Mitraand Varuṇa,confer upon us auspicious and honourable wealth, comprisingmaleprogeny, and cattle, and (pious) acts.
verses.griffith_verse: All ye, the Gods whom Savitar the Father of truth, and Varuṇa and Mitra govern, Give us prosperity with hero children, and opulence in kine and various treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सविता पश्चातात्सविता पुरस्तात्सवितोत्तरात्तात्सविताधरात्तात् ।सविता नः सुवतु सर्वतातिं सविता नो रासतां दीर्घमायुः ॥
verses.transliteration: savitā́ ǀ paścā́tāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ purástāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ uttarā́ttāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ adharā́ttāt ǀsavitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ suvatu ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ savitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rāsatām ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Savitar, Savitar from cast and westward, Savitar, Savitar from north and southward, Savitar send us perfect health and comfort, Savitar let our days of life be lengthened!
verses.wilson_translation: May Savitāon the west, Savitā on the east, Savitā on the north, Savitā on the south, may Savitāsend us all desired wealth, may Savitā bestow upon us long life.
verses.griffith_verse: Savitar, Savitar from cast and westward, Savitar, Savitar from north and southward, Savitar send us perfect health and comfort, Savitar let our days of life be lengthened!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVII. Sūrya.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Do homage unto Varuṇa's and Mitra's Eye: offer this solemn worship to the Mighty God,Who seeth far away, the Ensign, born of Gods. Sing praises unto Sūrya, to the Son of Dyaus. May this my truthful speech guard me on every side wherever heaven and earth and days are spread abroad.All else that is in motion finds a place of rest: the waters ever flow and ever mounts the Sun. No godless man from time remotest draws thee down when thou art driving forth with winged dappled Steeds.One lustre waits upon thee moving to the cast, and, Sūrya, thou arisest with a different light. O Sūrya, with the light whereby thou scatterest gloom, and with thy ray impellest every moving thing,Keep far from us all feeble, worthless sacrifice, and drive away disease and every evil dream. Sent forth thou guardest well the Universe's law, and in thy wonted way arisest free from wrath.When Sūrya, we address our prayers to thee to-day, may the Gods favour this our purpose and desire. This invocation, these our words may Heaven and Earth, and Indra and the Waters and the Maruts hear.Ne’er may we suffer want in presence of the Sun, and, living happy lives, may we attain old age. Cheerful in spirit, evermore, and keen of sight, with store of children, free from sickness and from sin,Long-living, may we look, O Sūrya, upon thee uprising day by day, thou great as Mitra is! Sūrya, may we live long and look upon thee still, thee, O Far-seeing One, bringing the glorious light,The radiant God, the spring of joy to every eye, as thou art mounting up o’er the high shining flood. Thou by whose lustre all the world of life comes forth, and by thy beams again returns unto its rest,O Sūrya with the golden hair, ascend for us day after day, still bringing purer innocence. Bless us with shine, bless us with perfect daylight, bless us with cold, with fervent heat and lustre.Bestow on us, O Sūrya, varied riches, to bless us in our home and when we travel. Gods, to our living creatures of both kinds vouchsafe protection, both to bipeds and to quadrupeds,That they may drink and eat invigorating food. So grant us health and strength and perfect innocence. If by some grievous sin we have provoked the Gods, O Deities, with the tongue or thoughtlessness of heart,That guilt, O Vasus, lay upon the Evil One, on him who ever leads us into deep distress.

verses.sanskrit: नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत ।दूरेदृशे देवजाताय केतवे दिवस्पुत्राय सूर्याय शंसत ॥
verses.transliteration: námaḥ ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ cákṣase ǀ maháḥ ǀ devā́ya ǀ tát ǀ ṛtám ǀ saparyata ǀdūre-dṛ́śe ǀ devá-jātāya ǀ ketáve ǀ diváḥ ǀ putrā́ya ǀ sū́ryāya ǀ śaṃsata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do homage unto Varuṇa's and Mitra's Eye: offer this solemn worship to the Mighty God, Who seeth far away, the Ensign, born of Gods. Sing praises unto Sūrya, to the Son of Dyaus.
verses.wilson_translation: (Having offered) adoration to Sūrya, the beholder of Mitraand Varuṇa, the mighty, the divine, thefar-seer, the god-born, the manifester (of all things), the son of heaven; celebrate the rite enjoined by him, andsing his praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Do homage unto Varuṇa's and Mitra's Eye: offer this solemn worship to the Mighty God, Who seeth far away, the Ensign, born of Gods. Sing praises unto Sūrya, to the Son of Dyaus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सा मा सत्योक्तिः परि पातु विश्वतो द्यावा च यत्र ततनन्नहानि च ।विश्वमन्यन्नि विशते यदेजति विश्वाहापो विश्वाहोदेति सूर्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́ ǀ mā ǀ satyá-uktiḥ ǀ pári ǀ pātu ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ dyā́vā ǀ ca ǀ yátra ǀ tatánan ǀ áhāni ǀ ca ǀvíśvam ǀ anyát ǀ ní ǀ viśate ǀ yát ǀ éjati ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ út ǀ eti ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this my truthful speech guard me on every side wherever heaven and earth and days are spread abroad. All else that is in motion finds a place of rest: the waters ever flow and ever mounts the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: May that world of truth everywhere protect me, through which it is that the heaven and earth, and daysand nights, extend; all the rest of creation which trembles has rest (there); the waters daily (flow), the sun risesevery day.
verses.griffith_verse: May this my truthful speech guard me on every side wherever heaven and earth and days are spread abroad. All else that is in motion finds a place of rest: the waters ever flow and ever mounts the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न ते अदेवः प्रदिवो नि वासते यदेतशेभिः पतरै रथर्यसि ।प्राचीनमन्यदनु वर्तते रज उदन्येन ज्योतिषा यासि सूर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ te ǀ ádevaḥ ǀ pra-dívaḥ ǀ ní ǀ vāsate ǀ yát ǀ etaśébhiḥ ǀ pataráiḥ ǀ ratharyási ǀprācī́nam ǀ anyát ǀ ánu ǀ vartate ǀ rájaḥ ǀ út ǀ anyéna ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ yāsi ǀ sūrya ǁ
verses.english_translation: No godless man from time remotest draws thee down when thou art driving forth with winged dappled Steeds. One lustre waits upon thee moving to the cast, and, Sūrya, thou arisest with a different light.
verses.wilson_translation: No ancientrākṣasaabides,Sūrya, near you when you desire to yoke to your chariot your rapidsteeds; one ancient radiance follows (you) while you rise with another.
verses.griffith_verse: No godless man from time remotest draws thee down when thou art driving forth with winged dappled Steeds. One lustre waits upon thee moving to the cast, and, Sūrya, thou arisest with a different light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येन सूर्य ज्योतिषा बाधसे तमो जगच्च विश्वमुदियर्षि भानुना ।तेनास्मद्विश्वामनिरामनाहुतिमपामीवामप दुष्ष्वप्न्यं सुव ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ sūrya ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ bā́dhase ǀ támaḥ ǀ jágat ǀ ca ǀ víśvam ǀ ut-iyárṣi ǀ bhānúnā ǀténa ǀ asmát ǀ víśvām ǀ ánirām ǀ ánāhutim ǀ ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-svápnyam ǀ suva ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Sūrya, with the light whereby thou scatterest gloom, and with thy ray impellest every moving thing, Keep far from us all feeble, worthless sacrifice, and drive away disease and every evil dream.
verses.wilson_translation: With that light,Sūrya, with which you disperse the darkness, and with that radiance with which youquicken every moving thing, remove from us all famine, neglect of oblations, sickness and evil dreams.
verses.griffith_verse: O Sūrya, with the light whereby thou scatterest gloom, and with thy ray impellest every moving thing, Keep far from us all feeble, worthless sacrifice, and drive away disease and every evil dream.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्य हि प्रेषितो रक्षसि व्रतमहेळयन्नुच्चरसि स्वधा अनु ।यदद्य त्वा सूर्योपब्रवामहै तं नो देवा अनु मंसीरत क्रतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasya ǀ hí ǀ prá-iṣitaḥ ǀ rákṣasi ǀ vratám ǀ áheḷayan ǀ ut-cárasi ǀ svadhā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀyát ǀ adyá ǀ tvā ǀ sūrya ǀ upa-brávāmahai ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ maṃsīrata ǀ krátum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sent forth thou guardest well the Universe's law, and in thy wonted way arisest free from wrath. When Sūrya, we address our prayers to thee to-day, may the Gods favour this our purpose and desire.
verses.wilson_translation: When invoked, you who are genitive le protect the rite of every (worshipper); you rise after the svadhāofferings; when today we call upon you, may the gods be propitious to our sacred acts.
verses.griffith_verse: Sent forth thou guardest well the Universe's law, and in thy wonted way arisest free from wrath. When Sūrya, we address our prayers to thee to-day, may the Gods favour this our purpose and desire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं नो द्यावापृथिवी तन्न आप इंद्रः शृण्वंतु मरुतो हवं वचः ।मा शूने भूम सूर्यस्य संदृशि भद्रं जीवंतो जरणामशीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ naḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ śṛṇvantu ǀ marútaḥ ǀ hávam ǀ vácaḥ ǀmā́ ǀ śū́ne ǀ bhūma ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ sam-dṛ́śi ǀ bhadrám ǀ jī́vantaḥ ǀ jaraṇā́m ǀ aśīmahi ǁ
