verses.english_translation: This invocation, these our words may Heaven and Earth, and Indra and the Waters and the Maruts hear. Ne’er may we suffer want in presence of the Sun, and, living happy lives, may we attain old age.
verses.wilson_translation: May heaven and earth, may the waters, may Indra, and the Maruts, hear this our invocation and thisour praise; may we not be in sorrow at the sight of the Sun; diving long, may we attain a prosperous old age.
verses.griffith_verse: This invocation, these our words may Heaven and Earth, and Indra and the Waters and the Maruts hear. Ne’er may we suffer want in presence of the Sun, and, living happy lives, may we attain old age.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वाहा त्वा सुमनसः सुचक्षसः प्रजावंतो अनमीवा अनागसः ।उद्यंतं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिवे ज्योग्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvā́hā ǀ tvā ǀ su-mánasaḥ ǀ su-cákṣasaḥ ǀ prajā́-vantaḥ ǀ anamīvā́ḥ ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀut-yántam ǀ tvā ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ jyók ǀ jīvā́ḥ ǀ práti ǀ paśyema ǀ sūrya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cheerful in spirit, evermore, and keen of sight, with store of children, free from sickness and from sin, Long-living, may we look, O Sūrya, upon thee uprising day by day, thou great as Mitra is!
verses.wilson_translation: May we, constantly happy in mind, sound of sight, blessed with posterity, exempt from sickness,devoid of sin, daily (worship you); may we, enjoying long life behold you,Sūrya, who are the cherisher of yourfriends rising day by day.
verses.griffith_verse: Cheerful in spirit, evermore, and keen of sight, with store of children, free from sickness and from sin, Long-living, may we look, O Sūrya, upon thee uprising day by day, thou great as Mitra is!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महि ज्योतिर्बिभ्रतं त्वा विचक्षण भास्वंतं चक्षुषेचक्षुषे मयः ।आरोहंतं बृहतः पाजसस्परि वयं जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ bíbhratam ǀ tvā ǀ vi-cakṣaṇa ǀ bhā́svantam ǀ cákṣuṣe-cakṣuṣe ǀ máyaḥ ǀā-róhantam ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ pā́jasaḥ ǀ pári ǀ vayám ǀ jīvā́ḥ ǀ práti ǀ paśyema ǀ sūrya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sūrya, may we live long and look upon thee still, thee, O Far-seeing One, bringing the glorious light, The radiant God, the spring of joy to every eye, as thou art mounting up o’er the high shining flood.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, enoying (long) life, day by day behold you,Sūrya, who glance over all things, invested withgreat lustre, radiant, giving joy to every eye, and rising above the vast and mighty (ocean).
verses.griffith_verse: Sūrya, may we live long and look upon thee still, thee, O Far-seeing One, bringing the glorious light, The radiant God, the spring of joy to every eye, as thou art mounting up o’er the high shining flood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य ते विश्वा भुवनानि केतुना प्र चेरते नि च विशंते अक्तुभिः ।अनागास्त्वेन हरिकेश सूर्याह्नाह्ना नो वस्यसावस्यसोदिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ te ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ ketúnā ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ ī́rate ǀ ní ǀ ca ǀ viśánte ǀ aktú-bhiḥ ǀanāgāḥ-tvéna ǀ hari-keśa ǀ sūrya ǀ áhnā-ahnā ǀ naḥ ǀ vásyasā-vasyasā ǀ út ǀ ihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou by whose lustre all the world of life comes forth, and by thy beams again returns unto its rest, O Sūrya with the golden hair, ascend for us day after day, still bringing purer innocence.
verses.wilson_translation: Golden-haired Sūrya, by whose guidance all beings move (by day), and repose by night, do youcome to us with freedom from sin, and more felicitous (life) every day.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou by whose lustre all the world of life comes forth, and by thy beams again returns unto its rest, O Sūrya with the golden hair, ascend for us day after day, still bringing purer innocence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शं नो भव चक्षसा शं नो अह्ना शं भानुना शं हिमा शं घृणेन ।यथा शमध्वंछमसद्दुरोणे तत्सूर्य द्रविणं धेहि चित्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ cákṣasā ǀ sám ǀ naḥ ǀ áhnā ǀ śám ǀ bhānúnā ǀ śám ǀ himā́ ǀ śám ǀ ghṛṇéna ǀyáthā ǀ śám ǀ ádhvan ǀ śám ǀ ásat ǀ duroṇé ǀ tát ǀ sūrya ǀ dráviṇam ǀ dhehi ǀ citrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bless us with shine, bless us with perfect daylight, bless us with cold, with fervent heat and lustre. Bestow on us, O Sūrya, varied riches, to bless us in our home and when we travel.
verses.wilson_translation: Be propitious to us with light; be propitious to us with sunshine; be propitious to us with warmth; bepropitious to us with frost; and grant us,Sūrya, various wealth, whereby we may prosper on the road and in thehouse.
verses.griffith_verse: Bless us with shine, bless us with perfect daylight, bless us with cold, with fervent heat and lustre. Bestow on us, O Sūrya, varied riches, to bless us in our home and when we travel.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं देवा उभयाय जन्मने शर्म यच्छत द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ।अदत्पिबदूर्जयमानमाशितं तदस्मे शं योररपो दधातन ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ devāḥ ǀ ubháyāya ǀ jánmane ǀ śárma ǀ yacchata ǀ dvi-páde ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǀadát ǀ píbat ǀ ūrjáyamānam ǀ ā́śitam ǀ tát ǀ asmé íti ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǀ arapáḥ ǀ dadhātana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, to our living creatures of both kinds vouchsafe protection, both to bipeds and to quadrupeds, That they may drink and eat invigorating food. So grant us health and strength and perfect innocence.
verses.wilson_translation: Bestow, gods, felicity upon both (classes) of our living beings, bipeds and quadrupeds, so that,whether they be eating or drinking, they may be strong and healthy; so grant to us happiness, plural asure andfreedom from sin.
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, to our living creatures of both kinds vouchsafe protection, both to bipeds and to quadrupeds, That they may drink and eat invigorating food. So grant us health and strength and perfect innocence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वो देवाश्चकृम जिह्वया गुरु मनसो वा प्रयुती देवहेळनं ।अरावा यो नो अभि दुच्छुनायते तस्मिंतदेनो वसवो नि धेतन ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vaḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ cakṛmá ǀ jihváyā ǀ gurú ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ vā ǀ prá-yutī ǀ deva-héḷanam ǀárāvā ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ducchuna-yáte ǀ tásmin ǀ tát ǀ énaḥ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ ní ǀ dhetana ǁ
verses.english_translation: If by some grievous sin we have provoked the Gods, O Deities, with the tongue or thoughtlessness of heart, That guilt, O Vasus, lay upon the Evil One, on him who ever leads us into deep distress.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever sin, great and exciting the wrath of the gods, we have committed against you, O gods, bythe tongue, or the working of the mind, do you,Vasu, transfer that sin to him, who assailing terrifies us.
verses.griffith_verse: If by some grievous sin we have provoked the Gods, O Deities, with the tongue or thoughtlessness of heart, That guilt, O Vasus, lay upon the Evil One, on him who ever leads us into deep distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXVIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O INDRA, in this battle great and glorious, in this loud din of war help us to victory,Where in the strife for kine among bold ring-decked men arrows fly all around and heroes are subdued. At home disclose to us opulence rich in food, streaming with milk, O Indra, meet to be renowned.Śakra, may we be thine, the friendly Conqueror's: even as we desire, O Vasu, so do thou. The godless man, much-lauded Indra, whether he be Dāsa or be Ārya, who would war with us,—Easy to conquer he for thee, with us, these foes: with thee may we subdue them in the clash of fight. Him who must be invoked by many and by few, who standeth nigh with comfort in the war of men,Indra, famed Hero, winner in the deadly strife, let us bring hitherward to-day to favour us. For, Indra, I have heard thee called Self. capturer, One, Steer! who never yields, who urges even the churl.Release thyself from Kutsa and come hither. How shall one like thee sit still bound that he may not move?

verses.sanskrit: अस्मिन्न इंद्र पृत्सुतौ यशस्वति शिमीवति क्रंदसि प्राव सातये ।यत्र गोषाता धृषितेषु खादिषु विष्वक्पतंति दिद्यवो नृषाह्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: asmín ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ pṛtsutáu ǀ yáśasvati ǀ śímī-vati ǀ krándasi ǀ prá ǀ ava ǀ sātáye ǀyátra ǀ gó-sātā ǀ dhṛṣitéṣu ǀ khādíṣu ǀ víṣvak ǀ pátanti ǀ didyávaḥ ǀ nṛ-sáhye ǁ
verses.english_translation: O INDRA, in this battle great and glorious, in this loud din of war help us to victory, Where in the strife for kine among bold ring-decked men arrows fly all around and heroes are subdued.
verses.wilson_translation: You shout,Indra, in this glorious and arduous conflict, and assist us to the acquisition (of spoil), in thisbattle where cows are won and men overpowered, wherein the weapons descend on every side upon the fierceand courageous combatants.
verses.griffith_verse: O INDRA, in this battle great and glorious, in this loud din of war help us to victory, Where in the strife for kine among bold ring-decked men arrows fly all around and heroes are subdued.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स नः क्षुमंतं सदने व्यूर्णुहि गोअर्णसं रयिमिंद्र श्रवाय्यं ।स्याम ते जयतः शक्र मेदिनो यथा वयमुश्मसि तद्वसो कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ kṣu-mántam ǀ sádane ǀ ví ǀ ūrṇuhi ǀ gó-arṇasam ǀ rayím ǀ indra ǀ śravā́yyam ǀsyā́ma ǀ te ǀ jáyataḥ ǀ śakra ǀ medínaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ vayám ǀ uśmási ǀ tát ǀ vaso íti ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: At home disclose to us opulence rich in food, streaming with milk, O Indra, meet to be renowned. Śakra, may we be thine, the friendly Conqueror's: even as we desire, O Vasu, so do thou.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, heap up in our dwelling famous riches, comprising food and herds of cattle; may we,Śakra, be vigorous (through the favour) of you, the victorious; grant us,Vasu, that which we desire.
verses.griffith_verse: At home disclose to us opulence rich in food, streaming with milk, O Indra, meet to be renowned. Śakra, may we be thine, the friendly Conqueror's: even as we desire, O Vasu, so do thou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो नो दास आर्यो वा पुरुष्टुतादेव इंद्र युधये चिकेतति ।अस्माभिष्टे सुषहाः संतु शत्रवस्त्वया वयं तान्वनुयाम संगमे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dā́saḥ ǀ ā́ryaḥ ǀ vā ǀ puru-stuta ǀ ádevaḥ ǀ indra ǀ yudháye ǀ cíketati ǀasmā́bhiḥ ǀ te ǀ su-sáhāḥ ǀ santu ǀ śátravaḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ vayám ǀ tā́n ǀ vanuyāma ǀ sam-gamé ǁ
verses.english_translation: The godless man, much-lauded Indra, whether he be Dāsa or be Ārya, who would war with us,— Easy to conquer he for thee, with us, these foes: with thee may we subdue them in the clash of fight.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the praised of many, may he who proposes to assail us, whether he be adāsa, anārya, or anenemy of the gods; through your aid may all (such) foes be easily overcome by us; through you may we destroythem in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: The godless man, much-lauded Indra, whether he be Dāsa or be Ārya, who would war with us,— Easy to conquer he for thee, with us, these foes: with thee may we subdue them in the clash of fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो दभ्रेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भूरिभिर्यो अभीके वरिवोविन्नृषाह्ये ।तं विखादे सस्निमद्य श्रुतं नरमर्वांचमिंद्रमवसे करामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ dabhrébhiḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhū́ri-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ abhī́ke ǀ varivaḥ-vít ǀ nṛ-sáhye ǀtám ǀ vi-khādé ǀ sásnim ǀ adyá ǀ śrutám ǀ náram ǀ arvā́ñcam ǀ índram ǀ ávase ǀ karāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him who must be invoked by many and by few, who standeth nigh with comfort in the war of men, Indra, famed Hero, winner in the deadly strife, let us bring hitherward to-day to favour us.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us bring before us today for ur protection that Indra, the pure, the renowned, the leader of rites,who in the main-destroying, all-devouring conflict, is the winner of wealth; who is to be invoked by few and many.
verses.griffith_verse: Him who must be invoked by many and by few, who standeth nigh with comfort in the war of men, Indra, famed Hero, winner in the deadly strife, let us bring hitherward to-day to favour us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्ववृजं हि त्वामहमिंद्र शुश्रवानानुदं वृषभ रध्रचोदनं ।प्र मुंचस्व परि कुत्सादिहा गहि किमु त्वावान्मुष्कयोर्बद्ध आसते ॥
verses.transliteration: sva-vṛ́jam ǀ hí ǀ tvā́m ǀ ahám ǀ indra ǀ śuśráva ǀ ananu-dám ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ radhra-códanam ǀprá ǀ muñcasva ǀ pári ǀ kútsāt ǀ ihá ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ kím ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvā́-vān ǀ muṣkáyoḥ ǀ baddháḥ ǀ āsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: For, Indra, I have heard thee called Self. capturer, One, Steer! who never yields, who urges even the churl. Release thyself from Kutsa and come hither. How shall one like thee sit still bound that he may not move?
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, showerer of benefits, I have heard of you, the self-mutilator, the giver of unexpected strength,encouragin the prosperous; set yourself free from Kutsa, and come here; how should such a one as you remainso bound?
verses.griffith_verse: For, Indra, I have heard thee called Self. capturer, One, Steer! who never yields, who urges even the churl. Release thyself from Kutsa and come hither. How shall one like thee sit still bound that he may not move?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XXXIX. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As ’twere the name of father, easy to invoke, we all assembled here invoke this Car of yours,Aśvins, your swiftly-rolling circumambient Car which he who worships must invoke at eve and dawn. Awake all pleasant strains and let the hymns flow forth: raise up abundant fulness: this is our desire.Aśvins, bestow on us a glorious heritage, and give our princes treasure fair as Soma is. Ye are the bliss of her who groweth old at home, and helpers of the slow although he linger last.Men call you too, Nāsatyas, healers of the blind, the thin and feeble, and the man with broken bones. Ye made Cyavāna, weak and worn with length of days, young again, like a car, that he had power to move.Ye lifted up the son of Tugra from the floods. At our libations must all these your acts be praised. We will declare among the folk your ancient deeds heroic; yea, ye were Physicians bringing health.You, you who must be lauded, will we bring for aid, so that this foe of ours, O Aśvins, may believe. Listen to me, O Aśvins; I have cried to you. Give me-your aid as sire and mother aid their son.Poor, without kin or friend or ties of blood am I. Save me before it be too late, from this my curse. Ye, mounted on your chariot brought to Vimada the comely maid of Purumitra as a bride.Ye, came unto the calling of the weakling's dame, and granted noble offspring to the happy wife. Ye gave a ain the vigour of his youthful life to tge sage Kali when old age was coming nigh.Ye rescued Vandana and raised him from the pit, and in a moment gave Viśpalā power to move. Ye Aśvins Twain, endowed with manly strength, brought forth Reblia when hidden in the cave and well-nigh dead,Freed Saptavadliri, and for Atri caused the pit heated with fire to be a pleasant resting-place. On Pedu ye bestowed, Aśvins, a courser white, mighty with nine-and-ninety varied gifts of strength,A horse to be renowned, who bore his friend at speed, joy-giving, Bhaga-like to be invoked of men. From no side, ye Two Kings whom none may check or stay, doth grief, distress, or danger come u on the manWhom, Aśvins swift to hear, borne on your glowing path, ye with your Consort make the foremost in the race. Come on that Chariot which the Ṛbhus wrought for you, the Chariot, Aśvins, that is speedier than thought,At harnessing whereof Heaven's Daughter springs to birth, and from Vivasvān come auspicious Night and Day. Come, Conquerors of the sundered mountain, to our home, Aśvins who made the cow stream milk for Śayu's sake,Ye who delivered even from the wolf's deep throat and set again at liberty the swallowed quail. We have prepared this laud for you, O Aśvins, and, like the Bhṛgus, as a car have framed it,Have decked it as a maid to meet the bridegroom, and brought it as a son, our stay for ever.

verses.sanskrit: यो वां परिज्मा सुवृदश्विना रथो दोषामुषासो हव्यो हविष्मता ।शश्वत्तमासस्तमु वामिदं वयं पितुर्न नाम सुहवं हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ vām ǀ pári-jmā ǀ su-vṛ́t ǀ aśvinā ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ doṣā́m ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ havíṣmatā ǀśaśvat-tamā́saḥ ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ vām ǀ idám ǀ vayám ǀ pitúḥ ǀ ná ǀ nā́ma ǀ su-hávam ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: As ’twere the name of father, easy to invoke, we all assembled here invoke this Car of yours, Aśvins, your swiftly-rolling circumambient Car which he who worships must invoke at eve and dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: We from very ancient times invoke,Aśvins, by a name as venerable as that of a father, this yourglorious chariot, which travels all around, which turns, well, and which is to be invoked morning and evening bythe worshipper.
verses.griffith_verse: As ’twere the name of father, easy to invoke, we all assembled here invoke this Car of yours, Aśvins, your swiftly-rolling circumambient Car which he who worships must invoke at eve and dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चोदयतं सूनृताः पिन्वतं धिय उत्पुरंधीरीरयतं तदुश्मसि ।यशसं भागं कृणुतं नो अश्विना सोमं न चारुं मघवत्सु नस्कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: codáyatam ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ pínvatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ út ǀ púram-dhīḥ ǀ īrayatam ǀ tát ǀ uśmasi ǀyaśásam ǀ bhāgám ǀ kṛṇutam ǀ naḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ sómam ǀ ná ǀ cā́rum ǀ maghávat-su ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Awake all pleasant strains and let the hymns flow forth: raise up abundant fulness: this is our desire. Aśvins, bestow on us a glorious heritage, and give our princes treasure fair as Soma is.
verses.wilson_translation: Stimulate,Aśvins, our words of truth, perfect (our) sacred rites, and inspire (our) numerous facultires;this (is what) we wish; grant us a glorious portion (cf. wealth); put us like prosperous Somaamong the affluent.
verses.griffith_verse: Awake all pleasant strains and let the hymns flow forth: raise up abundant fulness: this is our desire. Aśvins, bestow on us a glorious heritage, and give our princes treasure fair as Soma is.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमाजुरश्चिद्भवथो युवं भगोऽनाशोश्चिदवितारापमस्य चित् ।अंधस्य चिन्नासत्या कृशस्य चिद्युवामिदाहुर्भिषजा रुतस्य चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: amā-júraḥ ǀ cit ǀ bhavathaḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ anāśóḥ ǀ cit ǀ avitā́rā ǀ apamásya ǀ cit ǀandhásya ǀ cit ǀ nāsatyā ǀ kṛśásya ǀ cit ǀ yuvā́m ǀ ít ǀ āhuḥ ǀ bhiṣájā ǀ rutásya ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye are the bliss of her who groweth old at home, and helpers of the slow although he linger last. Men call you too, Nāsatyas, healers of the blind, the thin and feeble, and the man with broken bones.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Nāsatyās, are the good fortune of a damsel growing old in (her father's) mansion; thepreservers of the famishing, the protectors of the object, of the blind, of the feeble, they call you the physicians ofthe sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye are the bliss of her who groweth old at home, and helpers of the slow although he linger last. Men call you too, Nāsatyas, healers of the blind, the thin and feeble, and the man with broken bones.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरथाय तक्षथुः ।निष्टौग्र्यमूहथुरद्भ्यस्परि विश्वेत्ता वां सवनेषु प्रवाच्या ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ cyávānam ǀ sanáyam ǀ yáthā ǀ rátham ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yúvānam ǀ caráthāya ǀ takṣathuḥ ǀníḥ ǀ taugryám ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ pári ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ tā́ ǀ vām ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ pra-vā́cyā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye made Cyavāna, weak and worn with length of days, young again, like a car, that he had power to move. Ye lifted up the son of Tugra from the floods. At our libations must all these your acts be praised.
verses.wilson_translation: You made the aged Cyavana, when like a worn out chariot, again young and able to go; you bore theson of Tugraabove the waters; all these your (exploits) are to be celebrated at our sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye made Cyavāna, weak and worn with length of days, young again, like a car, that he had power to move. Ye lifted up the son of Tugra from the floods. At our libations must all these your acts be praised.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुराणा वां वीर्या प्र ब्रवा जनेऽथो हासथुर्भिषजा मयोभुवा ।ता वां नु नव्याववसे करामहेऽयं नासत्या श्रदरिर्यथा दधत् ॥
verses.transliteration: purāṇā́ ǀ vām ǀ vīryā́ ǀ prá ǀ brava ǀ jáne ǀ átho íti ǀ ha ǀ āsathuḥ ǀ bhiṣájā ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvā ǀtā́ ǀ vām ǀ nú ǀ návyau ǀ ávase ǀ karāmahe ǀ ayám ǀ nāsatyā ǀ śrát ǀ aríḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ dádhat ǁ
verses.english_translation: We will declare among the folk your ancient deeds heroic; yea, ye were Physicians bringing health. You, you who must be lauded, will we bring for aid, so that this foe of ours, O Aśvins, may believe.
verses.wilson_translation: I proclaim,Aśvins, your ancient exploits among the people, for you were the physicians, the bestowersof felicity; we count you two worthy to be praised for (our) preservation; so that this worshipper Na-satyās, maybelieve (in you).
verses.griffith_verse: We will declare among the folk your ancient deeds heroic; yea, ye were Physicians bringing health. You, you who must be lauded, will we bring for aid, so that this foe of ours, O Aśvins, may believe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं वामह्वे शृणुतं मे अश्विना पुत्रायेव पितरा मह्यं शिक्षतं ।अनापिरज्ञा असजात्यामतिः पुरा तस्या अभिशस्तेरव स्पृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ vām ǀ ahve ǀ śṛṇutám ǀ me ǀ aśvinā ǀ putrā́ya-iva ǀ pitárā ǀ máhyam ǀ śikṣatam ǀánāpiḥ ǀ ájñāḥ ǀ asajātyā́ ǀ ámatiḥ ǀ purā́ ǀ tásyāḥ ǀ abhí-śasteḥ ǀ áva ǀ spṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Listen to me, O Aśvins; I have cried to you. Give me-your aid as sire and mother aid their son. Poor, without kin or friend or ties of blood am I. Save me before it be too late, from this my curse.
verses.wilson_translation: I here, (ghoṣā), invoke you. Here my (invocation),Aśvins, give me (wealth) as parents give to a son;before (it come) beyond the reach of (a course) that has no relatives, ungrateful, without kinsfolk, without belief,(pursues me); save me from that curse before (it reaches me).
verses.griffith_verse: Listen to me, O Aśvins; I have cried to you. Give me-your aid as sire and mother aid their son. Poor, without kin or friend or ties of blood am I. Save me before it be too late, from this my curse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं रथेन विमदाय शुंध्युवं न्यूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्य योषणां ।युवं हवं वध्रिमत्या अगच्छतं युवं सुषुतिं चक्रथुः पुरंधये ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ráthena ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ śundhyúvam ǀ ní ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ puru-mitrásya ǀ yóṣaṇām ǀyuvám ǀ hávam ǀ vadhri-matyā́ḥ ǀ agacchatam ǀ yuvám ǀ sú-sutim ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ púram-dhaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, mounted on your chariot brought to Vimada the comely maid of Purumitra as a bride. Ye, came unto the calling of the weakling's dame, and granted noble offspring to the happy wife.
verses.wilson_translation: You brought, Śundhyu, the daughter of Purumitrato (her husband)Vimada; you came at Vadharimati's invocation, and gave excellent offsprin to her who was full of wisdom.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, mounted on your chariot brought to Vimada the comely maid of Purumitra as a bride. Ye, came unto the calling of the weakling's dame, and granted noble offspring to the happy wife.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं विप्रस्य जरणामुपेयुषः पुनः कलेरकृणुतं युवद्वयः ।युवं वंदनमृश्यदादुदूपथुर्युवं सद्यो विश्पलामेतवे कृथः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ víprasya ǀ jaraṇā́m ǀ upa-īyúṣaḥ ǀ púnaríti ǀ kaléḥ ǀ akṛṇutam ǀ yúvat ǀ váyaḥ ǀyuvám ǀ vándanam ǀ ṛśya-dā́t ǀ út ǀ ūpathuḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ viśpálām ǀ étave ǀ kṛthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye gave a ain the vigour of his youthful life to tge sage Kali when old age was coming nigh. Ye rescued Vandana and raised him from the pit, and in a moment gave Viśpalā power to move.
verses.wilson_translation: You made young again the life of the sage Kali, when approaching old age, you rescued Vandanafrom the well; you quickly enabled Viśapalā to walk.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye gave a ain the vigour of his youthful life to tge sage Kali when old age was coming nigh. Ye rescued Vandana and raised him from the pit, and in a moment gave Viśpalā power to move.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह रेभं वृषणा गुहा हितमुदैरयतं ममृवांसमश्विना ।युवमृबीसमुत तप्तमत्रय ओमन्वंतं चक्रथुः सप्तवध्रये ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ rebhám ǀ vṛṣaṇā ǀ gúhā ǀ hitám ǀ út ǀ airayatam ǀ mamṛ-vā́ṃsam ǀ aśvinā ǀyuvám ǀ ṛbī́sam ǀ utá ǀ taptám ǀ átraye ǀ óman-vantam ǀ cakrathuḥ ǀ saptá-vadhraye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Aśvins Twain, endowed with manly strength, brought forth Reblia when hidden in the cave and well-nigh dead, Freed Saptavadliri, and for Atri caused the pit heated with fire to be a pleasant resting-place.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, shedders of rain, you extricated Rebha when he was plural ced in a cave and was dying; youmade the heated fire-pit cool for Atri; you gave (liberty) to Saptavadhri.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Aśvins Twain, endowed with manly strength, brought forth Reblia when hidden in the cave and well-nigh dead, Freed Saptavadliri, and for Atri caused the pit heated with fire to be a pleasant resting-place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं श्वेतं पेदवेऽश्विनाश्वं नवभिर्वाजैर्नवती च वाजिनं ।चर्कृत्यं ददथुर्द्रावयत्सखं भगं न नृभ्यो हव्यं मयोभुवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ śvetám ǀ pedáve ǀ aśvinā ǀ áśvam ǀ navá-bhiḥ ǀ vā́jaiḥ ǀ navatī́ ǀ ca ǀ vājínam ǀcarkṛ́tyam ǀ dadathuḥ ǀ dravayát-sakham ǀ bhágam ǀ ná ǀ nṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ hávyam ǀ mayaḥ-bhúvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: On Pedu ye bestowed, Aśvins, a courser white, mighty with nine-and-ninety varied gifts of strength, A horse to be renowned, who bore his friend at speed, joy-giving, Bhaga-like to be invoked of men.
verses.wilson_translation: You gave,Aśvins, to Pedua strong white horse with nine-and-ninety (other) steeds, (a horse), active(in combat), putting to flight the friends (of the foe), worthy to be invoked, a source of deligght, like wealth to meṇ
verses.griffith_verse: On Pedu ye bestowed, Aśvins, a courser white, mighty with nine-and-ninety varied gifts of strength, A horse to be renowned, who bore his friend at speed, joy-giving, Bhaga-like to be invoked of men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न तं राजानावदिते कुतश्चन नांहो अश्नोति दुरितं नकिर्भयं ।यमश्विना सुहवा रुद्रवर्तनी पुरोरथं कृणुथः पत्न्या सह ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ rājānau ǀ adite ǀ kútaḥ ǀ caná ǀ ná ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ aśnoti ǀ duḥ-itám ǀ nákiḥ ǀ bhayám ǀyám ǀ aśvinā ǀ su-havā ǀ rudravartanī íti rudra-vartanī ǀ puraḥ-rathám ǀ kṛṇutháḥ ǀ pátnyā ǀ sahá ǁ
verses.english_translation: From no side, ye Two Kings whom none may check or stay, doth grief, distress, or danger come u on the man Whom, Aśvins swift to hear, borne on your glowing path, ye with your Consort make the foremost in the race.
verses.wilson_translation: Lofty soverigns, worthy of invocation, going on roads which are praised in hymns,Aśvins, the manwhom with his wife you plural ce in front of (your) car, encounters not from any quarter wickedness, difficulty, ordanger.
verses.griffith_verse: From no side, ye Two Kings whom none may check or stay, doth grief, distress, or danger come u on the man Whom, Aśvins swift to hear, borne on your glowing path, ye with your Consort make the foremost in the race.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तेन यातं मनसो जवीयसा रथं यं वामृभवश्चक्रुरश्विना ।यस्य योगे दुहिता जायते दिव उभे अहनी सुदिने विवस्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ téna ǀ yātam ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyasā ǀ rátham ǀ yám ǀ vām ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ cakrúḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀyásya ǀ yóge ǀ duhitā́ ǀ jā́yate ǀ diváḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ áhanī íti ǀ sudíne íti su-díne ǀ vivásvataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come on that Chariot which the Ṛbhus wrought for you, the Chariot, Aśvins, that is speedier than thought, At harnessing whereof Heaven's Daughter springs to birth, and from Vivasvān come auspicious Night and Day.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Aśvins, with the chariot that is swifter than thought, which the Ribhusmade for you; inconnection with which the daughter of heaven, (the dawn), is born and both the auspicious day and night from Vivasvat.
verses.griffith_verse: Come on that Chariot which the Ṛbhus wrought for you, the Chariot, Aśvins, that is speedier than thought, At harnessing whereof Heaven's Daughter springs to birth, and from Vivasvān come auspicious Night and Day.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता वर्तिर्यातं जयुषा वि पर्वतमपिन्वतं शयवे धेनुमश्विना ।वृकस्य चिद्वर्तिकामंतरास्याद्युवं शचीभिर्ग्रसिताममुंचतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vartíḥ ǀ yātam ǀ jayúṣā ǀ ví ǀ párvatam ǀ ápinvatam ǀ śayáve ǀ dhenúm ǀ aśvinā ǀvṛ́kasya ǀ cit ǀ vártikām ǀ antáḥ ǀ āsyā́t ǀ yuvám ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ grasitā́m ǀ amuñcatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come, Conquerors of the sundered mountain, to our home, Aśvins who made the cow stream milk for Śayu's sake, Ye who delivered even from the wolf's deep throat and set again at liberty the swallowed quail.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you two,Aśvins, climb the path to the mountain with your triumphant chariot; you have renovatedforŚayu(barren) cow; you liberated by your acts the quail that had been seized from the jaws of the wolf.
verses.griffith_verse: Come, Conquerors of the sundered mountain, to our home, Aśvins who made the cow stream milk for Śayu's sake, Ye who delivered even from the wolf's deep throat and set again at liberty the swallowed quail.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतं वां स्तोममश्विनावकर्मातक्षाम भृगवो न रथं ।न्यमृक्षाम योषणां न मर्ये नित्यं न सूनुं तनयं दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: etám ǀ vām ǀ stómam ǀ aśvinau ǀ akarma ǀ átakṣāma ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rátham ǀní ǀ amṛkṣāma ǀ yóṣaṇām ǀ ná ǀ márye ǀ nítyam ǀ ná ǀ sūnúm ǀ tánayam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have prepared this laud for you, O Aśvins, and, like the Bhṛgus, as a car have framed it, Have decked it as a maid to meet the bridegroom, and brought it as a son, our stay for ever.
verses.griffith_verse: We have prepared this laud for you, O Aśvins, and, like the Bhṛgus, as a car have framed it, Have decked it as a maid to meet the bridegroom, and brought it as a son, our stay for ever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XL. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YOUR radiant Chariot-whither goes it on its way?-who decks it for you, Heroes, for its happy course,Starting at daybreak, visiting each morning every house, borne hitherward through prayer unto the sacrifice? Where are ye, Aśvins, in the evening, where at morn? Where is your haltingplace, where rest ye for the night?Who brings you homeward, as the widow bedward draws her husband's brother, as the bride attracts the groom? Early ye sing forth praise as with a herald's voice, and, meet for worship, go each morning to the house.Whom do ye ever bring to ruin? Unto whose libations come ye, Heroes, like two Sons of Kings? Even as hunters follow two wild elephants, we with oblations call you down at morn and eve.To folk who pay you offierings at appointed times, Chiefs, Lords of splendour, ye bring food to strengthen them. To you, O Aśvins, came the daughter of a King, Ghoṣā, and said, O Heroes, this I beg of you:Be near me in the day, he near me in the night: help me to gain a car-borne chieftain rich in steeds. O Aśvins, ye are wise: as Kutsa comes to men, bring your car nigh the folk of him who sings your praise.The bee, O Aśvins, bears your honey in her mouth, as the maid carries it purified in her hand. To Bhujyu and to Vaśa ye come near with help, O Aśvins, to Sinjara and to Uśanā.Your worshipper secures your friendship for himself. Through your protection I desire felicity. Krsa and Śayu ye protect, ye Aśvins Twain: ye Two assist the widow and the worshipper;And ye throw open, Aśvins, unto those who win the cattle-stall that thunders with its serenfold mouth. The Woman hath brought forth, the Infant hath appeared, the plants of wondrous beauty straightway have sprung up.To him the rivers run as down a deep descent, and he this day becomes their master and their lord. They mourn the living, cry aloud, at sacrifice: the men have set their thoughts upon a distant cast.A lovely thing for fathers who have gathered here,—a joy to husbands,—are the wives their arms shall clasp Of this we have no knowledge. Tall it forth to us, now the youth rests within the chambers of the bride.Fain would we reach the dwelling of the vigorous Steer who loves the kine, O Aśvins: this is our desire. Your favouring grace hath come, ye Lords of ample wealth: Aśvins, our longings are stored up within your hearts.Ye, Lords of splendour, have become our twofold guard: may we as welcome friends reach Aryaman's abode. Even so, rejoicing in the dwelling-place of man, give hero sons and riches to the eloquent.Make a ford, Lords of splendour, where men well may drink: remove the spiteful tree-stump standing in the path. O Aśvins, Wonder-Workers, Lords of lustre, where and with what folk do ye delight yourselves to-day?Who hath detained them with him? Whither are they gone? Unto what sage's or what worshipper's abode?

verses.sanskrit: रथं यांतं कुह को ह वां नरा प्रति द्युमंतं सुविताय भूषति ।प्रातर्यावाणं विभ्वं विशेविशे वस्तोर्वस्तोर्वहमानं धिया शमि ॥
verses.transliteration: rátham ǀ yā́ntam ǀ kúha ǀ káḥ ǀ ha ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀ práti ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ bhūṣati ǀprātaḥ-yā́vānam ǀ vi-bhvám ǀ viśé-viśe ǀ vástoḥ-vastoḥ ǀ váhamānam ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ śámi ǁ
verses.english_translation: YOUR radiant Chariot-whither goes it on its way?-who decks it for you, Heroes, for its happy course, Starting at daybreak, visiting each morning every house, borne hitherward through prayer unto the sacrifice?
verses.wilson_translation: What (worshipper), O leaderes of rites, and where (abiding) glorifies for his good, by his praise at therite, your radiant moving chariot, going (to the sacrifice) at dawn, all-pervading, and bearing (wealth) day afterday to one man after another?
verses.griffith_verse: YOUR radiant Chariot-whither goes it on its way?-who decks it for you, Heroes, for its happy course, Starting at daybreak, visiting each morning every house, borne hitherward through prayer unto the sacrifice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः ।को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥
verses.transliteration: kúha ǀ svit ǀ doṣā́ ǀ kúha ǀ vástoḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ kúha ǀ abhi-pitvám ǀ karataḥ ǀ kúha ǀ ūṣatuḥ ǀkáḥ ǀ vām ǀ śayu-trā́ ǀ vidhávā-iva ǀ deváram ǀ máryam ǀ ná ǀ yóṣā ǀ kṛṇute ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where are ye, Aśvins, in the evening, where at morn? Where is your haltingplace, where rest ye for the night? Who brings you homeward, as the widow bedward draws her husband's brother, as the bride attracts the groom?
verses.wilson_translation: Where are you,Aśvins, by night? Where are you by day? Where do you sojourn? Where do youdwell? Who brings you into his presence in the same plural ce (of sacrifice) as on her couch a widow (brings) herhusband's brother, as a woman (brings) her husband (to her).
verses.griffith_verse: Where are ye, Aśvins, in the evening, where at morn? Where is your haltingplace, where rest ye for the night? Who brings you homeward, as the widow bedward draws her husband's brother, as the bride attracts the groom?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्जरेथे जरणेव कापया वस्तोर्वस्तोर्यजता गच्छथो गृहं ।कस्य ध्वस्रा भवथः कस्य वा नरा राजपुत्रेव सवनाव गच्छथः ॥
verses.transliteration: prātáḥ ǀ jarethe íti ǀ jaraṇā́-iva ǀ kā́payā ǀ vástoḥ-vastoḥ ǀ yajatā́ ǀ gacchathaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǀkásya ǀ dhvasrā́ ǀ bhavathaḥ ǀ kásya ǀ vā ǀ narā ǀ rājaputrā́-iva ǀ sávanā ǀ áva ǀ gacchathaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Early ye sing forth praise as with a herald's voice, and, meet for worship, go each morning to the house. Whom do ye ever bring to ruin? Unto whose libations come ye, Heroes, like two Sons of Kings?
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of rites), you are glorified at dawn like two ancient (monarchs) by the voice (of the caller)entitled to worship, you go day by day to the dwelling (of the worshipper); of whose (faults) are you thedestroyer? To whose oblations do you go like princes?
verses.griffith_verse: Early ye sing forth praise as with a herald's voice, and, meet for worship, go each morning to the house. Whom do ye ever bring to ruin? Unto whose libations come ye, Heroes, like two Sons of Kings?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां मृगेव वारणा मृगण्यवो दोषा वस्तोर्हविषा नि ह्वयामहे ।युवं होत्रामृतुथा जुह्वते नरेषं जनाय वहथः शुभस्पती ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ mṛgā́-iva ǀ vāraṇā́ ǀ mṛgaṇyávaḥ ǀ doṣā́ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ havíṣā ǀ ní ǀ hvayāmahe ǀyuvám ǀ hótrām ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ júhvate ǀ narā ǀ íṣam ǀ jánāya ǀ vahathaḥ ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as hunters follow two wild elephants, we with oblations call you down at morn and eve. To folk who pay you offierings at appointed times, Chiefs, Lords of splendour, ye bring food to strengthen them.
verses.wilson_translation: Like perons hunting two wild elephants, we praise you,Aśvins, with oblations night and day; at all dueseasons, leaders (of rites), (the worshipper) offers you the oblation; do you, who are rulers of the shining (rain),bring food to mankind.
verses.griffith_verse: Even as hunters follow two wild elephants, we with oblations call you down at morn and eve. To folk who pay you offierings at appointed times, Chiefs, Lords of splendour, ye bring food to strengthen them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवां ह घोषा पर्यश्विना यती राज्ञ ऊचे दुहिता पृच्छे वां नरा ।भूतं मे अह्न उत भूतमक्तवेऽश्वावते रथिने शक्तमर्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvā́m ǀ ha ǀ ghóṣā ǀ pári ǀ aśvinā ǀ yatī́ ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ ūce ǀ duhitā́ ǀ pṛcché ǀ vām ǀ narā ǀbhūtám ǀ me ǀ áhne ǀ utá ǀ bhūtam ǀ aktáve ǀ áśva-vate ǀ rathíne ǀ śaktam ǀ árvate ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you, O Aśvins, came the daughter of a King, Ghoṣā, and said, O Heroes, this I beg of you: Be near me in the day, he near me in the night: help me to gain a car-borne chieftain rich in steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Attending upon you,Aśvins, leaders (of rites), I,Ghoṣā, the daughter of king (Kakṣīvat), speak toyou and request you; be (present at) my (sacrifice) by day, and be (present) by night, be able, (to grant favour) tothe son of my brother, who has horses and a chariot.
verses.griffith_verse: To you, O Aśvins, came the daughter of a King, Ghoṣā, and said, O Heroes, this I beg of you: Be near me in the day, he near me in the night: help me to gain a car-borne chieftain rich in steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं कवी ष्ठः पर्यश्विना रथं विशो न कुत्सो जरितुर्नशायथः ।युवोर्ह मक्षा पर्यश्विना मध्वासा भरत निष्कृतं न योषणा ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ kavī́ íti ǀ sthaḥ ǀ pári ǀ aśvinā ǀ rátham ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ kútsaḥ ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ naśāyathaḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ ha ǀ mákṣā ǀ pári ǀ aśvinā ǀ mádhu ǀ āsā́ ǀ bharata ǀ niḥ-kṛtám ǀ ná ǀ yóṣaṇā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, ye are wise: as Kutsa comes to men, bring your car nigh the folk of him who sings your praise. The bee, O Aśvins, bears your honey in her mouth, as the maid carries it purified in her hand.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Aśvins, stand by your chariot; make it approach (the sacrifice) of the worshipper, as Kutsa(made his chariot approach) men, the fly carries your honey, Aśvins, in its mouth as a woman carries purified(honey).
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, ye are wise: as Kutsa comes to men, bring your car nigh the folk of him who sings your praise. The bee, O Aśvins, bears your honey in her mouth, as the maid carries it purified in her hand.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह भुज्युं युवमश्विना वशं युवं शिंजारमुशनामुपारथुः ।युवो ररावा परि सख्यमासते युवोरहमवसा सुम्नमा चके ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ bhujyúm ǀ yuvám ǀ aśvinā ǀ váśam ǀ yuvám ǀ śiñjā́ram ǀ uśánām ǀ úpa ǀ ārathuḥ ǀyuvóḥ ǀ rárāvā ǀ pári ǀ sakhyám ǀ āsate ǀ yuvóḥ ǀ ahám ǀ ávasā ǀ sumnám ǀ ā́ ǀ cake ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Bhujyu and to Vaśa ye come near with help, O Aśvins, to Sinjara and to Uśanā. Your worshipper secures your friendship for himself. Through your protection I desire felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: You came,Aśvins, to the rescue of Bhujyu, you came to the rescue of Vaśa, you came to Śiñjārato (hear) his desirable (praise); the offerer of oblations besieges your friendship; and I desire happiness throughyour protection.
verses.griffith_verse: To Bhujyu and to Vaśa ye come near with help, O Aśvins, to Sinjara and to Uśanā. Your worshipper secures your friendship for himself. Through your protection I desire felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह कृशं युवमश्विना शयुं युवं विधंतं विधवामुरुष्यथः ।युवं सनिभ्यः स्तनयंतमश्विनाप व्रजमूर्णुथः सप्तास्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ ha ǀ kṛśám ǀ yuvám ǀ aśvinā ǀ śayúm ǀ yuvám ǀ vidhántam ǀ vidhávām ǀ uruṣyathaḥ ǀyuvám ǀ saní-bhyaḥ ǀ stanáyantam ǀ aśvinā ǀ ápa ǀ vrajám ǀ ūrṇuthaḥ ǀ saptá-āsyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Krsa and Śayu ye protect, ye Aśvins Twain: ye Two assist the widow and the worshipper; And ye throw open, Aśvins, unto those who win the cattle-stall that thunders with its serenfold mouth.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily,Aśvins, you protect the feeble man; you protectedŚayu; you protect him who worshipsaccording to rule, and the widow, (Vadhrimati); you set open, O Aśvins, for the donors of oblations theseven-mouthed thundering cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: Krsa and Śayu ye protect, ye Aśvins Twain: ye Two assist the widow and the worshipper; And ye throw open, Aśvins, unto those who win the cattle-stall that thunders with its serenfold mouth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जनिष्ट योषा पतयत्कनीनको वि चारुहन्वीरुधो दंसना अनु ।आस्मै रीयंते निवनेव सिंधवोऽस्मा अह्ने भवति तत्पतित्वनं ॥
verses.transliteration: jániṣṭa ǀ yóṣā ǀ patáyat ǀ kanīnakáḥ ǀ ví ǀ ca ǀ áruhan ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ daṃsánāḥ ǀ ánu ǀā́ ǀ asmai ǀ rīyante ǀ nivanā́-iva ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ asmái ǀ áhne ǀ bhavati ǀ tát ǀ pati-tvanám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Woman hath brought forth, the Infant hath appeared, the plants of wondrous beauty straightway have sprung up. To him the rivers run as down a deep descent, and he this day becomes their master and their lord.
verses.wilson_translation: The bride,Aśvins, has been born, let the husband approach; may the plural nts spring up (for him) afterthe rain; for him may the streams flow as if from a declivity; may he invulnerable have the power of a husbandover her.
verses.griffith_verse: The Woman hath brought forth, the Infant hath appeared, the plants of wondrous beauty straightway have sprung up. To him the rivers run as down a deep descent, and he this day becomes their master and their lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जीवं रुदंति वि मयंते अध्वरे दीर्घामनु प्रसितिं दीधियुर्नरः ।वामं पितृभ्यो य इदं समेरिरे मयः पतिभ्यो जनयः परिष्वजे ॥
verses.transliteration: jīvám ǀ rudanti ǀ ví ǀ mayante ǀ adhvaré ǀ dīrghā́m ǀ ánu ǀ prá-sitim ǀ dīdhiyuḥ ǀ náraḥ ǀvāmám ǀ pitṛ́-bhyaḥ ǀ yé ǀ idám ǀ sam-eriré ǀ máyaḥ ǀ páti-bhyaḥ ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ pari-sváje ǁ
verses.english_translation: They mourn the living, cry aloud, at sacrifice: the men have set their thoughts upon a distant cast. A lovely thing for fathers who have gathered here,—a joy to husbands,—are the wives their arms shall clasp
verses.wilson_translation: The husbands who weep for the life (of their wives), make them sit down at the sacrifice, hold in a longembrace, (and) send the Pitṛsthis desirable offspring, upon these husbands the wives (bestow) happiness inorder to be embraced.
verses.griffith_verse: They mourn the living, cry aloud, at sacrifice: the men have set their thoughts upon a distant cast. A lovely thing for fathers who have gathered here,—a joy to husbands,—are the wives their arms shall clasp
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न तस्य विद्म तदु षु प्र वोचत युवा ह यद्युवत्याः क्षेति योनिषु ।प्रियोस्रियस्य वृषभस्य रेतिनो गृहं गमेमाश्विना तदुश्मसि ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tásya ǀ vidma ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ prá ǀ vocata ǀ yúvā ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ yuvatyā́ḥ ǀ kṣéti ǀ yóniṣu ǀpriyá-usriyasya ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ retínaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǀ gamema ǀ aśvinā ǀ tát ǀ uśmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of this we have no knowledge. Tall it forth to us, now the youth rests within the chambers of the bride. Fain would we reach the dwelling of the vigorous Steer who loves the kine, O Aśvins: this is our desire.
verses.wilson_translation: We do not know this (happiness) of his; do you, (Aśvins), clearly explain how it is that the young(husband) dwells in the bride's house; let us, Aśvins, go the dwelling of (my) dear youthful, vigorous, and manlyhusband; this is our desire.
verses.griffith_verse: Of this we have no knowledge. Tall it forth to us, now the youth rests within the chambers of the bride. Fain would we reach the dwelling of the vigorous Steer who loves the kine, O Aśvins: this is our desire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वामगन्त्सुमतिर्वाजिनीवसू न्यश्विना हृत्सु कामा अयंसत ।अभूतं गोपा मिथुना शुभस्पती प्रिया अर्यम्णो दुर्याँ अशीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ agan ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ vājinīvasū íti vājinī-vasū ǀ ní ǀ aśvinā ǀ hṛt-sú ǀ kā́māḥ ǀ ayaṃsata ǀábhūtam ǀ gopā́ ǀ mithunā́ ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ aryamṇáḥ ǀ dúryān ǀ aśīmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your favouring grace hath come, ye Lords of ample wealth: Aśvins, our longings are stored up within your hearts. Ye, Lords of splendour, have become our twofold guard: may we as welcome friends reach Aryaman's abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvins, rich in food, lords of water, twin (associates), may your good will devolve (upon us), may thedesires (of our hearts) be attained; you have been my protectors; may we, (being) beloved, attain the habitationof a husband.
verses.griffith_verse: Your favouring grace hath come, ye Lords of ample wealth: Aśvins, our longings are stored up within your hearts. Ye, Lords of splendour, have become our twofold guard: may we as welcome friends reach Aryaman's abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता मंदसाना मनुषो दुरोण आ धत्तं रयिं सहवीरं वचस्यवे ।कृतं तीर्थं सुप्रपाणं शुभस्पती स्थाणुं पथेष्ठामप दुर्मतिं हतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ mandasānā́ ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ ā́ ǀ dhattám ǀ rayím ǀ sahá-vīram ǀ vacasyáve ǀkṛtám ǀ tīrthám ǀ su-prapānám ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ sthāṇúm ǀ pathe-sthā́m ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-matím ǀ hatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even so, rejoicing in the dwelling-place of man, give hero sons and riches to the eloquent. Make a ford, Lords of splendour, where men well may drink: remove the spiteful tree-stump standing in the path.
verses.wilson_translation: Exulting, do you bestow riches, comprehendingmaleprogeny, in the house of my husband, on me,who desire to praise you; lords of waters, make the sacred ford good to drink; remove the tree that stands in theroad and the malevolent (enemy).
verses.griffith_verse: Even so, rejoicing in the dwelling-place of man, give hero sons and riches to the eloquent. Make a ford, Lords of splendour, where men well may drink: remove the spiteful tree-stump standing in the path.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्व स्विदद्य कतमास्वश्विना विक्षु दस्रा मादयेते शुभस्पती ।क ईं नि येमे कतमस्य जग्मतुर्विप्रस्य वा यजमानस्य वा गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: kvá ǀ svit ǀ adyá ǀ katamā́su ǀ aśvínā ǀ vikṣú ǀ dasrā́ ǀ mādayete íti ǀ śubháḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀkáḥ ǀ īm ǀ ní ǀ yeme ǀ katamásya ǀ jagmatuḥ ǀ víprasya ǀ vā ǀ yájamānasya ǀ vā ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Aśvins, Wonder-Workers, Lords of lustre, where and with what folk do ye delight yourselves to-day? Who hath detained them with him? Whither are they gone? Unto what sage's or what worshipper's abode?
verses.wilson_translation: Aśvinsof goodly aspect, lords of water, in what plural ce, among what people, do you today delight? Whonow detains you? To the house of what sage or of what sacrificer, have you gone?
verses.griffith_verse: O Aśvins, Wonder-Workers, Lords of lustre, where and with what folk do ye delight yourselves to-day? Who hath detained them with him? Whither are they gone? Unto what sage's or what worshipper's abode?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLI. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THAT general Car of yours, invoked by many a man, that comes to our libations, three-wheeled, meet for lauds,That circumambient Car, worthy of sacrifice, we call with our pure hymns at earliest flush of dawn. Ye, O Nāsatyas, mount that early-harnessed Car, that travels early, laden with its freight of balm,Wherewith ye, Heroes, visit clans who sacrifice, even the poor man's worship where the priest attends. If to the deft Adhvaryu with the meath in hand, or to the Kindler firm in strength, the household friend,Or to the sage's poured libations ye approach, come thence, O Aśvins, now to drink the offered meath.

verses.sanskrit: समानमु त्यं पुरुहूतमुक्थ्यं रथं त्रिचक्रं सवना गनिग्मतं ।परिज्मानं विदथ्यं सुवृक्तिभिर्वयं व्युष्टा उषसो हवामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: samānám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyám ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ ukthyám ǀ rátham ǀ tri-cakrám ǀ sávanā ǀ gánigmatam ǀpári-jmānam ǀ vidathyám ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ vayám ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ havāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: THAT general Car of yours, invoked by many a man, that comes to our libations, three-wheeled, meet for lauds, That circumambient Car, worthy of sacrifice, we call with our pure hymns at earliest flush of dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: At break of dawn, (Aśvins), we invoke with pious prayers your common chariot, praised of many,adorable three-wheeled, frequenting religious rites, traversing all space, suitable at sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: THAT general Car of yours, invoked by many a man, that comes to our libations, three-wheeled, meet for lauds, That circumambient Car, worthy of sacrifice, we call with our pure hymns at earliest flush of dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रातर्य��जं नासत्याधि तिष्ठथः प्रातर्यावाणं मधुवाहनं रथं ।विशो येन गच्छथो यज्वरीर्नरा कीरेश्चिद्यज्ञं होतृमंतमश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-yújam ǀ nāsatyā ǀ ádhi ǀ tiṣṭhathaḥ ǀ prātaḥ-yā́vānam ǀ madhu-vā́hanam ǀ rátham ǀvíśaḥ ǀ yéna ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ yájvarīḥ ǀ narā ǀ kīréḥ ǀ cit ǀ yajñám ǀ hótṛ-mantam ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, O Nāsatyas, mount that early-harnessed Car, that travels early, laden with its freight of balm, Wherewith ye, Heroes, visit clans who sacrifice, even the poor man's worship where the priest attends.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend,Nāsatyās, your nectar-bearing chariot, which is harnessed at dawn, and set in motion atdawn, with which, leaders (of rites), you go to the people who are engaged in worship, to the priest-administeredsacrifice,Aśvins, of (your) adorer.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, O Nāsatyas, mount that early-harnessed Car, that travels early, laden with its freight of balm, Wherewith ye, Heroes, visit clans who sacrifice, even the poor man's worship where the priest attends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध्वर्युं वा मधुपाणिं सुहस्त्यमग्निधं वा धृतदक्षं दमूनसं ।विप्रस्य वा यत्सवनानि गच्छथोऽत आ यातं मधुपेयमश्विना ॥
verses.transliteration: adhvaryúm ǀ vā ǀ mádhu-pāṇim ǀ su-hástyam ǀ agnídham ǀ vā ǀ dhṛtá-dakṣam ǀ dámūnasam ǀvíprasya ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ sávanāni ǀ gácchathaḥ ǀ átaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yātam ǀ madhu-péyam ǀ aśvinā ǁ
verses.english_translation: If to the deft Adhvaryu with the meath in hand, or to the Kindler firm in strength, the household friend, Or to the sage's poured libations ye approach, come thence, O Aśvins, now to drink the offered meath.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Aśvins, to Suhastya, whether as the ministrant priest bearing the Somain hishand, or as thecompetent lowly-minded feeder of the sacred fire; although you go to the sacrifices of (some other) sage, (yet)come, Aśvins, from them to the Soma (which I offer).
verses.griffith_verse: If to the deft Adhvaryu with the meath in hand, or to the Kindler firm in strength, the household friend, Or to the sage's poured libations ye approach, come thence, O Aśvins, now to drink the offered meath.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . EVEN as an archer shoots afar his arrow, offer the laud to him with meet adornment.Quell with your voice the wicked's voice, O sages. Singer, make Indra rest beside the Soma. Draw thy Friend to thee like a cow at milking: O Singer, wake up Indra as a lover.Make thou the Hero haste to give us riches even as a vessel filled brimful with treasure. Why, Maghavan, do they call thee Bounteous; Giver? Quicken me: thou, I hear, art he who quickens.Śakra, let my intelligence be active, and bring us luck that finds great wealth, O Indra. Standing, in battle for their rights, together, the people, Indra, in the fray invoke thee.Him who brings gifts the Hero makes his comrade: with him who pours no juice he seeks not friendship. Whoso with plenteous food for him expresses strong Somas as much quickly-coming treasure,For him he overthrows in early morning his swift well-weaponed foes, and slays the tyrant. He unto whom we offer praises, Indra, Maghavan, who hath joined to ours his wishes,—Before him even afar the foe must tremble: low before him must bow all human glories. With thy fierce bolt, O God invoked of many, drive to a distance from afar the foeman.O Indra, give us wealth in corn and cattle, and make thy singer's prayer gain strength and riches. Indra, the swallower of strong libations rich in the boons they bring, the potent Somas,He, Maghavan, will not restrict his bounty he brings much wealth unto the Soma-presser. Yea, by superior play he wins advantage, when he, a gambler, piles his gains in season.Celestial-natured, he o’erwhelms with riches the devotee who keeps not back his treasure. O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle.May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion. Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners!May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

verses.sanskrit: अस्तेव सु प्रतरं लायमस्यन्भूषन्निव प्र भरा स्तोममस्मै ।वाचा विप्रास्तरत वाचमर्यो नि रामय जरितः सोम इंद्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: ástā-iva ǀ sú ǀ pra-tarám ǀ lā́yam ǀ ásyan ǀ bhū́ṣan-iva ǀ prá ǀ bhara ǀ stómam ǀ asmai ǀvācā́ ǀ viprāḥ ǀ tarata ǀ vā́cam ǀ aryáḥ ǀ ní ǀ ramaya ǀ jaritaríti ǀ sóme ǀ índram ǁ
verses.english_translation: EVEN as an archer shoots afar his arrow, offer the laud to him with meet adornment. Quell with your voice the wicked's voice, O sages. Singer, make Indra rest beside the Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: Direct your laudation to him, (Indra), like an archer aiming a larger arrow (to its mark), like a decorator(applying his ornaments); surpass by your praises, sages, the praises of your adversaries; delight Indraworshipper, by the (offering of the)Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: EVEN as an archer shoots afar his arrow, offer the laud to him with meet adornment. Quell with your voice the wicked's voice, O sages. Singer, make Indra rest beside the Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दोहेन गामुप शिक्षा सखायं प्र बोधय जरितर्जारमिंद्रं ।कोशं न पूर्णं वसुना न्यृष्टमा च्यावय मघदेयाय शूरं ॥
verses.transliteration: dóhena ǀ gā́m ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣa ǀ sákhāyam ǀ prá ǀ bodhaya ǀ jaritaḥ ǀ jārám ǀ índram ǀkóśam ǀ ná ǀ pūrṇám ǀ vásunā ǀ ní-ṛṣṭam ǀ ā́ ǀ cyavaya ǀ magha-déyāya ǀ śū́ram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Draw thy Friend to thee like a cow at milking: O Singer, wake up Indra as a lover. Make thou the Hero haste to give us riches even as a vessel filled brimful with treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Control, worshipper, your friend (Indra), like a cow for your milking; awake, Indra, the author of decay;bring down for the distribution of wealth the hero who is pressed down with wealth like a vessel full (of water).
verses.griffith_verse: Draw thy Friend to thee like a cow at milking: O Singer, wake up Indra as a lover. Make thou the Hero haste to give us riches even as a vessel filled brimful with treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किमंग त्वा मघवन्भोजमाहुः शिशीहि मा शिशयं त्वा शृणोमि ।अप्नस्वती मम धीरस्तु शक्र वसुविदं भगमिंद्रा भरा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ aṅgá ǀ tvā ǀ magha-van ǀ bhojám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ śiśīhí ǀ mā ǀ śiśayám ǀ tvā ǀ śṛṇomi ǀápnasvatī ǀ máma ǀ dhī́ḥ ǀ astu ǀ śakra ǀ vasu-vídam ǀ bhágam ǀ indra ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Why, Maghavan, do they call thee Bounteous; Giver? Quicken me: thou, I hear, art he who quickens. Śakra, let my intelligence be active, and bring us luck that finds great wealth, O Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Why, Maghavat, do (the wise) call you the nourisher (of worshippers)? Quicken me, (Indra), withwealth, (for) I hear that you are the quickener (of the worshipper); may my understanding,Śakra, be productiveof works; grant us, Indra, adestinythat brings wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Why, Maghavan, do they call thee Bounteous; Giver? Quicken me: thou, I hear, art he who quickens. Śakra, let my intelligence be active, and bring us luck that finds great wealth, O Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां जना ममसत्येष्विंद्र संतस्थाना वि ह्वयंते समीके ।अत्रा युजं कृणुते यो हविष्मान्नासुन्वता सख्यं वष्टि शूरः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ jánāḥ ǀ mama-satyéṣu ǀ indra ǀ sam-tasthānā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ sam-īké ǀátra ǀ yújam ǀ kṛṇute ǀ yáḥ ǀ havíṣmān ǀ ná ǀ ásunvatā ǀ sakhyám ǀ vaṣṭi ǀ śū́raḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Standing, in battle for their rights, together, the people, Indra, in the fray invoke thee. Him who brings gifts the Hero makes his comrade: with him who pours no juice he seeks not friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: The people earnestly call upon you in battles,Indra, (they call upon you) when standing together inthe conflict; at this (call) Indra makes him his friend who offers oblations; the hero desires not friendship with himwho presents no libation.
verses.griffith_verse: Standing, in battle for their rights, together, the people, Indra, in the fray invoke thee. Him who brings gifts the Hero makes his comrade: with him who pours no juice he seeks not friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: धनं न स्यंद्रं बहुलं यो अस्मै तीव्रान्त्सोमाँ आसुनोति प्रयस्वान् ।तस्मै शत्रून्त्सुतुकान्प्रातरह्नो नि स्वष्ट्रान्युवति हंति वृत्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhánam ǀ ná ǀ syandrám ǀ bahulám ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ tīvrā́n ǀ sómān ǀ ā-sunóti ǀ práyasvān ǀtásmai ǀ śátrūn ǀ su-túkān ǀ prātáḥ ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ ní ǀ su-áṣṭrān ǀ yuváti ǀ hánti ǀ vṛtrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whoso with plenteous food for him expresses strong Somas as much quickly-coming treasure, For him he overthrows in early morning his swift well-weaponed foes, and slays the tyrant.
verses.wilson_translation: The bearer of the oblation who offers to Indrathe sharp Soma, like much moveable wealth (given tothe poor)-- for him in the fore part of the day Indra scatters his eager and well-armed (enemies), and defeats hisfoe.
verses.griffith_verse: Whoso with plenteous food for him expresses strong Somas as much quickly-coming treasure, For him he overthrows in early morning his swift well-weaponed foes, and slays the tyrant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्वयं दधिमा शंसमिंद्रे यः शिश्राय मघवा काममस्मे ।आराच्चित्सन्भयतामस्य शत्रुर्न्यस्मै द्युम्ना जन्या नमंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ vayám ǀ dadhimá ǀ śáṃsam ǀ índre ǀ yáḥ ǀ śiśrā́ya ǀ maghá-vā ǀ kā́mam ǀ asmé íti ǀārā́t ǀ cit ǀ sán ǀ bhayatām ǀ asya ǀ śátruḥ ǀ ní ǀ asmai ǀ dyumnā́ ǀ jányā ǀ namantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: He unto whom we offer praises, Indra, Maghavan, who hath joined to ours his wishes,— Before him even afar the foe must tremble: low before him must bow all human glories.
verses.wilson_translation: May the enemy of that Indraon whom we have laid our praise, the lord of affluence, who has grantedus our desires, be in the fear of him even when far off; may the food belonging to the country of the foe bowdown before him (to enjoy).
verses.griffith_verse: He unto whom we offer praises, Indra, Maghavan, who hath joined to ours his wishes,— Before him even afar the foe must tremble: low before him must bow all human glories.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आराच्छत्रुमप बाधस्व दूरमुग्रो यः शंबः पुरुहूत तेन ।अस्मे धेहि यवमद्गोमदिंद्र कृधी धियं जरित्रे वाजरत्नां ॥
verses.transliteration: ārā́t ǀ śátrum ǀ ápa ǀ bādhasva ǀ dūrám ǀ ugráḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ śámbaḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ téna ǀasmé íti ǀ dhehi ǀ yáva-mat ǀ gó-mat ǀ indra ǀ kṛdhí ǀ dhíyam ǀ jaritré ǀ vā́ja-ratnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: With thy fierce bolt, O God invoked of many, drive to a distance from afar the foeman. O Indra, give us wealth in corn and cattle, and make thy singer's prayer gain strength and riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Invoked of many, (Indra) drive far away the enemy with that fierce thunderbolt of yours; grant to us,Indra, wealth of barley and cattle; render to the worshipper his sacrifice productive of plural asant food.
verses.griffith_verse: With thy fierce bolt, O God invoked of many, drive to a distance from afar the foeman. O Indra, give us wealth in corn and cattle, and make thy singer's prayer gain strength and riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यमंतर्वृषसवासो अग्मंतीव्राः सोमा बहुलांतास इंद्रं ।नाह दामानं मघवा नि यंसन्नि सुन्वते वहति भूरि वामं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yám ǀ antáḥ ǀ vṛṣa-savā́saḥ ǀ ágman ǀ tīvrā́ḥ ǀ sómāḥ ǀ bahulá-antāsaḥ ǀ índram ǀná ǀ áha ǀ dāmā́nam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ ní ǀ yaṃsat ǀ ní ǀ sunvaté ǀ vahati ǀ bhū́ri ǀ vāmám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, the swallower of strong libations rich in the boons they bring, the potent Somas, He, Maghavan, will not restrict his bounty he brings much wealth unto the Soma-presser.
verses.wilson_translation: The Indrainto whom the sharp abundant Somaeffused by (the priests), the showerers (of the Soma),have entered; he, Maghavat, deserts not the donor of the sacrifice, but bestows ample wealth upon him whopresents libations.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, the swallower of strong libations rich in the boons they bring, the potent Somas, He, Maghavan, will not restrict his bounty he brings much wealth unto the Soma-presser.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत प्रहामतिदीव्या जयाति कृतं यच्छ्वघ्नी विचिनोति काले ।यो देवकामो न धना रुणद्धि समित्तं राया सृजति स्वधावान् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ pra-hā́m ǀ ati-dī́vya ǀ jayāti ǀ kṛtám ǀ yát ǀ śva-ghnī́ ǀ vi-cinóti ǀ kālé ǀyáḥ ǀ devá-kāmaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhánā ǀ ruṇaddhi ǀ sám ǀ ít ǀ tám ǀ rāyā́ ǀ sṛjati ǀ svadhā́-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, by superior play he wins advantage, when he, a gambler, piles his gains in season. Celestial-natured, he o’erwhelms with riches the devotee who keeps not back his treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Having driven away the assailant, he triumphs; at the time (of battle) he selects his antagonist as doesa gambler. The man who, desirous of gratifying the gods, withholds not his riches, him the powerful Indraassociates with wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, by superior play he wins advantage, when he, a gambler, piles his gains in season. Celestial-natured, he o’erwhelms with riches the devotee who keeps not back his treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गोभिष्टरेमामतिं दुरेवां यवेन क्षुधं पुरुहूत विश्वां ।वयं राजभिः प्रथमा धनान्यस्माकेन वृजनेना जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: góbhiḥ ǀ tarema ǀ ámatim ǀ duḥ-évām ǀ yávena ǀ kṣúdham ǀ puru-hūta ǀ víśvām ǀvayám ǀ rā́ja-bhiḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ dhánāni ǀ asmā́kena ǀ vṛjánena ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle. May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, invoked of many, may we escape all ignorance caused by poverty by means of our cattle; (maywe escape) all hunger by means of our barley; (may we acquire) the chief riches through the princes (of wealth);may we conquer by our valour.
verses.griffith_verse: O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle. May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पतिर्नः परि पातु पश्चादुतोत्तरस्मादधरादघायोः ।इंद्रः पुरस्तादुत मध्यतो नः सखा सखिभ्यो वरिवः कृणोतु ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pári ǀ pātu ǀ paścā́t ǀ utá ǀ út-tarasmāt ǀ ádharāt ǀ agha-yóḥ ǀíndraḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ utá ǀ madhyatáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ kṛṇotu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners! May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.
verses.wilson_translation: May Bṛhaspatidefend us from a malignant (foe) coming from behind, from above, or from below; may Indra defend us from foes in front and in the middle; may he, our friend, bestow wealth upon (us) his friends.
verses.griffith_verse: Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners! May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XLIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IN perfect unison all yearning hymns of mine that find the light of heaven have sung forth Indra's praise.As wives embrace their lord, the comely bridegroom, so they compass Maghavan about that he may help. Directed unto thee my spirit never strays, for I have set my hopes on thee, O Much-invoked!Sit, Wonderful! as King upon the sacred grass, and let thy drinking-place be by the Soma juice. From indigence and hunger Indra turns away: Maghavan hath dominion over precious wealth.These the Seven Rivers flowing on their downward path increase the vital vigour of the potent Steer. As on the fair-leafed tree rest birds, to Indra flow the gladdening Soma juices that the bowls contain.Their face that glows with splendour through their mighty power hath found the shine of heaven for man, the Āryas' light. As in the game a gambler piles his winnings, so Maghavan, sweeping all together, gained the SunThis mighty deed of thine none other could achieve, none, Maghavan, before thee, none in recent time. Maghavan came by turns to all the tribes of men: the Steer took notice of the people's songs of praise.The man in whose libations Śakra hath delight by means of potent Somas vanquisheth his foes. When Soma streams together unto Indra flow like waters to the river, rivulets to the lake,In place of sacrifice sages exalt his might, as the rain swells the corn by moisture sent from heaven. He rushes through the region like a furious Bull, he who hath made these floods the dames of worthy lords.This Maghavan hath found light for the man who brings oblation, sheds the juice, and promptly pours his gifts. Let the keen axe come forth together with the light: here be,.as erst, the teeming cow of sacrifice.Let the Red God shine bright with his refulgent ray, and let the Lord of heroes glow like heaven's clear sheen. O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle.May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion. Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners.May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

verses.sanskrit: अच्छा म इंद्रं मतयः स्वर्विदः सध्रीचीर्विश्वा उशतीरनूषत ।परि ष्वजंते जनयो यथा पतिं मर्यं न शुंध्युं मघवानमूतये ॥
verses.transliteration: áccha ǀ me ǀ índram ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ svaḥ-vídaḥ ǀ sadhrī́cīḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ uśatī́ḥ ǀ anūṣata ǀpári ǀ svajante ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ pátim ǀ máryam ǀ ná ǀ śundhyúm ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ ūtáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: IN perfect unison all yearning hymns of mine that find the light of heaven have sung forth Indra's praise. As wives embrace their lord, the comely bridegroom, so they compass Maghavan about that he may help.
verses.wilson_translation: My praises, all-acquiring, concentrated and eager, glorify Indra; they embrace Maghavat as wives(embrace) a husband; as (women embrace) a man free from defect for the sake of protection.
verses.griffith_verse: IN perfect unison all yearning hymns of mine that find the light of heaven have sung forth Indra's praise. As wives embrace their lord, the comely bridegroom, so they compass Maghavan about that he may help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न घा त्वद्रिगप वेति मे मनस्त्वे इत्कामं पुरुहूत शिश्रय ।राजेव दस्म नि षदोऽधि बर्हिष्यस्मिन्त्सु सोमेऽवपानमस्तु ते ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ gha ǀ tvadrík ǀ ápa ǀ veti ǀ me ǀ mánaḥ ǀ tvé íti ǀ ít ǀ kā́mam ǀ puru-hūta ǀ śiśraya ǀrā́jā-iva ǀ dasma ǀ ní ǀ sadaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ barhíṣi ǀ asmín ǀ sú ǀ sóme ǀ ava-pā́nam ǀ astu ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: Directed unto thee my spirit never strays, for I have set my hopes on thee, O Much-invoked! Sit, Wonderful! as King upon the sacred grass, and let thy drinking-place be by the Soma juice.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, of godly aspect, the invoked of many, my mind intent on you wanders not from your presence, Ifix my desire on you; take your seat like a prince upon this sacred grass, and may your drinking be of this Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Directed unto thee my spirit never strays, for I have set my hopes on thee, O Much-invoked! Sit, Wonderful! as King upon the sacred grass, and let thy drinking-place be by the Soma juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विषूवृदिंद्रो अमतेरुत क्षुधः स इद्रायो मघवा वस्व ईशते ।तस्येदिमे प्रवणे सप्त सिंधवो वयो वर्धंति वृषभस्य शुष्मिणः ॥
verses.transliteration: viṣu-vṛ́t ǀ índraḥ ǀ ámateḥ ǀ utá ǀ kṣudháḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ vásvaḥ ǀ īśate ǀtásya ǀ ít ǀ imé ǀ pravaṇé ǀ saptá ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ vardhanti ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ śuṣmíṇaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From indigence and hunger Indra turns away: Maghavan hath dominion over precious wealth. These the Seven Rivers flowing on their downward path increase the vital vigour of the potent Steer.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrabe the remover of thirst and hunger, for he, Maghavat, is lord over precious riches; theseseven rivers of the powerful showerer, (Indra), flowing down a declivity, augment food.
verses.griffith_verse: From indigence and hunger Indra turns away: Maghavan hath dominion over precious wealth. These the Seven Rivers flowing on their downward path increase the vital vigour of the potent Steer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयो न वृक्षं सुपलाशमासदन्त्सोमास इंद्रं मंदिनश्चमूषदः ।प्रैषामनीकं शवसा दविद्युतद्विदत्स्वर्मनवे ज्योतिरार्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: váyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vṛkṣám ǀ su-palāśám ǀ ā́ ǀ asadan ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ índram ǀ mandínaḥ ǀ camū-sádaḥ ǀprá ǀ eṣām ǀ ánīkam �� śávasā ǀ dávidyutat ǀ vidát ǀ sváḥ ǀ mánave ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ā́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As on the fair-leafed tree rest birds, to Indra flow the gladdening Soma juices that the bowls contain. Their face that glows with splendour through their mighty power hath found the shine of heaven for man, the Āryas' light.
verses.wilson_translation: As birds perch upon the leafy tree, so the exhilarating Somafillling the ladles (go) to (Indra), thesummit of them shines through their speed, may Indra spontaneously bestow excellent light upon man.
verses.griffith_verse: As on the fair-leafed tree rest birds, to Indra flow the gladdening Soma juices that the bowls contain. Their face that glows with splendour through their mighty power hath found the shine of heaven for man, the Āryas' light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृतं न श्वघ्नी वि चिनोति देवने संवर्गं यन्मघवा सूर्यं जयत् ।न तत्ते अन्यो अनु वीर्यं शकन्न पुराणो मघवन्नोत नूतनः ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛtám ǀ ná ǀ śva-ghnī́ ǀ ví ǀ cinoti ǀ dévane ǀ sam-várgam ǀ yát ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sū́ryam ǀ jáyat ǀná ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vīryám ǀ śakat ǀ ná ǀ purāṇáḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ ná ǀ utá ǀ nū́tanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As in the game a gambler piles his winnings, so Maghavan, sweeping all together, gained the Sun This mighty deed of thine none other could achieve, none, Maghavan, before thee, none in recent time.
verses.wilson_translation: As a gambler at plural y selects his adversary, so does Maghavat when he overcomes the rain-bestowingsun; no one, Maghavat, ancient or modern, is able to imitate this your vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: As in the game a gambler piles his winnings, so Maghavan, sweeping all together, gained the Sun This mighty deed of thine none other could achieve, none, Maghavan, before thee, none in recent time.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विशंविशं मघवा पर्यशायत जनानां धेना अवचाकशद्वृषा ।यस्याह शक्रः सवनेषु रण्यति स तीव्रैः सोमैः सहते पृतन्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśam-viśam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ pári ǀ aśāyata ǀ jánānām ǀ dhénāḥ ǀ ava-cā́kaśat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀyásya ǀ áha ǀ śakráḥ ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ ráṇyati ǀ sáḥ ǀ tīvráiḥ ǀ sómaiḥ ǀ sahate ǀ pṛtanyatáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Maghavan came by turns to all the tribes of men: the Steer took notice of the people's songs of praise. The man in whose libations Śakra hath delight by means of potent Somas vanquisheth his foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Maghavat, the showerer (of benefits), encompasses all people; he contemplates the praises ofmankind; the man in whose sacrificeŚakradelights, overcomes (foes) wishing to fight by means of his pungent Soma-libations.
verses.griffith_verse: Maghavan came by turns to all the tribes of men: the Steer took notice of the people's songs of praise. The man in whose libations Śakra hath delight by means of potent Somas vanquisheth his foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो न सिंधुमभि यत्समक्षरन्त्सोमास इंद्रं कुल्या इव ह्रदं ।वर्धंति विप्रा महो अस्य सादने यवं न वृष्टिर्दिव्येन दानुना ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ síndhum ǀ abhí ǀ yát ǀ sam-ákṣaran ǀ sómāsaḥ ǀ índram ǀ kulyā́ḥ-iva ǀ hradám ǀvárdhanti ǀ víprāḥ ǀ máhaḥ ǀ asya ǀ sádane ǀ yávam ǀ ná ǀ vṛṣṭíḥ ǀ divyéna ǀ dā́nunā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Soma streams together unto Indra flow like waters to the river, rivulets to the lake, In place of sacrifice sages exalt his might, as the rain swells the corn by moisture sent from heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: When the Somaflows towards Indra, as waters to the sea, as rivers to a lake, then the piousworshippers augment his greatness in the (sacrificial) abode, as the rain by its heavenly gift, (augments) thebarley.
verses.griffith_verse: When Soma streams together unto Indra flow like waters to the river, rivulets to the lake, In place of sacrifice sages exalt his might, as the rain swells the corn by moisture sent from heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषा न क्रुद्धः पतयद्रजस्स्वा यो अर्यपत्नीरकृणोदिमा अपः ।स सुन्वते मघवा जीरदानवेऽविंदज्ज्योतिर्मनवे हविष्मते ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ ná ǀ kruddháḥ ǀ patayat ǀ rájaḥ-su ǀ ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ aryá-patnīḥ ǀ ákṛṇot ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ sunvaté ǀ maghá-vā ǀ jīrá-dānave ǀ ávindat ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ mánave ǀ havíṣmate ǁ
verses.english_translation: He rushes through the region like a furious Bull, he who hath made these floods the dames of worthy lords. This Maghavan hath found light for the man who brings oblation, sheds the juice, and promptly pours his gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: As in the world an angry bull rushes (upon another), so does Indra, who directs (towards us) thewaters, the brides of the lord (of earth); when (the Soma) is effused, Maghavat bestows light upon the man, whogives promptly, who offers oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: He rushes through the region like a furious Bull, he who hath made these floods the dames of worthy lords. This Maghavan hath found light for the man who brings oblation, sheds the juice, and promptly pours his gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उज्जायतां परशुर्ज्योतिषा सह भूया ऋतस्य सुदुघा पुराणवत् ।वि रोचतामरुषो भानुना शुचिः स्वर्ण शुक्रं शुशुचीत सत्पतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ jāyatām ǀ paraśúḥ ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ sahá ǀ bhūyā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ su-dúghā ǀ purāṇa-vát ǀví ǀ rocatām ǀ aruṣáḥ ǀ bhānúnā ǀ śúciḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ śukrám ǀ śuśucīta ǀ sát-patiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the keen axe come forth together with the light: here be,.as erst, the teeming cow of sacrifice. Let the Red God shine bright with his refulgent ray, and let the Lord of heroes glow like heaven's clear sheen.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the axe (of Indra) be put forth together with light; may the easily milked cow of truth be(manifested) as of old; may the pure and radiant Indra shine with splendour; may the lord of the virtuous shinebrightly like the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the keen axe come forth together with the light: here be,.as erst, the teeming cow of sacrifice. Let the Red God shine bright with his refulgent ray, and let the Lord of heroes glow like heaven's clear sheen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गोभिष्टरेमामतिं दुरेवां यवेन क्षुधं पुरुहूत विश्वां ।वयं राजभिः प्रथमा धनान्यस्माकेन वृजनेना जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: góbhiḥ ǀ tarema ǀ ámatim ǀ duḥ-évām ǀ yávena ǀ kṣúdham ǀ puru-hūta ǀ víśvām ǀvayám ǀ rā́ja-bhiḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ dhánāni ǀ asmā́kena ǀ vṛjánena ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle. May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.
