verses.transliteration: evá ǀ devā́n ǀ índraḥ ǀ vivye ǀ nṝ́n ǀ prá ǀ cyautnéna ǀ maghá-vā ǀ satyá-rādhāḥ ǀvíśvā ǀ ít ǀ tā́ ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ śacī-vaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ turā́saḥ ǀ sva-yaśaḥ ǀ gṛṇanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even thus hath Indra Maghavan, truly bounteous, sped Gods and men with mighty operation. The pious glorify all these thine exploits, Lord of Bay Coursers, Strong, and Selfresplendent.
verses.griffith_verse: Even thus hath Indra Maghavan, truly bounteous, sped Gods and men with mighty operation. The pious glorify all these thine exploits, Lord of Bay Coursers, Strong, and Selfresplendent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN L. Indra Vaikuntha.
hymns.anukramani: ७ वैकुण्ठ इन्द्रः। इन्द्रः। जगतीः, ३,४ अभिसारिणी, ५ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I LAUD your Mighty One who joyeth in the juice, him who is shared by all men, who created all;Indra, whose conquering strength is powerful in war, whose fame and manly vigour Heaven and Earth revere. He with his friend is active, lauded, good to man, Indra who must be glorified by one like me.Hero, Lord of the brave, all cars are thy delight, warring with Vṛtra, or for waters, or for spoil. Who are the men whom thou wilt further, Indra, who strive to win thy bliss allied with riches?Who urged thee forward to exert thy power divine, to valour, in the war for waters on their fields? Thou, Indra, through the holy prayer art mighty, worthy of sacrifice at all libations.In every fight thou castest heroes on the ground: thou art the noblest song, O Lord of all the folk. Help now, as Highest, those who toil at sacrifice: well do the people know thy great protecting might.Thou shalt be Everlasing, Giver of success yea, on all these libations thou bestowest strength. All these libations thou makest effectual, of which thou art thyself supporter, Son of Power.Therefore thy vessel is to be esteemed the best, sacrifice, holy text, prayer, and exalted speech. They who with flowing Soma pray to thee, O Sage, to pour on them thy gifts of opulence and wealth,May they come forward, through their spirit, on the path of bliss, in the wild joy of Soma juice effused.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो महे मंदमानायांधसोऽर्चा विश्वानराय विश्वाभुवे ।इंद्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि श्रवो नृम्णं च रोदसी सपर्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ mahé ǀ mándamānāya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ árca ǀ viśvā́narāya ǀ viśva-bhúve ǀíndrasya ǀ yásya ǀ sú-makham ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ nṛmṇám ǀ ca ǀ ródasī íti ǀ saparyátaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I LAUD your Mighty One who joyeth in the juice, him who is shared by all men, who created all; Indra, whose conquering strength is powerful in war, whose fame and manly vigour Heaven and Earth revere.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship him who is exhilarated by the sacrificiial food, the mighty Indra; the leader of all men, thecreator of all, whose venerable strength and abundant food and wealth, heaven and earth adore.
verses.griffith_verse: I LAUD your Mighty One who joyeth in the juice, him who is shared by all men, who created all; Indra, whose conquering strength is powerful in war, whose fame and manly vigour Heaven and Earth revere.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो चिन्नु सख्या नर्य इनः स्तुतश्चर्कृत्य इंद्रो मावते नरे ।विश्वासु धूर्षु वाजकृत्येषु सत्पते वृत्रे वाप्स्वभि शूर मंदसे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ sákhyā ǀ náryaḥ ǀ ináḥ ǀ stutáḥ ǀ carkṛ́tyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ mā́-vate ǀ náre ǀvíśvāsu ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ vāja-kṛ́tyeṣu ǀ sat-pate ǀ vṛtré ǀ vā ǀ ap-sú ǀ abhí ǀ śūra ǀ mandase ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with his friend is active, lauded, good to man, Indra who must be glorified by one like me. Hero, Lord of the brave, all cars are thy delight, warring with Vṛtra, or for waters, or for spoil.
verses.wilson_translation: That Indra, kind to man, the lord of all, who is praised by his friend, is to be repeatedly honoured bymen like me; you, hero, protector of the good, are glorified in the all-sustaining food-producing cloud-imprisonedwaters.
verses.griffith_verse: He with his friend is active, lauded, good to man, Indra who must be glorified by one like me. Hero, Lord of the brave, all cars are thy delight, warring with Vṛtra, or for waters, or for spoil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: के ते नर इंद्र ये त इषे ये ते सुम्नं सधन्यमियक्षान् ।के ते वाजायासुर्याय हिन्विरे के अप्सु स्वासूर्वरासु पौंस्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: ké ǀ té ǀ náraḥ ǀ indra ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ iṣé ǀ yé ǀ te ǀ sumnám ǀ sa-dhanyám ǀ íyakṣān ǀké ǀ te ǀ vā́jāya ǀ asuryā́ya ǀ hinvire ǀ ké ǀ ap-sú ǀ svā́su ǀ urvárāsu ǀ páuṃsye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who are the men whom thou wilt further, Indra, who strive to win thy bliss allied with riches? Who urged thee forward to exert thy power divine, to valour, in the war for waters on their fields?
verses.wilson_translation: What men,Indra, are they who (are eminent in offering food to you, who are desirous of obtaining fromthe happiness and opulence, who send you (oblations) for the sake of strength (to fight) theasura, who (sentoblations) for the sake of obtaining spontaneously-flowing waters and cultivable lands, and manly vigour?
verses.griffith_verse: Who are the men whom thou wilt further, Indra, who strive to win thy bliss allied with riches? Who urged thee forward to exert thy power divine, to valour, in the war for waters on their fields?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भुवस्त्वमिंद्र ब्रह्मणा महान्भुवो विश्वेषु सवनेषु यज्ञियः ।भुवो नॄंश्च्यौत्नो विश्वस्मिन्भरे ज्येष्ठश्च मंत्रो विश्वचर्षणे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhúvaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ mahā́n ǀ bhúvaḥ ǀ víśveṣu ǀ sávaneṣu ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǀbhúvaḥ ǀ nṝ́n ǀ cyautnáḥ ǀ víśvasmin ǀ bháre ǀ jyéṣṭhaḥ ǀ ca ǀ mántraḥ ǀ viśva-carṣaṇe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Indra, through the holy prayer art mighty, worthy of sacrifice at all libations. In every fight thou castest heroes on the ground: thou art the noblest song, O Lord of all the folk.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, you have become mighty through our praise; you have have become adorable at all sacrifices,in every combat you are the caster down of the leaders (of hosts); beholder of all, you are the best, mostexcellent.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Indra, through the holy prayer art mighty, worthy of sacrifice at all libations. In every fight thou castest heroes on the ground: thou art the noblest song, O Lord of all the folk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवा नु कं ज्यायान्यज्ञवनसो महीं त ओमात्रां कृष्टयो विदुः ।असो नु कमजरो वर्धाश्च विश्वेदेता सवना तूतुमा कृषे ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ nú ǀ kam ǀ jyā́yān ǀ yajñá-vanasaḥ ǀ mahī́m ǀ te ǀ ómātrām ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ viduḥ ǀásaḥ ǀ nú ǀ kam ǀ ajáraḥ ǀ várdhāḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśvā ǀ ít ǀ etā́ ǀ sávanā ǀ tūtumā́ ǀ kṛṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Help now, as Highest, those who toil at sacrifice: well do the people know thy great protecting might. Thou shalt be Everlasing, Giver of success yea, on all these libations thou bestowest strength.
verses.griffith_verse: Help now, as Highest, those who toil at sacrifice: well do the people know thy great protecting might. Thou shalt be Everlasing, Giver of success yea, on all these libations thou bestowest strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे ।वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मंत्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ sávanā ǀ tūtumā́ ǀ kṛṣe ǀ svayám ǀ sūno íti ǀ sahasaḥ ǀ yā́ni ǀ dadhiṣé ǀvárāya ǀ te ǀ pā́tram ǀ dhármaṇe ǀ tánā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ mántraḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ út-yatam ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All these libations thou makest effectual, of which thou art thyself supporter, Son of Power. Therefore thy vessel is to be esteemed the best, sacrifice, holy text, prayer, and exalted speech.
verses.wilson_translation: You make swift all those sacrifices which, son of strength, you yourself support; may your protectionbe granted for the repulse (of enemies, may) wealth (be granted) for our support; the sacrifice, the hymn, thesacred text, the voice (is) raised (to you).
verses.griffith_verse: All these libations thou makest effectual, of which thou art thyself supporter, Son of Power. Therefore thy vessel is to be esteemed the best, sacrifice, holy text, prayer, and exalted speech.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये ते विप्र ब्रह्मकृतः सुते सचा वसूनां च वसुनश्च दावने ।प्र ते सुम्नस्य मनसा पथा भुवन्मदे सुतस्य सोम्यस्यांधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ te ǀ vipra ǀ brahma-kṛ́taḥ ǀ suté ǀ sácā ǀ vásūnām ǀ ca ǀ vásunaḥ ǀ ca ǀ dāváne ǀprá ǀ té ǀ sumnásya ǀ mánasā ǀ pathā́ ǀ bhuvan ǀ máde ǀ sutásya ǀ somyásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who with flowing Soma pray to thee, O Sage, to pour on them thy gifts of opulence and wealth, May they come forward, through their spirit, on the path of bliss, in the wild joy of Soma juice effused.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Indra, the reciters of pious hymns to you who assembled together when (the Soma) is effused,(worship you) for the donation of riches and treasures; may they be competent (to acquire) you felicity by thepathway of the mind; when you are exhilarated with the effused Soma food.
verses.griffith_verse: They who with flowing Soma pray to thee, O Sage, to pour on them thy gifts of opulence and wealth, May they come forward, through their spirit, on the path of bliss, in the wild joy of Soma juice effused.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LI. Agni. Gods.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LARGE was that covering, and firm of texture, folded wherein thou enteredst the waters.One Deity alone, O Jātavedas Agni, saw all thy forms in sundry places. What God hath seen me? Who of all their number clearly beheld my forms in many places?Where lie, then, all the sacred logs of Agni that lead him God-ward, Varuṇa and Mitra? In many places, Agni Jātavedas, we sought thee hidden in the plants and waters.Then Yama marked thee, God of wondrous splendour! effulgent from thy tenfold secret dwelling, I fled in fear from sacrificial worship, Varuṇa, lest the Gods should thus engage me.Thus were my forms laid down in many places. This, as my goal, I Agni saw before me. Come; man is pious and would fain do worship, he waits prepared: in gloom thou, Agni, dwellest.Make pathways leading God-ward clear and easy, and bear oblations with a kindly spirit. This goal mine elder brothers erst selected, as he who drives a car the way to travel.So,Varuṇa, I fled afar through terror, as flies the wild-bull from an archer's bowstring. We give thee life unwasting, Jātavedas, so that, employed, thou never shalt be injured.So, nobly born! shalt thou with kindly spirit bear to the Gods their share of men's oblations. Grant me the first oblations and the latter, entire, my forceful shares of holy presents,The soul of plants, the fatness of the waters, and let there be long life, ye Gods, to Agni. Thine be the first oblations and the latter, entire, thy forceful shares of holy presents.Let all this sacrifice be thine, O Agni, and let the world's four regions how before thee.

verses.sanskrit: महत्तदुल्बं स्थविरं तदासीद्येनाविष्टितः प्रविवेशिथापः ।विश्वा अपश्यद्बहुधा ते अग्ने जातवेदस्तन्वो देव एकः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahát ǀ tát ǀ úlbam ǀ stháviram ǀ tát ǀ āsīt ǀ yéna ǀ ā́-viṣṭitaḥ ǀ pra-vivéśitha ǀ apáḥ ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ apaśyat ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ jā́ta-vedaḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LARGE was that covering, and firm of texture, folded wherein thou enteredst the waters. One Deity alone, O Jātavedas Agni, saw all thy forms in sundry places.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods speak). Great and very dense is the covering enveloped by which,Agni, you have enteredinto the waters. Agni Jātavedas, one deity has beheld all your manifold forms.
verses.griffith_verse: LARGE was that covering, and firm of texture, folded wherein thou enteredst the waters. One Deity alone, O Jātavedas Agni, saw all thy forms in sundry places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को मा ददर्श कतमः स देवो यो मे तन्वो बहुधा पर्यपश्यत् ।क्वाह मित्रावरुणा क्षियंत्यग्नेर्विश्वाः समिधो देवयानीः ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ mā ǀ dadarśa ǀ katamáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ me ǀ tanváḥ ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ pari-ápaśyat ǀkvá ǀ áha ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ kṣiyanti ǀ agnéḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ sam-ídhaḥ ǀ deva-yā́nīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What God hath seen me? Who of all their number clearly beheld my forms in many places? Where lie, then, all the sacred logs of Agni that lead him God-ward, Varuṇa and Mitra?
verses.wilson_translation: (Agnispeaks). Who has beheld me? Which is it of the deities who has fully seen my manifold forms?Where Mitraand Varuṇa, do Agni's luminous vehicles of the gods abide?
verses.griffith_verse: What God hath seen me? Who of all their number clearly beheld my forms in many places? Where lie, then, all the sacred logs of Agni that lead him God-ward, Varuṇa and Mitra?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऐच्छाम त्वा बहुधा जातवेदः प्रविष्टमग्ने अप्स्वोषधीषु ।तं त्वा यमो अचिकेच्चित्रभानो दशांतरुष्यादतिरोचमानं ॥
verses.transliteration: áicchāma ǀ tvā ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ prá-viṣṭam ǀ agne ǀ ap-sú ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ yamáḥ ǀ aciket ǀ citrabhāno íti citra-bhāno ǀ daśa-antaruṣyā́t ǀ ati-rócamānam ǁ
verses.english_translation: In many places, Agni Jātavedas, we sought thee hidden in the plants and waters. Then Yama marked thee, God of wondrous splendour! effulgent from thy tenfold secret dwelling,
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods). We sought for you,Agni Jātavedas, who had entered in many ways into the waters, intothe plural nts;Yamarecognized you, who have adorable rays, blazing from your ten hiding-plural ces.
verses.griffith_verse: In many places, Agni Jātavedas, we sought thee hidden in the plants and waters. Then Yama marked thee, God of wondrous splendour! effulgent from thy tenfold secret dwelling,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: होत्रादहं वरुण बिभ्यदायं नेदेव मा युनजन्नत्र देवाः ।तस्य मे तन्वो बहुधा निविष्टा एतमर्थं न चिकेताहमग्निः ॥
verses.transliteration: hotrā́t ǀ ahám ǀ varuṇa ǀ bíbhyat ǀ āyam ǀ ná ǀ ít ǀ evá ǀ mā ǀ yunájan ǀ átra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀtásya ǀ me ǀ tanváḥ ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ ní-viṣṭāḥ ǀ etám ǀ ártham ǀ ná ǀ ciketa ǀ ahám ǀ agníḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I fled in fear from sacrificial worship, Varuṇa, lest the Gods should thus engage me. Thus were my forms laid down in many places. This, as my goal, I Agni saw before me.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agni). Divine Varuṇa, I have come hither, being afraid ofhotā, lest the gods should again associateme with him; my forms have therefore entered (into the waters) in various plural ces. I, Agni, do not consent (toundertake) that office.
verses.griffith_verse: I fled in fear from sacrificial worship, Varuṇa, lest the Gods should thus engage me. Thus were my forms laid down in many places. This, as my goal, I Agni saw before me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एहि मनुर्देवयुर्यज्ञकामोऽरंकृत्या तमसि क्षेष्यग्ने ।सुगान्पथः कृणुहि देवयानान्वह हव्यानि सुमनस्यमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ mánuḥ ǀ deva-yúḥ ǀ yajñá-kāmaḥ ǀ aram-kṛ́tya ǀ támasi ǀ kṣeṣi ǀ agne ǀsu-gā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ deva-yā́nān ǀ váha ǀ havyā́ni ǀ su-manasyámānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come; man is pious and would fain do worship, he waits prepared: in gloom thou, Agni, dwellest. Make pathways leading God-ward clear and easy, and bear oblations with a kindly spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods). Come,Agni, the devout Manu(is) desirous of offering sacrifice; adorning yourself, youabide in darkness; make straight the paths traversed by the gods, and with a benevolent mind convey ouroblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Come; man is pious and would fain do worship, he waits prepared: in gloom thou, Agni, dwellest. Make pathways leading God-ward clear and easy, and bear oblations with a kindly spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नेः पूर्वे भ्रातरो अर्थमेतं रथीवाध्वानमन्वावरीवुः ।तस्माद्भिया वरुण दूरमायं गौरो न क्षेप्नोरविजे ज्यायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ bhrā́taraḥ ǀ ártham ǀ etám ǀ rathī́-iva ǀ ádhvānam ǀ ánu ǀ ā́ ǀ avarīvuríti ǀtásmāt ǀ bhiyā́ ǀ varuṇa ǀ dūrám ǀ āyam ǀ gauráḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṣepnóḥ ǀ avije ǀ jyā́yāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This goal mine elder brothers erst selected, as he who drives a car the way to travel. So,Varuṇa, I fled afar through terror, as flies the wild-bull from an archer's bowstring.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agni). The elder brothers of Agni performed that duty, as the driver of a chariot covers the roaḍ(They were slain), and therefore,Varuṇa, I fled afar through fear. I trembled as a wild ox (tembles) at thebowstring of the archer.
verses.griffith_verse: This goal mine elder brothers erst selected, as he who drives a car the way to travel. So,Varuṇa, I fled afar through terror, as flies the wild-bull from an archer's bowstring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुर्मस्त आयुरजरं यदग्ने यथा युक्तो जातवेदो न रिष्याः ।अथा वहासि सुमनस्यमानो भागं देवेभ्यो हविषः सुजात ॥
verses.transliteration: kurmáḥ ǀ te ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ajáram ǀ yát ǀ agne ǀ yáthā ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ríṣyāḥ ǀátha ǀ vahāsi ǀ su-manasyámānaḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ su-jāta ǁ
verses.english_translation: We give thee life unwasting, Jātavedas, so that, employed, thou never shalt be injured. So, nobly born! shalt thou with kindly spirit bear to the Gods their share of men's oblations.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods). We grant you life,Agni, which (is) exempt from decay, so that thus endowed,Jātavedas,you will not die; so, becoming conciliated, well- born, Agni, bear their portion of the oblation to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: We give thee life unwasting, Jātavedas, so that, employed, thou never shalt be injured. So, nobly born! shalt thou with kindly spirit bear to the Gods their share of men's oblations.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रयाजान्मे अनुयाजांश्च केवलानूर्जस्वंतं हविषो दत्त भागं ।घृतं चापां पुरुषं चौषधीनामग्नेश्च दीर्घमायुरस्तु देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: pra-yājā́n ǀ me ǀ anu-yājā́n ǀ ca ǀ kévalān ǀ ū́rjasvantam ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ datta ǀ bhāgám ǀghṛtám ǀ ca ǀ apā́m ǀ púruṣam ǀ ca ǀ óṣadhīnām ǀ agnéḥ ǀ ca ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ astu ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grant me the first oblations and the latter, entire, my forceful shares of holy presents, The soul of plants, the fatness of the waters, and let there be long life, ye Gods, to Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agni). Only grant to me, deities, the concentrated portion of the oblation the Prayājas and Anuyājasexclusively; (give me) the butter (the essence) of the waters, and man (the essence) of the plural nts; and let the lifeof Agni be long.
verses.griffith_verse: Grant me the first oblations and the latter, entire, my forceful shares of holy presents, The soul of plants, the fatness of the waters, and let there be long life, ye Gods, to Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तव प्रयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल ऊर्जस्वंतो हविषः संतु भागाः ।तवाग्ने यज्ञोऽयमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमंतां प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ pra-yājā́ḥ ǀ anu-yājā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ kévale ǀ ū́rjasvantaḥ ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ santu ǀ bhāgā́ḥ ǀtáva ǀ agne ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ayám ǀ astu ǀ sárvaḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ namantām ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine be the first oblations and the latter, entire, thy forceful shares of holy presents. Let all this sacrifice be thine, O Agni, and let the world's four regions how before thee.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods). Yours,Agni, be the Prayājas and Anuyājas exclusively; yours be the concentrated portions of the oblations; let this sacrifice; Agni, be all yours, and let the four quarters of space bow down beforeyou.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine be the first oblations and the latter, entire, thy forceful shares of holy presents. Let all this sacrifice be thine, O Agni, and let the world's four regions how before thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LII. Gods.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . INSTRUCT me, all ye Gods, how I, elected your Priest, must seat me here, and how address you.Instruct me how to deal to each his portion, and by what ' path to bring you man's oblation. I sit as Priest most skilled in sacrificing: the Maruts and all Deities impel me.Aśvins, each day yours is the Adhvaryu's duty: Brahman and wood are here: ’tis yours to offer. Who is the Priest? Is he the Priest of Yama? On whom is thrust this God-appointed honour?He springs to life each month, each day that passes; so Gods have made him their oblation-bearer. The Gods have made me bearer of oblations, who slipped away and passed through many troubles.Wise Agni shall ordain for us the worship, whether five-wayed, threefold, or seven-threaded. So will I win you strength and life for ever. O Gods, that I may give you room and freedom.To Indra's arms would I consign the thunder; in all these battles shall he then be victor. The Deities three hundred and thirty-nine, have served and honoured Agni,Strewn sacred grass, anointed him with butter, and seated him as Priest, the Gods’ Invoker.

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवाः शास्तन मा यथेह होता वृतो मनवै यन्निषद्य ।प्र मे ब्रूत भागधेयं यथा वो येन पथा हव्यमा वो वहानि ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devāḥ ǀ śāstána ǀ mā ǀ yáthā ǀ ihá ǀ hótā ǀ vṛtáḥ ǀ manávai ǀ yát ǀ ni-sádya ǀprá ǀ me ǀ brūta ǀ bhāga-dhéyam ǀ yáthā ǀ vaḥ ǀ yéna ǀ pathā́ ǀ havyám ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ váhāni ǁ
verses.english_translation: INSTRUCT me, all ye Gods, how I, elected your Priest, must seat me here, and how address you. Instruct me how to deal to each his portion, and by what ' path to bring you man's oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: instrumental uct me,Viśvedevās, since I am appointed Hotā, how sitting here I ought to praise you; declareto me your portion; how you have acquired it, and by what path I may convey the oblation to you.
verses.griffith_verse: INSTRUCT me, all ye Gods, how I, elected your Priest, must seat me here, and how address you. Instruct me how to deal to each his portion, and by what ' path to bring you man's oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं होता न्यसीदं यजीयान्विश्वे देवा मरुतो मा जुनंति ।अहरहरश्विनाध्वर्यवं वां ब्रह्मा समिद्भवति साहुतिर्वां ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ asīdam ǀ yájīyān ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ mā ǀ junanti ǀáhaḥ-ahaḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ ā́dhvaryavam ǀ vām ǀ brahmā́ ǀ sam-ít ǀ bhavati ǀ sā́ ǀ ā́-hutiḥ ǀ vām ǁ
verses.english_translation: I sit as Priest most skilled in sacrificing: the Maruts and all Deities impel me. Aśvins, each day yours is the Adhvaryu's duty: Brahman and wood are here: ’tis yours to offer.
verses.wilson_translation: Best entitled to the sacrifice, I have sat down as the Hotā; all the divine Marutsurge me( to bear theoblation); the office of the Adhvaryuis to be discharged daily,Aśvins, by you; let the moon be thebrahman, andlet it be also your oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: I sit as Priest most skilled in sacrificing: the Maruts and all Deities impel me. Aśvins, each day yours is the Adhvaryu's duty: Brahman and wood are here: ’tis yours to offer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं यो होता किरु स यमस्य कमप्यूहे यत्समंजंति देवाः ।अहरहर्जायते मासिमास्यथा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ yáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ kíḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ yamásya ǀ kám ǀ ápi ǀ ūhe ǀ yát ǀ sam-añjánti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀáhaḥ-ahaḥ ǀ jāyate ǀ māsí-māsi ǀ átha ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ havya-vā́ham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who is the Priest? Is he the Priest of Yama? On whom is thrust this God-appointed honour? He springs to life each month, each day that passes; so Gods have made him their oblation-bearer.
verses.wilson_translation: Who is this, who is the Hotā? (Afraid) of Yama, what offering does he bear that the gods accept?Agniis born day by day, and month by month, and so the gods have made for themselves a bearer of oblationṣ
verses.griffith_verse: Who is the Priest? Is he the Priest of Yama? On whom is thrust this God-appointed honour? He springs to life each month, each day that passes; so Gods have made him their oblation-bearer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मां देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहमपम्लुक्तं बहु कृच्छ्रा चरंतं ।अग्निर्विद्वान्यज्ञं नः कल्पयाति पंचयामं त्रिवृतं सप्ततंतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́m ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ ápa-mluktam ǀ bahú ǀ kṛcchrā́ ǀ cárantam ǀagníḥ ǀ vidvā́n ǀ yajñám ǀ naḥ ǀ kalpayāti ǀ páñca-yāmam ǀ tri-vṛ́tam ǀ saptá-tantum ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Gods have made me bearer of oblations, who slipped away and passed through many troubles. Wise Agni shall ordain for us the worship, whether five-wayed, threefold, or seven-threaded.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have made me the bearer of oblations returning after departure, and passing many difficultplaces; (saying) this Agniis wise; he will accomplish the sacrifice for us, whether it be that of the five ways, thethree kinds, or the seven threads.
verses.griffith_verse: The Gods have made me bearer of oblations, who slipped away and passed through many troubles. Wise Agni shall ordain for us the worship, whether five-wayed, threefold, or seven-threaded.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो यक्ष्यमृतत्वं सुवीरं यथा वो देवा वरिवः कराणि ।आ बाह्वोर्वज्रमिंद्रस्य धेयामथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयाति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ yakṣi ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ yáthā ǀ vaḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ várivaḥ ǀ kárāṇi ǀā́ ǀ bāhvóḥ ǀ vájram ǀ índrasya ǀ dheyām ǀ átha ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ jayāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: So will I win you strength and life for ever. O Gods, that I may give you room and freedom. To Indra's arms would I consign the thunder; in all these battles shall he then be victor.
verses.wilson_translation: Gods, I solicit of you immortality and excellentmaleoffspring, that I may offer you adoration. I cause Indra to take the thunderbolt in hishands, wherewith he may overcome all these hostile hosts.
verses.griffith_verse: So will I win you strength and life for ever. O Gods, that I may give you room and freedom. To Indra's arms would I consign the thunder; in all these battles shall he then be victor.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् ।औक्षन्घृतैरस्तृणन्बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्धोतारं न्यसादयंत ॥
verses.transliteration: trī́ṇi ǀ śatā́ ǀ trī́ ǀ sahásrāṇi ǀ agním ǀ triṃśát ǀ ca ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ náva ǀ ca ǀ asaparyan ǀáukṣan ǀ ghṛtáiḥ ǀ ástṛṇan ǀ barhíḥ ǀ asmai ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ hótāram ǀ ní ǀ asādayanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Deities three hundred and thirty-nine, have served and honoured Agni, Strewn sacred grass, anointed him with butter, and seated him as Priest, the Gods’ Invoker.
verses.wilson_translation: Three thousand three hundred and thirty-and-nine deities worshipped Agni, they sprinkled (me) withbutter, they strewed the sacred grass, and then made the invoker of the gods sit down.
verses.griffith_verse: The Deities three hundred and thirty-nine, have served and honoured Agni, Strewn sacred grass, anointed him with butter, and seated him as Priest, the Gods’ Invoker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIII. Agni Saucika Gods.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE hath arrived, he whom we sought with longing, who skilled in sacrifice well knows its courses.Let him discharge his sacrificial duties: let him sit down as Friend who was beforeUs. Best Priest, he hath been won by being seated, for he hath looked on the well-ordered viands.Come, let usworship Gods who must be worshipped, and pouring oil, laud those who should be lauded. Now hath he made the feast of Gods effective: now have we found the secret tongue of worship.Now hath he come, sweet, robed in vital vigour, and made our calling on the Gods effective. This prelude of my speech I now will utter, whereby we Gods may quell our Asura foemen.Eaters of strengthening food who merit worship, O ye Five Tribes, be pleased with mine oblation. May the Five Tribes be pleased with mine oblation, and the Cow's Sons and all who merit worship.From earthly trouble may the earth protect us, and air's mid realm from woe that comes from heaven. Spinning the thread, follow the region's splendid light: guard thou the path ways well which wisdom hath prepared.Weave ye the knotless labour of the bards who sing: be Manu thou, and bring the Heavenly People forth. Lovers of Soma, bind the chariot traces fast: set ye the reins in order and embellish them.Bring hitherward the car with seats where eight may sit, whereon the Gods have brought the treasure that we love. Here flows Asmanvati: hold fast each other, keep yourselves up, and pass, my friends, the river.There let us leave the Powers that brought no profit, and cross the flood to Powers that are auspicious. Tvaṣṭar, most deft of workmen, knew each magic art, bringing most blessed bowls that hold the drink of Gods.His axe, wrought of good metal, he is sharpening now, wherewith the radiant Brahmaṇaspati will cut. Now, O ye Sapient Ones, make ye the axes sharp wherewith ye fashion bowls to hold the Amṛta.Knowing the secret places make ye ready that whereby the Gods have gotten immortality. Ye with a secret tongue and dark intention laid the maiden deep within, the calf within the mouth.They evermore are near us with their gracious help: successful is the song that strives for victory.

verses.sanskrit: यमैच्छाम मनसा सोऽयमागाद्यज्ञस्य विद्वान्परुषश्चिकित्वान् ।स नो यक्षद्देवताता यजीयान्नि हि षत्सदंतरः पूर्वो अस्मत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ áicchāma ǀ mánasā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ayám ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ yajñásya ǀ vidvā́n ǀ páruṣaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ yakṣat ǀ devá-tātā ǀ yájīyān ǀ ní ǀ hí ǀ satsat ǀ ántaraḥ ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ asmát ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE hath arrived, he whom we sought with longing, who skilled in sacrifice well knows its courses. Let him discharge his sacrificial duties: let him sit down as Friend who was before Us.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods). He whom we sought with (anxious) minds has arrived; he who understands the sacrificeand is acquainted with its different parts; may he who is most skilled in worship, sacrifice for us at the worship ofthe gods, being seated (at the altar), taking plural ce among (the priests), and preceding us.
verses.griffith_verse: HE hath arrived, he whom we sought with longing, who skilled in sacrifice well knows its courses. Let him discharge his sacrificial duties: let him sit down as Friend who was before Us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अराधि होता निषदा यजीयानभि प्रयांसि सुधितानि हि ख्यत् ।यजामहै यज्ञियान्हंत देवाँ ईळामहा ईड्याँ आज्येन ॥
verses.transliteration: árādhi ǀ hótā ǀ ni-sádā ǀ yájīyān ǀ abhí ǀ práyāṃsi ǀ sú-dhitāni ǀ hí ǀ khyát ǀyájāmahai ǀ yajñíyān ǀ hánta ǀ devā́n ǀ ī́ḷāmahai ǀ ī́ḍyān ǀ ā́jyena ǁ
verses.english_translation: Best Priest, he hath been won by being seated, for he hath looked on the well-ordered viands. Come, let usworship Gods who must be worshipped, and pouring oil, laud those who should be lauded.
verses.wilson_translation: Thehotā, most skilled in worship, has been sanctified by his seat (at the altar); he contemplates thesacred offerings reverently plural ced (before him); let us speedily worship with ghī the gods to whom worship isdue; let us praise those who are entitled to praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Best Priest, he hath been won by being seated, for he hath looked on the well-ordered viands. Come, let usworship Gods who must be worshipped, and pouring oil, laud those who should be lauded.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: साध्वीमकर्देववीतिं नो अद्य यज्ञस्य जिह्वामविदाम गुह्यां ।स आयुरागात्सुरभिर्वसानो भद्रामकर्देवहूतिं नो अद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: sādhvī́m ǀ akaḥ ǀ devá-vītim ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ yajñásya ǀ jihvā́m ǀ avidāma ǀ gúhyām ǀsáḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ surabhíḥ ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ bhadrā́m ǀ akaḥ ǀ devá-hūtim ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now hath he made the feast of Gods effective: now have we found the secret tongue of worship. Now hath he come, sweet, robed in vital vigour, and made our calling on the Gods effective.
verses.wilson_translation: He has today made our banquet to the gods efficacious; we have obtained the mysterious tongue ofsacrifice; he has come, fragrant, clothed with life; he makes our oblation to the gods today auspicious.
verses.griffith_verse: Now hath he made the feast of Gods effective: now have we found the secret tongue of worship. Now hath he come, sweet, robed in vital vigour, and made our calling on the Gods effective.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराँ अभि देवा असाम ।ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ adyá ǀ vācáḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ masīya ǀ yéna ǀ ásurān ǀ abhí ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ásāma ǀū́rja-adaḥ ǀ utá ǀ yajñiyāsaḥ ǀ páñca ǀ janāḥ ǀ máma ǀ hotrám ǀ juṣadhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This prelude of my speech I now will utter, whereby we Gods may quell our Asura foemen. Eaters of strengthening food who merit worship, O ye Five Tribes, be pleased with mine oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agnispeaks). I communicate today the best advice by which we gods may overcome theasuras; doyou who are the eaters of sacrificial food, who are entitled to worship, and you five orders of men, be plural ased bymy (discharge of) the office ofhotā.
verses.griffith_verse: This prelude of my speech I now will utter, whereby we Gods may quell our Asura foemen. Eaters of strengthening food who merit worship, O ye Five Tribes, be pleased with mine oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषंतां गोजाता उत ये यज्ञियासः ।पृथिवी नः पार्थिवात्पात्वंहसोऽंतरिक्षं दिव्यात्पात्वस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: páñca ǀ jánāḥ ǀ máma ǀ hotrám ǀ juṣantām ǀ gó-jātāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀpṛthivī́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pā́rthivāt ǀ pātu ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ divyā́t ǀ pātu ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Five Tribes be pleased with mine oblation, and the Cow's Sons and all who merit worship. From earthly trouble may the earth protect us, and air's mid realm from woe that comes from heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: May the fiver orders of men, may those who were born for the sake of ghī, may those who areentitled to worship be plural ased by my (discharge of) the office ofhotā; may earth preserve us from all earthly sin;may the firmament preserve us from heavenly (sin).
verses.griffith_verse: May the Five Tribes be pleased with mine oblation, and the Cow's Sons and all who merit worship. From earthly trouble may the earth protect us, and air's mid realm from woe that comes from heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तंतुं तन्वन्रजसो भानुमन्विहि ज्योतिष्मतः पथो रक्ष धिया कृतान् ।अनुल्बणं वयत जोगुवामपो मनुर्भव जनया दैव्यं जनं ॥
verses.transliteration: tántum ǀ tanván ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ bhānúm ǀ ánu ǀ ihi ǀ jyótiṣmataḥ ǀ patháḥ ǀ rakṣa ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ kṛtā́n ǀanulbaṇám ǀ vayata ǀ jóguvām ǀ ápaḥ ǀ mánuḥ ǀ bhava ǀ janáya ǀ dáivyam ǀ jánam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Spinning the thread, follow the region's splendid light: guard thou the path ways well which wisdom hath prepared. Weave ye the knotless labour of the bards who sing: be Manu thou, and bring the Heavenly People forth.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods) spreading out the sacrifice, follow the illuminator of the world (the sun); protect theluminous paths (of the gods) constructed by sacred acts; may Agnirender the pious works of the worshipper freefrom defect; become Manu, genitive rate the people of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Spinning the thread, follow the region's splendid light: guard thou the path ways well which wisdom hath prepared. Weave ye the knotless labour of the bards who sing: be Manu thou, and bring the Heavenly People forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षानहो नह्यतनोत सोम्या इष्कृणुध्वं रशना ओत पिंशत ।अष्टावंधुरं वहताभितो रथं येन देवासो अनयन्नभि प्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: akṣa-náhaḥ ǀ nahyatana ǀ utá ǀ somyāḥ ǀ íṣkṛṇudhvam ǀ raśanā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ utá ǀ piṃśata ǀaṣṭā́-vandhuram ǀ vahata ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ yéna ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ánayan ǀ abhí ǀ priyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lovers of Soma, bind the chariot traces fast: set ye the reins in order and embellish them. Bring hitherward the car with seats where eight may sit, whereon the Gods have brought the treasure that we love.
verses.wilson_translation: (The gods to one another). Drinkers of the Soma, bind (the horses) that are to be fastened to the pole;prepare the reins; caparison (the steeds); accompany everywhere (in your cars) the chariot which has eightseats with which the gods bring us acceptable (wealth).
verses.griffith_verse: Lovers of Soma, bind the chariot traces fast: set ye the reins in order and embellish them. Bring hitherward the car with seats where eight may sit, whereon the Gods have brought the treasure that we love.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्मन्वती रीयते सं रभध्वमुत्तिष्ठत प्र तरता सखायः ।अत्रा जहाम ये असन्नशेवाः शिवान्वयमुत्तरेमाभि वाजान् ॥
verses.transliteration: áśman-vatī ǀ rīyate ǀ sám ǀ rabhadhvam ǀ út ǀ tiṣṭhata ǀ prá ǀ tarata ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀátra ǀ jahāma ǀ yé ǀ ásan ǀ áśevāḥ ǀ śivā́n ǀ vayám ǀ út ǀ tarema ǀ abhí ǀ vā́jān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here flows Asmanvati: hold fast each other, keep yourselves up, and pass, my friends, the river. There let us leave the Powers that brought no profit, and cross the flood to Powers that are auspicious.
verses.wilson_translation: The aśmanvatī flows along; be alert; rise up, cross over, may friends; here let us leave those whoare unhappy, so that we may cross over to auspicious sacrificial viands.
verses.griffith_verse: Here flows Asmanvati: hold fast each other, keep yourselves up, and pass, my friends, the river. There let us leave the Powers that brought no profit, and cross the flood to Powers that are auspicious.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वष्टा माया वेदपसामपस्तमो बिभ्रत्पात्रा देवपानानि शंतमा ।शिशीते नूनं परशुं स्वायसं येन वृश्चादेतशो ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tváṣṭā ǀ māyā́ ǀ vet ǀ apásām ǀ apáḥ-tamaḥ ǀ bíbhrat ǀ pā́trā ǀ deva-pā́nāni ǀ śám-tamā ǀśíśīte ǀ nūnám ǀ paraśúm ǀ su-āyasám ǀ yéna ǀ vṛścā́t ǀ étaśaḥ ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tvaṣṭar, most deft of workmen, knew each magic art, bringing most blessed bowls that hold the drink of Gods. His axe, wrought of good metal, he is sharpening now, wherewith the radiant Brahmaṇaspati will cut.
verses.wilson_translation: Tvaṣṭāknows the arts of fabricating (drinking vessels), the most skilful of artificers bearing thesacred drinking cups out of which the gods drink-- verily he sharpens his axe of good metal, wherewith thewhite- complexionedbrahmaṇaspaticuts them.
verses.griffith_verse: Tvaṣṭar, most deft of workmen, knew each magic art, bringing most blessed bowls that hold the drink of Gods. His axe, wrought of good metal, he is sharpening now, wherewith the radiant Brahmaṇaspati will cut.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सतो नूनं कवयः सं शिशीत वाशीभिर्याभिरमृताय तक्षथ ।विद्वांसः पदा गुह्यानि कर्तन येन देवासो अमृतत्वमानशुः ॥
verses.transliteration: satáḥ ǀ nūnám ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ sám ǀ śiśīta ǀ vā́śībhiḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ amṛ́tāya ǀ tákṣatha ǀvidvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ padā́ ǀ gúhyāni ǀ kartana ǀ yéna ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now, O ye Sapient Ones, make ye the axes sharp wherewith ye fashion bowls to hold the Amṛta. Knowing the secret places make ye ready that whereby the Gods have gotten immortality.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily being sages, (Ṛbhus) sharpen the instrumental uments with which you fabricate the cups for the nectaṛDo you, who are wise, prepare the mysterious paths whereby tte gods have attained to immortality.
verses.griffith_verse: Now, O ye Sapient Ones, make ye the axes sharp wherewith ye fashion bowls to hold the Amṛta. Knowing the secret places make ye ready that whereby the Gods have gotten immortality.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गर्भे योषामदधुर्वत्समासन्यपीच्येन मनसोत जिह्वया ।स विश्वाहा सुमना योग्या अभि सिषासनिर्वनते कार इज्जितिं ॥
verses.transliteration: gárbhe ǀ yóṣām ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ vatsám ǀ āsáni ǀ apīcyéna ǀ mánasā ǀ utá ǀ jihváyā ǀsáḥ ǀ viśvā́hā ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ yogyā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sisāsániḥ ǀ vanate ǀ kāráḥ ǀ ít ǀ jítim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye with a secret tongue and dark intention laid the maiden deep within, the calf within the mouth. They evermore are near us with their gracious help: successful is the song that strives for victory.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts) plural ced a feminine le in the enveloping hide (of a dead cow), and a calf in the mouth (of adead cow), with mind and tongue, aiming (at deification); daily the genitive rous (fraternity of theṚbhus) offerssuitable praises (to the gods), granting victory over our foes.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye with a secret tongue and dark intention laid the maiden deep within, the calf within the mouth. They evermore are near us with their gracious help: successful is the song that strives for victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I SING thy fame that, Maghavan, through thy Greatness the heavens and earth invoked thee in their terror,Thou, aiding Gods, didst quell the power of Dāsas, what time thou holpest many a race, O Indra. When thou wast roaming, waxen strong in body, telling thy might, Indra, among the people,All that men called thy battles was illusion: no foe hast thou to-day, nor erst hast found one. Who are the Ṛṣis, then, who comprehended before our time the bounds of all thy greatness?For from thy body thou hast generated at the same time the Mother and the Father. Thou, Mighty Steer, hast four supremest natures, Asura natures that may ne’er be injured.All these, O Maghavan, thou surely knowest, wherewith thou hast performed thy great achievements. Thou hast all treasures in thy sole possession, treasures made manifest and treasures hidden.Defer not thou, O Maghavan, my longing: thou, art Director, Indra, thou art Giver. To him who set the light in things of splendour, and with all sweetness blent essential sweetness,To Indra hath this welcome hymn that strengthens been uttered by the votary Bṛhaduktha.

verses.sanskrit: तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा यत्त्वा भीते रोदसी अह्वयेतां ।प्रावो देवाँ आतिरो दासमोजः प्रजायै त्वस्यै यदशिक्ष इंद्र ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́m ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ kīrtím ǀ magha-van ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ bhīté íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ áhvayetām ǀprá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ atiraḥ ǀ dā́sam ǀ ójaḥ ǀ pra-jā́yai ǀ tvasyai ǀ yát ǀ áśikṣaḥ ǀ indra ǁ
verses.english_translation: I SING thy fame that, Maghavan, through thy Greatness the heavens and earth invoked thee in their terror, Thou, aiding Gods, didst quell the power of Dāsas, what time thou holpest many a race, O Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: (I celebrate), Maghavat, the great glory (you have acquired) by your might; when heaven and earthalarmed called upon you, you did defend the gods, and destroy (their) adversary; (I celebrate your glory),Indra,in that you gave strength to one person n (the worshipper).
verses.griffith_verse: I SING thy fame that, Maghavan, through thy Greatness the heavens and earth invoked thee in their terror, Thou, aiding Gods, didst quell the power of Dāsas, what time thou holpest many a race, O Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदचरस्तन्वा वावृधानो बलानींद्र प्रब्रुवाणो जनेषु ।मायेत्सा ते यानि युद्धान्याहुर्नाद्य शत्रुं ननु पुरा विवित्से ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ácaraḥ ǀ tanvā́ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ bálāni ǀ indra ǀ pra-bruvāṇáḥ ǀ jáneṣu ǀmāyā́ ǀ ít ǀ sā́ ǀ te ǀ yā́ni ǀ yuddhā́ni ǀ āhúḥ ǀ ná ǀ adyá ǀ śátrum ǀ nanú ǀ purā́ ǀ vivitse ǁ
verses.english_translation: When thou wast roaming, waxen strong in body, telling thy might, Indra, among the people, All that men called thy battles was illusion: no foe hast thou to-day, nor erst hast found one.
verses.wilson_translation: When you proceed,Indra, increasing in form, and proclaiming your prowess among mankind, false isthat your (wandering), false the combats which you have narrated; you (find) now no enemy (to attack), did youformerly find one? person n you have genitive rated at once both mother and father (or earth and heaven)?
verses.griffith_verse: When thou wast roaming, waxen strong in body, telling thy might, Indra, among the people, All that men called thy battles was illusion: no foe hast thou to-day, nor erst hast found one.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क उ नु ते महिमनः समस्यास्मत्पूर्व ऋषयोऽंतमापुः ।यन्मातरं च पितरं च साकमजनयथास्तन्वः स्वायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ké ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ te ǀ mahimánaḥ ǀ samasya ǀ asmát ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ántam ǀ āpuḥ ǀyát ǀ mātáram ǀ ca ǀ pitáram ǀ ca ǀ sākám ǀ ájanayathāḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ svā́yāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who are the Ṛṣis, then, who comprehended before our time the bounds of all thy greatness? For from thy body thou hast generated at the same time the Mother and the Father.
verses.griffith_verse: Who are the Ṛṣis, then, who comprehended before our time the bounds of all thy greatness? For from thy body thou hast generated at the same time the Mother and the Father.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चत्वारि ते असुर्याणि नामादाभ्यानि महिषस्य संति ।त्वमंग तानि विश्वानि वित्से येभिः कर्माणि मघवंचकर्थ ॥
verses.transliteration: catvā́ri ǀ te ǀ asuryā́ṇi ǀ nā́ma ǀ ádābhyāni ǀ mahiṣásya ǀ santi ǀtvám ǀ aṅgá ǀ tā́ni ǀ víśvāni ǀ vitse ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ kármāṇi ǀ magha-van ǀ cakártha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Mighty Steer, hast four supremest natures, Asura natures that may ne’er be injured. All these, O Maghavan, thou surely knowest, wherewith thou hast performed thy great achievements.
verses.wilson_translation: Four are theasura-slaying uninjurable forms of you the mighty one: you know them all wherewith,Maghavat, you have achieved your exploits.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Mighty Steer, hast four supremest natures, Asura natures that may ne’er be injured. All these, O Maghavan, thou surely knowest, wherewith thou hast performed thy great achievements.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं विश्वा दधिषे केवलानि यान्याविर्या च गुहा वसूनि ।काममिन्मे मघवन्मा वि तारीस्त्वमाज्ञाता त्वमिंद्रासि दाता ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ víśvā ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ kévalāni ǀ yā́ni ǀ āvíḥ ǀ yā́ ǀ ca ǀ gúhā ǀ vásūni ǀkā́mam ǀ ít ǀ me ǀ magha-van ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ tārīḥ ǀ tvám ǀ ā-jñātā́ ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ asi ǀ dātā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast all treasures in thy sole possession, treasures made manifest and treasures hidden. Defer not thou, O Maghavan, my longing: thou, art Director, Indra, thou art Giver.
verses.wilson_translation: You have in your keeping all treasures, which are yours exclusively, whether they be manifest orhidden; thwart not, therefore, Maghavat, my desire (for wealth); for you are cognizant (of my desire), you are thedonor.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast all treasures in thy sole possession, treasures made manifest and treasures hidden. Defer not thou, O Maghavan, my longing: thou, art Director, Indra, thou art Giver.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अदधाज्ज्योतिषि ज्योतिरंतर्यो असृजन्मधुना सं मधूनि ।अध प्रियं शूषमिंद्राय मन्म ब्रह्मकृतो बृहदुक्थादवाचि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ádadhāt ǀ jyótiṣi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ásṛjat ǀ mádhunā ǀ sám ǀ mádhūni ǀádha ǀ priyám ǀ śūṣám ǀ índrāya ǀ mánma ǀ brahma-kṛ́taḥ ǀ bṛhát-ukthāt ǀ avāci ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him who set the light in things of splendour, and with all sweetness blent essential sweetness, To Indra hath this welcome hymn that strengthens been uttered by the votary Bṛhaduktha.
verses.wilson_translation: To that Indra, who has deposited the light in luminous bodies, who has flavoured sweet things withsweetness, this acceptable invigorating praise has been recited by Bṛhaduktha, the author of the prayer.
verses.griffith_verse: To him who set the light in things of splendour, and with all sweetness blent essential sweetness, To Indra hath this welcome hymn that strengthens been uttered by the votary Bṛhaduktha.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FAR is that secret name by which, in terror, the worlds invoked thee and thou gavest vigourThe earth and heaven thou settest near each other, and Maghavan, madest bright thy Brother's Children. Great is that secret name and far-extending, whereby thou madest all that is and shall be.The Five Tribes whom he loveth well have entered the light he loveth that was made aforetime. He filled the heaven and earth and all between them, Gods five times sevenfold in their proper seasons.With four-and-thirty lights he looks around him, lights of one colour though their ways are divers. As first among the lights, O Dawn, thou shonest, whereby thou broughtest forth the Stay of Increase,Great art thou, matchless is thine Asura nature, who, high above, art kin to those beneath thee. The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him.Behold the Gods’ high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living. Strong is the Red Bird in his strength, great Hero, who from of old hath had no nest to dwell in.That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many. Through these the Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in power to smite down Vṛtra,—Who through the might of Indra's operation came forth as Gods in course of Law and Order. All-strong, performing works with his companion, All-marking, rapid Victor, Curse-averter,The Hero, waxing, after draughts of Soma, blew far from heaven the Dasyus with his weapon.

verses.sanskrit: दूरे तन्नाम गुह्यं पराचैर्यत्त्वा भीते अह्वयेतां वयोधै ।उदस्तभ्नाः पृथिवीं द्यामभीके भ्रातुः पुत्रान्मघवंतित्विषाणः ॥
verses.transliteration: dūré ǀ tát ǀ nā́ma ǀ gúhyam ǀ parācáiḥ ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ bhīté íti ǀ áhvayetām ǀ vayaḥ-dhái ǀút ǀ astabhnāḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ abhī́ke ǀ bhrā́tuḥ ǀ putrā́n ǀ magha-van ǀ titviṣāṇáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FAR is that secret name by which, in terror, the worlds invoked thee and thou gavest vigour The earth and heaven thou settest near each other, and Maghavan, madest bright thy Brother's Children.
verses.wilson_translation: Your form held secret (by men) with averted faces, is far from here; when (heaven and earth) alarmed,called upon you for the sustenance (of the world), then you did fix in their proximity the heaven and earth,illumining, Maghavat, the sons, of (your) brother.
verses.griffith_verse: FAR is that secret name by which, in terror, the worlds invoked thee and thou gavest vigour The earth and heaven thou settest near each other, and Maghavan, madest bright thy Brother's Children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महत्तन्नाम गुह्यं पुरुस्पृग्येन भूतं जनयो येन भव्यं ।प्रत्नं जातं ज्योतिर्यदस्य प्रियं प्रियाः समविशंत पंच ॥
verses.transliteration: mahát ǀ tát ǀ nā́ma ǀ gúhyam ǀ puru-spṛ́k ǀ yéna ǀ bhūtám ǀ janáyaḥ ǀ yéna ǀ bhávyam ǀpratnám ǀ jātám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ priyám ǀ priyā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ aviśanta ǀ páñca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Great is that secret name and far-extending, whereby thou madest all that is and shall be. The Five Tribes whom he loveth well have entered the light he loveth that was made aforetime.
verses.wilson_translation: That mighty mysterious form, desired of many, wherewith you have engendered the past, and(engender) the future, the ancient manifested light, the beloved of Indra, into which the five (orders of beings)delighted enter.
verses.griffith_verse: Great is that secret name and far-extending, whereby thou madest all that is and shall be. The Five Tribes whom he loveth well have entered the light he loveth that was made aforetime.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ रोदसी अपृणादोत मध्यं पंच देवाँ ऋतुशः सप्तसप्त ।चतुस्त्रिंशता पुरुधा वि चष्टे सरूपेण ज्योतिषा विव्रतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ apṛṇāt ǀ ā́ ǀ utá ǀ mádhyam ǀ páñca ǀ devā́n ǀ ṛtu-śáḥ ǀ saptá-sapta ǀcátuḥ-triṃśatā ǀ purudhā́ ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀ sá-rūpeṇa ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ ví-vratena ǁ
verses.english_translation: He filled the heaven and earth and all between them, Gods five times sevenfold in their proper seasons. With four-and-thirty lights he looks around him, lights of one colour though their ways are divers.
verses.wilson_translation: He has filled heaven and earth (with his ethereal form) as well as the mid-heaven; he contemplates invarious aspects the five orders of beings, the classes of seven in their seasons, with the thirty-four (deities),(endowed) with light of like nature, and with various functions.
verses.griffith_verse: He filled the heaven and earth and all between them, Gods five times sevenfold in their proper seasons. With four-and-thirty lights he looks around him, lights of one colour though their ways are divers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदुष औच्छः प्रथमा विभानामजनयो येन पुष्टस्य पुष्टं ।यत्ते जामित्वमवरं परस्या महन्महत्या असुरत्वमेकं ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ uṣaḥ ǀ áucchaḥ ǀ prathamā́ ǀ vi-bhā́nām ǀ ájanayaḥ ǀ yéna ǀ puṣṭásya ǀ puṣṭám ǀyát ǀ te ǀ jāmi-tvám ǀ ávaram ǀ párasyāḥ ǀ mahát ǀ mahatyā́ḥ ǀ asura-tvám ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: As first among the lights, O Dawn, thou shonest, whereby thou broughtest forth the Stay of Increase, Great art thou, matchless is thine Asura nature, who, high above, art kin to those beneath thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Since you, Uṣas, did shine forth the first of luminaries, whereby you did beget the nourishment ofnourishment (the Sun); unequalled is the mighty greatness of you who are mighty, since your relationship isdownwards (towards us), though you are stationed on high.
verses.griffith_verse: As first among the lights, O Dawn, thou shonest, whereby thou broughtest forth the Stay of Increase, Great art thou, matchless is thine Asura nature, who, high above, art kin to those beneath thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विधुं दद्राणं समने बहूनां युवानं संतं पलितो जगार ।देवस्य पश्य काव्यं महित्वाद्या ममार स ह्यः समान ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-dhúm ǀ dadrāṇám ǀ sámane ǀ bahūnā́m ǀ yúvānam ǀ sántam ǀ palitáḥ ǀ jagāra ǀdevásya ǀ paśya ǀ kā́vyam ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ adyá ǀ mamā́ra ǀ sáḥ ǀ hyáḥ ǀ sám ǀ āna ǁ
verses.english_translation: The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him. Behold the Gods’ high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living.
verses.wilson_translation: The grey-haired has swallowed the warlike (man) the scatterer of many foes, in battle being young;behold the power of the deity (endowed) with might; he dies today, he is alive tomorrow.
verses.griffith_verse: The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him. Behold the Gods’ high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शाक्मना शाको अरुणः सुपर्ण आ यो महः शूरः सनादनीळः ।यच्चिकेत सत्यमित्तन्न मोघं वसु स्पार्हमुत जेतोत दाता ॥
verses.transliteration: śā́kmanā ǀ śākáḥ ǀ aruṇáḥ ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ sanā́t ǀ ánīḷaḥ ǀyát ǀ cikéta ǀ satyám ǀ ít ǀ tát ǀ ná ǀ mógham ǀ vásu ǀ spārhám ǀ utá ǀ jétā ǀ utá ǀ dā́tā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong is the Red Bird in his strength, great Hero, who from of old hath had no nest to dwell in. That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many.
verses.wilson_translation: Vigorous with (innate) vigour, (comes) a purple-coloured bird, mighty, heroic, ancient, having no nest;that which he knows is truth, and is not vain; (he is) the conqueror and distributor of desirable wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong is the Red Bird in his strength, great Hero, who from of old hath had no nest to dwell in. That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऐभिर्ददे वृष्ण्या पौंस्यानि येभिरौक्षद्वृत्रहत्याय वज्री ।ये कर्मणः क्रियमाणस्य मह्न ऋतेकर्ममुदजायंत देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ebhiḥ ǀ dade ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyā ǀ páuṃsyāni ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ áukṣat ǀ vṛtra-hátyāya ǀ vajrī́ ǀyé ǀ kármaṇaḥ ǀ kriyámāṇasya ǀ mahnā́ ǀ ṛte-karmám ǀ ut-ájāyanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through these the Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in power to smite down Vṛtra,— Who through the might of Indra's operation came forth as Gods in course of Law and Order.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrabestows fertilizing energies (accompanied by these Marutsin whose company the thunderersends down showers in order to destroy sin; the deities who were born for giving rain (to assist) in the actperformed be great Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Through these the Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in power to smite down Vṛtra,— Who through the might of Indra's operation came forth as Gods in course of Law and Order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युजा कर्माणि जनयन्विश्वौजा अशस्तिहा विश्वमनास्तुराषाट् ।पीत्वी सोमस्य दिव आ वृधानः शूरो निर्युधाधमद्दस्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: yujā́ ǀ kármāṇi ǀ janáyan ǀ viśvá-ojāḥ ǀ aśasti-hā́ ǀ viśvá-manāḥ ǀ turāṣā́ṭ ǀpītvī́ ǀ sómasya ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ yudhā́ ǀ adhamat ǀ dásyūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: All-strong, performing works with his companion, All-marking, rapid Victor, Curse-averter, The Hero, waxing, after draughts of Soma, blew far from heaven the Dasyus with his weapon.
verses.wilson_translation: Accomplishing his duty with their assistance, the all-powerful Indra, the destroyer of the wicked, theall-wise, the quick subduer of foes, descending from heaven, and quaffing the Soma, invogirated and a hero, hedemolishes the Dasyuswith his thunderbolt.
verses.griffith_verse: All-strong, performing works with his companion, All-marking, rapid Victor, Curse-averter, The Hero, waxing, after draughts of Soma, blew far from heaven the Dasyus with his weapon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HERE is one light for thee, another yonder: enter the third and he therewith united.Uniting with a body be thou welcome, dear to the Gods in their sublimest birthplace. Bearing thy body, Vajin, may thy body afford us blessing and thyself protection.Unswerving, stablish as it were in heaven thine own light as the mighty God's supporter. Strong Steed art thou: go to the yearning Maidens with vigour, happily go to heaven and praises:Fly happily to the Gods with easy passage, according to the first and faithful statutes. Part of their grandeur have the Fathers also gained: the Gods have seated mental power in them as Gods.They have embraced within themselves all energies, which, issuing forth, again into their bodies pass. They strode through all the region with victorious might, establishing the old immeasurable laws.They compassed in their bodies all existing things, and streamed forth offipring in many successive forms. In two ways have the sons established in his place the Asura who finds the light, by the third act,As fathers, they have set their heritage on earth, their offspring, as a thread continuously spun out. As in a ship through billows, so through regions of air, with blessings, through toils and troublesHath Bṛhaduktha brought his seed with glory, and placed it here and in the realms beyond us.

verses.sanskrit: इदं त एकं पर ऊ त एकं तृतीयेन ज्योतिषा सं विशस्व ।संवेशने तन्वश्चारुरेधि प्रियो देवानां परमे जनित्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ te ǀ ékam ǀ paráḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ te ǀ ékam ǀ tṛtī́yena ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ sám ǀ viśasva ǀsam-véśane ǀ tanváḥ ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ edhi ǀ priyáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ paramé ǀ janítre ǁ
verses.english_translation: HERE is one light for thee, another yonder: enter the third and he therewith united. Uniting with a body be thou welcome, dear to the Gods in their sublimest birthplace.
verses.wilson_translation: This (light) is one (portion) of you, and this other is one (portion); with your third light enter into (outerradiance); on the entrance of the body into (the sun), the supreme birthplace of the gods, become lovely andbeloved.
verses.griffith_verse: HERE is one light for thee, another yonder: enter the third and he therewith united. Uniting with a body be thou welcome, dear to the Gods in their sublimest birthplace.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तनूष्टे वाजिंतन्वं नयंती वाममस्मभ्यं धातु शर्म तुभ्यं ।अह्रुतो महो धरुणाय देवांदिवीव ज्योतिः स्वमा मिमीयाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tanū́ḥ ǀ te ǀ vājin ǀ tanvám ǀ náyantī ǀ vāmám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dhā́tu ǀ śárma ǀ túbhyam ǀáhrutaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ dharúṇāya ǀ devā́n ǀ diví-iva ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ svám ǀ ā́ ǀ mimīyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bearing thy body, Vajin, may thy body afford us blessing and thyself protection. Unswerving, stablish as it were in heaven thine own light as the mighty God's supporter.
verses.wilson_translation: May this body (the earth) conveying your body,Vājin, give precious wealth to us and happiness toyou; an ddo you, without stumbling, enter among the great gods for their support; and the light that is in heaven(the sun) and your own (light).
verses.griffith_verse: Bearing thy body, Vajin, may thy body afford us blessing and thyself protection. Unswerving, stablish as it were in heaven thine own light as the mighty God's supporter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वाज्यसि वाजिनेना सुवेनीः सुवितः स्तोमं सुवितो दिवं गाः ।सुवितो धर्म प्रथमानु सत्या सुवितो देवान्त्सुवितोऽनु पत्म ॥
verses.transliteration: vājī́ ǀ asi ǀ vā́jinena ǀ su-venī́ḥ ǀ suvitáḥ ǀ stómam ǀ suvitáḥ ǀ dívam ǀ gāḥ ǀsuvitáḥ ǀ dhárma ǀ prathamā́ ǀ ánu ǀ satyā́ ǀ suvitáḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ suvitáḥ ǀ ánu ǀ pátma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong Steed art thou: go to the yearning Maidens with vigour, happily go to heaven and praises: Fly happily to the Gods with easy passage, according to the first and faithful statutes.
verses.wilson_translation: You are,Vājin, (strong) through food; you (are) well-beloved; urged thereto follow (the object of your)praise; urged thereto proceed to heaven; urged thereto pursue the duties that are the most important and sure ofreward; urged thereto follow the gods; urged thereto follow (the light), descending (from heaven).
verses.griffith_verse: Strong Steed art thou: go to the yearning Maidens with vigour, happily go to heaven and praises: Fly happily to the Gods with easy passage, according to the first and faithful statutes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: महिम्न एषां पितरश्चनेशिरे देवा देवेष्वदधुरपि क्रतुं ।समविव्यचुरुत यान्यत्विषुरैषां तनूषु नि विविशुः पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: mahimnáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ caná ǀ īśire ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ adadhuḥ ǀ ápi ǀ krátum ǀsám ǀ avivyacuḥ ǀ utá ǀ yā́ni ǀ átviṣuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ ní ǀ viviśuḥ ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Part of their grandeur have the Fathers also gained: the Gods have seated mental power in them as Gods. They have embraced within themselves all energies, which, issuing forth, again into their bodies pass.
verses.wilson_translation: Our progenitors (the Aṅgirasas) were lords over the might of those (divinities), they having becomegods imposed their will upon the gods; they attained also (the radiances) which shone forth, and they againentered the bodies of those (gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Part of their grandeur have the Fathers also gained: the Gods have seated mental power in them as Gods. They have embraced within themselves all energies, which, issuing forth, again into their bodies pass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहोभिर्विश्वं परि चक्रमू रजः पूर्वा धामान्यमिता मिमानाः ।तनूषु विश्वा भुवना नि येमिरे प्रासारयंत पुरुध प्रजा अनु ॥
verses.transliteration: sáhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ pári ǀ cakramuḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ pū́rvā ǀ dhā́māni ǀ ámitā ǀ mímānāḥ ǀtanū́ṣu ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ ní ǀ yemire ǀ prá ǀ asārayanta ǀ purudhá ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǁ
verses.english_translation: They strode through all the region with victorious might, establishing the old immeasurable laws. They compassed in their bodies all existing things, and streamed forth offipring in many successive forms.
verses.wilson_translation: By their powers they traversed the whole world, measuring the ancient divisions (till then)unmeasured; they restricted all existent beings to their proper forms; they distributed in many directions (light)among the people.
verses.griffith_verse: They strode through all the region with victorious might, establishing the old immeasurable laws. They compassed in their bodies all existing things, and streamed forth offipring in many successive forms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्विधा सूनवोऽसुरं स्वर्विदमास्थापयंत तृतीयेन कर्मणा ।स्वां प्रजां पितरः पित्र्यं सह आवरेष्वदधुस्तंतुमाततं ॥
verses.transliteration: dvídhā ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ ásuram ǀ svaḥ-vídam ǀ ā́ ǀ asthāpayanta ǀ tṛtī́yena ǀ kármaṇā ǀsvā́m ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ pítryam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ávareṣu ǀ adadhuḥ ǀ tántum ǀ ā́-tatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: In two ways have the sons established in his place the Asura who finds the light, by the third act, As fathers, they have set their heritage on earth, their offspring, as a thread continuously spun out.
verses.wilson_translation: The sons (ofĀditya, the Aṅgirasas), established by the third act of duty, the mighty, all-wise (sun) inhis two-fold (condition of rising and setting); our progenitors (having begotten) their own progeny, deposited inthe best (of them) the paternal strength, (making) an extended line (of progeny).
verses.griffith_verse: In two ways have the sons established in his place the Asura who finds the light, by the third act, As fathers, they have set their heritage on earth, their offspring, as a thread continuously spun out.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नावा न क्षोदः प्रदिशः पृथिव्याः स्वस्तिभिरति दुर्गाणि विश्वा ।स्वां प्रजां बृहदुक्थो महित्वावरेष्वदधादा परेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: nāvā́ ǀ ná ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ áti ǀ duḥ-gā́ni ǀ víśvā ǀsvā́m ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ bṛhát-ukthaḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ ávareṣu ǀ adadhāt ǀ ā́ ǀ páreṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: As in a ship through billows, so through regions of air, with blessings, through toils and troubles Hath Bṛhaduktha brought his seed with glory, and placed it here and in the realms beyond us.
verses.wilson_translation: As men pass over the water to the several quarters of the earth in a ship; (as they pass over) alldifficulties by the blessings (of fortune),Bṛhadukthaby his might has committed his own offspring to those onthis side, and to those on the other side.
verses.griffith_verse: As in a ship through billows, so through regions of air, with blessings, through toils and troubles Hath Bṛhaduktha brought his seed with glory, and placed it here and in the realms beyond us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIL Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser's sacrifice:Let no malignity dwell with us. May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out to reach the Gods,That perfecteth the sacrifice. We call the spirit hither with the Soma of our parted sires,Yea, with the Fathers' holy hymns. Thy spirit come to thee again for wisdom, energy, and lire,That thou mayst long behold the sun! O Fathers, may the Heavenly Folk give us our spirit once again,That we may be with those who live. O Soma with the spirit still within us, blest with progeny,May we be busied in the law.

verses.sanskrit: मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिंद्र सोमिनः ।मांतः स्थुर्नो अरातयः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ prá ǀ gāma ǀ patháḥ ǀ vayám ǀ mā́ ǀ yajñā́t ǀ indra ǀ somínaḥ ǀmā́ ǀ antáríti ǀ sthuḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ árātayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LET us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser's sacrifice: Let no malignity dwell with us.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us not depart,Indra, from the path; let us not (depart) from the sacrifice of the offerer of thelibation; let not our adversaries remain (in our plural ce).
verses.griffith_verse: LET us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser's sacrifice: Let no malignity dwell with us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो यज्ञस्य प्रसाधनस्तंतुर्देवेष्वाततः ।तमाहुतं नशीमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ yajñásya ǀ pra-sā́dhanaḥ ǀ tántuḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ ā́-tataḥ ǀtám ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ naśīmahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out to reach the Gods, That perfecteth the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May we obtain (the favour of) him to whom burnt offerings are presented, (Agni), who is the thread, theperfecter of sacrifice, drawn out (by the priests) to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out to reach the Gods, That perfecteth the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मनो न्वा हुवामहे नाराशंसेन सोमेन ।पितॄणां च मन्मभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: mánaḥ ǀ nú ǀ ā́ ǀ huvāmahe ǀ nārāśaṃséna ǀ sómena ǀpitṝṇā́m ǀ ca ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call the spirit hither with the Soma of our parted sires, Yea, with the Fathers' holy hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: We call upon the spirit (of Subandhu) with the Somaappropriated to the progenitors, with the praisesepithet of the Soma.Yajus. 3.53 reads stomena: praise is of to kinds, that of gods and men, the latter isnārāśamsaḥ, whence the epithet narāśaṃsa means, suited to man; that is, to deified men orpitṛs].
verses.griffith_verse: We call the spirit hither with the Soma of our parted sires, Yea, with the Fathers' holy hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ त एतु मनः पुनः क्रत्वे दक्षाय जीवसे ।ज्योक्च सूर्यं दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ te ǀ etu ǀ mánaḥ ǀ púnaríti ǀ krátve ǀ dákṣāya ǀ jīváse ǀjyók ǀ ca ǀ sū́ryam ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit come to thee again for wisdom, energy, and lire, That thou mayst long behold the sun!
verses.wilson_translation: May (your) spirit (Subandhu) come back again to perform pious acts; to exercise strength; to live; andlong to see the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit come to thee again for wisdom, energy, and lire, That thou mayst long behold the sun!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्नः पितरो मनो ददातु दैव्यो जनः ।जीवं व्रातं सचेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ dádātu ǀ dáivyaḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǀjīvám ǀ vrā́tam ǀ sacemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Fathers, may the Heavenly Folk give us our spirit once again, That we may be with those who live.
verses.wilson_translation: May our progenitors, may the host of the gods, restore (your) spirit; may we obtain (for you) theaggregate of the functions of life.
verses.griffith_verse: O Fathers, may the Heavenly Folk give us our spirit once again, That we may be with those who live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयं सोम व्रते तव मनस्तनूषु बिभ्रतः ।प्रजावंतः सचेमहि ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ soma ǀ vraté ǀ táva ǀ mánaḥ ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀprajā́-vantaḥ ǀ sacemahi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Soma with the spirit still within us, blest with progeny, May we be busied in the law.
verses.wilson_translation: Soma, fixing our minds, on your worship and its details, may we, blessed with progeny, obtain (theaggreagate of the functions of life)
verses.griffith_verse: O Soma with the spirit still within us, blest with progeny, May we be busied in the law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LVIII. Mānas or Spirit.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THY spirit, that went far away to Yama to Vivasvān's Son,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, that passed away to earth and heaven,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, away to the four-cornered earth,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away to the four quarters of the world,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, away unto the billowy sea,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away to beams of light that flash and flow,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, went to the waters and the plants,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, that visited the Sun and Dawn.We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away, away to lofty mountain heights,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away into this All, that lives and moves,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away to distant realms beyond our ken,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here. Thy spirit, that went far away to all that is and is to be,We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn heie.

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते यमं वैवस्वतं मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ yamám ǀ vaivasvatám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: THY spirit, that went far away to Yama to Vivasvān's Son, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: THY spirit, that went far away to Yama to Vivasvān's Son, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते दिवं यत्पृथिवीं मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ dívam ǀ yát ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, that passed away to earth and heaven, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, that passed away to earth and heaven, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते भूमिं चतुर्भृष्टिं मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ bhū́mim ǀ cátuḥ-bhṛṣṭim ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to the four-cornered earth, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to the four-cornered earth, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते चतस्रः प्रदिशो मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ cátasraḥ ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away to the four quarters of the world, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away to the four quarters of the world, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते समुद्रमर्णवं मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ samudrám ǀ arṇavám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, away unto the billowy sea, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, away unto the billowy sea, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते मरीचीः प्रवतो मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ márīcīḥ ǀ pra-vátaḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away to beams of light that flash and flow, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away to beams of light that flash and flow, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते अपो यदोषधीर्मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ apáḥ ǀ yát ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, went to the waters and the plants, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, went to the waters and the plants, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते सूर्यं यदुषसं मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ sū́ryam ǀ yát ǀ uṣásam ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, that visited the Sun and Dawn. We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, that visited the Sun and Dawn. We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते पर्वतान्बृहतो मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
