verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ párvatān ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to lofty mountain heights, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to lofty mountain heights, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते विश्वमिदं जगन्मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ víśvam ǀ idám ǀ jágat ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away into this All, that lives and moves, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away into this All, that lives and moves, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते पराः परावतो मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ párāḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away to distant realms beyond our ken, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away to distant realms beyond our ken, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते भूतं च भव्यं च मनो जगाम दूरकं ।तत्त आ वर्तयामसीह क्षयाय जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ bhūtám ǀ ca ǀ bhávyam ǀ ca ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jagā́ma ǀ dū́rakám ǀtát ǀ te ǀ ā́ ǀ vartayāmasi ǀ ihá ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy spirit, that went far away to all that is and is to be, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn heie.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy spirit, that went far away to all that is and is to be, We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn heie.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LIX. Nirrti and Others.
hymns.anukramani: १० बन्धु श्रुतबन्धुर्विप्रबन्धुर्गौपायनाः।१-३ निर्ऋतिः,४ निर्ऋतिः सोमश्च, ५-६असुनीतिः, ७ पृथिवी-द्वयन्तरिक्ष-सोम-पूष-पथ्या-स्वस्तयः,८-१० द्यावापृथिवी, १० (पूर्वार्धस्य) इन्द्र- द्यावापृथिव्यः। त्रिष्टुप् , ८ पंक्तिः,९ महापंक्तिः, १० पंक्त्युत्तरा।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . His life hath been renewed and carried forward as two men, car-borne, by the skilful driver.One falls, then seeks the goal with quickened vigour. Let Nirrti depart to distant places. Here is the psalm for wealth, and food, in plenty: let us do many deeds to bring us glory.All these our doings shall delight the singer. Let Nirrti depart to distant places. May we o’ercome our foes with acts of valour, as heaven is over earth, hills over lowlands.All these our deeds the singer hath considered. Let Nirrti depart to distant places. Give us not up as prey to death, O Soma still let us look upon the Sun arising.Let our old age with passing days be kindly. Let Nirrti depart to distant places. O Asuniti, keep the soul within us, and make the days we have to live yet longer.Grant that we still may look upon the sunlight: strengthen thy body with the oil we bring thee. Give us our sight again, O Asuniti, give us again our breath and our enjoyment.Long may we look upon the Sun uprising; O Anumati, favour thou and bless us. May Earth restore to us our vital spirit, may Heaven the Goddess and mid-air restore it.May Soma give us once again our body, and Pūṣan show the Path of peace and comfort. May both Worlds bless Subandhu, young Mothers of everlasting Law.May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee. Health-giving medicines descend sent down from heaven in twos and threes,Or wandering singly on the earth. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee. Drive forward thou the wagon-ox, O Indra, which brought Usinarani's wagon hither.May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.

verses.sanskrit: प्र तार्यायुः प्रतरं नवीयः स्थातारेव क्रतुमता रथस्य ।अध च्यवान उत्तवीत्यर्थं परातरं सु निर्ऋतिर्जिहीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tāri ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ návīyaḥ ǀ sthā́tārā-iva ǀ krátu-matā ǀ ráthasya ǀádha ǀ cyávānaḥ ǀ út ǀ tavīti ǀ ártham ǀ parā-tarám ǀ sú ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ jihītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: His life hath been renewed and carried forward as two men, car-borne, by the skilful driver. One falls, then seeks the goal with quickened vigour. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.wilson_translation: May the life of Subandhube augmented so as to be more lasting and newer, as men conveyed in acar (are carried on) by a skilful (driver); he who falls from life, increases (his) desire to live; may Nirṛtidepart faroff.
verses.griffith_verse: His life hath been renewed and carried forward as two men, car-borne, by the skilful driver. One falls, then seeks the goal with quickened vigour. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सामन्नु राये निधिमन्न्वन्नं करामहे सु पुरुध श्रवांसि ।ता नो विश्वानि जरिता ममत्तु परातरं सु निर्ऋतिर्जिहीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́man ǀ nú ǀ rāyé ǀ nidhi-mát ǀ nú ǀ ánnam ǀ kárāmahe ǀ sú ǀ purudhá ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ jaritā́ ǀ mamattu ǀ parā-tarám ǀ sú ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ jihītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here is the psalm for wealth, and food, in plenty: let us do many deeds to bring us glory. All these our doings shall delight the singer. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.wilson_translation: (When) the hymn (is being sung) let us offer (sacrificial) food, like a treasure (to Nirṛti) for the sake ofriches, and many kinds of sacrificial viands; may she, being praised, partake of all these our (offerings); may Niṛrti depart far off.
verses.griffith_verse: Here is the psalm for wealth, and food, in plenty: let us do many deeds to bring us glory. All these our doings shall delight the singer. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभी ष्वर्यः पौंस्यैर्भवेम द्यौर्न भूमिं गिरयो नाज्रान् ।ता नो विश्वानि जरिता चिकेत परातरं सु निर्ऋतिर्जिहीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ sú ǀ aryáḥ ǀ páuṃsyaiḥ ǀ bhavema ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhū́mim ǀ giráyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ájrān ǀtā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ jaritā́ ǀ ciketa ǀ parā-tarám ǀ sú ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ jihītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we o’ercome our foes with acts of valour, as heaven is over earth, hills over lowlands. All these our deeds the singer hath considered. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, by our manly exertions, overcome our enemies, as the Sun the earth, as thunderbolts theclouds; she, being praised, knows all these our (exploits); may Nirṛtidepart far off.
verses.griffith_verse: May we o’ercome our foes with acts of valour, as heaven is over earth, hills over lowlands. All these our deeds the singer hath considered. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मो षु णः सोम मृत्यवे परा दाः पश्येम नु सूर्यमुच्चरंतं ।द्युभिर्हितो जरिमा सू नो अस्तु परातरं सु निर्ऋतिर्जिहीतां ॥
verses.transliteration: mó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ soma ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǀ páśyema ǀ nú ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ut-cárantam ǀdyú-bhiḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǀ jarimā́ ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ parā-tarám ǀ sú ǀ níḥ-ṛtiḥ ǀ jihītām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us not up as prey to death, O Soma still let us look upon the Sun arising. Let our old age with passing days be kindly. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.wilson_translation: Give us not up,Soma, to death; may we (long) behold the rising sun; may our old age brought on by(passing) days be happy; may Nirṛtidepart far off.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us not up as prey to death, O Soma still let us look upon the Sun arising. Let our old age with passing days be kindly. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असुनीते मनो अस्मासु धारय जीवातवे सु प्र तिरा न आयुः ।रारंधि नः सूर्यस्य संदृशि घृतेन त्वं तन्वं वर्धयस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: ásu-nīte ǀ mánaḥ ǀ asmā́su ǀ dhāraya ǀ jīvā́tave ǀ sú ǀ prá ǀ tira ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀrarandhí ǀ naḥ ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ sam-dṛ́śi ǀ ghṛténa ǀ tvám ǀ tanvám ǀ vardhayasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Asuniti, keep the soul within us, and make the days we have to live yet longer. Grant that we still may look upon the sunlight: strengthen thy body with the oil we bring thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Asunīti, give us back the (departed) spirit; extend our life that we may live (long); establish us that wemay (long) behold the sun; do you cherish the body with the ghī (that we have offered).
verses.griffith_verse: O Asuniti, keep the soul within us, and make the days we have to live yet longer. Grant that we still may look upon the sunlight: strengthen thy body with the oil we bring thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असुनीते पुनरस्मासु चक्षुः पुनः प्राणमिह नो धेहि भोगं ।ज्योक्पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरंतमनुमते मृळया नः स्वस्ति ॥
verses.transliteration: ásu-nīte ǀ púnaḥ ǀ asmā́su ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ púnaríti ǀ prāṇám ǀ ihá ǀ naḥ ǀ dhehi ǀ bhógam ǀjyók ǀ paśyema ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ut-cárantam ǀ ánu-mate ǀ mṛḷáya ǀ naḥ ǀ svastí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give us our sight again, O Asuniti, give us again our breath and our enjoyment. Long may we look upon the Sun uprising; O Anumati, favour thou and bless us.
verses.wilson_translation: Restore to us, Asunīti, sight and breath, and enjoyment in this world; long may we behold the risingsun; make us happy, gracious (goddess), with prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: Give us our sight again, O Asuniti, give us again our breath and our enjoyment. Long may we look upon the Sun uprising; O Anumati, favour thou and bless us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्नो असुं पृथिवी ददातु पुनर्द्यौर्देवी पुनरंतरिक्षं ।पुनर्नः सोमस्तन्वं ददातु पुनः पूषा पथ्यां या स्वस्तिः ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ásum ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dadātu ǀ púnaḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀpúnaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ dadātu ǀ púnaríti ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ pathyā́m ǀ yā́ ǀ svastíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Earth restore to us our vital spirit, may Heaven the Goddess and mid-air restore it. May Soma give us once again our body, and Pūṣan show the Path of peace and comfort.
verses.wilson_translation: May earth restore the (departed)soulto us; may the divine heaven, may the firmament (restore it);may Somarestore body to us; may Pūṣanrestore to us speech, which is prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: May Earth restore to us our vital spirit, may Heaven the Goddess and mid-air restore it. May Soma give us once again our body, and Pūṣan show the Path of peace and comfort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शं रोदसी सुबंधवे यह्वी ऋतस्य मातरा ।भरतामप यद्रपो द्यौः पृथिवि क्षमा रपो मो षु ते किं चनाममत् ॥
verses.transliteration: śám ǀ ródasī íti ǀ su-bándhave ǀ yahvī́ íti ǀ ṛtásya ǀ mātárā ǀbháratām ǀ ápa ǀ yát ǀ rápaḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ pṛthivi ǀ kṣamā́ ǀ rápaḥ ǀ mó íti ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ āmamat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May both Worlds bless Subandhu, young Mothers of everlasting Law. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.wilson_translation: May the great heaven and earth, the parents of sacrifice, (grant) happiness to Subandhu; heaven andearth, remove all iniquity; let heaven (take away) iniquity; may no ill ever approach you.
verses.griffith_verse: May both Worlds bless Subandhu, young Mothers of everlasting Law. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव द्वके अव त्रिका दिवश्चरंति भेषजा ।क्षमा चरिष्ण्वेककं भरतामप यद्रपो द्यौः पृथिवि क्षमा रपो मो षु ते किं चनाममत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ dvaké íti ǀ áva ǀ trikā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ caranti ǀ bheṣajā́ ǀkṣamā́ ǀ cariṣṇú ǀ ekakám ǀ bháratām ǀ ápa ǀ yát ǀ rápaḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ pṛthivi ǀ kṣamā́ ǀ rápaḥ ǀ mó íti ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ āmamat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Health-giving medicines descend sent down from heaven in twos and threes, Or wandering singly on the earth. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Remedies come down from heaven by two and threes; one wanders singly in heaven; heaven andearth remove all iniquity; let heaven (take away) iniquity; may no ill ever approach you.
verses.griffith_verse: Health-giving medicines descend sent down from heaven in twos and threes, Or wandering singly on the earth. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समिंद्रेरय गामनड्वाहं य आवहदुशीनराण्या अनः ।भरतामप यद्रपो द्यौः पृथिवि क्षमा रपो मो षु ते किं चनाममत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ indra ǀ īraya ǀ gā́m ǀ anaḍvā́ham ǀ yáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ávahat ǀ uśīnárāṇyāḥ ǀ ánaḥ ǀbháratām ǀ ápa ǀ yát ǀ rápaḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ pṛthivi ǀ kṣamā́ ǀ rápaḥ ǀ mó íti ǀ sú ǀ te ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ āmamat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drive forward thou the wagon-ox, O Indra, which brought Usinarani's wagon hither. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Send,Indra, the active ox, who may bring the cart (laden with) the uśīnarāṇi grass; heaven andearth, remove all iniquity; let heaven (take away) iniquity; may no ill ever approach you.
verses.griffith_verse: Drive forward thou the wagon-ox, O Indra, which brought Usinarani's wagon hither. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LX. Asamati and Others.-
hymns.anukramani: १२ बन्धु: श्रुतबन्धुर्विप्रबन्धुर्गौपायनाः,६ अगस्त्यस्वसा एषां माता ऋषिका। १-४,६ असमातिः, ५ इन्द्रः,७-११ जीवः,१२ हस्तः।अनुष्टुप्,१-५ गायत्री, ८-९ पंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BRINGING our homage we have come to one magnificent in look.Glorified of the mighty Gods To Asamati, spring of gifts, lord of the brave, a radiant car,The conqueror of Bhajeratha Who, when the spear hath armed his hand, or even weaponless o’erthrowsMen strong as buffaloes in fight; Him in whose service flourishes Iksvaku, rich and dazzling-bright.As the Five Tribes that are in heaven. Indra, support the princely power of Rathaprosthas matched by none,Even as the Sun for all to see. Thou for Agastya's sister's sons yokest thy pair of ruddy steeds.Thou troddest niggards under foot, all those, O King, who brought no gifts. This is the mother, this the sire, this one hath come to be thy life.What brings thee forth is even this. Now come, Subandhu, get thee forth. As with the leather thong they bind the chariot yoke to hold it fast,So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security. Even as this earth, the mighty earth, holds fast the monarchs of the wood.So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security. Subandlin's spirit I have brought from Yarna, from Vivasvān's Son,Brought it for life and not for death, yea, brought it for security. The wind blows downward from on high, downward the Sun-God sends his heat,Downward the milch-cow pours her milk: so downward go thy pain and grief. Felicitous is this mine hand, yet more felicitous is this.This hand contains all healing balms, and this makes whole with gentle touch.

verses.sanskrit: आ जनं त्वेषसंदृशं माहीनानामुपस्तुतं ।अगन्म बिभ्रतो नमः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ jánam ǀ tveṣá-sandṛśam ǀ mā́hīnānām ǀ úpa-stutam ǀáganma ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ námaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BRINGING our homage we have come to one magnificent in look. Glorified of the mighty Gods
verses.wilson_translation: We have come to the person n of splendid appearance, the honoured of the mighty, bringing himreverential homage.
verses.griffith_verse: BRINGING our homage we have come to one magnificent in look. Glorified of the mighty Gods
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असमातिं नितोशनं त्वेषं निययिनं रथं ।भजेरथस्य सत्पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ásamātim ǀ ni-tóśanam ǀ tveṣám ǀ ni-yayínam ǀ rátham ǀbhajé-rathasya ǀ sát-patim ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Asamati, spring of gifts, lord of the brave, a radiant car, The conqueror of Bhajeratha
verses.wilson_translation: To Asamāti, the destroyer (of foes), radiant, a quick-moving chariot, (for the bringing of benefits),(the descendant) of Bhajeratha, the protector of the good.
verses.griffith_verse: To Asamati, spring of gifts, lord of the brave, a radiant car, The conqueror of Bhajeratha
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो जनान्महिषाँ इवातितस्थौ पवीरवान् ।उतापवीरवान्युधा ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ jánān ǀ mahiṣā́n-iva ǀ ati-tastháu ǀ pávīravān ǀutá ǀ ápavīravān ǀ yudhā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who, when the spear hath armed his hand, or even weaponless o’erthrows Men strong as buffaloes in fight;
verses.wilson_translation: Who, whether armed or unarmed with a sword, overcomes adversaries in fight, as (a lion destroys)buffaloes.
verses.griffith_verse: Who, when the spear hath armed his hand, or even weaponless o’erthrows Men strong as buffaloes in fight;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्येक्ष्वाकुरुप व्रते रेवान्मराय्येधते ।दिवीव पंच कृष्टयः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ ikṣvākúḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vraté ǀ revā́n ǀ marāyī́ ǀ édhate ǀdiví-iva ǀ páñca ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him in whose service flourishes Iksvaku, rich and dazzling-bright. As the Five Tribes that are in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: In the good government of whose (realm) the opunlent and victorious Ikṣvākuprospers (so that) thefive orders of men (are as happy) as if they were in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Him in whose service flourishes Iksvaku, rich and dazzling-bright. As the Five Tribes that are in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र क्षत्रासमातिषु रथप्रोष्ठेषु धारय ।दिवीव सूर्यं दृशे ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ kṣatrā́ ǀ ásamātiṣu ǀ rátha-proṣṭheṣu ǀ dhāraya ǀdiví-iva ǀ sū́ryam ǀ dṛśé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, support the princely power of Rathaprosthas matched by none, Even as the Sun for all to see.
verses.wilson_translation: Maintain,Indra, vigour in the Rathaproṣṭha Asamātis, as (you maintain) the sun in heaven for thesight (of all).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, support the princely power of Rathaprosthas matched by none, Even as the Sun for all to see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अगस्त्यस्य नद्भ्यः सप्ती युनक्षि रोहिता ।पणीन्न्यक्रमीरभि विश्वान्राजन्नराधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: agástyasya ǀ nát-bhyaḥ ǀ sáptī íti ǀ yunakṣi ǀ róhitā ǀpaṇī́n ǀ ní ǀ akramīḥ ǀ abhí ǀ víśvān ǀ rājan ǀ arādhásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou for Agastya's sister's sons yokest thy pair of ruddy steeds. Thou troddest niggards under foot, all those, O King, who brought no gifts.
verses.wilson_translation: Yoke the two red horses to your chariot, for the nephews of Agastya, and overcome,rājā, all theniggard withholders of oblations.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou for Agastya's sister's sons yokest thy pair of ruddy steeds. Thou troddest niggards under foot, all those, O King, who brought no gifts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं मातायं पितायं जीवातुरागमत् ।इदं तव प्रसर्पणं सुबंधवेहि निरिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ mātā́ ǀ ayám ǀ pitā́ ǀ ayám ǀ jīvā́tuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agamat ǀidám ǀ táva ǀ pra-sárpaṇam ǀ súbandho íti sú-bandho ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ níḥ ǀ ihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the mother, this the sire, this one hath come to be thy life. What brings thee forth is even this. Now come, Subandhu, get thee forth.
verses.wilson_translation: This (Agni) your mother, this your father, this the giver of life to you, has arrived; come back,Subandhu, to this your (body) that is capable of motion. Come forth.
verses.griffith_verse: This is the mother, this the sire, this one hath come to be thy life. What brings thee forth is even this. Now come, Subandhu, get thee forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा युगं वरत्रया नह्यंति धरुणाय कं ।एवा दाधार ते मनो जीवातवे न मृत्यवेऽथो अरिष्टतातये ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ yugám ǀ varatráyā ǀ náhyanti ǀ dharúṇāya ǀ kám ǀevá ǀ dādhāra ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jīvā́tave ǀ ná ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ átho íti ǀ ariṣṭá-tātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: As with the leather thong they bind the chariot yoke to hold it fast, So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.
verses.griffith_verse: As with the leather thong they bind the chariot yoke to hold it fast, So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथेयं पृथिवी मही दाधारेमान्वनस्पतीन् ।एवा दाधार ते मनो जीवातवे न मृत्यवेऽथो अरिष्टतातये ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ iyám ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ mahī́ ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ imā́n ǀ vánaspátīn ǀevá ǀ dādhāra ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ jīvā́tave ǀ ná ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ átho íti ǀ ariṣṭá-tātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even as this earth, the mighty earth, holds fast the monarchs of the wood. So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.
verses.griffith_verse: Even as this earth, the mighty earth, holds fast the monarchs of the wood. So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमादहं वैवस्वतात्सुबंधोर्मन आभरं ।जीवातवे न मृत्यवेऽथो अरिष्टतातये ॥
verses.transliteration: yamā́t ǀ ahám ǀ vaivasvatā́t ǀ su-bándhoḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ abharam ǀjīvā́tave ǀ ná ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ átho íti ǀ ariṣṭá-tātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Subandlin's spirit I have brought from Yarna, from Vivasvān's Son, Brought it for life and not for death, yea, brought it for security.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agnispeaks). I bring the spirit of ASubandhu from Yama, the son of Vivasvat, for life, not for death,but for security.
verses.griffith_verse: Subandlin's spirit I have brought from Yarna, from Vivasvān's Son, Brought it for life and not for death, yea, brought it for security.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न्यग्वातोऽव वाति न्यक्तपति सूर्यः ।नीचीनमघ्न्या दुहे न्यग्भवतु ते रपः ॥
verses.transliteration: nyák ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ áva ǀ vāti ǀ nyák ǀ tapati ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀnīcī́nam ǀ aghnyā́ ǀ duhe ǀ nyák ǀ bhavatu ǀ te ǀ rápaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wind blows downward from on high, downward the Sun-God sends his heat, Downward the milch-cow pours her milk: so downward go thy pain and grief.
verses.wilson_translation: The wind blows downwards, the sun burns downwards, the cow yields her milk downwards, so be(hand) has all medicaments; this has a blessed touch.
verses.griffith_verse: The wind blows downward from on high, downward the Sun-God sends his heat, Downward the milch-cow pours her milk: so downward go thy pain and grief.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं मे हस्तो भगवानयं मे भगवत्तरः ।अयं मे विश्वभेषजोऽयं शिवाभिमर्शनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ me ǀ hástaḥ ǀ bhága-vān ǀ ayám ǀ me ǀ bhágavat-taraḥ ǀayám ǀ me ǀ viśvá-bheṣajaḥ ǀ ayám ǀ śivá-abhimarśanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Felicitous is this mine hand, yet more felicitous is this. This hand contains all healing balms, and this makes whole with gentle touch.
verses.griffith_verse: Felicitous is this mine hand, yet more felicitous is this. This hand contains all healing balms, and this makes whole with gentle touch.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE welcome speaker in the storm of battle uttered with might this prayer to win the Aśvins,When the most liberal God, for Paktha, rescued his parents, and assailed the seven Hotras. Cyavāna, purposing deceptive presents, with all ingredients, made the altar ready.Most sweet-voiced Tūrvayāṇa poured oblations like floods of widely fertilizing water. To his oblations, swift as thought, ye hurried, and welcomed eagerly the prayers he offered.With arrows in his hand the Very Mighty forced from him all obedience of a servant. I call on you the Sons of Dyaus, the Aśvins, that a dark cow to my red kine be added.Enjoy my sacrifice, come to my viands contented, not deceiving expectation. ' Membrum suum virile, quod vrotentum fuerat, mas ille retraxit. Rursus illud quod in juvenem filiam sublatum fuerat, non aggressurus, ad se rerahit. Quum jam in medio connessu, semiperfecto opere, amorem in puellam pater impleverat, ambo discedentes seminis paulum in terrae superficiem sacrorum sede effusum emiserunt. Quum pater suam nilam adiverat, cum eā congressus suum semen supravirameffudit. Tum Dii benigni precem (brahma)progenuerunt, et Vastoshpatim, legum sacrarum custodem, formaverunt. Ille tauro similis spumam in certamine jactavit, tunc discedens pusillaximis huc profectus est. Quasi dextro pede claudus processit, "inutiles fuerunt illi mei complexus," ita locutus. 'The fire, burning the people, does not approach quickly (by day): the naked (Rākṣasasapproach) not Agni by night; the giver of fuel, and the giver of food, he, the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcoming enemies by his might.' Uttering praise to suit the rite Navagvas came speedily to win the damsel's friendship.They who approached the twice-strong stable's keeper, meedless would milk the rocks that naught had shaken. Swift was new friendship with the maid they quickly accepted it as genuine seed and bounty.Milk which the cow Sabardughā had yielded was the bright heritage which to thee they offered. When afterwards they woke and missed the cattle, the speaker thus in joyful mood addressed them:Matchless are singers through the Vasu's nature; he bringeth them all food and all possessions. His followers then who dwelt in sundry places came and desired too slay the son of Nṛṣad.Resistless foe, be found the hidden treasure of Śuṣṇa multiplied in numerous offspring. Thou, called Effulgence, in whose threefold dwelling, as in the light of heaven, the Gods are sitting,Thou who art called Agni or Jātavedas, Priest, hear us, guileless Priest of holy worship. And, Indra, bring, that I may laud and serve them, those Two resplendent glorious Nāsatyas,Blithe, bounteous, man-like, to the sacrificer, honoured among our men with offered viands. This King is praised and honoured as Ordainer: himself the bridge, the Sage speeds o’er the waters.He hath stirred up Kakṣīvān, stirred up Agni, as the steed's swift wheel drives the felly onward. Vaitarana, doubly kinsman, sacrificer, shall milk the cow who ne’er hath calved, Sabardhu,When I encompass Varuṇa and Mitra with lauds, and Aryaman in safest shelter. Their kin, the Prince in heaven, thy nearest kinsman, turning his thought to thee thus speaks in kindness:This is our highest bond: I am his offspring. How many others came ere I succeeded? Here is my kinship, here the place I dwell in: these are my Gods; I in full strength am present.Twice-born am I, the first-born Son of Order: the Cow milked this when first she had her being. So mid these tribes he rests, the friendly envoy, borne on two paths, refulgent Lord of fuel.When, like a line, the Babe springs up erectly, his Mother straight hath borne him strong to bless us. Then went the milch-kine forth to please the damsel, and for the good of every man that liveth.Hear us, O wealthy Lord; begin our worship. Thou hast grown mighty through Āśvaghna's virtues. And take thou notice of us also, Indra, for ample riches, King whose arm wields thunder!Protect our wealthy nobles, guard our princes unmenaced near thee, Lord of Tawny Coursers. When he goes forth, ye Pair of Kings, for booty, speeding to war and praise to please the singer,—I was the dearest sage of those about him,—let him lead these away and bring them safely. Now for this noble man's support and comfort, singing with easy voice we thus implore thee:Impetuous be his son and fleet his courser: and may I be his priest to win him glory. If, for our strength, the priest with adoration to win your friendship made the laud accepted,That laud shall be a branching road to virtue for every one to whom the songs are suited. Glorified thus, with holy hymns and homage:—Of noble race, with Waters, God-attended—May he enrich us for our prayers and praises: now can the cow be milked; the path is open. Be to us, then, ye Gods who merit worship, be ye of one accord our strong protection,Who went on various ways and brought us vigour, ye who are undeceivable explorers.

verses.sanskrit: इदमित्था रौद्रं गूर्तवचा ब्रह्म क्रत्वा शच्यामंतराजौ ।क्राणा यदस्य पितरा मंहनेष्ठाः पर्षत्पक्थे अहन्ना सप्त होतॄन् ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ itthā́ ǀ ráudram ǀ gūrtá-vacāḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ krátvā ǀ śácyām ǀ antáḥ ǀ ājáu ǀkrāṇā́ ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ pitárā ǀ maṃhane-sthā́ḥ ǀ párṣat ǀ pakthé ǀ áhan ǀ ā́ ǀ saptá ǀ hótṝn ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE welcome speaker in the storm of battle uttered with might this prayer to win the Aśvins, When the most liberal God, for Paktha, rescued his parents, and assailed the seven Hotras.
verses.wilson_translation: The fierce-voiced (Nābhānediṣṭha repeated) through his intelligence this praise of Rudra, in themidst of the ceremony at the assembly (of the Aṅgirasas), which (praise) his parents, making (the partition) andhis brothers engaged in giving (the shares accomplished); he perfected the seven priests (therewith) on the dayon which the rite was to be matured.
verses.griffith_verse: THE welcome speaker in the storm of battle uttered with might this prayer to win the Aśvins, When the most liberal God, for Paktha, rescued his parents, and assailed the seven Hotras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इद्दानाय दभ्याय वन्वंच्यवानः सूदैरमिमीत वेदिं ।तूर्वयाणो गूर्तवचस्तमः क्षोदो न रेत इतऊति सिंचत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ dānā́ya ǀ dábhyāya ǀ vanván ǀ cyávānaḥ ǀ sū́daiḥ ǀ amimīta ǀ védim ǀtū́rvayāṇaḥ ǀ gūrtávacaḥ-tamaḥ ǀ kṣódaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rétaḥ ǀ itáḥ-ūti ǀ siñcat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cyavāna, purposing deceptive presents, with all ingredients, made the altar ready. Most sweet-voiced Tūrvayāṇa poured oblations like floods of widely fertilizing water.
verses.wilson_translation: He (Rudra) bestowing on his worshippers the gift (of wealth) and the defeat (of their foes),castingdown (therākṣasas) with his weapons, has constructed the altar; rapid in movement, most fierce in speech,and shedding the procreative fluid like water around.
verses.griffith_verse: Cyavāna, purposing deceptive presents, with all ingredients, made the altar ready. Most sweet-voiced Tūrvayāṇa poured oblations like floods of widely fertilizing water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मनो न येषु हवनेषु तिग्मं विपः शच्या वनुथो द्रवंता ।आ यः शर्याभिस्तुविनृम्णो अस्याश्रीणीतादिशं गभस्तौ ॥
verses.transliteration: mánaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yéṣu ǀ hávaneṣu ǀ tigmám ǀ vípaḥ ǀ śácyā ǀ vanutháḥ ǀ drávantā ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ śáryābhiḥ ǀ tuvi-nṛmṇáḥ ǀ asya ǀ áśrīṇīta ǀ ā-díśam ǀ gábhastau ǁ
verses.english_translation: To his oblations, swift as thought, ye hurried, and welcomed eagerly the prayers he offered. With arrows in his hand the Very Mighty forced from him all obedience of a servant.
verses.wilson_translation: (I call you to these) oblations, to which hastening, (Aśvins), swift as thought at the invitation of theworshipper, you rejoice my (worshipper) who, affluent in the wealth of sacrifice, mixes (the oblation) with hisfingers in your presence, (holding) in hishandthe sacrifice intended (for you).
verses.griffith_verse: To his oblations, swift as thought, ye hurried, and welcomed eagerly the prayers he offered. With arrows in his hand the Very Mighty forced from him all obedience of a servant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णा यद्गोष्वरुणीषु सीदद्दिवो नपाताश्विना हुवे वां ।वीतं मे यज्ञमा गतं मे अन्नं ववन्वांसा नेषमस्मृतध्रू ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇā́ ǀ yát ǀ góṣu ǀ aruṇī́ṣu ǀ sī́dat ǀ diváḥ ǀ nápātā ǀ aśvinā ǀ huve ǀ vām ǀvītám ǀ me ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ gatam ǀ me ǀ ánnam ǀ vavanvā́ṃsā ǀ ná ǀ íṣam ǀ ásmṛtadhrū ítyasmṛta-dhrū ǁ
verses.english_translation: I call on you the Sons of Dyaus, the Aśvins, that a dark cow to my red kine be added. Enjoy my sacrifice, come to my viands contented, not deceiving expectation. '
verses.wilson_translation: When the dark night rettires before the purple oxen (of the chariot of the dawn), I invoke you,Aśvinschildren of heaven; be desirous of my sacrifice; come to my food and to my viands like (two horses) eatingtogether, oblivious of offence.
verses.griffith_verse: I call on you the Sons of Dyaus, the Aśvins, that a dark cow to my red kine be added. Enjoy my sacrifice, come to my viands contented, not deceiving expectation. '
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रथिष्ट यस्य वीरकर्ममिष्णदनुष्ठितं नु नर्यो अपौहत् ।पुनस्तदा वृहति यत्कनाया दुहितुरा अनुभृतमनर्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: práthiṣṭa ǀ yásya ǀ vīrá-karmam ǀ iṣṇát ǀ ánu-sthitam ǀ nú ǀ náryaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ auhat ǀpúnaríti ǀ tát ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛhati ǀ yát ǀ kanā́yāḥ ǀ duhitúḥ ǀ ā́ḥ ǀ ánu-bhṛtam ǀ anarvā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Membrum suum virile, quod vrotentum fuerat, mas ille retraxit. Rursus illud quod in juvenem filiam sublatum fuerat, non aggressurus, ad se rerahit.
verses.wilson_translation: (Rudra), the benefactor of man, whose eager, virile energy was developed, drew it back whendisseminated (for the genitive ration of offfspring); again the irresistible (Rudra) concentrates (the energy) which wascommunicated to his maiden daughter.
verses.griffith_verse: Membrum suum virile, quod vrotentum fuerat, mas ille retraxit. Rursus illud quod in juvenem filiam sublatum fuerat, non aggressurus, ad se rerahit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मध्या यत्कर्त्वमभवदभीके कामं कृण्वाने पितरि युवत्यां ।मनानग्रेतो जहतुर्वियंता सानौ निषिक्तं सुकृतस्य योनौ ॥
verses.transliteration: madhyā́ ǀ yát ǀ kártvam ǀ ábhavat ǀ abhī́ke ǀ kā́mam ǀ kṛṇvāné ǀ pitári ǀ yuvatyā́m ǀmanānák ǀ rétaḥ ǀ jahatuḥ ǀ vi-yántā ǀ sā́nau ǀ ní-siktam ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ yónau ǁ
verses.english_translation: Quum jam in medio connessu, semiperfecto opere, amorem in puellam pater impleverat, ambo discedentes seminis paulum in terrae superficiem sacrorum sede effusum emiserunt.
verses.wilson_translation: When the deed was done in mid-heaven in the proximity of the father working his will, and thedaughter coming together, they let the seed fall slightly; it was poured upon the high plural ce of sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Quum jam in medio connessu, semiperfecto opere, amorem in puellam pater impleverat, ambo discedentes seminis paulum in terrae superficiem sacrorum sede effusum emiserunt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पिता यत्स्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन्क्ष्मया रेतः संजग्मानो नि षिंचत् ।स्वाध्योऽजनयन्ब्रह्म देवा वास्तोष्पतिं व्रतपां निरतक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: pitā́ ǀ yát ǀ svā́m ǀ duhitáram ǀ adhi-skán ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ rétaḥ ǀ sam-jagmānáḥ ǀ ní ǀ siñcat ǀsu-ādhyáḥ ǀ ajanayan ǀ bráhma ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vā́stoḥ ǀ pátim ǀ vrata-pā́m ǀ níḥ ǀ atakṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Quum pater suam nilam adiverat, cum eā congressus suum semen supra viram effudit. Tum Dii benigni precem (brahma) progenuerunt , et Vastoshpatim, legum sacrarum custodem, formaverunt.
verses.wilson_translation: When the father united with the daughter, then associating with the earth, he sprinkled it with theeffusion; then the thoughtful gods begot Brahma; they fabricated the lord of the hearth (of sacrifice); the defenderof sacred rites.
verses.griffith_verse: Quum pater suam nilam adiverat, cum eā congressus suum semen supra viram effudit. Tum Dii benigni precem (brahma) progenuerunt , et Vastoshpatim, legum sacrarum custodem, formaverunt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स ईं वृषा न फेनमस्यदाजौ स्मदा परैदप दभ्रचेताः ।सरत्पदा न दक्षिणा परावृङ्न ता नु मे पृशन्यो जगृभ्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ná ǀ phénam ǀ asyat ǀ ājáu ǀ smát ǀ ā́ ǀ párā ǀ ait ǀ ápa ǀ dabhrá-cetāḥ ǀsárat ǀ padā́ ǀ ná ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ parā-vṛ́k ǀ ná ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ nú ǀ me ǀ pṛśanyáḥ ǀ jagṛbhre ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ille tauro similis spumam in certamine jactavit, tunc discedens pusillaximis huc profectus est. Quasi dextro pede claudus processit, "inutiles fuerunt illi mei complexus," ita locutus.
verses.wilson_translation: He, like the showerer (Indra), cast foam around in the combat, and came away from us with a niggardmind; he advances not a step, relinquishing the donations; though skilled in rapine, he seizes not these my(cows).
verses.griffith_verse: Ille tauro similis spumam in certamine jactavit, tunc discedens pusillaximis huc profectus est. Quasi dextro pede claudus processit, "inutiles fuerunt illi mei complexus," ita locutus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मक्षू न वह्निः प्रजाया उपब्दिरग्निं न नग्न उप सीददूधः ।सनितेध्मं सनितोत वाजं स धर्ता जज्ञे सहसा यवीयुत् ॥
verses.transliteration: makṣú ǀ ná ǀ váhniḥ ǀ pra-jā́yāḥ ǀ upabdíḥ ǀ agním ǀ ná ǀ nagnáḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sīdat ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀsánitā ǀ idhmám ǀ sánitā ǀ utá ǀ vā́jam ǀ sáḥ ǀ dhartā́ ǀ jajñe ǀ sáhasā ǀ yavi-yút ǁ
verses.english_translation: 'The fire, burning the people, does not approach quickly (by day): the naked ( Rākṣasas approach) not Agni by night; the giver of fuel, and the giver of food, he, the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcoming enemies by his might.'
verses.wilson_translation: The fire, harming the people, does not approach quickly (by day); the naked (rākṣasasapproach)not Agniby night; the giver of fuel, and the giver of food, he, the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcomingenemies by his might.
verses.griffith_verse: 'The fire, burning the people, does not approach quickly (by day): the naked ( Rākṣasas approach) not Agni by night; the giver of fuel, and the giver of food, he, the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcoming enemies by his might.'
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मक्षू कनायाः सख्यं नवग्वा ऋतं वदंत ऋतयुक्तिमग्मन् ।द्विबर्हसो य उप गोपमागुरदक्षिणासो अच्युता दुदुक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: makṣú ǀ kanā́yāḥ ǀ sakhyám ǀ náva-gvāḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ vádantaḥ ǀ ṛtá-yuktim ǀ agman ǀdvi-bárhasaḥ ǀ yé ǀ úpa ǀ gopám ǀ ā́ ǀ águḥ ǀ adakṣiṇā́saḥ ǀ ácyutā ǀ dudhukṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uttering praise to suit the rite Navagvas came speedily to win the damsel's friendship. They who approached the twice-strong stable's keeper, meedless would milk the rocks that naught had shaken.
verses.wilson_translation: The Aṅgirasas, who were engaged in the nine months;' ceremonial, reciting the praise suited to therite, quickly attained the friendship of the maiden; those who seated in the two seats (heaven and earth) came totheir protector, as they had no donation, milked forth the inexhaustible (waters).
verses.griffith_verse: Uttering praise to suit the rite Navagvas came speedily to win the damsel's friendship. They who approached the twice-strong stable's keeper, meedless would milk the rocks that naught had shaken.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मक्षू कनायाः सख्यं नवीयो राधो न रेत ऋतमित्तुरण्यन् ।शुचि यत्ते रेक्ण आयजंत सबर्दुघायाः पय उस्रियायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: makṣú ǀ kanā́yāḥ ǀ sakhyám ǀ návīyaḥ ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rétaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ ít ǀ turaṇyan ǀśúci ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ ā-áyajanta ǀ sabaḥ-dúghāyāḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ usríyāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Swift was new friendship with the maid they quickly accepted it as genuine seed and bounty. Milk which the cow Sabardughā had yielded was the bright heritage which to thee they offered.
verses.wilson_translation: Quickly (obtaining) the friendship of the maiden, they poured forth water like new wealth, when theyoffered to you (Indra) the pure riches, the milk of the cow, that yields ambrosia.
verses.griffith_verse: Swift was new friendship with the maid they quickly accepted it as genuine seed and bounty. Milk which the cow Sabardughā had yielded was the bright heritage which to thee they offered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पश्वा यत्पश्चा वियुता बुधंतेति ब्रवीति वक्तरी रराणः ।वसोर्वसुत्वा कारवोऽनेहा विश्वं विवेष्टि द्रविणमुप क्षु ॥
verses.transliteration: paśvā́ ǀ yát ǀ paścā́ ǀ ví-yutā ǀ budhánta ǀ íti ǀ bravīti ǀ vaktári ǀ rárāṇaḥ ǀvásoḥ ǀ vasu-tvā́ ǀ kārávaḥ ǀ anehā́ ǀ víśvam ǀ viveṣṭi ǀ dráviṇam ǀ úpa ǀ kṣú ǁ
verses.english_translation: When afterwards they woke and missed the cattle, the speaker thus in joyful mood addressed them: Matchless are singers through the Vasu's nature; he bringeth them all food and all possessions.
verses.wilson_translation: "When (the worshippers) find (the stalls deserted) by the cattle" (then the performer of the rite)exclaims, "(Indra), plural asing to his adorer, the affluent lord of affluence, the compassionate, the sinless, quicklyrecovers all the wealth (that has been carried off)."
verses.griffith_verse: When afterwards they woke and missed the cattle, the speaker thus in joyful mood addressed them: Matchless are singers through the Vasu's nature; he bringeth them all food and all possessions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिन्न्वस्य परिषद्वानो अग्मन्पुरू सदंतो नार्षदं बिभित्सन् ।वि शुष्णस्य संग्रथितमनर्वा विदत्पुरुप्रजातस्य गुहा यत् ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ pari-sádvānaḥ ǀ agman ǀ purú ǀ sádantaḥ ǀ nārsadám ǀ bibhitsán ǀví ǀ śúṣṇasya ǀ sám-grathitam ǀ anarvā́ ǀ vidát ǀ puru-prajātásya ǀ gúhā ǀ yát ǁ
verses.english_translation: His followers then who dwelt in sundry places came and desired too slay the son of Nṛṣad. Resistless foe, be found the hidden treasure of Śuṣṇa multiplied in numerous offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Then the attendant (rays of light) quickly gathered round him, and (theasuras) dwelling in manyregions sought to destroy the son of Nṛṣad, but the irresistible (Indra) found the well-knit mail ofŚuṣṇa, whoseoffspring was numerous, which was hidden in the cave.
verses.griffith_verse: His followers then who dwelt in sundry places came and desired too slay the son of Nṛṣad. Resistless foe, be found the hidden treasure of Śuṣṇa multiplied in numerous offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भर्गो ह नामोत यस्य देवाः स्वर्ण ये त्रिषधस्थे निषेदुः ।अग्निर्ह नामोत जातवेदाः श्रुधी नो होतर्ऋतस्य होताध्रुक् ॥
verses.transliteration: bhárgaḥ ǀ ha ǀ nā́ma ǀ utá ǀ yásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ tri-sadhasthé ǀ ni-sedúḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ ha ǀ nā́ma ǀ utá ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀ śrudhí ǀ naḥ ǀ hotaḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ hótā ǀ adhrúk ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, called Effulgence, in whose threefold dwelling, as in the light of heaven, the Gods are sitting, Thou who art called Agni or Jātavedas, Priest, hear us, guileless Priest of holy worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Whether Bhargais the name of that radiance, on the triple seat of which those who are gods areseated, as if in heaven, or whether it be Agni, or Jātavedas; invoker (of the gods), who are the ministrant priestof the sacrifice, hear our guileless invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, called Effulgence, in whose threefold dwelling, as in the light of heaven, the Gods are sitting, Thou who art called Agni or Jātavedas, Priest, hear us, guileless Priest of holy worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्या मे रौद्रावर्चिमंता नासत्याविंद्र गूर्तये यजध्यै ।मनुष्वद्वृक्तबर्हिषे रराणा मंदू हितप्रयसा विक्षु यज्यू ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tyā́ ǀ me ǀ ráudrau ǀ arci-mántā ǀ nā́satyau ǀ indra ǀ gūrtáye ǀ yájadhyai ǀmanuṣvát ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣe ǀ rárāṇā ǀ mandū́ íti ǀ hitá-prayasā ǀ vikṣú ǀ yájyū íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: And, Indra, bring, that I may laud and serve them, those Two resplendent glorious Nāsatyas, Blithe, bounteous, man-like, to the sacrificer, honoured among our men with offered viands.
verses.wilson_translation: And,Indra, let those two brilliant sons of Rudra, the Nāsatyās, (be present) at my praise andsacrifice; being propitious to (me seated) on the strewn grass, as (at the sacrifice of)Manu, cheerful, liberal ofwealth to the people, deserving of adoration.
verses.griffith_verse: And, Indra, bring, that I may laud and serve them, those Two resplendent glorious Nāsatyas, Blithe, bounteous, man-like, to the sacrificer, honoured among our men with offered viands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं स्तुतो राजा वंदि वेधा अपश्च विप्रस्तरति स्वसेतुः ।स कक्षीवंतं रेजयत्सो अग्निं नेमिं न चक्रमर्वतो रघुद्रु ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ stutáḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ vandi ǀ vedhā́ḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ ca ǀ vípraḥ ǀ tarati ǀ svá-setuḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ kakṣī́vantam ǀ rejayat ǀ sáḥ ǀ agním ǀ nemím ǀ ná ǀ cakrám ǀ árvataḥ ǀ raghu-drú ǁ
verses.english_translation: This King is praised and honoured as Ordainer: himself the bridge, the Sage speeds o’er the waters. He hath stirred up Kakṣīvān, stirred up Agni, as the steed's swift wheel drives the felly onward.
verses.wilson_translation: This royal (Soma), this glorified creator, is praised (by all), and, like a sage, constituting his owncause-way, he traverses the firmament; he made Kakṣīvattremble, he (made)Agni(shake) as horses (agitate)the light- whirling, revolving-wheel (of a chariot).
verses.griffith_verse: This King is praised and honoured as Ordainer: himself the bridge, the Sage speeds o’er the waters. He hath stirred up Kakṣīvān, stirred up Agni, as the steed's swift wheel drives the felly onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स द्विबंधुर्वैतरणो यष्टा सबर्धुं धेनुमस्वं दुहध्यै ।सं यन्मित्रावरुणा वृंज उक्थैर्ज्येष्ठेभिरर्यमणं वरूथैः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ dvi-bándhuḥ ǀ vaitaraṇáḥ ǀ yáṣṭā ǀ sabaḥ-dhúm ǀ dhenúm ǀ asvám ǀ duhádhyai ǀsám ǀ yát ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ vṛñjé ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ jyéṣṭhebhiḥ ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ várūthaiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vaitarana, doubly kinsman, sacrificer, shall milk the cow who ne’er hath calved, Sabardhu, When I encompass Varuṇa and Mitra with lauds, and Aryaman in safest shelter.
verses.wilson_translation: The kinsman of the two (worlds,Agni), the conveyer (of all), the sacrificer, (made) theambrosia-yielding cow, which had not given birth, to yield milk (forŚayu), when he praises Mitra,Varuṇaand Aryaman, with most excellent and choice hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: Vaitarana, doubly kinsman, sacrificer, shall milk the cow who ne’er hath calved, Sabardhu, When I encompass Varuṇa and Mitra with lauds, and Aryaman in safest shelter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्बंधुः सूरिर्दिवि ते धियंधा नाभानेदिष्ठो रपति प्र वेनन् ।सा नो नाभिः परमास्य वा घाहं तत्पश्चा कतिथश्चिदास ॥
verses.transliteration: tát-bandhuḥ ǀ sūríḥ ǀ diví ǀ te ǀ dhiyam-dhā́ḥ ǀ nā́bhānédiṣṭhaḥ ǀ rapati ǀ prá ǀ vénan ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ paramā́ ǀ asyá ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ ahám ǀ tát ǀ paścā́ ǀ katitháḥ ǀ cit ǀ āsa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Their kin, the Prince in heaven, thy nearest kinsman, turning his thought to thee thus speaks in kindness: This is our highest bond: I am his offspring. How many others came ere I succeeded?
verses.wilson_translation: The kinsman of the earth, the utterer of praise (belonging) to you (who abides) in heaven,Nābhānediṣṭha, the supporter of the rite, desiring (the recompense), repeats (this praise); the (heaven) ourmost excellent bound (is the site) of the (sun), and I was after many (degrees) descended from hiṃ
verses.griffith_verse: Their kin, the Prince in heaven, thy nearest kinsman, turning his thought to thee thus speaks in kindness: This is our highest bond: I am his offspring. How many others came ere I succeeded?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं मे नाभिरिह मे सधस्थमिमे मे देवा अयमस्मि सर्वः ।द्विजा अह प्रथमजा ऋतस्येदं धेनुरदुहज्जायमाना ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ me ǀ nā́bhiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ me ǀ sadhá-stham ǀ imé ǀ me ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ayám ǀ asmi ǀ sárvaḥ ǀdvi-jā́ḥ ǀ áha ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ idám ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ aduhat ǀ jā́yamānā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here is my kinship, here the place I dwell in: these are my Gods; I in full strength am present. Twice-born am I, the first-born Son of Order: the Cow milked this when first she had her being.
verses.wilson_translation: This (aerial voice) is my bond of affinity; here, (in the solar orb) is my abiding-plural ce; these are myresplendent (rays); I am this all; I am the twice-born; the first-born of truth; the cow, as soon as born, milked forthidentical withĀditya; sā yā vāg asau saādityaḥ, that which is vāk is that Ādityaḥ:Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa10.5.1.4]. the forests, terminates (in the fire of sacrifice), who upward rising, like a line, adorable, quickly subdues (hisfoes). him, unchangeable, the augmenter of happiness, his mother has brought forth.
verses.griffith_verse: Here is my kinship, here the place I dwell in: these are my Gods; I in full strength am present. Twice-born am I, the first-born Son of Order: the Cow milked this when first she had her being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधासु मंद्रो अरतिर्विभावाव स्यति द्विवर्तनिर्वनेषाट् ।ऊर्ध्वा यच्छ्रेणिर्न शिशुर्दन्मक्षू स्थिरं शेवृधं सूत माता ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ āsu ǀ mandráḥ ǀ aratíḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ áva ǀ syati ǀ dvi-vartaníḥ ǀ vaneṣā́ṭ ǀūrdhvā́ ǀ yát ǀ śréṇiḥ ǀ ná ǀ śíśuḥ ǀ dán ǀ makṣú ǀ sthirám ǀ śe-vṛdhám ǀ sūta ǀ mātā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So mid these tribes he rests, the friendly envoy, borne on two paths, refulgent Lord of fuel. When, like a line, the Babe springs up erectly, his Mother straight hath borne him strong to bless us.
verses.griffith_verse: So mid these tribes he rests, the friendly envoy, borne on two paths, refulgent Lord of fuel. When, like a line, the Babe springs up erectly, his Mother straight hath borne him strong to bless us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा गाव उपमातिं कनाया अनु श्वांतस्य कस्य चित्परेयुः ।श्रुधि त्वं सुद्रविणो नस्त्वं याळाश्वघ्नस्य वावृधे सूनृताभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ úpa-mātim ǀ kanā́yāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ śvāntásya ǀ kásya ǀ cit ǀ párā ǀ īyuḥ ǀśrudhí ǀ tvám ǀ su-draviṇaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ yāṭ ǀ āśva-ghnásya ǀ vavṛdhe ǀ sūnṛ́tābhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then went the milch-kine forth to please the damsel, and for the good of every man that liveth. Hear us, O wealthy Lord; begin our worship. Thou hast grown mighty through Āśvaghna's virtues.
verses.wilson_translation: The words of the desirable (praise), of a certain tranquil person n (Nābhānediṣṭha), attain theprototype (Indra). Do you, who are the giver of wealth (Agni), hear us; offer sacrifice, you are magnified by thesincere eulogies of Aśvaghna.
verses.griffith_verse: Then went the milch-kine forth to please the damsel, and for the good of every man that liveth. Hear us, O wealthy Lord; begin our worship. Thou hast grown mighty through Āśvaghna's virtues.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध त्वमिंद्र विद्ध्यस्मान्महो राये नृपते वज्रबाहुः ।रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीननेहसस्ते हरिवो अभिष्टौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ viddhí ǀ asmā́n ǀ maháḥ ǀ rāyé ǀ nṛ-pate ǀ vájra-bāhuḥ ǀrákṣa ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ maghónaḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ sūrī́n ǀ anehásaḥ ǀ te ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ abhíṣṭau ǁ
verses.english_translation: And take thou notice of us also, Indra, for ample riches, King whose arm wields thunder! Protect our wealthy nobles, guard our princes unmenaced near thee, Lord of Tawny Coursers.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, king of men, who are the bearer of the thunderbolt, regard us now to (give us) greatriches, and protect us who are affluent in (oblations), who utter (your) praise; may we, lord of bay steeds, (be)free from blame on your approach.
verses.griffith_verse: And take thou notice of us also, Indra, for ample riches, King whose arm wields thunder! Protect our wealthy nobles, guard our princes unmenaced near thee, Lord of Tawny Coursers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अध यद्राजाना गविष्टौ सरत्सरण्युः कारवे जरण्युः ।विप्रः प्रेष्ठः स ह्येषां बभूव परा च वक्षदुत पर्षदेनान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ yát ǀ rājānā ǀ gó-iṣṭau ǀ sárat ǀ saraṇyúḥ ǀ kāráve ǀ jaraṇyúḥ ǀvípraḥ ǀ préṣṭhaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ eṣām ǀ babhū́va ǀ párā ǀ ca ǀ vákṣat ǀ utá ǀ parṣat ǀ enān ǁ
verses.english_translation: When he goes forth, ye Pair of Kings, for booty, speeding to war and praise to please the singer,— I was the dearest sage of those about him,—let him lead these away and bring them safely.
verses.wilson_translation: Since, royal (Mitraand Varuṇa), the impetuous (Yama) now approaches in expectation of (the gift of)cattle, and desiring praise for the sacrificing (band of the Aṅgirasas); the sage (Nābhānediṣṭha) has beenheld most dear by them; may he accomplish (what has to be effected), and make them successful.
verses.griffith_verse: When he goes forth, ye Pair of Kings, for booty, speeding to war and praise to please the singer,— I was the dearest sage of those about him,—let him lead these away and bring them safely.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा न्वस्य जेन्यस्य पुष्टौ वृथा रेभंत ईमहे तदू नु ।सरण्युरस्य सूनुरश्वो विप्रश्चासि श्रवसश्च सातौ ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ jényasya ǀ puṣṭáu ǀ vṛ́thā ǀ rébhantaḥ ǀ īmahe ǀ tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀsaraṇyúḥ ǀ asya ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ vípraḥ ǀ ca ǀ asi ǀ śrávasaḥ ǀ ca ǀ sātáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now for this noble man's support and comfort, singing with easy voice we thus implore thee: Impetuous be his son and fleet his courser: and may I be his priest to win him glory.
verses.wilson_translation: And for the contentment of this victorious (Varuṇa), praising (him) without an effort, we solicit this (ofhim), (that) his progeny, a swift horse, (may be ours), and you, (Varuṇa), are wise, and (are occupied) inprocuring us food.
verses.griffith_verse: Now for this noble man's support and comfort, singing with easy voice we thus implore thee: Impetuous be his son and fleet his courser: and may I be his priest to win him glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवोर्यदि सख्यायास्मे शर्धाय स्तोमं जुजुषे नमस्वान् ।विश्वत्र यस्मिन्ना गिरः समीचीः पूर्वीव गातुर्दाशत्सूनृतायै ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ yádi ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ asmé íti ǀ śárdhāya ǀ stómam ǀ jujuṣé ǀ námasvān ǀviśvátra ǀ yásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ sam-īcī́ḥ ǀ pūrvī́-iva ǀ gātúḥ ǀ dā́śat ǀ sūnṛ́tāyai ǁ
verses.english_translation: If, for our strength, the priest with adoration to win your friendship made the laud accepted, That laud shall be a branching road to virtue for every one to whom the songs are suited.
verses.wilson_translation: If the priest offers homage to you two (Mitraand Varuṇa) for the sake of your friendship and ourinvigoration, on (the formation of) which (friendship) the praises (of the Aṅgirasasgo) everywhere in a commondirection; may he give (plural asure) to the utterer of praise like an ancient road.
verses.griffith_verse: If, for our strength, the priest with adoration to win your friendship made the laud accepted, That laud shall be a branching road to virtue for every one to whom the songs are suited.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स गृणानो अद्भिर्देववानिति सुबंधुर्नमसा सूक्तैः ।वर्धदुक्थैर्वचोभिरा हि नूनं व्यध्वैति पयस उस्रियायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ at-bhíḥ ǀ devá-vān ǀ íti ǀ su-bándhuḥ ǀ námasā ǀ su-uktáiḥ ǀvárdhat ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hí ǀ nūnám ǀ ví ǀ ádhvā ǀ eti ǀ páyasaḥ ǀ usríyāyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glorified thus, with holy hymns and homage:—Of noble race, with Waters, God-attended— May he enrich us for our prayers and praises: now can the cow be milked; the path is open.
verses.wilson_translation: Being praised with reverence and hymns thus, "the god-accompanied (Varuṇa) of good lineage,together with the waters"; may he be magnified; (attracted) by hymns and prayers (may he) now (approach); thepath of the milk of the cow is open (for his worship).
verses.griffith_verse: Glorified thus, with holy hymns and homage:—Of noble race, with Waters, God-attended— May he enrich us for our prayers and praises: now can the cow be milked; the path is open.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त ऊ षु णो महो यजत्रा भूत देवास ऊतये सजोषाः ।ये वाजाँ अनयता वियंतो ये स्था निचेतारो अमूराः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀ bhūtá ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀyé ǀ vā́jān ǀ ánayata ǀ vi-yántaḥ ǀ yé ǀ sthá ǀ ni-cetā́raḥ ǀ ámūrāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be to us, then, ye Gods who merit worship, be ye of one accord our strong protection, Who went on various ways and brought us vigour, ye who are undeceivable explorers.
verses.wilson_translation: Adorable divinities, be consentient for our great preservation, both you who, going in variousdirections, are the bringers of food, and you who, being no longer perplexed, are the discoverers (of the cattle).
verses.griffith_verse: Be to us, then, ye Gods who merit worship, be ye of one accord our strong protection, Who went on various ways and brought us vigour, ye who are undeceivable explorers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXII. Viśvedevas, Etc.
hymns.anukramani: ११ नाभानेदिष्ठो  मानवः। विश्वे देवाः, १-६ अंगिरसो वा, ८-११ सावर्णेदानम्। जगती, ५,८,९ अनुष्टुप् प्रगाथ: =(६ बृहती, ७ सतोबृहती ) १० गायत्री, ११ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE, who, adorned with guerdon through the sacrifice, have won you Indra's friendship and eternal life,Even to you be happiness, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise. The Fathers, who drave forth the wealth in cattle, have in the year's courses cleft Vala by Eternal Law:A lengthened life be yours, O ye Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise. Ye raised the Sun to heaven by everlasting Law, and spread broad earth, the Mother, out on every side.Fair wealth of progeny be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise. This kinsman in your dwellingplace speaks pleasant words: give car to this, ye Ṛṣis, children of the Gods.High Brahman dignity be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise. Distinguished by their varied form, these Ṛṣis have been deeply moved.These are the sons of Aṅgirases: from Agni have they sprung to life. Distinguished by their varied form, they sprang from Agni, from the sky.Navagva and Daśagva, noblest Aṅgiras, he giveth bounty with the Gods. With Indra for associate the priests have cleared the stable full of steeds and kine,Giving to me a thousand with their eightmarked cars, they gained renown among the Gods. May this man's sons be multiplied; like springing corn may Manu grow,Who gives at once in bounteous gift a thousand kine, a hundred steeds. No one attains to him, as though a man would grasp the heights of heaven.Savarnya's sacrificial meed hath broadened like an ample flood. Yadu and Turva, too, have given two Dāsas, well-disposed, to serve,Together with great store of kine. Blest be the hamlet's chief, most liberal Manu, and may his bounty rival that of Sūrya.May the God let Ssvarni's life be lengthened, with whom, unwearied, we have lived and prospered.

verses.sanskrit: ये यज्ञेन दक्षिणया समक्ता इंद्रस्य सख्यममृतत्वमानश ।तेभ्यो भद्रमंगिरसो वो अस्तु प्रति गृभ्णीत मानवं सुमेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ yajñéna ǀ dákṣiṇayā ǀ sám-aktāḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ sakhyám ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśá ǀtébhyaḥ ǀ bhadrám ǀ aṅgirasaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ astu ǀ práti ǀ gṛbhṇīta ǀ mānavám ǀ su-medhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: YE, who, adorned with guerdon through the sacrifice, have won you Indra's friendship and eternal life, Even to you be happiness, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.wilson_translation: You, who associated with sacrifice and pious donations, have acquired the friendship of Indraandimmortality; upon you,Aṅgirasas, may good fortune attend; welcome, sages, the son of Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: YE, who, adorned with guerdon through the sacrifice, have won you Indra's friendship and eternal life, Even to you be happiness, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य उदाजन्पितरो गोमयं वस्वृतेनाभिंदन्परिवत्सरे वलं ।दीर्घायुत्वमंगिरसो वो अस्तु प्रति गृभ्णीत मानवं सुमेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ut-ā́jan ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ go-máyam ǀ vásu ǀ ṛténa ǀ ábhindan ǀ parivatsaré ǀ valám ǀdīrghāyu-tvám ǀ aṅgirasaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ astu ǀ práti ǀ gṛbhṇīta ǀ mānavám ǀ su-medhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Fathers, who drave forth the wealth in cattle, have in the year's courses cleft Vala by Eternal Law: A lengthened life be yours, O ye Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.wilson_translation: May length of life be yours,Aṅgirasas, our progenitors, who drove forth the wealth of cattle, and bymeans of your sacrifice when the year was ended, demolished (theasura)Bala; welcome, sages, the son of Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: The Fathers, who drave forth the wealth in cattle, have in the year's courses cleft Vala by Eternal Law: A lengthened life be yours, O ye Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य ऋतेन सूर्यमारोहयंदिव्यप्रथयन्पृथिवीं मातरं वि ।सुप्रजास्त्वमंगिरसो वो अस्तु प्रति गृभ्णीत मानवं सुमेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ ṛténa ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ā́ ǀ árohayan ǀ diví ǀ áprathayan ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ mātáram ǀ ví ǀsuprajāḥ-tvám ǀ aṅgirasaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ astu ǀ práti ǀ gṛbhṇīta ǀ mānavám ǀ su-medhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye raised the Sun to heaven by everlasting Law, and spread broad earth, the Mother, out on every side. Fair wealth of progeny be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.wilson_translation: May the possession of posterity be yours,Aṅgirasas, who elevated by the (power) of sacrifice the Sun in heaven, and made the maternal earth renowned; welcome, sages, the son of Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye raised the Sun to heaven by everlasting Law, and spread broad earth, the Mother, out on every side. Fair wealth of progeny be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं नाभा वदति वल्गु वो गृहे देवपुत्रा ऋषयस्तच्छृणोतन ।सुब्रह्मण्यमंगिरसो वो अस्तु प्रति गृभ्णीत मानवं सुमेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ nā́bhā ǀ vadati ǀ valgú ǀ vaḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀ déva-putrāḥ ǀ ṛṣayaḥ ǀ tát ǀ śṛṇotana ǀsu-brahmaṇyám ǀ aṅgirasaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ astu ǀ práti ǀ gṛbhṇīta ǀ mānavám ǀ su-medhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This kinsman in your dwellingplace speaks pleasant words: give car to this, ye Ṛṣis, children of the Gods. High Brahman dignity be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛṣis, sons of the gods, this (Nābhānediṣṭha) addresses to you in the house of (sacrifice) hisbenediction, hear it; may divine splendour,Aṅgirasas, be yours; welcome, sages, the son of Manu.
verses.griffith_verse: This kinsman in your dwellingplace speaks pleasant words: give car to this, ye Ṛṣis, children of the Gods. High Brahman dignity be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विरूपास इदृषयस्त इद्गंभीरवेपसः ।ते अंगिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः परि जज्ञिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: ví-rūpāsaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ té ǀ ít ǀ gambhīrá-vepasaḥ ǀté ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ té ǀ agnéḥ ǀ pári ǀ jajñire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Distinguished by their varied form, these Ṛṣis have been deeply moved. These are the sons of Aṅgirases: from Agni have they sprung to life.
verses.wilson_translation: These Ṛṣis, however different in form, were verily of profound piety; they are the Aṅgirasaswhohave been born as the sons of Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: Distinguished by their varied form, these Ṛṣis have been deeply moved. These are the sons of Aṅgirases: from Agni have they sprung to life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये अग्नेः परि जज्ञिरे विरूपासो दिवस्परि ।नवग्वो नु दशग्वो अंगिरस्तमो सचा देवेषु मंहते ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ agnéḥ ǀ pári ǀ jajñiré ǀ ví-rūpāsaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ pári ǀnáva-gvaḥ ǀ nú ǀ dáśa-gvaḥ ǀ áṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ ǀ sácā ǀ devéṣu ǀ maṃhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Distinguished by their varied form, they sprang from Agni, from the sky. Navagva and Daśagva, noblest Aṅgiras, he giveth bounty with the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Among those who have sprung from Agniin many forms, (and spring) from heaven, the chief Aṅgirasa, the celebrator of the nine-month rite, the celebrator of the ten-month rite, accompanied by the godsbestows (upon me wealth).
verses.griffith_verse: Distinguished by their varied form, they sprang from Agni, from the sky. Navagva and Daśagva, noblest Aṅgiras, he giveth bounty with the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रेण युजा निः सृजंत वाघतो व्रजं गोमंतमश्विनं ।सहस्रं मे ददतो अष्टकर्ण्यः श्रवो देवेष्वक्रत ॥
verses.transliteration: índreṇa ǀ yujā́ ǀ níḥ ǀ sṛjanta ǀ vāghátaḥ ǀ vrajám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ aśvínam ǀsahásram ǀ me ǀ dádataḥ ǀ aṣṭa-karṇyáḥ ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ akrata ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Indra for associate the priests have cleared the stable full of steeds and kine, Giving to me a thousand with their eightmarked cars, they gained renown among the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The acceptors of oblations, with Indrafor their associate, have emptied pastures crowded with cows,and horses, giving me a thousand full-grown (cattle), they have gained renown among the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: With Indra for associate the priests have cleared the stable full of steeds and kine, Giving to me a thousand with their eightmarked cars, they gained renown among the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नूनं जायतामयं मनुस्तोक्मेव रोहतु ।यः सहस्रं शताश्वं सद्यो दानाय मंहते ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nūnám ǀ jāyatām ǀ ayám ǀ mánuḥ ǀ tókma-iva ǀ rohatu ǀyáḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ śatá-aśvam ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ dānā́ya ǀ máṃhate ǁ
verses.english_translation: May this man's sons be multiplied; like springing corn may Manu grow, Who gives at once in bounteous gift a thousand kine, a hundred steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May this Manu(Sāvarṇi) quickly be born, may he increase like (well- watered) seed, who sends meat once a thousand and a hundred horses for a present.
verses.griffith_verse: May this man's sons be multiplied; like springing corn may Manu grow, Who gives at once in bounteous gift a thousand kine, a hundred steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न तमश्नोति कश्चन दिव इव सान्वारभं ।सावर्ण्यस्य दक्षिणा वि सिंधुरिव पप्रथे ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ aśnoti ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǀ diváḥ-iva ǀ sā́nu ǀ ā-rábham ǀsāvarṇyásya ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ ví ǀ síndhuḥ-iva ǀ paprathe ǁ
verses.english_translation: No one attains to him, as though a man would grasp the heights of heaven. Savarnya's sacrificial meed hath broadened like an ample flood.
verses.wilson_translation: No one succeeds in reaching him; (elevated) like the summit of heaven, the liberality of Sāvarṇihasbroadened out like a river.
verses.griffith_verse: No one attains to him, as though a man would grasp the heights of heaven. Savarnya's sacrificial meed hath broadened like an ample flood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत दासा परिविषे स्मद्दिष्टी गोपरीणसा ।यदुस्तुर्वश्च मामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ dāsā́ ǀ pari-víṣe ǀ smáddiṣṭī íti smát-diṣṭī ǀ gó-parīṇasā ǀyáduḥ ǀ turváḥ ǀ ca ǀ mamahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yadu and Turva, too, have given two Dāsas, well-disposed, to serve, Together with great store of kine.
verses.wilson_translation: Yaduand Indraspeaking auspiciously, and possessed of numerous cattle, gave them like (appointed)servants, for the enjoyment (of Manu Sāvarṇi).
verses.griffith_verse: Yadu and Turva, too, have given two Dāsas, well-disposed, to serve, Together with great store of kine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रदा ग्रामणीर्मा रिषन्मनुः सूर्येणास्य यतमानैतु दक्षिणा ।सावर्णेर्देवाः प्र तिरंत्वायुर्यस्मिन्नश्रांता असनाम वाजं ॥
verses.transliteration: sahasra-dā́ḥ ǀ grāma-nī́ḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ riṣat ǀ mánuḥ ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ asya ǀ yátamānā ǀ etu ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀsā́varṇeḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ tirantu ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ yásmin ǀ áśrāntāḥ ǀ ásanāma ǀ vā́jam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Blest be the hamlet's chief, most liberal Manu, and may his bounty rival that of Sūrya. May the God let Ssvarni's life be leng thened, with whom, unwearied, we have lived and prospered.
verses.wilson_translation: May the donor of a thousand (cows), the head of the district, the Manu, never suffer wrong, may hisliberality go spreading (in glory) with the sun; may the gods prolong the life of Sāvarṇi(from whom) unwearied(in his service) we enjoy abundant food.
verses.griffith_verse: Blest be the hamlet's chief, most liberal Manu, and may his bounty rival that of Sūrya. May the God let Ssvarni's life be leng thened, with whom, unwearied, we have lived and prospered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIII. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY they who would assume kinship from far away, Vivasvān's generations, dearly loved of men,Even the Gods who sit upon the sacred grass of Nahuṣa's son Yayāti, bless and comfort us. For worthy of obeisance, Gods, are all your names, worthy of adoration and of sacrifice.Ye who were born from waters, and from Aditi, and from the earth, do ye here listen to my call. I will rejoice in these Ādityas for my weal, for whom the Mother pours forth water rich in balm,And Dyaus the Infinite, firm as a rock, sweet milk,—Gods active, strong through lauds, whose might the Bull upholds. Looking on men, ne’er slumbering, they by their deserts attained as Gods to lofty immortality.Borne on refulgent cars, sinless, with serpents' powers, they robe them, for our welfare, in the height of heaven. Great Kings who bless us, who have come to sacrifice, who, ne’er assailed, have set their mansion in the sky,—These I invite with adoration and with hymns, mighty Ādityas, Aditi, for happiness. Who offereth to you the laud that ye accept, O ye All-Gods of Manu, many as ye are?Who, Mighty Ones, will prepare for you the sacrifice to bear us over trouble to felicity? Ye to whom Manu, by seven priests, with kindled fire, offered the first oblation with his heart and soul,Vouchsafe us, ye Ādityas, sheitcr free from fear, and make us good and easy paths to happiness. Wise Deities, who have dominion o’er the world, ye thinkers over all that moves not and that moves,Save us from uncommitted and committed sin, preserve us from all sin to-day for happiness. In battles we invoke Indra still swift to hear, and all the holy Host of Heaven who banish grief,Agni, Mitra, and Varuṇa that we may gain, Dyays, Bhaga, Maruts, Prthivi for happiness: Mightily-saving Earth, incomparable Heaven the good guide Aditi who gives secure defenceThe well-oared heavenly Ship that lets no waters in, free from defect, will we ascend for happiness. Bless us, all Holy Ones, that we may have your help, guard and protect us from malignant injury.With fruitful invocation may we call on you, Gods, who give ear to us for grace, for happiness. Keep all disease afar and sordid sacrifice, keep off the wicked man's malicious enmity.Keep far away from us all hatred, O ye Gods, and give us ample shelter for our happiness. Untouched by any evil, every mortal thrives, and, following the Law, spreads in his progeny.Whom ye with your good guidance, O Ādityas, lead safely through all his pain and grief to happiness. That which ye guard and grace in battle, O ye Gods, ye Maruts, where the prize is wealth, where heroes win,That conquering Car, O Indra, that sets forth at dawn, that never breaks, may we ascend for happiness. Vouchsafe us blessing in our paths and desert tracts, blessing in waters and in battle, for the light;Blessing upon the wombs that bring male children forth, and blessing, O ye Maruts, for the gain of wealth. The noblest Svasti with abundant riches, who comes to what is good by distant pathway,—May she at home and far away preserve us, and dwell with us under the Gods’ protection Thus hatb the thoughtful sage, the son of Plati, praised you, O Aditi and all Ādityas,Men are made rich by those who are Immortal: the Heavenly Folk have been extolled by Gaya.

verses.sanskrit: परावतो ये दिधिषंत आप्यं मनुप्रीतासो जनिमा विवस्वतः ।ययातेर्ये नहुष्यस्य बर्हिषि देवा आसते ते अधि ब्रुवंतु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: parā-vátaḥ ǀ yé ǀ dídhiṣante ǀ ā́pyam ǀ mánu-prītāsaḥ ǀ jánima ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀyayā́teḥ ǀ yé ǀ nahuṣyásya ǀ barhíṣi ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ā́sate ǀ té ǀ ádhi ǀ bruvantu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY they who would assume kinship from far away, Vivasvān's generations, dearly loved of men, Even the Gods who sit upon the sacred grass of Nahuṣa's son Yayāti, bless and comfort us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the gods who, (coming) from afar proclaim their affinity (with men), and beloved by men, (support)the genitive rations of (Manu, the son of)Vivasvat; may they who are seated on the sacred grass of Yayāti, the sonof Nahuṣa, speak favourably unto us.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY they who would assume kinship from far away, Vivasvān's generations, dearly loved of men, Even the Gods who sit upon the sacred grass of Nahuṣa's son Yayāti, bless and comfort us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वा हि वो नमस्यानि वंद्या नामानि देवा उत यज्ञियानि वः ।ये स्थ जाता अदितेरद्भ्यस्परि ये पृथिव्यास्ते म इह श्रुता हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvā ǀ hí ǀ vaḥ ǀ namasyā́ni ǀ vándyā ǀ nā́māni ǀ devāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yajñíyāni ǀ vaḥ ǀyé ǀ sthá ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ pári ǀ yé ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ té ǀ me ǀ ihá ǀ śruta ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: For worthy of obeisance, Gods, are all your names, worthy of adoration and of sacrifice. Ye who were born from waters, and from Aditi, and from the earth, do ye here listen to my call.
verses.wilson_translation: All your appellations, gods, are to be revered and praised, and worshipped, and whether you aresprung from heaven, or from the firmament, or from earth, hear at this (solemnity) my invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: For worthy of obeisance, Gods, are all your names, worthy of adoration and of sacrifice. Ye who were born from waters, and from Aditi, and from the earth, do ye here listen to my call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येभ्यो माता मधुमत्पिन्वते पयः पीयूषं द्यौरदितिरद्रिबर्हाः ।उक्थशुष्मान्वृषभरान्त्स्वप्नसस्ताँ आदित्याँ अनु मदा स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: yébhyaḥ ǀ mātā́ ǀ mádhu-mat ǀ pínvate ǀ páyaḥ ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ ádri-barhāḥ ǀukthá-śuṣmān ǀ vṛṣa-bharā́n ǀ su-ápnasaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ ādityā́n ǀ ánu ǀ mada ǀ svastáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will rejoice in these Ādityas for my weal, for whom the Mother pours forth water rich in balm, And Dyaus the Infinite, firm as a rock, sweet milk,—Gods active, strong through lauds, whose might the Bull upholds.
verses.wilson_translation: To (these dieties) to whom the maternal (earth) yields the sweet- flavoured milk, and thecloud-invested, undepressed heaven (yields) ambrosia, to thoseĀdityaswhose strength is sacred praise, whoare bringers of rain, the doers of good actions, offer for your welfare laudation.
verses.griffith_verse: I will rejoice in these Ādityas for my weal, for whom the Mother pours forth water rich in balm, And Dyaus the Infinite, firm as a rock, sweet milk,—Gods active, strong through lauds, whose might the Bull upholds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नृचक्षसो अनिमिषंतो अर्हणा बृहद्देवासो अमृतत्वमानशुः ।ज्योतीरथा अहिमाया अनागसो दिवो वर्ष्माणं वसते स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǀ áni-miṣantaḥ ǀ arháṇā ǀ bṛhát ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ānaśuḥ ǀjyotíḥ-rathāḥ ǀ áhi-māyāḥ ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ varṣmā́ṇam ǀ vasate ǀ svastáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Looking on men, ne’er slumbering, they by their deserts attained as Gods to lofty immortality. Borne on refulgent cars, sinless, with serpents' powers, they robe them, for our welfare, in the height of heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods, the never-slumbering beholders of mankind, and entitled (to their adoration), have obtainedgreat immortality; conveyed in chariots of light, possessed of unsurpassable wisdom, devoid of sin, they inhabitthe exalted station of heaven for the well-being (of the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Looking on men, ne’er slumbering, they by their deserts attained as Gods to lofty immortality. Borne on refulgent cars, sinless, with serpents' powers, they robe them, for our welfare, in the height of heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सम्राजो ये सुवृधो यज्ञमाययुरपरिह्वृता दधिरे दिवि क्षयं ।ताँ आ विवास नमसा सुवृक्तिभिर्महो आदित्याँ अदितिं स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-rā́jaḥ ǀ yé ǀ su-vṛ́dhaḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ ā-yayúḥ ǀ ápari-hvṛtāḥ ǀ dadhiré ǀ diví ǀ kṣáyam ǀtā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ vivāsa ǀ námasā ǀ suvṛktí-bhiḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀ ādityā́n ǀ áditim ǀ svastáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Great Kings who bless us, who have come to sacrifice, who, ne’er assailed, have set their mansion in the sky,— These I invite with adoration and with hymns, mighty Ādityas, Aditi, for happiness.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods, who, kings over all, and most exalted, have come to the sacrifice, who, unassailable, abidein heaven; them, the mightyĀdityas, (the sage) worships with reverence, and with praises, and also Aditifor hiswell- being.
verses.griffith_verse: Great Kings who bless us, who have come to sacrifice, who, ne’er assailed, have set their mansion in the sky,— These I invite with adoration and with hymns, mighty Ādityas, Aditi, for happiness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को वः स्तोमं राधति यं जुजोषथ विश्वे देवासो मनुषो यति ष्ठन ।को वोऽध्वरं तुविजाता अरं करद्यो नः पर्षदत्यंहः स्वस्तये ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ stómam ǀ rādhati ǀ yám ǀ jújoṣatha ǀ víśve ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ manuṣaḥ ǀ yáti ǀ sthána ǀkáḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀ tuvi-jātāḥ ǀ áram ǀ karat ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ párṣat ǀ áti ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ svastáye ǁ
