verses.wilson_translation: Indrawith his voice as with an (armed)handclove Valathe defender of hte kine; desirous of themixture (of milk and Soma) he with (the Maruts)k, who were shining with person iration, destroyed Paṇiandliberated the cows.
verses.griffith_verse: As with a hand, so with his roaring Indra cleft Vala through, the guardian of the cattle. Seeking the milk-draught with sweatshining comrades he stole the Paṇi's kine and left him weeping.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स ईं सत्येभिः सखिभिः शुचद्भिर्गोधायसं वि धनसैरदर्दः ।ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वृषभिर्वराहैर्घर्मस्वेदेभिर्द्रविणं व्यानट् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ satyébhiḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ śucát-bhiḥ ǀ gó-dhāyasam ǀ ví ǀ dhana-sáiḥ ǀ adardarítyadardaḥ ǀbráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ varā́haiḥ ǀ gharmá-svedebhiḥ ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ví ǀ ānaṭ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with bright faithful Friends, winners of booty, hath rent the milker of the cows asunder. Bṛhaspati with wild boars strong and mighty, sweating with heat, hath gained a rich possession.
verses.wilson_translation: Together with his true brilliant wealth-winning friendly (Maruts) he destroyed the detainer of the cows;Brahmaṇaspati, with the showerers (of benefits), the conveyers of desirable (water), the frequenters of sacrifice,acquired wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: He with bright faithful Friends, winners of booty, hath rent the milker of the cows asunder. Bṛhaspati with wild boars strong and mighty, sweating with heat, hath gained a rich possession.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते सत्येन मनसा गोपतिं गा इयानास इषणयंत धीभिः ।बृहस्पतिर्मिथोअवद्यपेभिरुदुस्रिया असृजत स्वयुग्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ satyéna ǀ mánasā ǀ gó-patim ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ iyānā́saḥ ǀ iṣaṇayanta ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ mitháḥ-avadyapebhiḥ ǀ út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ asṛjata ǀ svayúk-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They, longing for the kine, with faithful spirit incited with their hymns the Lord of cattle. Bṛhaspati freed the radiant cows with comrades self-yoked, averting shame from one another.
verses.wilson_translation: They with truthful mind searching for the cows resolved by their exploits to make him the lord of cattle;Bṛhaspatiwith his self-yoked (allied) mutually defending each other from reproach, set free the kind.
verses.griffith_verse: They, longing for the kine, with faithful spirit incited with their hymns the Lord of cattle. Bṛhaspati freed the radiant cows with comrades self-yoked, averting shame from one another.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं वर्धयंतो मतिभिः शिवाभिः सिंहमिव नानदतं सधस्थे ।बृहस्पतिं वृषणं शूरसातौ भरेभरे अनु मदेम जिष्णुं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vardháyantaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ śivā́bhiḥ ǀ siṃhám-iva ǀ nā́nadatam ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ śū́ra-sātau ǀ bháre-bhare ǀ ánu ǀ madema ǀ jiṣṇúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: In our assembly with auspicious praises exalting him who roareth like a lion, Maywe, in every fight where heroes conquer, rejoice in strong Bṛhaspati the Victor.
verses.wilson_translation: Magnifying the victorious Bṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits), roaring in mid-heaven like a lion, letus praise him in the conflicts where heroes win, with auspicious praises.
verses.griffith_verse: In our assembly with auspicious praises exalting him who roareth like a lion, Maywe, in every fight where heroes conquer, rejoice in strong Bṛhaspati the Victor.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदा वाजमसनद्विश्वरूपमा द्यामरुक्षदुत्तराणि सद्म ।बृहस्पतिं वृषणं वर्धयंतो नाना संतो बिभ्रतो ज्योतिरासा ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ásanat ǀ viśvá-rūpam ǀ ā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ árukṣat ǀ út-tarāṇi ǀ sádma ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vardháyantaḥ ǀ nā́nā ǀ sántaḥ ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ āsā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When he had won him every sort of booty and gone to heaven and its most lofty mansions, Men praised Bṛhaspati the Mighty, bringing the light within their mouths from sundry places.
verses.wilson_translation: When he acquires food of various kinds, when he ascends the sky or the northern stations, (the godsare) extolling Bṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits), with their mouth, being in various (quarters), bearing light.
verses.griffith_verse: When he had won him every sort of booty and gone to heaven and its most lofty mansions, Men praised Bṛhaspati the Mighty, bringing the light within their mouths from sundry places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सत्यामाशिषं कृणुता वयोधै कीरिं चिद्ध्यवथ स्वेभिरेवैः ।पश्चा मृधो अप भवंतु विश्वास्तद्रोदसी शृणुतं विश्वमिन्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: satyā́m ǀ ā-śíṣam ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ vayaḥ-dhái ǀ kīrím ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ ávatha ǀ svébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀpaścā́ ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ bhavantu ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ tát ǀ rodasī íti ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ viśvaminvé íti viśvam-invé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fulfil the prayer that begs for vital vigour: aid in your wonted manner even the humble. Let all our foes be turned and driven backward. Hear this, O Heaven and Earth, ye All-producers.
verses.wilson_translation: Make good our prayer for the bestowal of food; you protect through your movements even (me) yourprayer).
verses.griffith_verse: Fulfil the prayer that begs for vital vigour: aid in your wonted manner even the humble. Let all our foes be turned and driven backward. Hear this, O Heaven and Earth, ye All-producers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो मह्ना महतो अर्णवस्य वि मूर्धानमभिनदर्बुदस्य ।अहन्नहिमरिणात्सप्त सिंधूंदेवैर्द्यावापृथिवी प्रावतं नः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ arṇavásya ǀ ví ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ abhinat ǀ arbudásya ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ áriṇāt ǀ saptá ǀ síndhūn ǀ deváiḥ ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ prá ǀ avatam ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra with mighty strength cleft asunder the head of Arbuda the watery monster, Slain Ahi, and set free the Seven Rivers. O Heaven and Earth, with all the Gods protect us.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraby his might has cleft the brow of the vast watery cloud, he has slain Ahi; he has made the sevenrivers flow; do you, heaven and earth, along with the gods, protect us.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra with mighty strength cleft asunder the head of Arbuda the watery monster, Slain Ahi, and set free the Seven Rivers. O Heaven and Earth, with all the Gods protect us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXVIII. Bṛhaspati.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LIKE birds who keep their watch, plashing in water, like the loud voices of the thundering rain-cloud,Like merry streamlets bursting from the mountain, thus to Bṛhaspati our hymns have sounded. The Son of Aṅgirases, meeting the cattle, as Bhaga, brought in Aryaman among us.As Friend of men he decks the wife and husband: as for the race, Bṛhaspati, nerve our coursers. Bṛhaspati, having won them from the mountains, strewed down, like barley out of winnowing- baskets,The vigorous, wandering cows who aid the pious, desired of all, of blameless form, well-coloured. As the Sun dews with meath the seat of Order, and casts a flaming meteor down from heaven.So from the rock Bṛhaspati forced the cattle, and cleft the earth's skin as it were with water. Forth from mid air with light he dravc the darkness, as the gale blows a lily from the fiver.Like the wind grasping at the cloud of Vala, Bṛhaspati gathered to himself the cattle, Bṛhaspati, when he with fiery lightnings cleft through the weapon of reviling Vala,Consumedḥim as tongues cat what teeth have compassed: he threw the prisons of the red cows open. That secret name borne by the lowing cattle within the cave Bṛhaspati discovered,And drave, himself, the bright kine from the mountain, like a bird's young after the egg's disclosure. He looked around on rock-imprisoned sweetness as one who eyes a fish in scanty water.Bṛhaspati, cleaving through with varied clamour, brought it forth like a bowl from out the timber. He found the light of heaven, and fire, and Morning: with lucid rays he forced apart the darkness.As from a joint, Bṛhaspati took the marrow of Vala as he gloried in his cattle. As trees for foliage robbed by winter, Vala mourned for the cows Bṛhaspati had taken.He did a deed ne’er done, ne’er to be equalled, whereby the Sun and Moon ascend alternate. Like a dark steed adorned with pearl, the Fathers have decorated heaven With constellations.They set the light in day, in night the darkness. Bṛhaspati cleft the rock and found the cattle. This homage have we.offered to the Cloud God who thunders out to many in succession.May this Bṛhaspati vouchsafe us fulness of life with kine and horses, men, and heroes.

verses.sanskrit: उदप्रुतो न वयो रक्षमाणा वावदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः ।गिरिभ्रजो नोर्मयो मदंतो बृहस्पतिमभ्यर्का अनावन् ॥
verses.transliteration: uda-prútaḥ ǀ ná ǀ váyaḥ ǀ rákṣamāṇāḥ ǀ vā́vadataḥ ǀ abhríyasya-iva ǀ ghóṣāḥ ǀgiri-bhrájaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ abhí ǀ arkā́ḥ ǀ anāvan ǁ
verses.english_translation: LIKE birds who keep their watch, plashing in water, like the loud voices of the thundering rain-cloud, Like merry streamlets bursting from the mountain, thus to Bṛhaspati our hymns have sounded.
verses.wilson_translation: Like birds swimming in water when keeping watch, like the sound of the roaring thunder-cloud, likesounding torrents falling from the clouds, the worshippers glorify Bṛhaspati.
verses.griffith_verse: LIKE birds who keep their watch, plashing in water, like the loud voices of the thundering rain-cloud, Like merry streamlets bursting from the mountain, thus to Bṛhaspati our hymns have sounded.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं गोभिरांगिरसो नक्षमाणो भग इवेदर्यमणं निनाय ।जने मित्रो न दंपती अनक्ति बृहस्पते वाजयाशूँरिवाजौ ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ āṅgirasáḥ ǀ nákṣamāṇaḥ ǀ bhágaḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ nināya ǀjáne ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ anakti ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ vājáya ǀ āśū́n-iva ǀ ājáu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Son of Aṅgirases, meeting the cattle, as Bhaga, brought in Aryaman among us. As Friend of men he decks the wife and husband: as for the race, Bṛhaspati, nerve our coursers.
verses.wilson_translation: The son of Aṅgirasapervading him with his brightness has, like Bhaga, brought Aryamanto the cows;as Mitra(unites his radiance) with the people, so has he united husband and wife;Bṛhaspati, send (yourwide-spread rays to your worshippers) as (a warrior sends his) horses to battle.
verses.griffith_verse: The Son of Aṅgirases, meeting the cattle, as Bhaga, brought in Aryaman among us. As Friend of men he decks the wife and husband: as for the race, Bṛhaspati, nerve our coursers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: साध्वर्या अतिथिनीरिषिराः स्पार्हाः सुवर्णा अनवद्यरूपाः ।बृहस्पतिः पर्वतेभ्यो वितूर्या निर्गा ऊपे यवमिव स्थिविभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: sādhu-aryā́ḥ ǀ atithínīḥ ǀ iṣirā́ḥ ǀ spārhā́ḥ ǀ su-várṇāḥ ǀ anavadyá-rūpāḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ párvatebhyaḥ ǀ vi-tū́rya ǀ níḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ūpe ǀ yávam-iva ǀ sthiví-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, having won them from the mountains, strewed down, like barley out of winnowing- baskets, The vigorous, wandering cows who aid the pious, desired of all, of blameless form, well-coloured.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspatibrings unto (the gods), after extricating them from the mountains, the cows that are theyielders of pure (milk), ever in motion, the objects of search and of desire, well-coloured and of unexceptionableform, (as men bring) barley from the granaries.
verses.griffith_verse: Bṛhaspati, having won them from the mountains, strewed down, like barley out of winnowing- baskets, The vigorous, wandering cows who aid the pious, desired of all, of blameless form, well-coloured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आप्रुषायन्मधुन ऋतस्य योनिमवक्षिपन्नर्क उल्कामिव द्योः ।बृहस्पतिरुद्धरन्नश्मनो गा भूम्या उद्नेव वि त्वचं बिभेद ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-pruṣāyán ǀ mádhunā ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónim ǀ ava-kṣipán ǀ arkáḥ ǀ ulkā́m-iva ǀ dyóḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ uddháran ǀ áśmanaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ bhū́myāḥ ǀ udnā́-iva ǀ ví ǀ tvácam ǀ bibheda ǁ
verses.english_translation: As the Sun dews with meath the seat of Order, and casts a flaming meteor down from heaven. So from the rock Bṛhaspati forced the cattle, and cleft the earth's skin as it were with water.
verses.wilson_translation: Saturating (the earth) with water, scattering the receptacle of rain, the adorable Bṛhaspati, raising upthe cattle from the rock as (he raises) a meteor from the sky, rent the skin of the earth (with the hoofs of thecattle) as (Parjanyarends it) with rain.
verses.griffith_verse: As the Sun dews with meath the seat of Order, and casts a flaming meteor down from heaven. So from the rock Bṛhaspati forced the cattle, and cleft the earth's skin as it were with water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप ज्योतिषा तमो अंतरिक्षादुद्नः शीपालमिव वात आजत् ।बृहस्पतिरनुमृश्या वलस्याभ्रमिव वात आ चक्र आ गाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ támaḥ ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ udnáḥ ǀ śī́pālam-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ājat ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ anu-mṛ́śya ǀ valásya ǀ abhrám-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cakre ǀ ā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forth from mid air with light he dravc the darkness, as the gale blows a lily from the fiver. Like the wind grasping at the cloud of Vala, Bṛhaspati gathered to himself the cattle,
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspatidrove away the darkness from the firmament with light as the wind (blows) the Śīpālafrom the water; guessing (them to be there), he swept the Vala's cows together to himself as the wind (sweeps)the clouds.
verses.griffith_verse: Forth from mid air with light he dravc the darkness, as the gale blows a lily from the fiver. Like the wind grasping at the cloud of Vala, Bṛhaspati gathered to himself the cattle,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदा वलस्य पीयतो जसुं भेद्बृहस्पतिरग्नितपोभिरर्कैः ।दद्भिर्न जिह्वा परिविष्टमाददाविर्निधीँरकृणोदुस्रियाणां ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ valásya ǀ pī́yataḥ ǀ jásum ǀ bhét ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ agnitápaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀdat-bhíḥ ǀ ná ǀ jihvā́ ǀ pári-viṣṭam ǀ ā́dat ǀ āvíḥ ǀ ni-dhī́n ǀ akṛṇot ǀ usríyāṇām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, when he with fiery lightnings cleft through the weapon of reviling Vala, Consumedḥim as tongues cat what teeth have compassed: he threw the prisons of the red cows open.
verses.wilson_translation: When Bṛhaspatidemolished with rays burning like fire the weapon of the malignant Vala, he devouredhim (encompassed by his followers) as the tongue (consumes) that which is encompassed by the teeth; he mademanifest the hiding- plural ce of the kine.
verses.griffith_verse: Bṛhaspati, when he with fiery lightnings cleft through the weapon of reviling Vala, Consumedḥim as tongues cat what teeth have compassed: he threw the prisons of the red cows open.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पतिरमत हि त्यदासां नाम स्वरीणां सदने गुहा यत् ।आंडेव भित्त्वा शकुनस्य गर्भमुदुस्रियाः पर्वतस्य त्मनाजत् ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ ámata ǀ hí ǀ tyát ǀ āsām ǀ nā́ma ǀ svarī́ṇām ǀ sádane ǀ gúhā ǀ yát ǀāṇḍā́-iva ǀ bhittvā́ ǀ śakunásya ǀ gárbham ǀ út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ párvatasya ǀ tmánā ǀ ājat ǁ
verses.english_translation: That secret name borne by the lowing cattle within the cave Bṛhaspati discovered, And drave, himself, the bright kine from the mountain, like a bird's young after the egg's disclosure.
verses.wilson_translation: When Bṛhaspatihad discovered that name of the lowing kine in their plural ce in the cave, by his ownstrength he extricated the cattle from the rock as (breaking) the eggs of a bird (one extricates) the embryo.
verses.griffith_verse: That secret name borne by the lowing cattle within the cave Bṛhaspati discovered, And drave, himself, the bright kine from the mountain, like a bird's young after the egg's disclosure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्नापिनद्धं मधु पर्यपश्यन्मत्स्यं न दीन उदनि क्षियंतं ।निष्टज्जभार चमसं न वृक्षाद्बृहस्पतिर्विरवेणा विकृत्य ॥
verses.transliteration: áśnā ǀ ápi-naddham ǀ mádhu ǀ pári ǀ apaśyat ǀ mátsyam ǀ ná ǀ dīné ǀ udáni ǀ kṣiyántam ǀníḥ ǀ tát ǀ jabhāra ǀ camasám ǀ ná ǀ vṛkṣā́t ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vi-ravéṇa ǀ vi-kṛ́tya ǁ
verses.english_translation: He looked around on rock-imprisoned sweetness as one who eyes a fish in scanty water. Bṛhaspati, cleaving through with varied clamour, brought it forth like a bowl from out the timber.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspatilooked round upon the cowsshutup in the cave like fish in a dried up pool; he seized Valawith a shout, cutting him off like a bowl from a tree.
verses.griffith_verse: He looked around on rock-imprisoned sweetness as one who eyes a fish in scanty water. Bṛhaspati, cleaving through with varied clamour, brought it forth like a bowl from out the timber.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोषामविंदत्स स्वः सो अग्निं सो अर्केण वि बबाधे तमांसि ।बृहस्पतिर्गोवपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्जानं न पर्वणो जभार ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ uṣā́m ǀ avindat ǀ sáḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ agním ǀ sáḥ ǀ arkéṇa ǀ ví ǀ babādhe ǀ támāṃsi ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ gó-vapuṣaḥ ǀ valásya ǀ níḥ ǀ majjā́nam ǀ ná ǀ párvaṇaḥ ǀ jabhāra ǁ
verses.english_translation: He found the light of heaven, and fire, and Morning: with lucid rays he forced apart the darkness. As from a joint, Bṛhaspati took the marrow of Vala as he gloried in his cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Bṛhaspatifound the dawn, the sun,Agni; he dispersed the gloom with light; he seized (the cattle fromthe rock)) of Valasurrounded by the kine as (one extracts) marrow from a bone.
verses.griffith_verse: He found the light of heaven, and fire, and Morning: with lucid rays he forced apart the darkness. As from a joint, Bṛhaspati took the marrow of Vala as he gloried in his cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिमेव पर्णा मुषिता वनानि बृहस्पतिनाकृपयद्वलो गाः ।अनानुकृत्यमपुनश्चकार यात्सूर्यामासा मिथ उच्चरातः ॥
verses.transliteration: himā́-iva ǀ parṇā́ ǀ muṣitā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ bṛ́haspátinā ǀ akṛpayat ǀ valáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀananu-kṛtyám ǀ apunáríti ǀ cakāra ǀ yā́t ǀ sū́ryāmā́sā ǀ mitháḥ ǀ ut-cárātaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As trees for foliage robbed by winter, Vala mourned for the cows Bṛhaspati had taken. He did a deed ne’er done, ne’er to be equalled, whereby the Sun and Moon ascend alternate.
verses.wilson_translation: As the trees (bemoan) their leaves carried off by the winter, so Valabemoaned his kine (carried off) by Bṛhaspati; he did that which cannot be imitated, which cannot be repeated, whereby sun and moon mutually rise(day and night).
verses.griffith_verse: As trees for foliage robbed by winter, Vala mourned for the cows Bṛhaspati had taken. He did a deed ne’er done, ne’er to be equalled, whereby the Sun and Moon ascend alternate.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि श्यावं न कृशनेभिरश्वं नक्षत्रेभिः पितरो द्यामपिंशन् ।रात्र्यां तमो अदधुर्ज्योतिरहन्बृहस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद्गाः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ śyāvám ǀ ná ǀ kṛ́śanebhiḥ ǀ áśvam ǀ nákṣatrebhiḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ apiṃśan ǀrā́tryām ǀ támaḥ ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ áhan ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ bhinát ǀ ádrim ǀ vidát ǀ gā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a dark steed adorned with pearl, the Fathers have decorated heaven With constellations. They set the light in day, in night the darkness. Bṛhaspati cleft the rock and found the cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: The protecting (deities) have decorated the heaven with constellations as (men decorate) a brownhorse with golden trappings; they established darkness in the night and light in the day;Bṛhaspatifractured therock and recovered the cows.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a dark steed adorned with pearl, the Fathers have decorated heaven With constellations. They set the light in day, in night the darkness. Bṛhaspati cleft the rock and found the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदमकर्म नमो अभ्रियाय यः पूर्वीरन्वानोनवीति ।बृहस्पतिः स हि गोभिः सो अश्वैः स वीरेभिः स नृभिर्नो वयो धात् ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ akarma ǀ námaḥ ǀ abhriyā́ya ǀ yáḥ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ā-nónavīti ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ vīrébhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: This homage have we.offered to the Cloud God who thunders out to many in succession. May this Bṛhaspati vouchsafe us fulness of life with kine and horses, men, and heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: We have offered this homage to Bṛhaspati, who lives in mid-heaven, who recites in order many(sacred stanzas); may he bestow upon us food, with cows, with horses, with son, with dependants.
verses.griffith_verse: This homage have we.offered to the Cloud God who thunders out to many in succession. May this Bṛhaspati vouchsafe us fulness of life with kine and horses, men, and heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXIX. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Auspicious is the aspect of Vadhryasva's fire good is its guidance, pleasant are its visitings.When first the people Of Sumitra kindle it, with butter poured thercon it crackles and shines bright. Butter is that which makes Vadhryaiva's fire growstrong: the butter is its food, the butter makes it fat.It spreads abroad when butter hath been offered it, and balmed with streams of butter shines forth like the Sun. Still newest is this face of thine, O Agni, which Manu and Sumitra have enkindled.So richly shine, accept our songs with favour, so give us strengthening food, so send us glory. Accept this offering, Agni, whom aforetime Vadhryasva, hath entreated and enkindled.Guard well our homes and ople, guard our bodies, protect thy girt to us which thou hast granted. Be splendid, guard us Kinsman of Vadhryasva: let not the enmity of men o’ercome thee,Like the bold hero Cyavāna, I Sumitra tell forth the title of Vadhryaiva's Kinsman. All treasures hast thou won, of plains and mountains, and quelled the Dāsas' and Āryas' hatred.Like the bold hero Cyavāna, O Agni, mayst thou subdue the men who long for battle. Deft Agni hath a lengthened thread, tall oxen, a thousand heifers, numberless devices.Decked by the men, splendid among the splendid, shine brightly forth amid devout Sumitras. Thine is the teeming cow, O Jātavedas, who pours at once her ceaseless flow, Sabardhuk,Thou. art lit up by men enriched with guerdon, O Agni, by the pious-souled Sumitras. Even Immortal Gods, O Jātavedas, Vadhryasva's Kinsman, have declared thy grandeur.When human tribes drew near with supplication thou conqueredst with men whom thou hadst strengthened. Like as a father bears his son, O Agni, Vadhryasva bare thee in his lap and served thee.Thou, Youngest God, having enjoyed his fuel, didst vanquish those of old though they were mighty. Vadhryasva's Agni evermore hath vanquished his foes with heroes who had pressed the Soma.Lord of bright rays, thou burntest up the battle, subduing, as our help, e’en mighty foemen. This Agni of Vadhryasva, Vṛtra-slayer, lit from of old, must be invoked with homage.As such assail our enemies, Vadhryasva, whether the foes be strangers or be kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit: भद्रा अग्नेर्वध्र्यश्वस्य संदृशो वामी प्रणीतिः सुरणा उपेतयः ।यदीं सुमित्रा विशो अग्र इंधते घृतेनाहुतो जरते दविद्युतत् ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrā́ḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ sam-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ vāmī́ ǀ prá-nītiḥ ǀ su-ráṇāḥ ǀ úpa-itayaḥ ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ su-mitrā́ḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ágre ǀ indháte ǀ ghṛténa ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ jarate ǀ dávidyutat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious is the aspect of Vadhryasva's fire good is its guidance, pleasant are its visitings. When first the people Of Sumitra kindle it, with butter poured thercon it crackles and shines bright.
verses.wilson_translation: May Agni's regards be benevolent to Vadhryaśva; may his guidance be auspicious, his approaches(to the sacrifice) favourable; when the Sumitrapeople first kindled Agni, then fed with butter and brilliantly blazinghe is glorified.
verses.griffith_verse: Auspicious is the aspect of Vadhryasva's fire good is its guidance, pleasant are its visitings. When first the people Of Sumitra kindle it, with butter poured thercon it crackles and shines bright.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृतमग्नेर्वध्र्यश्वस्य वर्धनं घृतमन्नं घृतम्वस्य मेदनं ।घृतेनाहुत उर्विया वि पप्रथे सूर्य इव रोचते सर्पिरासुतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛtám ǀ agnéḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ várdhanam ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ánnam ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ asya ǀ médanam ǀghṛténa ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ paprathe ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ rocate ǀ sarpíḥ-āsutiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Butter is that which makes Vadhryaiva's fire growstrong: the butter is its food, the butter makes it fat. It spreads abroad when butter hath been offered it, and balmed with streams of butter shines forth like the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: May ghī be the augmenter of the Agniof Vadhryaśva; may ghī be his food; may ghī be hisnutriment; sacrified to with ghī he expands exceedingly; he shines like the sun, when the clarified butter ispoured out for him.
verses.griffith_verse: Butter is that which makes Vadhryaiva's fire growstrong: the butter is its food, the butter makes it fat. It spreads abroad when butter hath been offered it, and balmed with streams of butter shines forth like the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते मनुर्यदनीकं सुमित्रः समीधे अग्ने तदिदं नवीयः ।स रेवच्छोच स गिरो जुषस्व स वाजं दर्षि स इह श्रवो धाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ mánuḥ ǀ yát ǀ ánīkam ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ sam-īdhe�� ǀ agne ǀ tát ǀ idám ǀ návīyaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ revát ǀ śoca ǀ sáḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ juṣasva ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ darṣi ǀ sáḥ ǀ ihá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Still newest is this face of thine, O Agni, which Manu and Sumitra have enkindled. So richly shine, accept our songs with favour, so give us strengthening food, so send us glory.
verses.wilson_translation: May that your army of flame,Agni, which Manu, which Sumitrahas kindled, be the newest; do youshine wealthily; do you graciously accept our praises; do you destroy the might (of our foes), do you grant usabundance.
verses.griffith_verse: Still newest is this face of thine, O Agni, which Manu and Sumitra have enkindled. So richly shine, accept our songs with favour, so give us strengthening food, so send us glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं त्वा पूर्वमीळितो वध्र्यश्वः समीधे अग्ने स इदं जुषस्व ।स नः स्तिपा उत भवा तनूपा दात्रं रक्षस्व यदिदं ते अस्मे ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ pū́rvam ǀ īḷitáḥ ǀ vadhri-aśváḥ ǀ sam-īdhé ǀ agne ǀ sáḥ ǀ idám ǀ juṣasva ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sti-pā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ bhava ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǀ dātrám ǀ rakṣasva ǀ yát ǀ idám ǀ te ǀ asmé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Accept this offering, Agni, whom aforetime Vadhryasva, hath entreated and enkindled. Guard well our homes and ople, guard our bodies, protect thy girt to us which thou hast granted.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Agni, whom Vadhryaśva propitiating you formerly kindled, accept this; be the proector of oursacrifices, be the protector of our bodies; preserve this wealth which has been given to us by you.
verses.griffith_verse: Accept this offering, Agni, whom aforetime Vadhryasva, hath entreated and enkindled. Guard well our homes and ople, guard our bodies, protect thy girt to us which thou hast granted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भवा द्युम्नी वाध्र्यश्वोत गोपा मा त्वा तारीदभिमातिर्जनानां ।शूर इव धृष्णुश्च्यवनः सुमित्रः प्र नु वोचं वाध्र्यश्वस्य नाम ॥
verses.transliteration: bháva ǀ dyumnī́ ǀ vādhri-aśva ǀ utá ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ tārīt ǀ abhí-mātiḥ ǀ jánānām ǀśū́raḥ-iva ǀ ghṛṣṇúḥ ǀ cyávanaḥ ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ prá ǀ nú ǀ vocam ǀ vā́dhri-aśvasya ǀ nā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be splendid, guard us Kinsman of Vadhryasva: let not the enmity of men o’ercome thee, Like the bold hero Cyavāna, I Sumitra tell forth the title of Vadhryaiva's Kinsman.
verses.wilson_translation: Kinsman of Vadhryaśva, be the possessor of food and our protector; let no one assail you, (for youare) the overcomer of men; like a resolute warrior (you are) the overthrower (of enemies); I,Sumitra, celebratethe names of the kinsmen of Vadhyaśva.
verses.griffith_verse: Be splendid, guard us Kinsman of Vadhryasva: let not the enmity of men o’ercome thee, Like the bold hero Cyavāna, I Sumitra tell forth the title of Vadhryaiva's Kinsman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समज्र्या पर्वत्या वसूनि दासा वृत्राण्यार्या जिगेथ ।शूर इव धृष्णुश्च्यवनो जनानां त्वमग्ने पृतनायूँरभि ष्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ ajryā́ ǀ parvatyā́ ǀ vásūni ǀ dā́sā ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ ā́ryā ǀ jigetha ǀśū́raḥ-iva ǀ ghṛṣṇúḥ ǀ cyávanaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ pṛtanā-yū́n ǀ abhí ǀ syāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All treasures hast thou won, of plains and mountains, and quelled the Dāsas' and Āryas' hatred. Like the bold hero Cyavāna, O Agni, mayst thou subdue the men who long for battle.
verses.wilson_translation: You have gained mountain-treasures beneficial to men, (you have defeated the hostilities) of strongmen,Dāsasand Vṛtras, like a resolute warrior, do you,Agni, the overthrower (of enemies), overcome thosewho are desirous of battle.
verses.griffith_verse: All treasures hast thou won, of plains and mountains, and quelled the Dāsas' and Āryas' hatred. Like the bold hero Cyavāna, O Agni, mayst thou subdue the men who long for battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घतंतुर्बृहदुक्षायमग्निः सहस्रस्तरीः शतनीथ ऋभ्वा ।द्युमांद्युमत्सु नृभिर्मृज्यमानः सुमित्रेषु दीदयो देवयत्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: dīrghá-tantuḥ ǀ bṛhát-ukṣā ǀ ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ sahásra-starīḥ ǀ śatá-nīthaḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀdyu-mā́n ǀ dyumát-su ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ mṛjyámānaḥ ǀ su-mitréṣu ǀ dīdayaḥ ǀ devayát-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Deft Agni hath a lengthened thread, tall oxen, a thousand heifers, numberless devices. Decked by the men, splendid among the splendid, shine brightly forth amid devout Sumitras.
verses.wilson_translation: This Agnito whom a long series (of sacrifices has been addressed), who is bright with many rays,covering thousands (in the form of ghī), the leader of hundreds (of burnt offerings), the mighty one, brilliantamong the brilliant, (is) being glorified by the priests; shine (Agni) upon the devout Sumitras.
verses.griffith_verse: Deft Agni hath a lengthened thread, tall oxen, a thousand heifers, numberless devices. Decked by the men, splendid among the splendid, shine brightly forth amid devout Sumitras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे धेनुः सुदुघा जातवेदोऽसश्चतेव समना सबर्धुक् ।त्वं नृभिर्दक्षिणावद्भिरग्ने सुमित्रेभिरिध्यसे देवयद्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ su-dúghā ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ asaścátā-iva ǀ samanā́ ǀ sabaḥ-dhúk ǀtvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ dákṣiṇāvat-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ su-mitrébhiḥ ǀ idhyase ǀ devayát-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine is the teeming cow, O Jātavedas, who pours at once her ceaseless flow, Sabardhuk, Thou. art lit up by men enriched with guerdon, O Agni, by the pious-souled Sumitras.
verses.wilson_translation: In you,Jātavedas, is the cow easy to be milked, yielding ambrosia as it were inexhaustibly in battle,you are kindled,Agni, by the devout Sumitraswho are entitled to the sacrificial donation.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine is the teeming cow, O Jātavedas, who pours at once her ceaseless flow, Sabardhuk, Thou. art lit up by men enriched with guerdon, O Agni, by the pious-souled Sumitras.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवाश्चित्ते अमृता जातवेदो महिमानं वाध्र्यश्व प्र वोचन् ।यत्संपृच्छं मानुषीर्विश आयंत्वं नृभिरजयस्त्वावृधेभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ vādhri-aśva ǀ prá ǀ vocan ǀyát ǀ sam-pṛ́ccham ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́yan ǀ tvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ ajayaḥ ǀ tvā́-vṛdhebhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even Immortal Gods, O Jātavedas, Vadhryasva's Kinsman, have declared thy grandeur. When human tribes drew near with supplication thou conqueredst with men whom thou hadst strengthened.
verses.wilson_translation: The immortal gods have proclaimed your greatness.Jātavedas, Vadhryaśva (Agni); when humanbeings, came to inquire (who would slay theasuras), then you with (the gods), the leaders of all, fostered by youdid overcome (those who impeded the ceremony).
verses.griffith_verse: Even Immortal Gods, O Jātavedas, Vadhryasva's Kinsman, have declared thy grandeur. When human tribes drew near with supplication thou conqueredst with men whom thou hadst strengthened.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पितेव पुत्रमबिभरुपस्थे त्वामग्ने वध्र्यश्वः सपर्यन् ।जुषाणो अस्य समिधं यविष्ठोत पूर्वाँ अवनोर्व्राधतश्चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: pitā́-iva ǀ putrám ǀ abibhaḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ vadhri-aśváḥ ǀ saparyán ǀjuṣāṇáḥ ǀ asya ǀ sam-ídham ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ utá ǀ pū́rvān ǀ avanoḥ ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like as a father bears his son, O Agni, Vadhryasva bare thee in his lap and served thee. Thou, Youngest God, having enjoyed his fuel, didst vanquish those of old though they were mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: Vadhryaśva, honouring you,Agni, plural ced you upon the altar as a father (plural ces) his son (upon hislap); plural ased with his fuel, youngest (of the gods), you did slay the ancient obstructers of the rite.
verses.griffith_verse: Like as a father bears his son, O Agni, Vadhryasva bare thee in his lap and served thee. Thou, Youngest God, having enjoyed his fuel, didst vanquish those of old though they were mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शश्वदग्निर्वध्र्यश्वस्य शत्रून्नृभिर्जिगाय सुतसोमवद्भिः ।समनं चिददहश्चित्रभानोऽव व्राधंतमभिनद्वृधश्चित् ॥
verses.transliteration: śáśvat ǀ agníḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ śátrūn ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ jigāya ǀ sutásomavat-bhiḥ ǀsámanam ǀ cit ǀ adahaḥ ǀ citrabhāno íti citra-bhāno ǀ áva ǀ vrā́dhantam ǀ abhinat ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ cit ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vadhryasva's Agni evermore hath vanquished his foes with heroes who had pressed the Soma. Lord of bright rays, thou burntest up the battle, subduing, as our help, e’en mighty foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniby means of the priests of Vadhryaśva pouring out libations always conquers his foes; you(Agni) shining with varied splendour, have consumed the battle; (your praiser) self-fostered has destroyed hispowerful (assailant).
verses.griffith_verse: Vadhryasva's Agni evermore hath vanquished his foes with heroes who had pressed the Soma. Lord of bright rays, thou burntest up the battle, subduing, as our help, e’en mighty foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयमग्निर्वध्र्यश्वस्य वृत्रहा सनकात्प्रेद्धो नमसोपवाक्यः ।स नो अजामीँरुत वा विजामीनभि तिष्ठ शर्धतो वाध्र्यश्व ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ sanakā́t ǀ prá-iddhaḥ ǀ námasā ǀ upa-vākyáḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ájāmīn ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ ví-jāmīn ǀ abhí ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ śárdhataḥ ǀ vādhri-aśva ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Agni of Vadhryasva, Vṛtra-slayer, lit from of old, must be invoked with homage. As such assail our enemies, Vadhryasva, whether the foes be strangers or be kinsmen.
verses.wilson_translation: From a long period has this Agnithe slayer of foes been kindled (by the oblation) of Vadhryaśva; (heis) to be addressed with reverence; do you, (Agni, kindled in the) family of Vadhryaśva, overcome our enemies,both those who have no kinsmen and those who have many kinsmen.
verses.griffith_verse: This Agni of Vadhryasva, Vṛtra-slayer, lit from of old, must be invoked with homage. As such assail our enemies, Vadhryasva, whether the foes be strangers or be kinsmen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXX. Āprīs.
hymns.anukramani: ११सुमित्रो वाध्र्यश्वः। आप्रीसूक्तं = (१ इध्मः समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा, २ नराशंसः, ३ इळ:, ४ बर्हिः, ५ देवीर्द्वारः, ६ उषासानक्ता, ७ दैव्यौ होतारौ प्रचेतसौ, ८ त्रिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः, ९ त्वष्टा, १० वनस्पतिः, ११ स्वाहाकृतयः) । त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ENJOY, O Agni, this my Fuel, welcome the oil-filled ladle where we pour libation.Rise up for worship of the Gods, wise Agni, on the earth's height, while days are bright with beauty. May he who goes before the Gods come hither with steeds whose shapes are varied, Narasarhsa.May he, most Godlike, speed our offered viands with homage God-ward on the path of Order. Men with oblations laud most constant Agni, and pray him to perform an envoy's duty.With lightly-rolling car and best draught-horses, bring the Gods hither and sit down as Hotar. May the delight of Gods spread out transversely: may it be with us long in length and fragrant.O Holy Grass divine, with friendly spirit bring thou the willing Gods whose Chief is Indra. Touch ye the far-extending height of heaven or spring apart to suit the wide earth's measure.Yearning, ye Doors, with those sublime in greatness, seize eagerly the heavenly Car that cometh. Here in this shrine may Dawn and Night, the Daughters of Heaven, the skilful Goddesses, be seated.In your wide lap, auspicious, willing Ladies may the Gods seat them with a willing spirit. Up stands the stone, high burns the fire enkindled: Aditi's lap contains the Friendly NaturesYe Two Chief Priests who serve at this our worship, may ye, more skilled, win for us rich possessions. On our wide grass, Three Goddesses be seated: for you have we prepared and made it pleasant.May Iḷā, she whose foot drops oil, the Goddess, taste, man-like, sacrifice and well-set presents. Since thou, God Tvaṣṭar, hast made beauty perfect, since hou hast been the Aṅgirases' Companion,Willing, most wealthy, Giver of possessions, grant us the Gods’ assembly, thou who knowest. Well-knowing, binding with thy cord, bring hither, Lord of the Wood, the Deities' assembly.The God prepare and season our oblations may Heaven and Earth be gracious to my calling. Agni, bring hither Varuṇa to help us, Indra from heaven, from air's mid-realm the Maruts.On sacred grass all Holy ones be seated and let the Immortal Gods rejoice in Svāhā.

verses.sanskrit: इमां मे अग्ने समिधं जुषस्वेळस्पदे प्रति हर्या घृताचीं ।वर्ष्मन्पृथिव्याः सुदिनत्वे अह्नामूर्ध्वो भव सुक्रतो देवयज्या ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ me ǀ agne ǀ sam-ídham ǀ juṣasva ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀ práti ǀ harya ǀ ghṛtā́cīm ǀvárṣman ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ sudina-tvé ǀ áhnām ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: ENJOY, O Agni, this my Fuel, welcome the oil-filled ladle where we pour libation. Rise up for worship of the Gods, wise Agni, on the earth's height, while days are bright with beauty.
verses.wilson_translation: Graciously accept,Agni, this my fuel (plural ced) on the plural ce of libation (the altar); delight in thebutter-laden (spoon); most wise, rise up upon the lofty plural ce of the earth for the propitiousness of the daysthrough the worship of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: ENJOY, O Agni, this my Fuel, welcome the oil-filled ladle where we pour libation. Rise up for worship of the Gods, wise Agni, on the earth's height, while days are bright with beauty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ देवानामग्रयावेह यातु नराशंसो विश्वरूपेभिरश्वैः ।ऋतस्य पथा नमसा मियेधो देवेभ्यो देवतमः सुषूदत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ agra-yā́vā ǀ ihá ǀ yātu ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ viśvá-rūpebhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ pathā́ ǀ námasā ǀ miyédhaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ devá-tamaḥ ǀ susūdat ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he who goes before the Gods come hither with steeds whose shapes are varied, Narasarhsa. May he, most Godlike, speed our offered viands with homage God-ward on the path of Order.
verses.wilson_translation: May Narāśaṃsa, the preceder of the gods, come here with his horses of various forms; deserving ofadoration, chief of the gods, may he effuse (oblations) to the gods by the path of the sacrifice with praise.
verses.griffith_verse: May he who goes before the Gods come hither with steeds whose shapes are varied, Narasarhsa. May he, most Godlike, speed our offered viands with homage God-ward on the path of Order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शश्वत्तममीळते दूत्याय हविष्मंतो मनुष्यासो अग्निं ।वहिष्ठैरश्वैः सुवृता रथेना देवान्वक्षि नि षदेह होता ॥
verses.transliteration: śaśvat-tamám ǀ īḷate ǀ dūtyā́ya ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́saḥ ǀ agním ǀváhiṣṭhaiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀ ā́ ǀ devā́n ǀ vakṣi ǀ ní ǀ sada ǀ ihá ǀ hótā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men with oblations laud most constant Agni, and pray him to perform an envoy's duty. With lightly-rolling car and best draught-horses, bring the Gods hither and sit down as Hotar.
verses.wilson_translation: Men offering oblations adore the eternal Agnito (induce him to perform) the duty of messenger (to thegods); do you with your stalwart draught horses and your well-turning chariots bear (our offering) to the gods,and sit down here as the ministrant priest.
verses.griffith_verse: Men with oblations laud most constant Agni, and pray him to perform an envoy's duty. With lightly-rolling car and best draught-horses, bring the Gods hither and sit down as Hotar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि प्रथतां देवजुष्टं तिरश्चा दीर्घं द्राघ्मा सुरभि भूत्वस्मे ।अहेळता मनसा देव बर्हिरिंद्रज्येष्ठाँ उशतो यक्षि देवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ prathatām ǀ devá-juṣṭam ǀ tiraścā́ ǀ dīrghám ǀ drāghmā́ ǀ surabhí ǀ bhūtu ǀ asmé íti ǀáheḷatā ǀ mánasā ǀ deva ǀ barhiḥ ǀ índra-jyeṣṭhān ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ yakṣi ǀ devā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the delight of Gods spread out transversely: may it be with us long in length and fragrant. O Holy Grass divine, with friendly spirit bring thou the willing Gods whose Chief is Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: May our (sacred grass) acceptable to the gods, twining crookedly be stretched out, may it be long,lengthy, and fragrant; with mind free from wrath, divine Barhis, offer worship to the gods desiring (the sacrifice),of whom Indrais the chief.
verses.griffith_verse: May the delight of Gods spread out transversely: may it be with us long in length and fragrant. O Holy Grass divine, with friendly spirit bring thou the willing Gods whose Chief is Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवो वा सानु स्पृशता वरीयः पृथिव्या वा मात्रया वि श्रयध्वं ।उशतीर्द्वारो महिना महद्भिर्देवं रथं रथयुर्धारयध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ vā ǀ sā́nu ǀ spṛśáta ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ vā ǀ mā́trayā ǀ ví ǀ śrayadhvam ǀuśatī́ḥ ǀ dvāraḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ devám ǀ rátham ǀ ratha-yúḥ ǀ dhārayadhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Touch ye the far-extending height of heaven or spring apart to suit the wide earth's measure. Yearning, ye Doors, with those sublime in greatness, seize eagerly the heavenly Car that cometh.
verses.wilson_translation: Be in contact, doors, with the lofty height of heaven, or expand according to the measure of the earth;desiring the gods, desiring a chariot, sustain without might the shining chariot (that is mounted) by the mightygods.
verses.griffith_verse: Touch ye the far-extending height of heaven or spring apart to suit the wide earth's measure. Yearning, ye Doors, with those sublime in greatness, seize eagerly the heavenly Car that cometh.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवी दिवो दुहितरा सुशिल्पे उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।आ वां देवास उशती उशंत उरौ सीदंतु सुभगे उपस्थे ॥
verses.transliteration: devī́ íti ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitárā ǀ suśilpé íti su-śilpé ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ sadatām ǀ ní ǀ yónau ǀā́ ǀ vām ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ uśatī íti ǀ uśántaḥ ǀ uráu ǀ sīdantu ǀ subhage íti su-bhage ǀ upá-sthe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here in this shrine may Dawn and Night, the Daughters of Heaven, the skilful Goddesses, be seated. In your wide lap, auspicious, willing Ladies may the Gods seat them with a willing spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: Radiant daughters of heaven, Dawn and Night, sit down on the plural ce of sacrifice; O you, who aredesirous and possessed of affluence, may the gods desirous (of oblations) sit down on your spacious lap.
verses.griffith_verse: Here in this shrine may Dawn and Night, the Daughters of Heaven, the skilful Goddesses, be seated. In your wide lap, auspicious, willing Ladies may the Gods seat them with a willing spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वो ग्रावा बृहदग्निः समिद्धः प्रिया धामान्यदितेरुपस्थे ।पुरोहितावृत्विजा यज्ञे अस्मिन्विदुष्टरा द्रविणमा यजेथां ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ grā́vā ǀ bṛhát ǀ agníḥ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ priyā́ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ áditeḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀpuráḥ-hitau ǀ ṛtvijā ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀ vidúḥ-tarā ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ā́ ǀ yajethām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Up stands the stone, high burns the fire enkindled: Aditi's lap contains the Friendly Natures Ye Two Chief Priests who serve at this our worship, may ye, more skilled, win for us rich possessions.
verses.wilson_translation: (When) the grinding-stone is uplifted, the mighty Agnikindled, the acceptable vessels (ready) on thelap of earth; (then), most learned priests, who take the foremost plural ce, bestow wealth upon us at this sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Up stands the stone, high burns the fire enkindled: Aditi's lap contains the Friendly Natures Ye Two Chief Priests who serve at this our worship, may ye, more skilled, win for us rich possessions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरिदं वरीय आ सीदत चकृमा वः स्योनं ।मनुष्वद्यज्ञं सुधिता हवींषीळा देवी घृतपदी जुषंत ॥
verses.transliteration: tísraḥ ǀ devīḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ idám ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sīdata ǀ cakṛmá ǀ vaḥ ǀ syonám ǀmanuṣvát ǀ yajñám ǀ sú-dhitā ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ íḷā ǀ devī́ ǀ ghṛtá-padī ǀ juṣanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: On our wide grass, Three Goddesses be seated: for you have we prepared and made it pleasant. May Iḷā, she whose foot drops oil, the Goddess, taste, man-like, sacrifice and well-set presents.
verses.wilson_translation: Sit down, you three goddesses, upon this broadbarhis, we have spread it out for you; Iḷā, radiant(Sarasvatī) and bright-footed (bhāratī) accept our sacrifice and well-presented oblations as if they were Manu's.
verses.griffith_verse: On our wide grass, Three Goddesses be seated: for you have we prepared and made it pleasant. May Iḷā, she whose foot drops oil, the Goddess, taste, man-like, sacrifice and well-set presents.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देव त्वष्टर्यद्ध चारुत्वमानड्यदंगिरसामभवः सचाभूः ।स देवानां पाथ उप प्र विद्वाँ उशन्यक्षि द्रविणोदः सुरत्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: déva ǀ tvaṣṭaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ cāru-tvám ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ yát ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ ábhavaḥ ǀ sacā-bhū́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ vidvā́n ǀ uśán ǀ yakṣi ǀ draviṇaḥ-daḥ ǀ su-rátnaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Since thou, God Tvaṣṭar, hast made beauty perfect, since hou hast been the Aṅgirases' Companion, Willing, most wealthy, Giver of possessions, grant us the Gods’ assembly, thou who knowest.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Tvaṣṭā, since you have attained to beauty (through our oblations), and have become theassociate of the Aṅgirasas, do you, the bestower of wealth, possessed of precious treasure, and knowing (towhom each portion belongs), offer the food of the gods (to them).
verses.griffith_verse: Since thou, God Tvaṣṭar, hast made beauty perfect, since hou hast been the Aṅgirases' Companion, Willing, most wealthy, Giver of possessions, grant us the Gods’ assembly, thou who knowest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् ।स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥
verses.transliteration: vánaspate ǀ raśanáyā ǀ ni-yū́ya ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vakṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǀsvádāti ǀ deváḥ ǀ kṛṇávat ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ ávatām ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ hávam ǀ me ǁ
verses.english_translation: Well-knowing, binding with thy cord, bring hither, Lord of the Wood, the Deities' assembly. The God prepare and season our oblations may Heaven and Earth be gracious to my calling.
verses.wilson_translation: Vanaspati, who are intelligent, having fastened it with a rope, convey the food of the gods; may thedivine (Vanaspati) taste it, may he take the oblations (to the gods); may heaven and earth protect my invocatioṇ
verses.griffith_verse: Well-knowing, binding with thy cord, bring hither, Lord of the Wood, the Deities' assembly. The God prepare and season our oblations may Heaven and Earth be gracious to my calling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इंद्रं दिवो मरुतो अंतरिक्षात् ।सीदंतु बर्हिर्विश्व आ यजत्राः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ agne ǀ vaha ǀ váruṇam ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ naḥ ǀ índram ǀ diváḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ antárikṣāt ǀsī́dantu ǀ barhíḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ā́ ǀ yájatrāḥ ǀ svā́hā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ mādayantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, bring hither Varuṇa to help us, Indra from heaven, from air's mid-realm the Maruts. On sacred grass all Holy ones be seated and let the Immortal Gods rejoice in Svāhā.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring,Agni, to our sacrifice Varuṇaand Indrafrom heaven, and the Marutsfrom the firmament, maythe adorable universal gods sit down on the sacred grass, and may the immortal deities rejoice in (the oblationpresented with) thesvāhā.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, bring hither Varuṇa to help us, Indra from heaven, from air's mid-realm the Maruts. On sacred grass all Holy ones be seated and let the Immortal Gods rejoice in Svāhā.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXI. Jnanam
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHEN-men, Bṛhaspati, giving names to objects, sent out Vāk's first and earliest utterances,All that was excellent and spotless, treasured within them, was disclosed through their affection. Where, like men cleansing corn-flour in a cribble, the wise in spirit have created language,Friends see and recognize the marks of friendship: their speech retains the blessed sign imprinted. With sacrifice the trace of Vāk they foIlowed, and found her harbouring within the Ṛṣis.They brought her, dealt her forth in many places: seven singers make her tones resound in concert. One man hath ne’er seen Vāk, and yet he seeth: one man hath hearing but hath never heard her.But to another hath she shown her beauty as a fond well-dressed woman to her husband. One man they call a laggard, dull in friendship: they never urge him on to deeds of valour.He wanders on in profitless illusion: the Voice he heard yields neither fruit,nor blossom. No part in Vāk hath he who hath abandoned his own dear friend who knows the truth of friendship.Even if he hears her still in vain he listens: naught knows he of the path of righteous action. Unequal in the quickness of their spirit are friends endowed alike with eyes and hearing.Some look like tanks that reach the mouth or shoulder, others like pools of water fit to bathe in. When friendly Brahmans sacrifice together with mental impulse which the heart hath fashioned,They leave one far behind through their attainments, and some who count as Brahmans wander elsewhere. Those men who step not back and move not forward, nor Brahmans nor preparers of libations,Having attained to Vāk in sinful fashion spin out their thread in ignorance like spinsters. All friends are joyful in the friend who cometh in triumph, having conquered in assembly.He is their blame-averter, food-provider prepared is he and fit for deed of vigour. One plies his constant task reciting verses. one sings the holy psalm in Sakvari measures.One more, the Brahman, tells the lore of being, and one lays down the rules of sacrificing.

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यत्प्रैरत नामधेयं दधानाः ।यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्प्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ prathamám ǀ vācáḥ ǀ ágram ǀ yát ǀ prá ǀ áirata ǀ nāma-dhéyam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀyát ǀ eṣām ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ yát ǀ ariprám ǀ ā́sīt ǀ preṇā́ ǀ tát ǀ eṣām ǀ ní-hitam ǀ gúhā ǀ āvíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHEN-men, Bṛhaspati, giving names to objects, sent out Vāk's first and earliest utterances, All that was excellent and spotless, treasured within them, was disclosed through their affection.
verses.wilson_translation: That,Bṛhaspati, is the best (part) of speech which those giving a name (to objects) first utter; thatwhich was the best of those (words) and free from defect, (Sarasvatī) reveals it though secretly imparted, bymeans of affection.
verses.griffith_verse: WHEN-men, Bṛhaspati, giving names to objects, sent out Vāk's first and earliest utterances, All that was excellent and spotless, treasured within them, was disclosed through their affection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सक्तुमिव तितउना पुनंतो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमक्रत ।अत्रा सखायः सख्यानि जानते भद्रैषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ॥
verses.transliteration: sáktum-iva ǀ títa-unā ǀ punántaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ vā́cam ǀ ákrata ǀátra ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ sakhyā́ni ǀ jānate ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ lakṣmī́ḥ ǀ ní-hitā ǀ ádhi ǀ vācí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where, like men cleansing corn-flour in a cribble, the wise in spirit have created language, Friends see and recognize the marks of friendship: their speech retains the blessed sign imprinted.
verses.wilson_translation: When the wise create Speech through wisdom winnowing (it) as (men winnow) barley with a sieve,then friends know friendship; good fortune is plural ced upon their word.
verses.griffith_verse: Where, like men cleansing corn-flour in a cribble, the wise in spirit have created language, Friends see and recognize the marks of friendship: their speech retains the blessed sign imprinted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायंतामन्वविंदन्नृषिषु प्रविष्टां ।तामाभृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवंते ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñéna ǀ vācáḥ ǀ pada-vī́yam ǀ āyan ǀ tā́m ǀ ánu ǀ avindan ǀ ṛ́ṣiṣu ǀ prá-viṣṭām ǀtā́m ǀ ā-bhṛ́tya ǀ ví ǀ adadhuḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ tā́m ǀ saptá ǀ rebhā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ navante ǁ
verses.english_translation: With sacrifice the trace of Vāk they foIlowed, and found her harbouring within the Ṛṣis. They brought her, dealt her forth in many places: seven singers make her tones resound in concert.
verses.griffith_verse: With sacrifice the trace of Vāk they foIlowed, and found her harbouring within the Ṛṣis. They brought her, dealt her forth in many places: seven singers make her tones resound in concert.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वः पश्यन्न ददर्श वाचमुत त्वः शृण्वन्न शृणोत्येनां ।उतो त्वस्मै तन्वं वि सस्रे जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvaḥ ǀ páśyan ǀ ná ǀ dadarśa ǀ vā́cam ǀ utá ǀ tvaḥ ǀ śṛṇván ǀ ná ǀ śṛṇoti ǀ enām ǀutó íti ǀ tvasmai ǀ tanvám ǀ ví ǀ sasre ǀ jāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ uśatī́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: One man hath ne’er seen Vāk, and yet he seeth: one man hath hearing but hath never heard her. But to another hath she shown her beauty as a fond well-dressed woman to her husband.
verses.wilson_translation: One (man) indeed seeing Speech has not seen her; another (man) hearing her has not heard her; butto another she delivers her person n as a loving wife well-attired presents herself to her husband.
verses.griffith_verse: One man hath ne’er seen Vāk, and yet he seeth: one man hath hearing but hath never heard her. But to another hath she shown her beauty as a fond well-dressed woman to her husband.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत त्वं सख्ये स्थिरपीतमाहुर्नैनं हिन्वंत्यपि वाजिनेषु ।अधेन्वा चरति माययैष वाचं शुश्रुवाँ अफलामपुष्पां ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ tvam ǀ sakhyé ǀ sthirá-pītam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ enam ǀ hinvanti ǀ ápi ǀ vā́jineṣu ǀádhenvā ǀ carati ǀ māyáyā ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ śuśru-vā́n ǀ aphalā́m ǀ apuṣpā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: One man they call a laggard, dull in friendship: they never urge him on to deeds of valour. He wanders on in profitless illusion: the Voice he heard yields neither fruit,nor blossom.
verses.wilson_translation: They call one man firmly established in the friendship (of Speech), they do not exclude him from (thesociety of) the powerful (in knowledge); another wanders with an illusion that is barren, bearing Speech that iswithout fruit, without flowers.
verses.griffith_verse: One man they call a laggard, dull in friendship: they never urge him on to deeds of valour. He wanders on in profitless illusion: the Voice he heard yields neither fruit,nor blossom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्तित्याज सचिविदं सखायं न तस्य वाच्यपि भागो अस्ति ।यदीं शृणोत्यलकं शृणोति नहि प्रवेद सुकृतस्य पंथां ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tityā́ja ǀ saci-vídam ǀ sákhāyam ǀ ná ǀ tásya ǀ vācí ǀ ápi ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ asti ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ śṛṇóti ǀ álakam ǀ śṛṇoti ǀ nahí ǀ pra-véda ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǁ
verses.english_translation: No part in Vāk hath he who hath abandoned his own dear friend who knows the truth of friendship. Even if he hears her still in vain he listens: naught knows he of the path of righteous action.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has abandoned the friend who knows the duty of a friend, in his speech there is not a particle(of sense); what he hears, he hears amiss; for he knows not the path of righteousness.
verses.griffith_verse: No part in Vāk hath he who hath abandoned his own dear friend who knows the truth of friendship. Even if he hears her still in vain he listens: naught knows he of the path of righteous action.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अक्षण्वंतः कर्णवंतः सखायो मनोजवेष्वसमा बभूवुः ।आदघ्नास उपकक्षास उ त्वे ह्रदा इव स्नात्वा उ त्वे ददृश्रे ॥
verses.transliteration: akṣaṇ-vántaḥ ǀ kárṇa-vantaḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ manaḥ-javéṣu ǀ ásamāḥ ǀ babhūvuḥ ǀādaghnā́saḥ ǀ upa-kakṣā́saḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǀ hradā́ḥ-iva ǀ snā́tvāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǀ dadṛśre ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unequal in the quickness of their spirit are friends endowed alike with eyes and hearing. Some look like tanks that reach the mouth or shoulder, others like pools of water fit to bathe in.
verses.wilson_translation: Friends possessing eyes, possessing ears, were (yet) unequal in mental apprehension; some seemedlike pools reaching to the mouth, others reaching to the loins, others like pools in which one can bathe.
verses.griffith_verse: Unequal in the quickness of their spirit are friends endowed alike with eyes and hearing. Some look like tanks that reach the mouth or shoulder, others like pools of water fit to bathe in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हृदा तष्टेषु मनसो जवेषु यद्ब्राह्मणाः संयजंते सखायः ।अत्राह त्वं वि जहुर्वेद्याभिरोहब्रह्माणो वि चरंत्यु त्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: hṛdā́ ǀ taṣṭéṣu ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ javéṣu ǀ yát ǀ brāhmaṇā́ḥ ǀ sam-yájante ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ tvam ǀ ví ǀ jahuḥ ǀ vedyā́bhiḥ ǀ óha-brahmāṇaḥ ǀ ví ǀ caranti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǁ
verses.english_translation: When friendly Brahmans sacrifice together with mental impulse which the heart hath fashioned, They leave one far behind through their attainments, and some who count as Brahmans wander elsewhere.
verses.wilson_translation: Although Brāhmaṇaswho are friends concur in the mental apprehensions which are conceived bythe heart (of the wise), yet in this (assembly) they abandon one man (to ignorance of the sciences) that are to beknown, others again who are reckoned as Brāhmaṇas (wander at will in the meanings of the Veda).
verses.griffith_verse: When friendly Brahmans sacrifice together with mental impulse which the heart hath fashioned, They leave one far behind through their attainments, and some who count as Brahmans wander elsewhere.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमे ये नार्वाङ्न परश्चरंति न ब्राह्मणासो न सुतेकरासः ।त एते वाचमभिपद्य पापया सिरीस्तंत्रं तन्वते अप्रजज्ञयः ॥
verses.transliteration: imé ǀ yé ǀ ná ǀ arvā́k ǀ ná ǀ paráḥ ǀ cáranti ǀ ná ǀ brāhmaṇā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ suté-karāsaḥ ǀté ǀ eté ǀ vā́cam ǀ abhi-pádya ǀ pāpáyā ǀ sirī́ḥ ǀ tántram ǀ tanvate ǀ ápra-jajñayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those men who step not back and move not forward, nor Brahmans nor preparers of libations, Having attained to Vāk in sinful fashion spin out their thread in ignorance like spinsters.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who do not walk (with the Brāhmaṇas) in this lower world not (with the gods) in the upperworld-- they are neither Brāhmaṇas nor offerers of libations; they, devoid of wisdom, attaining Speech, havingsin producing (Speech), becoming plural ughmen pursue agriculture.
verses.griffith_verse: Those men who step not back and move not forward, nor Brahmans nor preparers of libations, Having attained to Vāk in sinful fashion spin out their thread in ignorance like spinsters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे नंदंति यशसागतेन सभासाहेन सख्या सखायः ।किल्बिषस्पृत्पितुषणिर्ह्येषामरं हितो भवति वाजिनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: sárve ǀ nandanti ǀ yaśásā ǀ ā́-gatena ǀ sabhā-sāhéna ǀ sákhyā ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀkilbiṣa-spṛ́t ǀ pitu-sániḥ ǀ hí ǀ eṣām ǀ áram ǀ hitáḥ ǀ bhávati ǀ vā́jināya ǁ
verses.english_translation: All friends are joyful in the friend who cometh in triumph, having conquered in assembly. He is their blame-averter, food-provider prepared is he and fit for deed of vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: All frinends rejoice when the friendly (libation), the support of the assembly (of the priests), has arrived(at the sacrifice); for (Soma), the remover of iniquity, the giver of sustenance, being plural ced (in the vessels), issufficient for their invigoration.
verses.griffith_verse: All friends are joyful in the friend who cometh in triumph, having conquered in assembly. He is their blame-averter, food-provider prepared is he and fit for deed of vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋचां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान्गायत्रं त्वो गायति शक्वरीषु ।ब्रह्मा त्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिमीत उ त्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛcā́m ǀ tvaḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ āste ǀ pupuṣvā́n ǀ gāyatrám ǀ tvaḥ ǀ gāyati ǀ śákvarīṣu ǀbrahmā́ ǀ tvaḥ ǀ vádati ǀ jāta-vidyā́m ǀ yajñásya ǀ mā́trām ǀ ví ǀ mimīte ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: One plies his constant task reciting verses. one sings the holy psalm in Sakvari measures. One more, the Brahman, tells the lore of being, and one lays down the rules of sacrificing.
verses.wilson_translation: One (the Hotā) is diligent in the repitition of the verses (of the Ṛk); another (the Udgātā) chantsthe Gāyatra(the Sāman) in the Śakvarī metre; another the Brahmadeclares the knowledge of what is to bedone; another (the Adhvaryu) measures the materials of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: One plies his constant task reciting verses. one sings the holy psalm in Sakvari measures. One more, the Brahman, tells the lore of being, and one lays down the rules of sacrificing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXII. The Gods.
hymns.anukramani: ९ लौक्यो बृहस्पतिः, बृहस्पतिरांगिरसो वा, दाक्षायणी अदितिर्वा। देवाः। अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET US with tuneful skill proclaim these generations of the Gods,That one may see them when these hymns are chanted in a future age. These Brahmaṇaspati produced with blast and smelting, like a Smith,Existence, in an earlier age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang. Existence, in the earliest age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang.Thereafter were the regions born. This sprang from the Productive Power. Earth sprang from the Productive Power the regions from the earth were born.Dakṣa was born of Aditi, and Aditi was Dakṣa's Child. For Aditi, O Dakṣa, she who is thy Daughter, was brought forth.After her were the blessed Gods born sharers of immortal life. When ye, O Gods, in yonder deep closeclasping one another stood,Thence, as of dancers, from your feet a thickening cloud of dust arose. When, O ye Gods, like Yatis, ye caused all existing things to grow,Then ye brought Sūrya forward who was lying hidden in the sea. Eight are the Sons of Adid who from her body sprang to life.With seven she went to meet the Gods she cast Martanda far away. So with her Seven Sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age.She brought Martanda thitherward to spring to life and die again.

verses.sanskrit: देवानां नु वयं जाना प्र वोचाम विपन्यया ।उक्थेषु शस्यमानेषु यः पश्यादुत्तरे युगे ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ nú ǀ vayám ǀ jā́nā ǀ prá ǀ vocāma ǀ vipanyáyā ǀukthéṣu ǀ śasyámāneṣu ǀ yáḥ ǀ páśyāt ǀ út-tare ǀ yugé ǁ
verses.english_translation: LET US with tuneful skill proclaim these generations of the Gods, That one may see them when these hymns are chanted in a future age.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us proclaim with a clear voice the genitive rations of the gods (the divine company), who, when theirpraises are recited, look (favourably on the worshipper) in this latter age.
verses.griffith_verse: LET US with tuneful skill proclaim these generations of the Gods, That one may see them when these hymns are chanted in a future age.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणस्पतिरेता सं कर्मार इवाधमत् ।देवानां पूर्व्ये युगेऽसतः सदजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ etā́ ǀ sám ǀ karmā́raḥ-iva ǀ adhamat ǀdevā́nām ǀ pūrvyé ǀ yugé ǀ ásataḥ ǀ sát ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: These Brahmaṇaspati produced with blast and smelting, like a Smith, Existence, in an earlier age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang.
verses.wilson_translation: Brahmaṇaspatifilled these (genitive rations of the gods) with breath as a blacksmith (his bellows); in thefirst age of the gods the existent was born of the non-existent.
verses.griffith_verse: These Brahmaṇaspati produced with blast and smelting, like a Smith, Existence, in an earlier age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवानां युगे प्रथमेऽसतः सदजायत ।तदाशा अन्वजायंत तदुत्तानपदस्परि ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ yugé ǀ prathamé ǀ ásataḥ ǀ sát ǀ ajāyata ǀtát ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ajāyanta ǀ tát ǀ uttāná-padaḥ ǀ pári ǁ
verses.english_translation: Existence, in the earliest age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang. Thereafter were the regions born. This sprang from the Productive Power.
verses.wilson_translation: In the firsst age of the gods the existent was born of the non- existent; after that the quarters (of thehorizon) were born, and after them the upward-growing (trees).
verses.griffith_verse: Existence, in the earliest age of Gods, from Non-existence sprang. Thereafter were the regions born. This sprang from the Productive Power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूर्जज्ञ उत्तानपदो भुव आशा अजायंत ।अदितेर्दक्षो अजायत दक्षाद्वदितिः परि ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ḥ ǀ jajñe ǀ uttāná-padaḥ ǀ bhuváḥ ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ ajāyanta ǀáditeḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ ajāyata ǀ dákṣāt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ áditiḥ ǀ pári ǁ
verses.english_translation: Earth sprang from the Productive Power the regions from the earth were born. Dakṣa was born of Aditi, and Aditi was Dakṣa's Child.
verses.wilson_translation: The earth was born from the upward-growing (tree), the quarters were born from the earth; Dakṣawas born from Aditi, and afterwards Aditi from Dakṣa.
verses.griffith_verse: Earth sprang from the Productive Power the regions from the earth were born. Dakṣa was born of Aditi, and Aditi was Dakṣa's Child.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अदितिर्ह्यजनिष्ट दक्ष या दुहिता तव ।तां देवा अन्वजायंत भद्रा अमृतबंधवः ॥
verses.transliteration: áditiḥ ǀ hí ǀ ájaniṣṭa ǀ dákṣa ǀ yā́ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ táva ǀtā́m ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ajāyanta ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́ta-bandhavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For Aditi, O Dakṣa, she who is thy Daughter, was brought forth. After her were the blessed Gods born sharers of immortal life.
verses.wilson_translation: Aditi, who was your daughter,Dakṣa, was born; after her the gods were born adorable, freed from thebonds of death.
verses.griffith_verse: For Aditi, O Dakṣa, she who is thy Daughter, was brought forth. After her were the blessed Gods born sharers of immortal life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्देवा अदः सलिले सुसंरब्धा अतिष्ठत ।अत्रा वो नृत्यतामिव तीव्रो रेणुरपायत ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ devāḥ ǀ adáḥ ǀ salilé ǀ sú-saṃrabdhāḥ ǀ átiṣṭhata ǀátra ǀ vaḥ ǀ nṛ́tyatām-iva ǀ tīvráḥ ǀ reṇúḥ ǀ ápa ǀ āyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: When ye, O Gods, in yonder deep closeclasping one another stood, Thence, as of dancers, from your feet a thickening cloud of dust arose.
verses.wilson_translation: When, goeds, your abode in this pool well-arranged, then a pungent dust went forth from you as if youwere dancing.
verses.griffith_verse: When ye, O Gods, in yonder deep closeclasping one another stood, Thence, as of dancers, from your feet a thickening cloud of dust arose.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्देवा यतयो यथा भुवनान्यपिन्वत ।अत्रा समुद्र आ गूळ्हमा सूर्यमजभर्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ devāḥ ǀ yátayaḥ ǀ yathā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ ápinvata ǀátra ǀ samudré ǀ ā́ ǀ gūḷhám ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ajabhartana ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, O ye Gods, like Yatis, ye caused all existing things to grow, Then ye brought Sūrya forward who was lying hidden in the sea.
verses.wilson_translation: When, gods, you filled the worlds (with your radiance) as clouds (fill the earth with rain), then youbrought forth the wun hidden in the ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: When, O ye Gods, like Yatis, ye caused all existing things to grow, Then ye brought Sūrya forward who was lying hidden in the sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्वस्परि ।देवाँ उप प्रैत्सप्तभिः परा मार्तांडमास्यत् ॥
verses.transliteration: aṣṭáu ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ yé ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ pári ǀdevā́n ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ ait ǀ saptá-bhiḥ ǀ párā ǀ mārtāṇḍám ǀ āsyat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eight are the Sons of Adid who from her body sprang to life. With seven she went to meet the Gods she cast Martanda far away.
verses.wilson_translation: Eight sons (there were) ofĀdityawho were born from her body; she approached the gods withseven, she sent forth Mārtāṇḍaon high (TaittirīyaĀraṇyaka1.13.3)
verses.griffith_verse: Eight are the Sons of Adid who from her body sprang to life. With seven she went to meet the Gods she cast Martanda far away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं ।प्रजायै मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तांडमाभरत् ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá-bhiḥ ǀ putráiḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ ait ǀ pūrvyám ǀ yugám ǀpra-jā́yai ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ tvat ǀ púnaḥ ǀ mārtāṇḍám ǀ ā́ ǀ abharat ǁ
verses.english_translation: So with her Seven Sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age. She brought Martanda thitherward to spring to life and die again.
verses.wilson_translation: With seven sons Aditiwent to a former genitive ration, but she bore Mārtāṇḍafor the birth and death(of human beings).
verses.griffith_verse: So with her Seven Sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age. She brought Martanda thitherward to spring to life and die again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU wast born mighty for victorious valour, exulting, strongest, full of pride and courage.There, even there, the Maruts strengthened Indra when. his most rapid Mother stirred the Hero. There with fiend's ways e’en Pṛśni was seated: with much laudation they exalted Indra.As if encompassed by the Mighty-footed, from darkness, near at hand, forth came the Children. High are thy feet when on thy way thou goest: the strength thou foundest here hath lent thee vigour.Thousand hyenas in thy mouth thou holdest. O Indra, mayst thou turn the Aśvins hither. Speeding at once to sacrifice thou comest for friendship thou art bringing both Nāsatyas.Thou hadst a thousand treasures in possession. The Aśvins, O thou Hero, gave thee riches. Glad, for the race that rests on holy Order, with friends who hasten to their goal, hath IndraWith these his magic powers assailed the Dasyu: he cast away the gloomy mists, the darkness. Two of like name for him didst thou demolish, as Indra striking down the car of Uṣas.With thy beloved lofty Friends thou camest, and with the assurance of thine heart thou slewest. War-loving Namuci thou smotest, robbing the Dāsa of his magic for the Ṛṣi.For man thou madest ready pleasant pathways, paths leading as it were directly God-ward. These names of thine thou hast fulfilled completely: as Lord, thou boldest in thine arm, O Indra.In thee, through thy great might, the Gods are joyful: the roots of trees hast thou directed upward. May the sweet Soma juices make him happy to cast his quoit that lies in depth of waters.Thou from the udder which o’er earth is fastened hast poured the milk into the kine and herbage. When others call him offspring of the Courser, my meaning is that Mighty Power produced him.He came from Manyu and remained in houses: whence he hath sprung is known to Indra only. Like birds of beauteous wing the Priyamedhas, Ṛṣis, imploring, have come nigh to Indra:Dispel the darkness and fill full our vision deliver us as men whom snares entangle.

verses.sanskrit: जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुराय मंद्र ओजिष्ठो बहुलाभिमानः ।अवर्धन्निंद्रं मरुतश्चिदत्र माता यद्वीरं दधनद्धनिष्ठा ॥
verses.transliteration: jániṣṭhāḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ sáhase ǀ turā́ya ǀ mandráḥ ǀ ójiṣṭhaḥ ǀ bahulá-abhimānaḥ ǀávardhan ǀ índram ǀ marútaḥ ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀ mātā́ ǀ yát ǀ vīrám ǀ dadhánat ǀ dhániṣṭhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOU wast born mighty for victorious valour, exulting, strongest, full of pride and courage. There, even there, the Maruts strengthened Indra when. his most rapid Mother stirred the Hero.
verses.wilson_translation: You have been born, (Indra), for strength, for slaying (enemies); powerful, adorable, most mighty,extremely proud; the Marutsanimated Indra in the (Vṛtra-fight) when (his) sustaining mother sustained the hero.
verses.griffith_verse: THOU wast born mighty for victorious valour, exulting, strongest, full of pride and courage. There, even there, the Maruts strengthened Indra when. his most rapid Mother stirred the Hero.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्रुहो निषत्ता पृशनी चिदेवैः पुरू शंसेन वावृधुष्ट इंद्रं ।अभीवृतेव ता महापदेन ध्वांतात्प्रपित्वादुदरंत गर्भाः ॥
verses.transliteration: druháḥ ǀ ní-sattā ǀ pṛśanī́ ǀ cit ǀ évaiḥ ǀ purú ǀ śáṃsena ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ té ǀ índram ǀabhívṛtā-iva ǀ tā́ ǀ mahā-padéna ǀ dhvāntā́t ǀ pra-pitvā́t ǀ út ǀ aranta ǀ gárbhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: There with fiend's ways e’en Pṛśni was seated: with much laudation they exalted Indra. As if encompassed by the Mighty-footed, from darkness, near at hand, forth came the Children.
verses.wilson_translation: The material troop of (Indra) the injurer encamped around Indra, (accompanied) by the swift-moving(maruts); they animated him with abundant praise; like (cattle) penned up within a great stall, the embryonic(waters) issued from the (Vṛtra) who had arrived in the form of darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: There with fiend's ways e’en Pṛśni was seated: with much laudation they exalted Indra. As if encompassed by the Mighty-footed, from darkness, near at hand, forth came the Children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋष्वा ते पादा प्र यज्जिगास्यवर्धन्वाजा उत ये चिदत्र ।त्वमिंद्र सालावृकान्त्सहस्रमासंदधिषे अश्विना ववृत्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṣvā́ ǀ te ǀ pā́dā ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ jígāsi ǀ ávardhan ǀ vā́jāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀtvám ǀ indra ǀ sālāvṛkā́n ǀ sahásram ǀ āsán ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ aśvínā ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: High are thy feet when on thy way thou goest: the strength thou foundest here hath lent thee vigour. Thousand hyenas in thy mouth thou holdest. O Indra, mayst thou turn the Aśvins hither.
verses.wilson_translation: Vast, (Indra), are your feet; when you advance, the Vājas, and whatsoever (deities are) thereanimated you; you, Indra, hold a thousand jackals in yourmouth, may you bring back the Aśvins.
verses.griffith_verse: High are thy feet when on thy way thou goest: the strength thou foundest here hath lent thee vigour. Thousand hyenas in thy mouth thou holdest. O Indra, mayst thou turn the Aśvins hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समना तूर्णिरुप यासि यज्ञमा नासत्या सख्याय वक्षि ।वसाव्यामिंद्र धारयः सहस्राश्विना शूर ददतुर्मघानि ॥
verses.transliteration: samanā́ ǀ tū́rṇiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yāsi ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ vakṣi ǀvasā́vyām ǀ indra ǀ dhārayaḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ aśvínā ǀ śūra ǀ dadatuḥ ǀ maghā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: Speeding at once to sacrifice thou comest for friendship thou art bringing both Nāsatyas. Thou hadst a thousand treasures in possession. The Aśvins, O thou Hero, gave thee riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Hastening in battle you approach the sacrifice; you bring the two Nāsatyāsto friendship (with us);you,Indra, possess a heap of treasures, thousands (in numbers); the Aśvins, hero, gave us riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Speeding at once to sacrifice thou comest for friendship thou art bringing both Nāsatyas. Thou hadst a thousand treasures in possession. The Aśvins, O thou Hero, gave thee riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंदमान ऋतादधि प्रजायै सखिभिरिंद्र इषिरेभिरर्थं ।आभिर्हि माया उप दस्युमागान्मिहः प्र तम्रा अवपत्तमांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: mándamānaḥ ǀ ṛtā́t ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-jā́yai ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ iṣirébhiḥ ǀ ártham ǀā́ ǀ ābhiḥ ǀ hí ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dásyum ǀ ā́ ǀ ágāt ǀ míhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ tamrā́ḥ ǀ avapat ǀ támāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Glad, for the race that rests on holy Order, with friends who hasten to their goal, hath Indra With these his magic powers assailed the Dasyu: he cast away the gloomy mists, the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrarejoicing at the sacrifice accompanied by hisswift-moving riends (the Maruts, gave) wealth to thepeople; he has come with them against the Dasyuto destroy his illusions; he has scattered the dark rain-cloudsand the gloom.
verses.griffith_verse: Glad, for the race that rests on holy Order, with friends who hasten to their goal, hath Indra With these his magic powers assailed the Dasyu: he cast away the gloomy mists, the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सनामाना चिद्ध्वसयो न्यस्मा अवाहन्निंद्र उषसो यथानः ।ऋष्वैरगच्छः सखिभिर्निकामैः साकं प्रतिष्ठा हृद्या जघंथ ॥
verses.transliteration: sá-nāmānā ǀ cit ǀ dhvasayaḥ ǀ ní ǀ asmai ǀ áva ǀ ahan ǀ índraḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ánaḥ ǀṛṣváiḥ ǀ agacchaḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ ní-kāmaiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ prati-sthā́ ǀ hṛ́dyā ǀ jaghantha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Two of like name for him didst thou demolish, as Indra striking down the car of Uṣas. With thy beloved lofty Friends thou camest, and with the assurance of thine heart thou slewest.
