verses.wilson_translation: You have expelled the two of the same name, you have destroyed the Vṛtraas (he destroyed) the cartof the dawn; you advance with the mighty friends (the Maruts), who were eager (to slay the Vṛtra); youdemolished his precious limbs.
verses.griffith_verse: Two of like name for him didst thou demolish, as Indra striking down the car of Uṣas. With thy beloved lofty Friends thou camest, and with the assurance of thine heart thou slewest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं जघंथ नमुचिं मखस्युं दासं कृण्वान ऋषये विमायं ।त्वं चकर्थ मनवे स्योनान्पथो देवत्रांजसेव यानान् ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ jaghantha ǀ námucim ǀ makhasyúm ǀ dā́sam ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣaye ǀ ví-māyam ǀtvám ǀ cakartha ǀ mánave ǀ syonā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ áñjasā-iva ǀ yā́nān ǁ
verses.english_translation: War-loving Namuci thou smotest, robbing the Dāsa of his magic for the Ṛṣi. For man thou madest ready pleasant pathways, paths leading as it were directly God-ward.
verses.wilson_translation: You have slain the slave Namuciendeavouring (to disturb) the sacrifice, making his illusionspowerless against the Ṛṣi; you have made easy for Manuthe paths to the gods, so as (to make) the waysstraight.
verses.griffith_verse: War-loving Namuci thou smotest, robbing the Dāsa of his magic for the Ṛṣi. For man thou madest ready pleasant pathways, paths leading as it were directly God-ward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमेतानि पप्रिषे वि नामेशान इंद्र दधिषे गभस्तौ ।अनु त्वा देवाः शवसा मदंत्युपरिबुध्नान्वनिनश्चकर्थ ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ etā́ni ǀ papriṣe ǀ ví ǀ nā́ma ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ indra ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ gábhastau ǀánu ǀ tvā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ madanti ǀ upári-budhnān ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ cakartha ǁ
verses.english_translation: These names of thine thou hast fulfilled completely: as Lord, thou boldest in thine arm, O Indra. In thee, through thy great might, the Gods are joyful: the roots of trees hast thou directed upward.
verses.wilson_translation: You have filled these waters, you,Indra, who are the lord (of all) bear (the thunderbolt) in yourhands;the gods glorify you (who are endowed) with strength; you have made the clouds with their roots upwards.
verses.griffith_verse: These names of thine thou hast fulfilled completely: as Lord, thou boldest in thine arm, O Indra. In thee, through thy great might, the Gods are joyful: the roots of trees hast thou directed upward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चक्रं यदस्याप्स्वा निषत्तमुतो तदस्मै मध्विच्चच्छद्यात् ।पृथिव्यामतिषितं यदूधः पयो गोष्वदधा ओषधीषु ॥
verses.transliteration: cakrám ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ ap-sú ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-sattam ǀ utó íti ǀ tát ǀ asmai ǀ mádhu ǀ ít ǀ cacchadyāt ǀpṛthivyā́m ǀ áti-sitam ǀ yát ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ ádadhāḥ ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the sweet Soma juices make him happy to cast his quoit that lies in depth of waters. Thou from the udder which o’er earth is fastened hast poured the milk into the kine and herbage.
verses.wilson_translation: When his thunderbolt rode everywhere in the firmament, it also subjugated the water to him; the waterwhich is let loose upon the earth puts milk into cows and herbs.
verses.griffith_verse: May the sweet Soma juices make him happy to cast his quoit that lies in depth of waters. Thou from the udder which o’er earth is fastened hast poured the milk into the kine and herbage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वादियायेति यद्वदंत्योजसो जातमुत मन्य एनं ।मन्योरियाय हर्म्येषु तस्थौ यतः प्रजज्ञ इंद्रो अस्य वेद ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvāt ǀ iyāya ǀ íti ǀ yát ǀ vádanti ǀ ójasaḥ ǀ jātám ǀ utá ǀ manye ǀ enam ǀmanyóḥ ǀ iyāya ǀ harmyéṣu ǀ tasthau ǀ yátaḥ ǀ pra-jajñé ǀ índraḥ ǀ asya ǀ veda ǁ
verses.english_translation: When others call him offspring of the Courser, my meaning is that Mighty Power produced him. He came from Manyu and remained in houses: whence he hath sprung is known to Indra only.
verses.wilson_translation: Although (some) say he came from the horse (the sun), I know that he is the offspring of strength; hecame from wrath, he stands in the homes (of his enemies);Indraknows whence he was born.
verses.griffith_verse: When others call him offspring of the Courser, my meaning is that Mighty Power produced him. He came from Manyu and remained in houses: whence he hath sprung is known to Indra only.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयः सुपर्णा उप सेदुरिंद्रं प्रियमेधा ऋषयो नाधमानाः ।अप ध्वांतमूर्णुहि पूर्धि चक्षुर्मुमुग्ध्यस्मान्निधयेव बद्धान् ॥
verses.transliteration: váyaḥ ǀ su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ seduḥ ǀ índram ǀ priyá-medhāḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ nā́dhamānāḥ ǀápa ǀ dhvāntám ǀ ūrṇuhí ǀ pūrdhí ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ mumugdhí ǀ asmā́n ǀ nidháyā-iva ǀ baddhā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like birds of beauteous wing the Priyamedhas, Ṛṣis, imploring, have come nigh to Indra: Dispel the darkness and fill full our vision deliver us as men whom snares entangle.
verses.wilson_translation: The swift-moving well-flying (rays of the sun), living sacrifices, discerning (the future), deservingknowledge, invested Indra, dissipate the darkness, fill out the light; release us like men bound with a net.
verses.griffith_verse: Like birds of beauteous wing the Priyamedhas, Ṛṣis, imploring, have come nigh to Indra: Dispel the darkness and fill full our vision deliver us as men whom snares entangle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I AM prepared to laud with song or worship the Noble Ones who are in earth and heaven,Or Coursers who have triumphed in, the contest, or those who famed, have won the prize with glory. Their call, the call of Gods, went up to heaven: they kissed the ground with glory-seeking spirit,There where the Gods look on for happy fortune, and like the kindly heavens bestow their bounties. This is the song of those Immortal Beings who long for treasures in their full perfection.May these, completing prayers and sacrifices, bestow upon us wealth where naught is wanting. Those living men extolled thy deed, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle,Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose Sons are many and her streams past number. Sacivan, win to your assistance Indra who never bends, who overcomes his foemen.Ṛbhukṣan, Maghavan, the hymn's upholder, who, rich in food, bears man's kind friend, the thunder. Since he who won of old anew hath triumphed, Indra hath earned his name of Vṛtra-slaycr.He hath appeared, the mighty Lord of Conquest. What we would have him do let him accomplish.

verses.sanskrit: वसूनां वा चर्कृष इयक्षंधिया वा यज्ञैर्वा रोदस्योः ।अर्वंतो वा ये रयिमंतः सातौ वनुं वा ये सुश्रुणं सुश्रुतो धुः ॥
verses.transliteration: vásūnām ǀ vā ǀ carkṛṣe ǀ íyakṣan ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ vā ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ vā ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀárvantaḥ ǀ vā ǀ yé ǀ rayi-mántaḥ ǀ sātáu ǀ vanúm ǀ vā ǀ yé ǀ su-śrúṇam ǀ su-śrútaḥ ǀ dhúríti dhúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I AM prepared to laud with song or worship the Noble Ones who are in earth and heaven, Or Coursers who have triumphed in, the contest, or those who famed, have won the prize with glory.
verses.wilson_translation: Indradesiring to bestow (wealth) is attracted by the inhabitants of heaven and earth (for theacquisition) of riches, either by pious acts or by sacrifices; (he is attracted) either by those swift-moving (person ns)who acquire wealth in battle or by those who being successful (inflict) successful injury.
verses.griffith_verse: I AM prepared to laud with song or worship the Noble Ones who are in earth and heaven, Or Coursers who have triumphed in, the contest, or those who famed, have won the prize with glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हव एषामसुरो नक्षत द्यां श्रवस्यता मनसा निंसत क्षां ।चक्षाणा यत्र सुविताय देवा द्यौर्न वारेभिः कृणवंत स्वैः ॥
verses.transliteration: hávaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ nakṣata ǀ dyā́m ǀ śravasyatā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ niṃsata ǀ kṣā́m ǀcákṣāṇāḥ ǀ yátra ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́rebhiḥ ǀ kṛṇávanta ǀ sváiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Their call, the call of Gods, went up to heaven: they kissed the ground with glory-seeking spirit, There where the Gods look on for happy fortune, and like the kindly heavens bestow their bounties.
verses.wilson_translation: The animating invocation of these (Aṅgirasas) pervaded heaven; (the gods) with minds desirous offood kissed the earth; and there beholding (the lost cattle), the gods for their own benefit made (illumination) likethe sun by their glorious radiance.
verses.griffith_verse: Their call, the call of Gods, went up to heaven: they kissed the ground with glory-seeking spirit, There where the Gods look on for happy fortune, and like the kindly heavens bestow their bounties.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयमेषाममृतानां गीः सर्वताता ये कृपणंत रत्नं ।धियं च यज्ञं च साधंतस्ते नो धांतु वसव्यमसामि ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ eṣām ǀ amṛ́tānām ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀ yé ǀ kṛpáṇanta ǀ rátnam ǀdhíyam ǀ ca ǀ yajñám ǀ ca ǀ sā́dhantaḥ ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ dhāntu ǀ vasavyám ǀ ásāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the song of those Immortal Beings who long for treasures in their full perfection. May these, completing prayers and sacrifices, bestow upon us wealth where naught is wanting.
verses.wilson_translation: This (is) the praise of these immortal (Gods), who bestow wealth at the sacrifice; perfecting our praiseand sacrifice, may they bestow upon us unequalled riches.
verses.griffith_verse: This is the song of those Immortal Beings who long for treasures in their full perfection. May these, completing prayers and sacrifices, bestow upon us wealth where naught is wanting.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तत्त इंद्रायवः पनंताभि य ऊर्वं गोमंतं तितृत्सान् ।सकृत्स्वं ये पुरुपुत्रां महीं सहस्रधारां बृहतीं दुदुक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ pananta ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ ūrvám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ títṛtsān ǀsakṛt-svám ǀ yé ǀ puru-putrā́m ǀ mahī́m ǀ sahásra-dhārām ǀ bṛhatī́m ǀ dúdhukṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those living men extolled thy deed, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle, Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose Sons are many and her streams past number.
verses.wilson_translation: Your men praised (you) then,Indra, (those) who wished to break into the vast (stall) full of cattle; whomilked the extensive once-genitive rating earth, mother of many children, the showerer of thousands (of blessings).
verses.griffith_verse: Those living men extolled thy deed, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle, Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose Sons are many and her streams past number.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शचीव इंद्रमवसे कृणुध्वमनानतं दमयंतं पृतन्यून् ।ऋभुक्षणं मघवानं सुवृक्तिं भर्ता यो वज्रं नर्यं पुरुक्षुः ॥
verses.transliteration: śácī-vaḥ ǀ índram ǀ ávase ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ ánānatam ǀ damáyantam ǀ pṛtanyū́n ǀṛbhukṣáṇam ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ su-vṛktím ǀ bhártā ǀ yáḥ ǀ vájram ǀ náryam ǀ puru-kṣúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sacivan, win to your assistance Indra who never bends, who overcomes his foemen. Ṛbhukṣan, Maghavan, the hymn's upholder, who, rich in food, bears man's kind friend, the thunder.
verses.wilson_translation: Celebrators of holy rites, select for your protection Indrathe unsubdued, the tamer of hostile hosts;mighty, opulent, much glorified, who, loud-shouting, is the bearer of the thunderbolt, which is friendly to man.
verses.griffith_verse: Sacivan, win to your assistance Indra who never bends, who overcomes his foemen. Ṛbhukṣan, Maghavan, the hymn's upholder, who, rich in food, bears man's kind friend, the thunder.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्वावान पुरुतमं पुराषाळा वृत्रहेंद्रो नामान्यप्राः ।अचेति प्रासहस्पतिस्तुविष्मान्यदीमुश्मसि कर्तवे करत्तत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ vavā́na ǀ puru-támam ǀ purāṣā́ṭ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ nā́māni ǀ aprāḥ ǀáceti ǀ pra-sáhaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ uśmási ǀ kártave ǀ kárat ǀ tát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Since he who won of old anew hath triumphed, Indra hath earned his name of Vṛtra-slaycr. He hath appeared, the mighty Lord of Conquest. What we would have him do let him accomplish.
verses.wilson_translation: When Indra, the destroyer of cities, had slain the most mighty (Vṛtra), then he the Vṛtra-slayer filledthe waters; he was manifest (to all), the subduer of enemies, the lord of all, the most opulent; may he do thatwhich we desire to have done.
verses.griffith_verse: Since he who won of old anew hath triumphed, Indra hath earned his name of Vṛtra-slaycr. He hath appeared, the mighty Lord of Conquest. What we would have him do let him accomplish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXV. The Rivers.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE singer, O ye Waters in Vivasvān's place, shall tell your grandeur forth that is beyond compare.The Rivers have come forward triply, seven and seven. Sindhu in might surpasses all the streams that flow. Varuṇa cut the channels for thy forward course, O Sindhu, when thou rannest on to win the race.Thou speedest o’er precipitous ridges of the earth, when thou art Lord and Leader of these moving floods. His roar is lifted up to heaven above the earth: he puts forth endless vigour with a flash of light.Like floods of rain that fall in thunder from the cloud, so Sindhu rushes on bellowing like a bull. Like mothers to their calves, like milch kine with their milk, so, Sindhu, unto thee the roaring rivers run.Thou leadest as a warrior king thine army's wings what time thou comest in the van of these swift streams. Favour ye this my laud, O Gan!gā, Yamunā, O Sutudri, Paruṣṇī and Sarasvatī:With Asikni, Vitasta, O Marudvrdha, O Ārjīkīya with Susoma hear my call. First with Trstama thou art eager to flow forth, with Rasā, and Susartu, and with Svetya here,With Kubha; and with these, Sindhu and Mehatnu, thou seekest in thy course Krumu and Gomati. Flashing and whitely-gleaming in her mightiness, she moves along her ample volumes through the realms,Most active of the active, Sindhu unrestrained, like to a dappled mare, beautiful, fair to see. Rich in good steeds is Sindhu, rich in cars and robes, rich in gold, nobly-fashioned, rich in ample wealth.Blest Silamavati and young Urnavati invest themselves with raiment rich in store of sweets. Sindhu hath yoked her car, light-rolling, drawn by steeds, and with that car shall she win booty in this fight.So have I praised its power, mighty and unrestrained, of independent glory, roaring as it runs.

verses.sanskrit: प्र सु व आपो महिमानमुत्तमं कारुर्वोचाति सदने विवस्वतः ।प्र सप्तसप्त त्रेधा हि चक्रमुः प्र सृत्वरीणामति सिंधुरोजसा ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ vaḥ ǀ āpaḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ kārúḥ ǀ vocāti ǀ sádane ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀprá ǀ saptá-sapta ǀ tredhā́ ǀ hí ǀ cakramúḥ ǀ prá ǀ sṛ́tvarīṇām ǀ áti ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ójasā ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE singer, O ye Waters in Vivasvān's place, shall tell your grandeur forth that is beyond compare. The Rivers have come forward triply, seven and seven. Sindhu in might surpasses all the streams that flow.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters, the worshipper addresses to you excellent praise in the dwelling of the instrumental tutor of the rite;they flowed by sevens through the three (worlds); but the Sindhusurpasses (all) the (other) streams in strength.
verses.griffith_verse: THE singer, O ye Waters in Vivasvān's place, shall tell your grandeur forth that is beyond compare. The Rivers have come forward triply, seven and seven. Sindhu in might surpasses all the streams that flow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र तेऽरदद्वरुणो यातवे पथः सिंधो यद्वाजाँ अभ्यद्रवस्त्वं ।भूम्या अधि प्रवता यासि सानुना यदेषामग्रं जगतामिरज्यसि ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ aradat ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yā́tave ǀ patháḥ ǀ síndho íti ǀ yát ǀ vā́jān ǀ abhí ǀ ádravaḥ ǀ tvám ǀbhū́myāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-vátā ǀ yāsi ǀ sā́nunā ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ ágram ǀ jágatām ǀ irajyási ǁ
verses.english_translation: Varuṇa cut the channels for thy forward course, O Sindhu, when thou rannest on to win the race. Thou speedest o’er precipitous ridges of the earth, when thou art Lord and Leader of these moving floods.
verses.wilson_translation: For your course,Sindhu,Varuṇatore open a path, since you hastened towards food; you go by alofty road down upon the earth, by which (road) you reign in the sight of all worlds.
verses.griffith_verse: Varuṇa cut the channels for thy forward course, O Sindhu, when thou rannest on to win the race. Thou speedest o’er precipitous ridges of the earth, when thou art Lord and Leader of these moving floods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवि स्वनो यतते भूम्योपर्यनंतं शुष्ममुदियर्ति भानुना ।अभ्रादिव प्र स्तनयंति वृष्टयः सिंधुर्यदेति वृषभो न रोरुवत् ॥
verses.transliteration: diví ǀ svanáḥ ǀ yatate ǀ bhū́myā ǀ upári ǀ anantám ǀ śúṣmam ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ bhānúnā ǀabhrā́t-iva ǀ prá ǀ stanayanti ǀ vṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ yát ǀ éti ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ róruvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: His roar is lifted up to heaven above the earth: he puts forth endless vigour with a flash of light. Like floods of rain that fall in thunder from the cloud, so Sindhu rushes on bellowing like a bull.
verses.wilson_translation: The sound goes forth in heaven above the earth; (Sindhu) with shining wave animates his endlessspeed; as rains issue thundering from the cloud, so Sindhu (thunders) when he advances roaring like a bull.
verses.griffith_verse: His roar is lifted up to heaven above the earth: he puts forth endless vigour with a flash of light. Like floods of rain that fall in thunder from the cloud, so Sindhu rushes on bellowing like a bull.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्वा सिंधो शिशुमिन्न मातरो वाश्रा अर्षंति पयसेव धेनवः ।राजेव युध्वा नयसि त्वमित्सिचौ यदासामग्रं प्रवतामिनक्षसि ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ sindho íti ǀ śíśum ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ mātáraḥ ǀ vāśrā́ḥ ǀ arṣanti ǀ páyasā-iva ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀrā́jā-iva ǀ yúdhvā ǀ nayasi ǀ tvám ǀ ít ǀ sícau ǀ yát ǀ āsām ǀ ágram ǀ pra-vátām ǀ ínakṣasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like mothers to their calves, like milch kine with their milk, so, Sindhu, unto thee the roaring rivers run. Thou leadest as a warrior king thine army's wings what time thou comest in the van of these swift streams.
verses.wilson_translation: Like mothers crying for their sons, (the other rivers) hasten towards you,Sindhu, like cows with theirmilk; you lead your two wings like a king going to battle when you march in the van of the streams that aredescending (with you).
verses.griffith_verse: Like mothers to their calves, like milch kine with their milk, so, Sindhu, unto thee the roaring rivers run. Thou leadest as a warrior king thine army's wings what time thou comest in the van of these swift streams.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं मे गंगे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि स्तोमं सचता परुष्ण्या ।असिक्न्या मरुद्वृधे वितस्तयार्जीकीये शृणुह्या सुषोमया ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ me ǀ gaṅge ǀ yamune ǀ sarasvati ǀ śútudri ǀ stómam ǀ sacata ǀ páruṣṇi ǀ ā́ ǀasiknyā́ ǀ marut-vṛdhe ǀ vitástayā ǀ ā́rjīkīye ǀ śṛṇuhí ǀ ā́ ǀ su-sómayā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Favour ye this my laud, O Gan!gā, Yamunā, O Sutudri, Paruṣṇī and Sarasvatī: With Asikni, Vitasta, O Marudvrdha, O Ārjīkīya with Susoma hear my call.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept this my praise,Gaṅgā,Yamunā,Sarasvatī,Śutudri, Paruṣṇi,Marudvṛdhawith Asiknī,and Vitazstā; listen, Ārjikīya with Suṣomā.
verses.griffith_verse: Favour ye this my laud, O Gan!gā, Yamunā, O Sutudri, Paruṣṇī and Sarasvatī: With Asikni, Vitasta, O Marudvrdha, O Ārjīkīya with Susoma hear my call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तृष्टामया प्रथमं यातवे सजूः सुसर्त्वा रसया श्वेत्या त्या ।त्वं सिंधो कुभया गोमतीं क्रुमुं मेहत्न्वा सरथं याभिरीयसे ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛṣṭá-amayā ǀ prathamám ǀ yā́tave ǀ sa-jū́ḥ ǀ su-sártvā ǀ rasáyā ǀ śvetyā́ ǀ tyā́ ǀtvám ǀ sindho íti ǀ kúbhayā ǀ go-matī́m ǀ krúmum ǀ mehatnvā́ ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ī́yase ǁ
verses.english_translation: First with Trstama thou art eager to flow forth, with Rasā, and Susartu, and with Svetya here, With Kubha; and with these, Sindhu and Mehatnu, thou seekest in thy course Krumu and Gomati.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Sindhu, in order to reach the swift-moving Gomatī, have united, yourself first with the Tṛṣṭāmā; (now be united) with the Susartu, the Rasā, the Śveti, the Kubha, and the Mehatnu, inconjunction with which streams you do advance.
verses.griffith_verse: First with Trstama thou art eager to flow forth, with Rasā, and Susartu, and with Svetya here, With Kubha; and with these, Sindhu and Mehatnu, thou seekest in thy course Krumu and Gomati.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋजीत्येनी रुशती महित्वा परि ज्रयांसि भरते रजांसि ।अदब्धा सिंधुरपसामपस्तमाश्वा न चित्रा वपुषीव दर्शता ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛ́jītī ǀ énī ǀ rúśatī ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ pári ǀ jráyāṃsi ǀ bharate ǀ rájāṃsi ǀádabdhā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ apásām ǀ apáḥ-tamā ǀ áśvā ǀ ná ǀ citrā́ ǀ vápuṣī-iva ǀ darśatā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Flashing and whitely-gleaming in her mightiness, she moves along her ample volumes through the realms, Most active of the active, Sindhu unrestrained, like to a dappled mare, beautiful, fair to see.
verses.wilson_translation: Straight-flowing, white-coloured, bright-shining (Sindhu) bear along in its might the rapid waters; theinviolable Sindhu, the most efficacious of the efficacious, is speckled like a mare, beautiful as a handsomewoman.
verses.griffith_verse: Flashing and whitely-gleaming in her mightiness, she moves along her ample volumes through the realms, Most active of the active, Sindhu unrestrained, like to a dappled mare, beautiful, fair to see.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वश्वा सिंधुः सुरथा सुवासा हिरण्ययी सुकृता वाजिनीवती ।ऊर्णावती युवतिः सीलमावत्युताधि वस्ते सुभगा मधुवृधं ॥
verses.transliteration: su-áśvā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ su-ráthā ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǀ hiraṇyáyī ǀ sú-kṛtā ǀ vājínī-vatī ǀū́rṇā-vatī ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ sīlámā-vatī ǀ utá ǀ ádhi ǀ vaste ǀ su-bhágā ǀ madhu-vṛ́dham ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rich in good steeds is Sindhu, rich in cars and robes, rich in gold, nobly-fashioned, rich in ample wealth. Blest Silamavati and young Urnavati invest themselves with raiment rich in store of sweets.
verses.wilson_translation: The Sindhuis rich in horses, rich in chariots, rich in clothes, rich in gold ornaments, well-made, rich infood, rich inwool, ever fresh, abounding Sīlamā plural nts, and the auspicious river wears honey-growing(flowers).
verses.griffith_verse: Rich in good steeds is Sindhu, rich in cars and robes, rich in gold, nobly-fashioned, rich in ample wealth. Blest Silamavati and young Urnavati invest themselves with raiment rich in store of sweets.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुखं रथं युयुजे सिंधुरश्विनं तेन वाजं सनिषदस्मिन्नाजौ ।महान्ह्यस्य महिमा पनस्यतेऽदब्धस्य स्वयशसो विरप्शिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-khám ǀ rátham ǀ yuyuje ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ aśvínam ǀ téna ǀ vā́jam ǀ saniṣat ǀ asmín ǀ ājáu ǀmahā́n ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ panasyáte ǀ ádabdhasya ǀ svá-yaśasaḥ ǀ vi-rapśínaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sindhu hath yoked her car, light-rolling, drawn by steeds, and with that car shall she win booty in this fight. So have I praised its power, mighty and unrestrained, of independent glory, roaring as it runs.
verses.wilson_translation: Sindhuhas harnessed his easy-going, well-horsed, chariot, with it may he bring (us) food; the might ofthis inviolable, great, renowned (chariot) at this sacrifice is praised as mighty.
verses.griffith_verse: Sindhu hath yoked her car, light-rolling, drawn by steeds, and with that car shall she win booty in this fight. So have I praised its power, mighty and unrestrained, of independent glory, roaring as it runs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVI. Press-stones.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I GRASP at you when power and strength begin to dawn: bedew ye, Indra and the Maruts, Heaven and Earth,That Day and Night, in every hall of sacrifice, may wait on us and bless us when they first spring forth. Press the libation out, most excellent of all: the Pressing-stone is grasped like a hand-guided steed.So let it win the valour that subdues the foe, and the fleet courser's might that speeds to ample wealth. Juice that this Stone pours out removes defect of ours, as in old time it brought prosperity to man.At sacrifices they established holy rites on Tvaṣṭar's milk-blent juice bright with the hue of steeds. Drive ye the treacherous demons far away from us: keep Nirrti afar and banish Penury.Pour riches forth for us with troops of hero sons, and bear ye up, O Stones, the song that visits Gods. To you who are more mighty than the heavens themselves, who, finishing your task with more than Vibhvan's speed,More rapidly than Vāyu seize the Soma juice, better than Agni give us food, to you I sing. Stirred be the glorious Stones: let it press out the juice, the Stone with heavenly song that reaches up to heaven,There where the men draw forth the meath for which they long, sending their voice around in rivalry of speed. The Stones press out the Soma, swift as car-borne men, and, eager for the spoil, drain forth the sap thereofTo fill the beaker, they exhaust the udder's store, as the men purify oblations with their lips. Ye, present men, have been most skilful in your work, even ye, O Stones who pressed Soma for Indra's drink.May all ye have of fair go to the Heavenly Race, and all your treasure to the earthly worshipper.

verses.sanskrit: आ व ऋंजस ऊर्जां व्युष्टिष्विंद्रं मरुतो रोदसी अनक्तन ।उभे यथा नो अहनी सचाभुवा सदःसदो वरिवस्यात उद्भिदा ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛñjase ǀ ūrjā́m ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ índram ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ anaktana ǀubhé íti ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ áhanī íti ǀ sacā-bhúvā ǀ sádaḥ-sadaḥ ǀ varivasyā́taḥ ǀ ut-bhídā ǁ
verses.english_translation: I GRASP at you when power and strength begin to dawn: bedew ye, Indra and the Maruts, Heaven and Earth, That Day and Night, in every hall of sacrifice, may wait on us and bless us when they first spring forth.
verses.wilson_translation: I propitiate you at the commencement of the food-possessing (dawns); you reveal Indra, the Maruts,heaven and earth; both heaven and earth being united attend on us in all the chambers of sacrifice; (may they fillus) with wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: I GRASP at you when power and strength begin to dawn: bedew ye, Indra and the Maruts, Heaven and Earth, That Day and Night, in every hall of sacrifice, may wait on us and bless us when they first spring forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदु श्रेष्ठं सवनं सुनोतनात्यो न हस्तयतो अद्रिः सोतरि ।विदद्ध्यर्यो अभिभूति पौंस्यं महो राये चित्तरुते यदर्वतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ sávanam ǀ sunotana ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hásta-yataḥ ǀ ádriḥ ǀ sotári ǀvidát ǀ hí ǀ aryáḥ ǀ abhí-bhūti ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ maháḥ ǀ rāyé ǀ cit ǀ tarute ǀ yát ǀ árvataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Press the libation out, most excellent of all: the Pressing-stone is grasped like a hand-guided steed. So let it win the valour that subdues the foe, and the fleet courser's might that speeds to ample wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Pour forth this excellent libation; the stone grasped by thehandis like a horse when the grinder(effuses the Soma). The animating (worshipper) acquires virile strength overpowering (his foes) when (the stone)bestows horses for the sake of great wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Press the libation out, most excellent of all: the Pressing-stone is grasped like a hand-guided steed. So let it win the valour that subdues the foe, and the fleet courser's might that speeds to ample wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिद्ध्यस्य सवनं विवेरपो यथा पुरा मनवे गातुमश्रेत् ।गोअर्णसि त्वाष्ट्रे अश्वनिर्णिजि प्रेमध्वरेष्वध्वराँ अश��श्रयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ sávanam ǀ vivéḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ purā́ ǀ mánave ǀ gātúm ǀ áśret ǀgó-arṇasi ǀ tvāṣṭré ǀ áśva-nirniji ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ adhvarā́n ǀ aśiśrayuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Juice that this Stone pours out removes defect of ours, as in old time it brought prosperity to man. At sacrifices they established holy rites on Tvaṣṭar's milk-blent juice bright with the hue of steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May this (sacrificial) work of this grinding-stone the effusion of the Soma, spread as it went formerlyalong the path to Manu; when the son of Tvaṣṭā, hidden by the (stolen) cows, and assuming the form of ahorse, (was to be slain), the worshippers had recourse at the sacrifices to the inviolable (upper grinding-stones).
verses.griffith_verse: Juice that this Stone pours out removes defect of ours, as in old time it brought prosperity to man. At sacrifices they established holy rites on Tvaṣṭar's milk-blent juice bright with the hue of steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप हत रक्षसो भंगुरावतः स्कभायत निर्ऋतिं सेधतामतिं ।आ नो रयिं सर्ववीरं सुनोतन देवाव्यं भरत श्लोकमद्रयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ hata ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ bhaṅgurá-vataḥ ǀ skabhāyáta ǀ níḥ-ṛtim ǀ sédhata ǀ ámatim ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ sárva-vīram ǀ sunotana ǀ deva-avyám ǀ bharata ǀ ślókam ǀ adrayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drive ye the treacherous demons far away from us: keep Nirrti afar and banish Penury. Pour riches forth for us with troops of hero sons, and bear ye up, O Stones, the song that visits Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Drive away the disturbingrākṣasas; keep off Nirṛti; prohibit all malignity; effuse for us riches withmale progeny; bear, stones, the praise that delights the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Drive ye the treacherous demons far away from us: keep Nirrti afar and banish Penury. Pour riches forth for us with troops of hero sons, and bear ye up, O Stones, the song that visits Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवश्चिदा वोऽमवत्तरेभ्यो विभ्वना चिदाश्वपस्तरेभ्यः ।वायोश्चिदा सोमरभस्तरेभ्योऽग्नेश्चिदर्च पितुकृत्तरेभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ámavat-tarebhyaḥ ǀ vi-bhvánā ǀ cit ǀ āśvápaḥ-tarebhyaḥ ǀvāyóḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ sómarabhaḥ-tarebhyaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ cit ǀ arca ǀ pitukṛ́t-tarebhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To you who are more mighty than the heavens themselves, who, finishing your task with more than Vibhvan's speed, More rapidly than Vāyu seize the Soma juice, better than Agni give us food, to you I sing.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Adhvaryu) praises you who are stronger even than heaven, quicker in work that Vibhvan, morediffusive of the Somathan Vāyu, more bountiful of food than Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: To you who are more mighty than the heavens themselves, who, finishing your task with more than Vibhvan's speed, More rapidly than Vāyu seize the Soma juice, better than Agni give us food, to you I sing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भुरंतु नो यशसः सोत्वंधसो ग्रावाणो वाचा दिविता दिवित्मता ।नरो यत्र दुहते काम्यं मध्वाघोषयंतो अभितो मिथस्तुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhurántu ǀ naḥ ǀ yaśásaḥ ǀ sótu ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ vācā́ ǀ divítā ǀ divítmatā ǀnáraḥ ǀ yátra ǀ duhaté ǀ kā́myam ǀ mádhu ǀ ā-ghoṣáyantaḥ ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ mithaḥ-túraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Stirred be the glorious Stones: let it press out the juice, the Stone with heavenly song that reaches up to heaven, There where the men draw forth the meath for which they long, sending their voice around in rivalry of speed.
verses.wilson_translation: May the renowned stones bring us the effused Soma, (may they establish us) with brilliant praise inthe brilliant (Soma-sacrifice), where the priests milk forth the desirable Soma, crying out all around, and racingeach other.
verses.griffith_verse: Stirred be the glorious Stones: let it press out the juice, the Stone with heavenly song that reaches up to heaven, There where the men draw forth the meath for which they long, sending their voice around in rivalry of speed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुन्वंति सोमं रथिरासो अद्रयो निरस्य रसं गविषो दुहंति ते ।दुहंत्यूधरुपसेचनाय कं नरो हव्या न मर्जयंत आसभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: sunvánti ǀ sómam ǀ rathirā́saḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ asya ǀ rásam ǀ go-íṣaḥ ǀ duhanti ǀ té ǀduhánti ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ upa-sécanāya ǀ kám ǀ náraḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ ná ǀ marjayante ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Stones press out the Soma, swift as car-borne men, and, eager for the spoil, drain forth the sap thereof To fill the beaker, they exhaust the udder's store, as the men purify oblations with their lips.
verses.wilson_translation: The swiftly-moving grinding-stones effuse the Soma, desiring praise, they milk forth Soma; they milkforth for the spinkling (of Agni); the leaders (of rites) purify the oblations with their mouths.
verses.griffith_verse: The Stones press out the Soma, swift as car-borne men, and, eager for the spoil, drain forth the sap thereof To fill the beaker, they exhaust the udder's store, as the men purify oblations with their lips.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एते नरः स्वपसो अभूतन य इंद्राय सुनुथ सोममद्रयः ।वामंवामं वो दिव्याय धाम्ने वसुवसु वः पार्थिवाय सुन्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ naraḥ ǀ su-ápasaḥ ǀ abhūtana ǀ yé ǀ índrāya ǀ sunuthá ǀ sómam ǀ adrayaḥ ǀvāmám-vāmam ǀ vaḥ ǀ divyā́ya ǀ dhā́mne ǀ vásu-vasu ǀ vaḥ ǀ pā́rthivāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, present men, have been most skilful in your work, even ye, O Stones who pressed Soma for Indra's drink. May all ye have of fair go to the Heavenly Race, and all your treasure to the earthly worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: You stones, leaders (of rites), youu are the doers of good works; you who express the Somafor Indra,(make) all desirable wealth for the glory of heaven; you (give) all treasures to the earthly effuser.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, present men, have been most skilful in your work, even ye, O Stones who pressed Soma for Indra's drink. May all ye have of fair go to the Heavenly Race, and all your treasure to the earthly worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As with their voice from cloud they sprinkle treasure so are the wise man's liberal sacrifices.I praise their Company that merits worship as the good Martits' priest to pay them honour. The youths have wrought their ornaments for glory through many nights,—this noble band of Maruts.Like stags the Sons of Dyatis have striven onward, the Sons of Aditi grown strong like pillars. They who extend beyond the earth and heaven, by their own mass, as from the cloud spreads Sūrya;Like mighty Heroes covetous of glory, like heavenly gallants who destroy the wicked. When ye come nigh, as in the depth of waters, the earth is loosened, as it were, and shaken.This your all-feedin sacrifice approaches: come all united, fraught, as ’twere with viands. Ye are like horses fastened to the chariot poles, luminous with your beams, with splendour as at dawn;Like self-bright falcons, punishers of wicked men, like hovering birds urged forward, scattering rain around. When ye come forth, O Maruts, from the distance, from the great treasury of rich possessions,Knowing, O Vasus, boons that should be granted, even from afar drive back the men who hate us. He who, engaged in the rite's final duty brings, as a man, oblation to the Maruts,Wins him life's wealthy fulness, blest with heroes: he shall be present, too, where Gods drink Soma. For these are helps adored at sacrifices, bringing good fortune by their name Ādityas.Speeding on cars let them protect our praises, delighting in our sacrifice and worship.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्रप्रुषो न वाचा प्रुषा वसु हविष्मंतो न यज्ञा विजानुषः ।सुमारुतं न ब्रह्माणमर्हसे गणमस्तोष्येषां न शोभसे ॥
verses.transliteration: abhra-prúṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vācā́ ǀ pruṣa ǀ vásu ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yajñā́ḥ ǀ vi-jānúṣaḥ ǀsu-mā́rutam ǀ ná ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ arháse ǀ gaṇám ǀ astoṣi ǀ eṣām ǀ ná ǀ śobháse ǁ
verses.english_translation: As with their voice from cloud they sprinkle treasure so are the wise man's liberal sacrifices. I praise their Company that merits worship as the good Martits' priest to pay them honour.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts), plural ased with our praise like water-drops sent down by clouds, shower wealth; they arethe genitive rators (of the world) like sacrifices abounding with oblations; I have not praised the mighty band of Maruts (adequately) for their honour or of their glory.
verses.griffith_verse: As with their voice from cloud they sprinkle treasure so are the wise man's liberal sacrifices. I praise their Company that merits worship as the good Martits' priest to pay them honour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रिये मर्यासो अंजीँरकृण्वत सुमारुतं न पूर्वीरति क्षपः ।दिवस्पुत्रास एता न येतिर आदित्यासस्ते अक्रा न वावृधुः ॥
verses.transliteration: śriyé ǀ máryāsaḥ ǀ añjī́n ǀ akṛṇvata ǀ su-mā́rutam ǀ ná ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ áti ǀ kṣápaḥ ǀdiváḥ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ étāḥ ǀ ná ǀ yetire ǀ ādityā́saḥ ǀ té ǀ akrā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The youths have wrought their ornaments for glory through many nights,—this noble band of Maruts. Like stags the Sons of Dyatis have striven onward, the Sons of Aditi grown strong like pillars.
verses.wilson_translation: The destructive (Maruts) made ornaments for their decoration many hostile hosts cannot overcomethe band of Maruts; the moving sons of heaven do not issue forth, the swift-going sons of Aditido not increase (inglory).
verses.griffith_verse: The youths have wrought their ornaments for glory through many nights,—this noble band of Maruts. Like stags the Sons of Dyatis have striven onward, the Sons of Aditi grown strong like pillars.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ये दिवः पृथिव्या न बर्हणा त्मना रिरिच्रे अभ्रान्न सूर्यः ।पाजस्वंतो न वीराः पनस्यवो रिशादसो न मर्या अभिद्यवः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ barháṇā ǀ tmánā ǀ riricré ǀ abhrā́t ǀ ná ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀpā́jasvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ panasyávaḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who extend beyond the earth and heaven, by their own mass, as from the cloud spreads Sūrya; Like mighty Heroes covetous of glory, like heavenly gallants who destroy the wicked.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts), who through the might of heaven and earth have emerged from their own person ns asthe sun emerges from the cloud, (are) desirous of praise like powerful heroes, and radiant like men whooverpower their enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: They who extend beyond the earth and heaven, by their own mass, as from the cloud spreads Sūrya; Like mighty Heroes covetous of glory, like heavenly gallants who destroy the wicked.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युष्माकं बुध्ने अपां न यामनि विथुर्यति न मही श्रथर्यति ।विश्वप्सुर्यज्ञो अर्वागयं सु वः प्रयस्वंतो न सत्राच आ गत ॥
verses.transliteration: yuṣmā́kam ǀ budhné ǀ apā́m ǀ ná ǀ yā́mani ǀ vithuryáti ǀ ná ǀ mahī́ ǀ śratharyáti ǀviśvá-psuḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ ayám ǀ sú ǀ vaḥ ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ satrā́caḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǁ
verses.english_translation: When ye come nigh, as in the depth of waters, the earth is loosened, as it were, and shaken. This your all-feedin sacrifice approaches: come all united, fraught, as ’twere with viands.
verses.wilson_translation: In your collision, as in the transit of waters, the earth is not shaken, is not shattered; this manifoldsacrifice comes towards you; approach united as if laden with food.
verses.griffith_verse: When ye come nigh, as in the depth of waters, the earth is loosened, as it were, and shaken. This your all-feedin sacrifice approaches: come all united, fraught, as ’twere with viands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं धूर्षु प्रयुजो न रश्मिभिर्ज्योतिष्मंतो न भासा व्युष्टिषु ।श्येनासो न स्वयशसो रिशादसः प्रवासो न प्रसितासः परिप्रुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ pra-yújaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ jyótiṣmantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhāsā́ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀśyenā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ svá-yaśasaḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ pravā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ prá-sitāsaḥ ǀ pari-prúṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye are like horses fastened to the chariot poles, luminous with your beams, with splendour as at dawn; Like self-bright falcons, punishers of wicked men, like hovering birds urged forward, scattering rain around.
verses.wilson_translation: You (move along) like horses harnessed to the chariot-poles with reins; at break of day you (areendowed) with radiance like the luminaries (of heaven); you are like hawks, like the destroyers of foes, desirousof renown; you cover the ground like travellers, you move everywhere.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye are like horses fastened to the chariot poles, luminous with your beams, with splendour as at dawn; Like self-bright falcons, punishers of wicked men, like hovering birds urged forward, scattering rain around.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र यद्वहध्वे मरुतः पराकाद्यूयं महः संवरणस्य वस्वः ।विदानासो वसवो राध्यस्याराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोत ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ váhadhve ǀ marutaḥ ǀ parākā́t ǀ yūyám ǀ maháḥ ǀ sam-váraṇasya ǀ vásvaḥ ǀvidānā́saḥ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ rā́dhyasya ǀ ārā́t ǀ cit ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyota ǁ
verses.english_translation: When ye come forth, O Maruts, from the distance, from the great treasury of rich possessions, Knowing, O Vasus, boons that should be granted, even from afar drive back the men who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Maruts, you come from a distance, then,Vasus, distributors of abundant, desirable, covetedwealth, do you scatter afar our concealed foes.
verses.griffith_verse: When ye come forth, O Maruts, from the distance, from the great treasury of rich possessions, Knowing, O Vasus, boons that should be granted, even from afar drive back the men who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य उदृचि यज्ञे अध्वरेष्ठा मरुद्भ्यो न मानुषो ददाशत् ।रेवत्स वयो दधते सुवीरं स देवानामपि गोपीथे अस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ut-ṛ́ci ǀ yajñé ǀ adhvare-sthā́ḥ ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ dádāśat ǀrevát ǀ sáḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhate ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ sáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ápi ǀ go-pīthé ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who, engaged in the rite's final duty brings, as a man, oblation to the Maruts, Wins him life's wealthy fulness, blest with heroes: he shall be present, too, where Gods drink Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: The worshipper who engaged in worship at the sacrifice, accompanied with praise, presentsdonations (to the priests) as if to the Maruts, he enjoys food with riches, andmaleprogeny; may he be present atthe god'ssoma-drinking.
verses.griffith_verse: He who, engaged in the rite's final duty brings, as a man, oblation to the Maruts, Wins him life's wealthy fulness, blest with heroes: he shall be present, too, where Gods drink Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमा आदित्येन नाम्ना शंभविष्ठाः ।ते नोऽवंतु रथतूर्मनीषां महश्च यामन्नध्वरे चकानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ ū́māḥ ǀ ādityéna ǀ nā́mnā ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhāḥ ǀté ǀ naḥ ǀ avantu ǀ ratha-tū́ḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ maháḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́man ǀ adhvaré ǀ cakānā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For these are helps adored at sacrifices, bringing good fortune by their name Ādityas. Speeding on cars let them protect our praises, delighting in our sacrifice and worship.
verses.wilson_translation: May those protecting deities who are entitled to be worshipped at sacrifices, who under the name ofĀdityas are the bestowers of felicity, may they (the Maruts) accelerating their chariots, and desirous of theample (oblation), upon their arrival at the sacrificed protect our praise.
verses.griffith_verse: For these are helps adored at sacrifices, bringing good fortune by their name Ādityas. Speeding on cars let them protect our praises, delighting in our sacrifice and worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXVIII. Maruts.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Ye by your hymns are like high-thoughted singers, skilful, inviting Gods with sacrifices;Fair to behold, like Kings, with bright adornment, like spotless gallants, leaders of the people: Like fire with flashing flame, breast-bound with chains of gold, like tempest-blasts, self-moving, swift to lend your aid;As best of all foreknowers, excellent to guide, like Somas, good to guard the man who follows Law. Shakers of all, like gales of wind they travel, like tongues of burning fires in their effulgence.Mighty are they as warriors clad in armour, and, like the Fathers' prayers, Most Bounteous Givers. Like spokes of car-wheels in one nave united, ever victorious like heavenly Heroes,Shedding their precious balm like youthful suitors, they raise their voice and chant their psalm as singers. They who are fleet to travel like the noblest steeds, long to obtain the prize like bounteous charioteers,Like waters speeding on with their precipitous floods, like omniform Aṅgirases with Sāma-hymns. Born from the stream, like press-stones are the Princes, for ever like the stones that crush in pieces;Sons of a beauteous Dame, like playful children, like a great host upon the march with splendour. Like rays of Dawn, the visitors of sacrifice, they shine with ornaments as eager to be bright.Like rivers hasting on, glittering with their spears, from far away they measure out the distances. Gods, send us happiness and make us wealthy, letting us singers prosper, O ye Maruts.Bethink you of our praise and of our friendship: ye from of old have riches to vouchsafe us.

verses.sanskrit: विप्रासो न मन्मभिः स्वाध्यो देवाव्यो न यज्ञैः स्वप्नसः ।राजानो न चित्राः सुसंदृशः क्षितीनां न मर्या अरेपसः ॥
verses.transliteration: víprāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀ su-ādhyáḥ ǀ deva-avyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ su-ápnasaḥ ǀrā́jānaḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ su-sandṛ́śaḥ ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye by your hymns are like high-thoughted singers, skilful, inviting Gods with sacrifices; Fair to behold, like Kings, with bright adornment, like spotless gallants, leaders of the people:
verses.wilson_translation: They (the Maruts) are like Brāhmaṇassanctified by pious praises, they are instrumental tutors of holy riteslike the propitiators of the gods by sacrifices; decked with various ornaments, and handsome like kings, devoid ofsin like men (who are the lords) of habitations.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye by your hymns are like high-thoughted singers, skilful, inviting Gods with sacrifices; Fair to behold, like Kings, with bright adornment, like spotless gallants, leaders of the people:
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्न ये भ्राजसा रुक्मवक्षसो वातासो न स्वयुजः सद्यऊतयः ।प्रज्ञातारो न ज्येष्ठाः सुनीतयः सुशर्माणो न सोमा ऋतं यते ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ bhrā́jasā ǀ rukmá-vakṣasaḥ ǀ vā́tāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sva-yújaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ-ūtayaḥ ǀpra-jñātā́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyéṣṭhāḥ ǀ su-nītáyaḥ ǀ su-śármāṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sómāḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ yaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like fire with flashing flame, breast-bound with chains of gold, like tempest-blasts, self-moving, swift to lend your aid; As best of all foreknowers, excellent to guide, like Somas, good to guard the man who follows Law.
verses.wilson_translation: (You) who like Agni(are endowed) with splendour, who have golden ornaments upon your breasts,who like the winds (are) self-yoked, swift-moving, who like the extremely wise (are) venerable and able guides,and like the Somathe giver of delight, (do you com) to the (worshipper) going to the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Like fire with flashing flame, breast-bound with chains of gold, like tempest-blasts, self-moving, swift to lend your aid; As best of all foreknowers, excellent to guide, like Somas, good to guard the man who follows Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वातासो न ये धुनयो जिगत्नवोऽग्नीनां न जिह्वा विरोकिणः ।वर्मण्वंतो न योधाः शिमीवंतः पितॄणां न शंसाः सुरातयः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́tāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǀ jigatnávaḥ ǀ agnīnā́m ǀ ná ǀ jihvā́ḥ ǀ vi-rokíṇaḥ ǀvármaṇ-vantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yodhā́ḥ ǀ śímī-vantaḥ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsāḥ ǀ su-rātáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shakers of all, like gales of wind they travel, like tongues of burning fires in their effulgence. Mighty are they as warriors clad in armour, and, like the Fathers' prayers, Most Bounteous Givers.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Maruts), who like the winds cause (the gods) to tremble and move swift; blazing like the flames offires, (who are) the achievers of heroic deeds like warriors clad in mail; munificent donors like the praises ofancestors.
verses.griffith_verse: Shakers of all, like gales of wind they travel, like tongues of burning fires in their effulgence. Mighty are they as warriors clad in armour, and, like the Fathers' prayers, Most Bounteous Givers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रथानां न येऽराः सनाभयो जिगीवांसो न शूरा अभिद्यवः ।वरेयवो न मर्या घृतप्रुषोऽभिस्वर्तारो अर्कं न सुष्टुभः ॥
verses.transliteration: ráthānām ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ arā́ḥ ǀ sá-nābhayaḥ ǀ jigīvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śū́rāḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǀvare-yávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ ghṛta-prúṣaḥ ǀ abhi-svartā́raḥ ǀ arkám ǀ ná ǀ su-stúbhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like spokes of car-wheels in one nave united, ever victorious like heavenly Heroes, Shedding their precious balm like youthful suitors, they raise their voice and chant their psalm as singers.
verses.wilson_translation: Who (are) united to a common centre like the spokes (of the wheels) of chariots, brilliant like victoriousheroes, sprinkling water like benevolent men, sweet-voiced like men who recite praise.
verses.griffith_verse: Like spokes of car-wheels in one nave united, ever victorious like heavenly Heroes, Shedding their precious balm like youthful suitors, they raise their voice and chant their psalm as singers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वासो न ये ज्येष्ठास आशवो दिधिषवो न रथ्यः सुदानवः ।आपो न निम्नैरुदभिर्जिगत्नवो विश्वरूपा अंगिरसो न सामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ jyéṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ didhiṣávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ nimnáiḥ ǀ udá-bhiḥ ǀ jigatnávaḥ ǀ viśvá-rūpāḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who are fleet to travel like the noblest steeds, long to obtain the prize like bounteous charioteers, Like waters speeding on with their precipitous floods, like omniform Aṅgirases with Sāma-hymns.
verses.wilson_translation: Who (are) most excellent and swift like horses, lords of cars and munificent like the possessors ofwealth, swiftly moving like rivers with water flowing from a height, (accompanied) everywhere with hymns like themultiform Aṅgirasas.
verses.griffith_verse: They who are fleet to travel like the noblest steeds, long to obtain the prize like bounteous charioteers, Like waters speeding on with their precipitous floods, like omniform Aṅgirases with Sāma-hymns.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावाणो न सूरयः सिंधुमातर आदर्दिरासो अद्रयो न विश्वहा ।शिशूला न क्रीळयः सुमातरो महाग्रामो न यामन्नुत त्विषा ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ síndhu-mātaraḥ ǀ ā-dardirā́saḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ viśváhā ǀśiśū́lāḥ ǀ ná ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ su-mātáraḥ ǀ mahā-grāmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́man ǀ utá ǀ tviṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Born from the stream, like press-stones are the Princes, for ever like the stones that crush in pieces; Sons of a beauteous Dame, like playful children, like a great host upon the march with splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: Having streams for mothers like the grinding-stones which send forth moisture; ever destroying(enemies) like destructive thunderbolts; having tender mothers like sportive infants; (endowed) with splendourlike a great crowd of men in a procession.
verses.griffith_verse: Born from the stream, like press-stones are the Princes, for ever like the stones that crush in pieces; Sons of a beauteous Dame, like playful children, like a great host upon the march with splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषसां न केतवोऽध्वरश्रियः शुभंयवो नांजिभिर्व्यश्वितन् ।सिंधवो न ययियो भ्राजदृष्टयः परावतो न योजनानि ममिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣásām ǀ ná ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ adhvara-śríyaḥ ǀ śubham-yávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśvitan ǀsíndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yayíyaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yójanāni ǀ mamire ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like rays of Dawn, the visitors of sacrifice, they shine with ornaments as eager to be bright. Like rivers hasting on, glittering with their spears, from far away they measure out the distances.
verses.wilson_translation: Who, radiant in sacrifices like the rays of the dawn, shine with their ornaments like those expectant ofgood fortune, (who) swift-moving like rivers, having bright weapons, have traversed leagues like mares who havejourneyed from far, (may they come to our sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: Like rays of Dawn, the visitors of sacrifice, they shine with ornaments as eager to be bright. Like rivers hasting on, glittering with their spears, from far away they measure out the distances.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुभागान्नो देवाः कृणुता सुरत्नानस्मान्त्स्तोतॄन्मरुतो वावृधानाः ।अधि स्तोत्रस्य सख्यस्य गात सनाद्धि वो रत्नधेयानि संति ॥
verses.transliteration: su-bhāgā́n ǀ naḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ su-rátnān ǀ asmā́n ǀ stotṝ́n ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vavṛdhānā́ḥ ǀádhi ǀ stotrásya ǀ sakhyásya ǀ gāta ǀ sanā́t ǀ hí ǀ vaḥ ǀ ratna-dhéyāni ǀ sánti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, send us happiness and make us wealthy, letting us singers prosper, O ye Maruts. Bethink you of our praise and of our friendship: ye from of old have riches to vouchsafe us.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine Maruts, magnified (by our praise), render us, your praisers, prosperous and opulent; come tothis friendly laudation, for your precious bounties have been long (bestowed upon us).
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, send us happiness and make us wealthy, letting us singers prosper, O ye Maruts. Bethink you of our praise and of our friendship: ye from of old have riches to vouchsafe us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXIX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ७ सौचीकोऽग्निर्वैश्वानरो वा, सप्तिर्वाजंभरो वा। अग्निः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I HAVE beheld the might of this Great Being. Immortal in the midst of tribes of mortals.His jaws now open and now shut together: much they devour, insatiately chewing. His eyes are turned away, his head is hidden: unsated with his tongue he eats the fuel.With hands upraised, with reverence in the houses, for him they quickly bring his food together. Seeking, as ’twere, his Mother's secret bosom, he, like a child, creeps on through wide-spread bushes.One he finds glowing like hot food made ready, and kissing deep within the earth's recmes. This holy Law I tell you, Earth and Heaven: the Infant at his birth dovours his Parents.No knowledge of the God have I, a mortal. Yea, Agni knoweth best, for he hath wisdom. This man who quickly gives him food, who offers his gifts of oil and butter and supports him, -Him with his thousand eyes he closely looks on: thou showest him thy face from all sides, Agni. Agni, hast thou committed sin or treason among the Gods? In ignorance I ask thee.Playing, not playing, he gold-hued and toothless, hath cut his food up as the knife a victim. He born in wood hath yoked his horses rushing in all directions, held with reins that glitter.The well-born friend hath carved his food with Vasus: in all his limbs he hath increased and prospered.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यमस्य महतो महित्वममर्त्यस्य मर्त्यासु विक्षु ।नाना हनू विभृते सं भरेते असिन्वती बप्सती भूर्यत्तः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ asya ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ ámartyasya ǀ mártyāsu ǀ vikṣú ǀnā́nā ǀ hánū íti ǀ víbhṛte íti ví-bhṛte ǀ sám ǀ bharete íti ǀ ásinvatī íti ǀ bápsatī íti ǀ bhū́ri ǀ attaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I HAVE beheld the might of this Great Being. Immortal in the midst of tribes of mortals. His jaws now open and now shut together: much they devour, insatiately chewing.
verses.wilson_translation: I have beheld the might of the adorable (Agni) immortal in (the hearts of) mortal beings; his two jaws,divided asunder,shuttogether; devouring without masticating consume much (fuel).
verses.griffith_verse: I HAVE beheld the might of this Great Being. Immortal in the midst of tribes of mortals. His jaws now open and now shut together: much they devour, insatiately chewing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गुहा शिरो निहितमृधगक्षी असिन्वन्नत्ति जिह्वया वनानि ।अत्राण्यस्मै पड्भिः सं भरंत्युत्तानहस्ता नमसाधि विक्षु ॥
verses.transliteration: gúhā ǀ śíraḥ ǀ ní-hitam ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ ásinvan ǀ atti ǀ jihváyā ǀ vánāni ǀátrāṇi ǀ asmai ǀ paṭ-bhíḥ ǀ sám ǀ bharanti ǀ uttāná-hastāḥ ǀ námasā ǀ ádhi ǀ vikṣú ǁ
verses.english_translation: His eyes are turned away, his head is hidden: unsated with his tongue he eats the fuel. With hands upraised, with reverence in the houses, for him they quickly bring his food together.
verses.wilson_translation: His head is deposited in a cavern; his eyes are wide apart; with his tongue he devours the woodwithout masticating; (the priests) approaching on food reverently offer him oblations among the people withupliftedhands.
verses.griffith_verse: His eyes are turned away, his head is hidden: unsated with his tongue he eats the fuel. With hands upraised, with reverence in the houses, for him they quickly bring his food together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र मातुः प्रतरं गुह्यमिच्छन्कुमारो न वीरुधः सर्पदुर्वीः ।ससं न पक्वमविदच्छुचंतं रिरिह्वांसं रिप उपस्थे अंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ mātúḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ gúhyam ǀ icchán ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ ná ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ sarpat ǀ urvī́ḥ ǀsamám ǀ ná ǀ pakvám ǀ avidat ǀ śucántam ǀ ririhvā́ṃsam ǀ ripáḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seeking, as ’twere, his Mother's secret bosom, he, like a child, creeps on through wide-spread bushes. One he finds glowing like hot food made ready, and kissing deep within the earth's recmes.
verses.wilson_translation: Longing for the abundant creepers of the maternal (earth, longing for) their more excellent concealed(root), he creeps like a child; he has found the tree shining like ripe grain, upon the lap of tthe earth, tasting (theether).
verses.griffith_verse: Seeking, as ’twere, his Mother's secret bosom, he, like a child, creeps on through wide-spread bushes. One he finds glowing like hot food made ready, and kissing deep within the earth's recmes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्वामृतं रोदसी प्र ब्रवीमि जायमानो मातरा गर्भो अत्ति ।नाहं देवस्य मर्त्यश्चिकेताग्निरंग विचेताः स प्रचेताः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ ṛtám ǀ rodasī íti ǀ prá ǀ bravīmi ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ mātárā ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ atti ǀná ǀ ahám ǀ devásya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ ciketa ǀ agníḥ ǀ aṅgá ǀ ví-cetāḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This holy Law I tell you, Earth and Heaven: the Infant at his birth dovours his Parents. No knowledge of the God have I, a mortal. Yea, Agni knoweth best, for he hath wisdom.
verses.wilson_translation: This (that) I declare unto you, heaven and earth, (is) the truth; as soon as born, the embryo devoursthe parents; I who am a mortal know not (the condition) of the deity;Agni, (OVaiśvānara), is discriminating, heis exceedingly wise.
verses.griffith_verse: This holy Law I tell you, Earth and Heaven: the Infant at his birth dovours his Parents. No knowledge of the God have I, a mortal. Yea, Agni knoweth best, for he hath wisdom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अस्मा अन्नं तृष्वादधात्याज्यैर्घृतैर्जुहोति पुष्यति ।तस्मै सहस्रमक्षभिर्वि चक्षेऽग्ने विश्वतः प्रत्यङ्ङसि त्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ ánnam ǀ tṛṣú ǀ ā-dádhāti ǀ ā́jyaiḥ ǀ ghṛtáiḥ ǀ juhóti ǀ púṣyati ǀtásmai ǀ sahásram ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakṣe ǀ ágne ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ asi ǀ tvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: This man who quickly gives him food, who offers his gifts of oil and butter and supports him, - Him with his thousand eyes he closely looks on: thou showest him thy face from all sides, Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: He who quickly offers him food, makes oblations to him with dripping Soma, and delights him (withfood); (Agni) looks upon him with a thousand eyes; you, Agni, are everywhere present.
verses.griffith_verse: This man who quickly gives him food, who offers his gifts of oil and butter and supports him, - Him with his thousand eyes he closely looks on: thou showest him thy face from all sides, Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं देवेषु त्यज एनश्चकर्थाग्ने पृच्छामि नु त्वामविद्वान् ।अक्रीळन्क्रीळन्हरिरत्तवेऽदन्वि पर्वशश्चकर्त गामिवासिः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ devéṣu ǀ tyájaḥ ǀ énaḥ ǀ cakartha ǀ ágne ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ nú ǀ tvā́m ǀ ávidvān ǀákrīḷan ǀ krī́ḷan ǀ háriḥ ǀ áttave ǀ adán ǀ ví ǀ parva-śáḥ ǀ cakarta ǀ gā́m-iva ǀ asíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, hast thou committed sin or treason among the Gods? In ignorance I ask thee. Playing, not playing, he gold-hued and toothless, hath cut his food up as the knife a victim.
verses.wilson_translation: What wrathful act, what sin have you committed among the gods? Ignorant I ask you,Agni, sporting(here) not sporting (there), golden-hued; eating what is to be eaten, you cut (your food) into pieces as the knife(cuts up) the cow.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, hast thou committed sin or treason among the Gods? In ignorance I ask thee. Playing, not playing, he gold-hued and toothless, hath cut his food up as the knife a victim.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विषूचो अश्वान्युयुजे वनेजा ऋजीतिभी रशनाभिर्गृभीतान् ।चक्षदे मित्रो वसुभिः सुजातः समानृधे पर्वभिर्वावृधानः ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣūcaḥ ǀ áśvān ǀ yuyuje ǀ vane-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́jīti-bhiḥ ǀ raśanā́bhiḥ ǀ gṛbhītā́n ǀcakṣadé ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ānṛdhe ǀ párva-bhiḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He born in wood hath yoked his horses rushing in all directions, held with reins that glitter. The well-born friend hath carved his food with Vasus: in all his limbs he hath increased and prospered.
verses.wilson_translation: Born in the woods, he has harnessed his steeds which move everywhere held in by straight-guidingreins; friendly and augmented by rays, he has distributed (wealth); he grows in strength nourished with logs ofwood.
verses.griffith_verse: He born in wood hath yoked his horses rushing in all directions, held with reins that glitter. The well-born friend hath carved his food with Vasus: in all his limbs he hath increased and prospered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXX. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ७ सौचीकोऽग्निर्वैश्वानरो वा, सप्तिर्वाजंभरो वा। अग्निः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI bestows the fleet prize-winning courser: Agni, the hero famed and firm in duty.Agni pervades and decks the earth and heaven, and fills the fruitful dame who teems with heroes. Blest be the wood that feeds the active Agni: within the two great worlds hath Agni entered.Agni impels a single man to battle, and with him rends in pieces many a foeman. Agni rejoiced the car of him who praised lim, and from the waters burnt away jarutha.Agni saved Atri in the fiery cavem, and made Nrmedha rich with troops of children. Agni hath granted wealth that decks the hero, and sent the sage who wins a thousand cattle.Agni hath made oblations rise to heaven: to every place are Agni's laws extended. With songs of praise the Ṛṣis call on Agni; on Agni, heroes worsted in the foray.Birds flying in the region call on Agni around a thousand cattle Agni wanders. Races of human birth pay Agni worship, men who have sprung from Nahus' line adore him.Stablished in holy oil is Agni's pasture, on the Gandharva path of Law and Order. The Ṛbhus fabricated prayer for Agni, and we with mighty hymns have called on Agni.Agni, Most Youthful God, protect the singer: win us by worship, Agni, great possessions.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निः सप्तिं वाजंभरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं श्रुत्यं कर्मनिष्ठां ।अग्नी रोदसी वि चरत्समंजन्नग्निर्नारीं वीरकुक्षिं पुरंधिं ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ sáptim ǀ vājam-bharám ǀ dadāti ǀ agníḥ ǀ vīrám ǀ śrútyam ǀ karmaniḥ-sthā́m ǀagníḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ví ǀ carat ǀ sam-añján ǀ agníḥ ǀ nā́rīm ǀ vīrá-kukṣim ǀ púram-dhim ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI bestows the fleet prize-winning courser: Agni, the hero famed and firm in duty. Agni pervades and decks the earth and heaven, and fills the fruitful dame who teems with heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnigives (his worshipper) a food-acquiring steed, Agni gives (him) a valiant son, renowned,assiduous in pious works; Agni travels beautifying heaven and earth; Agni (makes) as woman the bearer of maleoff-spring (and) intelligent.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI bestows the fleet prize-winning courser: Agni, the hero famed and firm in duty. Agni pervades and decks the earth and heaven, and fills the fruitful dame who teems with heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नेरप्नसः समिदस्तु भद्राग्निर्मही रोदसी आ विवेश ।अग्निरेकं चोदयत्समत्स्वग्निर्वृत्राणि दयते पुरूणि ॥
verses.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ ápnasaḥ ǀ sam-ít ǀ astu ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǀagníḥ ǀ ékam ǀ codayat ǀ samát-su ǀ agníḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ dayate ǀ purū́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Blest be the wood that feeds the active Agni: within the two great worlds hath Agni entered. Agni impels a single man to battle, and with him rends in pieces many a foeman.
verses.wilson_translation: May the fuel of the efficient Agnibe auspicious; Agni has penetrated the vast heaven and earth; Agnianimates (the worshipper) alone in battles; Agni destroys numerous enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Blest be the wood that feeds the active Agni: within the two great worlds hath Agni entered. Agni impels a single man to battle, and with him rends in pieces many a foeman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्ह त्यं जरतः कर्णमावाग्निरद्भ्यो निरदहज्जरूथं ।अग्निरत्रिं घर्म उरुष्यदंतरग्निर्नृमेधं प्रजयासृजत्सं ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ha ǀ tyám ǀ járataḥ ǀ kárṇam ǀ āva ǀ agníḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ adahat ǀ járūtham ǀagníḥ ǀ átrim ǀ gharmé ǀ uruṣyat ǀ antáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ nṛ-médham ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ asṛjat ǀ sám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni rejoiced the car of him who praised lim, and from the waters burnt away jarutha. Agni saved Atri in the fiery cavem, and made Nrmedha rich with troops of children.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniverily has protected Jaratkarṇa; he has consumed Jarūtha with his flames; Agni rescued Atriinthe hot fissure; Agni furnished Nṛmedha with progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni rejoiced the car of him who praised lim, and from the waters burnt away jarutha. Agni saved Atri in the fiery cavem, and made Nrmedha rich with troops of children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्दाद्द्रविणं वीरपेशा अग्निर्ऋषिं यः सहस्रा सनोति ।अग्निर्दिवि हव्यमा ततानाग्नेर्धामानि विभृता पुरुत्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ dāt ǀ dráviṇam ǀ vīrá-peśāḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ yáḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ sanóti ǀagníḥ ǀ diví ǀ havyám ǀ ā́ ǀ tatāna ǀ agnéḥ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ ví-bhṛtā ǀ puru-trā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni hath granted wealth that decks the hero, and sent the sage who wins a thousand cattle. Agni hath made oblations rise to heaven: to every place are Agni's laws extended.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnisending forth flames bestows wealth; Agni (gives a son to) the Ṛṣi who acquires a thousandcows; Agni spreads the oblation through heaven, the forms of Agni are manifested in many plural ces.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni hath granted wealth that decks the hero, and sent the sage who wins a thousand cattle. Agni hath made oblations rise to heaven: to every place are Agni's laws extended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निमुक्थैर्ऋषयो वि ह्वयंतेऽग्निं नरो यामनि बाधितासः ।अग्निं वयो अंतरिक्षे पतंतोऽग्निः सहस्रा परि याति गोनां ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ agním ǀ náraḥ ǀ yā́mani ǀ bādhitā́saḥ ǀagním ǀ váyaḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀ pátantaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ pári ǀ yāti ǀ gónām ǁ
verses.english_translation: With songs of praise the Ṛṣis call on Agni; on Agni, heroes worsted in the foray. Birds flying in the region call on Agni around a thousand cattle Agni wanders.
verses.wilson_translation: The Ṛṣis variously invoke Agniwith hymns; men when hard pressed in battle (invoke) Agni; the birdsflying in mid-heaven (invoke) Agni; Agni circumambulates thousands of cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: With songs of praise the Ṛṣis call on Agni; on Agni, heroes worsted in the foray. Birds flying in the region call on Agni around a thousand cattle Agni wanders.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो वि जाताः ।अग्निर्गांधर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्याग्नेर्गव्यूतिर्घृत आ निषत्ता ॥
verses.transliteration: agním ǀ víśaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ gā́ndharvīm ǀ pathyā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ agnéḥ ǀ gávyūtiḥ ǀ ghṛté ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-sattā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Races of human birth pay Agni worship, men who have sprung from Nahus' line adore him. Stablished in holy oil is Agni's pasture, on the Gandharva path of Law and Order.
verses.wilson_translation: The races who are of human birth praise (Agni, so do the men descended from king Nahuṣa; Agni,(hears) the voice which is fit for the path of sacrifice; Agni's path lies everywhere in ghī.
verses.griffith_verse: Races of human birth pay Agni worship, men who have sprung from Nahus' line adore him. Stablished in holy oil is Agni's pasture, on the Gandharva path of Law and Order.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नये ब्रह्म ऋभवस्ततक्षुरग्निं महामवोचामा सुवृक्तिं ।अग्ने प्राव जरितारं यविष्ठाग्ने महि द्रविणमा यजस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: agnáye ǀ bráhma ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ tatakṣuḥ ǀ agním ǀ mahā́m ǀ avocāma ǀ su-vṛktím ǀágne ǀ prá ǀ ava ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ ágne ǀ máhi ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ā́ ǀ yajasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Ṛbhus fabricated prayer for Agni, and we with mighty hymns have called on Agni. Agni, Most Youthful God, protect the singer: win us by worship, Agni, great possessions.
verses.wilson_translation: TheṚbhushave fabricated praise for Agni; we have recited pious praise to the mighty Agni; Agni,youngest (of the gods), protect your worshipper; Agni, bestow (on him) abundant wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: The Ṛbhus fabricated prayer for Agni, and we with mighty hymns have called on Agni. Agni, Most Youthful God, protect the singer: win us by worship, Agni, great possessions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXI. Visvakarman.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE who sate down as Hotar-priest, the Ṛṣi, our Father, offering up all things existing,—He, seeking through his wish a great possession, came among men on earth as archetypal. What was the place whereon he took his station? What was it that supported him? How was it?Whence Visvakarman, seeing all, producing the earth, with mighty power disclosed the heavens. He who hath eyes on all sides round about him, a mouth on all sides, arms and feet on all sides,He, the Sole God, producing earth and heaven, weldeth them, with his arms as wings, together. What was the tree, what wood in sooth produced it, from which they fashioned out the earth and heaven?Ye thoughtful men inquire within your spirit whereon he stood when he established all things. Nine highest, lowest, sacrificial natures, and these thy mid-most here, O Visvakarman,Teach thou thy friends at sacrifice, O Blessed, and come thyself, exalted, to our worship. Bring thou thyself, exalted with oblation, O Visvakarman, Earth and Heaven to worship.Let other men around us live in folly here let us have a rich and liberal patron. Let us invoke to-day, to aid our labour, the Lord of Speech, the thought-swift Visvakarman.May he hear kindly all our invocations who gives all bliss for aid, whose works are righteous.

verses.sanskrit: य इमा विश्वा भुवनानि जुह्वदृषिर्होता न्यसीदत्पिता नः ।स आशिषा द्रविणमिच्छमानः प्रथमच्छदवराँ आ विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ júhvat ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ ásīdat ǀ pitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ ā-śíṣā ǀ dráviṇam ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ prathama-chát ǀ ávarān ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE who sate down as Hotar-priest, the Ṛṣi, our Father, offering up all things existing,— He, seeking through his wish a great possession, came among men on earth as archetypal.
verses.griffith_verse: HE who sate down as Hotar-priest, the Ṛṣi, our Father, offering up all things existing,— He, seeking through his wish a great possession, came among men on earth as archetypal.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं स्विदासीदधिष्ठानमारंभणं कतमत्स्वित्कथासीत् ।यतो भूमिं जनयन्विश्वकर्मा वि द्यामौर्णोन्महिना विश्वचक्षाः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ āsīt ǀ adhi-sthā́nam ǀ ā-rámbhaṇam ǀ katamát ǀ svit ǀ kathā́ ǀ āsīt ǀyátaḥ ǀ bhū́mim ǀ janáyan ǀ viśvá-karmā ǀ ví ǀ dyā́m ǀ áurṇot ǀ mahinā́ ǀ viśvá-cakṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What was the place whereon he took his station? What was it that supported him? How was it? Whence Visvakarman, seeing all, producing the earth, with mighty power disclosed the heavens.
verses.wilson_translation: What was the station? What was the material? How was (it done)? So that the beholder of all,Viśvakarman(was) genitive rating and disclosed heaven by his might.
verses.griffith_verse: What was the place whereon he took his station? What was it that supported him? How was it? Whence Visvakarman, seeing all, producing the earth, with mighty power disclosed the heavens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वतश्चक्षुरुत विश्वतोमुखो विश्वतोबाहुरुत विश्वतस्पात् ।सं बाहुभ्यां धमति सं पतत्रैर्द्यावाभूमी जनयंदेव एकः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvátaḥ-cakṣuḥ ǀ utá ǀ viśvátaḥ-mukhaḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ-bāhuḥ ǀ utá ǀ viśvátaḥ-pāt ǀsám ǀ bāhú-bhyām ǀ dhámati ǀ sám ǀ pátatraiḥ ǀ dyā́vābhū́mī íti ǀ janáyan ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who hath eyes on all sides round about him, a mouth on all sides, arms and feet on all sides, He, the Sole God, producing earth and heaven, weldeth them, with his arms as wings, together.
verses.wilson_translation: Having eyes everywhere, and having a face everywhere, having arms everywhere, and having feeteverywhere, he traverses (heaven) with his arms, (earth) with his swift-moving (feet), and exists a god withoutcompanion genitive rating heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: He who hath eyes on all sides round about him, a mouth on all sides, arms and feet on all sides, He, the Sole God, producing earth and heaven, weldeth them, with his arms as wings, together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं स्विद्वनं क उ स वृक्ष आस यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः ।मनीषिणो मनसा पृच्छतेदु तद्यदध्यतिष्ठद्भुवनानि धारयन् ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ vánam ǀ káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ vṛkṣáḥ ǀ āsa ǀ yátaḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ niḥ-tatakṣúḥ ǀmánīṣiṇaḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ pṛccháta ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tát ǀ yát ǀ adhi-átiṣṭhat ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ dhāráyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: What was the tree, what wood in sooth produced it, from which they fashioned out the earth and heaven? Ye thoughtful men inquire within your spirit whereon he stood when he established all things.
verses.wilson_translation: Which was the forest, which the tree, from which they fabricated heaven and earth? Inquire, sages, inyour minds what (plural ce) he was stationed in when holding the worlds.
verses.griffith_verse: What was the tree, what wood in sooth produced it, from which they fashioned out the earth and heaven? Ye thoughtful men inquire within your spirit whereon he stood when he established all things.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या ते धामानि परमाणि यावमा या मध्यमा विश्वकर्मन्नुतेमा ।शिक्षा सखिभ्यो हविषि स्वधावः स्वयं यजस्व तन्वं वृधानः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ te ǀ dhā́māni ǀ paramā́ṇi ǀ yā́ ǀ avamā́ ǀ yā́ ǀ madhyamā́ ǀ viśva-karman ǀ utá ǀ imā́ ǀśíkṣa ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ havíṣi ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ svayám ǀ yajasva ǀ tanvám ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nine highest, lowest, sacrificial natures, and these thy mid-most here, O Visvakarman, Teach thou thy friends at sacrifice, O Blessed, and come thyself, exalted, to our worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant to your friends,Viśvakarman, at the oblation, your best, your worst and your intermediate forms,and to these do you yourself, possessor of the oblation, becoming augmented in person n (by oblations), offerworship.
verses.griffith_verse: Nine highest, lowest, sacrificial natures, and these thy mid-most here, O Visvakarman, Teach thou thy friends at sacrifice, O Blessed, and come thyself, exalted, to our worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वकर्मन्हविषा वावृधानः स्वयं यजस्व पृथिवीमुत द्यां ।मुह्यंत्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: víśva-karman ǀ havíṣā ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ svayám ǀ yajasva ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǀmúhyantu ǀ anyé ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ asmā́kam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sūríḥ ǀ astu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring thou thyself, exalted with oblation, O Visvakarman, Earth and Heaven to worship. Let other men around us live in folly here let us have a rich and liberal patron.
verses.wilson_translation: VIśvakarman, magnified by the oblation, do you of yourself worship earth and heaven; let other men(who offer no oblations) be everywhere confounded; may he, rich in oblations, be the granter of heaven at thisour (sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: Bring thou thyself, exalted with oblation, O Visvakarman, Earth and Heaven to worship. Let other men around us live in folly here let us have a rich and liberal patron.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतये मनोजुवं वाजे अद्या हुवेम ।स नो विश्वानि हवनानि जोषद्विश्वशंभूरवसे साधुकर्मा ॥
verses.transliteration: vācáḥ ǀ pátim ǀ viśvá-karmāṇam ǀ ūtáye ǀ manaḥ-júvam ǀ vā́je ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ hávanāni ǀ joṣat ǀ viśvá-śambhūḥ ǀ ávase ǀ sādhú-karmā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us invoke to-day, to aid our labour, the Lord of Speech, the thought-swift Visvakarman. May he hear kindly all our invocations who gives all bliss for aid, whose works are righteous.
