verses.wilson_translation: Let us this day invoke for our protection the lord of speech, the creator of all, who is swift as thought;may he, the bestower of all happiness, the doer of good works, be propitiated by all our oblations, (so as) togrant us his protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Let us invoke to-day, to aid our labour, the Lord of Speech, the thought-swift Visvakarman. May he hear kindly all our invocations who gives all bliss for aid, whose works are righteous.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXII. Visvakarman.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Father of the eye, the Wise in spirit, created both these worlds submerged in fatness.Then when the eastern ends were firmly fastened, the heavens and the earth were far extended. Mighty in mind and power is Visvakarman, Maker, Disposer, and most lofty Presence.Their offerings joy in rich juice where they value One, only One, beyond the Seven Ṛṣis. Father who made us, he who, as Disposer, knoweth all races and all things existing,Even he alone, the Deities' narne-giver,him other beings seek for information. To him in sacrifice they offered treasures,—Ṛṣis of old, in numerous troops, as singers,Who, in the distant, near, and lower region, made ready all these things that have existence. That which is earlier than this earth and heaven, before the Asuras and Gods had being,—What was the germ primeval which the waters received where all the Gods were seen together? The waters, they received that germ primeval wherein the Gods were gathefed all together.It rested set upon the Unborn's navel, that One wherein abide all things existing. Ye will not find him who produced these creatures: another thing hath risen up among you.Enwrapt in misty cloud, with lips that stammer, hymn-chanters wander and are discontented.

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुषः पिता मनसा हि धीरो घृतमेने अजनन्नन्नमाने ।यदेदंता अददृहंत पूर्व आदिद्द्यावापृथिवी अप्रथेतां ॥
verses.transliteration: cákṣuṣaḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ hí ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ene íti ǀ ajanat ǀ námnamāne íti ǀyadā́ ǀ ít ǀ ántāḥ ǀ ádadṛhanta ǀ pū́rve ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ aprathetām ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Father of the eye, the Wise in spirit, created both these worlds submerged in fatness. Then when the eastern ends were firmly fastened, the heavens and the earth were far extended.
verses.wilson_translation: The maker of the senses, resolute in mind, engendered the water, (and then) these two (heaven andearth) floating (on the waters); when those ancient boundaries were fixed, then the heaven and earth wereexpanded.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Father of the eye, the Wise in spirit, created both these worlds submerged in fatness. Then when the eastern ends were firmly fastened, the heavens and the earth were far extended.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वकर्मा विमना आद्विहाया धाता विधाता परमोत संदृक् ।तेषामिष्टानि समिषा मदंति यत्रा सप्तऋषीन्पर एकमाहुः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvá-karmā ǀ ví-manāḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ dhātā́ ǀ vi-dhātā́ ǀ paramā́ ǀ utá ǀ sam-dṛ́k ǀtéṣām ǀ iṣṭā́ni ǀ sám ǀ iṣā́ ǀ madanti ǀ yátra ǀ sapta-ṛṣī́n ǀ paráḥ ǀ ékam ǀ āhúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mighty in mind and power is Visvakarman, Maker, Disposer, and most lofty Presence. Their offerings joy in rich juice where they value One, only One, beyond the Seven Ṛṣis.
verses.wilson_translation: Viśvakarman, of comprehensive mind and manifold greatness, is all- pervading, the creator, thearranger and the supreme supervisor; him in whom the desires of their (senses) are satisfied with food, they callsecond line of the ṛca: him in whom they delight their forms (or plural ces) with water, him, those who are skille din Viśvakarman;Niruktanotes that at the universal sacrifice Viśvakarman Bhauvanaoffered up all beings and thenhimself].
verses.griffith_verse: Mighty in mind and power is Visvakarman, Maker, Disposer, and most lofty Presence. Their offerings joy in rich juice where they value One, only One, beyond the Seven Ṛṣis.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानि विश्वा ।यो देवानां नामधा एक एव तं संप्रश्नं भुवना यंत्यन्या ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ janitā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vi-dhātā́ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ véda ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀyáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ nāma-dhā́ḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ evá ǀ tám ǀ sam-praśnám ǀ bhúvanā ǀ yanti ǀ anyā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Father who made us, he who, as Disposer, knoweth all races and all things existing, Even he alone, the Deities' narne-giver,him other beings seek for information.
verses.wilson_translation: He who is our preserver, our parent, the creator (of all), who knows our abodes (and knows) allbeings, who is the name-giver of the gods-- he is one; other beings come to him to inquire.
verses.griffith_verse: Father who made us, he who, as Disposer, knoweth all races and all things existing, Even he alone, the Deities' narne-giver,him other beings seek for information.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त आयजंत द्रविणं समस्मा ऋषयः पूर्वे जरितारो न भूना ।असूर्ते सूर्ते रजसि निषत्ते ये भूतानि समकृण्वन्निमानि ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ā́ ǀ ayajanta ǀ dráviṇam ǀ sám ǀ asmai ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhūnā́ ǀasū́rte ǀ sū́rte ǀ rájasi ǀ ni-satté ǀ yé ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ sam-ákṛṇvan ǀ imā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him in sacrifice they offered treasures,—Ṛṣis of old, in numerous troops, as singers, Who, in the distant, near, and lower region, made ready all these things that have existence.
verses.wilson_translation: Those ancient Ṛṣis who adorned (with light) these beings in the animate and inanimate world, offerto him wealth (of sacrifice) as praisers with abundant (laudation).
verses.griffith_verse: To him in sacrifice they offered treasures,—Ṛṣis of old, in numerous troops, as singers, Who, in the distant, near, and lower region, made ready all these things that have existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्या परो देवेभिरसुरैर्यदस्ति ।कं स्विद्गर्भं प्रथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाः समपश्यंत विश्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: paráḥ ǀ divā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ ásuraiḥ ǀ yát ǀ ásti ǀkám ǀ svit ǀ gárbham ǀ prathamám ǀ dadhre ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yátra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sam-ápaśyanta ǀ víśve ǁ
verses.english_translation: That which is earlier than this earth and heaven, before the Asuras and Gods had being,— What was the germ primeval which the waters received where all the Gods were seen together?
verses.wilson_translation: What was that embryo which was beyond the heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods, beyondtheasuras, which the waters first retained, in which all the gods contemplated each other?
verses.griffith_verse: That which is earlier than this earth and heaven, before the Asuras and Gods had being,— What was the germ primeval which the waters received where all the Gods were seen together?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमिद्गर्भं प्रथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाः समगच्छंत विश्वे ।अजस्य नाभावध्येकमर्पितं यस्मिन्विश्वानि भुवनानि तस्थुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ gárbham ǀ prathamám ǀ dadhre ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yátra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sam-ágacchanta ǀ víśve ǀajásya ǀ nā́bhau ǀ ádhi ǀ ékam ǀ árpitam ǀ yásmin ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tasthúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The waters, they received that germ primeval wherein the Gods were gathefed all together. It rested set upon the Unborn's navel, that One wherein abide all things existing.
verses.wilson_translation: The waters verily first retained the embryo in which all the gods were aggregated, single deposited onthe navel of the unborn (creator), in which all beings abide.
verses.griffith_verse: The waters, they received that germ primeval wherein the Gods were gathefed all together. It rested set upon the Unborn's navel, that One wherein abide all things existing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न तं विदाथ य इमा जजानान्यद्युष्माकमंतरं बभूव ।नीहारेण प्रावृता जल्प्या चासुतृप उक्थशासश्चरंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ vidātha ǀ yáḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ jajā́na ǀ anyát ǀ yuṣmā́kam ǀ ántaram ǀ babhūva ǀnīhāréṇa ǀ prā́vṛtāḥ ǀ jálpyā ǀ ca ǀ asu-tṛ́paḥ ǀ uktha-śásaḥ ǀ caranti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye will not find him who produced these creatures: another thing hath risen up among you. Enwrapt in misty cloud, with lips that stammer, hymn-chanters wander and are discontented.
verses.wilson_translation: You know not him who has genitive rated these (beings); (his life) is another, different from yours;wrapped in fog, and foolish speech (do they) wander (who are) gluttonous and engaged in devotion.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye will not find him who produced these creatures: another thing hath risen up among you. Enwrapt in misty cloud, with lips that stammer, hymn-chanters wander and are discontented.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXII. Manyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE who hath reverenced thee, Manyu, destructive bolt, breeds for himself forthwith all conquering energy.Ārya and Dāsa will we conquer with thine aid, with thee the Conqueror, with conquest conquest-sped. Manyu was Indra, yea, the God, was Manyu, Manyu was Hotar, Varuṇa, Jātavedas.The tribes of human lineage worship Manyu. Accordant with thy fervour, Manyu, guard us. Come hither, Manyu, mightier tham the mighty; chase, with thy fervour for ally, our foemen.Slayer of foes, of Vṛtra, and of Dasyu, bring thou to us all kinds of wealth and treasure. For thou art, Manyu, of surpassing vigour, fierce, queller of the foe, and self-existent,Shared by all men, victorious, subduer: vouchsafe to us superior strengith in battles. I have departed, still without a portion, wise God! according to thy will, the Mighty.I, feeble man, was wroth thee, O Manyu I am myself; come thou to give me vigour. Come hither. I am all thine own; advancing turn thou to me, Victorious, All-supporter!Come to me, Manyu, Wielder of the Thunder: bethink thee of thy friend, and slay the Dasyus. Approach, and on my right hand hold thy station: so shall we slay a multitude of foemen.The best of meath I offer to support thee: may we be first to drink thereof in quiet.

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते मन्योऽविधद्वज्र सायक सह ओजः पुष्यति विश्वमानुषक् ।साह्याम दासमार्यं त्वया युजा सहस्कृतेन सहसा सहस्वता ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ manyo íti ǀ ávidhat ǀ vajra ǀ sāyaka ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ puṣyati ǀ víśvam ǀ ānuṣák ǀsahyā́ma ǀ dā́sam ǀ ā́ryam ǀ tváyā ǀ yujā́ ǀ sáhaḥ-kṛtena ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhasvatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE who hath reverenced thee, Manyu, destructive bolt, breeds for himself forthwith all conquering energy. Ārya and Dāsa will we conquer with thine aid, with thee the Conqueror, with conquest conquest-sped.
verses.wilson_translation: He who worships you,Manyu, the thunderbolt, the destroyer (of enemies), enjoys all might andstrength, combined; may we oversome the Dāsaand theĀryawith you for our ally, invigorating, strong andvigorous.
verses.griffith_verse: HE who hath reverenced thee, Manyu, destructive bolt, breeds for himself forthwith all conquering energy. Ārya and Dāsa will we conquer with thine aid, with thee the Conqueror, with conquest conquest-sped.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मन्युरिंद्रो मन्युरेवास देवो मन्युर्होता वरुणो जातवेदाः ।मन्युं विश ईळते मानुषीर्याः पाहि नो मन्यो तपसा सजोषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: manyúḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ manyúḥ ǀ evá ǀ āsa ǀ deváḥ ǀ manyúḥ ǀ hótā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀmanyúm ǀ víśaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ naḥ ǀ manyo íti ǀ tápasā ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Manyu was Indra, yea, the God, was Manyu, Manyu was Hotar, Varuṇa, Jātavedas. The tribes of human lineage worship Manyu. Accordant with thy fervour, Manyu, guard us.
verses.wilson_translation: Manyuis Indra; Manyu verily was a god; Manyu is the sacrificing priest (Agni), the omniscient Varuṇa;the people who are of human descent, praise Manyu; protect us, Manyu, well plural ased along with Tapas.
verses.griffith_verse: Manyu was Indra, yea, the God, was Manyu, Manyu was Hotar, Varuṇa, Jātavedas. The tribes of human lineage worship Manyu. Accordant with thy fervour, Manyu, guard us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभीहि मन्यो तवसस्तवीयांतपसा युजा वि जहि शत्रून् ।अमित्रहा वृत्रहा दस्युहा च विश्वा वसून्या भरा त्वं नः ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ ihi ǀ manyo íti ǀ tavásaḥ ǀ távīyān ǀ tápasā ǀ yujā́ ǀ ví ǀ jahi ǀ śátrūn ǀamitra-hā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ dasyu-hā́ ǀ ca ǀ víśvā ǀ vásūni ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither, Manyu, mightier tham the mighty; chase, with thy fervour for ally, our foemen. Slayer of foes, of Vṛtra, and of Dasyu, bring thou to us all kinds of wealth and treasure.
verses.wilson_translation: Come to us Manyuu, who are the strongest of the strong; with Tapasas your ally overthrow ourenemies; do you who are the slayer of enemies, the slayer of adversaries, the slayer of foes, bring to us allriches.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither, Manyu, mightier tham the mighty; chase, with thy fervour for ally, our foemen. Slayer of foes, of Vṛtra, and of Dasyu, bring thou to us all kinds of wealth and treasure.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि मन्यो अभिभूत्योजाः स्वयंभूर्भामो अभिमातिषाहः ।विश्वचर्षणिः सहुरिः सहावानस्मास्वोजः पृतनासु धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ manyo íti ǀ abhíbhūti-ojāḥ ǀ svayam-bhū́ḥ ǀ bhā́maḥ ǀ abhimāti-saháḥ ǀviśvá-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ sáhāvān ǀ asmā́su ǀ ójaḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: For thou art, Manyu, of surpassing vigour, fierce, queller of the foe, and self-existent, Shared by all men, victorious, subduer: vouchsafe to us superior strengith in battles.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Manyu, who are possessed of over-powering strength, self- existent, irate, the overcomer ofenemies, the beholder of all, enduring, vigorous, grant us strength in battles.
verses.griffith_verse: For thou art, Manyu, of surpassing vigour, fierce, queller of the foe, and self-existent, Shared by all men, victorious, subduer: vouchsafe to us superior strengith in battles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभागः सन्नप परेतो अस्मि तव क्रत्वा तविषस्य प्रचेतः ।तं त्वा मन्यो अक्रतुर्जिहीळाहं स्वा तनूर्बलदेयाय मेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: abhāgáḥ ǀ sán ǀ ápa ǀ párā-itaḥ ǀ asmi ǀ táva ǀ krátvā ǀ taviṣásya ǀ praceta íti pra-cetaḥ ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ manyo íti ǀ akratúḥ ǀ jihīḷa ǀ ahám ǀ svā́ ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ bala-déyāya ǀ mā ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have departed, still without a portion, wise God! according to thy will, the Mighty. I, feeble man, was wroth thee, O Manyu I am myself; come thou to give me vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Sage Manyu, taking no part in the worship of you, the powerful one, I have retreated (from before myfoes); worshipping not, I was angry with you; (yet) being (incorporated with) my body, approach me to give mestrength.
verses.griffith_verse: I have departed, still without a portion, wise God! according to thy will, the Mighty. I, feeble man, was wroth thee, O Manyu I am myself; come thou to give me vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं ते अस्म्युप मेह्यर्वाङ्प्रतीचीनः सहुरे विश्वधायः ।मन्यो वज्रिन्नभि मामा ववृत्स्व हनाव दस्यूँरुत बोध्यापेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ te ǀ asmi ǀ úpa ǀ mā ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ pratīcīnáḥ ǀ sahure ǀ viśva-dhāyaḥ ǀmányo íti ǀ vajrin ǀ abhí ǀ mā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtsva ǀ hánāva ǀ dásyūn ǀ utá ǀ bodhi ǀ āpéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come hither. I am all thine own; advancing turn thou to me, Victorious, All-supporter! Come to me, Manyu, Wielder of the Thunder: bethink thee of thy friend, and slay the Dasyus.
verses.griffith_verse: Come hither. I am all thine own; advancing turn thou to me, Victorious, All-supporter! Come to me, Manyu, Wielder of the Thunder: bethink thee of thy friend, and slay the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि प्रेहि दक्षिणतो भवा मेऽधा वृत्राणि जंघनाव भूरि ।जुहोमि ते धरुणं मध्वो अग्रमुभा उपांशु प्रथमा पिबाव ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ dakṣiṇatáḥ ǀ bhava ǀ me ǀ ádha ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jaṅghanāva ǀ bhū́ri ǀjuhómi ǀ te ǀ dharúṇam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ ubháu ǀ upa-aṃśú ǀ prathamā́ ǀ pibāva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Approach, and on my right hand hold thy station: so shall we slay a multitude of foemen. The best of meath I offer to support thee: may we be first to drink thereof in quiet.
verses.wilson_translation: Approach, be upon my right, let us slay a multitude of foes; I offer to you the best Soma, the sustainer;let us both drink it first in privacy.
verses.griffith_verse: Approach, and on my right hand hold thy station: so shall we slay a multitude of foemen. The best of meath I offer to support thee: may we be first to drink thereof in quiet.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIV. Manyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BORNE on with thee, O Manyu girt by Maruts, let our brave men, impetuous, bursting forward,March on, like flames of fire in form, exulting, with pointed arrows, sharpening their weapons. Flashing like fire, be thou, O conquering Manyu, invoked, O Victor, as our army's leader.Slay thou our foes, distribute their possessions: show forth thy vigour, scatter those who hate us. O Manyu, overcome thou our assailant on! breaking, slaying, crushing down the foemen.They have not hindered thine impetuous vigour: Mighty, Sole born! thou makest them thy subjects. Alone or many thou art worshipped, Manyu: sharpen the spirit of each clan for battle.With thee to aid, O thou of perfect splendour, we will uplift the glorious shout for conquest. Unyielding bringing victory like Indra, O Manyu, be thou here our Sovran Ruler.To thy dear name, O Victor, we sing praises: we know the spring from which thou art come hither. Twin-born with power, destructive bolt of thunder, the highest conquering might is thine, Subduer!Be friendly to its in thy spirit, Manyu, O Much-invoked, in shock of mighty battle. For spoil let Varuṇa and Manyu give us the wealth of both sides gathered and collected;And let our enemies with stricken spirits, o’erwhelmed with terror, slink away defeated.

verses.sanskrit: त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुजंतो हर्षमाणासो धृषिता मरुत्वः ।तिग्मेषव आयुधा संशिशाना अभि प्र यंतु नरो अग्निरूपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tváyā ǀ manyo íti ǀ sa-rátham ǀ ā-rujántaḥ ǀ hárṣamāṇāsaḥ ǀ dhṛṣitā́ḥ ǀ marutvaḥ ǀtigmá-iṣavaḥ ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ sam-śíśānāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ yantu ǀ náraḥ ǀ agní-rūpāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BORNE on with thee, O Manyu girt by Maruts, let our brave men, impetuous, bursting forward, March on, like flames of fire in form, exulting, with pointed arrows, sharpening their weapons.
verses.wilson_translation: May the leaders (of rites) wearing the form of Agni, (ascending) the same car with you,Manyu, whoare accompanied by the Maruts, proceed to combat, advancing, exulting, indignant, armed with sharp arrow,whetting their weapons.
verses.griffith_verse: BORNE on with thee, O Manyu girt by Maruts, let our brave men, impetuous, bursting forward, March on, like flames of fire in form, exulting, with pointed arrows, sharpening their weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निरिव मन्यो त्विषितः सहस्व सेनानीर्नः सहुरे हूत एधि ।हत्वाय शत्रून्वि भजस्व वेद ओजो मिमानो वि मृधो नुदस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ-iva ǀ manyo íti ǀ tviṣitáḥ ǀ sahasva ǀ senā-nī́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sahure ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ edhi ǀhatvā́ya ǀ śátrūn ǀ ví ǀ bhajasva ǀ védaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ mímānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ nudasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Flashing like fire, be thou, O conquering Manyu, invoked, O Victor, as our army's leader. Slay thou our foes, distribute their possessions: show forth thy vigour, scatter those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: Manyu, blazing like Agni, overthrow (our foes), come as our genitive ral, enduring (manyu) when invoked(by us) in battle; having slain the enemies divide (among us) the treasure; granting (us) strength, scatter (our)foes.
verses.griffith_verse: Flashing like fire, be thou, O conquering Manyu, invoked, O Victor, as our army's leader. Slay thou our foes, distribute their possessions: show forth thy vigour, scatter those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्व मन्यो अभिमातिमस्मे रुजन्मृणन्प्रमृणन्प्रेहि शत्रून् ।उग्रं ते पाजो नन्वा रुरुध्रे वशी वशं नयस एकज त्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáhasva ǀ manyo íti ǀ abhí-mātim ǀ asmé íti ǀ ruján ǀ mṛṇán ǀ pra-mṛṇán ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ śátrūn ǀugrám ǀ te ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ nanú ǀ ā́ ǀ rurudhre ǀ vaśī́ ǀ váśam ǀ nayase ǀ eka-ja ǀ tvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Manyu, overcome thou our assailant on! breaking, slaying, crushing down the foemen. They have not hindered thine impetuous vigour: Mighty, Sole born! thou makest them thy subjects.
verses.wilson_translation: Overthrow,Manyu, our assailant; advance against our foes, wounding, killing, annihilating them; (who)can resist your fierce might? O you who are without companion, subjecting them you lead them subject.
verses.griffith_verse: O Manyu, overcome thou our assailant on! breaking, slaying, crushing down the foemen. They have not hindered thine impetuous vigour: Mighty, Sole born! thou makest them thy subjects.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एको बहूनामसि मन्यवीळितो विशंविशं युधये सं शिशाधि ।अकृत्तरुक्त्वया युजा वयं द्युमंतं घोषं विजयाय कृण्महे ॥
verses.transliteration: ékaḥ ǀ bahūnā́m ǀ asi ǀ manyo íti ǀ īḷitáḥ ǀ víśam-viśam ǀ yudháye ǀ sám ǀ śiśādhi ǀákṛtta-ruk ǀ tváyā ǀ yujā́ ǀ vayám ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ ghóṣam ǀ vi-jayā́ya ǀ kṛṇmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Alone or many thou art worshipped, Manyu: sharpen the spirit of each clan for battle. With thee to aid, O thou of perfect splendour, we will uplift the glorious shout for conquest.
verses.wilson_translation: You are praised,Manyu, as (the conqueror) alone of many; animate us to contend with all men; withyyou, O you of unshorn radiance, for our ally, we raise aloud shout for victory.
verses.griffith_verse: Alone or many thou art worshipped, Manyu: sharpen the spirit of each clan for battle. With thee to aid, O thou of perfect splendour, we will uplift the glorious shout for conquest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विजेषकृदिंद्र इवानवब्रवोऽस्माकं मन्यो अधिपा भवेह ।प्रियं ते नाम सहुरे गृ���ीमसि विद्मा तमुत्सं यत आबभूथ ॥
verses.transliteration: vijeṣa-kṛ́t ǀ índraḥ-iva ǀ anava-braváḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ manyo íti ǀ adhi-pā́ḥ ǀ bhava ǀ ihá ǀpriyám ǀ te ǀ nā́ma ǀ sahure ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀ vidmá ǀ tám ǀ útsam ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā-babhū́tha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unyielding bringing victory like Indra, O Manyu, be thou here our Sovran Ruler. To thy dear name, O Victor, we sing praises: we know the spring from which thou art come hither.
verses.wilson_translation: Manyu, the giver of victory like Indra, irreproachable, be you our protector at this (sacrifice); enduringone, we sing to you acceptable praise; we know this to be the source whence you have become (mighty).
verses.griffith_verse: Unyielding bringing victory like Indra, O Manyu, be thou here our Sovran Ruler. To thy dear name, O Victor, we sing praises: we know the spring from which thou art come hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आभूत्या सहजा वज्र सायक सहो बिभर्ष्यभिभूत उत्तरं ।क्रत्वा नो मन्यो सह मेद्येधि महाधनस्य पुरुहूत संसृजि ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́-bhūtyā ǀ saha-jā́ḥ ǀ vajra ǀ sāyaka ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ bibharṣi ǀ abhi-bhūte ǀ út-taram ǀkrátvā ǀ naḥ ǀ manyo íti ǀ sahá ǀ medī́ ǀ edhi ǀ mahā-dhanásya ǀ puru-hūta ǀ sam-sṛ́ji ǁ
verses.english_translation: Twin-born with power, destructive bolt of thunder, the highest conquering might is thine, Subduer! Be friendly to its in thy spirit, Manyu, O Much-invoked, in shock of mighty battle.
verses.wilson_translation: (Manyu), your destructive thunderbolt, the over-powerer (of foes), twin-born with victory, you possessexceeding strength; be favourable to us, Manyu, in deeds, you who are invoked by many in the shock of battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Twin-born with power, destructive bolt of thunder, the highest conquering might is thine, Subduer! Be friendly to its in thy spirit, Manyu, O Much-invoked, in shock of mighty battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: संसृष्टं धनमुभयं समाकृतमस्मभ्यं दत्तां वरुणश्च मन्युः ।भियं दधाना हृदयेषु शत्रवः पराजितासो अप नि लयंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-sṛṣṭam ǀ dhánam ǀ ubháyam ǀ sam-ā́kṛtam ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dattām ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ manyúḥ ǀbhíyam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ hṛ́dayeṣu ǀ śátravaḥ ǀ párā-jitāsaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ ní ǀ layantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: For spoil let Varuṇa and Manyu give us the wealth of both sides gathered and collected; And let our enemies with stricken spirits, o’erwhelmed with terror, slink away defeated.
verses.wilson_translation: May Varuṇaand Manyubestow upon us wealth of both kinds, undivided and completely our own, andmay our enemies, bearing fear within their hearts, be overcome and utterly destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: For spoil let Varuṇa and Manyu give us the wealth of both sides gathered and collected; And let our enemies with stricken spirits, o’erwhelmed with terror, slink away defeated.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXV. Sūrya's Bridal.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . TRUTH is the base that bears the earth; by Sūrya are the heavens sustained.By Law the Ādityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven. By Soma are the Ādityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth.Thus Soma in the midst of all these constellations hath his place. One thinks, when they have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma's juice;Of him whom Brahmans truly know as Soma no one ever tastes. Soma, secured by sheltering rules, guarded by hymns in Brhati,Thou standest listening to the stones none tastes of thee who dwells on earth. When they begin to drink thee then, O God, thou swellest out again.Vāyu is Soma's guardian God. The Moon is that which shapes the years. Raibhi was her dear bridal friend, and Narasamsi led her home.Lovely was Sūrya's robe: she came to that which Gatha had adorned. Thought was the pillow of her couch, sight was the unguent for her eyes:Her treasury was earth and heaven.ẉhen Sūrya went unto her Lord. Hymns were the cross-bars of the pole, Kurira-metre decked the car:The bridesmen were the Aśvin Pair Agni was leader of the train. Soma was he who wooed the maid: the groomsmen were both Aśvins, whenThe Sun-God Savitar bestowed his willing Sūrya on her Lord. Her spirit was the bridal car; the covering thereof was heaven:Bright were both Steers that drew it when Sūrya approached her husband's, home. Thy Steers were steady, kept in place by holy verse and Sāma-hymn:All car were thy two chariot wheels: thy path was tremulous in the sky, Clean, as thou wentest, were thy wheels wind, was the axle fastened there.Sūrya, proceeding to her Lord, mounted a spirit-fashioried car. The bridal pomp of Sūrya, which Savitar started, moved along.In Magha days are oxen slain, in Arjuris they wed the bride. When on your three-wheeled chariot, O Aśvins, ye came as wooers unto Sūrya's bridal,Then all the Gods agreed to your proposal Pūṣan as Son elected you as Fathers. O ye Two Lords of lustre, then when ye to Sūrya's wooing came,Where was one chariot wheel of yours? Where stood ye for die Sire's command? The Brahmans, by their seasons, know, O Sūrya, those two wheels of thine:One kept concealed, those only who are skilled in highest truths have learned. To Sūrya and the Deities, to Mitra and to Varuṇa.Who know aright the thing that is, this adoration have I paid. By their own power these Twain in close succession move;They go as playing children round the sacrifice.One of the Pair beholdeth all existing things; the other ordereth seasons and is born again. He, born afresh, is new and new for ever ensign of days he goes before the MorningsComing, he orders fr the Gods their portion. The Moon prolongs the days of our existence. Mount this, all-shaped, gold-hued, with strong wheels, fashioned of Kimsuka and Salmali, light-rolling,Bound for the world of life immortal, Sūrya: make for thy lord a happy bridal journey. Rise up from hence: this maiden hath a husband. I laud Visvavasu with hymns and homage.Seek in her father's home another fair one, and find the portion from of old assigned thee. Rise up from hence, Visvavasu: with reverence we worship thee.Seek thou another willing maid, and with her husband leave the bride. Straight in direction be the path:s, and thornless, whereon our fellows travel to the wooing.Let Aryaman and Bhaga lead us: perfect, O Gods, the union of the wife and husband. Now from the noose of Varuṇa I free thee, wherewith Most Blessed Savitar hath bound thee.In Law's seat, to the world of virtuous action, I give thee up uninjured with thy consort. Hence, and not thence, I send these free. I make thee softly fettered there.That, Bounteous Indra, she may live blest in her fortune and her sons. Let Pūṣan take thy hand and hence conduct thee; may the two Aśvins on their car transport thee.Go to the house to be the household's mistress and speak as lady ito thy gathered people. Happy be thou and prosper witlh thy children here: be vigilant to rule thy household in this home.Closely unite thy body with this; man, thy lord. So shall ye, full of years, address your company. Her hue is blue and red: the fienod who clingeth close is driven off.Well thrive the kinsmen of this bride the husband is bourid fast in bonds. Give thou the woollen robe away: deal treasure to the Brahman priests.This female fiend hath got her feet, and as a wife attends her lord. Unlovely is his body when it glistens with this wicked fiend,What time the husband wraps about his limbs the garment of his wife. Consumptions, from her people, which follow the bride's resplendent train,—These let the Holy Gods again bear to the place from which they came. Let not the highway thieves who lie in ambush find the wedded pair.By pleasant ways let them escape the danger, and let foes depart. Signs of good fortune mark the bride come all of you and look at her.Wish her prosperity, and then return unto your homes again. Pungent is this, and bitter this, filled, as it were, with arrow-barbs, Empoisoned andṇot fit for use.The Brahman who knows Sūrya well deserves the garment of the bride. The fringe, the cloth that decks her head, and then the triply parted robe,—Behold the hues which Sūrya wears these doth the Brahman purify. I take thy hand in mine for happy fortune that thou mayst reach old age with me thy husband.Gods, Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitar, Purandhi, have given thee to be my household's mistress. O Pūṣan, send her on as most auspicious, her who shall be the sharer of my pleasures;Her who shall twine her loving arms about me, and welcome all my love and mine embraces. For thee, with bridal train, they, first, escorted Sūrya to her home.Give to the husband in return, Agni, the wife with progeny. Agni hath given the bride again with splendour and with ample life.Long lived be he who is her lord; a hundred autumns let him live. Soma obtained her first of all; next the Gandharva was her lord.Agai was thy third husband: now one bornof woman is thy fourth. Soma to the Gandharva, and to Agni the Gandharva gave:And Agni hath bestowed on me riches and sons and this my spouse. Be ye not parted; dwell ye here reach the full time of human life.With sons and grandsons sport and play, rejoicing in your own abode. So may Prajāpati bring children forth to us; may Aryaman adorn us till old age come nigh.Not inauspicious enter thou thy husband's house: bring blessing to our bipeds and our quadrupeds. Not evil-eyed, no slayer of thy husband, bring weal to cattle, radiant, gentlehearted;Loving the Gods, delightful, bearing heroes, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds. O Bounteous Indra, make this bride blest in her sons and fortunate.Vouchsafe to her ten sons, and make her husband the eleventh man. Over thy husband's father and thy husband's mother bear full sway.Over the sister of thy lord, over his brothers rule supreme. So may the Universal Gods, so may the Waters join our hearts.May Mātariśvan, Dhātar, and Destri together bind us close.

verses.sanskrit: सत्येनोत्तभिता भूमिः सूर्येणोत्तभिता द्यौः ।ऋतेनादित्यास्तिष्ठंति दिवि सोमो अधि श्रितः ॥
verses.transliteration: satyéna ǀ úttabhitā ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ úttabhitā ǀ dyáuḥ ǀṛténa ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ tiṣṭhanti ǀ diví ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ śritáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: TRUTH is the base that bears the earth; by Sūrya are the heavens sustained. By Law the Ādityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Earth is upheld by truth; heaven is upheld by the sun; theĀdityasare supported by sacrifice,Somaissupreme in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: TRUTH is the base that bears the earth; by Sūrya are the heavens sustained. By Law the Ādityas stand secure, and Soma holds his place in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमेनादित्या बलिनः सोमेन पृथिवी मही ।अथो नक्षत्राणामेषामुपस्थे सोम आहितः ॥
verses.transliteration: sómena ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ balínaḥ ǀ sómena ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ mahī́ ǀátho íti ǀ nákṣatrāṇām ǀ eṣā́m ǀ upá-sthe ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ā́-hitaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: By Soma are the Ādityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth. Thus Soma in the midst of all these constellations hath his place.
verses.wilson_translation: By SomatheĀdityasare strong; by Soma the earth is great; Soma is stationed in the vicinity of these Nakṣatras.
verses.griffith_verse: By Soma are the Ādityas strong, by Soma mighty is the earth. Thus Soma in the midst of all these constellations hath his place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमं मन्यते पपिवान्यत्संपिंषंत्योषधिं ।सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुर्न तस्याश्नाति कश्चन ॥
verses.transliteration: sómam ǀ manyate ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ yát ǀ sam-piṃṣánti ǀ óṣadhim ǀsómam ǀ yám ǀ brahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ vidúḥ ǀ ná ǀ tásya ǀ aśnāti ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǁ
verses.english_translation: One thinks, when they have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma's juice; Of him whom Brahmans truly know as Soma no one ever tastes.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has drunk thinks that the herb which men crush is the Soma; (but) that which the Brāhmaṇas know to be Soma,, of that no one partakes. {i.e., no one partakes of it unless he has sacrificed; ifthe Soma be taken as the moon, 'no one' will mean 'no one but the gods'].
verses.griffith_verse: One thinks, when they have brayed the plant, that he hath drunk the Soma's juice; Of him whom Brahmans truly know as Soma no one ever tastes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आच्छद्विधानैर्गुपितो बार्हतैः सोम रक्षितः ।ग्राव्णामिच्छृण्वंतिष्ठसि न ते अश्नाति पार्थिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ācchát-vidhānaiḥ ǀ gupitáḥ ǀ bā́rhataiḥ ǀ soma ǀ rakṣitáḥ ǀgrā́vṇām ǀ ít ǀ śṛṇván ǀ tiṣṭhasi ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ aśnāti ǀ pā́rthivaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma, secured by sheltering rules, guarded by hymns in Brhati, Thou standest listening to the stones none tastes of thee who dwells on earth.
verses.wilson_translation: Concealed by means of coverings, protected by the Bārhats, OSoma, you abide listening to thegrinding-stones; no terrestrial being partakes of you.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma, secured by sheltering rules, guarded by hymns in Brhati, Thou standest listening to the stones none tastes of thee who dwells on earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्त्वा देव प्रपिबंति तत आ प्यायसे पुनः ।वायुः सोमस्य रक्षिता समानां मास आकृतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ tvā ǀ deva ǀ pra-píbanti ǀ tátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pyāyase ǀ púnaríti ǀvāyúḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ rakṣitā́ ǀ sámānām ǀ mā́saḥ ǀ ā́-kṛtiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they begin to drink thee then, O God, thou swellest out again. Vāyu is Soma's guardian God. The Moon is that which shapes the years.
verses.wilson_translation: When, O god, they quaff you, then do you renew yourself again;Vāyuis the guardian of Soma, themaker of years and months.
verses.griffith_verse: When they begin to drink thee then, O God, thou swellest out again. Vāyu is Soma's guardian God. The Moon is that which shapes the years.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रैभ्यासीदनुदेयी नाराशंसी न्योचनी ।सूर्याया भद्रमिद्वासो गाथयैति परिष्कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: ráibhī ǀ āsīt ǀ anu-déyī ǀ nārāśaṃsī́ ǀ ni-ócanī ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ bhadrám ǀ ít ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ gā́thayā ǀ eti ǀ pári-kṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Raibhi was her dear bridal friend, and Narasamsi led her home. Lovely was Sūrya's robe: she came to that which Gatha had adorned.
verses.wilson_translation: Raibhi was her companion; Nārāśaṃsī her slave;Sūrya's lovely dress was adorned by Gātha.
verses.griffith_verse: Raibhi was her dear bridal friend, and Narasamsi led her home. Lovely was Sūrya's robe: she came to that which Gatha had adorned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चित्तिरा उपबर्हणं चक्षुरा अभ्यंजनं ।द्यौर्भूमिः कोश आसीद्यदयात्सूर्या पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: cíttiḥ ǀ āḥ ǀ upa-bárhaṇam ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ āḥ ǀ abhi-áñjanam ǀdyáuḥ ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ kóśaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ yát ǀ áyāt ǀ sūryā́ ǀ pátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thought was the pillow of her couch, sight was the unguent for her eyes: Her treasury was earth and heaven.ẉhen Sūrya went unto her Lord.
verses.wilson_translation: Citti(mind) was the pillow, the eye was the collyrium; heaven and earth were the box when Sūryawent to her husband.
verses.griffith_verse: Thought was the pillow of her couch, sight was the unguent for her eyes: Her treasury was earth and heaven.ẉhen Sūrya went unto her Lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोमा आसन्प्रतिधयः कुरीरं छंद ओपशः ।सूर्याया अश्विना वराग्निरासीत्पुरोगवः ॥
verses.transliteration: stómāḥ ǀ āsan ǀ prati-dháyaḥ ǀ kurī́ram ǀ chándaḥ ǀ opaśáḥ ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ varā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ puraḥ-gaváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hymns were the cross-bars of the pole, Kurira-metre decked the car: The bridesmen were the Aśvin Pair Agni was leader of the train.
verses.wilson_translation: Hymns were the cross-bars (of the car); the Kurīra metre was the thong of the whip; the Aśvinswere Sūrya's groomsmen;Agniwas the leader of the procession.
verses.griffith_verse: Hymns were the cross-bars of the pole, Kurira-metre decked the car: The bridesmen were the Aśvin Pair Agni was leader of the train.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमो वधूयुरभवदश्विनास्तामुभा वरा ।सूर्यां यत्पत्ये शंसंतीं मनसा सविताददात् ॥
verses.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ vadhū-yúḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ aśvínā ǀ āstām ǀ ubhā́ ǀ varā́ ǀsūryā́m ǀ yát ǀ pátye ǀ śáṃsantīm ǀ mánasā ǀ savitā́ ǀ ádadāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma was he who wooed the maid: the groomsmen were both Aśvins, when The Sun-God Savitar bestowed his willing Sūrya on her Lord.
verses.wilson_translation: Somawas desirous of a bride; the two Aśvinswere the two groomsmen when Savitāgave Sūrya,who was ripe for a husband, (to Soma endowed) with intelligence.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma was he who wooed the maid: the groomsmen were both Aśvins, when The Sun-God Savitar bestowed his willing Sūrya on her Lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मनो अस्या अन आसीद्द्यौरासीदुत च्छदिः ।शुक्रावनड्वाहावास्तां यदयात्सूर्या गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: mánaḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ ánaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ utá ǀ chadíḥ ǀśukráu ǀ anaḍvā́hau ǀ āstām ǀ yát ǀ áyāt ǀ sūryā́ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Her spirit was the bridal car; the covering thereof was heaven: Bright were both Steers that drew it when Sūrya approached her husband's, home.
verses.wilson_translation: Mind was her chariot, and heaven was the covering, the two shining (orbs) were the oxen when Sūrya went to (her husband's) dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: Her spirit was the bridal car; the covering thereof was heaven: Bright were both Steers that drew it when Sūrya approached her husband's, home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋक्सामाभ्यामभिहितौ गावौ ते सामनावितः ।श्रोत्रं ते चक्रे आस्तां दिवि पंथाश्चराचारः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛk-sāmā́bhyām ǀ abhí-hitau ǀ gā́vau ǀ te ǀ sāmanáu ǀ itaḥ ǀśrótram ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ āstām ǀ diví ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ carācaráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy Steers were steady, kept in place by holy verse and Sāma-hymn: All car were thy two chariot wheels: thy path was tremulous in the sky,
verses.wilson_translation: Those two oxen yoked by the Ṛk and the Sāmanmarch equally; the two wheels were your ears; themoving path (was) in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy Steers were steady, kept in place by holy verse and Sāma-hymn: All car were thy two chariot wheels: thy path was tremulous in the sky,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुची ते चक्रे यात्या व्यानो अक्ष आहतः ।अनो मनस्मयं सूर्यारोहत्प्रयती पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: śúcī íti ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ yātyā́ḥ ǀ vi-ānáḥ ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ ā́-hataḥ ǀánaḥ ǀ manasmáyam ǀ sūryā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ arohat ǀ pra-yatī́ ǀ pátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Clean, as thou wentest, were thy wheels wind, was the axle fastened there. Sūrya, proceeding to her Lord, mounted a spirit-fashioried car.
verses.wilson_translation: The two swift-moving wheels were your pure (cars).Vāyuwas the fastened axle,Sūryamountedthe chariot of the Mind, going to her lord.
verses.griffith_verse: Clean, as thou wentest, were thy wheels wind, was the axle fastened there. Sūrya, proceeding to her Lord, mounted a spirit-fashioried car.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूर्याया वहतुः प्रागात्सविता यमवासृजत् ।अघासु हन्यंते गावोऽर्जुन्योः पर्युह्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: sūryā́yāḥ ǀ vahatúḥ ǀ prá ǀ agāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ yám ǀ ava-ásṛjat ǀaghā́su ǀ hanyante ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ árjunyoḥ ǀ pári ǀ uhyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bridal pomp of Sūrya, which Savitar started, moved along. In Magha days are oxen slain, in Arjuris they wed the bride.
verses.wilson_translation: Sūrya's bridal procession which Savitādespatched has advanced; the oxen are whipped along inthe Magha(constellations); she is borne (to her husband's house) in the Arjunī(constellations).
verses.griffith_verse: The bridal pomp of Sūrya, which Savitar started, moved along. In Magha days are oxen slain, in Arjuris they wed the bride.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदश्विना पृच्छमानावयातं त्रिचक्रेण वहतुं सूर्यायाः ।विश्वे देवा अनु तद्वामजानन्पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ aśvinā ǀ pṛcchámānau ǀ áyātam ǀ tri-cakréṇa ǀ vahatúm ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ tát ǀ vām ǀ ajānan ǀ putráḥ ǀ pitárau ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ pūṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When on your three-wheeled chariot, O Aśvins, ye came as wooers unto Sūrya's bridal, Then all the Gods agreed to your proposal Pūṣan as Son elected you as Fathers.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Aśvins, you came in your three-wheeled car soliciting the marriage of Sūrya, then all thegods, assented and Pūṣan(your) son chose (you as) his parents.
verses.griffith_verse: When on your three-wheeled chariot, O Aśvins, ye came as wooers unto Sūrya's bridal, Then all the Gods agreed to your proposal Pūṣan as Son elected you as Fathers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप ।क्वैकं चक्रं वामासीत्क्व देष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ áyātam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ vare-yám ǀ sūryā́m ǀ úpa ǀkvá ǀ ékam ǀ cakrám ǀ vām ǀ āsīt ǀ kvá ǀ deṣṭrā́ya ǀ tasthathuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O ye Two Lords of lustre, then when ye to Sūrya's wooing came, Where was one chariot wheel of yours? Where stood ye for die Sire's command?
verses.wilson_translation: When, lords of water, you came to the giver-away (to get)Sūrya, where was the one wheel of yourcar, where did you stand to make the gift?
verses.griffith_verse: O ye Two Lords of lustre, then when ye to Sūrya's wooing came, Where was one chariot wheel of yours? Where stood ye for die Sire's command?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वे ते चक्रे सूर्ये ब्रह्माण ऋतुथा विदुः ।अथैकं चक्रं यद्गुहा तदद्धातय इद्विदुः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ sūrye ǀ brahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ viduḥ ǀátha ǀ ékam ǀ cakrám ǀ yát ǀ gúhā ǀ tát ǀ addhātáyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ viduḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Brahmans, by their seasons, know, O Sūrya, those two wheels of thine: One kept concealed, those only who are skilled in highest truths have learned.
verses.wilson_translation: Sūrya, the Brāhmaṇasknow your chariot wheels in their season; the single wheel that isconcealed, the sages know it also.
verses.griffith_verse: The Brahmans, by their seasons, know, O Sūrya, those two wheels of thine: One kept concealed, those only who are skilled in highest truths have learned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूर्यायै देवेभ्यो मित्राय वरुणाय च ।ये भूतस्य प्रचेतस इदं तेभ्योऽकरं नमः ॥
verses.transliteration: sūryā́yai ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ ca ǀyé ǀ bhūtásya ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ idám ǀ tébhyaḥ ǀ akaram ǀ námaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Sūrya and the Deities, to Mitra and to Varuṇa. Who know aright the thing that is, this adoration have I paid.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer this adoration to Sūrya, to the gods, to Mitraand Varuṇa, (and to all those) who areconsiderate to created beings.
verses.griffith_verse: To Sūrya and the Deities, to Mitra and to Varuṇa. Who know aright the thing that is, this adoration have I paid.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वापरं चरतो माययैतौ शिशू क्रीळंतौ परि यातो अध्वरं ।विश्वान्यन्यो भुवनाभिचष्ट ऋतूँरन्यो विदधज्जायते पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: pūrva-aparám ǀ carataḥ ǀ māyáyā ǀ etáu ǀ śíśū íti ǀ krī́ḷantau ǀ pári ǀ yātaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀvíśvāni ǀ anyáḥ ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhi-cáṣṭe ǀ ṛtū́n ǀ anyáḥ ǀ vi-dádhat ǀ jāyate ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: By their own power these Twain in close succession move; They go as playing children round the sacrifice. One of the Pair beholdeth all existing things; the other ordereth seasons and is born again.
verses.wilson_translation: These two (the sun and moon) wandering in thought one after the other, youthful, sportive, approachthe sacrifice; one (of them) looks over all worlds, the other regulating the seasons is born repeatedly.
verses.griffith_verse: By their own power these Twain in close succession move; They go as playing children round the sacrifice. One of the Pair beholdeth all existing things; the other ordereth seasons and is born again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नवोनवो भवति जायमानोऽह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रं ।भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चंद्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥
verses.transliteration: návaḥ-navaḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ áhnām ǀ ketúḥ ǀ uṣásām ǀ eti ǀ ágram ǀbhāgám ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ dadhāti ǀ ā-yán ǀ prá ǀ candrámāḥ ǀ tirate ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, born afresh, is new and new for ever ensign of days he goes before the Mornings Coming, he orders f6r the Gods their portion. The Moon prolongs the days of our existence.
verses.wilson_translation: New every day (the moon) is born; the manifester of days he goes on front of the Dawns; hedistributes their portion to the gods as he goes; the moon protracts a long existence.
verses.griffith_verse: He, born afresh, is new and new for ever ensign of days he goes before the Mornings Coming, he orders f6r the Gods their portion. The Moon prolongs the days of our existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुकिंशुकं शल्मलिं विश्वरूपं हिरण्यवर्णं सुवृतं सुचक्रं ।आ रोह सूर्ये अमृतस्य लोकं स्योनं पत्ये वहतुं कृणुष्व ॥
verses.transliteration: su-kiṃśukám ǀ śalmalím ǀ viśvá-rūpam ǀ híraṇya-varṇam ǀ su-vṛ́tam ǀ su-cakrám ǀā́ ǀ roha ǀ sūrye ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ lokám ǀ syonám ǀ pátye ǀ vahatúm ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mount this, all-shaped, gold-hued, with strong wheels, fashioned of Kimsuka and Salmali, light-rolling, Bound for the world of life immortal, Sūrya: make for thy lord a happy bridal journey.
verses.wilson_translation: Ascend,Sūrya, the chariot made of goodkiṃśukawood and ofśalmali, multiform, decorated withgold, well-covered, well-wheeled, prepare the happy world of the immortals, your marriage procession to yourhusband.
verses.griffith_verse: Mount this, all-shaped, gold-hued, with strong wheels, fashioned of Kimsuka and Salmali, light-rolling, Bound for the world of life immortal, Sūrya: make for thy lord a happy bridal journey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीर्ष्वातः पतिवती ह्येषा विश्वावसुं नमसा गीर्भिरीळे ।अन्यामिच्छ पितृषदं व्यक्तां स ते भागो जनुषा तस्य विद्धि ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrṣva ǀ átaḥ ǀ páti-vatī ǀ hí ǀ eṣā́ ǀ viśvá-vasum ǀ námasā ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ īḷe ǀanyā́m ǀ iccha ǀ pitṛ-sádam ǀ ví-aktām ǀ sáḥ ǀ te ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ tásya ǀ viddhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rise up from hence: this maiden hath a husband. I laud Visvavasu with hymns and homage. Seek in her father's home another fair one, and find the portion from of old assigned thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise up from hence, for this (damsel) has a husband; I worship Viśvāvasuwith reverence and withhymns; seek for another maiden still dwelling in her father's house, decorated with ornaments; that is yourportion, know this (to your portion, take it) from your birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Rise up from hence: this maiden hath a husband. I laud Visvavasu with hymns and homage. Seek in her father's home another fair one, and find the portion from of old assigned thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उदीर्ष्वातो विश्वावसो नमसेळा महे त्वा ।अन्यामिच्छ प्रफर्व्यं सं जायां पत्या सृज ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ īrṣva ǀ átaḥ ǀ viśvavaso íti viśva-vaso ǀ námasā ǀ īḷāmahe ǀ tvā ǀanyā́m ǀ iccha ǀ pra-pharvyám ǀ sám ǀ jāyā́m ǀ pátyā ǀ sṛja ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rise up from hence, Visvavasu: with reverence we worship thee. Seek thou another willing maid, and with her husband leave the bride.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise up from here,Viśvāvasu, we worship you with reverence; seek another maiden, one with largehips; leave the bride with her husband.
verses.griffith_verse: Rise up from hence, Visvavasu: with reverence we worship thee. Seek thou another willing maid, and with her husband leave the bride.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनृक्षरा ऋजवः संतु पंथा येभिः सखायो यंति नो वरेयं ।समर्यमा सं भगो नो निनीयात्सं जास्पत्यं सुयममस्तु देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: anṛkṣarā́ḥ ǀ ṛjávaḥ ǀ santu ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ yánti ǀ naḥ ǀ vare-yám ǀsám ǀ aryamā́ ǀ sám ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ninīyāt ǀ sám ǀ jāḥ-patyám ǀ su-yámam ǀ astu ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Straight in direction be the path:s, and thornless, whereon our fellows travel to the wooing. Let Aryaman and Bhaga lead us: perfect, O Gods, the union of the wife and husband.
verses.wilson_translation: Smooth and straight be the paths by which our friends repair to the bride's father; may Aryaman, may Bhaga conduct us, and may the union of the wife and husband be easily accomplished, O gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Straight in direction be the path:s, and thornless, whereon our fellows travel to the wooing. Let Aryaman and Bhaga lead us: perfect, O Gods, the union of the wife and husband.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र त्वा मुंचामि वरुणस्य पाशाद्येन त्वाबध्नात्सविता सुशेवः ।ऋतस्य योनौ सुकृतस्य लोकेऽरिष्टां त्वा सह पत्या दधामि ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tvā ǀ muñcāmi ǀ váruṇasya ǀ pā́śāt ǀ yéna ǀ tvā ǀ ábadhnāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ su-śévaḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ yónau ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ loké ǀ áriṣṭām ǀ tvā ǀ sahá ǀ pátyā ǀ dadhāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now from the noose of Varuṇa I free thee, wherewith Most Blessed Savitar hath bound thee. In Law's seat, to the world of virtuous action, I give thee up uninjured with thy consort.
verses.wilson_translation: I set you free from the noose of Varuṇa, wherewith the adorable Savitāhad bound you; in the plural ceof sacrifice in the world of good deeds I unite you, unharmed, with your husband.
verses.griffith_verse: Now from the noose of Varuṇa I free thee, wherewith Most Blessed Savitar hath bound thee. In Law's seat, to the world of virtuous action, I give thee up uninjured with thy consort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेतो मुंचामि नामुतः सुबद्धाममुतस्करं ।यथेयमिंद्र मीढ्वः सुपुत्रा सुभगासति ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ itáḥ ǀ muñcā́mi ǀ ná ǀ amútaḥ ǀ su-baddhā́m ǀ amútaḥ ǀ karam ǀyáthā ǀ iyám ǀ indra ǀ mīḍhvaḥ ǀ su-putrā́ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ ásati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hence, and not thence, I send these free. I make thee softly fettered there. That, Bounteous Indra, she may live blest in her fortune and her sons.
verses.wilson_translation: I set you free from there, not from here; I plural ce you here firmly bound; grant,Indra, showerer, that this(damsel) may have excellent children, and be very fortunate.
verses.griffith_verse: Hence, and not thence, I send these free. I make thee softly fettered there. That, Bounteous Indra, she may live blest in her fortune and her sons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्याश्विना त्वा प्र वहतां रथेन ।गृहान्गच्छ गृहपत्नी यथासो वशिनी त्वं विदथमा वदासि ॥
verses.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ tvā ǀ itáḥ ǀ nayatu ǀ hasta-gṛ́hya ǀ aśvínā ǀ tvā ǀ prá ǀ vahatām ǀ ráthena ǀgṛhā́n ǀ gaccha ǀ gṛhá-patnī ǀ yáthā ǀ ásaḥ ǀ vaśínī ǀ tvám ǀ vidátham ǀ ā́ ǀ vadāsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Pūṣan take thy hand and hence conduct thee; may the two Aśvins on their car transport thee. Go to the house to be the household's mistress and speak as lady ito thy gathered people.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣanlead you hence, taking you by thehand; may the Aśvinsconvey you away in their car,go to the dwelling (of your husband) as you are the mistress of the house; you, submissive (to your husband),give orders to his household.
verses.griffith_verse: Let Pūṣan take thy hand and hence conduct thee; may the two Aśvins on their car transport thee. Go to the house to be the household's mistress and speak as lady ito thy gathered people.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इह प्रियं प्रजया ते समृध्यतामस्मिन्गृहे गार्हपत्याय जागृहि ।एना पत्या तन्वं सं सृजस्वाधा जिव्री विदथमा वदाथः ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ priyám ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ te ǀ sám ǀ ṛdhyatām ǀ asmín ǀ gṛhé ǀ gā́rha-patyāya ǀ jāgṛhi ǀenā́ ǀ pátyā ǀ tanvám ǀ sám ǀ sṛjasva ǀ ádha ǀ jívrī íti ǀ vidátham ǀ ā́ ǀ vadāthaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Happy be thou and prosper witlh thy children here: be vigilant to rule thy household in this home. Closely unite thy body with this; man, thy lord. So shall ye, full of years, address your company.
verses.wilson_translation: In this your (husband's family) may affection increase with offspring, be watchful over the domestic firein this house; unite your person n with this your husband; and both growing old together govern your household.
verses.griffith_verse: Happy be thou and prosper witlh thy children here: be vigilant to rule thy household in this home. Closely unite thy body with this; man, thy lord. So shall ye, full of years, address your company.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नीललोहितं भवति कृत्यासक्तिर्व्यज्यते ।एधंते अस्या ज्ञातयः पतिर्बंधेषु बध्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: nīla-lohitám ǀ bhavati ǀ kṛtyā́ ǀ āsaktíḥ ǀ ví ǀ ajyate ǀédhante ǀ asyāḥ ǀ jñātáyaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ bandhéṣu ǀ badhyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Her hue is blue and red: the fienod who clingeth close is driven off. Well thrive the kinsmen of this bride the husband is bourid fast in bonds.
verses.wilson_translation: Blue and red is (her form); devoted (to her) is left behind; her kinsmen prosper, the husband is boundin bonds.
verses.griffith_verse: Her hue is blue and red: the fienod who clingeth close is driven off. Well thrive the kinsmen of this bride the husband is bourid fast in bonds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा देहि शामुल्यं ब्रह्मभ्यो वि भजा वसु ।कृत्यैषा पद्वती भूत्व्या जाया विशते पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ dehi ǀ śāmulyám ǀ brahmá-bhyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ bhaja ǀ vásu ǀkṛtyā́ ǀ eṣā́ ǀ pat-vátī ǀ bhūtvī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ viśate ǀ pátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give thou the woollen robe away: deal treasure to the Brahman priests. This female fiend hath got her feet, and as a wife attends her lord.
verses.wilson_translation: Put away the garment soiled by the body; give wealth to the Brāhmaṇas; this Kṛtyāhaving becomeendowed with feet, enters the husband's heart as his wife.
verses.griffith_verse: Give thou the woollen robe away: deal treasure to the Brahman priests. This female fiend hath got her feet, and as a wife attends her lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्रीरा तनूर्भवति रुशती पापयामुया ।पतिर्यद्वध्वो वाससा स्वमंगमभिधित्सते ॥
verses.transliteration: aśrīrā́ ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ rúśatī ǀ pāpáyā ǀ amuyā́ ǀpátiḥ ǀ yát ǀ vadhváḥ ǀ vā́sasā ǀ svám ǀ áṅgam ǀ abhi-dhítsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unlovely is his body when it glistens with this wicked fiend, What time the husband wraps about his limbs the garment of his wife.
verses.wilson_translation: The (bridegroom's)bodyis lacking in beauty; shining with this wicked (Kṛtyā), when he wishes to clothe his own limbs with his wife's garments.
verses.griffith_verse: Unlovely is his body when it glistens with this wicked fiend, What time the husband wraps about his limbs the garment of his wife.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये वध्वश्चंद्रं वहतुं यक्ष्मा यंति जनादनु ।पुनस्तान्यज्ञिया देवा नयंतु यत आगताः ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ vadhváḥ ǀ candrám ǀ vahatúm ǀ yákṣmāḥ ǀ yánti ǀ jánāt ǀ ánu ǀpúnaríti ǀ tā́n ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ náyantu ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā́-gatāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Consumptions, from her people, which follow the bride's resplendent train,— These let the Holy Gods again bear to the place from which they came.
verses.wilson_translation: May the adorable gods drive back again to the plural ce whence they came the diseases which followfrom (other) people the wife's golden bridal procession.
verses.griffith_verse: Consumptions, from her people, which follow the bride's resplendent train,— These let the Holy Gods again bear to the place from which they came.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा विदन्परिपंथिनो य आसीदंति दंपती ।सुगेभिर्दुर्गमतीतामप द्रांत्वरातयः ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vidan ǀ pari-panthínaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ā-sī́danti ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀsu-gébhiḥ ǀ duḥ-gám ǀ áti ǀ itām ǀ ápa ǀ drāntu ǀ árātayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the highway thieves who lie in ambush find the wedded pair. By pleasant ways let them escape the danger, and let foes depart.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the robbers who approach the husband and wife reach them; may they by easy roads pass thedifficulty; may enemies keep aloof.
verses.griffith_verse: Let not the highway thieves who lie in ambush find the wedded pair. By pleasant ways let them escape the danger, and let foes depart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुमंगलीरियं वधूरिमां समेत पश्यत ।सौभाग्यमस्यै दत्त्वायाथास्तं वि परेतन ॥
verses.transliteration: su-maṅgalī́ḥ ǀ iyám ǀ vadhū́ḥ ǀ imā́m ǀ sam-éta ǀ páśyata ǀsáubhāgyam ǀ asyai ǀ dattvā́ya ǀ átha ǀ ástam ǀ ví ǀ párā ǀ itana ǁ
verses.english_translation: Signs of good fortune mark the bride come all of you and look at her. Wish her prosperity, and then return unto your homes again.
verses.wilson_translation: Fortunate is this bride, approach, behold her; having given her your congratulations, depart to yourseveral homes.
verses.griffith_verse: Signs of good fortune mark the bride come all of you and look at her. Wish her prosperity, and then return unto your homes again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तृष्टमेतत्कटुकमेतदपाष्ठवद्विषवन्नैतदत्तवे ।सूर्यां यो ब्रह्मा विद्यात्स इद्वाधूयमर्हति ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛṣṭám ǀ etát ǀ káṭukam ǀ etát ǀ apāṣṭhá-vat ǀ viṣá-vat ǀ ná ǀ etát ǀ áttave ǀsūryā́m ǀ yáḥ ǀ brahmā́ ǀ vidyā́t ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ vā́dhū-yam ǀ arhati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pungent is this, and bitter this, filled, as it were, with arrow-barbs, Empoisoned andṇot fit for use. The Brahman who knows Sūrya well deserves the garment of the bride.
verses.wilson_translation: This (garment) is inflaming, it is pungent; it is like stale Soma; it is like poison; it is not fit to eat; the Brāhmaṇa, who knows Sūrya, verily desires the bridal (garment).
verses.griffith_verse: Pungent is this, and bitter this, filled, as it were, with arrow-barbs, Empoisoned andṇot fit for use. The Brahman who knows Sūrya well deserves the garment of the bride.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आशसनं विशसनमथो अधिविकर्तनं ।सूर्यायाः पश्य रूपाणि तानि ब्रह्मा तु शुंधति ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-śásanam ǀ vi-śásanam ǀ átho íti ǀ adhi-vikártanam ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ paśya ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ tā́ni ǀ brahmā́ ǀ tú ǀ śundhati ǁ
verses.english_translation: The fringe, the cloth that decks her head, and then the triply parted robe,— Behold the hues which Sūrya wears these doth the Brahman purify.
verses.wilson_translation: Behold the forms of Sūrya, the āśasana (bordercloth) theviśasana(headcloth), the adhivikartana(divided skirt); of these the Brāhmaṇarelieves her.
verses.griffith_verse: The fringe, the cloth that decks her head, and then the triply parted robe,— Behold the hues which Sūrya wears these doth the Brahman purify.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गृभ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तं मया पत्या जरदष्टिर्यथासः ।भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरंधिर्मह्यं त्वादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: gṛbhṇā́mi ǀ te ǀ saubhaga-tvā́ya ǀ hástam ǀ máyā ǀ pátyā ǀ jarát-aṣṭiḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásaḥ ǀbhágaḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ savitā́ ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ tvā ǀ aduḥ ǀ gā́rha-patyāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I take thy hand in mine for happy fortune that thou mayst reach old age with me thy husband. Gods, Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitar, Purandhi, have given thee to be my household's mistress.
verses.wilson_translation: I take yourhandfor good fortune, that you may attain old age with me as your husband; the gods Bhaga,Aryaman,Savitā, Purandhi have given you to me, that I may be the master of a household.
verses.griffith_verse: I take thy hand in mine for happy fortune that thou mayst reach old age with me thy husband. Gods, Aryaman, Bhaga, Savitar, Purandhi, have given thee to be my household's mistress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तां पूषंछिवतमामेरयस्व यस्यां बीजं मनुष्या वपंति ।या न ऊरू उशती विश्रयाते यस्यामुशंतः प्रहराम शेपं ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́m ǀ pūṣan ǀ śivá-tamām ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayasva ǀ yásyām ǀ bī́jam ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ vápanti ǀyā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūrū́ íti ǀ uśatī́ ǀ vi-śráyāte ǀ yásyām ǀ uśántaḥ ǀ pra-hárāma ǀ śépam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Pūṣan, send her on as most auspicious, her who shall be the sharer of my pleasures; Her who shall twine her loving arms about me, and welcome all my love and mine embraces.
verses.wilson_translation: Pūṣan, inspire her who is most auspicious, in whom men may now seed, who most affectionate maybe devoted to us, and in whom animated by desire we may beget progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: O Pūṣan, send her on as most auspicious, her who shall be the sharer of my pleasures; Her who shall twine her loving arms about me, and welcome all my love and mine embraces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्यमग्रे पर्यवहन्त्सूर्यां वहतुना सह ।पुनः पतिभ्यो जायां दा अग्ने प्रजया सह ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ ágre ǀ pári ǀ avahan ǀ sūryā́m ǀ vahatúnā ǀ sahá ǀpúnaríti ǀ páti-bhyaḥ ǀ jāyā́m ǀ dā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ sahá ǁ
verses.english_translation: For thee, with bridal train, they, first, escorted Sūrya to her home. Give to the husband in return, Agni, the wife with progeny.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Gandharvas) gave Sūryato you,Agni, with her bridal ornaments; do you, Agni, give (us)husbands our wife back again withmaleoffspring.
verses.griffith_verse: For thee, with bridal train, they, first, escorted Sūrya to her home. Give to the husband in return, Agni, the wife with progeny.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनः पत्नीमग्निरदादायुषा सह वर्चसा ।दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतं ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaríti ǀ pátnīm ǀ agníḥ ǀ adāt ǀ ā́yuṣā ǀ sahá ǀ várcasā ǀdīrghá-āyuḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ jī́vāti ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ śatám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni hath given the bride again with splendour and with ample life. Long lived be he who is her lord; a hundred autumns let him live.
verses.wilson_translation: Agnigave the wife back again with life and splendour; may he who is her husband enjoying long lifelive a hundred years.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni hath given the bride again with splendour and with ample life. Long lived be he who is her lord; a hundred autumns let him live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमः प्रथमो विविदे गंधर्वो विविद उत्तरः ।तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ vivide ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ vivide ǀ út-taraḥ ǀtṛtī́yaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ te ǀ pátiḥ ǀ turī́yaḥ ǀ te ǀ manuṣya-jā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma obtained her first of all; next the Gandharva was her lord. Agai was thy third husband: now one bornof woman is thy fourth.
verses.wilson_translation: Somafirst obtained the bride; the Gandharvaobtained her next.Agniwas your third husband; yourfourth (husband) is born of man.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma obtained her first of all; next the Gandharva was her lord. Agai was thy third husband: now one bornof woman is thy fourth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय गंधर्वो दददग्नये ।रयिं च पुत्रांश्चादादग्निर्मह्यमथो इमां ॥
verses.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ dadat ǀ gandharvā́ya ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ dadat ǀ agnáye ǀrayím ǀ ca ǀ putrā́n ǀ ca ǀ adāt ǀ agníḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ átho íti ǀ imā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma to the Gandharva, and to Agni the Gandharva gave: And Agni hath bestowed on me riches and sons and this my spouse.
verses.wilson_translation: Somagave her to the Gandharva; the Gandharva gave her to Agni; Agni has given her to me andwealth and sons.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma to the Gandharva, and to Agni the Gandharva gave: And Agni hath bestowed on me riches and sons and this my spouse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इहैव स्तं मा वि यौष्टं विश्वमायुर्व्यश्नुतं ।क्रीळंतौ पुत्रैर्नप्तृभिर्मोदमानौ स्वे गृहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ evá ǀ stam ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ yauṣṭam ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśnutam ǀkrī́ḷantau ǀ putráiḥ ǀ náptṛ-bhiḥ ǀ módamānau ǀ své ǀ gṛhé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be ye not parted; dwell ye here reach the full time of human life. With sons and grandsons sport and play, rejoicing in your own abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Abide here together; may you never be separated; live together all your lives, sporting with sons andgrandsons, happy in your own home.
verses.griffith_verse: Be ye not parted; dwell ye here reach the full time of human life. With sons and grandsons sport and play, rejoicing in your own abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिराजरसाय समनक्त्वर्यमा ।अदुर्मंगलीः पतिलोकमा विश शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ janayatu ǀ prajā́-patiḥ ǀ ā-jarasā́ya ǀ sám ǀ anaktu ǀ aryamā́ ǀáduḥ-maṅgalīḥ ǀ pati-lokám ǀ ā́ ǀ viśa ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may Prajāpati bring children forth to us; may Aryaman adorn us till old age come nigh. Not inauspicious enter thou thy husband's house: bring blessing to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
verses.wilson_translation: May Prajāpatigrant us progeny, may Aryamanunite us together until old age; free from all evil omensenter your husband's abode, be the bringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds.
verses.griffith_verse: So may Prajāpati bring children forth to us; may Aryaman adorn us till old age come nigh. Not inauspicious enter thou thy husband's house: bring blessing to our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अघोरचक्षुरपतिघ्न्येधि शिवा पशुभ्यः सुमनाः सुवर्चाः ।वीरसूर्देवकामा स्योना शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: ághora-cakṣuḥ ǀ ápati-ghnī ǀ edhi ǀ śivā́ ǀ paśú-bhyaḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ su-várcāḥ ǀvīra-sū́ḥ ǀ devá-kāmā ǀ syonā́ ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not evil-eyed, no slayer of thy husband, bring weal to cattle, radiant, gentlehearted; Loving the Gods, delightful, bearing heroes, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.wilson_translation: (Look upon your husband) with no angry eye, be not hostile to your lord, be tender to animals, beamiable, be very glorious; be the mother ofmales, be devoted to the gods, be the bestower of happiness, be thebringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds.
verses.griffith_verse: Not evil-eyed, no slayer of thy husband, bring weal to cattle, radiant, gentlehearted; Loving the Gods, delightful, bearing heroes, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमां त्वमिंद्र मीढ्वः सुपुत्रां सुभगां कृणु ।दशास्यां पुत्राना धेहि पतिमेकादशं कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ mīḍhvaḥ ǀ su-putrā́m ǀ su-bhágām ǀ kṛṇu ǀdáśa ǀ asyām ǀ putrā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ dhehi ǀ pátim ǀ ekādaśám ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Bounteous Indra, make this bride blest in her sons and fortunate. Vouchsafe to her ten sons, and make her husband the eleventh man.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, showerer, make her the mother of sons, plural asing (to her husband); give her ten sons, make herhusband the eleventh.
verses.griffith_verse: O Bounteous Indra, make this bride blest in her sons and fortunate. Vouchsafe to her ten sons, and make her husband the eleventh man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सम्राज्ञी श्वशुरे भव सम्राज्ञी श्वश्र्वां भव ।ननांदरि सम्राज्ञी भव सम्राज्ञी अधि देवृषु ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-rā́jñī ǀ śváśure ǀ bhava ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ śvaśrvā́m ǀ bhava ǀnánāndari ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ bhava ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ ádhi ǀ devṛ́ṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Over thy husband's father and thy husband's mother bear full sway. Over the sister of thy lord, over his brothers rule supreme.
verses.wilson_translation: Be aqueento your father-in-law, be a queen to your mother-in-law, be a queen to your husband'ssister, be a queen to your husband's brother.
verses.griffith_verse: Over thy husband's father and thy husband's mother bear full sway. Over the sister of thy lord, over his brothers rule supreme.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समंजंतु विश्वे देवाः समापो हृदयानि नौ ।सं मातरिश्वा सं धाता समु देष्ट्री दधातु नौ ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ añjantu ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ hṛ́dayāni ǀ nau ǀsám ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ sám ǀ dhātā́ ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ déṣṭrī ǀ dadhātu ǀ nau ǁ
verses.english_translation: So may the Universal Gods, so may the Waters join our hearts. May Mātariśvan, Dhātar, and Destri together bind us close.
verses.wilson_translation: May the universal gods unite both our hearts; may the waters unite them; may Mātariśvan, Dhātāand the bountiful (Sarasvatī) unite both our hearts.
verses.griffith_verse: So may the Universal Gods, so may the Waters join our hearts. May Mātariśvan, Dhātar, and Destri together bind us close.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MEN have abstained from pouring juice they count not Indra as a God.Where at the votary's store my friend Vrsakapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all. Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vrsakapi hath wrought;Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all. What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vrsakapi,With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's foodful store? Supreme is Indra over all. Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the car,O Indra, that Vrsakapi whom thou protectest as a friend, Supreme is Indra over all. Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy.In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion sball be woo. Supreme is Indra over all. No Dame hath ampler charms than , or greater wealth of love's delights.None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all. Mother whose love is quickly wibn, I say what verily will be.My,breast, O Mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering. Supreme is Indra over all. Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits add ample hips,Why, O thou Hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vrsakapi? Supreme is Indra over all. This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love,Yet Heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts’ Friend and Indra's Queen. Supreme is Indra over all. From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice.Mother of Heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all. So have I heard Indrāṇī called most fortunate among these Dames,For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra overall. Never, Indralni, have I joyed without my friend Vrsakapi,Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all. Wealthy Vrsakapayi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons,Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all. Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare,And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all. Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds,Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all. O Indra this Vrsakapi hath found a slain wild animal,Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all. Distinguishing the Dāsa and the Ārya, viewing all, I go.I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all. The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread!Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vrsakapi. Supreme is Indra over all. Turn thee again Vrsakapi: we twain will bring thee happiness.Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all. When, Indra and Vrsakapi, ye travelled upward to your home,Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all. Daughter of Manu, Parsu bare a score of children at a birth.Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.

verses.sanskrit: वि हि सोतोरसृक्षत नेंद्रं देवममंसत ।यत्रामदद्वृषाकपिरर्यः पुष्टेषु मत्सखा विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ hí ǀ sótoḥ ǀ ásṛkṣata ǀ ná ǀ índram ǀ devám ǀ amaṃsata ǀyátra ǀ ámadat ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ puṣṭéṣu ǀ mát-sakhā ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: MEN have abstained from pouring juice they count not Indra as a God. Where at the votary's store my friend Vrsakapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.griffith_verse: MEN have abstained from pouring juice they count not Indra as a God. Where at the votary's store my friend Vrsakapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परा हींद्र धावसि वृषाकपेरति व्यथिः ।नो अह प्र विंदस्यन्यत्र सोमपीतये विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: párā ǀ hí ǀ indra ǀ dhā́vasi ǀ vṛṣā́kapeḥ ǀ áti ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀnó íti ǀ áha ǀ prá ǀ vindasi ǀ anyátra ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vrsakapi hath wrought; Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrāṇīspeaks: You,Indra, much annoyed, hasten towards Vṛṣākapi; and yet you find no otherplace to drink the Soma; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vrsakapi hath wrought; Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किमयं त्वां वृषाकपिश्चकार हरितो मृगः ।यस्मा इरस्यसीदु न्वर्यो वा पुष्टिमद्वसु विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ ayám ǀ tvā́m ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ cakā́ra ǀ háritaḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀyásmai ǀ irasyási ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ aryáḥ ǀ vā ǀ puṣṭi-mát ǀ vásu ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vrsakapi, With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's foodful store? Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: What (favour) has this tawny deer Vṛṣākapidone to you that you should like a liberal (benefactor)bestow upon him wealth and nourish me;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vrsakapi, With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's foodful store? Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यमिमं त्वं वृषाकपिं प्रियमिंद्राभिरक्षसि ।श्वा न्वस्य जंभिषदपि कर्णे वराहयुर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ imám ǀ tvám ǀ vṛṣā́kapim ǀ priyám ǀ indra ǀ abhi-rákṣasi ǀśvā́ ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ jambhiṣat ǀ ápi ǀ kárṇe ǀ varāha-yúḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the car, O Indra, that Vrsakapi whom thou protectest as a friend, Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: This Vṛṣākapiwhom you,Indra, cherish as your dear (son)-- may the dog which chases the boar(seize) him by the ear (and) devour him; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the car, O Indra, that Vrsakapi whom thou protectest as a friend, Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रिया तष्टानि मे कपिर्व्यक्ता व्यदूदुषत् ।शिरो न्वस्य राविषं न सुगं दुष्कृते भुवं विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: priyā́ ǀ taṣṭā́ni ǀ me ǀ kapíḥ ǀ ví-aktā ǀ ví ǀ adūduṣat ǀśíraḥ ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ rāviṣam ǀ ná ǀ su-gám ǀ duḥ-kṛ́te ǀ bhuvam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
