verses.english_translation: Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy. In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion sball be woo. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: The ape has spoiled the beloved ghī-adorned (oblations) made to me (by worshippers); let mequickly cut off his head, let me not be the giver of happiness to one who works evil;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy. In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion sball be woo. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न मत्स्त्री सुभसत्तरा न सुयाशुतरा भुवत् ।न मत्प्रतिच्यवीयसी न सक्थ्युद्यमीयसी विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ mát ǀ strī́ ǀ subhasát-tarā ǀ ná ǀ suyā́śu-tarā ǀ bhuvat ǀná ǀ mát ǀ práti-cyavīyasī ǀ ná ǀ sákthi ǀ út-yamīyasī ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: No Dame hath ampler charms than 1, or greater wealth of love's delights. None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: There is no woman more amiable than I am, not one who bears fairer sons than I; nor one moretractable not one more ardent;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: No Dame hath ampler charms than 1, or greater wealth of love's delights. None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उवे अंब सुलाभिके यथेवांग भविष्यति ।भसन्मे अंब सक्थि मे शिरो मे वीव हृष्यति विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: uvé ǀ amba ǀ sulābhike ǀ yáthā-iva ǀ aṅgá ǀ bhaviṣyáti ǀbhasát ǀ me ǀ amba ǀ sákthi ǀ me ǀ śíraḥ ǀ me ǀ ví-iva ǀ hṛṣyati ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Mother whose love is quickly wibn, I say what verily will be. My,breast, O Mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: [Vṛṣākapispeaks]: O mother, who are easy of access, it will quickly be as (you have said); may my(father) and you, mother, be united; may it delight my (father) and your head like a bird;Indrais above all (theworld).
verses.griffith_verse: Mother whose love is quickly wibn, I say what verily will be. My,breast, O Mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किं सुबाहो स्वंगुरे पृथुष्टो पृथुजाघने ।किं शूरपत्नि नस्त्वमभ्यमीषि वृषाकपिं विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ subāho íti su-bāho ǀ su-aṅgure ǀ pṛ́thusto íti pṛthu-sto ǀ pṛ́thu-jaghane ǀkím ǀ śūra-patni ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ abhí ǀ amīṣi ǀ vṛṣā́kapim ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits add ample hips, Why, O thou Hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vrsakapi? Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: [Indraspeaks]: You who have beautiful arms, who have beautiful fingers, long-haired, broad-hipped,why are you angry with our Vṛṣākapi, O you wife of a hero; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits add ample hips, Why, O thou Hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vrsakapi? Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवीरामिव मामयं शरारुरभि मन्यते ।उताहमस्मि वीरिणींद्रपत्नी मरुत्सखा विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: avī́rām-iva ǀ mā́m ǀ ayám ǀ śarā́ruḥ ǀ abhí ǀ manyate ǀutá ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǀ vīríṇī ǀ índra-patnī ǀ marút-sakhā ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love, Yet Heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts’ Friend and Indra's Queen. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: [Indrāṇīspeaks]: This savage beast (Vṛṣākapi) despises me as one who has nomale(protector),and yet I am the mother of male offspring, the wife of Indra, the friend of the Maruts; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love, Yet Heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts’ Friend and Indra's Queen. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: संहोत्रं स्म पुरा नारी समनं वाव गच्छति ।वेधा ऋतस्य वीरिणींद्रपत्नी मह��यते विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-hotrám ǀ sma ǀ purā́ ǀ nā́rī ǀ sámanam ǀ vā ǀ áva ǀ gacchati ǀvedhā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vīríṇī ǀ índra-patnī ǀ mahīyate ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice. Mother of Heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: The mother who is the instrumental tutress of the ceremony, the mother ofmaleoffspring, the wife of Indra,goes first to the united sacrifice to battle, (and) is honoured (by the praisers); Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice. Mother of Heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राणीमासु नारिषु सुभगामहमश्रवं ।नह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: indrāṇī́m ǀ āsú ǀ nā́riṣu ǀ su-bhágām ǀ ahám ǀ aśravam ǀnahí ǀ asyāḥ ǀ aparám ǀ caná ǀ jarásā ǀ márate ǀ pátiḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So have I heard Indrāṇī called most fortunate among these Dames, For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra overall.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indraspeaks]: I have heard that Indrāṇīis the most fortunate among these women, for her lord Indra, who is above all (the world), does ot die of old age like other (men).
verses.griffith_verse: So have I heard Indrāṇī called most fortunate among these Dames, For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra overall.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाहमिंद्राणि रारण सख्युर्वृषाकपेर्ऋते ।यस्येदमप्यं हविः प्रियं देवेषु गच्छति विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ indrāṇi ǀ raraṇa ǀ sákhyuḥ ǀ vṛṣā́kapeḥ ǀ ṛté ǀyásya ǀ idám ǀ ápyam ǀ havíḥ ǀ priyám ǀ devéṣu ǀ gácchati ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never, Indralni, have I joyed without my friend Vrsakapi, Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: I am not happy,Indrāṇi, without my friend Vṛṣākapi; whose acceptable oblation here, purified withwater, proceeds to the gods;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Never, Indralni, have I joyed without my friend Vrsakapi, Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषाकपायि रेवति सुपुत्र आदु सुस्नुषे ।घसत्त इंद्र उक्षणः प्रियं काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣākapāyi ǀ révati ǀ sú-putre ǀ ā́t ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú-snuṣe ǀghásat ǀ te ǀ índraḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ priyám ǀ kācit-karám ǀ havíḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wealthy Vrsakapayi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons, Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: [Vṛṣākapispeaks]: O mother of Vṛṣākapi, wealthy, possessing excellent sons, possessingexcellent daughters-in-law, let Indraeat your bulls, (give him) the beloved and most delightful ghī, Indra is aboveall (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Wealthy Vrsakapayi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons, Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उक्ष्णो हि मे पंचदश साकं पचंति विंशतिं ।उताहमद्मि पीव इदुभा कुक्षी पृणंति मे विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ukṣṇáḥ ǀ hí ǀ me ǀ páñca-daśa ǀ sākám ǀ pácanti ǀ viṃśatím ǀutá ǀ ahám ǀ admi ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ubhā́ ǀ kukṣī́ íti ǀ pṛṇanti ǀ me ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare, And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.wilson_translation: [Indraspeaks]: The worshippers dress for me fifteen (and) twenty bulls; I eat them and (become) fat,they fill both sides of my belly; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.griffith_verse: Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare, And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषभो न तिग्मशृंगोऽंतर्यूथेषु रोरुवत् ।मंथस्त इंद्र शं हृदे यं ते सुनोति भावयुर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ tigmá-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ yūthéṣu ǀ róruvat ǀmantháḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ śám ǀ hṛdé ǀ yám ǀ te ǀ sunóti ǀ bhāvayúḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds, Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all. 18 O Indra this Vrsakapi hath found a slain wild animal, Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all. 19 Distinguishing the Dāsa and the Ārya, viewing all, I go. I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all. 20 The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread! Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vrsakapi. Supreme is Indra over all. 21 Turn thee again Vrsakapi: we twain will bring thee happiness. Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all. 22 When, Indra and Vrsakapi, ye travelled upward to your home, Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all. 23 Daughter of Manu, Parsu bare a score of children at a birth. Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.
verses.wilson_translation: [Indrāṇīspeaks]: Like a sharp-horned bull roaring among the herds, so may your libation plural aseworld).
verses.griffith_verse: Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds, Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all. 18 O Indra this Vrsakapi hath found a slain wild animal, Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all. 19 Distinguishing the Dāsa and the Ārya, viewing all, I go. I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all. 20 The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread! Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vrsakapi. Supreme is Indra over all. 21 Turn thee again Vrsakapi: we twain will bring thee happiness. Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all. 22 When, Indra and Vrsakapi, ye travelled upward to your home, Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all. 23 Daughter of Manu, Parsu bare a score of children at a birth. Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न सेशे यस्य रंबतेऽंतरा सक्थ्या कपृत् ।सेदीशे यस्य रोमशं निषेदुषो विजृंभते विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ rámbate ǀ antarā́ ǀ sakthyā́ ǀ kápṛt ǀsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ romaśám ǀ ni-sedúṣaḥ ǀ vi-jṛ́mbhate ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man who is impotent begets not progeny, but he who is endowed with vigour;Indrais above all(the world).
verses.wilson_translation: The man who is impotent begets not progeny, but he who is endowed with vigour;Indrais above all(the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: न सेशे यस्य रोमशं निषेदुषो विजृंभते ।सेदीशे यस्य रंबतेऽंतरा सक्थ्या कपृद्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ romaśám ǀ ni-sedúṣaḥ ǀ vi-jṛ́mbhate ǀsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ rámbate ǀ antarā́ ǀ sakthyā́ ǀ kápṛt ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [Indraspeaks]: He who is endowed with vigour begets not progeny, but he who is impotent; Indra isabove all (the world).
verses.wilson_translation: [Indraspeaks]: He who is endowed with vigour begets not progeny, but he who is impotent; Indra isabove all (the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमिंद्र वृषाकपिः परस्वंतं हतं विदत् ।असिं सूनां नवं चरुमादेधस्यान आचितं विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ indra ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ párasvantam ǀ hatám ǀ vidat ǀasím ǀ sūnā́m ǀ návam ǀ carúm ǀ ā́t ǀ édhasya ǀ ánaḥ ǀ ā́-citam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [Indrāṇīspeaks]: Let this Vṛṣākapi,Indra, take a dead wild ass, (let him take) a knife (to cut it up),a fire-plural ce (to cook it), a new saucepan, and a cart full of fuel; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.wilson_translation: [Indrāṇīspeaks]: Let this Vṛṣākapi,Indra, take a dead wild ass, (let him take) a knife (to cut it up),a fire-plural ce (to cook it), a new saucepan, and a cart full of fuel; Indra is above all (the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: अयमेमि विचाकशद्विचिन्वंदासमार्यं ।पिबामि पाकसुत्वनोऽभि धीरमचाकशं विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ emi ǀ vi-cā́kaśat ǀ vi-cinván ǀ dā́sam ǀ ā́ryam ǀpíbāmi ǀ pāka-sútvanaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ dhī́ram ǀ acākaśam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: [Indraspeaks]: Here I come to the (sacrifice) looking upon (the worshippers), distinguishing the Dāsaand theĀrya; I drink (the Soma) of the (worshipper), who effuses (the Soma) with mature (mind); I look upon theintelligent (sacrificer); Indra is above all (the world).
verses.wilson_translation: [Indraspeaks]: Here I come to the (sacrifice) looking upon (the worshippers), distinguishing the Dāsaand theĀrya; I drink (the Soma) of the (worshipper), who effuses (the Soma) with mature (mind); I look upon theintelligent (sacrificer); Indra is above all (the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: धन्व च यत्कृंतत्रं च कति स्वित्ता वि योजना ।नेदीयसो वृषाकपेऽस्तमेहि गृहाँ उप विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhánva ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ kṛntátram ǀ ca ǀ káti ǀ svit ǀ tā́ ǀ ví ǀ yójanā ǀnédīyasaḥ ǀ vṛṣākape ǀ ástam ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ gṛhā́n ǀ úpa ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Go home, Vṣs.ākapi, to the halls of sacrifice (from the lurking- plural ce of the enemy), which is desertand forest (how many leagues are there from there?) and from the nearest (lurking-plural ce);Indrais above all (theworld).
verses.wilson_translation: Go home, Vṣs.ākapi, to the halls of sacrifice (from the lurking- plural ce of the enemy), which is desertand forest (how many leagues are there from there?) and from the nearest (lurking-plural ce);Indrais above all (theworld).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै ।य एष स्वप्ननंशनोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ vṛṣākape ǀ suvitā́ ǀ kalpayāvahai ǀyáḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ svapna-náṃśanaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ éṣi ǀ pathā́ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come back,Vṛṣākapi, that we may do what is agreeable to you; you, who are the destroyer ofsleep, come home again by the road;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.wilson_translation: Come back,Vṛṣākapi, that we may do what is agreeable to you; you, who are the destroyer ofsleep, come home again by the road;Indrais above all (the world).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: यदुदंचो वृषाकपे गृहमिंद्राजगंतन ।क्व स्य पुल्वघो मृगः कमगंजनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I BALM with oil the mighty Rakṣas-slayer; to the most famous Friend I come for shelterEnkindled, sharpened by our rites, may Agni protect us in the day and night from evil. O Jātavedas with the teeth of iron, enkindled with thy flame attack the demons.Seize with thy longue the foolish gods' adorers: rend, put within thy mouth the raw-flesh caters. Apply thy teeth, the upper and the lower, thou who hast both, enkindled and destroying.Roam also in the air, O King, around us, and with thy jaws assail the wicked spirits. Bending thy shafts through sacrifices, Agni, whetting their points with song as if with whetstones,Pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas, and break their arms uplifed to attack thee. Pierce through the Yātudhāna's skin, O Agni; let the destroying dart with fire consume him.Rend his joints, Jātavedas, let the cater of flesh, flesh-seeking, track his mangled body. Where now thou seest Agni Jātavedas, one of these demons standing still or roaming,Or flying on those paths in air's midregion, sharpen the shaft and as an archer pierce him. Tear from the evil spirit, Jātavedas, what he hath seized and with his spears hath captured.Blazing before him strike him down, O Agni; let spotted carrion-eating kites devour him. Here tell this forth, O Agni: whosoever is, he himself, or acteth as, a demon,Him grasp, O thou Most Youthful, with thy fuel. to the Mati-seer's eye give him as booty. With keen glance guard the sacrifice, O Agni: thou Sage, conduct it onward to the Vasus.Let not the fiends, O Man-beholder, harm thee burning against the Rākṣasas to slay them. Look on the fiend mid men, as Man-beholder: rend thou his three extremities in pieces.Demolish with thy flame his ribs, O Agni, the Yātudhāna's root destroy thou triply. Thrice, Agni, let thy noose surround the demon who with his falsehood injures Holy Order.Loud roaring with thy flame, O Jātavedas, crush him and cast him down before the singer. Lead thou the worshipper that eye, O Agni, wherewith thou lookest on the hoof-armed demon.With light celestial in Atharvan's manner burn up the foot who ruins truth with falsehood. Agni, what curse the pair this day have uttered, what heated word the worshippers have spoken,Each arrowy taunt sped from the angry spirit,—pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas. With fervent heat exterminate the demons; destroy the fiends with burning flame, O Agni.Destroy with fire the foolish gods' adorers; blaze and destrepy the insatiable monsters. May Gods destroy this day the evil-doer may each hot curse of his return and blast him.Let arrows pierce the liar in his vitals, and Visva's net enclose the Yātudhāna. The fiend who smears himself with flesh of cattle, with flesh of horses and of human bodies,Who steals the milch-cow's milk away, O Agni,—tear off the heads of such with fiery fury. The cow gives milk each year, O Man-regarder: let not the Yātudhāna ever taste it.If one would glut him with the biesting, Agni, pierce with thy flame his vitals as he meets thee. Let the fiends drink the poison of the cattle; may Aditi cast off the evildoers.May the God Savitar give them up to ruin, and be their share of plants and herbs denied them. Agni, from days of old thou slayest demons: never shall Rākṣasas in fight o’ercome thee.Burn up the foolish ones, the flesh-devourers: let none of them escape thine heavenly arrow. Guard us, O Agni, from above and under, protect us fl-om behind us and before us;And may thy flames, most fierce and never wasting, glowing with fervent heat, consume the sinner. From rear, from front, from under, from above us, O King, protect us as a Sage with wisdom.Guard to old age thy friend, O Friend, Eternal: O Agni, as Immortal, guard us mortals. We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni, thee a Sage,Of hero lineage, day by day, destroyer of our treacherous foes. Burn with thy poison turned against the treacherous brood of Rākṣasas,O Agni, with thy sharpened glow, with lances armed with points of flame. Burn thou the paired Kimīdins, brun, Agni, the Yātudhāna pairs.I sharpen thee, Infallible, with hymns. O Sage, be vigilant. Shoot forth, O Agni, with thy flame demolish them on every side.Break thou the Yātudhāna's strength, the vigour of the Rākṣasa.

verses.english_translation: I BALM with oil the mighty Rakṣas-slayer; to the most famous Friend I come for shelter Enkindled, sharpened by our rites, may Agni protect us in the day and night from evil.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer clarified butter to the powerful Agni, the slayer ofrākṣasas, I approach the most spaciousdwelling, the friend (of worshippers); Agni sharpening (his flames) is kindled by pious men; may he guard us frommalignant spirits by day and by night.
verses.griffith_verse: I BALM with oil the mighty Rakṣas-slayer; to the most famous Friend I come for shelter Enkindled, sharpened by our rites, may Agni protect us in the day and night from evil.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: O Jātavedas with the teeth of iron, enkindled with thy flame attack the demons. Seize with thy longue the foolish gods' adorers: rend, put within thy mouth the raw-flesh caters.
verses.wilson_translation: Jātavedas, who have teeth of iron, consume the Yātudhānas' flame when kindled, destroy thedestructive (spirits) with your tongue, cut up the eaters of flesh, and put them in your mouth.
verses.griffith_verse: O Jātavedas with the teeth of iron, enkindled with thy flame attack the demons. Seize with thy longue the foolish gods' adorers: rend, put within thy mouth the raw-flesh caters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Apply thy teeth, the upper and the lower, thou who hast both, enkindled and destroying. Roam also in the air, O King, around us, and with thy jaws assail the wicked spirits.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the destroyer (of therākṣasas), who have two (rows of teeth), sharpening them both, applythem to (the rākṣasas, and preserve) both the upper and the lower (world); and march, radiant (Agni, againstthe rākṣasas) in the firmament, seize theyātudhānaswith your jaws.
verses.griffith_verse: Apply thy teeth, the upper and the lower, thou who hast both, enkindled and destroying. Roam also in the air, O King, around us, and with thy jaws assail the wicked spirits.

verses.english_translation: Bending thy shafts through sacrifices, Agni, whetting their points with song as if with whetstones, Pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas, and break their arms uplifed to attack thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, do you, bending your arrows by means on your sacrifices and praise, and sharpening thejavelins with your splendours, pierce with them theyātudhānasto the heart, break their arms when raisedagainst you.
verses.griffith_verse: Bending thy shafts through sacrifices, Agni, whetting their points with song as if with whetstones, Pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas, and break their arms uplifed to attack thee.

verses.griffith_verse: Pierce through the Yātudhāna's skin, O Agni; let the destroying dart with fire consume him. Rend his joints, Jātavedas, let the cater of flesh, flesh-seeking, track his mangled body.

verses.wilson_translation: Wherever you now behold him,Agni Jātavedas, whether standing or moving, or passing along thepaths in the firmament, do you, O shooter sharpening (your arrows), transfix him with your shaft.
verses.griffith_verse: Where now thou seest Agni Jātavedas, one of these demons standing still or roaming, Or flying on those paths in air's midregion, sharpen the shaft and as an archer pierce him.

verses.wilson_translation: And defend me,Jātavedas, with your darts when I am seized, (defend me) from the Yātudhānaswho has seized me; anticipating him, do you,Agni, blazing fiercely, slay him; may the swift-flying vultures, theflesh-eaters, devour him.
verses.griffith_verse: Tear from the evil spirit, Jātavedas, what he hath seized and with his spears hath captured. Blazing before him strike him down, O Agni; let spotted carrion-eating kites devour him.

verses.wilson_translation: Agni, youngest of the gods, announce (to me present) at this (your sacrifice), which is your Yātudhāna who does this; destroy him with your kindled flame; beholder of men, consume him with yourbrilliance.

verses.wilson_translation: Today,Agni, when the married pair curse each other, then the praisers produce bitter words (in angeragainst each other), do you pierce the Yātudhānasthrough the heart with your arrow, which is genitive rated fromyour wrathful mind.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, what curse the pair this day have uttered, what heated word the worshippers have spoken, Each arrowy taunt sped from the angry spirit,—pierce to the heart therewith the Yātudhānas.

verses.english_translation: With fervent heat exterminate the demons; destroy the fiends with burning flame, O Agni. Destroy with fire the foolish gods' adorers; blaze and destrepy the insatiable monsters.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroy the Yātudhānaswith your scorching fire; destroy therākṣasas,Agni, with your heat;destroy with your radiance those who believe in vaid gods, fiercely blazing, destroy the insatiable.
verses.griffith_verse: With fervent heat exterminate the demons; destroy the fiends with burning flame, O Agni. Destroy with fire the foolish gods' adorers; blaze and destrepy the insatiable monsters.

verses.wilson_translation: Let all the gods today destroy the murderous (Yātudhāna); let our sharp imprecations encounterhim; may the arrows hit the speaker of falsehood in a vital part; may the Yātudhāna go into the bondage of theall-pervading Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: May Gods destroy this day the evil-doer may each hot curse of his return and blast him. Let arrows pierce the liar in his vitals, and Visva's net enclose the Yātudhāna.

verses.griffith_verse: The fiend who smears himself with flesh of cattle, with flesh of horses and of human bodies, Who steals the milch-cow's milk away, O Agni,—tear off the heads of such with fiery fury.

verses.wilson_translation: The milk of the cow is annually produced, let not the Yātudhānaconsume it, O beholder of men;whichever of them would like to satiate himself with the ambrosia, do you,Agni, pierce that contending(rākṣasa) with your flame in a vital part.

verses.english_translation: Let the fiends drink the poison of the cattle; may Aditi cast off the evildoers. May the God Savitar give them up to ruin, and be their share of plants and herbs denied them.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the Yātudhānadrink poison from the cattle; let the (rākṣasas) hard to overcome be cut topieces for the sake of Aditi; may the divine Savitāgive them over (to destruction), may they be deprived of thefood of herbs.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the fiends drink the poison of the cattle; may Aditi cast off the evildoers. May the God Savitar give them up to ruin, and be their share of plants and herbs denied them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Agni, from days of old thou slayest demons: never shall Rākṣasas in fight o’ercome thee. Burn up the foolish ones, the flesh-devourers: let none of them escape thine heavenly arrow.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, have from old time opposed the Yātudhāna; therākṣasashave never overcome you inbattles; burn murderous flesh-eating (rākṣasas) one by one; let them not escape your divine weapon
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, from days of old thou slayest demons: never shall Rākṣasas in fight o’ercome thee. Burn up the foolish ones, the flesh-devourers: let none of them escape thine heavenly arrow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Guard us, O Agni, from above and under, protect us fl-om behind us and before us; And may thy flames, most fierce and never wasting, glowing with fervent heat, consume the sinner.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Agni, protect us on the south, on the north, on the west, and on the east; may these, yourundecaying, scorching, blazing (flames), consume the perpetrator of wickedness.
verses.griffith_verse: Guard us, O Agni, from above and under, protect us fl-om behind us and before us; And may thy flames, most fierce and never wasting, glowing with fervent heat, consume the sinner.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: From rear, from front, from under, from above us, O King, protect us as a Sage with wisdom. Guard to old age thy friend, O Friend, Eternal: O Agni, as Immortal, guard us mortals.
verses.wilson_translation: Royal Agni, who are a sage, protect us by your wisdom on the west, on the east, on the south, on thenorth; do you, O friend, who are undecaying, (preserve me), your friend, to old age; do you who are immortal,(protect) us who are mortal.
verses.griffith_verse: From rear, from front, from under, from above us, O King, protect us as a Sage with wisdom. Guard to old age thy friend, O Friend, Eternal: O Agni, as Immortal, guard us mortals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni, thee a Sage, Of hero lineage, day by day, destroyer of our treacherous foes.
verses.wilson_translation: We meditate, strength-born Agni, on you, the accomplisher (of rites), the sage, of fearful form, thedestroyer of the treacherous day by day.
verses.griffith_verse: We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni, thee a Sage, Of hero lineage, day by day, destroyer of our treacherous foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Burn with thy poison turned against the treacherous brood of Rākṣasas, O Agni, with thy sharpened glow, with lances armed with points of flame.
verses.wilson_translation: Consume,Agni, the treacherousrākṣasaswith your all-pervading sharp flame, with yourflame-pointed darts.
verses.griffith_verse: Burn with thy poison turned against the treacherous brood of Rākṣasas, O Agni, with thy sharpened glow, with lances armed with points of flame.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.english_translation: Burn thou the paired Kimīdins, brun, Agni, the Yātudhāna pairs. I sharpen thee, Infallible, with hymns. O Sage, be vigilant.
verses.wilson_translation: Consume,Agni, these pairs of Yātudhānasand Kimīdins; I whet you, O sage, the invincible one,with my praises; wake up.
verses.griffith_verse: Burn thou the paired Kimīdins, brun, Agni, the Yātudhāna pairs. I sharpen thee, Infallible, with hymns. O Sage, be vigilant.

verses.english_translation: Shoot forth, O Agni, with thy flame demolish them on every side. Break thou the Yātudhāna's strength, the vigour of the Rākṣasa.
verses.wilson_translation: Destroy,Agni, with your flame, the impetuous might of the Yātudhāna; break the strength of therākṣasa.
verses.griffith_verse: Shoot forth, O Agni, with thy flame demolish them on every side. Break thou the Yātudhāna's strength, the vigour of the Rākṣasa.

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXVIII. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: १९ आंगिरसो मूर्धन्वान् , वामदेव्यो वा। सूर्य-वैश्वानरोऽग्निः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DEAR, ageless sacrificial drink is offered in light-discovering, heaven-pervading Agni.The Gods spread forth through his Celestial Nature, that he might bear the world up and sustain it. The world was swallowed and concealed in darkness: Agni was born, and light became apparent.The Deities, the broad earth, and the heavens, and plants, and waters gloried in his friendship. Inspired by Gods who claim our adoration, I now will laud Eternal Lofty Agni,Him who hath spread abroad the earth with lustre, this heaven, and both the worlds, and air's mid-region. Earliest Priest whom all the Gods accepted, and chose him, and anointed him with butter,He swiftly made all things that fly, stand, travel, all that hath motion, Agni Jātavedas. Because thou, Agni, Jātavedas, stoodest at the world's head with thy refulgent splendour,We sent thee forth with hymns and songs and praises: thou filledst heaven and earth, God meet for worship. Head of the world is Agni in the night-time; then, as the Sun, at morn springs up and rises.Then to his task goes the prompt Priest foreknowing the wondrous power of Gods who must be honoured. Lovely is he who, kindled in his greatness, hath shone forth, seated in the heavens, refulgent.With resonant hymns all Gods who guard our bodies have offered up oblation in this Agni. First the Gods brought the hymnal into being; then they engendered Agni, then oblation.He was their sacrifice that guards our bodies: him the heavens know, the earth, the waters know him. He, Agni, whom the Gods have generated, in whom they offered up all worlds and creatures,He with his bright glow heated earth and heaven, urging himself right onward in his grandeur. Then by the laud the Gods engendered Agni in heaven, who fills both worlds through strength and vigour.They made him to appear in threefold essence: he ripens plants of every form and nature. What time the Gods, whose due is worship, set him as Sūrya, Son of Aditi, in heaven,When the Pair, ever wandering, sprang to being, all creatures that existed looked upon them. For all the world of life the Gods made Agni Vaiśvānara to be the days' bright Banner,—Him who hath spread abroad the radiant Mornings, and, coming with his light, unveils the darkness. The wise and holy Deities engendered Agni Vaiśvānara whom age ne’er touches.The Ancient Star that wanders on for ever, lofty and. strong, Lord of the Living Being. We call upon the Sage with holy verses, Agni Vaiśvānara the ever-beaming,Who hath surpassed both heaven and earth in greatness: he is a God below, a God above us. I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals.On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother. These two united paths bear him who journeys born from the head and pondered with the spiritHe stands directed to all things existing, hasting, unresting in his fiery splendour. Which of us twain knows where they speak together, upper and lower of the two rite-leaders?Our friends have helped to gather our assembly. They came to sacrifice; who will announce it? How many are the Fires and Suns in number? What is the number of the Dawns and Waters?Not jestingly I speak to you, O Fathers. Sages, I ask you this for information. As great as is the fair-winged Morning's presence to him who dwells beside us, Mātariśvan!Is what the Brahman does when he approaches to sacrifice and sits below the Hotar.

verses.sanskrit: हविष्पांतमजरं स्वर्विदि दिविस्पृश्याहुतं जुष्टमग्नौ ।तस्य भर्मणे भुवनाय देवा धर्मणे कं स्वधया पप्रथंत ॥
verses.transliteration: havíḥ ǀ pā́ntam ǀ ajáram ǀ svaḥ-vídi ǀ divi-spṛ́śi ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ júṣṭam ǀ agnáu ǀtásya ǀ bhármaṇe ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dhármaṇe ǀ kám ǀ svadháyā ǀ paprathanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: DEAR, ageless sacrificial drink is offered in light-discovering, heaven-pervading Agni. The Gods spread forth through his Celestial Nature, that he might bear the world up and sustain it.
verses.wilson_translation: The whole world swallowed up, hidden in darkness, was made manifest when Agniwas born; thegods, heaven and earth, the waters and the plural nts rejoiced in his friendship.
verses.griffith_verse: DEAR, ageless sacrificial drink is offered in light-discovering, heaven-pervading Agni. The Gods spread forth through his Celestial Nature, that he might bear the world up and sustain it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गीर्णं भुवनं तमसापगूळ्हमाविः स्वरभवज्जाते अग्नौ ।तस्य देवाः पृथिवी द्यौरुतापोऽरणयन्नोषधीः सख्ये अस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: gīrṇám ǀ bhúvanam ǀ támasā ǀ ápa-gūḷham ǀ āvíḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ jāté ǀ agnáu ǀtásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ utá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ áraṇayan ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ asya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The world was swallowed and concealed in darkness: Agni was born, and light became apparent. The Deities, the broad earth, and the heavens, and plants, and waters gloried in his friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: Sent by adorable gods I praise the undecaying and mighty Agni, who by his radiance has spread forththe earth and this heaven, the two worlds and the firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: The world was swallowed and concealed in darkness: Agni was born, and light became apparent. The Deities, the broad earth, and the heavens, and plants, and waters gloried in his friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवेभिर्न्विषितो यज्ञियेभिरग्निं स्तोषाण्यजरं बृहंतं ।यो भानुना पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमामाततान रोदसी अंतरिक्षं ॥
verses.transliteration: devébhiḥ ǀ nú ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yajñíyebhiḥ ǀ agním ǀ stoṣāṇi ǀ ajáram ǀ bṛhántam ǀyáḥ ǀ bhānúnā ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ utá ǀ imā́m ǀ ā-tatā́na ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antárikṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Inspired by Gods who claim our adoration, I now will laud Eternal Lofty Agni, Him who hath spread abroad the earth with lustre, this heaven, and both the worlds, and air's mid-region.
verses.wilson_translation: Who propitiated by the gods was the first offerer of oblations, whom his worshippers anoint withclarified butter-- he,Agni Jātavedas, quickly made that which can fly, that which can walk, that which isstationary, that which is moveable.
verses.griffith_verse: Inspired by Gods who claim our adoration, I now will laud Eternal Lofty Agni, Him who hath spread abroad the earth with lustre, this heaven, and both the worlds, and air's mid-region.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो होतासीत्प्रथमो देवजुष्टो यं समांजन्नाज्येना वृणानाः ।स पतत्रीत्वरं स्था जगद्यच्छ्वात्रमग्निरकृणोज्जातवेदाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ā́sīt ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ devá-juṣṭaḥ ǀ yám ǀ sam-ā́ñjan ǀ ā́jyena ǀ vṛṇānā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ patatrí ǀ itvarám ǀ sthā́ḥ ǀ jágat ǀ yát ǀ śvātrám ǀ agníḥ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Earliest Priest whom all the Gods accepted, and chose him, and anointed him with butter, He swiftly made all things that fly, stand, travel, all that hath motion, Agni Jātavedas.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as you abide,Agni Jātavedas, on the brow of the universe, together with the sun, we havecome to you with praises, with hymns, with prayers; you are adorable, the satisfier of heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Earliest Priest whom all the Gods accepted, and chose him, and anointed him with butter, He swiftly made all things that fly, stand, travel, all that hath motion, Agni Jātavedas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्जातवेदो भुवनस्य मूर्धन्नतिष्ठो अग्ने सह रोचनेन ।तं त्वाहेम मतिभिर्गीर्भिरुक्थैः स यज्ञियो अभवो रोदसिप्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ mūrdhán ǀ átiṣṭhaḥ ǀ agne ǀ sahá ǀ rocanéna ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ ahema ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ rodasi-prā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Because thou, Agni, Jātavedas, stoodest at the world's head with thy refulgent splendour, We sent thee forth with hymns and songs and praises: thou filledst heaven and earth, God meet for worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis the head of all beings by night; then the sun rising early is born; (the wise know) this to be thewisdom of the adorable gods, that the swift- moving sun being intelligent moves through the firmameṇṭ
verses.griffith_verse: Because thou, Agni, Jātavedas, stoodest at the world's head with thy refulgent splendour, We sent thee forth with hymns and songs and praises: thou filledst heaven and earth, God meet for worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् ।मायामू तु यज्ञियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: mūrdhā́ ǀ bhuváḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ náktam ǀ agníḥ ǀ tátaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ jāyate ǀ prātáḥ ǀ ut-yán ǀmāyā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tú ǀ yajñíyānām ǀ etā́m ǀ ápaḥ ǀ yát ǀ tū́rṇiḥ ǀ cárati ǀ pra-jānán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Head of the world is Agni in the night-time; then, as the Sun, at morn springs up and rises. Then to his task goes the prompt Priest foreknowing the wondrous power of Gods who must be honoured.
verses.wilson_translation: He who shines visible to all through his greatness radiant, having his station in the sky, resplendentinhim,Agni, the unversal gods, the guardians of men's bodies, have presented an oblation with the voice of
verses.griffith_verse: Head of the world is Agni in the night-time; then, as the Sun, at morn springs up and rises. Then to his task goes the prompt Priest foreknowing the wondrous power of Gods who must be honoured.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दृशेन्यो यो महिना समिद्धोऽरोचत दिवियोनिर्विभावा ।तस्मिन्नग्नौ सूक्तवाकेन देवा हविर्विश्व आजुहवुस्तनूपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: dṛśényaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ árocata ǀ diví-yoniḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀtásmin ǀ agnáu ǀ sūkta-vākéna ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ā́ ǀ ajuhavuḥ ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lovely is he who, kindled in his greatness, hath shone forth, seated in the heavens, refulgent. With resonant hymns all Gods who guard our bodies have offered up oblation in this Agni.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods first genitive rated the words of the hymn, then Agni, then the oblation; he is the (object of the)sacrifice of these deities, the protector of the body; him the heaven knows, him the earth and the waters, know.
verses.griffith_verse: Lovely is he who, kindled in his greatness, hath shone forth, seated in the heavens, refulgent. With resonant hymns all Gods who guard our bodies have offered up oblation in this Agni.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूक्तवाकं प्रथममादिदग्निमादिद्धविरजनयंत देवाः ।स एषां यज्ञो अभवत्तनूपास्तं द्यौर्वेद तं पृथिवी तमापः ॥
verses.transliteration: sūkta-vākám ǀ prathamám ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ agním ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ havíḥ ǀ ajanayanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǀ tám ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ veda ǀ tám ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ tám ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: First the Gods brought the hymnal into being; then they engendered Agni, then oblation. He was their sacrifice that guards our bodies: him the heavens know, the earth, the waters know him.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniwhom the gods genitive rated, in whom all beings have offered oblations-- he, the straight-going, haswarmed by his \radiance, by his might, the earth and his heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: First the Gods brought the hymnal into being; then they engendered Agni, then oblation. He was their sacrifice that guards our bodies: him the heavens know, the earth, the waters know him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं देवासोऽजनयंताग्निं यस्मिन्नाजुहवुर्भुवनानि विश्वा ।सो अर्चिषा पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमामृजूयमानो अतपन्महित्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ájanayanta ǀ agním ǀ yásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ ájuhavuḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀsáḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ utá ǀ imā́m ǀ ṛju-yámānaḥ ǀ atapat ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, Agni, whom the Gods have generated, in whom they offered up all worlds and creatures, He with his bright glow heated earth and heaven, urging himself right onward in his grandeur.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have by praise engendered Agniin the sky, who fills heaven and earth by his functions, theyappointed the joy-bestowing Agni to his three- fold condition, he brings the manifold plural nts to maturity.
verses.griffith_verse: He, Agni, whom the Gods have generated, in whom they offered up all worlds and creatures, He with his bright glow heated earth and heaven, urging himself right onward in his grandeur.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनंछक्तिभी रोदसिप्रां ।तमू अकृण्वंत्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: stómena ǀ hí ǀ diví ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ agním ǀ ájījanan ǀ śákti-bhiḥ ǀ rodasi-prā́m ǀtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ akṛṇvan ǀ tredhā́ ǀ bhuvé ǀ kám ǀ sáḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ pacati ǀ viśvá-rūpāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then by the laud the Gods engendered Agni in heaven, who fills both worlds through strength and vigour. They made him to appear in threefold essence: he ripens plants of every form and nature.
verses.wilson_translation: When the adorable gods, plural ced him and Sūrya, the son of Aditi, in heaven; when the swift-movingpair (Agniand Vaiśvānara) appeared, then all beings beheld them.
verses.griffith_verse: Then by the laud the Gods engendered Agni in heaven, who fills both worlds through strength and vigour. They made him to appear in threefold essence: he ripens plants of every form and nature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदेदेनमदधुर्यज्ञियासो दिवि देवाः सूर्यमादितेयं ।यदा चरिष्णू मिथुनावभूतामादित्प्रापश्यन्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ ít ǀ enam ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ diví ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ āditeyám ǀyadā́ ǀ cariṣṇū́ íti ǀ mithunáu ǀ ábhūtām ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ prá ǀ apaśyan ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time the Gods, whose due is worship, set him as Sūrya, Son of Aditi, in heaven, When the Pair, ever wandering, sprang to being, all creatures that existed looked upon them.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods made Agni Vaiśvānara, the indicator of days, for the sake of the whole world, whostretched out the radiant dawns, and as he moves along scatters the darkness with his light.
verses.griffith_verse: What time the Gods, whose due is worship, set him as Sūrya, Son of Aditi, in heaven, When the Pair, ever wandering, sprang to being, all creatures that existed looked upon them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वस्मा अग्निं भुवनाय देवा वैश्वानरं केतुमह्नामकृण्वन् ।आ यस्ततानोषसो विभातीरपो ऊर्णोति तमो अर्चिषा यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: víśvasmai ǀ agním ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vaiśvānarám ǀ ketúm ǀ áhnām ǀ akṛṇvan ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ tatā́na ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ ápo íti ǀ ūrṇoti ǀ támaḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀ yán ǁ
verses.english_translation: For all the world of life the Gods made Agni Vaiśvānara to be the days' bright Banner,— Him who hath spread abroad the radiant Mornings, and, coming with his light, unveils the darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise and adorable gods engendered the imperishable Agni Vaiśvānara; he overcame (with hislight) the ancient swift-moving Nakṣatra, the overseer of the adorable (deity), mighty and great.
verses.griffith_verse: For all the world of life the Gods made Agni Vaiśvānara to be the days' bright Banner,— Him who hath spread abroad the radiant Mornings, and, coming with his light, unveils the darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानरं कवयो यज्ञियासोऽग्निं देवा अजनयन्नजुर्यं ।नक्षत्रं प्रत्नममिनच्चरिष्णु यक्षस्याध्यक्षं तविषं बृहंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: vaiśvānarám ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ agním ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ajanayan ǀ ajuryám ǀnákṣatram ǀ pratnám ǀ áminat ǀ cariṣṇú ǀ yakṣásya ǀ ádhi-akṣam ǀ taviṣám ǀ bṛhántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wise and holy Deities engendered Agni Vaiśvānara whom age ne’er touches. The Ancient Star that wanders on for ever, lofty and. strong, Lord of the Living Being.
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify daily with praises the brilliant and sage Agni Vaiśvānara, the god who overcomes by hismight both heaven and earth, (burning) both below and above.
verses.griffith_verse: The wise and holy Deities engendered Agni Vaiśvānara whom age ne’er touches. The Ancient Star that wanders on for ever, lofty and. strong, Lord of the Living Being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानरं विश्वहा दीदिवांसं मंत्रैरग्निं कविमच्छा वदामः ।यो महिम्ना परिबभूवोर्वी उतावस्तादुत देवः परस्तात् ॥
verses.transliteration: vaiśvānarám ǀ viśváhā ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ mántraiḥ ǀ agním ǀ kavím ǀ áccha ǀ vadāmaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ mahimnā́ ǀ pari-babhū́va ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ utá ǀ avástāt ǀ utá ǀ deváḥ ǀ parástāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call upon the Sage with holy verses, Agni Vaiśvānara the ever-beaming, Who hath surpassed both heaven and earth in greatness: he is a God below, a God above us.
verses.wilson_translation: I have heard that there are two paths for Pitṛs, gods and mortals; all this universe which is betweenthe paternal (heaven) and the maternal (earth) proceeds on its way by these two (paths).
verses.griffith_verse: We call upon the Sage with holy verses, Agni Vaiśvānara the ever-beaming, Who hath surpassed both heaven and earth in greatness: he is a God below, a God above us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वे स्रुती अशृणवं पितॄणामहं देवानामुत मर्त्यानां ।ताभ्यामिदं विश्वमेजत्समेति यदंतरा पितरं मातरं च ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ srutī́ íti ǀ aśṛṇavam ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ahám ǀ devā́nām ǀ utá ǀ mártyānām ǀtā́bhyām ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ éjat ǀ sám ǀ eti ǀ yát ǀ antarā́ ǀ pitáram ǀ mātáram ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals. On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother.
verses.wilson_translation: The associated two (heaven and earth) support (Agni) moving, born from the head, sanctified bypraise; diligent, rapid, radiant, he appears in the presence of all beings.
verses.griffith_verse: I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals. On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वे समीची बिभृतश्चरंतं शीर्षतो जातं मनसा विमृष्टं ।स प्रत्यङ्विश्वा भुवनानि तस्थावप्रयुच्छंतरणिर्भ्राजमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ bibhṛtaḥ ǀ cárantam ǀ śīrṣatáḥ ǀ jātám ǀ mánasā ǀ ví-mṛṣṭam ǀsáḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tasthau ǀ ápra-yucchan ǀ taráṇiḥ ǀ bhrā́jamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These two united paths bear him who journeys born from the head and pondered with the spirit He stands directed to all things existing, hasting, unresting in his fiery splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: When the lower and upper (fire) disputed "which of us twain leaders of sacrifice knows the work best?"then the friends (the priests) were competent (to offer) sacrifice, they came to the sacrifice; who declares this?
verses.griffith_verse: These two united paths bear him who journeys born from the head and pondered with the spirit He stands directed to all things existing, hasting, unresting in his fiery splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्रा वदेते अवरः परश्च यज्ञन्योः कतरो नौ वि वेद ।आ शेकुरित्सधमादं सखायो नक्षंत यज्ञं क इदं वि वोचत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ vádete íti ǀ ávaraḥ ǀ páraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yajña-nyóḥ ǀ kataráḥ ǀ nau ǀ ví ǀ veda ǀā́ ǀ śekuḥ ǀ ít ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ nákṣanta ǀ yajñám ǀ káḥ ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ vocat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Which of us twain knows where they speak together, upper and lower of the two rite-leaders? Our friends have helped to gather our assembly. They came to sacrifice; who will announce it?
verses.wilson_translation: How many fires are there, how many suns, how many dawns, how many waters? I address you, OPitṛs, not in rivalry, I ask you, sages, in order to know (the truth).
verses.griffith_verse: Which of us twain knows where they speak together, upper and lower of the two rite-leaders? Our friends have helped to gather our assembly. They came to sacrifice; who will announce it?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कत्यग्नयः कति सूर्यासः कत्युषासः कत्यु स्विदापः ।नोपस्पिजं वः पितरो वदामि पृच्छामि वः कवयो विद्मने कं ॥
verses.transliteration: káti ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ káti ǀ sū́ryāsaḥ ǀ káti ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ káti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svit ǀ ā́paḥ ǀná ǀ upa-spíjam ǀ vaḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ vadāmi ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ vaḥ ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ vidmáne ǀ kám ǁ
verses.english_translation: How many are the Fires and Suns in number? What is the number of the Dawns and Waters? Not jestingly I speak to you, O Fathers. Sages, I ask you this for information.
verses.wilson_translation: As long,Mātariśvan, as the swiftly-moving (nights) cover the face of the dawn, (so long) the Brahman, the inferior sitting down (to perform the work) of the Hotā, approaching the sacrifice supports (theceremony).
verses.griffith_verse: How many are the Fires and Suns in number? What is the number of the Dawns and Waters? Not jestingly I speak to you, O Fathers. Sages, I ask you this for information.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN LXXXIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I WILL extol the most heroic Indra who with his might forced earth and sky asunder;Who hath filled all with width as man's Upholder, surpassing floods and rivers in his greatness. Sūrya is he: throughout the wide expanses shall Indra turn him, swift as car-wheels, hither,Like a stream resting not but ever active he hath destroyed, with light, the black-hued darkness. To him I sing a holy prayer, incessant new, matchless, common to the earth and heaven,Who marks, as they were backs, all living creatures: ne’er doth he fail a friend, the noble Indra. I will send forth my songs in flow unceasing, like water from the ocean's depth, to Indra.Who to his car on both its sides securely hath fixed the earth and heaven as with an axle. Rousing with draughts, the Shaker, rushing onward, impetuous, very strong, armed as with arrowsIs Soma; forest trees and all the bushes deceive not Indra with their offered likeness. Soma hath flowed to him whom naught can equal, the earth, the heavens, the firmament, the mountains,—When heightened in his ire his indignation shatters the firm and breaks the strong in pieces. As an axe fells the tree so be slew Vṛtra, brake down the strongholds and dug out the rivers.He cleft the mountain like a new-made pitcher. Indra brought forth the kine with his Companions. Wise art thou, Punisher of guilt, O Indra. The sword lops limbs, thou smitest down the sinner,The men who injure, as it were a comrade, the lofty Law of Varuṇa and Mitra. Men who lead evil lives, who break agreements, and injure Varuṇa, Aryaman and Mitra,—Against these foes, O Mighty Indra, sharpen, as furious death, thy Bull of fiery colour. Indra is Sovran Lord of Earth and Heaven, Indra is Lord of waters and of mountains.Indra is Lord of prosperers and sages Indra must be invoked in rest and effort. Vaster than days and nights, Giver of increase, vaster than firmament and flood of ocean,Vaster than bounds of earth and wind's extension, vaster than rivers and our lands is Indra. Forward, as herald of refulgent Morning, let thine insatiate arrow fly, O Indra.And pierce, as ’twere a stone launched forth from heaven, with hottest blaze the men who love deception. Him, verily, the moons, the mountains followed, the tall trees followed and the plants and herbage.Yearning with love both Worlds approached, the Waters waited on Indra when he first had being. Where was the vengeful dart when thou, O Indra, clavest the demon ever beat on outrage?When fiends lay there upon the ground extended like cattle in the place of immolation? Those who are set in enmity against us, the Ogaṇas, O Indra, waxen mighty,—Let blinding darkness follow those our foemen, while these shall have bright shining nights to light them. May plentiful libations of the people, and singing Ṛṣis’ holy prayers rejoice thee.Hearing with love this common invocation, come unto us, pass by all those who praise thee. O Indra, thus may we be made partakers of thy new favours that shall bring us profit.Singing with love, may we the Viśvāmitras win daylight even now through thee, O Indra. Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best hero in the fight where spoil is gathered,The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रं स्तवा नृतमं यस्य मह्ना विबबाधे रोचना वि ज्मो अंतान् ।आ यः पप्रौ चर्षणीधृद्वरोभिः प्र सिंधुभ्यो रिरिचानो महित्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: índram ǀ stava ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ yásya ǀ mahnā́ ǀ vi-babādhé ǀ rocanā́ ǀ ví ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántān ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ papráu ǀ carṣaṇi-dhṛ́t ǀ váraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ prá ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ riricānáḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I WILL extol the most heroic Indra who with his might forced earth and sky asunder; Who hath filled all with width as man's Upholder, surpassing floods and rivers in his greatness.
verses.wilson_translation: Praise Indra, the chief leadere (of rites), whose glory surpasses the lustre (of others), and the ends ofthe earth; the sustainer of man, who exceeding the ocean in magnitude, fills (heaven and earth) with radiance.
verses.griffith_verse: I WILL extol the most heroic Indra who with his might forced earth and sky asunder; Who hath filled all with width as man's Upholder, surpassing floods and rivers in his greatness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स सूर्यः पर्युरू वरांस्येंद्रो ववृत्याद्रथ्येव चक्रा ।अतिष्ठंतमपस्यं न सर्गं कृष्णा तमांसि त्विष्या जघान ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ pári ǀ urú ǀ várāṃsi ǀ ā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vavṛtyāt ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǀátiṣṭhantam ǀ apasyám ǀ ná ǀ sárgam ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ támāṃsi ǀ tvíṣyā ǀ jaghāna ǁ
verses.english_translation: Sūrya is he: throughout the wide expanses shall Indra turn him, swift as car-wheels, hither, Like a stream resting not but ever active he hath destroyed, with light, the black-hued darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: The heroic Indracauses numerous rays of light revolve as a charioteer (effects the rotation of) thewheels of the chariot; he destroys by his radiance the black darkness like a restless active horse.
verses.griffith_verse: Sūrya is he: throughout the wide expanses shall Indra turn him, swift as car-wheels, hither, Like a stream resting not but ever active he hath destroyed, with light, the black-hued darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानमस्मा अनपावृदर्च क्ष्मया दिवो असमं ब्रह्म नव्यं ।वि यः पृष्ठेव जनिमान्यर्य इंद्रश्चिकाय न सखायमीषे ॥
verses.transliteration: samānám ǀ asmai ǀ ánapa-vṛt ǀ arca ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ásamam ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀví ǀ yáḥ ǀ pṛṣṭhā́-iva ǀ jánimāni ǀ aryáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ cikā́ya ǀ ná ǀ sákhāyam ǀ īṣé ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him I sing a holy prayer, incessant new, matchless, common to the earth and heaven, Who marks, as they were backs, all living creatures: ne’er doth he fail a friend, the noble Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Sing along with me a new song, unceasing, surpassing heaven and earth, to him who like thepṛṣṭha(praises), born at sacrifices, overcomes his enemies,Indrawho desires no friend.
verses.griffith_verse: To him I sing a holy prayer, incessant new, matchless, common to the earth and heaven, Who marks, as they were backs, all living creatures: ne’er doth he fail a friend, the noble Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्राय गिरो अनिशितसर्गा अपः प्रेरयं सगरस्य बुध्नात् ।यो अक्षेणेव चक्रिया शचीभिर्विष्वक्तस्तंभ पृथिवीमुत द्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: índrāya ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ániśita-sargāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ prá ǀ īrayam ǀ ságarasya ǀ budhnā́t ǀyáḥ ǀ ákṣeṇa-iva ǀ cakríyā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ víṣvak ǀ tastámbha ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will send forth my songs in flow unceasing, like water from the ocean's depth, to Indra. Who to his car on both its sides securely hath fixed the earth and heaven as with an axle.
verses.wilson_translation: I will utter praises to Indrain unceasing flow, (I will send) waters from the depth of the firmament (tohim) who has fixed heaven and earth on both sides by his acts as the wheels of a chariot (are fixed) by the axle.
verses.griffith_verse: I will send forth my songs in flow unceasing, like water from the ocean's depth, to Indra. Who to his car on both its sides securely hath fixed the earth and heaven as with an axle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपांतमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवांछरुमाँ ऋजीषी ।सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́pānta-manyuḥ ǀ tṛpála-prabharmā ǀ dhúniḥ ǀ śímī-vān ǀ śáru-mān ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀsómaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ atasā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ ná ǀ arvā́k ǀ índram ǀ prati-mā́nāni ǀ debhuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Rousing with draughts, the Shaker, rushing onward, impetuous, very strong, armed as with arrows Is Soma; forest trees and all the bushes deceive not Indra with their offered likeness.
verses.wilson_translation: Appeasing wrath, striking quickly, intimidating foes, doer of great deeds, armed with weapons,possessing the stale residue,Somanourishes all the Atasa woods, they oppose no impediments against Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: Rousing with draughts, the Shaker, rushing onward, impetuous, very strong, armed as with arrows Is Soma; forest trees and all the bushes deceive not Indra with their offered likeness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न यस्य द्यावापृथिवी न धन्व नांतरिक्षं नाद्रयः सोमो अक्षाः ।यदस्य मन्युरधिनीयमानः शृणाति वीळु रुजति स्थिराणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ dhánva ǀ ná ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ná ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ akṣāríti ǀyát ǀ asya ǀ manyúḥ ǀ adhi-nīyámānaḥ ǀ śṛṇā́ti ǀ vīḷú ǀ rujáti ǀ sthirā́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma hath flowed to him whom naught can equal, the earth, the heavens, the firmament, the mountains,— When heightened in his ire his indignation shatters the firm and breaks the strong in pieces.
verses.wilson_translation: Of whom neither heaven and earth, nor the water, nor the firmament, nor the mountains (are theobstructions) for him doth the Somaexude, when his wrath reaching his enemies destroys the strong and breaksthe firm.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma hath flowed to him whom naught can equal, the earth, the heavens, the firmament, the mountains,— When heightened in his ire his indignation shatters the firm and breaks the strong in pieces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जघान वृत्रं स्वधितिर्वनेव रुरोज पुरो अरदन्न सिंधून् ।बिभेद गिरिं नवमिन्न कुंभमा गा इंद्रो अकृणुत स्वयुग्भिः ॥
verses.transliteration: jaghā́na ǀ vṛtrám ǀ svá-dhitiḥ ǀ vánā-iva ǀ rurója ǀ púraḥ ǀ áradat ǀ ná ǀ síndhūn ǀbibhéda ǀ girím ǀ návam ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ kumbhám ǀ ā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ akṛṇuta ǀ svayúk-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As an axe fells the tree so be slew Vṛtra, brake down the strongholds and dug out the rivers. He cleft the mountain like a new-made pitcher. Indra brought forth the kine with his Companions.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra) slew Vṛtraas an axe (cuts down) a tree; he demolished the cities (of the foes), he dug out therivers; he shattered the cloud like a new pitcher; with his allies (the Maruts) he recovered the cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: As an axe fells the tree so be slew Vṛtra, brake down the strongholds and dug out the rivers. He cleft the mountain like a new-made pitcher. Indra brought forth the kine with his Companions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं ह त्यदृणया इंद्र धीरोऽसिर्न पर्व वृजिना शृणासि ।प्र ये मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम युजं न जना मिनंति मित्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ ṛṇa-yā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ asíḥ ǀ ná ǀ párva ǀ vṛjinā́ ǀ śṛṇāsi ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ yújam ǀ ná ǀ jánāḥ ǀ minánti ǀ mitrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise art thou, Punisher of guilt, O Indra. The sword lops limbs, thou smitest down the sinner, The men who injure, as it were a comrade, the lofty Law of Varuṇa and Mitra.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, who are wise, punish the guilt (of worshippers); you cut off their sins as a sword (cuts off)the limbs (of victims); (you cut off) the people who (ignorantly) injure the supporting (function) of Mitra, and Varuṇa, (which is) as it were their close friend.
verses.griffith_verse: Wise art thou, Punisher of guilt, O Indra. The sword lops limbs, thou smitest down the sinner, The men who injure, as it were a comrade, the lofty Law of Varuṇa and Mitra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र ये मित्रं प्रार्यमणं दुरेवाः प्र संगिरः प्र वरुणं मिनंति ।न्यमित्रेषु वधमिंद्र तुम्रं वृषन्वृषाणमरुषं शिशीहि ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ mitrám ǀ prá ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǀ prá ǀ sam-gíraḥ ǀ prá ǀ váruṇam ǀ minánti ǀní ǀ amítreṣu ǀ vadhám ǀ indra ǀ túmram ǀ vṛ́ṣan ǀ vṛ́ṣāṇam ǀ aruṣám ǀ śiśīhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men who lead evil lives, who break agreements, and injure Varuṇa, Aryaman and Mitra,— Against these foes, O Mighty Indra, sharpen, as furious death, thy Bull of fiery colour.
verses.wilson_translation: Against those who sinfully offend against Mitra,Aryaman, your companons (the Maruts) and Varuṇa,against these your enemies sharpen,Indra, showerer (of benefits), your rapid showering radiant thunderbolt.
verses.griffith_verse: Men who lead evil lives, who break agreements, and injure Varuṇa, Aryaman and Mitra,— Against these foes, O Mighty Indra, sharpen, as furious death, thy Bull of fiery colour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो दिव इंद्र ईशे पृथिव्या इंद्रो अपामिंद्र इत्पर्वतानां ।इंद्रो वृधामिंद्र इन्मेधिराणामिंद्रः क्षेमे योगे हव्य इंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ īśe ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ párvatānām ǀíndraḥ ǀ vṛdhā́m ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ médhirāṇām ǀ índraḥ ǀ kṣéme ǀ yóge ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra is Sovran Lord of Earth and Heaven, Indra is Lord of waters and of mountains. Indra is Lord of prosperers and sages Indra must be invoked in rest and effort.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrarules over heaven, Indra rules over earth, over the waters, and over the clouds; Indra rules overthe great and over the wise; Indra is to be invoked for the acquisition and preservation (of wealth).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra is Sovran Lord of Earth and Heaven, Indra is Lord of waters and of mountains. Indra is Lord of prosperers and sages Indra must be invoked in rest and effort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्राक्तुभ्य इंद्रः प्र वृधो अहभ्यः प्रांतरिक्षात्प्र समुद्रस्य धासेः ।प्र वातस्य प्रथसः प्र ज्मो अंतात्प्र सिंधुभ्यो रिरिचे प्र क्षितिभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ aktú-bhyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ prá ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ áha-bhyaḥ ǀ prá ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ prá ǀ samudrásya ǀ dhāséḥ ǀprá ǀ vā́tasya ǀ práthasaḥ ǀ prá ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántāt ǀ prá ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ ririce ǀ prá ǀ kṣití-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vaster than days and nights, Giver of increase, vaster than firmament and flood of ocean, Vaster than bounds of earth and wind's extension, vaster than rivers and our lands is Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrais vaster than the nights, vaster than the days, vaster than the firmament or the receptacle of theocean, vaster than the wind, or space or the ends of the earth; Indra exceeds the rivers and mankind.
verses.griffith_verse: Vaster than days and nights, Giver of increase, vaster than firmament and flood of ocean, Vaster than bounds of earth and wind's extension, vaster than rivers and our lands is Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र शोशुचत्या उषसो न केतुरसिन्वा ते वर्ततामिंद्र हेतिः ।अश्मेव विध्य दिव आ सृजानस्तपिष्ठेन हेषसा द्रोघमित्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ śóśucatyāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ketúḥ ǀ asinvā́ ǀ te ǀ vartatām ǀ indra ǀ hetíḥ ǀáśmā-iva ǀ vidhya ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sṛjānáḥ ǀ tápiṣṭhena ǀ héṣasā ǀ drógha-mitrān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forward, as herald of refulgent Morning, let thine insatiate arrow fly, O Indra. And pierce, as ’twere a stone launched forth from heaven, with hottest blaze the men who love deception.
verses.wilson_translation: May your unbroken weapon,Indra, proceed (against your foes), like the banner of the shining dawn,like a stone cast down from heaven, pierce those whose friendship is deceitful with your consumingloud-sounding (weapon).
verses.griffith_verse: Forward, as herald of refulgent Morning, let thine insatiate arrow fly, O Indra. And pierce, as ’twere a stone launched forth from heaven, with hottest blaze the men who love deception.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अन्वह मासा अन्विद्वनान्यन्वोषधीरनु पर्वतासः ।अन्विंद्रं रोदसी वावशाने अन्वापो अजिहत जायमानं ॥
verses.transliteration: ánu ǀ áha ǀ mā́sāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ít ǀ vánāni ǀ ánu ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀánu ǀ índram ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vāvaśāné íti ǀ ánu ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ajihata ǀ jā́yamānam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, verily, the moons, the mountains followed, the tall trees followed and the plants and herbage. Yearning with love both Worlds approached, the Waters waited on Indra when he first had being.
verses.wilson_translation: The months attend upon Indraas soon as born, the forests attend upon him, the plural nts, themountains, the affectionate heaven and earth, and the waters (attend upon) him.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, verily, the moons, the mountains followed, the tall trees followed and the plants and herbage. Yearning with love both Worlds approached, the Waters waited on Indra when he first had being.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कर्हि स्वित्सा त इंद्र चेत्यासदघस्य यद्भिनदो रक्ष एषत् ।मित्रक्रुवो यच्छसने न गावः पृथिव्या आपृगमुया शयंते ॥
verses.transliteration: kárhi ǀ svit ǀ sā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ cetyā́ ǀ asat ǀ aghásya ǀ yát ǀ bhinádaḥ ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ ā-ī́ṣat ǀmitra-krúvaḥ ǀ yát ǀ śásane ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ā-pṛ́k ǀ amuyā́ ǀ śáyante ǁ
verses.english_translation: Where was the vengeful dart when thou, O Indra, clavest the demon ever beat on outrage? When fiends lay there upon the ground extended like cattle in the place of immolation?
verses.wilson_translation: Where was your (shaft)Indra, (which ought) to be hurled (against your enemies) when you did cleavetherākṣasashastening to war, and when the Mitrakru lay on the ground there in confusion like cattle at theplace of immolation?
verses.griffith_verse: Where was the vengeful dart when thou, O Indra, clavest the demon ever beat on outrage? When fiends lay there upon the ground extended like cattle in the place of immolation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शत्रूयंतो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि व्राधंत ओगणास इंद्र ।अंधेनामित्रास्तमसा सचंतां सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्ताँ अभि ष्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: śatru-yántaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ naḥ ǀ tatasré ǀ máhi ǀ vrā́dhantaḥ ǀ ogaṇā́saḥ ǀ indra ǀandhéna ǀ amítrāḥ ǀ támasā ǀ sacantām ǀ su-jyotíṣaḥ ǀ aktávaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ abhí ǀ syuríti syuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those who are set in enmity against us, the Ogaṇas, O Indra, waxen mighty,— Let blinding darkness follow those our foemen, while these shall have bright shining nights to light them.
verses.wilson_translation: May those adversaries,Indra, who press upon us, fiercely opposing us, and assembled in numbers,be overwhelmed with thick darkness, and may the bright (days) and nights overpower them. hymn you, and disregarding all other worshippers, come to us with your protection.
verses.griffith_verse: Those who are set in enmity against us, the Ogaṇas, O Indra, waxen mighty,— Let blinding darkness follow those our foemen, while these shall have bright shining nights to light them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरूणि हि त्वा सवना जनानां ब्रह्माणि मंदन्गृणतामृषीणां ।इमामाघोषन्नवसा सहूतिं तिरो विश्वाँ अर्चतो याह्यर्वाङ् ॥
verses.transliteration: purū́ṇi ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ sávanā ǀ jánānām ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ mándan ǀ gṛṇatā́m ǀ ṛ́ṣīṇām ǀimā́m ǀ ā-ghóṣan ǀ ávasā ǀ sá-hūtim ǀ tiráḥ ǀ víśvān ǀ árcataḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May plentiful libations of the people, and singing Ṛṣis’ holy prayers rejoice thee. Hearing with love this common invocation, come unto us, pass by all those who praise thee.
verses.griffith_verse: May plentiful libations of the people, and singing Ṛṣis’ holy prayers rejoice thee. Hearing with love this common invocation, come unto us, pass by all those who praise thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा ते वयमिंद्र भुंजतीनां विद्याम सुमतीनां नवानां ।विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गृणंतो विश्वामित्रा उत त इंद्र नूनं ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ te ǀ vayám ǀ indra ǀ bhuñjatīnā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ su-matīnā́m ǀ návānām ǀvidyā́ma ǀ vástoḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ viśvā́mitrāḥ ǀ utá ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ nūnám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, thus may we be made partakers of thy new favours that shall bring us profit. Singing with love, may we the Viśvāmitras win daylight even now through thee, O Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: May we, the descendants of Viśvāmitra, sincerely praising you,Indra,by day for your protection,obtain your protecting (favours), may we obtain your recent (favours).
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, thus may we be made partakers of thy new favours that shall bring us profit. Singing with love, may we the Viśvāmitras win daylight even now through thee, O Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke in this conflict for our protection the pure, the opulent Indra, the most heroic in the fight,
verses.griffith_verse: Call we on Maghavan, auspicious Indra, best hero in the fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XC. Puruṣa.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . A THOUSAND heads hath Puruṣa, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet.On every side pervading earth he fills a space ten fingers wide. This Puruṣa is all that yet hath been and all that is to be;The Lord of Immortality which waxes greater still by food. So mighty is his greatness; yea, greater than this is Puruṣa.All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths eternal life in heaven. With three-fourths Puruṣa went up: one-fourth of him again was here.Thence he strode out to every side over what cats not and what cats. From him Virāj was born; again Puruṣa from Virāj was born.As soon as he was born he spread eastward and westward o’er the earth. When Gods prepared the sacrifice with Puruṣa as their offering,Its oil was spring, the holy gift was autumn; summer was the wood. They balmed as victim on the grass Puruṣa born in earliest time.With him the Deities and all Sādhyas and Ṛṣis sacrificed. From that great general sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up.He formed the creatures of-the air, and animals both wild and tame. From that great general sacrifice Ṛcas and Sāma-hymns were born:Therefrom were spells and charms produced; the Yajus had its birth from it. From it were horses born, from it all cattle with two rows of teeth:From it were generated kine, from it the goats and sheep were born. When they divided Puruṣa how many portions did they make?What do they call his mouth, his arms? What do they call his thighs and feet? The Brahman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Rājanya made.His thighs became the Vaiśya, from his feet the Śūdra was produced. The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth;Indra and Agni from his mouth were born, and Vāyu from his breath. Forth from his navel came mid-air the sky was fashioned from his headEarth from his feet, and from his car the regions. Thus they formed the worlds. Seven fencing-sticks had he, thrice seven layers of fuel were prepared,When the Gods, offering sacrifice, bound, as their victim, Puruṣa. Gods, sacrificing, sacrificed the victim these were the earliest holy ordinances.The Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ।स भूमिं विश्वतो वृत्वात्यतिष्ठद्दशांगुलं ॥
verses.transliteration: sahásra-śīrṣā ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀ sahasra-akṣáḥ ǀ sahásra-pāt ǀsáḥ ǀ bhū́mim ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ vṛtvā́ ǀ áti ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ daśa-aṅgulám ǁ
verses.english_translation: A THOUSAND heads hath Puruṣa, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. On every side pervading earth he fills a space ten fingers wide.
verses.wilson_translation: Puruṣa, who has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet, investing the earth in alldirections, exceeds (it by a space) measuring ten fingers.
verses.griffith_verse: A THOUSAND heads hath Puruṣa, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. On every side pervading earth he fills a space ten fingers wide.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरुष एवेदं सर्वं यद्भूतं यच्च भव्यं ।उतामृतत्वस्येशानो यदन्नेनातिरोहति ॥
verses.transliteration: púruṣaḥ ǀ evá ǀ idám ǀ sárvam ǀ yát ǀ bhūtám ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ bhávyam ǀutá ǀ amṛta-tvásya ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ánnena ǀ ati-róhati ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Puruṣa is all that yet hath been and all that is to be; The Lord of Immortality which waxes greater still by food.
verses.wilson_translation: Puruṣais verily all this (visible world), all that is, and all that is to be; he is also the lord of immortality;for he mounts beyond (his own condition) for the food (of living beings).
verses.griffith_verse: This Puruṣa is all that yet hath been and all that is to be; The Lord of Immortality which waxes greater still by food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतावानस्य महिमातो ज्यायांश्च पूरुषः ।पादोऽस्य विश्वा भूतानि त्रिपादस्यामृतं दिवि ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́vān ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ átaḥ ǀ jyā́yān ǀ ca ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀpā́daḥ ǀ asya ǀ víśvā ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ tri-pā́t ǀ asya ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ diví ǁ
verses.english_translation: So mighty is his greatness; yea, greater than this is Puruṣa. All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths eternal life in heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Such is his greatness; and Puruṣais greater even than this; all beings are one-fourth of him; his otherthree-fourths, (being) immortal, (abide) in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: So mighty is his greatness; yea, greater than this is Puruṣa. All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths eternal life in heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिपादूर्ध्व उदैत्पुरुषः पादोऽस्येहाभवत्पुनः ।ततो विष्वङ्व्यक्रामत्साशनानशने अभि ॥
