verses.transliteration: tri-pā́t ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ út ǀ ait ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀ pā́daḥ ǀ asya ǀ ihá ǀ abhavat ǀ púnaríti ǀtátaḥ ǀ víṣvaṅ ǀ ví ǀ akrāmat ǀ sāśanānaśané íti ǀ abhí ǁ
verses.english_translation: With three-fourths Puruṣa went up: one-fourth of him again was here. Thence he strode out to every side over what cats not and what cats.
verses.wilson_translation: Three-fourths of Puruṣaascended; the other fourth that remained in this world proceeds repeatedly,and, diversified in various forms, went to all animate and inanimate creation.
verses.griffith_verse: With three-fourths Puruṣa went up: one-fourth of him again was here. Thence he strode out to every side over what cats not and what cats.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्विराळजायत विराजो अधि पूरुषः ।स जातो अत्यरिच्यत पश्चाद्भूमिमथो पुरः ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ virā́ṭ ǀ ajāyata ǀ vi-rā́jaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ áti ǀ aricyata ǀ paścā́t ǀ bhū́mim ǀ átho íti ǀ puráḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From him Virāj was born; again Puruṣa from Virāj was born. As soon as he was born he spread eastward and westward o’er the earth.
verses.wilson_translation: From him was born Virāt. and from Virāt.Puruṣa; he, as soon as born, became manifested, andafterwards (created) the earth (and) then corporeal forms.
verses.griffith_verse: From him Virāj was born; again Puruṣa from Virāj was born. As soon as he was born he spread eastward and westward o’er the earth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्पुरुषेण हविषा देवा यज्ञमतन्वत ।वसंतो अस्यासीदाज्यं ग्रीष्म इध्मः शरद्धविः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ púruṣeṇa ǀ havíṣā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ átanvata ǀvasantáḥ ǀ asya ǀ āsīt ǀ ā́jyam ǀ grīṣmáḥ ǀ idhmáḥ ǀ śarát ǀ havíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When Gods prepared the sacrifice with Puruṣa as their offering, Its oil was spring, the holy gift was autumn; summer was the wood.
verses.wilson_translation: When the gods performed the sacrifice with Puruṣaas the offering, then Spring was its ghī, Summerthe fuel, and Autumn the oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: When Gods prepared the sacrifice with Puruṣa as their offering, Its oil was spring, the holy gift was autumn; summer was the wood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं यज्ञं बर्हिषि प्रौक्षन्पुरुषं जातमग्रतः ।तेन देवा अयजंत साध्या ऋषयश्च ये ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ yajñám ǀ barhíṣi ǀ prá ǀ aukṣan ǀ púruṣam ǀ jātám ǀ agratáḥ ǀténa ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ayajanta ǀ sādhyā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǁ
verses.english_translation: They balmed as victim on the grass Puruṣa born in earliest time. With him the Deities and all Sādhyas and Ṛṣis sacrificed.
verses.wilson_translation: They immolated as the victim upon the sacred grass Puruṣa, born before (creation); with him thedeities who were Sādhyasand those who were Ṛṣis sacrificed.
verses.griffith_verse: They balmed as victim on the grass Puruṣa born in earliest time. With him the Deities and all Sādhyas and Ṛṣis sacrificed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्यज्ञात्सर्वहुतः संभृतं पृषदाज्यं ।पशूंतांश्चक्रे वायव्यानारण्यान्ग्राम्याश्च ये ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ yajñā́t ǀ sarva-hútaḥ ǀ sám-bhṛtam ǀ pṛṣat-ājyám ǀpaśū́n ǀ tā́n ǀ cakre ǀ vāyavyā́n ǀ āraṇyā́n ǀ grāmyā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǁ
verses.english_translation: From that great general sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up. He formed the creatures of-the air, and animals both wild and tame.
verses.wilson_translation: From that victim, in whom the universal oblation was offered, the mixture of curds and butter wasproduced, (then) he made those animals over whom Vāyupresides, those that are wild, and those that aretame.
verses.griffith_verse: From that great general sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up. He formed the creatures of-the air, and animals both wild and tame.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्यज्ञात्सर्वहुत ऋचः सामानि जज्ञिरे ।छंदांसि जज्ञिरे तस्माद्यजुस्तस्मादजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ yajñā́t ǀ sarva-hútaḥ ǀ ṛ́caḥ ǀ sā́māni ǀ jajñire ǀchándāṃsi ǀ jajñire ǀ tásmāt ǀ yájuḥ ǀ tásmāt ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: From that great general sacrifice Ṛcas and Sāma-hymns were born: Therefrom were spells and charms produced; the Yajus had its birth from it.
verses.wilson_translation: From that victim, in whom the universal oblation was offered, the ṛccas andsāmanswere produced;from him the metres were born; from him theyajus. was born.
verses.griffith_verse: From that great general sacrifice Ṛcas and Sāma-hymns were born: Therefrom were spells and charms produced; the Yajus had its birth from it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादश्वा अजायंत ये के चोभयादतः ।गावो ह जज्ञिरे तस्मात्तस्माज्जाता अजावयः ॥
verses.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ ajāyanta ǀ yé ǀ ké ǀ ca ǀ ubhayā́dataḥ ǀgā́vaḥ ǀ ha ǀ jajñire ǀ tásmāt ǀ tásmāt ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ ajāváyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From it were horses born, from it all cattle with two rows of teeth: From it were generated kine, from it the goats and sheep were born.
verses.griffith_verse: From it were horses born, from it all cattle with two rows of teeth: From it were generated kine, from it the goats and sheep were born.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्पुरुषं व्यदधुः कतिधा व्यकल्पयन् ।मुखं किमस्य कौ बाहू का ऊरू पादा उच्येते ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ púruṣam ǀ ví ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ katidhā́ ǀ ví ǀ akalpayan ǀmúkham ǀ kím ǀ asya ǀ káu ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ káu ǀ ūrū́ íti ǀ pā́dau ǀ ucyete íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: When they divided Puruṣa how many portions did they make? What do they call his mouth, his arms? What do they call his thighs and feet?
verses.wilson_translation: When they immolated Puruṣa, into how many portions did they divide him? What was his mouth called, what his arms, what his thighs, what were his feet called?
verses.griffith_verse: When they divided Puruṣa how many portions did they make? What do they call his mouth, his arms? What do they call his thighs and feet?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणोऽस्य मुखमासीद्बाहू राजन्यः कृतः ।ऊरू तदस्य यद्वैश्यः पद्भ्यां शूद्रो अजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇáḥ ǀ asya ǀ múkham ǀ āsīt ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ rājanyáḥ ǀ kṛtáḥ ǀūrū́ íti ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ yát ǀ váiśyaḥ ǀ pat-bhyā́m ǀ śūdráḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Brahman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Rājanya made. His thighs became the Vaiśya, from his feet the Śūdra was produced.
verses.wilson_translation: His mouth became the Brāhmaṇa, his arms became the Rājanya, his thighs became the Vaiśya;theŚūdrawas born from his feet.
verses.griffith_verse: The Brahman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Rājanya made. His thighs became the Vaiśya, from his feet the Śūdra was produced.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चंद्रमा मनसो जातश्चक्षोः सूर्यो अजायत ।मुखादिंद्रश्चाग्निश्च प्राणाद्वायुरजायत ॥
verses.transliteration: candrámāḥ ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ cákṣoḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ajāyata ǀmúkhāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ agníḥ ǀ ca ǀ prāṇā́t ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth; Indra and Agni from his mouth were born, and Vāyu from his breath.
verses.wilson_translation: The moon was born from his mind; the sun was born from his eye;Indraand Agniwere born from his mouth,Vāyufrom his breath.
verses.griffith_verse: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth; Indra and Agni from his mouth were born, and Vāyu from his breath.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाभ्या आसीदंतरिक्षं शीर्ष्णो द्यौः समवर्तत ।पद्भ्यां भूमिर्दिशः श्रोत्रात्तथा लोकाँ अकल्पयन् ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́bhyāḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ antárikṣam ǀ śīrṣṇáḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ sám ǀ avartata ǀpat-bhyā́m ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ díśaḥ ǀ śrótrāt ǀ táthā ǀ lokā́n ǀ akalpayan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Forth from his navel came mid-air the sky was fashioned from his head Earth from his feet, and from his car the regions. Thus they formed the worlds.
verses.wilson_translation: From his navel came the firmament, from his head the heaven was produced, the earth from his feet,the quarters of space from his ear, so they constituted the world.
verses.griffith_verse: Forth from his navel came mid-air the sky was fashioned from his head Earth from his feet, and from his car the regions. Thus they formed the worlds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्तास्यासन्परिधयस्त्रिः सप्त समिधः कृताः ।देवा यद्यज्ञं तन्वाना अबध्नन्पुरुषं पशुं ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ asya ǀ āsan ǀ pari-dháyaḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ saptá ǀ sam-ídhaḥ ǀ kṛtā́ḥ ǀdevā́ḥ ǀ yát ǀ yajñám ǀ tanvānā́ḥ ǀ ábadhnan ǀ púruṣam ǀ paśúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Seven fencing-sticks had he, thrice seven layers of fuel were prepared, When the Gods, offering sacrifice, bound, as their victim, Puruṣa.
verses.wilson_translation: Seven were the enclosures of the sacrifice, thrice seven logs of fuel were prepared, when the gods,celebrating the rite, bound Puruṣaas the victim.
verses.griffith_verse: Seven fencing-sticks had he, thrice seven layers of fuel were prepared, When the Gods, offering sacrifice, bound, as their victim, Puruṣa.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् ।ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñéna ǀ yajñám ǀ ayajanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ tā́ni ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ āsan ǀté ǀ ha ǀ nā́kam ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ sacanta ǀ yátra ǀ pū́rve ǀ sādhyā́ḥ ǀ sánti ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gods, sacrificing, sacrificed the victim these were the earliest holy ordinances. The Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: By sacrifice the gods worshipped (him who is also) the sacrifice; those were the first duties. Thosegreat ones became partakers of the heaven where the ancient deities the Sādhyasabide. 10.091.01 Damūnas, being glorified by his diligent (worshippers), desiring food upon the footmark of Iḷā, iskindled in the chamber (of sacrifice), the offerer of every oblation, the object of veneration, the lord, theresplendent, to him who desires his friendship.
verses.griffith_verse: Gods, sacrificing, sacrificed the victim these were the earliest holy ordinances. The Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BRISK, at the place of Iḷā, hymned by men who wake, our own familiar Friend is kindled in the house;Hotar of all oblation, worthy of our choice, Lord, beaming, trusty friend to one who loveth him. He, excellent in glory, guest in every house, finds like a swift-winged bird a home in every tree.Benevolent to men, he scorns no living man: Friend to the tribes of men he dwells with every tribe. Most sage with insight, passing skilful with thy powers art thou, O Agni, wise with wisdom, knowing all.As Vasu, thou alone art Lord of all good things, of all the treasures that the heavens and earth produce. Foreknowing well, O Agni, thou in Iḷā's place hast occupied thy regular station balmed with oil.Marked are thy comings like the comings of the Dawns, the rays of him who shineth spotless as the Sun. Thy glories are, as lightnings from the rainy cloud, marked, many-hued, like heralds of the Dawns’ approach,When, loosed to wander over plants and forest trees, thou crammest by thyself thy food into thy mouth. Him, duly coming as their germ, have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life.So in like manner do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore. When, sped and urged by wind, thou spreadest thee abroad, swift piercing through thy food according to thy will,Thy never-ceasing blazes, longing to consume, like men on chariots, Agni, strive on every side. Agni, the Hotar-priest who fills the assembly full, Waker of knowledge, chief Controller of the thought,—Him, yea, none other than thyself, doth man elect at sacrificial offerings great and small alike. Here, Agni, the arrangers, those attached to thee, elect thee as their Priest in sacred gatherings,When men with strewn clipt grass and sacrificial gifts offer thee entertainment, piously inclined. Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man.Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home. When mortal man presents to thee Immortal God, Agni, his fuel or his sacrificial gift,Then thou art his Adhvaryu, Hotar, messenger, callest the Gods and orderest the sacrifice. From us these hymns in concert have gone forth to him, these. holy words, these Ṛcas, songs and eulogies,Eager for wealth, to Jātavedas fain for wealth: when they have waxen strong they please their Strengthener. This newest eulogy will I speak forth to him, the Ancient One who loves it. May he hear our voice.May it come near his heart and make it stir with love, as a fond well-dressed matron clings about her lord. He in whom horses, bulls, oxen, and barren cows, and rams, when duly set apart, are offered up,—To Agni, Soma-sprinkled, drinker of sweet juice, Disposer, with my heart I bring a fair hymn forth. Into thy mouth is poured the offering, Agni, as Soma into cup, oil into ladle.Vouchsafe us wealth. strength-winning, blest with heroes, wealth lofty, praised by men, and full of splendour.

verses.sanskrit: सं जागृवद्भिर्जरमाण इध्यते दमे दमूना इषयन्निळस्पदे ।विश्वस्य होता हविषो वरेण्यो विभुर्विभावा सुषखा सखीयते ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ jāgṛvát-bhiḥ ǀ járamāṇaḥ ǀ idhyate ǀ dáme ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ iṣáyan ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀvíśvasya ǀ hótā ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ su-sákhā ǀ sakhi-yaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: BRISK, at the place of Iḷā, hymned by men who wake, our own familiar Friend is kindled in the house; Hotar of all oblation, worthy of our choice, Lord, beaming, trusty friend to one who loveth him.
verses.griffith_verse: BRISK, at the place of Iḷā, hymned by men who wake, our own familiar Friend is kindled in the house; Hotar of all oblation, worthy of our choice, Lord, beaming, trusty friend to one who loveth him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स दर्शतश्रीरतिथिर्गृहेगृहे वनेवने शिश्रिये तक्ववीरिव ।जनंजनं जन्यो नाति मन्यते विश आ क्षेति विश्यो विशंविशं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ darśata-śrī́ḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ gṛhé-gṛhe ǀ váne-vane ǀ śiśriye ǀ takvavī́ḥ-iva ǀjánam-janam ǀ jányaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áti ǀ manyate ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ kṣeti ǀ viśyáḥ ǀ víśam-viśam ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, excellent in glory, guest in every house, finds like a swift-winged bird a home in every tree. Benevolent to men, he scorns no living man: Friend to the tribes of men he dwells with every tribe.
verses.wilson_translation: Of manifest glory, he resorts as a guest to every house (of his worshippers) to every forest; friendly toman, like one going to all men, he disregards them not; kind to all, he dwells among all men, (he presides ove4r
verses.griffith_verse: He, excellent in glory, guest in every house, finds like a swift-winged bird a home in every tree. Benevolent to men, he scorns no living man: Friend to the tribes of men he dwells with every tribe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुदक्षो दक्षैः क्रतुनासि सुक्रतुरग्ने कविः काव्येनासि विश्ववित् ।वसुर्वसूनां क्षयसि त्वमेक इद्द्यावा च यानि पृथिवी च पुष्यतः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-dákṣaḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ krátunā ǀ asi ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ ágne ǀ kavíḥ ǀ kā́vyena ǀ asi ǀ viśva-vít ǀvásuḥ ǀ vásūnām ǀ kṣayasi ǀ tvám ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ dyā́vā ǀ ca ǀ yā́ni ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ ca ǀ púṣyataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most sage with insight, passing skilful with thy powers art thou, O Agni, wise with wisdom, knowing all. As Vasu, thou alone art Lord of all good things, of all the treasures that the heavens and earth produce.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Agni, are vigorous with vigour, you are active with acts (of piety), you are wise withwisdom, knowing all things. You are the dispenser ofwealth, you abide alone, you are lord of the treasures ofheaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Most sage with insight, passing skilful with thy powers art thou, O Agni, wise with wisdom, knowing all. As Vasu, thou alone art Lord of all good things, of all the treasures that the heavens and earth produce.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रजानन्नग्ने तव योनिमृत्वियमिळायास्पदे घृतवंतमासदः ।आ ते चिकित्र उषसामिवेतयोऽरेपसः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः ॥
verses.transliteration: pra-jānán ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ yónim ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ íḷāyāḥ ǀ padé ǀ ghṛtá-vantam ǀ ā́ ǀ asadaḥ ǀā́ ǀ te ǀ cikitre ǀ uṣásām-iva ǀ étayaḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya-iva ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Foreknowing well, O Agni, thou in Iḷā's place hast occupied thy regular station balmed with oil. Marked are thy comings like the comings of the Dawns, the rays of him who shineth spotless as the Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: Sagacious Agni, you sit at your station suited to the sacrifice and anointed with butter at the foot-markof Iḷā. your quick-moving rays are manifested like those of the dawns, beautiful as those of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Foreknowing well, O Agni, thou in Iḷā's place hast occupied thy regular station balmed with oil. Marked are thy comings like the comings of the Dawns, the rays of him who shineth spotless as the Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तव श्रियो वर्ष्यस्येव विद्युतश्चित्राश्चिकित्र उषसां न केतवः ।यदोषधीरभिसृष्टो वनानि च परि स्वयं चिनुषे अन्नमास्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ varṣyásya-iva ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ cikitre ǀ uṣásām ǀ ná ǀ ketávaḥ ǀyát ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ abhí-sṛṣṭaḥ ǀ vánāni ǀ ca ǀ pári ǀ svayám ǀ cinuṣé ǀ ánnam ǀ āsyé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy glories are, as lightnings from the rainy cloud, marked, many-hued, like heralds of the Dawns’ approach, When, loosed to wander over plants and forest trees, thou crammest by thyself thy food into thy mouth.
verses.wilson_translation: Your glories,Agni, like the lightnings of the rain-cloud are manifested many-tinted, like themanifestations of the dawn, when quitting the plural nts and the forests, you gather on all sides food for your mouth.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy glories are, as lightnings from the rainy cloud, marked, many-hued, like heralds of the Dawns’ approach, When, loosed to wander over plants and forest trees, thou crammest by thyself thy food into thy mouth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमोषधीर्दधिरे गर्भमृत्वियं तमापो अग्निं जनयंत मातरः ।तमित्समानं वनिनश्च वीरुधोऽंतर्वतीश्च सुवते च विश्वहा ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ gárbham ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ tám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ agním ǀ janayanta ǀ mātáraḥ ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ samānám ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ ca ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ antáḥ-vatīḥ ǀ ca ǀ súvate ǀ ca ǀ viśváhā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, duly coming as their germ, have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life. So in like manner do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore.
verses.wilson_translation: The plural nts bear him as the embryo (conceived) in due season; the maternal waters bring forth Agni;yes, the trees and the pregnant creepers bring him forth daily like themselves.
verses.griffith_verse: Him, duly coming as their germ, have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life. So in like manner do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वातोपधूत इषितो वशाँ अनु तृषु यदन्ना वेविषद्वितिष्ठसे ।आ ते यतंते रथ्यो यथा पृथक्छर्धांस्यग्ने अजराणि धक्षतः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́ta-upadhūtaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ váśān ǀ ánu ǀ tṛṣú ǀ yát ǀ ánnā ǀ véviṣat ǀ vi-tíṣṭhase ǀā́ ǀ te ǀ yatante ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ pṛ́thak ǀ śárdhāṃsi ǀ agne ǀ ajárāṇi ǀ dhákṣataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, sped and urged by wind, thou spreadest thee abroad, swift piercing through thy food according to thy will, Thy never-ceasing blazes, longing to consume, like men on chariots, Agni, strive on every side.
verses.wilson_translation: When, agitated by the wind and quickly moving through the beloved (trees), you spread aboutdevouring the food, the imperishable energies of you,Agni, the devourer, rush forth like charioteers.
verses.griffith_verse: When, sped and urged by wind, thou spreadest thee abroad, swift piercing through thy food according to thy will, Thy never-ceasing blazes, longing to consume, like men on chariots, Agni, strive on every side.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मेधाकारं विदथस्य प्रसाधनमग्निं होतारं परिभूतमं मतिं ।तमिदर्भे हविष्या समानमित्तमिन्महे वृणते नान्यं त्वत् ॥
verses.transliteration: medhā-kārám ǀ vidáthasya ǀ pra-sā́dhanam ǀ agním ǀ hótāram ǀ pari-bhū́tamam ǀ matím ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ árbhe ǀ havíṣi ǀ ā́ ǀ samānám ǀ ít ǀ tám ǀ ít ǀ mahé ǀ vṛṇate ǀ ná ǀ anyám ǀ tvát ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, the Hotar-priest who fills the assembly full, Waker of knowledge, chief Controller of the thought,— Him, yea, none other than thyself, doth man elect at sacrificial offerings great and small alike.
verses.wilson_translation: (The priest) selects you, (Agni), the giver of intelligence, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the invokerof the gods, the chief overcomer of foes, the councillor, alike verily at the lesser and at the greater oblation andnone other than you.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, the Hotar-priest who fills the assembly full, Waker of knowledge, chief Controller of the thought,— Him, yea, none other than thyself, doth man elect at sacrificial offerings great and small alike.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिदत्र वृणते त्वायवो होतारमग्ने विदथेषु वेधसः ।यद्देवयंतो दधति प्रयांसि ते हविष्मंतो मनवो वृक्तबर्हिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ átra ǀ vṛṇate ǀ tvā-yávaḥ ǀ hótāram ǀ agne ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀyát ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ dádhati ǀ práyāṃsi ǀ te ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ mánavaḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here, Agni, the arrangers, those attached to thee, elect thee as their Priest in sacred gatherings, When men with strewn clipt grass and sacrificial gifts offer thee entertainment, piously inclined.
verses.wilson_translation: The performers of sacred rites, devoted to Agni, to you, select you as the ministrant priest at sacrificesin this world, when the devout worshippers bearing oblations and strewing the clipped sacred grass offer youfood.
verses.griffith_verse: Here, Agni, the arrangers, those attached to thee, elect thee as their Priest in sacred gatherings, When men with strewn clipt grass and sacrificial gifts offer thee entertainment, piously inclined.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तवाग्ने होत्रं तव पोत्रमृत्वियं तव नेष्ट्रं त्वमग्निदृतायतः ।तव प्रशास्त्रं त्वमध्वरीयसि ब्रह्मा चासि गृहपतिश्च नो दमे ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ agne ǀ hotrám ǀ táva ǀ potrám ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ táva ǀ neṣṭrám ǀ tvám ǀ agnít ǀ ṛta-yatáḥ ǀtáva ǀ pra-śāstrám ǀ tvám ǀ adhvari-yasi ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ca ǀ ási ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ dáme ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man. Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home.
verses.wilson_translation: Yours,Agni, is the function of the Hotā, yours the duly-performed function of the Potā, yours thefunction of the Neṣṭā, you are the Agni of the sacrificer, yours is the office of the Praśāstā, you act as Adhvaryu, and you are the Brahmāand the lord of the mansion in our abode.
verses.griffith_verse: Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man. Thou art Director, thou the ministering Priest: thou art the Brahman, Lord and Master in our home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्तुभ्यमग्ने अमृताय मर्त्यः समिधा दाशदुत वा हविष्कृति ।तस्य होता भवसि यासि दूत्यमुप ब्रूषे यजस्यध्वरीयसि ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ agne ǀ amṛ́tāya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ dā́śat ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ havíḥ-kṛti ǀtásya ǀ hótā ǀ bhavasi ǀ yā́si ǀ dūtyám ǀ úpa ǀ brūṣe ǀ yájasi ǀ adhvari-yási ǁ
verses.english_translation: When mortal man presents to thee Immortal God, Agni, his fuel or his sacrificial gift, Then thou art his Adhvaryu, Hotar, messenger, callest the Gods and orderest the sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: The mortal,Agni, who presents to you, the immortal, fuel at the offering of the oblation-- you are his Hotā, you go on his errant (to the gods), you direct (the ceremonial), you offer the sacrifice, you act as theofficiating priest.
verses.griffith_verse: When mortal man presents to thee Immortal God, Agni, his fuel or his sacrificial gift, Then thou art his Adhvaryu, Hotar, messenger, callest the Gods and orderest the sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमा अस्मै मतयो वाचो अस्मदाँ ऋचो गिरः सुष्टुतयः समग्मत ।वसूयवो वसवे जातवेदसे वृद्धासु चिद्वर्धनो यासु चाकनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ asmai ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ vā́caḥ ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ ṛ́caḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ su-stutáyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ agmata ǀvasu-yávaḥ ǀ vásave ǀ jātá-vedase ǀ vṛddhā́su ǀ cit ǀ várdhanaḥ ǀ yā́su ǀ cākánat ǁ
verses.english_translation: From us these hymns in concert have gone forth to him, these. holy words, these Ṛcas, songs and eulogies, Eager for wealth, to Jātavedas fain for wealth: when they have waxen strong they please their Strengthener.
verses.wilson_translation: May these laudatory words, these eulogistic verses, these voices (proceeding) from us, reach him thegiver of wealth,Jātavedas; these wealth- desiring (words) in which when they are perfected, the perfecterdelights.
verses.griffith_verse: From us these hymns in concert have gone forth to him, these. holy words, these Ṛcas, songs and eulogies, Eager for wealth, to Jātavedas fain for wealth: when they have waxen strong they please their Strengthener.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमां प्रत्नाय सुष्टुतिं नवीयसीं वोचेयमस्मा उशते शृणोतु नः ।भूया अंतरा हृद्यस्य निस्पृशे जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ pratnā́ya ǀ su-stutím ǀ návīyasīm ǀ vocéyam ǀ asmai ǀ uśaté ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀbhūyā́ḥ ǀ ántarā ǀ hṛdí ǀ asya ǀ ni-spṛ́śe ǀ jāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ uśatī́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This newest eulogy will I speak forth to him, the Ancient One who loves it. May he hear our voice. May it come near his heart and make it stir with love, as a fond well-dressed matron clings about her lord.
verses.wilson_translation: I will address this new laudatory hymn to the ancient Agni, who is gratified (by praise). May he hear uṣMay I be in the centre of his heart, to touch it, like a loving well-attired wife (in the heart) of her husband.
verses.griffith_verse: This newest eulogy will I speak forth to him, the Ancient One who loves it. May he hear our voice. May it come near his heart and make it stir with love, as a fond well-dressed matron clings about her lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्नश्वास ऋषभास उक्षणो वशा मेषा अवसृष्टास आहुताः ।कीलालपे सोमपृष्ठाय वेधसे हृदा मतिं जनये चारुमग्नये ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ṛṣabhā́saḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ vaśā́ḥ ǀ meṣā́ḥ ǀ ava-sṛṣṭā́saḥ ǀ ā́-hutāḥ ǀkīlāla-pé ǀ sóma-pṛṣṭhāya ǀ vedháse ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ matím ǀ janaye ǀ cā́rum ǀ agnáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: He in whom horses, bulls, oxen, and barren cows, and rams, when duly set apart, are offered up,— To Agni, Soma-sprinkled, drinker of sweet juice, Disposer, with my heart I bring a fair hymn forth.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer graceful praise with all my heart to Agni, the drinker of water, whose back is sprinkled with Soma, the ordainer (of the rite), to whom vigorous horses and bulls and barren cows and sheep are consignedas burnt offerings.
verses.griffith_verse: He in whom horses, bulls, oxen, and barren cows, and rams, when duly set apart, are offered up,— To Agni, Soma-sprinkled, drinker of sweet juice, Disposer, with my heart I bring a fair hymn forth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहाव्यग्ने हविरास्ये ते स्रुचीव घृतं चम्वीव सोमः ।वाजसनिं रयिमस्मे सुवीरं प्रशस्तं धेहि यशसं बृहंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: áhāvi ǀ agne ǀ havíḥ ǀ āsyé ǀ te ǀ srucí-iva ǀ ghṛtám ǀ camví-iva ǀ sómaḥ ǀvāja-sánim ǀ rayím ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ pra-śastám ǀ dhehi ǀ yaśásam ǀ bṛhántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Into thy mouth is poured the offering, Agni, as Soma into cup, oil into ladle. Vouchsafe us wealth. strength-winning, blest with heroes, wealth lofty, praised by men, and full of splendour.
verses.wilson_translation: The oblation has been poured,Agni, into your mouth, like butter into the ladle, like Somainto thespoon. Bestow upon us riches conferring food, (comprehending)maleprogeny, excellent renowned andabundant.
verses.griffith_verse: Into thy mouth is poured the offering, Agni, as Soma into cup, oil into ladle. Vouchsafe us wealth. strength-winning, blest with heroes, wealth lofty, praised by men, and full of splendour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCII. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I PRAISE your Charioteer of sacrifice, the Lord of men, Priest of the tribes, refulgent, Guest of night.Blazing amid dry plants, snatching amid the green, the Strong, the Holy Herald hath attained to heaven. Him, Agni, Gods and men have made their chief support, who drinks the fatness and completes the sacrifice.With kisses they caress the Grandson of the Red, like the swift ray of light, the Household Priest of Dawn. Yea, we discriminate his and the niggard's ways: his branches evermore are sent forth to consume.When his terrific flames have reached the Immortal's world, then men remember and extol the Heavenly Folk. For then the net of Law, Dyaus, and the wide expanse, Earth, Worship, and Devotion meet for highest praise,Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra were of one accord, and Savitar and Bhaga, Lords of holy might. Onward, with ever-roaming Rudra, speed the floods: over Aramati the Mighty have they run.With them Parijman, moving round his vast domain, loud bellowing, bedews all things that are within. Straightway the Rudras, Maruts visiting all men, Falcons of Dyaus, home-dwellers with the Asura,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman look on with these, and the swift-moving Indra with swift-moving Gods. With Indra have they found enjoyment, they who toil, in the light's beauty, in the very Strong One's strength;The singers who in men's assemblies forged for him, according to his due, his friend the thunderbolt. Even the Sun's Bay Coursers hath lie held in check: each one fears Indra as the mightiest of all.Unhindered, from the air's vault thunders day by day the loud triumphant breathing of the fearful Bull. With humble adoration show this day your song of praise to mighty Rudra, Ruler of the brave:With whom, the Eager Ones, going their ordered course, he comes from heaven Self-bright, auspicious, strong to guard. For these have spread abroad the fame of human kind, the Bull Bṛhaspati and Soma's brotherhood.Atharvan first by sacrifices made men sure: through skill the Bhṛgus were esteemed of all as Gods. For these, the Earth and Heaven with their abundant seed, four-bodied Narāśaṁsa, Yama, Aditi,God Tvaṣṭar Wealth-bestower, the Ṛbhukṣaṇas, Rodasī, Maruts, Viṣṇu, claim and merit praise. And may he too give car, the Sage, from far away, the Dragon of the Deep, to this our yearning call.Ye Sun and Moon who dwell in heaven and move in turn, and with your thought, O Earth and Sky, observe this well. Dear to all Gods, may Pūṣan guard the ways we go, the Waters’ child and Vāyu help us to success.Sing lauds for your great bliss to Wind, the breath of all: ye Aśvins prompt to hear, hear this upon your way. With hymns of praise we sing him who is throned as Lord over these fearless tribes, the Self-resplendent One.We praise Night's youthful Lord benevolent to men, the foeless One, the free, with all celestial Dames. By reason of his birth here Aṅgiras first sang: the pressing-stones upraised beheld the sacrifice-The stones through which the Sage became exceeding vast, and the sharp axe obtains in fight the beauteous place.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञस्य वो रथ्यं विश्पतिं विशां होतारमक्तोरतिथिं विभावसुं ।शोचंछुष्कासु हरिणीषु जर्भुरद्वृषा केतुर्यजतो द्यामशायत ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñásya ǀ vaḥ ǀ rathyám ǀ viśpátim ǀ viśā́m ǀ hótāram ǀ aktóḥ ǀ átithim ǀ vibhā́-vasum ǀśócan ǀ śúṣkāsu ǀ háriṇīṣu ǀ járbhurat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ketúḥ ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ aśāyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: I PRAISE your Charioteer of sacrifice, the Lord of men, Priest of the tribes, refulgent, Guest of night. Blazing amid dry plants, snatching amid the green, the Strong, the Holy Herald hath attained to heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: You (gods, adore) the charioteer of the sacrifice, the lord of men, the invoker of the gods, the guest ofnight, the resplendent (Agni). Blazing amid the dry (bushes) preying upon the green, the showerer of desires, thebanner (of light), the adorable, he reposes in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: I PRAISE your Charioteer of sacrifice, the Lord of men, Priest of the tribes, refulgent, Guest of night. Blazing amid dry plants, snatching amid the green, the Strong, the Holy Herald hath attained to heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इममंजस्पामुभये अकृण्वत धर्माणमग्निं विदथस्य साधनं ।अक्तुं न यह्वमुषसः पुरोहितं तनूनपातमरुषस्य निंसते ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ añjaḥ-pā́m ǀ ubháye ǀ akṛṇvata ǀ dharmā́ṇam ǀ agním ǀ vidáthasya ǀ sā́dhanam ǀaktúm ǀ ná ǀ yahvám ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ puráḥ-hitam ǀ tanū́-nápātam ǀ aruṣásya ǀ niṃsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him, Agni, Gods and men have made their chief support, who drinks the fatness and completes the sacrifice. With kisses they caress the Grandson of the Red, like the swift ray of light, the Household Priest of Dawn.
verses.wilson_translation: Both (men and gods) have made Agnithe speedy protector, the upholder of duty, the accomplisher ofthe sacrifice; they have recourse to him (who is) vast as the sun, the precursor of the dawn, the son of thebrilliant (Vāyu).
verses.griffith_verse: Him, Agni, Gods and men have made their chief support, who drinks the fatness and completes the sacrifice. With kisses they caress the Grandson of the Red, like the swift ray of light, the Household Priest of Dawn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बळस्य नीथा वि पणेश्च मन्महे वया अस्य प्रहुता आसुरत्तवे ।यदा घोरासो अमृतत्वमाशतादिज्जनस्य दैव्यस्य चर्किरन् ॥
verses.transliteration: báṭ ǀ asya ǀ nīthā́ ǀ ví ǀ paṇéḥ ǀ ca ǀ manmahe ǀ vayā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ prá-hutāḥ ǀ āsuḥ ǀ áttave ǀyadā́ ǀ ghorā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ā́śata ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ jánasya ǀ dáivyasya ǀ carkiran ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, we discriminate his and the niggard's ways: his branches evermore are sent forth to consume. When his terrific flames have reached the Immortal's world, then men remember and extol the Heavenly Folk.
verses.wilson_translation: We desire that our notion of that adorable (Agni) may be true, and that our oblations may be to him forfood. When his formidable (flames) attain immortality, then may our priests scatter (oblations for the benefit) ofthe divine being.
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, we discriminate his and the niggard's ways: his branches evermore are sent forth to consume. When his terrific flames have reached the Immortal's world, then men remember and extol the Heavenly Folk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य हि प्रसितिर्द्यौरुरु व्यचो नमो मह्यरमतिः पनीयसी ।इंद्रो मित्रो वरुणः सं चिकित्रिरेऽथो भगः सविता पूतदक्षसः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ prá-sitiḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ urú ǀ vyácaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ mahī́ ǀ arámatiḥ ǀ pánīyasī ǀíndraḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ cikitrire ǀ átho íti ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ pūtá-dakṣasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For then the net of Law, Dyaus, and the wide expanse, Earth, Worship, and Devotion meet for highest praise, Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra were of one accord, and Savitar and Bhaga, Lords of holy might.
verses.wilson_translation: The vast heavven, the spacious firmament, the glorious unbounded earth, (do) homage (to the Agni)of the sacrifice; and Indra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Bhaga, and Savitā, whose strength is purified, unite to recognize (hisexcellence). the circumambient (Indra) sweeping over a wide space, roaring in the belly (of the firmament), sprinkles the wholeworld.
verses.griffith_verse: For then the net of Law, Dyaus, and the wide expanse, Earth, Worship, and Devotion meet for highest praise, Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra were of one accord, and Savitar and Bhaga, Lords of holy might.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र रुद्रेण ययिना यंति सिंधवस्तिरो महीमरमतिं दधन्विरे ।येभिः परिज्मा परियन्नुरु ज्रयो वि रोरुवज्जठरे विश्वमुक्षते ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ rudréṇa ǀ yayínā ǀ yanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ mahī́m ǀ arámatim ǀ dadhanvire ǀyébhiḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ pari-yán ǀ urú ǀ jráyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ róruvat ǀ jaṭháre ǀ víśvam ǀ ukṣáte ǁ
verses.english_translation: Onward, with ever-roaming Rudra, speed the floods: over Aramati the Mighty have they run. With them Parijman, moving round his vast domain, loud bellowing, bedews all things that are within.
verses.griffith_verse: Onward, with ever-roaming Rudra, speed the floods: over Aramati the Mighty have they run. With them Parijman, moving round his vast domain, loud bellowing, bedews all things that are within.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्राणा रुद्रा मरुतो विश्वकृष्टयो दिवः श्येनासो असुरस्य नीळयः ।तेभिश्चष्टे वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमेंद्रो देवेभिरर्वशेभिरर्वशः ॥
verses.transliteration: krāṇā́ḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ śyenā́saḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ nīḷáyaḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ caṣṭe ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ arvaśébhiḥ ǀ árvaśaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Straightway the Rudras, Maruts visiting all men, Falcons of Dyaus, home-dwellers with the Asura,— Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman look on with these, and the swift-moving Indra with swift-moving Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: The Maruts, the sons of Rudra, mixing with men, the hawks of the sky, the inhabitants of the cloud,(are) performing (their functions); with those horse-owing deities,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman, and Indra, the lord ofhorses contemplates (the rite).
verses.griffith_verse: Straightway the Rudras, Maruts visiting all men, Falcons of Dyaus, home-dwellers with the Asura,— Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman look on with these, and the swift-moving Indra with swift-moving Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रे भुजं शशमानास आशत सूरो दृशीके वृषणश्च पौंस्ये ।प्र ये न्वस्यार्हणा ततक्षिरे युजं वज्रं नृषदनेषु कारवः ॥
verses.transliteration: índre ǀ bhújam ǀ śaśamānā́saḥ ǀ āśata ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ dṛ́śīke ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ páuṃsye ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ arháṇā ǀ tatakṣiré ǀ yújam ǀ vájram ǀ nṛ-sádaneṣu ǀ kārávaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Indra have they found enjoyment, they who toil, in the light's beauty, in the very Strong One's strength; The singers who in men's assemblies forged for him, according to his due, his friend the thunderbolt.
verses.wilson_translation: Those who praise him find protection in Indra; (those who praise him find) universal vision in the sun;(those who praise him find) manly vigour in the vigorous (Indra); those worshippers who diligently offer adorationto Indra (acquire) the thunderbolt as their ally in the dwellings of men.
verses.griffith_verse: With Indra have they found enjoyment, they who toil, in the light's beauty, in the very Strong One's strength; The singers who in men's assemblies forged for him, according to his due, his friend the thunderbolt.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूरश्चिदा हरितो अस्य रीरमदिंद्रादा कश्चिद्भयते तवीयसः ।भीमस्य वृष्णो जठरादभिश्वसो दिवेदिवे सहुरिः स्तन्नबाधितः ॥
verses.transliteration: sū́raḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ harítaḥ ǀ asya ǀ rīramat ǀ índrāt ǀ ā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ bhayate ǀ távīyasaḥ ǀbhīmásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ jaṭhárāt ǀ abhi-śvásaḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ stan ǀ ábādhitaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even the Sun's Bay Coursers hath lie held in check: each one fears Indra as the mightiest of all. Unhindered, from the air's vault thunders day by day the loud triumphant breathing of the fearful Bull.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun urging his steeds (in obedience to) his (commands) delights (in his presence); every (god) isin fear of the powerful Indra; from the belly of the formidable sighing showerer (of benefits) the all-enduringirresistible (deity) thunders day by day.
verses.griffith_verse: Even the Sun's Bay Coursers hath lie held in check: each one fears Indra as the mightiest of all. Unhindered, from the air's vault thunders day by day the loud triumphant breathing of the fearful Bull.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तोमं वो अद्य रुद्राय शिक्वसे क्षयद्वीराय नमसा दिदिष्टन ।येभिः शिवः स्ववाँ एवयावभिर्दिवः सिषक्ति स्वयशा निकामभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: stómam ǀ vaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ śíkvase ǀ kṣayát-vīrāya ǀ námasā ǀ didiṣṭana ǀyébhiḥ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ svá-vān ǀ evayā́va-bhiḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ sísakti ǀ svá-yaśāḥ ǀ níkāma-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: With humble adoration show this day your song of praise to mighty Rudra, Ruler of the brave: With whom, the Eager Ones, going their ordered course, he comes from heaven Self-bright, auspicious, strong to guard.
verses.wilson_translation: Address praise today with reverence to Rudrathe powerful destroyer of the heroes, (who isaccompanied) by the mounted (Maruts), the granters of wishes, together with whom he, propitious, possessingkinsmen, besprinkles (the worshippers) from heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: With humble adoration show this day your song of praise to mighty Rudra, Ruler of the brave: With whom, the Eager Ones, going their ordered course, he comes from heaven Self-bright, auspicious, strong to guard.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते हि प्रजाया अभरंत वि श्रवो बृहस्पतिर्वृषभः सोमजामयः ।यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमो वि धारयद्देवा दक्षैर्भृगवः सं चिकित्रिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ pra-jā́yāḥ ǀ ábharanta ǀ ví ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ sóma-jāmayaḥ ǀyajñáiḥ ǀ átharvā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ ví ǀ dhārayat ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dákṣaiḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ sám ǀ cikitrire ǁ
verses.english_translation: For these have spread abroad the fame of human kind, the Bull Bṛhaspati and Soma's brotherhood. Atharvan first by sacrifices made men sure: through skill the Bhṛgus were esteemed of all as Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Inasmuch as Bṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits) and the kindred of Soma(the Visvedevās),bestow food (for the support) of people,Atharvanwas the first to invigorate (the gods) with sacrifices; withstrength the gods and Bhṛgusdiscovered (the cattle).
verses.griffith_verse: For these have spread abroad the fame of human kind, the Bull Bṛhaspati and Soma's brotherhood. Atharvan first by sacrifices made men sure: through skill the Bhṛgus were esteemed of all as Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते हि द्यावापृथिवी भूरिरेतसा नराशंसश्चतुरंगो यमोऽदितिः ।देवस्त्वष्टा द्रविणोदा ऋभुक्षणः प्र रोदसी मरुतो विष्णुरर्हिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ bhū́ri-retasā ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ cátuḥ-aṅgaḥ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀdeváḥ ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣáṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ rodasī́ íti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ arhire ǁ
verses.english_translation: For these, the Earth and Heaven with their abundant seed, four-bodied Narāśaṁsa, Yama, Aditi, God Tvaṣṭar Wealth-bestower, the Ṛbhukṣaṇas, Rodasī, Maruts, Viṣṇu, claim and merit praise.
verses.wilson_translation: They the heaven and earth, abounding with waters, the Narāśaṃsa rite with its four fires,Yama,Aditi, the divine Tvaṣṭā, (Agni) the giver of wealth, theṚbhus,Rodasī, the Maruts, and Viṣṇuareworshipped (by us).
verses.griffith_verse: For these, the Earth and Heaven with their abundant seed, four-bodied Narāśaṁsa, Yama, Aditi, God Tvaṣṭar Wealth-bestower, the Ṛbhukṣaṇas, Rodasī, Maruts, Viṣṇu, claim and merit praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्य न उशिजामुर्विया कविरहिः शृणोतु बुध्न्यो हवीमनि ।सूर्यामासा विचरंता दिविक्षिता धिया शमीनहुषी अस्य बोधतं ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ uśíjām ǀ urviyā́ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ áhiḥ ǀ śṛṇotu ǀ budhnyáḥ ǀ hávīmani ǀsū́ryāmā́sā ǀ vi-cárantā ǀ divi-kṣítā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ śamīnahuṣī íti ǀ asyá ǀ bodhatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: And may he too give car, the Sage, from far away, the Dragon of the Deep, to this our yearning call. Ye Sun and Moon who dwell in heaven and move in turn, and with your thought, O Earth and Sky, observe this well.
verses.wilson_translation: And may the wise Ahi of the firmament hear the copious (pulse) of us eager (worshippers) at theoffering of oblations. May the revolving sun and moon dwelling in heaven, the earth and sky, comprehend bytheir intelligence (the purport) of this (our praise).
verses.griffith_verse: And may he too give car, the Sage, from far away, the Dragon of the Deep, to this our yearning call. Ye Sun and Moon who dwell in heaven and move in turn, and with your thought, O Earth and Sky, observe this well.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये ।आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ naḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ carátham ǀ viśvá-devyaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ avatu ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ iṣṭáye ǀātmā́nam ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vā́tam ǀ arcata ǀ tát ǀ aśvinā ǀ su-havā ǀ yā́mani ǀ śrutam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dear to all Gods, may Pūṣan guard the ways we go, the Waters’ child and Vāyu help us to success. Sing lauds for your great bliss to Wind, the breath of all: ye Aśvins prompt to hear, hear this upon your way.
verses.wilson_translation: May Pūṣanprotect all our moveable (property); may Vāyu, the friend of the Viśvedevās, thegrandson of the waters, preserve us for the celebration of the sacrifice. Worship the wind, thesoulof all, (toobtain) excellent (food);Aśvins, who are worthy to be invoked, hear us on your way.
verses.griffith_verse: Dear to all Gods, may Pūṣan guard the ways we go, the Waters’ child and Vāyu help us to success. Sing lauds for your great bliss to Wind, the breath of all: ye Aśvins prompt to hear, hear this upon your way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विशामासामभयानामधिक्षितं गीर्भिरु स्वयशसं गृणीमसि ।ग्नाभिर्विश्वाभिरदितिमनर्वणमक्तोर्युवानं नृमणा अधा पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: viśā́m ǀ āsā́m ǀ ábhayānām ǀ adhi-kṣítam ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀgnā́bhiḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ áditim ǀ anarváṇam ǀ aktóḥ ǀ yúvānam ǀ nṛ-mánāḥ ǀ ádha ǀ pátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: With hymns of praise we sing him who is throned as Lord over these fearless tribes, the Self-resplendent One. We praise Night's youthful Lord benevolent to men, the foeless One, the free, with all celestial Dames.
verses.wilson_translation: We glorify with praises Agni, the self-famous, who dwells among these fearless beings; we praise theirresistible Aditi, together with all the wives (of the gods); we praise the young (lord) of night (the moon), wepraise the friend of man (the sun), we praise (Indra) the lord (of all).
verses.griffith_verse: With hymns of praise we sing him who is throned as Lord over these fearless tribes, the Self-resplendent One. We praise Night's youthful Lord benevolent to men, the foeless One, the free, with all celestial Dames.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रेभदत्र जनुषा पूर्वो अंगिरा ग्रावाण ऊर्ध्वा अभि चक्षुरध्वरं ।येभिर्विहाया अभवद्विचक्षणः पाथः सुमेकं स्वधितिर्वनन्वति ॥
verses.transliteration: rébhat ǀ átra ǀ janúṣā ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ áṅgirāḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ūrdhvā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cakṣuḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀyébhiḥ ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ ábhavat ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ su-mékam ǀ svá-dhitiḥ ǀ vánan-vati ǁ
verses.english_translation: By reason of his birth here Aṅgiras first sang: the pressing-stones upraised beheld the sacrifice- The stones through which the Sage became exceeding vast, and the sharp axe obtains in fight the beauteous place.
verses.wilson_translation: Aṅgirasa, the prior in birth, praises (the gods, here); the uplifted stones behold (the Somaof) thesacrifice, through which (stones) the sage Indrahas been exalted, (and his) thunderbolt brings forth excellentwater, (producing) food on watery way.
verses.griffith_verse: By reason of his birth here Aṅgiras first sang: the pressing-stones upraised beheld the sacrifice- The stones through which the Sage became exceeding vast, and the sharp axe obtains in fight the beauteous place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIII. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १५ तान्वः पार्थ्यः। विश्वेदेवाः। प्रस्तारपंक्तिः २,३,१३ अनुष्टुप् , ९ अक्षरैः पंक्तिः, ११ न्यङ्कुसारिणी, १५ पुरस्ताद्बृहती ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MIGHTY are ye, and far-extended, Heaven and Earth: both Worlds are evermore to us like two young Dames.Guard us thereby from stronger foe; guard us hereby to give us strength. In each succeeding sacrifice that mortal honoureth the Gods,He who, most widely known and famed for happiness, inviteth them. Ye who are Rulers over all, great is your sovran power as Gods.Ye all possess all majesty: all must be served in sacrifice. These are the joyous Kings of Immortality, Parijman, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa.What else is Rudra, praised of men? the Maruts, Bhaga, Pūṣaṇa? Come also to our dwelling, Lords of ample wealth, common partakers of our waters, Sun and Moon,When the great Dragon of the Deep hath settled down upon their floors. And let the Aśvins, Lords of splendour, set us free,—both Gods, and, with their Laws, Mitra and Varuṇa.Through woes, as over desert lands, he speeds to ample opulence. Yea, let the Aśvins Twain he gracious unto us, even Rudras, and all Gods, Bhaga, Rathaspati;Parijman, Ṛbhu, Vāja, O Lords of all wealth Ṛbhukṣaṇas. Prompt is Ṛbhukṣan, prompt the worshipper's strong drink: may thy fleet Bay Steeds, thine who speedest on, approach.Not mans but God's is sacrifice whose psalm is unassailable. O God Savitar, harmed by none, lauded, give us a place among wealthy princes.With his Car-steeds at once 'hath our Indra guided the reins and the car of these men. To these men present here, O Heaven and Earth, to us grant lofty fame extending over all mankind.Give us a steed to win us strength, a steed with wealth for victory. This speaker, Indra—for thou art our Friend—wherever he may be, guard thou, Victor! for help, ever for helpThy wisdom, Vasu! prosper him. So have they strengthened this mine hymn which seems to take its bright path to the Sun, and reconciles the men:Thus forms a carpenter the yoke of horses, not to be displaced. Whose chariot-seat hath come again laden with wealth and bright with gold,Lightly, with piercing ends, as ’twere two ranks of heroes ranged for fight. This to Duḥśīma Pṛthavāna have I sung, to Vena, Rama, to the nobles, and the King.They yoked five hundred, and their love of us was famed upon their way. Besides, they showed us seven-and-seventy horses here.Tānva at once displayed his gift, Pārthya at once displayed his gift; and straightway Māyava showed his.

verses.sanskrit: महि द्यावापृथिवी भूतमुर्वी नारी यह्वी न रोदसी सदं नः ।तेभिर्नः पातं सह्यस एभिर्नः पातं शूषणि ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ bhūtam ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ nā́rī íti ǀ yahvī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ ródasī íti ǀ sádam ǀ naḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pātam ǀ sáhyasaḥ ǀ ebhíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pātam ǀ śūṣáṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: MIGHTY are ye, and far-extended, Heaven and Earth: both Worlds are evermore to us like two young Dames. Guard us thereby from stronger foe; guard us hereby to give us strength.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth, be great and spacious; mighty Rodasī, be ever with us like wives; with these (yourprotections), protect us from (the foe who is) stronger (than we), with these protect us in the might (of ourenemies).
verses.griffith_verse: MIGHTY are ye, and far-extended, Heaven and Earth: both Worlds are evermore to us like two young Dames. Guard us thereby from stronger foe; guard us hereby to give us strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञेयज्ञे स मर्त्यो देवान्त्सपर्यति ।यः सुम्नैर्दीर्घश्रुत्तम आविवासत्येनान् ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñé-yajñe ǀ sáḥ ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ saparyati ǀyáḥ ǀ sumnáiḥ ǀ dīrghaśrút-tamaḥ ǀ ā-vívāsāti ǀ enān ǁ
verses.english_translation: In each succeeding sacrifice that mortal honoureth the Gods, He who, most widely known and famed for happiness, inviteth them.
verses.wilson_translation: That man plural ases the gods at every sacrifice who, being most versed in protracted texts, worshipsthem with gratifying (oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: In each succeeding sacrifice that mortal honoureth the Gods, He who, most widely known and famed for happiness, inviteth them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वेषामिरज्यवो देवानां वार्महः ।विश्वे हि विश्वमहसो विश्वे यज्ञेषु यज्ञियाः ॥
verses.transliteration: víśveṣām ǀ irajyavaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ vā́ḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀvíśve ǀ hí ǀ viśvá-mahasaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye who are Rulers over all, great is your sovran power as Gods. Ye all possess all majesty: all must be served in sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Lords of all worlds, (give us) the abundant wealth of the gods; for (you) all are endowed with greatglory (you) all are to be worshipped at the sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye who are Rulers over all, great is your sovran power as Gods. Ye all possess all majesty: all must be served in sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते घा राजानो अमृतस्य मंद्रा अर्यमा मित्रो वरुणः परिज्मा ।कद्रुद्रो नृणां स्तुतो मरुतः पूषणो भगः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ gha ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ mandrā́ḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀkát ǀ rudráḥ ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀ stutáḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pūṣáṇaḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These are the joyous Kings of Immortality, Parijman, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa. What else is Rudra, praised of men? the Maruts, Bhaga, Pūṣaṇa?
verses.wilson_translation: They are the lords of the ambrosia, adorable,Aryaman,Mitra, the circumambient Varuṇa,Rudra, whois hymned by the priests, the Maruts,Pūṣan,Bhaga.
verses.griffith_verse: These are the joyous Kings of Immortality, Parijman, Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa. What else is Rudra, praised of men? the Maruts, Bhaga, Pūṣaṇa?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो नक्तमपां वृषण्वसू सूर्यामासा सदनाय सधन्या ।सचा यत्साद्येषामहिर्बुध्नेषु बुध्न्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ náktam ǀ apā́m ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀ sū́ryāmā́sā ǀ sádanāya ǀ sa-dhanyā́ ǀsácā ǀ yát ǀ sā́di ǀ eṣām ǀ áhiḥ ǀ budhnéṣu ǀ budhnyáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come also to our dwelling, Lords of ample wealth, common partakers of our waters, Sun and Moon, When the great Dragon of the Deep hath settled down upon their floors.
verses.wilson_translation: And (you two Aśvins) showering wealth, (you) sun and moon, (lords) of the waters, equally rich,(come) by night to our abode, when Ahirbudhnyasits down in their company in the firmamental (clouds).
verses.griffith_verse: Come also to our dwelling, Lords of ample wealth, common partakers of our waters, Sun and Moon, When the great Dragon of the Deep hath settled down upon their floors.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो देवावश्विना शुभस्पती धामभिर्मित्रावरुणा उरुष्यतां ।महः स राय एषतेऽति धन्वेव दुरिता ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ deváu ǀ aśvínā ǀ śubháḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ mitrā́váruṇau ǀ uruṣyatām ǀmaháḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣate ǀ áti ǀ dhánva-iva ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: And let the Aśvins, Lords of splendour, set us free,—both Gods, and, with their Laws, Mitra and Varuṇa. Through woes, as over desert lands, he speeds to ample opulence.
verses.wilson_translation: And may the divine Aśvins, the lords of pure (water), and Mitraand Varuṇaprotect us with theirbodies; he (whom they protect) acquires ample riches, (and passes) through misfortunes as (a traveller through)a desert.
verses.griffith_verse: And let the Aśvins, Lords of splendour, set us free,—both Gods, and, with their Laws, Mitra and Varuṇa. Through woes, as over desert lands, he speeds to ample opulence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत नो रुद्रा चिन्मृळतामश्विना विश्वे देवासो रथस्पतिर्भगः ।ऋभुर्वाज ऋभुक्षणः परिज्मा विश्ववेदसः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ rudrā́ ǀ cit ǀ mṛḷatām ǀ aśvínā ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ráthaḥpátiḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀṛbhúḥ ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ viśva-vedasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, let the Aśvins Twain he gracious unto us, even Rudras, and all Gods, Bhaga, Rathaspati; Parijman, Ṛbhu, Vāja, O Lords of all wealth Ṛbhukṣaṇas.
verses.wilson_translation: And may the Rudras, the Aśvins, make us happy, (may) the universal gods, the lord of chariots,Bhaga,Ṛbhu,Vāja, Ribhukṣaṇa, the circumambient (Vāyu) and the omniscient (deities make us happy).
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, let the Aśvins Twain he gracious unto us, even Rudras, and all Gods, Bhaga, Rathaspati; Parijman, Ṛbhu, Vāja, O Lords of all wealth Ṛbhukṣaṇas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुर्ऋभुक्षा ऋभुर्विधतो मद आ ते हरी जूजुवानस्य वाजिना ।दुष्टरं यस्य साम चिदृधग्यज्ञो न मानुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛbhúḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ vidhatáḥ ǀ mádaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǀ jūjuvānásya ǀ vājínā ǀdustáram ǀ yásya ǀ sā́ma ǀ cit ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prompt is Ṛbhukṣan, prompt the worshipper's strong drink: may thy fleet Bay Steeds, thine who speedest on, approach. Not mans but God's is sacrifice whose psalm is unassailable.
verses.wilson_translation: The mighty (Indra) is resplendent (through the sacrifice), the joy of the worshipper is resplendent;vigorous are the two horses of you rapidly approaching, whose hymn is unassailable (by therākṣasas); (this)sacrifice is apart, not human.
verses.griffith_verse: Prompt is Ṛbhukṣan, prompt the worshipper's strong drink: may thy fleet Bay Steeds, thine who speedest on, approach. Not mans but God's is sacrifice whose psalm is unassailable.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृधी नो अह्रयो देव सवितः स च स्तुषे मघोनां ।सहो न इंद्रो वह्निभिर्न्येषां चर्षणीनां चक्रं रश्मिं न योयुवे ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛdhí ǀ naḥ ǀ áhrayaḥ ǀ deva ǀ savitaríti ǀ sáḥ ǀ ca ǀ stuṣe ǀ maghónām ǀsahó íti ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ váhni-bhiḥ ǀ ní ǀ eṣām ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ cakrám ǀ raśmím ǀ ná ǀ yoyuve ǁ
verses.english_translation: O God Savitar, harmed by none, lauded, give us a place among wealthy princes. With his Car-steeds at once 'hath our Indra guided the reins and the car of these men.
verses.wilson_translation: Make us, divine Savitā, free from shame; you are praised (by the priests) of the opulent; may Indra,accompanied by the bearers (of water), unite the strength of us men here, like the chariot-wheel and reinṣ
verses.griffith_verse: O God Savitar, harmed by none, lauded, give us a place among wealthy princes. With his Car-steeds at once 'hath our Indra guided the reins and the car of these men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऐषु द्यावापृथिवी धातं महदस्मे वीरेषु विश्वचर्षणि श्रवः ।पृक्षं वाजस्य सातये पृक्षं रायोत तुर्वणे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ eṣu ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ dhātam ǀ mahát ǀ asmé íti ǀ vīréṣu ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀpṛkṣám ǀ vā́jasya ǀ sātáye ǀ pṛkṣám ǀ rāyā́ ǀ utá ǀ turváṇe ǁ
verses.english_translation: To these men present here, O Heaven and Earth, to us grant lofty fame extending over all mankind. Give us a steed to win us strength, a steed with wealth for victory.
verses.wilson_translation: Heaven and earth, grant to these our sons great renown, extending over all mankind; grantsustenance for the acquisition of strength, sustenance together with wealth for the overthrow (of enemies).
verses.griffith_verse: To these men present here, O Heaven and Earth, to us grant lofty fame extending over all mankind. Give us a steed to win us strength, a steed with wealth for victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतं शंसमिंद्रास्मयुष्ट्वं कूचित्संतं सहसावन्नभिष्टये ।सदा पाह्यभिष्टये मेदतां वेदता वसो ॥
verses.transliteration: etám ǀ śáṃsam ǀ indra ǀ asma-yúḥ ǀ tvám ǀ kū́-cit ǀ sántam ǀ sahasā-van ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀ sádā ǀ pāhi ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀmedátām ǀ vedátā ǀ vaso íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: This speaker, Indra—for thou art our Friend—wherever he may be, guard thou, Victor! for help, ever for help Thy wisdom, Vasu! prosper him.
verses.wilson_translation: Mighty Indra, do you, who are well affected towards us, ever protect this worshipper wherever he maybe, so that he may attain his desire; instrumental uct me,Vasu, by your wisdom.
verses.griffith_verse: This speaker, Indra—for thou art our Friend—wherever he may be, guard thou, Victor! for help, ever for help Thy wisdom, Vasu! prosper him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतं मे स्तोमं तना न सूर्ये द्युतद्यामानं वावृधंत नृणां ।संवननं नाश्व्यं तष्टेवानपच्युतं ॥
verses.transliteration: etám ǀ me ǀ stómam ǀ tanā́ ǀ ná ǀ sū́rye ǀ dyutát-yāmānam ǀ vavṛdhanta ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀsam-vánanam ǀ ná ǀ áśvyam ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ ánapa-cyutam ǁ
verses.english_translation: So have they strengthened this mine hymn which seems to take its bright path to the Sun, and reconciles the men: Thus forms a carpenter the yoke of horses, not to be displaced.
verses.wilson_translation: May (the priests) strengthen this my hymn, the destroyer of the enemies (of the gods), of brilliant pathlike, the rays in the sun, as the carpenter (sends forth) the upright car.
verses.griffith_verse: So have they strengthened this mine hymn which seems to take its bright path to the Sun, and reconciles the men: Thus forms a carpenter the yoke of horses, not to be displaced.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वावर्त येषां राया युक्तैषां हिरण्ययी ।नेमधिता न पौंस्या वृथेव विष्टांता ॥
verses.transliteration: vavárta ǀ yéṣām ǀ rāyā́ ǀ yuktā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ hiraṇyáyī ǀnemá-dhitā ǀ ná ǀ páuṃsyā ǀ vṛ́thā-iva ǀ viṣṭá-antā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whose chariot-seat hath come again laden with wealth and bright with gold, Lightly, with piercing ends, as ’twere two ranks of heroes ranged for fight.
verses.wilson_translation: Those whose (praise) arrives, accompanied by wealth, of them it is (as) a golden (ornament), likemanly powers in battle reaching the conclusion as it were, without an effort.
verses.griffith_verse: Whose chariot-seat hath come again laden with wealth and bright with gold, Lightly, with piercing ends, as ’twere two ranks of heroes ranged for fight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र तद्दुःशीमे पृथवाने वेने प्र रामे वोचमसुरे मघवत्सु ।ये युक्त्वाय पंच शतास्मयु पथा विश्राव्येषां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ tát ǀ duḥ-śī́me ǀ pṛ́thavāne ǀ vené ǀ prá ǀ rāmé ǀ vocam ǀ ásure ǀ maghávat-su ǀyé ǀ yuktvā́ya ǀ páñca ǀ śatā́ ǀ asma-yú ǀ pathā́ ǀ vi-śrā́vi ǀ eṣām ǁ
verses.english_translation: This to Duḥśīma Pṛthavāna have I sung, to Vena, Rama, to the nobles, and the King. They yoked five hundred, and their love of us was famed upon their way.
verses.wilson_translation: This I proclaim in the presence of Duśīma, Pṛthavāna,Vena, the mighty Rāma, and (other)opulent (princes); those who (come), having yoked five hundred (chariots), their affection for us is renowned onthe road.
verses.griffith_verse: This to Duḥśīma Pṛthavāna have I sung, to Vena, Rama, to the nobles, and the King. They yoked five hundred, and their love of us was famed upon their way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधीन्न्वत्र सप्ततिं च सप्त च ।सद्यो दिदिष्ट तान्वः सद्यो दिदिष्ट पार्थ्यः सद्यो दिदिष्ट मायवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ átra ǀ saptatím ǀ ca ǀ saptá ǀ ca ǀsadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ tā́nvaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ pārthyáḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ māyaváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Besides, they showed us seven-and-seventy horses here. Tānva at once displayed his gift, Pārthya at once displayed his gift; and straightway Māyava showed his.
verses.wilson_translation: Strongest of them Tānvapromptly demanded seven and seventy (cows), Pārthya demandedall three names may refer to the same person n].
verses.griffith_verse: Besides, they showed us seven-and-seventy horses here. Tānva at once displayed his gift, Pārthya at once displayed his gift; and straightway Māyava showed his.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIV. Press-stones.
hymns.anukramani: १४ अर्बुदः काद्रवेयः सर्पः। ग्रावाणः। जगती, ५, ७, १४ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET these speak loudly forth; let us speak out aloud: to the loud speaking Pressing-stones address the speech;When, rich with Soma juice, Stones of the mountain, ye, united, swift to Indra bring the sound of praise. They speak out like a hundred, like a thousand men: they cry aloud to us with their green-tinted mouths,While, pious Stones, they ply their task with piety, and, even before the Hotar, taste the offered food. Loudly they speak, for they have found the savoury meath: they make a humming sound over the meat prepared.As they devour the branch of the Red-coloured Tree, these, the well-pastured Bulls, have uttered bellowings. They cry aloud, with strong exhilarating drink, calling on Indra now, for they have found the meath.Bold, with the sisters they have danced, embraced by them, making the earth reecho with their ringing sound. The Eagles have sent forth their cry aloft in heaven; in the sky's vault the dark impetuous ones have danced.Then downward to the nether stone's fixt place they sink, and, splendid as the Sun, effuse their copious stream. Like strong ones drawing, they have put forth all their strength: the Bulls, harnessed together, bear the chariot-poles.When they have bellowed, panting, swallowing their food, the sound of their loud snorting is like that of steeds. To these who have ten workers and a tenfold girth, to these who have ten yoke-straps and ten binding thongs,To these who bear ten reins, the eternal, sing ye praise, to these who bear ten car-poles, ten when they are yoked. These Stones with ten conductors, rapid in their course, with lovely revolution travel round and round.They have been first to drink the flowing Soma juice, first to enjoy the milky fluid of the stalk. These Soma-eaters kiss Indra's Bay-coloured Steeds: draining. the stalk they sit upon the ox's hide.Indra, when he hath drunk Soma-meath drawn by them, waxes in strength, is famed, is mighty as a Bull.. Strong is your stalk; ye, verily, never shall be harmed; ye have refreshment, ye are ever satisfied.Fair are ye, as it were, through splendour of his wealth, his in whose sacrifice, O Stones, ye find delight. Bored deep, but not pierced through with holes, are ye, O Stones, not loosened, never weary, and exempt from death,Eternal, undiseased, moving in sundry ways, unthirsting, full of fatness, void of all desire. Your fathers, verily, stand firm from age to age: they, loving rest, are not dissevered from their seat.Untouched by time, ne’er lacking green plants and green trees, they with their voice have caused the heavens and earth to hear. This, this the Stones proclaim, what time they are disjoined, and when with ringing sounds they move and drink the balm.Like tillers of the ground when they are sowing seed, they mix the Soma, nor, devouring, minish it. They have raised high their voice for juice, for sacrifice, striking the Mother earth as though they danced thereon.So loose thou too his thought who hath effused the sap, and let the Stones which we are honouring be disjoined.

verses.sanskrit: प्रैते वदंतु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यो वाचं वदता वदद्भ्यः ।यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेंद्राय सोमिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ eté ǀ vadantu ǀ prá ǀ vayám ǀ vadāma ǀ grā́va-bhyaḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ vadata ǀ vádat-bhyaḥ ǀyát ǀ adrayaḥ ǀ parvatāḥ ǀ sākám ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ ślókam ǀ ghóṣam ǀ bháratha ǀ índrāya ǀ somínaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: LET these speak loudly forth; let us speak out aloud: to the loud speaking Pressing-stones address the speech; When, rich with Soma juice, Stones of the mountain, ye, united, swift to Indra bring the sound of praise.
verses.wilson_translation: Let these (stones) speak; let us reply to the speaking stones, and do you (priests) utter (praise); when,you solid, quick-moving stones, you utter the noise of praise together to Indra, (then you become) full of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: LET these speak loudly forth; let us speak out aloud: to the loud speaking Pressing-stones address the speech; When, rich with Soma juice, Stones of the mountain, ye, united, swift to Indra bring the sound of praise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एते वदंति शतवत्सहस्रवदभि क्रंदंति हरितेभिरासभिः ।विष्ट्वी ग्रावाणः सुकृतः सुकृत्यया होतु��्चित्पूर्वे हविरद्यमाशत ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ vadanti ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásra-vat ǀ abhí ǀ krandanti ǀ háritebhiḥ ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǀviṣṭvī́ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ su-kṛtyáyā ǀ hótuḥ ǀ cit ǀ pū́rve ǀ haviḥ-ádyam ǀ āśata ǁ
verses.english_translation: They speak out like a hundred, like a thousand men: they cry aloud to us with their green-tinted mouths, While, pious Stones, they ply their task with piety, and, even before the Hotar, taste the offered food.
verses.wilson_translation: They roar like a hundred, like a thousand (men); they cry aloud with green-tinted faces; obtaining thesacrifice, the pious stones through their piety partake of the sacrificial food, even before (Agni), the invoker (ofthe gods).
verses.griffith_verse: They speak out like a hundred, like a thousand men: they cry aloud to us with their green-tinted mouths, While, pious Stones, they ply their task with piety, and, even before the Hotar, taste the offered food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एते वदंत्यविदन्नना मधु न्यूंखयंते अधि पक्व आमिषि ।वृक्षस्य शाखामरुणस्य बप्सतस्ते सूभर्वा वृषभाः प्रेमराविषुः ॥
verses.transliteration: eté ǀ vadanti ǀ ávidan ǀ anā́ ǀ mádhu ǀ ní ǀ ūṅkhayante ǀ ádhi ǀ pakvé ǀ ā́miṣi ǀvṛkṣásya ǀ śā́khām ǀ aruṇásya ǀ bápsataḥ ǀ té ǀ sū́bharvāḥ ǀ vṛṣabhā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ arāviṣuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Loudly they speak, for they have found the savoury meath: they make a humming sound over the meat prepared. As they devour the branch of the Red-coloured Tree, these, the well-pastured Bulls, have uttered bellowings.
verses.wilson_translation: They speak, they received into their mouth the sweet (Soma), they roar (like the eaters of flesh) overthe roasted meat; chewing the branch of the purplle tree, the voracious bulls have bellowed.
verses.griffith_verse: Loudly they speak, for they have found the savoury meath: they make a humming sound over the meat prepared. As they devour the branch of the Red-coloured Tree, these, the well-pastured Bulls, have uttered bellowings.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहद्वदंति मदिरेण मंदिनेंद्रं क्रोशंतोऽविदन्नना मधु ।संरभ्या धीराः स्वसृभिरनर्तिषुराघोषयंतः पृथिवीमुपब्दिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhát ǀ vadanti ǀ madiréṇa ǀ mandínā ǀ índram ǀ króśantaḥ ǀ avidan ǀ anā́ ǀ mádhu ǀsam-rábhya ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ svásṛ-bhiḥ ǀ anartiṣuḥ ǀ ā-ghoṣáyantaḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ upabdí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They cry aloud, with strong exhilarating drink, calling on Indra now, for they have found the meath. Bold, with the sisters they have danced, embraced by them, making the earth reecho with their ringing sound.
verses.wilson_translation: They cry aloud calling upon Indrawith the intoxicating effused (Soma), they took the sweet Soma intotheir mouth, seized by the sister (fingers) the bold stones danced, filling the earth with shouts.
verses.griffith_verse: They cry aloud, with strong exhilarating drink, calling on Indra now, for they have found the meath. Bold, with the sisters they have danced, embraced by them, making the earth reecho with their ringing sound.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुपर्णा वाचमक्रतोप द्यव्याखरे कृष्णा इषिरा अनर्तिषुः ।न्यङ्नि यंत्युपरस्य निष्कृतं पुरू रेतो दधिरे सूर्यश्वितः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ akrata ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀ ā-kharé ǀ kṛ́ṣṇāḥ ǀ iṣirā́ḥ ǀ anartiṣuḥ ǀnyák ǀ ní ǀ yanti ǀ úparasya ǀ niḥ-kṛtám ǀ purú ǀ rétaḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ sūrya-śvítaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Eagles have sent forth their cry aloft in heaven; in the sky's vault the dark impetuous ones have danced. Then downward to the nether stone's fixt place they sink, and, splendid as the Sun, effuse their copious stream.
verses.wilson_translation: The well-gliding stones made a noise in the firmament; they danced (like) the black deer in the stall;they exude down from the upper stone the expressed (Soma); white as the sun they yield abundant moisture.
verses.griffith_verse: The Eagles have sent forth their cry aloft in heaven; in the sky's vault the dark impetuous ones have danced. Then downward to the nether stone's fixt place they sink, and, splendid as the Sun, effuse their copious stream.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उग्रा इव प्रवहंतः समायमुः साकं युक्ता वृषणो बिभ्रतो धुरः ।यच्छ्वसंतो जग्रसाना अराविषुः शृण्व एषां प्रोथथो अर्वतामिव ॥
verses.transliteration: ugrā́ḥ-iva ǀ pra-váhantaḥ ǀ sam-ā́yamuḥ ǀ sākám ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ dhúraḥ ǀyát ǀ śvasántaḥ ǀ jagrasānā́ḥ ǀ árāviṣuḥ ǀ śṛṇvé ǀ eṣām ǀ protháthaḥ ǀ árvatām-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like strong ones drawing, they have put forth all their strength: the Bulls, harnessed together, bear the chariot-poles. When they have bellowed, panting, swallowing their food, the sound of their loud snorting is like that of steeds.
verses.wilson_translation: Bearing the burden of the sacrifice, yoked with (the Soma), they extend themselves like spiritedhorses; when panting and extracting (the Soma), they cried aloud, their snoring is heard like that of horses.
verses.griffith_verse: Like strong ones drawing, they have put forth all their strength: the Bulls, harnessed together, bear the chariot-poles. When they have bellowed, panting, swallowing their food, the sound of their loud snorting is like that of steeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दशावनिभ्यो दशकक्ष्येभ्यो दशयोक्त्रेभ्यो दशयोजनेभ्यः ।दशाभीशुभ्यो अर्चताजरेभ्यो दश धुरो दश युक्ता वहद्भ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: dáśāvani-bhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-kakṣyebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-yoktrebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-yojanebhyaḥ ǀdáśābhīśu-bhyaḥ ǀ arcata ǀ ajárebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ dhúraḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ váhat-bhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To these who have ten workers and a tenfold girth, to these who have ten yoke-straps and ten binding thongs, To these who bear ten reins, the eternal, sing ye praise, to these who bear ten car-poles, ten when they are yoked.
verses.wilson_translation: Worship (priests), those imperishable (stones) which have ten workers, ten girths, ten yokes, tenagents, ten encompassers, which are possessed of ten burdens, which bear (the sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: To these who have ten workers and a tenfold girth, to these who have ten yoke-straps and ten binding thongs, To these who bear ten reins, the eternal, sing ye praise, to these who bear ten car-poles, ten when they are yoked.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते अद्रयो दशयंत्रास आशवस्तेषामाधानं पर्येति हर्यतं ।त ऊ सुतस्य सोम्यस्यांधसोऽंशोः पीयूषं प्रथमस्य भेजिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ dáśa-yantrāsaḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ téṣām ǀ ā-dhā́nam ǀ pári ǀ eti ǀ haryatám ǀté ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sutásya ǀ somyásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ aṃśóḥ ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ prathamásya ǀ bhejire ǁ
verses.english_translation: These Stones with ten conductors, rapid in their course, with lovely revolution travel round and round. They have been first to drink the flowing Soma juice, first to enjoy the milky fluid of the stalk.
verses.wilson_translation: These stones, having ten reins, swiftly moving, their delightful whirling goes round; they first tasted theambrosia of the fragment of food of the expressed Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: These Stones with ten conductors, rapid in their course, with lovely revolution travel round and round. They have been first to drink the flowing Soma juice, first to enjoy the milky fluid of the stalk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते सोमादो हरी इंद्रस्य निंसतेऽंशुं दुहंतो अध्यासते गवि ।तेभिर्दुग्धं पपिवान्त्सोम्यं मध्विंद्रो वर्धते प्रथते वृषायते ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ soma-ádaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ índrasya ǀ niṃsate ǀ aṃśúm ǀ duhántaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ āsate ǀ gávi ǀtébhiḥ ǀ dugdhám ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǀ índraḥ ǀ vardhate ǀ práthate ǀ vṛṣa-yáte ǁ
verses.english_translation: These Soma-eaters kiss Indra's Bay-coloured Steeds: draining. the stalk they sit upon the ox's hide. Indra, when he hath drunk Soma-meath drawn by them, waxes in strength, is famed, is mighty as a Bull.
verses.wilson_translation: These devourers of Somakiss Indra's horses, milking forth the juice they repose upon the cow, Indrahaving quaffed the sweet Soma milked forth by them increases, waxes broad, grows vigour.
verses.griffith_verse: These Soma-eaters kiss Indra's Bay-coloured Steeds: draining. the stalk they sit upon the ox's hide. Indra, when he hath drunk Soma-meath drawn by them, waxes in strength, is famed, is mighty as a Bull.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषा वो अंशुर्न किला रिषाथनेळावंतः सदमित्स्थनाशिताः ।रैवत्येव महसा चारवः स्थन यस्य ग्रावाणो अजुषध्वमध्वरं ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ vaḥ ǀ aṃśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ kíla ǀ riṣāthana ǀ íḷā-vantaḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ sthana ǀ ā́śitāḥ ǀraivatyā́-iva ǀ máhasā ǀ cā́ravaḥ ǀ sthana ǀ yásya ǀ grāvāṇaḥ ǀ ájuṣadhvam ǀ adhvarám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Strong is your stalk; ye, verily, never shall be harmed; ye have refreshment, ye are ever satisfied. Fair are ye, as it were, through splendour of his wealth, his in whose sacrifice, O Stones, ye find delight.
verses.wilson_translation: The Somais your showerer (at the sacrifice); you are unharmed, (like those) abounding in food, youare constantly feeding; like the wealthy (possessed) of splendour, you, O stones, are beautiful (at the sacrifice ofhim) whose sacrifice you delighted in.
verses.griffith_verse: Strong is your stalk; ye, verily, never shall be harmed; ye have refreshment, ye are ever satisfied. Fair are ye, as it were, through splendour of his wealth, his in whose sacrifice, O Stones, ye find delight.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
