verses.sanskrit: तृदिला अतृदिलासो अद्रयोऽश्रमणा अशृथिता अमृत्यवः ।अनातुरा अजराः स्थामविष्णवः सुपीवसो अतृषिता अतृष्णजः ॥
verses.transliteration: tṛdilā́ḥ ǀ átṛdilāsaḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ aśramaṇā́ḥ ǀ áśṛthitāḥ ǀ ámṛtyavaḥ ǀanāturā́ḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǀ stha ǀ ámaviṣṇavaḥ ǀ su-pīvásaḥ ǀ átṛṣitāḥ ǀ átṛṣṇa-jaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bored deep, but not pierced through with holes, are ye, O Stones, not loosened, never weary, and exempt from death, Eternal, undiseased, moving in sundry ways, unthirsting, full of fatness, void of all desire.
verses.wilson_translation: Splitting, but unsplit, you, O stones, are untiring, unrelaxing, immortal, free from disease, undecaying,rising and falling, powerful, unthirsting, not genitive rating thirst.
verses.griffith_verse: Bored deep, but not pierced through with holes, are ye, O Stones, not loosened, never weary, and exempt from death, Eternal, undiseased, moving in sundry ways, unthirsting, full of fatness, void of all desire.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ध्रुवा एव वः पितरो युगेयुगे क्षेमकामासः सदसो न युंजते ।अजुर्यासो हरिषाचो हरिद्रव आ द्यां रवेण पृथिवीमशुश्रवुः ॥
verses.transliteration: dhruvā́ḥ ǀ evá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ yugé-yuge ǀ kṣéma-kāmāsaḥ ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yuñjate ǀajuryā́saḥ ǀ hari-sā́caḥ ǀ harídravaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ráveṇa ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ aśuśravuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Your fathers, verily, stand firm from age to age: they, loving rest, are not dissevered from their seat. Untouched by time, ne’er lacking green plants and green trees, they with their voice have caused the heavens and earth to hear.
verses.wilson_translation: Your progenitors (the mountains), stable from age to age, desirous of repose, seek not to mix with(religious) assemblies; exempt from decay, enjoying the Soma, flowing green (with Soma), they made heavenand earth resound with their clamour.
verses.griffith_verse: Your fathers, verily, stand firm from age to age: they, loving rest, are not dissevered from their seat. Untouched by time, ne’er lacking green plants and green trees, they with their voice have caused the heavens and earth to hear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तदिद्वदंत्यद्रयो विमोचने यामन्नंजस्पा इव घेदुपब्दिभिः ।वपंतो बीजमिव धान्याकृतः पृंचंति सोमं न मिनंति बप्सतः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ vadanti ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ vi-mócane ǀ yā́man ǀ añjaḥpā́ḥ-iva ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ upabdí-bhiḥ ǀvápantaḥ ǀ bī́jam-iva ǀ dhānya-kṛ́taḥ ǀ pṛñcánti ǀ sómam ǀ ná ǀ minanti ǀ bápsataḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This, this the Stones proclaim, what time they are disjoined, and when with ringing sounds they move and drink the balm. Like tillers of the ground when they are sowing seed, they mix the Soma, nor, devouring, minish it.
verses.wilson_translation: The stones proclaim it with their clamour at the issue of the Soma, like the quick-protecting (chariots)on the road; like cultivators sowing the seed, they, devouring the Soma, mix it, and do not hurt it.
verses.griffith_verse: This, this the Stones proclaim, what time they are disjoined, and when with ringing sounds they move and drink the balm. Like tillers of the ground when they are sowing seed, they mix the Soma, nor, devouring, minish it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुते अध्वरे अधि वाचमक्रता क्रीळयो न मातरं तुदंतः ।वि षू मुंचा सुषुवुषो मनीषां वि वर्तंतामद्रयश्चायमानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: suté ǀ adhvaré ǀ ádhi ǀ vā́cam ǀ akrata ǀ ā́ ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mātáram ǀ tudántaḥ ǀví ǀ sú ǀ muñca ǀ susu-vúṣaḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ ví ǀ vartantām ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ cā́yamānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They have raised high their voice for juice, for sacrifice, striking the Mother earth as though they danced thereon. So loose thou too his thought who hath effused the sap, and let the Stones which we are honouring be disjoined.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Soma) being effused at the sacrifice, they made a noise like (children) at plural y, striking theirmother. Proclaim the praise of (the stone), which has effused (the Soma), let the honoured stones revolve.
verses.griffith_verse: They have raised high their voice for juice, for sacrifice, striking the Mother earth as though they danced thereon. So loose thou too his thought who hath effused the sap, and let the Stones which we are honouring be disjoined.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCV. Urvasi. Purūravas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Ho there, my consort! Stay, thou fierce-souled lady, and let us reason for a while together.Such thoughts as these of ours, while yet unspoken in days gone by have never brought us comfort. What am I now to do with this thy saying? I have gone from thee like the first of Mornings.Purūravas, return thou to thy dwelling: I, like the wind, am difficult to capture. Like a shaft sent for glory from the quiver, or swift-steed winning cattle winning hundreds.The lightning seemed to flash, as cowards planned it. The minstrels bleated like a lamb in trouble. Giving her husband's father life and riches, from the near dwelling, when her lover craved her,She sought the home wherein she found her pleasure, accepting day and night her lord's embraces. Thrice in the day didst thou embrace thy consort, though coldly she received thy fond caresses.To thy desires, Purūravas, I yielded: so wast thou king, O hero, of my body. The maids Sujirni, Sreni, Sumne-api, Charanyu, Granthini, and Hradecaksus,—These like red kine have hastened forth, the bright ones, and like milch-cows have lowed in emulation. While he was born the Dames sate down together, the Rivers with free kindness gave him nurture;And then, Purūravas, the Gods increased thee for mighty battle, to destroy the Dasyus. When I, a mortal, wooed to mine embraces these heavenly nymphs who laid aside their raiment,Like a scared snake they fled from me in terror, like chariot horses when the car has touched them. When, loving these Immortal Ones, the mortal hath converse with the nymphs as they allow him.Like swans they show the beauty of their bodies, like horses in their play they bite and nibble. She who flashed brilliant as the falling lightning brought me delicious presents from the waters.Now from the flood be born a strong young hero May Uruvasi prolong her life for ever Thy birth hath made me drink from earthly milch-kine: this power, Purūravas, hast thou vouchsafed me.I knew, and, warned thee, on that day. Thou wouldst not hear me. What sayest thou, when naught avails thee? When will the son be born and seek his father? Mourner-like, will he weep when first he knows him?Who shall divide the accordant wife and husband, while fire is shining with thy consort's parents? I will console him when his tears are falling: he shall not weep and cry for care that blesses.That which is thine, between us, will I send thee. Go home again, thou fool;ṭhou hast not won me. Thy lover shall flee forth this day for ever, to seek, without return, the farthest distance.Then let his bed be in Destruction's bosom, and there let fierce rapacious wolves devour him. Nay, do not die, Purūravas, nor vanish: let not the evil-omened wolves devour thee.With women there can be no lasting friendship: hearts of hyenas are the hearts of women. When amid men in altered shape I sojourned, and through four autumns spent the nights among them,I tasted once a day a drop of butter; and even now with that am I am contented. I, her best love, call Urvasi to meet me, her who fills air and measures out the region.Let the gift brought by piety approach thee. Turn thou to me again: my heart is troubled. Thus speak these Gods to thee, O son of Iḷā: As death hath verily got thee for his subject,Thy sons shall serve the Gods with their oblation, and thou, moreover, shalt rejoice in Svarga.

verses.sanskrit: हये जाये मनसा तिष्ठ घोरे वचांसि मिश्रा कृणवावहै नु ।न नौ मंत्रा अनुदितास एते मयस्करन्परतरे चनाहन् ॥
verses.transliteration: hayé ǀ jā́ye ǀ mánasā ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ ghore ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ miśrā́ ǀ kṛṇavāvahai ǀ nú ǀná ǀ nau ǀ mántrāḥ ǀ ánuditāsaḥ ǀ eté ǀ máyaḥ ǀ karan ǀ pára-tare ǀ caná ǀ áhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ho there, my consort! Stay, thou fierce-souled lady, and let us reason for a while together. Such thoughts as these of ours, while yet unspoken in days gone by have never brought us comfort.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā) speaks). How indignant wife, with mind (relenting), stay awhile, let us now interchangediscourse. These, our secret thoughts, while unspoken, did not yield us happiness even at the last day.
verses.griffith_verse: Ho there, my consort! Stay, thou fierce-souled lady, and let us reason for a while together. Such thoughts as these of ours, while yet unspoken in days gone by have never brought us comfort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: किमेता वाचा कृणवा तवाहं प्राक्रमिषमुषसामग्रियेव ।पुरूरवः पुनरस्तं परेहि दुरापना वात इवाहमस्मि ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ etā́ ǀ vācā́ ǀ kṛṇava ǀ táva ǀ ahám ǀ prá ǀ akramiṣam ǀ uṣásām ǀ agriyā́-iva ǀpúrūravaḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ duḥ-āpanā́ ǀ vā́taḥ-iva ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: What am I now to do with this thy saying? I have gone from thee like the first of Mornings. Purūravas, return thou to thy dwelling: I, like the wind, am difficult to capture.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī. What can we accomplish through such discourse? I have passed away from you like thefirst of the dawns. Return Purūravā, to your dwelling; I am as hard to catch as the wind.
verses.griffith_verse: What am I now to do with this thy saying? I have gone from thee like the first of Mornings. Purūravas, return thou to thy dwelling: I, like the wind, am difficult to capture.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इषुर्न श्रिय इषुधेरसना गोषाः शतसा न रंहिः ।अवीरे क्रतौ वि दविद्युतन्नोरा न मायुं चितयंत धुनयः ॥
verses.transliteration: íṣuḥ ǀ ná ǀ śriyé ǀ iṣu-dhéḥ ǀ asanā́ ǀ go-sā́ḥ ǀ śata-sā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ ráṃhiḥ ǀavī́re ǀ krátau ǀ ví ǀ davidyutat ǀ ná ǀ úrā ǀ ná ǀ māyúm ǀ citayanta ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a shaft sent for glory from the quiver, or swift-steed winning cattle winning hundreds. The lightning seemed to flash, as cowards planned it. The minstrels bleated like a lamb in trouble.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). The arrow is not to be cast from the quiver for glory. I am no longer the impetuousdespoiler of the cattle (of the enemy), nor of their hundred-fold (riches). My prowess having lost its strength, (mymight) no longer flashes forth; (my warriors) the terrifiers (of the foe) hear not my shout in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a shaft sent for glory from the quiver, or swift-steed winning cattle winning hundreds. The lightning seemed to flash, as cowards planned it. The minstrels bleated like a lamb in trouble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सा वसु दधती श्वशुराय वय उषो यदि वष्ट्यंतिगृहात् ।अस्तं ननक्षे यस्मिंचाकंदिवा नक्तं श्नथिता वैतसेन ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́ ǀ vásu ǀ dádhatī ǀ śváśurāya ǀ váyaḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ yádi ǀ váṣṭi ǀ ánti-gṛhāt ǀástam ǀ nanakṣe ǀ yásmin ǀ cākán ǀ dívā ǀ náktam ǀ śnathitā́ ǀ vaitaséna ǁ
verses.english_translation: Giving her husband's father life and riches, from the near dwelling, when her lover craved her, She sought the home wherein she found her pleasure, accepting day and night her lord's embraces.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśi). If, Uṣas, thisŪrvaśī, offering food and wealth to her father-in-law, loves (her husband),she has gone from the neighbouring house to her husband's home, where she loved (her lord), being delightednight and day by his embraces.
verses.griffith_verse: Giving her husband's father life and riches, from the near dwelling, when her lover craved her, She sought the home wherein she found her pleasure, accepting day and night her lord's embraces.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेनोत स्म मेऽव्यत्यै पृणासि ।पुरूरवोऽनु ते केतमायं राजा मे वीर तन्वस्तदासीः ॥
verses.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ sma ǀ mā ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ śnathayaḥ ǀ vaitaséna ǀ utá ǀ sma ǀ me ǀ ávyatyai ǀ pṛṇāsi ǀpúrūravaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ te ǀ kétam ǀ āyam ǀ rā́jā ǀ me ǀ vīra ǀ tanváḥ ǀ tát ǀ āsīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thrice in the day didst thou embrace thy consort, though coldly she received thy fond caresses. To thy desires, Purūravas, I yielded: so wast thou king, O hero, of my body.
verses.wilson_translation: Thrice a day,Purūravā, have you embraced me, you have loved me without a rival; I have followed(you) to your dwelling, you, hero, have been the sovereign of my person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Thrice in the day didst thou embrace thy consort, though coldly she received thy fond caresses. To thy desires, Purūravas, I yielded: so wast thou king, O hero, of my body.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या सुजूर्णिः श्रेणिः सुम्नआपिर्ह्रदेचक्षुर्न ग्रंथिनी चरण्युः ।ता अंजयोऽरुणयो न सस्रुः श्रिये गावो न धेनवोऽनवंत ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ su-jūrṇíḥ ǀ śréṇiḥ ǀ sumné-āpiḥ ǀ hradé-cakṣuḥ ǀ ná ǀ granthínī ǀ caraṇyúḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ añjáyaḥ ǀ aruṇáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sasruḥ ǀ śriyé ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ anavanta ǁ
verses.english_translation: The maids Sujirni, Sreni, Sumne-api, Charanyu, Granthini, and Hradecaksus,— These like red kine have hastened forth, the bright ones, and like milch-cows have lowed in emulation.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). Sujūraṇi,Śreṇi, Sumna-āpi, Hradecakṣus, Granthinī, and the swift-moving(Ūrvaśiwho arrived) they, decorated and purple-tinted, did not go first, they lowed like kine for protection.
verses.griffith_verse: The maids Sujirni, Sreni, Sumne-api, Charanyu, Granthini, and Hradecaksus,— These like red kine have hastened forth, the bright ones, and like milch-cows have lowed in emulation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समस्मिंजायमान आसत ग्ना उतेमवर्धन्नद्यः स्वगूर्ताः ।महे यत्त्वा पुरूरवो रणायावर्धयंदस्युहत्याय देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ asmin ǀ jā́yamāne ǀ āsata ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ īm ǀ avardhan ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ svá-gūrtāḥ ǀmahé ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ purūravaḥ ǀ ráṇāya ǀ ávardhayan ǀ dasyu-hátyāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: While he was born the Dames sate down together, the Rivers with free kindness gave him nurture; And then, Purūravas, the Gods increased thee for mighty battle, to destroy the Dasyus.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī). As soon as he was born the wives (of the gods) surrounded him, the spontaneouslyflowing rivers nourished him, for the gods reared you,Purūravā, for a mighty conflict, for the slaughter of the Dasyus. (Nirukta, 3.47).
verses.griffith_verse: While he was born the Dames sate down together, the Rivers with free kindness gave him nurture; And then, Purūravas, the Gods increased thee for mighty battle, to destroy the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सचा यदासु जहतीष्वत्कममानुषीषु मानुषो निषेवे ।अप स्म मत्तरसंती न भुज्युस्ता अत्रसन्रथस्पृशो नाश्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sácā ǀ yát ǀ āsu ǀ jáhatīṣu ǀ átkam ǀ ámānuṣīṣu ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ ni-séve ǀápa ǀ sma ǀ mát ǀ tarásantī ǀ ná ǀ bhujyúḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ atrasan ǀ ratha-spṛ́śaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áśvāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When I, a mortal, wooed to mine embraces these heavenly nymphs who laid aside their raiment, Like a scared snake they fled from me in terror, like chariot horses when the car has touched them.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). When, becoming their companion, (Purūravā) the mortal associated with theseimmortal (nymphs) who had abandoned their bodies, they fled from me like a timid doe, like horses harnessed toa chariot.
verses.griffith_verse: When I, a mortal, wooed to mine embraces these heavenly nymphs who laid aside their raiment, Like a scared snake they fled from me in terror, like chariot horses when the car has touched them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदासु मर्तो अमृतासु निस्पृक्सं क्षोणीभिः क्रतुभिर्न पृंक्ते ।ता आतयो न तन्वः शुंभत स्वा अश्वासो न क्रीळयो दंदशानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ āsu ǀ mártaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāsu ǀ ni-spṛ́k ǀ sám ǀ kṣoṇī́bhiḥ ǀ krátu-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛṅkté ǀtā́ḥ ǀ ātáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śumbhata ǀ svā́ḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ dándaśānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, loving these Immortal Ones, the mortal hath converse with the nymphs as they allow him. Like swans they show the beauty of their bodies, like horses in their play they bite and nibble.
verses.wilson_translation: When a mortal mixing with these immortal nymphs has conversed with them with words and actions,they (becoming) ducks do not show their bodies, like plural yful horses champing (the bit).
verses.griffith_verse: When, loving these Immortal Ones, the mortal hath converse with the nymphs as they allow him. Like swans they show the beauty of their bodies, like horses in their play they bite and nibble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विद्युन्न या पतंती दविद्योद्भरंती मे अप्या काम्यानि ।जनिष्टो अपो नर्यः सुजातः प्रोर्वशी तिरत दीर्घमायुः ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-dyút ǀ ná ǀ yā́ ǀ pátantī ǀ dávidyot ǀ bhárantī ǀ me ǀ ápyā ǀ kā́myāni ǀjániṣṭo íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ náryaḥ ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ prá ǀ urváśī ǀ tirata ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: She who flashed brilliant as the falling lightning brought me delicious presents from the waters. Now from the flood be born a strong young hero May Uruvasi prolong her life for ever
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī) who shone like flashing lightning, bringing me the desirable dews (of heaven, hasappeared); a son able in act and friendly to man has been born; Ūrvaśī has prolonged my lengthenedexistence.
verses.griffith_verse: She who flashed brilliant as the falling lightning brought me delicious presents from the waters. Now from the flood be born a strong young hero May Uruvasi prolong her life for ever
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञिष इत्था गोपीथ्याय हि दधाथ तत्पुरूरवो म ओजः ।अशासं त्वा विदुषी सस्मिन्नहन्न म आशृणोः किमभुग्वदासि ॥
verses.transliteration: jajñiṣé ǀ itthā́ ǀ go-pī́thyāya ǀ hí ǀ dadhā́tha ǀ tát ǀ purūravaḥ ǀ me ǀ ójaḥ ǀáśāsam ǀ tvā ǀ vidúṣī ǀ sásmin ǀ áhan ǀ ná ǀ me ǀ ā́ ǀ aśṛṇoḥ ǀ kím ǀ abhúk ǀ vadāsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy birth hath made me drink from earthly milch-kine: this power, Purūravas, hast thou vouchsafed me. I knew, and, warned thee, on that day. Thou wouldst not hear me. What sayest thou, when naught avails thee?
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī). you have been born thus to protect the earth; you have deposited this vigour in me;knowing (the future) I have instrumental ucted you (what to do) every day; you have not listened to me; why do you nowaddress me, neglectful (of my instrumental uction)?
verses.griffith_verse: Thy birth hath made me drink from earthly milch-kine: this power, Purūravas, hast thou vouchsafed me. I knew, and, warned thee, on that day. Thou wouldst not hear me. What sayest thou, when naught avails thee?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कदा सूनुः पितरं जात इच्छाच्चक्रन्नाश्रु वर्तयद्विजानन् ।को दंपती समनसा वि यूयोदध यदग्निः श्वशुरेषु दीदयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ jātáḥ ǀ icchāt ǀ cakrán ǀ ná ǀ áśru ǀ vartayat ǀ vi-jānán ǀkáḥ ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ sá-manasā ǀ ví ǀ yūyot ǀ ádha ǀ yát ǀ agníḥ ǀ śváśureṣu ǀ dī́dayat ǁ
verses.english_translation: When will the son be born and seek his father? Mourner-like, will he weep when first he knows him? Who shall divide the accordant wife and husband, while fire is shining with thy consort's parents?
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). When shall a son (born of you) claim me as a father, and crying, shed a tear onrecognizing (me)? What son shall sever husband and wife who are of one mind, now that the fire shines uponyour husband's parents?
verses.griffith_verse: When will the son be born and seek his father? Mourner-like, will he weep when first he knows him? Who shall divide the accordant wife and husband, while fire is shining with thy consort's parents?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रति ब्रवाणि वर्तयते अश्रु चक्रन्न क्रंददाध्ये शिवायै ।प्र तत्ते हिनवा यत्ते अस्मे परेह्यस्तं नहि मूर मापः ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ bravāṇi ǀ vartáyate ǀ áśru ǀ cakrán ǀ ná ǀ krandat ǀ ā-dhyé ǀ śivā́yai ǀprá ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ hinava ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ asmé íti ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ ástam ǀ nahí ǀ mūra ǀ mā ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will console him when his tears are falling: he shall not weep and cry for care that blesses. That which is thine, between us, will I send thee. Go home again, thou fool;ṭhou hast not won me.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī). Let me reply. (Your son) will shed tears, crying out and calling aloud when the expectedauspicious time arrives; I will send you that (child) which is yours in me, depart to your house, you cannot,simpleton, detain me.
verses.griffith_verse: I will console him when his tears are falling: he shall not weep and cry for care that blesses. That which is thine, between us, will I send thee. Go home again, thou fool;ṭhou hast not won me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुदेवो अद्य प्रपतेदनावृत्परावतं परमां गंतवा उ ।अधा शयीत निर्ऋतेरुपस्थेऽधैनं वृका रभसासो अद्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: su-deváḥ ǀ adyá ǀ pra-pátet ǀ ánāvṛt ǀ parā-vátam ǀ paramā́m ǀ gántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀádha ǀ śáyīta ǀ níḥ-ṛteḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ ádha ǀ enam ǀ vṛ́kāḥ ǀ rabhasā́saḥ ǀ adyúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy lover shall flee forth this day for ever, to seek, without return, the farthest distance. Then let his bed be in Destruction's bosom, and there let fierce rapacious wolves devour him.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). (Your husband) who sports with you may now depart, never to return, (depart) toproceed to a distant region. Either let him sleep upon the lap of Nirṛti, or let the swift-moving wolves devour hiṃ
verses.griffith_verse: Thy lover shall flee forth this day for ever, to seek, without return, the farthest distance. Then let his bed be in Destruction's bosom, and there let fierce rapacious wolves devour him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुरूरवो मा मृथा मा प्र पप्तो मा त्वा वृकासो अशिवास उ क्षन् ।न वै स्त्रैणानि सख्यानि संति सालावृकाणां हृदयान्येता ॥
verses.transliteration: púrūravaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ mṛthāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ prá ǀ paptaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ vṛ́kāsaḥ ǀ áśivāsaḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ kṣan ǀná ǀ vái ǀ stráiṇāni ǀ sakhyā́ni ǀ santi ǀ sālāvṛkā́ṇām ǀ hṛ́dayāni ǀ etā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nay, do not die, Purūravas, nor vanish: let not the evil-omened wolves devour thee. With women there can be no lasting friendship: hearts of hyenas are the hearts of women.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśi). Die not,Purūravā, fall not, let not the hideous wolves devour you. feminine le friendships donot exist, their hearts are the hearts of jackals.
verses.griffith_verse: Nay, do not die, Purūravas, nor vanish: let not the evil-omened wolves devour thee. With women there can be no lasting friendship: hearts of hyenas are the hearts of women.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्विरूपाचरं मर्त्येष्ववसं रात्रीः शरदश्चतस्रः ।घृतस्य स्तोकं सकृदह्न आश्नां तादेवेदं तातृपाणा चरामि ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ví-rūpā ǀ ácaram ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ ávasam ǀ rā́trīḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǀghṛtásya ǀ stokám ǀ sakṛ́t ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ āśnām ǀ tā́t ǀ evá ǀ idám ǀ tatṛpāṇā́ ǀ carāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: When amid men in altered shape I sojourned, and through four autumns spent the nights among them, I tasted once a day a drop of butter; and even now with that am I am contented.
verses.wilson_translation: When changed in form I wandered among mortals. I dwelt (with them) four delightful years. I ate oncea day a small quantity of butter; satisfied with that I now depart.
verses.griffith_verse: When amid men in altered shape I sojourned, and through four autumns spent the nights among them, I tasted once a day a drop of butter; and even now with that am I am contented.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंतरिक्षप्रां रजसो विमानीमुप शिक्षाम्युर्वशीं वसिष्ठः ।उप त्वा रातिः सुकृतस्य तिष्ठान्नि वर्तस्व हृदयं तप्यते मे ॥
verses.transliteration: antarikṣa-prā́m ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́nīm ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣāmi ǀ urváśīm ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀúpa ǀ tvā ǀ rātíḥ ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ tíṣṭhāt ǀ ní ǀ vartasva ǀ hṛ́dayam ǀ tapyate ǀ me ǁ
verses.english_translation: I, her best love, call Urvasi to meet me, her who fills air and measures out the region. Let the gift brought by piety approach thee. Turn thou to me again: my heart is troubled.
verses.wilson_translation: (Purūravā). I,Vasiṣṭha, bring under subjectionŪrvaśīwho fills the firmament (with lustre) andmeasures out the rain. May (Purūravā), the bestower of the auspicious rite, abide near you; come back-- myheart is burning.
verses.griffith_verse: I, her best love, call Urvasi to meet me, her who fills air and measures out the region. Let the gift brought by piety approach thee. Turn thou to me again: my heart is troubled.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इति त्वा देवा इम आहुरैळ यथेमेतद्भवसि मृत्युबंधुः ।प्रजा ते देवान्हविषा यजाति स्वर्ग उ त्वमपि मादयासे ॥
verses.transliteration: íti ǀ tvā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ imé ǀ āhuḥ ǀ aiḷa ǀ yáthā ǀ īm ǀ etát ǀ bhávasi ǀ mṛtyú-bandhuḥ ǀpra-jā́ ǀ te ǀ devā́n ǀ havíṣā ǀ yajāti ǀ svaḥ-gé ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvám ǀ ápi ǀ mādayāse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus speak these Gods to thee, O son of Iḷā: As death hath verily got thee for his subject, Thy sons shall serve the Gods with their oblation, and thou, moreover, shalt rejoice in Svarga.
verses.wilson_translation: (Ūrvaśī). These gods said to you, Aiḷa, since you are indeed subject to death, let your progenypropitiate your gods with oblations, you shall rejoice (with me) in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus speak these Gods to thee, O son of Iḷā: As death hath verily got thee for his subject, Thy sons shall serve the Gods with their oblation, and thou, moreover, shalt rejoice in Svarga.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १३ बरुरांगिरसः, सर्वहरिर्वा ऐन्द्रः। हरिः। जगती, १२-१३ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: In the great synod will I laud thy two Bay Steeds: I prize the sweet strong drink of thee the Warrior-God,His who pours lovely oil as ’twere with yellow drops. Let my songs enter thee whose form hath golden tints. Ye who in concert sing unto the goldhued place, like Bay Steeds driving onward to the heavenly seat,For Indra laud ye strength allied with Tawny Steeds, laud him whom cows content as ’twere with yellow drops. His is that thunderbolt, of iron, goldenhued, gold-coloured, very dear, and yellow in his arms;Bright with strong teeth, destroying with its tawny rage. In Indra are set fast all forms of golden hue. As if a lovely ray were laid upon the sky, the golden thunderbolt spread out as in a race.That iron bolt with yellow jaw smote Ahi down. A thousand flames had he who bore the tawny-hued. Thou, thou, when praised by men who sacrificed of old. hadst pleasure in their lauds, O Indra golden-haired.All that befits thy song of praise thou welcornest, the perfect pleasant gift, O Golden-hued from birth. These two dear Bays bring hither Indra on his car, Thunder-armed, joyous, meet for laud, to drink his fill.Many libations flow for him who loveth them: to Indra have the gold-hued Soma juices run. Tle gold-hued drops have flowed to gratify his wish: the yellow dro s have urged the swift Bays to the Strong.He who speeds on with Bay Steeds even as he lists hath satisfied his longing for the golden drops. At the swift draught the Soma-drinker waxed in might, the Iron One with yellow beard and yellow hair.He, Lord of Tawny Coursers, Lord of fleet-foot Mares, will bear his Bay Steeds safely over all distress. His yellow-coloured jaws, like ladles move apart, what time, for strength, he makes the yellow-tinted stir,When, while the bowl stands there, he grooms his Tawny Steeds, when he hath drunk strong drink, the sweet juice that he loves. Yea, to the Dear One's seat in homes of heaven and earth the Bay Steeds' Lord hath whinnied like a horse for food.Then the great wish hath seized upon him mightily, and the Beloved One hath gained high power of life, Thou, comprehending with thy might the earth and heaven, acceptest the dear hymn for ever new and new.O Asura, disclose thou and make visible the Cow's beloved home to the bright golden Sun. O Indra, let the eager wishes of the folk bring thee, delightful, golden-visored, on thy car,That, pleased with sacrifice wherein ten fingers toil, thou mayest, at the feast, drink of our offered meath. Juices aforetime, Lord of Bays, thou drankest; and thine especially is this libation.Gladden thee, Indra, with the meath-rich Soma: pour it down ever, Mighty One! within thee.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते महे विदथे शंसिषं हरी प्र ते वन्वे वनुषो हर्यतं मदं ।घृतं न यो हरिभिश्चारु सेचत आ त्वा विशंतु हरिवर्पसं गिरः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ mahé ǀ vidáthe ǀ śaṃsiṣam ǀ hárī íti ǀ prá ǀ te ǀ vanve ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀ haryatám ǀ mádam ǀghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ cā́ru ǀ sécate ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ viśantu ǀ hári-varpasam ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the great synod will I laud thy two Bay Steeds: I prize the sweet strong drink of thee the Warrior-God, His who pours lovely oil as ’twere with yellow drops. Let my songs enter thee whose form hath golden tints.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorified your bay horses,Indra, at the great sacrifice. I solicit the agreeable exhilaration of you, thedestroyer. May my praises attain to you, whose form is yellow, who, with your horses, shower (water) likebeautiful butter.
verses.griffith_verse: In the great synod will I laud thy two Bay Steeds: I prize the sweet strong drink of thee the Warrior-God, His who pours lovely oil as ’twere with yellow drops. Let my songs enter thee whose form hath golden tints.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हरिं हि योनिमभि ये समस्वरन्हिन्वंतो हरी दिव्यं यथा सदः ।आ यं पृणंति हरिभिर्न धेनव इंद्राय शूषं हरिवंतमर्चत ॥
verses.transliteration: hárim ǀ hí ǀ yónim ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ sam-ásvaran ǀ hinvántaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ divyám ǀ yáthā ǀ sádaḥ ǀā́ ǀ yám ǀ pṛṇánti ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ śūṣám ǀ hári-vantam ǀ arcata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye who in concert sing unto the goldhued place, like Bay Steeds driving onward to the heavenly seat, For Indra laud ye strength allied with Tawny Steeds, laud him whom cows content as ’twere with yellow drops.
verses.wilson_translation: You, who have praised the horse, the seat of Indra, urging the horses so that (Indra may reach) thedivine assembly, do you worship the horse- possessing might of Indra, whom men delight with the golden-tinted Soma as kine (with their milk).
verses.griffith_verse: Ye who in concert sing unto the goldhued place, like Bay Steeds driving onward to the heavenly seat, For Indra laud ye strength allied with Tawny Steeds, laud him whom cows content as ’twere with yellow drops.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो अस्य वज्रो हरितो य आयसो हरिर्निकामो हरिरा गभस्त्योः ।द्युम्नी सुशिप्रो हरिमन्युसायक इंद्रे नि रूपा हरिता मिमिक्षिरे ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ asya ǀ vájraḥ ǀ háritaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ háriḥ ǀ ní-kāmaḥ ǀ háriḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀdyumnī́ ǀ su-śipráḥ ǀ hárimanyu-sāyakaḥ ǀ índre ǀ ní ǀ rūpā́ ǀ háritā ǀ mimikṣire ǁ
verses.english_translation: His is that thunderbolt, of iron, goldenhued, gold-coloured, very dear, and yellow in his arms; Bright with strong teeth, destroying with its tawny rage. In Indra are set fast all forms of golden hue.
verses.wilson_translation: That is his thunderbolt, yellow, made of iron, the destroyer (of foes), desirable, the destroyer (of foes),it is in hishands; he is) possessed of riches, handsome jawed, possessed of a shaft and anger which deestroys(his foes)-- many golden-tinted forms are mixed in Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: His is that thunderbolt, of iron, goldenhued, gold-coloured, very dear, and yellow in his arms; Bright with strong teeth, destroying with its tawny rage. In Indra are set fast all forms of golden hue.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवि न केतुरधि धायि हर्यतो विव्यचद्वज्रो हरितो न रंह्या ।तुददहिं हरिशिप्रो य आयसः सहस्रशोका अभवद्धरिंभरः ॥
verses.transliteration: diví ǀ ná ǀ ketúḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhāyi ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ vivyácat ǀ vájraḥ ǀ háritaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ráṃhyā ǀtudát ǀ áhim ǀ hári-śipraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ sahásra-śokāḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ harim-bharáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As if a lovely ray were laid upon the sky, the golden thunderbolt spread out as in a race. That iron bolt with yellow jaw smote Ahi down. A thousand flames had he who bore the tawny-hued.
verses.wilson_translation: He has been plural ced (by his worshippers) in the sky, like the banner (of light, the sun). His desirablebolt reaches (the foe) as the bay horses (of the sun reach their aim) through speed. The iron (thunderbolt), withyellow jaws, which smote Ahi, (he,Indra), lord of horses, shone with a thousand lustres.
verses.griffith_verse: As if a lovely ray were laid upon the sky, the golden thunderbolt spread out as in a race. That iron bolt with yellow jaw smote Ahi down. A thousand flames had he who bore the tawny-hued.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वंत्वमहर्यथा उपस्तुतः पूर्वेभिरिंद्र हरिकेश यज्वभिः ।त्वं हर्यसि तव विश्वमुक्थ्यमसामि राधो हरिजात हर्यतं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám-tvam ǀ aharyathāḥ ǀ úpa-stutaḥ ǀ pū́rvebhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ hari-keśa ǀ yájva-bhiḥ ǀtvám ǀ haryasi ǀ táva ǀ víśvam ǀ ukthyám ǀ ásāmi ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ hari-jāta ǀ haryatám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, thou, when praised by men who sacrificed of old. hadst pleasure in their lauds, O Indra golden-haired. All that befits thy song of praise thou welcornest, the perfect pleasant gift, O Golden-hued from birth.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, with yellow locks, when praised by ancient worshippers, you did desire the oblation; you whoare manifested of a golden hue desire your universal praise, your peculiar and delightful (sacrificial) food.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, thou, when praised by men who sacrificed of old. hadst pleasure in their lauds, O Indra golden-haired. All that befits thy song of praise thou welcornest, the perfect pleasant gift, O Golden-hued from birth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता वज्रिणं मंदिनं स्तोम्यं मद इंद्रं रथे वहतो हर्यता हरी ।पुरूण्यस्मै सवनानि हर्यत इंद्राय सोमा हरयो दधन्विरे ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vajríṇam ǀ mandínam ǀ stómyam ǀ máde ǀ índram ǀ ráthe ǀ vahataḥ ǀ haryatā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀpurū́ṇi ǀ asmai ǀ sávanāni ǀ háryate ǀ índrāya ǀ sómāḥ ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ dadhanvire ǁ
verses.english_translation: These two dear Bays bring hither Indra on his car, Thunder-armed, joyous, meet for laud, to drink his fill. Many libations flow for him who loveth them: to Indra have the gold-hued Soma juices run.
verses.wilson_translation: These two delightful bay horses bring the thunderer, the rejoicing and laudable Indra, in his car to theexhilaration (of the Soma); for him the beloved one many libations of the yellow-tinted Soma are stored up.
verses.griffith_verse: These two dear Bays bring hither Indra on his car, Thunder-armed, joyous, meet for laud, to drink his fill. Many libations flow for him who loveth them: to Indra have the gold-hued Soma juices run.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अरं कामाय हरयो दधन्विरे स्थिराय हिन्वन्हरयो हरी तुरा ।अर्वद्भिर्यो हरिभिर्जोषमीयते सो अस्य कामं हरिवंतमानशे ॥
verses.transliteration: áram ǀ kā́māya ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ dadhanvire ǀ sthirā́ya ǀ hinvan ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ turā́ ǀárvat-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ jóṣam ǀ ī́yate ǀ sáḥ ǀ asya ǀ kā́mam ǀ hári-vantam ǀ ānaśe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tle gold-hued drops have flowed to gratify his wish: the yellow dro s have urged the swift Bays to the Strong. He who speeds on with Bay Steeds even as he lists hath satisfied his longing for the golden drops.
verses.wilson_translation: Yellow-tinted (Soma) is stored up sufficient to whet his desires, the yellow-tinted Soma urges his twoswift bay horses for the salwart (Indra). His (chariot) which rushes with spirited bay horses to the conflict, hasreached his desire (the sacrifice) in which the Soma is presented.
verses.griffith_verse: Tle gold-hued drops have flowed to gratify his wish: the yellow dro s have urged the swift Bays to the Strong. He who speeds on with Bay Steeds even as he lists hath satisfied his longing for the golden drops.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हरिश्मशारुर्हरिकेश आयसस्तुरस्पेये यो हरिपा अवर्धत ।अर्वद्भिर्यो हरिभिर्वाजिनीवसुरति विश्वा दुरिता पारिषद्धरी ॥
verses.transliteration: hári-śmaśāruḥ ǀ hári-keśaḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ turaḥ-péye ǀ yáḥ ǀ hari-pā́ḥ ǀ ávardhata ǀárvat-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ vājínī-vasuḥ ǀ áti ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ pā́riṣat ǀ hárī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: At the swift draught the Soma-drinker waxed in might, the Iron One with yellow beard and yellow hair. He, Lord of Tawny Coursers, Lord of fleet-foot Mares, will bear his Bay Steeds safely over all distress.
verses.wilson_translation: The yellow-bearded, yellow-haired, iron-hearted Indra, the drinker of the yellow (Soma), who has beeninvigorated by the Soma which has to be quickly quaffed, who is rich in sacrificial food through his swift bayhorses, may he drive his two bay horses safe through all difficulties.
verses.griffith_verse: At the swift draught the Soma-drinker waxed in might, the Iron One with yellow beard and yellow hair. He, Lord of Tawny Coursers, Lord of fleet-foot Mares, will bear his Bay Steeds safely over all distress.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्रुवेव यस्य हरिणी विपेततुः शिप्रे वाजाय हरिणी दविध्वतः ।प्र यत्कृते चमसे मर्मृजद्धरी पीत्वा मदस्य हर्यतस्यांधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: srúvā-iva ǀ yásya ǀ háriṇī íti ǀ vi-petátuḥ ǀ śípre íti ǀ vā́jāya ǀ háriṇī íti ǀ dávidhvataḥ ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ kṛté ǀ camasé ǀ mármṛjat ǀ hárī íti ǀ pītvā́ ǀ mádasya ǀ haryatásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: His yellow-coloured jaws, like ladles move apart, what time, for strength, he makes the yellow-tinted stir, When, while the bowl stands there, he grooms his Tawny Steeds, when he hath drunk strong drink, the sweet juice that he loves.
verses.wilson_translation: He whose bay horses alight (upon the Soma) like two ladies, whose yellow jaws tremble (witheagerness) for the sacrificial food, (is praised) when having drunk of the delicious exhilarating Soma in theprepared cup, he rubs down his bay horses.
verses.griffith_verse: His yellow-coloured jaws, like ladles move apart, what time, for strength, he makes the yellow-tinted stir, When, while the bowl stands there, he grooms his Tawny Steeds, when he hath drunk strong drink, the sweet juice that he loves.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत स्म सद्म हर्यतस्य पस्त्योरत्यो न वाजं हरिवाँ अचिक्रदत् ।मही चिद्धि धिषणाहर्यदोजसा बृहद्वयो दधिषे हर्यतश्चिदा ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ sádma ǀ haryatásya ǀ pastyóḥ ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǀ hári-vān ǀ acikradat ǀmahī́ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ áharyat ǀ ójasā ǀ bṛhát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yea, to the Dear One's seat in homes of heaven and earth the Bay Steeds' Lord hath whinnied like a horse for food. Then the great wish hath seized upon him mightily, and the Beloved One hath gained high power of life,
verses.wilson_translation: The dwelling of the gracious (Indra) is in heaven and earth; exhilarated by the Somahe rushesimpetuously as a charger to battle. The earnest prayer desires (Indra endowed) with might; you bestow amplefood on the devout (worshipper).
verses.griffith_verse: Yea, to the Dear One's seat in homes of heaven and earth the Bay Steeds' Lord hath whinnied like a horse for food. Then the great wish hath seized upon him mightily, and the Beloved One hath gained high power of life,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ रोदसी हर्यमाणो महित्वा नव्यंनव्यं हर्यसि मन्म नु प्रियं ।प्र पस्त्यमसुर हर्यतं गोराविष्कृधि हरये सूर्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ háryamāṇaḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ návyam-navyam ǀ haryasi ǀ mánma ǀ nú ǀ priyám ǀprá ǀ pastyám ǀ asura ǀ haryatám ǀ góḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ háraye ǀ sū́ryāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, comprehending with thy might the earth and heaven, acceptest the dear hymn for ever new and new. O Asura, disclose thou and make visible the Cow's beloved home to the bright golden Sun.
verses.wilson_translation: You (Indra) who are the object of desire (fill) heaven and earth with your greatness, you desire gratefulpraise ever new and new; O powerful one, make manifest the desirable dwelling of the water to the
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, comprehending with thy might the earth and heaven, acceptest the dear hymn for ever new and new. O Asura, disclose thou and make visible the Cow's beloved home to the bright golden Sun.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वा हर्यंतं प्रयुजो जनानां रथे वहंतु हरिशिप्रमिंद्र ।पिबा यथा प्रतिभृतस्य मध्वो हर्यन्यज्ञं सधमादे दशोणिं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ haryántam ǀ pra-yújaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ráthe ǀ vahantu ǀ hári-śipram ǀ indra ǀpíba ǀ yáthā ǀ práti-bhṛtasya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ háryan ǀ yajñám ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ dáśa-oṇim ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, let the eager wishes of the folk bring thee, delightful, golden-visored, on thy car, That, pleased with sacrifice wherein ten fingers toil, thou mayest, at the feast, drink of our offered meath.
verses.wilson_translation: Let your horses yoked to the chariot bring you,Indra, the yellow- jawed, desiring (the sacrifice), to (thevicinity) of the worshippers; when you, desiring the sacrifice, prepared by the ten fingers, drink of the collectedsweet-flavoured Soma, (let them bring you) to the battle.
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, let the eager wishes of the folk bring thee, delightful, golden-visored, on thy car, That, pleased with sacrifice wherein ten fingers toil, thou mayest, at the feast, drink of our offered meath.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपाः पूर्वेषां हरिवः सुतानामथो इदं सवनं केवलं ते ।ममद्धि सोमं मधुमंतमिंद्र सत्रा वृषंजठर आ वृषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: ápāḥ ǀ pū́rveṣām ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ sutā́nām ǀ átho íti ǀ idám ǀ sávanam ǀ kévalam ǀ te ǀmamaddhí ǀ sómam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ indra ǀ satrā́ ǀ vṛṣan ǀ jaṭháre ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Juices aforetime, Lord of Bays, thou drankest; and thine especially is this libation. Gladden thee, Indra, with the meath-rich Soma: pour it down ever, Mighty One! within thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of horses, you did drink of previous libations, this sacrifice is for you alone; exhilarate yourself.Indrawith the sweet Soma; showerer of copious rain, shower it into your belly.
verses.griffith_verse: Juices aforetime, Lord of Bays, thou drankest; and thine especially is this libation. Gladden thee, Indra, with the meath-rich Soma: pour it down ever, Mighty One! within thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVII. Praise of Herbs.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HERBS that sprang up in time of old, three ages earlier than the Gods,—Of these, whose hue is brown, will I declare the hundred powers and seven. Ye, Mothers, have a hundred homes, yea, and a thousand are your growths.Do ye who have a thousand powers free this my patient from disease. Be glad and joyful in the Plants, both blossoming and bearing fruit,Plants that will lead us to success like mares who conquer in the race. Plants, by this name I speak to you, Mothers, to you the Goddesses:Steed, cow, and garment may I win, win back thy very self, O man. The Holy Fig tree is your home, your mansion is the Parna tree:Winners of cattle shali ye be if ye regain for me this man. He who hath store of Herbs at hand like Kings amid a crowd of men,—Physician is that sage's name, fiend-slayer, chaser of disease. Herbs rich in Soma, rich in steeds, in nourishments, in strengthening power,—All these have I provided here, that this man may be whole again. The healing virtues of the Plants stream forth like cattle from the stall,—Plants that shall win me store of wealth, and save thy vital breath, O man. Reliever is your mother's name, and hence Restorers are ye called.Rivers are ye with wings that fly: keep far whatever brings disease. Over all fences have they passed, as steals a thief into the fold.The Plants have driven from the frame whatever malady was there. When, bringing back the vanished strength, I hold these herbs within my hand,The spirit of disease departs ere he can seize upon the life. He through whose frame, O Plants, ye creep member by member, joint by joint,—From him ye drive away disease like some strong arbiter of strife. Fly, Spirit of Disease, begone, with the blue jay and kingfisher.Fly with the wind's impetuousspeed, vanish together with the storm. Help every one the other, lend assistance each of you to each,All of you be accordant, give furtherance to this speech of mine. Let fruitful Plants, and fruitless, those that blossom, and the blossomless,Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, release us from our pain and grief; Release me from the curse's plague and woe that comes from Varuṇa;Free me from Yama's fetter, from sin and offence against the Gods. What time, descending from the sky, the Plants flew earthward, thus they spake:No evil shall befall the man whom while he liveth we pervade, Of all the many Plants whose King is, Soma, Plants of hundred forms,Thou art the Plant most excellent, prompt to the wish, sweet to the heart. O all ye various Herbs whose King is Soma, that o’erspread the earth,Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, combine your virtue in this Plant. Unharmed be he who digs you up, unharmed the man for whom I dig:And let no malady attack biped or quadruped of ours. All Plants that hear this speech, and those that have departed far away,Come all assembled and confer your healing power upon this Herb. With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say:O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes. Most excellent of all art thou, O Plant thy vassals are the trees.Let him be subject to our power, the man who seeks to injure us.

verses.sanskrit: या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा ।मनै नु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ tri-yugám ǀ purā́ ǀmánai ǀ nú ǀ babhrū́ṇām ǀ ahám ǀ śatám ǀ dhā́māni ǀ saptá ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: HERBS that sprang up in time of old, three ages earlier than the Gods,— Of these, whose hue is brown, will I declare the hundred powers and seven.
verses.wilson_translation: I think of the hundred and seven applications of the brown-tinted plural nts, which are ancient, beinggenerated for the gods before the three ages.
verses.griffith_verse: HERBS that sprang up in time of old, three ages earlier than the Gods,— Of these, whose hue is brown, will I declare the hundred powers and seven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं वो अंब धामानि सहस्रमुत वो रुहः ।अधा शतक्रत्वो यूयमिमं मे अगदं कृत ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ vaḥ ǀ amba ǀ dhā́māni ǀ sahásram ǀ utá ǀ vaḥ ǀ rúhaḥ ǀádha ǀ śata-kratvaḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ imám ǀ me ǀ agadám ǀ kṛta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, Mothers, have a hundred homes, yea, and a thousand are your growths. Do ye who have a thousand powers free this my patient from disease.
verses.wilson_translation: Mothers (of mankind) a hundred are your applications, a thousandfold is your growth; do you who fulfila hundred functions, make this my (people) free from disease.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, Mothers, have a hundred homes, yea, and a thousand are your growths. Do ye who have a thousand powers free this my patient from disease.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओषधीः प्रति मोदध्वं पुष्पवतीः प्रसूवरीः ।अश्वा इव सजित्वरीर्वीरुधः पारयिष्ण्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: óṣadhīḥ ǀ práti ǀ modadhvam ǀ púṣpa-vatīḥ ǀ pra-sū́varīḥ ǀáśvāḥ-iva ǀ sa-jítvarīḥ ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ pārayiṣṇváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be glad and joyful in the Plants, both blossoming and bearing fruit, Plants that will lead us to success like mares who conquer in the race.
verses.wilson_translation: Rejoice, plural nts, bearing abundant flowers and fruit, triumphing together (over disease) like (victorious)horses, sprouting forth, bearing (men safe) beyond (disease).
verses.griffith_verse: Be glad and joyful in the Plants, both blossoming and bearing fruit, Plants that will lead us to success like mares who conquer in the race.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओषधीरिति मातरस्तद्वो देवीरुप ब्रुवे ।सनेयमश्वं गां वास आत्मानं तव पूरुष ॥
verses.transliteration: óṣadhīḥ ǀ íti ǀ mātaraḥ ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ devīḥ ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀsanéyam ǀ áśvam ǀ gā́m ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ ātmā́nam ǀ táva ǀ puruṣa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Plants, by this name I speak to you, Mothers, to you the Goddesses: Steed, cow, and garment may I win, win back thy very self, O man.
verses.wilson_translation: "plural nts!" thus I hail you, the divine mothers (of mankind). I will give to you, oḥ physician, a horse, acow, a garment-- yes, even myself.
verses.griffith_verse: Plants, by this name I speak to you, Mothers, to you the Goddesses: Steed, cow, and garment may I win, win back thy very self, O man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थे वो निषदनं पर्णे वो वसतिष्कृता ।गोभाज इत्किलासथ यत्सनवथ पूरुषं ॥
verses.transliteration: aśvatthé ǀ vaḥ ǀ ni-sádanam ǀ parṇé ǀ vaḥ ǀ vasatíḥ ǀ kṛtā́ ǀgo-bhā́jaḥ ǀ ít ǀ kíla ǀ asatha ǀ yát ǀ sanávatha ǀ púruṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Holy Fig tree is your home, your mansion is the Parna tree: Winners of cattle shali ye be if ye regain for me this man.
verses.wilson_translation: Your abode is in the Aśvattha, your dwelling is established in the Palāśa, you are assuredly thedistributer of cattle, inasmuch as you bestow them on the physician.
verses.griffith_verse: The Holy Fig tree is your home, your mansion is the Parna tree: Winners of cattle shali ye be if ye regain for me this man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यत्रौषधीः समग्मत राजानः समिताविव ।विप्रः स उच्यते भिषग्रक्षोहामीवचातनः ॥
verses.transliteration: yátra ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sam-ágmata ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ sámitau-iva ǀvípraḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ucyate ǀ bhiṣák ǀ rakṣaḥ-hā́ ǀ amīva-cā́tanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who hath store of Herbs at hand like Kings amid a crowd of men,— Physician is that sage's name, fiend-slayer, chaser of disease.
verses.wilson_translation: Where, plural nts, you are congregated like princes (assembled) in battle, there the sage is designated aphysician, the destroyer of evil spirits, the extirpator of disease.
verses.griffith_verse: He who hath store of Herbs at hand like Kings amid a crowd of men,— Physician is that sage's name, fiend-slayer, chaser of disease.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अश्वावतीं सोमावतीमूर्जयंतीमुदोजसं ।आवित्सि सर्वा ओषधीरस्मा अरिष्टतातये ॥
verses.transliteration: aśva-vatī́m ǀ soma-vatī́m ǀ ūrjáyantīm ǀ út-ojasam ǀā́ ǀ avitsi ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ asmái ǀ ariṣṭá-tātaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Herbs rich in Soma, rich in steeds, in nourishments, in strengthening power,— All these have I provided here, that this man may be whole again.
verses.wilson_translation: The Aśvāvatī, the Somāvatī, the Urjayantī, the Udojasā)-- all these plural nts I praise for thepurpose of overcoming this disease.
verses.griffith_verse: Herbs rich in Soma, rich in steeds, in nourishments, in strengthening power,— All these have I provided here, that this man may be whole again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उच्छुष्मा ओषधीनां गावो गोष्ठादिवेरते ।धनं सनिष्यंतीनामात्मानं तव पूरुष ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǀ óṣadhīnām ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ gosthā́t-iva ǀ īrate ǀdhánam ǀ saniṣyántīnām ǀ ātmā́nam ǀ táva ǀ puruṣa ǁ
verses.english_translation: The healing virtues of the Plants stream forth like cattle from the stall,— Plants that shall win me store of wealth, and save thy vital breath, O man.
verses.wilson_translation: The virtues of the plural nts which are desirous of bestowing wealth issue from them, man, (towards) yourbody like cattle from the pen.
verses.griffith_verse: The healing virtues of the Plants stream forth like cattle from the stall,— Plants that shall win me store of wealth, and save thy vital breath, O man.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इष्कृतिर्नाम वो माताथो यूयं स्थ निष्कृतीः ।सीराः पतत्रिणीः स्थन यदामयति निष्कृथ ॥
verses.transliteration: íṣkṛtiḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ vaḥ ǀ mātā́ ǀ átho íti ǀ yūyám ǀ stha ǀ níḥ-kṛtīḥ ǀsīrā́ḥ ǀ patatríṇīḥ ǀ sthana ǀ yát ǀ āmáyati ǀ níḥ ǀ kṛtha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Reliever is your mother's name, and hence Restorers are ye called. Rivers are ye with wings that fly: keep far whatever brings disease.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily Iṣkṛti is your mother, therefore are you (also)Niṣkṛtis; you are flying streams; if (a man) is illyou cure him.
verses.griffith_verse: Reliever is your mother's name, and hence Restorers are ye called. Rivers are ye with wings that fly: keep far whatever brings disease.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अति विश्वाः परिष्ठाः स्तेन इव व्रजमक्रमुः ।ओषधीः प्राचुच्यवुर्यत्किं च तन्वो रपः ॥
verses.transliteration: áti ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ pari-sthā́ḥ ǀ stenáḥ-iva ǀ vrajám ǀ akramuḥ ǀóṣadhīḥ ǀ prá ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀ yát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ tanváḥ ǀ rápaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Over all fences have they passed, as steals a thief into the fold. The Plants have driven from the frame whatever malady was there.
verses.wilson_translation: The universal all-pervading plural nts assail (diseases) as a thief (attacks) a cow-shed; they drive outwhatever infirmity of body there may be.
verses.griffith_verse: Over all fences have they passed, as steals a thief into the fold. The Plants have driven from the frame whatever malady was there.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिमा वाजयन्नहमोषधीर्हस्त आदधे ।आत्मा यक्ष्मस्य नश्यति पुरा जीवगृभो यथा ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ vājáyan ǀ ahám ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ háste ǀ ā-dadhé ǀātmā́ ǀ yákṣmasya ǀ naśyati ǀ purā́ ǀ jīva-gṛ́bhaḥ ǀ yathā ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, bringing back the vanished strength, I hold these herbs within my hand, The spirit of disease departs ere he can seize upon the life.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as I take these plural nts in myhandmaking (the sick man) strong, thesoulof the maladyperishes before (their application) as (life is driven away from the presence) of the seizer of life.
verses.griffith_verse: When, bringing back the vanished strength, I hold these herbs within my hand, The spirit of disease departs ere he can seize upon the life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्यौषधीः प्रसर्पथांगमंगं परुष्परुः ।ततो यक्ष्मं वि बाधध्व उग्रो मध्यमशीरिव ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ oṣadhīḥ ǀ pra-sárpatha ǀ áṅgam-aṅgam ǀ páruḥ-paruḥ ǀtátaḥ ǀ yákṣmam ǀ ví ǀ bādhadhve ǀ ugráḥ ǀ madhyamaśī́ḥ-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: He through whose frame, O Plants, ye creep member by member, joint by joint,— From him ye drive away disease like some strong arbiter of strife.
verses.wilson_translation: From him, oḥ plural nts, in whom you creep from limb to limb, from joint to joint, you drive away diseaselike a mighty (prince) stationed in the midst of his host.
verses.griffith_verse: He through whose frame, O Plants, ye creep member by member, joint by joint,— From him ye drive away disease like some strong arbiter of strife.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: साकं यक्ष्म प्र पत चाषेण किकिदीविना ।साकं वातस्य ध्राज्या साकं नश्य निहाकया ॥
verses.transliteration: sākám ǀ yakṣma ǀ prá ǀ pata ǀ cā́ṣeṇa ǀ kikidīvínā ǀsākám ǀ vā́tasya ǀ dhrā́jyā ǀ sākám ǀ naśya ǀ ni-hā́kayā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fly, Spirit of Disease, begone, with the blue jay and kingfisher. Fly with the wind's impetuousspeed, vanish together with the storm.
verses.wilson_translation: Fly forth, sickness, with the jay, with the blue jay, with the velocity of the wind, perish along with theiguana.
verses.griffith_verse: Fly, Spirit of Disease, begone, with the blue jay and kingfisher. Fly with the wind's impetuousspeed, vanish together with the storm.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अन्या वो अन्यामवत्वन्यान्यस्या उपावत ।ताः सर्वाः संविदाना इदं मे प्रावता वचः ॥
verses.transliteration: anyā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ anyā́m ǀ avatu ǀ anyā́ ǀ anyásyāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ avata ǀtā́ḥ ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ sam-vidānā́ḥ ǀ idám ǀ me ǀ prá ǀ avata ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Help every one the other, lend assistance each of you to each, All of you be accordant, give furtherance to this speech of mine.
verses.wilson_translation: Let each of you, plural nts, go to the other, approach the one (to the vicinity) of the other; thus being allmutually joined together, attend to this my speech.
verses.griffith_verse: Help every one the other, lend assistance each of you to each, All of you be accordant, give furtherance to this speech of mine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याः फलिनीर्या अफला अपुष्पा याश्च पुष्पिणीः ।बृहस्पतिप्रसूतास्ता नो मुंचंत्वंहसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ phalínīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ aphalā́ḥ ǀ apuṣpā́ḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ puṣpíṇīḥ ǀbṛ́haspáti-prasūtāḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ muñcantu ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let fruitful Plants, and fruitless, those that blossom, and the blossomless, Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, release us from our pain and grief;
verses.wilson_translation: Whether bearing fruit or barren, whether flowering or flowerless, may they, the progeny of Bṛhaspati,liberate us from sin.
verses.griffith_verse: Let fruitful Plants, and fruitless, those that blossom, and the blossomless, Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, release us from our pain and grief;
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मुंचंतु मा शपथ्यादथो वरुण्यादुत ।अथो यमस्य पड्बीशात्सर्वस्माद्देवकिल्बिषात् ॥
verses.transliteration: muñcántu ǀ mā ǀ śapathyā́t ǀ átho íti ǀ varuṇyā́t ǀ utá ǀátho íti ǀ yamásya ǀ páḍbīśāt ǀ sárvasmāt ǀ deva-kilbiṣā́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: Release me from the curse's plague and woe that comes from Varuṇa; Free me from Yama's fetter, from sin and offence against the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: May they liberate me from the sin produced by curse, from the sin caused by Varuṇa, from the fetters OYama, from all guilt caused by the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Release me from the curse's plague and woe that comes from Varuṇa; Free me from Yama's fetter, from sin and offence against the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवपतंतीरवदंदिव ओषधयस्परि ।यं जीवमश्नवामहै न स रिष्याति पूरुषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ava-pátantīḥ ǀ avadan ǀ diváḥ ǀ óṣadhayaḥ ǀ pári ǀyám ǀ jīvám ǀ aśnávāmahai ǀ ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ riṣyāti ǀ púruṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time, descending from the sky, the Plants flew earthward, thus they spake: No evil shall befall the man whom while he liveth we pervade,
verses.wilson_translation: The plural nts, falling from heaven, said, "The man, whom living we pervade, will not perish".
verses.griffith_verse: What time, descending from the sky, the Plants flew earthward, thus they spake: No evil shall befall the man whom while he liveth we pervade,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या ओषधीः सोमराज्ञीर्बह्वीः शतविचक्षणाः ।तासां त्वमस्युत्तमारं कामाय शं हृदे ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sóma-rājñīḥ ǀ bahvī́ḥ ǀ śatá-vicakṣaṇāḥ ǀtā́sām ǀ tvám ǀ asi ǀ ut-tamā́ ǀ áram ǀ kā́māya ǀ śám ǀ hṛdé ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of all the many Plants whose King is, Soma, Plants of hundred forms, Thou art the Plant most excellent, prompt to the wish, sweet to the heart.
verses.wilson_translation: The which have the Somafor their king, and are numerous and all- seeking of them you (O Soma) arethe best; be very bountiful to the affectionate heart.
verses.griffith_verse: Of all the many Plants whose King is, Soma, Plants of hundred forms, Thou art the Plant most excellent, prompt to the wish, sweet to the heart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या ओषधीः सोमराज्ञीर्विष्ठिताः पृथिवीमनु ।बृहस्पतिप्रसूता अस्यै सं दत्त वीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sóma-rājñīḥ ǀ ví-sthitāḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ ánu ǀbṛ́haspáti-prasūtāḥ ǀ asyái ǀ sám ǀ datta ǀ vīryám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O all ye various Herbs whose King is Soma, that o’erspread the earth, Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, combine your virtue in this Plant.
verses.wilson_translation: plural nts, which have the Somafor your king, who are scattered over the earth, the offspring of Bṛhaspati, give vigour to this (infirm body).
verses.griffith_verse: O all ye various Herbs whose King is Soma, that o’erspread the earth, Urged onward by Bṛhaspati, combine your virtue in this Plant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा वो रिषत्खनिता यस्मै चाहं खनामि वः ।द्विपच्चतुष्पदस्माकं सर्वमस्त्वनातुरं ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ riṣat ǀ khanitā́ ǀ yásmai ǀ ca ǀ ahám ǀ khánāmi ǀ vaḥ ǀdvi-pát ǀ cátuḥ-pat ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sárvam ǀ astu ǀ anāturám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Unharmed be he who digs you up, unharmed the man for whom I dig: And let no malady attack biped or quadruped of ours.
verses.wilson_translation: Let not the digger hurt you, not (the sick person n) for whom I dig you up; may all my bipeds andquadrupeds be free from disease.
verses.griffith_verse: Unharmed be he who digs you up, unharmed the man for whom I dig: And let no malady attack biped or quadruped of ours.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याश्चेदमुपशृण्वंति याश्च दूरं परागताः ।सर्वाः संगत्य वीरुधोऽस्यै सं दत्त वीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ idám ǀ upa-śṛṇvánti ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ dūrám ǀ párā-gatāḥ ǀsárvāḥ ǀ sam-gátya ǀ vīrudhaḥ ǀ asyái ǀ sám ǀ datta ǀ vīryám ǁ
verses.english_translation: All Plants that hear this speech, and those that have departed far away, Come all assembled and confer your healing power upon this Herb.
verses.wilson_translation: Both the plural nts that I hear this (prayer), and those which are removed far off, all coming together,give vigour to this (infirm body).
verses.griffith_verse: All Plants that hear this speech, and those that have departed far away, Come all assembled and confer your healing power upon this Herb.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओषधयः सं वदंते सोमेन सह राज्ञा ।यस्मै कृणोति ब्राह्मणस्तं राजन्पारयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: óṣadhayaḥ ǀ sám ǀ vadante ǀ sómena ǀ sahá ǀ rā́jñā ǀyásmai ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ brāhmaṇáḥ ǀ tám ǀ rājan ǀ pārayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say: O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes.
verses.wilson_translation: All the plural nts, together with Somatheir king, declare, "We save him, O king, to whom the Brāhmaṇaadministers (us)".
verses.griffith_verse: With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say: O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वमुत्तमास्योषधे तव वृक्षा उपस्तयः ।उपस्तिरस्तु सोऽस्माकं यो अस्माँ अभिदासति ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ ut-tamā́ ǀ asi ǀ oṣadhe ǀ táva ǀ vṛkṣā́ḥ ǀ úpastayaḥ ǀúpastiḥ ǀ astu ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ abhi-dā́sati ǁ
verses.english_translation: Most excellent of all art thou, O Plant thy vassals are the trees. Let him be subject to our power, the man who seeks to injure us.
verses.wilson_translation: You (Soma) are the best of the plural nts, to you (all) trees are prostrate; may he be prostrate to us, whoattacks us.
verses.griffith_verse: Most excellent of all art thou, O Plant thy vassals are the trees. Let him be subject to our power, the man who seeks to injure us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCVIII. The Gods.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COME, be thou Mitra, Varuṇa, or Pūṣan, come, O Bṛhaspati, to mine oblation:With Maruts, Vasus, or Ādityas, make thou Parjanya pour for Santanu his rain-drops. The God, intelligent, the speedy envoy whom thou hast sent hath come to me, Devapi:Address thyself to me and turn thee hither within thy lips will I put brilliant language. Within my mouth, Bṛhaspati, deposit speech lucid, vigorous, and free from weakness,Thereby to win for Santanu the rain-fall. The meath-rich drop from heaven hath passed within it. Let the sweet drops descend on us, O Indra: give us enough to lade a thousand wagons.Sit to thy Hotar task; pay worship duly, and serve the Gods, Devapi, with oblation. Knowing the God's good-will, Devapi, Ṛṣi, the son of Rstisena, sate as Hotar.He hath brought down from heaven's most lofty summit the ocean of the rain, celestial waters. Gathered together in that highest ocean, the waters stood by deities obstructed.They burried down set free by Arstisena, in gaping clefts, urged onward by Devapi. When as chief priest for Santanu, Devapi, chosen for Hotar's duty, prayed beseeching,Graciously pleased Bṛhaspati vouchsafed him a voice that reached the Gods and won the waters. O Agni whom Devapi Arstisena, the mortal man, hath kindled in his glory,Joying in him with all the Gods together, urge on the sender of the rain, Parjanya. All ancient Ṛṣis with their songs approached thee, even thee, O Much-invoked, at sacrifices.We have provided wagon-loads in thousands: come to the solemn rite, Lord of Red Horses. The wagon-loads, the nine-and-ninety thousand, these have been offered up to thee, O Agni.Hero, with these increase thy many bodies, and, stimulated, send us rain from heaven. Give thou these ninety thousand loads, O Agni, to Indra, to the Bull, to be his portion.Knowing the paths which Deities duly travel, set mid the Gods in heaven Aulana also. O Agni, drive afar our foes, our troubles chase malady away and wicked demons.From this air-ocean, from the lofty heavens, send down on us a mighty flood of waters.

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते प्रति मे देवतामिहि मित्रो वा यद्वरुणो वासि पूषा ।आदित्यैर्वा यद्वसुभिर्मरुत्वान्त्स पर्जन्यं शंतनवे वृषाय ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ práti ǀ me ǀ devátām ǀ ihi ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ vā ǀ ási ǀ pūṣā́ ǀādityáiḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ sáḥ ǀ parjányam ǀ śám-tanave ǀ vṛṣaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: COME, be thou Mitra, Varuṇa, or Pūṣan, come, O Bṛhaspati, to mine oblation: With Maruts, Vasus, or Ādityas, make thou Parjanya pour for Santanu his rain-drops.
verses.wilson_translation: : Go,Bṛhaspati, on my behalf to the gods, whether you are Mitra, or Varuṇa, or Pūṣan, orassociated with theĀdityas, the Vasus, or the Maruts-- do you cause Parjanyato send down rain forŚantanu.
verses.griffith_verse: COME, be thou Mitra, Varuṇa, or Pūṣan, come, O Bṛhaspati, to mine oblation: With Maruts, Vasus, or Ādityas, make thou Parjanya pour for Santanu his rain-drops.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ देवो दूतो अजिरश्चिकित्वांत्वद्देवापे अभि मामगच्छत् ।प्रतीचीनः प्रति मामा ववृत्स्व दधामि ते द्युमतीं वाचमासन् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ajiráḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ tvát ǀ deva-āpe ǀ abhí ǀ mā́m ǀ agacchat ǀpratīcīnáḥ ǀ práti ǀ mā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtsva ǀ dádhāmi ǀ te ǀ dyu-mátīm ǀ vā́cam ǀ āsán ǁ
verses.english_translation: The God, intelligent, the speedy envoy whom thou hast sent hath come to me, Devapi: Address thyself to me and turn thee hither within thy lips will I put brilliant language.
verses.wilson_translation: Let a divine messenger quick and intelligent sent,Devāpi, by you come to me. Come,Bṛhaspati, tome, turning towards me; I have in my mouth a brilliant eulogium for you.
verses.griffith_verse: The God, intelligent, the speedy envoy whom thou hast sent hath come to me, Devapi: Address thyself to me and turn thee hither within thy lips will I put brilliant language.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मे धेहि द्युमतीं वाचमासन्बृहस्पते अनमीवामिषिरां ।यया वृष्टिं शंतनवे वनाव दिवो द्रप्सो मधुमाँ आ विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ dhehi ǀ dyu-mátīm ǀ vā́cam ǀ āsán ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ anamīvā́m ǀ iṣirā́m ǀyáyā ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ śám-tanave ǀ vánāva ǀ diváḥ ǀ drapsáḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Within my mouth, Bṛhaspati, deposit speech lucid, vigorous, and free from weakness, Thereby to win for Santanu the rain-fall. The meath-rich drop from heaven hath passed within it.
verses.wilson_translation: Put,Bṛhaspati, in my mouth a brilliant eulogium, prompt and free from defect, by which we two mayobtain rain from heaven forŚantanu, the sweet drop (sent by you) has entered (our voice).
verses.griffith_verse: Within my mouth, Bṛhaspati, deposit speech lucid, vigorous, and free from weakness, Thereby to win for Santanu the rain-fall. The meath-rich drop from heaven hath passed within it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो द्रप्सा मधुमंतो विशंत्विंद्र देह्यधिरथं सहस्रं ।नि षीद होत्रमृतुथा यजस्व देवांदेवापे हविषा सपर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ drapsā́ḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ viśantu ǀ índra ǀ dehí ǀ ádhi-ratham ǀ sahásram ǀní ǀ sīda ǀ hotrám ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ yajasva ǀ devā́n ǀ deva-āpe ǀ havíṣā ǀ saparya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the sweet drops descend on us, O Indra: give us enough to lade a thousand wagons. Sit to thy Hotar task; pay worship duly, and serve the Gods, Devapi, with oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: May the sweet drops of rain fall upon us; grant us,Indra, a thousand chariot-loads. Sit down,Devāpi,to your duties as Hotā; in due season sacrifice to the gods, worship them with oblations. functions as Hotā. He has brought down from the upper to the lower ocean the rain waters of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the sweet drops descend on us, O Indra: give us enough to lade a thousand wagons. Sit to thy Hotar task; pay worship duly, and serve the Gods, Devapi, with oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आर्ष्टिषेणो होत्रमृषिर्निषीदंदेवापिर्देवसुमतिं चिकित्वान् ।स उत्तरस्मादधरं समुद्रमपो दिव्या असृजद्वर्ष्या अभि ॥
verses.transliteration: ārṣṭiṣeṇáḥ ǀ hotrám ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ ni-sī́dan ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ deva-sumatím ǀ cikitvā́n ǀsáḥ ǀ út-tarasmāt ǀ ádharam ǀ samudrám ǀ apáḥ ǀ divyā́ḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ varṣyā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing the God's good-will, Devapi, Ṛṣi, the son of Rstisena, sate as Hotar. He hath brought down from heaven's most lofty summit the ocean of the rain, celestial waters.
verses.griffith_verse: Knowing the God's good-will, Devapi, Ṛṣi, the son of Rstisena, sate as Hotar. He hath brought down from heaven's most lofty summit the ocean of the rain, celestial waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मिन्त्समुद्रे अध्युत्तरस्मिन्नापो देवेभिर्निवृता अतिष्ठन् ।ता अद्रवन्नार्ष्टिषेणेन सृष्टा देवापिना प्रेषिता मृक्षिणीषु ॥
verses.transliteration: asmín ǀ samudré ǀ ádhi ǀ út-tarasmin ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ ní-vṛtāḥ ǀ atiṣṭhan ǀtā́ḥ ǀ adravan ǀ ārṣṭiṣeṇéna ǀ sṛṣṭā́ḥ ǀ devá-āpinā ǀ prá-iṣitāḥ ǀ mṛkṣíṇīṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Gathered together in that highest ocean, the waters stood by deities obstructed. They burried down set free by Arstisena, in gaping clefts, urged onward by Devapi.
verses.wilson_translation: In this upper ocean the waters stood dammed up by the gods; set free by Devāpi, the son ofṚṣṭiṣeṇa, they were sent forth over the plural ins.
verses.griffith_verse: Gathered together in that highest ocean, the waters stood by deities obstructed. They burried down set free by Arstisena, in gaping clefts, urged onward by Devapi.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यद्देवापिः शंतनवे पुरोहितो होत्राय वृतः कृपयन्नदीधेत् ।देवश्रुतं वृष्टिवनिं रराणो बृहस्पतिर्वाचमस्मा अयच्छत् ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ śám-tanave ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǀ hotrā́ya ǀ vṛtáḥ ǀ kṛpáyan ǀ ádīdhet ǀdeva-śrútam ǀ vṛṣṭi-vánim ǀ rárāṇaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ asmai ǀ ayacchat ǁ
verses.english_translation: When as chief priest for Santanu, Devapi, chosen for Hotar's duty, prayed beseeching, Graciously pleased Bṛhaspati vouchsafed him a voice that reached the Gods and won the waters.
verses.wilson_translation: When Devāpi, the PurohitaforŚantanu, engaged in his functions of Hotā, compassionating (him),slicited Bṛhaspati, to whom the gods listen, who begs for rain, (Bṛhaspati) being plural ased gave him a voice.
verses.griffith_verse: When as chief priest for Santanu, Devapi, chosen for Hotar's duty, prayed beseeching, Graciously pleased Bṛhaspati vouchsafed him a voice that reached the Gods and won the waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं त्वा देवापिः शुशुचानो अग्न आर्ष्टिषेणो मनुष्यः समीधे ।विश्वेभिर्देवैरनुमद्यमानः प्र पर्जन्यमीरया वृष्टिमंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ śuśucānáḥ ǀ agne ǀ ārṣṭiṣeṇáḥ ǀ manuṣyáḥ ǀ sam-īdhé ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ anu-madyámānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ parjányam ǀ īraya ǀ vṛṣṭi-mántam ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni whom Devapi Arstisena, the mortal man, hath kindled in his glory, Joying in him with all the Gods together, urge on the sender of the rain, Parjanya.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, whom the mortal Devāpi, the son of Ṛṣṭiseṇa, lighting you, has kindled, do you, beingpropitiated with all the gods, send down the rain- laden cloud.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni whom Devapi Arstisena, the mortal man, hath kindled in his glory, Joying in him with all the Gods together, urge on the sender of the rain, Parjanya.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वां पूर्व ऋषयो गीर्भिरायंत्वामध्वरेषु पुरुहूत विश्वे ।सहस्राण्यधिरथान्यस्मे आ नो यज्ञं रोहिदश्वोप याहि ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ āyan ǀ tvā́m ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ puru-hūta ǀ víśve ǀsahásrāṇi ǀ ádhi-rathāni ǀ asmé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ rohit-aśva ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: All ancient Ṛṣis with their songs approached thee, even thee, O Much-invoked, at sacrifices. We have provided wagon-loads in thousands: come to the solemn rite, Lord of Red Horses.
verses.wilson_translation: You have ancient sages approached, with hymns; you, O invoked of many, all worshippers (address)at sacrifice; (give) us thousands of chariot-loads, come to our sacrifice, lord of red horses.
verses.griffith_verse: All ancient Ṛṣis with their songs approached thee, even thee, O Much-invoked, at sacrifices. We have provided wagon-loads in thousands: come to the solemn rite, Lord of Red Horses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतान्यग्ने नवतिर्नव त्वे आहुतान्यधिरथा सहस्रा ।तेभिर्वर्धस्व तन्वः शूर पूर्वीर्दिवो नो वृष्टिमिषितो रिरीहि ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ agne ǀ navatíḥ ǀ náva ǀ tvé íti ǀ ā́-hutāni ǀ ádhi-rathā ǀ sahásrā ǀtébhiḥ ǀ vardhasva ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śūra ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ rirīhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The wagon-loads, the nine-and-ninety thousand, these have been offered up to thee, O Agni. Hero, with these increase thy many bodies, and, stimulated, send us rain from heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: These ninety-and-nine thousands of chariot-lords have been offered,Agni, to you; with them, O hero,nourish your many bodies; and thus solicited sends us rain from heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: The wagon-loads, the nine-and-ninety thousand, these have been offered up to thee, O Agni. Hero, with these increase thy many bodies, and, stimulated, send us rain from heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एतान्यग्ने नवतिं सहस्रा सं प्र यच्छ वृष्ण इंद्राय भागं ।विद्वान्पथ ऋतुशो देवयानानप्यौलानं दिवि देवेषु धेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ agne ǀ navatím ǀ sahásrā ǀ sám ǀ prá ǀ yaccha ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ índrāya ǀ bhāgám ǀvidvā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ ṛtu-śáḥ ǀ deva-yā́nān ǀ ápi ǀ aulānám ǀ diví ǀ devéṣu ǀ dhehi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give thou these ninety thousand loads, O Agni, to Indra, to the Bull, to be his portion. Knowing the paths which Deities duly travel, set mid the Gods in heaven Aulana also.
verses.wilson_translation: Give,Agni, these ninety thousands to the showerer,Indra, as his share; knowing the paths traversedby the gods in due season plural ce the Aulāna (Śantanu), in heaven among the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Give thou these ninety thousand loads, O Agni, to Indra, to the Bull, to be his portion. Knowing the paths which Deities duly travel, set mid the Gods in heaven Aulana also.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने बाधस्व वि मृधो वि दुर्गहापामीवामप रक्षांसि सेध ।अस्मात्समुद्राद्बृहतो दिवो नोऽपां भूमानमुप नः सृजेह ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ bā́dhasva ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǀ ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ ápa ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ sedha ǀasmā́t ǀ samudrā́t ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ bhūmā́nam ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ sṛja ǀ ihá ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, drive afar our foes, our troubles chase malady away and wicked demons. From this air-ocean, from the lofty heavens, send down on us a mighty flood of waters.
verses.wilson_translation: Demolish,Agni, our enemies, demolish their strongholds, drive away disease, drive away therākṣasas from this ocean, from vast heaven send own upon us here abundance of rain.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, drive afar our foes, our troubles chase malady away and wicked demons. From this air-ocean, from the lofty heavens, send down on us a mighty flood of waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN XCIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT Splendid One, Loud-voiced, Farstriding, dost thou, well knowing, urge us to exalt with praises?What give we him? When his might dawned, he fashioned the Vṛtra-slaying bolt, and sent us waters. He goes to end his work with lightning flashes: wide is the seat his Asura glory gives him.With his Companions, not without his Brother, he quells Saptatha's magic devices. On most auspicious path he goes to battle he toiled to win heaven's light, full fain to gain it;He seized the hundred-gated castle's treasure by craft, unchecked, and slew the lustful demons. Fighting for kine, the prize of war, and I roaming among the berd be brings the young streams hither,Where, footless, joined, without a car to bear them, with jars for steeds, they pour their flood like butter. Bold, unsolicited for wealth, with Rudras he came, the Blameless, having left his dwelling,Came, seized the food of Vamra and his consort, and left the couple weeping and unsheltered. Lord of the dwelling, he subdued the demon who roared aloud, six-eyed and triple-headed.Tṛta, made stronger by the might he lent him, struck down the boar with shaft whose point was iron.
