He raised himself on high and shot his arrow against the guileful and oppressive foeman.Strong, glorious, manliest, for us he shattered the forts of Nabus when he slew the Dasyus. He, like a cloud that rains upon the pasture, hath found for us the way to dwell in safety.When the Hawk comes in body to the Soma, armed with his iron claws he slays the Dasyus. He with his potent Friends gave up the mighty, gave gusnia up to Kutsa for affliction.He led the lauded Kavi, he delivered Atka as prey to him and to his heroes. He, with his Gods who love mankind, the Wondrous, giving like Varuṇa who works with magic,Was known, yet young as guardian of the seasons; and he quelled Araru, four-footed dernon. Through lauds of him hath Auśija Ṛjiśvan burst, with the Mighty's aid, the stall of Pipru.When the saint pressed the juice and shone as singer, he seized the forts and with his craft subdued them. So, swiftly Asura, for exaltation, hath the great Vamraka come nigh to Indra.He will, when supplicated, bring him blessing: he hath brought all, food, strength, a happy dwelling.

verses.sanskrit: कं नश्चित्रमिषण्यसि चिकित्वान्पृथुग्मानं वाश्रं वावृधध्यै ।कत्तस्य दातु शवसो व्युष्टौ तक्षद्वज्रं वृत्रतुरमपिन्वत् ॥
verses.transliteration: kám ǀ naḥ ǀ citrám ǀ iṣaṇyasi ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ pṛthu-gmā́nam ǀ vāśrám ǀ vavṛdhádhyai ǀkát ǀ tásya ǀ dā́tu ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ tákṣat ǀ vájram ǀ vṛtra-túram ǀ ápinvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT Splendid One, Loud-voiced, Farstriding, dost thou, well knowing, urge us to exalt with praises? What give we him? When his might dawned, he fashioned the Vṛtra-slaying bolt, and sent us waters.
verses.wilson_translation: What marvellous (wealth), comprehensive and laudable, do you,Indra, knowing (what is needed),bestow upon us for our advantage? What gift (has been made to us) upon the development of his strength? Hefabricated the Vṛtra- slaying thunderbolt, and let the waters flow.
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT Splendid One, Loud-voiced, Farstriding, dost thou, well knowing, urge us to exalt with praises? What give we him? When his might dawned, he fashioned the Vṛtra-slaying bolt, and sent us waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स हि द्युता विद्युता वेति साम पृथुं योनिमसुरत्वा ससाद ।स सनीळेभिः प्रसहानो अस्य भ्रातुर्न ऋते सप्तथस्य मायाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ dyutā́ ǀ vi-dyútā ǀ véti ǀ sā́ma ǀ pṛthúm ǀ yónim ǀ asura-tvā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ sasāda ǀsáḥ ǀ sá-nīḷebhiḥ ǀ pra-sahānáḥ ǀ asya ǀ bhrā́tuḥ ǀ ná ǀ ṛté ǀ saptáthasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He goes to end his work with lightning flashes: wide is the seat his Asura glory gives him. With his Companions, not without his Brother, he quells Saptatha's magic devices.
verses.wilson_translation: Armed with the bright lightning he goes to the (scene of) adoration; endowed with might he has seatedhimself on the spacious plural ce (of sacrifice); he (is) triumphant with his companions (the Maruts); the wiles of hisseventh brother do not (prevail) at the rite.
verses.griffith_verse: He goes to end his work with lightning flashes: wide is the seat his Asura glory gives him. With his Companions, not without his Brother, he quells Saptatha's magic devices.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स वाजं यातापदुष्पदा यन्त्स्वर्षाता परि षदत्सनिष्यन् ।अनर्वा यच्छतदुरस्य वेदो घ्नंछिश्नदेवाँ अभि वर्पसा भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ yā́tā ǀ ápaduḥ-padā ǀ yán ǀ sváḥ-sātā ǀ pári ǀ sadat ǀ saniṣyán ǀanarvā́ ǀ yát ǀ śatá-durasya ǀ védaḥ ǀ ghnán ǀ śiśná-devān ǀ abhí ǀ várpasā ǀ bhū́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: On most auspicious path he goes to battle he toiled to win heaven's light, full fain to gain it; He seized the hundred-gated castle's treasure by craft, unchecked, and slew the lustful demons.
verses.wilson_translation: Going to the battle, marching with easy gait, desiring the spoil, he set himself to the acquisition of all(wealth). Invincible, destroying the phallus-worshippers, he won by his prowess whatever wealth (was concealedin the city) with the hundred gates.
verses.griffith_verse: On most auspicious path he goes to battle he toiled to win heaven's light, full fain to gain it; He seized the hundred-gated castle's treasure by craft, unchecked, and slew the lustful demons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स यह्व्योऽवनीर्गोष्वर्वा जुहोति प्रधन्यासु सस्रिः ।अपादो यत्र युज्यासोऽरथा द्रोण्यश्वास ईरते घृतं वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ yahvyáḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ árvā ǀ ā́ ǀ juhoti ǀ pra-dhanyā́su ǀ sásriḥ ǀapā́daḥ ǀ yátra ǀ yújyāsaḥ ǀ arathā́ḥ ǀ droṇí-aśvāsaḥ ǀ ī́rate ǀ ghṛtám ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fighting for kine, the prize of war, and I roaming among the berd be brings the young streams hither, Where, footless, joined, without a car to bear them, with jars for steeds, they pour their flood like butter.
verses.wilson_translation: The victorious Indra, coming among the clouds, quickly moving, offers the abundant waters on the rich(plural ins) where his associates (the rivers) footless, and without conveyances, having pitchers for horses, pour outwater like ghī.
verses.griffith_verse: Fighting for kine, the prize of war, and I roaming among the berd be brings the young streams hither, Where, footless, joined, without a car to bear them, with jars for steeds, they pour their flood like butter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स रुद्रेभिरशस्तवार ऋभ्वा हित्वी गयमारेअवद्य आगात् ।वम्रस्य मन्ये मिथुना विवव्री अन्नमभीत्यारोदयन्मुषायन् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ áśasta-vāraḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀ hitvī́ ǀ gáyam ǀ āré-avadyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀvamrásya ǀ manye ǀ mithunā́ ǀ vívavrī íti ví-vavrī ǀ ánnam ǀ abhi-ítya ǀ arodayat ǀ muṣāyán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bold, unsolicited for wealth, with Rudras he came, the Blameless, having left his dwelling, Came, seized the food of Vamra and his consort, and left the couple weeping and unsheltered.
verses.wilson_translation: May he, our unsolicited benefactor, the mighty one, from whom blame is far removed, come with the Rudras, having quit his dwelling. I think of the two (parents) of Vamra, who are free from fever. Having obtained(the enemy's) food, he called aloud while stealing it.
verses.griffith_verse: Bold, unsolicited for wealth, with Rudras he came, the Blameless, having left his dwelling, Came, seized the food of Vamra and his consort, and left the couple weeping and unsheltered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इद्दासं तुवीरवं पतिर्दन्षळक्षं त्रिशीर्षाणं दमन्यत् ।अस्य त्रितो न्वोजसा वृधानो विपा वराहमयोअग्रया हन् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ dā́sam ǀ tuvi-rávam ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ ṣaṭ-akṣám ǀ tri-śīrṣā́ṇam ǀ damanyat ǀasyá ǀ tritáḥ ǀ nú ǀ ójasā ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ vipā́ ǀ varāhám ǀ áyaḥ-agrayā ǀ hanníti han ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the dwelling, he subdued the demon who roared aloud, six-eyed and triple-headed. Tṛta, made stronger by the might he lent him, struck down the boar with shaft whose point was iron.
verses.wilson_translation: The sovereign Indraattacking him overcame the loud-shouting, six- eyed, three-headed Dāsa, and Trita, invigorated by his strength, smote the water-laden (cloud) with his iron-tipped finger.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of the dwelling, he subdued the demon who roared aloud, six-eyed and triple-headed. Tṛta, made stronger by the might he lent him, struck down the boar with shaft whose point was iron.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स द्रुह्वणे मनुष ऊर्ध्वसान आ साविषदर्शसानाय शरुं ।स नृतमो नहुषोऽस्मत्सुजातः पुरोऽभिनदर्हंदस्युहत्ये ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ drúhvaṇe ǀ mánuṣe ǀ ūrdhvasānáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ arśasānā́ya ǀ śárum ǀsáḥ ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ asmát ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ abhinat ǀ árhan ǀ dasyu-hátye ǁ
verses.english_translation: He raised himself on high and shot his arrow against the guileful and oppressive foeman. Strong, glorious, manliest, for us he shattered the forts of Nabus when he slew the Dasyus.
verses.griffith_verse: He raised himself on high and shot his arrow against the guileful and oppressive foeman. Strong, glorious, manliest, for us he shattered the forts of Nabus when he slew the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सो अभ्रियो न यवस उदन्यन्क्षयाय गातुं विदन्नो अस्मे ।उप यत्सीददिंदुं शरीरैः श्येनोऽयोपाष्टिर्हंति दस्यून् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ abhríyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yávase ǀ udanyán ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ gātúm ǀ vidát ǀ naḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀúpa ǀ yát ǀ sī́dat ǀ índum ǀ śárīraiḥ ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ áyaḥ-apāṣṭiḥ ǀ hanti ǀ dásyūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, like a cloud that rains upon the pasture, hath found for us the way to dwell in safety. When the Hawk comes in body to the Soma, armed with his iron claws he slays the Dasyus.
verses.wilson_translation: Like the aggregated cloud desiring to pour water on the pasturage, he found the way to our dwellingwhen he approached the Somawith his limbs, like a hawk with heel of metal he smites the Dasyus.
verses.griffith_verse: He, like a cloud that rains upon the pasture, hath found for us the way to dwell in safety. When the Hawk comes in body to the Soma, armed with his iron claws he slays the Dasyus.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स व्राधतः शवसानेभिरस्य कुत्साय शुष्णं कृपणे परादात् ।अयं कविमनयच्छस्यमानमत्कं यो अस्य सनितोत नृणां ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ śavasānébhiḥ ǀ asya ǀ kútsāya ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ kṛpáṇe ǀ párā ǀ adāt ǀayám ǀ kavím ǀ anayat ǀ śasyámānam ǀ átkam ǀ yáḥ ǀ asya ǀ sánitā ǀ utá ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with his potent Friends gave up the mighty, gave gusnia up to Kutsa for affliction. He led the lauded Kavi, he delivered Atka as prey to him and to his heroes.
verses.wilson_translation: Let him overthrow the mighty with powerful (weapons); he destroyedŚuṣṇafor the sake of the liberal Kutsa; he humiliated Kavi, who praised him, who was the giver of form to Indraand his men.
verses.griffith_verse: He with his potent Friends gave up the mighty, gave gusnia up to Kutsa for affliction. He led the lauded Kavi, he delivered Atka as prey to him and to his heroes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं दशस्यन्नर्येभिरस्य दस्मो देवेभिर्वरुणो न मायी ।अयं कनीन ऋतुपा अवेद्यमिमीताररुं यश्चतुष्पात् ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ daśasyán ǀ náryebhiḥ ǀ asya ǀ dasmáḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ māyī́ ǀayám ǀ kanī́naḥ ǀ ṛtu-pā́ḥ ǀ avedi ǀ ámimīta ǀ arárum ǀ yáḥ ǀ cátuḥ-pāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, with his Gods who love mankind, the Wondrous, giving like Varuṇa who works with magic, Was known, yet young as guardian of the seasons; and he quelled Araru, four-footed dernon.
verses.wilson_translation: Bountiful (to his worshippers) with his (Maruts) friendly to men, wonderful with brilliancies, havingmagical power like Varuṇa, he was known as desirable, protecting the seasons, he destroyed,Araru, who wasfour-footed.
verses.griffith_verse: He, with his Gods who love mankind, the Wondrous, giving like Varuṇa who works with magic, Was known, yet young as guardian of the seasons; and he quelled Araru, four-footed dernon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य स्तोमेभिरौशिज ऋजिश्वा व्रजं दरयद्वृषभेण पिप्रोः ।सुत्वा यद्यजतो दीदयद्गीः पुर इयानो अभि वर्पसा भूत् ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ auśijáḥ ǀ ṛjíśvā ǀ vrajám ǀ darayat ǀ vṛṣabhéṇa ǀ píproḥ ǀsútvā ǀ yát ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dīdáyat ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ várpasā ǀ bhū́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through lauds of him hath Auśija Ṛjiśvan burst, with the Mighty's aid, the stall of Pipru. When the saint pressed the juice and shone as singer, he seized the forts and with his craft subdued them.
verses.wilson_translation: Ṛjiśvā, the son of Uśijawith Indra's praises shattered the cow pen of Pipru with the thunderbolt;when having expressed (the Soma), the venerable sage recited his praises, (Indra) proceeding against the cities(of the enemy) triumphed with his body.
verses.griffith_verse: Through lauds of him hath Auśija Ṛjiśvan burst, with the Mighty's aid, the stall of Pipru. When the saint pressed the juice and shone as singer, he seized the forts and with his craft subdued them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा महो असुर वक्षथाय वम्रकः पड्भिरुप सर्पदिंद्रं ।स इयानः करति स्वस्तिमस्मा इषमूर्जं सुक्षितिं विश्वमाभाः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ maháḥ ǀ asura ǀ vakṣáthāya ǀ vamrakáḥ ǀ paṭ-bhíḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sarpat ǀ índram ǀsáḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ karati ǀ svastím ǀ asmai ǀ íṣam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ su-kṣitím ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ abhārítyabhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So, swiftly Asura, for exaltation, hath the great Vamraka come nigh to Indra. He will, when supplicated, bring him blessing: he hath brought all, food, strength, a happy dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: In this manner, O mighty (Indra), Vamraka approached Indra on foot, to bring an ample oblation. Mayhe, being approached, grant us prosperity, may he bring us food, drink, a secure dwelling and all (good things).
verses.griffith_verse: So, swiftly Asura, for exaltation, hath the great Vamraka come nigh to Indra. He will, when supplicated, bring him blessing: he hath brought all, food, strength, a happy dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN C. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Be, like thyself, O Indra, strong for our delight: here lauded, aid us, Maghavan, drinker of the juice.Savitar with the Gods protect us: hear ye Twain. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Bring swift, for offering, the snare that suits the time, to the pure-drinker Vāyu, roaring as he goes,To him who hath approached the draught of shining milk. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. May Savitar the God send us full life, to each who sacrifices, lives aright and pours the juiceThat we with simple hearts may wait upon the Gods. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. May Indra evermore be gracious unto us, and may King Soma meditate our happiness,Even as men secure the comfort of a friend. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Indra hath given the body with its song and strength: Bṛhaspati, thou art the lengthener of life.The sacrifice is Manu, Providence, our Sire. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Indra possesseth might celestial nobly formed: the singer in the house is Agni, prudent Sage.He is the sacrifice in synod, fair, most near. We ask for freedom and complete felicity, Not often have we sinned against you secretly, nor, Vasus, have we openly provoked the Gods.Not one of its, ye Gods, hath worn an alien shape. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. May Savitar remove from us our malady, and may the Mountains keep it far away from whereThe press-stone as it sheds the meath rings loudly forth. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Ye Vasus, let the stone, the presser stand erect: avert all enmities and keep them far remote.Our guard to be adored is Savitar this God. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Eat strength and fatness in the pasture, kine, who are balmed at the reservoir and at the seat of Law.So let your body be our body's medicine. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. The singer fills the spirit: all mens, love hath he. Indra takes kindly care of those who pour the juice.For his libation is the heavenly udder full. We ask for freedom and complete felicity. Wondrous thy spirit-filling light, triumpliant; thy hosts save from decay and are resistless.The pious votary by straightest pathway speeds to possess the best of all the cattle.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र दृह्य मघवंत्वावदिद्भुज इह स्तुतः सुतपा बोधि नो वृधे ।देवेभिर्नः सविता प्रावतु श्रुतमा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ dṛ́hya ǀ magha-van ǀ tvā́-vat ǀ ít ǀ bhujé ǀ ihá ǀ stutáḥ ǀ suta-pā́ḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǀdevébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ prá ǀ avatu ǀ śrutám ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be, like thyself, O Indra, strong for our delight: here lauded, aid us, Maghavan, drinker of the juice. Savitar with the Gods protect us: hear ye Twain. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Consume, afluent Indra, (the foe that is) like you (in might); praised on this occasion, do you who arethe drinker of the libation be favourable to our advancement. May Savitā, with the gods, defend our sacrifice;we long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Be, like thyself, O Indra, strong for our delight: here lauded, aid us, Maghavan, drinker of the juice. Savitar with the Gods protect us: hear ye Twain. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भराय सु भरत भागमृत्वियं प्र वायवे शुचिपे क्रंददिष्टये ।गौरस्य यः पयसः पीतिमानश आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: bhárāya ǀ sú ǀ bharata ǀ bhāgám ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ prá ǀ vāyáve ǀ śuci-pé ǀ krandát-iṣṭaye ǀgaurásya ǀ yáḥ ǀ páyasaḥ ǀ pītím ǀ ānaśé ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring swift, for offering, the snare that suits the time, to the pure-drinker Vāyu, roaring as he goes, To him who hath approached the draught of shining milk. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer to (Indra) the cherisher (of all) the share suited to the season; (offer it) to Vāyu, the drinker ofthe pure (Soma), who clamours as he travels, who obtains a draught of white milk; we long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring swift, for offering, the snare that suits the time, to the pure-drinker Vāyu, roaring as he goes, To him who hath approached the draught of shining milk. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो देवः सविता साविषद्वय ऋजूयते यजमानाय सुन्वते ।यथा देवान्प्रतिभूषेम पाकवदा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ṛju-yaté ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǀyáthā ǀ devā́n ǀ prati-bhū́ṣema ǀ pāka-vát ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Savitar the God send us full life, to each who sacrifices, lives aright and pours the juice That we with simple hearts may wait upon the Gods. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitāgenitive rate well-dressed food for our sincereyajamānaas he offers the libation,so that we may be in good favour with the gods; we long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: May Savitar the God send us full life, to each who sacrifices, lives aright and pours the juice That we with simple hearts may wait upon the Gods. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो अस्मे सुमना अस्तु विश्वहा राजा सोमः सुवितस्याध्येतु नः ।यथायथा मित्रधितानि संदधुरा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ astu ǀ viśváhā ǀ rā́jā ǀ sómaḥ ǀ suvitásya ǀ ádhi ǀ etu ǀ naḥ ǀyáthā-yathā ǀ mitrá-dhitāni ǀ sam-dadhúḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra evermore be gracious unto us, and may King Soma meditate our happiness, Even as men secure the comfort of a friend. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrabe favourably disposed towards us every day, may the royal Somaaccept our praise, sothat they may bestow upon us friendly treasures; we long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: May Indra evermore be gracious unto us, and may King Soma meditate our happiness, Even as men secure the comfort of a friend. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र उक्थेन शवसा परुर्दधे बृहस्पते प्रतरीतास्यायुषः ।यज्ञो मनुः प्रमतिर्नः पिता हि कमा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ukthéna ǀ śávasā ǀ páruḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ pra-tarītā́ ǀ asi ǀ ā́yuṣaḥ ǀyajñáḥ ǀ mánuḥ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra hath given the body with its song and strength: Bṛhaspati, thou art the lengthener of life. The sacrifice is Manu, Providence, our Sire. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: By his laudable strength Indrasupports my limb; you,Bṛhaspati, are the prolonger of my life. May thesacrifice, the sage Manu, (being) our protector, (grant) us happiness. We long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra hath given the body with its song and strength: Bṛhaspati, thou art the lengthener of life. The sacrifice is Manu, Providence, our Sire. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्य नु सुकृतं दैव्यं सहोऽग्निर्गृहे जरिता मेधिरः कविः ।यज्ञश्च भूद्विदथे चारुरंतम आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ nú ǀ sú-kṛtam ǀ dáivyam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀ jaritā́ ǀ médhiraḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀyajñáḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhūt ǀ vidáthe ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra possesseth might celestial nobly formed: the singer in the house is Agni, prudent Sage. He is the sacrifice in synod, fair, most near. We ask for freedom and complete felicity,
verses.wilson_translation: The divine force of Indrais well constructed;Agni(abides) in our dwelling, the praiser of the gods, thereceiver of oblations, the sage, and is worthy of sacrifice at the altar, beautiful and most near (to us). We long forthe universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra possesseth might celestial nobly formed: the singer in the house is Agni, prudent Sage. He is the sacrifice in synod, fair, most near. We ask for freedom and complete felicity,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वो गुहा चकृम भूरि दुष्कृतं नाविष्ट्यं वसवो देवहेळनं ।माकिर्नो देवा अनृतस्य वर्पस आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vaḥ ǀ gúhā ǀ cakṛma ǀ bhū́ri ǀ duḥ-kṛtám ǀ ná ǀ āvíḥ-tyam ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ deva-héḷanam ǀmā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ ánṛtasya ǀ várpasaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not often have we sinned against you secretly, nor, Vasus, have we openly provoked the Gods. Not one of its, ye Gods, hath worn an alien shape. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: We have not done any great evil in secret from you, nor any open (action) causing the anger of thegods, O you givers of wealth; let not, O gods, (the possession) of an unreal form be our (lot). We long for theuniversal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Not often have we sinned against you secretly, nor, Vasus, have we openly provoked the Gods. Not one of its, ye Gods, hath worn an alien shape. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपामीवां सविता साविषन्न्यग्वरीय इदप सेधंत्वद्रयः ।ग्रावा यत्र मधुषुदुच्यते बृहदा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ savitā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ nyák ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ápa ǀ sedhantu ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀgrā́vā ǀ yátra ǀ madhu-sút ǀ ucyáte ǀ bṛhát ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Savitar remove from us our malady, and may the Mountains keep it far away from where The press-stone as it sheds the meath rings loudly forth. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May Savitādrive away (our) disease, may the mountains keep off our most heinous (sin), where thestone( the effuser) of the sweet Somais abundantly praised. We long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: May Savitar remove from us our malady, and may the Mountains keep it far away from where The press-stone as it sheds the meath rings loudly forth. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वो ग्रावा वसवोऽस्तु सोतरि विश्वा द्वेषांसि सनुतर्युयोत ।स नो देवः सविता पायुरीड्य आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ grā́vā ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ astu ǀ sotári ǀ víśvā ǀ dvéṣāṃsi ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyota ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ pāyúḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Vasus, let the stone, the presser stand erect: avert all enmities and keep them far remote. Our guard to be adored is Savitar this God. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: May the stone be uplifted, gods, when I make the libation; disperse all my secret adversaries; the god Savitā is our adorable protector. We long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Vasus, let the stone, the presser stand erect: avert all enmities and keep them far remote. Our guard to be adored is Savitar this God. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्जं गावो यवसे पीवो अत्तन ऋतस्य याः सदने कोशे अंग्ध्वे ।तनूरेव तन्वो अस्तु भेषजमा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: ū́rjam ǀ gāvaḥ ǀ yávase ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ attana ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ sádane ǀ kóśe ǀ aṅgdhvé ǀtanū́ḥ ǀ evá ǀ tanváḥ ǀ astu ǀ bheṣajám ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eat strength and fatness in the pasture, kine, who are balmed at the reservoir and at the seat of Law. So let your body be our body's medicine. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Eat abundant fodder in the pasture, O cows, who are anointed in the hall of sacrifice in the cow-stall;may (your) body be the remedy for (our) body. We long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: Eat strength and fatness in the pasture, kine, who are balmed at the reservoir and at the seat of Law. So let your body be our body's medicine. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: क्रतुप्रावा जरिता शश्वतामव इंद्र इद्भद्रा प्रमतिः सुतावतां ।पूर्णमूधर्दिव्यं यस्य सिक्तय आ सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: kratu-prā́vā ǀ jaritā́ ǀ śáśvatām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ sutá-vatām ǀpūrṇám ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ divyám ǀ yásya ǀ siktáye ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: The singer fills the spirit: all mens, love hath he. Indra takes kindly care of those who pour the juice. For his libation is the heavenly udder full. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrais the fulfiller of pious acts, the glorifier of all, the guardian of the offerers of libations, theauspicious forethought, for his libation the divine pitcher is filled (with Soma). We long for the universal Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: The singer fills the spirit: all mens, love hath he. Indra takes kindly care of those who pour the juice. For his libation is the heavenly udder full. We ask for freedom and complete felicity.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चित्रस्ते भानुः क्रतुप्रा अभिष्टिः संति स्पृधो जरणिप्रा अधृष्टाः ।रजिष्ठया रज्या पश्व आ गोस्तूतूर्षति पर्यग्रं दुवस्युः ॥
verses.transliteration: citráḥ ǀ te ǀ bhānúḥ ǀ kratu-prā́ḥ ǀ abhiṣṭíḥ ǀ sánti ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ jaraṇi-prā́ḥ ǀ ádhṛṣṭāḥ ǀrájiṣṭhayā ǀ rájyā ǀ paśváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ góḥ ǀ tū́tūrṣati ǀ pári ǀ ágram ǀ duvasyúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wondrous thy spirit-filling light, triumpliant; thy hosts save from decay and are resistless. The pious votary by straightest pathway speeds to possess the best of all the cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: Your splendour,Indra, is wonderful, fulfilling our pious acts, desirable; your efforts replenishing thewealth of your worshippers are irresistible; (therefore) Duvasyu hastens in front of the victim cow, (leading it) witha straight cord.
verses.griffith_verse: Wondrous thy spirit-filling light, triumpliant; thy hosts save from decay and are resistless. The pious votary by straightest pathway speeds to possess the best of all the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १२ बुधः सौम्यः। विश्वे देवा, ऋत्विजो वा । त्रिष्टुप् ४, ६ गायत्री, ५ बृहती, ९,१२ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WAKE with one mind, my friends, and kindle Agni, ye who are many and who dwell together.Agni and Dadhikrās and Dawn the Goddess, you, Gods with Indra, I call down to help us. Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport.Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward. Lay on the yokes, and fasten well the traces: formed is the furrow, sow the seed within it.Through song may we find bearing fraught with plenty: near to the ripened grain approach the sickle. Wise, through desire of bliss from Gods, the skilful bind the traces fast, And lay the yokes on either side. Arrange the buckets in their place securely fasten on the straps.We will pour forth the well that hath a copious stream, fair-flowing well that never fails. I pour the water from the well with pails prepared and goodly straps,Unfailing, full, with plenteous stream. Refresh the horses, win the prize before you: equip a chariot fraught with happy fortune.Pour forth the well with stone wheel, wooden buckets, the drink of heroes, with the trough for armour. Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour, wide and many.Make iron forts, secure from all assailants let not your pitcher leak: stay it securely. Hither, for help, I turn the holy heavenly mind of you the Holy Gods, that longs for sacrifice.May it pour milk for us, even as a stately cow who, having sought the pasture, yields a thousand streams. Pour golden juice within the wooden vessel: with stone-made axes fashion ye and form it.Embrace and compass it with tenfold girdle, and to both chariot-poles attach the car-horse. Between both poles the car-horse goes pressed closely, as in his dwelling moves the doubly-wedded.Lay in the wood the Soviran of the Forest, and sink the well although ye do not dig it. Indra is he, O men, who gives us happiness: sport, urge the giver of delight to win us strengthBring quickly down, O priests, hither to give us aid, to drink the Soma, Indra Son of Nistigri.

verses.sanskrit: उद्बुध्यध्वं समनसः सखायः समग्निमिंध्वं बहवः सनीळाः ।दधिक्रामग्निमुषसं च देवीमिंद्रावतोऽवसे नि ह्वये वः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ budhyadhvam ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ agním ǀ indhvam ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀdadhi-krā́m ǀ agním ǀ uṣásam ǀ ca ǀ devī́m ǀ índra-vataḥ ǀ ávase ǀ ní ǀ hvaye ǀ vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WAKE with one mind, my friends, and kindle Agni, ye who are many and who dwell together. Agni and Dadhikrās and Dawn the Goddess, you, Gods with Indra, I call down to help us.
verses.wilson_translation: Awake, friends, being all agreed; many in number, abiding in one dwelling, kindle Agni. I invoke you,Dadhikra, Agni, and the divine Uṣas, who are associated with Indra, for our protection.
verses.griffith_verse: WAKE with one mind, my friends, and kindle Agni, ye who are many and who dwell together. Agni and Dadhikrās and Dawn the Goddess, you, Gods with Indra, I call down to help us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मंद्रा कृणुध्वं धिय आ तनुध्वं नावमरित्रपरणीं कृणुध्वं ।इष्कृणुध्वमायुधारं कृणुध्वं प्रांचं यज्ञं प्र णयता सखायः ॥
verses.transliteration: mandrā́ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tanudhvam ǀ nā́vam ǀ aritra-páraṇīm ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀíṣkṛṇudhvam ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ áram ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ prā́ñcam ǀ yajñám ǀ prá ǀ nayata ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport. Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.
verses.wilson_translation: Construct exhilarating (hymns), spread forth praises, construct the ship which is propelled by oars,prepare your weapons, make ready, lead forth, O friends, the herald, the adorable (Agni).
verses.griffith_verse: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport. Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युनक्त सीरा वि युगा तनुध्वं कृते योनौ वपतेह बीजं ।गिरा च श्रुष्टिः सभरा असन्नो नेदीय इत्सृण्यः पक्वमेयात् ॥
verses.transliteration: yunákta ǀ sī́rā ǀ ví ǀ yugā́ ǀ tanudhvam ǀ kṛté ǀ yónau ǀ vapata ǀ ihá ǀ bī́jam ǀgirā́ ǀ ca ǀ śruṣṭíḥ ǀ sá-bharāḥ ǀ ásat ǀ naḥ ǀ nédīyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ sṛṇyáḥ ǀ pakvám ǀ ā́ ǀ iyāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lay on the yokes, and fasten well the traces: formed is the furrow, sow the seed within it. Through song may we find bearing fraught with plenty: near to the ripened grain approach the sickle.
verses.wilson_translation: Harness the plural ughs, fit on the yokes, now that the womb of earth is ready, sow the seed therein, andthrough our praise may there be abundant food; may (the grain) fall ripe towards the sickle.
verses.griffith_verse: Lay on the yokes, and fasten well the traces: formed is the furrow, sow the seed within it. Through song may we find bearing fraught with plenty: near to the ripened grain approach the sickle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सीरा युंजंति कवयो युगा वि तन्वते पृथक् ।धीरा देवेषु सुम्नया ॥
verses.transliteration: sī́rā ǀ yuñjanti ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ yugā́ ǀ ví ǀ tanvate ǀ pṛ́thak ǀdhī́rāḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ sumna-yā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Wise, through desire of bliss from Gods, the skilful bind the traces fast, And lay the yokes on either side.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise (priests) harness the plural ughs, they lay the yokes apart, firmly devoted through the desire ofhappiness.
verses.griffith_verse: Wise, through desire of bliss from Gods, the skilful bind the traces fast, And lay the yokes on either side.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निराहावान्कृणोतन सं वरत्रा दधातन ।सिंचामहा अवतमुद्रिणं वयं सुषेकमनुपक्षितं ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ ǀ ā-hāvā́n ǀ kṛṇotana ǀ sám ǀ varatrā́ḥ ǀ dadhātana ǀsiñcā́mahai ǀ avatám ǀ udríṇam ǀ vayám ǀ su-sékam ǀ ánupa-kṣitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Arrange the buckets in their place securely fasten on the straps. We will pour forth the well that hath a copious stream, fair-flowing well that never fails.
verses.wilson_translation: Set up the cattle-troughs, bind the straps to it; let us pour out (the water of) the well, which is full ofwater, fit to be poured out, and not easily exhausted.
verses.griffith_verse: Arrange the buckets in their place securely fasten on the straps. We will pour forth the well that hath a copious stream, fair-flowing well that never fails.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इष्कृताहावमवतं सुवरत्रं सुषेचनं ।उद्रिणं सिंचे अक्षितं ॥
verses.transliteration: íṣkṛta-āhāvam ǀ avatám ǀ su-varatrám ǀ su-secanám ǀudríṇam ǀ siñce ǀ ákṣitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I pour the water from the well with pails prepared and goodly straps, Unfailing, full, with plenteous stream.
verses.wilson_translation: I pour out (the water of) the well, whose cattle troughs are prepared, well fitted with straps, fit to bepoured out, full of water, inexhaustible.
verses.griffith_verse: I pour the water from the well with pails prepared and goodly straps, Unfailing, full, with plenteous stream.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रीणीताश्वान्हितं जयाथ स्वस्तिवाहं रथमित्कृणुध्वं ।द्रोणाहावमवतमश्मचक्रमंसत्रकोशं सिंचता नृपाणं ॥
verses.transliteration: prīṇītá ǀ áśvān ǀ hitám ǀ jayātha ǀ svasti-vā́ham ǀ rátham ǀ ít ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀdróṇa-āhāvam ǀ avatám ǀ áśma-cakram ǀ áṃsatra-kośam ǀ siñcata ǀ nṛ-pā́nam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Refresh the horses, win the prize before you: equip a chariot fraught with happy fortune. Pour forth the well with stone wheel, wooden buckets, the drink of heroes, with the trough for armour.
verses.wilson_translation: Satisfy the horses, accomplish the good work (of plural ughing), equip a car laden with good fortune, pourout (the water of) the well, having wooden cattle-troughs having a stone rim, having a receptable like armour, fitfor the drinking of men.
verses.griffith_verse: Refresh the horses, win the prize before you: equip a chariot fraught with happy fortune. Pour forth the well with stone wheel, wooden buckets, the drink of heroes, with the trough for armour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्रजं कृणुध्वं स हि वो नृपाणो वर्म सीव्यध्वं बहुला पृथूनि ।पुरः कृणुध्वमायसीरधृष्टा मा वः सुस्रोच्चमसो दृंहता तं ॥
verses.transliteration: vrajám ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ vaḥ ǀ nṛ-pā́naḥ ǀ várma ǀ sīvyadhvam ǀ bahulā́ ǀ pṛthū́ni ǀpúraḥ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ ā́yasīḥ ǀ ádhṛṣṭāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ susrot ǀ camasáḥ ǀ dṛ́ṃhata ǀ tám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour, wide and many. Make iron forts, secure from all assailants let not your pitcher leak: stay it securely.
verses.wilson_translation: Construct the cow-stall, for that is the drinking plural ce of your leaders (the gods), fabricate armour,manifold and ample; make cities of metal and impregnable; let not the ladle leak, make it strong.
verses.griffith_verse: Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour, wide and many. Make iron forts, secure from all assailants let not your pitcher leak: stay it securely.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वो धियं यज्ञियां वर्त ऊतये देवा देवीं यजतां यज्ञियामिह ।सा नो दुहीयद्यवसेव गत्वी सहस्रधारा पयसा मही गौः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ dhíyam ǀ yajñíyām ǀ varte ǀ ūtáye ǀ dévāḥ ǀ devī́m ǀ yajatā́m ǀ yajñíyām ǀ ihá ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duhīyat ǀ yávasā-iva ǀ gatvī́ ǀ sahásra-dhārā ǀ páyasā ǀ mahī́ ǀ gáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither, for help, I turn the holy heavenly mind of you the Holy Gods, that longs for sacrifice. May it pour milk for us, even as a stately cow who, having sought the pasture, yields a thousand streams.
verses.wilson_translation: I attract, O gods, for my protection, your adorable, divine mine, which is deserving of sacrifice andworship here; may it milk forth for us, like a large cow with milk, giving a thousand strreams, (having eaten)fodder and returned.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither, for help, I turn the holy heavenly mind of you the Holy Gods, that longs for sacrifice. May it pour milk for us, even as a stately cow who, having sought the pasture, yields a thousand streams.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ तू षिंच हरिमीं द्रोरुपस्थे वाशीभिस्तक्षताश्मन्मयीभिः ।परि ष्वजध्वं दश कक्ष्याभिरुभे धुरौ प्रति वह्निं युनक्त ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tú ǀ siñca ǀ hárim ǀ īm ǀ dróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ vā́śībhiḥ ǀ takṣata ǀ aśman-máyībhiḥ ǀpári ǀ svajadhvam ǀ dáśa ǀ kakṣyā́bhiḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ dhúrau ǀ práti ǀ váhnim ǀ yunakta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pour golden juice within the wooden vessel: with stone-made axes fashion ye and form it. Embrace and compass it with tenfold girdle, and to both chariot-poles attach the car-horse.
verses.wilson_translation: Pour out the golden-tinted Somainto the bowl of the wooden cup, fabricate it with the stone axes, girdit with ten bands, harness the beast of burden to the two poles (of the cart).
verses.griffith_verse: Pour golden juice within the wooden vessel: with stone-made axes fashion ye and form it. Embrace and compass it with tenfold girdle, and to both chariot-poles attach the car-horse.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उभे धुरौ वह्निरापिब्दमानोऽंतर्योनेव चरति द्विजानिः ।वनस्पतिं वन आस्थापयध्वं नि षू दधिध्वमखनंत उत्सं ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ dhúrau ǀ váhniḥ ǀ ā-píbdamānaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ yónā-iva ǀ carati ǀ dvi-jā́niḥ ǀvánaspátim ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ asthāpayadhvam ǀ ní ǀ sú ǀ dadhidhvam ǀ ákhanantaḥ ǀ útsam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Between both poles the car-horse goes pressed closely, as in his dwelling moves the doubly-wedded. Lay in the wood the Soviran of the Forest, and sink the well although ye do not dig it.
verses.wilson_translation: The beast of burden pressed with the two cart-poles, moves as if on the womb of sacrifice having twowives. plural ce the chariot in the wood, without digging store up the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Between both poles the car-horse goes pressed closely, as in his dwelling moves the doubly-wedded. Lay in the wood the Soviran of the Forest, and sink the well although ye do not dig it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कपृन्नरः कपृथमुद्दधातन चोदयत खुदत वाजसातये ।निष्टिग्र्यः पुत्रमा च्यावयोतय इंद्रं सबाध इह सोमपीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: kápṛt ǀ naraḥ ǀ kapṛthám ǀ út ǀ dadhātana ǀ codáyata ǀ khudáta ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀniṣṭigryáḥ ǀ putrám ǀ ā́ ǀ cyavaya ǀ ūtáye ǀ índram ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra is he, O men, who gives us happiness: sport, urge the giver of delight to win us strength Bring quickly down, O priests, hither to give us aid, to drink the Soma, Indra Son of Nistigri.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, you leaders, is the giver of happiness; excite the giver of happiness, stimulate him, sport withhim for the acquisition of food, bring down here, O priests, Indra, the son of Niṣṭigrī, to drink the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra is he, O men, who gives us happiness: sport, urge the giver of delight to win us strength Bring quickly down, O priests, hither to give us aid, to drink the Soma, Indra Son of Nistigri.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १२  मुद्गलो भार्म्यश्वः। द्रुघणः, इन्द्रो वा। त्रिष्टुप्, १,३, १२ बृहती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FOR thee may Indra boldly speed the car that works on either side.Favour us, Much-invoked! in this most glorious fight against the raiders of our wealth. Loose in the wind the woman's robe was streaming what time she won a car-load worth a thousand.The charioteer in fight was Mudgalani: she Indra's dart, heaped up the prize of battle. O Indra, cast thy bolt among assailants who would slaughter us:The weapon both of Dāsa and of Ārya foe keep far away, O Maghavan. The bull in joy had drunk a lake of water. His shattering horn encountered an opponent.Swiftly, in vigorous strength, eager for glory, he stretched his forefeet, fain to win and triumph. They came anear the bull; they made him thunder, made him pour rain down ere the fight was ended.And Mudgala thereby won in the contest well-pastured kine in hundreds and in thousands. In hope of victory that bull was harnessed: Kesi the driver urged him on with shouting.As he ran swiftly with the car behind him his lifted heels pressed close on Mudgalani. Deftly for him he stretched the car-pole forward, guided the bull thereto and firmly yoked him.Indra vouchsafed the lord of cows his favour: with mighty steps the buffalo ran onward. Touched by the goad the shaggy beast went nobly, bound to the pole by the yoke's thong of leather.Performing deeds of might for many people, he, looking on the cows, gained strength and vigour. Here look upon this mace, this bull's companion, now lying midway on the field of battle.Therewith hath Mudgala in ordered contest won for cattle for himself, a hundred thousand. Far is the evil: who hath here beheld it? Hither they bring the bull whom they are yoking..To this they give not either food or water. Reaching beyond the pole it gives directions. Like one forsaken, she hath found a husband, and teemed as if her breast were full and flowing.With swiftly-racing chariot may we conquer, and rich and blessed be our gains in battle. Thou, Indra, art the mark whereon the eyes of all life rest, when thou,A Bull who drivest with thy bull, wilt win the race together with thy weakling friend.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते रथं मिथूकृतमिंद्रोऽवतु धृष्णुया ।अस्मिन्नाजौ पुरुहूत श्रवाय्ये धनभक्षेषु नोऽव ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ rátham ǀ mithu-kṛ́tam ǀ índraḥ ǀ avatu ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀasmín ǀ ājáu ǀ puru-hūta ǀ śravā́yye ǀ dhana-bhakṣéṣu ǀ naḥ ǀ ava ǁ
verses.english_translation: FOR thee may Indra boldly speed the car that works on either side. Favour us, Much-invoked! in this most glorious fight against the raiders of our wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: May (Indra) by his prowess protect your cart (mudgala) that has no companion, defend us, O invokedof many, in this memorable conflict in the recovery of our wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: FOR thee may Indra boldly speed the car that works on either side. Favour us, Much-invoked! in this most glorious fight against the raiders of our wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्स्म वातो वहति वासोऽस्या अधिरथं यदजयत्सहस्रं ।रथीरभून्मुद्गलानी गविष्टौ भरे कृतं व्यचेदिंद्रसेना ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ sma ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ vahati ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ ádhi-ratham ǀ yát ǀ ájayat ǀ sahásram ǀrathī́ḥ ǀ abhūt ǀ mudgalā́nī ǀ gó-iṣṭau ǀ bháre ǀ kṛtám ǀ ví ǀ acet ǀ indra-senā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Loose in the wind the woman's robe was streaming what time she won a car-load worth a thousand. The charioteer in fight was Mudgalani: she Indra's dart, heaped up the prize of battle.
verses.wilson_translation: The wind raised her vesture when she won a thousand cart-loads. Mudgalānī was the charioteer inthe quest of the cattle, the army of Indrarecovered (the spoil) taken in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Loose in the wind the woman's robe was streaming what time she won a car-load worth a thousand. The charioteer in fight was Mudgalani: she Indra's dart, heaped up the prize of battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंतर्यच्छ जिघांसतो वज्रमिंद्राभिदासतः ।दासस्य वा मघवन्नार्यस्य वा सनुतर्यवया वधं ॥
verses.transliteration: antáḥ ǀ yaccha ǀ jíghāṃsataḥ ǀ vájram ǀ indra ǀ abhi-dā́sataḥ ǀdā́sasya ǀ vā ǀ magha-van ǀ ā́ryasya ǀ vā ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yavaya ǀ vadhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Indra, cast thy bolt among assailants who would slaughter us: The weapon both of Dāsa and of Ārya foe keep far away, O Maghavan.
verses.wilson_translation: Restrain,Indra, the thunderbolt of the malignant threatening (foe); ward off,Maghavan, the secretweapon (of our foe), be he DāsaorĀrya.
verses.griffith_verse: O Indra, cast thy bolt among assailants who would slaughter us: The weapon both of Dāsa and of Ārya foe keep far away, O Maghavan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्नो ह्रदमपिबज्जर्हृषाणः कूटं स्म तृंहदभिमातिमेति ।प्र मुष्कभारः श्रव इच्छमानोऽजिरं बाहू अभरत्सिषासन् ॥
verses.transliteration: udnáḥ ǀ hradám ǀ apibat ǀ járhṛṣāṇaḥ ǀ kū́ṭam ǀ sma ǀ tṛṃhát ǀ abhí-mātim ǀ eti ǀprá ǀ muṣká-bhāraḥ ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ ajirám ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ abharat ǀ sísāsan ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bull in joy had drunk a lake of water. His shattering horn encountered an opponent. Swiftly, in vigorous strength, eager for glory, he stretched his forefeet, fain to win and triumph.
verses.wilson_translation: Rejoicing, he drank up the pool of water, he cleft the mountain peak, he went against the enemy;endowed with vigour, eager for fame, assailing the quick-moving (foe), he seized him with his two arms.
verses.griffith_verse: The bull in joy had drunk a lake of water. His shattering horn encountered an opponent. Swiftly, in vigorous strength, eager for glory, he stretched his forefeet, fain to win and triumph.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न्यक्रंदयन्नुपयंत एनममेहयन्वृषभं मध्य आजेः ।तेन सूभर्वं शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जिगाय ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ akrandayan ǀ upa-yántaḥ ǀ enam ǀ ámehayan ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ mádhye ǀ ājéḥ ǀténa ǀ sū́bharvam ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásram ǀ gávām ǀ múdgalaḥ ǀ pra-dháne ǀ jigāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: They came anear the bull; they made him thunder, made him pour rain down ere the fight was ended. And Mudgala thereby won in the contest well-pastured kine in hundreds and in thousands.
verses.wilson_translation: Approaching the bull, they made him roar in the midst of the battle. I,Mudgala, have thereby gained inwar hundreds and thousands of cattle well- pastured.
verses.griffith_verse: They came anear the bull; they made him thunder, made him pour rain down ere the fight was ended. And Mudgala thereby won in the contest well-pastured kine in hundreds and in thousands.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ककर्दवे वृषभो युक्त आसीदवावचीत्सारथिरस्य केशी ।दुधेर्युक्तस्य द्रवतः सहानस ऋच्छंति ष्मा निष्पदो मुद्गलानीं ॥
verses.transliteration: kakárdave ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ ávāvacīt ǀ sā́rathiḥ ǀ asya ǀ keśī́ ǀdúdheḥ ǀ yuktásya ǀ drávataḥ ǀ sahá ǀ ánasā ǀ ṛcchánti ǀ sma ǀ niḥ-pádaḥ ǀ mudgalā́nīm ǁ
verses.english_translation: In hope of victory that bull was harnessed: Kesi the driver urged him on with shouting. As he ran swiftly with the car behind him his lifted heels pressed close on Mudgalani.
verses.wilson_translation: The bull has been yoked for the destruction of the enemy; his long- haired yoke-fellow made him roar;
verses.griffith_verse: In hope of victory that bull was harnessed: Kesi the driver urged him on with shouting. As he ran swiftly with the car behind him his lifted heels pressed close on Mudgalani.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत प्रधिमुदहन्नस्य विद्वानुपायुनग्वंसगमत्र शिक्षन् ।इंद्र उदावत्पतिमघ्न्यानामरंहत पद्याभिः ककुद्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ pra-dhím ǀ út ǀ ahan ǀ asya ǀ vidvā́n ǀ úpa ǀ ayunak ǀ váṃsagam ǀ átra ǀ śíkṣan ǀíndraḥ ǀ út ǀ āvat ǀ pátim ǀ ághnyānām ǀ áraṃhata ǀ pádyābhiḥ ǀ kakút-mān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Deftly for him he stretched the car-pole forward, guided the bull thereto and firmly yoked him. Indra vouchsafed the lord of cows his favour: with mighty steps the buffalo ran onward.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage (Mudgala) has fitted up the frame of the cart, he has harnessed the bull, training him to hiswork;Indraprotected the lord of the inviolable (cows), the buffalo rushed along with speed.
verses.griffith_verse: Deftly for him he stretched the car-pole forward, guided the bull thereto and firmly yoked him. Indra vouchsafed the lord of cows his favour: with mighty steps the buffalo ran onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनमष्ट्राव्यचरत्कपर्दी वरत्रायां दार्वानह्यमानः ।नृम्णानि कृण्वन्बहवे जनाय गाः पस्पशानस्तविषीरधत्त ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ aṣṭrā-vī́ ǀ acarat ǀ kapardī́ ǀ varatrā́yām ǀ dā́ru ǀ ā-náhyamānaḥ ǀnṛmṇā́ni ǀ kṛṇván ǀ baháve ǀ jánāya ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ paspaśānáḥ ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ adhatta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Touched by the goad the shaggy beast went nobly, bound to the pole by the yoke's thong of leather. Performing deeds of might for many people, he, looking on the cows, gained strength and vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Wielding the goad (Indra) with the braided hair proceeded happily, fastening the strap to the wood (ofwon hundreds and thousands of cattle in war.
verses.griffith_verse: Touched by the goad the shaggy beast went nobly, bound to the pole by the yoke's thong of leather. Performing deeds of might for many people, he, looking on the cows, gained strength and vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमं तं पश्य वृषभस्य युंजं काष्ठाया मध्ये द्रुघणं शयानं ।येन जिगाय शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः पृतनाज्येषु ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ tám ǀ paśya ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ yúñjam ǀ kā́ṣṭhāyāḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ dru-ghanám ǀ śáyānam ǀyéna ǀ jigā́ya ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásram ǀ gávām ǀ múdgalaḥ ǀ pṛtanā́jyeṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here look upon this mace, this bull's companion, now lying midway on the field of battle. Therewith hath Mudgala in ordered contest won for cattle for himself, a hundred thousand.
verses.griffith_verse: Here look upon this mace, this bull's companion, now lying midway on the field of battle. Therewith hath Mudgala in ordered contest won for cattle for himself, a hundred thousand.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आरे अघा को न्वित्था ददर्श यं युंजंति तम्वा स्थापयंति ।नास्मै तृणं नोदकमा भरंत्युत्तरो धुरो वहति प्रदेदिशत् ॥
verses.transliteration: āré ǀ aghā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ nú ǀ itthā́ ǀ dadarśa ǀ yám ǀ yuñjánti ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ā́ ǀ sthāpayanti ǀná ǀ asmai ǀ tṛ́ṇam ǀ ná ǀ udakám ǀ ā́ ǀ bharanti ǀ út-taraḥ ǀ dhuráḥ ǀ vahati ǀ pra-dédiśat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far is the evil: who hath here beheld it? Hither they bring the bull whom they are yoking.. To this they give not either food or water. Reaching beyond the pole it gives directions.
verses.wilson_translation: Who has thus beheld the evils near athand? The (bull) which they yoke, they stop; to him they bringneither fodder nor water. Being above (the bull) he bears the chariot-pole announcing (victory to his lord).
verses.griffith_verse: Far is the evil: who hath here beheld it? Hither they bring the bull whom they are yoking.. To this they give not either food or water. Reaching beyond the pole it gives directions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: परिवृक्तेव पतिविद्यमानट् पीप्याना कूचक्रेणेव सिंचन् ।एषैष्या चिद्रथ्या जयेम सुमंगलं सिनवदस्तु सातं ॥
verses.transliteration: parivṛktā́-iva ǀ pati-vídyam ǀ ānaṭ ǀ pī́pyānā ǀ kū́cakreṇa-iva ǀ siñcán ǀeṣa-eṣyā́ ǀ cit ǀ rathyā́ ǀ jayema ǀ su-maṅgálam ǀ sína-vat ǀ astu ǀ sātám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like one forsaken, she hath found a husband, and teemed as if her breast were full and flowing. With swiftly-racing chariot may we conquer, and rich and blessed be our gains in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: As a wife who has been abandoned rejoices to find her husband, as a cloud expanding when pouringforth rain with the aid of the earth's disc; with her eager (to recover the cattle) for our charioteer, may we win (theprize), may good fortune, together with food, be given to us.
verses.griffith_verse: Like one forsaken, she hath found a husband, and teemed as if her breast were full and flowing. With swiftly-racing chariot may we conquer, and rich and blessed be our gains in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं विश्वस्य जगतश्चक्षुरिंद्रासि चक्षुषः ।वृषा यदाजिं वृषणा सिषाससि चोदयन्वध्रिणा युजा ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ víśvasya ǀ jágataḥ ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ indra ǀ asi ǀ cákṣuṣaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ yát ǀ ājím ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ sísāsasi ǀ codáyan ǀ vádhriṇā ǀ yujā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, Indra, art the mark whereon the eyes of all life rest, when thou, A Bull who drivest with thy bull, wilt win the race together with thy weakling friend.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, are the eye of the whole world, when, showerer (of benefits), urging on your two vigoroussteeds, harnessed to the car, you engage in battle.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, Indra, art the mark whereon the eyes of all life rest, when thou, A Bull who drivest with thy bull, wilt win the race together with thy weakling friend.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIII. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: १३ ऐन्द्रोऽप्रतिरथः। इन्द्रः, ४ बृहस्पति:, १२ अप्वा देवी, १३ मरुतो वा। त्रिष्टुप् , १३ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SWIFT, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people,With eyes that close not, bellowing, Sole Hero, Indra. subdued at once a hundred armies. With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, Victor, bold, hard to overthrow, Rouser of battle,Indra. the Strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye warriors, now, now vanquish in the combat. He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band rings hosts together,Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows. Bṛhaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen.Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies. Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing,The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kine-winner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra. Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it.-Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage. Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra, the pitiless Hero, wild with anger,Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless,may he protect our armies in our battles. Indra guide these: Bṛhaspati precede them, the guerdon, and the sacrifice, and Soma;And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish. Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuṇa, and Maruts, and Ādityas.Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer high-minded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble. Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits of my warring heroes.Urge on the strong steeds' might, O Vṛtra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward. May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be the arrows of our army.May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset. Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies and depart, O Apva.Attack them, set their hearts on fire and burn them: so let our foes abide in utter darkness. Advance, O heroes, win the day. May Indra be your sure defence.Exceeding mighty be your arms, that none may wound or injure you.

verses.sanskrit: आशुः शिशानो वृषभो न भीमो घनाघनः क्षोभणश्चर्षणीनां ।संक्रंदनोऽनिमिष एकवीरः शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: āśúḥ ǀ śíśānaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ghanāghanáḥ ǀ kṣóbhaṇaḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀsam-krándanaḥ ǀ ani-miṣáḥ ǀ eka-vīráḥ ǀ śatám ǀ sénāḥ ǀ ajayat ǀ sākám ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SWIFT, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people, With eyes that close not, bellowing, Sole Hero, Indra. subdued at once a hundred armies.
verses.wilson_translation: The fleet-going Indra, like a formidable bull sharpening (his horns), the slayer of foes, the exciter ofmen, loud-shouting, ever-vigilant, the chief of heroes overthrew at once a hundred hosts.
verses.griffith_verse: SWIFT, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people, With eyes that close not, bellowing, Sole Hero, Indra. subdued at once a hundred armies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: संक्रंदनेनानिमिषेण जिष्णुना युत्कारेण दुश्च्यवनेन धृष्णुना ।तदिंद्रेण जयत तत्सहध्वं युधो नर इषुहस्तेन वृष्णा ॥
verses.transliteration: sam-krándanena ǀ ani-miṣéṇa ǀ jiṣṇúnā ǀ yut-kāréṇa ǀ duḥ-cyavanéna ǀ dhṛṣṇúnā ǀtát ǀ índreṇa ǀ jayata ǀ tát ǀ sahadhvam ǀ yúdhaḥ ǀ naraḥ ǀ íṣu-hastena ǀ vṛ́ṣṇā ǁ
verses.english_translation: With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, Victor, bold, hard to overthrow, Rouser of battle, Indra. the Strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye warriors, now, now vanquish in the combat.
verses.wilson_translation: With Indrathe loud-shouting, the vigilant, the vigtorious, the warlike, the unconquerable, the daring,the hurler of arrows, the showerer, (as your ally) conquer you warriors, you leaders, that (hostile host) andovercome it.
verses.griffith_verse: With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, Victor, bold, hard to overthrow, Rouser of battle, Indra. the Strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye warriors, now, now vanquish in the combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इषुहस्तैः स निषंगिभिर्वशी संस्रष्टा स युध इंद्रो गणेन ।संसृष्टजित्सोमपा बाहुशर्ध्युग्रधन्वा प्रतिहिताभिरस्ता ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ íṣu-hastaiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ niṣaṅgí-bhiḥ ǀ vaśī́ ǀ sám-sraṣṭā ǀ sáḥ ǀ yúdhaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ gaṇéna ǀsaṃsṛṣṭa-jít ǀ soma-pā́ḥ ǀ bāhu-śardhī́ ǀ ugrá-dhanvā ǀ práti-hitābhiḥ ǀ ástā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band rings hosts together, Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, with the arrow-bearing (maruts), armed with swords, the subduer, the warrior, who encountershim, the drinker of the Soma, the strong- armed, having a powerful bow, who shoots with well-aimed arrows(conquer with his help).
verses.griffith_verse: He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band rings hosts together, Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पते परि दीया रथेन रक्षोहामित्राँ अपबाधमानः ।प्रभंजन्त्सेनाः प्रमृणो युधा जयन्नस्माकमेध्यविता रथानां ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ pári ǀ dīya ǀ ráthena ǀ rakṣaḥ-hā́ ǀ amítrān ǀ apa-bā́dhamānaḥ ǀpra-bhañján ǀ sénāḥ ǀ pra-mṛṇáḥ ǀ yudhā́ ǀ jáyan ǀ asmā́kam ǀ edhi ǀ avitā́ ǀ ráthānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bṛhaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen. Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies.
verses.wilson_translation: Come with your chariot,Bṛhaspati, who are the slayer of Rākṣasas, discomfiting your enemies,
verses.griffith_verse: Bṛhaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen. Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बलविज्ञायः स्थविरः प्रवीरः सहस्वान्वाजी सहमान उग्रः ।अभिवीरो अभिसत्वा सहोजा जैत्रमिंद्र रथमा तिष्ठ गोवित् ॥
verses.transliteration: bala-vijñāyáḥ ǀ stháviraḥ ǀ prá-vīraḥ ǀ sáhasvān ǀ vājī́ ǀ sáhamānaḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀabhí-vīraḥ ǀ abhí-satvā ǀ sahaḥ-jā́ḥ ǀ jáitram ǀ indra ǀ rátham ǀ ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ go-vít ǁ
verses.english_translation: Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing, The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kine-winner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Known by his strength mighty, heroic, overpowering, vigorous, enduring, fierce, attended by heroes,attended by mighty men, the offspring of strength, the possessor of water, do you,Indra, ascend your triumphantchariot.
verses.griffith_verse: Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing, The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kine-winner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गोत्रभिदं गोविदं वज्रबाहुं जयंतमज्म प्रमृणंतमोजसा ।इमं सजाता अनु वीरयध्वमिंद्रं सखायो अनु सं रभध्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: gotra-bhídam ǀ go-vídam ǀ vájra-bāhum ǀ jáyantam ǀ ájma ǀ pra-mṛṇántam ǀ ójasā ǀimám ǀ sa-jātāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vīrayadhvam ǀ índram ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sám ǀ rabhadhvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it.- Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage.
verses.wilson_translation: Imitate in heroism, you kindred warriors, follow, friends, in prowess this Indra, who is the breaker ofmountains, the acquirer of water, armed with the thunderbolt, conquering the swift (foe), destroying (the enemy)by his might.
verses.griffith_verse: Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it.- Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि गोत्राणि सहसा गाहमानोऽदयो वीरः शतमन्युरिंद्रः ।दुश्च्यवनः पृतनाषाळयुध्योऽस्माकं सेना अवतु प्र युत्सु ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ gotrā́ṇi ǀ sáhasā ǀ gā́hamānaḥ ǀ adayáḥ ǀ vīráḥ ǀ śatá-manyuḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀduḥ-cyavanáḥ ǀ pṛtanāṣā́ṭ ǀ ayudhyáḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sénāḥ ǀ avatu ǀ prá ǀ yut-sú ǁ
verses.english_translation: Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra, the pitiless Hero, wild with anger, Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless,may he protect our armies in our battles.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, bursting open the clouds with force; pitiless, heroic, with hundredfold anger, invincible, theoverthrower of armies, irresistible, protect our armies in battles.
verses.griffith_verse: Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra, the pitiless Hero, wild with anger, Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless,may he protect our armies in our battles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र आसां नेता बृहस्पतिर्दक्षिणा यज्ञः पुर एतु सोमः ।देवसेनानामभिभंजतीनां जयंतीनां मरुतो यंत्वग्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ āsām ǀ netā́ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ etu ǀ sómaḥ ǀdeva-senā́nām ǀ abhi-bhañjatīnā́m ǀ jáyantīnām ǀ marútaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ ágram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra guide these: Bṛhaspati precede them, the guerdon, and the sacrifice, and Soma; And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indrabe the leader of these (hosts), may Bṛhaspati,Dakṣiṇā,Yajña, and Somago before, letthe Marutsmarch in the van of the destroying and victorious armies of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra guide these: Bṛhaspati precede them, the guerdon, and the sacrifice, and Soma; And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्य वृष्णो वरुणस्य राज्ञ आदित्यानां मरुतां शर्ध उग्रं ।महामनसां भुवनच्यवानां घोषो देवानां जयतामुदस्थात् ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ ādityā́nām ǀ marútām ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ ugrám ǀmahā́-manasām ǀ bhuvana-cyavā́nām ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ jáyatām ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuṇa, and Maruts, and Ādityas. Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer high-minded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble.
verses.wilson_translation: (May) the mighty force of the showerer Indra, of the royal Varuṇa, of theĀdityasand Maruts(beours). The shout of the magnanimous and victorious deities, the subverters of the worlds, has arisen.
verses.griffith_verse: Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuṇa, and Maruts, and Ādityas. Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer high-minded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उद्धर्षय मघवन्नायुधान्युत्सत्वनां मामकानां मनांसि ।उद्वृत्रहन्वाजिनां वाजिनान्युद्रथानां जयतां यंतु घोषाः ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ harṣaya ǀ magha-van ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ út ǀ sátvanām ǀ māmakā́nām ǀ mánāṃsi ǀút ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ vājínām ǀ vā́jināni ǀ út ǀ ráthānām ǀ jáyatām ǀ yantu ǀ ghóṣāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits of my warring heroes. Urge on the strong steeds' might, O Vṛtra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward.
verses.wilson_translation: Excite,Maghavan, my weapons, (excite) the spirits of my heroes; slayer of Vṛtra, let the speed of thehorses be accelerated, let the noises of the chariots be increased.
verses.griffith_verse: Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits of my warring heroes. Urge on the strong steeds' might, O Vṛtra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकमिंद्रः समृतेषु ध्वजेष्वस्माकं या इषवस्ता जयंतु ।अस्माकं वीरा उत्तरे भवंत्वस्माँ उ देवा अवता हवेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ índraḥ ǀ sám-ṛteṣu ǀ dhvajéṣu ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ íṣavaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ jayantu ǀasmā́kam ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ út-tare ǀ bhavantu ǀ asmā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ devāḥ ǀ avata ǀ háveṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be the arrows of our army. May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset.
verses.wilson_translation: When the banners are intermingled, may Indrabe our (defender), may those arrows which are ours bevictorious may our warriors be triumphant; gods, protect us in battles.
verses.griffith_verse: May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be the arrows of our army. May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अमीषां चित्तं प्रतिलोभयंती गृहाणांगान्यप्वे परेहि ।अभि प्रेहि निर्दह हृत्सु शोकैरंधेनामित्रास्तमसा सचंतां ॥
verses.transliteration: amī́ṣām ǀ cittám ǀ prati-lobháyantī ǀ gṛhāṇá ǀ áṅgāni ǀ apve ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀabhí ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ níḥ ǀ daha ǀ hṛt-sú ǀ śókaiḥ ǀ andhéna ǀ amítrāḥ ǀ támasā ǀ sacantām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies and depart, O Apva. Attack them, set their hearts on fire and burn them: so let our foes abide in utter darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Bewildering the mind of our foes, Apva, seize their limbs and depart, proceed against them, burn intheir hearts with sorrow, let our enemies be covered with thick darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies and depart, O Apva. Attack them, set their hearts on fire and burn them: so let our foes abide in utter darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेता जयता नर इंद्रो वः शर्म यच्छतु ।उग्रा वः संतु बाहवोऽनाधृष्या यथासथ ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ ita ǀ jáyata ǀ naraḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatu ǀugrā́ḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ santu ǀ bāhávaḥ ǀ anādhṛṣyā́ḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Advance, O heroes, win the day. May Indra be your sure defence. Exceeding mighty be your arms, that none may wound or injure you.
verses.wilson_translation: Advance, warriors, and conquer; may Indragrant you happiness, may your arms be strong, so that youmay be invincible.
verses.griffith_verse: Advance, O heroes, win the day. May Indra be your sure defence. Exceeding mighty be your arms, that none may wound or injure you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIV. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Soma hath flowed for thee, Invoked of mat Speed to our sacrifice with both thy Coursers.To thee have streameld the songs or mighty singers, imploring, Indra, drink of our libation. Drink of the juice which men have washed in waters, and fill thee full, O Lord of Tawny Horses.O Indra, hearer of the laud, with Soma which stones have mixed for thee enhance thy rapture. To make thee start, a strong true draught I offer to thee, the Bull, O thou whom Bay Steeds carry.Here take delight, O Indra, in our voices while thou art hymned with power and all our spirit. O Mighty Indra, through thine aid, thy prowess, obtaining life, zealous, and skilled in Order,Men in the house who share the sacred banquet stand singing praise that brings them store of children. Through thy directions, Lord of Tawny Coursers, thine who art firm, splendid, and blest, the peopleObtain most liberal aid for their salvation, and praise thee, Indra, through thine excellencies. Lord of the Bays, come with thy two Bay Horses, come to our prayers, to drink the juice of Soma.To thee comes sacrifice which thou acceptest: thou, skilled in holy rites, art he who giveth. Him of a thousand powers, subduing foemen, Maghavan praised with hymns and pleased with Soma,—Even him our songs approach, resistless Indra: the adorations of the singer laud him. The way to bliss for Gods and man thou foundest, Indra, seven lovely floods, divine, untroubled,Wherewith thou, rending forts, didst move the ocean, and nine-and-ninety flowing streams of water. Thou from the curse didst free the mighty Waters, and as their only God didst watch and guard them.O Indra, cherish evermore thy body with those which thou hast won in quelling Vṛtra. Heroic power and noble praise is Indra yea, the song worships him invoked of many.Vṛtra he quelled, and gave men room and freedom: gakra, victorious, hath conquered armies. Call we on Maghayan, auspicious Indra. best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered,The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.

verses.sanskrit: असावि सोमः पुरुहूत तुभ्यं हरिभ्यां यज्ञमुप याहि तूयं ।तुभ्यं गिरो विप्रवीरा इयाना दधन्विर इंद्र पिबा सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ásāvi ǀ sómaḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ túbhyam ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ yajñám ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ tū́yam ǀtúbhyam ǀ gíraḥ ǀ vípra-vīrāḥ ǀ iyānā́ḥ ǀ dadhanviré ǀ indra ǀ píba ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma hath flowed for thee, Invoked of mat Speed to our sacrifice with both thy Coursers. To thee have streameld the songs or mighty singers, imploring, Indra, drink of our libation.
verses.wilson_translation: The Somahas been effused for you, (Indra), the invoked of many, come quickly to the sacrifice withyour two bay horses; our praises recited by the wise, moving quickly, are addressed to you; drink, Indra, of thelibation.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma hath flowed for thee, Invoked of mat Speed to our sacrifice with both thy Coursers. To thee have streameld the songs or mighty singers, imploring, Indra, drink of our libation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्सु धूतस्य हरिवः पिबेह नृभिः सुतस्य जठरं पृणस्व ।मिमिक्षुर्यमद्रय इंद्र तुभ्यं तेभिर्वर्धस्व मदमुक्थवाहः ॥
verses.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ dhūtásya ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ píba ǀ ihá ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sutásya ǀ jaṭháram ǀ pṛṇasva ǀmimikṣúḥ ǀ yám ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ vardhasva ǀ mádam ǀ uktha-vāhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink of the juice which men have washed in waters, and fill thee full, O Lord of Tawny Horses. O Indra, hearer of the laud, with Soma which stones have mixed for thee enhance thy rapture.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of bay steeds, drink at this ceremony of the Somathat has been shaken up with the water, fillyour belly with the libation offered by the priests, which the grinding-stones desired to express for you,Indra; doyou who are carried by hymns enhance your exhilaration with these (hymns).
verses.griffith_verse: Drink of the juice which men have washed in waters, and fill thee full, O Lord of Tawny Horses. O Indra, hearer of the laud, with Soma which stones have mixed for thee enhance thy rapture.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रोग्रां पीतिं वृष्ण इयर्मि सत्यां प्रयै सुतस्य हर्यश्व तुभ्यं ।इंद्र धेनाभिरिह मादयस्व धीभिर्विश्वाभिः शच्या गृणानः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ ugrā́m ǀ pītím ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ iyarmi ǀ satyā́m ǀ pra-yái ǀ sutásya ǀ hari-aśva ǀ túbhyam ǀíndra ǀ dhénābhiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mādayasva ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ śácyā ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To make thee start, a strong true draught I offer to thee, the Bull, O thou whom Bay Steeds carry. Here take delight, O Indra, in our voices while thou art hymned with power and all our spirit.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of bay steeds, showerer (of benefits), I send you strong good drink that you may proceed;Indra,who are glorified for your prowess, be exhilarated at this (ceremony) with praises, with all rites.
verses.griffith_verse: To make thee start, a strong true draught I offer to thee, the Bull, O thou whom Bay Steeds carry. Here take delight, O Indra, in our voices while thou art hymned with power and all our spirit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊती शचीवस्तव वीर्येण वयो दधाना उशिज ऋतज्ञाः ।प्रजावदिंद्र मनुषो दुरोणे तस्थुर्गृणंतः सधमाद्यासः ॥
verses.transliteration: ūtī́ ǀ śacī-vaḥ ǀ táva ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀprajā́-vat ǀ indra ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ sadha-mā́dyāsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Mighty Indra, through thine aid, thy prowess, obtaining life, zealous, and skilled in Order, Men in the house who share the sacred banquet stand singing praise that brings them store of children.
verses.wilson_translation: Powerful Indra, they stood in the dwelling of the man (who instrumental tuted the rite), enjoying food togetherwith the offspring, through your protection and prowess, desiring you, knowing the ceremonies, glorifying you,and partaking of the exhilaration.
verses.griffith_verse: O Mighty Indra, through thine aid, thy prowess, obtaining life, zealous, and skilled in Order, Men in the house who share the sacred banquet stand singing praise that brings them store of children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रणीतिभिष्टे हर्यश्व सुष्टोः सुषुम्नस्य पुरुरुचो जनासः ।मंहिष्ठामूतिं वितिरे दधानाः स्तोतार इंद्र तव सूनृताभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: pránīti-bhiḥ ǀ te ǀ hari-aśva ǀ su-stóḥ ǀ su-sumnásya ǀ puru-rúcaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀmáṃhiṣṭhām ǀ ūtím ǀ vi-tíre ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ stotā́raḥ ǀ indra ǀ táva ǀ sūnṛ́tābhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through thy directions, Lord of Tawny Coursers, thine who art firm, splendid, and blest, the people Obtain most liberal aid for their salvation, and praise thee, Indra, through thine excellencies.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of bay horses, by the right guidance of you who are deservedly praised, the bestower ofhappiness the illustrious, the men your praisers, OIndra, have acquired your most gracious assistance forexcelling (other suppliants) through your favours.
verses.griffith_verse: Through thy directions, Lord of Tawny Coursers, thine who art firm, splendid, and blest, the people Obtain most liberal aid for their salvation, and praise thee, Indra, through thine excellencies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप ब्रह्माणि हरिवो हरिभ्यां सोमस्य याहि पीतये सुतस्य ।इंद्र त्वा यज्ञः क्षममाणमानड्दाश्वाँ अस्यध्वरस्य प्रकेतः ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ sómasya ǀ yāhi ǀ pītáye ǀ sutásya ǀíndra ǀ tvā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ kṣámamāṇam ǀ ānaṭ ǀ dāśvā́n ǀ asi ǀ adhvarásya ǀ pra-ketáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the Bays, come with thy two Bay Horses, come to our prayers, to drink the juice of Soma. To thee comes sacrifice which thou acceptest: thou, skilled in holy rites, art he who giveth.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of bay horses, come with your two bays to our adorations to drink of the effused Soma; thesacrifice,Indra, reaches to you who are enduring; cognizant of the sacrifice, you are the donor of the reward.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of the Bays, come with thy two Bay Horses, come to our prayers, to drink the juice of Soma. To thee comes sacrifice which thou acceptest: thou, skilled in holy rites, art he who giveth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रवाजमभिमातिषाहं सुतेरणं मघवानं सुवृक्तिं ।उप भूषंति गिरो अप्रतीतमिंद्रं नमस्या जरितुः पनंत ॥
verses.transliteration: sahásra-vājam ǀ abhimāti-sáham ǀ suté-raṇam ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ su-vṛktím ǀúpa ǀ bhūṣanti ǀ gíraḥ ǀ áprati-itam ǀ índram ǀ namasyā́ḥ ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ pananta ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him of a thousand powers, subduing foemen, Maghavan praised with hymns and pleased with Soma,— Even him our songs approach, resistless Indra: the adorations of the singer laud him.
verses.wilson_translation: Our praises celebrate the irresistible Indra, the dispenser of abundant food, the overcomer of enemies,the delighter in the libation, the possessor of opulence, the well-praised; the adorations of the worshipper glorify(him).
