verses.griffith_verse: Him of a thousand powers, subduing foemen, Maghavan praised with hymns and pleased with Soma,— Even him our songs approach, resistless Indra: the adorations of the singer laud him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्तापो देवीः सुरणा अमृक्ता याभिः सिंधुमतर इंद्र पूर्भित् ।नवतिं स्रोत्या नव च स्रवंतीर्देवेभ्यो गातुं मनुषे च विंदः ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ su-ráṇāḥ ǀ ámṛktāḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ síndhum ǀ átaraḥ ǀ indra ǀ pūḥ-bhít ǀnavatím ǀ srotyā́ḥ ǀ náva ǀ ca ǀ srávantīḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ mánuṣe ǀ ca ǀ vindaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The way to bliss for Gods and man thou foundest, Indra, seven lovely floods, divine, untroubled, Wherewith thou, rending forts, didst move the ocean, and nine-and-ninety flowing streams of water.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven divine meandering rivers with which you,Indra, the destroyer of cities, replenished theocean, flow unimpeded; you did discover the nine-and-ninety flowing rivers (and their) path for gods and men.
verses.griffith_verse: The way to bliss for Gods and man thou foundest, Indra, seven lovely floods, divine, untroubled, Wherewith thou, rending forts, didst move the ocean, and nine-and-ninety flowing streams of water.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपो महीरभिशस्तेरमुंचोऽजागरास्वधि देव एकः ।इंद्र यास्त्वं वृत्रतूर्ये चकर्थ ताभिर्विश्वायुस्तन्वं पुपुष्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ abhí-śasteḥ ǀ amuñcaḥ ǀ ájāgaḥ ǀ āsu ǀ ádhi ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀíndra ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ tvám ǀ vṛtra-tū́rye ǀ cakártha ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ pupuṣyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou from the curse didst free the mighty Waters, and as their only God didst watch and guard them. O Indra, cherish evermore thy body with those which thou hast won in quelling Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: You did release the great waters from the malignant (obstructer), you were the only god who watchedover them; with those waters which you have employed for the destruction of Vṛtra, may you, all vivifying Indra,cherish your own person n.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou from the curse didst free the mighty Waters, and as their only God didst watch and guard them. O Indra, cherish evermore thy body with those which thou hast won in quelling Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वीरेण्यः क्रतुरिंद्रः सुशस्तिरुतापि धेना पुरुहूतमीट्टे ।आर्दयद्वृत्रमकृणोदु लोकं ससाहे शक्रः पृतना अभिष्टिः ॥
verses.transliteration: vīréṇyaḥ ǀ krátuḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-śastíḥ ǀ utá ǀ ápi ǀ dhénā ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ īṭṭe ǀā́rdayat ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ákṛṇot ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ sasahé ǀ śakráḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ abhiṣṭíḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heroic power and noble praise is Indra yea, the song worships him invoked of many. Vṛtra he quelled, and gave men room and freedom: gakra, victorious, hath conquered armies.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrais the chief of heroes, the doer of great deeds, to whom praise is well offered; yes, and the voiceof praise lauds him the invoked of many. He slew Vṛtra, he created light;Śakra, the conqueror, has overcome(hostile) hosts.
verses.griffith_verse: Heroic power and noble praise is Indra yea, the song worships him invoked of many. Vṛtra he quelled, and gave men room and freedom: gakra, victorious, hath conquered armies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रमस्मिन्भरे नृतमं वाजसातौ ।शृण्वंतमुग्रमूतये समत्सु घ्नंतं वृत्राणि संजितं धनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: Call we on Maghayan, auspicious Indra. best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat; the leader in thefood-bestowing strife, hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Call we on Maghayan, auspicious Indra. best Hero in this fight where spoil is gathered, The Strong, who listens, who gives aid in battles, who slays the Vṛtras, wins and gathers riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ११ कौत्सो दुर्मित्रः सुमित्रो वा। इन्द्रः। उष्णिक्, १ गायत्री वा २,७ पिपीलिकमध्या, ११ त्रिष्टुप् ।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream.The juice is ready to ferment. He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes,With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give. Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fearsThe sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory. Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him:Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way. Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as ’twere for food,The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws. The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength,Like skilful Mātariśvan with his power and might, The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain,With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament. Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns:Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice. When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice,Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship. Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop.Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle. As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here,What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.

verses.sanskrit: कदा वसो स्तोत्रं हर्यत आव श्मशा रुधद्वाः ।दीर्घं सुतं वाताप्याय ॥
verses.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ stotrám ǀ háryate ǀ ā́ ǀ áva ǀ śmaśā́ ǀ rudhat ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǀdīrghám ǀ sutám ǀ vātā́pyāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream. The juice is ready to ferment.
verses.wilson_translation: When,Vasu, (will our) praise (reach) you desiring it? (when) will he, (like) a dam, obstruct and letloose the long-protracted for the sake of wind- driven (rain)?
verses.griffith_verse: WHEN, Vasu, wilt thou love the laud? Now let the channel bring the stream. The juice is ready to ferment.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हरी यस्य सुयुजा विव्रता वेरर्वंतानु शेपा ।उभा रजी न केशिना पतिर्दन् ॥
verses.transliteration: hárī íti ǀ yásya ǀ su-yújā ǀ ví-vratā ǀ véḥ ǀ árvantā ǀ ánu ǀ śépā ǀubhā́ ǀ rajī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ keśínā ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǁ
verses.english_translation: He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes, With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give.
verses.wilson_translation: (OIndra), to whom belong the two bay horses, well-trained, active, swift, courageous, brilliant as thetwo worlds, do you, who are lord (of bay horses), bestowing (wealth upon us), desire (our praises).
verses.griffith_verse: He whose two Bay Steeds harnessed well, swerving, pursue the Bird's tail-plumes, With Rowing manes, like heaven and earth, he is the Lord with power to give.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप योरिंद्रः पापज आ मर्तो न शश्रमाणो बिभीवान् ।शुभे यद्युयुजे तविषीवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ yóḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ pā́paje ǀ ā́ ǀ mártaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śaśramāṇáḥ ǀ bibhīvā́n ǀśubhé ǀ yát ǀ yuyujé ǀ táviṣī-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fears The sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory.
verses.wilson_translation: Indrarepelled (him), being like a mortal tired and frightened in (the combat with) the offspring ofiniquity (Vṛtra), when being associated with the forces (of the Maruts), he has been prepared for splendour.
verses.griffith_verse: Bereft of skill is Indra, if, like some outwearied man he fears The sinner, when the Mighty hath prepared himself for victory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सचायोरिंद्रश्चर्कृष आँ उपानसः सपर्यन् ।नदयोर्विव्रतयोः शूर इंद्रः ॥
verses.transliteration: sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ cárkṛṣe ǀ ā́ ǀ upānasáḥ ǀ saparyán ǀnadáyoḥ ǀ ví-vratayoḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him: Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the friend of man, for his exhilaration, comes mounted in his chariot, granting him favour, thehero Indra, (the driver) of the two neighing and prancing (steeds).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra with these drives round, until he meets with one to worship him: Indra is Master of the pair who snort and swerve upon their way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधि यस्तस्थौ केशवंता व्यचस्वंता न पुष्ट्यै ।वनोति शिप्राभ्यां शिप्रिणीवान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ádhi ǀ yáḥ ǀ tastháu ǀ kéśa-vantā ǀ vyácasvantā ǀ ná ǀ puṣṭyái ǀvanóti ǀ śíprābhyām ǀ śipríṇī-vān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as ’twere for food, The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has mounted the two long-maned and all pervading steeds for the nourishment (of thesacrificer) asks (for the Soma) with his two jaws, possessing mighty jaws.
verses.griffith_verse: Borne onward by the long-maned Steeds who stretch themselves as ’twere for food, The God who wears the helm defends them with his jaws.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रास्तौदृष्वौजा ऋष्वेभिस्ततक्ष शूरः शवसा ।ऋभुर्न क्रतुभिर्मातरिश्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ astaut ǀ ṛṣvá-ojāḥ ǀ ṛṣvébhiḥ ǀ tatákṣa ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ śávasā ǀṛbhúḥ ǀ ná ǀ krátu-bhiḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength, Like skilful Mātariśvan with his power and might,
verses.wilson_translation: Of glorious strength (associated) with the glorious (maruts) he was renowned; the hero abiding in thefirmament wrought with his strength as theṚbhuswith their wonderful works.
verses.griffith_verse: The Mighty sang with Lofty Ones: the Hero fashioned with his strength, Like skilful Mātariśvan with his power and might,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वज्रं यश्चक्रे सुहनाय दस्यवे हिरीमशो हिरीमान् ।अरुतहनुरद्भुतं न रजः ॥
verses.transliteration: vájram ǀ yáḥ ǀ cakré ǀ su-hánāya ǀ dásyave ǀ hirīmaśáḥ ǀ hírīmān ǀáruta-hanuḥ ǀ ádbhutam ǀ ná ǀ rájaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain, With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament.
verses.wilson_translation: The golden-bearded (Indra), lord of bay horses, who made the thunderbolt for the easy destruction ofthe Dasyu, who has irresistible jaws like the vast firmament.
verses.griffith_verse: The bolt, which pierced at once the vitals of the Dasyu easy to be slain, With jaw uninjured like the wondrous firmament.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव नो वृजिना शिशीह्यृचा वनेमानृचः ।नाब्रह्मा यज्ञ ऋधग्जोषति त्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛjinā́ ǀ śiśīhi ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ vanema ǀ anṛ́caḥ ǀná ǀ ábrahmā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ jóṣati ǀ tvé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns: Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitigate,Indra, our iniquities, may we, by our hymns, extermiante those who offer no hymns. Thesacrifice, unaccompanied by prayer, distinct (from that which is performed with prayer), is not grateful to you. in the hall of sacrifice, accompanied by the sacrifice, you, the friend of man, (ascend) the vessel of your glory.
verses.griffith_verse: Grind off our sins: with song will we conquer the men who sing no hymns: Not easily art thou pleased with prayerless sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वा यत्ते त्रेतिनी भूद्यज्ञस्य धूर्षु सद्मन् ।सजूर्नावं स्वयशसं सचायोः ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvā́ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ tretínī ǀ bhū́t ǀ yajñásya ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ sádman ǀsa-jū́ḥ ǀ nā́vam ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice, Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship.
verses.griffith_verse: When threefold flame burns high for thee, to rest on poles of sacrifice, Thou with the living joyest in the self-bright Ship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रिये ते पृश्निरुपसेचनी भूच्छ्रिये दर्विररेपाः ।यया स्वे पात्रे सिंचस उत् ॥
verses.transliteration: śriyé ǀ te ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ upa-sécanī ǀ bhūt ǀ śriyé ǀ dárviḥ ǀ arepā́ḥ ǀyáyā ǀ své ǀ pā́tre ǀ siñcáse ǀ út ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop. Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle.
verses.wilson_translation: May the spotted cow yield milk for mixing with your (Soma), may the ladle for the mixture wherewithyou pour it into your own vessel be free from defect.
verses.griffith_verse: Thy glory was the speckled cup, thy glory was the flawless scoop. Wherewith thou pourest into thy receptacle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतं वा यदसुर्य प्रति त्वा सुमित्र इत्थास्तौद्दुर्मित्र इत्थास्तौत् ।आवो यद्दस्युहत्ये कुत्सपुत्रं प्रावो यद्दस्युहत्ये कुत्सवत्सं ॥
verses.transliteration: śatám ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ asurya ǀ práti ǀ tvā ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ astaut ǀ duḥ-mitráḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ astaut ǀā́vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ dasyu-hátye ǀ kutsa-putrám ǀ prá ǀ ā́vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ dasyu-hátye ǀ kutsa-vatsám ǁ
verses.english_translation: As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here, What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.
verses.wilson_translation: When, you, mighty (Indra, gave) hundredfold (riches),Sumitrapraised you thus,Durmitrapraised youthus, when at the slaughter of the Dasyusyou did protect Kutsa's son, when at the slaughter of the Dasyus youprotected Kutsa's darling.
verses.griffith_verse: As hundreds, O Immortal God, have sung to thee, so hath Sumitra, yea, Durmitra praised thee here, What time thou holpest Kutsa's son, when Dasyus fell, yea, holpest Kutsa's darling when the Dasyus died.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVI. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skilful men weave garments.That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather. Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet.Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered. Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship.Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers. Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest;Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling. You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuṇa, the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament, like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations). You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes), and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels), do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay. Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like the Ṛbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches. With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies. (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice). Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow.Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers. Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward. May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries.Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Aśvins' longing.

verses.sanskrit: उभा उ नूनं तदिदर्थयेथे वि तन्वाथे धियो वस्त्रापसेव ।सध्रीचीना यातवे प्रेमजीगः सुदिनेव पृक्ष आ तंसयेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: ubháu ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nūnám ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ arthayethe íti ǀ ví ǀ tanvāthe íti ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ vástrā ǀ apásā-iva ǀsadhrīcīnā́ ǀ yā́tave ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ ajīgaríti ǀ sudínā-iva ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ taṃsayethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skilful men weave garments. That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather.
verses.wilson_translation: You both demand the oblation (Aśvins), you spread out the ceremonials as two weavers (strentch)cloths; (the instrumental tutor of the rite) praised you associated together to attain (his desires); like two fortunate daysyou bestow food.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skilful men weave garments. That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उष्टारेव फर्वरेषु श्रयेथे प्रायोगेव श्वात्र्या शासुरेथः ।दूतेव हि ष्ठो यशसा जनेषु माप स्थातं महिषेवावपानात् ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣṭā́rā-iva ǀ phárvareṣu ǀ śrayethe íti ǀ prāyogā́-iva ǀ śvā́tryā ǀ śā́suḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ithaḥ ǀdūtā́-iva ǀ hí ǀ stháḥ ǀ yaśásā ǀ jáneṣu ǀ mā́ ǀ ápa ǀ sthātam ǀ mahiṣā́-iva ǀ ava-pā́nāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet. Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered.
verses.wilson_translation: Like two longing oxen (to the pastures), you have recourse to those who fill you (with oblations); youapproach like two horses prepared for the fray; employed to bring treasure; you are like two (royal) messengersrenowned among the people; turn not away (from our oblation) like two buffaloes from the drinking-trough.
verses.griffith_verse: Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet. Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: साकंयुजा शकुनस्येव पक्षा पश्वेव चित्रा यजुरा गमिष्टं ।अग्निरिव देवयोर्दीदिवांसा परिज्मानेव यजथः पुरुत्रा ॥
verses.transliteration: sākam-yújā ǀ śakunásya-iva ǀ pakṣā́ ǀ paśvā́-iva ǀ citrā́ ǀ yájuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gamiṣṭam ǀagníḥ-iva ǀ deva-yóḥ ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsā ǀ párijmānā-iva ǀ yajathaḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship. Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers.
verses.wilson_translation: Connected toegether like the two wings of a bird, you came to the sacrifice like two choice animals;radiant as Agni(at the offering) of the devout (worshipper), like two perambulating priests you celebrate worshipin many plural ces.
verses.griffith_verse: Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship. Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपी वो अस्मे पितरेव पुत्रोग्रेव रुचा नृपतीव तुर्यै ।इर्येव पुष्ट्यै किरणेव भुज्यै श्रुष्टीवानेव हवमा गमिष्टं ॥
verses.transliteration: āpī́ íti ǀ vaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ pitárā-iva ǀ putrā́ ǀ ugrā́-iva ǀ rucā́ ǀ nṛpátī ivéti nṛpátī-iva ǀ turyái ǀíryā-iva ǀ puṣṭyái ǀ kiráṇā-iva ǀ bhujyái ǀ śruṣṭīvā́nā-iva ǀ hávam ǀ ā́ ǀ gamiṣṭam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest; Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling.
verses.wilson_translation: You are kinsmen to us, like parents (to) sons, like two fierce shining fires, like two princes hastening togive protection, like two bestowers of food are you for the nourishment of men, like two luminaries for theenjoyment (of our worshippers), like two quick horses you came to our invocation.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest; Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वंसगेव पूषर्या शिंबाता मित्रेव ऋता शतरा शातपंता ।वाजेवोच्चा वयसा घर्म्येष्ठा मेषेवेषा सपर्या पुरीषा ॥
verses.transliteration: váṃsagā-iva ǀ pūṣaryā́ ǀ śimbā́tā ǀ mitrā́-íva ǀ ṛtā́ ǀ śatárā ǀ śā́tapantā ǀvā́jā-iva ǀ uccā́ ǀ váyasā ǀ gharmye-sthā́ ǀ méṣā-iva ǀ iṣā́ ǀ saparyā́ ǀ púrīṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuṇa, the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament, like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).
verses.wilson_translation: You are like two plural asantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitraand Varuṇa, the two bestowers of felicity,veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plural mp with fodder, abiding in the firmament, liketwo rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).
verses.griffith_verse: You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuṇa, the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament, like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सृण्येव जर्भरी तुर्फरीतू नैतोशेव तुर्फरी पर्फरीका ।उदन्यजेव जेमना मदेरू ता मे जराय्वजरं मरायु ॥
verses.transliteration: sṛṇyā́-iva ǀ jarbhárī íti ǀ turphárītū íti ǀ naitośā́-iva ǀ turphárī íti ǀ parpharī́kā ǀudanyajā́-iva ǀ jémanā ǀ maderū́ íti ǀ tā́ ǀ me ǀ jarā́yu ǀ ajáram ǀ marā́yu ǁ
verses.english_translation: You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes), and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels), do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.
verses.wilson_translation: You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons ofare victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.
verses.griffith_verse: You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes), and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels), do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पज्रेव चर्चरं जारं मरायु क्षद्मेवार्थेषु तर्तरीथ उग्रा ।ऋभू नापत्खरमज्रा खरज्रुर्वायुर्न पर्फरत्क्षयद्रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: pajrā́-iva ǀ cárcaram ǀ jā́ram ǀ marā́yu ǀ kṣádma-iva ǀ ártheṣu ǀ tartarīthaḥ ǀ ugrā ǀṛbhū́ íti ǀ ná ǀ āpat ǀ kharamajrā́ ǀ khará-jruḥ ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ná ǀ parpharat ǀ kṣayat ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like the Ṛbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to crossover to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like theṚbhus, your chariot attained itsdestination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like the Ṛbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घर्मेव मधु जठरे सनेरू भगेविता तुर्फरी फारिवारं ।पतरेव चचरा चंद्रनिर्णिङ्मनऋंगा मनन्या न जग्मी ॥
verses.transliteration: gharmā́-iva ǀ mádhu ǀ jaṭháre ǀ sanérū íti ǀ bháge-avitā ǀ turphárī íti ǀ phā́rivā ǀ áram ǀpatarā́-iva ǀ cacarā́ ǀ candrá-nirnik ǀ mánaḥ-ṛṅgā ǀ mananyā́ ǀ ná ǀ jágmī íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies. (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).
verses.wilson_translation: With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies,(you are), armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success throughthe mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies. (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बृहंतेव गंभरेषु प्रतिष्ठां पादेव गाधं तरते विदाथः ।कर्णेव शासुरनु हि स्मराथोऽंशेव नो भजतं चित्रमप्नः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhántā-iva ǀ gambháreṣu ǀ prati-sthā́m ǀ pā́dā-iva ǀ gādhám ǀ tárate ǀ vidāthaḥ ǀkárṇā-iva ǀ śā́suḥ ǀ ánu ǀ hí ǀ smárāthaḥ ǀ áṃśā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ bhajatam ǀ citrám ǀ ápnaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow. Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers.
verses.griffith_verse: Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow. Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आरंगरेव मध्वेरयेथे सारघेव गवि नीचीनबारे ।कीनारेव स्वेदमासिष्विदाना क्षामेवोर्जा सूयवसात्सचेथे ॥
verses.transliteration: āraṅgarā́-iva ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayethe íti ǀ sāraghā́-iva ǀ gávi ǀ nīcī́na-bāre ǀkīnā́rā-iva ǀ svédam ǀ ā-sisvidānā́ ǀ kṣā́ma-iva ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ suyavasa-át ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward.
verses.wilson_translation: Like two loud-sounding (clouds), you send forth the sweet (Soma); like two bees (you deposit milk) in(the udder of) the cow which has its opening turned downwards; like two labourers you are dripping withperspiration, like a tired cow eating sweet herbage, you attend.
verses.griffith_verse: Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋध्याम स्तोमं सनुयाम वाजमा नो मंत्रं सरथेहोप यातं ।यशो न पक्वं मधु गोष्वंतरा भूतांशो अश्विनोः काममप्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛdhyā́ma ǀ stómam ǀ sanuyā́ma ǀ vā́jam ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mántram ǀ sa-ráthā ǀ ihá ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǀyáśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pakvám ǀ mádhu ǀ góṣu ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhūtá-aṃśaḥ ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ aprāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries. Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Aśvins' longing.
verses.wilson_translation: May we increase our praise, (Aśvins), may we offer you food, come hither in the same chariot to ourworship; and accept the sweet food prepared from within the cows. Bhūtāṃs;a has fulfilled the desires of thelearned.
verses.griffith_verse: May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries. Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Aśvins' longing.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVII. Dakṣiṇā.
hymns.anukramani: ११ दिव्य आंगिरसः, दक्षिणा वा प्राजापत्या। दक्षिना, दक्षिणादातारो वा। त्रिष्टुप् , ४ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THESE men's great bounty hath been manifested, and the whole world of life set free from darkness.Great light hath come, vouchsafed us by the Fathers: apparent is the spacious path of Guerdon. High up in heaven abide the Guerdon-givers: they who give steeds dwell with the Sun for ever.They who give gold are blest with life eternal. they who give robes prolong their lives, O Soma. Not from the niggards-for they give not fireely-comes Meed at sacrifice, Gods’ satisfaction:Yea, many men with hands stretched out with Guerdon present their gifts because they dread dishonour. These who observe mankind regard oblation as streamy Vāyu and light-finding Arka.They satisfy and give their gifts in synod, and pour in streams the seven-mothered Guerdon. He who brings Guerdon comes as first invited: chief of the hamlet comes the Guerdon-bearer.Him I account the ruler of the people who was the first to introduce the Guerdon. They call him Ṛṣi, Brahman, Sāma-chanter, reciter of the laud, leader of worship.The brightly-shining God's three forms he knoweth who first bestowed the sacrificial Guerdon. Guerdon bestows the horse, bestows the bullock, Guerdon bestows, moreover, gold that Rsisters.Guerdon gives food which is our life and spirit. He who is wise takes Guerdon for his armour. The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble.The light of heaven, the universe about us,—all this doth sacrificial Guerdon give them. First have the liberal gained a fragrant dwelling, and got themselves a bride in fair apparel.The liberal have obtained their draught of liquor, and conquered those who, unprovoked, assailed them. They deck the fleet steed for the bounteous giver: the maid adorns herself and waits to meet him.His home is like a lake with lotus blossoms, like the Gods’ palaces adorned and splendid. Steeds good at draught convey the liberal giver, and lightly rolling moves the car of Guerdon.Assist, ye Gods, the liberal man in battles: the liberal giver conquers foes in combat.

verses.sanskrit: आविरभून्महि माघोनमेषां विश्वं जीवं तमसो निरमोचि ।महि ज्योतिः पितृभिर्दत्तमागादुरुः पंथा दक्षिणाया अदर्शि ॥
verses.transliteration: āvíḥ ǀ abhūt ǀ máhi ǀ mā́ghonam ǀ eṣām ǀ víśvam ǀ jīvám ǀ támasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ amoci ǀmáhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ dattám ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ urúḥ ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀ adarśi ǁ
verses.english_translation: THESE men's great bounty hath been manifested, and the whole world of life set free from darkness. Great light hath come, vouchsafed us by the Fathers: apparent is the spacious path of Guerdon.
verses.wilson_translation: The great (splendour) of Maghavanhas becomemanifest (for the rites) of these (worshippers); all lifehas been extricated from darkness, the vast light bestowed by the progenitors has arrived, a spacious path forthedakṣiṇāhas been displayed. (I Maghavan: Mqaghavan = the sun, at whose rising and at midday thedakṣiṇā is to be given, not at sunset; cf. RV. 5.77.2].
verses.griffith_verse: THESE men's great bounty hath been manifested, and the whole world of life set free from darkness. Great light hath come, vouchsafed us by the Fathers: apparent is the spacious path of Guerdon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उच्चा दिवि दक्षिणावंतो अस्थुर्ये अश्वदाः सह ते सूर्येण ।हिरण्यदा अमृतत्वं भजंते वासोदाः सोम प्र तिरंत आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: uccā́ ǀ diví ǀ dákṣiṇā-vantaḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀ yé ǀ aśva-dā́ḥ ǀ sahá ǀ té ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀhiraṇya-dā́ḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ bhajante ǀ vāsaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ soma ǀ prá ǀ tirante ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: High up in heaven abide the Guerdon-givers: they who give steeds dwell with the Sun for ever. They who give gold are blest with life eternal. they who give robes prolong their lives, O Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: (Saramā). I come, the appointed messenger of Indra, desiring,Paṇis, your great hidden treasures;through fear of being crossed the (water) helped us, thus I passed over the waters of the Rasā.
verses.griffith_verse: High up in heaven abide the Guerdon-givers: they who give steeds dwell with the Sun for ever. They who give gold are blest with life eternal. they who give robes prolong their lives, O Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दैवी पूर्तिर्दक्षिणा देवयज्या न कवारिभ्यो नहि ते पृणंति ।अथा नरः प्रयतदक्षिणासोऽवद्यभिया बहवः पृणंति ॥
verses.transliteration: dáivī ǀ pūrtíḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǀ ná ǀ kava-aríbhyaḥ ǀ nahí ǀ té ǀ pṛṇánti ǀátha ǀ náraḥ ǀ práyata-dakṣiṇāsaḥ ǀ avadya-bhiyā́ ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ pṛṇanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not from the niggards-for they give not fireely-comes Meed at sacrifice, Gods’ satisfaction: Yea, many men with hands stretched out with Guerdon present their gifts because they dread dishonour.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Paṇis). What is Indralike, OSaramā? What is the appearance of him as whose messenger youhave come to this plural ce from afar? (They then say to one another:) Let her approach; let us make friends withher, and let her be the lord of our cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Not from the niggards-for they give not fireely-comes Meed at sacrifice, Gods’ satisfaction: Yea, many men with hands stretched out with Guerdon present their gifts because they dread dishonour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शतधारं वायुमर्कं स्वर्विदं नृचक्षसस्ते अभि चक्षते हविः ।ये पृणंति प्र च यच्छंति संगमे ते दक्षिणां दुहते सप्तमातरं ॥
verses.transliteration: śatá-dhāram ǀ vāyúm ǀ arkám ǀ svaḥ-vídam ǀ nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǀ té ǀ abhí ǀ cakṣate ǀ havíḥ ǀyé ǀ pṛṇánti ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ yácchanti ǀ sam-gamé ǀ té ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ duhate ǀ saptá-mātaram ǁ
verses.english_translation: These who observe mankind regard oblation as streamy Vāyu and light-finding Arka. They satisfy and give their gifts in synod, and pour in streams the seven-mothered Guerdon.
verses.wilson_translation: (Saramā). I do not believe that he can be subdued; he as whose messenger I have come to thisplace from afar subdues (his enemies). The deep rivers do not conceal him; you,Paṇis, slain by Indra, will sleep(in death).
verses.griffith_verse: These who observe mankind regard oblation as streamy Vāyu and light-finding Arka. They satisfy and give their gifts in synod, and pour in streams the seven-mothered Guerdon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दक्षिणावान्प्रथमो हूत एति दक्षिणावान्ग्रामणीरग्रमेति ।तमेव मन्ये नृपतिं जनानां यः प्रथमो दक्षिणामाविवाय ॥
verses.transliteration: dákṣiṇā-vān ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ eti ǀ dákṣiṇā-vān ǀ grāma-nī́ḥ ǀ ágram ǀ eti ǀtám ǀ evá ǀ manye ǀ nṛ-pátim ǀ jánānām ǀ yáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ ā-vivā́ya ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who brings Guerdon comes as first invited: chief of the hamlet comes the Guerdon-bearer. Him I account the ruler of the people who was the first to introduce the Guerdon.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Paṇis). These are the cows which you, auspicious Saramā, coming to the extremities of thesky, demand. Who will give them up to you without a combat? And our weapons are sharp.
verses.griffith_verse: He who brings Guerdon comes as first invited: chief of the hamlet comes the Guerdon-bearer. Him I account the ruler of the people who was the first to introduce the Guerdon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमेव ऋषिं तमु ब्रह्माणमाहुर्यज्ञन्यं सामगामुक्थशासं ।स शुक्रस्य तन्वो वेद ति��्रो यः प्रथमो दक्षिणया रराध ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ evá ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ yajña-nyám ǀ sāma-gā́m ǀ uktha-śásam ǀsáḥ ǀ śukrásya ǀ tanváḥ ǀ veda ǀ tisráḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ dákṣiṇayā ǀ rarā́dha ǁ
verses.english_translation: They call him Ṛṣi, Brahman, Sāma-chanter, reciter of the laud, leader of worship. The brightly-shining God's three forms he knoweth who first bestowed the sacrificial Guerdon.
verses.wilson_translation: (Saramā). Your words,Paṇis, are not in the plural ce of armies; your sinful bodies will not be equal toarrows. Let your path be difficult to follow, let Bṛhaspatishow no favour to either (your words or your person ns).
verses.griffith_verse: They call him Ṛṣi, Brahman, Sāma-chanter, reciter of the laud, leader of worship. The brightly-shining God's three forms he knoweth who first bestowed the sacrificial Guerdon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दक्षिणाश्वं दक्षिणा गां ददाति दक्षिणा चंद्रमुत यद्धिरण्यं ।दक्षिणान्नं वनुते यो न आत्मा दक्षिणां वर्म कृणुते विजानन् ॥
verses.transliteration: dákṣiṇā ǀ áśvam ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ gā́m ǀ dadāti ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ candrám ǀ utá ǀ yát ǀ híraṇyam ǀdákṣiṇā ǀ ánnam ǀ vanute ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ātmā́ ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ várma ǀ kṛṇute ǀ vi-jānán ǁ
verses.english_translation: Guerdon bestows the horse, bestows the bullock, Guerdon bestows, moreover, gold that Rsisters. Guerdon gives food which is our life and spirit. He who is wise takes Guerdon for his armour.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Paṇis). This treasure,Saramā, secured in the mountain is composed of cows, horses andriches; the Paṇis protect it who are good watchers; you have come to this lonely spot in vain.
verses.griffith_verse: Guerdon bestows the horse, bestows the bullock, Guerdon bestows, moreover, gold that Rsisters. Guerdon gives food which is our life and spirit. He who is wise takes Guerdon for his armour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न भोजा मम्रुर्न न्यर्थमीयुर्न रिष्यंति न व्यथंते ह भोजाः ।इदं यद्विश्वं भुवनं स्वश्चैतत्सर्वं दक्षिणैभ्यो ददाति ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ mamruḥ ǀ ná ǀ ni-arthám ǀ īyuḥ ǀ ná ǀ riṣyanti ǀ ná ǀ vyathante ǀ ha ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀidám ǀ yát ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ sváḥ ǀ ca ǀ etát ǀ sárvam ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ dadāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble. The light of heaven, the universe about us,—all this doth sacrificial Guerdon give them.
verses.wilson_translation: (Saramā). Excited by the Soma, the Ṛṣis, the Aṅgirasasof the nine months' rite, headed by Ayasya,will come here; they will partition this herd of cattle, then the Paṇiswill retract their words.
verses.griffith_verse: The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble. The light of heaven, the universe about us,—all this doth sacrificial Guerdon give them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भोजा जिग्युः सुरभिं योनिमग्रे भोजा जिग्युर्वध्वं या सुवासाः ।भोजा जिग्युरंतःपेयं सुराया भोजा जिग्युर्ये अहूताः प्रयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ surabhím ǀ yónim ǀ ágre ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ vadhvám ǀ yā́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǀbhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ antaḥ-péyam ǀ súrāyāḥ ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ yé ǀ áhūtāḥ ǀ pra-yánti ǁ
verses.english_translation: First have the liberal gained a fragrant dwelling, and got themselves a bride in fair apparel. The liberal have obtained their draught of liquor, and conquered those who, unprovoked, assailed them.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Paṇis). You have indeed come here,Saramā, constrained by divine power; we will make youour sister, do not return, we will share the cattle with you auspicious one.
verses.griffith_verse: First have the liberal gained a fragrant dwelling, and got themselves a bride in fair apparel. The liberal have obtained their draught of liquor, and conquered those who, unprovoked, assailed them.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भोजायाश्वं सं मृजंत्याशुं भोजायास्ते कन्या शुंभमाना ।भोजस्येदं पुष्करिणीव वेश्म परिष्कृतं देवमानेव चित्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: bhojā́ya ǀ áśvam ǀ sám ǀ mṛjanti ǀ āśúm ǀ bhojā́ya ǀ āste ǀ kanyā́ ǀ śúmbhamānā ǀbhojásya ǀ idám ǀ puṣkaríṇī-iva ǀ véśma ǀ pári-kṛtam ǀ devamānā́-iva ǀ citrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: They deck the fleet steed for the bounteous giver: the maid adorns herself and waits to meet him. His home is like a lake with lotus blossoms, like the Gods’ palaces adorned and splendid.
verses.wilson_translation: (Saramā). I recognize not fraternity nor sisterhood;Indraand the terrible Aṅgirasasknow (mykindred); my (masters) desiring the cattle overshadowed (yoru habitation) when I came; depart hence,Paṇisto adistant (spot).
verses.griffith_verse: They deck the fleet steed for the bounteous giver: the maid adorns herself and waits to meet him. His home is like a lake with lotus blossoms, like the Gods’ palaces adorned and splendid.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भोजमश्वाः सुष्ठुवाहो वहंति सुवृद्रथो वर्तते दक्षिणायाः ।भोजं देवासोऽवता भरेषु भोजः शत्रून्त्समनीकेषु जेता ॥
verses.transliteration: bhojám ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ suṣṭhu-vā́haḥ ǀ vahanti ǀ su-vṛ́t ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vartate ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀbhojám ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ avata ǀ bháreṣu ǀ bhojáḥ ǀ śátrūn ǀ sam-anīkéṣu ǀ jétā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Steeds good at draught convey the liberal giver, and lightly rolling moves the car of Guerdon. Assist, ye Gods, the liberal man in battles: the liberal giver conquers foes in combat.
verses.wilson_translation: Go hence,Paṇis, to a far-off distant (spot), let the cattle come forth in due order bursting through (thedoor) the concealed cattle which Bṛhaspati, the Soma, the grinding stones and the wise Ṛṣis have found.
verses.griffith_verse: Steeds good at draught convey the liberal giver, and lightly rolling moves the car of Guerdon. Assist, ye Gods, the liberal man in battles: the liberal giver conquers foes in combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CVIII. Saramā. Paṇis.
hymns.anukramani: ११ पणयोऽसुराः। सरमा देवता। २,४,६,८,१०-११ सरमा देवशुनी ऋषिका। पणयो देवता। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WHAT wish of Saramā hath brought her hither? The path leads far away to distant places.What charge hast thou for us? Where turns thy journey? How hast thou made thy way o’er Rasā's waters. I come appointed messenger of Indra, seeking your ample stores of wealth, O Paṇis.This hath preserved me from the fear of crossing: thus have I made my way o’er Rasā's waters. What is that Indra like, what is his aspect whose envoy, Saramā, from afar thou comest?Let him approach, and we will show him friendship: he shall be made the herdsman of our cattle. I know him safe from harm: but he can punish who sent me hither from afar as envoy.Him rivers flowing with deep waters bide not. Low will ye be, O Paṇis, slain by Indra. These are the kine which, Saramā, thou seekest, flying, O Blest One, to the ends of heaven.Who will loose these for thee without a battle? Yea, and sharp-pointed are our warlike weapons. Even if your wicked bodies, O ye Paṇis, were arrow-proof, your words are weak for wounding;And were the path to you as yet unmastered, Bṛhaspati in neither case will spare you. Paved with the rock is this our treasure-chamber; filled full of precious things, of kine, and horses.These Paṇis who are watchful keepers guard it. In vain hast thou approached this lonely station. Ṛṣis will come inspirited with Soma, Aṅgirases unwearied, and Navagvas.This stall of cattle will they part among them: then will the Paṇis wish these words unspoken. Even thus, O Saramā, hast thou come hither, forced by celestial might to make the journey.Turn thee not back, for thou shalt be our sister: O Blest One, we will give thee of the cattle. Brotherhood, sisterhood, I know not either: the dread Aṅgirases and Indra know them.They seemed to long for kine when I departed. Hence, into distance, be ye gone, O Paṇis. Hence, far away, ye Paṇis! Let the cattle lowing come forth as holy Law commandeth,Kine which Bṛhaspati, and Soma, Ṛṣis, sages, and pressing-stones have found when hidden.

verses.sanskrit: किमिच्छंती सरमा प्रेदमानड्दूरे ह्यध्वा जगुरिः पराचैः ।कास्मेहितिः का परितक्म्यासीत्कथं रसाया अतरः पयांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: kím ǀ icchántī ǀ sarámā ǀ prá ǀ idám ǀ ānaṭ ǀ dūré ǀ hí ǀ ádhvā ǀ jáguriḥ ǀ parācáiḥ ǀkā́ ǀ asmé-hitiḥ ǀ kā́ ǀ pári-takmyā ǀ āsīt ǀ kathám ǀ rasā́yāḥ ǀ ataraḥ ǀ páyāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: WHAT wish of Saramā hath brought her hither? The path leads far away to distant places. What charge hast thou for us? Where turns thy journey? How hast thou made thy way o’er Rasā's waters.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Paṇis). With what intention has Saramācome to this plural ce? Verily the way is long and difficultto be traversed by the person vering. What is the motive of your coming to us? What sort of wandering was yours?How have you crossed the waters of the Rasā?
verses.griffith_verse: WHAT wish of Saramā hath brought her hither? The path leads far away to distant places. What charge hast thou for us? Where turns thy journey? How hast thou made thy way o’er Rasā's waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्य दूतीरिषिता चरामि मह इच्छंती पणयो निधीन्वः ।अतिष्कदो भियसा तन्न आवत्तथा रसाया अतरं पयांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ iṣitā́ ǀ carāmi ǀ maháḥ ǀ icchántī ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ ni-dhī́n ǀ vaḥ ǀati-skádaḥ ǀ bhiyásā ǀ tám ǀ naḥ ǀ āvat ǀ táthā ǀ rasā́yāḥ ǀ ataram ǀ páyāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: I come appointed messenger of Indra, seeking your ample stores of wealth, O Paṇis. This hath preserved me from the fear of crossing: thus have I made my way o’er Rasā's waters.
verses.griffith_verse: I come appointed messenger of Indra, seeking your ample stores of wealth, O Paṇis. This hath preserved me from the fear of crossing: thus have I made my way o’er Rasā's waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कीदृङ्ङिंद्रः सरमे का दृशीका यस्येदं दूतीरसरः पराकात् ।आ च गच्छान्मित्रमेना दधामाथा गवां गोपतिर्नो भवाति ॥
verses.transliteration: kīdṛ́ṅ ǀ índraḥ ǀ sarame ǀ kā́ ǀ dṛśīkā́ ǀ yásya ǀ idám ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ ásaraḥ ǀ parākā́t ǀā́ ǀ ca ǀ gácchāt ǀ mitrám ǀ ena ǀ dadhāma ǀ átha ǀ gávām ǀ gó-patiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavāti ǁ
verses.english_translation: What is that Indra like, what is his aspect whose envoy, Saramā, from afar thou comest? Let him approach, and we will show him friendship: he shall be made the herdsman of our cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: What is that Indra like, what is his aspect whose envoy, Saramā, from afar thou comest? Let him approach, and we will show him friendship: he shall be made the herdsman of our cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाहं तं वेद दभ्यं दभत्स यस्येदं दूतीरसरं पराकात् ।न तं गूहंति स्रवतो गभीरा हता इंद्रेण पणयः शयध्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ tám ǀ veda ǀ dábhyam ǀ dábhat ǀ sáḥ ǀ yásya ǀ idám ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ ásaram ǀ parākā́t ǀná ǀ tám ǀ gūhanti ǀ sravátaḥ ǀ gabhīrā́ḥ ǀ hatā́ḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ śayadhve ǁ
verses.english_translation: I know him safe from harm: but he can punish who sent me hither from afar as envoy. Him rivers flowing with deep waters bide not. Low will ye be, O Paṇis, slain by Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: I know him safe from harm: but he can punish who sent me hither from afar as envoy. Him rivers flowing with deep waters bide not. Low will ye be, O Paṇis, slain by Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमा गावः सरमे या ऐच्छः परि दिवो अंतान्त्सुभगे पतंती ।कस्त एना अव सृजादयुध्व्युतास्माकमायुधा संति तिग्मा ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ sarame ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ áicchaḥ ǀ pári ǀ diváḥ ǀ ántān ǀ su-bhage ǀ pátantī ǀkáḥ ǀ te ǀ enāḥ ǀ áva ǀ sṛjāt ǀ áyudhvī ǀ utá ǀ asmā́kam ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ santi ǀ tigmā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These are the kine which, Saramā, thou seekest, flying, O Blest One, to the ends of heaven. Who will loose these for thee without a battle? Yea, and sharp-pointed are our warlike weapons.
verses.griffith_verse: These are the kine which, Saramā, thou seekest, flying, O Blest One, to the ends of heaven. Who will loose these for thee without a battle? Yea, and sharp-pointed are our warlike weapons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असेन्या वः पणयो वचांस्यनिषव्यास्तन्वः संतु पापीः ।अधृष्टो व एतवा अस्तु पंथा बृहस्पतिर्व उभया न मृळात् ॥
verses.transliteration: asenyā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ aniṣavyā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ santu ǀ pāpī́ḥ ǀádhṛṣṭaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ étavái ǀ astu ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ubhayā́ ǀ ná ǀ mṛḷāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even if your wicked bodies, O ye Paṇis, were arrow-proof, your words are weak for wounding; And were the path to you as yet unmastered, Bṛhaspati in neither case will spare you.
verses.griffith_verse: Even if your wicked bodies, O ye Paṇis, were arrow-proof, your words are weak for wounding; And were the path to you as yet unmastered, Bṛhaspati in neither case will spare you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयं निधिः सरमे अद्रिबुध्नो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्न्यृष्टः ।रक्षंति तं पणयो ये सुगोपा रेकु पदमलकमा जगंथ ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ ni-dhíḥ ǀ sarame ǀ ádri-budhnaḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvebhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ ní-ṛṣṭaḥ ǀrákṣanti ǀ tám ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ yé ǀ su-gopā́ḥ ǀ réku ǀ padám ǀ álakam ǀ ā́ ǀ jagantha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Paved with the rock is this our treasure-chamber; filled full of precious things, of kine, and horses. These Paṇis who are watchful keepers guard it. In vain hast thou approached this lonely station.
verses.griffith_verse: Paved with the rock is this our treasure-chamber; filled full of precious things, of kine, and horses. These Paṇis who are watchful keepers guard it. In vain hast thou approached this lonely station.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एह गमन्नृषयः सोमशिता अयास्यो अंगिरसो नवग्वाः ।त एतमूर्वं वि भजंत गोनामथैतद्वचः पणयो वमन्नित् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ gaman ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ sóma-śitāḥ ǀ ayā́syaḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ náva-gvāḥ ǀté ǀ etám ǀ ūrvám ǀ ví ǀ bhajanta ǀ gónām ǀ átha ǀ etát ǀ vácaḥ ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ váman ǀ ít ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ṛṣis will come inspirited with Soma, Aṅgirases unwearied, and Navagvas. This stall of cattle will they part among them: then will the Paṇis wish these words unspoken.
verses.griffith_verse: Ṛṣis will come inspirited with Soma, Aṅgirases unwearied, and Navagvas. This stall of cattle will they part among them: then will the Paṇis wish these words unspoken.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा च त्वं सरम आजगंथ प्रबाधिता सहसा दैव्येन ।स्वसारं त्वा कृणवै मा पुनर्गा अप ते गवां सुभगे भजाम ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ ca ǀ tvám ǀ sarame ǀ ā-jagántha ǀ prá-bādhitā ǀ sáhasā ǀ dáivyena ǀsvásāram ǀ tvā ǀ kṛṇavai ǀ mā́ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ gāḥ ǀ ápa ǀ te ǀ gávām ǀ su-bhage ǀ bhajāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even thus, O Saramā, hast thou come hither, forced by celestial might to make the journey. Turn thee not back, for thou shalt be our sister: O Blest One, we will give thee of the cattle.
verses.griffith_verse: Even thus, O Saramā, hast thou come hither, forced by celestial might to make the journey. Turn thee not back, for thou shalt be our sister: O Blest One, we will give thee of the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाहं वेद भ्रातृत्वं नो स्वसृत्वमिंद्रो विदुरंगिरसश्च घोराः ।गोकामा मे अच्छदयन्यदायमपात इत पणयो वरीयः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ veda ǀ bhrātṛ-tvám ǀ nó íti ǀ svasṛ-tvám ǀ índraḥ ǀ viduḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ghorā́ḥ ǀgó-kāmāḥ ǀ me ǀ acchadayan ǀ yát ǀ ā́yam ǀ ápa ǀ átaḥ ǀ ita ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ várīyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brotherhood, sisterhood, I know not either: the dread Aṅgirases and Indra know them. They seemed to long for kine when I departed. Hence, into distance, be ye gone, O Paṇis.
verses.griffith_verse: Brotherhood, sisterhood, I know not either: the dread Aṅgirases and Indra know them. They seemed to long for kine when I departed. Hence, into distance, be ye gone, O Paṇis.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दूरमित पणयो वरीय उद्गावो यंतु मिनतीर्ऋतेन ।बृहस्पतिर्या अविंदन्निगूळ्हाः सोमो ग्रावाण ऋषयश्च विप्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: dūrám ǀ ita ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ út ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ minatī́ḥ ǀ ṛténa ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ávindat ǀ ní-gūḷhāḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víprāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hence, far away, ye Paṇis! Let the cattle lowing come forth as holy Law commandeth, Kine which Bṛhaspati, and Soma, Ṛṣis, sages, and pressing-stones have found when hidden.
verses.griffith_verse: Hence, far away, ye Paṇis! Let the cattle lowing come forth as holy Law commandeth, Kine which Bṛhaspati, and Soma, Ṛṣis, sages, and pressing-stones have found when hidden.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CIX. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: ७ जुहूर्ब्रह्मजाया, ब्राह्मः ऊर्ध्वनाभा वा।विश्वेदेवाः। त्रिष्टुप् , ६-७ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Mātariśvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Bliss-bestower.And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman. King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort.Mitra and Varuṇa were the inviters: Agni as Hota; took her hand and led her. The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort.She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded. Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven Ṛṣis who sate them down to their austere devotion:Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion. The Brahmacari goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods’ own body.Through him Bṛhaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma. So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again.The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife, Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods’ aid, from sin,They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.

verses.sanskrit: तेऽवदन्प्रथमा ब्रह्मकिल्बिषेऽकूपारः सलिलो मातरिश्वा ।वीळुहरास्तप उग्रो मयोभूरापो देवीः प्रथमजा ऋतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ avadan ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ brahma-kilbiṣé ǀ ákūpāraḥ ǀ saliláḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀvīḷú-harāḥ ǀ tápaḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛténa ǁ
verses.english_translation: THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Mātariśvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Bliss-bestower. And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman.
verses.wilson_translation: These spoke first about Brahmā's sin, the boundless (sun), the water- god (Varuṇa), the wind-god(Vāyu), the fierce, wide-consuming fire, the source of happiness, (Soma), the divine waters, the first-born sonsof the truthful (Brahmā).
verses.griffith_verse: THESE first, the boundless Sea, and Mātariśvan, fierce-glowing Fire, the Strong, the Bliss-bestower. And heavenly Floods, first-born by holy Order, exclaimed against the outrage on a Brahman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमो राजा प्रथमो ब्रह्मजायां पुनः प्रायच्छदहृणीयमानः ।अन्वर्तिता वरुणो मित्र आसीदग्निर्होता हस्तगृह्या निनाय ॥
verses.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ púnaríti ǀ prá ǀ ayacchat ǀ áhṛṇīyamāna�� ǀanu-artitā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ hasta-gṛ́hya ǀ ā́ ǀ nināya ǁ
verses.english_translation: King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort. Mitra and Varuṇa were the inviters: Agni as Hota; took her hand and led her.
verses.wilson_translation: First, the royal Soma, without being ashamed, restored Brahmā's wife (to Bṛhaspati),Varuṇawasthe inviter, and Mitra,Agnias the ministrant priest taking her by thehand, led her (to her husband).
verses.griffith_verse: King Soma first of all, without reluctance, made restitution of the Brahman's consort. Mitra and Varuṇa were the inviters: Agni as Hota; took her hand and led her.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हस्तेनैव ग्राह्य आधिरस्या ब्रह्मजायेयमिति चेदवोचन् ।न दूताय प्रह्ये तस्थ एषा तथा राष्ट्रं गुपितं क्षत्रियस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: hástena ǀ evá ǀ grāhyáḥ ǀ ā-dhíḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́ ǀ iyám ǀ íti ǀ ca ǀ ít ǀ ávocan ǀná ǀ dūtā́ya ǀ pra-hyé ǀ tasthe ǀ eṣā́ ǀ táthā ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ gupitám ǀ kṣatríyasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort. She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded.
verses.wilson_translation: And (the gods) said (to Bṛhaspati), "This plural dge of hers is to be taken by thehand, this is the wife of Brahmā; she has not made herself known to the messenger sent (to seek her), so is the kingdom of a kṣatriyaprotected".
verses.griffith_verse: The man, her pledge, must by her hand be taken when they have cried, She is a Brahman's consort. She stayed not for a herald to conduct her: thus is the kingdom of a ruler guarded.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवा एतस्यामवदंत पूर्वे सप्तऋषयस्तपसे ये निषेदुः ।भीमा जाया ब्राह्मणस्योपनीता दुर्धां दधाति परमे व्योमन् ॥
verses.transliteration: devā́ḥ ǀ etásyām ǀ avadanta ǀ pū́rve ǀ sapta-ṛṣáyaḥ ǀ tápase ǀ yé ǀ ni-sedúḥ ǀbhīmā́ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ brāhmaṇásya ǀ úpa-nītā ǀ duḥ-dhā́m ǀ dadhāti ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven Ṛṣis who sate them down to their austere devotion: Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion.
verses.wilson_translation: The ancient deities spoke about her, the seven Ṛṣis who were engaged in penance. The terrible wifeof Brahmahas been brought back (to her husband); (penance) elevates into the highest heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus spake of her those Gods of old, Seven Ṛṣis who sate them down to their austere devotion: Dire is a Brahman's wife led home by others: in the supremest heaven she plants confusion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मचारी चरति वेविषद्विषः स देवानां भवत्येकमंगं ।तेन जायामन्वविंदद्बृहस्पतिः सोमेन नीतां जुह्वं न देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: brahma-cārī́ ǀ carati ǀ véviṣat ǀ víṣaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ bhavati ǀ ékam ǀ áṅgam ǀténa ǀ jāyā́m ǀ ánu ǀ avindat ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sómena ǀ nītā́m ǀ juhvám ǀ ná ǀ devāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Brahmacari goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods’ own body. Through him Bṛhaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: He leads the life of a Brahmacārin, even adoring all the gods; he becomes a portion of the gods;therefore,Bṛhaspatiobtained his wife (formerly) brought him by Soma, as the gods receive an offering.
verses.griffith_verse: The Brahmacari goes engaged in duty: he is a member of the Gods’ own body. Through him Bṛhaspati obtained his consort, as the Gods gained the ladle brought by Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्वै देवा अददुः पुनर्मनुष्या उत ।राजानः सत्यं कृण्वाना ब्रह्मजायां पुनर्ददुः ॥
verses.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ vái ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ adaduḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀrā́jānaḥ ǀ satyám ǀ kṛṇvānā́ḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ púnaḥ ǀ daduḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again. The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife,
verses.wilson_translation: The gods gave her back again, men also gave her back, and kings confirming (the gift) gave Brahmā's wife back again.
verses.griffith_verse: So then the Gods restored her, so men gave the woman back again. The Kings who kept their promises restored the Brahman's wedded wife,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्दाय ब्रह्मजायां कृत्वी देवैर्निकिल्बिषं ।ऊर्जं पृथिव्या भक्त्वायोरुगायमुपासते ॥
verses.transliteration: punaḥ-dā́ya ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ kṛtvī́ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ni-kilbiṣám ǀū́rjam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ bhaktvā́ya ǀ uru-gāyám ǀ úpa ǀ āsate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods’ aid, from sin, They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods having given back Brahmā's wife, and made her free from sin, having partaken of the foodof the earth, sat down to (the sacrifice of) the widely hymned Bṛhaspati.
verses.griffith_verse: Having restored the Brahman's wife, and freed them, with Gods’ aid, from sin, They shared the fulness of the earth, and won themselves extended sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CX. Āprīs.
hymns.anukramani: ११ जमदग्निर्भार्गवः, जामदग्न्यो रामो वा। आप्रीसूक्तं = (१ इध्मः समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा, २ तनूनपात् , ३ इळ:, ४ बर्हिः, ५ देवीर्द्वारः, ६ उषासानक्ता, ७ दैव्यौ होतारौ प्रचेतसौ, ८ त्रिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः, ९ त्वष्टा, १० वनस्पतिः, ११ स्वाहाकृतयः) । त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jātavedas.Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy. Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and waysof Order, make them pleasant.Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts ourhymns of praise and worship. Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus.Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods’ Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly. By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking.Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom. Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands.Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance. Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station,Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty. Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worshipAs singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction. Let Bhāratī come quickly to our worship, and Iḷā showing like a human being.So let Sarasvatī and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated. Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvaṣṭar, thou who knowest.Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature. Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season.Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter. Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods’ preceder.May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.

verses.sanskrit: समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान्यजसि जातवेदः ।आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वांत्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ deváḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ yajasi ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀā́ ǀ ca ǀ váha ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ tvám ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ asi ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jātavedas. Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy.
verses.wilson_translation: Kindled today,Jātavedas, in the dwelling of the worshipper, you who are divine, sacrifice to the godṣBear (the oblation), you who respect your friends, who are intelligent; you are the wise, far-seeing messenger (ofthe gods).
verses.griffith_verse: THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jātavedas. Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त्स्वदया सुजिह्व ।मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधंदेवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥
verses.transliteration: tánū-napāt ǀ patháḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yā́nān ǀ mádhvā ǀ sam-añján ǀ svadaya ǀ su-jihva ǀmánmāni ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ utá ǀ yajñám ǀ ṛndhán ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ ca ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ adhvarám ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and waysof Order, make them pleasant. Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts ourhymns of praise and worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Pure-tongued Tanūnapāt, flavour the paths of the sacrifice which lead (to success), moisteningthem with the sweet (Soma); elevating our praises and our rite by understanding, convey our sacrifice to thegods.
verses.griffith_verse: Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and waysof Order, make them pleasant. Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts ourhymns of praise and worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आजुह्वान ईड्यो वंद्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ।त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान्यक्षीषितो यजीयान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-júhvānaḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ vándyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ agne ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀtvám ǀ devā́nām ǀ asi ǀ yahva ǀ hótā ǀ sáḥ ǀ enān ǀ yakṣi ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yájīyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus. Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods’ Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are the invoker (of the gods), and are to be solicited and praised, come, being propitiated,along with the Vasus; you, O mighty (Agni), are the invoker of the gods; do you, who are most entitled to worship,solicited by us, offer them adoration.
verses.griffith_verse: Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus. Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods’ Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यते अग्रे अह्नां ।व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितये स्योनं ॥
verses.transliteration: prācī́nam ǀ barhíḥ ǀ pra-díśā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ vṛjyate ǀ ágre ǀ áhnām ǀví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prathate ǀ vi-tarám ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ áditaye ǀ syonám ǁ
verses.english_translation: By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking. Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.
verses.wilson_translation: In the beginning of the day the sacred grass, pointing eastwards, is strewn with the prescribed (text)as a covering for the earth (of the altar); they spread it out far and wide as a plural asant (seat) for the gods and Aditi.
verses.griffith_verse: By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking. Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः ।देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥
verses.transliteration: vyácasvatīḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ śrayantām ǀ páti-bhyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ śúmbhamānāḥ ǀdévīḥ ǀ dvāraḥ ǀ bṛhatīḥ ǀ viśvam-invāḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ bhavata ǀ supra-ayanā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands. Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance.
verses.wilson_translation: Expanding wide, let the doors give access as gracefully decorated wives give access to theirhusbands, divine doors, spacious and admitting all, be easy of entry for the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands. Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ सुष्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ susváyantī íti ǀ yajaté íti ǀ úpāke íti ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ sadatām ǀ ní ǀ yónau ǀdivyé íti ǀ yóṣaṇe íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ surukmé íti su-rukmé ǀ ádhi ǀ śríyam ǀ śukra-píśam ǀ dádhāne íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station, Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.
verses.wilson_translation: May the adorable Day and Night, the givers of sound repose, having approached, sit down in theplace (of sacrifice), two divine feminine les, majestic and richly ornamented, bearing beauty of a bright form.
verses.griffith_verse: Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station, Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता ॥
verses.transliteration: dáivyā ǀ hótārā ǀ prathamā́ ǀ su-vā́cā ǀ mímānā ǀ yajñám ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ yájadhyai ǀpra-codáyantā ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ kārū́ íti ǀ prācī́nam ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pra-díśā ǀ diśántā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction.
verses.wilson_translation: Divine ministers, prior (to those of earth), repeaters of pious praise, instrumental tuting the sacrifice at whichmen are to worship, (sit down) stimulating (the priests) at the sacrifices, makers (of praises), indicating theeastern fire with the prescribed (text).
verses.griffith_verse: Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयंती ।तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ bhā́ratī ǀ tū́yam ǀ etu ǀ íḷā ǀ manuṣvát ǀ ihá ǀ cetáyantī ǀtisráḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ idám ǀ syonám ǀ sárasvatī ǀ su-ápasaḥ ǀ sadantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Bhāratī come quickly to our worship, and Iḷā showing like a human being. So let Sarasvatī and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.
verses.wilson_translation: May Bhāratīcome quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḷā thinking (of what she has to do), like a humanbeing; may Sarasvatīalso-- the three gracious goddesses, sit down upon this plural asant sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Let Bhāratī come quickly to our worship, and Iḷā showing like a human being. So let Sarasvatī and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयांदेवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imé íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ jánitrī íti ǀ rūpáiḥ ǀ ápiṃśat ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀtám ǀ adyá ǀ hotaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yájīyān ǀ devám ǀ tváṣṭāram ǀ ihá ǀ yakṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvaṣṭar, thou who knowest. Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.
verses.wilson_translation: To the divine Tvaṣṭā, who decked the parental heaven and earth and all the worlds with livingforms, to him, O priest, who are venerable and wise, being solicited byu us, offer oblation here today.
verses.griffith_verse: Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvaṣṭar, thou who knowest. Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उपावसृज त्मन्या समंजंदेवानां पाथ ऋतुथा हवींषि ।वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदंतु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन ॥
verses.transliteration: upa-ávasṛja ǀ tmányā ǀ sam-añján ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀvánaspátiḥ ǀ śamitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ svádantu ǀ havyám ǀ mádhunā ǀ ghṛténa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season. Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer of your own will in due season the food (and other) oblations of the gods besmearing it. Let Vanaspati,Śamitā, the divine Agni, sweeten the oblation with honey and butter.
verses.griffith_verse: Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season. Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः ।अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sadyáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ ví ǀ amimīta ǀ yajñám ǀ agníḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ abhavat ǀ puraḥ-gā́ḥ ǀasyá ǀ hótuḥ ǀ pra-díśi ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vācí ǀ svā́hā-kṛtam ǀ havíḥ ǀ adantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods’ preceder. May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as he was born,Agniconstructed a sacrifice, he was the preceder of the gods; may the godspartake of the oblation presented with thesvāhāthrough the voice of him thehotāof the sacrifice at theeastern station.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods’ preceder. May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings.Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent. The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's OffipringWith mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions. Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Sūrya.He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken. Praised by Aṅgirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monsterFull many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation. The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Śuṣṇa.The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar. The Vṛtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vṛtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty,Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent. When the Dawns come attendant upon Sūrya their rays discover wealth of divers colours.The Star of heaven is seen as ’twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth. Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them.Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre? Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion,Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting. Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them.Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.

verses.sanskrit: मनीषिणः प्र भरध्वं मनीषां यथायथा मतयः संति नृणां ।इंद्रं सत्यैरेरयामा कृतेभिः स हि वीरो गिर्वणस्युर्विदानः ॥
verses.transliteration: mánīṣiṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ bharadhvam ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ yáthā-yathā ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ sánti ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀíndram ǀ satyáiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayāma ǀ kṛtébhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ vīráḥ ǀ girvaṇasyúḥ ǀ vídānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings. Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent.
verses.wilson_translation: Offer, worshippers, to Indrapraise agreeable to the thoughts of men; let us incite Indra hither withsincere adoration, for he, the hero, capable (of granting our wishes, is desirous of laudation.
verses.griffith_verse: BRING forth your sacred song ye prudent singers, even as are the thoughts of human beings. Let us draw Indra with true deeds anear us: he loves our songs, the Hero, and is potent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतस्य हि सदसो धीतिरद्यौत्सं गार्ष्टेयो वृषभो गोभिरानट् ।उदतिष्ठत्तविषेणा रवेण महांति चित्सं विव्याचा रजांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ ádyaut ǀ sám ǀ gārṣṭeyáḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ ānaṭ ǀút ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ taviṣéṇa ǀ ráveṇa ǀ mahā́nti ǀ cit ǀ sám ǀ vivyāca ǀ rájāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's Offipring With mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions.
verses.wilson_translation: Sustainer of the abode of the water, (the firmament), he shone brightly; the bull, the offspring of a cowwhich has only borne once, met the cows, with a loud roar he sprung up, he pervaded the vast worlds.
