verses.griffith_verse: The hymn shone brightly from the seat of worship: to the kine came the Bull, the Heifer's Offipring With mighty bellowing hath he arisen, and hath pervaded even the spacious regions.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद स हि जिष्णुः पथिकृत्सूर्याय ।आन्मेनां कृण्वन्नच्युतो भुवद्गोः पतिर्दिवः सनजा अप्रतीतः ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ kíla ǀ śrútyai ǀ asyá ǀ veda ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ jiṣṇúḥ ǀ pathi-kṛ́t ǀ sū́ryāya ǀā́t ǀ ménām ǀ kṛṇván ǀ ácyutaḥ ǀ bhúvat ǀ góḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ sana-jā́ḥ ǀ áprati-itaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Sūrya. He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken.
verses.wilson_translation: On hearing our praise Indraknows our wishes; victorious, he opens a path for the sun; making himself Menā, he came (to the sacrifice), he was unassailable, the lord of cattle, (the lord) of heaven, eternal,unsurpassed.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra knows, verily, how to hear our singing, for he, victorious, made a path for Sūrya. He made the Cow, and be became the Sovran of Heaven, primeval, matchless, and unshaken.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो मह्ना महतो अर्णवस्य व्रतामिनादंगिरोभिर्गृणानः ।पुरूणि चिन्नि तताना रजांसि दाधार यो धरुणं सत्यताता ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ arṇavásya ǀ vratā́ ǀ amināt ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀpurū́ṇi ǀ cit ǀ ní ǀ tatāna ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ yáḥ ǀ dharúṇam ǀ satyá-tātā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised by Aṅgirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monster Full many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation.
verses.wilson_translation: Praised by the Aṅgirasas,Indrahas by his might injured the functions of the mighty cloud; he has sentdown abundant rains, he who (at other times) has supported the supporting (cloud) in heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised by Aṅgirases, Indra demolished with might the works of the great watery monster Full many regions, too, hath he pervaded, and by his truth supported earth's foundation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रो दिवः प्रतिमानं पृथिव्या विश्वा वेद सवना हंति शुष्णं ।महीं चिद्द्यामातनोत्सूर्येण चास्कंभ चित्कंभनेन स्कभीयान् ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ veda ǀ sávanā ǀ hánti ǀ śúṣṇam ǀmahī́m ǀ cit ǀ dyā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ atanot ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ cāskámbha ǀ cit ǀ skámbhanena ǀ skábhīyān ǁ
verses.english_translation: The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Śuṣṇa. The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the counterpart of heaven and earth, is cognizant of all sacrifices, he is the slayer ofŚuṣṇa; hespread out the spacious heaven with the sun (to light it up); best of proppers, he propped up (the heaven) with aprop.
verses.griffith_verse: The counterpart of heaven and earth is Indra: he knoweth all libations, slayeth Śuṣṇa. The vast sky with the Sun hath he extended, and, best otpillars, stayed it with a pillar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वज्रेण हि वृत्रहा वृत्रमस्तरदेवस्य शूशुवानस्य मायाः ।वि धृष्णो अत्र धृषता जघंथाथाभवो मघवन्बाह्वोजाः ॥
verses.transliteration: vájreṇa ǀ hí ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ástaḥ ǀ ádevasya ǀ śū́śuvānasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀví ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ átra ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ jaghantha ǀ átha ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ bāhú-ojāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Vṛtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vṛtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty, Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent.
verses.wilson_translation: The slayer of Vṛtra, you have laid him low with the thunderbolt; resolute Indra, you have nowovercome by your powerful (bolt), the devices of the impious (asura), confiding in his own strength; you,Maghavan, were strong-armed.
verses.griffith_verse: The Vṛtra-slaver with his bolt felled Vṛtra: the magic of the godless, waxen mighty, Here hast thou, Bold Assailant, boldly conquered. Yea, then thine arms, O Maghavan, were potent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सचंत यदुषसः सूर्येण चित्रामस्य केतवो रामविंदन् ।आ यन्नक्षत्रं ददृशे दिवो न पुनर्यतो नकिरद्धा नु वेद ॥
verses.transliteration: sácanta ǀ yát ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ citrā́m ǀ asya ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ rā́m ǀ avindan ǀā́ ǀ yát ǀ nákṣatram ǀ dádṛśe ǀ diváḥ ǀ ná ǀ púnaḥ ǀ yatáḥ ǀ nákiḥ ǀ addhā́ ǀ nú ǀ veda ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the Dawns come attendant upon Sūrya their rays discover wealth of divers colours. The Star of heaven is seen as ’twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth.
verses.wilson_translation: When the dawns are associated with the sun, his rays acquire wonderful beauty; but when theconstellation of heaven is not seen, no one really knows (his rays) as he moves.
verses.griffith_verse: When the Dawns come attendant upon Sūrya their rays discover wealth of divers colours. The Star of heaven is seen as ’twere approaching: none knoweth aught of it as it departeth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दूरं किल प्रथमा जग्मुरासामिंद्रस्य याः प्रसवे सस्रुरापः ।क्व स्विदग्रं क्व बुध्न आसामापो मध्यं क्व वो नूनमंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: dūrám ǀ kíla ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ āsām ǀ índrasya ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ pra-savé ǀ sasrúḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀkvá ǀ svit ǀ ágram ǀ kvá ǀ budhnáḥ ǀ āsām ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ mádhyam ǀ kvá ǀ vaḥ ǀ nūnám ǀ ántaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them. Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre?
verses.wilson_translation: The first of those waters, which issued forth at Indra's sending, went very far. Where, waters, is yourbeginning, where your root, where is your centre, where indeed is your termination?
verses.griffith_verse: Far have they gone, the first of all these waters, the waters that flowed forth when Indra sent them. Where is their spring, and where is their foundation? Where now, ye Waters, is your inmost centre?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सृजः सिंधूँरहिना जग्रसानाँ आदिदेताः प्र विविज्रे जवेन ।मुमुक्षमाणा उत या मुमुच्रेऽधेदेता न रमंते नितिक्ताः ॥
verses.transliteration: sṛjáḥ ǀ síndhūn ǀ áhinā ǀ jagrasānā́n ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ etā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ vivijre ǀ javéna ǀmúmukṣamāṇāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ mumucré ǀ ádha ǀ ít ǀ etā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ ramante ǀ ní-tiktāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion, Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting.
verses.wilson_translation: You have set at liberty the streams which had been swallowed by Ahi; they rushed forth with rapidity;the waters which longed to be liberated were set free and now the pure (streams) never stop.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou didst free rivers swallowed by the Dragon; and rapidly they set themselves in motion, Those that were loosed and those that longed for freedom. Excited now to speed they run unresting.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सध्रीचीः सिंधुमुशतीरिवायन्त्सनाज्जार आरितः पूर्भिदासां ।अस्तमा ते पार्थिवा वसून्यस्मे जग्मुः सूनृता इंद्र पूर्वीः ॥
verses.transliteration: sadhrī́cīḥ ǀ síndhum ǀ uśatī́ḥ-iva ǀ āyan ǀ sanā́t ǀ jāráḥ ǀ āritáḥ ǀ pūḥ-bhít ǀ āsām ǀástam ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ pā́rthivā ǀ vásūni ǀ asmé íti ǀ jagmuḥ ǀ sūnṛ́tāḥ ǀ indra ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them. Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.
verses.wilson_translation: They hasten associated together to the ocean, like loving wives (to a husband); (Indra), the witherer offoes, the demolisher of cities, is their impeller of old; may our oblations, the treasures of earth, and our copiouspraises, proceed, Indra, to your dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: Yearning together they have sped to Sindhu: the Fort-destroyer, praised, of old, hath loved them. Indra, may thy terrestrial treasures reach us, and our full songs of joy approach thy dwelling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRINK of the juice, O Indra, at thy plea. sure, for thy first draught is early morn's libation.Rejoice, that thou mayst slay our foes, O Hero, and we with lauds will tell thy mighty exploits. Thou hast a car more swift than thought, O Indra; thercon come hither, come to drink the Soma.Let thy Bay Steeds, thy Stallions, hasten hither, with whom thou cornest nigh and art delighted. Deck out thy body with the fairest colours, with golden splendour of the Sun adorn it.O Indra, turn thee hitherward invited by us thy friends; be seated and be joyful. O thou whose grandeur in thy festive transports not even these two great worlds have comprehended.Come, Indra, with thy dear Bay Horses harnessed, come to our dwelling and the food thou lovest. Pressed for thy joyous banquet is the Soma, Soma whereof thou, Indra, ever drinking,Hast waged unequalled battles with thy foemen, which prompts the mighty flow of thine abundance. Found from of old is this thy cup, O Indra: Śatakratu, drink therefrom the Soma.Filled is the beaker with the meath that gladdens, the beaker which all Deities delight in. From many a side with proffered entertainment the folk are calling thee, O Mighty Indra.These our libations shall for thee be richest in sweet meath: dvink thereof and find them pleasant. I will declare thy deeds of old, O Indra, the mighty acts which thou hast first accomplished.In genuine wrath thou loosenedst the mountain so that the Brahman easily found the cattle. Lord of the hosts, amid our bands be seated: they call thee greatest Sage among the sages.Nothing is done, even far away, without thee: great, wondrous, Maghavan, is the hymn I sing thee. Aim of our eyes be thou, for we implore thee, O Maghavan, Friend of friends and Lord of treasures.Fight, Warrior strong in truth, fight thou the battle: give us our share of undivided riches.

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र पिब प्रतिकामं सुतस्य प्रातःसावस्तव हि पूर्वपीतिः ।हर्षस्व हंतवे शूर शत्रूनुक्थेभिष्टे वीर्या प्र ब्रवाम ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ píba ǀ prati-kāmám ǀ sutásya ǀ prātaḥ-sāváḥ ǀ táva ǀ hí ǀ pūrvá-pītiḥ ǀhárṣasva ǀ hántave ǀ śūra ǀ śátrūn ǀ ukthébhiḥ ǀ te ǀ vīryā́ ǀ prá ǀ bravāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: DRINK of the juice, O Indra, at thy plea. sure, for thy first draught is early morn's libation. Rejoice, that thou mayst slay our foes, O Hero, and we with lauds will tell thy mighty exploits.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indra, at will of the effused libation, for it is poured out at the morning sacrifice, and is first drunkby you; exult, hero, in slaying your foes, we will glorify your heroic exploits with hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: DRINK of the juice, O Indra, at thy plea. sure, for thy first draught is early morn's libation. Rejoice, that thou mayst slay our foes, O Hero, and we with lauds will tell thy mighty exploits.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्ते रथो मनसो जवीयानेंद्र तेन सोमपेयाय याहि ।तूयमा ते हरयः प्र द्रवंतु येभिर्यासि वृषभिर्मंदमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jávīyān ǀ ā́ ǀ indra ǀ téna ǀ soma-péyāya ǀ yāhi ǀtū́yam ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ prá ǀ dravantu ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ yā́si ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ mándamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou hast a car more swift than thought, O Indra; thercon come hither, come to drink the Soma. Let thy Bay Steeds, thy Stallions, hasten hither, with whom thou cornest nigh and art delighted.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Indra, to the Soma-drinking with your chariot, which is swifter than thought; let your bays, thevigorous steeds with which you go along rejoicing quickly, hasten hither.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou hast a car more swift than thought, O Indra; thercon come hither, come to drink the Soma. Let thy Bay Steeds, thy Stallions, hasten hither, with whom thou cornest nigh and art delighted.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हरित्वता वर्चसा सूर्यस्य श्रेष्ठै रूपैस्तन्वं स्पर्शयस्व ।अस्माभिरिंद्र सखिभिर्हुवानः सध्रीचीनो मादयस्वा निषद्य ॥
verses.transliteration: háritvatā ǀ várcasā ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ śréṣṭhaiḥ ǀ rūpáiḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ sparśayasva ǀasmā́bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ huvānáḥ ǀ sadhrīcīnáḥ ǀ mādayasva ǀ ni-sádya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Deck out thy body with the fairest colours, with golden splendour of the Sun adorn it. O Indra, turn thee hitherward invited by us thy friends; be seated and be joyful.
verses.wilson_translation: Decorate your person n with most beautiful forms with the golden radiance of the sun; invoked by usyour friends,Indra, sit down and be exhilarated, accompanied by the Maruts.
verses.griffith_verse: Deck out thy body with the fairest colours, with golden splendour of the Sun adorn it. O Indra, turn thee hitherward invited by us thy friends; be seated and be joyful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य त्यत्ते महिमानं मदेष्विमे मही रोदसी नाविविक्तां ।तदोक आ हरिभिरिंद्र युक्तैः प्रियेभिर्याहि प्रियमन्नमच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ tyát ǀ te ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ mádeṣu ǀ imé íti ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ná ǀ áviviktām ǀtát ǀ ókaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ yuktáiḥ ǀ priyébhiḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ priyám ǀ ánnam ǀ áccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: O thou whose grandeur in thy festive transports not even these two great worlds have comprehended. Come, Indra, with thy dear Bay Horses harnessed, come to our dwelling and the food thou lovest.
verses.wilson_translation: You whose greatness (manifested) in your exhilarations the vast heaven and earth, do not separate;come,Indra, with your beloved bay horses harnessed to your chariot, come to our dwelling to (partake of) the(sacrificial) food that is agreeable to you.
verses.griffith_verse: O thou whose grandeur in thy festive transports not even these two great worlds have comprehended. Come, Indra, with thy dear Bay Horses harnessed, come to our dwelling and the food thou lovest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्य शश्वत्पपिवाँ इंद्र शत्रूननानुकृत्या रण्या चकर्थ ।स ते पुरंधिं तविषीमियर्ति स ते मदाय सुत इंद्र सोमः ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ śáśvat ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ indra ǀ śátrūn ǀ ananu-kṛtyā́ ǀ ráṇyā ǀ cakártha ǀsáḥ ǀ te ǀ púram-dhim ǀ táviṣīm ǀ iyarti ǀ sáḥ ǀ te ǀ mádāya ǀ sutáḥ ǀ indra ǀ sómaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Pressed for thy joyous banquet is the Soma, Soma whereof thou, Indra, ever drinking, Hast waged unequalled battles with thy foemen, which prompts the mighty flow of thine abundance.
verses.wilson_translation: That Soma, drinking constantly of which,Indrayou have destroyed the enemies (of the worshipper)with an inimitable weapon-- that Soma prompts your powerful, abundant (laudation), it is effused Indra, for yourexhilaration.
verses.griffith_verse: Pressed for thy joyous banquet is the Soma, Soma whereof thou, Indra, ever drinking, Hast waged unequalled battles with thy foemen, which prompts the mighty flow of thine abundance.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं ते पात्रं सनवित्तमिंद्र पिबा सोममेना शतक्रतो ।पूर्ण आहावो मदिरस्य मध्वो यं विश्व इदभिहर्यंति देवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ te ǀ pā́tram ǀ sána-vittam ǀ indra ǀ píba ǀ sómam ǀ enā́ ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀpūrṇáḥ ǀ ā-hāváḥ ǀ madirásya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ yám ǀ víśve ǀ ít ǀ abhi-háryanti ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Found from of old is this thy cup, O Indra: Śatakratu, drink therefrom the Soma. Filled is the beaker with the meath that gladdens, the beaker which all Deities delight in.
verses.wilson_translation: This your cup,Indra, has been long since provided by us, drink the Somafrom it,Śatakratu; thegoblet is full of the sweet Soma, which all the gods desire.
verses.griffith_verse: Found from of old is this thy cup, O Indra: Śatakratu, drink therefrom the Soma. Filled is the beaker with the meath that gladdens, the beaker which all Deities delight in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि हि त्वामिंद्र पुरुधा जनासो हितप्रयसो वृषभ ह्वयंते ।अस्माकं ते मधुमत्तमानीमा भुवन्त्सवना तेषु हर्य ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ hí ǀ tvā́m ǀ indra ǀ purudhā́ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ hitá-prayasaḥ ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ hváyante ǀasmā́kam ǀ te ǀ mádhumat-tamāni ǀ imā́ ǀ bhuvan ǀ sávanā ǀ téṣu ǀ harya ǁ
verses.english_translation: From many a side with proffered entertainment the folk are calling thee, O Mighty Indra. These our libations shall for thee be richest in sweet meath: dvink thereof and find them pleasant.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, showerer of benefits, men in several plural ces, offering acceptable food, invoke you; these oursacrifices to you are most full of the sweet (Soma); take plural asure in them.
verses.griffith_verse: From many a side with proffered entertainment the folk are calling thee, O Mighty Indra. These our libations shall for thee be richest in sweet meath: dvink thereof and find them pleasant.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र त इंद्र पूर्व्याणि प्र नूनं वीर्या वोचं प्रथमा कृतानि ।सतीनमन्युरश्रथायो अद्रिं सुवेदनामकृणोर्ब्रह्मणे गां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ pūrvyā́ṇi ǀ prá ǀ nūnám ǀ vīryā́ ǀ vocam ǀ prathamā́ ǀ kṛtā́ni ǀsatīná-manyuḥ ǀ aśrathayaḥ ǀ ádrim ǀ su-vedanā́m ǀ akṛṇoḥ ǀ bráhmaṇe ǀ gā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: I will declare thy deeds of old, O Indra, the mighty acts which thou hast first accomplished. In genuine wrath thou loosenedst the mountain so that the Brahman easily found the cattle.
verses.wilson_translation: I will proclaim now,Indra, your ancient first-achieved exploits; resolved to sent rain, you did cleave thecloud, you made the cow easily discoverable for the Brāhmaṇa
verses.griffith_verse: I will declare thy deeds of old, O Indra, the mighty acts which thou hast first accomplished. In genuine wrath thou loosenedst the mountain so that the Brahman easily found the cattle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि षु सीद गणपते गणेषु त्वामाहुर्विप्रतमं कवीनां ।न ऋते त्वत्क्रियते किं चनारे महामर्कं मघवंचित्रमर्च ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ sú ǀ sīda ǀ gaṇa-pate ǀ gaṇéṣu ǀ tvā́m ǀ āhuḥ ǀ vípra-tamam ǀ kavīnā́m ǀná ǀ ṛté ǀ tvát ǀ kriyate ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ āré ǀ mahā́m ǀ arkám ǀ magha-van ǀ citrám ǀ arca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the hosts, amid our bands be seated: they call thee greatest Sage among the sages. Nothing is done, even far away, without thee: great, wondrous, Maghavan, is the hymn I sing thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of the companies (of the Maruts), sit down among the companies (of the worshippers), they callyou the most sage of sages; without you nothing is done in the distance; have in honour,Maghavan, our greatand various adoration. of wealth, (the wishes of) your friends; make war (for us), you warrior endowed with real strength, give us a sharein the undivided riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of the hosts, amid our bands be seated: they call thee greatest Sage among the sages. Nothing is done, even far away, without thee: great, wondrous, Maghavan, is the hymn I sing thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभिख्या नो मघवन्नाधमानान्त्सखे बोधि वसुपते सखीनां ।रणं कृधि रणकृत्सत्यशुष्माभक्ते चिदा भजा राये अस्मान् ॥
verses.transliteration: abhi-khyā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ nā́dhamānān ǀ sákhe ǀ bodhí ǀ vasu-pate ǀ sákhīnām ǀráṇam ǀ kṛdhi ǀ raṇa-kṛt ǀ satya-śuṣma ǀ ábhakte ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ bhaja ǀ rāyé ǀ asmā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aim of our eyes be thou, for we implore thee, O Maghavan, Friend of friends and Lord of treasures. Fight, Warrior strong in truth, fight thou the battle: give us our share of undivided riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Aim of our eyes be thou, for we implore thee, O Maghavan, Friend of friends and Lord of treasures. Fight, Warrior strong in truth, fight thou the battle: give us our share of undivided riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXTII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Heavens and the Earth accordant with all Gods encouraged graciously that vigorous might of his.When he came showing forth his majesty and power, he drank of Soma juice and waxed exceeding strong. This majesty of his Viṣṇu extols and lauds, making the stalCthat gives the meath flow forth with inight.When Indra Maghavan with those who followed him had smitten Vṛtra he deserved the choice of Gods. When, bearing warlike weapons, fain to win thee praise, thou mettest Vṛtra, yea, the Dragon, for the fight,Then all the Maruts who were gathered with dice there extolled, O Mighty One, thy powerful majesty. Soon as he sprang to life he forced asun. der hosts: forward the Hero looked to manly deed and war.He cleft the rock, he let concurrent streams flow forth, and with his skilful art stablished the heavens' wide vault. Indra hath evermore possessed surpassing power: he forced, far from each other, heaven and earth apart.He hurled impetuous down his iron thunderbolt, a joy to Varuṇa's and Mitra's worshipper. Then to the mighty powers of Indra, to his wrath, his the fierce Stormer, loud of voice, they came with speed;What time the Potent One rent Vṛtra with his strength, who held the waters back, whom darkness compassed round. Even in the first of those heroic acts which they who strove together came with might to execute,Deep darkness fell upon the slain, and Indra won by victory the right of being first invoked. Then all the Gods extolled, with eloquence inspired by draughts of Soma juice, thy deeds of manly might.As Agni eats the dry food with his tcetlv, he ate Vṛtra, the Dragon, maimed by Indra's deadly dart. Proclaim his many friendships, met with friendship, made with singers, with the skilful and the eloquent.Indra, when he subdues Dhuni and Cumuri, lists to Dabhīti for his faithful spirit's sake. Give riches manifold with noble horses, to be remembered while my songs address thee.May we by easy paths pass all our troubles: find us this day a ford wide and extensive.

verses.sanskrit: तमस्य द्यावापृथिवी सचेतसा विश्वेभिर्देवैरनु शुष्ममावतां ।यदैत्कृण्वानो महिमानमिंद्रियं पीत्वी सोमस्य क्रतुमाँ अवर्धत ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ asya ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ sá-cetasā ǀ víśvebhiḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ánu ǀ śúṣmam ǀ āvatām ǀyát ǀ áit ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ indriyám ǀ pītvī́ ǀ sómasya ǀ krátu-mān ǀ avardhata ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Heavens and the Earth accordant with all Gods encouraged graciously that vigorous might of his. When he came showing forth his majesty and power, he drank of Soma juice and waxed exceeding strong.
verses.wilson_translation: May the concurring heaven and earth, together with all the gods, preserve that strength of Indra,where by achieving (great deeds), he obtained the greatness that is appropriate to him, and having drunk the Soma, he, eminent for his prowess, increased (in strength).
verses.griffith_verse: THE Heavens and the Earth accordant with all Gods encouraged graciously that vigorous might of his. When he came showing forth his majesty and power, he drank of Soma juice and waxed exceeding strong.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तमस्य विष्णुर्महिमानमोजसांशुं दधन्वान्मधुनो वि रप्शते ।देवेभिरिंद्रो मघवा सयावभिर्वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अभवद्वरेण्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ asya ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ójasā ǀ aṃśúm ǀ dadhanvā́n ǀ mádhunaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rapśate ǀdevébhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sayā́va-bhiḥ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ jaghanvā́n ǀ abhavat ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This majesty of his Viṣṇu extols and lauds, making the stalCthat gives the meath flow forth with inight. When Indra Maghavan with those who followed him had smitten Vṛtra he deserved the choice of Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Viṣṇuoffering the portion of the Soma, glorified by his own vigour that greatness of his.Indra, thelord of wealth, with the associated gods having slain Vṛtra, became deserving of honour.
verses.griffith_verse: This majesty of his Viṣṇu extols and lauds, making the stalCthat gives the meath flow forth with inight. When Indra Maghavan with those who followed him had smitten Vṛtra he deserved the choice of Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृत्रेण यदहिना बिभ्रदायुधा समस्थिथा युधये शंसमाविदे ।विश्वे ते अत्र मरुतः सह त्मनावर्धन्नुग्र महिमानमिंद्रियं ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛtréṇa ǀ yát ǀ áhinā ǀ bíbhrat ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ sam-ásthithāḥ ǀ yudháye ǀ śáṃsam ǀ ā-víde ǀvíśve ǀ te ǀ átra ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sahá ǀ tmánā ǀ ávardhan ǀ ugra ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ indriyám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, bearing warlike weapons, fain to win thee praise, thou mettest Vṛtra, yea, the Dragon, for the fight, Then all the Maruts who were gathered with dice there extolled, O Mighty One, thy powerful majesty.
verses.wilson_translation: When you did encounter the indestructible Vṛtra, wielding your weapons for combat, you acquirerenown; all the associated Marutsof their own accord magnified your great might appropriate to Indra.
verses.griffith_verse: When, bearing warlike weapons, fain to win thee praise, thou mettest Vṛtra, yea, the Dragon, for the fight, Then all the Maruts who were gathered with dice there extolled, O Mighty One, thy powerful majesty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञान एव व्यबाधत स्पृधः प्रापश्यद्वीरो अभि पौंस्यं रणं ।अवृश्चदद्रिमव सस्यदः सृजदस्तभ्नान्नाकं स्वपस्यया पृथुं ॥
verses.transliteration: jajñānáḥ ǀ evá ǀ ví ǀ abādhata ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ apaśyat ǀ vīráḥ ǀ abhí ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ ráṇam ǀávṛścat ǀ ádrim ǀ áva ǀ sa-syádaḥ ǀ sṛjat ǀ ástabhnāt ǀ nā́kam ǀ su-apasyáyā ǀ pṛthúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soon as he sprang to life he forced asun. der hosts: forward the Hero looked to manly deed and war. He cleft the rock, he let concurrent streams flow forth, and with his skilful art stablished the heavens' wide vault.
verses.wilson_translation: As soon as born he discomfited his assailants; the hero contemplated his own manly prowess in war;he divided the cloud, sent forth the flowing waters, and with the determination to do a good deed, upheld the vastheaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Soon as he sprang to life he forced asun. der hosts: forward the Hero looked to manly deed and war. He cleft the rock, he let concurrent streams flow forth, and with his skilful art stablished the heavens' wide vault.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदिंद्रः सत्रा तविषीरपत्यत वरीयो द्यावापृथिवी अबाधत ।अवाभरद्धृषितो वज्रमायसं शेवं मित्राय वरुणाय दाशुषे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́t ǀ índraḥ ǀ satrā́ ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ apatyata ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ abādhata ǀáva ǀ abharat ǀ dhṛṣitáḥ ǀ vájram ǀ āyasám ǀ śévam ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ dāśúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra hath evermore possessed surpassing power: he forced, far from each other, heaven and earth apart. He hurled impetuous down his iron thunderbolt, a joy to Varuṇa's and Mitra's worshipper.
verses.wilson_translation: Indraadvanced with vast (armies); he overcame with his might (his foed stationed between) heavenand earth; confident, he wielded his metal thunderbolt (to do) good to Mitra,Varuṇa, and the donor (of theoblation). when fierce he cut Vṛtrato pieces by his strength-- (Vṛtra who) obstructed the waters, and was encompassed bydarkness.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra hath evermore possessed surpassing power: he forced, far from each other, heaven and earth apart. He hurled impetuous down his iron thunderbolt, a joy to Varuṇa's and Mitra's worshipper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्यात्र तविषीभ्यो विरप्शिन ऋघायतो अरंहयंत मन्यवे ।वृत्रं यदुग्रो व्यवृश्चदोजसापो बिभ्रतं तमसा परीवृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya ǀ átra ǀ táviṣībhyaḥ ǀ vi-rapśínaḥ ǀ ṛghāyatáḥ ǀ araṃhayanta ǀ manyáve ǀvṛtrám ǀ yát ǀ ugráḥ ǀ ví ǀ ávṛścat ǀ ójasā ǀ apáḥ ǀ bíbhratam ǀ támasā ǀ pári-vṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then to the mighty powers of Indra, to his wrath, his the fierce Stormer, loud of voice, they came with speed; What time the Potent One rent Vṛtra with his strength, who held the waters back, whom darkness compassed round.
verses.griffith_verse: Then to the mighty powers of Indra, to his wrath, his the fierce Stormer, loud of voice, they came with speed; What time the Potent One rent Vṛtra with his strength, who held the waters back, whom darkness compassed round.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या वीर्याणि प्रथमानि कर्त्वा महित्वेभिर्यतमानौ समीयतुः ।ध्वांतं तमोऽव दध्वसे हत इंद्रो मह्ना पूर्वहूतावपत्यत ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ kártvā ǀ mahi-tvébhiḥ ǀ yátamānau ǀ sam-īyátuḥ ǀdhvāntám ǀ támaḥ ǀ áva ǀ dadhvase ǀ haté ǀ índraḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ pūrvá-hūtau ǀ apatyata ǁ
verses.english_translation: Even in the first of those heroic acts which they who strove together came with might to execute, Deep darkness fell upon the slain, and Indra won by victory the right of being first invoked.
verses.wilson_translation: (In the midst of) the first exploits to be performed by them which (Indraand Vṛtra) achieved strivingwith their utmost might, Vṛtra being slain, the thick darkness was destroyed, and Indra in his might came at thefirst challenge.
verses.griffith_verse: Even in the first of those heroic acts which they who strove together came with might to execute, Deep darkness fell upon the slain, and Indra won by victory the right of being first invoked.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वे देवासो अध वृष्ण्यानि तेऽवर्धयन्त्सोमवत्या वचस्यया ।रद्धं वृत्रमहिमिंद्रस्य हन्मनाग्निर्न जंभैस्तृष्वन्नमावयत् ॥
verses.transliteration: víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ádha ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyāni ǀ te ǀ ávardhayan ǀ sóma-vatyā ǀ vacasyáyā ǀraddhám ǀ vṛtrám ǀ áhim ǀ índrasya ǀ hánmanā ǀ agníḥ ǀ ná ǀ jámbhaiḥ ǀ tṛṣú ǀ ánnam ǀ āvayat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then all the Gods extolled, with eloquence inspired by draughts of Soma juice, thy deeds of manly might. As Agni eats the dry food with his tcetlv, he ate Vṛtra, the Dragon, maimed by Indra's deadly dart.
verses.wilson_translation: Then all the gods magnified your exploits with praise, accompanied with libations of Soma; (andpeople) quickly devoured Vṛtra, the obstructer of water, wounded by Indra's slaughtering (weapon), as Agnidevours food with his teeth.
verses.griffith_verse: Then all the Gods extolled, with eloquence inspired by draughts of Soma juice, thy deeds of manly might. As Agni eats the dry food with his tcetlv, he ate Vṛtra, the Dragon, maimed by Indra's deadly dart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूरि दक्षेभिर्वचनेभिर्ऋक्वभिः सख्येभिः सख्यानि प्र वोचत ।इंद्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दंभयंछ्रद्धामनस्या शृणुते दभीतये ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́ri ǀ dákṣebhiḥ ǀ vacanébhiḥ ǀ ṛ́kva-bhiḥ ǀ sakhyébhiḥ ǀ sakhyā́ni ǀ prá ǀ vocata ǀíndraḥ ǀ dhúnim ǀ ca ǀ cúmurim ǀ ca ǀ dambháyan ǀ śraddhā-manasyā́ ǀ śṛṇute ǀ dabhī́taye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Proclaim his many friendships, met with friendship, made with singers, with the skilful and the eloquent. Indra, when he subdues Dhuni and Cumuri, lists to Dabhīti for his faithful spirit's sake.
verses.wilson_translation: Celebrate the numerous benevolent (acts of Indra) with clever affectionate praises, together with texts;for adoration.
verses.griffith_verse: Proclaim his many friendships, met with friendship, made with singers, with the skilful and the eloquent. Indra, when he subdues Dhuni and Cumuri, lists to Dabhīti for his faithful spirit's sake.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं पुरूण्या भरा स्वश्व्या येभिर्मंसै निवचनानि शंसन् ।सुगेभिर्विश्वा दुरिता तरेम विदो षु ण उर्विया गाधम��्य ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ purū́ṇi ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ su-áśvyā ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ máṃsai ǀ ni-vácanāni ǀ śáṃsan ǀsu-gébhiḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ tarema ǀ vidó íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ gādhám ǀ adyá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Give riches manifold with noble horses, to be remembered while my songs address thee. May we by easy paths pass all our troubles: find us this day a ford wide and extensive.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Indra, grant me ample riches and excellent horses with which I may honour (the gods)proffering praises; with well-acquired (riches) let us cross over all iniquity, accept our praise today with the mighṭto cross over with ease].
verses.griffith_verse: Give riches manifold with noble horses, to be remembered while my songs address thee. May we by easy paths pass all our troubles: find us this day a ford wide and extensive.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXIV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: १० वैरूपः सध्रिः, तापसो धर्मो वा। विश्वे देवाः।त्रिष्टुप्, ४ जगती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Two perfect springs of heat pervade the Threefold, and come for their delight is Mātariśvan.Craving the milk of heaven the Gods are present: well do they know the praisesong and the Sāman. The priests beard far away, as they are ordered, serve the three Nirrtis, for well they know them.Sages have traced the cause that first produced them, dwelling in distant and mysterious chambers. The Youthful One, well-shaped, with four locks braided, brightened with oil, puts on the ordinances.Two Birds of mighty power are seated near her, there where the Deities receive their portion. One of these Birds hath passed into the sea of air: thence he looks round and views this universal world.With simple heart I have beheld him from anear: his Mother kisses him and he returns her kiss. Him with fair wings though only One in nature, wise singers shape, with songs, in many figures.While they at sacrifices fix the metres, they measure out twelve chalices of Soma. While they arrange the four and six-and-thirty, and duly order, up to twelve, the measures,Having disposed the sacrifice thoughtful sages send the Car forward with the Rc and Sāman. The Chariot's majesties are fourteen others: seven sages lead it onward with their Voices.Who will declare to us the ford Apnana, the path whereby they drink first draughts of Soma? The fifteen lauds are in a thousand places that is as vast as heaven and earth in measure.A thousand spots contain the mighty thousand. Vāk spreadeth forth as far as Prayer extendeth. What sage hath learned the metres' application? Who hath gained Vāk, the spirit's aim and object?Which ministering priest is called eighth Hero? Who then hath tracked the two Bay Steeds of Indra? Yoked to his chariot-pole there stood the Coursers: they only travel round earth's farthest limits.These, when their driver in his home is settled, receive the allotted meed of their exertion.

verses.sanskrit: घर्मा समंता त्रिवृतं व्यापतुस्तयोर्जुष्टिं मातरिश्वा जगाम ।दिवस्पयो दिधिषाणा अवेषन्विदुर्देवाः सहसामानमर्कं ॥
verses.transliteration: gharmā́ ǀ sám-antā ǀ tri-vṛ́tam ǀ ví ǀ āpatuḥ ǀ táyoḥ ǀ júṣṭim ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ jagāma ǀdiváḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ dídhiṣāṇāḥ ǀ aveṣan ǀ vidúḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sahá-sāmānam ǀ arkám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Two perfect springs of heat pervade the Threefold, and come for their delight is Mātariśvan. Craving the milk of heaven the Gods are present: well do they know the praisesong and the Sāman.
verses.wilson_translation: The two sources of heat (AgniandĀditya) spreading to the limit (of the horizon), have pervaded thethreefold (universe);Mātariśvanhas come to give them plural asure; (when) the shining (rays) reached theadorable (sun), having the brilliancy of the Sāman, sustaining (the universe), they attained the water of heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: Two perfect springs of heat pervade the Threefold, and come for their delight is Mātariśvan. Craving the milk of heaven the Gods are present: well do they know the praisesong and the Sāman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो देष्ट्राय निर्ऋतीरुपासते दीर्घश्रुतो वि हि जानंति वह्नयः ।तासां नि चिक्युः कवयो निदानं परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: tisráḥ ǀ deṣṭrā́ya ǀ níḥ-ṛtīḥ ǀ úpa ǀ āsate ǀ dīrgha-śrútaḥ ǀ ví ǀ hí ǀ jānánti ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀtā́sām ǀ ní ǀ cikyuḥ ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ ni-dā́nam ǀ páreṣu ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ gúhyeṣu ǀ vratéṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: The priests beard far away, as they are ordered, serve the three Nirrtis, for well they know them. Sages have traced the cause that first produced them, dwelling in distant and mysterious chambers.
verses.wilson_translation: The three Nirṛtisdo obeisance for the gist (of oblations), for (the gods), the far-famed sustainers (ofthe universe), know (their obeisance); the wise have ascertained the primary cause of these (divinities) who(exist) in the conspicuous (or) in the hidden observances.
verses.griffith_verse: The priests beard far away, as they are ordered, serve the three Nirrtis, for well they know them. Sages have traced the cause that first produced them, dwelling in distant and mysterious chambers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते ।तस्यां सुपर्णा वृषणा नि षेदतुर्यत्र देवा दधिरे भागधेयं ॥
verses.transliteration: cátuḥ-kapardā ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ su-péśāḥ ǀ ghṛtá-pratīkā ǀ vayúnāni ǀ vaste ǀtásyām ǀ su-parṇā́ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ ní ǀ sedatuḥ ǀ yátra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dadhiré ǀ bhāga-dhéyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Youthful One, well-shaped, with four locks braided, brightened with oil, puts on the ordinances. Two Birds of mighty power are seated near her, there where the Deities receive their portion.
verses.wilson_translation: The quadrangular (altar) youthful, handsomely decorated, bright with oblation, clothes herself in piousrites; the two birds, the showerers of oblations, have sat down thereon where the gods receive their share.
verses.griffith_verse: The Youthful One, well-shaped, with four locks braided, brightened with oil, puts on the ordinances. Two Birds of mighty power are seated near her, there where the Deities receive their portion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एकः सुपर्णः स समुद्रमा विवेश स इदं विश्वं भुवनं वि चष्टे ।तं पाकेन मनसापश्यमंतितस्तं माता रेळ्हि स उ रेळ्हि मातरं ॥
verses.transliteration: ékaḥ ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǀ sáḥ ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ ví ǀ caṣṭe ǀtám ǀ pā́kena ǀ mánasā ǀ apaśyam ǀ ántitaḥ ǀ tám ǀ mātā́ ǀ reḷhi ǀ sáḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ reḷhi ǀ mātáram ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of these Birds hath passed into the sea of air: thence he looks round and views this universal world. With simple heart I have beheld him from anear: his Mother kisses him and he returns her kiss.
verses.wilson_translation: One of the birds has entered the firmament; he contemplates this whole world; with mind mature Ibeheld him night athand; him the mother licks, he licks themother.
verses.griffith_verse: One of these Birds hath passed into the sea of air: thence he looks round and views this universal world. With simple heart I have beheld him from anear: his Mother kisses him and he returns her kiss.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति ।छंदांसि च दधतो अध्वरेषु ग्रहान्त्सोमस्य मिमते द्वादश ॥
verses.transliteration: su-parṇám ǀ víprā ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ ékam ǀ sántam ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ kalpayanti ǀchándāṃsi ǀ ca ǀ dádhataḥ ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ gráhān ǀ sómasya ǀ mimate ǀ dvā́daśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Him with fair wings though only One in nature, wise singers shape, with songs, in many figures. While they at sacrifices fix the metres, they measure out twelve chalices of Soma.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise seers through their praise make into many forms the bird which is (only) one; and holding the(seven) metres at the sacrifices, they measure twelve bowls of Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Him with fair wings though only One in nature, wise singers shape, with songs, in many figures. While they at sacrifices fix the metres, they measure out twelve chalices of Soma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: षट्त्रिंशांश्च चतुरः कल्पयंतश्छंदांसि च दधत आद्वादशं ।यज्ञं विमाय कवयो मनीष ऋक्सामाभ्यां प्र रथं वर्तयंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ṣaṭ-triṃśā́n ǀ ca ǀ catúraḥ ǀ kalpáyantaḥ ǀ chándāṃsi ǀ ca ǀ dádhataḥ ǀ ā-dvādaśám ǀyajñám ǀ vi-mā́ya ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ manīṣā́ ǀ ṛk-sāmā́bhyām ǀ prá ǀ rátham ǀ vartayanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: While they arrange the four and six-and-thirty, and duly order, up to twelve, the measures, Having disposed the sacrifice thoughtful sages send the Car forward with the Rc and Sāman.
verses.wilson_translation: Filling thirty-six and four vessels, and holding the metres as far as twelve, measuring out the rite bytheir intelligence, the sages complete the sacrifice with the ṛk and thesāman.
verses.griffith_verse: While they arrange the four and six-and-thirty, and duly order, up to twelve, the measures, Having disposed the sacrifice thoughtful sages send the Car forward with the Rc and Sāman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्दशान्ये महिमानो अस्य तं धीरा वाचा प्र णयंति सप्त ।आप्नानं तीर्थं क इह प्र वोचद्येन पथा प्रपिबंते सुतस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: cátuḥ-daśa ǀ anyé ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ asya ǀ tám ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ vācā́ ǀ prá ǀ nayanti ǀ saptá ǀā́pnānam ǀ tīrthám ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ yéna ǀ pathā́ ǀ pra-píbante ǀ sutásya ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Chariot's majesties are fourteen others: seven sages lead it onward with their Voices. Who will declare to us the ford Apnana, the path whereby they drink first draughts of Soma?
verses.wilson_translation: There are fourteen other great developments of him, seven sages conduct him by prayer; who maydeclare the expanded plural ce of sanctity at this (rite), the path by which they drink of the libation.
verses.griffith_verse: The Chariot's majesties are fourteen others: seven sages lead it onward with their Voices. Who will declare to us the ford Apnana, the path whereby they drink first draughts of Soma?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रधा पंचदशान्युक्था यावद्द्यावापृथिवी तावदित्तत् ।सहस्रधा महिमानः सहस्रं यावद्ब्रह्म विष्ठितं तावती वाक् ॥
verses.transliteration: sahasradhā́ ǀ pañca-daśā́ni ǀ ukthā́ ǀ yā́vat ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ tā́vat ǀ ít ǀ tát ǀsahasradhā́ ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ sahásram ǀ yā́vat ǀ bráhma ǀ ví-sthitam ǀ tā́vatī ǀ vā́k ǁ
verses.english_translation: The fifteen lauds are in a thousand places that is as vast as heaven and earth in measure. A thousand spots contain the mighty thousand. Vāk spreadeth forth as far as Prayer extendeth.
verses.wilson_translation: The fifteen chief forms (are found) in a thousand plural ces; as heaven and earth are, so verily in that; thethousand great (functions) are in a thousand plural ces; as Brahmāis variably developed, so is Speech.
verses.griffith_verse: The fifteen lauds are in a thousand places that is as vast as heaven and earth in measure. A thousand spots contain the mighty thousand. Vāk spreadeth forth as far as Prayer extendeth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कश्छंदसां योगमा वेद धीरः को धिष्ण्यां प्रति वाचं पपाद ।कमृत्विजामष्टमं शूरमाहुर्हरी इंद्रस्य नि चिकाय कः स्वित् ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ chándasām ǀ yógam ǀ ā́ ǀ veda ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ dhíṣṇyām ǀ práti ǀ vā́cam ǀ papāda ǀkám ǀ ṛtvíjām ǀ aṣṭamám ǀ śū́ram ǀ āhuḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ índrasya ǀ ní ǀ cikāya ǀ káḥ ǀ svit ǁ
verses.english_translation: What sage hath learned the metres' application? Who hath gained Vāk, the spirit's aim and object? Which ministering priest is called eighth Hero? Who then hath tracked the two Bay Steeds of Indra?
verses.wilson_translation: What grave person n knows the application of the metres? Who utters the words appropriate to thefunctions (of the) different priests? Whom do they call the eighth of the priests, the independent? Who has donehonour to the two bay horses of Indra?
verses.griffith_verse: What sage hath learned the metres' application? Who hath gained Vāk, the spirit's aim and object? Which ministering priest is called eighth Hero? Who then hath tracked the two Bay Steeds of Indra?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भूम्या अंतं पर्येके चरंति रथस्य धूर्षु युक्तासो अस्थुः ।श्रमस्य दायं वि भजंत्येभ्यो यदा यमो भवति हर्म्ये हितः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhū́myāḥ ǀ ántam ǀ pári ǀ éke ǀ caranti ǀ ráthasya ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ yuktā́saḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀśrámasya ǀ dāyám ǀ ví ǀ bhajanti ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ yadā́ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ bhávati ǀ harmyé ǀ hitáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Yoked to his chariot-pole there stood the Coursers: they only travel round earth's farthest limits. These, when their driver in his home is settled, receive the allotted meed of their exertion.
verses.wilson_translation: Some (horses) proceed to the limit of the earth; they stand still harnessed to the yoke of the chariot;(the gods) apportion among them the alleviation of fatigue, when the charioteer is plural ced (ready to drive them) totheir dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: Yoked to his chariot-pole there stood the Coursers: they only travel round earth's farthest limits. These, when their driver in his home is settled, receive the allotted meed of their exertion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXV. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . VERILY wondrous is the tender Youngling's growth who never draweth nigh to drink his Mothers' milk.As soon as she who hath no udder bore him, he, faring on his great errand, suddenly grew strong. Then Agni was his name, most active to bestow, gathering up the trees with his consuming tooth;Skilled in fair sacrifice, armed with destroying tongue, impetuous as a bull that snorteth in the mead. Praise him, yourGod who, bird-like, rests upon a tree, scattering drops of juice and pouring forth his flood,Speaking aloud with flame as with his lips a priest, and broadening his paths like one of high command. Thou Everlasting, whom, far-striding fain to burn, the winds, uninterrupted, never overcome,They have approached, as warriors eager for the fight, heroic Trita, guiding him to gain his wish. This Agni is the best of Kaṇvas, Kaṇvas' Friend, Conqueror of the foe whether afar or near.May Agni guard the singers, guard the princes well: may Agni grant to us our princes' gracious help. Do thou, Supitrya, swiftly following, make thyself the lord of Jātavedas, mightiest of all,Who surely gives a boon even in thirsty land most powerful, prepared to aid us in the wilds. Thus noble Agni with princes and mortal men is lauded, excellent for conquering strength with chiefs,Men who are well-disposed as friends and true to Law, even as the heavens in majesty surpass mankind. O Son of Strength, Victorious, with this title Upastuta's most potent voice reveres thee.Blest with brave sons by thee we will extol thee, and lengthen out the days of our existence. Thus, Agni, have the sons of Vrstihavya, the Ṛṣis, the Upastutas invoked thee.Protect them, guard the singers and the princes. With Vaṣaṭ! have they come, with hands uplifted, with their uplifted hands and cries of Glory!

verses.sanskrit: चित्र इच्छिशोस्तरुणस्य वक्षथो न यो मातरावप्येति धातवे ।अनूधा यदि जीजनदधा च नु ववक्ष सद्यो महि दूत्यं चरन् ॥
verses.transliteration: citráḥ ǀ ít ǀ śíśoḥ ǀ táruṇasya ǀ vakṣáthaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ mātárau ǀ api-éti ǀ dhā́tave ǀanūdhā́ḥ ǀ yádi ǀ jī́janat ǀ ádha ǀ ca ǀ nú ǀ vavákṣa ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ máhi ǀ dūtyám ǀ cáran ǁ
verses.english_translation: VERILY wondrous is the tender Youngling's growth who never draweth nigh to drink his Mothers' milk. As soon as she who hath no udder bore him, he, faring on his great errand, suddenly grew strong.
verses.wilson_translation: Wonderful is the conveyance of (the oblation by) the tender infant, who does not come to his parentsto drink, although the udderless (world) gave him birth; he immediately bears (the oblation to the gods) fulfillingthe important office of their messenger.
verses.griffith_verse: VERILY wondrous is the tender Youngling's growth who never draweth nigh to drink his Mothers' milk. As soon as she who hath no udder bore him, he, faring on his great errand, suddenly grew strong.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्ह नाम धायि दन्नपस्तमः सं यो वना युवते भस्मना दता ।अभिप्रमुरा जुह्वा स्वध्वर इनो न प्रोथमानो यवसे वृषा ॥
verses.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ha ǀ nā́ma ǀ dhāyi ǀ dán ǀ apáḥ-tamaḥ ǀ sám ǀ yáḥ ǀ vánā ǀ yuváte ǀ bhásmanā ǀ datā́ ǀabhi-pramúrā ǀ juhvā́ ǀ su-adhvaráḥ ǀ ináḥ ǀ ná ǀ próthamānaḥ ǀ yávase ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Then Agni was his name, most active to bestow, gathering up the trees with his consuming tooth; Skilled in fair sacrifice, armed with destroying tongue, impetuous as a bull that snorteth in the mead.
verses.wilson_translation: The most active Agni, the giver of wealth, is nourished with ghī (by the worshippers), he who withflaming tooth devours the forests; devoutly worshipped with the uplifted goblet (he is, nourished) like a lordlywell-fed bull amidst (fresh) pasture.
verses.griffith_verse: Then Agni was his name, most active to bestow, gathering up the trees with his consuming tooth; Skilled in fair sacrifice, armed with destroying tongue, impetuous as a bull that snorteth in the mead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं वो विं न द्रुषदं देवमंधस इंदुं प्रोथंतं प्रवपंतमर्णवं ।आसा वह्निं न शोचिषा विरप्शिनं महिव्रतं न सरजंतमध्वनः ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ vaḥ ǀ vím ǀ ná ǀ dru-sádam ǀ devám ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ índum ǀ próthantam ǀ pra-vápantam ǀ arṇavám ǀāsā́ ǀ váhnim ǀ ná ǀ śocíṣā ǀ vi-rapśínam ǀ máhi-vratam ǀ ná ǀ sarájantam ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praise him, yourGod who, bird-like, rests upon a tree, scattering drops of juice and pouring forth his flood, Speaking aloud with flame as with his lips a priest, and broadening his paths like one of high command.
verses.wilson_translation: (Glorify) him, (worshippers), the divine, like a bird seated upon a tree, demanding sacrificial food,clamorous, wood-consuming, water-shedding, like one bearing (the oblation) in his mouth, mighty with radiance,simultaneously illuminating the paths, like the great functionary (the sun).
verses.griffith_verse: Praise him, yourGod who, bird-like, rests upon a tree, scattering drops of juice and pouring forth his flood, Speaking aloud with flame as with his lips a priest, and broadening his paths like one of high command.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि यस्य ते ज्रयसानस्याजर धक्षोर्न वाताः परि संत्यच्युताः ।आ रण्वासो युयुधयो न सत्वनं त्रितं नशंत प्र शिषंत इष्टये ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ yásya ǀ te ǀ jrayasānásya ǀ ajara ǀ dhákṣoḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́tāḥ ǀ pári ǀ sánti ǀ ácyutāḥ ǀā́ ǀ raṇvā́saḥ ǀ yúyudhayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ satvanám ǀ tritám ǀ naśanta ǀ prá ǀ śiṣántaḥ ǀ iṣṭáye ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou Everlasting, whom, far-striding fain to burn, the winds, uninterrupted, never overcome, They have approached, as warriors eager for the fight, heroic Trita, guiding him to gain his wish.
verses.wilson_translation: O imperishable Agni, the invincible winds spread around you (who are) rapid in movement, anddesirous of consuming (the forest), like combatants( the priests) calling aloud, anxious to bestow (the oblation),glorify you, the mighty, stationed in the three (altars).
verses.griffith_verse: Thou Everlasting, whom, far-striding fain to burn, the winds, uninterrupted, never overcome, They have approached, as warriors eager for the fight, heroic Trita, guiding him to gain his wish.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इदग्निः कण्वतमः कण्वसखार्यः परस्यांतरस्य तरुषः ।अग्निः पातु गृणतो अग्निः सूरीनग्निर्ददातु तेषामवो नः ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ agníḥ ǀ káṇva-tamaḥ ǀ káṇva-sakhā ǀ aryáḥ ǀ párasya ǀ ántarasya ǀ táruṣaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ pātu ǀ gṛṇatáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sūrī́n ǀ agníḥ ǀ dadātu ǀ téṣām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Agni is the best of Kaṇvas, Kaṇvas' Friend, Conqueror of the foe whether afar or near. May Agni guard the singers, guard the princes well: may Agni grant to us our princes' gracious help.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, the most earnest of eulogists, the friend of those who praise the lord, the destroyer of enemies,whether far off or near, may Agni protect those who adore him, may Agni (protect) those who offer oblation, may Agni give to us who are both these protection.
verses.griffith_verse: This Agni is the best of Kaṇvas, Kaṇvas' Friend, Conqueror of the foe whether afar or near. May Agni guard the singers, guard the princes well: may Agni grant to us our princes' gracious help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वाजिंतमाय सह्यसे सुपित्र्य तृषु च्यवानो अनु जातवेदसे ।अनुद्रे चिद्यो धृषता वरं सते महिंतमाय धन्वनेदविष्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: vājín-tamāya ǀ sáhyase ǀ su-pitrya ǀ tṛṣú ǀ cyávānaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ jātá-vedase ǀanudré ǀ cit ǀ yáḥ ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ váram ǀ saté ǀ mahín-tamāya ǀ dhánvanā ǀ ít ǀ aviṣyaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do thou, Supitrya, swiftly following, make thyself the lord of Jātavedas, mightiest of all, Who surely gives a boon even in thirsty land most powerful, prepared to aid us in the wilds.
verses.wilson_translation: OAgni, who has fair ancestors, (I have) arrived quickly to (praise) you, the most bountiful bestower offood, the overcomer (of foes), the Jātavedas, (I who offer) the best to you, the most mighty being, the protectorin calamity, with your capable (bow).
verses.griffith_verse: Do thou, Supitrya, swiftly following, make thyself the lord of Jātavedas, mightiest of all, Who surely gives a boon even in thirsty land most powerful, prepared to aid us in the wilds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवाग्निर्मर्तैः सह सूरिभिर्वसु ष्टवे सहसः सूनरो नृभिः ।मित्रासो न ये सुधिता ऋतायवो द्यावो न द्युम्नैरभि संति मानुषान् ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ agníḥ ǀ mártaiḥ ǀ sahá ǀ sūrí-bhiḥ ǀ vásuḥ ǀ stave ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ sūnáraḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀmitrā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ sú-dhitāḥ ǀ ṛta-yávaḥ ǀ dyā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dyumnáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sánti ǀ mā́nuṣān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus noble Agni with princes and mortal men is lauded, excellent for conquering strength with chiefs, Men who are well-disposed as friends and true to Law, even as the heavens in majesty surpass mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: In this manner,Agni, the son of strength, is glorified by (us his) worshippers, together with piousmortals, for the sake of wealth-- (his worshippers) who, like delighted friends, desiring the sacrifice, like shining(ones), overcome (hostile) men through his might.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus noble Agni with princes and mortal men is lauded, excellent for conquering strength with chiefs, Men who are well-disposed as friends and true to Law, even as the heavens in majesty surpass mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्जो नपात्सहसावन्निति त्वोपस्तुतस्य वंदते वृषा वाक् ।त्वां स्तोषाम त्वया सुवीरा द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ॥
verses.transliteration: ū́rjaḥ ǀ napāt ǀ sahasā-van ǀ íti ǀ tvā ǀ upa-stutásya ǀ vandate ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ vā́k ǀtvā́m ǀ stoṣāma ǀ tváyā ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǀ drā́ghīyaḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ dádhānāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Son of Strength, Victorious, with this title Upastuta's most potent voice reveres thee. Blest with brave sons by thee we will extol thee, and lengthen out the days of our existence.
verses.wilson_translation: "Offspring of food! vigorous (Agni)", thus the praise of Upastuta, showering forth oblations, glorifiesyou. "Let us praise you; through you let us obtain excellentmaleprogeny, enjoying long protracted life". them and the pious, worshippers. With uplifted faces, calling outvaṣaṭ! vaṣaṭ! they reached you; with upliftedfaces they reached you, calling outnamas! namas!
verses.griffith_verse: O Son of Strength, Victorious, with this title Upastuta's most potent voice reveres thee. Blest with brave sons by thee we will extol thee, and lengthen out the days of our existence.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इति त्वाग्ने वृष्टिहव्यस्य पुत्रा उपस्तुतास ऋषयोऽवोचन् ।तांश्च पाहि गृणतश्च सूरीन्वषड्वषळित्यूर्ध्वासो अनक्षन्नमो नम इत्यूर्ध्वासो अनक्षन् ॥
verses.transliteration: íti ǀ tvā ǀ agne ǀ vṛṣṭi-hávyasya ǀ putrā́ḥ ǀ upa-stutā́saḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ avocan ǀtā́n ǀ ca ǀ pāhí ǀ gṛṇatáḥ ǀ ca ǀ sūrī́n ǀ váṣaṭ ǀ váṣaṭ ǀ íti ǀ ūrdhvā́saḥ ǀ anakṣan ǀ námaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ íti ǀ ūrdhvā́saḥ ǀ anakṣan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus, Agni, have the sons of Vrstihavya, the Ṛṣis, the Upastutas invoked thee. Protect them, guard the singers and the princes. With Vaṣaṭ! have they come, with hands uplifted, with their uplifted hands and cries of Glory!
verses.griffith_verse: Thus, Agni, have the sons of Vrstihavya, the Ṛṣis, the Upastutas invoked thee. Protect them, guard the singers and the princes. With Vaṣaṭ! have they come, with hands uplifted, with their uplifted hands and cries of Glory!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXV1. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vṛtra.Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra. Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma.Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper. Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee.Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen. Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers.With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer. Dash down, outffaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons.I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle. Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman.Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body. To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger.Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee. Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma.With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes. I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters.Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.

verses.sanskrit: पिबा सोमं महत इंद्रियाय पिबा वृत्राय हंतवे शविष्ठ ।पिब राये शवसे हूयमानः पिब मध्वस्तृपदिंद्रा वृषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: píba ǀ sómam ǀ mahaté ǀ indriyā́ya ǀ píba ǀ vṛtrā́ya ǀ hántave ǀ śaviṣṭha ǀpíba ǀ rāyé ǀ śávase ǀ hūyámānaḥ ǀ píba ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ tṛpát ǀ indra ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vṛtra. Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink (Indra) the Somafor the invigoration of your organs, drink, most mighhty one, for the death of Vṛtra; drink when invoked for wealth, for strength; drink of the exhilarating Soma, and being satisfied, Indra,shower down (blessings).
verses.griffith_verse: DRINK Soma juice for mighty power and vigour, drink, Strongest One, that thou mayst smite down Vṛtra. Drink thou, invoked, for strength, and riches: drink thou thy fill of meath and pour it down, O Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य पिब क्षुमतः प्रस्थितस्येंद्र सोमस्य वरमा सुतस्य ।स्वस्तिदा मनसा मादयस्वार्वाचीनो रेवते सौभगाय ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ piba ǀ kṣu-mátaḥ ǀ prá-sthitasya ǀ índra ǀ sómasya ǀ váram ǀ ā́ ǀ sutásya ǀsvasti-dā́ḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ mādayasva ǀ arvācīnáḥ ǀ reváte ǀ sáubhagāya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma. Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper.
verses.wilson_translation: Drink,Indra, your excellent portion of this renowned Somaeffused and poured forth; the giver ofprosperity, be delighted in your mind, (be) turned towards us to bestow riches and happiness.
verses.griffith_verse: Drink of the foodful juice stirred into motion, drink what thou choosest of the flowing Soma. Giver of weal, be joyful in thy spirit, and turn thee hitherward to bless and prosper.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ममत्तु त्वा दिव्यः सोम इंद्र ममत्तु यः सूयते पार्थिवेषु ।ममत्तु येन वरिवश्चकर्थ ममत्तु येन निरिणासि शत्रून् ॥
verses.transliteration: mamáttu ǀ tvā ǀ divyáḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ indra ǀ mamáttu ǀ yáḥ ǀ sūyáte ǀ pā́rthiveṣu ǀmamáttu ǀ yéna ǀ várivaḥ ǀ cakártha ǀ mamáttu ǀ yéna ǀ ni-riṇā́si ǀ śátrūn ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee. Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen.
verses.wilson_translation: May the celestial Somaexhilarate you,Indra; may that which is effused at terrestrial rites exhilarateyou; may that exhilarate you through the influence of which you have bestowed wealth; may that exhilarate youwhereby you scatter foes.
verses.griffith_verse: Let heavenly Soma gladden thee, O Indra, let that effused among mankind delight thee. Rejoice in that whereby thou gavest freedom, and that whereby thou conquerest thy foemen.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ द्विबर्हा अमिनो यात्विंद्रो वृषा हरिभ्यां परिषिक्तमंधः ।गव्या सुतस्य प्रभृतस्य मध्वः सत्रा खेदामरुशहा वृषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ dvi-bárhāḥ ǀ amináḥ ǀ yātu ǀ índraḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ pári-siktam ǀ ándhaḥ ǀgávi ǀ ā́ ǀ sutásya ǀ prá-bhṛtasya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ satrā́ ǀ khédām ǀ aruśa-hā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers. With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, who deserves the twofold adoration, (of praise and prayer), who goes everywhere, theshowerer of benefits, come to the offered sacrificial food with his two bay horses; O slayer of enemies,(exhilarated) at our sacrifice (by drinking) of the Somaeffused upon the cow-hide and poured (into the cups),rush like a bull upon the dispirited (foes).
verses.griffith_verse: Let Indra come, impetuous, doubly mighty, to the poured juice, the Bull, with two Bay Coursers. With juices pressed in milk, with meath presented, glut evermore thy bolt, O Foe-destroyer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि तिग्मानि भ्राशयन्भ्राश्यान्यव स्थिरा तनुहि यातुजूनां ।उग्राय ते सहो बलं ददामि प्रतीत्या शत्रून्विगदेषु वृश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tigmā́ni ǀ bhrāśáyan ǀ bhrā́śyāni ǀ áva ǀ sthirā́ ǀ tanuhi ǀ yātu-jū́nām ǀugrā́ya ǀ te ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ bálam ǀ dadāmi ǀ prati-ítya ǀ śátrūn ǀ vi-gadéṣu ǀ vṛśca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dash down, outffaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons. I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle.
verses.wilson_translation: Brandishing your sharp, shining weapons, pierce the solid bodies of the evil spirits. I give to you whoare fierce, foe-subduing strength; having assailed the enemies, cut them to pieces in the midst of their clamour.
verses.griffith_verse: Dash down, outffaming their sharp flaming weapons, the strong-holds of the men urged on by demons. I give thee, Mighty One, great strength and conquest: go, meet thy foes and rend them in the battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: व्यर्य इंद्र तनुहि श्रवांस्योजः स्थिरेव धन्वनोऽभिमातीः ।अस्मद्र्यग्वावृधानः सहोभिरनिभृष्टस्तन्वं वावृधस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ aryáḥ ǀ indra ǀ tanuhi ǀ śrávāṃsi ǀ ójaḥ ǀ sthirā́-iva ǀ dhánvanaḥ ǀ abhí-mātīḥ ǀasmadryák ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ sáhaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ áni-bhṛṣṭaḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ vavṛdhasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman. Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body.
verses.wilson_translation: Stretch out for us, lord Indra, varied food, (stretch out) your strength like strong bows against ourenemies; mighty in our presence by your vigour and irresistible still augment your form.
verses.griffith_verse: Extend afar the votary's fame and glory, as the firm archer's strength drives off the foeman. Ranged on our side, grown strong in might that conquers, never defeated, still increase thy body.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं हविर्मघवंतुभ्यं रातं प्रति सम्राळहृणानो गृभाय ।तुभ्यं सुतो मघवंतुभ्यं पक्वोऽद्धींद्र पिब च प्रस्थितस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ havíḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ túbhyam ǀ rātám ǀ práti ǀ sam-rāṭ ǀ áhṛṇānaḥ ǀ gṛbhāya ǀtúbhyam ǀ sutáḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ túbhyam ǀ pakváḥ ǀ addhí ǀ indra ǀ píba ǀ ca ǀ prá-sthitasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger. Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Imperial Maghavan, to you this oblation is offered; accept it, not displeased; for you, Maghavan, thelibation is effused, for you (the cake is) toasted; eat it,Indra, and drink the libation poured (upon the altar).
verses.griffith_verse: To thee have we presented this oblation: accept it, Sovran Ruler, free from anger. Juice, Maghavan, for thee is pressed and ripened: eat, Indra, drink of that which stirs to meet thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अद्धीदिंद्र प्रस्थितेमा हवींषि चनो दधिष्व पचतोत सोमं ।प्रयस्वंतः प्रति हर्यामसि त्वा सत्याः संतु यजमानस्य कामाः ॥
verses.transliteration: addhí ǀ ít ǀ indra ǀ prá-sthitā ǀ imā́ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ cánaḥ ǀ dadhiṣva ǀ pacatā́ ǀ utá ǀ sómam ǀpráyasvantaḥ ǀ práti ǀ haryāmasi ǀ tvā ǀ satyā́ḥ ǀ santu ǀ yájamānasya ǀ kā́māḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma. With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes.
verses.wilson_translation: Eat,Indra, these oblations plural ced (upon the altar); accept the food, the toasted (cakes), and the Soma. Provided with sacrificial viands we delight you; let the desires of the instrumental tutor of the rite be fulfilled.
verses.griffith_verse: Eat, Indra, these oblations which approach thee: be pleased with food made ready and with Soma. With entertainment we receive thee friendly: effectual be the sacrificer's wishes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रेंद्राग्निभ्यां सुवचस्यामियर्मि सिंधाविव प्रेरयं नावमर्कैः ।अया इव परि चरंति देवा ये अस्मभ्यं धनदा उद्भिदश्च ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ indrāgní-bhyām ǀ su-vacasyā́m ǀ iyarmi ǀ síndhau-iva ǀ prá ǀ īrayam ǀ nā́vam ǀ arkáiḥ ǀáyāḥ-iva ǀ pári ǀ caranti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yé ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dhana-dā́ḥ ǀ ut-bhídaḥ ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters. Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.
verses.wilson_translation: I direct my eulogy of Indraand Agni; with sacred prayers I directed (my praise) like a vessel (launched)upon the ocean; like holy priests, the gods themselves reverence us, being the donors (to us) of wealth and theextirpators (of our foes).
verses.griffith_verse: I send sweet speech to Indra and to Agni: with hymns I speed it like a boat through waters. Even thus, the Gods seem moving round about me, the fountains and bestowers of our riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXVII. Liberality.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape.The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him. The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat,Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him. Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble.Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles. No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing.Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him. Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway.Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling. The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin.He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker. The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows.Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend outyalues him who gives not. He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed.Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together. The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal.Twins even diffier in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.

verses.sanskrit: न वा उ देवाः क्षुधमिद्वधं ददुरुताशितमुप गच्छंति मृत्यवः ।उतो रयिः पृणतो नोप दस्यत्युतापृणन्मर्डितारं न विंदते ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ kṣúdham ǀ ít ǀ vadhám ǀ daduḥ ǀ utá ǀ ā́śitam ǀ úpa ǀ gacchanti ǀ mṛtyávaḥ ǀutó íti ǀ rayíḥ ǀ pṛṇatáḥ ǀ ná ǀ úpa ǀ dasyati ǀ utá ǀ ápṛṇan ǀ marḍitā́ram ǀ ná ǀ vindate ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape. The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him.
verses.wilson_translation: The gods have not assigned hunger as (the cause of) death, for deaths approach the man who haseaten; the riches of one who gives do not diminish, he who gives not finds no consoler.
verses.griffith_verse: THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape. The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य आध्राय चकमानाय पित्वोऽन्नवान्त्सन्रफितायोपजग्मुषे ।स्थिरं मनः कृणुते सेवते पुरोतो चित्स मर्डितारं न विंदते ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ādhrā́ya ǀ cakamānā́ya ǀ pitváḥ ǀ ánna-vān ǀ sán ǀ raphitā́ya ǀ upa-jagmúṣe ǀsthirám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ kṛṇuté ǀ sévate ǀ purā́ ǀ utó íti ǀ cit ǀ sáḥ ǀ marḍitā́ram ǀ ná ǀ vindate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat, Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him.
verses.wilson_translation: He who, possessed of food, hardens his heart against the feeble man craving nourishment, againstthe sufferer coming to him (for help), and pursues (his won enjoyment even) before him, that man finds noconsoler.
verses.griffith_verse: The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat, Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इद्भोजो यो गृहवे ददात्यन्नकामाय चरते कृशाय ।अरमस्मै भवति यामहूता उतापरीषु कृणुते सखायं ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhojáḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ gṛháve ǀ dádāti ǀ ánna-kāmāya ǀ cárate ǀ kṛśā́ya ǀáram ǀ asmai ǀ bhavati ǀ yā́ma-hūtau ǀ utá ǀ aparī́ṣu ǀ kṛṇute ǀ sákhāyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble. Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles.
verses.wilson_translation: He is liberal who gives to the suppliant desiring food, wandering about distressed; to him there is anample (recompense), and he contracts friendship with his adversaries.
verses.griffith_verse: Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble. Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानाय पित्वः ।अपास्मात्प्रेयान्न तदोको अस्ति पृणंतमन्यमरणं चिदिच्छेत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ yáḥ ǀ ná ǀ dádāti ǀ sákhye ǀ sacā-bhúve ǀ sácamānāya ǀ pitváḥ ǀápa ǀ asmāt ǀ prá ǀ iyāt ǀ ná ǀ tát ǀ ókaḥ ǀ asti ǀ pṛṇántam ǀ anyám ǀ áraṇam ǀ cit ǀ icchet ǁ
verses.english_translation: No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing. Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him.
verses.wilson_translation: He is not a friend who gives not food to a friend, to an associate, to a companion; let him turn awayfrom him, that is not a (fitting) dwelling; let him seek another more liberal lord.
verses.griffith_verse: No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing. Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पृणीयादिन्नाधमानाय ��व्यांद्राघीयांसमनु पश्येत पंथां ।ओ हि वर्तंते रथ्येव चक्रान्यमन्यमुप तिष्ठंत रायः ॥
verses.transliteration: pṛṇīyā́t ǀ ít ǀ nā́dhamānāya ǀ távyān ǀ drā́ghīyāṃsam ǀ ánu ǀ paśyeta ǀ pánthām ǀó íti ǀ hí ǀ vártante ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǀ anyám-anyam ǀ úpa ǀ tiṣṭhanta ǀ rā́yaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway. Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the very rich man satisfy his suitor, let him look forward to a more protracted route, for richesrevolve from one man to another, as the wheels of a chariot turn round.
verses.griffith_verse: Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway. Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मोघमन्नं विंदते अप्रचेताः सत्यं ब्रवीमि वध इत्स तस्य ।नार्यमणं पुष्यति नो सखायं केवलाघो भवति केवलादी ॥
verses.transliteration: mógham ǀ ánnam ǀ vindate ǀ ápra-cetāḥ ǀ satyám ǀ bravīmi ǀ vadháḥ ǀ ít ǀ sáḥ ǀ tásya ǀná ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ púṣyati ǀ nó íti ǀ sákhāyam ǀ kévala-aghaḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ kevala-ādī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin. He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker.
verses.wilson_translation: The inhospitable man acquires food in vain. I speak the truth-- it verily is his death. He cherishes not Aryaman nor a friend; he who eats alone is nothing but a sinner.
verses.griffith_verse: The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin. He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कृषन्नित्फाल आशितं कृणोति यन्नध्वानमप वृंक्ते चरित्रैः ।वदन्ब्रह्मावदतो वनीयान्पृणन्नापिरपृणंतमभि ष्यात् ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣán ǀ ít ǀ phā́laḥ ǀ ā́śitam ǀ kṛṇoti ǀ yán ǀ ádhvānam ǀ ápa ǀ vṛṅkte ǀ carítraiḥ ǀvádan ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ávadataḥ ǀ vánīyān ǀ pṛṇán ǀ āpíḥ ǀ ápṛṇantam ǀ abhí ǀ syāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows. Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend outyalues him who gives not.
verses.wilson_translation: The plural ughshare furrowing (the field) provides food (for the plural ughman); a man travelling along a roadacquires (wealth for his master) by his movements; a Brāhmaṇaexpounding (the Veda) is better than one notexpounding it; (so) let the man who gives become a kinsman to the man who gives not.
verses.griffith_verse: The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows. Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend outyalues him who gives not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एकपाद्भूयो द्विपदो वि चक्रमे द्विपात्त्रिपादमभ्येति पश्चात् ।चतुष्पादेति द्विपदामभिस्वरे संपश्यन्पंक्तीरुपतिष्ठमानः ॥
verses.transliteration: éka-pāt ǀ bhū́yaḥ ǀ dvi-pádaḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakrame ǀ dvi-pā́t ǀ tri-pā́dam ǀ abhí ǀ eti ǀ paścā́t ǀcátuḥ-pāt ǀ eti ǀ dvi-pádām ǀ abhi-svaré ǀ sam-páśyan ǀ paṅktī́ḥ ǀ upa-tíṣṭhamānaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed. Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has but one foot takes a longer time on a journey than he who has two; he who has two feetcomes after him who has three; he who has four feet comes up overtaking the two-footed (and three-footed),beholding their traces as he passes by.
verses.griffith_verse: He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed. Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समौ चिद्धस्तौ न समं विविष्टः सम्मातरा चिन्न समं दुहाते ।यमयोश्चिन्न समा वीर्याणि ज्ञाती चित्संतौ न समं पृणीतः ॥
verses.transliteration: samáu ǀ cit ǀ hástau ǀ ná ǀ samám ǀ viviṣṭaḥ ǀ sam-mātárā ǀ cit ǀ ná ǀ samám ǀ duhāte íti ǀyamáyoḥ ǀ cit ǀ ná ǀ samā́ ǀ vīryā́ṇi ǀ jñātī́ íti ǀ cit ǀ sántau ǀ ná ǀ samám ǀ pṛṇītaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal. Twins even diffier in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.
verses.wilson_translation: The twohandsare alike, but they do not perform the same work; two cows calving at the same timedo not yield the same milk; two twins have not the same strength; two person ns of the same family do not displayequal liberality.
