verses.griffith_verse: The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal. Twins even diffier in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, refulgent among men thou slayest the devouring fiend,Bright Ruler in thine own abode. Thou springest up when worshipped well the drops of butter are thy joyWhen ladies are brought near to thee. Honoured with gifts he shines afar, Agni adorable with song:The dripping ladle balms his face. Agni with honey in his mouth, honoured with gifts, is balmed with oil,Refulgent in his wealth of light. Praised by our hymns thou kindlest thee, Oblation-bearer, for the GodsAs such do mortals call on thee. To that Immortal Agni pay worship with oil, ye mortal men,—Lord of the house, whom none deceives. O Agni, burn the Rākṣasas with thine unconquerable flameShine guardian of Eternal Law. So, Agni, with thy glowing face burn fierce against the female fiends,Shining among Uruksayas. Uruksayas have kindled thee, Oblation-bearer, thee, with hymns.Best Worshipper among mankind.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणं दीद्यन्मर्त्येष्वा ।स्वे क्षये शुचिव्रत ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ háṃsi ǀ ní ǀ atríṇam ǀ dī́dyat ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ ā́ ǀsvé ǀ kṣáye ǀ śuci-vrata ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI, refulgent among men thou slayest the devouring fiend, Bright Ruler in thine own abode.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, observer of purity, you destroy the devouring (gloom), shining among men in your won dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI, refulgent among men thou slayest the devouring fiend, Bright Ruler in thine own abode.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठसि स्वाहुतो घृतानि प्रति मोदसे ।यत्त्वा स्रुचः समस्थिरन् ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ tiṣṭhasi ǀ sú-āhutaḥ ǀ ghṛtā́ni ǀ práti ǀ modase ǀyát ǀ tvā ǀ srúcaḥ ǀ sam-ásthiran ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou springest up when worshipped well the drops of butter are thy joy When ladies are brought near to thee.
verses.wilson_translation: You spring up when piously invoked, you delight in the oblations when the ladles are brought nearyou.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou springest up when worshipped well the drops of butter are thy joy When ladies are brought near to thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स आहुतो वि रोचतेऽग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा ।स्रुचा प्रतीकमज्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rocate ǀ agníḥ ǀ īḷényaḥ ǀ girā́ ǀsrucā́ ǀ prátīkam ǀ ajyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Honoured with gifts he shines afar, Agni adorable with song: The dripping ladle balms his face.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who is to be glorified with the voice (of praise), blazes up when invoked, he is sprinkled with theladle before (the other gods).
verses.griffith_verse: Honoured with gifts he shines afar, Agni adorable with song: The dripping ladle balms his face.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृतेनाग्निः समज्यते मधुप्रतीक आहुतः ।रोचमानो विभावसुः ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛténa ǀ agníḥ ǀ sám ǀ ajyate ǀ mádhu-pratīkaḥ ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀrócamānaḥ ǀ vibhā́-vasuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni with honey in his mouth, honoured with gifts, is balmed with oil, Refulgent in his wealth of light.
verses.wilson_translation: Agniis anointed with butter, having a face of honey, invoked, radiant, irradiating all.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni with honey in his mouth, honoured with gifts, is balmed with oil, Refulgent in his wealth of light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जरमाणः समिध्यसे देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन ।तं त्वा हवंत मर्त्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: járamāṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ idhyase ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ havya-vāhana ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ havanta ǀ mártyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Praised by our hymns thou kindlest thee, Oblation-bearer, for the Gods As such do mortals call on thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Bearer of oblations, glorified by the worshippers, you are kindled for the gods; as such do mortalsinvoke you.
verses.griffith_verse: Praised by our hymns thou kindlest thee, Oblation-bearer, for the Gods As such do mortals call on thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं मर्ता अमर्त्यं घृतेनाग्निं सपर्यत ।अदाभ्यं गृहपतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ martāḥ ǀ ámartyam ǀ ghṛténa ǀ agním ǀ saparyata ǀádābhyam ǀ gṛhá-patim ǁ
verses.english_translation: To that Immortal Agni pay worship with oil, ye mortal men,— Lord of the house, whom none deceives.
verses.wilson_translation: Mortals, worship with ghī the immortal Agni, the indestructible, the master of the mansion.
verses.griffith_verse: To that Immortal Agni pay worship with oil, ye mortal men,— Lord of the house, whom none deceives.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अदाभ्येन शोचिषाग्ने रक्षस्त्वं दह ।गोपा ऋतस्य दीदिहि ॥
verses.transliteration: ádābhyena ǀ śocíṣā ǀ ágne ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ tvám ǀ daha ǀgopā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dīdihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, burn the Rākṣasas with thine unconquerable flame Shine guardian of Eternal Law.
verses.wilson_translation: With your indestructible flame,Agni, do you consume the Rākṣasas; shine, the defender of thesacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, burn the Rākṣasas with thine unconquerable flame Shine guardian of Eternal Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमग्ने प्रतीकेन प्रत्योष यातुधान्यः ।उरुक्षयेषु दीद्यत् ॥
verses.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ prátīkena ǀ práti ǀ oṣa ǀ yātu-dhānyáḥ ǀuru-kṣáyeṣu ǀ dī́dyat ǁ
verses.english_translation: So, Agni, with thy glowing face burn fierce against the female fiends, Shining among Uruksayas.
verses.wilson_translation: Do you,Agni, with your brightness, consume the feminine le fiends, shining in your outspread dwelllingṣurukṣayaḥ = occupying many mansions, i.e. theyajamānas].
verses.griffith_verse: So, Agni, with thy glowing face burn fierce against the female fiends, Shining among Uruksayas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तं त्वा गीर्भिरुरुक्षया हव्यवाहं समीधिरे ।यजिष्ठं मानुषे जने ॥
verses.transliteration: tám ǀ tvā ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ uru-kṣáyāḥ ǀ havya-vā́ham ǀ sám ǀ īdhire ǀyájiṣṭham ǀ mā́nuṣe ǀ jáne ǁ
verses.english_translation: Uruksayas have kindled thee, Oblation-bearer, thee, with hymns. Best Worshipper among mankind.
verses.wilson_translation: The masters of many mansions have, by their praises, kindled you,Agni, the bearer of oblations, whoare most adorable among human beings.
verses.griffith_verse: Uruksayas have kindled thee, Oblation-bearer, thee, with hymns. Best Worshipper among mankind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXIX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted meHave I not drunk of Soma juice? The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of meHave I not drunk of Soma juice? I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earthHave I not drunk of Soma juice? Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or thereHave I not drunk of Soma juice? In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below:Have I not drunk of Soma juice?, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament:Have I not drunk of Soma juice? I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods:Have I not drunk of Soma juice?

verses.sanskrit: इति वा इति मे मनो गामश्वं सनुयामिति ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: íti ǀ vái ǀ íti ǀ me ǀ mánaḥ ǀ gā́m ǀ áśvam ǀ sanuyām ǀ íti ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: Thus, indeed, thus my mind (resolved): " I will give cows and horses to my worshippers", for I haveoften drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS, even this was my resolve, to win a cow, to win a steed: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र वाता इव दोधत उन्मा पीता अयंसत ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vā́tāḥ-iva ǀ dódhataḥ ǀ út ǀ mā ǀ pītā́ḥ ǀ ayaṃsata ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: Like the winds violently shaking (the trees), the draughts (of Soma) have lifted me up, for I have oftendrunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Like violent gusts of wind the draughts that I have drunk have lifted me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उन्मा पीता अयंसत रथमश्वा इवाशवः ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ mā ǀ pītā́ḥ ǀ ayaṃsata ǀ rátham ǀ áśvāḥ-iva ǀ āśávaḥ ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: The draughts (of Soma) have lifted me up like swift horses (drawing) a chariot, for I have often drunkof the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: The draughts I drank have borne me up, as fleet-foot horses draw a car: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप मा मतिरस्थित वाश्रा पुत्रमिव प्रियं ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ mā ǀ matíḥ ǀ asthita ǀ vāśrā́ ǀ putrám-iva ǀ priyám ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: The Praise (of the pious) has come to me like a lowing cow to her beloved calf, for I have often drunkof the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: The hymn hath reached me, like a cow who lows to meet her darling calf: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं तष्टेव वंधुरं पर्यचामि हृदा मतिं ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ vandhúram ǀ pári ǀ acāmi ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ matím ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: I revolve the song of praise in my heart as a carpenter (making) a charioteer's seat, for I have oftendrunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: As a wright bends a chariot-seat so round my heart I bend the hymn: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि मे अक्षिपच्चनाच्छांत्सुः पंच कृष्टयः ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ me ǀ akṣi-pát ǀ caná ǀ ácchāntsuḥ ǀ páñca ǀ kṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: The five castes have not eluded the gloance of my eye, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Not as a mote within the eye count the Five Tribes of men with me: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि मे रोदसी उभे अन्यं पक्षं चन प्रति ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ me ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǀ anyám ǀ pakṣám ǀ caná ǀ práti ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: Both heaven and earth (are) not equal to one half of me, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: The heavens and earth themselves have not grown equal to one half of me Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि द्यां महिना भुवमभीमां पृथिवीं महीं ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ dyā́m ǀ mahinā́ ǀ bhuvam ǀ abhí ǀ imā́m ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ mahī́m ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earth Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: I excel the sky in greatness, (I excel) this great earth, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: I in my grandeur have surpassed the heavens and all this spacious earth Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हंताहं पृथिवीमिमां नि दधानीह वेह वा ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: hánta ǀ ahám ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ imā́m ǀ ní ǀ dadhāni ǀ ihá ǀ vā ǀ ihá ǀ vā ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or there Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: Lo! I will plural ce this earth (where I will), either here or there, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Aha! this spacious earth will I deposit either here or there Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओषमित्पृथिवीमहं जंघनानीह वेह वा ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: oṣám ǀ ít ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ ahám ǀ jaṅghánāni ǀ ihá ǀ vā ǀ ihá ǀ vā ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: I will drive the scorching (sun) either here or there, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: In one short moment will I smite the earth in fury here or there: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दिवि मे अन्यः पक्षोऽधो अन्यमचीकृषं ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: diví ǀ me ǀ anyáḥ ǀ pakṣáḥ ǀ adháḥ ǀ anyám ǀ acīkṛṣam ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: One of my wings is in the sky; the other I dragged below, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: One of my flanks is in the sky; I let the other trail below: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहमस्मि महामहोऽभिनभ्यमुदीषितः ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ asmi ǀ mahā-maháḥ ǀ abhi-nabhyám ǀ út-īṣitaḥ ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: I am (the sun), the greatest of the great, raised to the firmament, for I have often drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: 1, greatest of the Mighty Ones, am lifted to the firmament: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गृहो याम्यरंकृतो देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहनः ।कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥
verses.transliteration: gṛháḥ ǀ yāmi ǀ áram-kṛtaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ havya-vā́hanaḥ ǀkuvít ǀ sómasya ǀ ápām ǀ íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.wilson_translation: Receiving the offering I go, graced (by the worshippers), bearing the oblation to the gods, for I haveoften drunk of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: I seek the worshipper's abode; oblation-bearer to the Gods: Have I not drunk of Soma juice?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour.As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful. Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dāsa,Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation. All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants.Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle. Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful.With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yātudhānas harm thee. Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat.I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour. Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skilful, most energetic, Āptya of the Aptyas:He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals. Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower.Thou stablishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion. Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra.He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open. Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person.The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.

verses.sanskrit: तदिदास भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं यतो जज्ञ उग्रस्त्वेषनृम्णः ।सद्यो जज्ञानो नि रिणाति शत्रूननु यं विश्वे मदंत्यूमाः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ āsa ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ yátaḥ ǀ jajñé ǀ ugráḥ ǀ tveṣá-nṛmṇaḥ ǀsadyáḥ ǀ jajñānáḥ ǀ ní ǀ riṇāti ǀ śátrūn ǀ ánu ǀ yám ǀ víśve ǀ mádanti ǀ ū́māḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour. As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.
verses.wilson_translation: That was the chiefest in all worlds, from whence the fierce one, the rich in radiance, was born; assoon as born, he destroys the foes, he in whom all living beings delight.
verses.griffith_verse: IN all the worlds That was the Best and Highest whence sprang the Mighty Gods, of splendid valour. As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, be in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वावृधानः शवसा भूर्योजाः शत्रुर्दासाय भियसं दधाति ।अव्यनच्च व्यनच्च सस्नि सं ते नवंत प्रभृता मदेषु ॥
verses.transliteration: vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ bhū́ri-ojāḥ ǀ śátruḥ ǀ dāsā́ya ǀ bhiyásam ǀ dadhāti ǀávi-anat ǀ ca ǀ vi-anát ǀ ca ǀ sásni ǀ sám ǀ te ǀ navanta ǀ prá-bhṛtā ǀ mádeṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dāsa, Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Waxing in strength, the very powerful, destructive (Indra), implants fear in the Dāsa; both theinanimate and the animate (world) is purified by him. Nourished in your exhilaration (all creatures) are assembled.
verses.griffith_verse: Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dāsa, Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वे क्रतुमपि वृंजंति विश्वे द्विर्यदेते त्रिर्भवंत्यूमाः ।स्वादोः स्वादीयः स्वादुना सृजा समदः सु मधु मधुनाभि योधीः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ krátum ǀ ápi ǀ vṛñjanti ǀ víśve ǀ dvíḥ ǀ yát ǀ eté ǀ tríḥ ǀ bhávanti ǀ ū́māḥ ǀsvādóḥ ǀ svā́dīyaḥ ǀ svādúnā ǀ sṛja ǀ sám ǀ adáḥ ǀ sú ǀ mádhu ǀ mádhunā ǀ abhí ǀ yodhīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants. Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle.
verses.wilson_translation: To you all (worshippers) offer adoration, whether those propitiators be two or three. Combine thatwhich is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness, unite that honey with honey.
verses.griffith_verse: All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants. Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win. quickly with our meath that meath in battle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इति चिद्धि त्वा धना जयंतं मदेमदे अनुमदंति विप्राः ।ओजीयो धृष्णो स्थिरमा तनुष्व मा त्वा दभन्यातुधाना दुरेवाः ॥
verses.transliteration: íti ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ dhánā ǀ jáyantam ǀ máde-made ǀ anu-mádanti ǀ víprāḥ ǀójīyaḥ ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ sthirám ǀ ā́ ǀ tanuṣva ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ dabhan ǀ yātu-dhā́nāḥ ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful. With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yātudhānas harm thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Verily the pious praise you, (Indra), the giver of wealth in your repeated exhilaration; spread out for usresolute Indra, great and durable (affluence); may the malignantyātudhānasnever harm you.
verses.griffith_verse: Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful. With mightier power, Bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yātudhānas harm thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वया वयं शाशद्महे रणेषु प्रपश्यंतो युधेन्यानि भूरि ।चोदयामि त आयुधा वचोभिः सं ते शिशामि ब्रह्मणा वयांसि ॥
verses.transliteration: tváyā ǀ vayám ǀ śāśadmahe ǀ ráṇeṣu ǀ pra-páśyantaḥ ǀ yudhényāni ǀ bhū́ri ǀcodáyāmi ǀ te ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ vácaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ sám ǀ te ǀ śiśāmi ǀ bráhmaṇā ǀ váyāṃsi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat. I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: Through you we destroy (our foes) in battles, beholding the numerous (hosts) which we have to fight; Iurge your weapons with words (of praise), I prepare your viands with a sacred verse.
verses.griffith_verse: Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat. I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्तुषेय्यं पुरुवर्पसमृभ्वमिनतममाप्त्यमाप्त्यानां ।आ दर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून्प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि ॥
verses.transliteration: stuṣéyyam ǀ puru-várpasam ǀ ṛ́bhvam ǀ iná-tamam ǀ āptyám ǀ āptyā́nām ǀā́ ǀ darṣate ǀ śávasā ǀ saptá ǀ dā́nūn ǀ prá ǀ sākṣate ǀ prati-mā́nāni ǀ bhū́ri ǁ
verses.english_translation: Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skilful, most energetic, Āptya of the Aptyas: He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise (Indra) who is worthy of praise, multiform vast, supreme, most accessible of the accessible; heassails with might the seven Dānavas, he overpowers many opposing hosts.
verses.griffith_verse: Worthy of praises, many-shaped, most skilful, most energetic, Āptya of the Aptyas: He with his might destroys the seven Danus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि तद्दधिषेऽवरं परं च यस्मिन्नाविथावसा दुरोणे ।आ मातरा स्थापयसे जिगत्नू अत इनोषि कर्वरा पुरूणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tát ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ ávaram ǀ páram ǀ ca ǀ yásmin ǀ ā́vitha ǀ ávasā ǀ duroṇé ǀā́ ǀ mātárā ǀ sthāpayase ǀ jigatnū́ íti ǀ átaḥ ǀ inoṣi ǀ kárvarā ǀ purū́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower. Thou stablishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.
verses.wilson_translation: You deposit the lesser and the greater wealth in the mansion in which you are satisfied with food; youfix the two wandering mothers, you accomplish many works.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou in that house which thy protection guardeth bestowest wealth, the higher and the lower. Thou stablishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इमा ब्रह्म बृहद्दिवो विवक्तींद्राय शूषमग्रियः स्वर्षाः ।महो गोत्रस्य क्षयति स्वराजो दुरश्च विश्वा अवृणोदप स्वाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́ ǀ bráhma ǀ bṛhát-divaḥ ǀ vivakti ǀ índrāya ǀ śūṣám ǀ agriyáḥ ǀ svaḥ-sā́ḥ ǀmaháḥ ǀ gotrásya ǀ kṣayati ǀ sva-rā́jaḥ ǀ dúraḥ ǀ ca ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ avṛṇot ǀ ápa ǀ svā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra. He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.
verses.griffith_verse: Brhaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeats these holy prayers, this strength of Indra. He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा महान्बृहद्दिवो अथर्वावोचत्स्वां तन्वमिंद्रमेव ।स्वसारो मातरिभ्वरीररिप्रा हिन्वंति च शवसा वर्धयंति च ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ mahā́n ǀ bṛhát-divaḥ ǀ átharvā ǀ ávocat ǀ svā́m ǀ tanvám ǀ índram ǀ evá ǀsvásāraḥ ǀ mātaríbhvarīḥ ǀ ariprā́ḥ ǀ hinvánti ǀ ca ǀ śávasā ǀ vardháyanti ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person. The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.
verses.wilson_translation: Thus the great Bṛhaddiva, son of Atharvan, repeated his diffused (praise) to Indra. The unsulliedsiister (streams) abiding in the mother (earth), to Indra, and augment him with strength.
verses.griffith_verse: Thus hath Brhaddiva, the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person. The spotless Sisters, they who are his Mothers, with power exalt him and impel him onward.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXI. Ka.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings.He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation? Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandments all the Gods acknowledge -.The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation? Who by his grandeur hath become Sole Ruler of all the moving world that breathes and slumbers;He who is Loord of men and Lord of cattle. What God shall we adore with our oblation? His, through his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasā his possession:His arms are these, his are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation? By him the heavens are strong and earth is stedfast, by him light's realm and sky-vault are supported:By him the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation? To him, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit,When over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation? What time the mighty waters came, containing the universal germ, producing Agni,Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation? He in his might surveyed the floods containing productive force and generating Worship.He is the God of gods, and none beside him. What God shall we adore with our oblation? Neer may he harm us who is earth's Begetter, nor he whose laws are sure, the heavens' Creator,He who brought forth the great and lucid waters. What God shall we adore with our oblation? Prajāpati! thou only comprehendest all these created things, and none beside thee.Grant us our hearts' desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेक आसीत् ।स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇya-garbháḥ ǀ sám ǀ avartata ǀ ágre ǀ bhūtásya ǀ jātáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀsáḥ ǀ dādhāra ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ utá ǀ imā́m ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings. He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: Hiraṇyagarbhawas present at the beginning; when born, he was the sole lord of created beings; heupheld this earth and heaven-- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings. He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: य आत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्व उपासते प्रशिषं यस्य देवाः ।यस्य च्छायामृतं यस्य मृत्युः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ātma-dā́ḥ ǀ bala-dā́ḥ ǀ yásya ǀ víśve ǀ upa-ā́sate ǀ pra-śíṣam ǀ yásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀyásya ǀ chāyā́ ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ yásya ǀ mṛtyúḥ ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandments all the Gods acknowledge -. The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: (To him) who is the giver ofsoul, the giver of strength, whose commands all (beings), even the godsobey, whose shadow is immortality, whose (shadow) is death-- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandments all the Gods acknowledge -. The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः प्राणतो निमिषतो महित्वैक इद्राजा जगतो बभूव ।य ईशे अस्य द्विपदश्चतुष्पदः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ prāṇatáḥ ǀ ni-miṣatáḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ rā́jā ǀ jágataḥ ǀ babhū́va ǀyáḥ ǀ ī́śe ǀ asyá ǀ dvi-pádaḥ ǀ cátuḥ-padaḥ ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who by his grandeur hath become Sole Ruler of all the moving world that breathes and slumbers; He who is Loord of men and Lord of cattle. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: (To him) who, by his greatness, has verily become the sole king of the breathing and seeing world,who rules over this aggregate of two-footed and four- footed beings -- let us offer worship with an oblation to thedivine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: Who by his grandeur hath become Sole Ruler of all the moving world that breathes and slumbers; He who is Loord of men and Lord of cattle. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्येमे हिमवंतो महित्वा यस्य समुद्रं रसया सहाहुः ।यस्येमाः प्रदिशो यस्य बाहू कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yásya ǀ imé ǀ himá-vantaḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ yásya ǀ samudrám ǀ rasáyā ǀ sahá ǀ āhúḥ ǀyásya ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ yásya ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: His, through his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasā his possession: His arms are these, his are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: Through whose greatness these snow-clad (mountains exist), whose property men call the ocean withthe rivers, whose are these quarters of space, who are the two arms -- let us offer worship with an oblation to thedivine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: His, through his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasā his possession: His arms are these, his are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येन द्यौरुग्रा पृथिवी च दृळ्हा येन स्वः स्तभितं येन नाकः ।यो अंतरिक्षे रजसो विमानः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ugrā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ ca ǀ dṛḷhā́ ǀ yéna ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ stabhitám ǀ yéna ǀ nā́kaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́naḥ ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: By him the heavens are strong and earth is stedfast, by him light's realm and sky-vault are supported: By him the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: By whom the sky was made profound and the earth solid, by whom heaven and the solar sphere werefixed, who was the measure of the water in the firmament -- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: By him the heavens are strong and earth is stedfast, by him light's realm and sky-vault are supported: By him the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं क्रंदसी अवसा तस्तभाने अभ्यैक्षेतां मनसा रेजमाने ।यत्राधि सूर उदितो विभाति कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ krándasī íti ǀ ávasā ǀ tastabhāné íti ǀ abhí ǀ áikṣetām ǀ mánasā ǀ réjamāne íti ǀyátra ǀ ádhi ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ út-itaḥ ǀ vi-bhā́ti ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit, When over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: Whom heaven and earth established by his protection, and shining brightly, regarded with their mind,in whom the risen sun shines forth -- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: To him, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit, When over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आपो ह यद्बृहतीर्विश्वमायन्गर्भं दधाना जनयंतीरग्निं ।ततो देवानां समवर्ततासुरेकः कस��मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ ha ǀ yát ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yan ǀ gárbham ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ janáyantīḥ ǀ agním ǀtátaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ sám ǀ avartata ǀ ásuḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time the mighty waters came, containing the universal germ, producing Agni, Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: When the vast waters overspread the universe containing the germ and giving birth to Agni, then wasproduced the one breath of the gods -- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: What time the mighty waters came, containing the universal germ, producing Agni, Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यश्चिदापो महिना पर्यपश्यद्दक्षं दधाना जनयंतीर्यज्ञं ।यो देवेष्वधि देव एक आसीत्कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ pari-ápaśyat ǀ dákṣam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ janáyantīḥ ǀ yajñám ǀyáḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ ádhi ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ā́sīt ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: He in his might surveyed the floods containing productive force and generating Worship. He is the God of gods, and none beside him. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: He who by his might beheld the waters all around containing the creative power and giving birth tosacrifice, he who among the gods was the one supreme god -- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: He in his might surveyed the floods containing productive force and generating Worship. He is the God of gods, and none beside him. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मा नो हिंसीज्जनिता यः पृथिव्या यो वा दिवं सत्यधर्मा जजान ।यश्चापश्चंद्रा बृहतीर्जजान कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ hiṃsīt ǀ janitā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vā ǀ dívam ǀ satyá-dharmā ǀ jajā́na ǀyáḥ ǀ ca ǀ apáḥ ǀ candrā́ḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ jajā́na ǀ kásmai ǀ devā́ya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Neer may he harm us who is earth's Begetter, nor he whose laws are sure, the heavens' Creator, He who brought forth the great and lucid waters. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.wilson_translation: May he do us no harm who is the parent of the earth, or who the unerring support (of the world) begatthe heaven, and who genitive rated the vast and delightful waters -- let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
verses.griffith_verse: Neer may he harm us who is earth's Begetter, nor he whose laws are sure, the heavens' Creator, He who brought forth the great and lucid waters. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यो विश्वा जातानि परि ता बभूव ।यत्कामास्ते जुहुमस्तन्नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणां ॥
verses.transliteration: prájā-pate ǀ ná ǀ tvát ǀ etā́ni ǀ anyáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ jātā́ni ǀ pári ǀ tā́ ǀ babhūva ǀyát-kāmāḥ ǀ te ǀ juhumáḥ ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ vayám ǀ syāma ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prajāpati! thou only comprehendest all these created things, and none beside thee. Grant us our hearts' desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession.
verses.wilson_translation: No other than you,Prajāpati, has given existence to all these beings; may that object of our desiresfor which we sacrifice to you be ours, may we be the possessors of riches.
verses.griffith_verse: Prajāpati! thou only comprehendest all these created things, and none beside thee. Grant us our hearts' desire when we invoke thee: may we have store of riches in possession.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome.May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches. O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance.Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law. Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper,Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee. The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice,The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives. First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta,The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhṛgus gave thee light and glory. Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper,Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice. They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence.Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice. Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One.Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.

verses.sanskrit: वसुं न चित्रमहसं गृणीषे वामं शेवमतिथिमद्विषेण्यं ।स रासते शुरुधो विश्वधायसोऽग्निर्होता गृहपतिः सुवीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: vásum ǀ ná ǀ citrá-mahasam ǀ gṛṇīṣe ǀ vāmám ǀ śévam ǀ átithim ǀ adviṣeṇyám ǀsáḥ ǀ rāsate ǀ śurúdhaḥ ǀ viśvá-dhāyasaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome. May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches.
verses.wilson_translation: I glorify him who is of wonderful radiance like the sun, the desirable, the giver of happiness, the guest(of man), the benevolent. He bestows vigour (upon the worshippers);Agni, the remover of sorrow, the sustaineerof all, the invoker (of the gods), the lord of the mansion.
verses.griffith_verse: I PRAISE the God of wondrous might like Indra, the lovely pleasant Guest whom all must welcome. May Agni, Priest and Master of the household, give hero strength and all-sustaining riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जुषाणो अग्ने प्रति हर्य मे वचो विश्वानि विद्वान्वयुनानि सुक्रतो ।घृतनिर्णिग्ब्रह्मणे गातुमेरय तव देवा अजनयन्ननु व्रतं ॥
verses.transliteration: juṣāṇáḥ ǀ agne ǀ práti ǀ harya ǀ me ǀ vácaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ vidvā́n ǀ vayúnāni ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀghṛ́ta-nirnik ǀ bráhmaṇe ǀ gātúm ǀ ā́ ǀ īraya ǀ táva ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ajanayan ǀ ánu ǀ vratám ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance. Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law.
verses.wilson_translation: Accept,Agni, being well plural ased, my praises, author of great deeds, (you are) cognizant of all objectsof knowledge; anointed with butter, stimulate the movements of the Brāhmaṇa; the gods produce (rewards)after your worship.
verses.griffith_verse: O Agni, graciously accept this song of mine, thou passing-wise who knowest every ordinance. Enwrapped in holy oil further the course of prayer: the Gods bestow according to thy holy law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सप्त धामानि परियन्नमर्त्यो दाशद्दाशुषे सुकृते मामहस्व ।सुवीरेण रयिणाग्ने स्वाभुवा यस्त आनट् समिधा तं जुषस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: saptá ǀ dhā́māni ǀ pari-yán ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀ dā́śat ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ su-kṛ́te ǀ mamahasva ǀsu-vī́reṇa ǀ rayíṇā ǀ agne ǀ su-ābhúvā ǀ yáḥ ǀ te ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ tám ǀ juṣasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper, Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Traversing the seven regions (of the universe), immortal Agni, bestow wealth, giving liberally to thepious liberal giver. Gratify with easily obtainable riches, together with fair offspring, him who feeds you with fueḷ
verses.griffith_verse: Immortal, wandering round the seven stations, give, a liberal Giver, to the pious worshipper, Wealth, Agni, with brave sons and ready for his use: welcome the man who comes with fuel unto thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं पुरोहितं हविष्मंत ईळते सप्त वाजिनं ।शृण्वंतमग्निं घृतपृष्ठमुक्षणं पृणंतं देवं पृणते सुवीर्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: yajñásya ǀ ketúm ǀ prathamám ǀ puráḥ-hitam ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ saptá ǀ vājínam ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ agním ǀ ghṛtá-pṛṣṭham ǀ ukṣáṇam ǀ pṛṇántam ǀ devám ǀ pṛṇaté ǀ su-vī́ryam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice, The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives.
verses.wilson_translation: The seven (priests) bearing oblations worship Agni, the emblem of sacrifice, the first of the gods, thefamily priest, the possessor of food, the hearer (of our prayers), the anointed with butter, the shedder of moisture,propitiating the worshipper who propitiates him, divine, endowed with excellent might.
verses.griffith_verse: The seven who bring oblations worship thee, the Strong, the first, the Great Chief Priest, Ensign of sacrifice, The oil-anointed Bull, Agni who hears, who sends as God full hero strength to him who freely gives.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं दूतः प्रथमो वरेण्यः स हूयमानो अमृताय मत्स्व ।त्वां मर्जयन्मरुतो दाशुषो गृहे त्वां स्तोमेभिर्भृगवो वि रुरुचुः ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hūyámānaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāya ǀ matsva ǀtvā́m ǀ marjayan ǀ marútaḥ ǀ dāśúṣaḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀ tvā́m ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rurucuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta, The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhṛgus gave thee light and glory.
verses.wilson_translation: You are the chief and most excellent messenger; do you, invoked by us to partake of the ambrosia,become exhilarated; the Marutsdecorated you in the dwelling of the donor of the oblation; the Bhṛgushaveglorified you with hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: First messenger art thou, meet for election: drink thou thy fill invited to the Anirta, The Maruts in the votary's house adorned thee; with lauds the Bhṛgus gave thee light and glory.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इषं दुहन्त्सुदुघां विश्वधायसं यज्ञप्रिये यजमानाय सुक्रतो ।अग्ने घृतस्नुस्त्रिर्ऋतानि दीद्यद्वर्तिर्यज्ञं परियन्त्सुक्रतूयसे ॥
verses.transliteration: íṣam ǀ duhán ǀ su-dúghām ǀ viśvá-dhāyasam ǀ yajña-príye ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀágre ǀ ghṛtá-snuḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ ṛtā́ni ǀ dī́dyat ǀ vartíḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ pari-yán ǀ sukratu-yase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper, Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Milking the easily milked cow (of sacrifice) of her all-sustaining food, for the benefit of the piousinstitutor of the rite, OAgni, doer of good deeds, anointed with butter, illumining the three regions, presiding(over the hall of sacrifice), going round the sacrifice, you accomplish each holy rite.
verses.griffith_verse: Milking the teeming Cow for all-sustaining food. O Wise One, for the worship-loving worshipper, Thou, Agni, dropping oil, thrice lighting works of Law, showest thy wisdom circling home and sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वामिदस्या उषसो व्युष्टिषु दूतं कृण्वाना अयजंत मानुषाः ।त्वां देवा महयाय्याय वावृधुराज्यमग्ने निमृजंतो अध्वरे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ dūtám ǀ kṛṇvānā́ḥ ǀ ayajanta ǀ mā́nuṣāḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ mahayā́yyāya ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ ā́jyam ǀ agne ǀ ni-mṛjántaḥ ǀ adhvaré ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence. Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Men worshipped you,Agni, at the opening of the present dawn, appointing you their messenger to thegods; the gods have magnified you for their adoration, sprinkling butter upon you at the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: They who at flushing of this dawn appointed thee their messenger, these men have paid thee reverence. Gods strengthened thee for work that must be glorified, Agni, while they made butter pure for sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि त्वा वसिष्ठा अह्वंत वाजिनं गृणंतो अग्ने विदथेषु वेधसः ।रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धारय यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ tvā ǀ vásiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ahvanta ǀ vājínam ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ agne ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀrāyáḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ yájamāneṣu ǀ dhāraya ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One. Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.
verses.wilson_translation: The pious Vasiṣṭhainvoked you,Agni, at the sacrificial meetings, praising you, the mighty one;continue the sustenance of riches among the instrumental tutors of the rite, and do you (gods) ever cherish us withblessings.
verses.griffith_verse: Arrangers in our synods, Agni, while they sang Vasisistha s sons have called thee down, the Potent One. Maintain the growth of wealth with men who sacrifice. Ye Gods, preserve us with your blessings evermore.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXIII. Vena.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Pṛśni.Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle. Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent,Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace. Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers.Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amṛta. Knowing his form, the sages yearned to meet him: they have come nigh to hear the wild Bull's bellow.Performing sacrifice they reached the river: for the Gandharva found the immortal waters. The Apsaras, the Lady, sweetly smiling, supports her Lover in sublimest heaven.In his Friend's dwelling as a Friend he wanders: he, Vena, rests him on his golden pinion. They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward;On thee with wings of gold, Varuṇa's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama. Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons;Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us. When as a spark he cometh near the ocean, still looking with a vulture's eye to heaven,His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the lowest region.

verses.sanskrit: अयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भा ज्योतिर्जरायू रजसो विमाने ।इममपां संगमे सूर्यस्य शिशुं न विप्रा मतिभी रिहंति ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ venáḥ ǀ codayat ǀ pṛ́śni-garbhāḥ ǀ jyótiḥ-jarāyuḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́ne ǀimám ǀ apā́m ǀ sam-gamé ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ śíśum ǀ ná ǀ víprāḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ rihanti ǁ
verses.english_translation: SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Pṛśni. Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle.
verses.wilson_translation: This Vena, enfolded in the membrane of light, urges on (the waters) the germs of the Sun in thefirmament of the water; the sages cherish him at the confluence of the waters, and the sun with endearments likea child.
verses.griffith_verse: SEE, Vena, born in light, hath driven hither, on chariot of the air, the Calves of Pṛśni. Singers with hymns caress him as an infant there where the waters and the sunlight mingle.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रादूर्मिमुदियर्ति वेनो नभोजाः पृष्ठं हर्यतस्य दर्शि ।ऋतस्य सानावधि विष्टपि भ्राट् समानं योनिमभ्यनूषत व्राः ॥
verses.transliteration: samudrā́t ǀ ūrmím ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ venáḥ ǀ nabhaḥ-jā́ḥ ǀ pṛṣṭhám ǀ haryatásya ǀ darśi ǀṛtásya ǀ sā́nau ǀ ádhi ǀ viṣṭápi ǀ bhrā́ṭ ǀ samānám ǀ yónim ǀ abhí ǀ anūṣata ǀ vrā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent, Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace.
verses.wilson_translation: The cloud-born Venasend the water from the firmament; the back of the azure (sky) is beheld. Heshone on the summit of the water in heaven; the troops praised their common abode.
verses.griffith_verse: Vena draws up his wave from out the ocean. mist-born, the fair one's back is made apparent, Brightly he shone aloft on Order's summit: the hosts sang glory to their common birthplace.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानं पूर्वीरभि वावशानास्तिष्ठन्वत्सस्य मातरः सनीळाः ।ऋतस्य सानावधि चक्रमाणा रिहंति मध्वो अमृतस्य वाणीः ॥
verses.transliteration: samānám ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vāvaśānā́ḥ ǀ tíṣṭhan ǀ vatsásya ǀ mātáraḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ sā́nau ǀ ádhi ǀ cakramāṇā́ḥ ǀ rihánti ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ vā́ṇīḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers. Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amṛta.
verses.wilson_translation: The many waters occupy a common station, clamouring around like the assembled mothers of the calf;wandering above the summit of the water they utter the praises of the sweet-flavoured ambrosia.
verses.griffith_verse: Full many, lowing to their joint-possession, dwelling together stood the Darling's Mothers. Ascending to the lofty height of Order, the bands of singers 'sip the sweets of Amṛta.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: जानंतो रूपमकृपंत विप्रा मृगस्य घोषं महिषस्य हि ग्मन् ।ऋतेन यंतो अधि सिंधुमस्थुर्विदद्गंधर्वो अमृतानि नाम ॥
verses.transliteration: jānántaḥ ǀ rūpám ǀ akṛpanta ǀ víprāḥ ǀ mṛgásya ǀ ghóṣam ǀ mahiṣásya ǀ hí ǀ gmán ǀṛténa ǀ yántaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ síndhum ǀ asthuḥ ǀ vidát ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ amṛ́tāni ǀ nā́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Knowing his form, the sages yearned to meet him: they have come nigh to hear the wild Bull's bellow. Performing sacrifice they reached the river: for the Gandharva found the immortal waters.
verses.wilson_translation: The pious, knowing his form, praised him, for they followed the city of the great deer; approaching hmwith sacrifice, they reached the flowing (water), for the sustainer of the waters knows the ambrosial (fluids).
verses.griffith_verse: Knowing his form, the sages yearned to meet him: they have come nigh to hear the wild Bull's bellow. Performing sacrifice they reached the river: for the Gandharva found the immortal waters.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्सरा जारमुपसिष्मियाणा योषा बिभर्ति परमे व्योमन् ।चरत्प्रियस्य योनिषु प्रियः सन्त्सीदत्पक्षे हिरण्यये स वेनः ॥
verses.transliteration: apsarā́ḥ ǀ jārám ǀ upa-siṣmiyāṇā́ ǀ yóṣā ǀ bibharti ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀcárat ǀ priyásya ǀ yóniṣu ǀ priyáḥ ǀ sán ǀ sī́dat ǀ pakṣé ǀ hiraṇyáye ǀ sáḥ ǀ venáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Apsaras, the Lady, sweetly smiling, supports her Lover in sublimest heaven. In his Friend's dwelling as a Friend he wanders: he, Vena, rests him on his golden pinion.
verses.wilson_translation: The Apsaras, smiling affectionately like a wife at her lover, cherishes him in the highest heaven; shewanders in the abodes of her beloved; he,Vena, being loved, sits, down on his golden wing.
verses.griffith_verse: The Apsaras, the Lady, sweetly smiling, supports her Lover in sublimest heaven. In his Friend's dwelling as a Friend he wanders: he, Vena, rests him on his golden pinion.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नाके सुपर्णमुप यत्पतंतं हृदा वेनंतो अभ्यचक्षत त्वा ।हिरण्यपक्षं वरुणस्य दूतं यमस्य योनौ शकुनं भुरण्युं ॥
verses.transliteration: nā́ke ǀ su-parṇám ǀ úpa ǀ yát ǀ pátantam ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ vénantaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ ácakṣata ǀ tvā ǀhíraṇya-pakṣam ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dūtám ǀ yamásya ǀ yónau ǀ śakunám ǀ bhuraṇyúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward; On thee with wings of gold, Varuṇa's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.
verses.wilson_translation: Those desiring you in their hearts contemplated you travelling as a strong-winged bird in the sky, thegolden-winged messenger of Varuṇa, the bird which nourishes (the world) in Yama's dwelling.
verses.griffith_verse: They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward; On thee with wings of gold, Varuṇa's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वो गंधर्वो अधि नाके अस्थात्प्रत्यङ्चित्रा बिभ्रदस्यायुधानि ।वसानो अत्कं सुरभिं दृशे कं स्वर्ण नाम जनत प्रियाणि ॥
verses.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ nā́ke ǀ asthāt ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ citrā́ ǀ bíbhrat ǀ asya ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀvásānaḥ ǀ átkam ǀ surabhím ǀ dṛśé ǀ kám ǀ sváḥ ǀ ná ǀ nā́ma ǀ janata ǀ priyā́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons; Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us.
verses.wilson_translation: The Gandharvāstood erect upon the firmament, brandishing towards us his wonderful weapons,investing all in his beautiful diffusive (form), they make them visible, like the sun he genitive rated the precious(rains).
verses.griffith_verse: Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons; Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्रप्सः समुद्रमभि यज्जिगाति पश्यन्गृध्रस्य चक्षसा विधर्मन् ।भानुः शुक्रेण शोचिषा चकानस्तृतीये चक्रे रजसि प्रियाणि ॥
verses.transliteration: drapsáḥ ǀ samudrám ǀ abhí ǀ yát ǀ jígāti ǀ páśyan ǀ gṛ́dhrasya ǀ cákṣasā ǀ ví-dharman ǀbhānúḥ ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀ cakānáḥ ǀ tṛtī́ye ǀ cakre ǀ rájasi ǀ priyā́ṇi ǁ
verses.english_translation: When as a spark he cometh near the ocean, still looking with a vulture's eye to heaven, His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the lowest region.
verses.wilson_translation: When (Venaas) the drop of rain approaches the firmament, contemplating (all things) with the eye ofthe hawk in the supporting (firmament), then the sun, shining with brilliant radiance, makes the precious(showers) in the third sphere.
verses.griffith_verse: When as a spark he cometh near the ocean, still looking with a vulture's eye to heaven, His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the lowest region.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXIV. Agni, Etc.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions.Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness. I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways,While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers., looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order.I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship. I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra.Away pass Agni, Varuṇa and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour. These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuṇa, if thou dost love me,O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom. Here is the light of heaven, here allis lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region.Let us two slaughter Vṛtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee. The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuṇa with no violence let the waters flow.Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have eau lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone. These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead;And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vṛtra. They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters.The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.

verses.sanskrit: इमं नो अग्न उप यज्ञमेहि पंचयामं त्रिवृतं सप्ततंतुं ।असो हव्यवाळुत नः पुरोगा ज्योगेव दीर्घं तम आशयिष्ठाः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ úpa ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ páñca-yāmam ǀ tri-vṛ́tam ǀ saptá-tantum ǀásaḥ ǀ havya-vā́ṭ ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ puraḥ-gā́ḥ ǀ jyók ǀ evá ǀ dīrghám ǀ támaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ aśayiṣṭhāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions. Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.
verses.wilson_translation: Come,Agni, to this our sacrifice, which has five oblations, three- fold, spread out by seven (priests); bethe bearer of our oblations, be our preceder, you have long been sleeping in profound darkness.
verses.griffith_verse: COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions. Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अदेवाद्देवः प्रचता गुहा यन्प्रपश्यमानो अमृतत्वमेमि ।शिवं यत्संतमशिवो जहामि स्वात्सख्यादरणीं नाभिमेमि ॥
verses.transliteration: ádevāt ǀ deváḥ ǀ pra-cátā ǀ gúhā ǀ yán ǀ pra-páśyamānaḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ emi ǀśivám ǀ yát ǀ sántam ǀ áśivaḥ ǀ jáhāmi ǀ svā́t ǀ sakhyā́t ǀ áraṇīm ǀ nā́bhim ǀ emi ǁ
verses.english_translation: I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways, While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agnispeaks). From being no divinity I issue a divninty from the cave at the solicitation (of the gods),and being manifest I attain immortality; when being inauspicious I abandon the sacrifice as it becomesauspicious, through my (old) friendship I come to the binding touch-wood.
verses.griffith_verse: I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways, While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पश्यन्नन्यस्या अतिथिं वयाया ऋतस्य धाम वि मिमे पुरूणि ।शंसामि पित्रे असुराय शेवमयज्ञियाद्यज्ञियं भागमेमि ॥
verses.transliteration: páśyan ǀ anyásyāḥ ǀ átithim ǀ vayā́yāḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ ví ǀ mime ǀ purū́ṇi ǀśáṃsāmi ǀ pitré ǀ ásurāya ǀ śévam ǀ ayajñiyā́t ǀ yajñíyam ǀ bhāgám ǀ emi ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order. I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.
verses.wilson_translation: Beholding the guest of another family, I have created the manifold abodes of sacrifice; I repeatpraises, (wishing) good luck to the paternal foe- destroying (race of deities), I pass from a plural ce unfit for sacrificeto a plural ce where sacrifice can be offered.
verses.griffith_verse: 1, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order. I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बह्वीः समा अकरमंतरस्मिन्निंद्रं वृणानः पितरं जहामि ।अग्निः सोमो वरुणस्ते च्यवंते पर्यावर्द्राष्ट्रं तदवाम्यायन् ॥
verses.transliteration: bahvī́ḥ ǀ sámāḥ ǀ akaram ǀ antáḥ ǀ asmin ǀ índram ǀ vṛṇānáḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ jahāmi ǀagníḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ té ǀ cyavante ǀ pari-ā́vart ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ tát ǀ avāmi ǀ ā-yán ǁ
verses.english_translation: I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra. Away pass Agni, Varuṇa and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour.
verses.wilson_translation: I spent many years within this (altar), preferring Indra I abandon the progenitor;Agni,Soma,Varuṇa,fall (from their power); returning, I protect that kingdom which awaits me.
verses.griffith_verse: I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra. Away pass Agni, Varuṇa and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निर्माया उ त्ये असुरा अभूवंत्वं च मा वरुण कामयासे ।ऋतेन राजन्ननृतं विविंचन्मम राष्ट्रस्याधिपत्यमेहि ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ-māyāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tyé ǀ ásurāḥ ǀ abhūvan ǀ tvám ǀ ca ǀ mā ǀ varuṇa ǀ kāmáyāse ǀṛténa ǀ rājan ǀ ánṛtam ǀ vi-viñcán ǀ máma ǀ rāṣṭrásya ǀ ádhi-patyam ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǁ
verses.english_translation: These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuṇa, if thou dost love me, O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom.
verses.wilson_translation: Theseasuraswere deprived of their magical power; if you,Varuṇa, desire me, (then), O king,separating truth from falsehood, come and enjoy sovereignty over my realm.
verses.griffith_verse: These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuṇa, if thou dost love me, O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं स्वरिदमिदास वाममयं प्रकाश उर्वंतरिक्षं ।हनाव वृत्रं निरेहि सोम हविष्ट्वा संतं हविषा यजाम ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ sváḥ ǀ idám ǀ ít ǀ āsa ǀ vāmám ǀ ayám ǀ pra-kāśáḥ ǀ urú ǀ antárikṣam ǀhánāva ǀ vṛtrám ǀ niḥ-éhi ǀ soma ǀ havíḥ ǀ tvā ǀ sántam ǀ havíṣā ǀ yajāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here is the light of heaven, here allis lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region. Let us two slaughter Vṛtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee.
verses.wilson_translation: (Agnior Varuṇaspeak). This, OSoma, is heaven; this verily was beautiful this (was) the light, thebroad firmament; let us together slay Vṛtra; come forth; we worship with an oblation you who are yourselfoblation.
verses.griffith_verse: Here is the light of heaven, here allis lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region. Let us two slaughter Vṛtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कविः कवित्वा दिवि रूपमासजदप्रभूती वरुणो निरपः सृजत् ।क्षेमं कृण्वाना जनयो न सिंधवस्ता अस्य वर्णं शुचयो भरिभ्रति ॥
verses.transliteration: kavíḥ ǀ kavi-tvā́ ǀ diví ǀ rūpám ǀ ā́ ǀ asajat ǀ ápra-bhūtī ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ sṛjat ǀkṣémam ǀ kṛṇvānā́ḥ ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ várṇam ǀ śúcayaḥ ǀ bharibhrati ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuṇa with no violence let the waters flow. Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have eau lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage (Mitra) by his wisdom fixed his body in the sky;Varuṇawith but a wslight effort let loose thewaters, conferring happiness, like wives, the pure rivers assume his (white) tint.
verses.griffith_verse: The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuṇa with no violence let the waters flow. Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have eau lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता अस्य ज्येष्ठमिंद्रियं सचंते ता ईमा क्षेति स्वधया मदंतीः ।ता ईं विशो न राजानं वृणाना बीभत्सुवो अप वृत्रादतिष्ठन् ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ jyéṣṭham ǀ indriyám ǀ sacante ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ īm ǀ ā́ ǀ kṣeti ǀ svadháyā ǀ mádantīḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ īm ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rā́jānam ǀ vṛṇānā́ḥ ǀ bībhatsúvaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ vṛtrā́t ǀ atiṣṭhan ǁ
verses.english_translation: These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead; And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vṛtra.
verses.wilson_translation: They sustain his most excellent energy, he approaches them delighting him with (sacrificial) food; likesubject choosing a king, they, smitten with fear fled from Vṛtra.
verses.griffith_verse: These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead; And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vṛtra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: बीभत्सूनां सयुजं हंसमाहुरपां दिव्यानां सख्ये चरंतं ।अनुष्टुभमनु चर्चूर्यमाणमिंद्रं नि चिक्युः कवयो मनीषा ॥
verses.transliteration: bībhatsū́nām ǀ sa-yújam ǀ haṃsám ǀ āhuḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ divyā́nām ǀ sakhyé ǀ cárantam ǀanu-stúbham ǀ ánu ǀ carcūryámāṇam ǀ índram ǀ ní ǀ cikyuḥ ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ manīṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters. The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.
verses.wilson_translation: The sage called the sun the ally of those who are frightened, abiding in the friendship of the waters ofheaven; the wise have honoured with their praise Indra, who ceaselessly moves after the Anuṣṭup.
verses.griffith_verse: They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters. The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXV. Vāk.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and All-Gods I wander.I hold aloft both Varuṇa and Mitra, Indra and Agni, and the Pair of Aśvins. I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvaṣṭar I support, Pūṣan, and Bhaga.I load with wealth the zealous sdcrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship.Thus Gods have stablished me in many places with many homes to enter and abide in. Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them,—each man who sees, brewhes, hears the word outspokenThey know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it., verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods and men alike shall welcome.I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Ṛṣi, and a Brahman. I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion.I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated Earth and Heaven. On the world's summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean.Thence I extend o’er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead. I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence.Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur.

verses.sanskrit: अहं रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिश्चराम्यहमादित्यैरुत विश्वदेवैः ।अहं मित्रावरुणोभा बिभर्म्यहमिंद्राग्नी अहमश्विनोभा ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ carāmi ǀ ahám ǀ ādityáiḥ ǀ utá ǀ viśvá-devaiḥ ǀahám ǀ mitrā́váruṇā ǀ ubhā́ ǀ bibharmi ǀ ahám ǀ indrāgnī́ íti ǀ ahám ǀ aśvínā ǀ ubhā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and All-Gods I wander. I hold aloft both Varuṇa and Mitra, Indra and Agni, and the Pair of Aśvins.
verses.wilson_translation: I proceed with the Rudras, with the Vasus, with theĀdityas, and with the Viśvedevās; I support both Mitra and Varuṇa,Agniand Indra, and the two Aśvinṣ
verses.griffith_verse: I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Ādityas and All-Gods I wander. I hold aloft both Varuṇa and Mitra, Indra and Agni, and the Pair of Aśvins.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं सोममाहनसं बिभर्म्यहं त्वष्टारमुत पूषणं भगं ।अहं दधामि द्रविणं हविष्मते सुप्राव्ये यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ sómam ǀ āhanásam ǀ bibharmi ǀ ahám ǀ tváṣṭāram ǀ utá ǀ pūṣáṇam ǀ bhágam ǀahám ǀ dadhāmi ǀ dráviṇam ǀ havíṣmate ǀ supra-avyé ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvaṣṭar I support, Pūṣan, and Bhaga. I load with wealth the zealous sdcrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation
verses.wilson_translation: I support the foe-destroying Soma,Tvaṣṭā,Pūṣanand Bhaga; I bestow wealth upon the instrumental tutorof the rite offering the oblation, deserving of careful protection, pouring forth the libation.
verses.griffith_verse: I cherish and sustain high-swelling Soma, and Tvaṣṭar I support, Pūṣan, and Bhaga. I load with wealth the zealous sdcrificer who pours the juice and offers his oblation
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं राष्ट्री संगमनी वसूनां चिकितुषी प्रथमा यज्ञियानां ।तां मा देवा व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा भूरिस्थात्रां भूर्यावेशयंतीं ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ rā́ṣṭrī ǀ sam-gámanī ǀ vásūnām ǀ cikitúṣī ǀ prathamā́ ǀ yajñíyānām ǀtā́m ǀ mā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ adadhuḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ bhū́ri-sthātrām ǀ bhū́ri ǀ ā-veśáyantīm ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship. Thus Gods have stablished me in many places with many homes to enter and abide in.
verses.wilson_translation: I am the sovereignqueen, the collectress of treasures, cognizant (of the Supreme Being), the chief ofobjects of worship; as such the gods have put me in many plural ces, abiding in manifold conditions, entering intonumerous (forms.
verses.griffith_verse: I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship. Thus Gods have stablished me in many places with many homes to enter and abide in.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मया सो अन्नमत्ति यो विपश्यति यः प्राणिति य ईं शृणोत्युक्तं ।अमंतवो मां त उप क्षियंति श्रुधि श्रुत श्रद्धिवं ते वदामि ॥
verses.transliteration: máyā ǀ sáḥ ǀ ánnam ǀ atti ǀ yáḥ ǀ vi-páśyati ǀ yáḥ ǀ prā́ṇiti ǀ yáḥ ǀ īm ǀ śṛṇóti ǀ uktám ǀamantávaḥ ǀ mā́m ǀ té ǀ úpa ǀ kṣiyanti ǀ śrudhí ǀ śruta ǀ śraddhi-vám ǀ te ǀ vadāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them,—each man who sees, brewhes, hears the word outspoken They know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it.
verses.wilson_translation: He who eats food (eats) through me; he who sees, who breathes, who hears what is spoken, does sothrough me; those who are ignorant of me perish; hear you who have hearing, I tell that which is deserving ofbelief.
verses.griffith_verse: Through me alone all eat the food that feeds them,—each man who sees, brewhes, hears the word outspoken They know it not, but yet they dwell beside me. Hear, one and all, the truth as I declare it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहमेव स्वयमिदं वदामि जुष्टं देवेभिरुत मानुषेभिः ।यं कामये तंतमुग्रं कृणोमि तं ब्रह्माणं तमृषिं तं सुमेधां ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ evá ǀ svayám ǀ idám ǀ vadāmi ǀ júṣṭam ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ utá ǀ mā́nuṣebhiḥ ǀyám ǀ kāmáye ǀ tám-tam ǀ ugrám ǀ kṛṇomi ǀ tám ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ tám ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ tám ǀ su-medhā́m ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1, verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods and men alike shall welcome. I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Ṛṣi, and a Brahman.
verses.wilson_translation: I verily of myself declare this which is approved of by both gods and men; whomsoever I will, I render
verses.griffith_verse: 1, verily, myself announce and utter the word that Gods and men alike shall welcome. I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Ṛṣi, and a Brahman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं रुद्राय धनुरा तनोमि ब्रह्मद्विषे शरवे हंतवा उ ।अहं जनाय समदं कृणोम्यहं द्यावापृथिवी आ विवेश ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ dhánuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tanomi ǀ brahma-dvíṣe ǀ śárave ǀ hántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀahám ǀ jánāya ǀ sa-mádam ǀ kṛṇomi ǀ ahám ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
verses.english_translation: I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion. I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated Earth and Heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: I bend the bow of Rudra, to slay the destructive enemy of the Brāhmaṇas, I wage war with (hostile)men. I pervade heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: I bend the bow for Rudra that his arrow may strike and slay the hater of devotion. I rouse and order battle for the people, and I have penetrated Earth and Heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं सुवे पितरमस्य मूर्धन्मम योनिरप्स्वंतः समुद्रे ।ततो वि तिष्ठे भुवनानु विश्वोतामूं द्यां वर्ष्मणोप स्पृशामि ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ suve ǀ pitáram ǀ asya ǀ mūrdhán ǀ máma ǀ yóniḥ ǀ ap-sú ǀ antáríti ǀ samudré ǀtátaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tiṣṭhe ǀ bhúvanā ǀ ánu ǀ víśvā ǀ utá ǀ amū́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ varṣmáṇā ǀ úpa ǀ spṛśāmi ǁ
verses.english_translation: On the world's summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean. Thence I extend o’er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead.
verses.wilson_translation: I bring forth the paternal (heaven) upon the brow of this (Supreme Being), my birthplace is in the midstof the waters; from thence I spread through all beings, and touch this heaven with my body.
verses.griffith_verse: On the world's summit I bring forth the Father: my home is in the waters, in the ocean. Thence I extend o’er all existing creatures, and touch even yonder heaven with my forehead.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहमेव वात इव प्र वाम्यारभमाणा भुवनानि विश्वा ।परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्यैतावती महिना सं बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ evá ǀ vā́taḥ-iva ǀ prá ǀ vāmi ǀ ā-rábhamāṇā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀparáḥ ǀ divā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ etā́vatī ǀ mahinā́ ǀ sám ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence. Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur.
verses.wilson_translation: I breathe forth like the wind giving form to all created worlds; beyond the heaven, beyond this earth(am I), so vast am I in greatness.
verses.griffith_verse: I breathe a strong breath like the wind and tempest, the while I hold together all existence. Beyond this wide earth and beyond the heavens I have become so mighty in my grandeur.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: ८ शैलूषिः कुल्मलबर्हिषो, वामदेव्योऽहोमुग्वा। विश्वेदेवाः। उपरिष्टाद्बृहती,८ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man,Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes. This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,Whereby ye guhrd the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes. These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes. Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes. Ādityas are beyond all foes,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.
