These lead us safely over all, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes. May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman:May the Ādityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defence beyond our foes. As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered.So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.

verses.sanskrit: न तमंहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यं ।सजोषसो यमर्यमा मित्रो नयंति वरुणो अति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ ná ǀ duḥ-itám ǀ dévāsaḥ ǀ aṣṭa ǀ mártyam ǀsa-jóṣasaḥ ǀ yám ǀ aryamā́ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ náyanti ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Neither sin nor sorrow, O gods, affect the man whom Aryaman,Mitraand Varuṇa, being alike plural asedby him, conduct beyond (the reach of) his enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: No peril, no severe distress, ye Gods, affects the mortal man, Whom Aryaman and Mitra lead, and Varima, of one accord, beyond his foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तद्धि वयं वृणीमहे वरुण मित्रार्यमन् ।येना निरंहसो यूयं पाथ नेथा च मर्त्यमति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: tát ǀ hí ǀ vayám ǀ vṛṇīmáhe ǀ váruṇa ǀ mítra ǀ áryaman ǀyéna ǀ níḥ ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ pāthá ǀ nethá ǀ ca ǀ mártyam ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Whereby ye guhrd the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.
verses.wilson_translation: We implore that (protection) of yours,Varuṇa,Mitra, and Aryaman, whereby you preserve a man fromsin, and lead him beyond (the reach of) his enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: This very thing do we desire, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Whereby ye guhrd the mortal man from sore distress, and lead him safe beyond his foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ते नूनं नोऽयमूतये वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।नयिष्ठा उ नो नेषणि पर्षिष्ठा उ नः पर्षण्यति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ nūnám ǀ naḥ ǀ ayám ǀ ūtáye ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀnáyiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ neṣáṇi ǀ párṣiṣṭhāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣáṇi ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May this Varuṇaand Mitraand Aryamanbe our protection, may they lead us to the spot to which weshould be led, and make us cross over to the spot to which we should cross over beyond (the reach of) ourenemies.
verses.griffith_verse: These are, each one, our present helps, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. Best leaders, best deliverers to lead us on and bear as safe beyond our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यूयं विश्वं परि पाथ वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।युष्माकं शर्मणि प्रिये स्याम सुप्रणीतयोऽति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yūyám ǀ víśvam ǀ pári ǀ pātha ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀyuṣmā́kam ǀ śármaṇi ǀ priyé ǀ syā́ma ǀ su-pranītayaḥ ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman, protect the universe; may we abide in your blessed felicity, O excellentleaders, beyond (the reach of) our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye compass round and guard each man, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: In your dear keeping may we be, ye who are excellent as guides beyond our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आदित्यासो अति स्रिधो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।उग्रं मरुद्भी रुद्रं हुवेमेंद्रमग्निं स्वस्तयेऽति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ādityā́saḥ ǀ áti ǀ srídhaḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀugrám ǀ marút-bhiḥ ǀ rudrám ǀ huvema ǀ índram ǀ agním ǀ svastáye ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ādityas are beyond all foes,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May theĀdityas,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman, (lead us) beyond (the reach of) the malignant; let usinvoke the fierce Rudrawith the Maruts, and Indraand Agnifor our welfare, (that they may plural ce us) beyond (thereach of) our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Ādityas are beyond all foes,—Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: Strong Rudra with the Marut host, Indra, Agni let us call for weal beyond our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नेतार ऊ षु णस्तिरो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।अति विश्वानि दुरिता राजानश्चर्षणीनामति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: nétāraḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ naḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀáti ǀ víśvāni ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These lead us safely over all, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May the leaders Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman, (lead) us apart (from wickedness), may the kings of menlead us beyond all calamities, beyond (the reach of) our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: These lead us safely over all, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, These who are Kings of living men, over all troubles far away beyond our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शुनमस्मभ्यमूतये वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ।शर्म यच्छंतु सप्रथ आदित्यासो यदीमहे अति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: śunám ǀ asmábhyam ǀ ūtáye ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀśárma ǀ yacchantu ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀ ādityā́saḥ ǀ yát ǀ ī́mahe ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: May the Ādityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defence beyond our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman(bestow) upon us felicity for our protection; may theĀdityasgrant usthat abundant happiness which we solicit, (and lead us) beyond (the reach of) our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: May they give bliss to aid us well, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: May the Ādityas, when we pray, grant us wide shelter and defence beyond our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथा ह त्यद्वसवो गौर्यं चित्पदि षिताममुंचता यजत्राः ।एवो ष्वस्मन्मुंचता व्यंहः प्र तार्यग्ने प्रतरं न आयुः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ gauryám ǀ cit ǀ padí ǀ sitā́m ǀ ámuñcata ǀ yajatrāḥ ǀevó íti ǀ sú ǀ asmát ǀ muñcata ǀ ví ǀ áṃhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ tāri ǀ agne ǀ pra-tarám ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered. So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.
verses.wilson_translation: As you, adorable Vasus, set free the cow fastened by her foot, even so remove sin away from us, andprolong,Agni, our protracted life.
verses.griffith_verse: As in this place, O Holy Ones, ye Vasus freed even the Gaud when her feet were fettered. So free us now from trouble and affliction: and let our life be lengthened still, O Api.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVII. Night.
hymns.anukramani: ८ कुशिकः सौभरः, रात्रिर्वा भारद्वाजी। रात्रिः। गायत्री।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot:She hath put all her glories on. Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth:She conquers darkness with her light. The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place:And then the darkness vanishes. So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visitedAs birds their nest upon the tree. The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies,Even the falcons fain for prey. Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away;Easy be thou for us to pass. Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues:O Morning, cancel it like debts. These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, acceptThis laud as for a conqueror.

verses.sanskrit: रात्री व्यख्यदायती पुरुत्रा देव्यक्षभिः ।विश्वा अधि श्रियोऽधित ॥
verses.transliteration: rā́trī ǀ ví ǀ akhyat ǀ ā-yatī́ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ devī́ ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀvíśvāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ adhita ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot: She hath put all her glories on.
verses.wilson_translation: The divine Night approaching looked upon many plural ces with her eyes, she has assumed all beautieṣ
verses.griffith_verse: WITH all her eyes the Goddess Night looks forth approaching many a spot: She hath put all her glories on.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ओर्वप्रा अमर्त्या निवतो देव्युद्वतः ।ज्योतिषा बाधते तमः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ urú ǀ aprāḥ ǀ ámartyā ǀ ni-vátaḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ ut-vátaḥ ǀjyótiṣā ǀ bādhate ǀ támaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth: She conquers darkness with her light.
verses.wilson_translation: The immortal goddess has filled the expandeed (formament), the low plural ces and the high plural ces, shefights the darkness with lustre.
verses.griffith_verse: Immortal. she hath filled the waste, the Goddess hath filled height and depth: She conquers darkness with her light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: निरु स्वसारमस्कृतोषसं देव्यायती ।अपेदु हासते तमः ॥
verses.transliteration: níḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svásāram ǀ akṛta ǀ uṣásam ǀ devī́ ǀ ā-yatī́ ǀápa ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ hāsate ǀ támaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place: And then the darkness vanishes.
verses.wilson_translation: The advancing goddess prepared (the way for) her sister Dawn, and then the darkness departs.
verses.griffith_verse: The Goddess as she comes hath set the Dawn her Sister in her place: And then the darkness vanishes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सा नो अद्य यस्या वयं नि ते यामन्नविक्ष्महि ।वृक्षे न वसतिं वयः ॥
verses.transliteration: sā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ adyá ǀ yásyāḥ ǀ vayám ǀ ní ǀ te ǀ yā́man ǀ ávikṣmahi ǀvṛkṣé ǀ ná ǀ vasatím ǀ váyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visited As birds their nest upon the tree.
verses.wilson_translation: May she be favourable to us today upon whose approach we re-enter (our dwellings), as birds(re-enter) their nest upon the tree.
verses.griffith_verse: So favour us this night, O thou whose pathways we have visited As birds their nest upon the tree.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नि ग्रामासो अविक्षत नि पद्वंतो नि पक्षिणः ।नि श्येनासश्चिदर्थिनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ní ǀ grā́māsaḥ ǀ avikṣata ǀ ní ǀ pat-vántaḥ ǀ ní ǀ pakṣíṇaḥ ǀní ǀ śyenā́saḥ ǀ cit ǀ arthínaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies, Even the falcons fain for prey.
verses.wilson_translation: Men have re-entered (their dwellings), and beasts and birds and the swift hawks.
verses.griffith_verse: The villagers have sought their homes, and all that walks and all that flies, Even the falcons fain for prey.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यावया वृक्यं वृकं यवय स्तेनमूर्म्ये ।अथा नः सुतरा भव ॥
verses.transliteration: yaváya ǀ vṛkyám ǀ vṛ́kam ǀ yaváya ǀ stenám ǀ ūrmye ǀátha ǀ naḥ ǀ su-tárā ǀ bhava ǁ
verses.english_translation: Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away; Easy be thou for us to pass.
verses.wilson_translation: Keep off, O Ūrmya, the she-wolf, keep off the wolf and the robber, and be safely passed by us.
verses.griffith_verse: Keep off the she-wolf and the wolf, O Urmya, keep the thief away; Easy be thou for us to pass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप मा पेपिशत्तमः कृष्णं व्यक्तमस्थित ।उष ऋणेव यातय ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ mā ǀ pépiśat ǀ támaḥ ǀ kṛṣṇám ǀ ví-aktam ǀ asthita ǀúṣaḥ ǀ ṛṇā́-iva ǀ yātaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues: O Morning, cancel it like debts.
verses.wilson_translation: The all-embracing black diffused darkness has approached me, discharge it, Uṣas, as if it were adebt.
verses.griffith_verse: Clearly hath she come nigh to me who decks the dark with richest hues: O Morning, cancel it like debts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप ते गा इवाकरं वृणीष्व दुहितर्दिवः ।रात्रि स्तोमं न जिग्युषे ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ te ǀ gā́ḥ-iva ǀ ā́ ǀ akaram ǀ vṛṇīṣvá ǀ duhitaḥ ǀ divaḥ ǀrā́tri ǀ stómam ǀ ná ǀ jigyúṣe ǁ
verses.english_translation: These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, accept This laud as for a conqueror.
verses.wilson_translation: I have brought (these verses) before you like kine; accept, O Night, daughter of the sky, (my oblation)as the eulogy of one about to conquer.
verses.griffith_verse: These have I brought to thee like kine. O Night, thou Child of Heaven, accept This laud as for a conqueror.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXVIII. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies.May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat. May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni.Mine be the middle air's extended region, and may the wind blow favouring these my wishes. May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me.Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us. For me let them present all mine oblations, and let my mind's intention be accomplished.May I he guiltless of the least transgression: and, all ye Gods, do ye combine to bless us. Ye six divine Expanses, grant us freedom: here, all ye Gods, acquit yourselves like heroes.Let us not lose our children or our bodies: let us not benefit the foe, King Soma! Baffling the wrath of our opponents, Agni, guard us as our infallible Protector.Let these thy foes turn back and seek their houses, and let their thought who watch at home be ruined. Lord of the world, Creator of creators the saviour God who overcomes the foeman.May Gods, Bṛhaspati, both Aśvins shelter from ill this sacrifice and sacrificer. Foodful, and much-invoked, at this our calling may the great Bull vouchsafe us wide protection.Lord of Bay Coursers, Indra, blew our children: harm us not, give us not as prey to others. Let those who are our foemen stay. afar from us: with Indra and with Agni we will drive them off.Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras have exalted me, made me far-reaching, mighty, thinker, sovran lord.

verses.sanskrit: ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्वस्तु वयं त्वेंधानास्तन्वं पुषेम ।मह्यं नमंतां प्रदिशश्चतस्रस्त्वयाध्यक्षेण पृतना जयेम ॥
verses.transliteration: máma ǀ agne ǀ várcaḥ ǀ vi-havéṣu ǀ astu ǀ vayám ǀ tvā ǀ índhānāḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ puṣema ǀmáhyam ǀ namantām ǀ pra-díśaḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǀ tváyā ǀ ádhi-akṣeṇa ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ jayema ǁ
verses.english_translation: LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies. May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat.
verses.wilson_translation: May glory Agni, be mine in battle, may we, kindling you, cherish your person n, may the (inhabitants ofthe) four quarters bow down before me, may we with you for our leader overcome (hostile) armies.
verses.griffith_verse: LET me win glory, Agni, in our battles: enkindling thee, may we support our bodies. May the four regions bend and bow before me: with thee for guardian may we win in combat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मम देवा विहवे संतु सर्व इंद्रवंतो मरुतो विष्णुरग्निः ।ममांतरिक्षमुरुलोकमस्तु मह्यं वातः पवतां कामे अस्मिन् ॥
verses.transliteration: máma ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vi-havé ǀ santu ǀ sárve ǀ índra-vantaḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀmáma ǀ antárikṣam ǀ urú-lokam ǀ astu ǀ máhyam ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ pavatām ǀ kā́me ǀ asmín ǁ
verses.english_translation: May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni. Mine be the middle air's extended region, and may the wind blow favouring these my wishes.
verses.wilson_translation: May all the gods be on my side in battle, the Marutswith Indra,Viṣṇuand Agni; may the expandedfirmament be mine, may the wind blow (propitiously) to this my desire.
verses.griffith_verse: May all the Gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts led by Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni. Mine be the middle air's extended region, and may the wind blow favouring these my wishes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मयि देवा द्रविणमा यजंतां मय्याशीरस्तु मयि देवहूतिः ।दैव्या होतारो वनुषंत पूर्वेऽरिष्टाः स्याम तन्वा सुवीराः ॥
verses.transliteration: máyi ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ā́ ǀ yajantām ǀ máyi ǀ ā-śī́ḥ ǀ astu ǀ máyi ǀ devá-hūtiḥ ǀdáivyāḥ ǀ hótāraḥ ǀ vanuṣanta ǀ pū́rve ǀ áriṣṭāḥ ǀ syāma ǀ tanvā́ ǀ su-vī́rāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me. Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the gods bestow wealth upon me, may (their) blessing be upon me, may the sacrifice in which thegods are invoked be (beneficial) to me, may my invokers of the gods be the first to propitiate them; may we beunharmed in body and blessed withmaleoffspring.
verses.griffith_verse: May the Gods grant me riches; may the blessing and invocation of the Gods assist me. Foremost in fight be the divine Invokers: may we, unwounded, have brave heroes round us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मह्यं यजंतु मम यानि हव्याकूतिः सत्या मनसो मे अस्तु ।एनो मा नि गां कतमच्चनाहं विश्वे देवासो अधि वोचता नः ॥
verses.transliteration: máhyam ǀ yajantu ǀ máma ǀ yā́ni ǀ havyā́ ǀ ā́-kūtiḥ ǀ satyā́ ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ me ǀ astu ǀénaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ ní ǀ gām ǀ katamát ǀ caná ǀ ahám ǀ víśve ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ vocata ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For me let them present all mine oblations, and let my mind's intention be accomplished. May I he guiltless of the least transgression: and, all ye Gods, do ye combine to bless us.
verses.wilson_translation: May (my priests) offer for me whatever oblations of mine (there may be); may the purpose of my mindbe sincere; may I not fall into any kind of sin; universal gods, bless us.
verses.griffith_verse: For me let them present all mine oblations, and let my mind's intention be accomplished. May I he guiltless of the least transgression: and, all ye Gods, do ye combine to bless us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: देवीः षळुर्वीरुरु नः कृणोत विश्वे देवास इह वीरयध्वं ।मा हास्महि प्रजया मा तनूभिर्मा रधाम द्विषते सोम राजन् ॥
verses.transliteration: dévīḥ ǀ ṣaṭ ǀ urvīḥ ǀ urú ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛṇota ǀ víśve ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ vīrayadhvam ǀmā́ ǀ hāsmahi ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ mā́ ǀ tanū́bhiḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ radhāma ǀ dviṣaté ǀ soma ǀ rājan ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye six divine Expanses, grant us freedom: here, all ye Gods, acquit yourselves like heroes. Let us not lose our children or our bodies: let us not benefit the foe, King Soma!
verses.wilson_translation: You six mighty goddesses, bestow upon us ample (wealth); universal gods, display prowess here; letus not be bereft of our offspring, or be harmed in our bodies, may we not become subject to our enemy, royal Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye six divine Expanses, grant us freedom: here, all ye Gods, acquit yourselves like heroes. Let us not lose our children or our bodies: let us not benefit the foe, King Soma!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने मन्युं प्रतिनुदन्परेषामदब्धो गोपाः परि पाहि नस्त्वं ।प्रत्यंचो यंतु निगुतः पुनस्तेऽमैषां चित्तं प्रबुधां वि नेशत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ manyúm ǀ prati-nudán ǀ páreṣām ǀ ádabdhaḥ ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ pári ǀ pāhi ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀpratyáñcaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ ni-gútaḥ ǀ púnaríti ǀ té ǀ amā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ cittám ǀ pra-búdhām ǀ ví ǀ neśat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Baffling the wrath of our opponents, Agni, guard us as our infallible Protector. Let these thy foes turn back and seek their houses, and let their thought who watch at home be ruined.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are an invincible protector, do you defend us, baffling the wrath of our enemies; let themreturn grumbling to their homes, may the intelligence of those watchful (foes) be at once destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: Baffling the wrath of our opponents, Agni, guard us as our infallible Protector. Let these thy foes turn back and seek their houses, and let their thought who watch at home be ruined.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: धाता धातॄणां भुवनस्य यस्पतिर्देवं त्रातारमभिमातिषाहं ।इमं यज्ञमश्विनोभा बृहस्पतिर्देवाः पांतु यजमानं न्यर्थात् ॥
verses.transliteration: dhātā́ ǀ dhātṝṇā́m ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ yáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ devám ǀ trātā́ram ǀ abhimāti-sahám ǀimám ǀ yajñám ǀ aśvínā ǀ ubhā́ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ pāntu ǀ yájamānam ǀ ni-arthā́t ǁ
verses.english_translation: Lord of the world, Creator of creators the saviour God who overcomes the foeman. May Gods, Bṛhaspati, both Aśvins shelter from ill this sacrifice and sacrificer.
verses.wilson_translation: The creator of creators, he who is the protector of the universe, (him I praise), the divine defender, thedestroyer of enemies; may the two Aśvins,Bṛhaspati, and the gods, protect this sacrifice, and save the sacrificerfrom disappointment.
verses.griffith_verse: Lord of the world, Creator of creators the saviour God who overcomes the foeman. May Gods, Bṛhaspati, both Aśvins shelter from ill this sacrifice and sacrificer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उरुव्यचा नो महिषः शर्म यंसदस्मिन्हवे पुरुहूतः पुरुक्षुः ।स नः प्रजायै हर्यश्व मृळयेंद्र मा नो रीरिषो मा परा दाः ॥
verses.transliteration: uru-vyácāḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ mahiṣáḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yaṃsat ǀ asmín ǀ háve ǀ puru-hūtáḥ ǀ puru-kṣúḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pra-jā́yai ǀ hari-aśva ǀ mṛḷaya ǀ índra ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ririṣaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ párā ǀ dāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Foodful, and much-invoked, at this our calling may the great Bull vouchsafe us wide protection. Lord of Bay Coursers, Indra, blew our children: harm us not, give us not as prey to others.
verses.wilson_translation: May the omnipresent (Indra), the mighty one, who is invoked by many, and lauded by many, bestow ablessing on this our sacrifice; be gracious to our offspring, Indra, lord of bay horses; harm us not, desert us not.
verses.griffith_verse: Foodful, and much-invoked, at this our calling may the great Bull vouchsafe us wide protection. Lord of Bay Coursers, Indra, blew our children: harm us not, give us not as prey to others.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ये नः सपत्ना अप ते भवंत्विंद्राग्निभ्यामव बाधामहे तान् ।वसवो रुद्रा आदित्या उपरिस्पृशं मोग्रं चेत्तारमधिराजमक्रन् ॥
verses.transliteration: yé ǀ naḥ ǀ sa-pátnāḥ ǀ ápa ǀ té ǀ bhavantu ǀ indrāgní-bhyām ǀ áva ǀ bādhāmahe ǀ tā́n ǀvásavaḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ upari-spṛ́śam ǀ mā ǀ ugrám ǀ céttāram ǀ adhi-rājám ǀ akran ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let those who are our foemen stay. afar from us: with Indra and with Agni we will drive them off. Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras have exalted me, made me far-reaching, mighty, thinker, sovran lord.
verses.wilson_translation: May those who are our foes be driven off; may we through Indraand Agnidestroy them; may the Vasus, the Rudras, and theĀdityasmake me the high- reaching, fierce, intelligent, supreme ruler.
verses.griffith_verse: Let those who are our foemen stay. afar from us: with Indra and with Agni we will drive them off. Vasus, Ādityas, Rudras have exalted me, made me far-reaching, mighty, thinker, sovran lord.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXIX. Creation.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THEN was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it.What covered in, and where? and what gave shelter? Was water there, unfathomed depth of water? Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider.That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever. Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness this All was indiscriminated chaos.All that existed then was void and form less: by the great power of Warmth was born that Unit. Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit.Sages who searched with their heart's thought discovered the existent's kinship in the non-existent. Transversely was their severing line extended: what was above it then, and what below it?There were begetters, there were mighty forces, free action here and energy up yonder Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation?The Gods are later than this world's production. Who knows then whence it first came into being? He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it,Whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.

verses.sanskrit: नासदासीन्नो सदासीत्तदानीं नासीद्रजो नो व्योमा परो यत् ।किमावरीवः कुह कस्य शर्मन्नंभः किमासीद्गहनं गभीरं ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ ásat ǀ āsīt ǀ nó íti ǀ sát ǀ āsīt ǀ tadā́nīm ǀ ná ǀ āsīt ǀ rájaḥ ǀ nó íti ǀ ví-oma ǀ paráḥ ǀ yát ǀkím ǀ ā́ ǀ avarīvaríti ǀ kúha ǀ kásya ǀ śárman ǀ ámbhaḥ ǀ kím ǀ āsīt ǀ gáhanam ǀ gabhīrám ǁ
verses.english_translation: THEN was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it. What covered in, and where? and what gave shelter? Was water there, unfathomed depth of water?
verses.wilson_translation: The non-existent was not, the existent was not; then the world was not, not the firmament, nor thatwhich is above (the firmament). How could there by any investing envelope, and where? Of what (could there be)felicity? How (could there be) the deep unfathomable water?
verses.griffith_verse: THEN was not non-existent nor existent: there was no realm of air, no sky beyond it. What covered in, and where? and what gave shelter? Was water there, unfathomed depth of water?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न आसीत्प्रकेतः ।आनीदवातं स्वधया तदेकं तस्माद्धान्यन्न परः किं चनास ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ mṛtyúḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ ná ǀ tárhi ǀ ná ǀ rā́tryāḥ ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ pra-ketáḥ ǀā́nīt ǀ avātám ǀ svadháyā ǀ tát ǀ ékam ǀ tásmāt ǀ ha ǀ anyát ǀ ná ǀ paráḥ ǀ kím ǀ caná ǀ āsa ǁ
verses.english_translation: Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider. That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever.
verses.wilson_translation: Death was not nor at that period immortality, there was no indication of day, of night; That Oneunbreathed upon breathed of his own strength, other than That there was nothing else whatever.
verses.griffith_verse: Death was not then, nor was there aught immortal: no sign was there, the day's and night's divider. That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तम आसीत्तमसा गूळ्हमग्रेऽप्रकेतं सलिलं सर्वमा इदं ।तुच्छ्येनाभ्वपिहितं यदासीत्तपसस्तन्महिनाजायतैकं ॥
verses.transliteration: támaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ támasā ǀ gūḷhám ǀ ágre ǀ apra-ketám ǀ salilám ǀ sárvam ǀ āḥ ǀ idám ǀtucchyéna ǀ ābhú ǀ ápi-hitam ǀ yát ǀ ā́sīt ǀ tápasaḥ ǀ tát ǀ mahinā́ ǀ ajāyata ǀ ékam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness this All was indiscriminated chaos. All that existed then was void and form less: by the great power of Warmth was born that Unit.
verses.wilson_translation: There was darkness covered by darkness in the beginning, all this (world) was undistinguishablewater; that empty united (world) which was covered by a mere nothing, was produced through the power ofausterity.
verses.griffith_verse: Darkness there was: at first concealed in darkness this All was indiscriminated chaos. All that existed then was void and form less: by the great power of Warmth was born that Unit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कामस्तदग्रे समवर्तताधि मनसो रेतः प्रथमं यदासीत् ।सतो बंधुमसति निरविंदन्हृदि प्रतीष्या कवयो मनीषा ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́maḥ ǀ tát ǀ ágre ǀ sám ǀ avartata ǀ ádhi ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ rétaḥ ǀ prathamám ǀ yát ǀ ā́sīt ǀsatáḥ ǀ bándhum ǀ ásati ǀ níḥ ǀ avindan ǀ hṛdí ǀ prati-íṣya ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ manīṣā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit. Sages who searched with their heart's thought discovered the existent's kinship in the non-existent.
verses.wilson_translation: In the beginning there was desire, which was the first seed of mind; sages having meditated in theirhearts have discovered by their wisdom the connexion of the existent with te non-existent.
verses.griffith_verse: Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire, the primal seed and germ of Spirit. Sages who searched with their heart's thought discovered the existent's kinship in the non-existent.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तिरश्चीनो विततो रश्मिरेषामधः स्विदासीदुपरि स्विदासीत् ।रेतोधा आसन्महिमान आसन्त्स्वधा अवस्तात्प्रयतिः परस्तात् ॥
verses.transliteration: tiraścī́naḥ ǀ ví-tataḥ ǀ raśmíḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ adháḥ ǀ svit ǀ āsī́t ǀ upári ǀ svit ǀ āsī́t ǀretaḥ-dhā́ḥ ǀ āsan ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ āsan ǀ svadhā́ ǀ avástāt ǀ prá-yatiḥ ǀ parástāt ǁ
verses.english_translation: Transversely was their severing line extended: what was above it then, and what below it? There were begetters, there were mighty forces, free action here and energy up yonder
verses.wilson_translation: Their ray was stretched out, whether across, or below, or above; (some) were shedders of seed,(others) were mighty; food was inferior; the eater was superior.
verses.griffith_verse: Transversely was their severing line extended: what was above it then, and what below it? There were begetters, there were mighty forces, free action here and energy up yonder
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: को अद्धा वेद क इह प्र वोचत्कुत आजाता कुत इयं विसृष्टिः ।अर्वाग्देवा अस्य विसर्जनेनाथा को वेद यत आबभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ addhā́ ǀ veda ǀ káḥ ǀ ihá ǀ prá ǀ vocat ǀ kútaḥ ǀ ā́-jātā ǀ kútaḥ ǀ iyám ǀ ví-sṛṣṭiḥ ǀarvā́k ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ asyá ǀ vi-sárjanena ǀ átha ǀ káḥ ǀ veda ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā-babhū́va ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation? The Gods are later than this world's production. Who knows then whence it first came into being?
verses.wilson_translation: Who really knows? Who in this world may declare it! whence was this creation, whence was itengendered? The gods (were) subsequent to the (world's) creation; so who knows whence it arose?
verses.griffith_verse: Who verily knows and who can here declare it, whence it was born and whence comes this creation? The Gods are later than this world's production. Who knows then whence it first came into being?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इयं विसृष्टिर्यत आबभूव यदि वा दधे यदि वा न ।यो अस्याध्यक्षः परमे व्योमन्त्सो अंग वेद यदि वा न वेद ॥
verses.transliteration: iyám ǀ ví-sṛṣṭiḥ ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā-babhū́va ǀ yádi ǀ vā ǀ dadhé ǀ yádi ǀ vā ǀ ná ǀyáḥ ǀ asya ǀ ádhi-akṣaḥ ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǀ sáḥ ǀ aṅgá ǀ veda ǀ yádi ǀ vā ǀ ná ǀ véda ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it, Whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.
verses.wilson_translation: He from whom this creation arose, he may uphold it, or he may not (no one else can); he who is itssuperintendent in the highest heaven, he assuredly knows, or if he knows not (no one else does).
verses.griffith_verse: He, the first origin of this creation, whether he formed it all or did not form it, Whose eye controls this world in highest heaven, he verily knows it, or perhaps he knows not.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXX. Creation.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,—This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back. The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it.These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sāma-hymns their weaving shuttles. What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter?What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship? Closely was Gāyatrī conjoined with Agni, and closely Savitar combined with Usnih.Brilliant with Ukthas, Soma joined Anustup: Bṛhaspati's voice by Brhati was aided. Virāj adhered to Varuṇa and Mitra: here Triṣṭup day by day was Indra's portion.Jagatī entered all the Gods together: so by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis. So by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis, when ancient sacrifice sprang up, our Fathers.With the mind's eye I think that I behold them who first performed this sacrificial worship. They who were versed in ritual and metre, in hymns and rules, were the Seven Godlike Ṛṣis.Viewing the path of those of old, the sages have taken up the reins like chariot-drivers.

verses.sanskrit: यो यज्ञो विश्वतस्तंतुभिस्तत एकशतं देवकर्मेभिरायतः ।इमे वयंति पितरो य आययुः प्र वयाप वयेत्यासते तते ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ tántu-bhiḥ ǀ tatáḥ ǀ éka-śatam ǀ deva-karmébhiḥ ǀ ā́-yataḥ ǀimé ǀ vayanti ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ yé ǀ ā-yayúḥ ǀ prá ǀ vaya ǀ ápa ǀ vaya ǀ íti ǀ āsate ǀ taté ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,— This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back.
verses.wilson_translation: The sacrifice which is extended on every side by the threads (of created things) spread out by theworship of the gods for a hundred and one (years), these our progenitors, who have preceded us, weave it,weaving forwards, weaving backwards, they worship (Prajāpati) when (the world) is woven.
verses.griffith_verse: THE sacrifice drawn out with threads on every side, stretched by a hundred sacred ministers and one,— This do these Fathers weave who hitherward are come: they sit beside the warp and cry, Weave forth, weave back.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुमाँ एनं तनुत उत्कृणत्ति पुमान्वि तत्ने अधि नाके अस्मिन् ।इमे मयूखा उप सेदुरू सदः सामानि चक्रुस्तसराण्योतवे ॥
verses.transliteration: púmān ǀ enam ǀ tanute ǀ út ǀ kṛṇatti ǀ púmān ǀ ví ǀ tatne ǀ ádhi ǀ nā́ke ǀ asmín ǀimé ǀ mayū́khāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ seduḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sádaḥ ǀ sā́māni ǀ cakruḥ ǀ tásarāṇi ǀ ótave ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it. These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sāma-hymns their weaving shuttles.
verses.wilson_translation: The first man spreads out this (web), the first man rolls it up, he spread it above in this heaven; thesehis rays have sat down on the seat (of sacrifice), they have made the prayers serve as shuttles for weaving.
verses.griffith_verse: The Man extends it and the Man unbinds it: even to this vault of heaven hath he outspun, it. These pegs are fastened to the seat of worship: they made the Sāma-hymns their weaving shuttles.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कासीत्प्रमा प्रतिमा किं निदानमाज्यं किमासीत्परिधिः क आसीत् ।छंदः किमासीत्प्रउगं किमुक्थं यद्देवा देवमयजंत विश्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: kā́ ǀ āsīt ǀ pra-mā́ ǀ prati-mā́ ǀ kím ǀ ni-dā́nam ǀ ā́jyam ǀ kím ǀ āsīt ǀ pari-dhíḥ ǀ káḥ ǀ āsīt ǀchándaḥ ǀ kím ǀ āsīt ǀ prá_ugam ǀ kím ǀ ukthám ǀ yát ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ devám ǀ áyajanta ǀ víśve ǁ
verses.english_translation: What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter? What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship?
verses.wilson_translation: What was the authority (of the sacrifice), what was thelimitation, what was the first cause, what wasthe clarified butter, what was the enclosure, what was the metre, what was pra-uga text, when the universal godsoffered worship to the gods?
verses.griffith_verse: What were the rule, the order and the model? What were the wooden fender and the butter? What were the hymn, the chant, the recitation, when to the God all Deities paid worship?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अग्नेर्गायत्र्यभवत्सयुग्वोष्णिहया सविता सं बभूव ।अनुष्टुभा सोम उक्थैर्महस्वान्बृहस्पतेर्बृहती वाचमावत् ॥
verses.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ gāyatrī́ ǀ abhavat ǀ sa-yúgvā ǀ uṣṇíhayā ǀ savitā́ ǀ sám ǀ babhūva ǀanu-stúbhā ǀ sómaḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ máhasvān ǀ bṛ́haspáteḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ ǀ vā́cam ǀ āvat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Closely was Gāyatrī conjoined with Agni, and closely Savitar combined with Usnih. Brilliant with Ukthas, Soma joined Anustup: Bṛhaspati's voice by Brhati was aided.
verses.wilson_translation: Gāyatrībecame the associate of Agni,Savitābecame combined with Uṣṇik,Somaradiant withsacred praises (was united) with Anuṣṭup,Bṛhatīgave efficacy to the words of Bṛhaspati.
verses.griffith_verse: Closely was Gāyatrī conjoined with Agni, and closely Savitar combined with Usnih. Brilliant with Ukthas, Soma joined Anustup: Bṛhaspati's voice by Brhati was aided.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विराण्मित्रावरुणयोरभिश्रीरिंद्रस्य त्रिष्टुबिह भागो अह्नः ।विश्वांदेवांजगत्या विवेश तेन चाकॢप्र ऋषयो मनुष्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: virā́ṭ ǀ mitrā́váruṇayoḥ ǀ abhi-śrī́ḥ ǀ índrasya ǀ tri-stúp ǀ ihá ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ áhnaḥ ǀvíśvān ǀ devā́n ǀ jágatī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǀ téna ǀ cākḽpre ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Virāj adhered to Varuṇa and Mitra: here Triṣṭup day by day was Indra's portion. Jagatī entered all the Gods together: so by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis.
verses.wilson_translation: Virāt. was the glory of Mitraand Varuṇa;Triṣṭubhwas Indra's portion of the midday (oblation) atand 5 answer the question, what was the metre? Two of the other questions- those relating to the butter (ājya)and the enclosure (paridhi)-- have been answered, in the Puruṣa sūkta, 10.90; cf.Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa3.12.9]. beholding them with the eye of the mind, I glorify those who of old celebrated this sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Virāj adhered to Varuṇa and Mitra: here Triṣṭup day by day was Indra's portion. Jagatī entered all the Gods together: so by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चाकॢप्रे तेन ऋषयो मनुष्या यज्ञे जाते पितरो नः पुराणे ।पश्यन्मन्ये मनसा चक्षसा तान्य इमं यज्ञमयजंत पूर्वे ॥
verses.transliteration: cākḽpré ǀ téna ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ yajñé ǀ jāté ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ purāṇé ǀpáśyan ǀ manye ǀ mánasā ǀ cákṣasā ǀ tā́n ǀ yé ǀ imám ǀ yajñám ǀ áyajanta ǀ pū́rve ǁ
verses.english_translation: So by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis, when ancient sacrifice sprang up, our Fathers. With the mind's eye I think that I behold them who first performed this sacrificial worship.
verses.griffith_verse: So by this knowledge men were raised to Ṛṣis, when ancient sacrifice sprang up, our Fathers. With the mind's eye I think that I behold them who first performed this sacrificial worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सहस्तोमाः सहच्छंदस आवृतः सहप्रमा ऋषयः सप्त दैव्याः ।पूर्वेषां पंथामनुदृश्य धीरा अन्वालेभिरे रथ्यो न रश्मीन् ॥
verses.transliteration: sahá-stomāḥ ǀ sahá-chandasaḥ ǀ ā-vṛ́taḥ ǀ sahá-pramāḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ saptá ǀ dáivyāḥ ǀpū́rveṣām ǀ pánthām ǀ anu-dṛ́śya ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ anu-ā́lebhire ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmī́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: They who were versed in ritual and metre, in hymns and rules, were the Seven Godlike Ṛṣis. Viewing the path of those of old, the sages have taken up the reins like chariot-drivers.
verses.griffith_verse: They who were versed in ritual and metre, in hymns and rules, were the Seven Godlike Ṛṣis. Viewing the path of those of old, the sages have taken up the reins like chariot-drivers.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXI. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ७ सुकीर्तिः काक्षीवत्। इन्द्रः,४-५ अश्विनौ। त्रिष्टुप् , ४ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern.Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful. What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order,So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship. Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies.Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship. Ye, Aśvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice,And aided Indra in his work with Namuci of Asura birth. As parents aid a son, both Aśvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous Powers and wisdom.When thou, with might. hadst drunk the draught that gladdens, Sarasvatī, O Maghavan, refreshed thee. Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious.May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigou r. May we enjoy his favour, his the Holy may we enjoy his blessed loving kindness.May this rich Indra, as our good Protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.

verses.sanskrit: अप प्राच इंद्र विश्वाँ अमित्रानपापाचो अभिभूते नुदस्व ।अपोदीचो अप शूराधराच उरौ यथा तव शर्मन्मदेम ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ prā́caḥ ǀ indra ǀ víśvān ǀ amítrān ǀ ápa ǀ ápācaḥ ǀ abhi-bhūte ǀ nudasva ǀápa ǀ údīcaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ śūra ǀ adharā́caḥ ǀ uráu ǀ yáthā ǀ táva ǀ śárman ǀ mádema ǁ
verses.english_translation: DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern. Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.
verses.wilson_translation: Victorious Indra, drive off all our foes, those who dwell in the east, and those who dwell in the west,(drive) off, O hero, those who dwell in the north, and those who dwell in the south, that we may rejoice in yourexceeding felicity.
verses.griffith_verse: DRIVE all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Conqueror, and the eastern. Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कुविदंग यवमंतो यवं चिद्यथा दांत्यनुपूर्वं वियूय ।इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोवृक्तिं न जग्मुः ॥
verses.transliteration: kuvít ǀ aṅgá ǀ yáva-mantaḥ ǀ yávam ǀ cit ǀ yáthā ǀ dā́nti ǀ anu-pūrvám ǀ vi-yū́ya ǀihá-iha ǀ eṣām ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ bhójanāni ǀ yé ǀ barhíṣaḥ ǀ námaḥ-vṛktim ǀ ná ǀ jagmúḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order, So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship.
verses.wilson_translation: As the growers of barley often cut the barley, separating it uin due order, so do you, (OIndra), bestowhere and there nourishment upon those who have not neglected the performance of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order, So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who went not to prepare the grass for worship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि स्थूर्यृतुथा यातमस्ति नोत श्रवो विविदे संगमेषु ।गव्यंत इंद्रं सख्याय विप्रा अश्वायंतो वृषणं वाजयंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ sthū́ri ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ yātám ǀ ásti ǀ ná ǀ utá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ vivide ǀ sam-gaméṣu ǀgavyántaḥ ǀ índram ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ víprāḥ ǀ aśva-yántaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vājáyantaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies. Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.
verses.wilson_translation: The cart has not arrived in due season, nor does he acquire fame in battles, (let us), the sages,desiring cattle, desiring horses, desiring food, (solicit)Indra, the showerer, for his friendship.
verses.griffith_verse: Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies. Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं सुराममश्विना नमुचावासुरे सचा ।विपिपाना शुभस्पती इंद्रं कर्मस्वावतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ surā́mam ǀ aśvinā ǀ námucau ǀ āsuré ǀ sácā ǀvi-pipānā́ ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ índram ǀ kárma-su ǀ āvatam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye, Aśvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice, And aided Indra in his work with Namuci of Asura birth.
verses.wilson_translation: You, OAśvins, lords of light, having drunk the grateful (libation), jointly preserved Indrain battleagainst the Asura Namuci.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye, Aśvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice, And aided Indra in his work with Namuci of Asura birth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रमिव पितरावश्विनोभेंद्रावथुः काव्यैर्दंसनाभिः ।यत्सुरामं व्यपिबः शचीभिः सरस्वती त्वा मघवन्नभिष्णक् ॥
verses.transliteration: putrám-iva ǀ pitárau ǀ aśvínā ǀ ubhā́ ǀ índra ǀ āváthuḥ ǀ kā́vyaiḥ ǀ daṃsánābhiḥ ǀyát ǀ surā́mam ǀ ví ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ sárasvatī ǀ tvā ǀ magha-van ǀ abhiṣṇak ǁ
verses.english_translation: As parents aid a son, both Aśvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous Powers and wisdom. When thou, with might. hadst drunk the draught that gladdens, Sarasvatī, O Maghavan, refreshed thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Both the Aśvinsdefended (you),Indra, like two fathers (defending) a son with glorious exploits; when(triumphing) through the deeds of valour, you drank the grateful libation,Sarasvatīapproached you, OMaghavat.
verses.griffith_verse: As parents aid a son, both Aśvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous Powers and wisdom. When thou, with might. hadst drunk the draught that gladdens, Sarasvatī, O Maghavan, refreshed thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रः सुत्रामा स्ववाँ अवोभिः सुमृळीको भवतु विश्ववेदाः ।बाधतां द्वेषो अभयं कृणोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥
verses.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ su-trā́mā ǀ svá-vān ǀ ávaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ su-mṛḷīkáḥ ǀ bhavatu ǀ viśvá-vedāḥ ǀbā́dhatām ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ ábhayam ǀ kṛṇotu ǀ su-vī́ryasya ǀ pátayaḥ ǀ syāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious. May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigou r.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, the protector, the possessor of treat wealth, the all- knowing, be favourable (to us) with hisprotections; may he confound our enemies, may he make us free from fear, may we be the parents of excellentmale offspring.
verses.griffith_verse: Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious. May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigou r.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम ।स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इंद्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥
verses.transliteration: tásya ǀ vayám ǀ su-matáu ǀ yajñíyasya ǀ ápi ǀ bhadré ǀ saumanasé ǀ syāma ǀsáḥ ǀ su-trā́mā ǀ svá-vān ǀ índraḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ ārā́t ǀ cit ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyotu ǁ
verses.english_translation: May we enjoy his favour, his the Holy may we enjoy his blessed loving kindness. May this rich Indra, as our good Protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: May we be ever in (the enjoyment of) the favour of that adorable divinity (retained) in his favourablethoughts, and may the protecting and opulent Indradrive away far off us those who hate us.
verses.griffith_verse: May we enjoy his favour, his the Holy may we enjoy his blessed loving kindness. May this rich Indra, as our good Protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXII. Mitra. Varuṇa.
hymns.anukramani: ७ शकपूतो नार्मेधः। मित्रावरुणौ, १ द्युभूम्यश्विनः। विराड्रूपा, १ न्यङ्कुसारिणी, २,६ प्रस्तारपंक्तिः, ७ महासतोबृहती।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice,And may the Aśvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss. As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk.So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends. And when we seek to win your love and friendship, weẉho have precious wealth in our possession,Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuṇa, the King of all men.The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great.This sin hath Sakaputa here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth,When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful. Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven.Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light. Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood.These our disheartened tribes Nrmedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.

verses.sanskrit: ईजानमिद्द्यौर्गूर्तावसुरीजानं भूमिरभि प्रभूषणि ।ईजानं देवावश्विनावभि सुम्नैरवर्धतां ॥
verses.transliteration: ījānám ǀ ít ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ gūrtá-vasuḥ ǀ ījānám ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ abhí ǀ pra-bhūṣáṇi ǀījānám ǀ deváu ǀ aśvínau ǀ abhí ǀ sumnáiḥ ǀ avardhatām ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice, And may the Aśvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.
verses.wilson_translation: The Heaven liberal of treasure (prospers) the sacrificer, the Earth (prospers) the sacrificer because ofthe ornament, the divine Aśvinsprospered the sacrificer with blessings.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice, And may the Aśvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ता वां मित्रावरुणा धारयत्क्षिती सुषुम्नेषितत्वता यजामसि ।युवोः क्राणाय सख्यैरभि ष्याम रक्षसः ॥
verses.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vām ǀ mitrāvaruṇā ǀ dhārayátkṣitī íti dhārayát-kṣitī ǀ su-sumnā́ ǀ iṣitatvátā ǀ yajāmasi ǀyuvóḥ ǀ krāṇā́ya ǀ sakhyáiḥ ǀ abhí ǀ syāma ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk. So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.
verses.wilson_translation: Mitraand Varuṇa, who sustain the earth, we worship you, the givers of felicity, for the sake ofattaining our desires; may we, through your favour for the performer (of the sacrifice), overcome therākṣasas.
verses.griffith_verse: As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk. So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अधा चिन्नु यद्दिधिषामहे वामभि प्रियं रेक्णः पत्यमानाः ।दद्वाँ वा यत्पुष्यति रेक्णः सम्वारन्नकिरस्य मघानि ॥
verses.transliteration: ádha ǀ cit ǀ nú ǀ yát ǀ dídhiṣāmahe ǀ vām ǀ abhí ǀ priyám ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ pátyamānāḥ ǀdadvā́n ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ púṣyati ǀ rékṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ āran ǀ nákiḥ ǀ asya ǀ maghā́ni ǁ
verses.english_translation: And when we seek to win your love and friendship, weẉho have precious wealth in our possession, Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up
verses.wilson_translation: May we, when we present to you (oblations), quickly alight upon desirable wealth, and the genitive rousman who fosters his wealth, may his riches not depart from him.
verses.griffith_verse: And when we seek to win your love and friendship, weẉho have precious wealth in our possession, Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असावन्यो असुर सूयत द्यौस्त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ।मूर्धा रथस्य चाकन्नैतावतैनसांतकध्रुक् ॥
verses.transliteration: asáu ǀ anyáḥ ǀ asura ǀ sūyata ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ tvám ǀ víśveṣām ǀ varuṇa ǀ asi ǀ rā́jā ǀmūrdhā́ ǀ ráthasya ǀ cākan ǀ ná ǀ etā́vatā ǀ énasā ǀ antaka-dhrúk ǁ
verses.english_translation: That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuṇa, the King of all men. The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great. This sin hath Sakaputa here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth, When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful. 6 Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven. Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light. 7 Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood. These our disheartened tribes Nrmedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.
verses.wilson_translation: (Mitra), scatterer of darkness, the Heaven gave birth to you the other; you,Varuṇa, are sovereignover all. The head of (your) chariot desired (this sacrifice); opposing the destroyer, (the rite) is not (vitiated) bythe smallest defect.
verses.griffith_verse: That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuṇa, the King of all men. The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great. This sin hath Sakaputa here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth, When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful. 6 Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven. Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light. 7 Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood. These our disheartened tribes Nrmedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मिन्त्स्वेतच्छकपूत एनो हिते मित्रे निगतान्हंति वीरान् ।अवोर्वा यद्धात्तनूष्ववः प्रियासु यज्ञियास्वर्वा ॥
verses.transliteration: asmín ǀ sú ǀ etát ǀ śáka-pūte ǀ énaḥ ǀ hité ǀ mitré ǀ ní-gatān ǀ hanti ǀ vīrā́n ǀavóḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ dhā́t ǀ tanū́ṣu ǀ ávaḥ ǀ priyā́su ǀ yajñíyāsu ǀ árvā ǁ
verses.english_translation: This iniquity (found) in this Śakapūta, when Mitrais propitious, destroys opposing heroes, when thei.e., Mitra or Varuṇa; avaḥ = food; when the approaching Mitra (or Varuṇa) gives protection to the sacrificial ritesand bodies of the worshipper who delights him with oblations].
verses.wilson_translation: This iniquity (found) in this Śakapūta, when Mitrais propitious, destroys opposing heroes, when thei.e., Mitra or Varuṇa; avaḥ = food; when the approaching Mitra (or Varuṇa) gives protection to the sacrificial ritesand bodies of the worshipper who delights him with oblations].
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवोर्हि मातादितिर्विचेतसा द्यौर्न भूमिः पयसा पुपूतनि ।अव प्रिया दिदिष्टन सूरो निनिक्त रश्मिभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvóḥ ǀ hí ǀ mātā́ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ vi-cetasā ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ páyasā ǀ pupūtáni ǀáva ǀ priyā́ ǀ didiṣṭana ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ninikta ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O (Mitraand Varuṇa), endowed with various wisdom, your mother Aditi, the earth, (is) for thepurification (of all things) by its libations, as the heaven (purifies by its rain); you display before us precious(treasures), and wash us with the sun's rays.
verses.wilson_translation: O (Mitraand Varuṇa), endowed with various wisdom, your mother Aditi, the earth, (is) for thepurification (of all things) by its libations, as the heaven (purifies by its rain); you display before us precious(treasures), and wash us with the sun's rays.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

verses.sanskrit: युवं ह्यप्नराजावसीदतं तिष्ठद्रथं न धूर्षदं वनर्षदं ।ता नः कण���कयंतीर्नृमेधस्तत्रे अंहसः सुमेधस्तत्रे अंहसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ hí ǀ apna-rā́jau ǀ ásīdatam ǀ tíṣṭhat ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ dhūḥ-sádam ǀ vana-sádam ǀtā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ kaṇūka-yántīḥ ǀ nṛ-médhaḥ ǀ tatre ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ su-médhaḥ ǀ tatre ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: For you, brilliant through your functions, have sat down; now mount, (each of you, his) chariot, whichrests on the yoke, which abides in the forests, (to overcome) those (people) who clamour against us; Nṛmedhawas preserved (by you) from sin, the pious worshipper was preserved from sin.
verses.wilson_translation: For you, brilliant through your functions, have sat down; now mount, (each of you, his) chariot, whichrests on the yoke, which abides in the forests, (to overcome) those (people) who clamour against us; Nṛmedhawas preserved (by you) from sin, the pious worshipper was preserved from sin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896) / H. H. Wilson (1866)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place.Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies. Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth.Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies. Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs.Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would srnite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth. The robber people round about, Indra, who watch and aim at us,—Trample them down beneath thy foot; a conquering scatterer art thou. Whoso assails us, Indra, be the man a stranger or akin,Bring down, thyself, his strength although it be as vast as are the heavens. Close to thy friendship do we cling, O Indra, and depend, or, thee.Lead us beyond all pain and grief along the path of holy Law. Do thou bestow upon us her, O Indra, who yields according to the singer's longing,That the great Cow may, with exhaustless udder, pouring a thousand streams, give milk to feed us.

verses.sanskrit: प्रो ष्वस्मै पुरोरथमिंद्राय शूषमर्चत ।अभीके चिदु लोककृत्संगे समत्सु वृत्रहास्माकं बोधि चोदिता नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: pró íti ǀ sú ǀ asmai ǀ puraḥ-rathám ǀ índrāya ǀ śūṣám ǀ arcata ǀabhī́ke ǀ cit ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ loka-kṛ́t ǀ sam-gé ǀ samát-su ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ bodhi ǀ coditā́ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place. Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: Adore fervently the might of that Indrawhich goes before his chariot; he who makes room for us in the(the adoration paid by us); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: SING strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place. Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं सिंधूँरवासृजोऽधराचो अहन्नहिं ।अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्ञिषे विश्वं पुष्यसि वार्यं तं त्वा परि ष्वजामहे नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ síndhūn ǀ áva ǀ asṛjaḥ ǀ adharā́caḥ ǀ áhan ǀ áhim ǀaśatrúḥ ǀ indra ǀ jajñiṣe ǀ víśvam ǀ puṣyasi ǀ vā́ryam ǀ tám ǀ tvā ǀ pári ǀ svajāmahe ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.wilson_translation: You have sent the rivers away downwards, you have slain Ahi; you are born,Indra, without an enemy,you grant all that is desirable, as such we embrace you; may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies bedestroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि षु विश्वा अरातयोऽर्यो नशंत नो धियः ।अस्तासि शत्रवे वधं यो न इंद्र जिघांसति या ते रातिर्ददिर्वसु नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sú ǀ víśvā ǀ árātayaḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ naśanta ǀ naḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀástā ǀ asi ǀ śátrave ǀ vadhám ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ jíghāṃsati ǀ yā́ ǀ te ǀ rātíḥ ǀ dadíḥ ǀ vásu ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs. Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would srnite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: May all our assailants, who make no offerings, quickly perish, may our praises (be successful); you,Indra, hurl the weapon at the foe who seeks to slay us, may that liberal (hand) of yours be the giver of wealth (tous); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs. Thy bolt thou castest, at the foe, O Indra, who would srnite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो न इंद्राभितो जनो वृकायुरादिदेशति ।अधस्पदं तमीं कृधि विबाधो असि सासहिर्नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ jánaḥ ǀ vṛka-yúḥ ǀ ā-dídeśati ǀadhaḥ-padám ǀ tám ǀ īm ǀ kṛdhi ǀ vi-bādháḥ ǀ asi ǀ sasahíḥ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: The robber people round about, Indra, who watch and aim at us,— Trample them down beneath thy foot; a conquering scatterer art thou.
verses.wilson_translation: The man who, like a wolf, prowls around us, OIndra, cast him beneath our feet, for you are theresister, the overcomer (of foes); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: The robber people round about, Indra, who watch and aim at us,— Trample them down beneath thy foot; a conquering scatterer art thou.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो न इंद्राभिदासति सनाभिर्यश्च निष्ट्यः ।अव तस्य बलं तिर महीव द्यौरध त्मना नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ indra ǀ abhi-dā́sati ǀ sá-nābhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ níṣṭyaḥ ǀáva ǀ tásya ǀ bálam ǀ tira ǀ mahī́-iva ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ádha ǀ tmánā ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Whoso assails us, Indra, be the man a stranger or akin, Bring down, thyself, his strength although it be as vast as are the heavens.
verses.wilson_translation: He who assails us,Indra, whether he be of the same caste or of degraded caste-- scatter of yourselfhis host, (though it be vast) as the wide heaven; may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: Whoso assails us, Indra, be the man a stranger or akin, Bring down, thyself, his strength although it be as vast as are the heavens.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वयमिंद्र त्वायवः सखित्वमा रभामहे ।ऋतस्य नः पथा नयाति विश्वानि दुरिता नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥
verses.transliteration: vayám ǀ indra ǀ tvā-yávaḥ ǀ sakhi-tvám ǀ ā́ ǀ rabhāmahe ǀṛtásya ǀ naḥ ǀ pathā́ ǀ naya ǀ áti ǀ víśvāni ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ nábhantām ǀ anyakéṣām ǀ jyākā́ḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhánva-su ǁ
verses.english_translation: Close to thy friendship do we cling, O Indra, and depend, or, thee. Lead us beyond all pain and grief along the path of holy Law.
verses.wilson_translation: Devoted to you,Indra, we strive after your friendship; lea\d us by the path of sacrifice beyond all evils;may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.
verses.griffith_verse: Close to thy friendship do we cling, O Indra, and depend, or, thee. Lead us beyond all pain and grief along the path of holy Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्मभ्यं सु त्वमिंद्र तां शिक्ष या दोहते प्रति वरं जरित्रे ।अच्छिद्रोध्नी पीपयद्यथा नः सहस्रधारा पयसा मही गौः ॥
verses.transliteration: asmábhyam ǀ sú ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ tā́m ǀ śikṣa ǀ yā́ ǀ dóhate ǀ práti ǀ váram ǀ jaritré ǀácchidra-ūdhnī ǀ pīpáyat ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ sahásra-dhārā ǀ páyasā ǀ mahī́ ǀ gáuḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do thou bestow upon us her, O Indra, who yields according to the singer's longing, That the great Cow may, with exhaustless udder, pouring a thousand streams, give milk to feed us.
verses.wilson_translation: Give to us,Indra, (the cow) who gives milk to the worshipper according to his desire, so that themighty cow, possessed of an unfailing udder, the shedder of a thousand streams, may supply us plural ntifully withmilk.
verses.griffith_verse: Do thou bestow upon us her, O Indra, who yields according to the singer's longing, That the great Cow may, with exhaustless udder, pouring a thousand streams, give milk to feed us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXIV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ७,१-६ (पूर्वार्धस्य) मान्धाता यौवनाश्वः,६ (उत्तरार्धस्य) ७ गोधा ऋषिका। इन्द्रः। महापंक्तिः, ७ पंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven.So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life. Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness.Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life. Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies.With all thy powers, O Śakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down: As thou, O Śatakratu, thou, O Indrv, shakest all things downAs wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold. Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall.Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass. Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor!As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan. Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command.Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.

verses.sanskrit: उभे यदिंद्र रोदसी आपप्राथोषा इव ।महांतं त्वा महीनां सम्राजं चर्षणीनां देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ yát ǀ indra ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ā-paprā́tha ǀ uṣā́ḥ-iva ǀmahā́ntam ǀ tvā ǀ mahī́nām ǀ sam-rā́jam ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven. So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Indra, who will both heaven and earth (with light) like the dawn- - the divine progenitress hasgiven birth to you, the mighty (gods), the sovereign of man; the auspicious progenitress has given you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: As, like the Morning, thou hast filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven. So as the Mighty One, great King of all the mighty world of men, the Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव स्म दुर्हणायतो मर्तस्य तनुहि स्थिरं ।अधस्पदं तमीं कृधि यो अस्माँ आदिदेशति देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ sma ǀ duḥ-hanāyatáḥ ǀ mártasya ǀ tanuhi ǀ sthirám ǀadhaḥ-padám ǀ tám ǀ īm ǀ kṛdhi ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ ā-dídeśati ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.wilson_translation: Enfeeble the strength of the malicious man, cast under foot him who tries to kill us; the divineprogenitress has given you birth, the auspicious progenitress has given you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess Mother brought thee forth, the Blessed Mother gave thee life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव त्या बृहतीरिषो विश्वश्चंद्रा अमित्रहन् ।शचीभिः शक्र धूनुहींद्र विश्वाभिरूतिभिर्देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ tyā́ḥ ǀ bṛhatī́ḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ viśvá-candrāḥ ǀ amitra-han ǀśácībhiḥ ǀ śakra ǀ dhūnuhi ǀ índra ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies. With all thy powers, O Śakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:
verses.wilson_translation: Destroyer of enemies,Indra,Śakra, shake down upon us by your exploits those abundant, all-shiningviands, (accompanied) with all your protections; the divine progenitress has given you birth, the auspiciousprogrenitress has given you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Shake down, O Slayer of the foe, those great all splendid enemies. With all thy powers, O Śakra, all thine helps, O Indra, shake them down:
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव यत्त्वं शतक्रतविंद्र विश्वानि धूनुषे ।रयिं न सुन्वते सचा सहस्रिणीभिरूतिभिर्देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ yát ǀ tvám ǀ śatakrato íti śata-krato ǀ índra ǀ víśvāni ǀ dhūnuṣé ǀrayím ǀ ná ǀ sunvaté ǀ sácā ǀ sahasríṇībhiḥ ǀ ūtí-bhiḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: As thou, O Śatakratu, thou, O Indrv, shakest all things down As wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold.
verses.wilson_translation: When you,Indra,Śatakratu, shake down (upon us) all blessings, (then bestow) upon the offerer of thelibation wealth also, together with your thousandfold protections; the divine progenitress has given you birth, theauspicious progrenitress has given you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: As thou, O Śatakratu, thou, O Indrv, shakest all things down As wealth for him who sheds the juice, with thine assistance thousandfold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अव स्वेदा इवाभितो विष्वक्पतंतु दिद्यवः ।दूर्वाया इव तंतवो व्यस्मदेतु दुर्मतिर्देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ svédāḥ-iva ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ víṣvak ǀ patantu ǀ didyávaḥ ǀdū́rvāyāḥ-iva ǀ tántavaḥ ǀ ví ǀ asmát ǀ etu ǀ duḥ-matíḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall. Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Let your radiant (weapons) fall down everywhere round about like drops of person iration; let the enemydepart from us like the stems of thedūrvagrass; the divine progenitress has given you birth, the auspiciousprogrenitress has given you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Around, on every side like drops of sweat let lightning-flashes fall. Let all malevolence pass away from us like threads of Darva grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घं ह्यंकुशं यथा शक्तिं बिभर्षि मंतुमः ।पूर्वेण मघवन्पदाजो वयां यथा यमो देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र्यजीजनत् ॥
verses.transliteration: dīrghám ǀ hí ǀ aṅkuśám ǀ yathā ǀ śáktim ǀ bíbharṣi ǀ mantu-maḥ ǀpū́rveṇa ǀ magha-van ǀ padā́ ǀ ajáḥ ǀ vayā́m ǀ yáthā ǀ yamaḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ jánitrī ǀ ajījanat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor! As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan.
verses.wilson_translation: For you, sapient (Indra), wield your might like a long hook; you drag (your foes),Maghavan, as a goatwith its fore-foot (drags) a branch; the divine progenitress has given you birth, the auspicious progrenitress hasgiven you birth.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great Counsellor! As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch, O Maghavan.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नकिर्देवा मिनीमसि नकिरा योपयामसि मंत्रश्रुत्यं चरामसि ।पक्षेभिरपिकक्षेभिरत्राभि सं रभामहे ॥
verses.transliteration: nákiḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ minīmasi ǀ nákiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ yopayāmasi ǀ mantra-śrútyam ǀ carāmasi ǀpakṣébhiḥ ǀ api-kakṣébhiḥ ǀ átra ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ rabhāmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command. Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.
verses.wilson_translation: O gods, we never injure (you), we never inflict annoyance (on you), we follow the teaching of themantra; we take hold of you at this (sacrifice) with wings and arms.
verses.griffith_verse: Never, O Gods, do we offend, nor are we ever obstinate: we walk as holy texts command. Closely we clasp and cling to you, cling to your sides, beneath your arms.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXV. Yama.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods,The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires. I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old,On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again. Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less carWhich thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way. The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child!This hath the Sāman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship. Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away?Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made? When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared.A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind. Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods:Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्वृक्षे सुपलाशे देवैः संपिबते यमः ।अत्रा नो विश्पतिः पिता पुराणाँ अनु वेनति ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmin ǀ vṛkṣé ǀ su-palāśé ǀ deváiḥ ǀ sam-píbate ǀ yamáḥ ǀátra ǀ naḥ ǀ viśpátiḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ purāṇā́n ǀ ánu ǀ venati ǁ
verses.english_translation: IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.
verses.wilson_translation: In that leafy tree where Yamadrinks with the gods, there the progenitor, the lord of the house, invitesus to join themen of old.
verses.griffith_verse: IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पुराणाँ अनुवेनंतं चरंतं पापयामुया ।असूयन्नभ्यचाकशं तस्मा अस्पृहयं पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: purāṇā́n ǀ anu-vénantam ǀ cárantam ǀ pāpáyā ǀ amuyā́ ǀasūyán ǀ abhí ǀ acākaśam ǀ tásmai ǀ aspṛhayam ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old, On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.
verses.wilson_translation: (At first) I beheld him with anguish inviting me to join the men of olden times, and walking with that felldesign; but afterwards I longed for him.
verses.griffith_verse: I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old, On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं कुमार नवं रथमचक्रं मनसाकृणोः ।एकेषं विश्वतः प्रांचमपश्यन्नधि तिष्ठसि ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ kumāra ǀ návam ǀ rátham ǀ acakrám ǀ mánasā ǀ ákṛṇoḥ ǀéka-īṣam ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ prā́ñcam ǀ ápaśyan ǀ ádhi ǀ tiṣṭhasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car Which thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way.
verses.wilson_translation: The new chariot, wheelless, single-poled, but turning everywhere, which you, my child, mentallyformed-- you stand thereon though you see it not.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car Which thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं कुमार प्रावर्तयो रथं विप्रेभ्यस्परि ।तं सामानु प्रावर्तत समितो नाव्याहितं ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ kumāra ǀ prá ǀ ávartayaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ víprebhyaḥ ǀ pári ǀtám ǀ sā́ma ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ avartata ǀ sám ǀ itáḥ ǀ nāví ǀ ā́-hitam ǁ
verses.english_translation: The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child! This hath the Sāman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship.
verses.wilson_translation: The chariot which you, my child, have driven down to me from the sages above, the Sāmanhasdriven it back again from hence plural ced on a ship. made?
verses.griffith_verse: The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child! This hath the Sāman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: कः कुमारमजनयद्रथं को निरवर्तयत् ।कः स्वित्तदद्य नो ब्रूयादनुदेयी यथाभवत् ॥
