verses.transliteration: káḥ ǀ kumārám ǀ ajanayat ǀ rátham ǀ káḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ avartayat ǀkáḥ ǀ svit ǀ tát ǀ adyá ǀ naḥ ǀ brūyāt ǀ anu-déyī ǀ yáthā ǀ ábhavat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away? Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made?
verses.griffith_verse: Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away? Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यथाभवदनुदेयी ततो अग्रमजायत ।पुरस्ताद्बुध्न आततः पश्चान्निरयणं कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yáthā ǀ ábhavat ǀ anu-déyī ǀ tátaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ ajāyata ǀpurástāt ǀ budhnáḥ ǀ ā́-tataḥ ǀ paścā́t ǀ niḥ-áyanam ǀ kṛtám ǁ
verses.english_translation: When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared. A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind.
verses.griffith_verse: When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared. A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं यमस्य सादनं देवमानं यदुच्यते ।इयमस्य धम्यते नाळीरयं गीर्भिः परिष्कृतः ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ yamásya ǀ sádanam ǀ deva-mānám ǀ yát ǀ ucyáte ǀiyám ǀ asya ǀ dhamyate ǀ nāḷī́ḥ ǀ ayám ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ pári-kṛtaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods: Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.
verses.wilson_translation: This is the dwelling of Yama, which is called the fabric of the gods; this pipe is sounded for his(gratification), he is propitiated by hymns.
verses.griffith_verse: Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods: Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXVI. Kesins.
hymns.anukramani: १ जूतिः, २ वातजूतिः, ३ विप्रजूतिः, ४ वृषाणकः, ५ करिक्रतः, ६ एतशः ७ ऋष्यश्रृंगः (एते वातरशना मुनयः)। केशिनः = अग्नि-सूर्य-वायवः। अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . HE with the long loose locks supports Agni, and moisture, heaven, and earth:He is all sky to look upon: he with long hair is called this light. The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue.They, following the wind's swift course go where the Gods have gone before. Transported with our Munihood we have pressed on into the winds:You therefore, mortal men. behold our natural bodies and no more. The Muni, made associate in the holy work of every God,Looking upon all varied forms flies through the region of the air. The Steed of Vāta, Vāyu's friend, the Muni, by the Gods impelled,In both the oceans hath his home, in eastern and in western sea. Treading the path of sylvan beasts, Gandharvas, and Apsarases,He with long locks, who knows the wish, is a sweet most delightful friend Vāyu hath churned for him: for him he poundeth things most hard to bend,When he with long loose locks hath drunk, with Rudra, water from the cup.

verses.sanskrit: केश्यग्निं केशी विषं केशी बिभर्ति रोदसी ।केशी विश्वं स्वर्दृशे केशीदं ज्योतिरुच्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: keśī́ ǀ agním ǀ keśī́ ǀ viṣám ǀ keśī́ ǀ bibharti ǀ ródasī íti ǀkeśī́ ǀ víśvam ǀ sváḥ ǀ dṛśé ǀ keśī́ ǀ idám ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ucyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: HE with the long loose locks supports Agni, and moisture, heaven, and earth: He is all sky to look upon: he with long hair is called this light.
verses.wilson_translation: The radiant (Sun supports)Agni, the radiant one (supports) water, the radiant one supports theheaven and earth, the radiant one is for the visibility of the whole diffused (universe)-- this light is called theradiant one.
verses.griffith_verse: HE with the long loose locks supports Agni, and moisture, heaven, and earth: He is all sky to look upon: he with long hair is called this light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मुनयो वातरशनाः पिशंगा वसते मला ।वातस्यानु ध्राजिं यंति यद्देवासो अविक्षत ॥
verses.transliteration: múnayaḥ ǀ vā́ta-raśanāḥ ǀ piśáṅgā ǀ vasate ǀ málā ǀvā́tasya ǀ ánu ǀ dhrā́jim ǀ yanti ǀ yát ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ávikṣata ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue. They, following the wind's swift course go where the Gods have gone before.
verses.wilson_translation: The Munis, the sons of Vātaraśana, wear the yellow dirty (vestments of bark), they follow the courseof the wind, when they have assumed the (power of) gods.
verses.griffith_verse: The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue. They, following the wind's swift course go where the Gods have gone before.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उन्मदिता मौनेयेन वाताँ आ तस्थिमा वयं ।शरीरेदस्माकं यूयं मर्तासो अभि पश्यथ ॥
verses.transliteration: út-maditāḥ ǀ máuneyena ǀ vā́tān ǀ ā́ ǀ tasthima ǀ vayám ǀśárīrā ǀ ít ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yūyám ǀ mártāsaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ paśyatha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Transported with our Munihood we have pressed on into the winds: You therefore, mortal men. behold our natural bodies and no more.
verses.wilson_translation: Exhilarated by the sanctity of the Muniwe have mounted upon the winds; behold, mortals, (in them)our forms!
verses.griffith_verse: Transported with our Munihood we have pressed on into the winds: You therefore, mortal men. behold our natural bodies and no more.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंतरिक्षेण पतति विश्वा रूपावचाकशत् ।मुनिर्देवस्यदेवस्य सौकृत्याय सखा हितः ॥
verses.transliteration: antárikṣeṇa ǀ patati ǀ víśvā ǀ rūpā́ ǀ ava-cā́kaśat ǀmúniḥ ǀ devásya-devasya ǀ sáukṛtyāya ǀ sákhā ǀ hitáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Muni, made associate in the holy work of every God, Looking upon all varied forms flies through the region of the air.
verses.wilson_translation: The Muniflies through the firmament, illumining all objects, the friend of each deity, appointed forpious works.
verses.griffith_verse: The Muni, made associate in the holy work of every God, Looking upon all varied forms flies through the region of the air.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वातस्याश्वो वायोः सखाथो देवेषितो मुनिः ।उभौ समुद्रावा क्षेति यश्च पूर्व उतापरः ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́tasya ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ vāyóḥ ǀ sákhā ǀ átho íti ǀ devá-iṣitaḥ ǀ múniḥ ǀubháu ǀ samudráu ǀ ā́ ǀ kṣeti ǀ yáḥ ǀ ca ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ utá ǀ áparaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Steed of Vāta, Vāyu's friend, the Muni, by the Gods impelled, In both the oceans hath his home, in eastern and in western sea.
verses.wilson_translation: The steed of the wind, the friend of Vāyu, the Muni, who is instrumental gated by the deity, repairs to bothoceans, the eastern and the western.
verses.griffith_verse: The Steed of Vāta, Vāyu's friend, the Muni, by the Gods impelled, In both the oceans hath his home, in eastern and in western sea.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अप्सरसां गंधर्वाणां मृगाणां चरणे चरन् ।केशी केतस्य विद्वान्त्सखा स्वादुर्मदिंतमः ॥
verses.transliteration: apsarásām ǀ gandharvā́ṇām ǀ mṛgā́ṇām ǀ cáraṇe ǀ cáran ǀkeśī́ ǀ kétasya ǀ vidvā́n ǀ sákhā ǀ svādúḥ ǀ madín-tamaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Treading the path of sylvan beasts, Gandharvas, and Apsarases, He with long locks, who knows the wish, is a sweet most delightful friend
verses.wilson_translation: Wandering in the track of the Apsarasasand the Gandharvas, and the wild beasts, the radiant (Sun),cognizant of all that is knowable, (is my) sweet and most delightful friend.
verses.griffith_verse: Treading the path of sylvan beasts, Gandharvas, and Apsarases, He with long locks, who knows the wish, is a sweet most delightful friend
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वायुरस्मा उपामंथत्पिनष्टि स्मा कुनन्नमा ।केशी विषस्य पात्रेण यद्रुद्रेणापिबत्सह ॥
verses.transliteration: vāyúḥ ǀ asmai ǀ úpa ǀ amanthat ǀ pináṣṭi ǀ sma ǀ kunannamā́ ǀkeśī́ ǀ viṣásya ǀ pā́treṇa ǀ yát ǀ rudréṇa ǀ ápibat ǀ sahá ǁ
verses.english_translation: Vāyu hath churned for him: for him he poundeth things most hard to bend, When he with long loose locks hath drunk, with Rudra, water from the cup.
verses.wilson_translation: Vāyuchurned for him, the inflexible (thunder) ground it when the radiant (Sun), along with Rudra,drank the water with his cup.
verses.griffith_verse: Vāyu hath churned for him: for him he poundeth things most hard to bend, When he with long loose locks hath drunk, with Rudra, water from the cup.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXVII Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: ७,१ भरद्वाज:, २ कश्यपः, ३ गौतमः, ४ अत्रिः, ५ विश्वामित्रः, ६ जमदग्निः, ७ वसिष्ठः। विश्वेदेवाः। अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low.O Gods, restore to life again the man who hatb committed sin. Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land.May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away. Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind;For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods. I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe.I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away. Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts’ band deliver him:All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease. The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away.The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee. The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands,With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.

verses.sanskrit: उत देवा अवहितं देवा उन्नयथा पुनः ।उतागश्चक्रुषं देवा देवा जीवयथा पुनः ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ devāḥ ǀ áva-hitam ǀ dévāḥ ǀ út ǀ nayatha ǀ púnaríti ǀutá ǀ ā́gaḥ ǀ cakrúṣam ǀ devāḥ ǀ dévāḥ ǀ jīváyatha ǀ púnaríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low. O Gods, restore to life again the man who hatb committed sin.
verses.wilson_translation: O gods, raise again the man, O gods, who has sunk; O gods, give life again to the man, O gods, who
verses.griffith_verse: YE Gods, raise up once more the man whom ye have humbled and brought low. O Gods, restore to life again the man who hatb committed sin.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: द्वाविमौ वातौ वात आ सिंधोरा परावतः ।दक्षं ते अन्य आ वातु परान्यो वातु यद्रपः ॥
verses.transliteration: dváu ǀ imáu ǀ vā́tau ǀ vātaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ síndhoḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀdákṣam ǀ te ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vātu ǀ párā ǀ anyáḥ ǀ vātu ǀ yát ǀ rápaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land. May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.
verses.wilson_translation: These two winds blow to the regions which are far beyond the ocean; may the one bring you vigour,may the other blow away all evil.
verses.griffith_verse: Two several winds are blowing here, from Sindhu, from a distant land. May one breathe energy to thee, the other blow disease away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वात वाहि भेषजं वि वात वाहि यद्रपः ।त्वं हि विश्वभेषजो देवानां दूत ईयसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vāta ǀ vāhi ǀ bheṣajám ǀ ví ǀ vāta ǀ vāhi ǀ yát ǀ rápaḥ ǀtvám ǀ hí ǀ viśvá-bheṣajaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ī́yase ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind; For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Breathe, wind, medicinal balm; blow away, wind, all evil; for you are the universalmedicine, you moveas the messenger of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither, O Wind, blow healing balm, blow all disease away, thou Wind; For thou who hast all medicine comest as envoy of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वागमं शंतातिभिरथो अरिष्टतातिभिः ।दक्षं ते भद्रमाभार्षं परा यक्ष्मं सुवामि ते ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ agamam ǀ śántāti-bhiḥ ǀ átho íti ǀ ariṣṭátāti-bhiḥ ǀdákṣam ǀ te ǀ bhadrám ǀ ā́ ǀ abhārṣam ǀ párā ǀ yákṣmam ǀ suvāmi ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe. I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away.
verses.wilson_translation: (The wind speaks). I have come to you with plural asures and with protections; I have brought youfortunate vigour, I drive away your disease.
verses.griffith_verse: I am come nigh to thee with balms to give thee rest and keep thee safe. I bring thee blessed strength, I drive thy weakening malady away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रायंतामिह देवास्त्रायतां मरुतां गणः ।त्रायंतां विश्वा भूतानि यथायमरपा असत् ॥
verses.transliteration: trā́yantām ǀ ihá ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ trā́yatām ǀ marútām ǀ gaṇáḥ ǀtrā́yantām ǀ víśvā ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ yáthā ǀ ayám ǀ arapā́ḥ ǀ ásat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts’ band deliver him: All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease.
verses.wilson_translation: May the gods give (us) protection in this world, may the company of the Marutsprotect us, may allbeings grant protection so that this (person n) may be free from sin.
verses.griffith_verse: Here let the Gods deliver him, the Maruts’ band deliver him: All things that be deliver him that he be freed from his disease.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आप इद्वा उ भेषजीरापो अमीवचातनीः ।आपः सर्वस्य भेषजीस्तास्ते कृण्वंतु भेषजं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́paḥ ǀ ít ǀ vā ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bheṣajī́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ amīva-cā́tanīḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ sárvasya ǀ bheṣajī́ḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ te ǀ kṛṇvantu ǀ bheṣajám ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away. The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee.
verses.wilson_translation: Waters verily are medicinal; waters are the dissipators of disease; waters are themedicinesforeverything; may they act asmedicineto you.
verses.griffith_verse: The Waters have their healing power, the Waters drive disease away. The Waters have a balm for all: let them make medicine for thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हस्ताभ्यां दशशाखाभ्यां जिह्वा वाचः पुरोगवी ।अनामयित्नुभ्यां त्वा ताभ्यां त्वोप स्पृशामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: hástābhyām ǀ dáśa-śākhābhyām ǀ jihvā́ ǀ vācáḥ ǀ puraḥ-gavī́ ǀanāmayitnú-bhyām ǀ tvā ǀ tā́bhyām ǀ tvā ǀ úpa ǀ spṛśāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands, With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.
verses.wilson_translation: The tongue (being cleansed) by the ten-branchedhands(of Prajāpatiis) the forerunner of speech;with those (hands) the removers of disease we touch you.
verses.griffith_verse: The tongue that leads the voice precedes. Then with our ten-fold branching hands, With these two chasers of disease we stroke thee with a gentle touch.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXVIII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vṛtra limb from limb,When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call. Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath.Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law. In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ārya found a match to meet his Dam foe.Associate with Ṛjiśvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura. He boldly cast down forts which none had e’er assailed: unwearied he destroycd the godless treasure-stores.Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart. Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vṛtra-slayer whets his darts and deals fordi wounds.Bright Uṣas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there. These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other reft of sacrifice.Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.

verses.sanskrit: तव त्य इंद्र सख्येषु वह्नय ऋतं मन्वाना व्यदर्दिरुर्वलं ।यत्रा दशस्यन्नुषसो रिणन्नपः कुत्साय मन्मन्नह्यश्च दंसयः ॥
verses.transliteration: táva ǀ tyé ǀ indra ǀ sakhyéṣu ǀ váhnayaḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ manvānā́ḥ ǀ ví ǀ adardiruḥ ǀ valám ǀyátra ǀ daśasyán ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ riṇán ǀ āpáḥ ǀ kútsāya ǀ mánman ǀ ahyáḥ ǀ ca ǀ daṃsáyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vṛtra limb from limb, When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.
verses.wilson_translation: The bearers of oblations (the Aṅgirasas),Indrahonouring the sacrifice, have through your friendshiptorn Valato pieces, when praise (being offered) desiring to give the dawns to Kutsa(you were engaged in)freeing the waters, and Ahi's exploits (were foiled).
verses.griffith_verse: ALLIED with thee in friendship, Indra, these, thy priests, remembering Holy Law, rent Vṛtra limb from limb, When they bestowed the Dawns and let the waters flow, and when thou didst chastise dragons at Kutsa's call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अवासृजः प्रस्वः श्वंचयो गिरीनुदाज उस्रा अपिबो मधु प्रियं ।अवर्धयो वनिनो अस्य दंससा शुशोच सूर्य ऋतजातया गिरा ॥
verses.transliteration: áva ǀ asṛjaḥ ǀ pra-sváḥ ǀ śvañcáyaḥ ǀ girī́n ǀ út ǀ ājaḥ ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ ápibaḥ ǀ mádhu ǀ priyám ǀávardhayaḥ ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ asya ǀ dáṃsasā ǀ śuśóca ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ṛtá-jātayā ǀ girā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath. Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.
verses.wilson_translation: You have sent forth the genitive rative (waters), you have cleft the mountains, you have fetched forth thecows, you have quaffed the delicious Soma, you have caused the trees of the forest to grow; through his exploitsby means of the voice produced for the sacrifice the sun has shone bright.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou sentest forth productive powers, clavest the hills, thou dravest forth the kine, thou drankest pleasant meath. Thou gavest increase through this Tree's surpassing might. The Sun shone by the hymn that sprang from Holy Law.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वि सूर्यो मध्ये अमुचद्रथं दिवो विदद्दासाय प्रतिमानमार्यः ।दृळ्हानि पिप्रोरसुरस्य मायिन इंद्रो व्यास्यच्चकृवाँ ऋजिश्वना ॥
verses.transliteration: ví ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ amucat ǀ rátham ǀ diváḥ ǀ vidát ǀ dāsā́ya ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ ā́ryaḥ ǀdṛḷhā́ni ǀ píproḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ māyínaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ví ǀ āsyat ǀ cakṛ-vā́n ǀ ṛjíśvanā ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ārya found a match to meet his Dam foe. Associate with Ṛjiśvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.
verses.wilson_translation: The sun unyoked his chariot in the midst of the sky, (when) theĀrya(Indra) encountered the Dāsaassociated with Ṛjiśvan, Indra destroyed the stronghold of the guilefulasura, Pipru.
verses.griffith_verse: In the mid-way of heaven the Sun unyoked his car: the Ārya found a match to meet his Dam foe. Associate with Ṛjiśvan Indra overthrew the solid forts of Pipru, conjuring Asura.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अनाधृष्टानि धृषितो व्यास्यन्निधीँरदेवाँ अमृणदयास्यः ।मासेव सूर्यो वसु पुर्यमा ददे गृणानः शत्रूँरशृणाद्विरुक्मता ॥
verses.transliteration: ánādhṛṣṭāni ǀ dhṛṣitáḥ ǀ ví ǀ āsyat ǀ ni-dhī́n ǀ ádevān ǀ amṛṇat ǀ ayā́syaḥ ǀmāsā́-iva ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ vásu ǀ púryam ǀ ā́ ǀ dade ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀ śátrūn ǀ aśṛṇāt ǀ virúkmatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He boldly cast down forts which none had e’er assailed: unwearied he destroycd the godless treasure-stores. Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart.
verses.wilson_translation: Bold (Indra) has annihilated the (hitherto) unbaffled (hosts of theasura), the objects of Ayasya'sadoration has despoiled the impious of their treasures; the sun as if with the (aid of the) moon has seized uponthe wealth of the cities (of theasuras), glorified (by his worshippers), he has demolished the foe with his blazing(thunderbolt).
verses.griffith_verse: He boldly cast down forts which none had e’er assailed: unwearied he destroycd the godless treasure-stores. Like Sun and Moon he took the stronghold's wealth away, and, praised in song, demolished foes with flashing dart.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयुद्धसेनो विभ्वा विभिंदता दाशद्वृत्रहा तुज्यानि तेजते ।इंद्रस्य वज्रादबिभेदभिश्नथः प्राक्रामच्छुंध्यूरजहादुषा अनः ॥
verses.transliteration: áyuddha-senaḥ ǀ vi-bhvā́ ǀ vi-bhindatā́ ǀ dā́śat ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ tújyāni ǀ tejate ǀíndrasya ǀ vájrāt ǀ abibhet ǀ abhi-śnáthaḥ ǀ prá ǀ akrāmat ǀ śundhyū́ḥ ǀ ájahāt ǀ uṣā́ḥ ǀ ánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vṛtra-slayer whets his darts and deals fordi wounds. Bright Uṣas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra), leading an irresistible army, slaying Vṛtrawith the pervading piercing (bolt), gives (wealth tohis worshippers), thins the (hosts of theasuras) which have to be attacked; (the whole host of the enemy) wasafraid of Indra's wide-destroying thunderbolt, the purifying (sun) came forth, Uṣas left her cart.
verses.griffith_verse: Armed with resistless weapons, with vast power to cleave, the Vṛtra-slayer whets his darts and deals fordi wounds. Bright Uṣas was afraid of Indra's slaughtering bolt: she went upon her way and left her chariot there.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एता त्या ते श्रुत्यानि केवला यदेक एकमकृणोरयज्ञं ।मासां विधानमदधा अधि द्यवि त्वया विभिन्नं भरति प्रधिं पिता ॥
verses.transliteration: etā́ ǀ tyā́ ǀ te ǀ śrútyāni ǀ kévalā ǀ yát ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ékam ǀ ákṛṇoḥ ǀ ayajñám ǀmāsā́m ǀ vi-dhā́nam ǀ adadhāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dyávi ǀ tváyā ǀ ví-bhinnam ǀ bharati ǀ pra-dhím ǀ pitā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other reft of sacrifice. Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.
verses.wilson_translation: These wondrous exploits are yours alone, in that you unaided have injured the chief neglector ofsacrifice; you have plural ced in the sky the regulator of the months through your aid the paternal (heaven) upholdsthe circumference of the wheel (of the Sun's car) which has been shattered (by Vṛtra).
verses.griffith_verse: These are thy famous exploits, only thine, when thou alone hast left the other reft of sacrifice. Thou in the heavens hast set the ordering of the Moons: the Father bears the felly portioned out by thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXXXIX. Savitar.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre;He in whose energy wise Pūṣan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman. Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region.He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit. He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure.Savitar, like a Godẉhose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra. Waters from sacrifice came to the Gandharva Visvavasu, O Soma, when they saw him.Indra, approaching quickly, marked their going, and looked around upon the Sun's enclosures. This song Visvavasu shall sing us, meter of air's mid-realm celestial Gandharva,That we may know aright both truth and falsehood: may he inspire our thoughts and help our praises. In the floods' track he found the bootyseeker: the rocky cow-pen's doors he threw wide open.These, the Gandharva told him, Rowed with Amṛta. Indra knew well the puissancc of the dragons.

verses.sanskrit: सूर्यरश्मिर्हरिकेशः पुरस्तात्सविता ज्योतिरुदयाँ अजस्रं ।तस्य पूषा प्रसवे याति विद्वान्त्संपश्यन्विश्वा भुवनानि गोपाः ॥
verses.transliteration: sūryá-raśmiḥ ǀ hári-keśaḥ ǀ purástāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ út ǀ ayān ǀ ájasram ǀtásya ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ pra-savé ǀ yāti ǀ vidvā́n ǀ sam-páśyan ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ gopā́ḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre; He in whose energy wise Pūṣan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman.
verses.wilson_translation: Savitā, the solar-rayed, the yellow-haired, sent up the undying light from the east; at his commandthe wise Pūṣan, the preserver, follows, looking upon all creatures.
verses.griffith_verse: SAVITAR, golden-haired, hath lifted eastward, bright With the sunbeams, his eternal lustre; He in whose energy wise Pūṣan marches, surveying all existence like a herdsman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नृचक्षा एष दिवो मध्य आस्त आपप्रिवान्रोदसी अंतरिक्षं ।स विश्वाचीरभि चष्टे घृताचीरंतरा पूर्वमपरं च केतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: nṛ-cákṣāḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ āste ǀ āpapri-vā́n ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antárikṣam ǀsáḥ ǀ viśvā́cīḥ ǀ abhí ǀ caṣṭe ǀ ghṛtā́cīḥ ǀ antarā́ ǀ pū́rvam ǀ áparam ǀ ca ǀ ketúm ǁ
verses.english_translation: Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region. He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit.
verses.wilson_translation: Beholding mankind he sits in the midst of the sky, filling (with light) the heaven and earth and thefirmament; he illumines the all-pervading (quarters of space), the bright-pervading (intermediate points), and thehindmost, the foremost, and the hindmost mark.
verses.griffith_verse: Beholding men he sits amid the heaven filling the two world-halves and air's wide region. He looks upon the rich far-spreading pastures between the eastern and the western limit.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: रायो बुध्नः संगमनो वसूनां विश्वा रूपाभि चष्टे शचीभिः ।देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मेंद्रो न तस्थौ समरे धनानां ॥
verses.transliteration: rāyáḥ ǀ budhnáḥ ǀ sam-gámanaḥ ǀ vásūnām ǀ víśvā ǀ rūpā́ ǀ abhí ǀ caṣṭe ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀdeváḥ-iva ǀ savitā́ ǀ satyá-dharmā ǀ índraḥ ǀ ná ǀ tasthau ǀ sam-aré ǀ dhánānām ǁ
verses.english_translation: He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure. Savitar, like a Godẉhose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra.
verses.wilson_translation: The root of riches, the acquirer of treasure illumines by his functions all (visible) forms;Savitā, like agod, whose attribute is truth, stands like Indrain the battle for riches.
verses.griffith_verse: He, root of wealth, the gatherer-up of treasures, looks with his might on every form and figure. Savitar, like a Godẉhose Law is constant, stands in the battle for the spoil like Indra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वावसुं सोम गंधर्वमापो ददृशुषीस्तदृतेना व्यायन् ।तदन्ववैदिंद्रो रारहाण आसां परि सूर्यस्य परिधीँरपश्यत् ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvá-vasum ǀ soma ǀ gandharvám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ dadṛśúṣīḥ ǀ tát ǀ ṛténa ǀ ví ǀ āyan ǀtát ǀ anu-ávait ǀ índraḥ ǀ rarahāṇáḥ ǀ āsām ǀ pári ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ pari-dhī́n ǀ apaśyat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Waters from sacrifice came to the Gandharva Visvavasu, O Soma, when they saw him. Indra, approaching quickly, marked their going, and looked around upon the Sun's enclosures.
verses.wilson_translation: Beholding Soma, the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, the waters have come forth by means of the sacrifice;Indraimpelling them knew of this (their approach), and looked round the rims of the sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Waters from sacrifice came to the Gandharva Visvavasu, O Soma, when they saw him. Indra, approaching quickly, marked their going, and looked around upon the Sun's enclosures.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विश्वावसुरभि तन्नो गृणातु दिव्यो गंधर्वो रजसो विमानः ।यद्वा घा सत्यमुत यन्न विद्म धियो हिन्वानो धिय इन्नो अव्याः ॥
verses.transliteration: viśvá-vasuḥ ǀ abhí ǀ tát ǀ naḥ ǀ gṛṇātu ǀ divyáḥ ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́naḥ ǀyát ǀ vā ǀ gha ǀ satyám ǀ utá ǀ yát ǀ ná ǀ vidmá ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ hinvānáḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ naḥ ǀ avyāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This song Visvavasu shall sing us, meter of air's mid-realm celestial Gandharva, That we may know aright both truth and falsehood: may he inspire our thoughts and help our praises.
verses.wilson_translation: May the celestial Gandharva Viśvāvasu, the measurer of the water, declare to us that which is thetruth, and that which we do not know; accepting our praises. (Viśvāvasu), protect our sacrifices.
verses.griffith_verse: This song Visvavasu shall sing us, meter of air's mid-realm celestial Gandharva, That we may know aright both truth and falsehood: may he inspire our thoughts and help our praises.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सस्निमविंदच्चरणे नदीनामपावृणोद्दुरो अश्मव्रजानां ।प्रासां गंधर्वो अमृतानि वोचदिंद्रो दक्षं परि जानादहीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: sásnim ǀ avindat ǀ cáraṇe ǀ nadī́nām ǀ ápa ǀ avṛṇot ǀ dúraḥ ǀ áśma-vrajānām ǀprá ǀ āsām ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ amṛ́tāni ǀ vocat ǀ índraḥ ǀ dákṣam ǀ pári ǀ jānāt ǀ ahī́nām ǁ
verses.english_translation: In the floods' track he found the bootyseeker: the rocky cow-pen's doors he threw wide open. These, the Gandharva told him, Rowed with Amṛta. Indra knew well the puissancc of the dragons.
verses.wilson_translation: (Indra) discovered the cloud in the region of the rivers, he set open the portals of (the waters) whosedwelling is in the clouds; Indra, (in the form of) the Gandharva(viśvāvasu), proclaimed the ambrosial (waters),he knew the strength of the dragons.
verses.griffith_verse: In the floods' track he found the bootyseeker: the rocky cow-pen's doors he threw wide open. These, the Gandharva told him, Rowed with Amṛta. Indra knew well the puissancc of the dragons.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXL. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ६ अग्निः पावकः। अग्निः। सतोबृहती, १-२ विष्टारपंक्तिः, ६ उपरिष्टाज्ज्योतिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AGNI, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams!Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper, with strength, the food that merits laud. With brilliant, purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light.Thou, visiting both thy Mothers, aidest them as Son: thou joinest close the earth and heaven. O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice ihyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs.In thee are treasured various forms of strengthening food, born nobly and of wondrous help. Agni, spread forth, as Ruler, over living things: give wealth to us, Immortal God.Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to conquering power. To him, the wise, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches un der his control,Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, givest him wealth that conquers all. The men have set before them them for their welfare Agni, strong, visible to all, the Holy.Thee, Godlike One, with ears to hear, most famous, men's generations magnify with praise-songs.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने तव श्रवो वयो महि भ्राजंते अर्चयो विभावसो ।बृहद्भानो शवसा वाजमुक्थ्यं दधासि दाशुषे कवे ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ táva ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ máhi ǀ bhrājante ǀ arcáyaḥ ǀ vibhāvaso íti vibhā-vaso ǀbṛ́hadbhāno íti bṛ́hat-bhāno ǀ śávasā ǀ vā́jam ǀ ukthyám ǀ dádhāsi ǀ dāśúṣe ǀ kave ǁ
verses.english_translation: AGNI, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper, with strength, the food that merits laud.
verses.wilson_translation: Your,Agni, is the most excellent sacrificial food; your flames, O opulent in radiance, blaze fiercely;wise and widely luminous (Agni), you bestow upon the donor (of the oblation) the choicest food with strength.
verses.griffith_verse: AGNI, life-power and fame are thine: thy fires blaze mightily, thou rich in wealth of beams! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper, with strength, the food that merits laud.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पावकवर्चाः शुक्रवर्चा अनूनवर्चा उदियर्षि भानुना ।पुत्रो मातरा विचरन्नुपावसि पृणक्षि रोदसी उभे ॥
verses.transliteration: pāvaká-varcāḥ ǀ śukrá-varcāḥ ǀ ánūna-varcāḥ ǀ út ǀ iyarṣi ǀ bhānúnā ǀputráḥ ǀ mātárā ǀ vi-cáran ǀ úpa ǀ avasi ǀ pṛṇákṣi ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ubhé íti ǁ
verses.english_translation: With brilliant, purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy Mothers, aidest them as Son: thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, who are of purifying radiance, of unsullied lustre, of full brightness, you issue forth withsplendour; visiting your parents (like) a son, you protect (the worshippers), you unite both heaven and earth.
verses.griffith_verse: With brilliant, purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy Mothers, aidest them as Son: thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्जो नपाज्जातवेदः सुशस्तिभिर्मंदस्व धीतिभिर्हितः ।त्वे इषः सं दधुर्भूरिवर्पसश्चित्रोतयो वामजाताः ॥
verses.transliteration: ū́rjaḥ ǀ napāt ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ suśastí-bhiḥ ǀ mándasva ǀ dhītí-bhiḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǀtvé íti ǀ íṣaḥ ǀ sám ǀ dadhuḥ ǀ bhū́ri-varpasaḥ ǀ citrá-ūtayaḥ ǀ vāmá-jātāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice ihyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs. In thee are treasured various forms of strengthening food, born nobly and of wondrous help.
verses.wilson_translation: Son of strength,Jātavedas, rejoice in our adorations, (be) satisfied by our offerings, (theworshippers) have plural ced before you viands of many sorts of wonderful efficacy, of excellent origin. {Son ofstrength: ūrjonapāt= grandson of waters; or, non-injurer; or, food].
verses.griffith_verse: O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice ihyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs. In thee are treasured various forms of strengthening food, born nobly and of wondrous help.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इरज्यन्नग्ने प्रथयस्व जंतुभिरस्मे रायो अमर्त्य ।स दर्शतस्य वपुषो वि राजसि पृणक्षि सानसिं क्रतुं ॥
verses.transliteration: irajyán ǀ agne ǀ prathayasva ǀ jantú-bhiḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ rā́yaḥ ǀ amartya ǀsáḥ ǀ darśatásya ǀ vápuṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ rājasi ǀ pṛṇákṣi ǀ sānasím ǀ krátum ǁ
verses.english_translation: Agni, spread forth, as Ruler, over living things: give wealth to us, Immortal God. Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to conquering power.
verses.wilson_translation: Contending with enemies, bestow upon us, immortal Agni, riches; you shine with a graceful person n,you fulfil (the purpose of) the enjoyable rite.
verses.griffith_verse: Agni, spread forth, as Ruler, over living things: give wealth to us, Immortal God. Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to conquering power.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इष्कर्तारमध्वरस्य प्रचेतसं क्षयंतं राधसो महः ।रातिं वामस्य सुभगां महीमिषं दधासि सानसिं रयिं ॥
verses.transliteration: iṣkartā́ram ǀ adhvarásya ǀ prá-cetasam ǀ kṣáyantam ǀ rā́dhasaḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀrātím ǀ vāmásya ǀ su-bhágām ǀ mahī́m ǀ íṣam ǀ dádhāsi ǀ sānasím ǀ rayím ǁ
verses.english_translation: To him, the wise, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches un der his control, Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, givest him wealth that conquers all.
verses.wilson_translation: (We praise you), the perfecter of the sacrifice, the sage, the lord of great wealth, the giver of what isdesirable; you bestow auspicious and abundant food, and enjoyable riches.
verses.griffith_verse: To him, the wise, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches un der his control, Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, givest him wealth that conquers all.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋतावानं महिषं विश्वदर्शतमग्निं सुम्नाय दधिरे पुरो जनाः ।श्रुत्कर्णं सप्रथस्तमं त्वा गिरा दैव्यं मानुषा युगा ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtá-vānam ǀ mahiṣám ǀ viśvá-darśatam ǀ agním ǀ sumnā́ya ǀ dadhire ǀ puráḥ ǀ jánāḥ ǀśrút-karṇam ǀ sapráthaḥ-tamam ǀ tvā ǀ girā́ ǀ dáivyam ǀ mā́nuṣā ǀ yugā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The men have set before them them for their welfare Agni, strong, visible to all, the Holy. Thee, Godlike One, with ears to hear, most famous, men's generations magnify with praise-songs.
verses.wilson_translation: Men for the sake of happiness plural ce before them Agni, the speaker of truth, the mighty, thecontemplator of all; the posterity of Manuin pairs (propitiate) with praises you, whose ears are open (to praises)who are most renowned, and the (minister) of the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: The men have set before them them for their welfare Agni, strong, visible to all, the Holy. Thee, Godlike One, with ears to hear, most famous, men's generations magnify with praise-songs.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . TURN hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind.Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth. Let Aryarnan vouchsafe us wealth, and Bhaga, and Bṛhaspati.Let the Gods give their gifts, and let Sūnṛtā, Goddess, grant us wealth. We call King Soma to our aid, and Agni with our songs and hymns,Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and the Brahman Priest Bṛhaspati. Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Gods swift to listen, we invoke,That in the synod all the folk may be benevolent to us. Urge Aryaman to send us gifts, and Indra, and Bṛhaspati,Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī and the Strong Courser Savitar. Do thou, O Agni, with thy fires strengthen our prayer and sacrifice:Urge givers to bestow their wealth to aid our service of the Gods.

verses.sanskrit: अग्ने अच्छा वदेह नः प्रत्यङ्नः सुमना भव ।प्र नो यच्छ विशस्पते धनदा असि नस्त्वं ॥
verses.transliteration: ágne ǀ áccha ǀ vada ǀ ihá ǀ naḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ naḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ bhava ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ yaccha ǀ viśaḥ ǀ pate ǀ dhana-dā́ḥ ǀ asi ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: TURN hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind. Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, speak to us here, be favourably disposed towards us; bestow upon us (riches), lord of men, foryou are the giver of wealth to us.
verses.griffith_verse: TURN hither, Agni, speak to us: come to us with a gracious mind. Enrich us, Master of the house: thou art the Giver of our wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र नो यच्छत्वर्यमा प्र भगः प्र बृहस्पतिः ।प्र देवाः प्रोत सूनृता रायो देवी ददातु नः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ naḥ ǀ yacchatu ǀ aryamā́ ǀ prá ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ prá ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀprá ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ utá ǀ sūnṛ́tā ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ devī́ ǀ dadātu ǀ naḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let Aryarnan vouchsafe us wealth, and Bhaga, and Bṛhaspati. Let the Gods give their gifts, and let Sūnṛtā, Goddess, grant us wealth.
verses.wilson_translation: May Aryaman, may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati, may the gods give liberally to us; may the truth-speakinggoddess (Sarasvatī) bestow riches upon us.
verses.griffith_verse: Let Aryarnan vouchsafe us wealth, and Bhaga, and Bṛhaspati. Let the Gods give their gifts, and let Sūnṛtā, Goddess, grant us wealth.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे ।आदित्यान्विष्णुं सूर्यं ब्रह्माणं च बृहस्पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: sómam ǀ rā́jānam ǀ ávase ǀ agním ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ havāmahe ǀādityā́n ǀ víṣṇum ǀ sū́ryam ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ ca ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: We call King Soma to our aid, and Agni with our songs and hymns, Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and the Brahman Priest Bṛhaspati.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke for our protection the royal Soma, (we invoke)Agniwith praises, (we invoke) theĀdityas,Viṣṇu,Sūrya,Brahmāand Bṛhaspati.
verses.griffith_verse: We call King Soma to our aid, and Agni with our songs and hymns, Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and the Brahman Priest Bṛhaspati.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रवायू बृहस्पतिं सुहवेह हवामहे ।यथा नः सर्व इज्जनः संगत्यां सुमना असत् ॥
verses.transliteration: indravāyū́ íti ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ su-hávā ǀ ihá ǀ havāmahe ǀyáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ sárvaḥ ǀ ít ǀ jánaḥ ǀ sám-gatyām ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ ásat ǁ
verses.english_translation: Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Gods swift to listen, we invoke, That in the synod all the folk may be benevolent to us.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke the adorable Indraand Vāyuand Bṛhaspation this occasion, that all our race may befavourably inclined to us in the acquisition (of wealth).
verses.griffith_verse: Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Gods swift to listen, we invoke, That in the synod all the folk may be benevolent to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अर्यमणं बृहस्पतिमिंद्रं दानाय चोदय ।वातं विष्णुं सरस्वतीं सवितारं च वाजिनं ॥
verses.transliteration: aryamáṇam ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ índram ǀ dā́nāya ǀ codaya ǀvā́tam ǀ víṣṇum ǀ sárasvatīm ǀ savitā́ram ǀ ca ǀ vājínam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Urge Aryaman to send us gifts, and Indra, and Bṛhaspati, Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī and the Strong Courser Savitar.
verses.wilson_translation: Stimulate to liberality Aryaman,Bṛhaspati,Indra,Vāta,Viṣṇu,Sarasvatī, and the food-bestowing Savitā.
verses.griffith_verse: Urge Aryaman to send us gifts, and Indra, and Bṛhaspati, Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī and the Strong Courser Savitar.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं नो अग्ने अग्निभिर्ब्रह्म यज्ञं च वर्धय ।त्वं नो देवतातये रायो दानाय चोदय ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ naḥ ǀ agne ǀ agní-bhiḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ yajñám ǀ ca ǀ vardhaya ǀtvám ǀ naḥ ǀ devá-tātaye ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ dā́nāya ǀ codaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Do thou, O Agni, with thy fires strengthen our prayer and sacrifice: Urge givers to bestow their wealth to aid our service of the Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Augment our prayer and sacrifice,Agni, with your fires; do you at our sacrifice stimulate (the gods) togive us wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: Do thou, O Agni, with thy fires strengthen our prayer and sacrifice: Urge givers to bestow their wealth to aid our service of the Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength.Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard. Keep the destructive lightning far away from us. Thy birth who seekest food is in the falling flood, Agni: as Comrade thou winnest all living things.Our coursers and our songs shall be victorious: they of themselves advance like one who guards the herd. And thou, O Agni, thou of Godlike nature, sparest the stones, while caring up the brushwood.Then are thy tracks like deserts in the corn-lands. Let us not stir to wrath thy mighty arrow. O'er hills through vales devouring as thou goest, thou partest like an army fain for bootyAs when a barber shaves a beard, thou shavest earth when the wind blows on thy flame and fans it. Apparent are his lines as he approaches the course is single, but the cars are many,When, Agni, thou, making thine arms resplendent, advancest o’er the land spread out beneath thee. Now let thy strength, thy burning flames fly upward, thine energies, O Agni, as thou toilest.Gape widely, bend thee, waxing in thy vigour: let all the Vasus sit this day beside thee. This is the waters' reservoir, the great abode of gathered streams.Take thou another path than this, and as thou listest walk thereon. On thy way hitherward and hence let flowery Durva grass spring upLet there be lakes with lotus blooms. These are the mansions of the flood.

verses.sanskrit: अयमग्ने जरिता त्वे अभूदपि सहसः सूनो नह्यन्यदस्त्याप्यं ।भद्रं हि शर्म त्रिवरूथमस्ति त आरे हिंसानामप दिद्युमा कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ agne ǀ jaritā́ ǀ tvé íti ǀ abhūt ǀ ápi ǀ sáhasaḥ ǀ sūno íti ǀ nahí ǀ anyát ǀ ásti ǀ ā́pyam ǀbhadrám ǀ hí ǀ śárma ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ ásti ǀ te ǀ āré ǀ híṃsānām ǀ ápa ǀ didyúm ǀ ā́ ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength. Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard. Keep the destructive lightning far away from us.
verses.wilson_translation: This person n,Agni, was your praiser, for there is nothing else attainable, O son of strength; holy is thehappiness derived from you, a triple defence; remove far from us, who are susceptible of harm, your scorchingflame.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH thee, O Agni, was this singer of the laud: he hath no other kinship, O thou Son of Strength. Thou givest blessed shelter with a triple guard. Keep the destructive lightning far away from us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रवत्ते अग्ने जनिमा पितूयतः साचीव विश्वा भुवना न्यृंजसे ।प्र सप्तयः प्र सनिषंत नो धियः पुरश्चरंति पशुपा इव त्मना ॥
verses.transliteration: pra-vát ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ jánima ǀ pitu-yatáḥ ǀ sācī́-iva ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ ní ǀ ṛñjase ǀprá ǀ sáptayaḥ ǀ prá ǀ saniṣanta ǀ naḥ ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ caranti ǀ paśupā́ḥ-iva ǀ tmánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thy birth who seekest food is in the falling flood, Agni: as Comrade thou winnest all living things. Our coursers and our songs shall be victorious: they of themselves advance like one who guards the herd.
verses.wilson_translation: Exalted is the birth of you,Agni, who are desirous of (sacrificial) food; you preside like a councillorover all created beings; our praises flowing smoothly proceed to you, as herdsmen of their own will (go slowly)before (their flocks).
verses.griffith_verse: Thy birth who seekest food is in the falling flood, Agni: as Comrade thou winnest all living things. Our coursers and our songs shall be victorious: they of themselves advance like one who guards the herd.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत वा उ परि वृणक्षि बप्सद्बहोरग्न उलपस्य स्वधावः ।उत खिल्या उर्वराणां भवंति मा ते हेतिं तविषीं चुक्रुधाम ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vā ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ pári ǀ vṛṇakṣi ǀ bápsat ǀ bahóḥ ǀ agne ǀ úlapasya ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀutá ǀ khilyā́ḥ ǀ urvárāṇām ǀ bhavanti ǀ mā́ ǀ te ǀ hetím ǀ táviṣīm ǀ cukrudhāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: And thou, O Agni, thou of Godlike nature, sparest the stones, while caring up the brushwood. Then are thy tracks like deserts in the corn-lands. Let us not stir to wrath thy mighty arrow.
verses.wilson_translation: Blazing Agni, you destroy many a shrub, as you burn; and (the sites) of the tilled fields are laid waste,may we never rouse to anger your terrible flame.
verses.griffith_verse: And thou, O Agni, thou of Godlike nature, sparest the stones, while caring up the brushwood. Then are thy tracks like deserts in the corn-lands. Let us not stir to wrath thy mighty arrow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदुद्वतो निवतो यासि बप्सत्पृथगेषि प्रगर्धिनीव सेना ।यदा ते वातो अनुवाति शोचिर्वप्तेव श्मश्रु वपसि प्र भूम ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ut-vátaḥ ǀ ni-vátaḥ ǀ yā́si ǀ bápsat ǀ pṛ́thak ǀ eṣi ǀ pragardhínī-iva ǀ sénā ǀyadā́ ǀ te ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ anu-vā́ti ǀ śocíḥ ǀ váptā-iva ǀ śmáśru ǀ vapasi ǀ prá ǀ bhū́ma ǁ
verses.english_translation: O'er hills through vales devouring as thou goest, thou partest like an army fain for booty As when a barber shaves a beard, thou shavest earth when the wind blows on thy flame and fans it.
verses.wilson_translation: When you move burning above and burning below, you scatter yourself like a devastating host; whenthe wind fans your flame, you shave the earth as a barber shaves a beard.
verses.griffith_verse: O'er hills through vales devouring as thou goest, thou partest like an army fain for booty As when a barber shaves a beard, thou shavest earth when the wind blows on thy flame and fans it.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यस्य श्रेणयो ददृश्र एकं नियानं बहवो रथासः ।बाहू यदग्ने अनुमर्मृजानो न्यङ्ङुत्तानामन्वेषि भूमिं ॥
verses.transliteration: práti ǀ asya ǀ śréṇayaḥ ǀ dadṛśre ǀ ékam ǀ ni-yā́nam ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ ráthāsaḥ ǀbāhū́ íti ǀ yát ǀ agne ǀ anu-mármṛjānaḥ ǀ nyáṅ ǀ uttānā́m ǀ anu-éṣi ǀ bhū́mim ǁ
verses.english_translation: Apparent are his lines as he approaches the course is single, but the cars are many, When, Agni, thou, making thine arms resplendent, advancest o’er the land spread out beneath thee.
verses.wilson_translation: His lines (of flame) are visible, like one array of many chariots, when clearing away (the forests) withyour arms (of flame) you march,Agni, over the prostrate earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Apparent are his lines as he approaches the course is single, but the cars are many, When, Agni, thou, making thine arms resplendent, advancest o’er the land spread out beneath thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्ते शुष्मा जिहतामुत्ते अर्चिरुत्ते अग्ने शशमानस्य वाजाः ।उच्छ्वंचस्व नि नम वर्धमान आ त्वाद्य विश्वे वसवः सदंतु ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ te ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǀ jihatām ǀ út ǀ te ǀ arcíḥ ǀ út ǀ te ǀ agne ǀ śaśamānásya ǀ vā́jāḥ ǀút ǀ śvañcasva ǀ ní ǀ nama ǀ várdhamānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ adyá ǀ víśve ǀ vásavaḥ ǀ sadantu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now let thy strength, thy burning flames fly upward, thine energies, O Agni, as thou toilest. Gape widely, bend thee, waxing in thy vigour: let all the Vasus sit this day beside thee.
verses.wilson_translation: May your withering flames,Agni, arise; may your light (arise), and the swift movements of you whenyou are praised; rise up, stoop down, increasing in might; may all the Vasusthis day attend upon you.
verses.griffith_verse: Now let thy strength, thy burning flames fly upward, thine energies, O Agni, as thou toilest. Gape widely, bend thee, waxing in thy vigour: let all the Vasus sit this day beside thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपामिदं न्ययनं समुद्रस्य निवेशनं ।अन्यं कृणुष्वेतः पंथां तेन याहि वशाँ अनु ॥
verses.transliteration: apā́m ǀ idám ǀ ni-áyanam ǀ samudrásya ǀ ni-véśanam ǀanyám ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǀ itáḥ ǀ pánthām ǀ téna ǀ yāhi ǀ váśān ǀ ánu ǁ
verses.english_translation: This is the waters' reservoir, the great abode of gathered streams. Take thou another path than this, and as thou listest walk thereon.
verses.wilson_translation: This is the abode of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean; pursue,Agni, a different path from this; goby this (path) according to your plural asure.
verses.griffith_verse: This is the waters' reservoir, the great abode of gathered streams. Take thou another path than this, and as thou listest walk thereon.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आयने ते परायणे दूर्वा रोहंतु पुष्पिणीः ।ह्रदाश्च पुंडरीकाणि समुद्रस्य गृहा इमे ॥
verses.transliteration: ā-áyane ǀ te ǀ parā-áyane ǀ dū́rvāḥ ǀ rohantu ǀ puṣpíṇīḥ ǀhradā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ puṇḍárīkāṇi ǀ samudrásya ǀ gṛhā́ḥ ǀ imé ǁ
verses.english_translation: On thy way hitherward and hence let flowery Durva grass spring up Let there be lakes with lotus blooms. These are the mansions of the flood.
verses.wilson_translation: Both at your arrival,Agni, and at your departure, may the floweringdūrvagrasses spring up; maylakes (be formed) and lotuses (therein); may these be the dwellings of the ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: On thy way hitherward and hence let flowery Durva grass spring up Let there be lakes with lotus blooms. These are the mansions of the flood.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLIII. Aśvins.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . YE made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal.When ye restored to youth and strength Kakṣīvān like a car renewed, Ye freed that Atri like a horse, and brought him newly-born to earth.Ye loosed him like a firm-tied knot which Gods unsoiled by dust had bound. Heroes who showed most wondrous power to Atri, strive to win fair songs;For then, O Heroes of the sky, your hymn of praise shall cease no more. This claims your notice, Bounteous Gods! - oblation, Aśvins! and our love,That ye, O Heroes, in the fight may bring us safe to ample room. Ye Twain to Bhujyu tossed about in ocean at the region's end,Nāsatyas, with your winged sterds came nigh, and gave him strength to win. Come with your joys, most liberal Gods, Lords of all treasures, bringing weal.Like fresh full waters to a well, so, Heroes come and be with us.

verses.sanskrit: त्यं चिदत्रिमृतजुरमर्थमश्वं न यातवे ।कक्षीवंतं यदी पुना रथं न कृणुथो नवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tyám ǀ cit ǀ átrim ǀ ṛta-júram ǀ ártham ǀ áśvam ǀ ná ǀ yā́tave ǀkakṣī́vantam ǀ yádi ǀ púnaríti ǀ rátham ǀ ná ǀ kṛṇutháḥ ǀ návam ǁ
verses.english_translation: YE made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal. When ye restored to youth and strength Kakṣīvān like a car renewed,
verses.wilson_translation: You made this Atri, ever diligent in worship, (swift) to run to the goal like a horse, and you renewed Kakṣīvat as (a wheelwright renews) a car.
verses.griffith_verse: YE made that Atri, worn with eld, free as a horse to win the goal. When ye restored to youth and strength Kakṣīvān like a car renewed,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्यं चिदश्वं न वाजिनमरेणवो यमत्नत ।दृळ्हं ग्रंथिं न वि ष्यतमत्रिं यविष्ठमा रजः ॥
verses.transliteration: tyám ǀ cit ǀ áśvam ǀ ná ǀ vājínam ǀ areṇávaḥ ǀ yám ǀ átnata ǀdṛḷhám ǀ granthím ǀ ná ǀ ví ǀ syatam ǀ átrim ǀ yáviṣṭham ǀ ā́ ǀ rájaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye freed that Atri like a horse, and brought him newly-born to earth. Ye loosed him like a firm-tied knot which Gods unsoiled by dust had bound.
verses.wilson_translation: This Atri, whom the irresistible (asuras) dragged bound like a swift horse, you unloosed like a strongknot, (setting him) the youngest born upon the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye freed that Atri like a horse, and brought him newly-born to earth. Ye loosed him like a firm-tied knot which Gods unsoiled by dust had bound.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नरा दंसिष्ठावत्रये शुभ्रा सिषासतं धियः ।अथा हि वां दिवो नरा पुनः स्तोमो न विशसे ॥
verses.transliteration: nárā ǀ dáṃsiṣṭhau ǀ átraye ǀ śúbhrā ǀ sísāsatam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀátha ǀ hí ǀ vām ǀ diváḥ ǀ narā ǀ púnaríti ǀ stómaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vi-śáse ǁ
verses.english_translation: Heroes who showed most wondrous power to Atri, strive to win fair songs; For then, O Heroes of the sky, your hymn of praise shall cease no more.
verses.wilson_translation: Leaders (of rites), of goodly aspect and radiant, design to accept Atri's praises, and so the praise ofyour worshipper (is) to be sung again to you leaders (of rites).
verses.griffith_verse: Heroes who showed most wondrous power to Atri, strive to win fair songs; For then, O Heroes of the sky, your hymn of praise shall cease no more.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: चिते तद्वां सुराधसा रातिः सुमतिरश्विना ।आ यन्नः सदने पृथौ समने पर्षथो नरा ॥
verses.transliteration: cité ǀ tát ǀ vām ǀ su-rādhasā ǀ rātíḥ ǀ su-matíḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀā́ ǀ yát ǀ naḥ ǀ sádane ǀ pṛtháu ǀ sámane ǀ párṣathaḥ ǀ narā ǁ
verses.english_translation: This claims your notice, Bounteous Gods! - oblation, Aśvins! and our love, That ye, O Heroes, in the fight may bring us safe to ample room.
verses.wilson_translation: Munificent Aśvins, my offering and praise (is) for your recognition, because, leaders (of rites), youprotect us at the sacrifice in the spacious sacrificial hall.
verses.griffith_verse: This claims your notice, Bounteous Gods! - oblation, Aśvins! and our love, That ye, O Heroes, in the fight may bring us safe to ample room.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: युवं भुज्युं समुद्र आ रजसः पार ईंखितं ।यातमच्छा पतत्रिभिर्नासत्या सातये कृतं ॥
verses.transliteration: yuvám ǀ bhujyúm ǀ samudré ǀ ā́ ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ pāré ǀ īṅkhitám ǀyātám ǀ áccha ǀ patatrí-bhiḥ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ sātáye ǀ kṛtam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Ye Twain to Bhujyu tossed about in ocean at the region's end, Nāsatyas, with your winged sterds came nigh, and gave him strength to win.
verses.wilson_translation: You came with winged (steeds) to Bhujyu(immersed) in the ocean, at the world's end, perturbed; and,leaders, of truth, you restored him to your worship.
verses.griffith_verse: Ye Twain to Bhujyu tossed about in ocean at the region's end, Nāsatyas, with your winged sterds came nigh, and gave him strength to win.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ वां सुम्नैः शंयू इव मंहिष्ठा विश्ववेदसा ।समस्मे भूषतं नरोत्सं न पिप्युषीरिषः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vām ǀ sumnáiḥ ǀ śamyū́ ivéti śamyū́-iva ǀ máṃhiṣṭhā ǀ víśva-vedasā ǀsám ǀ asmé íti ǀ bhūṣatam ǀ narā ǀ útsam ǀ ná ǀ pipyúṣīḥ ǀ íṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come with your joys, most liberal Gods, Lords of all treasures, bringing weal. Like fresh full waters to a well, so, Heroes come and be with us.
verses.wilson_translation: Prosperous,, most adorable, all-knowing, come to us and decorate us with blessings, as a (cow's)udder is adorned with abundant food.
verses.griffith_verse: Come with your joys, most liberal Gods, Lords of all treasures, bringing weal. Like fresh full waters to a well, so, Heroes come and be with us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLIV. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ६ तार्क्ष्र्यः सुपर्णः, यामायन ऊर्ध्वकृशनो वा। इन्द्रः। गायत्री, २ बृहती, ५ सतोबृहती, ६ विष्टारपंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality,Belongs to thee, the Orderer. Here, by us, for the worshipper, is the wise bolt that works with skill.It brings the bubbling beverage as a dexterous man brings the effectual strong drink. Impetuous Ahīśuva, a bull among cows of his,looked down upon the restless Hawk. That the strong-pinioned Bird hath brought, Child of the Falcon, from afar,What moves upon a hundred wheels along the female Dragon's path. Which, fair, unrobbed, the Falcon brought thee in his foot, the red-hued dwelling of the juice;Through this came vital power which lengthens out our days, and kinship through its help awoke. So Indra is by lndu's power; e’en among Gods will it repel great treachery.Wisdom, Most Sapient One, brings force that lengthens life. May wisdom bring the juice to us.

verses.sanskrit: अयं हि ते अमर्त्य इंदुरत्यो न पत्यते ।दक्षो विश्वायुर्वेधसे ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ hí ǀ te ǀ ámartyaḥ ǀ índuḥ ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pátyate ǀdákṣaḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ vedháse ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality, Belongs to thee, the Orderer.
verses.wilson_translation: This immortal Soma, the giver of strength, the giver of long life to all, hastens like a swift horse to you(Indra), the creator.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS deathless Indu, like a steed, strong and of full vitality, Belongs to thee, the Orderer.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयमस्मासु काव्य ऋभु���्वज्रो दास्वते ।अयं बिभर्त्यूर्ध्वकृशनं मदमृभुर्न कृत्व्यं मदं ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ asmā́su ǀ kā́vyaḥ ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ vájraḥ ǀ dā́svate ǀayám ǀ bibharti ǀ ūrdhvá-kṛśanam ǀ mádam ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ ná ǀ kṛ́tvyam ǀ mádam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here, by us, for the worshipper, is the wise bolt that works with skill. It brings the bubbling beverage as a dexterous man brings the effectual strong drink.
verses.wilson_translation: This (Indra), adorable among us and brilliant, is a thunderbolt for the donor (of the oblation against hisfoes); he cherishes the exhilarating (worshipper) ūrdhvakṛśana, asṚbhu(cherishes) the exhilaratingcelebrator of holy rites.
verses.griffith_verse: Here, by us, for the worshipper, is the wise bolt that works with skill. It brings the bubbling beverage as a dexterous man brings the effectual strong drink.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: घृषुः श्येनाय कृत्वन आसु स्वासु वंसगः ।अव दीधेदहीशुवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ghṛ́ṣuḥ ǀ śyenā́ya ǀ kṛ́tvane ǀ āsú ǀ svā́su ǀ váṃsagaḥ ǀáva ǀ dīdhet ǀ ahīśúvaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Impetuous Ahīśuva, a bull among cows of his, looked down upon the restless Hawk.
verses.wilson_translation: May the brilliant, (Indra), who is a benefactor among thwese his own (people), for the sake ofthe hymn;Suparṇa, the son of the Tārk.sya. ahiśuvaḥ = name of anasura; the subject of the verb may be Soma and not Indra].
verses.griffith_verse: Impetuous Ahīśuva, a bull among cows of his, looked down upon the restless Hawk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं सुपर्णः परावतः श्येनस्य पुत्र आभरत् ।शतचक्रं योऽह्यो वर्तनिः ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ su-parṇáḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ śyenásya ǀ putráḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ábharat ǀśatá-cakram ǀ yáḥ ǀ ahyáḥ ǀ vartaníḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: That the strong-pinioned Bird hath brought, Child of the Falcon, from afar, What moves upon a hundred wheels along the female Dragon's path.
verses.wilson_translation: The som whom Suparṇa, the son of the falcon, brought from afar, the bestower of many boons, whois the stimulator of Ahi.
verses.griffith_verse: That the strong-pinioned Bird hath brought, Child of the Falcon, from afar, What moves upon a hundred wheels along the female Dragon's path.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यं ते श्येनश्चारुमवृकं पदाभरदरुणं मानमंधसः ।एना वयो वि तार्यायुर्जीवस एना जागार बंधुता ॥
verses.transliteration: yám ǀ te ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ cā́rum ǀ avṛkám ǀ padā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ ábharat ǀ aruṇám ǀ mānám ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀenā́ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tāri ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ jīváse ǀ enā́ ǀ jāgāra ǀ bandhútā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Which, fair, unrobbed, the Falcon brought thee in his foot, the red-hued dwelling of the juice; Through this came vital power which lengthens out our days, and kinship through its help awoke.
verses.wilson_translation: Whom the falcon brought to you (Indra) with his claw, beautiful, unassailable, purple-tinted, themeasurer of food-- by it, food and old age was prolonged for living, by it affinity was awakened.
verses.griffith_verse: Which, fair, unrobbed, the Falcon brought thee in his foot, the red-hued dwelling of the juice; Through this came vital power which lengthens out our days, and kinship through its help awoke.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: एवा तदिंद्र इंदुना देवेषु चिद्धारयाते महि त्यजः ।क्रत्वा वयो वि तार्यायुः सुक्रतो क्रत्वायमस्मदा सुतः ॥
verses.transliteration: evá ǀ tát ǀ índraḥ ǀ índunā ǀ devéṣu ǀ cit ǀ dhārayāte ǀ máhi ǀ tyájaḥ ǀkrátvā ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ tāri ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ krátvā ǀ ayám ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ sutáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: So Indra is by lndu's power; e’en among Gods will it repel great treachery. Wisdom, Most Sapient One, brings force that lengthens life. May wisdom bring the juice to us.
verses.wilson_translation: So then by Indu,Indraobtains among the gods great brilliancy; by your sacrifice, O doer of gooddeeds, food and old age is prolonged, by our sacrifice this (Soma) is poured out by us.
verses.griffith_verse: So Indra is by lndu's power; e’en among Gods will it repel great treachery. Wisdom, Most Sapient One, brings force that lengthens life. May wisdom bring the juice to us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLV. Sapatnibadhanam.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FROM out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power,Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself. Auspicious, with expanded leaves, sent by the Gods, victorious plant,Blow thou the rival wife away, and make my husband only mine. Stronger am , O Stronger One, yea, mightier than the mightier;And she who is my rival wife is lower than the lowest dames. Her very name I utter not: she takes no pleasure in this man.Far into distance most remote drive we the rival wife away. I am the conqueror, and thou, thou also act victorious:As victory attends us both we will subdue my fellow-wife. I have gained thee for vanquisher, have grasped thee with a stronger spell.As a cow hastens to her calf, so let thy spirit speed te me, hasten like water on its way.

verses.sanskrit: इमां खनाम्योषधिं वीरुधं बलवत्तमां ।यया सपत्नीं बाधते यया संविंदते पतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: imā́m ǀ khanāmi ǀ óṣadhim ǀ vīrúdham ǀ bálavat-tamām ǀyáyā ǀ sa-pátnīm ǀ bā́dhate ǀ yáyā ǀ sam-vindáte ǀ pátim ǁ
verses.english_translation: FROM out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power, Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself.
verses.wilson_translation: I dig up this most potent medicinal creeper, by which (a wife) destroys a rival wife, by which shesecures to herself her husband.
verses.griffith_verse: FROM out the earth I dig this plant, a herb of most effectual power, Wherewith one quells the rival wife and gains the husband for oneself.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्तानपर्णे सुभगे देवजूते सहस्वति ।सपत्नीं मे परा धम पतिं मे केवलं कुरु ॥
verses.transliteration: úttāna-parṇe ǀ sú-bhage ǀ déva-jūte ǀ sáhasvati ǀsa-pátnīm ǀ me ǀ párā ǀ dhama ǀ pátim ǀ me ǀ kévalam ǀ kuru ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious, with expanded leaves, sent by the Gods, victorious plant, Blow thou the rival wife away, and make my husband only mine.
verses.wilson_translation: O (plural nt) with upturned leaves, auspicious, sent by the gods, powerful, remove my rival and make myhusband mine alone.
verses.griffith_verse: Auspicious, with expanded leaves, sent by the Gods, victorious plant, Blow thou the rival wife away, and make my husband only mine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत्तराहमुत्तर उत्तरेदुत्तराभ्यः ।अथा सपत्नी या ममाधरा साधराभ्यः ॥
verses.transliteration: út-tarā ǀ ahám ǀ ut-tare ǀ út-tarā ǀ ít ǀ út-tarābhyaḥ ǀátha ǀ sa-pátnī ǀ yā́ ǀ máma ǀ ádharā ǀ sā́ ǀ ádharābhyaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Stronger am 1, O Stronger One, yea, mightier than the mightier; And she who is my rival wife is lower than the lowest dames.
verses.wilson_translation: Excellent (plural nt), may I too be excellent, excellent among the excellent, and may she who is my rival bevile among the vile.
verses.griffith_verse: Stronger am 1, O Stronger One, yea, mightier than the mightier; And she who is my rival wife is lower than the lowest dames.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नह्यस्या नाम गृभ्णामि नो अस्मिन्रमते जने ।परामेव परावतं सपत्नीं गमयामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ asyāḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ gṛbhṇā́mi ǀ nó íti ǀ asmín ǀ ramate ǀ jáne ǀpárām ǀ evá ǀ parā-vátam ǀ sa-pátnīm ǀ gamayāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Her very name I utter not: she takes no pleasure in this man. Far into distance most remote drive we the rival wife away.
verses.wilson_translation: I will not even utter her name, no (woman) takes plural asure in that person n; may we remove the otherrival wife to a distance.
verses.griffith_verse: Her very name I utter not: she takes no pleasure in this man. Far into distance most remote drive we the rival wife away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहमस्मि सहमानाथ त्वमसि सासहिः ।उभे सहस्वती भूत्वी सपत्नीं मे सहावहै ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ asmi ǀ sáhamānā ǀ átha ǀ tvám ǀ asi ǀ sasahíḥ ǀubhé íti ǀ sáhasvatī íti ǀ bhūtvī́ ǀ sa-pátnīm ǀ me ǀ sahāvahai ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am the conqueror, and thou, thou also act victorious: As victory attends us both we will subdue my fellow-wife.
verses.wilson_translation: I am triumphing, you are triumphant; we two being powerful will triumph over my rival.
verses.griffith_verse: I am the conqueror, and thou, thou also act victorious: As victory attends us both we will subdue my fellow-wife.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उप तेऽधां सहमानामभि त्वाधां सहीयसा ।मामनु प्र ते मनो वत्सं गौरिव धावतु पथा वारिव धावतु ॥
verses.transliteration: úpa ǀ te ǀ adhām ǀ sáhamānām ǀ abhí ǀ tvā ǀ adhām ǀ sáhīyasā ǀmā́m ǀ ánu ǀ prá ǀ te ǀ mánaḥ ǀ vatsám ǀ gáuḥ-iva ǀ dhāvatu ǀ pathā́ ǀ vā́ḥ-iva ǀ dhāvatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: I have gained thee for vanquisher, have grasped thee with a stronger spell. As a cow hastens to her calf, so let thy spirit speed te me, hasten like water on its way.
verses.wilson_translation: I make you the triumphant (herb) my pillow, I support you with that more triumphant (pillow); let yourmind hasten to me as a cow to her calf, let it speed on its way like water. not fear assail you?
verses.griffith_verse: I have gained thee for vanquisher, have grasped thee with a stronger spell. As a cow hastens to her calf, so let thy spirit speed te me, hasten like water on its way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLVI. Aranyani.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GODDESS of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight.How is it that thou seekest not the village? Art thou not afraid? What time the grasshopper replies and swells the shrill cicala's voice,Seeming to sound with tinkling bells, the Lady of the Wood exults. And, yonder, cattle seem to graze, what seems a dwelling-place appears:Or else at eve the Lady of the Forest seems to free the wains. Here one is calling to his cow, another there hath felled a tree:At eve the dweller in the wood fancies that somebody hath screamed. The Goddess never slays, unless some murderous enemy approach.Man eats of savoury fruit and then takes, even as he wills, his rest. Now have I praised the Forest Queen, sweet-scented, redolent of balm,The Mother of all sylvan things, who tills not but hath stores of food.

verses.sanskrit: अरण्यान्यरण्यान्यसौ या प्रेव नश्यसि ।कथा ग्रामं न पृच्छसि न त्वा भीरिव विंदतीँ ॥
verses.transliteration: áraṇyāni ǀ áraṇyāni ǀ asáu ǀ yā́ ǀ prá-iva ǀ náśyasi ǀkathā́ ǀ grā́mam ǀ ná ǀ pṛcchasi ǀ ná ǀ tvā ǀ bhī́ḥ-iva ǀ vindatī́m̐ ǁ
verses.english_translation: GODDESS of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight. How is it that thou seekest not the village? Art thou not afraid?
verses.griffith_verse: GODDESS of wild and forest who seemest to vanish from the sight. How is it that thou seekest not the village? Art thou not afraid?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: वृषारवाय वदते यदुपावति चिच्चिकः ।आघाटिभिरिव धावयन्नरण्यानिर्महीयते ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛṣa-ravā́ya ǀ vádate ǀ yát ǀ upa-ávati ǀ ciccikáḥ ǀāghāṭíbhiḥ-iva ǀ dhāváyan ǀ araṇyāníḥ ǀ mahīyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: What time the grasshopper replies and swells the shrill cicala's voice, Seeming to sound with tinkling bells, the Lady of the Wood exults.
verses.wilson_translation: When the ciccika replies to the crying vṛṣārava,Araṇyāniis exalted, resonant, as with cymbalṣ
verses.griffith_verse: What time the grasshopper replies and swells the shrill cicala's voice, Seeming to sound with tinkling bells, the Lady of the Wood exults.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत गाव इवादंत्युत वेश्मेव दृश्यते ।उतो अरण्यानिः सायं शकटीरिव सर्जति ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ gā́vaḥ-iva ǀ adanti ǀ utá ǀ véśma-iva ǀ dṛśyate ǀutó íti ǀ araṇyāníḥ ǀ sāyám ǀ śakaṭī́ḥ-iva ǀ sarjati ǁ
verses.english_translation: And, yonder, cattle seem to graze, what seems a dwelling-place appears: Or else at eve the Lady of the Forest seems to free the wains.
verses.wilson_translation: It is as if cows are grazing, and it looks like a dwelling, and Aranyāni at eventide, indeed, dismissedthe carts.
verses.griffith_verse: And, yonder, cattle seem to graze, what seems a dwelling-place appears: Or else at eve the Lady of the Forest seems to free the wains.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गामंगैष आ ह्वयति दार्वंगैषो अपावधीत् ।वसन्नरण्यान्यां सायमक्रुक्षदिति मन्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: gā́m ǀ aṅgá ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ hvayati ǀ dā́ru ǀ aṅgá ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ ápa ǀ avadhīt ǀvásan ǀ araṇyānyā́m ǀ sāyám ǀ ákrukṣat ǀ íti ǀ manyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here one is calling to his cow, another there hath felled a tree: At eve the dweller in the wood fancies that somebody hath screamed.
verses.wilson_translation: This man calls his cow, another cuts down the timber; tarrying in the forest eventide, one thinks thereis a cry.
verses.griffith_verse: Here one is calling to his cow, another there hath felled a tree: At eve the dweller in the wood fancies that somebody hath screamed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: न वा अरण्यानिर्हंत्यन्यश्चेन्नाभिगच्छति ।स्वादोः फलस्य जग्ध्वाय यथाकामं नि पद्यते ॥
verses.transliteration: ná ǀ vái ǀ araṇyāníḥ ǀ hanti ǀ anyáḥ ǀ ca ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ abhi-gácchati ǀsvādóḥ ǀ phálasya ǀ jagdhvā́ya ǀ yathā-kā́mam ǀ ní ǀ padyate ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Goddess never slays, unless some murderous enemy approach. Man eats of savoury fruit and then takes, even as he wills, his rest.
verses.wilson_translation: But Araṇyāniinjures no one unless some other assail him; feeding upon the sweet fruit, hepenetrates at will.
verses.griffith_verse: The Goddess never slays, unless some murderous enemy approach. Man eats of savoury fruit and then takes, even as he wills, his rest.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आंजनगंधिं सुरभिं बह्वन्नामकृषीवलां ।प्राहं मृगाणां मातरमरण्यानिमशंसिषं ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ñjana-gandhim ǀ surabhím ǀ bahu-annā́m ǀ ákṛṣi-valām ǀprá ǀ ahám ǀ mṛgā́ṇām ǀ mātáram ǀ araṇyāním ǀ aśaṃsiṣam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now have I praised the Forest Queen, sweet-scented, redolent of balm, The Mother of all sylvan things, who tills not but hath stores of food.
verses.wilson_translation: I praise the musk-scented, fragrant, fertile, uncultivated Araṇyāni, the mother of wild animals.
verses.griffith_verse: Now have I praised the Forest Queen, sweet-scented, redolent of balm, The Mother of all sylvan things, who tills not but hath stores of food.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXLVII Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I TRUST in thy first wrathful deed, O Indra, when thou slewest Vṛtra and didst work to profit man;What time the two world-halves fell short of thee in might, and the earth trembled at thy force, O Thunder-anned. Thou with thy magic powers didst rend the conjurer Vṛtra, O Blameless One, with heart that longed for fame.Heroes elect thee when they battle for the prey, thee in all sacrifices worthy of renown. God Much-invoked, take pleasure in these princes here, who, thine exalters, Maghavan, have come to wealth.In synods, when the rite succeeds, they hymn the Strong for sons and progeny and riches undisturbed. That man shall find delight in well-protected wealth whose care provides for him the quick-sought joyous draught.Bringing oblations, strengthened Maghavan, by thee, he swiftly wins the spoil with heroes in the fight. Now for our band, O Maghavan, when lauded, make ample room with might, and grant us riches.Magician thou, our Varuṇa and Mitra, deal food to us, O Wondrous, as Dispenser.

verses.sanskrit: श्रत्ते दधामि प्रथमाय मन्यवेऽहन्यद्वृत्रं नर्यं विवेरपः ।उभे यत्त्वा भवतो रोदसी अनु रेजते शुष्मात्पृथिवी चिदद्रिवः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrát ǀ te ǀ dadhāmi ǀ prathamā́ya ǀ manyáve ǀ áhan ǀ yát ǀ vṛtrám ǀ náryam ǀ vivéḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀubhé íti ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ bhávataḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ánu ǀ réjate ǀ śúṣmāt ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ cit ǀ adri-vaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I TRUST in thy first wrathful deed, O Indra, when thou slewest Vṛtra and didst work to profit man; What time the two world-halves fell short of thee in might, and the earth trembled at thy force, O Thunder-anned.
verses.wilson_translation: I have faith,Indra, in your first wrath, whereby you did slay Vṛtra, and did undertake a work friendly toman; when both heaven and earth were inferior to you, the firmament trembled at your might, O wielder of thethunderbolt.
verses.griffith_verse: I TRUST in thy first wrathful deed, O Indra, when thou slewest Vṛtra and didst work to profit man; What time the two world-halves fell short of thee in might, and the earth trembled at thy force, O Thunder-anned.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं मायाभिरनवद्य मायिनं श्रवस्यता मनसा वृत्रमर्दयः ।त्वामिन्नरो वृणते गविष्टिषु त्वां विश्वासु हव्यास्विष्टिषु ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ māyā́bhiḥ ǀ anavadya ǀ māyínam ǀ śravasyatā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ardayaḥ ǀtvā́m ǀ ít ǀ náraḥ ǀ vṛṇate ǀ gó-iṣṭiṣu ǀ tvā́m ǀ víśvāsu ǀ hávyāsu ǀ íṣṭiṣu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou with thy magic powers didst rend the conjurer Vṛtra, O Blameless One, with heart that longed for fame. Heroes elect thee when they battle for the prey, thee in all sacrifices worthy of renown.
verses.wilson_translation: Irreproachable Indra, with mind intent on glory you have your deceptions slain the deceptive Vṛtra.The worshipper chooses you when he seeks for his (stolen) cattle, and in all sacrifices accompanied withinvocations.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou with thy magic powers didst rend the conjurer Vṛtra, O Blameless One, with heart that longed for fame. Heroes elect thee when they battle for the prey, thee in all sacrifices worthy of renown.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऐषु चाकंधि पुरुहूत सूरिषु वृधासो ये मघवन्नानशुर्मघं ।अर्चंति तोके तनये परिष्टिषु मेधसाता वाजिनमह्रये धने ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ eṣu ǀ cākandhi ǀ puru-hūta ǀ sūríṣu ǀ vṛdhā́saḥ ǀ yé ǀ magha-van ǀ ānaśúḥ ǀ maghám ǀárcanti ǀ toké ǀ tánaye ǀ páriṣṭiṣu ǀ medhá-sātā ǀ vājínam ǀ áhraye ǀ dháne ǁ
verses.english_translation: God Much-invoked, take pleasure in these princes here, who, thine exalters, Maghavan, have come to wealth. In synods, when the rite succeeds, they hymn the Strong for sons and progeny and riches undisturbed.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, the invoked of many, be gracious to these Suris, who thereby prospering attain, OMaghavan, toopulence; (who) adore the powerful one at the sacrifice for (the sake of obtaining) a son, a grandson, thefulfilment of their desires, and honourable wealth.
verses.griffith_verse: God Much-invoked, take pleasure in these princes here, who, thine exalters, Maghavan, have come to wealth. In synods, when the rite succeeds, they hymn the Strong for sons and progeny and riches undisturbed.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स इन्नु रायः सुभृतस्य चाकनन्मदं यो अस्य रंह्यं चिकेतति ।त्वावृधो मघवंदाश्वध्वरो मक्षू स वाजं भरते धना नृभिः ॥
