verses.english_translation: From every member, every hair, disease that comes in every joint, From all thyself, from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
verses.wilson_translation: I banish disease from each limb, from each hair, from each joint where it is genitive rated, from your wholeperson.
verses.griffith_verse: From every member, every hair, disease that comes in every joint, From all thyself, from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXIV. Dream-charm.
hymns.anukramani: ५ प्रचेता आंगिरसः। दु:स्वप्ननाशनम्। अनुष्टुप् , ३ त्रिष्टुप्, ५ पंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . AVAUNT, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away.Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold. A happy boon do men elect, a mighty blessing they obtain.Bliss with Vaivasvata they see. The live man's mind seeks many a place. If by address, by blame, by imprecation we have committed sin, awake or sleeping,All hateful acts of ours, all evil doings may Agni bear away to distant places. When, Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, our deeds are wrongful and unjust,May provident Aṅgirasa prevent our foes from troubling, us. We have prevailed this day and won: we are made free from sin and guilt.Ill thoughts, that visit us awake or sleeping, seize the man we hate, yea, seize the man who hateth us.

verses.sanskrit: अपेहि मनसस्पतेऽप क्राम परश्चर ।परो निर्ऋत्या आ चक्ष्व बहुधा जीवतो मनः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápa ǀ ihi ǀ manasaḥ ǀ pate ǀ ápa ǀ krāma ǀ paráḥ ǀ cara ǀparáḥ ǀ níḥ-ṛtyai ǀ ā́ ǀ cakṣva ǀ bahudhā́ ǀ jī́vataḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: AVAUNT, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold.
verses.wilson_translation: Lord of the mind, begone, depart, proceed to a distance; look at Nirṛtifar off; the mind of a living beingis manifold.
verses.griffith_verse: AVAUNT, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: भद्रं वै वरं वृणते भद्रं युंजंति दक्षिणं ।भद्रं वैवस्वते चक्षुर्बहुत्रा जीवतो मनः ॥
verses.transliteration: bhadrám ǀ vái ǀ váram ǀ vṛṇate ǀ bhadrám ǀ yuñjanti ǀ dákṣiṇam ǀbhadrám ǀ vaivasvaté ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ bahu-trā́ ǀ jī́vataḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: A happy boon do men elect, a mighty blessing they obtain. Bliss with Vaivasvata they see. The live man's mind seeks many a place.
verses.wilson_translation: Men solicit the boon of good fortune, they acquire abundant good fortune, (I desire) the auspicioussight of Vaivasvat; the mind of a living being is variously (directed).
verses.griffith_verse: A happy boon do men elect, a mighty blessing they obtain. Bliss with Vaivasvata they see. The live man's mind seeks many a place.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदाशसा निःशसाभिशसोपारिम जाग्रतो यत्स्वपंतः ।अग्निर्विश्वान्यप दुष्कृतान्यजुष्टान्यारे अस्मद्दधातु ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ ā-śásā ǀ niḥ-śásā ǀ abhi-śásā ǀ upa-ārimá ǀ jā́grataḥ ǀ yát ǀ svapántaḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-kṛtā́ni ǀ ájuṣṭāni ǀ āré ǀ asmát ǀ dadhātu ǁ
verses.english_translation: If by address, by blame, by imprecation we have committed sin, awake or sleeping, All hateful acts of ours, all evil doings may Agni bear away to distant places.
verses.wilson_translation: Whatever sin we have committed by speaking to (others), speaking against (others), speaking (evil)about (others), whether walking or sleeping, may Agniremove all such hateful sins far from us.
verses.griffith_verse: If by address, by blame, by imprecation we have committed sin, awake or sleeping, All hateful acts of ours, all evil doings may Agni bear away to distant places.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदिंद्र ब्रह्मणस्पतेऽभिद्रोहं चरामसि ।प्रचेता न आंगिरसो द्विषतां पात्वंहसः ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ indra ǀ brahmaṇaḥ ǀ pate ǀ abhi-drohám ǀ cárāmasi ǀprá-cetāḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ āṅgirasáḥ ǀ dviṣatā́m ǀ pātu ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: When, Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, our deeds are wrongful and unjust, May provident Aṅgirasa prevent our foes from troubling, us.
verses.wilson_translation: OIndra, OBrahmaṇaspati, whatever sin we run into, (save us thereform), and may Pracetasof the Aṅgirasas protect us from the malignity of our enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: When, Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, our deeds are wrongful and unjust, May provident Aṅgirasa prevent our foes from troubling, us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अजैष्माद्यासनाम चाभूमानागसो वयं ।जाग्रत्स्वप्नः संकल्पः पापो यं द्विष्मस्तं स ऋच्छतु यो नो द्वेष्टि तमृच्छतु ॥
verses.transliteration: ájaiṣma ǀ adyá ǀ ásanāma ǀ ca ǀ ábhūma ǀ ánāgasaḥ ǀ vayám ǀjāgrat-svapnáḥ ǀ sam-kalpáḥ ǀ pāpáḥ ǀ yám ǀ dviṣmáḥ ǀ tám ǀ sáḥ ǀ ṛcchatu ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dvéṣṭi ǀ tám ǀ ṛcchatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: We have prevailed this day and won: we are made free from sin and guilt. Ill thoughts, that visit us awake or sleeping, seize the man we hate, yea, seize the man who hateth us.
verses.wilson_translation: We have triumphed today, we have won, we have become free from guilt; may evil designs formed inwaking or sleep be transferred to him whom we hate, be transferred to him who hates us.
verses.griffith_verse: We have prevailed this day and won: we are made free from sin and guilt. Ill thoughts, that visit us awake or sleeping, seize the man we hate, yea, seize the man who hateth us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXV. Viśvedevas.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GODS, whatsoe’er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction,For that let us sing hymns and make atonement. Well be it with our quadrupeds and bipeds. Auspicious be the Dove that hath been sent us, a harmless bird, ye Gods, within our dwelling.May Agni, Sage, be pleased with our oblation, and may the Missile borne on wings avoid us. Let not the Arrow that hath wings distract us: beside the fire-place, on the hearth it settles.May, it bring welfare to our men and cattle: here let the Dove, ye Gods, forbear to harm us. The screeching of the owl is ineffective and when beside the fire the Dove hath settled,To him who sent it hither as an envoy, to him be reverence paid, to Death, to Yama. Drive forth the Dove, chase it with holy verses: rejoicing, bring ye hither food and cattle,Barring the way against all grief and trouble. Let the swift bird fly forth and leave us vigour.

verses.sanskrit: देवाः कपोत इषितो यदिच्छंदूतो निर्ऋत्या इदमाजगाम ।तस्मा अर्चाम कृणवाम निष्कृतिं शं नो अस्तु द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
verses.transliteration: dévāḥ ǀ kapótaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yát ǀ icchán ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ níḥ-ṛtyāḥ ǀ idám ǀ ā-jagā́ma ǀtásmai ǀ arcāma ǀ kṛṇávāma ǀ níḥ-kṛtim ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
verses.english_translation: GODS, whatsoe’er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction, For that let us sing hymns and make atonement. Well be it with our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.wilson_translation: O gods, let us worship for that, desiring which the pigeon sent as Nirṛti's messenger, has come to this(ceremony); let us make atonement, may prosperity be given to our bipeds and quadrupeds.
verses.griffith_verse: GODS, whatsoe’er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction, For that let us sing hymns and make atonement. Well be it with our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: शिवः कपोत इषितो नो अस्त्वनागा देवाः शकुनो गृहेषु ।अग्निर्हि विप्रो जुषतां हविर्नः परि हेतिः पक्षिणी नो वृणक्तु ॥
verses.transliteration: śiváḥ ǀ kapótaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ anāgā́ḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ śakunáḥ ǀ gṛhéṣu ǀagníḥ ǀ hí ǀ vípraḥ ǀ juṣátām ǀ havíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pári ǀ hetíḥ ǀ pakṣíṇī ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛṇaktu ǁ
verses.english_translation: Auspicious be the Dove that hath been sent us, a harmless bird, ye Gods, within our dwelling. May Agni, Sage, be pleased with our oblation, and may the Missile borne on wings avoid us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the bird sent to our dwellings, the pigeon, be auspicious, O gods, and void of offence, so that thewise Agnimay approve of our oblation, and the winged weapon (of mischief) depart from us.
verses.griffith_verse: Auspicious be the Dove that hath been sent us, a harmless bird, ye Gods, within our dwelling. May Agni, Sage, be pleased with our oblation, and may the Missile borne on wings avoid us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हेतिः पक्षिणी न दभात्यस्मानाष्ट्र्यां पदं कृणुते अग्निधाने ।शं नो गोभ्यश्च पुरुषेभ्यश्चास्तु मा नो हिंसीदिह देवाः कपोतः ॥
verses.transliteration: hetíḥ ǀ pakṣíṇī ǀ ná ǀ dabhāti ǀ asmā́n ǀ āṣṭryā́m ǀ padám ǀ kṛṇute ǀ agni-dhā́ne ǀśám ǀ naḥ ǀ góbhyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ púruṣebhyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ astu ǀ mā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ hiṃsīt ǀ ihá ǀ devāḥ ǀ kapótaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let not the Arrow that hath wings distract us: beside the fire-place, on the hearth it settles. May, it bring welfare to our men and cattle: here let the Dove, ye Gods, forbear to harm us.
verses.wilson_translation: May the winged weapon (of mischief) do us no harm; he takes his plural ce upon the touchwood, the seatof Agni; may prosperity attend our cattle and our people, let not the pigeon, gods, do us harm in this (dwelling).
verses.griffith_verse: Let not the Arrow that hath wings distract us: beside the fire-place, on the hearth it settles. May, it bring welfare to our men and cattle: here let the Dove, ye Gods, forbear to harm us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यदुलूको वदति मोघमेतद्यत्कपोतः पदमग्नौ कृणोति ।यस्य दूतः प्रहित एष एतत्तस्मै यमाय नमो अस्तु मृत्यवे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ úlūkaḥ ǀ vádati ǀ moghám ǀ etát ǀ yát ǀ kapótaḥ ǀ padám ǀ agnáu ǀ kṛṇóti ǀyásya ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ prá-hitaḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ etát ǀ tásmai ǀ yamā́ya ǀ námaḥ ǀ astu ǀ mṛtyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: The screeching of the owl is ineffective and when beside the fire the Dove hath settled, To him who sent it hither as an envoy, to him be reverence paid, to Death, to Yama.
verses.wilson_translation: May that which the owl shrieks be in vain, (and may it be in vain) that the pigeon takes his plural ce uponthe fire; may this reverence be paid to Yama, (the god of) Death, as whose messenger he is sent.
verses.griffith_verse: The screeching of the owl is ineffective and when beside the fire the Dove hath settled, To him who sent it hither as an envoy, to him be reverence paid, to Death, to Yama.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ऋचा कपोतं नुदत प्रणोदमिषं मदंतः परि गां नयध्वं ।संयोपयंतो दुरितानि विश्वा हित्वा न ऊर्जं प्र पतात्पतिष्ठः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛcā́ ǀ kapótam ǀ nudata ǀ pra-nódam ǀ íṣam ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ pári ǀ gā́m ǀ nayadhvam ǀsam-yopáyantaḥ ǀ duḥ-itā́ni ǀ víśvā ǀ hitvā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ū́rjam ǀ prá ǀ patāt ǀ pátiṣṭhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Drive forth the Dove, chase it with holy verses: rejoicing, bring ye hither food and cattle, Barring the way against all grief and trouble. Let the swift bird fly forth and leave us vigour.
verses.wilson_translation: (Praised) by our hymn, O gods, drive out the pigeon, who deserves to be driven out, exhilarated (byour oblation), bring us food and cattle, dissipating all our misfortunes; abandoning our food, may the swift(pigeon) fly away.
verses.griffith_verse: Drive forth the Dove, chase it with holy verses: rejoicing, bring ye hither food and cattle, Barring the way against all grief and trouble. Let the swift bird fly forth and leave us vigour.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVI. Sapatnanāśanam.
hymns.anukramani: ५ ऋषभो वैराजः, ऋषभः शाक्वरो वा। सपत्न्घ्नम्। अनुष्टुप् , ५ महापंक्तिः।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror:Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine I am my rivals’ slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt,And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet. Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string.Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me. Hither I came as conqueror with mighty all-effecting power,And I have mastered all your thought, your synod, and your holy work. May I be highest, having gained your strength in war, your skill in peacemy feet have trodden on your heads.Speak to me from beneath my feet, as frogs from out the water croak, as frogs from out the water croak.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषभं मा समानानां सपत्नानां विषासहिं ।हंतारं शत्रूणां कृधि विराजं गोपतिं गवां ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṣabhám ǀ mā ǀ samānā́nām ǀ sa-pátnānām ǀ vi-sasahím ǀhantā́ram ǀ śátrūṇām ǀ kṛdhi ǀ vi-rā́jam ǀ gó-patim ǀ gávām ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine
verses.wilson_translation: Make me,Indra, (renowned like) a bull among my equals, victor over my rivals, the slayer of my
verses.griffith_verse: MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहमस्मि सपत्नहेंद्र इवारिष्टो अक्षतः ।अधः सपत्ना मे पदोरिमे सर्वे अभिष्ठिताः ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ asmi ǀ sapatna-hā́ ǀ índraḥ-iva ǀ áriṣṭaḥ ǀ ákṣataḥ ǀadháḥ ǀ sa-pátnāḥ ǀ me ǀ padóḥ ǀ imé ǀ sárve ǀ abhí-sthitāḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: I am my rivals’ slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt, And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet.
verses.wilson_translation: I am the destroyer of my enemies, like Indra, unharmed and unwounded; may all these my foes be castdown under my feet.
verses.griffith_verse: I am my rivals’ slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt, And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अत्रैव वोऽपि नह्याम्युभे आर्त्नी इव ज्यया ।वाचस्पते नि षेधेमान्यथा मदधरं वदान् ॥
verses.transliteration: átra ǀ evá ǀ vaḥ ǀ ápi ǀ nahyāmi ǀ ubhé íti ǀ ā́rtnī ivetyā́rtnī-iva ǀ jyáyā ǀvā́caḥ ǀ pate ǀ ní ǀ sedha ǀ imā́n ǀ yáthā ǀ mát ǀ ádharam ǀ vádān ǁ
verses.english_translation: Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string. Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me.
verses.wilson_translation: I bind you here, like the two extremities of the bow the bowstring; restrain them, lord of speech, thatthey may speak humbly to me.
verses.griffith_verse: Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string. Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभिभूरहमागमं विश्वकर्मेण धाम्ना ।आ वश्चित्तमा वो व्रतमा वोऽहं समितिं ददे ॥
verses.transliteration: abhi-bhū́ḥ ǀ ahám ǀ ā́ ǀ agamam ǀ viśvá-karmeṇa ǀ dhā́mnā ǀā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ cittám ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ vratám ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ahám ǀ sám-itim ǀ dade ǁ
verses.english_translation: Hither I came as conqueror with mighty all-effecting power, And I have mastered all your thought, your synod, and your holy work.
verses.wilson_translation: I have come triumphant with power, equal to any exploit; I seize upon minds, your pious observances,your prowess in war.
verses.griffith_verse: Hither I came as conqueror with mighty all-effecting power, And I have mastered all your thought, your synod, and your holy work.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: योगक्षेमं व आदायाहं भूयासमुत्तम आ वो मूर्धानमक्रमीं ।अधस्पदान्म उद्वदत मंडूका इवोदकान्मंडूका उदकादिव ॥
verses.transliteration: yoga-kṣemám ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā-dā́ya ǀ ahám ǀ bhūyāsam ǀ ut-tamáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ akramīm ǀadhaḥ-padā́t ǀ me ǀ út ǀ vadata ǀ maṇḍū́kāḥ-iva ǀ udakā́t ǀ maṇḍū́kāḥ ǀ udakā́t-iva ǁ
verses.english_translation: May I be highest, having gained your strength in war, your skill in peace my feet have trodden on your heads. Speak to me from beneath my feet, as frogs from out the water croak, as frogs from out the water croak.
verses.wilson_translation: Seizing upon your goods and chattels, may I victorious; I walk upon your heads; cry aloud frombeneath my feet, like frogs from (below) the water, like frogs from (below) the water.
verses.griffith_verse: May I be highest, having gained your strength in war, your skill in peace my feet have trodden on your heads. Speak to me from beneath my feet, as frogs from out the water croak, as frogs from out the water croak.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVII. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice.Bestow upon us wealth with many hero sons: thou, having glowed with Fervour, wonnest heavenly light. Let us call Śakra to libations here effused, winner of light who joyeth in the potent juice.Mark well this sacrifice of ours and come to us: we pray to Maghavan the Vanquisher of hosts. By royal Soma's and by Varuṇa's decree, under Bṛhaspati's and Anumati's guard,This day by thine authority, O Maghavan, Maker, Disposer thou! have I enjoyed the jars., too, urged on, have had my portion, in the bowl, and as first Prince I drew forth this my hymn of praise,When with the prize I came unto the flowing juice, O Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, to your home.

verses.sanskrit: तुभ्येदमिंद्र परि षिच्यते मधु त्वं सुतस्य कलशस्य राजसि ।त्वं रयिं पुरुवीरामु नस्कृधि त्वं तपः परितप्याजयः स्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: túbhya ǀ idám ǀ indra ǀ pári ǀ sicyate ǀ mádhu ǀ tvám ǀ sutásya ǀ kaláśasya ǀ rājasi ǀtvám ǀ rayím ǀ puru-vī́rām ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ naḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ tvám ǀ tápaḥ ǀ pari-tápya ǀ ajayaḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice. Bestow upon us wealth with many hero sons: thou, having glowed with Fervour, wonnest heavenly light.
verses.wilson_translation: For you,Indra, is this Somapoured forth, you rule over the effused (Soma of) the jar; do you bestowupon us riches with numerous sons, you did win heaven, performing arduous penance.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice. Bestow upon us wealth with many hero sons: thou, having glowed with Fervour, wonnest heavenly light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्जितं महि मंदानमंधसो हवामहे परि शक्रं सुताँ उप ।इमं नो यज्ञमिह बोध्या गहि स्पृधो जयंतं मघवानमीमहे ॥
verses.transliteration: svaḥ-jítam ǀ máhi ǀ mandānám ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ hávāmahe ǀ pári ǀ śakrám ǀ sutā́n ǀ úpa ǀimám ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ ihá ǀ bodhi ǀ ā́ ǀ gahi ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ jáyantam ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ īmahe ǁ
verses.english_translation: Let us call Śakra to libations here effused, winner of light who joyeth in the potent juice. Mark well this sacrifice of ours and come to us: we pray to Maghavan the Vanquisher of hosts.
verses.wilson_translation: We summon to the libations the mightyŚukra, the conqueror of heaven, exhilarated by sacrificialfood; take notice of this our sacrifice here and come; we solicit (for wealth)Maghavan, victorious over his foes.
verses.griffith_verse: Let us call Śakra to libations here effused, winner of light who joyeth in the potent juice. Mark well this sacrifice of ours and come to us: we pray to Maghavan the Vanquisher of hosts.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सोमस्य राज्ञो वरुणस्य धर्मणि बृहस्पतेरनुमत्या उ शर्मणि ।तवाहमद्य मघवन्नुपस्तुतौ धातर्विधातः कलशाँ अभक्षयं ॥
verses.transliteration: sómasya ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhármaṇi ǀ bṛ́haspáteḥ ǀ ánu-matyāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śármaṇi ǀtáva ǀ ahám ǀ adyá ǀ magha-van ǀ úpa-stutau ǀ dhā́taḥ ǀ vídhātaríti ví-dhātaḥ ǀ kaláśān ǀ abhakṣayam ǁ
verses.english_translation: By royal Soma's and by Varuṇa's decree, under Bṛhaspati's and Anumati's guard, This day by thine authority, O Maghavan, Maker, Disposer thou! have I enjoyed the jars.
verses.wilson_translation: (Engaged) in the worship of the royal Somaand of Varuṇa, (present) in the protecting (dwelling) of Bṛhaspati and Anumati, (I am assiduous) in your praise,Maghavan;Dhātāand Vidhātā, I have fed on thepitcher.
verses.griffith_verse: By royal Soma's and by Varuṇa's decree, under Bṛhaspati's and Anumati's guard, This day by thine authority, O Maghavan, Maker, Disposer thou! have I enjoyed the jars.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रसूतो भक्षमकरं चरावपि स्तोमं चेमं प्रथमः सूरिरुन्मृजे ।सुते सातेन यद्यागमं वां प्रति विश्वामित्रजमदग्नी दमे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá-sūtaḥ ǀ bhakṣám ǀ akaram ǀ caráu ǀ ápi ǀ stómam ǀ ca ǀ imám ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ sūríḥ ǀ út ǀ mṛje ǀsuté ǀ sāténa ǀ yádi ǀ ā́ ǀ ágamam ǀ vām ǀ práti ǀ viśvāmitrajamadagnī íti ǀ dáme ǁ
verses.english_translation: 1, too, urged on, have had my portion, in the bowl, and as first Prince I drew forth this my hymn of praise, When with the prize I came unto the flowing juice, O Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, to your home.
verses.wilson_translation: Enjoined by you, I have prepared the food at the (sacrifice) about to be performed, and as chiefworshipper I complete this hymn of praise. (Indraspeaks): The Somabeing poured out in your respectivedwellings, OViśvāmitraand Jamadagni, (offer praise) when I come with (the wealth) which I am going todistribute.
verses.griffith_verse: 1, too, urged on, have had my portion, in the bowl, and as first Prince I drew forth this my hymn of praise, When with the prize I came unto the flowing juice, O Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, to your home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXVIII. Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O THE Wind's chariot, O its power and glory! Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder.It makes the regions red and touches heaven, and as it moves the dust of earth is scattered. Along the traces of the Wind they hurry, they come to him as dames to an assembly.Borne on his car with these for his attendants, the God speeds forth, the universe's Monarch. Travelling on the paths of air's mid-region, no single day doth he take rest or slumber.Holy and earliest-born, Friend of the waters, where did he spring and from what region came he? Germ of the world, the Deities’ vital spirit, this God moves ever as his will inclines him.His voice is heard, his shape is ever viewless. Let us adore this Wind with our oblation.

verses.sanskrit: वातस्य नु महिमानं रथस्य रुजन्नेति स्तनयन्नस्य घोषः ।दिविस्पृग्यात्यरुणानि कृण्वन्नुतो एति पृथिव्या रेणुमस्यन् ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́tasya ǀ nú ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ráthasya ǀ ruján ǀ eti ǀ stanáyan ǀ asya ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀdivi-spṛ́k ǀ yāti ǀ aruṇā́ni ǀ kṛṇván ǀ utó íti ǀ eti ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ reṇúm ǀ ásyan ǁ
verses.english_translation: O THE Wind's chariot, O its power and glory! Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder. It makes the regions red and touches heaven, and as it moves the dust of earth is scattered.
verses.wilson_translation: (I proclaim) the greatness of the impetuous Vāyu, his voice spread thundering around; he movesalong sweeping the sky, tinting purple (the quarters of the horizon), he advances, raising the dust of the earth.
verses.griffith_verse: O THE Wind's chariot, O its power and glory! Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder. It makes the regions red and touches heaven, and as it moves the dust of earth is scattered.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं प्रेरते अनु वातस्य विष्ठा ऐनं गच्छंति समनं न योषाः ।ताभिः सयुक्सरथं देव ईयतेऽस्य विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ prá ǀ īrate ǀ ánu ǀ vā́tasya ǀ vi-sthā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ enam ǀ gacchanti ǀ sámanam ǀ ná ǀ yóṣāḥ ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ sa-yúk ǀ sa-rátham ǀ deváḥ ǀ īyate ǀ asyá ǀ víśvasya ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ rā́jā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Along the traces of the Wind they hurry, they come to him as dames to an assembly. Borne on his car with these for his attendants, the God speeds forth, the universe's Monarch.
verses.wilson_translation: Solid masses advance to meet the wind; the mares come to him as to battle; associated with themandin the same car the divinity proceeds, the sovereign of all this world.
verses.griffith_verse: Along the traces of the Wind they hurry, they come to him as dames to an assembly. Borne on his car with these for his attendants, the God speeds forth, the universe's Monarch.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंतरिक्षे पथिभिरीयमानो न नि विशते कतमच्चनाहः ।अपां सखा प्रथमजा ऋतावा क्व स्विज्जातः कुत आ बभूव ॥
verses.transliteration: antárikṣe ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ ī́yamānaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ní ǀ viśate ǀ katamát ǀ caná ǀ áharíti ǀapā́m ǀ sákhā ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛtá-vā ǀ kvá ǀ svit ǀ jātáḥ ǀ kútaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ babhūva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Travelling on the paths of air's mid-region, no single day doth he take rest or slumber. Holy and earliest-born, Friend of the waters, where did he spring and from what region came he?
verses.wilson_translation: Traversing the firmament by its paths, (Vāyu) rests not for a single day; the friend of the waters, thefirst-born, the utterer of truth-- where has he been genitive rated, whence was he manifested?
verses.griffith_verse: Travelling on the paths of air's mid-region, no single day doth he take rest or slumber. Holy and earliest-born, Friend of the waters, where did he spring and from what region came he?
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आत्मा देवानां भुवनस्य गर्भो यथावशं चरति देव एषः ।घोषा इदस्य शृण्विरे न रूपं तस्मै वाताय हविषा विधेम ॥
verses.transliteration: ātmā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ yathā-vaśám ǀ carati ǀ deváḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀghóṣāḥ ǀ ít ǀ asya ǀ śṛṇvire ǀ ná ǀ rūpám ǀ tásmai ǀ vā́tāya ǀ havíṣā ǀ vidhema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Germ of the world, the Deities’ vital spirit, this God moves ever as his will inclines him. His voice is heard, his shape is ever viewless. Let us adore this Wind with our oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Thesoulof the gods, the germ of the world, this divinity moves according to his plural asure; his voicesare heard, his form is not (seen); let us worship that Vātawith oblations. nutritious life-sustaining (waters);Rudra, have compassion upon the food which has feet.
verses.griffith_verse: Germ of the world, the Deities’ vital spirit, this God moves ever as his will inclines him. His voice is heard, his shape is ever viewless. Let us adore this Wind with our oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXIX. COWS.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices.May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra. Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni,Whom the Aṅgirases produced by Fervour,—vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection. Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,—Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring. Prajāpati, bestowing these upon me, one-minded with all Gods and with the Fathers,Hath to our cow-pen brought auspicious cattle: so may we own the offspring they will bear us.

verses.sanskrit: मयोभूर्वातो अभि वातूस्रा ऊर्जस्वतीरोषधीरा रिशंतां ।पीवस्वतीर्जीवधन्याः पिबंत्ववसाय पद्वते रुद्र मृळ ॥
verses.transliteration: mayaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vātu ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ ū́rjasvatīḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ riśantām ǀpī́vasvatīḥ ǀ jīvá-dhanyāḥ ǀ pibantu ǀ avasā́ya ǀ pat-váte ǀ rudra ǀ mṛḷa ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices. May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices. May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: याः सरूपा विरूपा एकरूपा यासामग्निरिष्ट्या नामानि वेद ।या अंगिरसस्तपसेह चक्रुस्ताभ्यः पर्जन्य महि शर्म यच्छ ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ sá-rūpāḥ ǀ ví-rūpāḥ ǀ éka-rūpāḥ ǀ yā́sām ǀ agníḥ ǀ íṣṭyā ǀ nā́māni ǀ véda ǀyā́ḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ tápasā ǀ ihá ǀ cakrúḥ ǀ tā́bhyaḥ ǀ parjanya ǀ máhi ǀ śárma ǀ yaccha ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni, Whom the Aṅgirases produced by Fervour,—vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection.
verses.wilson_translation: Grant great felicity,Parjanya, to those cows who are of similar forms, of different forms, or of singleforms, whose names Agniknows through the sacrifice, or those whom the Aṅgirasascreated in this world bypenance.
verses.griffith_verse: Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni, Whom the Aṅgirases produced by Fervour,—vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या देवेषु तन्वमैरयंत यासां सोमो विश्वा रूपाणि वेद ।ता अस्मभ्यं पयसा पिन्वमानाः प्रजावतीरिंद्र गोष्ठे रिरीहि ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ tanvám ǀ áirayanta ǀ yā́sām ǀ sómaḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ véda ǀtā́ḥ ǀ asmábhyam ǀ páyasā ǀ pínvamānāḥ ǀ prajā́-vatīḥ ǀ indra ǀ go-sthé ǀ rirīhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,— Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring,Indra, to the cow-house (the cows) who offer their bodies to the gods, those of whom Somaknows all the properties, those that nourish us with their milk, and those that have calves.
verses.griffith_verse: Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,— Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्रजापतिर्मह्यमेता रराणो विश्वैर्देवैः पितृभिः संविदानः ।शिवाः सतीरुप नो गोष्ठमाकस्तासां वयं प्रजया सं सदेम ॥
verses.transliteration: prajā́-patiḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ etā́ḥ ǀ rárāṇaḥ ǀ víśvaiḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sam-vidānáḥ ǀśivā́ḥ ǀ satī́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ go-sthám ǀ ā́ ǀ akarítyakaḥ ǀ tā́sām ǀ vayám ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ sám ǀ sadema ǁ
verses.english_translation: Prajāpati, bestowing these upon me, one-minded with all Gods and with the Fathers, Hath to our cow-pen brought auspicious cattle: so may we own the offspring they will bear us.
verses.wilson_translation: May Prajāpatibestowing these (Cows) upon me concurring with the universal gods and the Pitara,bring the auspicious cattle to our cow-pen, may we be in possession of their progeny.
verses.griffith_verse: Prajāpati, bestowing these upon me, one-minded with all Gods and with the Fathers, Hath to our cow-pen brought auspicious cattle: so may we own the offspring they will bear us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXX. Sūrya.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life;He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o’er many a land. Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens,He rose, a light, that kills Vṛtras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes. This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud.All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength. Beaming forth splendour with thy light, thou hast attained heaven's lustrous realm.By thee were brought together all existing things, possessor of all Godhead, All-effecting God.

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राड्बृहत्पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर्दधद्यज्ञपतावविह्रुतं ।वातजूतो यो अभिरक्षति त्मना प्रजाः पुपोष पुरुधा वि राजति ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-bhrā́ṭ ǀ bṛhát ǀ pibatu ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ dádhat ǀ yajñá-patau ǀ ávi-hrutam ǀvā́ta-jūtaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ abhi-rákṣati ǀ tmánā ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ pupoṣa ǀ purudhā́ ǀ ví ǀ rājati ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o’er many a land.
verses.wilson_translation: Let the radiant (Sūrya) drink much sweet Soma, bestowing unbroken life upon the lord of thesacrifice; (Sūrya), who impelled by the wind protects his people of his own accord, nourishes them and shinesin various plural ces.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o’er many a land.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राड्बृहत्सुभृतं वाजसातमं धर्मंदिवो धरुणे सत्यमर्पितं ।अमित्रहा वृत्रहा दस्युहंतमं ज्योतिर्जज्ञे असुरहा सपत्नहा ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-bhrā́ṭ ǀ bṛhát ǀ sú-bhṛtam ǀ vāja-sā́tamam ǀ dhárman ǀ diváḥ ǀ dharúṇe ǀ satyám ǀ árpitam ǀamitra-hā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ dasyuhán-tamam ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ jajñe ǀ asura-hā́ ǀ sapatna-hā́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light, that kills Vṛtras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.
verses.wilson_translation: The radiant light is born mighty, well-cherished, the abundant bestower of food, eternal, deposited inthe supporting sustainer of the sky, the slayer of adversaries, the slayer of the Vṛtras, abundantly slaying the Dasyus, the slayer of the Asuras, the slayer of rivals.
verses.griffith_verse: Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light, that kills Vṛtras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरुत्तमं विश्वजिद्धनजिदुच्यते बृहत् ।विश्वभ्राड्भ्राजो महि सूर्यो दृश उरु पप्रथे सह ओजो अच्युतं ॥
verses.transliteration: idám ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ jyótiṣām ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ ut-tamám ǀ viśva-jít ǀ dhana-jít ǀ ucyate ǀ bṛhát ǀviśva-bhrā́ṭ ǀ bhrājáḥ ǀ máhi ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ dṛśé ǀ urú ǀ paprathe ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ ácyutam ǁ
verses.english_translation: This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud. All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength.
verses.wilson_translation: This light, the best of lights, the most excellent, is called the conqueror of all, the conqueror of wealth,mighty, all-illumining, radiant, mighty,Sūryadisplays to view his vast power, his unfailing lustre.
verses.griffith_verse: This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud. All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजंज्योतिषा स्वरगच्छो रोचनं दिवः ।येनेमा विश्वा भुवनान्याभृता विश्वकर्मणा विश्वदेव्यावता ॥
verses.transliteration: vi-bhrā́jan ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ sváḥ ǀ ágacchaḥ ǀ rocanám ǀ diváḥ ǀyéna ǀ imā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ ā́-bhṛtā ǀ viśvá-karmaṇā ǀ viśvádevya-vatā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Beaming forth splendour with thy light, thou hast attained heaven's lustrous realm. By thee were brought together all existing things, possessor of all Godhead, All-effecting God.
verses.wilson_translation: Illumining the whole (world) with your radiance, you have attained (Sūrya) the luminous region ofheaven, by which (radiance) animating all pious acts and addressed to the universal gods, all living beings arecherished.
verses.griffith_verse: Beaming forth splendour with thy light, thou hast attained heaven's lustrous realm. By thee were brought together all existing things, possessor of all Godhead, All-effecting God.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXI. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FOR Iṭa's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car,And hear the Soma-giver's call. Thou from his skin hast borne the head of the swift-moving combatant,And sought the Soma-pourer's home. Venya, that mortal man, hast thou, for Āstrabudhna the devout,O Indra, many a time set free. Bring, Indra, to the east again that Sun who now is in the west,Even against the will of Gods.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्यमिटतो रथमिंद्र प्रावः सुतावतः ।अशृणोः सोमिनो हवं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyám ǀ iṭátaḥ ǀ rátham ǀ índra ǀ prá ǀ āvaḥ ǀ sutá-vataḥ ǀáśṛṇoḥ ǀ somínaḥ ǀ hávam ǁ
verses.english_translation: FOR Iṭa's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car, And hear the Soma-giver's call.
verses.wilson_translation: You have protected,Indra, this chariot of Iḷā, who offered libations; hear the invocation of thepresenter of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: FOR Iṭa's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car, And hear the Soma-giver's call.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं मखस्य दोधतः शिरोऽव त्वचो भरः ।अगच्छः सोमिनो गृहं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ makhásya ǀ dódhataḥ ǀ śíraḥ ǀ áva ǀ tvacáḥ ǀ bharaḥ ǀágacchaḥ ǀ somínaḥ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou from his skin hast borne the head of the swift-moving combatant, And sought the Soma-pourer's home.
verses.wilson_translation: You have carried off the head of the trmbling sacrifice from his skin; come to the dwelling of thepresenter of the Soma.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou from his skin hast borne the head of the swift-moving combatant, And sought the Soma-pourer's home.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्यमिंद्र मर्त्यमास्त्रबुध्नाय वेन्यं ।मुहुः श्रथ्ना मनस्यवे ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyám ǀ indra ǀ mártyam ǀ āstra-budhnā́ya ǀ venyám ǀmúhuḥ ǀ śrathnāḥ ǀ manasyáve ǁ
verses.english_translation: Venya, that mortal man, hast thou, for Āstrabudhna the devout, O Indra, many a time set free.
verses.wilson_translation: You have often,Indra, let loose the mortal Venya, against Manasyu, the son of Astrabudhna.
verses.griffith_verse: Venya, that mortal man, hast thou, for Āstrabudhna the devout, O Indra, many a time set free.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्वं त्यमिंद्र सूर्यं पश्चा संतं पुरस्कृधि ।देवानां चित्तिरो वशं ॥
verses.transliteration: tvám ǀ tyám ǀ indra ǀ sū́ryam ǀ paścā́ ǀ sántam ǀ puráḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀdevā́nām ǀ cit ǀ tiráḥ ǀ váśam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring, Indra, to the east again that Sun who now is in the west, Even against the will of Gods.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring forward that Sūrya,Indra, who is lingering behind, the beloved of the gods, (awhile) concealedfrom them.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring, Indra, to the east again that Sun who now is in the west, Even against the will of Gods.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXII. Dawn.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path. Come with kind thoughts, most liberal, rousing the warrior's hymn of praise, with bounteous ones, As nourishers we tie the thread, and, liberal with our bounty, offer sacrifice. Dawn drives away her Sister's gloom, and, through her excellence, makes her retrace her path.

verses.sanskrit: आ याहि वनसा सह गावः सचंत वर्तनिं यदूधभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ vánasā ǀ sahá ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ sacanta ǀ vartaním ǀ yát ǀ ū́dha-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path.
verses.wilson_translation: Come, (Uṣas), with the desirable (radiance); let the cows who are of full udders accompany yourchariot.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: आ याहि वस्व्या धिया मंहिष्ठो जारयन्मखः सुदानुभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ vásvyā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ máṃhiṣṭhaḥ ǀ jārayát-makhaḥ ǀ sudā́nu-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Come with kind thoughts, most liberal, rousing the warrior's hymn of praise, with bounteous ones,
verses.wilson_translation: Come, (Uṣas), with kindly thoughts; (it is the season) most honoured by the genitive rous, and whichbrings the sacrifice to completion.
verses.griffith_verse: Come with kind thoughts, most liberal, rousing the warrior's hymn of praise, with bounteous ones,
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पितुभृतो न तंतुमित्सुदानवः प्रति दध्मो यजामसि ॥
verses.transliteration: pitu-bhṛ́taḥ ǀ ná ǀ tántum ǀ ít ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ práti ǀ dadhmaḥ ǀ yájāmasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: As nourishers we tie the thread, and, liberal with our bounty, offer sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: Like bearers of food, liberal in our gifts, we spread the thread (of sacrifice before the dawn), andworship (her).
verses.griffith_verse: As nourishers we tie the thread, and, liberal with our bounty, offer sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उषा अप स्वसुस्तमः सं वर्तयति वर्तनिं सुजातता ॥
verses.transliteration: uṣā́ḥ ǀ ápa ǀ svásuḥ ǀ támaḥ ǀ sám ǀ vartayati ǀ vartaním ǀ su-jātátā ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dawn drives away her Sister's gloom, and, through her excellence, makes her retrace her path.
verses.wilson_translation: Uṣas drives away the darkness of her sister (night); her genitive rative benevolence (harnesses) herchariot.
verses.griffith_verse: Dawn drives away her Sister's gloom, and, through her excellence, makes her retrace her path.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIII. The King.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable.Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away. Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved.Stand stedfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp. This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power.May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmaṇaspati, on him. Firm is the sky and firm the earth, and stedfast also are these hills.Stedfast is all this living world, and stedfast is this King of men. Stedfast, may Varuṇa the King, stedfast, the God Bṛhaspati,Stedfast, may Indra, stedfast too, may Agni keep thy stedfast reign. On constant Soma let us think with constant sacrificial giftAnd then may Indra make the clans bring tribute unto thee alone.

verses.sanskrit: आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधि ध्रुवस्तिष्ठाविचाचलिः ।विशस्त्वा सर्वा वांछंतु मा त्वद्राष्ट्रमधि भ्रशत् ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ ahārṣam ǀ antáḥ ǀ edhi ǀ dhruváḥ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ ávi-cācaliḥ ǀvíśaḥ ǀ tvā ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ vāñchantu ǀ mā́ ǀ tvát ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ ádhi ǀ bhraśat ǁ
verses.english_translation: BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away.
verses.wilson_translation: I have consecrated you, (Rasa); come among us, be steady and unvacillating, may all your subjectsdesire you (for their king), may the kingdom never fall from you.
verses.griffith_verse: BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand stedfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इहैवैधि माप च्योष्ठाः पर्वत इवाविचाचलिः ।इंद्र इवेह ध्रुवस्तिष्ठेह राष्ट्रमु धारय ॥
verses.transliteration: ihá ǀ evá ǀ edhi ǀ mā́ ǀ ápa ǀ cyoṣṭhāḥ ǀ párvataḥ-iva ǀ ávi-cācaliḥ ǀíndraḥ-iva ǀ ihá ǀ dhruváḥ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ ihá ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ dhāraya ǁ
verses.english_translation: Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved. Stand stedfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp.
verses.wilson_translation: Come into this (kingdom), may you never be deposed, unvacillating as a mountain; stand firm here like Indra; establish your kingdom in this world.
verses.griffith_verse: Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved. Stand stedfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इममिंद्रो अदीधरद्ध्रुवं ध्रुवेण हविषा ।तस्मै सोमो अधि ब्रवत्तस्मा उ ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥
verses.transliteration: imám ǀ índraḥ ǀ adīdharat ǀ dhruvám ǀ dhruvéṇa ǀ havíṣā ǀtásmai ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ bravat ǀ tásmai ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power. May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmaṇaspati, on him.
verses.wilson_translation: May Indra, gratified by the perpetual oblation, firmly establish this (prince); may Soma, may Brahmaṇaspati address him (as their votary).
verses.griffith_verse: This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power. May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmaṇaspati, on him.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ध्रुवा द्यौर्ध्रुवा पृथिवी ध्रुवासः पर्वता इमे ।ध्रुवं विश्वमिदं जगद्ध्रुवो राजा विशामयं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhruvā́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ dhruvā́ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dhruvā́saḥ ǀ párvatāḥ ǀ imé ǀdhruvám ǀ víśvam ǀ idám ǀ jágat ǀ dhruváḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ viśā́m ǀ ayám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Firm is the sky and firm the earth, and stedfast also are these hills. Stedfast is all this living world, and stedfast is this King of men.
verses.wilson_translation: Firm is the heaven, firm is the earth, firm are these mountains, firm is this entire world, so may this kingof men be firm.
verses.griffith_verse: Firm is the sky and firm the earth, and stedfast also are these hills. Stedfast is all this living world, and stedfast is this King of men.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ध्रुवं ते राजा वरुणो ध्रुवं देवो बृहस्पतिः ।ध्रुवं त इंद्रश्चाग्निश्च राष्ट्रं धारयतां ध्रुवं ॥
verses.transliteration: dhruvám ǀ te ǀ rā́jā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ dhruvám ǀ deváḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀdhruvám ǀ te ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ agníḥ ǀ ca ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ dhārayatām ǀ dhruvám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Stedfast, may Varuṇa the King, stedfast, the God Bṛhaspati, Stedfast, may Indra, stedfast too, may Agni keep thy stedfast reign.
verses.wilson_translation: May the royal Varuṇa, the divine Bṛhaspati, may Indraand Agniever give stability to your kingdom.
verses.griffith_verse: Stedfast, may Varuṇa the King, stedfast, the God Bṛhaspati, Stedfast, may Indra, stedfast too, may Agni keep thy stedfast reign.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ध्रुवं ध्रुवेण हविषाभि सोमं मृशामसि ।अथो त इंद्रः केवलीर्विशो बलिहृतस्करत् ॥
verses.transliteration: dhruvám ǀ dhruvéṇa ǀ havíṣā ǀ abhí ǀ sómam ǀ mṛśāmasi ǀátho íti ǀ te ǀ índraḥ ǀ kévalīḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ bali-hṛ́taḥ ǀ karat ǁ
verses.english_translation: On constant Soma let us think with constant sacrificial gift And then may Indra make the clans bring tribute unto thee alone.
verses.wilson_translation: With a constant oblation we handle the constant Soma; therefore, may Indrarender your subjectpeople their prayers.
verses.griffith_verse: On constant Soma let us think with constant sacrificial gift And then may Indra make the clans bring tribute unto thee alone.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIV. The King.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious.With this, O Brahmaṇaspati, let us attain to royal sway. Subduing those who rival us, subduing all malignities,Withstand the man who menaces, withstand the man who angers us. Soma and Savitar the God have made thee a victorious KingAll elements have aided thee, to make thee general conqueror. Oblation, that which Indra. gave and thus grew glorious and most high,—This have I offered, Gods! and hence now, verily, am rivalless. Slayer of rivals, rivalless, victorious, with royal sway,Over these beings may I rule, may I be Sovran of the folk.

verses.sanskrit: अभीवर्तेन हविषा येनेंद्रो अभिवावृते ।तेनास्मान्ब्रह्मणस्पतेऽभि राष्ट्राय वर्तय ॥
verses.transliteration: abhi-varténa ǀ havíṣā ǀ yéna ǀ índraḥ ǀ abhi-vavṛté ǀténa ǀ asmā́n ǀ brahmaṇaḥ ǀ pate ǀ abhí ǀ rāṣṭrā́ya ǀ vartaya ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious. With this, O Brahmaṇaspati, let us attain to royal sway.
verses.wilson_translation: By the abhivarta oblation, whereby Indrahas conquered (everything), do you, OBrahmaṇaspati, bringname is suggested by the repetition of the derivatives of abhivṛti].
verses.griffith_verse: WITH offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious. With this, O Brahmaṇaspati, let us attain to royal sway.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभिवृत्य सपत्नानभि या नो अरातयः ।अभि पृतन्यंतं तिष्ठाभि यो न इरस्यति ॥
verses.transliteration: abhi-vṛ́tya ǀ sa-pátnān ǀ abhí ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ árātayaḥ ǀabhí ǀ pṛtanyántam ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ abhí ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ irasyáti ǁ
verses.english_translation: Subduing those who rival us, subduing all malignities, Withstand the man who menaces, withstand the man who angers us.
verses.wilson_translation: Having overcome our rivals, and those who are our enemies, do you attack him who assails us, andhim who behaves insolently towards us.
verses.griffith_verse: Subduing those who rival us, subduing all malignities, Withstand the man who menaces, withstand the man who angers us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अभि त्वा देवः सविताभि सोमो अवीवृतत् ।अभि त्वा विश्वा भूतान्यभीवर्तो यथाससि ॥
verses.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ abhí ǀ sómaḥ ǀ avīvṛtat ǀabhí ǀ tvā ǀ víśvā ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ abhi-vartáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásasi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Soma and Savitar the God have made thee a victorious King All elements have aided thee, to make thee general conqueror.
verses.wilson_translation: May te divine Savitā, may Somaestablish you, (rājā), may all beings establish you, so that youmay be supreme.
verses.griffith_verse: Soma and Savitar the God have made thee a victorious King All elements have aided thee, to make thee general conqueror.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: येनेंद्रो हविषा कृत्व्यभवद्द्युम्न्युत्तमः ।इदं तदक्रि देवा असपत्नः किलाभुवं ॥
verses.transliteration: yéna ǀ índraḥ ǀ havíṣā ǀ kṛtvī́ ǀ ábhavat ǀ dyumnī́ ǀ ut-tamáḥ ǀidám ǀ tát ǀ akri ǀ devāḥ ǀ asapatnáḥ ǀ kíla ǀ abhuvam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Oblation, that which Indra. gave and thus grew glorious and most high,— This have I offered, Gods! and hence now, verily, am rivalless.
verses.wilson_translation: That oblation whereby Indrabecame heroic, renowned and eminent, I have offered, O gods, (to you),may I become freed from my rivals.
verses.griffith_verse: Oblation, that which Indra. gave and thus grew glorious and most high,— This have I offered, Gods! and hence now, verily, am rivalless.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: असपत्नः सपत्नहाभिराष्ट्रो विषासहिः ।यथाहमेषां भूतानां विराजानि जनस्य च ॥
verses.transliteration: asapatnáḥ ǀ sapatna-hā́ ǀ abhí-rāṣṭraḥ ǀ vi-sasahíḥ ǀyáthā ǀ ahám ǀ eṣā́m ǀ bhūtā́nām ǀ vi-rā́jāni ǀ jánasya ǀ ca ǁ
verses.english_translation: Slayer of rivals, rivalless, victorious, with royal sway, Over these beings may I rule, may I be Sovran of the folk.
verses.wilson_translation: May I become without a rival, the destroyer of my rivals, obtaining the sovereignty, overcoming (myfoes) so that I may reign over these beings and over my people.
verses.griffith_verse: Slayer of rivals, rivalless, victorious, with royal sway, Over these beings may I rule, may I be Sovran of the folk.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXV. Press-stones.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law:Be harnessed to the shafts, and press. Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence:Make ye the Cows our medicine. Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength,Look down with pride on those below. May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you as Law commands for himWho sacrifices, pouring juice.

verses.sanskrit: प्र वो ग्रावाणः सविता देवः सुवतु धर्मणा ।धूर्षु युज्यध्वं सुनुत ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ vaḥ ǀ grāvāṇaḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ suvatu ǀ dhármaṇā ǀdhūḥ-sú ǀ yujyadhvam ǀ sunutá ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitāurge you, stones, by his sustaining (action), be yoked to the chariot-poles,express (the Soma).
verses.griffith_verse: MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावाणो अप दुच्छुनामप सेधत दुर्मतिं ।उस्राः कर्तन भेषजं ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ ducchúnām ǀ ápa ǀ sedhata ǀ duḥ-matím ǀusrā́ḥ ǀ kartana ǀ bheṣajám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence: Make ye the Cows our medicine.
verses.wilson_translation: Drive away, stones, the malevolent (folk), drive away evil intention, make our cattle a remedy (againstdistress).
verses.griffith_verse: Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence: Make ye the Cows our medicine.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावाण उपरेष्वा महीयंते सजोषसः ।वृष्णे दधतो वृष्ण्यं ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ úpareṣu ǀ ā́ ǀ mahīyánte ǀ sa-jóṣasaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣṇe ǀ dádhataḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣṇyam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength, Look down with pride on those below.
verses.wilson_translation: The stones consentient with the central pivot are honoured, giving energy to the sprinkling (Soma).
verses.griffith_verse: Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength, Look down with pride on those below.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: ग्रावाणः सविता नु वो देवः सुवतु धर्मणा ।यजमानाय सुन्वते ॥
verses.transliteration: grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ nú ǀ vaḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ suvatu ǀ dhármaṇā ǀyájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you as Law commands for him Who sacrifices, pouring juice.
verses.wilson_translation: May the divine Savitāquickly urge you, stones, by his sustaining (action) for the sake of theworshipper, who makes the libation.
verses.griffith_verse: May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you as Law commands for him Who sacrifices, pouring juice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVI. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . WITH hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the Ṛbhus' mighty deeds.Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow. Bring forth the God with song divine, being Jātavedas hitherward,To bear our gifts at once to heaven. He here, a God-devoted Priest, led forward comes to sacrifice.Like a car covered for the road, he, glowing, knows, himself, the way. This Agni rescues from distress, as ’twere from the Immortal Race,A God yet mightier than strength, a God who hath been made for life.

verses.sanskrit: प्र सूनव ऋभूणां बृहन्नवंत वृजना ।क्षामा ये विश्वधायसोऽश्नंधेनुं न मातरं ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sūnávaḥ ǀ ṛbhūṇā́m ǀ bṛhát ǀ navanta ǀ vṛjánā ǀkṣā́ma ǀ yé ǀ viśvá-dhāyasaḥ ǀ áśnan ǀ dhenúm ǀ ná ǀ mātáram ǁ
verses.english_translation: WITH hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the Ṛbhus' mighty deeds. Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow.
verses.wilson_translation: The Sunus, (the sons) of theṚbhus, advance boldly to battle; supporters of all, they have spreadover the earth as (a calf) over the mother cow.
verses.griffith_verse: WITH hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the Ṛbhus' mighty deeds. Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: प्र देवं देव्या धिया भरता जातवेदसं ।हव्या नो वक्षदानुषक् ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ devám ǀ devyā́ ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ bhárata ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀhavyā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ vakṣat ǀ ānuṣák ǁ
verses.english_translation: Bring forth the God with song divine, being Jātavedas hitherward, To bear our gifts at once to heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: Bring forward the divine Jātavedasby means of divine wisdom; may he bear our oblations (to thegods) in succession.
verses.griffith_verse: Bring forth the God with song divine, being Jātavedas hitherward, To bear our gifts at once to heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयमु ष्य प्र देवयुर्होता यज्ञाय नीयते ।रथो न योरभीवृतो घृणीवांचेतति त्मना ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ syáḥ ǀ prá ǀ deva-yúḥ ǀ hótā ǀ yajñā́ya ǀ nīyate ǀráthaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yóḥ ǀ abhí-vṛtaḥ ǀ ghṛ́ṇi-vān ǀ cetati ǀ tmánā ǁ
verses.english_translation: He here, a God-devoted Priest, led forward comes to sacrifice. Like a car covered for the road, he, glowing, knows, himself, the way.
verses.wilson_translation: This ministrant priest devoted to the gods is brought (here) for the sacrifice; radiant as theswift-moving sun, uniting (the oblation and the gods) surrounded (by the priests,Agni) knows of himself (how toworship the gods).
verses.griffith_verse: He here, a God-devoted Priest, led forward comes to sacrifice. Like a car covered for the road, he, glowing, knows, himself, the way.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अयमग्निरुरुष्यत्यमृतादिव जन्मनः ।सहसश्चित्सहीयांदेवो जीवातवे कृतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ uruṣyati ǀ amṛ́tāt-iva ǀ jánmanaḥ ǀsáhasaḥ ǀ cit ǀ sáhīyān ǀ deváḥ ǀ jīvā́tave ǀ kṛtáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: This Agni rescues from distress, as ’twere from the Immortal Race, A God yet mightier than strength, a God who hath been made for life.
verses.wilson_translation: This Agnisaves from peril caused by man as (well as) from peril caused by the immortals, a godstronger than strength, created for life-producing (sacrifice).
verses.griffith_verse: This Agni rescues from distress, as ’twere from the Immortal Race, A God yet mightier than strength, a God who hath been made for life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVII. Māyābheda.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THE sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might.Sages observe him in the ocean's inmost depth: the wise disposers seek the station of his rays. The flying Bird bears Speech within his spirit: erst the Gandharva in the womb pronounced it:And at the seat of sacrifice the sages cherish this radiant, heavenly-bright invention. I saw the Herdsman, him who never resteth, approaching and departing on his pathways.He, clothed in gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.

verses.sanskrit: पतंगमक्तमसुरस्य मायया हृदा पश्यंति मनसा विपश्चितः ।समुद्रे अंतः कवयो वि चक्षते मरीचीनां पदमिच्छंति वेधसः ॥
verses.transliteration: pataṅgám ǀ aktám ǀ ásurasya ǀ māyáyā ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ paśyanti ǀ mánasā ǀ vipaḥ-cítaḥ ǀsamudré ǀ antáríti ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakṣate ǀ márīcīnām ǀ padám ǀ icchanti ǀ vedhásaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THE sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might. Sages observe him in the ocean's inmost depth: the wise disposers seek the station of his rays.
verses.wilson_translation: The wise behold their mind; (seated) in their heart the Sun made manifest by the illusion of theasura;the sages look into the solar orb, the ordainers (of solar worship) desire the region of his rays.
verses.griffith_verse: THE sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might. Sages observe him in the ocean's inmost depth: the wise disposers seek the station of his rays.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: पतंगो वाचं मनसा बिभर्ति तां गंधर्वोऽवदद्गर्भे अंतः ।तां द्योतमानां स्वर्यं मनीषामृतस्य पदे कवयो नि पांति ॥
verses.transliteration: pataṅgáḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ mánasā ǀ bibharti ǀ tā́n ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ avadat ǀ gárbhe ǀ antáríti ǀtā́m ǀ dyótamānām ǀ svaryám ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ padé ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ ní ǀ pānti ǁ
verses.english_translation: The flying Bird bears Speech within his spirit: erst the Gandharva in the womb pronounced it: And at the seat of sacrifice the sages cherish this radiant, heavenly-bright invention.
verses.wilson_translation: The Sun bears the (sacred) word in his mind the Gandharvahas spoken it, (abiding) within the womb;sages cherish it in the plural ce of sacrifice, brilliant, heavenly ruling the mind.
verses.griffith_verse: The flying Bird bears Speech within his spirit: erst the Gandharva in the womb pronounced it: And at the seat of sacrifice the sages cherish this radiant, heavenly-bright invention.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानमा च परा च पथिभिश्चरंतं ।स सध्रीचीः स विषूचीर्वसान आ वरीवर्ति भुवनेष्वंतः ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ gopā́m ǀ áni-padyamānam ǀ ā́ ǀ ca ǀ párā ǀ ca ǀ pathí-bhiḥ ǀ cárantam ǀsáḥ ǀ sadhrī́cīḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ víṣūcīḥ ǀ vásānaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ varīvarti ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ antáríti ǁ
verses.english_translation: I saw the Herdsman, him who never resteth, approaching and departing on his pathways. He, clothed in gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.wilson_translation: I beheld the protector (the Sun), never descending, going by his paths to the east and to the west;clothing (with light) the (four) quarters of heaven and the intermediate spaces, he constantly revolves in the midstof the worlds.
verses.griffith_verse: I saw the Herdsman, him who never resteth, approaching and departing on his pathways. He, clothed in gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXVIII. Tārkṣya.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant,Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Tārkṣya for our weal will we call hither. As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety.Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you. He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Sūrya with his lustre, and the waters—His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as the young maid repelleth not her lover.

verses.sanskrit: त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानां ।अरिष्टनेमिं पृतनाजमाशुं स्वस्तये तार्क्ष्यमिहा हुवेम ॥
verses.transliteration: tyám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú ǀ vājínam ǀ devá-jūtam ǀ sahá-vānam ǀ tarutā́ram ǀ ráthānām ǀáriṣṭa-nemim ǀ pṛtanā́jam ǀ āśúm ǀ svastáye ǀ tā́rkṣyam ǀ ihá ǀ huvema ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Tārkṣya for our weal will we call hither.
verses.wilson_translation: Let us invoke here for our welfare that Tārkṣya, who is mighty, the commissioned of the gods, thevictorious, the outstripper of chariots, of irresistible car, the overthrower of hosts, the swift.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Tārkṣya for our weal will we call hither.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्रस्येव रातिमाजोहुवानाः स्वस्तये नावमिवा रुहेम ।उर्वी न पृथ्वी बहुले गभीरे मा वामेतौ मा परेतौ रिषाम ॥
verses.transliteration: índrasya-iva ǀ rātím ǀ ā-jóhuvānāḥ ǀ svastáye ǀ nā́vam-iva ǀ ā́ ǀ ruhema ǀúrvī íti ǀ ná ǀ pṛ́thvī íti ǀ báhule íti ǀ gábhīre íti ǀ mā́ ǀ vām ǀ ā́-itau ǀ mā́ ǀ párā-itau ǀ riṣāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety. Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you.
verses.wilson_translation: Repeatedly invoking the liberality (of Tārkṣya), as (we do that) of Indra, let us mount upon it for ourwelfare as upon a ship; O heaven and earth, vast, expanded, manifold, profound, may we not suffer harm nowfrom (Tārkṣya's) coming to or departing from you.
verses.griffith_verse: As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety. Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सद्यश्चिद्यः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान ।सहस्रसाः शतसा अस्य रंहिर्न स्मा वरंते युवतिं न शर्यां ॥
verses.transliteration: sadyáḥ ǀ cit ǀ yáḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ páñca ǀ kṛṣṭī́ḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ apáḥ ǀ tatā́na ǀsahasra-sā́ḥ ǀ śata-sā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ ráṃhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ sma ǀ varante ǀ yuvatím ǀ ná ǀ śáryām ǁ
verses.english_translation: He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Sūrya with his lustre, and the waters— His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as the young maid repelleth not her lover.
verses.wilson_translation: He who has by his strength rapidly spread out the waters for the five castes like the sun by his light--thousand-yielding, hundred-bestowing is his course, like an unfailing arrow, none can stop it.
verses.griffith_verse: He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Sūrya with his lustre, and the waters— His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as the young maid repelleth not her lover.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXIX. Indra.
hymns.anukramani: ३ क्रमेण- शिविरौशीनरः, काशिराजः प्रतर्दनः, रौहिदश्वो वसुमनाः। इन्द्रः। त्रिष्टुप्,१ अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share.If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise. Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey.Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain. Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present.Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठताव पश्यतेंद्रस्य भागमृत्वियं ।यदि श्रातो जुहोतन यद्यश्रातो ममत्तन ॥
verses.transliteration: út ǀ tiṣṭhata ǀ áva ǀ paśyata ǀ índrasya ǀ bhāgám ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀyádi ǀ śrātáḥ ǀ juhótana ǀ yádi ǀ áśrātaḥ ǀ mamattána ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise.
verses.wilson_translation: Rise up, look to the portion of Indrasuitable to the season; if it be cooked, offer it; if uncooked, gratifyhim (by praise).
verses.griffith_verse: Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रातं हविरो ष्विंद्र प्र याहि जगाम सूरो अध्वनो विमध्यं ।परि त्वासते निधिभिः सखायः कुलपा न व्राजपतिं चरंतं ॥
verses.transliteration: śrātám ǀ havíḥ ǀ ó íti ǀ sú ǀ indra ǀ prá ǀ yāhi ǀ jagā́ma ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ ádhvanaḥ ǀ ví-madhyam ǀpári ǀ tvā ǀ āsate ǀ nidhí-bhiḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ kula-pā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vrājá-patim ǀ cárantam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain.
verses.wilson_translation: Go,Indra, quickly to the oblation which is cooked, the sun is advanced nearly to the middle of hisroad; your friends sit around you with their offerings as the protectors of a family (attend upon) the migrating lordof the mansion.
verses.griffith_verse: Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: श्रातं मन्य ऊधनि श्रातमग्नौ सुश्रातं मन्ये तदृतं नवीयः ।माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य दध्नः पिबेंद्र वज्रिन्पुरुकृज्जुषाणः ॥
verses.transliteration: śrātám ǀ manye ǀ ū́dhani ǀ śrātám ǀ agnáu ǀ sú-śrātam ǀ manye ǀ tát ǀ ṛtám ǀ návīyaḥ ǀmā́dhyandinasya ǀ sávanasya ǀ dadhnáḥ ǀ píba ǀ indra ǀ vajrin ǀ puru-kṛt ǀ juṣāṇáḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present. Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.
verses.wilson_translation: I consider (the oblation) as cooked in the udder (of the cow), I consider it cooked in the fire, I considerthis pure and fresh (oblation) well- cooked;Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, doer of many deeds, drink wellpleased of the curd of the noon-day sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present. Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXX. Indra.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty.In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches. Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance.Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us. Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o’er the people.Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ससाहिषे पुरुहूत शत्रूंज्येष्ठस्ते शुष्म इह रातिरस्तु ।इंद्रा भर दक्षिणेना वसूनि पतिः सिंधूनामसि रेवतीनां ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ sasahiṣe ǀ puru-hūta ǀ śátrūn ǀ jyéṣṭhaḥ ǀ te ǀ śúṣmaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ rātíḥ ǀ astu ǀíndra ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ dákṣiṇena ǀ vásūni ǀ pátiḥ ǀ síndhūnām ǀ asi ǀ revátīnām ǁ
verses.english_translation: O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty. In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
verses.wilson_translation: Indra, invoked of many, you triumph over your enemies; pre-eminent is your strength, may yourgenerosity be shown on this occasion; bring treasures with your righthand; you are the lord of thewealth-conveying rivers.
verses.griffith_verse: O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty. In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः परावत आ जगंथा परस्याः ।सृकं संशाय पविमिंद्र तिग्मं वि शत्रूंताळ्हि वि मृधो नुदस्व ॥
verses.transliteration: mṛgáḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ kucaráḥ ǀ giri-sthā́ḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ jagantha ǀ párasyāḥ ǀsṛkám ǀ sam-śā́ya ǀ pavím ǀ indra ǀ tigmám ǀ ví ǀ śátrūn ǀ tāḷhi ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ nudasva ǁ
verses.english_translation: Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
verses.wilson_translation: Terrible are you as a wandering lion who dwells in the mountains; come from a far-off, distant (world);having whetted your rapid and sharp bolt, destroy our enemies,Indra, put to flight our opponents.
verses.griffith_verse: Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: इंद्र क्षत्रमभि वाममोजोऽजायथा वृषभ चर्षणीनां ।अपानुदो जनममित्रयंतमुरुं देवेभ्यो अकृणोरु लोकं ॥
verses.transliteration: índra ǀ kṣatrám ǀ abhí ǀ vāmám ǀ ójaḥ ǀ ájāyathāḥ ǀ vṛṣabha ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀápa ǀ anudaḥ ǀ jánam ǀ amitra-yántam ǀ urúm ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ akṛṇoḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o’er the people. Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
verses.wilson_translation: You have been born,Indra, endowed with protecting and desirable vigour; benefactor of mankind, youdid drive away the man who was unfriendly(to us), you prepared a spacious region for the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o’er the people. Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXI. Viśvedevas.
hymns.anukramani: ३ क्रमेण- प्रथो वासिष्ठः, सप्रथो भारद्वाजः, धर्मः सौर्यः। विश्वेदेवाः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . VASIṢṬHA mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu,Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.. These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence.From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Agni, Bharadvāja brought the Brhat. They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended.From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Sūrya did these sages bring the Gharma.

verses.sanskrit: प्रथश्च यस्य सप्रथश्च नामानुष्टुभस्य हविषो हविर्यत् ।धातुर्द्युतानात्सवितुश्च विष्णो रथंतरमा जभारा वसिष्ठः ॥
verses.transliteration: práthaḥ ǀ ca ǀ yásya ǀ sa-práthaḥ ǀ ca ǀ nā́ma ǀ ā́nu-stubhasya ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ yát ǀdhātúḥ ǀ dyútānāt ǀ savitúḥ ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ ratham-tarám ǀ ā́ ǀ jabhāra ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: VASIṢṬHA mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.
verses.wilson_translation: Vasiṣṭha, whos (son) is Pratha by name, and whose (son) is Sapratha, has (with them) borne awayfrom Dhāta, and from the radiant Savitā, and from Viṣṇu, therathantaraportion of the oblation which isoffered with theanuṣṭupverse.
verses.griffith_verse: VASIṢṬHA mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अविंदंते अतिहितं यदासीद्यज्ञस्य धाम परमं गुहा यत् ।धातुर्द्युतानात्सवितुश्च विष्णोर्भरद्वाजो बृहदा चक्रे अग्नेः ॥
verses.transliteration: ávindan ǀ té ǀ áti-hitam ǀ yát ǀ ā́sīt ǀ yajñásya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ paramám ǀ gúhā ǀ yát ǀdhātúḥ ǀ dyútānāt ǀ savitúḥ ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ bharát-vājaḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀ ā́ ǀ cakre ǀ agnéḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence. From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Agni, Bharadvāja brought the Brhat.
verses.wilson_translation: They discovered (the Bṛhat) which has been put away, the most excellent substance of the sacrificewhich was hidden;Bharadvājatook the Bṛhat from Dhātā, the radiant Savitā,Viṣṇu, and Agni.
verses.griffith_verse: These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence. From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Agni, Bharadvāja brought the Brhat.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तेऽविंदन्मनसा दीध्याना यजुः ष्कन्नं प्रथमं देवयानं ।धातुर्द्युतानात्सवितुश्च विष्णोरा सूर्यादभरन्घर्ममेते ॥
verses.transliteration: té ǀ avindan ǀ mánasā ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀ yájuḥ ǀ skannám ǀ prathamám ǀ deva-yā́nam ǀdhātúḥ ǀ dyútānāt ǀ savitúḥ ǀ ca ǀ víṣṇoḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryāt ǀ abharan ǀ gharmám ǀ eté ǁ
verses.english_translation: They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended. From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Sūrya did these sages bring the Gharma.
verses.wilson_translation: Those brilliant deities discovered by their intelligence the principal means of sacrifice which has to beeffused, whichleads to the gods; these (priests) have taken the Gharmafrom Dhātā, the radiant Savitāand Viṣṇu.
verses.griffith_verse: They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended. From radiant Dhātar, Savitar, and Viṣṇu, from Sūrya did these sages bring the Gharma.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXII. Bṛhaspati.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . BṚHASPATI lead us safely over troubles and turn his evil thought against the sinner;Repel the curse, and drive away ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort! May Narāśaṁsa aid us at Prayāja: blest be our Anuyāja at invokings.May he repel the curse, and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort. May he whose head is flaming burn the demons, haters of prayer, so that the arrow slay them.May he repel the curse and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.

verses.sanskrit: बृहस्पतिर्नयतु दुर्गहा तिरः पुनर्नेषदघशंसाय मन्म ।क्षिपदशस्तिमप दुर्मतिं हन्नथा करद्यजमानाय शं योः ॥
verses.transliteration: bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ nayatu ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǀ tiráḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ neṣat ǀ aghá-śaṃsāya ǀ mánma ǀkṣipát ǀ áśastim ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-matím ǀ han ǀ átha ǀ karat ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: BṚHASPATI lead us safely over troubles and turn his evil thought against the sinner; Repel the curse, and drive away ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort!
verses.wilson_translation: Let Bṛhaspati, the overcomer of difficulties, put aside (all sins), let him thrust aside the weapon of thecalumniator; may he hurl down the inglorious (enemy), may he baffle the malevolent, and bestow upon thesacrificer health and prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: BṚHASPATI lead us safely over troubles and turn his evil thought against the sinner; Repel the curse, and drive away ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort!
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नराशंसो नोऽवतु प्रयाजे शं नो अस्त्वनुयाजो हवेषु ।क्षिपदशस्तिमप दुर्मतिं हन्नथा करद्यजमानाय शं योः ॥
verses.transliteration: nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ avatu ǀ pra-yājé ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ astu ǀ anu-yājáḥ ǀ háveṣu ǀkṣipát ǀ áśastim ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-matím ǀ han ǀ átha ǀ karat ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May Narāśaṁsa aid us at Prayāja: blest be our Anuyāja at invokings. May he repel the curse, and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.wilson_translation: May Narāśaṃsa protect us at the Prayāja rite; may he be (the giver of) felicity to us as the Anuyāja (divinity) at oblations; may Bṛhaspatihurl down the inglorious (enemy), may he baffle the malevolent,and bestow upon the sacrificer health and prosperity.
