verses.griffith_verse: May Narāśaṁsa aid us at Prayāja: blest be our Anuyāja at invokings. May he repel the curse, and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: तपुर्मूर्धा तपतु रक्षसो ये ब्रह्मद्विषः शरवे हंतवा उ ।क्षिपदशस्तिमप दुर्मतिं हन्नथा करद्यजमानाय शं योः ॥
verses.transliteration: tápuḥ-mūrdhā ǀ tapatu ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ yé ǀ brahma-dvíṣaḥ ǀ śárave ǀ hántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀkṣipát ǀ áśastim ǀ ápa ǀ duḥ-matím ǀ han ǀ átha ǀ karat ǀ yájamānāya ǀ śám ǀ yóḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: May he whose head is flaming burn the demons, haters of prayer, so that the arrow slay them. May he repel the curse and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.wilson_translation: May Tapurmūrdhā consume therākṣasas, who are the enemies of the Brāhmaṇas, (and thenproceed) to slay (their) malignant (chief); may Bṛhaspatihurl down the inglorious (enemy), may he baffle themalevolent, and bestow upon the sacrificer health and prosperity.
verses.griffith_verse: May he whose head is flaming burn the demons, haters of prayer, so that the arrow slay them. May he repel the curse and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIII. The Sacrificer, Etc.
hymns.anukramani: ३ प्रजावान् प्राजापत्यः। १ यजमानः, २ यजमानपत्नी, ३ होत्राशिवः। त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . I SAW thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed.Bestowing offspring here, bestowing riches, spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children. I saw thee pondering in thine heart, and praying that in due time thy body might be fruitful.Come as a youthful woman, rise to meet me: spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children. In plants and herbs, in all existent beings I have deposited the germ of increase.All progeny on earth have I engendered, and sons in women who will be hereafter.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं त्वा मनसा चेकितानं तपसो जातं तपसो विभूतं ।इह प्रजामिह रयिं रराणः प्र जायस्व प्रजया पुत्रकाम ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ tvā ǀ mánasā ǀ cékitānam ǀ tápasaḥ ǀ jātám ǀ tápasaḥ ǀ ví-bhūtam ǀihá ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ ihá ǀ rayím ǀ rárāṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ jāyasva ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ putra-kāma ǁ
verses.english_translation: I SAW thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed. Bestowing offspring here, bestowing riches, spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.wilson_translation: (The wife speaks). I beheld you in my mind conversant (with sacred rites), born of penance, renownedfor penance; enjoying in this world progeny and riches, do you who are desirous of offspring beget offspring.
verses.griffith_verse: I SAW thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed. Bestowing offspring here, bestowing riches, spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं त्वा मनसा दीध्यानां स्वायां तनू ऋत्व्ये नाधमानां ।उप मामुच्चा युवतिर्बभूयाः प्र जायस्व प्रजया पुत्रकामे ॥
verses.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ tvā ǀ mánasā ǀ dī́dhyānām ǀ svā́yām ǀ tanū́ íti ǀ ṛ́tvye ǀ nā́dhamānām ǀúpa ǀ mā́m ǀ uccā́ ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ babhūyāḥ ǀ prá ǀ jāyasva ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ putra-kāme ǁ
verses.english_translation: I saw thee pondering in thine heart, and praying that in due time thy body might be fruitful. Come as a youthful woman, rise to meet me: spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.wilson_translation: (The Yajamānaspeaks). I behold you in my mind radiant (with beauty), beseeching (your husband'sapproach) to your body at due season; may you, who are youthful, come up to me; bear offspring, you who aredesirous of offspring.
verses.griffith_verse: I saw thee pondering in thine heart, and praying that in due time thy body might be fruitful. Come as a youthful woman, rise to meet me: spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अहं गर्भमदधामोषधीष्वहं विश्वेषु भुवनेष्वंतः ।अहं प्रजा अजनयं पृथिव्यामहं जनिभ्यो अपरीषु पुत्रान् ॥
verses.transliteration: ahám ǀ gárbham ǀ adadhām ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǀ ahám ǀ víśveṣu ǀ bhúvaneṣu ǀ antáríti ǀahám ǀ pra-jā́ḥ ǀ ajanayam ǀ pṛthivyā́m ǀ ahám ǀ jáni-bhyaḥ ǀ aparī́ṣu ǀ putrā́n ǁ
verses.english_translation: In plants and herbs, in all existent beings I have deposited the germ of increase. All progeny on earth have I engendered, and sons in women who will be hereafter.
verses.wilson_translation: (Thehotāspeaks). I implant the seed in vegetables, the germ in all living beings; I engender progenyupon the earth; I beget children on other women.
verses.griffith_verse: In plants and herbs, in all existent beings I have deposited the germ of increase. All progeny on earth have I engendered, and sons in women who will be hereafter.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIV.
hymns.anukramani: ३ त्वष्टा गर्भकर्ता, विष्णुर्वाप्राजापत्यः। १ विष्णु-त्वष्ट्ट-प्रजापति-धातारः, २ सिनीवाली- सरस्वत्यश्विनः, ३ अश्विनौ। अनुष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . MAY Viṣṇu form and mould the womb, may Tvaṣṭar duly shape the forms,Prajāpati infuse the stream, and Dhātar lay the germ for thee. O Sinīvālī, set the germ, set thou the germ, Sarasvatī:May the Twain Gods bestow the germ, the Aśvins crowned with lotuses. That which the Aśvins Twain rub forth with the attrition-sticks of gold,—That germ of thine we invocate, that in the tenth month thou mayst bear.

verses.sanskrit: विष्णुर्योनिं कल्पयतु त्वष्टा रूपाणि पिंशतु ।आ सिंचतु प्रजापतिर्धाता गर्भं दधातु ते ॥
verses.transliteration: víṣṇuḥ ǀ yónim ǀ kalpayatu ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ piṃśatu ǀā́ ǀ siñcatu ǀ prajā́-patiḥ ǀ dhātā́ ǀ gárbham ǀ dadhātu ǀ te ǁ
verses.english_translation: MAY Viṣṇu form and mould the womb, may Tvaṣṭar duly shape the forms, Prajāpati infuse the stream, and Dhātar lay the germ for thee.
verses.wilson_translation: May Viṣṇuconstruct the womb, may Tvaṣṭāfabricate the members, may Prajāpatisprinkle (theseed), may Dhātācherish your embryo.
verses.griffith_verse: MAY Viṣṇu form and mould the womb, may Tvaṣṭar duly shape the forms, Prajāpati infuse the stream, and Dhātar lay the germ for thee.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: गर्भं धेहि सिनीवालि गर्भं धेहि सरस्वति ।गर्भं ते अश्विनौ देवावा धत्तां पुष्करस्रजा ॥
verses.transliteration: gárbham ǀ dhehi ǀ sinīvāli ǀ gárbham ǀ dhehi ǀ sarasvati ǀgárbham ǀ te ǀ aśvínau ǀ deváu ǀ ā́ ǀ dhattām ǀ púṣkara-srajā ǁ
verses.english_translation: O Sinīvālī, set the germ, set thou the germ, Sarasvatī: May the Twain Gods bestow the germ, the Aśvins crowned with lotuses.
verses.wilson_translation: Sustain the embryo,Sinīvāli, sustain the embryo,Sarasvatī, may the divine Aśvins, garlanded withlotuses, sustain your embryo.
verses.griffith_verse: O Sinīvālī, set the germ, set thou the germ, Sarasvatī: May the Twain Gods bestow the germ, the Aśvins crowned with lotuses.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्ययी अरणी यं निर्मंथतो अश्विना ।तं ते गर्भं हवामहे दशमे मासि सूतवे ॥
verses.transliteration: hiraṇyáyī íti ǀ aráṇī íti ǀ yám ǀ niḥ-mánthataḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀtám ǀ te ǀ gárbham ǀ havāmahe ǀ daśamé ǀ māsí ǀ sū́tave ǁ
verses.english_translation: That which the Aśvins Twain rub forth with the attrition-sticks of gold,— That germ of thine we invocate, that in the tenth month thou mayst bear.
verses.wilson_translation: We invoke your embryo which the A'vins have churned with the golden pieces of touchwood, that youmay bring it forth in the tenth month.
verses.griffith_verse: That which the Aśvins Twain rub forth with the attrition-sticks of gold,— That germ of thine we invocate, that in the tenth month thou mayst bear.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXV. Aditi.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . GREAT, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of Three Gods,Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. O'er these, neither at home nor yet abroad or pathways that are Strange,The evil-minded foe hath power Nor over him,. the man on whom the Sons of Aditi bestow Eternal light that he may live.

verses.sanskrit: महि त्रीणामवोऽस्तु द्युक्षं मित्रस्यार्यम्णः ।दुराधर्षं वरुणस्य ॥
verses.transliteration: máhi ǀ trīṇā́m ǀ ávaḥ ǀ astu ǀ dyukṣám ǀ mitrásya ǀ aryamṇáḥ ǀduḥ-ādhárṣam ǀ váruṇasya ǁ
verses.english_translation: GREAT, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of Three Gods, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
verses.wilson_translation: May the great, brilliant, unassailable protection of the three (deities),Mitra,Aryaman, and Varuṇa, be(granted to me).
verses.griffith_verse: GREAT, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of Three Gods, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: नहि तेषाममा चन नाध्वसु वारणेषु ।ईशे रिपुरघशंसः ॥
verses.transliteration: nahí ǀ téṣām ǀ amā́ ǀ caná ǀ ná ǀ ádhva-su ǀ vāraṇéṣu ǀī́śe ǀ ripúḥ ǀ aghá-śaṃsaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: O'er these, neither at home nor yet abroad or pathways that are Strange, The evil-minded foe hath power
verses.wilson_translation: Let not their malignant enemy have power over dwellings, or roads, or enclosures.
verses.griffith_verse: O'er these, neither at home nor yet abroad or pathways that are Strange, The evil-minded foe hath power
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै पुत्रासो अदितेः प्र जीवसे मर्त्याय ।ज्योतिर्यच्छंत्यजस्रं ॥
verses.transliteration: yásmai ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ prá ǀ jīváse ǀ mártyāya ǀjyótiḥ ǀ yácchanti ǀ ájasram ǁ
verses.english_translation: Nor over him,. the man on whom the Sons of Aditi bestow Eternal light that he may live.
verses.wilson_translation: (Nor the enemy of) the mortal upon whom the sons of Aditibestow the eternal light (of life) that he maylive.
verses.griffith_verse: Nor over him,. the man on whom the Sons of Aditi bestow Eternal light that he may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVI. Vāyu.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FILLING our hearts with health and joy, may Vāta breathe his balm on usMay he prolong our days of life. Thou art our Father, Vāta, yea, thou art a Brother and a friend,So give us strength that we may live. The store of Amṛta laid away yonder, O Vāta, in thine home,—Give us thereof that we may live.

verses.sanskrit: वात आ वातु भेषजं शंभु मयोभु नो हृदे ।प्र ण आयूंषि तारिषत् ॥
verses.transliteration: vā́taḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ vātu ǀ bheṣajám ǀ śam-bhú ǀ mayaḥ-bhú ǀ naḥ ǀ hṛdé ǀprá ǀ naḥ ǀ ā́yūṃṣi ǀ tāriṣat ǁ
verses.english_translation: FILLING our hearts with health and joy, may Vāta breathe his balm on us May he prolong our days of life.
verses.wilson_translation: May Vātabreath into our hearts a healinv balm, bringing happiness; may he prolong our lives.
verses.griffith_verse: FILLING our hearts with health and joy, may Vāta breathe his balm on us May he prolong our days of life.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: उत वात पितासि न उत भ्रातोत नः सखा ।स नो जीवातवे कृधि ॥
verses.transliteration: utá ǀ vāta ǀ pitā́ ǀ asi ǀ naḥ ǀ utá ǀ bhrā́tā ǀ utá ǀ naḥ ǀ sákhā ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ jīvā́tave ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
verses.english_translation: Thou art our Father, Vāta, yea, thou art a Brother and a friend, So give us strength that we may live.
verses.wilson_translation: You,Vāta, are both our father and our brother and our friend; cause us to live.
verses.griffith_verse: Thou art our Father, Vāta, yea, thou art a Brother and a friend, So give us strength that we may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यददो वात ते गृहेऽमृतस्य निधिर्हितः ।ततो नो देहि जीवसे ॥
verses.transliteration: yát ǀ adáḥ ǀ vāta ǀ te ǀ gṛhé ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ ni-dhíḥ ǀ hitáḥ ǀtátaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ dehi ǀ jīváse ǁ
verses.english_translation: The store of Amṛta laid away yonder, O Vāta, in thine home,— Give us thereof that we may live.
verses.wilson_translation: The store of ambrosia,Vāta, which is plural ced in your house, give us of it that we may live.
verses.griffith_verse: The store of Amṛta laid away yonder, O Vāta, in thine home,— Give us thereof that we may live.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk:So may he bear us past our foes. Who from the distance far away shines brilliantly across the wastes:So may he bear us past our foes. The Bull with brightly-gleaming flame who utterly consumes the fiendsSo may he bear us past our foes. Who looks on all existing things and comprehends them with his view:So may he bear us past our foes. Resplendent Agni, who was born in farthest region of the air:So may he bear us past our foes.

verses.sanskrit: प्राग्नये वाचमीरय वृषभाय क्षितीनां ।स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ agnáye ǀ vā́cam ǀ īraya ǀ vṛṣabhā́ya ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: Raise the hymn to Agni, the benefactor of mankind; may he bear us (safe) beyond (the reach of) thosewho hate us.
verses.griffith_verse: To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यः परस्याः परावतस्तिरो धन्वातिरोचते ।स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ párasyāḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ dhánva ǀ ati-rócate ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who from the distance far away shines brilliantly across the wastes: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May (Agni), who from a great distance shines fiercely upon the desert tract that he has attained, bearus (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.
verses.griffith_verse: Who from the distance far away shines brilliantly across the wastes: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो रक्षांसि निजूर्वति वृषा शुक्रेण शोचिषा ।स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ ni-jū́rvati ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ śukréṇa ǀ śocíṣā ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: The Bull with brightly-gleaming flame who utterly consumes the fiends So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: May (Agni), the showerer of benefits, who, his pure radiance destroys therākṣasas, bear us (safe)beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.
verses.griffith_verse: The Bull with brightly-gleaming flame who utterly consumes the fiends So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो विश्वाभि विपश्यति भुवना सं च पश्यति ।स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ abhí ǀ vi-páśyati ǀ bhúvanā ǀ sám ǀ ca ǀ páśyati ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Who looks on all existing things and comprehends them with his view: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: The Agnithat glances at all thelokas, should protect us from the ill-will of enemies.
verses.griffith_verse: Who looks on all existing things and comprehends them with his view: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: यो अस्य पारे रजसः शुक्रो अग्निरजायत ।स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥
verses.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ asyá ǀ pāré ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ śukráḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ájāyata ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ parṣat ǀ áti ǀ dvíṣaḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Resplendent Agni, who was born in farthest region of the air: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.wilson_translation: The Agnithat appears in the celestial sphere above us in the form of illumined light, should protect usfrom all kinds of sorrows and troubles.
verses.griffith_verse: Resplendent Agni, who was born in farthest region of the air: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXVIII. Agni.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . Now send ye Jātavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous SteedTo seat him on our sacred grass.. I raise the lofty eulogy of Jātavedas, raining boons,With sages for his hero band. With flames of Jātavedas which carry oblation to the Gods,May he promote our sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: प्र नूनं जातवेदसमश्वं हिनोत वाजिनं ।इदं नो बर्हिरासदे ॥
verses.transliteration: prá ǀ nūnám ǀ jātá-vedasam ǀ áśvam ǀ hinota ǀ vājínam ǀidám ǀ naḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā-sáde ǁ
verses.english_translation: Now send ye Jātavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass.
verses.wilson_translation: Urge the food-giver,Jātavedas, (as) a horse, to sit down upon this our sacred grass.
verses.griffith_verse: Now send ye Jātavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अस्य प्र जातवेदसो विप्रवीरस्य मीळ्हुषः ।महीमियर्मि सुष्टुतिं ॥
verses.transliteration: asyá ǀ prá ǀ jātá-vedasaḥ ǀ vípra-vīrasya ǀ mīḷhúṣaḥ ǀmahī́m ǀ iyarmi ǀ su-stutím ǁ
verses.english_translation: I raise the lofty eulogy of Jātavedas, raining boons, With sages for his hero band.
verses.wilson_translation: I offer earnest and ample praise to this Ja-tavedas, the showerer (of benefits), whose sons areintelligent (worshippers).
verses.griffith_verse: I raise the lofty eulogy of Jātavedas, raining boons, With sages for his hero band.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: या रुचो जातवेदसो देवत्रा हव्यवाहनीः ।ताभिर्नो यज्ञमिन्वतु ॥
verses.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ rúcaḥ ǀ jātá-vedasaḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ havya-vā́hanīḥ ǀtā́bhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ invatu ǁ
verses.english_translation: With flames of Jātavedas which carry oblation to the Gods, May he promote our sacrifice.
verses.wilson_translation: May he invest our sacrifice with those bright (flames) of Jātavedas, that are the bearers of theoblation to the gods.
verses.griffith_verse: With flames of Jātavedas which carry oblation to the Gods, May he promote our sacrifice.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CLXXXIX. Sūrya.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THIS spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east,Advancing to his Father heaven. Expiring when he draws his breath, she moves along the lucid spheres:The Bull shines out through all the sky. Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it rules supreme through thirty realmsThroughout the days at break of morn.

verses.sanskrit: आयं गौः पृश्निरक्रमीदसदन्मातरं पुरः ।पितरं च प्रयन्त्स्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ayám ǀ gáuḥ ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ akramīt ǀ ásadat ǀ mātáram ǀ puráḥ ǀpitáram ǀ ca ǀ pra-yán ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: THIS spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east, Advancing to his Father heaven.
verses.wilson_translation: This moving many-coloured (Sun) has arrived, he has sat down before his mother (earth) in the east,and advances to his father heaven.
verses.griffith_verse: THIS spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east, Advancing to his Father heaven.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: अंतश्चरति रोचनास्य प्राणादपानती ।व्यख्यन्महिषो दिवं ॥
verses.transliteration: antáríti ǀ carati ǀ rocanā́ ǀ asyá ǀ prāṇā́t ǀ apa-anatī́ ǀví ǀ akhyat ǀ mahiṣáḥ ǀ dívam ǁ
verses.english_translation: Expiring when he draws his breath, she moves along the lucid spheres: The Bull shines out through all the sky.
verses.wilson_translation: His radiance penetrates internally, drawing (the air) down (through the lungs) after having sent it up,the mighty one beholds the sky.
verses.griffith_verse: Expiring when he draws his breath, she moves along the lucid spheres: The Bull shines out through all the sky.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: त्रिंशद्धाम वि राजति वाक्पतंगाय धीयते ।प्रति वस्तोरह द्युभिः ॥
verses.transliteration: triṃśát ǀ dhā́ma ǀ ví ǀ rājati ǀ vā́k ǀ pataṅgā́ya ǀ dhīyate ǀpráti ǀ vástoḥ ǀ áha ǀ dyú-bhiḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it rules supreme through thirty realms Throughout the days at break of morn.
verses.wilson_translation: The thirty stations of the day and night shine with (the sun's) rays, the gvoice (of praise) is addressedto the Sun.
verses.griffith_verse: Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it rules supreme through thirty realms Throughout the days at break of morn.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXC. Creation.
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born:Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose. From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced,Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye. Dhātar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon.He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतं च सत्यं चाभीद्धात्तपसोऽध्यजायत ।ततो रात्र्यजायत ततः समुद्रो अर्णवः ॥
verses.transliteration: ṛtám ǀ ca ǀ satyám ǀ ca ǀ abhī́ddhāt ǀ tápasaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ ajāyata ǀtátaḥ ǀ rā́trī ǀ ajāyata ǀ tátaḥ ǀ samudráḥ ǀ arṇaváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
verses.wilson_translation: Truth (of thought) and truthfulness (of speech) were born of arduous penance, thence was nightgenerated, thence also the watery ocean.
verses.griffith_verse: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रादर्णवादधि संवत्सरो अजायत ।अहोरात्राणि विदधद्विश्वस्य मिषतो वशी ॥
verses.transliteration: samudrā́t ǀ arṇavā́t ǀ ádhi ǀ saṃvatsaráḥ ǀ ajāyata ǀahorātrā́ṇi ǀ vi-dádhat ǀ víśvasya ǀ miṣatáḥ ǀ vaśī́ ǁ
verses.english_translation: From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced, Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye.
verses.wilson_translation: From the watery ocean was the year afterwards produced, ordaining nights and days, the ruler ofevery moment.
verses.griffith_verse: From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced, Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सूर्याचंद्रमसौ धाता यथापूर्वमकल्पयत् ।दिवं च पृथिवीं चांतरिक्षमथो स्वः ॥
verses.transliteration: sūryācandramásau ǀ dhātā́ ǀ yathāpūrvám ǀ akalpayat ǀdívam ǀ ca ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ ca ǀ antárikṣam ǀ átho íti ǀ sváḥ ǁ
verses.english_translation: Dhātar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon. He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.
verses.wilson_translation: Dhātāin the beginning created the sun and moved the heaven, the earth, the firmament, and thehappy (sky).
verses.griffith_verse: Dhātar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon. He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

hymns.title: HYMN CXCI. Agni.
hymns.anukramani: ४ संवनन आङ्गिरसः। १ अग्निः,२-४ संज्ञानम्। अनुष्टुप् , ३ त्रिष्टुप्।
hymns.griffith_hymn_text: . THOU, mighty Agni, gatherest up all that is precious for thy friend.Bring us all treasures as thou art enkindled in libation's place Assemble, speak together: let your minds be all of one accord,As ancient Gods unanimous sit down to their appointed share. The place is common, common the assembly, common the mind, so be their thought united.A common purpose do I lay before you, and worship with your general oblation. One and the same be your resolve, and be your minds of one accord.United be the thoughts of all that all may happily agree.

verses.sanskrit: संसमिद्युवसे वृषन्नग्ने विश्वान्यर्य आ ।इळस्पदे समिध्यसे स नो वसून्या भर ॥
verses.transliteration: sám-sam ǀ ít ǀ yuvase ǀ vṛṣan ǀ ágne ǀ víśvāni ǀ aryáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀiḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀ sám ǀ idhyase ǀ sáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vásūni ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǁ
verses.english_translation: THOU, mighty Agni, gatherest up all that is precious for thy friend. Bring us all treasures as thou art enkindled in libation's place
verses.wilson_translation: Agni, showerer (of benefits), you who are the lord, you verily combine with all creatures, you are kindled upon the footmark of Iḷā (the altar); bring unto us riches.
verses.griffith_verse: THOU, mighty Agni, gatherest up all that is precious for thy friend. Bring us all treasures as thou art enkindled in libation's place
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: सं गच्छध्वं सं वदध्वं सं वो मनांसि जानतां ।देवा भागं यथा पूर्वे संजानाना उपासते ॥
verses.transliteration: sám ǀ gacchadhvam ǀ sám ǀ vadadhvam ǀ sám ǀ vaḥ ǀ mánāṃsi ǀ jānatām ǀdevā́ḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ yáthā ǀ pū́rve ǀ sam-jānānā́ḥ ǀ upa-ā́sate ǁ
verses.english_translation: Assemble, speak together: let your minds be all of one accord, As ancient Gods unanimous sit down to their appointed share.
verses.wilson_translation: Meet together, talk together, let your minds apprehend alike; in like manner as the ancient godsconcurring accepted their portion of the sacrifice.
verses.griffith_verse: Assemble, speak together: let your minds be all of one accord, As ancient Gods unanimous sit down to their appointed share.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानो मंत्रः समितिः समानी समानं मनः सह चित्तमेषां ।समानं मंत्रमभि मंत्रये वः समानेन वो हविषा जुहोमि ॥
verses.transliteration: samānáḥ ǀ mántraḥ ǀ sám-itiḥ ǀ samānī́ ǀ samānám ǀ mánaḥ ǀ sahá ǀ cittám ǀ eṣām ǀsamānám ǀ mántram ǀ abhí ǀ mantraye ǀ vaḥ ǀ samānéna ǀ vaḥ ǀ havíṣā ǀ juhomi ǁ
verses.english_translation: The place is common, common the assembly, common the mind, so be their thought united. A common purpose do I lay before you, and worship with your general oblation.
verses.wilson_translation: Common be the prayer of these (assembled worshippers), common be the acquisition, common thepurpose, associated be the desire. I repeat for you a common prayer, I offer for you with a common oblation.
verses.griffith_verse: The place is common, common the assembly, common the mind, so be their thought united. A common purpose do I lay before you, and worship with your general oblation.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)

verses.sanskrit: समानी व आकूतिः समाना हृदयानि वः ।समानमस्तु वो मनो यथा वः सुसहासति ॥
verses.transliteration: samānī́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ā́-kūtiḥ ǀ samānā́ ǀ hṛ́dayāni ǀ vaḥ ǀsamānám ǀ astu ǀ vaḥ ǀ mánaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ vaḥ ǀ sú-saha ǀ ásati ǁ
verses.english_translation: One and the same be your resolve, and be your minds of one accord. United be the thoughts of all that all may happily agree.
verses.wilson_translation: Common, (worshipppers), be your intention; common be (the wishes of) your hearts; common be yourthoughts, so that there may be thorough union among you.
verses.griffith_verse: One and the same be your resolve, and be your minds of one accord. United be the thoughts of all that all may happily agree.
verses.translator: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
